title: “Great place!”
text:
I booked two second floor rooms at the Orchard Garden Hotel, one room with two doubles and one with a king. Both rooms were excellent. They were both very quiet and the beds were super comfy.
We didn't interact much with the staff, but had no complaints with anyone. You do have to wait a few minutes to get your car, but they tell you that in advance, so we planned accordingly.
We did not eat at the hotel restaurant because there were so many other places to eat in SF. There are a couple great places right across the street.
This is a great hotel in a great location. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
This large property is located in downtown Boston, about a $20 cab ride from Logan Airport. My room was located on one of the upper floors had gorgeous views of Boston and the harbour. There were plenty of elevators to the higher floors, so never experienced any wait time. This is a busy hotel. I arrived mid-afternoon, experienced a small wait during checkin and my room was ready. The king room was large, with the expected amenities of a Westin. WiFi is extra $13 and the mini bar costs are high. While not as gorgeous as other rooms I've stayed, you're paying for the location of the hotel. It's an easy walk to Newbury Street (shopping) and Boylston Street (food) and sits directly across from Back Bay Station (should you want to take the train (T) from the airport or anywhere else for that matter. Across the street is the simply gorgeous Boston Public Library - make sure you take a tour, as well as their local food store, Shaws, should you want to grab snacks during your day travel. Near by is the Prudential Center and the hotel is attached to an upscale mall. The location is the best in the city - 10 minute cab ride to Cambridge (Harvard/MIT) or walk to some of the best restaurants in the country. 
I had breaksfast in the hotel (pricey buffet and the service was poor), but also ate in the

title: “Convenient Spot”
text:
Based on previous reviews I made a mental checklist on things to look for:
Isolated location? I didn't see any convenient places within walking distance. If you're going elsewhere to eat, be prepared to drive or make a substantial walk. It also seems like there are no other people around unless they're in their cars. 
Parking ? Yes, $13 out back, $24 valet. Thanks for the warning. I can understand why someone might be uncomfortable walking from the back lot (see above). I felt okay, but I'm sure my wife would have reservations if she were alone.
Staff? Check in and out was quick and convenient, the front desk staff I dealt with was friendly and informative and even the cleaning people acknowledged us and were friendly.
Elevator problems? We didn't have any problems, but we were amused at the warning signs and the printed explanation in the hotel information packet. Yes, it's a long term problem.
Chipped bathtub? Sure, there they are. It didn't affect the operation, but with the repairs and old tiles, it almost felt like you stepped into a different level of room to shower.
Hair in the drain? None, but I have a headful of my own, if needed. The bathroom, as well as the rest of the room, was very clean.
The location was convenient for us because it was just a few blocks from the rental car center and our plans to explore the coast to the north of town (Santa Barbara) as well as south (Orange Coast). We had a late arrival and early departure, so being near the airport helped with time. 
We got back fairly late one night and had appetizers in Shula's, which were very good. Also, our package included the breakfast buffet. Since it was included, I forgot to note the price, but we were very pleased with the quality, selection and attention of the staff.
The pool area was very nice and there were families using it most of the time that we were there. I didn't have a chance to check out the exercise facility. 
We were pleased with our experience as everything went off without a glitch. Based on this stay and, for a reasonable price, we'd stay here again and not discourage anyone from trying it.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: Wont stay anywhere else unless I have to . Very close to Wharf, China Town, Little Italy adn cable cars!

title: “Nice but not Gaga over zaza”
text: I Guess I don't get it. or maybe at 50 I am just getting old. the rooms were nice . the staff was nice. nothing overwhelming. just had a feeling I was paying about 50 percent too much. our theme suite wasn't as much eclectic as it was kookie. still I kind of liked it and maybe would go back if I had a good deal.

title: “Felt like history in the making”
text:
During the first week of July, I spent 3 nights at the World Center Hotel. I had read the reviews and knew that the hotel was near the construction site of Ground Zero, so was prepared for some noise and land-moving equipment nearby. As it turned out, this was one of the most intriguing aspects of my trip to NYC. From my room I could see the fenced-in site, being readied for September 11, 2011. From the restaurant terrace on the top of the World Center Hotel, one had a bird's eye view of the various construction projects underway: fountain, financial center and memorial. It was amazing. 
The hotel itself reminded me of a European boutique hotel. Desk staff were helpful in sending me to the nearby subways, and offering tips for sightseeing. Location is convenient-walking distance to Wall Street, Battery Park, restaurants.. 
My room was small but carefully designed with bedside digital temperature controls, comfy bed, and modern expensive bathroom fixtures. My only criticism related to housekeeping services. Late one evening I put my room service tray outside my door for pickup, and it was the 2nd evening before it was removed. On my 2nd morning I did not leave the room til late morning, removing the "do not disturb" sign. On my return early evening for freshening up before again setting out, my room had not been cleaned/bed made. When I reported this to the front desk, I was advised it was too late to have this done, but they would bring up fresh towels if I put the old ones outside my door. So I did this; a minor inconvenience. Guess I would have appreciated more in the way of service, or a later acknowledgment of concern by the staff. 
All in all, I found the World Center Hotel a "find", especially at the price for a Manhattan hotel. I would recommend it now, for once the construction is completed, the budget-minded won't be able to afford it!

title: “Large room for Manhattan - uite good overall”
text: The room was larger than your typical NYC boutique hotel room and it was very clean and modern. Beds are very comfy with nice bedding. The hallways are nothing fancy and the property lacks a restaurant, bar or pool however the breakfast/happy hour area on the 2nd floor is quite nice and the neighborhood is chock full of places for drinks and eating. Great location. Overall pretty good! Was not disappointed. A bit pricy but delivered on a good amount of classiness in general.

title: “Great Stay”
text: Renaissance Hotel & Times Square, a winning combination.Room very comfortable, staff very friendly. If you are going to New York then this is the best location to stay and this has to be one of the best hotels.

title: “Sleeping in Seattle”
text: This older but renovated hotel in the Queen Anne neighborhood of Seattle, is conveniently situated close to several attractions and sights to see in Seattle. The roof top viewing deck is a great place to watch the sunset or view the skyline at night. The rooms are clean, comfortable affordable,and quiet for being in the city. Several restaurants close by, a grocery store if you prefer to stay in your room for meals, a movie theater, and Seattle Center and Space Needle, all are within walking distance of the hotel. Staff very friendly and willing to assist.

title: “Very Desolate (even in the middle of Austin) But otherwise ok”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for three nights on a business trip. I traveled alone and thought I would be able to walk across the street and get some food, but the ONLY place in walking distance (if alone and a lady) is a gas station (and I would not have gone at night). I would not advise booking this hotel if you are alone and without personal transportation.
The hotel staff was pretty nice. The room was pretty clean. I did not find any bed bugs. I would tell you to stay, if at all possible on the lake side. The traffic noise really interrupted my sleep. I had to eat there (since I could not go anywhere) and the food was more than edible.

title: “Great location fat guy on reception very rude and sullen”
text: Hi we stayed in the wellington for one night only in January. Check in in very slow and as we only had 1.5 days in new york to see the sights we got rather annoyed at one particular fat red headed employee who from the start of the checkin was very unhelpful sullen and didnt want to answer any of our questions. Rooms very basic ask for a high floor as noise is very high in the area. The bathroom you could hardly swing a cat. But the location made up for all of this.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
We chose this hotel because the last time our convention was in Philadephia this hotel was so incredible - staff and facilities. This stay was the polar opposite. We were at the hotel for a week and had some good experiences and mostly adequate to bad experiences.
On Saturday I was gone all day to a meeting but my roommate stayed away from the room so the maid could clean the room. She might as well stayed in the room and done her work. When I arrived back in the room at 3p the room had not been cleaned. Not knowing the maid's cart was on the floor most of the day I went down to the business center to check email. Getting back up to the room at 4p my roommate called down to the desk to find out when they were going to clean the room and was told that the maids were leaving for the day but that they would get one to clean our room. At 5p I called to find out whether they were going to clean the room since I had a 6:30p dinner. The maid finally showed up at 5:15p but did a lousy job including wiping glasses with a dirty rag. The front desk called at 6p to find out whether our room had been cleaned. They apologized by saying that the hotel had been full. The hotel was full but not with unexpected guests; they knew they were going to be full but did not have adequate staffing. 
I could have put this off to poor planning if this had been the only bad experience. The front desk staff were rude to my roommate when she checked in and were unhelpful several times when I asked a question. On our last night we asked a bellhop to pick up boxes for shipping. After 2 hours and calling several times to find out how long till someone would be up, we wanted to go to bed. My roommate went down and got a cart and we took them down ourself. The bellhop told us that they were never told of our request; he said if he had that he would have been right up.

title: “Not the Best Western”
text: A good location with yachts on either side of the hotel and a nice room although a little way from restaurants and any night life. Car parking was a bit difficult. We had a door to the front of the room that led to a small seating area on the front. When we arrived we were given a ticket for a complimentary American breakfast in the restaurant. On arriving in the restaurant we had to wait some 10 minutes to order and were, eventually, given a coffee. We then had to wait 30 minutes and eventually gave up on the breakfast. There was no one around to take our complaint and we had wasted the best part of an hour not getting breakfast. Eventually the hotel provided a couple of muffins and danish to see us through the morning. Not well organised in the restaurant and it wasn't really busy in there.

title: “Great Family Vacation Spot”
text: I've stayed here many times while in San Diego, both for business and on vacation. They remodeled the rooms within the last few years, which is good as many of them were quite tired. The hotel property really has a resort feel but is not really high-end as much as it is family-friemdly. The beach is a short walk from almost every room (and is far less crowded than may other area beaches) and there are lots of pools throughout the property, and there are also bike rentals, mini-golf, and tennis on-site, so you can stay on the grounds and still have lots to do. Sea World is less than a 2 minute drive away, and downtown is only about a 15 minute trip. It's not really convenient for business other than on-site conferences but makes for a great getaway if you happen to be in the San Diego area. It can also get pricey during peak summer months, as is expected, but you can find great deals and often get upgraded by going during off-peak times. Overall, I really like this hotel and hope to be back again soon.

title: “Great Hotel, Perfect Location”
text: The room was very clean. The hotel grounds are well kept and the whole place feels very new and comfortable.

title: “Friendliest Staff”
text: The front desk had the friendliest staff I've ever encountered. All of the reps were very helpful and happy. Brandy and Ally were especially memorable. Rooms were clean and spacious. The rooms were not glamorous but I wasn't expecting that. They were great rooms for the price and especially the location. Free continental breakfast along with internet in the rooms as well as in the lobby at no cost.

title: “Great location, very good hotel”
text: My wife and I just returned from a two-night stay at Hotel Sax. We were almost put-off by some negative comments in older TripAdvisor reviews but decided to keep our reservation. It was good that we did! The location of the hotel was great, our room, although one of their smaller rooms was much more than adequate, very comfy bed and, although the decor is a bit odd, the welcoming attitude of EVERY staff member was excellent: doorman, porter, check-in, concierge and cleaning crew. Only one negative: Don't have the corned beef hash for breakfast. It was vile.

title: “Very run of the mill”
text: Having read good reviews of this hotel we were sadly dissapointed. Arriving after a 10 hour flight from the UK the bored and uncharacteristig girl at the check in desk informed us, we had no booking. We gave her the confirmation print out, which was greeted with a shrug. After a lenghy, silent tapping on her computer she graciously said we could stay and gave us the key and pointed to the lift. We had booked and pre paid for a delux twin room and were given a queen room. The room was not cleaned and the bed unmade. Anyway after another long wait we eventually got a clean room with a king bed. But the hotel is bland and the staff throughout the place pretty uninterrested in the guest. Food in the restaurant below standart of a 4* establishment. Not worth the money!

title: “Good Hotel for Reasonable Price”
text:
A pleasant surprise resulted from our Internet searches at Trip Advisor! Have you ever searched for a good, well-located hotel in NYC?! Some of the prices are staggering, and then you see what you got for your money - like one double bed, a 200-year-old room, and no air-conditioning! 
Well, you need to look at the Hilton Garden Inn - Times Square. The hotel is really WELL situated - 8th at 48th - walking distant to theaters, Times Square, Rockefeller Center, close to bus stops, cabs right at the door. Four nights - grand total (with one movie) $1,270 - $319.00 per night, including the super-high NYC taxes (20%). The hotel seems small, but there is a lobby area with seating and TV and coffee, tea, and hot chocolate, plus a concierge desk, plus the check-in desk. Internet access facility adjacent to the lobby, as well as a small store for miscellaneous travel and gift items. Plentiful, fast elevators. Free USA Today. 
Best of all - while the rooms are small-ish, everything in the standard-size room is NEW and large-sized! King-size bed, HDTV, microwave, hair dryer, LOTS of linens, closet with hangers, great shower, desk, chair, luggage rack. Oh! It IS air-conditioned; not all hotels in NYC are! Attached to the lobby is a nice restaurant - Pigalle; open morning, noon, and night. Breakfast is the most reasonably priced service. Give this one a try if you are trying to avoid rates of $400+ per night in Manhattan.

title: “Rude Staff”
text:
We Chose Days Inn Sea Word/Airport because it offered a shuttle from the airport to the hotel and also to the cruise terminal. Also because it was affordable and could hold more people (suites).
I called the day before we were to leave the airport and was assured that getting the shuttle from the airport would be no problem. Got to the airport and called the hotel only to find that they would not answer the phone. Tried for nearly a half hour when someone suguested we call another Days Inn. They got a hold of the hotel (by radio?) and told us that the shuttle would be to get us in about 15 minutes. After sitting at the airport for over 2 hrs the shuttle finally comes.
After arriving at the hotel to check in, we calmly asked why they didn't answer the phone and that we had been waiting for over two hours. The girl at the desk immediately copped an attitude and refused to even help us. We got another employee to help us be she was also rude. Told my husband to sit down and shut up if we wanted to be helped. We were also told we could get our money back and go elsewere.
I paid almost three hundred dollars for two rooms. I didn't choose this hotel to be treated like crap. Then they said they didn't even have my reservation after I had confirmed it several times before. They finally found both reservations, but only one room was ready. Checked into that room while they finished cleaning the second room. Made a reservation for the next day's shuttle to take us to the cruise terminal.
The rooms were both clean, and somewhat updated. House keeping staff was polite in giving extra towles for pool. Pool is somewhat small but adequate. Hotel is near a Walgreens, Target and shopping center. We ate at the Sizlzler. All within walking distance. 
I booked this through hotels.com. The price was good for a one nights stay, but I can't say that I would stay at any Days Inn again after the way we were treated. I am in the process of contacting this hotel chain for their comments and to resolve this.

title: “We loved the staff and the hotel”
text: We loved the staff at this New York hotel, we were there during the hurricane last weekend when they had staff not able to get to work as all public transport was shut down, the staff stayed in the hotel so they could cook and clean the next day, amidst some very trying times they were extremely helpful and curteous at all times, they went above and beyond their job descripion to help everyone. We were part of a group of 18 people and everyone felt the same as we did. Also the hotel is only 18months old and very nice, lovely rooms and very quiet. Only 2 blocks from Times Square so very convenient.

title: “Perfect location!”
text: The hotel is clean and parking is free and location is perfect, right behind the Kodak Theatre takes 2 min. to get there! Pls. be aware that it's old and not fancy. Staff was friendly and helpfull.

title: “disappointing”
text:
The lobby of this hotel looks great, and the location is excellent (close to Metro, Convention Center, and tourist sites) but from the moment I arrived I experienced various disappointments. First, I had been expecting a FedEx package that, according to the tracking #, had already arrived, but the front desk had no record of it and the shipping/receiving office kept switching me over to the security office, which would either not answer or answer, put me on hold and then cut me off; then they called to say the package had arrived and to come get it; I was about to go downstairs and they called and said they DIDN"T have it. I went to complain at the front desk and they insisted the tracking number I gave them wasn't valid and made me go back up to my 12th-floor room to check it on my computer (at a cost of $13) rather than let me use their computer--only to then call and apologize because they DID have my package....
Next, the room was just okay, in that they had skimped on anything they could possible skimp on. The bathroom has NO COUNTERTOP--just a tiny sink basin; I had to put my things on the back of the toilet. The blinds don't close all the way, the lights are insufficient.... The best thing was the very comfy bed and excellent pillows.
Next, this is one of those hotels that charges you for everything; the gym was included (and very nice) but internet and all meals (the food was indeed good) were extra. For instance, coffee at breakfast cost $3.50! A cup of coffee...
Finally, one night during my stay, the fire alarm went off and we were all instructed not to take the elevator, so I went down 12 flights of stairs (with some unfortunate family with 2 kids and a crying baby behind me) and was waiting outside when I saw an employee who looked a little too blase about the whole thing. I asked if this happened often, and he said "About twice a week."
So, despite the great location and nice lobby, I don't recommend this place.

title: “Stay Out Of Venice”
text:
I got an ocean front room when I stayed here. While the inside of the room was very pretty, all exposed brick and lofty looking, and the staff were as helpful as they could be, I never once felt safe. There is no one there at night, and I saw homeless men walking down the main halls more than once. My room was low enough that if I'd left the shutters open anyone could look up into my room, thus making a ocean front room pointless since I never opened the blinds. Some of the windows didn't lock properly and could in theory be accessed by the adjoining rooftop of the building next door. I found a few bugs in the kitchenette. The washroom was drafty and cramped, and trying to have a shower in the claw foot tub was very annoying.
While I would never stay here again, I also wouldn't stay in Venice Beach ever again either. It's wonderful to visit for the day, go on a Saturday and see the boardwalk in full swing, go to the canals, and Abbot Kinney, but really if you want to have a fun, safe vacation, don't go here.

title: “Superb location”
text:
The biggest advantage of this hotel is its location, right behind Hollywood Highland (we loved hanging out there in the evenings).
also the free parking and easy access to all the sights is a big plus. 
would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “comfortable, clean and close to attractions”
text: We loved our stay at the dunes. The rooms were very clean and the clerks were extremely friendly and helpful. There is a restaurant and lounge on location and the food was very good and the people very friendly. I would stay here again and hope to do so in the future. I'm glad we picked the dunes for our stay.

title: “Great Location, Lots of Positives, One Negative”
text:
Located within walking distance of lots of neat attractions including the UT campus and LBJ library (note that most of the library is closed until mid-December), several museums, the Texas state capitol and the French Quarter-like 6ixth Street and Red River districts.
The hotel includes two nice pools (one in, one out), very good workout facilities and a genuinely friendly server at the morning coffee bar. Other staff were very friendly and helpful as well. Nice view from rooms that face downtown (request a room opposite the I-35 side of the property).
The one negative is that the room was clean, but not sparkling, and we found a number of long black hairs in and around the bathroom that didn't come from us.
Still would recommend for the many positives.

title: “Convenience, service and efficiency”
text:
We had a flawless stay at the Marriott Marquis. I was not expecting much: this is an older hotel and a huge one at that...but I was blown away by the service of the staff, which was more like that of a small boutique hotel than a gigantic conference center. It was really impressive and made a big difference in our stay....front desk very attentive to our group, housekeepers cheerfully cleaning up the havoc wrecked by our kids in the room, great room service, great concierge who lined up several things for us...
No, the rooms are not stylish and new, but they are perfectly clean and functional. Note: this is not a charming, soulful hotel: it's a huge conference center. I wouldn't stay here for a romantic getaway...but it was perfect for our needs (traveling with kids for family event). The fantastic pool on the 4th floor was a hit with the kids, as was the Yerba Buena playground across the street. Centrally located...I thought the location was great. There's a Starbucks in the lobby that was also quite useful! We had a drink in the bar at the top of the building and the view is really special...great for a snack and a glass of wine...

title: “Perfect Location”
text: I made my first trip to San Franscisco with my husband over the 4th of July weekend. The city is absolutely beautiful and there is so much to see and do there. The Grand Hyatt at Union Square is perfectly located. We were in the middle of it all: shopping, restaurants, and walking distance to some key attractions. We stayed on the club level which offered some great views. Although the hotel is due for renovations it was still nice and clean. It was obvious that although they haven't updated in a while they have maintained it fairly well. The club level lounge is a bit small but the service was good. The room and bathroom were a bit small and the bathrooms do not have separate showers. We would definitely stay there again, especially since renovations are under way.

title: “Good location, but needs a facelift”
text:
A friend and I stayed at the Radisson Warwick for two nights in April. While the location is excellent, our experiences with the hotel itself were less than stellar. 
Our room was adequate, but the bathroom was horrible. It was so small that the toilet paper holder was on the wall behind the toilet (where it was nearly impossible to reach), and there was no towel rack. There was a huge water stain above the shower. It looked fresh, so I touched the ceiling to make sure it wasn't wet, and I when I did, plaster crumbled all over the place. 
When I book a room on Priceline or Hotwire I don't expect the best rooms, but this one was next to the elevator AND across the hall from the ice machine, which meant constant noise at all hours. I slept horribly both nights, even with earplugs. 
The common areas of the hotel were very nice, and it seems like it was once a really nice hotel, but the rooms (and especially the bathrooms) could use some updating.
Also, if you're driving to the hotel, be aware that the nearest parking garage is right before the hotel. If you pass it to check in first, be prepared to loop around a maze of one-way streets to get back to it. It's $20/day, which is reasonable for the area.

title: “Not my favorite out of other Boston Starwood choices...”
text:
My husband and I just stayed at the W for one night, this past weekend. Arrival & check-in were quick & easy. We headed up to our room (5th floor), put the key in and began to open the door - when someone in the room yelled "I'm busy!". Surprised... we shut the door and went back to the reception desk. Side note: Prior to our arrival - I had e-mailed the hotel (at their invitation) twice - asking for a low floor room and early check-in. I had not received a response by the time we arrived. I have done the same with the Westin and the Sheraton and always received a response.
They gave us another room (12th floor), citing a computer glitch. They offered us two drink tickets at the bar and to credit our SPG account 1,000 points.
The rooms are very nice - although I think they try too hard to be hip & trendy. There is an appearance of quality - but in reality, there are chinks in that armour... e.g. the towel hanger pulls out of the wall, the soap dishes in the shower are loose, the light switch on the lamp falls off.... small silly stuff, but a series of these things gives a sense of lack of quality. That being said - the BEST part about the room is the bed & the sheets. Super comfortable and cozy!!! No quality skimping there, which - in a hotel is critical, The room was very clean, as well. No complaints there.
On other reviews I had read about the wierd bathroom - and I agree that is one area where the attempt to be hip & trendy went a bit too far. What wasn't clear to us from other reviews is that the toilet is actually separated from the shower & sink area by a door. Some of the reviews made it sound like there was no door - only a screen.
We made use of the Acura Experience - which was super convenient and our driver was great! 
Upon returning to the hotel at night - we asked the bar for bottled water for our drink tickets - and were told that the two tickets only equaled one bottle of water?!? So, that's what we took - but it seemed really bizarre. The bar was packed at midnight - with a very young, noisy crowd.
Check out is as 12, which is nice with the option of a 4PM late check-out for no additional fee - also a nice beefit - not sure if that is specific to Starwood members or not... The street/ambulance noise is real - but no different than many downtown hotels. The location is great for walking access to all the attractions.

title: “A nice place, with a few cautions”
text:
This review was heading for 2-star country but was redeemed by the manager's concern. 
Call it a 3.5.
First, the positives - 
 Our room was typical Holiday Inn, perfectly adequate for the purpose. The location is convenient to attractions, and walking a few blocks you can be inside the Ride Free Area for public transportation. The neighborhood is not elegant, but we didn't feel it was sketchy as another reviewer did. Internet service was good; we don't have wifi on the laptop,so being able to still plug into a data port was very helpful. Staff was helpful but not totally knowledgeable, we had a heck of a time figuring out how to get the bus downtown, Parking is convenient, though it's really a tight squeeze getting in and out.
Now the problem - 
 Our room was really noisy. The exhaust vent in the bathroom was audible in the bedroom. More troublesome, there was a more or less constant machinery noise behind the wall near the window, perhaps the a/c or plumbing system. Normally, I'd just ask to be moved. In this case I didn't because we had very limited time to tour the city. When we checked out I mentioned this to the manager behind the desk, who apologized, scolded me gently for not complaining sooner, and knocked off our parking fees. So, I'd recommend it, but listen carefully before you unpack..

title: “Another great stay and a great room service dinner at the Wyndham Garden.”
text:
Well, I stayed here again last night after the UT game, and it was an even better stay than last time. The hotel restaurant was closed early that night, so me and my father ended up getting two gourmet burgers from room service once we figured out how to use the phone in the room. The burgers were exceptionally tasty because they used a special kind of sweet bun made by Sheila Parton, a baker out of Houston. There are only two other places that used Sheila Parton buns, and one of them, the Stables in Houston, closed down 5 years ago. The other is in Ingram near Kerrville. 
 The staff was very good, just like last time. I like how "laid back" they were here. The lady that brought us room service wasn't dressed formally, but in a burnt orange T-Shirt with a musical staff. When she brought the wrong drinks for my dad, she didn't mind going back down and getting it right.
 The shower was just as good at getting me clean from sweating in humidity at the football stadium as it was last time. The shampoo and soap were top of the line.
 The room was fantastic for the most part, but it wasn't totally flawless. They really could use a new flat-screen TV to replace the older one, the fan was loud, but that didn't bother me one bit, my bed kinda felt a little saggy on my side, but for me, it actually made it more comfortable for me, and I had to use a towel to block out the light from the hallway. They also could use a microwave and a mini-fridge, as two of the three Sprites that I got from room service were kinda warm, but they got chilled in the chilly room, which was good. The rest of the room, from the comfy, ergonomic office chair to the leather recliner to the comfy Be Well bedding, was exceptional. I also like how the fan was already on and had cooled the room when we entered it, even though the power switch by the door that you need to put your key into was off.
 Overall, there are things that can be done in the rooms, but once they do them, this hotel will be perfect. I look forward to staying at the Wyndham Garden again.

title: “Large hotel in great downtown location”
text: The hotel is a huge hotel positioned right at the end of 16th Street Mall. The room was very large if a little basically furnished, clean and with an incredible view. I was on the 22 floor of the building across the road from the reception. The view was directly down 16th Street with snow capped mountains in the distance, one of the best hotel views I have ever experienced, ask reception for a room on this floor in this direction if possible. The hotel has an outstanding gym, the best I have ever seen in a hotel with at least 20 weights machines and around the same number of cardio machines, in addition to free weights. It also has an outdoor pool (not used because of snow). Just off the reception area are several cafes, a soup takeaway and a bar/restaurant with an exceptional tap list of over 100 beers and good food. Overall a very comfortable if slightly impersonal hotel with excellent amenities and a great location.

title: “Best hotel in downtown Seattle”
text:
This is the best location in downtown Seattle. It is also the best priced hotel for this class of hotel in downtown. 
I use to live in Seattle and always walked by this hotel and would look in through the large window where the bar is located and would always want to go inside. It has a warm and inviting look to it and I was not one bit disspointed. 
First of all, the staff is excellent. From the valet that greets you when you drive up, to the front desk personnel, and the personnel that maintains the rooms, everyone is superb. 
The room was very nice with great beds and wonderful bed linens. The bathroom is a bit small but this is the price you pay for staying in an older hotel in the heart of downtown. The small bathroom was a small sacrifice considering the hotel has rooms with two queen size beds and is located on the same block as Westlake center and is only a few blocks to Pike Place Market. The rooms are also beautifully renovated and the property does not show its age.
As I mentioned, you could not get a better location. It is located on the same block as Westlake Center. From here you can take the monorail to the Seattle Center. Nordstrom is only a block away and Pike Place is about three blocks away. 
I finally did go to the beautiful bar inside the hotel I use to look at years ago as I walked by and it was wonderful. They have some great drinks on the menu and you can order food here as well. We only had breakfast in the hotel's restaurant and it was excellent.

title: “Comfortable hotel in great location”
text: I stayed at the Hotel Madera recently during a short business trip to Washington DC. The hotel is perfectly located just 2 blocks from the DuPont Circle Metro Station, a great location for restaurants and shops and local transportation. The room was comfortable, quiet and nicely equipped. Most importantly, I had great service while there. The staff couldn't have been more helpful. When I wanted to find a local post office, one of the staff walked half way with me to point me in the right direction. I did not eat at the restaurant but local Washingtonians told me it was a very good place. I would recommend again for travelers who want a quiet and home-like environment with very friendly and caring staff and real comfort.

title: “Decent Hotel, Very Close to Graceland, But very rundown & somewhat scary area...”
text:
I gave this hotel a 2-Star rating simply because of the location (And i don't mean the location to Graceland, because that would be excellent - its practically next door) But I mean the surrounding areas to Graceland and the hotel.
This area is sooooo rundown and in the words of Elvis - "In the Ghetto" - I was honestly a little creeped out staying here. I actually would have rather stayed at a hotel a little further away from Graceland and made the small drive (There is actually an area about 4 BLOCKS away in Mississippi where they have tons of Hotels and restuarants and is very nice- i think the road was Goodman road? Anyway you just make a left there and you are in a nice area with lots of things). 
This Days Inn hotel is a 2 story hotel with outside corridors so that makes it feel even more unsafe - We actually went to the lobby to ask about where we could go get something to eat and ask about how "safe" the area was... the receptionist told us "that the area was decent and to make sure we lock up our stuff" along with the info about where we could go eat... however we couldnt find the road she spoke of and had to come back to the hotel to get further details (this was about 7:30pm) and she had actually LOCKED UP the lobby office!! So you had to wait until she hit a button @ 7:30 in the evening (it was still light out) to open the lobby door and let you in to speak with her... so i think that explains the area & surroundings a bit to you.
But that was my complaint with this hotel... yes the hotel was pretty decent, the rooms were clean, it had a comfortable bed and even had a fridge and microwave (They allowed dogs - this is good becuz we travel with our 2 small dogs) - The service was decent as well there. I suppose if your plan is to only be there one night and you are there specifically to see Graceland (As we were) then it could work for you - However be prepared to be in a very unimpressive / SCARY area. 
PS: The breakfast buffet is very limited & the 24 hour Elvis movie channels play the same movie over and over 24 hours a day and not one movie after the other (Which was a little disapointing) - The guitar shaped pool is pretty cool...

title: “'Would never stay here again'”
text: Myself and my father stayed here September 2011 for three nights and hated every minute the room l stayed in stunk something cronic,and the room my father stayed in we would have to say was haunted seriously he stayed in a end room,and the side of his room their was knocking and banging every night we were there.All l can say is l plan in the future to go back to San Diego as it is a really beautiful city but l plan on staying at the Holiday inn across from the Maritime Museum as that looks a really nice CLEAN hotel,please do not stay at this hotel!!

title: “Awesome.....”
text: Loved Loved Loved this hotel and our room was awesome.. We had 2 double bed suite and the linens, cleanliness of the room was over the top. We had a corner room looking at the Chrysler Building what more can you ask for. The service was outstanding.. Great location and decent price for a weekend in New York. Would book this hotel the next time I come to New York.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text: This is a fantastic hotel in a great location & for a very reasonable price. You can easily walk to Times Square, Central Park & many other attractions. David on reception kindly let us check in early & noted my request for a room on a high floor with a view. Room is a good size with plenty of room for clothes & bathroom is a good size. The bed was huge, but too soft for me (my only slightly negative comment). Overall a great stay & would recommend for anyone to stay here. TIP get a car from the hotel to the airport, cheaper than a taxi & a limo came for us :).

title: “Excellent Week in New York...”
text:
Having stayed at other hotels in New York.... The Pod cant be beaten, great location, helpful bell staff, the reception staff were a little off hand, but this is no different from any other hotel Ive stayed at in New York.
The room was small.... But large enough! Especially as we spent very little time there... Just sleeping... The communal bathrooms, were always clean and avaliable, In the mornings they got abit messy, but that was the busiest time. The lights above your room door are a nice touch and save you having to run out and check if they are free.

title: “Excellent location, lovely bar, great nights' sleep”
text: This is a lovely older hotel. Everything was great. The room was not ready at noon, but they were apologetic and stored our luggage. We had beers on the fantastic patio on Congress. we had wonderful local microbrews. The room was smallish, but not tiny as other reviewers said. It was all the room you really need. Others have mentioned the 25 dollar valet, which I've come to expect in urban hotels. The Valet was very quick and efficient. The rooms were very nicely decorated. All of the staff were helpful. I had a 160 dollar room with Priceline and it was well worth it. Especially as it was close to everything we wanted to do. I enjoy walking, and made it to the walking trail to Zilker Park in about ten minutes. Great Stay.

title: “Great location but noisy hotel with minimal service”
text:
The hotel is in a great location for seeing the sights in San Francisco.
I would avoid this hotel if you are a light sleeper or have young kids as the rooms are not very big and sound proofing is an issue.
The elevators are old and pretty small as well so it's not ideal if you are in a rush or trying to get up to your room when it is busy.
Having said all this, it is great value for the location and for San Francisco room rates.

title: “Loved it, first rate all around.”
text: I will continue to stay here from now on, as I am often in the area. Had the choice of several hotels in the area, and I have stayed at most of them. Luckily, this time we chose this one. Although our room was not ready, we got there early, they made us feel comfortable and welcome. Brought us water while we waited in a comfortable area. Brought our room keys when it was ready and apologized for any inconvenience. The staff was attentive and knowledgeable. The room was clean, bright, well maintained and perfect. It is across from the mall which is an added benefit. The area it quiet, as was our room. The bed was amazingly comfortable. It was hard to wake up, it felt so good. I have no idea why others rated this anything but excellent. As a seasoned traveler, my advise, stay here!

title: “Worried about mixed reviews so I checked this out in advance but...”
text:
DID NOT STAY! I had booked a reservation in June through a special deal at travel ticker. The price was excellent under $215 per night for a stay in October of this year which is the middle of high season in the city. The price since then has been averaging about $269 per night. I stayed with a friend for a few days in June because her roommate was traveling and went there in person to check it out. If I had not I probably would have stayed and been upset.
You would think it was fine from the street view and because it was a Radisson and on Lexington Avenue but I was disappointed almost immediately when I walked in. The condition of the lobby was old and worn looking. I was still trying to keep an open mind and proceeded to the front desk and told them I had a reservation in October but was concerned because of some bad reviews and asked to see a room . I waited for over a half an hour for someone to come out and show me and nobody came out until I asked what was taking so long despite the fact I told them I posted regular reviews on Trip Advisor. I think they were hoping I would leave. I watched the front desk and while there were lots of people checking in I was not impressed with the attention paid to patrons at the front desk by the staff.
When someone did come out she was very pleasant and we took the elevator to a room. The condition of the hallways and the carpeting on the way to the room was disgusting and filthy. The room much to my surprise was very small but lovely. It was a standard queen. It turned out I was told the room I booked was even smaller, a petite room. Now I have stayed in small rooms in NYC before but this was already pretty small. I was told all the rooms were in similar condition but the overall condition of the hotel was dilapidated and not for me. I canceled my reservation.The only good thing I can say about my experience and the hotel is that it is in a great location.

title: “Great hotel”
text: We enjoyed being in the heart of the city in this lovely small hotel. The restaurant was surprisingly outstanding! Great staff!

title: “Great Hotel...in the heart of NYC!”
text:
I went to fabulous New York City for the very first time in December 2003, and this was the hotel I stayed in. GREAT location-in the heart of Times Square! Also-49 Floors, a couple of inside restaurants, and it's very own theatre for Thoroughly Modern Millie! I thought that it was a VERY nice hotel and the only problems we had were the elevators. 
The lines were slow but we didn't wait any longer than 5 or 10 minutes (usually not even that long). It is a big hotel so you should expect to wait in some lines. If you have plans, just leave a couple of minutes early to keep yourself on schedule! You should have no problems if you leave early! Just check when you check in for the fire escapes if you are nervous about the elevators or if you find yourself in a case of an emergency! But if you stay here, I promise that you'll enjoy it! Oh, the peanuts that you can get in the bar on the 8th floor are GOOD! Try some! I am going back in early April 2004, and unfortunately I have to stay somewhere else! :( I Hope you stay here, you won't regret it! I had a wonderful time at the Marriott Marquis New York! :)

title: “Location, location, oh... and did I mention? Location”
text:
My headline says it all... the location for the Tuscan Inn really can't be beat. Just a 2 block walk to the waterfront, one block to the cable car, right in the heart of Fisherman's Wharf and a short stroll to North Beach... you can't say that the hotel doesn't have location going for it.
Just finished a 5 night stay there for a family wedding in the Bay area. The lobby is amazingly comfortable and outfitted with many an outlet -- perfect for charging your phone or iPad while waiting for friends and relatives who have yet to arrive. The wine happy hour is also a nice touch (even if it was two buck Chuck being served on the night I was there.) My room (a King-size) was small, but very clean and the bathroom was a good size. Family members complained of a small bathroom, but that just wasn't the case with my room. I saw three or four different rooms and every bathroom I saw was a good sized one. The staff was amazingly helpful. One night while I was stranded elsewhere in SF and unable to get a cab to come pick me up, I even contacted the hotel to see if they could just hail one from there (where they are plentiful) and send it to me. They weren't successful, but they called back quickly to say that they had tried. Fantastic service.
Having said all that, I wouldn't categorize this hotel as a luxury property, but it's clean, comfortable and has great service.
And did I mention the location?

title: “Ideal for our family of 4”
text:
Have recently returned from a 4 night stay with my husband and 2 children (aged 8 & 10) and I have no complaints about this hotel at all!
We had a one bedroom apartment on the 14th floor which had two beds, sofa bed and full kitchen. As others have said, it's not exactly stylish but the rooms are huge, the beds are comfy, it is cleaned every day and the staff are friendly. 
We were able to walk to many places of interest without complaints from the children and when we wanted to go further Grand Central was a short walk away.
We had a couple of good breakfasts at the Frontier Diner which was close-by otherwise there are plenty of delis and restaurants to choose from if you are staying local.
One thing to note - when we arrived the hotel put us in a one bedroom apartment on the 9th floor by mistake (theirs not ours). We only spent about 5 mins in it before they moved us but it has to be said that room wasn't in as good condition - the carpet was much older with a few dodgy looking stains and the beds weren't as comfortable. The kitchen appliances also looked older. It wasn't bad enough to make us complain but the 2nd room was definately better - maybe they are rennovating from top to bottom? Might be an idea to ask for a higher floor.

title: “Great for the Price”
text: I paid $140 for this room (with tax). For that amount of money, I'd say the room was great. I didn't feel that the room was especially clean. The bathroom was spotless, but the carpet didn't seem clean in the room. As a matter fact, I found a child's toy behind the TV from a previous guest. Neither of the telephones in the room worked. And I hated that the Magnolia didn't offer 24 hour room service. They have great garden tubs in the bathroom, though; and I liked that a lot. Everyone was super friendly and like I say, it was a great stay for the price.

title: “The best (and only) slammer we spend a night in and thoroughly enjoyed it..”
text: Looking for a special place to celebrate the birthday of my wife, I decided to take up the advise of our son who lives in Boston and picked the Liberty Hotel. It was the right choice alright!. The champagne upon arrival, the nice room on the 9th. floor, the architecture of the place, the very helpful and friendly staffers, all was special and fun.

title: “What are they putting in the water here?”
text:
One of the most unique properties I've ever stayed at, you have to think of a stay at the SGH as more like going to your cool (rich) uncle's place than going to a hotel. I say that because each of the staff treated me more like a member of the family than as a guest at a hotel. 
The front door/bell stand guys were not only welcoming and professional, they were always eager to help. When I arrived at the hotel at 8PM on a Sunday night and approached the desk, the gentlemen was very nice and when I said "checking in", he addressed me by name. [Now stop and think about that one for a second - he was not only expecting me, he had taken the time to know me first - so here I stand in the middle of Manhattan and this guy knows my name. INC-RED-U-LOUS!)
Yes, the room was a bit small, but it was clean and beautifully appointed in rich, subtle furnishings. The bed was comfortable - but forget all of that. Let's come back to that remarkable staff. During my brief stay I encountered no less than 10 hotel staff, all who treated me like they were really happy I was there. Example: I step out the front door one afternoon and they are doing a photo shoot of the hotel. The general manager takes me by hand, a block away, and hails a cab for me. When I return to the room later that day, some gifts and a lovely note were in my room. I was embarrassed by the level of service I received and I'm not a cornfield hick by any stretch.
I have found my new home in NYC and I am happy to be able to post such a positive review of this establishment. Yes, I saw the negative remarks about the staff before I went and was a bit nervous - BUT - there is a truth to life, you reap what you sow. I hope those reviews mean that the staff have this attitude: "if you're going to be nasty to us, we're simply going to reflect that back to you."
Only dislikes:
-> The curtains are not "blackout" so your room lights up at dawn;
-> I could hear the water in the bathroom next door.
Both of these things are also true when I visit my uncle's house.

title: “Great hotel but under construction while I was there”
text: I stayed here for just shy of 3 months for a class at Fort Sam Jan-Mar 2012. The hotel was going through renovations at the time, so the quality of sleep wasn't as good as it normally would have been seeing as there was allot of noise from about 0600-1900. All in all, the staff was awesome, the location was great, and the finished hotel was impeccable. I will absolutely stay here again.

title: “Great location”
text: Spent a here night before flying home to the UK. The location of the hotel is great and the staff at the front desk were very helpful and accommodating. Were very pleased to be able to check in slightly early - we had been prepared to just leave bags and return later, also very pleased with the bag storage for our late check out on the next day. Compared to several hotels we have stayed in where the bags are out of sight in a cupboard to which everyone can get access we liked the locking together of the bags in a much more open area. The hotel was very open about the limited view from the lower rooms before we booked and we opted for a room facing the street. Not the quietest room that I have stayed in but you are in the middle of the city. Were slighltly worried about the size of the rooom before arriving but were pleasantly suprised - there was plenty of room for the two of us and there was a sofa as well (I think it would turn into a bed but we didn't need that), if you were staying longer the lack of hanging space for clothes may be an issue. My only reservation is about breakfast - not the quantity or quality (both were fine) but all was served on paper plates/bowls and in paper cups. Due to the position of the hotel maybe they would be better just not bothering with breakfast at all.

title: “Hip, Cool, clogged drain, cool non functional sink”
text:
I stayed here on a business trip. It has been a while since I stayed in Manhattan, so I can't tell if the price was expensive or not. If it were not Manhattan there is no doubt the ~ $400 rate was too high. 
That said, the beds were awesome. It was a little noisy - it sounded as if the window was open. It may have been, but the massive curtain was so awkward to move I didn't bother to look. I was so tired I fell right asleep. 
The furnishings were hip to the point of annoying: the lights were cool but not obvious in their operation, the sink was ridiculous - spitting out after brushing was like some sort of disgusting carnival game: you have to lean far over and hope you don't get your eye taken out by the lever used to turn the faucet in and off. And then the coup d' grace: the sink barely drained. 
There was a tiny ironing board. It worked but it was inconvenient. 
Anyway, did I say this place was hip and cool. If I were on a romantic weekend this place would be great: exceptional service, excellent bar, cool furnishings. However, for business you have to be prepared that this is not a business hotel. 
Location right near Chelsea Market is very good.

title: “This hotel keeps me coming back”
text:
Stayed for a long weekend over Labor Day. YES - it was crowded but it was a holiday weekend. With that in mind, the crowds were tolerable.
When I pulled up to the valet, I was asked what they could for me. When I said I wanted to drop off my bag and then park the car, I was a bit disappointed to be told to pull my car over and take the bag inside myself. Sure they were busy, but it was 104 outside and I hadn't intended to handle the bag myself.
This was a repeat trip and I decided to try the Cloub Club. Not sure that it is worth the extra money though. The Cloub Club employees were exremely hospitable and went out of their way to ensure you had a fresh drink or were partaking of the breakfast, appetizers, etc. But really can a person consume $150 worth of food and drinks per day!! You do get a small gift upon arrival and a packet of stationary at departure. 
I spent my days at the Revive Spa which never felt crowded. I am a spa junkie and must say that Winnie gave me the VERY BEST hot stone massage. When my 80 minutes were up, I wanted to beg her to start all over! Cheryl also does a excellent facial. I noted their names and will request both of them on my next visit. If you like either of those services, you will not be disappointed.
Dinner at Roy's was superb - very attentive service too. I like breakfast at Blue Sage - other meals there are OK - not great but not overpriced considering that you are in a hotel. 
Overall this hotel keeps me coming back - very comfortable rooms, 99% ot their employees are outstanding. Why stay anywhere else?

title: “Incredibly accomodating & easy to work with - definitly our first choice for group travel!”
text: The staff and hotel representatives that we intereacted with during the course of our stay (collegiate team travel) were a pleasure to work with and went above and beyond to help make our stay as easy as possible, which can often be a challenge for a group of 28. We had both breakfast and dinner with the hotel and the staff was always ready for our arrival and helped make each meal a relaxed and worry free experience. Although we had a 2 hour weather delay in one of our games that brought us back to the hotel much, much later than we anticipated the hotel staff, chef(s), hospitality department were still ready and waiting for us with the dinner they had prepared and planned for us. We will always look to the Hilton Charlotte University Place for any of our personal or team travel to the Charlotte area and we'll be sure to recommend it to all of our associates, colleagues, parents, players, and fans for their future travel to the Charlotte area. Thanks for making it an easy weekend for us!!

title: “Eh, average”
text: This hotel was perfectly average. The room and inside were clean. I really liked the free shuttle service. We took advantage of it several times to go to the 16th street mall downtown and not have to worry about parking. It's pretty old and some updates are definately needed but overall it was ok. My major complaint was the ice machine was not working on my floor. That was a pain.

title: “GREAT Location...Average service....newly remodeled rooms.”
text:
This hotel is recently remodeled. Great color schemes and room perks. It does have a smaller lobby and bar for a NYC hotel.
This hotel is on 51st and Lexington in the heart of midtown Manhattan. 5 blocks from times square and 6 blocks from the Chrysler building. There's a main subway station right outside the front door.
The staff is abrupt but efficient. Maid service is quick and efficient as well, very friendly.
The price is average for midtown Manhattan. Worth the $$

title: “Wonderful new hotel”
text:
I read mostly good reviews about this place and I agree. I know, the rooms are small. So what? I guess they should advertise this on their website or something. 
Because of you take the room size out of the equation, everything else is above expectations. 
I mean even the room size is not a big deal, granted we don't have any kids and did not have a lot of luggage. But I mean if you go there and you know you most likely are going to have a smaller room then it's not such a big deal.
From the moment you walk into the hotel you feel the difference, the smell, feel and look of everything is really well thought out. 
Check in was nice and quick. 
Our room was wonderful, it's nicely decorated, I loved the new bed and linen, I loved the desk and TV. There was something special about that room. The bathroom was again on the small side of things but still very nice. I liked it.
They don't have coffee in the room but they have complimentary coffee in the lobby all morning long. 
If you're reading this review you know the hotel is in a good location. There is a parking right across the street on Clark street that is 23 dollars for 24 hours. Not bad for Chicago. 
I got this hotel on priceline but I will not hesitate to book it again without priceline in the future. I am looking forward to trying their spa with my wife.
Go to the hotel Felix, you won't regret it.

title: “The staff was friendly, the room clean and cozy, the hotel very close to Back Bay and in a great neighborhood, and, well, free c”
text: The room wasn't huge, but I only needed a place to stay so it fit my purposes very well. It was also a lovely room and the inn is located in a charming little neighborhood. It's no more than a ten minute walk to Copley Square, nor more than five to Back Bay station, and it's very close to lots of restaurants and shopping without being right on the main drag. The staff was very friendly and there was the added benefit of free coffee at any time. The price was a bit high, but comparable or lower to any other place in the area, and I think this is one of the nicer places to spend your money if youre not looking for more than a home base while you explore Boston. I highly recommend it

title: “SUPERCALIFRAGILISTICEXPIALADOCIOUS”
text:
I have been making arrangements for the reunions of one of my army units for the past 25 years. We have stayed at hotels across the nation every year. Our 25th Annual Reunion was convened at this hotel on 24 May 2009. I always consult with all of our members about the hotel at which we stay. I have never been so enthusiastically responded to by all of our group. There was not one single complaint!
What we found was a delightful staff of people from the Sales Manager''s office with whom we made first contact through the front desk personnel. ALL were cheerful, courteous and most of all - HELPFUL in every instance. As to the amenities, they were fabulous. EVERYBODY remarked on what a good night's sleep they enjoyed, on the pleasure enjoyed in a shower that spewed forth water in any temperature desired. The placing of "USA Today" at your door each morning. But the staff was superb. I looked forward to going down to the Front Desk each morning to have some sort of (any sort of) conversation with the Desk Clerks, who were always, every morning the most delightful, enthusiastic and helpful people I've ever encountered. I am presently searching for a Crowne Plaza Hotel in Colorado Springs, CO where will have our next reunion.
To paraphrase a popular election campaign slogan: "IT'S THE PEOPLE . . . . "!"

title: “Updated Hyatt Regency in a great location”
text:
My wife and I just stayed at this hotel and I was very impressed by the renovation the hotel has undergone since I last stayed there (around 10 years ago). The hotel is very modern and chic, without being self-consciously so (i.e., there is no techno music in the background and the staff is not required to wear fitted black t-shirts). Our room was spacious and clean, with nice views of Washington. 
It should be noted that the neighborhood where the hotel is located is still somewhat in a transition process. Across the street is a dingy convenience store that looks the same now as it did 10 years ago. It is a reminder that the neighborhood used to be not-so-safe. Now, as the Union Station area has become trendier and gone more upscale (it has been dubbed "NoMA" for "North of Massachusetts Ave."), there is very little danger of being mugged. Still, the convenience store and a few others are remnants of the neighborhood's former grubbiness.

title: “Clean and accessible”
text:
Recently stayed here for a 4-day business trip. A Hilton hotel, this Homewood Suites was conveniently located right off the freeway and is nearby to a number of restaurants and shops. Check-in was quick. However, I was dismayed that a hold was placed on my credit card for an amount slightly higher than the total room charges. I understand that that is the usual hotel industry protocol, but it would be beneficial if the hotel would let travelers know upon check-in what their deposit requirements are rather than it being a surprise. Just a thought.
The suite was very clean, with two windows, a ceiling fan, 32" HDTV, and had all the conveniences for a 3-night stay: kitchenette with stove, frig, microwave and utensils. Slightly larger than the average hotel room. The bathroom was extremely clean and up-to-date. The king bed was comfortable with plenty of pillows.
The only problem I experienced was with the cooling system under the window. The control pad was non-responsive; I wasn't able to turn it off. I called for assistance and the front-desk help responded. He was not able to "fix" it, so I was asked if I needed it on and I said no, so he removed the cover housing to turn it off via the electrical circuit panel switch. Thank goodness for the ceiling fan or it would have been uncomfortable given that the temp outside climbed to near 90 degrees a couple of days.
The free breakfast was very good with plenty of hot and cold items to satisfy most people: eggs, sausage, biscuits, gravy, waffles, various muffins, pastries, breads, cereals, fruit, etc. Since my meetings didn't start until 10 a.m. each morning, it was nice to have time to sit down in the breakfast area (which was very comfortable and accommodating) to enjoy the meal, watching a couple of flat screen TVs and reading the paper. 
Other than the cooling issue, it was not enough to down-grade my review. Overall, I was pleased with the stay. The staff made me feel welcome at all times. I am certain I will be traveling there again for future meetings and will probably stay there. I would recommend it to others.

title: “Accurate Reviews”
text:
We stayed at The Excelsior from Sept. 24 - 30th and much of what we read on Trip Advisor was accurate. The hotel had a great location and was very clean. The front desk staff was not friendly or helpful at all, we never saw the concierge and the man working the incredibly small convenience store was always on the phone with personal calls and never made eye contact the entire time we struggled through the small space.
The breakfast was very expensive, so we went around the corner to various coffee shops and deli stores. 
Stay here for the clean rooms, proximaty to Central Park, the subway, the American Museum of Natural History and The Dakota.

title: “Dated hotel that was given 3.5 stars and should be 2.5.”
text: We found the location fine and staf fine. The room had a hole in the carpet and the mirror was not clean. My bath towel was musty. Our bed was certainly not comfortable but bouncy. The pool was pretty and nice. The decor was stuck in the early 90's.

title: “Confusing”
text: They needed to say it takes two elevators to get to the lobby. Waist of time. The restaurant was horrible. Rubber scallops and burnt cod...no apologies just that's the way it is. Wished we had known handicapped accessible meant around the corner through the woods to get anywhere. Not at all handicap friendly. Town most of all...nightmare to get anywhere handicap. Pet friendly so barking is accessible...if you don't like it they move you not the dog.

title: “All about the Belvedere”
text: As a travel agent I always get the low down on the best places to stay and usually I recommend this place to my clients. I love the location being only a short walk from Broadway/Times Sq/Central Park. For NYC it really is all about the location. Rooms are clean and comfy, as are the lovely beds and fluffy pillows! I have stayed here many times and find this hotel always used to pride itself on service. I feel the standards are slipping but I really hope they get it back on track. I really would recommend for value and location, as you shouldnt be spending all your time in the hotel room!!

title: “Very good Hyatt”
text:
A bit older Hyatt than the one a couple blocks away but still nice rooms with good service.
Nice location on the Riverwalk.
Not a bad walk to the convention center if that's why you're there but the other Hyatt is attached to the convention center and also on the Riverwalk.

title: “A wonderful stay!”
text:
This was my first trip to NYC. I found it overwhelming trying to choose from the multitude of places to stay in New York and finally settled on the Library Hotel. It was the perfect choice! 
There are cheaper options in NYC but trust me, the little extra is really worth it. 
The hotel is perfectly located - close to a lot of great sites and very easy access to the metro. The staff (Daniella and Billy, especially) were tremendous. So genuine and friendly. The lounge on the second floor was a wonderful respite amid busy days of shopping and sightseeing. The breakfast, all day coffee and snacks as well as wine and cheese reception were much appreciated. 
Can't wait to go back!

title: “Cool and comfortable”
text:
Spent only one night but found it to be cool & comfortable, with some great food & shopping options nearby. They gave me a free upgrade to a huge (by Manhattan standards) Superior King room. The decor was great -- modern but warm with some retro touches -- and my room had a beautiful view from the floor-to-ceiling window. The bed was comfortable and the linens were great. The only thing I missed: a big bathtub.
I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “Watch for parking prices!”
text:
I had a car with me, and knew that parking would be $22+tax a night. When I checked out, I was surprised to find out that after taxes it came to $26.84. That's a 22% tax! 
I went to the front desk to find out what the break down of the $4.84 was. But all they could say was the the it was just a 22% "service tax." Really not happy that the tax rate and break down on parking was not transparent.
I got the hotel through Hotwire when I had the area, Pike Place Market selected. Its a 20min walk so its no where in that area. They do have a shuttle bus that goes there.
The shuttle bus leaves every 30 mins and it was actually pretty handy if you're doing the normal tourist thing. 
Rooms where nice, the the roof top hot tub was cool. The pool was small and is less than 4 feet deep and was always full of children splashing around.
Even though its on the outskirts of downtown, the shuttle buses make up for its distance. 
I would actually stay there again, but only because they have a convenient shuttle bus.

title: “Staff here is very frendly professional and helpful”
text:
All of your staff here is very frendly professional and helpful.
Amy however is a jewel and i travel extensivly domestic and international.
She is your best asset

title: “Great Customer Service!”
text: I chose to stay here based on the great reviews and price. The staff is really friendly and quick to attend your needs. The concierge (Peter) was extremely helpful with guiding my wife and I through the city. The rooms were stunning and full of space.

title: “Beach Bash”
text: The location is the main selling point- right on dog beach- which is the main reason for our stay, we brought the dog. The rooms are basic, pretty clean but I wouldn't call them spotless but when traveling with a dog clean is good enough. The staff are friendly and accommodating- forgot a can opener and the staff cheerfully opened our cans in the office. Walking distance to the main street and restaurants, shops, etc. Prices are a good value.

title: “top of the bill (in more than one sense)”
text: This is one of the top hotels in the world. Stunning views over all Manthattan (depending on the room), with an exceptional bar with views over central park and columbus circle (on the first floor of the hotel which is thirty-something floor in the building). The rooms are very light, not large but big enough with -as said- stunning views if you are willing to put up the money for a top floor and a good view. The bathrooms are beautiful, ours had a window. The service is -as you would expect- impeccable, the bar worth a visit (make sure you reserve a table at the window and reserve you must). The gym is large, extremely clean and well-equipped, they also have a large pool. The location could't be better, being on Columbus Cicle within walking distance from Lincoln Center, Carnegie Hall and the Broadway Theatres. It will cost you, but you get what you pay for. And then some!

title: “Second stay at Newton”
text:
This was my second stay at the Hotel Newton. My daughter has been accepted to Columbia University so I will stay there again. The location is great, it is clean and the rates are reasonable. The room each time for me was small, but I always mistakenly reserve a single bed. 
I see that the manager reads these reviews so I wanted to give some constructive comments. The first is that there was no blanket on the bed. Only the thin bed spread. Not sure if this is the case in all rooms, but I did not enjoy that. Also when I was being checked in by Landry, it really felt like I was doing him a favor. He was more interested in talking to his coworker about how he would like to go to Texas and stay with his parents and sleep for a month. He is not an asset to your hotel. I read most of these reviews and it appears the majority of your front desk staff is very pleasant. He was not. I did encounter another front desk clerk in the evening who was quite nice. The last comment is that I was on the third floor and there were roofs and ac units that could accomodate a possible intruder. I could not for the life of me get the windows to lock. I was a single woman staying alone. So that concerned me some. But not enough to call for assistance. The situation could possibly have been remidied by staff. 
As stated, I will stay here again. I have an overall positive opinion of this property. Also see previous review.

title: “Pretty but Overated”
text:
So, as we drove up to the hotel for our first stay at the Edgewater we were very impressed with the views of the water. The valet staff for the most part were very helpful, though the cost of valet was a little much. Checking in was really easy and the staff were very pleasant. The lobby overlooks the water and is a beautiful place to relax and watch the boats go by. 
The hotel is centrally located and is very close to great restaurants and bars in the area.
Our room was located on the city side and we found that the trains running out side the hotel became a noisy with the sliding door open at night. I'm a hot sleeper and usually need some cold air circulation. So I closed the door and turned on the A/C unfortunately the A/C unit was so loud we had to turn it off. This was a real annoyance for the both of us for the rest of the trip. We would have asked for another room but our stay was only 2 nights and the hassle wasn't worth it. We expected of all things the A/C to run well in such an acclaimed expensive hotel. 
We stopped by the hotel restaurant twice on our trip. The first night we stopped by around 11pm for a nightcap and were pleasantly surprised to hear a great band playing covers which we really enjoyed. The service was great and the restaurant was very stylish and comfortable.
Our second restaurant visit was not as good as our first. We went by around 4pm the following day for a snack after a long day of sightseeing. We ordered a starter off of the bar menu and when it arrived it had an item in it that neither myself or my partner consume in our diets. I'm pretty diligent about reading menu ingredients because of my diet limitations. Any how when I told our server about the extra item she gave us a disgusted look, whisked away our plate and threw it in the garbage.
Our first instinct was that we had made a mistake and read the menu incorrectly, so I borrowed our neighbors menu to confirm my suspicion and indeed we were correct. No word of the item in the ingredient list. 
I tried to get her attention again soon after to tell her that the ingredient was not listed on the menu and when I did she told me I was wrong without looking at the menu.
Our newly made appy arrived and looked great though our server did not bring us new cutlery, which we also thought was odd as the previous ones were already soiled. My girlfriend had to go to the bar to get it. Basically I was thoroughly disappointed with that restaurant visit. The last thing you want on a romantic weekend is a disgruntled server to ruin the mood.
Another gripe is that there wasn't even free wireless in the lobby which is really not good in this day and age,though they did have a business center where you could use the internet.
All in all the hotel is very pretty though needs some revamping. Great area, great views, very nice helpful front counter and bell staff.

title: “Home Away From Home”
text: I have been staying at Hawthorn Suites, Dallas Love Field since February 2012, and the overall experience has been great. From the moment I checked in with Steven I felt welcome. His welcoming smile and warm personality made me feel at home instantly. He also remembered my name from that first day. That is remarkable for someone in the hospitality industry. I was impressed. All the other members of staff as well have made my experience a worthwhile one. Thanks to Steven, Elias, John, Julio, the lady who prepares breakfast and the other night staff. I recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Dallas.

title: “Brilliant place”
text:
A lovely hotel/hostal, was greeted at the door and was helped with my luggage, the reception were very nice too! Are room was on the 4th floor, we had a nice view out on to the street! We shared a bathroom which I was worried about after Reading the reviews on here! Well it was the first thing I checked, and it was really nice! Very clean and was kept that way through my four day stay! We experienced a snow storm whilst there and I didn't wake up cold not once, it was very warm! The only thing was the heater leaked slightly! The room was quite big with a walk in wardrobe! The whole hotel was kept very clean in my opinion, I think some of the previous reviews on here are of people who are expecting a 4* hotel! When booking it does state a hotel/hostal! 
The hostal is very close to everything! 96th street sub is round the corner! I would definatly stay here again!!

title: “My best stay ever!”
text: We enjoyed our stay at Sheraton Crescent Hotel, my wife and I were in Phoenix for a tournament, and the tournament ended about 1:30pm, because of gold membership from AmExp we were able to have a late checkout, unlike previous would have our luggage cook in the hot summer temperature. The staff was courteous and friendly; the club lounge was a traffic place for hangout and watch tv program of my own choice; with internets and breakfast secured floor package. It was the best value I have ever had.

title: “Clean!!!”
text: We loved our stay here. We would come again. Clean, safe, quiet. Breakfast very sufficient. Staff is very courteous. Our room was very large and spacious, could be a bit brighter, though. Everyone on staff was very friendly and helpful even the Maintenance supervisor who helped me find the laundry room. Just great customer service. We met the General Manager and he was wonderful, too. We are telling all our friends of our great visit to San Antonio at the Best Western Sunset Riverwalk!

title: “Disappointing”
text:
The pros: One of the least expensive hotels I've ever stayed in in LA. The room and bed were comfortable and the staff was very, very nice.
The cons: The staff had better be nice, considering all the problems we had with our brief stay. The bathroom door was broken and would not close. The remote control for the TV was broken and it took a full day to get it replaced.
