This was the single DARKEST hotel room I've ever stayed in in my life, and the bathroom, miserably, was the darkest part of all. Alas, the room was NOT dark enough to avoid seeing that there was actual graffiti painted on the wall of the room. How hard is it to paint over graffiti? Also annoying: I came home late and exhausted from my meeting to discover that, inexplicably, the keycard to my room had been disabled. It was just a matter of going downstairs to have it reactivated, but it was still very annoying. They also over-charged my card on the first night of my stay and took several days to adjust the charge. 
As others have noted, they advertise having FAR more TV channels than they actually have, and while there is a fitness room, the only treadmill was broken during our stay. 
The noise wasn't a problem and we stayed over weekend nights. All in all, I was bitterly disappointed to find out that I had friends who got a room at the Biltmore - right around the corner - for less than half the price of O Hotel. I cannot recommend this hotel.

title: “Convenient for Laker game”
text: 10 minute walk to Staples Center. Our room looked out onto the wall of another building. Very small bathroom. The handheld shower was not practical. Park in the garage immediately next to the Hotel, as its only $10 per day. Rooms were very clean but spartan.

title: “Perfect Hotel !!!!!!!!!!”
text: Just perfect, a few blocks from Time Square, really comfortable. The employees were friendly and helpfull. The hotel is really clean and well decorated. Situated in the hart of the city and close to central park. Wanna book a nice hotel, go to Wellington...

title: “beware the rooster”
text:
I just thought it would be courteous to other travellers to point out that this location is located next to either a farm or a house which keeps chickens and roosters. I discovered this fact when awoken by the sound of a rooster repeatedly from 4:30 am to the time I finally decided to finally check out at 7:30 am. If you're a heavy sleeper, have a good set of earplugs or just don't mind that kind of noise, then it's not a terrible experience.
As other reviewers have noted, the area is kind of seedy and it's definitely in one of the ugliest parts of los angeles, but the rooms themselves are clean and the check-in staff are fine. But I can't see myself ever staying here again.

title: “Lovely room, convenient location, great staff”
text: Stay for the decor - 21st century art deco revival. It's a fun change from the usual business hotels. A quick cab ride or a reasonable walk from downtown. Outstanding staff assistance with directions, restaurant referrals, etc. Will definately stay again.

title: “Historic but better for a visit not a stay”
text: The hotel is an interesting example of Frank Lloyd Wright architecture. But its more like a museum so go for a walk round. In in terms of staying there overnight it is just not that attractive. Low ceilings and small windows that don't show the views - typical FLW trademarks. The rooms are large but but a average and the pools aren't great too. There are much nicer hotels in Phoenix for the price. Small and terribly expensive restaurant - had to drive to the nearby mall for dinner!

title: “Nice property & alternative to the big hotels along the waterfront”
text:
I am not a fan of the W Hotels and try to avoid them. When Hyatt introduced this part of their hotel lineup to compete with the W I was worried it would suffer the same problems but in fact they do not. 
The rooms were nice but a bit compact but the bathroom is large. I love the combo of the handheld and rain shower. Decent soap products as well. Internet was fast and the bed was very comfortable. What I also liked is that the hotel provides FREE juices and bottled water in the room - unlike the W which charges a fortune for both. Nicely done Andaz. 
The gym is fine and the equipment in good shop. The roof top is wonderful with nice views and a great bar location. I had breakfast on the roof and the eggs benedict was excellent and home made. 
My only negative is that I was given a room on the street side which picked up all the noise from below.

title: “Just as it sounds”
text: Heartbreak Hotel was full of Elvis memorabilia. It had a nice gift shop. The room was ok. It seemed like it was maybe an older hotel that had been remodeled. The hallways were narrow. Bed was comfortable. It was very close to Graceland and we liked that. Most of the staff seemed helpful and friendly. We had pre-registered so check in was fast. Continental breakfast was provided. It was a little over-priced but overall it was a great experience for us on our first trip to Memphis. Probably would not stay there if we had not been visiting Graceland the next day.

title: “Good base for trip”
text:
The Airport Marriott is connected to the airport via a covered walkway wahich makes it very easy after a transatlantic flight. The hotel is an older Marriott and is beginning to show signs of age. Despite this the rooms offer all the standard Marriott features; clean, spacious, well appointed and with a fantastic bed. This Marriott also had a fantastic chef and I had some of the best food that I have had in a hotel bar/restaurant. Staff in the hotel were helpful and friendly. Although some distance from Center City the rates at this hotel are considerably better than in Center City itself and with the adjacent fast rail link geeting into Philly is hardly a problem at all. 
Good hotel well worth staying at for 1st/last night of trip but also a good base for a leisure stay at rates cheaper than central Philly.

title: “great hotel”
text: The hotel rooms were clean and well kept. The staff was friendly and helpful. For this price, we were one block away from the beach and in a central location. The pool was clean, and not crowded. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Highly Recommend the Hampton”
text: Just completed an overnight stay at the Hampton Inn Majestic Chicago. My family was in town for a couple days of shopping and to hear the Chicago Symphony. This appears to be an older building but the property has been VERY nicely renovated. Nicely decorated, large rooms, gracious staff and a good breakfast are all hallmarks of this hotel. We especially liked the location - close to the theater district, museums, shopping and restaurants. This Hampton will be my first stop when looking for future accommodations in the Windy City.

title: “Loved! Can't wait to return.”
text:
My fiance and I spent two nights at the W this past Memorial Day weekend, and were amazed from the moment we walked in. The photos on the W's website and on trip advisor do not do this swanky hotel justice. Every room is breathtaking and like nothing you've seen before. This is not your typical hotel by any means.
What we loved-
Location! Many restaurants close by, walkable bars!
Our room was awesome! We had a corner room on the 14th floor! Great views!
Iphone charger on one side of the bed and mulit charger on the other side! 
Decor was amazing
Acura Experience- quick service for a Saturday on a holiday weekend! No questions asked and complimentary Fiji water!
Friendly, helpful staff
Trace was delicious with a great atmosphere
Valet was ready to go! No waiting around after check out!
Loved the "good morning" "good afternoon" and "good evening" floor mats!
Best of all- Surprise champagne and dessert for my Fiance's birthday!!
The other stuff..
Comfy bed but queen bed in our room, not king?
We loved the open shower- but could be awkward for people sharing rooms
Beautiful people who know they are beautiful everywhere, especially at the pool and in the living room at night. Kind of annoying! 
Wished there was a quick service coffee/breakfast counter inside the hotel.
Overall- we loved it!!

title: “Great location for out of town sight seeing, and a fabulous staff to boot!”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for a family spring break week long trip to see Washington DC.
First the good - this hotel has a a simply fabulous staff. The concierge Kimu was amazing and a wealth of knowledge - we recommend talking to her before you arrive to plan your trip as we did.
The buffet breakfast was great value and a perfect way to start long days of sight seeing, walking and exploring from this excellent location - for a real Washington breakfast try Lincolns Waffles just around the corner.
But don't miss the in house restaurant Cure - an amazing dining experience featuring local and organic cuisine this is a quite exceptional dining experience under the masterful eye of executive chef Kevin Villalovos - not only a great chef, but also one who takes the time to meet and greet his diners in the restaurant and really listen to their opinions and suggestions....
The only not so great aspect of this hotel is that the rooms are a little 'tired', but I would imagine this hotel is on Hyatts list to get updated soon - it doesn't feel like the new Hyatt style...they are far from poor, just not up to the level one expects from a Grand Hyatt.
All that said, we would highly recommend this property for its great location, fabulous dining and amazing staff!!

title: “Would not stay here again”
text: We booked our room on priceline for a weekend stay in NYC. Although the hotel appears nice and the lobby is beautiful, the rest of the hotel is not very nice. The rooms are ridiculously small. Additionally, my husband and I had a room with a bed not much larger than a twin. When we requested a room with a larger bed, we were told we would have to pay extra. Our travel companions, who also booked through priceline had a room with a king bed without paying any extra. The front desk staff seemed as though they would rather be anywhere but there. The drinks in the lobby bar were overpriced and the wait staff unattentive. I would not stay at this hotel again.

title: “Loved the Beacon Hill Hotel & Bistro”
text: The Beacon Hill Hotel and Bistro is a superb small hotel in a great location. Reminds me of London. The staff was fantastic -- helpful with directions and reservations. Great selection of teas. Our room was splendid. Perfect point of departure for visiting Boston for the first time. We'll be going back for a second visit in the Spring.

title: “Stay away.”
text: Our car was broken into. Rooms dated and musty. Unimpressed in every way possible.

title: “Nice place”
text: Very efficiently run, clean and comfy. Nice amenities. I enjoyed my stay here, and felt very safe in the area it was located.

title: “Perfect Hotel Perfect Location”
text:
We stayed here in Feb 08 in room 515. The hotel is in a perfect location and is central to all the sights of New York. Our room was cleaned to perfection everyday and we found the staff to be very helpful. 
The breakfast room was a bit crowded some mornings but this wasnt too much trouble for us as you can take food out and eat it in your room. The breakfast had everything you could ever want and we even loaded up on bagals for pack lunches some days! The internet didnt work in our room but we did have a million channels on the t.v (perfect for watching sports!) 
The only thing I would say is that the taxi the hotel arrange to take you back to the airport is over twice the price of any you can hail from the street. My advice would be to check out and grab a taxi on the road, its far far cheaper! 
Overall this hotel is in a central location, secure and clean. A perfect stay in NYC!

title: “The Mayflower is an Elegant Hotel - We'll be back again!”
text:
(We added a review in January 2008, but don't see it listed so we're adding another!)
My husband and I spent a week at this lovely historical hotel during Christmas 2007 and we were overjoyed with the experience! We are Hilton Honors Members and reserved a room on the Executive Level and were treated like royalty. We were given the choice to have a full breakfast in the lovely hotel restaurant and the food was out of this world! 
Our room was spacious and each morning we woke to coffee and tea placed outside our door on a tray! What a delightful way to start the new day!
The hotel is close to the White House, where we were honored to have a candlelight tour of the White House Christmas decorations arranged through my senator. We also arranged a special walk down tour of the Washington Monument. You can do this by calling ahead to the Park Service,
We have visited Washington, DC many times with this being our first stay at the Mayflower. We will absolutely come back to this hotel, as our stay was a pleasure!

title: “The Manager made this birthday experience grandiose”
text: We recently had a birthday party at this hotel which a few of our other friends have as well and has been a big hit every time. The hotel gladly accommodates extra room for the "gathering", though not a babysitting club as parents are responsible for their own, obviously. The kids and parents loved the hot tubs and indoor pool. The rooms are huge and spacious with all the amenities of home. Plenty of everything we needed from a load of extra towels to a free morning breakfast.. One of the best free breakfasts I have ever encountered. Loaded with waffles, eggs, sausage, bagels and the list goes on!! Granted staff is always a little hit or miss no matter where you stay, but the manager here was attentive and spot-on.. I could not have asked for a better experience for what turned out to be the best birthday party ever!! A special Thank You to Mrs. Catherine.. We'll be coming back!!

title: “Room 127 beautiful view of the river!”
text: Well, i have stayed at alot of hotel chains all over the world, from Motel 6 to the Intercontinental chains and i didn't know what to expect at the Riverside. The front desk was helpful before and after check-in. The room was very small , i mean pretty small! The dimensions were about 7 x 10' with a full side bed No (headboard) a very old desk from the 50's. a lamp, 13 inch tv color (no cable) a microwave and a small frig. Small quarters for my wife and i but we like each other so it wasn't a problem:-). the bath was shower only. The room needed some paint but when the lights are out who cares. The room and the bath were very clean! The water was hot and had great pressure, clean linens, blankets, pillows. My pet peeve is when the stopper in the bathroom sink doesn't work but it worked! We felt safe in the room and in the neighborhood. Two blocks up the Subway, Zabars and H & H bagels among other shops. If you are going to ride the subway buy a one day pass $7.00, In a 24 period you can ride as much as you like and it is good for the bus also, there is also a weekend pass too. After after 3 days of shopping , visiting family and friends, sightseeing i can honestly say Riverside Towers was a great little find for 85.00 and we will stay there again! Small yes but you can break the bank and spend the extra 10 dollars for the suite! Hey,you can always stay at the Waldolf! Enjoy, T & T Turner

title: “I like this place ... nice solid Westin property”
text: It's not the newest Westin, but there is something that I like about this place. The dual circular towers are unique. I've always had an amazing view -- either of the water or the city. Be sure to ask for the highest floor they can get you on. The Westin heavenly bed is something to look forward to at the end of the day when you're away from home. The room service menu is a step above average and the staff is friendly. The location is walkable to good shopping and restaurants. It's not trying to compete with some of Seattle's more fancy boutique hotels, but I'll take it over some of the other mainline hotel brands any day. Oh, and one of these days I'm finally going to buy one of the fancy glass sculptures they have in the gallary on the lobby level. They're pretty amazing.

title: “Well located home away from home”
text: My wife and I had an extended (8-day) stay at The Surrey. Our room was of a high standard (overlooking Madison), and the combination of room, housekeeping standard and overall ambience did make it feel like a home away from home. The hotel is well located near Madison, Park, 5th Ave and Lexington, and close to the tube at 68th. Particularly appreciated was the pre-stay assistance I received from the Concierge - I had booked some ball game tickets on line from Australia well before we arrived, and arranged for them to be delivered to and held at the hotel. This was all attended to with a minimum of fuss, with the reception staff being aware of them when we checked in (very late at night), and the package then being delivered (without request) to our room the next day. Only a small thing, but one which was impressive in its service and attention to detail. Very happy to recommend The Surrey.

title: “Very Good”
text:
Just got back from California and stayed here for last 2 nights of our 10 day trip.... This place is very good. Spotlessly clean, close to all the sites and the staff couldn't do enough. Bell boys grab the luggage, check in easy. Computer facilities available free of charge to check in for the flight home too. Well recommended....
Cioppino's Italian is just across the road... Don't waste your money. Its CRAP.... Best to wander round the corner and eat at THE PUB.... great food and good value.

title: “Meh.”
text:
Surprised this is rated so high (which was the main reason we chose to stay at Hotel George). It was mediocre at best but not horrible by any means. The hotel itself had minor issues but my biggest concern was the general area.
Pros: very nice staff.
Cons: filthy carpet & dirty shower. View of office building behind us. Soup kitchen 2 blocks in the direction of where you'd want to walk to go to the sites. Lots of vagrants in that direction, though we felt pretty safe around the hotel at all hours. Lack of decent restaurants anywhere nearby (Irish place around corner had horrible food; smaller Irish place right next to it wasn't bad). Nothing really going on in that area after 8-9 PM. Most everything was closed. Couldn't even get snacks, food, or drinks except at a 24-hour booth in Union Station. 
It wasn't a bad hotel....just wasn't great. I've traveled quite a bit & Hotel George was somewhere in the middle of the pack...maybe a bit lower.
Don't let the proximity to Union Station fool you. It's not a major hub of the Metro so you're not gaining much of an advantage by staying here if you think it's easy access to the sites or to the Metro. You'd be better served to stay in a better area & use the train to get to Capitol Hill. That way you can leave it at night & go back to a better part of town with better restaurants & more things to do.

title: “Lots of strengths with a couple of weaknesses”
text:
Stayed this past week. Amazing outside area with two pools, fire pits, outside bar and hot tubes. This is the one of the strengths of the propery. The coincerge lounge in the south tower is nice (amazing views) but can get very crowded during breakfest. As others have indicated, the hotel gym is excellent.... The food in the restraunts was very good and not overpriced. The hotel room in the south tower was not anything special and the housekeeping was dissapointing and inconsistent. The front entrance is tough to get in and out of if you are trying to drop someone off and not leaving your car for valet parking. 
Bottom line: Very close to the convention center, gas lamp, petco field and right along the bay. Above average Marriott property. 
Tip - 
If you need a car renting at the Hertz at the airport is a lot cheaper than renting at the hotel.

title: “Poor customer service”
text: My first visit there was the first week of April 2012, came back the third week and service was so terrible it discounted the first stay completely and then some.

title: “DON'T HESITATE”
text: This was a wonderful hotel stay! My husband and I celebrated our wedding anniversary during a quick trip to Seattle and picked this hotel from the internet. Valet parking was on special for $5 which sounded like a deal. Little did I know that it has the nicest staff, comfortable accomadations, and the cleanest room I've ever stayed in. We had a congratulations card hand signed by several staff and a small box of chocolate covered cherries in our room. We were also given 2 free drink coupons by the front desk for Oliver's, the wonderful restaurant/bar at the hotel. We decided to walk around town and found the location wonderful for Pike's market and West Lake Center. My daughter was flying into town late from Boston and took the Metro from the airport and connected right next to the hotel. She really liked her room also. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel and would stay there again next time in Seattle.

title: “Excellent, new airport hotel”
text: Excellent room, one bedroom suite with full kitchen. Very clean. Friendly staff. VERY close to airport - remember, DIA is in the middle of nowhere.

title: “Great Location”
text: The Westin hotel is your typical "big city" hotel. The accommodations were average to good and the staff were friendly but didn't seem to take any interest in your requests. There food and spirits were good but nothing spectacular. The location of this hotel is a real plus...within a few blocks is your local nightlife district, where great food and lively entertainment could be found for all...

title: “Comfortable, clean hotel and great staff!”
text: We stayed in the Affinia in July 2011. We are a family with 2 teens and we thought the hotel worked great for us. I think the location is good, although it is about a 15 minute walk to Times Square. The kids grumbled about the location but I wanted to be in a little less crowded area. There are great restaurants right around the corner - ask at the front desk and they will give you all kinds of info about where to eat. We upgraded to a wonderful 2 bedroom suite. If you can spend a little extra, DO IT and upgrade. It was a fabulous room (with a view of the Empire State Building), lots of space to spread out, 2 bathrooms, and a small kitchen. Worked perfect with our 2 teenagers. All ammenities you could ever need were provided down to extra utensils when we brought dinner back to the room. The cleaning staff was so friendly, so helpful - we made a call and it was there at our front door. The front desk was personable, helpful, friendly - they took time to recommend plays to see, places to go, and how to get there. We loved the Affinia and I would stay there again.

title: “Dont stay anywhere else. Great with young children”
text: This is an excellent hotel. I stayed here last Oct 07 with a 22 month old and a 5 month old. The room facilities are great with small kids. I had a travel cot in main bedroom and travel cot in sitting room, so babies didnt wake each other up. There was still masses of room even with 2 travel cots and prams and everything that goes with it. I seriously cant recommend this hotel enough. We left this hotel as arranged on day 3 of trip to move onto the Sheraton in Framingham, what a disappointment as soon as we arrived we rang Doubletree and begged for a room for the rest of our 10 day stay, they accommodated us no problem. Did I already say I cant recommend this place enough!. Seriously dont bother with anywhere else. Ok so its a little outside of Boston Centre but they have a shuttle going regular to anywhere you could want to go. Stay here you wont be disappointed.

title: “A very pleasurable stay”
text: This was a great hotel. We had a room with two double beds in and although by the end of the stay it was rather cramped - 4 girls, 4 suitcases & 4 lots of shopping- it was well cleaned, tidy and the staff were very efficient. Its location was ideal, especially for Times Square and if you like Mexican food, go to the restaurant at the end of the road (turn left out fo the hotel).

title: “Great Home in the Heart of the City”
text: If you are looking for an intimate, upscale home in the heart of Chicago, you can't go wrong at the Talbott. The hotel staff is both friendly and helpful. The rooms and suites are well appointed, comfortable and well-kept. You get complimentary use of a world-class fitness center a few blocks away. Best of all, the value is extraordinary. My wife and travel for business all the time. We are so tired of cookie-cutter accommodations. Both of us loved the Talbott and we think you will too!

title: “Great, well maintained old fashioned charm”
text:
My young adult son and I stayed here for one night at the end of my birthday weekend, early February. Though a bit more expensive than deals at other boutique hotels in Union Square, the very positive reviews and ratings intrigued me and made me curious. The Chancellor's friendly, helpful staff, cozy charm, and clean old fashioned rooms were perfect. Watched the Super Bowl at the cute hotel bar, with elegant Irish bartender and other guests (all men except for me). Late dinner delivered, free of charge, from a nearby restaurant. Perfect stay!
So glad I chose the Chancellor, and look forward to staying there again.

title: “Perfect Escape”
text: Just spent 5 nights in a Valencia Casita at this lovely, tucked away resort in the Camelback Corridor- considered Phoenix, but on the edge of Scottsdale. The mediterranean villa architecture is a little unusual in these parts, and is stunningly beautiful. There is not a bad view to be had in this resort, with all kinds of intimate nooks in which to get lost, the sound of water everywhere. The grounds are planted with citrus trees, hibiscus, bouganvillea, palms- all very vibrant in the middle of the desert. The service is second to none, and all staff go out of their way to remember your name and use it each time they see you. Rick and Jose at the pool are particularly excellent at what they do. Be sure to leave the resort (though you won't want to!) to walk the 3 mile loop behind the hotel which goes into the foothills of Camelback Mountain. It's a bit steep and windy, but well worth the effort. The views are remarkable. Such a great way to start your day. The food at T Cooks is pricey, but excellent, and considered one of the best restaurants in the area. It's worth booking at least one treatment at the Alvadora Spa while there. So glad I found this special place in which to rest, relax and rejuvenate.

title: “Excellent facility - best concierge service in 25 years of travel”
text: Our stay in the Pointe Hilton Squaw Valley was great. Dave Richardson gave the best concierge service I've ever experienced. Facility slightly dated but amenities n service easily made up for it

title: “Nice location, very good value”
text: Very good view to Times Square from the restaurant

title: “Good Location, Not a great value for the price”
text:
I've stayed in the Westin City Center in Washington DC a couple of times this year. The location, about 3 blocks north of the White House, is great. Easy walking distance to the WH and the mall. A couple of blocks to the closest Metro stop. 
The hotel was just OK. The facility was clean. The staff was friendly and efficient. It seems a bit dated though. On my second visit I paid more for a larger room ($379/night). The positives- it was comfortable, quiet, and reasonable spacious. The downside- I had an interior view of the lobby. Poorly lit. The bath had an 80's look that seemed to have been patched over a few times. Smaller TV that was visible only from the bed. 
Nice desk though and a very comfortable bed.

title: “Glad to get this on Priceline”
text:
Won this 4-star hotel on Priceline at $72 a night for this two-night stay, which included New Year's Eve. The hotel lived up to the lofty ranking on Tripadvisor. The only thing I wasn't happy about was forgetting the camera for some pictures.
Hotel Monaco is a Kimpton Hotel located in town but only a couple blocks walk to the Inner Harbor. Rooms had high ceilings, modern decor and a clean, comfortable feel. Our king room only had a walk-in shower in the bathroom if that's a concern. I like the LG HD TV's and they offered about a dozed HD channels. We were on the 12th floor and found it very quiet in the evening, not bad considering the hotel seemed pretty full for New Year's.
Valet Parking is the only option at the hotel for $36 a night. There is a parking garage one block up on the left and it was only $21 a night. If we include the tip for valet, I probably saved $40 for the two nights by just walking one block. Be careful when pulling up to the hotel because there is no pull out from Charles Street. Curbside is the only option for unloading. As stated earlier the Harbor is an easy walk and we did it on a snowy, cold morning.
The restaurant/bar in the hotel is called B&O American Brasserie and we ate a quality dinner in there. It also has a modern theme, but moderately expensive if one is just looking for a quick bite. However, the smaller brick oven pizzas are excellent for only $9. The Caribou Coffee Cafe across the street was also a nice place to stop for some java.
As stated earlier the Harbor is an easy walk and we did it on a snowy, cold morning. I highly recommend this hotel for a great stay in Baltimore.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text:
This is not a luxury hotel, but it is a very functional hotel with a great location. It just became a Holiday Inn Express (possibly previously a Best Western) and has been completely renovated. The rooms are small but very functional, compact, and cute. All rooms have a micro fridge and free high speed internet. All rooms entrances face a courtyard and security was not an issue. There is NO pool. Best of all, parking is free and easily accessible. The hotel is near to many popular attractions and is right off the 405 on the Santa Monica Boulevard. The complimentary breakfast buffet is even more sparse than the usual Holiday Inn Express fare. Staff was very friendly.
I stayed there a total of 5 nights, over two weekends. If I am in the area in the future I would most likely stay there again.

title: “Great choice. Great location.”
text: I've stayed at Novotel about 5 times. Each time I was less pleased because rooms were getting old. I don't know if they've renovated. But anyway, the location is great. A few blocks from Times Square. Rooms were spacious and with all amenities. It's one of the best hotels to stay at if spending a New Years Eve in NY because there's always a huge party on the balcony and you can see all that's happening at Times Square wityhout having to be in the middle of the crowd

title: “Cozy Place”
text:
The room is cozy and i feel comfortable there. I love the bed and liners,
The memory was interesting....
The location is wonderful! Just walk for a few mitutes and we can get to the Times Square.

title: “Perfect for a visit to the Big Apple”
text: My wife and I stayed here with our 2 boys (11 and 13) for 3 nights. I used Marriott Reward points so it did not cost me a dime (would have been $1000). This trip was purely for pleasure and to expose my family to the big city. Whenever I plan a vacation, I do my homework. I read all the reviews and was a bit skeptical.... It was PERFECT! The location was excellent - near many major attractions, on the bus line, a 1 minute walk to the subway, close to hundreds of restaurants, a 4 minute walk to Times Square, 5 minutes from the theatre district.... We walked to Times Square, Rockafeller Center, St Patrick's Cathederal, the shopping area on 5th Avenue, Radio City Music Hall, Grand Central Station...many things are just in that area. As others have said, the street the hotel is on has a couple of porn shops, but no bad characters hanging out. And yes, it is literally across the street from the Port Authority Bus Terminal with some "interesting" people, but we never felt threatened, uncomfortable or ill at ease...it's the city and wherever we went we saw people from all walks of life. We didn't go out much at night because we were exhausted from the days activities, but we did venture out one night to a late dinner, 9:30 -11 pm, and there were so many people out and about that we never felt uncomfortable. We went to Times Square at night and it's a zoo with police at every corner. The hotel rooms are somewhat small...you are either laying on a bed or sitting in the desk chair. The rooms are well appointed and modern...we were on the 28th floor(very good view, but not amazing) out of 32 floors and had to wait for an elevator ocassionally. The breakfast area was great but crowded every morning with microwaveable breakfast sandwiches (that were pretty good), bagels, muffins, cereal, fresh fruit, toast, 4 different juices, great starbucks coffee...it saved us at least $30/day. If we couldn't find a seat, we would sit in the reception area near the entrance to the hotel. Front desk staff was friendly and helpful...I thought moreso than the Concierge. Parking was almost right before the hotel (towards 9th Ave) and it was $24/25 hours...yes a total ripoff, but that was a darn good rate compared to some of the other places we saw (it's just part of the big city experience). On the top floor of the hotel is a open air bar. You have to get to it through the lobby on a separate elevator. My wife and I went up one night for a glass of wine ($12) and enjoyed the view and conversation with other toourists. The bargain of the trip was the pizza place 1/2 block away towards 9th Avenue...$1.00/slice. My kids ate $30 worth during our stay and it was pretty good...that's what we had for lunch on our departure day. The other bargain of the trip was waiting in line on Sunday morning for rush tickets to see "How To Succeed in Business Without Really Trying" staring Daniel Radcliffe. We left the kids at the hotel to sleep in and walked to the theatre at 9:45 am. We sat on the sidewalk with about 100 other people and waited for the box office to open at noon. We drank coffee, read three newspapers and just people watched...it was perfect. We paid $30 for our seats and they were 5th row orchestra left...those seats were $192 a piece. We went back to the hotel, picked up the kids, took a subway to Chinatown for lunch and then back to the show at 3 pm. You will not be disappointed with the Fairfield Inn - location, location, location and clean, great beds and breakfast included. Now if I had had to pay the $1000 for 3 nights, I might not be quite so positive...but even if I stayed at the best hotel in NYC, I would still begrudge the cost for 3 nights...it's just not a value to us...but that's life in the big city.

title: “Perfect choice if you get a good price”
text:
Upscale (but not ultra high end), very comfortable (good rooms, not great), outstanding location (we had a terrific view of Central Park from the 37th floor), excellent food and service. 
Would stay again in a heartbeat for under $200/night. Over $200/night and you have to see what other bargains are out there since there are so many nice hotels in NYC.

title: “PERFECT in so many ways.”
text: Three-day Labor Day weekend. L'Enfant Plaza centrally located, on top of a major Metro station, block and a half to the Smithsonian Castle, excellent staff, sweet bar, gracious restaurant, lovely view of the Potomac, comfortable bed, clean room. Yes, the hotel is older, and in need of a some cosmetic upgrading in the rooms. But you will not find a better place to stay to visit Washington, DC. Expensive as all get-out when government is debating fiery issues; $99.00 a night over Labor Day, less with AAA discount.

title: “The Perfect Place in San Diego”
text:
I am so glad I stayed here. The hotel was very new and exceptionally clean. In years of vacations this staff was amongst the best I have ever encountered. The front desk, the room staff, the maintenance people, the waitresses, the bartender...everyone. 
 Beds were very Comfortable.
 Quiet, tucked away location with a beautiful path along water for your morning walk. Yet minutes from Old Town, Sea World, Little Italy and Mission Beach. Ample FREE parking where many other hotels are charging a premium. It is near the path of the jets taking off from the airport, but the noise was not a factor and I usually am very fussy with noise. Unguarded pool but it is only 3 to 4 feet. Great place and we will return.

title: “Fantastic Hotel!!”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights on the start of our honeymoon tour of the East Coast of America. The hotel is beautiful and very nicely decorated! The room was large with plenty of space, the bathroom was also a good size and the shower itself was powerful. The bed is very comfy, we really couldn't fault anything. To make our stay extra special the reception staff sent us champagne and truffles which was a lovely suprise!!! The staff are also very helpful. The only thing I could really complain about was the meal I had in the resturant which wasn't very nice although my husband said his was fine! The hotel is also in a brilliant location and we were able to find our way around easily - i'd recommend this hotel to my friends!!!

title: “|What a fabulous hotel!”
text: We recently stayed at Ink48 for three nights and it was fantastic! We were made to feel welcome as soon as we arrived. We had booked a City View Studio room which was amazing. We’ve stayed in NYC before and know how small the hotel rooms can be but this was huge. It had massive windows with great views of the Manhattan skyline and a lovely big bath tub in the room to lie in and admire it all – wow! Apart from the sheer size of the room, it was bright, clean and really well appointed, we would have been happy to spend most of our time in there! The rest of the hotel was also lovely – very chic and smart and yet with a relaxed feel to it. We enjoyed the wine hour and the restaurant was lovely with totally delicious breakfasts and great service. We also tried out the roof top bar which was really popular with people queuing to get in every night – no wonder, the views and atmosphere were great! Unfortunately, never got to try the spa as it was fully booked when I tried to make a reservation, my own fault for leaving it too late but I did try the 24/7 gym – small but with everything you needed! The staff were all really friendly and helpful, especially the concierge who booked the airport shuttle for us when we left. We had such a lovely time, would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone and we can’t wait to go back! OK it’s about 15-20 minutes walk from Times Square etc which might not be good for everyone, but we liked staying in this area – close to the Hudson and the brilliant Intrepid Air, Sea & Space Museum and there’s a great jogging track all the way along the riverside and fantastic H&H Bagel Bakery just round the corner!

title: “A Great San Fran Hotel!”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Fairmont SF in August 07.
When we arrived we were asked if we would like to upgrade for a small fee. ($50.00 more per night) $250.00 per night total) I thought that I had heard that story before but decided to do the upgrade. WOW! What a great room with a view of the Coit Tower, Alcatraz, Angel Island, beautiful roof tops, and blue sky and the beautiful bay.
The food prices are steep here. We did eat at other great more reasonably priced places. The Tonga room two floors down was fun at Happy Hour! The service was very good. Several people with attitudes but overall very nice people were found here.
This is one classy place to stay and we were glad we picked the Fairmont SF.
We checked out the Union Square area and found it was great for people watching and shopping but we preferred our Nob Hill more private location.

title: “Good Value for money and superb location!”
text:
I very much enjoyed my stay in this hotel.
It was quiet, comfortable, clean and very pleasant all round.
The desk staff were very helpful with any questions, their knowledge of the area was excellent (i have been to San Francisco before so I tested them)
The hotel although not "upper class" was still very nice the room size was adequate, the washing facilities were reasonable and the amenities were as you would expect form any nice hotel.
The MAIN attraction fore this hotel (for me personally) was the location, Fisherman's Wharf was an easy 2 block walk to the very heart of it all!.
Pier 39 was a brisk walk from the hotel location, and with the added benefit that all (or most) of the local tour companies and city trip buses stopped at convenient locations. with were with is a 1 - 3 min walk from the hotel!.
It's an excellent stay in a decently priced room, in the heart of it all......What more could you want!

title: “Great Time at the Library Hotel”
text: We had a wonderful stay at the Library Hotel for 7 nights in October. Excellent room (junior suite) with views up Madison Avenue. There are a large number of very positive reviews on Trip Advisor about this hotel (which was one of the reasons why I chose it for what was a special trip), and having stayed there I can now wholeheartedly agree !

title: “No Fish!!!!”
text: I was very disappointed with this hotel. I had read such great reviews and gave up a hotel with a pool to stay here under the premise that there would be a fish in the room to entertain my child. I emailed the hotel well in advance and they assured me they'd put one in the room. Upon check in they again told me the fish would be coming. Nothing happened. I called again and was finally told, hours later, that they had no fish, much to my child's disappointment. The reason given was vague - either the fish dies or they ran out. The point is that they never bothered to tell me this - I had to find out after many attempts and I don't like that kind of treatment at what is supposed to be a four star hotel. The room was not that clean, either (hair, dust), and the wallpaper was coming off the walls in spots. If I were to make a choice again, I'd go with a hotel with a pool. There are many other choices.

title: “Awesome Place! Definitely coming back!!!”
text: This place is just awesome! The staff was so great and helfpul. They had all sorts of discounts so I got a really good price. Plus, they helped me find all sorts of discounts for the nearby attractions. The pool is so beautiful with a waterfall. The rooms are really clean and they included a microwave and refrigerator, which was very helpful. They also had plenty of breakfast items that were free of charge. I ended up staying 4 nights and I already booked a few nights for the upcoming month. Try it out, you won't regret it.

title: “Elegant!!!”
text: Charming.....elegant.....beautiful! Stayed for a week in a beautiful suite. We had a wonderful dinner at the Bull and Bear. Stopped for post-show cocktails at Peacock Allley, and was given great off-the -beaten-path dinner recommendations from our bartender. Room service was perfect!

title: “Good hotel...Good location”
text: Hotel is absolutely fine..Room was spacious, clean and quiet, even for the first floor..Staff were helpful and courteous..Fairly easy to walk east and west and used subway for north/south trips..Just one thing to be aware of...Room advertised at $249 per night..After adding the FOUR different taxes, that became $289 per night

title: “Omni Hotel, 500 California”
text:
Our family stayed at the Omni for our spring break this year which was March17th-21st. Great service, excellent location in San Francisco and a clean and wonderful room. Our kids, ages 11 and 7, loved the attention from the staff. We loved the location to all the attractions in San Francisco. I would highly recommend the Omni. 
Only down side was the water pressure in the shower.

title: “Really nice hotel, unfortunate neighbourhood”
text:
The hotel even has a grand piano the foyer.
Elevator, stair, corridor widt, - it all matches the expectations.
Staff was helpful and friendly.
Walking around in the neighbourhood after 21:00 is not adviseable, - unless you outnumber the "owners of the street corners".

title: “Don't choose this one for your first stay in SF”
text:
If you book this hotel be sure to get there during the day. At night the streets around switch into a homeless-ghetto. They will probably not harm you, but you will definitely not feel safe walking around. We had a car and drove directly into the garage (btw. only valet parking is available at 25 USD/night and it probably does not belong to the hotel direcly). 
The hotel itself has spacious rooms with modern yet rather simple furnishing. Cleanliness is OK with couple of small deficits not worth mentioning. Probably all the rooms have nice floor to ceiling windows. 
The best thing about this hotel is the roof terrace where you can enjoy the breakfast during a sunny morning (don't expect much from the breakfast menu, but it's enough to start the day).

title: “Top Location”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights at the end of February and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. Our first impression of the hotel was positive. We were warmly welcomed by the doorman and receptionist upon arrival. We didn't make use of the valet parking as he was busy but we were able to park the car ourselves without any bother and it only cost us 70 dollars for the two nights parking.
Our room was on the same floor as the outdoor swimming pool (which was closed) and was clean and spacious with two double beds and a desk. We had a lovely dinner at the hotel restaurant and didn't think it was too expensive. I think we paid about 14 dollars for a burger and fries but it is the centre of Washington Dc after all!!
The location of the hotel is amazing. Within 10 minutes we were walking along the National Mall to the Washington Monument and it was only about 20 minutes walk to the White House.
A couple of small points - there was no complementary internet and no fridge in the room but all in all a thoroughly enjoyable stay.

title: “"Fantastic location, close to everything, good value for money in NYC"”
text: The Hampton Inn 35th Street, was a great little find for us, once we came to terms with the cost of hotels in New York! This hotel is more like a boutique hotel, small in comparison to some hotels, but still with all amenities. Sitting between 5th and 6th Avenue the location was fantastic !!! Everything I ever dreamed about seeing in NYC was within "walking distance" of our hotel and, if I felt it was a little far to walk, there was a subway entrance just down the road. Our room was small, but I've come to learn that almost ALL hotels room in NYC are smallish! Still, we had everything we needed. We also enjoyed a complimentary breakfast each morning, which was always welcomed! Congrats Hampton Inn, we loved staying with you and if we're ever lucky enough to come back to New York, we'll be staying with you!

title: “Not bad for the price”
text: Paid only 50 bucks from Priceline and the rooms were clean and bed was comfortable

title: “Great Value, Great Service”
text: The price was the best on that side of Jacksonville. The staff was friendly and efficient, from the guest desk to the cleaning service. The Inn is right off of the interstate, easy on and off. We had looked at a competitor right across the street and chose Ramada because of the amenities. The breakfast buffet was what really tipped the scales.

title: “Good but not perfect”
text: We spent 5 nights at the Holiday Inn Riverwalk on a vacation to visit friends and see the sights. Check in was flawless and friendly. We arrived on an early flight and our room was ready before 1PM. The main areas of the hotel are due for a make over according to several pictures on display. The overall impression is dated and a bit worn, but not shabby. The room, 2 doubles, was fine and the beds comfy. No problem at all with house keeping staff. The room was on the 4th floor and overlooked the Riverwalk. VERY convenient to downtown attractions and less than a block from a trolley stop. We took the airport shuttle so we didn't deal with on site parking. We only had appetizers and drinks at the bar but otherwise dined off site so I can't say anything about the food. The exercise room is recently redone as is the bar/restaurant. Incidentally, there is a Starbucks across the street, a nice bakery less than a block and a decent bagel place within a short walk. Although there is no free breakfast we never spent more than $10 for breakfast for 2. There is also a "grab and go" place off of the lobby and we did get coffee there once.

title: “Rooms are gross and they double charged us!”
text: I had requested a cot for our room when I made the reservation but when I got to the waterpark to check in they said that cots could not fit up in their elevators in the tower. Very bizarre since they were standard elevators. This meant our 10 year old son had to stay in the bed with us since there was no where else for him to sleep. Our room was disgusting. There was a huge water stain right outside of the bathroom which soaked the kid's socks. The wallpaper was peeling off and the sheets were scratchy and uncomfortable. The waterpark itself was fine, although they are very strict about the 48 inch height requirement. Our 6 year old son was not able to do any of the slides that he normally does because he was an inch to short. They also didn't have enough lifeguards- there was only one lifeguard running the 4 large slides. When we got home and got our bank statement we noticed they double charged us for our room (over $200). I called to have it taken off and they said they had us staying 2 nights.!

title: “Great Staff, fantastic view!”
text: Wife and I decided to get away one night for our anniversary. Stayed at Pier 5's highest rated room and in most case we were very impressed. The hotel employees were very friendly and Kevin at the front desk was very professional and will go out of his way to make your stay perfect. The view from our room was breathtaking. The suite was very nice but certainly could do with some updating when you factor in cost. Dont get us wrong the room itself was gorgeous just seemed a lil bit dated. All in all we would def. recommend this hotel and would go their ourselves again!

title: “Best no-car place in LA!!”
text:
by: a woman traveller from Manhattan
This is my new favorite place in LA.
It's a newly-refurbished boutique hotel with about 100 rooms and a very pleasant European-feeling lobby, decorated with candles and blown glass objects, and it's in the best possible location for a traveler without a car - it's as easy to walk to dozens or hundreds of restaurants and shops as it would be in downtown Manhattan. Furthermore, the shops themselves are exceptional, as 3rd Street is a prime area for fresh boutiques and top-notch LA vintage shopping.
My room was pleasant and large, with a king-size bed and a seting area with a sofa. Temperature control was excellent, service was pleasant, a view of the Hollywood Hills was agreeable, and a leaky faucet handle was repaired the instant I reported it.
The restaurant food is excellent. The cost of my room included breakfast, which was generous - a nice buffet and eggs or pancakes if you felt like ordering them; one day there were elegant French apple tarts, every day there was homemade (I think) banana and zucchini bread. (If I'd wanted to, I could have booked a room for $20 less without the breakfast and found a dozen places to eat for less outside the hotel, but I liked the convenience this time.)
From the money angle, it's worth noting that on nearby La Cienega it's easy to find nice simple chain places like Chipotle for a really fast, really cheap meal.
A small pool is set nicely with comfortable lounge chairs for sunbathing. A small exercise room adjacent to the pool has the essentials and I did not ever have to wait to use it.

title: “Looks can be decieving.....”
text: It was my wifes birthday so I just had a thought, lets take a weekend trip to San Antonio. I booked our room online,and thought I found a frugal priced room for the location. I was wrong, we pulled into the hotel in it looked as if we where entering a low income housing. The staff, they were okay for the most part. But the feeling my wife and I had both felt entering the hotel wasn't a good one. I had the misconseption that I was getting a nice size King suite. But after entering our room we could have stayed in a low budget motel for way less than half the price. NEXT TIME IT WILL NOT BE THIS AND NEXT TIME WHEN WE SEE A HOTEL ONLINE IT WILL HAVE TO BE A WELL KNOWN HOTEL. WOW I REALLY FEEL LIKE I WAS HOODWINKED....

title: “A Stay at the "W"”
text: My granddaughter and I attended a Christian Women's Conference at the American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas this past weekend and stayed at the W Dallas Victory Hotel just across the street. This hotel is state of the art in luxury. My only complaint was the lack of a restaurant. I know they had one last year, but they had closed it down for renovations. This was very inconvenient for us because there was no other place to eat but the bar and it had a limited menus. Other than that our stay was very nice.

title: “Fun n Friendly”
text: A great place to stay in San Francisco. Reasonable rates. Friendly Staff. My husband and I stayed a superior king room. We loved the vibe. It's not the newest or most modern of the Joie de Vie choices, but the vibe is way cool and we loved hanging out in the courtyard by the pool. It has been remodeled and the modern hip style was cool. I was surprised and impressed by the complimentary breakfast. Grateful for the free parking.

title: “Perfect Stay Great Location”
text: We stayed at the brand new Embassy Suites on the Riverwalk for a few days before Christmas. The hotel is beautiful. Our room was perfect, a corner suite with a balcony overlooking portions of the Riverwalk and a city view out of of the side windows. Our bed was very comfortable, and the suite was incredibly quiet. We couldn't hear guests in adjacent rooms or on adjacent floors. The staff was courteous, professional, and responded very quickly to our requests for additional towels, etc. The valet parking is a bit pricey, but we opted for the valet vs. the cheaper lot across the street. The valet staff was very quick and also very courteous; we weren't left waiting for our vehicle for more than a minute when we were heading out. We had dinner at Luke's the hotel restaurant one night. The food was fantastic, and the waitstaff was very accommodating. We loved the hotel and are looking forward to returning in the future.

title: “Defiantly will stay here again!”
text:
A bit late writing this review but neverless, it's deserved.
We stayed here with another couple over Canada's Victoria Day Weekend this year. I ended up "liking" their page on FB, got a 25% discount for booking this hotel through their Facebook page, made a comment on their wall about how we are coming down for a 10 year anniversary celebration and a belated birthday.....and we got an upgraded room! 
When we arrived in our room they had cupcakes for my belated birthday, a hand written note from the manager wishing me a happy birthday and a note from the staff, which they all signed, wishing me a happy birthday. Our couple we were with who were celebrating their anniversary also received the same nice touches.
Everyone from the bellboy, to the front line staff to the staff at breakfast, they were all very helpful and attentive.
The rooms were super big and clean. Bed was very comfortable. couldn't here a thing! Room was always made up by the time we got back from a long day. Love the single cup coffee machines in the room. 
The location of the hotel was great for what we wanted. We have almost stayed in every part of NYC and this was one of the last areas. 
We will defiantly be back to this hotel.

title: “Simply the best”
text: Gracious staff, great location, impeccable room, beautifully decorated, I'll never stay in any other hotel in Philly again; it was that good.

title: “Nice Hotel and Location”
text:
Hotel seemed brand new. Lobby is great with a small bar, restaurant, coffee house. Lobby is very comfortable with big touch screen information monitor, groups of couches, small tables with personal TV's, etc.
Room was very nice with new furniture, nice lighting, spacious, internet, flat screen TV, etc.
Cons: No fan in bathroom (not a good thing for my roomate after I beached one). Also bad acoustics. You can hear everything in the hallway and what the people in the next room are talking about and watching on TV. $14 parking is pretty steep considering the location. The Vagabond hotel next door had free waffles for breakfast--squat from Courtyard.

title: “Room nice, customer service bad”
text: The only thing I like about this hotel was that the room is cozy and the bed was extremely comfortble. Too bad customer service was not as good. When we checked in, the receptionist didn't care to give us the time of day (I guess because we did not look like "rich" people). We valeted the car, no one told us how we could get the car back so we asked the receptionist when we checked in. She abruptly told us you can call from your room and waved us off. No one offered any information about anything to us. Although the elevators were right behind us, it would have been courteous of her to point that out to us. That same night, we called valet to get our car to meet some friends for dinner. Per instructions in the guest book, we called valet 15 mins before we needed the car. We went down 15 mins later and waited another 45 mins before we finally got our car. We figured it wouldn't be worth it to valet the car anymore so we parked on the streets for the rest of our stay -especially when valet costs $50/night! Well, seems the hotel has a very inefficient valet service system, they charged us for the first night although we only parked for about 3 hrs. We explained to reception what had happened and to my disbelief, they actually removed the charges from our room. That was their saving grace.

title: “Thanksgiving Dinner”
text: Great food. Great service. Betty was awesome. Highly recommended.Love the decor. Can't beat the location and view. Right on beautiful Mission Bay. Good value for the tremendous variety of food. The complimentary boat cruise was a nice touch and a great end to an awesome meal.

title: “Enjoyed our stay”
text: We enjoyed our stay at this property. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Our room on the 12th floor had a view of the Empire State Building. The room was larger than we expected and the shower was quite large and the water pressure was excellent. The bed was probably the most comfortable bed we've ever slept on in a hotel.The air conditioner was pretty noisy, but we didn't need to use it much. Breakfast was the usual fare and was fine. The room and hotel were both very clean and the location was great. We walked or took the subway or a bus with ease. We tried a few of the restaurants that the hotel recommends and had good experiences at all-Mustang Sallys and a pizza place-Ciao Bella Napoli. We also went to Uncle Nick's Greek restaurant and had a nice meal. It is only a few blocks away too.

title: “Needs Improvement”
text:
We picked the Dana Hotel for an overnight Sunday stay because we wanted to be closer to the shopping areas, and support a boutique hotel. We foresake our typical choice of staying at the Stellar Burnham Hotel, for Dana. 
We found our stay disappointing. Perhaps it's the economy or the staff was too tired from the weekend revellers and didn't give much attention to those staying there on a Sunday night. We're not fussy travellers and don't need much apart from courteous, competent service. We didn't have that experience at the Dana. I'll highlight some of the good and bad points we experienced.
-- Positives:
Awesome bed.
Comfortable room: we have an asian inspired, cotemporary waterfront condo and were pleased with the decor.
--Negatives:
Check-in staff seemed like they were trying to replicate a cool, youthful, aloof urban energy. It came off as apathetic. One got the feeling that they were doing this job until they went to their "real jobs" later on.
Does this place really have a spa? Every time I have ever checked into a hotel that has a spa ... they at least tell you a little about it. This is true whether I have stayed at destination spa locations, or hotels where the spa is an amenity for a predominantly business clientele.
-- Aja Steak: was pleased with the subbtle Hawaiian flair in the menu. Fish was good quality. I think we got left-over rice on our maki, because it was terrible. Service was lower than average. Perhaps we got the Sunday, C level staff. They were poorly trained ....and I almost felt like piping up " ummmm ...are there any adults running this place?"
We have travelled internationally and stayed at numerous hotels. My basic rule is that if a place has an expensive, diverse selection of sakis and wines with limited descriptors; they should have someone on staff to discuss the selections. They didn't that night. Worse still, we had a flaky waitress who did not even seem to understand the qualitative distinctions between the food & drink selections on the menu. In an effort to be friendly/knowledgeable she tried to pipe in how did not know much about sakes ... but she loved the junmai daiginjo sakes. Her comment would have been acceptable if she knew what she was talking about (we are avid sake drinkers); but it's like someone who knows nothing about the varied construction & mechanisms in watches saying how they love the quality and mastery of how Cartier watches are built.
Next time, we'll stick to the Burnham Hotel. Kimpton just gets how to do boutique hotels, and they have shown that prowess nationally and internationally. Besides, they are in the same price range as the Dana.

title: “Good Hotel”
text:
We love Kimpton Hotels and stayed in 3 during our road trip to Cape Cod from DC. First time at the Eventi. The room was a good size and the bathroom/shower was amazing. We were on a high floor and had a nice view that our dogs actually loved looking out of during our stay. Got a $25 bar credit which we used at their restaurant: the food was good and we got the credit by knowing the secret summer password in addition to getting a mini bar credit and free wifi through Kimpton In Touch and of course enjoyed the wine hour.
Valet parking went smoothly. The only reason I don't give the hotel a 5 is because their was a strong smell of cleaning product when we got in the room. Normally I would have asked to move rooms, and I am sure I would have been quickly accommodated by the staff, but decided it wasn't worth the hassle and eventually it either went away or we got used to it. Interestingly the cold water didn't work and it took some time for someone to come up and fix it. Also, I had to call down 3 times for a dog bowl which is not typical of Kimpton service. Still I would recommend the hotel but will probably try another Kimpton property like the Ink 48 or Muse on my next visit.

title: “Where are the drawers?”
text:
I stayed 3 nights at this hotel for business. The hotel is located at the rear of the Domain shopping outdoor mall behind the parking lots. You have to take a little bit of a slow drive (1 lane/each way road) within the Domain to get to the hotel. It's not a big hotel. There are 6 floors.
This was my first experience with the aLoft brand. I don't like it, though there's definitely a market for it. It brings me back to my college days because this hotel felt like a really sweet brand new dorm that your really cool friends were able to get into. There's a DYI feel to it because you have a veneer of trendiness and then on closer inspection,it seems a bit cheap.
I had a king-size bedroom. The room measured around 250 sq foot. The bed was a true king size, though it was not a Starwood Heavenly bed. The bed was decent and I did not have any complaints with the sleep quality over my 3 nights. The comforter is on the lighter side (but this is Texas so there's no point in having very thick blankets). The bathroom is not truly a separate room because there's only a wall that separates it from the rest of the room. I thought the sink was too small and too low. There was always water getting onto the floor. There's a good-size walk-in shower. (No bathtub.) The handlebar on the glass shower door got loose on my 2nd night and I just left it as it was. The bath towels were Walmart quality.
There is no closet. What you have is a little bar opposite the sink to hang about 5 pieces of clothing. There are no drawers anywhere. There is plenty of shelf space throughout the room so I ended up just putting my used clothing in a bag on a shelf.
I got on the free WiFI and the connection speed was good on the 6th floor.
There are 2 elevators and it takes about 30 seconds or more to call it.
I paid a little bit over $150 per night (before taxes). In hindsight, I wouldn't have booked a room at this hotel for that rate, perhaps closer to $110. For business travelers, I would suggest sticking to the Four Points by Sheraton brand if you want to do low end Starwood. Otherwise, I think Hilton Garden Inn would get you more bang for the buck.

title: “Best Ever”
text: Spotless room, amazing private steam baths. Great team at the front desk. The views are amazing. 1 block to trains. Stores, restaurants, clubs all in walking distance. Breakfast downstairs in Co-Op with Michelle is an experience all on it's own. Simply the best!

title: “Very good hotel but room for improvement”
text:
This is actually a very good hotel. The rooms are nice, the restaurant is good and staff is very friendly. It shows that the hotel is recently renovated although the room doors to the hall way are not very good isolated. Everything that happens on the corridor will be witnessed in the rooms. In a previous review there were some complaints about the internet but that seems to be resolved completely. In room we had perfect wifi connections with 2 laptops an iPad and an iPhone. Congrats on that!
Although you can call for room service to clean you room at a certain time it is always a surprise whether they had cleaned the room or not. Very annoying when you return to the hotel after a day trip and the room is still not cleaned! This should be an easy fix and should be fixed right away.

title: “more like apt. than hotel”
text:
This was a very nice place to stay. It is more like an apartment than a hotel. You walk in to the entryway (with 4 small desks for check-in) and take the elevator to your room. The rooms were nicely decorated, were reasonable size for Mahattan, had a marble shower and granite counter in the bathroom.
We were there on a promotional trip to view a timeshare. On President's Day, the sales people were VERY busy, so we had a short (25 min rather than 90 min) non-pushy presentation. On a less busy day, they probably would have tried harder, but our sales lady had another presentation to go to and didn't want to waste time on us if we weren't interested.
As others have mentioned it is a very good location. We went down a few doors to Carnegie Hall for a concert and across the street to the Steinway store, we we played the pianos without a salesperson even entering the room.
Other travelers mentioned that there was not daily maid service, but the maid did come both mornings we were there.
It was a very good value for the promotional price ($150/night for 2 nights).
If I am to be nit-picky, I'd mention that the fan for the room heating/cooling is rather loud.
Tip: The main New York Public Library on 5h Ave.and 42nd St. has an exhibition room (free) with a Gutenberg Bible, Thomas Jefferson's handwritten draft of the Declaration of Independence, George Washington's handwritten Farewell Address and the first edition of Christopher Columbus' report on his explorations of America among other interesting items. Well worth visiting!

title: “Old, Outdated, Fancy Lobby, Room not worth that amount of money”
text: We stayed in SOHO for 2 nights earlier and paid half the price at the Hampton Inn. They had free breakfast, free wifi, and room that was twice as clean and twice the size of the Roosevelt. The room has an old rusty air con, dirty walls, broken shower. room 1581.

title: “A great place to stay near Union Square”
text: As has been our tradition, my wife and two daughters rent two rooms for two nights before Christmas at the JW Marriott for shopping at nearby Union Square and Holiday evening entertainment. This hotel has become our favorite at Union Squre because it is away from the crowds and frenzy and the rooms, public areas and restaurant have been recently renovated and are maintained in excellent condition. We also believe the hotel is superior to other hotels in the vicinity. The staff is very professional and accommodating. When the concierge was unavailable, the front desk took the initiative to make dinner reservations for us with preferred treatment.

title: “THE BEST HOTEL in UNIVERSITY PLACE”
text: I frequently stay at hotels in the Charlotte area to see how they are for my clients. As being a Travel Agent, you want to recommend the best of the best for clients to gain return business. The property is very well maintained. The staff is AWESOME - very polite and helpful. I normally deal with SALES office (Monique Stubbs-Hall) who in my opinion can run the HILTON by herself but on this stay I was able to interact with the front desk staff and they were absolutely wonderful and professional. I had a 2 night stay; my room was fabulous -nice view of the lake. Room was spacious and very clean. I did dine in for the breakfast buffet and can I tell you i could have stayed there all day. The food was fresh and very tasty. I really enjoy the cooked to order omlets!!! They have so many options and fresh pastries. Check in and Check out went very smooth. I will definitely be using the Hilton Charlotte University Place as my preferred hotel for clients and my personal stay. MANAGEMENT JOB WELL DONE!!!! ~ LEXONA AFFAIRS, LCC

title: “Excellent!”
text:
Just returned from a 3 night stay and have to say I was more than impressed. I picked this hotel from this website and was not disappointed. 
I arrived about 11.30am and was given a room immediately. Although on my own, I had a beautiful double room near the top of the hotel and, although the views aren't fabulous, I was still pleased with what I could see.
The room had a little kitchen area with fridge, microwave and coffee maker (come on you other brits, you can just put water through it to make tea most successfully, don't need a kettle).
Bathroom with bath, shower, hairdryer, and opposite that the wardrobe with iron, ironing board and very useful safe. 
All in all, this hotel has everything you need for a very comfortable, well positioned hotel in New York. Staff were superb as well.
I stayed at a 3 star, more expensive hotel 3 years ago, and it was disgusting.
I would, and have, recommended this hotel to everyone and look forward to returning myself as soon as I can.
Thank you Belvedere.

title: “Very small room, but I liked it overall”
text:
This is a small hotel. The rooms are small by most cities standards. However, I have stayed in smaller rooms in New York City (and paid a lot more $$).
The bathroom was decent size and amenities are good.
You can open the room's windows which was great since the weather was nice. 
I would stay here again.

title: “Great Choice”
text: We decided to stay here because we wanted to use our Hilton Honors Points. Previously we stayed at the Courtyard by Marriott downtown. We were pleasantly surprised with the hotel. It seemed to be in a much better area than downtown, probably because of the university, and was nicely renovated and clean. Our room was small, but very adequate for a one night stay. The bathroom was basic, small, but OK. No hair dryer as previous reviews stated, so I brought one along. We had trouble deciding on a restaurant within walking distance, and didn't feel like Italian or Japanese in and next to the hotel, or the fare at the White Dog, so we chose room service. It was excellent! The steak was very good and served nicely. Next time we will save the effort of walking around and simply use room service. Staff seemed helpful and courteous. Valet Parking is $30. per night, but that's expected here. We had the breakfast buffet in the morning, and that was very nice for $15.00 per person. We drove the 25+ blocks to Jefferson Hospital in the morning, but that only took 15 min. We will probably chose to stay here again when we need to go to Jeff simply because we like the area better, and the drive, rather than walking to the hospital is not a problem for us.

title: “All things considered, OK”
text: First of all, I thought the room I was in, and the facility in general was very nice. It is a rather large and spread out hotel, so one may be forced to walk a lot to get from one place to another, especially to banquet facilities across the street. Older design I suppose, doesn't seem like its necessarily an efficient use of space. The location downtown is perfect, if downtown is where you want to be. Breakfast was included in my stay, and though it could have been more elaborate, such would have been lost on me; I thought it was just fine. Restaurant service was a little slow when busy, but within reason. I had a car to park, and I must say the parking facility was disorganized. But I had no problems. Elevators are ample in number, no long waits. I might would consider this facility a five star with one exception--the reservations team. I must have spoken by phone with them a dozen times and when I arrived they still hadn't gotten my reservation right. The problem: I was reserving two rooms, one for myself and one for a colleague. Our itinerary changed a couple of times necessitating call backs, and the experience was akin to banging one's head on the wall. I'll take credit for my part in communication breakdown, but it really wasn't complicated. A very capable and warm young Asian women straightened all out when I arrived. As for room service personnel, I had no interaction as I chose to go with their "eco plan" and not have my room prepared anew each day. Can't critique the price as I was participating in a conference with a special rate, which rate was reasonable. We did have a banquet and the food was enjoyable. I would return, but I might have someone else call in the reservation!

title: “Good airport hotel”
text:
The Four Points meets all the expectations for an overnight stay. The rooms are basic but they are clean and roomy. 
There is a single restaurant at the hotel, which makes the hotel not so much viable for longer stays. There aren't any restaurants close by, and downtown Philadelphia is about a 20-25 minute drive. Therefore I'd think twice for extended stays.
Considering the price, this hotel is a good value for what it offers.

title: “Awesome Experience!”
text: I would HIGHLY recommend this hotel if you are staying in the downtown Boston area. It is a beautiful hotel and a perfect location. Close to Quincy Market, Little Italy and the Imax theater and the Aquarium. The staff is very friendly, Vicki at the front desk made our stay one of the best hotel experiences we have ever had. She went above and beyond as an employee. When i told her we were celebrating my husband's 50th birthday she sent a table of sweets, fruit and champagne (milk for the kids) to our room. She is one of the best employees of a hotel we have ever encountered. She was so good to us i had to surprise her with a little present because she deserved it! The hotel is clean, very stylish and a great spot to enjoy the beautiful view of the harbour. Great job Marriott Long Wharf!

title: “Dated, but certainly adequate for my needs”
text:
I was attending a seminar at the Hilton Conference Center, and this Clarion is literally across the street from it. I got a clean comfortable room for less than half the price of a room at the Hilton. The shuttle service to and from the airport was prompt and the drivers were courteous. The bedding and mattress were extremely comfortable.
 I couldn't go 5 stars because of the dated decor and the lack of any free breakfast, but really, this was a nice stay. A clean room, helpful staff, good location, and prompt shuttle were all at my disposal at a good price. By the way, they offer an AARP discount off of an already competitive price. This room was exactly what I needed.

title: “Great waiters and housekeeper”
text:
We enjoyed very much our stay in Doubletree last february. 
Our breakfast server NUR was the best, very kind and friendly.
Our housekeeper LUCIA also provided us great service.
Hope to stay there again soon.

title: “Great hotel, great location, great value”
text:
This Marriott surprised me in that it was very modern and stylish, but not overly so (like the Se hotel in San Diego). The rooms are a good size and modern, but warm, and everything about it was right: outlets easily available, little noise, nice bathroom amenities, comfortable bed, large desk, comfortable chair and ottoman, etc. I was here for business so I just wanted a large comfortable bed and low noise, and I got that. 
The staff was friendly and nice too. This is one of the better Marriott hotels I have stayed at in terms of having a nice, clean, modern and comfortable room. 
In addition, the location is great, near Petco Park and all of the shops and restaurants in the Gaslamp quarter. 
The value was good too $149 per night. 
The Residence Inn across the street looks nice too, but slightly more expensive (about $189).

title: “Comfortable and Convenient”
text: Clean, comfortable and convenient--the Silver Cloud--University did a fine job of meeting my needs while I was in Seattle visiting family in the Greenlake area. There aren't as many hotel choices in this northern section of the city. My relatives, who live near the hotel, recommended it and said that they often put up out-of-town guests there. While the Silver Cloud wasn't cheap, the lowest price I could get for my room was $129, it was more than adequate and included a substantial breakfast. The king size bed was comfortable, the room was immaculately clean, and the hotel was just a short walk from the extensive University Village shopping complex. I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again.

title: “Much better than the average airport hotel”
text:
We spent one night there on our arrival for our California/Hawaii trip and two nights on our return. I have stayed there before and thought it was a reasonable hotel for an airport stay but this time I thought it was excellent. We managed to get a very good deal price wise which always helps and the checkin was quick and efficient. The rooms have obviously been renovated and were very clean, the public areas are extremely nice and relaxed and the buffet breakfast about the best I have had in any type of hotel in the past ten years. We are silver members and were upgraded to the Concierge floor so maybe our room was better than other floors. The staff were helpful and very courteous and overall we were really pleased to have picked this hotel for our stopovers. Also extremely convenient for the airport. The only fly in the ointment were some of the staff in the bar/cafe who were certainly not great.
Otherwise well done Marriott.

title: “Superb... great location and AMAZING staff who go the extra mile”
text:
After a travelling trans-Atlantic with our kids and then taking a small tour of the Eastern Seaboard, we were thrilled to have the last leg of our trip in NYC at this wonderful hotel.
