The staff were beyond helpful, they were stellar! They were immediately attentive to the smallest whim (with 3 year old twins we get to hear lots of whims!) Our daughter saw a large contained of water with oranges and asked about about the oranges and within minutes of arriving in our room, they brought us two beautiful large oranges! My son got to ride up in the elevator with the luggage cart and another incredibly friendly member of staff. They were equally friendly and attentive throughout our entire stay.
The room overall was superb -- very large (esp for NYC!), clean, quiet, perfect for families (or anyone else!). 
The location is perfect -- we were within blocks of Central Park, the Central Park Zoo and tons of great restaurants and other attractions (the kids loved the tram to Roosevelt Island!).
My only disappointment is that I can't give the staff any higher than an "Excellent" rating

title: “Great hotel in a great location”
text: I stayed one night in this hotel with my girlfriend while we were over in America on holiday and couldn't fault this hotel. Location is ideal, couple blocks away from Times Square and 3-4 blocks away from the nearest subway. We turned up early, about 10am, to just drop off a bag to save us carrying it around NYC, but we were able to check in then and there. Nice wee room with great facilities; fridge, coffee machine, safe, cooker hobs. Bathroom was nice and modern with big walk in shower. Would happily recommend this hotel to anyone going to NYC and would stay here again.

title: “Stay Here!”
text:
This place is amazing...for a total $90/night, I stayed in their deluxe suite. The room is beautiful, the bed and couch are extremely comfortable, the TV is huge, the bathroom is lovely, and there was a complimentary laptop (with free wifi) and bag of snacks for us on the desk. I'm told they have theme rooms available too! Jacuzzi suite, Asian suite, etc.
The staff were very helpful and friendly, and they have a freakin' massage chair and Starbucks coffee machine in the lobby as well as a DVD/book rental library. And the free breakfast! It was amazing; lots of variety, hot and cold. Also of note is the free parking! 
Overall, I was amazed with this hotel. It exceeded my expectations and then some. I will always stay here when in Austin, and I suggest you do too.

title: “Good Location and Comfortable Bed”
text: If you don't plan to spend any time at the hotel, this is a great choice. Near Central Park and Broadway, the location couldn't be better. The lobby is packed with benches and hotel guests all the time. We assumed this was because cell phones don't work in rooms--there were 3 of us in 3 rooms and none of us could get a signal. The buffet breakfast was absolutely average, neither piping hot, nor interesting and so we were shocked at the $35 per head price.

title: “Good airport hotel for one night”
text: Me and my wife stayed here for one night after a 19 hours of travel from Belgium. It was the start of a month long trip through the US and Canada and really, all we needed was a good place to rest close to the airport. In that way, it was perfectly fine. We only stayed there from about 10 pm to 5 am (thank you, jetlag), so we only saw the lobby and our room, but it was good value. Nothing extraordinary, but you don't expect that from a chain hotel anyway and we weren't looking for that. Check-in was fine, beds were good and that's it, basically. They had what seemed like a good selection of free continental breakfast, but we didn't use it. Location was perfect for getting to/from the airport, but I wouldn't recommend it for people wanting to visit Denver. It's too much out of the way and there weren't a whole lot of eating options in the direct neighbourhood.

title: “My Sheraton Dallas Hotel X-Perience”
text:
I stayed at the Sheraton Dallas Hotel, in Dallas-Texas. I was on business for the 2011 NAD Festival of the Laity. It was another spiritually uplifting x-perience.
My room was comfortable, the breakfast was enjoyable and the hotel was in a great location. There were nice restaurants near the hotel (driving distance).
I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Not bad if you sleep in your clothes”
text: I know why the sheets have pictures of dogs on them. Cause they harbor flees and if you get in the bed you will be a host to a colony of fleas. I learned the next night sleep on top of the k9 sheet fully clothed. Just make sure you tuck in your shirt and pull your socks over your pant legs or you will be sorry.

title: “The FS New York stays true to its image”
text:
Best-in-class concierge service, interesting design (compared to the normally quite boring NYC luxury hotel standard trying too hard to deliver an 'old money' feel). Only downside is that the business centre charges far too much for standard office services that other FS properties provide for free.
I wouldn't think twice about staying here again, in particular if you're on a corporate rate and can get a good deal. A notch or two above Peninsula in my opinion.

title: “Much better than the reviews I read”
text: Upon reading the bad reviews of this hotel, we were a little leery in staying there, however, since our friend from out of town was staying in some apartments next door we decided to give it a try. We had a nice suite, very spacious, like a one bedroom apartment. There is an outdoor area with tables outside the lounge area, and it was extremely nice also. The staff was pleasant, and met our needs. The hotel is very close to Georgetown, and there is a Trader Joes across the street if you need some snacks. There were two flat screen TVs, and overall, it was a very nice experience. We have stayed at the Willard, Marriott, Mayflower, etc in DC and for the money, this hotel can't be beat. If you want to be right in the middle of the action of Dupont, or Adams Morgan, it is a good distance, but cabs right outside the hotel, took us wherever we wanted to go. We have certainly stayed in much worse for the money, and we loved the spaciousness of the suite. Be sure and look on their special rates and packages on their website. As for the parking rate, they are in line with any major city for valet parking. Overall, we truly enjoyed our stay.

title: “Beware of the 'Hobit Room' and exorbitant valet parking cost”
text:
My fiance and I live in the San Francisco Bay Area and pricelined this hotel for $125. We were spending the evening with friends in the North Beach area and wanted to stay the night so we didn't have to worry about driving.
I'll start with the good:
** The hotel lobby and rooms are high-quality with respect to construction, decoration and style - I would consider it a 4-star in this department.
** It's in a great location if you need access to the financial district, or if you'd like to spend an evening in the Italian-influenced North Beach area which has plenty of great restaurants and clubs. It's literally located 2-3 blocks from North Beach, so its an easy walk and you don't even need a cab.
Now for the bad:
** From the front door to the front desk, bellman to desk clerk to valet, the staff is totally mediocre.
** Beware of the guest rooms that end in 00 (e.g. 1800). They are miniature versions of the regular guestrooms that barely fit one full-sized bed (yes, smaller than a queen). The bath room is also much smaller - it can barely fit a small sink with virtually no counter space (no place for toothpaste here), a toilet and the shower. The shower head is way too low - literally at chest level on me (I'm not that tall). Our window had nice views, however, it upheld the miniature theme and occupied only about 25% of the outward facing wall. These rooms are also right next to the elevator which you can hear when in use, and across the hall from the ice machine and vending. Luckily I was extremely tired when we retired to the room from a long night out, so it didn't bother me too much.
** The valet parking cost is exorbitant at $42.00 + $5.88 tax for a total of $47.88 per night! When I arrived I just figured, "Sure, valet it - how much can it be, 20?" Buyer beware, I should have asked. It especially burns when you get poor service and you paid more than top-dollar for it. I'd recommend trying to self-park unless you have money to burn.
I think if you self-park, make sure you don't get one of the hobbit rooms, and don't care about poor service then this hotel is just okay. However, given my experience I don't recommend it.

title: “Total Health Hazzard! Avoid this place at all cost!”
text: I have stayed in many hotels in my lifetime. This is by far the absolute worst hotel in The United States of America. The bathrooms had extreme mold and caused my son problems breathing when he showered. We had to take him to the hospital. The tiolet overflowed when we got there and the heater broke. With proof of the hospital bill the Econo Lodge home office will not refund our money for the stay. Please avoid this hotel if you care for the safety of your family and your health.

title: “Frustration”
text: I booked a room with my daughter for a stay for a water polo tournament. I was told over the phone that the room rate was $89.00/Night. when I went to check out....$129.00/night. "That's the group rate we had you booked at" I told them what I was told over the phone.... The woman that I spoke with was not there and there was nothing they could do about it..... Never again will I stay at a Wyndham!

title: “Amazing hotel!”
text: I travel all over, and this hotel is the most amazing treasure ever! This hotel anticipates my every need before I even ask. They specialize in extra special customer service. The facility is immaculate. The manager personally greets guests in the lobby, remembering names and favorite room numbers. The lobby bar is inviting as well as relaxing. This hotel overlooks a peaceful lake which makes you feel like you are on vacation while you are working. I always look forward to making this location a stop on my itinerary. I appreciate every single aspect of this beautiful hotel.

title: “What could possibly go wrong...Everything!”
text:
I hate to be so negative because there were many friendly people working here who tried to help us, but...
1. Paid extra for a corner suite...which faced a rooftop garage.
2. TV in living room did not work.
3. Shower would not turn on.
4. Room had a bad odor
When we checked in, I asked about getting picked up at the Enterprise office so I could return the rental car a day early. They said just to call when I got there and the shuttle would be right there (10 minute drive). So I called and waited 1.5 hours (no shuttle). I called again...they said the driver didn't want to stop at Enterprise and I would have to get to the terminal to be picked up. Nice of them to call me about this. Enterprise took me to the terminal whereby I waited another 20 minutes for the shuttle from Embassy Suites to arrive.
That evening there was a reception with some free food and drinks which we went to. The lobby area is decorated with 100000's of gallons of flowing water and waterfalls and it opens to the roof, probably 80-100 feet up. This area was as cold and damp as a London tomb and even the help was shivering. We both got sick from this experience.
Upon checkout they did deduct $50 from our bill, which was to their credit. 
In spite of that, nothing about this hotel would make us ever consider staying there again, even though they allowed us to remain in the room 5 hours after checkout before getting to the airport (yes they took us and actually mercifully,got us there). A vacation trip is supposed to be a get away from stress, not a visit to stress and this hotel caused us both much of the latter.
The only redemption for this hotel was the 2 great, shivering cold ladies cooking omlettes down in the tomb. They deserve a raise or at least sweaters!!!

title: “The Best service EVER!!!”
text: From the moment my friend and I arrived at the hotel, we were greeted with smiles and wonderful attitudes, The doorman "D" was awesome along with the rest of the staff. They were all extremely helpful. They even pointed us in the right direction for events, restaurants and everything else in between, as it was our first time in the city. The hotel was very clean and the room was nice, stylish and very comfortable. I definitely would recommend this hotel for several reasons, the staff, the decor, and the location are just a few.

title: “Clean, Comfortable”
text: A co-worker and I stayed at the Comfort Inn for a night during our weekend in NYC (11/13). After reading various reviews of different places I was very nervous as to what to expect. This hotel worked well for us. It was very clean; this is what concerned me the most. I did not see 1 bug of any sort. The bathroom was also very clean, as well as bedding, towels (yes there were plenty for 2 girls), the floor, etc. The room was ready without any problems, all items in the room worked. A few things I have seen mentioned in previous reviews: Yes there is not much of a view, but I did not pick this hotel for the view, I picked it as a place to rest after sightseeing. Yes it is a little off the beaten path, but not once did I fear for our safety and not once did anyone bother us (we walked at night and day; and also took cabs to and from). What the location did offer was a quiet sleeping environment; forgot I was in the city. It did get a little noisy around 6:30am (we were by the elevators) could have been the cleaning people, late night partiers or early risers; whichever it was, it was not untolerable. We slept in and missed the continental breakfast; encountered no problems with staff. This place worked well as a nice, very clean and affordable (by NYC standards) resting spot.

title: “The garage isn't that bad.”
text:
OK. I have read a lot of reviews that warned me about the parking garage, so I was expecting the absolute worst. It was not hard to find if you come in on Washington. If you are driving north on I-65 and taking EXIT 111, you will be turning left on E. Washington. You will see a large glass area above the street called ArtsGarden. As soon as you drive under that, watch your street names. You will pass Illinois Street, and the Embassy Suite parking garage is the only parking garage ramp between Illinois Street and Capitol Street on the right hand side. It is immediately before a theatre on the right. You can't miss it. I am staying there now, and so far it is a typical Embassy Suites.. which is good to me.
I did bring my two and five year old, and one of the men (bellhop/concierge) at the entrance to the garage was very helpful and told me to just return when I was ready to unload my car. He went with me to my car in the garage, and we quickly unloaded everything on a cart which he brought to the room. So far, the service has been very good.

title: “Great location awful service”
text: I travel to the area often and I have never experienced such horriffic service from night and day managers to the clerk who lied about deposits held to all the guests. Never again will I stay there, I would rather commute from Maryland on a moped than deal with them. I never did get an answer why a cable was run under the carpet when you enter the room.

title: “Simple and easy”
text:
We stay here for 5 nights and we really its location that allowed us o stroll to most of the tourist locations in mid/downtown. If you have a chance try to reserve one of the rooms that have been recently redecorated (top floors). 
I was a little bit disappointed with the fact that wifi connection was not complementary

title: “Poor Service”
text: The hotel is in a good location. However, the front desk staff was very rude to me in my attempt to resolve a misunderstanding regarding a mistaken booking of two rooms when I only needed one. They made no attempt to resolve the matter in a fair manner. They simply said they had no authority in the matter and referred me to a manager who would not return any calls. We were in NYC to attend a wedding and the location of this hotel is good. However, the room we had was very small, the furnature was worn, the toilet ran constantly, the shower was very difficult to regulate in terms of temperature and there were bugs in the room. The staff was so unresponsive that it seemed pointless to ask for any assistance with these matters. I would never stay in the hotel again and would never recommend it to anyone.

title: “An Oasis in the Bustle of the City”
text:
We don't live very far away from Seattle and go there several times a year for performances, events, shopping, medical appointments and the like. This was our first stay at the Four Seasons, and we can't believe we haven't stayed there before. We thoroughly enjoyed our one night stay there this week and anticipate our next opportunity. 
We had a water view room on the 9th floor. We normally prefer rooms with windows that open so as to better control our environment, however, we found the ventilation system to be wonderfully responsive and were quite comfortable day and night. The room was very quiet. We heard no hallway noise. One was aware of the background traffic noise from the nearby elevated highway, but it was not obtrusive, and we slept like babies, The room was spacious and well appointed, with plenty of closet space, drawers, and storage for a longer stay. The bathroom was very large with a choice of hand held, conventional, or rain shower. The housekeeping was impeccable and when we requested something, the response was immediate.
We had lunch in the Art restaurant which was well prepared, artfully arranged, and very tasty. We dined out that night and had a pleasant walk back to the hotel about 10pm, It was a beautiful evening, there was still activity in the area, and we felt quite safe. Room service in the morning was delivered exactly when they said it would be and was perfectly prepared. 
We could see the pool area from our room, which although small is a delightful space. It is well landscaped with a small pool, nice hot tub, open pit fire with seating, and food/beverage service.
We highly recommend staying here.

title: “It's a good location...”
text:
I stayed two nights at the Hilton Fashion District while spending the weekend in New York. We arrived around lunchtime and the front desk had a room available but gave us the option of waiting a little while we could have an “upgraded room with a view of the Empire State Building.” I’ve seen the Empire State Building more than I need to but I decided to wait for a better room. The bell stand held our bags while we were getting lunch at Eataly. We returned a few hours later and checked in. The room key cards don’t need to be inserted into a slot to open the door, just waived in front of a key pad. That was convenient for entering the room. I didn’t need to get the card out of my wallet to open my room door. The room was clean but real small…though probably typical by New York standards. The bed was comfortable, sheets were clean. As for the view, well I could see the top of the ESB if I bent down to look but most of the window was filled with the drab building across the street. If this is an upgrade, the standard rooms are nothing to get excited about. The shower was all tile with glass doors which leaked all over the floor, even during a short shower, leaving the bathmat a soggy mess.
Breakfast was included with our room. It was served in the restaurant on the first floor which is called Rare. For Hilton Honors Gold and Diamond, there’s a choice between a buffet or a pre fixe menu which included a choice of eggs, French toast, or pancakes, a side of bacon or sausage, toast or cereal and a few other items. We were also served a good sized fruit bowl that was really good. Having a choice to order from menu or buffet was nice, not all Hiltons offer that. I had the buffet one morning which was pretty standard for a Hilton (breads, cereal, scrambled eggs, sausage and bacon, yogurt). The next morning I had over-easy eggs that were good as well. Juice and coffee or tea included. Service was good both days.
The hotel doesn’t have ice machines available. We asked where they were and were told “this is a full service hotel. Just call room service and they will bring you a bucket of ice.” What they didn’t tell us was that there was a $3 delivery charge! Plus you’ve got to tip the guy who brings it, so you’re paying $4-5 for a bucket of ice. That’s irritating. There’s a Duane Reade right down the street which sells ice for only $2. Pick up one there if you really need it. 
There are three elevators, but one seems to be reserved for the rooftop bar. Either that or it just wasn’t working while we were there. We waited for a while for an elevator several times when we were trying to leave. 
The location of this hotel is its best feature. It’s on W. 26th between 6th and 7th. You’re a short walk to shopping on 34th, about a 15 minute walk to Union Square, there are several subway stops nearby, and lots of good restaurants. It’s centrally located and an easy walk to a lot Manhattan has to offer. 
I probably won’t return to this Hilton. There are better hotels in the area in this price range.

title: “Please please please don't stay here!!!!!”
text:
My husband and I took our children out for the weekend and we booked a room here
. It was terrible from the moment we purchased it. First the key was not working to let us in the front lobby so we had to wait on the cleaning lady to open it which was awful. When we finally made it to the room it was disgusting! ! The furniture was ripped the carpet had stains on floor and there was an old chicken bone on the floor not to mention the room reeked of mildew! The elevator was broken so we had to climb 3 flights of stairs. When we wanted our money back ( which we requested as soon as we saw the conditions of the room) the cleaning lady called the manager and the manager refused to come to the hotel to give our refund she said we could get it back the next day at 1pm because the mananger states "I'm not getting out of bed to come return their money they can get it the nxtday at 1pm" how feasible is thatwhen ur on vacation??? we ended up staying at embassy suites down the road which was wonderful!!! Luckily we did get our money back the nxt day at 3pm. Again DO NOT stay here!!!!!

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
A friend that had stayed there some years previous recommended hotel 17 to me. She said it was very basic, a bit gloomy, but very good value. I love a bit of value so we decided to stay there during our trip in October.
First impressions were mixed, everything seemed so small and dark, and the décor bordered on gothic chintz. But after seeing the room I was really surprised. Everything was clean (if not a bit battered), the room was fair-sized and the bathroom and shower facilities were great. In fact, we never had to wait to use them and I saw the bathrooms and showers being steam cleaned every morning and night. Most reassuring!
The staff were helpful and all of the other guests seemed to be having a great time too. The best thing about the hotel was the location. It was so close to Union Square and all of the shops and eateries on 2nd. Everywhere seemed so easy to reach, yet the immediate area was so lovely to explore. I pretty much love just walking around and exploring when I go to another city, and stumbling across the Flatiron building and the Empire State Building in about a 30 minute walk was marvellous.
I would recommend the hotel to my friends who, like me, appreciate a good location and great value, and don’t mind staying somewhere a little worn. I would definitely stay there again, and hope to do so soon!

title: “Adequate hotel - great bar food!”
text:
The rooms are very dated in this hotel. The furniture should have been replaced years ago. Overall the facility is in need of a major remodeling investment. Hotel staff was not overly friendly or responsive. When I arrived in my room I reported to guest services that my room was missing the desk chair. 3 hours later - still no chair. I called again and they brought a straight backed, non-wheeled, chair in about 5 minutes. Not what I would've expected for a desk chair but OK for the one night I was staying. The room was clean. Provided toiletries (shampoo, soap, conditioner, etc.) were much better than standard both in quality and quantity. I couldn't get the sleep number bed to do anything noticeable. Water has hot with good pressure. 
The bar food however was amazing at this facility. After a very long and tiring work day we decided to eat at the hotel bar and watch a baseball game. TV was large and near our table. The service wasn't the speediest but the food was amazing. Huge quanitities, good quality, fresh and tasty. We had nachos, a standard hamburger and fish tacos. The hamburger my colleague ate must've had a 1/2 lb of beef, a thick slice of ham, cheese, and an egg - all on an extra large bun. My three fish tacos (one order) were large, with fresh and flaky fish. There was no way to finish it all. 
Breakfast service the next morning was not good. Very overpriced and slow non-attentive servers. 
Neighborhood doesn't look the best, but didn't venture out for a walk so it wasn't an issue for us. Probably wouldn't stay here again unless there weren't any other options.

title: “My favorite hotel in NYC”
text: I am in New York for work multiple times a year and love when I am able to stay in this place. Most hotel rooms in the city are quite small - not Trump SoHo. The rooms are fabulous and big. The bathroom is also quite spacious. The staff is extremely helpful and will do anything to make your stay better. The neighborhood is also great with a lot to do within walking distance. Everything about this place is 5 star.

title: “Location and People-Friendly”
text: I spent nearly a week in 70 Park and was very impressed by the friendliness of all staff members. The desk and the concierge Kevin were fountains of information and couldn't have been more helpful during a very busy time for me. I found the rooms to be a good size (I live in Europe so that is perhaps one of the reasons!) and l liked the modern decor. My bed was super comfortable, too. It is in walking distance of Times Square, Empire State Building, Fifth Avenue, Bryant Park, Grand Central Station, and after all that walking, they offer cold lemon/orange water in the lobby. They also have a nice cocktail hour in the lobby, offering their guests a delicious light "sangria"- but much better than what I know in Spain as sangria...as well as wine. Breakfast is pricey, so I would suggest eating somewhere else. (Good diner a block away). I would definitely recommend this hotel and would definitely stay here again.

title: “Nice place!”
text: Visited over Memorial Day weekend. Property is just less than a year old and everything is very fresh. The suite with two queen beds was quite large. Love having the living room seperate from the bedroom. Plenty of places to eat just a few steps away at the St. John's Town Center. I'd not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Great for a weekend getaway”
text: We stayed here for a fun weekend getaway. The hotel is great, was quiet and the breakfast buffet was fantastic. There is a lot to do nearby with movie theaters, a mall and tons of restaurants nearby. Parking is free and close to the freeway.

title: “Very nice. Windows may not open.”
text: In agreement with other positive reviews for this property. I was eligible for an upgrade to an executive suite, but those were all full. My stay was for just a single night so this did not matter to me. I had a room just above the fitness room and just about spitting distance from the bar in the middle of the lobby atrium. The bar looks like quite a happening place, but I was too exhausted to check it out. The room was very quiet and comfortable nevertheless, but this interior location had no openable windows. Air conditioner was a bit loud and I don't sleep well with air conditioners on so I would personally not spend a night here again. The restaurants and service are all extremely good, and I would return for those reasons, but not to stay another night unless the windows open to the outside somewhere. Savannah Bistro in particular, has by far the best hotel breakfast that I've ever had in a chain hotel in the US. I had the breakfast buffet there. Dinner buffet was good too.

title: “Truely grand”
text:
Had a great time here. Nice design, friendly staff, who went out of their way to accommodate requests. The gym was way above average for a hotel gym, and the wireless internet worked flawlessly. 
I am a big fan of the location- plenty of stuff to do and see, spitting distance from Soho and Chinatown and right by the Subway. I will definitely go back.

title: “showing some age”
text: This hotel is in a great location of the city especially for dining. The hotel staff was superior! They were very helpful, friendly and go out of their way to assist. The lobby was very spacious and lovely but our HUGE room was showing signs of wear and tear. You can hear everything that goes on in the hall, and they can hear everything that you are saying in your room from the hall. I mean talking in a normal or quiet voice people in the hall can hear you. But in the sleeping area of the room, you cannot hear your neighbors next door. We were on the 21st floor with a spectacular view! The breakfast in the morning was terrific and the service could not have been better. We got a great room rate and that is why we were there.There are museums walking distance. But after dark the entire city is dangerous. The entire weekend we saw NO police. We did not feel safe anywhere around this hotel after dark. I would never go back to downtown Philadelphia again but I would recommend this hotel!

title: “Unbelievable small room”
text: This recently renovated hotel has nice staff and a very nicely done lobby. The hotel room was easily the smallest hotel room in which I have ever stayed. It was almost two small for the two of us. The bathroom is up to date and an efficient use of space. The room was very clean. The window faced the other rooms across the building, so the tiny room felt even smaller due to the lack of light. Would I stay there again? Yes, if there was nothing else around at a reasonable price.

title: “Wonderful downtown hotel”
text: The Conrad Hilton Chicago is a hotel with charm, class and provides a quiet retreat amongst the busy downtown Chicago hussle and bussle. Strategically situated on Michigan Ave, it is a location within walking distance to the Theater district and all the great shopping Chicago is known for. Mike at the front desk was very accomodating (as was all the staff). Take advantage of the special Pillow menu (we ordered the relaxation and cold/flu versions) at no charge. We have stayed at the Conrad for both a romantic getaway and most recently, taking our daughters for a family vacation. Highly reccomended for all!!

title: “Great staff/location, beautiful rooms, but thin walls.”
text:
We stayed here for three nights just before New Year's Eve and overall we loved our stay. The rooms are beautiful and elegant, and stood up to the standard of a Fairmont (I've stayed in many Fairmonts before). The only issue we had with the rooms was that the walls are quite thin and you can hear almost everything going on in the hallway (including loud conversations before 7am....). Also, any doors slamming in the hall can be heard too. 
The staff were very friendly. When their marketing manager saw on Twitter that I was staying there and looking forward to sampling some 'chowdah', she sent a personalised card and map, noting the four best restaurants for chowder. Really nice touch. The staff at the front desk were quick and efficient, and happy to chat about restaurant questions I had, and to find out how our days went and what we got up to. 
As I said, overall, it was fantastic, except for the thin walls. Despite that, I'd still recommend it.

title: “Nice business hotel.”
text:
I stayed at the Manchester Grand Hyatt for a conference and had a nice time. Had I stayed there for a vacation and paid out of my own pocket, I may feel differently about my review.
The common areas of the hotel were wonderful but most of my negatives center around the room itself. First, the carpet in my room had stains in several places. I recognize that the hotel is older and that, since I was paying the conference rate, I probably didn’t get one of the nicer rooms, but multiple stains just make the room look not fresh and not clean. Second, I had a few issues with housekeeping. My expectation is that new hotel size shampoo and conditioner will be provided at least every other day (although really it should be every day). I shouldn’t run out of shampoo after three days in the hotel. Another thing about which I am particular is the ice bucket; upon arrival, I filled the ice bucket (and bag) with ice. Of course, the ice melted overnight; my expectation was that it would be emptied and another bag be provided. Neither of these occurred. A final issue is that the rooms are not sound proofed very well. The first night I was awoken at 3 am by the next room blasting music; I called the front desk and this was taken care of promptly. However, on subsequent nights, I could clearly hear the phones ringing and people moving about in neighboring rooms. In truth, my quality of sleep for the entire trip was not good.
On to the positives! The location is quite good; it is immediately adjacent to Seaport Village and near the convention center (not as close as the Marriott which is immediately next door to the convention center). The front desk staff are wonderful as are the restaurant staff. I ate at Sally’s, AnneMarie’s, Lael’s, the Lobby Bar, and Redfield’s while I was there. All were good and the service was wonderful. Internet and fitness center access were included with the conference rate: wifi was quick and the fitness center was nice.
I also tried Kin Spa. They have monthly specials and I tried a facial and body treatment. The locker room was a bit small as mentioned in other reviews. The facilities otherwise and the staff were all wonderful. Yes, it was pricey but I expect that at a resort hotel. I would definitely recommend Kin Spa.

title: “Decent hotel and super location but NOISE is terrible !”
text: Can't fault the facilities, the room is good, service is fine but seriously avoid staying here until the construction across the road is finished or you're a deep sleeper, the drilling and jackhammers are incessant and continue all day and all night, while the noise is not the hotel's fault, reception does not warn you and didn't even bother to ask how our stay was, which was annoying, plus no offer of discount when this complaint was raised.

title: “A wonderful hotel in a wonderful location.”
text: This hotel is beautiful. The location is perfect...in the heart of everything! The room was very clean and a nice size. Front desk and concierge were extremely helpful. It was also very quiet. I traveled with two teenage girls and they loved the experience. It was also our first time in San Francisco and we were so close to all the main attractions and shopping! I would definately stay here again.

title: “Great location with a full kitchen at regular hotel price!”
text: I was going to NYC on business and wanted a nice room to relax in at the end of the day, The room was very comfortable and roomy, with a full kitchen, (fridge with ice maker!), and while the bathroom was a bit small, it was well laid out with everything one needed. The staff was courteous and helpful, and there was a free hot breakfast everyday! Walking distance to great restaurants and Times Square! And it was priced comparably to hotels without these great features! Enjoyed our stay and will stay there again!

title: “Wonderful Hotel, friendly Staff, pleasurable experience”
text:
My husband and I stayed at The Surrey for 2 nights and truly loved it. We appreciated everything from the chic decor, to the personable staff. I am a nursing mother and was worried about not having a kitchen to store my milk. But, when I spoke with the front desk they immediately offered to put my milk in their freezer. I knew this was a unique scenario and was somewhat embarrassed but they made me feel so comfortable. 
This trip was to celebrate my 31st Birthday and the hotel made me feel so special in wishing me a Happy Birthday. The only downside, small downside, was the cost of the room service. The food was good, but nothing about it really stood out. But, this hotel made an impression on me and I love the UES. I lived on the UES for 4 years so it's like home for me. 
This hotel stay was so special and we will definitely be back - my husband's family lives on the East Coast, and we are in CA so I am looking forward to our next visit!

title: “Do not believe the lies about the airport shuttle, the breakfast, the pool, the dining opportunities in general,”
text: I travel a lot and staying at the Ramada Inn North was possibly one of the worst experiences I've ever had. First of all I was promised the airport shuttle would be available...and when I called to schedule it they said no problem, it would come every hour. As a woman travelling alone these things are important to know. My flight got in at 8:30, the shuttle arrived @ 9:45 pm! By the time we arrived t the hotel, the dining was closed. Then I was told the dining room was only open when there were enough guests to make it feasible. No, there is no continental breakfast. The pool was completely green. There as no water in the fitness room....and I ended up being overcharged after all that! Nothing in the business center worked.

title: “Great hotel; even better price”
text: Stayed at this hotel one night since I got in early for a conference. If you stay here you'll definitely need a car, but that's not a problem because parking is free. On top of that, free wifi as well. They also offer complimentary happy hour but I wasn't able to take advantage of that. The location is good; right off the main highway into Austin and there's a lot of places to grab a bite nearby (Applebee's, Sonic). The room was amazing - it had a separate seating and sleeping area. The bathroom was cool - it had a soaking tub and a rain shower. For those of you that are pretty adventurous, you'll like that the bathtub/shower is separated by a clear window into the sleeping area (see my pictures). Overall, can't beat the great price!

title: “Great Stay -- Will Stay Again”
text:
We stayed at the Excelsior for a long weekend in mid-march. The group consisted of my husband and me and our friend and her boyfriend. (All in our 20s.) We got a great deal through Travelocity -- two nights plus airfare from Pittsburgh for $519/couple. My husband and I stayed at the Excelsior several years ago and enjoyed our stay. So, I booked without consulting tripadvisor first. But I got worried when I read some of the reviews -- had the place gone to pot in those years? NO!
The hotel is a solid 3* joint. It has a lovely lobby and the front desk people were very pleasant, despite the fact that the hotel was full. (The poor bellman seemed a bit overwhelmed, but was very professional nonetheless.) The hotel also has a restaurant which is very well reviewed, but we never got the chance to step in as we were too busy running around the city. I was quite pleased with our room, which I conclude was an upgrade from what we booked. (Our room the first trip, though large for NYC, was not nearly as big.) We had a two-room, I guess it must be called, suite. The bedroom had a queen size bed and the adjoining room had its own television (which I couldn't get to show cable, but I didn't call to see what the deal was either since I didn't care) and a pull-out couch. The linens were of nice quality, as were the toiletries left for us. Though I didn't check, our friends apparently had the same type of room on the other side of our floor. The desk and a few cracked tiles in the bathroom did show some limited signs of wear -- but certainly not unattractive. I think the only reason I even noticed was because of some of the reviews I'd read on this website. 
Oh, and for the reviewer complaining about the street noise -- are you kidding me?! It's New York! While I didn't notice ANY street noise at the Excelsior, I certainly expect some when I have a street-facing room in NYC!
The hotel is in a great location. (I personally prefer to stay out of midtown b/c it's just not my scene.) There is a subway station at the end of the block, as is Central Park. The natural history museum is right across the street. We found things we want to do well within walking distance. (For example, we walked from Rockefeller Center through the Park to the hotel, which a stop at the Shake Shack to be a fun afternoon activity. If you stay at this hotel, you must stop at the Shake Shack!) 
All in all, the four of us were perfectly pleased by our stay. (It would have been a good deal even at much higher price!) As it turned out, I stayed an extra night in the City for business, transferring to the Benjamin (Lex at 50th) to be closer to my firm's NYC office since it was St. Pat's and I knew the City would be a mess. While the Benjamin was a bit nicer, I wouldn't pick it over the Excelsior except for the reason that brought me there in the first place.
Also -- for your reference (since I find these things to be important in evaluating a review) -- I travel reasonably frequently for business (staying in Hyatts and Omnis generally) and have stayed in NYC many times (for pleasure) at hotels such as the Hyatt at Grand Central, the Millennium Hilton, Le Parker Meridien, and the Sheraton.

title: “The Good, The Bad & The Ugly...”
text:
The Good:
I stayed at this hotel over a 2 week period in June '08. The first week was spent in a King Suite, and there was really no problems that could be mentioned other than the soaps and things were not restocked fully each day (no big deal!).
The Bad:
The second week was spent in a Double Double room. First thing to mention is the double beds are tiny. They may be okay for kids, or smaller people, but I found them very small, and certainly would not work for 2 people at all. This second stay was a complete joke! First thing that was wrong, was that the shower did not have hot water for the first 2 days of the stay. I had spoken to the manager on duty the first morning and maintenance was sent out, but the second morning the temperature of the water was the same... ICE COLD! I ended up speaking to the general manager, who was USELESS, she promised to to return my calls and never did. The assistant manager John finally resolved the problem. 
The Ugly:
There was NO internet in the rooms ALL WEEK! I realize or some this may be no big issue, but being there on business with no access to email and the internet was crazy! I was shocked that they could not resolve this problem the entire week, and every time I would call they would say, "Still working on it!".... Shocking! I would not wish my second stay at this hotel on my worst enemy, it was painful from start to finish...

title: “New, close to all attractions, helpful staff”
text: This is a new and comprehensive facility with all the best views of the mountains, city and close to the perfoming arts centers, the sports venues and the variety of local eating establishments, all within walking distance. The amenities are very good, comforting spa services, and their resturant has an excellent Chef and menu. Adults and families with children will find this the best choice if coming to Denver, no matter to if you stay in the city or as a staging for visiting the close by mountain attractions.

title: “Decent but didn't wow me”
text: We are Starwood Gold Preferred card holders so we were upgraded to the executive room which turned out to be really was nothing that special. It seemed like any other standard room except they provided a bathrobe. The room was very clean; the duvets and bed also comfortable. The blue airport shuttle was prompt and serviced a few other hotels too. We had a buffet breakfast in the hotel restaurant which was $20 each but the most economical choice in the restaurant given that single entrees averaged $15 in any event. There is a new Starbucks in the lobby too. The check-in staff and concierges' service was very good. We got the room for $100 per night. I don't think I'd pay more than this for this hotel though. The lobby is quite dark and so is the lighting in the rooms. I didn't like that WIFI is $12 in the room (although it's free in the lobby). There is a $5 shuttle to Manhattan Beach from the hotel too. The outdoor swimming pool did not have any lounge chairs out as it was too cold.

title: “Surprisingly good and great Quesidillas”
text:
The usual Marriott styling leaves you unimpressed as you enter the cramped lobby, but what was a nice surprise was the huge dining and bar area. This was very busy and there are many alcoves, some with TVs to hide away or you could eat at the big bar on 3 sides.
Excellent Sam Adams on tap and we ate Chicken Quesidillas and wings, best we have had for a long time.
Rooms are large, clean and with big Marriott beds.
Not a bad hotel layover place.
Free Internet everywhere

title: “a LOL hotel!”
text:
I dont know if you can call this hotel ... the staff was really friendly and the location 10+ . really awesome and close to Times Square.
But what the hell ! The room was something like 2 meters x 2 and the toliet 1 x 1. Stinky with stinky carpet and there was a heater which was looking like it was going to explode in a couple of seconds (I slept with the heater off and -15 outside but no worries, the room wont get too cold). I dont know why I give 3 out of 5 to this hotel, maybe because experiences like sleeping with the bombs in Iraq and Syria are the ones I would give 1 or 2 points (even if it was something unique) but I'm looking always at the bright side of life and I'm giving a good review thanx to the staff (they even let me deposit the luggages for an extra night when I was in D.C.) and the awesome location. You are in NY why would you stay in your hotel room all day long?!
Obviously is not for long stays but for 1-2 nights is ok. Breakfast is included.
If you are on a tight budget, consider this place too (or sleep at La Guardia airport which is not far and safe lol)

title: “Value for money”
text: This was a good hotel, fairly central location. A large room which had a fridge and microwave in it which was very handy. The breakfast was sufficient with plenty of choice. The bed was clean and comfortable. The staff were extrememly helpful and I would recommnd this hotel.

title: “Nice hotel, just needs minor work”
text:
I was in DC for the annual meeting of the American Academy of Otolaryngology this past weekend, and just left the Donovan House yesterday. Due to the conference, I didn’t spend too much time at the hotel, but did get to use all of their facilities and wanted to share my feedback. As other reviewers have mentioned, their restaurant, Zentan was great; arguably the best sushi I’ve ever had! The rooftop pool and bar are also nice, giving you a nice little oasis overlooking the chaos down on the city streets. My colleagues and I were pretty unanimous, however, that it looks much bigger on the hotel website than in person. And it was empty every time we were there (every night) despite the beautiful weather outdoors…kind of strange. But they do have an amazing wine hour reception in the lobby which was a nice way to unwind and mingle with other guests you otherwise probably wouldn’t talk to. 
The rooms are about the size of your average hotel room, although some of my colleagues that frequently stay at Kimpton’s say the rooms are smaller than at the other properties they’ve stayed at. The room was cleaned well enough, but housekeeping forgot to replenish towels and basic toiletries almost daily (seems to be a recurring problem based off what I heard from others at the hotel). Besides that, the only negative thing I can say is that external light creeps in over the top of the shades in the room, so the room is never 100% dark, no matter what time it is (heard the rooms facing the interior don't have this problem, however.) And the Internet is SLOW! 
As for the staff, the only person I ever really saw and had contact with was Darryl at the Front Desk. He was clearly sick and congested with a cold, but carried through and assisted me and my colleagues with our millions of questions (and gave genuine answers) which we appreciated. There were several times that there was a line and he was the only person both checking people in and answering the phone, even though you could see several people sitting and joking around in the little office behind the desk. The Concierge Desk is hidden next to the Front Desk, but you can probably save yourself the trouble looking for it as he was never there (Darryl assured me that there actually is a concierge, he was just off. It’s kind of strange that they don’t have a concierge on duty 7 days a week for a hotel located in the heart of the American capital!) Another strange thing I saw was one of the other guys working at the Front Desk actually talking on his cell phone at the desk, and when he saw me, he walked away and carried on his personal conservation over at the Concierge Desk! And from what I heard, it was definitely not work related; very unprofessional! 
However, overall, I would give the Donovan House another try and recommend it to others. It was a nice hotel, has nice rooms, and a great restaurant. If the management could just improve those areas that I pointed out (practical shades, proper housekeeping, full staff, etc.) I think this would really be close to a five-star boutique establishment.

title: “Nothing Special”
text: Wanted to stay at the Holiday Inn nearer Little Italy, but it was book. So we were able to use Priority Club points to stay at the 6th Ave. location. Lobby was a hole in the wall and the room was no bigger. You could easily get claustrophobic in a space so small. Priority Club got us a room on the 21st floor, but that only made the wait for the elevator that much longer. Breakfast was miserable and high priced- oatmeal, granola with yogurt, tea and coffee came to $30. Starbucks was a better deal. After 2 days we were advised to have the key card rekeyed, but of course we got all the way up to the room to find that the key card did not work. Not near Times Square and not near Little Italy or WTC area. Really not good for much. Someone said that in a few years the area will be better, but who wants to wait. No service elevator so you have to compete with the bellmen and cleaning staff for the lifts.

title: “room problems”
text: Stayed here for a week checking in on 4th March 04. Check-in took forever. We arrived at the desk and were told the room booked for us through Needahotel was small. The room was tiny a single sized room with double bed. We had booked a double the u.s. equivilant of a superior room. We had to pay and extra $250 to upgrade. We had stayed here before but never again. Staff and management blamed the differing gradings in hotel rooms in europe. We were shocked In all our travels to the U.S. we never encountered this problem.

title: “THE PERFECT HOTEL !!”
text: We got the Penthouse Loft, can't imagine staying anywhere else!! We had always stayed at Hotel Belleclaire and they stopped caring. Got a great deal OTA Penthouse Loft and we have not looked back. The cleanest, most spacious room ever. Private terrace w/great views of the Hudson to the west and Central Park to the east. The walls were all windows so the view came into the room. The bed was lucious. Always had a hard time leaving the bed to start the day. Service was beyond excellent. The guys down stairs always had a taxi for us. All staff was very friendly and helpful. The 72nd Street subway is close by for Times Square or Soho or Littly Italy. We had supper at Serefina, there in the hotel and it was great, again great service and food. We will alway come back here. THANKYOU FOR A GREAT TIME!

title: “Excellent downtown hotel for a decent price”
text: Staff is uniformly pleasant and look for ways to please you. I especially enjoyed talking to our waiter Jose, although everyone was so nice you would think you were in the mid-west. Hotel room was very clean and Internet was the best I have had in a hotel. I wish all hotels had this quality of internet. The only complaint was my wife thought the street noise was too loud in our room.

title: “Little Gem”
text: I just got back from Memphis, my friend and I stayed at the Days Inn at Graceland. What a little gem. It is just about 1/2 block from Graceland, so we walked from the hotel to Graceland, that saved paying the parking fee at Graceland. We were delighted as soon as we walked in, the lobby is decorated so cute....all kinds of great Elvis stuff. The staff was great, especially Tracy at the front desk, so friendly. We had a room to the back, nice & quiet. The guitar shaped pool & the pool area that is decorated like Vegas rocked. The room was clean & spacious, the beds really nice. There was a safe, microwave and small refrigerator. The room also was decorated with Elvis photos & was very pretty. They include continental breakfast in the price. Any questions I had were answered by polite staff. We went just down the road for dinner at Marlowe's, it was a wonderful Rib place. They will even come to the hotel and pick you up in a funky pink caddy for free. I would come back again to this hotel.

title: “Great hotel”
text: We spent two nights at the lovely San Carlos Hotel, on East 50th Street in NY. The room was luxurious and quiet, and the staff was great. The hotel has a very gracious feeling and is unlike many of the other NY hotels that have a commercial atmosphere. The room rate was inexpensive for New York, because we were there just after the holidays (end of the first week in January). There is a breakfast room just off the lobby, where a complimentary breakfast of pastries, cereals, and yogurt is available, and it is completely kosher for those guests who require it. I recommend this hotel highly and plan to stay there again.

title: “Great location”
text: Stayed here for two nights in July. For a family of four the room was a little compact but perfectly manageable. The bathroom at first glance looked good but could do with some attention, particularly the bath. The air con on the landings outside rooms was extremely cold. We found that a lot of light came into the room from around the door but we solved this by blocking most of the light using cushions from the bed. The concierge was helpful, recommending restaurants for us and advising us on opening times of attractions. The public areas are very good, a great place to meet our friends. We also ate in the hotel restaurant one evening. The food and service were good, the view was wonderful, however, it was rather cold with the air conditioning. We had requested a Manhattan view, but didn't get one.

title: “Beautiful hotel with amazing service!”
text: We loved our stay at Hotel Palomar. The staff is wonderful, kind and always willing to help in whatever you need. The free wine hour every day is a wonderful little bonus. The property is gorgeous and rooms were spacious and very nicely decorated! The location is perfect near everything you could possibly need and very close to highway access for anything else. The hotel is in a very nice part of dallas and is near many high class shops and dinig. I highly recommend this place and will definitely return when I'm back in the Dallas area

title: “EXCELLENT FRIENDLY HOTEL WITH WONDERFUL HELPFUL HAPPY STAFF”
text: We stayed here this week . The Comfort Inn is a very welcoming cosy hotel. Well situated .The staff were very helpful. I left a dress at another hotel and they helped me to get it sent on to the hotel. The rooms were very clean spacious and comfortable. Breakfast very good too

title: “Lovely place to hang your hat while in New York!”
text:
Nestled in the heart of New York, the Excelsior hotel is a great value. 
It is right across the street from Central Park and Museum of Natural History.
The staff are a bit cold, but hey... can't ask for everything.
This hotel is great: a ten minute walk to Broadway (shopping and dining) and a 10-20 minute subway trip to other major city attractions. 
Nice place to stay while in New York!

title: “Wonderful Stay!!”
text: Staff was wonderful. Room was great - on 7th floor overlooking the river. Pool area was clean and well stocked with towels. Beautiful view at night from the balcony in my room. The only time on my vacation I jumped into the pool with my granddaughter. Had a great time. She and I enjoyed the water taxi to the Landing where there are restaurants located. Will stay again.

title: “Sophisticated and cozy”
text:
Simply put, this is a sophisticated hotel in a great location with a wonderful staff. We stayed in a Beacon Hill Studio on the ninth floor, and it was fabulous. I admit to being a sheet snob, and very rarely do hotel sheets measure up for me, but theirs did. The fireplace and surround sound stereo added to the cozy and romantic atmosphere of the room. (There are controls for both next to the bed.) The marble bathroom with rain shower head was also very nice. 
We were very pleased with our stay at XV Beacon and highly recommend it.

title: “Great Location...Highly Recommend”
text: We stayed at the Hotel @Times Square June 17 -20 based on reviews from Trip Advisor.. We are a family of four with 2 teenagers. We found the hotel clean and comfortable with a friendly staff and great location to Times Square. We thought we got a good price on the internet then they gave us an additional 10% with our AAA card on check-in. We were on the 11th floor and used the back elevator which was a little slow but nothing too bad. The breakfast was a great way to start the day, coffee, cereal, fruit, donuts, bagels and yogurt. Would highly recommend.

title: “Perfect!”
text:
I will keep this short as previous reviews provide detailed and accurate info. This was my first visit to NY and I requested a quiet room - with so much to do in such a short time I wanted to try to get some quality sleep - This is exactly what we got. The room was at the rear of the hotel and considering the location we heard NO NOISE whatsoever.
Hotel was spotless, the staff were marvellous and responded quickly to any questions we had before and during our stay. 
I would never consider staying anywhere else if I was lucky enough to return to NY.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
Booked 2 rooms for a 2 night stop-over on the way to LA, chosen based on Trip Advisor reviews.
Whilst this was one of the best and well appointed hotels we stayed in during our holiday, that was expected and there were too many problems and niggles to rate it any higher.
Main problem was confusion with the booking. Having trailed our jet-lagged selves around the sights of Philly and returned to our rooms around 5 pm, my sons (in the twin room) received a phone call from reception - if we were staying another night, they would be happy to take our payment.
As this had already been booked, vouchers handed over, etc, I had to drag myself down to reception to sort out, which they did do (front desk staff were polite to the point of obseqiousness). All sorted out ok but good job they weren't full; shocking administration.
Rooms were huge, generally clean, but I was able write on the dust on the window cill. Bathroom was spacious and well-equipped, but with a stupid double-door arrangement. Too many of the 'style' statements lacked basic practicality and didn't add up to much 'style' in any event. Lack of tea/coffee making a minus although there was coffee from the restaurant/cafe in the morning.
Our double bed was huge but had some sort of mattress pad which had 'memory' - or was just too soft - and was horrible for those like me who turn around a bit during the night. Give me a good, firm mattress any day. Also (and not alone) was the 'fashion' of tons of cushion, pillows, which when reduced to the basics left you with a small pillow which your head fell off when you turned over. Campaign for Proper Pillows starts here!
Public spaces - bar, restaurant, etc - seemed limited, there was a lawyers convention one night and a wedding reception the next which limited space for hotel guests.
Good location, close to shops, bars restaurants.
Not as good as we hoped or expected.

title: “Great for one or two nights but no more than that!”
text: The hotel is a conference center and also directly across from the hospital on Georgetown University's campus. You should only stay there if you have hospital, University, or conference business. It is not for the sightseer/traveler and NOT for children. It lacks most amenities but it is still well-appointed, nicely furnished, and clean. It is a 3/4 mile walk one way to the main street nearby so keep that in mind although walking through campus and the beautiful Georgetown row houses is a treat. Watch the cobblestone sidewalks - they kill the feet! Because the hotel is at the end of an alley tucked into a corner, it is very quiet so a good night's sleep will be had by all.

title: “Fabulous Hampton Inn, super clean rooms”
text: Rooms are extremely clean. Room was also very quiet, and we had a very good night's sleep. Room interiors and lobby are updated and very nice. They are working on the exterior, although I hardly think it needed it. The lobby is very clean and organized as well. The front desk staff is very friendly and helpful. Breakfast is excellent, a good variety of food, compared to other Hampton Inn breakfasts. They keep a nice selection of lemonade, water , teas and coffees in the lobby throughout the day. This is probably the nicest Hampton I have been to, and I've stayed in about 10 different properties throughout the country. We would definitely stay here again, even if it is a short freeway's drive to other attractions.

title: “A clean, quiet option for the frugal traveler”
text: Located in lower Manhattan, one of the oldest parts of NYC, Club Quarters WTC is a modern reasonably priced hotel that more than met my needs. The room was quite large given the $125 price and spotlessly clean. This part of Manhattan is an archetecture lover's dream with some of the oldest buildings in NYC. True, it is far removed from most NYC landmarks and tourist spots, but they are all a subway ride away or, in , my case since I love to walk, I explored many areas by foot. I stayed on a weekend so there was no WTC contruction going on, and the area is pretty quiet at night. I would absolutely stay here again.

title: “Very nice place--with an exceptional location & value for price paid”
text: Our 3-night stay in Chicago was for theater, the Art Institute, and fine dining pleasure (but this hotel should also be great for business travelers, judging from the mix of hotel guests in the breakfast area). Our room was very nicely appointed in a clean, modern style-- actually identical to one shown on the website; super-comfortable king bed, nice couch & ottoman by the flat-screen TV, fridge & microwave/bar area very convenient. The shower & bathroom were equally nice, good size, great lighting & storage shelves, great shower, etc. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit-- only two relatively minor flaws: (1.) on one of our three-night stays, the housekeeper neglected to empty our ice bucket & replace the liner, and (2.) the breakfast, while free, was fairly typical/average for a chain hotel, with rubbery eggs & common, sugary pastries/breads. Neither of these issue was a big deal, and we would stay here again without hesitation!

title: “If you like smart 'business style' hotels, this is your place...”
text:
We spent two nights at the Hilton Universal City. Overall, the experience was pretty average, but it does serve a purpose.
Our experience was slightly marred by the fact that we turned up and they'd lost our reservation - then charged us a higher rate than we'd originally been quoted. They did put us in a lovely room with a great view of the studios and the hills. And it's very convenient for visiting Hollywood.
But all in all it's a fairly soulless place - and very expensive too. You have to pay for parking on top of your room, room service and telephone calls are extortionate and you have to pay for breakfast as well! It all adds up to a pricey trip.

title: “Enjoyable stay on the Riverwalk.”
text: Very nice hotel, rooms were nicely furnished/decorated. Noise from the street was a bit annoying since my room overlooked a busy street. Service was good as well. Hotel is right on the Riverwalk which was nice as well.

title: “Weekend Getaway”
text: The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The rooms were nice, but a little pricey for the quality. Great downtown location near subway lines. Awesome stay overall.

title: “Home away from home”
text: Great hotel, close to everything, always clean, great staff. They remember me by first name. Staff goes out of their way to find a room, get a room prepared for me. Good food selection in morning, always fresh. Room has everything I need and if not staff has got for me. Hotel has own promotions to enhance my stay experience.

title: “75 degrees is not a heated pool”
text:
If you don't want a heated pool in November, then read no further.
We were going to San Antonio for Thanksgiving and had one goal in mind- a heated pool for our 5 and 7 year old. The Grand Hyatt seemed ideal. It does have a great location and is close to the Riverwalk. Ever skeptical , I called the hotel in August to confirm that thepool was heated and would be fine for swimming in late November. I was reassured that it would be. Obviously, from my negative review this was not the case.The pool is heated to 75 degrees. Grand Hyatt, don't waste the money. No one was or is going to swim at that temperature. We talked to the front desk the first day. Nothing changed for our 3 day stay. Although, the rest of the hotel was fine this essential part was critical to us, and we felt cheated. If someone asks, be honest and don't tell them a pool is heated when it's only to 75 degrees. The parking is also very expensive at $23 a night. There is an $8 parking across the street.

title: “Well appointed hotel, mediocre restaurant, android staff”
text:
Good taste emanating from quality furnishings and fittings, mercifully free of glitz
Don’t believe the check in staff when told all the rooms are the same. Some suites don’t even have a bath. They don’t tell you that. They think you will enjoy traipsing around with a bellhop trying to find a room that meets your request.
The guest rooms are spacious but the public areas are draughty and cramped.
The bar is too small for a hotel of this size. Use of the adjacent seats and tables are only permitted for dining, even at 6pm when none were occupied.
It’s not surprising their restaurant is unoccupied. It gets a good review in Fodor but it’s pretty ordinary. It purports to be an Italian restaurant with pasta a speciality. Their Tagliatelle Bolognese was awful - pasta, cheese and a tasteless stale “meat” sauce heated together into a unappetising sticky blob. This isn’t cooking. It is mass catering. 
Allow at least 10 minutes to get from your room to the foyer. This is because the hotel has only 2 lifts which for most of the time go up & down together like Siamese twins.
Outwardly the check in staff are relaxed and courteous. In reality, even if you are on their e-data base as a previous customer (I was), the staff show no interest in guests as individuals. This was brought home to me by their random allocation of rooms that disregarded my specific emailed requests. This was awkward and embarrassing for the other couple we were with, for whom I had recommended this hotel 
Beware when booking. Their email system is haphazard. On numerous occasions my reservation email bounced back undelivered for no apparent reason and my two follow-up faxes asking what was going on were ignored. This problem persisted throughout 2009.
It is probably no coincidence that when the hotel sent me an email asking for feedback after my stay, it signed off with “Kind Regards” without giving a name. There we have it, a hotel whose computer offers me its kind regards. There is no general manager in this hotel, or if there is he/she prefers to remain in hiding.
I sent my feedback by email and it bounced back undelivered. I then sent it by fax, drawing attention to their inaccessible email. Did I get a response? Nah. It’s a shame. Nice furnishings but all for nothing if the staff are robots (mark I version).
Since they are indifferent to my feedback I decided to share it with fellow members of rip Advisor
I won't be returning to this hotel

title: “Perfect Location!”
text:
This is probably one of the best located hotels in New York! You are right in the heart of Times Square with all the big Broadway shows within literal walking distance out the front door. 
I would stay here again and would recommend to others to stay here as well. You can't beat the location!
Why only three stars??? I went on Priceline and got our room for two nights for an excellent price. If we had paid the regular price for this hotel we would have been very upset. We had a corner room with an excellent view but you could clearly see as you walked into the room all the damage that had been in the wall because of all the plaster. It was not a very professional job. Also the carpet was torn up or frayed in spots, there was a yellow stain on the wall by the toilet, hair that was definitely not mine or my husbands on the floor and tub of the bathroom, and there were stains on our sheets at the head of the bed. 
The biggest problem though was that we got charged a second time for our stay! I have been told that this will be remedied right away and am waiting to see the charge come off my bill in the next couple of days. In this regard they were quite helpful.
Internet is $15/day.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: The hotel is located centrally in midtown...easy access to all NY has to offer. We lucked out and got a corner room with a balcony (no access however), but the extra light coming into the room was great. Also, since it was a corner room, it was pretty spacious. The bathroom was small, but adequate. Overall the room was clean and well maintained and no beg bugs! I know these bugs have been an issue for NY hotels. We didn't try the restaurant on site, but we did go to the lobby lounge which served up great small bites in the evening and had a DJ on Fri and Sat night. The atmosphere is very inviting...pretty hip and fun. Whiskey Blue is another alternative for a bar, but you'll find the lobby bar area much more exciting. The service is excellent...they are a stickler for "whatever whenever" you wish for. Staff was even willing to run to the store for me for an emergencey purchase. We tried to book the Acura car but timing didn't work - apparently the car service is a separate concierge from the hotel concierge. It was a great weekend at the W. I would definitely go back.

title: “Tired and True”
text:
A property that is feeling its age, but with spacious rooms and a good location.
I had a great deal of difficulty on connecting to the Internet, and eventually gave up, using my I phone in stead of my computer.

title: “Amazing!”
text: I've stayed at many of the nice hotels in Boston over the years but have never experienced service like this. Every person that we dealt with went out of their way to make sure we were enjoying our stay. Our room was wonderful, too. We had a great view of the harbour (and I especially loved the in room espresso machine!) I'll definitely stay here when I return to Boston!

title: “Worth every penny”
text: My husband and I stayed in this hotel for new years eve and had a wonderful, wonderfl time. The room was beautiful and the service phenomenal. I had a massage at the spa and met my husband afterwards in the pool. The pool facilities are amazing - i wanted to spend an entire day in the locker rooom. They had fluffy towels, a menthol steam room and fancy bath products in the HEALTH CLUB showers. Back at the room we had a huge bathroom with tub and double shower. There were Molton Brown products there as well. The bed was divine and there was a remote control next to it on both sides that controlled the drapes and lights in the entire room. There was a welcome bag with little treats when we got there. The next morning i had breakfast with girlfriends in the little cafe next door which was wonderful, too. One of the best new years eves I have ever had.

title: “5 Star Rating”
text: I would highly recommend the Intercontinental Chicago Magnificent Mile Hotel. We've stayed there many times. The view is awesome, the attractions are within walking distance. And if you fall in love with a particular room...well they can help you out with that too. Lizette Marin has helped me for three years stay in our favorite room. She is awesome! The hotel is magical at Christmas time it is absolutely beautiful. I

title: “Prime Location”
text: Fantastic location, rooms very cosy, shame about the nosiy air con. The hotel has a old fashioned look about it which is very pretty. Breakfast is coffee and muffins in the reception area. Would definitly stay again!

title: “Comfortable, predictable and very spacious”
text:
I regularly stay here on business. I like it because the rooms are spacious and comfortable, the place is QUIET and there are never any suprises. This hotel never seems to be very busy during the week and I like that. The rates are generally low compared to similiar properties with smaller rooms. The furnishings in the lobby, hallways and rooms are a bit outdated, but in an old-fashined, comforting kind of way. The beds themselves though are modern and superior; very comfortable.
I love that it has self-parking instead of valet-only (common in San Diego); rates were $18 / day at the time of this writing. Car-sickness sufferers beware: parking is on the 11th floor of the parking structure - and it's a long and curvy route to get there; I always drop my girlfriend off at the bottom and have her meet me in the lobby (12th Floor).
The staff has generally been courteous and efficent; the food is standard fare and adequate; nothing to write home about. The windows open a couple of inches which is great on warm nights.
As far as I have seen, all of the suites are pretty much the same. The top three floors (25-27) gets you bathrobes and additional toiletries.
One word of warning: check your bill. I have had problems incurring unwarranted charges. Once I was charged for a night that I cancelled per hotel policy; once I was charged a higher rate than was on my confirmation; and once I was charged for minibar items that I didn't consume. All charges were refunded promptly when I brought them to their attention.

title: “Close to everything!”
text: Went to Memphis this weekend and stayed here. Nice place! Loved sitting on the balcony enjoying the music of Beale Street! Just wish breakfast was served later than 10 a.m. after late night on Beale!

title: “GREAT STAY!”
text: Was in the city for the night, and having searched the Internet for the best services for the price -- this hotel topped the list. The staff was professional and courteous. The room was clean and comfortable, and the breakfast was more than we expected. As a matter of fact, I am in the process of revisiting the city and will be staying at the exact same location -- it's worth the few xtra $$$ for superb customer service, comfortable room and sense of security. Super 8 Motel @ 8128 North Interstate 35 -- see ya soon!

title: “Great nights sleep”
text: We picked this La Quinta because of the reviews, the price and an online coupon. The desk clerk said that the property was only 3 years old. It looks nice, but is already shwoing signs of deffered maintenance...not a good sign (carpeting in our room was torn up, like the vacume cleaner ate it). Their waffle maker is in the shape of Texas, imagine that! We felt the breakfast was 'cheap' and not the quality we expected. I didn't like the fact that the desk clerk insisted on a copy of my drivers license. I guess that looking at it wasn't good enough. There is only parking on one side of the building, which wasn't very convenient. The hotel is hard to find along I-20. We had to look for it each night we came back to the room. It is behind Sonic and Luby's. All said, the rooms were very quiet and we got a great nights sleep.

title: “Beautiful Location, Nice Rooms”
text:
I stayed in the newer area of The Dana, and it was quite nice. I was on the ground floor and the room opened to the bay...delightful. The room was spotless and the furnishings up-to-date. As others have stated, you must have a car if you are going to stay at this relatively isolated property. But, hey, it's Southern California...of course you need a car!
My only complaint was that the free wireless did not work in my room (I guess you get what you pay for), so I had to take my iBook to the lobby for Internet access.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text:
This was our first time staying at this particular property but not our first time in New York, we love the area since its so convenient for us, the hotel room was beautiful, clean and very modern, the bathroom was huge especially for a NY hotel. The front desk service was impeccable as far as check-in and the friendly welcome we received. We had a great view of Times Sq and beyond out to the Hudson River. 
 We just booked another weekend getaway for December and it looks like this will be our choice of hotel again. Prices do run the gamut but the location is hard to beat if you want to be in the action.

title: “I love the Omni Hotel, San Diego”
text: I really enjoyed staying at the Omni Hotel in San Diego. I was there with a gal friend on vacation Sept. 2011to see the SF Giants play the Padres. We stayed 3ni 4days. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean and roomy. We did not know this but there is a pedestrian bridge that connects directly from the 4th floor to PetCo ballpark! Easy access and no lines to get in! We enjoyed the restaurant called McCormick & Schmicks! We had two meals there. Both dinners. The first meal we ate at the bar. The second, we sat in a booth. Both dinners were delicious!! We could not be more happy with the service in both the hotel and the restaurant. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone and will stay there again. The only disappointment was that the bathroom did not have any shelving for our personal items. No room to put stuff. No shower caddy either.

title: “Home away from Home”
text:
Great experience. This Hotel offers a very unique experience typical of W Hotels in general but even more WWWonderful. First of all the Union Square area is just electrifying with ambience and a more wide open feel than the more crowded midtown hotels. Much more of a European flair with the open Square with the open air markets right at your fingertips as you leave the hotel. Also for some reason the rooms are much larger than one would expect in Manhattan and larger than the other midtown W Hotels where I have also stayed. The staff was particularly friendly and it is obvious they get along with one another and there is a "team" feel to the experience.
