I have stayed there very frequently over the last few years and I have become a little sentimental about the place. No doubt! Give it a try!
Negative- The gym could have been a little larger and was tucked away in the basement but it had what I needed!

title: “Continues to be a great place!”
text:
This hotel is situated right in the middle of the theatre district. It's a great place to stay because it's so convenient both for walking, and riding the subway. The staff are attentive, helpful,, and friendly.
The room is nicely furnished, we had a great view of the town, the amenities are just what we needed. For that area of town, I believe our room was at least as large, if not larger than most other hotels. 
We did have an issue with an "odor" in our closet, but they changed our room the next morning, which was as quick as they could do so. (I didn't want them to spray anything in the room to just mask the odor, thus the room change was necessary). 
This was my third time in this hotel, and I'll definitely stay there again.

title: “Overpriced, underserved, out of date”
text: This hotel is quite expensive ($400+ per night) and yet fails to deliver on the minimum you'd expect from luxury pricing. The hotel room was fine, spacious even, but the carpet seemed dirty, and my room faced inward, which meant plain viewing into other guest rooms (and vice versa). Oddly there were two bathrooms, but each one tiny, dated and hard to navigate (no surface areas for your things, little room to turn around). Basics were out of place - the room didn't have a do not disturb sign and the power outlets seemed ancient and risky when I plugged in my laptop. Also, at that price point, does charging $12-15/day for internet access really make sense? The biggest frustration came the evening before my departure when I went downstairs to print my boarding pass. They have a dedicated computer and printer for that, which was nice, but the printer was not working. I asked the front desk person for help, and she pointed me upstairs to the business center (as opposed to offering to do it herself). So I went upstairs to try again on printing my boarding pass, only to see that all of the printers in the business center were also out of service.

title: “So-so visit”
text: The hotel is a little run down, the rooms aren't the cleanest either. The shuttle service took quite a long time even though we called twice so we ended up having to take a taxi. The employees were very friendly though.

title: “Great hotel and will recommend”
text:
We stayed here on a two-day pre-cruise site seeing trip. Staying at the hotel was myself, my husband and his service dog. We are both in wheelchairs and found the hotel to be VERY wheelchair accessible for our needs. Our room had a bathtub, large turnaround area in the bathroom area and plenty of well-placed grab bars. The sink/vanity and mirror were just outside the bathroom door. This was very handy for us both getting ready at the same time. The height of the bed was perfect for transferring in and out of our wheelchairs. The hotel also offers a courtesy shuttle which is equipped with a lift. There were plenty of grassy areas just outside the door for the service dog.
Coming into the room we were pleasantly surprised to be placed on the bayside where we had a beatiful view. I also was not expecting the wonderful balcony which was large enough for my wheelchair to roll completely outside. 
The hotel itself has a bright sunny exterior color which fit perfectly on the bay environment. Interiror, its public areas and hallways do need a bit of sprucing up and cleaning. Nothing major and certainly nothing that would keep me from recommending it to anyone. Mainly I just remember ceiling tiles and vents being dirty and the hallways having a slight musty smell. Nothing a good cleaning and air freshener system would not cure. The rest of the hotel was spotless.
Every employee we encountered was nothing but top notch and went out of their way to help. The first person we encountered was a very nice gentlemen who, after bringing our luggage, went as far as to offer my husband's service dog a fresh bowl of water and kept asking if anyting at all was needed. Shuttle drivers-nothing but helpful and very pleasant. Front desk employees were friendly and attended to the few requests we had with promptness.
We used the shuttle to go to and from the airport and the zoo. Both easy and pleasant experiences.
We ate our first night at Anthony's, a fish place just across the street. There is an outdoor area as well as a sitdown indoor area. We ate outdoors. Very reasonably priced. Good fresh seafood. 
We ate breakfast on the last morning at a deli just down the sidewalk. It was a full service breakfast with inside as well as outdoor seating. Again good food and very reasonably priced. Although it is the only meal we ate there, we noticed they did have a large menu offering all sort of deli sandwiches. Would definitely eat there again for a quick bite.
The purpose of our trip was a cruise. This hotel is directly across from the pier where the ship was docked. Upon waking, the cruise ship was the first thing we saw when we opened the curtains. We spent both evenings leisurely strolling the bay. There are a couple ship museums to tour and several local vendors set up along the bay area. 
I would feel comfortable recommending this hotel to anyone I know without hesitation. Its location and staff made it a great memorable stay in San Diego.

title: “Great Business Hotel and Location”
text:
Great hotel for business travelers. One of the larger rooms I've stayed in while in NYC. Good size desk, and no problems with wifi in the room (for a fee). The staff was friendly and willing to help. My room didn't have any type of view, but I'm sure some have great views of Central Park.
Will stay here again the next time I'm in NYC.

title: “A motel wanting to be a resort.”
text: The pools were nice. The furnishing is what you would see in a motel. Nothing luxurious about it.

title: “Great hotel and service! Will definitely come back!”
text: My Father and I stayed at The Iroquois for 4 nights in July over the 4th of July Holiday. Even before we arrived I had e-mailed the hotel for assistance in trying to locate a 4th of July cruise. Vanessa, the concierge, contacted me and provided several suggestions - one of which we took. She also provided us with a discount code for Cirque du Solei tickets at radio city. I cannot say enough about Vanessa. She was extremely responsive even before we arrive as well as while we were there. With regard to the hotel, it is beautiful and very clean. The location is great too! A couple of blocks to Times Square and about 4 or 5 to radio city. The subway is about 2 blocks away. I have been to New York many times, and this is truly the best hotel (service and location) that I have stayed at. I am looking forward to staying there again.

title: “Classy, clean, very central”
text:
Not an impressive building exterior unlike the Palomar across the street but starting from the entrance, lobby, hotel staff, bar, the sofitel frequent stay program (A-club), it is an impressive and comfortable experience. The rooms have a nice and spacious layout. The decor in general (bedrooms, hallways etc) is simple and modern (nothing fancy and French or antique by any means).
I have tried the luxury bedrooms and the suites and they are both very nice.
I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Good location”
text:
We have stayed in The Roosevelt Hotel on September 2011. Hotel is a little bit old, there is an uncomfortable smell in the floor we have stayed. When the air condition, which is very old, is on, the smell in the room becomes less. Prices are high, but it is average for NY.
The best thing about the hotel is its location. It takes 5-10 minutes walk to times square, 5 minutes walk to grand central terminal. If you like walking, you can visit lots of place by walking from the hotel including Empire States, Moma Museum, Times square, broadway, etc. Since location is very important to me, I am satisfied with the hotel.

title: “Excellent Choice, Location and Good Service”
text:
Stayed recently for weekend wedding and was pleasantly surprised by the good service and overall positive experience at this hotel. Had a very good group rate of $139 per night. We all arrived early and front desk did a good job of handling lots of early arrivals and special requests. The rooms were clean and very comfortable. Most of our rooms had windows facing inside so views were very dismal but no noise from the street to bother you. The hotel's location is very convenient for sightseeing but it is in a business area so weekends are pretty quiet. 
The rooms include both fridge and micro and coffee maker which I find very convenient. The hotel's pantry store was also very convenient -- we closed their little bar and then were able to buy a bottle of wine from the pantry to continue our celebration in our rooms. The night clerk even de-corked it for us. 
It was 98 degrees outside but the hotel was very comfortable
throughout our stay. Others have mentioned the pricey buffet breakfast and I would have to agree. We were kind of stuck there as we were meeting relatives and others in the wedding party for breakfast both mornings but if I were there on my own I would grab a cup of their free coffee in the lobby to wake up and then run down to starbucks which is a half a block away.
We did not use the metro (didn't notice the metro stop as a matter of fact) since we were all decked out for wedding activities and cabs were very easy to get. Loved the full service of the hotel with doormen and concierge being very very helpful. Don't be shy about asking the concierge for help -- he has a computer right there and he was extremely helpful.
This has nothing to do with this hotel or the specific location of the hotel but we all noticed the very high number of homeless people in DC. in general. Not sure why the high concentration but it was sadly noticeable. 
If you can get a decent rate I would definitely book this hotel.

title: “The Westin Copley Place to be!”
text:
We wrote ahead to let the Westin Copley Place know that we were coming for an all-too-rare family reunion, and they were kind enough to reserve a wonderful accommodation for our group that would be comfortable for pre-dinner cocktails and more! And comfortable it was...with spectacular 180 degree views over all of Boston! 
The newly renovated rooms and public spaces are Westin high style...no more tired or thread-bare for the Copley Place...this is top of the Brand! The WCP also enjoys an enviable position in Boston...literally connected to a wonderful indoor high-end mall, and nearby many fine restaurants, galleries & shops (think: Newbury Street and beyond!)
We enjoyed the SPG platinum complimentary buffet breakfast (with an option to upgrade to "full" declined, as the cold buffet was plenty.) 
The valet parking was a bit hectic around typical check-in time, but in their defense, it was a deluge out! Patience....
Thanks to all the management and kind staff for a wonderful weekend!

title: “Old World Charm”
text:
After checking out several small hotels, we booked a basic room with the Beresford Arms for a long weekend in January. After reading several reviews, I requested a room on a higher floor facing Jones Street because of traffic noise. The room we got was very nice, but small with a very small bathroom. We asked the desk clerk if there was another room available and he upgraded us (at no charge) to a larger room with two queen beds and a very large bathroom at the back of the hotel with a lovely view of the city lights. If charged this would have only cost us $10 more a night and I totally recommend going for these larger view rooms.
I loved the old fashioned charm of this hotel--the lobby is very nicely furnished with antique couches, chairs and desk with two computers for guest use. We took a tour of the Palace Hotel and the Beresford Arms is like a very mini-Palace. The continental breakfast was very nice, but lacked orange juice which I did purchase out of the well priced mini bar in our room but feel they could provide. 
The hotel is decenty located, only a few blocks from Union Square and about 6 blocks from center of city. Walking at night was not a problem although we were not out much past 11pm and there were always a lot of people around. 
Checking out was easy and they allowed us to store our luggage for the day since we had a late flight and wanted to do more shopping. Hotel personnel was very friendly and there is a board in the lobby with restaurant recommendations and discounts (be sure to pick up the Macy's discount).
All in all, this is a great hotel for the price and location and we would definitely stay again.

title: “Great pool, friendly staff”
text: We wanted a reasonable price and a hotel that would shuttle us to the airport early in the morning. The staff here was friendly and mroe than willing to help us with directions. We wanted to turn in our rental car the night before we flew home and this hotel provided us shuttle to the airport (only took about 10 minutes) at 5:30 AM. There are 2 computers for guests and they did not charge us to print our boarding passes (some hotels charge per page). The pool was a good size. We spent 3 hours there! I liked the stand up shower (no tub). Not sure if the beds were uncomfortable or if it was me, I just kept tossing and turning (could be because I knew we had to get up so early). Breakfast is provided from 5-10 AM so we were still able to eat before we left for the airport. Great bargain!

title: “Wonderful home base in NYC”
text:
I sometimes travel with my partner on his work trips, and in that capacity have twice stayed once at The Mansfield, and once on our own dime.
It's a wonderful little place - not spacious, but beautiful and functional as well. Very conveniently located to shopping and museums. Staff is very responsive, and the bar on the ground floor is a nice convenience.
The AC is excellent - this might sound like a minor issue, but in a good hot NYC summer it's worth noting.
On our first trip we were upgraded to a suite, and it was amazing. I felt completely spoiled. Truth be told, on the next trip getting the standard small room felt like a let down in comparison - but there's no place in NY I'd rather stay.

title: “Another business related sleep-over”
text: I have stayed at the Crowne Plaza on Market St. in Philadelphia several times in the past both for business and pleasure. This time I again stayed on a short business trip. I was able to have a top floor room with a king bed which was very quiet. The staff was very friendly, the room was clean, and I even won a free in-room movie with a scratch off card I was given on check-in. I just wish I had more time to stay and enjoy the facility instead of having to get up early and head off to work.

title: “Elegance as always !!”
text: Loved the Westin Waterfront !!! great lobby. bar, workout facility and pool. Service was excellent as always. Although I believe that the Westin at Copley Square is a better location for tourists, closer to shopping, bars, and restaurants. As always the heavenly bed is amazing and the bar was wonderful. Staff was extremely accommodating. As always Westin made for an excellent weekend get away !!! This hotel is across from the street from the Institue for Contemporary Art and next a convention center.

title: “Highly professional/friendly service supported by modern, sharp, clean Italian styling….. a truly pleasant and comfortab”
text: A sharp young professional team, welcome you to a high standard of service and comfort. The rooms are well styled and equipped; the linens are Frette (beautiful). The location puts you within walking distance of the best in NYC culture and dining, a great hotel, reasonably priced, enjoy Captain R McCall

title: “Fantastic value, good location - highly recommended!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights at the beginning of October 2008. 
Check in was smooth, and as requested, we was provided with a room on the top floor. The rooms are spacious and comfortable with a large safe (free of charge), tea/coffee making facilities, free wi-fi internet access and TV. 
Local calls are also free of charge. 
As well as the in room free wi-fi, the hotel also has 2 computers in the lounge area which offer free internet access and free printing facilities - perfect for doing online check-in prior to our next flight. 
The hotel provides free breakfast in the morning, which although did run empty towards the final half hour, was stocked with a wide varitety. 
In terms of location, this was our first visit to NYC and we found the hotel to be exactly where we would want to be. A short 5 minute walk to Macys and surrounding shops, a 15 minute walk to Times Square or just a 2 minute walk to the nearest subway. 
Hotel staff were friendly and attentive, and helped us to plan our routes around the city using the subway. 
The only thing I would say is the road the hotel is located on can get busy with lorries seemingly constatly driving along it. For this reason I would recommend requesting a room either at the back of the hotel, or a high floor room (the hotel is on 18 floors). 
Great location, brilliant value. Next time we visit NYC we will be staying here again!

title: “Quiet & Friendly”
text:
I just spend 2 nights at this hotel and while I had one minor problem with my room the staff at the front desk (especially Melissa) were extremely friendly and courteous and dealt with my issue in a speedy manner. 
The room was comfortable enough although the bathroom was pretty small but it was so quiet and for Manhatten that's something to treasure. 
The hotel is ideally located and I would have no hesitation in staying there again.

title: “Nice hotel, poor location, better when the construction is done.”
text: We stayed here 3 nights with our 3 kids on a family vacation. The hotel is clean, breakfast was awesome. The location is the only problem we had. Not near anything. I mean nothing. Not even a restaurant. The only thing near is rental car return. We got an awesome rate and had a car so in the end it was fine. The staff is great and the kids enjoyed the indoor pool. They are tearing down a building next door and the construction noise starts pretty early in the morning.

title: “Superior Service, Wonderful Experience for our Anniversary!”
text:
We had an wonderful experience at Le Parker Meridien in New York City. Even before our arrival, we experienced superior service. I had booked the room on the website at the regular rate, but realized later that I had enough Starwoods Preferred guest points to cash in for an award night. So I called the hotels, revenue office to find out if I could switch my reservation from cash to points. The person that I spoke with was excellent (I can't remember his name...maybe Jason?) He was very helpful and stayed on the line with me and the central reservation office until the sithover was complete. Thanks!
When we arrived at the hotel on the day of check-in, we were please to find that the property was modern and well appointed. I had alerted the hotel staff that we were celebrating our anniversary when I made the reservation and they pulled out all the stops to ensure that we had a great stay. From the time we arrived, every employee that we interacted with wished us a happy anniversary. Then, not 30 minutes after we got to our room, we received a lovely platter of chocolate covered strawberries and chocolate truffles with a nice note congratulating us on our anniversary. We both LOVE chocolate, so it was a welcomed treat :)
Our room was great. It was located on the 37th floor and we had a totally unobstructed view of Central Park. We sat in the window seat for almost an hour admiring the view. The hotel is conveniently located for anyone travelling to New York to experience the theatre and other attractions. It was not far from Broadway (a short cab ride of about $6) or from an array of well known restaurants. We went to the classic French Restaurant La Grenouille, which was excellent. All in all, we had a great time in New York and a memorable experience at Le Parker Meridien.

title: “Holiday weekend”
text: Good visit. Nice rooms. Beautiful public spaces but UNBELIEVABLY crowded with holiday visitors. As large midtown hotel go... it was a positive experience.

title: “Well located, funky, boutique hotel.”
text:
We stayed at Hotel Union Square from Feb 17-21 for a girls' long weekend getaway. I chose the hotel because of its price and proximity to Union Square and the BART. We were not disappointed when we arrived late in the evening to find the hotel was just a few minutes walk from the Powell St. BART station. The outside of the hotel is unassuming but the inside is quite stylish. It is a small hotel decorated in an art deco style. Our room (#308) was petite but clean and functional. This hotel is definitely not the most luxurious in town but the little extras (exposed brick, flat screen TVs, free WiFi, iPod docking stations) were appreciated. The only complaints were the teeny-tiny bathroom sink and the iPod docking station that was not iPhone compatible. The sink was so small that the floor would get wet when you washed your face. 
This hotel provided excellent value for money if you're the type who can live without perks such as on-site restaurant, gym or included breakfasts. I was expecting the room to be noisy because of the cable car on Powell Street but our room faced one of the side streets and wasn't that loud. Though I did wear earplugs when I slept. 
Bottom-line - If you're looking for a luxurious experience, this may not be the place for you. If you want a stylish, comfortable, inexpensive hotel in the middle of it all, give Hotel Union Square a try.

title: “Yourstay is the best place to stay in NYC”
text:
This was our 4th time to NYC. We usually stay in hotels, but this time after reading some good reviews on apartments in NYC, we decided to choose YourStay Broadway Apartments.
The building is located just across Macy's and a couple of minutes walking from the Empire State Building. We bought some food and we kept it in the fridge that was in the kitchen which was fully-equipped. We also brought with us some DVD'S because we knew that there is DVD in the apartment. My wife, brought her laptop, since she needed it for work, and we've been told that there is a wireless internet access, which worked great for us. The cables were free,and included all the channels (in the previous hotels we've been to, we had to pay for movies, but not in this apartment).
We used the Penn St. subway which was really close to the building, and had great time in NYC.
After this good experience, we will definitely stay again in a serviced apartments in the future, and we'll book again with Yourstay.

title: “Another Great Stay at the Beverly Garland Holiday Inn”
text: We were met by Keith, the concierge, at the front door and our check-in process was quick and easy. We were also given two complimentary drink coupons! Everyone was so friendly. The room was excellent with 4 pillows, one soft and one hard for each of us. The hotel was very busy with one wedding and another marketing event occurring but the staff was attentive and our service was quick and friendly. I would highly recommend the Beverly Garland to everyone. The best location and the friendliest people in LA!

title: “Great location for WTC”
text: Saw another review that described this hotel as "utilitarian" -- I would agree with that 100%. The room was clean and functional but very narrow. I felt like I was in a hotel in Germany. The room was very basic -- comfortable and functional but nothing more. Definitely a business hotel or room for a single business person -- not a family. The view from room 927 was of "nothing".

title: “My new go-to hotel in New York”
text:
This is a great hotel -- new, modern, beautiful rooms. I was a little hesitant about the location since this was a leisure stay, but I decided to give it a try and I'm glad I did. The main reason we stayed there was because it's one of the rare properties in NYC that allows large dogs. We were traveling with our 70-lb dog and most hotels in NYC have a max of 25 lbs. Conrad allows up to 75 lbs and doesn't charge an extra fee. Kudos to Conrad -- you'd never know our dog was there and he certainly leaves less evidence than most children! And as a bonus, their policy got me to try their hotel and we've now become big fans and will return even when we don't have our dog with us. I travel to NYC about 5-10 times a year on business, and will try to stay at the Conrad from now on.
The surrounding area of Battery Park City is great -- you have the whole west side Henry Hudson park, lots of green parks, playgrounds, waterfront restaurants... really nice.
We got upgraded to a corner suite through the e-standby upgrade program, for $70/night, and it was well worth it. Our suite was HUGE and beautiful. It was larger than most one-bedroom apartments I've seen in NYC.
You can't go wrong with this hotel, I highly recommend it.

title: “the small things mean everything”
text: Doubletree's new motto is "The small things mean everything", and this particular property showed just how true that is. Numerous small things went wrong with my stay that ultimately colored my perception of the entire hotel. I'd ordered a box of materials to be shipped to the hotel in advance, but there was no note on my account when I checked in that it had been received (this despite the fact that I had the name of the person who signed for it). It took two separate trips to the front desk before my package was finally delivered to my room. When I got ready for bed the first night, I noticed that there was no blanket on my bed, just a set of sheets. When I tried to call down to the front desk to ask for a blanket, I realized that neither of the phones in my room worked. I had to call on my cell phone to reach the front desk. The next morning, I found out there was no shampoo in my bathroom, which necessitated another cell phone call to the front desk. The first couple of days turned into a constant barrage of small things going wrong. If I'm going to stay in a postage-stamp–sized room in NYC with bad soundproofing, I'll do it at any of the other hotels I've stayed at that managed to at least get the small things right!

title: “really nice hotel,centrally located”
text: this is wonderful place to stay , walking distance of everything, good service clean well kept rooms, breakfast a little pricey at $18.00 , but good food.only draw back noisy due to planes landing and takeing off,but ckecked all major hotels in area are same noise wise, dont keep that from letting u enjoy hotel

title: “Never Again”
text: We stayed in this hotel in July of 2006 and we will never do it again. Our non-smoking room smelled of smoke worse than the smoking room our travelling companions had, the halls and elevator were filthy and we had several hundred dollars worth of shoes taken from our locked vehicle. There are no signs posted and their corporate offices refused to reimburse us because they do not consider the area high risk despite information to the contrary.

title: “Good value”
text: A special, original and nice Hotel, very good located, and very clean. Nice and helpful staff. A bit noisy outside during night.

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: We were in town for a weekend of shopping and dining and could not be more pleased with this hotel. Very clean, great staff and a great location. Couldn't ask for more. We had a little issue with some noisy neighbors one night but management took care of the problem and compensated us for the nuisance. You won't be disappointed!

title: “Absolutely Perfect”
text: This was the first time I visited New York and the location could not have been more perfect! I was steps away from Times Square!!! The hotel was nice, clean and felt very homey. The rooms were a little small, but I expect that in NY. Great staff and very accommodating with all our requests. I have recommended this to everyone back at home and I can't wait to come back again soon!!

title: “Loved it!!”
text:
Firstly a great hotel.
The sheraton was in a perfect location for us, pretty central and pretty close to the airport. 
Upon arrival we were greated by an amazing lobby, with marble floors and great lighting. The staff were fantastic, very helpful and the checkin was a breeze. 
We stayed in a standard room, which was fantastic, the room had 2 double beds and was great. I love the colour scheme of the room, and the beds were great!
The bathrooms were a different story, there were very dated and were not great, but the room really did make up for the bathroom. 
The sheets used by the shearton are top notch and soooo comfy. Another handy feature used by this hotel is in room check out which was great.

title: “A very nice stay on a cold night in Boston”
text: My girlfriend and I went to Boston on an impromptu overnight getaway. Being a Starwood member I opted to pick out a property in their realm, and they had some decent rates that night. The valet parking was quick and efficient both arriving and leaving. The lobby was full of a very loud, young party, but that was as noisy as the place got. Upon check-in, the clerk was friendly (and recognized my club membership). Most staffers you would run into in the hallways would greet you as well. We ended up in a 24th floor corner room looking at the Prudential Center from one side and the Christian Science HQ on the other side. It was the perfect romantic view. The room wasn't huge but it was sufficient for a couple with a king bed. The bathroom was clean and modern. Additionally, the wind was whipping and it was brutally cold that night, but outside of a stray siren or two at street level you couldn't hear the wind blow much at all, even given that there was a bit more window than wall compared to most hotel rooms. Given the aforementioned midwinter chill, we opted to walk to the connected Shops at Prudential to grab some dinner. We didn't really bother with any hotel amenities but the lobby bar looked nice upon walking by. Only thing that went wrong was our ironing board was pretty much a twisted wreck, otherwise the Sheraton Boston is a place I'd easily stay at again, especially in foul weather.

title: “Avoid the Hyatt Regency”
text:
I had not realised how down market the Hyatt Regency chain has now become – arriving late in Chicago from overseas with a Gold Hyatt Passport card and a guaranteed booking, they gave me a room which the “cleaners” had left in a disgusting state. When I refused the room the only offer was one where the bath room lights did not work. This hotel is large and impersonable, the rooms are basic and tired with a musty odour, better to eat at the many places close to the hotel or across the river.
Chicago hotels are generally of variable quality and conferences can result in large variation in room rates. Sofitel is a better than average business hotel, occasionally the Trump may have decent rates, but avoid the Hyatt Regency.

title: “forget cafe on the green”
text: The general service of the reception area and doormen was excellent. However ,the hotel is really let down by the poorly trained staff and money grabbing ploys in the restaurant Cafe on the Green. On 2 separate occasions our order was either wrong or incorrectly cooked. Having pointed this out the meals were taken away and returned still incorrect. As soon as you sit down to breakfast you are charmingly asked if they can offer you some fresh orange juice and coffee. When we get the bill we realise these cost 4 dollars each item. Thats 16 dollars for 2 people before we've eaten any food.Once we realised this we refused coffee and orange juice . The smiles soon disappeared. Are they on commission?We had noticed generally how well kids are looked after in the states but not at this hotel. One of the reasons we chose it was because they had a "kids programme". This meant receiving a backpack with colouring stuff and books. I was told they had run out because they had so many children staying. Where these mountains of children were I dont know because I didnt see them. If this is a feature of the hotel, doesnt someone check supply?Basically I feel this hotel is trading on past reputation. It needs to get its act together because someone has taken their eye off the ball

title: “Very convenient and reasonably priced”
text: We always try to stay at the Iroquois when possible. Very close to the theatre district plus convenient to anything in midtown. Hotel staff is very friendly (especially wanted to note Vanessa, Lisa and Bill). It's very comforting to have the staff remember your name when you return.

title: “Shag-a-Delic Suite - Loved It!”
text: Shag-a-Delic Suite was incredible! Staff was exceptional as always. Great location in Downtown Dallas, and the people watching... too much fun.

title: “everything you need”
text: new hotel, stylishly furnished and well maintained. huge rooms, big bathrooms, great location, close to the gaslamp district. all very easy-going and efficient. check out the rooftop bar on a warm night. great value!

title: “Heavenly”
text:
My job forces me to travel to DTW once a month from Los Angeles and I routinely stay at the Westin.
What else could a business travelor ask for? Great bed, easy access, respectable dining and nice gym. You will pay for the convenience, but it is well worth it.

title: “GREAT location, Perfect stay”
text: We were looking for someplace to stay near Pike Market and central to all of downtown Seattle but far enough away not be "touristy". Alexis was perfect. We got a great rate and then they upgraded us to a lovely suite. Enjoyed the hosted wine tasting every night, saved on our restaurant wine bill! Location couldnt have been more convenient to market, shopping and ferry to Bainbridge Island.

title: “Great views of the ballpark, some annoyances.”
text:
My family and I rather spontaneously decided to spend the night in Baltimore during a prolonged power outage in the DC metro. We arrived one hour before a 5pm Orioles game so traffic was bad. After fighting through the traffic we pulled up and were told that we better hurry to the garage if we want a spot as spots are hard to come by on game days. We then found a semi-legal spot in the hotel garage and were told that we probably would not be towed. This obviously was not the best start to out stay. But from then on, all went well.
The hotel is very clean, modern and looks nicer than a generic chain hotel. The view from the large gym and pool is of Camden Yards (the baseball stadium) and there is even a deck off the gym where people gather to watch the game. Rooms are modern, clean, and beds are great. The hotel is a good 4 long blocks from the inner harbor and one block from the convention center. After our difficult check in, check out could not have been easier or more efficient. I would consider staying at the Hilton again especially on a day when the Orioles are not in town.

title: “great location and helpful staff”
text: Great value in this hotel. It is walking distance to attractions including Empire State Bld, Times Square, Macy's, Bryant Park, NYC Library, Grand Central, Penn Station etc. The in room coffee and free breakfast (lobby level) was good and convenient for getting an early start on the day. The room was roomy, quiet, clean. The staff was friendly and helpful. The concierge was very helpful in hailing a taxi when we were using the taxi service instead of walking. The rooftop bar was great for happy hour (with outdoor heaters and a view of Empire State Bld). Overall a great place to stay and I would stay here again.

title: “Good hotel location is not ideal especially due to construction of the Freedom towers”
text: Very nice rooms and staff, expect a good solid Hilton service in a modern tower, however the construction in ground zero can still be bothersome. You will experience great views on the higher floors of Manhattan and Brooklyn as well as the new freedom towers. Would recommend staying there only when they have specials or bidding through Priceline as regular night price is the outrageous $500+

title: “What a Wonderful Place!”
text: I enjoyed my stay at the Hyatt Jacksonville very much. The staff was so welcoming and friendly that it was almost sad to leave them. The hotel is in a great location and it was fun to walk along the River and visit the Landing. The hotel was clean, good food and great service all the way around. The breakfast buffet was great and they use many natural ingredients and buy them from local farmers. Not a lot of junk food on the menu! Every menu item I had was great and I was there for a week so I tried many. I truly enjoyed my stay.

title: “This is a dump”
text:
I had to stay by the airport after last minute flight problems. It was a bad idea to stay at the Embassy Suites. The room needs renovating and even though I was checking in at 10pm after a long day and flight, the front desk rep took her own sweet time checking me in. Room service was pretty poor. I can't believe there are no irons?!?!
On the otherhand, the shuttle service was very speedy in picking me up from the aiport.
I now remember why I never stay at the Embassy Suites anymore!

title: “Surprisingly great and beyond expectation”
text:
Service was excellent for check in, lobby clean and desk staff courteous and kmowledgable. Room was small, but big enough for the two of us - Tv, and other electronics worked fin though number of TV channels limited. Location excellent on 46th street between 5th and 6th puts in the middle of Times Square, theatre, shopping, transportation, and restaurant availability also Moma and Rockefellar center.
Little bar on second floor was a good place to stop off for an night cap, travel desk was helpful in getting to airports and internet facilities worked with printer and paper supplied - liked the responsiveness of the staff

title: “Very nice!”
text: Stayed at this hotel on business. Very impressed with the spacious room and the excellent breakfast variety. Hotel staff was very courteous and helpful. Would stay again!

title: “Comfortable, spacious & convenient”
text: Good, comfortable, spacious, full-service hotel accommodation.Medium-sized. 368 Rooms. Mid-rise building. Conveniently and centrally located. Pleasant staff. Large, well furnished suite. In good condition. 2 x TVs. Coffee-maker & microwave. Hot breakfast included. Free happy-hour drinks and snacks. Free access to and use of computer room and its equipment. Negatives: • No free Wi-Fi.

title: “Definitely going back!”
text:
Finally! A great place to stay in Downtown Chicago that is affordable, clean, in a great location and with a superior staff! I couldn't believe the state rate was such a bargain, and even though the valet parking wasn't cheap, the service provided made it a good value.
The front desk staff on check-in was exceptional. Very polite, professional and friendly. We asked for directions and recommendations several times for restaurants, the lakefront, museums, and a local bar - all of their assistance was spot on. 
The guys at the valet stand were so helpful. We decided to go around the corner to get a bite to eat and asked them to keep the car close by so that we could use it afterward. They made the arrangements and did it all without skipping a beat. Though I would allow 15-20 minutes lead time when you call for the car from the garage.
As a Hilton Honors gold member, they upgraded me to a spacious suite with a king size bed in the bedroom, a full living room, and a kitchenette with a mini-fridge and microwave. The decor looked new and everything in the room worked great and was spotless. I loved the cabinetry they used (looked custom) and the granite countertops throughout.
The breakfast service was one of the best I've had at a Hampton. Lots of choices, including different selections for fresh fruit, and good hot entrees. Plus it's located on the second floor with great views of the street below. They had breakfast attendants who were responsive and helpful.
The doors to the rooms are not sound-proof however. But since I had a suite, the noise didn't make it through to the bedroom.
All in all, one of the best Hamptons I have visited.

title: “Great Location, Friendly Staff”
text:
CHECK-IN/ARRIVAL:
I stayed at the Baltimore Hampton Inn & Suites on Sunday August 19, 2007 with my wife and almost 3-year-old son. We stayed on a Hilton award night, so I can’t comment on value for the money. When we arrived, the valet parking was a little confusing; there was a little sign on a pole that explained the charges (Note, it is $28, not $25 as their web site indicates), but there was nobody around, and it didn’t seem obvious that you just stopped there. I parked at the curb and went inside where I found the valet guy. Check-in was simple and fast, we did so at about 4:45 pm. 
LOCATION: 
The location is good because it is only a short 2 block walk to inner harbor attractions. The area seemed ok during the day when there were people walking around to work etc, but I would be a little weary of walking around at night. Because we have the little one, we were back at the hotel by 8:00 so we didn’t need to walk around at night.
ROOM:
We were in room 627. The room was large but seemed to have a bad layout. There is a big space in from on the closet, but then the chair/ottoman is right next to the left side of the bed by the windows. It is a little tight getting in and out of the bed in the middle of the night in the dark. There is a desk with a standard office chair, a sitting chair with ottoman, king size bed, small “coffee” table, bench, and dresser/entertainment unit. The room has a TV small microwave, mini refrigerator, and coffee maker. There is no safe in the room. There is complimentary wired (cable provided) and wireless Internet access. The TV has pay per view and HBO, but only about 20 regular channels. The view from the window was an abandoned building (see photos). The room was quiet, not much street noise, but there were a couple of sirens during the night.
BATHROOM:
The bathroom was a decent size. Toiletries were “Purity Basics” brand, which I believe is a Hampton Inn brand. There was shampoo, conditioner, body wash, moisturizer, shower cap, shoe mitt, cotton balls/q-tips/nail file. There was a hairdryer as well. Water pressure in the shower was good, water stayed hot and the shower head was at a good height. 
RECREATION:
There is a fitness room and pool on the lower level. I didn't use the fitness room but it looked small and seemed to have an elliptical, bike, and treadmill. There was also a TV in the fitness room. The pool was an ok size for an indoor hotel pool. There was a very strong smell of chlorine when you entered the room. I was a little itchy after exiting. The towels at the pool are a joke, they were very small, not even 3 ft by 2 ft and very thin. 
MISC
The breakfast was pretty much the standard free continental breakfast. There was also a hot item, but I couldn’t tell what it was by looking at it. I think it was some sort of sausage inside an egg. All of the staff are extremely helpful and friendly. We forgot our toothbrushes and got 2 from the front desk.
CHECKOUT:
We had 9:00 am tickets for the aquarium so we checked out using video checkout around 8:30 to head over to inner harbor. We left our bags with the Valet. We came back around 2:00 pm to get our bags and car. Again, staff was friendly and asked us if we needed directions etc, while another valet got our car.

title: “Everything I wanted it to be for a first trip to NYC”
text:
Thought this place was great, great location, great service, clean
Rooms were small, as expected with NYC
Lovely little hidden gem
Elevators need some serious speeding up though

title: “Might be a good option”
text: The staff was very friendly. The room was was nice and clean. The breakfast more than adequate. But there are two problems. 1. Too far from a Metro station to walk ( they do provide a shuttle). 2. Hotel sits directly next to an Amtrac line. Wow! Talk about noise!!! If you get a room on the street side you may be ok. Otherwise forget it

title: “Ambience if you're adventurous”
text: I recently stayed here for three nights on business. If you are the adventurous type, you'll enjoy the unique experience this hotel offers. The concept of staying in a renovated train station has its appeal and I like the out-of-the-ordinary, so this definitely qualifies. It was fun exploring the building and viewing the vintage decor and train cars. Walking distance to all kinds of excitement in downtown Indy! Lunch in the hotel lounge was excellent, reasonably priced, and the room service chicken quesadillas I had for dinner were some of the best I ever ate. Staff is very friendly and helpful, a great crew! Fitness room was excellent. The king room I stayed in was adequate, the bed fair but I slept well enough. Wireless internet worked fine there although tv reception was fuzzy on half the channels. The room was on the side of the building away from the tracks, so noise from the trains was minimal. Other reviewers have mentioned the late-night noise in the hallways, and even though there are signs posted throughout reminding patrons of quiet time in the evening, there were still people (including children) yelling and running in the hallways late at night. In reality, people aren't always on their best behavior when staying at hotels, and let's face it, some people are just plain morons to begin with. I solved that problem long ago by traveling with a small fan or white noise machine to mask unwanted noise and I sleep just fine. Overall, this hotel may not be for everyone, but I enjoyed my stay and look forward to returning.

title: “Nice!”
text:
I know my title is lame but I don't know how else to frame this review. I stayed here for several nights with a group of friends and we had a great time. The rooms were within spec for me, perhaps not the newest, but clean and tidy. And the location was excellent! I loved being on Shelter Island. The locations is WAAAAY better than a hotel circle hotel I recently stayed at. They have a great pool...also free bikes(!) We got some bikes and biked all the way to dog beach and one of the best fish taco places I've ever been to (also on shelter island). We had a ground level room with a patio that opened out right on the Marina and hill beyond..what a view! At night it was truly beautiful. Large yachts right in front of you and the lights of the houses up on the hill...I loved it.
Also, right down the street walking distance is the Bali Hi. This restaurant is a must! The food and drinks good and the view and prices are great! 
I would recommend the Kona Kai in a heartbeat. I can think of several worse places to stay in SD off the top of my head but honestly none better.

title: “Needs updating badly”
text: We stayed recently for a conference and were a litle disappointed in the shape of the hotel. It is a little worn for the calibre of the hotel chain. I would stay there again, but I wouldn't make it a point to stay there for a vacation nor would I probably recommend it to family.

title: “On your own”
text: I booked an overnight at LAX Radisson, for our return from Fiji. Feb 14, we arrived around 1pm after a long flight, we could not check in it was too early. They told us we could sit in the lobby and wait. One of the employees suggested we might want to get on the trolley and go to the beach, have lunch. He gave us a schedule we went out to wait for the trolley. The schedule time and the arrival time of the trolley was about 40+minutes different. We waited, not having anything else to do. Had a great meal returned to the hotel about 4pm. We collected our luggage from the front desk, they placed it on a dolley and had the nerve to ask if we could get it, or "do you need any help". By this time I was ready to go to my room and collapse, and I wasn't about to tip anyone for their help at this point. Next time I will go for the trip straight home forget the overnight to relax. I thought the room was nice but the service was so poor it overshadowed everything else. BGP

title: “Elegant, but has seen better days”
text:
I booked this hotel last minute for $160 on hotwire ($190 including taxes), and what a phenomenal deal this was! Great midtown location, and I even got a nice corner room. I was also happy with the coffee maker in the room, the assortment of magazines, my choice of the NYTimes/Sun/FT newspaper in the morning (though you have to pay extra for the WSJ !!! - which should be blasphemy in this midtown location). 
However, the bathroom seemed a little shabby, it smelled like bleach, the room seemed bare, and as other reviews have mentioned my towels as well were stained and threadbare - just not what you would expect at a hotel like this, and certainly not at the prices I saw on its website or even other travel sites like travelocity. The people at the front desk were efficient but not especially friendly, though the bellmen were awesome. 
One gripe I have with all these so-called luxury hotels is the prices they charge for internet in the room - highway robbery! - but at least here, it was free in all the public areas and lobby. 
I would highly recommend it for the price I paid; I am not sure how it compares otherwise.

title: “Good Stay”
text:
I recently went up to San Fransisco to visit some friends and family but was on a budget and wanted a hotel or inn I could feel comfortable in, was cheap enough and didn't have shared bathrooms. I found it in the Bay Bridge Inn. 
Upon arrival I was greeted by the owner who was very nice and welcoming. I did have to wait for housekeeping to finish for a while, but it was fine as I just walked across the street to the am/pm market. The owner was friendly and outgoing and was nice enough to give me a map and detailed the best places to go, places to avoid and the best times to visit certain areas. The room was average and could use a fresh coat of paint but was overall very clean and tidy. There was an ironing board and iron in room which was a relief as I packed a bunch of dresses that were wrinkled! The area is okay with clean residential areas surrounding the inn, but if you are female traveling alone like I was and getting off the BART at Powell street (the nearest exit) I highly suggest paying the $6.50 cab fare to arrive at the hotel safely. I didn't at first and it was not that pleasant and I learned my lesson. 
Recommend the hotel and was the best room for my budget and I have no complaints.

title: “Good location, clean, comfortable rooms, great staff”
text:
Flew into Chicago the on July 14, 2012 and stayed two nights at the Fairfield. From O'Hare Airport, my friend and I took the subway to the hotel. Since we arrived around 9:30AM a room wasn't yet available, but "Bianca" was very friendly behind the desk and checked our luggage. When we returned around 4:00PM (took in a ballgame at Wrigley Field in between) we were informed that our request for a single room w/ two double beds could not be accommodated...so we were given an upgrade at no additional charge to a one bedroom suite (Room 1405) with a king-size bed and pullout sofa - a kind and much-appreciated gesture by the staff!
PLUSSES:
-clean, comfortable suite with two televisions and free internet access
-excellent adjustable air conditioning!
-great water pressure in bathroom
-genuinely welcoming and helpful staff (again, a big thanks to Bianca in particular)
-plenty of restaurants, entertainment and subway access within walking distance
DRAWBACKS (not much to complain about...minor criticisms):
-while the bathroom was clean and had great water pressure, it would have been better with a draw fan
-internet connection could have been a little faster, but was still acceptable
Overall, My friend and I enjoyed a great stay at this location. 'Hope to do it again.
SUBWAY DIRECTIONS FROM O'HARE: Take the Blue Line, transfer at Jackson, then take the Red Line three stops north to Grand. Walk two blocks north to Ontario Street, then about five blocks east. Fairfield will be on your left. Approximate commute time, walk included, should be about 60 minutes.
ADVICE: If traveling to/from hotel by subway, roller bags are highly recommended - it makes the walk considerably easier, especially on hot days.

title: “Decent stay but nothing stands out”
text:
Stayed a couple of nights at hampton Inn, Devner speer Blvd in August 2011.
On arrival was welcomed & promptly checked in. we were placed in a room overlooking the busy road and at times there was noticable traffic noise - not a deal breaker but for those sensitive to noise it worth asking at checkin where your room is located in the building.
Location: 
Convenient for Denver (if you have a car as we did) and this hotel offers reasonable rates as its not directly in the city centre.
Room:
Was very clean, bed was comfy. 
TV was flatscreen. 
Breakfast:
I know recent comments are very positive in regards to the breakfast but when we stayed in August the breakfast was in my opinion just a bit underwhelming/functional - lots of refined carbs, high sugar options, the limited fruit options had seen better days - ended up with an english muffin & peanut butter. 
Staff were very friendly though.
Hotel offers free parking which is much appreciated but the parking lot was full and the overspill area was dimly lit - I was with my other half but would have been a bit hesitant parking there alone/at night.
There is a pool which we did not use but it looked clean.
Check out was very efficient

title: “Clean and Great Locations”
text: The room was very clean, front desk staff at check in not very friendly almost rude. Bellman and the gentleman that helped store our bags and called a taxi on check out day, was fabulous, friendly and courteous. NO in room coffee... continental breakfast 13 dollars... I would stay again, but would bring a small kettle and coffee with me. There is a starbucks around the corner for anyone requiring coffee as soon as your eyes open. The location is fantastic.

title: “The Perfect New York Getaway”
text: I spent Mother's Day in NY visiting family, and had one of the most relaxing stays I've ever had in New York. I travel to New York often, but this was my first stay at the Roger Smith. The room was spacious and quiet. I didn't need much attention, but the staff was always helpful and friendly. I attended several Broadway shows, and enjoyed the short walk to Times Square each time. With a great breakfast each morning in their restaurant, and a comfortable room, I will most definitely be staying at the Roger Smith in future.

title: “Old fashioned interior, smelly room”
text:
When we entered our room (third floor, back side) it smelled a like deep-frying pan had been used. When I opened the curtain, the 'view' was on the hotel's airco machinery. The smell became also clear: there's a McDonald's on the (back)side of the hotel.
We asked for and got another room. It was larger and there was no smell. There was also a small kitchen, but it looked like it was built in the 70's, and not renovated since then.
Some more bad stuff:
- You have to pay for Wifi in your room. 
- The lobby looks like from the 70's.
- I could't find out how to turn off the bed light other than pulling the wire out of the wall socket
Now the good stuff:
- The door men are quite friendly
- On the 2nd floor there is a quite nice and modern area where you can have coffee and free wifi.
- Hotel's location is quite good
So you can probably get a better deal than this hotel.

title: “Bathroom needs an overhaul.”
text:
When we arrived everyone was attentive. The lobby has a fire going and the atmosphere was welcoming. The bedroom area was neat and clean. The closet was quite large. 
When we looked at our bathroom we were shocked. The tub was stained gray and had streaks. The caulk and grout showed mildew or worse. There were tiles missing from the bathroom floor. Paint was peeling from the bathroom walls. We at least expected a clean bathroom in good condition.

title: “Defines the best of boutique hotels”
text:
Stayed here for a great week in 2008. Searched for another place to try in 2009 but, after not finding a better combination of price, location and quality, returned for another week in 2009. We were not disappointed as overall presentation of the property remains superb and cannot see how location could be any better. If anything staff were even friendlier than last 
year and continue to deliver a high level of service in many small ways.
I would agree with another reviewer that the air conditioning output could be improved upon and water flow from the shower head was a bit low but these could in part be connected to green initiatives and did not detract significantly from overall stay. The in room WiFi was a great plus and allowed use of my iPod touch when searching for tourist info and restaurants. Will not bother looking elsewhere in future as this is hotel of choice for San Francisco.

title: “Nice enough, but not perfect”
text:
My husband and I spent one night with two children at the Renaissance. It's in a great location - directly across from South Park Mall - and is nice overall . The rooms are well decorated and the public areas (lobby, dining, bar, indoor pool and workout facility are nice.) The breakfast inclusive rate is worth it, especially with children - there's a generous buffet and you can also order omelettes and waffles along with the buffet. Every staff member went above and beyond - the service was close to what I usually find at a Ritz Carlton.
However it's not perfect - the bathroom was fairly clean, but not spotless, and the beds were too soft for our taste. The double/double rooms are small, and we had a room close to the elevator and vending which was extremely noisy.
Since it was so reasonable ($109 including breakfast for the 4 of us), I'd recommend it, but I'd ask for a room away from the elevator, or perhaps try a suite for about the same price at the other Renaissance near the airport/coliseum.

title: “Wow! Loved it!”
text: Very nice location, not much shopping, but in nicer area of Dallas. Little Oasis--when you step into this hotel it feels like you are in a dream! The decor is comfortable and trendy. The pool is a great place to relax. Mist spraying fans are all over the place and a bar with waitresses. They even can put a plastic cover over the pool and have a party outside. Trendy place for nightlife. The food is amazing!!! Attracts a very pretty/hansome crowd. Staff is very accomodating and not at all high priced. Love it!

title: “Substandard”
text: Although the basic functions of the hotel were working (lights, roof, bed, bathroom) this hotel is clearly working through significant management issues. The staff were very friendly but clearly untrained and overworked. The location of the hotel is on the fringes of downtown and hiking distance to museums. I did not feel comfortable walking into the park during the daytime just one block away due to a significant homeless population.

title: “Expected more from Hilton”
text: This Hilton needs a facelift! Although we got a reasonable group rate, it was not worth the money. The breakfast buffet was horrible. The parking was very inconvenient. The heater didn't work. The shower was dirty. We expect more from Hilton.

title: “Great place to stay for visitors to Washington”
text: Must be the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in, great choice at breakfast and a lovely part of town. Near Georgetown and the National Cathedral and very close to the beautiful Rock Creek Park which is great for a run through the woods, although pretty steep in places!

title: “Lovely eclectic hotel”
text: The Pan Pacific Seattle is a very nice hotel. The lobby has great decor, the front staff is very helpful, and the location was ideal. We like to walk, so the distance from the sites was not a problem. Our room was beautiful, loved the shower, toiletries, and comfortable Hypnos bed. Now I want a hypnos bed too! The linens and layout of the room were great, and we had a terrific view. Really we could not have asked for more. When we were leaving for the airport, we wanted to weigh our baggage, and the front desk was very obliging to let us borrow their handy scale to weigh our bags. I would definitely go back and I recommend the hotel highly.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text:
If you're expecting marble floors in the bathroom and a flat screen plasma in the room this isn't the place for you. The room is above average but not in sync with the price. What you're paying for is the location. Definitely request a room on the upper floors with a view of the water. 
The Manchester is within walking distance of Seaport Village, the trolley station, the USS Midway, and Petco Park. Hotel staff was plentiful, very friendly and accommodating.
Other posts mention a train at 2 AM in the morning but we didn't hear a thing. Occasionally we heard the crossing arms for the trolley but nothing that would wake you.
The food at both the event we were attending as well as the Hotel cafe was excellent. Treat yourself to a $12 martini and a cheese plate at the rooftop bar. The views at sunset are worth the price.

title: “Not so great”
text:
I didn't really enjoy my stay here, the rooms are dated and the hotel is very busy.
There is a Ruby Tuesday nearby, we dined there, food was good.

title: “4 Nights”
text:
We were upgraded to a Kingsize room on our arrival, no extra cost.
The room was spotlessly clean and maintained that way throughout our stay. It was a spacious room with hair dryer and Iron included. 
The staff were help full and pleasant, breakfast was plentyful if at times a little crowded. The cutlery and plates were disposable, but not really detramental to the meal.
The location was excellent, being at most about 200 metres from Macys. Thers was a subway stop at the end of the street with easy access to everywhere we could think of.

title: “Could not fault it!”
text: We booked this hotel on the BA website and was attracted by the price. We were not expecting much but were really suprised and pleased. The reception staff were friendly and even though we checked in early they had our room ready and had left a small gift as they knew it was my birthday. Some have commented on the size of the rooms but there was more then enough space. A queen bed, dressing table, a set of drawers, 2 bed side cabinets and a wardrobe big enough for clothes and 2 suitcases! The free safe is inside the wardrobe - which we had trouble working but someone arrived within 10 minutes to help! The view of the ESB from the roof top terrace was great. The hotel is in a great location, really central and close to Times Square. The sub-way is less then a minute from the hotel and a great way to get about. The breakfast was right up my street and certainly enough to keep you going to lunch, huge muffins, toast, bagels, cereal, fresh fruit with tea and coffee on tap all day. The reception staff were helpful and booked an attraction for us as well as arranging our return trip to the airport on the shuttle bus (slightly cheaper then getting a cab but just as good). This is a really great value for money hotel in a excellent location. Would stay here again and would happily recommend.

title: “Cheap place. Lots of "character".”
text: When you're checking online for a place in San Francisco and you see that the Renoir is cheaper than most other hotels in the area, there's a reason why. This hotel is fine if you all you need is a reasonably clean place to sleep. It's centrally located, and though the area is a bit shady-looking, I've never had any problems. Plenty of great restaurants nearby, as well as streetcars and buses. I stayed for five nights and one of the elevators was out of service, making for long waits. Though the sign said, "under repair", I never saw or heard anyone working on it. I'm not gonna lie, this isn't my favorite hotel in San Francisco, but its not that bad. I'll probably stay there again, because the price makes up for the hotel's shortcomings.

title: “Nice 4 Stars Hotel”
text: The hotel area in downtown is very nice and quit. the hotel have a nice pool and spa, and gym area. the room and the bed are very confortable. the valet park is VERY EXPENSIVE ($ 30.00) a day. but you can find a 10.00 flat rate park one block from the hotel. But you can stay there for sure. very nice hotel .

title: “Thought it would be nicer”
text:
Just went to Vegas/San Francisco and though the Fairmont would be the upscale hotel. Not so. The hotel is a beautiful landmark, lobby was spectacular. I cannot say we got the first class treatment. They seemed to nickel and dime you...$14.00 day WiFi, $17.95 for in room movie. Family of six went to holiday brunch for $140PP which include one mimosa. We found that out the hard way after they filled our glasses without telling us of the upcharge.
In room staff very friendly, rooms clean and beds comfortable. Great location, but, overall, we were dissapointed.

title: “Gave it a second chance!!! You decide”
text: I have stayed here twice and both times something has gone wrong. The first stay the cleaning job wasnt up to par, but thats ok stuff happens. Although the second stay where the refridgerator leaked water on the floor, the Heater/AC didnt work and not to meantion that I had to wait a long while for room service to deliver made me decide that it was time to switch hotels

title: “Clean and Comfortable”
text: Came to town for the OSU vs. Nebraska game. Conveniently right off of 71 which made it easy to get to and from. Only a 10 minute drive to campus without all of the hectic campus traffic! The room was very clean and the beds were comfortable. Very friendly staff who was more than willing to help out with anything that we needed. Hotel was quiet at night, parking was not an issue. Overall a great experience; I would stay here again.

title: “A very nice stay in a perfect location for us.”
text:
The hotel takes up nearly a city block and the lobby was quite large. The hotel does have a pool but be sure to ask for directions as the signs in the hotel weren't always apparent and you may be doing some walking depending on where your room is. 
The room was as expected for this level of hotel. We had a good amount of space to move around even with two queen beds. The bedding was well appointed and comfortable and the room furnishings were nice. (I think we even had a room that was yet to be remodeled and it was still nice). 
The location was perfect for us. It was within walking distance of: a parking garage to pick-up or drop off car rentals, Muni and BART. The area around the hotel was mostly nice. There were a good number of restaurants and stores and while there were the typical SF street crowd, we felt comfortable here.

title: “great location, great stafff, free parking”
text: We stayed three days and two nights at the Wharf Inn, in June, 2004. The staff was great and helpful. Best of all, the hotel is located in the middle of Fisherman's Wharf. The room rates are reasonable, especially if you factor in the free parking for guests, which saves at least $25 a day. The staff allowed my family to park prior to checkin time, so we could check out the sights. The boat for the Alcatraz tour is two blocks from the hotel, and this tour is a must see. I would stay there again, especially if I wanted to visit the Fisherman's Wharf, Cable Car Museum and Alcatraz.

title: “Great Hotel. Perfect Location”
text:
The Manchester Hyatt is a lovely Hotel. No complaints.
The service was excellent and the location was perfect. It was only a short 5-10 minute drive to Sea World and The San Diego Zoo.
The Hotel is also right next to Seaport Village which has many restaurants and shoppes. 
We had a corner room with great views of the bay and the city skyline. Awesome views!
We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Suite at Sofitel”
text: The suite we checked into had a balcony and looked out at GE Building and Rockefeller Center. Check and see if you can the Playbill rate. Regular rooms do seem a bit smaller but the suite is worth the price. You know you are in hotel that caters to the French. Excellent location if coming into Grand Central Station, you can walk to Times Square and Central Park.

title: “Extortion”
text: Hilton website advertised free wired internet. Even after showing them this, I was notified by a snobbish front desk staff that no such thing existed, and I'd have to pay $10/night for wireless. Rooms were terrible. Sure your lamps look fancy, but you don't even have a fridge or microwave. No complementary breakfast, no free airport shuttle, $15/night for a roll-away bed, and they actually wanted $10/night for parking. I consistently get way better service from even the cheapest of economy hotels. I feel used and extorted.

title: “Customer service is the best!”
text: This hotel has excellent customer service. You are immediately welcomed upon entering. It is located within minutes of highway 87 and the San Jose Airport. The rooms are great and the staff helpful. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in San Jose. Don't get surprised by the cost of parking. It was $19 when I stayed, but still worth the stay. The only challenge I had was regulating the room temperature.

title: “had the best time in the best room in the best location!”
text:
Date of stay from the 12th-17 december :) 
this is the second time i have stayed in park central last visit was 07 and i found the hotel fine, but a tad basic and my other traveller had problems with the room service but apart from that everything was fine. 
On this visit i and my boyfriend started looking at reviews and i was so scared reading the bad reviews on here, about staff rudeness, dirty bathrooms, smells, robbing, and not getting your moneys worth. 
Well, all the bad reviews must have stayed at a different hotel, it was perfect! 
i was hoping as it was the christmas period the hotel would have festive decorations, and whilst walking into the lobby it had several false xmas trees with white lights very cute :) 
due to BA loosing our bags when checking in we asked the person at the desk to keep a record and they should be getting deliverd later on in the evening she did ask if we needed any help with our bags atleast 3 times but we just laughed it off she may of had a long day. When asked if we needed 2 room keys we where told we where staying on the 20th floor! 
By reading reviews on here i do remember someone saying about asking for a room from the 16-26th floor as there better and more 'renevated' 
The lifts are better than last time and where instantly fast even though the hotel was packed in the lobby at all times, stepping out the decor was nice and we noted the room we where staying i (we loved it!) 2021 was a corner room, when entering it the bed was huge, maybe a superior king? but mainly i know of the room sizes anyway from the last visit but this was something else, we had 2 huge windows each looking out around broadway & leading to times square, from the north window we could see a huge wicked poster and the building around where so nice, if you lay in bed you could see a building (dont ask not sure, green triangle roof) all light up was very nice. After reading about bed bugs we checked everything, it was fine, spotless, big television coffee maker, desk, 2 telephones, armchair, 2 bed side tables and lights, and the bathroom was spotless (made sure to check for instant hot water) all park central complimetary things around the room, a walk in (kind of) closet with a safe, coathangers, iron, and 2 extra pillows and a little quilt, the bed had about 6 pillows on it though and it was very comfy to lye in, my boyfriend did complain however he woke up in the night quite cold and had to turn the heating on which was simple anyway. Room cleaning daily if required and lifts to go down where very quick. Because of the luggage still missing the front desk where very helpful by ringing jfk and also leaving our room phone messages of any progress, the doorman (big Al) greeted you every morning asking if we needed a cab he then recommended us to go get breakfast in the brooklyn diner (everyone go its really good and will fill you up all day - ask for pink lemonade its the best). One night we arrived back around 2am and where greeted by a very much alert member of staff saying good morning yet the bar was closed drinks could be brought up to the room haha! 
As for the staff's manners they where so polite and helpful we booked a shuttle to get from the hotel to JFK no problem with it and it was very cheap, we paid $5 to hold our luggage for an hour and 1/2 and after a trip to carneige deli (cheescake!) we where allowed to check out at 1pm instead of 12. It was a perfect trip and the location well, that is one of the main reasons we chose this hotel and around the christmas period with all the street decorations its loverly, not to mention the christmas cottage directly oppostie the main entrance, its a must if your bringing back trinket things. Times square is like 5 minutes away yet you cant hear anything at night nor in the hotel, we enjoyed it that much were already looking to go back and we may ask for the same room! :) 
It wasnt just look at getting the room all in all the hotel was brilliant along with the staff and also the little corner shop located by the lifts and back entrance the man working there was so helpful in advising on medicine for my boyfriends fever - advil. Wish we got them over here. Great hotel, no problems, amazing location & amazing room. New York we love thee.

title: “A nice surprise.”
text: Spacious, clean king suite. Free wifi. Plenty of outlets 4 electronics & you can get 2 them without moving furniture. No sign of bedbugs :). Free happy hour & breakfast. Good value. Cheap toiletries but hey, u can't have everything.

title: “Attractive, great restaurant, friendly staff, overwhelmed housekeeping”
text: This is a very pretty boutique hotel in a good location. Our room was small but very comfy and efficent use of space. Loved the leopard-print plush robes! The wine reception is relaxing at the end of the day. One day we were too tired to venture out again in the evening, so decided to try their own restaurant. We both had pasta dishes; both were delicious and very imaginatively prepared, and service was excellent. Only a few caveats - everything here is pricey, including parking and internet. Our room was not serviced until almost 5PM - and then only when we asked. The housekeeping staff seems frazzled and overwhelmed.

title: “Great hotel with great service”
text: I spent a couple days at the Alden Hotel and had a great time. The service was exceptional and the staff was truly accomodating. The location was very centrally located and I had easy access to all the things I had planned for the weekend. It was just a couple blocks from Allen Parkway running trail which leads to Memorial park. This is the best place to run in Houston. My room was stylish and comfortable. I am looking forward to my next trip to Houston in which I will definitely be staying at the Alden again.

title: “Very nice stay in the oldest hotel in America”
text: We stayed one night in the oldest hotel in America. The room was very well apportioned and equipped - with real coffee making machine. The hotel was well located for walking to various tourist areas and the sevice from everyone we met was excellent. The room rate was good value. The restaurant was superb. If we return to Boston as we may - will definitely book again.

title: “return visit”
text: I came across this hotel par accident in 2010 and was very impressed. When I booked again I hoped it would be as good the second time and it was. The staff are friendly and helpful but without being fussy

title: “Nice location yes..but worth the price?”
text: The location is great, a short walk downtown and on the walkway next to the marina and shopping. The staff was very courteous and helpful but I found for a hotel of this supposed caliber that the rooms were not that clean if that is important to you. I would be tolerant of Coke splatters on the wall and fingerprints on the windows at a Days Inn etc. but not when your paying 275 bucks a night.

title: “Dirty, drab, depressing.”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights earlier this year. The location is good. That's about the only good thing going for it. The building desperately needs cleaning and re-decorating, when you walk in everything seems to become sepia washed. The lady on reception (?Rosa) was lovely, the location was good and it has wifi so it's not all bad.
When we got to our room, it looked like it had been serviced but I dropped the cases and sat on the bed and my eyes settled straight away on the hairs on the bed of head and pubic origin. When I brought this to the attention of the chap at reception, he didn't apologise, didn't care, didn't react! I couldn't believe it. We got a change of blanket thankfully but who wants to stay in a place where there are pubic hairs in the room which has supposedly already been cleaned, a CSI team would have a field day with the carpet. We chose not to look any closer.
The room itself smelt oddly stale, not pleasant. The wall paper was peeling from the walls and had mould. The carpet was so grubby that neither of us wanted to walk on it in bare feet. Esp given the pubic hair situation. Water pressure was very poor, making showers a time consuming affair. The toilet was crammed into a space that left no room to use it comfortably. If you are proficient at yoga, you'll be fine though.
Breakfast was a a total disappointment. Cheap pastries and plastic cutlery, self served in a dim, depressing bar. Clear away a table to be able to sit down time. We tried it on day 1 and didn't even finish, choosing to use a deli nearby instead.
We went expecting budget hotel standard, a place to use only for sleeping, knowing it was cheap but the standard was very poor. I stay in a lot of hotels with work, of various standards and so have a very good basis for comparison. I am far from particular about food and hygiene, if you're reading this and thinking that I'm probably just an anal fusspot, I'm not. We went with "budget hotel" low expectations and were still disappointed. 
If you go to New York for a city break, you don't want to have to worry about the basics. We visited my sister who was staying in another hotel for the same price and it was everything you'd expect and want. If you're looking to book for a break and are unsure, I would cross this hotel off your list.

title: “Not with it with all the "fees" totalled at the end”
text:
So I got a good deal at this hotel. That is the reason why I stayed here. I stayed here for two nights. First the room was okay. Nothing special. Everything looked pretty dated. I read on their website that they did a multimillion dollar renovation. But I did not see anything of any sort in the room. Just a new flat screen TV. 
Towards the end of my 2 day stay when I got the bill under the door. It was for $65 dollars. $20 per day resort fee, $10 per day parking, $2.50 per day occupancy tax.
