I think they went over board to charge for parking. I understand when you get a hotel in a downtown area where space is limited and parking is underground and it costs to engineer these structures. But this hotel is in the middle of no where with TONS of open space for parking. Its not like you can take public transportation there. You HAVE to drive.
So I will never stay here again with the ridiculous $65.00 charge at the end of my 2 day stay.

title: “Excellent hotel; amazing garden tub; and comfy bed; would stay again!”
text: I enjoyed my stay at the Magnolia; they offer many amentities. However, I did not use most of them, lol. The garden tub was awesome, as well as the bed, and customer service. The only thing I had and issue with is the length of time it took valet to bring your car.

title: “Where "At Your Service" is more than a slogan!”
text: From the moment that we arrived (at 6 a.m. and after a long COLD evening of travel), we were greeted and treated like royalty from the desk manager, Milton, and staff. We three couples booked the "Adventure" on Travelzoo and were not sure what to expect from a Hotel that was under renovation. Let me tell you that the rooms, comfort of the beds, decor, snacks, attention to detail in directions, suggestions for resturants, shopping and area attractions, anything and everything that we asked of the staff, was all FIRST CLASS! The preformance of 'Wicked' and Devon's seafood resturant were supreme! I was amazed how the staff remembered our names and welcomed us back after each outing. We can hardly wait to return to the 'family' at the Affinia! Milton made our visit extremely Memorable! Thank You!

title: “Great Location.....maybe a little tired though”
text:
Stayed at this hotel after recommended by a friend and also the positive trip advisor reviews.
Fantastic location has to be the best thing for this hotel- very easy access to the subway and the main attractions. It was also very reasonably priced compared to a lot of the expensive hotels in NYC.
We had a room on the 9th floor and felt it was looking a little tired and in need of redecoration. The bathroom although clean on the whole had a very 70's feel to it! Room was unusually spacious though. 
Our room was at the front of the hotel and I did find it noisy during the night as I am a light sleeper- what felt like constant sirens - I figure this is par for the course in New York though and certainly did not detract from the overall hotel experience.
The main issues we foundother negatives were very slow lifts - certainly not enough for the size of hotel. Also the rooms and corridors were VERY hot!!!
Overall a good stay in NYC. Great location and good price. 
Overall a good stay and would recommend

title: “Great staff”
text: We had to come to phoenix for work. when we arrived everyone was so helpful and friendly.the rooms were great and the beds are to die for.when we went to the lobby bar looking for somewhere to eat.Jerry the bartender went above and beyond with helping us.We ended up staying at the bar alot longer then intended.he treated us like we were old friends.it was nice to feel like i was home away from home.You need more like him.thanks again jerry.

title: “Can I have my shoes back, please?”
text: I'm a frequent hotel guest in SF with approximately 120 Hotel nights each year, split between Marriot and Hilton. On my last visit, I left a brand new pair of workout shoes in my room. I called two days later, and they were gone. Aside from the shoes, this hotel is reasonable property. The common spaces are updated and pleasant. The breakfeast is very good for Hilton honors memebers. But, the rooms are a bit dated and they are musty. I prefer the other two Hilton properties over this one.

title: “Excellent location and hotel, but some drawbacks”
text: Terrific people throughout the hotel, could not have been nicer. Great location for being a tourist. Short ride in taxi if coming by Amtrak. Very clean and well appointed. Far less expensive than NYC hotels for quality of the hotel. Those are all very good. The drawbacks were expensive WiFi for reasons I don't understand. The bed mattress was not the usual Marriott good experience, possibly was old and needed replacing. And forget adult use of the pool which every day was wall to wall kids. There literally was barely room to get into the pool. Maybe an assigned adult hour a night would help. If not for these things might have given it 5 stars,

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text:
Just returned from a weekend stay. For a NYC hotel, this was great and priced well. My room was clean, the staff was friendly, each night of my stay they recommended GREAT places for dinner. I arrived early, 9:00am, and they checked my bags. 
Breakfast was free and was more then I expected. I would highly recommend this hotel and have plans to stay here during my next visit to NYC.

title: “Not acceptable for business travel”
text: There was no hot water and there were no free outlets, and none at all near the desk. In order to plug in a laptop, it was necessary to unplug a lamp and work while sitting on the floor or bed. Will not be staying here again.

title: “Wonderful”
text: It was a pleasure staying in the Inn at Cherry Creek

title: “Nice hotel”
text: Nice hotel in Greek town. Not much to do in the neighborhood but eat. Plenty of good Greek restaurants. Rooms clean and comfortable.

title: “Great value outside of downtown San Antonio”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel several times on business trips - and even held a multi-day meeting there! The rooms are well appointed. The beds are comfortable. The Omni Select Guest program gives plenty of great perks - like free wi-fi and one clothing item pressed for free. The turndown service is a nice touch. In addition, the program offers you choice of morning beverages delivered to your door. The room service team is prompt and accommodating - both for lunch and dinner/late night orders. 
The indoor/outdoor pool is great. 
Petra, at the bar, is the best! She is very attentive and friendly. They even have a pianist in the evenings as you sit and sip your cocktail or wine. The gift shop is stocked with both gift items and a bevy of items that anyone who travels might forget! They also offer a "coffee window" outside the restaurant if you just want a quick cup of Starbucks coffee to go. 
Since I've stayed there often, I would love to see some additonal variety on the menu.
They do have a complimentary local shuttle service but the semi-set schedule was too inconvenient for me. 
Overall - a great hotel I would definitely recommend to others.

title: “Wonderful!!”
text: We took our first family vacation to Sea World San Antonio and stayed here. The staff was wonderful! They were so helpful with everything, from, cleaning our room to giving directions around town. If we ever go back to San Antonio we will definitaley be going back to the Courtyard/Marketsquare!

title: “Adequate, well located”
text: Although a little on the high end for the current hotel market, what this hotel has to offer is location, location, location, not just in relation to the tourist areas like Faneuil Hall/Quincy Market and the wonderful North End Italian section of Boston, but it is in walking distance to T stops, bus routes, train stations and downtown. The staff was just adequate, nothing great. Although the concierge had sent a pro forma email before our arrival, no one responded when I asked questions back. We had to figure everthing out ourselves. The hotel is clean, comfortable, with small rooms and small windows. When I was given a near windowless, dark room because of late night arrival, the front desk was very accomodating about moving us the next morning. The price could be lower for what you get, but that factor is outweighed by the convenience of its location. The bar tender at the in house restaurant was very accomodating and the ambience very friendly.

title: “great place for families”
text:
Stayed one week, got a great rate thru the hotel website. Stayed in a double suite, had lots of space, good kitchen, sitting area, seperate bedroom, newly renovated, big bathroom, on the 4th floor, very quiet.
Breakfast was great, waffles, bagels, coffee, juice, yogurt, fruit- all included in rate. Had nice laudry facilities. Small pool but good size for little kids (cold, but this was December!)
Staff was lovely, parking directly under hotel for only $6 per day, we would certainly stay here again.

title: “nightmare in NY”
text:
don't go there!!!! we spent a night there, or better from 5 a.m. to 7 a.m, as we discovered to be surrounded by every kind of bug! I took about 30 louses and ticks off the bed! and a couple of big croaches on the wall! we went at the reception and asked our money back, they did't want to do it, so I went to the police station and made a complain to healt department. Moreover, we started telling all the guests of the hotel what happened to us. We got money back...but not our clothes (we throwed them away) and our trip to NY!
somebody should close that place!

title: “Great location, wonderful staff, clean rooms”
text: Location could not have been better - walking distance to Fifth Ave shopping, Times Square, Empire State Building, and Central Park entrance. Staff was wonderful! I was a solo traveler and they went out of their way to make sure I was comfortable. I had three different staff members catering to me and answering questions. Coffee/tea in the morning and afternoon was a great plus. Safe inexpensive luggage storage for check out. Room was small, but very clean and recently renovated (some of the rooms haven't been renovated yet, but you should expect that for the great price).

title: “Great staff, great location, amazing pool and over the top customer service”
text:
I recently stayed at the newly opened Dream Downtown hotel in the Meatpacking District. The hotel was amazing. As with any new hotel, they are still working out a couple of finishing touches (as it just opened) but the staff, the pool and vibe made up for any and all kinks. 
First of all, I picked Dream because it has a pool. And I’m so glad I did. There aren’t many hotels with outdoor pools in Manhattan to choose from…and I usually stay at the Empire near Columbus Circle. But based on this recent stay, I will always stay at Dream. The pool is beautiful (and really nice sized for Manhattan), they have great poolside cocktail/food service and the staff is very helpful and attentive. Not to mention the great (and cute) lifeguards. They have everything you need from floating chairs to sunscreen to towel service to saving your life. 
Aside from the pool, both restaurants (and room service) were amazing. The poolside café had great sandwiches and salads (and an extensive cocktail list) and the restaurant downstairs was packed every night. Please note I didn’t eat downstairs but did have apps and drinks and highly recommend. 
Hotel is great…has all of the amenities that you need…no need to really even venture out. But if you do, you’re right in the middle of Chelsea and the Meatpacking District. You can walk to shopping, restaurants, coffee, etc. Great location for business or leisure. 
All and all…highly recommended. I will definitely be staying there again. Great staff, great location, amazing pool and over the top customer service.

title: “Good location, Room was Spacious”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for our anniversary in March. The room was big (though, I have stayed here previously and gotten a very small room) and clean. The room could use a refresh and same with the halls outside but all in all, a pretty good stay.
The location is good for visitors to Boston, right near the Public park and along the Freedom trail. The bar downstairs is pretty good too... amazing leather couches that are so comfy you won't want to get up!

title: “The perfect place to stay when in Boston”
text: Staying at XV Beacon is a joy. This boutique hotel, with only 6 rooms per floor, is more like staying in an elegant turn of the century private residence than a hotel. Attention to detail reigns supreme. The rooms are very quiet and the bedding (Frette, of course) is among the most comfortable I have experienced. The bathrooms are well appointed and the rain shower head is outstanding. Each room has a gas fireplace, which was an unexpected and most welcome luxury. Guests have access to a complimentary Lexus sedan service, which is quite a plus and a money saver as well. The hotel restaurant is Mooo, so one doesn't have to go far for an excellent dining experience. Last, but certainly not least, the hotel staff is very professional, thoughtful and attentive. The only thing that we did not like about Beacon XV, was having to leave and go back to the real world....

title: “Loved this hotel!”
text:
I booked this trip as a surprise for my partner's Birthday - our first trip together in New York... We had a fantastic time and we loved this hotel!!!
I was concerned after reading reviews, regarding the size of the rooms especially as I booked it as a surprise. I was pleasantly surprised when we reached our room on the 15th floor. It wasn't huge, but we didn't expect it in New York City, it was definately bigger than what we expected. There was plenty of room, it was spotlessly clean and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was once again, very clean, had a small bath with a shower (which admittedly wasn't very powerful but ok). It was certainly not tatty as in other reviews, everything was in good order.
The staff were all really helpful and friendly, especially the doorman.
The location is brilliant, right around the corner from Time Square, only 15 mins or so walk away from Central Park and 10 min walk from the Empire States Building.
We had a fantastic time, in an amazing City in a great hotel. We'll definately be back to New York and the Time Hotel.

title: “Great location in a fantastic Hotel”
text:
Stayed at the Ritz Carlton for 3 nights. Fantastic hotel in great location, walking distance to the sights of Philadelphia. Excellant staff at this hotel. Friendly and willing to help at all times.
Free wifi with great access. Rooms maintained to a very high standard. Would recommend for both business and pleasure.

title: “2nd time we stayed, even better!!!”
text: This was the second time we've stayed here and it was even better than before. We stayed 11th to 16th December for my fiftieth birthday. Staff were very friendly, thanks to Matthew (Bellhop) for all your help, breakfast awesome, and location, location, location fantastic!! Room and ensuite excellent, bed made everyday, our maid was spanish speaking, danced as she worked and was very friendly. Loads to do in surrounding area, eating, drinking, shopping etc!! Macy's and ESB just a short stroll. Blue bus three day pass great value to see all the sights and we did a Viator dinner cruise....wow!! Times Square just a short walk away!! Saw Sister Act on Broadway, it was fantastic!!!

title: “You get what you pay for”
text: We stayed in the Powell Hotel in mid January 2005. We asked to see the rooms before checking in and got one of the 'updated' rooms. The room was somewhat cramped, but who spends all their time in the room. The bathroom was very upscale. We checked in around 2 pm and toured the town during the day. Arriving back to our room, it was a bit chilly. I turned on the radiator, but two hours later, no heat. I went downstairs to check about the heat and was told that it is on only from 5 pm to 5 am. OK.....so I waited until 5 pm. Still no heat. I went downstairs and asked about it again and they gave me an electric heater and extra blankets. I guess it is routine to not have any heat. The five days that we stayed there, the electric heater was our only heat. I was glad it wasn't any colder! The hot water takes about 5 minutes to arrive; so plan ahead with showers. After returning home, I sent a letter to the manager of the Powell, asking about the lack of heat, but they did not respond.

title: “It will suffice for one night”
text:
We chose the Clarion because of it's claim of "newly renovated rooms" and the online photos looked pretty nice. In actuality, the hotel is still rather run down with a fresh coat of paint and some new carpet. We only had plans to stay one night with an early morning flight out, so for one night it was OK. The beds were comfy and the hotel was quiet. And it has a restaurant upstairs so a full breakfast was easy in the morning. 
The gentleman at check-in was extremely helpful and the service was excellent. With the light rail 1 block away he helped us with how to take the train downtown for dinner and had recommendations for restaurants. This part of our experience was excellent.
If you are looking for something more than a quiet place to sleep, I wouldn't recommend the Clarion. It was OK for one night but I wouldn't plan to stay here during a vacation with my family. The service was very friendly and helpful though. Too bad the property is kind of run down.

title: “Excellent”
text: Customer service was quick and friendly, Room was clean and quiet even for being near a highway, well priced, the continental breakfast was good as well nice variety to choose from especially liked the waffles, would stay at again if in the area, much better than the holiday inn we got stuck with the night before. wish we could have found this place first

title: “Please! Do not, I repeat Do not go there.”
text:
I am astonished how people here can rate this place outstanding, excellent etc...
I have stayed at many 5 stars hotels over the years and I can tell you without hesitation: The four seasons at Beverly Hills, LA IS NO 5 STARS.
1. Rooms and worst suites too small and poorly designed.
2. Room service is a joke ! I dont even want to comment.
3. Staff appears to be under tremendous pressure to fake smile and pretend good service but clearly the face expressions and lack of dedication do betray a total lack of leadership in this place. Staff appears to operate out of fear!
4. You could never sense the presence of managerial personel. Staff everywhere from front desk to pool to restaurant clearly scrambled through requests.
5. Pool can qualify at best as a POND !
6. There appears to be some sort of financial distress in this place as cutting cost has become visible even to the non business oriented: Soap bars are not replaced until they have melted. Same for shampoo etc..., towels scarce and most hang right in front of the toilette bowl, each time you flush, its on your towel.
7. If anybody from four seasons company or Mister Bill Gates is reading this, please get a quality control team ovethere ASAP...

title: “Great hotel”
text: Came here for St. Paddy's day weekend and found this hotel to be great. Well situated, clean rooms, about a 5 minute walk to the subway. The concierge was oustanding and recommended some great sites and restaurants. Rooms were very comfortable and did not have any issues with noise. Would recommended if you are looking for a modern, fun hotel. Extremely comfortable beds.

title: “Absolutely first rate”
text:
This hotel is classy, luxurious and modern chic all in one. I loved it. The rooms are fairly spacious and the bathrooms are quite large (although not really "private"). Showers are totally open and the bathroom door was more of mini-blind. The amenities are nice, but not over the top. It’s a bit farther from the action of the River North or Magnificent Mile than I would prefer, but it was close to the conventions at McCormick Place. In terms of hotels in Chicago, this one has been the best.
I was hosting a morning breakfast at the hotel early in the morning and had a bit of crisis the night before. The staff stayed late (until almost 11:30pm) to accomodate my last minute changes to the meeting plan.
More on my time in Chicago:
http://justanothertravelblog.blogspot.com/2009/05/chicago-illinois.html

title: “Great hotel in great location”
text:
This hotel was almost directly across from Madisson Square Gardens and a short walk from the Empire State Building.
I went with a platonic male friend and we booked a suite as it was cheaper than two single rooms and not much more than a double room. It turned out to be an excellent choice as the room was very spacious, had two bathrooms and the living room had a comfortable double sofa bed. There was also a kitchen but we never ventured in it, too many great places to eat in NYC!
The staff were helpful but not intrusive. We booked a few trips through the reception (which saved us the hassle of queuing for tickets etc) and they gave us advice on which routes to walk, how far away things were etc
I used the gym daily. It was small but not poky and most importantly it had all the key equipment.
There is a 'Borders' opposite which offers free wifi, sadly there wasn't free wifi in the hotel.
There is so much to see and do in New York that I could write a huge review but it is best to go and explore it for yourself. My one recommendation would be to spend $50 on a two-day open top bus pass (vendors on most streets). You can hop on and off at your leisure, they come frequently and they cover every possible tourist attraction, hotspot and district you would want to see - the best way to take in the city if you are only on a short break. 
Also, take in a sport at Madisson Square Garden if you can. We were lucky enough to see an Amir Khan boxing match and the atmosphere was electric, a real experience to be amongst the American crowd!

title: “A Disappointment”
text:
After all the remarkable reviews on Trip Advisor, we decided to stay at the Omni when we visited San Francisco for the weekend. The good news was fast check in, unbelievable friendly and efficient staff, cookies in the lobby and a convenient location. Also, the room was spacious, clean and the windows open a little for fresh air. The bad news was the room and bathroom were very depressing and in much need of a facelift. The furniture was very old and the fabrics looked worn and outdated. Even the towels were threadbare and needed replacing.
Fortunately, they have started a renovation.

title: “Great Place to Stay!”
text:
Stayed one night on the riverwalk on a business trip. Loved this hotel. The people that work in this hotel are the best! I cannot say enough nice things about them. I asked for a river view upgrade and was given one without hesitation. 
The hotel was also very nice. The rooms were spacious and clean. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Fabulous!!!”
text: Fabulous Hotel, Sensational location ( next to Subway)short walk to Times Square, next to the theatres . One stop to Madison Square Gardens ( Penn Station ) One stop to Central Park. Great beds ,great bathroom, clean rooms and staff very helpful and friendly.The only thing is watch the mini bar you move something and you are charged- there is no room for your own drinks in the fridge. We solved that by filling up a bag with ice and using a makeshift esky. We ate at a restaurant called Ammanci in Little Italy Great Food !!! We bought tickets to Mary Poppins an hour before the show and got great seats. Try and catch a basketball game at Madison Square Gardens- The most amazing spectacle - a little exey on $ but well worth the new york experience. The people were brililant always asking if we needed assistance and the manners the new yorkers have are exceptional. WE LOVE NYC!!!!

title: “Perfect”
text: This is the perfect hotel. Everything about it. I can't think of anything bad to say. Come to think about it, I can't say anything mediocre about it. Service is perfect, food is perfect, room was awesome, (suite) and it was amazingly quiet for being steps from Times Square.

title: “Cozy, historic charm”
text:
We got this hotel on Priceline and it was guaranteed for 2 people. Called hotel to confirm 4 in the room, but they have few rooms with 2 beds, and those have twins. They do have have a few "family suites" with 2 rooms, and sleeping for 4. Luckily they had one and up-charged only $25 from our prepaid deal. 
The welcome shot of tequila was quite nice. The hotel is old/historic, but well maintained. The elevator is small and slow, but stairs are bright and functional if you are. Our room had comfortable beds, great colors and hand painted details. The windows were thin and the noise from the bar below was loud, so light sleepers beware. But the noise was only a constant din of voices not music. 
A few block walk from Union Square made our touristy stay easy and fun.
Breakfast was standard continental fare. Waffles were fresh and tasty.

title: “Plush and elegant”
text: My partner and I stayed here for 3 days at the beginning of July. This is a hotel where the staff are so helpful its almost too much. The decor is grandiose but then it is a boutique hotel. We never got round to eating in the hotel but the on-site pub is really good. Some fabulous touches from the receptionists, so if you want plenty of attentive service, the Lenox is for you. Try and meet Johnny, the world war 2 veteran octagenarian still working in the hotel. Boston is a fabulous place.

title: “Can't Believe this was a Holiday Inn”
text: New and trendy hotel with attractive rate. I've stayed in Holiday Inns and they don't look like this. Spacious suites and bathroom. The staff was super. Other friends were leaving at 6am, the staff made coffee and got them something to eat before the official breakfast hour. Check the times the shuttle runs to the airport. Also, when you arrive call to let them know you are waiting for a pick up from the airport. Fantastic place

title: “Not Great For Diamond Members”
text: This hotel has a beautiful lobby but the rooms are in need of repair. Beyond the check-in reception for diamond members it drops off quickly in service. They use to provide breakfast for Diamond members like every other Hilton brand of hotel but they took this,away. They also do not offer the Diamond member benefit for the Waldorf hotel brands. I have stayed here numerous times but I will choose one of the other New York Hilton hotels from now on. I will always be impressed with the history of this hotel but it is no longer the flagship Waldorf that goes to the Cavilieri or other Waldorf's in the chain. The suites I have had have been nice and the Tower is great.

title: “At Home in the Helmsley Park Lane”
text:
Stayed here for my 40th birthday, what a great find. Excellent location on Central Park South, away from all that typical NY noise with killer views of Central Park. Ask very nicely, if you fancy an upgrade, we got upgraded to the 33rd floor with city and park views - amazing! Here's a few helpful tips:
1. The Green Cafe (exit at the hotels back entrance and turn left, its just a few seconds walk on the left) does take away food and drink open 0600-1100 - huge selection 
2. 5th Avenue only a very short stroll with the excellent Bergdorf Goodman on the corner
3. The Heartland Bewery (one right next to the Empire State Building) is a great pub, expensive mind, but they brew their own beer and the food is lovely
4. Get to the Empire State Builing early to avoid the crowds, must see is the Observatory on the 102nd floor, an enclosed area
5. Have a drink at Whisky Park, only 2-3 mins walk from hotel, get a table with a view of Central Park
6. Go see the Planetarium show at the Museum of Natural History, it is truly outstanding
About the Hotel:
1. Yes it needs a make over, in particular our very tired bathroom, but you are not in New York to complain about pealing paint or seventies lighting, go have Sushi and a Cosmo instead
2. Beds are huge and very comfy, our room was tidied to perfection each day
3. Staff cannot be more helpful and curteous
4. Lifts are incredibly speedy
5. Room service is pricey , but fast, efficient and the best chips I have ever eaten
6. A great hotel with an excellent location and spectacular views, we will stay here every time!!!!

title: “Great, Clean, Comfortable Room”
text:
I travel often for business and stay at 4-5 star hotels as well as the usual Marriott Courtyard or Hilton Hotels. 
This Hotel was great. I reserved the King Executive which had windows facing Michigan Avenue as well as on the adjacent wall. We could not believe how quiet the room was-- no noise from Michigan Avenue or other guests, etc. Amazingly and wonderfully quiet hotel room. The room was well appointed, huge, and immaculate. (Any hotel that puts stark white comforters on the beds has confidence in its cleanliness and I always take that as a good sign.) The big surprise at this hotel was the dining. I almost never dine at the restaurants in a hotel at which I am staying. (usually too many great other options in a city) We had a case of the munchies upon checking in so we ordered appetizers via room service. Service was quick, sharp, and the food was very good. The next day, we had lunch at the 5th floor rooftop garden restaurant (outdoors) which has a fabulous view and again, was amazingly quiet given the location of this hotel. The food was FANTASTIC. We only ordered Maine lobster roll sandwiches so we were't expecting an amazing culinary experience....SURPRISE! The presentation was lovely and the lobster roll came on a platter with several "samplers"--- soup, cabbage slaw, homemade chips, and a sinful chocolate mouse cake. I've had lobster rolls in dozens of places up and down the eastern seaboard and I'll tell you that this was the best, most flavorful, and freshest I've had. The whole dining experience greatly exceeded my expectations. 
I would say that this hotel is a gem in the city and recommend it without reservation of any kind. Enjoy!

title: “Another great stay...it keeps getting better”
text:
I have stayed at the W Union Square a number of times and I keep returning because the folks at the hotel treat me great. But also the hotel is in a great location. It is close to all the things I enjoy about downtown Manhattan from the farmers market to the High Line.
High floor rooms with a park view are the best. And the recent update of the rooms now makes this an even better choice for Manhattan hotels. Great new and stylish furniture. And the improved windows keep out the street noise!
Overall a great Manhattan hotel in an excellent location.

title: “Wonderful hotel - great staff”
text: This is a lovely hotel with some of the friendliest and most helpful staff I have encountered.From check-in to check-out, my family and I were made to feel very special. Nothing was ever too much trouble, every question was met with a patient and helpful answer, and our every need was totally met. The family room we had was spotless, and a good size. The beds were extremely comfortable, the bathroom was spacious and very clean. The rooftop pool is a real plus - okay, it's not the biggest pool and at busy times you might struggle to get a chair/table at poolside. But it's a roof-top pool! I'd never seen one before, and our kids loved the buzz of having a swim and then looking down from the 11th floor to the street below. In all, a hotel that gets a total recommendation from our family.

title: “great lake view room and staff”
text: stayed over labor day weekend, old world architecture very high celings and a closet deep enough to store 2 mountain bikes! We got a lake view room, stay 11th floor or above, your right there across from grant park and the lake shore paths. Staff was excellent. I think people shun this hotel becausee of union pickets (for last 8 years). If you pick the lakeview room set you will enjoy if you are an outdoor type. If your just a shopper this is not your place. Breakfeast room service excellent or be up earlyy for great outdoor seating a short walk away. We will be back for any waterfront experience we need.

title: “Bugs!”
text: It was a very nice place for the price (though next to a strip club). The staff was friendly and the place SEEMED clean, but there is an obvious insect problem. The first time I went into the bathroom there was a cockroach scurrying across the floor. That's not really a dealbreaker, but in the middle of the night both myself and my brother were bitten multiple times by bugs. I'm praying that they were just flees and not bedbugs (dear god please let them not be bedbugs), but I don't have any evidence that they've followed me home yet. Still, I'll be ripping apart the sheets and doing a thorough mattress inspection of every hotel I stay at from now on. This was so disturbing.

title: “Very nice”
text: Our stay was very comfortable. The room was compact but lovely. The breakfast was really delicious. Although the staff and customer service was adequate, something was left to be desired on that count. The courtyard on the inside is very pretty and calming - a great place to gather a large family group.

title: “Surprisingly large room at a great price”
text: I was very surprised to find not only a large bedroom, but an attached small sitting room upon check in. I found this to be a great bargain for a Michigan Avenue Chicago hotel based on other stays in this city. The check in staff were very friendly, maid service prompt and thorough. I stayed there due to a conference and the conference room was comfortable, as well as the lunches that were served excellent. The bed was extremely comfortable and the room was very quiet. Great central Michigan Avenue location. I will definitely stay here again when given the opportunity.

title: “Park Central Hotel”
text:
This hotel was selected by my sig other. Location, price all were taken into consideration. 
Finding the hotel was easy...look for the flags and the barricades...
very unsightly. Once in the lobby you see where they took the pictures...nice lobby and bar. Check in was ok, but don't ask a question...that thousand yard stare was telltale. The Room...decent bed, the rest of the room was a dump. The shower was small, grungy...
glad I was there only one night and I pretty much can take anything. 
Over rated and there are way better hotels for the price....Not a great place considering the money they spent fixing it up...if they really did.

title: “Nice change from midtown”
text: Stayed here for the weekend. Great change from congested midtown. Nice view of Statue of Liberty from room; pleasant walk to Battery Park. Accessible to subway stops. Could have used help from hotel staff flagging cabs instead of being prey to "limo boys" charging twice the price of a cab ride. Did appreciate hotel staff stepping up, shooing away one sketchy person posing as a cab driver in a questionable car. Room was great, clean; housekeeping wonderful! If you do go to a show and plan to taxi back, realize traffic might double what you expected to pay for cab ride. If dining out, try Tribeca or Soho and you are all set. Ground Zero is next door. Don't miss St. Paul's Chapel.

title: “Great Location, Decent Rooms, High Price Tag”
text: My partner and I stayed here with some family while we were visiting NYC, and we mainly picked this hotel because of the name and the location. We knew it was a little pricey but we thought that it was pricey for a reason. Unfortunately, we were left wondering what that reason was. The only great things about the hotel were the location, the lobby, and the staff was nice. The rooms were okay, nothing special, the only good thing I can say about the room is that the view was nice. There was nothing horrible about the room, the bed was comfortable, it was somewhat spacious, but for the money we paid, it was just a standard hotel room. I think you pretty much pay for the location and for the name. We will not return to this hotel when we return to NYC.

title: “Great Hotel with the best possible location”
text: I love the Manhattan Club for its location and the energy of New York city. The hotel is well kept and the room size is large for a typical Manhanttan hotel. I can't wait to get back

title: “Clean, but noisy”
text: I was travelling with a colleague for business. Very easy to get to from the airport. But the location of the hotel is right off a busy highway, so the noise never stops. We even requested rooms that were not facing the highway directly, but that made no difference - the outside walls are too thin. That said, the staff was very nice and helpful, and there was a good free breakfast. Also, the free internet was great to have.

title: “Gorgeous hotel - perfect location”
text:
Stayed in hotel for 5 nights in nov 2010, for thanksgiving. 
Stunning hotel with grand lobby, also we got upgraded to executive floor, as our room had been given to another of our party, receptionist could not have done anymore also apologising for This inconvenience and sending proseco and strawberry to our room, we did not mind at all but this was delightful and much appreciated. 
Hotel was in an ideal location for many of the sights and attraction a NY has to offer, I cannot wait to return as this hotel and city is mesmerising. In luv with this hotel and the the city.

title: “Stay here every time in LA”
text: love the vibe...staff is awesome...restaurant is great for breakfast and dinner. rooftop is sick!

title: “Wonderful Valentine's Day getaway”
text: We had a wonderful stay here over Valentine's Day weekend. Our room was spacious and comfortable, and we heard almost no outside noise. The turndown service was wonderful, including the special Valentine's Day treat. The staff was wonderful, too. They have an excellent collection of DVDs that you can get for free to watch in your room, which we took advantage of during our stay. The location is also excellent, as it's right next to a "T" stop if you want to use mass transit to get around Boston. It's also within walking distance of many of the top sights in the city. As a newspaper lover, it was great being able to pick up a free London Times, NY Times or Boston Globe at the front desk, even on a Sunday! Even though we didn't have a laptop with us, it was nice to see that there is free Internet access in the guest rooms, which isn't always the case at the pricier hotels. A friend who lives in Boston told us the restaurant located in the hotel was excellent, although we never got a chance to sample the cuisine. If I got a good rate, I would definitely come back. I'm afraid this place is out of my price range with its normal rates.

title: “Clean, Comfortable, and Inviting!”
text:
We have stayed at a Club Quarters before in another city and were very satisfied with the experience, so decided to book a room in their DC location (we are not business members). The DC Club Quarters' front desk staff were friendly and helpful, with quick check-in and even quicker checkout. The rooms were average-sized for a downtown hotel and fit 2 adults quite comfortably. Room was very clean and attractive with nice amenities (radio/alarm with mp3 adapter, flatscreen tv, lots of workspace and electrical outlets, hairdryer, multiple full-length mirrors), and the bathroom was spotless, with good water pressure from the showerhead. The hotel itself was very secure; front door is keycard access only after a certain time, and elevators only operate with keycard.
The closest Metro stop (Farragut West) is footsteps away, though this entrance is only open during weekdays. If staying on the weekends, another entrance to Farragut West, and the Farragut North station, are both within easy walking distance. There are also a variety of coffee shops, restaurants, and pharmacies/convenience stores within walking distance.
We drove into DC and parked our car around the block on Eye St. that charges $22/24hrs. We forgot to ask the hotel if they validate parking so if you are driving, be sure to ask. Even still, we've found $22 to be on the low end when it comes to parking in the city. We did see several other nearby garages as well. With DC traffic in mind, we left the car in the garage all weekend and used the Metro or walked to our destinations.
Two great perks about Club Quarters: free wireless internet access, and free bottled water, which came in very handy during our walks around DC on a hot weekend.
We only have two complaints (though "complaint" is too strong of a word). Construction was occurring across the street when we stayed, so noise was a mild issue early in the morning. Also, the room's temperature was a little difficult to regulate. With the a/c turned on, it was either frigid or a tad too hot. But, as we stayed on a 90-degree weekend, we dealt with the cold air just fine!
The value of the hotel is fabulous; the price we paid for what we got wins out over other, more expensive downtown hotels we've experienced in the past. All in all, we would stay at the Club Quarters DC again in a heartbeat, and am looking forward to experiencing their hotels in other locations!

title: “The Grand Hyatt was great”
text: My husband and I recently extended a business trip to San Francisco into a short vacation, and stayed at the Grand Hyatt on Stockton Ave. It was a great experience. The room was modern, large enough for our comfort. The staff was very helpful. The location was great--just across the street from Union Square. A great value, particularly since the rates we got through Trip Advisor were better than I was quoted by our local travel agent. I highly recommend it. Our next trip to SF will include a stay at the Grand Hyatt.

title: “Top Notch Customer Service! and ..Great Location...Great Property”
text: I met with Ami at the check-in desk and she deserves a "Perfect 10" score! I have met Ami before at the other Hilton Times Square hotel I frequent - and was delighted to see her here today. Ami is very tuned in to the needs of her customers and I just wish she was behind the desk of every Hilton I enter. Ami and DoubleTree Hilton Suites - you are the best! Oh, and Hilton, you too!

title: “Awesome location”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at Washington Jefferson and would stay there again. The location was the best I have had in New York - only a couple of blocks down from times square, theatres right around the hotel and easy access to the metro. There was also a great bar a couple of doors down, which had good food and a great selection of drinks. 
The staff, although relaxed in service, were very friendly and gave great recommendations for things to do and where to eat.
Yes the rooms are small but all rooms are in New York and in this city - you really only need a room to sleep.

title: “Great place and staff !”
text:
Stayed here for 3 days in December in the Penthouse. Had a King bed downstairs and queen up in the loft. It had bathrooms upstairs and downstairs. The beds were very comfortable and the place was very neat and clean. The staff was very friendly.
It has a breakfast buffet with good choices though the food was just warm. The buildings sit very tightly together with not much of a view though the courtyards/pathways were very well landscaped. Rooms were very well soundproofed. One thing to be aware of is the jet noise on weekdays from the Air Base directly north of it. It's not too bothersome unless you plan on hanging out at the pool a lot. Had a great visit, would stay here again !

title: “Great stay and staff at Comfort Inn”
text: Have just returned from a five night stay at the Comfort Inn Midtown and found the hotel to be clean,comfortable and the staff helpful in every way. While the room was small it was clean and met our needs for two people. Everyone on the staff was friendly and the hotel is in an excellent location to Times Square, Theatres and Shopping. It is in walking distance to Rockefeller Center,NBC studios and David Letterman. Price is reasonable for Manhattan and we would stay there again in a heartbeat!

title: “Constant, ear-splitting noise”
text: Great hotel if you enjoy constant, ear-splitting noise. A DJ plays by the pool during the day, and they set up a large-screen TV and show movies by the pool at night. Both would be fine in moderation; however, the hotel plays everything at top volume so that it is impossible to relax with a book, listen to your own music on an ipod, or even have a conversation with the person next to you without yelling. If you have a pool-facing room you will have no way to avoid the racket without leaving the premises. Management is unresponsive to requests to reduce the volume. BIG THUMBS DOWN.

title: “Great location and staff”
text:
I was a bit concerned about the hotel secondary to the reviews, but I'm glad we booked here as the hotel was just fine. Every other Hilton property in the core area was booked because of the Yankees-Red Sox game. 
We arrived after the red-eye to a full hotel. I was expecting to leave the bags and go do some walking around the city before checking in. Luckily, they were able to accomodate us with a room right away. Love the front desk for expediting it and letting us know that no one had booked that specific room for the previous night. Able to get some shut eye before the day at hand. The front desk was so friendly and helpful. 
During the day, the housekeeping staff was amazingly helpful and accomodating. The entire staff from beginning to end was helpful and gracious.
Admittedly, some of the furniture in our room was older, but it was tasteful. The room had one of the largest flat screen TVs I've ever seen in a hotel room. The sound-proofing was acutally excellent except for the teens next door trying to get into our room. Cleared that up straight-away :-)
It is in the Financial District, so during the days on the weekends, it's pretty empty, but the walkability to all the attractions was awesome! We were able to walk to the Aquarium, Quincy Market, the North End, Chinatown, Boston Commons, etc. At night, the area is packed with college kids blowing off steam. I've never seen so many lines to get into clubs. It can get noisy and the testosterone can flow with some noisy "arguments" occuring outside the hotel.
In any case, I would have no reservations in recommending this hotel to anyone visiting Boston.

title: “Highlight of our Detroit stay”
text: We only had one night in Detroit and definately picked the best place to stay. The staff at Inn on Ferry Street patiently let us look at several rooms before deciding to spend the extra $20 for a suite w/ a beautiful sitting room. Cookies were delivered to our door minutes after our arrival. Breakfast included "make your own" waffles with fruit. Although we didn't use it, free shuttle service was available within a 5 mile radius. We wouldn't stay anywhere else in Detroit.

title: “This Hotel is a Gem”
text:
My husband I spent chose to spend our 40th anniversary weekend at INK48 - and I can't heap enough praise on Jeffrey Behrens, the Concierge Services Manager, who upgraded us, sent us champagne and chocolate, and was gracious and welcoming. The rest of the staff were equally friendly, as well. I can't tell you how much this matters - but it made the weekend that much more special for me. I noticed that everyone treated well, by the way, which is a mark of a great hotel staff, in my opinion. This sort of treatment keeps me wanting to return again and again.
Do I wish I had been in the room with the soaking tub, since my feet were killing me from all the walking we did? Sure! Unfortunately, the rate I nabbed didn't allow for such a luxury. One day...
Only one, little complaint - our shower head was so high up that I couldn't reach it to adjust it. I ended up using a hanger! Oops.

title: “Great location & good value!”
text: Yes the room decor and furniture is dated but the bathrooms have been renovated, the room is spacious, the bed is comfortable, and you are a few blocks away from Times Sq. and Broadway. For the price it's hard to beat the location and value you will have by staying at the Roger Smith Hotel.

title: “perfect location”
text: We stayed at Shelburne for 4 nights. At arrival at 4.30pm they didn't have a room ready which was very disappointing as we booked back in November. After we had spoken to the manager we got a really nice Bedroom Suite. The room was really clean and very comfortable. the location is almost perfect, central for all sightseeing and a great area for shopping, bars & restaurants. and check out the roof top for a fabulous view of the city.would definitely stay here again,

title: “Great choice for trip to baltimore Harbor”
text: We booked our annual convention here so we occupied hundreds of rooms for 3 days. Overall an excellent experience. It's a hotel combined with a 4 story mall so the layoff is a bit odd. The location is perfect only a few steps from the enterence to the harbor. My room had an amazing view of the water and ships. I was upgraded to a junior suite and it was fantastic. Dining room table, small bar, living room area, great corner room. Place has a restaurant on the first floor then most other amenities are on the 5th floor above the mall. Another restaurant and bar up there. Decent menu, friendly staff. The conference rooms were also on the 5th floor and the conference staff, service and food were excellent. Overall a great experience and I'd stay there again.

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: Great hotel, wonderful and big room, great location. Booked by ratestogo.com and got a great price. Highly reccommend it!!

title: “Very Nice”
text: This hotel is located very close to LAX. I don’t understand some of these reviews. My room was clean and updated. The gym was sufficient enough for me to get a nice workout in. There are one or two minor things I noticed but not enough to complain about I was only staying at this hotel for three nights not making a purchase. There’s a Mc Donald’s, Taco Bell, and convenience store located just steps away. The staff was very helpful and friendly. I believe the front desk worker name was Eric and he is a multitasker. I saw him checking guest in, getting luggage, giving directions, and answering the phone all at the same time. I will stay here again.

title: “Enjoyed our stay at Sheraton Boston”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights 16 -20 June. Arrived very late and received a warm welcome. The room was not huge, two double beds and very small bathroom. The hotel is centrally located and easy walking distance to everything we wanted to see. Very handy being next to the Prudential Centre. Good fitness room and great pool. In 2011 I find it amazing that hotels still charge for wifi, but there are computers in the lobby and free wifi to connect your own device in the lobby. We booked through Hotwire and I was happy with the hotel for the price I paid, I would have been disappointed if I had paid the rack rate.

title: “Loved the fireplace”
text:
Took advantage of a weekend special featuring the fireplace suites, supposedly the only wood-burning ones in a Boston hotel. The suite was great, although the furniture was rather oddly arranged (which we corrected). Service was outstanding; the fireplace butler arrived quickly with our choice of wood when summoned. When we had trouble connecting the DVD player to the TV, we requested help and a very capable maintenance person arrived within 10 minutes to take care of it. Although the place is not cheap, the bar offered some pretty decent food values.
Only complaint was that the room charge on the bill was higher than what was on the check-in card, and it took the desk clerk several tries to fix it upon checkout.

title: “Fabulous Location, Exceptional Value & Great Service”
text: If you want to stay somewhere that has character, than this is it, if you want a great loaction close to the trendiest parts of Manhattan, than this is it, it you want more money to spend shopping and eating out, than this is it., if you want a comfortable clean room with private bathroom and good service, than this is it. The Cosmopolitan is everything you want for a fabulous time in Manhattan, 10 minute walk to Soho, Greenwich, 10 minute subway ride to Times Square, Empire State etc... perfect loctation, City Hall down the road, rasy walk to Brooklyn Bridge, 5 minute walk to Ground Zero and New York's best kept secret Century 21, designer discount department store, and one of the best little cafe's right under the hotel Cosmoplolitan Cafe which has an old Victorian feel, very cosy and initimate, good home style food, great service, and has all day breakfasts, and a secret room for special occasions. Drop in any time for a bite to eat. We loved it and almost ate their almost every day, and we stayed 14 nights. Our fiirst time in New York from Sydney Austalia and would stay and eat here again! The only thing that takes a little getting used to is the noise from the street, but everything else was perfect for what we needed.

title: “Dog House”
text: There are only two good things to say about this hotel: 1) the close location to the port and 2) the restaurant next door. This place should almost be condemned. The carpet looked as if the doors had been opened for every stray dog in San Pedro to have run of the house. This could be a lovely place to stay when preparing to cruise because of the convenience. The owners should really consider revamping!

title: “Not enough attention to details to be up to Plus status yet”
text:
I am a Best Western Diamond status member and I've stayed at a number of different BW properties. I had 3 specific problems with this particular location. 
First, the wireless access speed was limited to 500 Kb/s downlink, 125 Kb/s up. I tested this on speedtest.net. Pretty much useless. I had to go across the street to the Panera to go fast enough to get any work done. 
Second, there appears to be limited attention, or not quite enough attention to the material condition of the property, as if the financial condition of the business is weak. The pool, advertised to be open in March was empty March 28-29th when it was 77 degrees and sunny, the door-hasp lock, (the one used to prevent access from outside the room) was affixed by very loose screws, such that opening and closing the door eventually caused it to open, and things just kind of had a shoddy feel.
Last, there was work being done on the lobby (it looked like to repair a leak) requiring opening a wall. This was a dusty job, (and loud). Several very ineffectual dust barriers were put up around the lobby, instead of sealing the worksite to minimize impact to the hotel workers, clients, or spaces.
Overall, the hotel feels like it is being run by someone not very involved with day to day operations.

title: “Glad to have been upgraded”
text: We flew to New York for 2 shows and an overnight stay. When we checked into the Millenium, not only were we given an early check-in (it was only 10:30am!), but we were upgraded to a room at The Premier Hotel. The room was big, by NYC standards and included some nice amenities (flat screen tv, coffee pot in room and a decent size bathroom). However, the lighting set up was weird-you could not have one bedside lamp on by itself. The other REALLY annoying thing about the hotel was the towels. They didn't seem to dry very well and, worse than that, they left huge amounts of lint on hands.body, hair. On the plus side-everyone we encountered at the hotel was very, very nice.

title: “Great place to stay, New!”
text: This Staybridge is brand new and the rooms are really comfortable and spacious. The staff was always friendly. The free breakfast was the best perk and free dinners on Tuesday-Thursday. I would definitely recommend to friends and family when they come to Austin.

title: “Nice hotel but beware”
text: Just returned back from the Hotel Chandler so all in all a nice clean hotel right in the middle of Manhattan a stones throw from the Empire State Building so the down side rooms quite small but everything you need ,complimentary Tea & Coffee available 24/7 but beware its located on the outside of the hotel restaurant in the mornings and throughout the day or later just inside make sure you use this and dont go into the restaurant to get a coffee or tea its very expensive ,you can make your own and take up to your room all the cups have lids,just ask at reception if you are in any doubt they are very helpful.So no real complaints about this hotel and would use again

title: “Loved it!”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights and really enjoyed it. The room we stayed in was spacious and nice. The lobby is beautiful. My only complaint was that our room was at the front of the hotel and we could hear the bellmen blowing their whistle for the cabs. Otherwise, we really enjoyed staying here.

title: “Impressed!”
text: Hilton Chicago is one of the most beautiful hotels I've ever stayed in. My room exceeded expectations! I was expecting one full bed, one bath and got double of both!!!! The room also had two closets, a large flat screen tv, and a computer. The computer was very helpful in finding attractions along with directions on getting to them. Although the hotel was packed, staff went above and beyond to make sure customers were happy.

title: “Old, clean hotel in a very inconvenient location”
text: We booked this hotel on Priceline-this hotel is not in walking distance of the Riverwalk at all. It is also several blocks from Market Square. It is simply downtown. It was clean but had a very old feel. I would not stay here again. It is right beside the interstate. There is no breakfast,etc. included. We were on fourth floor and elevators are quite slow.

title: “Great hotel, great deal”
text: Loved the hotel. Got it on priceline for $40 at a total of $51 a night for 3 nights. The rooms were huge. Flat screen and an a.c. that kept things frigid the way I like it. Great location right off beltway 8. I can't think of anything bad to say about the hotel. Maybe a little harder to access if don't make the right turn. Once agin this hotel is a winner.

title: “Normally a good business stop”
text: I have used the Coast Gateway Hotel near the Sea-Tac Airport for many years as a arrival and departure hotel and for a couple of meetings. Generally it is a decent place to stay. Rooms are clean but small, very convenient location. I have only had one bad night here and that was because of an extremely loud individual next door and his buddy who had a women there for awhile and played loud music and were very loud themselves. They slammed doors non-stop. I complained to the front desk twice and though they called the room asking them to keep it down the noise was louder, including the door being intentionally slammed very hard after the 2nd call from the front desk. The noise was from 230 to 530am when the individual finally went to sleep. The hotel did not offer me any compensation or change of rooms for a loss of a nights sleep. I stay here 16 nights a year and would have expected better treatment. The front desk is pretty lethargic and not very helpful at times. They take a hold on your credit card for incidentals even though there is no bar, restaurant or services in the hotel which I find irritating. Parking is sometimes very difficult because the hotel shares a parking lot with a busy BBQ place next door and I believe some people park there who have taken flights. Beds are comfortable and when quiet I have always rested well here. Several good places to eat within walking distance. And you can't get any closer to the airport than here.

title: “Pretty Good Hotel”
text:
The Skyline Hotel has a lot going for it.
Its in a good location for the Times Square/Broadway/7th Avenue area (about 10 minutes walk away).
Excellent service by the staff
Pleasant, clean rooms
A swiming pool (only opens early mornings and evenings)
The local area on 9th and 10th Avenues has a lot of bars, restaurants, delis and takeaways to cater for most tastes and pockets.
The local area seems safe, but slightly scruffy. So make sure you check Google street view before you book then you have an idea of what its like nearby.
To keep the costs down we went for the smallest twin rooms. Overall, these were bettter than I expected and at the back of the hotel (so less traffic noise), but the thin walls meant we could hear the nearby lifts (this was a minor problem for us)

title: “Disappointing and not what I expected at all”
text:
I so wanted to like this hotel and we were very excited to stay there, but I just ended up feeling disappointed. Our original costing was 290GBP for three nights plus tax but we ended up paying well over 400 GBP (including only one evening meal and without breakfast). This was after we had paid for all of the little taxes, parking fee, parking tax, green tax, city tax etc etc. The receipt was endless. I paid up feeling I could have booked somewhere far nicer for around that sum.
The building itself is an old motel which has, quite simply, just been painted over. I like what they are aiming to do and support the ethos but it just struck me as strange that they spent so much time and money putting up pictures of ducks and strange scratchy headboards in the rooms but the paintwork inside and outside is just shabby and undermines their efforts. The bathroom door had an ancient sign half painted over and it just seemed hurried and not well finished or particularly clean. On top of this the place has a strange smell and other than the bed, which was clean, I always felt a bit grubby there, even though the cleaners did the best they could.
The other problem was with getting some sleep. Although the bed was quite comfortable, the air con was ancient and old and made a huge amount of noise. When we couldn't bear it any more we switched if off but we could then hear the unit in the next door room through the paper thin walls. On another night some people stayed up late drinking and talking right outside our door which was also a bit frustrating when there was a whole huge bar area downstairs.
The location is good in that there is great shopping and a wonderful farmer's market just across the road, as well as nice cafes and a particularly good sandwich place down the road on the corner. We ate at Tart once but didn't eat there again, though the staff were great.
I liked the people and the atmosphere and so wanted to like this quirky place, but for the price and with the lack of sleep and feel of cleanliness, I just couldn't appreciate it.

title: “Great location...average hotel”
text:
This hotel was in an excellent location, literally round the corner from Central Park and right nr the subway. In New York you can't get a hotel which is nr everything as it's such a big city but this location was definatly one of the best, the furthest things away from us where the statue of liberty and world trade centre site as they were both down in the financial district. 
We were only there 4 days but managed to fit quite alot in, we went to the empire state building, maddame tussauds, Times square, World trade centre site, statue of liberty, central park, battery park, and also shopping on 5th avenue.
We never used the buses while we were there we always used the subway which was only $3. But to be honest you can walk to times sq from this hotel.
Only problem was the staff at the front desk were quite rude, we only ever ate breakfast in the hotel which was nice, quite a bit to choose from.

title: “First night was terrible!!! But the rest of the stay was fantastic!!”
text: Great hotel in a great position nice and close to Time Square. We were travelling as a family of 2 adults and 2 young children and received a great rate of $240 a night. After a long 30 hours trek from Australia we were looking forward to a good nights sleep and were excited to reach the hotel! We were given a room on the 8th floor (I have a feeling all hot-wire booking receive this floor....the lowest floor at the hotel), that had an adjoining room door. The beds were really comfy and we were having a great sleep until we were awoken at 1am by slamming doors and a party being thrown in the next room! We could hear their conversations clear as day even though they had music pumping as well so I rang security and they came up to tell them to keep the noise down. The "party' then decided to take themselves off to a bar, and things returned back to normal until we were once again awoken at 5am this time to the smell of marijuana wafting into our room!!!!!!! The walls were absolute paper thin and this time there was no music we could still hear there conversations clear as day, i was too nervous to ring security because I knew if we could hear them they could also hear us, so I decided to line towels underneath the gap in the adjoining room door way to block the smell and tried to get some sleep. At 7am I decided to ring the front desk and spoke to them about our horrible nights sleep and I was transferred to the manager to discuss the situation. To there credit they then upgraded us to a better room on the 28th floor for the rest of our stay. Now this room was amazing...... completely different experience and so quiet!!!!! If we had of been given this room from the start of our stay i would have definitely given this hotel a ratting of 5/5!

title: “an all around great place to stay”
text: especially all the staff members were very friendly people who tried to help me with whatever they can. comfort in is going to be my first choice in my next visit to ny.

title: “Fairfield Inn Good locations”
text: Ok, the room was small and there was no bar or restaurant but free breakfast was more than I expected and everything was refilled very fast. The room was clean. But the staff! They were the BEST. Very very friendly and helpful. Good location. Easy walk to most places - We did had to walk down the block for a taxi. We go to NYC about 3 to four times a year will stay here again. Make sure they stamp your parking ticket you will save money.. One minus, Only one Elevator was working and there was a big rush at check out time.

title: “Seen Boston already?”
text:
I live 20 miles outside Boston and my wife and I come into town quite often for a late dinner and a night over. I use priceline quite often and decided to try 4 stars /S.Boston,waterfront area. Knowing that the only 4 star properties available would include the Westin, I gave 100 bucks a shot. Sure enough, the Westin took it.
My comments on the hotel are as follows:
valet parking is pricey @ 36 bucks.
flat panel tv in room is a nice touch
The hotel is brand new so all of the bathroom fixtures, tub etc are clean and the bathroom mirror is great.
Legal Test Kitchen is a not your regular Legal Sea Food restaurant. Great place for dinner only 2 blocks away on D St. and an easy walk from the hotel.
I would recommend this hotel for someone attending a conference next door. Also, perfect for a copule that lives in New England who wants to try something new but doesn't feel the need to stay downtown to do the sightseeing thing.
Paul H.
Acton,MA

title: “Does what it says on the tin!!”
text:
My boyfriend and I have just returned from a trip to NYC and stayed at this hotel for 4 nights. We booked our flights well in advance but left booking a hotel rather late and as a result were unable to get rooms in our preferred locations. Many of the negative reviews seemed to be centred around the basement rooms so to counter this we telephoned the hotel direct and specifically requested a room above ground level!! 
The hotel is located on a fairly quiet street in midtown.The common areas and rooms are painted in rather drap institutional beige colours which is not very encouraging when you first get there. The corridors were narrow and as already stated there is no lift so it may mean lugging your bags yourself. 
Our room was a medium size with no views to speak of. The bathroom was surprisingly big with a bath tub aswell as a shower. It appeared to be newly tiled. The water temperature ranged from warm to warmy hot ( never hotty hot - which was a disappointment.) The whole place was spotlessly clean and given the wooden floors there was not a spec of dust ....even under the bed! The bed was small but adequate.The air con was efficient, adjustable and pretty quiet
 We met another couple who had a very small room but we managed a peek into one of the front rooms overlooking the street which seemed much bigger and a bit swankier than ours.

title: “Family-5 JAX”
text:
Family of 5 stayed at this hotel, 25-26 May, 2012, during JAX trip to attend the U.S. Men's Soccer game vs. Scotland. My first requirement for choosing this hotel was their capacity to accommodate 2 adults and 3 kids in a single room. Second requirement was a good location, in terms of a short drive to downtown. This hotel definitely met those requirements. 
Rooms were fairly up-to-date, clean and comfortable. Was surprised to find a good-sized bathroom, with an also up-to-date fit and finish. Wi-Fi access in the room was sometimes challenging, but once connected, worked fine. Complimentary morning breakfast was the standard Choice Hotels spread of breads, pastries, cereals, yogurt, waffles and a couple of hot items (rotating each morning). As with many hotels, the breakfast crowd exceeded capacity during peak hours, but they would set out the food items earlier than the published schedule, so early-risers could beat the crowd. Also, there is a Wendy's fastfood restaurant adjacent to the hotel. I believe there was a pool and fitness center, also on-site, but our schedule didn't allow time for those.
If we ever need to return to JAX and need a hotel within a short drive to downtown, this would be our pick.

title: “Family Fun Weekend”
text: Stayed here for the weekend with the family, a most enjoyable stay. Grounds were beautiful. Pools were ideally located. Convenient access to the freeways, shopping.

title: “SCC Retreat”
text:
We were welcomed upon our arrival by very pleasant helpful Registration personnel.The rooms are spacious; clean the beds are very comfortable.
Our group required a meeting place and we had at our disposal a large dining area. Since we were having a BBQ both Saturday afternoon and evening we were given the outside BBQ area with a pool off the main kitchen. Utinsels were made available for our use.
The full breakfast consisted of boiled eggs; make your own waffles; toast; and bagels. There were various fruits and sweet rolls available plus coffee and milk for cereals. 
We felt very welcomed and at home and will no doubt be back next year.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: This is a really beautiful hotel. The staff was very professional and friendly. the rooms are really gorgeous. Our room consisted of 2 rooms, the bedroom and a small living room. The hotel is centrally located, and there is lots of shopping all around it. I would definitely recommend.

title: “Beautiful hotel but scared my kid to death with the fire alarms!”
text:
I have to join the others in reporting the fire alarms. It happened TWICE during our stay and we were on the 8th floor so my kid was NOT happy. It was absolutely terrifying to run down 8 flights in a cramped stairwell. The first time it was 6 AM and the second was 1:30 AM. I had just convinced my daughter it was a fluke and wouldn't happen again when the second one occured. After the 2nd alarm, I talked to the front desk and they assured me management would call me which never happened. I looked into getting in a different hotel but this was July 4th weekend! Since we were stuck, I asked them to move us to the first floor which they did. Exhausted after not going to sleep until 3 AM, we had to pack all of our things and move. We almost missed the tour we had planned for the day. Also, it seems most of the staff we talked to were new and hadn't been working there long so they didn't know how to handle issues such as this. 
Overall it's a nice hotel in a great location. I felt much safer traveling with a small child in the Woodley Park area than if we were closer to downtown. Next time I would probably look into staying at the Marriott which is one block away.

title: “The Angeleno Hotel was a lifesaver!!!!”
text:
My family from Ohio was on a trip to California for 10 days -- 7 in LA and 3 in SD. Originally, we had our hotel reservation at the Comfort Inn & Suites in Hollywood for all 7 nights we were staying in LA. There was a huge problem at the Comfort Inn (see my review on this hotel!!!!!) and fortunately while we were waiting to check in there I called around and the Hotel Angeleno had rooms for us for all 7 nights. With AAA we received a rate for right at $150.00 a night. 
My daughter was attending basketball camp at UCLA and this hotel is only 5 minutes or so from Pauley Pavilion so that worked out great. We didn't consider this hotel earlier because it wasn't really near any attractions, however we had a car and it didn't matter anyway. 
This hotel is located right off of the 405 and is a short distance away from the beaches of Malibu and Santa Monica.
The 17 story hotel is a former Holiday Inn and has undergone a huge renovation recently. We were VERY PLEASED with our stay here.
The valet parking is $18.00/day which is a little steep but we ended up being "comped" our entire parking fees which was just great. The valet parkers work extremely hard and are very, very pleasant. The front desk workers were helpful as well. Several times they printed off directions for us on how to get somewhere and were informative on some ideas we had during our trip.
All rooms here have a private balcony. The room we had was on the backside and faced a group of condiminiums. Some face the 405 and others the parking lot. Our room had a HUGE bathroom and all the necessities and the shower was awesome. We kept some of our luggage underneat the sink it was so large!!!
The beds were incredible. They were high off the ground and very soft. We had a double bed room and both beds were good size. We had a flat screen TV and it had a great picture. There were drawers and a closet to store our clothes in too. We did not have a desk, but did not need one anyway.
The restaurant/night club on the 17th floor appeared to be very nice and it had a great view. We didn't eat there as a family although my spouse went there to get a take-out cheeseburger.
Overall, this was a great experience for my family. What looked like a total disaster to begin with ended up being just a great week for us in LA. I highly reccommend this hotel to all of you. This is a very clean hotel. The pool area is nice and has a workout room with weights and treadmills attatched to it.

title: “very good choice”
text:
I and my partner stayed at the Hilton for four nights for a long weekend in New York. The hotel is in the downtown area but easily accessible with public transport and a taxi ride to midtown is about $ 17. 
We arrived after a transatlantic flight in the evening and were immediately whisked in with the luggage all taken care of. The receptionist (Angie I think her name was) was extremely helpful as our request were a smoking room and a high floor. She excelled at this and we were given a fantastic room on the 54th floor overlooking ground zero and the Brooklyn Bridge. The room was exceptionally large by New York standards and had all the amnesties you could wish for: good internet connection (for a very reasonable $12/day), LCD TV, mini bar, large bathroom and excellent bed. The service overall was very efficient and friendly. The concierge helped us making restaurant reservations and taxis were flagged down very quickly.
The only downside of the stay was the varying service in the bar next to the lobby. The prices for the very same drink orders seem to vary between staff and at one point the bar tender refused to allow us to take the drinks upstairs (his explanation was that they were short of that particular style of glasses, well then order some more).
There are limited choices in the area for good food, but we tried Les Halles on 15 John St which was a good basic choice, 2 minutes from the hotel. Other than that you may have to travel a bit to get high quality restaurants. We loved Lever House Restaurant on 390Park Avenue.
I can highly recommend the Millenium Hilton (even if the spelling annoys me) and considering the normally ridiculous room rates in New York the Hilton is definitely a bargain.

title: “Extremely nice, comfortable hotel - great value”
text: I got the Hilton Garden Inn on a Priceline deal during a quick business trip to Houston. I've never stayed at a Hilton Garden-Inn, but had a great night at this Houston location. The HGI in general was extremely clean, very well decorated, and had a nice lobby and lounge and breakfast area. My room was huge, really huge, including the bathroom. Although it didn't have a couch, there was a nice desk area, along with a coffee maker, microwave and refrigerator. It was very functional and comfortable, and I would stay there again.

title: “You can't go wrong here--and this is coming from a hotel guy.”
text: Everything was flawless. If you have been finding it very difficult to make a decision and commit to a hotel in NYC, just choose this one. You can't go wrong--the service was personalized, people remembered my name, the amenities/soft goods/case goods were in great condition, and the location is outstanding. I will for sure be staying at this property whenever I visit the city.

title: “Fast and efficient service.”
text: Wow, the staff was so attentive and fast! Whenever I needed anything the front desk must have had the staff on speed dial all of the time. There was about 2 different times I needed extra towels and within 2 minutes of calling the front desk there was someone knocking on my door with fresh towels. It was to the point where I almost wanted to time how fast they would deliver service. Thanks for being so attentive and I can honestly say, very few hotels provide the fast service you guys do.

title: “Great place to stay in LA!”
text: Excellent location! Felt very comfortable. Short walk to Brentwood Village (where there are excellent resturants) and located in a safe area. Short car ride to Santa Monica and to other popular attractions. Excellent service, complimentary breakfast pastries in the morning and cookies in the evening. Very clean and modern decor. Excellent value!

title: “Super location, very clean hotel. First floor could be little noisy.”
text: Super location, very clean hotel. First floor could be little noisy.

title: “This hotel made our trip!”
text: Inn at the Opera was a very pleasant surprise: a slice of old San Francisco lodgings with completely modern amenities. Their personnel were attentive and accomadating, their restaurant superb, and their lodgings absolutely wonderful. Located a block from city hall, the hotel allows you to access any part of old San Francisco with a $10 cab ride. Absolutely the best!

title: “Overall, A Really Good Experience”
text: First off, if you are exploring the Art Museum area (Franklin Institute, Natural Science's, etc), you can't beat the location. It is right off the Parkway. Check in was really easy and the staff was absolutely wonderful and helpful. Concierge and bellmen were great and very knowledgable. One of the bellmen actually check to see if he had change to give us for the subway. It is a little far if walking to Old City of Historic areas, but you can walk to City Hall to catch the El. Hotel is starting to show its age in rooms, but lobby and common areas are still very nice. With a small room update, this hotel could really soar. Philly hotels can be really expensive, for not much value, so if you can get this hotel for a decent price, you should not be disappointed.

title: “VERY disappointing ...”
text: I came to Chicago with one of my staff for a trade show at the Navy Pier.
