This hotel was listed in the hotel package, had great pictures of their rooms and talked about their million dollar renovation. I thought it would be a nice change to stay at a 'boutique' hotel instead of the usual Sheraton, Hyatt, etc. Boy was I surprised when I arrived! The location is awesome but the check-in staff were terribly rude (what happened to customer service training?). There appeared to be a lot of people just hanging around in the lobby who were 'friends' of the staff. I got on the elevator and felt claustrophobic and wondered if I'd ever reach the 5th floor. When I got to my room, I wondered where the million dollars had been spent (maybe the prisms in the front windows were diamonds?). The room and bathroom were the smallest I'd ever seen - made European ones look huge! The window air conditioner was noisy (yes a window air conditioner!), windows hadn't been washed in a l-o-o-o-o-n-g time and the lock on the adjoining door didn't work properly. I immediately called downstairs (after trying to find another hotel in the area that could take us) and checked out. What a surprise - I was met with a very friendly voice who apologized for the inconvenience and wished me a good stay in Chicago. We left and went up the street to the 4 Points Sheridan on Rush Street. The staff were awesome, hotel exactly what I would expect for downtown Chicago but expensive.

title: “Excellent location, good value for the money”
text: Stayed for four nights on business/pleasure (Bruce Springsteen...). Rooms are comfortable, location is just great for Market St. meetings and just wandering the streets of Philli.

title: “disappointed”
text: i have stayed here before and previously quite liked this hotel due to close proximity to my various meetings I need to attend in the city, the White House, and great restaurants nearby. All this still is true of course. I just found the hotel rather dated, despite them undergoing renovations. The hotel room was small and dingy, carpets were not clean in the room or hallway. The executive lounge pathetic and tired. Even the 8pm free cookies looked old and the coffee machine didn't work in the lounge. I used to love the work-out center attached. It is now a new place called Mint. It's still a great workout place but unless you are Hilton Honors costs $15. There are certain things you expect now in good hotels such as iphone chargers in rooms that they just haven't gotten around to yet. For the price I think the Jefferson has nicer rooms. I hear the Westin nearby is decent and a lot less expensive.

title: “The clock stopped at The Burnham”
text: The Burnham is a treat, old style Chicago building in the Loop and close to businesses and entertainment. The restaurant and bar are superb (I am a fan of bloody marys and crabcakes). Its all cozy and warm without seeming small. I've stayed there about 5 times and keep going back. Superb service and...its pet friendly. Kind of nice to see a friendly pooch or two when I'm away from home.

title: “Great service.”
text: My husband and I stayed here as an early Valentine's celebration. The staff was very informative and accommodating.. especially Ahmad Bellman. He let us know about all of the hotel amenities and services with a friendly attitude, great sense of humor, and genuine kindness. We have stayed at The Westin before and each time it is continual great service. We have decided to use this hotel for all of our vacation stays from now on. The only suggestion I would make would be to not charge for Wi-fi or other amenities. I have been to other lower scale hotels that let you use wi-fi for free and also offer you little travel items you may have forgotten without charge.

title: “Great stay!”
text:
We just spend 5 nights at this hotel and we're very pleased with it. As the other reviewers mentioned, the rooms were small but clean. Hotel staff is very friendly and efficient. Location is great. We paid an avarage rate of $ 165 plus tax (fri -wed)
I've got just two more things to add to what has already been said about this hotel:
1. There now is luggage storage available for $ 3.00 a bag and they will store it for a maximum of 24 hours
2. Bring your earplugs! There is a lot of street noise because of the location.
We can highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Very nice for the price”
text: THe hotel itself is very nice. THe rooms are large and a fridge/micro is in the rooms. There is a convience store across the street as well. Each room has free high speed internet. The only downside is the breakfast is kind of lame. The typical continental, plus you can make your own waffels. The staff is very nice and courteous. Would recommend to those that are in the area to stay here. Our rate was 58/night king.

title: “Good value. Good service. Good location. Tiny room.”
text:
Pros:
-Clean
-Excellent, service-oriented staff
-Good location just off of Union Square
-Free wireless Internet (some offers)
-Comfortable, queen-size bed
-Some non-smoking rooms
-Soft, fluffy towels
-Jar of mints in room (nice touch)
Cons:
-Tiny room (really tiny)
-No air conditioning
-Wireless reception erratic (sometimes fine; sometimes took 10 minutes to load one page)
-cracked, chipped and peeling paint in bathroom

title: “Lovely”
text:
We stayed here for three nights in a superior apartment.
The room was very large with plenty of storage space. 
We were facing the courtyard which we did not particularily mind, as it meant a quiet room, or so I thought! The noise from the air conditioner unit was very loud.
The apartment had fresh flowers in, the toiletries were kiehl's, the towels fluffy, all in all a wonderful stay.
One thing that really did spoil it was on our last day, in the morning the maid knocked on our door, and without actually blatantly asking for a tip, it was as bad as, she kept asking if the room was up to our standard, which of course it was, nevertheless we did not expect the maid to knock on the door and blatantly ask for a tip. The hotel should train their staff a bit better!
In the 21st century and in the USA I did expect the hotel to provide complimentary wifi, but was dissapointed that it did not. I can not remember the price of connecting, but it was expensive.
Room service was a ridiculous price, almost $25 for a pot of coffee, the mini bar prices were unbelievable, a small bottle of water was around $9 (you can get a large bottle of exactly the same brand for $2 in the local shops!)
The Carlyle has an understated elegance, and definitly worth the stay.

title: “Committed Staff”
text: I specifically needed an ethernet cable connection to the Internet due to my work. We tried connecting in our first room but with no avail. The hotel sent their Internet technician, Ramon, to our room to help us out. He was so committed to helping us and wouldn't give up until everything was right. We even tried to tip him as a thank you but he politely refused. Once things were fixed and settled the hotel comped our Internet usage for the day. I would recommend The Westin to anyone traveling to San Diego.

title: “Excellent value for families”
text:
This was our second stay at The Bedford. We stayed 5 years ago when kids were much smaller - now aged 18 and 15 (boy & girl) we decided on the same hotel as a suite was much cheaper than 2 separate bedrooms in any comparable hotel.
The room had a large living area with 2 sofa beds - perfect for the kids, and also a small kitchenette with fridge, and ironing facilities. Whilst we were in a separate double bedroom. The only drawback being a single bathroom only accessible through the bedroom, but we managed perfectly fine.
Staff were efficient and helpful.
The hotel is handily placed right by Grand Central Station, and Chrysler Building. Empire State Building was viewable from our "living room", and 5th Avenue and Times Square are only a couple of blocks away.
Room, bedding, towels, etc all clean and tidy - TVs are old large models.
All in all excellent value particularly if you are travelling as a family (or indeed a group).

title: “unexpectedly clean and the staff was very kind”
text: I was in town on business was nervous about the location, I needed to be near St Davids and I was going to be walking. I called the hotel several times before booking my room. Joseph was so profestional made me feel comfortable. When I checked in the clerk must of read notes on my reservation because he made sure i was facing the lobby second floor.Made sure I felt safe. I feell the staff there went above there call of duty to make me feel safe. I will be staying there again for sure.

title: “Nice and Peaceful”
text:
Stayed here for a night to attend a wedding and we're not dissappointer. The hotel room
looks a little bit old, AC is a lil bit loud but overall it was a pleasnt stay.

title: “We like this hotel!”
text:
What can be better than a room with the view of the empire state building? I got excited when I was told my room had such a symbolic view. Originally I just booked the regular room which did not have the view. After I completed my booking, I got an email from the hotel asking if I would like to join the eStandby list which would allow me to upgrade my room to the city view room ( the one with the empire state view) for just $9 per day if they were available. So I thought, why not? Turns out, my decision is right! 
Speaking of the other aspects of the hotel, the room is relatively small. But given it's in NYC, I guess that's reasonable. After all, we still felt very comfortable. The service is good, the staff are very helpful. And most importantly, it's just less than 1 min walk from the hotel to subway station, 5 min walk to Macy's, 10min walk to Korean town where you can find food. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

title: “Nothing Spectacular, Especially for the Price”
text:
I like the Westin and most of the whole Starwood brand, but I certainly expected a bit more for the very steep price of $299 per night. Getting charged $11 for in room internet service was cheesy at best. The room was not all that large, and the usual bathrobe was nowhere to be found. Not much to eat - just a Starbucks in the basement/ground floor. The soap was a thin bar wrapped in cheap plastic - I certainly miss the Heavenly Soap that used to be wrapped in foil. 
What else - not enough towels, plenty of noise, not much of a view from the 6th floor. Don't get me wrong, its certainly a step up from the Motel 6. Can't beat the beds, nice work area, good temperature control, efficient check in, etc. 
But, for $300 a night in Denver, I'm expecting a lot more.

title: “Great location”
text: We stayed from April 17-April 25, 2006 with husband, and two children 7 and 10. Hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. Not a place to stay if you have trouble with stairs. The hotel is built on a hillside and each building has stairs. Has a parking ramp available for hotel guests. Only trouble with parking was on a Saturday night, find your spot early and stay in Old Town. Pool area was beautiful and gardens/grounds well tended. Rooms were clean, quiet and comfortable. The bathroom could use some updating. Nice to have a micro/fridge in room. Would have like to have a continental breakfast, but they did have good coffee in the lobby. Breakfast was expensive at onsite restraurant but we found a pretty good breakfast at O'Hungry's for $2.99 each just down the street. Lots of restraurants/bars within walking distance in Old Town with great Happy Hour specials on drinks and appetizers. Fun shopping as well. You can find more restraurants on the west side of Hwy 5 off of Taylor Street. Old Town is a great location, close to Zoo, Sea World, Downtown, Marina, Balboa Park, etc. We would stay here again.

title: “Beware of early checkout scam”
text:
I reserved three nights recently at the Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia. Due to a change in plans, I had to depart after my second night. When I called the front desk to inform them of my plans, they told me that I would be charged $75 as an "early check-out fee". Needless to say I was outraged and after much cajoling (including calling Hilton's National Reservation Number), they agreed to remove the charge.
They are counting on business travelers to blow-off the charge. The room was nice and it could not be more centrally-located. However, shady business practices always give me pause when considering various hotels.

title: “Fantastic room, fun hotel”
text:
I was looking for somewhere special to stay for a couple of nights in Seattle and picked The Alexis. I had read the reviews about building work and contacted the hotel about it. They confirmed that the work would be finished before I arrived so I booked a room.
I booked a spa suite and it was great with a huge bath in a massive bathroom. The room had a comfortable bed and a nice amount of space.
We arrived late in the evening and we asked concierge for a suggestion for getting a pizza or similar and they suggested we order a takeout and get it delivered to the room which we did. Nice of the hotel to allow food in to the room when the restaurant was closed.
Brunch was tasty in the Library Bistro, the Breakfast menu was less inspiring.
The hotel is a lot of fun, drawing on the table, painting postcards in the evening at the wine reception. The staff were all lovely and I enjoyed the stay very much.
For the price of the suite perhaps some breakfast could be included or maybe a small selection of drinks in the room, even just bottles of water rather than high priced mini bar produce but these are minor grumbles I have with most hotels.

title: “Decor Dated/Staff... so so”
text:
I'm a SPG Platinum member, so I thought I'd get an upgrade... Not.
On the plus side, the location is very good. Very central.
As many other have noted, the decor is dated. They still even have storage boxes at the reception for physical keys. It's obvious they haven't renovated in a long-long time.
In my bathroom, part of the wall had deteriorated (about the size of a half-dollar) and you could see rust around the edges.
I tried to register early, but my room wasn't ready, so the staff said they would hold it in storage and would deliver it to my room when it was ready. When I got back that evening, it was still in storage downstairs.

title: “Absolutely loved this hotel (location a little far from the action, though)”
text:
Oh my gosh! STAY HERE! This hotel was absolutely gorgeous! We stayed here for 3 nights and loved it. It is a little far from the downtown area for my taste, but based on the hotel condition and the rates, well worth the drive. We had an executive king and our room looked like it was brand-spanking new! The sheets were on the thin side, but they fit the mattress and never came loose. They also had a continental breakfast that a lot of hotels would envy. The staff on arrival and checkout were very accommodating. I'm not sure what the previous traveler was complaining about with the light coming in; there are shades that can be drawn to eliminate the light, however the room lighting with them drawn may have been a little dim for some people (maybe that's what they meant?).
When we come back to Memphis, we would like to stay a little closer to Beale Street (so as to not have to drive and park), but would not think twice to stay here again if there was nothing available in the downtown area at a reasonable rate.

title: “Excellent Staff”
text: Helix Hotel is a great place to be in DC! All of the staff that you encounter are amazing and adorable. The sleeping rooms are very large; however the bathroom is very small. Room service was great. I would definitely reccommend Helix to anyone traveling to DC on business. If you are traveling with a family...there is no pool. It is a bit far from a metro station, but a beautiful hotel and top notch staff!

title: “Weary, worn out look”
text: While my room was adequate, the hotel public spaces were quite dreary and worn. At least two of the computers on the main floor to which I was directed to print out my boarding pass were not connected to the printer next to them. If there were athletic facilities, I never found them. There were no materials in the room on hotel services and amenities. The location is not so hot either, away from restaurants.

title: “Nice Hotel!”
text: We stayed 3 nights here for the NHRA U.S. Nationals. The hotel was easy for find from the airport, which is a real plus, especially if you are flying in after dark. The room was clean and had a great layout! It was nice to have the tv in a separate living area. The beds and pillows were extremely comfortable. The vanity area could be a bit bigger. But I realize this airport is utilized mainly by people on business trips and are they are usually by themselves, so the vanity issue is probably no big thing to them. Breakfast was efficient and tasty. If you are looking for a full sized breakfast then this is not the place for you. The onsite restaurant makes sandwiches and meals 24 hours a day which is really handy if you are coming in after the restaurants in the area close. Last, this Hyatt was, in my opinion, the nicest hotel for the price that we paid.

title: “Fabulous Hotel!”
text: We spent Easter weekend at the Driskill this year and it was absolutely worth the money! The entire building is beautiful, historic and classy. The entire hotel staff was very professional and warm and friendly! The hotel bar is huge, comfortable and beautiful! The King size bed in our room was top of the line comfy! I can't say one bad word about The Driskill, well, one thing...I did not like paying the $28 per day mandatory valet service. But overall, everyone should take the time and money to experience a hotel like this, even if it you can only do it once in your life. Please do remember that all the rooms are different and have different layouts. I called and talked to a reservation specialist to make sure I knew exaclty what kind of room we were getting.

title: “Great Location! Good Prices!”
text:
While I did not personally stay here during my visit, I did have friends who did and did attend a workshop on location.
The location is great and central to all things Chicago and the rooms are typical Hilton Doubletree rooms. 
The meeting space was good and the catered meals were outstanding! 
Highly recommend either for a stay or a meeting.

title: “Lesson Number One!!”
text: Lesson number one is to bear in mind that the hotel is situated in Little Tokyo Los Angeles Downtown hence it's prime clientele is of Japenese origin. All other groupings are welcomed. The hotel itself is clean and well maintained. It has a restatuarant on the second floor and adjacent to it is a sport bar. The rooms are of moderate size and has no built-in cupboard (the Japenese sytle/taste). Next to the room entry there is a rail with coat hangers to utilize. They provide a bar fridge for private usage (ensure you switch it off on checking out). The bathroom is well styled. Behind the hotel, there is the Little Tokyo Shopping Mall. For transportation, there is always two "Yellow Cabs" (not the New York version but a LA registered copycat) parked outside. Otherwise one can surf the LAmetro website for bus and rail transport. Wifi is free throughout the hotel and in the foyer there are two flat screen PCs for free utilization next to a Coffee Shop. Also available in the foyer is a gift shop. The hotel is surrounded by various shops and cafes catering mostly Japenese taste.

title: “Great property, great price”
text: Just returned from a 2 night stay at the Springhill Suites in Jacksonville and I must say that this was a great property for the price paid. The room/desk area/bathroom was very clean and everything was in working order. The continental breakfast was standard, food was hot and plenty to choose from. Front desk staff was more than helpful with cancelling another reservation, getting us a few more towels and with directions. The hotel was close (within 10 miles) to the ALLTEL Stadium as well as the downtown area. There are plenty of restaurants in close proximity to the hotel-even a few within walking distance. I would definitely stay at this property again.

title: “Overpriced, shabby rooms, nice resort”
text: We arrived late for an overnight here. They had screwed up our reservation and we had 4 adults and two toddlers in a room with one bed and two cribs. The night security guard and desk clerk were very helpful and helped us schlep all our luggage from one end of the hotel to the other to a room that fit our original reservation for 2 beds and 2 cribs. The bathroom was very small and the room looked like it needed a refurb, being rather worn with an ancient HVAC system. It was very humid and the AC could not deal with it so we were cool and clammy, rather than cool. Shockingly, the beds were only double, not queen. The grounds around the facility and resort property were very nice and there was a lot to do. If you could stay here for the "amenities" and get it under $200 a night it might be worth it. Otherwise I would look at other "resort" type facilities in the area as you could likely do better.

title: “My wife and I were only in Chicago for a...”
text: My wife and I were only in Chicago for a quick few days, and were looking for a hotel that would be a good jumping off point for a cram-packed schedule (mass transit nearby, busy streets where you could easily flag a cab), at a decent price. Days Inn, in Lincoln Park, neatly fit the bill. Casey checked us in quickly and was full of advice on just about anything I asked about. He became my go-to guy for the next 3 days! At one point, he suggested we check out a specific local band, and even checked online to see when and where they were playing. As well, any of the other guys I talked to on the staff for our stay, were helpful and cool. It's like they staffed the joint with a bunch of my friends from college! Real comfortable. Real convenient. And real cool. I will be telling my friends to stay here in the future.

title: “rooms are clean and elegant”
text: rooms are very clean, nice bedding, friendly staff, great location. no coffee maker in the room, valet parking is $42 for overnight.

title: “Really nice boutique hotel”
text: I just spent 3 nights at the Monaco early in June and was extremely happy with this hotel. This is a medium size hotel, not overwhelming like too many giant business hotels in Chicago. The design is really nice and my room was quite large and comfortable. Bed was perfect, bathroom was OK, free Internet access very convenient, the big plus in my opinion was the large window with an alcove that provides prime views of the river. Spent hours there watching the activity on the street and the buildings around. Downtown location was convenient, not too far from multiple shopping destinations and from the new Millenium park (outstanding!). I wasn't blown away by the service but it was fine overall. All in all, I found this hotel a great value for the location, design and comfort. Will certainly go back.

title: “One minor, really, complaint”
text: Hubby and I stayed here for three nights while visiting family. The room, staff, bar and location were all top notch. Housekeeping and even turn down service. Very high end for the price. One teeny complaint, even on a higher floor and a corner room, we could not leave our drapes open because of complete lack of privacy. Definitely not the hotels fault that he buildings are so tight, but I'm a Florida girl and I missed my sunshine in the morning. It felt kinda gloomy but, as said, a really teeny complaint compared to everything else. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Meeting”
text:
I recently operated a program at the Westin Riverwalk. I cannot say enough good things. First and foremost the staff are the most friendly, courteous and helpful hotel staff that I have dealt with in a long time. My attendees even commented on how friendly the staff was.
As a meeting planner I very much appreciated the attentiveness of the staff to every detail of the meeting. I would like to give a huge shout out to the audio/visual company on site, PSAV, who were amazing. They went above and beyond what was required of them. I did not have one problem with any of their equipment. They were always there first thing in the morning double checking everything to ensure I had a great day.

title: “New York City”
text:
New York City, April 2009
My husband and I finally made it New York City this Spring and had a wonderful trip. We stayed at the Wyndham Midtown which was very clean and convenient to all attractions. It's a rehabbed place so the bedding & carpeting was new. Continental breakfast was included in our stay & they have a little patio in the back. The bathroom was very spacious which is unusual for NYC. We flew into JFK from St. Louis (Lambert) and then took the A-train & subway to Penn Station. We then walked to our hotel. The hop on hop off bus was perfect for our first two days there. The views from the top are amazing. After that we used our Metro Card for the subway which was pretty easy to use. We spent one day at Ellis Island & had purchased our ferry tickets online in advance. We got last minute Letterman tickets, but the highlight of our trip for me was the Broadway show "Blithe Spirit" featuring Angela Lansbury. The food at Dallas Bar-b-que in Times Square was delicious & inexpensive. It's a fun place to visit,, but wear good walking shoes and stop & pick up a map at the Visitor Center when you arrive.

title: “Sometimes it's the housekeepers fault.”
text:
I've seen the reviews. I can no longer speak about the main building only because they no longer allow smoking in that part of the hotel and we are now put in the rooms on the side. (my husband is a smoker) THey have redone their lobby and it looks nice. They've added an office space for internet usage and a very nice exercise facility.
Of course they are trying to update but I'm sure it's expensive to take care of all that needs to be done so I can appreciate the small steps here and there. 
In this case though, the housekeeping staff are the guilty ones for not reporting room issues.
It may be an older room and all but there is no reason for the shower curtain rod to be loose from the wall. Housekeeping should report this so it can be repaired before the next guest checks in.
THe coffee pot, my bad since I didn't realize it should have a lid. I told my husband it was clogged and he went to pull out the filter part to unclog and all the hot water burned his fingers... I guess we needed the pot lid to hold a lever in order for the coffee to automatically drip out. Afterward we made coffee again and held the part with a pen so it would drip out. Housekeepings fault again because they are to check that everything in the room is working and there.
The coffee maker outlet was not working. I tried the reset button and no luck so we had to move rthe maker to another outlet to get it to work. 
 But to their defense on this, if no one has told the hotel the outlet is not working then they can't fix it so now that I've told them, hopefully they will look into that for the next guest..
Yes, I reported the shower curtain rod right away only because I did not want to be blamed for it being broken.
I did leave a comment card in regards to everything else.
My fellow roomates on the other side of the hall were a bit noisy if you know what I mean but once we were in the room and turned on the TV, we did not hear them after that except the doors shutting kind of hard from time to time.
All in all, yes, I'll stay here again. I think the cost is high for the room but as far as the rooms compared to other hotels in the area, this is one of the lowest.
THey always seem to be busy which is a good sign as well.
THe night of my stay, the frontdesk recommended a pizza place and this was the best pizza and philly steak I've ever had. THe name had Cafe in it so if you stay here, definatly ask about this place.
I've learned from tripadvisor that every guest looks at things diferrently and you have to just take the good with the bad and hope for the best. Could this place be better, yes it could but if it was toatlly 100% percent perfect in every way, you'd be paying much more.

title: “Foe the price,, really???”
text:
Okay, the front staff was very nice. The place is very clean. But thats where it stops. They were the host hotel for the marathon. Told the runners they could use the shower after the race because they didnt allow late checkouts. One shower in a gym. What a joke. 
Biggest complaint. The bed, it was tilted downward,and the pillow was so big, noone I knew could even use the pillow. Its good for a pain the the neck. 
The shower head was the size of a baseball and trickled. The entire bathroom was cheap and old.
Just wasnt a quality hotel...

title: “Not so good for families”
text: We just came back from the hotel, we got a deal for only one night which came with free internet and two free breakfasts. The room was very clean, and since there are three of us, we called the front desk for a roll-away bed, but they said they don't allow roll-away beds due to fire codes. Every hotel I have stayed at has had a roll away bed, and I've seen hotel rooms that are bigger and smaller. We asked for a suite upgrade but they weren't available, so I had to sleep on the floor. I personally think they use that fire code excuse so families of three or more have to upgrade, but it doesn't work out when they are sold out of suites, but I think they should cater to families more than couples because it's very close to SeaWorld so I would think mostly families would be staying there. Anyway, the pool area was great. They had two water slides and a small one for little kids. The Red Marlin restaurant was very good but very overpriced, and it seemed like mostly everything was overpriced, but that might be for all Hyatts. Overall, it's a great place to go for rich couples, but if you have a family, I suggest another hotel.

title: “stayed there for a wedding”
text: The wedding was great; we stayed in the hotel for about 4 nights. There were a few issues with cleanliness of one of the rooms and a long wait for food in the hotel restaurant, but the hotel went well above and beyond to make up for it. The people in my party were very impressed. I would highly recommend this hotel for its quality service and fantastic location. Neat rooftop pool, and great atmosphere. I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “OK experience”
text: Stayed here one night prior to moving on to another hotel. Rates are very reasonable. Include waffle and juice breakfast. We had asked for a room not backing on the highway when we reserved 1 month before, but yet that's what we got. The highway is very loud and could be heard in our room. The room did require a good cleaning. I would not stay here longer than 1-2 nights.

title: “First Class all the way!”
text: My son and I stayed here while doing college visits in June. It was very clean, we splurged for the club level and it made our life so easy. When we were ready to head out to our next adventure, we stopped by the lounge grabbed a tea,coffee or water bottle and left. When we were on our way back in, grabbed fruit or a snack. They always had nice food presentation and were always pleasant. The hotel was clean/nice/new.The only glitch was a fire alarm early one morning where we climbed down 24 flights of stairs only to find out if was a false alarm. I felt like someone should have yelled in the stairwell that it was false. It wasnt very comfortable walking in the Ritz Lobby in your pajamas. Great location if you have a car. The concierge was eager to plan and help.I think her name was Patrice. I would stay here again!

title: “Fantastic location, value and comfort”
text:
This New York hotel has what you could expect no almost no matter your needs and demands. Excellent location in TriBeca with walking distance both downtown and uptown to Meatpacking, Union Square, Madison Squre, Greenwich Village, SoHo, Empire State Building, Brooklyn Bridge etc. With good shoes you could even walk to Central Park. If wearing high heals or sandals, the subway takes you everywhere, and the Canal Steet Station is 10 meters from the hotel. Large and spacious rooms with all necessary facilities, and tidy and accurate cleaning.
We stayed there for 8 days and was a group of 6 aged around 30-32. .
TriBeca is a great location close by the most beautiful locations in New York. TriBeca also offers some of New Yorks best restaurants and many celebrities has their favorite pubs & clubs here. We actually met 2 large movie/TV stars going for dinner in TriBeca.
Would recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Great Hotel In The Time Square Area”
text:
This hotel is a perfect choice if it fits your budget and you are looking for a hotel in the Time Square area.
It is only 2 minutes (walking) from Time Square. The staff is very professional, even the way that they handle your credit card back to you is very gentle ! ... The Concierge team is knowledgeable and friendly.
The rooms are modern and equipped with some necessary tech's. The bathroom has an electronic toilet that is heated and has a remote for controlling the toilet functions.
One down-side is that they have no printer or a business center, however, they asked me to send the document to them and they printed and sent it to my room. It was nice of them but it is not always the case that you can share your documents.
In conclusion, this is a nice property with professional staff. I will return to The Chatwal when i visit NYC again.

title: “First Class Customer Service”
text: I stayed at the Aloft Hotel in Harlem from 9/4 to 9/7. I had a great stay, and what made it unique and absolutely amazing was the front desk staff. What a group of first class individuals - great customer service is clearly their #1 priority and their PASSION. What a unique bunch of people that work there - and the two people who really stand out in my mind are Martha and Jeanie. They answered all of my questions / concerns during my stay there, and made it a joy to be in the lobby area. MY two friends who joined me on this business trip were also commenting about how great the customer service was there during our cab ride to La Guardia. I highly recommend this hotel - fantastic people, fantastic service, oh...and yes - the room was fantastic too.

title: “service, location..space great”
text:
We really enjoyed this hotel. Great service, complimentary drinks in the room for free?
In NY? A real espresso in the downstairs lobby for free?
When did you get that last time?
There were some issues with cleanliness in the room, but everything else was really great..even the room size...
when did you have THAT the last time in New York?
Try it, we liked it!

title: “Hard to leave”
text: My husband and I spent a wonderful weekend at the HG Inn and will definitely return to this hotel. Customer service was off the charts. Each employee that we encountered was there to make our stay pleasurable and comfortable. The location enabled us to walk the city with ease and be in close proximity to excellent restaurants. It was truly hard to leave after having been treated so nicely at every given moment of our stay.

title: “Great location, decent rooms”
text:
I was torn between giving this property a 3 or a 4. If I could, I would have rated it 3 1/2. 
Walking in the Driskill, we were very impressed. It is a beautiful building, both from the outside and in the lobby. 
After checking in, we took a shaky elevator ride to our room. The room was also nicely decorated in keeping with the historic atmosphere. Because it is such an old building, both the room and the bathroom were quite small, but that is to be expected.
The room had some nice touches, like bathrobes, a minibar, and an umbrella. Many items in the room were monogrammed with the Driskill's logo or an image of the hotel. But there were also some maintenance issues that I couldn't help but notice--the bathroom counter appeared to be coming off of the wall, the climate of the room was warm and humid, and the room key didn't always work. In my opinion, the hotel could have spent less money on personalizing the curtains, bed, and bathroom sink with their logo, and spent a bit more on maintaining the room. We paid for the room with reward points, so it didn't cost us anything, but had we shelled out several hundred dollars for it, we would have been disappointed.
There is a bar and restaurant in the hotel, but we did not visit either. The lobby is large and beautiful with many places to sit and relax. There are beautiful balcony porches with rocking chairs overlooking both Brazos and Sixth Streets, but unfortunately, these were locked.
Overall, this hotel has some great history behind it and the location can't be beat. It was very easy to walk to restaurants, bars, and shops.

title: “Enjoyed our weekend stay”
text:
Was able to check in early on Saturday. The reception desk was very helpful and friendly.
We were upgraded to a lovely suite overlooking Quincy Market. Great place to stay. 
Very convenient to the subway (T) . Walking distance to Aquarium.
Staff was very helpful with directions and questions.

title: “Love this hotel!”
text: The hotel's location in the heart of Times Square can't be beat. The subway and discount theater ticket booth is right across the street. The hotel more than met my expectations, from the very friendly and helpful doorman to the smiling front desk clerk. The rooms are fantastic! They are more like studio appartments.Loved the kitchenette.Beds very comfy. Would stay here again.

title: “A good old hotel, in a pretty good area, and a great value.”
text:
Like some others, I was nervous when they did not want my credit card to hold the room. However, I arrived and all was in order. 
Hotel Mayflower is nothing fancy, but it is the genuine article and fit my needs exactly. Was just looking for a clean hotel that was in a safe walking distance to the Moscone center. The walk was about one mile, but the neighborhood was fine if you walked down Bush Street. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting San Francisco that is trying to save money on hotel accommodations. 
The only negative was that I had trouble with the wi-fi. However, I never contacted the staff for assistance since my phone works as a hotspot. Just not worth my time to resolve the issue.

title: “Not perfect, but great location”
text: We stayed at the Herald Square Hotel in November 2006 and generally found the experience to be a positive one. The hotel is most definitely not the Ritz - but the value of the accommodation cannot be questioned. We struggled to find any hotel room in New York for the night we wanted to stay and were happy to pay $169 + tax for this hotel when we discovered it was available. The hotel looks far more luxurious from the outside and the grandeur of the building is evident, but walk inside and the illusion is lost and you cannot fail to be disappointed to see bullet proof glass surrounding reception and the slightly dated and unattractive decor in the foyer area. We were not lucky enough to to be given a refurbished room, so our's was fairly small and basic. However, it was clean and had a very comfortable bed. The air conditioning was incredibly noisy and the walls so thin that you could quite easily hear people in the adjoining room. It was nice, however, to be given complimentary coffee in the foyer and we even managed to connect our laptop to the wireless network which was free of charge. The location of the hotel in our opinion is the hotel's greatest asset. It was literally a stone's throw away from the Empire State Building and Macy's. Overall the Herald Square is a great option if you are looking for a well priced, clean hotel with no frills in a fabulous location. If you manage to get a refurbished room, then you will have hit the jackpot!

title: “an excellent stay”
text: For my husband and I this hotel scored excellent on all counts - the lobby area, the breakfast area and the bedroom/bathroom were spotless. The room we had (king with sofabed and balcony) was a very good size, had a comfortable bed, was well furnished and everything was in working order. All the staff that we had dealings with were both friendly and helpful. We found the location to be just what we wanted - convenient to most places but without all the noise and bustle of the main drag of the Riverwalk. It is a very short walk to the Riverwalk (out of the doors by the coffee shop, cross the road and down the steps and you are there!!). This is the more peaceful stretch of the Riverwalk but it is very pretty and well worth the walk. We used the path by the river to get to the Alamo and surrounding area with ease. I am so pleased to note that many other people are finding really positive things to say about this hotel. It is very good value for money. (I have recently received an email from the hotel to say that the coffee shop and restaurant are now open).

title: “Don't stay anywhere else.”
text:
What a great Hotel this is. Very friendly staff, ideal location, good price and loads of free coffee.
 This was my second stay in New York, and I would strongly recommend this Hotel.

title: “Very Strong Smoke and Mildew Odors”
text:
We had stayed at this motel about 5 years ago also for medical reasons and it has deteriorated horribly since. This visit we were unable to find another hotel to stay in, therefore, we ended up here by default for 2 nights. The first night we were on the first floor. This room had a very moldy smell and the room was very old. I immediately went to the drugstore next door to buy a candle to attempt to mask the odors. 
We had to use the hotel shuttle back from the hospital the first night. The desk had informed us the last shuttle had to be called in by 9:45 and back to the hotel by 10:00 pm. I called at 9:40 and was told the van would be there in 10 minutes-it came in less than 5 minutes which might have been a good thing except my daughter expected the 10 minutes they said and was not outside yet waiting with us. The driver stated he would not wait for her. Fortunately, she returned almost immediately.The driver did not get out to help us in despite the fact that we had several bags, a stroller and a baby in a car seat. The driver took off before our 4 month old was even in a seat to say nothing about the car seat being properly strapped in-- he just took off when the van door closed! The food in the restaurant was horrible (ate less than 10%) and overpriced. The windows were very old and did not feel secure for a first floor room. The chain lock on the door did not work properly. There was a second open door into the motel that had a card key but it was never locked allowing anyone into the hallways out of view of the main desk. The front desk person was not even at the desk later that evening when another party was checking in. These people were calling out "hello" when the staff appeared from a stairway.
The second night we were told we had to move to the second floor even though we had a baby with a stroller. We ended up hauling the stroller up the stairs by ourselves. The vending machines were broken. There was no staff available for any assistance. The second floor smelled so strongly of smoke that we both woke up with a headache. The only pleasant thing about this stay was one of the shuttle driver who was from Africa--he was the only helpful pleasant person we ran into during this stay. I would do everything within my power NEVER to stay here again!

title: “Great location for reasonable price!”
text: This little hotel was in a great, quiet location, near Adams Morgan (but away from the night noise), and a close walk to the metro. I really enjoyed walking around the neighborhood through the embassies - it was also a great place for jogging in the mornings! For the price we paid, this was an incredible bargain. There is a cute sitting area next to the lobby where they have complimentary cookies and coffee throughout the day. The staff are nice, and when our internet connection in the room did not work, they let us use another room for that. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: My husband and I just celebrated our 30th anniversary at your resort and I do not have adequate words to tell you what a wonderful time we had. Allie Garvey and the host of other employees that contributed to make our stay first class were Anita, JD.Armando, Francisco, Gabe, Denny, and Jesse, These employee's including Allison Garvey helped to make our special time wonderful. Whatever recognition can be given, it should be given to them. Everyone I know will know about the great time we had at your resort. Thank you for hiring such fantastic people to represent your establishment. A job well done!

title: “Well appointed rooms”
text:
Travelled May 2009. 
NYC is very expensive so this was a decent choice. Rooms had lights above door to tell you when toilets were free. You did have your own sink which was handy. Midtown wasn't my favourite neighbourhood, but transit was a close walk and there were several pubs and restaurants nearby. Overall we were happy with The Pod.

title: “great hotel for sightseeing”
text: stayed here for 5 night had a few doubts about the hotel after reading a few reviews on here after we had already booked but they were soon gone after we checked in the staff were very helpful as it was my first time in the big apple and wasnt to sure about getting around , the room we were given was on the 3rd floor facing the street wasnt the biggest room but it was very clean and bed was very comfortable and the noise from the street wasn't to much of an issue we were in new york after all so wasn't going to be very peaceful , the location is brilliant step out of the front door and times square is right there so its great for getting about to sightsee on foot . all in all i would highly recommend this hotel would definately stay here again good price for the location and good room the only issue we had really was that my girlfriend left her hand bag in a cab with our phones in so had to use the rooms phone the cancel the credit card and the bill we received was around $250 for 20mins of phone calls which was a big shock upon checking out so if you do stay here don't use the phone but other than that i couldn't speak highly enough of this hotel

title: “A Great Choice”
text:
We booked this hotel as part of a deal on the British Airways website that included the flights and accomodation with breakfast.
The first impression of the hotel was very good. Our taxi drew up inthe carriage drive and a member of staff was at hand to open the door for us. The reception area is large and has a great bustling atmosphere. The staff at reception were very courtious and helpful.
Our room was quite high up in the hotel and was really excellent. It was spacious, modern and very clean with a safe and flatscreen TV, kettle and ample wardrobe space. the bed and pillow were the best i have had at any hotel.
The `basic` breakfast that was included in the deal was more than ample, offering bagels, bread, fruit, cakes, cereal, yoghurt and plenty of american extras such as cheese, smoked salmon etc., For 4 dollars you could upgrade to include hot food and the japanese bar. All in all an excellent good quality breakfast.
At the end of our stay we were able to check in and print out our boarding cards from a machine in the reception area free of charge.
I would highly recommend this hotel and we were delighted with our choice

title: “Charming”
text: Inn At The Ballpark was charming, cozy, and classy. Decor is similar to a man's den: dark green, beige, and maroon, but it feels warm and inviting. Staff was helpful, breakfast buffet good, and the bar was relaxing. Great location!!!

title: “We'll be back”
text: We stayed here with our 3 children on a recent visit to San Francisco. The hotel's location close to Chinatown is brilliant, the atmosphere is Chinatown is buzzing and the local restuarants are delicious. The hotel staff were very helpful and friendly and the room was clean. We had a city view room but unfortunatley during our stay there were building works going on on the building over the road which meant that our city view was spoilt by very dirty windows and cranes etc. I fully understand however that this was not the hotels fault. A plus point for the hotel is the Starbucks in the lobby, the kids loved being able to go down and grab breakfast. We would definatley stay here again.

title: “Great Base from which to explore LA”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights, we were travelling along ther Coast and finished up in LA, this place was recommended by friends living nearby. Its a decent hotel with everything you need. the bed was supremely comfortable, there was a large flat screen TV and a fridge in the room. We could not fault it, there was a free breakfast and a Pizza Hut across the road, and 5 minutes away was the shopping district. Hollywood is only 10 minutes away and Venice beach 20 minutes in the car. 
It was the cheapest hotel we found, and paradoxiacally the best.

title: “Good value, great location”
text: My best friend and I were looking for an economical choice close to the museums and Central Park and the Excelsior was a good choice. We found it to be comfortable and we had a good view even though our room didn't face the park, the city-scape at night was really cool. The staff was pleasant and we didn't have any complaints, I slept great every night. There were plenty of places to eat within walking distance and we had a great time.

title: “I was scared to even walk barefoot on the carpet”
text:
I was stuck in Memphis overnight due to an airline problem and this was the only available room I could find. What a scary, disgusting hotel.
The room had the outdated, not-stylish-even-ten-years-ago furniture you see in the photos, and it had seen better days. The room's TV was a circa 1988 model into which someone apparently from Dallas (that's what it said) had carved their initials on the front. The bathroom had moldy, peeling paint on the ceiling. The bed had one of those polyester bedspreads with a pattern that hides stains that every other decent chain got rid of a few years ago because everyone knows how gross and disgusting hotel bedspreads are.
The only nice thing I can say is that the shaving mirror in the shower was really handy.
Seriously, it's like the place has not been touched in a decade. And this is a Holiday Inn SELECT, which is supposedly one of their better properties?
I had not stayed in a Holiday Inn property for a few years (I stay at Marriott and Starwood properties almost 200 nights a year, so I have seen a LOT of hotels) and based on what I saw here, I'm not anxious to try one again anytime soon. I'm shocked that something so disgusting would be a part of an international chain with any standards whatsoever.
I think I'll sleep in the airport next time if this is my only option.

title: “Top value in Manhattan, will be back”
text: Having stayed overnight in NYC dozens of times at an array of properties I suspect you would be hard-pressed to find better value in the City. You could pay more for space and amenities, but in its range the Library has little competition. Clean, new (rare in NYC), and has a personality. Well-appointed rooms that feel more "home" than corporate chain. One small criticism, when the doorman is absent/distracted in the evening, there is easy access to the elevator from the street, which could be a security issue. Having said that, I'll be back.

title: “Great Location”
text: My husband and I enjoyed our stay. We had a nice room with great view. We felt a little too old to be staying here (53), but only because we weren't able to stay out partying past 2, when neighborhood was still quite lively. The rooms are modern and bathrooms great! We didn't really notice noise problems we saw others complain about. I did use spa and that was a little strange where was set up in the basement (small curtained room), but the treatment was excellent.

title: “This Marriott is superb- don't believe the negative comments!”
text:
Don't believe the negative comments!!! Stayed here for total of 4 nights in August this year as part of an Archers Direct extended tour of California etc. The reception area is very impressive, vast, and stylish. The rooms were excellent- well furnished clean etc. Staff very friendly - front of desk man was hugely supportive and helpful when it emerged that our return flight to UK via New York was compromised by the impending hurricane.
Only criticism is that there is not much of a bar culture in this hotel. (But this is common in Amercan hotels) - it tended to be very quiet around the bar after 10 'clock. The food was a little expensive but come on these are hotel prices and there were plenty of alternative eateries around e.g. in the nearby Bonaventure building. 
So highly recommended!!

title: “Perfect Getaway Spot”
text:
I booked a room at this hotel using an online special that included valet parking and a credit to the restaurant next door all at a discount since we are from the NW. The front desk and valet service was friendly and attentive. Check in was a breeze. Based on all the other reviews here I expected the room would be on the small side so that was not a surprise at all. The bathroom and shower were smaller than I expected though but we managed. The decor was fun and hip. We appreciated the minibar and fridge as well as the pillow menu. We found the lobby to be very comfortable but I did notice that some of the furnishings were looking a little worse for wear (blue ottomans near fireplace). The location was fantastic. We walked to a show at the Paramount, took a cab to dinner, walked to an arcade and then back to the hotel one night. The next day we walked around and did a little shopping downtown. It was very nice to be close to everything. We also enjoyed happy hour at the adjacent restaurant. 
Liked Best: Service at front desk, valet
Liked Least: Tiny shower :)

title: “Worth it!”
text: Very nice hotel. Breakfast was very good. Cocktail hour was good. The bed was very comfortable. Room was small, but I believe that's a common thing in San Francisco. Close to public transportation, which was nice.

title: “Great view, great location, slightly worn hotel”
text: I often stay here for business and still like it, though it looks careworn and feels crowded these days. The bar is no longer the elegant place it used to be, and the bar food has headed in the direction of burgers - all depressing. Last time I was there I needed an adapter, which they were not able to lend me since `someone already had it' - that seems pretty feeble in what is supposed to be a really good hotel. However, it is in a great location, and the view from the rooms is wonderful, looking out over the historic city with the park directly in front, leading to views of the river. It used to be my favourite hotel anywhere, but I would probably not stay there now if it were not so convenient for my office.

title: “Happy hour!!! And beer upon check in!!!”
text: Now first of all the hotel is very nice. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The location is good, but the best part was the promotion we got when checking in and were handed a six pack of local beers!!! The happy hour was great with free food and drinks and music. All and all even with out the promotion the staff was friendly and the rooms neat and clean. I would recommend this to other travelers

title: “6 Girls Trip”
text:
Had a wonderful experience at this hotel. Nice clean rooms,awesome breakfast,wonderful bar.
I believe on Tuesdays thru Thursdays they have a free happy hour, I was there on a Thursday and it was a real treat... We were greated promptly when we arrived by one of the best bellmen I have every met!!!!!! All of us ladies travel a lot and Eddie is the best!!!! I would VERY much stay at this hotel again and would look Eddie up,made our stay even better,no issues at ALL!!!!

title: “Fantastic Hotel! - Everything you could want for a trip to NYC”
text: Stayed for 5 nights with 10 people and couldn't ask for better. Smack bang in the middle of the city - a gateway to everything. Empire State Building literally around the corner and subway entrance at end of street taking you to all destinations. I recommend getting a 7 day Metro Card - $25 for limitless subway and bus rides - well worth it. Breakfast was delicious - Bagels, cereals, waffles, toast, donuts, muffins, tea, coffee, juice and much more! Internet and printer available in reception which is handy for checking in for flights online etc. .Staff were very helpful, helped to book lots of trips- i would advise doing everything through them or at least seek their advice as there are a lot of touts and companies who sell fake tickets or give misguided info to sell you a product. Bar staff at Brendans, which is the bar attached to the hotel were brilliant - the drinks are very reasonable and the Cosmopolitans are really nice. They look after you and we had a free round of drinks for our custom. Also the bar food was to die for - MUST TRY. We had 3 in a room and two double beds in it. The beds were so comortable we wanted to take them home. Good size rooms and bathrooms and great closet space. The rooms were spotless - fully hoovered, towels changed and everything changed daily. We had a newly re-furbished room and was very well done. Some rooms are still being done out but will all be completed soon. If you are going soon the 4th Floor is already done out so you may want to request a room on that floor for now. The street the hotel is on has plenty of amenities, three Irish bars, fast food joints, Cocktail Lounge called Catwalk and various Souvenir shops. I recommend Digital Express dead opposite the hotel as the owners Charles and George are very helpful and will offer some discounts. There were 10 of us and we received way over $100 discount between us on all the souvenirs and memorabilia you could hope for. My only warning to anyone (not about the hotel) but about a tour Guide Company called Grayline. They do Hop on, Hop Off buses around the city. They offered us a package of hop on, hop off buses for 2 days which was fab, but also an express pass to Empire State and boat tour to, and to get off and see Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island. PLEASE BE AWARE their New York Water Taxi (small yellow boat) DOES NOT, I REPEAT DOES NOT stop off at the islands it just sails around. The only way to get to the islands is to go to battery park and use liberty cruises - the official company and pay $12.00 for a ticket which is very cheap. Also the Empire State part was not worth it because although it has a queue jump, if you get there early enough there is no queue anyway. So after paying $73 each we only used the bus, payed extra for an express Empire State pass we did not need and had to shell out another $12.00 for another Statue of Liberty Ticket. Apart from that we had the most amazing time - its the best city in the world in my opinion and the Hotel was certainly a big part of that experience.

title: “Fairly Enjoyable Visit”
text:
We spent three nights at the Hotel Monaco in Seattle and it was enjoyable but nothing out of the ordinary for a four star hotel. We enjoy staying at Kimptons if we are in a city that has them. 
They were able to check us in early which was nice. Never once, though, were we asked if we needed help with our bags. We booked the Queen-Queen room and it was a fairly good size. The hotel was very clean and housekeeping did a great job each day. It was inconvenient not having an ice machine on our floor. We had to request a gold fish three times before we got one on the second day. The Fitness Center was very small with limited equipment.
Of all the Kimptons we stayed in this one had the nicest lobby. It was very inviting and a great place to relax and read the paper. The evening social hour with complementary wine and beer was very nice. Like in the other Kimptons we have stayed in we always meet interesting people staying at the hotel. 
Didn't care for the Sazerac restaurant. The food wasn't bad but the service both times we ate there was terrible. Ordered room service once but had to cancel since they were forty minutes late and couldn't give us a delivery time.
Don't think we would stay at this hotel again.

title: “Very good stay”
text:
My husband, teenage son and I stayed atthe Affinia for 3 days in July 2008 and really liked the hotel.
It was handy fo all of the sights and was very comfortable and clean.
We had a room on the 34 floor with a view downtown - this was excellent but I think a view up town with the chrysler building may be better.
We had breakfast in the Barking dog cafe which was very good and reasonable.
42nd st. and Tmes sq are within walking distance by we also found the taxis to be reasonable.
We did the bus tour but we were unlucky on the first half of the trip as we had a foreign guide who spoke poor English so it was hard to understand what he said. Later we had an excellent native New Yorker who was very good.
It is worth going to Central park for lunch or a drink to get a rest from the hectic city. We ate at a cafe close to the Ball park and it was very nice.

title: “Nice for price but a few downsides”
text: I just returned from a four day stay at the Salisbury. It really is at a great location. Right in the middle of things and close to the subway. As other reviewers have mentioned, the decor is out of date, but it was clean so who cares. Our room was huge! The bathroom was quite small but clean. The minimal interaction I had with the staff was pleasant. The only complaints I have are that I couldn't control the heat (it would be burning up then cold) and the incredibly hard beds. It was like sleeping on a wooden board. I ended up moving to the sofa bed. The price was great but I would consider staying elsewhere simply because I don't enjoy waking up with neck and back pain when I'm on vacation.

title: “No sign of Matilda”
text:
Matilda is the Algonquin's cat but we didn't see her on our recent trip to NYC. We were warmly welcomed when we arrived and were given "one of the larger rooms" for our stay. Being a Platinum Marriott Rewards member I was also pleased to be offered free continental breakfasts.
Our room was reasonably sized but the bathroom was very small. Everything had been modernised whilst still retaining the historical feel of the hotel. The bed was one of the most comfortable that I have experienced. There are some minus points though. There are no tea or coffee facilities in the room, bath towels are rather small and the windows have blinds that don't completely keep the light out. We needed the earplugs that "Matilda had provided to help us in the city that never sleeps" paraphrasing the card left on my bedside table thanks to inconsiderate and noisy guests next door. We were at the side towards the back of the hotel so any background noise from outside wasn't intrusive.
The public areas are very pleasant and there is a large business facility along with gym and coffee facilities on the 2nd floor.
This was our 2nd stay in New York and whilst not disappointed with the Algonquin overall and its position which is nice and close to Times Square, Broadway and Macy's, if we ever return, on balance, we'll be more likely to return to where we stayed before.

title: “Amazing hotel, great staff, fab location, should be #1”
text:
Stopped here for our 20th wedding anniversary and had the best holiday ever!!!!!
Emailed the hotel prior to travelling to ask for a room with a great view. Had reply next day confirming my request and got exactly what i'd asked for up on the 17th floor.
Right from the start the staff were very welcoming and friendly. Randy the doorman made us feel right at home showing us to the room and giving great advice on location, direction and suggestions of what to do with your first few hour in New York...priceless.
We even had a ' Happy Anniversary ' cake waiting in our room when we got back...nice touch.
The room was a great size for New York it had a large plasma tv, a gorgeous bathroom with fab shower and the most comfortable bed i've ever slept in. 
Location was fantastic too. you are two blocks away from Times Square and 5th avenue is just at the end of the street.
There are some good eating places on 44th st too. If you turn right out of the hotel the diner at the end is a great place for breakfast, turn left and there's a lovely greek restaurant. Personally i'd give the indian a miss, expensive and not up to uk standard.
Cant sing the praises of the concierge Brooke enough. We really wanted to see our 1st Yankee's game while we were there and she sorted us out and got us GREAT seats.
I cant recommend this hotel enough, everyone we met could not do enough to make our stay perfect.

title: “Really hotel in the headquarters”
text: 3 nights we spent the night at this Kimpton hotel. Nothing stands in the way of a town stroll, because the hotel is ideally for it. One can run comfortably or reach the town with public means of transportation. For the hunger occasionally the Subway station is perfect nearby. I will spend my next vacation also at a Kimpton hotel. Result: To recommend only.

title: “Very nicely appointed rooms, and very friendly staff”
text:
This hotel is in a very good location. It doesn't look very impressive from the outside, but the rooms are very nice, as is the lobby area. The staff was also very friendly. 
The rooms are very well appointed, with lights that dim throughout, a very nice bathroom, and comfortable furniture.

title: “It's perfect for DEMF.”
text:
My boyfriend and I stay at The Leland every Memorial Day weekend. There is a massive 3 day long electronic festival in Hart Plaza that weekend. We live in Detroit but it’s a 20 min commute to get downtown so we stay down there for it. I guess we are just jaded to the filthiness and danger of the city. 
We love The Leland Hotel because it truly is an experience all in itself. The first year we went it took forever to checked in, the staff was (is) extremely unhelpful, and when we finally got up to our room (the elevators are as horrific as everyone has described) and begun to unpack, another couple unlocks our room door and walks in. The hotel double booked our room! We called the front desk to clear things up and they had us come to them and then had us bring a new room key to the other couple.
One of the years we stayed there we had been out all day at the festival. When we came back we found the main entrance blocked off and a hazmat crew was there. Someone had been stabbed right in front of the doors to the hotel and there was a huge puddle of blood on the ground. 
Another time, in the very early morning, we were verbally assaulted by someone who apparently worked in the hotel. The walls are paper thin. The people partying on either side of our room might as well have been sharing the bed with us while we were trying to rest. Something is always going to be broken or completely disgusting. But they make up for it down stairs. The City Club which is a Goth club year round isn’t so scary that weekend. In fact they pump out some of the best electronic music you’ll find anywhere in the world. The lobby is huge and has an old timey beauty to it. Like anything aged that was beautiful once. And the entire hotel vibrates with bass ‘til 7am. The lobby is like being inside a subwoofer. The connecting diner has veggie burgers. And the People Mover is right across the street. So any where you need to be in the city is no more than a few minutes away (unless there is a hockey game going on). We won’t stay anywhere else for that weekend. But that weekend only.

title: “Very disappointed! Don't stay here...”
text: Let me begin by saying this is a very fair review. I have literally stayed everywhere, from motels in small towns to Holiday Inn's to the Ritz. I am not super picky and I don't have to always stay at the nicest places. We booked this hotel based off the pictures and location... and it was a major disappointment. I would never stay here again, nor would I recommend it. When you enter the hotel lobby, it definitely doesn't match the rooms. Basically, they spent money on the lobby and really slacked on the rooms. As soon as I entered our room- it smelled so badly! It had a stale, musty smell to it. Bad first impression. It was also the smallest room I have EVER stayed in and we booked the largest room cateogory they offered. It felt like a cracker box. The bathroom was soooo little, with NO space on the counter to put any personal items. And the shower, oh my goodness. It was so little and has a half door- if that makes any sense. It only covers half of the shower! So, the floor was soaken wet after each shower. Ridiculous! In the shower was a wand that slid up and down the wall, or at least was supposed to. Well, it didn't stay at the top- so the water would constantly hit you at shoulder height, which made it impossible to wash your hair. It was also pointing straight at the wall so you basically had to be smashed up on the wall to get any water. Also, their toileteries are a joke- just tiny bottles of shampoo and conditioner- NO lotion. Let's talk about the noise- every night we could hear loud music, talking and booms and crashes. I think, perhaps, the music was coming from the bar?? Not sure about the other noises- you'd have thought Charlie Sheen was maybe in the room next to us?? We had to sleep with the tv on loudly and the air conditioning on high every night. I think the JW Marriott was only $30 more a night- I wish we would have stayed there. It was so nice! Bottom line- I felt dirty staying here. The room just seemed not clean. I showered as soon as I got home and washed all my clothes- even the ones I didn't wear on the trip, because I felt filthy from our room.

title: “Great Location for Seeing the DC sites”
text:
I stayed at the Embassy Suites with friends for a week-long girls' getaway. We were thrilled with the location -- very convenient to the Metro and walking distance to many attractions. 
The staff was always friendly and attentive. The concierge was helpful in making recommendations for our trip throughout the week.
The free breakfast was fresh (cooked to order eggs) and a great way to start our days. We even had diner there one evening and really enjoyed it. 
During our one week stay we only had 2 complaints: 
1) We knew there would be a lot of families staying at the hotel so we didn't expect to use the pool much (we were right with that assumption) but were hoping to relax a little in the hot tub late at night. Sadly, the tub was very sudsy the first day and got dirtier as the week progressed until we found it unusable and complained to staff. 
2) on our final night in DC we got back to our room and smell cigarette smoke. We called to complain and maintenance came by and explained that we were smelling the smoke from a smoking room below ours (we were on the 4th floor and smoking was on the 3rd) and it was coming through the vents. They did offer us a new room but since we were all un-packed and leaving the next day we decided to stay. They put some type of humidifier in the room and sprayed it with a room freshener to make is a little better. 
Overall I think the hotel room was spacious, conveniently located, and priced well for considering that a full breakfast is included. I would definitely consider staying there again. 
* one word of caution * the hotel does not have great cell phone reception in the room (at least not on 4). We all had different providers -- ATT was the best and was weak. Verizon was spotty and Sprint was usually the least reliable. Most of the time it didn't get a signal. The lobby of the hotel did however have good reception.

title: “excellent hotel with everything you'd want”
text: stayed here with a mixture of colleagues and family. rooms very clean. we were on 8th floor so very quiet up there. our 9 month old daughter needed "walked" in her pram to get her back to sleep at 2am - no problem - after 3 circuits around the 8th floor she was in the land of nod, helped by the soothing woosh of the running water of the water feature. This was a bit crazy, with the fish, but a unique feature. Breakfast good - agree gets very busy - especiallty over spring break - 100s of kids - but even then the staff remained calm under pressure. the eating area returns to peace and quiet very quickly at 9am after the early rush. nice pool, nice touch with happy hour. the walk up to Du Pont Circle - easy, not far at all. Shop across the road had basics - but we couldn't find fresh fruit and veg anywhere in central DC! Does everyone eat out all the time? Internet - $12 per 24hrs, good choice of movies. Perfect location to walk to Georgetown which was a lovely bonus with nice shops, bars and restaurants. Have stayed in various places in DC but def going back here.

title: “Overall, not too bad.”
text: This hotel is located near Massachusetts General Hospital, and is a few blocks away from a subway stop. The staff were very friendly and accomodating at check in and check out. The elevators were fairly quick in getting you to your floor. The rooms themselves were adaquate. However, we could here people taking and the television in the room next door, so the sound proofing was not totally perfect. The furnishing were a little bit worn, but not totally broken down. The king bed room was decent size, but the bathroom was really small. There was a good size closet for hanging clothes, a writing desk and a chair with duvet. Overall, not a bad place to rest your head, but certainly not a first class hotel. It proably deserves it's current star rating.

title: “Top venue!”
text:
Stayed in the hotel in early March 2008 [from UK], for 3 nights. Great location in NYC. Good room with good, but small bathroom. Hotel has a small well equiped gym. All the staff I spoke to were friendly, polite, helpful and cooperative.
The breakfast.............Absolutely superb!............Fantastic choice! 
Overall, very good hotel, nothing negative to comment on, would definitely stay there again.

title: “Adequate and clean”
text:
We have stayed at this hotel on three separate visits to NYC. The rooms are small, but the beds are comfortable and the place is clean. We had a problem with the thermostat on the last visit, but it was replaced efficiently. Good value for the price paid and the staff is friendly.
Do not use the restaurant next door (Tre Stelle, connected to the lobby). The breakfasts are overpriced and offer no variety.

title: “Lovely friendly hotel”
text: The hotel is in a lovely location very accesible for fishermans wharf and many other areas of SF are easily reached by buses. There is free parking which another plus point. The rooms are of a lovely side with comfy beds and a good size bathroom. There is also free internet access in reception which is very helpful. Also there is a bus stop outside the hotel where a tour bus stops so great for taking in the sights of the city. Breakfast was lovely with lovely coffee pastries, fruit juice and a lovely selection of teas. Would book again as is a good price and in a fab location.

title: “Lost Reservation”
text: I booked a room with Georgetown Hill Inn over a month in advance. A week prior to my trip I called to confirm the reservation and they had lost it. Never made it to the hotel. Dont bother with this hotel... there are plenty others that have a much greater level of professionality in the Georgetown area.

title: “Quaint, friendly Hotel”
text: This was my second visit and staff welcomed me back. The restaurant has good food, attentive servers and very helpful with tourist ideas. The hotel rooms are small but clean. Our room overlooked the site of John Kennedy's shooting. The hotel has a shuttle and there are great restaurants close by. There are a couple of parks near and within easy walking distance to the Convention Centre.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: This is a nice hotel in Austin. The rooms and the pool are a little small but the ambiance is pleasant and the quality is what you would expect from the Hyatt. We enjoyed our time here and would stay here again.

title: “Don't waste your time!”
text: The Holiday Inn on the Bay, was very disappointing. The front desk was rude and unaccomidating. You pay a ridiculous fee to park, which is so vaguely mentioned in the description, you don't realize they mean over $100 for 5 days!! Our room had a foul odor, not very clean, and VERY small. Elevator took forever! The in-house resturants were horrible. The "elephant" room, (unsure of exact name) had the worst breakfast buffet I have ever had! Phone fees were unusually high and unlisted in the hotel info. Room Service was fresh, and about the only posotive point about staying there. Not recommended for children!! POOL was very COLD and SMALL!! *Request an ocean view, (at least a $40 per day upgrade), or else you will have a balcony over looking the boiler room and the garbage. Nowhere near a beach, although the board walk is beautiful. No nearby shopping. The only resturants within walking distance are over priced and over rated. I will never stay at another Holiday inn after my experience with this.

title: “Excellent choice for San Francisco”
text: We stayed here for three nights in mid February, and it was wonderful. The hotel is clean and very well appointed. The front desk staff was most accomodating when we requested a room change. The rooms are spotless, spacious, and quiet if you have an inside room. The weather was cold and rainy while we were there, so we ate many meals at the hotel, and the food was very good at breakfast, dinner, and room service. However the dining room was short staffed, and service was slow, but everyone that was working was doing their best and had great positive attitudes. We will return.

title: “great hotel for the holidays”
text:
we stayed here over christmas and it was absolutely lovely, however almost empty (3% occupancy= ~30 rooms) we go a great deal on one of those name your price websites. cheapest times christmas and after schools dismiss for summer
staff was excellent and attentive, the room service food was good. they even brought a special christmas gift to everyone in the hotel.
we had a great stay in this huge hotel at the convention center, and will go back again next year, just check out before the 30th to avoid the new years eve crowd.

title: “excellent”
text:
As Marriott Platinum, we were given a two bedroom suite. Good beds, clean, big
bathrooms. Three TV's. Walking distance to Galleria Mall & its restaurants. Also many
other restaurants walkable. Gated entry, secure parking. Better than average free
breakfast. No complaints about this property.

title: “Great stay from start to finish.”
text: My sister and I stayed at the Baymont Inn on our trip to Dallas. Kudos to Sean who was there to check us in...he was the best. He printed out maps for us to easily get to the destinations that we wanted to visit while in Dallas. The rooms were nice and clean and I am a very picky hoteler. I don't like to stay in older run down hotels. I can't say enough about how nice this place was...there was even an indoor pool and hot tub. Breakfast was nice with waffles, eggs, meat and muffins. I would certainly stay here again if I ever went back to the Dallas area.

title: “Short stay but nice experience”
text:
