I stayed for two nights on business -- my company has an office in the neighboring office park. I did not spend too much time in my room or at the hotel; here are my impressions of my limited time there.
Nice room, comfortable king-size bed in a suite of sorts -- I had a small sitting room with a pullout loveseat, TV and desk, bathroom and separate bedroom (no doors between the rooms though). My only complaint was the loud fan from the AC unit and thin walls. i could hear the family next door clearly. 
One caution -- I scheduled two wake-up calls. One morning it came five minutes late (no big deal) and the other never came.
I had the bed and breakfast plan; the breakfast buffet was plentiful, tasty and had an attentive staff.
The hotel had a small indoor pool and hot tub and much larger outdoor pool with lap lanes and general pool area. Parking was easy.
The hotel is on the highway (though I never heard it from my room) and is adjacent to an office park and shopping area. The shopping included a few functional stores like CVS and a good selection of delis, restaurants, bars and a Starbucks.
The location was convenient to get to areas near 410, and downtown looked to be about 10 miles away.
Overall, it was a pleasant stay -- no real complaints.

title: “Excellent Service - Even before arrival”
text:
I am an administrative assistant and was in need of quickly adding to an existing reservation. Reservations Agent, Francisco Martinez, assisted me with this change. He accommodated all my requests accurately within or less than five minutes of each request. Service with a "smile" via both phone and email. A job well done even before the executives arrival.
Thanks!!

title: “High Tea and Colorado Royalty”
text:
I've stayed at the Brown Palace multiple times for conferences and have never had anything to complain about. It is an old building, so the rooms can be a bit small, but just staying here the staff makes you feel important and respected. You can feel the history of Denver in this hotel, knowing that Molly Brown stayed here and must have enjoyed a drink or in the beautiful, towering lobby.
If you have the time to bring friends for High Tea, well it is quite a marvelous experience. There are few places in Colorado that offer a proper tea service and this is one of the top.

title: “Great facility and staff this will be home when in Indy”
text: I stay at Hilton properties on a regular basis, I thought breakfast was until 10am. I arrived a little after 9am to find that they had closed the kitched. Lassandra was kind enough to turn on her cleaned grill and prepare an omelet for me. What an associate.

title: “Top Rate Experience”
text: After reading the reviews on numerous hotels in Memphis(scary), I decided to go with my instincts based on stays at other Drury hotels in my own state. WOW! This hotel was excellent in service, accomodations and price. I will definately stay at this hotel again and again!

title: “Wonderful Experience!”
text: We had a wonderful stay at The Iroquois. The accomodations, staff, and restaurant were all excellent. The highlight of The Iroquois is their Concierge, Marga. Her assistance both before our trip and during our trip couldn't have been more valuable. She made numerous reservations for us, followed up when clarification was needed, and then made excellent recommendations on sites to see (or not to see), restaurants, and Broadway shows. Not only is her knowledge of the city incredible, but she is an absolute joy to work with. The Iroquois is very fortunate to have her on their team.

title: “Beautiful Harbor Views”
text: I recently stayed at the Boston Harbor Hotel and it was wonderful. From the gracious doormen, to the helpful concierge, the service was excellent. The room I stayed in was immaculate, and also very large. It had two double beds, a separate couch / tv / desk area, and a big bathroom. Breakfast at the hotel was also very good, and the bar was packed at night. The view over the harbor was beautiful, and the location near all of the major restaurants was very convenient. Will definitely stay again.

title: “Turnaround Service”
text:
I stayed in the Hotel for six nights from September 2 - 8, 2012 and my Hhonours number is 716237358. My initial experience on arrival by about 21.30pm with my two sons was very unwelcoming as the front officer, Mr Luidin and his Team insisted that my reservation was cancelled. He claimed that the hotel notified me via email a day earlier. When I challenged the claim, he printed an email by Mr Destreza to me by 13.29pm same day while I was on transit to the hotel. The email gave me only up to 16.00pm to respond or my reservation would be cancelled. He also claimed that my two visa cards were faulty and offered to take me and my sons to another hotel.
It was when I put my foot down that we were going no other hotel that he offered us our room and asked us to pay $300 in cash to the hotel. This whole event took over an hour and was traumatic for me and my children who travelled over 6 hours by road from Boston to New York. All we needed was a room we rightly reserved to rest.
However, the next day I brought the two Visa cards which Mr Luidin and his Team rejected and one of them (1526) was swiped by Ms Zoribel and was okay. Ms Zoribel too was nicer and listened to us. Her disposition was quite pleasant and welcoming. We had her to commend for turning around out stay in that Hotel.

title: “Place to stay in New York City”
text: What a great find Affinia Manhattan is! We have stayed at many different hotels during our visits to the best city in the world but Affinia Manhattan outshines them all. I brought my preteen daughter and her friend, who had never visited NYC, during their February vacation and had the most delightful stay. The Affinia Manhattan hotel is right across from Penn Station and within walking distance to everything! Room was very roomy with two bathrooms, seperate bedroom and kitchen. Just perfect. Staff was lovely, helpful and breakfast was delightful. BRAVO!

title: “Great Stay”
text: We stayed here just 1 night in August 2012, We got a great last minute deal on expedia $150 per night. Check in was quick & super friendly, Chris checked us in suggested we speak to the concierge for anything we needed. The bell hop guy was very helpful too. Room & bed was small but spotless clean so it did the trick. I would stay here again next time in Boston.

title: “Nice hotel in a good location”
text:
The location is perfect, just in the center of Philadelphia. Our room was very nice and clean .. recently renovated. From the 32th floor we had a great view of the city and "Penn-Statue" on top of the city hall. Service was quick and friendly.
Parking was a little pricey, $32 for valet with in-out service.

title: “Nice room, amenities disappoint”
text: Stayed here for 2 nights in November 2012. King bedded room was well appointed with very nice walk in shower with rain shower head. Unfortunately the expected services for this new Marriott Collection of hotels fell short. Front desk personnel were very pleasant and helpfull with directions but there was no concierge at all. Apparently, they offer turndown service but only on request, and I only found out by reading this right before checking out. Room service trays were left in the hallways for hours and I should not have to ask for toilet paper , liquid soap and tissues to be restocked after the room is made up for the day. This was the first time that I can remember that a newspaper was not left at my door as a Marriott Rewards member , although they were available at the front desk. All in all the hotel was ok but there was very little to make it special.

title: “Location, location, location!!”
text:
We very much our visit to Boston. This hotel has a wonderful location within walking distance to shopping, parks, trolley tour, great restaurants and more. We loved the old world charm. We had a nice view of a fountain below and skyline. The doormen were polite and helpful, as well as the front desk. Lobby seems very dark but a very busy place as everyone meets there and since Internet is free in the lobby, many people are there reading emails etc. 
Our room was small but adequate. Beds ok. Our only problem was noise, in the hall and our neighbors who came in about midnight and continued to laugh and talk. If I had tried I could have heard every word. 
We would stay again just try to get an end of the hall room.
We got the first night on hotel tonight so we saved about 1/2 off Internet price.

title: “Fabulous stay.”
text:
Stayed at the Palomar in September with my husband. It was our first stay in Chicago and I was delighted that I had picked such a good hotel. I have used Kimpton Hotels before. The location was perfect, the room was very comfortable, but tea and coffee making facilities would have been the 'icing on the cake'. Lots of people seem to think that the sliding bathroom door is a problem, but quite frankly I didn't have a problem with it, after all, I wasn't staying there with a stranger! 
Finally all the staff were friendly and curtious.

title: “Classy, yet, not snoody.”
text: Stayed here on July 6th for a Tigers game. Extremely classy and down to earth staff all the way through hotel. We stayed here a couple of years ago and enjoyed it as well. This stay was even better. Hope to stay again next year for the Tigers game.

title: “Great Hotel..Close to the airport”
text:
Newer style Residence Inn. Probably the best of RI in JAX (except for location). The hotel is close to airport which made it convenient for weekly travelers like me. Can't say enough good things about the staff. They were very friendly and made me feel welcome. The gym just got updated with new equipment. 
The breakfast fare is your typical RI setup.

title: “Excellent service by friendly hotel staff”
text: The hotel staff are very friendly and they put in every effort to make our stay wonderful. Marcel at the front desk stands out - he is just exceptional in providing great customer service and does everything with a genuine smile. He gave us the warm double tree cookies which are so delicious. The bartender makes really good drinks and is a pleasure to interact with. The hotel has a complimentary shuttle to the airport and to nearby places which made it convenient for us. The train station is also a short 10 minutes walk from the hotel so moving around Boston was easy. We definitely enjoyed our stay at this hotel.

title: “Can't wait to go back”
text: The hotel was in a fantastic location, found the hotel staff very helpful, Rooms were spacious and cleaned everyday with fresh towels daily we asked for extra tea bags in the room which wasn't a problem. Would recomend this hotel to friends, would definately stay here again.

title: “Definitely for Wine Lovers”
text:
This property was comfortable and full of amenities. In the mornings, coffee and iced coffee were available. And, in the evenings, representatives from wineries around the region hosted the wine hour. It was a unique tasting experience and different from all other Kimpton wine hours.
The room was clean and nicely decorated. Another unique aspect about this hotel is that each room is named after a local winery and has signed prints from that winery hanging on the wall. Check-in and check-out were easy and all requests were accomodated without delay.
Overall, it was a worthwhile visit and I would definitely return if I am in the Seattle area again.

title: “Wonderful staff-big rooms”
text: I stayed at this Hotel 2/7-2/10 because of the great reviews on this site-and I am so glad I did-Everything about our stay was wonderful. nice, clean, big rooms and good price. Breakfast Buffet fit for a Queen. Very nice, helpful staff. Quiet, Great Location within walking distance to all the action, warm and cozy after a long day of fun in NYC. I can't say enough good things about "The Belvedere" I highly recommend this wonderful Hotel. and I will be back.

title: “Worst ever. PLEASE-- PLEASE read the reviews and don’t try this hotel that was my mistake”
text:
I had booked this on Hotel.com for 5 days. When I got there, there was NO WATER.. the front desk was awful, I called hotels.com and was on hold for 4 hours .. no kidding.. I got sick not just because of the smell and no water but it was blood on the pillows and sheets. And staff just said "here is a new pillow" and even that was dirty with blood. I had to go the ER. I called hotel.com so I can check out and get some money back. They kept hanging up on me finally after 10 hours of calling them.. i got thru someone nice.. how can a hotel not have water on?? This place is worst then a nightmare. PLEASE, save money and stay somewhere livable or go at the park and sleep. 
and BUGS all over the room..

title: “Great value for NoHo / SoHo / LES”
text: Great location in midst of active LES neighborhood, new building , excellent staff at desk / breakfast room , rooms bright though a tad small with a king bed in them , excllent shower / hot water / AC , all bells and whistles ; good value for money .

title: “Stay away from Days Inn Austin South!”
text: We were supposed to stay three nights but only stayed one. Fortunately, the La Quinta next door had a room available for the remainder of our stay, and the AARP rate at both hotels were just a few dollars apart. The Days Inn is in terrible shape. No place to hang clothes in our room, strange smell, black around the shower faucets, hair in the shower drain, dirty window, AC hardly kept the room cool. It is obvious the owner has put little into the upkeep, nor does he care about the guests. The La Quinta was terrific, and so glad we switched. No way would I recommend the Days Inn Austin South to anyone. I hope Days Inn corporate makes a visit--it gives the whole chain a bad name. I certainly won't stay at a Days Inn until I know the company raises its standards for franchises.

title: “A PERFECT Honeymoon Hotel!”
text: Stayed 3 nights at Cassa as part of our honeymoon travels. From the genuinely kind bellhop to the always-accomodating concierge staff, we had a wonderful experience. We stayed in a presidential 2-room suite that was clean, comfy, well-sized and decorated with great taste. Room service was delicious (try the french toast and berries and oatmeal!!!). Location was PERFECT for us, with great restaraunts, theater, and attractions in walking distance. We highly recommend staying at this charming hotel!

title: “So-So Experience”
text:
During a 3-day stay, the attention we received was just okay and the breakfast bar was disappointing in appearance and taste. The facility seemed dark and the staff, just adequate in giving attention to their its guests. The motel is in an outstanding location, but seems to lack the desire to compete with nearby motels. With more effort and training, management could turn lack-luster experiences into higher quality performance in today's travel needs.
Probably would not return.

title: “take every penny”
text: this hotel stole every penny they can from me. they charged you for everything parking, internet use etc. the snack bar was highly over priced once you get past the lobby the rest of hotel was like a holiday inn. the shower had 1 glass door that wouldnt move so water got on the floor. the sink was square so when you turned it on it splashed everywhere. elevators moved slow. parking we had to pay for parking.

title: “Dissatisfied with Stanford”
text: I was very dissappointed in the Hotel. The resturant below had the entire lobby and hallways smelling of fish. The continental breakfast was a joke. The rooms were small. I am familiar with the size of NYC hotel rooms and these were very small for the price. I thought the common areas as well as the rooms were not clean and in need of repair and refurbishing. I was really not at all satisified and will never stay there again. I am a little annoyed even with Travelocity for having the hotel on their list.

title: “Look no further for LAX hotel”
text: We spent three nights at this hotel in May and it really was a great airport hotel. I was picturing some ghastly concrete monstrosity as you often see but it was funky, clean and well located. Not housed on the airport but with great views of the end of the runway, there is a supermarket right next door and a few shops out on the strip mall. We ate at the restaurant (which was great and served excellent drinks, sports on the TVs and had a very relaxed vibe to the place) but unfortunately didn't get to use the pool area as we were too busy. I'd recommend this to other travellers and would stay here again.

title: “Amazing place to stay! Wonderful Anniversary weekend in San Francisco!”
text:
My husband and I celebrated our 1 year anniversary in San Francisco and stayed at this beautiful hotel! I did tons of research before on the different hotels in each area there. I am so happy we picked The Fairmont. Not only is it beautiful, but its full of history inside there as well. A lot of well-known people have stayed at this hotel throughout the years- so its also a landmark just on its own. Plus its amazing inside- one of the best hotel I have ever stayed in! It was also nice to stay in a place full of history and charm too! Made the experience that much more enjoyable! The place was decorated so beautifully, especially the lobby area. You really felt like you were in San Francisco while staying there!
They also upgraded our room to an amazing view of the Coit Tower and the SF. Bay Bridge. We couldnt stop staring out the window! It was by far the best view I have ever seen! Just beauitful! The room was just perfect with a large bath-tub inside the bathroom also. The room was very large and very nicely decorated. We just loved it! I am so happy to have stayed here on our trip, especially for our anniversary! They really went out of their way to make it a wonderful trip for us! We also had drinks one night at the hotel restaurant, The Tonga Room and it was really neat! Its a tropical themed restaurant and bar that has a tropical rain-storm every 15 minutes or so. We shared a drink made for two- the mai tai which was really good. The atmosphere was really nice there! Also, walk across the street to have dinner or drinks at The Top of The Mark- the view was amazing at night! 
Anyway this hotel is the perfect place to stay on a trip to San Francisco, epecially for a romantic weekend! =)

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: Stayed in a handicap room on the 18th floor of the hotel, the view was fantastic. It overlooked the city and was so much fun. The bed was so comfortable it made you relax and sleep wonderfully. I want to go back and stay again... It is 54 dollars to park your car that is a lot but in San Fransisco even for some places you park you car it cost like 3 dollars for 20 minutes. It is located right downtown in Union Square where a half a block you can get on the cable car and go to fisherman's wharf or whatever. It is a great location. My niece and I were going to see a show at the Opreahem theater and it was only three blocks from the hotel. Across the street we ate at a really good Italian restaurant. Highly recommend it..

title: “Good Hotel”
text: My mother and I stayed at this hotel from Dec. 27, 2004-Dec.29, 2004. The hotel was clean and hotel staff was very friendly, and helpful. The rooms were comfortable and clean. The hotel is in a very good location and is within walking distance to 5th Avenue, Time Square, Central Park, etc. The only down side is that the hotel does not include/have breakfast. Overall a great hotel, that I would highly recommend.

title: “Look out for hiden costs”
text: The property of this hotel is beautiful and is worth the staying here. The issue I have with my last stay is the following: "When I checked out I noticed that the hotel had charged a resort fee of $20, maid fee per day and bellman fee." They need to have this on their web site when you are booking a room so you know exactly how much you cost is going to be and should be explained to you in detail when you check-in. Ideally they would hand you a piece of paper explaining exactly what these fees are for, so you could review them in your room. I ended up tipping people during my stay not knowing that in general this was being charged on a daily basis during my stay.

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text:
Essentially this is a really lovely hotel. Traditional in style and sympathetically renovated. Rooms are very clean. Bathroom basic but everything you need and the hair dryer in the bathroom is very impressive. The hotel is perfectly located for everything you want to do. On our 2nd day there they put the Christmas tree up and decorations and it did look beautiful. There are just a couple of things I would point out. I stayed there with my 21 year old daughter. We checked in on the Friday afternoon and were impressed enough by our room. We set out for the City and arrived back around midnight and tucked ourselves up into bed to get ready for a full day sightseeing. We were rudely woken 3 times in the night by people passing our room and being loud then giggly. On looking through the spyhole I realised that it was teenagers. I rang down to reception on 2 occasions for security to ask them to calm down and remain in their rooms. Unfortunately this did not work and we had to confront them ourselves. In the end I naturally was concerned about any further incidents that I phoned reception and asked to be moved. Sure enough, not a problem, We were transferred from the 3rd to the 14th floor within half an hour (it was 5.30am by then). Our second room was actually slightly nicer than our first, but they were both superior rooms. When I spoke to the receptionist later that morning she explained that they sometimes book in students from schools and do have problems with them from time to time, that they are not responsible for their behaviour, that is down to their teachers. I feel that this is inappropriate for this hotel to accommodate students in this way as it is not a cheap hotel and their behaviour certainly spoilt our first night sleep. The second night we were woken at about 2am by 2 drunken Irishmen in the room next door who had the TV on loud and were shouting above it!! I do recommend the hotel but on booking (1) ask for a room away from the elevator as you can hear the 'ping' every time it arrives on your floor and people don't always lower their voices when stepping out. (2) double check that you have no students on your floor. (3) the walls are a little thin and you can hear the next rooms TV and hear them talking! 
On the whole it was a lovely hotel. The staff are a bit hot and cold, some are a bit stuffy and find it difficult to smile and some are extremely helpful. Particularly the bellboys. One thing I would ask all travellers is that when you are in a hotel, just to consider who is in the next room, they may not want to hear your TV.

title: “Loved the Bonaventure”
text:
The Bonaventure is a great hotel, and you can usually get a room for $55 using priceline.com. For one or two people, it is ideal. For more, the room would be tight. All rooms have floor-to-ceiling windows and spectacular views, so they seem bigger than they are. Excellent Sony radio (and KUSC classical music) by beds and large tv. Spacious, very nice bathrooms and thick, plush towels. Good beds and lovely comforters. In the seven story atria downstairs there are more than 30 restaurants and snack bars, so you can eat easily at any price you like. Nice High Rise Cafe on 4th level for simple breakfast at $4.29. You can also eat at lobby buffet for $17.95. Marcello's is good Italian restaurant, and also a good Chinese restaurant on 6th level.
The hotel is with a few blocks walk of Disney Hall, Chandler Music Pavilion, new cathedral, MOCA (Museum of Contemporary Art), and California Plaza with free outdoor concerts at noon almost every day. 
The hotel is a block away from the bus top for almost all parts of the city and the subway station is two blocks away. You can get anywhere in the city by bus or subway, and an all-day pass costs only $3 and a week's pass costs only $14. Even Pasadena with the Huntington Library and Norton Simon Museum is only a 25 minute metro ride away on Gold Line or 35 minute bus ride on # 79.
Bonaventure Hotel is a great resource with very friendly and helpful staff and fantastic concierges. Thanks much!

title: “A great hotel for non-business travelers”
text:
Loved this hotel and the staff; however, it is not set up appropriately for business travelers...at least my room wasn't. I was upgraded to a pool side room which was beautiful, but I was unpleasantly surprised when I went to plug in my lap top at the desk and there was no outlet to be had. The only outlet I could use was the one of the other side of the bed, so I had to have my laptop charging on my bed all night. Same for my cell phone. Definitely not a friendly hotel for those of us who need to work in the room.
I cannot complain about the room and bathroom/dressing area. Very lovely, and I felt pampered. The staff was extremely attentive except I was surprised that when hosting a guest in the hotel lounge, I had to go to the bar myself to get us drinks. I think when spending $21/glass of wine, I should expect to be waited on.
If you stay here, definitely apply for the President's Club. You get free Internet connection that way, and perhaps that's why I was upgraded to a nicer room. One complaint though regarding the TV channels....I ordered a hockey game through NHL Center Ice, but after it charged me, the channel was not available. The hotel credited my account, but I was surprised that it was not offered. Especially since the San Jose Sharks were the team playing.

title: “Typical Holiday Inn, but with a view”
text:
Overall, we were not overly disappointed with our stay at this location. But that is mostly because we got it for under $100 through Priceline. I would bet this is the go to location for Priceline when you check Chicago's River North and a 3 star place. 
The location is not a long walk from Michigan Avenue or some pretty nice restaurants, but compared to many other places, this one is quite a bit off the beaten path. 
The views, as many say, are pretty good. Can they be beat? From experience, yes. This one offers a nice view of the river and the Willis Tower topping other buildings. We believe our view from the Hyatt on Wacker was better this past winter (river and Hancock building if you get a west facing room). 
Room here was a typical outdated Holiday Inn room, but it was clean and somewhat comfortable. You could sometimes hear the El, despite being so high up, but it did not keep me awake. The air conditioner was somewhat noisy and older type. 
We did not use the other areas of the hotel, except to have the breakfast buffet at the in house restaurant. Get there early if you want a decent buffet. We slept in after a late night at Second City. Our 10:00 am buffett was cold. Upon complaint, we were not charged.
Keefer's, Smith and Wolensky, Harry Carey's, Sullivan's, Gene and Georgetti are nearby restaurants. I can only vouch for Keefer's as being very nice!!. Howl at the Moon and House of Blues are nearby great entertainment. 
Parking is on site, but a little bit of a walk and $39 per night. There is a parking garage about 1-2 blocks west, but I did not catch the price for comparison. 
Given the price we got, we were certainly satisfied. If you have to pay the nomal, full price, I would recommend elsewhere. 
Best of all, the staff were very courteous !! 
Probably a decent stay for a family with the decent size indoor pool.

title: “Enjoyed our stay!”
text: Funky, fun decor! Great staff! Nice perks! We had a discount on our room, otherwise it may have been a little on the expensive side. The only real negative was that the room had a bit of a smell to it (old building) and the bathroom was nice, but showing a little wear.

title: “Just One Night”
text: This may be the nicest hotel in Boston. There's something wonderful about staying right on Boston Harbor. If you're going to spend the money, choose a room with a view. My harbor view room was upgraded to a two room suite. Lovely decor. This hotel is upscale but extremely easy-going and friendly. I had dinner at the Rowe's Wharf Bar which is just where you want to be on your first night in this city. This is an expensive hotel and Boston is an expensive town. The Boston Harbor Hotel sets just the right mood for a traveler who wants to experience historic Boston.

title: “Nice hotel downtown, beware of Tenderloin”
text:
The Nikko hotel was a nice hotel but not what we would call fabulous. Clean, competent, courteous within walking distance of Union Square. The staff was friendly and accommodating. We dialed 360 on our room phone whenever we needed our car and the valet always had it ready. We were bidding on Priceline hoping for the Westin St. Francis but got the Nikko instead. We won the bid at $229 but paid an extra $20 when we checked in, hoping to get a nicer room. We'd stay there again for less than $240 but would not more. 
San Francisco is a great pedestrian city and you don't need your car to enjoy it. You won't enjoy paying $51 per day to park there either. The front desk will give you a map which, oddly enough, does not have the neighborhood Tenderloin detailed on it. You really, really want to avoid the Tenderloin. When you walk out of the hotel, go East then North or South but do NOT go West. We'd been to San Fran many times and always heard the Tenderloin is a place to avoid. We inadvertently walked block after block after block through it in the middle of the day, and we feel fortunate that it was uneventful. Normally I would not dwell on a neighborhood but another review suggested it is somehow adventurous or romantic to stroll through this neighborhood. It is neither, don't waste your time or put yourself at risk. Also, given the probable large portion of out of town visitors this hotel must accommodate, it's inappropriate that the hotel does not offer any words of caution to their guests.

title: “Bin Laden Lives Better in a Cave”
text:
I can honestly say this is the WORST place t stay in midtown NYC. I would rather stay at the Bates Motel and take my chances of being killed than stay here again.An outlet did not work ,the bathroom mold was thick, the faucet would not turn on, there was garbage under the bed, and we got a good room because we looked at 4 other rooms.
 WHEN I WROTE TO THE BETTER BUSINES BUREAU HOTEL CARTER'S RESPONSE WAS " WE ARE A LOW BUGET HOTEL IN NYC,WHAT DO EXPECT."

title: “Good value for the location”
text: Stayed here for 2 nights. Clean, nice staff, but the location is the real value. Easy to walk to places and close to most things in Charlotte. Love the free parking, but not a lot of spaces near the hotel and spaces are small if you have a large car/truck

title: “PLEASE - DO NOT WORRY! HOTEL IS FINE!”
text:
Hi there ...
After reading the reviews on this site, I was a bit concerned about spending 3 nights here. We had pre booked everything, travelling from LA to San Fran, then across to Vegas via Yosemite & Death Valley.
Anyway, the Metropolis Hotel ...
We arrived about 11pm and after checking in, an extremely helpful bell man escorted us to our room and carried our (heavy) cases for us.
The room itself was very pleasant - we were on the 5th floor - the room was a decent size, clean and quiet. It also had a tv and a fridge. :-) 
Yes, the guy on the front desk can be a bit grumpy at times, but we found that with a smile and a bit of politeness, he soon perks up and can be quite chatty.
The area the hotel is in is ideal - it is is very central and Union Square is less than 5mins walk away. Having read the reports on this site, I was expecting to arrive in a ghetto. Okay - the area is not the nicest - but anyone who has been out drinking in ANY city in England - will have seen more aggression and felt more threatened than you do there. I'm originally from Newcastle, now living in Manchester and both are far worse at 2am on a Saturday than the area surrounding the Metropolis.
One guy did ask us for money - but a polite "Sorry Mate" was met with a "Thank you Sir, Thank you Ma'am" and he went on his way.
We also walked along the edge of the Tenderloin District after midnight following a night at the theatre, again, with no hassle.
So, all in all - a decent hotel in a good location for central San Fran. One piece of advice however, if you are renting a car and travelling, look into postponing it for the few days you arte in San Fran. We paid £57 (about $99) to park our car at the hotel for the 3 days we were there (didn't use it with the cable cars and feet!) - and then realised the car rental place (Dollar) was almost next door - would have been cheaper to hand the car back in and rent another 3 days later!
Good luck and enjoy!
Feel free to email me if you'd like any more advice about this hotel.

title: “Great Location!”
text: My husband and I stayed here for NYE 2012. It was kind of a last minute trip and I was looking for a four star hotel close enough to Times Square and still available two weeks before NYE. I read some great reviews on Trip Advisor of the Iroquois and we decided to stay here. The room was clean, but extremely small, even by NYC standards, but I think we had the smallest room on our floor when looking at the evacuation routes and floor plan posted to our door. I had requested a king sized bed and a room facing the street, and while I was advised those requests would be considered, neither was fulfilled. The room was clean, but the queen bed was small - both mine and my husbands' feet dangled off the edge. Since we only stayed the weekend, it wasn't that big of a deal, but if our trip was longer it would have become a problem. They served complimentary hot apple cider every afternoon in the lobby, which was delicious. It is a small, boutique hotel, but reasonably priced in an amazing location - we did not have to cab or take the subway our whole weekend and we went to Central Park, Times Square, Broadway, 5th Avenue, Rockefellar Center and the Meat Packing District. I would consider it again for a weekend stay.

title: “The basics”
text: Great hotel if you don't plan on staying in a lot. One elevator was out of order which was a bit of a nuisance, and don't plan on sun bathing because the pool is surrounded by tall buildings. Other than that it was clean and efficient and the parking garage was very convenient albeit pricey.

title: “Great location!”
text:
Spent a weekend in NYC with a buddy of mine. Picked this hotel due to it's location and great reviews on tripadvisor.
The location is incredible. Did a lot of walking but was able to get everywhere for 4 days without using any public transportation. A few places worth mentioning:
Madison Square Garden, Times Square/Broadway, Central Park, Empire State - all within walking distance.
Hotel staff was great and very helpful. Room itself was pretty small and but very clean. I'm used to a lot of AC thus it felt a bit warm at night but the staff helped me out there too by providing a table fan.
Overall I would recommend this place to any single/couple but families might want to get a place with larger rooms.

title: “A Great Location in an Amazing Place...”
text:
This hotel is in a great location when you look at the map and is within walking distance of everything in New York you want to see. We didn't eat in the hotel but the rooms were very comfortable and clean and the people were really helpful and friendly. 
New York is a place which is hard to describe but if you stay at a place like this you can see everything you want to as its location sells it, theres a number of small Deli places within a few minutes walk where the food is excellent. 
Would highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “SUPER small room, but would go back”
text: This hotel has a great location @ 47th & 8th and is an easy walk to all the theatres and restaurants around Time Square. You can even walk to Central Park pretty easily. The room was clean, the staff were helpful and friendly, but the room is TEENY TINY. I mean, really, really small. I know hotel rooms in NYC are small normally, but I've been to NYC numerous times and this was the smallest room I've ever seen. The two of us had a hard time finding space to open 2 suitcases. Since we didn't spend much time in the room, the size really didn't bother me too much. I'd definitely go back. However, I wouldn't recommend it if you're claustrophobic, spend a lot of time in your room, or are a larger than average person.

title: “Fabulous hotel -- the best of Sheraton”
text:
I stay in Sheratons & Westins as often as possible, and this particular Sheraton is the best I've ever stayed in. The hotel is three years old and looks brand new. They have both valet & on-site self-parking, and the self-parking is very easy to access, with an elevator to the lobby that also can take you to the first 17 floors of the hotel.
If you can get an upgrade to the club floor, or have high enough status with SPG to get club access, it's well worth it. Continental breakfast in the club lounge is excellent, with a variety of menu items including a range of cold cereals, hard-boiled eggs, beautiful fresh fruit (both whole and cut-up), and Starbucks coffee, all complimentary. Unlike most hotel club lounges, this one is open from 6AM - 11AM 7 days a week (normally at Sheratons & Westins the club lounges are open only until 9 or 9:30 AM weekedays and closed on weekends). In the afternoon there is an excellent light finger-food buffet provided from 4PM - 7PM, also 7 days/week.
The staff here is exceptionally friendly & helpful. The on-site restaurant has excellent (but over-priced) food. And the hotel also offers 24 hour room service. Fitness center is state of the art. I simply can't think of anything bad to say about this hotel -- it will be my preferred hotel any time I'm in the Phoenix area.

title: “Matchless in Midtown”
text: This hotel is so well located, within walking distance of Grand Central Terminal, and ideal for theatergoers. It is a fairly new tall and narrow building squeezed between two larger ones so there's little natural light, but the rooms are what you'd typically expect from a Marriott Courtyard, and surprisingly roomy for Manhattan...clean with comfortable bedding and plush towels, free internet, good in-room coffee (avoid the lobby machine stuff), flat screen TV, and most of all, a very professional and helpful staff. (We did not choose to use their breakfast option). And the price...$299 for a king-size... is matchless for a nice place in midtown. We will definitely return.

title: “VERY NICE HOTEL, ODD LOCATION”
text: No problems with Hotel. Very Nice breakfast buffet. Great view of Boston Skyline. Hard to find entrance to Hotel due to highway on ramps. Can't walk to downtown but able to do long walk to Harvard. 15 minute walk to subway. Hotel has a shuttle that will take you Downtown and Harvard approx every hour till 9pm but must reserve this. Our room was clean with lots of space. No Bellman greeted us when we arrived so we took our luggage up ourselves. Only parking is their garage with a $30 fee pr night...ouch.

title: “Great Hotel with an Outstanding Location”
text:
Arrived in San Antonio in the middle of my four city Texas trip and this hotel was excellent.
LOCATION
The location of this hotel is right in the middle of downtown San Antonio, which is the perfect spot for the two main attractions of the Alamo and Riverwalk. Drove right up to the front door and had valet take the car. The valet cost $23 per day, but this was not bad for a couple of reasons. First, the hotel is in walking distance of the main attractions so a car is not needed and secondly, the price is comparable to other parking lots in the area for people driving to the attractions, yet not as close as the hotel. Now there are some reviews saying that the Alamo is 3-4 blocks away from the hotel. This may be true in "San Antonio" blocks, but being from NY my definition of the word "blocks" is different. The Alamo is about a 5 minute walk equal to about 1 1/2 NYC blocks. The San Antonio blocks are so short that I anticipated the walk to be much longer. A nice short walk to the historic area.
An entrance to the Riverwalk is about 150 feet away from the hotel. Perfect since you could do what you needed to do at the Riverwalk and be right at your hotel when done. There are a few shops in the area and a 2 minute walk to a nice sports bar where we watched Italy defeat Germany in the Euro Cup. The area of the hotel is very clean and very safe. After drinking at the bars at the Riverwalk until closing time (2am), we decided to take a stroll to see the Alamo at night. Very peaceful as the Alamo is guarded by armed officers 24 hours a day. Just to be in the front of the Alamo in the quiet of night is very special. 
ROOM, PRICE, CLEANLINESS and COMFORT
The price of the room was about $160, but we got the biggest suite they have. The room design was a bit awkward, but I was only sleeping there, not buying the unit. You walk in and there was the bathroom to the immediate left and the kitchen setup to the right. Had a microwave, sink, fridge (all new all stainless steel), but no stove/oven. After passing the kitchen it opened up into a HUGE room. The only problem is the beds are all in the open area. There is no separate sleeping quarters. The open space had a desk, chair and flatscreen TV that the people on the couch could see and then a random piece of wall that had a flat screen for the two beds to see. Everyone was in the same room and when both TV's are on you can hear each others shows. Don't know the purpose since you could see both TV's from one of the beds. 
The couch turned into a bed which was one of the more comfortable pull out beds. The regular queen beds were very comfortable and provided a great sleep. The A/C worked good, but since the beds were all the way over on the far side of the room, it seemed like the coldest area was the kitchen and desk areas because there were not any blowers near the beds. The second you check in, put the A/C on the coldest you can so the room can have the cold air move toward the beds. Remember, the bed area is much warmer than the open area. Don't be fooled. There was a window in the room but our view seemed to be a non usable enclosed hallway. Another design flaw. 
The bathroom was very clean and interesting. There were not bathroom bars of soap (you have to bring it if you want it), but soap dispensers on the wall of the shower. Liquid body soap and shampoo. I actually liked this idea and thought it was pretty cool. Since I was not sure how to work it, I nearly broke one of the things trying to get the soap out. Eventually, my college degree came in handy and I figured out how to use it. I think it is much better using the gel instead of using the same bar of soap that everyone in your suite will roll over their dirty bodies. The rest of the suite was perfectly clean...no issues at all.
BREAKFAST and OTHER AMENITIES
The lobby had some sort of 24 hour soda/juice kinda thing but to be honest I really didn't listen when they were telling me so I am not sure what it was. Since this was the ONLY day on my trip I was able to sleep late, I am unable to tell you about the breakfast which they do have and did sound good from other reviews. The lobby is very open and has computers, couches, bathrooms, front desk, ATM etc. all in one big area. Access to the hotel after a certain hour was by card key only so that is good to keep anyone from coming in off the streets to use the bathroom. 
I would not hesitate to use this hotel again if going back to San Antonio. Easiest location to get around, plenty of action, and plenty of good places to go.

title: “Perfect choice for us!”
text: We really struggled with choosing a hotel for San Francisco, but this is the perfect place for anyone traveling with a car. This is one of the few locations with free parking and great rates. It is a no frills place, but very roomy. We requested a remodeled room and it wasnt exactly stylish, but it had a great bed and lots of space in the room. We requested a top floor away from Lombard and had no noise issues. You have to make sure and turn the privacy nob on the door or housekeeping will walk in. Also, they start cleaning early so we put the privacy sign out if we were sleeping in. The hotel is a simple block walk up to the 30Muni which you take most everywhere. It's an easy drive to the Golden Gate Bridge or to go down the crooked part of Lombard. A few blocks back from the hotel there's a great little restaurant for breakfast, La Boulange. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “LOVED this place!”
text: My husband and I stayed here during the NFJS conference and loved it. The rooms are huge for the price (huge!), the hotel is one of the cleanest I've ever been privileged to stay in. The staff, including bellhops, janitors, maid staff are all beyond reproach in appearance, manner, attitude,mien, genuine willingness to help and go above and beyond if need be - even the poor girl from room service who was THRILLED to bring us cake 15 minutes after they closed. It's difficult to find a place nowadays that offers a comp breakfast, not to mention a made-to-order omelet station manned by house chefs and a full buffet! They also offer a manager's happy hour, Westin-like lobby and social areas, nice pool and fitness facilities.... I could go on. Embassy Suites is only a short 10 minute jaunt to Easton (OH YEAH!! Go hit the Northstar Cafe - not just organic but free-range grassfed meats as well!!), or a short ride to Bexley, the Conservatory, etc. We did Shakespeare in Schiller Park and it was just a 15 minute drive to the German Village. On otp of it all the very little air traffic we heard was exceedingly similar to morning runs on the The Beast - totally got my juice moving in the morning! We are utterly impressed and will DEFINITELY be back - next time with our children, most likely (I'm sorry fellow travelers)! Loved it Loved it Loved it Loved it!!!

title: “Typical Drury Inn”
text: This hotel is a bit older but well-maintained. The standard room was very clean but not spotless. Considering the breakfast and drinks/light supper, a good value. We have noticed at Drury Inns overall a sharp increase in pets. Having dogs at the 5:30 kickback where food is available is a personal turnoff. We will probably try a different hotel on our next visit.

title: “First class stay”
text: Stayed for two day weekend in July with my wife. Hotel is top notch in all respects, but not cheap. Suite rooms are huge. Walking distance to everything. Use your $100 food voucher @ the Sunday brunch in the hotel. I have never seen a brunch like this. They let you walk into the kitchen! Would highly recomend over Ritz for the stay and brunch.

title: “Great hotel all around”
text:
Great location, tons of restaurants close by. Great breakfast buffet. I travel alot and am used to the standard "free" breakfast, this was nothing like that. Much, much better. Different items each day, and high quality food. Cookies and milk at nice were great touch. 
It is a non-smoking hotel and when someone in a room next to mine kept smoking, they moved me to another floor without a second thought. I travel here for business and will return.

title: “SERVICE : ABOVE AND BEYOND !!!!!”
text: Greeted with a smile as soon as I arrived, Andrea and Oliva were outstanding, they went above and beyond to help me and my family. I strongly " reccccommmmendddd " this facility just for the way we were treated ! The room was clean, the restaurant had excellent food and the service was great ! Being close to the airport with the shuttle was convienant as well. I will be coming back, thanks again so much for making our stay so nice, Jack

title: “Great location but noisy”
text:
Positives: The Hampton is in a great location. At 8th and 51st it is within walking distance of all Broadway shows, great if you love the theatre. Wicked, Putnam County Spelling Bee, Odd Couple, jersey Boys, and Hairspray, just to name a few, are less than a block away. Also, it's a few feet form two major subway stations that take you anywhere else you need to go in Manhattan. The rooms are large for NYC, and nicely furnished. The staff was friendly and accomodatiing. Breakfast is included, which helps the budget when you're traveling with a family. For Manhattan it's not expensive...for anywhere else it is (almost $250 a night by the time you add in taxes).
Negatives: There was construction on their parking garage the 5 days we were there. Non-stop hammering noise started at 8 am and went to 6 pm. We were not warned about this in advance. One of our daughters was sick with the flu while there, and trying to rest with the nosie is impossible. The breakfast buffet is mediocre, and as it gets close to closing time they don't refill it. Also, the lines of people waiting to get into the breakfast area get longer in the 30 minutes before close.
Would we stay there again? Yes, but I'd first make sure that no further renovations or construction is occurring.

title: “Simply Fabulous”
text: My travelling party and I had a fabulous stay at Andaz. From the word go, the staff were extremely helpful and obliging. The hotel is clean, modern and inviting. The rooms are great! Ours was huge, decked out with the latest technology (flat screen TV with Media Centre, touch pad lighting, etc.). The beds are comfy and the shower is a haven with its rain-head and foot-bath!!! Wireless and non-alcohol mini-bar items were complimentary, which was a welcome touch - as was the free wine in the evening! Location is excellent - opposite the NY Public Library, close to Bryant Park, MoMa, TOTR, and the 5th Avenue shops. The food in the restaurant was tasty, well-priced, and most importantly in New York, the portions weren't too big!!! In a nutshell - do yourself a favour and stay at Andaz 5th Avenue on your next stay in New York!! :)

title: “Location Location Location”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights and found it generally acceptable? We did have some issues with dirty bed linen on arrival (a boot print on the pillowcase was kind of a clue) but it got sorted out. As other reviewers have noted, the location is great for walking to many Memphis attractions. Not sure why some reviewers feel the area is unsafe. I don't regard having to walk past a Greyhound station as particularly threatening. The room and bathroom were clean. The free wi-fi was good when it worked , but it did tend to disappear altogether at random times. There is a Denny's a couple of blocks away as a breakfast option, and a TGIF opposite the ballpark if you want to avoid the Beale Street tourist traps.

title: “Motel 6 - Tricks”
text: Stayed at the Motel 6 near sea world. I have never been in a Motel 6 before so maybe this is not a typical experience. We are a family of 4 and only recieved two towels and two wash cloths. Called the front desk and asked for more and was told they would not be ready until 12:00 Noon. So I guess we shouldn't have planned to shower in the morning. Another issue was the room had no clocks no pictures or etc - pretty stark. So since there was no clocks I asked for a wake-up call at 5:00 am - did not receive it - woke up on my own at 6:00 am in a panic. The room was clean but very small for $95 a night. I never been a motel/hotel where you need to put in your room key to get ice. I will not stay in a motel 6 again.

title: “Great for families”
text: Nice location and perfect for those with a family with the kitchenette. Surprised to see dishes including wine glasses supplied. Front desk was friendly and efficient. Pass key to access elevator which is a nice security feature. Right down the street from a liquor store and Walgreens too.

title: “3 star hotel at a 5 star price - and lots of side charges”
text: We chose Edgewater for our New Year's Eve get-away as it offered a very nice view of the Space Needle and the fireworks display, plus was billed as an iconic Seattle landmark that catered to many celebrities such as the Beetles, Led Zeppelin, etc. Unfortunately the price value didn't match the hype; particularly for the traveling family. We had booked a family suite with a balconey and a Space Needle view. Turns out you can't have both so we obviously opted for the view but now in a smaller room, (for the same price). On site parking is by valet only and is over $40 w/tax however there is a parking garage across the street for $21/day. Close to Pike Street Market and obviously the waterfront. Close to Seattle Center, and Space Needle but quite a hill climb. On site shuttle is available but not on demand; it's by their schedule. Very expensive restaurant on site but nearby is Spaghetti Factory. No luggage carts available; all controlled by bell hops; for a fee. (Small) gift shop has a bistro but limited hours. Lobby has a western lodge theme for some reason and then store-bought posters of various rock bands over the fireplace, (none autographed by-the-way). Rooms, decor, etc. Reminded me of a Travel Lodge type inn but at a 5-star hotel price. However will say all the staff was polite and tried to be accomodating.

title: “Feels like home”
text:
Travel across to DC frequently and staying at the RC Georgetown has become a home away from home. Staff are terrific, helpful and friendly. Food is great and nothing is ever too much trouble. Rooms are quiet, luxurious and staff very responsive.
Location is great as you are about 1 minute away from the heart of Georgetown. Some of the views could be better but that would be nit-picking.
An example for other hotels to follow.

title: “Downtown was a great stay”
text:
Just stayed overnight at the Downtown Marriott. Stayed in a standard room 2 queens with my 2 daughters 14,15. Still had plenty of room. Beds were very nice, really comfy pillowtops. Stayed there because of the proximity to the Kimmel, went to Wicked for the second time. My mother brother sister and sister-in-law stayed and enjoy it as well. Pool is very small(splash) whirlpool was nice. hotel was very clean. Asked for early check-in, but that didn't happen. Big KUDOS to mccarthys5 on TA, she really knows Philly. Any questions you may have she is dead on.Thanks for all the help. Went to Reading Terminal for lunch and my sis-in-law insisted on Down Home Diner.. mediocre at best. Out of Ribs and pork bar-b-que. Po boy was okay, my fried chicken was dry and overcooked. Left to get some Maalox, but stopped atr Bassett's. Lordy.. Redeemed!! Probably the best butter pecan ice cream I have ever had. For dinner we did Buddakan.. again easily (9 out of 10). Service lacked a bit, but we were a party of 8. reservation at 8:30, seated about 9:00. Drinks were good, Sangria was a little weak. Appetizers were excellent, food was as well. They stagger the order and encourage sharing, a good thing with 8 people. Bill was about $500 with drinks and appetizers I considered it a bargain. The biggest surprise was the breakfast buffett. It was really great. Fruit was fresh and sweet. Omelet station was magnificent. OJ was fresh squeezed. Waffles(at the omelet station), hot and crisp. When you book ask for the breakfast added and the buffett is only 4$ or so additional!!!!! What a bargain. Macy was close so the girls had a good time. Mom got on the Ducks, got wet but enjoyed the tour and Delaware river. The view of City Hall was nice and the architecture in Center City is great. What do I say about Wicked... We had a great time in the place of my birth. Thanks Courtyard Downtown Marriott et al... I'll add some pix later.
Kevin

title: “Charming and reasonable”
text:
I arrived way before check in time expecting to just leave off my bags. However they had a room available for me. The staff was consistently pleasant and helpful.
The theme of the hotel is, as you might guess, movies. Each room is named for a movie. Mine was The Graduate. No Mrs. Robinson, alas. Just her picture. Hehe.
The location is good. Close to Union Square. 
The room was clean. It was small. Hey, you're in San Francisco. You gonna sit in your room?

title: “30 minutes in this hotel is enough!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel last week on business. We stayed for exactly 30minutes! After a flight from london a boutique hotel, endorsed by leading hotels of the world sounded great. Here are 5 reasons NOT to go to the Whitehall Hotel:
1. Musty, dirty hotel.
2. Dirty, Bathrooms with taps etc that come off in your hand.
3. Piles of dirty bedsheets inthe corridors outside your door.
4. Worn carpets, yellowing walls surfaces and dust everywhere.
5. The rudest and most discurteous hotel manager I have every come accross
Escaping is not an option unlike your other reviewers we had to bargin our way out at $100 each! The four seasons accross the road where we moved to found this incredulous and were fantastic, we got a suite each for just $20 more. That is service! I know where I will revisit in future.

title: “Great, central location in downtown Chicago”
text:
I really like the location of this hotel with its proximity to Michigan Ave., West Hubbard St. and loads of restaurants, bars, pubs, shopping and everything else you'd want.
The hotel itself has great suites. The rooms are's elegant, but they are comfortable. A great size with a bedroom and a living area / kitchen combination. The living area is a good size with a sleeper sofa, an arm chair and a dining table. 
For business travel, they have all the connections for the LCD TV right out front making it easy to connect your laptop to the TV, plug in, etc. I really like the fact that there are numerous power outlets very conveniently located. I tend to have lots to plug in.
The staff are all friendly and attentive. As soon as I pulled up they had my bags out of the car, the elevator door open and I was on my way to the 6th floor for check-in.
This is a reasonably priced hotel where you'll have lots of space, decent food in the morning and evening, free internet access and a location that makes everything easy to get to. It's also a few minute walk to the RED line.

title: “Always the Palace.”
text: We visit NY. 3-4 times a year. From the door men to the maid service are all trained to make the customer feel special. We know NY very well and have stayed at least 10 comperable hotels, and we kept going to the Palace. The weekend deals are the best also.

title: “Good value but mediocre hotel in great location”
text: Stayed for 4 nights with my daughter in a fairly small twin room. Location is great - near Times Square; Central Park; 5th Avenue and hotel was pretty good value but it was really busy so checking in took a while, we had to wait for a porter to get up to the bedroom; then the room wasn't ready; shower wasn't hot at 4pm on two days running but fine in the morning; had to get someone to sort out the heating cos couldn't turn it off and the room consequently was boiling; at the end of our stay we asked them to sort out a taxi to JFK - was told it would be $45 plus taxes and tip - total of $61 - and that it'd take max one hour - when we got into the taxi, the driver said it could take up to 2 hours (rush hour - we left at 4pm - in fact it did only take 45 mins but I was a bit anxious about time) and he said the tip was for the hotel not for him (wasn't sure about this but paid tip anyway). All in all, given the location, the hotel was good value and as we went on a recommendation from a friend I didn't spend much time researching hotels. If you want great location and are prepared for a few smallish snags, it's fine.

title: “Great value for money”
text:
This hotel is in a great spot - close to transport and also within easy walking distance of many attractions and shops. It is also a very picturesque spot. The neighbourhood is quiet and residential. 
We stayed in a one bedroom suite. We liked the decor and found the bed comfortable. The living area and the bedroom were a good size but the bathroom and kitchenette were a bit small and our room had a strange layout with the bathroom and kitchen on either side of a narrow entrance. I would have preferred the bathroom to be ensuite but this is a minor thing. 
The bathrooom cleanliness needed a little attention to detail. I dropped my toothbrush and found that the floor under the vanity was a little dusty and there was an old bandaid and an old hair elastic under the vanity. It is for this reason that I haven't given the hotel five stars. 
It was great to have access to a Nespresso machine and the breakfast was fine, especially as it was included in the price. 
I liked the fact that the reception was downstairs and that you could make use of it, if you wanted. I really enjoyed the private feel of the apartment but some people might prefer having a more traditional hotel set-up.

title: “Ritz-Carlton quality”
text: The Kimpton chain hotels are amazing! When we arrived at Denver they facebooked us to ask if we were still coming and that they couldn't wait to see us and the dogs. They helped us get the luggage up to the room and also had pet beds and pet bowls waiting for us just like we had requested. Also they give you complimentry beer which was amazing and everynight they have wine you can go down to the lobby and drink it's really awesome. To sum this up it's a great hotel with great amenities I would recommend staying at any of the chains! :-)

title: “Modern, clean and big rooms.”
text: Very nice, modern, recently - 3yrs ago built. Bigger than usual rooms, comfortable beds, super close to both stadiums.

title: “First Time Experience”
text: This was our first time to this hotel. We had heard wonderfult things about this place but had no idea how great it actually would be. The staff was extremely accommodating, friendly and quick to make you feel welcome. It is a truly charming hotel. The room was clean, had a sectacular view, and many personal touches to make you feel at home. The hotel bar and restaurant was great. The location is close to everything. Everything about our stay was delightful. We will be back!!!

title: “Our third stay, and not a disappointment!”
text:
My Dad and I have always enjoyed this hotel, and this past weekend was no exception. We were in town for the Baltimore Grand Prix, which took place over Labor Day weekend. Access to the hotel was a challenge due to street closings, but the staff handled it well. They helped us with any transportation arrangements we needed, and had suggestions for lunch and dinner too.
We'd taken the train (the station is less than 15 minutes from the hotel), so the complimentary shuttle to the station was great, too. As always, our room was quiet and clean, and we also took advantage of breakfast each morning. Highly recommended. On our next trip to Baltimore, we'll be back!

title: “Best place to stay”
text:
Best location, a block away from Magnificent Mile and Lake Shore drive and quiet neighborhood-- what more can you ask. The inn is clean, suites are spacious, with a kitchenette, feels like home and free breakfast. The valet parking is $47 nightly, self parking across the inn is $37nightly.
The Inn does not have a swimming pool which is ok for me. Relaxing ambiance to live close to the lake. The breeze and the magnificent view of the lake, buildings and navy pier is the highlight to the place. This will be my official place to stay.

title: “Don't stay here if your would like housekeeping!”
text: Don't stay here!!! Our family was getting together from all over the country for a family event in Baltimore. We had 5 rooms. Only one of our rooms got housekeeping services, when our cousin complained about the lack of it. She did ask that the other family members rooms be serviced as well--they were not! If I threw the dirty towels outside my door on the floor, later in the day, I would find some clean ones in a plastic bag outside the door. Otherwise, I had to grab a housekeeper in the hallway and ask for some. Seriously, no service at all. No vacuuming, no trash removal, no beds made up, no bathroom cleaned etc. for the 4 nights we were there. The breakfast was not worth trying. Sure, this place is inexpensive, and the manager sounds so nice on phone, but if you want to spend a few nights here, I would not. We would never go there again.

title: “Magnolia overextends itself”
text: Rented two queen suites for a Saturday night. Hotel was full to capacity Friday night and hosting two holiday parties Saturday night. This is fine and good, but the Magnolia did not staff up properly to handle the busy-ness. Tried to check into my rooms at 3 PM and was denied. Finally got into one room at 4:30 and the other at 5:30. That simply is not acceptable when the published check-in time is 3 PM. The keys didn't work for one room. The suites were nice enough, but I must admit I was a bit disappointed with the stay. Oh, and checking out they tried to charge me a $25 parking free even though I didn't have a car. When I told the lady at the front desk, she didn't believe me and was reluctant to refund the charge. She called the valet and was surprised when he confirmed what I said, that I didn't have a car there.

title: “Great hotel in great location”
text: The Marquis has it all: location, amenities, staff. The basic room and bathroom were spacious. One great note. Through computer technology, there is never a wait for the elevators.

title: “Great place ...”
text: Beautiful hotel right on the river. Was going to stay at Four Seasons on the other side of the river but for $300 less per night the Hyatt was the perfect choice! Super clean rooms and bathrooms. Very comfortable. Perfect location for walking around town with the capital a few blocks up and tons of cool stores, restaurants and bars feet away.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We have just come back from a weekend stay in Jurys and we were not disappointed.
We arrived early and our room was not ready, so rather that leaving us waiting the receptionist gave us an upgrade. Lovely touch. The room was lovely, decor modern and unfussy , bed was huge and very very comfortable. I know it is a cliche but I loved the turn down service.
The staff were very very friendly. From the concierge to the bell boy, they could not have been more helpful answering all our questions and providing us with loads of suggestions of how to spend the weekend.
Free internet acess in the business center was an additional bonus.

title: “FANTASTIC HOTEL”
text:
Me and Hubbie stayed here from 25th to 29th October this year and we LOVED the hotel!! You HAVE to stay here if you are looking for a great hotel - I cant fault it!! They even left us bottle of red wine as an anniversary pressie along with a box of 4 choccies and a card!!
We were lucky enough to be given a room with 2 beds (I sleep badly so its great for hubbie to sleep without me :)!!
We were in room 1204 so didnt have a view but who needs one in New York - we were never in our room except to change for the evening or to sleep!!!
The view from the Rooftop bar was FANTASTIC - I just couldnt believe I was really seeing it!!
We had a burger in the Rare bar which was good (over charged us but that was easily sorted!)
Our room had always been cleaned by the time we got back late afternoon to get ready for the evenings and we always got downturn service!
The shower did actually take my breath away one day with the cold water because as others say - you have to get in the shower to turn it on but that isnt a big deal at all!! And I was never in the shower long enough for the light in the bathroom to turn off!
The beds were the BEST I have EVER slept in - thats the truth! 
The hotel is in a great place - you can walk to most places from here. We found the most gorgeous shop on 23rd street - fantastic fresh food and vegetables - so beautifuly presented that I want to live near there just to use the shop!!
One tip for new visitors to New York - get the shuttle bus from the aiport to the hotel (they are there in uniform as you come out of the airport) - its $19 each plus tip! We were really lucky we got on the same bus as 4 other couples so they started dropping people off at 97th st and came all the way down to 26th st (Fashion s6 hotel) last so we got a free view of half of New York!! And we got their card and so we rang them for the journey back to the airport and again it was £19 plus tip - we just gave the driver $50 each way!
Fashion 26 is a great hotel - the cupcakes are lovely but not the best (I was a bit disappointed to be honest). 
Please contact me if you want any tips or advice at all!!

title: “Depends on your idea of good”
text:
First of all, the good points: this hotel is half a mile to the Navy Pier, has an expansive free breakfast, indoor pool that was relatively clean and spacious rooms. Although, I can't say for sure, I think the State St location has slightly bigger rooms.
We stayed for 4 nights in June with 2 adults and 3 children. I always travel with a small fan because I cannot stand hearing a ton of noise. We were on the 9th floor and I could hear cars peel out on the street, followed 10 seconds later by police sirens all night the first night. So, to add to my fan, the second night I played nature sounds on my phone as well. 
My husband slept on the pull out couch and could hear the morning crew readying breakfast at 5am just as if they were outside the door. The atrium effect that all Embassy Suites have.
Thereafter, we could hear people in rooms on both sides of us. One with a baby that cried half the night and the other a room full of drunks guffawing until 3 am. This is something I have yet to experience in a hotel. I read about it all of the time. So another night with little sleep.
You have to go in through a lower entrance, then elevators to get to the lobby/reception. The bellmen quickly pointed us the way. There's an underground area where I guess the bellman will call a cab for you, but none ever offered when we were standing there. So we just walked out to the street and waved one down. 
If you're up for walking, a lot of places are within walking distance here. After walking from the red line, all over the airports, to and from the Navy Pier, my 4 year old had had enough. So we spent a bit more on cabs than planned.
We were very close to the Mile and walked the 2 blocks to window shop a couple of nights. There is a Dominick's grocery store across Columbus that has every thing you could need. 
I am on a restricted calorie diet and found the breakfast to be a bit difficult for me, but if you like cereal, yogurt and skim milk, this will work for you. Breakfast every day we were there was eggs, hash browns, sausage, bacon, and pancakes. They also had fruit but it looked like it had been rolled in liquid goop. If you were patient, there is an omellette station. There's everything to drink and I was especially pleased to find apple juice and a soda machine. I've given up soda, but happy to see it as an option. 
In every other Embassy Suites we've stayed in there was bottled water in the room on the check in, then after so many days. No bottled water and the vending machine dropped frozen solid drinks.
All in all, I don't think I would stay here again. I don't think it was horrible by any means, but if I'm going to pony up close to 3 a night, I want it be nicer than this hotel.

title: “great location”
text: The hotel at times square is a no frills place and we loved it because of its location, just two blocks away from times square. The hotel didnt even have a restaurant as one has all the eating joints around it .It serves you a complimentary continental breakfast :)

title: “Excellent hotel in downtown Philadelphia”
text: This hotel is in an excellent location (Rittenhouse Square). The staff was extremely helpful when I needed some printing done, as I was traveling on business. The hotel offers complimentary happy hour with wine & popcorn from 5-7pm and has coffee and tea in the lobby each morning. The hotel restaurant was also impressive. Note all Kimpton hotels offer free wifi once you become a Kimpton In Touch member, which is free.

title: “NICE FOR KIDS”
text:
First i like to mention, that some reviews on this site mix up this H.I with another one closer to downtown. there is NO Cruise Terminal and no trolley stop at the other side of the street.
The BAYSIDE H.I is at the beginning of Shelter Island and our experience was not a bad one.This is an older property, but our room in the main building was in good shape with comfortable beds. the hotel was very busy (over labour day weekend) and the pool was really a kids' place and maybe a bit small for a property this size. bikes were available for free and our son liked the 9 hole golf and the billard table (also free of charge). front desk employees were professional and helpful, except one big guy who really seemed to live in another world. he did not hand out "kids eat free" vouchers and could not answer any question, in fact i think he did not even understand questions.
surrounding the hotel is some lower income housing and expensive homes are within walking distance. the area does not give a bad feeling.
all in all i think we could have made a worse choice and considering that san diego is an expensive place, one should have reasonable expectations.

title: “A pleasant surprise in a convenient location - plus free parking in DC!”
text: We live in the neighborhood, so when the power went out we called the Savoy Suites. They had a room available, but I don't know why. OK, there is no pool. I get that. But you can walk to great restaurants and even to Georgetown. The rooms are spacious and well appointed. The place is clean and feels very safe, the parking is free, and the staff is very friendly. We had a view of the monuments from our 8th floor room (which had a jacuzzi). Tremendous! Give this place a try. Seems it is too much of a well kept secret....

title: “Travel-Agidda”
text:
To begin with I made the mistake of booking through an internet booking site, thus paying 50% more than most of the guests for the same or lesser rooms. My fault, not the hotel's, but it doesn't help. While the website advises that the hotel is "close to Union Station" it is in fact a full mile away. Check-in was awful; we arrived around noon and were allowed to store our bags until the 3pm check-in time, about which they were very strict: by 3pm, the lobby was filled with over 40 people who had arrived at various times during the afternoon but were not permitted to check in until exactly 3pm. The rooms have no irons or ironing boards; no mini bar; no microwave; things you'd get standard even at a much cheaper roadside location. Each room had a radiator and an air conditioning unit build into the window such that the window could not be opened; this became a problem during the night when the power in the room failed in the stifling heat. The desk clerk responded to my complaint that the circuits were overloaded and nothing could be done. That's probably true; the overhead light switch in the room sparked when I switched it! At one point during the day at least one of the elevators got stuck and a guest had to climb out. The free "high-speed" internet is so slow that a short video would take close to an hour to download. The shelf over the sink in our bathroom was broken, leaving absolutely no place to store toothbrushes, etc. Water pressure in the shower was poor (although we were on a high floor in this 12-storey building). We expected a complimentary continental breakfast, as their website advertised this, but when we got there, they told us they'd stopped doing that - although that's one of the features I'd paid for. 
The location is excellent - a block from the CTA Red Line and a block or so from Buckingham Fountain - in a very noisy but busy and safe area of the city. Despite the check-in fiasco and their inability to fix the power outages, the staff was very friendly and tried to be helpful.
The "fully equipped" business center consisted of one computer and a non-functioning printer.
This place was so much cheaper than anything else in the city, I should have realized it was too good to be true. I'd recommend it, because for the difference in price I'd volunteer to suffer. It's a glorified hostel, and if you can deal with that, this place is OK.

title: “A perfect end to our honeymoon”
text:
I booked the Villa Delle Stelle for the last 3 nights of our honeymoon about a year ago after reading the excellent reviews it had on trip advisor. It didn't disappoint.
We arrived weary after an epic trip round California, and walked in to find a bottle of red wine, a bagette and the most ripe brie I could imagine. Even a pinkt of mils and some chocs were waiting too. Perfect!
We stayed in the Parissien suite, which is beautiful. To the poster who commented on having to get our of bed for the lights, we found that too! The suite is very luxurious, just having a kettle, and begin supplied with PG tips teabags after 2 weeks of naff tea made in a coffee maker was amazing (sorry I sound so old and English).
The suite had everything we could think of to make the stay special. The only thing I can suggest it to have a computer available, as it took us hours to find somewhere to access the internet to book tickets for Universal as we would get an extra day free that way. 
LA itself was not as great as I had imagined, maybe at the end of our journey it was just a bit too much hard work! We enjoyed the movie star homes tour, and seeing the sights of Rodeo Drive and Beverley Hills. The folder in the suite was so well thought out, full of info, maps ect. it came in very handy.
We had an SUV, which fit in the space fine, right by the door, so not sure what the problems others have mentioned were.

title: “Perfect Location Downtown”
text:
This property has everything you could want! We stayed in a studio king and it was plenty of room for two people. They have an outdoor rooftop hot-tub that was really nice. Went here to see Jazz vs Nuggets at the Pepsi Center and I was able to walk to the free ride and then walk to the arena. Total travel time = 15 minutes. 
We took the free ride and then walked to Wynkoop. Great pub with great food and beer, I highly highly recommend it. We also took the public bus to the Denver Zoo which was awesome. If you do google maps it will tell you how to get to the property via public transit. The buses are cheap and a good way to go seeing as the airport is way in the eff out of the way.
This property is right near everything downtown. The staff was friendly and the free breakfast buffet was large and delicious. I will stay here again when/if I come back to Denver.

title: “fun and different hotel with amazing staff and great restaurant”
