text: The SLS is a different hotel located in the middle of everthing and a short ride from the center of beverly hills, with the price tag to match, but its a fun scene with a great weird design and amazing food-especially at Bazaar which is busy at night. yes it is very very dark as everyone says, especially in the room which was clean and modern but not as functional with the design. the staff is wonderful and attentive and really make you feel special, particularly Aaron at the front desk during check in who was helpful and nice and Danny the bellman who took time to sit with us explaining the local map and help plan what activities to do nearby, including dinner at Bazaar. he and everyone is right- amazing place to eat, even if pricey- its a must do! overall great and different place to stay with a great staff and fun night scene.

title: “very adequate_acceptable, magnificent location”
text: all you want and desire to do in chicago start from this hotel _most of the attraction can reached by foot from the hotel_the reception give you a very useful map when you check in >that's really great_the lay in the heart of downtown_ john hancock is 2 blocks behind_navy pier ,lake shore,windella boat,shops is very close,hotel itself is clean _room is not small neither big average i can say_they have a concierge which kept my luggage until evening coz my flight was in midnight,anyhow i recommended to everyone _don't need to pay much more_chicago is beautiful city. enjoy

title: “Great location and free parking”
text: It's a old hotel with old rooms, cordial reception, poor breakfast, slow wireless internet (free), but with a nice location and free parking (that's difficult in SF).

title: “Great hotel within walking distance to restaurants, shops, bart station, and union square park.”
text: This is the first time staying at this hotel. The price is reasonable compared to the other high end hotels. The hotel is located within walking distance to great restaurants, shopping, bart station, and the Union Square park. Our room was the standard room with the basic ammenities. It faced O'Farrel which was mainly a view of the street and parking structure. Staff was friendly. Valet was quick to retrieve the car.

title: “Great for families”
text:
My family and I (five people with three teenagers) spent the holday week at the Trump International Hotel. We had the PTS upgrade of adjoining one bedroom suite and a deluxe king bedded room. The accomodations were perfect. There was a common door to the hall and then a private hallway to the suite and bedroom. More than enough space and privacy. The health club was excellent with a more than adequate pool, sauna, steam room, plenty of towels, water, and robes. The breakfast was at the Jean-Georges Nougatine room, very contemporary and good. Service at breakfast could be slow at times though. The location of the hotel was excellent- easy access to subway, buses, Broadway, Lincoln Center, etc.
This is a hotel that is worth the money.

title: “Shameless price gouging”
text:
First it is in a terrible location unless you like being next door to a homeless shelter. Next they charged me over five hundred dollars for a room that was not worth two hundred. The police convention was in town and everyone was booked up. The place should be closed
Doughtelebaneseguy

title: “Unique Property, Conveniently Located”
text:
This is a great building and the room was exceedingly comfortable. The room had a convenience kitchen, abundant work/conversation space and a very comfortable bed and bath area. 
Customer service was excellent. I was greeted as soon as I entered, check in was immediate. I called for ice while I waited for the ice maker in my fridge and I had ice delivered right to my door - at 11 p.m. - within just a couple of minutes.
I was staying here only for one night for business, but could definitely make this my go to place for a future trip of much longer length.

title: “Love the hotel!”
text:
We stayed at the Conrad Chicago for 7 nights in May 2007 and absolutely love the hotel. The location is great, one block off of Michigant Ave., close enough to the Magnificent Mile without the noises, and 2 or 3 blocks north of the river. We were able to walk to the John Hancock building, the Art Institute, Nave Pier and State Street in the Loop. A $12 cab fare took us to the Museum Campus.
It has plenty of restaurants nearby within walking distance (love the Grand Lux Cafe on Michigan Ave.). It's also next to the relatively new North Bridge mall with Nordstrom as the anchor. The hotel is accessable on Michigan Ave. through the mall. 
The hotel staff is very courteous and check-in was very quick. We stayed on the 7th floor and the room is very clean with a spacious bathroom (separate bath and shower). The room has a 42-inch flat panel TV and an IPOD dock. The bed is very comfortable. The hotel also provides slippers and a bathrobe. We paid $219 per night. If we go back to Chicago, we would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: The location is great: a subway station on the corner; a few blocks from Central Park, a few blocks from Times Square, but you are far enough from the chaos that Times Sq can be. The room and the washroom were clean and fair. A bit cold, but okay. The lobby was always busy and they do not offer free wi-fi (asking for it does not cost a thing, though). However, it was not a problem to me. When you're in NYC, you won't spend a lot of time at the hotel. Park Central provided an excellent service for what I needed during my stay. Moreover, Elisabeth was very polite and kind to us; she was great!

title: “lovely weekend at the ritz”
text: We were just at the Ritz for a weekend getaway. The staff could not do enough for us. The room was lovely, and the lobby a great place to chill.

title: “Exactly as Expected”
text:
Booked this hotel when I went to New York, because I worked as a supervisor for an online travel company that frequently received complaints on this hotel, and I guess I was tempted to see what all the fuss was about.
First, yes, the rooms are VERY small. That was the primary complaint we received on the property. After staying here myself, I refunded any customer I dealt with that had complaints about the size of the room and was staying for more than one night. Being in Manhattan, I expected a room tinier than my studio apartment at home, but this pushed the envelope just a little too far, especially for the price they charge.
Yes, on to that price...Given this hotels location, and the overall property itself, I feel the price was on the high end of what fair would be. This is a beautiful property, but if I had to stay in their rooms for an extended time, I would have gone insane.
We also had an issue with hot water while we were there. Had none, called to front desk, and maintenance was sent up within about 15 minutes. Since the water had been running 20 minutes by then, it was luke warm. We were on our way to a show on Broadway, and really didn't have time to wait for them to fix the shower. So luke warm shower it was, and they assured us they would work on the problem while we were out.
When we arrived back at about 2AM, the problem was solved, and a nice basket and letter from the manager was there for us. Case closed, as we weren't going to let something so small ruin our trip. It was an issue, yes, but they resolved it exactly as they should have, quickly and efficiently.
If the price was right...I MIGHT stay again but for no more than a night or two. In the future I would probably stay outside of Manhattan in exchange for a bigger room.
I would reccommend to a friend if they were looking for location, as this hotel most definitely has that, but they would get a stern warning about the room size.

title: “GOTTA LOVE THE POD”
text: I stayed here Christmas Eve and it was a very positive experience. Modern place, space managed room. Room number 1140 I believe was the #, I'd definitely return. It had a terrace with a walk out to the roof, shared with another room across. The bathroom was very well laid out creative. The wall is glass, and when the bathroom door slides closed your mate can be viewed nude from the bathroom, sensual for my date and I. The room was small, queen bed was good, however, it was well thought out, I like this place a great deal and the rate that I paid from hotels.com was 116.97 american, all included, unbeatable deal. If I was offered this rate again I would not hesitate to make time to get back to The Pod.

title: “Great deal, if you can setttle for an aged beauty.”
text: i made a reservation for the Boston Park Plaza through hotwire, but was a bit concerned once i read the reviews here. I was actually surprised by the Park Plaza! It is a very large, stately hotel, that is rich in history and charm ( A radio station once broadcast from the penthouse, and servant/ valet doors within doors) . The rooms are very small...particularly with the kingsized bed...they are adequate, however, and while not top notch, it was clean enough to make up for the places it was showing its age. The location is amazing, and all the restaurants within the hotel make even lazing around the building more interesting than the holiday inn. Bottom line, probably not worth full price, but a marvelous steal on priceline or hotwire-- great for the young set.

title: “Not what I expected”
text:
Based on it's rating, I was really looking forward to this hotel, but it was not what I expected. We reserved a Deluxe Room with King Bed and it is probably the smallest room I have ever stayed in. The door to the room practically hits the bed when you open it, and the recliner was shoved into the corner and you couldn't move around it. . There was a small table and then the bathroom. That was it, which was pretty darn tight for two people for 3 nights. Not much space for our luggage and NO privacy, given that our bed was literally right next to the door...if you catch my drift.
Our room on the 8th floor faced another building's wall, so not much to look at either.The bathroom was sparse, a very small vanity which did not have enough room for two people's toiletries. We had little to no hot water. We would have to turn on the faucet and/or the shower and leave it on for a solid 10 minutes before it would start to warm up. Just weird, but I guess it's an old building. 
The complimentary drinks and buffet were nice, but no real healthy food (chicken strips, nachos, chips variety) and extremely overcrowded with people acting as if they hadn't been fed in days. Just made it not worth the effort. The neighborhood was just plain scary. Lots of people sleeping on the streets all around the hotel and numerous run down shops. 
The pool and hot tubs on the roof were great. Nice and warm. The fitness facilities were not that great. 4 treadmills, a wobbly elliptical, a recumbent bike and a couple weird weight machines. Nothing to write home about.
Hotel had easy access to the Riverwalk and had complimentary wi-fi (fabulous!) and a nice business center. 
But, no room service, no hotel bar, no hotel restaurant, no spa, and no pay per view movies (just standard cable), make this a sub-par hotel. Sorry, but next time I'll be at the Hyatt.

title: “Not up to Hilton standards in other cities”
text: The hotel was clean and the staff was friendly and helpful. This hotel was a nice place to stay, but not special in any way. I am a Hilton honors member, and it seems that Hilton's in other cities(downtown areas) are often more unique, upscale hotels. If traveling to an Francisco again, I would choose to stay in a more unique hotel.

title: “Room 211”
text:
Ok, hotel in a great location! room rates good, room clean and tidy, however our bed was like sleeping on the floor it was that hard.
Hotel, run of the mill, nothing out of this world, but you get what you pay for and it was clean.
Hotel staff, need a kick up the bottom!! No smiles, no good morning!! not very welcoming, cold attitudes!! GET IT SORTED

title: “As expected”
text:
I was really worried about staying at Hotel Carter after reading the reviews but I can say it wasn't any worse than I expected.
On arrival we were given the wrong room, it wasn't a problem to get it changed. The original room was worse than the one we ended up with. The bathroom and also the closet door didn't fit in the frame so didn't close properly and the toilet wasn't very clean looking. But the room we ended up with was better. 
The room was clean, sheets, bathroom etc. The bathroom was in full working order. We stayed for 4 night and the maid came after two nights to clean and change sheets. Also the view wasn't bad.
We had no problem with the staff apart from the fact that they didn't speak great english, but we got by and understood. Was just more annoying than anything else.
The lobby and the lifts do smell greasy but thankfully the lifts are pretty fast and there's three of them so you don't have to hang around there long.
We left our bags with them on the last day as we had an evening flight and they were fine and safe.
I wouldn't stay there again out of choice but I wouldn't be that worried if I really had to. The location is great and its cheap. Basically... it will do! What do people expect for a 1* hotel!

title: “Great Hotel-Super Convenient, Free Parking & Shuttle”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights to go to a Seahawks game and explore Seattle. We were very happy with our choice.
The FREE shuttle service was fantastic. It leaves the hotel on the hour and half hour and you call up the hotel to ask to be picked up when you're ready. We were able to take the shuttle to the stadium on game day which was incredibly convenient. It was about a 5-10 minute ride from the hotel to downtown.
Our room overlooked Lake Union and had a view of the space needle. It was comfortable and new. We didn't have any complaints about the heat, water, etc. Breakfast was standard but a nice spread for a free breakfast. The free parking was a nice plus as well. There were a few restaurants across the street overlooking the lake. We tried Joey's and enjoyed it - it was crowded on a Friday night but we didn't have to wait.
We would definitely stay here again.

title: “See you next year!”
text: Great room, exceptional staff and the updated "organic" restaurant is simply amazing! the seating areas around the hotel give opportunities for conversations without having to be in a "bar". Thank you - see you next year!

title: “My home away from home”
text: I live in Santa Monica, work in San Francisco, and have been staying at the Chancellor Hotel almost weekly for the past 12 years. Wes and his staff are always friendly, helpful and best of all - they always seem to get me a room even when the entire city is sold out! I'm reluctant to praise them too much because I don't want to be unable to get a room or to have the incredibly reasonable rates raised - but I love this place. It's simple, clean, friendly, reasonable and in a great location. Can't beat it.

title: “Good for a Holiday Inn Express”
text: I've heard Holiday Inn Expresses described as "bare bones" so I was pleasantly surprised to awaken to a decent breakfast set up in the morning. I particularly liked the ample, fluffy eggs. They were doing renovations while I was there, but this didn't result in any inconveniences. The staff was nice. My room was clean and the bathoom was fine and a decent size; my only issue was that it was a bit difficult to seal the shower curtain so that no water leaked out.

title: “Great value in downtown”
text:
I was a little worried about winning a 4-night stay here on Hotwire ($55/night) after I saw the mixed reviews, but we had a very good stay here. I'm just going to list my thoughts:
1. The room is not tiny like some in downtowns in bigger cities. We had a king-sized bed, desk, and small fridge and microwave. A side chair or love seat would have been nice, and there was enough room for one in the room.
2. The noise level is not that bad. We asked for a room away from Washington Street (busy road and demolition project going on across the street), and it was fine. We overlooked the parking lot, and the noise was not bad. We did hear a few helicopters from the heliport behind the hotel, but they weren't very distracting. The fan is good for creating white noise. We've had much noisier rooms in more expensive hotels on the northside of Indianapolis that face the freeway or the exit ramp. We didn't notice noise from other guests either.
3. The elevator is old and pretty small, but the plus is that they repainted it during our stay to spruce it up.
4. The free breakfast is fine: hardboiled eggs, waffles, bagels, toast, cereal, yogurt. I prefer scrambled eggs, but that's not a major shortfall. There's a Marsh grocery store a few blocks away, and we got some frozen breakfast sandwiches instead. Other downtown hotels tend to charge a lot of money for breakfast in their restaurant.
5. The staff is very friendly and helpful. They are a fabulous asset.
6. It was about a 10 minute walk to the Convention Center, which is very handy. 
For the price, this was a very good value.

title: “The staff here are the frosting on the cake.”
text: This was my fourth time staying here and it is always a great experience. The staff is incredibly helpful and welcoming and utterly without any of the "hipper than thou" attitude common in urban boutique hotels. The hotel is small and intimate and in a great location. The rooms make me feel like I'm living in a glamorous movie from the 40's (if you're looking for sleek and modern, this isn't it) and the breakfasts are great. What more can I say? It's a great hotel.

title: “Wonderful”
text: I had a wonderful experience. All the staff was very nice ad helpful. It is close proximity to a lot

title: “Good location”
text: Just a few steps from td garden. Very convenient to Faneuil hall and government center. Room comfortable size. Furniture looked tired. Paint job in our room was the worst ever seen. Blue splotches from paint all ever headboard. One elevator. Front desk staff indifferent. Good location for our purpose.

title: “Great Concept, reviewable execution”
text:
PLACE: A former prison? Genius!
SERVICES: "heartbreaking" room? First marketing rule: don't be overpromising...
PEOPLE: young and cool
CHERRY ON THE CAKE: the sliding scale to get into the hell!
GO THERE FOR: make an impression and play the though guy

title: “Location, location, location....”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Rex for a long weekend last year. The hotel location was a key feature, walking distance to Shops, restaurants, Museums and the Business center. The Hotel decor was very sophisticated and stylish. The room was spacious and very clean. The hotel staff was very friendly and eager to cater to any of our needs. Since our last trip to San Francisco we could not think of staying anywhere else. The Hotel Rex is San Francisco

title: “Great place for families”
text: We went April vacation week which was great - the only problem was that it was so crowded at the pool, the kids could literally not swim and it was so crowded at breakfast that it took almost a half an hour to get through the line to get food - otherwise, the staff was great and everything was wonderful. Had it been any other week, I'm sure it would not have been so crowded.

title: “Another Marriott Win in Boston”
text:
This was my first stay at the Marriott Copley Place/Back Bay; my previous trips to Boston were at the Financial District, Theatre District and Waterfront.
The bellstaff and doorman are great to work with! Charles and Tony were especially helpful during my stay, especially when I had several heavy boxes that needed shipping due to the conference I was working.
As one review mentioned, this is very much a conference hotel, so the hotel layout can get confusing. There are two sets of elevators, one for floors 1-27 and another for floors 1-5 then 27-38. The elevator chime is soft, so for someone hard of hearing like myself, I missed a few elevators at first. Once I got the hang of it, though, I was OK. 
My room was on the 17th floor and faced the Prudential center. I had a king bed and the room was very nicely sized for a hotel in the downtown area. the bedding was the newer collection and the television had been upgraded to the flat-screen. There was a small fridge in the dresser, which was nice although your items had to be cold before you put them in there. 
The bathroom was decently sized and for a 6-day trip, it was nice to be able to spread out. The water pressure was OK, especially if you enjoy the "rainshower" type of shower heads. If you're looking for a hard-driving shower, prepare to be disappointed.
The rest of the staff was very pleasant to work with and the bellman were very helpful in getting packages/items from the meeting rooms down to shipping/receiving or the UPS store. This is the first hotel I've stay at that has had a UPS store located inside (usually, it's FedEx or an independent company). While the staff was OK, it was very frustrating to learn that packages insured for over $999 were not accepted and that the packages would have to be taken down to shipping/receiving. The bellmen were very nice about it (obviously used to this little caveat), but I found it very frustrating.
Regarding the restaurants, yes they are a bit pricey and there are plenty of restaurants within walking distance. As a solo business traveler, I tend to default to the hotel restaurants because of safety concerns. Champions is decent and serves typical Marriott sports bar food; the Terrace Bar is a bit more upscale but has a smaller menu, and on Thursday and Friday nights, has live entertainment. Gourmeli's is decent as well.
BONUS: Shaw's 24-hour grocery store is located across the street, so you can bypass the expensive gift shop for sodas and munchies (as well as toiletries). 
My biggest complaint is about the internet service and Marriott's continuing insistence on charging $13/night for service. This is frustrating for a business traveler who needs the connectivity.
Overall, however, the Marriott is a good hotel. Perfectly located in the Back Bay, with access to the Prudential Center shopping plus three blocks away from Newbury Street shopping.

title: “More than adequate for a night or two”
text:
This is a good deal for staying one or 2 nights in downtown Denver, if that is where you need or want to be. It is very conveniently located near the 16th st mall, and all points of interest downtown. Public transit nearby is absolutely amazing. Iti s a mere 7 blockss ' walk to the free downtown shuttle service, and the RTD, which will get you simply to and from the airport for $11 each way. 
Colfax IS a very noisy street, and the rooms open up to the outside rather than on inside hallways ( pretty typical of Econolodge) , but the location is otherwise great. I have stayed in this area several times and never felt it was dangerous, but i do not walk around much here at night. The street noise was my only concern. But even as a very light sleeper I was able to get a full night's sleep.
Reception clerk was wonderfully helpful, earnest, and kind.

title: “Far better than expected”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for 5 nigths during the first weekend in december, check in, check out was not heartwarming but efficient, security, bellstaff and concierge were all very freindly and offered tourist tips and tricks without us asking them - nice approach.
I have worked 18 years in the hotel industry and you can take my word for it; this hotel is far better than the official rating, they might not have all the facilities and ammenities that you will find in a 4 or 5 star property and the rooms migth be a bit small, but this hotel has an unbeatable location, very clean rooms (recently refurbished), excellent housekeeping, efficient staff (not overly enthustiatic), nice toiletries from Crabtree and Evelyn and a pricetag that makes this hotel one of the best deals in Manhattan. 
So if you dont need slippers, lobster termidor in the middle of the night, a ballroom size room and hip desing fixture and furniture, but would like to get some value for money and a clean, safe hotel.......you should stay here.
The only "bad" thing I can think of is the breakfast, overprized and of very poor quality (like in many hotels) - you are better of going to Cafe Europe opposite Pen Station.

title: “Overall not bad, but rooms getting a bit shopworn”
text:
Just recently had two stays here totaling 7 days. Overall this is another one where a 2.5 rating could be given that's where I would place this. The lobby area & other items were updated, and service from the staff was great, but it appears that the management is really walking a fine line on the room upkeep.
The housekeeping did a great job of cleaning the items they do, but being here for a while you notice things like the desk chair on my first visit the arm fell off and the replacements all had bent backs, staining on the privaciy shades, the walls looking a little dingy, and the carpet really is getting to the point it needs to be deep cleaned or replaced.It looks like when they did the lobby overhaul they only did a very light redo on the rooms to meet the minimum required for the franchise.
The hotel has great choices for food around it & is super easy to access, so not a bad place if you need a quick stay on the south side of Indy, but don't expect to be dazzled by the room.
Tip: If you are staying for more than 1-2 days, you can get a week pass for $20.00 to the brand new LA Fitness down the street. About the nicest gym in the area and gives you a lot more options than the std. Courtyard gym. And Scotty's Brewhouse and Mucky Ducks are good dinner options.

title: “Great location, trains in the hotel ate a nice touch”
text: The hotel is right by the conference center and Lucas stadium. It is a bit dated and I had mixed results with the staff on customer service. I would stay here again for the location and hope that some items improve, but it is still OK for a few nights.

title: “Good hotel for a short stay”
text:
I was in SF for a couple of days starting on 11/12 and stayed here. The location is fantastic; It's on Sutter, 1/2 a block from Mason St, so it's very close to the cable car and Union Square; the heart of the city. The price, for SF, was fantastic, just $88 with a AAA discount plus tax of course and parking is $24 per day which is moderate by SF standards. They do need a 20 minute notice before your car will arrive so you need to factor that in when you need your car. The room was very tiny but if all you're doing is sleeping, it's fine,as the bed is quite comfortable. The continental breakfast is muffins, doughnuts and croissants and that's it. If you want more, you should go out and believe me, there is no shortage of places to eat in the city.
 The reason I say this is good for a short stay is because of the tiny bedrooms, the lack of a decent breakfast and the lack of amenities at the hotel.
 Oh, one last note; Saturday night when we got back, the block was jammed with people spilling out of the nightclubs and the noise level was incredible, but our room, on the back side was very quiet, so a backside room is the way to go.

title: “Welcoming boutique hotel”
text: Upon arrival and departure, the front door was opened for us. At check in we were offered a glass of champagne or water in a wine glass. Very nice. The lobby is refreshing and there is plenty of comfortable seating. Our room was spacious for a boutique hotel and the bathroom was plenty large enough. The bedroom had a desk/counter, bench seating and another comfortable chair. The air-conditioner was functioning well. There is a separate room in the lobby area where you can help yourself to coffee, espresso or teas. A very nice touch. Truly...if you spend too much time in your room in NYC, you are not enjoying the city life. The price was right (approx. $154/night) and it is centrally located to many sights in the city and only a few blocks from Central Park. I would return to The Shoreham and highly recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to NYC. My only complaint would be that the elevator button wasn't working well and would often pass our floor.

title: “Incomparable!”
text:
What a fabulous hotel! From its location directly on the Magnificant Mile and surrounded by the finest shopping, to the curtious staff and excellent restaurants and bars, this hotel is one of the best in Chicago. Our room was very clean and fresh, the public areas comfortable and the staff at the concierge and front desk very extremely helpful. 
This is the only place to stay to be in the cnetre of the action in Chicago. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

title: “Nice Hotel - Not worth the money!”
text:
Good location, just behind St Patrick's, 5th Avenue.
Nice room, though no coffee or tea making facilities. Previously stayed in the Affinia Dumont which was comfortable and had a small kitchen where you could make tea, breakfast etc and didn't cost as much as the New York Palace. Won't be returning to the New York Palace. Too expensive

title: “Haven't slept this great in years :-)”
text:
This is a lovely boutique hotel. Located just a couple of streets away from Times Sq. The metro and port authority bus terminal are around the corner. So is Dean & Deluca and a Starbucks and lot's of restaurants :-)
The lobby is small but nicely decorated with 4 iMacs available if you want to go on the internet. Behind the desk are very friendly and helpful staff.
I stayed in a king bedroom. And it was just great. It's all so new and fresh and clean. 
The bed was so comfortable. I haven't slept this great in years. And that's what you need when walking down the streets of NYC the whole day. You need a good nights rest to reload yourself for the next day. I also liked the turn down service with the chocolates on the bed and the card that says what the temperature will be the next day. An extra plus is the free wifi access so I could go on the internet on my iphone in the room.
I wish I had this room as my bedroom at home!
This was a good value for your money deal. Hope they keep the prices low. I'll definitely return if they do.

title: “Excellent, Spectacular, Amazing!!”
text: Our recent stay at The Drake exceeded our expectations and then some! The hotel is absolutely gorgeous! Every employee is super friendly and always available. Check in went smoothly- we added on the Romance Package to our stay for my husbands birthday celebration and WOW! It was worth every penny! Our room was upgraded for no charge to an Executive Suite with Lakefront views, champagne was delivered to our room, late check-out and a DELICIOUS breakfast at Drake Bros- all included in the package! They even brought a special dessert to my husband on a plate decorated with balloons and Happy Birthday written on it in chocolate while we were enjoying the amazing breakfast buffet! The lounges in the hotel are so comfortable and inviting, the concierge is very knowledgeable and I have to admit, Im a big fan of the sofa in the elevator! :) My only disappointment was in the pillows- woke up with a stiff neck. A little too hard for my liking. We will be going back to this hotel for sure in the near future. We felt like royalty! A++++++++!!!!

title: “Nice property but unfortunate incident at check-out”
text:
Nice property and was glad to see an alternative in SPG's Manhatten portfolio in the upscale segment. 
Close to Times Square - not the most prestigious location, but perfect if you are looking to see musicals or go to the theater; also close enough to other Midtown attractions or office buildings. Entrance is very understated (almost walked by once), lobby has a cool art deco feel. Nice rooms with good amenities and taste. Bathrooms are huge and feature the best rainfall shower I have seen in a hotel. Was given a room with a "terrace", which was quite useless as it was on the second floor of a courtyard and very noisy from various a/c outlets.
Staff is nice but no special efforts (e.g., remembering name, etc.). 
Most disturbing thing happened at check out; I asked for a cab and when I left the hotel, my luggage was loaded into a black town car. Naively, I thought that they were offering me free transport to the airport as a SPG Platinum. Once we got on our way, I asked the driver and he told me that the ride will be $60. That is not much more than a regular cab ($45) and it was a nice car. I do however find it very disappointing that the bell boy would just make that decision for me - particularly as the limo driver had to pay him off to get the ride. I know that these things go on "behind the scenes", but for a hotel of this league, this is - frankly - inexcusable.

title: “Great stay at the Best Western”
text: We just recently spent 4 nights at the Best Western Fiesta Inn on 10 West in San Antonio, Tx. It was a pleasure to pick a hotel which ended up with complete satisfaction. Even the lobby was presented very nicely as was the beautiful courtyard of which all the rooms faced. Our room was a handicapped accessable room and was very ample. We slept very soundly as we heard no noise from adjoining rooms. The parking lot gates were closed in the late evenings. Each day our room was done up to satifaction and the staff was very helpful and friendly. We only wish the breakfast bar had decaff coffee, skim milk and low-carb food choices.

title: “Our new favorite!”
text: My 12 year old daughter and go to Chicago and have a hotel we normally stay at, but now Sofitel is our new favorite. Great location, fabulous food and staff, we will be back for sure! The rooms were very nice and well appointed.

title: “Nice Place - Reasonably Priced in Hollywood”
text: This location is on Sunset Blvd, a block or so from Hollywood Blvd (near the main Hollywood attractions). Priced reasonably for this area. The hotel was clean and comfortable. Seemed to have some trouble with the keycard not working (this happened twice - stayed there 3 days). The indoor garage is $8.00 per day which you would need as parking on the street is very difficult as most areas are permitted or metered. The continental breakfast was just OK, no waffle maker, no yogurt (although they had bananas and apples), no eggs of any sort, had oatmeal and bagels and danish and cereal and juice. I like Starbucks coffee and even though there was a Starbucks on the corner I didnt go there as the coffee was fine. Breakfast bar opened at 6:30 AM promptly. As I said my rates were very reasonable (used the Entertainment Book discount) and accordingly my room was small but sufficient for only myself. Had to unglog the refrigerator as it was quite noisy - also a microwave in room. I liked the fact that there was a safe in the room free of charge. The internet was a little slow but free. There was no suitcase rack in the room when I arrived but one was delivered promptly. I would recommend a room on the upper level rather than on the main level. My room led out to a courtyard in the back of the hotel with a gate perhaps four feet high leading to the courtyard (no access to the courtyard). The courtyard was protected with barbed wire but I didn't feel comfortable leaving the sliding door open during the night which was the only source of outdoor ventilation. The bathroom area was small but nice and shower was newly tiled. The desk personnel were friendly and helpful and allowed for a late check out on departure day. Didnt use the outdoor pool (was there in the second week of December, 2011) but ate a midnight snack from In/Out Burger (which is next door (had to try it as there are none of those on the east coast) - 24 hr IHOP is across the street as well as a 7/11 - saw an altercation while taking a walk with a security guard from 7/11 and someone who must have tried to help himself without paying for his items) in the pool area. The outdoor pool area was well kept and attractive. About 3 blocks east is on Sunset Blvd is a guitar center that has a walk of fame in front of the building with many famous bands and singers - worth the walk. I dont think they had a fitness center but there is a nice L A Fitness about a 7 minute walk on Hollywood Blvd. All in all - a good place and a a good value.

title: “Lovely, convenient, friendly”
text: A lovely, clean, quiet place, with a staff whose goal seems to be to make you as comfortable as possible. As you reach their desk, the question is already forming, "What can I do for you?" And they mean it. They will move your car (to and from the parking garage they recommend), bring you tea (they have several types/flavors they are happy to share), order you a newspaper, or ferry bags to and from your room. They will snag hard-to-get-tickets and re-program your GPS. All done in a professional yet friendly and never obsequious manner. The rooms are exceptionally clean, the rain-forest walk-in shower is a dream you want not to end, and the little breakfast room is pleasant and convenient (and the food's pretty good without being exceptional). A place you want to come home to at the end of a day of sightseeing. A place you don't want to leave. Parlor for wine and/or sitting with friends, even a small garden deck.

title: “Can't do much better in NYC”
text:
My family and I just completed a stay at the Andaz 5th Avenue. Based on the quality of the rooms, the amenities that are Andaz-unique, and location, I'd highly recommend this to anyone looking for a great NYC experience.
Rooms
One of our rooms was an Andaz Suite, and the other was an XL View room. Both had nice, tall ceilings. Even without that, however, the rooms were amazingly spacious by NYC standards. The quality of construction and materials really stood out. The suite gave us what was most needed - comfort and space - but it also had some things that were pretty impressive (albeit unnecessary for our particular needs), including a full size refrigerator with freezer and dishwasher (Fisher & Paykel at that).
The XL View was quite nice as well, and came with a big lounge chair that allowed us to look out towards Fifth Avenue/NYPL. This room was on the 7th floor, so I do wonder if the view of the library would've been more impressive on the 3rd floor, which was an option offered to us at check-in.
Amenities
I probably won't mention anything new to folks who are familiar with the Andaz, but it's great to be in a hotel with complimentary Internet, as well as free drinks and snacks from the minibar (excluding alcohol). That alone is worth $20-$40/night if you're comparing it to other NYC hotels.
Location
You're within walking distance to Grand Central and the Bryant Park MTA station, which covers the 4,5,6,7,S,B,D,F and some other train line that I don't recall right now. It's also pretty easy to catch a cab in the area. If you want a snack, there are a fair amount of delis that are nearby. Very, very convenient.
Overall, I'd highly recommend this hotel, and look forward to staying here again.

title: “Abs gross”
text: Well, it was a place where u hesitate to touch anythng. Including the bathroom.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Excellant location, across the street from Shaw's seafood restaurant and very close to Nordstroms. Nice breakfast place and bar for after dinner drinks. The rooms were roomy and comfortable. Also went on a great tour, architecture boat tour.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text:
Although I stay at hotels in Chicago frequently, this was my first stay at the Sheraton. It is really a lovely property and the rooms are beautifully appointed. I was not there long enough to take advantage of any of the hotel's amenities, but the room, linens, lobby and elevators were first rate.
In recommending this hotel to friends, there are a couple of items I would mention. First is the location. The hotel is a bit isolated. I happen to love walking in the city so it is not a big deal for me to walk 3-4 blocks to Michigan Avenue or 6-7 blocks to the Red Line. But if the weather is bad I think you would pretty much need to take a taxi anywhere you wanted to go. The other issue is parking and the GPS location of the hotel. My GPS took me to an area under the back side of the hotel. Since there were parking garages nearby I called the hotel to confirm that was where I should park. The Sheraton representative directed me away from that area and eventually several blocks from the hotel before she decided she was unable to help me. Since she was not able to connect me to the concierge I called the hotel again and connected to the concierge who placed me on hold for several minutes while I pulled over to the side of the road in heavy downtown traffic. When he came back on the phone he directed me to turn north away from the hotel. When he realized he made a mistake I was unable to turn around for several blocks, but eventually found my way to the hotel. When I asked the doormen where to park, they directed me back to where my GPS had originally sent me - to the parking garage under the hotel. All of this took the better part of an hour by the time I finally parked - and then you have about a 15 minute journey from the garage through numerous hallways until you find the lobby (signage is minimal so use your instincts as to what escalators to use, etc). When finally at the registration desk, the wait was far longer than it should have been since there were only two clerks on duty and a lone of people had formed. It probably seemed longer than it really was since I was now tired, sweaty, had frayed nerves and was late for an appointment. But when I finally did get to register the clerk was extremely nice, and from then on out the experience was lovely.
I would absolutely stay here again as long as it was during nice weather when it would be pleasant to walk outdoors.

title: “Insect”
text: I stayed there for 5 days and developed a rash. The doctor said is due to mites.

title: “Overall a good hotel, and a good place to stay.”
text:
My wife and I were in town to go to the US OPEN in pebble beach. After reading reviews of the hotel I decided to stay here. I am glad I did. The hotel is very nice and clean. It doesnt have a pool, but we were with out kids so didnt matter to us. They do have a 24 hour sauna, which we didnt use either. I was a little nervous after getting to our room and seeing that we were on the "LOUD" side of the hotelas described by others. We were on the 8th floor and barely heard the train going by and every once in awhile we heard the planes fyling overhead, but nothing that kept us up or woke us up. 
We got a room that included free parking and breakfast. While the free parking was great, the free breakfast was at best average. It looks really nice when you walk in and see alll the food there, but it was disappointing. 
I would stay here again without hesitation. It was a great location and with in walking distance of the downtown scene.

title: “Not sure how this is a LUXURY hotel”
text: The location is great, but I was surprised this is a luxury hotel. The rooms are very small, the sheets and towels are not high quality, and the room service took 2 min just to answer the phone. I would rather stay at the Lennox suites and pay half the price for twice the room.

title: “Yet another Kimpton knocks it out of the park!”
text:
A few days before our check-in, we got an email from Ali at the Alexis, asking us if there was anything she could do in advance of our arrival. I figured it was a form letter, but I replied anyway, letting her know I had a package coming and asking if the amazing blue cheese fries were still available at the Library Bar.
To my surprise, Ali emailed me back, letting me know that the fries were still available (and delicious) and that she'd keep an eye out for my package.
Then I asked if I could give the Kimpton code word (if you don't know about the code word, look for it on their Facebook and Twitter - it leads to many nice surprises), and she said I could and arranged for an upgrade!
OMG, our room was fabulous! It was a big suite with an amazingly comfortable couch, a great bedroom and even a dining room table. And on that table was resting a bottle of wine, some absolutely delicious truffles and a card from Ali with a coupon for free blue cheese fries! YUM!!!!
The room had a peek view of the bay (I took some photos of the Bainbridge ferry coming in) as well as a nice view of the city. It's in an old building that's been renovated, so the layout has some quirks, but that's part of its charm. The decor had a modern opulence to it; it was the sort of decor I could see myself actually living with.
Someone elsewhere said that they don't have free WiFi. That is not entirely correct. So long as you're a member of their frequent stayer program, Kimpton InTouch (which is free), you get free WiFi. We had it and it was both strong and fast.
The location of the Alexis is very central and convenient; it's a short walk to both the ferry terminal and the University Metro/Sound Transit bus station. One warning: on weekends every Starbucks, Peet's and other coffee shop within a six block radius is closed, except for the Cherry Bean. Fortunately, the Alexis offers free coffee in the lobby, so all is not lost!
The front desk staff is super-knowledgeable about everything both locally and further out. We wound up chatting in the lobby with someone who was looking for wine tasting. We'd just come back from Woodinville, so we had a lot to rave about with regards to wine - but it turns out the gentleman at the front desk knew TONS about the Woodinville wine scene and had lots of insights!
The only thing I will note - and I wish now that I had said something while I was there, because I know they would have fixed it - is that the bed in our room was unusually, startlingly firm. I've stayed at other rooms in the Alexis and never had that problem, so I imagine it is a quirk of that particular room. (Probably because some previous occupant felt the bed was not firm enough and the Alexis fixed it for them!)
We'll be back in July - and we'll be back at the Alexis again!

title: “We had a nice stay at this hotel”
text:
We only had a short time to stay in San Diego, so I didn't want to waste time traveling back and forth to the beach. I found this and a couple of other hotels in San Diego that were ON THE BEACH and picked this one at the request of my husband, who felt more comfortable going with an established "brand name." (Best Western)
The area, Pacific Beach, is very crowded both with residents and travelers. However, upon our request we were placed in a room that was VERY quiet and faced an apartment house next door rather than the beach or the pool. This was important to us as we have a toddler who goes to bed early and is a light sleeper. I know we had people staying in the rooms on either side of us and above us, but I never heard them. The only time we had a problem with noise was when the noisy frat boys staying under us decided to have a drink on their patio at 2:30 in the morning (more on that later). They didn't stay outside long (I think someone had complained about the noise, and they went inside) and we didn't have another problem with it on other nights. We did have a small balcony, which was nice, as well as a table with two chairs and a bar with two barstools where our toddler could eat his meals.
The room we got was nice, very clean, the bathroom looked like it had been recently refurbished. The bedspread, couch and some other furnishings were a bit worn but nothing we couldn't live with. The room had a queen bed and a pullout queen sofa. With the sofa folded up, the room was spacious; with the bed out, not so much, so we only left the bed out at nighttime. Overall it was a pretty average room but we don't have champagne tastes :) There was good closet space but the bathroom does not have a bathtub, perhaps for water-conservation reasons. We had to have our 2-year-old take showers with us instead of the baths he is used to, which was a new experience for him, but not a problem; actually after the first time he enjoyed the shower a lot.
The hotel's common areas are a little worse for the wear and it's apparent the hotel has been there for some time, but otherwise are OK. We saw hotel workers painting, cleaning, etc. the whole time we were there, so I think they are trying to keep up with it, but with a large volume of people through the building, plus the sea air to contend with, it's probably an uphill battle. Everything was clean and the hotel does have some nice amenities, including a microwave and refrigerator in the room we got along with a washer and dryer on the floor beneath us to wash seawater-soaked towels and clothes. There is on-site parking you pay extra for, which I was glad to have after I saw how congested the general area is and watched people circle to find parking places. Despite high foot traffic in the area the parking lot for the hotel is secure and we didn't have any problems with our car when we were there. There is a Ralph's grocery store about 2 blocks from the hotel, so we were able to buy groceries and keep them in the in-room refrigerator, which was great for us and would be a real advantage to this hotel over others, as it's always helpful (I think) to be able to keep some food in the room. The pool was nice but be aware I think they use purified saltwater for it; the water was very salty for pool water, but the pool was clean and the area was well-policed for garbage, etc. The best part of all was the beach access: walk past the pool to a door in the glass wall facing the ocean, and you are on the boardwalk with the beach just steps away. We could hear the ocean from our side-facing room (although we couldn't see it unless we looked around the corner of the building, but that was fine with us :) and that, to me, was the best part of the hotel.
The one advisory I have for families is that this area is apparently Party Central for high school and college kids looking to hang out on the beach. The boardwalk in front of the hotel has constant activity and is quite loud (shouting, laughing, boomboxes and stereos going, etc.). I would not have wanted to stay in the front of the building facing the beach, or facing the pool; it would have just been way too noisy. The boardwalk was a very interesting place to take walks but I don't know if I would have wanted to put up with it for longer than the three days we were there. If you are looking for peace and quiet, this is probably NOT the hotel to stay in in San Diego. For us, having a small child, it could have been a disadvantage. If you have teenagers, however, I would think this would be a great place to stay as they would have plenty of opportunities to meet other teenagers. The area is well-patrolled by police, lifeguards, and private security from the hotels, so there wouldn't be much fear of anything bad happening.
All in all, though, I found the hotel to be very pleasant and was satisfied with what we got for the amount of money we paid. We have stayed at places with far fewer amenities that cost more money in other cities we have visited. I am not sure we would stay here again if we were going to be in town longer next time, but I would recommend this to other travelers who don't mind (or are actively seeking) a lot of activity where they stay.

title: “Darkest Hotel I've stayed in”
text:
I have read the reviews listed below on tripadvisor, and I think they do a great job reviewing this hotel. I just wanted to add a quick note to anyone who might be bothered by the two problems we had with the Hard Rock, hope this helps you when picking a place to stay in chicago.
I usually get a little depressed if I'm surrounded in darkness. This is just a problem for me, so it might not have the same effect on other guests. The lobby is almost completely black, the hallways and doors are dark grey, and the rooms were the most uncomfortable grey I ever seen. It didn't help that the four days we were in Chicago were cold, dark, and raining. 
The other problem we had was when we ordered a roll-a-way. The fee was $25.00. It is a airbed that inflates. Once inflated, however, it did not fit anywhere in the room. We tried everything we could think of, but it would have to be folded over in order to fit. Didn't seem safe at all to me, I'm sure that it can't meet safety codes. Our son slept in our bed. When I asked the staff that I didn't want to be charged $25.00 because the bed could not fit in the room, they looked at me like I was crazy. Surely this must be a problem everytime someone orders the 'airbed'.
Or, maybe the dark hotel was having an effect on me. 
I'm usually fairly easy going, but I think there might be better hotels for your stay in Chicago.

title: “Boston Bliss”
text: Spent 3 days in Boston with friends for our 20th wedding anniversary. So happy we selected the Lenox Hotel based on Trip Advisor reviews. Exceeded our expectations. Staff was exceptional. They were all bright, friendly and helpful. Special thanks to Keith, Tom, John, Vincent and Nina for all their recommendations and help. Hotel is lovely - beautiful old hotel - well maintained. Location was good.. easy to get around Boston (booked Trolley tour - 2 days easy to use, entertaining). Can't wait to return.

title: “LOVED the NYMA”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the NYMA in October for our first trip to New York. After doing much research on hotels we were very pleased upon arrival. We had a Business King on the 18th floor. The room was very spacious with a view of the Empire State building. It was super clean and very quiet. The only minor complaint was that the elevators were a little slow. Breakfast was average and crowded. We ate there once.But you are in New York....go out for breakfast!
This hotel was on Korean Way with about a 10 min walk to Times Square. We would not hesitate to book this hotel again......a great find in New York City for the price.

title: “Not your standard Hilton Garden”
text: Rooms are dated and common areas a bit beaten up but both are very clean. Parking is off sight but a very short walk, shorter than one would walk at a large hotel or shopping mall. Service is friendly. The pool area is nice. As a guest you get access to City Gym in lieu of a workout room. This is connected to the hotel through an interior hallway. Gym has saunas, steam rooms, showers, whirlpool, classes, basketball courts, the whole bit. Bring your swim suit is you want to use all gym facilities. I was upgraded to a 2 room suite with my Hilton Honors status. My room was a great value at only $89.

title: “If you could sleep in the lobby, it would be fine.”
text: Rooms on the north side of the hotel get the music from the club on Main Street well into the early morning. Until I informed the desk, because I noticed barricades going up on the street, staff had no clue tabout the mardi gras parade one block away. They were therefore useless to assist in planning for parking and getting around by foot which affected our own activities. Rate was hardly a bargain and not so much as a paper under the door or a cup of coffee in the lobby. Forget valet for your car: call was answered only once in 5 separate tries so go down and wait. 49 cents/minute for internet time in the business center! Visit the lobby and stay somewhere else.

title: “Affordable Memphis Gem!”
text:
I stayed at the Comfort Inn Downtown June 9-12th while in town on business. I booked my room at the hotel website and received exactly what I asked for (higher floor, king room, river view). A bountiful breakfast buffet (including waffles, biscuits and gravy, 3 types of cereal, yogurt, toast, bagels, fresh fruit, coffee, tea, juices) is included in the room rate. Breakfast is served from 6-9 on weekdays, 7-10 on weekends. The hotel also puts cookies out in the afternoon. Parking in the secure basement of the hotel is $5.00 per night. The only thing to be aware of is that, if you use the in-room safe you will be charged $1.09 per day...I did not see any signs and was not informed of this at check-in. It's honestly the only "negative" I have about my stay.
I can honestly say that the employees at this hotel are the friendliest I've encountered. They are absolutely professional, but also know their guests and are very engaging. Rooms are nicely decorated with pictures of local scenes and kept very nice. There is a microwave and small fridge in the room, and a computer in the lobby for your use. There is also wi-fi in the room.
As others have mentioned, Beale Street is a short 10-minute walk or a quick $1.00 tram ride. As a solo female traveler, I walked during the day/afternoon, but felt more comfortable taking the tram late at night. Panhandlers are out all the time, but are not aggressive.
For those interested in nightlife, every Wednesday in summer is bike night on Beale. The area comes alive with bikes, bikers and those out to observe both. A great bar is Silky O'Sullivan's, which has dueling pianos and a drink called the Diver (definitely something you don't want to drink alone!). The Peabody is a definite must-see ("Duck Walk" is at 11:00 and 5:00 daily). Also, a little place called the Creperie is located next to Peabody Place Mall...awesome breakfast, entree and dessert crepes made in front of you.
I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Hotel is an absolute rip-off”
text:
I booked from Australia for the New Years Eve package. When I requested confirmation thru the hotel, I was told not to worry it was on the system.
When I arrived at the hotel on New Year's eve, I was told that I had not been booked under the New Years Eve Package and that if I wanted to be considered for the viewing deck, i would have to pay an additional $800.00 for a family of 4. 
The hotel management were inefficient and uninformed. My booking had not recorded the New Years Eve package. I was forced to pay an additional $500 until the hotel could find my email and record of my many phone calls confirming the package.
The worst part of this exclusive package was that all I paid for was a chance to stand outside the hotel for half and hour from 11.30-12.00 to see the ball drop. 
There was in fact no real viewing deck as one would expect, rather a poor street view from the front of the hotel.
Apart from this, the room service I ordered served raw baked potatoes. The room was very small and had a stale smell. The carpets were stained and bedding not up to standard.
I will never recommend this hotel under any circumstances.

title: “7th trip to New York: It was fine”
text:
My mother, who is 73, and I go to New York to see shows and walk Central Park. Traditionally, we have stayed at hotels closer to Times Square i.e., Omni Berkshire and Warwick Hotel. 
If this were my first visit to New York, and I wanted to enjoy the night life, lights, and action......I would choose hotels closer to the theater district. I would select for economical reasons, perhaps, Milford Plaza or Hotel Edison. Friends of mine have stayed there and enjoyed themselves.
HOTEL BELLECLAIRE: The hotel is small and currently being renovated on some floors. My senior mother and I could have cared less about the elevators. We were on the third floor and used the stairwell. 
In my opinion, this is not a place for children or teens. The hotel rooms are small, the televisions barely work, but that being said, it was fine for us. Honestly, I think it depends on what you are looking for. We did reject one of the bigger rooms on the 7th floor because the carpet was badly stained. The front desk is friendly and accomodating and changed our room immediately. 
My mother's room and mine were both clean (315 and 318). The view was nonexistent and the air conditioners rather loud. The bathrooms were spotless; no problem with hot water and I think the tile was new. The bed was comfortable and I smelled no unpleasant odors. I have a nose for mold, mildew, and other unpleasantries.....every thing was fine. I also have trouble sleeping at night, but found no problem here. It is an older place, however, the paint is fresh, a brownish-yellow, and the carpet looks somewhat newish. The halls are narrow, if you are on the big side, hmm.....find a bigger place. I noticed that there were a lot of airline staff who stayed here as well. 
The location, for me, was excellent. I wanted to stay in a residental area, to see more of the REAL New York, and so I did. The subway is two blocks away and you can get to Times Square in five minutes if you have two dollars. Not a bad deal! The area is safe, too. Just around the corner is a grocery store, with a huge selection of cheeses, chocolates, deli items, and imported beers. There is a great "trendy" breakfast place on Amsterdam called Sara Beth's. It is a local favorite and if you want a good Jewish breakfast, somewhere on Broadway (that's your street) and hmmm......86 or 87, you can find incredibly fresh lox, herring, etc. If you ask, once you get to that area, people would know the name. You can walk to Times Square from the hotel. It takes about 30/45 minutes.

title: “impeccable”
text: everything was great, food, room, service, concierge. i would definately recommend it.

title: “Great bed”
text: This hotel advertises their bed as a selling point. It was very comfortable. The hotel itself was average in it's service & ammenities. It's a great location to stay if you just want to walk out of your room & be near the tourist attractions and great seafood restuarants. I would stay there again if they offered a special price. We paid $89.00 and it was worth that, but not much more.

title: “Close to tourist areas and transportation”
text:
Pros: A block from Fisherman's wharf and Pier 39 tourist areas. Clean rooms were very well decorated with flat screen TVs and Sleep Number beds. Nice outdoor patio with large sitting area around a firepit. Staff were very helpful. Located on the "F" streetcar route. Lots of restaurants close, including an IHOP next door & Denny's about 3 blocks down on Beach Street.
Cons: Small rooms could use better lighting. No fridge or microwave in room. Hotel is not very soundproof from outside noise and we were woke up every night from traffic. No restaurant in hotel.

title: “In dowtown close to jeorgetown”
text: In a strategic position, comfortable hotel. Perhaps it's a time to change furniture inside. Including in the rooms.

title: “Dingy”
text:
This hotel needs a good cleaning, or at least the 10th floor does. My first room had black stains all over the carpet, which I was willing to overlook until I got in the shower and a yellow substance filled the tub. I couldn't get the substance out of the tub because the drain didn't work. Gross.
So, I called the front desk and had them move me. They put me in another room on the 10th floor which also had black stains all over the carpet. The shower in this room is not super clean either. There is black mold between a few of the tiles.
Everything in this hotel is also super expensive. The restaurant, which has excellent service, is pricey and the pedicures in the spa are $50+. I will say that the service in the restaurant makes the price worth it. The food and wine is excellent, and I had a delicious pecan crusted salmon with fresh veggies.
The decor in the hotel is a mixture of beige, white and brown, and it's a bit sparse. The rooms have a lonely, empty feeling because there just isn't much on the walls. The dirty carpet just makes them seem neglected. In a $200.00 a night hotel I expect more cleanliness and hospitality.

title: “Nice hotel, good size to rooms, needs a few updates”
text:
I recently started working a big project with CSX (4 blocks up the river from this hotel) and the hotel offers an outstanding contractor rate.
Rooms are big. Even the standard 2-queen "deluxe" room is very large with a huge bathroom and plenty of open floor space.
No complaints about cleanliness at all. Rooms here are very clean.
Minor complaint is this - the 27" tube TV set is circa 1985. Lousy picture and limited channel selection. Not sure why it is taking hotel chains so long to get with the 2000's and get flat screen TV's with digital pictures. But this needs to be addressed at a major bustling hotel. It's not like this it the Motel 6 or something. It's a nice big downtown hotel. 
Also some of the furnishings are old looking. Out of date lamps, chairs, etc..
Bed was very firm and comfortable. No complaints there.
Plenty of eating options both in and around the hotel. The location of this place can't be much better. Right on the waterfront and walking distance to everything.
Will be lodging here again several times over the next few months. Looking forward to it.

title: “Helpful and friendly staff - great location too.”
text: Stayed for three nights - very nice room. The staff was helpful with any request or questions we had. Location was great, plus they have a complimentary shuttle to a lot of the downtown area. I would definitely stay here on my next visit to Denver.

title: “Great place to stay near the airport”
text: My wife and I got in late (2 am) and they were very friendly and welcoming. Very clean place. I tend to judge hotels on their breakfast. If they have a good breakfast selection, they are alright in my book. This place had an excellent breakfast selection. I would stay here again just for that.

title: “Good location, very friendly staff”
text:
Location very convenient to Airport and destination.. Convenient shuttle from Airport with a good schedule.
Staff all very friendly and accommodating
Breakfast room large with very friendly staff made a great start to each day. Good buffet selection and made to order eggs. Fresh juices and good coffee.
On a previous trip, there was a constant hum of equipment from outside the room but not an issue on this trip.
Shopping across the road and adjacent and many restaurants close by.

title: “Very pleased with this hotel”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at the Affinia Gardens over the July 4 weekend. We both enjoyed our stay and definitely recommend this hotel as clean and very comfortable. The staff is great, and the morning of our check out, I noticed that both Nigel and Pedro were wonderfully supportive of a family who's kids were being a tad noisy in the lobby. The parents, who were anxiously trying to quiet their children, were told not to worry, that the staff understood that the kids were understandably excited. The hotel not only is family friendly, but somehow it is very quiet and conducive to a restful (and romantic) stay.
The bed was great, and the 6 pillow option, at no extra charge, a boon to those, who like me, often carry our own pillow to avoid the overly hard, or bulky pillows provided by hotels. We had a comfortable couch, as well, which we appreciated. There was even a kitchen, with apartment size stove, full refrigerator, dishwasher and microwave, a pot and pan, and dishes. The day we left, they held our bags for us after check-out, without charge, until the evening.
We felt fortunate to stumble across this hotel, conveniently located to Central Park and other amenities, in a lovely neighborhood. It also happens to be located near Barbaresco Restaurant, a wonderful, quiet Italian place, which we highly recommend. Food is fresh, specials interesting and varied, the staff friendly, knowledgeable and engaged in their craft. 
We both highly recommend the Affinity Gardens and feel that, especially for the price, it is great discovery. A real pleasure to stay at!

title: “Great Staff ... "needs some investment"”
text:
Every, and I do mean EVERY staff person we came in contact with over four days was amazing. Hilton and the hiring and training departments should be proud. 
 This hotel was built in 1936 and was bought by the US during WW II and then bought and redone by Conrad Hilton. It was the largest hotel in the US, 3000 rooms, a hospital, 18-hole golf course on the roof ... what a great history. President Obama was there during election night 2008 ... Grant Park, where he held his wonderful speech is just across the street. The property is full of history.
On to our stay. Our room had amazing views of Lake Michigan ... which meant a morning sun. Hum. I'm certain it would be wonderful during the winter ... but we were there during the summer. The bathroom window was huge, no blinds ... I needed my sunglasses in the morning... and it was hot, really HOT. I am not making this up. Be careful ... one of the switches (unmarked) turns on the baseboard heat, which you do Not Need in the summer! This is the voice of experience.
The air conditioning is TERRIBLE. It never got below 70, even when set to 65 (the lowest setting). It was very, very warm. I realize they are working with old systems. But I'll bet someone, somewhere could make the adjustments necessary to make the old systems work. 
We are Diamond Hilton members, so I'll mention the Executive area. Well, we have been spoiled, I guess. This was at the bottom of all the Executive lounges. The area looks as though it's been carved from a hall, in a neglected space. The "view" of Lake Michigan is limited. The breakfast was fine, and limited. 
The evening offerings were sad. In other Hiltons (in Paris, Athens, London, Lyon, and others around the world) there are offerings of wine, wonderful food and comfortable seating in the evening. The Hilton Chicago offered small tables, really horrid evening food and pay-by-the-glass ordinary drinks. We were very disappointed. I expected more from Hilton Chicago.
We were really looking forward to our stay in this classic property, we would have to think about staying again.

title: “Complete Crap”
text: I would NEVER recommend this hotel. There isn't any service, you check yourself in and out through a kiosk. That probably wouldn't haven't bothered me if I didn't have a streetside room and could hear EVERYTHING on the street, including the moving trucks in the middle of the night. I woke-up at 3 a.m. to what sounded like construction on the streets. The windows are old school and provide zero insulation. Room was fantastically small, which I can also live with, but when I asked to be moved b/c of the noise, they couldn't/wouldn't accomodate. Oh, and they say there's a "fitness center," but that's a joke/lie. There's a couple of machines shoved in a room, one of which didn't work. How it gets a 3 star rating is beyond me.

title: “Fave new hotel in Chicago!”
text: I love boutique hotels so I was excited to try out a stay at the Ivy. From the moment my husband and I walked in, we felt like we were in a mini cosmopolitan hotel (Vegas) - the decor is just so beautiful and clean. You can tell this place is all about customer service, everyone was so nice and helpful, felt like I was at a 5 star hotel. Excellent staff, down to the bellman and the maids! Even though we had to wait until 3 for our room, it was perfectly fine because this hotel has the best freakin location ever. Steps away from everything Chicago. We booked a studio room and it was just so cute and comfy and best of all- clean!! Amazing shower and loved the lighting throughout the room. Also loved coming back in the evening to some cookies and brownies, very nice touch. I am so excited to come back and stay here. I felt like the whole stay was worth the price, which was very reasonable considering the location. We also had a chance to chill out on their roof terrace while the sun was still out and again received amazing service amongst a serene comfy atmosphere... All in all,I think I've finally found my favorite boutique hotel in Chicago and I highly recommend this hotel to anyone who is reading this! Can't wait to book my next trip :)

title: “Wonderful Getaway”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Bay Club Hotel and Marina on July 27, 2011 to celebrate our wedding anniversary. The front desk service was friendly and efficient. Very unexpectedly, we were upgraded to a junior suite on the second floor. The room had two balconies and overlooked the marina. The accommodations were spotless and very inviting, with a comfortable king bed and a sitting area with a comfy couch, two chairs, and a coffee table. The room itself was very quiet, but guests should be aware that Humphreys next door features outdoor concerts on summer evenings and the music and applause are very audible from the Bay Club. The hot buffet breakfast in the morning included potatoes, sausage, bacon, and scrambled eggs plus toast, fresh fruit, and cereal. The food was only lukewarm, but tasty nonetheless. My husband and I did not appreciate that the tv in the breakfast room was turned to FOX "News." That we could have done without. However, all in all, our stay was very enjoyable and we would not hesitate to return.

title: “Very nice hotel in great location”
text:
The Crowne Plaza is very nice, with great rooms and public spaces and friendly staff.
It is located right on the riverwalk on the south side of the river, adjacent to the Main St. bridge, so you can can easily enjoy the riverwalk and restaurants on the south side of the river, or stroll across the bridge into downtown. Or they have a shuttle that will take you various places. The night views of the lit up city and the blue-lit bridge are gorgeous.
The pool and deck area are really great, either to enjoy alone or to have an event. The in-house breakfast restaurant is small but nice, with a buffet and limited cook to order food. There is a Ruth's Chris inside as well.
My only two complaints are: there should be a hot tub in the pool area, and the fitness center is pretty pitiful for such a nice hotel. A little more space and put in one Universal-type machine, guys.

title: “Historic Hotel in Downtown Austin”
text: Love this place with it's unique and historic charm. Our room was nicely decorated and very comfortable...not overly spacious but perfect for our needs. This hotel is located in downtown Austin right on 6th Street. You can walk to tons of cool restaurants and bars from here. I highly recommend it!

title: “Nicest folks in the city!”
text:
We we lucky and were assigned the Hilton Hotel in the Financial District through PriceLine. The front desk clerk, Stephen excelled in friendliness and gave each member of our party a cordial welcome and assigned us beautiful rooms with fabulous views of Nob Hill - all on the same floor. The women from 3 generations of our family came to the city to honor our Mother's birthday and one would have thought it was an event at the hotel! 
Lovely suggestions for meals during our weekend, detailed directions to city attractions, handwritten maps, the manager on duty one morning even gave me his cell phone in case I got lost and needed help finding my way back to the hotel. 
My mother was in the travel business for 50 years, most of our family are experienced travellers and we are IMPRESSED. 
The hotel itself is clean, modern, comfortable and well maintained. I believe it has been recently upgraded and remodeled. The real attraction at this place is its people. We will definitely go back.

title: “Beautiful spacious rooms and friendly service.”
text: Great location, right next to UCLA and within 5 minutes walking distance of shopping and dining. Booked the Grand Tour of LA with the concierge and loved it. The rooms are truly wonderful; lots of room kick back and relax or work on my computer.

title: “Birthday celebration.....”
text:
We stayed at the Renaissance Worthington for my 50th birthday celebration. We splurged and got the Romance package which included a bottle of champagne and chocolate covered strawberries upon arrival, nightly turndown service and breakfast each morning.
 We reserved a corner Terrace Suite which was beautifully decorated and very spacious. We had an awesome view of dowtown Ft. Worth from the terrace and the floor to ceiling windows in both the sitting area and the bedroom. The fresh yellow roses in vases around the suite were a nice touch. The bed was oh so comfortable as the feather pillows were like sleeping on a cloud. The hotel staff was very prompt and helpful with any request that we had.
 The only negative comment I will make is that the Sunday Brunch at the Worthington was a big disappointment. When it was on the bridge overlooking downtown, it was fabulous with beautiful and plentiful displays and as a nice touch had live piano music playing in the background.
 The Brunch we had at this visit was not at all worth the $30 a person price tag.
The champagne was cheap and bitter. The displays were boring and unimaginative. Most of the food was bland. The brunch was to start at 10:00 am , but the carving station wasn't ready until almost 11:00 am and I was told the chef was late getting the prime beef started and it was obvious he was rushed as the beef was unedible it was so rare! The desserts were still almost frozen. The breakfast items were ok and I had a pretty decent made to order omlet. But they need to bring back the elegance and variety of the past Sunday Brunch or knock down the price. 
All in all we had a fantastic stay.....but when staying again, will venture out somewhere else for Sunday brunch.

title: “spectacular !!”
text: I am sitting in my room this very minute writing my review because I am so pleased with our experience here that I could not wait until I got home. I just came upstairs from eating my fantastic FREE continental breakfast. Eggs, sausage (bacon yesterday) bagels, toast, cereal, muffins, belgian waffles, fresh fruit, 4 kinds of juices, coffee and specialty teas. I am not even sure if I got everything. The room is exceptionally clean, and very roomy by NYC hotel standards. The front desk people have been more than kind and friendly. I personally booked this room based on these reviews only, so that is why I am writing mine so quickly. Everything is within walking distance and for the price I don't think there is a better deal out there. My husband and our 2 young daughters were here for a yankee game and the american girl doll store. It has just been a wonderful experience and I am so sad to leave tomorrow. I would highly recommend this hotel and for sure would stay here again. Oh and the fridge is great for leftovers with the microwave on top to reheat them. Free wireless internet also worked perfectly. If I could give this hotel 10 stars I would. Not one single complaint about anything. This is the best hotel in midtown and a great value for the money.

title: “Great Bachelor Party Weekend Experience”
text:
I'm from the area, but had the opportunity to stay at the W for a buddy's bachelor weekend in May. We left on Sunday very impressed. The guest rooms had plenty of space and were very clean. They put out a nice amenity for us in each room since it was my buddy's bachelor weekend: 6 beers in each room and some mixed nuts. Very nice.
We started each evening off at POV (the rooftop bar) and loved it. The service was great, the drinks were stiff and fantastic and the view was amazing. We had a great time.
We ordered breakfast to the room after the first night and it tasted great, considering there was a lot of food that we ordered. The server was very nice and personable.
The folks at the front desk were very nice as well and treated us well. Overall, the service and quality of the hotel were great and the experience was perfect for a bachelor weekend. I highly recommend this hotel for young people (35 and under) who want a different experience that they can't get at a hotel like the Willard or another more "buttoned up" property.

title: “Times Square Below”
