text: We arrived here very early at 10:00 am, having disembarked from the Brooklyn cruise terminal, expecting to be told to dump our cases and come back after lunch. Far from it - the receptionist couldn't have been more helpful and quickly found us a room. We weren't happy with the room because it was close to the lifts and noisy, so we asked to be moved, fully expecting to be told 'like it or lump it', since they had tried to accommodate our early arrival. Not so, again they couldn't be more helpful and found us another room in a different location, no noise. Shamefully I can't remember the name of the lady who helped us, but she was a gem. Otherwise the hotel is what you expect of Crown Plaza, good facilities, impersonal and efficient. The location is of course superb, that is if you like Times Square. One small nag, we ate in the Brasserie one evening, and this is not a good experience, recommend you avoid this if you can.

title: “best trip ever!”
text: we stayed here and it was terrific...the staff, the hotel quality, and the locations was awesome...wish we were there more time, just a quick weekend getaway...great place to go back too, the hotel is right on the river and has great views...will be back soon!

title: “The new hotel of choice in Times Square”
text:
Having stayed in innumerable Times Square hotels over years, I can safely say this new Intercontinental is the best combination of location, service, style and efficiency. Note that "affordability" is not on that list. At $369/night, it's more costly than many of its competitors. 
The IC wins points for a friendly, attitude-free staff who genuinely were trying to please. There were rough moments here and there (a young concierge who suggested we make our own phone calls to secure dinner reservations or confirm museum tours, as well as some surprisingly uneven housekeeping), but overall the staff was commendable. 
Brand, spanking new, the hotel is still immaculate in the public areas and the rooms. The room size is arguably the IC's greatest claim to fame: They are much more spacious than the typical cave-like NYC hotel room. Plenty of light, plenty of outlets, plenty of surfaces on which to place your new New York purchases. 
Located on 44th Street at 8th Ave, the IC has all the benefits of access to Times Square, but without the noise that bedevils hotels a little closer to the action. Plus, 9th Ave north of 44th has become a restaurant Mecca, with lots of innovative and economical choices that outshine the snooze-worthy options on Restaurant Row. Todd English's Ca Va, the restaurant inside the IC, was fine but not memorable.

title: “Yotel is unlike any hotel you've ever stayed in before.”
text:
I found Yotel on the web. The pictures on the website showed that it was definitely different from the old-line hotels of New York. I loved the look of the hotel in the pictures, and was not disappointed to find that the actual hotel matched up to the pictures. Sometimes you can be fooled by a wide-angle lens picture. 
My cabin was small (which I knew from the website that it would be) and pristine.The layout of the cabin/room was designed to maximize the available space. 
I had a great view of the city and the location of the hotel is great. It was about a 10 minute walk to Times Square and the theaters. 
The restaurant was trendy and the food was great. I loved the "small plates/tapas" presentation of the food. 
My one complaint was the staff on Four. The young man that checked me in on the first floor could not have been nicer. However, at no point during my stay did anyone on Four acknowledge me in any way. I never even got a cursory "Good Morning" nor the traditional "Have a good night, sir". In fact, no one at Mission Control even made eye contact with me. Their attitude and aloof mannerism prevented me from even asking about the great smelling body wash products.
In summary, new and trendy are great, but don't forego tradition when it comes to common courtesy to your guests. 
I will stay at Yotel again, and the next time I hope the Four staff are a little more humble when it comes to the treatment of the guests. 
Remember: no guests, no paychecks. 
David Atchley
Johnson City, TN

title: “Dull, ugly and boring!”
text:
Sorry to say but this place is in real need of a few things: although the rooms are well maintained, it needs updating, Poor lighting in rooms, pre-historic tv's and cold "concrete" feel decor. The place has the atmosphere of a concrete block - extremelyy dull with no warmth or character - dont believe it is possible to build a hotel any cheaper.
That being said, I agree with some of the other reviews, if you just need a room while attending a game AND you get it cheap it should suffice. Anything needed more than that, go elsewhere.
The staff are friendly - its the place itself that lets them down

title: “Exciting”
text:
My second visit to this hotel was as i remembered from my first visit two years ago,centrally located on 7th avenue, just a short walk to central park, an 8 minute walk to times square, broadway is even closer.
There is a metro stop under the hotel,buses are regular opposite hotel.
hotel staff very friendly especially the concierge boys who go the whole mile to assist(plus tip).
Our room was on the second floor on thec east wing, down a few steps six i think and then the lift.
We had a very large room but no view which was not a problem as we only used the room for sleeping and not the local sights.

title: “Just perfect, it's the little details that make it the best”
text: For once a hotel where the reviews for it's greatness came true and they aren't just based on the food, or the lobby, or the bar, but the actual room where you are staying. I'm sure the other aspects here are great as well, but the room is great. The bed is so comfortable and the pillows are perfect. Haven't found such great pillows at a hotel in years. Even the outlet on the desk is a piece on top of the desk with about 8 outlets instead of having to unplug a lamp and the TV and crawl under the desk just to plug in your laptop when working. I love the Zebra and Leopard robes, and the stemless wine glasses just for water glasses, and the lotion and the Q-tips and cotton balls are great. Even really expensive hotels have become stingy with these types of items lately. Overall very happy.

title: “It was ok...”
text:
The room was good, big, big TV, high speed internet, very clean. 
I had to buy a Shampo, because they had a bad one. 
But for my next visit to SF (which I hope will happen soon) I'll go there again...

title: “Wow, needs better management”
text: This was my secound try at this newly converted hotel. I checked in and was advised that because of my frequency status I had been upgraded. I had been careful to book a room with a full bath since I knew that most of their rooms only have 3/4 baths. My room description had said double vanity which I had had previously so I knew It was probably like my last room. The upgraded room only had a single vanity making me question the "upgrade". I ordered dinner and specifically asked for a cart not a tray, so I could sit and watch Television. The meal arrived on a tray but the very helpful attendant quickly corected that but when he removed the cover we realized it wasn't what I had ordered. I decided to forgo dinner. As I prepared for bed I tried to close the blackouts but they wouldn't come together. I called and a maintenance man was immediately sent and tried to repair the problem, but we both came to the conclusion that it waas not fixable as it was a design flaw. I thought I could live with it and decided to try to sleep through it. Unfortunaltey the ray of light split the bed right in half and caused a fitful night of sleep. On my way out at 6:45am the next morning I asked for an emailed copy of my bill which I was assured would be sent. A week later no bill had been received. I phoned and someone assured me they would send me a copy. Two more weeks went by and I sent a comment to SPG asking for a copy of the bill. I received a canned response assuring me I would receive a copy of the bill. A week after receiving thiis I copied and pasted the response in another comment asking again for a copy of the bill. Another canned response saying I would receive a copy. It has been a week and still no copy received from anyone. If this is how their top frequency guests are treated I don't hold out much hope for the rest of their guests.

title: “Spotless and in a good location”
text:
Our experience at this hotel was very good. The rooms are always spotless and in good repair.
I hate to be picky however .......
1. the shower head was terrible. No matter how I adjusted it I had to stand within inches of the head and on the drain to get water. Change the head so it shoots water out farther. I would probably not stay here again because of this.
2. the location of the toilet paper roll is quite a distance behind you causing you to "twist around" in an uncomfortable position....why not use a portable holder?
3. the toilets are the "highest" I have encountered which is good for a tall person like me however my wife's feet would not reach the floor.

title: “Great staff at the Paradise Point”
text:
The decor is a bit outdated but the location and fire pits along the beach make up for it. Beautiful grounds. Great location for weddings which was the purpose of my visit. The staff is very accommodating. A maintenance guy came to replace a light bulb that had burnt out on my porch and asked if there was anything else I needed. I jokingly said, not unless you can build me a step to get on the beach (without having to walk down a little ways where there were steps). Within an hour he had returned with a railroad tie and made a step for me to access the beach right by my room! 
I saw bird poop mentioned in another review, well, there are lots of ducks and they do leave lots of poop around. In fact, be careful not to leave your door open or you might end up with some in your room! These ducks are rather bold!

title: “A great choice for your stay in New York city”
text:
This is my first time writing a review on a hotel (I read them all the time but have never written one) but this deserved a "thumbs up". First, the recently renovated hotel was done tastefully! Second, the entire staff (bell hops and doorman included) couldn't have been nicer or more helpful. Lastly, but so important is that Fashion 26 is in an area that allows you to visit others parts of Manhattan on foot. Oh, and not as pricey as sooo many other "just okay" hotels in Manhattan.
Be sure and have dinner at Tre Dici on the same street as Fashion 26.

title: “Awesome Stay at this Business Hotel...”
text:
Let me first of say, this was one of my best hotel stays in a while with Hilton...
I called the hotel a few days before to ensure my reservation was in order and was told yes we have you all set and we'll reserve you on the Top Floor (6th floor) no problem...
I arrived at the hotel and was greeted very nicely by the doorman and he helped me up to the lobby area (a short flight of stairs) or an elevator to the Main Lobby...
I was checked-in by Andrea (who might I say is a very hard worker) and very customer service oriented...
I was given a room on the Sixth Floor (Room 611)...when I walked into the room, I had a nice King Size Bedded Room and had a wonderful view of the City and Skyscrapers etc.
I also noticed a fruit basket (bearing bananas, oranges, apples, grapes, strawberries) and a hand-written note from Taryn (Front Desk Manager) welcoming me back to the hotel, a very nice touch might I add... 
The hotel is located directly next to Tufts Medical Center and City Place...The Orange "T" stop is directly next to the hotel as well...
The best thing about this hotel is that you have full access to the Wang YMCA from the second floor (which is great since you get private access) into the Y...
When you get to the lobby of the Y just show your key sign the sheet and your set to use an indoor heated pool, whirlpool, myraid of excerise equipment, basketball, yoga classes, you name it they got it...
I was truly impressed by all the wonderful customer service and will definately be back in the future..
I will add a few other things that I noticed:
"If you park your car there it is $40 to park overnight"
"Ask for a room on a higher floor facing the city"
"If your a Gold or Diamond you get a nice treat bag when you arrive and breakfast coupons for continental breakfast, if you want to get the full hot buffet is an additional $5 plus tax"

title: “Great Location and Service”
text:
My son has lived in Seattle for 8 years and when he first moved out there we stayed downtown. I did not realize how perfect the Marriott's location was and the value was for your money. First and foremost is the view! Wow! How wonderful to wake up to the sight of the bay and the cruise ship in port. My son is the executive chef at the Steelhead diner at the Market which is only a few steps away. Having been a Marriott member for many years I have found most of the west coast properties to have amazing service, cleanliness and value for your money. The hotel staff is always helpful and attentive. If on arrival your room is not ready they call when it is so you do not have to hang around waiting. If you are taking one of the cruises the pier is not only right across the street but the bellman also transports your luggage for you!
Marriott Waterfront has become the only hotel I will stay in when visiting my son now.

title: “Didn't want to leave!”
text: My husband and I were in Manhattan in June 2012 for 4 days on a combination business/vacation trip, and had a GREAT experience at the Waldorf Astoria! During our entire stay, everyone on the hotel staff, from the doormen, to the bell staff, to the front desk staff, the restaurant servers and especially housekeeping, were incredibly friendly, professional, knowledgeable and accommodating! We loved it! There was a slight mishap with our room assignment when we checked in (they gave us a room that was already occupied by other travelers - oops!), so they immediately more than made up for it by upgrading us to a corner suite with an incredible view of the NYC skyline, including the Chrysler building and East River. It was amazing! In addition, the 24 hour room service menu was extensive and all of the food was delicious and delivered to our room exactly as ordered and within the time frame promised. Their restaurants and bars were also wonderful, and the hotel tour was incredibly interesting! Last year, we stayed in the Waldorf Towers, which were also luxurious, and where we likewise had incredible views and even a private balcony! We can't wait to go back!

title: “Very Convenient”
text:
If you have a layover or need a hotel by the airport the Doubletree is very convenient. Especially if you;d like to avoid renting a car. 
The Homewood Suite in Kingwood is another option but about a 20 minute drive.
ARRIVAL
The shuttle bus came in about 20 minutes after i called. 
DEPARTURE
The shuttle bus leaves every half hour from the hotel back to airport. It leaves on time and takes maybe 10 minutes.
ROOM & FOOD
I'm a Hilton diamond member. No room upgrade which was a disappointment. They recommended a Chinese place for delivery which was awful. The breakfast buffet was standard. Some fresh fruit which was nice. 
Room was standard for a doubletree. Spacious, desk, sitting chair, nice TV. Cooling system was a bit off, got really cold even at 72 degree setting.

title: “Beautiful grand hotel, sensational views”
text: We had a 3 night stay at the Fairmont in August to celebrate my wifes 50th birthday. I rang ahead to advise the hotel and we were delighted on arrival to find they had upgraded us to the 23rd floor. The panoramic view from the bedroom window was nothing short of stunning, we had the Golden Gate bridge to the left and Alcatraz in front of us. The room was elegantly furnished with very comfortable beds and a large luxurious bathroom. The foyer was grand and very welcoming and the staff were both friendly and courteous whilst being very efficient. If you don't want to pay for the breakfast each morning (which by the way is as good as any we have had), there is the option of a coffee shop on the ground floor that has a selection of muffins and pastries. The hotel is in a great location for all you would want to see in the city. There are good public transport options although the cable trams that run past the hotel cafe are a little costly at $6 a person. Worth doing once for the experience however. If you decide that you are going to walk to and from the hotel be prepared for a few steep hills. The only criticism we had was that the Hertz representative based in the hotel was rude and dismissive and a shame that this behaviour becomes associated with the hotel.

title: “Great little resort, but the carpets need replacing.”
text:
I enjoyed my day at the Lakeway quite a bit, actually. It is a very lovely resort, and pretty clean except for one thing: the carpets were filthy. That's really my only gripe. They must replace the carpeting.
There were no problems at check-in. The receptionist was very nice, and very helpful.
The room was great! My party stayed in a giant king room with a balcony. The balcony gave us a fantastic view over the lake. The bed was VERY comfortable, and the shower was fantastic! It was a very lovely room. The Internet was a bit spotty, but we weren't far from a convention building, and the pre-function area in that building was a great place to get internet and be away from hustle and bustle.
The pool area is amazing. I quite enjoyed the adults-only pool with the swim-up bar. Resting against the wall while water cascaded down my back felt good. I also really enjoyed the water slide in the kids pool, as well as the hot tub.
I liked the restaurant, Josey's. We had short rib nachos as an appetizer, and they were very good. I also liked my chicken fried beef tenderloin. The restaurant was not too bad.
The Back Porch in the lobby has a good happy hour, but I enjoyed the morning coffee bar that's there more. The barista, a very nice African-American lady, did a good job with yummy lattes, and also gave me a free shot of espresso. I appreciated the espresso, although I might not try one again for a while because it is strong. I do believe they serve Lavazza coffee at the Back Porch, since that's the in-room coffee.
This is a very nice resort, but the carpets were pretty bad. Also, it can be hard to find in its tucked away location, especially in the dark. So bring a GPS. I noticed there were some bad reviews, but I REALLY enjoyed it here.

title: “Awesome Place”
text: This hotel was great, centrally located and I had no complaints! I loved the room and the service was very good and the people were polite and helpful. I hate staying in chain hotels and this one was nice and had some interesting history.

title: “Disapointed!”
text:
We picked the Parker Meridien because it was so close to Carnegie Hall. 
What a mistake that was! 
Carpet was threadbare in a lot of spots and bathrooms were smaller than any I have ever seen. 
Slow elevators and poor baggage service. 
The view was decent but not worth the price. Breakfast was also way overpriced

title: “Nice Spot and Reasonable”
text: Great spot overlooking the Marina with well appointed modern rooms. We had a Deluxe Bay view over looking the marina with breakfast and it was a great couple of nights. The pool area was nice, clean and sheltered from the wind. The grounds and facilities were well kept and the layout was fine once you got used to it. My only beef with the place is the internet and parking fees which add about $25/day to your room which I figure is a bit dated.

title: “Ideal location, great service, very comfortable room”
text:
I just returned from a 5-night stay at this lovely hotel in San Francisco's Union Square. The hotel is very nicely situated in the heart of Union Square, just steps away from all the shopping and great restaurants this neighborhood is known for. It's also just a few blocks from Chinatown, and a metro/bus ride to almost anywhere in the city. I was in town for a conference at the Moscone Center, which was an easy 8-minute walk away. The location is one of the best features of this hotel.
The hotel itself is very nice. The rooms are very comfortable, with modern decor and lots of great practical elements like a big desk, lots of easy to reach outlets and internet connections (and not just at the desk, but next to the bed as well), and a very nice bathroom with one of the best lit mirrors I've seen (great for makeup application). The view from my room was great- mostly city, with peeks of the bay behind the buildings. I would highly recommend you try to get a bay-view room on as high a floor as possible for the best view. 
The only issue I ran into during my stay was the lack of sound insulation in my room. There was a connecting door with the adjacent room, which was closed the entire time, but which let a surprising amount of noise from the other room into mine (and vice versa I imagine). I could hear conversations from the other room clearly from mine, and I did feel a bit self conscious that everything that I was saying could be heard by my neighbor as well. It didn't bother me enough to switch rooms, but if you're a light sleeper or are bothered by this, I would request a room without a connecting door. 
Overall, I really enjoyed my stay. The service was great (super fast room service), the rooms were very comfortable, the restaurant on the 36th floor had spectacular views, and the location is really ideal. I would definitely return to this hotel, and would recommend it highly to others.

title: “Not up to par”
text:
We stayed here two nights and each day our opinions of the place declined. The first night's room had an air conditioner that was so noisy we had a difficult time sleeping. The WiFi was unreachable. Parking was $18.00 per day (it was $5.00 per day across the street). The location is at the very end of the River walk and the water taxi turns around outside the hotel and goes back downstream. A typical breakfast buffet will run you $11.00.
After complaining the next morning we were able to move to a room where the air conditioner worked just fine. The next time we go to San Antonio we will stay elsewhere.

title: “Excellent would stay again and longer next time”
text: My husband, 12 year old son and myself stayed a couple of nights to see a Red Sox game. This was a perfect location and the Staff was amazing, the building was well kept. The rooms were especially clean. Hats off to the housekeeping department and the Director of housekeeping. Well done all around. I manage a hotel myself and was pleased on how clean the entire building was. there was a pleasant smell in the lobby everytime I would walk in I commented on it. The pool area was always clean and picked up the fitness center was the same. Couldnt find not one thing wrong with our stay. The whole experience was great and will return. Our room was a corner unit on the 20th floor and my husband was so excited he could see fenway from our bedroom that was the best. He was like a little kid!

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
Stayed at the Castle Inn for 4 nights from August 4 2004 - on our family trip of a lifetime!! We chose the Castle Inn based on reviews from this site - and we were so pleased we did.....it is a great place to stay for discovering San Francisco. Our room was extremely clean - if you are looking for a 4/5 star hotel, then this is not the place - but, if you are looking for a friendly welcome, clean rooms, all at a good price, then we thoroughly recommend this place. My two kids were enamoured with Marshall and his advice of where and where not to go (!) .....and they loved the danish pastries/cereal bars which we grabbed to go each morning. Very happy memories of San Francisco ....... let's hope we can come back soon! 
Thanks Marshall and Arlene, from the Webb family.

title: “My New Favorite Hotel”
text:
My husband took me to NYC last weekend for my birthday. He was able to get a great deal on Travelzoo for a room at Park South, but I was unaware that he had called the hotel the day before we left to arrange for a complimentary upgrade. I loved the look of the hotel. It was built in the early 1900's so it had a lot of character and charm. It wasn't your typical chain, which we really liked. The room was large for NYC and had a view of the Chrysler Building. The bathroom was a little small, but that wasn't a problem. Loved the bath products and the room was very clean. 
Breakfast was included in the price of the room. It was served in the Black Duck Restaurant which was attached to the hotel. Breakfast included croissants, bagels, cheeses and meats, hard-boiled eggs, fruits and some of the best coffee I've ever had. A nice plus was that it was served until 11:00. We had a meal in the restaurant on Monday night and it was delicious. I had shrimp cocktail and the most delicious clam chowder and my husband had scallops. Yummy! Saturday night we listened to live jazz and enjoyed some drinks in the restaurant. We spent a lot of time there. Partly because it was so cold while we were in New York, but also because it was such a relaxing place to be.
Everyone we came in contact with in the hotel was so nice and professional. The location was perfect. Right around the corner was a French restaurant, Les Halles owned by Anthony Bourdain. I got escargot and I do believe they were the best I've ever had. My husband had the steak, frites, and salad special. I had a bite of the steak and it melted in your mouth. Around the other corner from the hotel was another French restaurant, La Petite Auberge. We were a little disappointed in the food, but the chocolate mousse was to die for!
All in all, this short vacation was one of the best ever. A big part of the reason why was because of our hotel. The best compliment to the hotel is that I'm planning a girl's trip to New York in October and I'm already making plans to stay at Park South. The thing about New York is that it is so addictive. As soon as you leave you start planning your next trip. It's the greatest city in the world!

title: “What is all the Hype about this Hotel?”
text:
I have to say that after all I had read in Guide Books and on the Internet about this Hotel I was pretty disappointed. There is nothing particularly bad about it but it just didn’t live up to expectation. The location isn’t bad – just on the edge of the Gas Lamp District - but because of the Convention Center there is no sea view – in fact no view at all to speak of. The rooms were adequate but by no means grand although I did have to complain about a blocked sink twice before it was fixed. The other thing I didn’t like was that there were pretty big gaps under the room doors (why?) and one aftrenoon whilst waliking down the corridor I could hear quite clealy a couple making out which I really didn’t need. Not much privacy.
The staff are pleasant and helpful – especially the Consierge who gave us lots of good advice about things to do, how to get to places etc.
Despite the above I wouldn’t stay there again as I think the location isn’t particualrly great and for what it is I feel it is overpriced.

title: “Perfectly Fine, Nothing Fantastic”
text:
The five days I spent at the Ritz-Carlton Central park marked my first visit back to New York since I moved away from the city. I splurge when I travel... and am usually a Four Seasons addict, but the FS New York property leaves much to be desired, so I tried to find the most luxe hotel in NYC. After looking at this website, and the Ritz-Carlton website, I decided to stay at this hotel. 
I booked a Park-View room for $590 per night, through AmEx Platinum. Upon arrival, I was given Club Lounge access as an upgrade. The first room the receptionist escorted me to was unacceptable: dark, shabby (fringe torn off the curtains), and an ugly gold color that didn't suit my tastes. I didn't like the room, so she was kind enough to show me two others, one of which was perfectly lovely. The bellman kindly moved my luggage and the flowers and giftbasket which had been placed in the room before my arrival (however, they lost the cards that arrived with them, so I had no idea who they were from until someone said, "Did you get the flowers???").
Yes, the rooms are nice... but nothing to die for. (Sometimes I wonder what the homes of Tripadvisor users must look like since they're drooling over hotel room decor...) Small but elegantly furnished. 
Room service is a little better than average. 
The lobby and bar was happening every night, but the restaurant was EMPTY. 
The whole "club lounge" concept isn't my scene. Guest excited about FREE FOOD and drinks hovering around appetizer platters is disappointing. 
It is a lovely hotel, and the service is good. But, is this the best NYC has to offer? Is this as good as it gets? If so, I'm terribly disappointed. I imagined so much more. I think every hotel should aspire to be like the George V is Paris: absolutely flawless.

title: “The best location with parking!”
text: Great little find! Two mins walk from Hollywood Blvd and all it's sights. Rooms large and clean, Alber on the front desk is fantastic, helpful and friendly! breakfast is easy and plentiful , free wifi and parking.. Too easy! Stayed with husband and we loved it! It's probably the equivalent of an Australian 3 star motel. Not glamorous but perfect for a cheap stay in Hollywood!

title: “Stayed 3 months”
text:
I stayed 3 months at this hotel on business.
As a platinum status member, being on club level and having a good concierge lounge is important.
I love the rooms. They are like new, well maintained, clean, and large. The lobby is big and decor is modern. Overall, this is my hotel of choice in this area if the price is right, and it was.
The downside was concierge lounge. The hot food was useless for all 3 months. They never had anything I liked but the cheese and crackers, and the dessert. When they put the aged cheddar out, my weight becomes an issue. Great cheeses! But lousy hot food, and the lady was not friendly to me for all 3 months. You would think that after 3 months, she would go out of her way to be nice. She was usually watching TV and was too busy. In contrast, the morning staff in the concierge lounge were very friendly, and the food there was as expected.
If they cleaned up their act on the night time concierge lounge, I would give them 5 stars.
The front clerk staff is friendly and professional. The one Asian room service lady was awesome. She was very nice and I looked forward to seeing her. Room service food is good but nor great. Fish is always fresh and tastes great. They can also prepare it the way you want, not just what the menu says.

title: “A rare exemplar of fine service and dedication to quality.”
text: The female manager was excellent, -she provided me the kind of attention and service one would get visiting a relative. I forogt my phone charger and she charged my phone for me, -even took phone messages for me. Got me a late checkout and a complimentary breakfast due to their iron soiling my blouse. The room was an excellent business workers suite.

title: “They Get It”
text: This was our first stay at this property, Excellent service and a great location. I would stay here again for sure.

title: “Roomy and well located”
text:
Well positioned opposite the railway station and with a view of the Capitol. Small reception area leading into the Irish pub with outdoor sitting area. Good size rooms with slightly overbearing decoration. 
Breakfasted and a light lunch - both acceptable rather than outstanding. Walking distance to most of the attractions.

title: “The James is Fantastic!”
text:
The James Hotel is one wonderful surprise after another. Behind its unassuming facade is a hotel dedicated to art and the edge of its SoHo neighborhood. During my all too brief stay at the hotel, I was met with the friendliest and helpful staff, who were willing to go above and beyond to help with anything that I needed. It was also apparent that the hotel takes pride in delivering a consistent experience that is based in art, from the decor of the lobby and hallways to the overall details in the structure the hotel and furniture in the rooms.
If you are looking for a unique New York experience, do yourself a favor and stay at The James.

title: “Excellent location in SoMA !”
text:
Stayed 4 nights there, I was expect worst than that actually, quite surprised. Nice hotel, in a perfect location + free wifi, 2 minutes from Powell station (BART/MUNI), 2 minutes from Market Street, 10 minutes from the SFMOMA. Just avoid, the little details like lack of paint in some spots in the room, thin wall, no safe. As well, I think it was a bit pricey, I know it was the World Series in SF but it was 190$ a night. I still will recommend the Pickwick Hotel.
PROS:
*Location in central SoMa
*Free wifi
*Confortable bed
*Free ''Keurig'' coffee in the room
*2 minutes from Powell station
*1 minute from Westfield Mall
CONS:
*Lack of paint in some spots, a renovation will be good for the hotel
*thin wall, could hear the people beside my room
*when you turn on the hot water, it's make a loud noise
*no safe to put your valuables
*a bit pricey for what it is

title: “Good value for the money”
text: Stayed here with my daughter over the Memorial Day weekend and have no regrets for the price I paid. We had a $207/night non-refundable rate booked directly with the hotel. For the location, this was a great deal! We were on the 18th floor overlooking 6th Ave. Noise was normally not a problem. One night around 2:30am, there was excessive sirens and horn honking but this is New York. Did not experience this on other nights. This is a large hotel and it attracts groups. Lines for check-in, conceirage (excuse spelling) and taxis were never more than 5 deep. All staff was helpful. Only complaints were that the in room air never seemed to go below 70 but hallway was freezing, no coffee/tea maker in room and housekeeping never resupplied toiletries unless you asked; however, when I asked, they left double. I have previously stayed at Westin Times Square and Andaz 5th Avenue. If you are looking for low cost and great location, this is a good choice.

title: “Great place to stay!!”
text: This place has a great staff. Very caring from the moment you walk in, to the time you check out, they make sure you have everything you need to be comfortable. The rooms were very nice and clean. like any other Holiday Inn Express, they offer complimentary breakfast but the breakfast attendant was very nice. It was nice to have her ask us about our stay and give us ideas on things to do and see in the area. Overall a great stay. We will definitley stay here again when traveling to El Paso!!

title: “Pricey space themed hotel”
text: High price with complimentary breakfast limited to muffins and coffee, very small room, and not overly helpful staff. It may be convenient to Times Square but there are more nicer, much more afforable places accessible via the Subway.

title: “Good but crowded.”
text: My friends and I stayed at a Deluxe room, and I was hoping it was a big room. Anyway our stay was great, and it is walking distance for many places. There are always a loooooot of people in this hotel, but rooms are quiet.

title: “Very good value for money”
text:
Hotel very convenient for families with children.
No fancy stuff but everything you need and the price was definitely right (less that 200 usd/night).
Location close to CP, subway station, and if you don't mind to walk you can easiliy reach 5th avenue or Times Square in half hour or so.

title: “Good value, honest hotel ,right on Times Square”
text:
Went on a family 4 night stay in New York over hallowe'en 07, the first time I've been back there in 30 years - what's happened to all the rubbish, grime and rude people in the meanwhile? It's cleaner, friendlier and felt a lot safer than most cities in the UK. The people were brilliant; proud of their city and keen to help a stranger. We had a ball - even our teenage boys (normally not that easy to please) were swept away with the place.
The Novotel is, I guess, a bit tired and needs a revamp sometime soon, and yes, that lift that you need to use to get to reception from the main street, is a bit slow and irritating. But if you really need to look at that level of detail then I think you're missing the point of being in NYC. Look past these details and you see a servicable hotel, reasonably priced (for New York!) that is clean, friendly and perfectly situated. As others have said, you haven't come to NYC to mope around the hotel.The reception staff were really helpful and very polite;Ian at reception was a gem and worthy of special mention, as is Yves the concierge. We ate breakfast in the hotel because the boys ate free, otherwise we'd have gone to one of the many delis in the area for a lot less. The view is good over breakfast but we did feel a little herded.
We we go back to the Novotel - certainly, if the price was right. However, we wouldn't feel the urge to stay at Times Square next time; anywhere near to the subway is near to almost anywhere in Manhattan, and we'll want to chill a little next time having already done the 'must-sees'

title: “A great place ... in January.”
text:
This was the first trip to San Diego for my wife and me and we wanted to experience the fabled Southern California beach culture. We're both in our 60's, so by experience I mean, watch.
We stayed for three nights Saturday-Monday after previously staying in Point Loma for three nights.
We choose Pacific Shores Inn based on Travel Advisor reviews and the Inn's website. I was somewhat concerned when there was no way to verify my reservation via email (which I made directly by phoning the Inn, since their website did not offer me all the room choices I knew were available.) I wound up calling the Inn prior to leaving on vacation to verify the reservation. Once we arrived everything was exactly as requested.
We asked for an upper level 2Q N/S room with kitchen, and a view of the ocean, if possible. The room was huge, with a separate kitchen area and table, a large main room with another table, and a very large walk in closet. The bathroom was above average, but the door was right next to one of the beds. 
About four rooms shared an outside balcony and each room had its own plastic table and chairs set outside into a little alcove by each room's door.
There was a view of the ocean from the balcony, but since the boardwalk and beach was less than a half-block away we simply walked through the parking lot and there it was (except for one other property in front of the Inn).
A pleasant surprise was the coin laundry. The Continenal breakfast was the standard rolls, coffee,fruit and juice, but the coffee was very good.
One wing of the Inn was being extensively remodeled, the rooms were essentially being gutted and rebuilt. I would strongly suggest that you request an upper level room, and the one's with kitchens don't cost a lot more and appear to be a lot larger.
Housekeeping was good, the staff was pleasant (I learned that the motel did not have an internet connection in the office except for the reservation system, which explains the lack of email confirmation.) 
The Inn is located near the northern end of the beach/boardwalk, which was great because it was less crowded and noisy, yet in a block or two you were right in the middle of the beach scene.
We were fortunate to be there when the surf was unusually high and saw high waves, and dozens of surfers up and down the coast. Some of the surfers had come from long distances to take advantage of the waves and a few were staying at the Inn.
The weather was perfect, sunny and in the 70's which was what we were seeking after a tough Wisconsin winter. The mid-January price was great , the room was perfect ...... but, I wouldn't want to stay there from Spring Break until the end of the year unless I was much younger, because Pacific Beach is striclty a youth-oriented destination most of the year.
We had a few times where the outside noise in the parking lot was excessive, I imagine most of the time the area has a college-town atmosphere. I didn't see any children at the Inn, and almost none in the entire area.
Along the boardwalk on the beach bluff there were numerous restaurants and bars, and the shopping area was eclectic. It is a great place to soak up the sun and people-watch, plus you can walk the beach for hours.
I would stay there again, at the right time of the year.

title: “Excelent Hotel !!!!”
text:
My family and I stayed at this hotel last year on our trip to Charlotte (12/31/2010) The Hotel was extremely clean, the staff was excelent. 
Will definitely stay again.

title: “Friendly atmosphere! Great coffee!”
text:
Having spent 4 days in tis hotel, I can say one thing for sure - they serve great coffee in their lobby, but the room coffee is bad!! Anyways the good thing about the hotel is that its a very old - almost 100 years old building and they have maintained the authenticity... however in a way that is also the bad thing as the rooms are small.
The staff is very friendly and really go all out to help you, so that was a good experience. The location is perfect - so one can try out P.F Changs!
In all I recommend the hotel

title: “Remembering the Herald Square”
text: I think we've finally found a hotel that meets all our needs for NYC. It was close enough to the city that we could walk to most of our destinations, the room wasn't overly large, but fit our criteria. The bathroom was a little cramped, but enough to shower and everything. The staff was friendly and accomidating. All and all a great stay and will definatly be staying there again. Nice clean affordable rooms, you can't go wrong at the Herald Square Hotel.

title: “Awful experience”
text: This is one of the worst hotels I've ever stayed in. My fellow business companion booked a non-smoking room but they did not have it when we arrived. Despite giving the front desk their cell number for the manager who was not onsite to call, he never did. They advertise free wireless Internet. However it was worthless as it kept going in and out. I called the support number based on the wi-fi card they had in the room only to find they don't service the hotel! Why then is the card & number in their rooms? The hotel staff could'nt say! Rooms are dimly lit and the two TV's had poor reception - good luck watching a baseball game if you want to see the ball! I had hoped to try the continental breakfast buffet at least, but it was sparse and with only 4 tables I had no place to sit even if I wanted to. If I was on my own dime I would have eaten the cancelation fee of a nights stay and left and checked in at a beautiful Hilton Homestead Suite a quarter mile away. Run don't walk away from this dump! ......FYI this is the first hotel I've ever rated in 25+ years of business travel, but it was just awful.

title: “All you could ask for- marvellous staff, lovely rooms, and central to everything!”
text: Staff so helpful and welcoming- I phoned and the staff member helped me with shuttle and then welcomed me so nicely at the hotel. It was late and I was exhausted but the staff member was patient, professional and so kind. Room lovely, very comfy. Next morning, staff helped me with organising return shuttle and happily looked after my bags so I could explore one last time! A marvellous trip and a marvellous hotel- highly recommend! Caz

title: “amazing breakfast buffett”
text: free shuttle from airport, walking distance to T, amazing wkd breakfast buffett, nice gym, friendly staff, good value...can't go wrong here!

title: “Good value”
text:
Having been open for just a few weeks, we were happy to try this hotel. Centrally located, clean, and modern. As you enter, the hotel bar welcomes you. The reception is just around the corner. There are several couches in the lobby you can relax in. They could do something with noise reduction in the lobby though. There was always a crowd in the lobby, and trying to weave through them to get to the hotel elevators could be difficult. Our room on the 9th floor didn't have a very good view (parking lot). An atrium view would've been more interesting, as it looks out to the other rooms windows that resemble an urban surrounding--red brick walls and windows. From the 5th to the 10th floor, you have this view. There is a small business center with modern furniture. The staff was pleasant and helpful, esp. doorman Zam Zam. Thank you!
I would recommend the hotel if they could get a good promotional rate, otherwise, there are other hotels in the city to try out.

title: “Horrible night's sleep - Avoid this hotel”
text:
If you want a good night sleep, STAY AWAY FROM THIS HOTEL.
Family and I were supposed to stay at Windsor for two nights, but checked out after one after having one of the worst nights sleeps we ever had. 
Beds/pillows were the most uncomfortable of any hotel we ever stayed at. These were horrible. Note to Windsor: Don't buy the cheapest beds/pillows you can find.
Additional problems included:
* headboard on one of the beds broke off and fell to the floor
* couch had rips in it
* walls paper-thin - could easily hear people in room next door (and I don't think they were overly loud)
* room was way too hot and there was no way to adjust it down
Given the price of the room we were definitely not expecting the Ritz...but we were expecting a lot more than we got from Windsor.
Avoid this hotel and spend the few dollars more to stay at Embassy Suites next door. That's where we moved after our horrible night here.

title: “Fantastic stay, will return.”
text: Excellent hotel, friendly staff, 2min walk from Union station. Will definitely stay at Liaision again.

title: “Excellent Staff, Very comfortable hotel”
text: I was visiting Houston on business for two days last week and stayed at this hotel. The staff was extremely helpful and friendly, and obviously genuinely care about the quality of their hotel. My room was very clean, comfortable and quiet. I was expecting to hear noise from adjacent rooms as you often do in hotels, but I really didn't hear anything. The only things that might need improvement are the size of the workout room (very basic), and the complimentary breakfast was fairly limited. There are plenty of places to eat around the hotel, and it was fun to go out and explore Houston. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Place”
text: This is a great place to stay if you are traveling out of Philadelphia airport. The staff was wonderful, the place is beautiful. Food was good and a great deal if you want to leave your car while on vacation. We normally fly out of Baltimore, but no more! The hotel is very close to the airport, the shuttle runs every 20 minutes. A better hotel, closer and cheaper than where we normally stay in Baltimore.

title: “Very Helpful Staff, Fenway Park Location”
text:
I found the staff at this hotel to be extremely helpful and polite. The furniture is a little old and outdated, and perhaps could use a refresher. I stayed in the Luxury Suite, a very large area for the price. Huge floor to ceiling windows, a great view, high ceilings, really a special place. I noticed while booking that suite ranges in price from $599 to 719 (I'm guessing it depends on whether the Red Sox are playing.)
The hotel is literally across the street from Fenway Park, so if you're in town for a game, you can't go wrong. However, I was not in town for a game, and I felt the area was not what I would have wanted. It's very big on nightclubs for the young. Being older, and not at all interested in Boston baseball, I prefer other areas of Boston; but that's my preference.
Overall, a really nice hotel, in need of some refurbishing, and if you ever wanted to splurge on a grand suite, the Luxury Suite is the way to go. At $599, it's a steal.

title: “great base in new york”
text: myself and my daughter went there for a shopping trip and sight seeing trip, it was the best 4 days i,v had for years. we got there early but couldnt check in until 3pm, we left our bags in the holding area and went to find our bearings. we got back about 3.15pm our room wasn,t ready so we were soo tired we just sat in the lobby until about 3.30pm, tried to check in again but still the room wasn,t ready, we met a lovely man called mahomed at reception and he gave us a different room on the31st floor. it was a great corner room with views of the empire state building and madison square garden, and 2 double beds.... so a big thank you to mahomed, you made our stay just great and we can,t wait to go back.

title: “Wonderful location, a value--if you can get in”
text: We love staying here when we're in Chicago. The staff is always attentive and helpful. You can't beat the rates and the breakfast is ample. With its being located close to Wrigley Field and De Paul, it's not easy to get reservations so if you know well in advance, get in. Parking is extra but in the great scheme of things not overpriced. Rooms are clean and well-appointed.

title: “Good hotel”
text: one the whole this is a very good hotel, we booked this because of his proximity to unerversal studios (walkable & free shuttle bus). good sized clean rooms, comfortable beds, very nice pool with lots of sunbeds and facilities.The staff were very friendly. No resort fee is charged but there was a higher than adverage charge for parking and internet access.

title: “What a difference a year makes; Don't know that we'll return.”
text:
We came back to Omni because it's in a great area (the historic district), the bed was divine, and the service first rate. We arrived early and they allowed us to go to our room (what a treat). They were the same courteous, well-manner staff we left behind. The room, however, was not. The bed was so hard we both woke up in pain. The pillows had quills sticking into our faces. We called and asked for two more - they were worse than worse and felt like something that had foam was robbed and stuffed into pillow cases.
The plasma TV, the least of our problems, was far left of the bed. Nice feature, poor placement. The curtains didn't close all the way. We closed them with pant hangers; really!
I called in the morning and the head of the front desk was up and was switching our rooms in less than ten minutes. Hurrah. We also got passes for two free breakfasts. No sleep, free breakfast, it was a nice thought. The 2nd room had a TV (normal size) whose volume control didn't work. We weren't calling them about this. There was a leak of cold air in the room. So, we turned up the heat and felt cold air all night. The bed was minimally better, the pillows were much better. We slept a little better. We were both exhausted the following morning and left without following up on these other problems. Someone else can deal with them.
When we went downstairs on Sunday, they were serving coffee, danish, and bagels. The room where people were eating was a mess (I was concerned about sitting down). They were out of hot water, coffee, you name it - this was quickly rectified but by then, I was getting ready to leave and go elsewhere for coffee.
I've stayed at the Sheraton, Hilton, B&Bs, L'Efant Plaza, etc. Some had problems, others did not. But, the amount of money we spent did not equal what we received. It applied somewhat to the superb service. If I need a place with great service, I'll go back. If I need a place to sleep, I will have great trepidations... you should as well. At this moment, about one week later, I still would not return. There must be other places in Philly to stay.

title: “I've found my new Chicago "Home" Hotel”
text: Beautiful boutique hotel, very nice well appointed rooms, larger than average. The location is perfect....on a quiet side street, yet only a short walk to N. Michigan Ave. The staff was very pleasant, they made you feel at home. There is a very nice restaurant adjacent where we had breakfast at a sidewalk table. I've stayed in Chicago dozens of times at a dozen hotels, but this is where I'll be staying next time. We're done with the crowded, noisy, chain hotels and their mediocre rooms and inflated prices.

title: “Nice Historic Hotel”
text: When staying in San Francisco it shouldn't be about how great or updated the hotel is, since you are in a city that requires and demands exploration! The Opal though was a nice addition to our trip. It is centrally located and the theater is next door; if you find time to fit in a movie. The room wasn't fancy and outdated compared to most hotels, but definitely served its purpose for sleeping. My only real complaint about the room would be that it lacked a fan in the bathroom and after a hot shower it takes a very long time to defog. The staff was pleasant and the hotel has a few amenities: Continental breakfast (mainly carbs, but they did have hard boiled eggs every morning),basement coin laundry, fitness center, hot water, coffee and tea in the main lobby all day! Electronic key fob entry into the hotel and room which certainly increases the feeling of safety. All in all a great place to stay on a budget and still enjoy your trip!

title: “Great Staff & Management”
text: Very good hotel stay this pass weekend at Westin San Francisco Market Street. The staff & management were excellent. It is in a very good location near a subway.

title: “Loved the Moore.”
text:
Perfect for a night before and a night after our cruise. Family of four, with two teenaged children. We had a suite both times, two rooms with a bathroom in the middle for $121. Can't beat it. We were on the 3rd floor the first time, 6th floor the second time. Both floors were updated. It is an older building, but there was fresh paint, it was clean and we even a a towel elephant in the bathroom! TV and fridge in the room, internet in the lobby. Two blocks from the fish market, about 1/2 mile from Whole Foods. 
The desk clerks were great, helpful and stored our luggage after we checked out. Buses are free, so we were able to get around easily. Seattle has some interesting characters, I don't think they are limited to the Moore hotel area. There seemed to be a lot of tattoed, body pierced folks and homeless people. We are from the Philadelphia area, so this was not so unusual for us, but I can see how some people might be afraid. We had to go to the drugstore in the evening, and we felt safe. 
One regret is that we did not have a room away from the street. Apparently, the suites all face the street. I did hear the street noise at night, and that woke me. But, the rest of my family was not bothered by it. Otherwise, it was a nice place to stay on a budget. We don't go for fancy accommodations, we go to see the sights.

title: “Terrible experience, to say the least.”
text: I've never experienced such an all around terrible hotel experience; even when I have had the unfortunate occassion of staying at a low budget hotel/motel. 1. Only one of the two rooms reserved for my party were available. 2. (Two) double beds rooms were reserved, only one king bed w/sofa sleeper available. 3. After checking in and settling into king room, we had to be moved because of the wet carpet due to bad plumbing. 4. The sofa sleeper in the new room had broken legs. 5. The television did not work. 6. Ceiling tile were molded and missing. 7. 3 guests were registered in room, housekeeping would only leave towels for two. If the cliche "you get what you pay for" is true, I'd say we need a refund! Horrible!!!!!

title: “Good night”
text:
Stayed in the hotel just for 1 night and for this cant estimate thoroughly all facilities over there. Would notice that guy on a reception was very friendly and professional. Had a nice corner room in japanese style with an exellent view of a city from a balcony. Could hear a bit noise from a street in midnight but slept quietly. 
Considering that it is a japanese district, needed to walk some distance in order to find suitable restaurant.

title: “No Better place for Families to stay.”
text: Don't expect a 5 star hotel here, BUT your not paying for one either. The furniture is old and stained, the sink and toilet are old and out dated and this was our 4th time to stay here because with a now 5 year old son there is no better place to in San Antonio to stay. There was always kids he could play with in the pool, sand area or playground equipment. There was free drinks and ice cream, decent breakfast, beautiful grounds, very friendly and helpful staff..... and an absolutely GREAT value for your money. It is the quietest motel we've ever stayed in. We definetly plan to be here again.. During our stay we went to the zoo, the Riverwalk, Sea World, etc. The motel is as central as you can get.... Thanks Hill Country.......

title: “Another Truly Amazing Stay at a Great Property in the Perfect Location!!”
text:
Hyatt Regency Chicago
Date of Stay: Wednesday, March 14 - Friday, March 16, 2012
Length of Stay: 2 Nights
In a nutshell, this is a truly wonderful and newly renovated hotel, with absolutely excellent customer service, top-notch dining that is perfectly located along the Chicago River!
Now, for my detailed review:
First, I must say that this review builds upon prior review of this property -- for further information and some more details on this property, please see my prior review:
-November 2010, entitled: “A truly AMAZING Hyatt!! A perfect location with stellar service!!” (posted November 8, 2010)
Having stayed at this property before, my wife and I were expecting similarly excellent service, and we were most definitely not let down. The Hyatt Regency Chicago provided us with the perfect place to stay in Downtown Chicago. 
We arrived very late at night, due to a late flight from Florida. Upon arrival at Chicago O'Hare, we were met by a driver that had been arranged for us by the Concierge at this excellent property -- if you need to get to this property from either of the Chicago area airports, I highly recommend contacting the hotel concierge prior to your arrival as he or she will be able to arrange a very skilled driver for an extremely reasonable price! Our driver arrived right on time to pick us up, and he was extremely professional and courteous, quickly getting us to the entrance to the Hyatt Regency Chicago.
Upon arrival in the lobby, we we met by an excellent bellman who assisted us with our luggage, and who directed us to the Hyatt Gold Passport Check-in Desk. This property has excellent front desk service, with a very large and separate area dedicated solely to the needs of Hyatt Gold Passport Members. Check-in was extremely quick and efficient at this dedicated Hyatt Gold Passport Desk -- we were welcomed by name and thanked for being repeat guests and loyal Diamond Level Gold Passport Members. And, within a matter of moments, we were on our way up to our Suite, room 3614. All-in-all, a very quick and efficient check-in offering excellent customer service.
Upon arrival at our room, we were very excited to see that we were once again in an excellent suite -- the suites at this property are extremely nice, and I highly recommend splurging and booking a suite at this newly renovated property. As we walked into our room through the double doors, we entered into a beautiful tiled entryway, with a wet bar directly to our left and a large and freshly entered bathroom to our right. The bathroom had clearly been recently renovated, offering a beautiful vanity, plush towels, a very large shower and a toilet. This bathroom had a separate entry into the bedroom portion of the room as well. Going back into the entry way, directly in front of us, we had an extremely comfortable couch with a coffee table, and a large HD-television. To the left of this living area was a dining area, complete with a large dining table and a nicely sized computer desk. And, all the way across both the dining area and the living area there were wonderful floor-to-ceiling windows, offering a beautiful view of the Chicago Skyline and slight view of the Chicago River. Then, as for the bedroom, it was equipped with an extremely soft and comfortable Hyatt Grand Bed, a computer desk, a large HD-television and similar floor-to-ceiling windows. All-in-all, an excellent and freshly renovated room that provided for a truly wonderful stay!
In addition to the excellent room, this property has some truly top-notch dining experiences.
For breakfast, I highly recommend "The Bistro at 151." This restaurant offers an excellent buffet at a reasonable rate. However, we opted to order off of the menu instead -- and, we were extremely happy with our selections ... I highly recommend the Eggs Benedict! Breakfast was truly one of the best hotel breakfasts that we have ever experienced.
Additionally, for drinks at light appetizers, the "BIG Bar" is wonderful! Offering up beautiful city views, excellent appetizers and truly tasty strong drinks. "BIG Bar" should not be missed for anyone who enjoys a good drink.
Furthermore, for anyone like us that enjoys a truly amazing steak, "Stetson's Chop House" should not be missed. As the property description indicates, this is truly one of the finest steakhouses in Chicago. Offering an excellent wine selection, AMAZING service and truly succulent steaks, you should not miss "Stetson's."
In addition to the excellent dining, this property truly is in the perfect location -- just across the Chicago River from the "Magnificent Mile" aka "Michigan Avenue" which offers very excellent shopping and dining. It is also a very quick cab ride to all of the area museums -- and, if you want to visit Chicago's excellent museums, make sure to speak with the hotel concierge, as this property often has specials and discounts which can save you a lot of money.
All-in-all, the Hyatt Regency Chicago is a truly wonderful and newly renovated property that offers excellent service in a prime location. This property should not be missed by anyone traveling to Chicago!

title: “Perfectly located”
text:
First off, Courtyard by Marriott is absolutely perfect for me and my family. 
During my stay I planned to do a little holiday shopping and sightseeing. This Courtyard location turned out to be perfect. The Courtyard brings one word to mind, consistency. I have stayed at more than a dozen or so in many states and each have all been a delight.

title: “Fun time”
text: I wasn't in my room other than to sleep but the interior design and layout was fantastic for the "cabins". It was a great use of space without making you feel too cramped in your room. Very modern. Great happy hour at the bar.

title: “Very Chic Hotel! Great Location!”
text: The W Hotel in Times Square is a very chic hotel, in a great location! It's perfect if you will be taking in Broadway show! The staff was very friendly and courteous. The rooms are small, but nice. I was there on the weekend and the bar in the lobby can fill up and get pretty noisy, but it's part of the ambience of the hotel. The club in the basement of the hotel was cool and had decent music. I would recommend the hotel, but search around for a good rate as it can be expensive. It's a nice hotel, but don't overypay. We spent around 234.00 a night in November. The hotel restaurant, Blue Fin, is excellent but expensive. If you want ambience, and a great location, then I would recommend staying at the W Times Square!

title: “Overall nice hotel”
text: We stayed at this hotel last week and it exeeded all of our expectations The. J. W. Suite was very nice, clean and spacious.We loved the location because we were very close to Grand Central Station.The breakfast was a little overpriced. All-in-all another great Marriott experience!

title: “Loved it!”
text: My best friend and I take a yearly vacation and Seattle was our next stop. Last minute, we decided to stay at this hotel for 2 nights. It was awesome! It had a lodge type feel and the front desk workers were helpful and friendly. We stopped at the bar for a drink and the bartender was a fine gentleman who was happy to serve us. The highlight of the hotel: incredibly close to public transportation. You can walk down the hill and hop on the Sound Transit. It took us 20 minutes and $2.50 to get to the Space Needle (had to see it). I would absolutely stay here again!

title: “Disappointed the way it ended”
text:
I stayed here after reading some positive Tripadviser reviews despite its low ranking. I felt all the staff at this hotel initially went out of their way to make my stay at their hotel special. From the moment I checked in, the staff did more than I would expect at any hotel. They offered me a welcome basket while upgrading me. And they would call me asking if there was anything they could do. I ordered room service and they gave me a free fruit plate. I was aware the rooms do not have a bathtub, but I was surprised how big the shower was. Also there was no fridge, but the ice machine was right outside my door.
On the 2nd day of my stay, I discovered the upgrade I got wasn't that good. The room was connected to rooms on my left and right, and there was a noisy family on my left. They were so loud it was like them being in the same room with me. I am basically a quiet person. They can't hear me but I can hear them. I know I did not pay for the rooms on my sides, but even the front desk girl who checked me in later acknowledged that yes, one of the negatives of my upgraded room is that is connected to 2 other rooms. I just got the feeling that the hotel wasn't exactly fully occupied, so it's not like they could not have left the room next to me vacant. If I had to choose between an upgrade and a room not connected to another room, I would always pick the latter, since I have had bad experiences with connected rooms. But since I got used to the upgraded room and wasn't staying long, I did not ask for another room. I personally don't understand why they have connected rooms. If a family wants to stay in a hotel, why not just book a suite, why have connected rooms? I must say I am disappointed it had to end this way. I guess it was too good to be true, that I was given a wonderful room for one day, and that I couldn't have a 2nd good day. But hotels are always like that. They go out of their way to cater to you, then they do something stupid to ruin your stay. I doubt I'll be staying here again, upgrade or not. There are just too many new and good hotels in Baltimore.

title: “great location”
text: there was a nice room with a fridge and microwave...the staff was wonderful and extremely helpful...the hotel is in a perfect location to times square and the subway station...id stay here again

title: “Awesome hotel - great location. LOVED IT.”
text:
Stayed here just over a week ago for 4 nights with my partner. Perfect location in the Lower East Side. Had a very stylish corner room witha steam shower, the size of the room itself was a real surprise - it was big! And the bed was by far the best bed we have had in any hotel. HUGE and soo comfortable.
The room had an Ipod dock for the alarm clock which was a great touch, and one of the best mini bars I have seen. They even breing you fresh cookies with the turn down service each night. Lots of great little touches make this one of the better hotels we have stayed in.
Walking distance to very cool bars and restaurants. No problem at all with the reception being on the second floor.
Only negative is that the check in time is not until 4pm - which is pretty late. Our room wasn't ready until 4:20 - but it was worth the wait. Reception staff weren't amazingly friendly, but they helped us with everything we needed when asked.
Would absolutely stay here again next time we are in NYC.

title: “Best Service”
text:
I recently stayed at the Houston Marriott for a two week business trip. I had horrible experiences at recent hotels I stayed at and almost dreaded 2 weeks in the hotel. Upon arrival, Matt Jones, at the front desk, immediately greeted me. He made sure I had everything I needed for the stay and notified me of the concierge services through out the week. 
During the stay, I was greeted by the ENTIRE front desk staff when I came in everyday. They made the long stay feel like I was home. One evening I did not feel well after a dinner out (I won't mention the restaurant), Matt called my room to make sure I was ok and asked if there was anything they could do. Matt also knew I was watching Netflix and helped with some great movie choices. I truly appreciated the over and above service I received during that time. 
I have recommended this Marriott to numerous coworkers and friends. I will definitely stay there again.

title: “Nice Room, Poor Service”
text:
First of all, if you are going to book on their website, keep checking back. The rates go up and down from in the mid 150's to the mid 250's for the same date.
Our rate was $179 for a king. When I first called I asked if there was a room with 2 queens, since we have 3 small children. I was told that the room limit is 3 people due to fire safety. This was ridiculous so I ignored it.
Both my wife and I lived in SF, so we are familiar with the area. The hotel is South of Market, very close to 6th street, one of the worst parts of the downtown area, rivaled only by the Tenderloin. You're not going to want to take nightly strolls heading South, and you don't want to park on the street (if you can find it). You'll be broken into. Upon arrival I was suprised at how small the driveway is. It was crowded with cars and difficult to unload. The lobby is small but nice, sort of like a W hotel. The rooms were very modern, and our view from the 26th floor looked out to the Eastbay. It was pretty, but the other side of the hotel, with views of the City, would have been better. Despite having asked that the liquor cabinet be locked electronically, it wasn't, and our 2 year old opened it, which, we were warned, would result in a charge. It did not. The prices were outrageous...$6.50 for a bag of peanut M&Ms.
We ordered an appetizer from room service. It was a very small sandwich with proscuitto on it. Delivered, it was $20 tip included, but the delivery guy still stood there waiting for a tip.
When I checked in I asked that a pull out bed be delivered to the room, but was told to call roomservice once we were settled. We began calling at 9:00 p.m. Nothing came. We then called again at 10:00 p.m. Again nothing. A third call was made at midnight. Nothing. Finally at 2:00 a.m. I called and the bed was delivered. The guy said he was sorry and waived the charge for the bed. Nice.
All in all, it's a good deal for $150-175 a night, it's clean, and has great views. The location is in a bit of a sketchy area, but it'll be safe as long as you only head North. I wouldn't even walk up 5th street at night. If you are going to Moscone Center, it's VERY close, and would be a perfect location.
On another note, while we were leaving for dinner Saturday night, the bar was packed...with flamboyent gay men. Not sure how they found it, but this would appear to be the newest hotspot for this type. Not that there's anything wrong with that....

title: “Pretty from the outside, but the service is AWFUL!”
text:
My family and I stayed at this hotel about nine years ago, and we were extremely satisfied by the service and value we received from this hotel, however this was not the case this year, October 2010.
We arrived early due to being on a red-eye flight, and we were told our room would not be ready for about 3-4 more hours. We waited in the lobby, but were restricted from bringing any luggage or outside food/drink into the lobby. I have no idea why this is since the lobby is not very classy, nor is there anything you could damage by having your luggage in there.
When we got to our room, we were disapointed by the size. The room was quite small and the beds were extremely hard. The bathroom was only large enough for one person, which made it difficult for 4 girls to get ready.
We purchased some cupcakes to share with the 4 of us, so we asked the hotel cafe if we could borrow a knife to cut them. We explained we were staying there, showed our room key, and they still would not allow it unless we ate there at that time.
The security guards were also quite rude and abrupt. You have to show your room key to even get on an elevator, which was sometimes quite inconvenient.
When we told the front desk about our bad experiences with the hotel, they were indifferent.

title: “Stay at this hotel if you want to be kept up by picketers”
text: Stayed at this hotel earlier this week. The room was extremely dark and dingy, and the window overlooked an alley (therefore no natural light). I felt like I was staying in a cave. I arrived very late and was hoping to get a restful sleep, but was woken up by picketers at the Madison Hotel around the corner (who start at 7:00 am every morning, go all day and use a very loud horn). The toilet had plumbing problems in my room, and the housekeeping manager gave me attitude when they wanted to clean my room (I had been gone from the room all day, returned at 4:00 pm and they made me feel like it was my problem that they hadn't cleaned the room and wanted in before their shift ended at 4:30 pm). There was a conference going on at the hotel which jacked up the price of the room to $430/night. There is NO WAY I would ever pay this or stay at this hotel again. It needs a major update. Worst Westin ever.

title: “Romantic Anniversary Stay”
text: My wife and I enjoyed our Anniversary weekend here in the Brazos Suite. We started with lunch at 1886 Cafe sitting on 6th street watch the city action. The Hippie Hollow breakfast dish and Vegetarian Flatbread were amazing. The room was fantastic with traditional decor and very spacious balcony. The hotel concierge helped with planning a couples massage and also having flowers delivered to the room before we arrived. We enjoyed many places within walking distance to the hotel. We live in Austin and felt like we were on Vacation. Looking forward to the next time.

title: “Great Value”
text: This Microtel is relatively new. The staff are extremely helpful and friendly. The room we were in was very small but it served our needs. Everything was clean and the breakfast offered protein, fruit, and the usual cereal and muffins. We would return here again.

title: “Great value, Well situated to explore the city.”
text:
We found the hotel to be in an excellant location, very close to broadway. Every morning we took a different route into the city, either taking different route through central park or getting on the underground, less than a 10 minute walk away. There were lots of restaurant nearby & Carmines restuarant was an american family experience we will never forget, it had an amazing feel to it & did amazing food.
The room was an average size, but had a clean double bed, nice wooden furniture & adequate heating & window shutters. The bathrooms are shared but that was just a compromise we were happy to make, for being able to stay in the city at a far more reasonable price. There are 2 bathrooms per floor, which contained a shower over bath and toilet. We always found them to be clean & in full working order, and were usually available. But the problem poeple might experience I guess, in this situation, is that you can't guarentee that the person you follow in, has left it in a fit state! There was only 1 time I had to go to another floor to use a shower but, it was only a walk down the corridor & up in the lift. The lift was quite small but we managed with our big suitcases ok!
The people were always friendly with us on reception but we only ever had to ask for basic directions and they were always helpful with that.

title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text:
I happened upon this hotel when the hotel I usually stay at was all booked up. I was pleasantly surprised. I used AAA to get a discount and they also upgraded me to a King Deluxe for free. It turned out to be a great place to stay. At the bottom of Nob Hill, it was near a bus line and easy walking distance to downtown and Chinatown. 
The rooms, lobby, and restaurant are beautifully decorated in a middle-eastern theme and the whole place was spotless. The restaurant was excellent, and the staff was friendly and very helpful. They seemed to make it a point to ensure I was satisfied. I was. Be sure to ask for a room on one of the upper floors. I was on the 8th and didn’t hear any street noise. 
By the way, check out Crustaceans Restaurant. It’s only 3 blocks from the hotel and it is fantastic. The noodles and crab are both out of this world. Kind of pricey, but worth it.

title: “Great Base to Explore Seattle”
text: We were cruising from Seattle and chose the Paramount Hotel for an overnight stay based on its central location. Arriving into SeaTac Airport, we took the Sound Transit Link. Forty minutes and $2.75 (per person) later, we were getting off at the Westlake Center stop and making the short three block walk to the hotel. Check in was quick and efficient, the 4th floor room overlooked a courtyard and faced 7th Ave. It was clean, spacious and stocked with nice Gilchrist & Soames toiletries. One point, about 4 a.m. a trash or recycling truck was emptying a receptacle in the area which made quite a bit of glass or bottle clanking noise. The location is fantastic for shopping, sightseeing and enjoying central spots. We walked to Pike Place Market in the afternoon then again for breakfast the following morning. Conveniently located to banks, drug stores, restaurants and all manner of clothing stores. Whole Foods Market Westlake is about a 10 minute walk and is stocked with a great selection of prepared foods. We would definitely stay at the Paramount again.

title: “One of the best!”
text: My sister and I stayed here several years ago and we could not fault the hotel, room or staff. The room has it's own kitchen with a large fridge, cooker and coffee machine (provided with coffee bags, sugar etc.daily). The beds were incredibly comfortable, ideal after a day on your feet sightseeing! The bathroom was small but perfectly adequate with luxury towels and toiletries. It is not a cheap hotel but well worth the money, well located on 7th Avenue and within walking distance of all the usual tourist places. My sister took her daughter back there last year and my daughter is going to the hotel for her honeymoon in October. There is a Starbucks opposite and a great Irish pub down the road as well as an on site place to eat and shops all around. It is also opposite Madison Square Gardens. All in all, nothing to moan about at all and highly recommended to all travellers

title: “Great Location, poor hotel”
text:
I had to book a late business trip to New York and thought I would stay for the weekend. I was meant to take at the Barclay Hotel in Mid town but they had no rooms left. So, having looked at the website, I choose the Roosevelt as my meetings were all very close to the hotel. 
On arrival, the hotel looks very grand and from a scene out of Mad Men. 1950's decor on a grand level. So, was quite impressed. However, reservation staff were quite rude on check in as they carried on their conversation in Spanish. I had booked a king size room and got a queen twin room. the room was tiny, had damp on the walls, carpet was dirt and everything was so old looking.
