The bathroom was clean but very dated. i asked to be moved to the another room but was told the hotel was full. This was quite unlikely as the hotel has over 1000 rooms. However, the bar and food was good and was enjoyed. 
We paid £250 per night and felt ripped off. Not worth it at all. 
The only thing that was good was the location. Its a ten minute walk to Time Sq and 5th Avenue.

title: “Architecturally beautiful”
text:
I just spent a week at the Arizona Biltmore. As a frequent traveller for business (a two to three times per month), my needs might be a bit different than the leisure traveller.
I would definitely recommend the hotel and stay there again, however, the more detailed comments I have are as follows:
I found the Biltmore to have good size, user-friendly rooms that were clean, well maintained and with a wonderful bathroom and tub. There was high speed internet access in the room (which was great), but the channels that were available on the TV were disappointing.
Room service and the restaurants were of good quality, but not exceptional. In general food was very expensive, but not out-of-line with most hotels of this level.
The resort was architecturally beautiful and well maintained. The staff in general were very friendly and accommodating with the exception of the concierge staff. I generally rely heavily on concierge staff to handle dinner reservations, suggestions for shopping, help with booking hotel services etc. I felt that the concierge services at the Biltmore were sub par and in some cases mistakes were made on my requests.
Since I was travelling for a group function, the hotel applied gratuities for housekeeping and the bell man directly to my bill. I found this quite annoying as I didn't use the bell man, and I would like to be able to decide for myself what type of tip and service I receive from the housekeeping staff. Also, I had booked some time with the tennis pro, and when I when I was presented with the chit to sign, there was also room for a gratuity. I found this a little odd as I had paid an egregious amount for the service to begin with and felt that tipping a tennis professional a little odd.
The resort is laid out on a large amount of land so it requires a few minutes of walking to get anywhere. This is fine for the able bodied, but I think would prove extremely difficult for anyone with mobility issues.
The Biltmore was right beside the Arizona Canal which was wonderful for running. One could run or walk several miles in either direction without having much interference from traffic etc.
The Biltmore had several pools that could be used for leisure or lap swimming, and had a nice workout room and spa as well.

title: “A bit disappointing”
text:
I stayed at the Salisbury with my Husband in October for 4 nights, from Monday to Friday. We booked through Expedia and the main reason we chose this hotel was the price and the location. I had read other reviews that said the rooms were big, and I did agree to some extent. Indeed the rooms are big for New York, and in any medium priced New York hotel the view is going to be of opposing buildings, as it is such a built up city. When we arrived at reception, check in was no problem. The lifts are extremely slow and one was out of order. The hotel lobby is quite dated, the corridors are the same. Our room was large with a small kitchen section, en suite and a small 'walk in' wardrobe with a safe you can lock with a key. The room was pleasant enough and as mentioned the view was of the opposing buildings. The bathroom was clean, and in our kitchen section (behind the door) there is a kitchen unit, a sink, a fridge and microwave. Just up the street is a supermarket that sells everything, so we bought cereal and milk with re-usable bowls and had breakfast in our room. There is a pizza restaurant next door, but it is very expensive and the staff are quite rude and beligerent about tips... 12% wasn't enough for them and the returned our tip with 17% written in bold across the receipt... even though one main course was late! Not the typical service you get in America. 
We found the locaton of the hotel good, and it was an 8 minute walk to Times Square, even closer was Central Park which was literally 2 minutes on foot. There are many stores and restaurants near by and an expensive diner across the street... $60 for 2 soups and a sandwich, but New York is expensive in general for eating out. I had no trouble sleeping- we faced the street and there was only a small noise from the traffic outside. The big problem were the 'bed bugs' which I was not aware of until I noticed a large red swelling on my neck and another on my Husband's ankle- we found out on our return that bed bugs can be a problem in the city. Another low point was the cockroach that strolled into the bathroom on our second night, which put me off getting up in the middle of the night to go to the loo- maybe I over-reacted, but I only ever stay in hotels and have never seen a cockroach on any holiday before (not even in Tunisia!). The internet was also really expensive... $16 per day if I remember correctly...
Overall if you want a budget hotel close to Central Park, and you don't mind old decor and the chance you might find the odd cockroach or two, then this is the hotel for you. I won't be staying there again, I would probably stay for one less night and pay more for a better hotel... if it's your one and only trip to New York, go for the Plaza... it looked amazing!

title: “The Drury was very comfortable and clean, and great location.”
text: The hotel was convenient and comfortable. Free hot BFK, WiFi and light dinner, snacks, cocktails. Good beds. Very close to the Riverwalk. Staff friendly and accommodating.

title: “excellent location-enjoyable stay”
text:
We stayed in hotel frank in may this year, found it comfortable, clean, nice decor, staff friendly and helpful. location excellent, very central
We were warned about protesters but must have been lucky and missed them so had no impact on us at all

title: “Lovely room, great breakfast”
text: We just spent a night at the Sofitel in Philadelphia. The staff was very nice from check-in to check-out. We had a standard room which was very large with a great bathroom. Our weekend rate was reasonable and included breakfast. The waiter was extremely nice and the meal was very good. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Perfect location”
text: This hotel is in a perfect location to see the many sights and right in the heart of Manhattan. Just one minute or so to the nearest underground, Madison Square Gardens, the Empire State Building, Broadway theatre land and Times Square are all about 10 minutes walk away. There is a cafe adjoining the hotel entrance on one side and a bar on the other. Didn't venture into the bar but the cafe is perfect for getting that last minute latte on the go! The hotel reception staff are friendly and the maids are too. The breakfast is alot to be desired though - abit of a let down - plastic cutlery and paper plates, paper cups etc!! The breakfast is from 7.30am until 10am, it is best to get in the queue by 7.30am otherwise there will be no seats left. There's the usual breads, cereals and fruit, tea, coffee and orange juice-nothing too grand but just enough to set you up until lunchtime. Our room was fairly small for a double, the bed seemed small for a UK double too. The rooms are so hot and the thermastat didnt seem to work, we had to sleep with the window open but can be quite noisy - all in all though, great hotel, perfect location, amazing city!

title: “Location location location”
text: You cannot beat the location of this place. I have been to NYC a few times and always stayed in 2 star hotel a little way out as my thinking was that in NYC you only sleep in the room. Family man now with young children so a good location was essential. Rooms clean and tidy. We were checked in very fast and also check out was very fast. Only one fault was no tea and coffee making facility in the room. We only used the lobby bar on two occasions a pleasant place to sit and watch the world go by. If you want a good diner turn left out of the hotel and go to the Astro diner just one block up. We will stay here again.

title: “Great location, great price, small room.”
text: The Hotel Indigo was great! The price was awesome for the location! Right across the street from the Alamo, only a couple of blocks from the mall and the riverwalk. The room was small and had ants, but was pretty clean overall. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was nice. This hotel is pet friendly, and we had a great experience with our 2 dogs. We would definitely stay again, just maybe upgrade for the larger room (we got the cheapest room available). There is no parking, your options are Valet or to find your own downtown. I highly recommend the Valet option, both for the convenience and the value.

title: “Recommend to anyone - Brilliant”
text:
Me and my partner booked a trip to NY for my 30th birthday and our surprised engagement.
We booked 5 nights at the Salisbury hotel in NY based on reviews from Trip Advisor, and price per night compared to others in the area, now having been there myself i would recommend this hotel to anyone. 
We paid £148 per night and the rooms were better than expected, we had two large beds, flat screen TV, two walk in cupboards worth of space, free safe in the room, coffee and tea making facilities, a microwave, fridge, ironging board, basically everything you could possible need!!!
Our rooms were made and fresh cups glasses every day.
I had seen previous comments on having to wait for the lift for lengthy times, but for the 6 days that we were there this was not a problem that we experienced, and we were on the 17th floor, so the lift was a must!!!
There was more noise outside of a night than what we are normally use to living at home, but we were so tired from all of the walking around NY, and the bed were so comfortable i have to say that both me or my partner didn't have any problems in sleeping, we struggled to keep our eyes open, and one night we were in bed at 9pm fully exhausted!!!
We had the bargin of a breakfast which was $4 a head the first morning, there were muffins, doughnuts, boiled eggs, toast soft cheese, cereal, fruit salad, fruit juice tea, coffee etc available, which for $4 we thought was a fantastic!!
We did go out for breakfast on recommendation of one of the tour guides for an 'all you can eat buffet breakfast' which personally i hated, it was not my cup of tea, and this was $7.99 and then you paid extra for drinks! and the food was, well if i had of just stuck to the fruit i would of thought better, but that could just be my personal taste.
I am allergic to eggs, and one thing we noticed was all their breakfasts are with egg, so on one other morning we went to a restaurant for breakfast, and i ordered something off the menu, but asked if they could not put egg on my plate, i was told that it would cost different, and i said ok no problem, what i didn't expect was a plate of sausages (3 sausages), plate of bacon (rather well done portion of scratchings i would say)and plate of mushrooms which cost me nearly $15 - that was nearly £10 for a breakfast!!!! All because i did not want egg!!!
For the remaining part of the holiday we went back to having our breakfasts back at the hotel, as we didn't see anywhere / one who gave such a great breakfast for the money - superb value!!!
As previous people have advised the decor at the hotel is a bit out of date, but this really doesn't matter, you are hardly there, and when you are there, you are sleeping so this is just a small point to make, the hotel staff were really helpful and couldn't do enough during our stay and more importantly it was extremely clean - brilliant, if i was to go to NY again, i would definately come back to the Salisbury!!!

title: “Perfect for the money”
text: If you're looking for a safe, comfortable and reasonably priced hotel, this is it. The hotel and the room was very clean and the FREE parking was a plus and easy to park. The staff was very helpful and and very nice to deal with. A good location away from the crowd of the Wharf, yet close enough to get around. Restaurants close by as well as a Walgreens for shopping to fill your fridge or heat something in your microwave.

title: “Nice property.”
text:
Stayed here for a quick overnight after getting on a very early flight out of SAT the next morning.
The room was an excellent deal for $120 a night.
The hotel is quite new and looks it. Rooms are very kept up as are the common areas. 
The front desk staff was very friendly as were the valets who unflinchingly 1) fetched my phone after I left it in my car (running down the street to grab the other valet) and 2) delivering my car to me at 5:15 in the morning.
The location is terrific - near the Alamo, the Riverwalk and lots and lots of restaurants. I highly recommend going to the Palm which is two doors down for the after 9:00 pm bar memu.
My only knock on the place is that my room did not have a tub - shower only. Not sure if this is the norm there, but if you are dying for a bathtub, better be sure to ask for it.

title: “wonderful place to stay”
text: I recently spent 5 nights in Denver on business. Stayed in a king suite - fabulous!!! Dreamy bed, plush towels, walk-in closet with bathrobes, real bathtub, strong shower, living and dining area, full kitchen, huge windows and ceilings... My only complaint would be lack of exhaust fan in the bathroom. The staff were SOOOOO friendly and helpful, free beer and wine 5:30-6:30, free cookies and milk 8-10, great room service not horribly overpriced, outstanding free breakfast ("real" eggs, sausage, oatmeal, etc), bar, lounge area with pool table and library nook... I didn't want to go home!

title: “Surprisingly Fantastic”
text: This hotel is so much nicer than expected, although I knew it would be convenient for the sight-seeing I was anticipating. The rooms were huge, there were always lots of fresh towels, it had a complete kitchen, and as a bonus, a washer and dryer close to the bathroom. The hot continental breakfast was varied enough that each morning we had something a little different, but always good. The staff was helpful and friendly, as was everybody we met in Chicago. We had a great time, and felt the hotel stay made everything just about perfect!

title: “Amazing Hotel in a Great Location!”
text: Stayed at the Alexis from December 7-9 2011 and enjoyed everything about it. Large, clean room and friendly, attentive staff. I would absolutely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Seattle.

author.location: New York, New York, United States

title: “Great time at the Tremont!”
text: We arrived late at night. Our door lock battery was dead. Liz was extremely nice and helpful. She gave us a free upgrade for the inconvenience. We had a great view and nice room. Extremely clean, perfect location, and charming! It is an older hotel with slow elevators, but it wasn't a big deal. The location being next to so many food and shopping options was perfect for us! I would definitely return!!

title: “Fabulous Service!!”
text:
I had not been to NYC in 30 some years, so I was quite surprised to see how much Times Square had changed. I found the area to be quite friendly, reasonably clean, and safe. Nice surprise!
 The staff at the Staybridge, from the moment we arrived, was nothing short of fantastic! We had ridden motorcycles for 12 hours in 85 degree weather and I am sure we looked like heathens when we arrived at the hotel.
 However, Louis, was extremely helpful and courteous and found "Jamie" to help us with luggage and finding the rest of our party. I cannot tell you how much we appreciated him!!!He walked down the block with me to find my husband so we didn't have to lug our bags all the way back from the parking garage. He was uncommonly helpful, and very nice and friendly. 
 My only concern with Jamie is he has never been on a Harley! Management would do well to repay his professional demeanor and excellent service with arranging a ride on the back of a nice new Ultra Classic. I am not kidding.
 I also found the people at the desk to be very friendly, engaging, and professional. I would absolutely stay here again. I felt like I was leaving new friends by the time we left.

title: “Surprisingly good stay”
text:
After reading other reviews, I was hesitant to stay at the Omni. However, with many other locations booked and the reasonable price ($90 per night), I decided to take the risk.
The hotel is located outside of the downtown and SoCo area. However, with a car the drive to central Austin, Hill Country, and the airport is quick and easy.
Several reviewers commented on the noise level and I will confirm that the hotel is not located on a quiet street - it is right alongside large highways and roadways. There is highway noise. If you're looking for a very quiet spot, this isn't for you. However, the noise wasn't unbearable and I had no trouble sleeping.
As for the rooms and the amenities, this is not a luxury hotel but a solid 3 1/2 start place. The rooms were comfortable, the pool was fine, the workout area always had machines available.
Finally, I have to remark on the wonderful staff. Whenever I had questions the people were really helpful. There is a shuttle that brings you to the airport which was a great convenience. The staff did go out of their way - I had a mishap at the airport and they were very helpful.
Overall, I would recommend this hotel and would stay again.

title: “BEST PRICE AND SERVICE”
text: We enjoyed our stay because of nice staff and good location of the property. The price is reasonable for DC. We stayed in room on the parking side and it is very quit. The bus #70 is across the street and it will take to the downtown and national mall.

title: “Decent Hotel in the Heart of the Mag Mile”
text:
I used to live in Chicago for 10 years so staying at a hotel in my town is a little strange. With the exception of the Westin on Michigan, I don't know what the other hotels in Chicago are like and cannot make a fair comparison. With that said, the Park Hyatt itself was very nice, but I was a little disappointed in the rooms b/c growing up in Chicago, I always heard people talk about how fancy the rooms are. 
My husband and I got a king looking west with pretty decent city views. I'm not sure the room is worth the price, but if you want to be close to the shopping on Michigan and a cab's ride from State Street, this is an fine hotel. Nothing will blow you away, but then again, the hotel gives you nothing to complain about. The best part of the stay for me was the food. Our cheese and wine tray was superb, and the breakfast at NoMi was excellent.

title: “Trendy hotel with Great View & Location”
text: I prefer this hotel to the W Hotel City Center. The rooms seem slightly bigger and many provide a great view of the Lake. It is also convenient to Michigan Avenue and Streeterville nightlife. It was a comfortable stay and I would stay here again for the right price. The Acura car service is a nice amenity. The only negative was that the hotel lobby and elevators always seemed crowded - a lot of people like this hotel for the nightlife and partying, so don't stay here if you want a more serene atmosphere.

title: “Extraordinarily Chic, Cool, and Comfortable!”
text: This has now become my new New York City Hotel! This hotel has done everything right. Location, design, decor, service, amenities--perfect. From our welcome to our departure, we were treated superbly during our 3-night stay. My 2 granddaughters (ages 6 and 3) were treated like princesses and they cannot wait to return. Two weeks ago, we had all stayed at a 5-star hotel in Beverly Hills, which was quite nice; however, had we stayed there AFTER our Trump Soho experience, we would have been a little disappointed, to say the least. The icing on the cake was our incredible view of the Macy's 4th of July Fireworks from our fabulous suite. Our special thanks go to Kensa, for her gracious and professional manner.

title: “Not a Hilton you'd expect”
text: My teen daughter and teen nephew stayed at the Hilton on the first weekend of August 2006. We Had a 22nd fl suite with 2 bathrooms. The check in was great and courteous and we enjoyed the interior beauty of this Chicago landmark. The linens were soft and the pillows dreamy with super comfortable beds. The location to the Field Museum and Millineum Park is minutes away. Only a couple of small concerns that I can say and it is when a bathroom is cleaned by the staff they could take the time to wipe off the grime from the light switch covers, and remove the black mold from the shower curtain, a little gross. Also when we checked in around 6 p.m. and we were on our floor to get to our room, we had to somewhat dodge the food trays left along the floor from the other suites. We went out for the evening and arrived after 11 p.m. and the trays were not taken away. The next morning I wanted to express my concerns at the front desk and there was no way we would get thru the line ups before 30 minutes. For the location I would recommend to stay but the cleanliness is a concern.

title: “Great location, amazing hotel”
text: Booked this using Marriott points, so cannot comment on the price. Loved the location, especially the fact that it is connected to the Mall. Use the parking lot downstairs and get it validated by the hotel - it is very convenient. Used the pool with my son - he loved it. Nothing to complain about.

title: “Good but could improve”
text:
First of all, the location is very good on the 8th Street close to Times Square. The room had comfortable beds, a workdesk, free Internet Access and a flat TV. 
But there is also some negative stuff. The staff at the service center and the small shop did seem to be rather tired and bored. There was also construction work nearby with loud sound between 9 AM and 6 PM. The bathroom was functional but really need some remodeling now.

title: “Nice upgrades in room including turn down service, chocolate and fruit in the morning.”
text: Compared to the Peabody the only other 4 star in town this is equal in quality. More modern and smaller hotel. Room was actually nicer, but misses the historical aspect and a bit further of a walk from everything. Well worth it!

title: “Horrible Hotel”
text:
Because we have children, I was looking for a family hotel and chose this one as it was close to the Wharf. The entire experience was horrible - I booked a King room with a sofa bed and they sent me (along with tons of luggage) to the wrong room and then finally gave me the room I requested after badgering the manager. The bell hops were not very friendly and the front desk staff was a joke. Having laundry facilities means $2 washers & dryers in the back of the parking garage and its closed at 10:00 PM. The rooms were very old and not very clean. 
The sofa bed was so old and horrible that my son wound up sleeping the King bed with my husband and I. Thank goodness we brought our own crib for our daughter - would hate to see what the hotel would have given me. The entire facility was very worn. Upon checkout they did not ask me for my parking pass, so when I thought I was done and could drive away - they held my car "hostage" in the garage while I went back upstairs to wait in line again.... Very bad deal and not a very good price either. Lots better choices around the Wharf.

title: “Snotty and Overpriced; arrogant staff”
text:
I've stayed at Vitale 3 times. The usual decline in service and experience after the first year post-opening is happening here too.
The aromatheraphy bath products that made the shower seem so luxurious in days gone by are no longer from Fresh Corp....they're now generic flavorless gels from some innofensive and unknown maker...clearly cutting costs.
The port cochere where you enter the lobby is now home to 20 flies mating.
I didn't enjoy waiting 10 minutes for the valet to get my car. But I really didn't enjoy listening to the remaining 2 valets (one of which seemed to be the lead) share stories about the hot girls they wanted to bed and showing each other pictures of these girls on their iPhones.
There's a feeling like you'd better not touch anything in the room or else a charge would apply to your account....for instance, a personal oxygen can placed in the bathroom discreetly advises you that there will be a $16 charge. If you turn on the TV, you have to dig through the 7 major menu sections of pay content ($20 for a movie) before you can get out to the local news (last option on the menu) and I never did find CNN, MSNBC, or MTV...rooms don't seem to have full cable.
And then there's the lovely matter of the small card folded discretely in the envelope with the extra room key which states that they are honored to charge your room account an extra dollar to support some local state funded/run park...unless you get down to the front desk and opt out of their scheme. Very sneaky, very tacky...and this on top of a nearly $300 per night rate. Felt very much like a poor person was nickle and diming me to death and that I should pay attention to every piece of written matter in my room lest I inadvertently miss a fee clause in my interaction with it and be levied a surcharge for not bringing my lawyer with me to protect me from the hotel's sad revenue generating sneakiness. This last bit with the $1 that you had to opt-out really ruined my sense that the hotel was a hospitality experience...felt like I was just there to be pumped.
Also, don't get the Bay view rooms...they're mostly views of a building across the street and there's a 20-something's lounge on that whole side of the building whose music and drunken expense account partyers you can hear until 1AM. 
Vitale is located at one of the lowest elevations in San Fran...the sewer drains outside the building often smell of stale sewer. Unfortunately or coincidentally, my bathroom smelled of the same stale sewer, but this may have been a mold problem from the cutout in the glass shower wall intended for turning on the shower, which however also allows a good rain shower on the whole toilet by the end of your shower....go potty before you shower or you'll need to towel off again after using the toilet...which explains the funky smell in there.
Oh, and $45 a night for parking....
Watch your back with these people...they'll try to charge for more things that you'd think.

title: “Short stay at the Grand Hyatt”
text:
We stayed at this hotel from August 23rd till 27th , 2011.
The main entrance was still under renovation and lots of people lingering outside the main entrance.
The check in was very good, comparable to most 4 stars hotel.
Internet is chargeable at a cost of about US$ 14.00 a day (24 hours period)
TV programes was lousy. Room was very spacious.
Room service was excellent.
Location was fantastic, just next door to the Grand Central Station.
Lots of food stalls ib there and some were close by.
Didn't eat at the hotel as it was still under renovation.
There was a restaurant on the ground floor, didnt try that either.
DO NOT, i repeat , DO NOT ASK the hotel to book you a TAXI, i was told by the conceige that a taxi would cost me US$ 220.00 to go to the Cruise Ship terminal which was less than 15 miles away.
I hailed a cab from opposite the hotel and it only cost me US$ 27 including toll.
I couldn't be bothered to complaint to the hotel management about that silly piece of advice.
My advice, if you need to travel alot on subways, trains.buses, BUY a one WEEK ticket at a cost of US29.00 
It is worth every penny cost a single trip would cost you $2.25
you can buy multiple journey trips in one card and also for as many person as you like. You will need ot buy it from a clerk who man the booth near the subway entrance.
They usually accept cash only.
also, NO newspaper for hotel guest. 
Will I stay again? Yes if it is a good deal. BOOK early and you will get the best rates.
I paid US$258 per nite and booked 4 to 5 months in advance. If you book last mint , expect to pay between $ 360 to $ 400 a room.

title: “Nice Airport Property-Quality Marriott!”
text:
Stayed at this property with my wife for one night before an early AM flight. Won this property on Priceline which I was very pleased about. Have stayed here before and enjoyed our stay then, as much as this time.
Arrived very late so didn't get to experience anything extra at the property. However on previous stays enjoyed the pool (indoor very nice) and the lobby bar also very nice. The lobby bar when we checked in at midnight was packed. Very busy, but I view that as a good sign.
Check in was incredibly quick, with very nice folks working. We stayed on the lower floor all the way in the back of the property, which is to be expected for a Priceline win. Room was typical Marriott quality so was not disappointed at all. Was not bothered by any noise or door slamming throughout our short stay. Checked out very early and hopped on the 5:45 complimentary shuttle Shuttle leaves every 30 minutes which works great for the short trip to Seatac.
There is not much super close to this property besides a 7-11 convenience store, so plan accordingly. 
I would for sure stay at this property again for a quick overnight stay. Stay here with confidence. Great job as usual Marriott.

title: “Great Luxury City Hotel”
text:
Hotel is part of a building complex consisting of a multiplex movie theater, fitness center and some retail stores. Once finding the entrance, as it is on a small side street surrounded by many one-way blocks, we were greeted with a warm and welcoming reception.
The hotel is newly built and very polished as one would expect at a Ritz Carlton. Staff was very friendly and very accommodating with any of our requests. We were always addressed by our name and the housekeeping staff went above and beyond our expectations. Even having my children's favorite candy waiting in the room upon return from a day sightseeing. We stayed in a suite that was very comfortable, the bathroom was overly spacious and furnishings were high quality. Very quiet at night so no trouble sleeping. If possible try to stay on club level as you have access to lounge which provides daily continental breakfast (excellent fresh fruits), light snacks in afternoon and complimentary cocktails in evening.
The fitness center and spa are not run by hotel but rather a large chain. So you basically leave the hotel from the elevator and gain access through the building complex. Fitness center was one of the largest I have been to with every machine imaginable including basketball and racquetball courts. Be warned though the pool inside is just a lap pool, not for kids to play.
As far as dining , the restaurant was still under construction, so we only experienced the bar which seemed to get an after work crowd but still very cozy and pleasant.
Overall we had an enjoyable three day stay, felt the accommodations were excellent and would recommend the Ritz as a good value for a luxury city hotel.

title: “Dream resort for kids free vacation”
text: My husband and I spent a week vacation on this resort and it was way, way beyond our expectations! Everything was tasteful and upscaled, from the Italien gardens with all the colors ( we were there in March), to the pool area where you can just relax and wait for the great flat bread or drinks to be served by your chair. The dinner and breakfast tastes sinfull, and was close to other attractions. Every time we think back on our best vacation this place is first on our list! And don't miss the Yoga classes weekend morning, outdoors, on the terrace and with Camelback Mountain view!!!

title: “Fantastic Priceline Stay”
text:
We got a lovely 4* room for $71/per night. The hotel was perfectly wonderful--clean, pretty rooms, great service, excellent location.
We are big fans of the Westin Heavenly Bed, and the Renaissance bed we had was just as good. Our room was spotless and fresh, and more importantly, available at 10:30am. We had arrived after a nightmare red-eye from Seattle, and were expecting only to check our bags with the bellman, but the staff assured us a room was waiting for us! We went straight to bed, and slept great!
Room service was delicious and prompt. Starbucks in the lobby was a real plus for 2 Seattleites! We also enjoyed the lounge, although the Cosmopolitan I had was pretty sweet--but strong!
The staff was helpful and courteous. This was so worth the price...in fact, it was worth much more than what we paid.
Location is between the Chinatown and Convention metro stops--a bit of a walk if you have lots of luggage or aren't comfortable walking 2-3 city blocks. But it's also right on the Circulator Bus Route to Georgetown and the corridor there. Very convenient! The area is up and coming with regards to nightlife, and there are several hot restaurants and nightclubs within walking distance.
Seriously, you can't go wrong with this hotel--I would recommend it to anyone.

title: “Perfect Hotel! Perfect Location!”
text: I stayedv at the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square for 2 nights while on vacation in new York. The Hotel is located just in the center of the theatre district, so there is nothing far for you to walk and enjoy what ever you are lokking for. The room is like any othre Hilton garden Inn, fair size, refrigarator, perfect and comfort beds, desk and bathroom with all the necessary staff. The staff are very helpfull. We arrived very early, around 7 oclock in the morning and we had to wait not more than 3 hours for uor room. We left our laggage at the storage room and went out for an early tour. The price for the room was around $200 a night, which is about half the average in this area. On the other night we went to the mamma Mia at the garden theatre, located one block from the hotel. We bought the tickets at the TKTS office for 40% off the regular price. It was a great show. We had only 2 nigts, so we took the daily bus tour, for $44 each. If you are short in time and want to see the important places, take the bus tour. You can't go wrong with this hotel. It's location, service and price making it Best Value for the Manhattan visitor.

title: “Renovated”
text: I just wanted to post that I was satisfied with my experience at this Motel 6. I read the reviews and was very leary about staying at the hotel. However, it was a last minute reservation and everything near Columbus was either booked or terribly expensive. This hotel was recently remodeled. My room was clean with a new flat screen TV. The bed was comfortable and the internet access quick and easy. I was pleased by the facility as a value priced hotel. Front desk was helpful.

title: “Very Restful”
text: I always look forward to spending a night in the Doubletree San Jose. The beds and rooms are very comfortable and I always get a great night of sleep.

title: “Hotel Stay”
text: It was a nice hotel and within walking distance to Old Town. The room were nice and everyone was friendly. I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Excellent!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel between 23rd and 28th August on the back of Trip Advisor reviews and it really lived up to the hype.
Nothing was too much trouble for the staff there, from the concierge, reception staff, maids and waiters. Absolutely first rate service.
Had an executive room overlooking St Patrick's Cathedral which was fantastic and also granted access to the executive lounge. As others have noted, this was well worth it. Breakfast, lunch, afternoon snacks, evening nibbles and free evening bar all made it worth while. Especially if you're out and about locally and need a quick break back at the hotel! Well worth the extra money and would strongly recommend it.
Hotel is perfectly positioned for fifth avenue shops and only a short walk from Central Park, the Empire State and Times Square, plus pick up points for the many city bus tours.
Didn't eat or drink in the hotel restaurant and bar (the executive lounge did all this!) so couldn't comment but everything else spot on.

title: “Best thing about San Jose”
text: We travelled to San Jose for a football game and left impressed. Driving south we had no problem finding the hotel. Bellman was at the entrance to assist with bags. Check in was fast. We even were put in our room hours early which was great. Room service was promt and food was warm. lobby bar very lively on A friday night with live music and many locals that came there for there for the dancing. loads of fun. Surrounding area has many dining places to explore as we did. Can't wait to have an excuse to visit again.

title: “Loved the Westin”
text:
Better late then never with my review, but because we had such a wonderful stay, I had to get my review on the site.
My sister, a friend and myself went to NYC for a girl's weekend. I booked online through Orbitz and got a great rate for the Westin at $359/night. We arrived around 11am and although we couldn't check in at that time, the hotel staff was very accomodating in holding our luggage and promised a room would be ready by 3pm. So we went for lunch and shopped a bit. We arrive a little after 3pm and as promised, our room was ready. The room was amazing! Beautiful marble bathroom, complimentary robe and slippers and a wonderful view of the Empire State Building. Everything was very clean and the beds were comfortable. Although we only stayed for one night, it was a very relaxing one. I would highly recommend the Westin for anyone staying in NY. A first-class hotel!

title: “Great hotel, great location and great service”
text:
I came to Chicago for business October 24th. I searched all of downtown for a good deal. Everything seemed to be so expensive or gross and scary. I came across the Days Inn in Lincoln Park and found it to be fairly close to downtown. It is a hike from Ohare but fairly easy to the city. There is plenty of restaurants and stores within walking distance. The rooms are quiet and very clean. All white bed linens. Not the biggest room (queen size bed) but it is exceeds your expectations of a Days Inn. The bathroom is very clean and nice. I found the front desk to be very helpful and friendly.
For my first trip into a big city alone, the hotel made me feel very safe, secure and comforted. An unhappy hotel experience was the last thing I needed. I would highly recommend and encourage others to stay here.

title: “Excellent choice for the price”
text: It's a great place, well-priced place to stay. Room is large by SF standards and well-appointed. Convenient location. I highly recommend it.

title: “Nice Hotel, pricey Internet”
text:
Overall a good hotel. Comfortable bed, good size room for NYC and a nice bathroom. Rooms are oddly shaped but functional.
Internet is $17.00 for 24 hours which is ridiculous but sadly becoming the norm.
Breakfast is not included but you are so close to everything you can grab something at one of the 3 Starbucks around the block.
Rooms are quiet, staff decent. Awesome location.

title: “Good hotel with slow elevators”
text: The hotel is clean and nice, with comfortable beds and kind staff. There is no bar, they do not serve any alcohol and the elevators are slow. The neighborhood toward convention center is OK, but in the opposite direction it is a little scary. Well, all said but that on busy hours you may expect some hot water problem. The window blind would not let you have a dark room in the day time. So many cons? well not really, still satisfied for a business trip.

title: “Ultra convenient and accomodating hotel”
text:
It was a fantastic central San Fran location. Trolley rides were just across the street. You could catch the BART (SF train system) to and from SFO by walking a mere 5 minutes/2 blocks. Very convenient. $10 taxi ride down to Fisherman's Wharf where you can pick up an Alcatraz Ferry tour. 
The rooms were really nice and comfortable. Nice bedding and view. 2Q bed rooms were large and it was nice to have a vanity/dressing area right outside the bathroom. We didn't get to eat at this hotel for breakfast or any other meal. 
You don't need a car in SF. Transportation is everywhere. 
Definitely would recommend The Handlery!

title: “W Seattle”
text:
If you like the W experience, you'll feel right at home in the Seattle property. It's always dark and moody to convey a sense of sophisptication, but it's still a quality upscale business hotel beneath all the branding. The corner suites are very comfortable, with amenities I actually use (adequate deskspace, DVD player, a bathtub large enough to bathe in). 
The gym is small but features quality equipment unlike so many other business hotels. The bar is actually a happening hot spot, and I feel comfortable lounging in the hotel lobby with the free WiFi. The attached restaurant, Earth & Ocean, is overrated and quite expensive. 
Like most Ws, the staff are all pretty young hipsters, who nonetheless provide (for the most part) friendly service. I woud highly reccomend the hotel for those who are not bothered by the air of exclusivity that the brand projects, particularly if you can get good rate. In my experience, it has wildly fluctuated throughout the year for both 2006 and 2007.

title: “Lots to do out the front door”
text:
We stayed at this Holiday Inn as a concession to late booking on Valentine's Day weekend and it became one of the best ideas we ever had. 
Pros:
-Not your traditional Holiday Inn decor
-Pillow menu! Pick your favorite kind of pillow!
-Best of all: this Holiday Inn has a little company in their lobby that can rent you kayaks, bicycles, or segways. We rented a double kayak and were on our way in minutes on the lake. The value of having all of that right there for the weekend was fantastic.
-Lakefront path right outside the door. We enjoyed running and walking up and down the lakefront, enjoyed the parks, and watching the crew teams. Felt like we lived there!
-Free shuttle to airport and downtown (if you don't feel like walking). The shuttle's priority is going to the airport so the one out of two times that we inquired about it, it was busy. Not a big deal because it's an easy walk downtown anyway.
-Movie theatre in the hotel if you're bored. Didn't use it but after returning late one night there was a group of guys enjoying popcorn and the big leather chairs. Not bad if you don't feel like going out! Although you're in Austin...
Cons that are not really cons:
- Bathroom was still your typical hotel bathroom with the crappy soap- who cares!
-Getting into the hotel parking lot is a little tricky, but after the first time you'll be fine. It shouldn't deter you from staying here. That's stupid.
- Walk into downtown: 10 minutes. Awesome actually and not hilly. We're from Chicago and we walk everywhere so it wasn't a big deal. We switched hotels on Monday because my husband was there for work and the company was paying for it - Sheraton on 11st St. Not really closer to anything than this Holiday Inn and a lot more hilly to get to and from the downtown area. Plus, although it may look more luxurious, it didn't have the little perks that the Holiday Inn had.

title: “Lovely place”
text: I love small boutique hotels, this is the place for me, the edwardian is a quaint and lovely hotel. The minute I walked in the lobby I felt at home, it has a lot of caracter, it is a typical small boutique hotel, my room is cozy, very clean, I was surprised to see a large bathroom, don't expect a large typical motel room. The front desk people are helpful and are very good with directions. The other plus for this hotel is the location it is perfect for public transportation. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great location and very responsive staff - Felt right at home!”
text: Yes, it's an older hotel and may not be the finest luxury hotel in the city, but if you don't care too much about giant plazma TVs in every room and state-of-the-art faucets, this is the place to stay in downtown San Antonio. Walk out the door and you're twenty steps from the Alamo, across the street from the River Walk, right next door to the the Rivercenter Mall and an easy walk to the Convention Center and Alamodome. Absolutely the best location of any downtown hotel. Location, location, location, right? But there's a whole lot more. Namely, great service. Bill Brendel, the General Manager, and his unpretentious, down-to-earth staff made us feel right at home. You get the feeling of staying at a nice bed and breakfast rather than at a sterile, cold hotel. The free breakfast is a big plus. And, oh yes, the Crockett is very, very reasonable pricewise - even during high demand times like Fiesta San Antonio or when large conventions hit downtown. I'm trying to think of a negative, but I just keep coming up with more positives. Here's another positive. They have a very large, secure parking lot. Just pull up to the portico and a nice, unpretentious (have I used that word before in this review?) valet will take care of everything. Just leave your car in the lot for you entire stay and walk to wherever you need to be in the downtown area.

title: “Ditto What they said!”
text: Thanks to other travelers who gave full marks to this property- It is indeed a great place to stay. The staff here has NOT forgotton they are in the hospitaltiy business. 4 guys in town for a convention, we took two rooms and all was in order. Easy walk to convention center, breakfast was very convenient, free coffee in the lobby, prompt advisement of faxes received, just a real nice property that has their staff well trained, professional and human! Extra effort by Jim the bartender in divining our dining needs and (Ryan,Bryan?) in making reservations for us. Mo's Steakhouse very good, Mikado pretty good, Shula's way too expensive. Self parking $12, with in/out privilages. Many other hotels that charge far north of $ 139/night could take a lesson from this group.

title: “wonderful stay”
text: we had a great time and a great stay at the Villa florence. from the time we checked in with Cora to the time we left saying goodby to Clarence the Concierge who really gave us great recommendation, it was by those recommendations that we found ourselves having a great time in SF. the rooms at the Villa Florence are very cozy, and clean, at check in we were ask if we wanted a quiet room or a room facing the street, this area is very busy and often nosiy, we choose a room facing the street, living in NOLA the noise was not a problem for us, every night one of the street musician would play Sun Rise Sun Set, this was heard throughtout our room, how romantic!!!! if you are a person that like peace and quiet please do not get a room facing the street. this was our first vist to SF, and what an experience. the hotels location is great, right in Union Square, within walking distance to great shopping, wonderful resturants and plenty of good coffee stops. the cable car runs in front of the hotel, and the ticket booth to ride the cable car is located only 2 blocks away on market and powell, you really would want to purchase a pass, the pass would allow you to hop on and off other wise it would cost you $5.00 everytime you get on, this car will take you to the Wharf. at the Wharf we took a Trolley Tour which was a great way to see SF. we went to the City of Sausalito by way of ferry, the ferry ride and city was wonderful. hats off to VF and Clarence for a wonderful stay and great trip

title: “Fantastic location, run down hotel, poor service!”
text:
If location is your biggest concern this is the hotel for you. Just 1 minute walk from Powell St. station and a starting location for the fabulous cable cars, right in the heart of the shopping district and only 10 minutes walk (uphill) from Union Sq.
However (and it is a big one) the hotel is scruffy and although the room was visibly clean, don't look under the bed! My view was of the roof of the next building and it was difficult to sleep due to the constant noise of the building's air-con which was directly outside of my window.
The staff were not helpful and spoke poor english. Requests I made on booking were completely ignored, with no apology. Finally DO NOT rely on a reception wake-up call, all three mornings they forgot!

title: “Best Hotel in Seattle”
text: My dad, sister and myself stayed for 4 nights in May, and were very impressed. My dad had a queen city view room, with a huge bathroom. The room itself was lovely, but would have been tight with more than one person. Not much of a view from that side of the hotel. My sister and I were across the hall, in a delux and OMG the view was amazing.. Top floor with a 3 sided window overlooking the market and all of Elliot Bay. Our room was huge and so was our bath..Love everything about this hotel. Unassuming staff, amazing sheets, coffee in room, great products, and wonderful restaurants right next to the hotel..If you are going to Seattle and want the best hotel there, this is it...

title: “Townhouse Delight”
text: If you want a true New York experience without sacrificing any of the niceties of hotel ammenities, this is the place to stay. This classic townhouse is situated on a quiet street, but is within a short walk of Central Park, the 72nd street subway, and an abundance of taxis on the Avenues. We stayed in 'The Library', which is the entire top floor. The rooms were well appointed and lacked for nothing. We have stayed at condos with minimal accesories like dishes, but the Inn provides everything you could think of or want including food, wine, snacks, glasses, pots, pans, etc. etc. Even a washer/dryer! Since this is a 4 unit Inn, so you have complete privacy. But the owners were always available when called. We were entirely delighted.

title: “Train, boats and planes”
text:
If you like the sound of trains, boats and planes when you are trying to sleep then this is the place for you. The hotel is in a perfect location for local transport, good eateries and seafront views. 
The breakfast offered (costing $10) in the Elephant and Castle leaves something to be desired compared with other American breakfast food outlets. The eggs were great but the bacon and fried potatoes were cold and possibly cooked about 2 hours previous. We had to request a reheating of the food.

title: “hgi very satisfactory”
text: stayed for 3 nights with last night in sofitel which i will review shortly.location is excellant with jewel shop and subway stop across road and mag mile around corner.room good size with fridge etc and clean.staff always helpful.weber grill attached to it lively-breakfast average.hgi not luxurious but very comfortable and well priced.fridge in room a bit noisy so we plugged it out overnight!in summary no hesitation in recomending hgi.

title: “Will not get the full NYC experience staying here.....”
text:
I normally don't write reviews, but I felt like I actually had a lo of pros and cons to share about this hotel. 
PROS
-right across the street from the subway! take the subway people, it will be your best friend. I mastered the subway to anywhere i needed to go. Including battery park to see the statue of liberty. 
-Housekeeping left a message letting me know when and where i could reach them since i had a "do not disturb sign". Made it very easy to get my room cleaned later. 
-nice welcome with a cookie, adds a little extra. 
-Location is close to 5th ave. took minutes to walk to saks, NBA store, gucci... etc
-stayed in many NYC hotels... was roomy compared to most
-business center... slow computers but printing available... that's expected though
-free wireless in lobby only
CONS
-raining when we got there and bell hop was NO WHERE TO BE FOUND. 
-went outside later that day asked bell hop to hail a cab... told us very rudely that we were just going to have to wait for a while because he was busy. 
- front desk ladies... you have some good ones, some bad ones... the ones that work around 10pm were the most crabby and gave short answers... the early morning/day ladies were soo nice and helpful. very very impressed with their service.
-WORST THING... THE FEMALE CONCIERGE LADY.... i've never met someone so rude, unhelpful, and annoyed by her job. I refused to go back to her. Such attitude and could offer no advice.
- molding in bathroom, tub had cracks and was very old.
they mainly need to work on their customer service. It ruins the whole trip having rude people assist you. for the price you pay for the hotel though, it's relatively cheap in NYC standards.... and thats what you get... cheap service
if you are absolutely on a budget, stay here. in NY you're out and about most of the time. If you can spare an extra 150 or 200 and upgrade even a little, YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT. I guess the only thing i really liked about the hotel was the location to everything... but trust me.... there are other hotels with good locations and better service. For those of you just thinking that I had a bad encounter with the service, trust me, you will feel cheated out of your NYC experience staying at this place.

title: “Dramatic, Gorgeous and Unique”
text:
The NoMad has a dramatic, classy and timeless feel. It's old Parisian yet so fresh and updated. In the rooms, its rich, dark leather headboards and dark wooden tables contrast beautifully against the luxuriously plump, snow white linens. The gorgeous bed blankets are saturated in rich hues. The hardwood floors look and feel like the authentic, antique planks you'd find in old European hotels. On the floor is a beautiful rug (again) with a special antiquity about it. In the bathroom are white and gray marble counters, shiny faucets and mosaic floors all throughout. The website photos are exactly as pictured but I've added a couple more. The Parlor Restaurant (and there are several areas to eat in this hotel) was outstanding!! This Swiss chef has to be one of the most acclaimed in NYC. I don't think I've ever had duck cooked so exquisitely ... yum. The four of us had a couple of meals there and everything was just great--every time. 
Unfortunately, the NoMad's service was not that great--not terribly bad, but no where near what it needs to be. Some expert hospitality training would do wonders. One other minor, yet rather frustrating aspect of this hotel is that the lighting in the Lobby, The Library and The Atrium was too dark. We were not the only ones to notice this. Every other eating area was just right--intimate, private and very lovely. 
At night we took a cab. During the day it felt pretty safe to walk everywhere, but it's in a run down area at 28th and Broadway. And though within just a few blocks you can be in some really great areas of Manhattan, the actual neighborhood itself is not desirable and it doesn't feel that safe. I really hope this area of the Flatiron District can rise up to the standard of this great hotel. 
This is a perfectly wonderful and gorgeous boutique hotel (though too pricey for the neighborhood and the average service), but overall it was a treat for us to be guests for 4 days.

title: “Location & service excellent, perfect for a quick trip to NYC”
text:
I first must clarify that I am a Starwood Preferred Member. I was traveling to New York on very short notice and prefer to stay at W or Westin hotels. Although the online reservation system was showing availability, I was having difficulty booking my dates. I called Starwood Preferred and received excellent service - they were even able to secure 2 nights for me with my Starwood points over a weekend during the ridiculously busy month of December in Manhattan. I cannot say enough good things about the Starwood Preferred staff. 
The hotel was excellent during our stay, but again was free for us with the use of my points. I would not have paid the $550 rack rate for the nights I was there, but I wouldn't pay $550 for a night at any hotel in New York! That's just me. However, Christmastime in New York is always ridiculously expensive so it is to be expected to pay that much. 
The front desk staff was very friendly, accommodating and willing to help with whatever we needed. Our room was not yet available, but they called my cell phone the moment that it opened up. The bell staff was integral in providing us with cabs and umbrellas to get to our destinations - we visited during a massive rain-changing-to-snow storm. 
The lobby area and both bars were lively at all times of the day, which is something I like - I was there for vacation so I felt a great sense of community and fun with my fellow travelers enjoying the common spaces along with myself and my guest. The hotel's location is perfect for visiting many tourist destinations and makes for some great walking around the city. 
Rooms are small - but this is New York, so it wasn't unexpected. More like a boutique hotel than a "typical" hotel. The bed and shower of course are beyond comfortable. I appreciated the eclectic decor inside the rooms. 
All in all, I would highly recommend this hotel for travelers to New York looking for a little more of an upscale, young, trendy stay, especially if it is more affordable around non-holiday time.

title: “Great as usual!”
text:
As always I was totally satisfied with my stay at Red Roof/ Manhattan. I requested a room facing the street and although it can be a bit loud due to traffic late at night, I always request a room facing the street to enjoy the "view."
I arrived hours prior to check-in time and was given a key to my room. The room was very neat and clean. If you ever need anything for your room just ask one of the housekeepers; they are quite friendly and helpful! 
This stay was my first time trying the breakfast buffet. The bagels and donuts were fresh and I was glad I stopped in for a quick snack.
I have been staying here for years and have yet to be disappointed!

title: “Central Location”
text:
Stayed here for 8 nights so I feel we gave this hotel a good shot. Our check in was smooth even though we had to do it ourself. This might put some people off as it is similar to airport self check in - hit and miss. As for the room - overall quite pleasantly decorated but missing an item I would consider essential - coffee maker. The 24 hour market in the lobby comes to the rescue but I guess it's the nuisance factor here. The pillows were numerous but way too soft as was the bed. I don't understand why so many hotels are using pillow top beds - they sag on the sides where people constantly sit. (I am a firm mattress advocate.)
The hotel is very busy - every 2nd evening there seemed to be an event in the lobby or the ballroom. These were big affairs and they impacted on the elevators and added to the general noise level within the hotel.
The location is the reason we decided to stay here - being right at Grand Central was the deciding factor and the subway was well used by us.

title: “Don't Judge a Book by its Cover”
text:
Made reservation online, 2 weeks ahead, and saved a bunch by joining Choice Club, paying in advance - hint#1. Flew in from NC and we are only here one night - needing a place to sleep and adjust to time zone before hitting the 'real' part of out trip. NOT located in the best part of Denver - off major highway, close to what you need - restaurant on site serves less than average food with great service and there is a bar. Outdoor pool, smoking and non smoking rooms, free wi-fi - rooms have refrig and micro and in room coffee. There is also coffee in the lobby 24/7. 
Free excellent breakfast
The hotel is older but recently remodeled and well kept - room was average size, clean and well maintained - for $62.00 we were really pleased.
Would stay here again for a night inna heart beat -

title: “Great little hotel in a fabulous location”
text: This hotel is in a great location, tucked away but right in the middle of all the action of the gaslamp district. The service was good, fast, and friendly. A great place to stay if you want a convenient location, a quirky historic feel, and don't mind doing without amenities that a lot of the larger hotels can offer for a fee (ie. fitness center, restaurant, etc).

title: “I liked it”
text: Waterfront means you are about a mile from downtown. The WTC T-station is less than a ten minute walk and there are a few interesting places to eat int the area including Yankee Lobster and Atlantic Beer Garden which were both interesting and had pretty good food. The hotel room (king bed) was spacious with a large bath and 37" HDTV. The bed itself was huge and very comfortable as advertised. Plenty of pillows, towels etc. No complaints with housekeeping or the front desk. All the staff we encountered were extremely professional and helpful. This may sound strange, but great elevators. There are seven and not having to wait for one and being transported to the eighth floor in about five seconds was great considering the hotel was fairly full during our stay. Internet access in room is pricey but to be expected, free in lobby. I'm glad we did not have a car. I think it was at least $45 per day parking. However if you wanted a cab, there were always available out front. We did not eat in the hotel restaurant. I looked at the menu and was amazed at the prices they would charge for standard fare. They are not open for dinner and do not have Sunday brunch. The attached pub is OK. Great for a late night snack or a beer while watching the Olympics. Overall only four stars because of location and overpriced restaurants and other services.

title: “Great Location near the Presidio”
text: Very cute little place. Try to get a kitchenette. If you stay on the street, it will be noisy as Lombard is Hwy 101 at that point, going to the Golden Gate Bridge. Great shopping and dining one block over on Chestnut. convenient by bus to all the popular tourist attractions.

title: “Perfect Location - Main thing to consider when you're vacationing to New York!”
text:
This was my 4th time to NY and was the best location I have stayed in yet. Even though the interior of the rooms etc were not ideal we spent hardly any time in the room so it was perfect for somewhere to sleep and shower! I would much rather stay in an average hotel with this location rather than a nice one that is a 30 minute walk to where I want to be!
Arrived a few minutes before and check in, checked in without any problems. Although we asked for 3 rooms together (as there was 6 of us travelling) and in hindsight I wish we had just left them to book the rooms for us as we may have had one of the "nicer" rooms on the higher floors that I have read about on here. I think we were on the smoking floors as when you exited the lift you were hit by a musty smell but it wasn't too bad in the rooms and we kept the windows open while we weren't in the room. One of the lifts was being maintained each day so they could be a bit slow at times, we used the stairs once. 
We didn't actually eat in the hotel (too many places to choose from outside!) so I cannot comment on the cafe but every day it looked full.
I think that once this hotel has been fully renovated it would definitely get 5 stars from me.
Also - people cannot complain about the rooms being small, this is New York! And unless you want to pay over $600 a night for a room you can't expect to have the space.

title: “Excellent Accommodations”
text: I always try to stay in CS hotels when I travel and I must say that this is one of the best that I have seen. The breakfast was great, the spa could have been a little warmer but the pool was just right (probably around 87 degrees). The staff was friendly. The only problem was the parking, which was a little tight. If the hotel van did not park in front of the building it would be a little better. At one point the van and an employee vehicle was in front of the door for an extended period.

title: “Nice hotel we better work on the food”
text: The hotels was great from the room to the attraction for the kids. But fo the Price the food was not up to par at all.

title: “Great night !”
text: Stayed here last night.Very clean ! Nice suite, great beds ! Breakfast had plenty to offer, price was good for a metropolitan area.Friendly, helpful front desk. Microwave, fridge-couches etc. plus fast, free wifi. Only complaint-love to watch house hunters channel on tv- not available, only 27 channels and that was not one of them. All in all a good experience !

title: “Contemporary semi refurbished hotel”
text: The location of the hotel was pretty good. The beggars waiting outside the front door were something else though. A city notorious for beggars - the location of the hotel was right in the thick of them all. Quite unnerving for a 20-something woman walking alone during the day or night. The hotel appears to have had some sort of remodeling done - however parts of the room laughed at the others. Ie The main bedroom was very modern, slick plasma etc but then the bathroom was old and a bit tired-looking & cramped. No space to place any of your toiletries and barely space to swing a cat. Quite pricey for the value - we paid $166 + tax USD/nt for a king room and then about $130/nt for a Queen. Moved down to the Marina District half way through our stay and found it to be EXCELLENT. Gorgeous location in the midst of Union St & Chestnut St. Both streets are lined with little boutiques, great coffee shops, wine bars, cute little restaurants and there wasnt one beggar in sight! A short bus ride to the city if you wanted some of the city nightlife.

title: “Big on character, small on space”
text: My husband and I stayed here during a long weekend trip to San Francisco for our 2nd wedding anniversary. We chose this hotel because of its architecture and character and we were not disappointed! The building is older and has a beautiful lobby and bar area. Our room was equally well maintained, although the room was rather small and the bathroom was very small. However when we travel we do not tend to spend much time in our hotel room, so this did not bother us all that much. The staff was friendly and helpful, and the location was great...right near the action in Union Square. I'd recommend this hotel.

title: “Great Break from the every day stay!”
text: We stayed here in February for a nice night of relaxation and refuge from the busy work week.. Room was very large, clean and more than what we needed for a night away. Breakfast in the morning was a great benefit altho it a bit scarse from previous Embassy Suites that we have stayed at.Options were a bit limited but still plenty to pick from compared to other non Embassy suite properties. We had previously stayed at the Embassy Suites in Anaheim on a Disney trip and the food choices were alot more varied and lots of food available too....the afternoon reception was a nice touch also, a good margarita and snacks to boot! Will definately stay here again.....C.

title: “Fantastic hotel, amazing location”
text:
This hotel is fantastic. We got a king deluxe for $200 per night off travelzoo. I cannot understand why anyone would complain when looking at the other reviews. Room was fantastic, lovely decor and very clean. Communal areas were spotless and a wine reception was help every night in the lobby. I cannot complain about anything, I only have good things to say about the place. When I return to NYC I will definatley stay here.
Location great too, just a few blocks from Grand Central.
All in all a great hotel

title: “Wonderful staff, food, scenery”
text: This Hyatt is a bit out of the way and the furnishing is a tad dated, but its other sterling features make it worth a visit. First of all, hotel staff don't come any better than this in terms of courtesy, friendliness and efficiency. Wherever you go in this resort, someone is smiling at you. If you call any department for assistance, it arrives and quickly. Everyone goes out of their way to make your stay great. Next, the food is a solid notch above typical hotel restaurant fare. They have an outstanding "Perfect" margarita which I enjoyed on two different nights, to-die-for baby back ribs, and a succulent grilled chicken breast. My husband had the cowboy chili and said it tasted really great and was incredibly hearty with chunks of steak. Breakfast was great --fresh orange juice, good bacon, good sausage, yummy multi-grain toast and I loved their decaf. Finally, the hotel grounds are just beautiful -- Texas hill country at its best. It was so peaceful gazing out at the lovely oaks which are everywhere and the walking trail was serenity itself. A group of migrating ducks took up residence on the grounds and we enjoyed watching them at the bird feeders. Finally, you'll get a good night's sleep on the spotlessly clean linens, upscale mattress and comfy pillows. The hotel also has a well-equipped gym and a spa. If you're looking for a few days of rest in the San Antonio area, this hotel might fit your bill. Tip: for a meal you'll never forget, don't miss a lunch or dinner at the amazing restaurant, Ernesto's Gourmet, just north of I-410 and Vance Jackson on Jackson Keller. Other than our peaceful days at the Hyatt Regency Hill Country, Ernesto's was the highlight of our trip.

title: “not suitable for business travel”
text:
The hotel is average at best. The rooms are so small that there isn't room to put the luggage rack and be able to walk around. I needed to do some work but there wasn't enough room to pull out the chair from desk in order to sit down. I struggled to get the chair out from betweem the desk and the bed so I could sit on the side of the desk to work. The mini bar is so close to the bed that the door cannot be opened more than halfway. The bed and linens and cleanliness were average. I bed is very low to floor making it uncomfortable to sit on the bed and with only one desk chair there isn't any other option except to lay down.
The breakfast room is uninviting along with the buffet. Plastic furniture along with plastic and paper dishes. No room service either.

title: “Good hotel, ideally located and good service”
text: I was skeptical when I arrived at the Soho Grand, because of the average rating in trip advisor, some of the comments on the site and the fact that we already visited it some years ago and were not particularly impressed at the time. I must admit I have been pleasantly surprised. The location is ideal, right in the middle of Soho, perfect. The staff is helpful. Yes, they are gorgeous and sometimes have an attitude, so what? That's part of the charm of it. But what is new is that they are also helpful. The room is relatively small but decent, the bed is gorgeous, the room is clean and the bathroom is nice and they were nice with late check out. Now, one thing that is really bad is the breakfast. Don't even try it for one day. Totally overpriced, no buffet, and portion are for fashion people. "Swiss porridge or muesli" was a joke (some dry oat with thick yoghourt, who on earth can eat that without choking). Anyway, apart from breakfast, a good place to remember and I acknowledge the efforts they have made to make the staff less arrogant and more helpful. I would come back here.

title: “Good location downtown”
text: We have stayed at Fairmonts all over the US. This one is one of the older Fairmonts, but still very nice. We had a suite which was definitely very spacious. We notified the front desk that it was our anniversary prior to arrival, and we were greated wtih a lovely dessert sampler with Happy Anniversary written in chocolate. That was a very nice touch.

title: “Great place to stay in San Francisco”
text: My husband and I booked the Tuscan Inn Fisherman's Wharf based on the reviews we read on the computer and were not disappointed. Everything went smoothly from the moment we checked in. I loved the decor of the room and found it to be modern, calm and restful. We had a room with a King sized bed and although the room was small it was bright and very clean. The Manager's wine tasting in the lobby at 5 every evening gave guests a chance to meet and mingle. A very nice touch. It was our wedding anniversary during our stay and the Manager sent a bottle of sparkling wine to our room. That was a nice touch. The location is perfect being so close to the Wharf and Pier 39 and the Powel St. Cable cars. I only regret not staying at the Tuscan Inn for a third night as there is so much to do in the area. We traveled down the coast to Los Angeles after our stay in San Francisco and I must say that the Tuscan Inn was my favourite place to stay in California.

title: “Great hotel for San Fran Downtown/Convention Center”
text:
I would recommend this hotel for people wanting a central location in downtown SF or someone coming to SF for a convention being held at the Marcone Convention center. Nice lobby and many people to help you make plans around the city at the desk.
Stayed 6 nights in the Marriott Marquis in downtown San Francisco. King bed. Standard sized room. Nice amenities. TV location near the window was an odd location for watching from bed. I had to turn the TV about 45 degrees for a head on view.
This was a great hotel for me because of the central location. It is also 1 block from the Marcone Convention center, which was the reason for my trip to SF. Very easy walk.
Sky bar: Bar on the top floor of the hotel with amazing views of the city. No need to go anywhere else. We had all the people in our group coming to our hotel for the view. Made for a nice short walk home at the end of the night.
Very close to Market street where you can catch all kinds of mass transit including the BART or trolly or surface bus. Very convenient to get anywhere in SF. Just use google map directions and it was very easy. 3 blocks from Union Square, another nice shopping area. 
Hot tub was really big and well maintained; this was used more than a few times on my trip. Also had a lap pool and very good work out facilities.
Nearby shopping included a walgreens for incidentals and foot. The hotel was even nice enough to bring us a minifridge free of charge to keep some bottled water cool for day trips.
Did not use parking so can not comment on this service but valet is available; also self parking available on Mission street some of our friends used and might be cheaper.
CON: Not near the water or the warf; will need to do 20min walk to water (near bay bridge) or taxi/bus/trolly to the fishermans warf. The F trolly will take you right to the warf and picks up on Market street and is very easy to do.

title: “Close to Qualcomm and Clean”
text: We went to SD to see a pre-season Charger game. This hotel is close and convenient to both the stadium, restaurants and most importantly, a Target! The bed was super comfortable and the room was spotless. We've stayed at this location before and will stay here again.

title: “Good Bargain -- solid experience”
text: I have stayed at this hotel a couple of times. I think the rooms vary in terms of size and how recently they've been updated. For example, this past time my furniture was very worn and looked like it needed replacement. The reason why I would recommend this hotel is because they offer ridiculous deals sometimes -- and they are prices that are unheard of in NYC. The location is good. Staff is friendly. Biggest complaint is that the elevators suck. Totally slow. You will waste a lot of time trying to get to and from your room.

title: “Impossible to get a good night's sleep -- hotel also way understaffed”
text:
Wow, what a horrible stay. 
I stayed at the Whitehall for four nights after booking it via Hotwire, which gave it four stars.
The worst problem: No sleep. The hotel is very noisy (very old, thin windows and doors), and the heat in our room went on overdrive every night. My husband and I each woke up at least three times a night: At least once because it was 75+ degrees in our room, despite the thermostat being set in the low 60s, and a couple of times because of noise from outdoors or the hallways. 
I did complain to the front desk after a couple nights of this. The manager called my room a couple of times (during the day, when I was out), but never reached me. He did have my cell phone number, which he never attempted to call.
At one point, someone from the front desk sent up an engineer. He came up, put his hand in front of the vent, said, "It's working," and left. 
So we were stuck with a horrible room. 
I had plenty of other complaints, but they were minor. However, when added up, they made for one of the worst hotel stays I’ve had in years. Here’s a sample:
Very shabby hotel: It seemed fairly clean (although don’t use the phones in the rooms without wiping them down first – they actually smelled bad). But lots of things were falling apart. There were cracks between the windows and their frames. The water wasn’t reliably hot, and whenever our neighbor flushed his or her toilet, the water would actually stop running for a second. 
Understaffed: The staff were all very nice, but there weren’t enough of them. I had to wait in a long line when I arrived, as only one person was working at the front desk. Once I checked in, I went up to my room on the ninth floor. Key didn't work. Trudged back down, bags in tow, only to have to wait another 15 minutes in the line. Got my key fixed, went back up -- nope, still couldn't get into my room. Downstairs, another long wait, and this time a bellhop came up with me. Turned out there was a trick to opening the door -- you had to hold the handle in the down position, and THEN insert the key card. So it took me close to an hour to get into my room.
Basically, it seems like this hotel is riding on its location. It has the feeling of a place that hasn't been maintained well at all, and hasn't been invested in for many years. Many of the front desk people and bellhops were very nice, but world-class service can't make up for lack of sleep and a hotel that is shabby and falling apart.
I actually changed my travel plans and checked out a night early. It was great to finally get a full night of sleep.
Other cons: Limited room service hours. Poor fitness center.

title: “A Pleasantly Unique Experience”
text:
Was detailed to Washington DC for 30 days and needed to find a hotel that could accommodate me for that length of time. Tara McNamara, one of the hotel staff, went above and beyond to make my stay there memorable. Upon arrival I had fresh flowers and a bottle of wine in my room. Another staffer, Mannette, made sure my nightly turn down service was efficient and pleasant. The bed was extremely comfortable and the room was very quiet. Not everything was perfect. I failed to get a wake up call, because the phone wasn't working properly, but one of the hotel staff came up and knocked on my door to make sure I was awake. I also had a new phone in my room when I returned later that evening...
I know that this was not a typical hotel stay, but the service, the food and the room were all impeccable. The Mandarin Hotel staff went out of their way to make my extended stay more enjoyable and I highly recommend giving them a shot if you are in the area.

title: “Great location, nice grounds and pool but otherwise a disappointment”
text:
I was disappointed with this stay. I checked in at 2 pm and the room was not ready. The agent asked for a my phone number. I never got a call and went back after 4. The room was ready.
