The biggest problem was the room looked and felt dirty, mostly the carpet and the window shades. Gross! I was also given a room that must get many complaints. A very loud ice machine is directly outside the door. This is also a concert venue and the door opens to a view of the stage. Very loud.
What I did like were the lovely grounds and pool and the amazing bayside location. The free bike rentals were a nice treaty, too.

title: “nice”
text: The staff was very friendly. Full breakfast that was above average. The room was ok. Great location. Mall across the street. Right off I77

title: “Great value in NYC”
text: The Library Hotel is a nice value for NYC. The design is modern and comfortable and the staff is really friendly and helpful. The location was great for visiting family on the upper west side. I'll definitely stay here again.

title: “Wonderful Hotel - Fantastic Time in NY”
text:
Belvedere Hotel is a beautiful, clean and affordable hotel centrally located to everything in NY. The desk staff were incredibly professional, courteous and helpful. The bellmen were the best I've ever seen - helpful in every respect. Concierge was helpful and had wonderful suggestions. Maid service was helpful and did an impeccable job with the rooms. The only thing negative in regards to the hotel were the elevators. Very small and slow - but there is an elevator down the hall, a service elevator, that we used more often than not and then it wasn't a problem at all. Our room was roomy, beautiful, tastefully decorated, with a nice sized bathroom and kitchenette. It exceeded our expectations and we would definitely stay here again because the whole experience was just wonderful. It was our first time to NY and we couldn't have been more happy with the accommodations.
I would suggest the Hop On/Hop Off bus tours. The stop is just down the street from the hotel and it is a wonderful form of transportation because all of the stops are located near sights worth seeing. The tour guides are incredibly informative with their knowledge of the history of NY. We learned something new every time we took this bus and we had the three day/one night loop pass. 
Two of our favorite places to eat were Cafe Lalo (featured in the movie "You've Got Mail") and a very tiny restaurant called Rice and Beans (or was it Beans and Rice?). The food here was excellent! And we enjoyed the restaurant because it opened on to the street so we were able to people-watch. 
Ellis Island is another "must see" - incredible place! And sunset from the Empire State Building was beautiful.
We loved NY and can't wait to go back!

title: “Great rooms, ideal location”
text: These folks rescued my family and me in the middle of the night once - so I owe them. This recent stay was my longest here. Breakfast is OK, dinner is not as nice as other Homewoods I've stayed at, but OK as well. GREAT service from the people hosting breakfast and dinner though. All the staff seems very attentive and friendly. This is a fantastic location - central to shopping, Sea World isn't far, downtown is an easy drive, very close to the airport, Harbor Island, Shelter Island, Point Loma. If you're "old Navy" you might have gone to boot camp here as the hotel is on the grounds of the old Navy Training Command (NTC San Diego). You don't pay for parking. There are a couple of restaurants just across the parking lot. I was in a corner king suite with a perfect view and plenty of room to spread out. I was on the third floor and heard a LOT of noise from a VERY heavy-footed person above me. Sounded like Frankenstein clomping around! On shorter stays I've been in an efficiency and these are just a tad bigger than a normal hotel room, but still have a kitchenette. I've stayed many places in SD, but this just might be my pick for next time when travelling with family. The area around the old NTC has been very well preserved with memorials and beautiful grounds. Super area for running, walking or taking kids to nearby parks and playgrounds.

title: “Surprisingly great!”
text:
I stayed at the Elan Modern Hotel based on the reviews from the tripadvisor.
I was extending my conference-stay in L.A. for a couple of days and staying on my own, wanted a good and safe hotel. 
I booked via booking.com and bought also a 3-day Go LA Card - pays you back twice if you want to see the main touristic attractions and do not have many days for that. 
When I arrived at the hotel, it was nice and very clean, staff very pleasant. Walking through the corridor I was asking myself why this hotel was rated nr.1 in such a city as L.A. There was nothing wrong, but I was not so much impressed. But then after the porter, who was helping me with my suitcase closed the door, I found myself in a spotlessly elegant room, where every detail was though of! The AC was perfect, fridge full of soft drinks and also some wine and beer, big TV with up to 20 channels plus a VCR, plus a choice of some very good films to get from the reception. For a woman a provided good iron was a must. Great bathroom with a bath-tube, nice toiletries, a bathrobe, thick towels of all sizes. Every evening when I came to the room, a small lamp was on, a few chocolate bonbons with a wish of a good sleep and a weather forecast for the next day on the bed, that was a very nice homely touch. WiFi was included in the price of the room. Breakfast was very good although basic - yoghurt, cereals, fresh bagels, marmalade, boiled eggs, great coffee, some fruits. The concierge was truly amiable and helpful every day with my questions about "the best way to get there and there..", they were absolutely amazing. The hotel is very close to the shopping mall - Beverly Center. The area is ok, safe. It is in West Hollywood. Overall I had a perfect stay in the Elan Hotel, for three stars is is exceptional. I would advise it to my friends.

title: “Great choice!”
text:
Really good location, great comfort & design, good value! Good restaurants & shops at walking distance. Union Square is just 4 blocks away! 
No parking available nearby though, which was a downside since we had a rental.

title: “Friendly staff, comfortable rooms, great breakfast and dinner.”
text:
The majority of the staff was friendly and courteous. The rooms were comfortable and well equipped. Breakfast and dinner were both great and yummy, but a little difficult to justify the added cost of the room, especially for one person. Very convenient, nonetheless. The rooms have DVD players, great for bringing your own movies, but maybe it's time to upgrade to Blue-Ray, and home theater surround sound (OK, maybe I'm asking for too much now). 
Now for the bad stuff: The sliding closet doors were "broken." They were not riding in the rails, making them hard to open and close. The shower door handles were not aligned properly, also making them hard to open and close. These were common themes in two rooms on two trips in consecutive weeks. I did not report these to maintenance. Seems like the cleaning staff could/should notice these things (especially the shower doors), and be proactive in reporting these items themselves. They are pretty obvious. Also the stopper in one bathroom sink would not close fully to allow a puddle of water for shaving. I adjusted it myself. The stopper in the bathroom in the second room was leaking under the sink. I hand tightened the fitting to stop the leak. Silly little things, but they detract from otherwise great rooms.

title: “Trendy, perfect for some, wrong place for others”
text: Traveled to San Diego for a business conference near the convention center. Its located 7 or 8 blocks from the convention center area, perhaps 5 or 6 blocks from the gaslamps, so its close enough for nice walks for food and entertainment. Hotel has music playing in the lobby area, is definitely catering to a young trendy population. First night at the hotel my room was right above the pool - a mistake if your tired and just want to get a good night of sleep. However, the hotel staff was very responsive, easily allowed me to switch rooms in the morning. Overall the hotel is well designed, rooms are very comfortable and modern. Would consider staying again, especially if staying as part of a group of friends or colleagues.

title: “Good location; Not so great property”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel with my wife and son the night before an early morning flight for vacation. I had high expectations being that we had a great experience earlier in the year at the Courtyard next door but was disappointed shortly after check in. First, the front desk staff was fast and friendly during check in and check out. However, once we got to the room we found that it was cleaned to the typical Marriott standard that I'm used to (I'm a multi-year Marriott Platinum member so I stay at a lot of Marriott's). The bathroom toilet was dirty and the rooms were exceptionally loud with noise from neighboring rooms and the hallway. In addition, we took our son to the pool for a swim but found it to look exceptionally dirty and not well maintained. Needless to say, I was disappointed with the overall experience. Next time we fly out, we'll be sure to stay at the Courtyard next door.

title: “Clean and affordable”
text:
What else to ask.
Nice rooms, nice indoor pool and very good fitness center. Flat TV, fridge, microwave.
We would go there again for sure.

title: “Not a bad choice”
text:
I stayed at the Seattle Westin in late July, 2012. We stayed on the 37th floor.
Pros. Centrally located for shopping, close to the Seattle Science Centre, only a 15 minute walk from the Victoria Clipper.
Cons. Lousy water pressure, a 40 minute walk to Safeco field, have to pay for WiFi, local beer in the mini bar priced out at over $10.00 when re-stocking fee and taxes are added, $7.00 per day charge if you put anything of your own in the mini bar.
If visiting Seattle to see Baseball or Football, I would recommend the Crown Plaza as it is closer to the parks. For shopping, the Westin gets my nod as a good choice.

title: “quirky rooms”
text: stayed at this hotel for 3 nights on a trip around California. It's a good budget hotel, all the rooms are different with the walls as displays of art. The room was basic and on the small side, but very clean and modern, with a good size shower. loved the bagels at breakfast, but there were no tables on thebreakfast room and you have to eat on a tray. It's next door to China town and the main shopping district, so the location makes up for everything.

title: “Feels like home”
text: A friend and I spent 4 nights at the Intercontinental Barkley in late January. We were mixing business and pleasure and found ourselves racing in and out of the hotel 3-4 times a day. Every time we walked into the lobby, we felt like we were coming home. The lobby is warm and cozy, even though it's large. Our room was excellent: big enough for 2 queen sized beds with plenty of room to walk around. The bathroom was updated and also large. Beds, bed linens and towels excellent quality. We had to ask Guest Services for extra blankets and a new hair dryer (a moment of panic there!) and they came immediately and were very kind and helpful.

title: “will go back in a heartbeat”
text: This was my first time staying in downtown Chicago, so keep that in mind. This is the first time I have felt compelled to give a review here, so that alone should tell you something! There are a couple of things about Hotel Felix that really impressed me. First, the staff was extremely friendly, but it wasn't forced. Second, the room we stayed in was on the small side, but that didn't matter to me. The bed and pillows were so comfortable that I stripped the bedding in the morning looking for brand tags so I can get the same thing in my home! It was the best night of sleep I've had in a long time. The bathroom was nice with a spacious shower. The sink was a bit shallow for my liking but not really a big deal. I will stay here again if the opportunity arises.

title: “Fantastic Location, A Peaceful Rest on Embassy Row”
text:
We stayed here from a Thursday to Saturday in March. We got lucky with beautiful, even hot, early Spring weather. We were visiting a nearby school and just sightseeing. 
The location really is superb -- within a short walk to Dupont Circle and new downtown, and just a bit more to the White House area. Massachusetts Avenue (Embassy Row) and the streets to the north are quite charming. The hotel overlooks charming (if busy) Scott Circle. We changed rooms after our first room had no light as it looked directly onto the next building (a negative for at least one side of the hotel). The room we ended up with looked over the Circle -- a beautiful view.
The lobby is spacious and comfortable, with the usual free internet usage. The restaurant in the hotel is actually pretty good (but about par with other Marriott locations). The staff was nice and helpful.
The space was clean, and the room was fine if basic. The bathroom was not spacious or well designed -- typical of these types of hotels. However, the bed and furnishings were comfortable enough.
The best thing is the location for the price. Also, it is a comfortable base for exploring the nearby areas. I would stay here again.

title: “Very accomodating and great suites”
text: We have stayed numerous times at On the Ave. The suites are great and they treat you like family. The bathroom had a TV in it. Great location on the west side of town. Frequently have discounted rates oin their website, or emails sent to previous guests. Angie is a great hotel manager.

title: “historical details- value for money”
text:
Hotel with a lot of history and full off original details. the room we had is classified as "renovated", this was alright for the room although the attached bathroom was rather small , (original size - 1920ies) and "renovated " by painting the tiles. On site restaurant provides good basic food -
combination of location, service and ambiance - great value for money

title: “Comfortable stay”
text: Myself and my two kids stayed here the night before flying out of jacksonville. The hotel was very clean. The room was spacious and had a fridge, microwave and flat screen tv. Kids liked the pool and whirlpool. Bed were very comfortable. Breakfast was awsome....eggs, sausage, biscuts and gravy, pancakes as well as the other normal fare. We will be staying here again.

title: “Great hotel, good service, let down by ridiculous food prices”
text:
I stayed at the JW Marriott in Houston on business in February 2009. I have previously stayed at Marriott Hotels on business and always enjoyed great service and facilities. 
The hotel is approx.45 mins away via taxi from the airport. The hotel itself is in central shopping district of Houston, and is located directly opposite the Galleria shopping centre, which has several cafes and bars. 
The hotel itself is a modern tower block building, which has a well laid out and luxurious reception. It has an adjoining bar downstairs, and a restaurant//breakfast area on the 2nd floor. In addition, there is a Starbucks on the ground floor which is open in the mornings only.
Check-in was fast with no problems - staff were friendly, efficient and helpful even though they were extremely busy. 
The room was HUGE, with two comfortable beds, and all bathroom fittings worked - plenty of towels and toiletries! TV was excellent - a large LCD screen - with a good range of channels - in particular, the pay-for-view options were extremely good. However - you had to pay for internet access, which in my opinion is a complete rip-off in this day and age. I also used the Fitness Centre on the 5th floor - this is fabulously equipped, and the pool is terrific - 25m long, heated, with most of it outdoors. a
I ordered delivery from the hotel room service several times, and service was fast and excellent. In addition, I ate breakfast every day during my stay; this is where the hotel falls down BADLY. Staff frequently ignored me, and often presented me with the wrong bill. In addition, the charge for what I ate was ridiculously high - $12 for a bowl of cereal?!?!? Just as well it was going on expenses!
This is a good hotel, and it could be great IF Marriot didn't charge for its internet, and reviewed its ludicrous food prices.

title: “Almost Paradise”
text:
This is one classy hotel, and we absolutely enjoyed the festivites at New Year's Eve Party on the 2nd floor. Our room was lovely, well-supplied and in a great location. Everything exceeded our expectations until about 1:00 a.m. New Year's Day when we were locked out of our room due to a mix-up over our bill. 
Frankly, I still cannot believe how we were treated. The front desk would not tell us anything except to come down, and there were no free elevators what with the party still going on and the hotel full. Nor would they send anyone up, and they did not explain that there was a problem with the credit card. WHY did they not have this supposed problem when we checked in? Surely they verified it would go through. At about 1:30 am, feeling I had no other option, I called security. 
They escorted me (using the service elevator) to the front desk. They told me I had to go back upstairs and get a different form of payment. We had cash and I brought it down. This was embarrassing; his credit card had hundreds available on it. On Monday when he called his bank he was informed that not only had we paid cash for our room they had processed a payment on his card as well. Hummmmmm.
I wish I could relive that night without the embarrassing "locked out" episode. It would have been a perfect night.

title: “Fantastic Location”
text:
My husband and I spent 2 nights at the Downtown Courtyard with our 3 young sons and had a fantastic stay. We booked our room through Kayak for a great price and had a fifth floor room with a view of the clock tower...beautiful! 
Check-in was a breeze. The room was very nice...thick and comfy carpet. No noise fron other rooms. The beds were really comfortable...memory foam mattress and nice pillows. The bathroom was clean...towels were thick and soft. The hotel and room was very clean. 
The location is great...just 2 blocks from Reading Terminal. Reading Terminal is full of fresh meats, flowers, produce, food, etc. Bassetts Ice Cream is beyond amazing, Old City Coffee has wonderful coffee, and we had the best omelettes at Down Home Diner...all in Reading Terminal! 
We were in town for the King Tut exhibit (we loved it!) and we walked to other museums and we also walked to the liberty bell.
My kids went to the pool once and they had a blast. It's open late and the entire pool was shallow...which was great for our kids!
We will stay here again!

title: “Much Better Than The Reviews”
text:
Booked this hotel for business as I am a Starwood member, but was concerned having looked at the reviews here. 
The staff were very courteous, appropriate and helpful. The room was very nice - I did get a corner room in the north tower which helped. A little noisey but bearable. Liked the shower only bathroom - clean and modern.
And in reference to comment that the location isnt walkable to the harbour district....I am assuming this person doesnt walk further than from their car to their house! 6 blocks is not a trek!

title: “Automatic Relaxation and Rehydration”
text: Just by being here you become calm, peaceful, and drink way more water than you ever thought possible. The classes are wonderful, spa treatments terrific and food yummy.,

title: “Great location! Beautiful room!”
text:
I would definitely stay at the Belleclaire again. This is a beautiful early 1900's building with tons of character. We had room 806...a large round room from which you could see Central Park. The room had pretty wood floors, a flat screen TV with modern furniture, and a soft bed with a warm down comforter. The bathroom was small with a noisy pipe, but was always clean. I found the hotel staff to be very friendly and family oriented (the owner's 2 little girls were helping distribute hotel keys to guests). 
The location is perfect! There are tons of grocery stores, restaurants, cafes, and shopping in the area. It is bustling, but much less touristy than Midtown. Everything you want to do/see is easily accessible with a subway stop only 2 blocks away. 
If you are looking for a generic-Hampton Inn experience, this is not the place for you. There are quirks...there is no true concierge, no morning breakfast, the paint is chipped here and there, the elevator is small. But if you're looking to stay in the real New York, for a decent price, and charming accommodations, you can't go wrong here.

title: “3 Star experience for 5 star price”
text: I'm a frequent Intercontinental guest so always expect to have a good experience. For that reason, I booked the Barclay for a 3 day visit to New York with my wife. Despite an excellent location and a decent gym, I found the service to be very poor. Hair from other people on the bathroom floor is always a bit freaky, and a king size bed with a mattress which swayed from side to side at the slightest movement meant that sleeping felt like being on the deck of a ship (this was surprising because intercontinental usually has great beds). Finally, the poor service was grating- being chased out of the breakfast room for inadvertently sitting down 10 minutes before it opened for example. Most of the staff really don't seem to care. And no room service from 12 to 5 at night, which means if you're on European time like we were, you better have some snackbars at the ready when you wake as normal at 2. Is this a perfectly reasonable hotel for new york if you're paying $150 a night? Sure, that's about what is its worth. But if you paid $300 as I did, you just feel let down.

title: “What a disappointment…”
text: As other reviewer pointed out, this hotel was overrated. It has to be lower than 3 stars, two maybe. There is no way this hotel meets the Crown Plaza standards that I know. The size of room wasn’t too bad but the bedding, mattress, bathroom and other things are so outdated that even though house cleaning is done properly it can’t be justified. Well, if there isn’t much hotel can do about the aged building then one thing they can do and have a control over is the customer service. Kind service can overcome a lot of things. Unfortunately that’s not what we were experienced. Seven couple made weekend gateway golf trip in Dublin, Ohio. We booked a room via Travelocity. It was a deal that you don’t know the hotel until you book it. Once the hotel name was revealed we selected the room type, king size bed. It got booked and confirmed. When we checked in the room, it had two double beds. We went back to the front desk and asked about our reservation. The lady at the front desk, Ashely S. wasn’t even look its availability and told us that they were out of the king size bed room. We told her we booked king size bed and she told us, “If you book it via 3rd party then nothing will be guaranteed.” What? Are you serious? We told her that we know it was available two minutes ago, only then she gave us the king size bed room very unwillingly, trust me her attitude expressed enough how she feels about this like pounding countertop when she took the key, etc, and adding, “We are not supposed to change the room…”??? We were standing feeling as if we begged for a free room and she was doing our favor? Was I supposed to be just grateful that you gave us a room because we booked it via 3rd party??? This hotel seriously needs better management. It runs and acts like a motel or inn. What a disappointment…

title: “Lovely, Peaceful Oasis”
text:
Fairly new, contemporary hotel in a quiet condominium complex on a wharf right across from The North End.
Our room was quite spacious, with a view of the water and Coast Guard base. It was fun watching the Coast Guard ship embark right in front of our window. Comfortable bed, very large flat panel and nice bath and closet.
We selected the lowest priced king room and found it quite adequate.
Fitness facility, which is shared by the condos, is also new and up to date.
Breakfast at the restaurant was good, but quite expensive.
Staff at this hotel were all friendly and courteous. We did not dine here as the restaurant menu was not appealing. I understand that they are changing over to a new restaurant.
The only negative was the very high parking fee. $42/day.
We will be back in the warmer weather to enjoy the outdoors

title: “Nice Place”
text: The Hotel was very nice, Staff was especially nice and helpful, especially assistant front desk Manager Loic Pichardo who went above and beyond. The Location and amenities this property provides are awesome. Everything is immaculately maintaind including the pools, rooms, restaraunts, lobby etc. The property was built in 1962 so it has been there a while but it has been refurbished pretty well. It is very close to Sea World and beaches as well as oold town and gas Lamp. If possible try to get a room along the beach/inlet.

title: “Great hotel, great location.”
text: I stayed here for business. It was a great location, as I could walk to where I needed to be on JFK boulevard. The rooms are wonderful and very spacious and clean. The breakfast is first rate, and the manager's reception is fantastic, with unlimited alcoholic beverages and snacks. I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “Incredibly comfy bed.”
text: We stayed at the Maxwell for 2 nights and loved it! It's hard to find a comfy bed and pillows when your traveling and both were amazing. We went for a first ever NFL game and the location was close enough to walk to the stadium once we took the free shuttle to Pike's Market. Great bar in the hotel with drink specials on game days. Really reasonable! Easy access to the I-5 if you're driving.We've booked for another date in December as we liked it so much.

title: “This place will cause you Heartbreak once you've stayed there”
text:
Wrote to hotel directly last year after staying to voice my complaints but surprisingly they never even bothered to acknowledge me.
Plastic knives and forks for breakfast served in a filthy lounge/bar area.
No safety deposit boxes for each room.
A manager who had little interest in discussing our concerns and issues with us.
Totally over rated/priced hotel due to proximity to Graceland, there are lots of other hotels just down the road that I wished we had stayed in.

title: “Usually friendly but not this weekend”
text:
I do love this hotel and walk all my out of town guests here to promote it. A few have stayed here due to my showing them the hotel. The people that work here are usually very lovely but I took some people here this weekend and we weren't treated with the same welcoming experience as before. I was actually embarressed and my guests felt awkward as well. I'm ashamed to say, they won't be staying here due to the way we were treated. 
I tried to show them the patio on 16 and they said it was full to capacity. I just wanted to at the very least let them look out through the window and they made us feel very unwelcome. I tried to show them the restaurant (all things I've done before) and they just seemed to want us out. Later I took them to other hotels and they came right away out with the menu and times of service. I won't give up on Trump as they have been good in the past but needless to say, I'm a little afraid if this happens again.
When the hotel opened they were so kind as to walk me around to spa/pool and everywhere. I've since promoted and shown it off and it's due to how welcoming they were. I'm hoping this was an off weekend but it was upsetting to say the least.

title: “Enjoyable stay, but wouldn't stay again.”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights early June. Arrived early from Anaheim Doubletree (fantastic hotel) and were checked in straight away. Room was very spacious, full ocean view. Kids liked the pool although the pool area is quite small and they offer lemonade by the poolside which is very nice. Not sure how everybody seems to get such a good rate, but we booked through hotel website at $420 a night! This was our most expensive hotel during a 3 week stay, but certainly not the best. You are paying for the view. The hotel does not have a restaurant, so any room service is brought in from outside restaurants. The breakfast is served in a very small room downstairs. You can have cereals, small selection of fruit and toasted bagels, It's the same every day and there were never enough bowls etc, so you had to have polystyrene bowls which you are supposed to use if you want to take breakfast to your room. The most disappointing thing is the surrounding area, it's a dump!! The hotel said they had restaurants that you could sign a tab and they would bill the hotel, so that you did not have to carry your wallet around at night, this seems to me its because the area is so dreadful. We were recommended one restaurant by a local chap who got chatting to us outside the hotel, its called Nicks by the beach, very nice food and good service, its about a five block walk. All other nights we drove into the city and went to Seaport Village, about a 15 min drive. It's on the waterfront and has some good restaurants. We also went to La Jolla which is lovely. Wonderful area, great restaurants. Very easy to get to Seaworld and San Diego Zoo, both about 10 - 20mins drive. If we stayed here again, we would stay in La Jolla and certainly not Pacific Beach, the other reviews have said this is a dump, but I didn't quite believe it until I saw it. Unless you are really into surfing and under 25, stay elsewhere.

title: “Clean Doubletree”
text: We found the Doubletree at Delmar to be very clean and tidy. The employees were very friendly and service-oriented. It happened to be farther north than we had expected since our main visit was to Coronado, but the travel to and from outside of traffic hour was about 20 minutes. We would stay here again if we were wanting to see sites close by such as La Jolla Cove or Mission Bay.

title: “Loved it. Can't wait to stay here again.”
text: We spent one night at the hotel. It was decorated really cool; feels like you are walking into a hotel in the old days. Didn't experience the ghostly ecounters that some guests talk about. We will definately stay here again.

title: “Excellent location.”
text: This hotel is great, service is fantastic and location is perfect. Highly recommend.

title: “A good choice in San Francisco”
text:
Arriving in your room at the Castle Inn you might find yourself a little disappointed. The room is modestly sized, and the chances are you'll have a view of the walkway connecting the rooms which overlook the courtyard (car park). However, this place has plenty of good things going for it and proved to be an excellent option for our stay in San Francisco.
The greeting was fantastic. After being given the keys to our room we were invited back to reception where the receptionist provided us with books and maps of the city, along with superb advice as to where to go and what to see.
Although a little small, the room was spotless and very well decorated. The shower head had a number of interesting settings, including the pulse massage which was well appreciated after being enveloped in the cold SF fog. The 'kitchen' area was a little odd, comprising a microwave, coffee maker and fridge, but little in the way of utensils. This isn't a complaint as the facilities were well appreciated, rather it's an observation.
The Inn stands just off highway 101, which meant that it was easy for me as a tourist to find, and to get back on to to reach the airport on the final day of my stay.
A short walk around the corner on to Polk Street finds you among a good range of good quality coffee shops, bars and restaurants, as well as an organic market and chilled food takeaway which did a fantastic won ton salad. There is little other accomodation in this area so it feels like you are living among the locals. Unfortunately we weren't told about the free breakfast, but I think this was our gain as we found a fantastic 'boulangerie' nearby selling a delicious range of pastries and fantastic coffee.
Although this hotel isn't in the middle of the tourist hustle, it is only a fifteen minute walk from Fisherman's Wharf. If you want to stay somewhere residential, away from the tourists, but on the doorstep of the sights, then as long as you keep your expectations realistic the Castle Inn shouldn't disappoint.

title: “Overpriced”
text:
We had this hotel booked for us trough Round the World Experts. We paid around £350 for two nights and having looked at the prices in these other reviews, feel that we were ripped off.
Room 212 was quite large but in an L shape and although there was room for a bigger bed, it was a very small double and it was pressed up against a chest of drawers, on which I banged my elbow in the night. The views were not good and the window blind slats were broken in places. We left the blinds alone for fear of further breakage and therefore were not able to have daylight in the room. The air conditioning worked well.
The hotel desk staff were polite and quite helpful. The room next to ours was very noisy one night with a lot of comings and goings until at least 3am when we finally got to sleep, which led to a lot of conjecture about what might be taking place in that room.
The location is good, near the subway and also Central Park. There is a good little Diner just around the corner. You could only use Wfi from the lobby. The airport shuttle bus that the hotel booked for us to return us to JFK arrived on time and was cheaper than taking a cab. However the price from JFK airport to anywhere in New York appears to be fixed at £52 plus toll charge, total $59 plus tip. Wait in the line outside of the airport and let the official get the taxi for you, then you can be sure of getting a fixed price official cab rather than an unlicenced cab which may cost you far more and may not be insured

title: “Best Ever”
text: If you are going to Baltimore, there is only one place to stay - 4 East Madison Inn. From the moment I telephoned and spoke with one of the partners, to the time we checked out, I have never been so cosseted nor comfortable. 4 Madison is located in midtown Baltimore commonly called Mt. Vernon. This area has every conceivable restaurant and shop within a 4-block radius, not to mention 3 lovely parks. If one has to wander further, there are shuttles, buses and taxis galore. But I digress. Sandy and co-owner Betty were there to greet us like family members. The Inn is a huge converted townhome, replete with gorgeous antiques and a staircase that one guest could not stop admiring. (For those who are not stair climbers, there is an elevator.) Each room is breathtakingly furnished, but for the ladies there are no nasty hotel amenities. The products, from soaps to shampoo to hand creams, are top of the line, specialty shop brands. The sheets are Ralph Lauren, and yes, there are soft, thick, heavenly terry bathrobes hanging in the closet. For those who think a B&B means sharing a bath, this is not your typical inn. Each room has its own full bath with enough room to spread out his and her toiletries. If that is not enough, then let's talk service. Sandy and Betty are only concerned with your needs and comfort. They ask what time YOU would like breakfast and what YOU would like. One day I went on a walking tour and when I came back, Sandy was concerned that I hadn't eaten, "made" me sit down, and served me a lovely plate of fresh fruit (I'm talking mangos, a melon to die for, cherries , etc.), cheese and scrumptious bread. For the gourmand, her lunches are divine (I don't know where she found the asparagus, but I haven't seen anything that tender in decades) and 4 Madison East had just begun to serve dinner. One can dine inside or in the garden, which was lovingly restored replete with a koi pond. Their staff is equally charming and kind. There is nothing too small to ask for and voila, you have it. Have I said enough, I hope so, because this is the only place to stay.

title: “Downtown Option - Great Location, Service, and Rooms”
text:
Have been to Detroit many times, but this is the first time I have stayed here. Service was great, rooms were very modern and nicely furnished. They were on the smaller side, but the floor to ceiling windows were wonderful. We had a corner room that had fantastic views of downtown and Ford Field and Tiger Stadium. 
Bed was comfy, room was well supplied with linens and coffee maker. Plenty of lamps, outlets, and nice desk. Minibar was also nice, pretty good selection and the prices were great for a minibar. For example a beer was $3. 
We ate at Bistro 555 for dinner and the food was good, the breakfast and buffet looked good as well. 
The hotel has free valet parking and WIFI and also offers room service menu. 
As others have stated tv service would stutter here and there. No big deal unless you were watching a game or something. 
The location is perfect. You are connected to the greektown casino by a covered skywalk. You can also walk right out the front door and be right by all of the restaurants and shops in Greektown. Tiger Stadium, Ford Field, the Fox Theater are all very close by. You also have easy access to the people mover which is only 75 cents. 
I am a travel agent who is very fussy about where I stay. I normally was staying at the MGM hotel which is very nice, but gets very pricey. I also went to view the Atheneum Hotel and those rooms were very nice, modern, clean, and all suites for a good price. All three of these have easy access to great restaurants, bars, events, and casinos. I would stay at all three hotels, would just depend on the price at this point.

title: “Great Location, slept well!!”
text:
I have a hard time sleeping anywhere but home. This hotel was great. I slept so well and woke up well rested every morning. Was a nice change from other hotels. 
The location was great, really close to everything. I would definitely recommend this hotel to others!

title: “Great Stay”
text: Wonderful hotel and incredibly friendly and helpful staff. From Ali at the car check-in to Big Dave, to the Managers and especially Christina, who helped with last second room requests, everyone was simply outstadning. Room was sopacious weklll-maintained and lovely. Overall an exemplary expreicne.

title: “Small double room”
text:
Double rooms very small. Not worth the money. Parking $32 a night . This room costed us $270 after tax and parking. 
The base price was $206.
I think they should tell you about the parking up front before booking the room.

title: “Comfortable rooms with good location”
text: Went up to Denver for my birthday and had a great time at the Bronco's game, Bruce Springseen concert. My only disappointment was that unlike other Four Seasons Hotels I have stayed at, they would not provide a car to either of these events. Otherwise the hotel was nice.

title: “great location”
text: Stayed here in August 2007 with my Mum and Dad. Hotel was in a great location just a short walk from times square. Only stayed three nights and can't comment on breakfast as we ate at a diner just along the road. Also didn't realise there was a pool on the roof-which we couldn't have used anyway as it was raining while we were there. The beds were very comfortable and the room was really clean. I was 16 at the time so later on in the evening my mum and dad sat in the bar area and I was able to use the computer facilities right next to the bar. Overall a short but great stay.

title: “Awesome Location”
text:
We've just returned from a weekend at the Sir Francis Drake. We had a wonderful time. I found a rate online. I then found that the hotel will match some internet rates. So I called them directly and they did match the rate. Rooms on floors on floor 2-15 were $112; for $8 more we could get rooms on floors 16-20. We paid the extra. The price listed on the door in our room was $499 for 2 people. We had a fanstastic view of the city, Union Square, and a hint of the Bay. We had a king room on the 20th floor. Our only complaint was that we were directly under the dance floor of the Starlight Room and they have music til 2 am on the weekends. We were so exhausted from hiking around SF that it almost lulled us to sleep! 
Our room had a king size bed, a desk, a flat screen tv, a fridge (that had room to put our own drinks). There were only 3 drawers to put clothes however. The room had a huge walk in closet. Our friends stayed in a queen room on the 17th floor. They had the same amenities, but a different layout since it is an old building.
We took advantage of the drag brunch at the Starlight room on the weekends. It was a hoot!
The location is great! We took BART from the airport to Powell Street Station then hiked the 4 blocks uphill to the hotel. The cable cars stop right outside the front door of the hotel and go to two locations on Fisherman's wharf. It's $5 one way or you can purchase a 1, 3 or & 7 day pass. We got the 3 day pass for $18. It's good for MUNI, cable cars, and trolley cars (everything except BART).
There are plenty of restaurants, bars, and shopping in close proximity. If we ever return to San Francisco we will definately stay here!

title: “Jawdropping Impressive”
text:
Enjoyed 2 fantastic nights with my girlfriend in April 2008 prior to boarding the QE2. I knew i was not going to be disappointed as the hotel had been recommended by a very discerning English friend. Our room was on the 25 floor and was a "London Suite". I did not expect it to be a "real"suite,that is 2 separate rooms. The beds were incredibly comfortable with a quilted matress sheet. There was a dressing room area, and a bathroom with a double walk in shower. The staff could not have been nicer which was just as well as we arrived around midnight and i was not in the mood for hastle. The conceirge service was very helpful as my girlfriend had a list of shops to visit in a very busy 2 day schedule. The hotel is incidently excellently positioned for shopping and sightseeing. The downstairs restaurant and bar is mixed together which is a bit odd. That being said the full afternoon tea was fantastic and the lightest scones i have ever tasted (Mr Ramsey's reciepe i wondered) and breakfast was excellent. No vast portions thank godness for English appetites.
There aren't many hotels that i can say i would like to rush back to but the London was one of them.

title: “Brilliant”
text:
Fabulous hotel, the room was amazing 5* quality, the biggest bed ever, luxury bathroom, excellent coffee machine. The room service was brilliant and reasonable for this quality of hotel. 
2 very minor negatives (however don’t let them put you off!) 
1– They tried to sell us an upgrade as we were checking in. Always find that a bit pushy and it makes you worry about the quality of the room you have. Don’t be tempted to upgrade, the quality of the standard room is amazing! 
2-It is not well located for using public transport. It is not convenient for the underground. Be prepared to use taxis and walk. We really enjoyed the ‘longish’ walk into town. That said the hotel is in the heart of the fashionable/classy North End, so there are lots of lovely bars and restaurants on your door step. 
I will definitely stay here again and recommend it to everyone!

title: “Mile High Magic”
text: Even though the magic was gone from the Denver Broncos on New Years day our stay at the Hotel VQ was very enjoyable. Both of us felt the bed was oh so comfy; the room and halls were quiet even though we spent New Years Eve there. The shuttle service to downtown Denver was quick and easy. Front desk service was and always has been great and I would like to especially recognize "Israel" who is a waiter upstairs in the Sky Bar for his excellent service with a smile. The dinner upstairs was good; and the view can not be beat. Once again thanks to Linda for taking my call and making my reservation. There was a problem with the north elevator breaking down during our stay which caused me to have to walk up and down 7 flights of stairs 4 times but I don't mind a little excercise and I know that it is hard to get vendors to work on Holidays.......

title: “A Great Airport Overnight Stay!”
text: Stayed here en route to Grand Cayman after a long flight. Such a genuine efficient and friendly welcome from Jeff at the front desk. Lovely Club floor room, in great condition with that wonderful Sweet Sleeper bed. I have absolutely no idea what the previous reviewer is talking about in terms of the hotel being old and worn. I am a Starwood Gold member, therefore a very frequent Sheraton guest and this property was most certainly in very good condition, and our room was perfect.The lounge was closed the next morning because of thanksgiving and we were kindly given 2 free buffet breakfasts at check in to compensate for that. I am not usually a fan of buffets BUT this one was absolutely wonderful, fresh, hot food really hot, delicious mains, lots of fruits, cereals and breads, so much variety. We were very well looked after by the most charming lady (wish I could remember her name) and did not bemoan the loss of our free lounge "continental" breakfast at all. A friendly trip to the airport in the free shuttle and we were away. Thanks Sheraton Houston for making our in transit stay after a long flight and day very very relaxing!

title: “Great value”
text: This hotel was great, especially for the price I paid while staying in downtown Chicago. Everyone was very helpful, especially Diane Pena.

title: “Very Good”
text: It is a clean and modern hotel with comfortable bed. The room was wide, as anywhere else in North America. The cleanliness was very good. The location is good with many restaurants & shops around. A little bit on the luxury side, but the price is also on expensive side.

title: “Best Location in SF”
text: This hotel was recently renovated so everything in the room was fresh, new and clean (we had a bay room view w/balcony). Excellent location ~ across the street from to Pier 39 and within walking distance to the pier for Alcatraz cruises and the Trolleys. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

title: “Not what I expected...”
text: I stayed at the Belevedere a couple of years ago, and it was okay - so I booked again. Come to find out the entire hotel has different rooms. The rooms they show online are not the standard or deluxe room you get when you check in. Our room was old and outdated. Everything smelled like smoke, even though this is a non-smoking hotel. The bathroom was small and the tv was maybe 19". It had the old fashion bedspreads, etc... So we stayed one night, checked out the next morning and went to the Hampton Inn a couple of blocks away. Loved the Hampton - new beds, down comforter, etc...

title: “Cheap but in major need of maintenance”
text: I picked this hotel because it was close to my business appointments and I don't like to be on the road much. The previous reviews were pretty good so I thought I'd give it a chance. The desk staff was friendly although they were odd about giving me a receipt. I thought that was sort of strange and very unlike any other hotel I've ever stayed at, and I travel a lot. The room was spacious and adequate but there were some issues. It was extremely hot in the room and took about 24 hours to cool down. The AC the whole time was finicky, not even touching the controls would cool the room too much, some mornings it was freezing in the room, and others it was much warmer. The safe did not work and they couldn't really help to square it away. There were a number of serious maintenance issues, the toilet seat was dangerously loose, the towel rack was falling off the wall, the hairdryer obviously had overheated before and was dangerous to use. The refrigerator did not start cooling until the day I left and water/food was warm most of the time. The paint scheme was in dire need of a full repaint, there were many different colors that were close but not a match. The tile in the tub was in a terrible state, looked like streaks of some sort of silicone sealant smeared on it rather than fixing it correctly. There was a faint odor in the room, which was stronger in the hallway. I really can't put my finger on what it was, but it wasn't right. On top of all this there were holes in the wall, drywall and debris behind the bed, stains on the carpet and furniture and the bedding had seen better days. The couch had a nasty looking stain that was easy to hide by turning the cushion over which the staff should have done. The comforter look like it had cigarette burns on it, and the bed was sunken in. The drapery was ineffective, no dampening film on the window made it easy to see in as the drape did not cover the window well at all. I won't stay here again, but it was cheap and near where I needed to be, really I just needed a place to store my gear and sleep, so it barely covered that.

title: “Quick Easter Weekend Getaway”
text: My family and I visited the Arizona Grand Resort for Easter weekend. We travelled with our 3 kids (ages 11,11 and 13). The reason we picked this hotel was because of the Oasis Waterpark. The resort is nicely located, easy access to restraunts and shopping. When we arrived the employee at the check-in desk wasn't as friendly as we expected and was not clear to where our room was located. We ended up finding it on our own. We booked the Resort Queen Suite which was big enough for our family. The only down side about the room is that the bathroom sink is located on the outside of the bathroom that is adjoined to the bedroom. The bathroom itself was a bit small but our family of 5 managed pretty well. Housekeeping did a pretty good job cleaning the room everyday. Now one thing I have to point out is that some room are actually adjoined by a door. When we arrived the door that adjoined our room with the one next door was actually unlocked. Thankfully the next door room was empty and we locked the door. For some families this may be a safety concern so if you stay at this hotel double check that the door that adjoins your room with the room next door is locked. Overall our stay was pleasent the concierge staff were espescially friendly and the waterpark is a nice addition. If you're family is looking for a cheap affordable place to stay in Phoenix this in not the hotel for you. For our stay of 4 nights we ended up spending about $1000 just to book this hotel not including meals. There are lots of other hotels that offer a great rate plus breakfast. But if you're looking for a nice resort aimed at a family vacation and are willing to spend a little more then the Arizona Grand is the right choice. Overall we enjoyed our stay and hope to return in the future.

title: “Oldie but goodie”
text: I stayed one night and was pleasantly surprised. My room had a great view of downtown and the decor had a warm modern feel. This is an older hotel but well taken care of. Seems it was recently remodeled. The pool I did not use but it looks like a great space to spend a summer evening. I did eat dinner in the restaurant and the food was fair. I had the grilled chicken Alfredo which was a little bland. The staff was warm and friendly and when my TV would not work they had someone up immediately to fix it. The Best Western next door looked a little scary so I opted to park on the side with construction. There is a Denny's across the street but nothing else within walking distance. I would stay again.

title: “Good hotel. Could hear next room through the doors”
text:
It WAS a nice hotel. Couldn't ask for a better location. Across the street from the Architectural River tours, down one block from Millennium Park, down two blocks and across the bridge to the Magnificent Mile. Perfect location and great hotel did equal full of conference goers, weddings and families on vacation. 
If the people in the next room were close to the adjoining doors you could hear them talking, but since it isn't a party hotel it wasn't bad and all was quiet at night. But room felt new and very clean. Bed was very nice and comfortable. 
I was there for a conference in the same hotel. The basement conference rooms had huge pillars that obstructed the sight lines during some of the talks. 
Workout room was small and had barely any empty floor space for mats. For the price it should have had a pool. But otherwise it was a very good hotel.

title: “Stay somewhere else. This hotel is over priced for what you get.”
text: So I stayed at The Blake Hotel expecting nice rooms and amenities and I was really disappointed. No free wifi in hotel room, the shower was ridiculous water got all over the tiny bathroom floor. No mini fridge in room. No ice maker or vending on each floor of the hotel. Instead there is an ice maker on two of the floors int the entire hotel. The thermostat in the room was very old and it didn't work well. It could never cool the room sufficiently. I recommended staying somewhere else where you get more bang for your buck.

title: “A Doctor's Visit Became a Pleasant Adventure”
text: Dealing with a disability and a walker and luggage is challenging. The staff, especially the valet people (Craig and Debbie) treated us with the utmost patience,care, and respect. They gave us the feeling, they were happy to be with us. For people with disabilities----there are three restaurants inside the building. --We took the early hotel bus to Johns Hopkins Hospital. The bus driver was also helpful with the walker. --And at the end, I, the caretaker, got a voucher and went to a super gym, while my husband read in the comfortable chairs of the lobby.

title: “Elegant decor, helpful staff, nice rooms; good value.”
text:
Found $107 rate on Hotwire for a Sunday night. Arrived to find large, gracious lobby and friendly staff, who considerately found us a room "high in the tower, with a good view." This put us on the "Starwood Preferred Guest Floor" with great city views. (There was no extra charge from the original rate.) The room was large, with two double beds and a huge bay window. The room had a flat-screen TV. The bathroom was also large, very clean, with new-looking modern fixtures. Starbucks coffee and Tazo tea are provided in the room. Having our small son with us, we checked out the pool, which is small; fortunately it wasn't crowded. The pool deck is very large with lots of lounging furniture, tables etc... would be nice to have cocktails there. In all the guest areas of the hotel, modern decor prevails in cool grays and greens-- very tasteful and soothing. Also, they use a "white tea" fragrance for all their bath products that is absolutely divine (even the lobby smells good). On the negative side, parking is not included in the nightly rate, and the ramp is prohibitively expensive, causing us to use a pay lot one block away. Also, there is no vending... sodas and snacks available at desk for astronomical price. Wi-Fi in the rooms will cost you a "connection fee," as will a local call.
 I feel that it was a good value for me, because the rate was so low; but if I had paid $150 or more, the cost of the add-ons would have left me peeved.

title: “Great Experience”
text: We attended a football game with an alumni group and stayed at the Omni. We never felt like part of a "package" but as a special guest. The hotel was neat and clean and the service exceptional. Courtesy driver was personable and informative. Night staff at desk went out of his way to find information about Sunday Mass.

title: “perfect”
text: The stay was nothing less than perfect! the rooms were clean and the staff was really nice. they took care of everything from the beginning until the end. Breakfast is REAL breakfast, they have a midnight snack buffet for the guests and that was really neat as well. overall, i would stay here over and over!

title: “Location, location.....and luxury!”
text: We just returned from our second stay ay the Hay Adams in Washington, DC...our first was before the new pres stayed there so i was concerned that the hotel had become to snooty. I am glad to report we had a wonderful stay and loved every minute of it! I had booked the cheapest rate available thru their website (I knew it would overlook the alley for that rate) but upon arrival I was offered an upgrade for $70.00 more a night. We took it. The room was overlooking the church on the 4th floor, beautiful room but it was across from the elevators so we could hear people coming and going at times. I did not request a room change(probably would next time) because the hotel staff was able to let us check into our room at 10AM. We had an early flight and upon arriving it was raining, and we were tired and did not feel like walking around DC in the rain. We spent a lazy morning in our room after a wonderful (expensive breakfast) in the dining room. We spent the next 4 days walking around DC and enjoying the hotel location to everything.. Also the security staff were able to escort us to the hotel roof ( closed after 9/11 except for private venues) where you have a breathtalking view of the White House and all other historical sites. From the time we walked in to the check out (late!), and the wonderful cookies at the check in reception, the great burgers in the bar , .we a great stay!

title: “Hotel Magnolia - a lot for the money”
text: We stayed at Magnolia for a business event nearby. They provide a full buffet breakfast that goes beyond most free hotel breakfasts (eggs, meat, toast, oatmeal, fruit, yoghurts, juices, coffee, etc.). Late afternoon happy hour consists of free wine or beer (limited selections). Evenings they have a variety of milks and cookies - the white macadamia nut chocolate chips were delicious. We booked for 3 nights and were upgraded to a suite which was quite large - dining table, living area and separate bedroom. Staff was friendly and helpful with directions and storing a bicycle for us. It's a convenient downtown location. Rooms were clean, just slightly dated. Bathroom is small for 2 people, but very adequate and modern.

title: “Warm Friendly Clean and Homey”
text:
We were in town for a 2 day medical appointment and the staff of the The Francisco Bay Inn were friendly and extremely helpful. They helped us in many ways including providing helpful recommendations on the best local Thai place for take out. The room was super clean and the general feeling was that of a homey relaxing weekend. The front desk staff were friendly and always had enough time for us. There were more than enough towels in the spacious bathroom as well as plenty of hot water in the morning. The coffee / pastries in the morning down in the lobby are a nice touch. The refrigerator was clean as was the coffee maker. This is more than worth the asking price per night. 
Both of us are locals to the general Bay Area and need to come to the City several times a year and after our last experience with The Francisco Bay Inn, we have decided to stay there. We highly recommend it to anyone who needs a great clean place to stay while visiting San Francisco. Excellent!

title: “I prefer this one!”
text:
Controversially I actually prefer this property to the meatpacking Standard which I think is great...but having stayed in both what I liked about this hotel over the other is this...
Feels less pretentious.The prevention level at the standard, in particular the top floor bar is astonishing. 
Smaller and more intimate. How I like a boutique hotel to be. 
Less crowded and generally more relaxing. 
I believe this is a relatively recent purchase and was something else originally and will be refurbed but I liked it how it was. Yes the rooms are a bit small, pretty standard ( no pun intended) with NY but it all was just lovely.
Can't say much else other than would love to come back sometime!

title: “A very nice Marriott...but not a "JW Marriott"”
text:
The location is wonderful if you have some down time...right across from the huge and very upscale Galleria mall. The hotel is what you would expect from a typical (and very nice) Marriott hotel. However, it is not a typical JW Marriott which would be much more upscale in its room and hotel decor. I stayed on a concierge floor so the rooms were probably the nicest....clean, flat screen TV, comfortable bed, renovated carpets and bathroom. I would definitely stay here again but they should just call it a Marriott hotel.
The lobby has a bar/restaurant which I ate in one evening after a full day of business and I was just too tired to go to any of the walking distance restaurants which are really nice. However, I was very pleasantly surprised that for "bar food", the food was excellent and nicely presented!

title: “Millennium Hotel”
text: This was a pretty cool looking Hotel but it need a few new up dates like the TV. We are in the age of Flat Panel TVs. Also they should have Wifi. Other then that Awsome Hotel would recommend.

title: “Excrement on the Bathroom tiles”
text:
We were booked into this hotel for 5 nights via an agent. The website looked great. The hotel and rooms looked clean bright and fresh. Unfortunately, this could not have been further from the truth.
The hotel was very dark. It didn't matter what time of day it was, there was very little natural day light. To say the place was dirty was an understatement. 
The room we were shown to had excrement on the bathroom tiles, the bath had several hairs in it and the base was chipped with chunks of ceramic missing. The light switch sparked as I flicked it on. In the bedroom a cold wind howled through the window and there was no sound proofing. Not really acceptable in December, we were freezing! 
The window surrounds were thick with black dirt with surplus to requirement screws lying around! The linen on the bed had black dirty marks on them. There were loose wires hanging out that appeared to have been stuffed behind some sort of plastic base in the corner of the room. The general state of the paint work was tired and chipped. This hotel should not have been rated a 4 star. I have since been advised that it has been down graded once already.
We complained to reception and were shown two other rooms of the same standard by Katie Hayari-Barea. She agreed with our concerns in the rooms and said they were not acceptable but then threatened to have security throw us out because we were complaining? I would like to add that at no stage did either my partner or myself use bad or abusive language.
I cannot comprehend how this hotel has got so many positive reviews. I can only assume that the majority of these must be fake.
We ended up moving to The Novotel in Times Square. It was really nice. Clean bright and reasonably priced and the staff were great.

title: “A decent if somewhat over priced hotel downtown.”
text:
The Omni is nice but this property is starting to show its age. Things look a little tatty and the rooms feel a little tired. 
My stay was decent but the lighting felt dingy and the bed was incredibly hard and felt cheap. Always something of a surprise when paying in the $400 range. 
Air conditioning was wheezy and a little lacking meaning the temp in the bedroom was hard to control. Add to this that the noise through the picture window behind the bed was loud, not an experience I will rush to repeat. Service was however extremely courteous and friendly. If the owners refurbish and invest in decent mattresses and new towels this hotel can command a premium price, until then shop around.

title: “Close to the Museums”
text: We checked in on May 26th 2006 around 5pm: Myself (40,female) my husband (41) and three 'teen's' (14, 13 and 12). The check in staff were helpful in telling us about some upcoming events and gave Raquel (12) a really good tour guide booklet. We had 2 rooms, one for the kids, and one for the parents. We ate at the Hotel Restaurant, "Smithsons". 2 out of 3 of The kids are (as expected) picky. The buffet seemed to accomodate everyone somewhat. Our bill was about $80. They had pork, mashed potatoes and veggies which I found to be pretty good. The picky kids had to make do with pizza, which they really did not care for but they did eat. The staff at the restaurant were very nice and accommodating...the ice cream machine would not work, and when we brought to the hostess attention, she brought everyone their own icecream from the kitchen. We went for a walk and found everything closer than I had expected (even after reading many Travel Advisor Reviews). Over the course of the 3 days we crammed in 5 days worth of touring, we walked to the Smithsonian Natural HIstory Museum (first day - a hit with the kids) the American HIstory Museum, the Washington Memorial, and many other sites. If your kids are up for a night walk, Taxi to the Lincoln Memorial around 5-6pm and walk the Memorials. We ended up at Jefferson Memorial and got a taxi home and it was incredible (albeit the kids were exhausted). The room had a coffee maker, the refrig, which we didn't opt for was $5 extra per day. THe room did not have a safe but I kept my purse in the drawer and it was not touched. The Bath & Bodyworks Shampoo, Conditioner, Lotion and Soap were a nice touch. We received a newspaper (usa today) on some days. (Our vacation was during Memorial Day holiday which probably affected that). The hotel has an ATM machine. Stamps were expensive - so bring them with you. THe Gift shop is small and doesn't sell alcohol. Wine in the bar sells for Minimum $18 a bottle (Beringer white zinfindel) to bring to your room, so if you want to save money - bring it. Many places I had read about on Travel Advisor (Wall Street Deli, CVS store) were closed for the holiday weekend. I would also only expect the pool to be open in the summer(June-August). There was a sign at the elevator that explained that rabbits were at the Pool (which is at the top of the building with a great view of the Capitol) which I found charming. They do not know how the rabbits got there. The girls tried to swim - it was too cold - but enjoyed the rabbits which are not tame and scared of humans but you can watch them. Taxi's are available from the hotel, and the charge from DCA is only $10. My husband is parsimonious and HAD to order pizza from Domino's for the kids (not the hotel pizza which is Pizza Hut) and it took 1 and 1/2 hour to get there. Not sure what the Pizza Hut experience would have been. But Don't order Dominos. McDonalds is VERY close. Quizno's is close also. Room Service Breakfast was $60. Husband and son got eggs/pancakes/sausage/hash browns, daughters got cereal and I got Denver Omelet/hashbrowns. The cereal comes with "Fruit extra for $1.50" when I only saw one banana I called to tell them they shorted us a 'fruit' only to be told that the banana should have been 'cut into 2 pieces'. ($3.00 for a 'full' banana????). Anyway - they brought me another banana plus an apple juice at 'no charge' so I was satisfied. The main thing that impresses me about this hotel is that my forgetful husband left the cord to the camcorder. He called the hotel AFTER our visit and they found it and mailed it to us - we received it today. THAT"S SERVICE!!! That really impressed me. If you want to eat at Hard Rock Cafe - you may want to get reservations. Although we got a table in 1/2 the time. The Hard Rock is next door to the Ford Theater which was a surprise and really cool. I really thought this hotel was a great choice and I only found it through using Tripadvisor - for the first time! I'm using Trip Advisor to plan our next vacation now.

title: “You will think you are wearing a crown at the Crowne Plaza”
text: We stayed in Charlotte four nights in order to attend the National Square Dance Convention. The hotel was on the convention hotel list as the Best Western, when we made our reservations and they faxed us the details of our confirmation. We are members of the Gold Crown Club and Priority Club hotels so we would get credit on our account either way. About a month before our arrival, we called the hotel to confirm our reservation and were told that we would be entitled to the same rate quoted by BW, a hot breakfast daily, and shuttle service to the Convention Center or anywhere within 3 miles of the hotel. There were many square dancers staying at the hotel and we kept the shuttle drivers busy. They are to be commended for their courteous, helpful and "go out of the way" attitude. The room was large and well appointed. We didn't discover the room darkening curtain until the next morning, however. The room came with little net bags with sleep inducing things in them: a satin eye cover, ear plugs, lavender spray to make the pillows smell nice and a CD to play in the radio/CD player by the bed, to help put you to sleep. We didn't need them after we discovered the shade. There was a little noise from the street, but not much. The breakfast was biscuits and sausage gravy in addition to eggs, bacon, sausage, potatoes, bread, sweet rolls, cereal, fruit, juice, milk, coffee and tea. It was enought to keep us going all day. It was served in the dining room with cloth napkins and an attentive, smiling staff to help when needed. One night they had a "special" in the bar that included a free appetizer when you bought a bottle of wine. We had five big shrimp in the shrimp cocktail and enough wine for two nights. We had a great time in Charlotte and were treated very well at the Crowne Plaza Hotel.

title: “Clean & Comfortable”
text: Fairly new construction; rooms clean; better than average "continental" breakfast for a budget hotel. Great location near airport & major freeways. Their in room movie vendor was being changed, but some of the staff didn't know, so first day I asked they told me erroneously that it must be my remote, and that they would call me back, but never did. Had to inquire again NE t day, and got the "real" answer.

title: “Great stay in a great city !”
text: Stayed at the Algonquin for our annual girls trip to NYC. Stayed 3 nights in a suite and it was great. Beautiful decor, great staff, big room, great comfy beds.... We stayed at Marriott Marquis last year and were hesitant about staying somewhere else but it was AWESOME !

title: “Perfect for a Weekend Visit”
text: Wanted to spend the weekend in the city for a friend's birthday and jumped at The Standard when it appeared on Jetsetter. We got the corner king room and the view did NOT disappoint. Outstanding views of the city and the bed was super comfortable. I loved that the bathroom floor was heated -- a nice touch as your getting ready for a night out on the town. Hotel staff was very responsive and helpful. Started our night at the hotel bar -- it was only so-so. Staff there didn't really seem as into the customers as they were each other and the barstools were painfully low.

title: “friends together”
text:
centrally located...many restaurants within steps...many open late until 11pm...great breakfast bakeries and sit down cafes...Hertz, Avis rentals within blocks...trolley steps away. wtaerfront location
the hotel itself is quiet- despite location, recently rennovated..helpful hotel staff.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
When traveling to Chicago we usually stay near the airport because it is cheaper. Decided to stay downtown, and the Hilton had very good rates compared to similar hotels. Staff was very friendly and efficient. 
Room was nice, and the kids enjoyed the pool while I made use of the whirlpool. You can self park next door with the validated rate of $26/day vs. $44 to valet. 
The hotel is a perfect location, near enough to Michigan Ave to walk, and a Red Line subway stop in front of the hotel. 
I would have liked to have a breakfast included with the room... that was the only draw back.

title: “Rejuvenating DC stay”
text: Accompanied my hubby to a conference in DC at the Mandarin Oriental where the hotel was comfortable, the bed heavenly, the decor understated Asian elegant. Awesome viiew of the Washington Monument from our room I enjoyed spending time in and around the pristine swimming pool with lap lane and comfy cushioned lounge chairs sunlit and with surprising harbor views. The women's spa facilities were superb with excellent steam room, therapy pool and shower feature. The bath and spa products were magnificent. The house keeping services were timely and unobtrusive. Because not many nearby dining options, ate several delectable meals at SouWest restaurant. hotel has a most convivial bar with live music in the evening. All service was uniformly excellent throughout the hotel even though the large scale doesn't allow it to be very personal. There were extra touches such as delivery of several daily newspapers, complimentary morning coffee service in the lobby and several free movie channels. A CVS and Starbucks next door supplied added conveniences. The concierge was helpful with easy directions to the Bureau of Printing and Engraving and Holocaust museum, easy walks close by. Hubby and I took quick walk to the nearby DC Wharf for fresh seafood lunch. other sights were also within easy walking or cab distance, as was a Metro stop. I had a fabulous time all in all, and amazed to end a city stay feeling so relaxed and refreshed.

title: “Reccommended”
text: Stayed just 1 night, after flying to LA before travelling inland, quality place, clean and well maintained, exellent staff, enjoyed the wine with the mangers in the evening and the breakfast before setting off. Well priced and well located for exploring LA.

title: “Clean and Comfortable”
text:
We stayed here for one night and were very comfortable in our room. The room was clean and the staff friendly.
Good value for money.

title: “A lovely , relaxing base from which to explore New York”
text:
As soon as I stepped from the sidewalk , I felt instantly relaxed. The staff are polite , friendly and knowledgeable , and the small size of the hotel gives it a personal touch that I haven't experienced before.
 Unlike other reviewers , I did not find the room to be small (we had a suite which worked out about £200 more for 6 nights) , and even though the sounds of the city were still evident , I slept like a log in one of the most comfortable hotel beds I've ever been in.
 The buffet breakfast is made up of pastries,bread,cereal and yoghurts with a wide selection of drinks , many of which are available throughout the day. Wine and cheese is served in the evening , the atmosphere is laid-back and its easy to forget where you are as you relax.
 The location is very central , about a 10 minute walk to Macys, 15 to Bloomingdales/Central park , and the Grand Central subway station in 5 minutes away.
 I would certainly return , and have no hesitation in recommending The Library to anyone.

title: “"Lack of basic facilities"”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights in September and apart from it's location there was nothing to like about it.The room I was allocated was situated at the rear of the building and was really quite cold because the heater was not working.There was no extractor fan in the bath/shower room,so after a shower there was condensation everywhere.The bed was very uncomfortable due to a very uneven and lumpy mattress,it only had one decent cover over the sheet,a small spare one I found in the cupboard helped,but not much.The biggest disappointment for me was the absence of a tea/coffee making facility in the room,surely a must have basic nowadays,especially for the price paid.Lesser hotels provide this facility,so why not this one?
I stayed in six hotels of varying standards while on holiday in the U.S. and would stay in all of them again.All,that is,except the Excelsior.I would not recommend this hotel because of the reasons stated,which is a pity because a couple of members of staff were helpful and it is in such a nice location.

title: “Nice location - staff could be better”
text: The best part of this hotel is the location - right downtown on the trolley line. The room was clean when we got there and the staff was friendly. We stayed for 3 nights and, unfortunately, had to nag housekeeping and the hotel staff to get the room cleaned. Towels/shampoo/soap were not replaced, even when housekeeping "remembered" that our room existed. No housekeeping came one day and came and only made the bed (with old linens) the next day. We had to find our own clean towels and toiletries. Otherwise a nice place to stay.

title: “Perfect Midtown Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Belvedere July 18-21, 2006. Having had some negative experiences in the past at Manhattan hotels, we were very pleasantly surprised by the quality of the Belvedere for the price ($200 a night, which to me is high, but not by NYC standards). All the staff members we encountered were friendly and efficient. Our room was spacious and looked recently renovated - very clean and pleasantly decorated. The bathroom fixtures also appeared to be new and well cared for. Housekeeping was great. The lobby and elevators were lovely old art deco. The view from our room (16th floor) was breathtaking. The 2 elevators are very small; this never caused us any problem until the day we checked out. Lots of others were checking out also and the volume did cause a wait of 10 minutes for the elevator. We didn't eat at the restaurants - had breakfast around the corner at the Olympic, which served good, hearty food for a reasonable price. The location of this hotel can't be beat for access to the theatre district, the great Hell's Kitchen restaurants and all other midtown attractions. I highly recommend!

title: “worked out just fine for me”
text: i stayed here for three nights last summer. i reserved a room w/private bath, and i think that's the way to go unless you want to feel like you're in a hostel. yes, you should be prepared to carry your own luggage up three or four flights of stairs, and the stairwells are kind of gross, but my room was perfectly clean and the bed was fine. i like the upper west side location-- as a female traveling alone, it's a neighborhood i feel safe in.

title: “Love Boston”
text: This was our first trip to Boston and it was fantastic. This charming hotel was very comfortable and great location. The staff was very helpful and friendly. From the minute we pulled up, we were greeted and felt very comfortable. The room was nice and roomy. Our room had two queen beds and the free coffee in the morning in the lobby was very nice. We were just a block from terrific shopping and great restaurants were all around us. I would defiantly recommend this hotel. We took the trolly tour that departed just around the corner from the hotel and it was a great way to see the city.

title: “Great Hotel, Excellent Staff”
text:
This is the third time we have stayed at the Elan in the last two years. Each time the staff have been excellent and very helpful. From the two Michaels on the front desk, Efrem (hope that's spelt right) out the front to the housekeeping staff nothing was too much trouble.
The breakfast and the wine and cheese are a nice touch and very much appreciated. Other little touches like the ice water and lemonade in the foyer really make a difference.
The location is hard to beat. The Beverley Centre is a minutes walk away, a CVS store even closer, a 10-15 min walk to the Grove and Farmers Market, many resturants near by.

title: “Never Ever”
text: Checked in Today, i ordered a superior Room and what I get is a very Small Room, Not possible to use for two People. They promise to make it better for tomorrow, we will See.

title: “First class stay!”
text:
