We stayed here for the weekend as an anniversary celebration. The room was fantastic. There was a large L shaped sofa (with a hide a bed) that had a rolling ottoman opposite the king sized bed. A large flat screen TV was on a swivel between the two, so watching the Olympics from either the sofa or the bed was comfy. Better yet the remote had an easy to use sleep timer - a rare and wonderful feature!
The hotel has a free shuttle that will take you to and from any destination within a 1 mile radius of the hotel. This covers nearly all downtown restaurants, the space needle, Pike Place Market, the Pacific Science Center, and great shopping. We didn't have to wait more than 10 minutes for the shuttle any time we called. It was fantastic.
The complimentary breakfast is one of the best I've ever had. Several hot selections that were interesting: bagel with ham, egg, tomato and spicy sauce; potato roll with ham, egg, and cheese; french toast; plus all the usual continental breakfast things you usually see.
The staff were all friendly and helpful. 
My only criticism would be that there are only 2 elevators and sometimes they run a little slow. Also the staff got a little overwhelmed during breakfast service. But it was still yummy.

title: “Great rates, clean rooms, and excellent service”
text: I stayed at the Courtyard Marriott twice recently. The service was extremely curteous and helpful, and the rooms were impecably clean. The room was spaceous and everything worked as it's supposed to. I'll definitely be staying here again.

title: “Trip to see Titanic Exhibit...”
text:
Stayed at the Westin. The lobby is breathtaking. The clerk was more than willing to change our room to a larger one, upon our arrival. They were very kind about giving dinner recommendations (go to the Burgundy Room on High Street for Tapas and Jeni's for ice cream!). The room was fantastic. Starbucks coffee with personal coffeemaker. Lovely bathroom. Very clean. Bed was truly heavenly. Would stay again and again. All thumbs up!
Only sidenote is parking-- lot is very small and there was a wedding there while we were staying. The spaces were so tight you needed a crowbar to get into your car. The parking attendants from Westin assured us that they would watch and make sure no drunk people smashed our doors getting into their car. All was well.

title: “Fairmont only fair.”
text:
We checked in Labor Day afternoon. Just to stay overnight was $209 not including the parking fee and taxes, which brought the total to almost $300.00. 
While the room was spacious and clean, it was just okay. And, we only had luke warm water for a shower after checking in. Something about maintenance cleaning out the system. 
Since the busy holiday weekend was over, the hotel was like a tomb. We saw maybe a handful of other guests the entire 24 hour period. Then what's with the exorbitant rate?
It was nice to be within a couple blocks of Original Joe's, but I'll stay elsewhere next time.

title: “Almost 100 stays”
text: Over the last 18 months I have stayed at this hotel almost 100 nights! It is an incredible place! Starting with Steve the night manager and ending with the best bacon on the breakfast buffet. The rooms are large and up to date, the place is clean and they are always replacing something (carpet, fixtures etc) to keep it up todate. I will always stay at this hotel when visiting Seattle.

title: “Beautiful, Clean, and Great Location”
text:
Stayed 4 nights at this Ritz. Traveling for pleasure. Loved the location. Far enough away from the touristy stuff but close enough to enjoy the touristy stuff. Super comfy beds.
Hotel is one block (up a STEEP hill) to the cable cars, which got me everywhere I needed to go. 
Concierge was FANTASTIC. Helped with restaurant recommendations and reservations. Helped get us acclimated to the area etc. 
Indoor pool was nice and clean. Wish it stayed open a bit later but it met our needs

title: “Wonderful 40th Birthday!”
text:
My husband and I just returned from our long and wonderful weekend stay at The Essex House. We stayed here 3 years ago when it was a Starwood property. 
We loved our stay! The newly renovated rooms are spacious and relaxing! We had a king room overlooking Central Park. We had two huge windows overlooking the park with a telescope to focus in on the park. We also enjoyed the comfortable beds, the sensored lights that turn on from the nightstands and bathroom in the dark...very cool, and flat screen television. We always had a clean room and plenty of drawer and closet space...not always the case in some NYC hotels.
The bathroom...which is very important for us...what amazing! We had a huge tub and a separate tile/glass door shower! Also, the thick towels and cool rose colored bowl sink...a nice extra. The bath gel, lotions and hair products from The Cornelia Spa smelled great.. 
A nice touch, they remembered it was my birthday..only mentioned it when booking, a small cake and champagne in our room...how nice after a great dinner at Le Bernadin, going to Jersey Boys and a special treat when we came back!
We love the Essex House...great job and pleasant staff!

title: “Comfortable Luxury”
text: Very modern hotel. Great location, easy access. Four Seasons quality in every aspect. The staff was superior and attentive. Had a small issue with computer access, but it was quickly remedied and made for a wonderful stay. Property is very new, well-maintained, and most importantly QUIET. I had a restful sleep after a long travel day and felt refreshed and ready for business the next day. I will definitely add this hotel to my favorites!

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: This hotel is well maintained and well run. Rooms are quite nice for the price and the pool area is lovely. It is near the Market Square attractions. Overall, a good value.

title: “nice for new york”
text: My husband and I spent our honeymoon at the Barclay over Thanksgiving and had a lovely stay. Yes, if you look beyond the period reproduction furniture and varnished woodwork that creates an impressively grand first impression, you will see dings and dents on walls, and dusty and torn carpet in corners. It is indeed an older hotel and if you pay particular attention, it shows. But the cleanliness and comfort levels of the room we had were impressive for New York, and the staff were notably friendly, expedient and competent. Our only complaints were paper-thin walls (perhaps due to ours being an adjoining room) and an ancient tube television with remote that we had to have fixed twice during our stay. Oh, and wireless internet should really be standard and free at a hotel of this rating. So the Barclay is not perfect, but perfect is hard to find in NYC, especially at a reasonable price. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “$20 to use the Fitness Center”
text: Fellow travelers take note - notwithstanding the hotel website's touting of the Equinox Spa and fitness center as available for guests, there is no mention that it costs $20 per day to use the fitness center - that little surprise is saved for your arrival only upon questioning. FYI.

title: “Nice, cozy place”
text: Nice, cozy place, right by the financial district. It's also a short cab ride to downtown, Little Italy, and Fisherman's Wharf. Chinatown is walking distance, but you do have to climb hills! It's nice little place, I would stay there again.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text:
Recently spent a long weekend at the Distrikt Hotel. Could not find a fault and versus other hotels we looked at great value for money.
Staff very friendly and helpful, room modern and well equiped. Located a couple of blocks across from time square hotel was in a great central location for getting round Manhattan.
If lucky enough to go back to New York, will definitly stay here again

title: “Welcoming”
text: Great locatiion,front desk extremely nice accomodated my request eventhough they were full dealing with othet guests, they always made me feel special,Gina ,Lois ,davId the room was in a quite location that i immediately went to bed. i asked for a late checkout and surprisingly i was not disturbed

title: “Tournament Hotel”
text: Stayed at this hotel as it was the host hotel for a tournament in the area. BUT it is the host hotel for numerous tournaments in the area so if you are looking for peace and quiet... good luck. Room was good, roomy, beds were too small, but the microwave and fridge in the room helped. Still, a little pricey compared to other equivalent hotels in the area. The only major complaint I would have was the customer service was really awful. The front desk staff did not make you feel welcome and it was like pulling teeth trying to get them to answer anything or do anything. Probably wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Great location, good hotel, good price”
text:
The Cow Hollow is perfectly placed for exploring San Francisco on a budget - we actually did quite a lot of walking round here, and it's near all the bus/tram routes (which we found rather infrequent, but then in London they come every 5 minutes!). The hotel had plenty of secure parking (a big bonus, especially if you want to leave the car for a couple of days). The rooms were a good size, clean, fairly up-to-date. The staff were really helpful with any questions we had, and as they are locals it's well worth picking their brains on local restaurants, pubs and clubs. The guy who booked us in let us know that he'd put us in the quietest room he had left, which was a nice touch.
The inn is also near Chestnut Street, which has a number of boutique shops and also a couple of supermarkets on it.

title: “Don't Be Fooled By Price Alone”
text: Rooms and food are average. Stay and park sounds like a good deal. Use it only if you have no need to get anywhere on time. Upon return we waited 45 minutes for the shuttle even after being told after our second call that it would be two minutes. It was actually twelve. We departed but turned around twice to go back for others. Service is not in the vocabulary of this far below average motel.

title: “Not your average Courtyard”
text: This property is unlike the business park Courtyards from the 80s/90s, the layout and feel borders on a "full service" ambiance. It has been kept up to date over the years with tasteful renovations and the rooms are always comfortable and a great value. Travelers coming in on the BART or CalTran do have a few block walk, but cabs are a good option if you have plenty of luggage or there's always the 10 or 12 MUNI lines that run up 2nd Street from Market. Valet Parking is VERY expensive so if you must have a rental, it is always wise to try to find street parking or maybe a lot down the street. Lastly, the service the F&B outlets especially The Whispers lounge does seem a bit impersonal and overal lacking. Overall though a good solid stay each time.

title: “New. Fair.”
text: The hotel looks brand new. The furniture is appropriate. It is really clean.

title: “Change the Sheets???”
text: Upon a late arrival, I climbed in bed to find a pair of footie socks from a previous occupant!! I took them to the front desk and gave them to the receptionist there who assured me the manager would be informed. I never heard from the manager nor was I compensated for such poor housekeeping! I was also awakened @ 3-5 am by my neighbors who were talking with their door closed yet they sounded like they were in my room! Breakfast was great and the room was spacious,but the dirty bed was a deal breaker for us to be able to recommend them or stay at one again!

title: “Small rooms but good view”
text: My room was small & smelt of stale smoke but fine for €100 per night. The hotel is huge and not very modern but it was a pleasant stay with great views.

title: “Great Staff”
text:
I recently traveled to Phoenix for work. After a long day and flight, I was exhausted. As I approached the front desk, the receptionist greeted me and helped me check in. She was very pleasant and helpful. Her personality was great and she had me laughing. For some reason this is what I needed at that time. Any time I had a question, they were there to help.
The staff was great, the food was great and the room was clean and comfortable. I travel often for work and when I come back to Phoenix, I wil make sure I stay here too.

title: “Pretty good”
text:
Needed to try and different hotel from The Dylan where I have stayed before and I'm glad I did. T
he Library is a nice small hotel, fairly unremarkable, not somewhere I'd take the Mrs for a romantic break but is plum in the middle of everything, has good staff, is clean, got a bit character and everything seems to work.
Will stay again.

title: “Perfect Weekend”
text: I took my wife for her 50th birthday to New York for the weekend and did we time it perfect. Weather was around 70 and sunny. I had let the hotel know we were celebrating her birthday and when we arrived there was a birthday cake and candles waiting in the room. The room was very clean and there was some noise from the street but very little, and you are in Times Square. We were in a perfect location for a weekend stay, close to some great bars, and restaurants. We took the Gray Line, hop on hop off bus, and were able to see alot of sights( Empire State Building, Little Italy, Chiiatown, Staten Island Ferry, Central Park). You just need to do some research so you know where things are before you get there. Be sure to try the Carnegie Deli, great sandwiches.

title: “A historic gem of a hotel in downtown Columbus. Relaxing and nice!”
text:
During a recent stay at the Westin Columbus, we were able to channel our inner historian in total relaxation. This gem of a hotel, in the heart of downtown Columbus is a rare find and a fantastic hotel destination for any family. The Westin Columbus is the oldest Westin hotel in North America. Opened as The Great Southern Hotel in 1897, it is a stately and historic monument to the great city of Columbus. From the time it was open until the hotel closed for a brief period in 1982, every sitting US President was a guest at the hotel.
The charm is apparent from the moment you step in. Marble floors, dark, pristine woodwork adorn each nook of this amazing building and the original stained glass windows set it apart. The hotel lobby welcomes adults and children alike with large sofas and chairs in a variety of sitting areas around the 2 levels that make up the common lobby area. We spent quite a bit of time just exploring. The large ballroom was simply breathtaking. An amazing place for a wedding reception with enormous stained glass windows, beautiful marble floors & high ceilings.
[----]
After checking in and riding up the historic elevator to the sixth floor, we stepped into our beautiful rooms. If you are traveling with more than one child, we always suggest booking adjoining rooms (if your budget allows). We stayed in a spacious corner suite that allowed us to set up a crib (provided by the hotel) and still have room to spare. A small dining table and sofa area made it feel more like a nice New York loft than a hotel room. Ask for a room looking down High Street. You'll have a beautiful view of downtown Columbus. We were thrilled wake up Saturday morning to watch over 50,00 people started down High Street in the Race for a Cure that raised over $2.5 million for breast cancer research! It was a pretty amazing site.
Connected to our room was a smaller, yet equally beautiful room with 2 double beds for our boys. Each room is full of character that only a historic building can offer such as large scale windows with over-sized ledges and ceilings that were 10-12 feet high.
There is something to be said for a great hotel when your 3 year old sleeps until 9am instead of the normal 6:30. They not only slept in but they crawled back in bed to color, to watch Food Network and just to cuddle up in the duvet. (As I am writing this, my 3 year old just packed his pajamas, his bunny, and flashlight in his suitcase. He wants to go back to the hotel and there is no talking him down. He is going to be ready no matter what.)
As with all Westin hotels, the bedding is incredibly sumptuous and soft, heavenly if you will. We absolutely love the billowy down comforters, down pillows, and crisp white sheets Westin spoils their customers with. As a self professed coffee snob, I was happy to not just tolerate my morning cup of joe but actually enjoyed my coffee both mornings thanks to the complimentary Starbucks coffee in each room.
Our boys felt so at home during our stay. The large flat screen TV in each room has a great selection of channels for kids (Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, PBS Kids & most importantly for Canaan, Food Network) and the nice sized bathtub made for a very fun evening bath time. I have to comment on the fact that the bathrooms are fantastic as well. With huge mirrors, marble floors and their 'heavenly' double-head shower you kind of feel like royalty.
If you can time your visit out right you may just be able to catch a performance at the beautifully restored Southern Theater which is attached to the hotel. Saturday evening, during our stay, The Ohio State University students were performing an opera. You are also only a mile away from the Columbus Blue Jackets, NHL hockey. It is an amazing venue with a full agenda of entertainment so be sure to check out their schedule.
The hotel restaurant, High Street Grill, was a great option for breakfast. The breakfast buffet was priced very reasonably and was really delicious. Our younger son opted for the kids Belgian waffle (which was really large). Mike went for the blueberry and orange pancakes that was a nice change from the typical buttermilk pancakes on most menus.
Every staff member we encountered during our stay was incredibly friendly and helpful. Our server at the restaurant, David, was so charming and sweet to our boys and the valet staff always had a smile and a kind word to say when we came and went.
Many great areas of downtown Columbus are within walking distance or a short drive of the hotel. German Village, the Short North Arts District, and the Brewery District are close by and are some of our favorites places to visit when in Columbus. Even when in the heart of downtown you can get to mega-shopping centers like Easton or Polaris in 15-20 minutes. Ohio State is just on the other side of downtown so it is a great place to stay if you are going to a football or basketball game as well.

title: “Has Trip Advisor become a new free advertising place for Jet Luxury and LHW?”
text:
Honestly I feel like I have to write a review for those of you who don't just want to read about jet luxury. Compared to other new five star hotels, there is absolutely nothing!! that stands out at the Setai. (maybe the air quality) 
The decor is extremely blah and I have a hard time believing that someone under 40 appreciates it. And if you like the Nespresso machine you can buy one for your house with the amount you'll be paying for taxes.
New York is known for amazing concierge. The only Staff I did find that was full of personality and stood out were the ones working at the bar. I would highly recommend the bar on fifth and you don't have to stay at the Setai for that.

title: “Affordable, Great Location, Beautiful Rooms”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel for one night. We sprung for a junior suite, so our room was quite spacious and we had a view overlooking Century 21 and the new WTC construction. We knew about the construction ahead of time and were interested in seeing how the rebuilding project was coming along. The view was actually pretty sweet! And the noise was very minimal - it didn't keep us up or anything like that. The room itself was tastefully decorated and very comfortable. 
If you're planning a trip to NY and want to do the downtown touristy stuff, this is a great place to stay - essentially on top of the WTC, walking distance to Battery Park City, Statue of Liberty tours, Wall Street, etc. There's also a subway stop nearby - maybe a block away.

title: “Great location and friendly staff”
text: Conveniently located near the Grove and Wilshire Boulevard, this boutique hotel offered excellent service, a great location and most accomodating staff. Even though off-street parking is not available, on-street permits are provided. The continental breakfast was much better than most and the staff extremely helpful. Rooms are spacious, clean and include a large screen TV.

title: “Not worth the price.”
text:
I stayed here because of the close proximity to the Convention center. The room was average, no better than Holiday Inn. Holiday Inn atleast provides free wifi and breakfast. This hotel has a water pipe problem and whenever one of my neighbors takes a shower it sounds like a 747 is landing in the room. It vibrates so hard that the shower handle has fallen off and into the tub twice. I told the staff and they just said they'd call maintenance. No "I'm sorry" or "thanks for letting us know" or offer to move me to another room. Several of the staff behind the counter were not very helpful either, chatting with each other vs assisting me. Others were very good though. There is mold on the grout in the shower. Only 30 channels on the TV, no Comedy Central. Coffee is terrible, no microwave, no airport shuttle service. I had an $18 grilled cheese sandwich and soup delivered to my room and the soup was terrible, bland, like nursing home food! Also, they kept having these alarms going off with overhead with instructions to vacate the building and then the elevators would be blocked off. On the bright side, the bed was very comfortable. The hotel does have a lot of amenities, but you will pay dearly for them all. 
This is my first and last stay in a Hilton hotel.

title: “Very convenient, historic property when staying in NY”
text: Less then 10 mins from the subway on the river. The bathroom has a view of the Statue of Liberty. Bunk rooms are small and bathroom is shared - but perfectly adequate for the budget traveller. Close to Chelsea markets and plenty of restaurants in the west village

title: “The staff steals”
text: We stayed here when our flight was snowed in. We left the hotel at 8:30 am in the hotel's shuttle back to the airport. When we arrived at the airport we called the front desk to say that we had left the ipod plugged into a lamp on the desk. The guy at the front desk said he'd go up to our room. I called back to the front desk 15 minutes later he said that when he opened the door the sheets had been taken off of the bed and the ipod wasn't there. We were told that the the woman who had cleaned the room said she hadn't been in there (even though security said her key card had opened the door). We have called and stopped back to the hotel. Eventually the GM credited us our room for that night but that only covers 1/3 the cost of the ipod. It is upsetting to know that your belonging are not safe in their rooms. As a side note room service took 90 minutes to arrive.

title: “Amazing experience!”
text:
The location is ideal- just footsteps from the heart of NYC. I also felt very comfortable staying there alone as a small female. 
The kitchenette in the suite made all the difference in saving money on eating while in the city. And the cost was amazing for all that came with the room!
The front desk was helpful and very knowledgable of transportation, entertainment and resources. My only complaint was that the front desk staff was small so sometimes I had to wait in a line just to ask a quick question.
Upon arriving I got to spin a wheel for members and got some free candy which was a big plus.
It was hard to stay sleeping due to traffic outside my window but it's NYC after all so I can't fault the hotel for that. 
The lobby was comfortable and had complementary lemonade in the afternoons as well as books or games to check out to use. 
For the value I paid, it went above and beyond.

title: “Top pick for airport hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed here one night on our way to Chicago a couple of weeks ago. The hotel and it's staff could not have been better. It was a terrific bargain as we took the park and fly pkg. which allowed us free parking for the week we were gone. The location was perfect and the 24hr shuttle was available for us early the next morning. Our room and the restaurant were very good.
The following morning at the airport I discovered that I'd left my prescription sunglasses in the room so I called security and spoke with the night manager, Bryan Williams, who's concern seemed so genuine as he assured me the glasses would be sent that day priority mail to me in Chicago. Sure enough, the next morning I received the package with the glasses. How gratifing it was to work with an employee such as Bryan who followed thru on this matter and I will surely recommend this hotel to anyone looking for an exceptional airport hotel.

title: “Another great stay here!”
text:
Stayed here one night with wife and two sons (7 and 4) to be close to Minute Maid Park. I did this a year ago with the boys and returned for this year's trip. You can't beat this place for a downtown sporting event - free parking, walking distance to Minute Maid Park or Toyota Center (felt safe walking back late from baseball game). The indoor pool is small, and it was very cold this time. The breakfast was great - well beyond typical HI Express, with scrambled eggs, sausage, and biscuits/gravy.
Room was very clean and comfortable. Internet worked well.
Had no encounters with panhandlers in the parking lot.
I definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “I wouldnt stay unless I had to!”
text: I had called ahead to see if we could check in early. When I got there the people at the front desk were very helpful and did let us check in early as agreed. When we got up to the room it was okay. I started looking around as soon I noticed stains on the lounge chair. The bathtub still had hair and water stains. I pulled back the little duvet cover and there were pieces of skin on the blanket. Yuck! I called down to the front desk and told them what I had found. They said they would send up housekeeping. I pulled off all the sheets, blankets and pillow cases.Two hours later when I finally calmed down I decided to get out of that room, still no housekeeping. I spoke with the front desk and they apologized and sent someone up as we were leaving. When we returned ofcourse the bed was made and the tub had been cleaned. Ofcourse they left a laminated note about how gallons of water are used everyday to clean hotel sheets and blah blah blah. Basically it said as a guest it was my choice to have my sheets cleaned everday or conserve water and not. I could care less, all I know is I want new linens and not skin flakes on the bed from the previous guest. Who knows if they really changed everthing or not but the appearance to skin flakes were gone, and the pillow cases didn't have hair on them. The tub was clean but there was stilll hair on the wall that I had to clean myself. The lobby is has been updated but the rooms need work. The bathrooms are updated with larger tiles and granite counter tops, but had stains in the walls. I was not impressed especially coming froma 4 star hotel in Dupont circle the two previous nights. The Hotel was close to the monuments, within walking distance, but not in the best neighborhood in the other direction.The grounds are kept up and clean. The pool looked okay although I didnt swim. There aren't many restaurants right by the hotel. McDonalds is the only fast food. Your also right by the free way. Go to Justins Cafe by the Nationals Stadium for good beer, pizza and such.

title: “LAX close!”
text: HAve stayed many times and had a good experiance. This Weston is a little older but the rooms a good and the nights sleep is great and LAX is less than 5 minutes away. Great way to start our trip.

title: “Really great place to stay”
text: Wonderful two-night stay at the Topaz for my husband and me while visiting relatives. Service was excellent and friendly. They helped us with early check-in after red eye flight and with airport transportation on the way home. The room decor is chic and contemporary which we really liked. You can't get a better location than Dupont Circle area -- nice neighborhood, good food, easy Metro access, plenty to see nearby. The price was very reasonable for a big-city hotel. It was my second stay at a Kimpton, and I'm very impressed with their unique properties and customer orientation.

title: “Best deal in Frisco”
text: We stayed at the Nob Hill Motor Inn on the 16th, 17th and 18th of June and can't say enough good things about this motel. The location is perfect, the room was clean and comfortable, free parking, continental breakfast and a very helpful and FRIENDLY staff. Thanks Frank and Judy for making this a memorable vacation.

title: “Great location”
text: Fantastic location and very friendly staff. They were handing us water bottles as we entered and exited. We lucked into a corner room so had a huge room. I do think it's crazy that the more inexpensive hotels have free wi-fi but you have to pay at the Hilton. We were at a Hampton Inn the night before and had free wi-fi and breakfast. To be fair, the coffee cups in the room were disposable at the Hampton.

title: “Wonderful Facilities, Great People”
text:
Since the moment I got to the hotel, staff made me feel at home. 
Loved the location of the property within walking distance from Riverwalk and the view from the room overlooking the Alamo. Rooms were clean and comfortable with all the expected amenities plus a little extra effort in the bathroom supplies. 
Will gladly stay at the Crockett anytime !!

title: “Good location and value for NYC - clean and updated”
text: Finding a nice hotel in NY can be pretty tricky, especially if you don't want to fork over the $500+/nt for the high end hotels (which are very nice- just pricey). This place was a nice little surprise. Not the best I've stayed in, but it was clean, quiet, and in a good location, and for the price, its hard to do better. The staff were very friendly, especially the gentleman working the front desk in the evenings. A few things did bother me, like the size of the rooms. Yes it is standard NY, but I was very disappointed that the standard room came with a double. The room was surprisingly clean and well appointed. Lots of wood accents and the bathroom was very nice as well. All in all, it was a nice hotel and I may stay here again if I want to do NY on a budget.

title: “Very Hip Hotel with Comfortable Room”
text: Very good experience at the Palomar in Dupont Circle. Great location, 5 minute walk to the Metro. We stayed in a suite, with our two kids., which was very spacious and comfortable. We didn't make it to the daily happy hour -- but it looked very nice, with lots of activity in the lobby. Staff was very friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Perfect”
text: We stayed for 2 nights in April. Easy walking distance to Graceland. Rooms and grounds clean and well kept. The bed was very comfy with lots of pillows. Microwave and fridge in room was nice. Loved the shower rod that extends the curtain out so you have more room. The hotel offers discounts to Graceland tour and Memphis tour and also for Marlowe's restaurant. Tracy at the front desk was very helpful. I loved the guitar shaped pool even though it was empty because it was early in the season. We enjoyed the Elvis movies in the room. The lobby has lots of Elvis memorabilia but the rooms just have a few pictures, not overdone. I would definitely recommend it!

title: “Great Location”
text: Right next door to the metro and only a few blocks walk to the national mall and museums. Didn't use pool or restaurant so can't comment there. Room was clean and perfectly adequate for a short stay. Staff was fantastic, friendly and helpful at every turn.

title: “Graet value for the money”
text: Hotel Metropolis is a fine hotel. Yes, it is steps away from what might scare someone from the suburburbs, but if you are a person with an opened mind you will enjoy the added "flavor". The staff was very helpful and cheerful. The hotel itself is fine for the money ($100) I loved that the shower head was adjustable (at 6 ft I hate doing the shower limbo) and the wireless internet that actually work well. I also enjoyed that the windows opened so I could enjoy the sounds of a city full of life. So if you want to save some money and enjoy the city, this is the hotel for you, if you want to insulate yourself from the city and its beautiful people, stay at the one of the many airport hotels and it will be just like you never left home.

title: “Impeccable”
text: The hotel is beautifully decorated, fresh and clean. I love the location--many good restaurants and shopping nearby. The rooms and beds are very comfortable and roomy by NYC standards. We were originally given a room with a view of "ground zero" and the Hudson River in the background. When we found this too depressing we requested another room and were given a room with a view of the Brooklyn Bridge with no problems. We enjoyed the view and our stay very mush. Great staff! Only one complaint was that when we left for breakfast and came back to our room the maid had already stripped our bedding off. It was only 9AM!

title: “Not worth it. Put money towards the Hilton.”
text: I I arrived at hotel early at 12:37pm. I had to wait a few moments to have a clerk help. I asked to check in early she said no after letting the person in front of me check in. I had to wait until 2 pm to check in. Even then she said they may not have a room ready.

title: “Very Friendly, nicely placed”
text: NIce hotel, and very helpful and friendly staff. I had a few problems with parking (valet was completely jammed, and the self park card they gave me didn't work), but they went out of their way to make it up, and overall, I was really impressed with the hotel. I was particularly impressed with the front desk staff, who were really helpful.

title: “Lovely boutique hotel”
text:
We enjoyed our stay very much. The hotel is in the Dupont Circle neighborhood, so not directly in the middle of the city; taxi at rush hour from Union Station cost us $30; $12 on the way back on Sunday morning. You can take the Metro if you arent hauling a lot of luggage. Bear in mind, the hotel is about a 5-block walk from the Dupont Circle Metro station, uphill, so you wont want to be dragging luggage uphill.
I was concerned when we were given a room on the second floor that looked right out on a sidestreet, but this was the quietest room I have stayed in for a long time, and I travel a lot for business.
Hotel staff was very accommodating. Upon request, they provided a map of both the Metro and the local attractions, as well as a list of restaurants within walking and driving distance. We had some problems with the toilet - not unusual for an old building - which were addressed quickly and pleasantly.
The room was small but comfortable with a working fridge and a comfortable king sized bed and spacious bath. Vending machines offering snacks and beverages (except for bottled water) were on alternating floors.
We were within walking distance of several diverse restaurants, shops, and the Metro station. The Metro was easy to use to get to the National Mall. Taxis were readily available.
Food was not cheap, but was of good quality. If you are like me and like to buy soda and snacks from the local convenience store, you may find this a challenge - we couldnt find any. If you are looking for a really great burger joint, go to Five Guys on Connecticut; you wont be sorry.
The only downsides were little things. Besides expensive meals, there was the Internet. I was told there was no free access, so I paid 9.95 to log on from the room. Later, in the elevator, saw a note to guests saying there was free Internet from the Lounge. The room was comfortable, but there was no where to sit except the bed. The housekeeping staff left a bag of trash in a nook by our room; apparently forgot to take it away when s/he cleaned up.
We enjoyed our stay and will definitely stay at the Churchill again.

title: “A very pleasant (and needed) surprise!”
text:
I was returning from a vacation at the Grand Canyon where the lodgings were a bit stark (but clean). I had not stayed at a Radisson Hotel in years and was a bit wary considering the online price I paid--about $70! The website promised me a comfortable bed (a sleep number bed), and I needed that very much after five nights at the Grand Canyon lodge. 
What a great surprise! The hotel was easy to find, and I got a parking space right out front! The registration person was friendly, helpful, and fast. I was in my room in no time. And what a great room! The bed was marvelously comfortable, and the room had a great work/relaxing area (with a flat screen television)--and free Internet! Everything was very clean as well. Needless to say, I had a wonderful night's sleep and felt refreshed and ready to face the long flight home the next day.Without a doubt, I would stay at this hotel again.

title: “I stay here all time, however this time I was truly DISAPPOINTED”
text:
I want to start with ROmeo at the front desk was great and did give us a nice room. Now as for this trip, I usually stay here when traveling for business, so it was a natural choice to stay here for a personal trip.
TOTALY DISAPPOINTED. I guess i have to be traveling for business to have great service. my disappointment is really with the rooftop which even though it separate fro the hotel, it bears the same name and is in the same building and the service was horrible particularly for a hotel guest.
Unfortunately I'm traveling to NYC in two weeks for work and don't think I will be staying here anytime in the near future...

title: “Comfortable, friendly & great location”
text: My wife & I stayed for 3 nights after picking hotel from reviews on TA. Its a modern hotel, very comfortable fairly spacious rooms (We had a corner room overlooking the Granary Burial Ground- not that spooky). Bed & bedding extremely comfortable, plenty of lighting, armchairs, iPod alarm & DVD player,safe,free wi-fi (If you join Kimpton in-touch loyalty scheme), iron & ironing board. Bathroom large with a great large walking shower. Good quality complimentary toiletries. Minor issue was hairdryer only had a 2foot lead so one had to bend down to use the dryer and the mirror at the same time. Staff extremely friendly & helpful - suggested alternate nearby locations for breakfast (we followed advice & had one breakfast at Paramount Breakfast Bar - Charles St. great for good value omelette, home fries etc). Nice touch was complimentary wine every evening 5-7pm (1, 2 or more glasses if you wished) But the real benefit was the location close to Boston Common, Faneuil Hall and right on Freedom Trail. Would stay there again. Good quality accommodation at good price (Booked via net but some months in advance)

title: “Great Location”
text: We recently had the opportunity to visit New York prior to a New England cruise and chose the Omni as our pre and post cruise hotel. The location of the hotel was perfect for first time visitors to New York! We could walk to so many iconic landmarks and the hotel staff were very helpful with restaurant reservations and directions. The whole experience was amazing and we were very pleased with the Omni!

title: “Was a pleasurable experience”
text: It is an older hotel so it isn't perfect, but it was clean. The service was great. The lobby is gorgeous. It is downtown Los Angeles ALL areas down there are bad at night, you just make sure you go outside with a group - you will be fine. They have covered secured parking and have security in lobby. We never felt unsafe.

title: “Excellent NYC Hotel”
text: I stayed here when it was a Red Roof Inn and it was great. It is even better now. It is clean and quiet and the location is great!

title: “Excellent, relaxing stay”
text:
Stayed in an executive suite for $369 plus taxes per night booked online direct with accor hotels. Bedroom was very spacious with huge balcony (pity it had 2 inches of snow on it which never melted due to the freezing weather last week!), very spacious separate lounge also.
Bathrooms are lovely, particularly liked the little touches like fresh flowers and candles. Forgot to take conditioner and shower gel but no probs as toiletries were replenished daily.
Found all the staff very polite and helpful and all the expected staff were present whenever we entered or left the building.
Had dinner on our first night - fillet mignon for me and lobster ravioli for my husband- and thoroughly enjoyed it. Also had breakfast twice and was impressed by choice available and service of staff.
The location of the hotel couldn't be better and yet once inside you would never know that you were in the heart of midtown.
In short, we have been to New York a few times and this was by far the best hotel we've stayed in.

title: “Great location.”
text:
The Magnolia is a wonderful hotel, a contemporary hotel located in a building from the 1920's. It is fun and hip, and walking distance to many restaurants. The staff are delightful. 
The room could be a bit brighter, but it was not a major problem. 
A bit noisy when the clubs close and people return to the hotel late at night. 
For what we paid, the value was outstanding. We would stay here again when next in Dallas.

title: “Wyndham Jacksonville Riverview”
text: The hotel staff is very friendly, tehy are attentive to your needs and quick to assist. Housekeeping does a wonderful job without being to overbearing about your items being left out. There were a couple of things about this property I didn't like. 1st. It's old, and I do mean old you can see the dingy carpets and the old fixtures and stucco style painting and trim. The conference rooms have very old and stained carpet and I wouldn't want to hold a wedding reception here. It is conveniet to the river and downtown Jacksonville. All in all I probably wouldn't stay here again, but for the price I don't think you will find anything better in Jacksonville.

title: “Not the best”
text:
PROS: Very clean and comfortable rooms, friendly staff, widescreen plasma tv (no high-definition broadcasts though), very comfortable beds/pillows, excellent climate control, great view either side (if you don't mind looking at ground zero on the hudson river side [they refer to over-looking ground zero as "city view"]), pool and excercise room, easy subway access to everywhere.
CONS:No king beds facing away from ground zero, only queen (which looked like full size), construction on ground zero 7 days a week from about 6:00 am to 3:00 pm (muffled noise), no coffee in rooms (have to go to restaurant to purchase and coffee was not good and not hot), no in-room refrigerator, charge for high-speed internet access (no wireless in rooms), walls not as sound-proof as other hotels (fine unless you have noisy people next to you or want to sleep in on ground zero side).
If this hotel added a few MINOR ammenities like FREE in-room coffee and refrigerator and FREE wireless internet access, I would have felt better about the construction noise and the price. The way they nickel and dime I was surprised that they didn't charge to use the toilet. Penny-wise and pound foolish. 
Overall a comfortable, somewhat noisy average stay. C+

title: “Great location, average hotel”
text: My partner and I stayed for 3 nights at the Best Western River North in September. It was the start of a road trip travelling north around Lake Michigan, into Canada including Toronto and Niagara and back down to Chicago. Our main concerns were a good location and free parking and the hotel certainly provided that but we had issues with our room (No. 329) overlooking the back of the building and a very noisy deli and side street. The room was spacious, definitely one of the larger ones we came across on the trip and the bed was clean and comfortable but the decor was old and drab and there was a musty smell in the corridor. The air con was very noisy and we needed to have this on at night. We stayed at several Best Westerns on our trip and the drab brown decor and musty smell seems to apply to almost all of them. I think this group is falling way behind the Hampton Inns (by Hilton) and Marriott group hotels and the difference in price is not that much. The hotel offers free internet and coffee in the lobby which is fairly standard for most hotels. They have an on site restaurant, Pizzeria Ora which was ok for breakfast. There are many dining options nearby and within a couple of blocks and this appears to be a safe area. However, this hotel was not cheap even for a large city and the location and free parking are the two big pluses but we would choose a different hotel next time. Chicago is lovely but despite the location this hotel is not the best.

title: “Excellent customer service & Pleasant Stay”
text: The hotel was clean and kept. The staff is very friendly and courteous. I had an amazing night of sleep thanks to the comfortable bed and pillows. The room was clean and everything operable. No Complaints!!

title: “Good but....”
text:
As other reviewers have stated this is not a 4 star hotel. The reason why is the details. 
Location:
The location is in the heart of The Magnificent Mile, perfect location and easy access to the "L", shopping, food, cabs, Navy Pier, and a variety of tours.
First impression:
The front of the hotel is actually on the side, not Michigan Ave due to shops below. The bell boy station is on the ground floor while the lounge and check in are on the second flood. The hotel lobby is nice but again is just lacking some details to make it a 4 star. 
Rooms:
We were able to check in early and they bumped us up from a petite to a queen. The queen room #923 was still small but nice. The bathroom is what you would expect from a 2-3 star hotel. No counter space at all. Lacks towels (only 2) we had to call daily for more. The fridge has smart tech so if you even move it they will bill you! I was just looking at what they had and they billed me $26! They were nice enough to take it off, so that was nice. The bed was fine and overall the room was nice but again it is the details that kill the hotel. Scratches, paint chips, wallpaper that is peeling, paint touch ups that were a little different then the original paint (lazy), and what I was shocked to see was the cheapest of light fixtures in the bathroom. Something you might see in your garage! 
Staff:
We had a nice experience with the staff. As I said very nice, let us check in early, gave us a free upgrade, fixed my bill, held our luggage when we checked out. The staff was great. I did witness a bellboy that was a little rude to a teenage kid who pushed a button in the elevator after it had already been pressed and the bell boy said "it was already pushed why would you push it man!?"...I thought that was a little rude. 
The Tip, Top, Tap is now just a ballroom and they must make good money renting it out because it would make a cool restaurant with the views....however, I'm not sure they would have the attention to detail to pull it off.
I would stay here again, but they need to pay attention to the little things to get it right. For me the price and location were right, we were out and about most of the time so we didn't have a lot of time to see everything with the hotel. 
Good hotel that could be better....

title: “Fantastic!”
text:
My wife and I stayed here on a Saturday night while visiting friends in the city. As we had arrived in the East Bay, the easy access from BART was great. 
We arrived at the hotel at 1:00, and were allowed to check-in early as our room was ready. We were also upgraded from the basic room to a waterfront room. Prompt and courteous service from every staff member we encountered. 
The hotel has a beautiful aesthetic - very relaxing. The furnishings in our room were top-notch, with very comfortable beds. Though our room overlooked the Embarcadero, it was very quiet. The hotel provides a nice stereo with Hotel Vitale branded "mood music" CDs, which were surprisingly cool. Free wifi - which is such a rare treat in nicer hotels - and great bath products. We also enjoyed the Sunday Chronicle delivered to our room. 
This is a great hotel for vacationing in SF, and it seems like it would be an excellent option for business travel as well.

title: “Good experience with a few exceptions”
text:
We stayed at the Alex for five days and found it to be a pleasant experience. The central location made it as easy to walk uptown as downtown and there are many terrific breakfast places en route to tourist destinations. Our suite was modern, spacious, and in good condition and we received prompt attention when we had questions or difficulties with any of the features. Hotel staff were friendly and courteous. 
The only difficulties we had were with the amenities of the hotel such as the televisions, lighting fixtures, the shower, locks and the elevator. These were far from person friendly and generally took some practice to operate with any success. The elevator in particular seemed to have a mind of its own (we nicknamed it Hal) and would often stop at every floor to see if there were people who might like to get on. Other times, it would assign the elevator the furthest away to your floor while others came and went. This is apparently a very hi-tech set up but it left us a bit anxious about getting up and down to our room on the 31st floor. 
All in all though The Alex was a great place to stay and we received a very reasonable deal with flight on expedica.

title: “The perfact hotel, perfact service amazing rooms, great food and wonderful kids club. If you can afford it, it will be the best”
text: We love this place. It's our 4th time here, we have been here every thanksgiving in the past 3 years. It's a really special place here, amazing, amazing, amazing service and care. Even if they mess up, which rarley happens they will know how to make you feel better. The staff is super helpful and nice, spa is UNBELIVBLE and my kids loves the kids club here. I have only good things to say.

title: “Not terrible but doesn't live up to the hype”
text:
This hotel is living off its former glory. It desperately needs a makeover. What was considered luxurious and well designed 30 years mow seems run of the mill and verging on tacky.
The tv set was a 30 year old clunker from Zenith. I don't care much for television when I travel (I don't think I turned it on once). I just mention it because it's an apt metaphor for my entire experience.
For starters, I arrived at 4pm only to find out that my room was not ready. They took my cell phone number so they could call me when they were ready for me, but they never called. I popped by at 6 to discover that my room was ready and was left to wonder if they ever would have called me. (no apologies either).
When I got to my room (which was no easy task as room 410 isn't even listed as a possibility on the signs facing the elevator) I was shocked to see how small it was (considering the amount of time it took to clean, check out is at 11 am by the way). It's one of those deals where opening the door to the bathroom almost collides with your bed. As for the view, I suspect some people in prison enjoy a better vista.
They offer a complementary continental breakfast but I wonder what continent they are referring to. No customary cereal, cheese, or yogurt options. Just a sad fruit salad and a muffin or white or whole wheat toast. Again, I thought of prison as the service was less than smiley.
The best thing about this place is the wonderful location and the building itself, one of the Chicago's oldest skyscrapers.
Everything else was a disappointment.

title: “It's all about location, location”
text: The selling point forthis hotel is location. It is across the road from Penn Station, near Macy's , close to subway connections , other key tourist destinations such as the Empire State Building If you are travelling by train in the US then this is a great location for a night or two. The rooms are quite clean if rather compact but we found it a comfortable overnight stay

title: “Excellent customer service but improvements can be made to rooms.”
text: The rooms are nice but they could use children's channels (Disney channel, Nickelodeon, Toon Disney, etc...) instead of making parent's pay $9.99 for a package of Disney programs that can be viewed for a 24-hour period. Free wireless internet would also be good. A refrigerator and/or microwave in the room could also improve the room. The restaurants in the hotel were good and employees at the Starbucks cafe were very friendly.

title: “Great Hotel Great Service”
text: I loved the Doubletree at Southpark. The rooms were very nice, clean, and well kept. The hotel staff was very proffessional and polity. We had a great weekend at the Doubletree Guest Suites hotel. I can not wait for next years Great Grapes! Wine Arts and Food Festival at the Southpark Mall.

title: “Great Value”
text:
We stayed at the Affinia Manhattan for 7 days in April 06, we were allocated a suite on the 27th floor, the suite was quite a substantial size and consisted of a seperate kitchenette complete with microwave, fridge and oven, a storage cupboard with safe, a lounge with chair, sofa, disc player and tv, goodsize bedroom with an absolutely brilliant bed ,another store cupboard, tv and a adequate size bathroom.
The decor and furnishings were more budget orientated but overall very clean.
The staff were very helpful, so where's the catch, well it can be noisy, located on 7th Avenue opposite Penn and Madison there is constant traffic from the early hours of the morning until the late,late hours of the night but hey! this is Manhattan after all, and you soon acclimatise to the bustle and the noise.
There is no restaurant in the actual hotel as such, but there is Niles restaurant next door where you can breakfast, lunch and dine if you so wish,although personally we found this to be expensive and not that great a cuisine.
Maceys is just a couple of blocks uptown and if like us you are visitors to the states call into the Maceys visitor centre prio to purchasing your Calvin Clein or Donna Karen, show some ID and get a discount card worth another 11% on all you buy, use as many times as your budget will allow.
For getting around we purchased the Metro 7 Day card for approx 28$ p/person this allows you unlimited travel on the underground and on the buses, this is really good value when you consider that a two day pass on the tourist bus can cost 90$ p/person
Overall the Affinia Manhattan is in a great location and offers excellent value.
Have a great holiday.

title: “Easy access to all major sites”
text:
We had driven past the Seal Rock Inn on several occasions during our previous stays in the city, always assuming that it would be out of our price range. We have tried several other hotels on the west side in the Sunset District with less than satisfactory results. 
Prior to booking the rooms I used Trip Advisor to look at past reviews and was somewhat concerned with a couple of reviews I read. The reviewers had been negative about both the motel and restaurant. We elected to give the place a try, and were glad that we did. None of the concerns addressed by the negative reviews were experienced by us during our stay. 
The location just can't be beat. We tend to spend most of our time with our 7 year old daughter checking out the Zoo, Exploratorium, Academy of Sciences, spending time along the ocean and in Golden Gate Park. The Seal Rock Inn is located adjacent to Sutro Park and trails are available literally just across the street. Very easy access to all out favorite haunts and easy to access Fishermans Wharf if so desired.
The room was spacious and clean. The bathroom had been recently remodeled and was well done with new fixtures and new tile. 
The management and staff were friendly and helpful. 
The restaurant staff was pleasant, although the service was a little slow. The food was average and the pricing also average for the San Francisco area. 
Overall we were quite pleased with our experience and will return to the Seal Rock on our next trip, and subsequent trips as well.

title: “great hotel, excellent location!”
text:
this was my first trip to boston. we chose the parker house for it's great ratings and superb location. we were not disappointed. i loved the location - i did a lot of sightseeing by foot and the freedom trail is literally right outside the hotel's door.
the lounges and restaurant were nice and the rooms very comfortable. i would definitely stay here again.

title: “Terrific Hotel”
text:
I stayed for two nights over the weekend, and can't say enough good things about the hotel! It was in a great location - right across from City Hall. Check in was quick and smooth by friendly staff. The room was very spacious, clean and comfortable. The king size bed was the best part of the room. 
The free continental breakfast in the morning was out of this world, with everything from hot items - eggs, sausage, pancakes, and the make your own waffle station, to the cold items - yogurt, fresh fruit, donuts, and cereal.
The hotel was in walking distance to the historic area (where I highly recommend the Ride the Duck tour). There were many great restaurants and bars all in walking distance.
I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Wonderful Place To Stay”
text:
We just got back for a 4-day stay at the Manhattan Club. It was an ideal location, our junior suite was clean, nicely furnished and larger than most accommodations in NYC. The only negative comment we have is that they let no one check in before 4:00 P.M. Suddenly at 4:00 P.M., all the rooms were ready. We got caught in a terrible rain downpour and were soaked by the time we arrived at The Manhattan Club at 2:00 P.M. we kept checking to see if we could get into our room to change into dry clothes: however, that was not going to happen. 
We did not let this spoil our stay. The accommodations were excellent. I would not hesitate to stay there again.
The Simms
Virginia

title: “AMAZING Hotel! Perfect stay!”
text: I just returned from an amazing trip to NY and a perfect stay at The James! Do yourself a favour and book this hotel immediately! The doormen, lobby, receptionists, rooms, turn down service, rooftop pool/deck/bar. Everything about it is fantastic. New to the area? Ask CHRIS or GIOVANNI (doormen) for ANYTHING and they will have the answer. They truly made my stay amazing and I can't thank them enough. Stay at The James...thank me later!

title: “Cheap, clean and central”
text: Stayed here two weeks ago with my boyfriend and really enjoyed it. It's so central making it easy to get around and cheap because all the main transport routes are on your doorstep. The rooms are small but cosy and clean as the shared the bathrooms and toilets - no queing either which was a bonus. The complimentary tea and muffins were a nice start to the day and the staff were fairly helpful. All in all good value for a city base to explore from.

title: “Pricey but worth it”
text:
If you don't mind old, this is a place to do business, enjoy the city and pamper yourself.
Good solid old style service, Voyagecritic litte bit biased because they found me a great room amidst the chaos created by the storm in NY...
Great restaurants, very good bars, 10th floor lounge has breathtaking view
perfect location
Will i go back? Yes

title: “Good place for a stop over”
text: I've stayed at this hotel twice for a stop over on arrival in LAX and found it to be absolutely fine. If you book nice and early you'll get an excellent price and the rooms are decent and clean. Agree the shuttle bus can be a bit slow to turn up but upsides outway this. 2 tips for long haul travellers looking for a stop over. Never pick up your hire car until the next morning (this could save you money and definitely will save you hassle when your tired) & if your looking for some food/drink the Marriott is very walkable from this hotel (200 metre's max) and has an excellent sports bar to relax in.

title: “Great conference hotel”
text:
We used the Omni Fort Worth for a 600-person conference. We had a great experience. All of the hotel staff were so accomodating and hospitable. The rooms were large and comfortable - and the bathrooms were awesome! Huge shower stalls.
Everything was very clean and comfortable, and beautifully decorated. The flair of Fort Worth was present in all of the details. The hotel restaurant - Cast Iron - had a delicious Sunday brunch, and their lunch and dinner options were great as well.
The location of the hotel was right across the Convention Center, but a couple block walk up to Sundance Square where the restaurants and nightlight were.

title: “The Worst Experience”
text:
Although recently renovated, this hotel does not live up to the expensive redo. Staff is smug and non responsive to guests' needs. Telephone operator is not always available to answer your calls (the hotel itself sometimes will not answer),and sometimes your wake up calls will be forgotten. Rooms are inadequately furnished (my room did not have shelfing for my clothes in the closet), although the bed is indeed very confortable. Door staff is more for show than help, since they are always busy either talking to each other or checking out passing people on the street.
As a whole, I would not recommend this hotel, it was a very disappointing stay.

title: “Enjoyable stay - busy hotel”
text: We spent the Easter long weekend in Chicago and stayed at the Hyatt Regency. The location was very convenient. Close to Magnificent Mile, within walking distance of Navy Pier, only a few blocks from the subways and close to the 146 bus to Museum campus. The coffee shop in the lobby is open 24 hours which made it very convenient for the really early risers or getting a late night snack. The Bar above the lobby level was also a great location to enjoy a drink after a busy day of sightseeing or shopping. The hotel is very large and very busy so you do need to be acceptable to a large convention hotel environment. We had a room at the end of the hall and although it was far from the elevator, we didn't have any issues with noise that others have commented on. The negative part was that there doesn't seem to be enough elevators for the size of the hotel when the hotel is full. Therefore at times when the convention that was inhouse was in motion, a couple of times we waited up to 10 minutes to get onto an elevator to go to the lobby. Also, although there are minibars in the room, the hotel visibly discourages (almost threatens) guests to not put any of your own items in there so if you have medication to store, it might be worth mentioning it at checkin. Oveall, the staff at the hotel were friendly and helpful. Our group was able to take advantage of great packages that included parking or breakfast which added good value to the room rate.

title: “Staff is tops and facilities are excellent”
text: Second stay at the sought after Hampton Inn at Phillps Place in Charlotte in the last two months. This hotel presents as a luxury hotel and offers a much warmer friendlier atmosphere than its competitor, the full scale Marriott nearby where I have also stayed. Stay at the Marriott if you like to put your credit card in a machine (hated this) to get a morning cup of coffee in the lobby. If you want a bar on sight, the Marriott offers dining and a couple of options on foot. Stay at the Hampton if you like coffee in your room and breakfast included and a lighter brighter lobby. Stay at the Hampton if you want some superb options just out the door for dining and shopping in a nice outdoor shopping upscale village atmosphere. First stay had adjoining rooms with kitchenette for a get away for four college roommates having a reunion after 30 plus years. We loved being able to walk to Charlotte's fine dining and shopping options from this hotel. Second stay at the Philips Hampton this week solo included the same pleasures for dining and a room with a safe, coffee, frig and many comforts. After enjoying a late check out, I worked a couple more hours in the attractive and sunny dining area online on my laptop with the staff's gracious support. This time I had packed a lot of high end costume jewelry packed because I was attending black tie events. I had it locked up in the safe in my Hampton room and of course I walked out and drove home without it and didn't even miss it for 24 hours after I got home. Called the Hampton South Park at Phillips Place and Whitney answered the phone and immediately reassured me that my jewelry was locked up in the manager's office safe and sound where it had been found and immediately turned into the office. Manager Greg called me personally to arrange for FedEx shipping and proper insurance. Jewelry case arrived at my house quickly with every item in it just as I left it. Kudos to Whitney at the front desk and to Greg for the follow-up phone calls and rapid and kind action and response. This hotel doesn't really need my positive review but I can assure you it is friendly and a luxury property with an exceptional management staff.

title: “THE ONLY PLACE TO STAY IN SAN DIEGO”
text: Well where do I begin. I have been staying at this outstanding hotel for the last several years. First off, the location is the best, right near the Seaport Village and near the Gaslamp district (Convention center is also nearby) and the San Diego Trolley (Metro) is 50 feet away. That being said, the hotel is outstanding. Very modern and so clean. Checking in is a breeze (if your a Platinum or Diamond member with Hyatt you have your own check in area) as I am a Diamond member. The rooms are oustanding and the views are incredible. Every room has some sort of view of the harbor and/or city. The rooms are very modern and spacious. The beds are the most comfortable ones around it is even hard to get up in the morning. The pool area is great and inviting. The service is impeccable, every one of the staff members goes out of their way to assist you and make your stay most memorable. The restaurant choices are all good too and the Top of the Hyatt bar and lounge on the 40th floor is a view to die for. You must have a drink there. When issues come up sometimes during our stays, they were fixed promptly and it was made right. Example went to the Grand Club to get a snack, but since they were extremely busy no items left in the club, so I told the front desk and presto the items I wanted were delivered to my room free of charge. It is those extra things that count. In seeing some of the other reviews, I don't know what happened during their stays, but if you are not happy speak to someone in charge to make it right. That is what Hyatt does for its guests. Enjoy your stay at this hotel, you will like it.

title: “San Antonio Gem!”
text:
From the moment we arrived, we realized that the staff was going to go above and beyond in every way possible. We were greeted in the front carport and asked if we were interested in valet parking. We said yes, our bags were removed from the car and we were shown into the lobby. We got to the front desk where a friendly clerk asked if we wanted a king suite or a double queen suite. We went to our king suite and found a lovely sitting room with large flat screen TV and, appropriately, Spanish styled furniture, then on to the dressing area with beautifully appointed bath, large counter with coffee fixings and mini bar for those who would choose to use it . Beyond that area was the bedroom with our very comfortable king bed and another large flat screen TV. The bed area was private and had a door to close it off from the sitting area where one could use the sofa sleeper. 
After a full day of sightseeing and enjoying the Riverwalk in San Antonio, we returned to our hotel and enjoyed the beautiful evening on the patio outside the lower level bar. The patio is right on the water and we sat and watched the boat cruises go past for awhile. We soon returned to our room and had a very comfortable and quiet night's sleep.
We checked out in the morning and found Natalie, another very well-trained desk assistant to help us. While we waited, the bellhop kindly asked if he could order our car to brought over. Every part of our experience at the Hotel Contessa was pleasant and we recommend the hotel and will stay there again when we return to San Antonio. Hotel Contessa is in a very convenient part of San Antonio, within walking distance of nearly all of the major attractions. You will not be disappointed if you stay there!

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text:
Had origianlly looked into staying at the Embassy Suites, but wasn't sure if they had a hot tub, so in my inquiry the 800 number operator told me about the Hilton Garden Inn. The weekend rate was cheaper than the Embassy Suites price and I was also able to get into a room with a whirlpool tub. 
The Hilton Garden Inn was a great value. The staff was very friendly and courteous and did everything they could to assist us. They have a free shuttle to places within a 5 miles radius of the hotel, which is great if you aren't into walking around after dark, and when we were there it was raining. Upon arrival when we asked for restaurants close by they provided us with a sheet of paper and a brochure of the Uptown dining. We found this information very helpful. Also they provided us with sheets that had directions to the Verizon Wireless Ampitheatre and also the South Park Mall, which were very easy to follow and helped out a lot. 
When we took the shuttle to Uptown for dinner and lunch, both times the drivers were very nice and when we called them to pick us up, we did not have to wait longer than 10 minutes. The shuttle runs until 11pm (or maybe till midnight) and we were able to enjoy ourselves at dinner and not have to worry about driving back to the hotel or paying for a cab. 
We were glad that you were able to park for free, which is a plus in my book.
Our room was very clean and fresh. The whirlpool tub was great and the room was very spacious. 
We ate at the hotel's restaurant one afternoon and the food was great and a decent price when you compare it to some of the dining available Uptown. For us, dining in the hotel that evening was more convenient and worked out great. They serve large portions and we were able to snack on the leftovers later that evening since our room was equipped with a fridge and a microwave.
All in all, we truly enjoyed our stay. We were happy that we happened upon this hotel and got a great weekend rate. Charlotte was wonderful and we will definitely stay here when we come back! 
And as far as things to do in Uptown, we found that there were several places to eat and unwind and I liked the fact that the police were highly visible and alert (especially on a Friday night in a downtown area). I never felt unsafe while out at night with the late night crowd. Plus Uptown is very modern and beautiful.

title: “super soundproof windows, comfy hotel”
text:
would probably only stay here again if have business in the hotel/immediate area. it's a bit out of the way to get to the rest of the city, tho it's convenient for the airport and south station via silver line. the 6min cab ride to the airport is $20 or something. very good, friendly service all around. the rooms are comfortable enough tho feel like a nicer business hotel than a 5-star. the bathrooms are standard and the shower has low water pressure, probably cause the hotel is green. would be cozy to have a thick down comforter on the bed (they use thin down quilts), felt a bit chilly at night. free wifi!! quite unusual these days. fridge and microwave upon request came in handy after having to extend our stay 3 days due to hurricane sandy. the windows here must be like bulletproof. couldn't hear a thing from outside while sandy was practically blowing trees in half. but regular noise from neighboring guestrooms was audible, conference calls, TV, shower, door and drawers open/close etc. parking on-site, cabs readily available out front.
the gym here is above average from normal hotel gym, probably because it is an actual member gym. in addition to a bunch of cardio and weight machines, there's bench, pullup and pulley weights setup, couple kettlebells. the pool is 50ft, 3 lanes and has kickboards and floaty dumbbells. never had to share lanes for laps. they closed the pool for maintenance in the middle of our stay and arranged for guests to use other hotel pools, which was quite accommodating. renaissance 2 blocks away has a 25yd pool with 2 lanes, no training aids. seaport gym is nicer than renaissance.
room service was quite tasty and fast and some items really not so expensive ($6 chicken caesar, wow!). aura may have had an off night the night we went because of sandy. quite a few food options in the area from mortons to some trendy bars, rosa mexicano, dunkin donuts, yankee lobster seafood shack. 7-11 across the street is convenient for snacks and water. flour bakery is a short walk away, for great sandwiches and sticky buns. barbara lynch's menton and sportello are also not too far.

title: “Great for families/adult trips”
text:
This is our 5th trip here for a long weekend. We've been as a couple and brought the kids (5 & 2) this time.
Pros: 
Staff is friendly and helpful
Free parking (valet optional)
Free (slow) wifi in rooms. Fee for faster wifi
Kids club - basically hourly babysitting and they offer breakfast/lunch/dinner for kids for an extra $5. Wii and video games for older kids. Crafts and toys for younger kids
Summer stuff - extra water slide, smores, outdoor movie.
Free shuttle to La Cantera mall and Six Flags Fiesta (save $17 on parking and curb drop off at Fiesta!!)
Cheap Six Flags Fiesta tickets available to purchase in gift shop. You don't have to stand in line to purchase tickets at Fiesta and they're even cheaper at the Westin than the prices online.
Close to shops, restaurants.
Adult pool is separate and a bit secluded from other pools.
Onsite Starbucks.
Cons:
Club Lounge was not always stocked. On a prime summer weekend where the hotel was sold out, they did not keep the club lounge stocked with water/coffee. I won't pay for upgrade to Club Lounge at this Westin. I've been to others that are better.
Hall noise can be loud with kids during the summer.
No shade for baby pool so make sure you have plenty of sunscreen, hats for little ones.
Also bring pool your own pool toys, small floaties as they only have noodles (that I saw). They sell small floaties in the gift shop for $7.

title: “Friendly and welcoming”
text: Good location, with trolley car stop only a block away, very friendly hosts who enhanced our stay with many tips on things to do.

title: “Loved this hotel.”
text:
Just spent 6 nights at this hotel and couldn't be more happy! The rooms are a great size with all the usual conveniences. The staff were very friendly and helpful. 
We used the courtesy shuttle bus each evening and found the service excellent. My only complaint was that the hotel wasn't located downtown, but having said that there were plenty of places for us to go each evening.
Would defnitely stay again.

title: “stay anywhere but here!!!”
text: Dont stay here! It was dirty! The website said they had a pool but when we got there it was drained. We asked and the manager said its been drained for a year if you dont like it go somewhere else! Horrible hotel only one working elevator and one working ice machine for 17 floors. The worst place I have ever stayed.

title: “Nice hotel, good area!”
text:
Great price! Helpful employees!
The room was OK. The mattress felt a little saggy, the carpet was damp by the bathroom when we arrived, the paint was chipped on the ceiling. No refrigerator. But no big deal as we were only there to sleep.
The area was great! Felt very safe. About a 15-20 minute walk to sights. 
The Sky Top bar was very busy on Saturday night (as usual, we were told). Made it up there on Sunday and it was very nice.

title: “Great location, 3 stars indeed”
text:
I spent there six nights in December. This hotel has a fantastic location , just a short distance from a seaside with a magnificent view over San Franciso Brigde and Alcatraz, 8 mins walk to the famous Pier 39 or 3 mins walk to THAT tram first stop. And its situated in the picturesue Fishermans' Wharf with a lot of fantastic seafood shops and restaurants.
Try to find some time and go for "the best hot chocolate with the best view in the world" - Ghirardelli! My sons loved these chocolates as souvenir gifts when I brought them some home.
Hotel is very average, elderly, used and with the slow staff. I was supposed to stay in another Marriott just a few blocks further and it is much better - some members of our group stayed there, so I have comparison.
One final note about San Francisco. There is no shops with toys which is a real nighthmare discovery for "mum-in-business-trip-intstead -being -present-in-nativity-school -show"! It took me a day to find it out! So better buy straight these delicious chocolates there instead of toys. Itself SanFran is spectacular BUT everybody knows it. Next time I have to stayhowever in another hotel definietely!

title: “Everything is perfect”
text:
The 2 rooms we had where spacy, the bathrooms very elegant. Everything was clean.
The position of te hotel is very good, in the haert of Manhattan. A subway station is nearby. Employees are very nice, kind and trendy. The whole hotel is trendy.
Everything is perfect. That's it.

title: “Looks ghetto but not bad at all”
text: When I first arrived the outside was kinda ghetto looking. The person that checked me in was very nice. They did ask for a 25.00 hold on a debit or credit card. Wouldnt do a cash deposit. My room had a king size bed that was really comfy, had a couch that was nice.. The tv has very few good channels but who goes to watch tv. Towels were really crunchy, not soft at all. They did give shampoo and soap. Over all for the money I would stay again.

title: “Perfect hotel for our family”
text: I've never written a review before, but I had to write this one just because we had such a great experience. Our family of four (two kids age 12) made same day reservations on the spur of the moment. The price was very reasonable and the room was wonderful. We had a king size bed, a pull out sofa, and a rollaway bed. The two people at the front desk (Orlando and Mueed) were helpful, friendly, and informative. The pool was great for our kids after a day of touring the Mall. We took the subway to the hotel, and also the next morning to Arlington Cemetary. We also walked from the hotel to the White House in the early evening, and back. We ate at Johny Rockets which was a couple blocks away. Clean, quiet, reasonably priced, friendly; what more could you ask for?

title: “Fabulous.”
text: At first my friends and i were kind of skeptical because of the reviews on here. we booked it anyway because it was close to everything we wanted to do and it was a good price. we arrived and the staff was friendly and everything looked remodeled and new. we were pleasantly surprised. the rooms were very clean and tidy. the beds and the pillows were really comfortable. a lot of people mentioned the homeless but they dont bother you and theyre easy to ignore. overall great experience and great stay. will definitely stay again if given the chance.
