title: “No reason to stay or dine anyplace else.”
text: Service and dining are exceptional. It's simple elegance. Staff attentive and service personalized.

title: “Best hotel for the best price in Manhattan”
text:
My husband and I have been to NYC several times and I've never stayed anywhere better - and at such a good price! When visiting NYC again, we will definitely stay at the Wingate.
Our room was well-sized for a Manhattan hotel; very clean and well-decorated. Everything looks just like the pictures on their Web site. The location is great for accessing the subway and Penn Station, and is in walking distance of many major shopping areas. It is located in the Garment District, so there aren't a ton of local restaurants, but that's a minor detraction. (I do recommend Lazarro's on W. 38th St. between 7th and 8th for a nearby, casual Italian restaurant with good pizza.) 
What impressed us the most about the Wingate was how efficient they were and how many amenities were included in what was (at about $263 a night, *including* tax) a very inexpensive rate for an above-average Manhattan hotel. All of the following were FREE or inclusive: bottled water in our room every day; wireless and wired internet access in the room; a business room downstairs with an internet-ready computer plus printer; access to a small but good gym downstairs; and a warm and cold breakfast buffet. We also had a mini-fridge, microwave, and coffee maker (with free coffee) in our room. Plus, the hotel is very accommodating when it comes to storing luggage (both before we checked in - as we'd arrived early, and when we checked out - as we had an evening flight). All in all, the hotel was everything you'd expect to find in an above-average business hotel - but it was pretty amazing to find it at that price in Manhattan!

title: “Just returned, Birthday Celebration & Relaxation”
text: Let me start by saying, I travel a lot! A whole lot, for work as well as pleasure. As such I stay in a lot of hotels. I have NEVER, EVER stayed in a hotel this nice. That includes Trump Towers in Vegas and New York! This place blows the doors off of both, for one reason the staff! The service, the staff the "gentlemanly" approach was unreal. You owe it to yourself to experience this place. We have decided to return at least once a year. Wow! Wow! Wow!!

title: “Exceptional Employee”
text: I want to say that I believe I encountered the best hotel employee I have ever had the pleasure to work with. Halimah was a front desk attendant at Beacon and was always kind and considerate and very quick to respond to concerns. All of the staff was very good to work with but Halimah was exceptional.

title: “My home away from home”
text:
I wish I could live at the Homewood Suites in Seattle. We stayed for several days and I wish we could have stayed longer. From the moment we arrived, the staff at the hotel were sincerely friendly and helpful. From the very top of the management team to the housekeeping staff, everyone had a smile and a moment to chat.
Our room was wonderful for a longer stay. We had the ability to store food in the large refrigerator and cook for ourselves on the stove. You should note that if you wash your own dishes and leave them out to dry, housekeeping will load them into the dishwasher. When in doubt, they'll opt for sanitizing the dishes.
The shuttle to area attractions was a fantastic service. We used it every day and saw so much of Seattle. The included weekday dinners were also quite nice. The food was hearty and plentiful, and there is wine available if you're a drinker. I can't wait to come back!

title: “warm welcome and great service”
text:
it is a big and busy hotel. however the nice and warm welcome and help by the recetion desk person (Ms. Akada Phillip) made the hotel enjoyable.
the room isin good shape and renovated. the bathroom is clean. location is great and close to the theater district. i recommnd this hotel

title: “couldn't have asked for a better hotel”
text: I'm becoming a big fan of Intercontinental hotels, the beds are incredibly comfortable and huge. Service fantastic as usual, great food, and only a few minutes walk from the centre of times square.

title: “Excellent value - wonderful location.”
text: We've stayed at this hotel twice, and have enjoyed the property each time. It is hard to imagine a better value in NYC - and the Upper West Side location is perfect.

title: “Great bargain on Priceline!”
text: Plug in 3-star hotel and Downtown Memphis on Priceline, and you get a great hotel room for $50. The Marriott is a well-maintained, large convention hotel located just blocks from all downtown attractions. You can't beat it for the price.

title: “Outstanding Hotel and Staff”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Nikko for 6 days in July 2011. Upon arrival, we used "Super Shuttle" from SFO which was about a 30 minute ride, efficient and convenient. The Hotel Nikko is located in the Union Square area but very close to the Tenderloin Area (Be very leery of this). Don't be surprised to see the homeless going thru the garbage cans and ash trays in front of the hotel, it's not only prevalent near the hotel but this seems to be the norm instead of the exception in San Francisco. The hotel is very convenient to public transportation, The Westfield Shopping Center, shopping, food and Walgreens. Again, the homeless are all around the city, sleeping in public areas, camped out in front of Walgreens and other stores with signs asking for money, or walking in the shopping area asking for money as you pass, this was a complete turn off for our view of San Francisco and would not recommend it for a family vacation. Not sure why this is accepted, however, it with the very low police presence observed, it gave us a very unsafe, unsettling feeling. As we were walking to the Cable Cars one afternoon, we observed a very dirt homeless woman walking thru the crowd removing her clothes, when she removed her shirt and was topless, another homeless male yelled at her to put her clothes but she continued walking. We did not stick around to see what happened. It was unsightly especially for children present. The city in our view was dirty; areas had strong smells of urine as we walked down Market St to the Pier area. The people of San Francisco are very friendly for the most part, but we encountered several young people (both male and female) on the "F Line" (Transportation to/from Pier areas) on two different trips using strong profanity and vulgarity along with littering and spitting on the Tram Car, we were appalled to see such disregard to their surroundings and the city. 
Back to the Hotel Nikko, this was a saving grace, the hotel is beautiful, the staff was awesome (friendly and very helpful). We stayed on in an Imperial Club Room (24th floor) which allowed us to take advantage of the evening reception of wine, beer, finger food, cheese and crackers nightly which was a great way to begin your night time activities. The room had a king size bed/pillows that was so comfortable and inviting, the room had all the amenities to make our stay relaxing and cozy. The bathroom was posh and large, we wanted to take the shower home with us, and water pressure was excellent which lacked nothing. The Imperial Club Room came with a continental breakfast (Bagels, pastries, fruit, and cereal along with coffee, tea or juice) which was sufficient to get started in San Fran. We took advantage of the breakfast buffet in the hotel’s restaurant, Anzu, which was superb. They offered a full Japanese Breakfast along with a full American Breakfast with Grilled Salmon, Eggs, Sausage, Bacon, Miso Soup, Lox, Meats etc. (this was a gourmet breakfast). We can’t say enough of the quality of our stay at the Hotel Nikko. Thank you staff and management!
Back to the surrounding area, we stayed over 4th of July Weekend. During our stay, there was a shooting two blocks from the hotel (Tenderloin Area) and a Police “BART” Officer shot and killed an armed drunk a few transit stops from the hotel. Union Square is two blocks away (make sure you go in the right direction) where you can catch the open top sightseeing buses, we took the blue bus but I would recommend the red ones as we saw a lot more of them and more frequent pickups. You catch the Cable Cars at Powell and Market along with the “F” Line (Tram Car to Fisherman’s Wharf), the Cable Cars are $6 per ride each way and the F and buses are $2 each way. You can buy a weekly transport card (Good discount is you plan on using public transportation) in the visitor center at Powell and Market. The visitor center is down stairs on Powell at Market St. Shopping in the area is no way up to par what you find in New York City. We found some good lunch options on the lower level of the Westfield Shopping Center and they have a Bristol Farms (Market) as well.
We will not go in depth here for the sightseeing we did, but highly recommend: Alcatraz (a must, but get tickets on line before you go), Fisherman’s Wharf (Touristy, expensive but fun), Muir Woods (Giant Redwoods) make sure you have enough time to spend there, AT&T Park (saw a Giants Game) and of course the Golden Gate. We saw what we wanted to see in San Francisco and more than we wanted to however, in our future we will go to cities that provide a feeling of a safer, secure environment.

title: “Perfect location, very accommodating staff.”
text: Very conveniently located in Georgetown, steps from the shopping on M Street and a short stroll to the Harbor area for dining. From the moment we arrived asking to park our car well before check-in time until the moment we left, every staff member was extremely pleasant and helpful. Given that our car was packed to the gills with an entire dorm-room full of stuff, the on-site garage was a comfort and a big convenience. Our room was quite large and even had a door to a tiny walled-in patio to have our morning coffee. The continental breakfast was perfectly adequate with fruit, pastries, juice etc. Even though we had a room just off the lobby, it was very quiet, especially since there are french doors between the living area and main bedroom. Bathroom was clean and large, though the water pressure was a little lame. Would most definitely stay here again. Good value for the money. A tad hard to find as the GPS had a different idea regarding the address. Go to the entrance to Washington Harbor and then turn up Thomas Jefferson. Only other caveat would be regarding the tour bus they offer tickets to-not the best tour company. "Open-Air" is better.

title: “Great price, great location--a definite revisit”
text: My daughter, 8-year old granddaughter and I just stayed for four nights (6/27-7/1/09) If you're looking for a clean room, clean bathroom, great location and great price--this is the place. The staff was helpful (when needed), the room was adequate (no frills), but it suited all our needs. I will definitely stay again the next time I am in NYC (if they have any rooms available--they fill up fast).

title: “Fantastic location, ideal hotel for visiting New York”
text:
I went for 5 nights to NY with a friend for a holiday. We got a taxi from Newark airport to the hotel which cost $80 (including tolls and tip). The hotel is about a 100m walk from the centre of Times Square so is in an ideal location! Although we didn't pay extra for a view of Times Sq, we could still see part of it and had a good view anyway. There were a coupel metro stations very close to the hotel which took you anywhere in Manhattan. We paid $27 for a 7 day metro pass which was well worth it. The hotel lobby is on about the 5th floor which is very modern and inviting. There is a large restaurant (Cafe Nicole) and an outdoor terrace which overlooks Times Square and is very fashionably styled. We ended up enjoying drinks out here most nights rather than bothering with any other bars. Definitely one of the best views of any bar in Manhattan.
Our room was very spacious. We asked for a twin room which comprised of 2 double beds (a double bed each!!) and a large bathroom. Beds were very comfortable and rooms were cleaned daily. There was a new flatscreen TV with loads of channels and the option of pay movies. We also had a large wardrobe, a powerful hairdryer in the bathroom and an iron and ironing board. The only ever so slight problem was the shower was slightly erratic but still quite powerful. Although we overlooked a busy road on the edge of Times Square, the windows were soundproof so we slept soundly the whole time. The air conditoning was lovely and cool. We didn't pay the rather extortionate price of $20 per day for breakfast; instead we went to a place about 50 metres up the road called 'Cosmic Diner' every day for breakfast. It was reasonably priced and did everything you could imagine for breakfast. Overall I would definitely stay in this hotel again if I came to New York.

title: “One night stay”
text: I took my staff out for our annual Christmas party to San Francisco. I own a timeshare there and they are really flexible about booking. I was able to book four one night stays on the same night, and it counts as four of my seven days for the year. The service is great, the rooms are comfortable, and it is quiet. It is also a block from Union Square. It was nice to be able to walk back from Union Square at midnight and not be worried about my safety.

title: “Lovely and competent staff, great food, but cleanliness needs to improve”
text: The staff is absolutely wonderful and friendly. They'll do everything they can to help you. The dinner is also very good (simple food and great taste). The cleanliness, however, is very deficient. My room was not properly cleaned in several times (I believe that the dishwasher was turned on without any detergent at all, the dishes were usually dirty even after a full cycle, for my surprise). In one occasion, someone forgot a very wet and dirty sponge (yuck!) over my clothes which were in the couch. The staff proved to be great by immediately sending the clothes to the laundry, no cost. A couple of days later, a dirty wet towel was forgotten next to my bed. The walls are also very thin, you can hear everything from the room above. I also had problems with the hot water, but once again, the staff made everything to fix it asap.

title: “Very nice place to stay”
text: We came here after a cruise package. We were all tired. The staff was very quick about getting all of us checked in. The rooms were wonderful. A huge bed, coffee and tea in the room. There was also a very big desk with wi fi hook up. They have a shuttle that will take you to not only the airport or light rail but also the mall or select places to eat. We would stay here again.

title: “Great place for Gaslamp”
text:
A group of friends and I decided to take a random trip to San Diego. I booked the hotel using Priceline and got a real good rate, about 50% off. Once we got the hotel we noticed that it was right next to the baseball stadium (Petco Park), and literally a few hundred yards from the Gaslamp district. This was perfect because we did most of our travels there.
We did go to the beach one day but the traffic was pretty bad, and getting out of the hotel was annoying. Even though the hotel and rooms are very well presented, the rooms are a bit smaller than most 4 star hotels.
I would say that if you were looking to hang out in downtown San Diego most of the time, and could afford $150-$200 a night, then this hotel would be a good choice. Otherwise, if you want to hit up the beaches for most of your travels, then maybe downtown San Diego isn't your best choice.

title: “Good experience”
text: I stayed here one night when the roads were too bad for travel, so I was not here long. Everything was fine on my visit. I really liked the individual TVs on the gym equipment. They had a decent workout area. I had a good salmon salad for dinner at the bar. I found that they serve some of the same food there as they do in the restaurant, but it costs less in the bar area. It was very crowded with people watching the BCS championship, but the service was still good. I had the breakfast buffet also. I especially liked that they had the green chile on the breakfast bar.

title: “Great value and service”
text: I recently traveled to Seattle on business and stayed for a little sight seeing on the weekend. The SpringHill Suites was a great choice for me. I found the service to be excellent and the room provided more space than a regular hotel. The front desk was very helpful in providing me with directions to my different appointments and then for weekend plans. It was also great to be so close to the freeway and to downtown. I did notice the other two recommondations are from over a year ago...and this feels like a different hotel. I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Adequate size room - bizarre furnishings”
text: Contrary to some previous reviews, I found my room to be small but adequate in size. The furnishings, however, were another story. A large marble table was at the end of the bed with barely enough room to get in and out of the chair. Two low chairs that looked like they belong in the children's furniture section at IKEA were also in the room as was a bench that was totally incongruous. In fact the furniture was probably the ugliest I have ever encountered in a hotel room. On a more positive note, the staff was superb, the lobby attractive and the breakfast area especially nice. The hotel's wi-fi had the best signal I have ever found in a hotel. The in-room safe was another good feature. So for a well located River North hotel and a reasonable rate, Hotel Cass is recommended, as long as you don't mind the bizarre furnishings.

title: “Outstanding Service!”
text: Christina and her staff were outstanding, going out of their way to win you over! Food and bar were excellent. Cookies are great! Definitely staying here on the next trip to San Antonio.

title: “Convenient Location”
text:
This Hotel is central to the Texas Harris Methodist Hospital and this section of Fort Worth Shopping district. Next Door is an I HOP great breakfasts, and next to A really good Steak house.
Do really shop the rate you pay, it can vary from $92 to over $200 for the same room.
It is corporate managed Hotel so the rates are set at head office.
The staff are really nice, they have a decent free breakfast as well.
Wouls stay there again.

title: “Nice Rooms, Mediocre Staff, Good Location”
text:
The Westin Market Street is about 4 -5 blocks from Unions Square where the Westin St. Francis is located (a much, much older hotel). The hotel is located across from the SFMOMA and other museums - right on the BART line. All the rooms except for Suites are idential size; "Standard", "Deluxe" and "Deluxe Grand" are idential - except for Floor of the hotel => higher floor numbers with "Views" are Deluxe or Grand. The views are NOT great from most rooms - don't bother paying up. Also, DO NOT get a room by the elevators - or near the lower roof top generators - way to noisy. They tried to "Upgrade" our Deluxe to Grand Deluxe by the elevators - we passed!
Pros:
Super Cheap Rooms - we paid $149 per night for a Deluxe Room
Great Location / Modern Hotel
Very Comfortable Beds
Flat Screen TV
Cons:
Mediocre Staff - not the Four Seasons or St. Regis (but its $200 per night cheaper)
No Night Life at Bar/Restaurant
Poor Common Space
Smallish Bathrooms
Average to Poor Views in most rooms.
Overall => at $149; the bed is great and so is the location.

title: “Amazing service, clean and large rooms at a very good rate!”
text: Read some good reviews about this comfort suites and i am absolutely amazed. They treat me like a 5 star hotel would. Rooms are great, staff is super friendly. The owner actually came and personally asked how our stay was. Feel very comfortable at this hotel and highly recommend it. Will stay here from now on!

title: “Great Location but needs some work”
text:
Stayed from June 30 - July 6th. Marriott Platinum member and used points for stay.
PROS
- Location. In the heart of Times Square and close to everything.
- Bed. Wonderful to sleep on.
- View. Was upgraded to a room on the 41st floor that looked down on Times Square. Could also see the cruise ships docked.
- Fitness Center. Plenty of equiptment and room.
CONS
- Towels. Worst towels of any hotel I have stayed at. I am 150 - 180 nights per year in hotels, and these towels had no fluff and actually hurt your skin to dry off. These towels have been in use for far too long. Horrible.
- Spotty service. As a platinum member and it being a full service Marriott I expect some services. Turn down service. Did not receive every night. Not sure why, but of the 6 nights, only 3 nights did we receive turn down service. Newspapers. I rcvd the USA Today each day. On the 30th floor which is where the concierge lounge is at - they received the USA Today, NY Times, and Wall St Journal at their door. As a platinum member, I get this no matter what floor I am at, but didn't here.
I have read many complaints about the elevators. My take is - at peak times, they are slow and crowded. The rest of the time, they are great. The problem, is you punch in your floor # and are told what elevator you will ride. Many of the guest are either impatient or don't know how it works, so everyone presses in their floor # multiple times, gets on any elevator, etc. Not enough staff close by to help individuals or explain the system. Every day, I explained the system to a confused guest. Shouldn't staff be doing this?
I would rather stay at the Renaissance - Times Square if I needed a Marriott property on Broadway. Currently, this is nothing more than an average property with an above average price (above average points and price).

title: “Great Weekend at the Bristol”
text: Staff is great, courteous, and accommodating. Intimate Bar. I considered the food better than average. Easy walk to PetCo Stadium and and Bay as well as Horton Plaza. I came into town on the train and walked the 5 blocks to the hotel. If you are looking for a small boutique hotel in San Diego close to the Gaslight District and other great attractions, definitely put the Bristol on your list. I will be back.

title: “Very nice”
text:
Good room, Clean, plus free laundry room, Helpful staff, Good breakfasts... The pool was well kept, the kitchenettes in the room were a god send plus plenty of room in the fridge for beer and leftovers from the BBQ
All in all a nice stay. The only negative was there was no ATM on site, (across the street at the Hilton there was though)

title: “Good renovation”
text:
This is my second review of this hotel.
I stayed here exactly a year ago when the renovations were still underway. The wait is worth it and the work has been sensitively carried out.
We stayed in the Winthrop suite. Nice view down onto the Freedom trail and some historic buildings.
Yes, the rooms are a little tight on space (bathrooms particularly) but more than adequate and are attractively furnished.
Staff are very friendly (particularly after coming up from NYC!) and helpful.
Some friends from the UK staying in a Back Bay hotel visited and were blown away by the public areas. They were paying the same price for a standard chain hotel.
I recommend it - but pick your room carefully if you want space.

title: “Excellent hotel, superb staff.”
text:
I spent 11 nights in the Wyndham Boston, and found it to be an excellent hotel. Staff were top-notch, and quality of service second to nothing.
Only small gripes would be, no pool and tiny Gym. Tip-join their members club (free) via their website before you book, and then you truly get treated royally .i.e upgrade to suites, free calls, free welcome snacks, daily papers etc.

title: “My new favorite DC business hotel”
text: This was a great stay in DC. Reasonably priced, clean, free wi-fi and bottled water... I love the simple pleasures of Four Points hotels. As a SPG Gold member, I also got a nice upgrade to a suite with a separate bedroom and kitchenette, when my room wasn't ready because I checked in early. This came in handy when I had some friends back to my room after the bars closed. The bar also had friendly guys working there, and a delicious half-price burger I thoroughly enjoyed. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “New York”
text: The Salisbury Hotel was a superb location. The rooms were large and roomy, but in need of a lick of paint. Poor service and no facilities as such. Poor all round. Like I said, the best was the location.

title: “Needs Outdoor Pool, Otherwise Perfect”
text:
Came down with the girlfriend to the Ballantyne for a wedding at the hotel. Beautiful place. My third stay at a Luxury Collection property, after a great one in London and an above-average stay in south Florida. 
Stayed here for 2 nights and loved the hotel. Beautiful resort in the southern suburbs of Charlotte. Very nice facade, looks new, and nicely appointed lobby. Guestrooms are large and very attractive, however our room, like half the hotel, faces a shopping center across the street, which is not a great resort-style view. Very comfy bed however, and nice bathroom amenities. Provided mouth wash, which is rare, but welcome.
Had a few rounds of drinks with wedding people at the Gallery bar. Beautiful bar and very adorable bartender made this a fun experience. Bar menu includes a ton of unique cocktails the girlfriend enjoyed ordering and they all came out delicious. Golf the next day was great, very playable course and friendly staff members. Lunch at the turn was a bbq pulled pork sandwich which was surprisingly good. 
A little pissed that the spa couldn't fit me in for a massage, which was frustrating and the major design flaw of the hotel is the fact there is no outdoor pool deck. On an otherwise beautiful 90 degree day, I was forced to take a nap lying down in the rough off the 18th fairway. Not the ideal situation. Other people were crowding off a small patch outside the indoor pool, but it was very makeshift. They need to improve this yesterday. 
There is a small, but effective sauna in the pool lockeroom which was a treat and the food that night at the wedding was outstanding. Did not taste like banquet food, far superior. 
All in all, a great place, my issues are with the overcrowded spa, no outdoor pool, and lastly it was somewhat awkward getting my golf bag back and forth from the lobby to the pro shop when arriving and leaving the hotel. They don't have a good system and I went nuts when the bellman didnt have my golf bag as I was checking out (they had to rush it from the golf clubhouse), which was a debacle. Overall, would still come back, and this time make the spa appointment months in advance.

title: “Pleasant Stay in New York”
text:
We had a very pleasant experience at the Best Western President Hotel. The room was comfortable. We had a broken iron but the problem was remedied by housekeeping. The wireless was slow but worked. 
Suny, at the front desk, was absolutely fantastic. She was friendly and went out of her way to be helpful - providing us directions, suggestions etc. Due to bad weather our flights were canceled and Suny worked to acommodate us with our reservation rate. - The location is great - close to everything. I would recommend this hotel.

title: “son's air force bmt graduation”
text: nice and close to the base.. just what we were looking for after driving from va. would recomend for anyone . during your childs air force bmt graduation. nice staff,,clean rooms,, nice pool area.. a little more at breakfast but hay its free !!!

title: “Great place for a family reunion”
text:
This hotel was selected to house the our family for the reunion. For the price we got a lot of things.
 1. The conference room for the get together. 
 2. A large breakfast in the mornings.
 3. Popcorn and soda all day.
 4. Kick back is free dinner, hot dogs, veggies and dip, baked potatoes etc.
 5. A great room and confortable bed.
 6. Free internet/Wi Fi.
 7. Free fax.
 8. Low price, $80 included all taxes.
 9. Great indoor/outdoor pool.
10. Very Accommendating for sizeable group.

title: “Best of Boston, for real!!”
text: I absolutely love this hotel!!! The lobby is amazing. The decor and the fragrances were wonderful. But the most awesome thing about the lobby was Richard and Jason, the concierge. They were the best concierge that I have come by in a long time. The staff in the hotel make everything so welcoming and inviting. I was even able to meet the rooms director and it's clear that everyone in the hotel are the most professional from beginning to end. The hotel is walking distance to EVERYTHING! The restaurants in the area are wonderful. And walking to Fenway Park eating ice cream to watch Yankees v. Red Sox was awesome. I will definitely be returning there soon. Another relaxing week in cool Boston is in order.

title: “Close to perfect: no parking”
text: Lovely hotel, great service. The only downside is that it does not own a parking. There's a public one two block aways (very cheap $12 / 24hrs) but considering my car was packed with some shopping, I did not sleep that well, does not look that safe. It is close to the mall but besides the riverwalk, the area is not that amazing.

title: “New Yorker Hotel, New York City, Visited Sep 2011”
text:
This was our second time in New York but first time at the New Yorker. We stayed here as it had been recomended by my colleagues at Thomson and I wanted it to be special as it was our honeymoon. The hotel itself is very big, like most in New York and the room was small but it was very clean and had lots of wardrobe space for all of the new clothes we bought. We stayed on the 33rd floor but it was never a problem as the lifts were very fast and reliable. Last time we stayed in Times Square and struggled to find good, reasonable food but this time we had no problems at all because the hotel has its own diner and restaurant. The diner was exactly how you imagine an american diner to be and I looked forward to the experience every day.
The location of the hotel is second to none, right next to Macy's and perfect view of the empire state building. Was central to everything and much easier to get around than last time. We found in Times Sqaue that it was just too busy and you get so much hassle from the touts that everywhere takes twice as long to get to. However you dont get this up at the New Yorker and you are closer to the tube stations,shops and bars.
We went to an amazing Korean one night called Hang Kawi I think and it was the best authentic food and restaurant I have ever been to. It does not look much from the outside but go inside, you wont be disappointed.

title: “For what you pay, it was not worth it!!!!! at all!!!!!”
text: I went for my fiancé's birthday, and thought it was going to be a great stay.But instead it was a big head ache.No one knew what they were doing!!!! At check in they didn't give us our voucher for breakfast, so at breakfast while we were eating I had to run down to the lobby and get one ,so I wouldn't have to pay an other 50 $ just for breakfast.Then the room we got, the bed was so old as soon as we sat on it, it made the loudest noise's.Next-We got the massage package which I paid a arm and a leg for and they told us we could take care of the payment when we went for the massage.So when we went for our massage, they told us we had to take care if it down stairs at the lobby ...So we had to run all the way to the lobby and fix that!!! Ridiculous!!!!!!!!! by the time we got back for out massages the people were rushing us because we were late for our appointment!!!Then we ordered room service, and it took a hr for our lunch, and then aftrer an hr we got a call from the kitchen saying they dropped our food, so it was going to be an 30 min!!!! I don't see why I had to deal with this much crap when im paying $600 for a room!!!!` will never stay there again.

title: “Modern and fresh”
text: The location of this hotel is really good – in a quiet street not too far away from the main attractions. The room was stylish. Unfortunately we did not find the beds very comfortable, as the mattresses were too hard.

title: “TERRIBLE”
text: This hotel is AWFUL and the staff is so rude!! My friends and I bought tickets for their Halloween party and the tickets jumped from $10 to $35. Then they said coatcheck is free with tickets but charged us anyway. The bouncer yelled at my best friend to put away her umbrella and when she said "it wouldnt hurt to say PLEASE," he said "I dont HAVE to say please," like he's God of the front door or something. The cheapest drink I could get was $10 for a beer and everything else was around $20 because they INCLUDE 18% GRATUITY THEMSELVES!! Probably cuz the know everyone will be so frustrated with them at that point that no one would want to tip. Anyway, it was a horrible experience. STAY AWAY.

title: “Loved Residence Inn Capitol DC”
text: Our family loved the Residence Inn Capitol DC! We stayed there for 7 days in May, 2005, and when we return to DC we'll stay there again. We arrived at the hotel at 9:00 in the morning, tired after our long night flight -- yet they gave us our reserved room right away! (check-in time was @ 3:00 p.m.) We were able to freshen up, then venture out to the metro, which was just around the block! We rode the metro to the Eastern Market to shop for fresh produce & breads, etc. (the Residence Inn Capitol DC is equipped with full kitchens...) The mall is only 3 blocks away, so everyday we either walked to the mall to see the Capitol, the Supreme Court, the diverse museums, the National Archives, the Botanic Garden, etc. Or we'd hop on the metro and ride it to the Memorials or Arlington. The complimentary breakfasts every morning were GREAT: eggs, potatoes, sausage, pancakes, french toast, waffles, bagels & cream cheese, oatmeal, yogurt, cereal, toasts, muffins, pastries, fresh fruit, melons, coffee, tea, hot chocolate and juices. Their breakfasts gave us the energy we needed for all of our sight-seeing! In the evening, after a full day of exploring, we'd return, exhausted, back to Residence Inn Capitol -- and they had complimentary hot dinners waiting for their guests! (M, T, W) They also provided a variety of board games, which we checked out and enjoyed playing in our suite. (You can play in their lobby also.) The TV's & free movies were great too. We enjoyed the swimming pool & hot tub nightly, and if we weren't too wiped out, we'd work out in the exercise room next to the pool. We found Residence Inn Capitol's staff to be extremely attentive, friendly, and professional. Never did we see a sloppy dining area -- even on Saturday and Sunday mornings at breakfast. We had an excellent family vacation at Residence Inn Capitol DC! Looking forward to our return. (May 2005)

title: “I would stay again”
text:
I didn't have any major problems during my stay. The location of the hotel is great and the room and the shared bathrooms were tidy and neat. Despite opting for a shared bathroom, I never had problems accessing the bathrooms. The hall was indeed dimly lit, the lights could have been brighter. My room was on the second floor and on that floor the only view from the window is the wall of the neighbouring building, that didn't disturb me too much though. There was constant noise coming from outside the window but fortunately it wasn't too loud, so it didn't bother me much.
The negative experiences were that my cardkey stopped working twice (the reception reprogrammed it immediately though) and the somewhat indifferent attitude of some of the reception staff. The hotel also didn't answer my e-mail inquiry about one particular thing before my arrival. Some time after making my reservation I decided to have it confirmed. The first time I was told to "call back tomorrow" in a rude manner but when I called back the next day everything went fine. They have different reception staff on different days though and some them are nice, depends on whom you happen to be talking to. Being a late check-in (after 6 pm) was no problem for me. I just e-mailed the hotel that I will be checking in late and the check-in went smoothly even though they never answered that e-mail either. Well, at least it seems like the e-mails are getting through.
Despite some negative experiences, I would stay at this hotel again.

title: “Great location.”
text:
As a result of reviews here on trip advisor we booked the Orchard Hotel for 4 nights this may. This hotel is situated in a really great location. The Orchard is close enough to Union Square and China Town but not too close. The Tram Line is just outside the hotel.
The Bed was so comfortable and the room was really nicely decorated with a good sized bathroom. I note some people have commented that the price was not too good but compared to London prices The Orchard is a real Gem.
The only downside is the breakfast which is not that great but adequate. If you decide to stay at the Orchard the pizza place opposite the hotel serves nice pizza. Me and my husband really enjoyed a pizza pesto.

title: “GREAT Location Good Value”
text: Stayed here five nights in May 2009. Excellent location, clean rooms, friendly staff, hipster atmosphere, and a good price. I was traveling with my (then) eleven year old daughter. Concierge went out of his way to provide information to us, was as kind as could be to her and upon check out, one of his staff stored our bags for about five hours so we had somewhere secure to leave them. The room was on the small side and somewhat noisy at times due to street noise, but I expected this and it was not an issue. Bathroom was updated nicely, rainfall shower and also on the smaller side. Again, not an issue. We are planning to return to SF shortly and I look forward to another stay here.

title: “Decent hotel”
text: We stayed for 4 nights in March. We found the hotel location to be very good, about 15 mins walk to Pier 39 area, but along the flatter route around the bay. It is close to the windy part of Lombard St also. We had a small mix up in the booking - we had requested a 2 queen room from an internet travel agent (which was not guarenteed) and when we arrived we found that we had a one bed king booking. We had to take this for one night but the hotel staff were able to swap to the 2 bed room for the other 3. The room was quite small but ok really, clean enough and quite quiet. Breakfast was ok, fairly decent selection of food but busy and used plastic cutlery. Rates were reasonable and would consider it again.

title: “Fine new hotel, good Midtown location”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights in February - quick theatre getaway weekend. This is a new building with a small footprint; each floor only has 10 rooms. Very clean and well-kept. We were 8 floors up and street noise was minimal. Room had a small fridge (not "mini-bar") and microwave. Location is excellent; it's just steps from the subway, 6th Avenue and Broadway. Macy's flagship store is right there; Times Square is an easy walk up Broadway. 
We got an outstanding $129 Travelzoo rate - though the online rates were only $10 more. Check-in was quick (we arrived early, no problem), easy and very friendly; check-out was painless and fast.
Only reasons this wasn't 5 *s across the board: the beds had kind of a soft top (too squishy for our liking), and the heater was kind of noisy on this cold weekend.

title: “Awesome Spa”
text: The Spa is unbelievable. If u go, plan on staying all day even if u only have one session. Tons to do & relax at the heated pool in your comfortable robe & slippers. Lunch is wonderful & very reasonable.

title: “Awesome Hotel, Very Plush, The Best Stay Ever”
text:
This is a great hotel. It stands up for the Hilton Brand. It can get expensive as things will add up. It is by no means for you if you are on a budget. It has most ammenities that can be found in a hotel and is in a great location.
I stayed here with my wife and two young kids. Parking can be expensive and is located in a parking garage across the street. I had to catch an early morning flight, so I used the business center for a charge to print my itenerary. There was a train station located less than two blocks in which I walked to at 5:00 in the morning with no problems. The last stop was Chicago O'hare and it took about 45 minutes. The cost was $2.50.
The beds were very comfortable and the decor was lovely in the room. We did get a fridge with no charge because we have medicine that required refrigeration. That was a small gift at 1am when we checked in. Restuarants are located well within walkind distance as well as public trasportation and taxi's were readily available. I would stay here again if I can afford to and need to be in Chicago.

title: “great hotel and staff”
text: We have nothing to say but great things about this hotel. When we were looking for a hotel to get dressed and prepare for the wedding we thought of the Beacon Hotel, we stayed for the weekend back in 2007 and loved the layout of the hotel, the ambiance, the suite and the staff. We booked a king-size bed suite for our preparations, due to having our wedding fall on a holiday (Labor Day weekend) most of the larger suites were booked. On the same day of our wedding, Omar Ibrahim (assistant GM) was very accommodating and upgraded our room to the best suite we could have dreamed of. The room was very spacious and elegant. It was perfect. We had the best view, and we took our wedding pictures inside the suite and all over the hotel. We felt so lucky and grateful for Omar’s hospitality. We are very thankful and we highly recommend this hotel for all visitors who want to travel around DC. The hotel itself is situated in a perfect location with walking distance to shops, stores and scenic spots. Most importantly, what made Beacon Hotel the best hotel in the DC area are the people like Omar who went out of his way to make sure guests like us have the best experience in this hotel. Thank you very much Omar, and thank you to the staff of Beacon Hotel.

title: “Small room but excellent location”
text: My wife and I spent a Friday and Saturday here to escape from Hurricane's Sandy's havoc in New York. It is a small hotel with smallish rooms and a tiny bathroom better designed for one person on a business trip than a couple but the very favorable weekend rate made up for the tightness. The hotel is perfectly located for business in the middle of Boston's financial district which is a warren of narrow and dark streets with little of appeal. Do not be put off tough because all Boston's charms surriound this area so the hotel is very centrally located and you can easily walk to all Boston's many pleasures. Although no car is ever needed in Boston, and the hotel is easily walkable from Amtrak's South Station and the State Street T from Logan Airport, if you have one you can park on the streets during the weekends. Just be sure to read the all the parking restriction signs very carefully.

title: “Great Pool!”
text: We were in town for only two nights for a family wedding. Two other cousins and their families also stayed. The rooms were so spacious and clean, the included breakfast was nicer than expected... and the pool area was very "resort-like". It was such a great place to hang out with family. I would definitely recommen, asd this hotel to families with young or older children. The room with two full beds is separate from the living area. You have a large kitchen area with small fridge, sink, and microwave, as well as plenty of counter space, two flat screen televisions, a large table to be used as a desk or eating area, and a queen pull out couch. Free shuttle service to the airport too!

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Very nice rooms with a flatscreen tv and comfortable beds. The service was good and the location near the convention center was quite convenient. The valet parking is a bit inconvenient and expensive, though. Overall, good choice and priced right.

title: “Excellent hotel and location”
text:
I recently spent 4 nights at this hotel. I had a room with a balcony overlooking the bay. The view was beautiful but I didn't really spend much time out on the balcony (although it has two chairs and a table). The room was nice and clean and a good size. Everything seemed very new. The bathroom had a nice large shower (but no tub). Free wifi is available in the hotel lobby/bar area on the first floor, but it costs $12.95/day in the rooms. 
The best thing about the hotel is its location. It's right on the bay with walking distance to shops, restaurants, and the USS Midway on the bay. Also walking distance to the gaslamp district which has a great nightlife of restaurants and bars. The train in front of the hotel is a little loud and I was still able to hear it up in my room on the 14th floor, but it didn't keep me awake at night.
There's a nice outdoor bar/lounge area near the pool, although drinks/food are expensive.

title: “Very large and well located Hilton. If you're an HHonors member, don't expect special treatment unless you're Platinum.”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights as a reward stay in exchange for 140,000 HHonors points. We had a large, 2 queen bed room on the 23rd floor (this is a big hotel) and my Gold status got us free entry into the spa/pool. I talked my way into Executive Lounge access on check-in, but note that this is usually reserved for Platinum members.
The executive lounge has a cold breakfast buffet, fairly naff evening nibbles and soft drinks only. There is also one PC with free internet access. You can also pick up free wifi from the integrated coffee shop "Java Jive" in the lobby. Parking is $17 for 24 hours (ouch) but you can park in the Austin Convention Centre lot right next door for $7 a day with 3 re-entries (although it's technically no overnight stays). If you're staying over a weekend, it's worth knowing that parking on street is free all day Saturday and Sunday, and before 08:30 and after 17:30. T
he pool/spa was pretty good, but there are separate gender specific sauna/steam rooms (not sure if this is a US thing?) so you won't be able to sweat it with your loved one.
Location wise, the hotel is good as it's within a few blocks of all the bars and night-life on 6th Street, but yet not so close as to be noisy. If you're a runner, you can do a nice loop South from the hotel until you hit the river, and then along the river until you get bored.
For HHonors members, I found that the on property rewards are tiered at this hotel, and geared towards Platinum - sure you get some goodies for being Gold, but the Hilton treatment I'm used to (space available upgrade, free breakfast etc) seemed to be reserved for Platinum members.

title: “Not Bad...Pretty good.”
text: The Hotel Saint James is a bare bones type of Hotel. No room service or anything like that, but the location is perfect, right in the heart of time square. The biggest plus for this hotel is the cleanliness, it is very clean! I loved that. It was a bit pricey for what it offered but in a way the cleanliness of the hotel made up for it. The staff was very friendly, with the exception of one rude older balding gentleman (I do not know his name). I would most probably stay at the Hotel Saint James again...it was a good experience and a great location. **But could have been slightly cheaper for what it offered.**

title: “Consistently Marriot”
text: I stayed at this property several years ago and was extremely happy so I booked a room again. It was just as nice as before. Cozy and clean room with a great view of the Washington Monument. I love the indoor pool for kids and the workout center has everything I need and room to spare. The concierge was very helpful even though we didn't end up booking the sight-seeing tour we were considering. I also like the ability to print our boarding passes from the lobby. Great location too.

title: “Great hotel!”
text:
I really enjoyed staying at this hotel. I'm on a limited budget, so it was nice to have such a comfortable and well equipped room for under $100. The beds were fantastic with nice linens. Contrary to what another reviewer wrote, the linens on my bed I had were very clean. The desk chair was top notch. The bathroom was spotless and had nice Neutrogena toilettries.
The convenience to Metro was much appreciated. It is directly across the street.
I didn't take advantage of the restaurant downstairs. It was too expensive. There is a Cosi restaurant next door that would be a more affordable and quicker option. The hotel had a small (about the size of a closet) food store downstairs with limited pantry type options.

title: “Don't bother”
text:
Being straight to the point:
pros:
good location
well trained and kind staff
clean
nice utensils
cons:
poor lighting
akward furniture (I got a bruise steping out bed!)
challenging bath facet (no way to turn the water on - COLD - without getting wet.)
inconvinient flush (u must be strong to press it all the way)
way too small - even the suite
no NY1 (how come we couldn't watch the local news channel?)
overpriced
suggestion:
go to Affinia Gardens!

title: “You can do better”
text: stayed for 3 nights during the first week of January 2006. Although the lobby is well done, the rooms mirror motel standards. Also I was uncomfotable leaving my car in their parking lot each night after noticing broken glass from a previous 'break in' covering one of the slots.

title: “Will be back!”
text: We had a business conference and had the opportunity to stay at the Allegro. A refreshing change from the usual Marriott properties we often frequent, and our first stay in a Kimpton property in memory. Overall we rate it great, and will be back!

title: “Great value”
text: Free parking, free breakfast and super comfy beds! Did I mention its on the river and a 10 min walk from the center of the river walk and Alamo? It's also about $100 cheaper than many of the other river walk hotels. Check out San Antonio's b-cycle program for bike rentals! There is a b-cycle station 0.2 miles from the hotels front door.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
I stayed at the hotel for two nights in late March with my wife and daughter on a spring break college tour. The Eventi is the nicest Kimpton I have ever stayed in. We stayed in a 1 bedroom suite so my daughter slept on the fold out couch. 
Mostly positives listed below and a few negatives:
It was my daughters birthday so when we arrived at the room there were two cupcakes and a bottle of champagne (nice touch)
The bathroom was an A++++. Workout room A+++Bed A++
Negatives
no good restaurants within walking distance
the area directly around the hotel is a bit dirty
the restaurant attached to the hotel Bar Basque is over priced with bad service and average food
Would I stay here again: YES

title: “Very pleased”
text: My husband and I took the kids to Chicago fo the weekend for their birthdays. We stayed at the Four Points Sheraton downtown. The hotel was very clean and the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The location was great.. we were close to a lot of places that I wanted the kids to see. Would recommend this hotel for your next stay.

title: “50/50”
text:
I stayed at this hotel in August for 1 week. When we arrived to our room I could have cried. The walls in the bedroom were filty dirty and the carpet had huge stains on it. It was a nightmare. I have to admit that the bathroom was very clean so that was something. We had arrived late as night so we had to stay at least one night. When I woke in the morning I didnt mind it too much. We then decided to stay and give it a shot. The halls were really old fashioned, the stairs were disgusting, like something from fauly towers. 
It was very close to Times Square and there was a realy lovely Deli downstairs which was cheap. I would not stay at the hotel again but if you were on a budget it was okay. i have to say that the bed linen was always clean and we had fresh towels every day.

title: “Everything was great !”
text:
What a great surprise we got when we arrived ! We stayed in the Casa del Mar section which is more recent. This is such a nice motel type hotel for a Best Western... a notch above what we are use to !
Our room was large and nicely decorated. We also got free parking and free internet. Water is on both side of the hotel : the bay side with a view of Downtown San Diego quite nice at night and the marina side. A boardwalk goes on both sides. Across the street there is a small playground. The Casa del Mar's heated pool and jacuzzi are right along side the Marina.
The location is also great. Not a lot of traffic at night since we are at the end of the Island. Not far from the ocean, downtown San Diego, Old town, Sea World and the zoo. Really close to the airport without hearing any noise from the plane from our room. 
With AAA we got a wonderful deal for 99$ for all this... unbelievable !!!
Even for a little more per night we would come back here anytime !!!

title: “Great overall stay but unusual pool experience”
text:
I stayed with my 3 kids in April 2012. Staff was friendly and knowledgeable and check in was quick with fresh baked cookies nearby. Our room had 2 queen beds and was very clean. Not a lot of extra room to move around in with just enough room for a chair between the bed and window. 
Breakfast in the morning was prepared well - not something that you can always find with hotel food. The server was pleasant and kept everything well stocked. She was also helpful at the waffle station and pointing out syrup and such. 
We were the only ones in the pool around 6:00. The kids splashed around and had a good time, although the room was very hot as I was just sitting and watching the kids. There are tables and lounge chairs available - in all a very clean environment. We left for dinner and when we returned to the pool area around 9:00, there were a couple more families there. After sitting in there about 20 minutes I noticed the strangest thing. 6 of the 7 kids in the pool were having coughing fits. It was enough to make me look up from my paper and notice what was happening. My son who has not had an asthma flare up in 3 years came over to me and told me that it felt like he couldn't breathe. As soon as we left the pool area he was fine. I'm not sure what caused the problem, but because it was happening to nearly all the kids, I suspect that it wasn't coincidence.
I would stay here again, but keep a close eye on my kids if they are swimming due to the odd experience of the group coughing.

title: “Excellent!”
text: This is my second time staying at the Parc 55 hotel and will not be the last. I love this hotel it is my favorite. The service is great, everyone is helpfull. One night the ladies at the front desk got my sister and me on the guest list for Infusion Lounge, to which we had a great time. Our stay was very pleasant, the service was great all around from the valet, technical support, guest service to bell service.

title: “Something a little different. for the business traveler”
text:
When you travel all the time you get used to nice accomodations (and some not so nice) and just generally don't want a lot of surprises. So when I spent a night this week in Houston at Hotel Indigo I was surprised...but pleasantly.
Hotel Indigo had all the amenities that I use when traveling - a comfortable bed with great pillows, easy to work with lighting so I could read in bed, a small desk area with internet connection, a closet with a nice robe if I went wild, and a basic phone system to connect me with the hotel as needed. 
The surprise was the design. We've all visited hotel rooms that were so beige and I felt myself being drawn into the room with curiousity when I opened the door to shades of blue and green (and I liked it.) I immediately noticed that the floor wasn't carpeted... it was Pergo and immaculate. Walking into the main room the bed took up most of the space but there was seating, a place for your suitcase, an armoire for the TV & closet, and a workable desk (not a lot of space) for your computer with hookup if needed. The walk-in shower was partially enclosed in glass but open to the rest of the bath (made for a great, pulsing shower as I rushed to get ready the next day.)
My only complaint? The comfortable bed took up a lot of space so you sort of feel you need to go to bed....which I did. If you wanted to do some exercises in your room you'd have trouble. But to just come in from a long-day in airports. Nice.
Oh, I had breakfast and a very acceptable tomato/spinach omelette was prepared for me just quickly enough. I like this place and would go back.

title: “Strongly recommended”
text:
We are a party of 6 with young kids and grandparents. Omni SD is one of the best bell /valet staffs I have encountered among hotels. They are friendly, welcoming and helpful. Througout our stays of 5 nights, we are greeted with big smiles anytime we entered the hotel, nice suggestions on where to go, provide us umbrellas when raining, They are professional, excellent, and provide outstanding service. Upon arrival, I told them I will be parking somewhere and not using the valet parking, they are totally cool, they continue to help with the luggages, and you do not feel the pressure or discontent. (Parking across the street is $16 per day) Check-in took 5 minutes, they got our rooms pre-check-in, with adjoining room as requested, and high floor, with excellent view of the city.
For kids:My 2 kids received a gift of cool toys right after check-in, which my daughter was very happy and impressed. It is a little treat but it changes their mood right away. We went into our rooms and there are cookies and milk awaiting for them, again, another surprise and treat. You can also ask front desk to lend you a kid bag which consists of books and games for them to read and play during their stay. My kids said it is the best hotel they had experienced so far ;D 
The rooms are good size, everything is great and clean. bed are very comfortable, no complaints at all. it is a 4 stars and it live up to the rating without problem, I will even rate them a 4.5. 
The Select guest allows us to use internet for free and free beverages, a nice treat. 
Location is perfect, 2 blocks from Gaslamp, the area is safe and clean. CVS in 2 blocks, We travel mostly with our car, and park across the street from the hotel. 
I will not write more as others has written a lot about the hotel, If you travel with young kids, and elderly, are worry about cleaniness, space, safety... I can tell you Omni is excellent, throughout our stay, there is nothing I can complain about or pick on, and I can be picky because we are traveling with kids and elderly. I do not feel the pressure, pretentious staff sometimes experienced with a 4 stars and up, they make us very comfortable, and I strongly strongly recommend it to all.

title: “Cozy for the price & location”
text: My family and I had a great visit in Washington and we were very comfortable at the District Hotel. The rooms are small, the elevator is broken, nevertheless, it is a cozy hotel with a friendly and helpful staff. Also, the location is great, and we were able to safely walk to the White House and museums (took a cab to the Capitol). Anyway, we had no problem with bed bugs or fleas and were there for 4 nights. If you are on a budget and want to stay in downtown DC, then I highly recommend the District Hotel. *My only complaint besides the broken elevator is the wi-fi internet....it was spotty and never worked in the room. I was able to access it on my laptop in the business room.

title: “Clean and Comfortable Rooms”
text:
I won this 3* hotel through Priceline for a rate of $62/night. I stayed one night in March 2008. This hotel is located off of I-15 in Rancho Bernardo. We have no problem finding the hotel and check-in was easy and fast. We were assigned a room in bldg 16. It is a little bit of a walk from the parking lot, but it wasn't too bad. We had a room on the second floor. It was big and spacious with a king bed. There were three sinks in the room. One inside the bathroom along with the toilet and bathtub. Another is outside of the bathroom. There is a sink in the bedroom area as well with plenty of counterspace along with a coffee machine. 
The hotel is about a 20-30 minute drive from the airport and about a 20 minute drive to the Wild Animal Park. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone, especially at the great price I got through Priceline.

title: “Value for money, central location”
text: Was here with family (no children) for shopping and sight-seeing and it was perfect. Right by Macy's, walking distance from Empire State and Times Square and 42nd Street etc. Perfect for 1st time visitors who want to be close to the main sights. Hotel was very busy, and popular. Good diner open 24 hours within the hotel. Nice bar for drinks too. We were luck enough to get rooms above 20th floor - which meant brighter and quieter. Room 2409 in particular was fabulour. Windows all around, with views out over 34th street west to the Hudson. We didnt pay extra for this room even though we felt it was a room 'with a view'!! Rooms were small enough but very clean indeed. Lovely bed linen etc. Wardrobe and bathroom a little jaded - but again, very clean.

title: “Great value”
text: While traveling between Utah and Missouri, we spent Saturday night at the Country Inn & Suites. This was our second stay at this inn. Room was comfortable. Desk staff was very helpful and provided information on local (walk-to) restaurants. Inn had complimentary cookies and coffee in lobby and a good breakfast. Great weekend rates and good value anytime.

title: “Amazing staff!!!!!!”
text:
I am from Australia and stayed for 4 nights. From the minute we arrived we were met by the amazingly friendly and helpful valet. The lovely girl on reception referred to us by name everytime she saw us. Amazing location right across the road from the baseball stadium!! 
Overall amazing experience with super helpful staff! Thank you.

title: “The Hudson - Hip, Hop And Happenning!”
text:
Well, what can I say about the Hudson that hasn't already been said?...
This is quite possibly the funkiest hotel I have ever stayed in. It's in a great location close to Central Park and Columbus Circle subway station and has some great ameneties nearby (diners/drug store etc). 
The bar and restaurant are great and the welcome you get is outstanding...As for the food...WOW!
Yes, the rooms are small but let's face it, you're in a city that never sleeps so what else do you need apart from a bed to rest your weary head after a hard day/night?!

title: “Nice small and clean hotel”
text: Greg the manager left us 2 very nice notes as we arrived way too late, nevertheless the hotel is located directly at venice beach, we were unlucky to arrive late and leave very early in the morning, if you go there, be sure to take an ocean view room and enjoy the ocean.

title: “Love the older hotels of Denver!!”
text:
I did the "Do not Disturb" package with my sister for a girls weekend. Fun place, heated pool on the top floor, the front desk folks were way accommodating, they had a local car service that took us around town. Our rooms were great, balcony, clean and comfy beds. The bathrooms were a bit small, but good for one person.
I have told all my friends to stay local and check this place out. The breakfasts that were part of the package were awesome as well as Mary the young lady that delivered them to us each morning. Thanks for a great stay!!

title: “Not bad at all !!!”
text:
We stayed at the skyline in dec 05. I was really worried about the hotel as I have read some not too good reports, and we had been earlier in the year, and stayed over on lexington ave in a really lovely hotel. As we had booked so late, that the skyline was the only hotel available.
The exterior of the hotel could do with alittle tlc, but when you get in the reception is clean maybe slighlty dated, but not too bad. The rooms are fantastic they are huge, which is highly unusual for nyc they are decorated well, bathroom was clean and has also been recently re-fitted.
It took about 8-10mins to walk to time square, and there are loads of fab restaurants around the hotel, and some really nice deli's for breakfast.
This was a fantastic trip and would really recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to experience nyc at its best.

title: “Pretty darn good for the price”
text: If you want to stay close to downtown (abt 5 mins), close to the freeway, have decent food, excellent service, and pretty spectacular views (from the top floors) and not max out your credit card - this is probably the best place to stay in denver.

title: “Great hotel if you don't mind a little walking”
text: Great hotel. Clean, comfortable, quiet, friendly and helpful staff. Big room. The only downside was that it's kind of off the beaten track. But if you don't mind a 10-minute walk to/from public transportation each day (BART and MUNI), I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “worst embassy suite ever”
text:
Staff knew nothing about Boston, public transportation, location Brandeiss and no one would help
Air conditioning did not work
Asked for non smoking and put in a "non smoking room" but could still smell smoke on floor and in room, could not get room switched
2 lamps broken
breakfast disorganized, dirty silverware, out of juice
driveway cannot accomodate van

title: “Visit the lobby and move on!”
text: This hotel is living off of its historical and modern political visitors, in my opinion. We stay in Denver semi-regularly as a quick getaway/overnight for us. I can think of multiple downtown hotels as good, if not better than this hotel for less (Marriott, Hyatt, Ritz-Carlton, Hilton, etc.). The atrium area when you first enter is indeed impressive, especially considering how old the property is, built in 1892. However, for travelers I'd recommend stopping by, maybe have a meal or their afternoon tea, take some pictures, and find another hotel. My exception to this suggestion will be to mimic what we did using Marriott points (it became part of the Marriott family a couple of months ago). The Brown Palace claims to be top-end, and prominently displays its awards at the desk, but doesn't live up to it in my mind. As a very regular traveler, business and pleasure, here are just some of the reasons it is not worth it's price point as to details expected at this level of hotel: 1-bar of soap for sink and shower, 1 coffee cup, small bathrooms (albeit beautiful and with 2 shower heads), no comfy chair in room (ours had 3 dining room type chairs even with ample room for a larger one that you might actually want to sit in), noise (as they are all about drawing people into their atrium, it is noisy), crowded check-in/checkout area (as they set up for afternoon tea by 9AM), old and stained furnishings in sitting area, disingenuous staff (I get in the hospitality world what it means to work in a property of this supposed caliber, doesn't mean you have to lose your perspective on normal and genuine kindness to all.), no pool, and the fitness center is actually across the street and shared with another property (that's less than half the price per night). On a positive note, they do allow pets, for $100 deposit, but so do many downtown Denver properties. For out-of-state visitors, drive the 70+ miles south to stay at the Broadmoor for about the same price point and a much better hotel experience! For those taking in sites in downtown Denver, there are plenty of other full-service properties that are better.

title: “My stay at the Best Western”
text: I was so pleased with my visit! I'm especially happy with the delicious complementary breakfast. I found the salt water pool to be refreshing and different from what I'm use to! I was very impressed and would recommend this location for everyone!

title: “Great hotel in Times Square!”
text: We traveled to NYC for a week and stayed at the Marriott. We have traveled multiple times over the years to NYC, and this is our favorite hotel in the city of all the different hotels that we have visited. The location to Times Square is excellent and the overall quality and comfort of the rooms is excellent. The rooms are very large and well appointed. The bathroom is fine. My only negative about the room is the quality of the matress. It is not as comfortable as other hotels in this class. We stayed recently in NYC at the Westin and the matress and quality of sleep was superior, but overall the Marriott is our favorite and we will return! The city has strong reputation for many of the hotels having bed bugs and we are very cautious and concerned about this when booking hotels in NYC. We checked our room for any signs and our room was very clean and we found zero signs of any bed bugs. I highly recommend this hotel for your visit to NYC if you are wanting to stay near Times Square.

title: “Loved our stay!”
text:
I was told that the Crowne Plaza took over the management of this hotel from the Hilton, and what a terrific job they've done! Everything was so clean and beautiful, and the service and friendliness of the staff was excellent. The beds are the most comfortable of any I've ever slept in at any hotel, and the amenities and little extras made us feel very special. I highly recommend this hotel. While the other side of the river might have had more to offer in terms of walking to locations, the water taxi at a reasonable price took care of that. When I go back to Jacksonville, this is the place I'm going to stay. Great exercise room too with machines that work. I rate it five stars. The only downside was the location of the pool in a place that groups used for parties. ... 
SJB Lexington, KY

title: “Everything I expect from La Quinta.”
text: Clean rooms, Good breakfast, quiet (I was on the side away from the highway and away from the street), friendly staff, fairly convenient location (there is some construction on the 635, but La Quinta can't really fix that), next to IN N OUT Burger, price was what I expect for a La Quinta of this level of quality. I was very pleased with the place. Cons: shower head is a little low (I'm 5'11"), and water pressure was a little low (but not intolerable).

title: “Comfortable but not too comfortable”
text: We stayed here because it was the most reasonably priced hotel in the downtown Austin area. It was nice because we could walk to bars and restaurants and the South Congress bridge. The hotel was comfortable and the staff were friendly, but some of the amenities were lacking. The "free" Internet was slow, so slow you couldn't stream anything on it without it being very choppy. If you wanted a faster Internet, you had to put in a credit card number and buy it. I felt that was kind of a scam to say they had free Internet when they hardly had Internet, and to get it at a normal speed you had to pay an arm and a leg. There was also no breakfast buffet which was disappointing. There was more of a "stand" with apples and granola bars and coffee. Other than the breakfast and the Internet being slow everything else was fine.

title: “Great view, good location close to Grand Central”
text:
Stayed here over Labor Day weekend with my husband. Husband had work in the city on Friday and we stayed over the weekend to watch the US Open. Work booked the hotel and it ended up being a great location for our needs.
Our room was quite large especially for NYC and we had a great view of the Empire State Building. The room was clean and although it needs some updating was fine for our needs. (We basically just slept and showered here). Grand Central station is a few blocks away. This worked out great since Flushing Meadows (where the US Open is) is on the same line that goes from Grand Central. I've definitely stayed at better hotels in NYC, but if you can get a good price, this is a decent option.

title: “OK, but not up to Hilton's typical quality”
text: This hotel looks very nice upon entering, and the location is amazing if you want to go to a baseball game--I could literally watch the game from our conference room on the third floor, and the ballpark's just across the street. That being said, as far as hotels go, and Hiltons in particular, I've had better. There were just minor troubles that kept adding up to make my stay less than great: the room was way too hot and took forever to cool off once I turned the A/C on (think 7 hours, not 30 minutes), one side of the mattress felt like the springs were broken, and the colors on the TV were way off. But the best of all was that my wake-up call arrived 15 minutes early. It may not seem like a big deal, but when I'm on a work trip and don't get enough sleep as it is, the last thing I want it to wake up earlier than I have to and feel disoriented and confused about what time it is when I'm stumbling around without my glasses in the morning. Oh, and I also got charged twice for internet, but they did fix that at the front desk at check-out. We also ate in the restaurant, which was fine, but the service was a bit hit or miss. Overall, not bad, but definitely not great either. I'd probably try to stay elsewhere the next time I'm in Baltimore.

title: “very average”
text:
My husband, 3 year-old daughter and I (former Chicago residents) have stayed in this hotel four times in the past 12 months. Our most recent was Oct 2005. Each time we stay we say we do not want to return but still keep coming back! The location, as has been mentioned, is perfect. I love it. The staff, overall are very friendly. The rooms are quite shabby and really need updating (for example, the couches are quite worn). I have never seen the pool too busy but it always too cold. During our last stay I asked twice to have the heat increased in the pool. The first person told me it could not be increased, the second was able to turn it up slightly. The view from the pool is beautiful. The equipment in the work out room is all fairly new and well kept/clean.
Each time we plan a trip to Chicago I look and look and end up at the Doubletree because of the price. You can stay in hotels with the same level of rooms and pay _much_ more in similar locations (The Embassy Suites, for example). If you are willing to put up with a few issues (shabby room, cold pool, good but not great service) in exchange for a fabulous location and a low rate then the Doubletree is the place.

title: “Price and Location”
text:
Recently stayed here with my husband for almost 2 weeks. If your main criteria are price and location, then this is the place for you. If you want amenities, you need to keep looking.
It is 1.1 miles to the mall from the hotel. We were there for the Smithsonian museums, so we wanted to be within walking distance. Other than L'Enfant Plaza, all the hotels are over $200/night, with most running you closer to $300-$400/night plus fees. This hotel has free underground parking if you need a car, but if you plan to just go to the mall, you can walk. The rate we paid was under $100/night for a room with balcony overlooking the Washington Channel.
The building is older, but charming when you walk in. The rooms are very dated and aren't maintained like most hotels. The wallpaper was peeling, there was some mildew on the grout in the shower, wood damage to the doors, the handle on the armchair kept popping off, etc. However, it was clean. Given some of the reports of bed bugs in DC, I checked the mattresses thoroughly and they were bug free and we never were bit.
The WiFi is free but very intermittent and weak - 1-3 bars out of 5. The TV has cable, but the picture quality is more like old-fashioned rabbit ears for most channels and only 2 came in clearly. There is no fridge in the room, but with the balcony and it being so cold this time of year, we used our balcony to keep drinks cold. There is a full ironing board in the room if you need it. They provided hair dryer, shampoo, soap, and lotion. There was a large desk with armchairs on either side. There is no coffee pot. The room was a decent size.
There is a lounge in the hotel. They serve happy hour from 4-7p with a few complimentary hors d'oeuvres. The mixed drinks were a reasonable $4, and they were generous with the alcohol. The downside of this lounge is that 3 nights of the week, there is very loud music. We were on the second floor and on Fri/Sat nights, when they seemed to have a band there, it was very loud in our room past midnight. You could hear the DJ music on the other nights as well. There is a restaurant in the hotel (Pier 7) that we had dinner in one evening - ok food, high-ish prices. There is also a cafe type place that is open during the morning and serves breakfast. We never ate there, but that is where I would run down in the morning to grab a cup of coffee. 
If you head south on Water St from the hotel, you will hit a Safeway and the Metro station in 2 blocks. If you head north, you hit the Fisherman's market area in 2 blocks which was fun to see and has one to-go eatery called "Jimmy's Grill" that has very affordable and generous portions of fried seafood, homemade pies, and more that seemed very popular.
The area itself is well lit and we never had any issues walking to and fro. There was one homeless gentleman camped out about a block away that we ended up nicknaming "The Giggler" as he always giggled when someone walked by, but he never approached us. We would feel safe bringing our children to this area.

title: “Grand Hotel Great Stay”
text: Stayed 3 nights with my wife and could not have asked for anything more.As a Hilton Honors member I had a very large room overlooking the lake.The bed was comfortable,room temperatures perfect and the whole place had a look of a grand hotel.One tip if you must have a car,park across the street behind the hotel about 20.00 a day,the Hilton and any other hotel on Michigan are about 50.00 a day.

title: “Dissappointed”
text: On arriving after a long flight, our room wasn't ready, so we went to have some lunch and when we arrived back at the hotel we were given our room. Much to my dissappointment we were given a room with two double beds after calling down to reception the gentlemen told me that was what i booked . After explaining that was not so, he allocated us to another room with a king bed saying a gentlemen would bring up our new room key, on arriving at our door he seemed annoyed that we didn't like the room and wanted to move. Also didn't like the paper cups provided to make your coffee in your room.

title: “Great place especially for the price”
text: The Best Western Hotel Tomo was a great place to stay. The hotel doesn't offer amenities such as valet parking or free breakfast, but the location and price more than make up for that. The room was clean and the staff was very friendly. The parking lot is small but there is a large lot within walking distance. Also within walking distance are scores of restaurants and shops. I recommend this hotel to anyone looking to travel on a budget who likes a clean room and a great neighborhood to roam around in.

title: “NIce hotel, great location but poor service!”
text:
Location is perfect for San Francisco, downtown is only 5 mins away. Lovely design of hotel-as you'd expect from Starck! Poor customer service in general:
1. Wasn't offered help with luggage on arrival (3 suitcases aswell as hand baggage and our 2 year old daughter)!
2. Not showed around / advised of the facilities the hotel provided upon check in.
3. Doorman 2 of them-rarely opened the door-whats the point?! Also all bar one were miserable!
