4. Concierge very limited knowledge of the area, I felt I knew more yet it was my first visit to the city.

title: “A hostel - not a hotel”
text:
I stayed here in August in one of the standard cabins on the 5th floor (room 534). I had read reviews online after I had already booked and was very worried about bed bugs. I requested a room that was bed bug free and was told that the 5th floor generally was not yet infested. 
The room was VERY small, smelled of cigarette smoke and wasn't stylish at all. Dirty carpets, bathrobes with holes and worst of all in the august heat no aircon and only a very basic fan. 
I had hoped for a pocket sized boutique hotel, but got a bog standard hostel instead. 
The location is great if you want to get a feel for the real west village life away from the tourist sites. Great restaurants and cool bars within walking distance. A very safe area. 
I didn't see the captains rooms, so cannot comment on them. 
I definately wouldn't stay here again. I had a look at the new NoMad hotel and I think it's worth paying the extra for.

title: “Wonderful Hotel In Back Bay, MA”
text: Came here for Business, but will be back for my own personal stay. Close to the station and many other fun places. Back Bay is a great neighborhood and has many places to eat & drink. This stylish hotel had amazing service, clean, and a great price. The room was perfect and the bed was so fluffy. A must Recommend.

title: “You get what you pay for”
text:
You can't beat this hotel for price and convenience, however...we stayed just one night and both woke up with major sinus problems! The congestion/pressure/headache is incredible. Now, I can't prove it was the room, but we went to bed feeling fine. We had difficulty getting the room to a comfortable temperature and ran the air all night---I don't know if there is a mold issue or what, but something in the room/air/environment made us sick.
Otherwise, the room was moderately clean, if rather shabby. 
The price makes it hard to complain.

title: “Fabulous stay - great hotel”
text: This hotel is in a great location and all you would expect from a 4* hotel.The hotel rooms were large and comfortable with a high standard of cleanliness. The service was friendly but not overwhelming and all requests met with no fuss. Great restaurant and bar facilities. fabulous stay.

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
The Renaissance Hotel is a large high end establishment right in the heart of the Inner Harbor. From a location perspective, you really can’t do any better than this hotel. The lobby, rooms and corridors were all lovely; the beds very comfortable. The staff was uniformly polite and professional. Food at the Watertable restaurant was a little too pricey for our taste, although the breakfast at The Ground Floor Cafe & Bar was not unreasonable and well prepared. There is a nice indoor heated pool which we found quite relaxing. Negatives for the establishment included a $24 per day parking fee and a $12.95 per day internet fee, if you wanted to go online. (Indeed after doing the math, I signed up for a smartphone with 3G internet access. I decided it was a better use of my money. If the Holiday Inn, Hampton Inn, Panera Bread, Starbucks, Wendy’s and McDonalds can provide free internet, you wonder why the management at Marriott cannot figure out how to do the same thing.) These annoyances were offset by a reasonable room rate obtained through my job.
Despite my screed, this was a wonderful hotel and I would gladly stay there again.

title: “They take nickle and diming you to a WHOLE new extreme!”
text:
When I booked this hotel, I was extremely excited because I got it through priceline.com for $80/night. A great deal for a young, broke family of five just looking to get away for the weekend. When we got there, the man at the front desk asked if we would be parking our car there. Surprised, I said yes. He then rings me up, and informs me that parking is $37/night plus tax. I was shocked. But it was 10:30 at night and my three children under 4 years old were in the car just exhausted. So I said Ok.
 I asked about continental breakfast. "Oh, it's $21/person," came the reply. Really? In this economy? You're going to CHARGE that much for something the majority of hotels- including the majority of Holiday Inn's!- give for FREE??! OK. Well, luckily I had packed fruits, bread, peanut butter and protein bars. 
So I went on to my next question: "Is there a mini fridge in the room?" "Nope", came the flippant response. "If you want a fridge it's an extra twenty-five bucks a night."
Now, this might be standard for hotels to charge extra for an "ammenity" like this, but by this point I was just livid by how they were trying to squeeze money out of us. And it just got worse when we went to the room!
There was a list by the phone of breakfast options you could order. $14.95 for the "deluxe" breakfast - your choice of juice, choice of white or wheat toast, a piece of fruit, and coffee or tea. If you wanted to order food a la carte, a PIECE of toast was $2.95! More than a loaf of bread!
And, if you wanted to watch your favorite TV episodes while you were there, you couldn't turn on the TV to ABC or NBC, standard channels in ANY hotel room I've ever been to, INCLUDING Holiday Inn's. You had to BUY the episode on pay per view. That's right, to watch Grimm we would've had to pay $5.95. 
All in all, my issues lie in the fact that I paid $90 for parking (more than one night for five people to stay in one of their hotel rooms!) And that they were just trying to squeeze as money from you as they could. The lady that was supposed to be helping us find our tour bus could barely speak English and had us waiting for an hour at the wrong spot. So that was irritating. All in all I would NEVER stay in another Holiday Inn if this is an example of how they conduct business. I have stayed many times in Holiday Inn Express before and have really enjoyed it. I guess the express means they treat you better and give you more value for you dollar.

title: “Clean”
text: Very clean and priced good. Beds were okay but room did have refrigerator and microwave which was great since we have little ones that need snacks before bedtime. Breakfast was okay.

title: “Perfectly Wonderful”
text: We live near Boston and we choose this hotel for special occasions. It is comfortable and beautifully kept. A very special place that is staffed with people who do their best to make your stay wonderful. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “The Worst”
text: This place was FILTHY and disgusting!!!! The carpet was so dirty it turned my socks totally black. There was water leaking from the back of commode and the floor and rug were soppinng wet. The tub and sink were so dirty and there was a foreing substance dripping down the walls in the shower. Only had one pillow case on pillow and they smelled bad. The "so called" breakfast was dry cereal and old bagles from the day before. Will NEVER stay in this god awful place again.

title: “Loved the Warwick”
text: My husband and I spent three nights at the Warwick, arriving on November 29. We got a great rate on Priceline, which may account for the fact that our room faced the interior (9th floor) and the sound of the building's outside heating units could be heard slightly. When asked about an outside view, the front desk responded it would be $50 per night extra. We opted not to change room. Other than the no view room, we loved the Warwick, the rooms are clean, well appointed, and comfortable. Yes as others said the room was a bit warm but again not a big deal for a short stay. The lobby is beautiful and I loved the ambience of the entire hotel. I definitely would stay here again as it's steps from MOMA, close to subway, and near great places to eat and shop.

title: “Worst service ever”
text: Upon checking in the representative advised me that there was only an allowance of 6 visitors, and their names had to be on a list, followed with a letter of the Hotel's policies that required a signature. On the letter it stated if you have any questions or concerns to contact the manager. I asked to speak with a manager and was advised by Matthew the gentleman working the front desk that Eugene wouldn’t be in until 9:00 p.m. I checked in around 3:00 p.m. or a little after, and didn’t understand why a manager of a large Hotel chain wasn’t on staff, and the Indianapolis Black Expo event was going on, one of Indianapolis Largest events every year. I left my contact information for Eugene to contact me, and expressed my concerns with the front desk staff. I’ve known several people that have had large Bachelorette gatherings last year; my brother had a small Birthday gathering at this hotel a few years ago, and was never asked to give names of guest coming in and out of hotel. I understand every hotel has policies, but they should be in effect at all times especially if it’s regarding the fire hazard code, which was addressed to me. My concerns were I find it hard to believe every guest are asked to sign a policy letter, and the policies addressed on the letter seems to have been revised due to the event being held in town “not your typical policy form”. I’m only speaking from experience; in my opinion this is something that was being asked for because of the event being held in town, and I felt a sense of discrimination which is not a good feeling to have. The Super Bowl was hosted here this year and I am sure that the guest that stayed here during that time (February 2012) did not experience such. I just don't believe that if it had guest at all during this event then the staff didn't have time to take down names of everyone coming in and out of the hotel to visit the staying guest. I am sure that Homewood did because all of the hotels in the downtown area were sold out for that event. I would like to start with Euguene came up to my hotel room around 10:00 p.m., with another gentleman that he didn’t even acknowledge to me. I felt it was very inappropriate to come and knock on the door, for one I could have been in the shower, not in the room, just stepped out or what have you. I don’t understand why he didn’t call the room, or my cell phone which was provided to Matthew at the front desk. Also, if you have a guest with a complaint when you got in at 9:00 p.m. why did it take you an entire hour to contact me. When I stepped out the room, he told me who he was, and that I had called corporate with a complaint and what were my issues. His approach was very unprofessional, lacking extreme customer service, and he was very condescending. He’s a Manager and first impressions are everything they set the tone of a business, and he really didn’t make Home wood suites a place I would ever step foot in. I expressed my concerns, and he came back with the hotel policies, and that he felt offended that I felt there was discrimination going on. He was very nasty, he didn’t listen to me and that’s customer service one on one, listen to your customers. I’m a nurse and deal with patients everyday and no you can’t please everyone, and no one likes to hear complaints but that’s life, and if you give the complaint your attention you may be able to please that one person that one time, and position your business to reap the benefits of good customer service. He stated these rules have been into effect every since he started, which they might be but aren’t enforced on a regular. Honesty is everything, and during the check in process if they would of said, it’s an event in town, and to monitor the safety of the building and traffic if your having any visitors your only allowed so many, and we will put their names on a list and give it to security, it’s not normally enforced but we have to during big events, there would have been no problems on my end. I was so frustrated, and disappointed with Eugene's behavior, it made me get out of character because of his attitude, demeanor and tone that he used while speaking with me. He proceeded to tell me to lower my tone, its guest in the building, and if he was so concerned with the guest why come up to my room where the guests are staying, As a good Manager he would have called either my room or my cell first before just barging up to my room. You already know you have a customer that’s upset, I’m not hard to please I’m like anybody else that spends their money, you want to feel valued. The gentleman he was with was being more expressive, and acknowledging with his facial expressions when I was speaking as if he understood my concerns, why couldn’t Mr. Eugene. I asked him why is security only downstairs after 10:00 p.m. checking names, and not on staff at all times, checking guest coming in and out of the hotel, and he responded in a very condescending way “I know what your doing, I know what your trying to do”, that’s not how you talk to a guest staying at your Hotel, and you call your self a Manager. Mr. Eugene told me I could put six people name on a list, he could give me a banquet room, or give me a refund and we could leave. He kept referring to a party, like we had a lot of people in the room. I rented the room because my brother came from out of town for the event, and it was his Birthday, so I made some light abderves, and had a few family members in the room and we were going to an event being held that night. I would never rent a room with the intentions of being disruptive to other guest, if I wanted to have a party I would have rented a facility. What we were doing weren’t out of the norm, no one complained on us, we weren’t being loud. I proceeded with we'll be glad to leave because that’s what you want us to do, my father was in the room and he’s 63 years old, he was upset my mom was upset, everyone it was humiliated at how we were treated. If your going to spend $232.00 a night on a room, I would recommend another hotel that’s going to appreciate your business, like the JWM Marriott a beautiful hotel that speaks for itself.

title: “Superior service!”
text: The Dupont Hotel staff is among the most pleasant and professional I have ever encountered. I had booked on a defunct internet discount site and found myself without an actual reservation through no fault of the hotel. They were able to find alternate accomodations for the one night they could not house my family and we were able to complete our DC vacation at The Dupont. The concierge staff is without equal and reception, doormen and others were extremely courteous and helpful. The location right at Dupont Circle is great as well.

title: “Modern hotel with pleasant, helpful staff”
text:
We got a really good deal on our room, a very large room with king bed. Clean, nice bathroom and shower. The usual amenities for a hotel of this caliber, including morning paper delivery outside room door, large flat screen TV, iPod docking station. I was merely surprised at the fee to use the internet at the business center. However, one was able to view and print boarding pass for no charge.
Would stay again.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
Stayed during SXSW Festival.
Pros:
* Located across from convention center and within walking distance to all parts of SXSW.
* Comfortable beds and pillows.
* Working A/C (although I had a hard time finding how to turn it off - light switch behind the drapes did the trick)
* Good shower
* Full restaurant and Starbucks on site
* Parking garage underground
* Computer with internet in lounge area
* Friendly valet guys
Cons:
* Charge for parking
* Unable to park trailer due to underground lot, but we knew this beforehand (it is stated on their website); We found a lot near the capitol and he gave us a discounted rate (charged for only two spaces, although we took up more) and he allowed us to leave it overnight, although the lot was only open until 3 AM. 
* Inflated rates during SXSW

title: “Horrible Hotel, Glorified Hostel, Terrible Customer Service”
text:
One good thing I can say about this hotel is it is in a great location right in Times Square. Otherwise, it is horrible. The customer service is unlike anything I have experienced before, the worst. You can't keep your room key and must turn it in each time you leave the hotel since it is an actual door key. The keys are always all over the front desk for anyone to take. You can't have more than 1 person in a room without paying an extra fee. The furniture in the entire place is falling apart. The AC window unit was very loud and wasn't on when I entered the room which was about 90 degrees upon arriving. The bathroom was tiny but clean. You could only open the window an inch in the bathroom to let the steam out since there was no screen on it and the pigeons outside would come in. The 20" TV was on a cart that was so low to the floor that you could not watch it from the bed. The closet was so small that you could not shut the closet door unless the hangers were sideways. I would never recommend this hotel to anyone nor would I ever stay there again. It was a glorified hostel that charges way to much. If you have ever seen the 1980's movie Big with Tom hanks, this is the nasty hotel that he stays in in NYC. It doesn't look much better than it did back then. 
If you want somewhere for the same price that is nice, 4 blocks from Times Square, and has exceptional service; look at the Hampton Inn Times Square South. This was a great hotel.

title: “Great Place to Stay in NYC”
text: This motel was absolutely wonderful. Rooms were spacious & clean, free continental breakfast each morning & the staff was great. We were in NYC during the Christmas Season and having hot chocolate,coffee, & tea available to us at all times in the lobby when we arrived back to our rooms was a nice treat. When we asked about getting a taxi to get back to Laguardia airport on time, the staff just took over & took wonderful care of us. Lincoln towncar was ready & waiting for us when we got to the lobby at 6am the morning we checked out for the same price as taking the cab into the city when we arrived. If this Arkansas traveler ever returns to the big apple this is absolutely the place I will be staying.

title: “Loved everything about the hotel”
text: Eventi was simply perfect. I can't think of one complaint about the hotel. The location is great, just two blocks from the subway and on sixth avenue. The hotel staff is very friendly, they ask about your day and I would especially like to thank Bobby and Dwayne for their politeness. The room is spacious enough (it was only my husband and I), the bathroom being the highlight as it was big, well-lit and clean. Sure, the price is a little over our usual budget, but we decided to indulge because it was our one-year anniversary. I hope I can stay here again on my next trip to NY! If you're a Kimpton Intouch member, you get free wifi too!

title: “Not bad for the money”
text:
We stayed here for one night during the weekend of June 23rd. The hotel is located on the edge of Lincoln Park, walking distance from the zoo, Wrigley Field and transportation. There are several restaurants within walking distance as well. The hotel is very old but seems to be well kept. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. We arrived earlier in the morning, several hours before our check-in time. They pre-registered us and allowed us to obtain our parking early so we had a place to park before our room was ready. The room was very tiny will a full size bed, two bed side tables and a flat screen tv on the wall. It had a walk-in closet and a tiny bathroom with a full tub, shower and sink. The door to the bathroom would not open all the way because the toilet was directly behind the door. It did not have the greatest view but we was not there to sit and look out the window. The room was very clean and had enough amenities to accommodate our one night stay. They offer a continental breakfast in the morning with juices, milk, coffee, yogurt, assorted dry cereals, pastries, bagels, and toaster waffles. 
To end, by no means is this a 5 star hotel or even close to a Hilton. Probably closer to a Best Western but much older. The hotel is very old and decor is very outdated but adds a lot of character to the building. If you need a nice clean place to stay for a night or two, this would be a great place. It might get a little cramped if you were staying longer or if you have more then two people.
The price point was on the lower end of the other hotels that we looked at. Just remember that this is Chicago and you get what you pay for. If you have high expectations of getting the royal treatment for very little money, it is probably not going to happen!

title: “Location is not so central, but the staff and food make it worth the stay!”
text:
Stayed here for 5 days on business. Good workout room with sauna. Indoor and outdoor pool. Pool bar, restaurant is great service and food! 
The staff has been very helpful. Just don't try and make a reservation at the front desk. For some reason it must be done over the phone or online. A VERY good deal can be found on priceline.
All in all standard Marriott quality, you won't be disappointed!

title: “awesome location...good fit for this trip”
text:
as soon as i was able to move my room from next to the elevator (i can hear the cables moving) i was more confident at having a good night's sleep.
the downside was that the room away from the elevator shaft was way smaller than the one by the elevator...so if you have a hearing deficiency, go for the bigger room!
rooms were clean and staff was efficient. location was great!

title: “Big loud party hotel with great location”
text:
We've stayed in a few Manhattan hotels over the past few years and this is our first time at a chic hotel like this one. My wife and I are both middle age, so we're passed the late night party stage. Our flight was delayed coming into NYC and we arrived at the hotel at 10:30pm on a friday night. By that time, the lineup at the front for the parties was quite long (picture lots of tall girls in ultra short dresses), and the lobby was blaring with club music and party goers. I could barely hear the very pleasant girl at the checkin counter.
We stayed on the 10th floor, room 1018. While we liked the funky cool design of the hotel and the rooms, being close to the top floor from 10pm til 3am was terrible due to the extremely loud club music on the rooftop lounge. Both Fri and Sat nights the music was pumping to at least 3am (luckily we're deep sleepers due to all the walking from the day), but you could feel the bass thumping in your pillow and bed as we tried to fall asleep. Sunday was boys night at the rooftop patio, and music ended a bit earlier (around 9pm I think). So if you're a light sleeper, insist on getting a lower level room.
The layout and size of the room is fine (for Manhanttan standards), the bed is comfy but a bit on the soft size. The bathroom has many faults, including the terrible sink and faucet which you just can't use to wash your face without splashing water everywhere. The rain shower head also has very little coverage, so don't even think about showing with your spouse (so much for the romantic getaway), plus there's no tub either, just a large standing shower area. Our sink faucet didn't have proper hot water flow, and I had called the front desk to send their "engineer" to fix the problem, but after my return at the end of the day, the problem was still not fixed.
While we didn't go into the pool, we did walk thru and it looked like a nice little area to rest in during the warmer months of the year. The rooftop patio is also gorgeous with nice comfy sofa chairs and a fantastic view.
The best part of the hotel was the location, right around the corner from Chelsea Market (great coffee at Ninth Ave Espresso and breads/pastries from Amy's bread, fresh seafood from the fish market), and also a short walk to get to the new High Line walk way. Subway stations also nearby, and plenty of good restaurants as well.
So if you are staying here on a weeknight Sun - Thurs, then you'll have a lovely quiet stay, but on a Fri and Saturday night, be prepared to wade thru the throng of party goers as you come and go from your hotel.

title: “AirForce family's”
text:
I stayed so I could see my son graduate from BMT and I recommend them to any family coming to LackLand. I stayed 2 nights and requested no housekeeping and put the DND sign on my door so I can't evaluate the house keeping. I did stop the housekeeper outside my room for more coffee and she was very pleasant. The front desk was very nice and helpful. They helped me with my late cab and recharged my camera batteries since I forgot mine. I spent most of my time on Base but I did walk to the gas station so I could stock my "fridge" with drinks and some snacks and also walked to the Denny's for dinner. The highways are very confusing and under construction so I really recommend using a cab instead of a rental car. Due to the high humidy the door didn't shut completely automatically so give it a pull or push when you come and go to make sure it's closed all the way. The base is around the corner so I was on base where I needed to be in 10 min. (a 10$ cab ride including tip) my first night ( Thurs) was $58. and the second (Friday) was $61. so you cant beat the price. It saved me money to use with my son and location saved me time also. I didn't use the pool or laundry area so I can't comment but I enjoyed my stay and felt safe which meant alot since I was a women traveling alone.
Steph

title: “Good hotel in great location - loved SF!”
text: We used this hotel as our first base in SF to San Diego road trip. Booked thru Trailfinders and our main contact Ryan could not have been more helpful. Everybody at Trailfinders was knowledgeable and helpful and would highly recommend! Ryan came up with draft itinerary and we tweaked the hotels using TripAdvisor and we were not really disappointed. All recent reviews for the Chancellor are about right! Perfect location - hotel not luxurious - in fact a little tired - but staff were friendly and we are very comfortable. We asked for a quiet room - we are very light sleepers. Room initally allocated was on the 2nd floor at the rear but dark and quite noisy due to aircon units on neighbouring buildings. Were moved to a much lighter room on 9th floor by very helpful and understanding receptionist. Still some aircon noise but would be fine for most "normal" sleepers! Would consider hotel nexttime and would recommend. We didn't eat at the hotel but ate for 3 nights in Scala's just across the road which was excellent (do book first if pos)! NB booked car thru Alamo via Trailfinders for our departure day - they are very handily located for Union Sq (there are other hire firms nearby) and despite the perceived nightmare of driving in central SF it was very simple to get out of town heading south (towards Monterey) using their directions and satnav/GPS which would highly recommend (about £20). Car (auto VW Jetta) was reliable and easy to drive.

title: “Loved the Riverfront”
text: Stayed here on business. Loved it, but it's pricey and we weren't paying. It's right on the St. Johns River, the view was delightful, the bed was heavenly and the service was wonderful. Upon our arrival we were served fresh lemonade in the lobby. It's a beautiful facility.

title: “Good location; okay hotel; almost no closet/drawer space”
text: Just your average hotel...nothing special. Pros: Good location between Times Square and Central Park. Clean. Good water pressure in the shower. Friendly enough staff. Starbucks coffee in the in-room coffee makers. Nice fitness room with cardio and free weights. Cons: Small rooms and very little closet/drawer space (My husband and I were there for 5 days climbing over our luggage and storing half of our folded clothes on the closet shelf and top of dresser; claustrophobic and messy...drove me nuts!). TINY bathroom with only one sink. Bring your own shampoo, soap and lotion. Theirs is eh.

title: “Tough Reviewer, worth every cent.”
text: We are tough reviewers from Perth, (two Adults and one 9 yo girl) from Western Australia on hotel stays, and we found the Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn value for money and provided everything we needed. We stayed from the 16th to the 19th of December 2010. I chose the location to visit Universal Studios and the Hollywood area. The hotel provides a free regular shuttle service to Universal studios and when needed a drop off and pickup at the North Hollywood Metro station. The room had two comfortable queen beds, provided laundry rooms and a pool and spa. The staff were very friendly and helpful, the hotel is ideally located to explore the area via car (which we didn't) or public transport. For our needs, the Beverly Garland ticked all the boxes. We highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Thanksgiving in NYC”
text:
We were charmed by the Shelburne Murray Hill.......Our family of 4 made our first trip to the city over the Thanksgiving Holiday. We chose this hotel because we wanted to experience brownstone type living. It was like we had our own mini apartment! We even cooked in a couple times. We enjoyed walking from this great location and found
that everyone we encountered was helpful. 
There were several little resteraunts close by and a grocery within a couple blocks. And Grand Central Station was just about 5 blocks away. 
If you are looking for sleek and modern, this is not the hotel for you. But if you are looking for charming and genteel then you will enjoy.

title: “Awesome!”
text: The day of check in the hotel was able to let us check in early. Olivia @ the front desk was fabulous knowing it was one of our birthdays she made sure we had champange and boston cream pie! The traditional room is a great price and big enough for 2. The location is supurb, we walked to everything. The only bad thing is my truck was damaged in the valet garage. Not a little ding a huge dent!!!! But overall the Omni parker is a great place. We will stay here every time we visit Boston. Just to update...the Valet manager called today 9/11/11 to appologize and he was very nice! It means alot to me.

title: “Great hotel”
text: What a great hotel! My son (age 8) absolutely was captivated my the fish and the turtles in the atrium. He was able to feed them upon request from the front desk for food. The breakfasts were awesome saving us a minimum of $30/day (we stayed 5 days so $150 savings there). The cocktail hour(s) were nice and relaxing..a nice touch. The steakhouse was awesome (thanks George) for food and service. Everyone was great. yes, lots of renovation going on but, no noise that I heard. The outdoor pool was chilly but a beautiful area. The computer that the guests could use was a bit outdated and kept jamming on me while checking emails. The room was great. Loved it and we would come again! And the weight room helped us work off some of those coktails and popcorn. THANKS.

title: “summer camp for Elvis fans”
text: While the photos of the heartbreak hotel website do represent the lobby accurately we found our room to look NOTHING like the ones shown on the website. We were given a handi-capped access room with no outside windows, seriously the window we had looked down onto the dining area on the main floor. The room itself was spacious all be it shabby, the carpet looked old, the room smelled off, and the bathroom hadn't been updated in years. When we check in we asked for a non smoking room and this is what they gave us, no other rooms were available so we were stuck. The dining area/bar was cheap and under serviced. The buffett breakfasts simply awful for anyone who's the least bit health conscience. Elvis Presley was a world class entertainer, shame the "official" Elvis hotel is so shabby and cheap. After two nights we decided to check out and move to the Hampton Suites in Downtown, Memphis.

title: “Never Again”
text:
I stayed here for 2 nights and my god that was too long!
Unfortunately at the same time a load of teenagers were staying too - presumably on a school trip.
What follow was having to listen to them in the hall ways.
Another great delight was the ice bucket machine which was opposite my room and the door wasn't closable to the room - again lots of nice noise.
The room was huge but not fantastic. The bathroom was grotty and looked like it needed a good clean down.
I barely saw any staff around to be honest and when I had to go down the receiption to get my suitcase they didn't seem bothered that I took it myself upstairs even though portage was included! Went down for breakfast and they weren't organised at all, the food looked manky and cold and the hosts didn't speak English. I walked out and headed for Starbucks which is close by.
If you don't care about class and want to stay in a cheap place then this is ideal - not bad location that's all I'll say but as my first trip and hotel stay in New York it didn't make me want to go back any time soon.

title: “A great place to stay!”
text: My husband and I stayed here because of medical appointments at UCSF. The location was ideal--right across the street from the hospital's shuttle service and also within walking distance to the hospital. The staff was wonderful and helpful in so many ways--can't say enough good things about them! The rooms we were in were immaculately clean and comfortable, and we found the decor charming. It was convenient to city transportation, restaurants, cafes and a great sports pub was two doors away. Whole Foods is a block away and there are other food stores and a drug store that is close by. We would definitely stay here again!

title: “Not comfortable at all!!!”
text: Originally planned to stay there for a week since the kitchen suite sounded appealing, but we arrived there and the hallway smelled bad of something that burnt and other unpleasant odors mixing in the air as well. Our bed was the most uncomfortable. I couldn't sleep at night. Checked out immediately the next day. Staff was nice though. This place is more suitable for people who need a place to stay for work. ie. construction workers. I will not go back again.

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text: This hotel is very nice. I like that it is close to downtown/ the Galleria and restaurants.... The room was very nice.....Will stay again when I return to Houston.

title: “Nice corner room”
text: Was given a corner room for my 2 nights stay at Hilton Boston Downtown - spacious and quiet. The location was just great for business in downtown Financial District; also within easy walking distance to South Station, Faneuil Hall and the Aquarium. Helpful staff at the concierge. Considered myself lucky to get it under $200 a night just before St. Patrick's Day.

title: “Great location, great price, no frills.”
text: Recently stayed at the Moore Hotel from June 25-June 30. First of all, the location is fantastic. You are within walking distance of The Space Needle, Pike Place Market and Safeco Field. My wife and I took in all of these during our stay, walking to all. There is a monorail a couple of blocks down to take you to the Space Needle if you wish and the light rail is also a couple blocks away if you choose not to walk to the ballpark and Chinatown. Secondly, the price was excellent. We travel to at least one major city each summer and this is the first time we've been able to stay in the middle of the city for less than $100 a night. That's a huge plus, cutting down on cab rides after a night out on the town or subway/rail fares. The downside, and these are minimal for people traveling for a vacation, is that there are very few frills here. The rooms are very basic, it's an older hotel. You won't see a flat screen TV in your room and the bathroom had old style sinks and the shower was actually a combo shower/old style bathtub. The wireless internet only worked in the lobby, though it is free there. There is also a PC in the lobby that anyone can use if they need to for no charge. For people like us that are there to see the city sights and spend very little time in our hotel room, these things weren't an issue. If you're looking for creature comforts, stay somewhere else. Overall, our experience was positive, and I would recommend this hotel to any leisure traveler. An added note for people who enjoy the nightlife, there is a pub located next door that had a lot of character. It seems to be a hangout for locals, but they treated us very well. We felt very comfortable there.

title: “good stay”
text: The hotel was great! room service was especially courteous and the bed and showerhead were awesome. top pick for a business trip in the area, but not a weekend getaway. my stay was better than expected, but would only go back for work.

title: “A Very Unique Hotel”
text: One of the most unique hotels I've stayed at. The hotel is built into a mountain...And it's not all connected, the mountainside is adorned with dozens of buildings which make up the hotel rooms...All are outside access (the room door goes right to the outdoors, not a hallway), which I generally hate, but works well here. Big, comfortable rooms. One particular restaurant sticks out as 'AMAZING' to me--'A Different Pointe of View' has some of the most romantic views I've ever seen...It's at the top of the mountain, and you can see the entire Phoenix valley below. VERY COOL, VERY ROMANTIC. (And very expensive). Food and service isn't anything special, but it's worth it just for the views. If it's not summer and you can get one, get an outside table or a windowfront inside. Regardless, after dinner, go down a level to the outside bar for coctails to enjoy the view.

title: “Printers need ink, otherwise, very good value”
text:
This Courtyard is a great location near the 805 freeway. It is very quiet with very nicely kept grounds, a pool, and relaxation areas. Staff was very courteous and we had a very nice and fast check in. Nice lobby with plenty of comfortable seating. A car is a must if staying at this property.
Free parking.

title: “Consistently good!”
text:
We recently stayed here again, making it our third stay in the last 5 years. And I can honestly say this hotel gets better every time.
This hotel is extremely family friendly and appears to have been renovated quite recently. Staff are always attentive, professional and accomodating. Had occasion to be working on my laptop in the lobby where no one would've noticed me and I could hear the day manager (Juan?) training his staff. I was most impressed with the attitude he was trying to convey to them. Rooms are always clean and they have really user-friendly, remote controlled air-conditioning systems.
The hotel is conveniently located and even sells passes for the local attractions. A free, continental breakfast is offered every day and there are even a few hot items. We are not big breakfast eaters, so this is ideal.
We always request a room that has a king bed and an attached room with bunk beds for the kids (the room is separated by french doors). Although this type of room is not wheelchair accessible, all of the showers have handles and the hotel does provide shower chairs. Unfortunately, they do not provide wheelchairs so bring your own.
We actually stayed here on two separate stops during our SoCal vacation and were pleased with the service and value both times. Over the last five years, we have stayed here another two times and the level of service is consistent. We look forward to staying here each time we come to San Diego. Keep up the great work!

title: “Prime Location hotel for around $100 - what do you expect?!”
text:
I gave the hotel the Neutral rating because I am taking location & price in consideration. No this is not some First Class establishment but you are prime location in NEW YORK and only paying a little over $100 a night! If you are expecting the Waldorf then quit being cheap and shell out the money for the Waldorf! I travel A LOT and the hotel was much as I expected considering I can easily walk to Times Square and Penn Station - it is well worth what I paid. The check in process was a nightmare. Think the computers were down & they should have found a way to handle that better but other than that I was fine with my stay.
I agreed with the fellow that if this is your one & only time to do NY and you are wanting to do it right then keep shopping. If you are tight on money though you will save a mint on taxis here as well.

title: “Excellent location”
text: We visited as a family and found rooms to be very clean with nice bathroom products to use and good quality slippers and robes which is always a bonus! Cheese and wine was lovely every evening. Breakfast was fresh and topped up quickly when needed. Location is excellent for a short stay and the subway easy to use.

title: “Could not stay here with children”
text:
Please do yourself a favour and book somewhere else! I did not like this hotel at all! From the moment I drove in, things went badly. the first sight I was greated with was a lady in slippers being ejected from the hotel bar at 3 int he afternoon.
I was travelling with an infant and when I went to check in, I had to wait 20 minutes while the front desk staff member finished taking bookings, even though my daughter was fussing; This was not just finishing the call she was on, but taking three other calls while I waited.
When I was served, I was told I had an upgrade to a King size room - I would hate to see what a standard room was!
I was then given a map of how to get to my room. The enterance was not through the lobby but further down in the carpark. Even at 3pm, it was dark and I did not feel safe. None of the lights worked in the buttons for the lift, so I couldn't tell whether it was working or not. There was no security to get into the lift area or the corridors of the hotel. When I enterred my room, I had trouble locating the light switch, which was half hidden behind the buitl in wardrobe. It only turned ont he light at the entrance. The room was so dark I could see in. I felt my way to the nearest lamp which did not work (later found out it was not plugged int). I had to grope my way across the room to open the curtains to let some light int
The room was clean and neat but in need of some maintenance. Most of the furniture had scratches on it. The sheets did not fit the mattress properly and there was no top sheet - just a comforter.
The door to the bathroom stuck and was difficult to open. The coffee maker was located beside the toilet - a common theme in Austin.
The room was small and filled with furniture. Even though i had specified I was travelling with a infant when I made the booking and the baby was present when I checked in, there was no space to set up the cot.
The worst part was the noise from the freeway. Even the noise from the air conditioner could not drown it out.
In the end, I stayed for 10mins, left and found another hotel. When I checked out, I was informed I was not eligible for a refund because I had used the room for an hour (everything in the room was left untouched),
For me, the worst part was the lack of security travelling with a baby. It was also not acceptable that I would have to stack up furniture to make space in the room so my daughter had somewhere to sleep.
I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Wyndam Garden at the end of May this year as part of a holiday to New York and Florida. I was a lttle apprehensive about the accommodation but I shouldnt have. We had a great stay at this hotel. The room was a reasonable size and was well equipped, and it was spotless. We stayed with our daughter and the room was sufficient for the three of us. It was a good location to visit the city and you have all that you need by way of coffee shops and food outlets to meet your needs. The hotel staff were excellent and exptremely helpful nothing was a bother. I have and would recomment this hotel to others and i look forward to visiting again.

title: “Magnolia hotel was fabulous and would highly recommend!!!”
text: Magnolia hotel was outstanding- clean, convenient, and very modern! Love the free cocktails, cookies, and breakfast!!!

title: “I look forward to staying here again”
text: I stayed here for one night after buying a groupon. I must admit i didnt expect much but i was delighted with the hotel. The staff were so friendly and the recently-renovated rooms are modern and very comfortable. The public areas are a little dated but they clearly pay a lot of attention to cleanliness, which matters far more to me. The location is amazing, particularly for tourists. If you have a car, i recommend parking around the corner at Union Station, as it costs half as much as parking at the hotel.

title: “All we wanted and more”
text:
We stayed 3 nights and were really pleased with the hotel. We had 2 rooms, ours was on the inside of the bulding and our daughter's was on the outside. There were complimentary shower gels, soaps, shower caps, shampoos and moisturisers in the bathrooms and slippers and dressing gowns in ourt rooms. The air conditioning was rather noisy outside our window as all the air conditioning units were on the roofs there. The glass was frosted so we weren't looking at them and they weren't a problem otherwise. (We switched our air-con off overnight and it was much quieter.)
The staff were all very helpful and polite and everywhere was kept clean.
Breakfast was plentiful and we could eat as much as we wanted. It consisted of cookies, breads, fresh fruit, cereals, bagels, cream cheese, fruit juices and a variety of coffees and teas. During the day, fruit, coffee, tea and cakes were left out and replenished regularly. In the early evening, fruit, biscuits, cheeses, wine, coffee and teas were available and regularly topped up. 
A computer and printer were available with access to the Internet at all times. The location of the Hotel, just half a minute's walk from Times Square, was excellent.

title: “Hotel was awesome, weather not so much!”
text:
The Westin Georgetown is an exceptional hotel which is close to The Mall and other tourist locations. Personnel are exceptionally helpful and very friendly!
Would stay here again in a minute!

title: “Marvelous Chicago Vacation”
text: My stay at the Hotel Monaco was an absolute pleasure. The staff were always friendly, courteous and professional. The room was on the top floor and had a river view, which I highly recommend. Eventhough the hotel is located downtown there were no noticable city "noises". Bed comfort outstanding! I also appreciated the personal touch of "goldfish". Service to the room was impecable and I never encountered any problems. The location was perfect....very centralized in order to tour the city and it's attractions. The restuarant located adjacent to the hotel is fantastic. Enjoyed daily complimentary continental breakfast (waiter excellent). It's very difficult to say what I enjoyed most about Hotel Monaco as it provides everything you need to feel comfortable, safe and content during a vacation to a city I've never been to previously. If you like to watch tv, don't expect a lot of channels (maybe 25) But I wasn't there to watche tv so not an issue for me. I would highly recommend Hotel Monaco! Lastly, if you are flying to Chicago for a vacation and all of your activities will be within City limits and nearyby communities, get a metro pass for the train/bus. I purchased the 3 day one for $14,00 and it was well worth it. Very simple public transportation.

title: “Good value for money”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights in June, lovely clean room, 2 large double beds and 2 bathrooms, as there were 3 of us sharing this was very handy. Very central, Tic Toc diner attached to the hotel is great and very convenient, reception staff very helpful, free safe deposit box, loved our stay at this hotel.

title: “Try the Residence Inn”
text:
This place has been renovated recently - but it should have been demolished and reconstructed. We had a room (suite) on the street side facing west - NOISY and hot!!! The a/c didn't put out enough cool air. Luckily the engineer on site added a little more juice after we complained and things got a little better. The decor is 1960s - it should have been spiffier with the remodel. The room came with breakfast, but they charged us anyway at the "restaurant". There are units that don't abut the street, which appear to be better (quieter). You would have thought that the hotel staff would have put us there (since we had a large group of rooms), but it didn't happen.
I like the Residence Inn which is 3-4 blocks away. It's way better than this place.

title: “Good location in downtown Boston”
text:
Stayed before in some other CQ and is same style.
Typical business hotel, decent-sized rooms (but small bathroom), free wi-fi, confortable, clean, nothing exceptional. Very good location in central Boston.
Minus
- Very small reception, sometimes pretty busy (I noticed same super small reception/only one person in check counter in other CQ, PLEASE add more people and you create more jobs, ya know, don't save on staff, it is annoying waiting for a long time or having to do the electronic check-in, i go to an easyHotel for that). Anyway staff seemed friendly.
- Restaurant/breakfast is in Irish pub in same building. So if you are in the mood of continental breakfast (they just basically have English breakfast), go somewhere else (there are plenty of Starbucks and the alikes in the area).
- Bit overpriced (at least when I booked).

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Great hotel, centrally located, and very clean. I'd definately stay here again.

title: “Wonderful for families!”
text: When we are looking for a quick weekend getaway we stay here! The waterpark/pool area is great for the entire family! Our kids like Greatwolf Lodge but we don't really care for it. This is our compromise! Food at the restaurants is very good. Great for golf, however that really isn't our thing. Close enough to the Riverwalk or Six Flags, Sea World or even Schlitterbahn if you are looking for day trips. I would highly recommend!

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: Stayed in this hotel one night not knowing what to expect. It was outstanding! Location was great. Little Italy, China Town, Soho, Brooklyn bridge all in walking distance. Valet had took care of my care and had it there right on time. Breakfast was excellent. Service great. Room small but clean. Recommendation from valet for dinner was perfect. I plan on coming back on a leisure trip.

title: “One night stay”
text:
This was a very nice hotel with a few issues. There were issues with the hot water not getting to my room, so they had to move me. They were very nice about it and gave me a gift basket for the inconvenience. The room is a studio suite and the layout is very nice and open. The bathroom had been remodeled, so now it is a large walk in shower instead of a bathtub with a shower. There was a coffee maker and a refrigerator, but no microwave. There is a nice desk area, but the plugs for the computer did not work.
The hotel is a not easy to get into or out of and there was some construction. The lobby and the breakfast were both nice and the help was very nice. Now that I know how to get there, I would stay again.

title: “Reasonably good”
text:
Stayed for three nights in Dallas. The service at Best Western
Market Center was nice and very helpful. 
The location could be better. 
The room was OK and clean, but our "view" was a corridor wall 
of the hotel. By the looks of it, we had the worst view. Bad luck?
There was a safe in the room, but it didn't work and we were
told that a repairman was coming in three days. 
There was a ice-making machine on the grounds, but it did not work. 
They advertised for a complimentary wireless Internet conection, 
but it did not work. But they had a room with a computer and
additional LAN-plugs comlimentary for guests. That we thought
was really nice. 
The pool and jacuzzi were also very nice.
So despite of the things that did not work and the "view"
we found the hotel quite O.K. and the price was very reasonable.

title: “what a lovely hotel”
text: we have just got back from the comfort inn central park west on 71st street we stayed from monday the 29th until friday the 3rd. what a lovely hotel the staff are very helpful at reception was brilliant. Dale the receptionist was very helpful if you needed anything and thomas in the evening was just as helpful and the complementary breakfast there was more than enough coffee, doughnuts. muffins,waffles,and cereal overall it was a nice stay the hotel staff were very good. rooms are very clean and tidy not the biggest but big enough. the location is good about a 15 min walk to time square and its a quieter road so hardly no noise in the evening and there are enough restaurants in 72nd street to accommodate everyones taste on the whole its well worth the cost

title: “I love old hotels, but.....”
text: Where do I start? My husband was in Los Angeles on business and my daughter and I decided to tag along and make it a vacation. The company that he works for, has offices located just two blocks away and has an agreement with this hotel. Therefore, we didn't choose it, nor did we have to pay for it. That being said, entering the hotel lobby is like going back in time. It is spectacular! The entire 1st floor is wonderful. The staff are exceptional and are really the very best part of this hotel. From the car attendant, bartender, check-in staff to the people working room service. All these people were wonderful! The room that we had on the 8th floor, was not! I've heard that they have done renovations on the Club Level floors, but they need to renovate the entire place. Our room was roomy, but there was tape on the walls, holding things in place. The carpet was ratted and frayed. The bathroom was tiny and had holes in the walls, marks on the door and the door would not shut. I had to go to another floor to get to the ice machine, which I didn't mind, but I was the only person in the halls and it reminded me of the hotel in the movie The Shining. It just gave me a creepy feeling. My husband asked the other people there for the conference what they thought of the hotel and they all said the same thing. The lobby area is beautiful, but the rest is creepy and needs to be renovated. I've stayed at many old hotels in large cities and I loved the character and charm they possess. Letting a hotel get rundown, is not adding to it's charm. I liked the area that the hotel was in and we caught the Hop On, Hop Off bus just across the street from the hotel on Grand Avenue in order to tour Hollywood, Santa Monica, L.A., etc... We won't be staying at this hotel again, until I read a review that says that the rooms have been renovated.

title: “Fantastic location but very small rooms”
text:
My husband and I stayed here while in San Francisco for a conference. The location was fantastic: 2 blocks to the Moscone Center (conference), 2 blocks to Union Square, and walking distance to the Pier. Directly down the street from the BART station, so you wouldn't have to take the taxi to/from the airport.
The rooms were adequate, but extremely small. We had a double room with a private bath. Although cozy, the size of the room really should only be for one person. 
If you want comfort, this is not your hotel as the rooms are extremely small. But if you want value and convenience, the Mosser is not a bad choice.

title: “all style, no space ( or light)”
text:
Firstly, let me say that there are a lot of good things about this hotel.........the staff are actually very decent,the sky terrace (open until 10) is very impressive,the breakfast is pretty sumptious,the rooms are well thought out for such a tiny space,the ac works a treat,there are vending and ice machines on each floor to save paying minibar( forgive me,mini basket)prices.
However,the combination of a lack of room space ( just me in a "double" room),the extremely low lighting thoughout the hotel,and the general uptightness of a hotel trying to be ubercool made this one of the more claustrophobic travelling experiences ..
.The sad pretentiousness of not putting a name sign in front of the hotel,the trip on the escalator that leads up to the dimly lit lobby ,the rooms that made me think Houdini had it easy; all little things that started to grate until I actually dreaded going back.Only for it was a business trip with others,I would have bolted for a a hotel that would have offered a more relaxed environment.
Next time,I will pay more heed to the "rooms warning".When the other reviewers say the rooms are tiny,they are not being overly fussy or narky; it is simply the truth.

title: “Californian finds a Great hotel”
text: My favorite place to stay in DC...the rooms are so clever and comfortable with all the necessary comforts for a business traveler...the staff is exceptionally nice, and they absolutely "get" customer service.

title: “Not for Europeans!”
text: As a recent "European" visitor who has also stayed at other Manhattan Hotels, the Hudson is very poor value for money. As stated in other reviews, this hotel is so dark & noisy. The rooms are very small particulary if sharing with access to the toilet and shower virtually impossible for the "larger" framed folk.

title: “Great venue amazing staff”
text:
I found the convention staff to be very professional and responsive. It was important to me that in the planning and execution of our conference that every thing would go smoothly and that my colleagues would get the maximum benefit of our time together. Patti and Nicki made sure that every planned for detail was handled in a timely way and the unexpected was handled with grace and a genuine smile.
The grounds provide a very tranquil beautiful setting and the meeting space and break out rooms assigned to our event were perfect for our needs.

title: “Wonderful place, Wonderful staff”
text: I could not have asked for more from a hotel. The room was lovely. The view great. The location suberb. The staff may have been the best thing of all. Wonderful, helpful, friendly. I'd stay here again in a minute.

title: “Great Location for Camden Yards & Inner Harbor”
text:
My husband & I stayed at this hotel last week to see two Red Sox games. Yes, it is an old hotel, but if you're prepared & go in knowing that....you'll be fine. The staff at the front desk are wonderful. Very friendly & informative. The elevator doors are *slow* to open/close & certain ones shake more than others. Our room was on the 7th floor, down a side hallway across from the service elevators ~ which I wasn't keen on, but honestly ~ the noise wasn't a problem. The room was clean but basic, nothing to write home about (*old* tv w/ ok reception/no counter space in the bathroom, etc) & I didn't care for the sleep number bed, but now I know for next time.
We did order room service the 1st night (club sandwich) & we were told they were out of ham, so it would just be a turkey club....no big deal. The food was delivered quick & hot. We tried to order it again the 2nd night, but we waited for over an hour & called to cancel the order since it was almost midnight ~ again, not the end of the world.
The location of this hotel is the best thing it has going for it. A quick walk from the light rail drop from BWI, not to mention both Camden Yards & the Inner Harbor.

title: “beauty of newyork”
text: i have stayed in this hotel ,, enjoyed alot,, the great thing in this hotel was it has a restaurant in the top floor touching the sky with delicious food and good ambience. the rooms were very neat and clean with a good service.

title: “Fantastic Family Holiday”
text:
My husband, two children and I just spent our annual Christmas weekend in Chicago. We chose to stay at the Waldorf Astoria this year and we all enjoyed the stay very much. The kids were especially tickled by the tv in the mirror and the fireplace (I even brought garland to make it more festive : )
 We all agree that the staff was very friendly and that they made us feel so welcome. We had a large suite and each night the very friendly housekeepers came up to make the sofa bed with comfy linens and pillows. They also left adorable mini robes and slippers for the kids! Another nice touch was when the doormen handed us nice large umbrellas as we walked out into the rain on Saturday.
The only frustration we experienced was with the restaurant the concierge recommended. We asked for something nearby with interesting atmosphere and good food. The place he enthusiastically endorsed was a good distance away. We had to cab it, and with so many great restaurants right here, it seemed like a waste of time. The restaurant had quite typical atmosphere and unremarkable food. He definitely could have steered us to a number of much better restaurants. We ate at LeColonial the next night...just steps away with very rich atmosphere, extensive menu and wonderful French Vietnamese food. Try the egg rolls wrapped in crispy lettuce!
Other than that our stay was quite enjoyable! We will return and make our own restaurant selection next time ; )

title: “Rooms are SMALL; Consider other options.”
text:
Man oh man, luckily I could reach the top of the closet...had to store everything up there. The room was very clean; the bathroom was adequate. the TV was nice. It was just too small. I know this sounds like an exaggeration, but if both of us were in the room, one of us needed to be in the bed (unless the other person was in the bathroom). I also picked this location because of it's proximity to Greenwich Village. It is true that Greenwich Village is about six or seven blocks away. However, the hotel is also on the "final glidepath" to the Holland tunnel. What this means is if the traffic is backed up in the Holland tunnel, it can take you 45 minutes to travel the last three blocks to your hotel. It also presents a problem when trying to check out. Overall, I would rate this as a fairly serious problem (I parked four blocks away. The morning we left it took me almost an hour to go around the block because of the Holland tunnel traffic).
Also, getting ice is a total drag. You have to use your key to make the elevator move. You also have to switch elevators in the lobby and take a separate one to the basement. As if that were not bad enough, the ice bucket they give you is probably 20 ounce capacity. Honestly, it is so small, that you almost laugh when you pick it up. Really, I have never seen anything like it. It is just a joke. And the glasses were also very small. Now that I think about it, it is almost like they were afraid to pick normal size tools or implements for fear of making the room look as tiny as it was. 
The one thing that I really liked about this room is that you could open the window. You know how it is: you're in a small room high up in the sky with an obstructed view. It's nice to be able to open the window a few inches and get some fresh air and hear some city noises. Somehow it makes it seem less claustrophobic. also, to be fair, the bed was comfortable. Internet was free. However, these positives were probably not enough to make me want to stay here again. Let's put it this way: I would examine a lot of other options before I selected this hotel (oh and did I mention that parking is $65 per day?)
Something that happened really wasn't the fault of the staff. However, they clearly did not fret very much about it. For some reason, probably alcohol induced, several women in a neighboring room chose to go out in the hallway at 2 AM and have a "cat fight." I am sure this woke everybody on the floor up. The problem is the hotel staff took 10 or 15 minutes to get up to the floor. By that time the fight had fizzled out and the girls had returned to the room. No apology was offered by the management. When we made an inquiry the next morning we got this response "what… Oh yeah, I heard something about that... sorry."
While this was not a hotel horror story, I was semi-desperate when I booked this room. I probably would have to be semi-desperate to stay here again.

title: “best value under the summer sun”
text:
the pointe hilton hotels offer most probably the best summer deals of all resorts in the phoenix area. check their websites if you plan to visit during those undescribeble hot summer month. adjacent lookout mountain golf course is beautiful, yet challenging. must try. the resort appears like a small spanish/mexican village with narrow streets and their suites built up the hill (phoenix mountain preserve). the suites are freshly renovated and large with a bedroom, a sitting area, balcony and 2tv's. furthermore you'll find a fully stocked minibar and a small wet bar with coffee, tea etc.
it offers various little hidden pools spread out the resort and 2 mainpools with (snack-)bar and slide in the centre. we tried the mexican and pointe in thyme restaurants, both offer good affordable food. room service is also ok and not too expensive. 
2 supermarkets are just down the road (5min drive) for all extras. overall a fine resort especially when travelling with kids due to the given extras. we'll be back.
p.s. welcoming and competent check in staff

title: “Beware the discount rooms!”
text: We booked this hotel for one night through Hotels (which was the booking agent for Entertainment). When we arrived at 4:00 pm, we were told the room was not yet cleaned, even though the Hotels print-out claimed Check-in was at 3:00 pm. The clerk insisted that they had a 4:00 pm check-in, but we were still asked to wait a half hour! When I insisted that we wanted to check-in NOW, they finally located a cleaned room on the first floor. We got into the room and discovered that, for $169.50, we had a room overlooking the parking lot! I returned to the desk to request a room with a marina view. One of those rooms, just across the hall from ours, was clean and empty. No, she insisted, that room was for a patron who'd paid FULL price (just $9.00 more than what we paid). I offered to give her the $9 so that we could have the room, but she insisted that it was already booked. This was a MONDAY night, so it's doubtful the rooms were all booked. To get a good view, we were told that all that was available was a suite, for an additional $100 per night. WE were treated like 2nd class citizens, and the clerks at the desk were arrogant and unpleasant. Needless to say, we were disappointed, angry, and unhappy with the accomodations. A warning to all who think they're getting a "good deal" on Hotels. You get what you pay for. In this case, I believe we overpaid for what we got. Never again for this hotel OR for Hotels.

title: “Clean! Great for business travel!”
text: I just spent 2 nights at this hotel this week, and I couldn't find anything wrong with it. My room was perfectly clean and the staff was great.

title: “Great Service & Well-Maintained”
text: I recently stayed at the CPD while working at a multi-day non-profit fundraiser. The room was very clean and constantly maintained. Any and all requests of the staff were quickly fulfilled and always with a smile. It was such a nice experience and a relief knowing that my lodging needs were being met and I could return after a long-day to a clean room with a comfortable bed. I look forward to returning.

title: “Overall Good guest service, especially from Amanda behind the front desk.”
text: My friend & I arrived early in the morning after a red eye & were not technically supposed to check in until 3pm. The hotel checked us in & suggested we go to breakfast since they didn't think they would have a room available for some time. After we came back, we technically still had several more hours until we were guaranteed a room but one of the front desk concierge, Amanda told us she knew where we were waiting in the lobby & would flag us down when the first room was available. Needless to say, we only waited about 30 minutes & were able to check in well before we were supposed too. This was great customer device, especially after flying all night & wanting to grab a few hours of sleep. If I had to add one price of constructive criticism, I will admit we weren't too happy to pay for our bags to be held prior to have our room available as we were already staying at the hotel, and these services should be complimentary to guests.

title: “My favorite hotel in SF”
text: This is my second time here - love it. The location on the water is awesome, close to subway access and cabs and restaurants. The Ferry Building food market is across the street. Love that when I come down in the morning there's good coffee, in the afternoon lemonade & iced tea, in the evening wine, and at night fresh baked cookies. Rooms are awesome - clean & stylish, super comfy beds. Best of all it's my favorite thing - a very cool upscale hotel without any pretense. Only thing - don't use the YMCA that's attached, it's kinda um... not good.

title: “Underwhelming hotel”
text:
I stayed here two nights for business. The rate was reasonable for Manhattan meaning tiny room and not much in amenities. As small as the room was, the bed was comfortable. there was no cooler in the room or coffee maker. The cookie I got at my late check in was all dried out and there were no apparent amenities for my Hilton Honors gold status. 
The room as very warm because inspite of it being Novemember, the temperatures outside were balmy and humid in the 60s. The ac and room fan were not working for the season however thank goodness the windows could open which aired it out at the expense of outside noise.
Last, for some reason this hotel charges to store luggage with the bell desk, 2 bucks for this privilege. Welcome to NY city.

title: “Good moderate price stay for business travel”
text: This hotel is fairly new and offers comfortable beds and great front desk service. Good spot for business travel. You get a good size room with a fridge and microwave. It's close to shopping and restaurants - so makes it easy for an extended stay.

title: “Great little hotel near Wall Street”
text: This HI Express is new; the rooms are small but have all the amenities including frig, microwave, wi-fi, great bathroom fixtures. It's 2 blocks from the South Seaport (food court), close to the Brooklyn Bridge and the departing point to the Statue of Liberty.

title: “Great Location”
text: Great Location on 7th avenue makes it convenient to Carnegie Hall, Central Park, Broadway theater district and 5th avenue shopping. Subways are right outside the door Rooms are a bit run down and in need of a facelift. Do not leave food out in your room, I had a mouse visit. Good security after dark. Reasonably priced for NYC.

title: “Loved it”
text: I've been meaning to write this review forever...ok for a year since my fiance and I stayed here. I loved this hotel. Our room was exceptionally clean, extremely spacious, and we had a wonderful experience overall. There were always fresh, chilled (and free) bottles of water in our room whether we came back mid-day or in the evening. I loved the turn down service. The concierge was great (I wish I remember his name!) and extremely knowledgable. He was probably close to my age, so he catered all of his recommendations to me and knew exactly where to send me for fish tacos. I think the location was great as well. We did end up renting a car for a few days during our stay to explore the areas outside of San Diego.

title: “A surprise in NW”
text:
Our usual haunts in Bethesda and Friendship Heights were charging a seriously ridiculous amount of money for the weekend rates. I decided to try hotels.com for the first time and found a satisfactory rate for the Savoy Suites Hotel in NW DC near the National Cathedral for a 2-night stay.
Pros: 
The staff!! I don't know if they hire individuals who understand customer service or train the staff to be particularly responsive, but every single person was warm, welcoming and attempted to find answers to or solve every small question/problem over the weekend. 
Rooms: large, clean, new bathrooms, free WiFi (what a pleasure!). They upgraded us to a room with a kitchenette. Nice to have the microwave. I think all rooms have a mini-fridge. The bathrooms are on the small side and the shower (no tub) has a glass wall and no curtain. A little unusual, but it worked. Copious amounts of hot water no matter what time of day. The bed is terrific - beats the sleep numbers bed in other properties with ease, multiple pillows, great a/c system that doesn't bark at you when the compressor kicks in. There is a safe in the room.
Free parking - how I love free parking! I have a pet peeve about the cost of parking in DC and we no longer stay in the downtown area since $34 - 50 per night is beyond my budget for the privilege of parking my vehicle. We were in and out of the underground garage multiple times a day all weekend and not having to wait for valet was a pleasure. 
We spontaneously ate at the restaurant this morning for breakfast. The hotel gave us a 20% off coupon for use in the hotel over the weekend. Breakfast consisted of the usual buffet fair but the omelets were truly cooked to order and this is the first hotel restaurant I have EVER eaten in that actually crisps their bacon. 
Whole Foods is down the block. We brought breakfast back to the hotel on Saturday morning.
Cons: We were helping a relative move, were out of the room at 8 AM on Saturday and it took until the end of the day for the room to be straightened. We had already come back to the hotel mid-afternoon, showered again and were on our way out for the evening before the room was cleaned. We were on the second floor facing a seriously unattractive garage area with some parked vehicles. Ask for a room on the third or fourth floor to avoid this. The plus side was that the rear facing room was quiet and there was little noise from Wisconsin Avenue, including some construction noise up the block on Friday evening. If we did not travel to DC as frequently as we do, I think I would have been disappointed by the view. It might be worthwhile for the hotel to consider upgrading this area with some paint/plants to ensure that every guest has something pleasant to look at from their windows. 
The location is in a truly beautiful, quiet residential neighborhood of NW DC. It was ideal for us, but a family touring the city will not be able to just 'pop' out of the hotel and be in the tourist areas near the mall. I'm not sure I would stay here if I had very young children who might tire by the end of a day of museum and event hopping. The hotel does offer free shuttle bus service and the DC bus system also works well. 
Bottom Line: Give it a try. We were pleasantly surprised by this lovely boutique hotel that met all our needs this weekend. Kudos to the Savoy!

title: “Great stay!”
text: Stayed for an anniversary June 9. Room was a very large suite, with a separate living area, bedroom and bathroom (shower big enough for 2!). We were upgraded to a high floor with an incredible view and enjoyed a fabulous dinner at Maze, the Gordon Ramsey restaurant on the premises. Great value for a NYC hotel. Loved the pampering ammenities...slippers, robes, etc.

title: “PLEASANT STAY AND VONVINIENT”
text: Stayed at this hotel during my short trip to San Antonio. I was a little turned off by the reviews on here but I did not feel like spending much money so I gave it a shot. It was definetly not a close to a 5 star hotel but for the charge I was pleased with my stay. I liked the convinent loccation and it was close to stores and shopping. Only 10-15 minutes to downrown and other attractions such as Sea world. I would recomend this hote for any one that is on a short trip and dont want to spend a furtune. The styaff was also very friendly.

title: “Lovely Hotel and Superb Service”
text:
I've stayed on the OMNI San Francisco several times on business, and each stay has been wonderful. After staying in excellent hotels just about everywhere, I can truly say that the Omni staff is one of the very best. Courteous and attentive without being fawning, and truly helpful. Lovely lobby and rooms are well appointed and immaculate. Even if you're going to stay here one night, it's a good idea to sign up for the Omni Rewards program, as it gives you complimentary Internet service and other perks, including coffee service, newspaper of your choice, etc. 
Also: on one of my trips, I brought along my two children. Was a little apprehensive about that, but they were treated beautifully. Complimentary milk and cookies, packets of kid stuff (also comp) and staff was very gracious with them. They also helped me find a reliable professional babysitter, who was also excellent. 
In sum, this is one of my favorite hotels and I highly recommend!

title: “My pain meds were stolen from this hotel”
text: While we enjoyed the hotel, the restaurant and the bar in this hotel, our stay which was for our 33rd wedding anniversary was certainly tainted by my pain meds being stolen out of our room while were out site seeing that day. My fault probably but I had undergone recent cervical surgery and when we decided to go walking around the city that day, decided holding the purse would aggravate my neck situation. Took out my cash and credit cards, never giving my pain meds a thought. The disturbing problem here is that I put my purse in my suit case under clothes, essentially thinking I was burying it (I was naive yes!) My purse, as my kids describe it is a black hole and not easily gone through, so the thief really had to dig threw it. I went to take a half of pill when we returned home after site seeing, eating lunch, etc. for at least 5 hours. I noticed that only 5 pills were left in the bottle and thought this must be my old bottle as I had just had it refilled and there were 50 pills (norco) in that rx. Being that we were away, I thought I'd dig through my purse later and perhaps grabbed the old bottle before we left. We got home Sunday night and I didn't leave the house for 2 days. I went to take another pill a couple of days later and then decided to look through my purse only to find both the old and the new bottle and probably 45 or so pills missing. I called my surgeon's nurse who sadly wasn't surprised at all. Her comment was hmm, they left some on the bottom of the pill bottle, right. Yes, I said. That way you don't notice it right away, apparently an old hotel trick. I called the hotel only to be told that only my husband and I had entered the room along with an 8 year veteran housekeeper. Those drugs went missing at that hotel which is sad because otherwise I would highly recommend it. The restaurant was great, beds very comfy, check in/check out process great. I sure learned a lesson the hard way here though. Moral of the story, beware anywhere you stay.

title: “Another nice stay at this Doubletree”
text: Redbirds baseball was going on. Lots of music playing on Beale Street. Memphis in May was about to start. Went to a concert at Minglewood and the staff was very accommodating with cabs and valet parking. Check in was delightful. Staff was really nice. Now doing a cocktail hour in the lobby. Pool area was closed, which was unexpected.

title: “Above and beyound in service hotel.”
text: I have stayed at 100's of Hotels and I would put this Hotel stay at the top of my list. I just wished it was not for business and my husband was with me. He would of loved it! From reservations, bell hop, front desk, bar, restraunt, room service & housekeeping... The staff showed pride in their work and experience. The service was exceptional!
