The view from my room every morning was beautiful as I enjoyed my cup of coffee before class. The bed was cozy too. I usally order extra pillows but did not need too because the bed was so nice. Slept thourgh the night. They went above and beyond with service & caring. I would highly recommend this hotel and to enjoy using all of the properties amenities.

title: “Wish I Could LIVE here !”
text: I stumbled onto the Conrad Chicago when searching for a new place to stay in Chicago during my annual trip to attend the Chicago Midwinter Dental meeting, and am I GLAD I did ! The Conrad is an establishment everyone should have the opportunity to experience! Everybody from the doorman , to the front desk ladies to the house keeping staff were as professional and accommodating as one could ask! All this culminating with a cheerful positive response to our late check out request ! Plus it's attached via internal walkways to Nordstroms and a very nice , brand new looking mall and food court! The wireless internet is FREE , the mattresses are incredible , and the work out area is nicely outfitted. What's not to like !? Highly recommended !

title: “Renewed soul and great down time”
text: The staff were very friendly and helpful. Jeff, the shuttle driver, was a great conversationalist and really added to the good vibe of our trip. Amber and various other front desk staff were very genuine and easy to talk to. The Handlery offers an old school feel and a very clean environment. We will definitely be back.

title: “Awful!”
text:
This hotel was so awful that we actually canceled our second night and checked out the same night we checked in. We had family staying at the Hilton so we chose to sleep on a cot in their room instead! The lobby is deceivingly nice....but once you get up the stairs, you feel like you are checking into a college dorm. The room was smaller than a NY studio apartment and not clean. The bathroom tile that was supposed to be white, was not. The toilet was equivalent to a gas station rest stop facility and made an awfully loud noise each time it was flushed. I guess stepping over the homeless people as we went to check in should have given us our first clue. It's worth it to pay more when staying in San Francisco.
john, nj

title: “Great service, ideal location, will return”
text: We had several criteria for choosing a hotel for our recent family holiday. Even though a small fee was charged for parking, it was nominal, considering that we didn't have to drive a distance and pay for parking. Location is an easy walk a few blocks away from Seattle Centre/Space Needle in one direction and Pike Place Market in the other plus the free bus system is only a couple of blocks down. Service is the tops, especially by Maria who deserves a medal for juggling so many tasks and still being helpful to everyone asking for assistance. We arrived a little earlier than check in time, but were able to get into our room even though the hotel was crazy busy. Rooms are on the small side, but super clean with a bar size fridge that kept our water and drinks cold, and wifi access. Air conditioning was a little noisy, but worked well. Continental breakfast had lots to choose from both hot and cold. The neighborhood was a little sketchy, but felt safe. A couple of blocks up you will find a Walgreens for snacks and any other trip necessities. Everything about the Loyal Inn, including the reasonable price makes this is an ideal place to stay in Seattle. We'll be back again.

title: “Excellent Value, location”
text:
This center city hotel is within easy walking distance of many attractions,several small, interesting restaurants, bars, clubs, boutique shopping (check out the cheese selection in Di Bruno's food emporium!), and Rittenhouse Square. Discounted rates are available through various internet reservation services but were matched upon request to the hotel chain's reservations center. I had asked for early check in when I reserved and had quick service when I checked in at about 12:30 p.m. The front desk staff was friendly, very knowledgeable about the area, gave good recommendations, provided specific and correct directions to where I wanted to go, and printed off additional info about a place I asked about. On this summer afternoon, the lobby had complimentary iced tea and lemonade available (can be combined to make Arnold Palmer's favorite drink!), and at 5 p.m., the staff served complimentary wine in the lobby that was very, very good. The single king room was a bit tight, but clean, very upscale, modern, and trendy. This wasn't all show and no substance though, as the furnishings were very well thought out and practical. The bathroom had a pocket door, the sink was offset on the vanity, allowing ample space for my toiletries, there was a close up mirror , plenty of excellent towels (but no wash cloths). The king bed was very comfortable and there was a large flat screen TV (but no Comedy Channel) and one of the easiest to use alarm clocks I have ever encountered in a hotel. There is only valet parking ($37) but after walking around the neighborhood, I found that there was a garage next to the Barnes and Noble on Rittenhouse Square, and one garage in the 1300 block of
 Walnut St. where you could self park for substantially less. Please note that the valet car pickup is around the corner from the hotel and not in front where you drop off your car--I waited for an extra half hour out front before anyone put the 2's and 2's together as to why I was standing there with my luggage at 6:15 a.m.! There are no guest vending machines for ice but ice was promptly delivered after a call to customer services. Although I did get exceptional service in face-to-face conversations with front desk people, be aware that this location and the chain's service center are staffed mostly by twenty somethings and therefore their service in response to phone and e-mail requests is often oriented to that age group. If you do not have an internet-connected cell phone that you check constantly, if you expect a specific response instead of just receiving internet links, and/or if you want a specific question answered instead of being told to check online/onscreen menus, you may be disappointed.

title: “Convenient location, big rooms - good hotel.”
text:
I booked a room with a treadmill, not realizing that Dupont Circle is not so far from downtown DC, and if you like walking you can get all the exercise you need during the day sightseeing. My room was nice and big. The bathroom is small but fine. The room was well cleaned, although I agree that some of the overall decor is looking a bit tired in some areas. The front desk staff were always friendly.
Dupont Circle is a good place to stay. It is on the Metro Red Line, and close enough to downtown and Georgetown to walk. There's lots of food, ATMs, and pharmacies nearby. The park in the middle of the circle is filled with people hanging out after work on summer nights. I felt safe all the time.
I'd stay here again.

title: “Not worth to be called a Waldorf Astoria - Rooms are Motel 6 level”
text:
I attended a conference and booked a room as a Hilton Honors Diamond member. Usually, you receive room upgrades to the executive level with free breakfast and any other Hilton I stayed in tries to accommodate the wishes of their members with regard to room location within the property. Not so the Biltmore: I was given a standard room (they said it was an upgrade but in that case the basic rooms must be a hole in the wall) that, despite my request, was located at a street so that I had to close the window at night not to be disturbed by traffic noise. 
No free breakfast either. All you get is a two-drink coupon limited to $14/drink. Overall a miserable check-in experience especially in light of room availability and available upgrades to other HH with entry level memberships. 
The bed was substandard with a worn out mattress. The balcony was dirty but could not be used anyway due to the cold location (no sun at all). There was not even a coffee maker in the room. See other comments on the rooms in the terrace wing ("Needs work").
The spa was another negative highlight: the exercise equipment can be called prehistoric and the sauna is not hot when one arrives (during standard traffic/business hours).
The grounds are kept neatly but the entire building needs a bit more TLC to be called "in excellent shape".
The bar and the restaurant served excellent drinks and food with good service although, despite housing several conferences, the main restaurant was closed for lunch, which led to up to 30-min waiting time: totally unacceptable.
Another point worth to mention was the business center: extortion! $7.50 for 15 minutes computer use, and on top of that $1 per printed page. Fortunately, the clerk at the business center printed my pages from my USB drive, and I did not have to use their computer.

title: “BMT Graduation”
text: When we arrived we were a little early however the staff was very accommodating and let us check in early. They also handed us a map of the base and a schedule and showed us exactly where to go that next morning. The rooms we very clean and the room service was great. Also in the mornings they had breakfasts set up and it was really good and fast which was great for the early mornings. Wonderful for the price!

title: “Good service and nice, clean rooms”
text: I'm from Scandinavia and stayed one night in May at the hotel and liked it very much. The service was very friendly (girl at the desk) and polite. The room was so much better than I expected for the price I paid. Spacious room was very clean and the wlan for my computer worked fine. Television good too. Absolutely good value for the money!

title: “Excellent value if cigarette smoke doesn't bother you”
text:
We stayed 3 nights. The staff are very friendly. The location is very central. The hotel is very clean. Although the decor is dated, that is easily overlooked given the price per night and the positive aspects noted above. Our room was on the 7th floor at the back and was quite quiet.
My only complaint is that there are no non-smoking rooms/floors. This was not a problem on the first 2 nights, but on the third a smoker in presumably the next room, caused our room to smell of smoke.
If it wasn't for the smoke, I would certainly stay here again without hesitation. Even with it, I'd probably take my chances because you can't find such clean hotel at such an affordable place in NYC, but really wish they would allocate a few floors as non-smoking.

title: “A pleasant stay in a boutique hotel with a great location in the Loop”
text:
I stayed two nights in May 2012 and was overall quite pleased. Would not hesitate to return and would recommend it, provided you don't need a full service hotel with a grand lobby. This hotel has a great location, helpful staff, modern and clean rooms and public areas, and a compelling price (booked through Travelocity's 'mystery hotel' arrangement).
There are actually two hotels sharing the same building and entrance, the Central Loop Hotel and the Chicago Guest Quarters. They have a common lobby and some of the same facilities, but the rooms are on different floors.
The name of the hotel aptly describes its location: It is about as well located in the Loop as one could imagine. If you are coming in from O'Hare, take the CTA Blue Line to Monroe or Jackson and walk to the hotel in five minutes. If it is rush hour, you will get there quicker than a taxi. In any event, you will save yourself a bundle on the cab fare.
The reception staff were friendly and efficient. There are kiosks for self-checkin, but the staff handled it for me.
My room was on the sixth floor. Each room shares a small side corridor with another room, which is off the main corridor. So, your room door is very close to the other room door, and a noisy neighbor coming and going could be bothersome, but that wasn't the case for me.
The room was smaller than most hotels, but well laid out and equipped. Furniture and furnishings looked almost new. Large stall shower in the bathroom, but no tub. Bathroom lighting was terrific. Room had a built-in desk, minifridge, microwave and coffee maker. Fast and free Wifi. Very comfortable bed with lots of pillows. Housekeeping did a great job before and during stay. Room was spotless. The room is well lit, which is important as it doesn't get a lot of natural light from its one window.
I did not utilize the restaurant. There are plenty of restaurants of all types and price points in the neighborhood. There is a 7/11 across the street with a good variety of hot and cold breakfast foods.
The exercise facility has four treadmills, two elliptical trainers, one all purpose weight machine, free weights, and a stretching area. The room and equipment were very clean and well maintained.
There is an unmanned business center with PCs and printers. No charge to use.
Overall, I think the Central Loop Hotel presents a very good value proposition: A good, clean, modern hotel, with free wifi, exercise room and business center, but with smaller rooms, no gift shop, no grand lobby, no room service, no minibar, etc. If you don't need the frills you can save yourself a lot of money.

title: “The Best Hotel I've ever stayed at!”
text: Stayed at the Willard while on a business trip with my mom and we loved it. Our room had a view of the Washington Monument and the Lincoln Memorial. It's close to the White House (just a block away). The beds are beyond comfortable and the staff are first class professionals. We spent a couple evenings at the Round Table bar near the lobby and received excellent service. We enjoyed everything about this hotel.

title: “Not as good as many reviews suggest”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights in August during the NYIGF @ Javitz. Had problems the moment we checked in. Made a reservation many months prior for a 'city view' and paid extra for that privilege. However, hotel management has a different definition on the meaning of a view. They gave us a room that faced a inner area, towards a brick wall. When we brought this to their attention, instead of apologizing, they were visably annoyed that we were persistant in requesting them change our room. Finally, they gave us a room that was slightly above the roof of nearby building but I would hardly call this a 'VIEW'. We were not nasty to them so I think it is extremely poor customer service for hotel management to have attitude towards guests who expect what they paid for. We were willing to stay in an inferior room but they should somehow adjust the price accordingly. In the end, the room we got was spacious enough but starting to look a little worn out which is suprising since it is a relatively a new hotel. The bathroom was very small and hardly any room on the vanity for toiletries. So women beware if you come with a suitcase of makeup! LOL. Sink in bathroom leaked, towels were thin, worn out, had holes and/or slight tears. Will find and post the pics to prove this. Beds were horrible unless you love beds in which you sink in and need to climb out of the hole. To me, a bed should be firm but comfortable. Highlight staying here was entering the hotel lobby every time with the idiotic hotel manager, smiling like a clown and saying robotically "Welcome back!" even if you stepped out two minutes earlier to buy something. Very amusing since it was the manager that gave us attitude in the first place. 
After the whole check-in experience, we did not complain further. We tried to make the best of it since it was prepaid. However, we will not stay here again.

title: “Travelzoo Deal”
text: Cannot complain at the price offered through Travel Zoo. We arrived to discover an enormous generator running full throttle outside. Unfortunately the hotel had received a power cut a few days prior which had yet to be fixed. Our room was on the top floor above the generator, so not much sleep for us, after walking all over Boston that day. An older hotel with charm and friendly staff, and an overpowering smell of cleaning fragrance in the entry foyer. Our bed was very firm to sleep on along with the pillows. No give or take there. We overslept, so ate breakfast around the corner at Dunkin' Donuts.

title: “A Great Stay”
text:
Three generations of us spent a long July 4th weekend here and couldn't have been happier. We booked through Expedia, so when we checked in we asked for two rooms near each other. After some browsing through the computer system, the front-desk person not only found rooms across the hall from each other . . . .they were ready for us to check in, even though it wasn't even noon yet.
The service was excellent and the staff was extremely polite. Our only complaint was the bathrooms were small. On the other hand, the linens were thick and plentiful, unlike many one sees today.
We liked the location and because my mother no longer has the tolerance for public transportation, we either walked or took cabs, and there were always cabs at the entrance.
Last but not least, we got a rate at half the usual rate, which made it that much nicer.

title: “Soo Noisy and terrible service”
text:
The hotel is beautiful... but if you stay in any of the suites beware of the noise! Bar accross the street was extremely noisy...We also found the resturant service to be subpar. Pretty disappointed stay overall considering the prices were much higher than normal for OU/Texas weekend. 
Bell boys were great with directions and front desk did reccomend a great restaurant but overall won't stay here again..

title: “6 Wonderful night”
text: I was in San Francisco as every year for the Fancy food Show I usually stay at the Powell hotel in the same part of town but last year I fund a visitor in my room a big black cockroach and was just very discusted I decide to upgrade to the Wyndham and was I very satisfied a beautiful room with a great view, great service, I really enjoy my stay and will be back again

title: “Beautiful Views, Friendly Staff, Excellent Value”
text:
I selected this hotel as part of a surprise birthday trip for my husband's 40th birthday. I was pleased with the cleaniless of our room, as well as the excellent complimentary breakfast we had each morning. This hotel is an amazing value! We had a view of the bay,as well as the Golden Gate Bridge. It was relatively close to Fisherman's Wharf , but quite a walk to the Presidio. We did have a maintenance issue as our bathtub would not drain properly, but it was quickly resolved. The only "minus" for us was that the wi-fi signal was weak, not allowing us to use FaceTime to video chat with our kids back home.
Check- in and out was extremely easy and efficient. Every morning we were greeted by a friendly staff member. This was impressive!
Overall, it was a great stay in the city of San Francisco and I would recommend this hotel. You can't beat the location, views, and free breakfast!

title: “Unique experience in great location”
text: Cool compact rooms. I was so glad I had my own bathroom in my room. It's like a fancy pants hostel---and I mean that with much respect. We had a great stay.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: Having stayed in a couple of grotty DC hotels, the Hampton Inn came as a very pleasant surprise. It is only a short walk from the metro, and 10 mins from the Mall. Our room was clean, quiet, spacious and comfortable. The bathroom was spotless, with the shower having good pressure. The air conditioing was quiet and efficient. We enjoyed the complimentary breakfasts - where we had the choice of cooked meals or cereals/toast/fruit. The front desk service was efficient, and they looked after us when we asked for a slightly later check out time. All in all, a lovely hotel that we will certainly stay at again, and recommend to anyone.

title: “Don't stay if you want to sleep”
text:
The DJ at the nightclub goes until 2:30 a.m. He is loud with a resounding bass and you will not miss a note in your room. It's hard to sleep anyway as the room is very hot due to central heating so you must alternate between the room to cold with the window open and too hot with it closed. Calls to the front desk elicit mumbled apologies and no action. 
On the upside the toiletries are nice.

title: “Great Location Down Town - Would stay again”
text: I stayed here for business, it is located just off the I5 and is 10min walk from pike place market. They have soo much shopping all around. If you go to seattle make sure you do the market stroll and go to the original starbucks down there all very cool to see. The Westin is very nice, the rooms were a bit smaller then I expected but I guess when downtown they try to use as much space as possible. The rooms were clean and I would stay again strictly for location. We also were on the 20somtheing floor so very nice view. I am not sure how much it cost as it was a business trip so I can't judge whether I would pay what they charge to stay there again but overall a decent hotel.

title: “Great location”
text: We arrived late due to airline cancellation but when the hotel couldn't accept my honors card they gave me an upgrade! when i didn't have my party pass they gave me a comp! walking distance to the Magnificent Mile and the Water Tower, Hersey,Ghiradelli, all the shopping you could ask for and a perfect spot for the hopper bus! Rooftop pool overlooking the city had an absolutely incredible view!

title: “watch out something really wrong here”
text: went into room and someone had taken a dump in the bathroom desk clerk is stupid he didn't see anything wrong with it......also a man was hanging out in a parked car...waiting for his girl friend said the desk clerk....i think they use this hotel for something else and the guy in the car is watching for cops...2 girls that checked in prior to us looked the part....we lefft....

title: “Not a good choice for business travelers”
text: First stay at an Aloft and was not impressed at all. Rooms have a college dorm feel. The desk was very small. TV was not viewable from the desk, so forget working out of your room while watching CNBC. Food was terrible... tomato and mozzarella salad was below the quality of what you would get at an airport "grab and go" station. For an brand new hotel near the airport, I found it noisy. You can hear every car on the street and every plane taking off. I love the W hotels, but can't understand why Starwood would tarnish the W brand by associating it with the Aloft chain. I will never stay at an Aloft again.

title: “Best Fairfield I've seen”
text:
Used this room the night before an early flight and was pleasantly surprised with the property. As a Marriott Platinum member I spend 80-100 nights in hotels per year. This hotel is as nice as a Courtyard or Springhill Suites. Very clean, much more upscale than other Fairfields I've visited and a very welcoming and friendly staff.
I will stay here again if I am in the area.

title: “Select a different hotel until the Time is renovated”
text:
I decided to try the Time hotel when i stayed in NYC in October 2005 for business. The location is certainly optimal, and the hotel has potential, but I was very disappointed by the state of disrepair... We were given an incorrect room on our first night's stay. As a compromise, i was upgraded to a suite for the second evening. The sheets in the room were obviously dirty, and when i requested new sheets, they were brought up to me, but the staff did not offer to put them on the bed. I changed them myself.
the furnishings and carpets are threadbare, sometimes ripped and chipped and quite obviously cheap and old.
The service was friendly, but i would not go back. Your money could be better spent elsewhere.

title: “You have to love this old lady!”
text: There are alot of reviews here complaining about the size of the rooms etc. I have just returned from a business trip and spent 3 nights at the San Carlos. Look, if you want a large, sterile, uber modern hotel room you will have to book a large modern hotel and leave your personality at reception. There's plenty of those to choose from in Phoenix. If you want some history, with a little querkiness thrown in then San Carlos is great. It IS old, but isn't that the point? Americans flood to London for history. Bad news is, history is OLD. The rooms are not huge, but doesn't that refelect the architecture of the time? The bathroom was not modern. Hello! You will not find anything remotely modern here, except perhaps the service and free wi-fi. The third floor roof pool is wonderful, I had it to myself. The staff - I was welcomed by Keith - were all very friendly. There's a bar right next to the lobby which is dark and cool and again Misty the bar tender was great. A few yards away is a very friendly Irish bar with the best selection of whisky I have ever seen. Nice beers too. Everthing is a short walk away including the theater and conference center. A cab stand is one minute away. The San Carlos' floors creaked, the doors creaked, the elevator was rickety, the rooms were probably bigger before the 100th layer of paint was put on the walls! Business or pleasure, dare to be different, go on! Thanks San Carlos, don't change.

title: “Room was nice but customer service was questionable”
text:
I enjoyed the room, which was nice, and the breakfast, which was above average. What was rather disappointing was being left stranded at the stadium after the ball game. One of the lobby staff was very enthusiastic and helpful the night before recommending and giving us a ride to a local restaurant. When we mentioned that we were going to the ballgame the next night he promised to shuttle us there and pick us up.
When we were ready to leave for the game the gentleman was not around but another staff member offered to take us to the stadium. On the way there he informed us that they would not be able to pick us up afterwards. Because of this we had to take a $40 cab ride back to the hotel (Thanks for nothing!!)
It's funny that we saw a Mariott shuttle picking people up at the stadium. Perhaps we will try that hotel out the next time we are in town!

title: “Excellent location”
text:
My husband I stayed here for 8 nights at the beginning of October to celebrate my 40th birthday. We had a room on the 18th floor with view of the Chrysler building. The room was lovely, the bathroom well equipped with toiletries etc. Even provided a bottle of Champagne on ice because we'd told them it was my 40th birthday treat. Every night the turn down service included 2 bottles of water, which we used to take out with us during the day time. 
Hotel is situation just 5 minutes walk from Times Square and about 15 mins from Empire State Building. Hotel staff very courteous at all times. 
Yes, the Gaby restaurant is pricey, we had breakfast there on my birthday and it was 3 times what we'd been paying at the Red Flame (highly recommend their pancakes and french toast!) a few doors down on the same street - but special birthdays require special treatment. 
Recommend joining the Sofitel priviledge card scheme, but do so in advance because our card didn't arrive in time for the trip so we missed out on the free drink at the bar mentioned in other reviews, however, we did get late checkout (4pm) which was great for us as we had late night flight.
Would definitely stay there again and pay a little extra for a higher floor room having seen photos of other rooms.
Agree with other reviewers about Grayline sightseeing bus, Empire State Building and Rockefeller Centre (top of the rock) if only for the elevator experience!

title: “Great stay, great hotel!”
text: Our stay at the Staybridge Suites, Times Square, really couldn't have been much better. The staff were freindly and helpful. The rooms were new, and the beds were some of the most comfortable I've ever slept in! The free breakfast was great and there was also free laundry. The street that the hotel was on, was kind of small and dirty, but we still felt very safe there. We were just a very short walk to the "heart" of Times Square and I walked back and forth often by myself, even without my husband. We were very happy with our choice.

title: “Great Hotel!!!”
text: This was the best hotel experience that I have had in a long time. I was very pleased with the cozy feel of the hotel. As a woman traveling alone I felt safe and this is one of the reasons I prefer valet parking. The hotel and room were clean and comfortable. I used the community work area to check emails and to print out an article that had to do with my business in town. I used the pool and I appreciated the feeling of privacy the pool area offers. The breakfast was wonderful and someone would be hard pressed to say they don't offer something for everyone. Every member of the staff (housekeeping, valets, front desk, breakfast staff) that I encountered were friendly and seemed to genuinely care that my experience at this hotel was a positive one. I definitely plan on staying here again if I need a room in downtown Dallas.

title: “Excellent hotel!”
text:
Just stayed at the Marriott Financial this past weekend 2/25/05-2/27/05. Very nice hotel, clean, quiet, nice staff and felt very safe (saw security walking the floors). 
We were in a spacious corner room looking over the harbor and battery park.. The best features were the fabulous breakfast buffet with made to order waffles and omelets, swimming pool for the kids, very comfortable beds and friendly staff. 
It’s a little bit away from the hustle and bustle – which is good if you want to wind down. 
Drove in and it was easy to find and the car was very close by in a monitored lot. 
All in all a very nice comfortable hotel. Will definitely stay there again.

title: “It doesn't need to be any better”
text: The first thing that I liked was that no one grabbed my suitcase to "help" me bring it to my room. I was asked whether I needed assistance; when I answered in the negative, I was left alone. That's how it was on departure as well. The room was clean and comfortable, with high quality soaps and shampoo. They even gave us a larger room at no extra cost so that I could be close to the suite that I reserved for my father and his caregiver. The complimentary fruit and sweet rolls in the morning were first rate; too bad, no capuccino, but the coffee was good. There was also tea and hot chocolate. No wireless in the hotel, but two computers in the lobby were free for e-mail and Internet. The free wine (house label) served with the cheeses in the afternoon was mediocre, but the host or hostess made up for it by making the atmosphere warm and family-like. The neighborhood isn't fancy, but okay, and if you enjoy walking, the hotel is conveniently located for getting to Union Square, the Civic Center, or the cable car. We spent four nights at the Beresford Arms, with absolutely nothing to complain about. Spending more elsewhere would just have been a waste of money.

title: “Incredible Experience”
text:
I had a wonderful experience at W New York. I was skeptical about staying here because the reviews are kinda harsh, but I had to experience the W on my own. Before booking my room, I registered online and became a preferred guest. If you have AAA, it's an added bonus. The only good thing about becoming a preferred guest is the chance upon check-in that you may get upgraded. Well, we did! My husband and I booked the wonderful room and it was about 250sq ft. I loved everything about the room. The rooms down comforters and pillows were great. The chic, modern look was everything I expected. I loved the hints of red in the room, which made it romantic. The extra (which is not on the W website) is the shower. The bathroom is small, but the sink is huge and the shower (no bath) has a rainfall shower head. You can't beat that!!! 
The extra's make up for the smallness of the room. I got an incredible deal through the NYC visitor's center which has a Paint the Town discount on this hotel for Dec. and Jan. I paid $179 and it was worth it. The code when calling the W hotel is NYCPT. The room is normally $390. I would NOT pay this price. The noise- well, your in New York. I would say we heard honking going on till midnight. I have to sleep with the t.v. on so it didn't bother me. The bed is so comfortable, it shouldn't matter. The location- The W was closer than we thought to everything. It is walking distance to 5th Ave (about 3 blocks) and Rockefeller Center is about 4 blocks. You should get there within 5 mins. of walking. Take a cab to Time Square. Restaurants- Steaks- Go to Sparks around the corner it was delicious. Hamburgers-Prime Burgers on 51st across the street from the Cathedral, the BEST! Italian - we went to Rocco's and saw Mama - she was so nice. Order the spagetti and Mama's meatballs, it was the best. The penne pasta was not cooked all the way. All in all, this hotel experience was worth the money. The bar in the hotel (Whiskey Blue) is small, packed, and pricey. Drop the bags in the hotel and see the town and expect to get back to a comfortable bed and a hot wonderful shower.

title: “Needs a makeover!”
text:
This hotel is rated as 4-Star by Hotwire.com. I got three nights for $110/night.
Gripes:
- It doesn't feel like a 4-Star hotel, by any measure of "luxury". Rooms are furnished with a lot of old, worn, once-nice furniture. However, carpets and walls and draperies feel worn, old, and therefore dirty - you cringe and try to avoid. Similar for the half-remodelled bathroom.
- 19" TV?! 
- NOT a business hotel! There is a small table which is located next to the window (facing another window) - a far far way from the speakerphone placed on the bedside table....which leads me to...
- No available cell service in my room. I had to go downstairs to take a few conference calls. For others, I had to rig up a workstation on the bed with the power cord to my laptop in one direction and the phone cord in another direction to the wall on the other side.
- heating/AC is a bit dated and slightly wheezy
Pluses:
- free internet (come on - everyone's gotta have this now)
- coffee and tea downstairs in the mornings
If you need to be right in Union Square, sure, this is probably a decent choice. It is clear of the sketchy side of Tenderloin. 
However, personally,I usually try to get a good rate in the Embarcadero where the hotels tend to be newer and with larger rooms.

title: “First Class Hotel”
text:
This is a wonderful hotel - beautifully decorated and clean. The staff is very professional and personable. If you need to stay near Bush Intercontinental Airport, there is no better place to stay. It is by far the nicest hotel of all the hotels at the airport. The others are all accessible by hotel shuttles. This one is connected to the airport. A short train ride stops at all three terminals. Surprisingly the hotel is very quiet considering it sits right beside the airport runways, with planes taking off and landing every few minutes. If you love to watch planes, be sure to ask for a room in the rotunda. 
Allies American Grill, on the lower level, has a great breakfast buffet. The food is delicious - homemade granola, smoothies, fresh fruit, and loads of other goodies. I've never seen an omelet station like the one here. The chef had an incredible assortment of ingredients to make any kind of omelet. 
The Flight Lounge on the top level is a pretty busy place. And don't miss CK's Revolving Restaurant on the roof of the Marriott. Great place for a romantic dinner, and a spectacular view of the airport and the city, especially at night.

title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text: Based on previous reviews, when I discovered that this was the hotel assigned to me by Priceline...I was scared! However, I was pleasantly surprised. Check in was smooth. Stayed in a room in the east tower adjacent property. The adjacent section seemed to be a little older then the main lobby building but definitly nicer looking then the outside of the east tower. Room was not extravegant but clean and modern looking. Very comfortable bed and pillows. Sunday brunch was amazing! I'd go back just for the brunch. Walked all around the hotel and the grounds are very nice. Tennis courts, two pools, work out room and a game room kept my kids busy. I actually wished we were staying more then one night so we could enjoy the facilities more. Hotel is right on the marina so you get to enjoy the boats and the water. Excellent location, easy to get to Zoo, Gaslamp district, ect. I would definitly stay here again.

title: “My Stay”
text:
This is the forth time I have stayed at this hotel.
I like everything about the stay. That is why I come back and will continue to.
The rooms are laid out to be comfortable. Furnishings are designed to make you feel at home. The employees are likable and accommodating.
Tuesdays and Thursdays they offer happy hour that is a treat.

title: “Highly Recommend!”
text: We arrived here totally exhausted and jetlagged! Staff were very pleasant and accommodating. The room was large and airy and beautifully decorated. The king bed was one of the comfiest beds I''ve ever slept in! There was also plenty of room for your belongings, though as we were only staying one night we didn't unpack. Bathroom was also spacious and well equipped. Breakfast was contintental but a very good choice of dishes. We used the bar in the evening and it was ample for our requirements and has access to free internet. There is also a restaurant and a swimming pool, but we didn't used either. Location is about 5-10 mins in a free shuttle, which worked very well. Couldn't have asked for a better airport location. Would definately recommend for an airport stay.

title: “Close to EL, good shopping,”
text:
We stayed her labor day weekend Friday night through Monday. It was in a good location if you plan on taking the EL. It was right by good shopping on State Street. I would recommend asking for room on opposite side of El, like we did and we didnt hear anything that loud. You could hear it but it didnt disrupt your sleep. 
We requested early check in as we arrived at 11a.m. and they said come back at 1pm and we did...still not ready...so we came back at 2 still not..finally at 3 which is the stadnard check in....
Didnt eat or drink here...

title: “HAPPY FOR THE $ SPENT”
text: We got a bargain on line and honestly for the price you can not ask for more. The service was great and we got what we paid for. My husband and I will stay there again for those same deals.

title: “The ratings say it all!”
text: Great motel with a spacious room for our family of four. We were initially disappointed that the family suite was already booked but it didn't matter in the end as our 2 beds room was just perfect! Night times were quiet and we slept well. Good position - walked to North Beach, Fisherman's Wharf, cable cars etc. Free parking!! Breakfast at Pat's Cafe was a delight.

title: “Fantastic location”
text: I stayed at this Hilton for a weekend - it is in a great location near restaurants and shops, and the room was very large and comfortable, as was the bed. The staff were friendly and helpful. I would recommend this hotel for anyone visiting Chicago.

title: “Not good enough”
text: Quite disappointed with this hotel. Room clean and nice but windows did not open because of some work being done to the outside??, small bathroom, staff at reception not friendly apart from one, absolutely overpriced in everything: internet $15.00 a day, breakfast too expensive and it cost $3.50 per bag to leave in luggage room when checking in or out of hotel. Gym was closed for renovation. Overall not up to Hilton standard and would certainly not go back. Very average

title: “One of the better convention hotels”
text: This Hilton is huge, and is the site of many conventions. But it is very efficiently run, and the service is congenial. It is convenient to everything: within walking distance of the Powell St. station with BART service to/from the airport and the cable car terminus, or, in the other direction to Union Square and the Chinatown gate. There are plenty of affordable dining options with a block or two such as the Old Siam Thai, or try John's Grill for steaks, seafood, and jazz. There are many different room varieties, so be sure to ask where/what kind you're getting before you leave the check-in desk. And be prepared to pay for wifi, and steeply for parking.

title: “Average if you are on a budget”
text:
I met two girlfriends in San Francisco for a four-day stay and was not in charge of reservations this trip. A friend who has not been to SF previously booked the room and I can pretty much roll with most anything so wasn't too worried after reading a few reviews.
The property is an older motor lodge on Lombard which carries a heavy amount of traffic most any time of day or night. With a room facing the road you will either need a cocktail before bed or sleep with the tv on. Also, the elevator apparently has been out of service for months so be prepared to carry your bags up a few flights of stairs. Again, realizing the discount not huge issues, just wouldn't be my choice for either. 
The rooms appear to have been remodeled at some point in the past and the bathroom updated. Carpets were stained but beds were "ok" for comfort and linens. Very limited lighting and electrical plugs so if you have more than a person or two be prepared when it comes to drying your hair, makeup, getting ready in general. 
Staff was friendly and they do offer coffee, english muffins and bananas/oranges in the AM. Enough to give you a boost to start the day. 
I would recommend for younger travelers on a budget. Would make a different choice in the future but overall an average accomodation.

title: “Nice hotel..”
text: My family and I stayed there this past Saturday night. The hotel is renovated so it is very clean! The rooms were nice, but my only complaint was that the walls do seem to be thin. The people in the room next door came in at 2:30 am and I could hear them in the bathroom, toilet flush etc. Also, I could constantly hear the elevator going up and down all night which was very annoying. Not sure if I am super sensitive to noise as I do not see any other complaints about this. We got a gret price, so it was hard to complain. The staff was very nice at check in. We had breakfast at the hotel (just ok), nothing fancy at the buffet. But once again, staff was extremely nice. Also, great location close to shopping, restaurants and the T.

title: “nice location, average price”
text:
Ok so it is a Westin which means it is pretty much the same as every other Westin on the planet.
I did particularly like the double head shower design- very comfortable. 
The location is great for the charlotte convention center and a couple of blocks walk from central Charlotte (i.e. restaurants, bars, etc). 
I did not like the lack of willing to call a cab, where the airport car service was pushed a little too hard. 
There is parking at 18 USD per day and it is easy to find a space. 
Overall it is what you would expect from Westin!

title: “Park Plaza was great!”
text:
Overall great experience! I stayed with my husband and 9 year old son in a standard double room. We had plenty of room and found the beds comfortable. Great location...we walked to Boston Common, loewr half of the Freedom Trail, Prudential Tower, Fanueil Hall and to the convenient and nearby T station to get to places further away. Lots of restaurants and food court to choose from in the area. Staff was very helpful with suggestions for family restaurants, making calls for us about bike rentals, and taking care of our airline online check-in.
My only complaint would be the wait for the elevators at some times during the weekend, especially on Sunday morning. We were only a couple of floors up, so we quickly learned our way on the back staircase, which is not all that well marked.
I would definitely stay at this hotel again. Watch for dropping prices as it gets closer to your travel date. I found incredible deals on hotels.com 2 weeks before we were traveling.

title: “Offers what major hotels can't”
text:
We booked this hotel based on some research, trip advisor reviews and the rates. We actually tried to find another hotel because some of the trip advisor reviews had us worried, especially since it was my wife's first trip to New York, I wanted her to have the best experience possible. I'm glad we couldn't find another hotel!
As soon as we stepped in the lobby we were impressed with the atmosphere, it is an older hotel lobby, but clean and well kept.
We booked a regular queen room but were upgraded to a suite on the 15th floor. The room was beautiful. Very clean, remodeled, still had that older 60's feel to it at the same time. I believe the 15th floor is the only one that has a little balcony you can step out on and look around. The balcony is not big, just big enough to sit down for a cup of coffee, but a great view of the Empire State builiding, and look around the corner and there was the Chrysler building too!
The staff was very friendly and helpful whenever we had a question.
The bedford is literally a couple minutes walk from Grand Central and about 15 minute walk from Times Square. The taxi cost about $28 from La Guardia ($5 Tunnel fee....customers have to pay bridge and tunnel fees.) When we checked about a bus, it was $12/ea. for the same ride. A taxi to Times Square was about $11. There is a Starbucks right across the street and a Dunkin Donuts just a few doors from there on Lexington.
If you are looking for a nice place to eat, not fancy, just good food, with friendly staff....go to Scotty's around the corner. We hadn't eaten all day and got back from the night tour from the city (10:30pm) and failed to get something at Times Square. It's family owned and open 24hrs. The food was made to order, not re-heated, made right in front of you. Great little diner with the neighborhood feel, seemed pretty popular with the locals, half the people knew the owner. Not sure about Bloom's, but Scotty's was small neighborhood prices with big plates of food.
GREAT hotel, best value, we will return when we go back to the city.

author.location: So Ca, but wishing I was in the Caribbean!

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
I am writing this review late but I wanted to put my positive review up here so this lovely hotel gets the credit it deserves. We also booked our stay at the chancellor based on the reviews in trip advisor and I must say it lived up to all expectations. I contacted Wes Tyler via e-mail during the holiday weeks to make a reservation. He was very helpful and made the process quite easy. In addition, he was kind enough to extend a special the hotel was running for an additional day, making this stay a tremendous value. 
In terms of the hotel itself, our room was beautifully decorated and quite comfortable. I do not look for large hotel rooms when I travel because I am not traveling to San Francisco to stay in a hotel room the entire time; I am there to see the city. That being said the rooms are clean and the hotel is well maintained. In addition, the location of this hotel is perfect. It is easily accessible to public transportation leading all over the city and to the airport. 
The hotel staff is very nice and there are some very nice touches that they include. The hotel provides an umbrella for your use, it was in our closet. Since it rained almost every day we were in the city this was greatly appreciated. They have fresh coffee and cookies (really good cookies!) all day and offered apples and muffins in the morning. They have two computers in the lobby that guest can utilize. My husband inquired about a firm pillow and was given a list of several different types of pillows that he could choose from. When we returned from our outing his pillows were in the room. Finally, the rubber ducky in the bathroom is a cute touch.
We enjoyed our stay and we were impressed by all this hotel had to offer for such a great rate. We would certainly stay here again.

title: “Nice view and clean rooms”
text:
I stay here for my business trips especially when I have to stay over the weekend. I can walk down to Lake Union and relax, walk the other direction and I'm downtown or a bit further and I'm at Pike's Place. 
The breakfast buffet is delicious but a bit much I you want a light breakfast before a meeting. 
It's a bit pricey but always clean with friendly staff.

title: “Top Notch Business Hotel”
text: I stayed here for a week long training session. This hotel is great. The staff is very attentive but not uptight in the least. The rooms are well appointed, comfortable and clean. The meeting facilities are extremely functional. Best of all, the food in this hotel is great. So many hotel just do so so on the food, but the Renaissance was great. It is also in great downtown location as long as you don't Seattle's hills.

title: “Great location, great staff and great rooms.”
text:
Had 5 nights at the Sancuary Hotel, great rooms and super clean, we knew it was going to be a clean stay after arriving to our hall way, it was spotless, so where the rooms, great fun staff at the desk and awesome rooftop bar, loved our stay, thanks guys
Cheers
Bozzies

title: “Great hotel”
text: We stayed here in June 2004 for 3 nights. We loved the friendly, relaxed atmosphere and the opportunity to meet fellow guests at the "happy hour" in the hotel lobby each evening. The location of the hotel provides easy walks to numerous area attractions. Our room was a little small but very clean and well appointed. We enjoyed our stay there so much we returned for another night before leaving the San Francisco area. Highly recommended.

title: “Very Impressed Customer”
text: What a great staff! The moment I checked in I knew this would be a great hotel. I travel every week for business so I can tell immediately what my stay will be like as soon as I arrive. The complimentary shuttle ffrom the airport was timely and the driver exceptional. He knew all about the local area and gave me an overview of the many local attractions. I have not been back to this hotel in over a year and it was nice to see how many local venues are available next door to the hotel. I checked in and the warm attentive service was refreshing. They even walked me to the elevator as they went through the available hotel services!! The room was clean and quiet which allowed me to be super productive over the three day stay. I reccommend you try the on site restaurant and room service as both were outstanding especially the service. I received a survey from Marriott a few days after departing the DFW area. Their highest ranking is a 10 and I was more than happy to score 10 in all categories. I look forward to returning to this hotel in the future.

title: “Loved it!!”
text: We must have had a different room type from the previous reviewer. Our room could not have been more perfect. Two full beds with a tv centered in the middle, computer desk with chair, plus an arm chair in the corner. Room was very clean and fresh. Bathroom was roomy and well stocked with shampoo, conditioner, lotion, as well as plenty of towels, hand towels, make up mirror, and a hair dryer. If I had to think of something to complain about, it would be lack of snack machines and the little store not being open the whole time we were there. But that is minor. We were there for baseball games, and we could not have stayed at a better place. Staff was very friendly and helpful. We travel several times a year both as a family and just my husband and me. I am very picky about hotels, and besides the Kalahari Resort in Sandusky, OH, this may be the nicest place we've ever stayed. Thanks for a wonderful weekend!

title: “Great place to relax and escape the tourist atmosphere of Midtown”
text:
After spending four days in midtown Manhattan to see all the attractions, we wanted to get away from the hectic tourist fray of Central Park and relax by New York Harbor/explore lower Manhattan. If you know what to expect, this is really the ideal place to do just that: there is no better place to stay in lower Manhattan. While this hotel certainly has significant shortcomings as noted on TripAdviser, you come here for the spectacular views, which is why I would wholeheartedly stay here again. Even though I have experienced better accommodations at other Ritz Carlton’s (I have stayed at several lifetime), the unique location of this hotel made my stay worthwhile. 
ROOM: The rooms were nicely appointed but seemed pretty non-descript in terms of décor. We had a city view room for $325 per night, which I thought was I pretty good value. Even though the hotel opened in 2002, the carpet and furnishings were starting to show slight aging. The television was not flat screen and was certainly on the small side. Having just stayed in two Hampton Inns with flat screen TV’s in North Carolina, it is certainly time for an upgrade! However, on a positive note, both the beds and the bathroom were done in typical Ritz Carlton style. The bathrooms featured a separate walk in shower, deep soaking tub, and were of course loaded with marble. As expected, the beds had Frette linens, feather duvets, ext. The quality of the room was certainly not poor, actually well above average, but the consensus is that the rooms need a renovation.
SERVICE: While the service was courteous at all times and the concierge was helpful in booking attractions and restaurants, the service didn’t meet expectations considering what I had heard. What happened to the Ritz Kids cold milk and fresh cookies for the kids upon arrival? What happened to the Teddy Bears at turn down service? These were perks provided to guests when the hotel opened that have since phased out. While the lack of this does not make the service at the Ritz Carlton Battery Park poor, per se, but just disappointing because this was advertised when the hotel opened. Also the service at the Rise Bar was unusually slow and housekeeping could be inconsistent at times. Overall the staff was friendly and helpful but slightly under the quality of the service I had experienced at other Ritz Carlton’s. 
DINING: We did not eat at the hotel restaurant, 2 West, because we had heard there were better options in the area. While there were no better restaurants within walking distance, we ate in Tribeca/Soho/Greenwich village. For dinner, we ate at the Aguagrill in Soho, Nobu in Tribeca, and Babbo in Greenwich Village, all of which were spectacular experiences. For seafood, Japanese, and Italian respectively, there are no better options in the city. For breakfast, I recommend eating at the French brasserie Balthazar, which is commonly rated as one of the top brunches in the city. While there are some cases where the hotel restaurants are the best (see the Dining Room in the Ritz Carlton Buckhead), this is not the case here. Both Zagat and AAA rated 2 West below the caliber of most Ritz Carlton restaurants. However, the Rise Bar was a great experience. However, it’s odd how they closed the outdoor terrace at night for safety reasons. Located on the top floor with an expansive view of New York Harbor and the Statue of Liberty, I can’t image a better location for a bar in the city. Certainly rivals the central park views of the Mandarin Oriental in Midtown. 
Didn’t even see the Spa. They also don’t have a pool which is odd. 
OVERALL: Without a doubt, the Ritz Carlton Battery Park is the best alternative if you are looking to get away from the hustle and bustle of the tourist areas. But even though it is isolated from much of the attractions, we were still able to explore Chinatown, Little Italy, Ground Zero, the World Financial Center, Ellis Island, and the Statue of Liberty. If you are going to explore New York City, I recommend exploring lower Manhattan in addition to Midtown. In comparison to the other five diamond hotels in the city, the Ritz Carlton Battery Park is substantially cheaper (for us, $300 per night cheaper). While parts of the hotel are in need of a quick renovation and the lobby is a bit small, it still lives up to the Ritz Carlton name in most ways.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: We were here for 3 nights. Very knowledgeable and friendly staff. Great at giving advice on how to get around, restaurants and other things we needed. Rooms had fridge, microwave and tv. Free parking and only half a block to the bus and 2 blocks to the cable car! We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Beautiful NY view”
text:
I really enjoyed my stay at Fairfield Inn during August. The room was quite large and the staff friendly and helpful. My room had a beautiful view of Empire State Building, exactly the kind of thing you wish to see from the window when you are in NY.
We had to change our first room because of some problems with air conditioner, but the new one was as good as the previous, with the same amazing view.
Location was good too; breakfast was good, maybe the room was a little small e some mornings we had to wait to get a table.

title: “Great rooms. My favourite for comfort and convenience in New York.”
text:
I have stayed in the Trump Soho a couple of times recently. The first time I was travelling with my wife and we had an exquisite suite. The second I was on my own with a deluxe room.
Both times the rooms have been amazing compared with my other experiences in New York.
The views from the large windows have been wonderful. The space great for New York, especially Soho. I love the soho area and the hotel is a a great combination of comfort, modernity and efficiency. There are no doubt hipper places in NY and certainly better restaurants but I have never been more comfortable in New York. It's not cheap but what is in NY and so much more worth it than 60 Thompson or Soho Grand.
I cannot praise it higher than to say I was almost disappointed when a 3rd trip recently got cancelled at the last minute.

title: “Fun Hotel”
text:
I only stayed one night at the Hotel Gansevoort and overall enjoyed it. 
The decor is very trendy. Comfortable bed and nice amenities in the room (internet, flat screen TV, etc.). I was disappointed I didn't get to see the famed pool or lounge.
I had 2 general complaints:
1) Don't plan on getting any work done at this hotel. There was only the smallest of desks in the room. (I hesitate to even call it a desk).
2) It felt like everything in the room was for sale. Items for sale were all over the room- - hair-care products, vitamins, etc. - not just in the well-stocked mini-bar.

title: “Incredible Stay”
text:
I'm usually very cynical about hotels and don't typically write to praise a hotel. This hotel breaks the mold and has impressed me to the point of writing a positive review.
The staff was incredibly friendly and professional: from the concierge acknowledgment to us as we walked in to the bellman remembering our names throughout the entire stay...we truly felt important. The rooms were very clean with plenty of room and plenty of amenities. 
The staff was incredibly helpful with great food recommendations that were both affordable and close. They also were helpful in general San Francisco information.
This hotel bumps up against the tenderloin area, but I would never have guessed that there was ever any danger. My wife and i never once felt that we were in a threatening or uncomfortable situation concerning our safety.
My only complaint with the hotel is minor in that the toilet seat would not stay up as I tried to use the restroom...my wife found this trick useful :).
The Serrano Hotel was so good that my wife and I decided to call and book another Kimpton hotel when we return to San Francisco...We booked the Prescott Hotel. 
Nothing but the highest praises for the Serrano Hotel, the staff, and the Kimpton properties.

title: “Old Hotel and Feels it”
text:
The best thing that can be said about the hotel was the location. It is in the heart of San Jose, right near the federal court house. But over all, i was not impressed.
The hotel looks old from the outside and feels it. The room did not seem like it was updated recently. It was also a very large room, but it was very empty (not sure why you would have no furniture in a large room). The tv was far from bed and difficult to see. 
bathroom was modern and nice.
Big problem was breakfast, there was none. We were told to go to the hotel next door (which I wished I stayed at).
Finally, there was a problem with my bill. I called to take care of it, was told it would be corrected, and had to call back a week later when nothing was done.
Overall, hotel is ok, but nothing special

title: “Absolutely loved it!”
text: Stayed at this hotel with college friends. It is in the heart of Times Square and the theater district. It was fantastic. The rooms are large and have a nice view. The staff was nice and very helpful. I loved being so close to everything and being able to walk to restaurants and the theater. They have a great work out facility, but I did not have time to use it. It is pricey, but reasonable if you share the cost with others. We had adjoining rooms which was nice.

title: “don't stay here too many better choices”
text: Wow really surprised because the Sheraton is normally a great hotel chain. Rooms really cold, old floor heater didn't work well at all thought it was remodeled. Old shower and bath. Thank god I was only here one night too loud couldn't sleep and I was put in a room with two beds even though only me and a lovely view of a bus yard

title: “great location, great price”
text: ideal spot for long weekend and chance to wander the Magnificent Mile. Friendly staff, clean rooms, ok breakfast but free and good start with hot cup of coffee. Very reasonably priced when everything else was going double or more. Have stayed in this chain in San Diego also. Love the suite layout.

title: “Great Stay Fantastic Location”
text:
Very happy with our recent stay. Great location - easy walk to 5th Avenue (Lord & Taylor to the Left, Sak's to the Right), 3 blocks to Broadway where you will find Times Square, Theatres, stores open till 1am, resaturants, and the Hop on Hop Off buses. 
Deli's, Starbucks, the footcourt in Grand Central are all within 2 blocks or less of the hotel.
The superior double room size was similar to what you would find at a Hampton Inn/Holiday Inn across the country. No counter space in bathroom; just a small shelf above the toilet. Room was quiet, clean, with comfotrable beds. 
There are computers for guest use, charges apply, except for boarding passes which are free. Would definately stay again on future trips.

title: “Great location, Great Value”
text: We stayed here for 5 nights in March 2006 and were very happy with our choice. The room was spacious and clean, the breakfast generous and the staff were very friendly. My only negative observation is that there is very poor soundproofing around the bathrooms as has been previously mentioned - I was woken at 7am every morning by the people next door showering etc. - not the best when you are trying to get over an 11 hour flight plus an 8 hour time difference. Other than that, the Inn is terrific value for money and I'd definitely stay there again.

title: “Outstanding Service at the pool!”
text: We just visited the Arizona Biltmore for a "girl's" weekend and had a wonderful time. We spent the first day lounging by the pool and were instantly treated to exceptional service by Aaron and his staff. They went out of their way to make us feel welcome, attended to our every need, and even convinced us to change our plans for the next day and spend a second full day with them by the pool. In addition to the great treatment at the pool, the staff also didn't even hesistate when we asked for late night "room service" on the patio outside the lobby (enjoying the great weather). When asked what was on the menu, the response was "whatever you'd like." All in all, a wonderful weekend. We will definitely be going back again!

title: “Overpriced, overhyped”
text:
The very smart gentlemen on reception gave us warm towels to freshen up with, but just when I thought we were going to get a glass of champagne too they discovered, on going to the open bottle behind the till, "no glasses!" and did nothing to find some, so no champagne for us. 
The rooms were tiny. The view was of a building site opposite. The cleaning woman had left a card telling me who it was who'd cleaned my room; she'd also left beside the card the dirty rag she'd been doing the cleaning with, presumably so I'd know she'd been hard at it. 
The bar was noisy, brash and inhabited by people with more money than sense, with a smattering of idiots thrown in for good measure. I'm ashamed to say we joined them later on and fitted in well. 
The main bright spot of this otherwise overpiced, overhyped hotel was the staff outside the front door, who were uniformly polite, cheerful and helpful, pointing out the (wonderful) Pepolino restaurant just up the road when we needed somewhere to eat.

title: “great hotel”
text:
Myself, my partner and another couple stayed here for 4 nights at the beginning of the month and we were not disappointed with the hotel. The hotel was clean, the staff were very friendly and the location was brilliant only a short walk to empire ste builing times sqaure and macys.
There was plently of places to eat around the hotel aswell, we stayed in a 1 bed suite and it was lovely we had 2 bathrooms a small kitchen. The maid was here evryday and i could not fault the cleanliness. WE were on the 20th floor, and yes there was some noise but what do you expect in the big apple, we never came all the way from scotland for some peace and quiet.
Would definitely recommend this place and will stay here again when i come back

title: “Classic Great NYC Hotel”
text: I chose this hotel because its old and classic New York hotel and I was not disappointed. The Lobby was fantastic. Service was sober and quick. Location is great : subway just near the hotel entrance and about 10minutes walk to Time Square. I had metro room which was surprisingly spacious. Bed was wide and good to sleep. Bathroom was old but in good condition and everything works. Room was cleaned every day and towels changed. Even if spaces are clearly old they are in clean and in good shape. Every rooms are located at least in 19th floor. I asked a room with views to Manhattan and get it. I could saw Empire State building right from my bed. Great stay , I would definitely come back here !

title: “Big Rooms Great Location.”
text: I'd have to say, reading the reviews on this hotel started me off with a bad outlook on staying at Affinia Manhattan. When I arrived to the hotel, it was in a great location and the staff was very helpful once I got their attention. The lobby is beautiful with a very modern bar/restaurant connected. The parking is outrageously expensive but...it IS New York City. I called ahead and spoke with an employee who changed my room as I requested one with a decent view. When I arrived the room was massive and very clean. The beds are comfortable but the sheets leave a little to be desired. The staff accomodated every request I had and went above and beyond what I asked. Over all great place to stay if you aren't incredibly picky :)

title: “Nice but not the Best”
text: I went here from June 23-24, 2010; after my flight back to Minneapolis was canceled due to mechanical problems on the plane. We left the next day; enjoyed a poolside dinner at the restaurant the night before. The pool, just like the one in La Jolla I stayed at for the past week (La Jolla Shores Hotel), went from 3 1/2 feet to 8 1/2 feet. Only; the La Jolla one only had 3 1/2, 4 1/2, and 8 1/2 foot depth markings plus the meter depths; while the one here had ones saying 3 1/2, 4 1/2, 5 1/2, 7 1/2, and 8 1/2 feet. They didn't have meter/ yard depths and skipped the 6 1/2 foot marking. Just like La Jolla, the hot tub was 3 1/2 feet. I really liked the pool and cafe. Friendly staff. The only access to my room was from outside, but I didn't care. Nice hotel. This inn deserves a nice 8.

title: “Good location, great owners!”
text: I found this hotel to have many great things going for it, the best of which are the friendly and down-to-earth owners, Frank & Judy, who gave my friend and I good tips on restaurants around the neighborhood (which are fairly copious) and all the public transit info we needed to get around SF successfully. Another thing I appreciated was the location. It's conveniently sandwiched between the Wharf and the popular downtown destinations (Civic Center, Union Square, etc.) so that you can access both via cable car (just a short walk to the Powell/Hyde line!) during the day and still return to a quieter haven for sleeping at night. Overall our stay was great: the neighborhood was quiet, the room was clean, and the price was better than average. Even considering minor flaws (a broken coffee pot) there was nothing truly regretable about this place (a quick call to the office, and Frank had a new pot in minutes). I would stay here again in a heartbeat!

title: “Really nice place”
text: We stayed at the watertown feb 2003 and were very impressed. They have a lot of cool perks that go above and beyond what most hotels would offer. The decor is all brand new and very stylish (what Ikea wants to be), and all very pretty. Be sure to request one of the complimentary carts - we requested the "spa cart" and got a lot of enjoyment out of the bath salts and gadgets. You won't get a cart unless you request one. The complimentary "continental" breakfast includes some cool items like hard-boiled eggs and french toast. The gym is very small but the bicycle rentals were a lot of fun. Oh yeah, and instead of the usual vending machine, they have a little "store" at the front desk for middle of the night munchies, so you get to buy them from a real person and you don't have to worry about having the right change. Overall this was a very pleasurable experience. Would definitely recommend.

title: “Great location, fantastic staff - the best place to stay in san fran.”
text:
We rang ahead before we arrived to check we could have a courier package delivered to the hotel, and let slip that the package was our weding photos and we were on our honeymoon. The staff put us in the best room on the top floor (15th) and we arrived to find a bottle of champagne and card congratulating us on our wedding. What a great welcome!
The trams run right outside so its really easy to get around. Much less touristy around Union Square than down Fisherman's Wharf area. Stay here - its great.

title: “Too perfumy”
text: Actually a very pleasant place to stay, except for this one thing. From the time we stepped into the lobby, to the time we went into our room, my nose and eyes itched and my head hurt from the heavy air perfume. That was totally the only thing wrong with the place. But enough that I probably won't be staying there again.

title: “bedbugs”
text: woke up with arm bleeding, full of bites. called management shortly thereafter. got a call not from mgmt, but their insurance/stop loss people, who seemed to be faulting me for not going to a doctor. I cleaned up my arm and took care of the business I was there to do. the person I talked with offered me reimbursement for "ointments." I took pix of my bites. Then I got a letter stating they investigated and found no bedbugs. THEY HAD THE WRONG ROOM AND DATE. I am concerned that this problem never was taken care of, and at this point not sure of date. just would not stay there again, and really feel the management could have apologized. my diagnosis of bedbug bites was certain, and I was a bit traumatized waking up with my arms bleeding.

title: “diamond in the rough”
text: I have stayed at this hotel a handful of times and each time I like it more. I was in a suite with my kids this trip which was very large and with three kids you need alot of room. As always the customer service was excellent. For the price you would think you were staying at a 5 star hotel..

title: “Excellent - as usual!”
text: My husband and I stayed here for 2 nights; we've stayed here about 3 times before and I'd always pick this hotel when staying in Boston. The location is great because you're really close to the Prudential Center and Newbury Street. A lot of the cheaper hotels are much further out of town which is a shame because downtown Boston is so walkable and the location of the Lenox means you can pop back during the day to drop stuff off or have a nap before more shopping and sightseeing! It's not the cheapest hotel but the service is excellent, it's spotlessly clean and because it's an old building there are actually proper lights in the middle of each room! A real novelty after staying in modern hotels where there is NEVER enough light. I highly recommend the Lenox - it's probably not the most high tech or modern hotel in Boston, but it has real character and the staff are great. Stay here if you can!

title: “Would stay here again”
text:
There were 4 of us in our party staying at the Old Town Inn. It is really clean and comfortable and breakfast was really good, coffee, juices, bagels etc. were always fresh and topped up. It is really close to the Old Town area where the shuttles to downtown areas are available as well as taxis.
Check-in staff (Anna) was really friendly and helpful. Anna even took the time to try to help us check-in online as we were having difficulty in doing so, but it was a technical problem with the reservation system. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “CHECK YOUR ROOM!”
text:
4 of us went to the Conrad to celebrate a BIG BIRTHDAY. We got 2 rooms, which we'd booked several months in advance. 1 room was lovely. Our room had many problems, unfortunately. We checked in and just dropped our bags off to go to dinner at oceannaire (fabulous). When we returned to the room, around 11 pm, we realized we'd been given a handicap accessible room--not a big problem, so we thought.
We tried to read before bed, but BOTH of the reading lights were broken. 1 just hung limply and couldn't adjust except to hand toward the floor. The other DID adjust, but the bulb was burnt out--so no reading. In the morning when we went to shower, we realized that the HIGHEST the shower head would go was mid chest. (tough to wash one's hair, unless you crouched down, not to mention your neck and face). It was also a very small shower--unlike our friends who had the great double shower head large shower. Oh well. there was also only ONE large bath towel, although the room was clearly booked for 2 people.
We looked for robes after our shower--NONE. (our friends room DID have them).
So I don't know if all handicap accessible rooms are like this, or just ours, but for our special occasion, it certainly put a big damper on it.
I will say that the beds were VERY COMFORTABLE, the TV was great, so there were many good things about the room--but no reading light, a bad shower and no robes, we were very disappointed.
When we mentioned this at checkout they were very apologetic , but that didn't really improve our experience.
In short, not what we expected from this kind of hotel.

title: “The Reviews are right on”
text: This place was great. It was clean, brand new looking (all new furniture, carpet, etc), big rooms. the staff was extremely helpful, right next to public transportation and a couple blocks from the Cable Cars.

title: “Desperately Needing Refurbishment”
text:
ON THE PLUS SIDE: Good location on 57th Street, 5 minutes walk to Columbus Circle subway, 10 minutes walk to 5th Avenue. Fairly good amenities - bar, restaurant, gift shop. Some staff very helpful. Good local diners (especially The Flame on 9th). Good size double rooms.
ON THE MINUS SIDE: The whole place looks tired, dated and grubby. I had a mouldy crumbling bathroom with a toilet that only flushed sometimes. Sinks are in the bedroom not the bathroom! Stained carpets, furnishings and walls. Slow elevators. Some staff downright rude. Drinks and food in the bar and restaurant vastly overpriced. Room service available but no menus/tariffs/details of this in rooms. Everyone in my party of 41 said their rooms were cold.
Not good value for the price.

title: “great hotel but careful of the extras”
text: We stayed two nights at the Westin Boston Waterfront Hotel. The name is a little misleading. We caught slivers of the water from our bedroom window, but the general area is at the waterfront - hence the name. I did expect panoramic waterfront views but I wasn't disappointed because the hotel supeceded my expectations. We paid 4000 SPG points + $60 per night for the room and I hadn't expected to pay much more but walked away with a whopping $400 bill mainly on extras! The extras in this hotel are scandalous. $42 per day for parking, $12+ per day for internet (many hotels offer this for free), $5 for a plain bagel in the breakfast restaurant and the worst of all was the 15% restocking fee for the mini bar. Which is shocking, since when do vendors charge their customers to re-stock their shelves, its absurd. The only great thing is that my kids were under 5 and got to eat breakfast for free. The concierge were great, although we asked the reception lady to suggest a beach on Cape Ann, but would only recommend one down the road - it was like she had a mental block. Singing beach in Manchester-by-the-sea was lovely and only 40 min drive away. If you liked the natural stone flooring in the lobby, it is called Fossil Mint Sandstone. The only reason I know is because my company imports and sells this stone in England. The hairdryer didn't work in the bathroom, but everything else was clean and looked brand new. The concierge and vallet parking were very quick, friendly and efficient. Hate pets in hotels but didn't actually see any at all. Swimming pool was out of action but we were offered free swimming in another hote which we couldn't be bothered to take up. It's a bit out of the way for sightseeing on foot. You have to take a cab to most places or walk to the underground station. We took a cab to the Aquarium, telling the concierge where we were going. But no one bothered to mention that the hotel offers a free shuttle to nearby quincy market that we could have taken.

title: “The Westin is one of the best hotels in Philadelphia.”
text: I have stayed at the Westin Philadelphia often over the past few months for business. I have come to value the consistent excellence of this hotel. The staff at the Westin provides the highest level of service. The location of the hotel is ideal for work in the City of Philadelphia. I have found the Westin's rates to be less than many other high end hotels in the city making it a more affordable luxury hotel option. Finally, the heavenly beds at the Westin ensure that you wake up each morning rested and ready for the challenge of the day!

title: “Don't waste your time”
text: I had high hopes but I couldn't take a shower in the morning as something was wrong with the water. Still awaiting reply from the management after three letters.

title: “Phenomenal...all around!”
text: We loved our stay in this hotel! The service and attention to detail from the staff was outstanding! The rooms were clean and beautiful...also a great size compared to most NY hotels. The food from the restaurant was exceptional and THE VIEW!--from the roof deck took my breath away! I will definitely be a repeat guest as will my friends who were there with me!

title: “Vacation”
