text: Outstanding location, staff was wonderful, Tour bus stop in front of thehotel, parking is reasonable, views of the bay - magnificiant

title: “Reminded me of my first college apartment...”
text:
Ok, the location of this hotel cannot be beat. Close to Times square, 5th ave, Rockfeller center, Central park etc. really an awesome location. 
Staff was friendly enough, not overly intrusive nor did they go out of their way to engage, but that is fine. We didnt want to wait for our king sized bed so took a queen sized bed/room instead. We were on the 35th floor in a HUGE room, kitchen, dining area, living area, I think we had like 4 very sizable closets, 1.5 bathrooms, tons of space, so that was nice...however, the condition of the room was another story. Chipped, swollen laminate cupboards in the not very clean bathroom, kind of gross, worn out shag carpet. Dated furniture was kind of dirty, stained etc. LIke my review title noted, it reminded me of my first really bad college apt. They describe their fitness 'center' as state of the art....maybe back in the 80's...but not in 2012, yikes! We had free breakfast with our 4 night stay...we only took advantage of that one time, no more needs to be said on that count. There are not enough elevators for this tall of a building....despite staying on the 35th floor, we did take the stairs down a few times, I saw alot of people waiting, waiting, waiting and frustrated.
With all of this said, when one is in New York, there is plenty to do out side of the hotel so it depends on your perspective and what you have planned...if, however, you want a comfy, clean, modern hotel that cares about the condition of their rooms, you could probably do better. On the other hand, our friends stayed in a king bed room one floor below and they actually had a pretty nice room in better condition, a bit cleaner and not looking quite so worn...so , make sure you ask for what you want, size or condition of room.

title: “Had a good stay”
text: Staff were polite and approachable, room is clean but doesn't have a pleasant smell, a game for kids is with fee, a number to call the front desk is nowhere to find unless you are use to staying in a hotel, swimming pool is closed and no activities for kids to do, continental breakfast is good, basic necessities are available for free, it's near to the mall and airport . Overall stay is good.

title: “Amazing hotel stay 4.5/5”
text:
This is easily one of the nicest hotels I've stayed at when visiting new york. I traveled with my 10 year old niece and she loved the hotel and the room. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone. The room was a great size with a good (not great) view.
The location was fantastic and in decent walking distance to almost all of our activities. The hotel was somewhat costly, so if you're not going to spend a lot of time in the hotel, you might want to consider somewhere a little cheaper.

title: “Very Nice Even at Twice the Price”
text:
This hotel was assigned to us for $95 a night ($115 after taxes) as the 4.5 star option on Hotwire. I would have been willing to pay twice as much for this room.
We arrived at 10 and Olga at the front desk allowed us to check in 6 hours early. When we got into the room we were surprised by how large it was. The bathroom was even large (especially for a Chicago hotel room.) We booked a non-smoking king which left plenty of room for moving around.
The linens were plush, the tv and radio were very nice. Overall the little extra one expects for a 4+ star hotel were there....except an in-room coffee maker.
The staff are probably what made this stay a little better than expected. As already mentioned, Olga at the front desk was helpful at check-in and again when we were charged for a min-bar item we did not use.
The bell-men and parking attendents were extremely helpful, friendly, and always willing to go the extra step with directions or eating suggestions.
The location of this hotel is one block off Michigan and next to the Marriott. It was an easy walk to any of the attractions on Michigan Ave. and less than a $5 cab ride to Millenium Station. I highly recommend staying there if you get the chance.

title: “Perfect place to park, sleep, and fly at Indianapolis Airport”
text: We stayed here before an early morning departure from Indianapolis airport. The room was not luxurious, but it was clean and adequate for the sub-$100 rate for a room and parking. Shuttle service was on-time, friendly, and responded quickly when our plane returned at around 1:30 AM. Parking seemed reasonably safe behind the restaurant next door. Overall, the park, sleep, fly package is perfect for someone who doesn't want to drive to the airport for an early departure.

title: “Horrible, no genuine interest in customer service”
text: Traveling with my wife and small children. We booked two rooms adjoining each other for today. Upon arrival the rooms were not ready. We waited patiently. Then told us one of the two rooms would be ready and the other we would have to wait. We waited. At this point we get frustrated as our children are tired, my wife and I are tired. Their customer service did nothing. The rooms were not ready, and AGAIN they tell us we have to wait another two hours before getting our room. Ridiculous! We have been waiting since 1:30 this afternoon! This is unacceptable behavior. I have been treated better at lesser hotels. They have no genuine interest is making us feel warm and welcome. Instead a burden. They eventually offered us a room that was ready down the hall from our children. Preposterous behavior.

title: “Great location, great value hotel”
text:
This hotel is a great, no frills, value hotel. We stayed there one night to see some sights in the area. The room and main areas were clean. The furniture in the room is worn (but clean). The overall appearance of our room was a bit dated; popcorn ceilings, wallpaper, the worn furniture. But the beds were fine and the bathroom was updated (although no fan in there so it got too steamy when showering). 
The location is great. It is about three short blocks to the National Air & Space Museum and all of the sights along the National Mall. We easily walked to all of the sights. Only downside to the location was at night and early morning it is pretty desolate because it is surrounded by office buildings. There weren't many great food choices within short walking distance. There was a Starbucks, McDonalds, and deli on the same street and some food carts. 
We booked through the Holiday Inn website and took advantage of their Park & Stay package. $5 more than their standard room rate and it includes parking in their garage (normally $35 + tax per night). We were able to leave the car there after we checked out until 5pm, which was a huge plus!
I would probably stay closer to the White House for my next visit but this is a very good choice if you don't want to take the car or worry about public transportation and see all the sights.

title: “Great value without sacrificing quality”
text:
Stayed at the Club Quarters Rockefeller for 3 days. Accommodations are basic and rooms are clean and comfortable. This hotel has some amenities outlined on website that were not yet available, given this Club Quarters location recently opened. Rooms may be a bit small for two people if you plan to spend a significant amount of time relaxing in room.
Wasn't charged extra for early check-in but late check-out (3 pm) was $30.00. Room key didn't work when I returned to room after lunch. Was told that room keys automatically time out at regular check-out time and new room key could not be issued. Staff let us in room in a timely manner but next time won't pay for late check-out and will just have bags stored until ready to leave. Did notice that cigarette smoke smell came through from other rooms. Neglected to ask if there were non-smoking wings and/or floors.
Those issues aside, great location. Easy to get around NYC as subway lines nearby. Close to Broadway theaters. Within walking distance of Central Park. While hotel was in the middle of the Radio City Music Hall/Times Square area, room was quiet.
While it's not luxurious, not meant to be since it caters to business travelers. It has all the basics needed for a comfortable, pleasant stay. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Very nice but fairly costly”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a nearby event but I found the value very bad. The rooms were small-ish and we were afraid to touch things in fear we'd be charged for their use. It cost something like 90 cents even to make a local call. If you like fancy places with nice views of the state building and not much else, this place should be okay. I probably won't be going to Indianapolis again anytime soon, but if I ever do I'd definitely take my chances with a cheaper place.

title: “Fantastic service.”
text: My husband stayed here a couple of nights after our wedding as a make shift honeymoon since neither of us were able to go far that weekend. The service was above and beyond, the facilities are beautiful, and the location is fantastic. Very pleased.

title: “Honest Reivew”
text:
My boyfriend surprised me with a weekend trip to NYC for my 26th b-day. This was our first trip to NYC but we have traveled to many other large cities in the US. I have to admit that I was a little nervous about the hotel after reading what many others wrote about it on this site. 
We arrived at the W around noon on Friday and the check in was fast and friendly. We had a room on the 40th floor with a view of Times Square. Our room was clean, and more spacious than I expected. We loved the bed and the robes! The Bliss products also were a nice touch. 
He had arranged to have a birthday surprise waiting for me that night which consisted of rose petals leading to the bed and then a big heart of petals on the bed. Also, there were chocolate covered strawberries and champagne waiting for us with a nice card. (This was complimentary). This is an example of how they go out of their way to make your stay special. Also the next night a bottle of wine was sent to our room. (also complimentary!) 
All the workers were friendly and very helpful. 
We both enjoyed our stay at the W. The location was great for us first timers to NYC. 
We didn't hear much from outside while in our room so I don't know what others complained about. 
There are areas that this hotel could improve upon (not the the service) but overall we really enjoyed it. I would definately recomend this hotel to friends. I would also suggest contacting the hotel to see if you can get a better rate than the internet, and if not, see what they can do for you to make your stay more special.
For what we paid I feel we got a great deal!

title: “Good: Inexpensive, decent rooms. Bad: Poor service and noisy.”
text: No parking. Well, okay. 5 parking spots in front that were full. Didn't know this in advance. Had to drive around the block a few times before parking on a side street and carrying my bags up. Hostess was nice. The hotel itself and the rooms were clean and modern, although the bathroom could've used a bit more attention. Went down to the bar around 10. There were about 7 people and no bartender. After about 5 minutes an employee went it the back and I could hear him say, "There's a new guy out there." I waiting another 5 minutes before a young women appeared with a desert of some kind and served it to her friends. I knew this because they talked for about another 5 minutes before she finally greeted me. When I asked her about her bourbon selection, she had no idea, so I ordered beer. Over the course of that beer, I watch employees get off work and sit at the bar and other employees start to clean. It was like an after party an hour before the bar was to close. Even the manager was in attendance. My glass sat empty for another 10 minutes before was able to grab the bartender walking by me for another drink. It was at this time, I pulled out my phone and started making a review of my experience on Yelp. I was pleasantly surprised to find a coupon for checkin-in...$1 for my first drink. I alerted the bartender of this offer and she only charged me $2 for both drinks. She asked to see my review but I'm sure she'll see it soon enough. I left $5 on the table and went to bed. Around 8 am, construction or maintenance workers or just noisy maids work me up until I finally checked out around 10. I was waiting for the new hostess to ask me "How as your stay" but got nothing. Not even a smile. I checked out and have been anticipating filling this out ever sense. If The Pearl gets their service issues down, it's a great spot.

title: “Elegant Old World Charm: Classic Big City Hotel”
text: We stayed on the 20th floor of the Palmer House for work-related business. This is one of the prettiest Grand Hotels I've ever stayed in. The lobby is majestic, with soaring ceilings and big chandeliers -- everything is done on the grandest possible scale. I tend to prefer more contemporary boutique hotels, but even an adult feels like Eloise at the Plaza in a place like this. I loved the surroundings and just had three complaints: the hotel charges $15 per day to use wireless internet in your guest room, which seems like price gouging to me. And you also have to pay to use the gym, which also seemed unreasonable to me. Finally, our Queen bed was not especially comfortable, so I probably wouldn't stay there except that my company paid for the trip.

title: “Excellent Boutique Hotel - Just refuse to stay in Room 205 !”
text: Reserved through Booking.com. We were allocated room 205 whch has 2 generators directly outside the window and the noise is intolerable.Staff who were extremely helpful could not give us another room until the next day. This new room was on the 6th floor and made this hotel 'perfect'. Location is excellent and I would recommend this hotel to anyone. Just ensure you do not get room 205 though !

title: “Disgusting filthy dump Travelodge in Columbus, Ohio”
text: Sticky stuff on clock and on furniture, clock doesn't work, towels stained, dingy and the size of a hand towel, carpet had gum on it, what looked like milk stains? (who knows) and lots of other dirty spots, BLOOD on the inside of the bedspread (GROSS!!!), no kleenex tissue in dispenser in bathroom, no cable in the room; just local channels and no cable in dining area either (couldn't even watch the news while eating breakfast), dried up milk? splashes all over T.V. in our room, no hair dryer, only shower--no water from bath tub tap. This was probably the most terrible, horrible, filthy and disgusting hotel I have ever stayed in during my entire life!!! The only good things were the price (get what you pay for, I guess; location--right off the interstate and LOTS OF PARKING --sign of slow business???? Hummm . . . wonder why????????? (We stayed on a Saturday night--you'd think it would be busy.) Staff was nice and friendly but I had to get the guy to repeat himself 3 times before I could finally understand his English.

title: “European Service in the Southwest”
text: After close to 50 visits over the past 4 years I owe it to the friendly staff at the Icon to post a report. I discovered the Icon when it was at the end of an overlooked stretch of Main Street in downtown Houston. Since then I have returned loyally, often rescheduling a trip when over time they started to sell out their rooms occasionally. The staff could not have been friendlier and often greeted me by name when I arrived, from the doorman to the desk clerks. The rooms are elegant (although I miss the chocolate squares at night!) and the bathrooms the nicest in town. My only advice for businessmen looking for a good nights sleep is to avoid the rooms by the elevator, numbers 300, 400, 500, etc. They can be a little noisy at night. My only regret is that I have not dined more frequently at the restaurant. After scheduling dozens of dinners around the city I found to my chagrin not long ago that the Icon probably has one of the best steak houses in Houston. Finally, enjoy the neighborhood, particularly El Rey, the bodega across the street with the best cafe con leche in the United States, and Notsuoh (Houston spelled backward), a funky bar a few doors down on Main Street which Robert Pattison of Twilight discovered on a trip to Houston and has raved about ever since.

title: “Overall a great hotel. Staff could not handle unruly pot-smoking guests.”
text: Overall the day staff was great and friendly, but the night staff did not handle unruly pot-smoking/drunk college students. The aforementioned would head to the roof, slamming the door to the staircase constantly with open containers The hallways reek of pot, and the disturbance forced us to leave the room at 12:30 am. When we returned at 2:30 am, the same activity was occurring; door slamming and stoned/drunk 20-something's stumbling through the halls.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed at the Old Town Inn from Thursday through Monday in late September, 2nd floor, king size bed deluxe room. We paid on average $105/night. Bed was VERY comfy and room was clean, no smells, no noise problems. Great location to everything...right on the major highways going anywhere in SD and a short walk to Old Town. The breakfast was a nice touch, waffles and cereal were good. They helped us get San Diego Zoo tickets cheaper than the gate price. Very friendly staff also.
The hotel/motel is just that. A cheaper alternative to staying in a marriott or hilton or holiday inn, basically the same accomodations without the name. It's not going to blow you away as the best place you've ever stayed but it's a nice, cheaper alternative. Reminded me of a nicer version of a quality inn. Most important things to us was that it was clean, the bed was comfortable (surprisingly comfy actually) and that it was cheap. And the staff was very friendly and willing to help which was a bonus. I'd definitely recommend staying there.

title: “Solid 4 Star Hotel”
text: I stayed at Hotel Nikko during a business conference. Solid 4 star hotel with good services and services. Rooms are clean and adequately spacious, good bathroom amenaties and great location in the center of town. I nice touch that was not related to the hotel is that the Starbucks is attached to the hotel and opens at 5 am for us early risers. Too bad that newspapers are not delivered to the room but if you go downstairs early you have your pick of Journal, US Today or New York Times. One word of caution. The upcharge on services is terrible like most hotels. I shipped two small packages using the business center and they charged me $280!!!! Food service if you have a meeting there is expensive as is internet access ($5.95 per hour). Service and personnel were good.

title: “Better than reviews!”
text:
This hotel must be under new management because the bad reviews are so off! This hotel is better than any of the 4 stars I usualy stay at. They are hassels- this is easy and nice!
The nighborhood is not bad, its not beverly hills but its certainly better than anything in central LA!! Very nice room. Very easy parking. Aforadble. Safe and secure. I will be staying here again for
sure!

title: “Great Boston base”
text: I can only mirror whats already been said, fantastic location from which to explore Boston, not the most luxurious hotel, but clean, rooms are spacious and the service was good. Once the facelift and decorating is finished it will leave little to complain about - there was a very strange vending machine in one corridor from which you could get hot pizza - only in America!!

title: “What a great place to stay”
text:
I have just spent 4 wonderful nights in the Grand Hyatt. You could not ask for a more centrally located hotel to go shopping, dining, chilling out in union square over a coffee and of course the cable car terminal. After a very long trip from UK to San Fran, we were greeted at the front desk by `Wayne`, who was very pleasant, courteous and exactly the right person to greet you after a long haul. Checking in was a breeze and after chatting about our trip we were given a room higher up on the 29th floor overlooking Union Square. Wow!! What a view. Thanks again Wayne.
The rooms are very clean, tidy and the beds are comfortable. Our room had a mini-bar, TV, Alarm clock with i-pod docking and the usual iron, hair dryer and coffee making facilities. There is a room safe for your valueables, but if you want you can also get a box at reception.
There is a good gym on the 35th floor with the usual runners/cycles and x-trainers as well as weight machines. The kit all looks modern and you can plug your i-pod into them or watch TV on the individual screen. It does get busy around 0700. 
The staff and concierge are very polite and accomodating. They sell tour tickets on the open top bus at a discounted rate, the bus is definitely worth doing to get your bearings and introduce you to all the districts, plus it stops outside the Grand Hyatt and goes over the Golden Gate bridge.
A definite must is to go to the 36th floor for a drink or just to look out the panoramic window for a view of the bay and coit tower. We were fortunate to have great clear weather and had a fantastic view. Absolotely Wonderful.
We decided to eat in the restaurant, the service is very good and the duty manager made sure everything was to the customers satisfaction. The starters were great, but I felt the main didn`t match up to the 1st course and I have to say I have eaten better for less $$, although those times are few and far between. However, it is definitely worth the experience of looking out onto San Fran enjoying a meal and cool glass of wine, watching the sun set over the horizon, a definite tick in the box thing to do. If you don`t want a big meal, they also do bar food in the bar area and a to-go service.
I cannot fault the service and experience I had staying here, perhaps because I was on a high floor added to the experience, but I would definitely go back to the Grand Hyatt, if I were to return to San Fran.

title: “Great hotel, lousy beds!!”
text:
We spent the Easter long weekend in San Francisco with friends and stayed at this hotel. The hotel is in a fantastic location, minutes from Fishermans Wharf, pier 39, Ghiradelli Square etc. The cleanliness of the hotel is what I noticed first, fantastic, helpful staff, check in a breeze. The rooms are a bit small, but not as small as a few of the prevoius posts have indicated. We had a courtyard room and found it to be very quiet at night.
Now the only negitive part of this review, the beds are HORRIBLE!! They are worn out and when lying in it together you roll right in to the center! We asked our friends and they had the same problem! We asked the hotel manager about this and we were told that the hotel was replacing the beds one third of the hotel at a time!! If you stay at this hotel i hope you get a room with a NEW bed!!
The hotel hosts a wine reception between 5 and 6 and after a long day of site seeing it was nice to have a glass of wine and chat about your day with other guests. The restaurant that is attached to the hotel is nice, but with hundreds of choices all around you it is a hard choice.
The location will bring me back to this hotel but only after they get new beds!!

title: “Made a grown man cry!!!!!”
text: Please, please, please stay away from this sorry excuse for a hotel. Ok so we booked a late trip and went for the cheaper option but this place takes the biscuit. On entry the place doesnt look so bad but you just wait till you see the rooms. In fact, no don't wait to see the rooms, just don't go!!! Read the advice above a stay away..........

title: “Just Gorgeous!”
text: We stayed 8 nights in the Benjamin which had been recommended by friends. Even though we booked through Expedia, we got a corner suite which was suprisingly big and very comfortable. The bed was sooo comfortable and made more luxurious with the excellent linen and pillows. There were two plasma screens and an excellent business/work area. Th suit was spotless and the air very fresh. Excellent concierge and doorman. It is situated directly adjacent to the Waldorf-Astoria and I know who got the better deal!

title: “Highly recommended”
text:
My husband and I are two 25 year olds and it was our first time in NYC.
If you want a hotel, do not stay here! It's a wonderful home away from home instead. 
We stayed for 10 nights and wanted a place to sleep, without bell boys running after us and cheesy greetings every time we show our faces out of our room.
The staff are friendly when you ask for advise and are prompt to pass on all phone messages.
Fresh towels and a quick wipe down of the sink are provided daily, but we would have appreciated a change of linen at least once, as well as a sweep of the floor, which was fairly dusty by the time we left.. but not to worry. The shared toilet is no problem at all, it was always free and always clean.
Chelsea is a wonderful area, and the E train which goes both up and down town is only a 5 minute walk away, as is Murray's Bagels, which was frequented by us daily.
Great value for money - highly recommended if you want a fuss free place to stay.
The only cons I have to mention is poor internet signal inside the room on the 3rd floor (had to sit on the steps to use it) and a very average, squeaky bed.

title: “Unexpected Surprise”
text: Our stay was everything we wanted it to be!!! My fiancee and I were warmly welcomed when we arrived. Soon after we got checked in and were unpacking in our room, there was a knock at the door. It was one of the hotel employees with a complimentary bottle of champagne!! We were so surprised! What a way to kick off a vacation. We later ordered room service. The items on the menu were a bit pricey but it was money well spent. The portions are huge and the food is delicious. It gets better. There was a complimentary hot, fully stocked, and delicious breakfast including the likes of special made omelets, grits, eggs, bacon, waffles, sausage and so much more. There was also a complimentary happy hour with free select beers and wine between 5:30pm- 7:00pm. Not to mention the excellent customer service, clean and modernly decorated rooms, fantastic food and friendly atmosphere! The only down fall was that this particular hotel is about 30 minutes away from downtown (zoo, galleria, museums). Otherwise than that, everything was perfect! My fiancee and I will definitely be returning.

title: “Not impressed at all”
text: I am here for a work conference and travel frequently and hardly ever write a review but for this hotel I had too. The walls are paper thin, I could hear everything- thankfully I had ear plugs otherwise I never would have slept. I could hear people coming and going all hours of the night- it was horrible especially for the $225 per night price tag for that I would expect so much more! Not to mention their gift shop hours were horrible and it was difficult to just get bottled water except for the couple bottles in the room. If I can to Boston for personal travel I would never stay here!

title: “Nice stay”
text: This hotel deserves the greatest rate available. The location is fantastic, just around the corner in Times Square. The rooms are very nice, elegant and modern. And for whatever need you might have, very kind personnel is ready to assist you. Not to mention every morning a copy of the New York Times will be ready for you in front of your room door. Book with confidence, you won't regret it.

title: “Management makes this the best place to stay!”
text:
I’ve had to wait all this time to write this, as the rule is one cannot post on the same place in less than 90 days between posts.
On 30 May 11, we stayed at the Midway Carlton Inn in Chicago. We’d stayed at the motel a week or two before, and I wrote a glowing report of the motel. The management of the motel is outstanding, as was the service and the cleanliness of the room. We had received first class service the first time and fully expected it again.
So we were astounded at the difference 12 days made. This time, the room wasn’t so clean. This time, we needed to go down to the office to get hand towels. This time, there was no coffee, and the maid had failed to empty the coffee grounds from the last customer. The tub hadn’t been cleaned, indeed, it was clogged, something we didn’t find out until, unfortunately, the water backed up while I was showering. There were hairs a foot long in the tub. I have short hair, and my husband is bald.
So I left the housemaid a tip: a Canadian nickel. I also filled out the comment card, expressing my dismay at the poor cleaning job, the lack of attention to common details, and especially the dirty tub.
The next day, I was home, and received a phone call. I don’t remember her name, but the woman was calling from the Carlton Inn. She had received and read my comments and was appalled. This wasn’t their standard, she said, this was completely out of the ordinary. She apologized profusely, saying the maid was newly hired (and, I hope, considering her lackadaisical approach to doing a simple job like cleaning a room, fired). The woman said that, because of the poor service I’d received, she was going to credit (refund) my money for the cost of the room. She did. For the HIGHER rate.
She asked that I forgive her (as if she were to blame!) and to consider staying with them the next time I was in Chicago.
I was amazed, and mollified. I've seen worse housemaid performance, but was so surprised at the difference. I certainly didn’t expect a refund. But I was definitely impressed, all over again, with the high caliber of service I received from the Carlton Inn. It is apparent to me that the managers of Carlton Midway Inn take high quality service seriously. They pay attention to their customers comments, both good and bad, and act on them as needed. And they do it NOW.
I know they read Trip Advisor. So, I say, 
Yes, ma'am, I promise. The next time we're in Chicago, we will be staying at your Inn. Thank you for your prompt attention to the situation and its rectification. 
 As for folks reading my posts: I suggest you stay there, too.

title: “Very good hotel”
text:
I stayed in the hotel for 8 days. I selected this hotel because of the good reviews. I was especially looking for a quiet hotel, as I'm not a good sleeper, and I was not disappointed. I got a room on the 8th floor, at the 4th Street side; I didn't hear any noise! And the bed was very comfortable. The room was quite spacious, and very clean. The staff at the front desk were very friendly. The location is very good, close to the shopping area, Moscone Center and BART Powell station. My only complaint is about the lobby, which is small and cold. I didn't have dinner at the restaurant. The breakfast was okay, but I prefer a self-service breakfast.
C.K. Jansen, The Netherlands

title: “It's ok...”
text:
Pros: good sized room, big flat screen TV with lots of HD channels, free internet, full sized Starbucks in the lobby, free internet and printer in the lobby
Cons: a little noisy, pillows sucked, free internet is wired only (wireless for a fee), water pressure in shower was pretty poor
Stayed here for a business trip. I stayed at the Westin on 3rd Street a couple of weeks ago but didn't get the same great rate so I decided to check out the Courtyard. 
My room at the Courtyard had some funky noise at night. Some kind of intermittent clunking noise. Not terrible but enough that you notice it when you wake up during the night. 
I had the Goldilocks thing going with the pillows- they were either too flat or too puffy. 
Free internet is wired only. Bring a long ethernet cable if you like to work on your bed. 
To sum up, not a bad place to stay, but I will be checking for the discount rate at the Westin before re-booking at the Courtyard.

title: “Hidden Gem! Great Location, Great Staff, Excelent and Brand New Hotel”
text: Great Location very close to Times Square. Great Staff, anything you ask, they serve you! Wine hour with free wine every day. Very good Room. Perfect Beds.The only bad point is a bit of noise at night when you try to sleep because we're really close to the focus of excitement.

title: “Stay Here!”
text: Aside from the FANTASTIC location (3 blocks from Ford's Theater, the White House and directly across the street from the Metro stop) this place just works. We got a newly remodeled room and I had been sick and was sensitive to the new smell; they changed our room no problems, no questions, very happily. Then a power surge tripped the breaker and our floor had no power for only 30 min but the management was by no means stressed (which calmed me) told us to go to the bar-eat, drink all on them. The service in the bar/lounge is way better than any I have had in a long time- the employees were genuinely nice. Esp if you have children the flavored water (all day) and (yummy!) cookies set out in the lobby is nice to come back to after walking all day sightseeing. You will not be sorry you stayed here. On top of it all is was super-clean.

title: “Superb Hotel with excellent staff”
text: I travel to Washington D.C. on business frequently and about two years ago I discovered the perfect hotel for my stays. The Hotel Madera is a wonderful boutique hotel located just a five minute walk from DuPont Circle. The rooms are always very clean, more space then the average hotel room, and laid out well for work or company. The lobby is sleek and welcoming and they always have free wine between 5 and 7 at night. The Hotel staff is amazing. They are always spotlessly dressed, quick to greet you by name and have you checked in and room key in hand before you can even think twice about it. The Firefly restaurant is attached to the hotel and is an excellent place to eat. Great ambiance, excellent and personable staff with a menu that has something for everyone. The breakfast staff are very good at getting you settled, eating, and out the door to your meetings with ease and feeling pampered.

title: “Enjoyable experience”
text: My family and I stayed at this hotel over the Memorial Day weekend. Overall, we were very pleased. Hotel staff was pleasant, room was ready when we arrived and we had no problems with any type of noise. The room was very nice, beds were really comfortable and the pool and fitness center were also very enjoyable. It was close to the sights and we had a great weekend. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great for short stays”
text: My daughter and I were on our way to Purdue and our flight was going to arrive very late and we decided to stay in Indianapolis before heading north. The price was great at $39 a night and the airport location was wonderful. The hotel is located in a "business park" which was just okay and there is nothing around as far as restaurants or markets. The lobby is nothing special and the common hallways were pretty beat up, but the room was great. it was very nice and had Aveda bathroom products. In all we travelled for one week at four different hotels and this hotel had the Best pillows and hot shower with great water pressure. The free breakfast was very nice, lots of serve yourself choices. I would stay here again, though I would bring food from the airpport or somewhere.

title: “Why You Shouldn't Stay at the Roger Smith”
text:
We all want a hotel that can give us good value for our money. I'm sure you'll agree with me when I say there are some simple elements of a hotel that give it such value. One of which is service - and believe me, I'm a reasonable guy - but the Roger Smith Hotel's service is simply awful, and I want those of you who are thinking about staying here to reconsider.
I took a shuttle to the Roger Smith Hotel one late night. Upon being dropped off, the shuttle driver locked himself out of the van while it was still running - my bags were still in the van, as well. Ok, so a bit of a problem, but with the help of the hotel (because I'm a scheduled 5-night guest) you'd think we could get a locksmith or someone from AAA, etc. The guy working the front desk at the Roger Smith refused to pick up the phone and call for help. He said it had nothing to do with him or the hotel. Unbelievable. Show me some service and flexibility, man. I wasn't asking for the hotel to pay for the locksmith - I just wanted some assistance in finding somebody who could help. Something along the lines of a Yellow Pages search and telephone call on behalf of one of your guests......hotel customer service at the Roger Smith.....non-existent. Keep in mind as well: this was late at night and the front desk was clear of guests and phone calls. Yep, it was frustrating to say the very least.
That's my review. I honestly suggest you think about staying somewhere else - there are plenty to choose from.
I eventually got my bags with the help from someone working at a nearby Enterprise Rent-A-Car.

title: “Well presented but small”
text:
We used this hotel as a base for our first visit to New York along with a number of friends. Initially I was very disappointed with the size of our room. In truth there was very little space bar a path around the bed and with two large bags most of the floor was gone. Not much storage space either for clothes but I suppose that's to be expected of a small hotel like this. The room was very clean and well presented and the toilet/shower room (the wash basin was in the bedroom rather than the bathroom) was well maintained.
Having said all this some of the other couples in our group did get rooms that were much larger so there was an element of luck involved.
There is no bar or restaurant in the hotel but there are plenty of alternatives in the surrounding area and the hotel staff are very accomodating if you want to bring food/drink back in to the two rooms that are used as communal areas. Breakfast consists of cereal, various breads, ham and the usual beverages so is ample. A real selling point was the wine and cheese that was made available in the evening, especially if you are with a group.
As far as location goes it was fine. Only a couple of blocks away from Central Park and the subway so it was a good staging point but it would have been quite a walk to the main attractions in Downtown Manhattan....taxis were the best solution.
So in summary although I was disappointed with the size of the room and the lack of bar/restaurant I really can't fault the cleanliness or the service provided.

title: “Did everything but pack my bags!!!”
text: Exceptional in every way. With a very Large group and friendly, fully engaged staff met all needs, front desk to Internet capacity and power access in ballroom to power up all attendees laptops. Courteous and above the rim performance. Experience superior in every way. NOT A SINGLE GLITCH.

title: “Very Nice”
text: Staff are friendly,rooms are fantastic and great location!

title: “Great”
text: Was clean, good confort staff were really good. God experience and great location. it is very closer from Rockies park you can walk to the park or downtown. Around it you have mcdonalds, dominoes pizza, mexican restaurant, gas station, police station and public bus parade.

title: “Palomar Kimpton Dallas - Great Experience”
text: Stayed one night at the Palomar Dallas Kimpton last week on a business trip from NYC and had a terrific stay. Service was exceptional from check in staff, bartenders, dinner at the hotel's restaurant and especially the hotel service staff who were so accomodating that they went out and bought me a contact lens case when I called down to see if they had that item in their front desk supplies. They didn't carry lens cases so they went and bought me one and it was left in my room and I found it there when I returned from my dinner downstairs. Great experience and exceptional service and glad that they have staff members who care enough to make the extra effort required to make me feel important. Well done.

author.location: NYC York City, New York, USA

title: “Good for us”
text:
A good Motel 6; standard rooms with 2 queen size bed, ideal for family of 2 Adults + 2 kids; nice pool. Good location for visiting Sea World a few miles away. Nearest restauranr, Hunterd, very good but pricey; maybe better to order in pizza if you're on a budget. Would stay again. Note of warning to British visitors - San Diego starts the day overcast, so you forget to put on the sunscreen and wears hats before heading off the Sea World. Ouch !
Would recommend this hotel as a good budget hotel

title: “Diamond in the rough”
text: We found this hotel on the costco travel site. I loved the location and the view of the beach was fabulous. The room was comfortable, plenty of space, clean. I am a light sleeper, and found the room quiet and comfortable. I stayed on the second floor and could see dolphins swimming with the surfers, off our balcony. Just a beautiful vacation. Parking in the free area is difficult with the public, $17 fee for garage. They have added buildings at different times, that is where the extra point goes- it is a maze getting out of the hotel.

title: “If you are not Chinese, this location is exceptionally poor”
text:
Spent three nights here, my friend made the reservations. It is a very clean hotel, with comfortable beds and adequate in-room amenities. $166 per night for room with two double beds during my stay. No coffee maker, no fridge, but instant coffee in the lobby. 
Believe the other reviewers who state that the train noise is problematic -- it is astonishingly loud, even with the good quality, modern, double-paned windows. Pay $20 extra per night for the double-double-bed rooms -- there are only two per floor, they face the street not the train.
While this location is technically Soho (south of Houston St, with central Soho being trendy and filled with cafes and such), THIS HOTEL IS IN THE MIDDLE OF THE DOWNSCALE PART OF CHINATOWN, it is not even the touristy part of Chinatown. There is not a typical convenience store or diner within several blocks in any direction. There is no food other than chinese food for a LOONNNGGG distance in any direction, although a KFC is several blocks away (towards what tourists think of as Chinatown).
The nearest subway station is two LONG blocks away, in the direction away from the nicer part of Chinatown. After dark, the entire neighborhood shuts down because this is a business area, so there is NOTHING to do besides eat at a chinese restaurant. The walk back to the hotel after dark -- particularly at 11pm if you travelled up to Broadway to see a show -- is desolate and creepy. DO NOT try it alone, even though police officers are stationed near the East Broadway station and will offer escort to travelers walking alone, which is a very strong warning that you should heed.
In order to reach any tourist area other than Chinatown, you will have a long ride on the F train, and only the local F stops at the East Broadway station. If everything goes well, and you happen to catch the F quickly, and then catch your connecting train very quickly, you are still going to be AT LEAST 30 - 45 minutes to reach Times Square, Columbus Circle, etc. The time you spend waiting and traveling will leach daylight hours and personal energy out of your vacation, so do not be tempted by a "cheap" hotel rate in this incredibly poor location. If you spend an extra $50 a night to stay in a modest hotel closer to midtown you will make it back on subway fare and cabs that you won't need to take.
Having said that.... if you stay here you will want to bring a cooler for snacks and beverages. There are no bars, cafes, coffee shops for after-dinner drinks or dessert nearby, you will need to provide for yourself in your room. Bring a day pack because once you leave your room you will likely not return until dark - it is just too far. While in more typical areas of the city, remember to stop in a drug or convenience store to buy anything needed -- there are no stores of that type near Hotel 91 and you will be trapped in your hotel after dark unless you arrange for a cab.
Good things nearby: Wonderful dim sum and authentic chinese food 3 - 4 blocks away in the nice/tourist part of Chinatown. Little Italy several blocks away (but not walkable at night, there's another cab ride), lots of inexpensive but good personal services like beauty salons, foot massage/reflexology shops, chinese bakeries with interesting pastries to try. Sadly, that's about it. 
SHOP HARDER AND FIND A SIMILARLY-PRICE HOTEL CLOSER TO MIDTOWN!

title: “Not a good hotel experience”
text: Bathroom smelled of urine. Even after mentioning to staff, no attention to the smell was provided druing our 3 days at the hotel. The carpet was soiled in many places and ants were all over the room. I was particularly frustrated with the indifferent attitude of the staff. Have stayed in at least a dozen hotels in 2010, this was by far the worst experience. I would not recommend this hotel to a friend.

title: “Disappointing Fairmont Washington DC”
text:
Although this hotel is grand, and service is perfect, it does not measure up to other Fairmont hotels I have been at in several ways. I am on the fourth day of a six day business trip here:
Towels every day were threadbare. TV was small (14 inch) in a b attered cabinet whose doors did not fold back, making walking past impossible. Provided wobbly make up mirror with poor maginfication, and no where to sit in the bathroom to use it. Bathroom water pressure poor. Bathroom had no fan. Bathroom had useless TV sound button
Pillows were comfortable, bed was hard. Room was dingy. no clock some lamps didin't work
The location of th ehotel is perfect, quick walk to Georgetown and surrounding neighborhood was safe to walk in. Many tourists and business people.
Hotel needs an upgrade in many things to bring to standards of other Fairmonts.

title: “not a good choice”
text:
This hotel was not a nice place to stay and here is why:
1. The staff is not helpful. The day before we were to leave I asked if they had an alarm I could borrow-since there are no phones in the room a wake up call was not an option. They said 'no', they didn't have one. But, they could give a wake-up knock on the door. I scheduled one for 5:00am. Luckily I woke up on my own at 4:45 (not difficult as the constant sirens and traffic that you hear throughout the night make it difficult to sleep in the first place) because they never came to for the wake-up knock. When I went downstairs to check out no one was there. The phone was ringing, I called out 'hello' but no answer. I waited 15 minutes in the lobby before a man came out from a room behind the front desk rubbing sleep from his eyes. When I asked him about the wake up knock he said, 'I don't see no wake up knock here'. So, then I said to him, we also scheduled a ride to the airport yesterday for 5:30 am to the airport (something they offer for $45. Oh, he didn't have that written down either. Luckily there was another sleeping man that woke up and came out so he was able to drive us for the $45.
2. The place is dingy. The walls are dirty and EVERYTHING squeeks, I guess they've never heard of WD40. The blinds are dirty and broken.
3. The bed is one of the most uncomfortable beds I've ever slept on. And, it is a full, not even a queen. It has a plastic sheet underneath the the sheet-I guess they are worried about guests wetting the bed??? You can feel the springs.
4. It is very noisy.
5. The room is TINY. Barely enough room to walk around. Sink is in bedroom since there is no room in the bathroom for it. The bathroom is so small that you can touch elbow to elbow in the shower, and when you get out of the shower you practically step in the toilet.
6. The water temperature in the shower was the worst, it did not stay consistent for more than 5-10 seconds-then it went from scorching hot to freezing cold.
I do not recommend staying at this place.

title: “Not the best experience”
text: Stayed here three nights, minor complaint were that sheets on the bed were worn through, there were a lot of dogs in the hotel. What sent me away was realizing that the back door lock was broken, so there was open access into the hotel. I mentioned it to the front desk, but it was not repaired during my stay.

title: “Peace and quiet!”
text:
Stayed for a few days wiin August. Didn't use many of the facilities, the bar looked nice and the gymn adequate. Main focus was the room - very comfortable with good facilities, and so quiet and peaceful at night, completely isolated from the chaos that is Manhattan. Very rarely slept so well in the middle of a big city!
Location is a big plus - easy walking distance to Central Park, Time Square etc, shoppers will love being so close to 5th Avenue. Quite a distance to best nightlife, but the taxis are cheap and plentiful. One of the nicest rooftop bars, at the Peninsula Hotel, is just down the street
Some very minor quibbles aside - the lifts are slow and cramped, and I was told the cab they booked me to the airport would take credit cards when it didn't - this is a great place, highly recommended if you value location and a good night's sleep

title: “Affinia Shelburne”
text:
This hotel was the best priced 4* hotel I could find and I certainley was not disappointed. It is located in Lexington Avenue quite close to Grand Central Station so it is easy to get around to all the main places.
The hotel is newly refurbished so is clean and modern and was by far the most up to date in comparison with other hotels we popped in to.
The staff were really freindly and helpful and I would definately recommend this hotel to others.

title: “True Luxury Hotel”
text:
My partner and I spent four comfortable nights at the InterContinental San Francisco. We booked the room via Hotwire and secured an amazing rate. I have stayed at several InterContinental Hotels via Hotwire and always experienced a warm welcome and outstanding service. This stay was no different. 
Upon check-in, the front desk clerk informed us that we had been upgraded to a deluxe king room. Our spacious room was located on the twenty-seventh floor and featured floor to ceiling windows with a view of the port, freeway, and some lovely hillside neighborhoods. The king bed was sumptuously comfortable, so comfortable in fact that we lay down for a nap and ended up sleeping fifteen hours. The room also featured a sitting area, and flat screen TV. The large bathroom contained high-end toiletries and fine towels. The decor of the room, with its muted earth tones and tile work in the bathroom, was a soothing respite from the busy city below.
Service was friendly and efficient from check-in to check-out. We awoke early each morning and left the hotel for breakfast. Our room was always made when we returned an hour or two later. 
My one complaint about the hotel is that the restaurants and gift shop are terribly overpriced. A twenty ounce Coke at the gift shop cost $4.00. We would have liked to have sampled the bar and restaurant, but could not justify paying the outrageous prices.
Overall, the InterContinental provides luxury accommodations and attentive service in a convenient San Francisco location. We would gladly return.

title: “Comfortable”
text:
My stay at the Four Points Sheraton Lax was most accomodating, the entire hotel staff from check-in to parking service were very helpful, personable, courteous, and most all, always provided me service with a smile. My room was very comfortable, cleaned everyday ,and unlike many hotels, they provided their guest with a free bottle of water without a price tag attached, I thought that was an additional highlight to my stay, because I love to drink water and think it is very tacky that some hotels charge a guest for such a necessary element. 
The hotel is less than 5 minutes away from the LAX; not too far from other locations such as Manhattan Beach, Venice Beach, Santa Monica, and many other locations. 
I really like the Starwood program the hotel brand offers, because during your stay, you have the advantage of earning points for everything from room service, movies, parking and etc. I had no dislikes, everything was fine.

title: “Nice”
text: Nice, but the elevator was painfully slow - and crowded. No concierge on duty on a Sunday.

title: “Westin standard upheld-a find during the Boston marathon weekend”
text:
Booked via PL for 180$ for one night (Boston marathon weekend oblige)...and overall, it was a good deal. Early check-in was possible, and we managed to get a room with 2 beds...we were relieved!
The room itself was quite nice and roomy, with 2 very comfortable queen beds, LCD TV, work station, 12.95 $ for low grade wifi (hi speed is 18$...a bit of a rip off in this day and age), good sized bathroom with toiletries and bathrobe (only one, which we did not use), and a rather unspectacular view (well, its a PL booking).
The hotel is a bit out of the way, but close to World Trade Centre Silver line station (a bit more than 5 minutes walk) which connects to South Station and red line. We did walk to the Park Plaza and other locations, on a gorgeous day. Warning, Silver Line to airport is rather crowded during the day, and expect delays...count at least an hour.
Did not use the restaurant, nor the Starbucks, because of the marathon crowd. The gym is very well equipped but was very crowded, the pool was OK (I guess marathoners don't use pools cause it was me and another person swimming), but looking like a cheaper house version, with vinyl cloth lining...bizarre metallic Jacuzzi which did not work.
Overall, a pleasant stay...would come back with right price.

title: “Great place to stay in Chicago”
text:
I recently stayed for 4 nights and cant fault the hotel.
The Suites are very big and have everything you will need , comfortable beds and 2 big tv's with plenty if channels .
I had a very good rate and this includes a full breakfast , eggs any style cooked to order , suasage bacon biscuits n gravy toasts cereals etc etc 
Also the managers reception which I did not attend but includes drinks and snacks 5.30pm until 7.30pm every night.
Locatiopn is great near a nice supermarket that also has beer and wine and 3 blocks from Michigan Ave.
I would say that some of the front desk staff could vertainly be friendlier however that aside I would stay again

title: “Would not return”
text: We were rerouted to the Ritz Carlton from another hotel that had been overbooked for our conference. Upon arriving at the check in counter, the clerk was sullen & unwelcoming. He was clearly irritated when I asked whether a king sized bed was available rather than 2 doubles. He seemed even further irritated that I asked for 2 keys for the room after he had given me one. The staff we dealt with at check out was polite, however. The bellmen were very friendly and the room was clean but ordinary. It was not what I would have expected from a Ritz-Carlton.

title: “No views”
text: The George is well-run, guiet, clean and comfortable. The food is good. The problem with the hotel from my point of view is that most of the rooms look right out into other rooms. As a consequence one keeps their blinds down all the time. If this does not matter to you, the hotel is a good choice because everythng else is fine.

title: “Comfortable Stay”
text: I am surprised that there are some bad reviews here. We stayed 2 nights for a 50th High School Reunion and found it to be a really nice place to stay. The bar in the main room is a great gathering place with friendly service. The ballroom used for our dinner/dance was nice and spacious. Also the buffet that was provided by the Sol restaurant on-site had delicious food. Now...about the room, we had room #130, which had it's good points and bad points. The good - a clean spacious room, close to the lobby with a king bed and flat screen tv. Also, it had very good high speed internet reception. The bad - because this is a room that is inside, there are no outdoor windows, so we had a noisy fan beside the bathroom. It took some getting used to, but since we were enjoying the reunion at the same hotel, we didn't complain. If we stay another time, we would probably not want this specific room, but one similar that is not in the corner near any noisy equipment.

title: “Very nice pet-friendly hotel - loved the Happy Hour & Breakfast”
text:
The drinks / snacks at happy hour, pet friendly atmosphere, excellent staff, and overall clean room make the Drury a good value - despite the higher price.
Stayed last year with our dog and couldn't have been happier. The pool and hot tub were great (there's an outdoor "swim under" area that was refreshing in November). The breakfast and happy hour alone make up for the extra price you'll pay to stay. The room was nice but no view really to speak of and was a little loud. It was mostly clean, although we had a water issue by the bathroom door that we never reported, we just kept towels on it to keep it dry.
While they may need to do some maintenance in the room(s), the amenities are abound, and you'll have a great stay.

title: “Clean, comfortable, great location, but a bit smelly and noisy!”
text: We arrived at the hotel mid afternoon and check in was quick and easy, staff were polite and friendly, as they were throughout the whole stay. Our room was small but big enough, there was plenty of storage room and a clean but small bathroom. The decor was clean and modern. The location was seen, walking distance to all of the main attractions and sights. The only issues we had were noise, smell and temperature. It can be noisy on a weekend as it is right above a bar. There was also an awful smell, I suspect it was sewage from the drains outside, this lasted for the whole of our stay but there were workers around who seemed to be trying to fix the problem. The room was also cold at night, our bed was right beneath two windows and it was really drafty. We also didn't receive room service once during our stay, this wasn't a problem as we just asked when we needed clean towels etc but I expect to receive room service at least once in a 7 night stay. Despite the little issues we really enjoyed our stay here, the great location, security, free Internet and tv were great and if we returned to Philadelphia we would be sure to stay again.

title: “Customer Service”
text: When making my reservation at The Mark there were some difficulties getting our reservation but, Julita was very helpful in getting it straightened out. I cannot express to anyone how great she is at her job because without her assistance it would not have been possible for us to stay at the hotel. We need more people like her that demonstrate great Customer service. During our stay she also helped us by answering any question we had about the city and all the shows,shopping, and fine dining. The room service at The Mark is also outstanding and it is a beautiful hotel I would highly recommend to anyone and Thank you again Julita for your hard work and outstanding customer service you made our experience wonderful.

title: “Simply heavenly!”
text: After touring around the western coast of America, San Fransisco was our final stop. My boyfriend and I booked our stay at The Westin St. Francis months in advance at the very begining of the year. Our first impressions were very good - the lobby was fantastic, very grand!! However our joy was short lived. Upon reaching the check in desk we were informed that the hotel had been over booked and there were no rooms available for us, and they had booked us in at a hotel opposite. We had been given no prior notice of this rearrangement - and personally I think that because my boyfriend and I were not business clients, we were consequently down graded. We were assured that our 2nd and 3rd nights stay would be back at the Westin St. Francis however, and that we would be refunded for our first night in the alternative hotel. On arriving at this hotel it was clearly apparent that the two hotels were not of the same class or splendour, and although we agreed to the new arrangement we later returned to the Westin to voice our displeasure. To be honest the staff were very apologetic, and the reception manager explained that we were also going to be given an upgraded room when we returned the following day. We were not disappointed - we were booked in as Preferred Guests, and were given an absolutley fantastic room on the 26th floor of the tower building with an amazing view of the city. The bed was king size, and pillows and bedding were heavenly!! The duel headed shower made a very relaxing shower, and we were provided with bath robes, and gorgeous toiletries! On our arrival we were also sent up a letter of apology for our troubles, accompnied by a bottle of chilled champagne, strawberries, and a box of chocolates!! It would seem that it was worth the whole initial disappointment! Breakfast was also very good, although a little expensive at $50 including tax for a breakfast buffet for 2 people. The hotel itself is in a great location, with the cable car stop just outside. There are also plenty of shops in the surrounding area, and lots of great bars and restaurants near by. We would definately stay at this hotel again - the view from our window was worth every penny!!

title: “Don't Listen to Negative Reviews - This Place is Fine!”
text: I give this an excellent review just for the value alone. Where else can you stay for $79 a night, right near everything! And free Wi-fi! This hotel provides maximum value for the money. It isn't a 5 star hotel but you can't beat it for the location and cost. I stayed here last week and enjoyed my stay. The front desk staff was friendly. The hotel is old but well maintained and clean. They accommodated my request for a room in the rear of the building and it was quiet. The bed was comfortable and the view from the 6th floor window was wonderful! The immediate area is a bit lacking but once you walk a few blocks you 're in a great part of town. Right near downtown! I think people who give this hotel a bad review are expecting the Hilton or Ritz. You aren't going to get that but you will get great value for the money!

title: “Kinda Cool...”
text: This place is in a great location. The rooms are huge. It is a refurbished historic property. It is really well kept and kind of funky at the same time. It is quite charming. (Bring a 3 prong adaptor if you want to hook up your laptop. Plugs are few and there are not 3 prong plugs.

title: “Great base in DC!”
text: We have just stayed at this excellent hotel for 5 nights. Rooms are beautiful and exceptionally clean (building is newly renovated), beds are the best we have ever slept in! Great breakfast that fills you up for the busy day ahead and you can look forward to fresly baked cookies when you return in the evening. Very good location, within walking distance of all the local sites. Staff (especially Raj) are very warm, friendly and helpful including the hotel manager Mario who goes out of his way to welcome you and make you feel at home. Would not hesitate to stay here again and would recommend it to anybody..

title: “Good Stay”
text: Stayed at Crown Plaza on business trip to Denver. Must compliment the friendly and helpful staff. We were very jet lagged on arrival and decided to have a quick snack in the lobby bar. The barman was extremely friendly and upbeat. What a difference this makes. All the staff with the exception of a surly room maid were outstanding. When travelling on business I like to feel secure and they certainly lived up to expectations. Well done Crown Plaza.

title: “What a great hotel!”
text: Spent 4 nights at the Affinia Shelburne and loved it. Newly rennovated with the Affinia name. The rooms are very spacious (I was in the 1 bdrm suite). The roof top bar is lovely, music in lobby is hip, overall great experience. Be sure to check out My Affinia to select the aminities that are most important to you. I chose my pillow and yoga kit, at no additional cost. Would stay here again in a heart beat!

title: “Small but comfortable rooms, exceptionaly helpful staff”
text:
This is my second year staying at the Serrano. Whilst some rooms are a little tired around the edges, they are always spotlessly clean and the beds are really comfortable. Only a very short walk from Union Square, so you almost get the location, but you certainly don't get the price tag.
If you are coming and going during the day and want a coffee - the nearest Starbucks is in the Hilton just across the intersection, and there is a great little breakfast place just down the road to the right after you cross the street. We didn't eat at Ponzu this year after our experiences last year.
The only problem I do have with this hotel - and it has not changed since last year - is that because of the very large (and impressive) floor to ceiling front doors opening on an sensor system that keeps them open for quite a while after guests pass through, the lobby does get cold. This is only really a problem if you wait for other guests in the lobby or stay for the wine hour. And the only additional gripe during that hour is that there simply are not enough seats for everyone.
That said, I would stay here again in a heartbeat. The staff fall over themselves to be helpful, and with the added bonus of free wifi and $10 voucher for the mini bar - why would you stay elsewhere?

title: “Sofitel continues to deliver”
text:
The Davoodas stayed at Sofitel Water Tower Memorial Day weekend in a junior suite. It was our 4th stay at this marvelous hotel that we have come to think of as "home" more so than any of the other upscale hotels where we've stated. The staff are most professional and friendly, the accommodations high-quality and the location is hard to beat. 
We arrived about 12:30 pm, left the car with the valet and the luggage with the bellman. However, Mrs. D wanted to put her jewelry in the hotel safe. Alas, since the Sofitel has safes in each room, it does not have a lobby safe. But, the Director of Security offered the use of his personal lockbox behind the lobby of the hotel, which we gladly used. We spent the remainder of the day shopping. The Front Desk staff called me on my cell when our room was ready to occupy. They had fulfilled our request for a high-floor room with a view of the city. 
While the rooms are still easy on the eyes, I think it's time for a rehab/redecoration. There were some small stains on the carpet in our room and some marks on the trim and walls, and the piping on the edge of the black leather lounge chair in our suite was worn white - nothing to be upset about but at a four-star hotel, I expect better.
We had loved the Sofitel beds in past visits but the one in this room has seen better days. We both awakened with sore backs due to the soft bedding and lack of support. Also, I found it odd the bed lacked a top sheet - I would have sworn there were top sheets on our prior visits. We liked being able to 
Le Bar - what can one say...excellent drinks (generous pours) in pleasant surroundings and a tray of marinated olives and crisps to nibble while imbibing! We sat outside because the weather was so nice and service was excellent inside our out.
We did not dine at Cafe des Architects, but did enjoy a room -service breakfast that was very good and delivered on time and hot. I really liked the Sofitel coffee, but was disappointed when the croissants served to us were too dry. Mrs. D liked her omelet and my yogurt/berry parfait was delicious and cold.
Check-out was seamless and our car was awaiting delivery of our luggage and shopping bags.
Merci beaucoup, Sofitel!

title: “Clean, modern hotel w/very friendly staff”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 7 nights over 3 weeks for business. From checking in after 7pm each of the 3 weeks, to ordering dinner from their Guest Kitchen, to the free continental breakfast in the morning and free newspapers, this hotel made for a pleasant and comfortable stay. The staff is very friendly, and their response to just about any "Thank you" received is, "My pleasure". While small, the hotel is modern and comfortably appointed, both the lobby and guest rooms. I had to stay in a King Accessible a couple of nights because they were overbooked on standard Kings, which I really don't understand since the hotel was nowhere near being full...sounds like they need more Kings! It's a crap shoot on the A/C you'll get in your room: all are window units, but some are digital and others are old style turn knobs; some work better (and are less noisy) than others. As mentioned by others, the free continental breakfast is quite good with a nice selection of items - waffiles would be a good addition. The Guest Kitchen, as it's called, is open 24/7 (I believe) and you can order anything from sandwiches, wraps and burgers, to nachos and pizza. I must say I didn't try anything but the wraps and burger - the former are much better than the latter. They also offer free wi-fi, which is unusual amongst hotels in general - especially ones of this size and price point; it was a very nice bonus while traveling for business. All in all this is definitely one of the better small hotels I've stayed at due to the modern, comfortable decor, above average food (for a hotel of its size), and very service oriented staff who are happy to do whatever they can to make your stay comfortable and efficient. Although there are several other hotel options nearby, I would stay at the Hyatt Place again.

title: “You get what you pay for”
text: My wife and I are on a 7 week holiday around the southern states and needed affordable accommodation in locations that allowed us to get around without a car. This hotel was in a good location as it was 5 mins to nearest bus stop, and 20 mins to trains ( although these dont run that often), plus there are quite a few restaurant/eating options around the area ( Japanese, Chilli's, Denny's, BK). The lobby looks impressive, the rooms are spacious but a bit outdated. My main complaints would be very poor drainage in the shower, which meant you showered in an inch or so of water at your feet, the internet reception in our room didnt work ( it did work in the lobby though) and there was no breakfast. But for the price it was still reasonable.

title: “Perfect location! I loved it!”
text: Great hotel in the best location in NYC! It took a little while for me to get used to the fact that the lobby was not on the ground floor, but that was really no big deal. The service was excellent, and I just love the fact that it is right in the middle of Times Square! It will always be my #1 choice whenever I am in NY.

title: “What a view”
text:
We stayed here twice now. First time with a regular room on 17th floor overlooking the river, so nice, it was June, great location, close to miles of indoor walking malls/shops. Boston has Starbucks everywhere. river and boston harbour area
Just finished a 7 day stay on Friday, upgraded to a larger corner room on 29th floor, corner room overlooking, had 180 degree view of the city, beds were wonderful, "heavenly bed" ahh. plenty of places to find to eat, close by and in the hotel. 
great place to walk, have to say i did not like the taxis, always seemed expensive, grumpy drivers, underground tunnels left me thinking they were hiking up the fare taking longer routes on purpose, walking was always fun, brisk area, beautiful skies.
Westin Copely staff always friendly and helpful. We will stay here whenever in Boston

title: “Join Presidents Club!”
text: We recently earned premier status in the President's Club. What a great loyalty program! When we arrived, managers informed us they had read our on-line reviews of other Fairmont properties and hoped we would have a nice stay in D.C. We then were able to use our certificates for a room and suite upgrade. What a beautiful suite! The location is very convenient as within walking distance to Georgetown. As a premier member, you can also ask for the Lexus service which can bring you to some sites as well as the metro stop.

title: “Tired and worn out”
text: Hotel is tired and worn out. Everything is old. The bed sagged in the middle and was the most uncomfortable I have been since I last went camping and slept in a sleeping bag on the ground. I asked for an upgrade upon arrival and was told immediately no, as they were expecting a big crowd that night. I saw two people in the lobby during my entire night's stay. There is no room service. The view was nice but the only reason to stay here would be the incredible location.

title: “Convenience is the Key”
text: This Holiday Inn Express is located a few short blocks away from the Stadiums and almost adjacent to the location for the new Harrah's Casino (yet to be built). Great deal for those cruising from Baltimore, overnight stay, breakfast, shuttle to/from port AND park your car there while you're away, for LESS than the price of parking at the pier. Shuttle also available to take you to the Inner Harbor for dinner/shopping. On the downside, some rooms are fairly noisy from highway traffic noise.

title: “Spend a few more bucks & find something cleaner”
text: Front desk was ok, cleaning staff were fine, but the owner of this place, does not care to take pride in ownership. Mold in the bathroom, hair dryer falling apart with electrical wires hanging out, lamp shades melted from light bulb. The most amazing thing we saw was on the front window after 2 nights, this building may cause cancer, pregnant women should not be near this place. Why didint the front desk tell us about this we dont know. Looking through other pictures people have posted on this place, the piece of paper warning about this cancer causing building is there, taped to front window.

title: “Superb”
text:
I only have good things to say about our stay here. The hotel is one block away from Times Square, so the location is superb. There is an entrance to the subway (blue line A,C and E) just a few steps away from the lobby.
The rooms are a good size for NY hotels, modern and bright (15th Fl) and the bathroom is spacious too. The bathroom was well stocked with towels and amenities.
Room service was quick, accurate and efficient and all the staff throughout the hotel were friendly.
I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Hotel/Modern Ammenities”
text: You can't go wrong at this hotel. Great location, service, etc. I had a room problem at check-in. The front desk person was giving me the boilerplate on not being able to accommodate what had already been promised and noted. Five minutes after going to the less desirable room, management called and rectified the matter. This is an excellent, NYC hotel with professional, experienced staff, from the doormen to the restaurant staff.

title: “Chic, comfortable, convenient”
text: My stay at The Orchard was delightful, and I'd likely choose it again for my next SF visit. The room was very pleasant, fresh, and quiet, despite being in the downtown area. Bed was super comfy, and the bathroom spacious. Plush robes await in the closets. Breakfast room also very pleasant, though the service was slow (perhaps because a large group came in from outside the hotel for some celebration). Just a couple blocks from Union Square. For the environmentally conscious, you'll be pleased to find it's a "Green" hotel.

title: “Great location, good value for NYC”
text: This was our first family trip to NYC and this hotel was a pleasant surprise. Easy walk to Penn Station. Front desk staff very friendly and helpful. The rooms are small but clean and nicely appointed. For one night, it was okay for a family of four, all adult-size. More than two nights, I'm not sure. For the location and the price, it is truly a bargain. I could have gotten two rooms here for the price of one elsewhere and been very comfortable. Probably 5 on Value, but is there a 5 in New York City?

title: “Fantastic hotel experience”
text: The Sir Francis Drake hotel proved an excellent experience. Their customer service is exceeded only by the accommodations, including very comfortable beds. If I had to pick one "con" it would be the size of the rooms, but that is to be expected in large city hotels. Highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Happy New Year”
text: We stayed at the Clarion for New Year 2003-2004. The hotel was excellent. The staff were fantastic and so was the location. The only down side was the room size, although we cannot complain. The rooms were clean and a sufficient base for our stay. The bar/restaurant (the salmon river) which is part of the hotel was superb. Excellent food and drink made our stay in New York that extra lttle special.

title: “Wonderful Anniversary Weekend At Hyatt Mccormack Place Chicago”
text:
My wife and I recently celebrated our 40th wedding anniversary and what better a city to do that in than Chicago. We booked using Priceline and got a favourable rate. I contacted the hotel to advise them that this was a special occasion for us and inquired if an upgrade would be possible.
On check-in we were greeted by "Happy Anniversary...we have upgraded you to a suite." Music to our ears. And what a suite...it had about 1,000 sq. ft. about the size of a small condo. The view of Chicago's shoreline was amazing. The staff...each and every one went out of their way to be helpful.
We used valet parking which was a bit steep at $38. per day but the valet service was both prompt and curteous. One last thing about the hotel...their bar on the main level was warm and welcoming for a nightcap.
Several days we did not use the car at all. No problem, the #3 bus stops right in front of the hotel and runs right up Michigan Ave. to most key tourist attractions. During the week service is very frequent...less so on weekends. You can get a travel pass for unlimited Chicago Transit Authority travel for use on both busses and subway. Using the subway...red line involves a non user friendly walk to/from the subway station. The #3 bus is a much better bet.
Two suggestions for visitors who may not have visited this wonderful city in a long time...1. Tave the Architectural River Cruise- great. 2. Have dinner at Old Town Brasserie - the food, service, and piano player were all great. Super wine list as well.
Hope you enjoy as much as we did.

title: “DC Hilton on Connecticut Ave is great!”
text:
My husband and I checked into the Washington Hilton 3/28/12 and checked out 4/1/12. We were visiting DC to attend a funeral at Arlington National Cemetery, visiting friends who live in Georgetown, and family with a recent college grad still in DC. We loved the hotel! Very lively common areas in the lobby on the open plan, large high tables with outlets to take advantage of free wifi in lobbly, comfortable seating, bar and restaurant areas that blend into the lobby, large containers of ice water, with macerated mint, lemon, orange, pomegranate right by the front door, inviting coffee shop with healthy food and comfortable seating, lots of flat screen tvs.
We arrived on Wed at 10;00 PM., lobby crowded with attractive young people. 
Staff: every staff person I encountered made eye contact and greeted me! a great touch!
Outdoor patio: Outstanding! beautifully constructed, pavers, furniture, fire pits, bar service if you want it, large (for a city!!) perennial garden, loved it!
Room was quite small but I thought well designed.
