Bottom part of window opened for fresh air, lots of electrical outlets, lighted magifying mirror that could be moved, I liked the storage drawers in the vanity, liked the conservation of water and lighting that was evident. Armchair, ottoman and desk chair very comfortable. 
We have stayed in many hotels in DC over the past ten years, and while this is a big conference hotel, we loved it! Great location, very intelligent design, great vibe! We will be back!

title: “not the best but ok”
text: stayed here for 3 nights as a base to see New York.not a freindly welcome arrived at midday and was told to come back after 4pm asked if there was somewhere to leave our cases told yes but would have to pay.room was clean, tidy but basic no extras i:e coffee-tea facilities

title: “Middle of the road - better options in the area”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights in November, it was an OK hotel at best.
The rooms were very small, mine didn't have a desk. There was no sundries store (you had to walk to a nearby Walgreens), the mini-bar was one of those that charges you instantly if you remove something, so if you want to read a bottle of vitamin water, you get charged, the TV was mediocre, the phone didn't work, and there was no wired Internet connection. Internet services is $9.95 a night (via tMobile). Room service menu is very very limited.
The best thing about the hotel is the location in the heart of union square, about 5 blocks from Moscone. The sky bar is pretty nice as well, but next time I'll stay at the Hilton.

title: “Four Seasons Baltimore”
text: This was my first time staying at this Four Seasons property. The experience was Truly Exceptional! The attention to detail in the room, the front desk, all the staff I interacted with, far exceeded my expectation. If Baltimore is on your travel plans soon, I Highly recommend this property.

title: “Good place for those on a budget”
text:
I just got back from my round-the-world holiday so I thought I'd submit a review on the Castle Inn. I stayed there in April with my girlfriend.
On arrival it's one of those places where you're thinking "oh dear, what did I book?"
However once settled you see this hotel for what it's worth.
First the positives:
* The rooms are quite large. We had a double bed and there was a desk, television, wardrobe and bedside tables.
* The shower was fantastic, if a little confusing to figure out the first time. Plenty of water pressure and hot water. 
* Marshall in the front desk was really helpful with directions and telling us where to go in San Fran. He also drew an area on the map and told us not to go there (Tenderloin). The only downside was he was suffering from an ear infection when we were there so he was a bit grumpy.
* The location is fantastic, especially for budget travellers who need facilities like laundromats and internet (both are within a two minute walk of the hotel). Marshall also gives you a sheet explaining all the main attractions and how to access them via bus/tram. This piece of paper was my bible for the week. What a great idea!
There were a couple of negatives:
* Our room was facing the street and it can get a bit noisy in the early hours. I kept getting woken up by drunk guys stumbling home.
* Also, we came back to our room at around midday one day to find a couple of workmen in our room changing the blinds. We weren't warned that this was going to happen so we were a bit disappointed (especially since we weren't gone long so we left our valuables there). Let me stress that nothing went missing though, and the workmen were very apologetic for their intrusion.
Still, I'd recommend this hotel. It can be a bit daunting when selecting a hotel in San Francisco, particularly with all the hullaballoo about the dangers of the Tenderloin. If you in any way concerned about that, stay here. It's a nice part of town with nice eateries within five minutes walk.

title: “Highly recommended!”
text: After dropping our daughter off for a Boston Ballet summer intensive we "stumbled" upon this hotel after asking someone at Boston University for a restaurant recommendation in the neighborhood. We ended up at Eastern Standards, well above our standards, which, I can assure you, are are pretty high. We found out that the restaurant was connected to a hotel and decided to check it out. We were immediately impressed with the friendliness of the staff and the beautiful lobby. We decided to cancel our reservations at a chain hotel for when we were going to pick up our daughter and, at the same price we would have paid at the chain, we ended up in a beautiful, spacious room, overlooking Commonwealth Avenue (only down point: no coffee maker in the room). The hotel is steps away from Fenway Park, but even on we dind't hear a thing because of the well insulated, sound proof windows. We had dinner at Eastern Standard and Island Creek Oysters, both outstanding in food and service and so convenient. This will definitely be our hotel of choice whenever we stay in Boston!

title: “Fab-U-lous”
text: i was a tad nervous about staying at this hotel after some of the reviews i had read before hand. i had no problem checking in, and getting to our room. the elevator is tad small (older style with link door) but that just added to the feel to the hotel! the room are small as well. but enough rooms to keep your suitcase in, and freshen up throughout the day (you dont want to be in a hotel all day in new york city anyways!). there is a sink and a mirror in the room, as well as a tv. i also sneaked wireless internet off a neighbouring building *haha* also the SHARED washroom wasnt bad. clean showers, never waited to use one of the 2 washrooms on the floo. overall fabulous stay from feb. 10-13th, and would definitely stay again.

title: “Grand Hyatt San Antonio for the Woman's NCAA Tourament April 1st-7th 2010”
text: Well I excepted the rooms to a lot larger then they were. Make sure you book a Guest room with a King size bed an pay the lower price there were no extra draw space for two people were had to call housekeeping to get more hangers for are clothes. Because the Grand King room is the same size as a Guest room I'm was told once I check in and had already unpacked my stuff. Very miss leading on there website and when I called and talked to the front desk. Do upgarade to use the Grand Clud Level, this alouds you to use there VIP room on the 23rd floor, Breakfast, late afternoon snack and desserts from 8pm-10pm soads water juices. Beer and wine and mix drinks you do have to pay for by charging it to your room. Cheaper then getting it in there bar downstairs. Sorry but Grand Hyatt San Antonio does nt have a real gift shop. The restuarant food is pretty good, they have such a small selection for lunch and dinner, Wlak alonng the Riverwalk the have plenty of places to eat and sports bars and shopping. The Riverwalk Mall is on the otherside on the Marroitt right across the street and the Almo a couple blocks from there. If you like to walk everything is within walking distance. Room 2419 had a nice view, but there must been a problem with the water pressure I complained twice but no one at the front desk did a thing.

title: “Location is for Night Life”
text: We stayed at Wyndam Harbour Lights in December 2011. Overall, the hotel is clean and the staff was very helpful. The rooms are large in size and the decor was pleasant. However, at night the area is very loud. You can hear the party crowd well into the early mornings on the weekends. This hotel is located right in downtown San Diego - so in the mornings you will find homeless people sleeping on the streets and the smell from the night before can be over whelming. If you’re looking for a quiet location this isn't it, but if you’re interested in night life the Harbour Lights is in a prime location.

title: “Closest Hotel to the Convention Center”
text:
This was the "Official" hotel for our recent convention. The staff couldn't have been friendlier. The rooms were well appointed, but not exceptionally large. The common areas were elegant. The bar was swanky & hopping. The pool wasn't anything special, but the fitness area was nice.
I sent myself a package there, to avoid a carry-on fee from the Airlines. They charged me $20 to sign for it. I suppose that's standard, but it seemed a tad high.
If you're going to the convention center often, this is the place to stay. If you're going for the River-walk....I'd stay closer to the action.

title: “convenient, clean, friendly, good breakfast, some traffic noise”
text:
Stayed for three nights 4th-6th September 2009. Overall thought it was good. very convenient. Although parking is $20 +tax per day it was convenient to park (the ramp is steep so keep the speed down) and they kept a parking spot for us when we got back late one evening which was great. There is limited if no other convenient parking alternatives. Breakfast was good.
At night at the weekend the road is busy with concert traffic so there is some noise( I guess depends where your room is) and the aircon is too loud to keep on during the night ( like it cool at night) but to be honest I would stay there again.

title: “Lovely service from Antonio Torres”
text:
Stayed a week at the Westin while on business. The rooms were good, if a tad on the old side, as another reviewer mentioned. However, that didn't deter from my experience and I thought overall the service was pretty good. 
Particularly would like to mention the service I received during breakfast from Antonio. He remembered me and knew exactly what I wanted, from tea and water during breakfast, to coffee to go for after. I definitely felt like I was looked after and welcome. He's a gem and definitely made for a good experience!
-Christina

title: “Felt like home”
text: We stayed for 11 nights so it really did feel like home. Easy check in, Larry was very helpful to ask for advice on broadway shows, saw Wicked, oh how good it was. The queen x 2 deluxe room on 12 was very nice, and strangely quiet even on facing 8th. The Olympic diner across the street is a must for cheap hearty breakfast, and rather cool being my first real diner experience. It's true u can walk everywhere and the subway is easy. If your young or young at heart, find Johnny Utahs and ride their mechanical bull it's a hoot. I want to come back here soon.

title: “excellent stay”
text:
I stayed at Ritz Carlton Central Park for the first time and it is a truly excellent property and location, location, location! Our stay was absolutely terrific for 4 days being the 4th free. We arrived at about 12 pm, but this was not a problem for the hotel at all, our room on the highest floor with spectacular view of Central Park was already ready and waiting for us. There were no problems at all, staff was happy to help at any moment. The stuff in the executive Lounge was absolutely amazing, pleasant, and so polite, which really made our stay very special. We stayed 4 days before US OPEN and even met a boy in executive lounge every day there that was later singing OUR NATIONAL ANTHEM during the opening ceremony which we watched on TV on the day we returned home.
Our Deluxe room was well appointed, very spacious and luxuriously equipped. The interiors are designed in a very tasteful, classic fashion and, of course, impeccably clean. The Bathroom décor is outstanding and nice size with tons of marble.
We have stayed at top properties and this one may be quit pricy for some, but my wife dreamed of staying in the hotel on the highest possible floor with the view of Central Park in its entirety and unobstructed view and she couldn’t have chosen a better property to have her dream come true. Seeing her happy means a world to me. Ritz’s reputation and experience makes this hotel one of a kind. We have nothing but great memories of our stay.
There were no problems at all, staff was happy to help at any moment. During checkout we were asked about our stay, we were so attached to our life style at Ritz that we didn’t want to live and my wife shed a happy tear. Check out clerk went around the counter to give her a hug and we exchange sweet words which made us all happy.
Would stay again!

title: “Top Hotel for Break in NYC”
text:
Hotel was very very good. High quality finish throughout, very comfortable bed, lovely breakfast. Great location. Hotel is a few minutes walk from Rockefeller center and 5th avenue. The subway is right on your door. Only slight critique would be the night life tends to close around 11pm in the immediate area. Very minor issue as we were not in New York to get drunk. Breakfast was basic but perfectly acceptable, lovely fresh continental breakfast, decent coffee, fruit juices, yoghurts. You can eat as much as you like and grab a coffee before you head into New York. The door staff were great, they found us a taxi at rush hour in the rain which in NYC isn't the easiest thing to do.
The only problem we had was that our safe was not working when we arrived, (battery was duff) but this was fixed within 20 mins.
Overall, no complaints, would definitely return again.

title: “Perfect introduction to The Big Apple”
text: My sister & I travelled to NYC as a treat for her 40th birthday & we wanted a fairly central hotel where we would feel safe. The Helmsley did not disappoint, it was perfect. Friendly, helpful staff, beautiful decor, huge comfy beds & perfect location. It was everything we could have wished for & more.

title: “Wonderful location, great price”
text:
This hotel is in a great part of town -upper west side. Its surrounded by beautiful brownstones and lots of bakeries, restaurant and shops. Central Park is right down the street and the subway is around the corner. Its also near Lincoln Center. This is where you stay if you want a taste of living in NYC as oppposed to staying in the more touristy midtown areas. We stayed here 3 nights and loved it. We found it to be very safe and there are lots of people walking their dogs and riding bikes. Its a neighborhood and the people were very friendly - which is not what you'd expect in the Big Apple.
The rooms are very small (really small) but clean and really how much time do you spend in your room in NY anyway. The staff was very friendly too. I would definitely recommend this hotel especially if you don't want o spend a fortune or even close, for a hotel room. 
(We stayed here Feb/05)

title: “Unexpected upgrade”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights after an Alaska cruise and the Empire builder train from Seattle.
The hotel is less impressive from the outside than some of its neighbours (e.g. The Hilton nextdoor) but it is comfortable and clean and the staff are very helpful and accomodating.
 We were originally given a room on 5th floor overlooking the swimmingpool. It had no view of the city at all and we were disappointed as others checking in with us all seemed to be getting rooms much higher up. My husband enquired whether there was any chance of being moved to a room with a better view as we were unlikely to be in Chicago again and wanted to make the most of it. The lady on reception upgraded us to a suite on the 15th floor. We were astonished as it was much more than we had hoped for - it just goes to show that it never hurts to ask!
The rooms were spacious and clean with wonderful comfy beds - no safe, surprisingly but you could give your valuables to reception and they would lock them away safely. My husband used the pool - which was larger than usually found in this size hotel and a welcome addition.
Chicago is a lovely city, wonderful architecture and lakes/rivers. We were luck with the weather too as it was nice and warm - perfect for sight seeing. Would have liked to stay longer!

title: “Excellent Accomodation”
text: When I arrived it was about 8:30 PM. I requested an upgrade to my room (as a platinum member it's one of the perks), When I got the one bedroom suite it had only one King size bed. Since I was there with my sister I requested a room with two doubles. There was nothing available. Linda the receptionist was great, she gave us a two bedroom suite and we were thrilled. The suite was fantastic: two bedrooms with a queen bed in one and two doubles in the other, full kitchen, dining area, both bedrooms with own bathroom and TV and flatscreen TV in living area with pull out couch. The furniture is not the cheap stuff either that you usually find in t hotel at this price. The breakfast was amazing, lots of hot food, waffles, bacon etc and to go bags if you were in a rush. There was also an event called the sundown reception where you could eat and drink free Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday night. We're not talking appetisers here, there was barbque one night, cheeseburger in paradise another night and oriental the third night, oh and free beer and wine also (draft beer). I have never stayed an a hotel that had so much put on for the guests (for Free). There were three computers in the business room and free internet access, a fax, copier and printer were available also (again free). Laundry facilities were incredible, four washers and dryers so you didn't have to wait (free). We stayed through the indy 500 weekend (memorial weekend) and although the hotel was full there was no noise or trouble, the grounds are tightly secured by Larry. The grounds at the back of the hotel are beautiful with tables and barbques (the gas kind) so you could cook also if you wanted. Don't even question the quality of this hotel. Some days the maids didn't leave enough shampoo but who cares, ask and you shall receive. We stayed in room 210. Also located by the I69 and shopping. Honors Beauty College is a short walk down the street, get a full facial for $25, it's fantastic. Cheeseburger in paradise is next door, so if you want a few cocktails just nit over, no driving that was a great perk, and a real carribean feel with outdoor dining. Don't go to Petersons it's a rip off....

title: “wouldn't have it any other way”
text:
A very unique hotel experience, almost like staying at home in a big city.
Rooms are large, loved the locale.
Was skeptical after reading some of the negative reviews, but I'd stay there
again in a heartbeat.

title: “Charming and comfortable”
text:
This is a nice hotel, with a fancy lobby and interior. The rooms are older ("Historic"). We had the less expensive room, so no view of any kind and was a little tired.
Bed was comfortable and nice robes and generally pleasant enough. Otherwise nothing hugely stands out or lets down and so is a decent option. Not that close to downtown by foot, but plenty of transport close by.

title: “Very Nice Midtown locaton”
text:
First time at this hotel, stayed one night.
Was given an upgrade to a corner room on check in - rooms that end in 01 have side and front windows, and a great view down Ave/Americas. Room was good sized, bath was small. The door intruded into the room, I kept hitting it because it was in the way - this bath should have sliding doors for sure. Other than that room was clean, sizeable, and well appointed with fridge and microwave. Also - for being right in Midtown - this room was very quiet
As others have mentioned - breakfast was a feast - typical Residence Inn fare - was good.
Elevators were quick - no issue. Fitness room was disappointing - for a hotel this size it was really small and had good cardio equipment, but next to no weights or machines. Need an upgrade here.
One last thing - prices in the bar were crazy - even by NY standards.
One great thing about this hotel is the location. It really is convenient to things that you can walk to - and the subway is about a 3 minute walk away.

title: “Great hotel but an accounting headache”
text:
This is a nice property. It is conveniently located and the rooms are comfortable. This hotel has one of the nicest concierge lounges that I have experienced in my many stays at various Marriott hotels. 
However, beware business travelers, I probably spent at least two hours getting my bill e-mailed to me and my Marriott rewards points posted. I rely on the e-mailed bills to do my expense reports since I travel a lot and try avoid accumulating a lot of paper. I normally get the e-mails with my bill within 48 hours and my Marriott rewards account is updated at the same time. It took one fax, three phone calls, and two weeks to get this accomplished as to my stay at this hotel. The people in Utah contended that the hotel never closed out my account and the people at the Denver hotel couldn't seem to understand what my problem was.

title: “Good place to stay in LA”
text:
We stayed 3 nights in this wonderful, clean and nice facility.
The rooms are outstanding, clean, spacy and newly restaurated.
The pool could have a better filtering system, but is also very nice.
The staff is friendly and the breakfast is outstanding.
Unfortunatelly we got verbally more promised than later was given.
So we changed with one clerk to a non smoking room (wrong click on the reservation) for the first night and where told that we can stay all three nights there. On the next day nobody remembered and we had to upgrade to a suite for extra money. OK, it was my fault on the reservation first, but a promise should stay a promise!

title: “Great location and traditional upscale setting”
text: I stayed here on a girl's weekend with my mom just prior to Irene coming ashore. The location is a great jumping off point for Central Park and shopping.The hotel is classically decorated, with the lobby appointed in dark wood and decorated with large, oil paintings and soft lighting. The room itself was rather small and styled with striped fabric walls and nice wood furniture. The bed was extremely comfortable...the highlight of the stay I would say. The bathroom had nice marble finishes, a large tub and all the comforts you would expect of a nice hotel. The view from the room left a little to be desired...a view of the building interior walls. The service was pretty good overall...everything we asked for was taken care of. If you like the feeling of traditional luxury, you will like the Ritz Carlton. If you like a more contemporary, modern hotel experience, try the Mandarin Oriental on Columbus Circle.

title: “Nice (if you pay for the larger room/suite)”
text:
I the unique experience of viewing 2 rooms types during my stay. This was not under the most ideal circumstances, but it ended up okay in the long run. We original booked the "New Yorker Room with a view". The room (as most in New York are) was very small. After having gone through a "recent remodel", I was expecting more from this room. The quality of the renovation was pretty bad, as our bathroom had visible holes in the walls and floors and other areas where they had just painted over the poor patch jobs. The comment that my wife and I exchanged after a night in the room was that this was not a "4 star" hotel, as TripAdvisor had led us to believe. At best, I would say a 3 star. 
The morning of the second day of our stay, we were overcome with the smell of cigarette smoke (not hard in a small room). We determined that it was being blown INTO OUR ROOM through the vents. We instantly shut off the A/C in the room and I called the front desk. I was told that they would "look into it". After about 15 minutes, I turned on the A/C and the smell was gone. I assumed that the situation had been resolved. About 30 minutes later, the unmistakeable smell was back again and seemed to be worse than before. I called the front desk again and reported the situation. The person that I spoke to transferred me to her manager, which ended up in a voicemail. I left a message, explaining the situation, explaining the fact that my wife is allergic to smoke, and asked for a call back on my cell phone at their earliest convenience. On our way out of the building for the day, I stopped at the front desk in hopes of speaking to a manager in person. After providing a quick recap to the front desk associate, I was told that I was "wrong" and that the smell that I smelled was "not cigarette smoke", but was, instead, smoke from a fire that they had in one of the rooms. I explained to the woman that I knew that it was cigarette smoke and that it had started and stopped with about 45 minutes in between (something that a "fire" seemingly would not do). After she told me that I was mistaken one more time, I asked if I could leave my phone number for her manager and asked that she have them call me on my cell phone. After fumbling around for a minute, she produced a piece of paper and I wrote my contact information on it. At that time, a gentleman in a suite walked up (I assume from security) and the front desk attendant gave my newly written information to him. He assured me that he would "look into it" and "get back to me shortly." (This was at approximately 10:00 am.)
By 3:00 pm on the following day, I still hadn't heard from anyone regarding the situation. When we tried to get into our room, our room keys didn't work. I went back down and spoke with someone at the front desk and asked them to provide me with new keys. After receiving the new keys, I decided to try to speak to a manager again. After a short wait, a manager named Erica appeared. (For the record, Erica is the only reason that this review gets an "Average" rating instead of a "Poor" rating.) After I explained to Erica that I had called twice, left a voicemail once, spoken to the front desk once, and had never been called back, Erica went to work. The first thing she did was to apologize for the inconvenience (something that the first 4 individuals had failed to do). Based on the fact that they are in the hospitality industry, you would think that this would have been something that they teach the employees on the first day on the job. If it is, those 4 people were absent that day. Next, Erica explained that it was cigarette smoke that I was smelling and that they had caught the person responsible for it. The next thing Erica did was to offer us a different room. One of the few that they had available was a suite on one of the higher floors. This room was incredible and was worth every bit of the 4 stars that this hotel had promised.
Needless to say, had Erica not stepped in and been so accommodating, our stay would have been shorter and this review would have been even worse. Thank you, Erica, for understanding the customer is not always "WRONG".

title: “Stay at the Residence Inn”
text: It all started with the wonderful experience when I pulled up and was warmly welcomed by the valet attendant. I then entered the doors and got checked in and had a nice talk with the Front Desk clerk named Remington or "Remi" as she called herself. She was very nice, and kept a great conversation giving all the important information about the property as well. She did a great job with the process and we got the customer service that is expected. We then asked for suggestions for dinner and she sent us to the Oceanaire Restaurant; which was outstanding. That evening we also met Nicolette("Nicki") and she was a charm as well. The staff through out the hotel is what made this property stand out from the rest of Downtown hotels. I was very pleased with my stay and would be happy to return to this hotel if another trip to San Diego is made.

title: “A wonderful choice”
text:
We come to SF each summer for camp at the Exploratorium and are always looking for a homey place close by. The Marina Courtyard Motel fits this to a "T". The small, but comfortable, rooms are loaded with personality. The kitchens include gas stove, fridge, oven and dishware. Within a few minutes walk is Chestnut Street in the middle of the Cow Hollow district, where you will find everything from groceries to health clubs and enough lovely restaurants to eat from a different ethnicity each day for weeks. The hotel proprietors are super: responsive, polite and enthusiastic. Several of the rooms seem to be in their original 1939 condition, whereas others have been updated. This is reflected in modest price differences.
Suggestion: Ask for a room off of Lombard Street protected by the courtyard. Lombard is very noisy, causing us to vacate, for example, the Inn at the Presidio nearby.

title: “Loved the Langham”
text: Beautiful hotel. Staff exceedingly pleasant and helpful.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Stayed in the Park Central in March '08. Was very worried about it as some of the reviews on here are very negative. 
We checked in the hotel about 2.30pm, no problems what so ever, room was ready, we didn't have to wait to be seen to, person on the desk was polite and helpful. 
The room was bigger then i imagined, loads of space to fill with shopping bags. Bed was very comfortable. Bathroom was a good size, only negative thing being that the shower was not powerful at all, but this wasn't a big issue. Room was cleaned every day to a very good standard. 
Lifts were slow at times. Obviously more so at peek times of the day, but this didn't bother us too much. 
Location of the hotel was perfect! Few min walk to Times square or Central Park, 5th avenue and all the major attractions.
The booking desk was very helpful, even booking some restaurants for us and answering our questions and suggesting things to do. 
There is a Starbucks right next to the hotel and a subway across the road, plenty of other places to eat a few feet from the hotel. 
We didnt spend a great amount of time in the actual hotel, we knew from the beginning it would just be a place for us to sleep and wash really but we were no way disappointed.
There are a lot of negative reports on here but i can truly say that we had a great stay and would not hesitate in coming back here and would defo recommend it to anyone.

title: “Service is top notch”
text: My teenage daughter and I staid here for one night before a concert at the Verizon Center. The hotel is newly renovated and very modern inside. The staff was the most accommodating and friendliest I have ever encountered at a hotel. We could see the Verizon Center from our hotel window and it was a very quick and safe walk. Beds were very comfortable and room was ultra modern. It is also very easy walking distance to the Metro.

title: “everything was absolutely perfect!!!!”
text: six of us came for a birthday party that was in the same area. we had the valet parking, easy check in, things to do at the hotel, a great shower and a wonderful nights sleep. i cannot wait to go back.

title: “Nice conference hotel”
text:
I stayed here 3 nights for a conference. My room was clean and comfortable. The front desk staff was pleasant and efficient, and the food provided by hotel staff was above-average quality for conference food. The meeting rooms were nice with the usual amenities. The hotel is right on the Riverwalk, and within a stone's throw of the Alamo. 
I agree with another reviewer who said that internet access is inadequate at this hotel. Every budget motel along the interstate now has free wireless access, so why should the Hyatt sock me ten bucks a day? The free wireless supposedly available in the conference meeting rooms was unreliable -- difficult to get a connection and slow as molasses. It was the one real frustration in an otherwise pleasant stay.

title: “Horrible Staff!!!”
text: I will never stay here again! When we first arrived, the staff was moderately friendly, but definitely did not go out of their way to help. Once we got to our room, we found that the air conditioner was leaking all over the room. The floor was soaked!! We called the front desk and they said they would send a maintenance person up to work on it. An hour later, no one had arrived, so I called the front desk again. Finally someone came up to look at the AC. The man was very rude and told us we "might" be able to change rooms or we might have to deal until he can get a whole new AC unit installed. Luckily, we could switch rooms, but the front desk never apologized or anything! When we got settled into our new room, we began to shower and get dressed. The one blow dryer we used kept blowing the fuse. The maintenance man yelled at us and told us we could not use our blow dryer again. Well, being 3 girls in NYC, we couldn't do that and the power went out 3 more times! No one ever apologized for anyone being rude or for any inconvenience. The next day went alright until we went to pick up our stored luggage. The bell man got our luggage, asked if we needed a cab and walked away before we could even answer him. He could have cared less what we needed. The only positive part about the hotel is the decor and the location.

title: “Very nice. Close to blue line. Get the breakfast package.”
text: We just got back from a 3 day stay with 4 adults and 2 small children. This hotel was great. We got a room with 2 double beds and a sleeper sofa. The beds and pillows were so soft and comfy and even the sofa bed was comfy. Nobody treated us any different for bringing in children. We added a breakfast package to the room for only $16 more and it was fantastic. Eggs, bacon, oatmeal, cold cereal, yogurt and a nice selection of fresh fruit. The best was the nice woman at the breakfast bar who would make a custom omelet. The service was great, the hotel was very nice, and it was a short walk to the blue line which will get you anywhere you need to go. The only downside was, there is no fast food joints around (mcdonalds or hardees for example) we drove around blindly for almost an hour before just deciding to go to the Dominicks grocery store down the road, which was a great place with a huge variety of food and drink. I do not think you would regret staying at this hotel, unless you just had to be closer to downtown. Oh it also had a really nice looking bar, but we did not utilize that.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text: The Westin is within walking distance of many touristy sites. The view from the room- toward the Space Needle and Puget sound was breathtaking- try requesting a higher floor when you book. The room was okay, looked a bit "tired" but the easy access to the sights was worth it! Beware the parking fee is steep! We took the light rail, $2.50 per person one way, from the airport and the station is across the street from the hotel as is the monorail station to take you to the Space Needle. It is a 15 min walk to Pike Place Market, 25 to the waterfront but it is all up hill back, thank goodness for those taxi cabs! I rode the "Ducks" attraction with my 29 yr old son and we both enjoyed it! That also is within walking distance from the hotel. We had dinner at The Crab Pot and Elliots Oyster House, oh the fresh seafood.... We also had lunch at the Space Needle..pricey but.once in a lifetime experience. I actually took a picture of my entree as it was so beautifully presented! I VERY much enjoyed this trip.

title: “Was a little dissapointed”
text: Bungalow on Water DOES NOT look like the one they have posted on their website. It wasn't very clean at all and did NOT have the views they show - For that amount of money, I was expecting A LOT more and didn't get it. The pull out couch was the most uncomfortable thing I have every slept in and the noise across the bay, terrible! I do have to say that the staff was great and they helped us out a lot with our issues. Nice place, kids loved it but I liked the connecting rooms with garden views MUCH more than the bayside bungalow. Terrible service at the restaurant and Baleen was VERY overpriced. Haven't decided if we will go back.

title: “Great start to holiday!”
text: Arrived at the hotel about 3pm and our room was ready. Met by friendly reception staff who gave us maps of the city. Room was up to standard though view from the window was of the building next door. You can upgrade if you want a better view of the city or the Golden Gate Bridge. Breakfast was as expected, cakes, muffins, cereal and a cool 'make it yourself ' waffle maker. There was always plenty to eat with as much tea and coffee as you wished. The hotel was in a great location for Fishermans Whalf which was a short walk down the hill. Here you can catch the cable car to Powell street and downtown. The hotel is also on the corner of Lombard street, where the ' most crooked street in the world' is just over the ( very steep ) hill. Room was kept clean. I was told about the charge for car parking on this web site, but i was not told about the charge for the room safe by the reception staff. As i checked out , i was told that i had to pay for this service. I complained and they dropped the charge. So be warned! Other than that we had a plesant stay and would use this hotel again.

title: “Great location and beautiful hotel”
text:
I stayed here for a week during a conference and had no complaints. Staff was friendly and helpful. The hotel itself is in a wonderful location, and we could walk to the river and Newbury Street. Having a large shopping mall attached was great on the hot days when it was too humid to go outside, or when I had to run out to buy something I had forgotten to pack. 
I had a mini suite on a high floor, and the room and view was wonderful, including the super comfortable heavenly bed. The bathroom was a little small and dark, but manageable. Housekeeping seemed to come as soon as I left each morning, which was great because I was often running back to my room for things during the day and was happy to always see it made up.
The minibar selections could have been more plentiful, but was fine overall. Room service provided quick service, and the portions were very large and delicious. The hotel bar was nice for a quick drink or a bite to eat, and everybody in our group enjoyed the food there. 
As for the conference that was put on at the hotel, everything went off without a hitch. The hotel staff did a great job of putting on a large event, and the meeting rooms were modern and comfortable. The only issues with planning a large event here are that the catered meals were average at best (minus the delicious desserts), and there did not seem to be enough restrooms for a large meeting. Everybody resorted to running back to their rooms instead of waiting in long lines.

title: “one of the best I've stayed in”
text:
Beautiful hotel. A bit out of central Denver but there is a free minibus anywhere within about 7 miles - first come, first served but we had no difficulty.
A beautiful room, booked as part of a package but I think we got an upgrade, we did not actually book a suite. Very comfortable rooms and lovely huge beds. Excellent service from the front desk and the concierge.
If you are shopping at Cherry Creek the concierge recommended the Eggshell on Fillmore for breakfast, ask the shuttle to drop you there, its excellent.
Also we went to the Fruition restaurant 1313 East 6th on a recommendation, wonderful food and good value if you don't drink too much!

title: “~Wonderful~”
text: We had a wonderful time at this hotel! The setting is magnificent, right on the river walk with nice restaurants all around. We took the river taxi over to the landing and got to see fireworks right from our balcony also a nice walk to friendship fountain which was beautiful. We found the hotel to be clean, with nice decor and in a terrific location with a friendly staff!!! We will definitely be back!!

title: “Perfect!”
text: My wife and I spent a week in the hotel. Just left last Tuesday, 10/23/12. Hotel is very cozy and its location cannot be better. Facilities are very clean and our interaction with hotel staff was one courteous, friendly and helpful. Room was cleaned and ready very early, accommodating our schedules. Overall hotel & room decor suits our tastes very well. We're already looking for dates for a return stay. Thank you King & Grove!

title: “Great Location”
text:
This Hotel was exactly what I expected. It is very old and certain areas could do with a bit of refurbishment but I suppose that all adds to the character. The room was very spacious by New York standards and very clean although the decor leaves a lot to be desired. 
The location is great, we could see the empire state building from our room and everything we wanted was in walking distance or a short taxi ride. 
On the whole a reasonably priced hotel with clean and spacious rooms which is all you need when you're staying in New York as you don't really spend much time there.

title: “Excellent customer service!”
text:
Myself, my husband, and my 2 small children stayed for 3 nights in March 2012. We very much enjoyed our stay. I was concerned that our boisterous children would be a problem, but the staff welcomed them. A particular staff member was incredible. His name was John Dawson. He welcomed the children cordially, and gave them postcards, apple juice, and homemade cookies. This made the children feel very special, and made them very excited to stay at the Mayflower. 
This hotel is very convenient to the Metro station. We will definitely return to this hotel when we return to DC.

title: “Price, Location and Friendliness can't be beat”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights last week - 2 adults and a 6 year old. The hotel is not luxurious but it is clean and the staff is genuinely friendly. The rate we got on Priceline was less than $100 and that's simply unbeatable, plus there's free wireless. Location is perfect for those who like it downtown and it is close to both the 4,5,6 and A,C,E trains which make it super easy to get around.

title: “I had a good experience at this resort.”
text:
On a recomendation from a friend,I made a last minute reservation for two rooms here during easter vacation. I was a little nervous since I had read some negative reviews on this website. I called up the hotel's reservation line and got a rate of $169.00 each for two non-bayview rooms (the bay view rooms were sold out). Our rooms were clean and comfortable. One was bigger,and had a walk in closet. My mother took the smaller room and my wife and daughter and I took the bigger one. The bed was reasonably comfortable, but the pull out bed that my daughter slept on was not due to a very thin matress. I would recomend getting a room with two queens if you needed to sleep more than two people. The big room had a little private porch that I enjoyed sitting in in the afternoon. Our rooms were in the Orchid village part of the resort and the girl at the front desk said that it was quiet area away from the main pool, and it was. We enjoyed our rooms and I can only sumise that there must be some good rooms and some bad rooms at this resort
 The Baleen restaurant was expensive, but the food was excellent. Room service food was good, but pricy. At many of the self contained resorts in Southern Ca (Hotel del Coronando and Ritz Carlton Laguna Niguel come to mind) you are going to spend a fortune if you buy all your meals there. We brought food and wine with us (there are refridgerators in the rooms. Also,bring your own putters to play the resort putting course. They charge $9.00 a putter. I did not find trash on the beach as was mentioned in the previous review and enjoyed walking on the beach (which by the way is on a bay; no waves).
 I found this resort to be a peaceful place to retreat to after spending a day exploring San Diego and I would return here.

title: “Perfect Location with great amenities”
text:
What a great location this hotel has....easy walk to tons of restaurants, Michigan Ave., State Street, the river, etc. One block from the Red Line at Grand for further trips to Chinatown, Wrigley Field, or the Willis Tower.
I knew from TA that there would be some issues with noise as there is a Fire Station across the street. The hotel does provide earplugs in the lobby. It wasn't the Fire Station though that was the problem. We had a suite on the back alley side of the hotel, and there was a great deal of noise VERY early almost every morning from a trash truck or some other service vehicle!
Since we had a suite with 2 Doubles, a sofa bed, and a kitchenette, there was plenty of room for my family with 2 teenagers to spread out. The kitchenette even had granite and stainless steel appliances! There was a nice island type seating area in it for quick snacks too!
The hotel is one of the few with this great location that provides free wi-fi, complementary hot breakfast, and a USA Today or Wall Street Journal daily. We appreciated all these extras especially since the parking was $42 a night.
We definitely would stay here again, but would ask for a street side higher up room if it was available as a suite.

title: “Loved It!”
text: Just got back from a 4 night stay at the Courtyard Manhattan Midtown East - FABULOUS HOTEL!!!!! There were 4 of us - 2 moms, 2 16-yr-old daughters - and we had plenty of space. We had two queen beds and a pull-out sofa which we only used as a place to hold our stuff! There was a ton of room for our 4 huge suitcases plus shopping bags, and the bathroom was absolutely fine. We were on the 29th floor with a beautiful view of the Chrysler Building and the river - plus, it was so quiet up there! The service was excellent, and there are several restaurants close by that have free delivery - we ordered from a deli our first night and had delicious salads and sandwiches for a very reasonable price ($25 for the 4 of us!). There's a Duane Reade pharmacy right next door and Essa-Bagel 2 short blocks down the street. The subway station is 1/2 block away, Museum of Modern Art a short walk, and fantastic shopping up 3rd Avenue. I highly recommend this hotel and wouldn't hesitate to stay there again!

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text:
I booked this hotel through onlinehotels.com and got a great rate for any San Francisco hotel, let alone one of this standard.
We were on a long trip and asked to store some luggage at the hotel for 12 days days before our stay, which they did without any problems.
The rooms are large, and well equiped with a microwave, fridge, basic cutlery/crockery, tv, stereo and vcr. Complimentary wifi was also a huge bonus. A limited complimentary breakfast of pastries and coffee is also available.
The staff were very helpful. The only minor problem we had was that our deposit via the internet booking was not recognised as paid so it took quite a few minutes upon checkout to sort this out.
The location is a block from Union square.
I doubt you could find better in San Francisco for the price we paid and would not hesistate in recommending this hotel

title: “THE place to stay in New York City”
text:
BWHH was recommended by a friend who has stayed there several times. We stayed for 17 days and could not have been happier with the accommodation. It is so handy to everything: subway, buses, Broadway, Rockefeller Centre/Plaza and Times Square. The apartments are huge, with separate kitchen, living room, bedroom and bathroom. 
All of the staff were friendly and helpful, especially Sam the Man, and the delightful Mayran who manages the breakfast room. Yes, the breakfast room can be a little tight during busy periods, but we sometimes used the quaint outdoor patio which was secluded and tranquil. We never had the need to take a breakfast tray back to our room. The freshly-made waffles were a real treat, as were the munchkin donuts!
BWHH is one of the most comfortable, friendly and well-located places that I have ever stayed.

title: “Average old hotel, good value”
text: We stayed there a couple of days. Front desk person was as nice as she had to be, no more. Room and bed were ok. Decor is like something out of Clockwork Orange. -But it's the hotel's theme. Good value considering the location.

title: “A Lovely Refuge From A Busy City”
text: This review is overdue, as we stayed at the LA Athletics Club in December 2011. We are an Australian family of 5, and we had 2 adjoining rooms. The best things were: really lovely staff, very comfortable beds, nice breakfast, clean rooms and quiet hallways. The downtown location troubled my kids a little, but the easy access to the subway compensated for this. If you stay here, eat at the nearby restaurant Louis - sensational dinner place. Overall, the LAAC is made great by its staff.

title: “The Arizona "Hidden Fees" Biltmore”
text:
$25 Disclosed Resort Fee
+
$3 Housekeeping Grautuities/night automatically added, not disclosed
+
$10 Self-park/night automatically added, not disclosed 
+
$15.50 Banquets/Conference Group, automatically added, not disclosed
+
$12 Bellman/night, automatically added, not disclosed, didn't even use!!! and never offered.
Total undisclosed fees: $3X2, $10X2, $15.50, and $12 X 2: Total EXTRA for a 2 night stay: $65.50 plus $50 for the resort fee....
Anger---Priceless.

title: “Great location, great hotel and staff”
text: We chose this hotel for the convenience of being close to the cruise ship port, and couldn't be happier with the hotel, the staff, the location, and even a shuttle bus to the terminal ! We had a king room with a balcony overlooking the marina. The rooms were very nice and comfy bedding. The on site restaurant was great, and the staff very friendly and helpful. I would definately return.

title: “Every Chance I Get”
text: I've stayed at the Marines' Memorial Club many times over 20 years, through several renovations and upgrades to the rooms, restaurant and public areas. It has that warm and welcoming "club" feel, great amenities and the location next to Union Square and downtown is perfect whether you're in SF for business or pleasure. During my most recent stay in a 6th floor room (the room was immaculate and the view was awesome!), I realized in a panic near midnight that I was missing a critical piece of a presentation I was to give the next morning. Thanks to the 4th floor business center, which I accessed with my room key, I was able to use one of the club's PCs, free Web access, and a printer to recreate what I needed, at no charge. I recommend the Marines' Memorial for any individual or family who wants a friendly, comfortable, affordable place to stay with the added bonus of being in a beautiful building with a fascinating history.

title: “Fantastic Apartment Hotel. Great Staff, Awesome Location!”
text: I have been staying at Hollywood Orchid Suites pretty much every year since 2006. It is the only hotel I would even consider staying at while in LA? I love the fact that it is a full apartment with a kitchen and if you choose a separate bedroom. I have stayed here with both my wife and also on other occasions with my best friend. We always have a great time. The location CANNOT be beat, the staff are always super friendly and accommodate even the most demanding request. On my last trip with my friend we flew in from Sydney on a 14 hour flight and arrived at the hotel around 10am. They were kind enough to let us two jet-lagged guys check in early which was a massive benefit. I would recommend this hotel without question!

title: “Techno Trendy with Possiblities”
text:
While our overall experience at the W Seattle was positive, I will admit to some ambivalence about the place.
My wife had expressed an interest in staying at the W so I booked a stay there as part of a Mother's Day weekend celebration. Shortly after booking the room through the Starwood website, I received an email offer to upgrade to a "Spectacular" room for $30, which I accepted.
I also requested to have a special music CD playing when we entered our room. Via email I was connected with Adam Sinding who was my "Insider" for this request. I arranged to drop off the CD the day before our arrival. Adam was not there when I arrived for the drop-off and I was referred to the young concierge. She struck me immediately as affected and pretentious. I believe she had been trained that "putting on airs" somehow enhances the status of an establishment. I just find it off-putting.
Be prepared for awkwardness on arrival at the W. The drive-up entrance is extremely poorly laid out. You basically are in the street when you pull up and configuration of car/pedestrian access to the check-in area is convoluted and congested. To simplify our arrival we just parked in the adjacent (to the east) Olympic Hotel parking garage and walked the 100 feet or so to the entry.
Check-in went very nicely with the staff at the desk very friendly and helpful. (A quick note about staff, they seem to be uniformly amazingly young. This means that you should not expect a great breadth of experience in the hospitality industry.) Guests observed in the lobby area seemed mostly the t-shirt, grungy blue jean, running shoe crowd. This seemed a bit odd giving that the W is not really a cheap place to stay. 
One of the most striking aspects of the Seattle W is its decor and darkness. Lighting in the halls, elevators and other public spaces without windows is incredibly low and techno. For instance, one needs to be quite close (within a foot or two) of a room door to discern the room number. My wife called the decor "urban zen" and I think this is probably as good as any moniker.
Our room was extremely nice and spacious. And yes, the CD was playing at an appropriate volume when we walked in. The bed was extremely comfortable. The room had very large windows with peek-a-boo views of Puget Sound. A full size chaise was along one wall next to a very nicely equipped desk. The bath was large and had more towels than anyone could use. The faucet handle on the tub/shower was close to breaking so controlling water temperature and pressure was quite difficult. 
When our car and driver arrived to take us to our evening activities we again were reminded of the extremely poor layout of access to the hotel. The combination of arriving and departing guests, aggressive taxi drivers whipping about and traffic wizzing by make entering and exiting more than an adventure.
The Earth and Ocean Restaurant on-site again is very much on the trendy side. We found the staff extremely warm, friendly and professional. The menu selection could only be characterized as super-trendy. Fortunately, the W is in the heart of downtown so there are dozens of super dining options for those not in an adventurous culinary mood. 
One minor annoyance is that I still don't have a breakdown of what this little adventure cost. Apparently, the W billing system is not capable of providing an up-to-date itemization of charges upon check-out.

title: “Disappointing end to fabulous trip to USA”
text:
We had travelled from UK to California for a dream vacation. It was on most accounts! However. we had told our travel agent that we really just wanted to "chill out" in luxury for our last few days before flying back to London from LA. We were greeted on arrival and found reception staff friendly. Room was made available at 4.00pm. We were disappointed with standard of accomodation. The room was "dingy", poorly lit, small, furniture poor quality, carpet dowdy, wardrobe small, bathroom very small but clean. Had imagined something much better than this. The motel we stayed in in Santa Barbara was half the price and at least twice as good and the parking there was free! The gardens were nice and we liked the "adult" swimming pool. We felt the charges for parking were very high plus any extras. We did not complain but having had a fabulous trip to the USA and a wonderful experience covering California from North to South, this was a let down!
We decided to make the most of San Diego and what a great City you have! We loved every bit of it and that made up for the shortcomings of Paradise Point
We do feel that the management are holding back on their investment in keeping the accomodation up to a high standard. Its not what we would have expected or for that matter had been described by our UK Agent
We would not recommend Paradise Point but at the same time, we had the best vacation of our lives in California but we will forget our visit to this particular spot!

title: “Good stay, bad ending (Financially).”
text: Stayed at the Grand Central Hyatt on a guys weekend trip. The hotel and amenities were great as we had great service, breakfast buffett both days, and courteous staff who gave us great tips on the City. At checkout my room fees were zero as all we did was eat & sleep at the hotel. When I returned home I checked my bank account and the hotel had charged me $376.19 for incidentals (alarming) since this was not told to me. So after a call to the accounting dept those fee's were refunded immediately. Well after 2 more days another charge of $376.20 but this time it would take 3-5 days while all along overdrafting my account and causing me to be charged numerous bank fee's I called to try and get the hotel to re-imburse me for the $$$ to only be denied repeatedly, needless to say I'am still w/o the money and have no reason to recommend a hotel that robs it's customers w/o a gun. And I thought I would get robbed in the streets? All I had to do was check-in..

title: “Unbeatable Location and Service”
text: We had a lovely 9 night stay at the Chancellor in May, thanks to Tripadvisor's accurate guest reviews. Thank you Chancellor staff, you're the best! Everything we were looking for in a smaller intimate hotel, about 100 years old: location, location, location, fine service, a charming place for an anniversary trip. We were also in SF for a family wedding at the ritzy St Francis across the street. After studying the different Union Square hotels, we emailed the most promising, requesting a special extended stay quote, and then wrote the Chancellor, asking could they improve on the best offer received, which they did. We were able to stay for 9 nights for less than $1,500. They even had a card & anniversary gift for us. My son and daughter in law also reserved for a shorter stay. They were also delighted & kept saying what a charming hotel (how did you ever find such a gem?). All in all, it was better than we had anticipated. Kudos to the fine staff, who responded promptly & courteously, even providing a small fridge on request. Susan, who effortlessly handles gift shop and concierge duties, arranged for terrific sightseeing trips: wine country, the redwood forest, Monterey and Carmel, Yosemite Natl Park, city sightseeing. We saved so much money on accomodations, we were able to do it all. Airport shuttle is just $14. (Don't forget SF can be chilly & windy even in August. Dress in layers, and Enjoy.)

title: “Lovely Historic Hotel”
text:
The US Grant is a beautiful historic hotel in a great downtown location. If you are looking for elegant well appointed accomodations this is the San Diego hotel for you. The staff is wonderful - friendly, polite and accomodating - particularly the bell and check in staff. Everything was immaculately clean and we appreciated having our towels and toiletries replaced with the turndown service. Noise was not an issue. 
However, there were two cons that kept me from giving a 5 star review. Our room was overly warm despite setting the thermostat on 65 and neither my husband nor I could sleep due to the stuffiness. If we could have opened our windows or if a lighter duvet was available, we think it would have been better. As it was, it was really uncomfortable and we barely slept. The second con is that there are no bathtubs in standard rooms (unless you get an accessible room). That was disappointing.

title: “Couldn't Have Been Better”
text: Wife was a little nervous after reading some reviews, but once we arrived all her fears quickly dissappeared. From the underground gated parking, daily breakfast, in-room refrigerator & microwave, ocean view room to the staff that seemed to like going out of their way to make our stay memorable, we were more than happy with our choice. You are in walking distance of many restaurants (I've never had a Lobster BLT before) & bars (many with rooftop patios), and a 7-11 & a grocery store right across the street. The front dest personal were happy to share their favorites, both locally & within easy driving distance. (The Crabcatcher in La Jolla was one of ours). Loved watching the sunset over the Pacific from our room,plus walking out the door and onto the beach. We also noticed & appreciated the cleanliness that the staff took pride in: the rooms, the lobby, the breakfast area, and the pool area. If we had to be picky, my wife would like to have had a pillow-top mattress as we were there a week. We would definately go back again, and would reccommed this place to anyone.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
I have stayed at Kimptons before and I like unique hotels. So, we thought we would move over here after our room block was up at a generic hotel we were staying at for a wedding. Bad idea.
The first person that greeted us seemed really friendly and nice. Even though everyone around us was allowed to check-in, they told us we had to wait for a pet-free room. No big deal, we just checked our luggage and went on our way.
When we came back around 6pm, we had a different person who was much less friendly and less on-the-ball. We had to make sure our room, this time, was the pet-free one we were waiting for. When we got to it, we realize it was very small, which we had expected. What we didn't expect was how run-down it was. The pain job was crappy - peeling and parts, painted on the tile in others. Our toilet paper holder had graffiti written on it, which, didn't go with the aesthetic so I don't think it was intentional, but you never know. Our pet and allergy free room had a not-so-allergy-friendly moldy bathroom (and not just little bits of mold in the shower, a giant splotch of mold on the wall - see photo). 
There were also lots of super annoying things - like the windows don't have screens. So, if you want to get air, you need to also let in 100 flying insects. Our bathroom door handle was falling off, so I kept getting nervous I was going to get locked in there forever. And, finally, the most annoying, we had a "Raid the Mini-Bar" certificate for being In Touch members. However, they locked our mini-bar. I think it's far more annoying to have a perk that doesn't work than than to not have a perk at all. Especially combined with everything else. 
We didn't book discount, we booked on the Kimpton website because we wanted a quality experience - this was certainly not it.

title: “Historic and Chic”
text: This is a grand historic building and renovated rooms which is not always the case. The rooms were tastefully decorated, my room had a view of the city which was enjoyable. The kitchenette was a big plus. The breakfast was included and it had everything you want from a buffet breakfast. I liked that the internet was free and the business room was accessible. I liked the lobby with a big screen. The biggest asset this property had the staff. Especially the front desk people were very helpful. I had a flat tire in front of the hotel, the valet people were especially helpful. The beds were very comfortable. I also liked the location, it was across a very nice Italian restaurant and a diner/bar open till 2:00 AM.

title: “Not Satisfied”
text: My daughter reserved a room for herself and father from out of town, as it was a block from the court house, and they had a very important court hearing on July 5th. With the stress, my daughter left a very special one carat diamond ring that cannot be replaced from sentiment, along with 2 less valuable rings. After 2 calls, and finally my husband calling, we were told the cleaning person's name, and that they would talk to her. My husband offered a reward, knowing that would only admit guilt from someone, but that they would talk to her supervisor. A message on my daughter's cell phone, was left 2 days later that they did not find them in the room. I want this exposed, as a hotel is only worthy if one can trust them. Very disappointed that the rings were not returned.. and a sad daughter.

title: “excellent hotel, very welcoming”
text:
Excellent hotel, perfect location. 
The door man greats you at the door, the hotel staff are extremely welcoming, you get your bags taken to your room and the bell boy shows you around the room which are massive! We had a room on the 24th floor with a balcony over looking maddison square gardens. You have a choice of 6 pillows and you can change as many times as you want its great. The rooms are clean and tidy, we had a massive bed, small bathroom - but not too small , a large tv with loads of channels, a desk with chair, a sofa chair and a small kitchen area with everything you need and a huge fridge and freezer. I would definately recomment this hotel to everyone. Its in a central location, over the road is maddison square gardens and one block from macy's, times square and even central park are within walking distance.

title: “Not good!!!”
text: Sheets wur dirty, restroom was dirty, door would not lock had to put a chair against d door......smelled like cigarrets we asked for none smoking and a single bed did not get!!!

title: “Comfortable and Great Breakfast”
text:
We just returned from Denver and stayed at Quality Inn Central Denver. Our overall experience was overall good. Below are our pros and cons:
Pros:
Free breakfast daily - waffles, eggs, ham, biscuits, cereal, fruit, coffee and tea.
Great front desk service
Exercise room
Free wifi
Free parking
Close to tourist attractions via car
Free shuttle service to tourist attractions
Amazing bedding
Cons:
Wifi signal was weak
Few television channels
Room was a bit stale
Overall, we enjoyed our stay.

title: “Good location, nice hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed here for one night. Overall, the hotel was nice and comfortable. My biggest complaint would be the size of the rooms. For a hotel of this caliber, I would have expected a larger room and bathroom. Service was friendly and the parking garage was convenient ($18 per night). The hotel is a couple blocks away from a restaurant/shopping area but right next door to the Convention Center and NASCAR Museum.

title: “Fourth Stay - Everything Wonderful!”
text: My fourth stay at Millennium Broadway. Three friends were with me. They were impressed with the hotel as well. The location can't be beat. Great value!!!!

title: “Great for pet owners”
text:
My rating might give the wrong impression about our fondness for this hotel. It's roomy, has a certain charm, great restaurant staff and super for dog owners. The only reason I don't rate it higher is, it's old and a little bit rundown. If you want a fresh, very new feeling hotel, you won't like it. This hotel seems to have a certain faded charm.
However, everything in our rooms has always worked and been clean, and we like that we are welcomed when we travel with our pet.
The restaurant is good, though cold in the summer, and breakfasts are substantial.
The rooms are arranged around a central square patio in keeping with the Spanish style of the lobby. It makes for a long walk from the garage if you're on the other side of the square. Each room has a back set of French doors leading out to an outdoor walkway that looks down into the patio and pool.
The location makes it reasonably quick to get downtown, although if you have a route that avoids I-35 you're advised to use it. It's a little hard to access the hotel off the I-35 exit ramp, requiring you to cross about 3 lanes of traffic pretty quickly.
The rate, much lower than the downtown hotels, makes it worth it, however.

title: “Great location”
text: The Royalton was a great hotel. We visited NYC in August for my father's birthday. The hotel itself was more appropriate for my age group (34) compared with my parents (60). I think my father felt a little out of place. The design of the hotel is very trendy and the hallways are definitely not as dark as some other reviewers state. The room itself was great, it was alot larger than I was expecting. The staff was polite and courteous and helped us out when needed. The only thing I can say negative about the hotel was the design of the mirrors in the bathroom. The way they are angled made it difficult for my girlfriend to do hair/makeup. Overall I would stay here again in a heartbeat, perfect location and great rooms.

title: “Worst trip I ever had with my kids. Don't believe reservations or guarantees, even booking with them directly.”
text: We came March 18-20 to bring our 3 little ones to Sea World for the first time. Might I add, my husband and I work and are working on advanced degrees, and this was the first family vacation we'd ever taken--I wanted everything to go well. It DID NOT. I booked online directly, and then the next day called the hotel to be sure that I would have a suite that included a separate bedroom since we have three children who go to bed at 8:30pm. I told the front desk that we would be driving in from Houston, and that we wouldn't be arriving until late. I was on hold so long waiting to speak to someone that I had to hang up and call back. But I was assured that I had a "guaranteed" reservation, even arriving late. I even received a confirmation email with my room details. When we arrived at 11pm, we had no suite with a separate bedroom. I was livid, because the couple checking in in front of me did, in fact, receive a suite with TWO separate bedrooms. I spoke to the clerk, who basically told me he hadn't worked the two days, so he had no idea what was going on. He offered me two suites that had no bedroom, but they didn't adjoin, and I couldn't leave my children unattended. So we ended up in a regular room. The next morning, we were told breakfast ended at 9:30. We went down to breakfast at 8:55, and there was not enough food for all there, and no place to eat. We waited around for more to be made, and there was ONE person cooking one bowl of eggs at a time. My children were upset that they couldn't have eggs and bacon, too. We even asked for a tray to take food up to our room to eat, but we were told that they "don't usually do that". I went to speak to a manager, but he/she wasn't there. The person on duty told me I had to wait for another room to be cleaned before I could transfer. Since we had to wait on food, had to wait to get into another room, then move all of our stuff ourselves, we spent the first half of the day wasting time at the hotel instead of at Sea World. When I brought this to the attention of the front desk, I was offered 50 bucks off my room, despite the promise that "you'll be happy with your stay or it's free". The lady at the desk apologized, said she couldn't get ahold of the manager, and that she would email him and get back to me. I never heard from either of them--and I even left my cell phone number. The next morning, breakfast was another debacle. Still not enough food for all there and no place to sit. My 7 year old said it best--"Mom, next time let's stay at a different hotel that has food and the rooms we like." What a complete waste of money and time off. It was the worst hotel experience I ever had.

title: “Great hotel but wish we had a larger room”
text:
Every year my husband and myself make an annual trip with my brother and his wife to stay overnight and take in a show in Boston. This year I selected the Back Bay hotel based on all of the excellent reviews it received. I reserved the Deluxe room thinking that it would be larger and would have the walk in shower that was described on the website. We were assigned room 820 and when we walked in, I was a bit disappointed but just figured the rooms are smaller at this hotel especially it being a police station at one time. We met my brother prior to going to dinner and when I walked into his room, my mouth dropped. It was a nice spacious room with a huge bathroom. He was assigned room 238. He actually reserved a superior room but as it turned out, he received an upgrade. I did inquire at the desk and they did offer to change our room, but at that point we were settled in and heading off to dinner. I guess I would just be aware that not all the Delxue rooms are the same so when you do check in, make sure you receive what you think you are getting. 
We did up going to the bar later that night and it was fun. Great drinks! We had breakfast at the Stanhope Grille the next day as it was included in on the AAA package but it only included the buffet. I was fine with it but my husband would have preferred to order off the menu. He is a pancake lover and was not impressed with the pancakes at the buffet.
Construction at this hotel was a problem. We heard construction pretty much all night which was a bit annoying. Our room was on the 8th floor but we could still here it.
The beds are quite comfortable the staff are extremely friendly. From the time we entered the hotel and left, everyone was extremely nice.
The location of the hotel is excellent. We went to DaVincis for dinner which we all enjoyed which is only minutes away. We walked to the Citi performance Center which is also a nice walk away. Hightly recommend the Rockettes Christmas Show. It was excellent. We also parked at the garage at 100 Claredon which again is only a block away from the hotel. Look online for a coupon to park overnight for $19.00. Not sure what it would have been otherwise.
Lastly, check out Marshalls at 500 Boylston Street. I really enjoyed that with the two floors. Better selection then any Marshalls out in the suburbs.

title: “Nice Resort for Families with Children 12 and Under”
text:
I recently stayed at the hotel for five nights; the first three were for pleasure and the last two were for a business conference. The hotel is right across the highway from Sea World, about 15 mins from Fiesta Texas and 20 mins or so from downtown/riverwalk. I'm not sure of the exact age of the facility, but the rooms could use some updating. Our room was clean, but the commode was a little loose from the wall, there was a little mold in the bath tile and wallpaper was peeling away in a couple of spots. Not bad, just basically on par with one of the chain "Inns".
The reason I say it would be best for kids 12 and under is because most of the daily activities appeal to that age group. I was there with my teenage daughters and they were a little bored after the first day/night. The lazy river was a neat attraction and pools were nice. Had I paid the rate quoted by the hotel, I would've been disappointed. However, I paid a "travel site" rate and was fine with it. The daily resort fee does increase the rate a bit, but if you plan to stay on-site with smaller kids, you could easily fill up your day with activities. 
I didn't eat at the restaurants on-site because I read that the costs were a little high for the quality. Good news is that there are several chain restaurants and fast food places 5 mins or so down the road. 
All in all, I think a few nights with age ranges noted above would make for a fun family trip. Keep in mind that there are a LOT of kiddos at the hotel, so if you're looking for a tranquil, romantic getaway, you'd probably want to wait until school has resumed.

title: “Cool Staycation Spot”
text:
We stayed here for a one night staycation because we got a great deal online. It was a perfect spot for that purpose. If you're not from DC, it might not be the most convenient place ever b/c it's not right by the metro, but for us it was great. If the purpose of your trip is monuments/museums/White House, you might be better off somewhere a little more metro accessible.
The rooms are really cute -- they obviously put a lot of effort into decor and the place has a great vibe. Totally sign up for Kimpton Hotel In Touch points (or whatever they're called) before you stay there -- they'll give you a $10 "raid the mini bar" credit if you do. Plus, you get free internet (which I did not use but assume it would have worked fine).
The only somewhat disappointing thing was the bathroom. It was by no means bad but just wasn't as nicely done as the rest of the room. Could have used a newer/nicer shower head and a few other nice touches to measure up to everything else.
The gym was small but nice -- 2 ellipticals, treadmill, bike and free weights. 
If the price was right, we'd stay here again for a night or would recommend it to someone staying in that section of DC.

title: “Brill Location!!”
text: My Husband myself and my 14yr old daughter along with my Brother and sister in law stayed here at the end of October for 5 days.All I can say is that we all had a brilliant time.The reception staff were polite and helpful nothing seemed too much trouble.Rooms are slightly dated but they are clean and comfortable. Bathroom was spotless with a brilliant power shower and bed linen white and crisp.The beds were among the most comfortable we have ever slept in.Just what you need after a hard day sightseeing.The location was brilliant.Coming out of the main entrance turn right and 200m down the street was Macy's turn left and walk 200m and you were at the Empire state building.We were a 10 minute walk from times square.There is a buffet breakfast in the morning with cereal fruit juice boiled eggs bagels toast fresh fruit coffee and the biggest donuts i have ever seen in my life.It was more than enough to set you up for the day.Can I also recommend Brendans the bar that is attached to the hotel.We had a meal there one night which was really good.My daughter was always welcome as well if we popped in for a drink before going out.We would certainly use this hotel again and recommend it to friends.

title: “Great stay at the Distrikt for our New York Wedding”
text:
We stayed at the Distrikt from July 1-6, 2012. We were accompanied by about 12 close friends and family members for our wedding, about half of whom stayed at the Distrikt. Our flight was greatly delayed arriving into NYC; however, when we arrived at nearly 2 a.m. the front desk knew our names and greeted us warmly. There were even welcome pastries in our room.
The Distrikt is conveniently located near the Theatre Distrikt and Times Square. There are more attractive streets in the area, and the proximity to the Port Authority meant some 'interesting' characters about, especially late at night. However, the modern rooms, friendly staff and competitive pricing more than compensate for this.
Our room had a great view toward the Hudson River and was kept clean throughout our stay. We appreciated the late-afternoon turn-down service (which includes a chocolate and card with the weather forecast for the following day). Breakfast (or cocktails for that matter) are available in the small restaurant on the main floor.
Overall, a great stay. We would highly recommend the Distrikt Hotel.

title: “Comfortable, quiet hotel with accommodating staff”
text:
Spacious and comfortable suites. Complementary shuttle service that was always prompt and allowed us to save significantly on transportation costs. Front desk was always friendly and quite helpful. 
Ate dinner at the bar one evening. While the bartenders are jovial and entertaining, the food definitely receives a thumbs down. It might have been what I ordered, but it was over-priced and tasted horribly. It was the one and only negative about my entire stay. 
I definitely though would recommend this hotel.

title: “I love it - location is great, and it's a good price”
text:
It's easy to see why reviews about this hotel are divided. If you like chain-hotel style rooms and super-attentive service, with lots of lobby staff to help with your bags, monogrammed slippers in the room, and AC, then this place probably isn't for you. If you, like me, prefer the sort of hotels that are comfortable but not necessarily fancy, with a room or building that's old or quirky in some way, in a great location and with good free wifi, then this place is definitely worth looking at.
The two things that make this hotel are the location and the artwork.
