Yes, it's an old building with single glazing, so it can be a bit noisy, but I didn't hear anything as bad as some people seem to have. If you're sensitive to noise, perhaps ask for one of the rooms that looks out onto the internal courtyard. Mostly, the reason for the noise is that this hotel is right in the centre of the city, which was great for me and meant I could walk all over the place. To get further afield, the BART and light rail are just a couple of blocks away.
The artwork makes each room different, and some people's reviews seem to be based on whether or not they liked the room artwork - if you book on their website you can send an email with your favourite rooms (look on the site for pictures) and they will try to allocate you one of those on check-in. I got my first choice - and the paintings on the walls were beautiful. Next time I'm in SF, I'll try and stay in another one of the rooms - I'll definitely be coming back here rather than checking into a chain hotel.

title: “Don't Do It - Go Somewhere Else”
text: It is everthing it says it is not. It is not in a safe neighborhood if you are traveling alone. The room was stale smelling, musty and not in good repair. I stay at Holiday Inn Express locations all the time, and this is the worst. Their reveiws say they are only 1 mile from Sunset Strip...they are really 4 miles from where you would want to go. The walk to Hollywood Blvd, although ok during the day, is not one I would take alone at night as their are bums and homeless people all along the way. So, unless you want to take a taxi, you will miss the night life of Hollywood and Highland. I called before I went to ensure that it was safe to walk around and easy access as they stated. I was assured this was the case. It was not. Take it from a person who walks the streets of New York City and Chicago at night. This is not a place to stay if you want to feel secure. Also, the hotel is in poor condition and the cost is high for what they give you. Do yourself a favor and stay someplace else.

title: “Dirty hotel, poor service”
text: I was extremely unhappy with the service I received at this hotel. I do not generally write reviews of hotels. Who has the time? I have traveled all over the world and stayed in a variety of hotels. I really felt strongly that I needed to let others know that they should avoid this horrific experience. The location of the hotel is good. My main issue was that the hotel was not clean. When I arrived at my room, I found hairs all over the toilet. When I informed the management and asked to be moved, they appeared disinterested. After wating several hours, they finally agreed to move me to another room. At this point it was almost midnight. I moved all my belongings myself, as the management refused to help me move. When I got to the second room, I found that all the television would show was snow (no picture). Only a few minutes later, I saw a bedbug run across my bed. I was absolutely horrified. When I immediately called the management, the manager came to my room, and agreed to move me yet again. Again, he did nothing to assist me in moving at 1am. The third room they provided was adequate and without vermin. However, I though the building was extremely unsanitary and the service poor. I told management that I expected a refund or at least a discount. The manager refused to do either. As I said, I have stayed at many, many hotels, and this was clearly the worst experience I have ever had. Save yourself the horror and stay elsewhere.

title: “Below than average hotel at convenient location”
text:
Upon my arrival, after a very long journey, I desperately needed a glass of water. Proved an impossible task: The room had no mini-bar or fridge, the hotel had no bar or restaurant, plus no hope for room service. I had to go out to find a super market! But then it started to rain heavily.. 
On the next morning, breakfast was the next bad surprise: Basic in terms of buffet, and I could not believe my eyes when I saw plastic plates and knives/forks. Felt like a student house!
Room was average, hardly clean, with outdated airconditioning, which I had to switch off at night because it was too noisy to let me sleep. 
This a shame, because the location is very convenient.

title: “Good, but...”
text:
The lobby is nice, very pretty. The bar is nice, the courtyard is nice. The room, when I eventually got it, was nice. But a couple of things marred the experience. I asked for a courtyard room. None available when I arrived. To be fair, I arrived at 2 pm, and check in is supposedly at 4 pm. OK. Went out to the courtyard and had a good drink. Checked back. No room. Two hours later, room is available. One would think room would what you had asked for,or someone would mention that it was not. But no. I go up to the room and wait for the bellman. I look in the room. 
But wait! Room is NOT on the courtyard, but I HAD been charged the rate of the upgrade. Not acceptable. Bellman arrives with luggage. Tell bellman I am not staying in this room because it was not what I asked for. Bellman very accommodating, calls manager himself. Manager says, oh, sorry, no room available so he thought he would give me what was available. No, this is not what I asked for. Haul self back downstairs to wait some more. Manager calls on cell phone about 20 minutes later. Room is now available. Go back upstairs, with bellman. Room is what I asked for. Room is lovely. Clean, quiet. On courtyard, as initially requested.
Yet I am not exactly a happy camper, and no additional amenity is provided for the confusion and no apology is made for trying to put me in a room I did not ask for, and then charge the upgrade for the room that is not on the courtyard. I don't know if he thought I would just take it, or what. 
I liked the hotel overall, but this was a bobble in my enjoyment of the experience. I found the front desk somewhat noncommunicative. However, other staff such as the bartender, bellmen, front door staff, and the housekeeping staff all excellent in guest service. The room was immaculate. 
I did not find that the hotel was conveniently located for what I was there to do in DC, however there is a great Starbucks right across the street from the hotel. Go out the front door, turn right, go to the first street and look right. There it is! 
I didn't have room service so can't comment on that. My company paid for my trip. I am not sure, given all the options in DC and a previous really nice stay at a Kimpton in Dupont Circle, that I would choose this hotel again for future travel. It's not that they did anything terribly wrong, it's that they had an opportunity to do it right and missed it.
If you read my other reviews you will find I am generally very appreciative and forgiving. I can be pleased fairly easily. Yet, I was not.

title: “excellent hotel, service and jewell of a location by the beach”
text: We were at the Pacific Terrace for four nights and enjoyed every minute of it. From the time we checked in, the staff was courteous, polite and very helpful. The hotel is very well run and attentive to details. When we checked in, they offered a list of restaurants that you may consider for breakfast, lunch and dinner in their area acknowledging their dining room facility was somewhat limited. Our room was very comfortable, very clean and quiet. Good comfortable beds. The hotel is by the beach with a courtyard swimming pool overlooking the ocean. Our room had a fabulous view of the ocean and there is nothing in between the hotel and the ocean. Their cleaning staff and the director of guest services, Angela, were just extraordinary. I have never dealt with more honest people in my life. Four days after I had checked out of the hotel, I realized that I had dropped my wallet, $275 worth of Canadian dollars, somewhere in the closet below the safe and the wallet was probably out of sight from the cleaning staff. The cleaning staff retrieved it for me and the service manager sent it back to me by Fed Ex, following my delivery instruction. I have never dealt with more honest people in my life. Mario

title: “Has it All”
text:
The Independent is a great find in the never ending search for hotel that doesn't look or feel like every other chain hote. Unique entrance, incredilble service during check in process by a knowledgeable, corteous, professional young man named Jim. His suggestions & directions for our evening were all wonderful. What a pleasure it was to interact with an individual who actually seemed to enjoy his job.
Once in the room, we were very impressed tasteful Decor, wonderful size, very comfortable bed and the bathroom with exposed brick walls was excellent. 
If you like a boutique hotel in a great location with wonderful service stay at The Independent in Philidelphia. 
No negatives about our stay except we wish we could have stayed longer. We will be back!

title: “Fun stay..Hard to beat the location.”
text: My wife and I stayed here for 6 nights. The location is the best part of this hotel. The rooms are nothing fancy, but we just used it as a place to sleep at night, or to rest our feet for an hour or two during the day. All of the major sites are close by. We rented a car, and had to pay for parking, which is quite expensive. That said, if you're worried about how much things cost, you either didn't do much research, or you shouldn't be going to San Francisco in the first place. We used the rental car to drive to Napa and to Stanford.

title: “Business trip - great place”
text:
Got a great rate here for a trip and stayed for 2 days. great value, good vibe, clean rooms. Close to tech companies, union square, central location. 
very helpful front desk.

title: “Pay the extra 20 bucks and stay anywhere else”
text:
Any motel that you have to drive down an alley past a chinese restaurant and 2 cop cars should have screamed to us to turn around. We decided to keep our reservations anyways, but that was a mistake. 
The drug deals and meth addicts/hookers in the parking lot, meant we rushed right to our room. There we were hit with the stench of smoke and chemicals (despite being a smoke free room), a burnt comforter covering stained sheets, strange stuff on the walls, a non-draining sink with no hot water, a moldy shower, thin tiny towels, a TV with bunny ear quality signal, and a toilet that had been glued back together. 
I will admit that I tend to not leave reviews when I'm rather neutral on the subject, but this motel was a slum. Nothing has been "refreshed" as the website claims, unless you count the dirt that might get washed off during a rainstorm. I've spent 27 nights in hotels over the past year and this wasn't the cheapest one, but it was the worst. 
Please don't stay here if you want to enjoy your trip to beautiful San Diego.

title: “Average, at best - needs to do better....and they charged for freephone!”
text:
Stayed 1 night as part of a longer business trip. 
Was excited by the name and the reputation (and hadn't checked any reviews), but was disappointed by the experience
Room was extremely small, and didn't have a bath. I think the room was for people with disabilities given various bits and pieces in the bathroom. That said, anyone with a disability could not have gotten through the bedroom into the bathroom, given the lack of space. Shower-only meant the bathroom got flooded when shower was used. 
Air con unit was very noisy, and to turn it off meant the room was too hot (I couldn't get the window open). 
I had to make a call to the taxi company and i used the W phone in my room to call the freephone number - i got charged 2 dollars... not a lot of money but it's the princple... Woman at reception agreed it was out of order, but didnt offer to remove it! 
A constantly busy reception area, lots of people hanging around...the bar staff were totally unfriendly, i waited ages to ask to see the wine list and got it handed to be by some surly wannabe who was looking in another direction as she passed it over... then had to wait ages again to order the (mediocre but expensive) wine
Also a lot of rooms had left meal trays and plates outside their room which were there when i arrived at my room (7pm or so) and were still there 4 hours later. 
Overall impression pretty poor I'm afraid.

title: “Great Staff!”
text: Traveling on business, I stay at The Hotel Indigo quite often. I'm always well pleased with my stay much due to the great front desk staff... more particularly Lisa and Tom. Always going above and beyond to make me comfortable and assure a good restful stay, I cannot speak highly enough of these folks.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: We stayed here about 3 years ago. Great location and rooms. Will definitely be back.

title: “unusual place”
text: This hotel is located in an old building and they have done a fair job of fitting the rooms into the existing building. On the plus side, the front desk staff are friendly and accomodating, you can walk to a number of restaurants and down to the water from here. The down side, the elevator is iffy, the downstairs where breakfast is served smells mouldy. I never expect much from the free breakfast, they have eggs and sausage which sat in warmers for hours. Weird the free light show in my room.....

title: “The BEST”
text: I don't waste time writing reviews on hotels or anything else for that matter that I don't like. This Hotel just happens to be one of the best hotels in NYC. Why? The management & staff are the best that you will find anywhere in the hospitality industry. I have never been treated better in any other hotel in the city. That includes The W, Tribeca Grand, City Club, Morgans & many more. The room size was more than adequate & exceptionally clean. The hospitality starts as soon as you go through the door & are at the front desk. After checking in head to the lounge & Benny, Rebecca or Jolene will make you the best martini in the city. The location is also hard to beat. Just a couple of short blocks to the subway on 23rd & 7th. Will I go back? in a heartbeat!Thanks to Al, James , Parker & Tamara & all of their staff at Four Points Chelsea.

title: “The Hard Rock lives up to there name!”
text:
Go for the experience and you will love the service.
I had some needs that had to be addressed during my stay at the Hard Rock. All of the staff members were really 'in tune' to help me address my needs and make me feel like a total VIP.
I would recommend this hard rock again and again.
smiles

title: “Just what we expected and a little more...”
text: A good value for money hotel. Near to all the sites, places of NYC. Perfect location. It's near all of the major things you want to visit in walking distance. Only Wallstreet and 9/11 are far away. Times Square/Broadway 12 min. Top of the Rock, Chrysler building, 5th & Madison Ave, Grand Central, etc. ... all around the corner. Big rooms with all you need. Good food at the National. Pity the bar closes early at about 10.30 p.m.... but a couple of good ones nearby.

title: “Had a pleasant stay!”
text:
We were in town for the Chicago Marathon, and stayed here because it was walkable to the start/finish of the race (Grant Park), and could nicely accommodate 4 people in a suite. The location was great - everything is within walking distance, and the staff was friendly, helpful, and accommodating.
The decor of the rooms is a bit over the top, think "circus" theme, but I thought it was fun and different. Our suite had a HUGE, jetted soaking tub, and window seats the size of a twin bed (someone could easily sleep on one). The room could use slight updating, but really, it was fine. 
If you're a light sleeper, make sure you request a room away from the trains (which run right at the end of the block). We could hear them all night long in our room, and it was a big problem for two of us. If the hotel hadn't been full, we would have switched rooms. 
Loved the free nightly wine reception in the lobby, and the Wii is a fun touch and would be great for kids. Also loved the free wifi. The attached hotel restaurant was good, but not great; I wouldn't eat there again over all the other great places in Chicago. 
Definitely recommend to travelers looking for a reasonably priced 4-star hotel.

title: “Excellent hotel in Beverly Hills”
text:
My family and I checked into this hotel after a 2 night stay in Disneyland. My daughter got car sick on the way, and the hotel was very nice in sending up milk and cookies to the room as soon as we checked in.
We have stayed at some of the nices hotels in Beverly Hills and wanted to try out the SLS. They did not let us down. They checked us in and upgraded us to a nicer room. The Concierge and front desk staff were excellent with directions and suggestions. The location was amazing. You are a few minutes from Santa Monice, Rodeo Drive, The Grove, and walking distance to the Beverly Center.
The rooms are very nice, and the bed were extremely comfortable. The bathrooms are very modern, and the shower experience is unique. My daughters took 2 baths and showers a day just to have fun in there. 
I had a massage in the spa, and thought it was very nice. It was private, and plush. The spa staff were very accomodating. Would definitely reccomend using their services.
The hotel restaraunt, Bazaar, was very good. It is one of the highest rated in the area. There is a long wait to get reservations, but if you are staying in the hotel, they get you in immediately. You must experience this place. The food was great, and the decor is one of a kind. You don't want to miss it.
The pool is on the roof and very nice. There are cabanas to use, and the wait staff were very attentive.
I will be staying at the SLS everytime I come to Beverly Hills from now on. You really can't beat what you get and how you are treated.

title: “Decent stay in NYC”
text: This is a standard Hampton and great location for a trip to New York. The room was clean and the staff helpful. Free wifi was great. The only real complaint was the incredible amount of noise the house cleaning staff made. They were constantly shouting and using their radios very, very early each morning and overall pretty rude. We would stay here again for the right price but would probably look elsewhere next time.

title: “Great for solo-travelers”
text:
I did a last-minute booking (upon arrival to NYC), just opening a map and pointing my finger to the Times Square. So, in terms of location - it's excellent! (the street itself is quite scary thou:))
The room was tiny (couldnt unpack my suitcase), a bit noisy, the bed small (i called it 'mini-double':)), and the carpet - smelly... but i was too tired every night to even care!
Not sure about the prices with advance booking, but for me it was a 2-3 star quality hotel with a truly superb location

title: “Perfectly Priced, Located, and Fab Service”
text: My husband and I and our teenaged daughter spent the weekend for my son's SD university Parents' Weekend. We ended up spending more time at this fun boutique hotel than on campus, and my son opted to stay with us in our hotel. The hotel is chic, the service wonderful, the food from both room service and the restaurant was first rate, and the location right next to Petco Park and one block from the main drag was perfect. The 4th floor rooftop pool was so nice - away from the noise of the street, but enough going on (there's also full screen TVs in the rooftop bar to watch the Giants win the pennant) Our room actually faced the bar/pool which made me a tad anxious as to noise, but we heard nothing whatsoever. We walked everywhere, and had rented a Prius, so the overnight parking fee was cut in half (take note if you're staying - the parking rate is $35 which seems like a lot but all the downtown hotels charge the same - there is a public lot across the street for $20, but with the hybrid car rate of $17.50 we had somewhat of a bargain) Also to note: dogs are welcome - there were 5 or 6 staying, but we rarely saw them, and were glad when we did. (Heard no barking.) Something else to note about downtown San Diego in general: LOTS of homeless around (and I'm from San Francisco!) but it seems they mainly hang out down near Broadway - very sad.

title: “Thank you for a wonderful stay”
text: Everything I requested was furnished. The cleaning attendants were fabulous.

title: “Beautiful (but tired) Historic Hotel”
text:
We stayed with our teenagers overnight in this beautiful - but slightly tired - historic hotel and had a wonderful time. The kids loved the old world ambiance of the lobby.
STAFF: The service and staff were excellent! 
LOCATION:The location in downtown Boston is within walking distance of most things: The Commons, Downtown Crossing, Faniuel Hall, the New England Aquarium.
PARKING: Valet parking was $42 (but if you stay beyond 1PM the following day they only charge you an extra $12.) 
BREAKFAST: Breakfast is served in the grand old hotel dining room (like a trip back in time with it's high ceilings and potted palms). We chose the buffet for $23 per person. The usual selection of cereals, fresh fruit, juices, scrambled eggs, bagels, smoked salmon, etc. but they also have a chef on hand to cook omelets or eggs to order. In retrospect - had breakfast not been included in our package - I would have chosen something off the nice A La Carte Menu which would have been less expensive. So only do the buffet if you plan to eat a lot.
BARS: Not very exciting. There are two bars onsite - the Last Hurrah which is open all day and has the atmosphere of a cafe and the Parker Bar which opens at 5:00pm and is, disappointingly not nearly as nice as one would want it to be - we were looking forward to an old fashioned romantic bar with low lighting, deep leather chairs and dark wood but, it doesn't quite work and feels more in need of an atmospheric update than anything else.
ROOM: Rather than two rooms we went for a 1 bedroom suite which had a king bed in one room and a pull out couch in the other. The most important aspect of this room was that there was no door between the bedroom and the sitting area so there was no privacy. Still, the room was spacious and the price was good for the space (520 sq. ft.). Select a high floor and ask for a view or you may find yourself looking out on a wall. Our view was very nice and we were lucky enough to have a corner room so there were views from every window.
BEDS: The King was incredibly comfortable! But the couch was incredibly UNcomfortable. The kids didn't want to share the couch so we also asked for a roll away bed which proved more comfortable than the couch. 
BATHROOM: As others have noted, the bathroom was small but sufficient for our needs. Only we couldn't seem to get the plug to stay open so when showering the tub didn't fill up with water - we worked it out but I can imagine that this might really annoy someone paying so much.
HINT: Sign up for to be an Omni Select Guest - it's free and you get bonuses like free Wi-Fi, and hot coffee delivered to your room with a newspaper first thing in the morning - it's great!
I think that's it. Boston was great, the kids liked the hotel and the MIT Museum & the Mapparium (both great for teens). All-in-all I wouldn't book it again because it just seemed a bit tired to me but the price point for the room size (so we didn't have to get two rooms) and the location were good.

title: “Excellent Location & Service!”
text: The Back Bay Hotel is in the perfect location! Within walking distance to Newbury St (Shopping), The Prudential Center (shopping & duck tours), Boylston St (Restaurants/Shopping), The Freedom Trail/ Boston Common & much more. Just a 10 min cab ride from Little Italy if you didn't feel like walking. The rooms are very nice. My only complaint is that they could use a 'deep clean.' The bathroom had some dust along the baseboards, lamps and the remote control was very dusty. All of the important components were clean (bed linens, bathroom linens, toilet, sink, tubs & floors). The service is very good, valet was super easy to work with and same with the concierge! I would definitely stay here again, you just cannot beat the location!!

title: “Great Place to stay.”
text: We arrived a little early and only had to wait an hour, so we had lunch then our room was ready. It was great to get in before check in time. The location was great. Close to so many things, we just needed the subway to go to the museum of natural history. The hotel staff was wonderful from the front desk to the tremendous help from the concierge desk. There were 4 of us in the room, my husband and my 11, and 15 year old and there was plenty of room. The room was clean and comfortable. It was a great experience and I would recommend this hotel. Jaw 8

title: “Worst Hostel ever in my life!”
text:
The rooms (and the hotel in general) were far from clean. There were still hairs on the basin inside the room from the previous occupants.
The first room we got (so called "en-suite") had a toilet inside the room (not on a different room or with a door separating beds and toilet) running water all night just 2 metres from the beds. 
Following day, we got locked in the basement (where the lockers for the luggage were) because somebody left the door of the lift open on another floor and the only access was using the lift! Not safe in case of a fire and I have my doubts that it is legal to have such a space without other means of access especially when considering that all the electric wires were on the ceiling, exposed and clearly in a dangerous state.
For more than one day there was no hot water available for the shower and the towels available for the shower were dirty (we bought our owns and refused to use the ones made available!).
Unfortunately non-expensive places in NY fill up rather quickly, therefore we couldn't afford to move somewhere else so we had to spend an entire week at West End Studios & Hostel.
The location, albeit not close to the centre, was not too bad considering that tends to be considerably cheaper than central locations.

title: “GOOD!!!”
text: Clean and tidy, comfortable bed. Good location!!! Have some pastries / tea/ coffee for Breakfast in the hallway which you can take it to your room. Got a free glass of wine every evening. The restaurant is good too. I love this hotel :) Simple and Lovely!!!

title: “Good choice if you have business downtown”
text:
I only stayed here for only one day, but it was a pleasant stay. I've always found the service at Omni hotels to be excellent, and the Omni Jacksonville was no exception. Everyone was friendly and helpful from the moment we pulled up.
I recommend joining Omni's frequent stay program (Select Guest) - you get free wifi as well as complimentary coffee / tea delivered to your room each morning. Also you are automatically checked in when you arrive.
The room was spacious, comfortable, clean and relatively quiet. The king size bed was excellent. The bathroom had a huge countertop so plenty of space to spread out toiletries, etc. I had no problem accessing the wifi in my room. There was no street noise that I could hear. The only complaint is that the heat was somewhat noisy when it kicked on and off. Also I didn't see a personal safe in the room. I was only staying for one night, so it didn't really matter, but I'm used to having one to store my laptop or items I don't want to carry around. 
The hotel is walking distance from the riverfront, with a performing arts venue and shopping mall / food court just around the corner, but otherwise, this part of downtown Jacksonville seems a bit of a dead zone after business hours. The hotel restaurant is adequate, but if you're staying for a long time it may be better to be in a different location with a car to get around (or be willing to pay the parking fee). Overall though, I would stay here again if I had business in the area.

title: “a little disappointed”
text:
I was looking forward very much to our weekend visit to One Washington Circle after a nice conversation with Ian at reservations and booking the Bed and Breakfast package ($149 during the summer months). He had forgotten to mention in the e-mail confirmation that we were coming on this package so I brought it to his attention and requested he resend the confirmation. I got a cool response from the head of reservations without a personal note of any kind or confirmation. It simply said "You are coming on the Bed and Breakfast
package". I thought I had made a reasonable request, considering it included parking and breakfast. Ian was kind enough to upgrade us to the largest suite on a high floor. We had no trouble with noise at all. The suite was a little run down and depressing and the bathroom was very small. I was surprised the hotel was just finishing up renovations. Breakfast was fine, valet parking was promt. It took a call and a visit to the front desk to have them remove the parking charge from my bill, which of course they did. As someone mentioned before, housekeeping was strange. The first day we left at 8 and came back to freshen up at 3. The room hadn't been done. The next morning she knocked at 8:30 while were still dressing. I believe they are stiving to be a good choice in the area, but some kinks need to be worked out. Maybe others would enjoy the amenities of the room more and not be bothered as much as I was by the decor. Still the value was excellent.

title: “Nice, but would try others in the area”
text: Hotel was very nice, clean and friendly staff. A little off the beaten path. Taxi's rides were short, however I think we only had one friendly driver out of a dozen or so. It was nice to have no tipping services throughout the hotel, for sure a plus.

title: “The resturants are excellent”
text: I had the pleasure to stay at the Town and Country is association with a national convention. I ate often at the Terraces Resturant and was served by a fabulous wait staff. While all servers were exceptional Pati Muklevicz really stood out as pleasent, prompt and pleasent. I would return to the Hotel and resturant just so see Pati. The entire experience was wonderful!!! Thank you so much for the wonderful 7 days.

title: “Better than Perfect”
text:
I picked the London NYC among all other New York hotels as the best place to go for a romantic weekend during which I planned to propose to my girlfriend.
Julie Andrews, Executive Assistant, took care of my reservations and any questions I had with great professionalism and friendliness, which made me immediately feel welcome. She helped make this trip the most memorable time of our lives, no less.
Upon arriving at the hotel, we learned that we had received a free upgrade from the Sky Suite to the Apartment Suite (worth twice more), and were received in our room with a great bottle of champagne, delicious truffles, and more. I was truly wonderful; we both felt like royalty, and it made the perfect setting for the proposal. 
The Apartment Suite is truly luxurious, very, very spacious, and contains everything anyone could need during his stay in a hotel - large tub, two showers, huge masters bathroom, workspace with a flascreen TV, dining table, kitchen with microwave, fridge and freezer, living room with huge flat widescreen TV, a large bedroom with yet another flatscreen TV, plus amazing views in three directions (including Central Park, Hudson River and Times Square) through large windows that you can even open.
For the following two nights, I had reserved a Vista Suite on a top floor (49th), which felt just as luxurious, but in a smaller size that was still large for a hotel room. A bedroom as large as, or bigger than most hotel rooms I have seen, but with an adjacent living room just as big, plus a large bathroom with a huge shower containing two seperate shower heads (normal on one side, rainshower on the other side).
In both cases, the bed was most comfortable, there was no noise coming from outside (except some wind noise through a window that wouldn't close tightly in the masters bathroom and the occasional siren from an emergency vehicle, but nothing that could wake us up), and the rooms were very, very clean. In the Vista room, I asked for a vase, then later for a spoon, and received them both times quickly by a very professional employee.
The only downside I could find is that the TV could have been bigger in the Vista's bedroom, but that is probably only because I'm a fan of huge TV screens that aren't very good for your eyes anyway. Also in the Vista Suite, some water tends to drop on the floor out of the shower, but that's nothing an extra towel on the floor can't fix.
Every employee I met were most friendly and professional, from the Executive Assistant who took my reservations down to the cleaning lady who filled up my ice bucket for me, genuinely happy to help me in any way she could. I noticed some people have been complaining about the front desk employees, but I've had only great experience with them, be it while checking in, checking out, or in between. Doormen are most helpful and greeted us every time we passed by, pushing the revolving door for us or quickly calling a taxi when we needed one. As for the concierge service, I would say that the quality of the suggestions we were offered depended on who offered them, but it was always offered by a friendly employee who was always ready to serve you.
Finally, the hotel couldn't be in a better location, a few blocks away from everything: Central Park, Times Square, subways, theatres, restaurants, etc. 
Of course, all this luxury, space and comfort comes with a price, but I firmly believe it was worth every penny. I don't think you will find a better value for this kind of luxury anywhere else in downtown New York. Oh, and by the way, she said Yes!!

title: “perfect location”
text: We had a top floor room, plenty of space for the four of us. Wonderful stop- see the bean, the art gallery is truly world class, the Ledge is scary, the shopping excellent,the zoo terrific and free and having a cocktail in the John Hancock bar after the sun goes down is unforgettable- be patient, it is well worth the wait. The rooms are good, the pool wonderful in the summer and the staff friendly and efficient. Three minutes walk to the magnificent mile- my shopaholic daughter was in seventh heaven.

title: “We would definiatley book again! The Westin's outstanding staff really made this stay memorable for us!”
text:
Me and my friend had an absolutely amazing stay at the Westin San Diego!
A lady by the name of Michelle made our reservation process quick and easy, Leon at front desk gave us a warm welcome on our arrival and concierge Andrew was extremely helpful with getting tips and information on the local surroundings and fun things to do. Andrew also recommended a great spa for a massage, which was probably the best we ever had!!
We were very happy with our room; it was extremely large, very clean and had a great view of the water.
We enjoyed the breakfast buffet every single morning throughout our stay, where we were served by a very professional and cheerful young man by the name of Nate. I trust that he could make even the biggest morning grouch smile!
The complimentary airport shuttle was a great bonus for a carefree trip to the airport.
We would definiatley stay again!
NM+MS

title: “Hyatt Always Delivers”
text: It’s been my experience that you can’t go wrong with Hyatt. Even at this enormous hotel I still experienced high service levels, clean rooms and great amenities. Ask for a renovated room and/or a river view. The river view rooms are amazing, especially on the higher floors.

title: “really REALLY disappointing”
text: I foolishly assumed that the orange "NEW" logo on SPG.com meant that the hotel was actually new, and not an old hotel purchased from another chain. The rooms are not standardized like most Four Points. The furniture is dated, TVs are old, broken lampshades, stains EVERYWHERE, broken closet door, peeling wallpaper, etc. I could go on, but I paid a bargain rate; otherwise I would have probably checked right out. A few good points: carpets seemed new and clean, and comfortable Aeron desk chairs (that's about it). Room service prices relatively high compared to most other FP properties. Slow internet. I would NOT recommend this hotel, there are countless others nearby. Starwood obviously paid a bargain price to buy this property from Radisson, and then did the absolute minimum to convert it to a Four Points. Truly shameful.

title: “Underwhelmed, Better Places to Stay in NYC for the $$”
text:
I stayed one night in the Waldorf for a business trip lay over in NYC. When I arrived at the hotel in the evening, I expected to enter into the Waldorf's legendary lobby, but was met at the door by the member of a security detail with an earpiece who pointed me off to the side. No greeting, no explanation of why I couldn't walk through the lobby and no verbal direction of where I needed to go to check in. I understand that there was an event going on that evening, but at a hotel of the Waldorf's purpoted caliber, there should have been someone greeting arrivals, not a security guard pointing to a hallway.
When I finally got to the check in desk, the clerk was friendly and courteous. My room was clean and decent-sized for a NYC luxury hotel. I ordered a BLT through room service. Delivery was prompt and the sandwich was substantial, although it was slightly less expensive than a steak at other hotels.
Overall, I was underwhelmed. It's a great historic landmark to visit, but they don't have guest service to the degree of a Four Seasons or a Ritz.

title: “Fantastic”
text:
I have just returned from my trip to Chicago & can safely say that the Sheraton exceeded my expectations.
From the room to the staff, everything was excellent. The concierge staff recommended some great restaurants too, first off, Chicago Cut Steakhouse, which was along the riverside, where I had one the best steaks I've eaten & then there was the Grand Lux Cafe overlooking Michigan Avenue that had the biggest & juiciest rack of ribs you could ever ask for.
When I return to Chicago I would definitely be returning here.

title: “Friendly and service oriented staff”
text: I was so impressed more than anything with the staff of this hotel. I met Phil Baxter, the GM, at their beer tasting event. He was so friendly and service oriented. Edith at the front desk was so helPful and got my room totally square away. Marcela morales and Maria Gonzales were all smiles and very helpful at the restaurant both times I went to have breakfast. And once in said restaurant Patty was so accommodating and made me feel at home even though she was busy between numerous tables. This attention from top to bottom made my stay so much better.The only drawback I thought was the kind of slow service in the bar.

title: “Good value”
text:
This is not the Ritz so the 5 star review is based on this hotel category. It’s a nice updated hotel near the highway, very close to the stadium. It’s 15 minutes away from the zoo and downtown. Parking lot is sufficient and there is also a garage parking. The hotel was full during our stay, so the garage was full but there are parking spaces in the lot. Not issue with parking when we arrived around mid night. Next to the hotel is a small plaza with restaurants and Jack In the Box. The Thai restaurant in the plaza was very good. Across the road is another shopping plaza with more fast food, a super market, and gas stations.
We are priority club members and the front desk staffs knowledge that. They gave us cookies and a cold bottle water upon check in. Front desk staffs were very friendly and professional. The best staffs we’ve seen amount hotels. A+ for them. We have a double room facing the front on the first floor. We could hear the road noise even thought it wasn’t too loud. The beds are not queen size as advertised. They’re double size beds so it’s tight for 2 adults. The linens are nice, the towels are thick. The pillows and beds are comfortable. The sink is outside the bathroom and it works well if you have more than one person in the room. The bathroom is big with a shower over tub and toilet. It’s a nice touch to have plenty of shelves around the shower/ tub to put the toiletries.
We had breakfast at the hotel and they were very good, and good value. The omelets were delicious, the home fries were very tasty, and the toasts were very good, too. The service was a bit slow, so don’t expect a quick breakfast. The staffs were very friendly and they worked hard to meet the customers’ needs.

title: “Must stay here”
text:
My husband and I stayed here this past weekend and cannot say enough about what a lovely time we had. We did stay on the Gold floor, and were treated spectacularly by the staff. Our room was lovely and clean, if somewhat small. Elegant nonetheless, and befitting its age and history.
We felt very welcome, and the lounge was a spectacular bonus. We enjoyed the plentiful and delicious breakfast and hors d'ouvres, as well as the honor bar. Some evenings it was simply nice to relax and play Scrabble with a glass or two of wine!
There are negatives to every hotel review, but anyone unhappy with their stay at this lovely hotel should probably just not travel.
Well located to see all main spots of Boston. We walked to Fenway, Quincy Market, Boston Common... great location!
Highly recommend, can't wait to go back!

title: “Much To My Surprise”
text:
My first experience booking with Hotwire and at first I felt deceived, which is still somewhat true.
The hotel is going under renovations and when we first entered the room it was outstanding, but no water. The management was very accomodating to switch to another room and yet another, and finally we were settled to a wonderful staff and stay.
We were even compensated to complimentary parking.
Hotwire fails to mention that their is a parking fee, plus a fee to use the health club facilities which is connected with the YMCA.
Overall, I recommend it highly!
The best feature of the room are the beds which comes with a down comforter. These were updated.
Located smack in the middle of downtown, walking distance to many wonderful restaurants and attractions. Great time!

title: “Rooms are great, restaurant not so much”
text: This is not up to par with other Marriott properties. The room was excellent, as excepted, but the restaurant was just so so. I have been at other Marriotts and I have had better breakfasts and even the service was just ok. The hotel is obviously convenient if you are catching a flight and in that respect it is just the comfort and accessibility you need, otherwise, the Renaissance, downtown Columbus would be a better choice.

title: “Hip décor, tiny room, well-located”
text: I had stayed at another Morgans Group hotel (the Clift, in SF) and decided to give this one a go. Both hotels follow the same standard - impressively designed common areas and rooms a bit on the spartan side. Convenient midtown location (in Hell's Kitchen, actually). My room was smaller than the one I had at Clift's, but as the heater didn't work I got upgraded to a considerably bigger one. Service was impersonal. I especially enjoyed the bars - had a great burger while watching the snow fall down at Hudson Hall and great cocktails at the Hudson Bar.

title: “Great Service, Average Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Hilton San Jose for a week in July, from Monday to Sunday. The Hilton is attached to the San Jose Convention Center, meaning that is is very convenient if you're attending a conference there. This is a good hotel, but for a Hilton is a little lackluster.
Good: The location is right in the middle of San Jose, and easily accessible via the light rail. It's about a ten minute drive to SJC. Parking, while a little on the expensive side, is available and easily accessible in the parking garage located beneath the building. There are some good restaurants and a brewpub within walking distance. The service was also outstanding - the room was clean every day, and they even put a nice little towel underneath all my toiletries.
Bad: This is the first hotel I have been in in YEARS that DID NOT have wireless internet. WIRED internet is available (and quite fast), but it kind of restricts you to you leaving your laptop on the desk. If you bring a longer Cat-5 cable, you can connect up, but it's still a pain. The building itself and the rooms, while nice, are definitely starting to show their age. In general, the hotel, while nice, needs an update. This hotel is also right under the approach path for SJC, but the sound padding seemed to reduce it to a dull roar.
Overall: If this were a Holiday Inn, it would be an extremely nice hotel. But when you affix the Hilton name to it, it loses some of its luster because I generally expect more from a Hilton. Nothing extremely negative to say about it (other than the lack of wireless), but not quite up to the level of other Hiltons that I've stayed in.

title: “great hotel with style”
text: We had a chance to stay at the Westin and found it to be really pleasant. It is located in the area near the bustling Rittenhouse Square shopping and restaurant scene, yet was close enought to the business district for our needs. The staff at the Westin made a big difference in our stay. We enjoyed meeting Khalil Reed who ended up being really helpful during our stay. He was our 'go to' guy for all manner of things and really made the hotel and the city come alive for us. It is clear the Westin staff is highly motivated to treat guests well. That is something you don't see too much of anymore.

title: “Wouldn't stay there again”
text:
No free wireless internet; Amenities were lacking. Bathroom door was on a spring, so couldn't stay open without propping it open...No refrigerator in room, although there is a space for one. Safe located awkwardly in the closet. GM unwilling to prorate my weekly internet rate even though I was unable to access internet wirelessly for a day (engineer came to check it out, no explanation given). No service guide in the room...wanted to order room service but didn't know what I could order. Perhaps they didn't have it. Important to note: valet parking is $32/daily (in/out privelages) or self park $24 (no in/out privelages). Was disappointed overall. Okay experience with children, but if I were traveling with my sig other, definitely would have changed hotels if possible.
Note: construction site across the street, so expect to hear some pounding and drilling during the day.

title: “Great hotel”
text: We had a great experience at this hotel. Staff were very friendly. The hotel has been recently redecorated. The pool area was very clean with ample seating and fresh towels. Kids had a great time! The rooms were clean and neat. Beds were comfortable. We had dinner at the restaurant which was really great!! Waitstaff was very friendly and food was delicious with huge portions. The restaurant is nicely decorated. The same area has Starbucks coffee in the morning and pastries for sale. Even though thus hotel is by the airport, I never heard one airplane from the pool, lobby, restaurant or our room! I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Fine place, great location”
text:
New York has so many options that it is always hard to decide where to stay within a range of prices. The Sofitel is just steps from my office, which means also steps from the 5th Avenue, Times Square, Central Park, the Chrysler building, the Empire State building... honestly, location is fantastic.
The hotel feels quite small, actually. I have no idea how many rooms they have, but feels tiny, with a small entrance, a small restaurant, a tiny lobby and more tiny corridors in the floors. My room was OK, with a very comfortable bed, not impressive furniture, a good shower with excelent pressure and all nicely appointed. Unfortunately, soundproofing is not the top quality of the rooms, and in the morning I could hear a very disgusting noise from my neighbor, who seemed to be sick just when waking up. I stayed there four nights. Rooms was cleaned to perfect standards. 
Breakfast was not buffet and the tables were small, so not easy to set up a breakfast for 4 or 5 people. Still, products of top quality, delicious croissants, all very French. Hoewever, the service was not relaxing at all, making the start of a business day already a business day. People on holiday may feel that too. Had lunch one time, very nice, Sofitel style. Also had some drinks, bar looks nice and trendy.
Concierge was helpful, as so were the bellboys. Reception was helpful, although it took a while to do a check-out of the three rooms I was paying for.
All in all, not a remarkable stay as that was not what I was looking for, but all perfect and functional at usual NYC prices.

title: “Great location, Weak WiFi”
text: First off, the location is great! It is 1 block away from the wharf and convenient to a lot of tourist attractions. I was told the hotel had been renovated and the rooms were very cool and nice. The bathrooms could have been a bit better but was clean overall. I had a conference at the hotel so it was very convenient to go back and forth. There is also a very cool fire pit area outside where we spent a lot of time grabbing drinks and relaxing. The one thing that I had a major issue with was the WiFi. The signal was weak and terrible! For the price they were charging for so called "high speed" WiFi the signal was bad. I called the lobby twice to ask about it and the engineer even admitted the signal may not be that great and I should come downstairs to the lobby and use the free internet. I was not about to come down at 12AM to use so I just let it go. I have stayed at a lot of hotels and nowadays with such a reliance on fast WiFi I expect hotel to do a better job and provide a good service. I let the manager know it was unacceptable to be charging $10 a day for really weak service and hopefully they do something about it. The price for the room was a little too much as well. I understand it is in a great area and they have to compete but the hotel is not in the category of the price they are charging per night. Overall rooms were nice, service OK, location great!

title: “Fairly contemporary, but very pricey”
text:
As a summary, we had an incredible deal from an independent website for our room at the Alden. Otherwise, I would say the pricetag doesn't really match the product. We only saw a "standard" room--that is what my review is based on. This is a good hotel, no doubt. But not an elite "four star" hotel (yet?).
We stayed at the Alden-Houston in February of 2012. We traveled to Houston to attend a symphony event. The Hotel seems to be in a fairly good location--we could see Minute Maid Park from our room (probably about a mile away), and we were four blocks from Jones Hall. A street over on Texas Ave. and about a block down, there seemed to be quite a few bars and restaurants.
There is no parking for guests. Valet only. However, street metered parking is free after 6:00 p.m. on Fridays and through the weekend (if you can find a spot--we did luckily).
The room was fairly basic and fairly small, but comfortable enough. It was clean for all intents and purposes. The furniture had been re-arranged by a former guest, from what it looked like, and was not put back, but no big deal. Also, there was a beer glass, presumably from the bar downstairs, that was left outside our room and not picked up either day we were at the hotel.
The bathroom was nice--it had a large walk-in shower and contemporary Kohler fixtures, which was neat.
All in all, this looks like a hotel that is working hard to build up a good reputation, but I would say the rooms aren't quite ready to be in the $170 - $200/night range yet. Although it looks like they are trying to offer a sleek, modern design to rooms, it is still just an attempt. We would stay there again if we got the same great rate, but they are also a couple blocks further away from certain entertainment venues than other hotels. We definitely wouldn't pay full-price for a standard room. For comparison, there is a hotel directly across the street from Jones Hall that is $30 or so cheaper than the Alden's rates booking directly through the hotels...

title: “Hotel Monaco Chicago”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Monaco for two nights in mid-August of 2012. We had two River-View Mediterranean suites, 1411 and 911. Overall, we had a very enjoyable stay, but it wasn't as great as we were expecting it to be. Both suites were very good values and were of good size, although not as big as we expected. Kudos on the extremely comfortable sofa bed, something all too hard to find today. The rooms themselves were a little worn, chips and scratches, which was odd considering how newly renovated they were. On the downside, all 4 TVs had terrible reception. Not only that, but housekeeping was very spotty, turndown wasn't standard at all - one room didn't receive it at all. In addition, toiletries, including hand soap weren't replaced in one of the rooms. Another strange thing, though not the fault of the hotel, was the fact that a man from the adjacent building was peering into the Hotel Monaco with binoculars... a little creepy. All the employees we interacted with were very polite, so the service on the whole was excellent. That said, we had to wait until past 3 for one of the rooms, which wasn't a problem since we had two, but that was still a little annoying. They did get our NYTimes paper preference correct, which was very nice. The iced tea in the lobby was very good, and the free wine/sangria hour was nice before going to dinner. Although we didn't need it, we were informed coffee makers could be delivered to the rooms. The location was great, close to the L and to the sites. Yes, there was some street noise, but that's to be expected. The views from our rooms were great, especially from the comfy window seats. One note of advice, although we were at the end of the hall and didn't have this problem, the elevator music was extremely loud and may be a problem if you are close to them. Another strange thing was that if you're a Facebook fan of the hotel and indicate this on the reservation, you get free cupcakes, but even with 2 rooms for 5 people, we only received one, not even one in each room. The inner circle amenity was nice, and the mini bar credit which we only got for the other suite (again, strange) is always nice. Overall, we'd definitely stay here again, especially if we could get the same rates as this time.

title: “Very Pleased”
text: Traveled to NYC as a birthday getaway with my husband and the Benjamin did not let us down. The room was not outstanding but it was clean and and cozy. It was a nice size and included all that we needed and a little more. The location was great. It's right in the middle of things making getting anywhere you want to go easy. The staff was very helpful and friendly. After a couple of days there we felt at home. The only thing that I wished for was more available doormen. When we could find one, they were helpful. Other than that very minor issue we were very pleased with our stay. The value was great and we would stay again.

title: “Second Stay at a Ritz Carlton”
text: It was nice. The guests seem a bit on the stuffy side compared to the Four Seasons, and the room, bathroom and closet were quite small. It was very clean, the bed was comfortable, and the Club room had very good food. As far as service, when I arrived, there was not a "do not disturb" sign to display on my door and I called and requested one, which never arrived. Housekeeping was a bit stingy on soap, I had to request extra after every cleaning, there were plenty of towels, however. The Westend Bistro downstairs was amazing. I would highly recommend that.

title: “was unsure of this place but was...”
text: was unsure of this place but was surprised at wonderful location to shopping,eating and activities at the wharf. wharf inn much less expensive than nearby name hotels. parking available at Inn for no charge. would highly recommend

title: “OK if you get a good deal”
text:
We were pretty worried after reading all the negative reviews here, but we were pleasantly suprised by the Grand Hyatt. We visited with our 2 small children and requested 2 adjoining rooms. Initially, they put us in 2 double queens but when we called and requested a switch to 1K and 1 double Q they were nice and made the switch promptly. We found the rooms to be clean and adequate-the room had the stuffy, polyester floral quilt decor that you would expect from a Marriott. Our room was clean though and we left a note along with our housekeeping tip each day asking for fresh towels and we always had a nice clean room and fresh towels when we returned at the end of the day.
Our rooms had great views, although the first night we were woken by the noise from the trolley (once at 1:30 and once at 3:30 am) and I am NOT a light sleeper...and we were on the 14th floor! It was louder than I expected. But I didn't hear it at all the following 2 nights. Also, the walls were indeed pretty thin. I could hear people talking on the other side of our wall. Luckily, there were not too many other people staying on our floor-otherwise I would have been pretty stressed as it's hard to keep the kids totally quiet. 
There were indeed a lot of conventioners, but it seemed like the hotel did a good job separating them into the other tower away from vacationers so we didn't feel intruded upon. 
I had a great massage by Holly in the spa. The hotel had a convenient location. Overall, we had a pleasant stay. I don't think we would ever stay there again if it were just my husband and I traveling alone but for 2 adjoining rooms at $250 a piece, it was an OK deal...next time we travel with the kids though, I'd be tempted to try the Gaslamp Hilton. I bet we could get comparable rooms for even less. I'd give up the views.

title: “Bugs and Smell we didn't stay!”
text: The room smelled moldy and musty. There were 2 large cockroach type bugs in the bathroom. We did not stay!

title: “Beautiful view, Terrible customer service!!!!!”
text:
Myself, Wife and 5 month old daughter stayed in December at this Hiliday Inn as a christmas treat. I booked one of the rooms with a view of the Empire state building months in advance, and specified the need for a cot for our infant daughter at the time, 'no problem' he was told. We arrive in the early evening to an amazing view from our hotel room window of mid town NYC and the Empire state building in all its glory, Then noticed the lack of a cot. We contacted reception and were told one was on its way.... some hours later still no cot. I went down to reception at 10pm when we could wait no longer to be told then that they did NOT have one as they were allocated on a first come first served basis, then proceeded to hand me a pile of blankets so our baby could sleep on the floor!!!! Needless to say she did not but spent the night in our bed (against our better judgement). We copmplained to the manager the following morning who promised faithfully that they would have one for our second night. First day sight seeing done and exhaustion setting in we returned to our room at 8pm only to find AGAIN no cot for our daughter with a message from management saying they did not have one and for the inconvinience we could have some extra priority points and breakfast! I could not believe this, they expected us to put our baby on the floor again! At this point we had had enough and I went and demanded they got one from a near by hotel and was not moving from reception till they did, needless to say they found one after some frantic phone calls.
We have never had service like it, I simply could not believe that after pre-booking a cot they could (after check in) just not supply one and expect us to put her on the floor, as if we would! We have complained to holiday inn and it would seem that despite their satisfaction promise, mentioned all around the hotel, the customer service is as poor over here as it was there, we have been passed from pillar to post and still no joy, Still trying though.
My advice..... if travelling with children to NYC and are happy to have them sleep on the floor then by all means give it a go, if like us you're not so keen and want a bed provided or even decent customer service then I would give this one a wide birth.

title: “great location, great staff, cute retro style hotel”
text:
We booked this hotel on the recommendation of a friend who lives nearby and said it was centrally located. It really is! It is walking distance from the Farmers Market, The Grove Mall and the La Brea Tar Pits. There is a restaurant attached where we had breakfast several mornings. The pool, while not too large, is clean and convenient. There is a 7-11 and a Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf a few doors down. Across the street is residential condos. 
The rooms are small and basic. It was nice to have the mini fridge in the room. I liked the retro feel of the architecture outside, very 1960's rat pack! :-) 
Others have complained about the noise, our room was on the back side and the only thing we heard was one morning the garbage truck came to the houses on the street. Maybe its worse if you are on the other side, but its not a major intersection with people honking or anything that extreme. Just regular "cars driving by" noise. 
We paid $121 per night (Wednesday thru Sunday) which was a reasonable price in my opinion. Also the woman who was usually at the front desk was very nice and gave us some advice for our trip to LA. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “A real gem”
text:
The Chatwal is a small boutique hotel with well designed rooms and public areas in an art deco style.
Service on our three night stay was excellent and attentive from all members of staff. On arrival we were upgrated to a delightful suite. But the real discovery is to find a hotel in a quiet side street in the centre of New York that is just a few paces from the madness of Times Square! We thoroughly enjoyed the style, rooms,can-do staff attitude and location. We'll be back!

title: “Run For Your Life And Health!”
text:
The pictures show a "charming old hotel" which was something I was looking for. The reality couldn't be more different. No security, dirty, broken elevator (it has been broken for 8 months, could you believe it?). The tini tiny room was dirty, the carpet rotten, stains on the linoleum floor of the bathroom, the walls were rotten and appear to be made from cardboard, I am not lying. I complained with Travelocity and they told me they have been having too many complaints from this hotel and gave me a $100 certificate in return. I spent only one night and head for the Holiday Inn across the street for only $30 extra per night.
You want two words to describe this hotel? Homeless Shelter!
See the pictures attached to this review, you will see what I am talking about. PLEASE< PLEASE avoid this rotten hell hole, I am being serious and objective here.

title: “from south wales to southgate”
text: stayed there for 5 nights.. right in the heart of the city which was close to all the shops and sights.... hotel was amazing with view of the empire state building from our room....hotel staff were very friendly and the room/maid service were excellent.... i would recommed this hotel for anyone going to new york...

title: “Nice location and hotel--noisy”
text: I've stayed at many hotels on the Mag Mile in Chicago and no other was as noisy as the Marriott. Evidently this hotel is not insulated as well to block out sirens and city noise. The amenities were nice, updated and the location good. Staff was helpful. I would stay here again if the rate was good because it was a comfortable stay, other than the noise.

title: “Great in every way.”
text:
large beautiful upgraded room in great location with fabulous view and every amenity. 
would stay there again without a second thought.

title: “Mayflower Park Wonderful”
text:
Wow! What a wonderful hotel - such a shame we could only stay one night.
Location - Convenient to just about everything Seattle has to offer.
Rooms - Beautiful! Clean! Just like the photos.
Staff - Wonderful! Helpful! Funny! The Concierge was a riot who was also very, very helpful in booking things.
Room Service - for tired travellers it was quick and delicious.
Would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to stay in Seattle, it was a pleasure and when we can return again this is where we'll stay.

title: “Great view and a great room”
text: My boyfriend and I had the pleasure of staying on the 14th (top) floor. We had a view of the water/ships, city, even planes landing. We loved the the conveniences and furniture. Great for a romantic city stay or business traveler. Parking was $10/day though.

title: “Home away from home besides a few negatives”
text:
Upon arriving at hotel for hubby's business trip (my 1 yr.old and i came along), we were greeted by friendly front desk personnel by the name of Wen. Were shocked to see how small the efficiency room was that the hubby's company reserved for us. Talked to Wen (and remind you, it was a Sunday) and he contacted the hotel's sales manager and she contacted my hubby's company and we got upgraded to a one bedroom on the company's dime. They both went out of their way to accommodate us! The one bedroom is much more suitable for a family.
Room is spacious and the bedroom is seperate from the living room/kitchen/bathroom. Only complaints i have is that the entire second and third floor smell like curry powder. BLAH. The third floor and our room reek of it. The property has a nice pool that is upkept well and a nice grilling gazebo area with two newer grills and tables and chairs. Hotel is right off of Westheimer Road, which is a main road in Houston with tons of restaurants and shops. Weekly, the hotel puts on a meet and greet every Wednesday and provides free food and beer/soft drinks. Nice way to meet people. As far as feeling safe here, there are shady apartments behind the hotel (seperated by a tall fence) and we did not feel threatened during the day or night outside because the hotel has security at night time. It isn't an area that you can walk to things though. Westheimer is a four lane highway and the area has some shady characters walking around. There is a sonic right in front of hotel for last minute food. The staff were absolutely wonderful and accommodating and became like our family while we were here! Would reccommed this hotel to out of towners and business people.

title: “More rooms than the elevators can handle”
text:
This is a typical NY tourist hotel with lots of school kids on their trips to NY, lots of visitors from Europe (welcome!) and lots of great places for tourists to visit within a couple blocks from the hotel. In other words, I avoid places like this like the plague if I can.
This was my first return to the hotel in many years and it has been nicely updated although the wall graphics ( photos of places in NYC) make it a bit over-the-top. 
The room i had was nice, if over-priced, but taht is the price i paid for not making reservations earlier and it was the only hotel that was available for less than $500 a night last week near the offices I would be working in. 
The biggest complaint, other than hundreds of teenies standing around in the lobby waiting for their teachers was the elevators. It is a computer fix to a problem for big hotels with only 8 elevators where you tell the computer the floor you want and it directs you to the elevator going there. There are no buttons in the elevators themselves. While this is not the end of the world, if you leave your room at "rush hour" to go down to the lobby, you can wait for 15 minutes as i did both days for a car with a space for one person. There were 30 people in line both days.

title: “hotel is ok”
text: Rooms are not horrible but not very clean either. Staffs are not very friendly and hotel is not really in a great location.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: We had a truly wonderful stay at the Westin. It was Charming, elegant and the position on Union Square perfect. The staff friendly and helpful at all times. Loved the twin showerheads and the glass elevator. Our room was on the 21st floor with a view of the bay in the distance.

title: “~I wouldn't stay anywhere else~”
text: My husband and I regularly stay here for our anniversary which always falls on the weekend of the 4th and during the Taste of Chicago. I have always used Quickbook and book the Executive floor with a king bed- non smoking, floors 32 and above. I have never had to request a lakeview, and have always gotten one with a great view. In fact we have always gotten the rooms with a view of the fireworks! . We both take advantage of the free self serve bar (wine and liquor, mixed drinks) and comp hot and cold hourderves, cordial and desert hour on the weekends, and great breakfast nibbles (incl smoked salmon, trout, and cheeses and real squeezed juices) in the executive lounge- all comes with the executive level booking. I woudn't pass up spending the extra on the E level, if you take advantage of the perks it more than makes up for the cost. The free health club with the saunas and full window showers overlooking the river are wonderful after a long day walking around Chicago. The museums are a decent walk, and if you get tired they do have free trolley, and the busses are cheap and come by every 15min! Location can't be beat, close to major attractions, easy cab ride to ones farther away. The rooms are spacious and I've never had any problems with noise- they are much quieter than other hotels I've been at. The bathroom is something I want in my house! All in all this is the place to stay!

title: “Great Place to Stay in Memphis but some issues...”
text:
We booked this hotel for 3 nights then added another making it 2 reservations through the airline we were using. I called the hotel a few weeks prior to arrival and they had both at that time but when we arrived only the one for one night exsisted. 
Claressa at the front desk worked hard to try and sort this out and altough we did not get a king as requested but rather 2 doubles which was all that was left, she provided us with access to other facilities and breakfast which we really appreciated. Thisng didn't go all that smoothly during our stay but the room was large and the view of downtown and the river was nice so try to get that side. 
Valet parking is very friendly although expensive compared to on street however may be worth doing it to save any possible damges from being in an unsecure lot across the street. 
The best part is the trolley is righ outside the doors and takes you to Beale for a dollar each way. The Main Street mall is there as well and we enjoyerd the walk from and to Beale and the river several times. 
Beds are comfortable. We would recommend.

title: “Decent NYC Hotel”
text: I've stayed at the Doubletree a couple of times for business trips. The location is great (the 6 is right outside, so you can transfer to just about anywhere). The rooms are small, but that's to be expected in a city like NYC. I thought the rooms were fairly quiet considering it's on a major street.

title: “Landmark hotel still has it!”
text: Enjoyed everything about the Peabody. Great location, staff very helpful, rooms small but very nicely appointed. Only a couple of complaints -- $10 per night charge for hotel services, i.e. interntet, health club, even if you don't use them. This really adds up for a multi night stay and I didn't use the services. Also, bathrooms are pretty, but very small with no counter space for toiletries, etc.

title: “Trendy place, friendly staff, but they miss too many marks when it comes to attentive service.”
text: The hotel is in a great location...you are right in downtown Chicago, a.k.a. the "Loop". The staff is friendly, yet they miss too many marks when it comes to paying attention to details and/or the lack of service awareness towards the guest. We found interruptions by maids as soon as we checked into our room, but I think this is how the protocol is with this kind of hotel. Their version of knock on the door routine is very poor as they practically walked into our room not once but twice, unanswered! We also had someone scratching at our door early in the morning, but it definitely wasn't preventive maintenance as a "No" sign was outside our door alerting them to keep quite. Again, the "No" sign is the hotel's version of "Do Not Disturb". Funny! Room service is prompt, yet missing silverware items for appropriate food groups was common. The restaurant had descent food, the server was friendly and knowledgeable, yet dirty silverware was obvious. As for the 27th Floor Rooftop, the bartenders would handle and give you the incorrect money back and some went as far as keeping your change. The dropping of the hotel room charge(s) underneath the door of our room at around 4am and a knock on our door was totally inappropriate and inconsiderate as well. As good as the valet was in getting your car they were not as good as giving you your keys back! All of this for 2 small complimentary waters I would rather they take a little bit more pride in their job, but I imagine this would have to start with the people at the top who dismiss teaching their staff a certain level of attentive service. I don't want to come off too harsh, but I feel these are positive criticisms that can help.

title: “Convenient”
text:
Stayed for one night having arrived at LAX before travelling further into the USA. 
Hotel shuttle was prompt for pick-up.
Reception staff were friendly and polite although a little busy. 
The room was clean and tidy and of a fair size. 
Checkout was just as simple. There is also a hertz car rental desk within the reception area. We had booked to pick up a car from the main hertz lax premises however having enquired at the desk in the hotel the rep arranged for pickup from there at no extra cost.
Located very near to the airport and within walking distance of the proud bird restaurant.

title: “We felt pampered”
text: My husband and I went to Hotel Drisco (which we had never heard of before) as a gift. What a wonderful gift it was for us! We've never gone to a hotel where there was someone to open the front door for us or where the front desk hands you a plate with warm wet wash cloths to wipe your face and hands after your long trip to get there. Nice touch! The room was lovely (A King Suite-Wong Room). It had fresh whole fruit in a basket ready to eat, robes and slippers for each person and some special treats for use in the bathroom. The bed was soooo comfortable and we are a bit picky when it comes to hotel beds. The continental breakfast was just delicious and there was a great variety of foods and beverages to choose from that morning. I'm so glad we were able to go, and we are looking forward to coming back when our anniversary rolls around.

title: “Good value and spacious accommodation”
text: This is a good value hotel offering spacious suites: kitchen, living area, bedroom, bathroom. It is located in the Hillcrest area of San Diego with a variety bars and restaurants and offers good access to Balboa Park, downtown and old town. The on-site laundry was good if you are on a long stay in the US and need to do washing. Staff were friendly. Breakfast waffles made fresh to order were good, although the buffet was limited. Free tea and coffee in the room was a nice touch. Would thoroughly recommend this hotel.

title: “Amazing stay!!”
text: I booked the room through orbitz.com, and got a very surprising rate. Upon check-in I discovered that the room was directly next to an elevator, and microscopic in size. Honestly, there is no way two people could have stayed in this room. Make sure you tell them that you do not want this type of room. I walked back down to the front desk, and explained that I was on vacation with my girlfriend and the room was far too small. Without hesitation, they upgraded us at no charge to an absolutely amazing room. We could not have asked for more. The room was on one of the higher floors with a south view facing the downtown skyline. The bathroom was extremely spacious (about the size of the room we had initially) with a large walk in shower and separate tub that was as deep as a swimming pool (amazing!). Room service was prompt and the food was definitely impressive albeit a bit on the expensive side. Then again, room service isn't cheap anywhere. The hotel is within walking distance of countless bars and restaurants in the downtown area. The hotel has a shuttle service that was very convenient as well. One of the employees, Tank, took us to a number of destinations in the hotel's car. Absolutely the nicest and most helpful person at the Icon. If you're looking for a place to eat near the hotel, ask to be taken to the Last Concert Cafe which is roughly a mile away on Nance St. It is a historic restaurant in Houston with great Mexican food. I cannot say enough about the Icon Hotel in Houston. Honestly I don't have a single complaint, and can't wait to stay there again. I've stayed in just about every nice hotel in Houston, and since the Warwick Hotel is no longer, I wouldn't recommend many other places than the Icon.

title: “Good Location, Clean Room”
text: My wife and I stayed here for a four night stay. Nice central location a short walk from Seattle Center and downtown. Bus stop is right outside the hotel and can take you almost anywhere you want to go cheaply and easily. Room was very clean and well equipped and the bed was very comfortable. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Would not hesitate to stay here again when in the Seattle area.

title: “Still ambivalent after all these years”
text:
This is really a 3 and 1/2 star review, but I couldn't bear giving them a 4 star review and telling you all to downgrade it slightly.
Over the last 10 years, I have spent at least 3 nights every quarter in the Galleria area of Houston, and try different hotels on a regular basis to see how they continue to rate. However, my last stay at the Omni was over three years ago because of an absolutely abysmal experience. But my secretary convinced me that because this one of our corporate choices (which I regularly ignore), that I should at least give it a try again. I succumb to my secretary's logic, but only to be reminded that while the Omni appears to try hard, it's all surface fluff, with significant underlying systematic problems.
Simply put, after a horrendous stay three years ago, I was allowed to have "Deja vu all over again", with another mediocre stay.
The Omni started by repeating their error of three years ago. I specifically order a queen or king bed everytime I stay at any hotel. I don't like full size beds, and would rather sleep in a sleeping bag. Three years ago I show up late (because I fly in at the end of the day), with a guaranteed reservation (we'll always charge your credit card .... because we can!) and they claimed they didn't have a king size room (they only have kings and fulls). After telling them point blank that I'd go to another hotel, the "found" one room - a king in a basement like area that was dank and damp. It was a horrible stay.
So when I arrived on the Thursday before thanksgiving, once again they pull the same stunt. Not even bothering to argue, I simply pulled out my trusted iphone, fired up an app, and had a king reservation less than 2 miles away.
