But I wanted to be sure that I wouldn't be charged on my card for cancelling because they couldn't fulfill my reservation. That would take finding a manager, which since it was after 11PM, I wasn't terribly thrilled about waiting. However, knowing the Omni's mindset that they could do no wrong, I decided to wait.
The manager came and understood why I was cancelling. He was quite nice, and miraculously "found" a king room after all. I was tired. I had to leave in less than 7 hours. I decided to stay. -10 points for the bungled reservation and the diffident underling service, +5 for the manager's kindness and service.
Since I drove, I decided to park in self parking - for which you get the honor to pay a not small sum to enjoy. I forgot that the garage is literally a 1/4 mile away from the elevators and THERE IS NO DIRECT WAY FROM THE PARKING GARAGE TO THE HOTEL THAT DOESN'T REQUIRE YOU TO GO OUTSIDE FOR A VERY LONG PATH. Seriously. Because everyone knows that it never rains in Houston (/sarcasm off), the Omni has there garage without an inside path. But worse, when you're in the garage, you have to either leave from the middle and take this meandering path to the hotel (which requires you to go up and down stairs without any handicapped ramps, great if your dragging a heavy bag), or go back out on the road and either follow the road to the hotel entrance (a good 300 yards), or go by the service entrance and follow a path along the back to come in through the outside restaurant (btw, this is the Omni recommended route - I guess they don't want you to be hit by a car and have the Omni have to fight being responsible). -25 points for the stupidity
This abomination is all the more ridiculous because it would be simple to make an exit to the open air parking garage structure where it nearly abuts the Omni, create a bridge over a small culvert and then put you to the back of the building, where an entrance could be easily made. I asked about this three years ago, and I was told "it's in the plans to be done soon". Guess what? I asked again - same exact answer. - 25 points for the repeated stupidity
Now having had all of this remarkable annoyance, the room was perfectly appointed - simply grandly beautiful with every detail. The bathroom is grand, and probably bigger than my first apartment. Note that there is no in room coffee maker. But, when I awoke at 5AM and went down stairs, there was a free open coffee station with Starbucks coffee - very nice detail. I didn't notice if this was still there after the restaurant opened. +10 for thinking of your customer
My other quality checks were also precisely met. The internet was fast and free - very nice. +10 The showers water temperature and pressure did not vary - another check for quality. +10 There were no unsightly but slight overlooked problems that can easily be found in most hotels (a screw missing from a fixture, a stain on the carpet, etc.) Everything was perfectly in order. I admire this attention to detail and no how hard it is for a hotel to do this. +10.
The breakfast buffet is above average, with the wait staff being very attentive. However, note it's very expensive if not included with your room (~$20)
So, once you survive the fight to get to your room, it's a lovely experience - until you have to fight to get back to your car.
With just a few simple changes (actually have the rooms you reserve, and fix the &%$#%! path to the garage), the Omni would be a 5 star hotel, set in a beautiful high rise business park. Until then, I'll wait another 3 years to give this another review.

title: “Best Hotel in Boston: Beautiful Rooms and Unbeatable Service”
text: Why haven't I found this hotel before! From the doorman to the front desk staff to the bellman and room service waiter the friendliness and service could not have been better. Great location adjacent to the harbor and near Fanueil Hall and the North End, with gorgeous rooms.

title: “Nice but a little corporate”
text: Great service, warm greetings but the rooms are bland design wise. Spacious but sterile picky I know but a little warmth would be nice. Fearing is as always superb.

title: “Best stay so far at New York, Times Square”
text:
Best location if you want to stay at times square, theater district. Staff were very helpful, they even gave me a times square view room at no extra charge. Rooms are comfortable and clean for a family of four or five (the rooms can have two double beds with an extra sofa). Free wifi at lobby and at an extra charge in the rooms. BIG lobby on the eight floor with restaurant and shops. 
It is a big hotel with 40 plus floors. Elevator service is great. 
It has been the most pricy hotel I have stayed in NYC, still IT WAS WORTH EVERY PENNY......

title: “Great Hotel in the heart of Time Square”
text:
This is my go to hotel when I travel to NYC. If you want to get a feel for New York this is your hotel. I stayed for 4 nights in August with my husband and 3 kids. Here are my Pros & COns:
Pros:
-Walk out the lobby and BAM! you are in Time Square
-Rooms are spacious and modern- comfortably fit my family of 5.
-The TKS booth is acroos the street!
-Very close to the subway and taxis are everywhere
-Broadway is right there!
-Great shopping, food and entertainment close by.
Cons:
-It is very pricey-then again it is New York CIty
-The elevator system they use is very quirky
-The conceirge lounge is nice can be very busy in the morning. I am business traveler and a Marriott Gold member and have never seen a conceirge lounge get so busy. This was very annoying- i was here on business.

title: “Rude manager”
text: We stayed at this hotel in mid-January and while we found the rooms to be nice the manager was any thing but nice. To check in took us over an hour and a lot of attitude. We asked if we could get two double beds and were told because of the rate we got we couldn't without paying an additional fee. We then contacted Travelocity who contacted the hotel but the manager refused to give us the room even tough they weren't full. We ended up rebooking through Travelocity to get the room we wanted. The manager couldn't of been ruder. There are so many good hotels in NYC I wouldn't return to this hotel.

title: “Amazing! Best place we have stayed EVER”
text: What a gem! Staff are cool, friendly and helpful. Decor&rooms are cutting edge. Had an amazing night out thanks to tips from concierge. Location is central and so much to do near by. I run my own business and expect a lot from my holiday and this is the first time I've had no complaints! We used the bikes and the skateboards. Great addition. We are a mid 30's couple who like to find the 'find' and the nolitan is defo it! Even the yoga Matt was great... Stay there!

title: “Excellent hotel, highly recommended”
text:
Definetely not the cheapest hotel in LA, but very well located + very confortable.
Wifi rules are ridiculous (you have to pay 15$ per day per device) - if you have a PC and an ipad, you shoyuld pay 30$ per day (unless you know how to make your PC a wifi hotspot).

title: “What an Experience!”
text: The Brown Palace is absolutley amazing. From the location to the chocolates on your pillow at night with soft relaxing music playing - This is as good as it gets!! I loved being able to walk anywhere I wanted to go and the variety of things to do. This has got to be my favorite place to stay anywhere. I can't wait to go back again! The Brown Palace is my new favorite getaway!

title: “Just Your Average Westin Which is OK”
text:
As a Platinum SPG member, I stay at lots of Westin hotels. First time at this Westin. Experience was unremarkable with the exception that this Westin has a club loungethat served a decent breakfast - eggs, juice, toast, muffins, croissants, various cut up fruit, and oatmeal. 2 free computers and a printer in the lounge was a bonus. For $152 prepaid, this is a good deal. It is right next to LAX with free shuttle so very convenient. Yes, there is airport noise, so if planes landing and taking off are a problem for you, stay somewhere else. It is a busy hotel. It has the normal Heavenly bed and other pleasant furnishings.
Would I stay here again when departing early at LAX? Yes. Would I stay here for any other reason? No.

title: “close to airport.”
text: shuttle runs on the 1/2. food good, rooms small for embassy suites, seems older. average for this kind of hotel, a little dissapointed.

title: “Good, but just getting by.”
text:
On one side it's a marginal neighborhood and on the other up and coming. The property is in need of updating, but isn't bad it just seems to have been getting by. Now with the ballpark down the street and the new condos/apartments going up I hope the owners get on board.
My room was good, but was closer to roadside motel than major city hotel. Desk was broken and in danger of collapsing, something somebody should have caught. Toilet seat was like an amusement park ride until I tightened it up, again something somebody should have caught. The bottom line is that nobody seems to be attention to details....which is a shame because the property really does have potential. 
Thank goodness there's a McDonalds across the street as the $15.00 breakfast buffet is overpriced for what it offers....all or nothing and coffee isn't included.
I really want to like this hotel because there is so much potential, I just wish the owners would get it together.

title: “Love the Beds at this HGI”
text: I hadn't stayed at an HGI in a while. I was driving in from Chicago late at night and wanted a place just outside the city limited along 65. I arrived about 10:45pm and the parking lot was well lit which is important to me as a solo female traveler. The staff greeted me right away and offered me some bottled water. My room was very clean and had everything I needed. The bed was the pleasant surprise. It is one of those that has a dial to control the firmness. I slept so well that night. Usually I wake up a few times but I didn't once. The breakfast was excellent and the staff in the restaurant was very friendly. This may be my new go-to hotel for late night drives into Indy.

title: “Family trip to Boston”
text: We recently visited Boston with our two children, ages 2 & 4. The Hyatt Regency was centrally located between many of the places we visited, including the New England Aquarium, Boston's Children's Museum, and Boston Common. Each destination was easily within a 15 to 20 minute walk. We found our hotel room to be spacious & clean and made for a comfortable stay. The pool in the fitness center provided a nice place to unwind with the kids after hiking around town all day. While the breakfast buffet at the hotel is a bit pricey, the food selection is extensive and the staff is kid-friendly and accommodating. Chef Deirdre & our waiter Ardjan went out of their way each morning to entertain our children and make our dining experience memorable.

title: “Spectacular view, clean and friendly staff.”
text: We live less than 20 miles from Seattle. It is great to enjoy our beautiful city like a tourist. The view from our room was spectacular. We watched the sun set over Elliott Bay and the Olympic mountains. The staff is very friendly. There are plenty of restaurants and bars to go to within blocks. And of course the Pike Place Market is right below.

title: “The best place to stay in San Antonio”
text:
I've stayed here over 10 times on business and pleasure and there's no better place in San Antonio. This is especially true if you have kids. They will love playing in the pools and slide. Kids under 5 have their own pool and eat free in the restaurants.
The hotel is located on top of the tallest hill in SA and right next to Six Flags Fiesta Texas. It is also close to Seaworld. Most rooms have very nice views (except first or second floor) but the best ones are the pool view rooms. The best rooms are on the 3rd floor with a large pool view balcony (above the exercise area). These are the only rooms in the resort with a balcony large enough for sun bathing (besides some suites and villas).
Jr Suites are not worth the price because they are located in a bad corner and your window/view is actually smaller than regular rooms. Unless you get upgraded for free, don't pay for jr suites. However, the big specialty suites are worth it for special ocassions because you get the entire circular room (above the restaurants) with floor-to-ceiling windows and a separate bedroom. it also connect to another room to create a 2 bedroom suite. views are even better then from the restaurants. These are spectacular.
Villas are nice and large ones have kitchenettes but most are not much larger than regular rooms so make sure you know what you're getting. They are also a good walking distance from the main building. Villas have their own pool but it is small. Consider renting a golf cart if you want to go back and forth (restaurant, main pools) or have kids. They are good if you plan on playing golf and want to be near the club.
I rarely eat in hotel restaurants but this hotel is the exception. Most menu items from both restaurants are good and reasonably priced. To get good rates, check out the hotel's promotions and be sure to ask for government, aaa, or senior rates if you qualify. They recently advertised $199/nt including 4 passes to Six Flags.
This is the place to be when visiting San Antonio. Especially if you don't want to be with the crowds at the Riverwalk.

title: “Loved the Orchard Garden Hotel”
text:
We spent three enjoyable days in this hotel by default. We were travelling with 5 other friends and noticed 5 days before departure that we had booked another hotel to the one our friends were staying in. Having trawled the web we liked the look of Orchard Garden and its location. It is on Bush Street which is central(beside chinatown gate) and within a short ride of everything. It is san fran's first eco hotel(visit website).
A warm welcome met us on arrival and our room (double) while a bit on the small side was perfectly formed. Extremely comfortable bed with crispy bedlinen, free Wifi, flat screen TV. Marble bathroom with good lighting and toiletries. Buffet breakfast was included in our deal,juices,breads, fruit, cheese, cold meat,excellent. Breakfast menu available at an extra cost.Staff discreet and polite.
Overall this was a very positive experience for us. We felt safe and cared for. 300$/night B&B

title: “Lovely hotel, ideally situated”
text:
We stayed here as a couple. Hotel is lovely and clean, with complimentary breakfast, which had lots of choice, including cereals, fresh fruit, yoghurt, cooked breakfast, toast, bagels, and you can try your hand at making your own waffle!
Ideally situated, and close to the Magnificent Mile shopping area.

title: “Uber Stylish Comfort but Charged for Every Little Thing!”
text: The W Westwood is a truly hip, fun and comfortable hotel. The rooms are decorated beautifully, the staff is sweet and accommodating without being cloying, the restaurants are yummy. It's stylish while still plush. BUT, and this is a big one for me, they charge for EVERY LITTLE ITEM. And they charge A LOT. $32 A DAY for parking, $35 per USE!!! for the steamroom (crazy i know), $15 per day for the internet. It was totally infuriating. I truly can't get over a luxury hotel charging guests to use the steamroom. Don't dinky motels provide spa amenities free of charge? It just feels cheap and mean. Until they change these pricing policies, I will stay away.

title: “amazing rooms!!!!”
text:
the size of the room and charm of the hotel were great!!! a bit touristy area but that makes it exciting. best feature of room???? a long hallway away from the door which minimizes the hotel hallway noise.
looooooved having a fridge and microwave in the room!! and was able to walk around the beds, had a sitting area etc. highly recommend.

title: “Great Location but Loud”
text: We just got back from a one week stay at the Grand Hyatt in New York. The location was perfect for us as we used the subway system daily to get all around the city. Although the hotel is adjacent to Grand Central Station, you certainly don't hear the noise from it. The rooms are certainly not like typical Hyatt rooms. They are small with VERY SMALL bathrooms and lack the overall class of other Hyatts. The walls between rooms are ridiculously thin which can be problematic if noise bothers you. My room had a connecting door to the next room which made the situation even worse. I HIGHLY suggest you request a room WITHOUT a connecting door. The great location outweighed the noise for me but the noise certainly bothered me. We were on the 27th floor and could still hear the traffic outside so I doubt you are going to be able to find a very quiet place. Downstairs in Grand Central Station there are a lot of decent places to eat or grab pizza, bagels, baked goods ,etc.

title: “wouldn't stay anywhere else in Chicago”
text:
I stay at embassy suites in general because I can count on a good value and a standard of quality that I require. What sets this Embassy Suites apart
is the level of service and the culture of hospitality in every department.
My recent trip was during a huge snowstorm. My arrival was late but check
in took no time at all.The front desk staff took my coat and bag so that I could go right to the restaurant without going to my room first. When my departure was delayed and delayed my stay was extended with ease and empathy for my situation. As I had checked out before I knew that my train was cancelled, the front desk called house keeping who cleaned my room immediately. 
The staff made a real difference for me and their cheerful assistance was 
appreciated!

title: “Great place to stay in the city”
text: We are locals but needed a place to stay for the night. This was inexpensive and a great quality experience. The location with in Chinatown was convenient to subways. The room was quiet and very clean and modern. Service was super friendly and helpful. Everything we could have asked for during out short stay. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

title: “Beautiful Place to Stay”
text: I was a little worried about staying here but once we arrived, we knew it was the right place for us. The landscaping is beautiful and makes you feel like you are in a tropical garden, very Hawaiian. The pool and hot tub area are clean and beautiful. Upon our early check-in we were given a room that had not been renovated yet. I have to admit that we were very disappointed in this room and called the front desk to ask for another room. Although they were unable to change our room that night, they did change it the next day for the rest of our stay. The lower level king bed room that we stayed in had a nice patio complete with patio chairs and a table that faced the interior garden area (pool). There are some rooms that face the marina and some that face the harbor. Our first room faced the harbor and San Diego skyline, however, the parking lot and road are also there which I felt were noisy, not as peaceful as the garden rooms. There are no elevators so if you have an upper room, there will be stairs to climb. It appeared that upper level rooms had shared balconies with the room next door. This would be easily verified with the hotel front desk. The beds were pretty comfortable and the rooms with king beds were very roomy. We plan on returning to this hotel the next time we are in San Diego.

title: “My Last Stay on December 18th”
text: I have been staying at the InterContinental Barclays for the last 8 years. The service is impeccable and the rooms are bright and cheery. Most importantly, the people at the Guest Relations desk go out of their way to make your stay pleasant. Annmara Gayle always welcomes you with a pleasant face and tries to make sure that I get the room that I want. She always goes out of her way to make sure that my stay is excellent. My stay at the InterContinental Barclays always feels like a second home. When I come to the room, I always have fresh fruits and bottled water.

title: “NOT what we expected from a 4 * property”
text: Arrived at 1 pm and told that 4 of us (2 parents, 2 kids - 11 & 13 y/o) would have a king bed and no rollaways because the 2 double bed rooms were committed. The desk clerk offered extra bedding so the kids could sleep on the floor! All the rollaways had been "committed" as well. I paid $79 on hotwire for this room (the hotel was charging $89 on their website) due to low demand of the holiday season. I told the concierge my problem and he advised to call back at check in time at 3 pm to see if anything changed. The clerk who answered at 3 quickly informed me that there had been no changes and that they didn't expect any. The end. So I called hotwire at 6 pm before going back to the hotel. They agreed with me that this was unacceptable and tried twice to reach the hotel to see what the issue was - no one answered the phone. Around 7:30 pm we went to the front desk again and asked if there had been any changes. At that point we were offered a conference room suite with 2 rollaway beds. We took that option just so the kids could have a bed to sleep on, but my husband and I ended up sleeping on a very uncomfortable pull out sleeper sofa. This conference room did not have any beds, just a pull out sofa. We had asked for the rollaways around 7:30 I believe. At 9:30 they finally arrived. I made 2 phone calls to make sure they hadn't forgotten our request. Our kids were exhausted because of an early start to the day - and even at 8 pm wanted their beds - the fact that it took 2 hours to get them delivered - is not good service. I would probably not return to this hotel; however, it is close to Chinatown and the Circulator bus route so I would recommend it to others with a warning to make sure you clarify exactly the kind of room you want.

title: “Incredible experience!”
text: That sums it up! From the doorman who retrieved my bags to checkout, every staff member was friendly, acomodating, and extremely helpful. The hotel is immaculate and modern. Had a nice view of Inner harbor, even if it was 4 blocks away. 5-10 minute walk to Inner-Harbor with direct access to Convention Center, and Camden Yards right behind hotel. Great pool, except jacuzzi wasn't warm enough) and large workout area, nice restaurant, and bar. Minor drawback is that there is a WIFI charge of $10+ per day, which I don't feel is reasonable. What made the experience even more enjoyable is that I felt I was getting VIP attention since the occupany rate was below 30%! I highly recommend this hotel to everyone

title: “Omni is my new favorite!”
text:
I stayed at the Omni 1/13/2012 - 1/15/2012 in Room 517 while attending a business conference. From the moment I arrived at the hotel, I was greeted by Brandon - a very friendly doorman who offered his assistance with anything. My husband and I got ready to stand in line to check-in but within a few seconds was greeted by another employee (sorry, I didn't catch his name) who gave us our room key. I had requested an early check-in and they delivered! We bypassed the line and went directly to our luxurious room. I loooove the smell of the room and the entire hotel!!... like fresh laundry. Our morning beverages were delivered on time each day. The last night we were there, we were served room service by Tonya who works two jobs and had only 1 hour of sleep that day! We were impressed by her positive and upbeat attitude despite being sleep deprived. Omni... be sure to give kudos to her and to Brandon (mentioned earlier).
The beds were super comfortable; furnishings plush. Cool hidden TV in the bathroom mirror and you won't stumble in the dark.. as soon as your feet hit the floor, a light comes on near the floor and lights the way for you.
I will be traveling to St. Louis for business soon and look forward to the same excellent experience at the Omni Majestic there.

title: “Good price, but expect problems”
text:
I've arrived in NY i late evening. In hostel reception I heard that of course I have valid confirmed reservation, but they don't have free rooms ?!? I haven't got such serious situation in much more wild countries. But this is NY - the middle of civilisation ?!
Man in reception told me, that there is nobody responsible for that situation, and today it is impossible to solve the problem, so I should take myself and find any hotel as soon as I can (it wasn't easy). I returned to West Side Inn next day, they gave me back money for more expensive room in other hotel and gave me also little discount for next nights in West Side Inn. No simple word like "sorry". Next days I saw many times people on reception desk with the same problem. So I think - avoid this hostel.

title: “Golden butttered toast”
text: I stayed here on business one night. The property seems to be well managed - check in was fast and the reception employee had helpful information at hand about local restaurants and shopping. There are also workstations and printers in the lobby for printing airline boarding passes. I did not try any of the food options here so I cannot comment. The hallways could probably use a renovation but my room was clean and equipped with an LCD television, good desk and wireless internet. The gym was on the small side for a large property but had decent equipment. There is also a medium sized pool which I did not have a chance to try. Might be handy on longer stays. Parking was free and convenient. Overall, I think a good comfortable choice for business travellers needing or wanting to be near the airport. By the way, it is about 15 minutes drive to the rental car return.

title: “Excellent value for location and quality!”
text:
Just returned from our 17th wedding anniversary celebration trip to SF and Monterey. I used all of the info gathered right here on TripAdviser and I'm SO happy to have had a reliable source. This hotel's location was perfect- so close to the trolley and so easy to get to shops and restaurants. The room was bright and clean and we were rather impressed with the free wifi (high speed had a fee but the lower speed was free and worked great for internet surfing) as well as free movie checkout. We stayed in a very upscale hotel in Monterey which did not offer free wifi nor free movies so, in retrospect, this was a wonderful perk
The only downsides were the bed (a bit hard) and the lack of knowledge that the staff seems to have. No one could recommend where to get great coffee (shrugged their shoulders and suggested Starbucks, which there seem to be two of on every single block). 
BUT, for the price, I still rate this hotel quite high. It exceeded our expectations and we would happily recommend this hotel to friends.

title: “Horrible Service & Attitudes - Worst Hilton Stay In A Long Time”
text: All I can say is Wow - Wow in a bad way. The overall attitude of the staff from the moment I arrived to the moment I left was horrible - from the valet, to the front desk, to the conference wait staff, to the business center, to the manager - all just horrific. Internet runs up to $24 a day and self-parking is $18 per day - ridiculously high. There was never any attempt to make your stay feel special or that you were a welcomed guest. The property is actually fairly nice, but very spread-out. There are two large atriums that remind you of an Embassy Suites; however, the rooms are standard Hilton fare. Do yourself a favor and skip this one. There are many similar / nicer properties in and around the DFW area that actually welcome you as a guest.

title: “Not worth the money”
text: Recently spent 3 nights at the hotel and was disappointed. The landscaping on the property was a lot nicer than the rooms. The rooms were musty and the bed (a queen) was very soft. Only two pillows were provided and they too smelled musty. The rooms have a fride but no in room coffee pot. This facility is a temporary living facility as well as a travel hotel. People were coming and going all through the night. In addition, they had out actual keys, instead of key cards, which seemed a little weird considering this day and age. The continental breakfast was also disappointing. No healthy items were provided. It consisted of almost all carbs, bread, cheap doughnuts and cereal and only 1 kind of milk was provided. In addition, signs are posted tht you cannot take food back to the rooms (what's that about?) The front desk staff was a little rough around the edges and not so helpful. I will not book at this facility again. The rooms were not so clean and the cliental at the facility were a little unsavory. I know there are better value rooms in San Diego.

title: “Rare fine in the big city.”
text: My daughter, grandson, and I just spent a long weekend at the SCH. We had a suite that included two rooms, two queen beds and a sofa sleeper, and a kitchenette. It was huge compared to other places I've stayed in NYC. It was also clean. The continental breakfast was perfect for us, convenient with a nice selection of food items and drinks. My only disappointment was that no welcome basket was waiting for my grandson. I had written SCH asking for help in pulling together a little gift to make my 6-year-old grandson's first visit to NYC extra special. I was told they would put together a complimentary one, which would have been perfect. Unfortunately, it didn't happen. I just wish I would have known ahead of time, so I could have done something on my own.

title: “Why wouldn't you stay here???”
text: All Suite hotel, nice kitchen, seperate bedroom and living/dinning room. Comfy beds and pillows. Great for family's. Amazing rooftop swimming pool with view of washington monument. Friendly and accommodating staff, even loaded our car with our luggage while it was still in garage. Great neighborhood, less than two blocks to metro, whole foods & bus tour stop. Loads of restaurants within walking distance. 10 minute walk to lincoln memorial and white house.

title: “Lovely welcoming hotel with comfortable clean rooms”
text: Very welcoming hosts in an old building fully refurbished to a high and simple standard. The room was spotless, quiet and comfortable. One weakness was the breakfast. Best to skip it.

title: “Expensive for what I want from a hotel”
text: I stayed here this past weekend. I chose this hotel over the across the street Drury that I've also stayed at solely because I had a free night from my Priority Club Credit card that I needed to use. The location of either hotel is excellent, with very close proximity to the Arena, convention center and Short North entertainment district. We actually came in for an OSU game, with the campus a short drive (not walk) away. I stayed two nights, one free and one I pre-paid for to get the cheapest Advance (non-refundable) purchase rate. The room was o.k. and by hotel standards reasonably clean. We really didn't use any amenities other than the cable TV and 5 minutes of WIFI. I was told that the WIFI was complimentary due to my Priority Club status and that we also had a choice of discounted valet or bonus points because of it. I still need to confirm I wasn't charged for anything, as for some reason the hotel posted two pending transactions to my credit card of roughly $30plus. I don't have reason to expect that they won't get reversed on their own, but if not I'll post a follow-up to my review within the week. The room has the typical upscale foo-foo bedding do-dads that you have to find some place to put to sleep, but not as overdone as I've seen elsewhere. All in all nothing to complain about, but I can get the same nights sleep experience I typically want across the street a bit cheaper.

title: “Great Staff, Great Location, Lousy Elevator!”
text: This was my second stay at this hotel and I do like the old ambiance of the place, with the plush carpets, places for you to sit and the ease of entry. The staff are very friendly and I appreciated Jennifer's humor at the front desk. The elevator though was another story. I had to wait at least ten minutes for the thing. And the staff finally had one of their own operating the elevator. When I returned some hours later, the elevator again would ignore the button at the first floor and would not open unless someone from another floor happened to come to the first floor. Quite annoying. There was one guest who was being particularly obnoxious to the staff and the staff were calm in the midst of adversity which I appreciated. The room: I think offering four dollars for use of the bottled water was a bit much and the hotel should re-think its policy on that. The television was appreciated. The coffeemaker ran well and did its thing. The divider doors in 1203 do stick and not close correctly, but I didn't need that. Overall good experience. I would go again, as soon as they fix that elevator!

title: “excellent travel inn”
text: we have been staying at the travel inn 42nd street for the past 6 years and always exceptional value for money very clean very good position if your going and looking for a quality hotel you have got to try the travel inn you will pleased you did our son lives and works in ct USA is a regular visitor to the hotel , Ann & Peter Young Boston ENGLAND.

title: “Extremely helpful”
text: When we arrived at the Day's Inn I was so angry as we had been ripped off by the Taxi driver and was feeling really cranky, Tracey on the reception desk was great, she went out of her way for customers, Rooms are a little outdated but they were perfect for us as we were there to go to Graceland which is across the road,Breakfast was awesome, it was the best out of the 9 cities we visited while we were there. They even arranged a pink limo from Marlowes restuarant to come and get us for dinner... Yummo..

title: “nice hotel with pleasant staff”
text:
After a long and uncomfortable flight my girlfiend and I stayed at the Crowne Plaza for my birthday in june 2012.
We were welcomed by friendly and helpful staff who made us feel at home for our first trip to LA and gave us a few directions to certain places we wanted to visit on our first day there.
the room was very very nice much better then we expected and the service from the staff was top notch but one staff member Cody stood out from the rest, he was fun to chat to and have a laugh with when he wasn't to busy giving other people great service and also helping us on our last day when we had trouble with a our transport getting back to the airport 
The breakfast wasnt the best but it hit the spot nonetheless
the dinner was pretty decent i recommend the beverly burger coz that was very tasty and filling
the staff in the bar area was very good and they were very polite.
will certainly look to stay at this Crowne Plaza when were looking to stay in LA again
Thanks to all the staff we met there ;)

title: “One of the most important events of your life--plan to celebrate here!”
text: On Labor Day weekend 2012, our daughter and her new husband celebrated their wedding reception at the River Inn. We reserved 19 of the 28 rooms at this boutique hotel. In addition we hosted the reception at the River Inn Hall adjacent to the hotel and added a tented venue to hold additional guests. The quaintness of the River Inn as well as the unparalled service made their reception more than a moment but rather a weekend event. Most importantly for those reading this review, our reception was close to being a complete rain out due to a severe thunderstorm that came through the area. The entire team at the River Inn from Trisha to the gentleman at the front desk and Patrick made sure the guests were moved from the tent to safe areas at Tuggs, Paulettes or the River Inn Hall. When the weather let up, the hospitality team walked guests in and out of the buffet area and back to their seats with umbrellas to make sure everyone was served the excellent dinner prepared by Paulette's restaurant and remained dry for the rest of the celebration. Jill made sure that every room we reserved had all the small details that were requested such as children's cots, cribs and guests gifts were delivered to the rooms. It is easy to find places that will tell you what you want to hear. It is hard to find places that deliver with exceptional quality and above and beyond the expected. The River Inn is an establishment that makes each and every person feel special. The rooms are warm and inviting, the lobby peacful, the SMALL BAR fun and Paulettes.....well who doesn't want to eat at Paulettes! If you want to stay at a place where you breathe a sigh of relief when you walk in the door, this is it. AND if you want to hold a special event at a place that is more than a moment but a real experience, do it HERE!

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Very nice hotel - clean and comfortable. Stayed two nights in a suite with our 2 greyhounds. Staff was EXCELLENT! Only problem was the location - getting in and out was tricky due to the amount of traffic coming on/off San Jose Blvd, and I-295. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Pleasantly surprised.”
text: We stayed at enVision for 3 nights in late August. We absolutely loved this place and the friendly staff. Hello Reid and thank you for your endless patience with all my questions! The beds were so very comfortable. We had a quiet room at the back of the hotel overlooking the park. I would definitely stay here again. This hotel is not across the street from the T line but just a short walk away.

title: “A nightmare...”
text: This was definitely the worst hotel experience we had in years: The room we have been given was extremely dusty, there were lots of hairs in the bathroom and the leather cushion of a chair was completely ripped apart. We complained about the room in a friendly way and they have shown us 4 different rooms, that looked exactly the same (dust, lots of hairs, broken doors of closets, defect refridgerators...). Even the service person who carried our bags said, that he would not stay in one of the rooms for this amount of money per night and said they seem to have a problem with housekeeping. Afterwards we took one room, which was acceptable (although also not in a good condition) and found several bloodstains on the bed when we were going to sleep. The next day we had an appointment with a manager, who reacted quite harsh but at least after some discussion gave us one free night (of our six nights in total). The hotel definitely needs a renovation and we recommend to avoid this place in Seattle until then.

title: “Awesome Hotel!!”
text: Great hotel! Great staff! Great breakfast, and complimentary water, sodas, fruit etc. Love the fire place...Will definitely be back!

title: “Boutique Hotel with a ton of class”
text: Excellent hotel with wonderful staff that are very knowledgeable and attentive. The milk and cookies every evening and breakfast every morning were greatly appreciated by our entire team. A team of 12 people stayed here and we hosted a client reception in the downstairs private bar with pool tables and it was perfect. Everyone enjoyed their stay and the party was a hit. I would highly recommend this hotel in the heart of downtown Denver and walking distance to the Colorado Convention Center and many great restaurants, shopping and sites. I don't believe there was a pool or spa.

title: “Happy with this hotel choice”
text: Just got back from 3 nights in Memphis on vacation and enjoyed the Springhill Suites (stayed in the new building). Clean, rooms updated attractively, staff friendly. The bed was very comfortable and happy with the room layout of a couch and kitchen area too. Nice to be on the trolley line to take down if we didn't feel like walking. It is difficult to find and GPS/Mapquest directions won't work, followed someone on trip advisor's directions. Very nice breakfast in the morning too. This would be a good hotel to use as a couple or family and a ways away from the Beale Street action. Pretty park across the street too, although someone on trip advisor mentioned it being on the fringe of the seedy part of town and I'd agree with that, homeless in the park, etc.which seems a problem in Memphis. Only complaint was coffee maker didn't work and no hand towels/wash cloths provided. We did self parking next door for the $12/nite fee to have our car handy. Good choice for the price, although if you plan to be out late partying on Beale St., the trolley ends at 11 and you would not want to walk the 8-10 blocks or so back to this hotel and may want to stay closer to the action.

title: “Very Dissapointed”
text: Ugh. We got a deal on priceline but it was still very expensive for one night. The room was large, but my husband and I had the choice of 1 single bed (huh??) or 2 doubles. Not the best when you are celebrating an anniversary. No coffee maker or minibar in the room, and for that price, very disappointing. Little things (soap dish) were broken in the room also. The fitness center closed at 7 pm Saturday, which is exactly when I wanted to go. The place was very clean and the check in staff were nice. Too little, too late.

title: “Wonderful Service and Clean Hotel”
text: We were greeted by the most friendly valet to start with. Then a very nice front desk person checked us in. We went up to our room and we never heard anyone else in the hallway or anywhere it was like we had the hotel to ourselves. The hotel has been recently remodeled in fact it smelt new. The beds were so comfortable and the decor was warm and inviting. There is a $25 parking fee per day meaning you need to check out by check-out time so you won't have to pay for 2 days of parking. This will be the hotel we stay at next time we head down to Hollywood. We went down to see a Disney show at the El Capitan theater and the hotel was very close like 2 blocks away.

title: “Historic Hotel in Great Location”
text: We chose the Prescott because of the Union Square location and great last-minute deal they were offering. We were delighted. It has historic charm and all the extras. Highly recommend the club level with wine reception and breakfast included. If you want a large Mc Mansion room and giant TV, forget it. But if historic touches, nice staff and good food matters, stay here!

title: “Second time there!”
text: Friendly staff and decent rooms for a reasonable price.

title: “Very Average”
text:
My wife and 16 year old son stayed here for 3 nights at the end of October. First impressions were promising. The location was very convenient for the airport and public transport (T subway system just 5 mins way away). The porter was courteous and helpful and looked after our rental car whilst we checked in and then gave us directions to the Budget drop off. Things then seemed to go downhill a bit. Nothing major but nonetheless tangibly. First thing we noticed is that no complimentary shampoo was provided in the bathroom (the second day we got a half-filled - obviously used - bottle and it was only the third day that we got a full, fresh bottle!). Next we found that the aircon fan only worked on the 'Lo' setting which was insufficient one day when the outside temperature was exceptionally warm for the time of year. Then we discovered that the swimming pool was so small (and only 3' deep) that it should really be called a kids splash pool - don't go there expecting to swim! Next we discovered than the in-room Wi-Fi was $10 a night. No problem, we thought, the business center has complimentary internet access - but it was so slow /unreliable it was almost unusable, and in any case the room was stiflingly hot. Next they attempted to charge us $42 for 3 glasses of wine (correct charge should have been ~$18). Rather worryingly, on another occasion after we had ordered a bottle of wine to take to our room, the bar tender opened a fresh bottle for us - and then gave us a 3/4 full partly-used bottle! After complaining he claimed to have got the bottles mixed up. I'm not sure he deserves the benefit of the doubt . We also heard of others being double charged for drinks.....
On the plus side, the accommodation was much as we expected (but not exactly spacious) and the beds were comfortable. Breakfast was OK, but nothing special. Overall, this Embassy Suites was not a patch on, and far more expensive than, the last Embassy Suites that we stayed in (Las Vegas) and has slightly tarnished our view of the chain.

title: “Comfortable and ideally located hotel”
text:
We found this hotel extremely comfortable during our short stay in New York. The rooms are quite small but there is plenty of space to move around, store suitcase’s and hang up your clothes – all you need for a city break as you spend very little time in your room. The room and bathroom are very well appointed and immaculately clean.
Although the breakfast area is crammed into the entrance lobby we never found this to be a problem during our stay. The continental breakfast was ample for a start to the day and we always managed to find a seat.
The location is perfect for a tourist to the area. You are right in the middle of it and are no more than a few blocks and walking distance from 5th Avenue, Rockafella Centre, Times Square, Empire State Building and Central Park. Grand Central Station and a number of other subway stations are nearby, although the subway system is a little confusing to start with!
If you’re visiting in winter there is an ice skating rink in Bryant Park on 5th Avenue and 42nd Street which is a bit cheaper than those in Central Park and Rockafella Centre. This rink is still in a nice setting, especially during an evening.

title: “Nice French Experience”
text: Very nice hotel in good location. Staff very pleasant. French theme is charming. Easy to walk to lots of great restaurants.

title: “Great Location!!!”
text: In addition to be in the best location in Manhattan, this hotel is clean, large (in comparison with NY standards), has a spacious entrance hall and the staff are pleasant.

title: “A lovely base in Phoenix”
text: ABVI is really close to anything you need to get to in downtown, but at cheaper rates than you'd expect from such a central location. The Queen sized bed I slept in was large and comfortable, the bathroom had all the amenities you could ask for and the powerful air conditioning was a huge benefit. A flatscreen TV was the icing on the cake! I stayed here for two nights on my arrival from London and used ABVI as a base to explore downtown on foot. The staff were enormously helpful. ABVI will always be my first choice in Phoenix and I would recommend them to anyone.

title: “Very priceworthy hotel, perfectly situated in N.Y”
text: We stayed in this hotel for 7 nights in february. We can recommend this hotel to all of you who wants a clean and fresh hotel with great location and perfect staff. This is defenately a hotel we would return to if we should visit New York again in the future. I made a request before arriving for a room on a lower floor because I´m afraid of heights. I´m very pleased that the hotel granted my wish. This is a very priceworthy hotel.

title: “Historic Hotel”
text: The Menger is in a fantastic location. Close to the tourist center, attractions, Riverwalk, ice cream store and across from the Alamo. Beautiful hotel to walk around in. So many historic items to look at. The pool area is very nice as well. The room was OK.

title: “Greeted warmly and upgraded to a king suite!”
text:
Upon arriving at the Phoenix Park Hotel in Washington DC, we were welcomed with a smile. The front desk gentleman looked for our reservation, and had a troubled look on his face. The deluxe room I had booked -- with two beds -- were sold out for me and my daughter.
"Would you mind if you are upgraded to a King Suite? It has two floors, two baths and a spiral staricase."
Mind? We loved it! The room had space galore and two flat screen TV's. We stayed at the Phoenix Park during the final four nights of the 2012 London Olympics, and it was so memorable to relax after a long day of museum touring in this lovely room with two separate living areas. The layout was perfect. Thew spiral staircase was European styled black iron with shiny brass hand rails and solid wood steps. The interior was elegantly European and the thick white towels and robes were embossed with a regal Phoenix Park crest. The pillows, sheets and bedding were first rate.
We went to the gym one evening and it was small but well air-conditioned, and had everything we needed. There was a nice Irish pub in the lobby called the Dubliner, and the Fish & Chips was our favorite. I also liked the Sheperd's Pie. 
The Phoenix Park is located directly across the street from the Postal Museum. The best thing about the location was its proximity to Union Station -- which takes you anywhere. From Union Station, we were able to get to BWI airport (in less than one hour) for only $6 per person!
Also, a highlight of our stay in Washington DC was going on the Walk of the Town Tours. Don't miss it...we actaully went on two Walk of the Town Tours.

title: “simple but spotless, great value”
text: I was apprehensive about the location looking at a map, but it ended up being a great neighborhood with lots of restaurants nearby, and a short walk to the middle of downtown for my business meetings. Breakfast was good rolls, juice, and coffee, but I would have liked cereal too. The best surprise was free shuttle to/from the airport! I'd easily stay here again.

title: “Chelsea Inn, a real treasure”
text:
For seven nights we slept at this lovely inn. We really liked the atmosphere of our room, it gave us a cozy feeling. The location was perfect, close to a lot of subwaystations and Union Square. When we arrived at the Chelsea Inn the frontdesk was closed, but how nice was it to see a note attached to the frontdoor with your name on it, giving us instructions about what to do next. What can we say about the service...the rooms were always tidy and they arranged a great taxi to Newark Airport. One thing about the internetconnection, in our room it was impossible to use internet. We had to sit on the straircase to be connected. 
One piece of advice: with all the travellers from Europe staying at your inn, have a some wallsocketplugs so we can use/charge our European electronic devices. Even with instructions of the reception it was very hard to find one on our own.
We would most certainly come back!

title: “Omni Parker House - great place”
text: Omni Parker House is a great place to stay. Lobby is warmly decorated and friendly. Make sure you don't book a European room as they are too small. We upgraded to queen size bed and although the room was small, it was adequate and very comfortable. The hotel's location was excellent; concierge service good; valet service expensive ($35 night). Breakfast is also expensive; but do it once as service is good.

title: “Let down!”
text: Let down, nasty old bathroom. Hair n my towel, old cracked shower floor, stains on shower curtain, room was ok, but bathroom was yucky! Not like other microtels ive stayed @

title: “Great location, outstanding service!”
text:
Everything you'd expect from a W: sheek environment, quality comforts, lush bar, and outstanding service. We recently stayed in the W SF for our wedding anniversary, and every time I spoke with someone at the hotel (whether reservations, the concierge, housekeeping, in room dining, etc), they wished me a happy anniversary! They even brought a cheese and olive plate with a bottle of wine up to our room after we checked in.
On top of the wonderful W experience, the hotel is in a great location: within walking distance of so many of SanFran's great downtown attractions.
We will definitely be coming back again soon!

title: “Paramont Hotel”
text: Booked trip thru travelocity. Hotel and service was excellent. Probably didn't have best room in house but was located in a nice location for me as I was traveling alone. Service was very good and staff was friendly and helpful

title: “Excellent Location !!!”
text: The Affinia 50 was a very pleasant place to stay for a long weekend in the Big Apple. The location is excellent, 50th and 3rd Ave is a nice part of the Upper East Side. The subay was quite close and Rockefeller Center just down the street. The Guestroom was spacious and mine included a mini fridge. Thank goodness it did not have one of those sensor activated minibars that I think should be outlawed! The "Living Room" on the second floor ( right down from my Guestroom) was a nice place...had free coffee and tea and a computer with the internet to check email and bank balances ( NYC is expensive! ) . I would definitely reconsider staying here again, but hopefully at less than 350 a night. But Christmas time is always expensive in NYC.

title: “Good hotel and location”
text:
My husband, 14-yr-old son and I stayed here for 6 nights at the end of July. 
We took a cab to/from the hotel (~$17 ea way). It is within walking distance of the metro, but if you have luggage I would recommend a cab instead (you never know when the escalators may not be operating plus it's just a hassle to try to drag luggage around on a metro). We had a suite (dining room, living room w/ flat screen and pull out queen bed, and separate bedroom w/ king bed and tv), so there was plenty of space and the refrigerator and microwave were useful for leftovers. The room was clean and spacious, and housekeeping did a good job every day.
The breakfasts are pretty good -- you can make your own waffles, or stand in line for made-to-order eggs, and they have everything else buffet-style - scrambled eggs, pancakes, sausage, biscuits and gravy, hash browns, cold cereal, juice, coffee, muffins/danishes, yogurt, etc. You do need to get there early enough so they don't run out of something you might want (such as fruit). They are also very busy unless you get there early.
We did not go to any of the manager's cocktail parties, or use the pool or fitness rooms as we ended up either returning late in the evening, or, on the few days we got back early, we were too tired from the walking and heat to do anything but relax in our suite.
We also had 1 dinner at the hotel's Italian restaurant. We found it to be pretty good, better quality than we had expected for a hotel restaurant. Price-wise, it was about what you would expect from a hotel restaurant. (For fun restaurant, we really enjoyed the Capitol Grille on Pennsylvania Ave....it was expensive, but it was a really neat atmosphere. )
I would recommend this hotel for a family or business trip. (The reason I rated it 4 stars rather than 5 is I thought their rates were a bit expensive)

title: “A good choice.”
text: We spent 4 nights at the Miyako during a trip down the California Coast from San Francisco to San Diego. The hotel has a very pleasant feel to it, the rooms are comfortable, clean and spacious, and the staff very welcoming and helpful. The location in Little Tokyo is safe and quiet. But don't be put off by the Downtown address. There is plenty going on in the area and some very good pubs and restaurants. Ask the Bartender for some suggestions.

title: “We're so glad we stayed here!”
text:
We were a little worried about staying at this hotel because of poor reviews we had read online. But the price was so much cheaper than anything else in the area, that we decided to risk it. We needn't have worried! The location was fine--downtown SF is downtown SF. We never felt unsafe, even as we walked a mile to see a show late at night. The room with a 2nd sofabed was humongous! I've never had such a large hotel room without paying much more. It was perfectly clean, and the furnishings were very nice and elegant. There was a coffee maker, blow dryer, fridge, microwave, clock radio and internet access! The continental breakfast was great, the pool was beautiful, and the free parking was...well, free parking! 
The staff and other guests were extremely friendly and helpful.
I would most definitely stay here again, and recommend it to all my friends.

title: “Hit and miss”
text:
Location is excellent, checkin staff great, lobby gorgeous, but our room was pretty beat up (door took several tries to open the door, desk plug was broken, AC made a very loud clicking noise every time it came on, obvious water damage in bathroom, etc). I imagine it's tough keeping rooms nice to close to Beale. 
Memphis is lovely. Hotel is just okay.

title: “Guest friendly Hotel in D.C.”
text:
The Kimpton Topaz is a small hotel located just a few blocks from the Dupont Circle Red line Metro. The hotel is staffed by friendly and helpful people who not only aspire to make your stay comfortable but also make you feel welcome with frequent greetings and helpful advice. The area is safe with lots of eateries, bars, shops, etc. Also interesting to walk past the various embassies. 
We found the rooms quiet and comfortable. The bathroom is a bit cramped but otherwise our stay was very pleasant. Housekeeping was efficient and unobtrusive.
Our rate included breakfast and valet parking which is a real money-saver as hotels in the area can charge upwards of $40/night for parking. The lobby is quite small and the Topaz bar does double-duty as a breakfast area. Again cramped but still functional. We enjoyed the complimentary wine reception in the evening (5:00 - 6:00 pm) and the flavored water dispenser in the lobby. The hotel is advertised as pet-friendly which was a concern for us since we are not dog-people, but the small pets were few and harmless to have around.
Overall - highly recommended for a D.C. stay.

title: “Off the beaten track”
text:
Very nice hotel. Location is great, outside the tourist trap of mid-Manhattan. Neighbouhood is great with plenty of shops and restaurants, mainly on Columbus and Amsterdam avenues. Momofuki Milk Bar and Shaky Shack are 2 great near options to grab some food. Serafina and The Fatty Crab, the 2 restauration options of the hotel are also very commendable.
The train stop is at a 2 minutes walk (1 line) which takes you swiftly to all the hot spots in mid and lower Manhattan. It is really nice to get to your hood at night and have a walk and have something to eat on such a pleasant hood. You even have 2 multiplex theaters nearby and a Barnes & Noble. 
Rooms are very nice, bigger than NY standards. It is true that it is getting a little bit old-fashioned and that maintenance on the rooms varies, but still, the guestrooms are big, airy and very comfortable, mainly the beds. Amenities are Ok, including the complimentary coffee you can make in your room. Common terrace and deck at higher floors are also a treat.
Concierge staff is very friendly and helpful, and no negative surprises are met when checking in and out. Quality/price ratio is very good also for NYC standards, and you can always profit from the numerous free upgrade possibilities.
Some renovation works were underway in the façade during my last visit but my guest room was facing the lateral of the building so no problems for me.
I have stayed at many hotels in NYC and it still is a pleasure to visit the On the Ave. Very very commendable.

title: “Bay Club is the Best in San Diego!”
text:
We loved the location, the view, the free breakfast, the pool/hot tub, and the service and hospitalilty were the top reasons we will return. The hotel is older but it has a marine charm about it that makes it laid back and cozy. The food in the restaurant was fresh and delicious too! Our room was clean and a very comfortable bed. This is the best hotel we have ever stayed at in San Diego. Our friends stayed at the Marriot downtown, and paid twice as much with crappy service and no free breakfast. The staff was absolutely the best, making us feel like we were their #1 Priority!
Thank you Bay Club Personell, your top notch service made are 18th anniversary so memorable.
Dan and Melissa

title: “Family Robbed..No Holiday staying at your Inn!”
text:
This rating is for the Holiday Inn located on 125th West 26th Street, New York...
This was a family trip ...12 of us altogether. 5 children and 6 adults. When I selected a hotel, I explained to the Reservation host that we were traveling with children and room size, amenities and cost mattered.I reserved 3 rooms and paid $475.00 each for what felt like a closet. I paid for services that were not available..no room service ! The price I was quoted for my cars was 45.00 per car instead I was charged 200.00...Holiday Inn rip off !

title: “Hotel was a building site”
text:
The best thing about this hotel is its location - it is very convenient to many tourist attractions and to the T which is just outside the door.
However there were extensive renovations going on which we had not been warned about even though I had contacted the hotel to check my booking. Fron 7am there was noise from workmen who made no attempt to keep their voices down when passing our room at this early hour. Later on there were the usual building noises which spoilt our stay.
The front desk reception were quite unfriendly and not helpful. A request for fresh milk/cream for the coffee produced THREE consecutive jugs of sour milk.
A very disappointing experience.

title: “rooftop lounge”
text: I recently had visited the sky terrance at Ivy Hotel and had a great time. the atmosphere is exactly what Chicago needs. Its a hidden spot that i know will soon break out to everyone and become the place to go to at summer time. There are all cabans.sofas surrounding the rooftop so everyone that is there feels like they are VIP, the views are incredible. Lake Views! the music is my favorite, not too loud or to soft and just the right beat to get you going. Staff were all pleasent. drinks are pricey but i get why. You pay for location but its definitely worth it. Cant wait to go back!

title: “Recommended”
text: This is a great choice if you need a cheap, central place to sleep. Very friendly staff and easy to get to. It is 3 minutes from the main shopping district and within walking distance of lots of restaurants and bars. Breakfast is very basic, but there are some great diners very nearby, if you need some eggs or pancakes! My main negative comment would be the lack of air conditioning, as our room was very stuffy. Also, avoid the rooms overlooking Eddy St, as it's pretty noisy at night. Overall, I would recommend this hotel as a cheap base for a great city.

title: “Just OK”
text: The location was adequate for the Made in America event, but that's about the nicest thing I can say. The furniture is outdated, our floor smelled heavily of cigarette smoke despite being "non smoking" and the customer service was below average. The maids were the friendliest employees there, and 2 of 3 front desk staff that we worked with were rude, at best. Not worth the price.

title: “Clean and Affordable”
text: I stayed here over the weekend and was pleasently surprised. I was concerned when I saw the outside but the inside of the hotel was very nice. The room was clean and comfortable and the right price. We even had a sliver of a view of the riverwalk. To get to the heart of the riverwalk, it was about a 10 block walk. Not too bad. We also parked directly across the street for $10 ($5 per day). We walked back from the theater district at 11:00 pm and we felt safe. I think other reviewers might be paranoid. I would stay here again.

title: “Gothic design hotel in the heart of Times Square.”
text:
The rooms are really small but really well decorated, but what we expected - it's New York!!! Good Bed with very good fabric. Breakfast is very simple. 
Really good options to park the car, ask when check-in or when booking.

title: “Great Location but that's it”
text:
We stayed here for a few days before heading home and really only picked it as it was close to Universal Studios. The hotel was built in 1983 and I don't think anything has been upgraded since. It looks very old and tired. They still have old CRT TVs in huge ugly cabinets. The first room we had the bed was broken so that you kept sliding to the side as you tried to sleep. Then what ever was broken, would squeak and clang whenever you made the slightest movement. We complained the next day and they moved us to another room.
The rooms weren't very clean, lots of hair in the bathrooms, dusty and very grubby windows and curtains. The first room we had still had a dirty towel hanging on the back of the bathroom door when we checked in.
The freeway noise was only a humm in the background but you could here lots of noise from the surrounding rooms. The house keepers seemed to work in pairs and were extremely noisy almost yelling at each other in spanish. We tried to have an afternoon nap before flying home late at night, but they put an end to that.
The bar/lounge area in the foyer was closed more than it was open and the restaurant only seemed to do buffets, we were there over thanksgiving so maybe it was something to do with that. They also had private functions on when we were staying and these people would use all the seating in the reception area which meant we had to stand around waiting for shuttles, taxis etc. I thought this was very poor treatment for paying guests.
It's about a 5 minute walk to Universal studios and City Walk. City Walk is the place to go for dinner.
I'd only recommend this hotel if you are planning to go to Universal Studios.

title: “Great Stay”
text: I thoroughly enjoyed my trip at this hotel. the location is great. The Front Desk's customer service was excellent.The only negative is the size of the room,but, it is downtown Chicago.I would most definitely return to this hotel.

title: “Good place to stay”
text: The staff was very helpful and friendly. The resort is well maintained and is quite large (I wished I could have played the golf course but we traveled with friends who do not play golf). We stayed in the Sedona suites and it had several pools which were quite nice. The resort is just off of I-10 so it has easy access to all highways. The rooms are very clean and have nice beds to sleep on (very comfortable). As noted in other reviews the TV's are small . Overall, the place is very quite and restful. The rooms open up to a courtyard with pools and trees. We stayed for the bowl game and had the resort fee included with our room rate (alumni association deal). Would not think that the resort fee would be a good value in winter.

title: “Met my expectations of a Westin Hotel”
text: Stayed here in October for a convention. The hotel was extremely full and felt they did a great job of keeping common areas neat, housekeeping was fine, and the front desk was responsive when needed. The one thing I would recommended would be to expand the restaurant facilities and menu. They couldn't meet the demand of a full hotel, although they did provide names and numbers of local restaurants that would deliver food to the hotel. Location was great, particularly to the local Metro. The Metro platform was just outside the back of the hotel with extremely easy access. Two stops away from the Convention Center, which was very quick and convenient.

title: “Great Hotel / Great Value”
text: Our stay at your hotel was everything we had hoped for to make our trip that much better! Perfect location for us to stay while attending the remodeling expo...Staff was polite and very helpful with the surrounding area.

title: “Amazing Location and wonderful staff.”
text:
The Essex Inn was a GREAT place to stay. My whole family enjoyed it! The staff was very kind and always offered to show us plays to eat or tour. They were very helpful too! The housekeepers were a bit off though, missing small things like changing the empty toilet paper, and stuff like that, but over all they were nice. 
 The location worked VERY well, especially for sightseers like my family. It was close to the water and some rooms had beautiful views. Also it was very close to lots of the museums like the Art Institute, Field Museum, and Shedd Aquarium. Also the hotel offered a free shuttle bus at scheduled times to different locations. There were also some great restaurants and cafes nearby!!!
 The rooms were very cozy too. The bathroom was on the small side, but it worked wonderfully! Also I thought the beds were very comfortable, but thats a matter of opinion I guess. Most of the rooms had great views too of the water and Grant Park.
 The pool was very nice too. It was a beautiful place, and even had a life guard which is great for people with smaller children. The sauna wasn't always very hot but it was most of the time. There was also a gorgeous roof top garden!
 A restaurant in the lobby opened while we were there and the food was fantastic and priced reasonably! It was great to just go down the elevator to breakfast and such!
 I highly recommend this hotel to anybody. Its perfect for people with a low budget (they offer very good low priced rooms, and offer suites for higher prices) and for people with children. It also would be great for business trips and such. I will for surely be back here when my family returns to chicago. Thank you Essex!!

title: “Great Hotel, but far from the action”
text:
The hotel was quite nice. Great beds, quite rooms, and very clean. The staff was very helpful. The hotel is situated to support conventions, but sadly, it is a good $20 round trip taxi trip (with tip) to most of the places to visit in the city. This is not the place to stay if you are with your family and want to see Boston. It is the place to stay if you are a businessman and have no desire to leave the hotel. The Irish pub on site will serve your needs quite well.
The pool was closed for some form of work during my three day stay, but their fitness room was pretty good. As usual, they charged for internet in the room, but free wifi in the lobby. Parking is expensive ($32 a night), but pretty typical for the area.

title: “Fun Hotel in Los Angeles”
text:
This is a funky little motel style hotel in Los Angeles. We were offered cookies upon arrival by the very friendly desk staff. Made us feel relaxed at once. 
Downside was the staff member was not very helpful in assisting us with some ways of getting to the theme parks by shuttle buses however they always endeavoured to do their best for us. 
The pool is small and nothing to rave about but the decor is funky and they sell merchandise for the hotel. The rooms were spacious and very clean. Really comfy beds and a good nights rest can be had here.
There is a restaurant/cafe attached to the hotel called 'Tart' - great food and fantastic value for money. They will even deliver to your room if you need. It seems to be a hot spot for the rich and famous as the night we arrived they were shooting scenes for a movie in the cafe area, another day we had lunch next to cee lo green and another day they filmed for a reality show in Tart again. So much action going on!
Location is great, right across the road from the Farmers Markets (a MUST for great food and shopping). 10 Minute drive to Hollywood walk of fame and Beverly Hills - however this is good as LA is very big and everything is spread out. The hotel also offers free bike rental for its guests and the bikes seem to be in great quality.
The price was extremely reasonable and great value for money. I would stay again.

title: “Fantastic Place!”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for 2 nights. This is a fantastic hotel for staying in and around the sprawling Los Angeles. The hotel was very luxurious and provided the guests with everything that you could need.
The bedrooms were gorgeous and the beds could be adjusted to suit the needs of each individual. 
The pool facilities were also lovely as well, set outside in a nice shady area with a large dining table if you wanted to use it. The hot tub was gorgeous.
The hotel was not expensive at all and was a real find for our tour of California. Although the breakfast was not included in our price, for $10 a guest each morning you could have anything that you wanted and more besides. The breakfast was lovely. The hotel has an Italian restaurant also which we tried one night that was quite nice.
All in all this hotel was a great place to stay and comes highly recommended!

title: “Very good but not quite the WOW”
text: Being the first W hotel you would expect this one to have the WOW factor and be the flagship but it doesn’t quite get there. Don’t get me wrong this hotel is very nice and I would recommend it to anyone but compared to other W hotels it doesn’t stand out. The receptionist could barley raise a smile and the lobby was packed with people. We had a fantastic suite (for a good price) which was a good size for NYC but did feel a little dark. The bathroom was very small considering it was a suite. If the price is right then defiantly book this hotel but the W Union Square was better.

title: “Stylish boutique hotel”
text:
Fabulous boutique hotel - loved the decor. Best part was the large room with seating area (two plush chairs). Friendly and courteous staff - really went out of their way to make us feel welcome. We enjoyed the outdoor seating - good for catching up with friends with a drink from the bar. The hotel restaurant, Bolla, has excellent breakfast. For lunch walk a couple of blocks over to Nick & Sam's Grill - lots of choices from pecan crusted trout to burgers to pulled pork tacos. Reasonable walk to the West End & Dealey Plaza; lots of shops and restaurants (albeit many chains- Hard Rock, Hooters, etc). We wanted to try the pizza place NEO but did not have time. 
The only downside is that my room did not have a bath tub, only a shower (however it was a 2-person large shower.

title: “Horrible!!! Run down building and small room with nasty bed”
text: Small room, nasty small bed. The room smells like smoke even though its non smoking. Slow wifi. I dont know how much others paid for this but I was tranferred from extended stay roundrock cause they were overbooked. Staff was ok. But try to avoid this place.

title: “Great Location, Big Noise”
text: Booked this hotel for a 4-night stay based on TripAdvisor reviews. The location is nice...close to the theater district, convention center, Penn Station and shopping. Keep in mind that this property does not have the amenities one would expect from a typical Manhattan hotel: no bell staff or room service, and it was hard to tell if the restaurant was open or not. The included breakfast was decent for a free breakfast, but not great. On the other hand, the room was good sized for midtown, the hotel was very clean, and the bed was comfy. One word of warning: if you're not accustomed to street noise, request a room facing the back or on an upper floor. There is a great deal of construction going on on 35th Street, and every night between midnight and 3 am, a garbage truck shows up to haul away several dumpster-loads of construction debris. The hotel tries to help by providing earplugs and a white noise machine but I was awoken by this every night despite all efforts to block it out. I expected Manhattan to be noisy, but this was beyond the norm for NYC.

title: “Wouldn't bother with this hotel again”
text:
There are many LAX airport hotels so in choosing I selected by the name, Marriott, which I thought I could trust. The hotel seemed to have been recently renovated and all effort was put into the lobby and restaurants, very little into the rooms. They were average and had no amenities such as a mini-bar or even a shower cap as most hotels offer. The whole thing was bare bones. 
But the worst is when you book online they show-boat by asking questions about your preferences (do you want extra towels, high floor, feather pillows) then didn't acknowledge any of my choices. I asked for a high floor-we were on 9 of 18...glass half full I guess? I asked for extra towels-we didn't even get enough towels let alone extra...I also asked (at check-in) "what was the view" The response "a partial runway view" when in fact we were full on looking at the runway and trust me it was NOISEY-that's why he lied. They should not give the noisey room unless all other rooms are booked and even then it should be at a discount. 
I rented a Hertz car, through the Marriott LAX website link but then after waiting (for close to a half hour) at the Hertz desk in the rear of the hotel lobby I learned that my car was reserved down the street at another Hertz location so I was not able to get the car I had booked. I waited in another ridiculously long line for Starbucks (gift card in hand) and was told they don't take Starbuck's gift cards...? Why-he couldn't answer...Both mornings our room phone rang at 5am with someone else's wake up call that the hotel staff did not care to clear from the previous guest....My husband pulled the rental car out of the lot but misplaced the ticket. Instead of calling to learn that we checked in one day ago they billed me $143.00 for one night's parking. I went to the front desk and they charged me another $25 for parking and said to show the receipt to the parking attendant. He of course said he couldn't help and that we have to call back to talk to the manager the next day...so one night's parking will either cost me $175 or a lot of time and hassle on the phone trying to straighten out-
The whole thing was really a joke because they were trying to come across as so chic, for instance the drinking glass in the room is wrapped in paper that says "quench" and the do not disturb sign for the door says "brainstorming" It was all too "cool" but with zero ammenity or service to back it up. 
It was a total disappointment. Had they just offered a room in a convenient location without pretending to be able to offer more I would have been prepared, but I just really hated this hotel for misleading us...

title: “Just OK for a Westin”
text: I stayed here June 9 - 13 for a conference that took place at the Charlotte Convention Center. About the only good thing about the hotel, was that it was literally across the street from the convention center which was nice. Other than that, this hotel was just lacking for a Westin. I arrived at the hotel at 4:50 pm to check in and they did not have a room ready for me. I was stunned, since check in is typically at 3 pm and it was almost 5 pm. I kept complaining and they finally found a room for me. A co-worker arrived the next day at 5 pm and the same thing happened, no room was available yet. I had several boxes shipped to the hotel to my attention and it was like pulling teeth to get them (they were all there, I had the tracking information). My room was so so... but things were falling apart... the lock on the door was coming undone, my bathroom sink could be pulled from the wall, and some of the outlets did not work. It also seemed that the hotel was understaffed for a large convention. At the restaurant, Ember, service seemed slow... even though there were not many people in the restaurant. I don't know, I just wasn't overly impressed with this Westin.

title: “Very good value for the money”
text:
Just stayed there for 5 nights on a business trip. For sure its not a Marriott or Renaissance Hotel, but it has much more to offer than an average Fairfield Inn. Currently its a little bit hidden by some construction next door, but that does not cause to much extra noise (I did not even heard it from my room). The rooms are small, but there is still enough space to walk around in your room. The furniture and the decore are much better than in other Fairfield Inns (and some Marriott/Renaissance!). The room that end with 1-4 are facing the street and if you get a room above floor 10 you will overlook the building in front of you (this is the Bus Terminal).
