I stayed on floor 28 and had a nice view to some Times Square buildings and the hudson river. If you stay on the other side (rooms 5-8) the buildings are a little bit closer, but its not that you have a wall in front of your window (like I had in other more exepensive hotels already). You can even see the Empire State Building on the left side. The do have 3 elevators that stop on every floor. So I never had to wait more than 1 minute.
Breakfst is served till 10.30 and 11 am on weekends. Its the regular Fairfield Inn breakfast but they never did run out on anything during my stay. On every day I had no problems to get a table in the breakfast area, even it can be a little bit crowded there. In the lobby area they do have 3 pc with a printer without a fee (perfect if you forgot your laptop or need to print a boarding pass).
The gym is also a little bit bigger from what I know from other Fairfield Inns e.g. in Florida (free weights +stepper+bike+crosstrainer+TV on every machine).
I saw that some others did complaint about the location. Well, it is only 3-5 minutes away from Times Square, maybe 3 minutes from the next subway and Alamo/National is also not more than 3 minutes away. I walked to 5th Avenue every day (38th St.) and it took me only 15 minutes. There are some adult stores in the area, but they are everywhere in New York. And there is some police always present at the next corner in front of the Chase Manhatten Bank - so I never felt unsecure.
Overall and considering the rate that I got (between USD 139 and 169) I would defenitely return to this hotel.

title: “Clean & Comfortable - can't get any closer to Fenway!”
text: My wife and son recently vacationed throughout New England. To end our trip we spent one day touring Boston and going to a Red Sox/Yankee game. We wanted to be close to Fenway so that we would not have to drive after the game. We found this hotel to be the perfect choice....although not fancy, it was clean and comfortable. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a place to sleep after a Sox game. Actually, I could have hit the hotel with a rock from my seat at Fenway.

title: “Spectacular”
text: The Standard is one of the best hotels in NYC. Amazing location, design and staff. I would definitely recommend the hotel.

title: “Perfect hotel with great perks!”
text: This has to be one of the best hotels we have stayed at. The suite we stayed in was huge and at a great price. The hotel is very centrally located to everything to easily walk or to get on the free 16th street mall buses. Also great perks in the hotel with free drinks (beer & wine) from 5.30-6.30pm and free cookies and milk from 8-10pm (which were delicious) and continental breakfast included. The staff were very friendly and able to advise on things to see and places to eat. Special thanks to Pepe in the bar. I would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Denver, you wont be disappointed.

title: “A little jewel downtown”
text:
This is a really comfortable, funky and modern oasis in the midst of downtown Manhattan. Its beautiful entrance draws you in to a very smart, chic and friendly hotel that feels just a little bit different to other hotels. Bedrooms are really lovely and fresh and the hotel atmosphere is really classy and welcoming. Staff are very friendly, helpful and engage very professionally. 
This is a real little gem of a hotel , one which I'd recommend without reservation. We'll be back

title: “Comfortable Stay at a Reasonable Price”
text: My husband, 19 year old and 15 year old daughters and I stayed at the hotel while on a recent vacation to Boston. The front desk staff was extremely helpful and friendly. The outdoor courtyard area of the hotel was a nice place to eat breakfast or relax at the end of a day of sightseeing. Our room was just O.K. The room was clean, but it was somewhat small and the bathroom was very tight. I booked the hotel after reading other reviews and had noticed one reviewer saying she would not feel comfortable walking in the area at night. I would agree. The neighborhood, while convenient for the subway and a nearby mall, left me feeling like I would not want to be out at night. During the day, I did not feel that way. There is no pool at the hotel, but there is a very small exercise room down in what is basically the basement of the hotel. Shuttle service to the subway is available on a regular basis. Overall, for the price this was a good location and comfortable stay.

title: “not that great”
text: We weren't terribly impressed with this hotel. We were paying $180 a night during spring break (3-16 to 3-19). The room was old and kind of dirty. The cleaning service kept forgetting to leave toilet paper when they cleaned. The nightly reception always ran out of food. The beer was always pure foam. The margaritas were tasty and the variety of food at night and in the morning was good. The roof-top pool was really neat. My kids really enjoyed it. The fitness room was awful! Broken weight equipment, one bike, one treadmill, and one stair master. The location is good. Right across the street from Biga on the Banks- a great restaurant. The hotel is within walking distance to everything. Overall, it was okay but not worth $180 a night. We wouldn't stay at this property again.

title: “Reservations”
text:
I am so extremely disappointed in this establishment. I called for 4 days to book a room, I was put on hold for 15 min multiple times and even hung up on a few! After not getting a response from the front desk staff I eventually asked to speak with a manager. I was told by the front desk multiple times that there were no managers on duty! It took an entire day for me to be able to speak with a manager. I vocalized my concerns and the managers offer was to give my family 10 percent off! When I pointed out that I am a government employee and that my coworker received 20 percent off last month without having complications I still did not get anywhere!
The customer service is HORRIBLE and I wouldn't recommend that anyone go there!

title: “basic hotel. clean& quite. reasonably priced.”
text: Great Highway Inn is not in the most "exciting" part of the city. and its a basic hotel. but the staff is very nice and the place is very quite and quick walk to ocean beach. rooms are very nice for one or two people. as long as u have a rental car while visiting to get to other parts of san fran- ths hotel is perfect for those who like to return to quiet place after a day of sightseeing.

title: “Do Not Stay Here!”
text: Our room smelled, the door on the bathroom would not close, poor customer service and relations. They "staff" acted like they we doing us a favor. Hotel is not updated, parking tight, and not a pleasant experience at all!

title: “Comfort, location, and value (if you happen to get a great rate)”
text:
2 night business trip. The hotel is not necessarily a standout from the exterior, but has a great renovation job on the interior. Very nice decor, modernistic. I didn't even notice the reading lights on the headboard till night #2, as the way they were arranged was so artful! My room faced the brownstones, and was very quiet. Loved having windows that actually open. Loved bedside lights that actually dim at graduated levels. Nice amenities, comfy bed/bedding, fluffy towels, clean, clean, clean. The little details in the room really made it all come together - great lighting options, flat screen tv, keurig coffeemaker. Location was great - next to two malls and a supermarket, and right next to a subway station. I didn't go to the Brasserie (saw mediocre reviews elsewhere). Walked up just to see the rooftop pool, but it was locked and no one was there (that seemed a bit odd). The "business center" is a fairly small windowless room, not staffed. Wish I had more time to explore Boston, what a wonderful city! 
It was a last minute trip, and I was fortunate in snagging a very good discounted rate via the hotel's website. For what I/my business paid, it was an excellent value. 
Suggestion to the hotel: iPrefer members are supposed to receive complimentary upgrades when available -- it would be nice if the staff would indicate (at check in) if such an upgrade was not available - you shouldn't make the hotel guest ask/wonder.

title: “Not so loyal...This place is a joke!”
text:
This place could start by getting loyal Gold members reservations correct. Then they can clean out the wasps nest and bugs in the check in canopy, my wife was stung unloading some luggage. Once we got into a very dark room the only light came through the closed drapes with holes in them that were either eaten by bugs or just that old. The bath room had hair on the floor and we had to use the extra large bath towel as a floor mat. I would have called the front desk but we were already running behind trying to meet others for dinner reservations, so we let all this go. Later that evening I went looking for a soft drink, but all the machines in this place only accept quarters, no dollars. Where things get worse, is when I approach an empty front desk, and actually have to yell for the receptionist. who finally appears from the back after some time, just to tell me the "we don't have any quarters." 
WHAT A JOKE!
So later that evening as we go down to smoke outside the same attendent yells at us for going out a door in the hallway. As she was checking some customers in, handing them free water, she yells down the hallway rudely "you can't go out there". By this time I didn't care what this lady had to say, I just ignored her and we went out to this smoking section anyway. Oh and summing things up there's no coffee in the lobby after breakfasts, so get there early if you want any. Finally since I am a Gold member La Quinta sent me an email survey and I told explained the majority of this experience in it. The only response was a simple reply from the G.M. basically saying "sorry" but "thank you for your money." I won't be back, so don't wast your money here either. I personally think the Best Western at this exit is better and they will get my business when I'm in this area from now on...

title: “Terrible choice......Bed Bugs like it though!”
text: The staff was awful, very unable to provide service to customers or just didn't care to. The icing on the cake was the bed bugs..........WE'LL BE LEAVING NOW THANK YOU VERY MUCH!!!!! STAY SOMEWHERE ELSE REGARDLESS OF EXPENSE.

title: “Wonderful staff, great hotel at reasonable rates”
text: Just stayed here with my husband and our dog. The staff couldn't have been nicer or more helpful. They were friendly and attentive. The room we stayed in was perfect. Very comfortable and well appointed. They offer free wifi and complimentary breakfast. We would definitely stay here again and would recommend it to anyone wanting a reasonable priced hotel with a friendly staff in a great location.

title: “It was fine, but nothing special.”
text: The Hotel InterContinental is in an ideal location, right on Michigan Avenue. Everything was in good condition, perhaps recently renovated. The room was average size for a city hotel, but it did have a built in sofa under the window which was convenient. The bathroom was small and the tub was so small and shallow it would have been a better idea to rip it out and build a nicer shower. The bedding was very comfortable, but the towels were scratchy. Skip the in-room coffee, its bad, and go downstairs and get a cup at the SBUX in the lobby. If you're hungry, be warned the room service is pricey. There is a fun place behind the hotel called Reagle Beagle. The burgers were great and the drinks were inexpensive. Not a bad hotel, but nothing special.

title: “Carlton Hotel, NYC”
text: The Carlton Hotel in NYC is a classic hotel that has been updated. While the rooms are small, they are elegant and the hallways are quiet and nice. The lounge is a wonderful place for a drink. The lobby is charming. When you enter the hotel, you are surprised to see stairs leading down to the check in desk, but there is an elevator to the right that you can use. It seems many people miss that. The hotel is in a good location for either midtown or the village. Staff work hard to accommodate guest needs.

title: “I should've stayed at the InterContinental”
text:
I attend the SF Annual Folsom Street festival and usually stay at the Intercontinental which I love. Due to some event there the hotel was book solid so I decided to stay at the Marriott. What a huge mistake that was. The hotel had a dentist convention going on the day I checked in. This added to the 45 minute wait I had to endure time and again to have my car returned and picked up from valet service. For some unknown reason my room was warm and nothing I could do would make it cool. I complained to the front desk, the guy came and stated he resolved the issue, but yet the room was still warm. I called again, the gentleman returned and again said there is nothing wrong. After waiting some time and not seeing any difference I decided to just go out and hope for the best tomorrow.
The next day after a day of partying (after waiting another 45 minutes for my car and having a hot room I decided to spend all my time outside of the hotel) I return to my room and it is as I left, housekeeping never came by. I called the front desk to inquire what happened and was told that unfortunately at this late hour nothing could be done. So bascially I was to sleep in dirty sheets and use soiled towels? This was the worst response you could ever give to a guest staying at your property. The next day I checked out after I gave the GM a very scathing run down of all the horrific treatment I had to endure at his property. After that you best believe I will not return here again, from that point on, make mine InterContinental.

title: “Excellent - stayed on the new wing”
text: My wife and I tayed for two nights on the 1st week Aug. First impression was sour one when ushered into an old wing's 8th floor room - small, old and no view. Upon having politely complained to the manager about our room not meeting Hotel's great reputation, he (Marc) personally toured us to the rooms in the new wings. One of which we found great, on the corner 8th floor overlooking Geary St. Considering I called in the morning to book the night at $235, and even forgot to flash Starwood Gold membership, I think it turned out to be an excellent stay. Not a first class lobby and in-hotel stores. But the service and room quality beat them all. And it's great location - needless to mention!!

title: “Great location with all the mod cons”
text:
Stayed with a group of friends and was one of few places I could find that had multiple rooms available with 2x double beds.
It's located on the hudson side on town but convieniently on a 'down' avenue which made getting into lower manhattan much easier, which was exaclty what we needed as this trip was very much about getting out and about.
Rooms were great (as with most places in NYC not huge but certainly not over cramped either). 
Front desk staff really helpful and nice touch having apple computers in the lobby for last minute details checking (restaurants etc).
All in all a great hotels, very clean and modern and did exactly what we needed.

title: “surprised”
text:
My husband and I as well as two friends of ours went to Hurst to do some wine tasting. We checked into our hotel about 5:00p.m after an all day wine tour. It was a fast check in and we headed to our room. The hotel is very new- they were still doing some finishing touches around. We went to our room and were shocked! It was so nice, big flat screen t.v. and nice living area. They bed was great and there was a mini-fridge. We had reserved the lowest class room, and found out all the rooms were like this.
We wanted to drink some of our wine down in one of the nice gathering areas to watch the baseball game but didn't have a wine opener. We called the front desk and they said they would have one for us. We got off the elevator and the staff was waiting for us with four wine glasses and a wine opener set up in one of the private tv areas.! We have stayed at the Grand Hyatt in Singapore and San Fran, but were surprised that the Hyatt Place hotels had similar service for such a cheaper price. The hotel front desk also gave us great suggestions of places to eat. Great service!

title: “This place is a dump!”
text: OK so we recently were put here for comic con thru the hotel lottery....couldn't move because town was booked...did it serve its purpose? a place to sleep and shower, yes. However, I can not believe this place is a 3 star?! I have traveled a lot and have stayed at many hotels...I can not in my right mind imagine how this place rates 3 stars? First off, we checked in around 4pm and were given a room in the "motel" section i.e outdoor hallways and door access. After commenting on said room clerk responded since we were checking in so late(since when is 4pm late) we couldn't be moved. Clerk didn't seem to want to offer any info on much just gave me the keys, had me sign papers, and that's about it. Upon getting to the room after lugging all our luggage up flights of stairs boy were we disappointed. Even my two young sons, thought this place was a dump and asked if we could leave! Never would I recommend or stay here again.

title: “Fantastic Intimate Hotel”
text: This was the cleanest Hampton Inn I've stayed in. Cleaning staff is superb. There for the Superbowl, so it was centrally located. I had a great stay and happy hour is wonderful. They had a tex mex theme with wine, soda and beer to wash it down every night. Great little gym and plenty of parking. Manager is personable, which gave it that intimate feeling. Great stay!!

title: “Fabulous Stay - Highlighted by the Exceptional Service”
text: I had a FABULOUS stay at the W for the past four days. The hotel staff is exceptional, the room was great, and location is perfect--right in the heard of downtown. The service really stood out to me--for example, I was checking in with a friend and we inquired if our rooms were near each other (didn't expect this as we booked separately) the hotel staff said no--but would you like them to be? We said yes, and immediately re-booked us to adjoining rooms! Also, after I left, I realized I had left something in my room. A manager e-mailed me letting me know they found it and asked for my mailing address so he could mail to to me (or also said I could pick it up if it would be easier). The room was really cozy, yet still very stylish and hip! I just had a standard room with a King bed but it came with a wall long couch too. The room also came with a place to plug in your ipod and play music, TV, and a DVD player (which is nice for longer stays as it seems silly to pay so much for the pay per view movies). I love all the Bliss products in the bathroom and the bathroom was very chic and modern. Oh, and the hotel bar/restaurant Trace was excellent. Very yummy drinks and a good late night happy hour! I would highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Good business hotel in a convenient location”
text: I stayed here for 3 nights while on business and it's a beautiful swanky hotel (expected nothing less from the W). I thought the reception area was located in a weird place (the staff is not facing you as you walk in). I didn't get the room I reserved (King bed) but I just went back down to reception to get the correct room and it worked out fine. Lighting in all W hotels is very dim and that would be my only complaint. I like nicely lit, airy rooms but the room only had enough light during the daytime. We ate at Craft one night which I LOVED. Deliciously prepared dishes with food that's from local farms. There are also good restaurant options which are a short stroll away so I would definitely stay here again if I'm in Dallas for business or pleasure.

title: “BEWARE DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!!”
text: Please people if u love ur family do not stay here..Am not being funny AT ALL!! This place is a DUMP!!! It is meant for prostitutes,drug dealers, and drug addicts.. It was NASTY the health department need to SHUT It down. There is no way someone could sleep good here.. Please find somewhere else to go..Every thing was run down i was scared to touch anything,,Please KEEP DRIVING PAST!!!

title: “Slightly Disappointing”
text:
Stayed at the Empire for 7 nights on my Honeymoon two weeks ago. Overall we enjoyed our stay although I was disappointed that the hotel did nothing to make our stay extra special despite being aware it was our Honeymoon, I don't necessarily mean a free upgrade but just something to show they appreciated us choosing the Empire for such an important holiday! Apart from a half-hearted congratulations for the front desk on check -in the hotel did nothing else. We picked the Empire after lots of research and heard that they treated you really well but we did not fell that while we were there. 
Also, we were given a front facing room with a great view of the Lincoln Center but were not informed that there was road works going on in front of the hotel and were awoken at 7am every morning by loud drilling that continued for over an hour. We asked to move rooms after the first three mornings but were told no rooms were available. Fortunately the drilling stopped after day 4. 
So overall not bad but not as good as we had hoped.

title: “Charm and service in a super location!”
text:
This was our third stay at the Hotel Elysee, and it won't be our last. For people who prefer the intimate feel of a boutique hotel, the Elysee just can't be beat. When I booked the reservation, I mentioned that we were celebrating our 35th wedding anniversary. What a wonderful surprise we experienced when we our room was upgraded upon check-in! The gentleman at the front desk was both knowledgeable and eager to please, suggesting just the right spot for a quick lunch before we headed off to a show. His concern was genuine...and much appreciated.
Breakfast is included in the room rate, and it is served in an elegantly comfortable (my husband's words!) breakfast room. Fresh fruit salad, croissants, bagels, cereals, yogurt, teas, coffees...all delicious. 
It appears that there is a large variety of room sizes and configurations. The last time we stayed our room was on the small side, so double-check this if this is an issue. Our bed and linens were extrememly comfortable, but we did hear occasional noise from clanging of pipes. Although the decor of the building shows a tad bit of wear, it doesn't detract from the overall special feel of the place a bit. The Elysee is a gem!

title: “Great Hotel in a great Location”
text: My husband and I stayed here after a concert at Fenway park. it was an easy walk to/from the ball park and the hotel was clean and nice. The staff were all extremely friendly and helpful. My only regret is that we didn't plan to spend enough time to enjoy all the wonderful attractions that are within short walking distacne from this hotel...Coply Place, Newbury Street, Christian Science Church, Symphony Hall, Hancock Tower, etc., etc.!

title: “over priced, over rated”
text: This is not a hotel i would stay at again, unless I received a rate of less than $100/night. I did receive a very good rate from TravelZoo and maybe that's why we didn't received rude treatment as we checked in, For a so-called 4 star hotel, this is what we had as we checked in to the hotel. First a front desk woman who was short with me, and a bit rude, When I mentioned I was a Thompson member, she replied curtly that they were no longer a Thompson property. I asked when it had changed and she said 2 weeks ago. Well excuse me for not keeping up with your companies acquisitions! When we got to our room, there was hair in the sink, and a piece of hard candy stuck to the floor in the doorway, I kicked the candy out in the hallway, and it stayed there during the entire stay of 4 nights! One afternoon after our housekeeping service, we discoverd a bottle of anti-bacterial cleaner on our counter in the bathroom, with only 1 clean glass for 2 guests. They never left new soap or lotion until the last night. Needless to say we were not thrilled with the hotel, but I wll say it was a comfortable bed and a nice, large room. It seemed to me that they were extrremely cheap and a bit arrogant, except for a young lady working at the desk the night I went to their business computer service to print my boarding passes,. She was pleasant and helpful. A big thumbs down for the service but the room was comfortable.

title: “Excellent location and great service”
text:
We stayed at the Grand Hyatt a few days ago. We got a great pre-paid rate since we booked more than 3 days in advance. Upon check-in, we were upgraded to a partial ocean view room which was a nice surprise. The staff in general were very pleasant to deal with (except for the valet who didn't crack a smile at any point). 
The rooms are a decent size, but could be slightly bigger. The washrooms are very nice with marble flooring, showers, etc. and a soaking tub. The bed was okay - I prefer the Westin heavenly bed and find it more comfortable. The hotel is not located very close to the water so although there is a water view, there are some buildings in the way. 
The hotel is located right in the heart of the best shopping area in Seattle - it is only one block away from one of the main malls and the main shopping areas are all within a 5-10 min walk. If you are looking to relax and shop in downtown Seattle, it is hard to beat this hotel's location.

title: “Nice Place”
text:
Yeah, it's a big hotel... but the service was excellent. The front desk staff were attentive, and the concierge were on top of everything and very professional. 
It was a change for us because the last time we visited we stayed at a smaller "boutique" hotel near the Capitol building. But we wanted a change, something with more amenities.
The great thing about this hotel is it's location. Outside of the madness of the mall, it is within walking distance of the National Zoo. It is located almost on top of a metro stop which is great. Because you can park the car at the hotel, and not use it again for your entire stay! Just jump on the metro. Being a couple of metro stops out of the city you can also get better room rates. You are also a short cab ride to Georgetown, that's a must see spot for shopping and eating.
The hotel is also a nice place to just hang around, you can go to the pool and lounge around, hit the gym, or get a cocktail and sit down in one of the many sitting areas and read a book... or people watch.
Within walking distance of the hotel you'll find a variety of restaurants, many of which are good. Italian, Indian, Lebanese... you name it and you can probably walk to it from the hotel.
The place had a recent upgrade throughout. Our room was on a low floor and very spacious and well appointed. You are also allowed to bring a dog with you was long as it is under 25 pounds.
All in all it was a real good experience that will make me think about choosing this hotel when I head down to DC again.

title: “Wonderful staff, good location”
text:
I stayed at the Marriott Gaslamp recently for a week on a business trip. 
The location is great for business travelers and baseball fans - within walking distance to many restaurants, pharmacies, the convention center, Petco Park, and a trolley stop. For general tourists, the location is not is great, it's difficult to get to big San Diego sights like the beach and the San Diego Zoo.
The staff was very helpful, friendly, and quick to serve. When I couldn't find the TV remote, they brought up another remote within 15 minutes. When a waiter delivered a room service dinner one evening, we got into an interesting conversation about how one of the chefs on the TV show "Hell's Kitchen" used to work at the Marriott. Since I was travelling alone and missing home, it meant a lot that this very busy employee took a couple of minutes out of his day to make me feel welcome, and I made sure to eat in the restaurant after our conversation.
The room was always clean, and on a night I worked very late, I returned to find my covers turned down and cookies left by the bed. It was a small touch. but meant a lot after a 17 hour work day.
Some drawbacks - as mentioned in other reviews - there is no pool. Walls are paper thin. I could hear people talking at normal volume in the hall as if they were sitting in my room, which made it difficult to sleep with people passing up and down the hall. The sound of the elevator bells could be heard clearly in my room, and I was a few doors away from the elevators. The carpets in hallways seemed dingy, and sometimes it took a couple of days for bits of trash to get picked up in the hall. The food was good at the restaurant, but there was not much of a selection.
The hotel would be great for short visits, especially for those attending conventions or going to baseball games. Suggest keeping this hotel in mind, but looking at other hotels for longer stays or for trips if sightseeing is your primary reason for trip.

title: “Top Notch Hotel”
text:
I must say this is one of the nicest hotels I have ever stayed in!!! We stayed here for a Friend's Birthday and enjoyed a relaxing time. The pool area is breathtaking, it overlooks the city. The room had the look of a luxury hotel, without paying the high price!!!
I highly recommend this hotel over any other in the Indianapolis area. It is centrally located next to all the bars and entertainment!!!

title: “Nearly perfect”
text:
It seems this this establishment sparks either pure praise or harsh remarks from the reviewers. An 'either or' hotel. Well, I'm definitely either. I was sceptical after reading sour tales on TripAdvisor. After spending 5 nights there, my prejudices had turned into contentment.
There has been little doubt regarding the hotel's perfect location; it really sits smack in the middle of it.
The room I had on the 17th floor was large for a European. Not new, not very fancy, but it most certainly did the trick. The staff were very helpful and serviceminded and I enjoyed my daily chats with the cleaning lady in the mornings.
All in all a place in a city I will definitely come back to.

title: “Would stay here again!”
text: Would stay here again. Very good rate. Easy walk from Bart and 1 block from Union Square. Staff helpful, room clean, nice comfortable bed. Everything you might need (Walgreens), dining, close by.

title: “Just Above Average”
text:
I'm glad that I received a corporate rate and that I'll be reimbursed for my stay, as I wouldn't have been very pleased to pay the full rate out of my own pocket. The doormen were very friendly and helpful, but there was a very long line at check-in. The lobby is indeed very nice. The elevators took forever - never wait until the last minute to head out, as the elevator wait could sometimes take up to five minutes. I was very displeased after a very exhausting business day, a long wait for the elevator, finally arrived at my room - and my key card didn't work. I had to wait again for the elevator (at which time I started to wonder just how long it would take to walk down 18 flights of stairs), had my key activated again, and then wait for the elevator yet again.
The fitness center was really awesome - but very crowded. The fitness center charges $10 day, and expect to pay $10/day for Internet access. Beware that the rooms do not have WiFi, but instead force you to use a LAN cable, so you are tethered to the desk to work. A sign did mention that the public areas had WiFi but I never tested that out.
I asked for a glass of house white wine and was then presented with a bill for $14. Wow. I should have said no thanks, but my fault for not asking for a menu first, and I was just thinking about the long elevator wait that I'd have to endure just to get the glass back to my room.
The rooms were larger than I expected, but the bathroom was tiny, but very clean. The bedding was very comfortable. The mini-bars have been removed and they have two small bottled waters in your room - read the small print, they will charge you over $3 for that water.
Location was great, lobby was impressive, but I agree with a previous poster, a nice lobby doesn't make a nice hotel. I felt nickel and dimed and am only grateful I'll be reimbursed for everything (minus that extremely high priced glass of wine) and I wouldn't stay here again unless for business purposes.

title: “wonderful staff”
text:
This hotel was affordable and in a decent location but it was the staff that made this hotel stand out. From the front desk to the concierge desk they were wonderful and helpful!
The no-tipping policy was a bonus...although I felt a little guilty.
The only downfall...and it wasn't a big deal...was that we were a family looking for a hotel with a pool. The Seaport had a pool but it is a lap pool....my kids still enjoyed it but it wasn't what I was expecting.

title: “simply divine”
text: This is simply the best hotel I have ever been to. The service is impeccable. When we arrived the first time the front desk asked if we had been there before we said no, and he walked us to the elevators. I requested a high floor and what I got was simply perfect. From the room on the 22nd floor we had a gorgeous view of downtown Indy including the Lucas oil stadium. From the floor near the elevator we had a great view of the canal and white river statepark. I really did not expect this hotel to be as grand as the Conrad Chicago but far surpasses any of my expectations. Even my small request were met with promptness. I had requested a plastic fork and also a cell phone charger (25 deposit). What was also really accomadating is on our next arrival I requested the same room for the amazing views and it was granted.

title: “Great Stay”
text: Stayed at the Marriott Quorum Feb 15th-19th. Very nice hotel. The room we stayed in was very clean and the beds were comfortable. Took the free shuttle over to the Galleria which was nice. All around great hotel and can't wait to go back this summer.

title: “Fabulouso”
text: My wife and I spent two nights at the Carlton (January 22-24) and found it to be a truly wonderful hotel. The front lobby staff was the best I've ever encountered during my 40+ years of hotel stays. We believe that the hotel has been restored beyond its former glory and its location is convenient to all forms of transportation within the city. The room we had was spacious and our bed was extremely comfortable. We ate in the Country Cafe our first night at the hotel and loved the food so much that we ate there again the second night of our stay. We would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting NYC who wants the luxury of a four star hotel at reasonable prices!

title: “Incredible, Great Service!”
text:
I booked this hotel through Priceline at a rate of $75/night (Sat. - Tuesday). Hoping that I would get a hotel on the Riverwalk through Priceline, I was initially hesitant that it wasn't directly on the Riverwalk. It didn't matter though! Just a few minutes to walk to the Riverwalk, and the personnel at the Marriott Plaza made sure we enjoyed every minute of our stay...even for a cheap Priceline customer.
Several extraordinary steps this hotel took to make our stay special:
1. Upon checking in we asked if there was any sort of room upgrade we could have. The associate at the counter upgraded to a larger room (I don't think there are any suites at this hotel). When we got into our larger room (parking lot facing) we received a call and were told a courtyard room had just opened up and we could transfer to that room if desired. Much better view!
2. This was a surprise vacation for my wife and I, and after I booked the priceline rate I called the hotel requesting a non-smoking King. They asked if there was any special occasion...I told them it was our anniversay, so when we got into our room late the first night room service had delivered two desserts (chocolate covered strawberries and chocolate cake). 
2. Personnel delivered our luggage to us immediately (as we requested) since our baggage was mishandled by the airline. 
3. My wife left her jacket in the original room we were placed in, and we didn't realize it until we were at the airport on our way out of town. The hotel tracked the coat down within an hour and sent it to our home at no charge.
4. Everytime we left the hotel, concierges were very helpful and friendly asking if we needed anything - directions, taxi
5. Free use of internet in their business lounge.
We couldn't have asked for a better experience at this hotel.

title: “ParkNFly Beware”
text:
My husband & I have stayed at many ParkNFly hotels in the Seattle area. This is the first time we encountered miscommunication regarding when the number of days for parking actually begin. This hotel has "packages" 7-day & 10-day parking for a fee with 1-night stay. (Previous hotels actually had "free parking")
We were leaving 10/14 @ 6AM for Puerto Vallarta, Mexico travelling thru SanFrancisco & returning on 10/21 @ 11:30pm. When we checked in on the 13th, we paid the upgrade fee for 7-days of parking, "MasterPark" employees parked the car. Unbeknownst to us, our 1st day began the 13th when we checked in because they parked the car that evening. We should have parked the car in the Hotel parking lot for that evening, then handed the keys over in the morning, 3:30am prior to taking the shuttle over. However, while waiting for the shuttle we spoke to another party staying at the hotel & evidently someone had left their luggage in the car overnight in the hotel parking lot & it was missing the next morning. So...do not leave your luggage in the parked car!!!
Needless to say, our return flight was delayed; we arrived at 12:05am at Seatac & to the hotel approx. 12:40am. Technically we were in the 9th day, so they charged us $16.99!!!! for each day over the 7.
In summary, beware of ParkNFly offers that are not actually initiated & run by the hotel, the hotel staff may not be trained adequately. Clarify the exact dates included for parking with the parking company or hotel & have it in writing & initialed by the staff. Never leave luggage in parked vehicle. 
I feel very strongly that I couldn't possibly be the first guest to have this happen, hopefully it won't happen to future guests.

title: “Good Hotel in a Very Good Location”
text: I booked this hotel based on reviews read on TA. I found the location to be excellent. I travelled to Newyork from Washington DC and disembarked at Penn Station. I was able to easily walk from the train station to the hotel as it was literally just round the corner. The hotel itself is on a quiet street in the Chelsea area and i found it to be a great base to discover this great city. My room was not huge but from other reviews that I read about the size of hotel rooms in NYC, it was much bigger than I expected and was certainly more than adequate. There was a subway station at the end of the street which was excellent and was very easy to use.

title: “Wonderful Customer Service - Highly Recommend!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for the first time for a recent business trip. I arrived late in the evening - exhausted from traveling. The Manager on duty went above and beyond to make me feel genuinely welcomed from the very beginning. He provided first-class service all the way...
I always read travel reviews online, however this is my first time providing a review - simply because it was that great of an experience!
The hotel rooms were updated, nice, and spacious. Overall, I was extremely pleased with my choice of hotel during my stay and would absolutely 100% stay here my next time to Houston.
My only note for improvement would be the workout facilities - which worked fine but were somewhat outdated.

title: “International Elegance”
text: I frequently stay at the Palace when traveling to New York. The world comes here, as a few hours spent in the lobby will evidence. The rooms are large and traditionally furnished, which is what first attracted me to the hotel. But the service is great. They make it comfortable, warm place to stay. It is conveniently located behind St. Andrews and near the Rock. It can be very busy so book ahead if you can. Wonderful place. Just wish the internet connection was free in the rooms.

title: “Can't give any good reason to chose this hotel over others”
text:
I stayed here for two nights on business despite my home less than 25 miles away and honestly I think I would have been better off just staying at home and getting up early to get to my work event. The hotel has had a beautiful facelift in the lobby and even the rooms look pretty good. The furniture is all old and beat up still, really though who cares. It's the old windows that were an issue here for me, it was ridiculously noisy all night and valet is mostly to blame. They have turned what used to be a self parking lot into only valet and the drivers to they can drive faster (more reckless?) honk all though the garage all night long. Not to mention a train goes by right in front of the hotel. If you want sleep and are a light sleeper I would try a room on the back of the hotel, I was on the front 8th floor and it was not great!
Service at this hotel was poor, and pompous or slow and sweet. At the end of the night I wanted room service, when I called as I ordered they told me I had the wrong menu....ok I asked can you get me the right menu then, I was told I don't know at first but then assured it would be there in a few minutes. After 30 minutes and a hungry tummy I went down to the bell desk and asked them to deliver one, another 10 minutes and I was able to order. Room service food was pretty decent, slow but the man who delivered it was so nice it made up for it, he was this cute older Hispanic man that should have been running the place based on his customer service skills that the rest of the hotel lacked! 
Valet was a nightmare, constantly backed up with not enough employees, and the ones they did have we're not motivated to be speedy. 
The new chef restaurant at the top of reunion tower would have been a nice end to the night for dessert but casual dress is not acceptable, which is fine but the waiter acting like he was some sort of king and we were peasants was an I interesting spin on again the lack of customer service! Funny, so me I would compare this hotel to the rich jerk who thinks he's better than everyone else but really up to debt to his eyeballs, instead of the wealthy man that drives his old Chevy truck and is constantly gracious, if you can relate I would seek out a different Dallas hotel, I have stayed at several others who treat even the poor Chevy driver like a king, or at least a guest!

title: “Lived up to the great reviews”
text: Really, it was as good as all the folks here are saying. I have stayed in a number of other Kimpton hotels, including the Palomar brand, so I knew I wouldn't be disappointed, but for the price, this is the best of the best! While I have stayed in more lush Kimptons, for the price, location, great service, and 5 star cleanliness, this is tops. One small complaint....the bed will need to be replaced soon, but it wasn't terrible, just nearing the end of its life span. I really appeciated how quiet the rooms are, and how huge! Biggest room I've stayed at in a city (had a double queen, connecting to an executive king). I am so happy they honored our request for connecting rooms. As my children are older teens, many times the hotels do not make an effort or try to accomadate, but yay to the Palomar! Excellent in everyway!

title: “Nice Stay”
text: Okay, as a San Diego native, there is no question that the Sheraton still retains that California feeling. In fact if you take your self (Walking) outside of the hotel and to the East you will see an amazing view of downtown that even I did not know existed. In fact, you usually have to go to to the other side by way of the Coronado Bay Bridge to enjoy such a view. Minutes from the very best of San Diego: Balboa Park, San Diego Zoo and Gaslamp Quarter. I find at times that the hotel transported me to circa 1970's, but the pool and grounds more than made up for this. I do agree with the other reviewers: For a grander experience, the Marina Tower has exceptional service and closer to the middle of all of the action.

title: “Excellent for the Business Traveler”
text: Clean rooms and plenty of fresh towels. The staff was very helpful. Great restaurant located right next door. The breakfast buffet was very good with a lot of selection. I will defiantly stay here again.

title: “Location, location, location”
text: Who said that , well this must have been it, all round great hotel, would definately stay there again, get the van transfer to airport for 18 dollars, great value, missing the sound of the cable car bells already !!!!

title: “Not Worth it!”
text:
While this hotel was nice, it is NOT worth what they ask for. The beds were not as comfortable as they claim, They charge for items you did not use, such as $7 bottles of water! Yes SEVEN dollars!!!
They do not even offer free internet for your $200 a night!
Don't stay here... IT'S JUST NOT WORTH IT!!!

title: “Read On”
text: Stayed at this excellent boutique hotel, smaller than your usual US hotels and much better for that. Excellent accommodation we stayed in the love room, which is on the 11th floor with a small balcony ideal for sipping wine on in the early evening. The books in the rooms add to the ambiance of this delightful hotel. Breakfast is a very good continental spread and the complimentary wine and cheese served in the early evening was well received. The front of house staff couldn't have been more helpful in all respects. This was our first visit to New York and we will always choose to stay here on future visits.

title: “Great Place...Good Value...Well Maintained...Convenient Location...but...”
text: Stayed for 6 nights at the end of Aug 2010 through Labor Day. Location is close to airport (15-20 min) and right off of a major highway exit but a little tricky to find especially if arriving at night. Very nice lobby with easy check-in. Staff at the desk was very pleasant and efficient. Had a room on second floor overlooking the pool. Room was very clean and well maintained. Bedding was clean and comfortable...had plenty of clean towels at all times. The entire hotel is smoke-free and the clean air was very much appreciated. Pool is small but very well maintained...a staff person was out there every morning skimming, vacuuming, and testing the water. Never went in for a swim but many did and appeared to be having a great time. Complimentary in-room wi-fi and daily hot/cold breakfast buffet made this hotel a great value...the breakfast area has lots of seating and offers coffee/tea service 24/7 (nice touch for us tea-aholics!)...the staff even kept the buffet going well past the 10 am cutoff when it was busy, AND they kept bringing out more food, never running out as long as there were guests there in line. The ONLY problem was the location...it may be convenient to the earea's attractions (Sea World, the SD Zoo, etc...), but it's located near an adult entertainment area and there is only a Denny's nearby...the hotel does not have a restaurant of its own. You definitely need a car and parking there can be tight especially on weekends. Oh and they offer a complimentary airport shuttle (reservations required). Had a comfortable stay and would definitely stay there again.

title: “Absolutely a Beautiful Hotel!”
text: I can't say any more but this was a wonderful hotel to stay in! It is one of Boston's finer Grande Dame Hotels! I would highly recommend!

title: “Overbooked Hotel”
text:
Well, we arrived at midnight and our hotel was oversold. They kindly found us another one nearby after 15 min. The problem was all our extended family was supposed to be staying there, our Tourguide was picking us up at 9:30am at that hotel, etc. 
Thay did pay for the night at the Holiday Inn express Fisherman's wharf but we had booked our Hotel via Hotels.com and had paid in advance. They promised to make the refund quickly. They never did, now I've been 2 days on the phone (BTW, it's international long distance for me) with the Hotel and Hotels.com and nothing. 
Hotels.com promised they had already refunded my money but I have no email confirmation or anyway to really make sure they did. Amex has already charged 6% interest rates +tax on the entire stay. It's a nightmare.
I have no idea whose problem was it, the hotel or Hotels.com but I'm sure not using Hotels.com again or the Marriott.

title: “Don't be afraid! Stay at the Hudson!”
text:
Got the Hudson for $100 a night via Priceline (hey, it's January in NYC). I came away knowing I'd give them a great review on TripAdvisor because I think the place gets a bum rap here. After reading reviews here I was concerned, but the reviews actually helped me a lot as far as setting expectations goes. 
Front desk staff were exceedingly friendly and happily checked me in several hours early since my room was ready (yay). No attitude about me having booked through Priceline at all, which was something others have mentioned. I found the lobby and all the public areas VERY groovy and interesting! I did not find the hallways to be shabby or not well-maintained at all, they were just fine. Dark, of course, but not dirty or any of the other stuff folks have mentioned.
And yes, the room was extremely small - I believe it was approx 18 feet from the door to the wall behind the bed, slightly less wide - there is maybe a foot of wiggle room on either side of the bed. More than 1 person in the smallest room would be nearly unbearable in my opinion. 
Somehow I lucked out and had an actual wall between the center of the room and the shower. I didn't find that the shower curtain stuck to me while showering (lol). Nice Korres toiletries too. The bathroom was just the slightest bit...icky, the ceiling and showerhead looked like they could use a little work but for $100 a night I could hardly complain!
The bed was super comfy, but was indeed low to the floor. Not an issue for me. Even though I was on the 19th floor I could hear street noise so definitely bring earplugs to ensure a good night's rest. This is par for the course in New York so it really did not bother me. The heating pipes clicked and clacked a little when the heater fired up but again, nothing I couldn't handle and it died down quickly.
I did not go to any of the bars/restaurants at the Hudson because the prices are just outrageous. Hang a left out the front door and have breakfast at The Flame Diner on 9th Ave - it's a classic NY diner that ain't fancy, but the food's good and breakfast was less than $10 every day for me! The Belgian waffles are amazing, try one. :-) The coffee is great too. If you're a Starbucks fan, hang a right out the hotel door and it's just steps away.
There's also a giant shopping mall inside the CNN building just down the block, on Columbus Circle. All manner of chain stores plus a small Dean & Deluca foods-to-go area and even a Whole Foods in the basement! Subway of course is available at 59th St/Columbus Circle and you're just steps away from Central Park South.
Clientele was mostly young Euros using the hotel as a base. They all seemed happy enough to be in such a groovy place. I did see a few bewildered older folks, as in elderly (lol) and a couple of business travelers but overall the crowd skewed young. 
No probs at checkout, no phantom charges, and they gave me a keypass to use the PC in the business center to print out my boarding pass - just ask nicely and I'm sure you can do the same.
All in all, I would stay here again in a heartbeat for $100/night. If I paid $358/night (the going rate) or even $200 a night for the Hudson I'd probably have wanted to die or (kill someone) when I saw the room size and I'd probably pick severely at every aspect of the hotel. If you normally stay in 4-star digs then stay away because you will be disappointed/upset. But for more easygoing peeps with reasonable expectations of a NYC hotel - and who are on a budget, it really can't be beat.

title: “Perfect boutique hotel without the snobbiness.”
text: The beach restaurant's food is amazing! Service is impeccable and not snooty for such a top rate hotel and I've stayed all over the world. People here seem to genuinely want to please their guests. ESP the front desk staff and Spiro at the Beach rooftop bar. The whatever whenever service took care of everything we asked for!

title: “Great location, friendly staff”
text:
The best thing about the hotel is the location, close to the subway, Macy's, Empire State Building, Times Square etc. The staff were friendly and helpful. 
The room (single) was fairly spacious. The only negative thing that someone might have an issue with is the noise that you can occasionally hear from neighbours (probably due to wooden floors that don't dampen sounds). This did not bother me but if you were unlucky and got loud neighbours then it might be an issue.
Still overall I'd recommend this hotel to anyone visiting New York for the first time.

title: “Blood on the floor in the lobby..... go somewhere else.....”
text: Watch for a 3.00 weird charge when you check out.....

title: “Great location for touring the city!”
text:
We arrived before the designated check in time and the hotel offered to hold our bags while we went exploring. Our room was immediately upgraded to a room with two beds ( we booked for $123/ night on Priceline).
The staff could not have been more helpful at the Tudor. Although there was no outside view in the room, it was comfortable with a working air/heating system. One of the beds was a bit "cock-eyed"- but had no trouble sleeping. The bathroom was large- but had no fan. There are no coffee makers in the rooms.
The TV would only stay on a station for 5 minutes. The staff tried unsuccessfully to fix it three times. But we were in NYC and really did not need a TV (on Sat. we toured NBC and saw the actors at SNL rehearsing and we wanted to watch the show).
There are subway entrances just up the block and EVERYTHING is easy to get to. Starbucks and CVS are on the corner and a great deli down the side street. We are not in the best shape and we had no problem walking to Times Square, Rockefeller Center or Central Park.
Felt very safe at this hotel. It is an old building- but that was part of the charm! If you stay here, walk down the street and climb the stairs to Tudor City and check out their gardens.

title: “Perfect hotel perfect location good value”
text:
The hotel has the perfect location 2 blocks from Union Square, everything is perfect, the staff is very friendly and helpful the rooms are nice, clean and sound proof so you don't hear anything from the street. They have a gym on the last floor and an area to sit where you can have coffee or tea anytime of the day.
The whole family loved the hotel and it was a good value for your money. We would definitely go back to that hotel.

title: “Fabulous !”
text: Best stay ever in NY, classy, big rooms, clean and well appointed. Very upscale old style. Will go back there !

title: “Great location, but small rooms with thin walls.”
text: This hotel is along walk to Times Square action, but access to the subway and Penn Station for airport travel was very convenient. The room was very small and the door did not tightly seal; therefore, hallway noise was not blocked out. The staff was courteous, however, the room did not seem quite clean (maybe it was the old bedspread and thin towels?). I did check for bed bugs and did not find any thankfully. Overall, I would try another hotel next time.

title: “On it's way to being the hottest hotel in North America!”
text:
First off, I'd like to say that if you normally stay at a Fairmont or Marriott property for the bland and typical stay, STOP COMPLAINING ABOUT W HOTELS! It's obvious it's not for you and most likley knew that going in. The W brand is not about catering to family's or senior citizens. Not to say that it is incapable of doing so, but if you find the sights and sounds of W Hotels to be "tacky", loud or full of attitude, perhaps the first indication would be the types of bars and nightclubs attached to most W properties. It is not made for the "Over 40 Club".
The W Hollywood is an amazing new property that boasts a great mix of that warm contemporary feel, attention to detail and the most friendliness I have ever experienced at a hotel. The "Wonderful"/Traditional rooms are somewhat small but not crowded and you still manage to feel that you have more than enough space. The rooms are great but at the end of the day, how much time are you going to spend in it when you have the rest of this amazing hotel and Hollywood at your finger-tips?
"The Livingroom" is the main hotel bar located directly in the front lobby. In all of my travels, I have never experienced a more energetic and electric feel to a hotel bar. Vegas, Atlantic City, New York included, I have never seen a more happening hotel at night. I can only imagine what it will be like when Drai's Nightclub opens on the rooftop! A bartender by the name of Gio at "The Livingroom" also happens to be the luckiest and hardest working man in Hollywood. Only he knows what I mean by that!
The valet and front desk people will do anything for you and always carry a smile and greet you as you walk in out of the hotel.
As somebody who works in the hotel business, I'd say the W Hollywood is 98% there and seeing as they are barely a month old, that's a great place to be, in my opinion.
If you want to experience the very best of Hollywood and West Los Angeles with that special "Hollywood" flare, stay at this property. You won't regret it!

title: “Getting an overly bad rap . . .”
text:
OK--everyone is being a bit harsh on this hotel. Yes, there are some low points (food cost on site, parking was a bit hairy & expensive), HOWEVER, I thought it was quaint and my husband and I had a nice stay. Room was a bit small with some outdated furnishings, but clean and stocked. 
They didn't have our King bed we requested online so the front desk person gave us half price parking which I appreciated. I thought the grounds were fun and pretty with all the roses and greenery. 
We went to the little bar on the property and it was kinda lame, but the breakfast buffet was good. We got a zoo package and I felt like we got a decent deal for this hotel and zoo tickets. 
Considering it's San Diego (we drove from Arizona) and the hotel has easy access to the freeway, it was definitely an OK place.

title: “Enjoyed Our Stay”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at the Palomar. Check in was efficient and hotel personnel went out of their way to make guests feel welcome. There is a free wine hour which we took advantage two out of three nights during our stay. There is a fairly trendy restaurant attached to the hotel and many other options nearby. There is a decent fitness center and all the equipment was in working order. There is also an adjacent pool but no sauna or hot tub.
Our average sized room had high quality furnishings (although we have seen more comfortable beds at other locations) and a large hdtv. The bathroom was also nice although I prefer a regular door as opposed to the sliding door present in our room. The refrigerator in the room was large enough to store take-outs as well. Our south facing room also had a fine view.
We had a good stay and would recommend the Palomar to others for business or pleasure.

title: “Nice Value Hotel convenient to Boston Attractions”
text:
My friends and I needed a hotel for the night in Boston last minute. A good friend of mine recommended the Inn at Longwood (days inn).
I had heard of it before from my days of working in Boston, however, I had never stayed there.
We loved it! Great location, friendly staff and perfect hotel value for our needs.

title: “A Charming hotel on the Upper West Side”
text:
As a birthday present to myself I decided to spend a few days in NYC. For my stay I choose the “On the Ave” Hotel, which I can summarise as a very good choice. 
Not unexpected for June, NYC was hot and muggy and after a 7 hour flight I was keen to get to my new home for the next week and freshen up. Upon arrival I was impressed with the look of the hotel, inside and out. The staff at the reception desk behaved in a professional and friendly manner and in no time at all I was ascending in the lift to my room, a panoramic deluxe, on the 15th floor. The room itself was a little smaller than I had imagined, as I had based my expectations on the pictures supplied on the hotel web site, but I cannot say in any way that it felt cramped. On the plus side the bed was large and comfortable and the wall mounted television was huge! The bathroom was a good size and included a small shower room. The hotel room was finished off with a large balcony providing views to the North of Manhattan, and at a stretch Central Park. The décor of the room was a bit dated and could do with a freshen up, but in its favour it was very clean and a regular maid service kept it so. Unfortunately the maid service did not extend out to the balcony as rooms higher up had been using it as an ashtray. A quick sweep before my arrival would have left a better first impression. Two other points to note were the lack of room safe and the very slow lifts. I found it a bit of hassle to use the hotel safe on a daily basis and I would have much preferred a safe in the room.
The Hotel on the Ave is tucked away behind the corner of W77th and Broadway, on the Upper West Side, and is well situated for exploring NYC. With easy access to subway lines 1,2 & 3 from the station on 72nd street and subway line 1 on 79th street, travelling to other neighbourhoods takes no time at all. The hotel is also in a great location for exploring Central Park and the Upper East Side, which are just a short walk away. The surrounding area of the hotel is “quiet and leafy” by NYC standards and conveys a nice relaxed atmosphere with lots of brasserie style cafes and great little super markets. I should also note that the Manhattan Diner facing the hotel on the opposite corner is a great / cheap place to eat traditional American cuisine.
To sum up, I would recommend a stay at the Hotel On the Ave to anybody going to NYC for a visit and would definitely consider staying there in the future.

title: “okay”
text: This hotel was in a really great location right down from sea world. The staff was very helpful and very nice, The room was to the best of a motel 6 clean not saying that it was totally spotless. Tv was a great plues, along with wifi they do charge 4.95 to use it but hey small price to pay to have it and not use dial up. Now the things i didn't like very hard bed noise from behind and above my room i mean you could hear every movement they made above you. the price was also something usually its like 66.00 a night but i had to pay 81.00 so not to bad considering in a good location but could have gave there usual nightly rate. Food you may have to drive onto 410 to find something advice is unless you want fastfood call the place ahead of time.

title: “This Hotel Does Everything Right”
text: From the moment I walked in to the lobby to the time I left 5 days later this place feels different than any other hotel. I stay in 1-3 hotels each week and nobody does it better than theWit. There are always plenty of staff to help you feel special. The rooms exceed all other hotels. They are big, clean, modern, and have things like microwave and refrigerator which most other hotels do not. The restaurant on the first floor has great food. The fitness center is open 24 hours and have enough equipment for even the busiest of times. The service is the best and the staff are the friendliest. I can't say enough good about this hotel. I will be back!

title: “always impresses”
text:
This was our 3rd stay at this property. It never disappoints. Staff is friendly, helpful, courteous, and incredibly professional. My girls love the lollipops welcoming them in the lobby. The property is clean, neat, well maintained, and a pleasant experience from beginning to end. The room design works well for a family - 1 person in the shower, 1 person outside the bathroom getting ready for the day, kids love the swivel widescreen tv.
Breakfast is more than adequate with cereals, eggs, a meat selection, oatmeal, Texas shaped waffles, and yogurts to choose from. 
I would not recommend 1 room for 4 adults as the sofa bed would be terribly uncomfortable, but for the under 12 set, it works quite well. 
This property made us switch from Hilton to Marriott. And we are always happy that we made the switch. It is our go to hotel In San Antonio. A quick convenient walk to the Alamo and the RiverWalk are always good.

title: “Stop the Whining! This place is a find!”
text: I had booked this hotel knowing the location only. Raading the reviews I had some serious doubts but for the price and location it seemed worth the chance. Expecting the worst, I was pleasently surprised at the wonderful apartment like atmosphere and comfort of the room. The room was clean, spacious and had more than I expected. The "living room" was beautiful and a nice place to host visitors. With a small bar and modern kitchen it seemed like home. The bedroom was comfortable, clean and once more provided a private space away form the rest of the "apartment" The bathroom was a bit small but for NY standards quite sufficient. Two walk in closets, yes walk in closets, one in the foyer, and one in the bedroom provide more than enough space for my clothes, luggage, and the ironing board etc. Guest could actually hang there jackets up as they entered! Houskeeping was great and descrete, the front lobby awsome ,art deco, and the staff attentive. Based on the initial reviews and my experience, had I step into the twilight zone? If so book it next time! PS, the price for NY was incredible!

title: “One of the nicest hotels I've stayed at”
text: My boyfriend and I went to Chicago for Memorial Day weekend. I had found a great deal on Expedia ($109/night for a king room), and upon checking in, we were informed that we had received a complimentary upgrade to a junior suite. The suite was a large corner room that was clean, spacious, and modern. We had an excellent view of the city and were in a part of town with a wide variety of restaurants and shops and a few blocks from Michigan Ave. The staff were all very friendly from the minute I called to let them know we would be a late arrival to our checkout three days later. We were extremely pleased with the whole experience and would return again without any hesitation.

title: “Nice room - worst shower”
text: This hotel is incredibly convenient for anyone visiting Mass General. While the lobby is small, our room was nicely renovated. Our room, which was at the end of a hall, was quiet and well equipped but it would have been nice to have an in-room safe and a mini-fridge. The biggest negatives - the windows were filthy and the shower had the worst water pressure I've ever encountered in a hotel. It was actually difficult to take a shower with the little stream of water. The pool is rather small and lacks easy in steps (only ladders are provided).

title: “Great location”
text: Attended a business meeting at the hotel including an overnight stay. Right at Kenmore Square. We walked to Fenway Park for a Sox game in the evening. Rooms were nice and spacious. Service was very good. Staff friendly and helpful. And you cannot beat the location.

title: “Bargain stay”
text: Spent two nights on a business related trip. I found the hotel staff efficient and knowledgeable. Room was small but clean and had the basic needs met, it had a sink in the room. There were several bathrooms located in the hallway. Never had a problem accessing them. Don't believe you can find a better deal in NY. Great little breakast place aroung the corner on 2nd Avenue. Would stay again.

title: “Fine except for one problem”
text: I'd like to recommend this hotel as there are many positives. The location is convenient. The staff were pleasant. Although not plush, my room was well appointed, with a complete kitchen - spotless and well equipped - living/dining area and sleeping area with a queen bed that wasn't uncomfortable. The one thing holding me back is my room had a pretty strong musty/mildew smell. I probably should have asked for a different room but I figured I was only there for one night why bother. I don't know if it was just my room or a general problem.

title: “Great location, beautiful rooms”
text: We just finished a great weekend in Chicago. We have been to this hotel on several occasions and often try others as well, but this continues to be our favorite because it is consistently well maintained, has beautiful amenities, and a great location. This time our family booked a room through Priceline and snagged this lovely property for for only $90. (I did lots of research at other hotels, including this one, to get an idea as to the lowest posted prices for 5 star hotels and then bid $60 under the best price I found.)

title: “Wonderful Waldorf!”
text: Stayed here for 6 nights last year with my boyfriend on our first trip to NY from Europe. I have been in NY since and have stayed at other hotels, but nothing can compare to the Waldorf. The standard rooms here are nearly twice the size of what one normally gets in NY, the service, the staff are second to none. And the decor...and Art Deco lover's dream! It really is a piece of NY history and the atmosphere is buzzing. I'm going back again this Fall for a week, can't wait!

title: “They did redeem themselves”
text:
Initial impression was not good as months before, my friend and I had booked a twin room yet when we arrived we were told we were in a room with a king bed! However, they did redeem themselves by offering us an upgrade, a fabulous upgrade, unfortunately it was still in a room with a king bed but it was in a room with the most fantastic view of the city so I suppose we got over our problem with the bed.
Everything else about the hotel was great, the staff were helpful and hopefully once the renovation work is finished the hotel will look fab.

title: “A very good experience”
text: My wife saw this ad in Westways Magizine, so we tried it again and were very pleased with our stay. The rooms had been redone. Very clean. We had a coffee maker, a microwave and a refrig. The people at the front desk (especially LEO) were very plessent, helpful and accomadatihg. All in all we were pleased and will be back.

title: “Nothing special”
text:
Expecting a 4 star experience for our anniversary, the room was not special. It was small and average decor, older bathroom fixures. But did have a great view of the city. The sink is separate from the bathroom, which I don't like. The room was not cleaned well, we found a wine bottle on the floor that was not picked up by the cleaning staff. Internet was not complimentary with our room. We had to pay $10 for wifi. Its 2-3 miles to get to the busier parts of the city so each cab ride was about $11 + tip
Would NOT recommend this unless you are on business and need to be near McCormick place. For families, couples, try one of the many other options.

title: “Friendly staff, cool water shower”
text:
This is a small property located on 16th Street NW, a 1 mile walk to the White House. The neighborhood is quite pleasant and felt safe and comfortable. Neighborhood dining at a number of establishments quite nearby. A list was provided by the hotel. The staff was friendly and courteous. The bed was comfortable and the furnishings quite adequate. The toilet and shower were in the bathroom while the sink was in the main room. 
The only complaint was that the shower could not be adjusted to a comfortably warm temperature. The water in the sink ran hot, but the shower valve, which we told was relatively new, could not be adjusted past cool. When we complained, the manager at the front desk had us try the showers in two other empty rooms. One was inadequate, but the other was okay and we were allowed to use it. 
Before booking we read a review from October indicating the water in the shower was cool but whether it hadn't bee reported to the staff, or the repair just hadn't been made is unknown.

title: “Loved this Hotel. A Great Find.”
text: I stayed here from the 21st May - 26th May. With my husband and four kids and my brother. We were all very pleased with this Hotel. The maid cleaned everyday, only she didn't manage to clean to top of the headboard for some reason. It was quite dusty. The bathroom was clean with clean fresh towels in everyday. Television and playstation in the bedroom. We asked for two double non smoking rooms. I have a feeling that someone had used them to smoke in, there was a faint smell of smoke. We were given rooms overlooking the street. It was very noisy. It was even more noisy when the construction men decided to dig up the road at 1.00 AM in the morning. No one got any sleep that night. The rooms were very hot also, we didn't want to open the windows as we had young children with us. The people on the front desk were nice not overly pleasant but ok. The deli next door gets very busy on a morning so get down early. There is a new restaurant up the road called The Theatre Diner, this is very nice, very clean and the food is lovely. Would I stay again most definately.

title: “Memorial Weekend Trip”
text:
If I could give this hotel, 1,000,000 stars I would. It's the best of the best in Manhattan. Just perfection and that is a very difficult goal to achieve these days. The great standards are always maintained no matter what, and the rooms, food, service are truly outstanding! The cruise ambiance created a different twist which sets aside the Maritime from the rest of the clones. Absolutely beautiful experience in respect to all aspects of hospitality and totally fulfilled my senses. An impressive guest services that are the most courteous professionals I have encountered so far. My highest evaluations, recommendations.... And, we will be back! 
Thank you Matt Moore for a truly treasured weekend. Joseph Cuomo & Paula Buchele.

title: “Terrific boutique hotel”
text: Wonderful staff and amenities. Great location. First class rooms

title: “Great staff, lots of perks, nice rooms”
text: I found this hotel on Expedia. It was reasonably price in a central location near the Westlake Central Link Light Rail station which takes you to the airport on approximately 40 to 45 minutes for $2.50 one way. The hotel is also near all major tourist attractions in the city. The area surrounding the hotel can be dodgy at night but then again there are lots of dodgy areas in the downtown area. One just has to be aware of the surrounding. The staff is friendly and courteous and very knowledgeable. There is no internet access in the rooms but the computer room on the first floor can be use by all guest complementary. You can also bring you computer and connect to the internet cable. Rooms in the front can be noisy and because there is no A/C closing the windows is out of the question. However, the courtyard rooms are relatively quiet. There is some sort of rehab program going on so be prepare to see some odd people coming in and out.

title: “Good location just outside the hustle and...”
text: Good location just outside the hustle and bustle. The lobby is very nicely decorated. The room was a bit small but the king size bed was incredibly comfortable. Could use a little modernization from their tv's to their bathroom. Overall very pleased with the hotel for our weekend stay.

title: “Disappointed...”
text:
Not really sure how I could have been staying in the same property as all these rave reviews - but they were the reason I chose this hotel! Unfortunately, it did not live up to expectations for me. Yes, it is a great locationn and the rooms are a great size for central New York. Our king bed was very comfortable and the sheets were pristine and high quality. However, the room was not very clean. We found long black hairs on the couch and the carpet looked as though it had never seen the nozzle of a vacuum cleaner!! The dirt around the edges and in the corners was horrible and the carpet itself was shabby. The bathroom was far too small for a room this size and the fittings were cheap and nasty, with plastic panels around the walls above the bath instead of tiles and yellowing sealant that needed replacing. The cupboard was in an awkward place and poorly lit. Our room did not have an armchair and ottoman, as promised on the website, and it was very noisy - yes, I expected some street noise, but there appeared to be some sort of generator outside our room which provided a constant, loud, low pitched hum. 
It was my mistake not to complain as I realise I didn't give the hotel a chance to respond but as it was a trip I had planned for my husband's birthday, I didn't want to be negative about it. Complaining and changing rooms is a time-consuming business and we only had 3 days in New York - I didn't want to waste any time at all.
The free coffee in the lobby was nice but the breakfast was not the quality I would expect from a Hilton hotel. The cold choice was poor and the hot food was cold. We cancelled breakfast after the first morning of our stay so we could eat elsewhere and found better quality at a much lower price. 
If this had been a budget hotel, I might have felt quite pleased with it, but at $300 per night it represented very poor value. The Hilton we transferred to at the airport before an early morning flight home was beautiful - a completely different experience.

title: “Mostly on the Mark”
text:
My wife and I spent a quick weekend at the Mark with another couple. The service is gracious with European touches and the Mark’s rooms were generously sized, especially for NY standards.
Liked: Free wifi (rarity at this price point); location well suited for boutique shopping along Madison Ave; Jean-Georges restaurant was excellent; vibrant bar scene; well done room Crestron room controls; plenty of closet space; most comfortable beds ever!
Anomalies: Extreme room service pricing and delayed well beyond quoted time (as in 20 mins turned into >1 hour; questionable room servicing/cleaning

title: “Good, but not perfect hotel near DIA”
text:
My second stay at the Fairfield Inn and Suites Denver International Airport was good, but not perfect.
This hotel is conveniently located on Tower Road just off of Pena Blvd. That makes it a great choice for a pre or post airplane trip in or out of DIA. In addition it is also located near a few eateries, as well there is a full service supermarket and drug store just down the road. 
As was the case with my last stay I was able to get great a rate on this hotel by using Priceline’s “Name Your Own Price” feature. 
Check-in at this hotel was speedy and the staff was very friendly. 
Our room on the first floor was very clean and featured a flat screen TV, fridge, microwave, and desk with office chair. 
The free breakfast was good and feature homemade waffles, cereal, fruit, and drinks among other foods.
Near the breakfast area are a few computers with internet access. I used one to get directions to the aquarium downtown.
