On the downside the hot tub could have been a little warmer. In addition part of the parking lot was being repaved and upon returning from the Colorado Rockies I was unable to find a parking shot. I any event I ended up parking in the lot the belonged to a neighboring hotel.
In all our stay was good, but as I stated above was not perfect. The negatives though are not enough to keep me away from this hotel in future, especially if I get a similar deal with Priceline.

title: “Nice suite, but sub-par service.”
text:
This hotel was on a list recommended for cancer patients by Memorial Sloan-Kettering, and the website looked wonderful. We did get a special rate because of the hospital, so I reserved a suite, although NYC hotel prices always take me aback. We arrived early, but they were able to find us room to check right in. I couldn't get over how tiny the lobby was; and there were 4 employees crowded around the little desk; and one seemed more confused than the next.
When we got to our suite, it was really fantastic, big, very attractively decorated. The living room had comfortable furniture and very attractive lamps and decor. The bedroom was a bit crowded, but had a wonderful built-in closet with lots of shelves. The small bathroom had been recently remodeled; and could not have utilized the space any better. The shelves in the shower were great, and because the sink had little counter space, I loved the mirror and counter with lights on the opposite wall, behind the door. The kitchen was complete, but badly needed remodeling. However, how great is that to have a full kitchen, including dishwasher and microwave? 
It has been a long time since I had to pay for wifi in a hotel, and $14.95/day is steep. To get free wifi, you have to sit in the lobby which is only big enough for 3 people. Plus, even the one computer in the lobby can only be used to print boarding passes; otherwise, you have to pay $5.95 for 15 min. and $1.95 a page to print.
I was surprised that they did not have a shuttle to the hospital, as most others do; so we had to take a taxi. Since the hotel is in the middle of the block, very few taxis come down 64th St., so you are forced to walk over to 2nd or 3rd Ave. (depending on where you are going) to catch a cab in a timely fashion. That is not easy for a cancer patient, especially when it is cold and raining. Also each day there were tons of bags of trash stacked on the sidewalk from the building next door, blocking half the walk.
When we left the room in the morning, we hung the sign on the door for the maid to clean the room. When we returned 4 hours later, she had not been there. By that time my cancer patient was too ill to not go right to bed; so I just told them to skip it. I did get a note from manager that they were overly full and the maid couldn't get to all the rooms in a timely fashion. But I would think since there are so few rooms on each floor, they could check the doors and prioritize which ones got cleaned first. In all honesty, I guess I should have told the front desk as well when we left in the morning; but I have never had that problem before.

title: “Great location for the price and good service!”
text: I was in New York for the 2-day Avon Walk for Breast Cancer. It was my first trip to NYC and after searching for affordable hotels for months finally settled on this one - my son who traveled with me is in the Air Force and they gave us a great Military rate. The location was perfect, only a few blocks from Times Square, but nice to not be in the madhouse of Times Square every moment. Bryant Park across the street is very nice. Just around the corner is a great Chinese Restaurant, I can't remember the name, and also a wonderful Irish pub Gaby O'Hare's. The bar in the hotel was nice, but $13 for a glass of Chardonnay was a bit steep, pool table was a fun addition but needed some work. The staff was very helpful, arranging for a late checkout on Sunday so I could clean up after the Avon Walk before heading to the airport, even though they were booked for Sunday night. Hotel was very clean, great location, friendly helpful staff, free breakfast was good. No problems with the elevators that others have mentioned. For a family it would be a great hotel with the couch making out into a double bed and the full kitchen. I would definitely recommend the hotel and would stay again.

title: “ok stay”
text:
We are just home from a week long conference held at the Seattle Westin's Hotel downtown...positives include a great downtown location for shopping and sightseeing, nice restaurants within walking distance and walking tours of the city including the Needle within 10-20 minutes away, friendly staff, and as usual the Westin's beds are very comfortable...now the cons..
The elevators cannot handle large conference groups (took us 20 minutes for the elevator to arrive on our floor and take us to the conference level (the elevator arrived packed full with people all trying to get to the banquet floor for dinner) plus we had to report one elevator not working very well earlier in the week.
The banquet food was not equal to the price we paid for the banquet and they ran out of food for the one breakfast and the main luncheon...luncheon cost was $75 per person! 
The rooms were not cleaned well each day, especially the bathrooms and items like the ice bucket left with water inside the next day...this is why I gave only a two rating out of five...not up to the usual Westin's standard and we usually enjoy Westin's hotels!

title: “marilyns review”
text: everything was very satisfactory . the location was exactly where we wanted to be the staff were friendly and curteous overall we wre very pleased with our stay

title: “Very friendly; nice solid hotel”
text: Nothing fancy here, but a good respectable hotel. The check-in staff is incredibly friendly and responsive. The continental breakfast is very good (they even have bananas!) My room was clean and comfortable. The wireless internet (free) is sporadic but they let me borrow a cable (no deposit!) and it worked great. The location is very convenient for getting on the highway into downtown or to DFW. I didn't notice any excessive noise from the freeway. The only downside is that there aren't may places to eat close by. All in all, a great deal.

title: “loved the decor”
text: This was our second trip to san fran we really enjoyed our stay at this hotel very spacious room, very accomadating staff especially the guys at the front door.The room was great and the aveda toiletries were lovely.Our daugher liked the daily gift from the treasure box at the front desk.The free wine tasting was great.The restaurant attatched to the hotel was not so friendly, the food was fine .The location of the hotel was great however we stayed at nob hill before and found it less noisey at night. The only complaint we had from my daughter who is 11, she was scared by the amount of tramps begging, she counted 147 all together and it did freak her out although she was perfectly safe it is a little off putting .Some friends of ours have said the same.We are from the uk and we have travelled America we love the country,however we have many tramps in our city aswell but they are policed and kept away from the shopping areas. The italian restaurant just across the road from the hotel is superb and a tip I had from a san fran lady on a past flight was to try the cheesecake factory above macey's ,out on the roof is good to sit and see the city there is a massive queue but it is worth it and the shops are great too. We also drove to monterey bay aquarium/carmel which was a lovely day out as we had done all the other sights on our pevious visit.Definately try the tram ,it is worth the queue if there is one.what an experience on the outside standing!!!!!good fun.

title: “Good location”
text: We stayed at this hotel for only one night for a business meeting. The location was great being close to Copley Square but not in the midst of it. Newbury Street was only a couple of blocks away. The room itself was nothing exceptional although the bathroom was good-sized. I noted that the room, especially the bathroom, could have been cleaned more thoroughly. The bed was not very comfortable either. However, they did have a room for us when we checked in at 8am. The price was fairly comparable to any other 4-star hotel in Boston.

title: “almost perfect”
text:
Very nice location just a couple of blocks off North Michigan Ave. shopping area. Super comfortable beds and VERY CLEAN room. Included microwave & frig. We really liked the hot tub and the pool was comfortable temperature for this time of year. (actually warm enough to swim in). Staff was friendly and helpful. 
The only things wrong were quite minor. Such as heater blower could have been a bit quieter and bathtub was a bit slow to drain. 
Would definately recommend it for anyone wanting a clean,comfortable, well located, and resonably priced hotel.

title: “great location...incredible bed...sloooooooow elevators”
text:
Recently enjoyed a fine night's stay at the Doubletree Magnificent Mile. We were able to check in about an hour and a half early which was a great start. Ron, at the front desk, wasn't exactly rude, but he won't be winning any Chamber of Commerce awards either.
The hotel is pretty much full-service, and is close to pretty much everything in Chicago. We stayed on the 23rd floor and had a great view from our room. The bed and bedding was extremely comfortable and it was difficult to get out of bed. The bathroom was spacious and clean, and the shower's water pressure was good although it never got quite hot enough for my taste.
We had appetizers and drinks in the Market House restaurant, which seems to be a nice place, if a little pricey. The mini-burgers were pretty good. There is also a gift shop in the hotel with souvenirs, toiletries, snacks, etc. It was very, very expensive but may come in handy occasionally.
Previous reviews about ultra-slow elevators are accurate. Also, the gripes about paying for internet service are legitimate, also. We, too, avoided the $ 6 Pringles and the $ 8 bottled water, but it's available if that's your thing.
Ben, the bellman, was very helpful during our checkout. Our flight did not leave until 7:00 p.m. so after we checked out, the hotel held our luggage for a few more hours so we could continue exploring Chicago.
My wife fell in love with the bed, so we'll be staying here again next time we visit The Windy City.

title: “I would stay here again”
text: I have only stayed here and in the Hyatt next door,but hands down will ask to be assigned to this hotel again. My room was in excellent condition. And as it was on the inside, it was very quiet. The bed was excellent. Actually, my only complaint was they have not provided the assortment of power outlets near the desk which make business travelers really happy.

title: “Five star service at a great price.”
text: Great service. Loved the morning paper, juice and coffee. Free Internet when you join the rewards program. Close to restaurants and shopping. Had a medical issue while I was there and they were more than helpful. Plus......the morning wake up call started the day off great with a friendly and personable voice on the other end. Great place.

title: “Unique Hotel in the Heart of Times Square”
text:
I travel often, mostly on business. I do not normally review the hotels I stay in for business, but decided to review the Renaissance because it was unique, in positive and negative ways. Overall, I would recommend staying at the Renaissance, as long as you want to experience the unique hustle and bustle of Times Square. If you want a romantic or peaceful stay, I’d recommend booking a hotel overlooking Central Park. The hotel’s positives outweighed the negatives, in my opinion, and some of the negatives are issues common at many other NY hotels. 
Pros:
• Modern, funky décor in the rooms, lobby, and bar - the hotel has a very unique, modern décor. It has a newer and trendier feel than many other lower category Marriott or Hilton properties. The pictures of the lounge and lobby on Trip Advisor reflect the feel better than I can to describe. 
• Great location in the heart of Times Square - the hotel sits between 7th Avenue and Broadway, at the point Broadway dead ends into 47th Street, across the street from where you can buy tickets to the Broadway shows. There are subway lines on the same block that go anywhere you want in the city. You are in the middle of the frenetic action of Times Square the minute you step out of the hotel entrance. There are not many other places like it in the world and, if you want that experience, this is the place to stay. 
• RLounge – the hotel’s RLounge is perfectly situated to have a drink and enjoy the best views of the unique clutter of the heart of Times Square, especially at night. The hotel’s T.V. had a continual loop advertising Bruno Mars playing in the RLounge on New Year’s Eve, with spectacular views in the background. 
• Rooms – my room (1606) was clean, good sized for NY, trendy, had modern spacious bathrooms with T.V. speakers with independent volume control, marble counters, showers with a ledge around the inside and great water pressure, a coffee maker, new HDTV flat screen, glasses for water, wine and bottle openers, a modern chair with a lamp in the corner near the window, and views in all rooms looking out to the splashy billboards on 7th Avenue or Broadway. There is not a lot of room from the end of the bed to the work desk, but enough that it didn’t create a problem for me. My room was very quiet. I was on the 16th floor, and was very impressed that the window covering kept out all the noise from the street below. I didn’t hear my neighbors, but I am not sure the adjoining room was occupied. 
• Helpful staff – the concierge, Erick, was very helpful. He recommended a wonderful, authentic Italian restaurant, Tramonti, described the dishes and his recommendations, told us which waiter to ask for, and called ahead to make reservations. The restaurant was just what I was looking for. The front desk staff also was friendly and glad to help with directions for the subway and train station.
• Two elevators – some reviewers do not like the fact you take one elevator from the first floor to the second floor, which exits to the hotel’s main lobby and lounge, and where you find the second elevator that services the rest of the floors. However, I like this fact because the lounge feels more secure and private, as opposed to having the bars/lounge as you walk in the hotel off the street. If the hotel had been very busy, you would spend more time waiting for both elevators, however. I believe this is pretty common for many of the bigger hotels in NY. 
• Morning newspaper is provided at your door each morning
Areas for improvement
• I am not used to paying $18 for internet service, and find it irritating. I would prefer the hospital figure out a way to include it in the hotel room’s nightly rate. I think in today’s world, especially in business hotels, internet should be free. This may be a common charge in NY hotels. 
• Water bottle cost – the hotel offers bottles of water, at $8 each. Again, please include this in the normal rate. 
• Toiletries – it may have been a mere oversight, but the hotel cleaning staff did not provide a bar a new bar of soap the second day. I don’t mind, as I still had soap, but it made me wonder how well or carefully the room was cleaned.
• No eco program – again, not a reason not to stay elsewhere, but I do respect hotels that give guests the option to save water by not washing all the towels every day.

title: “This is a 4.5 star hotel?”
text:
I can't complain that much, because I didn't pay full retail for the room, but got the room through hotwire. With that said, the hotel is ok in and of itself, but for it being a 4.5 star hotel, it is lacking. First off, the walls are paper thin and so is the door. You can hear everything going on in the hallways and in the rooms next to you. Secondly, our door had to be shoved open and slammed shut. The security latch was not properly installed and would catch every single time, so you would have to muscle your way into and out of the room. Also, when we first got in the room we heard this mechanical noise. It was constant for a minute, then you would hear some other noise kick in, then one stop, and start, and stop, over and over. Looking out the window you could see why, all of the air conditioning units were outside the window, literally, outside the window. If we could have opened the window, we could have touched the air conditioning unit. We didn't mind the view, it was just the noise. It wasn't a particularly loud noise, but the constant changing in volumes and tones was annoying. Lastly, I noticed when taking a bath that the shower curtain had mold on it. 
The hotel staff were friendly enough (not helpful whatsoever though with the noise of the air conditioning unit) and has a good downtown location. It's an old hotel, so the rooms are small. You can probably get a better room at a "lower starred" hotel in the same general area.

title: “Chick Hotel in the Heart of Chicago”
text: We had an amazing time at this hotel. When you first walk in you're blown away by the trendy and sleek decor, it's kind of like walking into an upscale lounge. You can tell that 3/4s of the people in the lobby/lounge are not staying at the hotel but just having some drinks and enjoying the atmosphere. We were immediately asked if we would like to be upgraded to a larger room, which of course we obliged to. The room was nice and very crisp feeling. I took advantage of the fitness center every morning, which was clean and equipped with personal tvs, head phone, ipod docks and fruit. We also took advantage of the hotel's free Acura experience, which saved us a few taxi fares. Overall, this was a great experience and we would love to visit again.

title: “Beautiful hotel, less than perfect service.”
text:
The room was really very elegant and comfortable and the bed was wonderful...but...the staff was not very helpful or friendly. 
No one we phoned at the hotel seemed to have any knowledge about the rooms or have particularly good phone manners, but we booked one of their more expensive rooms hoping our needs would be covered. On arriving we were rushed into the front door, then, although we had requested an early check in (1 hour), were told our room would probably not be ready even by normal check in time! We later found out that rooms were, in fact, ready and available. Also, be sure to put out the privacy sign at night if you don't want to be disturbed early in the morning by housekeeping entering the room. 
We still enjoyed our stay, but now know not to expect much in the way of service.

title: “HIGHLY RECCOMMENDED”
text: My wife and i who are from New Zealand stayed for 4 nights and cannot say enough about the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff. Our room was on the 23rd floor and was kept immaculately by the cleaning staff. The food downstairs was first rate and i am sure when they get a full menu sorted it will be even better. Being new to NY i was a little concerned about room security but with the swipe card access requirements in the hotel we felt extremely safe. I will be recommending this hotel to anyone who needs to stay in a central location in NY.

title: “Best location and staff”
text: We stayed during first week of October and had a great stay. The staff upon check-in was exceptional. Our room was on a high floor as requested; it was large, clean and the bedding was crisp and comfortable. It was also very quiet and so sleep was wonderful. The property is larger than I expected and the outdoor eating areas and pool area were lovely. They have fresh flavored waters in the lobby at all times and it is just refreshing when you come in from a long day out. We had rented a vehicle and it was very easy getting in and out.

title: “A bit worn around the edges”
text: I stayed overnight for a business meeting so did not have a choice of hotel. I expected this hotel to be done in a grand Southern tradition, but it's badly in need of some touch-up pain and refurbishment. The lobby area is nice enough, but staff was not particularly welcoming and tended to ignore newly seated parties for a while (despite it not being very busy). The room was adequate and quiet, but fairly bare-bones, and the carpeting could have been much cleaner. Would not return.

title: “Ok for a Place to Stay”
text: Stayed here at the last minute while visiting a friend who lives close by. It's an ok place that's located between Sea World and Fiesta Texas, so it would be ok for a family to use this as just a place to sleep and shower while visiting these parks or for a one night stay while traveling.

title: “Poor service”
text:
Amazing view, fantastic room and appalling service from bar staff on roof terrace.
STAYED 5 nights and loved the room. Bit far out with nothing close by but the service from the bar staff did not match the price. WAITED 20 minutes for 2 drinks at $40 and no apology. Hardly anyone in bar hence shocking customer service. Visit for the view but don't stay...

title: “Dirty and smelly”
text: We had stayed at the Excelsior many times - primarily for the great location and reasonable price. This time...it WASN'T WORTH IT. Our room was dirty, the bathroom was dirty, the pillows were lumpy...and, worse, the whole place smelled! We had to throw open the windows each time we entered our room. And to top it off, the people at the front desk were RUDE. We will never stay at the Excelsior again.

title: “Nice place, good value”
text:
We paid USD85 per night and stayed from July 02-05. It was good value considering the location which is near to Time Square and 4 blocks away from Subway and the Empire State Building.
Room is small and if you have 2 large suitcases, only one can be opened for packing at anyone time. However the room is very clean and the shared bathroom are modern and 'dry'. We realised that there are quite a number of repeated guests and some of them have already stayed there more than twice.
The staff there is quite all right except that you can't get much information from them. A better choice will be the information centre at Time Square.
Will definitely recommend this place for budget-conscious travellers.

title: “First Class Hotel”
text:
Our family of 6 stayed at the Intercontinental Hotel for 1 night. I had reservations for 2 rooms. My family had to take 2 cabs from the airport to the hotel. The second cab arrived 30 minutes and $30 cheaper tha the one I was riding in. After my scenic trip of downtown Boston, my cabbie finally delivered me to my destination. I told him I was only paying the fare that my husband had paid his driver and I didn't appreciate his dishonesty . I had told him 3 times during the ride the hotel where I was staying. The cabbie became very irrate with me and got out of his taxi and begin to yell at me. The bellman at the hotel stood between me and the cabbie and took care of the situation and finally told him to leave. Very nice guy.
When I checked in I had been upgraded to a larger/nicer room with a harbor view. The rooms were very nice especially the bed and pillows. Normally I don't sleep well in hotels, but this night I slept like a baby. Fruit, a box of chocolates, and water was delivered promptly after check-in ( I am a member of the ambassador level).
I had contacted the concierge 1 week upon arrival to secure Red Sox tickets via e-mail. He promptly responded and found tickets immediately for our family. They were waiting for us at check-in - great seats I might add. 
Two of my children used the pool and loved it. I liked the fact that the pool was shallow. I worked out in the fitness facility and would work out in all hotels I stay in if they were like the Intercontinental Hotel. I watched t.v. on my treadmill as I ran and bottled water was available.
We ate breakfast in the restaurant on Sunday morning. Big mistake and very pricey. Our tab for 6 (including 2 children was $212.00). Service was not friendly or prompt nor was the food that good. Plus an 18% gratuity was added.
Wish we could have stayed longer. Rooms were spacious. bathrooms luxurious and spacious, and staff (except for dining) friendly and courteous.

title: “a great place to stay”
text: Just returned from 5 days at the Herald Square and want to write a review of gratitude. I was very surprised when I read the last few reviews. They could not have stayed at The Herald Square. The rooms at The Herald are amazingly upgraded and equal to rooms at other hotels for twice as much. They are spacious with super comfortable bed, flat screen TVs and quality fixtures and finish work. The staff was friendly and helpful. The location is centrally located. I also love the theme of Life Magazine, it is a museum experience to see the Life Magazine collectable covers. The Herald Square is the best kept secret in the city. low prices for a high price experience.i can't wait til the lobby is complete and look forward to staying there again soon. I highly recommend The Herald. Ron, newport beach ca.

title: “Loved the Affinia Dumont”
text: My three girlfriends and I (including an appellate court judge) just returned from a four-night ("ladies weekend") stay at the Affinia Dumont -- and can't stop talking about the hotel. First off, I booked the hotel for the group based on the past reviews and I am glad I disregarded the few bad reviews. The hotel was perfect for the four of us -- plenty of room (big by NYC standards); the kitchennette came in very handy (especially with the Murray Market next door); the location was great (away from noisy Times Square) and within walking/cab distance to just about anywhere; and the staff were extremely friendly and accommodating. We will definitely be staying here again on our next trip and have even told my husband that next time we are in NYC we too will be staying here. In one word the experience was truly "WONDERFUL"!

title: “Great central location”
text:
Great location.
Relaxed easy going hotel. Great doormen, really friendly, always remembered us.
Great concierge, very helpful. Check in staff were helpful too.
Rooms quite small, was hoping to be placed in a larger room after paying for a Wonderful room given my SPG Gold status. Ended up relocating rooms after being woken at 6am by renovations three days in a row- staff more than obliging. Bliss products great and a fantastic massage at the spa.

title: “Excellent value, very clean and comfortable.”
text: We stayed 5 nights at this hotel. We were pleased with the central location to everything. Our room was impeccably clean and was very comfortable. We would recommend this hotel to friends or family who were staying in the area. Only one minor complaint - the free wi fi internet only worked if we sat out by the pool. For some reason the signal was too weak in our room. But other than that we were very pleased with the hotel.

title: “A gem in the heart of the city.”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Park South for 3 days and 4 nights on a recommendation from my cousin and I can't say enough about the hotel. Of all the places we have ever stayed, this hotel has the best staff. They are always smiling and are willing to help with any request. The rooms are clean and are an excellent value considering a very good breakfast comes with it. And you can't beat the location. This will be our home in NYC the next time we visit.

title: “Top of the Mark”
text:
Great view, wonderful service, large renovated rooms, and super location. Breakfast was delicious, and the cold buffet sufficed, with numerous choices. From the moment I pulled into the entrance of the hotel to the front desk, everyone was very attentive and helpful. Parking rates, like the rest of San Francisco, was $60 per day, so my recommendation is to take taxis to and from the airport, or the BART, and walk around the city. This location affords you that opportunity, walk to Market, Chinatown, and the Embarcadero.
FYI, first checked into a room at the Four Seasons, and did not care for my room. Decided to stay here instead.

title: “Deserve top ratings!”
text:
Spent 3 nights in May 2012 in an Executive Suite. We were there to relax and enjoy some of the city's delights. Overall, have to say that this hotel deserves top ratings. There is very little that can be described as deficient.
The public areas of this property is fantastic - grand double story lobby area, with discreet front desk and almost private-like elevator entrance to the rooms. The furnishings in the lobby area and general public areas are of good quality and maintained well (most of the furnishings is now quite a few years old), while the cleanliness is consistent and held to a very high standard.
Our suite was fantastic - not the biggest rooms in the suite but definitely among the most well thought out and designed. Living room, bathroom and bedroom all had large windows with delicious views. The space almost immediately makes you feel at home. Comfortable yet elegant!
The bathroom was beautiful and stunning - lots of room and lots of amenities. Just ask if you need anything else (we did - needed extra shoe horn and a pair of scissors) and they'd get it for you. no questions asked and no changes on our bill.
The bed is great - feels luxurious and easy to fall asleep in.
But the best part of this hotel is the spa, gym and pool - well thought out and well maintained. Not as good as the Peninsula Bangkok spa and gym, but definitely great. 
And the staff - professional, courteous, friendly, willing to help and always greet you, regardless of where you are. This high standard of customer service and care makes this property ideal.
Finally, this property is much better maintained, much better organized, and much better facilities than the sister property in NYC.
The only complaint (a small one) is that you have to take one set of elevators to get to the lobby and then walk quite a distance to get the the next set of elevators to get to your room.

title: “Always Wonderful at The New York Palace!”
text: Stayed at the wonderful New York Palace again in March 2012 and May 2012. I must write another review to express how much I enjoy staying at the Palace. It is such an intimate hotel in the best part of the city. Always enjoy being able to walk to so many great places, and love walking through the courtyard to see St Patricks Cathedral each day. The rooms are always clean and the beds are very comfortable. As usual the service was fabulous. Will be back in November (or sooner)!

title: “Great for the business traveller, not for families”
text: We stayed at the Omni with two children as part of a bigger world we were undertaking. To start there was a BIG misunderstanding in regards to when our room was actually ready. Being extremely tired and not wanting to go to the city centre we ended up having a very expensive lunch in the hotel whilst waiting for our room (which was actually ready to start off with). The front desk staff were not helpful at all and were not friendly and the housekeeping staff just walked into the room without knocking. The room seemed old and tired, not matching the rest of the hotel, which is beautifully decorated. We would have liked a decent breakfast, but it was very expensive and they only had a cafe type shop offering only the minimum. Plus as there was some political conference going on, we had to wait in line for ages to be served. This is a lovely hotel with a great history and great location with numerous restaurants and a metro station nearby. Also, it doesn't take long to get into the city centre and RR airport. However, I do not recommend this hotel if you are on holiday. Just a note about internet access - you have to pay a lot (although free at other hotels). Be sure to sign up as an Omni guest member before you book/stay to have access to free internet. I have stayed in Washington DC before at Crystal City and I would recommend staying in that particular area if you are travelling with children.

title: “Good location , good price , good service”
text:
We have spent 3 nights at the Inn at Queen Anne coming from a cruise and going to cross the USA by train . We selected this hotel based on the reviews from Trip Advisor and its location to enable us to visit Seattle . 
 The hotel is very close to the Space Needle and also close to public transportation to reach the major points of interest . 
 Our room had a kitchenette that enabled us to have breakfast in our room and have a snack in the evening . There are two groceries nearby and a liquor store less than 100 yards from the hotel .
 The staff was extremely helpful and friendly . We specially appreciated their recommandations for sightseeing and transportation .
 The price for our stay was very good and we consider the overall value as excellent !

title: “Perfect Location!”
text: My hubby and I just returned from visiting Boston for the first time. After talking to some friends and family we opted to stay in the Financial District and we chose the Hilton. The location is without a doubt, absolutely PERFECT if you do not mind walking or taking the subway. We even took the subway to and from the airport. These rooms are small, but clean. There really are not any views unless you have a room to the front of the hotel, but even at that, it would be just the street. We did not mind because we do not spend that much time on exploration type trips such as this one. We walked to the harbour, to North End, to the parks, the Paul Revere Trail, shopping, everywhere! PERFECT LOCATION! Very pleasant staff!

title: “Perfectly bland”
text: We got a great price at this hotel because they offer a federal rate and my husband is a federal employee. That was the only great thing about this hotel. Not to say that it wasn't nice, however, nothing about this Westin impressed us. We stayed in a king deluxe on the 8th floor. The room was clean, the bathroom was small, we have no complaints but we will probably not stay here again on vacation. It would be fine for a business trip.

title: “Maybe...”
text: We stayed at the Fairfield for a weekend celebrating our 35th anniversary. We have stayed in Manhattan many times, and were surprised at how expensive this hotel was, in spite of getting a discounted rate. Once there the room was clean and nice enough, noise to a minimum considering we were right in the middle of the busiest of areas, the bed was comfortable etc. The breakfast area was very crowded- hard to find seat, though the food was just fine, with lots of options. The "concierge" didn't seem to know her business and did not offer to give us much help in securing tickets or other things we asked her about. This was disappointing. Overall it was an enjoyable weekend, but the hotel was lackluster overall.

title: “A Delightful Surprise”
text:
I thought this hotel was a delightful surprise.
I was going to be staying at the W, but heard from a friend that there was another hotel that started with a Z that was supposed to be good.
The lady at the reception desk was a bit cold, but I have never been to a hotel where they were super.
The entire experience up to my room was delightful. They had sweets (petite cakes) in the lobby by the elevators. When I got off on my floor, there was another coffee area. Everything is mood lit, including the dark elevators. I loved it! The room was great if you like dark, modern, fun. 
The concierge was delightful. Full of energy and very nice. The Valet boys were probably the best I have ever had! 
The Dragonfly bar staff were boring. This was probably my biggest disappointment.
This is not your normal W or Hyatt. This is a FUN hotel with style.

title: “Fab hotel, excellent location”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay here. The room was very spacious, with plenty of room for the bed, a dining table and a kitchen corner. The kitchen was very well kitted out, should you want to cook something or eat in - we never got around to it. Everything in the room was very clean, as was the bathroom.
There is a laundry room downstairs, free for guests to use, which was excellent for us, as we'd been travelling for a while.
There is a small 'shop' near reception where you can get drinks and some snacks, even frozen meals, and it was very reasonably priced, normal shop prices I think.
The staff were very helpful and friendly.
The location is excellent, just a few minutes from the craziness of Times Square, but down a quiet street.
Would definitely stay again!

title: “would not stay here again”
text:
would never stay here again... there is NO PARKING.... they have 4 spots for the hotel but i noticed the surfers park there and the hotel does nothing about it... even after i brought it to their attention.
there is NO internet access, not even for pay.... NO ACCESS
our toliet stopped up in the middle of the night and WE had to go get a plunger and fix it.
would not recommend this hotel

title: “It's the staff that stands out.”
text: I've stayed several times at the Loews Regency due to its location, moderate cost (for NYC), and excellent staff. This time was no exception. I arrived early (late morning) because of a business event I had to attend at noon, and my room was naturally not yet ready. But Dinah at the front desk did her usual outstanding job of greeting me and arranging a nice upgrade for me for later. When I came back mid-afternoon to check in, the room was ready and more spacious than I expected. As usual every staff person I encountered was friendly and attentive. You can find fancier hotels nearby at higher cost, but the Loews Regency will be just fine in simply taking care of you.

title: “Excellent room, great location. Good value via Hotwire”
text: Excellent room, great location. The deal via Hotwire was exceptional (less than $100) so the value was superb. Shame the high speed net isn't free.

title: “Good Location, Good Stay”
text: The hotel has a good location, great views from the 21st floor and a nice atrium runing from the 3rd to the 21st floor with glass elevators. It is a ten minute walk to the Bart station to get to the SF Airport. I was there attending a conference and the food and refreshment service was excellent. Wireless in the common areas was good and the technology room amenities were above average.

title: “Great Hotel, great staff!”
text: This hotel is clean, newly remodeled, and in a fantastic location! We stayed on the 47th floor and had a great view. They have several elevators, so you aren't stuck waiting in ridiculously long lines. Try the sunday brunch buffet---it's great. Ahmed at the front desk was extremely helpful in clearing up an issue with our bill. We'll be staying there again.

title: “We had a wonderful time at the SLS”
text:
My teenage daughter and I stayed at the SLS for three days. It was our first trip to LA and I feel that our stay at this hotel which was fantastic made our trip great. It was interesting, unique and a lot of fun, yet it was also sophisticated. From the time we arrived at the hotel the service given by the entire staff was incredible. They were friendly yet extremely professional. The hotel itself is beautiful. 
Our room was on the 7th floor. The rooms were a bit dark, but I still found them to be functional. It was very quiet and almost felt as if noone was around yet the hotel lobby was busy and I was told that they were at 100% occupancy. The bed was very comfortable and the bathtub/shower was great. We really enjoyed the large sized shampoo, shower gel etc provided in the room. The fitness center was very nice and well equipped for a hotel which is always a nice surprise. I was able to spend two afternoons at the pool which was fun yet relaxing. The poolside service was great. The location of the hotel was good for us, as it was close to Rodeo Drive and the Grove and not too far from Downtown LA which is where I had to take my daughter each morning.
The food served at the hotel was wonderful. We were not able to have dinner at Bazaar but did have the opportunity to enjoy breakfast at Tres and lunch poolside and everything we tried was fabulous. 
Next time we are in LA, we will definitely make an effort to stay at this hotel.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: My stay was great, hotel room was clean and restaurant was good as well. My only issue was paying for internet access. As a hotel offering Comic Con rates, it seems a bit silly that you would not include some kind of internet package or food package for people going to the Con. You know we will be using internet alot while staying there and charging $40 to use it for the weekend is stupid. Other Con hotels include it, so hopefully you change that for next year, or ill have to keep this hotel off my choice list.

title: “Wonderful weekend in the heart of the City”
text: My husband and I visited in late March as part of a job interview process. The staff was wonderful from the start; the lobby bartender was great and hanging out in front of the fire place was the perfect end to the first day. Recommendations for local restaurants were fantastic, and the front desk staff even thought to ask how the job interview went (he got the job!). I would highly recommend this to anyone trying to get a sense of the City from a great location.

title: “Clean, excellent service, even better location”
text:
On the riverwalk, taking 2 minutes to access the actual walkway from the lobby, this place is a gem. The rooms were sparkling clean, the in-room whirlpool was excellent. My only slight against the rooms is they showed a few, minor, minor signs of aging (worn carpet). 
The service at this hotel is the friendliest I have ever experienced, willing to offer any help requested. I couldn't have asked for a better stay.

title: “Great Location, Plus Parking”
text:
That this hotel has an actual parking lot that gives you control of your car (as opposed to a valet lot) is a great plus. That it has nicely remodeled rooms is another plus. Our room was clean and comfortable, and it gave us a great headquarters for visiting Hollywood. If you don't want to deal with city parking, the Metro is very convenient. 
I recommend that you ask for a room on the upper floor. We were on the first floor and heard plenty of thumps from the people above us. Also, the rooms aren't huge, so if you're traveling with a group or packing along several kids, it might get a little crowded in a hurry. But for a couple or a small family, there's plenty of room.
Note that the hotel is in the heart of Thai Town. If you like Thai food, you're in heaven. If you don't (like us), then don't plan on walking to a restaurant. But there's no shortage of food choices within a few minutes of driving or a Metro stop in any direction.
All in all, for the price, the remodeled rooms and the parking, I felt it was a solid value in a town not known for values. You won't get the Ritz, but you won't pay Ritz prices, either.

title: “A Wonderful Hotel!”
text: My sister, my friend, and I stayed at the Hotel Monaco from July 26 - July 30, 2010. The hotel is quite lovely. The rooms are very spacious and clean. All employees were friendly and went out of their way to be helpful. The gym was large and had many pieces of equipment. We especially like the morning coffee, afternoon cookies, and evening wine in the lobby. We would stay at this hotel again.

title: “Excellent”
text: Great find. Brand new hotel in the medical center didtrict. Staff was great, very friendly and professional. Close to hospitals TCU, Zoo, and just minutes from downtown or the stockyards. Beds very comfortable all around, great!

title: “Great hotel, but damn the details...”
text:
We arrived Saturday afternoon and took advantage of the valet parking. We checked in quickly and then walked to our room. The room was dirty! Unmade bed, beer cans on the night stand, etc. We call the front desk, the lady apologizes numerous times, and we're reassigned to another room. No upgrade was asked for or offered. Problem #2 came later that night with loud music coming from somewhere, some other floor we figure. Problem #3 came after we checked out and left the hotel. My wife kept commenting that she smelled smoke in our vehicle (neither of us smoke and she's pregnant and very sensitive to odors). After awhile we noticed a cigarette bud on the passenger side floor, and ashes at the front bottom of the window sill on both the driver and passenger doors.
Unacceptable issues in our opinion. The hotel is cool, hip, and markets itself as a step above the rest. We enjoyed the room, the bed, and the amenities, but the devil is in the details. It appears that the W corporation knows how to design and build a hotel, but the local management doesn't know how to manage. How else can you summarize rooms being marked clean when they're not and employees smoking in vehicles that have been entrusted to them? Disappointing.

title: “Loved it baby!”
text: I stayed here back in Dec 05 but only just signed up to do reviews. We have been to NY every year for the past 8. The W was our favourite hotel yet. We have previously stayed at Essex House, The Bentley, The Edison and Portland Square. We had a fantastic room on a high floor on the corner overlooking the Square. The room was cool and the bar even cooler! The place is really trendy and modern and we loved it. Sink a few cocktails and you are guaranteed a wonderful time. Can't wait to return.

title: “Nice but be very careful inspecting your valet-parked car!”
text: Fairmonts are typically top-notch managed properties and San Jose is no exception. Everything about what they do is typically at a standard above all others and from the standpoint of hotel experience, once again, it met our expectations. Yes, they can sometimes be expensive, but if you're looking for an experience where you need services and are dealing with complications of any kind, they are the hotel of choice. They are terrific. My one bad experience on this last visit was our observation that the valets were tossing around the cars in the garage like rag dolls. They have a sign saying 20 minutes to retrieve your car, so this is a case of too few valets for the job. I got to my next stop before I noticed my 2013 vehicle had suffered minor damage while in their possession. I reported it upon my arrival at the next Fairmont and so far, no response. None. For that one incident alone, I'd probably not go back and if you are letting them park a car, inspect it.

title: “Never Ever Again”
text:
All I expected from this hotel was a basic, clean room. I didn't get anything close to clean. Please read my other reviews to know that I am not someone who complains about a hotel, in fact this will be my first.
The girl at check-in was lovely. I felt terrible for her as they were doing work on the roof and the entire lobby smelt like a mix of gasoline and paint fumes. The poor girl had been working in those conditions the entire day. They had no air-conditioning in the lobby either. It smelt like that for the 2 days that we stayed there. 
Our room was filthy! Filthy dirty carpet that was lucky to have ever met with a vaccuum cleaner. A disgusting bathroom with chunks of soap that the previous guest had used still in the shower recess. (maybe even the guest before them, for all I know) Those soap chunks stayed there for our entire trip. Our bed did not have a bottom sheet that fitted, it didn't even reach the top of the mattress so that under the pillows there was no sheet so it all came off during the night and we were sleeping on the mattress. Don't get me started on the mattress......It was an old, uncomfortable mattress with springs that you could feel digging into you back - no matress protector either. I told the cleaning lady the next morning and she replaced the sheet with a fitted one however she didn't even come close to running a vaccuum through the room. She also left us with no face towels in the bathroom.
The first night we decided to eat at Damon's which is on the hotel property. 10% discount if you are a guest of the hotel. Our waitress was the only decent person working in the place. The hostess was just plain rude. The bar had no stock of anything. They were not honouring coupons that people had brought into the restuarant in the way that they were written. The food was edible. Just edible, nothing more.
I'm so disapointed that I had to write a review like this but please take my word on this......find annother place to stay.

title: “Not worth it, no way”
text:
The St. Regis reminds me of Texas culture: a mile wide and an inch deep. Once you get past all the very ostentatious artistic touches, you find that the design is ALL there is, because the management hasn't got all the practical details of running a hotel nailed down. At this price level, there should be absolutely NO negatives on one's list, but this property has many:
The street noise in the room is indescribable. Evidently Market Street, a block away, is a main route for fire equipment on that end of town, so an unrelenting cacophany of their sirens, horns, and bells goes on all night. The architects should have spent much more on soundproofing and far less on frippery.
No night lights. With the blackout curtains drawn, it is impossible to find the bathroom without awakening one's partner by turning on a light. A small thing, perhaps, but a continual annoyance unanticipated in a $450 room. The LCD control panel is handy, but it needs a brightness control.
The TV menu didn't reflect what was actually playing at the moment. Another minor inconvenience, but frustrating when one is trying to find a specific program. Motel 6 level service.
The hall carpets on our floor (15) had a track down the middle that appeared nearly worn out. My companion thinks the look was intentional. If so, it was a lousy style choice.
The food is run-of-the-mill hotel fare, only at Michelin 5-star prices. I don't care what you put in a short stack of pancakes - nothing makes them worth $16. But I will acknowledge that the coffee was awesome.
The housekeeping staff doesn't seem to understand the concept of a "Do Not Disturb" sign on the door to a guest room. On more than one occasion, we were napping with the sign "on" and a housekeeper let herself in to refresh towels or turn down the beds. Nice service; lousy co-ordination.
No coffee or tea in the room. I like a hot cup when I get out of bed (not when room service finds it convenient).
An iron and/or steamer in the room would be nice for those touch-ups that don't warrant a $20, 2-hour round trip to the valet.
In short, the amenities, details, finishing touches, weren't up to the standard one finds in a run-of-the-mill chain. For them to be lacking in a property of this price is near criminal.

title: “Hotel Indigo is a hidden NYC gem!”
text: My fiance and I stayed at this property during our birthday weekend and were pleasantly surprised at how this little boutique gem in Chelsea was romantic,cozy, and well appointed. It is right in the heart of the Fashion District and close to all public transportation, restaurants, and shopping. Also, the rooftop lounge is a big added bonus for a quick pre-dinner drink or night cap. It is not the Gansevoort rooftop lounge (Plunge) but it does the trick. The only reason I did not give this property a 5 out of 5 rating is that we both thought the staff could have been more accomodating and less rude. My fiance needed help with her bags and the doorman stood and watched as if she were invisible. The same occured when when I was checking out. The front desk staff were more interested in their converstion than helping patrons that day I suppose. Other than that, we would definitely stay again.

title: “Great Lincoln Park Value”
text: Clean, well maintained and safe. in very trendy GLU type urban neighborhood at Clark and Diversy. older building with horizontal rooms? flat screen TVS. Extra for parking garage around the corner, with unlimited in/out privileges. second stay...first on business a few years ago! This time with wife and kids.

title: “Romance Abounds... Great hotel... Great location... Great Service!!!”
text:
My husband and I just returned from celebrating our 25th wedding anniversary at the La Mansion Del Rio. We had a fabulous and romantic experience. We arrived early and found our room was already ready for check in. The front desk staff were aware that we were celebrating a special occasion and congratulated us at check in. 
We had booked a king balcony room and had requested the 6th floor, to allow for the view without the noise. We were not disappointed and received exactly what we had asked for. The room had all the charm that I had imagined with the exposed brick and old world charm. This is not your cookie cutter hotel. The bed was plush and the room was very clean. The balcony views are great! We enjoyed sitting out there at night after a long day on the Riverwalk.
We returned from dinner on the night of check in to find a bottle of iced champange on the desk and the bed turned down. This was not part of "our package". They simply wanted to help us celebrate. We received turn down service every night and complete consideration for the privacy sign on the door, with notes placed under the door asking if we needed anything. Everyone we encountered was friendly and ready to serve.
We had breakfast in the restaurant twice and found the food to be very good. The staff was attentive and atmosphere was relaxed. I think that is part of the charm.
We have stayed at several hotels in downtown San Antonio, both on the Riverwalk and a few blocks off. I would recommend this hotel to anyone... Families or couples. This is one you have to experience for yourself. You won't be disappointed!

title: “Lovely stay”
text: Stayed here after moving from the louder Hard Rock hotel. Beautifully appointed room, excellent staff. The bar and restaurant were great. I love that Andaz minibars offer complimentary soft drinks and limited snacks. When I'm paying over $200 for a room It's irritating to pay $5 for a bottle of water. The bed was very comfortable, but in the future I would ask for an outside facing room, as the interior ones prevent you from opening the drapes as you have ten other rooms looking in. And you may want an elevator close room if traveling with luggage, as the halls can be long. Friends were in an Andaz loft room and it was beautiful, but same thing, no view and lacked privacy. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again, but I would request a room in a better location.

title: “Perfect Location”
text: This hotel is located one block from Michigan Avenue and within walking distance of most major attractions. The staff was friendly and the rooms kept clean. Trader Joe's around the corner....so grab something for breakfast or lunch, as the rooms have a fridge and microwave. Would definately stay again on my next trip to this fabulous city!

title: “The Plaza 5*, Sofitel 4*? A joke...”
text: I arrived in New York on a short business/pleasure trip and promptly checked in at The Plaza, which, had I have read the reviews on here, would have avoided in the first place.I checked out after 3 hours and was recommended the Sofitel by a colleague. So there I headed.For both business and pleasure side of things (i.e. need an early night/come back late at night!) the hotel is perfect. Superb location, very (*VERY*) friendly and accomodating staff across the board (concierge/front desk/bar) and a fantastic room (had a "Superior Queen" - looked round a suite for an extra $100 a night and, had I have planned to stay in the hotel longer, I would have upgraded to).As a previous reviewer wrote, you can hear activity in the corridor sometimes, but I didn't find it too obstructive.How a hole like The Plaza can be a 5* hotel, versus the 4* Sofitel, I will never know.Will definately be using this hotel as "base" in my future visits, and will be recommending my colleagues and friends alike to do the same.If after you've stayed here you feel differently, I'm sure the staff would only be too willing to right any wrongs.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
I was a little nervous about staying in this hotel as it was not in Trip Advisor's top 10! but we got an excellent deal with Expedia when we booked it along with return flights from LA with Alaska Airlines. When we arrived I was pleasantly surprised. The rooms are very spacious and the beds were pretty comfy.
This hotel is in an amazing location, the shops, monorail, restaurants are all on your doorstep. We tried the buffet breakfast on the first morning, this was nice but quite pricey. The concierge was very helpful booking our trip to the Boeing factory. The top floor pool & gym are great. Our room was also very quiet which was good. The coffee maker was also a nice touch. We took the Gray Line downtowner bus from the airport which is a bargain at $17 return and stops directly outside the hotel. All in all this is a great hotel and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it especially if you can get it for a good price.

title: “WONDERFUL EXPERIENCE!!!!”
text:
I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at Mansion at Judges' Hill. I have read previous unflattering reviews and have to say that I did not experience any of those things! I came for a weekend with a dear friend for shopping/relaxing/visiting and we found the hotel to exceed all expectations. The Mansion at Judges' Hill is a BOUTIQUE hotel. It is not a large, sprawling complex. It is a small hotel in a formerly private home (mansion.) The photos on their website are exactly what you get. The furniture was beautiful and in excellent shape. The beds were plush and comfy. The bathroom was beautifully appointed with a wooden vanity, tile floors, LARGE tiled shower, beautiful gold mirror, etc. There was also a mounted, lighted, magnifying mirror for putting on makeup, etc. That came in handy for putting in contacts! There were Gilchrist and Soames shampoo, conditioner and lotion. The double queen room was roomy enough to easily accomodate 2 adults and 2 teens. It featured a very large dark wood armoire that housed a tv and could accomodate folded as well as hanging clothes. The full-wall draperies were gorgeous. The room had a very solid, luxurious feel. What you see on the website is exactly what you get. When we returned from a day of sightseeing/shopping the room had been tidied, towels replaced, and beds turned down. We felt very pampered. The staff was extremely polite and helpful. We mentioned that we were interested in having dinner at The Oasis while we were checking in. About an hour later as we were enjoying drinks in the courtyard an office clerk came out and delivered to us printed directions to The Oasis and even thoughtfully printed out a list of the times for sunset informing us that the best time to dine would be at sunset for the beautiful views!! She was right...we arrived and had dinner and it WAS beautiful. Thanks again! The courtyard I mentioned is one of my favorite places there.....it is covered by a beautiful canopy of trees....it was a great spot to have a drink and visit. We didn't have a chance to eat at the site's restaurant but do intend to do so on our next visit. I just cannot say enough positive things about my visit....it definitely exceeded all expectations. 
Just remember, it's a boutique hotel which means you won't find another like it! It's unique and is definitely NOT a huge, sprawling corporate affair. That's not what we wanted in the first place. It's everything they advertise it to be. 
I know I've gone over and above but I wanted to tell my story in light of some of the negative reviews I read. 
The Mansion at Judges' Hill is my all-time favorite place to stay now in Austin!!

title: “Awesome upgrade!”
text:
My husband planned a surprise night for me at the "W" last weekend. It has been one of our favorite spots for cocktails since it opened and we have often talked about staying overnight. Our experience has always been fun, it has a several lounges to choose from, each with it's own vibe. Music is central to Austin and it is well represented here as well. The service has always been excellent from the doormen to the interior staff. 
On this particular night as my husband told me he had packed a bag for me and we were staying over, the concierge told us we were being upgraded to the Presidential Suite. I thought she was kidding, but my husband has been a Starwood member for years and this was an appreciation upgrade to him. We have traveled world-wide and this was by far the classiest effort we have received. The suite was beyond wonderful with a magnificent view of Austin. We 
enjoyed room service as we did not want to venture out after checking in. 
We most certainly recommend the "W" for not only their lovely hotel, but because they go beyond imagination in service!

title: “poor customer service”
text: A few people actually did behave as if they worked in a 4 star resort. The staff at the Acqua restaurant and PATRICIA from the marketplace. Patricia went out of her way to be helpful. The staff at the front desk should be replaced - There are so many lovely hotels in san diego - I would not stay here again. -- grounds beautiful,attended a wedding, nicely done. rooms okay mine needed a better cleaning- dust covered tables. arrived early and expected to wait for my room in the tower. I did not want the villas but she said it was in the same villa as my other family members - it was NOT, lovely view of the parking lot and quite a walk to the rest of the family.. Decided to just endure since it was only a few days and I did not want the bride to feel things were anything but perfect. Gift bags from the wedding couple that were supposed to be delivered to the rooms took several inquiries before I got mine. My sister NEVER got hers. no one from the hotel seemed to care, she got tired of asking - no smiles, hope u enjoyed your stay, how were things etc. I did not have a car but seemed like the front desk clerk ( the same one that gave me the dusty room) chose who got charged or did not. The man before me at check out said he had a car and was questioning if he should be getting the $32 charge - the desk clerk said oh but" u did not have a car - right? " the man just said ok and left.

title: “Could be a fourstar hotel - but very poorly run”
text:
My husband and I just spent our First Anniversary there. We came into town on Saturday morning and had plans to see the Red Sox vs. Yankees as an anniversary girt. Upon arriving to the hotel we were impressed by the overall service being provided to the other guests. When it was our turn the young lady behind the front desk informed us our room was unfortunately not ready (at this point it was 1:30pm) but they would make it a priority as the previous guest had already checked out and to come back in an hour. We told her we were in a rush and needed to make the 4:10pm game at Fenway - she said no problem - we went and ate lunch and returned at 3pm. 
Upon returning we were asked to wait while they checked on the status of our room ...after waiting at the desk for ANOTHER 30 MINUTES We were informed it would be at least another 30 minutes until the room was cleaned. We then asked to be put in any room that was available - although we were supposd to be in a Junior Suite. We were checked in a very clean room with nice amenties, albeit many did not work properly such as the espresso machine and stereo - which had one small window which faced the interiorof the building. We had to rush to get a cab and did not arrive at the game until halfway through the first inning, which was very disappointing.
Upon checkout the next morning our bill came and was NOT adjusted to show the reduced rate for the King room as we were assured it would. When my husband went down to the desk to point this out the gentleman working informed him that the man working the prior day had been mistaken in telling us that - which was ridiculous and not our problem as far as we were concerned - and after telling him this he finally honored the previous front desk workrs promise. And then he offered us breakfast - whichhad already been promised to be taken care of the day before - although there was no note of that.
Overall this is a very clean hotel, with nice rooms and bathrooms - but we were let down by the service and for what we hoped to be a wonderful experience on our fist anniversary. All it did was cause us frustration and stress - over and over again. We had been planning on staying at a Doyle Hotel in London and most certainly will not based on this experience.

title: “Good location - Bad Service”
text: The hotel is in the middle of Financial District . That is a nice place so you can reach every point in San francisco easily. the hotel is avarege . neither the girl at the lobby nor his chinese manager knows english so it was hard to communicate and understood . the hallway was smelling so terrible that we were try not to breath for a while until we reach our rooms . the price is valuable ; location is good . but thats all .

title: “Loved this place.”
text: I was very pleased with my stay at this Candlewood. The staff were always friendly, smiling, and very helpful. Every day my daughter and I stopped at the front desk to ask for directions to our destination and we always received great directions. They don't offer daily housekeeping (which is about the only thing I wasn't happy with), however, they will give you clean towels any time you ask. Their outdoor pool was lovely and well-kept. If I ever plan to spend time in Indianapolis again I will definitely stay here.

title: “That's Riiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiitz, baby!”
text:
Life is very dark and very bleak. That's why we all need to drink champagne and stay at the Ritz (c) Truman Capote.
Legendary hotel on the 59 street aka Central Park South. It's the street full of luxury hotels including the Plaza, Essex House and Mandarin Oriental. You can have a carriage ride by the Central park. That's very pretty and very NYC but that's why the street smells like... you know...
I used to live couple blocks away so often had lunch or drinks at the hotel. The bars and lounges are nice.
I stayed there only once with my girlfriend after the New Year Eve party, and was pleasantly surprised the rooms were very clean and big, and very well decorated. 
If you're coming to NYC for a visit, I'd definitely recommend Ritz Calrton, just a great place to be in the very heart of the city!

title: “A great stay”
text:
I stayed at the Airport Radisson earlier this month and had a great experience. The front desk staff was very friendly and upgraded me to a suite for being a Club Carlson member. 
The room was clean, comfortable and spacious. 
 I had dinner at the hotel restaurant and it was fantastic. My server was friendly and upbeat and took excellent care of me. (red hair, dont remember her name :) )
 The shuttle made regular trips to the airport so that was one less thing for me to worry about the day I left. I travel to the Phoenix area every month or so and will definitely stay here again.

author.location: North Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, United States

title: “Might stay again”
text:
I was at the hotel for a conference in early November. This was the hotel for the conference organisers hence why I stayed there. 
Arriving at the airport I phoned the hotel to book a shuttle. The airport phones for hotels were broken so I phoned from my cell phone. The shuttle was due to arrive at 1015 but I phoned back to the hotel at 1030 as no shuttle. I thought I may have missed the bus but when it finally arrived at about 1050 the shuttle was obvious and distinctive.
WARNING - The shuttle bus is suited for people only. It is up steps with a narrow entrance. THERE IS NO LUGGAGE RACKS and if you are like me and have a large suitcase you need to sit in front row with the suitcase in the aisle. Luckily shuttle bus was never full otherwise impossible to get luggage on. Very surprised at this - seemed only hotel with no luggage space on shuttle buses.
Lobby and checkin were very nice. The staff throughout hotel were VERY friendly during my stay. However when travelling to room the corner pieces from walls has been removed to enable renovation of hotel, it looks very bad and put a damper on peoples views of hotel from outset.
The room was small by US standards but large enough by European standards. The room was clean and the bathroom was very clean. The room did have a slightly musty smell and the TV was very old and hard to get it to work. 
I tried breakfast on first morning, it was not good. Felt like a high school canteen but lower quality. Understand it is primarily a conference centre but they would not pass for a hotel you would stay at when not a conference centre.
I think these are issues that will improve with renovations but due the hotels location I doubt it would be a destination for anything other than conferences.

title: “Excellent Budget Hotel”
text:
Recently got back from a 5 night stay at Red Roof Inn, Manhattan. The location of this hotel is brilliant, 10mins walk from Times Square & Broadway and good subway access. 
Good sized room, plenty of space to move around even with the 2 massive suitcases. We booked 5 months in advance and requested a view of the Empire State Building, which we got. 
My sister & her husband, who were travelling with us, booked 2 months ago and were not so lucky with their room. Upon arrival they were put in a Smoking room despite having booked non-smoking. They immediately went to request a room change and were told that their booking wasn't an actual booking, merely a request. Unwilling to accept this they insited that they get a non-smoking room and the girl on reception was very unhelpful until the manager eventually stepped in and sorted things out. 
Breakfast was fine, good to fill up on before a day sight-seeing. The breakfast room is very small for the size of the hotel, but we only had to eat in our rooms on one day. 
We would definitely reccommend this hotel, excellent price and location, probably one of the best value hotels in New York.

title: “Good Hotel”
text: A very nice Hotel, within walking distance of the wharf and Pier 39. The room was very clean and spacious, with a very Comfortable bed. No problems at all. Would stay here again.

title: “Very nice upgrade”
text: Got upgraded to one of the casitas in my last stay during a conference. Very nice one bedroom, kitchen area, 1.5 baths, and 2 queen beds. I had a small problem with the drain in the main bathroom and it was fixed within a few hours. Very good room service.

title: “I know it's historic/iconic but...”
text:
I don't care for it. I've stayed at this hotel twice now, both for conferences. The rooms have been updated and parts of the lobby, but the rest looks like a step back to the 70s. Also the layout is annoying. There are different towers for rooms and the elevators don't stop on all floors - you have to take stairs/escalators to get to some floors. Finally the food is not good...
I'm usually a Westin fan but the decor/service of the hotel is not on par.

title: “truly 5 Star”
text:
this is one of the very best hotels I ever stayed at. I consider myself as a very demanding client, I have no problem paying a bit more but then again, I expect the best. And this hotel is truly 5 star.
Everybody seems to make sure you enjoy your stay, they know you by name. The rooms are fantastic, the food at the restaurant is outstanding. Service is spectacular and I am really sorry I only had three nights at this wonderful place.
If you feel you deserve the best, this is the place to be.
Truly, truly recommendation!!!!

title: “A wonderful escape in San Francisco”
text: this was the fourth joie de vivre property we stayed in during our honeymoon in california. each property is completely different and each has its own charm. we had a slight problem with our luggage here, probably a communication issue, but after around two hours it was delivered as well as a complimentary bottle of wine. the rooms r charming and ours had a fireplace which was certainly needed in the cold san francisco weather. it is conveniently located and within walking and public transportation access.

title: “I'd stay there again BUT...”
text:
I've read a lot, both good and bad, about the Custom hotel prior to my trip. The rooms, hotel, the staff is totally OK but the hotel is missing a few of the most important accommodations to be able to pass for a good airport hotel. 
1. Shuttle service forgot to pick us up. We booked shuttle 3 days prior to the trip (like the homepage said we could). We called, spoke to the front desk and sent en e-mail. When we arrived to LAX there was no shuttle there. Wohoo first time in US.. where to go? We had to call them again for them to pick us up. The explanation was that they had no booking from us. Come on! We are grown ups. Why even offer "the book before" service if it doesn't work? 
2. No coffee until 7 am. I mean people are jet lagged, they need coffee whenever during the day/night. Airport hotel means guests form all over the world. A coffee machine in the lobby could save lives. Luckily there was a coffee shop and food store where one can get coffee 5.30 during weekdays. I've had few other guests expressing the same issue and asking me where they could get coffee.
3. The smoking area outside of the hotel is horrible. The hotel is a non smoking facility but guests arrive from all over the world. They do smoke. Give them some space where they could take their coffee and cigarette (outside the hotel of course). A place to sit and a table? Even other co-smokers thought it was a joke. 
But all and all if you're a non smoking, non coffee drinking person who doesn't mind being stood up by booked shuttle service after a 17 hrs flight be my guest.. or the guest of Custom hotel.

title: “Clean, excellently located with good sized rooms”
text:
Rooms were clean, of generous proportions and well stocked with hotel amenities. The personalised rubber ducks were a quirky touch, and good for a souvenir upon returning home.
Staff were generally helpful, although seemed as if they were preoccupied in some instances. Sometimes staff were caught leaning or playing on mobile phones when guests were seemingly requiring service.
The fresh fruit and cookies in the lobby each day were appreciated and make a good morning or afternoon snack.
The location of the Chancellor is excellent - right in the heart of Union Square, only 1.6 miles down to fisherman's wharf and a stones throw away from Macy's, Bloomingdale's, Saks's and Nordstrom for any shopping requirements. 
Just over the hill from this hotel is Chinatown - this precinct is well worth the visit, where cheap eats, interesting shops and traditional culture still abound.
Requesting a room at the rear of the hotel is worth it if you are a light sleeper. Additionally, the mattresses are of a good quality, and coupled with the extensive pillow menu, one should get a good sleep in any of the Chancellors room.
In all, the price of this hotel, its central location and reasonably attentive staff make this hotel excellent for both families and the business traveler.

title: “Good Location - Bad Hotel”
text:
Stayed at his hotel in September, had booked a one bedroom suit and was given a studio apartment, but as there was three adults and one being my stepson who is 19 it was abit embarrassing when getting ready, Location good but hats about it. Staff unfriendly and not helpful what so ever..
Would not recommend this hotel to anyone, stay in a neighboring hotel around the same area..
Rooms and windows could do with a good clean room smelt musty.
Really enjoyed the holiday and weather was lovely, but would stay some where else next time.
I hope these reviews are read so they can make it better.

title: “Crowne Plaza Suites 9090 Southwest Freeway Houston TX 77074”
text:
I just stayed at this Crown Plaza Suites for a two week period in November taking part in a training program..As the name says, this is a suite hotel. The suites are among the nicer mid-price hotels at which I have stayed and are quite large. All face an inner courtyard that goes up multiple floors If you have problems with height, therefore, it would be best to ask for a lower level suite. The railings are ironwork and you can see the restaurant and lounge from the upper floors.
The suites consist of a living room in the front with a very nice kitchenette area and a good work space (good light; lots of outlets). The WiFi functioned superbly. There is a nice sofa, a chair with a hassock, and a fairly decent flat screen 32 inch LCD television that got good reception in both the living area and the bedroom. I felt that there was a limited selection of channels as compared to the comforts of home, but it seems to nbe a typical issue in many of the Hotels I have stayed in. The kitchenette consists of a small refrigerator and a microwave. There were very limited kitchen tools, cutlery, and so forth. There is a coffee pot with ceramic mugs, which are so much nicer than the plastic cups Holiday Inn makes available. Thery had Wolfgang puck coffee which was excellent and I felt that two packets of regular and one of decaf was a good and thoughtful touch.
The bedroom is separated from the living area by the bath and therefore is away from hall noise and has a complimentary safe which I thought was a very thoughtful touch. The bedrooms have windows opening to the exterior balcony.
The bath was very nice and there was plenty of hot water and large, fluffy towels and a bathrobe. The closets were more than adequate for a single traveler. I had a friend visit me over the weekend and there was plenty of room for her clothes as well. The hotel has laundry facilities on the third floors that consist of three washers and three dryer. They seemed to work very well (I used them). 
Front desk staff were very welcoming and helpful, including helping me to mail letters, which is not always the case. I am a priority Club Member and they handed me a "goody bag " full of complimentary items, a bottle of water, cookies and a pass for reserved parking in a few spaces up front at Check in. This was a great perk and I truly appreciated it. I had breakfast buffet every day in the restaurant which was included in my rate. The food was excellent with many choices was very good, but felt that the service was a little inconsistent.
There is a very nice gift shop staffed by helpful and friendly people on the ground floor. The lobby is quite nice with lots of comfortable seating and the Hotel offers a good bar with a decent selection of wines by the glass (or I suppose by the bottle). The bar is an open lobby bar and was a good place to sit during the day outside of class for work, email checking, and so forth.
The hotel has a decent fitness center which is located inside the indoor pool and Jacuzzi area. The equipment is acceptable and has a universal gym, treadmills, bicycle and free weights I did not use the pool, but It appeared to be quite inviting, and probably great for a dip at the end of the day.
The rooms at this hotel and the staff make it a great value. I would definitely stay and eat here. 
Larry Hamilton Lexington SC

title: “Fine Choice in Philadelphia”
text: Just spent an overnight at this lovely B&B. The service was outstanding, the attention to detail in the furnishings and breakfast impressive, the staff very helpful. Would be delighted to stay there again.

title: “A Welcome Return Visit”
text:
