We stayed at The Library 2 years ago and it was definitely one of the biggest reason for returning to NY. Sadly the unexpected upgrade we had received last time wasn't repeated but our Queen Deluxe was more than adequate for our stay. In fact the stay was great and only really less than perfect because the hotel was so much busier than the first time we visited. This meant arriving at breakfast often included a slightly embarrassing loiter for a space to sit. The only other downside was that the people staying in the room next to us seemed to relish letting the heavy room door slam at every opportunity! 
All in all highly recommended though possibly in danger of becoming too popular!

title: “Relax in New York”
text: I go to the big city to get away and Chelsea Pines is a great place to do that. The staff is very helpful with tips on what to see and how to get around. Go to the bookstore and get a small laminated map of the NYC subway system and you can get anywhere you want to go. I have stayed there 5 times and will definitely stay there for my next visit.

title: “Nice Hotel -”
text:
So much to say about this hotel - The hotel was nice, clean and quiet. Most of the staff was friendly, and would acknowledge you when you came in. The rooms were nice, and I did not have any issues with any requests I made - but I did have a problem with my billing when I left. 
It took contacting the Hotel General Manager and two full days to get it straightened out. 
I would recommend this hotel - just don't try and use two different forms of payment at checkout.

title: “Club Quarters - clean value hotel in Downtown Boston”
text:
This was our second stay in a Club Quarters (the other in Chicago) and we were not disappointed. CQ hotels are often much cheaper than other area hotels, and although members have first preference, reservations are often open to the public. As was our previous CQ experience in Chicago, rooms here are small and geared towards business travelers with not much but a bed, a desk, a small wall-mounted lcd tv, and a bathroom. I especially appreciated the desk where I could plug in my netbook and other electronics. Yes, there is free wireless Internet here and the speed seemed pretty good. As a guy, I especially appreciated the dark woods and plaids used in the decor. 
There is a filtered water machine on each floor, and I think they will provide bottles at the front desk. The location is close to several places of interest, although it's definitely in Downtown Boston among several tall buildings (ie. not much of a view from any of the windows here). It's a few short blocks walk from the State T-stop (in the Old State House) to this hotel. Also within a few blocks of several shops at Downtown Crossing, including large Marshall's and TJ Maxx stores. It's also a 15-minute walk to Faneuil Hall, Quincy Marketplace, the New England Aquarium, and the beautiful wharf area. If you're Catholic, be sure to check out the St. Anthony Shrine Church in the neighborhood. We went to Mass there and the music was some of the best "church music" we've heard! Finally, there's a nice Elephant and Castle restaurant connected to the hotel which features British pub-style food. I'm an E&C fan, so this was an added bonus for us.
My only complaint would be the long waits for the two slow elevators in the hotel. There were often groups of people waiting in the lobby for a ride upstairs and waits were often several minutes. Also, it's a nice security measure, but the elevator will not move until someone puts their room key in the slot by the elevator buttons.
For good value, clean but small rooms, and a location close to several Boston landmarks, you can't go wrong with Club Quarters Boston.

title: “Excellent Choice”
text: Impressed the minute I walked through the door. Decor was very modern and appealing (especially in the lobby). The front desk staff were all cordial, helpful and professional. The room had lots of space even with 2 queen beds. It was very clean, comfortable and inviting. Even the bathroom was spacious. The exercise room was well kept and sufficient enough for my short stay. Breakfast offered many choices, something for everyone. There was also security on site which made someone like me traveling alone even more comfortable. There are restaurants, drugstores, a mall, hospitals, even a Kroger nearby. Would definitely stay there again, this was a great pick - being there just felt good (and safe)!!

title: “NOT FOR ME”
text:
I was totally disappointed with this property. i didn't expect elegance; but I, certainly, did not expect a college dorm room. That is what you get in the standard queen room. The reviews I read on the property did not adequately prepare me for the reality.
Upon check-in, upgrades--starting at $20/night---are advertised. Understandably! The standard queen is a tiny, bare bones room. I have never stayed in anything quite like this---and, definitely, not for the price I paid. Fortunately, I was here for only one night.
The only plus for me was free internet access.
If you need to stay in this area and chose this hotel, UPGRADE, UPGRADE, UPGRADE.

title: “Nice hotel close to Camden Yards”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton for 3 nights in September and were very pleased with our stay. We happened to be there when the Orioles were out of town so the area was quieter than I'm guessing it is when they are in town. It's directly next to Camden Yards though, which means there's lots of sports bars in the area (helpful for watching college football games!). The hotel is also about a 10 minute walk to the Inner Harbor, with several restaurants on the way. There is also a free bus that has several routes around the city and there is a stop right outside the lobby.
We had a harbor view room, which was beautiful (don't expect the harbor to be your total view, there are other buildings in Baltimore that block a portion of it). The room was very clean and spacious and the bed was extremely comfortable. Service at the hotel was also great, friendly and helpful staff. Our only issue was that they double-charged us for parking but realized their mistake immediately and resolved the issue as soon as they could. While parking might seem expensive at $28/day, it was in line with every other hotel in the area and we had in/out privileges and had no issues with finding a spot. The bar was a little pricey but the drinks were strong and the bartender friendly.

title: “A great hotel in a great location”
text:
We stayed here for two nights over Thanksgiving. From the check-in to the check-out, everything was great. We could check in early and were upgraded to a club-level room. The room was on the 6th floor and very quiet.It was a good size and clean; the bed comfortable, the bathroom adequate (love the animal print robe!). The desk perfect for our laptop (free WiFi with the Kimpton loyalty program). 
Free drinks and nibbles in the club-level lounge. Continental breakfast downstairs was included for us (limited choices: coffee, tea, bread, butter, jam and fruit - perfect for me to start my day).
The location is great. Perfect if you want to go to Union Square, get the cable car, etc.
The best thing about the hotel, however, is the staff. Helpful, polite, nice. We felt valued and appreciated, pampered and cared for. Thank you!

title: “Dog Friendly Hotel!!”
text:
The location is slightly off the beaten path of the beach resort lifestyle and nightlife, however upon arrival, we were greeted with a warm smile, very helpful and dog friendly staff. When driving North on Mayport Rd. you may think to yourself, "I'm not to sure about this location?", "looks pretty far from anything." This hotel is only a short 5 min drive south to the heart of Atlantic and Neptune Beaches with dog friendly restaurants and bars. Or 5 minute drive north to Hanna park with 5 miles of dog-friendly beach (leashes are required), or just 25 miles North to Fernandina Beach!
Victoria and Amelia (Front Desk) assisted us with all of our questions, and offered assistance directing us to all the dog-friendly restaurants and beaches. Amelia doted on our dog (Lab mix), and she even baked hand made cookies for welcoming new guests and saying goodbye to the outgoing guests.....and they were the BEST cookies I have ever had!!
Once inside, you are transported to a 4 diamond hotel in the heart of a major city. The staff went above and beyond at every request. The hotel was immaculately clean! And the housekeeping staff was friendly and conscientious, even placing our dog's toys back in her dog bed. There is a complimentary continental breakfast that offers eggs, bacon, susage, biscuts and gravy as well as all the extra goodies. We were thoroughly impressed! The staff's care and concern for their guests (including the animals) was beyond reproach and I highly recommend this location at 2040 Mayport Rd. for a weekend getaway or even just an overnight.
A special thanks to Victoria and Amelia, you really made our stay special!!

title: “Pretty Nice”
text:
I just came back from a weekend in Philly. Stayed at the Hotel Palomar for 1 night, but wish we had more time or had gotten there earlier! (It took us a while because of the crazy monsoon that happened in the tri-state region!) Anyways, my boyfriend and I just got to Hotel Palomar around 8 pm. We had dinner reservations at Alma de Cuba (see my review on it- de-lish!), so we just wanted to dump our stuff and go. Was greeted with a smile at the front desk, and some sympathy for the ridiculous ride :) I had booked a queen, but was upgraded to a king deluxe, which was awesome. It happened to be in a corner room, which was oddly shaped, but faced the street, and had 3 windows. We were on the 11th floor, so it wasn't bad in terms of noise.
The room was smaller than other rooms I had stayed at (hotel palomar in Washington DC), but still had nice decor and cleanliness. The bathroom is smaller than usual, but my boyfriend and I were able to be in there without any hassle. I think the only downside would've been the sliding door, which i think a smaller kid might have issues closing because of the weight of the door, and the ease of pulling it wasn't there.
The walls weren't that thin that we could hear our neighbors, but I could hear doors slamming and footsteps (it was St. Patrick's Day, so I'm sure there were a few drunks trying to get back to their rooms). Also heard outside traffic from honking or ambulances, but as we were in the heart of the city and facing the street, it was obvious you would hear noise. It didn't bother me, and my bf didn't hear it - he was out like a light from the comfortable bed :)
We had brunch the next day at Square 1682 (or something like that!). Food was pretty good, and our waitress was extremely attentive. We lingered a bit, as they had newspapers out, so we sat and read a while. It was a little more money for brunch than usual, but it was in the hotel, and food was pretty good. I had the eggs entree and my bf had the french toast. We shared a fruit plate and had 2 teas- came out to about $32 or so. 
I did valet parking the night before (since we just wanted to get out of the car!). It was a bit pricey- $37 for the night, but it was fine by me. We checked out and had until 6 pm the next day to retrieve our car, so we just checked out, asked them to hold out luggage, and came back to get everything. Everyone- from the person who got me some toothpaste :), to valet, to portage, to even the hostess, was extremely efficient, super nice, and always made sure we were okay. This was my second stay at a Kimpton Hotel, and I really think its a bargain for the type of rooms, level of service and locations that they are in. I would recommend this one to anyone I know.

title: “Convenient”
text: This was my first stay at a Drury so I was surprised at the level of service. It was Mother’s Day weekend and all of the staff wished us a Happy Mother’s Day. Throughout the hotel staff greeted us in passing, a nice touch. I am not exactly a morning person so when the chipper young lady greeted us at our breakfast table I wasn’t prepared for her friendliness and welcoming greeting to Charlotte. She chatted just a tad bit too long for so early in the morning – just saying. The evening snack and beverage can easily be a small meal if you are tired and want to stay in. If you haven’t stayed in a Drury I recommend trying them. I will definitely book again. A lot of service and amenities for your dollar. And a nice shopping mall withing walking distance.

title: “They do that bit extra to make it a really nice stay.”
text: I stayed at a couple of places on this trip and the Library was by far the best one. The staff were very helpful and friendly from the outset. Obviously the services such as the cheese and wine (which was really nice!) give you a good feel about the place but I particularly liked their relaxed attitude - saying I could invite a friend to have the wine and cheese and that I was welcome to use the lounge during the day of departure, even after checking out. The location is excellent and the rooms were very nicely fitted out. It is certainly not the cheapest but it is well worth it - they do that bit extra to make it a really nice stay.

title: “Great Resort for Families”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a conference in August 2011. Great service, good food, clean rooms! The resort does seem to cater to families (which is fine) so there were a lot of children running around. Plenty of activities in the pool area scheduled throughout the week. I was traveling alone on business, but if you're planning a resort getaway with your children, consider Hyatt Hill Country outside San Antonio.

title: “Planning our next trip back”
text: The staff was most helpful above and beyond courteous! The rooms are very clean and comfortable. The neighborhood is safe, you couldn't ask for a better location!! Centrally located to walk most anyplace with easy subway access or catch a cab right out front. Quick, easy trip to Yankee Stadium!! Highly recommended!!

title: “Lovely ambience at Elysee”
text:
I tried the Elysee after the Library Hotel, where I've often stayed , was less than efficient at handling the reservation. The Elysee is less hip but, for me, more convenient and pleasant in its own way. The reservationist asked my preferences and then seemed pleased to offer a room with 2 exposures. 
With a chandelier, the well-appointed room (comfortable bed!) was peacefully Old New York-y, though the tub was shallow and there was big noise, even 10 floors up, from some semi-continuous garbage operation down 54th. 
Adding to noise were rambunctious kids on my floor. The front desk offered to address the issue, but, since I was staying only 2 nights, we just made a joke of it. 
Breakfast and the evening wine offerings were satisfying, in a comfy atmosphere. The staff were unfailingly polite and helpful; the hotel supplied an umbrella; and when I traipsed in from my wet wanderings, the Elysee truly felt like a refuge.

title: “Priceline says 3 star - Not even close.”
text:
We ended up with this hotel through a Priceline request of 3 star hotels.
This was NOT a 3 star hotel. We understood that New York City prices are generally way out of whack with what you get elsewhere, but the hotel seems to be pretty run down.
Having read other reviews we heard they were amidst renovations, so we tried to get a revamped room. The first room was a sardine can, so we moved to a room with 2 beds (my wife and I slept apart because the beds were so small). The updated room seemed to have a slightly newer bathroom, but not much else.
Problems we had:
- strange smell in room
- screaming kids across hall (not hotel's fault) but since the halls are so small and walls thin, you can hear alot.
- window shade didn't go down letting sunlight in early
- weak shower pressure
On the bright side - the staff was very courteous and the location is good for tourists. 
Long and short - DON'T USE PRICELINE FOR HOTELS. We ended up checking out a night early b/c the hotel was so beneath our expectations (and what we paid for), and Priceline has given us nothing but trouble with customer service. Their ratings for hotels have no merit, and their treatment of customers is beneath terrible.

title: “would not revisit”
text: Looks OK and well located. A group of us were staying and the general feedback was the same - tired rooms in need of updating. Bathrooms particularly small. Staff good.

title: “very nice. traveled with baby.”
text: We stayed here for a wedding across the street. I personally didn't see much green about it, but that's not why I was there. FYI breakfast closes at 10am. It wasn't fabulous but oh well. We had a 2 bed room and it was very large. We used their playpen and it worked out well. They also have laundry for $1 wash and $1 dry. However I didn't see detergent so keep that in mind. Parking can really add up, but be safe because someone had their car broken into ( she had her phone and GPS sitting in the seat for the world to see). If you are traveling in a group ask for your rooms to be close because we were placed in different towers of the hotel and had to use two elevators to get to the rest of our party. The computers/printers are free in the front lobby. We had appetizers and beer in the hotel bar at midnight. Every thing was extremely clean.

title: “HIDIOUS.”
text: Smells like Cigarette smoke and bug spray. This is a flea bag motel. If you are looking for a quaint and comfortable hotel... LOOK ELSEWHERE. The health department should close this place down.

title: “Want elegance and sophistication? Stay elsewhere.”
text:
My fiance and I stayed at the Palmer House Hilton the weekend of June 26th and from the moment we walked in, I regretted my choice of this hotel. We entered the lobby late Friday night and were met with loud hip-hop music being played. I actually walked around looking for the entrance to the club that I thought was off of the lobby until I realized it was being played through the house speakers! The lobby environment left a lot to be desired, I'll leave it at that.
Our room consisted of a double bed, 3 feet from the door and about 10 square feet of walking space after you account for the huge desk and dresser (which should not be in that room to account for the minimal space). Not only was the room TINY for 2 people, but it was also right off of the elevator lobby, and with the bed being 3 feet from the door, I was able to share in everyone's conversations as they exited/entered the elevator bank. The toilet that ran all night I'll chalk up to a small maintenance problem and these things just happen. 
Completely disappointed with the room, we headed down to the lobby for a drink. We watched the waiter pass us 3 times as he serviced the tables around us so my fiance walked up to the bar to get drinks himself. Paying $33 for 2 martinis (tip not included) was a little ridiculous but we figured those are downtown prices if only a bit inflated. 
If you decide to drive to the hotel, expect to pay $38/night for parking in the lot across the street from the hotel. There is no validation, this is the price the lot charges and the exact same price the hotel charges, so don't forget to include that in the room cost. We parked at the lot on Clark and Harrison the second night -walking distance and $8 for the night- after having learned our lesson and paying $32 for parking the first night, and were lucky enough to find free street parking the next day on Wabash and Jackson (beware of the "pay to park" meters that charge $4.25 for 1 hour of parking). 
Fitness center is $10 to use and don't expect anything by way of free water or anything else because everything they have to offer, they've put a price on. 
I should say that they did change our room after we complained about the noise/location/size to a normal sized room with a queen size bed and space enough for two people, but I think at that point, the damage had been done and had I been able to change hotels without penalty, I definitely would have. The location of the hotel is great because you're within walking distance to most everything and a short cab ride away to everything else, but I would NOT recommend staying here again to anyone. 
For the price (room, taxes, parking, fitness, etc), you can stay at a much nicer hotel and I highly recommend staying elsewhere.

title: “What a Rip Off”
text: For a Fairmont Hotel this is bottom of the barrel! The beds are aweful you can feel the springs poping thru when we asked the management about that they said all the beds are the same! While i was checking in...my husband had arranged for a massage for me at the Tova Day Spa, and when we tried to use the coupon the hotel gave us for the spa the next day...the Tova spa said, we can't honor that $25.00 off coupon the owner is not here. Left our name and number and Haven't heard anything! Heads up! the $210.00 massage I recieved was amatuer to say the best! I have stayed at Fairmonts and St Regis hotels and used there spa and this one was comparable to a Massage envy (massage's for $40.00). Don't waste your money. Oh Yeah and it's $26.00 a day to park your car for Hotel guest!!!!!

title: “Excellent STay - Really enjoyed and would definitely stay again”
text: I thought the hotel was great, it was very clean, the staff was attentive and very professional as well as helpful as it was my first time staying at this hotel

title: “amazing service”
text: I work for jetblue airlines and am constantly traveling we stay in a different hotel in a different city everynight, and this is one of the best locations we stay at. The staff at the hotel are exceptional, every person there is willing to go above and beyond to make you feel comfortable and at home and they all seem very genuine and sincere while helping you. Mandy one of the manager greeted us when we first got to the hotel and was incredibly friendly and apporoachable. Rooms come wtih a fridge and a microwave which is great, this hotel is deserving of the 5 star rating.

title: “Good airport hotel”
text: Easily accesible airport hotel with excellent shuttle service. Rooms are nice, warm and clean. Staff are helpful and it is a good choice.

title: “Great service, rooom needs attention”
text:
My company put on an event at the Sheraton Austin, and can say that the desk, catering and other staff were great, no issues here. The public areas and conference rooms were fine, and had not been in the hotel since it's remodel many years ago, it's nicer than I remember from my last stay.
My room, while nice sized and clean was a bit tired, wallpaper peeling from the wall in my room and there were huge cracked tiles in the shower, they'd been attempting some repair, but really the tiles need to be replaced. Can't speak to the state of the other rooms, this makes me wonder if I shouldn't go back to the Westin.
I'm afraid that I would not go out of my way to return to the Sheraton based on the maintenance level of the room. I travel a lot, and this was not up to standard.

title: “beautiful hotel,comfy beds,excellent customer service!”
text:
We just stayed at this beautiful new hotel for 10 days to visit with family and will definitely be back next year. We had two adjoining rooms for the 5 of us ( 2adults, 1 junior and 2 teens). The rooms were clean and comfy and gorgeous. What was especially pleasing was that there was so much storage space (armoire and dresser) that I unpacked everyones clothing. The bedding is what I call "pamper me bedding" , the kind you want to take home with you. The staff was friendly and professional at all times and took care of any quesion or issue that came up. We found the location of the hotel to be ideal. You are close to restaurants and shopping and not far from the beach. The hotel also has a smart board in the front lobby that you can look up and print direcions to all main attractions , eateries and shopping ( very cool! ) We used the pool and jacuzzi everyday. 
There is also an adjacent covered area that has seating for dining outdoors. We travel for both business and pleasure, this hotel is a great value with great people and amenities.

title: “It's like staying at my house, only more fun”
text: I love this hotel. I've stayed here twice, and will again the next time I stay in the city. It is comfortable, safe, tastefully decorated, has up-to-date amenities and is in a good location. A coworker found this place for me, so we could carpool on our way to work in south Chicago (she stays with friends in Wrigleyville). It looked like a nice place on the website, and the price was right - under $100 for a weeknight room. There's parking onsite, but I didn't use it. The area (Belmont & Clark Streets) has plenty of restaurants, shops, coffee shops, there are a few drugstores, and I saw a health food store around the corner. When I checked in, I was pleasantly surprised by the professionalism and courtesy of the gentlemen working the desk, and the comfy seating near the fire. My room was on the 3rd floor, a queen suite with the bed in an adjoining room. The room was charming and comfortable, nicely decorated and well-equipped. It was like a tiny apartment, and I loved it. In the bathroom, they use Gilchrist & Soames Essentiel Elements lavender-scented products. The bed was very comfortable, with plenty of pillows and a soft blanket at the bottom of the bed. Downstairs, they provide coffee and hot water for tea or cocoa, and serve a continental breakfast in the morning. I definitely recommend this hotel, though you should be aware of the possibility of noise from the L station next door.

title: “Sir Francis Drake stay”
text: We had a excellent stay. After the first night concerns, the staff dealt with our issue quickly and it was great. If you have a longer stay, which ours was six days, it would be nice to have a fridge in the room. Also, one comment, hopefully you can get along with your neighbour, as the walls are very thin and you can hear EVERYTHING, without any effort. The hotel is equipped with Wi-Fi at a cost, would be nice if it was cheaper or even free. It is a very beautiful hotel.

title: “Not a clean room and staff walked unannounced to a very unprivate room!”
text: If you don't mind tiny, I mean seriously tiny, bed touching the door tiny, having to clean up previous guest hair balls, staff walking in unannounced, no privacy in room, bad elevator smells and loud music, unfriendly staff, hmm what else can I stay, then this is the place for you. Not a good NY value. Spend the same amount and stay somewhere nice! Oh and I've slept on more comfortable mats in a tent in the wilderness.

title: “Sparkling Clean/Gracious Staff”
text: Our room was sparkling clean right down to the fresh bed covers/duvet. Breakfast is included and was very nice. The breakfast service staff worked very hard to keep everything stocked and replenished. A note about the valet parking - I have read the complaints. Baltimore is a city. It costs money to park in a city. Get over it. The valet guys work so hard to make their customer happy. Also a great feature is after check out you can leave your luggage with them in a locked room, them pick up your luggage and car at 5pm. If you want to stay later you just pay a small additional fee for the extra time. I was really impressed with the valet gentlemen! Thanks guys!

title: “Excellent Place to Stay!!”
text: My husband and I LOVED this place. We actually were driving around looking for hotels to stay at and came about this one. We've stayed at quite a few hotels in Dallas, and I'd have to stay I'd highly recommend this one over the rest. It offers the amenities you find at home allowing you to travel light. It comes equipped with laundry facilities and a gym, but even better, a dishwasher! I have yet to see any of the suite-like hotels I've stayed in come with a dishwasher. Needless to say, I was pretty estatic to see this - we are traveling at the moment with our baby, who needs bottles washed constantly, and it made things so much easier during our stay. On top of that, there is everything you need to cook with, which has only been offered to us in a personal condo we rented at one point. Maybe we're more used to the standard hotel, but our preference just changed, and for the price, this far outdoes the others! The personnel was friendly, and they have a tiny store for snacks (as well as microwaveable items, ice cream, etc) - really nice to have if you want to stay in for the night or forgot to get something before coming back to the hotel after a long day. We walked by a room where someone was actually cooking french toast in the morning - very nice to walk past! This was such a different experience than those you walk by and only smell something horrific coming from someone's room. Anyway - all in all, we would highly recommend.

title: “great stay at California Suites Hotel”
text:
We stayed at California Suites Hotel for 9 nights. We are very pleased about our stay there. The room was very clean and at night it was quiet! They have also a friendly staff and a large parking area. I Can recommand to anyone. We will come back someday. 
Au revoir et beaucoup de succes:-)

title: “Great Location Near CIty Hall, Historic Building”
text: The location is perfect for being a tourist in Philly. It's not right on top of the Liberty Bell, but it's a short walk. The Reading Terminal is nearby as is City Hall. The Building seems about 100 years old, with very tall ceilings, making big rooms feel even bigger. The downside for such a good location is that parking is expensive, I thought, valet was 38/day plus tax and tip. Can't have it both ways, I guess. Lobby is small, "shop" is smaller. The bedroom was very large with a king bed a desk, chaise with ottoman, and another setee. The bathroom had a very large shower/toilet room; but the sink area was too small, with insufficient counter space. Personally, I would have traded the in-room coffee maker for more space, but that's just me.

title: “Convenient, great place, great price”
text: Needed to stay downtown for business meetings, and found Club Quarters (usually a member-only hotel) available online at a great price. While the room was a little smaller than others I've had downtown, the location was great, the room was clean, quiet and in pristine shape, and the bar downstairs was very friendly and convenient. Great place to stay.

title: “Excellent Midtown Hotel”
text:
My wife, child and I stayed at the Belevedere for 6 nights on our first trip to the Big Apple. It was a wonderful place to go after wearing ourselves out sightseeing. The location was fantastic, as we could return easily for an hour or two of rest before heading out again. Near subways (we took the A train from JFK and back), Broadway theaters, Times Square, and Central Park. 
One of the best features was the kitchenette, which consisted of a mini-fridge and a microwave. Not a gourmet kitchen, but plenty to store cold beverages and left-overs. This feature saved us quite a few dollars in wasted food.
Next time we visit NYC, we'll try to stay there again.

title: “Great experience and they really do take care of you”
text:
Alright, I've been reading reviews on TripAdvisor for quite some time now and have
never written a review myself simply because i never deemed it necessary. Not in my interest you might say.But I really must show my appreciation of how much of a find the Chancellor Hotel is if you really want to have a good time in SF for a budget price yet still have a comfortable room and good service.
Now i'm a fairly young guy- mid twenties, but I'm pretty picky. After booking the hotel I was expecting a good location, clean and efficient rooms and a decent bathroom, not much else. But after staying there this past weekend with my girlfriend, I was really impressed on how much they've kept their standards high. We had a romantic time, even had a view, and the room has EVERYTHING you need. Safe, extra towels, extra covers, MP3 player, etc. . .
The rooms aren't huge, but they aren't tiny either. European is a good word for it, but the spacing is just right for two people and the beds were comfy. (I've lived in Europe for a few years so I can say that). 
Location is great, right across from Francis Drake Hotel which has a cool bar with a view in it, and right near the trams. Almost everything is accesible. Plus the staff were very helpful, even when one dude at the front desk had lost his voice completely the poor guy still strained his throat to tell me (very quietly but politely) good dinner spots on the map. Honestly, I was very impressed. And that's really not easy.
Would definetely stay there again and have recommended my picky friends to stay there aswell when they go to SF.

title: “Great experience”
text: Saying I'm not a huge fan of New York City is an understatement, but this hotel may make me change my mind. The front desk staff took great care of us and gave us an upgrade to a suite when our reserved room was still occupied. The location is wonderful - across from the park and right on the subway line. Rooms are modern and clean. I'll stay here again.

title: “Breathtaking location with above average service”
text: The Rancho Bernardo Inn is tucked away in the foothills about 15 miles north of San Diego proper- far enough away to feel like you are on vacation. The layout is very well done, making it feel as if you are staying in a much more intimate property. Food and beverage service was above average, and the staff seem very happy and committed. The grounds could use a little more upkeep and my room in particular was quite dated- but the view and landscaping were outstanding.

title: “Easter vacation at the PERFECT family hotel"”
text: Beautiful view, pools were hopping from sun up til sun down - but that was fine for us, meeting our 3 adult children here for a long Easter weekend. LOTS of activities for kids, really FUN to watch the watermelon eating contest and the under water egg hunt! Fantastic weather! Had Sunday brunch at the Red Marlin - could NOT beat the food and the views of the harbor. Staff were wonderful and so accommodating. Came pool side several times to see if everyone was having a good time, and we WERE! We'll be back!

title: “charming, central, woudl stay again”
text: My husband and I stayed here for 3 nights in November and loved the loaction. You pay and arm and a leg to stay downtown Boston so this was a rgeat option for us. I went in with trepidation but was plesantly surprised. Rooms were small and showed their age. Ours was clean however and the location made up for the room size. We did not spend much time in the hotel - only to sleep. There are theatres, lots of restaurants and pubs so close by. Beacon Hill, shopping, Commons, etc. We walked to Quincy Market- took about 20 minutes. I would definitely recommend this hotel but do not expect 5 star. Expect a 2 star and you should not be dissapointed.

title: “Worse than any creepy motel”
text:
We waited an hour (!!) outside with the suitcases at night until they found our reservation- not that they made such an effort to begin with nor have computers... only to get a room with sheets that haven't been replaced for god knows how long- it had hair all over it. The garbage was full. the room and bathroom were filthy and in a terrible condition (broken tiles, etc). No one cleaned the room during our stay. Terrible service - there was just no one to talk to.. I don't even think they spoke English.
JUST STAY AWAY FOR YOUR OWN SAKE

title: “For Starwood Status maintainance only”
text: We stayed one night on our way home to help maintain Starwood status. The property is relatively old and has been updated. The designer did not consider functionality in the update. There was minimal lighting in the room and bathroom making it hard to apply make up. We had to put suitcases under the few recessed lights in the room to see at all. There is no lighting to turn off at the bedside or reading lights. The bed is in the middle of the room with sharp corners on the frame--I banged my shin. The rooms still have the feel of an old hotel. The pool area is very nice and the lunch menu was good and tasty. The property is not very centrally located to the main shopping area of Beverly Hills but there is a complimentary drop off service and Danny the driver was very pleasant.

title: “Great place to stay if visiting Universal Studios and LA”
text:
Great locaton for couples and especially families. Pool with bar and BBQ make for happy family fun.
Very close to Universal Studios and a free shuttle bus to and from this venue allowed easy, cheap and stress free access to Universal Studios.
Room comfortable but could hear the noise from freeway traffic which made for a disturbed sleep. Would recomend double glazed windows to remove the traffic noise. Other than that the venue is exceptional. 
The restaurant on location is very good and service exceptional.

title: “Simply fantastic service, customer interactions and staff friendliness”
text:
I have been a road warrior for 20 years, staying at least 100 nights a year in 4 star hotels. I am pretty jaded about travel in general and it takes something major for me to raise an eyebrow. I spent a week here, having been at other W hotels before, so I kind of knew what to expect, but I was very surprised in a positive way. If you don't know about W Hotels, they have a strong hipster, eurocool vibe/decor, with "house music" pumping in the lobby and elevators at all hours. Granted, I am a bit too old for the hipster clubbing type scene, but it is kind of neat to stay at a hotel that isn't your standard look-feel hotel. But it isn't the bricks and mortar that motivated me to write this. Instead, EVERY single staff member I had contact with was happy, friendly and genuine. The front desk staff were great and absolutely NOT condescending as they sometimes can be at upper end hotels. The wait staff bent over backwards to respond to requests - and did so with HUGE smiles and happy banter. Even one of the maintenance guys I ran into in the lobby men's room called me by name (I guess he saw my nametag) and asked how I was doing. Overall, I was so impressed with the staff I sent an email to the W CEO and the property GM (with whom I had already chatted during my stay) complimenting them on their friendliness and customer service.
I can't recommend the W San Diego highly enough.

title: “Thumbs Up for Comfort!”
text: Stayed here 2 nights recently. Best thing was the comfortable bed! We had an inside (away from street) room which was very quiet at night. Place is well decorated, but here and there in our room was some chipped paint, but is expected for an older building. All amenities we needed were here, so would recommend. Only 2 blocks from BART, easy 30 minute ride to SFO.

title: “Fab stay at the Westin Riverwalk”
text: We just came back from our quick weekend wedding trip to San Antonio. The Westin Riverwalk was a wonderful homebase - excellent location, impeccably appointed lobby/rooms and great service. Basically, everything I expect from a Westin. Steven at the front desk made us feel welcomed and took care of all the logistics.

title: “Can not complain good value for money”
text:
We had this hotel as the start of 3 weeks touring the USA. I upgraded the room to overlook lake michigin. The staff were really friendly and the room was clean and quiet. When we arrived at the hotel the staff advised us on what to see and could not do enough to accomodate us. When we told them what time our flight was out of O'hare they advised us and helped us out with our travel arragements to ensure we made it on time.
Although it is not quite in the centre of chicago it is only 10 minutes to walk in and it always felt really safe around the hotel. I will definatly stay there again.

title: “My GABF week staying at the Ramada”
text:
Sure our room key never worked and getting home between 12 and 2am meant we attempted to insert and remove the key about a dozen times before begrudgingly waiting for the elevator for 3-5 minutes to come to our floor (just take the stairs - you're in Denver, you could use the exercise), just to take us to the front desk so they could give us another key that would only work once. But honestly, the amount of money I paid for this room for a week, a very expensive week mind you (GABF stole all my money, with my direct permission of course), made me exceedingly happy considering how understaffed yet pleasant the hotel staff was. My roommate for the week was able to take the shuttle to and from downtown all week while I was working my life away drinking beer for a minimum of 12 hours a day. 
The location is just outside the hustle and bustle of downtown, which is actually nice, because at night, once you're done festing, all you want to do is a.) drunk-snack or b.) sleep. I had the best (vacation) sleep of my life at this hotel - no distractions (besides the dinging of the elevator at all hours of the night; our room was right next to it), no fancy linens or towels or mints on the pillows. This is a 'I need a good place to sleep shower and... well the other s- thing you do in your hotel room.' The drive to downtown during the weekday morning traffic took about 10-15 minutes tops, on the weekend, I can't really remember how long it took, but it was definitely less. 
I wouldn't recommend the restaurant mostly because I was terrified to go in there, we never ate the complimentary breakfast because there are far better options downtown. 
Our original room was on the 4th floor, but the 4th floor is half smoking and half non-smoking rooms - which means, most rooms on the 4th floor probably reek of cigarettes; I instantly requested a new room and within minutes the blonde front desk girl came upstairs and delivered new room keys to us herself. Our new room, didn't smell. It was awesome. My nose is terribly sensitive to cigarette smoke, so maybe if you aren't as sensitive the 4th floor won't bother you. 
The night club is obnoxious. I think Thursday-Saturday night it was blasting hip hop or hispanic music; I was too tired to notice. Fortunately, on the 3rd floor, I couldn't hear the music at all, but I'd imagine if your room was on the 1st or 2nd floor you'd have a different experience.
When I return to Denver, there's a good chance I'd pick this hotel again.

title: “Basic but good value”
text:
The best thing about this hotel is the location - in soho. Given its a 3 star, as long as you are not expecting boutique, it's good soho value. 
 Staff were wonderfully friendly and helpful. Visitors from outside the US might find the breakfast on disposable utensils a litte strange, but at least these are now biodegradable. Breakfast is free, however, I couldn't stomach the rubbery caged-chicken eggs (were they eggs?) and spent some of the money saved on the room on organic egg breakfasts a block away at Sanctuary T's. For espresso try "Everyman Espresso", also on west broadway.
Bottom line: Basic, but good value.

title: “spacious clean convenient hotel”
text:
I was in NYC for Thanksgiving Week with my d-i-l and granddaughter, we rode the train from the deep south, got off at Penn Station which is right across the street from the Affinia Manhattan. This turned out to be a very happy accident on my part. The location of the hotel is central to all sights to behold in Manhattan. The subway is just around the corner. We took the subway every where, so fast and easy. We arrived at 11 in the morning, check in time was 3 or 4 pm but our room was available so we could take our baggage up, regroup for our plan of the day! That was wonderful. Our room was very roomy, had two double beds, a huge bathroom (handicap accessible is the reason I think.) A little kitchenette where we boiled water for tea and used the fridge for water. Nice to have the counter top to put stuff on... It is an older hotel that has been revamped...loved the beautiful details from the original building, cast bronze or brass elevator doors, the wide halls... Our concierge was very friendly and helpful...all the staff were friendly and helpful. they put up a gorgeous Christmas tree.
 These are the downsides which are and were not that big a deal to us. I would stay there again if I can get the good price I had that week. We were in one of the "newly" renovated rooms. There is a big wardrobe/dresser/desk cabinet in the room...not much closet space for a double room. The desk top was sprung and flopped unless the desk drawer underneath was open. There is an escaltor in the lobby but it just goes one way which was hard for my arthritic knees...still these are minor draw backs, some folks would not even notice the escalator or closet issue. Several Starbucks across the street and many place to eat breakfast or get deli foods. Yes, you hear city noises, I always travel with ear plugs so I slept well in the comfy bed and linens. nice!

title: “First and last time !”
text:
Just returned from a 3 night stay at the Raddison. My husband and I were here with our son and his partner. Although the holiday was booked at the same time our room was what the young lady on reception called " Petite " and our son was in a much larger room. Our son,s room faced the front of the hotel. We had a fantastic view of a huge fan that kicked in twice an hour. This although not really acceptable was much better than when the nightclub was in full force on Saturday night !!!!! I truly felt that i was actually in the nightclub itself, pity the music playing wasn,t really to my taste.
We didn,t bother complaining as we felt we were only there for a few days. People who wish to book this hotel if you are in a room similar to ours complain before unpacking and for your sake and sanity MOVE ROOMS.
A plus point it was in a good location. Good Italian a minutes walk away. Also go to Cafe Metro for breakfast, fantastic value for money.
Would I go to New York again too right but no way would I stay at the Raddison.

title: “Great place to stay on business”
text:
Stayed here for a business trip from 7/9-12/2012. Check-in was a breeze, staff were very friendly and helpful, gym had all the cardio and free weights I needed, room was spacious and comfy. Sales manager even had a welcome treat waiting for me in my room! Unheard of in this price range... 
The evening reception is great. Virgilio and Daniel at the bar were great. Hugo was great help too. 
The hotel is on Stemmons Freeway so if you don't have a car, downtown can seem close, but be oh so far. That was not an issue with me. Dallas, alas, is a driving city as public transport is not that great anyway. 
I will definitely be staying here next time I'm in Big D for business! 
Ivan C, San Francisco, CA

title: “Hotel Hollywood - so disappointed”
text: Sitting at hotel on our last day here. No facilities - bar or restaurant for evening meal although stated on line. When mentioned to reception the attitude was disgusting - told manager wouldn't see us but to post our comments on Tripadviser and we would be answered there! Hotel isn't within walking distance of any decent places to get food. The trip up Vermont Avenue is intimidating with many homeless people asking for food/money. Having travelled to America for several years and thoroughly enjoying it this is the worst experience we have encountered. Was so disappointed by the way our points were dealt with.

title: “Good hotel!”
text:
I've just come back from staying 2 nights at the Da Vinci with my boyfriend. It was the only place i could find for a decent price (which actually concerned me ) and based on the reviews I decided to try it out.
My boyfriend, who was a first-timer to NYC, did not think it was such a great deal, but I myself have visited several hotels in the city, and I think it's a really good deal!
The rooms are just big enough, and the bathroom was pretty spacious. There's a full length mirror which is rare in such hotels, and refrigerator which is nice to have.
Don''t expect any marble in the bathroom, and we did have some cold water sometimes in the middle of the shower which was annoying, but really for this price..what can you expect?!
Downside was window faced into a smelly alley, and we could not leave the window open. There was an A/C which could not be set to any temperature but the original FREEZING one. We complained about this and immediately they came to turn it down, later making our room too hot...luckily, the weather was good so it was ok for us. I thought it was nice they had at least responded to our requests.
The staff was nice also, and breakfast was small but yummy.
We did have to leave our stuff in the lobby, because they don't have a storage room, but it was fine and felt safe to me (very small hotel).
The location is just EXCELLENT, between times square and central Park.
I definitely recommend it as a great budget hotel!

title: “sleep rough instead!!!”
text: This inn is without doubt one of the worst places i have ever stayed in.... Not only is it dirty an unkempt but it is the place to stay if your rowdy noisy and a bit of a tosser with drink on you... the night porter sleeps in a chair in the lobby (classy), And the stairs look like they are a garbage shoot.. all in all the rooms are dirty, the staff are lacklustre, and were it not for the location it would have closed a long time ago. to save money, sleep rough instead

title: “Nice location”
text:
Hotel itself is very good, but there is no public wifi in the room or at the lobby.
I checked in around 11am, and they wanted to put me in the lower floor room. I was quiet upset due to the main reason I picked this hotel was for their view at upper level. I spent sometime at the front desk to communicate with them, and fortunately I got a room on the 31st floor facing 911 Memorial park. View was amazing,... :)
This single King bedroom was very spacy, but the AC makes funny noise from time to time.

title: “Good news, bad news”
text:
My feelings about my recent four day stay at this motel are best expressed as good news and bad news:
Good News: It is conveniently located about a mile from the airport and close to major freeways. Several restaurants and a Starbucks are 50 feet from the hotel entrance. 
Bad News: It took two days to figure out how to access it the motel, either by making U turns on a major street or wending my way through an office park. I got lost several times.
Good News: The staff is very friendly.
Bad News: The staff's competency is questionable. Twice they gave me the wrong number of days on my keycard, resulting in lockouts and a long hike to the office. Their directions about how to get on rte 87 going south sent me north on 101 toward San Francisco.
Good News: The bathroom, although small, was spotless and well equipped.
Bad News: While the sink had hot water, the shower water could not be coaxed to even body temperature. Showering meant a 'dash and splash' of the kind I have not done since boy scout camp.
Good News: The TV was good-sized and had many channels.
Bad News: The analog format could not be altered and made everyone look like Chris Christie.
For the price, this was not a bad place to stay, but be aware of potential surprise shortcomings.

title: “Fantastic hotel in excellent times square location”
text:
Stayed five nights at the Crowne Plaza Times Square. Fantastic location in which you walk directly onto times square (opposite the M&Ms store and next to Hershey's store) making it close to all amenities. Fantastic service from the hotel with the option to leave your luggage with the hotel until your check in time and after you have checked out until your flight. 
Stayed on the 42nd floor which had fantastic views with no noise from times square below. Fantastic spacious room. Would stay here again when next visiting New York.

title: “Repeat visit”
text: This was our second time staying at StayBridge Times Square and I am happy to report that nothing has changed! The hotel is exceptional - we had a studio with 2 beds which was plenty large enough for my daughter and me. The hotel was very clean, the complimentary breakfast was great and includes hot items. The staff are the extremely professional and oh so friendly - especially Brian, Jamie and Eddie. If we return to NYC again, we wouldn't consider staying anywhere else.

title: “Hotel was great. Service needs improvement.”
text:
We arrived at 4:15, check in is 3 pm. We were told the rooms weren't cleaned yet. That we had to wait up to an hour. We had to be at a wedding at 6 and needed the room. After much deliberation with staff he upgraded us to get us into a room. 
Valet brought our car around but never told us when we asked for it that it would be in front. We saw many cars being brouht to the covered area and we waited there. 
We just made the wedding with minutes to spare. 
My daughters room suddenly had a sewer smell fill the 
room. She was disturbed the next morning at 9 for room
 service for a total of three times. She finally got angry 
and ugly towards the staff before she was left in peace. 
Breakfast was lacking as well. Milk was not cold, no butter for pancakes. I think overall holiday inn would serve a better breakfast. 
Most guest seemed satisfied so I think it was just our turn to have a not so great experience.

title: “Nice hotel, good location”
text: Only stayed for one night. The welcome was good and the staff very helpful. The room was clean and very well presented. The location is great right next to Penn station so great for the LIRR straight from JFK and or accessing the subway system. The hotel has lots of history from when it was the largest hotel in New York in the 1920's, 1930's and famous for the people that stayed there. It was closed in the 60's but refurbished in the 1990's.Don't bother with the adjoining dinner to the hotel, food was not great and expensive for what it was. there are plenty of other places near by with better food.

title: “Great Location, Poor Housekeeping”
text:
The Admiral Fell Inn has a wonderful location and the decor is very charming. However, it begins to lose some of the charm due to poor housekeeping. I have stayed at this hotel twice this month and both times the room has not be thoroughly cleaned. Both times there was hair on the bathroom walls and in the shower. Candy wrappers are on the floor providing proof that the room had not been vacumed properly, if at all. On the first visit used linens were left in the room. 
It's a nice place to stay for convenience to local entertainment and restaurants they just need to get a better housekeeping staff.

title: “This really is all about location”
text:
The title says it all - what a great place to stay if you want to be near the centre of things.
We were on the first BA flight of the day from Heathrow so checked in early - about 1pm with no delay at all. Great service from receptionist and we were given access to Concierge Lounge on 46th floor for comp. breakfast as I am a Priority Club Platinum member - very welcome.
Room on 35th floor with a limited view of Times Square but great city-scape right out to the Hudson river. Bed probably the most comfortable I have ever slept in (which says a lot as I use hotels 2/3 nights per week). Very good sized room for NYC with all usual facilities.
Drinks may seem a little expensive but it is a Crowne Plaza right on Times Square - plently of choice around if you want something more reasonable. I can't comment on food, other than breakfast which was great, as we ate elsewhere but the menu looked ok.
Would I stay there again - without a doubt.
My top tips for your trip - great lunchtime sandwiches at Emmet O' Lunneys Irish Pub and Restaurant on West 51st - two mins away from hotel or at The Playwright (Celtic Pub) Bar and Restaurant on West 50th - only one min away. Sightseeing trip with Citysights NY very good - book the 2 day 'All Loops' trip to get the chance to see Upper Manhattan and Brooklyn as well as the usual downtown sights and they will also give you some discount vouchers and tickets for museums and a harbour cruise.
Have a great time.

title: “Highly Disappointed”
text: When booking this room it was nearly impossible to get a clear description or picture of the room you were signing up for. We booked a King Club Suite under the assumption it would be bigger than a standard room. We were WRONG. The room was one of the smallest I've ever stayed in, and the quality (aside from the very comfortable bed) was not great. For the amount of money paid for the "suite", it should have offered more. Although the service was good, the overall hotel room was a disappointment to say the least. I will not be staying at this hotel in the future, and warn anybody staying in the Denver Metro Area to stay away. You can find much nicer rooms for less money. I guess you're just paying for the name. I'll pass.

title: “Nice little place”
text: I was surprisingly thrilled with this place. It was immaculate with brand new furniture, a microwave and a fridge in a huge room. The bathroom was large and the shower was fabulous. The air conditioning was quiet and worked well. The manager was very friendly and helpful and the pool was well maintained. I was really surprised by how nice it was as the reviews I read were a little discouraging, but it was nice. The neighborhood left something to be desired, but the people were polite and friendly. I was by myself and was not afraid to go out alone at all. The very best thing was the transportation system. I didn't rent a car so I took the train everywhere. The station was a block from the hotel and the bus line ran by it. The train or Metro was easy to ride, cheap ( ride all day with a metro pass for 5.00) and the trains came every 10 minutes so standing alone in the station wasn't too intimidating. There was a walgreens, a McDonald's and a market one block down. I highly recommend it and would go back in a new york minute.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
Great reception staff and location. Bed was too soft.... Shower needs a curtain. 
 Room was clean and being on the 5th floor, it was very quiet. Took advantage of pass to 12th Street Gym - great facility. 
Hotel is definitely a repeat destination.

title: “Perfect for brief business trip”
text: Excellent value for the two nights I was in Dallas for training. The location was also perfect as I was only 3 miles away from the hospital where I was working. I scored a nice bargain through AAA for a king bed/sofa bed room which was plenty roomy enough for little ol' me. The sofa was a little worn but the room was clean and also had a microwave and fridge. The bathroom was the newest part as the tub and sink were all marble. I didn't use the pool so I can't comment on that, but I was pleasantly surprised at the fast wi-fi internet. The breakfast was slightly better than a continental one, but at least I got to fill up on eggs, sausages and toast before starting a long day. Staff were excellent as my card stopped working on the second day and they were very kind. Would stay here again.

title: “Nice hotel in good location”
text:
Enjoyed a two night stay at the Amalfi in early August with family members. We arrived quite early and although not able to check into a room yet, we were able to store our luggage until we we returned later. The hotel called us when the room was ready. Slight hiccup with the reservation as our confirmation showed a much lower price than what was showing on the computer, however that was corrected to show what was on our reservation confirmation (so make sure that you bring your confirmation with you!). 
The red line EL and the museum campus bus are only about a 5 minute walk from the hotel and are very convenient. We walked to Willis Tower and Navy Pier and both took about 20-25 minutes or so. On the walk to Navy Pier you cross over Michigan Avenue for some fantastic shopping on the magnificient mile! It is about a 10 minute walk to the Hard Rock Cafe and about a 5 minute walk to the Chicago Riverwalk. House of Blues is about a 1 minute walk from the hotel. There are a ton of restaurants, pharmacies, bars, starbucks and cafes all around. Harry Carry's is right across the street.
Cabs are plentiful, though pricey, and a welcome relief for a ride back to the hotel! Taxi from O'Hare to Amalfi was $45, from Museum of Science and Industry to Amalfi was $20 and from Hancock Observatory to Amalfi was $12. We bought 3 day passes for the CTA for $14 and used that to get around town as well. The pass was well worth it and can be used on the EL and on the busses.
Lou Malnati's pizza delivers to the Amalfi and eliminated an hour or more wait at their restaruant. Order early and request a set delivery time. They do not include any silverware or plates, so ask for paper products if you need it. We requested some plastic forks from the hotel and they were too busy to bring us any and would not let us come down to the front desk to pick them up ourselves!
The hotel breakfast had a great variety and was convenient being right on your floor. It is set up by the elevator and served coffee, tea, juices, bagels, donuts, breads, cereal, whole fruit, yogurt and string cheese. Being able to get your breakfast and bring back to your room was so nice. 
The room was clean and contained the usual hotel stuff, including the $8 bottle of water! At least they marked the bottle with the price. There was a refrigerator/mini bar (that took a key) in the room but we did not open it for fear of being charged for something that we did not take, but may have moved or looked at. The hotel has computers and printers so that you can check on your flight and print out your boarding pass. Three of us had iPhones and we had no issues with the internet connection or speed. Newspapers are available in the lobby. Ask at the desk for maps and they will give you a ton of maps of the area and brochures on things to do in Chicago. 
The bellman/doorman was super friendly and so helpful. He really made the stay at the hotel a great one. I would stay here again.

title: “Great location - friendly staff”
text: We stayed four nights with our three teenage children who are serious shoppers. This hotel is in the perfect location just off 5th Ave, close to all the big stores and theatres nearby. The rooms are comfortable and of good size. We found the staff at the concierge desk very helpful. Their dinning suggestions were spot on. Avoid breakfast at the hotel which is expensive. There are other local places to get breakfast (burger heaven and the Europa Cafe 2 blocks up Madison were good). We would return.

title: “Wonderful, near the Metro, near the White House”
text: I stayed here for business, but loved the hotel. The room was great, as was the service. The hotel bar/restaurant was very good, including a wonderful cook-to-order breakfast. It is right across the street from the McPherson Square Metro, so everything's in walking distance. The staff, especially in the restaurant, were all very helpful and friendly.

title: “Great location on the bay”
text: Large hotel -- excellent location, excellent spa, but pricey if you just want to use the gym. Didn't eat at the restaurants, but the conference catering was well done.

title: “Great value, good rooms”
text:
This was our first visit to Seattle. We chose this hotel based on the on the Trip Advisor reviews and were very pleased we did. The reception area is spacious and smart, the check in was quick and we were pleased to reach our room after a long flight. The size and quality of the room was a pleasant surprise, good size bedroom with bright and stylish decoration & spacious bathroom with walk in shower. Particularly liked that there's a vinyl floor covering in the bedroom, felt so much cleaner than carpet. For the price we thought it very good value. 
There is no restaurant but there's a coffee & cake kiosk in the lobby
The location is quiet and although its located away from downtown we found it very easy to find our way to the Seattle attractions. The hotel offer a courtesy car, can order you a taxi or its not far to the Space Needle monorail station.

title: “Great 3 days”
text: The Doubletree's have been hit and miss in my opinion but this was a terrific stay and a tremendous downown area. I'm a big sports fan and you get all of the ESPN stations and Fox sports. The fitness room is 5 star but unfortunately no swimming pool for the kids. You are in walking distance of restaurants. My suggestion would be shuttle from the airport, because of the $28 per night vallet charge. It's $12 if you park your own car. Denver also has FREE transportation downtown.

title: “Outstanding Hotel”
text: My husband, daughter and I stayed at the Casablanca for 3 nights in November --we were spending a long weekend in NYC to celebrate my birthday. I reserved a mini-suite at the Casablanca based on the trip advisor reviews. The room rate was pricey but when you consider the daily free happy hour, free breakfast and wi-fi, I thought it was competitively priced with other good NYC hotels. What distinguished Casablanca was the level of service which was outstanding. Everyone we met was so friendly and helpful and the hotel really is a gem. I would recommend it to anyone who values service and a great overall experience. I was sad to leave.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
We stayed three nights at the W. It was located perfectly for our visit to UCLA. The unique location was in a residential area immediately adjacent to lively Westwood Village and close to the bustle of Wilshire Boulevard. I loved the "walkability" of it. The rooms and common areas were artistically designed with deco/modern style furnishings but they accomplished a warm, welcoming feel that many such decors do not. The room, a small suite, was spacious, comfortable and highly functional as living quarters away from home. One surprising omission was that there was not coffee/tea service available in the room.
The pool area was lovely and lively. Workout facilities were good. We did not sample the restaurants. Will definitely stay here again.

title: “Fantastic!”
text:
I had the opportunity to stay at the W Lakeshore and I really had a great time. I love the W Brand and it certainly is not lacking W style. Registration was fast, easy, and courteous. Amy was great and gave me a great rundown of the hotel. The Spectacular room facing Lake Michigan was...well, spectacular. I loved the view and the sunrise each morning was lovely. The room was well appointed and spacious. I loved the large chaise lounge by the window, and of course the signature W bed.
Locationwise, it's easy to get around from this W, it's right on Lake Shore Drive, and about 6 blocks east of Michigan Ave, and a short taxi ride or adventurous walk to other destinations. If you don't feel like walking or a taxi, they have the complimentary Acura house car service available from 12pm-8pm to take you in style to anywhere within 5 miles (dropoff only) but be sure to make a reservation. Being from Chicago, I walked most places since I knew where I was going, but having extra options is always a great thing and definitely works well if you're new to the city.
The Living Room was fun and hip with a lot of people, even on a Tuesday night. It was definitely the place to see and be seen and there was a lot of good conversation with the bartenders and other guests. Brodie and another young lady were fantastic bartenders and a pleasure to speak with. The cocktail, wine and beer lists were great, and specialty cocktails were innovative and unique. I personally enjoyed the Gin Right. The 33rd floor Whiskey Sky was small and intimate with a good view of the city. Definitely go up there if you have time.
Reuben from Engineering was really helpful when my TV remote wasn't working, and Lakeshia from the W Store is a gem and was phenominal in assisting me with my purchase. Renee from Whatever/Whenever was nice and accomodating and Luis from In Room Dining was made the experience personalized which I enjoyed. Ashley at checkout was helpful and courteous and informative. 
All the people I mentioned (and the ones i forgot to) were amazing at what they do. The service was impeccable and I'd go as far to say that is was the best of any W I've ever been to. Thank you for a memorable and personalized W experience.
tl;dr (too long; didn't read) : great room, great service, great drinks, great time, go there.

title: “Historic Hotel”
text:
We stayed in the Custom House for three nights. We are 2 adults and 2 children. I asked for a high floor and we got it - right under the clock face. While the windows were small compared to the lower floors- there were only 2 suites on our floor as the floor plate is smaller at this level. The views stretched from a partial harbour view, North End/Charlestown, Cambridge, partial dowtown, government centre-so the views were good.
Overall the suite was small in size (but this is dictated by the floor plate and has to be expected given that this is a clock tower). When the sofa bed was pulled out there was little room to move about, mainly due to too many occasional tables in the living/dining/kitchen area. I had originally requested a rollaway bed (since the girls don't like sharing) but once I saw the size of the room I had to cancel it - it just wouldn't have fitted in. 
Our room had a king size bed - which left little room for anything else, as this room was small as well. I am generally very fussy about matresses and I can say this one was fine - very firm. 
The bathroom was off a lobby between both rooms. With four people travelling there was no space for all our bathroom stuff. A shelf over the wash basin would have been good for all that stuff. The extract did not work in the bathroom so one got a foggy mirror. 
We are very concious about the background noise of air conditioning at night. It was quite noisy and kept switching on/off throughout the night. Another issue was the supply grilles were directly over the sofa bed - so one daughter was cold and we had to request extra blankets for the sofa bed. 
The observation deck was very interesting as it is external and runs around all sides of the building. Also interesting was the rotunda lobby (with domed ceiling) and upper level (which was part of the original Custom House). The lower floors were all part of the original Custom House and the tower section was an addition about a century ago. 
There is a laundry in part of the games room which would be very useful for those staying for a longer period or those travelling with small kids.
The kitchen was stocked with washing liquid, laundry powder and coffee. There was no stove - just a microwave and a undercounter fridge.
As others have mentioned the location is very handy for transportation (three lines are close by), food and shopping. We stayed over a weekend so many of the breakfast places were closed since they mainly serve the downtown office community. However there is a Starbucks just up the street on State.
The staff were very helpful and friendly, expecially the guys who take care of valet/bags/doors. 
I choose this hotel because it was a hotel in an unusual architectural structure (not just an historic hotel- which can mean outdated facilities) and I wasn't disappointed. Expect an adapted reuse of the spaces and you won't be dissapointed.

title: “A Picture Perfect Wedding!”
text:
I recently had my wedding at Barton Creek Resort...and this small white review box isn't large enough for me to express what an amazing experience I had!!! Originally, my fiance and I had a difficult time trying to decide where we wanted our reception to be held. When Kristin Arntson (Dir. of Catering) personally followed up with us a week after our visit, she assured me that me that having my wedding at Barton Creek would be the best decision I could make. She was definitely right!! Her guidance and assistance throughout the whole process was priceless. I trusted her opinions and never felt as if she was trying to "sell" me any additional services that BCR offered. With all of the amenities, dining, and amazing hill country views that the resort had to offer, I began to feel like I was having a destination wedding just 20 minutes away from where I live! 
When the day of the wedding came, Kristin assured my mother and I that we didnt have to worry about a thing. She took care of all the set-up and organization so that we could just enjoy the day. The food, the service, and the execution of the entire event was definite perfection! My guests still rave about what a spectacular time they had the entire time at the resort. They said it was more like a weekend getaway for them...which was exactly what I wanted. Everyone spent the following day laying around the pool and golfing.
I couldn't have imagined a more perfect place to marry the most perfect man. I only wish I could've spent more time as a "spectator" rather than the busy bride! ;-)

title: “Decent room at a great price”
text:
My wife and I stayed one night at this property as part of a "Billy Bob's" Saturday night getaway to see Tanya Tucker in concert. We had spent the day at Winstar Casino in Oklahoma and needed a convenient room as we headed to Fort Worth. 
The hotel itself was right on the interstate and less than 5 miles from the Fort Worth Stockyards and Billy Bob's Honky Tonk......just what we wanted.
The room was clean and comfortable and the king bed was just fine. The only complaint we had was the bathroom. It was way too small for our liking and it appeared that the mirror had not been cleaned recently, at least not before our stay.
Overall, for the promotional price of $74.99, we thought the room was decent and the price was right.

title: “Disappointing”
text: Nice lobby & excellent quick to go breakfast available, free coffee all day long although no coffee facilities in room. Very welll located however room small & dated,very disappointing. Definately upgrade your room as you will not be too impressed. Would definately visit New York again however would stop elsewhere. Food expensive & very limited.

title: “Canterbury Stay”
text: I loved the room, it was similar to the photo displayed (but not exact, however it wasn't a diappointment). The hotel had a lavish atmosphere but the cost wasn't extravagant. I enjoyed the lobby, reminded me of a B&B I stayed at in London, UK. Was disappointed by the morning pastries but they do have a tea that is catered from a local merchant in the downtown area. The bellmen were helpful and friendly. The artwork in the lobby was enjoyable and the bellman on duty helped me to locate information on the artist displayed. I wish I had a meeting so I could use the conference room, it looked wonderful.

title: “Just as Described”
text:
We chose to stay at the Chancellor Hotel for four nights over the Mother's Day weekend, based on the positive reviews posted on this site. We were not disappointed. We asked for a quiet room, so they put us on the 11th floor. There was no traffice noise, but the walls between rooms must be paper thin or else there was a party going on in the room next door on two nights. Fortunately, they were quiet after 11pm so we had no problem sleeping.
Queen-sized bed was firm, which we like - much better than the soft beds they have put into the Marriott a few blocks away - and everything is provided in the nicely appointed bathrooms. Location just off Union Square (see picture) was excellent, with lots of good places to eat nearby. We chose places to eat from the Lonely Planet Guide, and they were all good. We particularly recommend the Thirsty Bear Brew Pub, near the convention centre, and McCormick and Kuletto's, near fisherman's wharf (great views - see picture).
Overall the Chancellor is an excellent choice for anyone wanting an above-average room without paying for the big lobbies and expensive restaurants found in the 5* hotels. But if you want a soft bed, 5* lobby/restaurants and air conditioning, stay somewhere else.

title: “It's definitely seen better days....”
text:
Once upon a time, when this was the flagship Westin (the corporate headquarters were just across the street) this was a classy, cool hotel: It had a excellent dining room, a coffee shop, two bars (one a Trader Vics!) and a full-service health club. 
Now everything about this place seems to be "on the cheap": no nice dining room, a banal "cafe" for breakfast, only one vapid bar (and that's in the lobby - very airport-ish), and a dirty workout space with no good locker facilities or even attendants.
The good thing about this hotel is the views: The guest rooms definitely have the best views in town. But the furnishings are tired and worn. 
It's OK for conventions, if you get a good rate, but it really is just a ghost of its former self.

title: “Hotel Pennsylvania in the shopping district.”
text:
As seen as above, this hotel is located in the shopping district of New York. It's a 2mins walk to Macy's, and you have three choices for taking the subway. The nearest subway is a 1min walk, and brings you to Times Square and Central Park (shops at 5th avenue). When coming from the airport, you have to take subway train "E", that will stop 3mins away from the hotel.
An exellent location!

title: “The best choice in NYC”
text:
This is the best hotel in NYC in my opinion. 
Although it is not in the Times Square area one can get there in about 15 min by taking the 6 train from 33rd/Park ave. one stop to Grand Central Station and the Times Square shuttle one stop to 7th avenue. This hotel is a few blocks from the Queens Midtown tunnel which makes for an easy arrival and return from LGA.
The Affinia Dumont has very comfortable beds and provides hypoallergenic bedding if needed. The staff is very pleasent and the door staff always welcome you back upon your return. I particulary like the fact that having a small lobby means you do not have to traverse through a crowd to get to the elevators and up to your room. I highly reccomend the Affinia Dumont

title: “My best NYC hotel experience”
text: So impressed with this hotel in every way. The subway enterance is literally beside the front door. My room was perfectly appointed, very clean &, most importantly, street noise-free (I slept til noon with no disturbances). The staff was welcoming, used my name, and were responsive to every request. Of all the places I've stayed in NYC, which is MANY, this is my favorite. Just perfect for me, not too silly-trendy, and not stuffy - just right and in a great spot, if you enjoy Tribeca and plan to use the subway.

title: “Amazing Place”
text: Took the free shuttle from LAX Airport and from the moment I arrived, I was welcomed by the many staff, at the door, in the Lobby and at the check-in desk. They remember their frequent quests and I was again Welcomed back and thanked for using the Westin LAX! My room was nice and clean! The young lady working the Westin Club Floor was so kind and friendly, she even went out of her way to get me some cranberry juice one evening. Thanks for making it my home away from home.....D.Wheaton

title: “Beautiful!”
text: Hotel Commonwealth was a wonderful experience! We spent the night with our two children and everybody had a great time. Wonderful accomodations, beautiful rooms and bath rooms. Fantastic cocktails downstairs in Eastern Standard Restaurant! Loved it!

title: “Stay AWAY!”
text:
There are protesters greeting you at the door currently at the hotel. New management laid people off and they are outside 12hrs/daily screaming at hotel guests. It is very unpleasant.
Go across the street to the Sofitel.
