I have stayed here in the past and have LOVED it. A horrific situation...not only for guests but for folks who have lost their jobs in this awful economy.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We were in New York for a wedding and some shopping. This hotel was ideally located, walking distance to most of the things that we wanted to do. 
At check-in we were given lots of choices and options for our room, and they accommodated our early check-in happily. Our room was spotless, large, and very comfortable. 
Throughout our stay we found the staff to be very helpful and pleasant. We will definitely stay here the next time we are in NYC.

title: “Too noisy for me”
text:
This is a nice location in an increasingly gentrifying neighborhood. (I was sorry to see that a little locally-owned health food store across the street was replaced by one of those "upscale edgy" clothing chains) You're about 20 minutes via CTA from Watertower, and 25-30 from Union Station, counting the time it takes to wait for the bus or train. You can eat your way around the world within 3 blocks.
I want to like this place...I've stayed here twice...but the plain fact is it's way too noisy on the street side. It's a constant rumble of buses, trucks, taxis honking, etc all through the night. Even with earplugs (thoughtfully provided right in the nightstand drawer!) I got very little sleep. The rooms off the street, overlooking the usual "courtyard" of mechanical things hidden from street view, are tiny and really only for a single.
If you're not bothered by noise, or better yet, if you're deaf, you will love this place. But light sleepers need to look elsewhere. The lack of sleep had a negative effect on my trip because I was tired all the time. I actually went to the library just to get a little quiet time...not a room you'd want to lounge in.

title: “Clean Hotel In A Perfect Location!”
text: This is a old hotel with a modern look. The hotel is very clean but the rooms are very small. The hotel is within walking distance of the Gas lamp Quarters. The parking is a little expensive $32.00 a night for Valet service. The only complaint I would have is there is no pool on site.

title: “Nice city - nice hotel”
text: The Boston Harbor Hotel is very nice. And wtih a fantastisk location in Boston. Stunning view of the harbor and to the new green areas, where the interstate highway used to be. Service is amazing and the standard is very high. A great hotel where I sure would love to come back!!

title: “Noisy and dirty”
text: This is the type of hotel that you will find great based on the story told by a series of carefully selected photos on a website. To me, this is the baddest experience as far as hotels in Manhattan. Here´s the deal: because of very poor insulation both in walls and windows, the room was noisy (able to hear the next room, not to mention the outside noise) , but also I had some much condensation in the windows meaning I was cold as well. The point is that regardless that I have this allergy problem (not hotel´s problem) and can not sleep with the air conditioning on, I could not get a good, repairing sleep because I was freezing and the noise was simply too much. I presented my complaint and found out that the Hotel manager, some czech lady unable to talk to me one to one, instead sent me a 2nd or 3rd in command with the message that she would not give any compensation or anything because the "hotel is great and either you pay now unless you want me to call security". Bottomline is that this hotel sucks. Oh, by the way, the bed sheets have holes and the pillows stink.

title: “If you like curry, this is the place for you; if not, stay soemwhere else”
text: I did not realize that Murrray Hill was Little India. Everything in this hotel, including the bedclothes, reaks of curry. I am very sensitive to odours and had to check out after 1 night of a 4 day stay. The room, otherwise was 'clean'. There is a window in the bathroom door and a window in the bathroom. This combination, although covered with a thin plastic film, allows too much light into the room, don't expect to sleep past first light of day, but at least you won't need an alarm clock. Great location 2 blocks from subway and walking distance to shopping dsitrict, but you have to be able to tolerate the above. I thought I was getting value for money, but once again, you get what you pay for!

title: “First pick for business hotel in this area”
text:
The best of the Westins. Really well cared for newer property, clean, contemporary design and good sized rooms, comfy beds, awesome showers, nice staff. Attached to Galleria so if you don't like OceanAire (wait, what?) in the hotel, then you can eat at Grand Lux (upscale Cheesecake Factory) or the sushi bar in the mall, both were good.
Hotel has an awesome rooftop/outdoor pool with cabanas for a quiet, late night swim. 
The downside - not sure I could find one with the hotel overall. There's limited parking in front of hotel, can park free in lower level ramp, and there's no elevator back up so you should leave your luggage with the bellman on the way in or out.
Do I want to stay again? Yes, and I will, in fact I already booked it!

title: “Everything was great!”
text: The facility was spotless. Every staff person we encountered had a pleasant and sincere greeting, and we had no problems or issues at check in or check out. We had a great room that was very spacious for New York standards. We could not have been happier with our stay, and will return here the next time our business takes us to this part of Manhattan. And, instead of the mediocre restaurants a couple of blocks away in Little Italy, try Parigot, just down the street on the corner of Layfayette and Grand.

title: “great views”
text: I stayed here last weekend. Had a room on the 15th floor with great views and a nice balcony. The room itself is quite ordinary..not as nice as a typical Hyatt. Close to sea world. Good location.

title: “Really disappointing”
text:
This is a grand old hotel, and the lobby and public spaces don't disappoint. Our room, however, did. Cramped, dark, with no place to sit comfortably and relax (except on the bed or at the desk), with a view of some sort of shaft. In order to tell if the sky was blue or gray, we had to crane our necks up from the corner of the window. 
The concierge staff was helpful if you could get to them; there were always a lot of people waiting in line at their desks and at the front desk. The cleaning staff was friendly and did a good job.
If the hotel cost less, one would take these inconveniences in stride, but when paying so much, one expects more. For less money, I think I would in future book a nicer room at, for instance, the Helmsley on Central Park South. Better location and you wouldn't feel depressed every time you returned from touring.
P.S. When, in answer to a question about my stay, I indicated my disappointment while checking out a friendly person at the desk gave me her name and said she would see I got a nice room next time I came. I probably won't take her up on it.

title: “The Parker was Fabulous!”
text:
After using your site to book Le Paker Meridien (aka "The Parker"), we were sad to see the negative post in late July. I called the management at The Parker, and they assured me the service and housekeeping would be grand! I felt emboldened if a little trepidatious, having the name of the GM in my pocket as we made our first trip to NYC! 
We arrived using a car service (much more economical than a taxi from Newark for four adults), and checked in at 2 pm. On this Thursday, we had the check in desk all to ourselves. Two front desk attendants with great personalities and lovely smiles helped us. Our friend's room was ready early, but our park view room wasn't quite ready, so the bellman took our bags and we ate lunch at Norma's at the hotel. 
After lunch, our room was ready, and we zoomed up 35 floors in the elevator to our Park View room. The room was small (as expected), but the view of Central Park made it feel quite large. It was spectacular! The room was clean, well-lighted, and comfortable. The bathroom was small but well-lit. It had an unfortunate design feature in that the door hit the toilet when you closed it! But, there was good water pressure, a nice shower head, lots of counter space, and there were always plenty of fresh towels. 
For $234/weekend night on Expedia, this room and location were unbeatable. I would go again in a heartbeat. They had great maps of Central Park in the room. The famed secret burger joint in the hotel was visited by our friends and well-loved. The concierge was available and helpful on many occasions. The Cima store had good coffee in the morning and a helpful staff. Room service was also on time and good. Quick tip: the newstand on 57th sells bottled water for $1!!! 
The automated check-out system was not operational, but when we went down right at noon (check out time), there was nobody in line, and we had a quick, pleasant check out. We stored our bags with the bellhop because our flight was later in the day. They politely warned us that 4 pm would be a "rush" on the bags, so we planned accordingly and got bags at 4:20 in plenty of time for our 4:30 car service back to Newark. 
The people in the hotel and restaurants of the City were just fabulous. We had doors opened for us, people wishing us a great vacation, oh, and I got a great haircut at Salon M on the Upper West Side as a walk-in on a Sunday! 
Loved the city, loved the hotel, loved Lion King (buy your tickets at Times Square at the TKTS booth and ask for best available seats). Can't wait to go back!

title: “Hilton, Chicago”
text: Historic and pricey building with smallish rooms that are clean and somewhat noisy. Our interior room had no view (another brick wall) but we weren't there for the view. Interactive in-room computer requires $$ to operate and there are fees for WiFi. Bathrooms are very small, could use some updating and our fixtures needed repair. Great public spaces and services. Have spent a lot less to stay at nicer places but would return here.

title: “Very cozy place.”
text: Stayed here on a whim, the rooms are very spacious and are well furnished. Also very clean!

title: “Ahhhhh!”
text: If you know what’s good for you, you won't stay at the Sohotel. Let me just mention a few thing... There were spiders on the toilet paper, no cable in the room, lets just say a closet was bigger than our room, and very early in the morning the fire alarm went off for no reason at all. And then when we asked them to turn it off they said that they couldn't so the fire alarm light was flashing all morning, try sleeping through that. The only good thing I can say about this hotel is that for the most part it was clean. So if you're looking for a cheap room with a crazy adventure then you might like the Sohotel. I on the other hand will never go back.

title: “Great in Every Way”
text: We just returned from a 2 night weekend stay at the W which was fantastic. I booked the room with Starwood points and as a Platinum member, was upgraded to a Marvelous Suite without having to ask. This was the first time in many visits to a Starwood hotel that I didn't have to ask for an upgrade. The room was great and our 2 year old daughter loved the incredible views of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier. The room was clean, spacious and had 2 plasma/lcd tvs - each with their own DVD player. The bed was very comfortable and the extra half bath was wonderful. Everyone on the staff was very accomodating. The location was great and we were able to quickly walk to Navy Pier. The museum campus with the Shedd Aquarium and Field Museum was only several minutes away. We had a chance to visit the hotel pool which was the perfect temperature and very clean. On Sunday we also enjoyed the complimentary hot tea and dessert in the lobby. Valet parking is $43 per night but the service was quick and we didn't have any issues. If I had to pay for my next stay, while a bit more expensive than other options in the area, the W is worth it.

title: “Not friendly or consistent”
text: I bought a package that was to include everything for my lodging but food and laundry services. The cost even was to include tax. When I arrived the room smelled of stale cigar smoke. I was told to turn the fan on while I went out for the evening and it would clear up. I came back at 2 am and the room still smelled. I couldn't get anyone to answer the phone at the desk. I was too tired after traveling all day and being at a tv show taping until after midnight in Burbank to pack everything up, go to the desk to try to find a person to talk with etc so I waited til the next day. I was then moved to the 14th floor which is to be a quite zone floor with no banging doors, no maid service until after 9 am etc. The floor was still noisy. The rooom I had also faced the airport and it was very noisy. I had to sleep with the heating/ac unit fan on high all night to try to drown out some of the noise. The parking garage costs $12 a day to park a car and they were not going to waive the fee until I showed them the paperwork that said my package included ALL fees and taxes. Finally after talking to 2 managers they waived the parking fee. The parking is a nightmare. You have to get a ticket when you go in and have it scanned in the hotel. Then most of the time when you go to leave the garage the machine won't scan it to let you out so you have to try to back up, find a parking space go get another ticket, go back to the hotel and have a new ticket scanned. Then try to leave again. Then when you go to come back into the garage the machine won't scan the ticket you have so you end up having a handful of parking tickets with you hoping one of them will work in the scan machine to let you in or out of the garage. It is a hugh pain in the neck and a BIG time waster. The rooms were ok but weren't cleaned everyday and the sheets were changed every 3 days uless you requested otherwise. The bed however was comfortable. The amenities they say are in the room are not necessarily there each day so don't count on them being there. There is always a line at the front desk as well and it also is a big time waster. I did find that Alfredo the concerige was very nice and helpful as was Cecelia t the front desk. I would use my money next time to stay somewhere cheaper as you get the same type of room and service at a cheaper place without all the parking hassel, airport noise roaring at night and expense of parking. The pool and hot tub are outside and well maintained. The fitted sheets didn't fit the bed and were 1/2 on and 1/2 off the bed.

title: “Felt like an escape even for Chicagoans!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at The James for Valentine's Day weekend just for something fun to do and to get out of our appt. The room was immaculate and extremely comfortable. The hotel is located in River North, an excellent spot for shopping, dinning, sightseeing in Chicago - which is always fun even for people who live here. I was impressed by the attention to detail, one example being Kiehl's shampoo and conditioner! In addition, the staff was inviting and friendly. Overall we loved our stay and will be back!

title: “Did Not Clean Room Between Nights”
text: On two night stay they did not enter room to change towels, tidy bath or even make beds. Even tho we removed our No Disturb sign at about noon and went out, front desk said since sign was up at noon, no maid service period. No effort to come back to do room! This is their policy regarding DND sign on door.

title: “Functional, but lacking in character”
text:
This was my first stay at a Homewood Suites. The suite was comfortable and spacious. The bathroom could have used better lighting, including a nite lite. Bed was fine, but ventilation blew directly on the sleeping area. Windows were sealed, leaving the room stuffy at times.
I found the breakfast and evening food provided to be institutional. It reminded me of college dorm cafeteria meals.
Not sure this brand is for me, but it wasn't bad for what was offered.

title: “Attentive staff make up for small losses”
text:
The Hyatt does what hotels used to do best and rarely do now - pay attention to the guest. They also do what hotel used to do and stopped doing long ago - provide less than lesser hotels automatically. Overall, it is a good deal.
Every staffer, without exception, was courteous, competent, and quick to help. Their eagerness and accessibility were constant, and it truly does make the guest feel good. 
What was missing that is often found in less expensive places was a decent coffee maker, free wifi, and daily paper (available to Hyatt gold passport holders). Some rooms - ours - have a very small window that has little sunlight or view at all. If that's important, ask first and don't use the electronic check-in desk. 
Very good exercise room, shallow pool more for lounging than stroking, a resident bagel/breakfast shop, sports bar with a strong menu, a fancy rooftop restaurant with accompanying prices, large meeting rooms and conference services, good bellman. 
I had a great rate because of a conference, so it was worth it. At rack rates I would think twice about it.

title: “TravelAgent Review”
text:
I went to the Seaport to work at the World Trade Center which is across the street from the Seaport. 
Location was fantastic
Cabs easily available in front of hotel
Doormen very friendly and personable, MOST of hotel staff same
AURA Bar/Resteraunt.... quite overpriced (but its a hotel resteraunt what do you expect?)
Aura BAR food ... decent to okay
The rooms furnishings and decor were average of a Radisson or low budget Marriott
Overall, we got the hotel free b/c was for business and if I had to work the area again, this hotel would be fine for 1-3 nights 
Had pool but NO JACUZZI or steam room/sauna
They did CHARGE us for the minibar which was NEVER touched (even had the string still attached) but they waived off our bill

title: “Great option and value”
text:
It´s a simple hotel, perfect to have a shower and sleep. It's clean, comfortable and offers a small breakfast (coffee, juice and muffins), which was fairly enough for us. The price is a good advantage if you are just looking for a place to rest comfortably at night. Other positive detail is the price of the valet, which was cheaper than others.
The one thing we didn't like that much was the location. During the day it was good, it's really near Market street and bus stops so there's no problem to access it. However, at night we were a bit cautious walking around, but nothing too dangerous (what we read online was worse than what it was in reality). You just have to be alert and avoid certain areas.
There is a bar nearby and we could hear some music, but it didn't bother.

title: “Don't stay here”
text: Booked a room online threw the hotel website. When I get there after a 5 1/2 hr drive from Sacramento they ask for a $100 deposit. No where did it say to leave a deposit on the website. They refused to take cash and said they would not charge my card that they were just going to put a hold on it. When checking out come to find out they took the $100 out of my accout because I used a debit card. (They never mentioned anything about running it for debit cards). I was told my account would not be credited for 5-7 business days. Seriously?? I asked for the manager he was useless as well. The "buffet" was crap and I'm not even a picky eater. The waffles are the frozen Eggo ones you buy at the store. And as we pulled around to room 210 there were 2 people sitting in a car smoking weed. Will not be staying here again.

title: “A good choice with very good service”
text:
Enjoyed a long weekend at the Sofitel Philadelphia. The location is more than central and convenient, the room generally nice, but the level of attentive service was perhaps the selling point. 
Desk and lobby staff were attentive and helpful; and cleaning staff kept the room notably in in very clean order. Room 624 was large if a bit oddly arranged with case and seating furniture set hard along one long wall, presumably to keep floor area open as I noticed it was one of the hotel's handicapped accessible rooms -- also with a rather oversized bathroom with good towels and L'Occitane amenities. The room has a Bose radio and a large flatscreen TV (though set far forward on a swivel stand atop a large cabinet, effectively undoing any space savings by sticking with the pattern for the old tube-style set.) Beds with their down toppers were very comfortable and the room quiet at night.
On checking in, I left the baggage with a porter to run out on an errand only to realized I'd misplaced my wallet. Assuming I might have left at the registration desk, I phoned the hotel and was connected immediately with a helpful security manager who investigated and immediately checked security CCTV footage where it was clear I had replaced my wallet in my pocket. All this was done within minutes and, again, very courteously. Overall, the rooms are at the lower end of 4-stars, with a couple of 5-star features. 
As for faults, the furnishings and fittings in the guest room were mostly of a sort of middling quality and showing a bit of wear - to echo a concern of other reviewers. While I saw the door staff jump to help a couple with a baby stroller, they were otherwise a little absent both in often being away from the doors or in not making any acknowledgment of the guests coming and going.

title: “Comfortable and good location”
text:
Spacious and comfortable rooms. Locational advantage of being near airport and a major mall, large number of food outlets with in walking distance.
Improvement required on the buffet breakfast quality and selection and in room internet speeds.

title: “Perfect spot for gameday weekend”
text: This is a great location and situation if you're heading to town for a game (or anything else on campus). The rooms were comfortable, clean and everything seemed new. Downstairs there is a great spot for breakfast, and the staff was extremely friendly and accommodating. Rates were moderate. We'd definitely stay again.

title: “Different for a JW”
text: Hotel is in a great location. Rooms are nice. We reserved 2 double beds. Beds were just a little bigger than a twin. 2people could not sleep in 1 bed. Shower was very very small. As Marriott gold members we had access to Executive Lounge. Selection was the worst I have ever seen for any Marriott. The drinks were to be paid for on the honor system. Strange for the lounge. Overall hotel was nice and clean but would not stay again for the price you pay.

title: “Great midtown location”
text: I stay here for business and also stayed recently with my wife for a long weekend. It is an excellent location for getting around Manhattan. Service however is average, rooms not made or cleaned after we got back from a full day of tourist activities. The restaurant is small as is the bar. No tea or coffee making facilities in room and if you feel like a night in on the cans watching footy, dont rely on the minibar!

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: We stayed here for 4 days in late May early June. It's a nice hotel but it's not kid friendly. The hotel has no pool. The complimentry breakfast was decent and the beds in the 1 bedroom suite were also decent. However, the pull out couch was afwul. It was very uncomfortable - and partially falling apart. Bring ear plugs - the halls can get loud. The hotel is 1 block from 16th street but a bit of a walk to the baseball stadium - however you can use the free bus on 16th street to get most of the way there. Overall it's a nice location and nice hotel.

title: “Good Hotel!”
text: A group of 5 women stayed here for 5 nights. The location is fairly close to the airport, but there are no restaurants in the area. Took us a few days to figure out the area and where things were located. The hotel is nice. Excellent breakfast. We didn't get to enjoy any of the dinners that they offer during the week. The 2 bedroom suite was perfect for 5 people.

title: “Philadelphia Airport Hilton”
text:
We have stayed at the Hilton Philadelphia Airport many times and it is always "high quality!" The entire staff is friendly, efficient and eager to be of help. We recognize this as an airport hotel and there are many business people who stay there. We don't fit that profile, since we are a retired couple who enjoy traveling. However, we are ALWAYS greetied like "old friends" especially by Tyrell (in the lobby and Alan, the Director of Sales) and are constantly amazed at how they can remember us!!! We stayed there on November 7th (the night before our flight to Arizona) and again on November 15th (on our return from Arizona). The night of the 15th we were surprised to receive a delightful fruit platter shortly after we got to our room. After a 5 hour flight, we can assure you that the fruit was delicious and welcome!!!! There is an excellent restaurant in the hotel as well as a Pub (with large TV screens showing the latest sports events.
We look forward to our next stay at the Philadelphia Airport Hilton!!

title: “Perfectly Fine”
text: Read all the negative reviews and almost booked another hotel -luckily I did not. The room was on the smaller side compared to some but more than enough for one business person. It was just like any other WESTIN in any other City except that it is was really cheap - this is the most inexpensive WESTIN I have ever seen.

title: “Needs Updating”
text:
Older hotel in Indy. Has a train station theme and train car rooms. Room was very outdated except for TV. Bed was old and had that springy feel - not comfortable and pillows had no substance to them. Bathroom had decay (see pics) and old wallpaper was showing its age. I guess that is what you get for the price.
I was worried about the train noise from reading other reviews but I didn't notice it at all. I think they spent too much money on the train station decor in the lobby and other areas rather than the actual rooms. Personally, the train station decor and theme doesn't excite me.

title: “Location +++ Hotel -----”
text:
If it's your first time in New York, I advise you to look for a hotel near the Times Square, where everything happens. This was the main reason why we've chosen Pennsylvania. The hotel is located in front of (literaly!) Penn Station, on the 7th Av. and 10 minutes walking distance from some of the main spots.
Regarding the hotel service, if you are looking for a pleasant place, with a nice service and a neat and comfortable room... forget Pennsylvania!
We've paid a little more for a room "Penn 5000", with breakfast included, thinking that we would have a bigger room but I can tell you that the only thing big in there was the furniture! Furthermore, the breakfast room was a standard room size for, what it seemed to me, a all floor, with only 4 tables... 
Hotels are expensive in New York, but I can guarantee you that this is not a "great value" for its service, only for its location!

title: “Great hotel, great location!!”
text: This hotel was wonderful, good size rooms for Manhattan! Rooms have a small kitchen area and great views of the city!!! Breakfast was wonderful but did end kind of early. Easy walk to most locations in the city, we had an amazing time! Thank you!!

title: “Absolutely Wonderful”
text: This hotel has by far been one of the best hotels I have stayed in. They have a breakfast worth getting up for and they even offer a dinner three nights a week. It is clean and rommy. The front desk staff is wonderful

title: “nice hotel, comfortable beds, staff unhelpful”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton for 3 nights. Overall a good stay and nice to come back to after a hard day's sightseeing.
The staff weren't all that helpful and if I'd had any real problems I feel I might be writing a different review.
The bathroom was a bit old and I was quite surprised to see that there was a suspicious grey ring around the bath I think due to age rather than lack of cleaning as the room and the rest of the bathroom were clean. No separate shower but a shower head over the bath tub which worked well most of the time. 
The beds were really comfortable and the room was fairly quiet.
We didn't eat in the hotel, preferring to visit local diners etc., but we did have morning coffee from the Starbucks attached to the hotel which was handy.
Overall a good hotel and a pleasant stay.

title: “Great Services”
text: My company meeting was held at the Bryant Park Hotel this year and i have to share that the servixces and the location is great. Darren at the front desk is wonderful Adolfo Ramirez was great as he offers the conference room was great with a very nice view and at a great price. The hotel is close to Times Square and the food is great.

title: “No Security - Building in Marginal Repair”
text: We picked this property because previous stays were excellent. This stay Aug 3, 2012 - Aug 4.2012 was much less satisfactory. There were minor things in disrepair. shower curtain rod was about to come out of the wall , bathroom sink faucet was loose, and other small stuff that did not affect our stay, more cosmetic than lack of functionality. Our room was never serviced by housekeeping the first day. We had to tell the front desk as we were leaving for dinner. They said they would send someone up to take care of it while we were at dinner. They did, but the next morning we had no coffee cups. they discarded the old ones but left none to replace them. On the morning of our departure we went out to find my truck had the rear door window broken out. The thieves stole new clothes just purchased as well as my radar detector and a pistol. The staff, as well as the police officer that took my report, said it is happening on a regular basis at this hotel. They have someone that supposedly walks the parking lot at night, but they have no fence around the property and no security cameras at all. There was another vehicle broken into the same night as mine. If you choose this hotel, don't leave anything that costs more than a dollar in your car.

title: “You will be disappointed”
text:
The hotel was in need of a remodel. The mattress was sunken on the sides. The carpet was worn out. The hotel has bad breath. 
The sheets on the bed were wrinkled up like they had not been changed from the last guest. The stuffing in the pillows has kind of petrified. The hotel in general does not look very clean. There is also a musty, stale smoke type of odor at this hotel.
The one good thing was a super fast internet connection. It was blazing fast! Also, come to think of it, the room was very large, but the bath was tiny.
My advice is to avoid this hotel.

title: “Live like a local on the Upper West Side”
text: This was our first visit to New York and my husband & I are so glad we chose the Beacon Hotel. It was everything other reviewers had described. Perfect location, close to subway (brilliant once you get the hang of it) & easy walking distance to Times Square. Our room was clean and tidy and having a kitchenette was so convenient for putting a quick healthy breakfast together. Fairway Supermarket just opposite has everything you could possibly need. Viand Cafe right next door where you can eat in or they will deliver to your room. The Beacon staff were all so friendly and no request was too much trouble (special mention to Dave who really looked after us). We loved our time in New York and staying at the Beacon was perfect. We would definately stay there again. Highly Recommended!

title: “Pretentious front desk, staff is great otherwise”
text:
Agree with FreqTrav99 on the poor service specific to the front desk only. Our stay was a last minute booking at the end of a snowboarding trip, we changed our hotel to be situated near the airport for our flight out in the morning. Called the reservation line for Marriott and hung up before booking since we were already in the lobby of the hotel, not realizing that they offer a lower rate for a better room over the phone vs showing up. The front desk guy didn't want to honor the rate for me and gave me the stink eye when I suggested that I'll just call back to book thru the Marriott hotline. He had no words, just completed with the transaction and gave me a key. Maybe his issue was more my sweatshirt and the enormous bags under my eyes from spending several days on the slopes? I thought I was in a Hilton, not the Waldorf Astoria --
The other staff members are just wonderful, a very nice gentleman skillfully handled alllllll our luggage (a ton of snowboard equipment, suitcases, laptops, shopping bags). Loved his Boston accent and his tips for getting to the airport and returning the rental, he even whistled while he put our stuff away! Same goes for the staff the bar, so accomodating and friendly. 
The room was spacious and had a great view. I want that chair/ottoman/chaise with tray for my home! :) 
On our floor, there was a sitting area by the elevators where you could lounge and watch the planes go by. Pretty cool and perfect for "unplugging" after a long day.

title: “Great Location”
text: Booked the premier room when I was there for a tradeshow in Javits Convention Center. About 20 minutes walk away. Macy's is just a stone throw distance away and the hotel is close to many major attractions liked Central Park, Soho, and Empire States Building which is just a street infront. They are nice enough to provide hot tea and coffee during the day at the breakfast area. But anytime that you need a cup of hot tea or coffee, there is a Keurig coffee maker in every room. Internet is complimentary too. Most importantly, after a day of work/shopping/sightseeing, you will be back to a wonderfully comfortable SERTA bed with heavy thread count soft sheets. The only complaint I have is that they dont replenish the toiletries.

title: “Good service and room.........surrounding area not the greatest but ok”
text: Booked this room for Rose Bowl trip as it's near my daughter's apartment. Hotel is a pretty typical Holiday Inn Express with excellent service and free internet and "hot breakfast". Parking was $10 per day but some other hotels in the area charge as much as $35. It is right off the 405 on Santa Monica Blvd so easy on and off freeway. Our room was clean and housekeeping was good. Plenty of hot coffee and typical HIE breakfast offerings. There were plenty of cinnamon rolls when we were there. :-) Scored an excellent, sub $80 rate, using Lastminutetravel.com. As others have mentioned immediate area surrounding hotel not the best, but far from "dangerous" and other side of the 405 is very high-end. I'd stay here again.

title: “Historical Hotel! Awesome location!”
text: Great rooms! Very spacious. This place is breathing history! There is a 4 Seasons Cafe and a Tully's Coffee stand in house. The staff was super polite and very accomodating. Any time I goto Seattle, I am staying here.

title: “Nice hotel near Union Square”
text: We stayed with some friends and had two rooms, both of which we upgraded for $20 to deluxe rooms. The upgrade added floor to ceiling windows and a king size bed. The rooms were located next to each other on the 23rd floor, however one room was large with a sitting area and the other was about 75% of the size and fairly compact. Parking is expensive at the hotel (about average with other hotels in the area) and the amenities in the room are fairly limited compared to other Starwood hotels I've stayed at. The room did include a personal coffee maker with Starbuck's coffee, which was an excellent touch and much easier to use then your average hotel coffee maker. Overall, a nice clean 4-star hotel in the Union Square area, but nothing amazing!

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
Stayed one night at this hotel for business. I had booked a king bed on the executive floor on the Hilton website. When I arrived, the executive floor was booked, so the front desk clerk gave me a suite with two double beds and a key that accessed the executive lounge. The room was large and comfortable, although I couldn't understand why the couch in the living area wasn't in front of the TV. In fact, no furniture was. But, it had a 2nd TV in the bedroom, so no big deal. Nice upgrade for the same price.
As for the executive lounge, it had a great view but that's about it. It's not worth the extra money for the weak munchies and "honor bar."
The hotel provides a "shuttle" to places close by. I went out the front door looking for the "shuttle" and found a Cadillac waiting for me. The driver was friendly and knowledgeable and not only dropped me at the front door of where I was going, he gave me his cell phone number so I could call him to come pick me up.
Places close by include the biggest mall I've ever seen (the Galleria, 4th biggest in the U.S.) and any shopping imagineable. Also, any restaurant you wanted was close by, although I eventually settled on room service, which was excellent.
The next morning the conceirge checked me in for my return flight then arranged all my transportation for that morning, including to my meeting and to the airport. 
Also, this Hilton advertises a fitness center. It's actually no more than a closet with a couple of treadmills. No matter, however, because just across the street the Bally's gives guests free admission. Very nice.
Overall, an excellent place to stay.

title: “Good location and in walking distance to Fenway Park. Steep prices though.”
text: Stayed here for one night to attend a Boston Red Sox game. I'm a hilton gold member so I usually stay at any Hilton family hotel. This hotel is walking distance to Fenway but you're looking at 10 to 15 minute walk. Breakfast in the lounge for members was good, but the man greeting me and accepting my breakfast vouchers was not as friendly. The waittress clearing the table was nice. I felt that location-wise, if you're going to a game, this hotel is adequate, but as for service, I've been to more friendlier hiltons that were the same price. I paid $299 a night which was steep, but expect exceptional service at price.

title: “We were short sheeted.”
text: Seiously, I woke up in the morning to realize that my feet were on the bare mattress, not a sheet. The only coffee available in the room was decaf. The room was small but comfortable with a unique style. When we needed a cab in the morning, the bellman had to run a different hotel to get it.

title: “DO NOT STAY AT THE ALEX”
text: I´ve been in NY more than 10 times... And every single time I stay in a different hotel to get different experiences. This time, although a friend of mine warned me about The Alex Hotel, I did like the site and the price (for the best room available) and I booked. Well, what can I say? It´s a 2 star hotel charging as a 5 star hotel. They do pretend to be a 5 star hotel, charging really high prices for the breakfast and for everything else you need. They do have good amenities (such as great brand of shampoo and lcd tv at the small, REALLY small bathroom) and.... That´s it. The staff are friendly (until you complain about something... After that you´ll feel their anger) and the entrance hall and elevators (lifts) are a joke! And talking about the staff, it´s too small. After two days, I gave up, lost some money (no, they didn´t give my money back) and moved to other hotel (The Pierre, not excellent, but 100 times better than The Alex...). Even the location of The Alex is not that good (The Wellington Hotel, chargind much more reasonable prices and much better than the Alex is much better located). If you´re thinking in staying at The Alex, save some money and just pick a 2 or 3 star hotel... It will, for sure, be better. Horrible experience.

title: “Poor hotel”
text: This hotel is tired, old, and pretty inconvenient to the Riverwalk. Our first room had a shower which didn't work properly, and when we complained, the owner fought us and then tried to put us in a lower-grade room. The location is bearable if you have a car, but it is between an interstate and a railroad.

title: “Not Worth It”
text: I wish I would've checked here before booking a room at this hotel. Now that i've read the reviews I also experienced some of the same problems. First off, when I went to check in they had 2 people working at the front desk. I was second in line and there were at least 10 people behind me. One good thing about Loews was the staff, they were very friendly. The room itself was huge. Very nice size. However, the cordless phone in the room did not work. There was no trash can in the bathroom and the lighting in the room would dim quite often. Now, onto the beds. I have NEVER slept on a bed so hard! I can't even begin to describe the way the bed felt. Let's just say, the floor felt better!! I called down to the front desk and told them about all of this and they did not offer to move me to another room or accomodate me in any other way. So for the price I paid to stay here ($250 a night) it was not worth it. I would suggest the Westin.

title: “Just OK”
text:
I stayed at the Chicago Renaissance for a conference for work. When I walked in I was pleasantly surprised by how nice the lobby was, and check in was a breeze. However, other than those two, my stay was just ok. Nothing wrong, but not great. The room is pretty spacious for being in a city, and the bed was very comfortable. However, the bathroom, while nicely appointed, had a funny smell. It came and went throughout my stay, as if it was coming from a vent to another room? Also, while the TV was nice, flat, wide-screen, the picture still came in fuzzy, which was weird. Not enough to ask to change, but it was weird. Also, I had to ask a few times to get any packages that came for me (the conference was in the hotel). This is likely a reflection on the banquets department rather than the bellhop. 
The good news is that the location was very convenient with quite a few restaurants within a five minute walk, and a cute cafe across the street for a quick breakfast. 
Next time I am in Chicago and have a choice of hotels, I wouldn't choose this one. There are just too many other, better choices in the same price range. It was fine, but for the price should have been better.

title: “Great value, colorful location”
text: After usually staying at midtown hotels for leisure trips in the past, we decided to opt for a different location. The positive reviews of the Mulberry Hotel, the affordable room rates and the location all appealed to us. When we first arrived, we had our doubts. The hotel is located in the middle of Chinatown, albeit on a quiet street, next to what is said to be the best dumpling place in town. Once we saw our room, however, we were more than satisfied. Two queen sized beds, lots of drawer and closet space and a good-sized bathroom. Plus overlooking a park where teenagers play volleyball and elderly Chinese practice tai chi. Never quite got the hang of the heater; it was generally too warm in the room. The location is central: Little Italy is two blocks away and Soho a couple of blocks further. Complimentary breakfast is served at Mama's, a quirky little place a few buildings down. You can choose between eggs and bacon, etc., an omelet or banana pancakes. We had breakfast there the first morning, after which we opted for a light start of the day at Starbucks (on Canal St., a five minute walk away and open as of 5:30 am). Wifi is free of charge and it's possible to print out boarding passes in the lobby. It's possible to make tea or instant coffee in the room and tea bags were replenished daily. Rooms were cleaned thoroughly each day. The staff were polite and helpful, although found the check-out policy rather rigid. We had a late evening flight and asked for a late check-out but the hotel strictly adheres to a 12 noon checkout. It is possible to store your bags there, however. In all, we spent an enjoyable four nights at the hotel and would not hesitate to stay there again in the future.

title: “Ramada Austin Central gave us bedbugs!”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed here ACL weekend, and thought that the hotel was nice enough. About 24 hours after leaving the hotel, we both started itching all over. Soon, raised red bumps appeared all over our bodies, probably 15-20 total each. After doing some research, we found that they were indeed BEDBUG bites. 
We contacted Ramada corporate, who told us to speak with the manager, Sam Wilson. A few days later, we received a letter from Mr. Wilson basically passing the buck. He stated that others had stayed in the room after us and had not reported bedbugs. He offered no sort of refund, grievance or apology other than a weak "thank you for staying with us and we trust you otherwise enjoyed your stay". 
I spoke with him recently, and he remained in denial about the situation simply stating that there must be some other reason that we developed begbug bites. He even admitted that they had a bedbug infestation 6 months ago which he said "had been dealt with"!
I cannot fathom where else we could have developed bedbugs that weekend other than the hotel we slept in. Ramada's refusal to right the situation has led me to post my review on various sites so that others can be made aware of their lackluster customer service. 
Beware of the bedbugs!

title: “Loved it!”
text: Can't really understand other reviews complaining about the staff, we found them to be helpful and friendly. For the price paid it was good, the area was great. Had no problems with the room or noise. You can walk to the gaslamp quarter and all of the resturants. Although, if you are staying in Little Itay you have to eat at Frippie's just up from the hotel, it is the best Italian food. I would stay here again for sure!

title: “Great Stay !!!”
text: My wife & I stayed at this hotel for our anniversary & could not have had a better time. Rhonda at the front desk checked us in and was wonderfull.We told her this was a special occasion and she did everything she could to make our stay one we would remember always. Our room was amazing. It had the most incredible views of both the city and of Navy Pier. The suite was not only spacious and clean, it had the most comfortable mattress and pillows on the bed we have ever experienced. The "continental" breakfast in the Executive Room was definitely NOT the continental breakfast we have had elsewhere. It was a full breakfast with so many delicious options to choose from. Not only was the food wonderful but the view was great as well. Everyone we came in contact with at the hotel was very friendly. The woman working in the Executive Room at breakfast was very friendly and attentive. The pool was very nice with the perfect water temperature. Incredible views there as well!! We could go on and on but the bottom line is that we would go back to the Swissotel in a heartbeat! From the moment we checked in with Rhonda to the time we sadly needed to check out, everything was way better than our expectations, which were already high due to the repution of the Swissotel.

title: “Excellent!!!”
text: After many years of making the Bristol Lounge my last stop of the evening, I got married here. I couldn't have asked for anything. No detail was left unturned. Living in Maryland and getting married in Boston I relied on the Four Seasons for everything and it was the most wonderful wedding!

title: “Most Incredible Hotel Stay Ever”
text: Stayed here for my wife's birthday courtesy of our son. Were upgraded by the hotel to a suite on the 53rd floor, with beautiful views of the Hudson river and a little of Central Park. Hard to imagine a better appointed room. Living room was all glass walls with fantastic views. The bed was extremely comfortable, and the bathroom well appointed. We've stayed in many places around the world and this was one of the most amazing experiences. We've been in the lobby for high tea once before, but this time enjoyed breakfast in the restaurant overlooking Central Park. Very tasty eggs benedict!

title: “Great location to Times Square and Theaters”
text: The Intercontinental Times Square is an ideal location if you want to be close to the action, but not kept up all night by noise. We had 3 rooms, with 3 teenagers and 3 moms. It was perfect for all of us, which isn't easy with those different ages and desires. Walking distance to great restaurants and the theaters. One of us actually had a handicapped room, which at first we wanted to change. However, the hotel was full, so we had to live with it. As it turned out, it was fine because the bathroom was larger (no tub tho, but I really don't take baths in hotels). The safe in the closet was on the floor though, which was awkward to use and there was no floor length mirror in the room or bath (Do handicapped people not need a mirror?) But overall, the hotel was great. And don't miss having a cocktail by the fireplace in the lobby and dinner in the fabulous CAVA restaurant by Todd English. Fabulous!

title: “Friendly and helpful staff, but no free wifi”
text: Nice place, clean and comfortable, great staff. But I would have liked free wifi. With that, I would have rated as excellent.

title: “3-day get away”
text:
My wife and teenage son and daughter had a good time at the resort. It was our first visit and basically lived up to our expectations. We would consider returning, but I feel that the rooms are over priced even given the very pleasant surroundings. I think the management needs to take a serious look at what type of resort it "wants to be." It should pick its clientèle carefully, then go after it with more style and amenities(!).
Pros:
The location and grounds are very good; we found the visit to be very relaxing. The staff (except for our check-in experience) were friendly and helpful. The room was clean and comfortable. We were located within a few seconds of a pool, which turned out to be great. The room was quiet and we didn't hear "pool" noise. We really enjoyed the water sports, which we thought was reasonably priced. We spent time on the resort beaches, which we all enjoyed.
Close proximity to downtown San Diego, Mission Beach and Sea World is a big plus.
Cons:
The were only two restaurants, which, were over priced. The "barefoot" restaurant had large portions and matching prices. Given the large number of families with small children, the resort could cater for this demographic a lot better. Too much wasted food. Our teenagers felt that that, other than the water sports, the resort had very little to offer them! This is a major gap in the resort or maybe they are sending a message.
We found a severe lack of "good" restaurants in the local area.
My wife and I didn't see that much for adults to do other than enjoying the surroundings (nice, but more is needed).
We did not get the types of beds we requested, and were not told about this at check-in - not good.

title: “excellent value for money in central new york. definitely one to go back to”
text: The HH is a small apartment-type hotel in a very central location. The reception staff are very helpful and were keen to please. The 2 bedroom apts are very large with a good lounge and full-sized kitchen and are a welcome change from small hotel rooms. They sleep six easily, although there is only one bathroom. The down side is the traffic if you are a light sleeper. We got used to it after the first two days. The one-bedroom apts do not face the street so are quieter. Ask for a high floor (there are only 9) if you are noise-bothered. The rooms and kitchen were cleaned daily. We would definitely come back to this apartment which is great value for money, located on E49th street, i.e. 7 streets from Times Square and 4 blocks from 5th Avenue. Highly recommended. Breakfast was also included in the price. It was basic but good quality.

title: “THE place to stay in LA. Fantastic accomodation, location, views and staff”
text:
This hotel is quite simply excellent. Nestled away in the Hollywood Hills, its location is superb. We, (2 adults and 2 kids aged 15 and 11) originally booked four nights at the hotel and ended up staying for six in August 2004. We booked direct with the hotel and got an excellent rate for a suite with full city views. The view from our balcony (which was big) was incredible - during the day and at night. The suite was large and tastefully furnished - a fully equipped kitchen with microwave, oven, toaster and coffee maker, queen sofa bed, armchair, dining table and desk with a master bedroom (king bed), large bathroom with a spa bath and shower. Plus 2 TVs!. This place is like having your own apartment in Hollywood. It is set in beautiful scenic gardens which stretch up from Franklin Ave (one block up from Hollywood Boulevard) to the Yamashiro restaurant. The pool is a good size - we had it mostly to ourselves during the entire stay - with a pagoda feature. You can see the Hollywood sign from the gardens of the hotel and look out across the whole of LA. 
The staff were extremely helpful at reception. The Continental breakfast (included in the rate) is served at the Magic Castle hotel - the sister hotel which is located at the foot of the hill. You can eat breakfast by the pool of the Magic Castle or take it back up the hill to your room. Excellent choice of cereals, croissants, pastries and juices. 
Nearby is the Hollywood and Highland Mall with loads of places to eat and drink - just alongside the Kodak Theatre, Chinese Theatre and Walk of Fame. 
We would strongly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting LA. Its in a great location for exploring Hollywood sights, Universal studios, Beverley Hills, Santa Monica and the northern beaches. And its tucked away in the hills so you feel both near and far away at the same time. 
The whole property is within security gates so a very safe place to stay and keep your car (parking is $8 a day). 
This hotel definitely made us stay longer in LA and we will definitely return in the future.

title: “Excellent hotel in even better location”
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay here. Our room was spacious with a very nice bathroom. Despite the train line running close to the hotel, the room was quiet. Location is excellent - Millenium park is on your doorstep, most tourist attractions are within walking distance and the hotel is easy to get to on the L line from o'Hare airport. Would definitely recommend it!

title: “20th Anniversary Trip”
text: We stayed at this location for our 20th Anniversary. The staff made us feel special and when we returned to our room they had a bottle of wine and a lovely card wishing us Happy Anniversary. The hotel is the perfect location for spending time in the city. We were pleasantly surprised that they provided free food and drinks for happy hour the breakfast was awesome. We would highly recommend this hotel to anyone that would like to stay in Denver.Thank you Residence Staff for making our time there special.

title: “Where's the Beef?”
text:
I'm confused. the Omni is a nice updated hotel in San Francisco's financial district, but notice I did not say great. I had a business meeting here. However, to get to a decent number of restaurants, shopping or even BART will require walking a few blocks. The bar is tiny and the restaurant is over priced, although this is where you get the beef as they specialize in steaks. The rooms are OK but unless you are on the top floor, you will be looking into another building!
Please don't get me wrong, the Omni is nice enough but you can get the same at almost any major San Francisco hotel and for less money. I don't understand or agree with it's high ranking.

title: “Horrible room and staff didn't care”
text: We booked our room on priceline. It was listed everywhere for about $400, we did the name your price bid and got a room for $199. Unfortunately we felt like they gave us the worst room in the hotel. It was on the first floor located between the women's restroom (used by the restaurant and bar patrons) and the staff entrance to the kitchen) and it smelled like body odor and there were several hairs in the bed. Until about 2am we heard the bathroom toilets flushing, women talking in the bathroom, and heels clicking on the tile floor. We called the front desk and asked to switch rooms and they said they were full there was nothing they could do. The noise finally stopped around 2:15am when the bar and restaurant cleared out and no one was using the bathroom next to our room. Then at 6am the kitchen noise started. People were bringing trays of glasses on dollies into the back entrance of the kitchen that were clinking. Staff were taking breaks outside of the kitchen and talking right outside our room. So we slept from about 2:15am until 6am. When we mentioned this to staff upon check out, we were told they would "look into it" but wouldn't do anything else. We had a horrible experience there and will not be returning.

title: “Fabulous stay at the Westin NY at Times Square”
text: We stayed at The Westin NYC Times Square from December 21-24th, and had an amazing stay. Being a Starwood Preferred Guest (SPG) was a great asset to our stay, as our room was upgraded and we had the most amazing views from our upper level corner room. We also were upgraded to Executive Club privileges, which greatly surprised us and made our stay that much more enjoyable. The room and bathroom were clean and elegant. The Westin Heavenly bed was truly that--especially after a long day of walking the city of New York! Though the weather was cold while we were there, we still took full advantage of staying in the heart of Times Square and walked everywhere for 3 days. The Westin's location cannot be beat--you are in walking distance from most tourist sites (and nearby to the TKTS booth, where you can get half-price show/theatre tix), yet the hotel is still quiet enough where you can relax. At night, our sleep was uninterrupted and we were blissfully ignorant of the honking horns and lights below. I recommend staying at the Westin for business or pleasure--it will surely be our choice when we return to NYC.

title: “Perfect for business travel”
text: Just 5 minutes from airport. Though hidden and deels like in a middle of forest. Nice breakfast is included. Very spacious working area in room. Good fitness centre. The best hotel for business travel in the area.

title: “It was cool...but overall, not impressed.”
text:
Well, let me start off by saying that Hotel Zaza is absolutely beautiful! The tapestries, the chandeliers, etc.. They have themed rooms which looked pretty cool. If you want a balcony room, make sure you just book it and not hope for that free upgrade. Balcony rooms are the first to go! You feel very welcomed from when you get out of your car to when you leave. The doorman was super nice and very personable. You can even bring a pet, although I don't know what the restrictions or charges are for that. Oh yeah, this is not a place to bring your kids unless they are 21+. It's a very poshy adult scene at Hotel Zaza. You will probably be a bit uncomfortable with your kids. 
The Rooms. The rooms are way cute with a very modern feel. We stayed in the deluxe 425 sq. ft. room. Our friend stayed in the smaller 384 sq. ft. room and it was also cute. Same decor, smaller room, so there's not too much space. It's worth the extra dollars to get the larger room. It's more open and roomier. We got the room on the "Club ZaZa Level" which is the 4th floor. You can only access this floor by swiping your card key in the elevator. But from what I heard, there really is no difference in rooms between a normal room and a Club Zaza level room. It's just a more secured floor. The bathroom was large and they let you use a complimentary robe. There are little toiletry baskets in the bathroom. Some is free (shampoo, conditioner, lotion) but the rest is not. So be careful when taking that stuff and be clear on which items you have to pay for and which items you don't. There is a price list in this basket. There is also a mini fridge and a snack basket in the room. The price list ranges from a $4 kit-kat (small size) to a $5 soda. There are liquor bottles in there as well from GreyGoose to Johnny Walker Black Label, to wines, and even champagne. Again, check the prices on these items before you grab. If you hate the noise and prefer quiet either stay at another hotel or ask to be placed at the opposite end of the pool/Dragonfly Lounge area. It is quite noisy. Our room was the furthest away (but facing the pool's direction, we had a clear view of the pool area) and we heard the music crystal clear. It didn't bother us, but if you're the type it would bother, I wouldn't recommend staying here. 
The Food. The food is great! I had brunch there and it was excellent! But be warned....four of us ate and only ordered 2 liquor drinks and our bill was $100...without the tip! I ordered a cheeseburger and 2 drinks for my husband one night (room service) and it was $30...without a tip. If you order room service, just order the food if you want a soda. It's $4 for a soda in the fridge, but $5-6 for the same soda on room service. The next morning we ate breakfast and it was just under $100 because we kept it at coffee and juice this time. 
Valet. Be warned that if you park your vehicle there it is $7 a day or $20 overnight fee. So if you're staying for three nights, you are paying $60 upon check-out. This is whether or not you are a guest!
Dragonfly Lounge/Night Life. The night life is popping on Fridays and Saturday nights! They have a DJ and it's really cool and fun. If you are a guest, enter the club through the roped off area in the main lobby area. Show them your card and you're in. Otherwise, you will be waiting in a LONG line outside to get in where non-guests are, and trust me, there is a lot of people who want to get in this place! The Dragonfly Lounge area is outside and VERY small. They pack people in pretty tight, so be careful not to fall into the pool! There is one bar, but the bar is only 5 ft. long, so if you want a drink (as a guest) get your drinks inside. There are doormen outside each door to go inside and will stop everyone who does not have a room key. So it's not as crowded inside or noisy. Plus you can relax and socialize at the bar or at the tables. I noticed on Friday and Saturday night there were security guards on the 4th floor when I was going back to my room. I'm not sure if this is on every floor on those nights, but it makes you feel a little safer that random people aren't going to be walking through the hallways, hopefully. Hint: If you aren't 21 then don't stay here. We saw so many people guests and non-guests getting denied at the door because they weren't of age. And they were not shy about denying people. A lot of people were denied access. One girl made a scene because she was a guest and she couldn't get in. 
All and all this is a pretty swanky hotel. Although we could have received an awesome and larger suite at another 5 star hotel for the same price. Is it worth the extra money? Not really, in my opinion. Like I said, you can get a lot more and better for the same price at another 5 Star hotel/resort. We feel a little like we wasted money for nothing. And trust me, we have stayed at some top of the line hotels/resorts and we do not mind spending more money for nicer amenities, etc.. But we were not that impressed with this hotel. I've received bigger, better, and nicer things for what we paid there.

title: “Crockett Hotel--okay but not great”
text: Stayed at the Crockett for a weekend visit to the San Antonio Missions. The hotel has a great, central location; in fact our room overlooked the Alamo. The staff was very accommodating and friendly and the room was clean with nice toiletries. The rest of the experience was just mediocre. The included breakfast was on par with a cheap motel. There was very little to choose from and the coffee was cool and watered down. The room was extremely small and the tiny bathroom had one of the worst layouts I've seen in years. This is obviously a very old hotel that has been updated and the staff is trying hard. However, the limitations of the building makes this a tough sell with all the modern competition around it.

title: “Good 20 Century experience”
text:
The location is great for a tourist/business trip. Michigan Avenue is right there. The nearest subway station is about 6/7 blocks away, but the bus runs right next to the hotel. 
The service is great, thou the hotel is quite old; which has it pluses and negatives. The rooms are spacious and we had a great lake view, however the decor itself is just what I would call "granny like". You can tell the hotel was the "it" place 50 years ago, I just think it needs some bringing it to the 21 century.
Room service was fairly quick.
I was there because of a conference my partner was attending, but for the same money I probably would stay somewhere less "old flashy" and more substance, such as a place with a good gym or wireless internet in the rooms. Again nothing wrong with the hotel, just personal preference.

title: “Had a good time”
text:
We had a very nice stay at this hotel. It is conveniently located to the typical tourist attractions and a short taxi ride from Union Station.
One of our rooms wasn't ready in a timely manner at check-in, but the staff gave us a comp for 2 meals in the American "Sea" Grille restaurant.
The rooms were clean and a good size.
I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Our Perfect Wedding”
text: We had our perfect wedding at the Maple Manor Hotel. The garden was magical, the dining room was beautiful, and the food was great! Monique, the hotel manager, also made our wedding stress free. I will definitaly have my anniversary there to relive our perfect day. :)

title: “Great location, clean, good service”
text: Stayed at this hotel attending a meeting which was held on-site. Piece of cake getting to the hotel from the airport on BART. Rapid check-in, although our two adjacent rooms were not ready at the time. Rooms are spacious and well-appointed. No real views. On the 11th floor, the room was quiet. I always love in-room coffee and the little one-cup device was perfect. Huge, comfortable bed. Good work desk and task chair. Didn't try the food in their restaurant, but the breakfast food at the conference was excellent. Easy walking to Union Square and Chinatown. Easy access to public transportation. Many decent restaurants in the area, within a 3 block radius. Lots of shopping, also.

title: “Radisson Warwick/Locust St/Center City”
text: This was an okay hotel, but I was expecting it to be "above average". The room we got was a larger one, which was wonderful, since we had 2 adults and 2 children in one room. I glanced in at some other rooms as I walked down the hall, and know this room to be especially spacious. Most of the staff was courteous, altho' one hotel operator was short with me when I called to get more towels to lay on the wet floor from when the toilet had overflowed unexplainedly the day before! It wasn't stopped up, and the overflow was completely unexpected...I wonder if this older hotel (it's on the National Historic Register) has pipes that need replacing? Also, the maid service was disappointing on some small points, like once our coffee mugs were rinsed/washed out and left to dry in the bathroom, and the bedspread was not replaced on one bed once, but left in a heap on the floor under the window. Also, lots of dirt under the beds. So it was "okay" we did not switch rooms, but this was not a luxury hotel. I will try another hotel on any future Philly trips.

title: “Best Holiday Inn I've stayed in”
text:
I have stayed in a number of Hoilday Inns over the years, but this is overwhelmingly the best so far. 
Its function is as a stopover before or after a flight, but you could easily use it as a base to tour the area. The location is excellent, and the shuttle bus to the airport is frequent and quick. My room was very comfortable and the bathroom was well equipped. Breakfast was good. There are several restaurants in the area if you don't want dinner in the hotel.
The hotel offers tours of the main attractions in the area, eg Disneyland, Universal Studios, the Getty Center etc, so you could easily visit LA and not have to use a car!

title: “Home away from home”
text:
This place is excellent, they really go the extra mile as soon as you walk in the door. Rooms are clean and mattress real comfortable.
The evening clerk even printed my boarding passes for free. I also had free wi-fi. Nice heated pool. Over all I had a great time, Cant wait to come back.

title: “Mediocre Marriott”
text: Don't believe those who say don't believe the negative comments! This Marriott has seen better days and management should seriously consider a renovation soon if they want to keep their loyal Marriott customers. The Lobby looks good yes, the service is friendly and efficient but the rooms definitely need to be updated. We booked this property for a one night visit, one 1-bedroom suite and 1 junior suite. We were upgraded to two 1-bedroom suites upon arrival but found the suites to have a cold, empty worn out feeling to them and dated, very dated. There is good deal of space but nothing seemed comfortable or well taken care of and definitely not an overall value. We prepaid these reservations online but later found out on our credit card statements were charged again; an easy fix but still be careful to watch your statements carefully. Overall, it's clean and will do the trick if you are in town on business but worth it, no. You have better value across the street at the Westin. I hate to say it but come on Marriott - time to renovate! Save this hotel from going under!

title: “Beautiful Design”
text:
The Onyx is a small, very stylish boutique hotel has been open only a short time. Most of the kinks that are inevitable in a new property seem to have been worked out. There is no restaurant, but there is a small bar area where light snacks and a complimentary continental breakfast are served; a complimentary glass of wine is also available here in the late afternoon. Newspapers (New York Times and Boston Globe) are also complimentary. There is a light 24 hour room service menu. 
Contrary to an earlier review here, I did not find my room too small or dark. My single king was quite beautifully decorated (with a lot of reds and blacks), and was one of the most restful and pleasant hotel rooms I have stayed in lately. The room was compact, but not at all cramped. It faced Portland Street, which was not noisy. I will definitely stay here again.
The location is either a plus or minus, depending on your needs. The hotel is half a block from the Fleet Center, which means that the neighborhood has many sports bars that become somewhat rowdy when Boston teams win. North Station is underneath the Fleet Center, which means good transportation connections (including commuter rail and two T lines). The North End, with a terrific selection of good Italian restaurants, is a short walk away. The walk to the North End will become substantially nicer when the landscaping on top of the Big Dig is finished in the next year or so. 
A few tips: One way to avoid the tempting but seriously overpriced goodies in the mini-bar is to shop at the 7 Eleven half a block away on Causeway Street. Across the street is an Au Bon Pain that has a very nice courtyard seating area (open only during regular office business hours). Down the street is Anthem, a trendy but pleasant New American restaurant with decent food, and a large bar area. A new steakhouse will open soon in the new Bullfinch Hotel on Merrimac Street, about two blocks away. Devotees of fast food will find some of the usual suspects on Causeway Street, facing the Fleet Center.

title: “perfect place to sleep b/c of location”
text: not too much to say about this place - just what you expect from the sheraton brand. seems close to the aiport which it is, and was doubtful because of how close the planes would fly but never bothered me.

title: “Very CUTE, WARM & CHIC hotel...”
text: OMG! At the last minute my husband and I decided to take a last minute, spontaneous trip for a conference in the state of Washington. The service of the staff, especially the manager made the trip for us both! I flew from Hawaiii and my husband flew in from Michigan. I arrived early and tired to the hotel, but I was accomodated immediately with a lovely room. In the first room we stayed at there was a glass shower behind the bed. How wild is that? Then we were upgraded into another chic room that had a revolving bathroom door with a mirror on it. My husband thought it was the coolest thing and would like to build one in our house. The complimentary breakfast and the mint scented amenities were nice to have. The ambiance of the place was so warm and cozy. The manager gave us a list of great places to dine at and visit and we enjoyed them all! Truly, it was the warm and kind service that made me feel at home and welcomed to the beautiful state of Washington. I strongly recommend giving the manager a raise! Thank you for having us. We look forward to making a trip back!

title: “Noisy room”
text:
Stayed here one night, at the executive floor. The room was large and nice, but very noisy. You could easily hear the ACs in the neighboring rooms and the traffic 25 stores down. 
The front desk at check in was at best uninterested, And I had to argue with the waiter at the breakfast about breakfast being included or not .
For that rate you could do much better in Philadelphia

title: “You get what you pay for”
text:
After reading the reviews on trip advisor, I knew what I was in for...no surprises. It was the cheapest hotel in the area without having to share a bathroom... Nothing impressive. Noisy. Small. Good for someone who only needs a place to sleep and wont be in the room very much.
The only thing that really disappointed was that someone from another hotel was at the desk and was having problems getting me checked in....apparently he was also cleaning the rooms...seemed a little questionable....
Overall, for being the cheapest hotel, I got what I paid for. Tolerable for a couple nights but dont set your standards too high.

title: “Ideal location in Financial District, average service”
text:
Booked a special 2 nights getaway for mid August 2012. Check-in was smooth, there is a carpark just opposite the hotel on the same street, (note reception is not located on the ground floor), especially enjoyed the warm chocolate chip cookies provided to greet you! Our room was located on the high floors but we never had to wait long for the elevators. Corridors are tiny but they saved the space for the room which is fine. Concierge gave us fantastic tips for restaurants! Cable TV was shut down for an entire evening which was very frustrating (with no compensation from hotel or perhaps gesture such as free wifi in room to keep us busy). But our biggest dissappointment came from housekeeping: bed sheets were not changed eventhough we had not requested to retain ours and worst of all I have forgotten personal items in the room and housekeeping who is in charge of lost and found never returned any of my calls! I eventually managed to speak to the hotel assistant manager who told me she would inform housekeeping to call me back. Again they never did. This leaves sore memories...
Pros:
Location
Great Concierge service
Warm chocolate chip cookies
Cons:
Housekeeping poor service
Aircondition noise in room
Cable TV breakdown for more than 8 hours

title: “You get what you pay for.”
text: I stayed at NY Palace for business a few years ago but was in and out in one night and didn't get to enjoy the City nor the location of this hotel for all of it's benefits. I just returned from a two-night stay in NYC with my mom to celebrate her birthday. I did a lot of research online to find a 4-star or better hotel that offered great accommodations, location, service, cleanliness and that wasn't going to cost me an arm and a leg. I also required a room with two queen-size beds as I'm not a fan of singles. My search resulted in two hotels that came down to the last as the kicker and the NY Palace, while more than I really wanted to spend, proved to be so worth the extra money that I laid out for an exceptional weekend. This hotel is a stand-out and did not disappoint on any of my criteria. I highly recommend your next stay here as you will so glad you sucked up the extra expense as it is so worth it. We walked to Central Park, the Theatre District, shopping on 5th Ave., Madison and even one block away from Park Ave. St. Patrick's Cathedral is literally right across the street as is 30 Rock so you can walk a block and say goodmorning to Matt, Meredith, Ann and Al, or ice skate. In addition, because of my mom's bday, they put a lovely chocolate cake in our room with a note from guest services welcoming us and wishing us a great stay in NYC and the Palace. I love the turn-down service at night. And I'm a light sleeper so really appreciated the clock on the night table having an option for white noise. We wanted for nothing, well except maybe for a couple more days.

title: “W Times Square”
text: We stayed at the W Times Square the weekend of Oct 25-29. It has a great location really close to all the touristy places to go. So, touristy there's no real NYers anywhere near there. Yea since the minute the door man opens your door you're surrounded by beautiful people. Really, I mean it there is not one unactracctive person employed there that has anyhting to do with the public. Thier service is good not great. The hotel itself is really modern. A little too dark for my taste. The rooms are kinda small and there are no drawers at all! You get a tiny closet and no drawers. Be prepared to live out of your suitcase. The view here is great especially if you get top floors. You can see a slice of the Hudson from almost all rooms. After staying there for 3 days I had to ask myself if it's really woth the $500+ a night. Im still wondering.

title: “Waterfront Location”
text: Spent two days at Baltimore Waterfront Marriott hotel and enjoyed our stay. The hotel is convenient to the tourist section of the Waterfront and Fells point. Upon our arrival the hotel staff was friendly and went out of their way to find us a room in spite of our early arrival. Our room was large with a fantastic harbor view. The bed was very comfortable but I didn’t sleep well, I could hear a humming noise and could not figure out where it was coming from. Both Waterfront tourist area and Fells Point (where locals hangout) are within walking distance and you should check them both out – very different. Food and drinks in Fells Point is half what you will pay at the tourist area. The Baltimore marathon put a damper on our plans; no tours were going due to the closing of the streets so we had to delay our trips to late afternoon. The hotel was packed however; we never waited long for the elevator or heard anyone in the halls or rooms next to us.

title: “Great Location Average Room”
text:
As other reviews stated this hotel is in a great location, just a few minutes walk from the Capitol, Union Station, Library of Congress, and Smithsonian museums. If you don't mind walking this is a great location. I did discover that staying just a little ways out of town most hotels had shuttles that were free and dropped me off without so much walking. If you come with a car you have to use the hotel parking. I didn't see anywhere else you could park. I spent three nights here and never did see any homeless people.
