Be warned the second floor is the ground floor and inside pool. So halls smell of chlorine. My room had a ground level window without bars that looked out onto a small alley/walkway. The curtains were see-through. I was a single woman traveler and did not feel safe but I couldn't get them to change my room. They must have trouble with getting enough staff for the weekend because I came back to my room at 3:30 PM on Saturday, my second night there, and it still hadn't been cleaned. 
I was disappointed in the room. As a Hyatt Regency I thought it would be nicer. Was smallest room I had on this trip. But it was clean. No tub just a shower. If you stay here be sure to book by calling them. I booked from their web site. But some friends booked by calling. They received free breakfast buffet for the same hotel rate. When I complained the staff said online booking was a different package. After some complaining they gave me the free buffet only because my friends’ rates included for up to 4 people and they were only 2. This is defiantly not a luxurious hotel, but very standard convention quality. I choose it because I got a great weekend rate of $119 a night. I'd probably look around for something else if I come to DC again.

title: “go hojo..................”
text:
i went to san diego with my friend it was sort of small trip. we stayed at howard johnson for 4 nights. it was nice to stay over there. they gave us good rate.the room was not enough spacious but it was quite clean and it was ok if you dont have too much baggage. in the room we had refrigerator, microwave, coffee maker, and also a safe. they got 7 HBO and showtime. free parking. in the morning they serve free breakfast and also free USA today. the location of the hotel was perfect with I-8 pass by and also it is quite near to san diego attraction. the hotel staff was nice and help us lot with directions. 
 in the back of hotel there was a pool and spa and also they got laundry. 
each day we got room service and they they also give us toiletry on asking for them. 
 i would like to stay at same howard johnson again as it was nice experience.

title: “Highly recommended”
text: The hotel is in a good location, with main routes through L.A. easily accessible and in a more commercial / residential area than a lot of hotels. The room was spacious (the bathroom was enormous) and both were clean. A buffet style breakfast is included in the room price and served in the lobby. If you bring a car with you, you'll need to pay the valet parking charge as there is nowhere in the vicinity to park your car on the road. The staff were courteous and efficient. I would definitely consider staying here again if I were to return to L.A.

title: “Great rooms and friendly staff”
text:
We loved this hotel for many reasons: very close to HOU airport, amazingly friendly reception (thanks, Paula!), huge rooms (loved the dividing wall between bedroom and living area, great for families where not everyone goes to sleep at the same time!), comfy beds, etc.
We would definitely stay here again!

title: “Look past reception”
text: No frills but big clean rooms and perfect location. Interior view but who needs it when you have Boston outside!

title: “Wonderful hotel - would definitely stay again”
text: There is not a lot to say about this hotel except that it shows how good American hotels can be. Staff were very welcoming, rooms big and beautifully decorated (mine had a nice view over a park), bathroom excellent, breakfast just about perfect and the gym and pool were brilliant.

title: “Disappointing Drake”
text: My husband and I stayed here over Easter weekend (also our anniversary) using our Hilton Honors points... chose the hotel for the ambiance, history and charm. Unfortunately, our experience was not what we hoped or expected. When asked for suggestions for brunch, the concierge produced a clipping from the Tribune (I prefer personal recommendations; anyone can read the Tribune!), the bathtub caulk was moldy, our air conditioner broke twice, and no turndown service was provided even though requested. Also, the walls were so paper thin, we heard our neighbors VERY clearly (especially on Easter morning when the neighbor kids got up at 6:30 a.m. to search for Easter Eggs in their room!) While not a horrible experience, it certainly wasn't what I expected from a stay at the famed "Drake."

title: “Average..expected more from the Hyatt.”
text:
I expected more since it was 'The Hyatt' 
 Food in center restaurant..poor. 
 Big Bar had nice decor, pricey
Room - clean, nicely decorated, bed and pillows were comfy
Bathroom - expected litte more, towels old, and worn could have been more plush.
Valet service - very helpful.
Front desk staff courteous.
Elevators - slow
Coffee shop - long line, warm soda

title: “Looks and feels like a budget boutique”
text:
We recently stayed for four nights at the Shoreham. I'd summarize this hotel as OK, but not really worthy of what I'd consider a 4-star boutique hotel. It aims to be a hip, modern hotel but with the obviously cheap materials (like the squeaky plastic headboards) and empty lobby bar, it's far from nice and hip. That said, if you can get a good rate, the location and friendliness of the Shoreham is fine.
After our first night, we requested a different room as we had a room that felt like one of the poorer rooms in the hotel. As it was on the 2nd floor and overlooked the interior of the building, we got an unpleasant view of bird poop and cigarette butts at eye-level. The massage chair was nice though. Our second room was on the 6th floor and seemed a bit nicer but I found both rooms to be on the unclean side. There was obvious "residue" on the toilet. I also found the beds to be on the uncomfortable/soft side. In our second room, the AC was really loud but we didn't mind as it provided some white noise to cancel out street noise.
Others have noted some of the perks here: the free wi-fi and espresso machine in the lobby are nice. The latter didn't work for me when I tried it, but there are good spots to get coffee nearby (Milk Bar on 56th, Zibetto Espresso Bar on 6th). 
Overall: I probably wouldn't stay at The Shoreham again. I prefer the Hilton Fashion District which often has comparable rates.

title: “Perfect Experience!”
text:
I can truly say say that my Peabody Experience was perfect, as expected we've been guests at the Orlando location and did not want to take a chance with another brand - worked out great. 
The Hospitality from the moment we arrived was excellent, each Peabody Associate that we interacted with was extremely caring and helpful.
Highlights included;
 - Breathtaking lobby
 - Mothers Day Brunch can't be beat
 - Accomodations were first class, the "upgrade" is something we'll never forget.
 - The Ducks will always be remembered, and the Duckmasters who were so professional and kind to my daughter who was an honorary duckmaster.
 - Cookies
 - On-site retail 
 - Roof top sunset 
Only regrets were that the roof top party's were not avaialble during our stay, and the concierge level happy hour selections were just average, except the cookies!
KKDWSKI

title: “Nice hotel...Great Location”
text: We chose Sofitel due to the location, which is perfect proximity if you want to be close to Times Square, Grand Central etc. The hotel was clean with a European vibe, thus "sofitel" branding. Our room was very spacious for nyc standards, and the washrooms had a separate tub/shower combination. We never ate at the hotel, other than ordering room service desert one evening, which was great. My husband ended up getting food poisoning after dinner one evening and there was a 24hr drug store right around the corner that I was able to scoot out to at 1am. Worth checking out...however see my review for this year's trip staying at the Eventi!

title: “a good mid budget offering in a central midtown location”
text: Dream was a pretty good hotel in Midtown. Pros: location, very comfy bed, very clean, friendly staff, good quality bathroom supplies (Occitane) Cons : Room a bit small (but fair size for the money by NYC standard), sad gym. A good solution for the mid range first time traveller to NYC who wants to be in the center of the action. Additional kudos because the hotel agreed to cancel at no charge part of our reservation last minute since we couldn't get there on time because of the bad weather.

title: “Basic, no frills but OK”
text: We stayed at the Wellington for two nights in late October. Due to an overbooking problem we were upgraded to a more deluxe room for this property - with a king size bed and a slight view of Carnegie Hall accross the street. Our room was spacious enough and bed was fairly comfortable. Room temperature controls did not seem to be connected to the heating/air condiitioning units and the room temperature seemed to fluctuate at its own will. The Wellington is in a very convenient location close to many famous sights. I would describe the hotel as well used as expected for such a centrally and convenient location. One front desk employee was especially helpful and efficient and another front desk staff was pleasant but seemingly overwhelmed and a bit bewildered. Overall however the service was satisfactory. The room rate was a good bargain for a Mid-town property. We will consider staying here again.

title: “Model of Excellence”
text:
What a great hotel. The staff need a special menion as without exception they appeared a very good team. From check in to breakfast staff and housekeeping to shuttle staff, they were all marvellous.
I woud be most comfortable staying here or several weeks!!
All the reviews are spot on. Do stay here if you are at DIA.

title: “Noisy, old and tired”
text: Easily the noisiest hotel I have encountered in decades. The hotel is deceiving as it has a beautiful entrance and lobby that looks brand new. However, this facade hides an old worn out hotel poorly constructed where noise abounds. They did have location as we were attending a wedding at the Karl Strauss Brewery just across the street.

title: “My favorite SeaTac hotel”
text: This is my favorite place to stay when I need to overnight at SeaTac for an early morning flight. The shuttle runs every 20 minutes, and the rooms are clean and comfortable. Free internet access in the lobby, and a nice wine selection at the bar. If you're up for the walk with your luggage, ask for a room overlooking the pond - and listen on the balcony to the frogs croaking through the night. And did I mention the chocolate chip cookies - waaarm chocolate chip cookies upon check-in. It's a bit more than I like to spend, but I enjoy it when I'm there. (EXCEPT - they say they're pet friendly, but with a $75 per night pet charge, I don't consider it "friendly" at all.)

title: “Everything was disappointing after the foyer...”
text:
Whilst I was initially impressed by the foyer that had been recently renovated to look like a modern, boutique hotel, everything after this was a total disappointment at the Capitol Skyline. 
We arrived tired and ready to enjoy a restful stay in a nice hotel with good service. We were welcomed by a long queue for the reception desk as there was only one staff member on duty and around 6 people waiting to be served. Eventually we were given our key and told how to get to our room (there was no concierge), so we made our way up to our Capitol view room. When we opened our door, we quickly realised that we had a pool view room. We then tried to log in to the internet but couldn't find any instructions on how to do so. In fact, there was no information in the room whatsoever. No booklet, flyer, pamphlet, not a thing! We called reception to complain about our room and ask about the internet and were told that the Capitol view rooms were all taken but we could have one on the next night if we wished. We were given a password for the internet but this was of no help as there was no internet signal in our room. We were not informed of any of these things when we checked in. Whilst the bed was comfortable and the room spacious, it was extremely dated and in stark contrast to the foyer. 
Feeling peckish, we decided to head down to the restaurant (no room-service) as we had seen the menu in the lift. When we got down there at 6:30pm, the restaurant was closed and when we asked at reception we were told that it was only going to be open for breakfast from now on. We were given instructions on how to walk to several average eateries 1km or more from the hotel and whilst we found one, it should be noted that we feared for our safety as we walked through the questionable surrounding suburbs. 
In the morning we went to breakfast which was included in our room- boiled eggs and pastries, most of which had run out. Again, in the restaurant there was only 1 staff member on to clear the tables, set the tables, replenish the food and take our breakfast tickets. 
I'll finish by saying that yes, the hotel is within walking distance to the Capitol building but be aware that it is not in a good part of town and does not have good restaurants or shops nearby.

title: “Hipness comes at a price”
text:
And in this case, it's not the nightly rate. It's the price of lack of warmth, lack of help, and mimimalist design that borders on austerity. 
I chose this hotel because it has very competitive rates when considering other mid-town hotels. It was also close to an event I was attending. There are other good things worth mentioning: cool, adjustable mood lighting in the rooms and an amazing shower that has multiple heads that you can position to shower you high and low. So what's my problem?
We were greeted by a desk person who was clearly having a few rough moments. When I put my garment bag on the counter, I was coldly informed that I was blocking the computer screen. After we were assigned a room, we wandered around looking for the elevators. We finally found them and took them to the 7th floor where we could NOT find our room number. We walked around the small hallways, trying to figure out whether we were on candid camera. We decided to return to the ground floor where the desk attendant was struggling with a large family, so we looked around and found another bank of elevators designated for room numbers that contained our room. Would it have been so hard to point in the direction of the correct elevators? I think not. 
The room was clean but very dark. Someone had sprayed a scent of some sort on the bed linens that was overpowering. Decoration was so very minimal - it left me cold. The bed wasn't the most comfortable, but not the worst. Would I return? Most likely not, despite all the positives.

title: “Vintage well located hotel”
text: We appreciate art deco, and this hotel had it in spades! From the lobby to the diner, to the fit-out of the rooms, it was all art deco. The room was definitely small and the bathroom tiny, but I have nothing to compare it to in New York. Everything worked and was comfortable, you could even open the window to get fresh air! The location was good, right near Madison Square gardens and Penn station. We got a package which included 2 tickets to the Empire State Building.

title: “Love it!”
text: I've stayed in several boutique hotels in San Francisco and the Chancelor is my favorite. It's clean and comfy. The rooms aren't as small as the other boutique hotels. In fact they have large walk in closets to keep all your luggage in. They give you a cute little rubber ducky, bath salts and a candy bowl. The location is perfect - walking distance to everything in Union Square and Bart. I found rates on-line for $69 - the best deal in the city. My only complaint...as with many hotels: not enough outlets for cell phone chargers, digital camera chargers and other stuff.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
We had been looking forward to spending New Year in New York for months and particularly chose the Hudson as we knew it had a good bar.
Although the communal areas are undeniably impressive, I think we would've been better off just visiting them and staying somewhere else. 
Our bedrooms were extremely small, not even big enough to get a full length view of your elf in a mirror (as you can't move far enough back without bumping into some furniture!) and not enough storage space. Also, for our whole 5 night stay our toilet was constantly flushing, despite us mentioning it to staff on many occasions.
The piece de resistance though was New Year's Eve. We had intended to at least have a few drinks in the Hudson Bar, if not bring in New Year in there, however we were disgusted to find out that there was to be a private party in ALL of the communal areas. The cost to get into this party was going to be over £180 for both of us. We could not believe that the Hudson did not even have one bar area for their paying guests. 
On the night itself, guests were made to feel most unwelcome and they even had bouncers checking your keys at the lifts. You really felt as though you should not be there.
Incidentally, we spent NYE at the W Hotel on Lexington Avenue, a hotel we had stayed in on our previous trip to NYC. THe W charged $10 entrance fee, which included access to their separate bar and their large hotel bar. The atmosphere was great and at midnight they came round and gave everyone a free glass of champagne, irrespective of whether you were staying there or not. The difference between the 2 hotels could really not have been greater and, unlike the Hudson, W were definitely not trying to rip you off.
We know which hotel we will be staying in next time!

title: “Great hotel close to all the city has to offer”
text: You don't have to go far to visit anything as the Essex hotel is so close to all that the city of Chicago has to offer..Its just a short walk from Lake Michigan and the views are lovely over the Lake. Helpful staff, but the room we had was a bit noisy when the traffic was full on into the evening...Although we were only on the 5th floor, so ask for a room higher up and maybe you wouldn't have this problem. Slept well though as the rooms were very spacious and we had 2 big comfy beds. Chicago is an amazing place and this is a good hotel to check it all out as about a mile or so from the real hussle aqnd bussle of the city.

title: “Wonderful new hotel, great service and food, excellent conference facilities”
text: This new hotel is a phenomenal choice for leisure and business travelers. I had the best food I've ever had during a business conference. Our suite, a parlor suite located on the 16th floor, was the best hotel room I've seen in a very long time. The suite was well-appointed, clean and neat. The bed, bathroom, toiletries, television, sound system, wave machine -- all were fantastic! I did not hear any noise from the amphitheater or shops across the street. Staff were very friendly and helpful, and the bellman remembered our names! I generally avoid downtown hotels, but this hotel was well worth the effort it takes to get there. All of the green features included in this hotel are a great addition to the usual Ritz luxury. Don't forget the fabulous pool and spa included for guests of the hotel.

title: “Can't beat the location”
text: Whether you are in town for business or pleasure, the Westin is a great location. Literally around the corner from the bars and restaurants of world-famous Beale Street. Our personal favorite: B.B. King's for good food and a great show. There are a lot of large and chain hotels within a few blocks, but the Westin is the closest to the action and is well kept. Starbucks on the premises, plus a restaurant. Garage parking next door.

title: “This hotel provides great customer service on a consistent basis.”
text: Whenever I arrive I am always greeted by Eduardo. Checking in is always easy and fast. Laura who works in the concierge lounge is always friendly. She remembers her hotel guests. Laura always remembers how I like my coffee and she ensures that the creamer I like to use is always available. Eduardo and Laura are both great assets to the Hilton family.

title: “Clean and safe hotel”
text: I reserved the room simply to be close to the HP Pavillion to see a concert. We were very surprised to find the hotel an excellent place to stay. The room was clean with all the basic necessities. Would recommend to anyone wanting to see a concert at the Pavillion.

title: “Thoroughly enjoyed our visit and will go back again”
text: Good sized room with fridge and all facilities and in a great area for restaurants, transport and bars etc. Free wi-fi and all day coffee. A new restaurant and bar is in process of being built. The existing breakfast area is not inviting as it uses part of the separate restaurant in the basement - no tableclothes and sometimes not enough seating. All in all to be well recommended for business or pleasure.

title: “the good, the bad and the ugly”
text:
This hotel has great potential. it has a beautiful location surrounded by water, But we felt like there was alot of mismanagement, especially in the restaurant. Most of the staff was o.k. but not exceptional. Out maid was a lovely women and took good care of our needs and the bar tender we met....another lovely woman, she is very good at her job, attentive and hard working.
The hotel itself feels like a good space, feels comfortable and looks pretty good, with of course some areas that just need some attention. The restaurant looks pretty good and has fabulous views. However we had an expensive meal the first night and it was awful. The sweet potato side dish should be banned from the earth, wow it was bad. The breakfast that came with the room package was good and we had a couple of other things in the bar that were good enough. we came to the conclusion that we should stay on the lower end of the menu. The price in the restaurant is far too high for the value, there are better restaurants that charge less fairly close by. the other thing we noticed is that there was never enough staff in the bar and restaurant. It was a holiday weekend, there were weddings and yet the bar was never open in the morning??? No Bloody Mary's or Mimosa's?? what a waste of opportunity. After traveling around the area we did like the location as it is a quiet neighborhood. we are unsure if we would go back to this hotel, but if we did we would avoid the restaurant except for breakfast.

title: “Really enjoyed our stay and will surely stay again.”
text: Any way you slice it up, this Doubletree was an excellent hotel for me and my family. It has an excellent location because you are in close proximity to just about everything. Our rooms looked just like new. It was a very clean and we were really impressed. All the staff members we encountered were pleasant and treated us great. The waitress that waited on us at the restraunt showed great enthusiasm for her job. The staff at the front desk was also very helpful and accomadating. My family and I had a great time there and my children were very upset when we had to check out to say the least. Keep up the great work!

title: “Like a Paris efficiency apartment in a glass box open on Manhattan”
text: Good design, great big bathtub with a view, pleasant work table with window that opens, literally, onto the city. Feels more like an apartment. Nice walking neighborhood, very friendly vibe.

title: “Long Queue, Bad Service, Faulty TV - Rip Off”
text:
After a 20 hour flight to have to camp in the lobby for 2 hours to get attended to by one of the 2 people on service for 40 waiting guests. Thje lobby looks wonderfull but this is only a scam hiding the fact that this hotel is run down and poorly maintained with incredibly bad service and cracked and peeling paint in the rooms. The TV was faulty and when i tried to complain there was no one to talk to.
This hotel has a captive audience with some of the airlines and therefore YOU are not inportant to them but as room fillers.

title: “Pure luxury. Good location, great views. Definately you get what you pay for.”
text:
Right at the top of the hill, but only a few blocks from Union Square and great shopping. The rooms were great with the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in. Bathrooms included separate shower and bath. Room had a desk and amazing view if the city.
Staff were great and helpful. I was there as part of a conference and the food we had was very good even when catering for a lot of people.
If you are staying there, it's worth getting a travel pass for the trolly's as it's a steep walk from union square, but a great location to explore from.
The Tonga Room is a must visit with great entertainments and drinks, even if our not staying at the hotel.

title: “Concierge Services”
text: Thought I should comment positively on the concierge, Dominic Alfonzetti, at The IC NY Barclay. He could not have been more gracious and helpful throughout our stay. Just a down to earth man who cared that the recommendations he gave for restaurants and theater were right for you. He was so personable, I felt like I was talking with a friend. The hotel, of course, is lovely, in a perfect location in the city, and classic NY. And thanks to Dominic, our trip was perfect.

title: “Not Bad”
text:
Stayed here for a whole week for a bowling tournament. There is no elevator, so we had to drag our balls up and down the stairs. Luckily, there were only 2 floors. The carpet needs to be replaced. But all in all it was clean and neat. The beds were soft and comfortable, the shower was powerful and never ran out of hot water, the supplied breakfast was a bit basic, but still nice. The staff was polite and helpful no matter what we asked them. 
It was right next to the highway, so commuting to the different alleys all over town was easy. I would recommend others to stay.

title: “Lovely Hotel - Great Service”
text:
The London is a wonderful boutique hotel in a perfect location. Each room is a suite withTV in each area and also free WiFi. Very good work desk and round table - perfect for meals (room service is fabulous and good selection). Comfortable seating area when with friends, too. Large well appointed bathrooms, robes, slippers, etc. Beds are very comfortable.
Wonderful restaurants in the area, but you do not need to go out because the two hotel restaurants are terrific. Close to MOMA, Central Park, shopping, theater. It is a few blocks from the Subway so it is easy to get downtown in a hurry. There is also a hotel car which and when it is available they will take you a reasonable distance. 
The staff is superb! They are ready to helping in every way and are knowledgeable. From the moment you arrive at the entrance you are made to feel at home. From check-in to housekeeping they take care of things smoothly and efficiently. If you had special requests for the room you can be sure that the items are there when you arrive or will be coming within 10 minutes. Ice machines on each floor so you do not have to call down for the basics. They can also bring in (very) small refrigerators (for drinks?) at no cost.
Concierge service is very good; be sure to ask them to book you into the Gordon Ramsey for a wonderful meal.
One thing to note is that the bedrooms only have bedside lamps so they are a bit darker than I like. I asked for a floor lamp and it was brought right away.

title: “Loved it”
text: My 17 yo son and I stayed here a couple of weeks ago. Very nice hotel. Staff very helpful. Definately would go back! Central location, near metro.

title: “Expensive with corrupt door staff”
text: Was at this hotel in July 2009 and ws impressed with the reception area of the hotel, rooms were quite small but didn't bother me much as i was afterall in New York and wouldnt be sitting around in my room often. Having paid 22dollars for a bottle of miller and a vodka lemonade i was awaiting my change when the young barman looked as if i was commiting a crime as he handed me my change and said "excuse me sir but you have to pay for gratitude services next time" I just looked at him and couldnt believe the cheek of it!! All he did was opened a bottle and poured a vodka? Also on my last day i was racially abused by some homeless, toothless black man outside the front door and the doorman stood and did nothing!! Also noticed some of the doormen getting tips from taxi drivers if they got them a fare which would cost abit of money. All in all new york is a great city but wouldn't stay at the hudson again, it seems to me that some of the staff just want dollars for doing as little as possible to help, however the staff on reception were very helpful when i needed them.

title: “Loved the room, great location!”
text: I really enjoyed this hotel. I prefer Marriott hotels and this Residence Inn is a good example of why. I originally had a one-bedroom/one-bath suite, but asked for an upgrade to a room with two bathrooms. The front desk upgraded us to a two-bedroom/two-bath suite. The suite was on the 26th floor and had several nice corner room views of the city. Overall, the room was a very comfortable, clean place to recuperate between sightseeing excursions, dining out, and going to a White Sox game. My bed was remarkably comfortable. The living room had a wall-sized picture window with a nice view of several of Chicago's skyscrapers. Breakfast was very good. Staff was friendly. I will stay here again!

title: “Excellent Hotel, Friendly Staff, Ideally situated in a fantastic location”
text: Hotel is situated within a stones throw of the beach. Ideally located close to some amazing resturants and vibrant bars. Rooms are clean and spacious with great views of the Pacific Ocean.

title: “PERFECT Location...PERFECT Service...PERFECT Comfort!”
text: LOVE this hotel! I initially picked this hotel because I had an early morning flight and the Detroit weather was questionable. I figured I could get a good night's rest before my trip and if there was a weather delay I would have a comfortable place to relax. I was fortunate with the weather as well as the hotel. I was greeted by an amazing front desk clerk and restaurant & bar staff that seemed excited to be spending their Christmas Eve servicing customers. The front desk clerk helped me with my boarding pass for the next day and changed my room to better meet my request of being close to an exit so I could easily go outside for a cigarette. The restaurant and bar staff weren't disgruntled over having to work on Christmas Eve but instead made the evening into a holiday atmosphere. I intend to use this hotel in the future for all my early morning flights and have already suggested it to friends and coworkers.

title: “Horrible receptionists who are obviously in the worng job!”
text:
Arrived after long long flight and nearly 3 hours at Customs at JFK to horrible receptionists who were completely disinterested After booking a superior room with 2 beds (I realise it is difficult in NY to specify beds but what's the point of the hotel saying this accommodation is available - you would go to one of the other hotels if hotel couldn't provide accommodate you were looking for) One of us had to sleep on a rollaway bed and tdesk staff old us to come back next day - we did and the next and the next and the next(were there for 10 days) each time we had to queue to speak to disinterested staff - because they had a corporate seminar going on they couldn't give us room with two beds. Receptionists worst I have encountered - frontline staff are one of the main marketing forces for any company but this lot failed miserably.
The superior room wasn't superior and I hate to think what the "normal" rooms look like - also room and surrounding corridor/halls very tacky and tired looking
The only plus was the restaurant and housekeeping staff who were all efficient and pleasant.

title: “Great Resort to Relax and Rejuvenate”
text:
I spent five days at the JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort in late April. Based on what I had read on TripAdvisor.com and based on information from a person in my office who had briefly visited the resort, I had some hesitation about staying here. I knew that it was in the middle of nowhere, and I also knew that it catered to large groups. Plus, I had the pleasure of staying twice at the JW Marriott Camelback Inn, both times for a business conference. I really enjoyed the Camelback and knew the experience at Desert Ridge would be quite different. However I got offered a package deal at Desert Ridge for a price that I couldn’t turn down and just wanted to relax in the desert for a few days
My first reaction was mixed. I checked in on a Saturday, and the place was busy, no doubt about it. It was hot and I was looking forward to a long swim, but the pools were crowded with kids. Plus, the one pool that seemed somewhat suitable for lap swimmers was closed for a special event. I asked the front desk if I could be comped to use the Spa pool, and they said fine. That was a nice bonus (and service proved to be excellent at the resort, during the course of my entire stay), since use of the spa facilities cost $25 at a minimum. The pool was beautiful, but I still felt it in no way compared to the spa pool at the Camelback.
Despite my initial mixed reaction, the place grew on me day by day. The Desert Ridge is the largest hotel in Arizona, but to me, it didn’t feel that way. The architect did a great job of making the resort seem like a manageable size. There is still quite a bit of walking to do, but not nearly as much as some of the big Vegas hotels. The hotel was pretty full over the weekend (and less so as the week went on), but for the most part, the restaurants, pool, and area by the pool never seemed congested. There were a couple of big groups there, but they never bothered me.
Rooms were quite large size and were very cheerful. The bathroom were large too, with a separate marble tub and shower. There were some quirks with the rooms: there seemed to be a waste paper basket only in the bathroom and not by the desk as well ; the shower leaked, unless you positioned the showerhead in a certain way, and there was no way to turn the light on the balcony off, meaning you had to completely close the curtains to get to sleep. But these complaints are relatively minor and in no way subtract from the great overall experience at the hotel.
I only ate at the Blue Sage, the casual restaurant. Great burgers at lunch and dinner; breakfasts was good, but not great. Prices were on the high side, but I’ve seen them higher elsewhere. However, unlike a lot of other resorts, you are not locked into eating only at the overpriced restaurants on the property. A short way from the hotel is an outdoor mall with a good food court, an Albertsons supermarket, Einstein Bagels and a bunch of casual restaurants including On the Border Café and California Pizza Kitchen. This really gives a guest a lot more options, in term of food. For those without a car, I think the hotel runs shuttles to this mall, and if it’s not scorching hot, it’s probably not a bad walk.
The best feature of this hotel for me was the beautiful two-level lobby and outdoor patio area, as well as the beautiful pool area. The resort was extremely conducive to relaxation. While it is true, that Desert Ridge is somewhat isolated and away from the heart of the action in Phoenix, I found it fairly easy and quick to get around by car, and since I’ve been to Phoenix many times, I preferred staying close by the hotel. By the end of my stay, I was dreading having to leave and return to the real world. In summary, I highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Clean Room, Great Management, Will Definitely Stay Again”
text: The management/owner of this hotel was extremely helpful, competent and friendly. We had a somewhat confusing check-in situation and he knew exactly what to do was was extremely courteous. We stayed three nights, checking in on a Friday, leaving on Monday. The room was extremely clean and looked recently remodeled. I was impressed with the energy efficiency of the hotel. You have to place your room key in a card slot near the door to activate the lights so when you leave, the lights automatically shut off. Everyday we were there, we saw the owner working around the business and he always asked if everything was ok and if we needed anything. The location of the hotel is great. It's right on Pacific Coast Highway and was centrally located to all the places we needed to be. The only complaint I have is the parking lot was rather small with tight spaces. It was a little hard to park the car. Overall, the quality of customer service received is the main reason I will definitely choose this hotel again in the future.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I stayed at the Crowne Plaza Philadelphia West for three days in mid-August. I was very pleased with the facility and the service. The room was well furnished and the bed was comfy. I ordered room service twice and the food was actually hot when it arrived. I had breakfast and lunch from their buffet and was pleasantly surprised at the quality and service. I would stay here again.

title: “great choice”
text: centrally located, nice size room especially for nyc. 2 queen beds and extra space in the room. The employees were very cordial. I would stay her again.

title: “2nd trip to the hotel”
text:
We stayed here for the 2nd time in August of this year. While we love the location, service was not as great this time as far as our free gift from mentioning the secret word and it being our anniversary. 
We requested early check in and while I know they never can promise it, we still had to wait on a room. It was not ready still at the usual check in time so they put us in a different room. When I asked if it was still a corner room the lady at the desk said yes however we got up there and it was not. We would rather they just be honest, leaves a bad taste in your mouth when you get the run around several times, it was almost like they did not know what to say.
If you are looking for a great steak dinner Ruths Chris is the place to go, the steak melts in your mouth!
Regardless, the hotel itself and the location is great so we will be returning next year for another game.

title: “Absolutely brilliant hotel. Top class with a warm welcome!”
text: I don't usually write hotel reviews but really felt I had to this time. Looking for a hotel in New York was always going to be a little challenging with our small budget, so when we read about the Affinia Manhatten on TripAdvisor and saw how reasonable the rates were, we thought it could be too good to be true. It certainly wasn't! It was amazing. I'm not just saying that. From the welcome we received to the customer service in the restaurant and bar, nothing was too much trouble for the friendly staff. I loved our room too - very clean and comfortable and very quiet with no street noise, even though the hotel was right in the thick of it. Location wise - the Affinia was spot on. The Empire State Building, Times Square and Grand Central are all within easy walking distance and it felt very safe, even late at night. My parents haven't been to NYC yet and I'm trying to encourage them to go. I'd definitely get them to book this particular hotel because they'd love it too. Thanks to everyone at Affinia. I loved everything about your fantastic hotel. And wow! What an entrance hall!

title: “Delightful stay at a lovely hotel!”
text:
My fiancee and I spent 5 nights at the W San Diego this past December. We've both stayed in a lot of hotels, and I've stayed in 3 different W's. This was by far my favorite of those 3 W hotels and one of my most favorite hotels in general. I feel many of the negative reviews here are off-base, I'll explain further at the end of this review.
First off, W hotels are modern-chic hotels with tasteful decorations, large lobby areas, luxurious rooms with extra comfortable bedding, and signature bars/restaurants. The San Diego location is no exception. The oversized multi-story lobby area is shared with a small bar and has lots of comfortable seating, and during the day projectors play different soothing scenes on the wall above the bar.
The hotel is centrally situated a few blocks from the restaurant-filled "Gaslamp district" in one direction, a few blocks from the waterfront in another, and about 12 blocks from the highway in a third direction. Besides the Gaslamp area and the restaurants in the hotel, there are several small eateries in the area immediately around the hotel.
The colors and decor of W San Diego are marine-themed and the bed and bedding were as comfortable as every other W I've been in. Luxurious fluffy down pillows, comforters, etc. A very nice bathroom, electronics, and furniture completed the effect. A small chalk board is a cute touch, and their loungey theme CD playing in the room when we walked in was also very nice.
The multiple bars and lounges in the hotel are popular; we arrived on a Saturday night and the lobby lounge was full of beautiful lounge-goers drinking expensive cocktails. We felt underdressed and dirty in the travel garb we had been wearing for the last 8 hours but quickly showered and changed and joined the beautiful people for dinner and drinks ourselves.
Service was impeccable. Very fast check-in, nice staff, polite and helpful valets and bartenders. The airy fitness center has an opening to the outside overlooking the pool and is available 24 hours. The latency of the in-room internet connection was very good as was its speed.
Now, to address the complaints that make for the see-saw rating on this hotel. I feel some people don't bother to read what W is about before staying here, and expect red-suited bellhops and obsequious doormen for this price range. However, this hotel is catering to the clientele that doesn't want all of that, and instead wants fashionable, chic, modern, efficient, and beautiful. W hotels including this one are NOT old-style hotels with fawning staff and floral bedspreads. For that sort of ambience, look elsewhere. If "hip" is something you want to replace, rather than be, this isn't the hotel for you.
A number of people have complained about lack of food in the immediate vicinity; these people apparently didn't go outside the hotel. There were at least 5 eateries within 1.5 blocks of the hotel, including Thai, and two deli/coffee-shops. The north end of the Gaslamp district is maybe a 10 minute walk away if you move slowly. The hotel's area is choice: not so close to the action as to be noisy, but close enough to get there quickly.
All of the staff we dealt with were helpful, efficient, and pleasant. Absolutely no complaints from our stay.
Minor quibbles with the hotel:
- Really expensive valet parking ($35 a day or so), but it does give you in and out as often as you want. All the major downtown hotels in S.D. charge like this, so this isn't W's fault. There's cheaper self-park nearby, IF you plan to come and go only once a day.
- Expensive food and drink. Not at all unexpected in a mainline hotel, and the drinks were normally priced for a lounge environment so not a quibble as much as an observation.
- Restaurant food was good but uneven, some dishes were stand-out, others were pretty but uninspired. Not surprising in trendy restaurants, but be prepared. Breakfast was very substantial and very good.
I would happily stay here again.

title: “Location, Location, Location!!!!!”
text: Don't tell too many people about this fantastic hotel right in the middle of it all!! Sure, it's old - you can tell by the plumbing in the bath - but it's clean. The lobby is nice - designed by the same architect as Radio City Music Hall - it is elegant with it's beautiful marble and magnificient chandeliers. But the very best part is that you can literally walk out the front or the back doors of the hotel and walk straight across the street into several theatres. It is 1/2 block from the tickets booth and just 1 1/2 blocks from Lindy's and Joe's Steakhouse. It is reasonably priced by New York city standards. Spent a few days there in July and thoroughly enjoyed the accommodations and the friendly and helpful staff.

title: “Great Midtown location”
text: Spent two nights here. Nice lobby without "through traffic.' I asked for a quiet room and was given one that did not directly face the street. However, as we walked down the hall towards the room, we could hear a child screaming loudly in the adjacent room. I called the desk and was immediately given a room on a high floor that was very quiet. No fuss or argument, no delay. Ditto no problem with late checkout. Nice restaurant and bar. Room itself was very good with kitchenette area including microwave, sink and minifridge. Would be very happy to stay here again.

title: “One of the worst hotels ever”
text:
This hotel is dishonest, dirty and unsafe. It's set up like an apartment complex with low lighting and its in a very grungy area.
First you cant find the place. No signage. After mapquest failed us we called the hotel and the clerk gave us WRONG directions.
After finally finding the place ,there were "thugs" in the parking lot blarring their stereos when we pulled up. I should have known then to go someplace else. 
They say they have wifi on website but they do not .
They have land lines and the entire time the internet did not work.
They say they have a pool but it was full of green sludge and was 
half covered and obviously completely unusable.
The A/C unit did not work. The sheets were stained. The rooms are "non smoking" and both rooms smelled strongly of smoke.
This is after being changed rooms twice this is the best room they had. Give me a break. The only decent thing about this hotel was the free breakfast. 
Not only would I NOT recommend this hotel. I would emplore people to find a cleaner, safer place to stay.
My two cents

title: “More on the Moore”
text:
There's not much more I can add to the other reviews, other than to say that our stay was equally satisfying. I used to live in Seattle so I didn't need travel help from the staff, but they were always pleasant over the phone and in person.
I love the location because I could walk to Pike Place each morning and watch them set up the market. It's also great to be able to walk to Bell Town restaurants and the Space Needle.
The room was funky and the hotel is a bit cavernous. We had a claw foot tub with a shower - the hot water was so weak that I never added cold when I took a shower - but it was just warm enough to be comfortable. We were serenaded awake each morning by seagulls - something that would not be as much of a problem if we'd had the window closed.
But overall, it's a good place to stay and I would definitely stay at the Moore again.

title: “We expected more...”
text:
To start my review I have to express that the hotel isn't bad at all. Especially the views on the Central Park are amazing and the hotel product is still new.
However, not just because of the management by MO but also due to image of the hotel had been dissapointed by our stay. The rooms has been nice with sound system for your ipod and books for bedside reading. And the view has been more than great. But the bathroom has been a joke for a new built hotel. It has been too small, not well designed and sparely equipped with amenities (e.g. just one bath gel and shampoo for bath tub/ shower).
The pool area and the gym reminded us on a community swimming pool. No space for sun chairs, the sauna has been right in the pool area, no changing rooms nor relaxation areas. It made the impression that they just built a pool to have it on the checklist.
Next critical service has been the business centre: they just converted a suite/ room into the business centre by palcing some desks/ PC's in an empty room. No atmosphere which nevertheless will be charged with 25$ for use.
Contrariwise the restaurant Asiate serves excellent food as well as a great atmosphere for breakfast. Definitely a place to spend an evening in style with great service and food. Thanks to the different levels nearly all tables having the same great view on the Central Park and NYC.
Overall we just missed the small things which separates a deluxe hotel from a regular five star hotel. And in terms of service the MO didn't reach the level of the Peninsula or Ritz.

title: “Avoid this hotel”
text: We were very dissappointed with this hotel. It was dark and dingy and the lobby floor was dirty. We did find however that the staff here was friendly and very nice. The room was clean but very much needed a remodeling. The pictures on the wall were very dated and the hallways dark and poorly lit. Would never stay at this property again and would not recommend it.

title: “small hiccups don't stop it from being a great experience”
text:
My sister and I stayed at this hotel for three nights during a nyc/dc memorial day break. We really, really enjoyed it!
If you stay at this hotel, you have to be looking for a certain type of experience. I wouldn't call this a business hotel, but it is cute and different and quirky. The coffee every morning is great and the bar/restaurant area is quite nice. 
The rooms are a bit dated, but that is part of the fun! My only real complaints on the rooms would be the air conditioning - it really never quite cooled the room. I understand it is a converted apartment building, but the pre-war heating/cooling system does not do the job. We had to leave the curtains completely closed (and warn housekeeping not to open them!) in order to not sweat the minute we entered the room. In the summer, you may want to think twice about staying here.
Oh, and a small thing - the robes, though cute, were scratchy from being washed too many times. 
The location is fairly good. It is about four blocks form Dupont Circle metro and only a few blocks from the white house. very nice for tourists, though get a map!
the staff was overall very friendly - seemed kind of young and on the fly, but friendly. One staff member did hold a personal call for about two minutes while I was waiting, but that is really just a nitpicky complaint. She was helpful.
look at the pictures - they don't lie. if it looks fun, you will really enjoy this spacious and funky hotel! oh, and free internet!

title: “Too bad it's above a nightclub!”
text: What a great place to stay - terrific location, reasonable rates - but please believe the others who reviewed this and mentioned the nightclub below! Maybe it's different during the week - we were there on a weekend - but the thumping, music, screaming, etc. went on until the club closed. If you can sleep through anything or will be at the nightclub until closing, this is the hotel for you. If not, stay elsewhere.

title: “Close to Denver Airport”
text: This was a great stop close to the airport and very affordable. The restaurant was impressive and reasonable. The shuttles are free to the airport and the bar seemed busy. Great staff too.

title: “fancy”
text: this is a fancy hotel within reasonable walking distance of the white house. it's a good find for people who want to see all the landmarks.

title: “Great stay from 10/11-10/14”
text: My wife and I celebrated our 10th ann. by visiting NYC. Never staying close to Times Square before during previous visits, we decided to try something new.......she chose Hotel Mela and it was a great pick for a place to stay in that area. Needless to say, but with great weather we were not in the room too often, however, it was such a nice place to return in the late evening and relax. The bed was very comfortable.....King size and the room it self was perfect for the 2 of us. She got a special deal, via the net, on the price, for three nights we paid 1119.00 (includes taxes, etc.) and for that area and time of the year we felt we had a good deal when comparing prices that seemed average and others were much higher for what appeared inferior............or ''over the top" places in the area that ranged from 500-700 a night. I would highly recommend the Hotel Mela. The staff was very helpful and thanks to John Paul, the concierge, for setting up the room for our arrival in a tasteful, 10th wedding ann. style, that my wife appreciated. Great location, staff and room!

title: “Good hotel, great bed”
text: Just a quick shuttle from the airport. The impressive lobby has a sunken bar. Rooms are nice with great french toiletries. I love the single serve coffee makers with Wolfgang Puck coffee and the great beds with fluffy pillows. Airport shuttle service was on time.

title: “Great Place!”
text: We booked this hotel for 2 nights while staying for my daughter;s graduation from Loyola College in Maryland. When we arrived, we found the hotel was in a shady area, but the hotel itself was very nice. The loby was beautifully decorated, and the front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. They even watched the Preakness with us on the lobby TV. Room was great, extemely comfy beds, great shower, everyhting was clean and up to date. Bathroom was small, but clean and had a great shower and sink area. There was also a small refriederator located in the dresser, which came in handy with 4 unfinished meals from La Scala in Little Italy. The breakfast area was nicely decorated, and the breakfast itself was normal, featuring Holiday Inn Express's Signature Cinnamon Buns, Coffee, Breakfast Drinks, Sausage, Eggs, Bagels, Muffins, Yogurt, etc. There is a well-equipped fitness center with 2 wide screen flat-panel tv's, and a business center with 2 computers and a printer/copier. The pool area was nice, but closed. Ypu have to pay for parking, but the lot is pretty secure. It is fenced in, and a room key is needed to access it. The exit uses a motorized gate. Although there was a homeless man wandering around when we checked out. I would highly reccomend this hotel for business travelers and budget travelers to the Baltimore area. Remember, the hotel is in a bad area, so I wouldn't walk anywhere from there. Otherwise, everything was GREAT!

title: “Over 100 room nights, but...”
text: Over the last two years I've probably spent three or four months worth of nights at The Palace. The primo Midtown location is unbeatable, and the rooms have it all. Enough space to sit and relax, plenty of desk space, total control over lighting and temp from a cool bedside master unit, and a bed that's as comfortable as it gets. The problem is in the public spaces. The WiFi is free in the cramped lobby area, so all the leisure guests hang out there (often sitting six or seven deep on the sofa) with their iPads or computers. Istana, the lobby restaurant, doesn't serve food later in the day. So if you want a sandwich in the afternoon or early evening, you've got to find another option. That's one reason why so many guests are seen hauling in bags of food from surrounding deli's. It could also be the oppressive room service rates. I've often paid more in service charges than for the food itself. You can't order anything without incurring these huge charges, and it makes you embarrassed to order in your room, no matter how convenient it would be. So much about this hotel is so right; I wish they could address these few annoyances.

title: “horrible”
text:
If you stay here you will be treated like DIRT from the desk clerks, you will get double billed on your credit card, and this hotel will charge an extra $9.95 as a destination fee which is not tax and is probably illegal. 
NEVER AGAIN.

title: “Perfect Boutique Hotel Steps Away from Times Square”
text:
I had such a positive experience at the Muse. From the moment you walk in, you feel welcomed. After a very nice chat with the folks at the front desk, we whisked away to our room which was extremely comfortable and homey. The spacing in the room made it feel like we were in our little cozy NY apartment and we settled right in.
The restaurant and lounge had a huge wine selection and although we didn't get to dine in or enjoy their daily wine reception, the menu and atmosphere looked great and we really wish we had!
One of the best parts of the stay was the incredibly thoughtful surprise that Lizardo, the front office supervisor, left for us to come home to. It was a beautiful cheese plate, bottle of red wine and a personalized Muse chocolate treat. It was so unexpected and so appreciated!
Check out with Ray, the front office manager, was a cinch and when there was a mistake on the bill it was corrected immediately and not made a big deal of. 
The location couldn't be better being steps away from Times Square and a short cab/metro ride to everything! I would suggest to anyone to stay here and hope that I can make my way back up to NYC soon to stay at the Muse.

title: “Best view in the city”
text: We stayed at the JW Marriott for one night this past weekend. I was impressed by how quickly I was greeted by the staff at the front desk and the quick check-in. We stayed on the 25th floor and had a spectacular view of the city. The bathroom was quite luxurious at first, but the door into the bathroom and shower door can make it a bit awkward to use, and the toilet paper holder is not easy to use as well. The room was quite spacious and had very contemporary decor. I felt that they did cut corners in quality of decor and furniture around the room. The mattress was firm and made it difficult to sleep peacefully through the night. My husband slept perfectly, and I understand that this may be different for everyone. The office chair was already showing some wear and tear, and the decor seemed cheap. JW could have put a little more effort into the quality in the rooms for being a luxury hotel, but it was overall a pleasant stay. I would stay again at a reasonable rate.

title: “Great Chicago hotel for families”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights over March Spring Break week with two young children, ages 4 and 7. This was a nice, clean hotel in a busy downtown area with an indoor pool close to kid-friendly restauarants.
The hotel room was newly remodeled and very nice and clean. There was an in-room safe, coffee maker, 2 large double beds, closet area, and a small sized bath with shower/tub. Staff were very nice, cleaning staff were always seen around the hotel keeping things clean. Coffee, tea, and granola bars are available in the lobby, and we saw a concierge desk staffed during the day. The hotel restaurant is a pizza place/bar at night and serves breakfast in the morning. Food was fine there, but service was very slow all 3 times we went. Parking is free with unlimited in/out privileges, which was a huge selling point for us as parking is very expensive downtown. 
The hotel is about 5 blocks walk from Michigan and the more touristy shopping district. It was about a 15-20 minute walk to American Girl Cafe. Directly across the street is a 50s-style McDonalds, on the corner is the Rainforest Cafe and Hard Rock Cafe. A 24-hour Walgreen's is 3 doors down, across from the Hard Rock, and this is a great place to get any toiletries you may have forgotten to pack or drinks, food, or snacks for your room. We stocked up on bottled water each morning there before treking off to the museums.
As another reviewer explained below, the hotel is actually 2 buildings connected on one floor. To reach the pool, lobby, or restaurant from the one building, you have to take 2 elevators and walk a bit down a hall between them. Other than that slight inconvenience, this was a great hotel in a good location for a good price. We got a very good rate at the hotel's website, but noticed the rate doubled about a month later. The pool was very busy the first time we used it, but the second time it was completely empty.

title: “More for your money”
text: This was my first experience with a Jameson Inn & it was great! Just an overnight stay, but this 2-star rated hotel was better than some 3-satrs. Staff was helpful when I needed to print a couple pages - let me use the front dest computer/printer. I overnight in the Jacksonville area twice a year & this will be my preferred hotel for future Jacksonville stays.

title: “Fabulous Hotel”
text: This place was fantastic! Excellent staff, very nice rooms with great view of the city. Its location on the Riverwalk is great. My two daughters age 6 and 10 loved the pools, especially the roof pool, it was neat swimming 23 floors up! It is also nice to have the big sign on top of the building, it kept me from getting lost around downtown since I could just look up and find the hotel. I look forward to going back. I travel a lot for business and hate staying at hotels, you know the feeling if you travel a lot, but this place was relaxing and enjoyable for me. Loved the happy hour every evening too. Free wireless internet. Parking is $18 a day valet with in/out privileges. I felt it was worth the cost.

title: “No Liquor, But still a great Hotel”
text: Kudos to the staff, you're awesome! Once I learned of the Liquor Laws of Mass I wasn't upset except that the bar prices are high and not in line with the guest experience of what is FREE at other properties. Either disclose upfront on the booking sites or consider that we are in -house guests and give us a break on cocktail hour. Six dollars for a bottle of beer is not guest friendly and a $25.00 hamburger is out of line for captive, tired and weary guests. Spent 4 nights at the property and everything was the quality that I have learned to accept as Embassy standard,the missing liquor and no mini bar in my room was a disappointment that you could change if you chose to, it's not always about the bottom line once you hoodwink the guest and offer no other choices. Price determines what and where we purchase, you won't get me again if I come to Boston.

title: “NGWeinberger”
text:
Absolutely marvelous experience; my single Queen came w a suite, wonderful desks; computer hook ups and plenty of outlets 
For charging iPads and cell phones; lovely breakfast, snacks and wines w crudités and cheese in evening; feels as if one I'd in an exclusive private condo- will always use this hotel- comfort in everyway. Bath spacious and several magnifying mirrors.

title: “Very nice place for the price”
text:
Plus +
1. Late check in available and the front desk clerk is extremely sweet.
2. The room was clean, bedsheet clean, nice tv and cable.
3. Large room, clean rug, clean towels. 
4. Plenty of soap and shampoo
NEGATIVES:
1. No Iron
2. No hot water only warm 
3. PARKING IS SCARY AND NO SECURITY GUARD, I REPEATEDLY ASKED THE FRONT DESK CLERK IF MY CAR WAS SAFE OUT THERE.
4. No room service
OVERALL I HAD A GOOD NICE STAY.

title: “Great location”
text:
Stayed here for two nights in mid September. Hotel is well located to all the shops and Chinatown. Cab fare to Fisherman's wharf is about $10 otherwise jump on one of the very crowded cable cars. Rooms are small but this city is so great, so dont waste your time sitting inside for too long.
Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Location”
text:
The Hotel Solamar is located in the Gaslamp area of town. Though it provides quick access to the bustling area of town, as well as the ballpark (we could see the ballpark from our windows) it is set off enough from the action. 
We did not experience any issues noise wise though could certainly see how rooms that front on the popular night spot that is the rooftop bar/pool could be quite noisy. 
Our room was clean and spacious (with a nice seating area and large bathroom) and the staff was most welcoming and helpful. The hotel had the usual Kimpton perks (wine and cheese hour in the evening, plush animal print robes, excellent selection of snacks in the mini bar)

title: “Wow, the staff here is so well trained and professional”
text: We stayed here for a three day golf experience. The total staff here is unbelievable. Great service, really interesting food, great golf staff, and an overall well-trained and focused group of employees who "get it" about customer service and support. We stay in a lot of high and middle level hotels and resorts and this is one of the best because of a well-trained staff and an overall positive group of people. We highly recommend this resort.

title: “Quiet, Comfortable & Clean”
text: I stayed at Affinia Gardens for a total of 5 nights. Take in mind while staying in New York you are going to have to deal with a high median in certain areas and Upper East Side is one of them. However for Affinia Gardens, considering it's location, the rate I was able to get was very attractive. I had actually booked a hotel at another location and then contacted Affinia Gardens which was closer to Lenox Hill Hospital and by which gave me an offer that I could not refuse. So let's get the negatives out the way first. The internet. I don't know how many reviews have to be written for this company to consider changing the way it provides internet service. It's really sad when you can go to Starbucks and get free internet yet to access internet in this hotel you will have to pay $14.95 for 24 hours, $62.95 for one week and if you by chance happen to stay for 1 month, (doubt anyone will) you will have to dish out $245.95. Now I don't know about you but I've stayed at many hotels before, with most having free internet (most recent B&B Carmine in Augusta, Italy), and very few charging. We live in the year 2012 and if hotels are going to provide this service, especially when your rooms are going to cost you over $400 a night, (for me it was a bit cheaper due to government rates) you should not have to pay. You do have the option of accessing the internet from Affinia's business room but that will cost you as well, $5.95 for 15 minutes. It's unfortunate that I had to take up this much of the review discussing internet. Anyways in all fair judgement I can not base my review upon internet solely the staff was very friendly & welcoming, (select few should probably smile more) & the rooms were bigger then average for a New York hotel. Everything was very clean except the floor in the bathroom could have been cleaned a little better because you could see how the dirt had built up in between the cracks but everything else was pretty much spotless. If you are also flying in from JFK or other surrounding airports the hotel offers it's own cab service to and from the airport but you would obviously have to notify them a head of time and inquire into the availability of this service. I paid $75 to get back to JFK from the hotel. A regular cab would have cost me $52, plus $6.50 toll and gratuity for the cab driver which varies upon how well you think the driver was which should be at least $5+ if going that far. I took the comfort in knowing I was going to have a cab waiting and went ahead and probably paid a little more for the hotel cab. Now to some extent you are going to have to deal with car horns in New York, (honking more then twice should be banned) so considering this when I say the area Affinia Gardens was in was quiet I'm comparing this to other parts of New York and in all honesty I slept great minus the ear plugs. Overall my experience here was very nice. My number one thing is, "Is the staff friendly?" and "Are the rooms clean?" and Affinia Gardens more then exceeded my expectations. I would stay here again for sure and probably make Affinia my first choice however, I would inquiry into whether or whether not this internet situation had improved. Thanks for the comfortable stay.

title: “Service was unbelievable”
text:
I will get to the room review in a second..but first wanted to talk about the service....outstanding from start to finish...personal note in my room, valet service was speedy and friendly! I left my iPhone charger in the car, so they said they would retrieve it for me (and did within minutes). Staff were helpful in recommendations, and even e-mailed me a few prior to my arrival.
In terms of the hotel...yes it's an old reconditioned hotel (old bathtub, small bathroom), but they made the best of the layout, it's quiet, the bed is super comfortable, and the reno is funky and cooll. Coffee Service in the morning, wine reception in the early evening...super close to Union Square and Chinatown (and a Starbucks across the street). One of the better hotels I have stayed in during travels to San Francisco!

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: This hotel was our first one in a 5 week holiday and it was great. We had a fantastic LARGE corner room, with great views of the city streets from our window and only 1 block away from the Whitehouse. So close to everything, good food in house or just around the corner. HIGHLY RECOMMEND TO ALL.

title: “never again”
text: Worst hotel I've ever stayed at. Very outdated, rude and uninformed employees and right next to the airport so all we heard were planes taking off and landing the entire time...

title: “Our favorite place to stay near LAX”
text:
Excellent location for LAX !!!!!!!!!! Great Greek Restaurant!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Clean,Comfortable,Quiet, slept well

title: “Very convenient airport hotel”
text:
I spent the night between flights and found the Westin to be very comfortable. Room was spotless and beds where fabulous with a great nights sleep.
Dining options worked well with lobby bar happy hour and restaurant.
A very easy return to the airport.

title: “Dated but good value/location”
text:
This hotel is obviously long in the tooth (for a ~ 30 yr old hotel) but still a good value and comfortable. Get a corner room if you can; great views and roomy.
We've stayed here 3 or 4 times in the last yr. The a/c is weak, but works ok. The bathrooms are small and simple, by today's standards, but adequate. The health club has ok equipment but is in serious need of upgrading. We stayed there primarily on wknds and given that the rate was ~ less than $100/day, we considered it a very reasonable choice. Great location/near SMU.

title: “Clean, convenient, great value for San Francisco”
text: My husband and I stayed at Marina Inn for four nights, three at the beginning of our vacation and one at the end before we flew out of San Francisco. While our rooms were small and very basic, the hotel was very clean and was exactly what we expected after reading other reviews. We were only in our room to sleep, and value was more important than luxury. It was perfect for us. While our first room was facing Lombard and was quite noisy at night due to that being a very busy street, we're both great sleepers so it wasn't a problem. Our second room faced Octavia and was much quieter. If noise is an issue for you, request a room facing Octavia. The staff was also a great help to us with figuring out transportation and directions in the city. We have nothing but good things to say about Marina Inn!

title: “LOVELY VISIT”
text:
My mother and I were exhausted when we arrived and Mohammed at reception went out of his way to make us feel welcome. That was much appreciated. Our room was lovely with very comfortable beds.
The location was perfect and we were able to get to all the places we anted to see very easily.
It felt like home every time we came back to the New Yorker and we would definitely stay there again. We visited shortly before Christmas and the lobby looked so festive!
The Tic Tock Diner and the Bar served up great food.
Many thanks.

title: “Spectacular!”
text: This hotel is gorgeous, inside and out. Our room was beautiful and spacious with one entire wall as a window. Spa-like bathroom with separate bathtub and shower, and two Frette robes and slippers. Room service dinner was delicious and the service was swift and impeccable. Best of all was the bed though - easily the most comfortable bedding I've had the pleasure of sleeping on. The only downside was having to check-out and return to normal life! Would definitely stay there again...permanently.

title: “Classic and comfortable. Wonderful restaurant (Juno). Beautiful origional architecture and decorated to match in an 1900”
text: Staff is friendly and professional. Check in and out was efficient. Rooms are great. Love the lounge. They specialize in Absinth if you're in to that. The bartender wears a white tux which goes with the classic 1930's (?) decor. Think rich man's private club.

title: “You call that a 4 star?!?”
text:
When I booked a 4 star hotel I was expecting so much more. I believe the hotel was nice at one time but this hotel needs serious renovations. Honestly I've stayed in nicer Holiday Inns. What kind of 4 star hotel doesn't have WiFi? They did have a cable hook up for a premium rate. 
I booked through priceline so I got the hotel for $115 a night. They failed to mention the $22 for parking or the $35 for valet parking. 
Now that I've complained enough, I'll talk about the good things. The location was great. If you plan on spending most of your time on the RiverWalk, you'll love the location. The people were very nice. Traffic was a bit noisy. They forgot to charge us for valet parking. We asked them about it and they said not to worry about it. 
Let's just say that with all the discounts that I received, I don't have too much to complain about BUT if I had paid full price... I'd be ripping on this hotel. I know Paris Hilton would never stay here.

title: “Overpriced paradise”
text:
Myself and a peer stayed at Paradise Point with our families while in San Diego on a business trip July 24 - 28th. We were referred here by our travel agent because it had a kids program that my kids (7 & 9) could stay at while I was in meetings. 
While the property was very pretty, it was not worth the $300 a night! The rooms were ok but nothing to write home about. The refridgerator knob was broken and it froze our drinks. A light bulb was missing over the bathroom vanity (which is very small) and I killed two spiders in the bathroom. The beds however were comfortable. My co-worker had no chairs on their patio. When they called about it they expected they would bring out nice chairs like the other patios had - they brought $5 plastic chairs. They were disappointed for the money they spent and value they recieved.
Plus a $16 a night parking fee is rediculous.
I was surprised that they charge for every amenity - tennis, fitness, etc. even the USA Today delivered to your room which most upscale hotels do not. The kids club was not geared for business travelers as the hours were 9:30 to 4:00 at a whopping price of $160 for 6 1/2 hours. There is no actual room for the kids like there is in other resorts they basically take the kids around the resort doing activites like playing tennis, walking on the beach, riding a bike, etc. My kids did have fun but the price and the times were not comparable to the other hotels with kids programs. 
The food was very overpriced and not very good. We ate at the pool and at the Barefoot restaurant - we would have gone out but there is not much around the resort close. I got a half hour massage at the spa and and found out that it is only for 25 minutes and they automatically charge a 20% gratuity! The treatments are all overpriced too - $72 for a 25 minute massage. 
On the 28th we moved to the Catamaran Hotel for the rest of our trip. The Catamaran has - which had similar type of grounds like Paradise but was $100 a day cheaper. We booked it through Southwest Airlines Vacation Package. We were pleasantly suprised that kids under 12 eat free at the Atoll restaurant, tickets for complimentary appetizers at the restaurant, complimentary cruise on Mission Bay for the family on the Bahia Bell, and tickets for 2 free hours in the arcade per child.
Our room was spacious and had a kitchen with a full size refridgerator, dishes and cookware. Which was great to save money on eating out every meal. Plus the hotel had a schedule of activites most of which were free including surfing lessons, movie on the beach with coke & popcorn, kyak lessons, etc. They also didn't charge like the Paradise Point for all of the amenities like the fitness center, tennis, etc. They did charge for parking but it was $9.00 a night and it was covered in a garage.
I would recommend that you save your money and stay at the Catamaran or elsewhere in San Diego instead of Paradise Resort.

title: “Inexpensive and Ok If You're Not Fussy”
text:
I stayed here for a night during a bicycle trip down the California coast. it was about the cheapest lodging I could find that wasn't a youth hostel.
If was OK. the room was a little funky, and certainly not fancy, but I didn't feel like I was going to get any lingering infections from it.
The evening I was there was pretty quiet. No horror stories.
I would stay here again if it was just me and I wasn't trying to impress anyone.

title: “Terrible, Terrible !!!”
text:
I had 4 luggages and a handbag. There's no elevator! I thought someone was going to help me with my luggages. These women at the front desk just kept staring at me! I asked for help, and the woman asked me why did I bring so many luggages? Great help, huh?
They are also racist! They give colored folks the worst rooms, and the non-colored better rooms. I am colored, so I should know!!!
Also, be careful about leaving your precious belongings...
If you can afford to stay somewhere better, then do so...you are saving yourself one of the worst places to stay in NYC
I will NEVER ever stay here again!

title: “It was a good one for the price”
text: The biggest drawback of this hotel is the tight parking space. Even people parked their car between two buildings and certainly that's not a parking space. The room was good and neat and so was the bathroom. The hotel staff was helpful except one old gentleman who does not have any curtesy at all. The breakfast was what you expect in a continental one and also there is a computer on the lobby you can use if you buy the card from the front desk. The neighborhood was good and safe as we returned our hotel around midnight with a baby. We got a good deal through expedia

title: “One Night Stay”
text:
Check in was quick, room and and entire hotel was spotless. Some great restaraunts down the street aways on Manor...I recommend Vivo Cocina. At the Dennys next to the hotel, ceasar salad was void of flavor and lettuce was limp.
I would definitely stay in this hotel again.

title: “Typical Conference Center Marriott”
text: Quick one night stay at the Copley Marriott. It's a conference center hotel, but we were there to celebrate our anniversary. The location is very convenient to the Boston Convention center -- and is in the heart of Back Bay. Our room wasn't spacious, but it is a city hotel. The new Marriott beds and linens are very comfortable. Concierge was very helpful in selecting a restaurant for dinner. Would recommend again - although if you're coming to Boston as a tourist I would recommend staying at the Long Wharf or Customs House instead as you'll be closer to the water and many of the tourist attractions the city has to offer.

title: “Love Seattle Warwick!”
text:
My husband's band was playing the Hardrock Cafe in Seattle a few weeks ago, so I booked several rooms for our friends and family that were planning on attending the show. I dealt with Tami Taylor, Senior Sales Manager, when booking the rooms and all I can say is Thank You Tami! Because of all the rooms I booked, Tami upgraded my husband and me to the Queen Victoria Suite, and it was fantastic! Everyone was so friendly and helpful and the newly redecorated 18th floor exectutive rooms are gorgeous. Everyone in our party had a fantastic stay. 
Thanks Warwick Seattle, we will be back!!

title: “This is, at most, a 2 star hotel”
text:
This place is disgusting! The first night we arrived late and we were tired from our 14 hour drive with our 5yo and infant, so we really didn't look around the room, we just went to bed.
