The next day however I noticed a few things as we were getting up and ready to leave for the day but really didn't have time to get into it. When we came back that evening I started looking around and noticed A LOT. There was a broken lamp shade, a trash can that really needed replacement, damage to the room door and bathroom door, some sort of dry splatter all over the doors, a huge buildup of dust and/or mold around the lighting fixture in the bathroom, the bottom side of the toilet seat was dirty, a brown lump of something on the heavy curtain and what looked like dried blood on the lite curtain, the desk chair was beaten up and the fabric was coming apart, dust build up on all the vents and light fixtures and the lotion bottle was previously used. 
To be fair, I called the front desk and asked for a supervisor to come see the room, she and her house keeper did and both seemed taken aback by what they saw. She did offer to switch rooms, but I turned it down since it was going to be more effort than it was worth, because we were leaving early in the morning. She did however send up some cookies, breakfast vouchers and an apology note, which was thoughtful one her part and I give her credit for doing this but this still does not excuse the state of the hotel and the nickel-and-diming we had to put up with. 
Around the hotel I found wall paper coming off the walls, trays of dirty dishes that sat in front of rooms for over 24 hours, the men’s bathroom had wall paper taped up over a large rip in the wall and it was obvious that it had been there a while plus a piece of plywood on the ceiling. 
Everything had a cost, parking, internet, water, luggage carts, etc. I am surprised there weren’t quarter slots in the lamps and TV. I have stayed at a lot of hotels, from high end to lower end and I have never had to pay extra for the basics, like internet. And I have never been told that I couldn’t get my own luggage cart, that I had to have a bellmen come and get.
This will be the only time I visit this hotel and I will make sure people I know are aware of this deceptive business.

title: “Wow - great hotel”
text:
What a great place. The hotel is around the corner from great shops and attractions like the Sears Tower and about five to ten minutes walk to the beach.
I stayed in a suite which was wonderful. The most comfortable sofa I have sat on in years. Huge LCD televisions with cable (High Def). A large bathtub with jacuzzi-type jets that massage you when you're lying in it., and a walk in shower. A large, comfortable bed too.
I'm just sorry I only stayed for a night.
One thing - I booked a standard room a few weeks in advance at a rate of about $300. When I checked their website again nearer the time, I could get a suite for the same price. It's worth checking the day before you arrive as prices seem to change all the time - you might get lucky like me and get a suite for the normal price of a standard

title: “Great Staff & Good Food”
text:
The staff was extremely friendly and personable. Went out of their way to make sure everything was okay.
Food was surprisingly good. Tasted more like home-cooked than most hotels.

title: “A great experience...”
text: After reading some of the reviews I was very hesitant about staying here...After arriving and expecting the worse it turned out to be just opposite.It was well worth staying there for the 3 days that we did...the staff were friendly and always were eager to help. We did the Marlowes run in the pink caddy as well as spending the afternoon on Beale st...The whole Elvis spectacle was amazing ...the lounge after 3pm always had live concerts playing as well as good priced drinks..I do believe you have to go with the idea of taking the whole concept in rather than going there and finding faults....Lost track of how many key chains I bought but you never can have enough...again it was a pleasure staying there.

title: “Hotel Staff”
text: The hotel staff is ok for the most part. Some were ok, some were not so great and some are absolutely fantastic (Brandi and Henry). Brandi is one of the nicest waitresses we have had (especially for a hotel) and Henry goes above and beyond his duties to make your stay and event as wonderful as possible.

title: “To see New York on a budget”
text:
The hotel is in a great location, central to most "touristy" places. The staff is mostly Korean, and it is in a Korean section of town, with a wide variety of restaurants (do not buy anything from the place called "Cafeteria" across the street - really bad food). The subway station is a few steps to the right of the hotel, on the corner of Broadway St. It is also within walking distance to the Empire State Building. Times Square is a short distance away, as well as all the shopping on Fifth Avenue, Herald Square and the big Macy's. 
There is a free basic breakfast every morning 7-10 am. We stayed on the 12th (top) floor - for $110/night it was a terrific price, considering that it's Manhattan. The con side? I know we only wanted a double bed, but it was the smallest hotel room I've ever stayed in! The hallways leading to the room were narrow as well. It was not super clean, but not really dirty either. The maid was helpful at fixing a broken shower knob, and so was the front desk at getting extra towels. There is a little mini-fridge in the room. The radiator/heater made sporadic noises in the middle of the night - we were told that the whole hotel is like that. Since I came to NY to sightsee, not to stay in my hotel room all day, it was a minor dissappointment but I would stay there again if I was on a budget and wanted a basic and decent place to stay.

title: “A great stay”
text:
The Wacker is a great hotel ideally situated in downtown Chicago with nice views, clean rooms and friendly staff. 
The rates were also decent.

title: “great”
text: we had a great time and it was right where we could go see attractions!! nice staff and great breakfast!

title: “Good experience”
text:
After reading other reviews, I was concerned about my plans to stay at this hotel. However, I stuck with my plans and spent 2 nights in late June. The hotel was fine for my purpose, which was to have a pleasant place to sleep with responsive customer service. This hotel supplied both. If I had wanted to stay at a resort where I spent my whole day on the site, I would have chosen a resort hotel.
The hotel's website location map was inadequate which caused me to wander around the area before phoning them and asking for directions . . . I should have used a better map. 
The area is close to Interstate 17 and, while overloaded with nearby restaurants and retail options, the area has sufficient selection of same.
I would recommend this hotel for anyone who is looking for a comfortable place to stay; it is not a resort nor is it a fleabag.

title: “Older motel but comfortable and clean”
text: Our stay there was very comfortable. If you are just looking for a place to rest after sightseeing, with no frills, this one works, for the money! The desk staff was friendly and helpful, even offering advice on tours, etc. The room was older and small, but very clean and gave us a restful night. Parking might be difficult for larger cars, but it is free--a rarity in SF!

title: “I think I have the answer to these widely varied reviews...”
text:
If you arrive in the daytime, the white walls show their wear, the decor is a little harsh, and the trendy vibe seems a bit too IKEA. I checked in late afternoon, sun streaming in and the room looked dingy, every defect showed. 
But like most things, when you hit evening and dim down the lights, it's much prettier. So when I returned later that night, the turn-down service had left me a dessert treat, turned on ambient lighting, and the room was actually quite beautiful. 
Note - housekeeping is lacking as of June 2011, bathroom floor was very unclean, I will spare you the detail, but they did come in and clean it for me. The coffee maker had used coffee pods in the water reservoir which was gross, but again, front desk came through and delivered a small pot of coffee prior to my 6AM call, which was a fine solution. 
In summary - trendy decor like a Zen inspired IKEA concept, responsive staff, generous room size, very nice towels, firm but comfy bed, small saltwater pool in the basement, decent size workout room. The downside: inadequate housekeeping, hefty fee for valet parking (required, no free or self park). For the money, I'd pick the Westin next door as a first choice for overall quality.

title: “a great time !”
text:
WOW what a deal..........my family and I will ALWAYS look for a Embassy suites we were very pleased and will definitly go back to this one! Staff was very friendly and outgoing,Piano player and Bass player ......what a treat...,breakfast was very good and timely and fresh thanks to the indoor pool,hot tub ,sauna, it saved the weekend because of the inclement weather I have paid this much and more for ALOT less at other motels..........oh yeah coctail hour was great we would really like to thank the bartender,cook and helpers and also thank you so much Kurt (piano player) it was a lasting experience and we will defintly be back! see you all soon! God bless!
Thanks again!

title: “Good but missing a few things to be great”
text:
For the price this hotel has nice amenities, however it is missing a few things to make it great. 
My wife and I stayed there one night. The hotel is in a good area with a great location. There are restaurants and activities super close to the hotel. 
The first thing that I have to knock on the hotel is the $36 valet parking that they hit you with as you are getting out of the car. It's not crazy expensive but somewhat unexpected and you really have no other options for parking.
After we got checked in we went to the Manager's Social. The Social was nice, the drinks were above the average of other socials. However, the food was pretty standard with chips and salsa. 
Our room was one of the nicer ones we have stayed in. However the door were confusing and so was the thermostat. Both caused several frustrations and several tires to figure out (my wife got locked out of the bedroom at 3am after using the bathroom). 
Our bathroom was nice but the artwork in the bathroom had water and mold spots on it. The bedroom had amazing linens. 
The next morning we hit up the weight room. It was ok, wish they had a few more weights and machines. The business room was ok too. The computers were slow and I had to switch computers several times as they froze. 
The breakfast was good, they had a nice spread with a ton of options. Chief BriaNick was extremely friendly as he made my custom order omelet.
Leaving the hotel was once again ok. The small parking garage was a traffic jam and it took several minutes of waiting to get our car. Once we got our car we had to wait another several minutes to leave as we waited on other guests to load their cars. 
Overall, this hotel was good. However, there are just a few minor things that if they touched up it could be great. For the cost, I expect these issues to be non-existent.

title: “Good addition to the Kimpton brand... but we'd still choose the Muse in NYC”
text: Well-located for Chelsea, the Flower District, and lower Midtown. Reasonably hip decor. We were upgraded to a suite - very petite, suggesting that standard rooms would be awfully small. Good bathroom but beware the slippery marble floor tile (why do we find this problem over and over again in hotels? Look into tumbled marble, decorators!) Bar Basque offers some fine house cocktails and tapas, but be selective on the latter -- go with the charcuterie, piquillo peppers, fried olives... flatbread pizzas overpriced and mediocre. Also good breakfasts in the dining room - well-prepared omelets, good steel cut oats... menu looked more interesting than buffet. Bar (and most rooms on the back side of the hotel facing away from Empire State Building) have an entertaining view of a large outdoor screen showing art videos. Underground parking easily accessible from the building. Service good.

title: “Comfortable and friendly”
text:
My husband, 2 year son and I stayed here just one night for a weekend getaway. We got a great rate through Hotwire.com and as such were very impressed with the value for our money!
The hotel itself is beautifully decorated and the beds were super comfy. We didn't try the pool ourselves, but the family traveling with us did and they loved it.
Customer service is generally very attentive. When we called down to the front desk or picked up our car from the valet, they always addressed us by name. Unfortunately, check-in took an ungodly amount of time--I think they were training someone new.
Restaurants in the hotel and immediately outside its doorway are not family-oriented, but several strip malls (including a Whole Foods market and TGIFridays) are just a short drive (or a brisk walk if you're so inclined) away via the highway overpass.
Its location isn't in the heart of what vacationers would typically seek in La Jolla. The main tourist and beach areas are aboue a 10 minute drive away. But we liked it as a roughly halfway point between San Diego and Carlsbad (Legoland).

title: “Great Hotel and location but terrible staff”
text:
I stayed for the July 4th weekend. The rooms were really nice and clean, loved the decor and the location. The area is really nice, we took a short walk and found really great bars. The bathroom was clean and I liked the shower (although it's kind of weird if your with a friend b/c you can see the person showering from the bedroom). Also REALLY close to the 1 train which is a plus. 
The only bad thing was the staff. The girl working at the concierge stand was really rude, didn't even acknowledge us when we walked up to her. The front desk staff wasn't that friendly either. They were also REALLY disorganized. We decided to stay an extra night and they ran my card and everything. The next morning they came banging on our door saying we had to be out. We went to the front desk and cleared it up, then later on they came banging again saying the same thing! Apparently no communication between the staff - the night person didn't tell the day person who didn't tell the afternoon person, and no one bothered to check the computer? 
I probably won't stay here again just b/c ofthe staff, which is a shame b/c I loved the hotel.

title: “Disappointed - will not return”
text:
When traveling, I look for location, amenities and comfort, plus value for the price. The Hilton Garden Inn Charlotte Uptown was booked for me, not by me, with all good intentions.
As a business traveler, I often get in late and must be up and out quite early, often as early as 5am.
Location is adjacent to major sports venue. Strike one. Urban center, so there is apt to be street noise that can permeate the rooms, and there was quite a bit of this - emergency vehicle sirens, loud auto sounds. Strike two. The hotel is not well insulated from outside sounds. The room doors and the rooms themselves are not designed to contain noise so it does not effect others. I could easily hear even not loud conversations in adjacent rooms on both sides as well as guests speaking not too loudly in the halls, even after 1am. I got precious few hours sleep that night!. Strike three, and they're OUT was the obtrusively loud plumbing sounds. When adjacent rooms used their facilities, whether it was the toilet, sink or shower/bath, I do not know. I just know that it created a roaring sound in MY room.
When I mentioned this to the desk person the next morning, she acknowledged each of my stated concerns, indicating that this is just the way it is at this property.
In addition, for anyone in need of ready and waiting cabs, this is another negative for this property. I requested a cab pick-up for 5:50am, and was assured one would be there and waiting. As you may have guessed, this did not happen. Despite their best effort, no cab was there. About 10 minutes later, one arrived, but it is somehow unsettling when one is on a tight schedule and relies on punctuality. Of course, I built in some fudge factor so I did not go nuts, but if you need reliance on either waiting cabs at-the-ready or reliable pre-arranged on-call cabs, you might be sorely disappointed in what this hotel can assure.
On the plus side, their FREE Internet in the room was quite fast, measured at about 9Mbps down and up. This was a pleasant surprise.

title: “Best hotel staff I've ever experienced”
text:
Stayed here last week based on Trip Advisor reviews, it was a fantastic hotel, lovely, spacious rooms, a little noisy in the hallway in the evening, but no complaints what so ever. The room was spot on and the highlight were undoubtedly the obliging, friendly staff who were extremely pleasant and always left us with a smile on our faces! 
The hotel is in a perfect area, steps from the shops, amazing restaurants, the Common and local to the subway (perfect for getting to the legendary Fenway Park!). Highly recommended.
Cheers Back Bay Hotel!

title: “Quality Hotel”
text: The room was clean and it smelled nice. The staff was very friendly and helpful because I needed help finding nearby restaurants and shopping malls. The internet was really fast unlike other hotels I've stayed at. I honestly do not have a single complaint about this holiday inn express. I would recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Wonderful place to stay!”
text: This was a great place to stay. It was clean, quiet and the staff was very friendly. I had a 2 bedroom suite shared with my daughter her husband and my granddaughter. We had plenty of room. The suite has a full kitchen with untensils so we could cook if we wanted but there were restaurants in walking distance and there was also places to get a massage or pedicure close. My only complaint was there was no childrens programming available on television that didn't have to be paid for. All in all this was a perfect place to stay with family!

title: “Superb Boston Location”
text: We stayed in this hotel for 2 nights, and definitely has the wow factor........location great great great, cleanliness superb superb superb, beds were so comfortable and we had the Red Sox stadium just outside our window. Alec at the reception was very professional and I would say all staff were very helpful, there is nothing I could fault in this grand hotel, we will definitely return and I would say to everyone looking to go to Boston, do not miss the opportunity of visiting a nice, friendly, great location hotel......thank you Commonwealth hotel, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay.......

title: “Horrible Customer Service in the Billing Dept”
text:
Stayed there for one night.... great atmosphere, horrible lighting, outstanding furnishings - typical neo W hotel. 
However, the Hotel likes to charge for everything - even for things you don't use. They charged me for drinking the water from the honor bar which i never touched. When i called the billing department to correct the charge, they were unapologetic, though they said they would reverse the charges only after i had to raise my voice. 
Watch your wallet! And good luck with the billing department -- shameful behavior!

title: “Best hotel in Manhattan”
text:
The Affina rooms all come with a small kitchen and the larger suites have an extra room with a sofa bed and an extra bathroom. Carl, the bellman, takes a personal interest in all the guest, insuring their stay is perfect. Margaret and Amanda in Guest Services are effiecient, professional, beautiful, and very helpful with the process of checking in and making sure everything is perfect.
The only think I don't like is that they charge for internet service. Internet is free (or worked into the price of the room) in a lot of hotels.
Still, it's a small price to pay for such a great on the road experience.

title: “Great place for families to bond - kids loved the park and great prices too”
text: We just got back from Carribean Cove in Indianapolis. My 7 & 9 year boys loved the waterpark, the arcade, ping pong, games and everything the hotel had to offer. It was great value - we got a two night special. With that we also received "kids eat free" coupons so it really helped with the $$. We looked at going to Great Wolf Lodge, but it was so much more $$ - plus we'd been there before. I can also say the staff at the Cove were super friendly and very service focused. The life guards take their jobs seriously and I appreciated their focus on water safety and helping the kids. It was a nice and clean waterpark. All in all, it was super value for the money. The hotel room we had was a little small and we're not used to double beds, but hey, we weren't there for the room anyway - the overall hotel was great and we plan to go back again!

title: “Omni South Park misses the mark, a blemish to the Omni brand”
text: I stayed at the Omni South Park Hotel with my family recently and I was disappointed with this Omni Hotel experience. I am an Omni Select Guest and have come to truly enjoy Omni Hotels for their luxury, value and select guest perks. First and foremost this hotel is far below the superb quality and experience I've had at several other Omni properties (full disclosure I had my wedding at an Omni and have a special connection to the chain). This hotel needs a complete renovation...badly. The entire property looks as though it has not received a facelift in 20+ years with rooms, corridors, and common areas worn and dated. This is unlike other outstanding properties I've stayed at in Tucson, Chicago, San Antonio, and Dallas. Although the bed was very nice and comfortable, the suite balcony door was practically immovable and created problems entering/exiting. There was a bat roosting in the balcony overhang and although it did not bother my wife and I, it was part of the overall deferred maintenence the hotel projected. Paint was peeling from the ceiling of the balcony. The hotel staff was excellent and although I did not report these issues initially while at the hotel, it is difficult to explain that a hotel requires this level work to the staff who are not responsible for renovations. Nice hotel, but certainly not worth the money for an expected luxury Omni stay.

title: “Great Place to Stay in New York”
text: We recently had to spend several days in New York while a family member was in the hospital there. The Murray Hill Inn was listed as one of the hotels that the hospital recommended on its website for out-of-towners. We could not have been more pleased that we chose The Murray Hill Inn. It has a distinctive European flavor and ambience. The room was clean, modern, and welcoming. The hotel is in a safe area, close to coffee shops, diners, and delis, and just a short walk to the subway station. The hotel staff was pleasant and accommodating. Our stay was reasonable in price and high in value. We highly recommend this hotel to travelers who are looking for good value for their money while staying in New York.

title: “Nice Hotel!”
text: Nice Hotel! Great View's of Downtown, and easy access to Hwy.

title: “Good Option for the West Side”
text:
The Omni Westside is one of the better, if not the best, hotel option on Houston's far west side. If you don't have any reason to want to stay on the west side, then it's probably not your best bet, but if business or personal needs require you to stay out there, then this may be your hotel, if you can get a good rate. 
The lobby and common areas of the hotel are quite nice, with water running throughout the large lobby, giving a relaxing, "resort" feel to the place. Through the many times that I've stayed there, the staff have always been vey helpful and friendly, with everything from the most routine item to assistance with special requests. 
The rooms themselves, however, can be "hit or miss." I have had very nice rooms there, but then on other occasions, I've had a room which was not so great, either due to the "musty" smell (Houston is always humid, so that smell can be a problem, if the hotel doesn't take steps to keep it in check.), or a cleanliness issue or a problem with something not working right. Not that this happens every time - like I said, I've often had a very nice room - but on occasion, there is some issue (usually a small one) with the room. That aside, however, I still come back, because it is still a pretty good hotel, and probably your best west side option. If I can't get a competitive rate, however, there are other acceptable options in the area.

title: “Central accommodation on Fisherman's Wharf”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights over the Labor day weekend. We were quickly checked in and given our room key. Our room was on the fourth floor and was very spacious for what we required. The room was impeccably clean. Ben, one of the porter's, was very kind and helpful. The location is great for getting on to the cable car and for hiring bikes (just next door) for the bike ride over the Golden Gate Bridge. I really recommend this and a burger for lunch at Bridgeway in Saulsalito. Also handy for walking up to fisherman's wharf. Check out time of 1200 was also really helpful. Overall a very pleasant stay at the Argonaut!

title: “Not as bad as I feared (after reading these reviews)”
text:
I tried to change my reservation after reading these reviews. Pack a little extra patience when you stay here, but I was ok with the result. 
Yes, it’s uber-hip. Avoid the pool on Sunday if you’re over 25. If you value your hearing, it may not be the place for you, but the rock memorabilia has some charms.
The room is fairly modern and adequate, but I packed earplugs and was staying on a high floor. I did face Petco park, but not enough to see the game (for that, you have to go to the Marriott). The electronics and remote took some patience, as does the shower. It definitely does look like someone has trashed a lobby or room: the phone was ripped out of one of the elevators, for example. 
It’s pricey, and definitely one of those hotels that charges extra for anything and everything: in room fee, fridge rental fee, everything in the room is for sale. The “turndown service” is nice, but a mandatory $15 for a swizzle stick. The gift shop has t-shirts that start at $100. 
The service has some rough spots, but it worked out for me. They did lose one of my packages for a couple of days; after three requests, it reappeared and they didn’t charge for delivery (Finally: one thing they didn’t charge!!).
The most irritating service element was that the lobby has kiosks rather than a line and at least three times I was waiting for an ‘star associate’ when another guest decided to nose in ahead of me. The associates never did anything, leading me to believe that a single queue is the only way to appease patient folks.

title: “Very goodf hotel in good, central location”
text: The Hyatt Regency is a newer hotel. It used to be the Swiss which was quite run down (according to various taxi cab drivers). It is up to Hyatt standards and is even a touch luxurious. Being newer, everything is in great shape. The location is also good, about 2 blocks from the start of the freedom trail, 2 blocks from Filene's and a few blocks from good places to eat. I was very pleased with it.

title: “great location, great service”
text: I stayed at Hotel Union Square for a few days while I was in San Francisco for a business conference. First of all the location was spectacular. Right in downtown, close to Union Square, financial district, and importantly for me, the Moscone Center. For the price you can't get any closer. The staff here was very personable, and helpful. Kasha and Jewel checked me in and were more than helpful recommending a place for dinner. I had read some reviews about rooms being small here, so I booked an executive room. The room was great, very spacious, clean, and quiet. Many thanks to the staff at Hotel Union Square, I'll be back any time I have business in San Francisco.

title: “Great location for shopping and dining.”
text:
Overall all great place to stay. 
Walking distance to shopping and restaurants.
There is a charge for internet access and parking can be a bit of a challenge if the hotel is hosting an event. 
Definitively will stay at this hotel again.

title: “Nice Room, Good Location”
text:
The Bonaventure's inside reminded me of a cross between an airport and low-end mall. The rooms were nice and clean. I especially liked how big our bathroom was and the abundance of towels provided. If you like big beds you'll like it here. We were told the rooms were recently renovated. The husband and I stayed here for one night and it was what we needed. If you are looking for a nice, clean room and safe place close to the good local downtown L.A. spots this is still a good place (with no frills). The service at registration was courteous. I hear the Suede lounge is pretty hip which is on the first floor. This used to be the spot in the 90's but the shine is a little tarnished.
3 1/2 rating (better than average)

title: “A good experience overall”
text:
We spent 4 days at this property. I had checked out the various criticisms from Trip Advisor first but found that we had no major issues. Yes, there were a few concerns: 1) we were initially given a room with one bed on the 5th floor very far from the elevators. It was quiet but the room smelled and had no view. After quickly complaining we were immediately (within 10 minutes) moved to room 845 which had two beds and an OK view for the same price. 2) the power plugs (wall sockets were all loose in the room), were too closely spaced for more than one device to be plugged in and in one case, anything plugged in fell out; 3) no frig in the room. The latter bothered me more than anything else but the ice machine was close by. 4) homeless folks are very visible in the adjacent blocks where we had to walk; this was initially intimidating, but did not cause us problems. 
On the good side: 1) great location just 2 blocks from Capitol Hill; 2) a deli is now located across the street where you can buy some groceries also; 3) the room we had was almost perfect in the sense that the bed comfort was great, bathroom amenities more than fine; flat screen TV had a good selection of channels; 4) the air conditioning system was easily adjustable and worked fine without a lot of noise; 5) we were close enough to the elevator and ice machine but heard none of the noise associated with those devices. 6) breakfast was fine and a good value considering you are in the middle of a very expensive city; 7) just two blocks from Union Station so if you have to travel anywhere by metro it is very convenient. 8) checkin and checkout were convenient and the staff was completely response to our needs and concerns; 9) two computers with free boarding pass printout capability were available which we used without incident.
I would stay here any time.

title: “Love this place!”
text: We always pick this Homewood Suites due to its location. Yes, it is busy and there are a lot of families who stay here. Everyone I have come across has been friendly, from the front desk to the maintenance man. If I could change something, I would get another waffle iron because I always seem to be stuck behind the person who drought his entire extended family and makes about 8 waffles. This actually did happen to me and I eventually left the line and went back and the person in front of me only made three. The seating in the dining room is cramped and if the meeting rooms aren't being used, I wish these could be opened up when they are busy. Often times there would be tables and no chairs because people take them from other tables. Or there would not be any high chairs for my son. I do love this place though,It is clean, the grounds are beautiful, breakfast is plentiful and yummy, as is the dinner, and there is free parking so that alone deserves fine stars

title: “views are terrific”
text: The Millenium Plaza ,One United Nations, is an excellent hotel for views.Just got back and stayed on the fortieth floor !! Hotel is spotless, rooms are big, and whilst it is a bit further out this means the hotel is very quiet.

title: “Request renovated rooms only”
text: Hotel rooms are being renovated now. Therefore some of them (already renovated ones) are absolutely great and the old ones are... well, really old (furniture and all interior, bathrooms, conditioning system, etc.) especially when you've seen the others. Location and service are totally great, it's just a huge diffeence that you can get for the same value.

title: “Te service was fantastic!”
text: I went to a conference an the people serving us stole my heart. They were very helpful, friendly and happy.

title: “Beautiful hotel!”
text: We stayed one night in July 2012 after we got off the Carnival Glory. Check in was super easy, they held our luggage for us and got us in our room very quick. Very clean rooms, big screen, comfy bed, nice glass shower. Overall amazing experience! They have a travel person in the front lobby that can answer any questions about travelling around town. Would stay there again.

title: “I Agree with the good oppinions”
text:
Hotel is in apublic area near park and water. Try to get a high floor with water view.
Good rooms, bads, kitchen, TV , bathroom , breakfast, and afternoon buffet. 
Room with pool table - free. wifi works fine, but not best reception in all the room.
Pool and hot Jacuzzi. 
All buldings have access only with room card- extra security.
Service is good , but too correct. FAst check in/out.

title: “Nikko, the place to stay centrally in San Francisco”
text:
We spent four nights at the Nikko San Francisco. This hotel is very centrally located at the bottom of Mason Street, close to Market Street, Powell Street (BART) Station, the Powell Street cable cars, shops and Union Square. Despite all the action at what seemed to be the height of the tourist season this was a quiet hotel.
The room we had on the 16th floor was comfortable with a nice view towards Market Street. The bathroom decor was okay but the water pressure in the shower was poor. There was no in room safe, but the reception staff were very helpful with a free safe deposit box. We found the staff to be efficient and friendly. Most of the guests seemed to be tourists from the Asia region and business people.
In summary, a comfortable well presented hotel in a great central location.

title: “Fantastic Hotel Great Location & Price”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights in April. It was a fantastic stay!
The rooms are small, but certainly big enough for 2 with cozy bedding and a modern clean bathroom.
Our room faced the street and there was some noise as well as that of water running from above when folks were showering.
The staff were friendly and knowledgeable although they could have used more than 1 person at check in time on the front desk.
The breakfast was more than adequate. 
The hotel and the rooms were very clean and the location is unbeatable for the price.
Would definitely stay again.

title: “Very Swank”
text: Very cool place. Stay here on a Friday Night and it was full of young Hollywood. You might call it a fashion show. Very fun to watch.

title: “Comfort Inn Midtown was a winner!”
text:
It is a bit risky choosing an inexpensive hotel in a good location in NYC. The Comfort Inn Midtown was a real winner for us. First of all, location was perfect - a half block off of Times Square. Next best thing was the friendly and very helpful staff. How pleasant it was to NOT see signs of frustrated, tired empolyees. They all went out of their way to offer help - especially "Sidibi" the bellhop. 
The rooms were crisp & clean and nicely furnished. Not all rooms were spacious like ours. We at first were assigned to a rather small room toward the back part of the hotel. We simply asked if there was another room with more space or a window view. They said there was (a handicap room), but that it was not yet ready. We gladly waited (sightseeing on Times Square). We were given room 602 with 2 windows with a view. Four days later 602 was needed for a handicap person and we gladly moved to 802. They actually moved all our things for us to the new room so that we could be on our way . Both rooms were spcaious and comfortable with lots of closet & drawer space. But keep in mind - this is New York where space is at a premium. About the only complaint we had was that the dining area was too small. But the food was good. So yes I would definitely go back to this hotel - and ask for a front room facing the street. We did not have any street noise the whole week we were there.

title: “Great Stay at Hotel ZaZa”
text: We just returned from a weekend at the Hotel Zaza in Houston. We really enjoyed the hotel. Our room was just lovely. Lots of space and great amenities. The hotel staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The restaurant was excellent. And the lounge at night was quite a scene. The pool on the weekend was also a scene, which was a bit of a pain as it is not the place to relax and chill out but rather quite a bit of a pick up scene. That was the only drawback, as it wasn't our thing. But the hotel was just great...good business center and great service overall. It's also in a really lovely section of Houston right next door to the Museum of Fine Arts. A really pretty area that was also very close to all major attractions. The light rail system is right outside the door. Just great!

title: “Loved the hotel”
text: We had trouble finding a hotel we stopped in here just to see how much it would be we thought it would be really expensive but it was very affordable. The room was very spacious and clean. The bed was very comfortable. We were a lttle worried about the neighborhood cause its said to be dangerous but absolutley nothing happened didnt even get woke up once. I would definitly stay here again.

title: “Chicago.”
text:
The Hotel was ideal for a long weekend in Chicago. It is in a busy area build on top of a shopping mall. The hotel was very clean and tidy with friendly helpfull staff.
The hotel is in an area that you feel save walking about at night.
The navy pier is about a 15 minute walk from the hotel, You can get the bus tours and the architectural boat trip from that area. 
Their is a good selection of restaurants close by the hotel, the John Handcock tower is only about 10 minutes from the hotel, well worth going to the top for the views.

title: “Felt like Royalty”
text: I encountered some of the most friendly staff. The size was big enough to offer amenities yet small enough to feel like you were a guest of the owners. The food was delightful and the rooms were lovely. I also enjoyed the fact that the resort fee covered gratuities - you could give a little extra if warranted. I would definitely go back when traveling to the Phoenix area either on business time or personal time.

title: “Really Good Value”
text: My mother, sister and I took a shopping trip to NY before Christmas and stayed in a 2 bed (1 sofa bed) suite on the 6th floor. It was absolutely perfect for us - brilliant location, right beside the restaurants and pubs of Little Italy & Soho and very close to the high street shops on Broadway. Our rooms were fantastic, very clean and excellant facilities (TV, kitchenette). The staff were very friendly and extremely helpful. I think our suite had been recently renovated, so you may want to check when booking on the type of room you are reserving. We will definitely be back.

title: “NEVER AGAIN!”
text: Do NOT waste you money on this hotel when Dallas has so much more to offer. It is old, but it is NOT charming! We paid a fortune for our run to get dirty windows, outdated carpet, dust on the furniture, and they even forgot our champagne! When you spend $600.00 for the room and package, it should include more than rose petaled made into a heart. 2 plug outlets didn't work, and when we brought it too the manager's attention, he only offered us 50.00 off. Please, that's not even 5% off, and he acted bothered! Try the Ritz, Hotel ZAZA, The Cresent, but DO NOT waste your money here!

title: “Fab hotel - but ruined by poor service”
text:
While most of my travel is business, this was with my husband and son. Loved the room and the hotel - beautiful and hip. Had dinner in the restaurant - which took forever. When we asked what the hold-up was between app and main course, the waitress told us that my scallop shell did not open, so the chef was re-cooking. While I was glad he was, (and it was great when it finally arrived), they could have let us know, and given us the choice to bring out the steaks for my husband and son. We were all exhausted and tired!
The next day, we were driving to DC and when we gave the bellman the ticket for the car, it took 50 minutes.... yes 50 minutes to get the car!!!! Needless to say, as much as we liked the facility (and the people were nice), we would probably not do it again.

title: “We were awoken by people in the next room at 2:45 a.m. We...”
text: We were awoken by people in the next room at 2:45 a.m. We called the front dest three times. Finally we moved to another room at 4:30. A few days later, the hotel manager called and said that the hotel did everything correctly. We certainly don't feel that way.

title: “Great Location and Staff”
text: Loved the location, 5 min. walk to Penn Station, 2 mins to subway on 27th st. The staff was excellent, hotel was very clean and comfortable. Breakfast bar was very crowded and too small for the amount of people using it, though.

title: “Good value hotel, well located.”
text: For a midtown hotel it was as good as you could expect; it was clean and well located. The hotel looks old and dated in areas, and there was no coffee making facilities in the room, but these are fairly small drawbacks. Reading other reviews I'd imagine I wouldn't have been so happy at paying $300 a night, but for what we paid, I was happy.

title: “Excellent customer service”
text: The front desk staff was exceptional. Especially Luisa Alvarado. They were friendly and very helpful.

title: “Super Clean But Outdated.”
text: One more overnight stay at a Drury Inn for my family. My understanding is...this is one the first properties built by Drury in 1981. Despite being older and outdated it is super clean. In addition, the staff is friendly and professional. The 5:30 Kickback was nice as was breakfast. I have grown to anticipate their fresh popcorn to help me unwind after our long drive. I was disappointed by the strong smell of cigarette smoke as we walked down the hall to our nonsmoking room. Also the pillows and mattresses were not up to par with some of their newer properties. Given that I only paid $79.99; I can not complain. It was more than adequate given the price, the age of the property and its location in relationship to I70, airports, Children's Hospital, Zoo & Museum. In short, I would gladly stay again at the Drury Inn East in Denver, CO.

title: “Garden of Eden”
text:
I've stayed at this W before and like the property and the location very much. Nothing, however, compares to the incredible service of Eden the Concierge. for a number of weeks in advance of my trip she helped me arrange for many fun activities. She made me feel like aVIP from the moment I wrote the first email - generally addressed to the Concierge. 
I'll never stay at any other hotel in Chicago (unless Eden switches to another).
Thanks Eden!!

title: “cute and friendly”
text: Luckily, my hotwire hotel booking turned out to be the Hotel Indigo. Everyone was so nice and went out of their way to make my stay pleasant. The rooms are clean and cute; the beds are comfy. I had a much better hotel experience than some of my colleagues who stayed at other hotels for twice the price.

title: “10/10”
text:
We stayed two nights at this Kimpton Argonaut San Francisco, good impression started from the moment we stepped down at the front gate. This hotel put good efforts in human touch, staff are really willing to assist and it's pretty much natural expression.
We had a pier view room with Alcatraz exactly right in the middle of the frame, single window not so big to give a panoramic view but great nevertheless. Nautical theme throughout the hotel and rooms are in good taste and very nice. Bathroom has all necessary amenities plus long list of items you can borrow at no cost and some for purchase.
This hotel stressed on being pet friendly, throughout the stay I haven't seen any pets around and no sign of hair or smell whatsoever in our room. I'm pretty allergic to smell but this hotel is absolutely clean.
Welcoming fucntion every afternoon were very good, lobby area is small but great. Location is very convenient for tramp connection and there seemed to be a good flow and availability of taxi at the front gate. 
Highly recommended and it's 10/10 for us.

title: “Brutal”
text: We know you get what you pay for so we were not expecting much. The room was dirty, the shower had mold due to a leaking faucet. We could deal with that, but when someone gets into your room while your gone and takes a number of personal belongings, you need to go somewhere more secure. When we told management, we were accused of making up the story to get a better rate. When we tried to check out because we didn't feel safe there, we were charged an extra $40.00 for a late checkout.

title: “Very happy with this hotel!”
text:
My son was visiting Seattle Pacific University, and we chose this hotel for its proximity to the college (about 2 miles away). I wasn't sure what to expect, but I got a good online rate ($129) and the pictures looked nice.
We were delighted with our room! We had a two-queens regular, non-view room (we knew we weren't spending much time there, so why splurge for extras this time...) and it was very spacious! We had a hide-a-bed couch and coffee table, huge flat screen tv with a good selection of channels, two sink areas and very nice amenities (Aveda bath products, Tully's coffee, and a GOOD blow dryer!) Towels were large and fluffy and plentiful. We were given a copy of the Seattle Times in the morning, which was a nice alternative to the usual USA Today!
Everything was spotless and the beds were very comfortable. My only complaint would be the heating/air system. It didn't seem to have a thermostat, (I could be wrong about this, as it was late when we went to bed, and I didn't spend a whole lot of time examining it--just turned it to a cooler temp) so it was just on or off and it was hard to get a comfortable sleeping temperature going. The fan wasn't overly loud, but it was a constant hum.
It was nice to have free underground parking (particularly when I saw plenty of ice-covered cars on the road in the morning!) and free internet service. There was also a small business center which was free to use.
We didn't use the pool or exercise room, but we looked at them and they were nice enough. The breakfast room was LOVELY with a fireplace, view of the lake and plenty of seating. Breakfast options were good (wafflemaker, bagels, pastries, muffins, hard-boiled eggs, fruit, cereal, yogurt, coffee, tea, hot chocolate, milk, juices). I was surprised at how many people were in the breakfast room, since we'd barely encountered anyone while we were there and the hallways and room were very quiet. We never had to wait for an elevator and there were plenty of parking spots in the garage.
The location was convenient for the college visit and also very convenient for freeway access, and close to downtown. 
The staff was professional and helpful. I would definitely stay here on future visits.

title: “When a hotel can't handle volume”
text:
Manhattan has such good public transportation (trains, buses) and is so walkable that it is not necessary to stay in midtown to visit the midtown/tourist areas. You will get more of the feel of the city that never sleeps and if you are not used to speed, you'll marvel at how quickly you can travel to different neighborhoods.
But, there are times, whether for conventions or group trips, when this Hilton will tempt you with a very good rate. And the location is two short blocks from the N and R subway, which will take you to the heart of Soho, on Prince Street in about 10 minutes. 
BUT, this is a hotel that is not designed for full capacity - the design can't handle the crowds. You quickly begin to fight to get into an elevator and wait 20 minutes to get into an elevator to descend to the first floor. It's hit or miss for housekeeping - for our stay, the bathroom didn't have cups, the maid forgot to give us towels, the pellegrino bottle in the mini-bar was curiously filled with flat, tap-tasting water, the coffee that emerged from the coffeemaker tasted awful, and the previous guest left a bandaid dangling from the inside of the sink that remained there for three days. 
Skip the executive lounge and walk west on 53rd to several nice restaurants - unless, you like waiting in line for a continental breakfast that was substandard compared to other Hilton hotels.
The hotel restaurant is pleasant but the prices are ridiculous - especially when you can eat well and inexpensively at coffee shops and restaurants nearby.
Even more troubling was the air quality in the building. Years ago, the windows could open, which probably enabled the building to 'breathe' - but it's all sealed now. Many of us felt headachey and slept poorly.
If you don't have to stay in this Hilton - for a tour or business - please try another hotel - consider the East Side hotels, even the hotels a bit north in the 70s on Broadway. You'll have a better experience in NYC.

title: “Stinky!!!!!”
text:
Let me start out by saying that my family and I are not used to staying in upscale hotels by any means. We stay at Days Inn or Travelodge quite often. Having read the other reviews on this site I was weary of staying here but still I thought maybe the other reviewers were just picky. 
From the outside the place looked decent enough, with a smallish pool that seemed clean and pleasant. The lobby was nothing great but still decent. Then I asked where the restroom was and was given a key and told it was up two floors on the elevator. My daughter and I took the ride while my husband checked in. As soon as I stepped into the elevator I noticed the horrible smell. It reminded me of old musty apartments where people had a bunch of animals or something....not good. Then we get to the bathroom and unlock it only to find more nasty smell. Like I said it was a mixture of old yuck and animals and smoke. I hoped that this wasn't going to be the case with our room but boy was I wrong.
On our walk to the room you couldn't escape the horrible smell, it was truly overwhelming. Sure enough once we walked into our room it got worse. It was the same smell with a TON of some sort of citrus cleaner over it. It actually burned our eyes and throat. 
At first glance the room looked okay but as I turned on more lights I wasn't impressed. The nightstands were literally covered in cigerette burns. All the furniture was marked up with black marks and dents and burns. Then I pulled back the bedspread and the sheets looked dirty and the bedspread and sheets both had a bunch of cigarette burns. Now the sheets weren't wrinkly or anything so they probably were clean but boy were they nasty looking. 
Onto the kitchen area I went. The microwave and stove and fridge were all okay and seemed fairly clean. The cabinets and counters were just old and icky looking. Like I said I am used to staying in places like days inn but this was just not what one would expect. It reminded me so much of really nasty apartments I looked at when I was younger! The bathroom wasn't nice by any means either, it wasn't the worst I've seen though. I guess I'd give it about a four out of ten.
Maybe I could've handled this place if I were only staying for one night, but then I wouldn't need a place with a kitchen if I were only staying one night. We were to be there six nights but I knew right away that there was absolutely no way I was staying there that long. For one thing I didn't want to bring my clothes in and end up having all of our stuff stink.
So for the first time in all my life we left in search of other lodging. We wanted to check out right then but it was the friday of memorial weekend and we were afraid we wouldn't find anything else. Luckily we did about 2 hours later. When we checked out the clerk didn't act suprised at all that we were leaving all ready (I'm assuming this sort of thing might happen a lot here). Then she told my husband she'd only charge him sixteen something dollars which was great.
So overall I would definately say DO NOT stay at this place. I did notice however that as we were leaving the place was literally filling up with people. I just wanted to warn them all not to do it!!!! 
I guess to sum it up all I can say is that the place smelled like an old stinky bar with lots of dogs and it looked just as bad. All in all if it wasn't for the horrid smell I might've tried to stick it out but all together it was just not worth spending our vacation being grossed out by our hotel room.

title: “Fantastic place to stay - Would stay again”
text: We came to town for the NASCAR races and this Hampton Inn was fantastic. Super clean and quiet room provided a great night sleep. Our room had one bed against the wall to the bathroom and facing the window rather than on the side wall shared with the next room. This was a layout I had not seen before, but I liked it. We saw signs for the airport, but never heard any noise from planes taking off or landing. We also loved the spacious shower and bathroom. The staff was friendly and helpful at check in or if we just had a question. Not a lot in the immediate area, but shopping and restaurants are a short drive away and the Speedway was less than a 30 minute drive. Breakfast had a good variety of choices. Nice indoor pool with whirlpool/hot tub also. After a day of walking all around the racetrack, the whirlpool jets were just what my aching legs needed - THANKS Hampton.

title: “Nicest Place for the money south of 183~”
text: Great Staff! Fantastic Room! QUIET~~~~~~ Breakfast was exceptional and there was PLENTY of it too! We'd stay here again and make the Big Mariott next door the number 2 choice!

title: “No guarantees on rooms”
text: Booked thru hotels.com. Thought I'd prepaid for two queens. Got there and sold out. Sorry. U get two doubles. Read the "fine" print is what I was told Hotel too busy and crowded. Elevators are horrible . Will not stay here again

title: “Spacious rooms, convenient location”
text: All suites provide lots of room for a family. There is a pull out sofabed and a separate bedroom. Both rooms have TVs. Coffee, creamer and sugar are provided with a coffee maker, a microwave and small refrigerator in the "living" room space occupied by the sofabed and a desk. Free Wi-Fi is also provided. What's NOT provided is breakfast. Most hotels these days offer a continental breakfast. The restaurant served a breakfast buffet for $8.95 with coffee, tea or soft drink, cereal, juice, fruits, eggs, bacon, sausage, grits, potatoes, biscuits and gravy. During the week, the buffet offers made-to-order waffles and/or omlets. Overall, it's a comfortable hotel, but priced at over $100 per night, I expected breakfast to be included.

title: “Wonderful Room, Great Hotel!”
text: We stayed here for one night to be close to the airport for an early morning flight out of LAX the next day. We were blown away by the beautiful lobby, the many restaurants (didn't get a chance to try any though!), and the fantastic room! We paid $139 for a double and the beds were luxurious! The room was wonderful and the free shuttle to the airport cannot be beat! I would definitely stay here again, it was worth every penny!

title: “World Class Service”
text: My wife and I stayed for two nights and were absolutely stunned to find world class service. We have travelled extensively throughout the world and have stayed in all classes of hotels. The staff and facilities of the Fairmont are equal to the leading hotels in major international cities (Hong Kong, New York, Seoul, San Francisco, Miami, Las Vegas etc.) We were given a complimentary upgrade to the Gold Floor and the already exquisite stay got even better. The location (four blocks to Georgetown or METRO) was perfect for exploring the city, shopping and night life. Aboslutely recommended.

title: “Metro Plaza Hotel”
text: First lets get something clear, this hotel is not a five star hotel so do not expect a restaurant or room service or flawless environment. This hotel gives you what it promises. Clean room in a clean and safe environment with an air conditioner and tv. I went to LA on a business trip and stayed in this hotel for 10 nights. Fine service, really clean rooms, nice staff and clean bathrooms. On a budget i got everything i needed. Location is also good as it is in near proximity to everything... about 20 minutes from glendale and 20 minutes from all areas... however it is 35 to 40 minutes from LAX which is fine depending on the traffic. You have restaurants near by as well as corner shops. another advantage it is 15 seconds away form the most popuylar sandwich bar in LA called Phillipe's which is great!!! bear in mind people drive for two hours just to come here and try the sandiwhces... it is in china town so you can also explore the area. the only negative thing about this area is that after 7 all the homeless and drug addicts come out so it can get a bit eerie. however just call a cab and sit in right outside the hotel so its never a problem. Service is good and fast. Overall got everything i asked for in a hotel of budget, no complaints what so ever and will most definitely stay there again if traveling on a budget. Highly Recommended!!

title: “GREAT...”
text:
Great place... read review just prior to this one and he says it all very well.... was there in April 2007 ... 2nd time in SF/Union square in past year.....
TIP: This hotel is affordable enough to just book it outright.... NOT worth playing games on HOTWIRE to get a "Union Square" hotel for $30 less b/c it can very shady very quickly .... 
The Powell is another nice affordable choice w/slightly bigger rooms... but overall the location, nice breakfast and value of the STRATFORD i will def go back there next time in SF....

title: “Nice Place”
text: I stayed here for 3 nights on business. This was my second time here. This hotel is very clean and comfortable and reasonably priced for what you get. Breakfast was typical for a Quality Inn. I’ll stay here again next time I’m in the area.

title: “Great hotel, fabulous location, pretentious staff!”
text:
The Tribeca Grand is a lovely stylish hotel in a fabulous location. Just on the doorstep of Greenwich Village, Soho, Little Italy & China Town and only a short walk to Lower East Side.
The lobby and room decor are relaxing and funky; I personally loved the dim lighting (it reminded me of The Clift Hotel in San Francisco).
The rooms are fairly spacious with everything you need to relax, bathrobes, comfy beds, free wifi etc.
The housekeeping department was outstanding, linen changed daily, rooms cleaned thoroughly, toiletries replenished everyday. 
We booked to include breakfast, however this was sparse to say the least. Either a choice of toast, bagel or pastries plus orange juice. Unfortunately they didn't have any fruit tea so I brought my own.
A little more choice would have been nice, some fresh fruit would have been appreciated. 
The biggest let down with breakfast was the pretentious staff, too busy talking to each other and preening themselves to be attentive. Yes they are good looking and hip but boy don't they know it!
This issues with the staff was apparent throughout the hotel with the exception of the housekeeping staff and the bell boys. The porter on the door (i believe he was from San Francisco but i'm not sure of his name) was extremely friendly, helpful and cuteous.
If The Tribeca Grand addressed the issues regarding certain members if staff it could become a great hotel not just a good one.
Having said this I wouldn't hesitate to return if the price was right!

title: “Hilton Club - Nice Place in the Heart of Midtown”
text: Select floor at the gigantic New York Hilton are dedicated to the Hilton Club. The Hilton Club offers the standards and kind of room you'd expect from a Hilton with the added convenience and service of a dedicated club room - serving a nice, light breakfast, snacks and drinks. The club is staffed with pleasant, knowledgeable personnel to assist with front desk and concierge duties. Rooms were last renovated in 2008, but still in good shape. Great Midtown location. Hotel accommodates large groups and conventions so elevator / lobby traffic can be heavy.

title: “Such a good deal for the price !”
text: I have stayed at the Marcel too many times to even count. I keep coming back to stay each time I'm in NYC because the Marcel is a small, friendly, boutique-ish hotel (by no means super luxe) that knows how to treat their clientel very well. The Marcel must be a great place to work because the staff through out the hotel from the front door guys to the front desk guys are the same group of people year after year. This lends to a really convial atmosphere and a team that could not be more helpful or accomodating. The rooms are cute (some cuter than others) with a sort of "design flair" decor. The bathrooms are not amazing, sort of dated and small but the comfortable ease at the Marcel just seems to make up for that, its sort of homey in a weird way. The roof garden deck and lounge area is really nice to hang out in especially during the week when the hotel in not super crowded. The view of the Empire State builiding in your chaise lounge a top the Marcel roof on crisp stary NYC evening would be tuff to match at any hotel. I could have my pick of places to stay in NYC but somehow the great welcome, chill atmosphere and excellent valure of the Marcel ( not to mention the quick walk to my office) keep me coming back, happily !

title: “Stil Retains Old Style Service”
text:
A sister hotel of the amazing Athenee Palace in Paris and if not at that standard, this aging hotel retains staff that really do care and are not just itinerant hotel workers. 
Fantastically located, busy and bustling but retaining a fair degree of personal attention.

title: “Stress Tested And A Pass With Flying Colours!”
text:
We have enjoyed our previous 5 or 6 stays at The Gansevoort enormously - excellent rooms, comfortable beds, great views and at the epicentre of, perhaps the most vibrant, and attractive scene in Manhattan. Superb shopping, amazing array of eateries all around, for those younger than us more night -life than you can handle, close proximity to The Hudson River and its attractive parkways, Chelsea Piers and the ground breaking High Line - a masterpiece of imaginative urban regeneration and renewal. 
Our 12 day visit in June really stress tested the hotel because one of us was not well and we had to spend lots and lots of time either confined to our room or within the hotel. The staff were so helpful and worked round us without complaint to service our room when convenient to us. We had lots of room service, all of which was prompt, well presented and value for money and the Concierge made helpful arrangements for medical care. 
There cannot be many Hotels in Manhattan that could make a difficult time experienced by us, as comfortable and reassuring as did all those staff at The Gansevoort Hotel. And if you are going to be stuck at your hotel for long periods, then lazing on relaxing loungers beside the roof-top pool appreciating the beautiful bodies all around and incredible views across The Hudson River to New Jersey, can't be all bad! 
To all of you at The Gansevoort.....stand up and take a bow ......you are stars.
We Shall be back!

title: “Excellent”
text:
We had an awesome time!!!! The rooms and hotel were in excellent condition, the staff and management were great and went above and beyond to assist us. 
I will definitely come back. 
Thank you Valencia for a great stay!!!

title: “Underwhelming”
text:
This was our first trip to New York and we'd always fancied a stay at this famous establishment.
Well it took three attempts at getting an acceptable room!! First one still had previous guest's make-up and tissues in the drawers and large stains on upholstery. Second one was clean but very ordinary, third one clean and spacious.
Restaurant downstairs kept us waiting for nearly half an hour after our booked time before we were able to sit down. A supposedly medium steak was in fact very rare, which meant another long wait for that person whilst we others proceeded with our meal. Quality of the steaks were otherwise super.
It is an interesting place to just sit in the lobby and people watch but it appears to be rather tired.

title: “First time in Chicago and it was wonderful. Staff/accomodations were outstanding. Will definitely stay again when I re”
text: Everyone was extremely courteous and professional. This was my first trip to Chicago and everyone made me feel at home. They answered all my questions and provided great details and information on places to go.

title: “Close to the Alamo & River Walk”
text: The closeness to the Alamo and River Walk are a plus for this hotel. The 2 star review doesn't do it justice. The only problem that we had with the hotel was our door would not close on its own. Told them about it 3 or 4 times and nothing was done about it by the time we left. Was good for the money, and the proximity to the Alamo, River Walk, Tower of the Americas, & Rivercenter Mall!! Would stay again!!

title: “Great Value!”
text: Yep the rooms were small...you're in New York City, you're not supposed to be in your room! We literally were there only to sleep and shower. The entire place was very clean; all the employees were very helpful and pleasant. This was my first time to New York City and I wasn't too crazy about Times Square, I guess you gotta see it though, but if I do go back to the Times Square area that's where I'm staying!

title: “Pleasantly surprised!”
text: This hotel surpassed our expectations! The room was very clean and the staff was always friendly, helpful, and quick to meet our needs. The only problem we had was that the WIFI connection was often very slow and would frequently drop. Their beds are rather firm (not a complaint, just a heads up). This location is centrally located, making it easy and quick to get to destinations. We would stay at this hotel again.

title: “Great hotel for a chic break on a budget”
text:
I visited this hotel with my husband for a romantic week away in New York. We were looking for all the comforts of a luxury hotel, but without the hefty price tag that comes with many of the top NYC hotels. And that's exactly what we got. From the moment we stepped through the door it was easy to forget that this is only a 3* hotel. The decor is classy and the lighting remincsent of a chic evening bar. The welcome was warm and the information full.
The rooms were well sized and the bed uber-comfy. The romms and communal areas were well air-conditioned, which was hugely weelcomed considering the May heat outside!
The bathroom was large, and the little extras were far more than you'd get in a hotel of simialar rating in the UK. I was particularly impressed with the his & hers bathrobes and slippers, and also the little bottles of conditioner (I expect shower gel, body lotion and shampoo as standard, but girls will understand that complimentary hotel shampoos often leave your hair feeling like straw so the little bottles of conditioner were a great touch!)
The hotel provides a complimentary breakfast, which was a lovely surprise because it was advertised as room-only in our hotel brochure. Alright, it wasn't out-of-this-world but considering it was free it was pretty good. A range of bagels, pastries, muffins, donuts, plus tea and fresh orange juice. And if you fancied something more, there was a menu of cooked options for reasonable prices. The hotel also caters at lunch and evening, although it always looked pretty empty, and there are so many places to eat in New York that we never got round to sampling it.
The bar area is lovely, but the prices are typically hotel (it cost us $21 plus tip for a beer and a Jack & coke). It was nice for a quick drink after a long night, but you can get two or three rounds for the same price elsewhere.
If there was one thing that lets the hotel down a litttle it's the lifts/elevators. There are only two lifts (plus the service lift) and it just isn't enough for 46 floors. You could spend five minutes just waiting for the lift to arrive, and when it did it was jam packed.
Locationally Flatotel is PERFECT. It's ten blocks (about five minutes) from the middle of Times Square and has the advantage of being just off the main street so is fairly quiet for a good night's sleep. Central park is five minutes away, as are Fifth Avenue for shopping and the Rockerfeller Centre. 
We loved our stay in New York and would stay at the Flatotel again in a snap.

title: “A posh modern hotel steps from the Capitol.”
text: I stayed at the JW Marriott for a conference. The lobby and public areas are stunning with thick carpeting and high ceilings. The rooms are furnished with modern furniture, and thick comforters. The rooms are small, but comfortable, and surprisingly quiet for the middle of a city. There are surprising touches throughout the hotel. The elevators are set up so that you enter a number of a floor, and a digital display tells you which elevator to get on. There is a nice gym on one of the lower floors. The bar also serves a fairly full menu. And there is a full size Starbuck's off the main lobby. The hotel is located close to several metro stops. There are many nearby restaurants. If you are sightseeing, you could walk to the Mall. I would recommend this hotel for either business or for a sightseeing trip. If you are driving, parking is off premises.

title: “Decent hotel in Universal City”
text:
My husband booked the room with the Hilton directly for the 2 of us. Upon arrival , we were given a room with 2 double beds, even though we had requested a king or queen. They have no wait list , so we had to check everyday to change rooms. Finally two days later a king was available, though they had no record at all of our request! After speaking to no less than 6 people! None the less, the rooms were very clean , very spacious with decent views. 
Room service menu is extensive and the food was excellent (pricey, of course).
The pool is very nice with an oasis like feel with lawn and cabanas , but poolside service is lacking. You have to really hunt for menus and a phone to place an order. It seems it would benefit everyone greatly to have easy access to smoothies, snacks and cocktails poolside. Nice hottub also.
It is a very large hotel so there is no real personal service, and often long waits for the elevator. 
The location is ideal, of course, for Universal area attractions, but a long way from LAX, Hollywood and the beach. Self-park is $15 a day, valet $20 a day.
Overall nice property. I would return if I had an event in Burbank/Universal CIty area.

title: “Just what you'd expect”
text:
Again a review that should be a half lower, but we can't factor in 1/2 ratings. Since their we're really no gotchas, rated it higher.
Location is not bad, but the shuttle from the Airport took forever to pick me up, we'll over an hour wait. Restaurants are about a half mile walk, and serval choices which are very good.
Room was as expected. Breakfast was okay, but the oatmeal was prepared very poorly. Managers reception did not include any drinks, which was a bit disappointing. Again the overall rating is a little high.
Stayed on an upper level floor, no noise issues that I noticed. Front desk staff did a good job. Would consider staying again when in Boston.

title: “Nice place for families”
text:
Large rooms-bigger than some apartments.
We stayed in a 2-room suite that had a seperate bedroom with a queen bed. Full kitchen, 2 full baths, dining area, living area with full sleeper sofa and fireplace.
The room was clean and well kept.
The kitchen was stocked with dishes and cookware.
There is a large outdoor pool with hot tub and tennis and basketball courts.
Guest laundry and free continental breakfast.
During the week, there is an evening social hour with free food and drinks.
Location is good with plenty of shopping and restaurants.
Staff is friendly and helpful.
The only drawbacks are the difficulty getting in and out of the parking lot onto the main road because of traffic and with the hospital close by, sirens at night.
We will stay again.

title: “Awful staff and poor service”
text:
I met awful staff she is a one of guest manager at the hotel.
Actually this hotel made a big mistake for my certain package and I had very inconveniences, however, the lady come up on the phone was so arrogant and temporize lots of excuses which are very inconsistency, but she never admit her mistakes. Not professional at all.
To my great surprise, she ordered front desk staff to ignore my calls since she worried to be pointed out her mistake, 
Also hotel description says there is "business center", but it is actually only one computer and printer which is broken.
Furthermore, one night no hot water running so I have to stay till after midnight and had to in wet bath towel till pluming work finished more than one hour.
This hotel is not Hyatt quality at all. Never recommend to stay here if you do not want to ruin the time in NY.

title: “Not a great hotel, but you could do worse”
text:
First off, my double room did not have queen beds, as advertised, they are full size. Also, they are spring mattresses, and fairly uncomfortable. I had very poor wireless internet in my room, (kept getting kicked off) which was at the end of one of the wings.
Staff was friendly and helpful, as far as they could be.
Hard to recommend this place without better beds and internet.

title: “Brisk and efficient but soulless”
text: A conference hotel in the architectural style of Stalin-discovers-concrete. Pretty it ain't and the balcony views look out on more of the same though you can see the Bay without standing on the wardrobe. Overnight parking rates are outrageous so don't even think about it unless you're one of the 1%. Breakfast can be eye-wateringly expensive too so try the Ferry Terminal nearby for something more reasonable. I've stayed here a couple of times and what it lacks in cosines and atmosphere it makes up for in business-like efficiency. The bathroom mirrors that deliver news and weather video streams are great fun - though not all rooms have these - and the knowledge of staff on the concierge desk is immense. Overall, it's a good place for a conference butit's a bit soulless if you're in SF for a getaway break.

title: “PERFECT”
text: From the moment you arrive till the moment you leave , the service is impeccable and they just make you feel like the most important person on earth . The location is great , near Newburry st. where you find good restaurants and nice shops . My wife was as happy as me . It is just a great place to stay and don't forget to talk with Jimmy the valet who is now 85 years old , in perfect shape and can talk to you about the Worl War 2 like if it was yesterday , Just a great person . Thanks for the great service .

title: “mindblowing!!”
text:
Well, What Can i say. 
This was a great hotel. Not brilliant but nearly there. 
I will deal with the criticism first;
1. Air - Con was tempremental.
2. No pool facilities, spa etc. 
3. Check in is a little hit and miss. 
The positives;
1. Brilliant location.
2. Large rooms (by new york standards)
3. Comfortable bed. 
4. Fantastic foyer - a visual delight.
5. Great bathroom. 
6. Friendly staff, nothing was too much trouble, 
Firstly, being next to Grand Central Station was a treat - the food hall in the lower area of the station is cheap and tasty. The pizza was especially good. There is no problem bringing food into the hotel, it is so big that no one would notice. There are not that many places to eat out in the evening close by that are particularly charming, its mostly tgi's, red lobster food. But, it is near to everywhere and provided you don't mind a ten minute walk there are plenty of places to eat. 
There are alot of deli type shops nearby that do salad boxes etc. these were delicious and inexpensive. Being next to grand central station breakfast is no problem, there are plenty of coffee shops. 
If you go out of the main door there is a fantastic diner under the railway arches. Breakfast is quite pricey but the pancakes were to die for. 
The front desk held bags on the last day of your stay and there are very good bathrooms downstairs in the hotel to allow you to freshen up. 
This hotel is enormous but the staff are lovely and when my ring disappeared down the sink the maintenence guy was there in minutes. The room was cleaned to a high standard. 
The main criticism was the air -con being a bit tempremental. We went in April and the weather was not overly warm but we had to sleep with the window open as the air con didn't work that well. New York is a noisy place, i loved the noise but i imagine many would not. 
Did alot of shopping arond for the best price and the hyatt website was the cheapest!!
Bryant Park and the Library are a few minutes walk, Times Square about 7 or 8 minutes. The Empire States Building about ten minutes. It really was brilliantly located. 
Although you miss the bars and restaraunts of greenwich, location wise it is perfect for sightseeing. Please walk through new york, it's safe, charming and i can't wait for my next trip. 
I would definatley stay here again, the hotel to me summed up new york perfectly big, bold, busy and classy!!

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text: Recently my wife and I stayed at the Hyatt for 4 nights. The hotel was very nice with exzcellent service . The hotel staff could not do enough for you. The sports bar has decent food and is a great place to watch a sporting event.

title: “Why all the negative reviews? W is for wonderful.”
text:
I had booked the W New York through Hotwire for a last-minute trip that required only one night's stay. After reading the reviews of the hotel I worried about what I had gotten myself into-- I kept reminding myself that it was only for one night. 
I was given a room on the 9th floor-- which to my surprise was totally refurbished and quite spacious by New York standards. There was a well-stocked minibar, a flat-screen TV with DVD player, an internet connection, and an ipod docking station. What more could one ask for? The decor is sleek and minimalist; unique was the sliding glass door to the bathroom (by not having a door that swings into the bath one actually gets the feeling of a more spacious bathroom). The room was, dare I say it, almost sexy. 
The clientele at the hotel bar would fit that description as well-- at 5pm on a Thursday afternoon the place was filled with young, moneyed trendsetters starting their weekend (very) early. It looked like a fun environment that I imagine gets quite wild on a Friday or Saturday night.
