The concierge was friendly and the check-in/out process was smooth. My only complaint was the lack of both a room service menu and phone book in my room; in addition, the E. 40s-50s aren't my favorite part of New York, but fortunately Grand Central is mere blocks away.

title: “Fantastic location, price & service!”
text: This hotel really is a new york gem. I have stayed here a few times and each time has been brilliant. As there was 4 adults we booked one of the family rooms which works out a great rate, it had 3 double beds and a seperate bedroom. The staff are all friendly and very helpful. You even get a free breakfast here which is basic but good. I have Coeliacs so i brought my own food from the uk and toasted my crumpets every morning which the staff were fine with. Such a fantastic location, 30 seconds to Macys and a few minutes to Bryant Park. The roof terrace is also pretty fab during the summer months... what a view! Overall fantastic visit every time.

title: “A Satisfactory Weekend Stay”
text:
Enticed by the $84 weekend rate, I selected the Courtyard Sorrento/La Jolla for a Friday night stay. If you are familiar with the Courtyard brand, this follows the blueprint. This is an older property, and the rooms still have the midnight blue carpet and the soft yellow wallpaper. There are signs that the hotel has seen better days - the lamps were misaligned, and there were scratches on the wall. But aside from the usual wear and tear, the room was clean and functional.
The hotel caters to business travelers, but there is pool and outdoor seating. The lobby has been updated, and the Bistro serves breakfast and basic meals. The Karl Strauss Brewery is a two-minute walk, so if you don’t have a car, this is a good dining option. Starbucks and Jamba Juice are two minutes in the opposite direction.
It is evident the hotel aims to please. I received a handwritten note on the morning of check out. When I stopped by the front desk, the associate was genuinely interested in my hotel experience. This was refreshing in an era where service is the exception rather than the rule.
In summary, many hotels do a lot less with a lot more. This is not a brand new property with dazzling amenities. But the commendable service, clean rooms, and the superb $84 rate add up to a satisfactory weekend stay.

title: “Excellent Hotel in Central Location”
text: We stayed this past weekend at the Hilton Garden Inn W35th. Simply, excellent. On arrival we were greeted immediately by the Concierge on duty Thomas Coll and served superbly by the Guest Relations Manager, T. Nascimento. Our room on the 20th floor, was very large and although beside the elevator was very quiet. Bed, was excellent with the ability to make it firmer or softer. Temperature controls worked excellent. There was a small fridge and a microwave. Coffee and tea. Overall an excellent room. Service within the hotel was friendly. All staff we encountered from Housekeeping to Maintenance to Servers in the restaurant always greeted you. Coffee and Tea downstairs was superb. At 5pm there were cookies and again coffee and tea. On departure, Thomas the Concierge, recommended an excellent limo service to take us flawlessly back to Newark Airport. W35th was temporarily blocked at that time due to a large crane in front of the hotel, yet Thomas communicated with the Limo driver as to exactly what time to pick us up and carried our bags to the vehicle. Excellent service Thomas, and thank you. Overall, an excellent stay and my wife and I would highly recommend this very nice hotel totally centrally located next to Macy's and all sorts of other interesting sites.

title: “fantastic, absolutely marvellous”
text: we had a fantastic time . we got married in the chapel at graceland. we had our honeymoon at heartbreak, we stayed nine nights,and did not want to leave. we up graded to the hollywood suite. geat room. very elvis presley style . the staff was very helpful and courteous. deffinately reccommend it. we can not wait to go back.

title: “Great hotel, especially for the price, but not particularly *trendy*”
text:
i booked this hotel for two reasons: a) it was ranked as one of tripadvisor’s top 10 trendiest hotels in the US for 2011 and b) it was priced right. 
the reviews are true: it’s definitely a four-star hotel at three-star prices. large slick rooms with hardwood floors, free parking, free (speedy, especially for free and hotel) wi-fi, and a flat-panel TV (albeit with very limited HD channels) with DVD player. you also get an in-room microwave, fridge, and keurig single-serving coffee machine. to go with these: a selection of k-cups, a pack of microwave popcorn, and two bottles of water to wash it all down. the beds are comfortable, towels plush.
a couple of minor quibbles:
* i had to wait to be checked in because there was only one person at reception and he had to juggle three phone calls before getting to me. still, i wasn’t in a rush, so not a big deal.
there was (raw) sugar, splenda, and equal, but no creamer, so i couldn’t enjoy any coffee (not worth calling for).
* the lotion, shampoo, conditioner, and soap are tommy bahama, which doesn’t fit with the hotel’s vibe. yes, it does have a tropical scent (to go with their pineapple theme), but tommy bahama is a bit too jimmy buffet when the hotel is trying to be jimi hendrix.
given the hotel’s great pricing, amenities, and location (just blocks away from seattle center), i’m definitely staying here again the next time i visit seattle! i wouldn’t call it trendy, though, just modern and well-themed.

title: “Great Location, basic service”
text:
As part of my series for my trip down the Eastern Megalopolis (Boston-DC), this is the Philadelphia stop. Like my hotel in New York, this was booked through the Air Canada website for Aeroplan points.
Initial impressions: We had travelled from New York to Philadelphia, arriving at the hotel around 11:30am. We walked the short distance from Suburban Station and went to check-in. Upon arriving, the gentleman verified our details and then asked if we'd like to leave our baggage. We seemed a bit confused so he explained that a check-in before 15:00 was charged $35. While I know that most hotels prefer that you not check-in before a certain time, if they have a room available they'll give it to you. I had never in my life heard of being charged for showing up 3.5 hours early. So, not wanting to pay effectively $10/hour for what would essentially be baggage storage, we left our bags with the front desk and went off for a bit. When we did finally check-in, while the gentleman did it for us, it would appear that all check-in/out functions are to be done on a kiosk. While I can appreciate that some prefer this manner, I personally do like having a bit of a personal touch when at a hotel. It's not like checking-in for a flight where over the course of the trip you'll encounter several members of that airline's staff. At a hotel, you often only get one or two chances for your company to make an impression. If I'm told to just use a machine, I get no personal engagement and I have no reason to want to reward that company with future business.
Location: Philadelphia is a very small city in many respects and the Club Quarters sits in the heart of the business, shopping and nightlife areas. A short walk to the towers of Center City and the shopping and restaurants of Rittenhouse Square and Walnut Street, and only a 15-20 minute walk to areas like the Gayborhood, the cultural areas around the Ben Franklin Institute and the Philadelphia Museum of Art (made famous by its steps and little-known boxer named Ricky... or something like that :) ) and the historical Independence Hall and Penn Landing areas, the location can't really be beat. Suburban Station is about 5 minutes away, which provides easy access to the airport and most of the SEPTA Regional Rail lines. 30th Street Station, where Amtrak goes in and out of, is not too far away either.
The Room: Finally being able to check in (after getting caught in a torrential downpour), we were able to check-in. The room was of decent size, was clean and had a complimentary bag of trail mix in thanks for putting up with an elevator modernization program that apparently slowed down service. To be honest, I didn't really notice any delays. The washroom was basic but decent, with a shower, sink and toilet, as well as a decent counter area for storage. The bed was quite comfortable, though as with other hotels, they only give you one pillow if you're two in the bed. Especially when they're down pillows, I like to have to since I sleep on my side.
Amenities: Being a business hotel, it's fairly basic, though there are some nice touches. The lobby is set up like a large business lounge. There are chairs, complimentary newspapers, as well as tea and coffee in the morning and water all day long. There are three computer workstations with complimentary internet access. I believe rooms have wireless internet as well, but I didn't bring my computer with me. There is a Davio's restaurant connected to the hotel, which is a nice place and certainly better than a lot of hotel restaurants. However, should you not be feeling Italian, there are no shortages of other places in the area.
Summary: Great place for business travellers. It's extremely quiet so I wouldn't probably recommend it for families travelling with young children. However, if you want a place that's a bit above bare bones, has internet and a great location, I'd recommend this place. The staff is friendly and the rooms are pretty nice. Given the price we got it for, I'd consider staying here again.

title: “Great Stay at Residence Inn”
text: We just returned from a 3 night stay at the Residence Inn Sorrento Mesa. As a long time Trip Advisor user, I researched a number of hotels before settling on a property for our first San Diego visit. I booked a good rate directly thru the hotel website. This Residence Inn lived up to its good reviews. We received a friendly welcome upon arrival. We were somewhat concerned as we pulled into the parking lot to see a very large portable generator humming along right next to the lobby. When we checked in we found out that the local utility company shut down power to many local businesses for the first two days of our stay and the hotel obtained a generator so as not to inconvenience guests. The generator was obviously up to the job, because we didn't notice any problems. We had a one bedroom queen suite which was spacious enough for the 3 or us. My 10 year old slept on the sleeper sofa and it was of better quality than many sleepers or rollaways we've had to use before. It would probably fit two children or one adult comfortably. Our bed was very comfortable and having the kitchen (full size fridge, microwave and dishwasher) was a plus. The pool and hot tub were great after a long day of seeing the sights! The property had a mix of families and business travelers. The complimentary breakfast was definitely a step above the standard "continental" fare with scrambled eggs, waffles, hashbrowns and variations of sausages, biscuits and gravy and croissants in additional to the more traditional offerings. The property is a good ways from downtown, but with a rental car it was still very convenient to all of the sights (about 15 minutes to each of the major attractions). A good map (or get directions on the complimentary internet access!) and it was pretty easy to get around! Our only complaint (and the ONLY reason we did not rate the property an Excellent) was that the airconditioning unit was pretty loud. The rooms were all very quiet and we didn't hear anything of our neighbors, but at night when the AC cycled on it was enough to wake both my husband and I. We tried turning it off, but the room was too stuffy, so ended up leaving the AC running all night. It was still a bit loud and took some getting used to, but was preferrable to being startled awake each time it kicked on! Overall, it was a great stay and we would definitely book there for future visits to San Diego!

title: “Mixed feelings about this place...”
text:
It is with mixed feeling that I have to give this place a negative review overall.
My son and I travelled to the USA in April of 2008 (holiday of a lifetime so far for me) starting in LA then to SF across to Boston then down to Martha's Vineyard and finishing in NYC at the Amsterdam before heading back home to Australia. This hotel was the worst we stayed at during our 3 weeks. But I need to qualify a few things.
NEGATIVES:
There is massive construction still taking place next door and it will continue for some time. Construction work starts exactly at 7.00am however, the workers turn up much earlier and start making a LOT of noise. The Amsterdam is literally about 3 feet away from the construction. It is very, very noisy during the week because of this. Trust me on this!!! But, to be fair, there is construction taking place all over NYC.
Rooms are very small and the sheets and blankets are thin. No elevator, tables, chairs, air-conditioning or coffee making facilities.
No elevators at all so you must haul your luggage up at least one fight of steep stairs
POSSITIVES:
Location. Everything and I mean everything is just a few blocks away. Subway, diner, grocery store, laundromat, tons of other places to eat, Central Park, bar, museum, Broadway, drug-store and on and on and on.
Bathroom was very clean and the cleaning staff were efficient and approachable.
I found all the staff friendly and helpful. If you have had negative experiences, then maybe it was your approach.
CONCLUSION: I would not stay here again UNTIL the construction work is finished. This is a very noisy place currently. Then again, you do not travel to NYC for peace and quiet. If you are not spending much time in your room (and who wants to?) then this place is okay. All the above aside we had a fantastic time in NYC and I would do it again tomorrow if I could.

title: “Mixed views about our stay”
text: We have mixed reviews about our stay at Chelsea Lodge. I knew what to expect but my partner was very underwhelmed when we arrived and saw our room It was tiny with a double bed, no toilet (as I already knew) and a shower in our room. During the night we were both very hot and uncomfortable, there was no way (that we knew of) to control the heat. The pipes made loud noise and in the morning it was very loud outside of our room in the lobby. People talking and walking up and down the stairs. The second night my partner was very sick from some seafood that he ate. We contemplated leaving the hotel as he was sick and uncomfortable, but we stayed and left first thing in the morning. Our stay was ok but I probably would not stay again.

title: “Great place to stay for the Big East Tournament”
text: I arrived the day before the BE tourney, and was greeted very warmly and very professional. Upon checking in they switched my room and I almost said something but kept quite, and thought is it was small I would ask to be moved. To my surprise my room was very large, had a desk, small fridge, a small pull out love seat, and a very large bathroom. I was put in a handicap accessible room. What a grate experience. Thank you New Yorker!!

title: “Outstanding”
text:
This hotel is outstanding.
From the moment I arrived and was met by the valet parking attendant, I knew this was going to be good.
Check in staff was pleasant and helpful. 
 I think because of my status, which I think is only preferred and not even to the silver level, I got a free breakfast buffet coupon. It was a full American breakfast buffet. Great surprise!
The hotel room was clean, updated and you have to love the bedding. 
Only two comments and they are both nits: 1) during the check in process, the check in staff person stated, “the valet parking costs are included in your bill”, which I thought meant “included in the price”, but what he really meant was the cost ($32) for the valet service will be “added” to the bill. 2) It seemed like the hot water was running low (I was on the 20th floor), as I had to keep increasing the hot water amount during my shower. Kind of an odd experience at a hotel, almost like being at your house after several people have taken a shower.
Overall though, a great hotel. Highly recommend this place

title: “Great deal, Great Location!”
text: I usually don't write reviews but I am an avid reader of reviews and I know how important they are. This was my second time in Seattle,last time I stayed at the INN at The Market. I debated whether to stay here or the Hyatt which was right in front of it. I got this room through Quikbook for 129.00 the night, the Hyatt was at 170.00. The rooms from the website looked less luxurious than the Hyatt but I have to say photos were deceiving. Very comfortable room, beds were queens not fulls. So comfortable. I slept better on these beds than the famous heavenly beds of the Westins where we had just stayed at when we came down from Vancouver. Small lobby very intimate but best of all was location. Two blocks away from all the shopping,Nordstrom, Barnes and Noble, West lake center and the monorail 3 blocks down. Pike Place market is about 6 blocks down on the same street. Don't know the concierges name, it would be the older man in the morning but he had great recommendations for restaurants, each one excellent and was so knowledgeable about the city and when was the best times to go to events. Highly recommend this hotel rooms, they were nice and clean and very comfortable. The best thing is they have an empty fridge so you can put all your goodies that you buy from pike place inside

title: “Great Hotel and Great Location”
text:
Travelling on my own I chose the New York Palace after a recommendation by a friend and stayed here for a week over the Memorial Day holiday. Hotel was fantastic more than I had expected. The staff at reception were very nice and helpful and checkin quick and all done with a smile. Requested the use of a kettle for my stay and it was delivered to my room and had it for the duration of my holiday. All the staff I came into contact with during my stay were very welcoming and happy to help which seemed the opposite to some of the reviews of the hotel.
The rooms are big in comparision to some hotels I've stayed in in New York. Huge king size bed, a big flat screen tv, not that I watched much on it as was busy seeing the city. The bathroom was a good size and the shower was great, lots of power and hot. Loved the makeup mirror and the nice Molton Brown toiletries. Room was very clean and bed turned down every night and 2 little chocolates left to enjoy. Loved the big safe as i could keep my ipad in it along with some expensive gifts. I did not use the mini bar or any of the drinks or food on top of cabinet as I knew they would be very expensive but with a Duane Reade drugstore 2 blocks away I got water, food and some toiletries I needed. 
The lobby area was always busy with people on their laptops, ipads and phones. It was a nice area to sit in and email family & friends but why not just give you it free in your room? Did not need to use the concierge as been to NYC so many many times and know it well but heard them giving out help and information to many guests and was amazed at there knowledge.
I had a room at the back of building on 15th floor with a view out to Park Ave which was fine as only spent time in the room to bring back my shopping/gifts and to sleep. it was a very nice quiet floor. I was on the side where the large crane was for most of my week stay and I never heard any noise from the work being done neither late into the night or early morning. There was a Starbucks opposite the entrance and every morning I headed down there for breakfast of a peach melba/granola pot and muffin all for around 8 dollars and well worth it, breakfast was just too expensive to eat in the hotel.
The hotel location was perfect, Madison Ave and 50th/51st Streets and one block to 5th Ave. I had all the shops I wanted so close to hand. Plenty of places to eat all so close to hand. I found Bills Bar & Burger Bar close to the Rockefeller Centre and it was a great place to eat in. The food was fantastic, it was on 51st St just off 5th Ave.
On the day I was checking out I had a late flight and asked if there were restrooms I could use to freshen up and was told I could use the showers and facilities in the fitness and spa centre as it was all complimentary. It was great as it was a hot humid day and around 5pm I was able to shower, freshen up my hair and change into my clothes for flight home. I thought this was a nice little perk for guests. Also on that day one of the porters was a real gent (unfortunately I cannot remember his name, very tall guy late 50's early 60's) I have a joint problem with one of my elbows and he very nicely weighed my case with travel scales I'd brought with me.
The New York Palace is a great hotel and if I can get as good a room rate as I had for this holiday on the next one then I will definitely be back. I've recommended it to all my family and friends and hopefully will return next time with my hubby.

title: “Very Good Value”
text: I enjoyed a small single room with shared bath in November 2002. The room was very small and austere, but comfortable and clean. The shower up the hall was spotless but very tiny - walk in and back out. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The location was first rate. It was a quiet safe neighbourhood near all the major attractions and transportation. For $79 a night Canadian - how could I complain. I only used the room to sleep in anyway. And I didn't see any naked people walking up the hall - as one reviewer put it. I will definitely stay there again.

title: “Close to everything.”
text: My family stayed here and loved the hotel. It was clean and had a great free breakfast. I visit the gym and I was really impressed. One day my family when coming into the hotel and it was pouring down raining. The hotel staff greeted us with warm towels to dry us off.

title: “Excellent in Every Way”
text: A colleague and I stayed 5 nights at the Shoreham while attending a conference in March and found it exceptional in its location, service, amenities, and overall comfort. The rooms ARE small, especially with a queen-sized bed, the water pressure in the shower is weak, and the hotel sign really ought to be lit for easier locating, but those were the only negatives. All of the staff were not only cordial and helpful, but went out of their way to ensure that we enjoyed our stay. At checkin, they explained every amenity the hotel had to offer--which included free videos and a free cappucino/coffee area. Our room had a vcr, cd player, safe, iron and ironing board, hairdryer, and very nice bath products--everything we could need for a short stay. We had no trouble getting a taxi and there are at least two subways within a short two block walk. One major plus for us was the amount of lighting in the room, which can be a problem in even the best hotels; there were overhead lights on the ceiling, above the bed, and along one wall, as well as individual table lamps on both sides of the bed. For someone who likes her room brightly lit and has a lot of evening ready to do, this was wonderful! We've stayed in the Marriot Marquis and the New York Hilton, and, while they are also top-notch, the Shoreham provides a quieter environment and friendlier, more personal service. We would definately stay there again.

title: “again a great stay in one of the kimpton hotels”
text:
Since I found this "chain" of hotels, I was never disappointed. I have stayed in Washington Georgetown, in Alexandria and in LA for the second time. This time with our teenage daughter, who loved it as much as we do.
The place is modern, rooms are roomy (we took the suite), and lobby is nice. The staff is very friendly and always ready with recommendations. We were recommended to have dinner at the napa valley grill. At the end of the dinner we received a plate with wonderful deserts because our hotel made the reservation for us. That was a nice touch!
The room was beautifully furnished, had very comfortable beds, even the pull-out bed for our daughter was comfortable. Service from all the employees was friendly and natural. We will definitely stay here again the next time in LA.

title: “Good value, good service and good location”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights on a business trip. 
1) Hotel has a small footprint with 8 rooms per floor.
2) Rooms are average size for NY, (smaller than other cities). 
3) Staff was very efficient and friendly. I had a couple of minor maintenance issues with the room which were addressed efficiently and speed.
4) I had a 3rd floor room facing the street, but street noise was not an issue
5) Had breakfast at the restaurant one day...typical overpriced hotel fare, (a lot of better values in the neighborhood).

title: “Not Bad”
text: I stayed here while on business in the area. Overall it the hotel is well kept and the rooms are your basic cookie cutter design with little personal feel. The staff at the desk is nice and the free breakfast is not bad. All in all I would stay here again. It was a good value for price.

title: “Great”
text:
Very comfortable rooms and amazing hospitality. We will be back next time in NYC
The location is amazing but busy with a lot of people but that's time square. The food is delicious. They treated us like kings

title: “Nothing spectacular; just a fine hotel.”
text:
Perfect location; lightning-fast check-in and check-out.
Room just average; very comfortable bed; desk with fax machine/printer; nice bathroom; tiny kitchenette.
Cord for high-speed internet, but prices and rates for the use nowhere to be found.
Thermostat broken in the room; AC blasting on high throughout the night; 60 degrees in the room (windows cannot be opened; could not turn off the AC beccause it would get too hot).
Old tube TV with crappy quality.
Regular check-in at 3pm; arrived at 1pm and had no problem cheking in.
Did not complain or had any interaction with the staff except for arrival/departure; therefore cannot comment on how problems are handled.

title: “I love the amenities of this hotel!”
text: This hotel is very service oriented. The rooms are clean & very nice and comfortable. The amenities of the full breakfast buffet, the evening free drinks & milk and cookies at bedtime are a fabulous bonus!

title: “great golf”
text: we just got back from 4 days at the rancho bernardo inn and we had a great time. the golf course is excellent - nicely maintained. we had a "stay and play" package which turned out to be pretty reasonable. our room was spacious and had a beautiful view of the golf course. restaurants are just "so so" and very expensive. the El Biz restaurant has a wonderful reputation but we didn't really like what we ordered for an entree. the pool is small for the size of the hotel and there aren't enough lounges on the pool deck. that's the only downside of the property. we would stay there again.

title: “Did You Hear About The Morgans?”
text:
Given the mediocre reviews the film received, it's probably not the most appropriate title, but it's the second Morgans hotel I've stayed in and the second great experience.
We'd stayed in the Mondrian in LA a few months previously and when I was going back to San Francisco, earlier this year, I only looked at the Clift. 
The room, the bar and the restaurant were all fantastic, but it was the staff that turned a good, stylish hotel into something really special. Thanks to Erica (great glasses), Noel and Kim (great Martinis) and especially to Jenny who was warm, funny and everything you'd hope your front of house would be. 
Next stop Miami, Boston, NYC . . . .

title: “Rude staff at check in”
text:
I stayed at the Westin Bonaventure on March 5, which was the evening before the LA Marathon. Granted, they were exceptionally busy, but the hotel parking lot was full and they very rudely told us to park in an independent lot across the street.
I had called 4 days prior to my stay requesting non-smoking with two double beds. At check in, the receptionist informed me that as a Priceline customer, I would get "any run of the mill room." In this case, smoking.
The carpets are dated and stained. The rooms are smallish, but decent. The lobby area is nice.
Overall, not 4 star hotel quality and if you book on Priceline, be prepared to be treated like a second class guest and they will tell you this to your face at check in.

title: “Much better than we expected!”
text: Having never visited New York before,i put my trust in my local travel agent to find me an affordable hotel,she came up with a great deal for flights and accomadation in a prime location.After looking on the internet and finding this site i was horrified to read so many bad reviews..rats!..rude hotel staff!dark dirty rooms!At this point i wanted to cancel.We are glad we didnt, as on arrival we found a team of helpful hotel staff who answered all questions we had,our room and bathroom were clean and cosy.The hotel is in a fab location for everything,the decor could do with a bit of a re-vamp but it will not ruin your stay here.This is an affordable hotel in the best location.

title: “Great location, amenable staff, good value”
text: I was very impressed with the Marriott East Side. Let me start by saying that I got an e-mail from the hotel about 3 days before our trip indicating that because they had a full house the night before we arrived, they weren't sure if they could meet our request of an early check in, and if they did they wouldn't guarantee the room type we wanted. So we had a plan to spend some time touring the city in the late morning/early afternoon in the expectation that we would not have access to the room, only to find they had upgraded us, provided a nicer room in the same type we had requested, and given us the early checkin we had wanted. So the staff was dealing aces from the very beginning and the rest of our stay was also great. Aside from the location which is close to everything in midtown and easy access to the subway, the next best thing about the hotel was a reasonable rate, particularly the deal we got for a 3 night weekend stay. In fact the only complaint of any kind that we had concerned a unexpected smell of cigarette smoke that seeped into our room around 10pm on the last night of our stay. It seemed to be coming in through the vent in the bathroom, which led me to believe that another guest was smoking in their bathroom even though the entire hotel is supposed to be non-smoking. We smelled it again in the morning so I reported it to the front desk upon checkout. Other than that random occurance, we had no complaints and would stay here again on a future trip to NYC.

title: “Convenient but small room!”
text: Stayed one night here with my wife on business. The only great thing is the location but otherswise the room was rather small and I'd say rather expensive and I would not stay here if I was paying myself. In general the service was good and the room was clean. There was a radio with an ipod dock and you can play your own ipod music easily. Some little special things like the memo paper was good quality with a "W' punched through it. I took several pieces of the paper as a souveneir!

title: “San Francisco Marriott - great hotel”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights in February 2007 over a long weekend. 
Our room was large and clean; and we had a nice view.
We had access to the concierge lounge, which was wonderful. They had pop, bottled water, coffee, tea, and snacks out 24-hours a day. There was a computer with free Internet access and printing available. There had a nice buffet breakfast, hot snacks and desserts out in the evening in the concierge lounge.
We took the subway/train from the airport to the hotel. The station was less than a 5 minute walk from the hotel. The hotel is also about a 5 minute walk to the street-car turn-a-round stop. There are quite a few malls and shopping areas around the hotel and it is about a 10 minute walk to Chinatown from the hotel.
There are other Marriott hotels in the Fisherman's Wharf area, which I would suggest staying at if you have small children or don't enjoy walking around a lot, because that is where most of the tourist action is at. The San Francisco Marriott is probably more suited for business people or shoppers. However, we don't mind walking around to get where we are going, so it was a great location for us.

title: “a fine stay”
text: I chose this place for a daddy-daughter weekend largely because of its location -- just opposite Marshall Fields on State and Washington. The highlight for me was the historic building that has been beautifully restored. The staff were very friendly, welcoming, and helpful. The rooms were well appointed and spotless. They also were very welcoming to my eight-year-old daughter. We had breakfast in the Atwood cafe in the lobby. The service was very good and service was fine as well. Would definitely recommend this for a weekend or other stay in downtown Chicago. Higher level rooms have a great view down State Street and are also a bit less noisy.

title: “Ideal spot for San Francisco stay”
text:
Stayed here with wife and 6 year-old son for two days SF sightseeing. Decent, clean rooms at a very competitive price with free parking. Located on a very quiet end of Lombard Street next to the Presidio with very easy bus access to all parts of the city.
Continental breakfast was as expected for similar stays we have had in California - coffee, juice, cereals and a pastry or two.
Many thanks go to Raymond, who is extremely knowledgeable about SF, its sights and things to do. He helped us with many aspects of our sightseeing and went out of his way to help us on more than one occassion.
We will be staying there the next time we visit San Fransisco, that's for sure.

title: “Fab location, good value for money if u are just looking for hotel to sleep in.”
text: Great location. So near Times Sq, Central Park, National History Museum etc. You can walk to all of these, no prob. Def recommend to anyone. Great value for money. We left early each morning and returned late each night so only interested in a hotel to sleep in. Rooms very average but got over it as was soooo excited about being in NY!! Hotel offers coffee and muffins in the morning. They are not great but will keep u goin until u get breakfast. 2 computers in the lobby. Very useful for maps etc. Hotel didnt charge for printing. We ate in the restaurant downstairs but thought it was a little overpriced. Nice food tho. Would defo stay again. Prices are great and would prefer to keep my money for clothes instead of spending on hotels!!

title: “Hotel Nine Zero, Boston”
text:
My wife & I love visiting Boston, we travel from Texas every summer to enjoy the city & catch a Red Sox game. For the past 3 trips in a row, we have stayed ath the Hotel Nine Zero. It is everything you expect from Kimpton - stylish decor, clean modern rooms, friendly & attentive service. For the price of other hotels in this area & around the Common, Hotel Nine Zero is great. We found the location to be perfect, 2 blocks from the Public Garden/Boston Common, and right on the Freedom Trail. It's about a 10 minute walk to Quincy Market. 
Every evening around 5pm they have a wine & cheese hour for the guests. Haven't sampled the restaurant, but there is a great pub with food just across the street. All in all, clean rooms, cool design and great location.

title: “Comfortably Average with friendly staff”
text:
Large beds and helpful staff. The rooms are equipped with an average renovation, new 42inch Philips flatscreen LCDs, and an old central air system (that has not been renovated). The closet space are definitely is from the 70s. Furniture are pretty much a 3.5*, but stretching a 4*. There is apparently no pool or sauna onsite, but it was suggested that it would have been possible to go to the Hilton Americana within a complimentary shuttle ride away (11 blocks).
The bonus are the fresh baked-styled cookies which the conceirge gives out when you check in. As a bonus for being a Hilton Honors Gold member, I was offered complimentary wifi. The staff were extremely helpful, and my room came with breakfast. 
You can pretty much get all the basics after a long flight ride and for a business trip. I would suggest it for someone who came to Houston just for the basics and need a place to stay without too much hassle. 
Overall: B+

title: “3 stars--NO WAY. Sorry guys this place is a dump.”
text: I have no idea why this hotel has three stars. It's pretty terrible. The decor, furniture, and electronics are extremely outdated. The fixtures are yellowed with age and the place smells of industrial cleaners admixed with mold. I fell sorry for this place. It looks like a holdover from glory days long past. It should definitely not keep it's 3 star rating. It needs a multimillion dollar overhaul. Customer service decent. Sketchy surroundings. I'd rather stay at a newly remodeled Motel 6....seriously.

title: “quality inn silver lake LA not quality!”
text: We needed a hotel in the Silver Lake area while visiting in Los Angeles and chose the Quality Inn at 250 Silver Lake Blvd. We had read very mixed reviews of this hotel but location was important to us. This is a very outdated hotel perched above busy Silver Lake Blvd. Walking in we were pleasantly greeted by the staff. The rooms in this hotel have entry from the outside so security wise we would suggest staying at least on the second floor and above. Neighborhood isn't the best so take precautions. The rooms are in dire condition with furniture uncomfortable at best. Bathrooms with dirty grout and generally in need of a redo. We could overlook the dated interior as we were only staying for a short stay, but could not accept the absolutely dirty wash cloths the maid brought us when cleaning the room! Poor quality, dirty linens just tipped this place over the edge. The only plus for this establishment is the price, $89.95 a night in LA is a bargain but you do get what you pay for. No recommendation for the Not Quality inn that is not near the convention center.

title: “Great stay with some nice touches”
text:
Stayed here recently for a wedding and had a great time. A few good points--
Nice pool area which I was not expecting. Had towels down by pool and lemon/lime cold water in the fitness center next to the pool. Also was a steam room in the fitness center.
Right next to the South Park mall, convenient for grabbing quick food.
Comfortable bed, a lot of pillows, normal sized bathroom, love seat couch in room. Good A/C in the room.
Gave us champagne when we were waiting in lobby. Also had chocolate covered strawberries and cookies.
Lobby bar stayed open late (2am) after they were about to close at midnight but the entire reception came back and they agreed to stay open.
Overall, very happy with this place. At $99 for the wedding rate, it was a great place.

title: “Nice Hotel.”
text:
Nice hotel. Great Location. Area is a little shady, but its no where near as bad as people make it out to be. Might not be a good idea to walk around late at night though. 
Full Kitchen with everything you would need in a kitchen. Comfortable bed and nice sitting area. 
Staff was friendly. They have free coffee all day and bagels and ceral and the like at breakfast. 
All around nice hotel and would recommend it to anyone.

title: “Nice view, nice room, disappointing service.”
text:
Got a room on concierge level (at 500$ a night...) with view of Statue of Liberty, which is nice. The location is also nice, and the room clean and nicely decorated.
Concierge lounge (CL) was disappointing - very small and closed on Friday afternoon/Saturday. Service was also disappointing: had to ask for access to the CL although it's included in the booking rate, nobody at CL door and the attendant was rude (condescendingly asking "do you get access with your room key"). The business center advertised as free service does not exist, it's now the Fedex Kinko which you have to pay to use for anything. In comparison, stayed at a couple of Hilton properties during the trip and the service there were amazing.

title: “Great Location/Amenities...Just In The Budget”
text:
We usually stay at more independent hotels when we go to New York for two reasons; usually a lot more inexpensive and predictable on the amenities/service (once you've found a good one). This trip was somewhat last minute and we looked at all of our usual locales and came up with nothing. The Millennium Hilton looked appealing because it was basically the same price as less than stellar comparables and it was right by all of the subway lines we needed.
Bottom line...we were blown away by the quality of the rooms, service, and location. It's basically a 4 star hotel in my opinion for NYC. Across the street from the WTC site its within blocks of almost all subway lines (W,Q,N,E,C,B,etc.). Would definitely stay there again if we could get the same deal (around $200), but have a feeling that its cheap only because of all of the construction going on in the area.

title: “We will not stay here again.”
text: We stayed here because we decided to take the Amtrak down for another one of my husband's visits to the USC medical center, and this hotel was conveniently located near Union Station. The service was good; however, the room was extremely outdated and old. Our air/heating unit did not work, so we had to keep our window open, which made it difficult to sleep with the noise from the streets. The pillows and bed were uncomfortable, the curtain was partially falling off the rod, the hotel and room had a bad odor, and most of the channels on the television were fuzzy. The free breakfast, too, was sad. Thankfully, when a disturbed man off the street got into the elevator with us on our way back from dinner in the evening, a security guard jumped in just as the doors were closing and accompanied us until he could escort the man back outside! The staff was wonderful, but it did not help with the overall experience. We will not stay here again.

title: “One of the Best Places to Stay in San Francisco”
text:
We are frequent travelers and have visited San Francisco on many occassions. We have stayed in different locations there. Tuscan Inn Fisherman's Wharf is one of the nicest and most pleasant places we have ever stayed when traveling-anywhere. We also felt this to be one of the safer areas for night walking when staying in Sn Francisco. We would gladly stay at Tuscan Inn again. 
The Tuscan Inn manager is Ed Sincoff. We met Ed for the first time when we stayed there recently. Ed is a very nice and capable businessman. I found Ed to be running a really nice hotel and learned he was respected by those who work for him. Jose is the gentleman at the front desk who I seemed to reach most often when I phoned the Inn. Jose and the numerous fellow staff people, I discovered, are very friendly and knowledgable. I noticed among everyone from clerks to cleaning people, to parking valets, all seemed to be enjoying their jobs at the Tuscan Inn and sharing San Francisco with visitors. 
Tuscan Inn is a larger, yet quaint, hotel centrally located in the Fisherman Wharf area of San Francisco. From the standpoint of the physical rooms, we choose upgraded rooms allowing us a bedroom seperated from the living room. This allowed privacy for office work, and privacy to enjoy the second LCD TV. The king bed was great- soft enough to be comfy and firm enough to allow wonderful sleep. While we were there I slept through the 4.0 earthquake. (Great bed!) The bath was a larger comfortable size, and had marble. The shower was wonderful with a lot of hot water and excellent pressure. The bath had an exhause fan. The room was clean and inviting. There were plenty of windows and they opened for ventilation. The heat/AC units were very efficent. 
The hotel itself is undergoing lobby renovation which may be done as of this writing. The new marble outside the building entry is very beautiful, as will be the new details being finished in the building lobby. There are two elevators, both with ample room. We seemingly never had to wait more than seconds for the elevator to arrive. 
The hotel does have a free coffee/tea bar in the mornings, and a managers free wine tasting each evening. The hotel has a nicer restaurant located in its building just feet from the entry. Plus the Fisherman Wharf area has all types of food, in all price ranges within walking distance any direction. (You must try the sour dough bread for breakfest Just two blocks onto the wharf. It is delicious!) If you need any supplies while at the Inn, there is a major drug store one-minute away on a neighboring block, and a Trader Joe grocery two-minutes walk on another street. 
I did see airport vans stopping at the Tuscan Inn. Plus Cable cars, retro trolley cars, regular large city buses and taxis are available within brief minutes of the Inn. For this reason your car is not necessary in the wharf area and can be cumbersome in most of San Francisco. But if you do have your car Tuscan Inn has a parking garage on premesis. Be aware, parking in San Francisco is not cheap-anywhere! If you are adventuresome and want to play ticket roulete with the meter people, you can park free overnight-until 7AM on many meters in the wharf area. But do read all parking signs carefully. There are more than 40 ways to get a parking ticket in SF. 
If you enjoy walking, Alcatraz tour boats are walkable from the Inn. If you want to sight see, why not walk to the Powell-Market street trolley and ride it across the city, and change cable cars to go yet another direction. Then on the way back, get off the cable car in China Town. Enjoy yourself shopping and sight seeing and then walk back down the hill to Tuscan Inn.
By then you will understand why my family believed Tuscan Inn is one of the best places to stay in San Francisco.

title: “Great Location”
text: On the Ave is a great hotel located a bit out of the heart of Manahattan, but only 2.5 miles from Times Square which is a quick subway ride. The subway station is 2 short blocks from the Hotel. The standard rooms are small, but when your in NY your there to see the sights and the night life, so unless your planning on spending a lot of time in your room it's a great choice. The staff was extremely helpful in recommending places to eat and see around the hotel.

title: “Excellent as usual !”
text: Excellent Stay ! Given the location and the quality of the Service !

title: “Fabulous place to stay in Boston”
text:
After travelling around New England for a couple of weeks we had come to expect cheerful and positive hotel staff, however none of them were in the same league as those at the Lenox. In some places it seems they were just putting into practice what they had learned on a course, here you felt they actually meant it and took a personal pride in your well being. The room was very comfortable and well equipped. The desk chair was particularly comfortable, when I discovered the retail price on the Internet I knew why! I will have to be a very good boy for Santa to bring me one of those at Christmas.
It had been our plan to eat out whilst in Boston but for various reasons ended up in the hotel restaurant. Here we found the food to be imaginative, good and fairly priced.

title: “really nice!”
text: room was attractive.very clean.has everything one would need.

title: “Beautiful Hotel!”
text: I had a wonderful time in San Diego. Unfortunately, I didn't get to see much of the hotel because I was in training all day, every day. The staff was extremely nice and I was given a warm yummy chocolate chip cookie when I checked in! My room was super clean and very comfortable. The lobby gift shop has a Starbucks and it opens at 6:30am. It was very convenient to grab something on my way out every morning. I really enjoyed staying here. The location was great and was connected to a shopping center with a sports bar. I highly recommend it!

title: “Nice hotel in a great position”
text:
Our family (4) enjoyed a nice stay at the Holiday Inn Express, Fishermans Wharf. Room was a good size, the breakfast was a good start to the day. Staff were friendly and the hotel is in a great location.
If you plan to go to Alcatraz then book before you get here as it is vey popular and can get booked up, we were very lucky and got on the tour the first day of our 3 day visit after that the tour was booked up for the rest of the time we were there.

title: “Doubletree's digs in Detroit”
text: I stayed at the Doubletree a few nights during the week and found it to be a quite respite. Room on the 10th floor (Hilton Honors floor) was well appointed with a living room space, good size bathroom, and separate bedroom. A chair in the living room could have been cleaner, and the toilet paper dispenser was almost out of reach, but otherwise, wonderful accommodations. A restaurant has a good breakfast buffet, and there is a sports bar with food and drinks. A hotel shuttle van will take you within several miles of the hotel, including to Greektown where there are lots of restaurants and activities. The only down side is there is not much in the walking vicinity, but the shuttle (or a People Mover...light rail) can get you almost anywhere for the adventures that await in downtown Detroit. I have stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn a few blocks away, and prefer this Doubletree's ammenities. Lastly, if you drive, be sure to valet park. It was $5 a day versus the parking lot next to the hotel which was $10 a day. My lesson learned, and hopefully will help you!

title: “Nice Hotel- But Unclean”
text: This hotel was recently renovated, and the rooms, while small, are updated with the latest amenities. I was on the 32nd floor and had an incredible view of the city. When I walked into the bathroom, things took a turn for the worse. There was soap in the shower from the previous occupant with a mysterious hair on it. I don't know if the hotel doesn't give the housekeeping staff enough time to clean all the rooms. On my second day, the cleaning was also shoddy. Its unfortunate that a hotel of this quality and recent upgrades can't keep up with the cleaning requirements. Beware of some of the extreme fees this hotel can charge. I attempted to make three phone calls to Houston through the room phone as I had bad cellphone reception in my room. The calls did not go through, but I was charged $9.00 per call for a call with a length of 0:01 on my bill (to be fair, the hotel did remove this charges when I complained). The attached conference center charges $100.00 for several hours of internet (not an exaggeration). The in room wifi is a little more reasonable with a fee of around $15.00/ day. I am a Hilton Diamond member, and this stay, reinforced my alliance with Hilton. While this hotel was nice, the cleaning issues were unacceptable. I have never had a cleaning complaint at a Hilton Brand (including Hamtpon Inns).

title: “Nice hotel, friendly staff, bit expensive”
text:
The hotel is located close to the airport, which is why I chose it.
Room was nice though not spectacular. Very quiet, no noise from the other rooms or the hall way.
I liked the free internet and was very impressed by the friendly and efficient staff.
When I made the reservation I chose to add breakfast for $ 6. The breakfast was really good, a buffet.
I did think the room was a bit expensive ($ 159 for a king room without the breakfast).
I will probably stay here again.

title: “W Style was long needed in DC”
text:
Have stayed here before and the place continues to hold it's own as a unique hotel in an area of "traditional" stuffy high end hotels. I like the Willard and all, but they all start to look the same as they try to mimic old aristocrat look and feels. I like that the W stands out a bit, yet is still a more Victorian-styled W so doesn't come across too art deco for the area....just enough. 
J&G Restaurant is superb and their wine bar downstairs has a great outdoor eating area during the summer. Club upstairs (POV) has insane views, but obviously more fun in the summer. 
Parking is expensive at $50 for valet or across the street for about half of that. Wish they had more options on that regard.

title: “Big room - Good for short stay”
text:
Stayed in the hotel for 2 nights on 16 day touring holiday in california.
Hotel was well located 5 mins walk from holiday bouv. (which was very dissapointing, tacky and full of hawkers) Room were clean and huge. Staff though were not very freindly, we asked about changing travelers check and mentioned we should try and find a bank, but could'nt tell us where the nearest one was.
Also not a hotel for people with a problem with stairs, we had to go up and down six filghts to get to our room which was only on the second floor.

title: “My new favorite hotel next to SeaTac”
text:
There's a SeaTac shuttle, free parking and good restaurants in the local strip mall. You can cross the street and go to Southcenter Mall.
All the rooms are suites with natural light in the Bedroom and a window onto the corridor/atrium in the living room.
It's usually one of the cheapest Hilton family hotels in the area, but very nice.

title: “Beautiful place and wonderful staff”
text: For the price this hotel is terrific. The office staff is out of this world. We drove for 18 hours overnight with 4 kids and arrived in Jacksonviile Beach at 6 a.m. We were tired and hungry. We looked for a buffet type restauraunt to no avail so I told my husband to head to the hotel. I went in and asked when we could check in, and to my suprise she checked me in right then and there. I told her we were looking for somewhere to eat breakfast and she said to get the kids and come in to eat the continental breakfast, which consisted of bisciuts and gravy, danishes, fruit, bagels and muffins. I was so happy and the rest of the family was also. Our room was very clean and we had a nice view of the pool. The whole place is beautifully landscaped also. It was a totally enjoyable stay. Will stay again.

title: “Nice place”
text: Priceworthy, good location, decent breakfast although a bit unorganized, friendly (mostly) staf. Fairly cramped place due to the tiny ground area, but room spacey enough. Spent for night with family. A good holiday hotel.

title: “Great shower”
text: The location is good for downtown. However, it is loud, you can hear the cars, the sirens, and every noise. The room is big, and the shower is just amazing. It is the most powerful shower I ever experienced. The bed is really comfortable. I enjoyed the hotel a lot. There is a great breakfast place within walking distance called Honey...go there.

title: “Great location”
text: I had the opportunately to stay at this hotel during the 4th July celebrations. Checked in early and and my room was ready for us. The staff were very friendly, professional and helpful. The room was very clean, the bed was very confortable even though I didn't stay in it very long and I had a view of the Empire State Building. Loved the soap, shampoo and lotion in the bathroom and especially the soft and fluffy white towels. I am very picky about towels. The location was perfect midway between Uptown and Downtown. Subway outside the door. Walking distance to Times Square, 5th Avenue, Macys and many restaurants. We had a wonderful full buffet breakfast in the Martinique restaurant. Very good service and the food was very good. If you wanted Eggs & Bacon or go healthy Yorgert and Fruit they had it. Good selection of wine in the bar .I liked the best the friendly staff whom I would talk to and joke with every day in the lobby. The location and the room was the best. I would definely come back to this hotel, very good deal for the price. I have just 1 critic, at the time of my visit the room safes were being overhauled so I was not able to leave my valuables in my room. I called the front desk and they said that I could leave my valuables in their safe. Other than that I really like the hotel. Diane from Montreal, Quebec, Canada

title: “Much better than reviews indicated”
text:
We purchased our reservation for a Seattle hotel through Priceline at an amazingly low price, but of course we didn't know where we would end up. After reading the tripadvisor reviews on the Marqueen, we were somewhat concerned. We needn't have been. We loved the location, since it wasn't in the middle of downtown, but was within walking distance to the monorail for easy access to downtown. The shops and restaurants in the area were charming, including the Cafe Ladro attached to the hotel. 
We had read that there were only sheer curtains in the rooms and that the light came in too early in the day. This has apparently been remedied, as the room-darkening shades allowed our teen-age daughter to sleep in past 11 am! As for the noise level, we were in a room at the back of the hotel and there was no more noise, perhaps less, than most hotels. The beds were absolutely the most comfortable we have ever had while traveling. The kitchen area, complete with a sitting area, microwave and a stocked refrigerator was a real plus. We experienced a pleasant staff, and thought that the older structure added character. 
Yes, it is an old building with a few related flaws, so if you are looking for a new "Motel 6" look, this hotel isn't for you. But if you want charm and style, try the Marqueen.

title: “Great base for plenty of culture and fun!”
text:
We (my wife, my brother and I) came to Seattle for PUSAFest 2010 and stayed at Warwick Hotel for 4 nights. Other reviews on this site had mentioned the street noise, so we requested a room on the upper echelons of the hotel and was accommodated with a fine room on one of the top floors.
The room was big and had a great view of the Space Needle. It was possible to hear some distant street noise, even through closed doors, but it was not a problem for us - and I always sleep with earplugs - besides the combined snoring of my wife and brother did more to keep me awake... :)
Our beds (Queen size) were a little too small for 2 big Europeans - and the single bed cover for two is annoying - however, it shall not detract from anything here. The bathroom was a little on the small side but had a nice tub.
There is no breakfast included but they serve a fine meal in the restaurant on the premises - alternatively a short (20 minute) walk to 13 Coins is highly recommended where they serve a most excellent breakfast and are open 24/7.
The hotel had a free internet service in the lobby (don't know about the rooms) where several pc's were available - handy for updating facebook and our friends at home about our adventures.
Staff at the hotel were friendly at all times and eager to help. There was a small mix-up with charged parking even if we never used it (intended too, so here is the likely cause) but the charge was quickly removed without fuss.
It is a small walk (about 15 minutes) to the city centre (the monorail station) and about the same distance to the harbour front.
We can highly recommend this place and will likely stay again - should we ever come back - though price, as always, will be a factor.

title: “Would not stay here again”
text: Although the location to Fenway is a plus, this hotel is in need of major renovation. Number one priority is that they get new beds. These were REALLY bad. They also need new bedspreads, curtains and carpeting. The smell in the room and in the hallways was also not good. There was one girl at the front desk that smiled and was helpful. I think her name was Natalie. The rest seemed like they couldn't care less. On the plus side, the location is great for Fenway. The bathroom was clean and there was hot water. The man in charge of the Chinese restaurant for breakfast was very nice and they had good coffee. If the management would work on these other important issues, it could be a great place. But the last straw for us was on the second day there was the definite strong odor of marijuana wafting down the hallway as we walked with our 7-year-old grandson. I also heard other people commenting about this. We would not stay here again. There are other hotels not that far from Fenway.

title: “Best Hotel Stay ever”
text: We recently stayed at this hotel while I was on a business trip for several days. The hotel itself was attractive and clean. The ammenities were great. The pool was excellent. The location was fantastic. We originally wanted to stay closer to the downtown attractions, but decided on this hotel based on price and we are not sorry at all. We easily made it downtown in 10 minutes during non rush hour times and the hotel itself was located near lots of shopping and dining options. The best part of the hotel was the staff. Over the course of the three nights we stayed, we came into contact with 10-15 different employees--house cleaning staff, maintenance, food service, desk workers, van drivers--every single employee was friendly and helpful. They were always asking how we were doing and checking to see if there was anything they could do to make us more comfortable. We were so impressed! We have never had this sort of attention at any chain hotel. We highly recommend this hotel to everyone seeking a nice hotel with staff that actually seems to care about what they do and the guests they serve.

title: “Our Home away from Home!”
text:
We have been staying at the Marcel for years, for long stretches of time, and appreciate being taken care of by the staff. 
Danny always greets us with a smile and was particularly awesome and helpful this trip. Not only did he always have ice sent to our room so one of us could ice our broken foot, but he also managed to retrieve a lost cell phone that was left in a car.
Zach and Michael, at the front desk, are always so accommodating and make sure that we are well looked after.
Raoul went above and beyond when he single-handedly carted our numerous suitcases from our room, to the way too small car, and managed to fit every piece in.
Looking forward to our next stay,
Karen Alweil Studio

title: “Hidden Gem”
text: Most hotels in New York City are cramped, overpriced, and the staff generally treat people like dirt. I found this hotel a great exception with yoga mats, hula hoops, a nice bar, free happy hour, and an amazing staff that went out of its way to help at every opportunity. My window shades did not work very well, but I was rarely in my room, so no biggie. Way to go!

title: “Brilliant Hotel in the heart of Boston”
text: We had an excellent stay at the Nine Zero Hotel. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful and the concierge, Thomas, made the stay extra special by arranging some birthday surpirses for my partner. The rooms are spacious with very comfy beds and great in room amentities. Our view from the room was amazing and it was also very centrally located. We loved Boston and this hotel. Can'e wait to return!

title: “Still Disappointing”
text:
This Hilton has sorely needed renovation for many years. When I stayed the renovation of the sleeping rooms was done, and the lobby was almost finished. It is really only a big convention hotel. The sleeping rooms are still small, and the bathroom is still very cramped (although not as bad as the Hilton Portland, OR). The new fixtures are just ok, nothing exciting. The only saving grace in the bathroom is that they retained the built-in shelves on the side of the sink, otherwise there would not be sufficient room for one's toiletry bag. Some rooms eliminated the tub and had a shower only. Didn't seem to make it that much more spacious from what I saw. The new furnishings are cheap. In my room they already had nicks and splits in the wood. Still no refrigerator or mini-bar, although there is a coffeemaker. The location is nice if one wants to go to the DuPont Circle area. The metro station is several blocks down by DuPont Circle. Otherwise, it is not as convenient as hotels near Capitol Hill or downtown.
The only reason why I stay here is that the convention I attend has no alternative, as no other hotel is large enough for it. Beware, if you are hosting an event here (reception, luncheon, dinner, etc.) - each time I have done so, the bill has been wrong. Other people's events were charged to my card (not apparent until the monthly statement arrived) and bar bill overcharged. They rectified the errors, but one has to review their bills carefully.

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Stay”
text: Me and my husband stayed at this hotel for 2 nights to get away for a little while. The hotel is nice and in the middle of everything. It is in Union Square. Very busy area but just minutes from the mall, stores, restaurants, China Town and the cable cars. The hotel employees were very nice. The rooms were nice considering the historic building. The only down fall was the parking. It was 40.00 a night for valet. We parked our car at the O'Farrel parking garage just a block down from the hotel for 30.00 a night which saved us about $20.00. We will be going back!

title: “Large rooms and right next to Bryant park.”
text: Had an OK stay here. The rooms were large, service was good. I suggest bringing ear plugs, as I found the traffic noise loud- which is expected given the location. I also smelled truck exhaust in the morning rush hour, yuck. The elevators are also slow and cramped. Stay here for the space and location.

title: “WHEN I COME TO AUSTIN FOR BUSINESS I ALWAYS STAY HERE!!! THE BEST EVER!!”
text: I come into austin several times a year for classes and the front desk staff is really friendly everytime I come. I really enjoy the full breakfast in the morning & happy hour on Tuesday & Wednesday. And the location is really close about 1 mile to where my classes are located. They have renovated the rooms and they look really nice.

title: “a great place to stay in NY”
text:
If you're looking for a great, new hotel on a great location in NY, Fashion 26 is the place to be!!!! Conveniently located near the Empire State Building, the Flat Iron district, Soho, Penn Station and Times Square: this is it.... It's a brandnew hotel, great, modern and nicely designed rooms with lots of extra's, great bathroom, super bed and spectacular views....
We loved it and we spent 6 nights in June...
The staff is most helpful and kind and we loooooved it!
If we go back for a trip to the Big Apple, we'll most certainly try to book there again!
Thank you again for a home away from home, Fashion 26, we love you !!!!Christel&Rudi

title: “Very very small room”
text:
I have stayed at various Kimpton hotels in other cities before, so was confident of a good experience, but when I got to my room, I was shocked by how small it was. I have made about 80 transatlantic trips to the US in the past 10 years and stayed at many hotels in this price and class range, and never ever stayed in a room so small. It is also badly designed for the small space. The bed has a metal four poster frame which blocks the already-tight squeeze past, and the chair at the desk at the bottom of the bed hits the bed if moved back. There is nowhere to put a suitcase without creating a trip hazard, and the TV must be observed from the bed or sitting right under it at the desk. There is a chair in the corner of the room, but rather pointlessly so as there is nowhere useful to put it. The room sizes are stated as 300-500 sq feet on the website. Including the bathroom space, I can't see how this room is much more than 230 sq feet and too much of that is taken up by the bathroom. It is somewhat ironic that the hotel sells itself as "pet-friendly" because you couldn't swing a cat in this room. 
So I asked the front desk, and they told me they were full, sorry, nothing they can do. When I said that I was coming back to Seattle in a few weeks and would not pay $290 for that room again, the receptionist curtly advised I should book a higher room category. Not likely. Different hotel, for sure. 
Pity really. The hotel seems to have a lot going for it. Nice funky decor, decent food, but the astonishing size of the room and the curt response by the front desk make this a no-go for me.

title: “Good service”
text: Good airport location. Front desk staff was always polite and helpful - dealt with 3 different staff members. Continental breakfast is sufficient. Rooms clean and quiet. Nice tv.

title: “Great, clean, convenient place to stay with FREE parking”
text:
This was our second stay (last time was August, 2010) and it hasn't changed. Our room was clean, had a safe, and the bathroom was spotlessly clean and had a great shower with lots of hot water and a sink outside of the bathroom to ease our morning preparations. The flat screen TV was nice but we only watched it for the weather as we were out and about in our very short stay in SF (off to Northern California). The hotel is very close to North Beach, Chinatown, and Fisherman's Wharf. While this would not be considered a luxury hotel by anyone's standards it fits my 5 star requirements (and I have stayed in many so-called luxury hotels that didn't meet my standards): clean with furnishings in good shape, all of the amenities, quiet room with a comfortable bed, near excellent places to eat, a friendly and helpful front desk staff, and free parking (almost unheard of in San Francisco where you can pay up to $40 a night for the "privilege”). There is no fancy lobby but I think in all of our travels (and we tend to do a major trip for pleasure at least 4 times a year) I have sat in the lobby 3 times. I believe the key to getting a quiet room here is to reserve well in advance and state your preferences. I asked for a room on the same side as "Bimbo's" as we were there during an evening when a performance was occurring and there was really no disturbance whatsoever (my husband is a very light sleeper and he slept like a log) (there is a cute view of the apartment building next door and the "pocket garden" which is very tranquil). The view from the room was incredible--Coit Tower, San Francisco skyline (including TransAmerica building) and there was NO street noise. I could be wrong, but our room was either 305 or 307. For breakfast you can walk up Columbus to La Boulange or one of the authentic Italian cafes (we go to La Boulange because my husband LOVES their granola with yogurt). We ate lunch (on our way in from SFO) at the Beach Chalet which is at the entrance to Golden Gate Park and across from the beach (down the street from the Cliff House) and had a wonderful meal there—my husband a salad with Ahi Tuna and myself a Crab Louis salad with the sweetest Dungeness crab meat and a super champagne or chardonnay vinaigrette dressing. This time around we ate dinner at Sotto Mare on Green Street just up the street from the hotel and highly recommend it if you love good seafood in an unpretentious atmosphere with fairly reasonable prices. My husband had sand dabs (a sweeter flounder) and I had prawns--yum, yum. 
In conclusion I would DEFINITELY stay here again and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for the things that make a great stay for me. We really enjoyed our stay and hope you will too!

title: “New, Clean, Comfortable”
text: I loved this place. Modern and well appointed. Convenient to downtown. Valet parking reasonable. Check-in parking a little crowded. This will be my preferred place to stay in downtown Indy and I will look for this hotel when I travel.

title: “Avoid like your life depends on it”
text: We just checked into this hotel an hour ago, we're now back on tripadvisor searching for somewhere else in NYC to stay! The staff are discourteous and unprofessional. The bag handler dragged my luggage down a set of stairs, loosening the handle. Room smells like chlorine, loud air conditioning, loose toilet seat, no view (which is fine, but this wasn't the cheapest room on offer). As a kicker, the Wifi is $14 USD / night PER DEVICE, so if you have 2-3 gadgets like we do, you're in for an extra $42/night for this 'service'. Do yourself a favour and find a better managed hotel.

title: “Great motel, close to airport--location a little scary”
text: We stayed here recently due to a family emergency. The location near the airport is not in one of the better neighborhoods in Phoenix, however, once we drove onto the property, we felt very safe and comfortable. There is a fence around the property, with a single entrance to drive through. The staff was great, and there is a computer with Internet access in the lobby. There is easy access to the Interstate also--just get your bearings before dark. They have a park and fly program, and although we didn't use it, I would have felt comfortable leaving my car there.

title: “punches well above its weight”
text: This is a superb hotel; great people; nice club level room; and fantastic location. I was bowled over by the experience and will be back! Every aspect of this hotel works. i enjoyed banter with the porters and the bar/restaurant staff could not do enough.

title: “We found our S.F. Pied-a-terre.”
text:
We stayed one night while in town to see an opera. We stay in S.F. 15-20 nights per year and usually book a four star hotel through hotwire. This time we decided to check the Intercontinental website to see how their price compared to the price of the hotel I assumed was the Intercontinental offered on hotwire. We were surprised to find a great bargain for California residents which included both valet parking and buffet breakfast for two. Much better that we could get from hotwire and we had better option on available rooms. We decided to join Intercontinental's Ambassador plan, booked an upgraded room and received a two level upgrade to a one bedroom suite on the 31st floor. 
This hotel is new, fresh and pretty hip for an establishment which must receive most of its visitors because of conventions at next door Moscone Center. Good bar and restaurant. Suzanne at the front desk was especially helfpul. This is a very reasonably priced hotel for the quality you receive. Do check their website for current offers. I think it is the one of the hotels where you really can get a better package by booking directly.
The only negative was all the ambulance sirens one could hear on Howard street on a Saturday night. Next time we will ask to try a room facing towards Market street.

title: “Really a great experience !”
text:
Stayed at the Radisson Martinique with the family for NY/Christmas sightseeing. I was happy with the whole experience. From check-in to departure, I was treated very nicely and well taken care of.
 The concierge was most informative about nearby breakfast options. (Seriously well informed) and directed us to a great place based on multiple criteria.
 I would highly recommend this hotel, not only for the location, but for the attentive staff.

title: “A Great Find in LA”
text: This is a small boutique hotel with a fantastic location. Rates are very reasonable and the staff was extremely helpful. I really enjoyed the comfortable bedding, silky sheets and the robe. Nice and quiet, I slept great. There are so many restaurants and great shopping in this neighborhood you don't really need to drive much.

title: “Nice Location and Service, Room Needed Work”
text:
While I was in New York for a brief conference, I decided to actually stay at the hotel where most of the events were being held. This was a change for me. Usually I'll stay elsewhere and just make my way to the hotel. I don't have a problem with the subway, and in fact typically enjoy it, but since the rate at the Affinia was one of the better ones, I decided that it would be easier to just stay there.
In general, I'm glad that I did. But you need to take it with a grain of salt, and be ready for what you'll get when you check in. Make sure that you realize that this is an older property, and you'll probably be okay with what you get when you arrive in your room.
Notably, the rooms are reasonably well upholstered, but they are on the small side, and the plaster is aging, so you will see some cracks, and some of them might be on the large side. You aren't going to see central air, and in fact you won't see a thermostat of any kind.
Instead, you get what is essentially a steam-controlled radiator to handle the heat that is expelled into the room. You'll also have a window unit (air conditioner) for cooling the room, but in the winter, these units are taped shut to keep cold air from coming into the room - so hope that you don't hit a hot spell or you'll have to open the window to cool things down.
Finally, you may want to make sure that you don't get a "17" room (517, 917, etc). This is because the main steam pipe runs through the closet, and it makes the room absolutely bake. Even opening the outside window, with outside temperatures in the 30s, kept the room a nice 65 degrees, so it was bearable - but it meant that the outside noise increased quite a bit. And even when closed, those windows don't block a lot of noise.

title: “OK for one night if you have an hotwire deal”
text:
Pros :
- location of course, right at the airport
- very clean
- you almost don't hear the planes which is amazing since you can see them from the window.
Cons :
- Not a surprise but the area around the airport sucks, good for one night but not more
- no self parking available when we were there (beginning of January). Had to pay valet or park in another private parking at the corner.
- no fridge in the room
- I could hear the people from the other room talking and could understand half of the words... Really bad sound isolation between the rooms.

title: “Be aware of the breakfast and restaurant.”
text:
Very, very small rooms. It´s like cabins.
The breakfsat is a disaster. Be aware, that the inkluded brekfast is only muffins and coffe- not bread or anything else at all. If you want anything else, you have to buy it, wich we did 2 times, but the brekfast was almost uneatable. A little omelet with burned potatos 15USD.
The dinner you can buy in the restaurant is also a disaster.

title: “Charming and cool”
text: We were there in 100 + temps. No problems with AC. Room was spacious, perfect location. Just visiting for the weekend. Will be back.

title: “Perfect lodging for conventions”
text:
This is the nicest Embassy Suites I've ever been in and the staff was fabulous. The beds were very comfy with a nice down comforter and an assortment of great pillows but none were the ones that look great on a made bed but give you a serious crick in your neck. The free happy hour and breakfast were fine but the location of that bar/restaurant was unremarkable. It was about a 30 second walk from the door of the hotel to the door of the Convention Center if you hit the cross walk light right which was great because it was 2 degrees F outside. My one complaint is that the coffee you can make in your room was literally undrinkable! I am not even picky about my coffee, drink Folgers or whatever at home, and I gave this one 2 sips and it made be shudder with disgust. Luckily there's a Starbucks right next door on the main floor (and the coffee at the free breakfast was OK too). 
Would be a great place with a family too because you can completely shut the door between the bedroom and the living room/bathroom areas. It's also just 2 blocks to the 16th street "mall" where there's lots of shopping and great restaurants.

title: “Good Value and Great Location”
text:
Stayed here recently for 4 nights.
