Check in was fine and efficient and the check in chap had a good sense of humour and showed interest in where we from, how long in NYC etc. Our room on the 11th floor was fine - yes the decor is a little dated but not horrendously so and the room was clean and quiet which in a city like New York is going something. The bed was comfortable and the room was serviced nicely in time for our return each day. The bed was comfrotable too and after long days pounding the streets we slept soundly. On the downside, there was no tea or coffee making facility, not that this troubled us. We never bothered with the hotel bar or restaurant for breakfast,lunch or dinner because there are so many eating/drinking options nearby.
To sum up - this was a good deal given the location,size of room etc. We found a deal on lastminute - pay for 3 nights get fourth free which made the total cost very economical relative to other similar hotels of a similar standard in the area and for the price I would stay again, having paid more in the past to stay in hotels with smaller/noisier rooms in NYC.

title: “Not as bad as reviews suggest”
text:
I have recently returned from a four night stay at this hotel and I was very nervous of what to expect after reading reviews on this site. I am pleased to say that my stay was most most enjoyable and the comments I read here unfounded.
We had a room on the 4th floor which was comfortable and clean. The bed was one of the most comfortable I have ever slept in. The decor was again clean without being flash and pretentious.
I would agree that the bathrooms are pretty small, but who spends long on holiday in their bathroom !!.
The location is good being right on Fishermans Wharf but not in middle enough to be noisy.
Don't be put off by staying here by reviews you may read here, I think some people must have very high expectations!!!!!

title: “Simple and spacious”
text: Siimple and basic is accurate, as well as the maze-like trudge to find the room. And it would have been nice to have been told when the free breakfast is offered. However, there are advantages: good free shuttle (haven't had a problem with this); hotel offers a day rate, which is great for when you have 7 hrs between flights; both times I've stayed there (2006 and 2008), the rooms have been very spacious; and there's a 24-hr Denny's restaurant adjacent to the hotel (mostly a breakfast place, but also sandwiches, salads, etc.). When I was there for a late supper at 11.30pm (friendly waintresses are happy to substitute salad if you don't want fries with everything), there were a couple of security guards conspicuously hanging out at the entrance (good or bad, depending on your point of view!).

title: “First Class Hotel”
text: Stayed at the US Grant for a business conference and brought my wife. A classy hotel with great service and well appointed stylish rooms. Food was first rate and the lounge/bar had great jazz music on the weekend. Location is great for touring the downtown area and all kinds of public transportation is nearby for venturing to other locations.. Street noise is a little intrusive (police and fire sires, must be a firehouse nearby) but it quiets down around bed time. Would definitely stay at the US Grant again.

title: “Amazing!”
text: Our stay at the Magnolia was amazing! The hotel was very clean, the staff was incredibly helpful and they went above and beyond what we expected. When we checked in, the woman at the front desk overheard us talking about it being my birthday. When we returned to our room later that night, the concierge staff had left us a plate of chocolate covered strawberrries and a birthday card. Completely unexpected! The valet guys are quick and incredibly helpful, as was the concierge. They even have a 7 passenger Tahoe that they can take you around downtown in - and our driver was funny, personable and knowledgeable. All in all an amazing stay, couldn't have asked for anything more!

title: “Nice Views, Great location”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights. We had a room on the 45th floor which had a great view. The staff was very friendly. There were a lot of events going on over the weekend and it was super busy but none of it affected our experience. The location was great, it is right on Michigan Ave sort of central to Sears tower, Wrigleyville, and Navy Pier. We would definately stay here again.

title: “Awesome Value! Immaculate hotel.”
text:
This is a little gem of a hotel, only a mile or two from Del Mar beach. When first approaching we were a little discouraged that it was in a corporate office area right off of the highway. But once you step inside, you are warmly greeted with a chocolate chip cookies which makes everything better! :-)
The rooms are decorated very nice! We had a view of the pool which was also pleasant (and not noisy). The rooms are stocked with Neutrogena cosmetics (including sunscreen!), and there is a Wolfgang Puck coffee machine which is nice.
There is a really nice pool that is quite relaxing too.
We booked on Priceline and paid $52 - bargain! For breakfast we simply drove to the beach for coffee and bagels because the breakfast prices at the hotel were a bit cha-ching.

title: “Excellent little hotel, great value, with one caution”
text:
This visit to NY I tried the Roger Smith Hotel and was very pleased with all things internal to the hotel, not to mention extraordinary low rates. There was a wondefully large and clean room with a desk and easy chairs, a spacious bathroom with shelves, thick walls ensuring privacy and quiet, a coffeemaker and fridge, free wifi, a public computer and printer, a very nice little restaurant, uniformly helpful staff, nice touches from the hotel's arts program, a comfortable bed, a workable TV and alarm clock, and an acceptable heating system. (There was no robe, room service, electronic gadgets, or haute decor, but these things should not be expected in this kind of hotel.) 
The one warning is that nearly every room faces Lexington Avenue, so one weekend night there were sirens and horns all night. Bring good earplugs and turn the heater/AC to "fan" to drown the din. 
The only other, minor caveat is not to expect well-lit, magnified, or full-length mirrors for grooming.

title: “Awesome & Awful!”
text: This hotel is fantastic in so many ways. Check-in was a breeze as we were warmly welcomed. Upon inspecting our corner room, I saw that it was 2 double beds for our romantic getaway, which was not what I had planned. In a few minutes after calling the front desk, the clerk personally came up to accompany us to the same room 2 floors higher with a king bed--perfect! It was a suite but we have never seen such spacious hotel accommodations. The living room was huge & the bedroom oversized as well. The bathroom was tiny, but not a problem. We have a round window that opened from the shower & it was fun to open it a crack & watch the street below as I showered! However, the street below was a problem overnight because the Sorrento is 2 blocks from the Virginia Mason emergency room entrance where all the ambulances begin & end. I was awakened by sirens all night long, & this wasn't even over a weekend! That is the only negative aspect of our stay, but it's enough to keep me from going back. We ate in their restaurant which was outstanding. We frequently utilized their free shuttle service to the downtown area. It is also close enough to walk if you have the energy and time and aren't carrying a boatload of shopping bags. We did not need a car while we were there which meant we did not use the valet. The staff was outstanding in every encounter I had with them. The beds were great, the view isn't great, but the windows were large. And the interior of the hotel is just plain gorgeous. The coffee bar is very nice since we love French-pressed coffee & there is a small frig in the room as well. I only wish it was in a quieter location. I booked this stay through booking.com and was pleased to find that this did not affect how we were treated at all.

title: “Decent Value, Would Recommend”
text:
We recently returned from a week in Boston and stayed the entire week at this hotel. 
As other reviewers have noted, I was a little apprehensive about staying here given some of the negative reviews that have been written. However, soon after arriving, my fears were quickly put to rest.
This is a grand, classic hotel and if anything, I felt humbled in its grandeur and opulence. Our room did have some wear here and there, but everything was clean and nothing was obviously in disrepair.
We stayed on the 15th floor, which cost a little more, but enjoyed the daily and complimentary breakfast buffet and hor'dourves. Our concierges were friendly and helpful, and the maid service was thorough.
After a week there, there were a couple of suggestions I would make, but these are minor in my opinion.
One is the gym---it has a lot of treadmills, but not much else in terms of work-out equipment. The other was the breakfast buffet, which while decent, could use a little more variety. The hor'dourves items varied, but not the breakfast ones. 
Overall, this is decent place to stay. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it and would be quite likely to stay here again.

title: “Great hotel, great location, great staff a must to stay here you won't be disappointed”
text:
We booked this hotel after we read the reviews on this site. We were not disappointed. Hotel is lovely very clean large rooms and a great location. We ate breakfast at the hotel and also in the evening on the one night. Loads of nice restaurants close by.
The staff were great, really helpful with advise and always smiling and cheerful. We were really grateful for their excellent customer care when we arrived at the airport to find we had left our mobile phone in the room. The staff at the hotel arranged for the phone to be bought to us at the airport.
We really do highly recommend this hotel
Thank you for making our stay so great and special.

title: “value for money although could do with updating”
text:
A friend and I stayed in this motel for 3 nights in August and initially was unhappy with the room we were allocated. The room upon arrival had a musty smell and could have done with a good airing prior to occupancy. When we pointed this out we were offered another bedroom which was only slightly better however this was easily remedied with a good household spray. The hotel is quite deceptive as it looks worn and in need of updating, definitely could do with a makeover! however what is offered as part of their service more than makes up for the appearance. 
The on site restaurant PAM PAM served up good well prepared meals although they take their time with your order which if you are having a leisurely day is fine. They will usually speed up if you tell them.
The motel offers free shuttle bus service to and from the airport greyhound terminus and to some of the attractions. You have to book this by completing a form and submitting it the day before. The facilities also include free internet service and a pool with hot tub. This was a real bonus as it was great to be able to relax by the pool. They also had onsite laundry facilities which again was very handy.
On the whole I enjoyed my stay in San Diego and although we did not have a car we were able to get around quite easily as the hotel is located near Trolley and bus stops and quite close to Old Town. The staff were generally helpful. 
I think for what we paid we got value for money and although I was a little put off by the outward appearance of the place It was always busy and full of people coming and going. Although, If I were to use this hotel again I would request the new block.

title: “Horrible, definitely not a 3.5 star”
text: Got this hotel through priceline bidding, so thank god I did not actually pay full price. The front desk staff was very nice and friendly, but when I got up to my room it smelled of smoke even though it was non-smoking. Room seemed very dirty and when I pulled the sheets down on the bed there was hair all over. Didn't seem like it had actually been cleaned. The whole vibe of the room and hotel was dirty and gross to me, I travel a lot so I know I'm picky but this place was so gross I actually opted to leave and go to another hotel. The only good thing about this hotel was that the front desk was very nice when I checked in, but it should definitely not be a 3.5 star, beware!

title: “Exceptional Visit”
text:
From the moment I spoke with Lynn O'Hare by phone to book our reservations at Independence Park Hotel, I knew we had chosen wisely. Upon our arrival she met us at the desk and gave us such good and clear directions about what to see and where to dine in the 24-hour period we had in the Old City. It was a thrill to stay in this historic hotel in the midst
of sites we had only read about in history books. The hotel was charming, and the staff so pleasant and friendly. We wished we had had more time to sight-see. We will count on a return trip as soon as possible when we have more time to spend in the "city of brotherly love"!

title: “Just perfect - book well ahead”
text:
This is a real gem in Manhattan. It isnt really an "Inn" , more of a bed and breakfast but with facilities and a genuine friendliness that shame many 5 star hotels in the city that go for twice the price or more. Where to start? The check in is friendly and efficient and the small but well informed staff are passionate about their city and can answer almost any question you may have ( they readily found us an Indian grocery in Midtown that sold henna hair dye when our own internet attempts had turned up nothing ).
Breakfast is included and features fresh tea and coffee, a huge range of breads, rolls , bagels and doughnuts and - a nice touch - bowls of strawberries and raspberries. There is a small plasme screen TV in the breakast area but it isnt loud or obtrusive and many people prefer the complimentary New York Times. Each morning a daily news sheet of what is on in Chelsea is slipped under your door, also featuring the weather forecast and "bread of the day ". 
The rooms are small ( this is an old NYC townhouse after all ) but cosy and well equipped with small plasma TVs, room safe, iron etc. The toiletries supplied are especially good and as well as the standard shampoo etc include mouthwash. Free wifi is available and I got an immediate and fast connection, although there is also a small business centre with PCs and a printer if you dont have a laptop. The rooms at the back might be quieter than those facing 14th Street.
Local transport linlks are very good with a subway stop a few steps away ( 14th St and 8th Avenue ). Usefully the A train stops here so if you had light luggage or dont mind a few stairs ( most NYC subway stations dont have escalators and not all have lifts ) you could get here from JFK on the subway without changing trains.
Nearby are some excellent places to eat and drink ( the Corner Bistro and Woody McHales bar stand out) and the hotel staff will give you excellent advice as well as directions. There are also all sorts of useful service business on 14th St ( dry cleaners, laundaries, pharmacies, supermarkets etc ) and several banks with ATMs including HSBC.
Some tips:
1. The stairs are narrow and there is no lift so consider taking only light luggage or, if you have big bags, leave them in the ( free ) secure baggage store downstairs and take only what you need up to your room.
2. Charlie the cat loves to be stroked!

title: “Best Deal Ever”
text: The hotel is located on the east side of I-35, right off the service road. I was there for 1 night. I made the reservation 2 weeks prior to my stay and got a really good deal. You won't have any problems looking for parking space and it's free. My check in experience was smooth. When I first walked into my room it felt and smelled clean. They give you a coffee maker with free coffee. I did use their free WiFi and did not have any problems with it. The bathroom was also clean and it comes with outlets and hair dryer. The only thing negative was that sometimes you can here people through the walls, but it never bothered me and I was well rested when I woke up.

title: “Ideal Location, Friendly Service in Boston”
text:
The Onyx Hotel in Boston is in a great location--a seemingly nondescript block, but very easy access to Government Center, TD Garden and a great stroll to the North End. It's a great hotel for tourists and business travelers alike.
Onyx Hotel staff is friendly, helpful and knowledgeable about the neighborhood and the city. Clearly a lot of thought has gone into communicating amenities to guests and ensuring one has a positive experience. Rooms are clean, decorated in a hip, urban style that suits the brand and the location. It can be noisy, especially on a game night, but that's a trade off you should expect booking a room in this part of town.
Be sure to join Kimpton's InTouch Guest Loyalty program for free WiFi, a Raid the Bar card and other amenities--although beware that if you book through some websites and not directly with Kimpton, you will not earn points for your stay--but you will still get special treatment!

title: “"great hotel; very convenient"”
text: Needing a hotel to catch an early flight, I was very impressed. The facility was excellent, staff was extremely courteous and helpful, and the shuttle service was terrific. Initially I was a bit apprehensive about booking a hotel so close to the airport but was definitely not disappointed. The price, especially for a weekend, was very reasonable and there were absolutely no negative aspects of my stay at this facility.

title: “Incredible 1 night stay”
text: I had an incredible night at On The Ave. We had a huge room with a great view of the city. The staff was friendly and super helpful. We were given early check in and extended check out without any problems or issues. I can't wait to come back!!

title: “Very efficient and fun”
text:
Had a great time. Lovely Pool, amazing breakfast, great reception and very nice room.
Only down side was the lack of knowledge of Bell Boys/ Porters about touring city and transport; but they were charming

title: “Better than expected”
text: This hotel is situated app. 2.2 miles from the convention center and 2 miles in the other direction is the magificant mile. Good hotel for business travellers. I stay in various Marriotts, Hyatts, etc and I never write reviews. But I would like to note that this hotel is extremely well kept and clean. It is not run down like most other chain like hotels in the main cities in the US. Also, live piano player in the entrance and beautiful ornate lobby is a plus! Starbucks downstairs makes breakfast easy and again, very well situated.

title: “Outstanding in every respect”
text:
We were recently guests at the DoubleTree Suites in Austin for six nights. Not only is the location excellent; the staff are extremely helpful and friendly. This is especially true of the valet/driver group who went out of their way to make this hotel's local transportation service available to us. This was important to us as we were without a car and needed local transportation to nearby restaurants, markets and St. David's Hospital.
Our adult daughter was with us for most of our stay, so we required a two-bedroom suite. The rooms have been recently renovated and are clean and quite comfortable. We also found the small kitchenette to be a great convenience to us as was the room service, restaurant and bar.

title: “Great Staff, Great Location”
text:
Stayed for 1 night as a Stopover at the end of our vacation to save some money. We were very impressed with the staff they were all so friendly and helpful. The room was small ( we had stayed in another NYC hotel the previous week which was larger but way more expensive) but it was immaculate, very clean, soft towels and comfy bed.
The location was a winner for us, the Scottish Bar across the road was pretty nice and we went to The View Bar at the Top of The Marriot Hotel for the cocktails, buffet and to experience a revolving bar/restaurant. Times Square is at the end of the block but we found the hotel to be quiet. Would stay again if on a short break.

title: “Perfect!!”
text: This was our first trip to New York and we wanted to stay somewhere pleasant with a good location...we got both!!! The location was great. It is in easy walking distance of Macy's, The Empire State building and Fifth Avenue. It wasn't too busy or noisy so we had the best of both worlds.The hotel staff were really friendly and helpful. Our room was very clean and the deco was pleasant. The "Barking Dog Bar and Grill" next door was great. It has a good menu and the service was always spot on. I would definately return to New York and stay in this hotel.

title: “Fantastic Location”
text:
Ok so the rooms are a bit small (we had a European room) but you cannot fault the location of the hotel, the service, and the decor of the rooms themselves. The most comfortable bed I have ever slept in.
The hotel is about a 5 min walk to Quincy market and Fanueil Hall, it's on the Freedom trail and restaurants and bars take no time at all to walk to. 
Recommendations for dinner - Legal Seafoods at the harbour.

title: “Aerie in the City”
text:
Our favoriite hotel in Chicago: moderately priced for the city, friendly, well located on State Street just north of the river within walking distance of good restaurants and shopping.
Most important: ask for a corner room, where floor to ceiling windows on two sides of the charming modern room open to city lights. Try the bar on the roof for a drink around the fire ring. 
Warning, however: don't order room service! Their in room dining is in complete disarray, and the food is marginal at best. There is a good restaurant across the street for breakfast and other meals (Bijan), and a great Italian bistro two blocks away (Quartino's), where they have great wines and genuine Italian regional meats.

title: “Not directly on the Riverwalk”
text:
Had to stay in San Antonio for a conference in October and picked the Hampton Inn because of its location and because the other conference hotels were already booked. If you are carrying a briefcase and laptop to the convention center this can be quite a walk on a hot day. This place is convenient to the Riverwalk - not directly on it. And if you are walking from the Riverwalk at night alone it can feel a little isolated.
That said, for the price, it wasn't a bad hotel. The noise levels, as mentioned in other reviews, can be annoying and the breakfast was so-so. But the room was clean and comfortable, the staff was friendly and helpful and the free internet access was excellent for business travel.
Not a deluxe property but cost-effective and clean.

title: “Excellent budget hotel”
text:
Stayed one night with a late check out 8pm which suited our travel itinerery.
Courteous, friendly and helpful staff. Very clean room, pool and garden area beautifully maintained. Bus just round the corner, restaurants nearby. Highly recommended.

title: “Splendid!”
text:
We loved it! The rooms are all suites, nicely and recently redecorated, the gym is wonderful, the spa is too, the grill off the main lobby offers excellent fare, the golf course is beautiful and challenging for good golfers, the grounds are lovely, there is a fabulous water park, great for the family. We were very pleased. It''s located on a giant mountain park where there is practically unlimited hiking, too.
cz

title: “Best sleep in a long time!”
text:
I just joined Trip Advisor and I am happy to make my first review for the Carlyle Suites Hotel! I recently stayed here with friends for a leisure weekend and I couldn't have asked for a better experience. First off, the hotel is extremely pet friendly! I was able to bring my dog Rocco, who had as warm of a reception as I did by the front desk staff (Thanks Carlos!)
The room was a good size, very clean and lots of closet space. The bathroom was new, all marble with chrome fixtures, a glass shower divider and cool bathroom amenities. But the best part was the bed! The Carlyle actually has tempur-pedic beds in every room. If you have never slept on one, then try this hotel ASAP! They have great support and the comfy duvets create a magical sleep.
They also have a full kitchen in the room with a fridge and stove too. Good WiFi and fancy coffee makers. This is a great hotel! I hope you like it too!

title: “Outstanding Service”
text: We booked this motel thinking that it would be ok for the price. We didn't want to spend a lot on a motel that we wouldn't be at much of the time. We was pleasantly surprised! The motel was nice, though the rooms could use a little updating, it was clean and comfortable. The pool was clean. What impressed us the most was the staff. They were the nicest and most helpful people! Helped with directions, advised of the best places to eat, thinks to see, and told stories of growing up around Elvis! Great experience, would definately stay there again!

title: “We had a great time despite the snowstorm”
text: This hotel was great for location , service and cleanliness. The food was not the best , but not terrible.Just across the street from Carmine's and Hugo Frogs. We had a great stay there, and only a few blocks from the Magnificent Mile for shopping,

title: “Why there are so many negative comments?”
text: I don't understand why there are so many negative comments? Hostelworld site there are not so much unhappy comments at this hotel so i trust they more. Ok, this is not five stars Hilton and maybe not best choice to honeymoon, except you love very old style ascetic accomodation :) Maybe this is more backpack travellers hotel and building is also old and not renovated at long time. But basic idea, you want only place to sleep, this was good choice. I was there 3 nights and i pay 50 bucks + taxes per night at single room with shared bathroom, it was a great deal. Ok, if you want better renovated room there are also other hotels and room prices are +200 dollars per night, go here. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Room was well cleaned (ok, room was old) and bed was comfortable, didn't see roachs or other bugs. Shared bathroom was also clean everytime. There was also tv, refrigerator and microwaveoven in the room and free wireless network work well also in my room. There was also "take away" breakfast in a lobby what was nice bonus. Rooms may be littlebit noisy in some times if windows are street side. There also floors keep creak noising so you decide is this negative or positive comment :) Location was excellent if you want watch traditional tourist places. I made daytrip to mall park seeking one museum, whitehouse, capitol... Second day i was Arlington cemetary and Georgetown. If i come back to Washington some day, i come back this hotel.

title: “Horrible place to stay”
text: Travelers beware, this is not a place you would want to stay. The rooms were sub-standard and it is a very long walk from the front desk to the rooms. The only place to eat on site is an Indian restaurant that smelled horrid. This hotel is not in the best part of the city and there is nothing within walking distance to have a bite to eat. We were woken very early in the morning with housekeeping in the hallways cleaning other rooms. Someone even knocked on our door before 8am to ask when we would be checking out. I was appalled since check-out wasn't until 11am. Also it is the ONLY best western that we have stayed at that wanted to charge us $4.00 each for a cold breakfast. Thank goodness there was a Tim Horton's across the street. If you have to stay here we suggest heading north on East Dublin Granville road towards the town of Worthington. There we found a wonderful little town with great shops and an awesome Irish Pub with great food and friendly people.

title: “Noisy but terrific location”
text:
We stayed 2 nights at the Omni last weekend. It is a beautiful hotel from the lobby to the rooms. The concierges were very helpful and the breakfast at the Parker House restaurant was excellent (I usually don't have breakfast in hotel restaurants because they tend to be overpriced and mediocre. This is not the case here). They have homemade corned beef hash, which is a rarity where I come from. 
The location is fantastic. We could easily take the Freedom Trail from the hotel. It has 2 metro stops nearby and everything you need to see is within walking distance or a metro ride away. The only downside to this superb location is the noisiness on the street below. We were on the 3rd floor and could hear the raucous revelers way into the evening. Our room was facing School Street. But that was the only downside. I hope to visit Boston again and I will stay at the Omni again.

title: “Alright hotel, but it aint the four seasons!!”
text: At first i was a bit iffy to stay here because the reviews on this hotel were not that great! Once I arrived all I was praying for was for my hotel room to be clean. Me and my partner have never stayed her before, and we are use to staying in the more pricey hotels but since this was just a weekend we wanted to ourselves we choose to try to spend less. My first thought when i walked n was, ok not bad. The service at the front desk was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean, the only thing that I did not like was that there was a burn hole in our sheets, even though we smoke and had a smoking room we did not expect that. I mean we smoke in our house and our sheets don't have holes so I would not expect to pay money to stay somewhere that has holes in their sheets!! We asked for new sheets and the ones we got were brand new. I slept very well in the room we were in. The bathroom was clean and neat. The only thing I can is you def. are not paying for luxury. The TV is not flat screen and has limited cable channels, and no DVD player. Overall my stay here with my partner was relaxing and quiet and we would def. stay here again. Don't let the reviews scare you!! You have to go and see for yourself!

title: “Good location in New York City”
text: Stayed there for 3 nights in June. This hotel is close to the subway line so access to the city is good , but far away from the buisest areas of the city. About a 15 minute walk to downtown. The rooms were not overly large, but the bed was very comfortable. The free breakfast was wonderful and the staff were very friendly and helpful. Had a problem with the shower head that I complained about that did not get fixed. This was the only problem I encountered. Taxis in NYC were cheap and very easy to get.

title: “Great hotel and close to many site seeing spots!”
text: The Westin Copely service was great. They were very helpful in many ways but mostly about getting around the city especially traveling with a 1 1/2 yr old! The room was nice and clean. We loved the location which was close to Newbury St and the Boston Commons. The hotel was also connected to a mall and had many restaurants in close proximity. The only thing I wasn't happy about was the crib. It was called the Westin Heavenly crib but there wasn't anything heavenly about it. My son did not like it at all. But all and all the pros out way the cons and I would definitely stay there again!

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: The rooms were outstanding and the hotel was elegant. Subway access was right on the corner and lots of shopping near by. Everything was within walking distance. The bar and restaurant seemed like it would have been great only the hostess took 20 minutes to even look up to ask us if we wanted to wait for a table. Other than that, great hotel in a great location. Try to find a discounted room otherwise it's a little pricey.

title: “Good, Clean and not worth the price”
text: Again I have not read any reviews about this hotel before writing this piece, this is just my opinion. I was booked here because the embassy suites down by the gallaria (sage road, where I always stay) was completely booked. This hotel like I said is clean, no microwaves or refrigerators, they do not offer complementary breakfast and charge $18 for valet or $14 to self park. Based on the value I can get around the Gallaria area for $234 after tax, this place is way below the totem pole. I thought the goal of a business was to attract customers? This hotel had nothing that will make me ever come back. The Embassy Suites, Homewood Suite & Hilton Garden Inn all on Sage road, in my opinion, are way better and a class above this so called HIlton.

title: “Excellent Harbor Views”
text:
The rooms are spacious for a manhattan hotel and the bellhops were always helpful with bags or in tracking down taxis. The view of the Statue of Liberty and Battery Park from the "Harborview" rooms are excellent.
Do the "bed and breakfast" plan if you can. For $40/day extra, we received the breakfast buffet for two and free valet parking (ballpark $120/day value)? It's an excellent value. 
Our only disappointment was with the Spa. The treatments were decent, but it is not a full-service spa that you would expect of the Ritz. It's basically two treatment rooms next to the fitness center. No place to relax before or after a treatment (no sauna/steam room/pool/etc.). And it's not like the treatments were less expensive than if it were a full-service spa.

title: “A Very Nice Place”
text:
This was my first stay at a Comfort Suites and I am now a fan. While certainly not in a garden setting it served my purposes well. The facility is especially nice. No worries about the bathroom being clean or if there are enough towels, etc. It is just a very professionally run operation and, in my view, a very good value for the money.
P.S.: There are a number of restaurants convenient to the hotel. If you happen to go to the "Shake and Steak" you'll want to try the butterfinger milkshake. Hey, the hotel has an exercise room:)

title: “Great staff, excellent value”
text: I had a great two-night stay here and would definitely stay again. Service at this hotel was excellent and the value was outstanding. The folks at the front desk were especially friendly, helpful and professional. The nightly rate was below almost of the hotels in the area. My room was very clean and came with a fridge and microwave. TV had about 70 channels if you care about that. I enjoyed the morning breakfast which -- though fairly basic (cereal, rolls, fruit, juice, coffee, etc) -- was more than adequate. Drawbacks? The elevator was a bit slow and a little messy at times because it was heavily used. Pool is quite small though well-maintained. The neighborhood behind the hotel is a bit dicey and might make some visitors uneasy, but I had no problems walking the four blocks or so along Commerce (the main street) to the Rivercenter convention area, even late at night. Just use your common sense. I saw several cops on bikes in the area. Hotel also has a shuttle that runs until about 10:30 if you're nervous. Parking was well-lit and secure. Unlike the earlier poster, I had no problems at all with the train. It passed by several times during my stay, but I barely heard it over the air conditioner. Overall, a great stay at an excellent hotel. A much better value than most of the overpriced hotels in the area.

title: “Good location, Small rooms/beds, Arrogance at the front desk”
text:
The location of this hotel is good, and the price reasonable (NYC Prices).
We booked 2 rooms for 6 people.
The rooms are very small, and the beds very small.
We asked to change room to a larger one, but the hotel only offers the same small room with small beds.
When we asked to get towels etc. in accordance with our booking (4 persons in one room) the front desk clerk got rude and showed arrogance that I did not understand. Next time in NYC I'll find another hotel...

title: “horrid New Years”
text: We attended a new years party that was put on by a different company but used the catering services of the hotel in which we stayed, the Hyatt Regency Capitol Hill. The Service provided by the hotel was horrible. I can not believe that the hotel agreed to host a new year's eve party with 3,000 people in attendance. It took over an hour to get from our room (7th floor) to the lobby. We finally used several sets of stairs and the employee entrance to get to the street (thank God there was no fire or emergency!). When we got to the party that the hotel was catering, half the bars promised were non existant. We waited in a very long line for a drink for almost two hours and never got one. The food that they had set up to feed 3,000 people consisted of a 10 foot long table being served from one side only. Finally, the following day it took us TWO HOURS to get our car out of vallet parking. We almost missed our flight home. NEVER AGAIN. NEVER will I stay at this hotel again. To boot, the food in the hotel is extremely expensive and not very good. Go to Hawaii people, it's cheaper than this hotel!

title: “Great location”
text:
We stayed 2 nights at the Eventi for President's Weekend. The location was great as we have a daughter who lives in the West end. We were able to get on street parking which was a big bonus without having to use the garage. Staff was very friendly. Room was on 16th floor with wonderful view of the Empire State building. Room was very clean, small, but extremely comfortable bed and pillows. Bathroom was very well equipped with nice shower, two nozzles, and nice amenities.Complimentary wine reception could have been attended each night we were there, but could only get to it once. This and coffee in the morning are nice additions.
Good location and quiet at night. Security is good in evening as we had to show our room key to get on the elevator! Also Pet friendly, as we saw pets, but never heard them!!

title: “Had a great time, very pleased.”
text:
After reading some of the reviews on her I was dubious to book this hotel.
I booked through[-] and although it is not the best hotel I have stopped in, it is by no means the worst.
I got a shuttle from JFK to the Pennsylvania, I was pleasently greeted by the doorman who pointed me in the right direction towards reception.
Once I got there, my room was ready and waiting and for the price I paid the room was satisfactory.
The only problem I had was getting to sleep due to all the "Sirens" going off all night, but just as in the movies it happens all the time and i'm sure others in more expensive hotels has the same problem now and again.
As with most New York hotels you are paying to be right in the middle of the action, the only time you are in your room is when you are asleep.
I was pleased with my room and the service i received the whole 4 days.
I would go back again in a second and happily stay at the Pennsylvania Hotel.

title: “Good location , so-so hotel.”
text: This hotel was only three blocks from the Capitol building so we could see a lot of sites with my family. The hotel is okay , food is very good but the service is a little slow at times, cleanliness could be better. For the money we spent I expected rooms to be nicer and more modern.

title: “Brilliant place to stay”
text:
Excellent place to stay particularly if you are visiting the Space center (only 2-3 mins drive). Rooms are large and very clean, breakfast was good and the staff were extremely friendly and helpful -great recommendations for evening meal. Superb value for money.
Michael B

title: “hospitality and charm on the riverwalk”
text: We absolutely love the Sheraton Gunther. It's a block from the Riverwalk and much more charming and peaceful than many of the mega hotels on the riverwalk. The location is fabulous and the staff really goes out of their way to make guests feel welcome. The rooms are stylish and fit the decorum of a historical landmark hotel. The restaurant has a baker with fresh pastries and starbucks coffee with patio dining and best of all interesting "people watching" Best of all our favorite Restaurant Bohanans is right next door.

title: “Great Location but No Housekeeping”
text:
I visited for a few nights in April on business. I travel often all over the US. The rate I paid was U$171/night. I must say I've driven in many big cities: New York, Philly, WashintonDC but Boston was the most challenging for me. Poor signage, windy roads, tunnels, one-ways & pedestrians darting into the street made me a little on-edge. On to the hotel...
Here's what I liked about the hotel:
1. Location is great. You can walk to many of the attractions. Beautiful, clean area. 
2. Valet, front counter staff friendly and helpful with directions and questions during check-in.
3. Quick and efficient service at the lounge/restaurant. Food was above average. Try the strawberry rhubarb dessert! Yum.
4. For the business portion we had a dinner in the meeting room. The dinner and service from catering was also above average. 
A few things I didn't like about the hotel which I see others wrote about are:
1. Dark, dingy rooms. I stayed in 1034. I didn't mind the view was a brick wall but as a result it received very little natural light. I little difficult to get good lighting to see anything.
2. Housekeeping. I left my room in the morning to go to the conference. I came back to drop off brochures, etc at 1:00pm. The room had not been cleaned. I went for lunch, visited with some friends and came back at 4:00pm to grab my walking map. The room had not been cleaned. I came back to change for dinner at 6:00pm to find my room 'cleaned'. He/She flipped the covers back over the bed and (OF COARSE) took the $10 tip and the pad with 'Thank You' written on it. I couldn't believe it! It made me wonder if the sheets had been changed before my arrival??? The ironing board was left out (I took it out to iron a shirt) and the towels in the bathroom were left on the floor. So much for tipping the housekeeping staff for good service. Perhaps the reason for a dark dingy room? I mentioned the problem to the front desk person on check out. He advised me that I needed to fill out a customer satisfaction card. I said I'm telling him for the hotel's benefit not so I can vent/complain. He again, politely, urged me to fill in the card. I didn't and left to catch my flight. Probably many good, hard-working housekeepers in this hotel but where is the management to ensure quality? 
I would not stay here again.

title: “no sleep”
text: Arrived around 5pm. Showered then out for our first time in the big apple. Stayed out until approx 10-30 pm, then back to hotel for a good nights sleep and an early start the next morning. No such luck. The constant noise from ground zero meant that we were awake at 2am, then could not get back to sleep. I ended up walking the streets of NY, at 5 am. My wife rang me at 8am to see if I was ok. Asked to be moved to another room only to be told hotel full.I think the hotel should be closed until all the work complete. Spoiled our first visit to NY.

title: “Nice place, good value for price”
text: I stayed at The Bay Club for a week in December '04 while attending a seminar on-site. The staff was very friendly during my stay. The common areas are clean and the view from the restaurant in to the marina is a nice change for a midwesterner like myself. I would definately rate their complimentary breakfast buffet one of the best I've experienced. My room was spacious, perhaps a little dated, but very comfortable and clean. The in closet safe was a nice touch. Since I was in a seminar all day and busy catching up on work in the evening I can't really comment on proximity to area attractions but it's convenient to the airport and there are a multitude of restaurant options nearby. While not a resort destination by any means, I would not have any issue recommending this propery.

title: “We loved the Park Plaza -- we held a family reunion there three years in a row!”
text:
We have been staying at the Park Plaza Hotel for the last 9 years, every time we came to the Los Angeles area to visit. We have enjoyed the excellent service and great accommodations so much that we have held our family reunion there for the last three years. 
We highly recommend the Park Plaza to anyone wanting a hotel that not only provides clean, comfortable rooms, but also friendly and professional service. The Park Plaza is close to The Grove, Farmer's Market, and other Los Angeles attractions, as well as being one block from a lovely park where guests may go to jog or picnic or enjoy other outdoor activities.
We consider the Park Plaza "our other home" whenever we come to Los Angeles.

title: “Pleasantly surprised!”
text:
We stayed at the Hudson for four nights during our first trip to NYC. The hotel was recommended to us by my partner’s colleagues, due to its location, however , after booking the trip and reading the reviews on TripAdvisor I was apprehensive (to say the least!) about our choice of hotel. My main concerns were the bathroom with glass wall (I value my privacy), and the stories of loud music coming from the club throughout the night.
Following an early morning and long flight, we arrived at the hotel almost spot on 3pm and went to check in- we were advised that check in was currently unavailable but to wait, and we would be called over 5-10 minutes later. 10 minutes later we noticed plenty of other people checking in without any problems, so my partner queued again and was successful in securing our room key. There were many others waiting around reception with their suitcases in the same predicament. 
The (standard) room was a very pleasant surprise- we were on the 10th floor, with no noise audible from the club (and relatively little from the street), the room had plenty of space for suitcases etc. and felt compact, rather than claustrophobic. The bathroom did have a clear glass wall, but when using the curtains outside and inside (there is a sheer curtain outside and two shower curtains on the inside) you couldn’t see a thing. My partner did struggle slightly with the size of the bathroom (he is 6ft 4in), but not enough to make it an issue. The bed was comfy, and the room was warm.
There are a number of great restaurants within walking distance from the hotel- our favourites were Eatery, El Centro and Sushi Damo- along with a great Whole Foods Store at Columbus Circle. Most of the time we walked around Manhattan (a slow walk from the hotel down to the financial district took a couple of hours), but the subway is easily accessible at Columbus Circle. We didn’t utilise any of the hotel amenities (e.g. gym, bar, cafeteria etc.) so can’t comment on those. The hotel doesn't offer free Wi-Fi so my suggestion would be to visit the Starbucks very close by (<2 min walk) and use theirs.
The only negative comment I do have is in relation to the staff at the reception desk, and I agree with other reviews that they can be very rude- in addition to our problems checking in, an example is one morning my partner wanted directions to a well known toy store, which happens to be round the corner from the hotel- we went up to a well staffed, empty desk and after eventually being acknowledged by the guy behind the counter were told (rather rudely) that we would have to go and ask the concierge. It would have taken him seconds to answer our question and we would have been left with a much better impression. Other than that we found New Yorkers in general to be most helpful, and certainly more helpful that strangers we encounter in the UK!

title: “We'll be back!!”
text:
My friend and I discovered, after reserving our Clipper tickets, that all the hostels in Seattle were full. ALL of them. We were determined to go, however, so we looked up hotels, not expecting anything we could really afford. Listing in order of most economical, the Panama stood out so we read the reviews. Most of the contributors do not like it at all, some even claiming the place is haunted & creepy. We figured it can't be too busy then, so I called about a double bed room and was told they had one open. We tried to reserve it over the phone with my friend's credit card but the clerk said a room was reserved for us that weekend. This made me a little nervous: after reading the reviews, I feared it wasn't too secure, and we were concerned about having nothing to fall back on. 
Well, we needn't have worried at all. Upon our arrival, yes the stairs were daunting, but it was so funny and quaint to see some dude sitting up there with his little table & drawer, writing in a book! After arranging our stay, we were shown to the next floor up ~ MORE STAIRS ~ and led to a very nice, tidy and extremely comfy, 2 double-bed room with filmy curtain and antique furniture. It felt like being in a classic movie! It really was beautiful. It had a bare, thrifty and commonsense atmosphere, but it was reassuring somehow. 
The ladies restroom down the hall has a clawfoot tub.... just make sure you check with management for a plug. I had to improvise with a wrapped piece of soap that just happened to fit in the drain quite nicely. Also, the hot water wasn't great so I settled for a cool pick-me-up instead of the hot soak I anticipated. Still, I mean to enjoy that tub next time we're there. 
... because we absolutely want to stay there again, for two nights instead of just one!

title: “Amazing customer service And breakfast staff”
text: Carol Williams was so courteous and was her breakfast team. Hot good breakfast. Loved my stay. Very honest staff and when I checked about the car breakin reviews they said it was true and the guy was caught. Will stay again.

title: “Made an ordinary Monday night, excellent!”
text: The service was excellent! Came in with no reservations looking for a room and were upgraded to a Penthouse suite. Christine made us feel so comfortable and as if we were VIP clients. The room was nicely decorated and the hotel had a rather sexy element to it. The bathrooms were my favorite, very swanky. Great balcony and an awesome lounge/ bar area downstairs. There's a Starbucks about 20 feet away, that's always a plus. The thing I liked least was not knowing how to work the radio. I definitely look forward to staying here again.... Round 2!

title: “Exceeded our expectations”
text: We had the pleasure of staying at the Seaport Hotel over Labor Day weekend. We were there for a wedding, and this was the recommended hotel. We are really happy we stayed here. The service was excellent, the rooms were clean and nicely furnished, bathrooms and toiletries were very high quality, and the food in the restaurants was good. The bellhops and front desk staff were very helpful. The only area that needs improvement is the concierge. The one time we tried to use the concierge (to ask for directions to the childrens museum), there were 3 people ahead of me, and she kept calling out for help, but nobody came. After waiting 10 minutes, I went over and asked one of the guys working the front door and got my answer in 10 seconds. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great location, Fabulous lobby, okay rooms”
text: In town for a conference and booked through Hotwire. Got a fabulous rate of $135 for a small, double bed room. Lots of good points to this hotel. Staff was friendly, lobby/entrance well appointed and location is exceptionally convenient. But lots of bad points too. Elevators were dead slow and stopped at floors where no people were there. The room itself was tiny, tiny, tiny. I was glad my colleague had to cancel at the last minute as it was way too small for two people. I liked the in-room fridge and the bathroom had all the necessities. Overall, the room and bath were a little grubby but acceptable. My main problem was that someone nearby was smoking (10 floors away from the nearest smoking floor) and it was venting INTO my bathroom. After a couple of days, I finally convinced someone to duct tape a piece of cardboard over the bathroom vent and that seemed to solve the problem. Breakfast had a great fruit salad and selection of okay pastries and bagels. There is no in-room coffee supplies and coffee is not available in the lobby until 7am weekdays and 7:30 weekdays. This was frustrating when I had to be at 8am meetings (no time to eat). I don't see why coffee can't be put out in the lobby at 6 or 6:30 when staff was clearly walking around with cups of coffee themselves. I also found the signs 'begging' for tips at breakfast rather offensive. Either pay your staff appropriately or do not have a maitre'd and server for a self-serve buffet. Why should I tip to be seated and to receive a bill that says "0.00"? Seems totally unnecessary. Overall, this was good value for NYC. Don't know if I would have paid the listed rates, but for the Hotwire rate, I was willing to put up with the inconveniences.

title: “Good location, good value for money”
text:
I've chose staying a the Milford whilst in NYC due to it's location and price. 
as i was traveling by myself, it was important for me that the hotel will be in a crowded location, and 8th avenue, between 44th & 45th streets is just that!
the hotel lobby and reception was in the midst of being renovated so it was a bit messy, but the staff were really nice. 
my room was unbelievably small, but it was fine by me as i didn't intend to stay too much in it anyway :) 
the view from the 28th floor was AMAZING, the room was clean and so did the bathroom. 
i'll definitely stay there again next time!

title: “Perfect location!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel recently while in town for the Boston Marathon. Despite the huge crowd for the marathon, the hotel staff was incredibly efficient, friendly, and helpful. The location of this hotel is absolutely perfect - right across the street from the Prudential center (and Prudential Center T station), very close to Symphony Hall, and 1 block from the marathon route. The hotel is also within walking distance to Fenway Park.
The room was average sized, but comfortable. There were really great views of the city from the window and the room was very very quiet - impressive considering the hotel was full. The room had a small refrigerator also. There are many restaurants nearby - both expensive and fast food. Near Symphony Hall, there is a CVS pharmacy and a Whole Foods Grocery store. There is a Starbucks in the lobby and a Cold Stone Creamery across the street!. We bought some groceries at Whole Foods and stocked our room refrigerator. Perfect for getting prepared for the marathon. My only complaint is the room rate was very high - but you definitely get what you pay for and it was worth it. 
The entire Back Bay area of Boston is a gem. We have visited several times and enjoy the area. Next time we come to Back Bay we will stay at this Hilton, if we can afford it!

title: “Good location”
text: We stay there this past weekend for a holiday getaway. We had a pinacle king room or a junior suite. This place needs some updating. The lighting is horriable and no table to enjoy meals brought in. It had only one sink in the bathroom area and the heating unit sounded like it was going to fall off the wall. The staff was nice and the restaurant was great and ended up eating two nights there. It was the holdays and the whole town was busy so things were hectic all over. But the Whitehall could use a little update. Oh the view for our junior suite was over the garbage area and when the trucks came at 5AM woke us up. Not a nice touch.

title: “Right in the Middle of the Action”
text:
We stayed 4 nights at the Hotel Mela in NYC in late August. We had booked a travel package deal which included flights and accommodation that was nearby to all of the attractions, modern, not too expensive, had good reviews and no bedbugs! We weren’t disappointed with Hotel Mela.
It is located less than one block from Times Square, the theatre district and was within walking distance of the Rockefeller centre, 5th Avenue, The Empire State Building and many other attractions. In addition, the subway was also nearby for sites that are a bit further away. 
The rooms although tiny (as expected for NYC) were clean and modern and contained all of the amenities required, such as an in room safe, coffee and tea making facilities, a fully stocked mini bar (which was the first I’d seen in our travels around the USA) and a television. The free in room WIFI was not the most reliable as the signal quite often dropped out, but for checking emails etc it did the job. With the mini bar, the hotel staff warned us, that it was sensor activated so if you move or touch anything you will be charged. Unfortunately this makes using the fridge to cool your own items not possible.
The room was fully air-conditioned but you could open the window if you wanted to get a little fresh air. The air-conditioner could be a little noisy as it turned on and off but not enough to bother us greatly. Considering we were in the central part of town the rooms were amazingly quiet mainly because of the double glazed windows.
I have to commend the housekeeping staff. Every morning we’d put our sign up that our room was ready for servicing and by the time we’d get back from breakfast it would already be done! I have never stayed somewhere where the room has been cleaned so quickly and efficiently everyday.
Complimentary newspapers were available every morning in the lobby for guests to read and the hotel restaurant, Saju Bistro, next door was a nice place to start the day with tasty breakfasts. It also serves French inspired meals all day and has a bar but we chose to eat lunch/dinner elsewhere. They did seem to struggle one morning when it was busy as there was a mistake with one of our dishes.
Being in the central part of town we were spoilt for choice with regards to eating. As we were unsure what was good we asked the hotel staff and their recommendation for John’s Shanghai Chinese food was well deserved. The restaurant staff were attentive and the food very tasty. 
Another hotel staff recommendation for traditional NYC style pizza was John’s Pizzeria (not sure if any relation to John’s Shanghai?) was also good. Great pizzas at a more than ample size including whole wheat crusts if you want to make it a little less bad for you! 
On our third night we had dinner at Virgil’s BBQ just a few doors up from the hotel. We highly recommend this place for that tasty US style BBQ smoked meat!
The hotel is more of a tourist hotel because of its location and so it may not be suited for business travel, especially since the Internet was not reliable. It would be helpful for Hotel Mela to have some more tourist information in the lobby, but other than that the hotel is in a fantastic spot and the staff are more than happy to offer assistance when asked. If I visit NYC again for pleasure I would certainly consider staying here.

title: “Rooms are just right for 2”
text: Staff was very helpful. Bottles for filtered water to go in halls. Beds were very comfortable and room was just the right size for 2. Clean not real big but if you are going to spend the day in the room why go to San Francisco

title: “A touch of heaven”
text: My young daughter and I were flying home from a lousy vacation in Mexico when our flight was delayed because of poor weather in Seattle. My friend called me and told me to try to book a hotel in Seattle because she didn't think we'd be able to make the 25 minute drive to our home. Our nightmare vacation seemed to never end, and I had no way to book a hotel because we were boarding a flight. To my surprise the airline had wireless and I was able to find out that my friend called every airport hotel and they were all booked, except for one room at the Cedarbrook lodge, so she booked it. We arrived at 3 am and the shuttle managed to pick us up in spite of the frozen, unplowed road. We were exhausted and I didn't think I could bare one more night in a bad hotel, after the disappointing trip, but to my shock, this hotel was gorgeous. I honestly (and I'm being honest here) almost wish I had saved the thousands of dollars on the disgusting Mexico (5 star) resort and just checked in a few miles from home. I could have slept a week. We snacked on fresh fruit and ice cream before bed. The rooms were so clean you could eat off the floors, as if no one had ever stepped foot into them before that day. The sheets were crisp, soft, with a big cozy comforter and my young daughter kept asking me if this was our new home...to which I answered, "yes". We slept like babies and in the morning went to the lobby for breakfast which was included in the price, and it was the best buffet breakfast I had ever seen..and I've traveled plenty. Homemade granola, hard boiled eggs, fresh juices, delicious breads. I cannot imagine even the most discriminating of travelers being disappointed in any way. I couldn't find anything to complain about and frankly I didn't think there was such a thing when it came to travel. As I write this, I realize that perhaps I should have checked in at Cedarbrook instead of booking my next trip. At least I know it is there if when I return from my long travel, I need a weekend reprieve. The only downside to this hotel, might be that it is not located in the center of Seattle. One definitely will need a car, or use public transportation to get to downtown Seattle.

title: “Great Gift Shop”
text:
I stayed at this hotel last week for a quick "in and out" meeting. I always try to find a nice item to take back for the kids....I must say I was soooo incredibly impressed with the staff of the hotel gift shop. The staff was working very hard to complete an inventory once the shop had closed......but Lorena welcomed me in to the shop, helped me find items to take back, all with the greatest smile! Awesome. As a frequent traveler, service means everything to me. Thank you Lorena and the store staff!!! 
Al........Philadelphia

title: “Beautiful hotel for a romantic stay”
text: This hotel is beautiful and elegant, and the staff was friendly. If you're interested in the history of the hotel, look for Cliff for a tour. You may even get to see the suites.

title: “Ideal and friendly”
text: I had visited Venice Beach briefly when staying at Santa Monica in 1994, so to find such an ideal location for a holiday was wonderful. A friend and I stayed for 7 days from 2-9 October 2007. We were made very welcome and nothing was too much bother for the staff who were always helpful, patient and showed us a very warm welcome. The room was brilliant, the best of our three centre Holiday (San Francisco and New York being the other two). Having the beach so close, the sound of the sea at night and the palm trees to give some shade - it couldn't have been better. Restaurants and bars in the immediate area were good for eating and a two minute walk to the bus stop for buses to Santa Monica and beyond were well situtated. There's lots of free day time 'enterntainment' on the Boardwalk too! A wonderful relaxing place. Blue skies and temperatures in the low 80's all week. We shall return! Highly recommended.

title: “good value, good location”
text: I have stayed a half-dozen times at The Mosser and am staying there again this month. I keep going back because it has a great location (right off Market, right by BART and MUNI, near Union Square), low price, clean rooms, and friendly desk service. It also has good coffee and fresh muffins for breakfast.

title: “Fantastic stay”
text:
Loved everything about the hotel - my room was spacious, clean and comfortable. I felt very relaxed and have rarely slept so well on a holiday.
I had an end room, so had no passing traffic, so heard no noise at all when sleeping.
I actually thought the hotel was a great location - I liked that it was in an area where normal people lived. I walked everywhere (two exceptions - cab home from the theatre and a cab to Battery Park one morning) - from 5th Avenue, Times Square, Central Park, but when just going to a walk I preferred to head south to Chelsea/Union Square area.
I ate in the hotel one night when I was tired and cold and it was delish ! I didn't make it up to the pool and bar ... I actually forgot about it.

title: “Overnight in LaLa land”
text: 2nd time in 4 months that I have stayed at this hotel. Great location. Company car took us to dinner in Beverly Hills and picked us up. Very nice touch. Rooms are nice, was upgraded to a suite this time. Staff extremely helpful and friendly. Valet a little pricy at $36.00 a night, but overall a great place to enjoy a night in LA!

title: “The name of the place (COMFORT INN) says it all”
text:
If you are looking for a clean affordable place to stay that is
conveniently located near all and ultra staff friendly, look no further, you've just found it! The Comfort Inn on N. Stemmons Freeway in Dallas offers a wide variety of amenities with no hidden cost."
Each room comes complete with it's own work desk and chair,
a microwave, coffee pot, refrigerator, lighted make up mirror,
blow dryer, satellite/cable tv, and not one, not two, but three
conveniently located phones. There's even one in the bathroom!
The room service was really good and the simply comfort of knowing that a hotel attendant was stationed at the front desk 
at all times was definitely an added plus for someone like me, 
who thoroughly enjoys the comfort of knowing your safe to sleep in a foreign place with the luxury of having such peace of mind. 
As a tourist, we truly enjoyed our stay at the Comfort Inn and we're sure that you will too. J.R. from New Jersey

title: “Beautiful, historic hotel with great customer service”
text: This hotel was absolutely beautiful. Apparently it is turning 100 years old this year but the restoration is impressive. I found all of the staff to be extremely customer friendly. The rooms were fairly spacious and elegant. The location is perfect and within walking distance of many sites in Boston. If you like to take mass transit, the T subway is literally 1 block from the hotel. They have a very nice roof top fitness center. It doesn't just have 1 treadmill. It has quite a few machines and a section with free weights, etc. Overall, great experience. I would definitely stay there again!

title: “Great Location, New Hotel & Nice rooms”
text:
I've been to NYC many times and stayed in various hotels. This is by far the best in terms of location, cleanliness, and service. My family and I stayed here a total of 5 nights in NYC. 
This hotel is very convenient. Its located right in the Herald Square area just a few steps away from Macy's. It's about a 5 minute walk to Times Square. The subway line is right in front of the hotel. Penn Station is also a block away.
The hotel has only been built up for 7months so it's really new and clean. The service was overall excellent. Free internet, buiness centre with free color printing, a gym. I was really impressed by how helpful the staff were.
The only draw back is it's one of the more expensive hotels and will set you back about $300 US per night.

title: “Convenience without the crowds during Comic-Con”
text:
Location: Wonderful hotel situated within walking distance of downtown San Diego & Seaport Village. We stayed at this establishment because we were attending Comic-Con and wanted to lodge closeby to the convention. After a long day of walking & sitting in panels amidst the crowds, the last we wanted to do was take a shuttle bus ride (although very convenient for others) to our destination. This gave us the opportunity to rest in our own room, when we wanted refuge from the convention. Plus we never had to deal with the huge crowds passing our way or major traffic along Harbor Blvd (at least fronting the hotel). There is a short walk to the downtown area for other eateries, nightlife and a grocery run. The city had beautiful weather during our stay, so we didn't mind travelling on foot to check out events outside the convention. 
Room: We stayed in a premium view king room in the Harbor Tower. At the time of our arrival, we were instantly greeted by the Hyatt workers for baggage assistance and were lucky enough to check-in early. The room was a bit dated, but definitely had the potential for upgrade. There was some construction remodelling during the time of our stay, so we can't wait to see what these changes will be someday. Very comfortable and clean, with a gorgeous view of the city. 
Food: Ordered room service a few times during our stay. The quality of the food was above average for the most part. We had no hestitation ordering from the hotel. We also ate the grand breakfast at Lael's (buffet in the Harbor Tower). Continental selection was wonderful, but wish there was a greater selection for the grand buffet. Loved the make-to-order omelettes, but was looking for a better meat (aside from bacon, sausage and mexican beef dish) and veggie selection. 
Service: Five stars for the hotel staff. Every member of the team was very helpful.
Overall: Would definitely recommend this hotel when attending a major SD convention. Price of the hotel is a bit on the high-side, but worth the money. Staff is very friendly and accommodating.

title: “AMAZING”
text: Stayed seven days and everything was wonderful especially the staff recommend it to everyone!!! The room came with cookware...everything was clean...and if you needed anything all you had to do was ask front desk and they will do there best to get it for you

title: “My AMAZING wedding weekend at the Sheraton Brookhollow!!”
text: I recently had my wedding at the Sheraton Brookhollow. The entire event/catering staff were so helpful and accommodating throughout the entire wedding planning process. They offer what few hotels/wedding venues can, they take care of the bridal cake, decorations, catering, and wedding planning all with their wedding packages which really takes a lot of the stress out of the wedding planning process. Their ballrooms are beautiful and can accommodate just about any size of wedding. We actually signed the contract during their renovation of the hotel after Ike. We took a big gamble as we had signed without seeing the final product of the ballroom and hotel. Well we surely weren’t let down! The hotel has been beautifully renovated We had several events planned at the hotel for the wedding weekend and catering staff was able to pull it all together for us, I did not even have to worry during the weekend about anything as everything was all taken care of. I have received nothing but amazing responses about our wedding, from the food to the decorations. I am so happy to hear that our wedding was one of the best weddings our guests have ever attended which makes our decision to have the wedding at the Sheraton Brookhollow such a great one. My husband and I will always have wonderful memories of this hotel and of the great experience we shared planning it and enjoying it! Surely the best time our lives thus far!

title: “Another good experience”
text:
Stayed 3 nights at the conference rate of $259 + tax per night. 
It's basically what you'd expect of a hotel of this class. The room was fine and comfortable. As a Marriott Gold member I get free wifi (normally ~$13 per day) and that worked well. It also gives be access to the Exec lounge and this is a nice large lounge with a good breakfast.
Gym is excellent with a large amount of good kit in a spacious area. No pool but a sauna/steam room (or something like that which I didn't use). The location is good with lots of amenities in the area. 
It's right next to the convention center which is a short walk away.

title: “Excellent Hotel in Great Location”
text: We stayed at the Andra one night in order to take in the King Tut Exhibition in Seattle. We chose the hotel because it was a partner with the exhibition and offered free parking (thank you!). From the time we arrived until we left, we can't say enough about how great everyone was. The bellhops were great, the front desk staff friendly and helpful. My husband forgot his toothbrush and they brought one up to our room in record time. We had a lovely 1 bedroom suite and it was clean and well-appointed. Even though we chose the hotel because of the exhibition we attended, I would choose this hotel again simply because it was good, clean and in a great location.

title: “dump”
text: This place is the worst value I have encountered in all my travels in the US. Dirty towels in the room, garbage left in the waste baskets, no in-room coffee maker, no bottled water, exaggerated claims about a "fitness facility", and it's in the dark ages with respect to internet access.

title: “A Washington gem”
text:
The Hotel George is that perfect mix of good value, convenient location and quality, with some lovely touches thrown in like free wine in the evenings. Our double queen bed room was not large but for the price we did extremely well.
While the hotel is perfectly situated for travel to and from Union Station, and is close to the Capitol and not far from the Mall, be aware that walking west towards Downtown takes you through some seedy areas. Our family certainly had no problems but then again we weren't out late either. 
The staff were tremendous and Kimpton have really done a great job with this hotel. Highly recommended.

title: “Great Value, Great Location”
text: I travel to San Diego quite often, and I am extremely glad I had the chance to experience Hotel Solamar. Typically I look to try different hotels on each visit, and Solamar was a pleasant surprise. I was greatly impressed by nearly every aspect of the hotel, and it made enjoying the Gaslamp district easy and affordable. Favorite Features: Pool Deck with Bar and Cabanas, 6Six restaurant, nice modern rooms, ballpark views from room. I was also very satisfied with the room value, as it felt inexpensive for a four star hotel!

title: “Generally good”
text: Excellent location, comfortable (but small) rooms and helpful staff. There was no gym that we could see though, despite it being advertised. I would stay there again, although it was too expensive to book two single rooms instead of a twin which was very disappointing. It was also very difficult to pay for anything by credit card in the bar - the staff insisted on putting everything on our room bill, even though we requested otherwise. They didnt seem to have faclities for taking a credit card separately. Other than that, the hotel was quiet despite being in a very central location. I would recommend asking for a room away from the lift though, as the "bing" noise went on day and night.

title: “Good location, inexpensive for the quality”
text: Had a great stay here - our room was very nice and in a nice location away from the beaches and dowtown but near enough to explore everywhere. San Diego itself is lovely and not too busy considering its a main city. We got a good deal on this hotel and decided to arrive early and stay an extra night - the reception staff were really helpful and accommodated us at the last minute.

title: “Was nothing it was supposed to be.”
text: The reservation was wrong. I was charged more than I was supposed to be. I had to pay MORE for the original reservation that I was supposed to receive. It was difficult to work with the front desk. Poor customer service. Everything was under construction. Place was a mess, and the elevator wasn't working well.

title: “Close to San Diego train station”
text:
Walked there after getting off a LA - San Diego train with full suitcase of luggage. Took about 15 mins walk to get there - straight road and then to the left.
Close to shops, good location.
First time I flushed the toilet it blocked. Raised this with the cleaning lady on our way out who said she will contact maintenance. When we got back it was fixed - wonderful service!
For the price you would probably expect something a little nicer unfortunately it is "good enough" - not bad but not outstanding.

title: “Good value with only minor drawbacks offset by price.”
text:
I would not pop a lot of cash for this place, but at an average of $148/night in an expensive city its a great value in a great location. 
Location: located just off the main Gaslamp district drag, it's very good for people wishing to experience the nightlife without the hassle of cabs and rental cars. It's also a short distance from the airport; I got here in 15 minutes in my rental. Parking is $36/night and that rate is pretty much standard. Petco park can be seen from the 9th floor lounge and is a few blocks away. Seaport/Midway/Ferry to Coronado is a bit longer, but if you don't mind a nice stroll down the city streets you can walk there in about 15 to 20 minutes. 
Room: clean and neat. Nice flat screen TV and very large bathroom, which I like. Keurig with four options (regular coffee, decaf coffee, breakfast tea, and a decaf tea). If you want more of one of these options, just catch your maid and she will likely give you one. Mine was a sweatheart and gave me a couple regular black coffees. I have a king room and the bed is one of the more comfortable hotel beds. It's neat and clean as well. Not much by way of views in my fourth floor room and no balcony. No mini fridge but they do provide a nice ice bucket and amble coffee mugs and glasses. Only one issue I have found is that the bathroom vent links to another room and I could hear people talking and their TV. I shut the bathroom door and it was fine. It's just weird to brush your teeth and hear a gaggle of women talking. Overall I think the style of the room is excellent. AC works well and temperature is comfortable. Comfortable desk chair and sitting chair. I like the room art. 
Amenities: only main drawback is no pool. They will provide a free USA today, which you can read on the 9th floor lounge/bar. The lounge/bar on the 9th floor is really nice and has a view of Petco Park. They also have a "meditation garden" on the 9th floor if you want a quieter place. Workout room is nice and clean, but lacking in terms of equipment. It's merely sufficient for a nice 30 minute treadmill. Hotel bar/restuarant food is decent, not great and not bad. Prices a little steep, but I've found that they are generally consistent with the higher priced food in the area. Drinks are poured on average and are average city prices ($8 for a double jack on the rocks.) All common areas are neat and clean, including a large lounge with ample seating. They will let you eat outside food in the lounge but not in the bar area, even if the bar is not serving food anymore. 
Customer Service: I saw the review of poor customer service and was a bit worried. I did not have this problem. Valet guys are nice and prompt. Also I have a rental, so I could care less how they treat it, but they were always courteous. Front desk check in was smooth even though I booked through hotels.com. My wife decided to join me half way through my business trip and I forgot to say that there would be two people staying and they just gave me an extra key with no fuss. I received pretty good restaurant recommendations consistent with requests, e.g., fine dining versus local blends. 
We don't have a problem with pets on our floor and they do not have solely pet floors. This could be a drawback, but not on my stay.

title: “NO HEARTBREAK HERE!!”
text: My sister and I stayed at Heartbreak Hotel Thanksgiving weekend. We had a room on the first floor and we were very pleased. After reading the recent reviews we were afraid we were going to be disappointed this stay...but we had a blast! The room was clean, there was no outside noise, the staff was excellent, no smokey halls as a previous post had stated and the food was good too!
