I cannot understand how this hotel gets the low ratings for being dirty, smelly and rundown. We enjoyed our time there and will stay again!

title: “Early Check-in Fee?”
text: This property is my go-to stay in Philadelphia for business, and I've probably stayed here 20 nights or more in the past year. Yesterday I got to the hotel early, about 11:15, and asked if they had a room available. After reminding me I was early, of which I was quite aware, the desk clerk informed me that yes, they had a room available, but that they would charge me $35 for the privilege of moving in early. This was not a room they had to clean; it was a room unoccupied the previous night. I politely declined and went off to run errands. This was my first ever experience in years and years of business travel being required to pay a fee to check in early. I was not pleased.

title: “Nothing but smiles”
text:
I stayed there with my wife for 3 nights. Overall a great experience in a geat city. Previous posters make some great points but do your homework prior to booking a trip to San Fran.
The hotel is at the top of Nob Hill so walking to the hotel is mostly uphill. However, walking to any location is fine as you are walking downhill. The hotel does offer limited courtesy transportation - well worth it. Most cab rides to the scenic areas cost less that 7 bucks.
We got the hotel for $140 per night on hotwire.com. Well worth the price. The staff was attentive and helpful. Very clean and very well appointed. Rooms are a little small - but very comfortable.
I will stay there again.

title: “Superb in All Regards”
text: The Crowne Plaza was outstanding all around. The front desk staff, particularly Raquel, were gracious and accommodating, the facility was up-to-date and clean, and the room was fresh and spacious. Needless to say, the location -- a few blocks north of Times Square -- is ideal for a tourist who wants to be in the heart of the NYC action. General Manager Gerry Hughes cares about hotel customers (as is evident from his posts on this site), and this concern shows in all aspects of the hotel. Bravo!

title: “Best Camden Yards Hotel (near Inner Harbour)”
text:
We stayed here over Mother's Day weekend for Saturday night which allowed us to take in the Saturday night and Sunday afternoon baseball games. Parking was a breeze with the parking garage beneath the hotel. For $28, this is the closest parking that you can possibly get to Camden Yards for more than 24 hours of parking in the city. The hotel is conveniently located to the Convention Center, Inner Harbour and other sites in downtown Baltimore. The pool and fitness center have awesome views looking into Camden Yards. The lobby and the rooms were very spacious and clean. Very Modern.
Great stay!

title: “Great stay!!”
text: I have stayed @ carefree inn about 5 times ive enjoyed every time never had any complaints. The staff are very friendly and helpful ive had a different room every time and they have all been nice and clean. Carefree inn offers a nice free breakfast and shuttles to ur destination which is good if you dont know ur way or dont wanna drive. Also you are very close to anything you might need restaurants, pharmacy, grocery whatever you might need i will continue to stay here anytime i have to travel back for my medical needs.

title: “Agood hotel becomes a great hotel in a crisis”
text:
Having had a week at the hotel in the beginning of October and loving it's location we immediately booked it again on our return from Canada.
Hurricane Sandy joined us at the hotel on the Sunday night and we realised that as our airline had cancelled its flight for the next 5 days we would need longer than a day. We were able to extend and reduced our rate by saving money on the usual very acceptable breakfast.
Using the hotel as our shelter base we ventured out every day and at no time were we not teated with great support from the hotel.
The concierge desk staff are the most helpful we have encountered and Melissa on the day of our check out fixed the account and topped off the great service by all staff at the hotel.
The crisis handling was magnificent.
Thank you Renaissance.was

title: “convenient with all basic facilities. average neighborhood”
text:
The hotel has all basic facilities : good parking locations, vending machines, business center (1 pc), free wifi, free breakfast. The bathroom is compatible with most hotels this size. The room was clean, as well as the bed's sheets. 
The hotel is aging : televisions are still old big ones, and had a greenish color. The TV image quality was also average. The room has some old looking furnishing : carpet, sofa, chair... While coming to the hotel,
 I was quite concerned about the neighborhood, as well as the specification that the hotel had "bullet proof windows". Indeed, there is a lot of protections for the guest : special glass doors to access the hotel, heavy doors, locks, and bullet proof windows. I didn't check that last part by myself. 
The external insonorisation was very good : no noise at all from the surrounding roads. However, the internal insolation was not as good and I could hear the neighboors arguing during the night.
Also, when booking with hotels.com, I paid a price 20 USD higher than the receipt I received at the end of my stay. That's around 25%.

title: “wonderful stay and centrally located.”
text: Stayed at this hotel for a business conference, The staff are very warm, friendly and helpful. Room was very nice. It is a very old hotel but has been redone. The history is everywhere and adds to the charm. Very Grand. Loved it. They were very accomodating to our conference. The food service was great and some wonderfully unique tasty treats. Loved watching all the old trolly cars go by and getting close enough to see where that particular was purchased.Walking distance to many restaurants from coffee shops to fast food to 4 star restaurants. A restaurant for every taste.

title: “Great location, avoid 4th floor”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights from the 19th February 07. We had specifically asked not to be on the 4th floor due to other reviews but, when we arrived, that was the only room availalbe. We were tired so decided to go with it - big mistake. The NY fashion show in the square was being demolished during the night and the noise unbearable - we had to put the fake bird noise machine on to attempt to drown out the outside racket. 
We moved to a room on the 8th floor the next night which, although was much smaller for the same price, was lovely and relatively quiet! 
Although the room service was expensive the food was excellent, the service was hit and miss though. They lost one breakfast order totally.
Overall, I would say that the location is excellent, the staff were all extremely helpful, the bar good fun and the koi restaurant superb, pricy food so great for a treat. 
I would stay again but insist on a room on the 8th floor or above.

title: “really is a great deal”
text: I stayed here for 30 nights. It was comfortable and quiet. It's not the Ritz Carlton but it's in a great location next to 24hr JackInTheBox and a gas station/convenience store. If you use coupons it will be cheaper than rent. I got 30 nights for just under 900 and I slept well the whole time. Like I said, the hotel is not elegant but for $30ish per night it's freaking awesome.

title: “Loved this hotel”
text:
We stayed here for a week while visiting New York. 
We parked in the hotel and upon arrival our bags were removed and car was parked within minutes.
Reception: Excellent service, fast efficient and very helpful
Room: We had a corner room which was quite big by NY standards. It included a large walk-in wardrobe that accommodated all of our luggage. The room itself was a little old but was spotless and comfortable. Given what we have paid in similar priced hotels in NY this was easily the biggest room we have stayed in.
Location: Perfectly located for all shops in 5th Avenue and approx a 15 minute walk to Union Square.
Overall I would highly recommend this hotel. It is a little old fashioned, but the service was perfect and coupled with a fantastic room and location, it was well worth the cost.

title: “Nice new modern hotel”
text:
This hotel has a new and modern contemporary look to it. The rooms are set up more like a studio apartment without a kitchen then a typical hotel room. The beds are very comfortable with higher end sheets, pillows, and comforters. The couch was huge and L shaped. It was comfortable enough to sleep on. There is a screen dividing the sitting and sleeping area. There is a huge flat screen T.V. that can be seen from the sitting area and the bed. The room also had a mini fridge. The bathroom was completely done in ceramic tile. There is no bathtub but, the shower is roomy and modern looking. 
If you are flying out they will let you park your car there for free. The airport shuttle runs 24 hours. The shuttle will even take you to nearby shops and restaurants. 
I think this location is a good choice for especially for business people and those who are flying out of the Jacksonville airport. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great stay at Paradise Point!”
text: The room was clean and comfortable. The grounds are beautiful and well maintained. The breakfast at the barefoot grill was very good.

title: “GEm of a hotel”
text: Not 5 star luxury, but everything that you could want in a hotel and much more. Excellent location, great service at the front desk. Nice sized room with modern decor. Room safe. Bedding was to die for. Quiet, secure. Good price even through regular internet pricing. Near downtown and Massachusetts Avenue. Not far from Dupont. They cleaned our room even after we left very late the first day, and we really did not expect it. I would stay there again without a second thought and would be happy for the opportunity. These people know how to run a hotel.

title: “A tranquil oasis in NYC”
text: We were struck by how quiet the hotel was (triple glazing in all the windows.) NIce to come back to somewhere calm and restful after walking round the city all day. Well located in Midtown. Very helpful staff - when we asked to use the business centre the concierge printed our boarding passes for us without charge. Authentic Japanese restaurant which could have been daunting, but the staff were very helpful with the menu. Breakfast buffet offered lots of choice but was quite expensive - but there are plenty of alternatives nearby.

title: “Great location, extremely friendly service.”
text: Perfect location in downtown Chicago. Walking distance to all major sites. Very friendly and helpful staff. Decent complementary breakfast. Clean, spacious rooms.

title: “Class and location”
text:
Our stay at the Hotel Burnham was four nights, from June 22nd through June 26th.
Upon arrival via taxi from Midway airport, we were greeted by Reggie, who took our luggage and directed us to the front desk. 
Check in was extremely polite and very fast. 
Reggie then showed us to our room on the 14th floor (of 15). He detailed a bit of the history of the hotel, and pointed out the various amenities. 
Our room overlooked State and Washington streets with a full view of Macy's (Marshall Fields) flagship store, the old Chicago Theatre (pretty at night, see pics) and in the distance the Marina City towers and the State Street bridge over the river.
The room was adequate in size (bigger than we expected) with a queen bed, settee by the window, entertainment unit with stocked honor bar. It also featured a very nice Panasonic radio/CD player with quality sound. A desk was bedside with free high speed internet connectivity.
The entry way/foyer allowed room for setting up the provided iron. A hairdryer was also provided. 
A safe took space on the floor of the closet, and was large enough to hold an oversized laptop computer, a good sized camera, and just about anything else we wished to put inside.
The bathroom was of economy size, but was immaculate, and provided L'Occitane toiletries. The linens and towels were of high quality, and they weren't stingy with them.
Temperature control was individual per room also.
The hotel itself (outside of the room) was amazing. The detail, and history provided a nice sense of time and place. It was built in 1895 as an office building and was one of the original skyscapers in Chicago (post fire I guess?). 
The trim, iron works, lighting, and carpeting were all wonderful. 
Starbucks coffee was provided every morning in the lobby, and there was a wine tasting available every day at 5pm. The sitting area was small but quaint.
The on site restaurant (The Atwood Cafe) always seemed to draw a crowd. Other than breakfast or drinks at the bar, however, we did not dine here. The breakfast, albeit pricey, was large and fulfilling and the service was a step above.
A special notice should be made as to the service we received at every turn. From the doormen to the front desk, concierge, room attendants, and restaurant, we were made to feel welcome and that our business mattered to them even though the site was full all week.
Very special thanks to Reggie, Alyssa, Keith, David, Antwon and Gus.
The noise mentioned in earlier posts does occur, but we found it minor and not consistent through the trip. There is a new tower being built right across the street from the rooms facing Washington/State, but it is now reaching 20+ stories in height. Most of the noise came from the construction at road level on the street.
The experience here was excellent and we highly recommend this hotel. 
Everything was in walking distance or a very short cab ride.
Two thumbs up.
Tips:
Food: 
Cafe Iberico on N LaSalle. GREAT Tapas.
VTK (Vong's Thai Kitchen) 
Lou Mitchell's for a classic Chicago Breakfast - All eggs double yolked!
Sites:
The Art Institute of Chicago - Could spend several days here.
Millenium Park (The Cloud, Serpentine Bridge etc)
Wrigley Field for a Cubs game
Hancock Tower, less crowds and better views than Sears tower.
Macy's (Old town shopping at it's finest)

title: “Nice business stay”
text: I stayed here when I was in Phoenix for business. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I was conveniently located close to the express ways so I could get to places quickly. The room was clean and nice looking. The business center was good and easily accessible. I did not eat in the restaurant, so I can’t comment on that. The only issue that I had was that the only way to get to my room on the fourth floor was via the elevator. The stairs were for emergency use only and I would have preferred to use the stairs for quicker access.

title: “Nice Hotel...”
text: Stayed in a jr. suite. First room they gave my husband and I was not that nice, floors were stained and didn't 'feel' clean. My husband went down to the front desk and they were very nice about changing our room to accomodate us, and gave us a nice jr. suite on the 33rd floor overlooking the river. The hotel itself is very nice and clean. Great location! Close to Newbury St. and attached to lots of shopping at Copley place. Would consider staying here again.

title: “Will Be Back!!!! Fantastic Hotel!!!!”
text: We checked into this hotel for our 2 year anniversary weekend, front desk were friendly and very quick, our room was very elegant-chocolate covered strawberries and champagne just like booked, very clean hotel and comfortable bedding, we had a great view, we kept bringing up the whole weekend how much we were satisfied with the hotel! We wished they had more parking places once it turns night it was hard to get a good parking place. We will definetly return in the future!!!!

title: “Great location”
text: Slightly bland hotel, very big but very clean, nice rooms. Excellent location - couldn't better it. lots of places to eat in or get take out from nearby. Went to Juniors for breakfast (opp on side street) and Carlinis - excellent italian family style service/portions.

title: “It's nothing special”
text: Please get there at a decent time or you have to use some strange night check in window. It's a decent hotel for the price and it's close to Fisherman's Wharf and Golden Gate Bridge. We have stayed there everytime we travel to San Fran, only because other hotels can be pretty pricy.

title: “Grand Dame”
text: Old grand dame with the frills hotel on 5th Avenue. Stayed 3 nights in June. Fitting of its reputation , the reception was very welcoming with many people assisting. Checkin was fast, and by the time I got to my room the luggage was there already. Okay, was a bit taken aback by , within 5 minutes of arrival, another man came in and introduced himself as my butler. Proceeded to offer to run my bath and unpack my suitcase. I kindly declined, this service is a bit too personal as i had been travelling for a week and have laundry to do. The most comfortable bed i have ever sleft in, ever !! Early morning coffee delivered promptly , a nice treat too.

title: “Great weekend at The Grand Hyatt”
text: My husband, kids, parents and I spent 2 nights at the Grand Hyatt in SF last August. The location of this hotel is great if you would like to stay downtown. It is right at Union Square, close to shops and tour stops. We had two adjoining rooms on the 15th floor. The view from both rooms was amazing. The rooms were recently remodeled. One of the rooms had a vanity right outside the bathroom which I thought was very useful. The beds were very comfortable and the bathroom, although a bit small, was functional and nice looking. The lobby was still under construction, so it got crowded at times but since we were not spending time in the lobby, this did not bother us that much. On the last night at the hotel, we had dinner at the rooftop restaurant which supposedly has one of the best view in SF. I say "supposedly" because we did not get to see anything since the fog had settled in. Overall, a great stay at the Grand Hyatt and I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Thoroughly recommended for a tourist stay in NY”
text:
stayed a week over new year with husband and 2 11yo daughters. got there at 2, told room would be ready at 3 then it was not, then nobody came to tell us it when it was. but apart from that things went pretty smoothly. hotel is a little distance from times square. is surrounded by theatres. felt entirely safe in the area - only concern was falling over in the snow. very convenient for subway which we got a pass for ($28 dollars each) which we had to get from the machines. the people in the booths were singularly unhelpful.
had a bed and breakfast deal but beware you have a choice from a much shortened menue. even having said that I thought the breakfast pretty good and they would vary things round a bit if you asked. loads of restauarants in the area. the hotel restaurant is not bad though the service the one time we ate there was poor - they tried serving the second course when one party member was still eating the first. suggest asking for a room with a view which means one at the front of the hotel. rooms are a little small and the bathrooms are tiny. useful microwave and fridge. excellent food emporium on the next corner so easy to stock up on snacks and drinks. room was nice and quiet. Charles, the front door man sorted out a car for us to go back to newark airport which was the same price as a cab and much more comfy.

title: “A little disappointing...”
text: Staid in this hotel the weekend of March 12, 2004. Although the lobby is beautiful and the staff friendly enough, we were disappointed in the appointments of the room. We staid in a junior suite which was very large with 2 king beds and plenty of room - however, the bathroom was one of the worst designs I've seen - no decent light at all, only one small sink, etc, the beds were VERY uncomfortable, and our view was of piled up rubbish and construction materials on a scaffold outside our window. As I said, service was good - but not exceptional. The hotel restaurant was very good but they played loud rock music throughout so although on decor they tried to create an ambiance - the music killed it. All in all had expected a higher degree of service and luxury based on what I'd read. We stayed at the Westin a few months ago and for $100 less per night had more comfortable beds and the equal amount of service and luxury.

title: “Very pleased with our stay . . .”
text: We had a wonderful stay. We had not been to the hotel since the recent remodel and were so impressed with the decor in the rooms. They have made every effort to upgrade even with the technology in the room. They held our luggage until our late train and it was like having another day in the city. We picked up the luggage about 8:00 PM and made our 9:20 train. They really go out of their way to please.

title: “Don't bring the kids”
text: Beautiful, ultra-modern place, but definitely not for the kids....Room service menu in our room was wrong; when I called, I was told "we've discontinued our children's menu." The pool was also quite unwelcoming. Lots of sophisticated 20 somethings lounging around, but the lifeguard was somewhat hostile to two little girls. I also found the prices exorbitant....granted, NYC is expensive, but a grilled cheese with fries, a bowl of pasta, and 2 bottles of water for $75.00!

title: “Great location, great rates !”
text: This is a very nice, clean, friendly hotel situated very conviently. We have a good room, big enough for 4 people. We had a drink at the bar and it also was a nice experience : good wine, reasonably priced, served with a smile. Here you get value for money.

title: “What a dump!!!!”
text: Wow! This place is terrible. Do not stay here. Carpets, mattress and sheets are all stained. A horrible stench of cigarettes greeted me as I opened the door. I'm using a towel to work the remote on my barely working television. There are bug exoskeletons in every corner of the room as well as stains in the bathtub, shower curtain and sink. This place scares me, but I am stuck. There are no other rooms in San Antonio and I have no transportation. I will not be sleeping tonight. I will be alert for bugs trying to eat me.

title: “New to the area”
text: I recently won a contest that booked me 2 nights at this hotel. Before you start thinking, "Gee, you stayed for free...complain much?", I want to say that this hotel and staff were genuinely courteous and the rooms were spacious, clean and comfortable. My gripe is with shuttles that were supposed to run every 20 minutes from the airport a mile away still had not made an appearance after an hour, which made us get a cab. New to the area, I did not realize we possibly could have walked through the highly congestive traffic. The desk clerk did offer me some complimentary drinks for my trouble and although I declined, I do appreciate the gesture. Upon my return to San Diego, as 2 days are not enough to visit, I would hope to find lodging here and explore more of this hotel as it seemed those staying were enjoying it very much.

title: “Great Giirls Weekend!!”
text: Just back from a great ladies getaway for a long weekend of eating, shopping, theatre-going and laughing! The Kimberly was an important factor in our enjoyable escape. The doormen were all very helpful and charming. The room was very comfortable,quiet and spacious ( by N.Y. standards) and the bed very comfy. The A/C worked very well during our extremely hot weather. Having been many times to N.Y. this hotel ranks highly in my mind. Location is ideal......close to Bloomingdales- 5 min. walk...and not far from Rockefellar Center and Fifth Ave. Fine breakfast places nearby.

title: “Great location for gay visitors”
text: I've stayed at Beck's for over 15 years whenever I am in SF. This is a gay-friendly motel in the heart of the Castro. It's clean, well-located and there are plenty of good places to eat and shop within walking distance. Public transit is near so you can just park in their lot and never have to drive while in SF (or get a parking ticket).

title: “Pleasantly surprised with my stay; recommend this hotel for conferences”
text:
Stayed here for a few nights with 2 other colleagues for a conference. During the days that we stayed it was were very hot and humid in San Antonio which influences how I rated this hotel.
The mixed reviews for this hotel had me come in with lowered expectations. For the most part though I had a good experience at this hotel. 
The biggest plus for the hotel was its location, conveniently located next to the Alamo and the riverwalk, the biggest attractions in San Antonio. It is also close to the convention center, and I would recommend this hotel if you don't want to pay too much for one of the (closer) name brand hotels. During our stay it was very hot and humid, something I'm not used to. Walking to and from the hotel and conference center was an issue for me as I developed a heat rash and had to dress professionally, but luckily we discovered you can cut through the Rivercenter Mall, which is across the street, to get to the convention center. This minimized the time spent outside by a couple of minutes.
The room itself was clean: the carpet, bathroom, and bed/sheets. The rooms had been recently remodeled with simple but pleasing decor. The room was a decent size for 3 people. The AC worked well. You also get free internet access in the rooms. And there is a computer in the lobby area (you have to pay for internet access) that you can use for airline check-in for free (has a printer).
The hotel provides a free continental breakfast: Texas shaped waffles, eggs (totally gross), toast, bagels, fruit, yogurt, cereal, milk, juice, coffee. I think everything was a lowfat alternative (which was why the eggs were disgusting) but I got tired of it very quickly. During the day they provided free ice tea, water, and coffee, and the ice (not ice tea) was greatly appreciated.
The hotel also has a pool and access to a gym (from what I heard) although I did not partake in either one.
The negatives of the hotel: others have mentioned this as well, but you have to use your key card to use the elevator. That may not seem like a big deal but it's kind of annoying when you have to whip it out everytime just to use the elevator. And if you're on different floors, everyone in the elevator has to use their key and punch the number of his floor. Along with that, both my colleagues and I had to have our key card reprogrammed several times during our stay. That was more annoying than the elevator thing, because twice I went to my hotel room after using it in the elevator and had to go back down to have the card reset.
The room I was in had a connecting door and you can hear your neighbors through that door. The only other negative thing was the water pressure in the bathroom. My colleague likened it to standing under a leaking faucet. The brightside to that was that you couldn't hear the shower if you were in the room.
Overall, I did enjoy my stay as the room was clean and cool (the heat felt very oppressive). The location was great for both conference going and tourism. The price was better than some of the other hotels. Staff were ok, I have nothing good or bad to say about them. I would stay here again.

title: “No Respect for thier Customers”
text:
once upon a time at the 11th ave hotel, there was an older patron who urinated on a mattress so bad that even the box spring was ruined...
what did the MANAGER do to prepare for the next client???
NOTHING. that might be the mattress you get when you visit this property. 
Dont beleive the Rosy reviews. these people dont care about anything except what is going on in thier quite Narrow Minds.
i stayed there for 2 months, BTW.... the room service people stole stuff out of my room and they would Re Arrange your stuff in order to see what you have for them to steal!!!
when i told the "management", they did nothing!

title: “Clean, quiet, safe”
text:
This cozy hotel - the Conwell Inn - is situated right in the middle of Temple campus in Philadelphia. Temple has its own police patrolling the area, so I felt very safe. The check-in process was a breeze, even after midnight. The bedsheets were clean, everything worked, and I can't complain about the sleeping experience. The mattresses are foam. It's also conveniently located next to bars and convenience shops.
The only minor complaints I have are that the hotel is a little difficult to find, and the parking lot is tricky to reach. In addition, if you're staying on a weekend during the school semester, you might have to deal with some nearby student noise.

title: “AWFUL PEOPLE AVOID AT ALL COSTS”
text: Made a reservation through Hotwire for three people. When we arrived they announced we would have to pat extra for two beds. I explained that is why we booked for three. I even had Hotwire call them and they refused to house us, even after we had paid for the room. I got a refund and moved to a much nicer hotel down the road. They are awful people just looking to rip off every poor sap they run into.

title: “Beauty is only skin deep”
text:
The charm of this property ends with the decor, which is lovely but not enough to outweigh the minuses. 
The bathroom is so small I couldn't sit down on the toilet. I had to step over the toilet to get out of the shower. The door to the room sticks open so I slept my first night with my door open, then had to bodyslam it to get it to shut thereafter. There's an iron but only a table top ironing board and not enough outlets. You can't keep your laptop and your iron plugged in at the same time. Got a Blackberry to charge too? Fuhgedaboudit. Ladies, don't bring dresses or a coat because once you put your suitcase in the "closet" (the only place it fits) there's no room for long hang anything.
The desk chair in the room is made of aluminum so dress warm to work there. If you get tired of working in your room (or perhaps claustrophobic), don't go to the lobby, restaurant or bar. The ever-present techno soundtrack is so loud you can't hear the person you're talking to on the phone even with the earpiece in. Besides, the restaurant food is mediocre anyway. 
This place is like that hostess in the ultra-chic restaurant that looks at you as if she's trying to decide whether you're cool enough to eat there, then serves you average food at elevated prices. Stay someplace where they know that hospitality means being hospitable.

title: “It's a NO!”
text:
My husband checked into this hotel a day earlier than me, the text he sent me was "OMG, this place is disgusting". This hotel was on the list of his company's NYC hotels but after this stay he has told the travel department to remove it IMMEDIATELY.
While he was checking in the receptionist rang housekeeping and asked if room 902 was ready, it obviously wasn't because she checked my husband into room 210. The kitchen fan vents INTO room 210! The room reeked of cooked foods from 9 am until 2am!!! The carpet was grungy, bathroom was dismal and the water pressure was pathetic. The hair dryer worked for 4 minutes before it over-heated and it was another 20 minutes before I could use it again! We left after my first and my husband's second night.
The hotel is situated in a very, very convenient location - that is pretty much the only good thing I can say about it.
Right next door to the hotel is a club, so on Friday and Saturday nights you are fighting your way through drunks loitering the sidewalk to the front door of the hotel. 
There is no security to speak of, as I was waiting to check out, a woman asked the receptionist if a MR X was in the hotel. The receptionist not only answered in the affirmative after looking up his name on the computer but supplied the woman the room number AND told her to go right up! 
Staff was unhelpful and indifferent. This was definitely a case of "you get what you pay for". We left and opted to pay 4X more at the Trump Tower at Columbus Circle.

title: “Ideal for a girls holiday”
text:
Spent 5 nights here for a girls holiday. Location is second to none, right beside rockefeller, subway and a short walk from central park. The room wasn't massive especially as there were three of us in it but wouldn't expect a large room in NYC. There was a double bed and a sofa bed, noise wasn't an issue for us (we were on the 6th floor), the water fountain is located in the gym and on the 7th floor where the terrace is.
There are safety deposit boxes at the reception if required. The rooftop terrace looks nice, we were unable to eat there as there is a dress code, no flip flops allowed!
With three of us staying in the room, we often hadn't been left enough towels and had to frequently ask for more, that was our only complaint really. Staff were plesant and accomodating and check in/out was speedy.

title: “A very good hotel with competitive room rates.”
text: A great little hotel with very competitive room rates. Some might find the rooms a little on the small side but, from my experience, most rooms in New York tend to be on the small side. Myself and my husband visited with two other couples who were also very impressed with the hotel. The location might not be central enough for everyone but there is an subway station about 300 yards from the hotel which takes you to Times Square in about 10 minutes.

title: “Fab hotel - Rooms are Small”
text:
PROS:
hotel is brand new, nothing is worn looking, all very fab!
Beds comfortable
Great Views (from high floors)
free mini cupcakes upon check in
Great location, super close to Penn Station
The room service staff was so nice! 
CONS:
Shower poorly laid out... no way to turn on the water without getting soaked! 
Rooms are small
TINY GYM - one elliptical, one bike, two treadmills, some free weights - with three people in the gym, there was no space to do a sit up
I will certainly be back! Compared to the Double Tree, Four Points, and Affinia in the neighborhood - this hotel really is a good one for it's price point.

title: “Rundown and not clean”
text:
We were drawn by the price and availability. This Ramada is old and dirty. The rooms were not clean. We were put on the 3rd floor but soon realized the Elevator Motor Assembly was behind the wall right behind the headboard! It made a squealing awful noise with each passenger ALL NIGHT LONG. It was impossible to sleep. They did move us to another room the following day when we asked to change. They didn't seem happy. This other room was even dirtier and older.The sheets were thread bare and the carpets dirty. I saw on my credit card account they charged us a higher rate other than what I signed on my bill.
The saving grace was the free shuttle to Logan and the T. Free breakfast is offered, breads,yogurt, and hot waffles.If you are not going to be in your room at all you may like this place for the price. NOT walking distance to anything ,but cheap.

title: “Stay in the Beach House (Room #29)”
text:
The nice stuff:
I stayed here for only one nite (passing thru town) and was very pleased with our sleep over. The room was large, had a separate couch, as well as a fridge and a microwave oven. The bathroom is *huge* with a separate shower and also a very nice 5' Jacuzzi tub that is surrounded on one side by mirrors. The room was set in a beach type motif with fish hanging from the ceiling in the bathroom.
The king size bed was very comfortable. The room was very clean. I had read earlier reports of water that wasn't barely warm and poor water pressure. I assure this was *not* the case in the Beach House. There was plenty of water pressure and hot water to go around.
The nit picking:
It rained while I was there during the nite and the a/c - heating unit is wall mounted and the water dripped dripped dripped onto the unit and made a lot of racket (I enjoy sleeping to the falling rain, but this was way too much). I would suggest they put some kind of awning above the unit, so the water would run off of it, instead of sounding like a snare drum inside the room.
Parking is on the street, but that was a very minor problem for us, as we always managed to get a parking spot nearby.
In closing, I would stay here, again.

title: “another great experience”
text: The rooms have great views, excellent beds, extremely clean. Room service has fantastic food. Personnel are friendly and helpful.

title: “This is the first Westin Hotel in the States - and it shows”
text:
Ok - this hotel is a Westin and my expectations were high
I know this is an old 70's (or earlier) building, and the lobby was renovated in the last 5 years probably
But when I walked into my bedroom I was disappointed with old carpet, stains on the couch. If I had not just driven through a snow storm I would have left the hotel and driven to the Westin in Bellevue.
The Bellman told me there is a $30 million dollar reno coming - and in my opinion it should have started 5 years ago.
The 5ft Ave Grill was the only food option in the morning for breakfast - but it was cafeteria style and there was only one guy taking orders and working the till and there were about 15 people in line...
I was very dissatisfied with that...but the food came quick and was good...
Last thing - the view is great - but the surrounding neighbourhood is really sketchy - never walk around alone at night in DT Seattle
I would NEVER return to this hotel until after the reno or they drop rates by 50%
Oh and the internet was terrible

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: We've just back after staying at Hotel Metro for 8 days. It's a nice hotel with a great location. Staff are friendly and helpful. Our room was nice and clean. Breakfast was fine. The restaurant was nice (we ate there only one evning, were too many other places to see). The bar on the rooftop in the 13th floor was great with an magnificant view of the Empire State Building which was a couple of blocks away. The gym was ok and good enough to be a "hotel gym". But back to the location. It was really great. Macy's two minutes walk away so my girlfriend was very happy for that. The Empire State building was as mentioned previously only a few blocks and some minutes walk away. The Madison Square Garden is only some minutes walk away. The 5th Avenue is only some minutes walk away. Times Square Garden is 10-15 minutes walk away. It was our first visit in N.Y. after 11 days in California and we were a bit sceptical after reading some reviews about the ruud staff, but we very satisfied there! Next time in N.Y. we'll definately stay in the same hotel. And we will recommend it to all our friends too.

title: “Old and dirty”
text: Booked an overnight in December for a Christmas present. 3 adults in a cramped room. Not very clean (and did not look as well presented as in the pictures). Needed a blanket for use on the pull out sofa (do not pull out - terrible!) - received a thin, flat, foam blanket sheet with holes in it. Kept requesting service personnel - room was hot, window in bedroom was open and we could not close, etc., etc., etc. Very disappointing - would not return here.

title: “A Nightmare”
text: This place was the worst i have been in there was no mini fridge to keep your drinks cool,no microwave to heat up the food no coffee pot no phone book nor bible ,the bed mattress were worn out people on the outside slamming doors too noisy could not rest all in all not a good place to stay

title: “It takes a lot to get 5 stars out of me”
text: But the Hotel Palomar earned it! This ultra pet friendly hotel is heavy on style and service. The staff goes out of it's way to make sure you and your pet have everything you could possibly need and the price a very reasonable. They have a lovely coffee, tea and chai bar in the morning, Hot chocolate bar in the afternoon and wine and snacks in the evening, all complimentary. I joined the kimpton rewards program online and made my reservations online where I could put in my preferences, so when I got to my room, there was a dog bed, water, dog treats, yoga kit, gold fish (to keep my dog company), my choice of newspaper etc. The little extra touchs go on and on. The gym was lovely as was the pool. I didn't eat in the restruant, but it looked nice.

title: “Great Restaurant Experience”
text: The lower restaurant at the Sheraton Brookhollow has great food and sizable portions. They have great service that I can attest to: My server Dee was nice enough to return my keys to the front desk after I left them laying on my table. Thanks so much, Dee!

title: “Perfect for Philadelphia Marathon”
text:
Partner and I were in town to run the marathon. The location was great; the price was fair for marathon weekend in the downtown part of a major city. The room itself had a generous amount of space -- we appreciated the kitchen and other amenities.
Every part of our experience was handled smoothly. I would stay here again for business or leisure.

title: “Convenient to airport; clean rooms and comfy beds”
text:
We stayed at the Best Western Airport in Seattle for one night to facilitate an early-morning flight. The hotel was easy to find off I5, and is located less than 10 minutes from the airport. The hotel has a free shuttle service to the airport (which we didn't need to use because we had a car). Checkin was fast and efficient; the front desk clerk was pleasant. The lobby is unremarkable, as are the hallways. Our room was located on the first floor, which made it easy to get luggage in and out of the room. The room itself was a pleasant surprise: it was clean and spacious, and had been recently renovated. The bathroom was also clean and amply-sized, with a granite countertop. The bath in our room had a shower only (no tub). The beds were very comfortable, with nice pillows. There was also a mini fridge in the room.
The only negative I have to report is that the back door from the parking lot was unlocked at the time of our arrival (midnight) and didn't require a room key for entry. It made me a little uncomfortable about the lack of security, but thankfully we didn't encounter any problems during our stay.
We received an extremely competitive room rate, so my expectations were pretty low. The experience delivered by the Best Western certainly exceeded my expecations and I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Less than OK”
text:
This hotel is very uneven. It is updated, but the renovation was fairly low quality and is starting to show wear.
As an example, I had two different lamp shades on my desk and bed table. Both were falling off. Does that ruin the room? No, but it does make you wonder how well taken care the room is taken care of as far as the cleanliness of the mattress, air filters, etc..
The hotel is very spread out and it can be difficult to find parking.
The staff was nice, and the room clean, but not in the class of a Marriott, Doubletree, etc.
If you want more than express hotel, but on the cheap, consider it, but look closely. There may be a better deal.

title: “Great location, friendly staff and very clean.”
text: The location is excellent. The most impressive was how great and friendly the staff was. Recommend it 100%

title: “Cant wait to return - fab location”
text:
The desk staff were very helpful answering any questions we had. The rooms were clean and compact. We had 2 double beds and not much space between them but as we were in NY we hardly spent any time in the room. Enough space to sleep. The bath room was very clean and an unexpected bonus was the mouth wash and moisturiser, the shower had shampoo and shower gel dispensers on the wall.
Vending machines in the basement along with a water/ice dispenser.
No breakfast available at the hotel but there is a diner on 9th and 34th - 5 min walk max.
You can get trad american breakfast - from 5 - 9 $ before 10am slightly more after 10am. We also had dinner there a few times as it is 24hrs.
I would like to see a mirror in the bedroom as this would allow others to get ready as the only mirror is in the bathroom.
Hotel is great value for money and really is close enough for all attractions, i have stayed further down in manhatten and the accomodation was bigger (and dearer) but this hotels location is much better and central.
free internet access for those who needed it
Cant wait to return

title: “Perfect location, great service, VERY CLEAN!!!”
text: My Mom and I booked a last minute trip to NYC last week. While other hotels were $400+, we found the Hotel Grand Union in our price range ($175/night) and very convenient. The hotel front desk workers were humerous, the hotel very clean, and the bathrooms roomy. The only downside was that the only room available was one full-size bed. Also, all rooms are smoking, however you would never have known anyone smoked in our room. All said, we would definetly stay there again!

title: “Trendy, slick well located”
text:
I stayed for business in two separate weeks in February and March. Had a great experience. Helpful staff, free wine happy hour (a little early 5 to 6, but free) , a nice bar restaurant in a nice neig.
Room. Very modern decor. First class toiletries and goodies. confortable mattress, clean sheets and towels.
Gym. Small but it seems to serve the hotel well. Never had to wait for a machine.
Restaurant. The brick oven pizza was excellent and fast.
Trendy bar a plus.
My only complain is that the wireless internet connection was dreadfully slow, in both rooms I stayed in.
I def. recommend it.

title: “Best NYC hotel experience ever!”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for 3 nights last week with our 2 1/2 year-old-daughter. We needed a hotel that was "child friendly" and this hotel certainly met our expectations from the moment we arrived to the moment we left. Everyone on the hotel staff was friendly and always greeted us with a smile and a cheerful "hello". Each time we entered or exited the hotel, the doorman was quick to open the doors for us, which was nice as we often had a stroller and several bags in tow. 
I booked the Bryant Park hotel via telephone a few weeks prior to our stay and spoke to Darren, who asked if we had any special requests. I said we would need a small refrigerator in our room to store our daughter's food. Sure enough, upon arrival to our room, a refrigerator was already set-up in our room--I didn't have to ask twice. (Thanks, Darren! You Rock!) As a matter of fact, we never had to ask twice for anything... whether we requested a bucket of ice or more bath towels--one quick phone call and our items were at our door within a few short minutes.
Our room (Junior Suite with King Bed) was absolutely huge, with an amazing view overlooking Bryant Park. The bathroom was equally large and so clean. It was all marble, with a deep soaking tub and separate rain shower. Our daughter loved taking baths every night, and we loved the rain shower. Now my wife wants to have one of those shower heads in our bathroom at home... I do, too!
Our daughter LOVED to ride the carousel at the park, and we all enjoyed the ice cream stand next to it. For breakfast, the Pax Deli on the corner was a good choice, and for lunch the sandwiches at the little sandwich shop next door were excellent. 
The location of the Bryant Park Hotel can't be beat. It's close enough to Times Square that you can walk there in five minutes, but it's far enough away so that you don't get caught up in the "touristy" hustle and bustle of the area. All the major subway lines are within a block or two, and we had no problem catching a cab at any time. 
Nicole at the reception desk was so cheerful, and she always took time to greet us as we came and went. And Eric, the Entertainment Planner/Concierge was always helpful with our unusual requests, such as "where can we find a place to get a good hot dog for our daughter?" and also with his recommendations on places to eat and things to do and see.
All told, we've stayed at dozens of hotels in different parts of New York City, and this was by far the one with not only the largest and cleanest rooms, but also the one with the friendliest, most accommodating and welcoming staff. We will definitely be booking The Bryant Park Hotel again... and again...

title: “comfortable & convenient”
text:
Stayed at this hotel before an early morning flight - complimentary airport shuttle provided -
also shuttle to subway making it easy to get into town. Very comfortable room & very reasonably priced. Would recommend for this purpose.

title: “Great hotel, will stay there again.”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Metro, NYC for 6 nights in July 2011. We arrived quite late, and received really friendly greetings from the two check-in staff.
Our room on the 9th floor was nice, a bit small, but we weren't in it much. The bed was most comfortable bed ever though, and we both slept really well every night. The bathroom was also small (but perfectly formed!). The shower was roomy and powerful! Free wifi and 24hr tea and coffee (available from the breakfast room) were also real bonuses.
Breakfast was a lot better than we were expecting...a great selection of delicious muffins and bagels delivered fresh every day. Breakfast room got a bit busy, but we could usually find somewhere to sit.
We didn't have drinks up on the roof terrace as there was a heatwave that week, and it was really hot up there, but the views were great from there.
The location of the hotel was also really good....just between 5th ad 6th avenues, with a metro station really close by. There's also a couple of good "Irish" bars next door (or just up the road), which we frequented.
We'd definitely stay there again!

title: “DON'T STAY HERE!”
text: I reserved a Deluxe King, described on the Hudson website as having a River or Courtyard View. I requested a quiet room on a high floor. My reservation was booked a month in advance and guaranteed with a credit card. I telephoned the hotel to alert them to my late arrival time and requested they hold the quiet room on the upper floor. I was assured they would. I arrived at 9:00pm. The staff was young, dressed in black and hipper than thou. I was shown a room on the 23rd floor. It had NO WINDOWS, just blinds covering a wall. It was a tomb. While I sat in the hallway of their overcrowded bar and had a $19.00 hamburger, they found me a room on the 7th floor with two drafty windows overlooking 9th Ave. The heater unit was located at the head of the bed, so you had to listen to the motor all night. Also, there was approximately a two-inch space between the end of the toilet seat and the wall. I'd have to be lowered down by a winch. The shower was so small that the shower curtains stuck to my body as I washed. The deadbolt on my door was broken. No sleep. Next morning, I vacated the room and was assured they would save a different room upon the check-out of other guests. I returned late, after working all day. No room. No notes on my record for the request. The manager claimed I had originally been given a room on the 17th floor with a view. Not true. When I told him I had been given room 2315 which had no windows, he said it wasn't true or even possible. He said there were no rooms without windows. He further insisted they fulfilled my requests by offering the room on the 17th floor. Not true. He said I was unhappy because I wanted "more windows." I said not "more windows" but a window. The River or Courtyard view? No view. He was rude, saying he would offer me a room with two doubles or a queen standard. I checked out and went to the Parker Meridien, which was great.

title: “Amazing place - made our Boston trip memorable!”
text:
It's hard to add anything to all the great reviews of the Lenox, but I had to add my praise to this special place. It's difficult to describe, but the Lenox has a different feel than any other hotel. We felt at home here for many reasons but most of all it comes down to the staff. They are all so welcoming - it is very apparent that The Lenox truly loves their guests and makes them feel that way. Every person, without exception, was friendly and very helpful. It was our first trip to Boston, celebrating our 35th anniversary, and we received an upgrade to a corner suite - it was stunning. Beautiful furnishings and a wonderful comfortable bed with high quality linens. We enlisted the help of the concierge several times and received accurate and helpful advise. The location is excellent, very convenient. We were also very happy with our choice of staying in the Back Bay area. We took at 2 day trip to Cape Ann (highly recommended) and when we returned, we stayed at a hotel on the waterfront for our last night since it was very close to the airport. Although beautiful, it lacked the charm and grace of The Lenox and the hustle and bustle of the area was totally different than the Back Bay.
Praise to City Table, too, for an excellent quick breakfast every morning. We usually avoid hotel restaurants since they are often overpriced and pretentious but not City Table. It was very convenient, delicious, and highly recommended.
We are so thrilled that we chose the Lenox for our vacation and hope to return to the beautiful Boston area soon. When we do, The Lenox will be our hotel.

title: “Good Value.”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this LaQuinta at the recommendation of our friend. It was only a short walk from Coors (baseball) Field. On/off the expressway was very easy. Tho we had reserved a king room, which had also bee3n confirmed by our booking site, we were given two doubles, with the explanation that booking thru Expedia does not reserve the requested room (???). Our room was on the third floor, in the corner. This made it difficult to access the internet. It was clean and functional, with a hair dryer and coffeemaker. The pool was outdoors. There is a Mexican restaurant next door. The biggest disappointment was the breakfast. An assortment of breads was offered, and some yogurt as well. Fruit was limited, and the only protein selection was a bowl of overcooked hard boiled eggs. Also, it should be noted that this is a pet friendly hotel. No worries, except for the fact that one gentleman allowed his little dog to roam the breakfast area off leash, adding to an already unappetizing breakfast.
Overall, however, this is a nice, clean, affordable, and friendly hotel, and would definitely recommend it to anyone visiting Denver.

title: “Fantastic upscale hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Manchester Grand Hyatt for four days as part of a business conference. The hotel is definitely opulent and in front of Seaport Village. A friend stayed with me - our hotel room was nothing terribly exciting - clean, airy with in-room safe and fridge. No microwave and no air fan in the bathroom. Our hotel room overlooked the spacious pool - which we didn't get a chance to try out. 
As a hotel guest, I did try out the 24 hour fitness centre. It is one of the better fitness centres that I've seen with full circuit weight machines, rows of ellipticals, bikes and treadmills, and a small mirrored wall area with cables, yoga mats, Bosu, and medicine balls. Fresh eucalpytus scented towels and water are included in the fitness centre, so you need to only bring down yourself. I'm not a big fan of working out while on business or vacation, but this fitness centre made it really hard to resist. 
I didn't get to experience any of the restaurants on-site, with the exception of two. The lobby area serves as a lounge and you can order drinks and a full meal. The service is not very good between 9 pm - 11 pm. I wouldn't wait there for a meal, but perhaps to take in a drink or two (tip: sit at the bar so you get faster service). The other thing to denote for caffeine lovers - there is no Starbucks on site. The nearest one is across the street located at another hotel. There is a small coffee shop on-site that serves Starbucks coffee, but it's quite expensive, the food selection is not great and the line-ups are very long. They get a lot of business, undoubtedly from conference delegates who are caffeine-deprived, but the food and drink is really not very good for such a grand hotel.
The hotel is within walking distance to downtown San Diego and it felt quite safe walking there during the day and night. If you don't want to go that far, you can always explore the restaurants and trinkets in Seaport Village, although it becomes quite deserted at night (not recommeded if you travel solo at night). Great coffee and eats await you in Seaport and there is a very lovely bookstore/cafe there that is absolutely charming and doesn't smell at all like Indigo or Barnes & Nobles. Seaport Village has a great seawall that you walk around for about 30 minutes in length - both ways. A great walk, especially if you have a dog.
If you're looking to get out of the area and venture into outlet shopping, you can take the trolley bus to the Las Americas Outlet, just outside the Mexican border. I went to this outlet about five years ago and scored big, but this time came back empty-handed. It's a pretty far trip by trolley and I recommend going during daylight hours. You may spend up to 6 hours there if you're a hard core shopper, less if you're only going to specific stores.
The trolley bus system in general is a bit confusing. Pay attention to the directions and to the bus signs. It is, however, the cheapest way to get around town so a little bit of inconvenience allows you to save your $$ for eats and shopping. 
San Diego is a really beautiful city any time of the year. The only other lasting impression I have is that it's a very dog-friendly city. We saw dogs everywhere from hotels to malls and all along Seaport Village (be sure to visit the doggie store in the Village for pampered pooch treats). I don't know if the Hyatt is a dog-friendly hotel, but we did see a few in the lobby so it's worth mentioning.
This hotel is probably the biggest Hyatt that I've ever stayed in. Were it not for the fact that my employer paid for this conference, I probably wouldn't be able to afford to stay at this place for vacation. Even with the minor hiccups (e.g. bad coffee on-site, boring but clean room), it is undoubtedly a 5-star hotel. 
The concierge desk also deserves mention as they were unfailing helpful with three requests: 1. getting my fridge up and running; 2. getting immediate drycleaning for my ketchup spill all over my white jacket; and 3. mapping out our transportation routes to get to where we needed to go.
My conclusion: if you are staying here for your conference - lucky you! Make time to enjoy the scenery outside the hotel and its on-site facilities. If you are debating on whether to book this hotel for your next San Diego vacation, try finding a price break on Hotwire or Priceline. You won't regret it once you pull up to the hotel.

title: “Best boutique in NYC”
text: Loved the location. Lower east side blew us away. Very up & coming social scene. The hotel is right next to the subway for a quick ride uptown. The rooms were extremely large for New York standards and also very clean. The atmosphere, despite reviews to the contrary, was extremely quiet and tranquil. The bagels in the morning were delicious. The staff's service was truly impeccable. Larry, Andy, Antonella, and Randy were all excellent hosts! More than anything, they want you to have the best time possible. They are full of great recommendations and always go above and beyond your expectations. The only possible suggestion concerns the beds, which were a bit hard. Would highly recommend! Made a perfect romantic getaway.

title: “Wow...”
text: When I was booking my 10 day 30th birthday treat in New York, I wanted something special and not too expensive. This hotel caught my eye and I was immediately seduced by the traveller photos on tripadvisor. However, although it was very cheap for what it seemed to be offering, it was a little more expensive than other hotels in the exact same area, and the money would only be justified if it really was as special as it looked (tripadvisor reviews vouched for the great amount of space, but as I was travelleing alone, charm and fantasy were much more important to me). I decided that it was too much of an expensive gamble and I went for the safe and cheaper bet of a well known chain hotel in the same area, which had raving reviews. Upon arriving in New York, even though I was satisfied with my hotel, I was curious to see 'The Kimberly' for myself (also since I'd fallen in love with New York, I wanted to check it out for future trips!) The staff were without exception immediately very welcoming, and I was shown around several different types of rooms! The lady that showed me around was obviously very proud of the hotel she worked in (that's always a good sign!). I just had to post this review on tripadvisor for all those who think this hotel is 'too good to be true' when they see the pics on the hotel website, and like me, opt for safer options and never discover the beauty of this rare place. The rooms are even more beautiful, spacious, and luxurious than they look on the website. From the gorgeous fluffy bedding to the luxrious carpet that your feet sink into as you enter the room. And so calm and sunny. I thought that being an appartment hotel it would be full of noisy kids, but actually it has more of a 'couples' feel to it than 'family' feel. It would certainly spoil the feel of the place if there were noisy kids running around, but it doesn't seem to have been designed with kids in mind. A word of advice - they have a mixture of dated and more renovated rooms. Personally, I prefer the dated ones (they're very well kept, and I prefer the charm and character of these), but I know some people would hate this decor, so don't forget to request a more modern renovated room if that's the case (I had a look at one of these too, and they are the same as the pics on the hotel website). As I say, I didn't stay here. But I fell in love with this hotel as soon as I saw it, and I thought that maybe there is someone out there reading these reviews, looking for something really unique and special for their trip to New York, and thinking like me, that it all looks too good to be true... I went for the safer option, and I was very lucky with my choice of hotel too, so I don't regret it, but I just thought this place deserved a special mention, since it really is a very special place in a wonderful location. And hopefully, someday soon, I'll be back here, and will be able to write another review...

title: “Treated like royalty at the Sofitel”
text: What a delight to stay at the Sofitel. I was taking my son to NYC for his 11th birthday and we could not have made a better choice for hotel. They upgraded us to a lovely view room and thoughtfully surprised us with a beautiful, personalized birthday cake and card for my son. How charming! The bathroom was sumptuous (loved the scent of the body lotion!) and the bed extremely comfortable. The concierge was very helpful as well. The location is walking distance, literally, to absolutely everything we wanted to see. Small but well equipped fitness center was never crowded. Room service arrived lickety-split and was virtually gourmet. On our last morning, I treated my son to the (very expensive) breakfast at Gaby's - WOW that was delicious. Highly recommend the Sofitel.

title: “Loved this Inn and Fell's Point!”
text: I must admit, I was worried after reading the reviews on here. But, I have come to realize that some people are just entirely too picky and that everyone's experience will differ. I am so glad I heeded the good reviews and ignored the bad because Admiral Fell Inn is spectacular. This hotel is not a luxury hotel, and it is not meant to me. It's a charming, boutique hotel with everythin you would need. Our room was very cozy with beautiful four-poster beds, and a great view of the cobblestone street. We did not have any trouble with noise, and the staff could not have been more accomodating and friendly. They even offered us an upgraded room! Our room was impeccably clean, and the bed was one of the more comfortable we've had in a hotel And we're picky! The location cannot be beat-right across from the Water Taxi, close to all the great shops and pubs. We loved Fell's Point! The breakfast, which was included with our room rate, was fantastic. A huge spread and a variety of items to please all palates. We were so happy we stayed here and will definitely stay here anytime we come back to the area! Ignore the naysayers on this review and stay at the Admiral Fell Inn!

title: “Philly Attractions Within Reach from CQ”
text:
I just returned from a relaxed, inexpensive overnight stay at the Club Quarters hotel in Philadelphia. I had read an assortment of reviews about this particular property in CQ 's international group of hotels, and those reviews caused some anxiety prior to arriving in Philly. However, I believe that a traveler should judge a hotel, or any other location for that matter, for himself or herself. Thus, I am pleased to report on my findings but ask you to try out this CQ hotel next time you are in Philadelphia but on a budget.
After departing 30th Street Station in Philly, 10 minutes later I stepped out of the taxi (a $5.60 fare -- not bad) in front of an inconspicuous building next to a Rite Aid. I knew that the building housing this Club Quarters hotel, at 1628 Chestnut Street, used to be a bank, and so I was not put off by the lack of fanfare one usually sees outside of a 3 1/2 star hotel. There was a security guard there who opened the door for me, but I later saw that there is not always a security guard downstairs. But I found the overall security to be fair, especially since the lobby is not located on the ground floor (it is on the second floor).
Checking in was a breeze because I checked my NYC attitude at the door. A pleasant smile on my face, I greeted the front-desk personnel and presented two items: the credit card that I used to book the room and a printout of the e-mailed confirmation number for my prepaid reservation. I was provided with verbal instructions on how to do an express checkout (an excellent system!), as well as given a brochure on touring options in Philadelphia. In the spacious lobby, there also were plenty of brochures from which to choose, including mini restaurant cards for famous eateries such as Geno's, Pat's Steaks, Jim's Steaks, Moshulu and Susanna Foo. Before checking out my room, I asked whether the on-site restaurant (Davio's) served breakfast and was told it did not, but I was provided with the names of eateries nearby (within one to two blocks) that served breakfast.
Keeping in mind that I was staying in Center City, which is Philly's business district, and that I arrived on the Saturday before Easter, I prepared for lots of closed venues. Not so! And to my (and other guests') delight! City Hall, one of the most beautiful and ancient buildings in Philadelphia, was just three long city blocks away (a five-minute walk).
As for the room itself, it was an efficiency upgrade, so I had a microwave oven in the room, a coffee pot in the bathroom (odd, but nice!), high ceilings, a TV with cable and reference materials on a shelf above the desk. Both the room and the corridors were spotless. My stay was quiet as well.
About the lobby: It is large and it is also cozy because of the many sofas and chairs. There are two computers with free, 24-hour Internet access, with a 30-minute limit per guest. I must admit that the last feature really enticed me to book a room at Club Quarters, aside from the $89/night price and the location, location, location.
By the way, directly across from CQ is Liberty Place, a mall in a high-rise building -- a building that forms a significant part of the Philadelphia cityscape.
Special tip #1: Take a trolly tour (------). I paid $23.00 (worth every penny) in cash when the complimentary shuttle picked me up in front of Club Quarters. (You can order your ticket or tickets on-line in advance of your trip.) The brightly colored trolley takes you around all of the famous sights in Philly, and you can hop on and off wherever there is a trolley stop. So, for example, if you want to shop at Reading Terminal Market, just get off the trolley when it stops to pick up additional passengers (carrying their tickets). The one thing to remember about the tour is that you must reserve your seat or seats by calling the aforementioned phone number 20 minutes to a half-hour before the start of the next tour. The trolley tours start daily at 9:30 a.m. and continue every half-hour. That means that after you hop off a trolley at a particular attraction, even if you spend hours at that place, you know there will be another trolley coming. You must keep in mind, however, that the last tour is at 4 p.m. They have night tours, but you should call the number I provided to find out about reservations and cost. I must mention that you also should ask Bev at ----- whether your hotel is served by the free shuttle that picks you up at your hotel and returns you there after the trolley tour. If you are staying at any hotel in Center City, you can be sure that the complimentary shuttle will be able to serve you.
Special tip #2: If you want to see special exhibits or go to the world-famous Philadelphia Zoo, do your best to buy your tickets on-line in advance of your trip. Sometimes there are Zoo packages connected to certain Philly hotels.
Special tip #3: After checking into your hotel, get to the Independence Visitors Center as soon as you can so you can pick up tickets (paid or free) to attractions that require tickets, such as the Liberty Bell. Luckily I saw the Bell when I was 11 or 12 because I had no time to pick up a ticket on this trip.
Special tip #4: If you are taking the train to Philly and arriving at 30th Street Station, you do not have to take a taxi cab to reach Club Quarters. Unless your bags are extremely heavy, save the $5.60 or $6.00 by catching the SEPTA train at 30th Street Station and ride it one stop to Suburban Station. The fare at Suburban Station is free!

title: “excellent location - nice stay”
text: I was here with my family on vaccation. The hotel rooms are very comfortable, the location (right next to union square) is excellent. It is also near the Bart (train) and many buses. No internet in the room for free - but you can go to the lobby to check your email while drinking a Latte (there is a Starbucks inside the hotel). Restaurants, diners and coffee shops all over the place. The hotel also has a good fitness center - treadmills are nice. All in all a great experience.

title: “Ditto!”
text: It's all been said before. Casablanca is a charming hotel with a great attention to detail and ambience. Rick's Cafe provides a comfortable haven and a variety of food and beverages.The staff are attentive and professional. A pleasant atmosphere abounds and guests are made to feel welcome at any time of the day. This consistency sets it apart from other hotels and is a credit to the all the staff. It really is a group effort. Thank you for making our stay such a positive experience.

title: “Tiny rooms - Breakfast on a first in first served basis !”
text:
We had to stay in this hotel during August 2011.
Not our choice.
Reservations at District Hotel (a sister hotel) dated October 2010 but upon arrival our rooms were not available.
We were transfered to Windsor Inn
There, we discovered that we could only have 2 small rooms for 2 persons each, but we were a party of 6 people !!!!! 
Nothing to be done at that point.
We got two inflated matresses that we had to inflate ourselves. One of them even lost air.
Once they were on the floor, we could not walk into the rooms, as they were both so tiny !!!
The room on the garden floor (the basement) was even more tiny, and unbearably noisy.
In the morning, bad surprise again. We came at 8:30 for breakfast (included into the price) and nothing was left. 
The person at the front desk said he could not help, and that breakfast was served upon a first in first served basis (but we still have to pây for it, whether served or not !!!).
Both hotels were a great disappointment for us for our first stay in Washington DC.

title: “A Great Hotel - Wonderful Location - Reasonbly Priced”
text:
Staying at Springhill Suites was a treat. Only a few months old this hotel's location was great - about 3 minute walk to Michigan Avenue and lots of restaurants and bars nearby. It was across from the "House of Blues" and right next door to the Westin River North.
Check-in was a breeze. The staff was friendly and very efficient. Parking was a bit steep at $42/day. If you have time and patience - you might want to drive around and look for a parking lot cheaper than this. 
Their hot breakfast buffet was ample - with a waffle station, sausages, eggs, a variety of breads/pastries, fruits, juices and coffee/tea/hot cocoa.
It was a bit odd that the "Check-in Lobby" was a floor up, and that it shared also the main lobby of the Residence Inn. As you exit the elevator, Springhill was on the left and Residence inn was to the right. 
The rooms were spacious and very clean. There was a flat screen TV that was conveniently positioned to be view from either the bed or the "living room" area. The comfy L shaped couch doubled as a sofa bed too. Beds are comparable to Westin's Heavenly bed. The suite had a coffee maker, microwave and a refrigerator.
We had free WiFi for 24 hours and that was very convenient. We got a discounted rate of $159 per night from Marriott's website. 
We were very happy with the Springhill Suites and would definitely stay there again!

title: “Upscale Intercontinental in upscale LA location”
text: Had an enjoyable stay at Intercontinental in Century City area of LA courtesy of Priceline. The hotel was rated four stars and deserves the rating. Hotel lobby and common areas are very nice and rooms were generous although beds were doubles rather than queens. Bathroom is spacious and had separate bath and shower. Location is a ten minute walk to Westfield Mall which has many shops and places to eat. Only negative is parking. Valet only option, $36 per night with tax and there is no on-street or public parking anywhere near the hotel. Other than that it was a very, very nice hotel with staff attentive and helpful. Nice outdoor pool on second floor. Last morning of our stay they were shooting a TV show in the lobby between 6 and 7 a.m. That was cool.............bunch of people all dressed up for a "pretend" wedding reception. Was a little out of place in my morning "walking" gear but nobody seemed to care.

title: “Did not provide in room Wifi as promised, inconsistent stories to me and to Priceline, general rudeness”
text:
Booked a room with in-room Wifi because I needed in-room Wifi.
Got there and they told me that there was no in-room Wifi because of renovation. I complained and they told me there was no solution.
I complained to Priceline (where I bought the room) and Days Inn told Priceline that they had told me on check in that they were giving me a room without Wifi, that if I had objected they could have given me a room with Wifi but now it was too late.
Were they telling the truth about the Wifi on check in or to Priceline? Who knows... but clearly they were lying one of those times.
I called up Priceline and demanded a partial refund. Days Inn finally agreed to give it, but complained to Priceline that I was being rude and that was the only reason they agreed - so I would leave the lobby where I was calling Priceline from.
Frankly, I think it is rude to sell a service you don't have. My heart bleeds for them.
It will be a cold day in Hell before I stay in another Days Inn.
In addition, the elevators were terrible - waited forever, no indication if they were going up or down.

title: “Newly remodeled, nice check in staff.”
text: We spent one night here. We stayed here to catch an early morning flight out of San Diego. Very close and convenient to car rental returns and hotel. Room have recently be remodeled. Very nice checkin staff. Rooms were very clean and beds were very comfortable.

title: “Even better this time”
text:
Stayed at the Park Central again and was not dissapointed!
The room we got was even better than last time: Spacious, very clean, good bathroom and flat-screen TV.
The location is perfect and after seeing the pictures of hotelrooms in other hotels: very, very good quality for a reasonable price in New York.
Highly recommended!

title: “Fine”
text:
The rooms are well done...they are nice and well appointed without being silly and overly stylized. The bathroom was a very good size and my wife was impressed with the large tub. The room was cleaned every day without issue. We could not be more pleased with the room. 
I was also surprised at how good the location was. I haven't been to Boston in a couple of years, so I didn't realize how walkable that area is now. South Station is just a couple blocks away and Fannuel Hall is just a short hike in the opposite direction. Haymarket, North Station, the North End are all easily accessable on foot. 
The bar was sort of a strange scene...kind of a forced-faux-trendy thing that honestly looked like it belonged in Orlando more than Boston. We ordered food off of the late-night menu and were genuinely impressed. The service, however, was adequate, but not actually good. (Our server clearly had somewhere else to be.)
Reception was definitely just ok...as was the Bellman. We also had a weird exchange with the Doorman who told us he could get a cab to take us to the Airport for $25...I flagged my own cab and it cost $17...weird.
The hotel itself was pretty perfect. We got a great price, and were pretty pleased all around. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great location, great price!”
text: Booked a stay here through an ad on travelzoo for $89 w/tax. Mostly clean rooms, friendly staff, GREAT location! Room was small but I was expecting as much. The location was absolutely perfect. My only complaint is that my friend dropped my parking stub at the front desk for me at 10:45PM and when I went to pick it up at 7:45AM, they could not find it. I had to wait 30 minutes for the parking garage to locate my car. This leads me to believe their front desk is poorly managed. Also, it was busy and their elevators are SMALL! Sometimes it took us 10 minutes to catch one. Would definitely stay here again though!!!

title: “Great!”
text: I stayed for long weekend with a friend and after the ride in hotel elevator was concerned about room. What a pleasant surprise we had when we got in to our room. Plush, comfy bedding, Trader Joe's and CTA Station around the corner as well as Museum Campus across the street, we were delighted! Tracy at the Front Desk accomodated our needs and I will stay there again and highly recommend Best Western Grant Park!

title: “Couldn't Be Better!!”
text:
Had a reservation for only one night and was suppose to go to another hotel with a very large group of our business partners!! That other hotel,(nameless of course), gave such a runaround, not caring for what they had said or done by losing contact,giving wrong info, and just a poor example of what not to do to clients that belong to a group of 20,000
+ , and how they ended up treating the large group that ended up there,
 The manager Jeff & Co. were so helpful and made it so easy to just stay there at the Four Points!!!
 Room was comfortable, clean, the breakfasts were great!! Staf couldn't do enough to make our stay a great experiance!! And the other business partners that stayed there too, said the same!! 
Thank You All for making us have a very nice stay!!
AL D, Boston ,Ma.

title: “Best value for money considering the location”
text:
