This hotel is probably the best value for money place we have been so far. 
The location could hardly be better-Greenwich Village, with its bars restaurants, cinemas. There are subways stations within short walking distance (if the weather is nice, you could walk all the way to WTC and Battery Park within 30-40 minutes).
It is not luxurious and the rooms are small, but it has all the necessities.
-the concierge was very helpful and friendly, as was hotel personnel in general,
-this is safe area and a safe place too stay, one of the best in Manhattan (if not the best),
-free wireless internet! A small TV, hair drier, slippers and bathrobes provided in the room, 
-the room and shared toilets are kept clean,
-free breakfast
I give it five stars primary due to the excellent value for money ratio.

title: “Valued hotel, newly decorated, convenient location”
text: A good hotel if you don't want to fork out large sums of money, as hotels in SF are generally on the expensive side. 5 min walk to Civic center BART and Muni station, so easy access to the airport and other places in the city, but not the most pleasant walk along the way to the station as it's full of urinary smell and homeless people around civic center. I have stayed in 2 hotels, 1 being just at the border of tenderloin/downtown, which is fine as long as you don't walk into tenderloin. I am fine with the homeless people but of course if you hv a choice you might want to stay in slightly nicer location with just 20$ more per night. However, the location of the hotel should not undermine the fact that it is nicely and newly-decorated, a comfy stay. no problem without air con. in May, the fan at the ceiling does cool the room well! Nice gym, swimming pool and free wi-fi, and a nice coffee place called SightGlass just 3 min away along the 7th Street. what more can you ask for?

title: “Great Location, Horrible Hotel”
text: I stayed here in February, when i seen the hotel I loved it, the foyer was elegant and lovely looking. However once we steeped out the lift there was a horrible smell, the bedroom was tiny with the beds up against the walls with barely any room to move. The view was of the bins in the yard and the ladders made it look so easy to get into our room throught the window. There were no facilities other than a very expensive shop. Would have really appreciated a restraunt or a swimming pool. However, the location of the hotel was excellent, the empire state building was on the next street. Perfect midtown location. But the hotel was terrible and I couldn't put up with it again.

title: “Great hotel, runs like clockwork”
text: I stayed here with a large group of people, and the hotel did an excellent job of catering to our needs. Rooms were fresh and clean appearing. Breakfast had great options and was out for our early departure. Staff were friendly and attentive. The management of this hotel clearly understand that it takes more than a vacancy sign to make a hotel work and it shows. I would definitely recommend this hotel to future Denver travellers. If it has a limitation it is the location that isn't anywhere near downtown but also not super close to the airport (15 minutes). I think this is more of an issue with Denver airport zoning (and all airport hotels here) than it is with this hotel specifically.

title: “You name it, they did it right....except the lack of free wi-fi in the room.”
text:
Just returned from a 5 night business stay at the Downtown HIlton for an industry conference. I've been to ton of these things all over the country and no matter how good they are, there's always some little thing that nags at me during my stay: inconvenient elevator location, lousy restaurants, mediocre room, bad location etc. Not this time: the Hilton Downtown really nailed every aspect of my visit and the conference, from early check in to late check out, from terrific breakfast options to an incredibly restful night's sleep. 
Rooms are generously sized (it is Texas after all) and the bed is flat-out fantastic. Everything was spotless and service, when needed, was top notch. My only complaint: no free wi-fi in the rooms. It'll cost you $13.95 a day for that luxury. It's a pet peeve of mine, but everything else was so outstanding that I'm willing to overlook that. On the bright side, there is free wi-fi in the lobby area and a LOT of places to hang out with your laptop and get some work (or surfing) done.
The location of this hotel is perfect for heading out to the 6th street scene in the evening. It's all within walking distance and there are several good restaurants (Iron Cactus was a favorite) and a ton of clubs with live music.
I definitely recommend this hotel!

title: “AWESOME HOTEL”
text: I was in town just one night for Haz-Mat Training, but this was beyond my expectations. The place was Grand in deed. Service was top notch. The room was amazing. Tried to watch TV and relax, but somehow it kept wanting me to buy movies. So I just hung out on the Indoor Balcony that each room has. I really loved it, Wish I could have stayed longer. Oh yeah, the Resturant there......Killer! Shuttle service drivers were professional and prompt. It was Wonderful..

title: “Really liked Hotel Valencia...”
text:
Hotel Valencia bills itself as "contemporary chic". That's a good description. Located on the famed San Antonio Riverwalk, this is a REALLY GOOD HOTEL.
Rooms are large, comfortable, and tastefully decorated. Very contemporary.
Common areas are trendy, chic, cool without taking it too far.
Beds were very, very comfortable. Morning coffee (complimentary in the lobby) was excellent. Service was very friendly.
They've had many, many celebrities stay here. All in all, I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “Better Than Average”
text: The hotel is a little tired, as some other reviewers have noted. Nothing looks brand-new, as it does on their web site images. However, it was not bad at all. Our room (#1118) was fairly clean and fairly large by New York standards - it had a comfortable Queen bed, a desk with a chair, plus two small armchairs and a round table in the corner. And, most importantly for us, it was unbelievably quiet. We heard nothing, day or night, other than room doors on our floor closing (our door, for example, took a little bit of force to close properly). Overall, I would recommend this hotel to most travelers (unless you are one of those people who won't settle for anything less than the Plaza), especially if you can get a good deal on it. We saw a lot of Europeans at the Tudor, most notably Spaniards and Scandinavians.

title: “Fantastic Hotel in a great Location”
text: My husband booked this hotel as a surprise for my 40th birthday. We arrived on the 27th December and stayed until New years day. I cant really fault anything about it. The rooms were lovely and spacious and we had a great view of the chrysler building.I would definetely go back to this hotel.

title: “Our Favorite Place to Stay in San Diego”
text: We've been traveling to the San Diego area for years and this ultimately is our favorite hotel and location. The staff is more than accommodating, the rooms are beautiful and the location is great. Don't miss the 2 for 1 happy hour!

title: “Perfect - especially for a family with young children”
text: Can't rave enough about this hotel. My husband was initially concerned that we had booked a hotel too far from the action, so we compromised 5 nights at Hotel Beacon, 4 nights at Novotel. After one night's stay at Hotel Beacon, we cancelled our Novotel booking. Having a room with a kitchenette meant we could sample the wonderful food on offer from Fairways across the street. Big Nicks Pizza is just a block away and great pizza. The subway is conveniently located and Central Park and Natural History Museum are in walking distance. Just downstairs is a Starbucks with free wifi. The staff were courteous and not overly friendly. We were on the 7th floor, the same floor as the laundry which we used a few times. All in all, we would thoroughly recommend this hotel for a family and we thought they were reasonably priced as well. If I'm ever fortunate enough to return to NYC I would definitely stay there!

title: “Great location, but very crowded”
text: The location can't be beat if you're looking to be right in Times Square. We used points for our recent stay, and can't complain about the size and quality of the room. We can't agree with previous reviews about thinning towels and moldy smells, as our room (14th floor) and towels were comfortable and plush. Housekeeping is a little understaffed, as the rooms did not get cleaned until 4p every day....which is usually when we headed back to the room to relax after walking all day. The hotel IS very crowded with convention and tour bus groups, which makes the lobby, bar, and elevators very congested. We thought that the 8th floor (lobby) bar could have stayed opened a little later than 8 or 9 on Thurs and Friday, but oh well. Overall, nice experience.

title: “Lobby service exceptional!!!!”
text: I just want to let everyone know what a fabulous place the JW Marriott San Antonio is. Beautiful resort and fantastic service!!!!! Thank you soooooo much to Megan, Paige, Michael P.Brandon,Paul, Ginny, Jennifer F., and Larissa. Management was always helpful Cenovio, Whitney, Randy and Randie. If you are planning a family vacation or even a romantic getaway this is the place to go. Will definitely visit again..... Didn't want to leave!!! Miss you already.....

title: “Great Place”
text: Quality Inn of Orange Park is a great place to stay. My family and I have stayed there numerous times,and the rooms has always been clean and well kept. Rechelle and the rest of the staff always go out of there way to make sure we are happy. I will stay here again.

title: “Great location for price.”
text: For the price this hotel was fine. We had read the reviews and therefore expected the rather tired level of decoration. The room itself was probably better than the communal areas. The location was excellent. At the end of the day you get what you pay for and I would recommend it as a place to stay to people who just want a convenient and value for money place to sleep.

title: “Helpful staff + Great location + Quiet room = Excellent Experience”
text: We stayed at the White Swan Inn for 3 nights and we could not have had a better stay! The room was clean and very quiet at night. The front desk staff were extremely helpful arranging for transportation and suggesting a restaurant in Noth Beach. The location was great for us! It was an easy walk to shopping in Union Square and Chinatown plus they are only 1 block off of the cable car line. It was also very easy to catch cabs right in front of the hotel. The complimentary breakfast was better than expected. We also appreciated the free water bottles in the mini-refrigerator in the room. We would definitely stay here again for our next visit to SF.

title: “Lovely oasis in Rancho Bernardo!”
text: Rancho Bernardo is a master planned community about 15 miles east of the coast in San Diego county. The Rancho Bernardo Inn is a lushly landscaped Spanish style resort with spa and golf course in the heart of the community and just a few minutes from Interstate 15. We live nearby and go there frequently to play the course or go to the beautiful spa but until this week, we never stayed there. Our room was comfortable and fresh and had a wonderful balcony overlooking the golf course. We enjoyed lunch and dinner at the outdoor restaurant, The Veranda. The service was impeccable and we were always met with a smile. The spa and spa pool are newer and beautiful. We did not use any spa services so did not have access to those facilities. The hotel pool and spa are a bit dated but have the "old California" feel. All in all, a wonderful place.

title: “Luxury and Service at a great value”
text: Wow! This is a very nice hotel. It is conveniently located off of I35, close to the Airport for those of you flying in with plenty to eat both close to the hotel as well as inside the hotel. The hotel has several restaurants on the property with a sports bar with several TV's for those that like to watch a good game. The rooms are very well maintained, stocked and extremely clean plus there is turndown service at night which is always a plus. Service was fantastic the week I was here even though the property was extremely booked with several events. Valet parking is a must at this property which will set you back $22.82 per day including tax so don't forget to add this to your room rates. If you call ahead of time, at least 10 minutes prior to needing your vehicle it will be there waiting for you.There are no particular good views per say. I had the Interstate road view which gave me front access to the fire trucks and ambulances riding up and down I35 at all hours of the night. Next time I will just get the rear view just to have it a bit quieter at night.

title: “The Good, the Bad and the Elevators”
text:
Our family of 4 stayed at the JW Marriott for 6 nights beginning April 1st. Overall, we loved our DC trip and can recount all the endless and enriching activities - White House tour, Capital tour, monuments, museums, great restaurants, shopping Georgetown, etc. We titled this review b/c we unanimously agreed on the following:
The Good - Awesome location within walking distance to most sites; quiet and clean rooms with nice finishes; comfortable beds; nice selection at the breakfast buffett for the Bed & Breakfast package. 
The Bad - Check-in was very slow b/c they had one person behind the counter and a line of 11 people waiting. Eventually, they called for more help and 3 additional people arrived at once (but we aren't certain where they all were for the 20 minutes we waited). Even worse, every morning the person who delivered the USA Today dropped them onto the floor in the loudest fashion possible. My husband swears he/she must have been REALLY tall b/c it woke us both up throughout the week - you heard thud, thud, thud all the way down the hall as they were dropped.
The Elevators - It was a busy week and they either have a terrible elevator system based on capacity or they were programmed horribly. Everyone hopped on the first elevator in any direction from desperation; many resorted to the stairs (we even walked from the 10th floor). It was truly annoying.
Despite all of this, we really thought the location and comfort of the rooms makes this hotel worth visiting, especially if you are visiting DC with kids. The hotel just really needs to fix those elevators and ask the paper delivery person to be more considerate.

title: “Amazing Stay”
text: This is the best place to stay in San Diego. The overall experience was fantastic. The staff was the best I have experienced at any hotel. From check-in with Magdalena to dinner with Alberto and Natalie, I have never felt so welcomed and waited on. There rooms are elegant and the bedding is the best I have ever slept in, I will never stay anywhere else when I visit San Diego.

title: “Excellent value with our grandkids”
text: We rented three queen sized beds and had microwave and refrigerator for our drinks, etc. The kids had a pool to work off some energy. It is very close to Fiesta Texas. The breakfast in the morning had something for every one in our party. The staff were very kind and helpful. We will be staying here again!

title: “Love the classic beauty in the desert.”
text:
I have been staying here on and off for business since March and not only does the staff greet me personally by name every time I walk in the door, but they accommodate all of my sometimes demanding requests. We have used the property for meeting space, catering and business dinners and each event is done with perfection. I've also had time to use the spa and all of the recreation facilities and the amenities are all beautiful.
The classic Frank Lloyd Wright building really sets this hotel apart from your typical Arizona resort.
And the staff here really goes out of their way to make you feel special. I've have valets deal with broken down Avis cars of mine personally! Where else does that happen?!

title: “Great location and atmosphere”
text:
The Tuscan Inn has a great location to tourist sites within San Francisco. Walking distance to Pier 39, bay ferries and tours, Ghirardelli Square, etc. Streetcars and cable cars are close to take you to Market Street, the Ferry Terminal, etc.
The Inn is clean, and welcoming. It has a good look, nice sitting area in the lobby, wine hour every night, friendly and helpful staff.
The rooms we had were a good size and clean. It was basic, but that was OK for us. I had trouble with the hot water in my shower but it was fixed the same day I reported the problem. 
I personally appreciated the free internet service in the hotel. 
All-in-all, compared to other hotels in the area, we were both impressed and happy with the Tuscan Inn and would recommend it. 
I did have to search through the usual online websites to find the best deal for rooms, but if you take time to look, I think you will be happy with the rates you get.

title: “AT HOME before my "forever home"”
text:
I most recently moved to Indianapolis. I wanted to take a month to find the right place to live so I decided to stay somewhere around the Keystone at the Crossing area. I found TownePlace Suites and from my call to make a reservation, I felt welcomed! 
The team there is fun yet professional. They really made my relocation a lot easier. So much so, I actually took 2 months to find my forever home because I was so comfortable there!!!
I was introduced to many of the local restaurants as they had them come in for happy hour hors d'oeuvres.

title: “Excellent Hotel For Business Travel”
text: This hotel has a great downtown location. I walked mostly to my office and to restuarants at night, but they did have a Courtesy Car which would take you where you needed to go. I can't comment on the restaurant because I didn't eat there ($$$), but the hotel is conveniently located within walking distance of several restaurants. The rooms were clean, quiet, and nicely appointed. I noticed another reviewer mentioned the phone message light constantly blinking, and yes that can be annoying. My room had a great view. The staff was extremely helpful. I misplaced my itemized bill (crutial for submitting my expense report) and they sent me a copy within half an hour of my contacting them. I definetly plan to stay there again whenever I am in Houston on business.

title: “Very nice room on club level, spacious, clean and quiet”
text: We like our room and the free drinks and snacks on the executive level. The hotel was nice with plenty of room to hang out with others in the lobby. They didn't seem used to carrying up bags to the room but did it. Great cookies upon check in. There for NCAA basketball tournament.

title: “Wow! LOVED It!!! Awesome family resort!!!! Can't wait to go back! 5 stars”
text: This was the best family vacation we have had! We usually stay in 1st class resorts and this place was fabulous! We were very impressed with our 1 bedroom unit on the 3rd floor with cathedral ceiling and beautiful views of the golf course and landscape. Everything was clean, well maintained and very comfortable and quiet. The wildflowers and native Texas trees and plants are stunning. The pools are fabulous. Our 2 kids LOVED it so much we never left to go to Sea World. Plenty of kids activities and family activities like square dancing, magic shows, wine tasting, live bands by the pool, arts and crafts, wine and cheese parties, etc. and even poker and spa nights for mom and dad! Staff was WONDERFUL. You will LOVE this resort!!!

title: “Odd layout, maintenance issues, casual staff...”
text:
In fairness, I should point out that I did not actually stay overnight here. I needed one more hotel stay for a free night promotion and this hotel had a great AAA Sunday night rate.
So I checked in, went up to the room, and spent a few hours finishing up some work in quiet. Then, around midnight, I left and slept in my own bed at home.
The room itself was decent. It was not especially large but did have a couch in a sitting area, along with a work desk, microwave, and mini-fridge. Standard TV in the bedroom area. The air conditioning also worked very well. Few minor issues: couch had stains and toilet ran all the time.
The room itself was very quiet, so I was surprised at how noisy it became when I opened the window. I-880 was right outside my window and yet the noise insulation had blocked it out well. (For reference, this was a third floor room way back in the far right corner of the hotel.)
The layout of the property is strange. It's apparently several buildings linked by walkways around central courtyards. Fortunately, the weather in San Jose is almost always sunny, otherwise it would be annoying (impossible?) to move around the property without going outside.
The clerk at check-in was not very professional. I had called over in advance to get a rate quote and she apparently forgot about my call - put me on hold, then picked the call back up but left me on the line without saying anything... like she had hit the wrong button and didn't realize I was there. The check-in itself was fine, asked for my room preferences, etc. But then later, when I was leaving, she and another clerk were carrying on a raucous conversation with a guest in the lobby and ignored me.
This hotel was ok and would certainly be fine at the $59 AAA rate I found. The regular rate that same night was $159 - not nearly worth it. There are plenty of other properties more convenient to the airport that offer a better guest experience.

title: “Fantastic service!”
text: Good hotel in good location. Staff and service was excellent.

title: “Bed bugs”
text: Location was great, buy the hotel room was dirty, untidy and I got bitten by bed bugs. Would not stay here again

title: “Great stay, lovely hotel, perfect location wonderful city”
text: We were delighted with our 2 night stay, familys first time in US and this hotel gave a great impression. Its location was ideal for all the sights we wished to visit. The staff were nice and the breakfasts were a fine start to the day. No faults that anyone can remember

title: “I enjoyed my stay at Ramada Inn, Chicago”
text:
I spent the last two weeks at Ramada Inn for professional development training as a teacher in Chicago. I was treated with the utmost respect and courtesy from our hostess, Jessie Coffey and Victoria Coats. These two employees made partonizing the resturant an enjoyable experience. The food was great, especially the mashed potatoes. Again, thanks, Jessie and Victoria.
Marcella Graves,
Youth Connection Charter School

title: “Lot like other hotels in SF except for the noise.”
text:
Check in guy was a dud. He didn’t even try to get us the type of room we wanted (king). When we offered to wait for our preffered room type, he said he didn’t want to hazard a guess. A platinum membership should get you the room type you request. When I tried again to get a king room, he tried to upsell us. He was only taught to upsell.
The rest of the staff was surprisingly nice, despite Mr. Checkin. I gave the bell man a tall order and he was exceedingly polite.
The room is fine, but beds are soft and lumpy. It’s just like any other hotel room in SF. Desk phone is next gen, and frankly, I couldn’t figure it out.
Wireless is PAINFULLY slow in the rooms. It did not get better during the week.
Soundproofing is really poor. The hallway noise is evident at most times; the sirens on Howard pierce a good night’s sleep. 
Lots and lots of twenty somethings checked in on Saturday night to go clubbing in SOMA (quad style). It was really a party hotel that night.

title: “New Chicago Favorite”
text: Perfect room design, fabulous balconies, and an airy, modern feel make this my new Chicago favorite for the money.

title: “Great Location & Super Staff”
text: This was a lovely "irish feel" hotel, excellent staff, priced well for NY, great location to main business areas and local shopping

title: “Great Location, Substandard Service and Rooms”
text:
We stayed here for two nights as a result of finding what appeared to be a good deal in an excellent location. I ended up being taunted by the Marriott, Waldorf, and W hotels right across the street for two straight days. 
When we checked in we were greated by an unpleasant front desk staff that seemed more interested in getting rid of us than getting us the double room we had booked. The room ended up appearing very old, the sheets dirty, and the bathroom in need of an update. Overall we were not happy with the stay.

title: “Great location”
text:
We stayed for 1 night Sept. 29-30. We arrived at 9:45am and were able to check-in which was nice because we wanted to drop our stuff and head for Michigan Ave. Beautiful room on the 14th floor with view of the Illinois Center and a sliver of Lake Michigan. Very nicely decorated with white comforters, a body pillow, other throw pillows. Large flat screen t.v., internet access, large desk, reclining chair. The bathroom had nice toiletries and a massaging shower head. Extra towels and pillows, iron & board in the closet. There was also a coffee maker that we didn't use. This is a very large hotel with 30(?) floors in the east tower we were in. Didn't go in the west tower. Very nice lobby area with restaurants and a gift shop. We didn't eat here, though. 
Excellent location for sightseeing as the architecture river tours leave from just below the hotel. Fannie Mae candy on the corner of Michigan & Wacker. Corner Bakery on the next corner. McDonald's behind the Wrigley buiding, Billy Goat tavern below the Wrigley Building, plenty of Starbucks around and a Walgreens nearby. Easy walk to Millennium Park and all the shops of Michigan Ave. Also walkable to Navy Pier although make sure you have your walking shoes on and if you're lucky you'll get to ride one of their free trolleys.

title: “enjoyed our stay”
text: We recently spent eight days at the resort and the staff was wonderful, so helpful at all times. The grounds are beautiful. Our room was comfortable. We ate at the hotel a few times and everything was wonderful..

title: “A Good Experience Gone Bad.”
text:
I'd like to say that first impressions are important, and sadly the first impression at this Hotel was not as we might have hopped for. Upon arriving, at 10pm PST, my wife and I were informed that our room would be located directly adjacent to the entrance of the hotel. But we were assured that the sleeping quarters were near the back of the room and that the noise of people entering and exiting would hardly be heard if we noticed at all. 
I could not help but notice that the door to our room was slightly blocked by the service door to an employee basement (service area). The clerk was very friendly, this did help. We entered the room; it was spacious, clean and sadly reeked of natural gas.
I am not a paranoid person, being a former employee of a restaurant that used natural gas I immediately knew the odor. My wife and I asked if we could have a new room. The clerk, who was very friendly, sadly informed us they were sold out for the night. After I informed him of our problem, he first attempted to turn the oven, off himself instead of calling someone in. 
I had to inform him hours later that his plan did not work. The clerk said at that point that he would have maintenance look at in the morning. We shared an awkward moment of silence, then I asked if they had a sister hotel were we could stay instead. I was told there was, I was refunded for the night at this hotel and charged for the night at the sister motel which was located at the end of the same block. The entire exchange took until 1am. Both clerks at both Hotels were friendly but neither offered more than verbal compensation for my displacement or troubles. I was happy they were both sorry for my trouble, but I would rather have been sleeping rather then trying to work out how to solve their gas leak issues at 1am, and then trying to find a place for my wife and I to sleep for the night.
We were actually quite lucky I knew of the problem, the dumfound clerk had no such experience with natural gas and had asked that we just sleep in the room anyway. Granted he suggested we leave a window open, and even that we put a fan near the window. But if we had done so we may have gotten deathly ill or worse. What I do know of natural gas is from Avista. Avista (a power company in Washington state) has told its customers that if you smell natural gas, GET OUT! And stay out until their technicians can look at the problem. Not go inside your house and sleep on it until maintenance can look at it in the morning, oh and put a fan in the window.
I repeat, he was a really nice guy and meant well.
End of Day 1
We stayed for another 6 days, instead of giving you a play by play of each day, as I had above. Let me sum up. 
Positive comments:
All employees and managers were very kind and also acted as quickly as possible to serve us as they could.
Negative comments:
• Unfortunately, our room was not serviced until we called at 7pm on one day.
• The toilet didn't work on 3 different occasions, and the service toilet they have for just such an occasion was also out of order.
• Bed sheets shorted every night
• Not enough electrical outlets. I own a CPAP machine which requires an outlet near the bed, no outlets located near the beds. Only behind them which required my wife and I to move the bed before I could use my medical device.
• No working clothes iron in the room. They did have one, but it didn’t work. And after the week we’d had so far I was sure they’d give me another one, but I didn’t want to risk what it might do to whatever I would try to iron. 
• No elevator to the 2nd floor (which normally wouldn't be an issue, but I didn't pack expecting to be lifting that kind of wait up a flight of stairs)
• Poor cable TV reception, I'm not even sure how you get back Cable reception. It's cable, how do you get bad cable reception? I don't know but somehow we didn't get all the channels that were listed in their hotel guide book as "local"
• Moldy sponge in which to clean the dishes provided by the hotel
• Had to run the taps for a while to get hot water, then couldn't get cold water, even though they ran out of two different faucets.
• The toilet seat would tip as you sat on it, so if you didn't try to balance while you were using it you might tip it over.
More Positive comments:
But don't let all these negative comments fool you. If you don't rent a car, and you want a location that is close to the metro (rail and buses) as well as a place that is within walking distance to many attractions,** and a friendly staff. This hotel will have what you want. The staff is very friendly, and so is the management. 
Summation:
In summation we were within 10 minutes of so many excellent LA attractions it almost made the hotel room worth it, almost. Our trip was schedule for a total of 9 days 8 nights, you might have noticed above we only stayed 7 nights. 
We decided it would be more cost effective to pay $100 to fly home than pay $129 to stay another night at the Hollywood Celebrity.
Footnote
**Man’s Chinese theater is awesome! Make sure to stop there on a weekend evening or a Friday night. The street performers are something else. And sign up to see the Jimmy Kimmel live show, its right across the street! Within 5 min of the hotel a live TV show!

title: “Absolutely beautiful!”
text: I chose this hotel for a weekend stay in Philadelphia after reading a lot of reviews on this site, and I'm pleased to say that this is by far the nicest hotel I've ever stayed in! My wife and I checked in immediately following our wedding and were greeted by the friendly and courteous staff. The room exceeded all of our expectations, was a lot larger than what most other hotels will offer in the city, and provided a great view overlooking the square. This hotel is definitely at the top of my list the next time I'm in the Phila. area.

title: “Last minute beach trip to San Diego”
text: Summer in Arizona is like living in an open oven, so many families like to trek across the desert to San Diego to escape. San Diego, however, is like Times Square at New Years so you need to plan ahead to find a decent hotel, condo, timeshare, etc. We decided last minute to drive over for one last beach trip before school starts so finding a decent place to stay near the ocean was not easy. Unless you can stay near the beach, it's dumb to go...why drive 6 hours to the beach if you have to stay inland? I looked at every condo rental site and all the beachfront hotels from Coronado to Carlsbad and there were just 2 or 3 available for 5 days in late July. I decided on this hotel because of its great location and have not been disappointed about that. A $5 water taxi ride took us to Sea World yesterday and we avoided the crowd and parking nightmare by coming in "the back door". Our ticket is good for consecutive days so we ran around the park in the morning doing all the rides and when the weekend crowd swelled, we took our water taxi back to the hotel and spent the rest of the afternoon at the beach. We plan to do the same tomorrow. The pool at the hotel, however, is in some sort of wind tunnel so the pool was not fun for the kids nor for us...it's the strangest thing. The first room they put us in was looking over a roof and air con unit...totally unacceptable...so I paid for an upgrade and we're now on the 17th floor, Concierge level, which is fabulous. Free breakfast in the a.m. and Happy Hour could replace dinner if desired...love the cocktail selection too. It doesn't get any better than having a free glass on wine in your room looking out at the beautiful ocean! We have a perfect view of the fireworks at SeaWorld which starts at 9:50 every night. For $300/night, this place is a bargain considering the other options, time of year, late booking and location.

title: “Lovely old style central location Hotel”
text: The Buckminster is noe fo the few Hotels that are really affordable if you want to stay in Back Bay. It's location is ideal for touring and directly opposite the underground station from which for around £1 you can go anywhere on the lines. There are numerous restaurants and cafes within walking distance and there are 2 convenience stores very nearby. Obviously there is s ome street noise at night but no more than the other expensive Hotels in the main areas. There is no Tea and Coffee in the rooms or room service but the bedroom was really spacious, lovely bed and bedding, it was clean, the bathroom was modern (with bath and overhead fixed showerhead which was a little disappointing as we prefer a detachable showerhead) and great and the TV child-friendly. There was A/C and Heating that you could control via a panel on the wall and the A/C was quiet! The staff were polite and helpful too - all in all a very nice place.

title: “Good location and very good service”
text: Near to transportation, attractions and restaurants. The personnel is very helpful giving directions and tips during our stay. Small rooms but enough for a short stay. Soap and other hygiene implements are made with natural and organic components.

title: “Frank Lloyd Wright on steroids”
text: This is an absolute MUST for anyone who admires the architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright. Although we learned there is some dispute as to who actually did the final design for the hotel and the many out buildings on the property, the architecture, lighting, furniture, landscape design are all clearly heavily influenced by Wright. We spent 3 days on the property leaving only to take a tour of Taliesin West (Wright's home and current architectural school less than 20 miles away) and we were constantly discovering new wonderful aspects of the hotel. In addition to the main building, there are 8 pools (have to go back to swim in the rest of them!) 2 full service restaurants (don't miss the lobster bisque and souffle) and a cafe, an enormous spa, tennis courts, I could go on. Tours of the hotel are offered 3 times a week - don't miss if you can work it in to your schedule. The grounds are so extensive that despite the fact we were there on a very busy, booked weekend, it was easy to wander the grounds without seeing another person. Both restaurants were excellent, bartenders imaginative - it was the perfect, pampered weekend. I went with a girlfriend I needed to catch up with and we had a blast, but I'm planning to go back with my husband as this is also a very romantic getaway. Not inexpensive - but I'm guessing it's possible to find good deals with a bit of planning.

title: “Truly wretched”
text:
Booked online coming and going from a trip out of state, which due to the ferry schedule here and my air travel times essentially required staying at the airport (or at least on the mainland). The first stay was okay... nothing too nice about it, but nothing ultra negative either. The second stay involved a 1:00 a.m. drunken fight in the hallway, hairs (other than my own) in the bed linens and bathroom, stains in the bathroom, and an overpowering scent of those cheap institutional disinfectants used in places such as schools and prisons. Also, the heater squeaked loudly. 
Had I not booked through Expedia, who are surely smart enough to have some clause which prevents me from any recompense, I would have gone to the front desk and demanded my money back and just tried my luck at another one of the dozens of hotels on the block. For what it's worth, the cabin attendants on my flight were like, "Oh No! Not the Clarion Sea-Tac!!!" They recommended the Radisson Gateway.

title: “A pleasant surprise!”
text:
I was looking for a not so expensive hotel within walking distance to Times Square to spend a weekend with my wife, since I had bought tickets to a show at B.B. King´s Blues Club & Grill and the Phantom of the Opera. Among the many hotels available, I found the Staybridge Times Square on Google Earth. I had seen some reviews online, talking about the shady businesses on the same street, but decided to give it a try, after looking at some photos of the hotel´s ammenities.
I have to admit that it is located on a street where you´ll see some shops you´d never go into, but that´s just half a block from 8th Ave. As soon as you get to 8th Ave., you´ll see a Dean & Deluca, and right next to it, one of the Muji stores. And let me make it clear that we never felt that this area wasn´t safe. Even around midnight, when we were coming back from a show, there were a lot of people on the streets and everything felt fine.
So, if you don´t mind the short walk to decent civilization, you´ll absolutely love the hotel. The staff was extremely courteous from the start, and although this was probably due to our reservation, they made it possible for us to check before at noon.
The room was one of the best ones I had ever slept in. The bed was very confortable (we felt like we weren´t going to have the strength to leave the bed and go to the show), and it was the first time we ever stayed in a room with a full refrigerator and a dishwasher, besides the microwave oven, electric stove, coffee maker, etc.
There were only two cons in our stay. The first was that in the room where we were located (end of the hall), you could hear a bit too much of closing doors (although that never prevented us from sleeping). The other was that our room was on the last floor, so water flow to the shower and sinks were inconsistent. But that´s easy to fix. Just ask for a lower room.
We will certainly stay there again, given another opportunity.

title: “Very Zen at the Westin.”
text: The location is great. Walking distance to Market street and all the downtown stores. The rooms are large. Modern furnishings and plasma TV. Beds are very comfortable. Stayed on 25th floor in Starwood Member room, so the view was great, overlooking the Ghery Museum & Yerba Buena Gardens.

title: “Great Hotel, Cold Shower”
text: Loved the hotel. Cool space/building. Walking distance to Hyatt convention center. Great welcome gift for Starwood Platinum level guests. However....Shower was cold at 6:30 am. That is my kryptonite for a hotel. I am sure something was amiss, thus my good rating. I am a fan of the Aloft properties and this one is really great. I just hope they figure out the water issue!

title: “Fabulous night view!”
text: SOoo glad we chose Drury Plaza at the river walk! The location has been great. The converted bank building was quirky and fun! Convenient to everything, with fabulous views from the rooftop terrace (23 floor). Beautiful view of San Fernando Cathedral from our room. Do Not Miss the roof top view-especially at night! Very crowded for the parade weekend but that just adds to the fun! More people watching! The terrace room was worth the extra $$ for us. Very interesting to watch the street scene! Kickback was crowded but nice. Had to wait on elevators, even gave up and took the stairs a few times! So if you dont like crowds dont come on parade weekend! Great time in San Antonio. Would love to come back and if I do, I would stay at Drury Plaza again!!

title: “Disappointed in W”
text: My wife and I decided to go to the first annual MystiQal event at Victory Center last Saturday night. She is a Gold Starwood Elite, and we used points for the stay. The check-in was smooth, the room was nice, but the experience in the lobby bar and the deck for the parade were extremely disappointing. Despite the rates charged for the hotel, the hotel became jam packed with street people, mostly drunk 20-somethings that were obviously not staying at the hotel. The Ghost Bar had an extremely rude doorman trying to control the door as well. I realize it was an attempt at trying to replicate Mardis Gras, and you have to put the stay in perspective, however management did a poor job of thinking this through. Long story short, we paid too much, even if it was points, to have a very mediocre experience. "W" may want to replace the word "wish" with "over-rated". on the bed pillow.

title: “Cute hotel for visiting, but not during the summer”
text: I recently stayed here during a business trip and was dismayed to find out that there was no air conditioning! Each of the rooms has heating, so they would be comfortable during the winter, but my room was 85 degrees when i checked in. Even with the door propped open and the window open for hours, it was still in the high 70s when i fell asleep. I liked the cleanliness and the style of the place, it was a nicely remodeled older property. The soaps and shampoos and such were an intoxicating blood orange smell which I absolutely loved.

title: “Pure class and convenience”
text:
Stayed here in March of 2012 and enjoyed it quite a bit. Has the feel of a boutique hotel with all the conveniences of a full service hotel. Great gym, great restaurant and most of all, great staff. Left some important documents inside the safe and after informing them, they promptly FedExed everything to my home address. They went above and beyond with everything that was done at the hotel.
 The hotel also has great infrastructure with a shopping mall across the street, and many great restaurants around the area. The staff will be happy to guide you in the right direction.
 Highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Just okay”
text:
The Days Inn Civic Center is very dated. The room was clean and the bed was fine. It was hard to get a feel for the place because we arrived at 12:30 am, the parking lot was full but the hotel is right off of the street and there were people walking by all night. 
It was a fine place to lay our heads down for 6 hours, but i wouldn't stay more than a night.

title: “Elegant, yet approachable”
text: We chose to stay here last minute after a late night in the city. Check-in was super easy and our room was bigger than we anticipated. We had a great view looking out over the city. This hotel is definitely on our short list of places to come back to when in San Francisco.

title: “James Dean stayed here”
text: Stayed in this hotel recently, awesome place. Very clean, friendly staff and location is perfect. No ifs no buts or maybe's...book this hotel you won't be disappointed!

title: “Hotel Stay Let Down By Sloppy Mistake”
text:
As a surprise start to our stay at the Sofitel New York my father had arranged with the hotel for a bottle of champagne (paid for by him) to be in our room on arrival. The champagne, in an ice bucket with glasses, was in the room but the housekeeping staff had forgotten to leave the note he had requested explaining who it was from. So, suspecting that the champagne was not complimentary and with no idea to the contrary, we left it unopened where we found it and there it stayed for the week of our stay and that was how it was left on our departure. Bizarrely, although housekeeping were (obviously) in our room on a regular basis, no one thought to enquire why we hadn't enjoyed our bottle of champagne. Confirming our thoughts, of course, that it wasn't complimentary. 
You can imagine our disappointment on our arrival back in the UK to discover we could have enjoyed that bottle of champagne - at any time during our stay! On phoning the hotel, guest relations apologised (as one might hope) and said they would refund my father the cost of the bottle of champagne - the least they could do! However, that could not change the fact that we'd missed out on what would have been a lovely start to our holiday. 
Also, on check in at the hotel, I was told my credit card would be charged $700 at that time for those additional services (mini-bar, telephone calls etc) that we might use during our stay. I said I did not object to paying for these things after our stay, clearly, but thought it unacceptable that my card would be charged in advance for services I might not use. Because of my objection, the 'pre-charge' was revised to $300 but it was not the best start to our stay. In the event, we ended up only making $15 worth of phone calls which I paid for in cash. These two experiences let down a stay at what was otherwise a pleasant and comfortable hotel.

title: “Great Value and Location”
text: We stayed at the Andaz Wall Street over the holiday weekend and had a positive experience overall. The hotel is located in a quiet area just a few blocks from the 2/3 trains, making it a quick subway ride to mid-town. It is also within walking distance of the Brooklyn Bridge, South Street Seaport, Battery Park, and 9/11 Memorial. We were upgraded to a suite for free, which was a nice perk. The room itself was spacious and very clean, and was equipped with free Wi-Fi, as well as free snacks and drinks from the mini fridge. There were a few downsides to our experience however, including our lack of “complimentary” breakfast that was supposed to be included in our hotel package. We were told that they were serving brunch instead of breakfast, which cost between $26-$36 per person + tip (~$80 for 2)?! The hotel also did not have hot water one evening from 9pm-6am due to some sort of construction in the area. This would have been fine had we been notified prior, but we arrived back to the hotel after 9pm and were forced to take cold showers. A notice had been placed in our room at some point during that afternoon, which we clearly did not see as we were out until that evening. Also, as an aside, be warned that some of the rooms (including ours) have all glass shower areas with no curtains, which may not be conducive if traveling with a friend, etc. While the toilet door was frosted, you could still see through when the light was on. The water from the bathroom sink and shower also ran onto the hardwood floor, which got a bit slippery. All in all, the hotel was a good value and offered pleasant staff, an extremely clean room, a convenient location, and a sleek atmosphere.

title: “I stay at this hotel everytime I am in Austin.”
text: This hotel is clean and the staff is very friendly and helpful. There is easy access to the x-way, airport and downtown.

title: “Nice place. Clean and great location”
text: I was only in the hotel for one night but the staff was accommodating and the rooms were comfortable. Gym was nice. Nice bar in the lobby and front desk staff were very friendly. Hotel was also not far from the airport.

title: “Teens will love this place”
text:
We were originally booked at another hotel, they offered to move us here for free. I let my birthday daughter (16) choose which hotel she wanted. After walking in the door with all of the water things in the ceiling and the modern decor, she and her friend opted for this hotel. It is truely beautiful. The front desk staff, especially Julian, were terrific, nice and helpful. When I asked for a coffee pot for my morning coffee, it was in my room when I returned with our bags (oh, they had a room ready for us-it was only 12)-free, like the other hotel I was booked at.
Yes, the rooms are a little small, but the teenagers loved all the "cool" stuff that decorated the room, the huge flat screen tv (with HBO, HBO2), bathroom stuff, robe, throw blanket and extremely comfortable bed. Airconditioner worked great. 
A personal thing that I was uncomfortable with (with the teenagers in the room) was the bathroom glass wall. You could see the silhouette of whom ever was in the bathroom. If you have a small child, he will not be able to reach the sink, shower was great/hot.
Security-I felt very safe-you need to use your room card to push any button to get above floor 7 (lobby). GYM-did not use, but took a look and am an exerciser-great modern equipment-lifting stuff and eliptical/treadmill kind of equipment. BAR/LIVINGROOM-saw many people hanging out, comfortably having a few-modern. FOOD-did not eat there as I could feed my whole family breakfast on the charge for just a yogurt and cereal. Went next door to get muffins and bananas at StarBucks.
LOCATION-Remember this IS Times Square, if you want peace-go to the country (it is where we are from-no lights, people & tons of stars in the sky). We were on the 31st floor and had a side view of times square, on this Memorial Day weekend Saturday night it was loud but when the airconditioner was on, we could not hear anything and we were so tired nothing could stop us from sleeping. The morning noise was not a problem at all. We walked to and from Penn Station, Gershwin Theater, and Build A Bear. 
As a mom with two pretty teenagers in the "big city" I felt very comfortable and safe walking all around. I have been here a few times before, just take precautions as you would anywhere. I googled maps to help with locations and directions and managed just fine.

title: “Not that bad..”
text: Before booking at Civic Center Inn, we wanted to read some reviews here and then decide. When we read the reviews a lot of them were saying that this hotel was terrible but it wasn't as bad as we thought it was going to be... The room is not very clean except for the very good bathroom. The location isn't the best for the neighborhood but it is well situated except that this place (near the hotel) is full of poor people and drug addicts. Also when we booked the website said that the breakfast was included but there was no breakfast at all in the hotel. You also have to know that wi-fi isn't available in all the rooms, but it is free and available in the lobby. The staff was very nice, and someone is here 24/7 to make sure that no one else than clients get in. I would say that for the price i would recommend this hotel if you don't need a five star.

title: “Outstanding service, surprisingly kid friendly, hip funky decor”
text:
Via Hotwire, I booked 2 rooms for one night during the President's Day weekend. The rate was $139/night...and I was initially a bit apprehensive about this being the hotel revealed. It looked very adult-oriented and the reviews have tended to reflect this opinion...and we had two families with one pre-schooler apiece. There wasn't even a mention of cribs being available on the website---although a lot of cool services available for dogs were highlighted. I wrote the property via their website to inquire about the cribs.
I quickly received a voice mail message from a very nice man who assured me that they had cribs and to call if I had any questions or further requests. And thus began an amazing experience with the Hotel Solamar's customer service from every single employee we dealt with---from the front desk check-in to the cleaning people we saw in the hall. Everyone seems genuinely delighted to see you and eager to offer recommendations on how to make your stay in the hotel and the area more enjoyable. And bear in mind our party had two almost 3-year old boys in tow (enough to make most people head for the hills). Parents will appreciate how one host named Gordie got down to my son's level, really listened and had a nice conversation with him, and then greeted him by name whenever he saw him. Each child was also presented with a little goody bag of toys, including a thoughtful pre-soaped, duck-shaped sponge that made bathtime a real treat. When the crib was delivered, it was already assembled and was made up with sheets---this in itself is rather unusual!
The rooms are a little small, but very well decorated in a hip, modern style. Even the bathrobes are funky----zebra and leopard skin patterned terry cloth! Hilarious! Our bellman who delivered our luggage also kindly pointed out that the honor bar doesn't have those annoying sensors that charge your room if any of the fridge contents get moved---so if you can refrigerate a few small items of your own. The one slight service gaffe was that there was no honor bar key in our room, and it took about half an hour for them to locate an extra one.
It seems that most people who get rooms via a discount website get placed on the 4th floor which is the same floor as their pool and poolside bar. The front desk lady was proactive in giving us our rooms facing away from the pool to limit our exposure to DJ noise (seeing as we had young kids), but there was some hallway rowdiness from partygoers entering/leaving the pool area. Nothing terrible though, and the pool closes at 9.
The hotel's restaurant JSix is gorgeously appointed, and serves delicious breakfast for a surprisingly reasonable price! Try the Chilaquiles which are amazing! Again, the wait staff were extremely gracious and accommodating to young children.
A couple blocks away, the excellent restaurant Basics serves just pizza and salad---but oh, what pizza and salad! The other family vacationing with us originally hail from New York, and they proclaimed it the best pizza they've had on the West Coast. Another great recommendation from the front desk!
The location is excellent, only a a few miles away from the San Diego zoo---and a far, far better choice than staying at one of the places on Hotel Circle (especially if you can get a Priceline or Hotwire deal). We will definitely be back!!!

title: “comfortable, safe, cozy, homey, well-working, helpful, cozy”
text: Between Amsterdam Ave and Broadway on 77st. Hudson river on one end, central park on the other. Nice suites. Lot's of food and breakfast right outside the door.

title: “Great Place!”
text: The location is IDEAL for shopping on Michigan Avenue. You are one block away from everything and on the same block as Garrett's popcorn. The rooms were clean and cozy, although ours was a bit chilly. Overall a good place to stay.

title: “Good value - a solid 3 Star”
text: This property is a solid 3 star. I like to stay in a an established hotel chain like a Holiday Inn if they have done a complete renovation. You can get good value and see what their designers have done to improve their worn out hotels to bring them up to date. Our room faced the back so it was very quiet. Older property, so the room is larger and nicely upgraded. Excellent beds, linens and pillows. Our air cooler did not work but that was not a problem for us on a one night stay. We were offered another room but declined.This location is out of the core of the business district but Seattle has easy transit. Close to the Space Needle and various attractions. Front staff friendly. Check in - check out easy. Highly recommend for families traveling or business travelers watching their bottom line. Previous reviews suggest there is "secure" parking? We parked in the underground parking which is very tight parking but it is not garage secured. This is a city folks and there is NO SECURE parking anywhere! Previous reviewer gave this hotel a bad review based on "non working room keys" and "items they left" behind were no longer there. As a seasoned traveler why would you wait 45 minutes in a hallway lobby for a hotel employee to bring up new room keys? I would wait 5 minutes and go down and get new ones? It is our responsibility to check the hotel room for our items before leaving. Hotel cleaners are given directions on what to do with items that they find. If they kept in lost and found all items they would have an entire room full. Important items such as glasses, contact lenses, computers and such I am confident they would keep for possible claim. But other items I would not expect them to keep. We must be realistic travelers.

title: “Great location - Friendly Staff”
text: Fabulous location. Short walk to Petco, the Convention Center, and all that the Gaslamp district has to offer. The gym is tiny (2 ellipticals, 2 treadmills) and so is the pool, but the rooms are comfy and have a full kitchen. I needed an extension cord, but the hotel did not have one so I had to run out to WalMart for that. The staff is friendly and helpful. Included breakfast is quite good, though if you want bacon or sausage you need to ask for that.

title: “Really enjoyed the Catamaran Resort”
text: Beautiful grounds, friendly staff, great location. Would definitely stay here again. Wildlife was fun to watch. Ducks, geese, fish, and the talking parrots. Landscaping makes the whole place feel very peaceful. Pool was nice. Arcade was great for the kids. Restaurant was good-recommend breakfast over dinner. Breakfast was very good and reasonably priced. Dinner was good, but spendy. Rooms were average, but fine. When I booked the room, I asked for a garden room, which I assumed would be in one of the 2 story buildings. We were given a room on the first floor of the tower , which had a patio and would have been fine, except for the constant noise of people coming and going at all hours, late night and early morning. After 2 nights of no sleep, we requested a new room, and were give a new room the next day. The new room was quiet and overlooked one of the ponds-very nice.

title: “A1 Service”
text:
The only thing better than the Bryant Park Hotel's location is their superb level of service. Their moto should be, "ask and you shall receive". 
From friendly & attentive people at check-in, to the concierge going out of their way to help. 
When turn down service came around, they always left a note, telling us to call them back as we had the "do not disburb" sign on. We did, and voila!!!
Great clean spacious rooms, fantastic ambiance, top notch service from employees who went out of their way to help, to great location. This is our second stay with them, and we're sure to go back.
Oh, and we received a free room upgrade, to a junior suite. It was 3 nites of bliss.
BONUS. Free valet parking for Friday & Saturday nites. Need I go on???

title: “5th Anniversary Weekend!!”
text: We go to the Hilton Baltimore every year for our Anniversary but they made it extra special for us this year - our 5th Anniversary!!! My husband absolutely LOVES this hotel - especially the view of the ballfield from their beautiful exercise room!! When we arrived - we were surprised that we had been upgraded for our anniversary to a top floor suite w/all the extras - Champagne and cheese/cracker tray delivery, jacuzzi tub, and executive floor rights! The Hilton Baltimore will be our forever anniversary get-away (except our 10th year - when we go to Bora Bora)!!! Thanks Hilton Baltimore!!!

title: “Great Conference Hotel”
text:
I recently stayed here four nights for a large conference. I found the facilities to be more than adequate, and the experience perfect for my first visit to Boston.
The hotel has a wonderful location. It is right across from the Boston City Garden and the Boston Commons, and very close to iconic Boston dining (eg: Legal Seafoods). We did not have a car until the last night, due to the exorbitant parking rate ($44/night, valet only), but did not really need one anyway (the T station is a block away).
Yes the hotel is old. That is the charm of it. Personally, I loved the classic Boston feel. The lobby is large and elegant, with many hotel reps ready to serve you. One person in particular, named Charles, approached me several times during my stay to answer any questions or concerns I had. I found the service to be top notch.
The rooms are classic and elegant. I slept very well each night I was there, and found the furnishings to be updated and well kept. The bathroom was classic, with vintage checkered tile and fixtures. Still, it was very clean and well ketp.
Overall, I loved my stay, and look forward to returning.

title: “Geat airport hotel!”
text: We were returning from New Zealand and had booked this hotel to spend two nights in Los Angeles to break-up the trip before returning home. We arrived at the hotel in Los Angeles from New Zealand at 8:30 am. When we went to the front desk expecting to store our luggage until the 3 pm check-in, but were pleasantly surprised. The person at the front desk asked if we would like our room now. Being exhausted from the all night flight we told him that would be great. The next day I went to the front desk to get infomation on how to get to downtown LA and Hollywood. They were very helpful and recommended the free LA shuttle bus to the metro and to purchase an all day metro pass. We had a great time. The rooms and the staff at this hotel were excellent. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Great location!”
text: Just stayed for 2 nights. Rooms were small but nice. Property newer and in good condition. Very quiet except for the opening and closing of other room doors. Bathroom was not as clean as it could have been. Found dried toothpaste on counter top and hair on toilet and shower. Nothing a few Lysol wipes couldn't handle. Most front desk folks were helpful and accommodating. One was very so-so - didn't want to be bothered with anything. For example, we wanted to have them hold our luggage on the day of departure and one guy at the desk paged a person to get it. 15 mins later still nobody to take luggage and no offer from front desk guy to do anything about it or re-page the person. We asked a women who appeared at the desk if she wouldn't mind paging the baggage person as we had been waiting and she profusely apologized that we had to wait and came over and took the bags herself - while Mr. can't be bothered just stood there. I would stay here again but it is a bit pricey if your paying regular rate. Great location.

title: “Excellent location for the price!”
text: This hotel was nice and the location close to Michigan Avenue was fantastic! I gave it a 4/5 because the room was very small and smelled a little musky. However, everything was very clean and neat. For the price you can't beat it.

title: “Great rooms”
text: The Southgate Tower rooms are huge compared to other hotels I have stayed in in NYC. The staff could not be nicer. It is a grande hotel and the hustle and bustle of the lobby is invigorating. Perfect if you are attending MSG or want to shop at Macy's. Their newly renovated bar and eatery is so "NEW YORK". Well done.

title: “Perfect Place to Stay in San Francisco”
text: We actually found this on Trip Advisor, and loved the reviews. We were looking for somewhere with close proximity to places we were looking to see. We were also thrilled to have free parking, which is hard to find in San Francisco. The room was really priced fairly. It looked online like they didn't have any rooms the size we needed availble, but with a quick phone call directly to the Columbus Motor Inn we were able to secure exactly the accomodations needed. It is located right on a bus line, and within 2 blocks of cable cars. You can easily walk to Fisherman's Wharf. There were 3 of us and we loved having a suite that had 3 Queen size beds. The 3rd bed was in a separate room with a small balcony off of it. I would never stay anywhere else in San Francisco!

title: “That was funny ...”
text: This has been one of the funniest times I've had in a while. I haven't laughed this hard in a few years ... from the vacuum cleaner in my face to when I walked in to the lumpy sandpaper beds to the 3ft leaf ridden pool to the semi-tropical/antartica air conditioner going off and on all night to the super efficient processed cookie cutter eggs and sausage patties to the I can't wait to get the hell out of here check-out. Other than that, it was great!

title: “Ideal for a stop over night before flight”
text:
Very close to LAX. Good value for a large hotel. We stayed 1 night before catching a flight. We just wanted a comfortable hotel where we could relax, order room service and watch a movie. This hotel provided that. We had a good night sleep considering we could see the runways from our room. It was very quiet.
It's a typical large hotel so don't expect character but it is very close to Manhatten beach in the car which is well worth a visit if you have time.

title: “Life in NYC”
text:
My mother and I stayed for almost a week in July and we loved our time at Morgans. Its location is convenient, with several major bus routes on its doorstep, plus Grand Central station nearby. We snapped up a Superior Room at an excellent price through Expedia, and the room was definitely spacious by NYC standards. The design made good use of the available space, and it was nice to have a built-in couch by the window. The bathroom was on the small side, but we loved the decor and the rain shower. The toiletries were good quality. 
The complimentary breakfast was served in the penthouse. The views upstairs are better, however seating downstairs is more comfortable. We were glad to be able to catch some tennis (Wimbledon was on) on one of the several TVs available while enjoying the excellent pastries on offer, as well as the yoghurt, juice, tea and coffee. Don't expect a European-style full buffet, but it is a good continental breakfast which certainly kept us full until dinnertime each day.
Staff were always friendly and welcoming and took care of the little details.
I can best describe the hotel as being like having our own chic NYC apartment to come home to each day, rather than staying at a "normal" hotel, which is a great way to experience NYC.

title: “Brad Wright- San Clemente CA”
text: We travel extensively, a by product of our profession. Our lifestyle and profession allows us to visit properties all over the world. We love Los Angeles and any chance we have to do business or visit L.A. we savor and appreciate the opportunity. Recently we stayed at the Luxe Hotel Sunset Blvd. Nestled hillside right off the 405 at Sunset. We'll just say....... unplanned privacy.... boutique........ impeccable service and rooms... Bel Air......affordable elegance............Romantic......and awesome customer service....... everyone knew our names by hour 2 thru 48.....Mr and Mrs. Wright....my Fiancée was quite flattered and entertained by this. It's a good stay and we took in Carlos Santana and Herbie Hancock at the Hollywood Bowl they went 95% instrumental and Carlo's wife stole the show on the .....DRUMS........she spike it stab it jailed it and waled away with the sway of the performers.

title: “Excellence service”
text: Staying nereby always on Hilton Hotels during my travel, it was a great pleasure to be back at New York Hilton. We always try to stay and enjoy in the Executive Area. The new Executive lounge is fantastic with nice and very helpful staff. The Executive Floor is well serviced. This Hotel is in the hart of New York with easy access to entire Manhattan in few minuts with neighbouring Metro. Very recommendable place to stay.

title: “Dark & with a Markup”
text:
The Clift lobby was very dark and cool. Staff was always pleasant, but not overly friendly. The PYT's who double as doormen could stand to be a little more attentive (they often failed to open the doors and managed to hail a cab for us that would only go to Oakland - we were headed to Russian Hill!). 
The room we had was smallish, but not at all uncomfortable - mirrors almost everywhere helped to maintain the illusion the room was a little bigger than it was. The room was very clean, and the bed and pillows in particular, were super comfortable. 
Shower pressure and temperature were perfect - almost too powerful on both counts! And the toiletries provided smelled great and worked well. I'm still using the body milk and hoping to find something comparable.
We were surprised the Clift charges $10 a day for internet for this high-end of a hotel. Room service is expected to be exhorbitant - but still was much more than expected with extra fees tacked on.
The location was great though - everywhere we wanted to go was easily accessed on foot or nearby public transportation. I'd be happy to stay at the Clift again.

title: “Perfect place for a family trip to San Diego”
text:
Brand new place located 10mn from Downtown San Diego.
Ideal for families. very large and comfortable suites. Very quiet and clean area.
To be recommended.

title: “Great hotel for a family vacation”
text: Not sure why this hotel gets sucjh poor reviews. Our 2 rooms were in the tower and were clean and well kept. We were on a high floor so the views were fantastic. The three pools and marshmellows roasts were favorites of our three teenage grand daughters. The concierge provided them wiht many beach activity options. The private boat to Sea World was also nice. This was the girls first trip to the West coast and the proximity to the ocean made for a great vacation. Lots restaurants in all price ranges close by as well. Locatio, Location, Location says it all.

title: “Unbeatable location”
text: The number one perk of the Broadway at Times Square is its location. Located 30 seconds from Times Square's epicentre, the hotel is a great value for what it offers. We were transferred here after the Ramada East Side, one of its partner hotels, ran out of rooms and chose to honour our reservation at this hotel. The rooms are very small yet comfortable and clean, with a closet to store suitcases. Breakfast is included, which is a huge plus as it saves you both the time and money of getting breakfast in New York. Highly recommended option for a stay near Times Square.

title: “Average Hotel, Great Location”
text:
We stayed one night in the smallest double room available at the Hard Rock. The hotel was fine, nothing special. The public areas are definitely nicer than the rooms. The staff was very nice and helpful in person.
They twice misquoted prices over the phone for--once we were told an extra cot costs $15 (it actually cost $25), and on another phone call we were told it costs $30 to use the valet and park overnight (it actually cost $46). I'm not sure what was going on there with the incorrect price quotes, and when we told them in person that we were misinformed over the phone they just stared back at us. That was a bit strange. 
Both bedside lamps did not work when we arrived in the room, but an employee was sent up immediately to replace the bulbs, so that was an impressive response. We were also granted a late check-out without any hassle, as well. (Although, the "front desk" button on our phone somehow went directly to housekeeping, and they were a bit rude and obviously irritated that we reached them both times that we made a call from the room.)
The walls in this hotel are very thin, we were woken by a screaming baby at 5:30 in the morning, and heard those wails for the next several hours. We could also hear everyone's conversations as they passed our room in the hall. We didn't mind as we weren't there for a relaxing weekend, but I wouldn't recommend this hotel for anyone who wants peace and quiet. You can hear everything going on around you.
We were pleasantly surprised to receive a code good for 10 free iTunes downloads upon checkout. 
The total cost was just over $250 for one night which seems a bit high for such an average room. If the price matched the room better I would have given this hotel a higher rating.

title: “Wonderful stay at Humphrey's”
text: Huge room, clean, comfy with wonderful views of the harbor. The grounds were beautiful, you felt you were in a lush tropical garden. The staff were friendly and very helpful. I always keep up with the entertainment they have, a wide variety of venues - could go back a dozen times if I had the time.

title: “Somewhere to sleep”
text:
We stayed in this hotel expecting the worse and actually it wasn't
that bad, ok it could do with a facelift but who goes to new york to sit in their hotel room? its just somewhere to get your head down and refuel for the next day. Also you can't beat the location of this hotel in fact we've booked again for this year.

title: “Good hotel, trapped in time”
text: No complaints, but as one other user pointed out, the decor in the Arena Hotel is very dated. Lots of berry and green and brass and wood. Anyway, I stay at this hotel frequently on business because of its excellent location right in downtown on the Alameda and only a couple of minutes away from the Arena and the train station. There is a CVS pharmacy next door, several restaurants down the street within walking distance, and the hotel serves a full hot breakfast every morning. I like that the hotel has 24 hour reception and security at night, unlike a motel. The rooms are big and comfy (make sure to ask for a room with a carpeted floor instead of the renovated rooms with laminate flooring), and each time I get one with a big jacuzzi tub that I never use. There is also a guest laundry on the 2nd floor that other guests seem to never use. Plenty of free parking. If you need to rent a car, there is an Enterprise location across the street and down a few blocks. Very quiet and the staff is always friendly and accommodating.

title: “This must be the worst hotel in New York”
text: The level of service here (I write from my very-much run-down room) sets a new low standard. Try calling reception, or the concierge.....50 rings....no answer. Try taking an elevator.......you MAY get one today. The rooms are old and tired. For over $500 a night this is an absolute travesty.

title: “Fantastic Service, Beautiful Hotel!”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights in mid November 2011. 
The location of the hotel is excellent - a short subway ride from Logan Airport to Copley Station (1 transfer) and the hotel is a minutes walk from the station exit.
The hotel backs onto Newbury Street which is full of dining options as well as fantastic shopping. The Prudential centre shopping mall is a few blocks down from the hotel and a great place to explore for a few hours.
The atmosphere in the hotel is fantastic and from the moment we were greeted by the doormen on arrival to the moment we checked out we felt at home. During check-in, the concierge noted that we were in Boston for a birthday trip and brought up a birthday card and chocolate cake on our first night to allow us to celebrate. It was an unexpected but lovely surprise!
We were also given an upgrade and were in a beautiful superior room on the 9th floor which provided lovely views across the back-bay area. The rooms were large and clean with a 32" television and 2 double beds. The room also had a fridge which was free to use for guests and each morning they fill it with complimentary bottles of water. The bathroom was luxuriously kitted out and included aveda bath products. 
We understand some reviews have noted the decor is old-fashioned and in need of an upgrade, however, we felt this added to the charm of staying in a period hotel.
The turndown service each night was a lovely touch and we looked forward to our chocolate truffle each night!
The hotel has 2 bars/restaurants inside it and also had a reasonably-priced room service menu. 
Each morning the lobby provides complimentary coffee for guests, and in the evening they provide a complimentary "seasonal treat" (apple cider and cookies whilst we were there).
Overall, we would certainly recommend this hotel for anybody looking for a base to explore the wonderful city of Boston. We would, hower advise to look for deals was we got our room for a fantastic price by booking through our airline - deals are out there so check before you book.

title: “great location, good price, large room with fridge”
text:
This is not the nicest place I've stayed in New York but it was great. It is not a luxury hotel. It is an older motel with large rooms, comfortable furnishings, large closets, and a refrigerator and microwave in the room. It is not elegant but it is clean and well-maintained. It is air-conditioned by a window unit which can leave the bathroom stuffy after a shower and can be a bit noisy. Neither was a big concern for us. The housekeeping staff was very responsive to our request for additional towels and remembered each day that we were there. 
It is in a great location. Walking distance from lots and a subway station on the corner. We would definitely stay here again... it is exactly what we wanted for a weekend trip with our daughter.

title: “Very Good Hotel, Great Location”
text: very good hotel - great location, concierge extremely helpful, decor is nice and the maid service was excellent (room was cleaned by the time we got back from breakfast each morning). They have coffee in the morning and wine hour each evening in the lobby. The location is great, 2 blocks from FW and 5-6 blocks from really good italian food in North Beach and Chinatown is in that area as well. The only problem we had was on our last day; we were awoken at 6am by the banging on the roof (they were trying to fix the boiler or something) when I called the front desk all they could say was, sorry (we had stayed on the top floor). Also, if you have a rental car, do not park there, it's upwards of $40 per day (with taxes) - park around the block at a pay garage which i think the sign said was $14 max per day. I had asked for late check out of 130pm and that was not a problem. Also, take the shuttle to the airport which is only $15 per person as opposed to taxi which is $40 each way.

title: “Outdated but good location”
text: The rooms here are outdated and felt musty to me. We stayed here because we were attending a conference in the hotel. They charged me $ for a package I had delivered which I have never encountered before at any hotel. The location is amazing and that is the big plus to this hotel. It was expensive due to the conference and I would expect more for that price. They need to renovate!

title: “Convenient 4 the arts, do not expect room to be cleaned tho”
text:
Very convenient hotel for the kimmel center, and other venues on avenue of the arts. However, getting your room cleaned appears to be not so convenient - as it did not happen for us (and the do not disturb sign was not on the door). 
Average hotel - nothing flashy.
