title: “A great destination area in LA”
text: I beleive this hotel and the entire LA Live complex was built less than two years ago. It's been a few years since I was in LA last and was expecting a dirty downtown experince as it was last time. WRONG! The city, developers and others have made this complex a destination worth visiting solely on its merits. Add in the surrounding attractions, theme parks beaches, etc.its hard to beat. Within the area of the hotel is the Nokia Theater, Staples Center and a number of great restaurants. Lots of activity. The hotel itself was very clean and comfortable. Staff was helpful and freindly.

title: “Excellent loaction, attractive design, small rooms”
text:
The location of this hotel is excellent, right across from the Boston Commons and the freedom trail, and very convenient to public transportation. 
The rooms are very attractive, but quite small. The beds were comfortable, and the airconditioning welcome. The room comes with free wi-fi, a big plus in my book, and a wine reception in the early evening. The staff was helpful.

title: “Not bad, but not great.”
text:
This isn't too bad of a place to stay. We have stayed here two years in a roll when we come to a convention in San Diego. The first year I went it was an okay experience. What I liked most was the staff was really friendly. There was construction although that you could hear starting at about 8 am each morning. This didn't bother us because we were getting up early. The breakfast is just juice, coffee and muffins. Simple but okay. The pool is really nice.
Our most recent stay in July was not so great as the first. I paid $139 for each night in a regular 1 bed room. The construction from last year was STILL being completed.
Our second morning there, our bathroom ceiling started leaking badly. The manager was not nice to us and didn not even apologize. We were given a new room in about an hour. But it was quite a hassle having to wait so long to use the restroom and shower - not to mention repacking and moving rooms. The manager's customer service was very poor. I was extremely disappointed how she treated her guests. We were not given an apology or any type of discount for the inconvience.
A new thing this year was they installed locks on the doors (they did not have them last year). So the added security was nice.
Our second room had crappy lighting, and you don't have many options of TV channels. The cable is really limited. The TV's do not have VCR's, nor can you attach your own (the TV's have no imputs).
Their blankets are kind of thin, so we always bring an extra one.

title: “Awesome Hotel - Fantastic Value”
text: The people at the hotel were extremely helpful with checkin, with the odd questions we asked, and also with our checkout. We were very pleasantly surprised by the room, it was extremely clean, and well appointed. It was the best night's sleep we've ever had staying at a hotel. We would most definitely recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a great value, extreme comfort, and very helpful and knowledgeable staff. The hotel had easy access to the freeway which helped since we aren't from that area. The hotel is located in the heart of Silicon Valley, and was conveniently located between San Jose and Santa Clara.. making everything you could want within a short walking/driving distance. And for those needing a hotel near the airport I would recommend this one, it even has a shuttle for your convenience. It's handicap accessible, and offers high speed internet, a pool, fitness room, business center, restaurant and bar/lounge. A 5 Star Hotel in our opinion.

title: “Good hotel, close to everything”
text:
Rooms where spacious, soundproof and clean, with a small kitchen which we didn't use.
The breakfast is complimentary, good quality and simple but everything to fill myself with energy for the they is there.
The complimentary drinks and food on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thurday were very good to socialize with other hotelmates. Wine (red and white) and beer (Budlight and Stella) and softdrinks could be drunk as much as you like.
Public transport is very close.
Free WLAN.
In the basement there are 3 wahing machine and tumble dryer which can be used for free.
The 24h market at the reception is also handy and not expensive in case you would like some drinks, snack or ice cream.
Only downside is the elevator for which you sometimes had to wait several minutes.
And there was only a shower for those who like to take a bath

title: “We simply loved it”
text:
The New York Palace is one of our favourites hotels in the world. We stayed for 1 week in March in one of the Tower rooms with amazing skyline view and extra concierce desk. The service was simply outstanding and our stay could not have been any better!
We ate in the GILT restaurant and although it was not the best meal we had in New York City, it was a very special evening in a stunning dining room with very good food and excellent wine.
We will definitely stay at the Palace again.

title: “Great Location”
text: We recently stayed at this hotel and were so glad we chose this hotel. I too booked many months in advance (which is always wise when traveling to SF). I took the advice of other guests and called to inquire about where our room would be (noise etc). We were given a room on the top floor (804) and there was no issue with noise other than noise from a busy city (to be expected). We had a great view from our room, but others in our group did not, they had a view of a brick wall. The hotel was willing to move them to the 8th floor if they so desired, which was great considering everything was pretty well booked up. The room was very clean, adorably appointed and we felt very secure. Yes, the elevator is old but so is the city, just added another layer of charming as far as I am concerned. The location could not be beat. Steps to Chinatown, many shops on stockton and union square, the cable cars and on and on. The staff was fantastic at accommodating requests and always did so with a smile. The free breakfast was pretty standard continental fare but did the job. We did not go to the tavern a lot, found the drinks and food pretty pricey, but a person should have one drink at least ( try the monkey gland or the grumpy uncle just to say you did!) This was our 3rd trip to SF and probably the best, great hotel and the location added much enjoyment to the trip!

title: “Stayed here two years in a row”
text:
Because the hotel location is very convenient. Staff is great and they serve Starbucks coffee in the morning. Complimentary breakfast offers a good variety of choices. However, the rooms are small and we have to have two rooms for four people. 
Location: It is only two blocks from Times Square. It's across the street from the Port Authority bus station and six blocks from Penn Stn. Subway station is just around the corner. Bryant Park is about 3 blocks away. Central Park is at 8th Ave and 59th St. The hotel is at 8th Ave and 40th St. We walked to Central Park every morning and it was a good walk. As other reviewers mentioned, the street between 8th and 9th Ave has a rough appearence/feel but I feel completely safe even at 10pm.
Food: many choices near the hotel from cheap eats to "need-a-second-mortage"! Cheap eat - John's pizza. Need a second mortage to eat at Inayka (on 40th St just across from 8th Ave) and Keene's on 34th or 36th St. Both good but expensive. Not something I'd do at home but a good treat on vacation. Also had lunch at Becco's which was ok. There are lots of restaurants on 9th Ave between 40th and 55th. My friend was going to take us to Room Service (Thai food) on 9th Ave but the wait was too long. Maybe next time.
We flew into Newark and caledl Dial 7 for a private cab at the airport. Fare was $58 inluding tolls. It took about an hour during rush hour.
We flew out of JFK and again used Dial 7. I think the fare was about $55. There is a $4 off coupon in one of the NYC tourist magazine. It took about 45 min. If you don't have lots of luggages, the E train (I believe) takes you there for $2!

title: “Lovely hotel close to the tourist sughrs”
text: Great hotel located within easy walking to the whitehouse, washinton monument, Lincoln memorial & GW university, as well as a metro stop close by. Staff were helpful & the room was very nice & also had a kitchen. Only complaint was wifi only available in the lobby.

title: “I will go back for sure!!”
text:
The staff is the best!! I was traveling solo for the 1st time in my life and I have to admit I was a little scared. Those feelings were gone in the 1st hour. The staff is by far the greatest! 
This hotel is not in the main hub of the Riverwalk. I liked it that way....very easy to get around either shuttle $4.00 all day! Or walking...riverboat or taxi! I highly recommend this hotel!!

title: “Nice HGI”
text: I just stayed one night while in town on business. The hotel is updated nicely, just like most all the HGI's. The room was clean, updated, and comfortable. They had a very nice gym/fitness center. It included cardio equip, weights, and a cable machine. I would recommend staying here if you are in the Jacksonville area.

title: “Surprised”
text:
Thought this was going to be a disaster based off of previous reviews, but very surprised. Hotel is clean and quiet. Staff is friendly, easy check in and out, and valet parking($16) 
This is not the Four Seasons, but in this price range its the best you will find in San Francisco.

title: “This hotel is wonderful. The service and staff is excellent.”
text: I would highly recommend this hotel. Exceptional staff, service and the restaurant is unbelievable.

title: “It's LOCATION & STAFF That Makes This Hotel...”
text:
The room was slightly above average. We have stayed in numerous Hilton Garden Inns that far exceed the rooms here.
But, someone has done an exceedingly marvelous job training the staff here to be thoughtful, courteous, helpful, kind and friendly. I encountered many employees on our floor going about their duties. Every time they would step to the side, stop, speak in a friendly a.d warm tone and yield the "right-away" to guests. I have NEVER seen a more smiley, warm and friendly staff in any hotel, even another Hilton.

title: “fab hotel”
text: I liked this hotel it was small very frindly staff and helpfull . there is no added luxarys in the rooms, the rooms are small . breakfast was good but service was slow . would stay her again .

title: “Service”
text: The hotel was great but the young lady at the front desk during check out was rude. She was very upset. I ask about a reward card and she didn't want to answer the questions. To be honest my wife told me she didn't want to stay there again. So great hotel but because of her poor customer service we will not stay there again. Sorry

title: “Somewhat disappointed”
text:
After staying in a 3-star hotel for a 3-day vacation, we checked in to Hilton for the work event. I was excited to get here, since this hotel is rated as 4-star, and is located right on the beach. Long story short, we were quite disappointed.
Sure, the rooms themselves were nice, the beds comfortable, the TV with digital cable has a good assortment of channels, in addition to the pay per view ones. The AC is quiet The towels are nice and thick, the bed linens are luxurious, and the furniture looks nice. The decorations in the rooms are tasteful. Our room had a balcony, from which we could see the beach. But... the bed uses flat, not fitted sheets, which get untucked with the blanket (remember that Seinfeld episode?). The armchair was uncomfortable, with the seat completely horizontal and the back reclined backwards, and no foot stool to rest your feet on, so when you sit on it, you slide forward.The hallways are plain and old, and look outdated. Our low-rise building had no elevator. I believe there is also a tower, which will likely have the elevators.
The part of Mission Bay that the hotel fronts is completely still, and carries little of the allure of the ocean front, While there are nice walking paths along the shore, this is not the place to enjoy the surf.
Now to the things that really get me - the room has no wireless internet, and while there is a wired connection in the room (not good for my tablet, cell phone, or computer without an RJ45 port), it costs $15 per day to use. Breakfast, should you choose to accept it, is nearly $20 per person. A non-optional expense, if you come with a car, as I did, is parking, which is a whopping $32 per night. Unlike hotels in busy urban areas, which have to share public parking, this hotel has abundant parking on property, so it is just a way to separate guests from their money. I feel they have to disclose this during the booking time. 
The staff were mostly helpful. But this does not take away from the feeling of being taken advantage of by the hotel. If the price is right, I might stay here again, but for over $200 a night, I think I can find a better beachfront hotel.
I would not really recommend it.

title: “fantastic stay at the southgate towers”
text: We stayed at the southgate for 3 nights at the end of march. We got a very nice welcome form the girl at the front desk and my request for a room with a view was accomadated. When we walked into the room, a 1 bedroom suite, we were very impressed. The room was much larger than we expected and was very clean and comfortable. We also had a great view of the empire state building. The kitchenette was small but more than adequate. As others have mentioned the beds are to die for. When I mentioned to the front desk that we were on a round the world trip I was told there is a guest laundry that we could use if we needed it. I don't think that this is told about very often and it is in the basement where the staff are working so if you need it make sure to ask to be shown where it is. It was a god send to us. The concierge would ahve to be the most helpful I have ever come across and although they were extremely busy they always took the time to help with my questions and directions. The location of the hotel is fantastic. We caught the subway from penn station across the road to everywhere we needed to go. All in all we had a very enjoyable stay at the southgate thanks to the friendliness of all the staff. I cannot reccomend this hotel enough.

title: “Yes!”
text:
We had to change our hotel due to Sandy. 
Because of his London sisters hotels, although not cheap, we gave this hotel a chance.
And yes, it is like many reviewers stated.
The reception and welcome are like you expected in a friendly way, the neigbourhood and the street are so good. The concierge was the one every hotel is looking for. 
There is a room for the guests where they can zip a glass, take a snap (like a bar with sofas).
The rooms are great with floor-to-ceiling windows, decoration in style for anyone who is classic, but also for anyone who likes more the modern things. 
Bathroom is clean and functional (by the way: good products).
The breakfast is a very good buffet (unfortanetely no normal bread) or there is a a-la-carte possibility.
One more thing, after one week I still remember the nice smell of the hallway.

title: “Who could ask for anything more!”
text:
We arrived at 8:00AM expecting to drop our luggage and go. To our surprise a room was available which was great as we needed to freshen up as we were on the go since 3:00AM. The room was very nice and comfortable. We were so impressed with the decor, not to mention the view of the city and Bryant Park.
The location was another reason we had choose this hotel. Minutes from most of the places we wanted to see. 
The best part about Bryant Park Hotel is the excellent service we received during our entire stay. The staff were so friendly and helpfull, it was incredible. For that reason we will always stay here when we visit New York. Thank you so much!!
Daniel and Dorothy Gaudet

title: “ELEVATOR PROBLEMS!!”
text:
Hotel was a disappointment in that I think of Doubletree as a suite hotel. It is not. Room was relatively small and definitely overpriced - even with an on-line bargain rate. I find it annoying as hotels charge for internet as an extra. That is the equivalent these days of charging for use of the television or shower. No fridge - but a minibar that is sensor activated. According to the warning sign , if your kid even touches (not takes) something the charge shows up on your bill. But the worst issue is the non-functioning elevator bank. The hotel was full and with only 3 (maybe 2) elevators functioning, the wait was nearly 20 minutes! Especially for lower floors because the small elevator was full by the time it got below the 15th floor. Apparently this was not an unusual occurrence. We asked a staff member who just rolled his eyes and said "always" This is unacceptable. 
Place was clean, staff friendly, but I would probably not choose to stay here again and would not recommend unless they figure out a way to address the elevator problem. I have never seen anything this bad anywhere, and I travel a lot!

title: “Liked the decor of the room.”
text:
I liked the anime wall prints that decorated the room. It added a nice touch. Also, liked the colorful yellow linens and the window seat. The art on the wall was also different and nice. 
I didn't like the bathroom. It was dark and looked like it needed to be remodeled. Also the TV remote didn't really work. The hotel looks like it's in the process of reinovating and will get better in a few years. 
It was a good place to stay that was affordable for a one night in SF.

title: “Excellent service all around!”
text:
Sheila and Edward were both amazingly wonderful with how they took care of us with the Hotel's shuttle service. They were both so very friendly and just amazing employees there.
Speaking of which, every employ there seems to work so hard as they don't just handle one job but multiple ones. VERY hard working people.

title: “Beautiful New Hotel in Downtown Detroit”
text:
I lucked out with finding a great rate on hotwire for this hotel while I was on a research trip in Detroit. The valet parking was great, as was the cleanliness and layout of the large suites. While the hotel's not in the best part of town - it's important to remember that Detroit has quite a desolate and empty downtown, although hardly an unsafe district (just empty) - and the hotel itself was in what seemed like a very safe area, about a minute from the nearby People Mover station. The round bar restaurant was also a good place to grab a quick bite to eat. 
The room itself was very large and well appointed. High speed internet was free and fast, and it felt more like a 'home' than your regular hotel. The hallways were clean, and the hotel was very quiet - I slept incredibly.
I'd recommend this hotel to anybody and will be staying here whenever I'm in the city. One can quickly get to any of the downtown Detroit restaurants and amenities without having to drive around. If you're considering staying in the suburbs, I'd recommend staying downtown - for all of the problems that Detroit has had and is having, they're genuinely trying to improve the city!

title: “Amazing Stay”
text:
Had an amazing experience at this hotel. Was the perfect hotel for my first trip to New York City 
I would defiantly get a park view room we made the mistake not making sure of this ahead of time. One great perk about the hotel you get private access to the residents only park.. and it is amazing!!! Truly New York at its best. The restaurant was amazing as were all the bars and the roof top. (although the roof top could use a little updating with less fake vines.). I would stay here again and again heck I would live here if I could.

title: “Average business hotel”
text: Nicely renovated rooms and accommodating staff but the hotel lacks a lobby to sit down in (perhaps that will change after the public area renovations are complete) and no business center to print a document from. The internet connections are absolutely horrible and should be included in the room rate. For a fee - it should be fast, reliable service. It's almost impossible to do business from your room. Even the wired service is horrible. The Hotel restaurant is really just average even with its lovely views of San Francisco Bay. The hotel has a great location. You can walk to almost everything.

title: “worth the money.”
text: Central location good view, big rooms and kitchen, very accomidating staff and keen to help where they could including getting us a town car back to the airport for no extra charge. Hotel resturant was average and overpriced, my wife ordered a French Onion soup and it came with an inch of mozerella melted on the top (this is New YOur I suppose)

title: “Convenient but dated.”
text:
For people visiting the Merchandise Mart there is no more convenient hotel, it's actually connected at the second floor. It also has great views of the Chicago River. That said, the rooms are beginning to show the age of the building and could use an updating. However the people were friendly the convenience is hard to beat. 
Concern: if you drive to Chicago, the fact that this hotel does not have its own parking garage is a concern. I had to park outside in an uncovered adjacent public parking lot and after having my car broken into during my last trip to Chicago, I really worried about the lack of an guarded garage or valet parking. Fortunately I was lucky but this is a concern.

title: “A relaxing, luxurious resort in the middle of nowhere”
text: I stayed at the RBI when I was on a 3-day conference, and I enjoyed the ambiance of the place. The Spanish colonial decor is very in keeping with the area. The grounds are beautiful, with Mediterranean courtyards and fountains. There are four computers for guest use, two in the lobby and two in the cafe, and a big flat screen TV in the room. The food served at the receptions was good, but not great--too many fried things. I did not have a chance to try the spa or the El Bizcocho Restaurant, but the food served at the bar was decent and very reasonably priced. The Veranda Restaurant was closed for remodeling. The property is rather remote, well off the freeway in the middle of a residential neighborhood, so it is not a place to stay if you are in the area for sightseeing or nightlife, but for a relaxing escape, this is the place!

title: “I will be back!”
text: I have been to NY a bunch of times but never stayed in the heart of Times Square. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay! The hotel was awesome and the staff was exceptional, especially Amanda! I would definitely would stay here again!

title: “Great Hotel from MCRD Graduation”
text: The hotel was a great location for the MCRD San Diago Graduation and family day. THe shuttle service was free and also offered shuttle service to area attractions. The pool was great and heated. Breakfast was great as well. We traveled with family and a small child and had everything we needed.

title: “Good location”
text: The Omni Hotel was in a good location with easy access to the downtown area. The hotel was fine, staff were nice but the beds were very uncomfortable and I had a back ache for 2 days. I can't remember the last time I got back pain after staying in a nice hotel. Overall the stay was fine but nothing spectacular.

title: “Stately San Francisco classic.”
text: My teenaged daughter and I spent a girl's getaway weekend at the Fairmont San Francisco and thoroughly enjoyed the hotel. We had a room with a bay view, huge walk in closet, high ceilings and very comfortable beds. The bathroom amenities were rather minimal, only shampoo, conditioner, bath gel, hand (bar) soap and body lotion, all in very small containers. They were definitely adequate for a short stay however. Room service was very pleasant and fairly quick. The hotel's location atop Nob Hill was fabulous but made for some steep walks in and out. The opulent lobby is truly gawk-worthy and fun to sit in to watch the world go by. All in all, I would definitely return to this lovely San Francisco institution.

title: “Great hotel, staff, service and location”
text: I've stayed at this Embassy more than once and have never had a bad experience. The staff has always been friendly and helpful. No problems with the accomodations and the rooms are surprisingly quiet on the State St. side, considering the volume of traffic. The hotel is very close to just about everything downtown including great restaurants, entertainment, museums, night clubs etc. Oh, and only 3 blocks from Michigan Ave. The concierge's are quite knowledgeable and anxious to help. Be sure to make use of them for help with your trip and take advantage of the free breakfast and Managers happy hour.

title: “Lovely old hotel and very well maintained. I would love to return.”
text: The hotel is a great classic place to stay in downtown Chicago. Location is perfectly near State street, the Art Institue, and many restaurants. The lobby is fantastically restored. While we did not have a drink in the lobby, we did have a cocktail in Potter's Lounge. My kids enjoyed the pool although it was quite small if you are looking to do laps in the morning. I was a bit disappointed to find that the gym was an extra charge.

title: “Good value, location. Accepts large dogs too!”
text: Received great weekend rate at this hotel--$150 total for a deluxe room with AAA membership. Staff was friendly and helpful. The deluxe rooms are large and include a balcony and sofa. The sweet sleeper bed was fantastic--we just wanted to lay in bed all day! The hotel is also great if you have a large dog to bring along. They didn't even charge us the $25 pet fee. All in all, a great place to stay--especially if you want to bring your pet.

title: “Above Average-But not centrally located”
text:
My family of 5 stayed here July 13-17,2005. We checked in early at 2:00pm, with no wait at all (When we left Sunday, early check-ins were coming in at 1pm, but there was a long,moving, line). One problem I did encounter at check-in was we had reserved a 2 bed room, plus rollaway. I had received an email from Hilton Reservattions stating the rollaway was at no charge, and even presented it to the clerk. He stated they made a mistake and the charge was $25/night. I was tired from the long flight and did not feel like arguing, but I will be sending a complaint letter to Hilton Cutomer Service.
The room was average size ( I actually expected smaller by the reports I had read), and the bathroom is cramped, but workable. The beds are VERY comfortable, probably the best I have slept on away from home. Our remote control was missing, and they sent one up immediately, with a coupon for more cookies for our trouble (Those cookies are GREAT !). The rollaway took 2 calls to finally get it delievered, and it was beat-up, but fine. The ice machine was broken the first day we were there, but fixed later, but I found it interesting that it is tucked away in the storage/housekeeping area, and I probably could have moved one of the rollaways stored in this area to my room and save the 25 bucks !
Our room was 1407, and had a very obstructed view of the hotel next door, but we did not need a view, and it likely kept the noise down. I agree with the earlier post, the gap at the bottom of the door is ridiculously large, allowing too much light and hallway noise in. Placing a towel in it at night resolved this issue.
We did not eat in the hotel, as it was never busy, and I would like to see more people eating there to feel that it is worth it. The Cafe Metro next door, and other close cafes were more that adequate for a good breakfast.
Location is the only problem we had, we will likely pick a more centrally located hotel next time.The Lexington line subway is right outside the door, and this was great going to Battery Park/Statue of Liberty, but not so for Times Square/etc. My wife and I did discover that going east, instead of heading to central Manhattan, that there is a plethra of great bars to visit. I would highly recommend JD's, an Irish Pub, I think near 53 (52nd?), between Lexington and 3rd Ave. A great Irish bartender gave us great insight to the city, and the atmosphere was great.
Overall, I little pricey for what we got, but clean and staff was average.

title: “Nice”
text: Cheap, clean, and the staff was really nice! Free hot breakfast too!

title: “Loved the Iroquois”
text:
"A Little Bit of Heaven in New York City"
We spent a weekend in hectic New York City around the Christmas holidays and had a wonderful experience I would like to share with everyone. We started out expecting to run into some problems, my husband and I and my daughter and her husband - from the time I booked the Iroquois everything went very smooth and very professional. When we got there I asked if perhaps we could get an upgrade and GUESS WHAT! they had a suite open and offered it to us at a minimal cost and we took it -WHAT A JOY!
Beautiful, clean and everthing we needed at our fingertips - the staff was very professional, offering us our privacy but taking care of all our needs. I loved it. The lounge and the restaurant are superb. I can't tell you the feeling of being in a hectic, busy city and feeling like you are at a bed and breakfast in the country. Quiet and cozy. The beds are especially comfy. I highly recommend the suite for comfort and room. I can't wait to go to the Iroquois again.

title: “Wonderful, unique place, but do not expect to use the internet, which is incredible at those prices”
text:
Hotel Bel Air is a stunning, a gorgeous property with outstanding service and amenities, on par with the very best hotels in the world. 
However, it suffers from one serious and incomprehensible issue. 
Even the Premium connection does not allow much more than email, and you may as well get rid of the "complimentary" one as it hardly can load Google (!). Most times, I cannot even load your connection page! 
I think it's a major issue that you should solve asap, as in 2012 all professionals (even on vacation) need a reasonably fast internet connection (and are used to fiber optic connection in a hotel like yours)
I honestly never saw a slower connection, in any hotel I've been in for the past 8 years or so. Test show it ranges from 0,1 to 0,8 Mg download...which is way below the cheapest DSL on the market today. 
Now all premium hotels are above 10 Mg, and even most cheap hotels. 
It's really hard to understand why you would not invest in internet, given the rest of the suite has the latest technologies. And a $2000/night price tag! 
Also, property is located in Los Angeles, not on some remote Pacific Island, where you would have to pull a cable from 5,000 miles away. 
In my case, I have to check out tomorrow as it's impossible to do any work, while I would have gladly stayed 3 weeks waiting from my new house to be completed.

title: “Secret palace”
text: Booked reservation online only seeing the pictures on their website. Very impressed! Clean, close to everything, high end, luxurious! Breakfast was from 0630-0930 amazing for the traveler with a varied schedule! Great military rate and friendly staff. Literally blocks from Valley High gate at Lackland. 10 minutes from downtown. Would definitely stay again!

title: “OUTSTANDING HOTEL AND STAFF”
text:
The hotel staff were very helpful and extremely pleasant. On my first ,morning there, I realized I had left my cufflinks at home. One of the staff at the front desk went back into the offices and came back with a brand new pair of W cufflinks for me to wear. He truly saved the day! (I dropped them off at the front desk when I was checking out for some other forgetful soul!) 
The lobby setting was very, very cool and my room was excellent as well. A 10 if the scale would go that high!!
Thank you and your staff for making my two days there so enjoyable.

title: “Home away from home”
text:
I stayed at the Residence Inn last month. It was comfortable, the rooms were spacious. The highlight was the free buffet breakfast!!...especially since the weather outside was freezing!!
Wish there was a doorman though..to help with the bags. This is a great hotel for persons who are frequent visitors to newyork..not first timers!!...Concierge service is not very evident!!

title: “Fantastic in every way”
text: We were exhausted after flying a red eye into Phoenix. We were picked up via complimentary shuttle at the airport and allowed to check in at 8:30 AM, almost unheard of. They then offered us complimentary breakfast upon check in. If you don't want to rent a car, this hotel is perfectly located not far from Chase Field and a number of restaurants. The room was spacious, beautifully appointed, and provided numerous amenities including FREE internet, a fitness room, and a more than adequate pool. Overall an A+++.

title: “Perfect hotel with a phenomenal location!”
text: You can stay right at the hotel and enjoy some of the best champagne and french food in Seattle, or you can walk a couple of blocks down to some of the best shopping around. Pike Place Market is literally 20 feet away and anything you need is close by. Without a doubt the best place to stay in seattle and the friendliness of the staff makes it an easy choice for me whenever I travel to seattle.

title: “Clean, Comfortable, and Convenient”
text: This trip was my first time in NYC in over 10 years, so obviously I considered myself a first timer. I chose this hotel because of its affordability and seems to be close to everything when I checked out its website. I was skeptical about the size of room and the shared bathroom situation. I'm just used to staying at hotels with a lot of square footage at a cheaper price like Las Vegas. But of course you cant compare that to NYC. I booked the bunk bed room because it was the cheapest and there was a big difference in price if I were to book the queen. Upon arrival I was surprised. The room was small but functional. I asked for a quiet room and that's what I got. The room was very clean and the bed was very comfortable. TV worked just fined for me. For those that are skeptical about sharing bathrooms, dont be. There are 4 bathrooms on each floor and each is located in different section of the floor. So I shared the bathroom with only about 5 other guests that were staying next to me, and keep in mind that 1 or 2 of the guests staying close to you have their own bathroom. Bathroom is frequently cleaned, everytime I go in to use it was fine. It also helps to have nice neighbors who keeps it clean as well. So if you like living in the dorms when you were in college, you'll like this. The crowd is pretty much international, a lot of Europeans. My floor was very quiet, however even though my room is tucked away in the corner and away from the elevators I can still hear people coming in and out but it didnt bother me at all since it was brief. The location and neighborhood is unmatched. I highly recommend this hotel especially for first timers. ATMs, Banks, Drug Stores, Restaurants and Subways are all very close within 1-2 blocks. It gives you a piece of mind that even though you're away from home but everything you need is accessible. 5th ave, Park ave, Rockefeller Center, Times Square are within walking distance and Central Park and Ground Zero memorial site are short subway rides away. I was a little afraid to take the subway but once you spend time learning the system it'll make your experience much more rewarding. You can go to mta.com to find out about fares, routes and schedules. You can even type in your location and destination on the website and it will show you which train to take, you can't go wrong. It will help you navigate the city. I love my NYC experience and can't wait to return. What I like the most about this trip is not just about NYC itself, but also the hotel that is affordable, comfortable and convenient. WiFi is available even though I feel it was a little too slow that'd like but will not complain since it was free. Staffs could have friendlier and more attentive. I didn't need my butt kissed but I was their guest, it'd be nice if they had anticipated my needs more and lose the attitude that they were doing me a favor by doing their job. This goes to the front desk. The conceirge was available when I checked in at night but nonexistent in the morning when I needed help. New Yorkers I met were very friendly in offering me assistance with directions. I've met them in the subway, Central Park, on the street and they were willing to help even when they were on the phone or jogging, so maybe I should have paid them? But I'd definitely return to The Pod.

title: “A good hotel in a convenient location.”
text: My husband and I, along with 10 members of his family, just stayed at this hotel Aug. 16-18 prior to leaving on a cruise. For the value and location, this is a good hotel. It's not even 2 miles from Jacksonville's airport and about 10 miles from the cruise terminal. If you need to rent a car and travel around Jacksonville, the exit to Interstate I-95 is 1 1/2 blocks away. The room was clean, plenty of towels, and very cool considering it was 97 degrees the 2 1/2 days we were there. And we didn't hear any of our neighbors in the next rooms at all. The hotel does have the free breakfast available; however, we chose to eat at the Waffle House (highly recommend that also--great waffles and hash browns) which is a block away. If you are looking for a simple, clean hotel in Jacksonville, I would highly recommend this hotel. If I ever visit Jacksonville again, I will automatically book this hotel.

title: “KnickerDump”
text: In desperate need of cleaning and updating. Dark, dingy rooms with patched ceilings and soiled comforters. Ripped rugs, chipped furniture, and the smell of cheap room freshener will make your stay most unpleasant. One plus, the staff is very friendly and accommodating.

title: “Great Rooms, Friendly Service!”
text: I travel to Dallas TX at least once per year and each time I go I stay at the Magnolia. I love the location and friendly and accomodating staff. The happy hour is fun and comfortable. It's always an enjoyable experience when I stay here.

title: “Exceptional service, fabulous reception, average accommodations.”
text:
Í've stayed at the Ritz Carlton in Philadelphia seven or eight times this year and I found that the service from the hotel staff is consistently exceptional. Granted, this property is considered "Luxury", so exceptional service is expected.
On the downside, the accommodations can best be described as "average". The rooms, though spacious, seem worn and due for a makeover.
Particularly annoying about this property is the fact that you can't order food in the lobby / bar after a certain time. In fact, the cocktail waitress suggested that we go to our room and order room service if we wanted something to eat.
All in all, I'd recommend the Ritz Carlton if you want to be within walking distance of the center city attractions.

title: “Average hotel, with a good room and location”
text:
It's functional, with a good room and confortable bed. It has a great a location and it's an easy walk to Newburry Street or even the city downtown.
There's a Starbucks in the lobby, wich is great if you're in a hurry early in the morning, and it's attached to the Prudential Center. Anyway, obviously you can get better food options nearby.
This is a big and old chain hotel, so you'll find exactly what you usually find on big and old chain hotels.

title: “Great view; great rates with AAA special”
text: Enjoyed our stay at the Mariott Marquis. Once in a life-time views of Times Square. Was able to get a special rate through Mariott and AAA with a Thursday check-in. Had a Times Square View room and really enjoyed the lights and watching the hustle below. The amenities and service were very acceptable. Subway was just a few blocks in either direction. Definitely a solid, high-end 3-star hotel.

title: “Incredible!”
text: We stayed at The Pierre for our son's wedding, and everything was perfect! Our room was upgraded to a gorgeous, spacious suite, the location on Central Park was perfect and the staff was incredibly attentive. I highly recommend The Pierre for anyone looking for a five star experience in Manhattan.

title: “Only If You're Desperate or Broke”
text:
I'll keep this short: I usually stay at Affinia properties in Manhattan and still fully recommend them. I often stay in the same neighborhood that the Hotel Pennsylvania is in because I see sporting events at Madison Square Garden. Ended up at the hotel because a friend had a free room there.
I wouldn't go back if THEY paid me. Room was TINY, cramped, linens were junky, etc. Line at check-in was like the security line at an airport: long and sluggish.
Worst - there was essentially no climate control in our room. Could NOT turn on any air-conditioning at all, so it was roughly 85 degrees in there at all times. Did NOT make for a comfortable sleeping night.
If you only care about having a roof over your head after a day/night of boozing and seeing sports at the Garden, MAYBE this is OK. But I'd recommend spending the extra $100 or so to stay elsewhere - such as the Affinia Manhattan next door.

title: “Best San Francisco Experience Ever”
text: The location is the best in the city. Steps from Union Square and a short cab ride to any of the sites in the city. The hotel is welcoming, clean and just beautiful. The staff at the front desk (Maria) are very friendly and helpful. The breakfast buffet was amazing. Robin was our server and was really great! I love this beautiful property with it's breath taking views and I hope to return again in the very near future.

title: “Really good upscale hotel.”
text:
There were high expectations before coming to this hotel and they were all met. From you entered the hotel via concierge and front desk you were very welcomed. From a standard room the bathroom was very nice. You felt really good staying here and the location in 44th between 5th. and 6th. Av is no drawback. 
Housekeeping did an excellent job and cleaned up in the evening as well.

title: “A Mom and Daughter Getaway”
text: My daughter and I traveled to New York, and stayed over the Memorial Day weekend. The Benjamin was perfect for our weekend! It was a safe location and close to all of our siteseeing and shopping and shows. They had no problem with our early check in. We went to the hotel spa the first night and both had wonderful massages and facials. We got back to our room to champagne sent up from the manager. The room service was wonderful with nightly turn downs when we arrived back to the hotel in the evenings. Everyone was friendly and very helpful with directions when we needed them. We enjoyed a weekend of elaxation and quality girl time at a wonderful location!

title: “Great location in manhattan”
text: We were greeted by a friendly front desk and our room was a good size for NYC and very clean. It took several calls to get a foam (non feather) pillow for our nephew but it got there eventually. Breakfast buffet was great with the kids and he wait staff was awesome. We were headed for MOMA was it was a simple walk across the street. We will be back.

title: “We had a great time”
text: It was what every as I rated above,and the staff was great,plus we got it for a cheap rate.A nice breakfast and the lobby is very nice

title: “fantastic hotel”
text:
This was one of the best situated hotels in a city that I've ever experienced! Directly in the heart of downtown Charlotte with great walking access to almost any area you could desire.
Rooms were typical of a strong Hilton brand - clean, comfortable, quiet.

title: “Great location”
text:
This boutique hotel, a block from Michigan Avenue is perfectly located for a visit to Chicago. 
The room we had was spacious, with a safe, a microwave and a refrigerator. The roof-top terrace was a charming place for an after dinner drink, with a lovely view of the skyline.
The only complaint I have is that the shower had absolutely nowhere to put a shampoo bottle, or anything else for that matter.

title: “Perfect Location, Okay Value”
text:
It's hard to find a better location in Chicago: on a quiet street just a block and a half off Michigan Avenue near Water Tower and Water Tower Place. The hotel runs lots of specials so we were able to get a room for what amounted to about $170 a night including taxes. It was billed as a "junior suite" and while the bathroom was huge and even better than the Penninsula around the corner, the room itself wasn't that large. The fold-out sofa bed was surprisingly comfortable as was the king bed. The hotel's website talks about its WI-FI access, but it's an extra charge. The hallways are my biggest complaint... odd pictures and very dark, like many W Hotels in the early 2000s... My Mom was convinced the artwork showed people jumping to their deaths from skyscrapers - It was all a bit funky and not in a good way.
The best tip is to avoid the $20 fee for breakfast and walk down to the end of Chestnut for a great breakfast at The Tempo Cafe, a diner that serves all the egg dishes in skillets right to your table. There's an authentic and less touristy Pizza place around the corner on State Street, Pizano's. Whatever you do, DON'T plan to park your car at the hotel - it's a whopping 47 bucks a night!!! The biggest complaint is that they have a tiny gym and no connected spa or pool, but the location and price make up for it. And they were sticklers for not surrenduring the room 'til exactly 3pm - we got there at 2:30 and were told to come back.

title: “nice place”
text: I enjoyed my stay there, nice and clean, best staff, walking distance from subway and many eatery places. A bit too crowdy neighberhood, but live and moving. I loved NY and it's partly owed to my hotel.

title: “Nice hotel overall”
text: We stayed here on a weekend trip. I booked the hotel via Priceline and got a great price. We were put on one of the lower floors. The room was small, but nicely appointed and clean. The bathroom was small with only a stand-up shower (no tub). The staff seemed friendly. As mentioned by previous reviewers, there were some noise issues, even with people talking in the hallway at a reasonable volume. The location was great, in particular, it is in close vicinity to the red, blue, and brown cta lines. I would stay here again. Based on previous reviewers and the website, I wonder if certain rooms are reserved for Priceline reservations.

title: “Will stay here again and again and again...”
text:
I'm writing this review almost one month since my stay at ink48. Why? Because I can't stop thinking about what a wonderful time I had in NYC and how much I enjoyed staying there. This boutique hotel is pretty close to perfect for the price, the rooms are exceptionally roomy, the whole place has a really cool vibe, which is to be expected from a Kimpton Hotel. The piece de resistance has got to be the rooftop. Magic! What an amazing view. I sat up there with my friends, ended up making new friends and reconnecting with an old friend. Great place to cuddle away with and get lost in conversation or mingle about and enjoy the delicious cocktails with a view of the Manhattan skyline and the Hudson. 
My friend had flown out from DC and we stayed for 3 nights. The service at ink48 was great, the beds were heavenly, and the staff was genuine and friendly. I have to take this moment to publicly thank John Markunas (front office manager) for being ridiculously awesome. Not only did he make sure we had a fantastic room and enjoyed our stay, which we did, but when I called him from CA to let him know another friend of mine was coming out to stay at ink for business...he made sure he also had a great room. (Wish I could forward you the numerous thank you texts!) 
I didn't get a chance to check out the spa or The Press Lounge...next time. This place may very well be my home away from home. Mi casa es su casa...you're welcome anytime at ink48. Say hi to John and have a drink for me at the rooftop.

title: “5000 star service!!!”
text: This quaint gay owned hotel is run by a fantastic manager Troy. The Chelsea pines inn is truly fabulousssss! What the rooms lack in newness is far surpassed by some of the finest service in the world! I have stayed in so many 5 star hotels that didn't have near the charm and personal touch that this has. Everyone that works there smiles and goes do way far out of thier way to go the extra 100 miles! Troy and all the guys that work there really take pride in what they do and it shows. Sure you can pay less elsewhere but if you want to be truly pampered in a low key relaxed homey environment this area in the village is great for straight and gays alike!

title: “It was a very comfortable stay in the heart of the city with all the leisure.”
text: We came to US from India as our one of the two sons is California in US., We flew to New York to visit Niagara but at the same time wanted to see New York city without undergoing hassles of driving. This hotel served our purpose and we did not have to make any compromises of peace in spite of being in the heart of the city. It is at a very convenient location with plenty of choices restaurants.

title: “Loved the Michelangelo..will stay again”
text: My Husband and I have just returned from our 6 day stay at the Michelangelo. Having read reviews at a number of internet sites I decided this was the hotel I wanted to stay at for our first ever trip to New York. I had to convince our travel agent to book the Michelangelo as it's not listed in any travel brochures in Australia. We were not disappointed. When we arrived after our long flight from Sydney the staff were very understanding and helpful. Our Executive room was spacious, very quiet and just lovely with a nice view over 7th ave. Added touches were the daily weather forecast ( in celsius), chocolates on the turned down bed and newspaper delivered to the door. The complimentary breakfast of pastries, muffins and coffee was a wonderful start to the day. The Michelangelo is so conveniently located. It's walking distance to Times Square, Madison Sq Garden, the subway and all the shopping areas. The only thing lacking from the room was tea & coffee making facilites, but then Starbucks is on the next corner or there is room service. We will certainly be staying at the Michelangelo next time we visit New York!!!

title: “Wonderful place to stay”
text: Trip advisor never disappoints and this is no exception. First, the staff was amazing at reception and Lisa and Anna serving breakfast were great. Ate the breakfast buffet everyday. Anna was a great trip advisor as she told us where to visit. Kurt, the manager, was more then helpful when we needed him. This property is located on an old Navy base. Trader Joe's, Vons, pizza place and more stores within the property. First day, we took the Old Time Trolly tour just to get a handle on which places we wanted to visit on our own and it picks you up right next door. Great location as you are so close to everything, literally everything from SeaWorld, Seaport Village, to down town San Diego to Old town, to Gas lamp district to Balboa Park, San Diego Zoo and Coronado Island. I was disappointed in Little Italy. Nothing to see or do except a few restaurants. Nothing beats L.I. in NYC. We did it all and we drove to Los Angeles and did the tour of Hollywood walk, Kodak Theatre and Graumans Chinese Theatre. Reminded me of Times Square in NYC. Very touristy. With all the traffic in San Diego this location was central and it really wasn't bad getting around. We hiked Torrey Pines and drove up the coast to Del Mar, Laguna Beach and Newport Beach. We rented bikes from Stay Classy bike rentals and they delivered the bikes to our hotel and picked them up when we were done. This was a l2 day trip for us. We rode/walked everyday on the bike path right outside the hotel property and biked to the Seaport Village on our bikes and to Point Loma Seafood which I recommend. Plane noise barely noticable. The rooms were clean and the beds comfortable. Sat by the fire pit during happy hour and met some nice people too. You can't beat this location and the hotel was very modern and clean. This was our first time to San Diego. My son moved to La Jolla and he was l5 minutes away taking the 5. Visit La Jolla cove and try the great restaurants in La Jolla too. We will be back.

title: “Nose-in-the-air”
text: My wife and I spend two nights at Eliot Hotel in November. A very pretentious place: at least two people open doors for you when you enter or exit, three waiters serve you in the hotel restaurant at a time with the fourth person responsible for your bread only. A separate guy just to push the elevator button. Tiny reception area, small elevators. We had a two room suite with windows facing an ugly back yard where they stored mattresses (see photo), and where 5 huge ventilation fans were located. Those fans produced endless noise which spoiled our stay substantially. The air conditioner/heater in the room itself was so noisy that we did not use it at all. Besides mentioned above it may be considered a good hotel: perfect location, polite personnel, spacious and clean rooms, good service.

title: “a perfectly nice place”
text: Did one night here this past weekend, It is a great location, three blocks from michigan avenue, property is very clean, clearly has been renovated. Weird old and kind of gross radiator in bathroom that was on and made it hot, other than that room was nice, clean no issues at all. One suggestion, park across Ohio not in the garage at hotel, it is 31 dollars a day there and 45 or more at hotel and the garage is literally across the street. No pictures, but web site pics are accurate. Cookie is a nice touch at check in, but be careful, it melts.

title: “A fabulous grand dame hotel with great cocktails”
text:
We stayed for 5 nights at the Roosevelt. The reception staff were exceptionally helpful, including letting us check in 6 hours early at no extra cost. The rooms aren't luxurious, but are comfortable and well serviced.
We particularly enjoyed the cocktail bar in the lobby and the waiters were really lovely, particularly Jose who treated us very well. The Berritini cocktail is delicious.
We wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel as an excellent base for exploring Manhattan.

title: “Good value, great location”
text: Just returned from a three night stay at the Red Roof Manhattan. The hotel has a superb location. We were on the 17th floor with a great view of the Empire State Building. Rooms are small but very clean. Breakfast is basic, but replenished on an ongoing basis so there's always enough to eat. Easy walking distance to Times Square, Broadway, Madison Square Gardens or the underground (but you won't see as much if you're not on foot!!). Would recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “A lovely stay!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here several days after Christmas. Neither of us are gamblers but we wanted to do something different. I'm so glad we did! We had a wonderful time! The room was beautiful, as was the view of Detroit. We had fun playing the one cent slot machines and appreciated the wide variety of dinner options we had since the hotel is located in Greektown. Parking was free and easy in the parking garage attached to the hotel. 
All in all, this was a fun getaway and a nice break from the norm.I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Best Buy For The $$$$ in San Diego”
text:
I have stayed at the Kings Inn many times on business and pleasure trips to San Diego. These are the facts, friend.
Excellent pricing. 
Great location
Large rooms with great beds.
Large pool with a resort feel.
2 good restuarants on site.
The kind of personal service you hope to find in a 5 star hotel.
Ricco and Macarena are the best (visualize capital letters here)!
Plus the best piano bar in the world is within walking distance.

title: “Ok, but not great”
text: The hotel was ok, had worse had better. Beds were very comfy which was nice after walking all day. Would have been nice to have a mini-fridge and coffee maker in the room though. One of the two phones didn't work. The shower was horrible, kind of like a camper hand held that you had to stick your head into the corner to try and wash your hair and the tub didn't drain properly. Conceirge really messed up in booking our shuttle back to the airport - she booked it for 3p.m. instead of 3 a.m.! Good thing we caught it in time to make it on time. Location was ok, a bit far from the action but good for the hop on hop off as a stop was just at the end of the street (less than 1/2 block). Views were terrific.

title: “Keep driving, fast!”
text: As long as we have a choice we will NEVER stay there again. The toilet seat in our bathroom looked like a Rhino sat on it with burn marks in the shower tub. The carpet was filthy, blankets had holes, the microwave didn't close/work. All of the lights had issuses working. We stayed for a week and near the end we were getting cold symptems. The guy that served breakfast was nice though he was very sloppy. He cleaned everything (counter, toaster, etc) with the same wet cloth without rinsing or changing it. Also, the ladel used for the waffle mix was rather filthy though it was used anyway. There was no one to clean the tables except yourself when you'd like one after waiting for a while in the tiny dinning area for a seat. The conference room was trashy. We asked 3 different employees to vaccuum it but no one ever did. Eventually we did it ourselves. Others that we traveled with experienced rooms with broken head boards, non-working refrigerators and witnessed/interrupted prostitution inside the conference room. There are NO extra pillows and we think the manager lives there with their family. There was no toilet paper in the main lobby bathroom and it looked as if it hadn't been cleaned for sometime. The doors to the rooms looked as if they'd been pried open. By the way, it is pet friendly which is a nice way of saying that dogs are constantly barking. One good thing is that we didn't find any bed bugs! )

title: “Excellent once again!”
text: We stayed at the HiltonTimes Square again this year and once again the staff exceeded expectations. From the bell stand staff to the front desk the staff was extremely friendly and helpful and did everything they could to make our stay enjoyable. Richard and Raquel at the front desk were especially helpful with getting us a room with a a great view, they both understand what great customer service is all about. The waitstaff at the restaurant was friendly and attentive but the prices are a little excessive but I guess you are in NYC. The hotel is in a great location in Times Square and within walking distance of most attractions and shows. Also a subway station isright next tothe front door if you are heading a little further uptown or downtown. I would highly recommend and will be staying here again next year. Once again thank you Richard and Raquel for making our stay so enjoyable.

title: “Quality 4-star with a few extra perks”
text:
Stayed here with family for combination business / vacation. The rooms are large and the beds very comfortable. The front of desk staff are all very efficient and courteous. The pool / exercise center is clean and well-appointed. No hot tub or sauna, unfortunately, and the pool is outdoors so it can get cold and windy. 
The milk and cookies provided every evening was a great touch, and adds to the family-friendly appeal of the hotel. We didn't eat in any of the restaurants but relied heavily on a late-night convenience store with a wide array or prepared foods. Again, a family-friendly alternative.
The hotel provides a town car service for around downtown, which can be convenient especially since parking is insanely expensive and, like most of Los Angeles, you do need to drive to get anywhere. 
The hotel is right on top of MOCA and the Disney Concert Hall, which can have its drawbacks especially if a special event is booked (as it was when we were there, and the noise was deafening). Other nearby points of interest include Calle Alameda, an outdoor Mexican market, and Little Tokyo. The Staples Center is nearby as well.
The downtown core is no longer the cultural wasteland it once was, and this hotel offers a convenient and very comfortable place to get to know the area.

title: “Great, but not quite perfect”
text:
I ordered a premium view king and was upgraded to a full suite (with the same great view). The room is very big, even by 1BR suite standards. If you are traveling with a child this is nice setup because the bedroom is roomy (big enough for a roll-away for junior) and very sealed off from the living room (so mom and dad can stay up late).
Overall, this is an outstanding hotel, and they get the basics right. It definitely lives up to it's price range and star rating. The rooms are very nicely decorated and clean, the rooms are quiet, they have nice views, the bathrooms are outstanding with separate soaking tub and so on. They are BIG rooms, especially by Manhattan standards.
However, I can only give the hotel four dots for a couple of shortcomings for a hotel of this caliber.
1. MIni-bar. I got a huge, very fancy fridge. Neat-o. Then there was nothing in it but some soda cans. Terrible. A mini-bar should have lots of variety of things to drink and eat, booze, wine, munchies, etc. This minibar had none of that. I also had to keep ordering drinks for the fridge (there were small), which is a bit strange since this huge fridge could hold hundreds if necessary.
2. Room service menu: a little thin. The GREAT news is that it's open 24 hours. However, it's not got a lot of variety and if you had to stay here more than a couple of days you'd pretty much hit everything within your taste. Also, the wine options were not listed on the menu at all, and was limited to "red" and "white". Again, not bad overall, but certainly sub-par for a hotel in this price range. Maybe they expect you to eat out (easy to do in the location) but after a long day's work sometimes you just need to hang out in the room and rest.
3. TVs. First, the TV in my living room basically didn't work (bad reception). The one in my bedroom did, so I didn't sweat it. If I had actually ordered this room as a suite, however, that would have been a bummer. Also, technology-wise, this is a older system without things like PPV and games that you expect from hotels these days.

title: “Managed to get by since we were not in the room much.”
text: This room was admittedly a great price for downtown DC. HOWEVER, the room was so small I had to rearrange the furniture to accommodate our luggage! (We were only there for a weekend.) The shower was awful, barely a trickle of water. The indoor pool on the top floor was too cold for the adults. Staff was nice enough.

title: “A room with a view”
text:
We stayed at the Sheraton Hotel and Marina for one night prior to our cruise.
It was great to have a shuttle from the airport to the hotel although it took a while for it to come even though the hotel is fairly close to the airport.
We stayed in the Bay Tower with a view over the harbour. The rooms were large although not in perfect condition.
This hotel is a reasonable distance from town. (Approx $15 by taxi).
This hotel was fine for one night but you really require a car if staying any longer.

title: “A very good hotel, just down the road from Times Square”
text:
A good hotel a 100 yards from Times Sq. Compementary coffee and tea in the lobby but its finished by 9-00am. The staff here are excellant and very helpfull. The rooms are quite spacious, but be warned if you get a room at the front of the hotel it's liable to be noisy at times in the early hours.
This hotel has just been refurmished but does not have a business centre, so if you need the internet take your laptop. There is free internet access in all the rooms
Virtually next door to the hotel there is a Bar and a indian and a chinese restaurant within spitting distance, we walked passed them several times before we realised the restaurants were there.
From JFK the bus is $18 each and the taxis are $45 +$5 toll + tip to anywhere in Manhattan.
By the way, the Saten Island ferry is free.

title: “Average - expensive - other choices steps away”
text: Stayed here as the client booked the room. The room was large and functional but it was the noisiest hotel room in NYC I have stayed in ... I stay in NYC about 30 days per year and I had to use my ear plugs to block out the street noise. It seemed very expensive in a cheep way -- meaning the nice mini bottle of water next to the bed was $7. I am not shy about prices but its been a while since the bottle NEXT to my bed had a price tag on it. Room service was excellent - my special order was done perfectly and delivered on time. There are only two elevators and about 25+ floors - the trip down in the morning frequently took over 5 minutes waiting for an elevator with space.

title: “Wonderful Trip!”
text:
Very expensive, but you get what you pay for. If you plan to stay here I suggest you go together with family and book a stay in the family villa section. It was worth it!
I booked this trip for my niece & nephew for their Spring Break. When I booked with the hotel I asked for a letter of confirmation. Included with this letter was the waterpark rules and hours of operation for everything they offer, which was great. I didn't have to rely on their website for accuracy. Check in is at 4pm and we got there at 3:45pm. It only took me 5 minutes to check in and everything went smoothly. Our room was in the newer family villa section and was wonderful! It was clean, spacious, and brand new. We loved it. The elevator was quick and we had a short walk to the waterpark. The kids just loved the waterpark! The water was heavily chlorinated, but tons of fun. The staff was very friendly. We ate dinner at the Sage Brush, which was kind of expensive for average food. But it was nice to not have to go out for dinner. Our waitress was nice and it only took about 20 minutes to be seated and have the food on the table. The arcade was great fun too. We had no problems with the plumbing, as other reviews have mentioned. However I did hear a lot of complaining from the folks who stayed in the "older section." When checking out there was a customer complaining to the manager, who was handling her quite nicely, making offers to discount her room, etc.

title: “Not sure what about this hotel was considered "high end"”
text:
This trip was business as well as a weekend away with my best friend.
The location was awesome! It was not too far from Hobby Airport or Reliant Stadium and it was a stones throw from some GREAT shopping and several restaurants. The hotel itself was just a hotel. Nothing special or fancy in my opinion. The front desk people were friendly and helpful but that's expected from a place like this. Nothing about this hotel was over-the-top, not the service, the decor, the room service and most certainly not the beds! It was a place to stay, no better or higher quality than places $100 cheaper. Average rating at best! I wasn't impressed!

title: “Not for me - ear plugs are a must at this hotel”
text: The Good: the hotel is clean and Melissa at the front desk was accomodating. We paid through priceline but she honored my starwood preferred gold member status and upgraded our room to a partial view of the bay. The maid service is exceptional. The bad: (1) elevator access. You always have to put your card in the reader slot in the elevator to get to your floor which makes for a cumbersome experience when your hands are full as ours often were. (2) No in-room cofffee which may seem trivial to some but a lifeline for me. The W offers coffee downstairs next to the lobby but they only had 1 pot and it was frequently empty which made for a very frustrating experience. (3) The "club" atmosphere with trance music being blasted in the lobby in the late afternoons and into the evenings was really annoying and made for a very loud hotel experience (I slept with ear plugs). (4) The rooms while clean and decorated elaborately in the same Blue/IKEA/funk complete with a chalk board and chalk, are small with limited shelf/drawer space and there is NO bathtub - shower only (and shower has no door). (5) There is no privacy in bathroom due to the apparently Asian inspired sliding bathroom door that really only blocks the opening to the bathroom, it actually does not close off the bathroom. (6) NO jacuzzi and a very, very small pool. (7) The gym was nice actually (with a variety of equipment) but with slatted doors it was open to the outside and an exhaust smell would come into the gym making it as though you were working out on the street next to a running diesel truck. (8) Location: next to a rather seedy section of down town, it was a good hike to the gas lamp district (Little Italy was closer) through vagrants and scary looking people and, with trains running through the night blaring their whistles, again, ear plugs are a must. (9) No onsite parking - you must use valet and at a whopping $32 per day, it really adds up. Good side- you can come and go as you like with no additional fee but the valets wanted tips each time they got your car for you. (10) the non front desk staff was rude and absolutely lacked elevator ettiquete. Other than the front desk who's sole job it is to greet and be courtious to guests, the rest of the staff we encountered were rude. As an example, one staff member actually brushed me out of the way so that she could get onto the elevator. I yielded to her and actually apologized, she however completely ignored me, pushed her way past me and jumped onto the elevator. We received similar treatment from other personnel. I gave it an average rating as you could definitely do worse and as an alleged 4 star hotel, it IS nice but it is just not my style with the loud club music, the rude staff and in short, the focus on a narrow niche market really missed its mark with me. Unless I am suckered into this hotel again through priceline or I get it for free, I will never stay at a W again.

title: “Appalled”
text:
I spent one night in this hotel and it was awful. The hotel décor looks tired and dusty, nothing like the photos online (and I’m used to hostels and third world hotels, so it’s not like my standards are through the roof). 
Also, I found what certainly appeared to be a bed bug and received some bites that my doctor said looked like bed bug bites. This was on a Wednesday night; the following Tuesday the hotel responded to my complaints and said they were planning to call the exterminator that afternoon (so they rented the room for almost a week without looking into it). 
They claim the exterminators didn’t find anything. I’m not totally sold, but regardless I find it appalling (and told the management as much) that they waited almost a week to bring in an exterminator and rented the room before they had confirmation that the room was safe.

title: “the best hotel in nw”
text: well went to visit familly in san antonio tx and love our stay at comfert suites the staff was great the place was clean , nice ,new and safe . i want to thank the lady who was so helpful and super nice . i cant remember her name but u will enjoy ur stay . were i plan on going back everytime were in sa tx

title: “Gorgeous hotel”
text: I love this hotel - I've stayed here for business and pleasure. The lobby and rooms are beautiful! The service is excellent! There was a minor problem with my bill when it arrived and I called them and they fixed it immediately. It's on top of an enormous Whole Foods which is so nice when you're traveling. It's great to have healthy eating options without a lot of hassle. Speaking of healthy eating, try the fruit and granola plate for breakfast - it's delicious!

title: “We Love It!”
text:
I wrote a review while staying at the property on September 8, 2011. Someone was trying to sabatoge the opening of this hotel and reported my review as "inappropriate" , it was deleted within a few days. It appears Trip Advistor does not really check a review.
The staff was very helpful, the room was beautiful and we loved the location. It will be my hotel of choice when I visit New York again and the price was a real bargain. We got a corner room because we wanted 2 queen sized beds, the view was fantastic, it was like I could just reach over and touch the Empire State Building, loved the remote controled drapes and the mirror/television in the bathroom. My Place deli right across the street. This is what people have to say about them:
http://www.menupages.com/restaurants/my-place-deli/
Jackie Aucoin
Near New Orleans, Louisiana
This is the fate of my first review.

title: “Excellent Hotel in outskirts of Denver”
text:
We were pleasantly surprised when the airlines put us up here due to an overbooked flight. This is an exceptional hotel. The hotel is beautiful as were the rooms. The hotel has an inside pool with much natural light and looks out on the outdoor pool (which was closed this time of the year). The fitness area is one of the best I've seen with newer equiptment. Customer service was great and there is a shuttle that runs every 1/2 hour to the airport. 
Within a short walk is an outdoor mall with a few fast food and casual restaurants. The business center has amazing fast internet access and the hotel has a nice italian restaurant should you desire to eat there.
We had been traveling through Denver after our family vacation and none of the hotels we stayed in during our vacation came close to this (despite being rated as highly). If we travel to Denver again, this will defintely be where we would stay.

title: “Great hotel - great location”
text:
We have stayed here 3 or 4 times and are returning again this year. Rooms large and clean and the location is brilliant. Close to central park and times square. Only negatives are the lifts are very busy and the large lounge bar seems to be rarely staffed, would be good to enjoy a mid-afternoon refreshement in there. Staff are helpful and friendly.
Would be good to here from people who could recommend a good quality, reasonably priced alternative for a future visit. We like a midtown location.

title: “Dismal stay so don't expect much”
text: My stay at the Sheraton was very interesting. I had stayed there a few years back and was not impressed and probably would not stay there again, however I decided to try Priceline for the first time and was excited to get a rate of only $90 per night for two nights for a so called 4 star hotel in Back Bay. Then I saw it was the Sheraton that accepted my bid. I did some research and many sites indicated that this hotel just went through a 73 million dollar renovation. I was excited thinking all rooms are redone and nice and this would be a great stay. Boy was I in for a shock! I was put in a room on the 19th floor in the north tower and right off the elevator I could tell nothing has been remodeled or changed. Everything dark and depressing from the 60s or 70s. I entered into a dismal room with so many issues. A small dirty bathroom with mold in the shower area. Dirty grout on the walls and floor of the bathroom. A rusted out shower curtain rod. Chipped and pealing paint on the door frame. The room itself had a dirty carpet. Stains on the walls. Door to the room and closets are original from 1965 when the hotel opened and are all dinged and dented and look terrible. In room TV would not display the channels so you never could see what station you were on. Cleaning staff missed many things like leaving more toliet paper and ice bucket liner. The only thing I can say positive about this hotel is that the check in staff were very nice and the climate control system worked very well. Other than that, it is important that people who choose this hotel know that if you stay there demand to be put in the south tower or stay elsewhere. The south tower has been totally renovated. I went to a few floors to look and the halls are all modern and nice. Some floors stated they are for "preferred guests. My own personal opinion is that anyone not paying full price is not a preferred guest and you get stuck in the dismal north tower. Don't be fooled by this hotel being connected to shopping malls, etc. There are so many better hotels I have stayed at in the general area with much higher standards. I did write to the management of Sheraton who agreed the room was terrible and pretty much just said sorry and they will address it, hope you try us again. Trust me that won't happen!

title: “Nice trip”
text: We had a nice trip. I was worried with reviewing some of the reviews prior to arriving, but it exceeded my expectations. The good = great valet staff, easy checkinand out, fabulous beds, clean room and great housekeeping staff. The not-so-good = hidden charges on those fancy little snacks they leave in the room, not a lot of dining choices with reasonable prices. I would stay here again.

title: “The Pod is the place to stay!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at The Pod in September and plan to be back in May. It's a great, hip, place to stay on a budget. It is not a resort and they clearly explain the concept so if you go knowing that the rooms are small, etc. you'll be fine. The bathrooms are clean and there was always one available, etc.
There's a great intimate French restaurant just next door. And for breakfast we stopped at Pax a couple of blocks away. You are very close to the subways, so that's great, too.
Great deal.

title: “perfect surroundings”
text: everything was perfect from the location to the service to the well designed room. the staff was pleasant and helpful in every way. the room was clean and appeared to be recently renovated with large flat screen tv's and an incredibly comfortable bed. this is the perfect spot for easy access to shopping, dining, drinking and exploring. i would definitley stay again.

title: “Terrific Stay”
text: I enjoyed our recent weekend here in pretty much every way. Virtually everyone we encountered was pleasant and polite. The property is impressive, immaculate, and conveniently located. Our kids enjoyed the pool, the "Greenway" parks in front of the hotel, and our suite with club-level access. The club was one of the nicer hotel clubs I've been in, with surprisingly nice wines and snacks in the evening and good breakfast offerings as well. We have stayed in many Intercontinental Hotels in recent years both in the U.S. and abroad, but this may be my new favorite.

title: “Excellent! We'll be back!”
text: My family and I stayed at the Drury for 4 nights and loved it! It was more than we expected from a two star hotel. We typically don't stay in any hotels/resorts below a three star. We stayed in a queen suite. It was great for our kids to have the extra room. The room is equipped with a fridge and microwave which is a must when traveling with small children. Despite all the families staying at the hotel, it was very quiet at night. The room and hotel was also very well kept and clean. The staff was very nice and professional. The pool was great on the rooftop and the FREE huge breakfast buffet each morning was excellent. They also offer free drinks and snacks each evening in the lobby. The security into the hotel is also nice. You have to have your room key to get EVERYWHERE! We have stayed at the Hyatt and the LaMansion on the River.
