The LaMansion was wonderful BUT the Drury is much better than the Hyatt! Don't waste your money on the Hyatt when you can stay at the Drury. The Drury is located next to the LaMansion Del Rio on the quiet end of the U but very convenient to all restaurants. The Texas Land and Cattle Co. Steakhouse is located in the bottom of the Drury. It was great food and easy access from the hotel. Check the Drury online website for internet deals. We highly reccommend the Drury, we love San Antonio and we will stay there again.

title: “pretty good hotel over all”
text: bar service was extremely slow, staff not too friendly, food was very good, room was nice but bathroom was dirty with hair on floor in several places...easy fixes! hotel was a very good hotel, wish the bed was taller, softer, bedding was very good.

title: “Almost like living in a co-op”
text: As a platinum Starwood Member, I ususally stay at full service hotels, but had a quick one day in Phoenix and decided to stay by the airport. This Aloft was a little removed from any activity, but an inexpensive5 min train to downtown Tempe was nice and this hotel was very clean, friendly and tastefully decorated, I felt like I did have a loft apartment in the desert! No onsite restaurant, but a full menu "store" for breakfast and lunch with nearby chain restaurant...however multiple call in for takeout places! Well done.

title: “Stay away!”
text: If you have any opportunity to stay elsewhere, do. If you can get your company NOT to use this hotel as their conevnion hotel, do. I came for a conference recently and although the location is close to the Arena District and Short North for entertainment and dining, this hotel allowed panhandlers to roam everywhere assaulting guests asking for money. Everyone in my group was approached 5-10X over two days --- in the elevators, at the bar, in the lobby, in the hallways. It was annoying and at night, scary. The staff either seemed unaware or didn't care. One night a man at the Sky Bar on the second floor sat down, ordered water, was brought a bowl of free bar snacks, and proceeded to ask everyone around him to buy him dinner and drinks. The waitress told him they didn't allow that kind of thing there, but it was obvious he was homeless, so I don't know why he was allowed to sit in the first place. It's too bad because the hotel is fine, but the security stinks and I would neve recommend this hotel to anyone unless they enjoy being stalked and harassed.

title: “excellent location, slightly stuffy”
text:
this hotel screams old money philadelphia. located above such stores as tiffany and ralph lauren, the hyatt is located downtown, just a quick walk from the broad street line, city hall, great shopping and dining on walnut, and rittenhouse square. seriously, the location cannot be beat, and is probably the greatest selling point for this hotel. 
we got a hotwire hot rate and stayed on the 16th floor, and while the view wasn't that impressive from our window, for the price we paid, i was more than happy with the room. although an odd design (the window was in an alcove, which made it pretty dark), it had a flatscreen tv, bathtub/shower, desk, ipod docking station, pod coffee maker, and a comfy bed. the decor is definitely not boutique hotel-esque, so don't expect clean, modern design - think more of the decor of a laura ashley store. nevertheless, the room was very clean and not dingy, save for a small water stain on the ceiling near the entrance to the room that looked pretty fresh (the floor appeared recently refreshed).
the hotel has a restaurant / bar, xix, which has a happy hour (not too many beer selections). the prices were ok, but the view was excellent and the booths were comfy. the vibe reminded me of mad men meets balmoral estate meets ancient rome.
the front desk staff were actually very friendly, which was a plus, since most hotels do not reward high-quality customer service anymore.
my only complaint was that the adjoining parking garage charged me $52 for the night (even with the hotel validation) and no one seems to be working in the garage - everything was automated. it wasn't until after multiple attempts i finally got someone to refund the overage today. this is not the hotel's fault, per se, just something to watch out for.
would definitely take another hotwire plunge and stay here again should i need a hotel in center city at a good price, but i would not pay "regular" price to stay here since i prefer more boutique type properties, like the palomar.

title: “Step Back in Time with Updated Amenities”
text: A last minute mini-vacation took us to The Gunter in downtown San Antonio. All of staff at The Gunter were very friendly and helpful, and it was noticed by us as we appreciated the service. The location is excellent - close to the Riverwalk, the Majestic Theater, and excellent restaurants like Bohanan's and The Palm. We had a Club Level King room, which was comfortable with the Sheraton Sleeper Bed, and the access to the Club was nice for breakfast and afternoon drinks and snacks. It was interesting walking around this historic hotel and learning some of its history. Additionally, it is a great value. We will return.

title: “Very Nice Airport Hotel”
text:
Positives:
*Very pretty hotel outside and in.
*Quick and efficient check-in.
*Room was fairly large, and the bathroom was well appointed.
*Excellent location for a terminal E departure...just walked right over.
Things to Consider:
*Not sure whether or not I actually received a room upgrade as a Diamond...seemed pretty standard, though it was on the corner with a pretty view of the city.
*Room service was just okay...somewhat underwhelming lobster roll.
Conclusions:
I would stay again depending on need for the location, and would consider it for a Boston stay if the rates were competitive. Good hotel.

title: “Decent rooms, expensive parking”
text: This hotel has an excellent location - walk to the Art Institute, M Park, Concert, etc. It offers decent rooms; check-in counter staff are very friendly and helpful; restaurants are good, too. Everything there meets expectations of a 4-star hotel. Downside is lack of swimming pool and parking is very expensive (>$50/night).

title: “Wheelchair Bound Travelers Stay Away”
text:
I traveled with my wife to this hotel, and we stayed for more than a week taking care of business.
I wanted to warn everyone who uses a wheel chair that the handicapped accessible rooms in this hotel are designed very badly. 
In order to get into the bathroom in the wheel chair, one has to get onto the side of a ramp about 3" tall and them make a nearly impossible 90 degree left turn to get in the bathroom door on a ramp which is too steep. 
It is clear to me that this ridiculous ramp into the bathroom has something to do with the plumbing of the hotel. Never in my life have I seen a "handicapped accessible hotel room" where the bathroom floor is 3 to 5" above the floor of the hotel room itself.

title: “Thank Goodness for the Hilton !!”
text:
When I was planning the trip to NYC as my daughter's 18th birthday present, I asked her if we should get a good hotel, or not bother, as we wouldn't be doing anything other than sleep in it. Well, thank goodness as any precocious 17 year old would, she wanted to spend the extra for a good hotel. So I chose the Millenium Hilton from the City & Show website, and actually got a pretty good deal.
As it turned out, my daughter was EXTREMELY ill for the trip, for all of the 5 days we spent there. It started when she fainted on the plane out there (a BIG BIG thank you to the wonderful guys on Continental Airlines who helped her out with oxygen). So we got to Newark, got our taxi to the hotel, and my daughter didn't leave after that (except for an hour in Bloomingdales and a pre-booked helicopter trip). She couldn't walk one block so didn't even see Ground Zero.
So we were stuck in our fantastic hotel room on the 44th floor, with our excellent view up towards the Empire State. As a busy working mum, I actually found the enforced stay very relaxing - we caught up on all of our movies on the big flat screen! The staff was very helpful, and the beds extremely comfortable. This hotel made what could have been an utterly miserable trip, bearable.
I had a meal in the restaurant one evening which was very pleasant. Also, the hotel is right next to Century 21, which is ideal for cut-price shopping. And the World Financial Centre is also worth a look, as well as the church across the road which at that time still held the memorabilia for the lost loved ones of the 9/11 tragedy.
The only problem (and why I'm not giving it a 5 rating) is that there were no instructions by the phone on how to ring an international call back home to Ireland, and I inadvertently dialled various numbers (including to Africa apparently!) and I had to work hard with the reception staff not to be charged an exorbitant amount.
I think I'd like somewhere more central next time, but if you want to be downtown, this is the place. My daughter recovered when we got back home of course, and we know someday we'll be able to laugh about it (just not yet!).

title: “For a good time in the Big Apple, don't try The Times!”
text: If you're looking for a great time in New York, check THE TIMES off your list! For $315 a night (1 bedroom suite), this hotel was a major ichhhhhhh! During a January stay, our room registered at a balmy 82 degrees. Hotel maintenance came up to fix it while we went out to dinner. When we returned, we found that the door was left "propped" open with all of our belongings ready for the taking. The hotel management's response was, "Oh sorry. Maintenance was just up in your room a few minutes ago." To top it off, the room temperature was never correct during our 4-night stay. Then, as if this wasn't bad enough, our room did not get cleaned one night. When we came back to find a messy room, we were told that it was too late for Housekeeping to take care of things. Housekeeping missed our room the next day, too. After two calls, though, our room did get cleaned at about 5:30 p.m. From the moment we encountered the surly front desk clerk, I knew that prepaying my hotel stay was a BIG mistake!!

title: “Nice stay, just make sure and get a room some distance from the elevator”
text: We stayed at this hotel to attend a work conference. The room, fitness center, and hotel were very nice as were the staff. My only complaint is that our third floor room was adjacent to the elevators AND the lobby and the combined noise was overwhelming most nights. The elevators sounded as if they were in the room with us, and due to the large convention next door, they ran almost constantly. The voices from people partying in the lobby area also were quite loud. We asked if we could be moved after the first night, but unfortunately the hotel was full. Five sleepless nights later, we were glad to leave. For the cost of this hotel, you would expect a little better soundproofing.

title: “Personal touch”
text: My wife and I have been coming to the Gateway Sheraton in Los Angeles for more than 10 years. Over the past few years, a number of employees have stood out by providing exceptional service. This includes two Concierge employees who work in the lounge on the 15th floor, Juan and Veronica. They are friendly and professional, always. Two bartenders in the restaurant's bar (Mario and Horatio) went out of their way to make us comfortable during this most recent stay. Both also provided exceptional service and were obviously very experienced and pro's at what they do. One addtional comment relates to Mark, the Food Services manager. Without knowing who he was, he answered several un-related food questions about the hotel and was more than helpful in guiding us to answer our questions. Hat's off to the staff at the Gateway!! Keep up the good work!!! BH

title: “Nice place for the price.”
text: I've been to San Diego before, but this was the first time I stayed at this hotel. I got a very low price online, and was pleasantly surprised at the quality of the hotel. The rooms are a bit run down, but clean. The staff was very nice, and I liked the sports bar. Overall, I would have expected less for the price, and I will stay again.

title: “Great location, ok everything else”
text: I stayed at the Best Western President Hotel during my trip to New York. I know I had read lots of bad reviews about it, and nothing surprised me. There were maid carts in the hallway the ENTIRE time we were there. There was a nasty fridge in the ice room that had some sticky, smelly plastic bag hanging out of it. The water started going so crazy in the shower, it was shooting out so fast, it literally felt like little water bullets were piercing my skin. The bed was not very comfortable. Blah, blah, blah. Normally I am one of those people who will pay extra for the view and the comfort because I generally like to stay in the room a lot while I am on vacation, just relaxing, but in New York, who cares. The location was fantastic!!! It's right in Times Square, everything is at your fingertips. We loved walking around at night and never felt unsafe. We explored every part of New York and it was a great place to come back to at night. We saw a great comedy show at the Broadway Comedy Club one night, we went to a cute Mexican restaurant that was kitty corner. We got to see Katherine Zeta-Jones exit the theatre after her performance unexpectedly. The man who checked us in was very pleasant, the fitness center was nice. The decor is fun and trendy. Maybe a little too trendy? I didn't like how the lobby was constantly full of people waiting to leave the hotel after check out and I wanted to ask the door man a question. I said to him "Can I ask you a question?". I was trying to be polite. He just stared at me. So I said "So, can I ask you a question?!" " So ask!" he said so rudely. Maybe I'm a good tipper, but not after that snide comment! All in all, I don't think I would choose to stay here again, but I'm still alive and I had a great time.

title: “Beautiful yet lacks....”
text:
First let me being by saying this is a beautiful hotel. Close to the Riverwalk, loved the room, atmosphere, grounds, etc. So I have no complaints as far as that goes.
However, I have been using priceline for years, and I have never been reminded constantly by the hotel that I am a "priceline" guest. It just sort of rubbed me the wrong way because I don’t think using priceline to book a room is a big deal. At no point were we asking for upgrades, extras, etc. This was just with minimal “check in/check out” interaction. I felt like the hotel staff could have been less concerned with the fact that we booked through priceline than whether or not we were enjoying our stay. 
All in all the room was great, location was great, etc. It was just one of those things that I felt was unnecessary and an area where the hotel could improve on.

title: “Fantastic place to stay while attending Convention Center event”
text: We stayed here while attending the Northwest Flower and Garden Show at the Convention Center in Feb, 2012, and really there is no place you can choose that is more convenient. It is right across the street. The hotel offered a great, reduced-price rate on the room and valet parking for the show, which was greatly appreciated. The hotel was lovely, the staff very helpful and friendly, and the beds were great. I've stayed in other distant hotels before for the Flower Show, and taken the bus downtown to the Covention Center. It worked fine, but nothing beats the convenience of being across the street. This is where I'll be booking for next year's Flower Show.

title: “Would not return”
text:
The location is excellent for exploring Boston. We had booked a room on the Club Floor but unfortunately our room was located directly across from the access to the lounge. This meant that we were woken at 6.30 am from the continuous stream of hotel residents and staff going in and out of the doors which rattled and banged, causing the door to our room to rattle on its hinges. 
The room itself was a good size but in need of updating. The bathroom was very small and shabby. The sink had a huge crack in it.
Given the problems with the location of our room, we were immediately upgraded to a suite at no extra cost for the duration of our stay. The suite was a good size but again the decoration was in need of updating. 
The Club lounge is not what it could be. The buffet breakfast is of good quality but extra staff is required as there were frequently tables that were left uncleared for long periods of time. I found it incredible that in the club lounge, you were not provided with mugs, cups and saucers or glasses for drinks. Only paper cups were provided!!
The staff were extremely helpful and courteous, however, this hotel falls far short of you expect for the price.

title: “Rooms and service are really bad”
text:
SUMMARY: location was great, but that was it. Service was bad, rooms were set up without thought (ie couldnt watch TV from the bed), bathroom was dirty and reeked of filth, and the customer service was underwhelming and disappointing (to put it politely). Save yourself the time and find a different place, there are enough hotels in the city in this price range that are far, far better. 
DETAILS: Stayed here over the weekend for a sunday night wedding that was taking place in the hotel. The location was perfect- right across from central park, lots to do in walking distance. But that was it.
When we wnt to check in, it took FOREVER. The line was really long and was not moving. Waited, waited, waited, until we FINALLY received our room. Room was a little shoddy - carpet was worn, furniture old and drab. I went to the bathroom and noticed that there was only one bathrobe and an empty hanger for the second with a tag that said "if you take the robe on this hanger, you will be charged $100". Well, I guess the occupants before me are getting charged $100... but why didnt housekeeping replace that robe? This was the least of my problems.
The bathroom shower was not clean - it actually reeked of dirt. Seems like they never scrubbed the tub or replaced the shower curtain, and years of dirt layered themsleves in the form of a film all along the inside of the shower curtain... was gross. 
The flatscreen TV was on the wall to the far left. But the bed didnt face that wall. And the bracket didnt swivel out. So guests cant watch TV from their bed, which is ridiculous. We needed to watch a movie while either sitting on the floor or on the one chair in the room, which we moved so that at least one of us could sit normally while watching. Ridiculous.
The clincher - the wedding was scheduled for 4pm. We stayed for two nights, and asked for a late check out at 4pm which I know they've offered to other guests. They said they could give me a check out at 2pm, but if I want 4pm, I need to pay the rate for an entire half day's stay! I couldnt believe it, I asked for a manager and explained that I'm part of a wedding party that was getting married in the hotel itself and we wanted the room so we could shower and get dressed, we'd be out by 4pm which is when the wedding starts. Surely they can accomodate that request rather than nickel and dime us for a whole half day when all we need is just two extra hours? Nope, no dice. It didnt matter that the wedding there was generating thousands of dollars in revenue for the hotel. They wanted the extra 150 bucks or whatever it was for a half day rate in order for me to have the room for the additional two hours. 
So, in sum, I wont go back. Theres a ton of hotels in NYC. This one was very expensive and simply didnt deliver. Waste of money.

title: “Glad we stayed!”
text:
Five ladies from Wisconsin stayed at the Hospitality House from May 24 thru the 29th. Five nights. We had no trouble finding it, the entrance is small and not fancy. We had a two bedroom/one bath, full kitchen, living, dining room combined. It was more than enough room. One bedroom had a king bed, the second a queen and the living room area had a full pull out bed in the sofa. Each bedroom had a TV as well as the main room. A few times we could have used another bathroom but we just took turns and finished with makeup, hair etc in the bedrooms. It was nice having the fruit, cereal, muffins, juice and milk every morning. The front desk was helpful. We were mostly there in the late evening as we did alot of the touristy things all day long. We could easily have had another adult with us.
The cost per night was $380.36, this included all fees and taxes. We each paid for one night. We all thought where it was located was great. We would hightly recommend it for a larger group wanting to stay together. Its in a nice area, restaurants right next door and shopping just up the street.

title: “nice hotel”
text: Not as close to the attractions people go to Philidelphia for. But very close to the Reading terminal market.

title: “Great hotel, excellent service”
text:
What a find! We paid a bit more than I wanted to for this hotel, but it was worth it.
We made the mistake of driving our rental car into SF. We had quite a bit of luggage I wanted to drop off at the hotel before we turned our car into the rental place. My husband parked in a tow zone while I sprinted into the hotel with our luggage. A staff member was quick to see my panic and took the luggage, no questions asked. When we arrived to the hotel later that night, they delivered the luggage to our room. The staff was amazingly professional and customer service was clearly their #1 priority. I asked about extra pillows and they were delivered promptly. The staff at the front desk made it clear they cared about whether I slept well or not. I was kind of floored by this.
The room was small but gorgeous. As a space planner myself, I enjoyed discovering ways they planned the small space to be functional. If you stay, notice the door and furniture placement. I didn't feel cramped at all. The room was perfection. We had a courtyard view and it was quiet. We slept with the windows open each night. The free wine and coffee were a nice perk.
The neighborhood was as good as it gets. This is the nicest part of SF, and the safest. We walked on the street at night and always made sure we were close to the hotel by sunset to avoid any precarious situations. There are plenty of food choices nearby and we even got Chinese delivery one night.
This is an excellent hotel. If I ever come back to SF, I will stay here.

title: “Not Bad but needs updating and some cleaning”
text:
Great location near the Riverwalk. Lobby looks great and most of the hotel property; however, the rooms can use improvement. The suites are comfortable and roomy. The carpets are dirty and there is a musty odor in the room. The bathroom toilet needed cleaning and even after housecleaning came to clean it the sides were left dirty. The hotel has a friendly staff and especially the Concierge was outstanding. Both during the day and evening the hotel desk clerks were rude and not welcoming, they could take lessons on respect and a welcoming attitude from the housecleaning staff. The food at a catered event was substandard and bland. You are better off going off hotel property for meals. Nearby ZINCS is outstanding, great food and very reasonable. Across the street DRINK has a decent happy hour. 
All in all, I would stay in the hotel again, however, there are better properties including the WESTIN across the street.

title: “Must love "vintage"”
text: If you don't love "vintage" you may not appreciate the Ocean Park Motel. I wasn't sure what I was getting, but we enjoyed ourselves here. The rooms here are much smaller than you may be used to, but this place has everything you need. The property is beautiful and the staff so helpful. We loved the location. The zoo and the beach are right here. The trolley can't be more convenient and parking is free. We stayed in a queen suite and used the kitchen quite a bit.

title: “Very nice”
text: Good location for business travel. Clean, quality room and facilities. Comfortable bed, big bathroom. Good meeting room, staff attended to us well. I was only there for one night, so your mileage may very.

title: “Great Stay...Hope we can go back...”
text: It has been in my to do list after I back from Holiday in SanDiego. Finally, I got time to write about this great place. My wife and I are from Malaysia and we find out this great place through trip advisor. At 1st we are quite Sceptical about all the great review on this place, until we arrive this wonderful place. The Inn is very clean, tidy and evens a small tiny detail they are doing it so well. The front desk lady is very sweet. She always gives us a lot of information for all the great food we can have in San Diego. We love it so much thank you. This place is located at a very strategic location. For those who do not drive, this is the right place to stay. It is only 5 min walk to Old town Station. It was a very memorable trip, thank you......

title: “Comfortable hotel, convenient location and the staff was great!”
text:
I was in NYC on a business trip in August stayed at the Marcel for approx 10 days. The front desk team was always attentive and helpful with suggestions on restaurants in the area as well as assisting my team who also stayed at the hotel.
The doormen were great! It rained several days while we were there and they had umbrellas ready and let us borrow them to walk to and from work. They were also there with a smile and a warm "Welcome Back" at the end of each work day.
I will definitely stay there again, in fact I will be there in just about a week.
The only issue I had while there was with the a/c and someone from maintenance responded within 15 minutes.

title: “Purse Stolen out of the Lobby”
text: If you stay at this Hampton make sure you keep an eye on your purse. The city bus stop is located on Riverside, right outside the front door. The Hampton parking lot has several signs warning you not to leave valuables in the car. Several pawn shops are located within five miles from this Hampton. The purse was stolen around 7 PM on Thanksgiving Day out of the hotel lobby. We have stayed at this Hampton several times prior to this stay and have enjoyed the employees, the convenient location, and the amenities. Since it was a holiday the "regular" employees were celebrating Thanksgiving with their families.

title: “Shocking !!!!! never again”
text:
My wife and i arrived 06 Nov 07 walked in to reception and thought [--] what have i done. i accept total responsibility for booking this hell hole the room was 8 foot square,plumbing
was the loudest i've ever heard the out look was into more windows,the wardrobe had 2 hangers and only one drawer
the location was a bit out but the subway system was excellent
but a bit dodgy for women at night ,getting the lift was a bit of a wait ,in the morning it was occupied and under the command of the cleaning staff(that's got be the joke of the year)the coffee out of the machine $1 would have been the only value in this joint but it only half filled the cup
Needless to sat the park bench across the street looked inviting
but was too cold.but cleaner

title: “Birthday at Marrakesh Hotel - Satisfying Experience”
text:
Having spent my previous birthday in Marrakesh, Morocco I decided to recapture the feeling by staying in a similarly named hotel for my birthday weekend this year. I was thoroughly satisfied with the experience.
The lounge was beautifully, elegant and definitely taken from a scene in acutal Marrkakesh. The sight of it transported me back in time. The doorman was cordial, the front desk staff was prompt and friendly. I had no problems at all and they tended to my requests in a wonderful fashion.
The room itself was a tad small and clean, but that's how it is in NYC. There was a flatscreen tv with cable, free internet, the bathroom was very clean, but again small. The authentic Morrocan furnishings were sparse, but the wall colors and painting nearly replicated a place we stayed in Casablanca. It was a great birthday treat! I'd stay again and recommend it to others.

title: “The original bedroom from hell”
text:
Just returned from a trip to New York
Stayed at the Hudson Hotel for 4 nights
It has all been said in previous reviews about the rooms
The standard double room sucks
The lighting does not hide the dirt ( stories about hip athmosphere hence the subjued lighting are just that stories and excuses for very weak room standard
I understand that to create athmosphere in the bars and restaurants subjued lighting can be effective , but in my opinion it is definitly not suitable for bathrooms or corridors
leading to the rooms.
The lighting in the bars and sitting areas in the lobby would be definitly an advantage for anyone having an illicit affair ( perhaps thats part of the reason for it )
The staff were wonderful and deserve to be working in a much better hotel.
I wont go into all the normal amenities missing from the first room we were allocated such as facilities for a cup of coffee or a safe for our passports but suffice to say when a safe was put into our upgraded room it was just placed on a shelf so that any body could just put it under their arm and walk away with it
What kind of managerial mentality can do such a thing ? 
Wonderful location. use the room just for sleeping or pitch a tent in the lobby
On second thoughts the tent in the lobby would be the better option.
So to the staff at the hotel i say thank you very much for doing your best to rectify the problems ( see below list )with the first room we were given
Extremly noisy air con unit ( making sleep impossible the first night after an 11 hour flight )
No safe in the room for passports etc/
No tea/coffee facility 
no hairdryer
Black stains on the toilet
Television placed so it was impossible to watch it
Bathroom so small it was almost impossible to use.
Lighting so low made it impossible to read or shave.
Ice machine on our floor not working.
I will certainly not return to this hotel and certainly not reccomend it to anyone
who has any idea of what constitutes a normal room.
Jess Vard
Israel

title: “Just Average”
text: Plain and simple - not up to the Marriott property standard. Our bathtub looked as if it was not cleaned at all. There was hair on each corner of the tub as well as in the tub. Also, it appears somone had rinsed there shoes in the tub as there was black spots of dirt in the tub. When I contacted the desk at 8:30 a.m. the desk agent had housekeeping contact me. House keeping could not come for at least another 15 minutes and I even offered to clean the tub myself if someone would bring a cleaning agent. We had to call guest service also to bring us coffee as it was not replaced when our room should have been cleaned. The watermarks on the bedside table pretty much proved that the room was on "spot" cleaned at best. What a shame for such a beautiful hotel with so much history...

title: “Nice, Clean Place”
text: We had a nice room on the 10th floor with a view of the city. Room was very clean. Twice daily housekeeping was nice for a fresh set of towels and soap. Ice delivered each evening, be sure and ask for a full bucket if you require ice. Nice place, nice room, nice bathroom (deep tub and separate shower). Location is on Rush (Bellevue). Lots of eating/drinking nearby. Close to Watertower place and Michigan shopping. Next time however, will probably stay closer to loop area, just my preference.

title: “Beautiful Decor. Comfortable”
text:
I recently traveled to Los Angeles with my boss. The Redbury had been recommended by other business travelers I know. The decor is really impressive. The rooms are a good size. I love the spacious kitchen and the record player. The bed was also very very comfortable. I would definitely stay here again. It was conveniently located and the parking was easy.
However, my boss & I took some business associates to the restaurant Cleos, for dinner. This was a BAD decision. The food was very flavorful. Alas, it was one of those "bomb went off" deafeningly loud restaurants. It's a real shame. We could not hear each other talk and it just became unpleasant to try and converse. So most of our meal was eaten somewhat quietly. We asked to have the music turned down -which they did for a few songs. And then it was back up loud again. So unpleasant to dine with this level of noise. the food was fantastic -but I would not eat there again due to the sound level.
I really think this hotel is unique and offers a great value when traveling to Los Angeles.

title: “Very impressed”
text: We stayed at La Quinta, Manhattan from 9/26/03-9/28/03. Our room was very nice for NYC. We had hot water and a nice cool room. The A/C worked great! The staff was helpful. There was not a shuttle to the airport. The second day we where there the maid did not leave any clean towels for us. We could see the Empire State building outside our window which was very neat. There was a continenatl breakfast that was tasteful. The elevator did run slow once in while. Location was awesome! I will go back, I was very satisfied.

title: “Great Hotel in Fabulous Location”
text:
Stayed at the Hotel Griffon for 3 days in a standard queen room last week. The hotel and room were very well appointed. It was not the smallest room I've stayed in, but not the largest either. It had an in-room coffee and tea maker. Biggest complaint was the lighting. Since the opaque window looked at four walls, there was very little natural light in the room. Otherwise, there were three small lamps. With every light on in the room and bathroom, it was still pretty dim.
No other complaints, though! Service was great! Location was FABULOUS! Within walking distance to everything. Peet's coffee and tea with fruit in the lobby every morning. Perry's Restaurant had a great patio area with a view of the Bay Bridge--happy hour too!
Overall a great stay. Would definitely stay here again!

title: “4 star prices at 2 star comfort!”
text: The whole resort is on beautiful grounds with a lot of potential to be a luxurious resort. There a few activities that can keep you and your family busy for about 2 or 3 days max. The resort is old and was renovated cheaply only too look good at first glance and in the pictures. The rooms are not clean enough to be satisfactory (hairs in the bathroom, dust webs on lamp shades, dust on bed frame, coffee cup rings on the coffee table) and makes the whole stay uncomfortable. The renovation of the resort was done cheaply and is felt throughout the rooms and suites by having furniture with nicks and cracks and uncomfortable sofa that where the fabric feels part plastic. The room's atmosphere was poor due to bad lighting. There is also the problem of pests; ants in most room. Overall based on the website and the prices I expected a lot more comfort than what the hotel offered. With so many hotel choices and resorts, I will never stay here again.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
I stayed there two months ago and it was a great experience. The check-in was fast, and the front desk attendant was very friendly. She recommended us where to go and how to get to every place in SFO. At 5 pm they had "the wine hour", in which you could taste as much wine as you want, and they had ice cream for kids. 
The room was perfectly cleaned and the bed so comfortable that we overslept the day we stayed there.
Maybe the only problem was that the bathroom was very small, and it didn't have an air extractor, so it was kind of uncomfortable, but since i stayed one night, it wasn't a huge problem.
I would really stay there again.

title: “Great Breakfast!”
text: Loews was in a great location, a brisk but reasonable walk to historical sites. Having a room on the top floor enabled us gorgeous views. We were very disappointed that the pool was closed the day we arrived as we had paid extra to use fitness. Our extra payment included breakfast on our floor and that was fabulous. The staff was very helpful and the room was slightly better than nice. The overall apperance of the hotel was mixed, a little tattered, but the marble and stone walls added elegance.

title: “Loved the hotel for many reasons”
text: My family and I stayed at the Embassy Suites for a week and enjoyed the hotel. The hotel is family friendly with an indoor pool and some video games (50 cents to play). There is a pool table next to the restauraunt, but you might have to wait in line to play. The location was an okay distance from all of the tourist spots. I can't not talk about the free breakfast and managers reception in the afternoon. The food is good and the drinks are also good, and when I tipped the bartender he put a little extra in my drinks, well that was my experience anyway. Overall the room was clean and the service good.

title: “Eeek-Going Green Doesn't Mean Better!”
text:
Okay, I am just going to put this in list form:
Pros:
1. Close to Sea World
2. Large Lobby
3. Business Center w/ Computer Access
4. Somewhat friendly cleaning staff
Cons:
1. Not enough parking! Had to park in a field in front of the property and tote our children to hotel after our Sea World adventure. Not fun in the least!
2. Think that they skimped on the insulation between the rooms to make a 'green' hotel. I could hear the family next to us talking in normal voices at 6 a.m. And I mean every single word.
3. Our water-saving toilet...ran the entire time!
4. They also skimped about 6 inches on the shower curtain! It wouldn't close and you just sat there in the shower and tried to get it to close while showering-very stressful!
5. Comforter was COMPLETELY stained and we didn't notice it until the next morning. The cleaning staff was very nice in changing it for us though.
6. I understand paying for the food you are delivering for room service, but there is a room service delivery charge as well? AND an 18% automatic gratuity? Not sure if this is standard now, but I was very surprised by this.

title: “Fantastic room and location”
text:
We stayed in the hotel for three nights and found it fantastic.
To be fair I will mention all the good and bad points. Good points are the location is second to none, very clean room with a good size ensuite. Bad points are that the room are very dark, windows upagainst a wall and there is no bar or eating facilities. But if your are looking for a well priced hotel in downtown NY then I would definately reccommend it.

title: “Nice little hotel, unbeatable location”
text: Stayed one night for Bay to Breakers run and it was great. Reserved a standard double bed room, saw some complaints about the size of the rooms, but that was not a problem at all. While not huge it was comfortably appointed including coffee maker, refrigerator, desk w/chair, and an additional chair. Room was toward the rear of the hotel and exterior noise was not a problem. We could however occasionally hear the upstairs neighbors, and doors slamming in the hallway.The hotel is historic with great character, but updated with amenities such as flat screen TV and wifi. Appreciated the fact that the entire hotel is non-smoking. The bed was not particularly comfortable, not horrible, but not great. For around $100 per night in the heart of S.F. you can't beat the value. Parking is a steal @ $25 per night. Last time I was in S.F. I paid $50 just for parking.

title: “Excellent Staff and Location”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Hotel Nikko from May 19 to May 21. When we checked in at 11:00 a.m. we were greeted by a very friendly clerk named Juan. He told us our room was ready and it had been upgraded.
 The room was good-sized by San Francisco standards, clean and had a nice view. Moreover, we had an excellent stereo that made our time in the room even better. 
 The hotel's Union Square location in superb. There is also a Starbucks adjacent to the hotel. I highly recommend the Nikko.

title: “Can never book a room for one night!”
text: I've tried booking one night about 6 times over the past 2 months. Never get a room. The hotel always holds aside rooms for convention visitors. I'm told I have to book a 2 night minimum. I'm a corporate client and they won't accommodate me for one night. Bad business. I won't ever contact them again for downtown accommodations.

title: “Great hotel, great service”
text: The Four Points is within walking distance to all of the downtown attractions in San Antonio. The friendly bellman, Christy hooked us up with the trolley schedule, local transportation and taxis. Excellent customer service thru-out the hotel.

title: “Great Location, Great Stay”
text: The Hollywood Orchid suites were great! We were able to check in at about 9am after a long flight from Australia so we were very happy about that. We had a room with a kitchen and it was a good size. The room was quite large as well. The internet was great and worked the whole time we were there - it was extremely fast as well. The breakfast was fine - bagels, bread, cereals, muffins, juice and fruit - a good way to start the day. The location is also excellent! It is so close to the Hollywood strip and also to Universal Studios. So easy to get anywhere from this hotel. The service and security was good as well - you needed a key to get in the door or the car park. We were recommended this place by a friend and were glad we stayed here - overall a great place and we would definately stay here again.

title: “The best location”
text: You could see time square from our room. It was christmas time when I stayed there with some of my family. The hotel was decorated very nicely for the holiday. There are a few very nice shops in the hotel lobby. It is a very large hotel and the elevator system was kind of confusing at first. The room we had was nice but nothing special in my opinion. It had two chairs and a table by the window which was nice since we had a time square view. The bed was nice, I slept well. The best part about the hotel was the location.

title: “Nice Hotel... but check your account upon leaving for unauthorized charges!!!”
text: I purchased a voucher to The Normandy Hotel a few months ago. I really liked the location of the hotel and since the voucher included free daily breakfast and a happy hour I figured what the heck... The stay was nice... I liked the room we had. I just wish the temperature didn’t stay at 74 degrees the entire time. It seems as though we were in a unit that had a set temperature and all they hotel attendees offered was a miniature fan. In all fairness they did also offer to move us to a different room if they temperature didn’t change OR if we just preferred to move. The breakfast was continental style with a few extra goodies... like Canadian bacon and boiled eggs... nothing too fancy but it was a nice extra. The service was wonderful throughout our stay EXCEPT it took 45 minutes to get fresh towels and parking is 28$ per night if you decided to use the garage... the good news is there is FREE street parking. The part that made me upset is that the hotel made 3 unauthorized charges on my account. In total they charged me $138 that I did not give them permission to take and had I not been a person who checks my account they would have gotten away with it. On top of that I have to wait to get MY money back... this is bananas! If you reserve a room at this hotel just make sure you check your account when you leave... other than that I would have given them four starts but now Im giving them two because you just DONT mess with people’s money and their accounts ESPECIALLY during a recession!

title: “Convenient and cheap...but you get what you pay for”
text:
Hotels in NY are generally expensive. This one is cheap. I was just there on a business trip and stayed one night. It is very convenient...we were able to walk everywhere. I agree that the rooms definitely need updating.....it is very dated. We had no problems with the staff being rude, they seemed polite. 
It's no worse then your typcial hotel at the Jersey shore....if you know what I mean. It served our purpose....we weren't in the room much at all.

title: “Outstanding Restaurant”
text: My husband and I stayed here on May 1 and May 2 while I was receiving treatment at UCLA Medical Center. We ate there both days and were very pleased with not only the food, but the staff as well. The staff was very polite and attentive to anything we needed. I spoke with the manager, Jose Ortega, to inform him how much we enjoyed our dining experience. I wish I could remember the name of the busboy who was especially helpful. Although he was not a waiter, he should be!!!! Thank you again for making a difficult time better.

title: “Fantastic Service and Wonderful Rooms”
text: This is a beautiful hotel very close to the Convention Center. The rates in December were fantastic- under 100 dollars per night. The service and the hotel were fantastic. The only complaint I had was the cost of parking per night - we had two vehicles and it cost 42 dollars per night to park them ---- ouch!

title: “Anything you could possibly need!”
text:
My mom and I stayed here for 2 nights on a short vacation to Seattle and were extremely happy with our accommodations here.
Check in was a breeze (if only our car rental had gone as smoothly) and the front desk clerk was cordial and friendly, giving us suggestions for attractions and dining nearby.
The room was clean and comfortable, and included a fridge, sink, coffee maker, and microwave in a pseudo "bar" area. They even included paper plates and utensils. 
Front desk and guest services were cordial and helpful, bringing me a full service set of extra coffee, mugs, spoons, sugar, half/half (which I suspect they borrowed from their on-site restaurant, Emerald Grill), when I only asked for extra packets of coffee and cream!
One of the best things about this hotel was the full business center, open 24-hours, which is FREE to hotel guests. It was spacious (not like the closet-sized ones I've used in other hotels), had 2 computer stations with printers and a copy machine... all free of charge. I was able to get some late night work done thanks to Holiday Inn.
My only two minor complaints are that the bathroom was rather small, and the indoor parking spaces ($10 per night) were also too small to fit a standard/full size sedan and most people ended up taking two spaces.
Overall, I am extremely happy with my stay here and wouldn't hesitate to go back.

title: “Outstanding personal attention and lots of personality”
text:
In October 2011, I planned a six-night trip to the East Coast. Initially planned as a New York City visit with a day trip to Philadelphia, it was eventually changed into an open-jaw itinerary where I would actually fly into Philadelphia first and spend the first two nights there. As I had never overnighted in Philadelphia before, I had to do some serious amounts of research to pick a hotel that I could accept. Eventually I booked at Alexander Inn, and am extremely glad to have done so.
- Booking -
The hotel takes reservations directly at its website. What I found charming right away is that the hotel's rates do not fluctuate with the seasons, but stay constant. The rates are also very reasonable; I paid about $150 per night including all taxes and fees for a very charming double.
- Location -
The hotel is located four blocks or so south of Market Street, the main east-west thoroughfare of Philadelphia City Center. It is not too far from Broad Street either. Both Market and Broad have subway lines, so this makes for very convenient mass transit access. Independence Hall is also a short walk away, as is the antiques district. Even the Franklin Institute and other museums are within a long walk of this hotel.
Moreover, the hotel's location is smack in the middle of Philadelphia's gay district, which makes for very good amount of energy especially when it comes to dining and nightlife. The hotel is a member of IGLTA (International Gay & Lesbian Travel Association) according to the website, and does seem to cater to gay male couples who travel often and have discerning tastes. This single lesbian, traveling solo, did just as well.
- Service -
The hotel feels a lot like European urban hotels; it is located on a very narrow strip of land, and holds only eight rooms per floor. The ground floor has the breakfast room and lounge; free continental breakfast is served daily. The basement has housekeeping department as well as a well-equipped gym that also hosts complimentary Internet stations. One elevator serves all the floors; it is small and slow but gets the job done quite well, and even has visitor information inside.
When I arrived in the morning hours, the reception was very happy to hold my luggage until the check-in time. The receptionist (older gentleman) even made sure to give me his name on a business card, so that I could call the hotel back to see if early check-in could be possible. The personal touch continued - the hotel staff continued to address me not merely as "ma'am" but by my name. The reception desk is also very happy to provide sightseeing tips for the Philadelphia area, which I appreciated immensely.
- Room -
My room was a nicely equipped double on the sixth floor. It had a window cubicle that extended beyond the wall, for a bit extra space. The bed was very comfortable. There was a sizable closet as well. The television hung above the closet, and while it was not of the modern flat-screen variety, it did have ample selection of channels, including Philadelphia visitor information. The bathroom was well stocked with top-notch toiletries, though it only had a nice shower rather than a full bath.
My only negative about the room (and the hotel for that matter) is wireless Internet access; the signal was quite weak from my room, 607, which was toward the far end of the floor, and my iPad was occasionally losing the signal.
- Afterthoughts -
This is a very charming hotel and I am glad to have stayed there. While I am used to staying at properties like this when traveling in places like Europe, I rarely do when traveling stateside. It made my experience all the more memorable, combined with the ultimate in personal attention from the staff. The location was fantastic as well.
This was my first overnight trip to Philadelphia, and I picked a great hotel. I will not hesitate to book here again for my future Philadelphia visits.

title: “Great location, helpful staff and comfortable rooms”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights in May 2012, having stayed at this Club Quarters a few years ago. The hotel is in a great location, with transport links very nearby, just two blocks from State T station. The hotel is central to several local attractions, including Quincy Market, Boylston shopping area and Boston Common. The hotel itself has a nice feel, with comfortable rooms and staff who were very helpful. We have no complaints, and would happily stay here again when visiting Boston.

title: “GOOD BUT NOT AS GOOD AS LAST TIME”
text:
We have just stayed 6 nights at ON THE AVE HOTEL in a penthouse suite (1509). We last stayed at ON THE AVE two years ago (Oct 2010) in a panoramic deluxe room (1407) and loved our stay. I placed a positive review on Tripadvisor at the time. We were a group of six this time so we took three rooms but I will only review my experience based on the one room (penthouse suite).
At the time of booking the recent stay I was concerned about two issues. The first was the new construction next to the hotel and the second was the slipping standards of the hotel, both of these have been written about on Tripadvisor.
Starting with the first issue of the adjacent construction, I wrote to the hotel shortly after booking expressing my concern that I didn't want our stay affected by noise and dust. Angie, the Front Office Manager responded immediately in a positive way by confirming that we will be accommodated as far from the construction as possible, which i can happily say we were so I thank her very much for this.
On the second issue of slipping standards, we noticed this time that housekeeping was NOT up to the standards we would have liked. Our carpets were really badly stained (which puts me off a hotel room immediately as its so in your face). A water bottle from a previous guest was under our bed for our entire stay of 6 nights and there was a tube of the body wash (from the bathroom amenities) under the chest of drawers also for the duration of our stay. Also our shower blocked (rectified after reporting it), the shower leaked onto the bathroom floor and there was not a spare roll of toilet paper and no bath floor mats one day (both rectified after we called guest services) but these things shouldn't happen with a good well supervised housekeeping department. 
The suite had no outdoor terrace furniture which disappointed us to a degree and the suite was very compact not really earning the title of a PENTHOUSE SUITE in my personal opinion but in keeping with the rate charged so this was not a big deal to us.
On checking out I was disappointed in the way the process was handled for the following reasons:
1/ We were not presented with our bill for checking. We were told what the total was and that was it. In all other hotels I have stayed at I have been given the bill for final review.
2/ The lady checking us out was confused about what we had already paid on check-in and what card (out of the two we used) had been charged already. She eventually sorted it out.
3/ To me this is the biggest mistake of all. The check-out staff member didn't ask us if we enjoyed our stay. I would have thought this was one of the most important and fundamental questions. Maybe it's not done in New York but I can't think of a hotel anywhere in the world where this question doesn't get asked. Does this mean that they don't really care?
Taking everything into consideration we still enjoyed our stay realizing that the rates are good for NYC for what we got. I really hope that the hotel will consider re-furbishing the rooms and lobby sometime so that we can stay there again. 
The location is really great, and so are many of the nearby restaurants. Serafina's Restaurant in the hotel on the ground floor offers good food (we ate there twice).

title: “Great Experience and Awesome Dance Club!”
text: I stayed with a friend at the Omni Houston Hotel for two nights in late August, and really enjoyed my time there. Since the weather was unbelievably hot and humid outside during our stay, it was quite refreshing entering the hotel to be cooled off. The quality of the room service food was terrific, (we ordered one breakfast and one dinner) and the concierge service was remarkable. Although we did not get a chance to use the pool since we had so many other items on our agenda, we had a great view of it and would have used it had we stayed for longer. Also, We spent a Saturday night at the Black Swan Dance Club which was a super fun experience!

title: “Magnificent Hotel and Central Location”
text: Booked this hotel through Expedia with no issues. From the time you enter the hotel lobby you feel welcome. The hotel and rooms are wonderfully decorated and staff make you feel right at home. The rooms are huge and super clean. Very comfortable beds. We had a very comfortable King suite with walk in closet and safe. We asked for a high floor quiet room and were accomodated. The room looked into an adjacent building wall but was so quiet as a result. You'd never know you were in the centre of Manhatten. Great location just a few blocks to the subway, time square, rockerfeller centre and broadway. You can walk everywhere or just get on the subway. Very safe area to walk around. The hotel includes a quick cofee/tea and pastry to start your morning with. This is enough to get you going. Very helpfull staff and doorman. Wouldn't hesitate to stay here.

title: “A Little Gem”
text: Our stay here was fabulous, Christian checked us in which was quick and easy. The rooms have everything you need plus some. The queen bed and pillows were the best so comfortable. Our only complaint is that the rooms are very small but apart from this great. The Staff very friendly. Free internet was a bonus as we used this a few times to contact our travel agent. Location for us was great , a block from Penn Station, which we used to travel to Washington DC. Directly across the street is a 99cents Jacks which sells everything and I mean everything, which was very handy for us. Over all we loved this hotel it really felt like home whilst we were in New York. Breakfast was adequent

title: “Perfect location!!”
text: Newbury Guest House is one of the best boutique hotels I have ever visited. From the moment we enter the hotel we were treated with first class service. Everyone at the hotel meets you with a smile and is willing to go the extra mile. It is located on the very trendy Newbury Street--perfect location. This hotel is a must when in Boston!!

title: “It is all the "little things" the hotel and staff did to make our trip to NYC one we will remember..Thank you!”
text: Fashion 26 was a fabulous place to stay! The staff was so friendly and willing to please. We were greeted by the doorman, Leo and the GM, Wayne Schneider. Their friendliness was the beginning of our wonderful stay.. The hotel is stylish, immaculate, yet warm and inviting. Did I say clean? It is soo clean!! The rooms are not huge, but the attention to detail and touches of luxury make up for it.. The high thread count bedding was awesome. I just loved the comfy bed w/ soft bedding and lots of pillows! We ate at Rare which had fabulous burgers, salads and appetizers ... even breakfast was delicious. My favorite was the rooftop bar which offered amazing views of the ESB and city.. I can't wait to come stay during the warmer weather when the roof top is open.. I stayed with a group ranging in ages. The children were greeted with rubber ducks in their sinks, cupcakes for dessert and much more. The adults had an atmosphere that was fun, but not stuffy. All the staff was so wonderful... which you do not find anymore. I just loved our stay and can't wait to go back. Thanks for making our stay special<3 I do not have one negative..

title: “Nice surprise!”
text: Our softball team booked with Jameson Inn for girl's softball nationals. Hotel is very clean and someone is always at front desk. Loved the matching uniforms the housekeepers had, they were also very nice and helpful. Breakfast was ok, waffel makers are nice.

title: “Frank and Albert Restaurant”
text: Sarah my waitress was the best. She recommended a fabulous chicken salad sans the pineapple(which I did not want). Even went out of her way to get me a personal item from he gift shop. I have never had this type of service before. I highly recommend this restaurant the food is amazing.

title: “Loved this hotel”
text:
When planning this too brief stay in San Francisco I couldnt decide if Union Square or the Fisherman's Wharf area would be best.
I am glad we decided on Fisherman's Wharf and especially glad we chose the Radisson Hotel.
The front desk staff were very welcoming and polite. And at checkout thanked us for staying and said they hoped we enjoyed our stay and it wasnt just by rote.
We didnt have a room with sleep number beds but the beds were very comfortable just the same with lovely bedding. Very well kept and clean.
The windows opened!!!-a bonus for us- and we had a great view of the bridge(in the distance), bay and Alcatraz. Free room safe, coffee and tea.
The hotel as mentioned by others does not have a restaurant for breakfast but it is literally next door to an IHOP and you can purchse a continental breakfast off a "cart" in the Lobby.
There is a Johnny Rockets fast food type restaurant as well as an exit right to the piers behind the small pool area.
Also there is an ATM machine just around the corner along with a 7 to 11 store.To the right as you exit the hotel.
Great location walked everywhere we wanted to go and loved Fisherman's Wharf even though it was very crowded. We were tourists! and part of the crowd!

title: “Customer service at it's best!!!”
text:
We had an amazing time at the Olive 8...it exceeded our expectations in every way. We weren't quite sure what to expect since this was our first stay with them but WOW! Everything was so organized and friendly that you'd swear you were someone important...clearly we're not :). 
THE ROOM...
We originally had booked a regular room but upon check in we were warmly welcomed and informed that we had been upgraded to a corner suite. It was a beautiful room with floor to ceiling windows that looked out to the Paramount Theater. The room was incredibly beautiful! 
ROOM SERVICE...(big kudos)
We decided to get room service that night to enjoy our anniversary evening in a private setting and after placing our order we were informed that we would be receiving a 20% discount on any room service orders during our stay. The food came even earlier than expected and was delicious. The gentleman who delivered our food even offered to open and pour our own bottle of wine at no additional cost...not a common practice in other hotels we've stayed in. 
OVERALL...
Long story short is you absolutely cannot go wrong if you decide to stay at the Hyatt Olive 8...truly one of the best experiences we've ever had. They re-established our confidence that some hotels really do care about their customers and want to do everything they can to ensure you've enjoyed your stay. 
FRONT DESK...
I also wanted to mention that we thoroughly enjoyed the professional and friendly gentleman that checked us in at the front desk. It really started our special weekend out just how we dreamed...thanks for making us feel like we really do matter and we wish you all the best. I can't remember his name right now but I believe he is from Hawaii :)...aloha to our friend!

title: “Good Quality”
text:
Stayed here on buisness in April. Its a good standard Westin, bit awkward for parking but ill forgive them that. Staff are welcoming and friendly and well versed on the city. The food is very good and fresh. The cocktails are to die for, very nice! Rooms are good quality and well maintained. 
As a buisness hotel, its well equiped, good wifi and nice buisness center. Overall I was very happy. I will be back in September for a conference.

title: “NYC”
text: It was a last minute visit, and its location near Penn Station, ESB and other major attractions was perfect! My room was clean and comfortable, checking in was fast and efficient; the front desk staff and housekeepers were professionals and attentive, with the exception of one their so called 'concierge'. Another plus is its proximity to Korea Town for cheap and delicious food! I will stay again!

title: “Crappy crap crap crap”
text:
I was just about to post a scathing review of this crummy hotel and the high speed crapped out. A cap of crap on a crappy hotel 
If you like hotels where things don't work and they pretend to care, this is for you. They do great lip service but no other kind. 
The price is high and the service almost approaches Motel 6. 
And tney don't clean the rooms unless you ask. 
Stay away.

title: “Deserves 6 stars”
text: Convenient location at epicenter of Tribeca/Soho; short walk to Chinatown/Little Italy/East Village/World Trade Ctr site. Bright, updated, pleasant lobby & public areas. Very spacious well-appointed rooms by NYC standards. Nice modern bathrooms. Most extensive cable selections of any hotel we've ever seen. Free internet. Staff friendlier and more accomodating than you'd get in Manhattan, KANSAS, much less NYC. Great 24/7 business center w/computers, printers, copiers, etc. In sum: a WINNER!

title: “What can I say... Poor, Poor & Poor”
text:
Stayed here over the weekend for a short business trip and although I loved the location I was absolutely appalled with almost everything else! I don't know how to begin but here goes.
Arrival: As I was driving a rented car, I needed to park my car temporarily to check-in (for about 10 minutes or so) but the gentlemen at the driveway insisted that I can't do that. In the end, I have to return the car 3 blocks away with half of my luggage (I dropped off 1 bag and left it at reception) and walk to the hotel with the luggage. Appalling!
Check-in: Check-in was relatively efficient.
Concierge: Appalling - I asked a relatively simple question - i.e. What time does the Smithsonian museums close during summer. She informed me it's a 5pm. Luckily I took the chance and went there anyway (as I thought they have longer hours in summer) - they were open until 7pm! I found out later that that information is on the front page of their website! Concierge should verify the information!
Service to the rooms: My room was missing a in-room dining menu and I requested for it. It took them one and a half hours to bring them to me. Also, housekeeping did not add an additional shower gel on the 2nd day and I requested for one. Took them 45 minutes to bring it up and the gentlemen told me that if I want more, I can get them myself as the trolley is parked just down the corridor. Is this what you call Service Express??? 
On the day of my checkout, housekeeping showed up at 9am (on a Sunday morning) to prompt me that I am checking out. As a gold SPG member, I have 4pm checkout rites (which I have informed the reception and got confirmation of that). It is rather intrusive and rude.
Reception: It is common practice that the reception of a hotel should carry change for the convenience of their guests. This one does not. In fact, the lady at the counter informs me (rather rudely) that they have only 100 dollar notes and I should buy something at the shop to get change. Which I did. This is not acceptable for a Starwood hotel.
Food: Breakfast is good albeit without variation. Had dinner once at the same restaurant and I was surprised to see a grasshopper in my salad (after I finished half of the salad). If I was not paying attention, I'd have consumed a rather exotic source of protein. However, the waitress was apologetic and they gave me a complimentary desert. Best service I received in my entire stay.
All in all, poor, Poor & POOR!

title: “Reliable comfort- price may vary”
text:
Just got badk from visiting our son who is at SMU in Dallas. We have stayed less expensive places, but when I can find the Palomar at a reasonable rate I grab it, because I know my bed will be clean and comfortable with those nice Italian linens, I will have a nice comfortable seating area in my room and a neat bathroom. I have always had friendly service in staying here. They often have manager's special wine receptions and the pool area is fantastic. Valet parking is expensive, (it is Dallas). If you join the Kimpton loyalty club for no charge, then you get free internet. 
One thing I've noticed is that the price can vary quite a bit depending on what is going on- I have seen it listed as quite expensive, then other times it has been cheaper than the Hampton Inn. Always worth looking around, then calling them to get them to match the best price you find..

title: “Location, location, location!”
text: This hotel is great value for money and situated in an ideal location. 20 minutes one way you are in central park, 10 minutes the other way times square and 20 minutes ahead 5th avenue! Situated a few blocks away from broadway you could not ask for more! The only downside was the rooms were a little small but they were clean and let's face it your in new York- you're not going to be spending much time in your room only somewhere to store your shopping bags!

title: “A Great Place to Stay”
text: The Iroquois hotel not only looks great it is a great place to stay. The staff is amazing and really goes above and beyond the call of duty. Every staff member you see says hello. Recently when I was staying at the hotel, one of my favorite shows The Game was premiering after a two year break,but unfortunately the hotel does not carry the channel BET. So I asked Caroline at the front desk if there was any way to view this channel to see the premier. Caroline advised that she would see what she could do and check with the staff to see if any could DVR the show and provide me with a copy. So the show premier Tuesday at 10pm and Wednesday morning when I woke up under my door was a copy of the premier. This staff is great! Thank you Caroline and Alex for all your efforts!

title: “Awesome place!!!! top-notch staff!!!”
text:
Our stay at the Yotel was fantastic! Instead of a stuffy front counter like in other hotels, staff greet you outside and in the open lobby. They always took the time to ask how your day was or if you need any help. The bar on the fourth floor has a beautiful outside patio with friendly staff as well. What a cool place to have a few drinks.The rooms were compact and had everything you need. We didn't spend much time in them. You couldn't get a better location either! 
It was our first time in NYC and we will stay there next time. 
We have been a lot of places, but have never experienced the cool, relaxed treatment we received from all staff. Top Notch!!!
Thanks Apollo and Hoolio for pointing us in the right direction every day! Special thanks to Kelly and Jamie our favorite bartenders too!!! And we can't forget Jimmy at the desk and all the others we met but can't remember their names.
see you maybe this fall!!!
Rob & Becky
Brighton, ON Canada

title: “Could have been cleaner, nice location for convention”
text:
This stay was very average for the Hyatt. The checking-in process was amazingly easy (all online); however, there was a line almost to the door during the busy times in the afternoon. Obviously, there are some staffing issues that need to be addressed. The hotel is very busy during my stay; there were at least three other meetings besides my own. 
Room service was quick and friendly, but I have to agree with the other reviewers who state the food is awful. I ate other food provided by the hotel during my meeting and found it to be equally mediocre. On the plus side, the coffee shop does a wonderful latte, and the staff there was excellent.
My room needed a new shower curtain (many rust stains) and the shower vent needed a thorough cleaning (caked with dust). I requested this be done after the first night, but it was never done. We also had to request for tolietries to be replaced which is a huge pet peeve of mine. Why is this so hard for housekeeping staff to do especially when there is a $5 tip sitting next to the empty bottles?
The bed was average. I liked the flat screen TV and the desk set up in the room. It was great for our laptop and eating room service.
The location is the main appeal of this hotel. I was so happy to be staying close by when I was hobbling along in high heels. It is a short walk to the 16th St mall and all the other fun downtown sights.

title: “Great location”
text: We stayed one night for a city vacation. This is a wonderful walking neighborhood with restaurants, bars and Lincoln Park. The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful. Vallet parking was worth the $20.00. A word of warning -- the doorway for our room and the bathroom were narrow but the room itself was big. The refrigerator and microwave were a bonus. Breakfast was adequate with cereals and fresh sweezed juice. The hotel was clean and a good value for Chicago.

title: “ALWAYS comfortable”
text: We travel to Houston frequently for medical care for my son. We are faithful to the Marriott brand and are never disappointed. This facility however is always TOPS on our list! The staff is very helpful, the rooms always clean and very comfortable and the breakfast is WONDERFUL especially considering its free. Great selection / variety of food and well prepared...better than Denny's or IHOP any day!!! Since this location is minutes from the Medical Center we stay here frequently. Due to my son's medical issues cleanliness is always on the top of our list of priorities when we travel. We can depend on Marriott properties to provide a safe hassle free environment that makes our trips away from home more comfortable. THANK YOU!!!

title: “Nice Stay for the Night”
text: Everything worked out great to stay the night before our flight...the only thing I would have them change is to get new pillows - ours were lumpy...

title: “Great Service!”
text: We came to Philly for a wedding with little time and money to spend. This hotel gave great service at a great price. Everyone was helpful and accommodating to our needs. The room was lovely--a terrific view and comfortable beds. We didn't have a chance to use the spa but we toured it and it looked fantastic. Side note: as we got out of our car after a 4 hour trip my 10 year old threw up in front of the hotel. The staff not only cleaned it up before I could turn around but they asked after her health and comfort through the next day.

title: “More for less!”
text: I have been a guest at Park Central for the past 7 weeks on business. Initially my room was very small, with a beautiful view of a brick wall. That is my only complaint, the front desk attendant agreed quickly due to the length of my stay that room was unsuitable. Yes, there has been a glitch or two, multiple check out-check ins, but Drita the guest services manager ironed them out without a blink of an eye. If every hotel had a Drita, no-one would ever have complaints! I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a great value, location, and quality of service!

title: “Great location and view”
text: We stayed in a stunning park-view room on a relatively high floor. The view was absolutely gorgeous, we never shut our blind! The decor in the room was awesome too; it fit well with the era of the hotel. The rooms, and particularly the bathroom, aren't modern, but they were spotlessly clean and again, fit in with the era of the hotel. The location was so convenient - it was nice to go for a stroll in the park when we felt like it, there were two subway stations in close proximity, Sarabeths next door was great for meals, as was the food court at the Plaza Hotel. My only complaint was that the staff in the lobby could have been more helpful/professional at times. We also realized only after our stay that continental breakfast was included - this was never mentioned to us during our stay. Overall, we enjoyed our time at the Helmsley Park Lane, mostly due to the view and location.

title: “Scrambeling cock roaches!”
text: Well the title says it all. Evertime I turned on the kitchen light there they were. My husband noticed bigger cockroaches outside. Not good. Kitchen is old and dated. They charge you $8.00 for parking that they don't tell you so be careful. On the plus side great location (you can walk to the galleria) big rooms but is not as nice as they residence inn in Albuquerque. This will not stop future trip reservations. But by the time they tack on the taxes and parking, your not getting a deal.

title: “Be aware”
text: We booked about a month prior to arrival, but upon it hotel stuff at reception informed us that they didn't receive any notification from booking.com and can't check us in since they're booked up. They phoned a nearby hotel and book a room for us, but $20/night more expensive. I booked via internet many times, but faced such dejective situation for the first time.

title: “Brilliant Trip of a lifetime”
text:
This was our first trip to New York to celebrate our wedding anniversary and we loved every minute of our stay. This hotel was fanatstic!
We stayed in a King Deluxe City View room on the 11th floor and we had the most amazing view out of our window!! The room was immaculate and I cannot fault anything. It was a decent sized room as I have noticed a few people saying rooms in NY are small. But the room was spacious and very clean. The bed was huge and extremely comfortable and my husband and I slept great. We heard little noise from the streets and traffic below. The bathroom was also great, fantastic shower and plenty of fresh towels. If you forget anything toiletries wise then reception can get it for you!! And again everything was very clean. 
Location was not a problem and we didn't mind having to walk a short 10 - 15 mins to Times Square, there are also plenty of lovely places to eat nearby a couple of blocks away. This meant we could enjoy the hussle and bussle of the inner city and the more peaceful side as well. I would also say getting a taxi anywhere shouldn't be a bother as we seen plenty of them passing and stopping at the hotel.
The rooftop bar is amazing, such a great place to chill after a busy day. I'll never forget the view. Drinks didn't seem any more pricey than anywhere else in NY. You definetley need to check it out.
The room service was superb, food was great and most of the staff were pleasant. I can't say anyone stood out in terms of service but we still enjoyed our stay. We would both stay here again.

title: “Good - but busy busy and can't handle it!”
text:
Overall a clean hotel, no real massive issues, very good location. Only issue was when we wanted to get our bags collected from our room and we waited a good half hour to even speak to the baggage folk. 
Overall good though. Wouldn't stay there again tho.

title: “Just OK”
text: Stayed one night while in town on business. Chose this hotel for two reasons: close to the location of my conference & the great rate I got on this hotel thru Expedia. Room was clean, nice Select Number king bed, and the waitress in the restaurant at breakfast was very friendly & efficient. The front desk personnel were not overly friendly. Of course, since it was near the airport, it was noisy in early evening & early morning. The room was clean but dark, even with 4 lamps lit, and the air conditioner unit was noisy. The room was either hot or too cold after running it for a while. The place is obviously older, & could use some upkeep/update, but it was clean & room was good size. It is "average", low 3-star rating by my estimation, but for the price was a good stay.

title: “Enjoyed my stay, good service & location.”
text:
We went to New York with six people and I was dreading the cost as we
were somewhat on a budget and in NY, your dollar doesn't stretch that
far. I booked the Morningside Inn as a compromise and was glad that I did.
The location is good, easy for the subway (four blocks walk down to 103rd street - we always took breakfast on the way from one of the decent, cheap restaurants there) and subway is about quarter of an hour into Time Sq. Didn't entirely feel comfortable with the area late at night but you could easily have caught a cab back as its not far out of the city. Tick for location.
When we turned up, the manager was unable to satisfy the booking as the internet had only shown my booking as one room not two. Not a problem - the manager sorted out extra beds for the room. While this mmigth not satisfy everyone, we were happy as the rooms were bigger than anything else that I had seen. all our requests (extra towels etc) were met with a smile and staff overall were helpful and happy. I ordered tickets off ebay and they were delivered and held by the fornt desk and given to me without even asking (I had forgotten!!)
Rooms were clean and warm (it was five degrees at the time in NYC!!! In April!!) and everything seemed to work. Beds were comfortable and while its no luxury location, it provides good, clean accommodation at a sensible price.
