I was happy and would happily return. By the way party of six was two girls, four blokes and we ordered a four person suite and a superior room with en suite. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking to spend their money or more important things in new York but that still want a nice, clean room to return to.

title: “great!”
text:
I stayed at the Westin Times Square last weekend for the first time. Had a corner room on the 41st floor with views of the Hudson River and Statue of Liberty. It was awesome! The hotel is in a great location, the subway is right there. Times Square is also right there. We originally had reservations at the Sofitel but changed them last minute, I am glad we did, it is off the beaten path. Skip Chevy's Mexican Rest., it located between the lobby and the theatres. It was overpriced and not that good. 
The Westin heavenly beds are the best. The heavenly shower was wonderful. There is not a long wait for the elevators, the Marriott Marquis is notorious for this.
We had dinner at TAO. It was delicious. I strongly recommend staying at Westin and becoming a Starwood prefered member. I am planning to stay there next time I am back in beautiful NYC.

title: “Best hotel of trip to Texas”
text: The staff in this hotel were outstandingly friendly, warm, and informative, and the lobby worth a trip on its own. Both factors contributed to setting the tone for our stay here. As others have mentioned, staying in the new part of this hotel requires an awkward trip involving two elevators and halls from the lobby, but our room was great, with a view and balcony overlooking the San Fernando Church and the beginning of the Riverwalk. There is easy access downstairs to the Riverwalk, and the The Alamo is a few blocks away. We loved the roof pool and its view of the city, and the breakfast and happy hour events.

title: “Nice choice”
text: Good location only a few blocks from Penn Station. Comfortable hotel with very helpful desk staff. Quiet, clean, nice room for NYC

title: “BEST CONCIERGE ON EARTH”
text:
Not to overshadow the rest of the Alexis staff, but we had the most incredible trip to Seattle because of the Alexis Hotel Concierge, Russell Hathaway. It was New Years Eve and we had never been to Seattle before. He - in so many words - planned out our entire itinerary. He made us multiple dinner reservations and let us choose where to go, laid out options for activities for the day and sent us champagne to our room for our anniversary. He went way above and beyond the call of duty and made our stay one we will never ever forget. Thank you, Russell.
In addition to the fabulous concierge, we loved the Alexis. It was walking distance to anything and everything - notably great restaurants and the pier. 
I would recommend the ferry to Bainbridge Island and the Underground Tour. Both made for fun and exciting days. 
I would definitely recommend the Alexis. Chic digs, great hotel bar called The Bookstore (we spent a lot of time there, it really is a gem) and kind, wonderful staff. We loved every minute of our stay.

title: “Great base for San Diego visit”
text: Not only are the views lovely but the location is perfect. The restaurants of the Gas Lamp Discount are conveniently across the street and it's easy to walk around the bay to the Maritime Museum. This is a large Hilton and if you are looking for a small boutique hotel, this is not the place for you but it is a very nice hotel. There is a nice pool and a spa (we didn't use the spa). Our room was on a high floor, the bed was very comfortable and I loved the chaise in front of the window! As honors Gold members we received discount coupons for the breakfast buffet and we dined there one morning. The selections were good and the service excellent. The 50% discount made it worth the money but without the discount, I think it makes more sense to go into the Gas Lamp District for breakfast. The Dole ship was unloading and I agree with others, it was fun to watch the process.

title: “A reasonable hotel option to see Washington DC”
text:
This hotel was very conveniently located about 5 blocks from the Whitehouse, 2 blocks from the metro and close by to several good restaurants (we recommend the Sichuan Pavillion, a great Chinese place on K street). There was also a CVS a block down. 
The rooms were a good size and there was a gym and pool free for guests to use. We did not use them however, so I am not sure on the size or equipment they feature. The rooms do not have a refrigerator, but they did have an iron and hairdryer. WiFi was offered in the lobby, but you must connect via Ethernet in the rooms. This was free of charge.
Down points are the parking costs at $38 a night - valet only, and the restaurant was poor in terms of quality, variety and cost. The cost of parking was higher than other local garages, so it felt to me like they prey a little on their guests.
The staff were very helpful and accommodating, despite us booking via Priceline at a reduced rate. Check-in was a little slow. Overall, we would go again, but we would not eat breakfast at the hotel.

title: “The worst place to spend a weekend - dont go there”
text:
The pictures here is not about nearly neighbourhood. All that hood smells like sever, be sure there is many dangerous individuals - gang members - i m not kiddin, taxi driver tell us after our horror weekend few necessary rules about life there. 
We heard that most provoking colours are red and blue, cause main streetgangs wear just this kind of clothes.
In the kitchen were ants... The hispanic woman-manager(maybe Jessie...) is really LIAR. She charged me $100 cause i smoked in balcony in front of rooom - not in room. First evening told me that i cant smoke just inside. It was no chance to discussion with her. 
And bonus - last night(about midnight) was running around our door crazy junkie guy screamin something about he was biting by snake - nothing nice... 
We, 4 slovak guys comming there from South Dakota were spending there just 3 nights but never more in Mission Inn.
Better under Golden Gate =)))
Tommy

title: “Suprisingly nice! Dont be worried about old reviews, this place was redone.”
text: I was worried when I had read some older reviews about this hotel. For the price I paid (under $100 per night!) It seemed too good to be true (or scary) when I booked it. The only other choice even close to the price was a best western, which was also concerning. But even though the outside of the hotel is a little dated, the lobby and rooms were very recently updated and comfortable. The room was not huge, but not small either. The bed was unbelieveably comfy and had nice linens instead of a nasty hotel bedspread. There was a flat screen tv, a mini fridge and a coffee maker. The ony things to note was there is either heat or AC depending on what system is on for the entire hotel, so one night we opened our window at night and closed it in the morning when it cooled down. Also the bathroom sink, although it had a nice big granite top, the basin is strangely small. This hotel was only a $5-$7cab ride to the museum, shedd aquarium and soldier field. The room rate was charged correctly and I wasn't even asked for my AAA card to get the discounted rate. If you are looking for a hilton, there is one right next door, but it is a nice respectable hotel and I was glad I rolled the dice. The best breakfast is at Yolks which 2 block south on Michigan.

title: “great location.... but?”
text:
First trip to NYC and alot of careful thought into chosing the "right" hotel, with the great help from tripavidsor reviews.
Location - absolutely fantastic!! - slap bang in the middle of Times Square - you weren't joking were you? 
Check in smooth and courteous, asked for a high level front facing room and got it no problem. View on to Times Square area first class! All the action day or night, but surpisingly very little noise!
Room, if I am honest was a little disappointing: "tired" looking, bathroom and general lighting very poor. Beds very comfortable!! - Linen a little worn - holes in sheets some days
Maid service very shoddy: family of 3 staying in 1 room and consistantly only enough towels / coffee / cups etc for 2 despite daily reminders - not a big deal, but it does take the edge off, having to keep asking for basics that should be there!
Heard about Conceiage "OMAH" and he really did live up to his name: he was great, giving us sound advice from someone who really did know what he was talking about - and a great guy too! Excellent.
Did not eat at the Hotel - too many places to try out - the deli's were fantastic - especially Maxi's deli / bar / restaurant just over the road - went there every other day - too full to eat there every day!!! New York food portions are s000 big!!!
Highly recommend the water taxi service - what a great way to see Manhattan and so inexpensive too!
Would I come back to New York - YES - have already planned our next trip, and are seriously thinking about staying at the Doubletree Suites opposite the Rennaisance - checked it out while we were there - new re-modelled suites very good (although agree with other reviews "bland") but certainly fit the bill for space, cleanliness, comfort, securtiy and location.
Stayed at the Renassaince for a week - loved the location, disappointed with the standard of cleanliness, attention to detail regarding maid service and the "tired" look of the rooms - Can't quite put my finger on why the Renassaince did not do it for us - I just think my expectations were too high!

title: “Good value”
text: OK for 1 night. Booked because of location; should have tried one of the others down the street. Brand new but nothing stellar.

title: “Nice for something a bit different”
text: Clean, small room. Restaurant downstairs was overpriced and doesn't fit with the theme of the place. They charged me for some charitable donation on my bill without asking me. Otherwise a decent place with some good restaurants nearby.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text:
We stayed here for my niece's Cheer competition and I have to say the rooms are beautiful and some of the nicest we have stayed in in a while. The service is excellent until something goes wrong and then everyone is polite but you get nothing accomplished. 
Our room door was not latching it would click as if it closed but would not close....since we did not double check the lock it seems we left our door ajar. While we were at the convention an Ipad 2 was stolen out of our room. The security staff ( Loss prevention) very nice until you finally get to a supervisor and I hope no one EVER has to deal with a man named Sergio Bertrand he was polite as he made me feel like a liar and a cock roach. I had given them 2 days business to come up with a resolution and he told me they needed a week to check the door....The short of it is the rooms manager was a nice person and has an idea of customer service....they did not pay for the ipad in full but did pay for half. I wasted and entire Sunday trying to make a police report and plenty more time on the phone trying o resolve this issue....The fact that two women and two children slept with the hotel room ajar should have made them want to do a little more I would think, maybe comp my sister her room or offer us another chance at better expeirence. We spent with valet and room service well over $400 for a one night stay I just think they should have offered a little more....I would never ask it should have been offered. 
So in short the facility is amazing and MOST of the people exceptional but please if you stay there MAKE SURE YOUR DOOR CLOSES......You will have to dance through circles to get it made right but in short I believe they will make it right.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
MHQ October 2011
Great value with super comfortable room. Staff very helpful and even allowed us into the room at 9am when we
arrived with two big suitcases. Shuttle arranged by very helpful guy on the front desk and it arrived exactly on time. Really loved being able to wander around the area and spoilt for choice on where to eat locally. Would highly recommend this hotel for location, cleanliness, and efficiency of staff.

title: “Home away from home!”
text:
The Hotel Beacon really lived up to our expectations! check in was easy the room was bright and HUGE especially by NYC standards!! There were 3 adults in a 1 brm suite, loads of storage/luggage space, we didn't utilise the kitchen much but i enjoyed having the coffee maker and fridge for snacks etc. The fairway market across the street is awesome for breakfast and their pizza's are delish! The viand cafe down stairs does free delivery and the food is good :)
because the UWS is a residential area it is really quiet and you get the real feel of what it would be like to live there (I WISH!) It was really nice to retreat back to a homey place; there are lots of restaurants and shopping close. The 72nd subway is 2 blocks away and in minutes you can be anywhere in the city!

title: “Amazing!”
text: I stayed at the Orchard during the fall of 2003 for a long weekend. We were a little wary about hotels because since I live in New York I understand how hard it can be to find a decent hotel even after you spend the nearly 200 per nite (ahem.. Crowne Plaza..ahem). We chose the Orchard because it was so high up on tripadvsisors list and it was so affordable- actually it was #1 then. When we got there we could hardly believed that we'd paid so little for so much. The rooms are spacious and beautifully decorated and it doesn't look generic or like a hospital a.k.a where youre afraid to touch the walls. The staff helped us with any questions we had. We rented movies from the front desk for free. And since I got sick during our stay it was really nice to have all of the comforts of home. The cleaning staff came in twice a day. The bell men were extremely nice. The hotel is located about 5 mins away from the huge cluster of other hotels and about 5 footsteps away from the trolley stop. I rave about it and I want there to be an Orchard in every city. I think its the best hotel I've been to- and I've been to many. And the price isnt bad either!

title: “Not the best experience”
text:
Stayed here for a week on a business trip because of the location and the king sized bed since my wife was with me on this trip. I wonder if the generally good Tripadvisor ratings for this place are still deserved. They have changed the name to Hyatt House now. Maybe it is under different management.
First the good news:
The room was well furnished with a full kitchen, a very nice microfiber sleeper sofa/sectional, a functional desk and desk chair, a good sized flatscreen TV and a king-sized bed. The AC was working fine. The room was facing the George Bush Park and was generally free of road noise. The breakfast included sausage and eggs, various breads, yogurt, fruit, cereals and various juices. The General Manager, maids, and breakfast room staff were very friendly. The bed was comfortable, although the sheets and duvet kept coming un-tucked.
Now the bad news:
The floors are apparently very thin. We were awakened by very heavy footsteps of people walking back and forth for 40 minutes above our room (we were on the second floor). This happened a couple of nights until the folks upstairs moved out. There was a loss of electricity for a few hours (no storms in the area, not sure what that was about). There was also a fire on our hallway, which forced full evacuation for a few hours. There was also a large tow-truck left running under our window for an hour or so when we were trying to get to sleep. We asked the front desk for two things: a) to be moved to 3rd floor room after we were woken by the folks upstairs. The 'tried to help' for two days, but kept saying to check back later. Never did find a better room for us. b) we asked for a late checkout on the last day so that my wife could stay in the room while I finished work. The front desk clerk said that we could stay until 2pm, no later. Any later and we would have to pay for an extra night. I said, OK, 2pm is is then (wife not happy). The next day we reminded the same clerk that we would check out at 2pm and she said 'No. We are expecting a large number of guests so unfortunately the regular check-out is 12pm.' We spoke to the manager who told us that it was fine to check out at 2pm. So, my wife shows up to sit in the lobby at 2pm and the manager sees her and says, 'Oh, you can stay in your room. Its OK.' So, back she goes to the room. 
The decor in the rooms is getting old. The carpet is wearing out and the bathroom sink cabinet is looks like it is painted-over particle board, which was coming apart. (The sink and shower were in good shape, however.)
All-in-all, this was a very mixed experience. I plan to return to the nearby Towneplace Suites if I need to stay in that area in the future.

title: “Disappointing - good service and location, but cold and uncomfortable”
text:
We stay in NYC fairly regularly and had booked a different hotel before switching our reservation to the London based on recommendations from friends. I had lived in London years ago and the idea of staying there appealed to my sense of nostalgia.
The location is excellent for midtown - close enough to walk to Carnegie Hall, Times Square and stores like FAO Schwarz, but far enough away to avoid crowds. 
At first we were intrigued by the subdued, modern decor, which is very attractive. But after a day, we found it annoying. We were upgraded to a suite at check-in but didn't even use the huge sitting room (except to hold packages) because the couch and chairs were very uncomfortable and the lighting dim enough to make reading or working at the desk difficult. The bed/bath area had only one flat surface for an open suitcase so we had to put one on the floor. The bed itself was very comfy and we slept well. We could hear noise from above us and unfortunately, there was all-night construction during one of our nights there. 
The bathroom was attractive/clean and we enjoyed the rainfall shower head. But the open glass panes are positioned in a way that one ends up getting sprayed with cold water when reaching in to turn on the water and during a shower, water sprays out onto the floor. The sink is very large but leaves plenty of room to put toiletries. Towels are inconveniently placed on shelves high up or close to the floor. If you need a hairdryer, bring your own because the one provided has very little air flow. 
We enjoyed a continental breakfast (included in our room) that consisted of fresh berries with cream, assorted breads, tarts, pastries, cereals, etc. We also enjoyed an afternoon tea that included a large number of pastries and sandwiches. 
We found the service excellent - from the bell hops to the concierge to the front desk staff. Everyone was friendly, but reserved, as one would expect in a British-style hotel. We had one error on our bill that was quickly resolved at the front desk. Earlier, when we realized we had forgotten a phone charger, the concierge promptly charged the phone for us. There is no extra charge for internet.
Although the location is great, I'd recommend walking around the corner to get a cab to avoid sitting in traffic that gets backed up on the block. 
Overall, if you prefer form over function and groove on modern decor, you'll probably enjoy the London. However, if you like more traditional, comfort-oriented surroundings, this probably isn't the place for you. There are many good things about the London, but it just wasn't a good fit for us.

title: “Very disappointing room service, unfriendly bartenders, poor cable”
text:
What a disappointment. The room itself is nice, but the service leaves a lot to be desired. The bartender was not friendly and had a sub par knowledge of drinks. I had to explain to him how to make simple things. 
Then I got room service. Do not make this mistake. The strip loin was overpriced, tiny, overcooked, and misrepresented in the menu. When I called to have my tray removed I explained my disappointment, and they did nothing about it.
The tv is nice, but the cable service is horrific. They have maybe 30 channels, most of which are in low definition. Low definition tv looks terrible on a high def tv. Why on earth would they pay to get a nice tv and put low quality programming on it?
Also, why does a 3.5 star hotel not have free wifi? Completely ridiculous. It's 2010.
There's also a spot in the bathroom ceiling that has been spackled (but not painted), half the headboard light is out, and one channel on the tv has no sound.

title: “Nice hotel for a good price!”
text:
Stayed there for 3 nights during Memorial Day Weekend.
The rates were reasonable unlike in other Starwood Hotels in NYC.
The rooms are a bit small (but let's face it: rooms in NYC are usually small), but
very modern, clean and nicely furnished. Staff was very friendly and check-in and
check-out experience were both very smooth and fast!
The Hotel is located on 25th Street and it is a 5 minute walk to MSG and Penn Station. Add another 5 to 10 minutes and you are at Times Square. So the location is quite convenient and you could even bring your car and park it on the street as you won't have any trouble finding parking space.
After staying at the Sheraton Manhattan for 3 times in the past where the rooms are a little aged and the rate is usually higher, I can really recommend this hotel, because it is good value for money plus you can earn starpoints!!!

title: “The location this hotel was in was not one of the best...”
text: We have stayed in San Fransico many times before. We needed to find a hotel that was close to the Financial district but most were already booked because of a conference that was going on in the city. It was not in a good location. One thing I must say is that the employees did go above and beyond, the were all very friendly.

title: “Average Room – within walking distance to everything.”
text:
Booked to stay in San Fran with my brother and his family. Had two rooms, side by side, found rooms compact, but everything we needed. Loved the Crabtree and Evelyn shower gel and soap. Check-in a bit of a nightmare – had to queue for some long time (Hilton club members jump the queue – which is nice for them, but frustrating for the non-members queuing with small children).
Probably would try to stay in a smaller hotel next time.

title: “No Internet”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 3 nights (6/20 to 6/22/2012), service was Ok.. Room service were so so. Only thing that I did not like is They did not have WiFi. They were keep telling me about different crap. No wifi access.. had to buy special deal from Verizon. Not really happy with it. I was there on business trip but got stuck.

title: “Small, friendly and great location”
text:
Spacious lounge, comfortable beds. A slightly larger kitchen amd more seats for the dining table would have been a bonus.
Easy access to bus and cable cars; both stop right outside. Easy walk to Fisherman's Wharf. Staff; very helpful.

title: “Not Great But You Get What You Pay For”
text:
Not a great hotel but you have to accept it for being so much cheaper than the rest.
pros:
1) nice lobby
2) cheaper
3) near subway
4) location
cons:
1) no secure luggage storage. 
2) noise from the street and floor above. hint, turn on the fan to drown it out with a constant buzz
3) not enough electrical outlets.
4) no counter or cabinet in the bathroom
5) envelope on the nightstand looking for tips from housekeeping (I've never seen this before)
6) my request for two double beds was accepted but not filled. bed was slightly smaller than a queen.
7) too much furniture for such a small room.
8) free high speed internet didn't work
9) 4pm check-in and 11am check-out
10) inconsistent water pressure/temperature
But after all the rough edges I'd still go back.

title: “its a shocker”
text: Possibly because the hotel is between brands - but mostly because they had not advised us that they were in fact between brands so. We had booked 3 nights a the Wyndham Gardens Hotel - fully expecting a full service hotel, with complimentary breakfast and what we got to was chaotic. The hotel was/is being refurbished, the rooms are T I N Y with one of the beds being so close to the airconditioner it might as well have been attached to the airconditioner. I was absolutely apauled. All credit to to the font of house staff, when I absolutely insisted that they find us alternative accommodation - they did after almost an hour and a half on the phone to other hotels in New York. It may well be fantastic when the refub is complete - for now, make another choice.

title: “Friendly and clean”
text:
I would stay here again based on the cleanliness of the hotel, the friendliness of the staff, and the location. I felt good knowing no bed bugs had been reported and that no pets are allowed on the property. 
I have only two reservations. I question the security measures, and we stayed in a suite which was very nice, but it had no kitchen equipment except for paper towels. We could have used utensils and a corkscrew, for example. 
I agree with DavidHBerkshire_UK, a recent reviewer, regarding staying here again on a revisit. I think this Hampton is definitely a good value.

title: “Clean & Convenient”
text: We spent three pleasant nights at the Carlyle Suites Hotel. The staff was very friendly & extremely helpful. Very comfortable beds & well stocked kitchen {equipment wise} which was great for breakfast & evening snacks. Location in DuPont Circle was very convenient. Sunday brunch was not well organized, but that's the biggest negative.

title: “Not quite up to scratch.”
text:
Stayed 4 nights mid April.
Had a few problems during our stay. 
Except for the noise at 2.30AM from a room next door (the occupants were evicted) the problems were minor but many.
Tess looked after us well in the compensation area, but after staying in two other hotels during our stay (Residence Inn B/Hills and Sheraton Marina San Diego) our expectations weren't quite met here.
The late checkout (6PM) was part of the compensation and it was gratefully accepted as we were flying back to Australia that night.
The "service" needs to be on the same level as the "style"

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text:
From the welcome at the front desk, to the last moment, this stay was great. Service was prompt, always with a smile and pleasant greetings, everyone let us know they wanted to be of service to make our stay tops. My room had a view of the Empire State Building and it was lovely at night. Room very clean, best hotel bed I've had in a very long time, bathroom luxurious...amenities high quality.
 They take making women traveling alone feel comfortable and safe very seriously. 
Concierge service guided us to fabulous steak house and gave us easy directions.

title: “Great Business Hotel in Washington DC”
text: Really nice rooms and great door man. Free internet and great rooms. Only negative was unclear with the bill. tried to pull a fast one. A bit loud outside during the night.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: My sister and I stayed at this hotel for one night in August of 2011. We live in Houston, but wanted to stay downtown for an evening event we were attending and we got a great deal on this hotel through Priceline.com. The room was nice, updated and clean. The check in was very fast, as was the valet service. We had a few drinks at the hotel bar located in the main lobby and recieved good service there. There was some construction going on at street level that could be heard early in the morning and might bother some people.

title: “Again- simply perfection”
text: This hotel has become a second home for us- because the staff is amazing. We have been here several times as a couple, and before we were a couple. The hotel greets us by name, the room is ready and- given we have a 2 year old - is ready for him. How the entire staff knows our name, and our son's name is genius. The lobby is beautiful, great flowers, but not overstated. The bar has an amazing house red Zinfandel, and has a patio to enjoy a cigar. The restaurant is classic Italian, and Sunday brunch makes you feel as if you are sinning. The rooms are comfortable, quiet, and connected.

title: “Nice Employees”
text:
I have stayed here many times. Every person I have encountered at the front desk is always so nice, friendly, and accommodating. Any special requests I have, are honored with speed and accuracy. They are so nice to my two doggies, too!
Comfortable beds/ great towels.

title: “Great location, great view!”
text:
Location of the hotel is fantastic. If you're taking the Metro, you can take the D Line and exit 34th & Herald Square. The hotel is literally like 3 buildings away once you exit the Metro. It is also right by Macy's. Time Square is a brisk 5 minute walk from Hotel Metro. Also, the roof top terrace of the hotel (which is open 24 hours for guests) has an amazing view of the Empire State Building.
Upon arrival, the hotel receptionist was polite, friendly, informative, & humorous. (The gentleman behind the desk greeted me by my name as I walked up to the counter to check in.) The lobby of the hotel was a bit hot, as well as the elevator.
We stayed in room 1010. It was located at the endof the hall. The room I booked was for a standard double. Even though this room was not one of the newly renovated ones, to my surprise, the room had a King size bed. 
Then room itself is rather spacious. It included a lounge chair and desk and desk chair. The end table next to the bed had a iHome docking station/alarm clock. The room also included a mini fridge. This room did not have central air. Instead it had a wall mounted A/C unit. Across the bed was the television set. There isn't a in room coffee machine, but downstairs in the lobby, there are coffee/tea available 24/7.
The restroom was a bit compact. It had a heater unit attached to the bottom of the wall. The shower water pressure was a bit lacking, but it did the job. There is a wall mounted hair dryer for use. The bathroom amenities included shampoo, conditioner, lotion, body soap, facial soap, and shower cap by Gilchrist & Soames.
On the 12th floor, there is a gym available for guests. It is also air conditioned. The gym has your standard treadmill as well as weight lifting stations. In addition, there is a water cooler in there if you need to hydrate during your workout.
Complimentary breakfast and complimentary wifi is available. 
Overall, it was a pleasant stay and I wouldn't mind staying here again next time I am in New York.

title: “Much better than we expected, great value!”
text:
We had three rooms here, and I must say the stay was brilliant! We are from the UK and wanted somewhere cheap and cheerful in San Diego before driving off on a business trip. We were really pleased with the hotel - from people who stay in numerous hotels around the world, this is much better than the 2-5 stars it apparently is. 
Surrounded by palms and hills, it has really nice grounds to begin with - you can park right outside the rooms, which were generous, clean and the bed was very comfortable. nice big rooms, with a good bathroom and all the amenities you would expect such as tea and coffee, iron, good tv, and so on. The pool area was fun, and a hot tub was an unexpected surprise - even if it was very hot! The bar isn't up to much in terms of atmosphere, but it has a pool table and ping pong which was pretty fun, and the breakfasts were plentiful and very good value - again, coming from the UK we were surprised at the choice and quality, especially for the price. We would definitely stay here again.
You really do need a car to get around but the hotel is easily accessible from the main highway and no distance to downtown San Diego and so on.
All the staff were very friendly as well.
The banana mudslide cocktail was pretty good too!

title: “Great Trip”
text: I read a lot of bad comments about this hotel, so when i booked my reservations i was scared a bid about the hotel.However I was totally surprised about the management, speaking different languages, assisting us with everything, I love this hotel and i will absolutely come back again even if i do live in Europe

title: “Great staff and location”
text: Just returned from a business/leisure trip. On first arrival, we were put in a room the size of a closet- do not let pictures fool you. However, we were promised an upgrade from the "standard" room the next day. Patience proved worthy. New room was much better and roomy. Staff was exceptional. To note: Raoul and Dan the doormen. Raoul knew us by name and made the big city feel small and quaint-which is the feel you get staying here. Front desk helpful so make sure you talk to them. Because of that, any hotel lack was forgivable. Place is clean and contemporary chic. Great location- central from everything. easy to get to subway and times-square and local eateries. Do not compare to your big chains but you will get a decent boutique hotel. Would return just for Raoul ,Dan and front desk staff.

title: “Thank you for Magical Customer Service Moment!”
text: I wanted to take a moment from my incredibly busy schedule to thank the management fom The InterContinental Hotel Dallas. My company spent several nights at this hotel during an event recently. And while the rooms, accommodations, bar and general hotel were as expected (absoutely TOP NOTCH), what was most impressive and the reason for my post, was the amazing customer service provided by management. I especially want to mention the Assistant General Manager Aref. A situation arose that the hotel did not have any control over...yet, he took customer service to the next level and created a magical customer service moment. I was so impressed with his diligence and promptness that I am now taking the time to thank him and the hotel...and will go out of my way to refer others to stay at this hotel and stay there myself again if the opportunity arises.

title: “Very good value ...”
text: Booked this hotel based on reviews - was not disappointed. Original booking price (on Hilton website) $275 for one night/twin room with breakfast - by careful weekly checking managed to get this down to $190 including breakfast, two free drinks at the bar and a $5 voucher to spend in the "pantry". Exceptional value. Rooms modern and fairly spacious with quality linens and towels. Free wi-fi in room. W 28th St is mainly filled with flower shops and the like but an ok area. Despite my Mother being in her late 70's it was not too far to walk to Times Square (in the rain!!!!). Staff at the hotel couldn't have been more helpful and the breakfast was excellent - freshly cooked to order and with good selection. Highly recommended.

title: “Great Customer Service”
text: I was traveling on business and stayed at this hotel. The staff were wonderful, assisting me with directions and helpful tips on the area. In addition to that, I went off and left my iPhone charger. I called the day after I returned from the trip and told them about leaving my charger. It had not been turned in, but they went ahead and sent me a brand new iPhone charger via overnight mail. I was so surprised that they went above and beyond to send me a new charger when they had not been able to locate mine. Truly great customer service!

title: “Friendly staff and clean room”
text:
Originally booked a five night stay during the week of Halloween. great location to begin with a stroll down to wall street, battery park and the WTC, along with the other surrounding neighborhoods in the lower manhattan part. Subways and bus stops are very close just a few minute walk and water taxies.
Now regarding the Hotel the lobby is small, the rooms are small even the double. but then again it's NYC rooms tend to be small. I Traveled here with family (4) on our second visit to NY. I had read mixed reviews on the hotel prior to booking so I was a bit concerned and skeptical on what to expect upon arival to the hotel. Small lobby and hallways, the rooms are small but cozy and comfortable, had Ac and heater system, flat screen t.v. Most importantly free WiFi, the bathroom was very tiny I think 5mm more and the door hits the toilet seat. Friendly and helpful staff.. 
The hotels restaurant is medium size with a bar, ate here only for breakfast twice, the food was ok, (personally I believe it needed more seasoning) otherwise it was good. I believe the hotel also has a gym? But not sure since there was no time.
As mention I originally had booked a 5 night stay but ended up staying an additional 3 nights due to hurricane Sandy who came along and caused some damage and shut down the airports. The hotel managed to work out our extended stay for the additional days along with giving us a discounted price which made our stay and pockets happy. "During the power blackout in lower manhattan" the hotel maintained open but with out power only generators the powered the hallways but not the rooms. This part of my review is based on how the hotel managed and how well planned are they during a natural disaster or such other event. 
To continue, no power in our rooms, so nights were a very quite and boring and somewhat cold for about 4 nights, only a drizzle of cold water came out of the shower. Some rooms toilet system worked and some did not. The hotel continued to provide clean towels. The staff was very helpful and attentive during this event they allowed guest to charge cell phone batteries in the lobby using a power strip that connected to I would guess a generator. Only one elevator worked, the hotel did provide free goodies at the entrance of the lobby, fresh fruit, bottles of water, cup cakes, cookies and crackers. Great job! 
Overall the hotel did a great job. However I believe they could had at least tried to power up the rooms (using the generator) that were occupied, so that guest would not be in the dark or even some hot water. 
To finish, my overall experience and stay at the Holiday Inn went great, great location, walking distance to many great restaurants, rooms are small but hey who travels to NYC and stays in the room? Friendy and helpful staff, and therefore I would possible consider in staying here again if I go back to NYC. I recommend this hotel, for the price you can't ask for much.

title: “Excellent Locatation, Okay Amenities”
text: Across the street from Grant Park, and less than a $10 cab ride to the train station or north side shopping and sightseeing. The building has unique and charming architectural features, amazing views, and old think walls that eliminate all building noise. It was great for our small group’s new year festivities but I can’t deny that I like the extra amenities that smaller boutique hotels offer.

title: “Beautiful upscale hotel - Valet service confusing at best”
text:
Room was spotless and extremely comfortable. Front Desk people were helpful and polite. Valet was uninterested and was verging on rude. Pulled in on Friday and tried to determine whether we would get Valet service or not. Valet would not give a straight answer as to when we had to have the car out the following day so not to be charged an additional day of Valet parking. Was told " Some time tomorrow " When asked the Valet a second time for clarification was treated like I was stupid. Decided to park on the street. 
Went out that night and came home around 1 am and asked the same question to the night valet, got the same answer. Decided to ask the front desk. Heard " tomorrow" again. It was actually a guest that told me that I should move the car by about 5PM so as to not get charged a second night. Was very frustrated at this point. Asked for Valet service anyways. 
That being said the night valet and the night desk person were extremely polite . When I called the next day for my vehicle, I again got the most curt reply when I went to pick my vehicle up. Because of that I decided to write this review. 
Other than the valet service, the staff was very kind and attentive, the hotel was clean and the location was great. I dont know if this would be my first pick, but I wouldn't object to staying here again.

title: “a really good place to stay”
text: short and simple the staff was polite and ready to help any time you needed help and the facility was clean and up to date. The hotel is also close to plenty of shopping and restaurants you won't have a problem finding both in walking distance

title: “Great location, but not at all worth half the rack rate”
text: We booked through Priceline, and got what we thought was a great deal. When we arrived we were assigned a room in the back corner of a floor, smaller than any room I have ever stayed in while traveling in the US (even in college). You could barely move around the end of the bed and you couldn't move in the shower without hitting the walls. There was a 1 inch gap under all the doors so it was not quiet Would not EVER recommend this hotel at half of rack rate. Only positives were location (3 blocks east of Times Square) and 1 of 2 concierge staff (put us on to great food, the other basically told us to look up and down the street outside the hotel and pick something). This place needs a lot of updating to stay competitive in NYC.

title: “Perfect.”
text:
Due to renovations we're having performed at the house, I was required to again spend an evening in a hotel. I have to admit, this was the first time I have ever stayed at a Starwood Hotel property. 
Some reviews are from people upset about how the hotel is on a one-way frontage road of Loop 610 @ Northwest Freeway and it's difficult to get in because of the construction. Well for those I say, Houston's freeways are always under construction, you should just expect that. Road construction should not factor in to your stay, its not a significant headache. Besides, they have shuttles if you really don't want to deal with the traffic. 
From the moment I arrived, I could tell something was different about this property. This hotel has been around for a long time. Having grown up in this part of Houston, I've passed this hotel hundreds, if not thousands, of times. From the outside, it looks like an older property, but the interior has been renovated within the past few years, and it certainly shows. 
Checking in was very fast, and the staff was very accommodating to my needs. I signed up for the Starwood Preferred Guest rewards program. I was able to pick my bed size, how high up the building I wanted to stay (sadly, no free upgrade to the 10th floor, but hey I was able to get room 732), and if I wanted foam or feather pillows. 
I have paid more for hotel rooms and gotten far less. When I entered the room, the decor was very nice, the room was already cooled for me. I could not find a single spec of dirt or dust anywhere. Believe me, I looked... as most guests do. There was absolutely nothing out of order (I had already attacked the bed in my photos).
The bed... let's talk about this bed. If I could have somehow gotten this bed into my luggage, I would have taken it with me. The mattress is firm and supportive, and I got a fantastic nights sleep. The linens were very soft, and the pillows were heavenly. Starwood obviously put some thought into their bedding. 
The room amenities were very interesting, as the coffee in the room was actually Starbucks, a nice HDTV with the most awesome smartphone app ... it's the Lodgenet app... download it to your Android or Apple phone... enter the code the TV gives you, and you can control the tv from your phone. The soap and shampoos seemed to be of nicer quality than other hotel's I've stayed in. 
Dinner for me was at the hotels' Cimmaron restaurant and had the bacon and bleu burger. Served on a pretzel roll... nice touch. The burger was made with obviously high quality ingredients. The staff in the hotel restaurant was very friendly, and anticipated my every need.
The hotel, while busy, was quiet and peaceful on the guest floors. 
Ah, the WiFi. I can't really say much about the internet here, because I work for the company that installed the WiFi here. As a matter of fact, I was the Project Coordinator back in either 06 or 07 that oversaw the technicians installation of the equipment at this facility. Personally, I didn't have any problems with the internet (trust me, I looked, my boss knew I was staying here and expected me to report back). I saw 6mbps down, and 2mbps up. This was plenty of bandwidth to stream Netflix and HBO Go on my tablet with enough bandwidth left over for everyone. But to anyone having issues with the internet, look on the workdesk. See that card talking about the WiFi? On the back there is a toll-free number to a call center in Austin, Texas. They're good people, they can help you. Bonus: The WiFi at this facility is free. 
Oh, and a tip about the vending machines: Even floors Coke Zero, Odd Floors Diet Coke, but it was just easier to go down to the gift shop in the lobby. 
I would most definitely stay at this hotel again. Maybe I'll plan another renovation to the house just to give me an excuse to stay here again, it was nice treating myself. Nice room, fun amenities, good food in the restaurant, and the most helpful staff of any property I've ever stayed in. I've got a new brand loyalty when selecting a hotel. 
To quote the title of my review, my stay was perfect.

title: “Disappointing Donatello: not much quality behind the marble facade”
text:
When I booked this hotel, the website stated renovations would be complete by February 2012. Now the website says by April but I wouldn't count on it. Our room had been renovated, although there was no safe yet installed and one window didn't close properly. Combined with the very thin glass windows, this made noise a serious problem. On the 9th floor at the back of the building, we were awakened at 7 a.m. on our first morning by a very loud and long (2 hrs) protest. Workers at the nearby Hotel Frank have been picketing for over a year and they want everyone to hear them. Protests continued through the week, culminating in a day long siege that began at 7 a.m. on our date of departure.
Best thing about this visit (aside from leaving) was the housekeeping staff -- friendly & efficient.
Average things: Front desk service.
Worst things: #1 - NOISE. In addition to outside noise, the plumbing is incredibly noisy. The toilets sound powerful but are not. Security personnel need to turn down their walkie-talkies while patrolling hallways. #2 - Showering was slightly dangerous as the water temperature fluctuated wildly depending on whether or not anyone else was using water. #3 - WiFi is hands down the slowest I've ever encountered -- anywhere in the world. #4 - Zingari Restaurant. Very average food & service and very overpriced. #5 - At check-in there is talk of a "welcome package". Aside from a map & some generally useless discount coupons, this is really a pitch to get guests to attend at 90-minute pitch about Shell Vacations.

title: “Excellent Renovation”
text: My wife and I stayed there for Valentine's Day weekend. Starwood has done a good job nenovating what was once a run down Hotel Washington while keeping the historical parts intact. The hotel has a great location close to the Mall and next to the Willard Hotel. I have been a Platinum Starwood member for a long time so we got very lucky with an upgrade to a suite. The room was excellent with large screen LCD HD TV's, nice tub and shower, etc. Since it is an old hotel, I would imagine that the regular rooms are probably on the smalish side like a New York city hotel but probably adequate. The restaurant in the lobby was excellent. The fitness facility was very good for a hotel - many cardio machines, dumb bells up to 50lbs., and few nice weight machines. All of the staff were very helpful. Overall, I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Good stay great breakfast.”
text: Good clean room, service was good. Elevators were very busy and had to take the stairs from 22 floor after waiting 15 mins. Breakfast was included with my stay, which was very good. There are better stays in Philly but I would stay again if got a good deal. Good location.

title: “convienent and pleasant”
text:
This hotel is right next to the Redbirds stadium. There a many good and interesting resturants and bars. The Peabody is nearby too. The security is very present and reasurring. The rooftop pool is nice but small. It also will close for the day if it rains. The rooms are very comfortable and relaxing. The staff is very nice and friendly.
The have expensive valet parking but there is other self parking nearby.

title: “The Palace Concierge Saved the Day”
text: I did not stay at the Palace Hotel but I was so impressed with the service when I had breakfast there that I was moved to write a review. At the end of breakfast at the Istana which is in the lobby area, my four year old girl decided the world was ending because her candy cane broke. She was crying uncontrollably and disrupting pretty much the entire lobby area. I hustled her out the front door to try to calm her down. Immediately the concierge (named Bitan I believe) came out and talked to my daughter until she was calm. He brought her a cup of water and a teddy bear and the tears were forgotten. They were so kind and helpful that I would stay at the Palace next time I'm in New York.

title: “Elvis, Elvis and more Elvis!”
text:
My partner and I stayed here for 4 nights as part of a tour. Perfect location for Gracelands but quite a way out of town and nothing around hotel expect for a couple of fast food places, but advised not to walk around at night. However we did use hotel shuttle which charges $5 each way (our Hotel in Nashville had a free shuttle). Our room was large and clean, no complaints. The complimentary breakfast and free tea or coffee at any time was a real bonus as the other 2 hotels we stayed we had to pay for it. We used the pink phone in reception and used the free cadillac ride to Marlowes where we had a good meal and full of Elvis memorabilia. The hotel was quite at night so had a good nights sleep.
As a previous reviewer said they are going to build a new hotel across the road, but I found the hotel to be fine for our needs. It had a nice retro feel to it and made a change from the many sterile corporate hotels I have stayed in. Elvis was on show 24/7 and we missed him when we left!! I was a bit worried by previous reviews but I would recommend this hotel to people wishing to stay right by Gracelands and for the Elvis experience. Miss B overseeing breakfast was a delight!

title: “It was really fantastic!”
text:
The owner was very nice and offered us a nice room for a fantastic rate! We stayed for two nights and went to see a lot of interesting places, which the hotelowner pointed out for us on a map of San Fransisco.
The room was also very clean. And the bed slept fantastic.

title: “Perfect!”
text: Really an excelent hotel!!! I do recommend it! Very friendly people, very comfortable and clean. Excelent!

title: “Only okay”
text: Stayed here for 3 nights in Sept whilst on vacation in the US. Upgraded to a junior suite which was very nice but because I had made 3 seperate bookings because of using hilton honors points one day our room wasn't made up by house keeping. We weren't charged for 2 of the days upgrades so guess I can't complain too much. However I would sugest checking to see if there is a conference on before you stay as the hotel was extremely busy when we there and the lobby area and restaurants were extremely busy. Would stay here again on honors points but would think twice about paying $250+ a night as I don't think it really warrants it.

title: “Charming European boutique hotel”
text:
From the moment we checked in, we were delighted with this hotel; it far surpassed our imagining. The staff members are capable, competent, well-informed and care about the guests. The decor is understated elegance accented with paintings and drawings featuring stringed instruments and scenes from operas. Our spacious Opera suite was perfect for the two of us; music was playing in the background since the radio was already tuned to a classical station. Beds are very comfortable and the suite was cleaned daily even though we were timeshare exchangers. Apples and freshly baked cookies greeted us every afternoon when we returned from exploring San Francisco neighborhoods. The complimentary Continental Plus breakfast is a great way to start the day.
The ballet and symphony halls are one block away.
We found the public transportation very convenient: bus stops are only half a block away and vintage streetcar, trolley car and BART stops are three blocks away. The cable cars are only a few blocks away by bus. 1- 3- or 7-day MUNI passes are economical and quickly more than pay for themselves. Also, this area of San Francisco is very flat so it's easy to walk around.
Ovation restaurant right in the hotel serves delicious meals beautifully served in a lovely, romantic atmosphere. In the background is live gentle jazz. Other restaurants are nearby within easy walking distance, but we were so enchanted by Ovation that we didn't try them.
The business center is minimal, but it does permit one to check email and surf the web and it is free.
We will definitely return to Inn at the Opera when we are in San Francisco.

title: “Nice hotel.”
text: Stayed for business in the middle of August. This was a nice hotel. Rooms were clean. Like the location - in the middle of the Stone Oak area at 1604/281. Straight shot to/from the airport, without all the plane noise of staying at the airport. Lots of restaurants all around. Close to a Walmart, in case you need to buy something (at any hour). Will definitely return.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the begining of November for 4 nights and have to say that The Nolitan exceeded all of my expectations! This hotel is fantastic! The location is awesome with many cool restaurants and bars with in walking distance. The staff were chatty, friendly and incredibly helpfull. 
The continental breakfast was basic but adequate. The room was wonderful. The views of the Manhattan skyline and the balcony made it feel like we had our own personal observation deck. The icing on the cake was the free use of hotel bicycles!

title: “Super Sofitel”
text: We stayed at the Sofitel for 4 nights, the room was a non refundable Queen Double on the 9th floor. It was just as the pictures showed, luxurious, immaculately clean and wonderfully quiet. The room was spacious, with a lovely bathroom, bedding and towels replaced daily. (Make sure you take advantage of the turn down service.) The bed was like sleeping on a marshmallow - heaven - just what you need after pounding the streets of Manhattan all day. We would recommend the "Red Flame Diner" - just a few doors down towards Times Square - the food is good and reasonably priced - we ate there every day for breakfast. Overall the stay was fantastic - the staff polite and the location second to none - just 7 blocks from the Rockerfeller Center and 2 blocks from Times Square, close to Fifth Avenue for shopping.

title: “Average service, no Wi-Fi, but okay given price”
text:
The guy in the reception was not friendly and did not try to help when my credit card did not work (he warned me that I could be checked out if I did not manage to get one working). The concierge was not friendly either.
Besides, there was no free Wi-Fi in the room (but available in the lobby).
However, considering the price, the overall quality of the hotel was descent.

title: “Great Stay at the Allerton”
text:
This was my first time visiting Chicago, and I booked the Allerton through Hotels.com. 
The hotel is in a perfect location on the Magnificent Mile. We walked pretty much everywhere we went. There is an L station a few blocks away. 
The room was not huge, but it's a big city and it's expected. The room was very clean, bed very comfortable and the bathroom was great. 
The lobby is not on the bottom floor, which is a little awkward. However, the bell men are great and ensure you get your luggage to the right place. 
The lobby was nice, with a firepit and a great bar to relax in at the end of the day. 
I didn't interact with the staff all too much, but when I did, they were very friendly and helpful.
I couldn't see any reason not to recommend staying here for your trip to Chicago!

title: “mice in da house”
text: more than one mice in my room......scary,small,gross and gross.

title: “Average to Slightly Above Average”
text: Location is great for CHerry Creek, great shopping and dining. The rooms or at least mine was a bit small. Hotel had limited staff on hand- which were very helpful and were able to get the room ready slightly before that dreaded statement, " Check in is not until 3(insert hour of choice)" This is the most easliy translated hotel excuse for we are understaffed or poorly trained or simply are not concerned for the tired business traveler. Just my pet peeve! However after some push back on my part they were able to expedite the room cleaning.

title: “location, location, location”
text: First time staying at Venice Beach and this place was great. The hotel was right on the pedestrian walk that borders the beach. You can’t get any closer! The front door is nestled between 2 shops which at first concerned me, but they closed by 6pm so this was no problem. Since the hotel is right on the beach parking is available a block or two away, but this wasn’t a problem either, because the nice guy who checked us in gladly volunteered to walk to our car to get our bags. Even though our room was only on the 3rd floor, my daughter loved the old-fashion elevator with the manual cage-like door. Our room had a lovely exposed brick wall and a great view of the ocean. I wish we had stayed longer at Venice Beach than at Disneyland!

title: “We Enjoyed Our Stay”
text:
We were a bit scared after reading the reviews, but we must have landed lucky. We were on the 4th floor, and although it was a struggle with the cases, well worth it when we saw the room. It was a huge room with 2 queen beds, large bathroom and a huge plasma TV, we were impressed. No problems incurred throughout our stay, although the noisy pipes kept on going all through the night, but hey your in New York, your too tired from all the sight-seeing to stay awake and hear them anyway.
Great little bar below the hotel, but ask how much before you pay for the drinks.
I would recomend this hotel, it was right round the corner from everywhere you would need.

title: “Great value”
text:
My husband and I just got back from a night at the Phoenix. We were there for a party at the Bambuddha Lounge, a great night spot adjacent to the hotel. 
The decor is what you see in the pictures: a funky revitalization of a 50's style motel. Our room was basic but quite clean and comfortable. There was a faint odor of cigarette smoke, even though it was supposedly non-smoking -- but it was faint enough not to bother us (our friends were initially assigned a much smokier-smelling room, but they asked to be switched and were accommodated). The front-desk staff was generally attentive and polite -- especially the night clerk, Luke. 
We were mostly surprised by what a great deal it was. We paid $133 with our AAA discount, including on-site parking and continental breakfast. Usually when breakfast is included at places like this, you're lucky to get coffee and doughnuts. Although not lavish, this one still exceeded my expectations: laid out buffet-style by the pool, it included coffee, several types of milk (soy, skim, whole, and half-and-half), OJ, several types of pastries (muffins, croissants, danishes, raisin bread), bagels with cream cheese (you could toast them if you liked), and whole fruit.
The only major downside is the neighborhood (the Tenderloin), which is down-and-out. Then again, since your car is parked right there with complete in-and-out access, you don't need to walk around. Although you should make an exception and head to Brenda's French Soul Food, around the corner, for what might be the most delicious brunch you'll ever have. 
Overall, I would recommend the Phoenix for the value-conscious who appreciate funky style.

title: “Not what we had expected from such an iconic name”
text:
We stayed at the Waldorf Astoria as part of a package arranged by Cunard after crossing from Southampton to New York on the Queen Mary which all went very well indeed. At the end of the trip we were transferred (together with a number of other guests) to the Waldorf Astoria hotel by Cunard. The entrance was very unimpressive since it was covered by scaffolding and we were taken round to a side entrance where there appeared to be no proper reception for us and our luggage. The driver of our transport tried to contact someone but to no avail and we just milled about not knowing where to go or whether we should wait for luggage to be taken to our room. It was all very haphazard and chaotic to say the least. Eventually a porter arrived and said he would take care of all the luggage and that we should check in at the main entrance some distance from where we were dropped off.
We did this and the reception clerk said our room was not ready but that it would definitely be ready by 3pm. at the latest and he took our mobile number and said he would contact us if the room was ready earlier, as he thought it would be. 
We were quite anxious to change before going out in the city as it was very hot but this was not possible.
We went out and about and returned at 3pm. as we had not heard anything to find that the room was STILL not ready.
We then had to wait a further two hours before the room was available. The reception clerk offered us two free drink vouchers but we did not think that was generous for the inconvenience we had suffered and we asked to see the manager.
She was apologetic and we asked if they would make breakfast available for the three mornings we were there as we had booked on a "room only" basis. She then offered to give us $150.00 dollars credit on our account to spend with them as we wished and we accepted this,thinking that would easily pay for three breakfasts.
We went down to breakfast the next morning and had the buffet breakfast which was nice and then got the bill which came to$118.00 including the mandatory service charge of 18%!!!
Apart from this we were very disappointed that there was a lot of work going on in the hotel including a full strip up and relay of the floor area in the main lobby which went on in the evening when we were hoping to have a quiet drink in the bar and listen to some music.
The room was quite nice but no WiFi which normally we find free, even in modest hotels, and the general service was adequate but in comparison to the fantastic service we had just enjoyed on the Queen Mary it all seemed a little offhand and casual.
New York was super and we had a great time there and in fairness the concierge service in the hotel was really excellent,so 3 stars is all we could manage for this VERY expensive hotel.

title: “Amazing”
text: Beautiful,Amazing,This motel is one of the best motels you have to stay at this place even if its just for fun or for business.Very nice area with tons of things to do,resturants,gifts,loved this motel

title: “Great spot, close to LAX”
text:
Great spot to stay, close to the airport. Sizeable rooms, nothing to fault! Shuttle service is great. 
We stayed here prior to our international flight home the next morning. Our flight was then cancelled by the airline and they subsequently put us up at the hilton for another night - alongside the other 400 passengers. The hilton staff were great with the whole situation and provided everything we needed - toothbrushes etc (given that we had no access to our luggage) and all handled it fantastically, and went out of their way to ensure we were as happy as possible, given the situation.
Would recommend!

title: “My home away from home in San Francisco”
text: We were made feel very much at home while staying at the Chelsea Motor Inn this past week. We felt very safe with the locked elevator entrance. Our room was very pretty and comfortable. We had a view of the Golden Gate Bridge out our window. The staff was friendly and helpful. The location was handy to public transportation. There were nice restaurants within easy walking distance. We wouldn't even consider staying anywhere else upon a return trip to San Francisco.

title: “Small rooms and slow elevators”
text:
I booked this hotel on points and I have to say I was a little dissapointed. The location is ok. It is fairly centrally located. The rooms were not that good though. I realize this is Manhattan and space is a premium but these rooms were excessively small. I mean, to open the bathroom door you had to squeeze around it. For the price, if I paid, it was extremely small and not that nicely anointed. 
Other qualms where that the sound didnt work on the tv. The elevators were painfully slow and always packed because of this. Lastly, the internet was also brutally slow. 
Would I go back? Maybe I'd it was the only one I could book on points in the area but other then that I would try elsewhere.

title: “Excellent Hotel Experience”
text: My husband and I returned last week from a perfect stay at the Arizona Biltmore. The hotel is lovely: the architecture is stunning, the furnishings are interesting and completely in keeping with the style of the buildings, and the grounds are breathtaking. Our room was spacious and comfortable (great bed and pillows) and the food was outstanding. However, an equally notable feature of the hotel was the topnotch service, from the room attendants to the restaurant servers to the front desk staff - it was clear that their primary goal was to make every guest feel welcome and happy. We had an issue with the temperature in our room and Chris, one of the front desk assistant managers, made certain that an engineer was sent to our room within minutes and he checked back with us regularly to ensure that the problem had been taken care of and that we were satisfied. He indicated the option to switch our room but we were otherwise so pleased with our accommodations that we wanted to stay put. He was friendly, pleasant, and a true professional. We had a wonderful getaway in Phoenix (so much to see and do), but it was our stay at the Biltmore that made our vacation just perfect.

title: “A Great Value”
text: We were very pleased with our stay here on our recent visit to Philly. An outstanding value located within easy walking distance of all we wanted to see.The friendly staff was another plus along with the great breakfast served on real china, not the paper and plastic foundat many places. Highly recommended for anyone heading to Philadelphia!

title: “Need a Little "Umph"”
text: Rather pricey, little value. Rooms are so-so - clean, but small and standard hotel-like decor. The bathroom is smaaaaaaaalllllllllll - my shoulder was rubbing the toilet paper roll - a larger person would not be comfortable here. Small hotels are not unusual in NYC, but they could've used more imagination in designing the space to make it more comfortable. The service in the bar and restaurant is lousy and the prices are ridiculous - even by NYC standards. Breakfast - $14 just for two eggs, no toast, no homefries - $30 for a three egg omlet, no toast, no homefried. The bar is just as bad - $14 for a glass of Fetzer! The worst wine ever - you can buy the bottle for $7! If you stay at this hotel - just eat and drink elsewhere. Also - they charge $60 to park your car - park it yourself - the garage is right across the street from the hotel and it's $40 per day.

title: “Good til the "bitter" end.”
text: The hotel was very nice. Stayed here because using hhonors points (great program, booked same evening & got free rooms using points). Very nice rooms, clean & very courteous staff at check-in. Free continental breakfast for being a gold hhonors participant. No continental breakfast in hotel restaurant. Told could use $7 toward $15 buffet which had black bananas first item, so passed. Watched an employee berate manager (with nasty looking nose injuries) in the middle of the empty restaurant.

title: “Great location and affordable for chicago!”
text: This hotel was 1.25 blocks from the Millenium park and the bean. Close to the metra and magnificent mile. Hotel staff was friendly and willing to help. Lobby was huge (the entire second floor). Room had the historic charm without being outdated. Bathroom was spacious and modern. Great hotel and location. Paid $110 which was fantastic for this time and Chicago

title: “Great View and Location”
text:
This hotel checks all the boxes:
- great location (we walked everywhere)
- very clean (it is newly renovated)
- friendly staff
- good price for being in the heart of it all
Plus the view was fantastic. We would stay here again.

title: “Howard Johnson”
text:
The location is good if you're going to watch a baseball game
it's about 15 minutes ride on the subway to the downtown area, and the hotel is about 10 minutes away from the station.
If you dont want to pay a lot of money on a hotel in the downtown area this is definitly a good option, since it's easy to get downtown from there.

title: “Atmosphere and location”
text: Two queen beds in a generously sized room set the stage for a comfortable stay for my friend and me at the Hotel Rex. We loved the warm colors of the decor, and especially the book-y bar and common area on the first floor. One could imagine the old Herb Caen crowd hanging around with their cigars and cocktails, discussing current events and good books. While the room had no coffee pot, the complimentary coffee downstairs was as good as any San Francisco coffee house. For breakfast, we walked around the corner to Sears for their famous comfy-food and crowds. Location isn't the only great feature of the Hotel Rex, but it sure doesn't hurt, with Union Square just a stroll away. Hotel staff are invariably warm, friendly, and helpful. An altogether great stay.

title: “Not A Great Experience...”
text: We have stayed with LaQuinta for years including this property. However this trip wasn't our usual good experience and these are housekeeping issues. Our room had fleas...got bites on my ankles. The clock was unplugged and the last thing one wants to do is have to figure out how to reset a digital clock at 10PM. Coffee grounds from previous guests still in coffeemaker. After showering, I started drying off w/ a clean bath towel and there was a 'gob of rubber' stuck in the towel. The green desk chair had something white spilled over 25% of it. This is a corporate owned hotel and not a franchise---so they really need to look at their housekeeping....

title: “Great place to stay in New York, affordable and close to everything!”
text:
Chelsea Star in New York City was a great place for our family to stay during our trip to NYC! It was the most affordable place I found when looking for a hotel. I wanted something close to Penn station and Chelsea Star is a block away. The room was all we needed, it was the Deluxe room that had two full beds and a private bath. chelsea Star also has other affordable rooms for the single traveler in which you share a bath down the hall. It was not fancy but everything was just what we needed. Everything was clean, they had coffee and tea available and a great patio to enjoy. A washer and dryer were available if needed. The only negative was that they did not have an elevator so we had to lug the suitcases up two flights of stairs. I would stay here again if going back to NYC!
.

title: “FANTASTIC Location!!”
text: I researched all hotels in NYC with a 3 Star or better rating, I was looking at several things; LOCATION, price, room size, to name a few. The Doubletree Time Square fit the bill perfect. The location is right in the thick of everything. We could walk to most things that we wanted to do. The suite was wonderful and It was large for a hotel in NYC. There were four girlfriends on a girls trip and we had plenty of room. The king size mattress in the bedroom was HEAVENLY!!! The sofa bed in the living room was comfortable also. I can't say enough about this property, I will definitely stay there again!

title: “Best Deal in New York City”
text: This was by far the best deal around for lower Manhattan. There were 5 women and their large luggage in our room (some of us larger than the others) and we were quite comfortable. Two queen and one sofa bed. The bathroom was alright and there was a bonus sink and vanity in the room which made it possible for two of us to get ready at the same time. Also desk and sitting chairs in the room. The room was way larger than expected. And the best thing of all - total for two nights for the 5 of us was $670.26 - $134 each for two nights in Manhattan. Located right across the street from the subway station which made it really easy to hop on and go downtown. Great little family style Italian/deli right down the street with LARGE, inexpensive servings which was handy after the long west/east coast flight. Close to Ground Zero and Statue of Liberty. This was a great place to stay for our quick two night stop prior to our cruise out of New York Harbor. The front staff and bellman were extremely nice and accommodating. Brought extra towels and pillos quickly. Overall I would not hesitate one bit to return to this location. We were thrilled with the accommodations.

title: “Great place but noisy”
text: Great service, great rooms, but lobby noises are heard in the living room of your suites. Counldnt get my kids to sleep because of the noise.

title: “Dream Resort -- Dream Staff”
text:
The Grand Del Mar is all things grand-- and I can't for the life of me find one negative thing to say about the property. I visited the GDM for a business conference in May of 2011 and was blown away by the beautiful grounds, gorgeous rooms (WHAT an amazing bathroom, right?!), delicious food, and incredible staff. You can read so many reviews on here that detail all the wonderful amenities of the GDM but I'd like to contribute a very brief experience I had to highlight something that most people don't even think about: service.
Upon departing from our room in the morning we were greeted by a cheerful, smiling maid who wished us a wonderful morning and an even better day; turning the corner, a maintenance worker waived hello, smiled to us and shouted "GOOD MORNING!"; upon entering the elevator there was a bellhop heading downstairs and he too, smiled kindly at us and struck up a pleasant conversation-- only to tell us to enjoy our day at the GDM.
To me, it was so impressive to see a group of people working for a property that truly LOVED their jobs. They loved it enough to have a smile on their face, acknowledge guests, and be personable. That happens so little these days and made a huge impression on us all. Just wanted to share!

title: “Nice Hotel, nice location.”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights in August (2 adults, 2 teenage children) and found it to be a very nice hotel. The main plus point being the location. The staff were very helpful and friendly. It was on the expensive side $376.00 per night, but this is probably because of the location more than anything else. We ordered a larger premier room with two queen beds which was a very good size. The room was at the rear of the building, so there was no view at all, but is was clean and very comfortable. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again. As for the lifts, we never waited more than 20 seconds.

title: “Pretty Good!”
text: The GOOD: exellent varied breakfasts(I was pleasantly surprised) Fine room decor good prices for rooms Excellent staff friendliness and service, from front desk and taxi man to restaurant staff NICE FOLKS who are well trained fast elevators good location nice restaurant nearby(Busboys and Poets) These folks take care of you RECOMMENDATIONS the bed duvets keep you too toasty that is they don't breathe enough. Other than that, sure we would keep coming back .GOOD JOB MANAGEMENT! you want people to return, and they will! not a perfect hotel, but just about all you need

title: “Decent room for the money”
text: Stayed here one night en-route to Southern FL. They billboards along 295 advertising all rooms $39.99. When I checked in they presented me with rates $48 - $55. I asked them whats up with that, and they said, all you have to mention is that you saw the sign, and they will give you the rate. Good Deal. Rooms are not huge, but big enough for 1 or 2, clean. Mine was supposed to be non smoking but had a slight smoky aroma that I mentioned in the morning while checking out. They took another $5 off. Cant beat $40 for a decent nights sleep. Fast free wifi, no continental but a coffee machine in the lobby. Adjacent to all kinds of eating and shopping.

title: “Poor Internet Connection”
text: The hotel is nice and reasonably confortable for NYC standard. The location is very good, as it is breakfast. I liked very much the bread! On the bad side, internet connection was terrible. Regardless the option that you select, there were several blackouts and most of the time the internet speed was extremely low (it took hours to download 10 megab). If you need to work using internet, I guess this hotel is not a good option. Also, we used the two tea bags in the rooms the first day, which were not replaced the following days. The heating system is noisy.

title: “Upscale decor, but not an upscale experience”
text: We stayed here for my friend's bachelorette party. Although the hotel itself is very trendy and modern, simple things like the breaker being out in the bathroom and the sink being stopped up and missing the pull to release the drain were bothersome. Even after they sent someone up to fix the breaker (in plain clothes?) it still didn't work. The front desk people aren't really knowledgeable about the area either. The hotel itself is lovely and the decor is amazing, but between the issues we had and the $25 a night parking I wouldn't run out in the streets screaming joy for it.

title: “Nothing but troubles...”
text:
I must say, for the amount of travel I do for my job, I generally have good luck with the hotels that I stay in. Unfortunately, I cannot say that for the L'enfant Plaza. From the moment I checked in, I had issues. 
I ended up checking in at about 10:30 in the evening - upon receiving my room key, I proceeded to my room on the top floor of the hotel. Upon entering my room, it sounded as though they booked me in the engine room of a cruise ship - the room was extremely loud, and I suspect that the air conditioning unit for the entire hotel was directly above this room. 
Knowing I wouldn't get a wink of sleep if I stayed in this room, I proceeded back to the front desk where I was told that the only room available was a "parlor" room. If you've read some of the other reviews of this hotel, you will immediately know that this is actually a room that doesn't have a bed. Wonderful... So my choices are the engine room or a room without an actual bed. I chose the latter....
Up to this room I headed.... The room was quite large, with a dining table that sat at least 8 people. The carpets were stained in multiple areas, and there were a number of cobwebs on the light fixtures. Again - I'm not too pleased with the room, but they had promised to move me to an actual room the following day.
