Since I was tired, and the only thing that they'd end up doing for me is putting me in another parlor room, I sucked it up and stayed in this room.
To the hotel's credit, they did move me to a suitable room the following day and did comp me a breakfast in their restaurant. The room that I ended up in after the first night was clean, but as many others have commented, this place needs a significant remodeling - the place reminded me of a late 1980's Marriott.
I was attending a conference at this hotel, and must also mention two things. First of all, the first day of the meeting, the air conditioning in the conference room was not working sufficiently. Many in attendance were visibly uncomfortable from the heat and humidity (myself included) - it made it difficult to concentrate. Also, the cellular and wifi signals in the conference rooms are non-existent. When you exit the room, the signal is fine in the foyer, but poor in the actual room. This made it difficult for me because I had a couple of calls I was expecting, so I found myself nervously exiting the room regularly.
One last experience I must mention... On the second night, I visited the bar and had a couple of drinks. When ready to retire for the evening, I asked for the bill and noticed that I was overcharged by one drink. When I brought it to the attention of the bartender, I was met with arguing that I did, in fact, have the drink in question. I like to consider myself a trustworthy person, and for the bartender to argue with me and question my truthfulness was an insult to me. I wasn't trying to scam him out of money, nor would it have been any skin off his back to just correct the bill. Knowing that I wasn't getting anywhere, I ended up just paying for the extra drink and leaving a lousy tip. He argued his way out of his tip.....
If I ever have to attend a meeting at this hotel in the future, I will probably stay elsewhere and use the Metro to get to the L'enfant - the Metro is actually conveniently located under the hotel, which makes getting around town quite convenient.
My recommendation - stay away from the L'enfant Plaza Hotel until significant changes are made to this property.

title: “Decent. Get what you pay for.”
text:
When I checked in, I was first placed to a single bed room that smelled heavily of pot. The people next door to that room are to blame were going in and out, slamming the door. 
I asked to change rooms...and I'm pretty sure I was placed to a room next to hookers, but it smelled better and was quiet. This was no fault of the hotel staff, however prepare to put up with sketchy and hilariously rediculous people staying there. 
Overall, the staff seemed to genuinely care. The man who checked me in seemed very sympathetic. Room was pretty clean, slept well.

title: “Brideshead for SoCal!”
text:
This place is ridiculous. On many web sites they show you photos taken from strategic angles to accent the positive. At the GDM, no photo can do it justice. Everything gleams with solid elegance. The furniture is museum quality, the amenities are just THERE, in reach, just what you need when you need it. The people are so nice you kind of wait for the other shoe to drop, but it never does. Just a great place.
We came in late September, which is a great choice. Their high season is August, and in September it's a little ghostly. There are more staff than guests, but you quickly get used to it being your own home. Another great thing about off-peak are the packages - suites normally running $700 go for $500 or less.
There are two main restaurants: Amaya is "casual" but terrific, while Addison is over the top - inspired by the French Laundry with a 10-course degustation (6, 4 and 3 course options are available) and a wine list running fully 190 pages. I recommend stopping by the afternoon of your meal and borrowing a copy of the wine list - that's the only way you can spend the necessary time. They have bottles from $60 to $12,000 (1982 Petrus). A truly outstanding meal.
It's really worth a trip to San Diego to spend a few nights here - especially if you're a golfer.

title: “kids loved the warm pool”
text: We stayed here on a lay over home from Cancun. It was great to have a comfortable bed and room on our final night of holidays. The kids loved the pool which was warmer than the ones at the resort in Cancun which we could not believe as we were in Seattle! The staff was friendly and we appreciated the cookies after a long flight when we were waiting to check inn. Just a nice touch! Shuttle was convenient and would definitely stay here again.

title: “Georgetown's Best Deal?”
text: We stayed at the Georgetown Suites 30th St. building for three nights last weekend while we visited our son at Georgetown University. We thought it was a very good deal. We had plenty of room, with a king sized bed, comfy chair, table with four chairs, bathroom and well-equipped kitchen. Everything was clean, spacious and comfortable. The decor is dated in style, but not worn or tired. The staff was helpful. There is free WiFi in the room or you can check email for free in the lobby business center. Great location, right in the midst of the Georgetown shops and restaurants, about a 15 minute walk to the University (uphill). The Circulator bus can be caught just up the block for going to the Mall. Great bran muffins at breakfast, among many other choices. The only down side was that the heat/air conditioning duct was a big vertical grid on the wall that blew right on the bed. Apart from that, it was a great deal for $150/night.

title: “Great Visit and really nice people!”
text:
Just returned from a four night stay at this Marriott. We were warmly welcomed by John the doorman who was extremely helpful from the time we arrived until the time we departed the hotel. He arranged for Town Car service to LGA in the most efficient manner.
The Front Desk staff was not overly friendly and did not welcome us but did immediately check us in early. 
We had WONDERFUL service in the restaurant by Caesar. He was friendly, helpful and very entertaining. We felt like we were at home every time we ate in the restaurant. 
Had Room Service twice for breakfast. Room service was expensive but fast and the food was good.
I did notice that the lobby will undergo renovation. While it is ok now, it does need a good facelift with restrooms on the same level. 
The hotel is located in midtown and you will need to take a cab if you are unable to walk a short distance to certain areas. The doormen are so nice and do an excellent job. You will not have to wait for long at all on a cab or limo.

title: “Must be a bunch of whiners who gave low ratings”
text:
I don't know what the low-raters are talking about. Although this used to be a "Super 8", you would never know it. I don't like Super8, BTW. I'm staying here right this minute and after staying one night, last night, I decided to stay for a week. At only $170 for the week rate, you can't beat a place like this! The staff is very friendly, the shuttle is speedy (airport and back only) and runs hourly, it's very quiet and you can't get cleaner rooms even at a 5 star hotel, and so what if breakfast is just bagels, muffins, danish, cereal, toast, milk and coffee. WHAT ARE YOU WHINING ABOUT? If you don't like the breakfast, there's a diner right outside.
Look, just stay here if you're on a budget and you won't regret it.

title: “Living in luxury at the Lenox”
text: Stayed here while I attended an environmental toxicology (SETAC) conference and my wife did an NSF workshop that both happened to be in Boston at the same time. Our stay was wonderful. Check-in was quick and easy (and they accomodated us two hours early). The room was fabulous with nice appointments, a great bathroom and a very luxurious bed. Our only negative was the view from our room, not bad but mostly of a roof top. Location was good with a fair amount of expensive and inexpensive dining within walking distance. Also had a Trader Joe's supermarket just 1.5 blocks away. I love to walk and Boston is definitely a walking town, with the start of the Freedom trail only about 6 blocks away, which I spent a day doing on foot. Overall, a wonderful experience I would love to repeat.

title: “OK at best”
text: We had an OK stay ay best, we paid full cost for 4 nights ($215 per), ended with a partial ocean view on the 2nd floor. A very small room (I'd say 200sq ft). It's like one of those hotel/motel/lodges which is on it's last legs which can't be fixed or not worth fixing (ie squeaky floors/thin walls). At best it is a $150 per night by ocean, or an $99 per night inland lodge.

title: “Nice change from the Gaylord”
text: I was attending a convention at the Gaylord Hotel in National Harbor and my wife and I decided to spend the last night in Washinton at the Churchill. Needless to say we will be saying at the Churchill next year and I will be taking the Subway and bus to the convention.

title: “Visiting Son in College”
text:
Great locations with many walk to shops. Hotel personnel were friendly.
Very pretty lobby and comfortable beds.

title: “Awesome stay”
text: It was my first time to Detroit and I had a great time. The hotel was close to everything I needed to see and the staff was very attentive. The casino facilities were great. My only regret was that there was no sports betting. I did not realize outside of Vegas that did not exist.

title: “Not that great”
text: I wouldn't go back. The rooms were tacky- horrible decorations and I found the staff at Olicia and some in the hotel very snobby.

title: “Okay if you just need a quick stop over”
text:
This hotel was fairly clean but very basic. Rooms had bed,tv and table. No tea/coffee making facilities. The wifi does not work unless you are in reception.
The area has nothing around and I would say a little unsafe to walk around in the evening.
Overall it wasn't too bad although I would suggest pay a little more and stay closer to downtown.

title: “Really enjoyed our stay!!!”
text: We greatly enjoyed our first trip to NYC 2 weeks ago. The Hilton Times Square was absolutely great. We stayed for 6 wonderful days. We felt safe and very comfortable. Slept great, loved the shower and big towels. Our view of the Empire State Bldg was wow! But I have to say it was a lifelong memorable trip thanks largely in part to their extremely wonderful customer service!!! Christian and Val in reception went above and beyond, very professional, patient in giving us directions, thoughtful, courteous, and Christian was very thoughtful in having a very nice bottle of champage and glasses delivered to our room for our anniversary! He also helped us when we were having internet trouble one night and got us going (no charge due to our trouble). They knew us by name and greeted us as we came and went each day. Location was fabulous. Only issue would be cost of their breakfast buffet ($30/person) and cost of laundry service, so bring plenty of clean clothes. We actually really enjoyed the breakfast at the Applebees next door. They serve until noon, great breakfast, free coffee/tea with order and comfortable big booths. Suggestions: make time to see the Brooklyn Bridge and see as much of Central Park as you can, its absolutely breathtaking. I would skip the CSI Experience. Comedy show tickets sold on street 2 for $20, was surprisingly a great time! NBC studio tour was neat and we scored tickets to see Jimmy Fallon the next night! Everyone recommended burgers at The Shake Shack and they were right, great food! Walking is very overwhelming, even with the subway so I would recommend the Hop on Hop Off Bus. We will def do that next time. We will be back at the Hilton next Summer! Thanks for a wonderful and memorable stay...

title: “Our stay was wonderful!”
text: The best thing about this hotel is the staff! They were very kind and helpful! They made our trip so special!

title: “Views versus noise”
text: This was the second time I stayed here. First time my room was halfway down a corridor and was at the back of the hotel. This time I was close to the toilets and over the street and the noise was dramatically different. Banging doors and traffic kept me awake most of the night. But.....I had a view of the Statue of Liberty this time round - my only reason for not asking to be moved. The air con was completely useless, and most of the tv channels had frozen. Quite cheap for NYC, but not overly impressed this visit.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Hotel is pretty good, with big rooms and comfortable. Been there for a week and had no complaints about it. Would go back for sure.

title: “Poor service”
text: Had to wait over half an hour for the "free" shuttle from the airport. The staff member at check in was very friendly and accomodated our needs. However, the staff at check out were extremely rude and unfriendly. The food was below par, not what I would expect from a Crowne Plaza hotel. Overall the hotel is clean and nicely decorated, however the service and food need work!

title: “4 Star Lobby with 3 Star Rooms”
text:
This hotel from the driveup to the lobby is very very nice, the rooms and hallways are lacking. The hotel lobby, restaurant, and general amenities are very nice and don't leave much to be desired.
The rooms however are extremely lacking. Once you exit the elevator the hotel drops a few notches on the cleanliness chain. The room really lacks any true amenities above what you would expect from any hotel. The room linens and decorations are old and were probably breathtaking in 1992 but not anymore. The art is old, the furniture has seen better days, and the showers are standard chain motel tubs.
The hotel lobby and Redfields Restaurant are awesome and really make the place worth the stay. The staff was also super friendly and professional.
The location is a bit of a walk from the Gaslamp and in a more secluded spot near the harbor.
The hotel is nice don't get me wrong but there are much newer and better located options in SD now. The center of the action has shifted over the years and is no longer focused in Seaport Village area. If you want a downtown San Diego walk out of your lobby and be in the action I would choose the following.
The Solomar, Omni, Marriot on K are all in the same price ranges and blow this hotel out of the water as far as service, amenities, location, and general perks.

title: “Good for the price”
text: Me And my small family stayed there while visiting kemah, it was homely. The staff was extremely helpful. I had accidentally booked my reservation for the wrong date and they help me fix it. It was easy to find and the room was ok. We will definitely stay there again in the future.

title: “Very Nice and Large Rooms; Excellent location and Staff.”
text: This was a busy hotel over Labor Day weekend. The customer service reps., valet personell, and housekeeping were all outstanding. The Suite we stayed in was very large and we really enjoyed the space.

title: “"Design-hotellish experience"”
text: There are elements in this hotel that would merit the design hotel label. However, for those looking for a design hotel experience, I advice to look elsewhere. This is a ok hotel with some nice service touches, like hotel-organized morning runs and refreshments after the run on the house (delivered to your room while you run) as well as wine hour every evening.

title: “Fab location”
text: We stayed at the Roosevelt Hotel from 2nd Feb till the 7th Feb 2009. We got a taxi from JFK which including tolls came to just under $50. We arrived at the hotel at about 4.30-5pm joined the small queue to check in. Check in was really easy just give your name show some photo ID (passport) and they need a credit card to authorise for any incidentals. I only had my bank card so handed that over but nothing was charged. We were booked into a cozy room but were upgraded at check in to a superior room. Sounds good but the only difference is the room is slightly bigger and has 2 double beds. The beds were really comfy if not slightly small , but we have a big bed at home so could just be us. The bathroom was compact but perfectly fine. The hotel is incredibly warm so we had to have the air on nearly all the time but you get used to it. Our room was on the 16th floor it was cleaned everyday and we had fresh towels everyday. This hotel is ideal if you are going to be out exploring New york everything is within walking distance and grand central station is just across the road. We didn't eat in the hotel although it did look nice we ate out as it was cheaper. When it was time to leave we checked out which just involved us handing over our door key and asked the doorman to order us a car, we got a lincoln town car back to JFK which was $60 including tip.

title: “Warm welcome, knowledgeable staff”
text:
We just stayed the last 2 nights here, my teenage son and I. This hotel is close to bus routes and within a 5 minute walk to the Presido and Science Museum. Many reviews have already been written about this hotel, and I can only reflect the good comments. From the moment we checked in we were welcomed with staff extremely knowledgeable about their own town, from how to get around on the Muni system to where the SF Guitar Center Store is and how do we get there.
I would recommend this hotel for the knowledge of the staff alone, but the healthy breakfast and great nights sleep we had, albeit in the middle of a huge city, certainly only added to our wonderful stay.
Thanks again to you all for being so wonderful!!!

title: “Friendly, inviting, beautiful property!”
text: When booking hotels in San Antonio you have a lot of options. And if you are like me, you look at various websites searching for the best deal. Well, Hotel Contessa had some pretty sweet deals!! This hotel was great. The staff were friendly and courteous, the restaurant was wonderful, the view of the riverwalk romantic and the rooftop pool just put it over the top for me. The rooms are well decorated suites. The shower is hot with good water pressure, the bed is comfortable and the living room area is well decorated with a 2nd large flat screen TV. And the room was very clean - the cleaning staff was great. The location is all you can ask for as we walked to everything (La Villita, The Alamo, etc). I have been to San Antonio many times, but this was a real treat. We will stay here again!

title: “Amazing customer service attitude...”
text: Amazing customer service attitude! Everyone you encounter is "out of their way" nice and helpful. Very comfortable beds.

title: “Delightful Upper East Side Boutique Hotel”
text: Chose this hotel for the first time for its proximity to my early meetings--and was not disappointed in any way. Their own website's 'best rate promise' beat my Platinum American Express travel agent by $80/night. Excellent location; generous sized "regular" room with all luxury appointments I would expect for a much higher rate. But the true winner here is the obviously superb service management philosophy. Had a minor issue that could have been catastrophic to my stay--but manager Jose Lema and housekeeping manager to the rescue and immediately ensured a prompt recovery. Lema made me feel he was personally engaged and involved in my complete satisfaction. Kudos to Lema and the general management of this hotel for exemplary customer service.

title: “Great Deal near the Riverwalk”
text: The hotel is located three blocks from the riverwalk in a secluded part of downtown - extremely quiet at night. The suite I was booked into was large & comfortable. The staff was extremely responsive & helped with dinner choices. Parking is a bit expensive ($12), but all hotels along the riverwalk have expensive parking. Nice bar, pool & atmosphere. Fitness center was well equipped.

title: “Great Location, Good Service”
text: This hotel is located approximately 15 minutes from downtown San Diego. Our room was of above average size and well appointed. The bed was comfortable and the amenities in the room were of above average quality. There was a microwave and small refrigerator in the room. The Islands Restaurant serves excellent breakfasts (pricey but delicious- appx $15 per person). There is a rather large swimming pool in the hotel; however, we did not use it as it was chilly outside (50 degrees). Parking is $12 per day for guest and Internet Service is $9.99 per day. Although we were not happy to pay for parking, we would defintely stay there again when we return to that area. We were able to use our cellphones (blackberry's modem to connect to the internet without problems).

title: “Worth every penny!”
text: We stayed at Renaissance July of 2011 and it is by far one of the best hotels I have stayed at thus far. The bed was to die for and a guarantee that you would have a great night of sleep. The hotel is centrally located in Time Square and its really cool to be able to come out at any given time and be surrounded by the hustle and bustle of Time Sqaure. The Hotel Bar that faces Time Sqaure is Awsome! Great for people who dont mind splurging to experience a A+++ Service.

title: “great value”
text:
The Ramada hotel is a great value for your money. My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel and everything about it was great. The shuttle service is excellent, the drivers are very knowledgable and made our trip easier. The rooms were cleaned daily and smelled fresh every day during our stay. The front end staff was helpful and suggested things to do and see for us. 
Contenental breakfast was a plus!!!
Right next door they have a bowling alley 24 hours to hang out all night. 
A very delightful experience and a money saver as well.
I would recommend this hotel to anybody

title: “Beautiful hotel, we'll be going back”
text: This hotel is very modern and updated and in a great location. It's easy to walk to Times Square or to catch the subway down the street. The staff was friendly and the rooms were very nice. There was a Keurig coffee maker in the room - very convenient and little mess. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Very stylish and relaxing stay at the Andaz”
text: This hotel was really a charm. The hotel staff was extremely friendly. We checked in the day after the blizzard hit, thankfully we got into the City just fine. Upon check in, we were offered complimentary coffee or tea which was nice after a long commute in. Rooms are great, huge in my opinion. Plenty of room at the desk to work, WI-FI in the rooms was easy to access and super fast. The decor was all modern and loved the rainfall shower. The complimentary work and non-alcoholic drinks were great since I am always thirsty and don't want to pay $4 for a bottle of water. We had complimentary cappuccinos during the entire stay which is another great perk as is the wine hour from 6-8. We just chilled, read the paper and sipped on some wonderful Malbec. For breakfast you can have some espresso or coffee with mini muffins and cookies, again complimentary. Overall the hotel was wonderful. Wall street area doesn't have a huge night light, but you are right around the block from the 2/3 so you can go anywhere in the City if you wanted to. Other subways are just another few blocks away. We found a few nice restaurants in walking distance so just takes some walking around and you will find stuff. We had a drink at BAR SEVEN FIVE, very good and the bar is also very chic and great service. I used the gym at the hotel which was huge and has ample machines and weights with bottled water and towels at all stations. Really superb hotel, I would definitely stay again.

title: “lemon”
text:

later, I asked Six avenune inn to keep heavey luggage for 2 days 
because I will come back to check in again but 
the front desk refuesed. Unbeliable. Othere average hotel

communication service to the room, It is terrible service not thinking for customers. If emergency happen,to family, how

 I willl not recommend to ohters to use this hotel.

title: “Consistent stay”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel for the last 15 years whenever I come to Seattle. I find the service to be fairly consistent and the staff to be very helpful and friendly. The rooms are clean and spacious. The beds are comfortable and as far as hotels go, their wireless internet service is faster than most hotels I stay at.
The only negative is their breakfast buffet. It's not worth the time or money to get. Order off the menu if you go to their restaurant.

title: “Nice Property, But Falls Short of Perfection”
text:
My gf and I spent a Saturday night here courtesy of Hotwire. On the whole, we thought it was a pretty nice property. The guest rooms and public areas are in excellent condition, as one would expect for such a new hotel. Desk, bell, and valet staff were courteous and efficient. Room was large enough, with a very nice bathroom. It's not the most convenient location for the tourist centers like Quincy Market, but the setting right along the waterfront made for a marvelous sunset walk.
Just a few quibbles: I have to agree with Riverspot's comments about the sliding window between the bathroom and bedroom. Every sound does indeed travel. This was a truly unfortunate design decision. The digital phones have an online directory that is tortuous to navigate. It must have taken me at least 5 minutes to find a way to call down for another robe (there was only one in the room). And when I finally did find the right menu item, no one answered the call after I let it ring for two minutes. I tried again later and someone picked right up, and the robe was there when we returned to the room several hours later.
Finally, although the TV was high-def, none of the channels were even digital, much less high-def. The picture quality on some of the channels was pretty bad.
Overall, this was a very pleasant stay and I would recommend the hotel. However, couples should be aware of the sliding bathroom window issue.

title: “no communication, deer in headlights vibe, useless”
text: Worst Starwoods hotel I have been to ever. No communication between staff, nickle and dime-y. Ever heard of a hotel charging a receiving fee for packages for a guest.. on top of that not advising the deliverer or the guest of this fee? Worst part is my thoroughness to make it easy for the hotel but the hotel was so dense in understanding that something will be delivered.. how can we make this easy? Its adjoined to the convention center, you'd think they'd have decent customer service.. Anyway, Le Meredien across town great! Seaport Boston Hotel great.. Westin = mush.

title: “After this visit, won't stay anywhere else!”
text: We booked this hotel for a two night stay 4/9-4/11 for my son and I for a whirlwind trip to NY then a drive down to Villanova, PA for a college visit. Booked it on a recommendation from a friend who stayed here in January and on recommendations from Tripadvisor.com. In addition, signed up for Hilton Rewards program prior to our arrival. Got what we felt was a great deal with the 10% Tripadvisor discounted as noted on this hotel's listing page ($260/night). We requested an early arrival on 4/9 as our plane landed at 9am. Once we got to the hotel at around 10am, we were initially told that we'd need to come back at 1pm. Raquel was behind the desk when we arrived and I mentioned the rave reviews she was getting for her service on Trip advisor. No sooner had we reached the elevator did she call our our name and said she could get us into the standard room we had requested---yipeee! This gave us the opportunity to unload our stuff and enjoy at least the two FULL days in NY. Because we were new Hilton Honors members, she included free internet access for us; she also gave us her email address so that if ever we came back, we could email her ahead of time and she'd make sure we were taken care of. We needed to get a taxi/car to the airport early on Wednesday AM. She took care of that with Kenny the bellman for us ahead of time so we didn't need to worry. Room was extremely clean with all amenities we needed. Bed was super comfy. Desk staff was always friendly, greeting us when we left and when we returned (even gave us some gummy bears when we stopped one of the times!). Upon our departure early Wednesday, the car that had been arranged hadn't gotten there yet, so the door man made sure to get us a car ASAP (I think he took one that was waiting on someone and switched them out with ours so that we could be on our way). The door man was wonderful---upon our arrival to the hotel, he stuck up for us when our taxi driver didn't even get out of the car to help us with the luggage; doorman gave a good, old fashioned "shout out" to the driver and promptly helped us with our bags. Overall this visit and stay made us want to stay a few days longer and we will no doubt be back to the Hilton again. Hotel location was perfect, right on 42nd St. between 7th and 8th Streets just off of the square which was a welcome respite. All theaters and main attractions in the area were less than a half mile walk in any direction. You would need a taxi ride to get to the harbor/Statue of Liberty and 9/11 areas (approx 3.5 mi. away) which we did. Loved it, loved it, loved it.

title: “What a GREAT Weekend!”
text:
I had the opportunity to spend the weekend at the Four Seasons Philadelphia and my experience was perfect! 
From the greeting upon arrival curb side to our departure a few days later; everyone associated with the hotel was friendly, helpful, and professional.
The location is perfect for first time guests to the city as well as those "in the know". We spent some time visiting the museums and being just steps away made the whole experience seem connected. 
I have been a guest a various Four Seasons hotels, and this hotel lives up to the reputation and experience you expect from a Four Seasons! 
We will be back!

title: “Superb service and well kept hotel”
text: Stayed one night here for a business meeting - it is truly a well kept, classy hotel. Definitely for the elegant traveler. Rooms are very comfortable and large, staff was incredibly friendly, and the restaurant (Juniper) was great. Beautiful courtyard to relax in too. Location is a bit outside of Georgetown but I'd still recommend this place.

title: “So So Essex”
text: Stayed at the Essex the last week of July 2004. Hotel was ok, rooms are small but that is to be expected in some of the older hotels. Beds are small, I think they are full-size. Carpets were in need of a shampooing. Very dirty and stained. Pool area is nice but, beware of peeling paint on the bottom of the pool. My daughter had dove into the pool to grab a toy from the bottom and had a paint chip wedged under her finger nail. We had to mention this to the desk people twice and no one seemed to want to report it to management. Another thing about the pool area, make sure you have your room key or you will be acosted by the desk clerk/lifeguard. If you have children under the age of 18, they are not permitted to use the new workout room. If we had been aware of that fact we would have picked another hotel, that information is not listed on the website (that I could find). Our children are in their teens and were not allowed to use the facilites.

title: “Excellent Service”
text: On my first visit to this hotel I experienced the best service possible. The front dest agent Veronica went over and beyond what was expected. My bags were misplaced at the airport and Brandon the manager at the time made sure they were delivered to me promptly when the airport dropped them off later on that evening. Whenever I have to return to the Dallas area i will always choose this hotel.

title: “Secluded cottage style San Diego jewel!”
text: Amazing is all I can say. Had all the amenities you can think of i.e. great food, bar atmosphere, great pools, lush/scenic gardens, golf course, and romantic cottage style rooms. This resort had the feel of a secluded wine country cottage. Service was excellent throughout my stay. My only suggestion for minor improvement would be at the front desk, it was often not staffed as they appeared to be in a back room. At such a luxurious resort and a holiday weekend (father's day) the front desk should never be empty. Despite this I would highly recommend for a qreat weekend with your sweetie. On my next visit, I have to try the spa as it looked amazing.

title: “Pretty Disappointing Service”
text:
Our first disappointment was calling before arrival to have the concierge book a reservation at Salty's, only to learn that the concierge was "gone for the day" at 4:15 p.m.
Upon arrival, we were assigned a room that was 76 degrees and wouldn't cool down.
Then, they had one of their employees (name not remembered) take us to another room that was 75 degrees.
Both rooms were in the South Tower on a sunny, 40-degree day and they obviously had no cooling capability available.
Third room was across from the elevator (we requested not near an elevator or ice machine) and reeked of chlorine.
Why would they try to put anyone in a room with a heavy chlorine odor?
Doesn't anyone on staff realize this is not a good idea?
At that point, the employee assisting us put me on the phone to a supervisor named Kathryn who sarcastically said "Sooooo, Mr. XXXX, I understand we don't have any rooms that please you?".
Kathryn clearly needs some remedial training in customer relations, or better yet, another job.
To which I replied that all we wanted was a room with working heating/cooling that didn't reek of chlorine and wasn't next to an elevator or ice machine.
Fourth room was in the North Tower and was nice, but the ice machine for that floor had been removed and not replaced.
We noticed that all four of the rooms we experienced had only one drinking glass in the bathroom.
Be advised that there are no bathroom exhaust fans in any of the Westin's rooms and plan on a steamy bathroom when you take a shower.
The Westin's location is superb, but they desperately need to pay attention to their level of service.

title: “No Problems”
text:
well, I must admit that I had already stayed at the Pennsylvania when I read these comments here. My girlfriend and I stayed there in April, having been lured by an (for New York City) unbeatable price, then prebooked over the net. However, when a friend of mine who was also looking for cheap accomodation in the Big Apple, shortly afterwards told me that he had read some not so favorable reviews on the net (quite possibly on this very page), we started having doubts, especially since my girlfriend was pregnant at the time.
But it was too late anyway, so we decided to give it a try. We arrived at Penn Station, so the hotel was literally across the street, which means a perfect location, with all the subways and a lot of attractions nearby. We were greeted by a spacious hall and had no problems whatsoever with the reception area. By the way, if some people here complain about having to stand in lines (which, by the way, we never had to): what do you expect when you stay a cheap places...your personal concierge?! We were lead to our first room in which, due to renovation, the TV didn't work but within fifteen minutes we finally settled down in another one and there we stayed for seven nights.
To summarize it all, we did not encounter cockroaches, did not hear any next door guest, did have clear water and, most important, a clean bathroom (the first one in the States which my girlfriend entered withour sandals or socks...and that was definitely the biggest compliment she could give ;-)...we had a perfect stay and I can only recommend this place!
Reading all these negative reviews I cannot help but wonder if these people have never before been to NYC - where cockroaches are common even in 5 star lodgings - and space is enormously expensive, resulting in rather tiny rooms...

title: “Still the best!”
text: This was our second stay at the Sofitel Manhattan. From sept. 18 to 25, we stayed 5 nights. Just like last May, the service was impeccable, the staff always helpful. I had requested a room with a view on the Chrysler building, which was given to us by a very kind man at the reception. The concierge unfortunately was not able to locate one of the best-known store for us, and we had to find it by ourselves. Apart from this very minor thing, the room was always super-clean with service twice a day, the bathroom was great, the location was unbeatable. We already know that our next trip in NYC will include nights at the Sofitel Manhattan, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for great quality and even luxury, for a still afordable price (the euro/USD exchange rate making it even easier for us from Europe).

title: “Decent hotel”
text: The location of the hotel is great, and reception staff friendly. The room was small, but OK. For a short stay, you don't need a lot of space. The plumbing in the bathroom is terrible though. Problems with flushing the toilet, shower impossible because temperature changes from freezing cold to burning hot... Daily but only very superficial cleaning in the bathroom.

title: “Great Service, Great Location, Great Price”
text:
Tired of the mid-town madness? My wife and I were and we thought it was time to shift downtown and enjoy a real neighborhood. That's exactly what we got at the Soho Courtyard.
First, let's get room size out of the way. Yes, the room was small, but hey... perhaps we are all getting a little too big! The bathroom was new and quite expansive so these remarks are limited only to the sleeping quarters. Otherwise the room was very clean and fresh. The furniture was new and nicely designed to modern tastes. We had a view facing east, and there was not much to look at save the large building acorss the street. Next stay, we'll try a room with a view facing the Hudson to the west. Altogether, the room was great, particular in light of the rate we paid. It was a great value.
Check-in was smooth and the service was spot on. Fast forward and suffice it to say that the service for the entire stay was impeccable. The manager, bell captain, breakfast servers... not a single problem. The entire staff is engaged and it shows. Kudos to all!
The neighborhood is the crown jewel for this location. After check-in, we walked north and had lunch at John's Pizza. John's was great and I ate too much. Strolled through the Village and truly enjoyed the vibe on a brilliant sunny afternoon.
In the evening, we got balcony tickets for Blue Man and really enjoyed the show. The venue is a short walk through the village and again, you'll feel the pulse. Tip - black attire is obligatory in NYC, however, black lights at the Blue Man Group will reveal galaxies of lint by end of show.
Subway lines are all around so moving about the island is pretty darn easy. The next day, we took the subway up to the Natural History Museum to see the butterfly exhibit. Highly recommended! If you get a chance, try the Gray Dog just a little to the north - it's great for lunch.
Checkout was easy and we lingered for a few minutes and shot the breeze with the staff. They were cool and down to earth. No goofy attitudes like so many other hotels. In summary, the hotel was fresh and clean, well managed with an engaged staff, and an excellent value.

title: “Second stay at the Bedford”
text:
I like this hotel so much I could live there ! Not surprising as this was an apartment building before it was a hotel, hence the great size rooms, very ample storage , the kitchenettes and ( joy of joys ) windows that open.
This was my 2nd. time at this hotel, last year I was travelling solo but this time with a friend so booked a suit. Once again great room size and storage ( HUGE by most NY hotel standards.)
The large lounge had its own storage ( containing digital safe for your valuables ) in addition to that in the bedroom, 2 double sofa beds and a decent size mirror so it was easy to work around only having one bathroom. For this reason though you may not want to go for max. possible room occupancy if it is an all girl trip !
Staff still as friendly and helpful as last time. Norman, (Mr. vacuum cleaner !) is a particulr favourite of mine. Yvette, our room service girl kept everything in tip top condition and anything we requested was dealt with immediately. 
Always plenty of hot water and fresh towels, although we did arrange that only the used towels ( left on the floor) be changed on a daily basis. 
As other postings have mentioned there are great food options on Lexington and at Grand Central, check out the food market on the lower level. If you are going to the upper west side visit Fairways supermarket on Broadway and 74th. street, this should be a tourist attraction in it's own right ! This is also the area to buy wine at a sensible price ( base of Brooklyn Bridge also good value).
Two things worth knowing about the hotel is that they do have a washer and a dryer for guest use, located in the basement, and , if you need a brolly ( umbrella ) just ask to borrow one at the reception desk.
I can't wait to stay at the Bedford again, for my next visit I will be treating myself to a Tower Suit with a balcony.
I hope the above is helpful for anyone travelling to NY.

title: “Not up to Jumeirah's usual standards!”
text: Writing to warn those of you used to staying in their beautiful hotels in the Middle East that this does not live up to expectations. Whilst the location is excellent and the rooms comfortable there is nothing luxurious about this hotel. Standard of bathrooms is average, cleaning standards not up to 5 star (dust on the doors and hairs in bathroom), staff are courteous but nothing more. Also there was no regard for our gold member status in the hotel, we had to request benefits several times and were not treated with any extra attention. We can only assume that these are standards acceptable in NY as we have not encountered them in any other Jumeriah resort or hotel. On arrival we waited an hour extra for our room, no upgrade was offered, only when dealing with a senior member of management were we offered a coffee for the delay. Breakfast is nice but for the price I would expect to be able to order fresh eggs. On a positive note the beds are exceptionally comfortable so we slept well! For 750 dollars a night would also be nice to have bfast included and a room which does not over look aircon units that turn 24/7.

title: “You get what you pay for”
text: This is the second time I stayed here, primarily because of it's proximity to my job. It's a Red Roof, not a Hilton, just a Red Roof. The location of the property is great for restaurants and it's not too far for San Antonio's attractions. I got "clean" in the shower and I slept in the bed. That's enough about that. They offer a shuttle service to the attractions and the airport. Basic continental breakfast with a Texas-shaped waffle. Swimming pool looks enticing, but it's not my thing. No complaints, I'd do it again.

title: “Mixed emotions!!”
text:
The view is nice, but that's about all. We paid a lot of money for a view only. The room is small, over crowed with furniture and was not well maintained or clean. In our 3rd floor end room (room 320) there was a king bed, loveseat, table and 2 chairs, small refrigerator with microwave on top of it, along with an air conditioner sitting on the floor, 1 night stand and dresser. The room has 2 sets of French doors but it is so crowded you cannot open but one set and that is if you move everything else to make room to open them. The bathroom is tiny. You have to sit on the toilet sideways to keep from having the sink in your face. The floors were so dirty that if you walked from the small bathroom to the bed (approx 6 feet) your feet would be black on the bottom from the dirty floor. The color of the decor was drab - dark brown and ugly painted walls. The curtain rods were broken and rusted so you had to fight with them to open up the French doors. The pillows were old and very over used - one we had even smelled terrible. The small area they had for you to hang clothes was rusted and you could not use it very easily.
Ocean Beach is a very diversified area and we loved the shops and restaurants but the Ocean Beach Hotel needs to be renovated and they charge way to much just for a view. 
Also beware the hotel sits right on the street and you hear all the road traffic all the people walking by and we had to sleep with ear plugs to drown out the noise that goes on all night. 
All in all the hotel needs HELP!!! But the Ocean Beach area is nice and fun!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This was a great hotel. I was there for 7 days for a conference!!! I loved the clean room, and especially the glass shower... I recommend this hotel to anyone that's going to be in the San Francisco area!!! Two thumbs up

title: “I would not do it again”
text: We came to Philadelphia to help a family member. We decided it was best to stay in a hotel instead of at the family member's house because of various reasons. To start check in was pretty rocky. The hotel did not seem to be worth the price they were charging per night. I was told at check that there is no parking. You have to park in any nearby lot which range from 10 dollars to 30 dollars depending on what time you park and if you need to leave the lot and return. The neighborhood is not that great but I think if are looking to be near the Convention Center it is great. I did not need to be near the convention ctr. I did not know that there was a homeless shelter nearby because lots of homeless people were strolling near the hotel. The air conditioning in the room did not work so we had to be moved. Once moved the A/C in that room did not work efficently. After many calls to the front desk I was finally told how to set the A/C for maximum benefit. THe room did finally cool down but it took a while. The staff was pretty courteous and the hotel smelled really nice. I could have stayed in a hotel with more stars and had on site parking/versus this low budget high priced plus extra for parking hotel. ALso there is a lot of construction going on in this area right now.( cant hold that against the hotel). KIDS THERE IS NO POOL. But I would not stay again.

title: “Great views”
text: Beautiful view from balcony and a great breakfast. Pool is very small as others have indicated. Room size was nice but instead of 2 queens there are 2 full size beds with a pullout full in the sofa. We brought an air mattress so it worked out but it would have been torture with three kids without it. The hotel is in Paradise Valley rather then Scottsdale (unless this is considered part of Scottsdale?). Emphasis is on golf but it was still has a lot to offer even if you don't. We stayed 3/30 through 4/2 and the weather was fantastic.

title: “We will definitely come back again!”
text:
My husband and I live in a suburb of Chicago and we stayed at the Hotel Palomar for one night to celebrate our wedding anniversary. I selected this hotel after reading the great reviews and because of the very competitive room rate. We had an excellent stay and a wonderful experience. 
Service was excellent! Soon after we left our car with the valet, he came looking for us because my husband had forgotten his phone in the car. Upon check-in, the concierge seemed geniunely interested in helping us and interested in the reason for our stay. We informed her that we were in the city to celebrate our anniversary. When we arrived to our room later that day, there was a complimentary bucket of champagne (albeit on the cheaper side) with a personalized note congratulating us on our anniversary. Nice touch!
Perfect location! Located in the River North area, we were able to walk to all of our destinations. 
Clean and comfortable room! The room was very clean and the bed and pillows were extremely comfortable. I also love the l'occitane bath products. Also, the size of the room was pretty good considering that it's in the city.
My husband and I will return to the hotel. You won't be disappointed with your stay.

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text: Rooms are updated and of a very good size, even for a suite hotel. Nice that they have a full door between bedroom and living area. Concierge Lounge had very friendly and helpful staff and food was kept clean and replensihed as needed. Nice feature that they are some distance from airport but still provide shuttle bus. Checkin staff also very frinedly and helpful. Excellent choice for a family who needs more room or a longer stay business person.

title: “Towers are a saving grace”
text: My father was undergoing open heart surgery. I read reviews and was very sceptical, "DONT BE". The Towers are fine. They provide a close and convenient access to the hospital or Childrens Hospital at a very resonable rate. It is safe, clean and very convenient. You can access the hospital ICU 24 hrs a day. Parking is safe, and the Towers provide passes so that you can go in and out of the parking garage without paying EXTRA cash.You cant ask for a better place to stay while you are remaining close to your loved one. The staff at the Towers were very helpful. We had pre-arranged to have a desent ref-freezer in the room, a microwave and coffee maker. If you stay anywhere else, you have to fight traffic and the like. The hallways are clean as noted above, and the room and bathroom were more than acceptable. This is not a five star hotel, HOWEVER it is not as bad as the other reviews state. I'm in Law Enforcement, and if I thought this hotel was the least a dump, I would not have let my mother(80 yrs old) stay here. The rugs have been replaced by the way, and the beds and the like are great and changed daily by the Towers maid staffing. This is a no brainer when you need to be close to your loved one. While at the Towers, I interacted with doctor's that spent the night on the same floor as I was on, and they had no problem with the accomadations... Your not taking a chance if you stay here. Roving security officers also patrol the floors occupied by hotel guests. I stayed eight days without a problem. (11-29-11)

title: “Very Good but rooms small !”
text: A great weekend in NYC as always. The hotel was OK but the rooms were very small , but as i was worned in advance this did not cause my heart to drop as can happen when you enter a small hotel room for the first time. In general the rooms are v clean the beds are v cumfy and the in room facilities good. will stay again but will have to pay extra for larger room.

title: “The hotel I judge all other hotels by”
text:
We booked this hotel to stay over New Year in 2006-2007, and we were not disappointed.
Our bags were taken from us the second we got out of our taxi by the hotel staff. The receptionist was fantastic, very efficient, friendly and helpful.
On first impressions of this hotel I was very impressed and it only got better.
The room was massive, with a seperate sitting area, with flat screen TV's in both rooms and very clean.
It is about a ten minute walk to the Empire State building and close to all transport links.
This is just the best hotel I have ever stayed at, and the fact that it seems pretty much booked solid for the next few months backs that up.
I would stay in this hotel again without hesitation.

title: “We made a good choice”
text: We were in DC for an event which had arranged a special rate, including breakfast, at this hotel. Otherwise it would have been out of our price range. We had a queen/queen room which was huge (by European standards), comfortable and well-appointed. The only extra thing we would have liked was a kettle to make tea/coffee. The breakfast selection was good but it was served in the bar area which we felt was not ideal - the seating arrangements are OK for having a drink but many tables were rather low for eating. The staff could not have been more helpful, sorting out any problems for us, advising on various things and going out to hail a taxi for us. The nearest metro station is about 10 minutes walk away. We thought the evening meal choice was rather limited and expensive but there are plenty eating places wiithin 10 minutes walk. We enjoyed the free wine hour on a couple of evenings - a nice extra. In summary, we're pleased we stayed here and would certainly consider staying again if we are ever back in DC.

title: “San Francisco and The Palace, Special Memories”
text:
My wife and I have now been staying for 4 years at the Palace, (our daughter attends Academy of Art, now a Senior) and although we have been only able to stay 4 times we always have pleasant memories of The Palace. We also stay at The Handlery, which is nice ( it also has a Sauna, and I am Scandinavian) but nothing compares to your Hotel.
My wife, Wanda and I both admire when an employee goes the extra step or two to make us feel special. Lydia in the Spa is one of those people.
Early in the morning, or after a long drive, Lydia has an energy and smile ( plus amazingly remembered our name) to brighten our day and gives the face of The Palace a great big smile. 
Congrats to you on the quality of The Palace and the smarts to place Lydia where everyone can enjoy and appreciate her.
Richard Lindroos
richard@eurocaroc.com

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
Beautifully appointed rooms. Spacious, with great furnishings and floor to ceiling windows. Room also had a very nice bathroom.
Overall, was a great experience at this very nice hotel.
The location is also great and close to the subway in Soho.

title: “Best Place Near Mile High”
text:
This seems to be the best place within walking distance of INVESCO/Mile High. It's a little less than a mile walk on a paved path that starts just across the street from the hotel. Quite a few local ticket holders parked nearby for the walk in to the stadium.
The hotel itself is typical Hampton Inn. Clean, comfortable enough, free wifi, free breakfast, refrigerator & microwave in the room, nothing fancy. We have no complaints about our stay at all. 
I wouldn't agree that the hotel is easy walking distance from all downtown attractions as some reviewers have seemed to suggest. But Denver isn't that big or that hard to navigate, so the hotel is definitely easy driving distance from everything.

title: “Old World Feel”
text: My husband and stayed at the O'Brien on July 12th and it was Wonderful. The room was small but beautifully appointed and the staff was awesome. If you are looking for a place for a quiet weekend or just a break in traveling (like us) it's the perfect place.

title: “Excellent Service, Great Location, Roomy Rooms”
text:
Loved our stay Sept. 26-28 at Magic Castle. As other reviewers have noted, the service was incredible -- we've stayed in Ritz-Carltons that didn't have as good service. Really. All of the staff was friendly, helpful, ready with great suggestions for dinner, always offering free snacks and sodas. I can't say enough good things about them.
That said, this isn't a five-star resort, so don't expect the rooms to be elegant. They're basically a converted apartment -- living room, dining area, kitchen, bathroom and separate bedroom. We loved that one of us could be watcing tv in the living room while the other slept late and since the bedroom had a door, there was no noise. It was great to have a fridge and a stove/oven, too so we could heat up leftovers and chill a bottle of wine. The rooms could use a little updating, though, which is why I didn't give it 5 stars. Everything was extremely clean, but definitely some wear-and-tear -- old paint on the tiles in the bathroom, cracks on the concrete walkways to the rooms, and wall units for air conditioners (which worked extremely well but were a little noisy). It didn't bother us in the least, but if you're used to everything being modern and perfectly maintained, this might not be the hotel for you.
The location was great -- 1 block walk from Kodak Theatre and Mann's Chinese, a few more blocks walk for shopping, restaurants and pubs (we liked Happy Ending for a beer -- definitely try the andouille corn dogs, the food was incredible for a pub). We felt safe walking in the neighborhood, even at night.
One more thing to mention about the hotel -- you can go to Magic Castle if you're staying here. It's a once-in-a-lifetime experience (a private members-only club) to see magicians perform up close. We probably saw 8 different shows + dinner over about 5 hours and the magicians were incredible. Make sure you go early, when it opens, so you can get in line for the best shows -- and prepare to wait -- we went on a Saturday night and had to wait 1 hour+ for the best shows (there were at least 250 people there). Dinner was good but pricey - $135 for two with one glass of wine each. And you do have to wear jackets and ties for men, very dressy dresses for women, we saw lots of people in black tie. It was a fabulous experience that you just can't get anywhere else.
I will definitely stay at Magic Castle Hotel again next time I'm in L.A.

title: “Great location - friendly staff”
text:
My girlfriend booked this hotel for a fun weekend away. I usually have good luck with hotels in Seattle, but this place is phenomenal. Not only is it modern and very comfortable (the beds are incredible), but the location can't be beat. It's right in the heart of the shopping district downtown and there are plenty of great restaurants nearby (try the Metropolitan Grill for happy hour). The room we stayed in had electric blinds that virtually black out the room, so you won't be woken up by the light creeping through the curtains. And when you eventually wake up, naturally there's a Starbucks in the lobby.
I've stayed in some good hotels in Seattle, but I'll return to the Hyatt next time I'm in town.

title: “Perfect Location”
text:
Just got back after spending 5 nights at the Fairmont. As said in previous reviews, the Hotel is gorgeous and rich with history but there is NO COFFEE in the rooms. I found this annoying when they have a drawer full of overpriced goodies in the room for a charge and Holiday Inns offer coffee in the rooms.
 The location very convenient, however if you plan on taking the cable car to Union or the Wharf, good luck! The hotel is at the highest part of the cable line, therefor the cable cars are full every time the y come by. What we did, go to Walgreens, but a pass that gets you on the cable cars, muni, and buses. Take the Cali & Market Car down to Embarcadaro, then walk to Union Square or take a street car to the Wharf. Saves you LOTS of time and aggregation.
Take a minute to go to the Top of The Mark restaurant for a meal or just a drink. It is located across from the hotel on California and Mason just before Powell. The breathtaking panoramic views of the city are amazing.
Lastly, if you want to go to the zoo, do NOT ask the concierge. We were given two separate sets of directions, everything with connections except to drive or taxi it, nothing direct. I took it upon myself and went to the muni station at the bottom of Powell and Market. I was told to hop on the L train which happens to have its last stop at the ZOO! 25 minutes and we were there. Afterwards, the concierge's didn't seem to like the fact that I thought they should give our directions to guests.
I would stay again, no doubt about it. It is in what I would consider the safest part of the city! PS Grace Cathedral is one block away for mass on Sunday If you wish to attend.

title: “Best bed ever !!!!”
text:
yeah room can be pretty small , but in a city that you have millions of things to do it was perfect ,I arrived there at 11 am , had to be in a metting at 3pm the lady who check me in told me till 3pm but she checked the system and was able to check in , nice small clean room, the guys at the front desk always willing to help , internet was perfect , upon check in you get an info. sheet with all that you need to know ,like the internet code , restaurant , where the gym is at ,
thank you guys for a nice stay, I was there for 2 nts 8/21-8/22

title: “Disappointing to say the least!”
text: Alright so I don't know if they post the time of the reviews that people write them but I think it's important to note that I am writing this in the hotel at two in the morning. This is my first night at this hotel and I originally stayed here because of the great location. Although it is in a nice location, this does not make up for the hotel's many drawbacks. The rooms are tiny. If you are used to staying at hotels with spacious rooms like the The Palace or The Pierre, you will be severely disappointed here. Even though I looked forward to the more chic, modern vibe of the hotel I found that it was haphazardly thrown together and the decor looked as if it was under construction. The worst aspect of the hotel is the noise level. Of course if you enjoy clubbing at ungodly hours in the morning, you will not be bothered by the constant stream of 25 year olds screaming and jumping around to pounding music at all hours of the night. But if you are anyone like me you will find that the "hotel" that you planned to stay at is actually a incubus of obnoxious bouncers! Once again, this hotel can be a nice stay for some people, but at 2 AM, with my room at 76 degrees, and no end in sight...I'm transfering to the Four Seasons.

title: “Great hotel with great staff, but parking and valet service not so great”
text:
I have been to this hotel several times as I am a huge baseball fan. I have never had any issues as the staff has been very professional, helpful, and courteous. The room has always been made to perfection. Although, this stay was quite different as they have instituted valet parking, or shall I say "partial" valet parking. The hotel has limited parking spaces, so you may get one, you may not. If you get one, the charge is now $29.95 per night (previous to this, it was free). The valet will only park your car once you get to the garage. They will not get it from the front of the hotel when you check in, nor will they bring it to the front door when you are ready to check out. You have to go down into the garage to retrieve your vehicle, only after they drive it to the garage entrance, which is at the back of the hotel. The particular valet I had didn't know how to drive a standard transmission and failed to let anyone know. He proceeded to my 2012 Jeep and decided he would try to learn how to drive a standard transmission; IN MY JEEP!!! The Jeep jumped and bucked and squealed and then finally stalled. I am not happy with this service!!! 
I will definitely consider other lodging options the next time I am in town for a baseball game.

title: “It's a hilton, what do you expect?”
text: Hiltons have always been nice hotels. The rates are ok here, kind of expensive for the leisure traveler. I was splitting the room with two other people, so it wasn't as bad. I stayed here two nights. The hotel was huge, and the rooms were very nice. It was hard to find the room however, since there were a lot of floors and the elevator was confusing. It was also hard to find people to take us to the room, but we finally got there. The bathroom was good and clean too. Go ahead and hide the key to the minibar like we did. Everything in it can be purchased at the Walgreens nearby for much cheaper. There is only wired internet in the room, and I didn't know that beforehand so I had to pay extra to use the wireless network. There is a starbucks downstairs near the lobby.I think wireless internet should be included with your bill. I would stay here again if I had the money.

title: “Refreshing...”
text: ...to get a hotel where the amenities are nice and the hotel staff is genuinely nice. The room came with a bottle of wine. The front desk is more than willing to help out with whatever you ask. In the morning when asked how my stay was, I jokingly said that everything was great, except the shaving cream (I used their complimentary shaving cream). The gentleman at the front desk told me that he would make a note of it and that he appreciated the feedback. This is something that was so minute, but you can tell that this hotel has crafted a culture of service. Highly recommended.

title: “Find someplace else to stay - huge disappointment”
text:
I’m sure you can find a better place to stay. I certainly will choose someplace else in the future.
The pluses: 
Close to the airport, friendly check in (and there was a line), comfortable bed.
The minus:
Cost!!! Almost $200 and that didn’t include breakfast or internet. Some packages may include those pluses. Very noisy being right next to the freeway. Not enough staffing at the front desk to handle rushes in the morning and evening.Worn out/dated.
I think was frustrated me the most was the request for a quiet room and was placed next to the freeway on a low floor. Yes, I could have gone down and requested a new room, but at 930pm and after a long day, I let it go.
Find a better place is my recommendation

title: “Great location, clean with great people.”
text: We had a great experience while staying at the Sheraton. It is close to everything, not just the wharf, this place will save you from many cab ride (by the way, many of the cab drivers are crazy drivers). The people at the hotel were really great, very informative (the concierge) and very polite and helpful. The outdoor seating area is a great place to relax morning or night. I would say the only reason why I didn't give it 5 stars is because the food is way over priced. There are many restaurants in the neighbourhood that are tasty and cheap! Oh and I had read reviews before hand that it was noisy, but we did not have that problem AT ALL! Slept like a baby!

title: “Comfortable at Stanford Court”
text: I booked three rooms for three nights for our family get-together in San Fransciso. Everyone really enjoyed comfy, clean rooms and the price was very reasonable on Priceline. All three rooms were newly renovated on the upper floors! Free champagn in the Lobby on Thursday evening welcomed us to the hotel - very nice. The concierge was fabulous! We had trouble getting reservations to The Slanted Door - a restaurant that was highly recommended to us. The concierge was able to book our reservations like magic. The concierge continued to be our best friend throughout the weekend. The hotel is undergoing renovations but we were only disturbed by noise on late Friday afternoon. Everything was quiet over the weekend. This is a nice location with easy access to public transportation. The trolleys were very crowded most of the time but well worth the wait to back to the hotel...as it's a very steep walk from almost any direction! We had breakfast at the hotel one morning and it was pleasant and delicious - although the service was a bit slow. We did have difficulty keeping ice in the room with no ice machine available. Room service would bring ice - but it usually took awhile. We took the hotel limo to SFO airport for a very reasonable price. Overall a very nice weekend!

title: “Affinia 50 experience”
text:
Dec. 17-21. This was our families first trip to New York City and we had high hopes for the Affinia 50. For starters check in time is suppose to be at 3:00pm. We arrived at 6:00pm only to be kept waiting by the incompitent staff saying our room was not ready yet. Thirty confusing minutes of waiting in the lobby were followed by our gracious host telling us we were being switched to a different room. The room we were given (1102) has a lovely view of a brick wall.
We returned to our room on our second night out on the town only to find that our room was not only unlocked but the door was left wide open. We are still doing inventory on personal items. The manager that responded to our complaint promissed a bottle of wine as compensation! This bottle of wine failed to reach us. Continental Breakfast? $17.00? A far better one is served for free at Motel 6. More to come on this...

title: “OMNI”
text: What a wonderful experience while visiting San diego for the first time. Luxury without being overbearing, efficient and friendly service in the dining room and at the check in desk, a knowledgeable concierge with the right advice (thanks Robert!) and the weather. All conbined to make the downtown experience there fabulous. A pool, a city view, and a location on the edge of what's happening in the downtown topped it off. Nice and simple. We would return anytime.

title: “Loved Pan Pacific”
text: We are Pan Pacific fans having stayed at several of their properties in Asia. Wish there were more of them in the US. We found the same attention to detail and caring service in the Seattle Pan Pacific as we have in the Asian properties. Location is good, room was great, enjoyed the dining experiences and loved the free shuttle that was available at certain times of the day. Tip: take it to the Needle as parking there is very expensive. I always love a hotel where the staff seems happy with their job. It is a sign of good management! That usually means it trickles down to the guest.

title: “Horrible, run fast - NEVER stay here.”
text:
Booked 6 nights - fled after one. They can keep my money - just to get out of the cat dropping rodent infested dump. NEVER stay here. I tried to save money and it was a STUPID decision on my part. I read the bad reviews and thought "no place can be that bad". It is. NYC is doing a disservice to tourists by letting this thing stay open. I would not stay here even if it was free. You pay me $100 per night, and then I might say.
The showers were filthy and could here people in the next box zipping and upzipping their zippers. NEVER, EVER stay here.

title: “Excellent hospitality and guest service with "heart"”
text: Hilton Garden Inn, a downtown Philly hotel, exemplifies outstanding hospitality and personal service at affordable rates far below those in other Center City hotels and far above other chain hotels. The posted commitment to "service with heart" is evident everywhere -- from Charles and Bell staff to Angela, Sandra and Natasha at Front Desk, to Housekeeping and Restaurant staff. How nice to be recognized and greeted by name upon every entry to the lobby. A prior request for room type to accommodate my husband's post-surgery sleeping requirement was received with caring understanding and a sincere willingness to do their best based on what would be available at check-in -- and later honored with complete satisfaction and comfort. Everyone greets you with a smile and "how are you doing today?" The location is excellent, within walking distance to many historical sites, shops and eateries; and convenient to all transportation options. Philly is a very clean and truly tourist-friendly city, and this Hilton property made our stay that much more enjoyable.

title: “Great Hotel but Poor Service ..”
text:
I use to love staying at the strand , but last two visits i was overcharged by over $220 since they now use an automated refreshment center that was EMPTY my entire 4 days stay and i was charged for every item in the refrigerator (but i haven't consumed anything)
the Hotel Stuff was very friendly and was able to refund the entire overhead charge, BUT having to stand in the lobby and disputing this charges on very visit is unacceptable ! please fix this situation 
to hotel is clean and nicely designed and in a great location other than the refreshment center this is a great place to stay in .

title: “We keep coming back-kid friendly with style”
text:
My husband and 2 daughters (ages 4 and 17 months) returned to the Biltmore for our 3rd Easter in a row. Each year we look at other places in Phoenix since we'll be in town to see family, but can't find a better mix of style, good restaurants, kid-friendly amenities and location than the Biltmore. 
With the addition of the Frank and Albert's casual restaurant, things have gotten even better. In the past we'd leave the resort to eat lunch or dinner at the nearby Cheesecake factory or California pizza kitchen because the resort lacked a kid-friendly restaurant. This year we booked an all-inclusive package that was terrific and so we ate about 10 times at Frank and Alberts and never exhausted the options. The food was really good--mostly organic fare, fresh ingredients, nice presentation--and the restaurant is very big with nice outdoor seating so we never felt like we were bothering the adult parties in the restaurant (a separate bar area helps, too). 
Our girls loved the paradise pool and playground, my husband played a round of golf (a bit pricey at about $300 covering greens fees cart rental and rented clubs but very nice), and I got spa treatments. In particular we had great service from Adrienne at Frank and Albert's and Judith at the squaw peak lawn.
The only downside is that lovely grounds are very spread out I wish I had brought a double stroller--getting from place to place is real hike and my girls occasionally fought over who was going to be carried and who was going to ride. And housekeeping usuallly comes late in the day so it can be challenging to coordinate naps; we opted to let the girls nap poolside in the shade, which was fine.
In all though, service was terrific and we'll likely return next year, particularly if they offer the all-inclusive package again.

title: “Almost perfect for the price.”
text: WE decided to stay at Le Meridien GAlleria because the proximity to the mall but not attached to it which would have cost much more. Rooms are extremely spacious and very clean and well decorated and appointed. The only reason why I did not give it 5 stars is because some of the services I always expect from this chain like spa were absent. None the less, if you are staying at this property it's because you are in Dallas to shop and therefore out of the hotel most of the day anyway. If I return to Dallas this is where I want to stay again.

title: “You get what you pay for”
text: For San Francisco, the location was very good and the price was quite reasonable. The doors were not very soundproof, but after each day of tiring touring we were not very disturbed by the noise in the hallway. The staff was very helpful. The room was overheated, but anyone who knew how to turn off a radiator and open a window could deal with it. Couldn't find a better deal for the money paid. Our room was waiting for us and we were satisfied. The "continental breakfast" was less than ok but the on site internet cafe provided a cheap supplement. This "review" mechanism did not allow me to give an accurate rating so I would say that the hotel is due a 3.8 out of 5.

title: “OMG don't stay here!!!!!!!!!!”
text: DO NOT STAY IN THIS HOTEL! The rooms are dirty, there are beg bugs! My friend has bites all over her body and I feel terrible about it! The service wasn't the greatest and the manager, a little Chinese woman was less than accommodating! DO NOT DO NOT DO NOT STAY HERE! Spend your money somewhere else, it will be worth it!

title: “This isn't a normal Super 8, it's like a 5 star hotel.”
text: This Super 8 Motel is downright awesome. When you check in, they give you a nice goodie bag filled with a bottled water and a bag of candies to keep your energy up or a way of saying thanks for checking in our hotel. The breakfast in the morning is good and they have things such as eggs, bacon and cereal to name a few. Also, there is FREE movies every night on Channel 11 after 6 pm every evening that you stay, so makes it even more worth the while. The massage that they claim is FREE is a massage chair. The front desk is very knowledgeable about the city overall and can tell you how to get anywhere. San Marcos is about 20 miles from the hotel and it has a outlet mall that everyone from all over the state comes to see. Overall, this SUPER 8 Motel is not your average motel, it's more than a Hilton or Holiday Inn can offer for cheaper! Go for it.

title: “Good location for work, bad hotel room for work”
text:
I was excited about this hotel as I was going to be there for a week for work. However, the rooms are REALLY small. My room faced the inner brick wall of the hotel. I was debating changing rooms when one of my colleagues told me not to bother. He said that he had an outer room that was directly facing Lexington and 50st street, which is one of the busiest intersections in the city and VERY noisy. So I stayed in my corner hovel...
The room was clean but it was impossible to work in! I had to take work back to the room and the lights were so dim I could barely see what i was doing. And ironically, the dim lights are all on dimmer switches so you can make them even dimmer if you want!
The staff was courteous and brought me another desk lamp so I could have to power of 2 ten watt LED lamps. The kitchen staff also brought me soy sauce when the sushi restaurant that I purchased delivery from forgot it. That was kind of them.
Overall, this place is great if you are in town not on business, but if that is the case you are better off staying in the SOHO/Village area!

title: “Great location”
text: Great location, with helpful staff. Only negative being the wifi charge if you exceed 2 hours per day usage.

title: “Great Place to Stay! Wonderful Staff!!”
text: I booked this hotel for a church group of 48 people visiting NYC last week. The hotel was very clean and the staff very accommodating to our needs! We worked with Daphne Moore & Anna Gaffney (Area Director of Sales & Marketing), who were very responsive to our questions and needs; they were great! The manager, Greg Riley, was also very friendly and helpful on our early morning arrival. All the staff that I came in contact with at the hotel were pleasant and seemed to enjoy their jobs( including Bryan L. and Keith K.)! The rooms were spotless and the beds/linens were asethetically pleasing, as well as very comfortable. A great find! We would definitely stay again!

title: “Worth the money!”
text: We loved this hotel! The entrance will take your breath! The dining room is one of a kind. Overall our room was very comfortable although a little tight with a rollaway. Be careful, the lady at the counter tried to charge me 50.00 a day for a rollaway but she later took this charge off. The staff overall was incredible. Especially the doorman Julio. Dont worry about a car. The public transportation is clean and dirt cheap. This hotel is seconds from everything. Myself and my family would definitely like to stay here again. The pool area is great!

title: “Great stay!”
text: There's been a few bad reviews for this place, I'm not sure why. Big rooms, very clean, quiet, right in the middle of the action in Chicago. Sure, the corridors are a bit dated, and it's a bit expensive for what it is, but then hotels in Chicago are expensive. I didn't eat or drink there because there are so many options close by. I'd say it's a great option if you can get a deal on a room!

title: “Great hotel but location not great for walkers”
text: Stayed at this hotel as part of my birthday vacation - location is not the best if you are travelling by method other than car - it's a bit of a walk to the train and especially so in the cold of December. The lobby and rooms were quite elegant - I can't believe how big the room was they gave me! Staff were for the most part okay, excellent in the business center, but had some difficulty trying to connect with a concierge, The only restuarant I saw was a sushi place - not what I'm looking for when I dine out. I don't remember internet access being free so I will say it was not. For $67 a night through Priceline, a good deal.

title: “great hotel!”
text:
