my husband and i stayed here for a long weekend over the canadian thanksgiving weekend. it was his birthday weekend, so we thought a nice getaway to the US would be nice. we usually go to vegas, so thought we would try somewhere else, and got a great deal on airfare from calgary. we booked three nights at the sheraton online on their website and got a great deal. matthew (the night manager) helped us arrange a car service to pick us up at the airport and take us back. this was great, and didnt cost us much more than a taxi would. this hotel is in a great location, a block from pier 39 and there is a safeway across the street!!
our flight got in at 8:30am, so we were at the hotel by about 9:30am, thinking we wouldnt get a room yet, but were suprised that they had one available! this was the thursday that fleet week started. so we got checked in, found our room on the 4th floor and got settled. the decor is great! the one downside, is yes, you can hear the street noise from outside, but it isn't terrible. 
the lounge downstairs has a few nice food options, but is a little pricey. on thing that was very annoying was the fire pits outside. my husband and i waited around for an hour one night trying to get one (we tried other nights too, but one night we did wait an hour) and they were always occupied by the same people every night, and they were always sitting there smoking cigarette after cigarette. we thought it would be nice and romantic to sit out there and have a drink, but the smokers always for first dibs, and sat there for hours on end. 
all in all, great hotel, amazing location and great service. would absolutely stay again

title: “Perfect Location”
text: This hotel is definitively a Kimpton. The decor is fun and it has all the trimmings of a boutique hotel. The location is fantastic. Several blocks away from the White House and across the street from the Spy Museum and the Verizon Center. Like most Kimptons this hotel is pet friendly. DC is a great town for walking around with a dog so being able to travel with your dog and stay in such a nice hotel is a real treat. The rooms can be on the small side. I opted for a step up from the standard room to have a little more space. The only negative about my stay was brunch at the hotel restaurant, Poste. It's a bit on the pricey side which I don't mind as long as the food and service are good. In this case the food was substandard and the service was lacking. There are many fabulous restaurants in DC, I would recommend avoiding Poste. Other than that, the Monaco is a great hotel and I would definitely stay there again the next time I'm in downtown DC.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: I do not really get what the complaints are about here. The staff was very nice. Rooms are clean and basic. We paid 100 a night on priceline and it was worth it, right near seattle center where you can also take the monorail to downtown. The showers had great water pressure. My only complaint would be the pillows. 2 flat pillows is not acceptable. They should either have 2 good ones or 4 pillows. We asked for 2 pillows and they were brought up to us. It was a minor thing, we would definitely stay again. We did not eat breakfast there so I cannot comment on that.

title: “Great choice for Medical Center area”
text: If you are doing business in the Medical center or there as a patient or relative with a patient, this is a great place to stay. Patient rate are available and there is a free shuttle to all the medical facilities in the area. Highly recommend.

title: “Nice place, a little pricey for families.”
text: Nice place overall. Large complex. Yes, the televisions are old, so if that is a major concern, this is not the place for you. There are a couple restaurants, and I don't think my family of 3 ate for less than $40 at any of them. (That of course does not include any alcohol) There is a $40/day resort fee, which includes internet, the Oasis Water Park, and the newspaper (?), a wonderful Fitness Center ***def not a hotel treadmill room, but rather a FULL gym***, valet service to a nearby mall and the restaurants on their property. This fee was not included in the package I booked on Allegiant - but I was aware of it from previous reviews. Would be nice if they could just include it in the package price. I spent half a day at the spa. It was nice - relatively expensive, but nice. My husband golfed at the resort and gives the course an overall rating of 8 out of 10. My daughter enjoyed the water park, as we did we all, but it was $4.92 for a fountain soda in a clear plastic cup smaller than any Red Solo. Overall, we really enjoyed ourselves and found that the resort provided us with a restful family vacation - but it came at somewhat high price. :-)

title: “We thought the property was hip, yet elegant”
text:
The room ( bedding, bath and view were excellent). The food in the Americano restaurant was wonderful. The ability to walk to the Ferry Plaza was fantastic.
We loved the property, and would highly recommend it

title: “Excellant location, staff are very helpful and kind ! Clean rooms!”
text: 1 min walk and your in times square. You couldnt ask for a better location! The staff r amazing ! They helped us plan our stay in new York and advised us on everything we needed to know as it was our first time to new York, The staff were our personal tourist guidE, if it wasn't for the staff we would have been lost in the big apple ! Clean rooms, but more importantly the service I received was a clear 10/10 !

title: “Cramped but Nice”
text: The Orchard Garden is conveniently located downtown, absolutely spoteless but without much character for the price. Our double was so small it was hard for two people to get by each other in the room. On the other hand, the beds are super, so if you are just using the hotel for sleep it's fine.We stayed in #208 facing Bush, and while the double windows kept out most street noise, the same could not be said for the interior . Could hear next door conversations, and had no "do not disturb " tag to hang on New Year's Eve. So Housekepping knocked at our door at 9AM ,as well as our neighbors, to a collective and vocal"go away" which could be heard all over the floor. So much for sleeping in on New Year's Day. Not much thought on management's part. Maybe less focus on the "Green" and a little more investment insulating their rooms from each other. All in it seems overpriced for what you get in value, unless you can get a deal--under $150

title: “Very nice hotel with employees to match”
text: The Hotel Lincoln is situated just across from Lincoln Park and has convenient access to transit. The hotel is nicely furnished, comfortable beds, nice bathrooms with updated fixtures and a retro decor very tastefully done. The employees were all very accommodating and helpful with even small things such as a recommendation for dinner or a question about a bus route. Great location for Cubs baseball fans!!

title: “Got a great rate, good location, nice sized rooms, friendly staff”
text:
Got a awesome rate here - $99 a night for a Radisson in NYC. Good location - about 4 blocks from Grand Central Station, about 5 blocks from Rockefeller Center. Away from the chaos and noise of Times Square but close enough to walk to sites and subway stops.
Room was a good size, especially for NYC, desk, flat screen, 2 drawer dresser, closet with safe and our room had 2 twin beds. Both room and bathroom were clean. 
Negative is the windows are definitely not soundproof, had asked for a high floor and unfortunately didn't get one - was told it wasn't available but could ask again the next night. We heard all the noise -trash trucks, sounds outside, etc..honking, sirens. 
Other then not having soundproof windows, I would recommend staying here - nice place and nice location

title: “A everything cost something hotel”
text:
If you are welling to spend money on every little details then this hotel is just for you.
(36$ a day for parking, 11$ for 24 hours of net, very expensive hotel restaurant). I am not saying this is not a good hotel, but at the end of the trip you feel like you could have more for the price. No fridge in room. No microwave. Very spacious rooms though and clean. The hotel is connected to the Prudential Center and to a metro station which is very convenient.

title: “Pleasently suprised”
text:
Having read some of the other reviews of this hotel , my wife & I were slightly apprehensive , but our fears were unfounded.
The hotel is in a great location , a few blocks from the Rockafeller centre & ideally placed for the subway at Grand central , it is within walking distance of Times square 5th avenue etc .
The staff were extremely plaesent & helpful particuarly the concierge's , the rooms were cleaned to an excellent standard & all staff said hello etc whenever you met them.
The hotel can be a bit noisy durung the night as the rooms are tigthly packed & the traffic is constant but I would be suprised if that wasnt the case in all areas of NYC .
We would definetly visit both the city & this hotel again & would throughly recommend it.

title: “The Funky Decor Is Awesome!”
text: We arrived late on our check in day and were quickly ushered into the hotel. The checkin took minutes and we were in our room within 15 minutes of arrival. Don't let the small "front desk" area fool you, this hotel offers great service. All calls were answered and responded to, immediately. If you need ANYTHING, ask for Richie, he is absolutely dedicated to helping you with whatever you need. (He went out to our vehicle to retrieve a pair of shoes for me)! The location is great and there are wonderful restaurants just a short walk from the hotel, and the quiet, tree lined street is great for a nice walk. This was my first stay at a Kimpton hotel, but I am looking forward to a return visit!

title: “Felt like an apartment rather than a hotel”
text:
My children and I visited DC for a long weekend and we were initally given a regular double bed room on the seventh floor. There was an odor in the room and I spoke to the front desk to inquire. The manager quickly offered to come to our room to check it out. He explained that it was due to cooking in the unit below us (he knew the occupants and they were staying temporarily from an embassy and used a spice that was strong smelling in their cooking). He offered to move us to another room. This had to have been an upgrade because we found ourselves in a much larger room with a view and a corner window on the 8th floor. It had a fold out couch which was nice since there were three of us and we could each have our own bed.
I want to compliment the manager for being so accomodating. I was not complaining but he wanted to be sure that we were completely satisifed so we were moved to this room and it made the entire experience much different for us as a result. I am not sure how many rooms are large like this particular corner room is but I would suggest to the traveler to inquire if you have three or four people in your party. It is nice to feel that you have space around you. 
What I really liked about this hotel is that it is in a residential area and has a residential feel to it. But, it is not a far walk to the Dupont Circle Metro. This was nice because I could walk out of the hotel in the evening or mornings to go for a walk and it felt as though we were living in DC and not tourists on a busy, commercial street. Residents were out and about in the evening and mornings walking their dogs, jogging and cycling. 
We chose to eat breakfast the first day in the hotel. the breakfast is certainly filling and adequate in the choices offered and the chef will make an omlette to order. So, there is nothing 'wrong' with the breakfast. However, I just thought that the breakfast room lacked ambience and I would suggest that the traveler scope out other breakfast places if they want a better atmosphere. This one was a bit 'blah'. But, if one is in a hurry and just wants to fill up on a breakfast bufffet, then the hotel breakfast is OK. 
One more thing I will mention is that every time we walked back into the hotel the folks there would say, "welcome home". They did make sure that we felt at home there and this is why I give this place a high rating.........That along with the value I think it provides. (Free parking in back of the hotel is a huge plus as other places have huge parking fees tacked on!!!) I liked the "green, eco friendly" products in the bathroom.

title: “highly recommended”
text: I can thoroughly recommend this hotel as excellent value for money. It is clean, decorated in boutique style, very relaxing, and has helpful staff. I followed the suggested of someone else who reported on this page and asked for a room on the inside courtyard, which was fine in terms of peace and quiet. It is very conveniently located for the Fisherman’s Wharf area. There is a pc carrel in the lobby and email can be accessed subject to a charge. The only possible complaint was that the sink in the bathroom had a crack in it, but it did not bother me enough to ask for a different room. All in all, however, an excellent choice, and I would stay there again. Also a ride to the airport could be arranged from the hotel, in a local transporter bus, for 15 dollars.

title: “Terrible - believe the bad reviews”
text: Stayed here in December '04. Pictures on web site looked very nice. Lobby lived up to pictures but rooms were appalling. We arrived to find they only had one room reserved for 5 adults despite having paperwork showing 2 rooms! Out of lift into hallway - terrible dirty carpets and hiddeous doors. One room had dirty towels and rubbish left by previous occupant, walls were full of holes from where picture have been hung and paper was hanging off the walls. The other room smelt of damp and smoke and the curtain was hanging from the window. We joined the huge queue of others complaining and were eventually given another room, still smoky but down as a none smoking room. Complained again and were moved a 3rd time, this room was still sub standard but we were only there 3 nights and didn't want to spend all our time in lobby with unhelpful staff complaining. Others we spoke to found bed linen dirty with hairs in, another walked into the room they were given to find someone else in bed! Everyone was complaining. Hotel APPALLING and staff UNHELPFUL - AVOID IT AT ALL COSTS!!!! It is famous for being where Glenn Millers stayed and wrote Pennsylvania 65000 - don't think it has been refurbished since he stayed there!!!!

title: “FROM NEW TO PEW!!”
text: Stayed at this hotel June 30th to July 3rd. What a difference from the early days!! I believe they are having problems with business going down? The people who stayed at this hotel were some of the biggest PIGS I have ever seen. I went down to breakfast at 6:30 am and all calm. Nice breakfast! Anyway I returned to my room and finished some work, I than returned downstairs to get a coffee refill and turned the corner only to find "THE PIGS" Their was food on the floor, no one bothered to put their trash in the garbage and it too was all over the floor!!! It looked like a herd of wild animals were being fed!!! I guess it was a holiday week and rates were low.... which in turn attracted the "animals" 10 to a room and the "free" breakfast!!! I believe it cost more to feed "THE PIGS" than they could have ever made up on the room rates. My god I seen one room with at least 8 kids and 4 teens!!!! This place was a great place to stay. A great staff and a great hotel....Now it is getting run-down and the "new" staff is rude and don't seem to care!!! What a difference!!! The rooms are dirty. Stains all over the couch, chair and bedspread!! YUCK!! MANAGEMENT TEAM TAKE A LOOK!!!

title: “Loved the Roosevelt Hotel”
text:
We booked a block at the Roosevelt hotel for our son;'s wedding the weekend of January 19th, 2008 at the Roosevelt Hotel. We also had a welcome reception at the hotel and the Bride's family booked a brunch on Sunday morning after the Saturday wedding. The reception and the rehearsal were held at the different site. The Roosevelt and their staff were just wonderful. There were a few minor gliches here and there with people not getting into their rooms fast enough etc. but all in all they could have not been more accommodating. They offered us a great rate for Manhattan and were just thrillled how the whole weekend turned out. I have no complaints. The location of the Roosevelt is just great in Manhattan, a very safe area, with lots of cute deli's and restautants close by if you don't want to do the hotel breakfast. The hotel's restaurant actually has very good food. Great lobby, and nice bar....everything you could want. It is an old hotel and some of the rooms are smaller, but they have renovated it and all of the beds are new and very comfy. I LOVED THE ROOSEVELT....go for it! 
Very pleased from Cape Cod

title: “Simple friendly hotel with a above Avg location”
text:
Recently stayed at the hotel for 5 days. I enjoyed the stay and for the price it was a value , hes sometime $300 a night is cheap in NYC. I booked thru hotels.com and had a petite room , yes it was small so so small , but doe my purposes and the price it was fine. Upon checking in I inquired about an upgrade which was avaiable the next day so all in I was paying $325 + tax (and yes plan on an additional 20% for the taxes) The second room on floor 9 was bigger and was very nice. I was given a WIFI Access code and the room was in working order and clean. 
The hotel has a nice lounge on floor 10 with a open sun deck , wifi for me was free and worked fine .... AC was fine as well ....
The hotel has no restaurant but next door is INOTECA a great wine bar .....
The location was great 20 blocks from Times SQ , 5 blocks from Union Sq and 2 blocks from Madison Sq Park. and 30 min stroll to Chinatown and Little Italy ......

title: “OK for a Couple of Nights”
text:
Good, not great, property due to age. Not pleased paying $240/night for a queen room in summer for what we got but must be market rate for downtown Baltimore. Generally clean room, but shower curtain had visible mildew and odor. 
Very friendly staff. Very well equipped exercise room overlooking a spacious pool on the roof of the 1st floor ballroom area. Within walking to the world-class Walters Art Gallery museum and the usual Baltimore tourist attractions. 
Shula's II is okay, but Tony's across the street on Park Avenue has excellent steak and crab cakes. Other good restaurants north on Charles St. including Cazbar, serving Turkish cuisine.

title: “Fantastic Location and Service”
text: Stayed here for 1 night, December 2nd. Would definitely stay here again. The staff was incredibly friendly, I was impressed by every employee I encountered. The room was great. Surprisingly big, bed was super comfortable, nice desk area, sitting area, big windows with a great view of the city. The bathroom is pretty small, but personally I'd rather have more space in the room area, so i didn't mind. It would be difficult for 2 people to get ready at the same time though. Overall a great experience!!

title: “fantastic stay”
text: When we arrived at the crown plaza in seattle we were greated with great desk clerks. They were very helpful. The room was fantastic!! Very clean with a wonderful view of the space needle. The Bed was also Fantastic I got a great night sleep! My only concern was the restaurant service was slow and the waiter was not friendly. it was a shame that on a saturday night that the restaurant was not filled with people, other than that I would definatly stay there again and would recommend this hotel to any one.

title: “Great spot for a quick trip!”
text: My husband and I stayed here to celebrate our one year anniversary. The location is right on the mark: not too close to the chaos of times square, not too far from grand central, and walkable to everything (in our opinion.) We try to walk everywhere when we visit the city, so we were looking for a mid-town location and this hotel was perfect. Although the lobby is small, the staff was extremely helpful and friendly at check-in. The hotel was even having a special promotion at the bar for buy one, get one free drinks (which we loved!) How often do you find that in the city? not to mention at a hotel bar. The bartender was very nice and accomodating. Our room was small, but that's to be expect. It was clean and had everything we needed. My husband had called ahead to tell them it was our anniversary, and they asked us what our plans were when we checked in. While we were out to dinner, they put a bottle of wine with 2 glasses and a note in our room, at NO extra charge! We were very happy with our stay and would definitely return.

title: “Our Little Apartment In Boston!”
text:
My wife, 1 year old and I stayed at the XV Beacon in a Studio room to support friends running the Boston Marathon. We paid for the more spacious Studio room because our daughter came with us on this family trip.
First of all, I found the hotel to be even more beautiful and well decorated than it looks in the candid photos or the website photos. The comments about worn furniture certainly was not true with our room or our friend's room. They are currently exchanging the old CRT tvs for wall mounted LCDs too which will make the rooms that more like your own apartment.
The location can not be beat if you ask me. The hotel is literally 250 meters from the edge of Boston Common. The service was over the top and never felt pretentious at all. The Lexus service was a nice touch too. Given the small nature of the hotel, the location and the georgous design on the rooms (looks very "old world" and modern at the same time) we felt almost like we had our own flat in the middle of Boston.
Overall, this was a fantastic hotel, and definately worth the money. We will stay here on any future trips to the Boston area for sure.

title: “I'd rather stay at the Fairmont”
text: The price of this room did not reflect the value of my stay. The rooms are much smaller than the Fairmont and the price was about the same. The hot water in the shower was not consistent and the maid service forgot to leave the breakfast room service request in my room (a big deal when you get back to your room at 9pm after a long day at work). I am not in a rush to come back here.

title: “Clean bang-for-your-buck hotel!”
text:
I stayed here as a teacher while chaperoning five high school teenagers on a school field trip. My priorities was a hotel in Baltimore that was safe, clean, and within walking distance of Inner Harbor. This hotel met all of the requirements.
Hotel features free in-room wi-fi, offers in-room safe ($5/night), choice of many TV channels, and free hot breakfast. The breakfast selection is very good: includes scrambled eggs, some sort of breakfast meat (sausage, bacon or otherwise), breakfast potatoes, toast, bagels, muffins, cereal, hot coffee and tea, juices (from concentrate), and yogurt. 
Front desk was helpful and informative. I saw the front desk assist a customer who was lost somewhere in Baltimore, and he patiently directed him via phone to the hotel! They helped us with getting to Camden Yards and taking the CCC, and various other things. 
For 40 - 80% off the price at a 4-star luxury hotel like Sheraton, Hilton, etc... this hotel offers many nice amenities that I can't imagine people complaining about this hotel! The 4-star luxury Baltimore hotel that we transferred from wanted $20 for breakfast and $13/device per day for wi-fi. So count your blessings that here, it is free!
My only complaint is that we had booked 3 rooms at the same time, and the three rooms were not only not together, they were on completely different floors! (One on the 1st floor, one on the 3rd, and one on the 4th). As a chaperone, this was VERY inconvenient. The front desk apologized and said they were fully booked so it was inevitable; but it was a real shame that if you make a reservation for multiple rooms, they were not kept together at all. (All rooms were double beds.. so I dont see why they couldn't have blocked off the rooms for us. And we checked in at a reasonable time... 4 PM in the afternoon)

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
I travel to New York about once a month for business. I don't care very much where I stay in terms of location in the city. I'm looking for a clean, safe, 4 star property. I usually try to book on priceline and the results are usually good.
This hotel is in the perfect location if you are a tourist. It is in the heart of times square. Steps away from the theater, the touristy restaurants, rockefeller center, etc. 
Check in at 5:30 p.m. was courteous and quick. My room was on the 18th floor. It was modern, clean and comfortable. There was a flat screen t.v. with movies and free hbo. 
I liked the fact that there was a guard by the elevators at all times to make sure that you were supposed to be in the hotel.
There was nothing amazing,or noteworthy about the service or hotel. However, if you are looking for a clean, safe, nice place to crash after busy New York Day, this is a good one.

title: “Renovated and great location!”
text: Stayed one night and really enjoyed it! We asked for a high floor and we were given the top (29th) floor, club level. Nice club level lounge with great view of back bay and cambridge. Service was great. I highly recommend this hotel and look forward to staying there again.

title: “Sub standard breakfast”
text:
Hotel was quite dated with a retirement home feel and smell to it. Rooms were very comfortable however, although our room looked out to the back of the hotel so was very dark. 
Breakfast consisted of a bowl of cereal and make your own toast. Not the continental breakfast it advertised. We found ourselves going out for a proper breakfast elsewhere. 
It was an average hotel in quite a central location. wifi also worked fine.

title: “Such a great stay!”
text: Our room was perfect - Larger than most hotel rooms in New York. Chairs that were actually comfortable to sit in. Pressed 100% cotton high threadcount sheets and a down duvet made the bed heaven. The most beautiful brown marble modern bath was so luxurous. The front desk help and bellmen were super helpful and nice. And the location was the best ever. Got the rate of $225 on priceline - the lowest rate on their home site was $325.

title: “Pretty cool”
text: This was a nice hotel. It was under construction when we stayed so it wasn't perfect looking. It was on the other side of the highway from the university and downtown, but we had a nice view. Parking and internet access was free so that was a plus. As you can tell in the picture with the bed, it could use some paint touch-ups, but like I said they were under construction so maybe things are being improved.

title: “Very reasonable, great service, pleasant stay”
text:
Keeping in mind that this is a budget-rate motel, you can't expect luxury accommodations. But the staff were very pleasant and helpful, there was always plenty of hot water, and the toilet flushed like it would suck you right in if you stood too close! The complimentary breakfast was satisfactory, where you could make your own delicious waffles shaped like the State of Texas, and enjoy apple and orange juices, fresh-brewed coffee, donuts and muffins, and cold cereal and milk. But the selection of fresh fruit only included a bowl of apples (I personally would have liked to have a banana with my breakfast). "Gary" at the front desk was most helpful with everything from directions to the Air Force Base and local attractions, to providing a box and tape for shipping items home to avoid paying the extra baggage rates at the airport. He remembered to follow up on our inquiries (asked the next day if we needed directions to the nearest P.O.) and saw to our every need with polite, genuine hospitality. We stayed 5 nights, and the price we were charged at check out was exactly what we were quoted when we checked in -- no surprises or added fees. The pool is smaller than it looks in the pictures, but I only got to use it once anyway because we were running around sightseeing and spending time with my son who had just graduated basic training at Lackland AFB. The guest laundry room was a nice bonus, so we could do a load of laundry before packing up to leave (washer and dryer each cost $1, and laundry detergent and dryer sheets were available at the front desk for $1 each). The rooms were nothing fancy -- typical cheap motel -- but clean and changed daily as needed (we re-used some towels, etc., to be "green"). The cable TV worked fine, there's was a 'fridge and microwave in the room, and I had no problems whatsoever with the free wifi, so we were happy.
If you're looking for luxury with no quirky details (like a door that didn't always close securely without monkeying with the lock!), then look for a higher-priced place. But if you just want a place to crash and stash your stuff while out running around, that's convenient to Lackland Air Force Base, for a great price and staff that is pleasant to deal with, book it! I would definitely return here again.

title: “great hotel, great location... you wont be disappointed!!!”
text:
Wen't to Phoenix from Canada to see Doctors at the Arazona Heart Institute.
Had to rely on internet research to find a hotel and was very pleased with our choice. The people there were great and very very helpful. They even sent the shuttle bus back to the hospital at 9:30 at night to pick us up and bring us back to the hotel after a late release from the hospital. Everything was great and just as advertised. We would certainly stay again and have no problem recommending this hotel to anyone visiting Phoenix.

title: “Stay down the street”
text:
Room was clean and bathroom very nice but service is spotty. Housekeeping and bar people rude 
& not up to par on dealing with hotel guests. No where to sit once the bar gets busy (6:00)
It took asking to see the manager of restaurant & bar to be able to have a 20 minute drink in the restaurant with guests. Overall The Mark needs to work on better customer service.

title: “Pretty standard stuff....”
text:
I've stayed here a couple of times for business. The hotel is easy to get to and is convenient for the freeway. There are a reasonable number of bars and restaurants in the area so plenty of choices for eating out. The hotel restaurant has a limited menu but the food is OK if you choose to eat in. The hotel facilities are fine - comfortable and clean. The restaurant and bar staff are great, the front desk staff are pleasant but don't really go the extra mile.
Management really should consider putting in guest laundry facilities and I'm not sure about the captive swans... it seems a shame to have 2 swans cooped up in a little indoor pool.
I would stay here again if in the area.

title: “Perfect location and nice hotel”
text: The hotel is beautiful, and of course the lobby is wonderful. The rooms are good, clean, and service great. Most of all the location is perfect to see the sights of Chicago. Easy access to public transit. Loved it all. Chicago is beautiful.

title: “Not what I expected...”
text: My wife and I, along with my mother in law, had planned to stay at the hotel for 4 nights during our recent visit to San Francisco but shortly after arrival decided to leave the next morning. For several weeks prior to our visit I had followed the reviews here on TA and due to the glowing reviews perhaps my expectations were a bit unrealistic. First of all the place isn't at all impressive from outside looking more like a parking garage than a hotel. But in all fairness most reviews noted this but what wasn't noted was the unimpressive decor on the inside. The concrete balconies surrounding the inner courtyard are plain and cold...it reminded me of an Alcatraz cell block. The room itself is indeed spacious but it feels "sterile". The carpets are a very strange pattern of dark "dashes" which, to us, wasn't easy on the eyes. I had requested a room with a view, but when I opened the blinds I was shocked to find myself staring at a bare wall only a few feet away. There is somewhat of a veiw from the rooftop, but again the furnishings there are cold and uninviting. Perhaps a family with children might appreciate the kitchen rendering the ability to prepare meals in-house, but don't book this hotel expecting any charm or elegance. It has a bare bones apartment like feel...adequate but nothing special. I will say the staff was very gracious and friendly not holding us to the 72 hr. cancellation policy.

title: “Smack in the middle of NYC”
text:
Top location, right next to Grand Central station, right in the middle of Manhattan! Beautiful designed and very large lobby. Stayed in a king exec room. The room itself was very spacious, the bathroom was actually very, very small. Could hardly move in it. 
I suppose for a huge hotel like this, it is very hard to keep service personal with so many guests. Because I felt more like a number, like one of the many. 
Hyatt rates this hotel as a category 6 hotel (in a rating from 1 to 6). Now I have seen Hyatts in Europe that are rated 3 or 4, but that have a way more elegant an luxury feel over them as this one has. So based on what, they rate Grand Hyatt NY as a top tier hotel, I don't know. 
Nevertheless, our stay was nice, we felt very comfortable, and enjoyed being in NYC on such a top location very much, and would recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Perfect Location for Sightseeing”
text: Just returned back from a 3 night stay at the Liasion Capitol Hill. My husband and I were absolutely thrilled with the location and it is a perfect base for sightseeing. Just a five minute walk from Union Train Station and Capitol Hill (which is absolutely stunning) and also, the main tour buses stop right outside :-) A ten minute walk from 7th street which has approximately 40 restaurants and cafes (we can definately recommend the Brewery and Chophouse if you fancy a great steak). The hotel is not the prettiest from the outside, but inside is a different story. The bedrooms are a great size and have huge, comfortable beds which you need after a hard days sightseeing! The shuttle service from Dulles Airport (shared van) cost $42 per couple each way, but a taxi could cost you around $75! We prebooked the shuttle for the return journey ($42 again) and they turned up on time. We definately recommend this hotel and would definately return. Thank you Liasion for a great stay.

title: “A Great Play to Stay”
text: Our stay at the Loyal Inn was part of a package deal from Hawaiian Airlines. While we were a bit skeptical about the location and star rating, we were pleasantly surprised by the facility! The staff were wonderful, rooms/lobby/spa were exceptionally clean, the location was out of the "touristy area" so we had no problem with traffic, AND there was a great restaurant (SHILLA) across the street!

title: “Majestic architecture, unsupported by Ritz experience”
text:
We stayed to celebrate two birthdays. We traveled from NY & DC. You are greeted with a large, imosing space. The bar area is in the center of the ground floor and the Eric Ripert restaurant is located off to the side. I travel a bit and love Phillie. The history and architecture remain a draw for me. The Ritz is a real cornerstone to the luxury scen there. I didn't feel the same allure to this property. Our room was on the 28th floor and it was small. The furniture was ratty and it didn't feel like a 4 star room at all. The linens and bedding were dated. 
We went to their mini spa. Nice space and well maintained. I found the staff sort of rough there. The masseuse did his best wasn't at the level that worked for me. 
We dined on site. Very quiet in the dining area but the 80s music and bae scene spilled over. Inconsistent experiences. The bar was filled with aging gents drinking a lot. Not the acen I would have expected. 
Check out was fine. Aside from the bellman mispacing the luggage and agruing with us about its location. The front door staff were friendly and attentive. I would give this a miss. Not a super Ritz property. Underwhelming. 
Do use the gym. It is tucked away but nice equipment

title: “Great location, average stay!”
text: We loved the location, very central, and easy to access many of Seattle's best sites! Rooms are average. Would have appreciated one more bar of soap so we did not have to keep swapping the soap between the sink and bath. Two wine glasses in the room, given there is wine in the bar, would be great and at least four water glasses..two int he washroom and tow in the main room would have been better. Coffee was replaced after having room coffee BUT no stir sticks the second night. My pen is not the best stir stick....ugh! Parking fees per nigh @ 38.00 is outrageous.

title: “Beautiful Room, Odd layout”
text: Beautiful room, comfortable and stylish. I loved the bathroom layout with access to the hall closet via sliding doors and of course I was pleased with the in- room Nespresso machine(my favorite at home) ! Was disappointed in having to leave our building to enter another to get to the fitness room, especially since it was freezing cold outside, and we also found it confusing because the ground level to the other building looked like a museum or other facility and there were no signs to indicate where you were going.

title: “Tiny Cell - Awful Airconditioner”
text:
The room was so small that our suitcase could not open up if placed anywhere on the floor. The a/c unit in the window, located next to the head of the bed, was old and loud. If we turned it "on" we could not sleep because of the noise. It did not have an intermediate switch to make it less noisy. If we kept it "off" then we would suffocate in the room and could hear all the noise from the street. The pillows were filled with somekind of plastic substance that made it impossible to sleep on them. Nowhere on the hotel website do they advise you of the room sizes. The description is deceptive and only refers to the ceiling height..
The only good thing about this hotel was the location. We were extremely disappointed and feel we were misled by the hotel and its webpage.

title: “Nice place, great location”
text: As said in other reviews, this place is in a great location. Just one block off Union Square. I was there with a conference but used to live in San Francisco, so I had mixed feelings. The other meeting participants LOVED the location and enjoyed the shoping and all the rest there is to do there. However, in a few blocks, you are really in the heart of the tenderloin, so it's necessary to be a little cautious and be aware of your surroundings. The hotel itself was nice. I stayed in the "club" rooms. A bit priceier but much bigger than the other rooms. A few other people in the group did not stay in this suite of rooms and complained about the small rooms. I haven't stayed in Union Square before, so I thought this was a nice place with a good meeting room.

title: “Batty Over The Hyatt Regency/Austin”
text:
The Hyatt Regency is classy enough in any city, but in Austin you have the added thrill of it being right next to the Congress Street Bridge--home to the largest bat colony in America. At dusk, thousands of bats emerge from the bridge struts and fly out over the river. Quite a site!
The hotel boasts the most comfortable hotel bed I've slept in this year. Plus their bar is awesome, they have sushi chefs just off the lobby who, if you challenge them to be creative, will prepare some of the yummiest sushi rolls around, and live music too. 
And did I mention they're in walking distance of the infamous Sixth Street and famous Threadgills? Well they are. Plus I could see the Aussie's outdoor volleyball courts from my window.

title: “Nice hotel for weekend stay”
text: This is a very nice, VERY well maintained hotel. My husband and I were there over the weekend and it was very quite. I guess they do most of their business during the week. We almost felt like we had the place to ourselves. We had a suite and paid less than you would expect to pay for a regular room. (Don't know if this is because weekends are slower.) Our suite was spacious and well maintained. In fact the entire property was clean and updated. Service was excellent! Although restaurants and shops are not within walking distance, there are dozens of restaurants a mile away. There is also a restaurant/bar in the hotel lobby. It has convenient access to I-35, and you can be downtown in about 15 minutes. We plan to use this hotel again for several upcoming trips to Dallas.

title: “Think twice about staying here - Multiple thefts have occured”
text:
I attended a NSM in Jan, where we had over 100+ employees staying for four days, all meals included, with snack and beverage service. The food was nothing extraordinary, and the service was fair.
My second day at the conference my BMW was stolen out of the parking lot sometime before 7:30 p.m. Valet and Security were less than helpful as was the Front Desk Manager. All they did was call the non-emergency police so I could make a report. They never offered to take me home (I'm a local resident) and when asked if I could use their car service (they have two Lincoln Town cars) they informed me they only drive within a 5 mile radius of the hotel and could not make an exception to take me to Carlsbad, when asked if they could pick up the tab for the taxi, they declined, and offered me a drink ticket for the bar. The front desk manager apologize and also informed me a few months back they had a flat screen TV stolen out of their room and a security guard assaulted. Word got out quickly that my vehicle was stolen and needless to say, the local employees were on edge and checking on their cars throughout the day, not a good way to spend your time at a National Sales Meeting.
For the amount of money they charge, their customer service is terrible and their security isn't any better. All in all a very poor experience and my company will not be going back, nor will the employees.

title: “Pay a little more and stay some where else.”
text:
Many of the reviews about this hotel rave about its location. Well the location aint great. The Hotel is situated around about 105th street. So thats atleast a 1 hour walk from Times Sq (60 blocks away). The subway station might not be far, but there are no bars/restaurants around this hotel, so you will spend every morning and every evening on the metro.
That said, when i got to this hotel, i did not even stay here.
I booked a twin room (travelling with my father) and on arrival was given a small double room. The bed was not even a double bed. The woman at reception had the cheek to send us up to the room, knowing it was not a twin room. The room was dark, and looked pretty unclean. My father did say the bathroom was ok, but i never looked at it. I was straight down to complain. I showed the woman on reception my printed hotel booking showing i had paid for a twin room, capable of sleeping up to 4 people. Did she care? No. She said, on our booking form it shows a double room. Great customer relations. I asked if they could move us into a twin. She said they were fully booked.
So i was forced to move to a different hotel, and i did not get a refund. I am claiming for a refund through my credit card.
Many have mentioned this is a budget hotel. Well it's not that cheap. We moved to a hotel opposite madisson Sq garden on 34th street, right in the middle of the action. Yes we had to pay around £125 more for 4 nights, but it was worth it. 
Just because this is NY dont think, this hotel is good value. The hotel is in a bad location. Its only close to the park. You will have to get on the subway morning and night, and the room i got looked awful. There are plenty of cheaper and better located hotels in NY.
Dont be fooled by these positive reviews. This hotel is rubbish. I was fooled by these reviews, "great location". I guess these people have never been to NY before, or simply dont know much about big cities. The location sucked. The hotel sucked. The girl on reception sucked.

title: “The company operating this hotel is a rip-off,stay away !!”
text: The company operating this hotel is a rip-off stay away they are liars !!! I had a an online reservation at this hotel for the Deluxe Double Double bedroom (3 nights) when I went in and talked to receptionist he made me wait for a while to check then he said you have reservation for single bed bedroom right? I said no it it is the Deluxe Double Double, then he said let me see and after a while he said the room was given to another person, and he start calling other hotels managed by the same company, he send us to another hotel claiming it is a sister hotel, and I asked if it has the same service he said yeah it is the same, I didn't rejected because I was very tired after a busy week and the difficulty finding a parking spot in that area. The other hotel ( district hotel) was not the same, it was far less grade than windsor. Apparently, these people don't know what reservation is, they only know how to take reservation and rip-off people. I sent a complaint email to the management and they didn't bother even to replay.

title: “Awesome hotel!”
text: The hotel was great! As soon as we walked in all we coud say was "WOW!" The inside is beautifuly decorated and the elevators were fast! Our room was great! We had huge marble batherooms and all the little things (lighted makeup mirrors, starbucks in the room, comfortable beds) really added up to make for a pleasant stay. The service was nice and so were the resteraunts. Oh and if possible reserve a room with a veiw to the riverwalk! It's amazing! The only bad things were the hotel rooms have bad insulation or something because we could hear the next door neighbors talking. You have to pay for valet parking and other wise you have to walk a bit.The other downside for up was that the pool was outdoors and not heated and it was to cold to swim! But other than that it was great!

title: “Coolest Shower Ever”
text: Stayed in DC for a conference and chose this hotel rather than the conference site . . . what a great move! The room was perfectly comfortable for one or two, super comfy bed and plenty of closet and drawer space for clothes. Really nice soaps and toiletries, and a hair dryer that actually WORKED! Amazing! The best feature, however, was the walk-in shower that physically stood in the middle of the room inside an opaque cylindrical structure. Totally fun. My only complaint is that the robes and towels smelled very faintly of hospital antiseptic - never had that happen before. And when I ordered room service, they neglected to inform me of the size of the portions, which ended up in me way over-ordering. Nevertheless, it's a great location and I would return again for sure!

title: “Pure luxury and professionalsim”
text: We lucked out on Priceline to get 2 nights for $55 each night. However, that did not include internet. The pool is nice and large (to 4' depth), the service prompt and very courteous, and we had a huge room with a great view and very comfortable bed.

title: “Comfy, easy to like”
text: I really like New Yorker Hotel, being there couple of times and going again. Hotel is perfectly located regarding to shops, metrolines, attractions, restaurants etc. Hotel lobby is giving the international atmosphere in an American style and personnel has always been really nice. Room size can vary a lot, I guess depending where you are booking from. Last time the size was nice and we had a great view to Empire State building. Hotel has a Tick Tock diner where one can have nice breakfast in a traditional American way: eggs in many forms, milkshakes, burgers, pancakes. Diner is busy many times, so be prepared to wait a bit, especially in the morning. (But also, diner is open 24/7, if I remember right...) All in all, very good hotel and definitely worth to visit!

title: “Trains and trolleys are noisy….”
text:
I stayed at the San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina for four (4) nights on business in mid-May 2012. The room with a king-sized bed was better than many (most) Marriott properties. The desk service, concierge, and housekeeping was truly exemplary. The property itself is beautiful, but maybe not if you don’t like twenty-five (25) or so floors. I used the workout room and it too was very, very nice. The pool area looked small, but sufficient and pretty.
The area is great. Great for restaurants, shopping, and my personal favorite – walking to a baseball game. The hotel is probably 3 blocks from Petco Park and entirely safe. Between the park and the hotel is the Gaslamp area which has restaurants and bars galore. 
In short, the hotel is ideal for seeing downtown San Diego.
The biggest downside, and I guess its pretty commonly known, are the all night trains which cross to the land side of the two towers. They are enough sometimes to wake anybody. Several of my party were on the water side of the hotel and reported not hearing any train noise at all. So…. If you have the option, take the sea side (west) for the view and the quiet.

title: “Great location”
text:
We have stayed at this Courtyard twice on our regular weekenders into Chicago. 
This is a brand-new property gleaming with a hip Northside vibe. Deep house fills the air in the lobby, which is adorned with sleek, mod furniture. The staff echoes this vibe and is very knowledgable about the many attractions, restaurants, bars and nightclubs in the surrounding blocks. 
The rooms are actually pretty large for a downtown property, and there's a great bar in the lobby that serves all types of mod martinis and cocktails. 
Beware that overnight parking is $30 in a neighboring garage (my only complaint, however you know that the hotel cannot help this).

title: “Magnolia: classy and very reasonably priced.”
text: I stayed at the Magnolia for two nights in Houston for a business meeting. The hotel was very attractive and the price was great. Rooms were large and comfortably appointed. I would definitely return. I forgot toothpaste, and I was ever so slightly disappointed that I had to return to the front desk to pick up a free tube; however, given the price we paid, I happily accept this compromise in the level of service.

title: “Our new favorite hotel in NYC”
text:
This hotel provides a good value for midtown manhattan. It's just a few blocks from Rockefeller Center and Times Square, close to a Metro station, a few blocks from Bryant Square Park and the Theatre District.
The check in was quick and easy, the hotel staff was helpful and kind. We had a room on the 11th floor, while the lift was a bit slow, the lack of street noise was a plus. 
Free breakfast consisted of apples, bananas, yogurt, oatmeal packets, bagels, toast, donuts and 3 kinds of cereal. Nothing special, but it was healthy and it was one less meal to buy!
My only complaint was with the free wifi. It worked about 30% of the time. There are two computers in the lobby, but mostly they were occupied by teenagers playing online games. I'd like to see the hotel add a few more wireless hubs to keep users connected. 
However, we'll be back on our next trip!

title: “Good location and price but too much street noise”
text:
My company booked this room for a trade show at Moscone Center. The location was good, very central to restaurants, BART and the convention center but the street noise made it miserable for sleeping. My room faced an Irish pub across the street, people were yelling, trash cans full of bottles being dumped in the dumpster after closing time all in the wee hours. The homeless situation around here is also quite alarming, they were performing in the street for money, playing drums (on 5 gal pails) and one guy was even blowing a trumpet until 2 am. The police didn't seem to bother them either. 
The hotel itself is ok for what we paid ~$160 I believe, my bathtub was in tough shape, needed a re-caulk. Also found a ponytail elastic on the back of the door with hair stuck in it. Kinda gross, poor attention to housekeeping detail. The free wireless internet was so slow I could not bear it. I would not stay here again if I could help it.

title: “NOT a Best Inn!”
text:
PRO'S:
-locations (very close to lombard street, a few bus stop - or a 20 mins walk - from the piers, it seems a safe area)
-price
-wifi
CONS:
- cleaness
- furnitures
- enviroment
-breakfast (coffee or tea and a poor crossait to be picked up in the reception because there isnt a table...however there is a pair of diner's just outside)

title: “By far THE WORST hotel stay ever!!!”
text:
Our hesitation about this hotel started hours before our stay when we called to verify our reservation and was sent to an answering service...not directly to the hotel. We arrived for the 4th of July festivities and to enjoy the historic sites of Philadelphia. 
Next, the two main elevators were NOT working, no one at the front desk informed us of this. A hotel guest saw us standing in front of the elevators and told us to take the service elevator to our floor.
The first room 708 looked great until I entered the bathroom and saw HAIR in the bathtub along with visible DIRT! I went to turn on a lamp and the light bulb was leaning to the side with the cord exposed...obviously not safe! I immediately sent my husband downstairs to the front desk to get us a different - CLEAN room.
He comes back with keycards to room 718, I take them and go to inspect the room. There was ANOTHER broken lamp and the bathtub was FILTHY! The dirt in the tub was clearly visible to the naked eye, disgusting.
I go down to the front desk to tell the employee (Goldie) that we have seen two rooms so far with filthy bathtubs. I asked her for another room and tell her that she can go look at 708 and 718 if she wants proof, she tells me that the rooms "are marked as clean so I don't know what you're talking about." 
She gives me the key to room 610. I go to the sixth floor only to find a bag of trash right in front of the service elevator, dirty sheets and towels lying in front of the ice machine and a room service tray with breakfast food on it that appeared to be several hours old. This is around 9pm at night. I enter the room only to find the same as the last three rooms but this one didn't have broken lamps.
I return to the front desk only to be greeted with a bad attitude by Goldie who asked "what are you going to do....stay or what????". She offered to have a different employee, Terence, show me TWO MORE rooms.
He shows me room 807 which was SO bad, I had to point out the obvious dirt in the tub. I said, "do you see all of that dirt?" He says, "oh you mean right around the mat...do you want this room?" I decline and he takes me to room 810 which was by far the cleanest of all. We stayed because we were traveling with a 4 year old, it was almost 11pm by this time and room rates were sky high due to the holiday. We missed the fireworks, dinner and any fun we thought we'd have because of the horrible conditions of this hotel.

title: “Everything is the best except prices”
text: This hotel is real 5 starts. i recommened to stay if money is not your problem

author.location: New York, New York, United States

title: “Decent but Rather Not”
text: Decent if you need to do business directly in the J-town area of downtown LA but really nothing special; average 2 to 3 star hotel at the very MOST and that's being too generous for these drab, dated rooms and I honestly feel like some Holiday Inn's are actually more comfortable. Service is icey cold; we prepaid for executive kings but they gave them away by the time we checked in (at around 7pm so it wasn't that late) and didn't blink an eye when putting us in a room with double beds; no apologies from the staff or even an offer to any of us for a discount or comfort amenities - apparently it was our problem or so it was meant for us to feel that way. Overall not a pleasant stay and would recommend staying elsewhere if you can!

title: “Just about acceptable”
text:
Check in was not particularly good, desk clerk was disinterested. First room I was given was not dirty and had not been cleaned, I returned to the desk and was allocated another room. This room was fine. Hotel is pretty basic, no on site facilities, and not a particularly interesting location, but convenient for the airport. For the price paid, I do not consider it was particularly good value, but for some reason, Philly is very expensive.
Clerk who checked me out was friendly and helpful.

title: “Wonderful Staff!”
text: The staff here is wonderful. I lost my cell phone outside of the hotel and a hotel employee, Manav, found the phone, went out of his way to find the owner (me) and get the phone back in my hands! Going out of his way to help me is typical of the Standard staff and I highly recommend this property.

title: “Wonderful”
text: The location is absolutely perfect - easy access to the garage, a ton of restaurants, clubs, and directly across from the Academy of Music and Merriam Theater. The room was very clean, and the staff were a pleasure.

title: “Would not recommend this hotel.”
text:
I Would not recommend this hotel.
Hotel is next to train tracks. Poorly managed.
Hallways stink. Carpet is stained. Drab....

title: “What a gem!”
text:
We had read such good things about this hotel on Trip Advisor, and we were not disappointed. We got a corner room on the top floor, and it was GREAT! The room was huge, spotlessly clean, very comfortable bed. Great view of the city. We were totally happy with the Nob Hill Motor Inn. Frank & Judy were so nice, and very helpful with directions, restaurants, and suggestions to make our first trip to the city more enjoyable. And you cannot beat the price in San Francisco.
We loved our stay, and will definitely be back.

title: “Very nice!”
text: We had a two bedroom/ two bath suite and a one bedroom suite. Both were spacious, quiet, well-equiped and clean. The hotel is close to the airport but far enough away that you cannot hear the air traffic. The fitness center has new equipment and the pool and whirlpool are spacious and clean. We would definately stay there again.

title: “Hawthorne Suites”
text: I found Hawthorne Suites on the internet and booked our rooms. I was a little skeptical, but when we arrived, we were pleasantly surprised. I asked for a room with a king size bed and we got a SUITE with a king size bed and a kitchenette. Normally, I would not consider a kitchenette, but it was a welcome surprise. The kitchenette had a full size fridge, microwave, dishwasher (yeah!!) and 2 burner range. It really helped us defray the cost of our meals!!! Also the staff was wonderful. Ms. Anna Tran (who works nights and weekends) was a wonderfully helpful young lady!!! Also the Hawthorne has a full breakfast buffet every day (scrambled eggs, cereal, toast, fruit, homefries and sausage, as well as coffee and juice). Monday through Thursday there is a complimentary happy hour type buffett (one night it was pasta, another night a baked potatoe bar). It was enough for a light dinner. all in all a great experience at this hotel and I recommend this...

title: “Cheated”
text: After prepaying for three nights we arrived to be told our rooms were not available. Instead the staff informed us to go to another hotel on the other side of town for the night where they had booked us a room. The staff considered it to be perfectly 'ok' and in their right to send us to the other hotel and were surprised when we complained. No refund was offered. Our rooms in the other hotel were filthy and noisy. Legally I am sure that Hilton have buried the ability to sell rooms but not provide them in their contract but I feel this activity should be not allowed. Please do not go to this hotel, you will not be guaranteed a bed.

title: “Great find!”
text: This was a great alternative to all the other big name hotels in the Square district. It's tiny (but quaint) lobby is a bit disconcerting at first.... but our room (an exectutive King w/ fireplace) was quiet large and comfortable. I can't comment on the standard room. But for the rate we paid (129$pn) Go for the biggest room you can get. You'll be paying 250+ to stay at the Westin across the street. I was really pleased w/ the little extras. They had a very nice continental breakfast and evening wine & snacks in the common areas of each floor everyday. The fireplace was usually burning which was nice since San Fran can be a bit chilly. The location was perfect. Had no problem walking around the city, catching a cab or taking a trolly. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “NY atmosphere just from the beginning”
text:
I stayed here for one whole week at March.
Great location near Rockefeller center and Times Square. A cool and petite hotel (also with small rooms) that keeps you safe from the traditional depressing accommodations of the big apple.
I can only complain about the non-existing restaurant, specially because weather was still cold, and sometimes there is nothing better than a soap or a hot chocolate before going to your room.
Anyway I totally recommend it!

title: “Brilliant hotel, what more do you need?”
text:
We stayed here for a week at the beginning of December.. It is located a few blocks off times square, nearest subway is he port authority- but its just as easy to walk to times square rather than taking shuttle over to it. 
Free breakfast was great for saving time and money each morning.. included: waffle maker, toast, bagels, buns, croissants, pastries, yoghurt, fruit, cereal, fruit juice, tea, coffee, bacon, eggs.. what else do you need?/ Plenty of cream cheese, butters, jams and maple syrup. staff always refilling everything! Didn't mind if you took it up to your room.. could be busy in the morning but we always got a seat.. 
free internet, computer and printer which was handy for checking in online
One lift in hall way- very slow but not a fault really of the staff... 
rooms cleaned very well, new soaps etc always stocked up
I would def stay here again if I got the same price, we paid £85 a night for the room.
On check out we got freshly made cookies each which were yummy as we waited on our taxi.

title: “Cafe Nicole @ Hotel Novotel”
text: Great food. Went there before seeing Jersey Boys on Broadway. Totally different than what I was expecting. We had heirloom tomato salad, crab cake, wild salmon appetizer with capers, onion and toast points with a cream cheese herb spread, and the seafood risotto. Every single thing was just delicious! Service was excellent, the waiter even took the salad off the bill because he saw that a little gnat had been buzzing by and landed on the dish. Can't wait to go back again:)

title: “Great Hotel ! Excellent Services !”
text: I am a business man from Miami, FL. I am in the Oil and Gas Industry and this hotel located in the heart of the Oil and Gas Corridor - Westchase Area. The hotel restaurant was great. Front desk was friendly and helpfull.

title: “Very good hotel for the price..clean, quiet, centrally located. Would reccommend!”
text: We were very glad to find a nice pet friendly hotel. We were able to bring our pit bull in without paying an additional fee. All together the room cost $75.00. The staff was very friendly and helpful, they let us look at two rooms when we got there and let us pick which one we wanted. The first room was right next to something for the pool that was really loud so we ended up taking the next room which was nice and quiet. It was clean and the bed was comfortable. You can order room service from a nearby restaurant and the food was very good but overpriced. I will definately stay there again when I go to Phoenix. If you have pets that you travel with this is a great place to go because they keep it clean and it is near a really nice park with hiking trails too.

title: “Amazing hotel”
text: I have to say I really loved this hotel, from the minute I arrived I felt totally relaxed. The staff at the reception were really nice and i was very impressed with the room. The bathroom especially was really really nice, seperate large bath and shower. On our last day when we were storing our luggage the guy at the front door offered to have a car there for us on when we got back to bring us to the airport. We were well impressed when the car turned out to be a limo at no extra charge. Location is spot on, 5 minute walk from everything you wanna see. Would definite recommend, myself and my boyfriend loved it.

title: “Great location”
text: My boyfriend and I have stayed at the Empire on two separate occasions. On both stays we have had good experiences. The rooms are fairly small (what rooms aren't in NYC) but nicely decorated. The bathroom is also very small and the open shower is a little incovenient. On our second stay with Empire we got stuck in a bad room, but they were very accommodating and moved us to a higher and larger room overlooking Lincoln Center. The rooftop bar is excellent and the lobby bar is great as well! The location of the Empire can't be beat. We will be back!

title: “The best experience”
text: We have our Fraternal Order of Eagles State convention there every year, Every year is better than the last. The newly remodeled entry & bar area are beautiful. We were greeted by none other than the famous Henry, the bell captian, He makes the trip so enjoyable. He smiles & greets you each and everytime he sees you. He erally pays extra attention when he is handling your belongins or just walking you to the courtyard. The manager was friendly too upon arrival. The only bad experience was on checking out a small in stature man check me out & didn't smie or make eye contact. That was overlooked as we pulled out to see Henry waving bye to us.

title: “friendly staff and great location”
text:
I usually stay at the Doubletree when I go to NY on business. It has a great location (lex and 51st), right next to the subway and walking distance from many restaurants and shops.
The rooms are fairly small but ok for NY's standards. The bathroom is quite small too but was very clean. the toiletries were very nice too. the room has cable internet (and you can get free WiFi in the lobby too). Decent size desk and big flat screen TV (my only recommendation there would be to also add non US channels... having BBC would be nice to have access to real international news).
Staff is super friendly and very efficient (checking in and out took no more than a couple of minutes each). 
It has a bar downstairs where you can also get some snacks but since it is so close to many nice restaurants I only went there once (and the food was nice).
Overall, it is not a five star hotel but its is quite good for NY and I would recommend staying at the Doubletree.

title: “Nice hotel, clean rooms.”
text:
Our family of 4 stayed at the Doubletree for 2 nights towards the end of June 2004. The front desk staff was a bit cool and detached. Not friendly, along with the bellhops. The room on the 26th floor or so was very clean, nicely furnished, large and clean bathroom. Wonderful view. Used the swimming pool, small but adequate. Hotel in a great location for walking to sites, across the street from some tourist bus services (pick-up/drop-off points). The buffet breakfast was good. The sit-down breakfast service (either menu order or buffet) was excellent. Our waitress was the nicest member of the hotel service staff that we encountered. Hotel was also right next to a parking garage which made it easy to self-park our van for the entire stay. Hotel bar food was expensive, but a good hold-over for our daughters till supper.
Be sure to visit the Marathon Grill a 2 block walk north. Very good food. The best smoothies ever.

title: “Renovations are out of this World!!!”
text: This is my fourth time staying at the Renaissance and it only gets better and better. The staff is great and always great you through out the hotel. They are always asking if they can help in anyway. The restaurant and bar is excellent and has an extensive beer and wine list. I would highly recommend this hotel for any traveler!

title: “Comfortable Beds”
text: The beds were so comfortable my 87 year old Mom did not want to leave them. We got a good deal on Priceline and the staff was so nice they got my husband and I a connecting room so we could look out for my Mom. It was walking distance to the Inner Harbor. The coffee and breakfast was not great so eat elsewhere if you can.

title: “good hotel for the price”
text: Visited Washington October 22-25th, 2004 with 2 teenagers and 2 adults. Hotel was in really nice area, Foggy Bottom, across from the Ritz and within walking distance to Georgetown . Metro not too far, a few blocks, seems further after a day of sightseeing. Hotel staff was okay, same as any other hotel in Washington, some staff helpful, some not. Nice hotel, nice room. The entire hotel appeared clean and renovated, not an older hotel as I expected. The only problem were the beds, they were so small. Could not fit two people in each bed. Much smaller than any chain hotel. Would suggest 1 king bed for 2 people or 2 beds, one for each person else you will not get any sleep! The lack of sleep did not make for an enjoyable weekend and I usually have no problem sleeping in hotel rooms. We found a low rate through AAA. Except for the beds, great hotel for the price. We also enjoyed the fact that we were not woke up by a rattling cart or a knock on the door early in the morning in order for our room to be cleaned. Actually got a phone call later in the day asking if we wanted any service.

title: “The Westin LAX always makes me feel at home.”
text:
I call the Westin LAX my home away from home. The staff from the front door to the back office are always extrodinary. I always know that they will do whatever it takes to help me with an event, luggage, faxing, you name it.
Daniela Hiles is exceptional to work with. I see her everywhere helping everyone and she is always the first to respond with a smile to any request.
Thank you Westin for creating such an amazing team at the LAX property!
Gail Kingsbury

title: “Charming hotel”
text: Rex Hotel is in a good location, the staff is nice and the room was quite and big enough for us with our 4 suitcases.The bar/ restaurant is pleasant and we had a glass of wine every night for free. The price is fair.

title: “You get what you pay for!”
text:
I got this hotel room on sale. For the price I paid, I guess I got what I paid for. It is old and outdated. The internet service keeps cutting out and cannot seem to support 2 computers in one room. My door isn't quite aligned, so I had to pull it in a bit to get the deadbolt to work. I think it's an "average" room for 2 stars. However, it's listed online as a 3 star hotel. I also do not agree that it is a "Plus" level when you read Best Western's description of their 3 levels. Honestly, it's ok if you aren't expecting a 3 star. When you think you are getting a 3-star, "Plus" hotel room, you probably won't be happy with it. 
This is actually my second room tonight. In the first room, the internet, TV, fridge, and microwave didn't work. The TV, fridge, and microwave are all in a wall unit. The front desk guy said they could either send someone in to fix the power and then I could call their help desk techs or he could move me to another room. I opted for a different room. Everything worked in the other room. 
I would stay here again if I needed to, but I would rather select a different location that better matches the star level and description.

title: “an evening to remember”
text:
We recently spent an unforgettable evening, on the night of the "River Lighting", in the beautiful La Babia room. The menu, the food, service and demeanor of the staff, was excellent. I had not been to the Westin Riverwalk for a number of years, (approx 10) and was delighted to find the same 5 star attention to details.Thank you! thank you, Sara O'Donnal, catering Sales, Mgr., Jackie Garcia, Assist., and Arturo Santa Cruz, director of banquets.You did a superb job. I have travelled, far and wide, to functions large, and small, and I can tell you, without hesitation, that your service, food etc., ranks amoungst the best. I look forward to returning, on my next visit to San Antonio, 
sincerely, Cynthia Gamboa

title: “Great NYC hotel at the right price”
text: We arrived before check-in time and were given a room right away--an upgrade to a one-bedroom suite. While the decor (in my view) was a little grim--it works better in a smaller space--the beds were excellent, the a/c was great, and the bathroom, while prettty small, was sparkling. The shower was wonderful. The kitchen pantry let us enjoy a drink and a bite before heading out to dinner. This hotel is a solid, reliable choice in a well-located residential neighborhood. When the price is right, it's a real winner.

title: “Great property - great service - unique experience”
text: The hotel was simply wonderful and the hospitality was great. The outdoor pool and bar area is very nice with fire pits and great bar service.

title: “large suites, at a reasonable price”
text: The rooms are large and comfortable, though sometimes a bit noisy as they overlook lexington avenue. comfortable king size beds. The breakfast is so so and quite overpriced: the nearby cafe del amore is a better and more affordable choice. The helpfulness of the staff at front desk is very variable. The hotel is at a 10 minutes walk from Grand Central and 25 minutes from Times square.

title: “Home away from Home”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the W San Diego during a recent business trip. I have stayed at other W hotels in the past and always look forward to stay again but when it comes to San Diego, W lives up to the name with superb service and a 100% customer service driven atmosphere. Melissa at the welcome desk got an "A". You made us feel at home right away. What a nice young lady. 
Beautiful hotel, bar and fantastic bedroom with the most comfortable beds and linens. Complimentary transportation by Acura is a plus. Everything from arrival to departure was pleasant. This is not the first time I stay at W and will not be the last one.

title: “Awesome Front Desk Staff!”
text:
We wandered in after making our way to Chicago by train for a quick escape from Indy and found a great group of employees who were sincerely friendly and went out of their way to make us feel welcomed and oriented for our first trip to this city. If any of them read this... we can't wait to see the Facebook video of you guys doing that dance!!
Our room was newly remodeled and looked fresh and was very clean, including the bathroom. I suppose it would be called small, but we don't care about size and it was very comfortable. 
If I had one thing to say about this hotel, it would be please don't come here. Because we want to keep this great gem as quiet as possible, so we can be sure to get a room anytime. We don't want to risk it becoming too popular! :-)

title: “What a Treasure”
text: The staff at this hotel was wonderful and very helpful. The decor was lovely and the room very comfortable and clean. The room we booked was not available so we were upgraded to a suite an no extra charge. The location was a comfortable walk to the White House and the Mall. The restaurant was convenient and the prices were in line if not less than other similar quality restaurants in the area and the food was very very good. This was an exceptional stay for the price and I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Kyle the bartender is fantastic”
text: Kyle is the reason I am rating this hotel a 5. If it wasn't for him I would not be returning. He is a great business professional & awesome at customer service. He is an asset to this hotel and I would recommend anyone staying at this hotel to visit with him. A thumbs up for Kyle.

title: “Amazing hotel!!!”
text:
The hotel is located at west hollywood, near Hollywood and Beverly hills, just behind Beverly Center. Its all about location!!! 
Elan seams that used to be an old building with renovations and the result its a cute small hotel!!! The best of it for me was the service. Everybody there were SO helpful and thats a really plus, for someone who is in LA for the first time! 
We arrived tired and late, about 10pm, and i have an amazing welcome!!! The check in was fast and the guy in the desk help us with tips about ATM, nearby restaurants. We did early quickly check out the next morning. 
They have a simple morning breakfast, continental breakfast and a wine and cheese service at the evening. We just came back to the hotel for picking our bags and were waiting for our cab and also offered us the wine and cheese service. 
For the price, the location and most of all the SERVICE, its value!!!

title: “Excellence”
text:
I am a former Four Seasons Hotel employee and must say that The Hotel Vitale is right on up there! Non smoking building keeps it smelling fresh and clean. Easy SFO airport bart ride into the Embarcadero station with the hotel right around the corner. Excellent location. The staff exceeded our expectations. Room was fantastic with the deep soaking tube and great view of the city. Room service YUM! The brussel sprouts and artichoke dish! We indulged in several menu items and they were all delicious! The Ferry Building convenient across the street.. We had the gluten free organic curry potato empanadas with salad. The ahi fish tacos, organic vegan donuts OMG .. We brought a dozen home. 
This is our new favorite hotel and will bring us back to SF in the future.

title: “Great Little Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the MAve for our honeymoon in October of last year. The staff we among the politest I've ever come across, and upgraded our room when we mentioned our honeymoon. They gave us lots of info about NYC as well. It was a good base, and if you don't mind doing some walking you can see a lot. 
The rooms are not large, but we weren't spending much time in our hotel room. They were very clean, as was the bathroom. You can hear noise from the street, but we didn't find that to be a big deal. We took advantage of the free coffee and pastries in the morning, but usually went out for breakfast at a little coffee shop around the corner. 
I enojyed our stay, and would definately recommend it to someone.

title: “Enjoyed our stay here.”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights at the start of September. We spent ages trying to find a suitable hotel in LA. Every time we found one we liked most of the reviews weren't good. having read the reviews for this hotel we were initially unsure but it seemed to be in a good location for the things we wanted to do. We needn't have worried it was lovely staying here. We had a second floor room to the side of the hotel and it was perfect. You hear a slight noise from the traffic but nothing that bothered us. The room was clean and well presented. Each night we returned to the room the bed was turned down and the light and the radio were on. Also on each bed was a little note with a cartoon on it and telling us the weather forecast for the next day with 3 little chocolates. Nice touch. 
Breakfast was great. Cereal, rolls, bagels, bread, yoghurt, eggs, fruit, tea coffeeand orange juice. Just fine to start the day rather than going out searching for breakfast. The wine and cheese reception was all very informal and fine to have at the end of the day on returning to the hotel. However it is from 5 to 7pm and may be a bit early for some.
