This was a perfect location for visiting Hollywood, Universal (only about 20min drive) and Santa Monica. The Beverly centre is just two blocks away. There is a 24 hr pharmacy nearby which sells a bit of everything. There are also several restaurants in the near vicinity.
The staff were all very helpful and Pablo one of the car valet staff was always so cheery. 
The only negative thing I would like to mention was that the matress cover was loose and the bottom sheet on the bed was rather short and I had to remake the bed each night to make it comfortable.
All in all we fully reccommend this hotel.

title: “positives trump the negatives”
text:
I have stayed at the Whitehall several times over many years...and the positives...small, old style, very well located, value, interesting and different rooms (latest was an upgrade to a huge suite with grand views), some high quality aspects (beds and linens!) more than outweigh the negatives...renovations needed, services limited, technology/elevators from other eras. 
You sense you're in a nice time warp movie sometimes at the Whitehall ("Where's my fedora?")...but it all combines for a comfortable, easy on the wallet, perfectly located, "homey" kind of stay. Staff are very helpful and aware of the "quirkiness" that is the the Whitehall.
It's not for everyone, if you like big, splashy and " tres moderne" (and the associated expense) you won't like the Whitehall...but it's an interesting ambiance the Whitehall has and an interesting clientele it attracts as well; plus the cost is VERY reasonable and you can spend your savings at the Rush Street feeding places or the Mag Mile shops...which are literally a step away. Enjoy it!

title: “Barely Average”
text: I stayed here on a business trip and found the hotel depressing. I checked in on a Sunday and the pool was open for a "pool party". Hotel guests attend for free and others for a cover charge. The music was extremely loud and reverberated throughout the hotel making it impossible to rest or relax in your room for even a few minutes which was problematic. Thinking that "if you can't beat em, join em", I went up to the pool to find a wall to wall 20 something crowd with standing room only in the pool. I have nothing against young people and certainly if I was in that age group I wouldn't have minded but if the hotel only has one pool I dont think they should have open functions that make the use of the pool unattractive to the average guest. The other thing that was kind of unsettking was the presence of security guards screening people getting into the elevators presumably to go to the pool party. It made me wonder if they have had problems before. This pool party went on for the entire day until 10PM. My next complaint is that the corridors are too dimly lit. I felt like I was walking down a dark street every time I wwnt to my room. The restaurant had excellent food but the service left a little to be desired which is a shame because the food really was great. Service was a bit slow and the waiters are not attentive, however the host did at one point tke notice and then stepped in. Two conferences were going on at the same time and the insulation between the two meeting rooms was exceptionally poor. We could hear everything going on at the other conference. The rooms were small but nicely decorated and clean. The location was convenient for a business trip (close to Union Station), but I think if I were traveling for pleasure, I might want to be closer to some of the restaurants and attractions. Simple ammenities like free wifi in the room were lacking, there was free wi fi in the lobby area but in the room there is a charge, When you are trying to work going to the lobby particularly a noisy lobby is not practical. Nowadays most hotels provide this ammenity in the room free of charge. The business center only had one computer and also charged a fee for internet access.

title: “~STAY HERE!~”
text: What a find this hotel is. It's a total oasis. The staff are wonderful, it's nice quality, the location great for those with downtown biz. Have been doing the NY travel scene for so many years I though tI knew everything. I didn't, but now I do :)

title: “Where do I begin...”
text: This is one of the most disappointing experience at a Sheraton Hotel. First, when we first walk into the lobby area, the entire place reeked of an overflowed toilet. Our room was decently remodeled but the sink and tub had cracks and chips, which would not have been too bad overall.....until we discovered the elevators don't work. The hotel must have been full as there was a convention of some sort, and most people, including us, had to use the service elevator. Positives are that club room access is great and the lady staff that was there the morning of May 27th is extremely nice and works hard to keep people happy. The hotel is right off the 8 freeway, so the room could be rather loud if your room faces the freeway. The gym and pool were not well-stocked with towels - I had to bring one from my room. It's also odd that there were no wash cloths provided in the hotels rooms. The ATM on the ground floor was not working. Hmm...when you stay somewhere for only two nights and start seeing so many things go wrong, it really makes you wonder how well the place is managed. We have been SPG members for over 10 years, and unfortunately, this was not one of the best...to say the least.

title: “family trip weekend”
text: they gave me a 2 bed room,the carpet,smelled like cirgrettes,and dewie.same night they moved me to a 2nd room,same deal.got a 2bed room,bed was undone,towels all over the bathroom floor.finally after 3rd time.i got a suite.whish i taught was getting from the begining.just a bad exprince.dont plan to stay there again.and they said rates when up,good luck.

title: “Mediocre Location”
text: My wife and I stayed here for a weekend in Chicago and had an okay experience. The location contrary to other reviews is not very good for a downtown Chicago hotel. Everything is at least a fifteen minute walk which in the winter in Chicago means a taxi ride. The other thing that you should know about this hotel is that they allow smoking everywhere. I don't necessarily mind people smoking but the lobby, the elevator lobbies and any area that was public had tons of people smoking and ashtrays everywhere. The pool/spa/excercise room was not very impressive either. It is accessible by walking through the business center corridor, wondering if you're going the right way and then coming to a pool that is extremely small. There is also no hot tub and the "spa" is a closet with a massage table. The concierge was helpful but the people that answer the "sheraton promise" phone told me that there was nothing they could do about ice being out on two floors. The beds were super comfortable. I think that this is probably a nice business hotel with top of the line conference and meeting facilities but for couples or families you can do MUCH better in downtown Chicago.

title: “Great Location, Great View”
text: We spend four days there and was impressed by the Property. The rooms were nice and comfortable. The staff was very helpful. The property is only 10 minutes from Sea World, and the Airport and only 15 minutes from the Zoo. A nice place the relax and to enjoy the view. We would go back again.

title: “Did not like my stay at the hotel”
text:
I booked my hotel through Expedia for a room with a double bed. Upon arrival at the hotel we were given a room with a Queen size bed. It was not what I asked paid for. The hotel changed our room for one with a King size bed, which would have been okay except the the toilet nearly overflowed and we had to call for maintenance to fix the toilet. I was disappointed that we had to pay for parking. Hotel was not three blocks from the Inner Harbor. We were located on the 6th floor, not all of the elevators stopped on six, you would have to press the 7th floor so we could get off on the 6 floor. 
The flyers for the attractions were not in sight they hidded in the corner of the hotel away from the reservation desk on the other side of the floor. 
The room was not clean the next day until 4:30 pm. We could not recline and rest before going out that evening.
The staff at the front desk was very pleasant.
The overall rating for my stay at the hotel in poor.

title: “Great Location For First Timers”
text:
I traveled to Chicago with three girlfriends to celebrate a milestone birthday. None of us had ever been to Chicago before, but I have had previous experiences staying with Affinia in New York, so decided that would be a good place to start. I never had to look anywhere else, because the hotel had exactly what we needed: a suite with two king beds, ensuring that all four of us would have a good night's rest and plenty of room to spread out. 
The room was enormous, as was the bathroom. My only complaints were that the bathroom, while luxe and containing one of the most amazing showers I've ever seen, did not have a tub, which two of us could have used for soaking some sore muscles. We also discovered on the first morning that the suite was only set up for two guests - there were not enough towels, glasses, coffee cups, etc.., and the pillows we had chosen from the pillow menu when making reservations had not been placed in the room. A stop at the front desk took care of the shortage issues, and we had excellent service and amenities for the rest of our stay. 
One day it poured buckets of rain outside, so we were delighted to discover you could borrow umbrellas from the front desk.
The location was perfect for newbies wanting to explore the downtown core of Chicago - we walked to many of our destinations, and when we needed a taxi, they were easy to get right in front of the hotel. We were on the 7th floor, in the front, and had absolutely no issues with noise from the street below. 
Affinia is my favorite chain, and I can't wait to revisit Affinia Chicago in the future.

title: “Great value - highly recommended”
text:
Given that New York hotels are extremely expensive, this one has to be considered in context. It’s pretty bare bones, but gives great value for what you pay. Just be sure you manage your expectations. The rooms are truly tiny, but with contemporary décor and very efficiently arranged. Very clean with sufficient amenities. Flat screen t.v., and free wireless internet. Location is central, convenient to restaurants, shops; striking distance to various sites and public transport. Staff is friendly and helpful. Bed was comfortable. My double room was fine for one person, but for two would be cozy at best. 
Consider it as an affordable option if you’re in New York and abhor the thought of paying several hundred for an average room.

title: “For $35/night probably a good deal. For $85 - run away.”
text:
CONS - 1970's building 20 feet from a major road, industrial/commercial area. They apparently added some mirrors and wood trim in the '80's and stopped updating and painting and possibly cleaning. 
Lots of traffic noise. Windows seem to be either slightly jammed open, or so cheap/thin that the outside noise makes you keep coming back to the window wondering if it is open.
Pillows are thinner than the towels. A number of guests? clients? coming in and out of the stairwell door at 2am. 
My room had a poorly patched area where the towel rack had been ripped out and then replaced. Showgirl style mirror with 12 light bulbs had dangling fixture. Mildew along the giant 1980's jacuzzi tub. 
The walls are so thin I could hear my neighbor get a text message at 2am, and the phone was on vibrate. 
PROS - Free parking. Massage parlor across the street has sign stating it's open late. 
Overall just tired, dingy, cheap and tacky.

title: “Exceptional customer service”
text: Hotel is in a great location, clean and customer service was exceptional!!

title: “Nice room, indifferent service”
text:
We stayed at the Serrano Hotel in May for 3 nights. Checked in at 10pm wasn't a problem, had only two rooms left to choose from -- one on second floor, or one on 7th floor by the elevator. We took our chances and chose the latter one. Surprisingly enough, you could barely hear the elevator doors opening/shutting. 
The hotel is located about 3 big blocks away from Union Square, not too bad of a walk. The room is very well decorated. King-size bed with soft sheets, Aveda toiletries, nice color theme throughout the room. Our view was the top of another building though. 
I asked to borrow an electric converter for my laptop one night, the housekeeper brought me a comforter. Hmm. After clarifying what I needed, he told me to ask the front desk the next morning. Not sure why he couldn't just tell the front desk himself. The next morning I went down and asked the front desk, without hesitation he said no, "we don't have it." So I asked again, specified again the type of converter I needed, he looked in a drawer and found one. When handing it to me he said "Be very careful with this, we only have one here.". Again, not really something I needed to hear.
We had an early flight out, so we checked out around 6:30 in the morning. The guy at the front desk seemed to be still half a sleep, we couldn't get any smiles or facial expressions out of him. The bellman came and asked if we needed a taxi to the airport, we politely declined and said we're going to take the BART. After walking 7 blocks with our two luggages, we saw that BART doesn't start until 8:30am on Sundays, but our flight leaves before 9am. Had no choice so we took the cab, paid almost 40 bucks for the ride. The entire time in the cab we were trying to think of reasons why both the front desk guy and bellman failed to inform us BART's operating time, knowing that we were heading there. 
I frequently stayed at Kimpton Hotels, never had I encountered this kind of indifferent service. I hope the manager of Serrano Hotel is reading this because I'd still an answer for the sub-standard service we received. As for other people who are considering staying here, don't. Pay a little extra and stay at Hotel Monaco or Palomar.

title: “Be careful of upgrades.”
text:
Jeremy, director front office, successfully sold us an upgrade (bait and switch)by telling is that our room was adjecnt to the bar which would be open till 2am. This he said was due to us being the last to Checkin. Walking awayfrom the desk I noticed 3 additional checkins. 
I was told that due to being a hotwire guest I get the lowest level of room available, regardless of what Hotwire may have told me. 
It's very disappointing that a hotel would need to have its own management engage in such activity.

title: “Good value, convenient location”
text: St Giles is located in midtown, very near to Grand Central Station and within walking distance of uptown locations like Central Park and downtown locations like Greenwich Village, as well as Times Square. The decor is old but this does not claim to be a ***** hotel. The real features are the spaciousness of the rooms, the very friendly and helpful staff, and great location. The staff were wonderful and assisted us with much courtesy and efficiency throughout our stay. There are many nearby restaurants. We enjoyed Mapo Tofu and Rare Bar and Grill. We will definitely return.

title: “Lovely room and good service”
text:
We totally enjoyed our stay at this hotel. As Starwood Preferred members, we were upgraded to the Executive Level and thus avoided being on the same floor with girls' softball teams who were visiting Columbus for a tournament. Our floor was quiet and serene, clean and comfortable. The suite was large enough for us to spread out a bit and enjoy the two televisions and the comfort of a sofa. We also enjoyed having two chairs at the desk where we spread a carryout meal one night. The free bottled water and the Starbucks coffee in our room added to our pleasure.
We received outstanding service from Alex T on the front desk. When our room wasn't cleaned as requested while we were out in midday, I called Alex and asked if it could be done soon. He not only arranged for it to be cleaned promptly, he called to follow up. I highly recommend this hotel. We also enjoyed a German Wurst and Beer restaurant within walking distance.

title: “Never going back”
text: I will not be going back to this hotel ever. It would be a much better value to stay at a holiday inn or some other chain. The room was dirty and the bathroom was merely tolerable. The kitchen in the room was horribly disgusting, and the fixtures looked dirty. Additionally, the elevators are excruciatingly slow. I waited for nearly 10 full minutes once for the elevators. The staff uses the same elevators as the guests which must slow it down even more, and it is not a pleasant experience to be crammed in an elevator with a cart full of dirty laundry. They do not change the linen daily either. The "lobby" could barely be called a room, and the breakfast room which was connected to it had some sort of coffee vending machine in the corner. Very unpleasant experience altogether that I would never recommend.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: We love the Doubletree Hotel! Room was very large, extremely comfortable bed, staff very helpful and friendly, great location and tons of amenities. We'll definitely be back!

title: “Nickel and DImed and just OK”
text:
Stayed with my daughter July 10-12 over a weekend. The room was nice enough, just as pictured. The Interior is nice enough. 
Like others, I got a great price on Hotwire and it is a good thing because they charge $12.00 per night for parking. The ticket machine in the parking garage ran out of tickets Sat morning and from then on the gate was just open. They still charged me.
Don't take the promise of a shuttle anywhere within 3 mi. too seriously - each time we tried to use it there was at least a 40 minute wait - so we wound up just driving. The trouble is they had two guys working both the Valet stand AND the shuttle. They do keep the hourly run over to the mall.
The strangest thing to me was there is NO coffee service in the lobby. My room only had decaf and I didn't want to wake my family so I went downstairs thinking every hotel has coffee in the lobby - not this one! A 4 star hotel and no coffee in the lobby??? Its a silly thing but it struck me as cheap after being nickeled and dimed over parking and Internet.
 It was just OK - if prices were about the same - I'd choose the Westin across the street.

title: “would definitely stay agin”
text:
Beautiful entrance/front desk area. Amazing food and service at the Seastar restaurant.
Very comfy beds. Nice bathrooms. Very quiet!!
great gym and spa.

title: “Outstanding service and comfortable place to stay”
text: My sister and I recently stayed here during a 5 day stay in LA. The rooms are very comfortable and clean. The service staff was wonderful, friendly and very helpful. Little Tokyo is in walking distance and a great place to find great food. If you are looking into doing some sightseeing and trying to figure out how to get there (Hollywood sights, Universal Studios, etc.), here are my top 3 options. First choice is taking the Metro. It's cheap and convenient. Second choice, take the taxi from the hotel. Ask first about prices as they my vary from one taxi company to another. Also, remember, LA traffic is terrible so the meter could be running for awhile. We took a taxi from Universal back to the hotel. The driver gave us an estimate of about $35. We got stuck on the highway a long time but at the end, honored that estimate! Third option for sightseeing. About three block or so from the hotel is the Hop-On-Hope Off tour company. Great way to see the sights. One more thing about transportation from the hotel. I don't recommend taking their town car that is available at the hotel. It is extremely expensive and could cost you as much as $100 for round trip transportation to Universal Studios! Overall, super hotel, good food at their restaurant downstairs as well as a beautiful little Japanese garden at their facility.

title: “Hippest place I've ever stayed”
text: Hotel San Jose offered an interesting mix of hipness and austerity, but above all else, it provided us with a perfect location from which to explore Austin. With plenty of great restaurants and bars within walking distance, we felt right at home in the neighborhood. The interior patio was a great place to relax with a beer or a glass of wine; the local DJ added to the experience on Wednesday night. Rooms are very spare, and the lighting provided for reading in bed is awful, but the amenities (shampoo, lotion, etc.) were elegant. Don't go for luxury, but do go for location; ask for a room away from the street and the patio.

title: “Great Location on Riverwalk”
text: Stayed here in early April for the Final 4. Great location right on the Riverwalk. Close to the Alamo and many great restaurants. Rooms are small and hotel is very pricey. There are many hotels on the Riverwalk, some of which I'm sure more affordable. Front desk staff was friendly and helpful.

title: “Excellent place for trendy and fun”
text: Stayed there for three days. We love design hotels and this one was excellent ! What a great surprise when we went on the roof to the lounge bar and swimming pool. They had their usual Saturday happy hour bar. What a moment !!! lovely place, what a swimming pool and place !!! to do just for that !!!

title: “Great stay, great location”
text: Perfect location for all things NYC, whether business or pleasure - this is a great spot!

title: “Decent enough, but borders some slimy neighborhoods”
text:
This hotel is OK if you have Diamond or Gold status with Hilton. At least you then get a nicer room, which is a little bit above average for a major hotel here. 
The big warning is about the neighborhood if you have kids. One side of the hotel is relatively close to Union Square and is sort of OK. The other side is filthy and the people in general are not something you'd want to expose your kids to. If you are on a budget on a business trip and really cannot find anywhere else to stay downtown-it is OK. Being within a couple blocks walk of a Bart station helps too.

title: “Right Across From Easton Town Center”
text: Was here for an over night shopping trip with my wife, location was perfect as the title says all the stores are across the street. Checked in around 5pm on a Saturday with no line and check in was fast. Room was a king bed on the fourth floor. Very spacious, comfortable and clean. The only suggestion I would have for the nice people at the Hampton Inn would be to replace the luggage cushion at the end of the bed with possibly a nice little couch. chair or futon as the computer chair that was provided was okay, just not enough. They had a breakfast, but we did not go to it so can't rate that. Nice little hotel and would stay there again if we were in the area.

title: “Excellent!”
text:
We picked this hotel based on reviews here, and I was not disappointed. Our room was neat and clean, the price was comparable to others in the area, the staff was friendly and helpful, and the location was great. We had a great time. 
Upon checking in, I asked about coupons for breakfast, and the person at the desk gave me a pass for 2 free breakfast buffets. Definitely make sure you do this, because the breakfast is fine, but not really worth the $12 per person they charge. They also seem to have a regular menu to choose from, but we just had the buffet. 
After our room was cleaned the first night, we found ourselves with only one clean bath towel. I called down for more towels and they arrived very quickly (within 10 minutes) and the desk staff person called a few minutes later to make sure we had gotten them. 
We were in town for a wedding west of Philly, and this was close to the interstate, so very convenient for getting to where we wanted to go. We also went into downtown Philly for the afternoon and it took only 20 minutes. 
My only complaint was the difficulty we had finding the hotel. Another reviewer here mentioned this, and I should have taken it more seriously! The directions on the website are USELESS, so don't take them. Even the Google maps directions were vague unless you are familiar with the area, so maybe call the hotel and get someone to give you specific directions? Once you actually get there, there is no sign at the entrance to tell you where to turn, so we found ourselves elated at finally finding it, only to despair as we drove past it again, realizing we would have to go back to the main road to turn around and start again. A little frustrating after a long flight. 
One more tiny complaint: my husband had to run back to the airport for a lost item and took the hotel shuttle, which was fine, but he waited a long time for it to come pick him up later. If you are relying on the shuttle, be sure to call and tell them when you'll be arriving, and give them plenty of time.

title: “i thought it was great!”
text:
my boyfriend and i checked in to the Phoenix Park hotel for an overnight stay...just a little vacation. we got down to the hotel around 11:30 on a sunday morning and asked if we could check in early. check in is normally 3 pm, but the staff member at the front desk said it was no problem so we went on up. the room we stayed in (406) was a pretty nice size. everything was very clean. the air conditioner blasted cold air all afternoon and evening. the only tiny problem we had was a leaky bathtub faucet. but you couldnt hear it from the bed so it wasnt really a problem at all. check out went very smoothly also. we got a very very good rate ($79/night from travelzoo). so i was very happy with the hotel. 
only a couple things to point out:
the hotel does not offer free parking. there is a government lot across the street that you can park in on the weekends for free. but if you car is not out of there by 7 am on monday, they will tow it. 
the hotel does offer valet parking for $25/day. we were only there sunday-monday, so this wasnt a big deal for us. 
the concierge wasnt very helpful to us. we were looking for a good ethnic restaurant to try. we ended up asking someone on the street. 
the hotel restaurant, the Dubliner, had a very good but overpriced breakfast menu. $12 for an omelet?! but i ate it, and it was delicious. 
also! when driving around DC, make sure you check the addresses. we were unfamiliar with the set up and ended up driving an hour and 15 mins looking for an ethiopian restaurant.

title: “Excellent location, excellent hotel”
text:
This hotel is fantastic - reasonably priced, clean and very well located. We paid about £100 a night plus tax. Breakfast isn't provided, but try the fantatstic Cafe Cosmopolitan right by the front door (this place has excellent oatmeal, granola and coffee)! 
The metro stop is just down stairs too - but you can walk to many places including the Financial District (and Ground Zero) = 10 minutes and Soho = 15-20 minutes. Everything else is about a 15 minute metro ride away.
The hotel is about 3 stars (ie no room service or mini bar), but is probably one of the cleanest hotels I have stayed in. The rooms are huge too. See if you can request room 522 because it is on the corner of the building and has a great view of the Empire State Building!
Enjoy! Ill be coming back next time I visit!

title: “Great stay”
text: I loved my stay at this hotel. I've been twice. While the rooms are small, ask for a corner room, and they will seem bigger because you get more window space. Especially if you overlook Broadway. Comfortable beds, and nice amenities.

title: “If you like Asian food then this is perfect”
text: The hotel is right in the heart of Korea Town. We loved the location for the food. Many restaurants there are open 24 hours. It is also very close to several subway lines and within walking distance to many attractions (Rockefeller Center, Empire State Building, 5th Ave, etc.). The hotel room was ok. Nothing special at all but it is clean enough. Compared to other hotels in downtown Manhattan, the price is fair.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text: I enjoyed the courteous staff, Debbie, Mandy, John, Clauda, Angie, and others, excellence facilities, clean/modern, and great location, near Galleria, Southwest Houston, Downtown, central location. This is a great value for the cost a must stay.

title: “Great Service”
text: The staff is very service-oriented. This is a good thing. Comfortable and clean and worth the price.

title: “Good value if prepared”
text: September 28, 2005. Five nights. Room 614. Hotels in San Francisco next to the Convention Center can be VERY expensive. This location is a boutique hotel. The rooms are very small. The queen size bed has 3 feet of space along one short length, five feet of space along one long length. A small closet has 10 hangers and that pretty much fills the space. There is a hair dryer, iron, and some bathroom amenities including towels. There is also a sink in the room. Be aware, however, that many floors have about twenty rooms for sleeping, with 2 bathrooms (male, female) and 2 shower rooms along the halls which everyone shares. Interestingly, during the five days we were there, we never had any wait for either shower or toilets. Maybe the floor was not filled, or maybe our early times for showers--around 6:30am--caused that. Wireless Internet connection is fee-for-service. However, one is only a block away from the Metreon, a large entertainment complex which offers completely free high-speed wireless in the area. From HotelKingdom, we got rooms for $80 a night after all taxes and charges. Yes, boutique hotels are probably an acquired taste. Compared to $240 a night across the street at the Marriott, however, it certainly was an equitable trade-off for us. A couple would realistically be the limit--not a location for families by any stretch.

title: “Great place stay”
text: Good bed, wonderful staff, sweet suites, excellent car service.

title: “You couldn't ask for better Inn Keepers”
text: I stay at this property in Phoenix almost every month and I could not ask for better accommodations and Linda and Barb and all the staff make my stays comfortable and worry free. They have recently done a complete renovation so you will be pleasantly surprised and pleased with your environment. Great Breakfast too!

title: “Best NY Hotel -- Ever”
text: I usually stay at the Washing Square Hotel but it was booked out. The Affinia Dumont was the perfect substitute. I had the largest bedroom I've ever had in NYC(see photos). The kitchen was a plus! The staff are as friendly as everyone says and bent over backwards...they supplied me with a bag of toiletries (toothpaste and brush; mending kit etc) and the small fruit basket is a great welcomer. Also pluses = the comfy dressing gown and the umbrella, the fruit at reception. Be sure to attend the Wed night "mixer"; the wine and cheese platter were impressive. I couldn't have asked for a better week in NYC. Warning, the hotel books out very very quickly and so don't hesitate. Hint: ask for a room overlooking the street--it never hurts to ask. Believe every single positive review here--I will always make the Affinia D my first choice every time (and I'm fussy...)

title: “I loved this hotel!”
text:
Stayed here the night before our return to Atlanta after a week in CO. Our flight was at the crack of dawn, so I wanted something close to the airport offering shuttle service. This place was great. Relatively new; suite style rooms with large sitting area, desk, wet bar, and fridge in one area with the bed behind a divider wall. Big bathroom, seperate vanity with sink.
Pleasant front desk; large attractive lobby with breakfast buffet; I used the laundry facilities, which were also clean and well lighted.
The hotel is on a street with numerous options for food, all within walking distance on a well-lighted street with sidewalks. Lots of people walking to and from dinner; very safe.
We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Nothing special”
text: Recently spent a Friday evening at the Langham. We chose this Hotel because of the Tripadvisor reviews and it's location. Overall, we were dissapointed with the service. The bartender was more interested in talking to his friends than taking orders, the concierge was misinformed (bad directions) and the valet parking was not professional. Our room was small with an immediate view of a concrete partition. It was reasonably well appointed with a comfortable king size bed. The bathroom was small. We found the lounge and restaurants areas out of the way. Because of this the entrance is subdued and lacking the activity that we think makes a luxury hotel exciting and inviting. We did not eat at the hotel although the dining areas were attractive. We found the area to be convenient (10 minute walk to Quincy market) and quiet. The Langham is a stately and attractive building but inside it lacks substance.

title: “good location”
text:
the tuscan inn has a good location, within easy walking distance to the wharf. there are many restaurants and attractions nearby
the hotel room was large-ish with one king bed for my daughter and myself.
very skimpy with the towels. (prompt when requested)
the ironing board was never put away, and the ice bucket was never cleaned out for me.
the bed was comfortable.
this is a safe area, i believe, for some may feel threatened by the Many Homeless wandering about. they are harmless. as i said, but some may not feel comfortable.
my teen daughter and myself felt perfectly safe at all times.
the staff, while all polite, looked a bit distracted, and frankly disengaged.
not the incredible, enthusiastic staff describes in such stellar terms by some lucky visitors. however, they were polite.

title: “Great hotel for traveling with infant”
text:
So this was our first big trip out of town with our 6 month old baby. I was very nervous about booking a hotel that would have all the conveniences of home and I hit the jackpot!
WHO STAYED HERE - 4 adults and 1 infant
WHY WE BOOKED THIS HOTEL - We booked this hotel because a)it was a suite b)it had a fridge and c)it was a Hilton. Also the location was close enough to 6th street for a 5 minute car ride, but far enough away so that we didn't have to hear drunk idiots outside our door at 3am. 
THE ROOM - The room was immaculately clean. There was a big bedroom and a nice sized living room with seating for 4 AND a table and 4 chairs. There was also a full length mirror in the bedroom. This is something you don't think you need until you're ready to walk out the door - then this becomes a very important amenity. The bedroom also had a large dresser and a huge wardrobe for storage. There were 2 flat screen tvs as well, both in fine working order. As well as the hairdryer worked. 
CONVENIENCES - There were 3 areas with sinks and mirrors. If you have a lot of people getting ready at the same time (especially women who are doing makeup) this is very important. We used 2 of the mirrors for getting ready, and the 3rd as a diaper changing station. The bedroom was big enough to setup my baby's pack and play and still have LOTS of room to spare. The walls were thick. I barely heard our neighbors and as far as I know, no one heard my baby crying. Also if you are a nursing mom, there is a fridge for your milk as well as a very small freezer section where you can put ice packs. 
The beds were comfy and the curtains were those awesome hotel curtains that COMPLETELY block out the light. This made for nice snoozing in the morning 
FREE STUFF - The free happy hour is just greatness. Its in the lobby which is an open air setting. There were people of all ages there, so we brought our baby down to enjoy the tall tropical plants and the koi fish pond. It was very relaxing after our long drive into town. The daily breakfast is absolutely amazing. Its not just cereal and bagels. They have eggs, meat and even a made to order omlette station. Plus coffee, milk, oj, etc. That saved the 4 of us probably $100 over 2 days alone! Another huge perk is free parking. We were constantly coming and going and we also had guests come visit us so this was an important amenity for us as well. 
STAFF - everyone was very accommodating from the front desk clerk, to the housekeeping, to the random worker who brought a clean flat sheet to our room. They really have their stuff together. 
MY ONLY COMPLAINT - is that after the first day, our room started to smell kind of musty. We were in room 411 if that helps at all.
I will be returning to Austin soon and at this point I see no reason to book another hotel.

title: “Top notch hotel on Santana Row”
text:
We attended this for a company kick off meeting in January 2007 and it was a perfect venue for the event. We hired about two floors worth of rooms (including some suites) and none of the guests were dissapointed.
We hope to go back again next year.

title: “Glass lifts, atrium and fabulous harbour views”
text: Well situated 4* hotel. WE flew into SFO and used BART to travel into the City $8.10 each way. Station right outside the hotel. Doesn't look much from the outside but stunning internal atrium. Helpful reception staff and concierge desk. Upgraded to harbour view with balcony (deal on at the time) after getting a book 2 get one night free with Expedia. Well equipped good sized room, nice to be able to sit out on balcony. Close to all amenities, cable cars stop right outside. Buy MUNI pass if you are there a couple of days (ask reception for directions). Saturday morning Farmers Market on the harbour front - well worth a stroll around, lots of things to try. Only downside having to pay for internet - come on Hyatt, if Holiday Inn Express can give this for free, you need to look at this again!!

title: “do it once”
text: We stayed at the Waldorf for two nights at the end of our trip after a longer stay in another New York hotel. There is no doubt that it is a beautiful property that is worth a visit, however, there is a constant feeling that the staff are only happy to serve you whilst they wait for someone more "important" to catch their attention. This was not the case in the other (more expensive) New York hotel that we stayed in.

title: “No faults to report”
text:
Stayed for 2 nights late March on the 46th Floor as we are Priority Club Members, this hotel was free with our Priority Points. We were also given access to the Club Lounge where we had free snacks & drinks late in the afternoon and a lovely buffet continental breakfast. 
I have stayed on Time Square before and have always been able to hear the hussle and bussle below but not on the 46th floor of the Crowne Plaza, very quiet indeed.
Extremely comfortable bed.
Excellent quick check in
No problems to report at all.

title: “Great location, otherwise average”
text:
One night stay from Heathrow en route to Memphis. This hotel is massive! Needed to take a convenient monorail train within the airport to reach it. Check in was very smooth and efficient (as would be expected from a Hilton). Spacious room, with view of runway with airplanes taking off one per minute, but no noise (must be triple glazed at least).
As I said the hotel is absolutely huge. Comfortable, but in great need of a major decorative overhaul to drag it out of the 1970s dark décor into the current era. We had a nice meal in the restaurant, slept very well, and set off very refreshed to continue our journey to Memphis – job done!
But not a hotel I would choose for any leisure purpose.

title: “Great room, excellently situated for exploring Manhattan”
text:
I really have nothing bad to say about this hotel. The rooms are spacious for NYC (at least the one I had on 29th floor was), very functional, stylish and clean. There's free coffee in the lobby 24-7 and the room is supplied with a coffee machine too - and a spacious fridge if you want to store foodstuff and drinks. The view was superb too - rare in Midtown - but obviously not all rooms will have a straight view to Empire State Building. For exploring the city the location is extremely convenient: there's a Subway station some 30 metres from the hotel that will bring you up- or downtown and you'll be in SoHo/Greenwich Village in 5-7 minutes. And, obviously, being adjacent to Times Square and the Port Authority Bus Station also lends lots of opportunities.
The service was efficient and professional too. We did not take breakfast at the hotel - there are plenty of delis etc around the corner, and the small space for serving breakfast surely can't service all customers, so I guess it is better to find food elsewhere.
This is surely the hotel I'll choose next time I go to NYC. It is not the cheapest, but it is very good value for the money.

title: “Classic gem”
text: Updated rooms, comfortable and affordable, excellence service, thank you!

title: “Great Stay”
text: A friend and I had to attend a conference at the new Westin. We were too cheap to pay to stay there. The Park Plaza was very nice. She scored a great rate on hotwire - less than $60 a night. The room and bathroom were smallish, but beautiful and clean. The lobby and staff were warm and accomodating. Would definitely stay again. The location is very central to downtown Boston. Plenty of things to do and places to eat very close.

title: “Slipped a notch...still great service but missing some small things”
text:
Another return visit for us
Smooth checkin (i believe they have the best front line/front desk I have ever seen), friendly, accurate, fast
On to the room.. I walk in my suite and in the bedroom there is a pile of dirty sheets! The rest of the room was spotless. I called and they asked if I wanted to change or have someone just pick up the sheets?
Also when i checked in they asked what paper I wanted. I replied that local indianapolis paper would be fine. I did mot get a paper on either morning. The little things were always perfect here, but not this trip.
The television in the bedroom needs to be changed. The screen was horrible
Concierge was great, bellman were great, and the front desk could teach other hotels that first impressions matter a lot among other things

title: “Wow”
text: Wow it was terrible. Never in my life will I ever stay there again. The room service was also terrible. A woman who's name I am not going to say slapped me for telling her she forgot my bacon.

title: “great hotel, amazing location!!!!!”
text: This is my second trip to this hotel, it's amazing! love the location, love the staff! i would stay here again, again and again.

title: “always a good night sleep”
text:
This is my favorite NYC hotel - the rooms are always comfortable and spotless and the beds are heaven-like. The service is excellent. Located a block off Times Square, The Muse is walking distance to nearly everywhere. 
hence, we return over and over whenever we visit NYC... and I'm a native New Yorker!!

title: “Millennium Broadway”
text: I was travelling with my husband and daughter and we had a very unfortunate incident at the hotel. I won't get into details, but I felt satisfied that the hotel rectified their mistake appropriately and to my satisfaction. I would reccomend this hotel to families, but only if they are prepared to reserve 2 adjoining rooms (as the rooms are small). The location was perfect, and I appreciated the quiet side street location as opposed to opening up directly to Times Square. We ate breakfast in the hotel most mornings, it was ok, nothing special. I would HIGHLY reccomend the "Times Square Deli" across the street for lunch or dinner. Their sandwiches delicious and enormous!

title: “Mixed Feelings”
text: Initially we were pleased with our choice - the room was a good size, though small bed, nice linens and design and good views. Good welcome at reception and able to have an optional smoking room. Breakfast was quite good with good waiting staff. But...........it is a party hotel. The pool area is small and when we were there taken over by a crowd who seemed to be there to drink all day. Not the sophisticated and peaceful area I imagined. In the evening it is worse as the rooftop becomes a club with people lining up to get in in the early hours of the morning then disrupting sleeeping (until then) guests as they leave. Front desk did not respond to calls to report sustained noise. After a while we termed it as a night club with ahotel attached. Dining facilities are very average for a hotel of this price and drinks are exorbitantly expensive - costing $4 or 5 more if no food is ordered! The area is very buzzy, maybe too buzzy but you have all the area offers on the doorstep - the Highline is well worth visiting and there are lots of restaurants to choose from.

title: “Best business trip....”
text:
The Westin is strategically located close to downtown but most importantly it is connected to the Galleria Mall with three levels containing anything you might want or need outside of the normal hotel amenities. The room was excellent and the bed did wonders for my lower back, much better than my own bed at home. The staff is great, the hotel is great....I was made to feel very important during my stay. 
Bobby B

title: “WOW Hotel”
text: Top notch hotel with impeccable rooms. Outstanding and very chic theme throughout. The room was beautifully designed for comfort. Well stocked bar and bathroom amenities. The mood lighting controls were a nice touch of class. The staff was very friendly and accommodating and you can't beat the location. The hotel room doors are a bit loud when they shut. It was a bit annoying in the morning hearing my neighbors leave. However, overall this was one of the most memorable hotel stays I've experienced and I will definitely return.

title: “It's all true!”
text:
I won't repeat all that has already been said about the excellent Sofitel New York, just to say that my wife and I had a wonderful experience staying for four days in April. The hotel is excellent with exceedingly friendly and helpful staff and can not be faulted.
A few ideas
1. Don't bother with the Empire States Building, the queues are very long (allow at least an hour) and the whole experience is tacky and tired.
2. Go to Top of the Rock which is excellent, the queues are short, the experience is better and there is much more room to look around and admire the views.
3. Try Rosen’s Deli, 23 East 51 Street, good deli in art deco surroundings.
4. Depending on your point of view either take your partner or avoid Diamond Street (47th Street). There are some amazing bargains in comparison to the inflated jewellery prices in the UK.
5. Finally, the pretzels are heavy going and one between two is sufficient!!

title: “Beautiful hotel - comfortable, great service”
text: We recently spent 5 nights in New York a On the Ave. The service at the hotel is first rate. The rooms are lovely - nicely appointed, very comfortable bed, beautiful bathroom. Our first room was very small - I had received an email saying I could upgrade for $60. Unfortunately, there were no rooms available on the weekend, but for our last two nights they upgraded us to a huge room, penthouse, big balcony and incredible views of the river and downtown. The hotel staff are incredibly pleasant, helpful and attentive. The location is great - the upper west side, very close to the park. We walked a lot in the neighbourhood - less frenetic than midtown and full of moms and babies in strollers and people dog walking. We also walked to Time Square at least once a day - a very nice walk either through the park or on the streets. And it is very close to the subway and a quick cab ride to downtown. Just fell into many excellent, not over priced, restaurants in the neighbourhood.

title: “Cosy Inn”
text: An old fashioned hotel/inn some 150 yards away from the SF Opera. Very charming reception with apples and cookies, bringing the luggage to our room and refusing a tip. Rooms old fashioned but cosy. Elegant restaurant, visited by many elegantly dressed opera goers. Reasonably priced.

title: “Very cool”
text: It's not too often cool and funky is comfortable and inexpensive. We just stayed this past weekend. They had a display of 6 different artists in the lobby and some theme rooms which were each decorated by a different artist. We stayed in a room which felt like SOHO. Very fun and this definitely isn't like staying at Holiday Inn. On the practical side, it was a great spot, perfectly clean and apparently recently renovated. The only negative was around lunchtime the French restaurant downstairs got going and we always got too hungry from the aroma.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
Stayed a few times on business, room always clean service always good.
The one thing I'll say about this building is that it's the most complicated labyrinth I've ever seen (and I travel a fair amount). The hotel lobby is on the 3d floor but the elevators are in a different part of the structure (across an elevated walkway); the street and river side entrances are on different levels and both entrances close at 9 PM leaving only the hotel entrance open that's tucked away on the side of the building. My first time in I arrived late at DTW, rented a car, parked in the garage, and had to circumnavigate the building on foot to find the entrance to get in. But don't hold that against the Marriott, just some architect who hopefully did not do that much work after this - though the bldg exterior is quite nice.
One cool feature of the building lobby (if you like cars) are the GM displays (GM offices are in the building) but this is tempered by the fact that most of the retail in the building closes at 6 PM when the work day ends so if you arrive on a late flight there are limited options for food.

title: “Bring your ear plugs.”
text:
Similiar to the other reviews. Hotel was clean, elegant and conveniently located right next to two subway stations (WTC and Fulton St). Bed was comfortable, bathroom was fairly new looking, toiletries were from Crabtree & Evelyn, room was $200 on Hotwire... 
All was well, until I woke up in the middle of the night to a jackhammer. Yes, construction at the WTC site is 24/7. I took a previous TA member's tip and asked for a room away from the construction site, but they didn't have anything available. Although the view facing the site is gorgeous, the noise at night was really annoying. I got ear plugs the next day. Bring them. You will need them if you are a light sleeper like me.
Aside from the noise issue, service at the hotel could be better. The concierge wasn't very helpful for dinner reservations, and we had to call housekeeping staff a couple of times to get a toothbrush.
Even with the inconveniences, we would stay at this hotel again (especially for $200). Next time, I will come prepared!
Happy travels.

title: “Second Visit Better than the First!”
text: We have stayed at the Half Moon before and were facing the marina. This time we chose to face the bay and the Marine Air Station. What a treat to wake up and open the shades to fine the morning sun greeting us. The room was clean, the staff responsive and helpful, and the food was excellent. When we go back, we will stay there.

title: “Clean, friendly but a little out dated”
text:
Stayed at this hotel in October, was welcomed by friendly staff and advised there was a free pasta night serving beer and wine that evening I could attend if I wanted to.
Had a comfortable stay at this hotel, the room was huge and had a lounge, kitchen (with a full sized American fridge and dishwasher), 46inch LCD TV, king sized bed and bath/shower. The room was a bit dated but still clean and comfortable. The beds were nice and there was a good selection of pillows. The AC had a mind of its own, I couldn't get it to reduce down in temperature to my preference so ended up turning it off and opening the windows. 
When I arrived I wanted to use the pool, however even though it was a nice day around 77 degrees as it was October it was classed out of season so it was closed. The gym was ok, bit small but had enough in there for a quick workout.
Breakfast was nice, reasonable selection of food included in the price. There is also a small business area you can use with a computer and printer. 
Although I only stayed for 1 night there didn't appear to be much to do nearby the hotel, so I headed into the main centre which took 20 mins by car. 
Down sides
• No Wifi
• Bit dated
• Noisy AC and appliances in the room
• No shower gels
Positives
• Good value
• Big rooms
• Free breakfast
• Free internet via a cable
• Free parking
• Free business centre
• Free gym

title: “great loaction for all the tourist activities”
text: we stayed her for four nights on a two week holiday from ireland which included l.a and las vegas.the hotel is in a brill location close to the pier and walking distance to many of the other attractions around.i really think this is an ideal location to stay if you want to sight see.union square is good for shopping but its a bit of a distance away and san francisco is very streched out when you decide to walk around.the rooms were clean and the beds very comfy.we only ate here once as there is so much variety outside the hotel aswell.the night we arrived we were so tired we got room service and i have to say the food was yummy.i loved there garlic parmesan fries.i would recomend trying their food at least once didnt bother with breakfast as we knew we would be getting seriously big portions in usa.parking is expensive i think around 40 dollars a night but its apparently like this all over san francisco.overall brill stay.get up early in the morning and stroll down to pier 39. its quiet and you get to watch the sealions without the crowds around.we also drank in knuckles which is a cool bar lots of large t.v screens with every kind of sport on at one time.

title: “Nicest Courtyard”
text: This Courtyard was the nicest one we have ever stayed in. Our room was small but the hotel is new and very up to date and clean. It has a lovely water location with pool and a great breakfast. We had received breakfast in our package. We stayed one night after a long flight and their free shuttle had stopped running and they picked up our tab for the cab--very nice! The front desk staff provided directions for sightseeing and were very friendly. A real winner!

title: “Aging Fast”
text:
The W Times Square has a great location if you're in the city for theater. Other than that, there are problems... This was my second stay at this property, but the first since 2004. 
The entry to the hotel is on 47th street, and is only an elevator lobby that takes you up to 7 which is the main lobby (or Living Room) as W likes to say. During the daytime, the lobby is a nice enough space with check in located off in an alcove. At night, the lobby turns into a nightclub. A source of revenue for the hotel - but very limiting to the paying guests who have no public area within the hotel to gather or relax outside of the room.
There is also the Whiskey Bar separate from the Lobby on street level (part of Blue Fin Restaurant, I think), but the W feels they also need to turn the lobby into a nightclub as well. It seeems to work for them as it was packed and loud every night. For the hotel guests, it was annoying.
The rooms are small and with exception of those ending in 10 or 11, have very limited views (facing either Marriott Marquis or an office building). Rooms ending in 10 & 11 face Broadway north toward Central Park, and if you are on a higher floor, you may even have a Park view. Actually, the rooms ending in 11 seem to have a larger floorplan with a sitting area. There are only 10 rooms per floors with 57 being the highest floor.
What I noticed on this visit was how the rooms have aged - not very well. I didn't find them to be dirty, as I had read in previous reviews. Everything was nice & clean. But they did seem very dated. 
The W is marketed as a trendy, boutique hotel. And they also try to sell a luxury image. I found this hotel failing both categories. 
The furnishings in the room were pretty beaten up, and just seemed cheap. The 'chair' they use is a white leather-like cube with no arms. Basically, it's an ottoman sitting in the corner with absolutely no function as a chair for lounging. You can physically sit on it, but not for long as it is just not comfortable. 
Which leaves the bed as the only place in the room to sit. If this were a less expensive property, that would be one thing. But the prices are quite high and this hotel participates in several luxury hotel collections (Amex Fine Hotels being one), which indicates a certain level of luxury and services. With that in mind, I have rated this property with only 3 stars.
I'll list a few positives and negatives that stood out:
The Good (in addition to location):
+ Bell Staff were very attentive and seemed genuinely interested in guest service
+ Nice flat panel TV's with nice range of channels (though only a very few were HD)
+ A good deli next door, which proved necessary as the Blue Fin restaurant only opened for limited hours. It had good selection of food and reasonable pricing
+ Comfortable Bed
The Bad:
- Rooms were small & furnishings were greatly lacking
- Very small bathrooms
- Lots of noise coming from hallways into the room (seemed like much of it was hotel staff servicing rooms during the day)
- No climate control in the rooms (Forget the thermostat on the wall)
- Limited usable public space and restaurant choice
SUMMARY - Great location for theater and a nice, comfortable bed for sleeping. Not especially trendy, aging fast.

title: “Loved the Fairmont”
text:
WOW - What a wonderful surprise!! Our stay at the Fairmont was a wonderful experience. The room was spacious, newly renovated and beautiful. Beds were comfortable, Huge flat screen TV was awesome, coffee /expresso machine was a real treat. My friend and I hightly recommend this hotel. We fell in love with the huge bathroom . We also enjoyed wearing the comfy White Fairmont Robes!! 
The location is close to Michigan Ave. The staff was very nice - Checked us in upon our arrival at 10:00 AM. The really AWESOME Surprise was the ride in the house car , a BENTLEY back to Union Station. Dean our driver was extremely nice.
This is a 5 star property - Nicest hotel We've stayed in.
And Yes, the price was right - Only 89.00 for the night.
We will definitely be back!!
FAIRMONT ROCKS!! We highly recommend!!

title: “Mario adds to the "Worldwide Wow. Now" @ the W on Lex”
text:
I just recently stayed at the W Hotel on Lexington ...and I must say it was a WONDERFUL experience for me and my significant other on our very special day........Mario Q. - Whatever/Whenever Talent was amazing! Mario helped put the WOW into our Anniversary weekend.
He called in advance of our stay to make sure if there were any special request for our Anniversary weekend. Furthermore, due to the very busy holiday weekend (Labor Day) Mario, took it a step further and personally made certain that our room was ready and available with a little welcoming surprise for our stay. The W staff was also very friendly and attentive during our stay....I would like to add that the W at Lexington has a very chic/cozy lounge, bar, decor, and unique ambience......it gives you the vibe that all are welcomed.
In closing, I highly recommend staying at the W at Lexington and if he is available ask for Mario Q.

title: “Family Friendly”
text:
Stayed here in late July. Served as our mid-point base for a friend's graduation from Lackland AFB, and as a jumping off point for other San Antonio attractions.
Clean rooms and a friendly staff seriously committed to being helpful and attentive to the needs of guests. 
The Ritz it ain't, but it's a great value in family hotel. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “It is "Micro"”
text: Chose the Microtel based on price, proximity to the airport and travelers reviews. We booked two rooms for three people. We wished we had been warned how appropriate the name "Micro" fit this hotel. Our room was barely large enough to walk around the full-size bed. Really not that comfortable for two people. The bathroom toilet seat kept falling down in both rooms, so there is a flaw in the design. Our sheets seemed way to small and kept coming up at the corners of the bed, they also had a cigarette burn in them, The top cover on the bed had ink marks and the light in the bathroom was burned out. We had to keep the heat light going to see in the bathroom. We were greeted by cigarette buts were at the elevator entrance on the floor. The hotel was quiet, breakfast- basic but adequate, staff very pleasant, they apologized for the problems but said the reasons for the problems were the guests that stayed there. The hotel is trying - but we would not re-book...Especially when in actuality, they charge $20 more for a room that is not pre-paid.

title: “Just perfect!”
text: I stayed only one night from 1 - 2 April 2005 in a suite overlooking the watertower. All staff were very friendly and helpful. The service was perfect and also the food in the main restaurant was very nice. In the later evening I enjoyed the bar, a very trendy and popular place in Chicago. The 2 bedroom suite and the lovely bathroom made me dreaming. This hotel is just perfect and in my opinion the best choice for Chicago. Absolutely wonderful, nothing to complain about.

title: “great”
text: i enjoyed sleeping on the large beds, the rooms were huge, the breakfast was amazing with so much food to choose from plus a chef who makes custom orders such as pancakes, omelets, etc

title: “Great location and service”
text:
We spent 4 nights at the Millenium park Fairmont and were very pleased with the experience. The room was very nice with great views of the city and lake and the room service dining was FANTASTIC, probably the best in-room dinner we have ever had. The bathroom also looked new and nice, but the shower was a big disappointment - it almost felt like I was trying to rinse my hair standing under the rain - no water pressure whatsoever. I wonder if this would be better on lower floors...
The location of the hotel is quite convenient, within walking distance of the magnificent mile, but not quite as busy and also close to the park. 
My only real complaint about this place was the price of the parking - it's outrageous. Nobody expects free parking anymore, but what this hotel charges is ridiculous. We ended up parking in a public lot across the street for half the price, and it turned out to be more convenient too, as we didn't have to spend hours standing in front of the hotel waiting for the car.... 
I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “LOVED it! Great location”
text:
I was very fearful of staying at a hotel in NYC after the numerous reports of bed bugs at various hotels. But this hotel was PERFECT! 
First off, no bed bugs in either of the two rooms we had for the entire stay! The rooms were VERY clean. I checked the mattresses, headboards and nooks & crannies of our rooms. The staff was amazing!! - Very friendly, willing to go the extra mile to make our stay comfortable. Fresh baked cookies in the afternoon! Check with the bellhop for any transportation needs - even ask the front desk before you arrive. Our bellman had a connection with a SUV that took us to the airport - it cost much less than our arrival SUV that I had booked online and the guy was much nicer.
There was breakfast every morning. It did get busy, but that was at the peak time and was to be expected. The food was standard but good. We ate there almost every morning (except when we splurged for Pastis in the Meatpacking District). It was a great way to start off our morning knowing that we'd rather spend our money on fancy dinner, a show, sightseeing, the museums or simple a cab after a long day of walking. It was an added value.
There was free wifi though most of us couldn't figure out how to sign up for it. If it was a big deal we would've called the front desk. 
The location was absolutely perfect. Very close to Central Park for morning jogs. Right next to the big theaters. Blocks to Times Square, but far enough away from the crazy busy chaos of it.
Great food options to those who are staying here: Toloache - great fancy mexican food. Delicious guacamole. mid to higher priced but worth it. On 50th near 8th. The West End Bar & Grill on the corner of 8th & 49th. Great casual food, beer, mixed drinks.Good prices.
I honestly can't say enough about how great this hotel was!

title: “This is a Wonderful Hotel, with Excellent Staff and Great Location”
text:
I love this Holiday Inn Express and would rate it to be amongst the very best I have ever been too. Let me tell you why I have this opinion. Before coming to this Hotel on this Occasion I emailed them and asked if I could have a parcel sent to them, I received a immediate and pleasant response that it would not be a problem as long as my name was on it and they would be happy to hold it for me till I arrive, as it turned out the items I ordered, which I thought would be delivered in one parcel where sent in three lots and each time the wonderful front office staff sent me an email and confirmed they had received a parcel and put it safely away for me, and how they were looking forward to my stay. Manny the front office manager has been an absolute star, with brilliant communications and just made me feel good with what started of being a simple thing being a little more complex.
 
This Hotel is so well located that its pricing feels like you should be out of town, but it’s not, its within two minute’s walk to the hustle and bustle of Hollywood Boulevard, and many of the great sites and highlights of Hollywood are your door step. The rooms are fabulous, large and roomy with everything you could need, keep in mind it’s not a 5 star Hotel, but they behave as it is, my point I suppose is that it’s all well above expectations. Its all marvellous the staff are some of the most friendly you can find and I enjoy coming in after a hard day out eating, drinking and being a tourist, to their friendly warm welcome. They give you a great sense of being home. My welcome on arrival, after a long flight from Sydney, was lovely, Manny was there to greet us and even gave us a selection of rooms, he is an Ambasadore for this hotel and the great IHG chain.
 
Let me tell you they have a pool which after coming from a rather cool Sydney winter was a warm relaxing relief to sit around in the sun. My day starts with an amazing breakfast, the selection is great, there is mostly everything to suit most tastes,  and I'm having the pancakes with bacon. They have yogurts and different eggs, and a good variety of other delights, the staff ,(  Marietta and Veronica) in the breakfast room are very nice and if something runs out just ask nicely and they are more than happy to get it. It is refreshing to have such nice and pleasant people when you are on such a special holiday. Returning to your spacious room and nap in some of the nicest beds youll find with the famous Holiday Inn pillow menu you will find your favourite pillow type, call housekeeping and its done. Theres a 32 inch flat screen TV and bar fridge with plenty of room for your own items, I mention this as I sometimes don’t even have room for my Insulin without bumping over bottles, but that’s not a problem here. The Housekeeping is excellent and unlike some Hotels very much not in your face or way, it all seems to just happen effectively and efficiently without interruption, which is the sign of good housekeeping.
 
Our check in was early and done beautifully and we were offered a small package of water and some other items as a welcome which was a nice touch. Thankyou Manny, Jessica, Maecala and to all the front office staff, I love this Hotel and its your passion and friendly manner, the attention to detail and the extra checking done by professionals like Manny  that make this a home away from home and a truly lovely place to stay. I should mention that this is my second stay in 9 months and that I am a Platinum Priority Club member and I am very IHG loyal. But I also will write reviews on what I experience be it good or bad.  This year The Holiday Inn chain, celebrates its 60th Anniversary, I would like to thank them for letting me be a part of this by every wonderful stay I have ever had and all the special memories.

title: “Disappointed with the Sheraton”
text:
This was our third time staying at the Sheraton Hotel in Downtown Seattle and it was our third time being disappointed. Our first two trips to this hotel were both Christmas trips (2005 and 2006) and our last trip was during the last week of August 2007. 
The first year that we booked this hotel we called them directly (after booking our room with an on-line service) to comfirm that they were the same hotel that hosts the famous Ginger Bread House competition for the local chefs. Once we arrived to the hotel, we were very surprised to find that the hotel was not only in shambles from being under construction, but that they had moved the Ginger Bread houses to another location entirely (an imprortant fact that they forgot to mention when we were calling to confirm that the Ginger Bread houses were indeed going to be there). 
On our second Christmas trip we decided to try bidding on a hotel with priceline.com. We were a little disappointed when we found out that the hotel that accepted our bid was the Sheraton. We decided that we would look on the bright side though and give the hotel a second chance. We thought that there was no way that the hotel could still be under construction, but once again we were greeted with the confusion and mess of construction. The place was a mess and the Ginger Bread Houses were still no where to be found.
This last trip (and it will be the last) we tried hotwire.com for the first time. And once again we ended up with the Sheraton. I again decided that I would be optimistic and hope for the best. I can say that I was happy to see that the lobby and new tower were no longer a construction zone, but I was still very disappointed with the floor that we stayed on and the room we were given. The table outside of the elevator had garbage on it and the hallway had bits of garbage all throughout that no one bothered to clean up during our stay. The room that they gave us looked out into the alley and there was scaffolding hanging outside of our window all three days that we were there. Not at all what I would expect from a four star hotel. I think that their star rating should be brought down a notch or two. 
Needless to say, I don't think that we will be staying at the Sharaton any time soon.

title: “Excellent location, service and suites”
text: We really enjoyed our stay here. All staff, especially Amy Choi at the front desk, were cordial beyond any hotel we have ever stayed in, and we were treated like royalty. Room was fantastic and we had need for nothing.

title: “Wonderful service”
text: We had a family birthday weekend at the hotel and I must express my gratitude for the hotel staff making this a fantastic weekend. Our rooms were close together as requested, clean and with plenty of towels. The hospitality room was perfect for our group to celebrate in style and included plenty of counter space and sink. Mandy, at the hospitality desk helped to arrange everything and I credit her for this fun filled time. Thank you Crowne Plaza River Oaks!

title: “Perfect”
text: Superior rehab of an historic bank building. Microbrew pub in the lobby with great food at affordable prices.

title: “Fabulous Beach Location”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Surfer Beach Hotel in August 2004. It was WONDERFUL. The location was perfect -- it's on the boardwalk and just steps to the most popular restaurants/bars and great shopping. The room was recently renovated and was very clean and comfortable. We had a gorgeous ocean view and could hear the surf from our room. The hotel is just minutes to the Gaslamp, La Jolla and Coronado. If you plan to spend time on the beach -- and I'd recommend that you do -- bring your own towels. The hotel's complimentary beach towels were tiny -- we each had to use three in order to lay down.

title: “As a native Bostonian I was blown away”
text:
I grew up in Roslindale. I lived two doors away from The Public Garden on Arlington Street. I went to Boston Latin School and thought I knew everything there was to know about my hometown. 
XV Beacon exceeded my every expectation. 
Whenever I visit BeanTown, it is my new home away from home.

title: “Fantastic rooms, still working out a few service kinks”
text:
I stayed here while on a business trip in Denver as we were able to get a great introductory rate. My room was large and comfortable, decorated in a clean, modern style. The beds were extremely comfortable and there was a nice workspace in the corner as well. The best part was definitely the bathroom - huge double sink area, fluffy bathrobes, great towels and bath amenities, tv in the mirror so you can catch the news while you get ready in the morning, large soaking tub, and separate shower with extra large rain shower head - awesome! 
I ate breakfast at the hotel as well as one dinner. Breakfast was good but nothing amazing, decent service. Dinner however was excellent - one of the best steaks I have ever eaten. Service was a bit over the top but friendly and informed. The bar seemed to be something of a hot spot, very busy all nights I was at the hotel.
The few issues I would have with this hotel are small service issues that are likely just due to the hotel being new. One - some crumbs on the room floor were not vacuumed up over the course of three days. Everything else was spotless, so this stuck out as an oversight. Also, lobby staff was nice but I wouldn't say above your standard decent hotel chain. While this didn't really bother me, I could see how people who are used to VIP treatment might find it less "5 star" than comparable properties. I don't think I would pay the normal price to stay here, but it was certainly a great value for the price I paid and if I were able to get a comparable deal another time, I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Location, location”
text: This new hotel is very fresh and clean with the usual amazingly helpful Kimpton staff who did all they could to make our weekend stay special. The free wine reception featured excellent wines and the event was well attended in the trendy and beautifully appointed living room. The roof bar is so popular there are red ropes outside to hold those waiting to enter. We didn't check out that scene but surmise it is quite popular. Our room had a park view which was nothing special, but at least we weren't looking out on another building or the courtyard which sounded rather bleak from the description given during our booking. Valet parking is $40/night, but we used a local garage about 2 blocks away and it was $18/day (but no in and out privileges). The beds and pillows are fantastic and the bathroom has a nice long counter so we can all put our cosmetics out without crowding. Our 8th floor room meant we could hear, not too distinctly, the music from the 10th floor bar. Don't stay on the 9th floor unless you like to party! Great location for historic district (Liberty Bell, Independence Hall) and great restaurants, as well as metro stop.

title: “Very nice room”
text: Just finished a three night stay for business and was impressed with the hotel. As a platinum guest I was upgraded to a 17th floor room - large and nicely appointed! I appreciated the bathroom with a shower stall rather than a tub with a shower head. The bed was comfortable, my view of the mountains great, hotel staff friendly and accomodating. Took advantage of the breakfast as well as the nightly apps in the club lounge, nothing amazing, but certainly nice to have. Overall great stay and good value for the rate. Looking forward to another stay in September...two weeks this time.

title: “great location, shame about the shower”
text: the staff were friendly and helpful, and the room was fine and clean though alittle small, however the bathroom had no shelf space to put anything and the shower was awful just dripped out so had to have bath everyday! No upgrade or drinks even though on honeymoon which would of been a nice gesture. a good hotel if you want to party all night, but not for us as we wanted to see the sights so wanted full night sleep so could be out and about during the day, which wasnt possible due to pool party/nightclub noise.

title: “Soooo great!”
text:
First of all - my expectations were pretty high due to tripadvisor, but i'm happy to say, that there were met!
We were 5 adults and had therefore booked an 2 bedr. suite after seeing the cosy pictures of the poolarea. Upon arrivel, however, we found out that we were located outside the actual hotel (at a complex on the side) and were therefore a bit more alone. This may work out for some people and all though it was a somewhat peaceful street we still felt a bit left to ourselves (and the noise were quite heavy compared to our next room!). We arrived late saturday but after having a chat with the reception on sunday, we were moved inside the actual hotel to, again, an amazingly huge suite with plenty of room for 5!
The free snacks and drinks were super for us - it was so easy that you could just get a bottle of water on your way out to explore LA. It would take forever to list the pros of this hotel, but I'm positive that this won't be my last visit to the magic castle hotel! 
On the con side I should mention that yes - the buildings are not brand new but the cosy feeling is priceless and, in my opinion, nowhere to be found at fancy new hotels!
Thanks to the entire staff at Magic Castle Hotel - great job!

title: “Excellent NYC hotel”
text: If you book a three star city centre hotel anywhere in the world, this is what you will get. The fact that it's North America means that it is Room Only. Now that we've got that out of the way, it is worth staying at this hotel because the location makes many of the City's most important sights walkable. Five minutes stroll gets you to Grand Central and that has all the Subway lines if you intend travelling down to the World Trade Centre or the Statue of Liberty/Battery Park area. There are some very good restaurants near the hotel and it has a 'Starbucks' adjacent to the lobby. Two things are free; ice at the end of each corridor and tea and coffee by the Lobby bar in the early morning. The staff were friendly and helpful and, overall this is a fine place to stay if you're spending your time sightseeing. It isn't luxurious, but it is perfect for a few days' stay.

title: “Nickel and Diming”
text:
There's nothing that annoys me more about a hotel then surprise fees. This hotel is valet park only, so you're already paying $25 more than the rate. But then there's also an $11 "amenities fee." What are the amenities? A pool and slow internet. 
Resorts can charge a resort fee. But hotels that charge extra for basic services should just raise their rate instead of tricking the customer.

title: “Decent Hotel but NO wireless internet available in hotel rooms”
text: Stayed at this hotel for a business conference, so was very frustrated that no wireless internet was available in the rooms. Wireless internet is available on the first and second floor common areas of the hotel, but you get kicked out at 2am.
