Internet can be purchased in your room, via an Ethernet cable, but only one laptop can be hooked up at a time. But rather annoying to have to pay for the internet on top of the expensive hotel rates. Otherwise, decent hotel.

title: “Unique location, excellent choice for business”
text: Happened to pick this spot on a non-Orioles night...Camden Yards is across the street. The hotel is in the upper echelon of Hampton Inns. Location is fun - multiple bars/restaurants within walking distance and very cheap on non-game days. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Marriott Marquis Times Square, NYC”
text: Although rather pricey, This hotel is an excellent place to stay, especially if you are interested in the Theater.

title: “elpaso”
text: stay in elpaso hotel was very good... the room was good very clean bathroom 116 was a little bit slow running

title: “Beautiful view of the marina”
text: I had a lovely 4 night stay at the Marina tower at the Sheraton Marina Hotel. The rooms were fairly small but they were nicely decorated and comfortable. There are several lovely pools and restaurants, most of which have a wonderful view over the marina. I noticed that at the weekends, the hotel had movie nights by the pool. I thought this was a lovely touch seeing as there were lots of families with children staying at the hotel. There is a great fitness centre with plenty of equipment for a decent workout. There are about 10 computers in the lobby with fast internet access as well as a printer. This was really useful as I found that there are very few internet cafes in America. Be aware that there are two towers, Bay and Marina. We stayed in Marina tower which seemed to have the main facilities. The other tower is only 5-10 minutes walk away but the shuttle can take you there for free.The hotel is very close to the airport and runs a free and regular shuttle bus to the airport. The only downside is that the hotel is quite far from downtown San Diego. However there was a Bay Shuttle which provided unlimited service to various locations for $1. The service stopped at 8pm on weekdays and 10pm at weekends. I did hear from one of the shuttle drivers that they were trialling the service so perhaps check whether it is still running if you are planning on staying at the hotel. The staff at the concierge were very helpful, although there was sometimes quite a long queue especially as this is where you purchase the bay shuttle tickets. Overall I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Sheraton and will definitely be back if I'm ever in San Diego.

title: “Like staying at a friends house!”
text:
The staff at the Omni was fantastic. The front desk staff made me feel warm and welcome, upgraded me to a bigger room upon arrival, brought up packages that had been delivered to me on a daily basis and even called up to the room to see if everything was to my satisfaction. 
The room was spacious, clean, well decorated and had everything one expects in a 4star establishment. The only remark is I could hear voices in the neighboring room one night.
I was chilly and raining one evening and I stayed in and ordered room service. Despite all the extra charges typical of room service, for a total of $25 I had an amazing lobster roll with fries and coleslaw. It was fresh, delicious and very generous.
Also, if you register for the Omni Select Guest loyalty program, you get complimentary hot and cold beverages delivered to the room every morning and complimentary wi-fi, daily paper, shoe shine, garment pressing and more!
I can't say enough great things about this hotel and will definitely be back!

title: “First Class Luxury”
text: What an amazingly luxurious hotel! I loved the view, the comfort, the central location to everything. The front desk personnel were extremely helpful and friendly. Although they were very nice and tried to help, I wish the concierge would have been a little more in tuned with our requests for transportation and dinner. We wanted to eat at laid back places and use the street cars and cable cars as much as possible but they kept suggesting taxi's and very expensive/exclusive restaurants. Overall this hotel was a great place to stay!

title: “Perfect location, cosy and trendy hotel, a few shortcomings”
text:
One of the hotels perfectly located to visit New York off TimeSquare. I certainly appreciated the black and white trendy decoration perfectly illustrated by various contributor's pictures. 
The staff is very welcoming and that worked for me from arrival to departure. 
Now as i often do i will list what i liked and did not like so much. 
On the bright side: the decoration did it for me, It is rather dark but modern and i like dark as it feels cosy. The bedding is very good. Going to bed feels like diving in a cotton ball (maybe a bit too soft for who likes hard bedding). Very clean overall. Wifi is not too expensive ($10/day). Smokers will appreciate the patio - so much nicer than the sidewalk to indulge! Bathrobe in room, ok amenities. Many will appreciate the bar on premises. Minibar in room well filled ($5 for softdrinks if i remember well). Large flat screen and selection of cable channels (a bit of a pain that many of chargeable and not flagged as such : you keep browsing. But TV is not the purpose of a visit to NY ! ) . 
There are a few things that came short for me. The room was very small. A medium size luggage hardly fit in it. The closet is small and hosts the fridge, there were no drawers and i could not unpack. The door to the corridor could provide better shiedling from corridor noises. I could hear my neighbors come and go as if they were in my room. Otherwise rooms to the back of the hotel are quiet (no traffic noise - beware of construction works across the street these days though. They run thru the night on week-ends - typical of NY ;-). The water in bathroom has regularly been more warm than hot. I seriously lacked power plugs by bedside. And finally two things i found rather not welcoming : there is a charge of $30 per stay if you use the fridge for your own items, and no coffee machine in room, even on demand (first time for me in years of travelling to NY...). 
The hotel has 8 floors+penthouse. Do not expect a view, And target a high floor for some 'space outside your window'.
But do not let all that turn you down , I list to inform fellow travellers in case any of these really matter to you when making a choice. 
I would say it is a good deal for a short stay in the city and at that location. Surely a trendy and welcoming place.

title: “Sweet - but the help....”
text:
My husband and I stayed boutique hotel and loved the ambiance. However, the hotel manager
should learn to speak to the his employees with a civil tongue. While I was at the front desk getting my room key, he was berating an employee in a tone that was very rude and unprofessional. Guests should not be exposed to this kind of behavior and it had a negative effect on my stay.
I am not sure that I will be staying here again.

title: “Very hip and high energy”
text: Very cool and chic atmosphere. Be prepared for the nightlife...it's crazy!

title: “Wonderful Hampton Inn!!!”
text: We stayed in a King-bed suite in this very impressive Hampton Inn July 14-15th while on vacation in Charlotte to go to Paramount Carowinds (don't miss their flying roller coaster!). It is located right off I-77 in a business park setting, but there were lots of families there. The lobby has a small sitting area decorated in an African lodge motif, and the entire hotel is decorated in that manner. We had a HUGE one bedroom suite with a full kitchen, a GIGANTIC bathroom with a whirlpool and a shower, and a somewhat small bedroom with a king-sized bed. And our rate was only $88 per night...for a large suite!!! Our only complaints were that we wanted a rollaway bed but management could never locate one for us, and the first night we requested extra pillows and a blanket but were told that the hotel was full that night and there were none available! Other than that, we were pleasantly surprised at this Hampton Inn & Suites. The FREE breakfast was great...not just rolls. There were biscuits and gravy, pancakes to heat up, bagels, cereal etc. All of this was taken care of by a very pleasant lady. Two big screen tv's were located in each corner of the main dining area. There was a manager's reception the first night we were there which we have only experienced at Embassy Suites. There were lots of good snacks, but the drinks were cans of beer and soda pop... but still an unexpected treat!! The staff was pretty nice and helpful. The hotel does provide a shuttle to the amusement park if you make a reservation. There is a brand new Ruby Tuesday restaurant right across the street, and many other chain restaurants just a few freeway exits away. There is a very nice pool that is thankfully in the shade in the hot afternoon. And the restrooms on the main floor look like something out of Las Vegas. I noticed a small exercise room and laundry facilities, and our floor had a pop, snack and ice machine. We all enjoyed our stay here and would highly recommend it to travelers to Charlotte!

title: “Low Budget for price”
text: My husband is disabled and I had written a request when I booked the room for a ground level room. I booked our room early in the season so there was no excuse for them not giving us a ground level room. Of course when we arrived they could not give us a ground level room "because they were booked 100%". They did have a filthy elevator that we had to use to get to our 3rd floor room. The room was sub par. I have been in much nicer rooms for much less cost. Every time we left and returned to the room we would have to turn off the AC because it kept defaulting to 66 degrees. It was moist and cold and smelled moldy in the room every time we came back. Also saw homeless defecating behind the hotel. We would never stay there again!!!!!

title: “Great LQ and great value”
text: I am a review reader so I did alot of reading before I decided where to stay. This LQ was an excellent stay and great value. The room was a king and very large. The room and bathroom were both exceptionally clean. OHHHH, the bed...very comfortable and so were the pillows. We travel all around Texas and I will definitely stay at this one again. I can not comment on the breakfast as when we went to check out and eat the dining area was full and we needed to get on the road. I love the fact that they have nicer bedspread, not the horrible flower quilted things most have. Nice flat screen tv also. The staff was quick and friendly at check in and check out.

title: “Comfortable Room”
text:
Saw a good deal US$174 (Fairmont Exterior Queen/ Queen) on expedia & called the Hotel to match price.
Line-up in front of Fairmont Member check-in counter was long, as everyone seem to be member now. The only privilege left is free internet usage. Requested for early check-in but room was not available on arrival.
When we went back to check in after dinner, the Front Reception gentleman was very cheerful & hospitable, significantly different from the lady in the morning.
The room was big and comfortable, with a huge walk-in closet.
There is no convenience store nearby. If you need water etc., remember to buy some before going back to the hotel.
Overall, an enjoyable stay.

title: “Outstanding Service, Excellent Location, OMNI magic”
text: I stayed here over New Years Eve. This was about my 4th time staying at this hotel. The staff are extraordinarily friendly. The hotel and rooms have a lovely old classic charm. While the hotel is dated, it is impeccably clean and renovated, and the age gives it a nice character. It has the OMNI magic all over it and what keeps me coming back to this location. The security was tight over NYE and they made sure all persons entering the elevator were guests that evening, which helped me feel safe. You get a great room for a great price, while receiving impeccable customer service. Make sure you join select guest so you get the free internet, free pressing/shoe shine, and your favorite beverage delivered to your room every morning! Love this hotel!

title: “Basic accommodations at a reasonable rate”
text: Very convenient location right off Broadway.Definitely not a plush hotel but adequate.

title: “Nice hotel for the price”
text:
Booked this on Hotwire and was very pleased for the price I paid. The staff was very friendly. The room was huge and not just by NYC standards. We had a corner room that had several windows, a small kitchenette and plenty of room to spread out your belongings. The bathroom had beautiful old marble and had that old NYC feel but when I say "old" I do not mean in a negative way but an historic way. There was a pleasant outdoor terrace on one of the upper floors that was a very nice surprise. It was fun to stay in clean but historic hotel that kept many of the details of the past.
Good fitness center with nice equipment with TVs.

title: “History at a cost!!!!”
text: Famous hotel with less than professional standards. Cell phone was missing/stolen from room during our stay. Reported upon leaving, two days later, management had "NO RECORD". Four weeks later after several phone conversations to the hotel to determine what had been done and requesting an insurance claim be placed, they said they would take care of it. I was never contacted again. Room cost over $300 and the curtains were filthy, rug tattered. History at a cost!!!

title: “No place to hang your clothes!”
text: I'm a fan of Kimpton hotels and this one, like others, has great style. This isn't one of their best, though. This is the first hotel room I've ever been in that didn't have anyplace to hang up my clothes - no closet, no wardrobe, no nothing. Which was definitely a bit of an issue as I was in town on business and had jackets and pants that needed a hanger. For that reason alone, I probably wouldn't stay here again on business. I would definitely recommend their Encore bar, though - great atmosphere and really good bar food!

title: “Nice location, adequate room”
text: Stayed here as a base for a relatives wedding. Our king room was very small, hard for 2 people to maneuver around the bed. The bathroom was especially small - very little room around the single sink for toiletries. We were at the end of a hall facing the front of the hotel and the property was quiet. Room rate included breakfast and the breakfast buffet was good. No extras at the property (pool, hot tub). Location was convenient for sightseeing and events around the wedding.

title: “TRY THE PANCAKES”
text: I stayed here on business, and was pleasantly surprised with the interior and level of service. The rooms are average with nothing outside of Embassy Suites Standard room, but the cook to order breakfast was fantastic. You have to try the pancakes as they something special here.

title: “The best”
text: Love this hotel; we always stay here the night before a vacation. Staff are friendly and accomodating, beds are very comfortable, quiet rooms. The restaurant and bar are pricey, but we generally don't eat dinner or breakfast at the hotel. The hotel has a security entrance into the airport, which is very convenient when travelling with small children.

title: “Convenient but noisy location”
text: We stayed here early August for our 10th anniversary. If you want to be central San Francisco to be able to walk to all sites then this place is perfect. I really liked the trendy lobby and setting but was disappointed with our room since it was much smaller than the photos suggested. There was no where to put our clothes and they did not even have hangers for our clothes. They were friendly and helpful at the desk and the free wine bar late afternoon was welcomed after walking all over this fine city. The noise from the street did make sleeping difficult but cannot fault them since thhates what happens with such a central location.

title: “A "thank you" card”
text: Nice and very clean. The first hotel to give us a Thank You card upon departure. Nice touch!

title: “A unique view of Times Square”
text: Great, trendy Hotel with a unique view of Times Square from their lounge. Very upscale and trendy with just the right amount of intimacy and comfort.

title: “Attentive Staff, Spacious Suites”
text: This is a great hotel for couples, singles, or girls' weekend. We had a corner junior suite, which was very spacious. The suite comfortable and they also have a Keurig, which is what we have at home. The service was great, from the valets to the front desk. We had the breakfast buffet, for the price you can't beat it. We also at dinner at the restaurant one night (I wouldn't recommend the calamari). All in all, good stay, excellent location if you want to shop at the Galleria Mall. It's trendy, and although I saw families there, I wouldn't bring young kids. We were able to get a great rate of $79 per night.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: This is a wonderful hotel right on the WATER. I believe it's the only hotel on the water in Seattle. The decor is a combination of lodge and contemporary but it works. I would recommend getting a water view room with a balcony. It's worth the extra price. Also, their restaurant is wonderful as well.

title: “Great value and location”
text: Stayed in this hotel for 4 nights at the beginning trip in the United States. After arriving from a 9 hour flight this hotel felt like a warm shower. The hotel entrance is hidden behind some of the rooms and from the outside it can not be separated from an average apartment building. When entering however, you know you have made a great choice coming here. Hotel personnel is friendly and the hotel lobby is cozy. The rooms have all basic amenities you need (including flat screen tv, an office, fridge). The hotel is a free printer available for boarding passes. The hotel's location is good; the Mall is accessible by foot and the subway is nearby. I liked this hotel best for its price; I payed only $100 per night and I recommend this place to everyone, as its price-quality value is simply great.

title: “Love this hotel”
text:
This hotel is great, the staff are so friendly with nothing being too much trouble. The rooms were so cool, floor to ceiling windows with views to die for, tv in the bathroom mirror, lovely shower, great bath. Great artwork on the Walls and around the hotel was stunning, the children enjoyed the outdoor pool & spa with great views downtown. This is my first stay at an Omni Hotel but it certainly won't be my last!
Well done for making my first trip to Dallas a great one!

title: “Stay Here!”
text: Super clean, inviting and had all the amenties you would expect from a hotel room costing 3X as much. Mr. Patel was both friendly and helpful. Walking distance to all of the downtown venues, and you can not beat the price!

title: “Solid Value, Clean Rooms”
text: Stayed here during a layover. Rooms are clean and comfortable. I really appreciated the free Internet and large desk. Ample sockets to recharge all of your electronic devices. They have items such as toothbrushes, razors, etc., for free at the front desk. I never had to wait long for the shuttle to pick me up. The only let down was the breakfast. A little bit too bread and cereal heavy. There are numerous fast food options surrounding the hotel, however.

title: “Nice Choice for Downtown - Wish they would try harder though”
text:
Recently stayed here for 3 night stay and overall was pretty satisfied. 
Got the basic room and it was definitely a cut above the standard NYC hotel room. Has all the bells and whistles of a NY boutique hotel room. (My particular room had a view of an alley, so a point off for the dreary view). Great Flat Screen TV where you could also access hotel info. Bed was really comfortable. Plenty of room to move around. Bathroom was well done in tile and glass. The shower logisitics are odd though. The only way in is through the glass door, and there is no way to "test" the water temp without going all the way in the shower and getting hit full force. Also, no door handle on the inside of the shower door, so the glass door slams shut and it's kind of off putting.
Maid service was very spotty. First day no service at all. I called down to the front desk at 5pm and was told housekeeping works til 6pm so no worries. At 6:30, I got a knock on the door for turndown service (Nice touch by the way) and they were shocked to discover that my room had not been cleaned. I had to leave the room for a half hour while they cleaned.
The next day I got maid service but no wAsh cloths or coffee for the coffee machine. Also no chocolate on the pillow for turn down service!!! Love that chocolate.
Some nice touches...mini cupcakes at check in! Free wifi.
Another area they really lost me though is the rooftop garden. At around 6pm they devote one of the elevators specifically to the rooftop bar. However, I suspect the bar isn't really "happening" as they would like, since there were never any lines for the roped off elevator with the smirking doorman. The lines were at the other 2 elevators where sweaty exasperated hotel GUESTS with luggage waited forever to try and get to their rooms. This is just silly and got on my nerves every night.
Also, the concierge SERIOUSLY underestimated the cost of a cabride to JFK.
Overall I think this is a really nice hotel, but they need to try a little harder to get near a level of someplace like a Kimpton Hotel. The devil is in the details and hopefully they will try a little harder, because there is much to like here.

title: “Awesome location!”
text:
The location is amazing for this hotel. It's right by light rail from the airport, up-scale shopping, plenty of restaurants and only six blocks from Pike's Place. I can't say enough good things. The staff were extremely helpful in getting cabs and answering questions in general. Rooms seem to have been renovated in the last few years, so up to date and very clean and a nice size.
My husband had to go to the Convention Center for business and it was literally one block away...so easy!

title: “Not the finest, but reliably good”
text: Depending on how luxurious your want your hotel stay in San Francisco, you can find more incredibly luxurious hotels than the Fairmont, but it continues to deliver in ways we find important. We stayed in the old section of the hotel out of choice- it has more character. First, we were able to get a really large, beautiful suite for less than any of the other Nob Hill or luxury hotels in the area. Yes, the furnishing showed a little sign of wear, but nothing was tacky, and the room was nicely decorated, and had that old hotel charm while still featuring enough amenities for us. What shone was the staff- friendly and efficient from start to finish, never pretentious- like they really valued our business. Everyone from the desk staff to room service to the valet was excellent. Staying at the Fairmont feels like coming home. What was the most impressive was how very quiet the room was! We were there over Labor Day weekend and feared noise. Though the hotel appeared to be full with many people checking in out front, we only briefly heard voices next door, and no noise in the hallways. The room service was incredibly quick every time, and the food was certainly better than many hotels we've stayed at. The Fairmont doesn't try to hard- there is no luxury 4-star restaurant on the premises (but tea in the Garden Court is lovely), no fancy spa, but the lobby is beautiful and still feels like a grand hotel. They seemed to really appreciate our business!

title: “clean, friendly and attractive”
text: This hotel was easy to reach from the interstate, staff was friendly, rooms and lobby were sparkling clean. In fact, the lobby was freshly mopped and smelled very fresh and sanitary while I was checking out. I did not have the free breakfast, but ate at Cracker Barrel which is right next door instead. But from what I saw, the breakfast looked attractive and ample. Even though it was a pet-friendly hotel, I did not notice any "pet" odor. I couldn't have been happier with this hotel. The rate was very reasonable also.

title: “Our Family Loved It!”
text:
I arrived at the Crowne Plaza in San Antonio after a 20 hour charter bus ride with 42 other family members! We stayed for a total of five nights and not one time did any of our group members find reason to complain. Check-in was a breeze; every staff member was attentive from the time we arrived to the day we left; and the rooms were clean, nicely furnished and ooooohhh so comfortable! One very nice touch was the sachet that each guest had in their room – it held everything needed to wind down for a peaceful night’s rest. 
In all, almost 200 of my family members checked into the Crowne Plaza for a three day family reunion. We used just about every amenity the hotel had to offer. Most of us ate from the breakfast buffet in the mornings - it was delicious. The swimming pool was a favorite gathering place in the evenings. And we even held our reunion banquet on the property. Everything was absolutely wonderful. Great accommodations, great staff, great food! Wherever our next reunion is held, I hope the reunion committee chooses to stay at a Crowne Plaza!!

title: “Nice hotel with nice amenities, but HORRIBLE STAFF!”
text: Our boss is very concerned with our safety so pays for us all to stay at a hotel the night of our Christmas party. We stayed at the Magnolia last year and were treated like royalty, this year was a different story. My boss put alot of effort into making sure things ran smoothly with numerous call in advance to make sure we were not charged for the room, valet service was complimentary, and that the Maggiano's dinner package was "good to go". None of this happened and the staff could not have cared less about helping us. The lack of caring was incredible!

title: “Lovely property”
text: Booked a weekend stay at this lovely Marriott property and hope to stay there again. From check-in to check-out things could not have been better. And the price was right! We had a great sleep both nights and the breakfast was delicious in the restaurant. It's not far from the city but has a golf course, walking trail, large swimming pool, tennis courts, and plenty of privacy from the hustle bustle of city life. Really enjoyed it.

title: “wonderful dining experience in this hotel”
text: I was not looking forward to dinner as I had low expectations of "another hotel restaurant." As I also explained to my waitress, Narah Bradley, I do not like to dine in restaurants alone, which I had to do that evening. That meal turned out to be one of the highlights of my trip. The food was simply delicious, the staff were very attentive. I was having trouble deciding what to order, my waitress guided me through to a wonderful selection of salad, soup, and bbq pork sliders, which her wine recommendation paired with perfectly. The salad I ordered was new to the menu (with pear and walnuts). A manager came by to explain how it was prepared and ask how I liked it. As good as the food was, Narah was even better, she really made me comfortable--like I wasn't dining alone. Wonderful waitress, wonderful food, certainly NOT "another hotel restaurant."

title: “Watch Out for Cancellation Fees”
text: Echoing other reviews, I have to emphasize: Don't book at this hotel unless you are absolutely certain of your stay. I signed up under a draconian 55-day cancellation policy that left me aghast when I tried to cancel 1 room out of the 2 that I booked. Even though I was still staying at the hotel, fewer people in my group were attending, but the hotel was not sympathetic. They will charge you if they have the right. To me, this says they care more about their bottom line than creating a good experience for their customers.

title: “Great getaway, great value, great location, and great hospitality”
text: we loved it there...and that woman overseeing the breakfast buffet with the russian accent is a keeper....hard workers, friendly, please let her know how much we appreciated her making us feel at home. she has dark hair and her basement flooded last weekend, but she is great and is a great ambassador for Residence Inn....she made me blueberry waffles that were great and i saw how she interacted with everyone. you are only as good as the people who work for you and she along with the others were top flight and professional and friendly and fun....the valets, the desk people, the housekeepers all were so much fun and so helpful. but please thank the breakfast lady who never stops moving. thanks again for a great visit to chicago . we will be back at your hotel...I promise.

title: “Great Location, friendly staff”
text: The hotel is in a great location with basic amenites including a swimming pool. Very close to the state capitol and sixth street w/restaurant and music venues.

title: “A perfect place to treat yourself to a theater weekend in NYC”
text: I took two teenage grandchildren for a birthday celebration weekend. This hotel is convenient and the staff is efficient and helpful. Lovely treat.

title: “Right by the ZOO!”
text:
We stayed at the Balboa Park Inn during the month of March. It was a beautiful time of year.
The staff was super friendly. We stayed in unit 23. I called to book and told them we had a 3 month old. They put a pack and play in the room for us. They also put a hair dryer in the room so I wouldnt have to drag it cross-country. We had a 3 bedroom suite. It was PERFECT for us! The staff brought pastries and fruit everyday, coffee/tea was in the room. The kitchen was great for us since we had an infant.
We could walk to the San Diego Zoo, couldn't be more then 1/2 mile away. The area is across from a school however we never heard any commotion. It's a very convenient location. 
They have $99 rooms, and the price is right!

title: “Love the Pacific Terrace”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Pacific Terrace Hotel October 29 & 30 and again on November 5th. The stay was very relaxing, as usual, the views from the oceanfront rooms is spectacular, especially at sunset!! The first leg of our trip we stayed in Room 319 which has the best afternoon sun!! The only thing that bothers me about this hotel at all is the charge for parking but even at that, it is convenient. Also, the elevators are a little flaky sometimes but it is only 3 floors so the steps are very easy to use.

title: “Excellent location, nice hotel, bumps in the night tho...”
text: All in all this was a great hotel in an excellent location. I was a little skeptical from the pictures, but am happy to say that they don't do the place justice. Our room even had a very sizable tv and surround sound system with full cable. Its somewhere between no-frills and deluxe. Free wi-fi, printing, coffee, tea and newspapers. Great dining recomendations and a very good rate (we stayed here on a special from hotels.com with our third night free). My only solitary, really minor complaint is that our room was next to a housekeeping closet, so every morning we would hear bumps while the staff rolled out the carts and vacuums. It wasn't bad enough to ask for a different room, just a bit annoying. Would highly recommend to friends looking to save.

title: “Saved by the great service”
text:
This boutique hotel is ok, but could be great with some updating. The staff here are exceptional....the concierge was so eager to assist with our plans and making reservations. Everyone from the valet to housekeeping greeted you with a smile. 
I booked two rooms, one for my husband and me, and one for my parents. Each of our rooms cost the exact same however, my parents room was very small, and the bathroom had a stand up shower with no tub that could use a serious scrubbing. Our room was much larger with a fireplace and a tub shower. The sink in our room was a little questionable with the dry wall behind it crumbling a bit from water damage, nothing a little caulk couldn't fix. I would only go back if I knew I would get the larger of the two rooms. There was a lot of street noise and noise from the people next to us. On the other hand, the location was excellent, and the staff was so pleasant, I was able to forget about some of the negatives.

title: “If the hotel find your valuables after you leave, they will never send them to you."”
text:
If you leave anything at this hotel, the hotel would never return it to you.
My family travelled to DC from NY metro area in April 2010, and stayed at this hotel.
After I returned home from DC, I found I had left my jacket in the closet of the room I stayed at. I called the hotel right away and the housekeeping lady found it for me and brought it to the front desk.
I gave them my credit card information plus the mailing address and chose "regular ground" as the shipping method, and the front desk employee promised she would maile it to me ASAP. For the next couple of months, I contacted the hotel over and over again to make the same request because they never returned it. Whenever I called, the hotel still kept it. Once, the lady at the front desk told me that she didn't have a box to put my jacket in so that she could mail (It's just a small casual jacket and I don't know what kind of a nice box they are looking for or even they need a box.) and wanted me to speak with the manager and transferred me to him. The manager never picked up the phone and I left voice messages so many times since then and never heard back from him. I even reported this to the Holiday Inn central customer complaint center and they eventually couldn't help me at all. Now, it's been fifteen months and I had already given up. However, I thought it's my obligation to let other travellers know about this.
Please never leave anything especially at this hotel.

title: “Convenience Central in Midtown Manhattan”
text: Conveniently located across from Madison Square Garden, a welcome and conveniently located refuge across from the train station, near everything. Recently desinger-renovated spacious rooms, nice views of the city on the upper levels, and very friendly and accomodating staff who take seriously the idea of making your stay as pleasant as possible. For the kids, King Kong stuffed animals greet them in every room.

title: “VIP treatment for special occasion”
text: When I made the reservation I mentioned that this was a 25th anniversary trip. The hotel responded to give us a memorable weekend. We were upgraded to a suite at check-in, roses were waiting in the room, and a bottle of champagne arrived later that evening. We felt very pampered and special. All of the staff were pleasant and helpful and seemed genuinely invested in making sure we were enjoying our stay. The wine reception was greatly appreciated, as was the free Sunday NY Times. Would highly recommend to anyone celebrating a special occasion. We'll be back for our 30th anniversary!

title: “Classy hotel”
text:
Beautiful hotel, great service( except for the bartender Sunday night who was a bit abrubt and impatient when i was deciding on my drink). We made the reservation in person while staying at another Seattle location and got a great deal. Executive suite with 2 twin beds for $299 with a $100 Visa gift card! 
Well appointed suite but no coffee maker in room. Hotel did provide a tea kettle at no charge when requested. Comfortable beds. Could hear traffic, even from the 10th floor though. Woke me up in the AM but I am a light sleeper anyway. Could hear some noise from adjacent rooms but not much. Doorman was very friendly and helpful.

title: “Awesome hotel for a couple to get away for a weekend”
text: My wife and I try to get away to a hotel once or twice a year. This time we picked the W hotel in Dallas, TX and it was awesome. We were unsure at first but got connected with one of the hotel staff that made sure our experience was special. We stayed in a WOW Terrace Suite overlooking Victory Park. The room was huge and the view was spectacular. I had coordinated a head of time to have some of my wife's favorite music and drinks in the room and it was all well prepared even for early check-in. The staff was very knowledgeable, courteous, and professional. Dinner at Craft was amazing. The food was excellent but the service was what set it apart. Great choice of hotel and dinner for a weekend away. Very thankful for the staff doing the extra things to make the night special.

title: “Hotel Giraffe is a hidden gem in Manhattan”
text: We travel to Manhattan several times a year and have stayed at various high end hotels. Over the past few years, Hotel Giraffe has become our hotel of choice mainly because the rooms are spacious, modern and very clean, the staff provide excellent customer service, and we like the amenities such as free high speed internet and in-room wi-fi. Overall, Hotel Giraffe is a good value. There is no restaurant on premises; however, there are plenty of restaurants nearby. The #6 Subway is conveniently located two blocks north on 28th Street.

title: “great location”
text: Booked as part of the virgin fly drive and what a great start to the holiday. Great location, on the waterfront. Boston's shopping centre, park, aquarium etc are all within walking distance. room was stunning. Food great and service excellent. It's not cheap, but then this is Boston! Just a shame the rest of the hotels virgin picked for us (superior package) weren't up to this standard.

title: “Great calm,relaxing, and quiet stay!”
text: Traveled here to attend a graduation and overall it was very relaxing. Check-in/check-out was good and fast. Cleanliness was good. Location of the stay was perfect for us since it was only a couple of minutes away to our destination. Value of the rooms was very good. Room itself was roomy. Now as for the sleep quality it was calm and quiet. Would definitely be returning back here if any other family or special occasions come up as well will recommend too.

title: “Great location”
text: A lot of people complain about the train noise but I did not find it a problem, I could hear them but they did not keep me up at night , great location across from the convention center and just two blocks from Petco Park. Only things that did bother me was the AC wasn't blowing cold enough for me and the bathroom door is on this auto close arm . Being picky now but a clock-radio with an iPod connection would have been great

title: “Nice stay at hotel rex”
text:
We just returned from 4 nights at the Hotel Rex. The best feature of this hotel is the location. It is easy to walk to the train, cable car, and a lot of dining options. The room was nice, but small. Nothing fancy. Bed, dresser, desk, and a standard hotel bathroom. The walls are thin, and there was a lot of street noise. Frommers recommended a room in the back to avoid street noice, but none was available for our stay. The room was clean.
There is no doorman, and someone can walk into the hotel and up the stars without being seen by the front desk. That being said we had no problems with security during our stay.
 There is a small business center with 15 min of free access a day. Front desk for the most part was very helpful. One hostess was rather aloof. But all were very helpful and knowledgable of the area.
The bar offered nice (but pricey)
 drinks, and the restaurant was very good. We had quite a bit of interaction with the chef. The food was great as was the service. 
Overall this was a nice stay. Not a destination hotel but a fine choice to stay in union square.

title: “Friendly Service, Quiet & Clean Room”
text:
What a terrific hotel! Super nice staff who treated myself and my associate very well, and a beautiful room! I even took photos to send to my family. I was impressed with how quiet the heating/cooling was. I slept well, and liked the size of the room. Nice ipod dock and TV. Clean bathroom and shower.
Down sides were the VERY LOUD garbage truck that came on Tuesday morning at 4 a.m.... and continued until 5 a.m.! Also, they were doing some sort of upgrade to the television, and I had few channels on night that I was there. When I had a problem with my ipod dock, I called for service, and immediately a service man came up. It was fixed quickly, and right afterward, the desk called to check on me. That was nice. There was no coffee maker in the room, but the coffee in the bar downstairs was fresh and delightful.
After I got home Sofitel sent me a survey about my experiences. I mentioned the garbage truck. Imagine my surprise when the next day I received a personalized response saying that they would address the problem! Honestly, I don't know what they can do about it. I mean, they have to collect the garbage, right? But I thought it was really cool that they actually read what I wrote.
My associate wondered if we were the only people on the floor because it was so quiet. We were next to each other and never heard one another, despite playing music and TV rather loud. That was remarkable! 
My associate had pet allergies, and that was a down side, since the hotel is pet-friendly. But luckily she didn't have any bad symptoms. They don't designate pet or non-pet rooms, apparently.
Overall, it was a very nice place, and I'd definitely stay there again.

title: “Comfortable stay.Food Menu can be worked on”
text: Went to NYC on work for 4 days.Good location.Helpful staff.Food options need to be worked on.

title: “Did not enjoy the stay”
text:
We arrived late afternoon, checked in , the phone by the bed did not work nor did the airconditioner. I called down to the receptionist to report a couple of problems only to get "yes" after I explaned the problems she said "okay". I finally asked her exactly what did okay mean? Would she be sending up a repair person or WHAT.
Finally she said yes. Okay we went out for about 3 hours came back and the room was warmer than before, I gues they fixed the air. I went down stairs to advise them the air still wasn't working properly. 
The repairman came back.
Needless to say it was the same repair man that had taken care of the problem earlier. He tried to convince us that he had fixed the problem
 1. He lowered the thermostat but the temperature in the room increased he argued that was normal
2. He said It usually take about 2 hours to cool off(we were gone 3 hours)once you adjust the thermostat.
I wentr back down stairs, this time the night manager was trying to explain how airconditoer systems work( I am from Florida trust me I know about airconditioners) 
Finally I demanded to be moved to another room. 
I went back upstairs with the manager, who shows up again the same repairman, by then I was in no mood to talk to him, so the manager told him to just go back down stairs and they'll discuss it later.
 Day 2 The cleaning staff did not leave wash cloths, had to call down stairs to get them.
3. Ther was no menu for the take out breakfast although there was a reference to the restaurant.
I donot plan to stay there again.

title: “Huge conference hotel with good facilities”
text:
The lobby of the Hilton Union Square is more reminiscent of an airport terminal than your average hotel. It is really enormous and constantly buzzing with people, usually including coachloads of in-coming and out-going foreign tourists and countless conference attendees. This gigantic public area has a starbucks inside, is filled with tables and chairs and offers free and fast wireless internet, so is a great place to pass time if waiting for a room or a meeting. The hotel is an easy 8-10 minute walk to the Bart station at Powell Street, from where it is a straight shot costing under 9 dollars to the airport (allow 45 minutes as there can be 10-15 minutes between trains at some times).
The rooms are perfectly fine and reasonably sized. What made mine on the 23rd floor particularly enjoyable to work in was the uninterrupted West-facing view over the city. I had a drink in the hotel's attached Urban Bar and that was a very pleasant place. Room service was very tasty and delivered fast and hot, but rather pricey I think. This is really a large business/conference hotel, for which it's fine, but I wouldn't recommend it for a family visit. For that, find something a little smaller and less frenetic.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: We were pleasantly surprised with our stay at Sofitel LA. The service was great, and we had a lovely meal at the inhouse restaurant. The rooms were spacious - we had booked a weekend deal that included an upgrade to a suite.

title: “Fabulous location!”
text: Stayed here for 3 nights around 4th of July. Booked at the last minute through Expedia and got a fantastic deal for this hotel. The location is ideal. Was able to check in at 10:30 a.m. on a Wednesday. Although our room had 2 double beds, it was non-smoking and overlooked the Riverwalk. Very clean and every staff member we passed always had a smile and was very friendly. Ate breakfast at the hotel one morning (Chaps)- pricey (which was to be expected,) but very good. Didn't try the buffet, although it looked really good. Try Zuni down the Riverwalk for breakfast. Half the price - great breakfast tacos! Had a Corona from the mini-bar, I think it was $6.00. I was actually expecting it to be more. My husband used the gym, which was very nice. Lots of cardio equipment and was usually empty. The pool on the roof is small, but has great views. There is also a hot tub. The bar by the pool is open Thursday through the weekend. The techno style music by the pool did become annoying after awhile. The lobby bar wasn't anything exciting, but a nice place for a drink. The Riverwalk was very pretty, except after the rain when everything drains into it. However, the clean up boats were out shortly after the rains to clean up. Would recommend doing the Riverwalk boat tour and the horse and carriage rides, as well as seeing the Alamo, the Menger hotel, and The Tower of the Americas. But I would avoid the Trolley tour. One hour of driving through the not-so-nice parts of San Antonio neighborhoods. It does stop at some of the Missions though, if you are interested in seeing them. Everything is within walking distance of this hotel, even El Mercado. While there, ate at Mi Tierra which was a disappointment. Try La Magarita instead. Paesano's on the Riverwalk was good for Italian. Rio Rio for Mexican was OK. Had drinks at Jim Cullum's outside the hotel - very expensive!! CVS is practically next door, which was very convenient. The only issue we had w/ noise was our last night (4th of July). We did hear people outside yelling in the streets (we were on the 5th floor). However, it was a holiday and a weekend. During the week, no problems. Was able to print our boarding passes for free before we left. I would definitely recommend this hotel when staying in San Antonio.

title: “Great Cruise Hotel”
text: A great value, very clean and the staff was the best. We left our car at the hotel for free for the week while on our cruise.

title: “Fantastic location great hotel”
text:
We have just returned from our trip to the Grand Hyatt, NYC. We stayed from boxing day until new years eve. We ordered breakfast the first morning which was really tasty came exactly at the time we specified and the bill was so easy to deal with upon check out, speaking of which they allowed late check out (1pm instead of 11am) for free anything further there would be a charge however I'm unsure of how much the charge was. The hotel was cleaned everyday and we were given new toiletries & towels every day, the room was very spacious with a closet to store cases, iron and ironing board & also a combination safe which you can set yourself. There was temperature control in the room which we didn't actually need as the room was warm enough. We had a view of the street and grand central from our room and the window could open. There is a place to store your luggage upon check out if needed for $2 per bag - although I've never had to pay for this service any where else before I would rather pay $2 than carry my suitcase around all day! There were also some plug sockets in and around the lobby waiting area to charge phone etc which came in handy for us. 
If you go out the hotel doors to the right and go in the first doors to grand central station take the escalator down to the right - this will take you to the 'shuttle' which is a subway train (there are 4) that only run directly between Times Square and Grand Central which was amazing! We paid $29 for a 7 day unlimited subway pass from which we got our monies worth! This is my 2nd time in NY and I did not use the subway system on my 1st trip as I'm claustrophobic, however the trams are quite big and run so frequently they are rarely too packed to get on, you can get practically anywhere in manhattan in 15 min - journies which would take over an hour by any other means. We got so many things done by travelling via subway and having the shuttle next door was amazing! 
I can't fault the hotel and would %100 go back it was clean, comfortable, contemporary decor, and brilliant location - we had a great time!

title: “Nice place to hang out”
text: Stayed here for 2 nights to be close to my daughters high school for a special event. Location was very convenient and neighborhood felt safe. Hotel is indeed urban although I think I may have appreciated it more had I been younger and hipper. Pool area and rooftop terrace were the place to be - very cool areas to hang out. Service was outstanding from check in to restaurant staff. Rooms very comfortable, especially the bed. While not typical of a hotel I would normally pick, I would return again as I really enjoyed the vibe.

title: “Most economical on the I-77 South Corridor”
text: One of the two hotels where I put up my out of town guests. Comfortable, clean and convenient.

title: “Nice Place”
text:
Flight from Vancouver to San Diego: We booked through Allegiant Air - out of Bellingham. Parking is $10.00 a day. You are usually stuck with mid week flight. You have to pay for carry on (if it won't fit under you seat in front of you) or check in luggage - $35.00 each bag, each way. Still cheaper than other Airlines out of YVR and Allegiant has direct flights with fairly good flight times. We used "The Dana's" shuttle service which was $6.00 each person 1 way & $7.00 each going back to the airport. Just call The Dana when you get off you flight!
Accomodations: The Dana on Mission Bay - 40% off sale. (Nov. 15 - Nov 20) Originally was looking on Expedia, but after looking at The Dana website it was hard to tell which room type you would get through Expedia, so we booked direct. They have an older side, which are smaller standard size rooms on 2 floors & most do not have outside seating. I think they all come with microwave, bar fridge & coffee maker. If I had my choice I would ask for a "Garden View" on the bottom floor - they had a private little patio outside, or a "Pool View" if I was taking kids.
We stayed on the newer side where the rooms are almost double in size & have a kitchenette with a bar fridge, microwave and a 1 cup coffee maker that came with 4 coffee's & 2 teas every day, along with plastic bowls, plates & cutlery. We had requested 2 queen beds as there were 3 of us. I slept on the pull out bed which I found very comfortable. The rooms all have large patio's with 1 lounger & 2 chairs. 3 stories high with an elevator. The Dana offers free shuttle to SeaWorld which is 5 minutes away. Otherwise a car is recommended and The Dana does charge $18.00/day for parking. They gave it to us for $10.00/day as we were staying for 6 days. The only negative was I found the bridge traffic a little noisy when sitting out on the patio on the newer side & no beach area - but nice path to walk along and pools & hot tubs were heated.
Food: Tried the Duck Taco's at the Firefly - different & tasty. The other restaurant is more everyday & more variety. Fish & Chips excellent. Breakfast's good. Calimari with a red sauce - not so good & we told them so they could improve for future guests!

title: “Renowned Landmark”
text: The revamped Roosevelt Hotel, host of the first Academy Awards in 1929, coordinates two L.A. aesthetics: a renovated but darkly haunted historical relic connected to a mod, pool-encircling glass inn. Mainly due to service glitches this hotel has taken a beating in reviews, perhaps understandably. (My telephone inquiry to the concierge about taxi fees was left unanswered). It is also true that The Roosevelt stands at the epicenter of clueless tourists adrift in Hollywood kitsch. It annoys to have the celebrated lobby partially cordoned off for private parties. But where else can one stay with a reasonable rate at an architectural icon to lounge on leather divans in the lobby? Is there a more ornate gallery ceiling in the city? Guest rooms are stuffed with libraries of obscure but up-and-coming style magazines and are decorated with photos of little-known cult stars. If you choose, you can have urban neon reflected into your room from the Roosevelt billboard or the Grauman Theatre but go down to enjoy bamboo and palm trees at the pool. Walk over to Hollywood and Vine to replace tourist food fare with ethnic fusion. The Coffee Bean next door offers penetrating Wi-Fi and you will find transportable cheap fare from the “Fast and Easy” market a half-block over. The hotel has its share of ripoffs ($3.50, I was informed, for using the in-room coffee maker once) and bargains (gourmet lunches in the main restaurant, free New York Times). As in many renovated cornerstone hotels, the rooms’ baths are cramped. Overall, a unique, worthy option if the internet helps it to meet your price point.

title: “Wonderful experience!!!”
text: We had a wonderful experience with this hotel the moment we walked in. The door man was very helpful helping us with our bags (and getting taxies when needed). We arrived about three hours early for check-in but to our surprise we were able to check in early and to top that off we were given an upgrade. The front desk clerk was so helpful and nice she was very personable and wonderful. The concierge was very helpful in suggesting places to go and providing a map and places to eat. (There is a great Italian restaurant one or two blocks from the hotel good food and bogo free martinis after 5) The room was comfortable and the beds were soft. The location is wonderful close to everything you can imagine. Central Park, Top of the Rock, 5th Ave, Broadway and MOMA are only blocks away. I would defiantly stay here again and would recommend to everyone traveling to NYC.

title: “Great Value if you get a good deal!!!”
text: The Renaissance New York Hotel 57 was a great hotel and a tremendous value. My wife and I stayed there for a weekend in April and I got a room for an incredible price via their website. The location was great and close to several subway lines. The room was extremely small (just a full size bed) but was definitely modern and nicely maintained. For the value, I definitely give this hotel five stars.

title: “Modern, Hip, Convenient and Reasonable”
text:
I took my teenaged daughter and her friend to New York City for two nights the week before Christmas. We stayed at the Yotel and had a fantastic time. I reserved a three-person room (double bed plus a bunk over the bed). When we arrived the reservation was not in the system, although I had the print-out -- so they gave us a four-person handicapped accessible room instead. Our room had a double bed plus a set of bunk beds, and lots of space, possibly because it was handicapped accessible. The double bed was quite comfy although it was a platform bed (no box springs). The girls reported that the bunks were comfy as well. 
We were on the 18th floor with a fantastic view. There was minimal street noise -- only heard sirens once. There were room-darkening shades but we chose to sleep with the shades open, for the view. There was a frosted glass door, open about a foot from the bottom of the door to the floor and a foot from the top of the door to the ceiling, between the bedroom and the bathroom. If you needed noise for privacy, you could always turn on a faucet. There was only a very small ridge between the bathroom floor and the shower floor, although that could have been because it was handicapped accessible. There was a shower curtain separating the shower from the rest of the bathroom. Water pressure was great and the heated towel rack was a nice luxury touch. There wasn't much storage space, but everything was very cleverly arranged. For example, there were little storage bins next to the wall-mounted flat screen tv. There were plenty of outlets for phones and laptops. 
The breakfast (muffins, coffee) was adequate although juice was not complimentary. The wifi was free and strong. There was "hip" music in the elevators. The robot that stored our luggage was entertaining, and it was nice to be able to store our luggage after check-out. 
The location is very convenient. We came on the bus, and the Yotel is only about five minutes' walk from the Port Authority bus station. Times Square is about ten minutes' walk away. If you forget anything, there is a CVS across the street. 
We had a very enjoyable stay at the Yotel and plan to return.

title: “Great service, nice property”
text: I just stayed for three nights on a business trip and was pleasantly surprised with the quality of this Comfort Inn. It had free WiFi and breakfast. The location made it convenient to walk to everything downtown. The employees were all on their toes. Not a single misstep there. The fitness room had nice, new equipment, free weights, cardio machines, etc. Very clean with ice water, towels and fruit. My room was one of the newly renovated corner king rooms. I highly recommend for the view and the clean, contemporary design. The bathroom also was updated with a large shower and glass door. It was very comfortable, even for someone with back issues. The only little thing was the temperature in the room was hard to get right... it was too hot no matter what I did. An engineer came up to fix it, but wasn't able to. (That's the four-star). Room service came from the Brown Hotel attached by skywalk and was excellent. So all around a great stay with all positive interactions with staff from the front desk to housekeeping! True professionals.

title: “Brand New Sweet Hotel”
text:
Hotel is very nicely decorated and in a decent location! Our room smelled fresh and NEW!! We walked to Camden Yards, about a 15 minute walk. The Aquarium is even closer, maybe 5-10 minute walk. It really wasn't too bad to get to Camden yards down Pratt since you can stop at the waterfront shops and there are plenty of places to eat between the hotel and the aquarium. 
Really liked the new shower, it had an overhead ceiling faucet, lots of pressure. Modern decorations and a giant tv. The bed was very cozy and I would definitely go back again!
The parking was a bit expensive ($27), but it was valet and they did come back with the car pretty quickly. The front desk staff could do a better job of listening to their customers, they tended to interject with their co-workers conversations (went up to the desk 3 times and each time similar circumstance), there was a bit of chaos as a result.

title: “Clean and Adequate”
text: Spent two nights at the Broadway Plaza. We arrived a day early, and while the hotel had rooms available, they wanted to charge $55 above the rate we had confirmed - so, we spent one night at the Edison (who accomodated us at the last minute) and two nights at the Broadway Plaza. The front desk was businesslike, and neither added or subtracted anything from our stay. The concierge Richard is very friendly and helpful. The room was clean and comfortable. Long waits for elevators is routine. Breakfast was nothing remarkable. Broadway Pizza next door serves a very nice breakfast for under $3.00. Subway is convienient. We did not like the neighborhood at all. Loud, vulgar, sweaty people crowd the sidewalks. It's not that we felt unsafe, it was just unpleasant. Plus, this hotel is not close to much of anything. But, that's why the price is so reasonable. Overall, we liked the Edison better.

title: “Clean and affordable”
text: It's by no means a top of the line motel but for the price it's fantastic! I wasn't expecting a luxury visit, just a place to bunk for the night and the Days inn fit the bill! Definitely worth the price and what not, the park and fly features was great too. Check them out!

title: “A pleasant surprise at a prime location”
text:
You'd expect a hotel at such a lovely location to either charge the hell out of your pocket, or provide you tiny rooms with bad service. Surprisingly, there is not compromise on either of those.
Rooms are comfy, very effective for the business traveler that also wants a walking distance from good shopping, bars, restaurant and lively Chelsea.
Free internet, good TV, morning papers and a cosy bed is what you'd look for in much more expensive hotels.
People have this prejudice about the lousy service level in New York. This hotel breaks this prejudice. Staff is very courteous.

title: “"Unforgettable Memories"”
text:
My husband and I had our wedding at the fabulous Grand Del Mar on April 18th 2009 and what a great time we had. Everything was absolutely amazing. Not one complaint. Our friends/family couldn't stop ranting and raving about how beautiful everything was. The staff is phenomenal. Every five star hotel should offer this kind of service.
Mr. and Mrs. Washington

title: “Good value, good location”
text: We (3 adults, related) were in Boston for 3 days of sight-seeing, looking for a not-too-expensive place to stay. This hotel is good value-- for Boston. We ended up sharing a room. It was a little tight-- the best they could give us was a room with 2 double beds. They said it was a fire hazard to have an extra cot in the room, so we made due. We bought the package that includes breakfast and wireless internet service. Staff were friendly, helpful, and we liked the location-- a very short walk to a "T" stop, which we found convenient. Breakfast was excellent, although it involved waiting in line to place our order, so don't be in a hurry if you want breakfast or coffee. You walk into their little store and order it as carry-out, giving them your coupon, or paying for it. Then eat it in a section of their lobby set up for dining In the pet peeves department: hotels that do not offer free coffee for guests in the lobby in the morning. All in all, we enjoyed our stay at this hotel and would stay there again.

title: “Recent stay”
text: Great friendly staff, well appointed room. Upgraded bathroom a real treat. Location great and the Lola restaurant is not to be missed.

title: “couldn't sleep due to a very noisy heater”
text: The room in this hotel is fine in general. The beds were nice and firm. They also provided free wireless and club access with continental breakfast. However, there were two big minuses in my opinion: 1) parking was only available via valet and was expensive ($35/day); 2) very noisy heater that shook the room as it started and stopped. It was so loud that I kept waking up at night. A call to the engineering department didn't help as this was apparently "normal". For the next day, I resorted to turning off the heater/fan although I had to wake up in the middle of the night to turn it back on for a few minutes as the the room got really cold. In my opinion, it doesn't matter how nice the hotel is but you have to be able to sleep through the night. Sadly, I can't really recommend this hotel unless they change the heater unit to a more quite one.

title: “Beware of the fishbowl!”
text:
I stay at the Hilton Anatole every two weeks on Friday night.
The hotel is basically ok, but everyone should know to avoid a certain room they have on every floor in the tower which is essentially a fishbowl. There are no windows to the exterior of the building, all windows are on the corridors, and you can hear people passing by and the elevators all night. 
Second problem, on certain floors and not necessarely in the tower you can hear loud music well into the wee hours of the nigt because they have a bar and disco. It's impossible to sleep.
Thid problem, but this is common to all Hilton hotels I have visited: their beds are so soft, I always wake up with an aching back.

title: “Relaxed Luxury”
text:
If you're planning a trip to Los Angeles, the W Hollywood is the place to stay. 
The hotel is not only chic but friendly. A rare combination. From the moment we entered we were treated as favored guests. The staff was always available to answer your questions and to offer help if needed. 
Our room was immaculate and the bed was very comfortable. It made it easy to sleep well and wake refreshed.
There is free internet access in the library/reception area and the Delphine Restaurant offers delicious entrees and once again great service. Highly recommend the chocolate cake. :) 
Enjoy!
.

title: “A good deal”
text:
After kicking around all the possibilities for a one-night stay @ the airport, we went with this hotel based mainly on price ($85). It was the right choice.
The staff was helpful, and the room was clean, quiet and modern. Free continental breakfast was fine -- coffee, cereal, rolls, juice, fruit.
The shuttle service is good, too. The morning we planned to leave the hotel, we had to go to one of the off-aiport rental car places and weren't sure if the shuttle would take us there. The driver who picked us up at the airport when we landed assured us it would, and sure enough the next day another driver dropped us at the rental car spot after making the rounds at the airport to drop off other passengers.

title: “Convenient location”
text: The hotel itself is very nice, clean and convenient to the convention center, exactly what you need and expect from an Hampton Inn. The area surrounding the hotel is not the most visually appealing but just a few blocks in any direction and you have a plethora of great restaurants and things to do. Self Parking is a giant jigsaw puzzle! Opt for valet and splurge on the extra $10.

title: “Welcoming Culture”
text: I have stayed at this hotel several times. A recent business trip from Phoenix had a significant flight delay, placing me at the hotel tired and crabby at 12;30 looking at a 4;30 wake up call for a long drive to tallahassee. Know that I am a diamond level hyatt member and stay at high end properties typically. I have never been greeted in such a welcoming manner. Pleasant conversation, my door card was printed and ready to go, and a freshly warmed large cookie and a cold energy drink. Mgmt must be behind this comfortable culture. My congrats and thanx. A special thanx to Theresa for caring and have such a passion for service. We even got into a short conversation about animals and strays. Most of us these days, especially business travelors who are away from their pets, shares a common interest in helping pets find homes. This place hires people like that. It rubs off. Would stay here again. Clean, fresh food ready to eat, great quick coffee, flat screen tvs and comfortable beds. Quick and easy no matter what the price (a bargain too!!).

title: “Great Location and a Good Value.”
text:
My wife and I stayed in this location for a short business trip. The property is larger than most Residence Inn locations. The grounds are fully appointed and very clean and well maintained. I did have a bit of trouble finding the elevators as it is such a large property and all the halls look the same it made navigation a bit difficult. They do have multiple entries that allow you to park quite close to your room no matter where it is located.
The breakfast is typical of this chain but this location I felt was a little above average in cleanliness and presentation. Overall, we had a comfortable stay at a very reasonable price. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “V good airport hotel”
text: Very easy to find, 5 min drive from airport, they have shuttle service. Complementary breakfast is nice, small, but good produce. The rooms are big, bed V comfy. For an airport hotel this is one of the best. Parking is just out front.

title: “Large, clean, and convenient.”
text: While planing our trip to New York, my son, who lives there suggested we stay away from the noisy and pricey Time Square area. He suggested the upper west end. I found Hotel Beacon on Trip advisor. We were very happy with our choice. The staff was helpfull and polite. The room was clean, had a great veiw, and with a separate bedroom was quit large. We took advantage of the kitchen and ate breakfast in. We loved the location. We walked to Time Square and back. We had easy access to the subway station. The hotel is close to Central Park. We walked from the hotel to the shops on 5th Ave. There are several restaurants in the area or you can buy food at the grocery store across the street and eat in. When we go back we will definitly stay there again.

title: “Old School”
text:
Booked this hotel through Priceline at $150 for the night because we literally couldn't afford our previous hotel's $465 a night price tag post Irene and our flights had been cancelled : (. After the ultra sofistication of our previous abode, the Algonquin felt like a 'real' hotel, hard to explain but it was strangely comforting. Room was small, bed super comfortable, bathroom tiny (and almost impossible to get into without physically out-muscling the sticky door), but the whole place was very endearing. We had a Manhatten (in Manhatten) in the Blue Bat and had a lovely chat with Mr. Cwong (??) who enlightened us about Matilda the hotel cat who I had previously thought was fictional.....she's not : )
Only downside was the hotel receptionist (Mr T- that's all I'll say) who was a bit burly and cursed a bit too much considering his job. Don't know if this is his normal demeanour or just because we were priceliners?????
All round? Comfortable (apart from the noisy AC - but Matilda does provide you with ear plugs :) :) :) ), great location and for the most part lovely staff.

title: “Excellent hotel for tourists!”
text: The Belevedere is in a great location - easy walking distance to Times Square, Rockefeller Center, etc., with lots of restaurants close by. The rooms are large by NYC standards and nicely decorated. (Note: beds are a little too firm.) The best thing about the hotel is the staff. They were all so nice and friendly and responded quickly to all of our requests (extra towels, information, cabs, etc.).

title: “tired hotel”
text: spent the weekend in NYC, second time at Hotel Pennsylvania. Must say I was disappointed. While the location is great, the hotel is tired looking and the rooms are dirty. Our hairdryer shorted out and started smoking, when we called the desk they said another one was in the closet. While that was convienient, why not remove the faulty on and decrease risk to the guest? The walls are peeling and there was dust in every corner. Also, we booked our room with another couple in January and requested rooms side by side...not! The staff are friendly and helpful, the hotel just needs some sprucing up!

title: “Beautiful Resort”
text: Beautiful Resort, beautiful, clean rooms with amenities and good hair dryer. Wonderful and professionnal staff. Good food and good service at the Firefly. Pool temperature just perfect. I am a travel agent and I rate this hotel a 4 1/2*. The only reason that I don't rate this hotel a 5* is because parking is not included in the price. I am a travel agent and I would recommend this hotel to my customers. I do think that a car is needed though. By the way, parking is free at Mission Beach.

title: “Lovely classic hotel”
text: We loved the location of this hotel - central to most things in DC.Lots of shops & restaurants around. We had an excutive king room, which was a very large room with extra comfortable space, flat screen TV, writing desk, 2 comfortable chairs. The amenities were at the high end of typical Marriott. There is a fairly casual restaurant & a coffee shop/bar - but no real upscale restaurant. The staff was helpful & professional. The only complaint we had is that the concierge lounge is not open on weekends, despite the fact that the hotel seemed quite busy.

title: “Unbelievable Service, Beautfiul Hotel”
text:
My girlfriend and I went for a weekend in Boston in June. We picked the Westin Copley because it was close to shopping and restaurants. We were blown away by the exceptional service and beautiful rooms. When we arrived after a two hour delay on the tarmac, we were greeted with a complimentary upgrade! They had lots of suggestions on restaurants, tours and shopping. The Hotel is connected to everything! My girlfriend and I are both very busy Moms, and the weekend away was just what we needed. I was able to go to the gym, get my hair done, have breakfast, all the while with smiling faces around me asking how they can be of assistance.
We also ordered room service - the food is exceptional. 
This is a superb Hotel and I would reccomend if you have a chance, you should stay here! I will be going back for sure.

title: “Stay away”
text:
We were forced to stay here since all the other hotels were booked in Houston. We previously stayed at the Bradford Suites nearby but that had been quickly snapped up by our relatives.
In one word: awful!
Room was dirty. Ants crawling all over the place. Dimly lit; I turned on all the lights in the room and I barely got 100 watts. Noisy from the road. Some guy started banging on our door at 5am! Outside door was peeling away or someone had previously jimmied it open; I couldn't tell. The towels were like sandpaper. Bathroom poorly lit and dirty. The tiles were held together with silicone that went all the way up the toilet to cover some crack.
My wife was crying because the place was so bad. My brother's family also stayed there and when we talked to his wife she said that she "was not impressed" and then shot a look at my brother who had picked the hotel.
The breakfast was cereal and some coffee and that is all they had.
Oh well ... all I can say is ... we stayed there one night and made it out alive and didn't pick up any cockroaches along the way.
For some reason, college kids must like this place since there were a lot of young girls bouncing around all over the place.

title: “Great location”
text: My wife and I stayed here for 3 nights and first off the main thing they've got going is the location, it cant be beat! Close to everything. Upon arrival we were asked if we'd like an upgrade to a room double the size of ours for around 30$ a night. We are glad we did as I've read reviews on the others! Room size was good and they've been recently renovated, although it looks like they just painted over old stuff and put in some fancy furniture. Now I don't really care about that sort of stuff in a hotel but it was obvious it was rushed or done cheaply so I thought I'd mention it. I know it is an old building but our room on the top floor had a massive, I mean massive, lean to it! We actually laughed when we walked in! We didnt care though, added character. Also as previously said by others the noise can be pretty bad if you are a light sleeper. Even with windows shut. It actually sounds like you have them open when they are shut it's that loud. You can't really help it too much with a cable car at your doorstep! Personally I actually like the noise so I couldn't of cared less. All up good hotel, good service, free wifi, best location. Couldn't ask for more. 8/10

title: “Convenient location”
text: The hotel is in a great spot for visiting the Fisherman's Wharf area. As suggested in other reviews, we requested a courtyard view room and it was quiet. When we arrived the receptionist said the room we requested was not ready, but we could get into another right away. When we said we would wait (to get the quieter room), Low And Behold, there was a room available right away. BE SURE to stand your ground if you have specified a particular room!. As said before, the free wine reception in the evening is Two Buck Chuck, drinkable, but certainly not anything to write home about. The Safeway across the street is convenient for snacks and sweet rolls. Got some rolls each night to have with our coffee in the morning. There is a great bookstore next door if you run out of reading material and also a Cost Plus store (didn't go in, but they usually have some great wines for reasonable prices if you want to pass on the two buck chuck). The room was very clean & adequate size. Bed a little soft. Parking is pricey. If you are a AAA member, be sure to get the discounted price.

title: “Worst check in I have EVER experienced!”
text:
Booked a four night stay at the Wellington for my 21st birthday present with my Mum back in March. We were so excited to be visiting New York (and any area of the US) for the first time. Little did we know we would be in tears within an hour of arriving at the Wellington...
Origninally, we had booked a standard double in the beginning, however, we later decided that because this was a special visit for my birthday we would see if we could get an upgrade, so we contacted the hotel directly about a month before our visit and the lady was very helpful and told us the price (including price) and nothing seemed too much hassle for her, just that we needed to pay it on check in.
When we arrived at the hotel, we was met by an extremely rude receptionist, no 'hi', just a 'passport and credit card please'. However, my mother and I had left a wide amount of cards at home as we prefer to not carry them all about, so I thought I only had my debit card which I wasn't prepared to use due to the charges, so passed over my Thomas Cook Cash Passport card (which we was told we could use everywhere), the receptionist was not happy to accept this and refused to take it, with no valid reason or explanation. I then asked if I could pay cash, again she was not satisfied with this and become even more rude and talking to us like filth. In the end, I told her to forget the upgrade as we had never been told about the credit card during any correspondence with the hotel before the trip. Again, she was not happy and wanted a card on file in case of any charges, I then gave her my debit card (which I was promised would not be used unless we made any charges). We were then sent up to our room, with no help from the bell boys even though they saw us struggling with out bags.
The first room was a twin single room, which was revolting. It smelt damp, was very dingy and the paint was peeling off the window sill. By this time, my mum and I were so angry we rung up Mastercard who provides the cash passports, and were told that there was NO REASON why the hotel can't accept it as it is used like a debit card. By this point, I was fuming and rung down to the manager, who again was very rude and inconsiderate. I then looked through my purse to find one of my mum's credit cards which I hadn't taken out, so we decided that we would get the upgrade. So again, we carried all our bags back to reception and upgraded the room. This time, the room was amazing. 21st floor with a view of Times Square and a King Size bed. Was very happy, until 4:30am......
