I ended up getting a phone call from my Bank (Halifax) informing me of some fradulent transactions on my account, when asked what charges they were, the hotel had taken $40 which was successfull, and had attempted to take another $180 dollars(which was rejected thankfully by the bank) again for the hotel upgrade!! I was advised to speak to reception in the morning. When I did this, they then told me that when we had paid for the upgrade on my mum's credit card, the lady had not added on the tax so i then had to pay an extra $25 dollars for their mistake. I asked to see the manager again, and he was very rude and abrupt, so I begrudgingly paid it, but vowed to never stay their again. 
All in all, it was the most stressful check in I have ever experienced, and I ended up visiting the shop attached to the hotel to get advice on transport and things as they were alot more helpful and friendly. 
All this ruined the beginning of an extremely special holiday for us, which ended up with us in tears. 
The restaurant attached was good but expensive and got very busy during peak periods, but we always managed to get aa table within 5 minutes and food was always prompt. The location of the hotel was brilliant, 10 minutes to Times Square and 5 minutes to Central Park, and a Subway station directly outside the hotel. 
I will not be staying in this hotel again!

title: “Hobby Airport Place To Stay”
text: I have stayed here many many times. This hotel takes care of you. Sure this is not a 5 star hotel, but this is a hotel where you can sleep well and be very close to the airport. The staff is professional and the small breakfast is great.

title: “Great Bargain”
text: Hotel Tomo is a bargain- I got a great rate online and it's in a nice quiet neighborhood which is centrally located, easy access to bus lines. Rooms are large and clean. We had a room facing the inner courtyard which was totally quiet- a rarity in SF. The Anime stylings may not be to your taste but you're not living there permanently! I liked the deer on our wall! The staff was friendly and very responsive- our mini-fridge wasn't working and was replaced within 15 min. I agree the "High Speed" internet was awful. Better to go to a local cafe than torture yourself waiting. Bathroom was normal sized- I've never had a big bathroom in SF in any of the historic luxury hotels that cost twice as much.

title: “My "Pointe" of view...”
text:
My "pointe" of view is from a business traveler staying at the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak resort during the week before Easter (spring break).  Please keep that in mind as you read my review.  I'm sure I would feel differently if I were here with a family during this time.
 
Arrival and check -in on Monday evening was fast and efficient.  The place is HUGE and it is difficult to find the reception area.  Once we were there, it was all good.  The bellman will give you a map and draw directions on it as to where you should try to park to be closest to your room.  It worked out fine, and we (my colleague and I) found our rooms with no trouble. (Stay tuned though...it got interesting later when we had to extend our stay another day...)
 
We had king suites and they were very nice.  There is a living room with a pull-out sofa, a vanity area with separate toilet/tub, and a bedroom with a king bed.  Outside the bedroom is a small patio with two chairs and a small table.  The layout was good, and there was plenty of room to move around.  It would be a great place to bring kids as the parents could get some privacy with the separate areas.  There are doors between the living room and vanity area, and another door between the vanity area and the bedroom.  
 
There is a mini-bar, but it was locked.  I asked to have it opened and they brought a key right away.  It is just a fridge, which is what I wanted it for anyway.  Being away from home for a week, I needed a place to store food and beverages.  I was quite disappointed that there was no microwave in the room.  That limited my food choices a lot, especially since we were working long hours and I just wanted to eat a quick something and go to bed each night! They want you to spend money at their restaurants, I'm sure.
 
Speaking of food...my colleague and I went to the Hole-in-the Wall grill the first night.  It was decent food, but the prices are exorbitant here!  It would have been cost-prohibitive for me to stay/eat here with my family of five.  For example, the lowest cost entree on the menu was a $13 salad.  This was not a fancy place folks...just a burger-salad-chicken-pizza type place for the family.  Everything was expensive throughout the resort.  You can walk to at least 3 good places to eat in 5 minutes or less...I suggest you do that.  There is a sports bar called Ghallager's (didn't try it), an Italian place called Tutti Santi (mid-range price, good food and atmosphere) and a deli (don't know the name) all in the same place right there. We did the deli for lunch a couple times and they're open for breakfast too. The food at the deli was fairly priced and good.
 
There is a Mickey D's just down the street right next to a grocery store.  Also a gas station and a couple of banks nearby, as well as many other restaurants within a 5 minute drive.  Do not pay to eat at the hotel.  All of their food and drinks are way overpriced! 
 
Kids programming: they have a kids club where you can take them for supervised activities (kind of like on a cruise ship). The place is definitely kid-friendly! There were about a million of them there this week! Mostly little kids, but a few young teens also. Some people let their kids make noise outside in the corridors a bit late for my taste (as a business traveler). However, I do realize this is a resort and people were on vaycay, so not a big deal, I guess.
Pools looked nice...didn't get to use them, but we were assured upon check-in that all pools are heated (which was laughable to us because we would not have the opportunity to use them with our grueling work schedule). The river ranch pool looked nice, and they have a lazy river. The pool in the center of the main hotel area also looked nice. I think there was a swim-up bar there and there is at least one hot tub.
Parking was a bit hit and miss. When we were in building 2 (south) we had better luck with parking close to our rooms. The last night when we were in the north building, we couldn't find a decent spot. The place was full!
Hugeness of it all: It is a huge hotel! You can get lost trying to find an ice machine! They do have signs to point you in the right direction though.
No free internet: This annoys the heck out of me! We were at a smaller chain hotel the last time (a couple weeks ago) and they have free internet (wireless or with a cord), but the freaking Hilton makes you pay $12/day for internet (cord) in your room! This is yet another example of the nickel-and-diming going on at this place. Luckily work was paying, so I didn't have to fork over the cash. I guess they have wireless in the lobby if you want to use it.
Broken coffee maker/no coffee: My in-room coffee maker began acting up on day 2 or 3. I left a note and they did replace it, but left no coffee! I had to call that night to have them bring me some coffee for the next morning. They are really fast when you call for something, I'll give them that. Service is fast. Everything else in the first room worked well. The rooms in building 2 are more updated than those in building one. For example, the bathroom in building one was smaller and had no exhaust fan. The rooms had the same basic layout, but the room in building 1 was a bit smaller.
Pleasant decor and surroundings—very nice views if you can ignore the parking lot. Lots of flowers and trees. Rooms are tastefully decorated. The courtyards in the interior part of the hotel were very nice, with fountains and vegetation. Everything was kept very clean, inside and out.
They had super huge, thick bath towels. Much better than what I'm used to at the Hampton or other mid-range chains. Hot water was plentiful, but the water pressure could have been better. The bed was very nice and comfortable. Lots of pillows and very comfy.
 
OK. So, we were at the hotel from Mon-Thur for work. Checked out Friday morning, but had to stay an extra day. We re-booked an extra night. This is where it got bad. We got off work late (a little before 9:00 pm, after a 14 hour day of work). Check in was efficient. However, now we had new rooms and they were in building 1, whereas we had been in building 2 the first few days. 
My room was on the third floor and as I walked toward it, I saw two women entering my room! I looked at the key, looked at the room number, and it was the right room. I knocked on the door and asked them if they were guests in this room (weird question, I'm sure), and they said yes. I told them the hotel had just given me a key to their room. They were very gracious and invited me in to use the phone to call the front desk to let them know they f*^#-ed up. Turns out, they transposed the last two numbers. They told me which room to go to (really far away) and sent up a bellman with the right key. At this point I was really angry. I told the guy this was unacceptable and did not tip him. Felt bad about that later...wasn't his fault. But, can you imagine if I had walked into a room that was occupied with sleeping children on the sofa bed, or a couple on their honeymoon, or whatever? 
New towels—not to whine, but the next morning the huge fluffy white towels were brand new. That is good, except you need to wash new towels before using them! I had little white fuzzies all over me after using them!
Another positive was the good security on golf carts all the time. I never felt unsafe here. Well, some of the corridors were dark at night. But there were so many people around and the outer parking areas were very well-lit.

title: “Great location at the Wharf”
text:
The hotel was OK, with a great location at Fisherman's Wharf. The outsidearea of the hotel was cosy, and the poolarea was fine. Johnny Rocket is very close to the hotel, and the food there was great.
Rent a bike and ride over Golden Gate to Sausalito. Awsome trip! Go to the marina to watch the sealions, kind of cool. You can also see Alcatraz from there.

title: “Downtown Gem”
text:
This hotel is for those who need to be close to a downtown office or meeting, but want to be in a block that is quiet, convenient, and near several subway lines. Gild Hall fits that description well. Room is very nice; bathroom nicely done, although with translucent glass door/walls, if you are traveling with someone, the slight lack in privacy might be an issue. Otherwise, very clean, very comfortable. Nice little business center on the 4th floor; I used one of 4 computers in there, and so no 'wi-fi' issue for me, as reported by others using their laptops. 
Buffet breakfast is a little pricey, but a short distance away is a Starbucks (open at 7am), and a place called Earl's Court, which has Soupman brand soups, Billy's brand cupcakes, and a lot of other nice food/goodies.
Staff is excellent (particular Evan, one of the bell men - very helpful). I did not try the restaurant or bar, but looked nice.

title: “No, no, no!!!”
text: I am a german student. In September 2002 I stayed one night in the Allen Lee Hotel. This is a very dirty place. The building on the outside looks old, but acceptable. The lobby is not verry clean and it smells a little bit, but no problem. As a greyhound user I ask for the special rate of 39$ per night. The manager behind the bulled proved window accepted this rate. I was happy and went upstairs. On the way upstairs the look became worser and worser and the smell became stronger and stonger. Then I opend the door of my room. I could not believe it. Inside there was a lot of dirt and dust. The carpet and the chair were felty, on the walls were fungi and a dry and bad small was in the hot air. The bed was smal and very aged. The bed linen was dirty, the air condition was out of order and the TV and telefon were verry antiquated. Inside the mirrow I could not see my reflaction and the wash basin beneath the mirrow was in a verry bad condition. Inside the rom was no bathroom and the shower in the hallway or better (hellway) looked not verry inviting. For me it was not possible to stay there longer than one nigth. It is better to stay the nigth on a park bench next to the homeless. There you have fresh air and a clean surrounding. I have seen a lot of things on my travels in Equador, Costa Rica south and west Africa, but I have never seen such a unhygienic and dirty Hotel like the Allen Lee Hotel. Before I went inside my room the roomservice had just done there job and the next morning they came to clean up the room. I ask me, what they have done there? And this Hotel is placed next to the White House in the center of Washington DC the so called capital of the world. Unbeliveable!!! P.S. the Homepage of the Allen Lee Hotel is the highlight of the day, if you have spend there one night.

title: “A comfortable classic style place.”
text:
We picked a warm time to visit Denver with daytime temperatures over 105. We wondered if we'd be able to sleep. We need not have worried.
Our spacious room had very effective air conditioning with a comfortable bed and the room was quiet so we slept great. Our room faced an office building and the on-site "night club" on the first floor got quiet by 11:30 so our sleep not disturbed.
The room was not new but the furniture was comfortable and the large bathroom was well maintained and clean with a nice big shower, separate tub, and two sinks with counter space. 
As we ventured out we discovered lots of good shopping and saw quite a variety of restaurants. There is a large mall a few blocks away and a premium grocery store and the staff was helpful with suggestions and directions. Traffic was light so this is a nice area to walk or ride bikes.

title: “Great Hotel and Great Location!!!!”
text: I booked our stay at The Orchard Hotel based on the reviews on tripadvisor and am glad I did. The location is centrally located and there is a cable car stop at the end of the block. Not to mention, Chinatown is just a couple blocks away and Union Square is also a short walk away. In addition, the hotel staff were friendly and helpful. They immediately greeted us and even tried to give us a room with a view (try to request this when you book the room). The breakfast was also very good. Coffee, orange juice, water and milk were provided as beverages. Fresh canteloupe, honeydew, yogurt, packaged oatmeal, bagles, cream cheese, hard boiled eggs, sliced deli meat and toast were also available. Breakfast was served buffet style and began at 8:30 a.m. It was nothing over the top, but it was free and fresh and very good! The rooms were decorated nicely, the bedding and furniture were pretty, and the bathrooms were also nice. Basically, the room was up-to-date as far as style and furniture/appliances. Appearances really come into consideration for me when choosing a hotel and this one met the bill. Not to mention, the price was affordable and the location was a bonus. I would recommend this hotel to anyone planning trip to San Francisco!

title: “Do YourSelf a Favor and Stay Somewhere ELSE!!!”
text: This is the 2nd time I have added a review for this hotel!! I guess when it is BAD they take it down!! This really gives others a swayed look at this hotel! This was the WORST stay EVER in a SPG property!! The Noise was horrible in the lobby, sitting area and outside!! And the answer I got from the girl at the bar was its Thursday and we also do it on Tuesday. Go figure! They are pet friendly and you can tell it!! Either by the hair or smell!!! This should be a Pet Hotel and people friendly!! But give them ear plugs also. I travel alot and work In the corp park--really close to hotel BUT its not about being close anymore--It's about being peaceful, Bigger and Better rooms! Shuttle to and from Airport, Nice people at the bar! There are BETTER hotels within 2-3 miles of the Corp Park with bigger rooms, SHUTTLE to anywhere PLUS airport!! and ALSO CHEAPER$$$. This place is NOT what is cracked up to be--but the reviews show to be--thats because they take down the bad ones--so lets try this again!! This is NOT a $189 per night Hotel!!!!

title: “Mini vacation at the airport”
text:
We expend one night before our flight , the hotel was clean and modern the room spacious and the staff was professional and friendly .
But the the most pleasant surprise was the outside HEATED pool!!! With a sunny sky,temp of 70 in November and a garden surrounded by big pine trees we had a blast!! We feel already in vacation ! You could not tell that we were at the airport . We will stay in the future Every time we flight from Houston.

title: “SCARY”
text:
I booked this hotel with a business partner and I for 2 nights. 
The whole experience left us wanting to leave immediately.
Upon arrival there was no one to greet us. We thought we had entered a lounge instead of a hotel, it took us a while just wandering around and eventually someone from the bar offered to help us.
On the first night, my business partner had a guy walk into her room at 2am, which she promptly screamed and was terrified. the only response from the hotel was " we will check into it" and we have never heard from them since.
The rooms were definitely NOT what I would consider of a boutique hotel quality. in fact I thought IKEA had better showrooms.
The air conditioning was extremely loud and the Wifi was slow.
Suffice I would not recommend this place unless you do not intend to sleep much and just use the hotel club instead.

title: “Very Misleading”
text:
They advertise a $15,000,000.00 upgrade and renos but is sure wasn't anywhere near our room. Room was dirty, from carpet to walls. Bathroom small and dated and I would not have bathed in a tub with peeling paint. A/C was either on or off so you were either too cold or too hot. Loud mechanical noise from the washroom. Both issues addressed with the front desk and both times the answer was I will send the engineer up. 
All though the location is great, it was not worth the cost. We left after one night and gave our business to the Sheraton.

title: “Great hotel, fantastic location, excellent service”
text:
Spent 5 nights at the Jumeirah Essex House in March 06, over St Patricks Day. The hotel is in a perfect location for shopping on 5th Ave, wandering in Central Park and of course, was fantastic for the St Patricks Day Parade.
The reception and concierge staff are very helpful and the lobby itself is spectacular - beautiful flowers every day. The room was a good size and the beds very comfortable. Only negative was that the air conditioning was noisy and difficult to get the temperature just right.
The bar is very pleasant (expensive, although that's hotel bars for you I guess!) and the bartenders are friendly.
Its very easy to get around from the hotel, either by taxi or subway and its well positioned for all the usual sightseeing and shops.

title: “what fun!”
text: Not only was the room (a spa room with king bed) luxurious, clean, large, and well appointed (hooks in the right places, sufficient night table space, good lighting, wonderful bathroom) but the place reeks with joy - - the staff seem to be having a wonderful time (they even, I think, share the gym with the guests, which is terrific) and behave as if they are playing, they jump to serve and apologize profusely if something goes wrong (and there are minor, really minor glitches, but still . . . . ). The robes are animal prints, and varied so there is no confusion (I was a leopard, my husband a zebra). The decor is cheerful, doesn't take itself seriously. The bed was extremely comfortable. Of course, the weather was perfect, and the Philadelphia restaurants (BYOB) were great, and Rittenhouse Square this morning was filled with flowers and vegetables and music . . . . .

title: “Convenient to Downtown and Nationwide Arena”
text: Very good hotel. Convenient location to Nationwide and to the theatre. We were there for the NCAA tournament and they lobby was all decked out. I arrived at 11am and my room wasn't ready, but the young lady at the front desk took my cell phone and called me as soon as the room was ready - which was shortly thereafter. Room was clean and quiet. Room service was also excellent. I'll stay there again when I return to Columbus.

title: “An Uptown Favorite”
text: Depending on the purpose of my trips, I tend to stay either at the Mondrian Soho or the Hudson. On my recent two trips to the Hudson we were upgraded to a Suite, which I must say was fantastic. Its hard to find a bigger hotel room in NYC. Richard the Front Desk manager was great and took care of all our needs. If we didn't feel like going downtown, the rooftop bar is a great place to hang out and have a drink. Only pitfall to staying uptown is the amount you spend on taxis heading out at night downtown. Overall, if you're not in need of a downtown hotel, this hotel gets my vote!

title: “Good location, great service - a good value for business travel”
text:
I stay at this particular property often, as I do a lot of business in San Antonio. The Hyatt Place San Antonio Airport has been my go-to hotel of choice for a couple of reasons.
First of all, the price is right - it fits within my company's expense parameters. Free parking, breakfast, and internet all within our required limits is getting harder to achieve these days.
Second, location; it's a short drive to anywhere in town. Even during rush hour I can get to the office in less than 30 minutes, which is great. I also like being across the highway from the Quarry Market, which means that I have a bunch of dining options without having to go far after a long day at work. Not where I might stay if I were coming to town to hang out on the Riverwalk, but as a result it's pretty calm and quiet. There is a train nearby which can be disturbing for light sleepers, but it's definitely not a party hotel.
Third, the rooms. Since I'm never in town for less than a week, I love having a room that is more of a mini-suite so I don't feel like I'm living from the edge of the bed. I can lounge on the sofa and watch (the large flat screen) tv and then go to bed without feeling so cramped. I also appreciate having a mini-fridge. A microwave would be nice, though. The rooms have always been clean and decently-appointed. Nothing fancy, but nothing old or in disrepair either. The fitness center is small, but I've never seen it so crowded that I couldn't use it.
Lastly, the staff. They're great. The little touches like calling me by name when I check in really make a difference. One time my flight was delayed so I missed the complimentary shuttle - they told me to take a taxi and that they would pay for it. After having some pretty lousy experiences at other hotels, these types of things really make me come back time after time.
It's not luxury, but for the price I think it's a great value.

title: “The Worst Hotel Ever!”
text:
This was the worst hotel I have ever stayed at! The front desk peple were very rude! The 1st night someone was trying to check in late at night while we were sleeping, & no one was at the front desk so that person just kept honking their horn! There were bugs in the room, the bathroom was disgusting, the pillows were harder than a rock, it looked like it was 2 pillows sewed together! I had to go to a store and buy a new pillow just so I could sleep! The next night we were awaken at 2:00 A.M. by screaming, profanity, cars screaching in parking lot, people running and stomping above us. It was alot of people partying extremely loud until 4:30 in the morning. We tried to call the front desk but noone answered, so we called the cops. The cops didnt even show up to do anything.
We payed $75/night, later we heard the Hilton by the airport was charging the same rate! So we will definately stay there next time.
I wouldnt recommend this hotel to my worst enemy!

title: “Comfortable and friendly boutique hotel .”
text: My husband and I travelled with 2 friends and booked 2 rooms for a stay of 3 nights . Check in is after 15.00 . We were greeted by friendly staff . Our rooms were a good size by New York standards and everywhere was very clean . The bathrooms did not have baths but the showers were very good and the towels white and fluffy . A Flat screen TV , i-pod docking station with alarm and a comfy chair were also in each room . The beds were large and comfy .We had a views of the Empire State Building . Although our rooms were fronting the street they were quiet and we heard no noise from adjoining rooms . The hotel is in the Garment district so easy walking to Times Square , Broadway , Empire State Building etc . The Street the hotel is on is nothing special but as it was in a handy spot it did not matter . The Hotel has a roof-top bar which is worth a visit as the view of the Empire State is great . Be warned though the drinks are expensive and they are served in plastic glasses !! Spending over $90.00 on a bottle of wine should at least deserve glass wine glasses we thought . The breakfast is a continental buffet with a decent choice . The restaurant at the hotel is due to open at the end of september . We enjoyed our stay at this friendly hotel and thought it a good base to stay in whilst visiting New York .

title: “Dated Hotel and noisy but good location”
text:
In reality this is not a 4 star hotel, it has some of the features of a 4 star but it loses out on dates room design and very poor sound insulation.
Firstly the good, parking is easy and the location is good for downtown Jax. Cannot be bettered. Reception were welcoming and cheery and I was given a 9th floor room over looking the river. Room furnishings are adequate quality but some were a little worn. Beds were comfortable and linens clean.
Bathroom is very small, typical of the era - would be difficult for 2 people to be in the bathroom at once. Traditional tub with shower head, water pressure and temperature were good, TV channel choice excellent with a flat screen TV.
Now the poor. Noise insulation of poorly fitting sliding glass doors non existant - even with fan running can easily hear traffic on bridge over the river - and thats just cars, Throw in a truck or motor bike and sleep becomes an issue. Poorly fitting door to corridor allows in even more noise, if the room next to yours go in and out a lot it sounds like they are opening you door - very noisy.
Souless bar and restaurant - OK for breakfast (decent breakfast with prompt service) but avoid for dinner. There are plenty of restaunrants nearby and a Ruth Chriss attached to hotel.
If you get a good room rate then fair enough - otherwise avoid, if you are a light sleeper look elsewhere.

title: “Caudalie Spa.. Facial with Aniko.. THE BEST!!”
text: A facial with Aniko at the Caudalie Spa at the Plaza is well worth it!! She is a really talented esthetician and was recommended to me years ago by Cornelia of Cornelia Day Spa fame. The spa is beautiful, intimate yet spacious and airy. It is a little quiet gem in a bustling city and hotel.

title: “Perfect!”
text: This Hotel has a perfect location. Only a few blocks from all the main sightseeing in NYC.The price can't be beat. The boutique rooms are very clean and trendy.They offer a nice little workout facility. Most of all the Staff at Hotel Mela was AMAZING!

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: We stayed in a Deluxe King room and were very impressed with the size of the room and all the amenities. We enjoyed the breakfast buffet in the rooftop bar each morning and a drink each evening as we looked out at a view of the Chrysler Building. The location of the hotel is convenient to restaurants, shops and the subway, and within walking distance to Central Park. The hotel staff was very friendly and accommodating and met all our needs. We have been to NYC a number of times in the past five years and have stayed in many nice hotels, but The Kimberly has taken over as our number one favorite!

title: “hotel with awesome location”
text:
i didnt have trouble at all finding this hotel after exiting.the bus from jfk. the lobby was under construction, didnt care that much though. my room was okay, clean and with enough space for all the 4 people. the fridge in the room was bad though. it didnt have power and there were old smelly things like pizza, cake, milkshakes etc in it. unfortunately the aircon didnt work so we were sweating like hell while being in there. breakfast was good with bagels, pastries, cereals, coffee, tea, orangejuice and milk.
all in all a really good place if u stay in there for a couple of days. staff is really nice and talkative too :)

title: “Great Hotel!”
text:
Best hotel we ever stayed near an airport. Even though the hotel had an open lobby design, bedroom is in the back of the suite and exceptionally quiet. Also, absolutely no airport or road noise. Food was excellent at the restaurant, lobby bar open until 11:00 for late night eating. Excellent staff. 
No free wifi though.

title: “Not so nice.”
text: This place seemed to have excellent reviews. Although the sheets appeared to be clean, the beds were barely made and there were blood splatters on the wall near the bed. The only nice part was that our shower had excellent water pressure. We changed hotels our second night in NYC.

title: “Quality hotel in great location”
text: Spent one Saturday night over St. Patrick's Day weekend. Was able to get an early check-in (before 12 noon). Desk staff was pleasant and efficient. The 25th floor room (2544) was a corner room with two exposures. Older but very nice and clean with relatively new furnishings. Bath was small but clean and serviceable. Great water pressure in the shower, but did notice the problem with maintaining a consistent temp. that has been mentioned in other reviews. Comfortable queen-size bed and nice linens. Had Sunday breakfast in the diner; very busy but efficient service and good food at decent price. Did express check-out with no problems. And the location can't be beat - practically across the street from Macy's and MSG. Would definitely stay again!

title: “Charming hotel, good location, large comfortable rooms”
text: Our friends selected this hotel, and we were trying to adhere to a $200- per night budget in San Francisco. These rooms fell well within that range, and when we arrived, we were upgraded to larger "suites". Ours had a turret sitting area on the top floor, and their room was huge. Very clean and comfortable. Good beds and an adequate breakfast. If you like red, you will love this hotel. Very Victorian furnishings and spacious public rooms. Modern granite baths.

title: “very nice”
text: As I walked into the hotel the doorman was oblivious to my wife and I as he continued to talk with another employee in language that would be offensive to most people. That was the only bad experience had here. The Lobby staff were friendly and helpfull the common areas and function rooms are gorgeous. As this is an old hotel I was worried that the room would be cramped and out of style it was a pleasant surprise to find that that assumption was wrong. The room was large enough and very modern. The restauarant was very pricey but the food was good and the service even better. If you are celebrating a special ocassion and price isnt an issue thier restaurant The oak room is a great choice. After dinner we had a drink and listened to live jazz in the lounge it capped off a totally enjoyable evening. I would reccomend this hotel to just about any type of party.

title: “Spacious and very clean room. Plenty of room in king suite for family of four”
text:
Pleasant Upper West Side location. Staff helpful. Walked to Lincoln Centre and AMNH in minutes. Convenient for Subway (direct to Times Sq, and right down to Wall St and Battery Park). Taxis also short ride and inexspensive to Midtown locations. Amazing supermarket across road for any provisions you require and plenty of local restaurants.
I highly recomment it.

title: “Perfect in-town getaway”
text: Wife's 30th bday getaway. Always greeted with exceptional service, from valet to the front desk. We didn't have to wait and you could tell it was a busy day for the hotel at check in. Room was ready, clean, spacious, and great view. Amanda at the front desk couldn't have been friendlier and more welcoming. Spent the day @ the W Pool. Great atmosphere and drinks. Service from Lacy was top notch. Dined at Craft that evening and crushed it. Pork Belly as an appetizer is a must as are the short ribs. If I had the funds I would by the bed and bedding. Best night of sleep I've had in ages. Will stay again.

title: “Stay far, far away.”
text:
If I could give this "hotel" zero stars, instead of one, I would have. This was absolutely the worst hotel I have ever stayed in, in my life. When calling to book a room, we were offered a "2 bedroom suite, with 2 beds in one bedroom, and one king in the other bedroom." So, we arrived expecting a suite with two BEDROOMS, and a common living area. When we arrived, we were dismayed to find that it was not, in fact, two bedrooms, just two regular hotel rooms connected by an interior door. Hotel staff needs to do a better job being clear on what exactly is being offered. Traveling with young children, having a separate living area was a must for naptimes, and bedtimes. 
We were also very dismayed at the general upkeep and cleanliness of the rooms. The carpet was so filthy, I refused to let my children take their shoes off, and the entire room smelled musty. The bathroom was so tiny one could barely step inside and close the door without actually getting into the shower, and there was grease from the door hinges all over the walls in the bathroom. The laundry area was extremely tiny, and our frustration was compounded by the fact that the dryers did not even work.
We were pretty disgusted, but it was late evening, and with several young, cranky children, we really had no other choice but to make the best of things. We got up the next morning (early since we were stuck in the same sleeping area as the children), to rinse out a curdled sippy cup, only to discover that there was an entire PART missing underneath the sink, which caused the dirty water, and curdled milk from the sink to out, all over our luggage (which we couldn't wash, since the dryers didn't work). We then found 2 cockroaches in the corner, when we moved the luggage, and were so disgusted, we knew we had to get out of there.
It was approximately 8:30 am, Monday morning when I went to the front desk to cancel our rooms, and get a refund on the night before, and the gentleman behind the desk informed me that a manager had to approve this, and there wasn't one available. I think it's pretty ridiculous not to have someone on property at all times who can handle large issues like this. But, since the gentleman behind the desk was nice, and it wasn't his fault, I agreed to wait. He reported the manager would be in anytime between now (8:30 am) and 9:00 am. So, we were already packed up and out of the room, and had our children in their car seats, in the vans, and had to just sit in the parking lot waiting. When I went back in, at 9:00 am, I was informed it would be another 10 minutes before he arrived. 15 minutes later, I go back in, and I'm told that the manager arrived, but when to the housekeeping office, and didn't take a phone so I have to wait some more. By this point I'm INCREDIBLY frustrated. I sit there another 10 minutes, when the guy behind the counter says "I'm going to try to reach him via radio." WHAT?!? You couldn't have tried this 10 minutes ago? As he goes in the back, another manager walks in the door and agreed to help me. 
We were able to cancel the following night, and get a refund for the night before, and the new manager seemed to take my concerns seriously, but the fact that I had to sit around for over an hour just to get someone who was able to take care of my concerns was absolutely ridiculous. Next time, perhaps these managers should spend an hour locked in a car with screaming children who are sick of sitting around and going nowhere, and perhaps they will be more accommodating.
We left, and were able to procure a much nicer property, right on the water for only $30 more per night. I wouldn't stay at this particular hotel again if they were paying ME.

title: “Nov. 2012”
text:
Convenient location - close to freeway.
This is an older Microtel so the rooms are larger.
On the negative side - the carpets needed a good shampooing.

title: “Thanks To Everyone At The Wyndham!”
text:
First I need to thank Chase, who helped me get to my romm Sat. afternoon and since I'm handicapped, it's pretty challenging in a wheel chair, or walker. He was friendly and spoke well of my Democratic group. 
Then Monica, at the front desk phone, was very courteous. 
And last to help make my Saturday great was Lori Nelson. She helped me get on this web-site and thru the detail to get started writing. 
Thanks! 
Shelley Hamlett

title: “Great Long Term Stay”
text:
I just finished staying off and on for about two months at the Residence Inn in Rancho Bernardo, and have to say that it was very enjoyable and worth while. I am relocating from the east coast to California, and although there is stress with that move and the home relocation, the stay at the Residence Inn and the inviting and pleasant staff made it feel like home.
Right from the beginning, the staff has been helpful, friendly, pleasant and efficient. Kelly and Cally were outstanding with directions, assistance with the room, handling mail, and anything else needed to make the stay more comfortable.
The manager, Casey, was very attentive, and happy to handle calls or conversations to discuss any issues. He is also great at communicating through email with questions. This is outstanding service for someone moving from another state, and trying to find balance in life, to be able to rely on outstanding staff that really show they care about their guests.
The hotel is a typical Residence Inn, with great rooms, and excellent breakfasts and dinners three nights a week. The location is fantastic, with many chain restaurants and independent restaurants to choose from with a short drive or walk. And the shopping nearby is fantastic, with many of the major chains, grocery stores, Trader Joes, etc. all very close. Housekeeping does a great job, and maintenance staff is fantastic. We had a closet door fall off the slider, and the maintenance help fixed it perfectly in minutes. 
There is great recreation nearby as well, with plenty of golfing within a short distance, and the beach is 15 minutes away. This is a great location, excellent family stay or long term hotel, but great for short term as well. The staff and management here are fantastic and CARE about their guests.
I have stayed at several other neighboring Residence Inns, and it just isn't the same. This is the place to stay!

title: “Not worth the hype”
text:
It wasn't a horrible experience, but I'm glad I didn't pay rack rate; my rate was $199 throughTravelzoo.com. 
The lobby decor does not strike me as modern, chic, hip, fun, etc. It's dark, and in the back of my head I couldn't help but think of how much you can hide by dimming the lights, using dark paneling, and painting the walls and ceilings grey. I didn't think the bar was particularly hip, chic, or fun, either. I visited the bar once, a glass of house wine cost me $14, and there was hardly anyone there. 
Basic room is not small, it's itty bitty. I'm only sleeping there, so I don't really care, but traveler's should be aware that the standard room is only about 9.5' x 9.5'. It barely fits a bed, with a 13" TV inside the narrow cabinet. The wall that separates the bedroom from the bath is glass, obviously to give the illusion of more space. 
I (woman alone) was put in the last room at the very end of the hallway, which I understand is a no-no in the industry. My room's door frame was cracked, and the chain lock hung on by one screw ... not very secure. The door wouldn't latch properly right away because of the crack (looked like maybe someone tried to kick the door in), so I asked the front desk to send someone up to look at it. When I showed him the cracked door, he jotted it down in his notebook to make sure someone looked at it, but made no offer of a more secure room for me. 
Breakfast restaurant is another very dark room, and was absolutely freezing cold on the two March mornings that I ate there (quickly, as it was so cold I couldn't wait to leave).
I just checked the Hudson website, and today's rack rate is about $499. That is just mind boggling to me! This hotel is so not worth it!

title: “This is what a hotel should be ........ Excellant”
text:
To find a hotel that ticks all boxes - are hard to find BUT the Library hotels is such one.
From start to finish the staff were superb and couldn't fault their professionalism in any way - courteous , friendly. The hotel does make the vistor appreciated - even on check out day - the offer to use the hotel facilities is a major plus , if you are waiting for a late flight. The ambience / atmosphere of the hotel is fanatastic and the location just makes it a great place to stay when visiting New York.

title: “Not worth the money! Dark and Dingy!”
text: I stayed here recenlty, the hotel is conisidered hip in design. I felt like I was in a different country really. The inside walls of the hotel are painted black, or better yet gun metal grey. The carpet was like and indoor outdoor black astro turf which was hard on the feet. The mattress is sitting pretty much right on the floor maybe 2 or 3 inches up, but not for someone with disabilities because it is way too low. the elevators reaked of cigarette smoke. My walk in closet at my home is larger than the room they gave me, these rooms are tiny lofty in their style. The structure seems very old. It felt as if I camped out over night in and office building, that is the best way to put it. My last complaint is their advertised complimentary breakfast which does not start until 7am.This is unreasonable for an airport hotel. This is LAX!!! People have early flights and we cant have juice. coffee, or something to eat until after 7am? I had an 8am flight and left the hotel at 6:30 am and could not get anything to eat, as it was all set up in the lobby covered in saran wrap, but was rudely told by the reception, that breakfast does not start until 7? I was like really? its all here and ready to go, and I am a paying customer, and all I really needed was a cup of coffee. I was told if I wanted coffee I could purchase it out of a machine or get coffee from a shop around the corner from the hotel. Needless to say this hotel was a complete dive in my view.

title: “Great hotel in the heart of downtown with excellent customer service”
text: Stayed for a week and found the hotel and service to be top notch. It's a classic old downtown hotel with character and its been nicely renovated. The staff provided excellent customer service - you couldn't ask for more. They were friendly, helpful and great. The adjacent restaurant & bar was very handy and welcome after a long day. It was a great combination.

title: “Bed Springs in my back!”
text: This hotel prides itself on being one of 6 or 7 "personality" hotels in the city. Yes, the room was adorned with fancy furniture, lights and art but, the beds were just awful! You could feel the springs in your back and I couldn't get to sleep till well after 3:00am! This hotel sits off of very busy Market street so if you plan to stay here bring ear plugs because the homeless people can get rowdy at night. The walls don't seem to be very thick either, since I could here people laughing and talking in the next room. The window was filthy! If you want a comfortable bed and a quiet setting, don't stay here!

title: “The Best”
text: From the second we arrived to the second we left - everything was perfect. Special mention to Betty the best concierge in the world. Each and every member of staff we came in contact with went above and beyond to make our stay exceptional. This is my No 1 hotel in Boston.

title: “don't listen to wha to read!!!!”
text:
DO NOT LISTEN TO ANY BAD REVIEWS REVIEWS YOU HEAR ABOUT THIS HOTEL!!
I was at this hotel only a few weeks ago and I was dreading it before I went. The day before i went (15/4/08) I read lots and lots of reviews from this hotel and none were positive! I expected the worst, people were saying it was like a prison and very unpleasant and dirty. I could not believe how wrong I was before gonig here. I'm an 18 year old and went with 3 other friends between 18-22, we all expect 100% hygiene and are very picky at where we stay. On arrival New York is out of this world its a dream place to be. The hotel reception was as luxorious asit appeared in the pictures, although it was filled with a school trip load of people which I dreaded as I thought it would be very noisy. After checking in I asked if it were possible to be upgraded and the staff member who could have smiled a little more did so at no more cost. My friends and I had a luxorious king size room each which was up to my stanards of cleanliness. Each room was cleaned every morning with fresh sheets and clean lining towels. Overall, my stay was very pleasant and this hotel is extremely excellent for location - 3 blocks from the Empire State Builiding, 1000 yards from Times Square, 1 block from Macy's department store and also literally across the road from Madison Square Gardens. This hotel had a great location and had very helpful staff in arranging trips, broadway shows etc. 
The only bad thing about this hotel was the fact that the staff didn't look happy at all but were relatively helpful. The corridors were slightly out-dated and the showers turned from ice cold - scolding hot - we never got a decent temperature and had to keep jumping in and out of the shower. Also the hotel views from our window on the 13th floor were limited to looking into another building across the road.
I would deffinetely recommend this hotel to anyone afterall you are in New York you are only in the hotel to sleep anyway!!

title: “Would definitely stay there again”
text: Just returned from staying at the Comfort Inn Midtown for 5 nights. Total price per night including taxes was $200. We usually stay at 3 or 4 star hotels but tried out a 2-star for a change (and price was much better). The hotel was small (in size and number of rooms) which was nice for a change. The elevator was big enough for about 8 people (or 3 with luggage). Warning - watch out for the elevator door! It slams FAST and HARD and I still have the bruise on my hand to prove it. The halls were very narrow. Our room was the smallest I have ever stayed in but was adequate. I called it a "one-way room" because only one person could walk around at a time! The window air conditioner was great and not loud at all - just a quiet hum. We were on the back facing the church next door and heard the church bells a lot which was nice. Actually, that was the only noise we heard the whole trip from our room. The bathroom was larger than I had expected. It even had a large frosted window in it and a large ledge to sit your stuff on. We only had the breakfast 2 mornings and it was fine - bagels, toast, boiled eggs, cereal, donuts, fruit, coffee, orange and apple juice, cappucino, coffee and tea. One person said there were only 4 tables in there, but there were 8 (I think). We did have to wait a couple of minutes one day. I think it would have been nice if the people who were finished would have left and given up their table instead of sitting there planning the day's itinerary while we stood there. The computer room (2 computers, free internet) was a nice plus because we could check on a few things while we were there. All the employees were friendly. One other thing - the doors really do SLAM when you leave your room. They usually started around 7 a.m. All you have to do is keep your hand on the handle and pull it shut and it won't slam. We couldn't figure out why people let them slam so much. Rude, I guess. Anyway, bottom line is this hotel was great for the money and location, I would highly recommend it if you wanted a nice place to sleep and shower, and we would definitely stay there again.

title: “Better than expected”
text: I decided to reserve at this hotel based on the rate and location. I found the staff to be helpful during the stay. The rooms were clean. And the breakfast was great. They even had strawberry topping to go with the self made waffles. Tea & homemade cookies in the lobby. Parking was $14, which was alot better then some of the other hotels in the area. I will stay again the next time I am in Philadelphia.

title: “Clean, Good Proximity, Great Value”
text:
We were looking for an inexpensive place to stay. I found this by chance by googling "hotels in san diego." It was a great find.
This place is NOT the WINN!! It's a budget hotel. It's location is within 5-15 minutes of anything you'd want to see in SD (except the Wild Animal Park, which is not in SD). The rooms are spotless. The staff was friendly. I thought the breakfast was more than mediocre. My husband and I eat cereal or instant oatmeal and hot tea/coffee for breakfast each morning on a typical day. This breakfast offered assorted danishes, fresh fruit, yogurt, 2 or 3 kinds of cereal, toast, butter, jams, syrup for your waffles made fresh on these wonderful waffle irons, coffee, tea, milk, orange, apple, papaya juice. I didn't taste the sausage, as this was the one thing that did not look too great.
I do agree with other reviewers about the size of the rooms. We did not even get a "suite." See my posted pictures with this review. Our room was a postage stamp just large enough for a king bed, small entertainment center, and a small table and 2 chairs, with NO room to spare. However, we weren't planning on hanging out in our rooms all day. We just needed a clean place to sleep, shower and eat a decent breakfast, and that is exactly what this hotel offers. The bed was very comfortable.
The bathroom, however, was quite spacious, immaculately clean, and had all necessities, including 6 fresh bath towels every day...and we were only two people in the room!
Also, my hubby and I used the hot tub...very nice...very hot. We also got in the pool. Note our stay was in December, gets cool at night. But between hot tub and heated pool, the swim was refreshing and relaxing. The pool area has its own towels.
I would surely recommend this place to my friends. It's simple, comfy, inexpensive, and has everything you need.

title: “special anniversary”
text: The hotel was right off of the highway and very easy to get to. We requested a high floor room and they gave us the 20th floor, right under the suites. The floor was very quiet and the view was fantastic. As we were leaving to make our 8:15 dinner reservations we heard a knock at the door and when we opened it room service was there. The server asked what the last name was and when i told him he brought in gourmet chocolates and champagne on ice. The note said "Happy Anniversary! thanks for staying with us - Jennifer at the front desk". Fabulous hotel staff need I say more? We will be staying there again soon.

title: “That's no lady, that's my roach!”
text:
I stayed at the Grand Union for 6 nights mid January 2005.
On checking in I noticed a cockroach crawling over my bag. I complained to the desk manager and he advised that it was not one of theirs and that I must have brought it in with me. Now I didn't knowingly bring a roach along for the ride, but who knows, it's possible - I didn't see any other insects during my stay.
The room was small but reasonably clean, grubby under the bed (I was checking for roaches) - but perhaps it's grubby under most hotel beds, I don't usually look.
Overall this was a pretty good deal - it's a good location for say a stroll to the Empire State building and the very local subway gets you up and down the eastside and on to connecting lines with ease. There are three internet terminals in the lobby - there is a charge for these but they are fast, handy and not exorbitant for checking e-mails. 
East 32nd street has some good Korean restaurants - I recommend Don's Bo Gam at no. 17 which has a modern but cosy bar on entering and good food in the restaurant beyond. It's friendly and relaxing and very close to the Grand Union.

title: “Good location”
text: We spent 3 nights here and booked this hotel with loyalty points. Our room was spacious and overall represented good value for the price. The reception staff were not overly helpful when we asked about leaving luggage. The refurbishment has still not been finished and as a result the bar and restaurant were totally lacking in atmosphere and very basic. The location was good and we were able to walk to most of the places that we wantedd to see. There were a lot of people visiting the adjacent hospital and not so many tourists. A good experience but not as good as we had hoped given that we thought that the works would have been finished by the time we were going.

title: “Not Worth the Money”
text: Well, we booked last minute, we like to stay at the Omni, but there was not any availabilty. So, we started calling other hotels, The Westin was the first one out of 5 or 6 that said they had a king bed room on the river. The price was $239 after the military discount. We booked and showed up at the hotel about an hour later. We checked in around 3, I heard them tell several other people that their rooms were not ready yet. To my surprise, our room was ready or so we thought. We got up to our room and opened the door and it had double beds. The bell hop called down to the front desk and we were told that they did not have any more king beds on the river, so we either had to stay in that room or move to the city view room with a king and a $40 discount. We agreed to move, they told us to wait in that room and they would bring the keys to the new room up as soon as it was ready. We waited about 30 minutes then called down stairs and they said they were checking on it and would call us back, after 15 minutes we just got our stuff and went downstairs. After about 10 minutes there and explaining everything we were finally given keys to our new room (1116). The rooms are pretty plain with a flatscreen t.v. and refrigerator. The tile in the bathroom along the bottom of the wall had gap in it, like it hadn't been caulked. The shower head looked like a dollar store one, it barely worked and had build-up all over it. On a good note, the bed and pillows were awesome. The bar downstairs is nice and has a nice outside area. But, I would not stay here again, we ended up paying about $230 after taxes and we had a view of an alley and a bad shower! Kind of put a damper on things! Also, when we checked out they had not given us the $40 discount and my husband spent about 20 minutes argueing with them to get the $40 taken off our bill.

title: “Not worth price of admission”
text: I recently stayed here for a conference that was taking place across the street. As far as location goes this was a great hotel to stay at as well as being right on the riverwalk. That being said there were a number of problems. First off why is there no free wi-fi? If your a paying guest you should be allowed free wi-fi (go to the starbucks in the mall across the street for free wi-fi.) Second: whenever I asked for directions from the staff they often got streets mixed up and was almost late to my event as a result. Finally The wait time for elevators was ridiculous and would wait almost fifteen minutes at times. Other than a convenient location for my conference this hotel ultimately disappointed.

title: “Solid 4 Star”
text:
Visiting Chicago for six days last week of August into early September. Chose the Conrad for its location at the south end of "Miracle Mile" and near the Chicago River. Hotel is connected to a small upscale mall with its main entrance on Rush St and an additional entrance through the mall onto Michigan Ave.
Lobby is located on the floor 5 accessed via an elevator from street level. Don't know what all the fuss is about with some reviewers - extra three minutes to get into the lobby of the hotel - not a major inconvience. In fact it offered a sense of greater security coming in off the street. There was never more than a 2 minute wait to get to the front desk - often service was available immediately. Outdoor and indoor restaurant located on this level as well. Only ate at the hotel for breakfast at the interior/indoor location - so I can only comment on this area. At all 5 breakfasts, food was fresh and promptly prepared. The non-ala carte waitered breakfast menu included eggs any style, toast with jams/butter, sausage, selection of cereals, fruit, OJ, coffee and a selection of teas. 
I had insisted on a number of items 3 weeks prior to arriving at the hotel when making my reservation - quiet area of the hotel limiting noise from external and internal sources; having the use of a mini fridge and a coffee maker during our stay. All were waiting for us upon our arrival on the 16th floor. As the hotel is only 17 floors, the street noise is not entirely eliminated - you'd probably have to at least be double the height- but the location of our room away from internal noise sources and not facing Michigan Ave was most likely the best the hotel could offer. 
Room had one king bed - pillows a little soft for our liking - otherwise fine. Quiet A/C. Well appointed with flat screen TV, sound system, ipod charger/radio, reading pot lights, seperate toilet room, shower and bath, makeup magnifying mirror.
During our six days, we were offered or asked no less than a dozen times, if we needed anything or how our stay was going. It was always unsolicited and offered by the front desk, the concierge, the maintenance staff or the restaurant staff. It added to the enjoyment of the vacation knowing that the hotel was genuinely concerned about our well-being.
Only downside, no pool. Although I was aware of this when booking, that combined with a spa, would have put the hotel teetering on a five-star rating. We did utilize the pool once at the Homewood Suites, a block away, but it wasn't worth the effort.
Would I stay again - yes - for the value and service, but I would look elsewhere if I wanted a pool/spa and a higher, somewhat quieter street/river location.

title: “Good value in NYC”
text: We stayed here back in 2009 the coldest weekend of the year, we came in for the International Motorcycle show at the Javits center. We paid $100 for our room. It was small but clean and everything worked. Bed was ok, didnt sleep much due to fire trucks, police sirens and horns honking all nite. Room was nice and toasty! Would stay again but not on the streetside of this hotel. I liked the history of the place that chains dont have.

title: “very nice hotel”
text: Stayed for several days with grandkids. Fantastic expeerience. Front desk upgraded us to a larger available room. Fantastic city and park views, 2 bathrooms, excellent in room dining service, and the pool on roof which got visited every day - great morning aquasize class; singing Bellman (really funny with grands).

title: “Not what I expected”
text: I would rate this a 2-Star at best. The room was not clean and was very small - had not been vacuumed, and there was hair in the shower and on one of the towels. It was also very loud with lots of kids running the halls.

title: “Most Horrible stay EVER!!”
text:
We usually stay at the Hilton but I wanted to give Hyatt a try because we had never stayed at a Hyatt. We booked a suite for a 2 night vacation package through Sea World and added an extra night directly through Hyatt. We planned on staying for 3 nights. From the time we walked up to the front desk it was disaster. First of all the young lady named Bekka greeted us as though it was painful for her to do so. And when we gave her the confirmation number she said we were only booked for 1 night. I had explained to her that we were booked for 2 nights originally through SW and added an extra night. She made calls and could not find anything but had said we were ok for 3 nights. She did not let us know anything about the Hotel or what the Hotel had to offer and did not even offer us what had come with the 3rd night stay ( a movie and 25% off meal in their restaurant and free parking). She has no buisness in the hospitality buisness because she lacked hospitable skills. Then we get to our room. Where do I start? The roomed smelled obnoxious because of the deodorizer the housekeeper used to cover the smells of the musky room, we had to pay for internet service and pay for cartoons on televsion for our daughter (this is unheard of to me),on the balcony was bird droppings from birds pirching over the balcony with no chairs on the balcony to sit. Parking is also 20.00 a day. We were paying almost $300.00 a night. The upgrades in this hotel are tacky and cheap looking. Very cold staff and very cold stay. Needless to say, we cancelled the original 2 night vactaion package through Sea World with the Hyatt and stayed only 1 night. We booked the remaining 2 night stay with Hilton San Diego Resort and Spa up the street. My gut did try to warn me as I was booking this trip to stay with Hilton where we have only got the BEST service in all our visits with Hilton. I 
 I have to mention that we are disappointed with Sea World as far as not even getting an apology for the waste of money and time Hyatt Regency Mission Bay caused and cost us. 
We will probalby not book a vacation package through Sea World in the future and we will NEVER stay at this Hyatt or any other Hyatt as long as we live. Do not waste your money or time here.

title: “be careful! misconduct in pricing”
text: last july I booked a room for one person for 5 days in september (from 5 to 10 september), 270 $ at day (tax inclused). the price was high but I hope the hotel was good. The night of 9 september two friends came in new york and stayed at the hotel @ times square, but they paid 200 $ for a room for two people, without reservation. 70 $ less the price I paid. Totaly I paid 350 $ more in 5 days. It's not correct. anyway the hotel has good location but it is nothing of special. With 270 $ you can find a lot of better solutions. The room are noisy and small. The breakfast bad.

title: “Don't go there - end of story”
text: Imagine a grotty little building in the worst part of a dirty city. That, is Ram's hotel. Nearly $80 a night they tried to charge me there. It's located in a ghetto foir crying out loud. The rooms smelt disgusting, the staff were rude, and I feared for my life when leaving the hotel. Avoid it like the plague.

title: “Great & clean, but evacuated 2xs in middle of night & left at 4AM”
text: At 1 AM and 3:15 AM, the fire alarm went off and we evacuated down 10 flights of stairs (with 2 young children in tow). After getting the 'all clear' the first time, we thought it was a prankster, then when it happened 1 1/2 hours later, the fireman told me it was a malfunction of the detector on floor 11. Therefore, only floors 10, 11 & 12 heard a siren to evacuate. I would only consider staying here again if I was told the problem was fixed. The firemen acted like it was a common occurence at the hotel as they didn't hustle into the building, but had to go in to shut off the siren. Besides that MAJOR issue, the hotel is close to Nationals Park, is very modern & clean with secure parking, and a very helpful staff.

title: “Very nice hotel!”
text:
Nice, clean hallways and rooms. Great views. Great lobby and bar. Bar staff is the hotel highlight...very friendly and helpful. Drinks are priced like an upscale hotel. Market prices in town are about 50% less. But, it was worth the price for the great atmosphere, service, and convenience.
This is the GM headquarters so GM is everywhere which didn't bother me. The lobby at center of complex can be confusing due to circular ramps but it provides great open spaces to the gallery. 
The rooms are very nice, bedding is comfortable and rooms are spacious. Views are excellent. The gym is exceptional! If you want to workout on your trip this is the place!

title: “close to convention center but rooms need an update”
text: i was one of many who swarmed to san diego for the comicon convention. the best reason to stay here is the proximity to the convention center. no need for a car or taxi. the lobby is very grand and the service upon check in was really attentive. unfortunately, the rooms don't measure up. the bathroom looks like the haven't been updated since the 80's and the toom was just kinda blah. old tv and furniture. i would definitely stay again for business but do hope the spruce the place up.

title: “Great Location”
text:
Booked with travelzoo rate on a superior room. If this is superior, I'd be very disappointed with a regular room. 
The room was on the 39th floor and smaller than expected. We did have a view of the Chrysler building from the window although we were surrounded by other taller buildings.
The room was clean, but the housekeeping staff never replaced our drinking glasses and we stayed 3 nights! My husband just went to the bar one night to get clean glasses.
Other room complaints include: hard bed, old TV with sound problems, no coffemaker and only 1 hanger. I had to call for a light bulb for the floor lamp and also requested hangers. The light bulb was furnished, but not the hangers.
The staff we met were good. Checkin was fast and professional. The concierge made good recommendations for inexpensive breakfast and sandwiches. We ate at Cranberry for a quick bite after arrving late. The Red Flame is an excellent diner on 44th between 5th and 6th Avenues. 
The redeeming factor for this hotel is the location. It was convenient to the theatres, times square, tours, etc. Loved the location!

title: “last resort”
text:
Location is central enough but is one of only a few things that the hotel has going for it. The rooms need a lot of work (painting and generally modernising). It is as they say " cheap and cheerful". Although bedrooms were cleaned on a daily basis there was a mouse spotted on the 14th floor so beware. General upkeep is low and in general it needs a good overall. 
Not too bad if only for laying head down for a few hours but does need a LOT of work

title: “Love the hotel grace!!!”
text:
My third time there this year and it was a dream as usual.
Beautifully designed, the hotel grace seems tucked away even though it is in the heart of times square. Excellent service, pristine, quiet it is the perfect place for a romantic weekend in nyc. Thoroughly enjoyed the bar although some of the patrons were a bit too scenester-y. The comfortable bedding and small but spacious enough rooms works out well but what really gets me every time is a quick dip in the pool and some time in the steam room after a night of fun in nyc. An absolute rock star way to start the day. The complimentary breakfast is delicious and they don't run out of food. The man who runs the breakfast was kind enough to toast my croissant and bring it to my table for me, they taste better that way he explained.
I can't praise Hotel Grace highly enough.
Oh, and they happily will outfit your room with hypo-allergenic bedding!!!

title: “Loved it”
text:
You can say that I've stayed in quite a few of the business hotels in the downtown/Magnificent Mile area: Marriott, Wyndham (Now Hyatt--haven't stayed in it as a Hyatt), Omni, InterContinental, Embassy Suites and the W Hotel a bit further away from Michigan. Although all of these are much more "luxurious" than the Four Points, I the Four Points competes well against them! Why? Because it is actually one block off of Michigan, so a little less noisy and it has a Trader Joes next door! No, really, because it has all that I need at a great rate: free wifi, a comfy bed and a good sized room with a couch and a great view. Check in was quick and nice. I am also a fan of small lobbies, so I liked that I could access the elevator quickly instead of walking a long way to get to the elevator.
I would say that the Wyndham and Omni are a little nicer, but at the price difference, I would choose the Four Points any day. I had mixed experiences at the InterContinental and Marriott, so would choose other hotels over them.

title: “Five star "star" of Baltimore that makes healing a wonderful experience”
text: I just had surgery at Johns Hopkins Hospital so I decided to stay at this hotel since it was outpatient surgery. What a right decision I made. This hotel is magnificent. Walking into the lobby made me feel so happy as I was greeted by multiple staff and cared for and pampered in every way. When I was driven up after the surgery, multiple staff immediately came to assist me to my room. The rooms are large, magnificent and extremely well appointed. There is even a television built into the bathroom mirror!!! The linens are wonderful and the hotel just gives a wonderful feel good experience. Housekeeping has been brought to a new level in this hotel. I received at least 3 calls from housekeeping in that they understood I was recovering from surgery and wanted to know if there was anything they could do to make me more comfortable in my room. The spa at this hotel is amazing with a jacuzzi that has a lounge chair in it. My husband and I are planning to return to this hotel for a relaxing vacation but it certainly made my recovery accelerated to be in such a wonderful surrounding. Five star cheers for this hotel and its amazing staff!!!!!

title: “Would not recommend”
text: This hotel is nothing like what they show on their website. On a positive note the room was an ok size (for a New York hotel) clean and in a good location other than that the staff were unfriendly, housekeeping inconsistent - some days we would get towels replaced but no coffee cups, sometimes 1 hand towel, cups and no bath towels (bit like faulty towers). We stayed for 10 nights and the soap was replaced once. The bathroom products were not what was advertised on their website nor was 'luxury” towels, sheets etc. The front desk area was small and always crowded with staff standing around talking which felt like we were imposing on a private function and not a paying guest of the hotel. On their website the hotel gives the impression of being somewhat boutique and unlike the other hotels but for the cost of the room I’m sure you would receive better service and amenities elsewhere. We asked them to arrange a taxi and without consultation they arranged a black ‘gypsy’ car for us. The whole vibe of the hotel just seemed like the guests were imposing on how the staff think things should be and what you want and need is irrelevant.

title: “Great hotel, perfect location for travellers”
text: I've stayed at this hotel several times for meetings. Generally speaking, airport hotels are just adequate, or they are overpriced. The DFW Grand Hyatt is an exception to that rule. The staff was courteous and helpful, the restaurant had wonderful food choices, and the rooms are comfortable and quiet. Highly recommended.

title: “contemporary comfort in the heart of seattle”
text:
went to seattle for a wedding and stayed at the hotel 1000. wow! we loved our room. who wouldn't like a bathtub that fills from the ceiling and molten brown bath products! the room had all the modern conveniences--ipod connector, lcd tv, etc. the services were great--they had complimentary shoe shine, clothes steaming, newspapers. they had prepackaged bags of ice in an ice chest right outside the room. the wife and i both got massages at the spa and got chocolate covered strawberries and champagne for valentines day--not to mention one of the best massages i've ever gotten (and i've gotten massages all over the world). the concierge was great and gave us directions and tips on everything (and provided umbrellas of course!). the customer service was top notch. 
as for location, you are within walking distance of a limitless supply of fantastic seafood restaurants as well as the museum of art and fish market. 
this hotel is an absolute gem. because we were going for a wedding and had a lot of friends in town spread out over a bunch of different hotels we got to see a lot of them. they all lacked the unique style and luxury of hotel 1000. we will definitely stay there again next time we are in seattle!

title: “A bit dated, but clean with reasonable facilities”
text:
The location is great for central Houston and the River Oaks/Richmond/Montrose/Galleria districts which have the most attractions for tourists. The area felt safe.
The hotel itself is clean if a little dated, and the main corridor did remind a couple of our party of the corridors of the Overlook Hotel from the Shining! However, the rooms were spacious and included a fridge, microwave and TV. The bathroom is slightly cramped, but sufficient.
The breakfast felt a bit sparse, with not as many options as other hotels, and polystyrene/styrofoam crockery an plastic cutlery felt a bit cheap and nasty.
We did get a good rate though for a hotel this conveniently located though, so overall, not bad!

title: “Excellent Affordable hotel , in a good location!”
text:
The hotel is a the Upper West Side, right next door the the Natural History Museum, a 5 minute walk in either direction to the subways ( Line 1 and Line A ) . The area is nice and safe with lots of eating places , bars and Starbucks nearby , The hotel offers free coffee/tea in the morning and it has free internet. The room was perfectly adequate for my stay , yes , the rooms and bathrooms are small (would only be a problem if you are FAT, then you might struggle with the bathroom.) but hey , if you are in NY , the only time you should be in your room is to sleep!! 
I found the staff friendly and helpful , particularly the night staff. I was happy with my stay here and the price I paid for a hotel in Manhattan, a city in which hotel rooms can be very expensive

title: “I love the location, and it is a very good hotel!”
text:
I love the location, it is the closest to Universal Studios and City Walk. I think that just the extra couple blocks of steps up hill to get to City Walk and the park would disuade one from staying at the Neighboring Sheriton. Since Hilton is so close we had no qualms about going back to the hotel to allow our little one to nap while Dad & our preteen swam in the pool. Then we would head back out for late afternoon at the park, and even back to hotel and back out to City Walk for the evening.
The pool is large heated and has cabana tents, food and drink service .
 I love that they have a little convienence refrigerator in the room
We stayed at the hotel a couple years ago and spent the big bucks to get a tower room one of the special the top floors with view of Universal Studios whivh was fun, but this visit we decided to save money and only had a 7th floor room and I have to say I would do this again because it was the same room, just no park view, and we found other thighs to spend the money on, like the fabulous seafood Buffett in the Hilton's Sienna Resturant and a front of the line pass for Universal Studios.

title: “horror story”
text:
Here is my horror story,and BTW if I could give this place no stars I would. I stayed for two nights at the the Holiday Inn in El Paso (the one that is down the street from theairport, IE on the corner of Airways boulevard. and I-10).
My horror story begins when I checked into the place. They put in in an older room, which I was not pleased with but hey, I was on business there, so I was not concentrating on comfort. Anyhow, I was told upon checking in that "A LIVE 
RADIO BROADCAST WOULD BE HELD HERE .......OH AND THERE WOULD BE 
"GUESTS" in ballroom one." 
Lets do a little arithmetic here:
Small (garbage) airport hotel + Live radio broadcast inviting everyone in the city to come on down to the HI and PARRTY = Big disaster for people paying to stay here. 
Forward to 9 PM, I notice a lot of screaming , and lot of honking and beer bottles being broken. I went outside my room, and noticed that a lot of people were trying to get into the hotel parking lot, as if there was a concert being held here, or a Yankees game. was contemplating going out to dinner thinking that this was going to be over by the time I came back from dinner. Before I could even get out of my spot five cars descended literally on it, and two guys were screaming at each other for my spot. 
I got so scared that I figured if I leave the hotel forget getting a parking spot, I will be backed up in traffic fighting to get into the hotel. 
Some guy in the parking lot named LEO was directing traffic, I very clearly told him that look, people who pay to sleep here should have parking spot, he dismissed me and very clearly acted as if he did not care. 
I immediately decided to go to the front desk. Traveling the parking lot felt like navigating a minefield full of urine and broken bottles of various alcoholic beverages. I was walking through a seedy bar, not a business and family friendly hotel. Before I got to the front desk, I passed the El Paso Police........doing there job arresting party revelers, a group of people who resemble the Hells Angels, and the Fire Marshall giving out tickets to people parked in the fire lane. 
Finally I go the the front entrance, again pushing through a pack of revelers, who by now had taken over the whole hotel. When I tried to speak to the hotel manager, I had to get in line as there were seven other disgruntled guests and one fire marshall who were pissed off enough to yell. 
In unison we angrily protested that it is 12 AM, we need to sleep there should be no club music blaring and that we have to put up with it. The manager basically tried to tell us that oh these are also "guests" EXCUSE ME......IF they did not PAY to SLEEP here THEY HAVE NO BUSINESS BEING HERE AT MIDNIGHT. To add insult to injury
when I called the hotline number the guy basically tried to shill that same excuse.
Finally at about 4 AM the music stopped. and eventually people went home.. and I decided never to stay at this place again. 
BTW : on a side note, my rental and my "nieghbour's" car had been vandalized. 
Luckily I had a damage waiver with my rental, but if I did not I would have sued 
Holiday Inn.

title: “Under construction, used to be here, you just missed it, etc. etc.”
text: Great location; service was not so great. Like other reviewers I felt it lacked character. My opinion is probably colored by the fact that the "gentleman" at the front desk was rude to me on check-in. There was a snafu with my reservations and I almost ended up with no place to stay and two teenagers in tow. I had spoken with Marriott directly and asked if this were the hotel next to Nordstrom on MI Ave, to avoid any confusion. They said yes, but apparently I had reserved with an outlying hotel. This one is IMMEDIATELY next to Nordstrom. The man at the front desk let me stay but told me "only this time" and then continued to lecture me. It was demeaning, but I was in a big city with no other decent reservations and felt stuck. I've stayed in Chicago many times and this is the only time I have almost cried at the front desk.
