The basketball court on the roof, which is advertised on the website, is no longer available - a disappointment to my children. They generally have only ONE elevator in service. The internet costs too much and works only sporadically. I paid for parking but the parking folks were not aware of it. The gift shop is not where it is supposed to be, never found it. The salon has moved. Nothing is where it is advertised in the hotel guide and half of the services are "out of service at this time". Almost nothing is as advertised or where/when it's supposed to be. Small rooms, but it is fine for a place to sleep in a good location. If you are accustomed to good service you will be disappointed and should take your business elsewhere. Perhaps it will be better once their renovations are completed.

title: “Great location but noisy pipes”
text: I loved the location and the view, but for the price I was disappointed. The room was no more than a standard hotel room, nothing special. The water pipes sounded like a jackhammer going off at 6am. The other issue is that one person has to take your luggage out of the car and into the lobby and another takes it to your room. This is not a resort, this extra handling is unnecessary .

title: “Charge for wirless...Really?”
text: This was a nice hotel but for the price wee paid I wasn't overly impressed. The biggest surprise was that the hotel charged $14.95 per day for wireless access. We stayed in the San Francisco area for 10 days at various hotels ranging from $69/night to $220/night. this was the only hotel that charged for wireless access.

title: “Fantastic stay”
text: We stayed at the Hamilton, Crowne Plaza Hotel from 20th May until 31st May 2012. We received a warm welcome from the reception staff and our luggage was taken to our room immediately. We were upgraded to an executive floor on our arrival, our room was on the top floor in the corner and it was light and airy. There is no refridgerator in the room but ice is freely available from a machine down the corridor. We found the staff to be very friendly and helpful at all times. Our room was cleaned well each day and it was very quiet in the evenings. Our complementary breakfast and access to the executive lounge helped to make our stay very special. Eden is a great host and welcomed us back each evening with delicious treats, we felt very pampered. Whenever we needed help from the concierge or at reception, the staff were always polite and friendly. The location is great and near to the Metro and the Mall. We would have liked to have had free wi-fi, but found a Starbucks a block away and took advantage of that. I would definitely recommend this hotel, we had a lovely stay.

title: “One of the best hotel stays ever”
text:
I would suggest staying at the SpringHill to anyone wanting to visit seattle.
The room was better then I expected, it was fairly large (king suite), certainly enough to accomidate 2 people. The staff was super friendly, even if you're just riding down the elevator together, they would ask how the day was doing .. what we plan on doing.. etc. The breakfast is amazing, by far the best free breakfast at any hotel that I've been to. The location is great, just 3 blocks from the bus station and the onramp to the highway is right in front. 
The $14 for valet kinda sucks, but it was included in our package and the valets are all good guys. There was a mix up with the keys and they apologized half a dozen times and you could tell they they felt really bad about the situation. 
People need to be realistic when it comes to lodging.. you're IN A HOTEL! Yes, there might be a hair or two in the room, and you might be able to hear slight hum of the highway (just ask for a room on the higher floors, we stayed on the 9th and it was pretty quiet)... and small things could go wrong, but just take it easy and let the staff take care of it. Unless you're paying a large amount of money ($200+/night), everything will not be perfect. 
For the quality, location, service and price.. springhill is hands down my top pick.

title: “Not the place for a romantic weekend!”
text:
Greeted by a cheery front desk associate who refused to depart from his memorized speech and routine to answer a simple question. Bad start. The hotel can't figure out if its a majestic hotel or chic nightclub. It is trying to be both and the conflict is a problem. On weekend nights, guests have to pass through bouncers and loud music and big chic crowds of twenty-somethings to get to your room.
Hotel is convenient to nice shops and bars in back bay area. Very convenient to the T.

title: “Ten Year anniversary”
text: Just spent a weekend for our 10 year anniversary. Very nice hotel. Told them we were celebrating our anniversary and when we checked in had a bottle of wine and a box of chocolates waiting for us. Great location close enough to walk to times square but far enough away to get away from the noise. Close to 5th ave. shops and central park. Service was outstanding. Served us in the Monkey Bar restaurant even though they were getting ready to close. we were the only ones in the restaurant which was a nice touch. The club room was great. Free wine and cheese during the week is a nice touch. Also serve free coffee and cookies all day. Great place to sit and relax! Would definitely recommend. Had a great time.

title: “comfortable and eclectic”
text:
1st of all Ben, good job with the Clarendon, sometimes you just cannot please everyone.
we were allowed early check in at around 11 am, wow! i was almost dying of exhaustion after climbing the camelback and the friendly staff kindly let us checked in 5 hours earlier than the regular check in time. 
i was going to whine about the AC (or lack of) in the room and the "elevator of death" as the previous reviewer put it but knowing that these problems are being looked into tell me that i am going back to Clarendon my next visit to Phoenic :)
i was extremely pleased to find out that the bed doesn't have the dirty useless bed spread because i am very likely to throw them on the floor as soon i see them anyway, and the sheets and pillows are very good quality, i had a very good night sleep despite not having the sheet on me (room was hot).
my husband had to remind me to mention about the out of order ice machine, and the craziness of the existence and non existence of the tv channel, they seemed to be disappearing.
we had to switch room after checked in for 3 hours because there was no wifi in the room, the staff made it very easy to move us to another room. have to mention about the shaded parking area, that's a big plus considering the high was 111F when we visited last week.
what you see is what you get from the hotel website, if bold colors and contemporary are not your cup of tea, you should probably check into a resort.
oh yea Ben, love the carpet! even considering getting something similar for the study.

title: “Great location and view”
text: We stayed in a one bedroom, Queen suite. The view from the living room was of MIchigan Avenue and the river. It was just great to watch the boat traffic on the river and all the shoppers on the street. The kitchen had a full size refrigerator etc. with plenty of dishes. The furnishings are comfortable and new. This is a very nice hotel. It is walking distance from Millenium Park and the Art Institue and a short cab ride to the Field Museum. Lots of great restaurants within walking distance in a great neighborhood for walking after dark.

title: “Nice hotel convenient to downtown and sports stadiums.”
text: Very nice property, I have gold status with Marriott and this is now one of my favorite properties. The rooms are nice with plenty of power for the business traveler, the lobby is modern with plenty of computers in the business lobby for flight check-in, and the workout room is fantastic not fancy but compared to other hotels a nice step-up.

title: “Superb in every way!!”
text: We stayed here for an anniversary celebration and ended up never leaving the hotel! The rooms were spacious (loved the Japanese soaking tub!), and the views were terrific, but it was really the service that made our stay incredible and will have us going back again. Champagne at check-in, every effort to get the exact room you want, attentive staff to your every need-it was almost too good to be true. The spa was lovely-much better than we expected for a downtown hotel, complete with men's and women's hamams. (Service was superb there as well). The real secret here is to upgrade to club access because the food is GOOD and the service amazing. (champagne served here, too!) We had so much tuna tartare that we cancelled our dinner rservations. The pool deck is great and they come by with chilled fruit cups and bottled water just as the sun is getting hot. Bellman was experienced and extremely helpful. Five star service and amenities all the way.

title: “Not 4 star”
text: This hotel is not 4 star - 3.5 max. Rooms are large but worn. Both ac units weren't working when I checked in and one kicked out again after fixing in the middle of a warm night. Bathroom was small and not very clean w make-up smudges on the walls and a tub that didn't empty well. Food in icon was fast and good but sausage raw. No mp3 player but good stereo. Could be a great place if redone.

title: “Comfortable, convenient and friendly”
text: My overall experience was extremely positive. The Westin is an attractive, centrally located hotel in downtown Philadelphia. From the front door, to the reception, to the concierge, EVERYONE was exceptionally friendly, knowledgable and helpful. My room was VERY comfortable and immaculately clean. Free wireless internet was a nice plus. I would certainly stay here again!

title: “Clean”
text: Good price and good stay!! Would love to go back and spend the time again...

title: “Great Service - Small Rooms”
text: The service at this Marriott was fantastic. Upon arrival, I was treated with the utmost courtesy and was checked in nearly 3 hours before the hotel's published check-in time. The lobby is nice and I excpected my room to be just as charming. Unfortunately the room itself was quite small and unimpressive. The two double beds in my room were teeny-tiny - making the room reminiscent of a dorm room for college students. Closet and dresser space were also limited. The marble bathroom was definitely the highlight of the room. I was very pleased with the breakfast buffet and the service in the restaurant. Overall, my experience here was average due to the disappointing room. My advice - if you choose to stay here, don't set your hopes too high. For a much lower rate, I was able to get a room at the Renaissance at LAX which was much nicer and more comfortable.

title: “Small Rooms, excellent location, great price.”
text:
Two blocks away from Shelter Island, across the street from the Sportfishing Landing, and in the heart of Point Loma, this motel features a full size mini-fridge and wi-fi (we didn't use). My husband took advantage of the breakfast of donuts, individually wrapped pastries, orange juice and coffee but I don't eat sugar so it was useless to me. Besides, with Perry's only a few minutes away, who'd fill up on that stuff?!
The bed was comfy, it was nice having the windows open and smelling the ocean air! But the rooms are small with a bed and folding chair in ours. The bathrooms were teeny and if you don't like sun shining into your room at 6:45am bring eye cover!
I think there might have been a second building and I'm certain had I been placed there I would have been let down and not prepared at all for it.
Overall it's a great price for a great location. I'd stay here again if I had something to do in the area, but otherwise, I think I'll continue looking for a San Diego gem.

title: “Nice and VERY convenient”
text: I've stayed here a number of times on business. It's a block from the convention center and the Light Rail stop, so very handy. Check in was quick and my room was ready when I arrived mid afternoon. My room was clean, had coffee and tea available and there were convenient electrical plugs in the lamp for both phone and laptop - big plus for us road warriors. The bed was way too soft for me this time and the sheets would not stay put. I've not had that experience here before, however. Annoying but do-able. During my latest stay, hotel staff easily accommodated a late check out, which was much appreciated.

title: “Great Experience”
text:
Stayed one night at the Embassy Suites and had a great experience. The lobby is beautiful and is a great first impression. My kids had a great time at the pool...found nothing wrong with it! 
The room was clean and plenty big. I'll admit that the couch and furniture in the den area could use some updating. 
My favorite part was the complimentary breakfast. It started at 6:00 am and was a continental plus "made to order". We had to leave for our flight before 6:00 am, but we were able to get a sample of some. There was plenty of muffins, danishes, toast, cereal, fruit, yogurt, etc. Great deal!

title: “A real treat”
text: Right on the riverwalk--beautiful hotel, even if I didn't really like the decor--quite modern and dark, but very glamorous. The room was beautiful, and we got a great deal, which included free valet parking. Stay away from the "Honor Bar" in the room, though: $6.00 for a bottle of water!, $4.00 for a pack of M&Ms! San Antonio is a wonderful place to visit, and this hotel was a joy to stay in.

title: “Overall pleased”
text:
Just returned from a three night stay at Marriott Gaslamp Quarter. Paid $229 per night for water view king standard room with AAA rate. 
This hotel has plenty of positive things going for it. Friendly & helpful staff greeting us by the curb and at the check in counter. Beautiful hotel throughout & doesn't feel like a chain hotel - very updated and modern for a Marriott. The best thing about this hotel is the LOCATION. Across the street from Padres stadium. We could see the people in the stands from our 18th floor room. One block from 5th Avenue, three blocks from Convention center & a nice 20 minute(?) walk to USS Midway. A few blocks away from Cafe 222.....very good breakfast place. 
The room itself was standard in size - just room enough for a wing chair with ottoman next to the king bed plus a desk with chair. The bedding and room finishes were very high-end and modern. The bathroom was not large but it also had nice high-end finishes that made up for it. The curved shower curtain rod was nice. The only gripe as far as the room goes is that we ran out of toilet paper on the morning we were to check out - thank goodness for kleenex. They never left us another roll after the initial extra roll at check in. That should never happen - how hard is it to start off stocking a couple of extra rolls just in case!? 
We were pleased overall with our stay and would stay here again in the future.

title: “Good Hotel, perfect location”
text:
This is a grate hotel for young copuls traveling to NYC.
We spened 5 nights.
It was clean, had a helpfull concierge.
Small rooms, but we did not go to NY to stay in a hotel so it did not matter.

title: “Great Convention Host”
text: Just spent 4 days at this facility. The staff is simply wonderful to work with. A great big Thank You to Darren, Moses and all the great staff that worked on the TAHV Convention. All rooms, from guest to meeting, were prepared and ready needed. Parking at this facility is some of the best around and with all the shopping and eateries within easy walking distance this is a great place to be.

title: “Unfriendly staff”
text: The manager at this hotel is not very accommodating to business travelers. Every business traveler knows that plans plans channge and the manager of this hotel charger me for a nights stay even through I had canceled the reservation before 6PM.

title: “Just what we needed”
text:
We stayed here one night prior to flying out on an early flight. As soon as we arrived we were asked, do you want a King, it will be $20 more, nope we don't need a King. Do you need parking? $20 more. We did, a little pricy, and didn't know about the price of parking by looking at the website prior. However to be honest the parking was abundent and secure.
I requested a very quiet room with NO adjoining room due to noise. Was given a key and lugged the bags up only to walk in and see an adjoining door. Back down to the lobby, given a new room. Back upstairs with bags, open the door, yup again an adjoining door. This time I called the front desk and was told a new key would be delivered. We went to the elevators to wait. After 10 minutes we went down to the front desk and got the key for ourselves. This time the room was perfect and was quiet.
Bed was very very comfortable, tv was new, amenities were great. Did encounter people smoking on our floor even though this is a non smoking hotel.

title: “Fantastic!!”
text: This facility is quite different. Beautiful grounds, very quiet, gorgeous facility and right next to the airport! I could hardly believe the location. It seems so quiet and secluded - but it's also very convenient. The staff is superb - extremely professional and customer oriented. We actually thought we were booking a hotel closer to downtown Seattle because of the address is Seattle. However, the location is really near the airport, and we did not realize the airport is a distance from downtown. But it was so lovely, and shuttle service is provided to the light rail, that we were glad we stayed here. The restaurant and lounge are exceptional, also. There are many meeting/conference rooms and not that many lodging rooms. Also, no gift shop, pool, spa or golf course, which was fine with us (in fact preferable). On each floor is a "living room" with sofas, books, TV and "goodies" like chocolate covered raisins, malt balls, bottled water, yogurt, string cheese, chips, and Hagen Das ice cream, all complimentary. We asked about the origins of the facility and learned that it was at one time the conference center for a large bank. After the bank fallout it was sold to a group of investors, including the investor of the Space Needle. The investment group converted it to a hotel open to the public. This explained why it is somewhat different, and quite special.

title: “Great price, even better location”
text: This was my second stay at the Executive Hotel in Seattle. It's very affordable if you're looking for someplace comfortable and in the heart of downtown Seattle. Rooms are a bit small, but clean and well kept. The hotel is within walking distance to just about every attraction, shopping, Pike's Place Market, the ferrys and Pioneer Square. Hotel staff is helpful and courteous. We grabbed coffee at the coffee shop right downstairs and there are an abundance of bars & restaurants within a few blocks for a quick bite. I would recommend this hotel to anybody looking for a no-frills, comfortable hotel for a few days.

title: “Nice hotel -- loved the location”
text:
My teenage daughter and I stayed for 5 nights in an executive king room. We were near the end of the hall on the 15th floor and the only noise we heard was construction at the school across the street one morning. Nicely remodeled room, on the small side but adequate for two. Bed was comfortable. Bathroom was nice but had no ventilation and no storage space. 
Front desk staff was pleasant but not overly friendly, concierge was helpful. Maid service was good, but they left our door ajar after cleaning one day and we didn't return until late that night. Luckily nothing was disturbed and we had our valuables with us or in the safe.
Loved the location within a quick walk to the subway, tons of restaurants, and theaters, but on a fairly quiet street away from the craziness of times square. Would stay there again.

title: “Beware of Overbooking”
text:
When I reserve a hotel room for over $500 a night I expect there to be a hotel room. This was not the case when my daughter and I arrived at the Renaissance. At 2:00 PM in the afternoon, after a delayed American Airlines flight, we were informed by the assistant manager that there was no room at the inn. They had overbooked 30 rooms because of a Radiologist Society of North America convention. They offered a comped and upgraded room at the Marriott Chicago Downtown, which was not where we wanted to be so we asked them to find something else. All of the other good hotels were booked so they drove us to the downtown hotel for one night. It was nice, but not what we wanted, so the next morning they drove us back to the Renaissance, where they upgraded our room and gave us two comped meals, breakfast and dinner. The comps and upgrades made the ordeal more acceptable.
After that we enjoyed the hotel and their amenities. The bar and restaurant were all very nice and the food was very good to excellent. The fitness rooms were also very nice. We never got to the pool, but I'm guessing that it met the hotel standards that I would expect from this establishment. We walked instead of taking the usual taxi. The location was very good when it comes to shopping and some theaters. I would definitely stay here again, but I think I would call the day before my flight and the day of my flight to confirm and make my previous experience known to the front desk.
Be sure to go to Second City for comedy, and see the "Jersey Boys" and "Wicked" when you visit. The art museums are something people should see as well. They were all great!

title: “good business hotel”
text:
stayed here one night on business.
I selected this hotel simply because the workshop that I was attending was held there. Seemed expensive, at ~$250/night, so I'd shop around if I were returning to the area. The hotel is about one mile from the airport, so very convenient in that regard. A complimentary shuttle runs every 15 minutes, and this is also a plus. My room (and based on what I saw, the other standard rooms) was not very big, but was well-appointed: luxurious king bed, chest of drawers, armchair with footstool, desk with work chair, Starbucks in-room coffee. The bathroom and amenities were nice. The room was clean and reasonably quiet. I did not bring my laptop, so can't comment on the internet connection, however, there is a business center with 2 computer stations where travelers can check email, etc, no charge. There is also a kiosk especially for doing airline web check-in so you can print your boarding pass, a nice touch. The hotel has an atrium, where the pool and jacuzzis are located. It is quite nice, with trees. The fitness room was better than I encounter at most hotels. They had a selection of cardio equipment: bikes, treadmills, elliptical trainers, plus some weight machines and free weights. There is a somewhat pricey cafe in the hotel. I had breakfast and lunch there. The food and service were good. There does not seem to be any other place to eat within walking distance. The staff were nice and courteous. Overall, I would recommend this hotel to a business traveler.

title: “very nice”
text: Entire staff was nice and helpful. Only downsides and they were few are low lighting in bathroom and ice only on even # floors. Staying there four days thats not a lot of problems for a nit picker. Very conveinient to SMU and premeir shopping locations.

title: “Overall, excellent hotel!”
text: My husband and I traveled with our two toddler children. The room was quite large, which is nice because we set up a travel cot and pack & play for the kids. Only a couple of minor complaints, one being there aren't really adequate hooks for hanging towels in the bathroom and I also wish the bathroom had a much stronger fan. Husband was impressed with the buffet, as he brought our food to the room and the staff accomodated our every need with trays and cups with lids.

title: “Great boutique hotel”
text:
Nice intimate setting in the heart of a big city. The customer service was outstanding. They really took the time to make us feel welcomed, even our 7mos beagle was treated special. 
The rooms are clean & the beds comfortable. If you like to avoid big crowds I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “slowest FREE wireless unless you want to pay for faster”
text:
FREE wireless was slower than a dial up modem, but feel free to pay extra for faster speed.
also.....stained carpet, broken lamps, peeling tub and shower surfaces, slamming doors, etc, etc, etc. 
Just stay elsewhere, there are a lot of options at LAX

title: “Enjoyed the hotel”
text: Humphrey'sLovely resort...great service. We enjoyed the view, pool, on site concerts. Location was 20 min from Park, zoo.

title: “VERY NICE HOTEL & STAY!”
text: Just came back today from a great stay at this hotel(Sat, May 26-Mon, May 28). We vallet parked @ $33 per night(which was a bit steep but comparable to the other Riverwalk hotels). Check in was a breeze and EVERYONE we came in contact with was super pleasant & acccomodating! We were greeted upon arrival, then sent over to the check in desk, where Tommy helped us and was incredibly friendly and attentive! We asked for a high level room and he accomodated us with room 1874. He told us where the pool, exercise room and restaurants were as well as what door to use to get us to the Riverwalk. He said the hotel was fully booked and we were a bit apprehensive about this but we NEVER had to wait for an elevator for an extended period. Our room was on the corner of the floor and was spacious and very clean. We had a cityview room and it was very nice. I'll admit, I was very apprehensive about this hotel. I initially won a bid off priceline and after I googled the hotel name, I was directed to a site about "bed bugs". It scared the pants off me! The reviews were all from 2011 and the first thing I did when I got to my room was check for them. The room was VERY clean and thankfully, none were found! The bed was very comfortable. Our room was cleaned by 11am, which was great for us! We spent a few hours at the pool and I love the poolside waiters! They were all very friendly. I did not like the Diamond Margarita that was made for me, so they took it back and asked if they could throw something "special" together for me. I agreed to it and the drink turned out to be VERY GOOD! Even for the hotel to be fully booked, we spent from 10am-2pm at the pool and never had issues with the area overflowing with people. We had Starbucks(Perks, is what the hotel calls it) and love how they aim to please with however you want your coffee made(Caramel Macchiato extra sweet). There are sooo many areas to sit and people watch, both inside and outside the hotel. We rapped up every evening at Bar Rojo with fresh sushi and drinks. THANK YOU MARIO for running the children out after 9pm even when the adults act like they can't read the signs and get upset at you doing your job! I applaud you at how you handle these situations as I witnessed parents flipping you off for doing so. I have children myself but I welcomed some time w/out all the noise! My husband and I really enjoyed our stay here and would do so again in a heartbeat! The hotel sits on the end of the riverwalk and it's PERFECT! VERY close to the Rivercenter Mall and we welcomed the little walk back every night. My only complaints would be that (1) They ran out of washcloths when they cleaned our room and we had to call room service for some and (2) They charged us for 2 vehicles, instead of 1 but they took it off immediately after we brought it to their attention-also the vallet told us we still owed and I had to show him my receipt. All in all, it was still a nice stay!

title: “Excellent Hotel in a Perfect Location”
text: We stayed in this hotel in December 2010. we thoroughly enjoyed our stay here, the location was perfect inbetween Katy and Galleria Area. Staff excellent, clean, comfortable and convenient. Parking wonderful. Laundry facilities, perfect for a family with kids. Nice family breakfast. Great atmosphere.

title: “Great location, clean, cheap, but Noisy”
text: As others have noted, this hotel is a great deal, given its location and price. And it was clean. But I have never stayed anywhere as noisy as this hotel. I literally wore my Bose headphones, turned on, both nights I stayed there. Even though it was cold out, the windows were in effect open because the ventilation unit was open to the street. Huge trucks honked their horns all night even when there wasn't traffic; it felt like I was in a bus terminal. And at 8am the pile driver on the construction site outside my door starting crashing down. And then some staff members sat right outside my door and settled into a very loud conversation (both mornings) so I had noise on both sides of my tiny room.

title: “Consistanly wonderful service and atmosphere.”
text: We have stayed in several Downtown Denver hotels - we go back to the Denver Magnolia!

title: “excellent choice”
text:
New building, good location close to the bus terminal and Tunnel exit, surrounding not pleasant. Good room amenities (incl a kitchenette), stylish modern design. Very long elevator wait time. The business center is a corner in the lobby with 3 public PC, long queues and a non-working printer.
Front staff was very helpful and kind, fast check-in and -out. Clean

title: “Everything a spa should be”
text:
This is a review of the Stoneleigh spa not the hotel.
Visited the spa with a Travelzoo coupon for a 50 minute massage. Arrived a little later than I wanted to so the guy at the desk led me right to the locker room. He did not give me a tour or explain the amenities but as I arrived right at my appointment time, that was understandable.
The spa is serene from the moment you walk in. I got my robe and slippers--the robe was the most luxurious robe I have ever had at any spa. I went right to the relaxation room where water and an assortment of organic teas was waiting. I got water and sat down on one of the comforable chairs. The room is dimly lit and quiet with nice chairs and footstools and even blankets. It was peaceful and serene which is what I love in a spa.
My massage with Leanne was fantastic, she listened to what I wanted, even providing a heating pad when I just happened to mention my feet were cold.
Afterwards, I sat and had some tea then changed into my suit and went and got in one of the two jetted tubs that are in the women's area--they are behind a curtain that said "Rainshower experience." There are two large tubs in this area and a private rainshower which I used after my soak. I finished my experience back in the relaxation room with one more cup of tea before I forced myself to leave.
The spa comes with all shower amenities as well as lotion, a hairdryer, brushes, combs and ponytail holders. At checkout, I was not asked for my Travelzoo voucher but was still only charged the 20% gratuity. The fact that I was using a voucher was never mentioned.
All in all, it was a wonderful spa day and of all the Dallas spas I've experienced, it was definitely one of the most relaxing. I plan to come back for spa week in April and am already looking forward to it--if I even wait that long.

title: “too expensive for what you get”
text: The outside river is great for kids, but the rooms compare to a motel 6! There is no room to turn around and they are dirty!!! We had bugs everywhere and the sheets looked as if they had not been laundered. Any resort that caters tofamilies should know that you need room for your family.

title: “Very decent but got the order wrong at first”
text:
We expressly asked for a roll away bed to go with our king size bed in our reservation, but when we got to the hotel, they informed us that they didn't have any left. This was going to screw things up royally since our daughter is no longer a toddler. They tried to call other hotels nearby to borrow one but to no avail. However, the young lady at the desk decided to give it another try in their own facilities and I followed her in to the laundry room where she found one tucked away in a corner. Happy just to have one, I didn't mind rolling the thing myself back to our room.
The roll away bed unfortunately was horrendous and our daughter complained of a backache the next day. The hotel was happy to move us to another room which had two queen beds at no extra charge. Fortunately, the second room was much more spacious and on one of the upper floors. With the exception of that first night, everything worked out fine. The staff was always courteous and helpful. 
The location is superb. It's a block and a half from Michigan Ave. and within walking distance to the Navy Pier. Lots of great restaurants in the neighborhood including the Capital Grille which serves outstanding steak. Have to have steak when in the Midwest, no question about that, and you have to have Chicago pizza when in Chicago. This hotel is within walking distance of all and at worst, a short cab ride away for those who don't like using their feet.

title: “Can Quirky Compete?”
text:
Hotel Max has gotten a lot of poor ratings. My experience did not match those. Service was excellent and the hotel did have artistic flare and sexappeal. Their restaurant food is excellent.
The biggest issue I have is with the bathrooms, which are the size of an airplane's. The sink is so small that you can't wash your face without soaking your feet. The toilet is located two inches from the wall. Worst of all, there was a huge 10 inch step up into the bathroom.
The other problem I had was with reservations. I made a reservation for four nights, but then found a special on their website that included parking and breakfast (after reading TripAdvisor reviews). The special was only available for the first two nights of my stay; I called reservations to confirm the new booking for the first two nights and retain only the last two nights of my first reservation. Of course when I checked in they had no reservation for the last two nights. The hotel was "completely sold-out" (someone in the hospitality industry can tell me what that means). The clerk could not get the manager to find us a room, but she did call other hotels until she found something. The positive outcome was that the other hotel was more comfortable.

title: “Great overnight stay”
text: I usually tend to flock toward Hampton Inns because they are so clean and nice. This one didn't disappoint me. We were on our way to California from Charlotte and needed a one night stay close to the airport. I had planned to stay the night, park in the extended lot at the airport and go about my vacation. I was surprised to hear from the desk help at checkin that they offered parking while you travel. So rather than paying $40 at the airport lot this Hampton inn provided free parking for 1 week and just $10 for any additional week. We were gone for 10 days so we only paid the $10. The lot was right next to the hotel and security was provided. THANK YOU HAMPTON INN... AGAIN! You have a loyal customer in us!

title: “Great location and amenities”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Drury in Sept 2010. We had a great room but the walk to the room from the lobby was quite long. The evening reception was nice. The location was great. Just a small walk to the main section of the river walk. Great bang for your buck.

title: “exercise room”
text: I was dissatisfied with the exercise room. They have only one stationary upright bike. By the time that it was vacant, I had to go to meetings and couldn’t do my work out routine.

title: “Why 4, 5 stars 1? Just 2 stars for me :(”
text:
The world known hotel chains, the one in Times Square NY is not much I liked. 
First, location ,location, location, that's why I did NOT like. There are many other hotels in other areas that easy to access, because of in the middle of Times Square, too crowded for blocks away in the morning to the late night, nothing is wrong with tourists but I hoped stay away from this area (the company booked this hotel, it was not my decision).
Second, too big anyway, even go to front desk, you need to go up from the street level, and then walk to guest room elevator, and elevator does not have security, meaning anybody can access to guest room levels, just complicated with weak security for $270/night hotel, don't you think ?
Third, attitude, management, I wanted to print my boarding pass for my flight on next day, so that I called to "guest assistance", I asked how can I print my boarding pass ? The operator hold my phone without saying anything and transferred to someone, and then same thing, and then the person #3 said I need to go the business center to do that, and she said I have to pay for using the BC ! I'm not staying at one of popular hotel for business people, and that's all you can do ? Again, this is not a cheap hotel, okay ? I complained for it, and this lady did transfer to the manager named Mr. Ibanez. Fortunately, this person did right thing finally, he asked me to send an email to him with the boarding pass in pdf, I did so and approximately 30 minutes later, one of employee delivered a hard copy of my boarding pass to my room :)
Finally, the room was not bad but nothing special except very nice Manhattan view from 29th floor, my room was typical Crown Plaza without refrigerator in the hot summer in NY, a nice big bed but I don't like this high bed flame, is that necessary this much high ? 
Anyway, I will definitely NOT come back this hotel, there are some cheaper and better hotels in Manhattan.

title: “Great location; great price.”
text: I typically stay at the Park Hyatt Washington when in D.C. The Phoenix Park clearly is not of the same caliber, but this time I wanted a hotel close to Union Station (the Phoenix Park is right across the street). The hotel is an older hotel, but is clean and comfortable. The room was of adequate size; the bed was comfortable. The Irish pub downstairs was nice and the hotel was convenient for a run on the Capital mall. For the price, the Phoenix Park was a tremendous value.

title: “Was hesitant about this place, but now It's my new first choice!”
text:
This is long review-- I have so much to say about this place!
I travel to San Diego 6-8 times a year, and I always stay downtown. I have about 4 or 5 usual haunts that I typically choose from, but this last trip, EVERYTHING was booked. I finally called this place and they had a room. I took it, only knowing that it was on 2nd street (I'd seen the sign from Broadway). After looking at the website I was a little bummed, thinking I was going to hate it. I like hotels with modern styling usually and typically stay at places like the W. This place did not look like my style at all from the photos. I was thinking it would be a musty old grandma type of place. 
And then I got there. 
Walking into the lobby is impressive. It's definitely an old European style that comes off horribly unless opulent enough to be glamourous and elegant. This place pulls it off. The staff at the front desk was very nice. The room was the biggest hotel room I've ever stayed in. Big corner tub in the bathroom, HUGE vanity with stool, four comfortable chairs in the room, and wall-to-wall, floor-to-ceiling window with an AMAZING view (I could see the harbor from my room, along with much of the beautiful downtown area). The photos of the rooms you see on the site don't do it justice at all. There's sliding glass doors and a cute little Juliet balcony. It is a bit outdated (I can't remember the last time I've seen a tube television in any of the hotels I frequent) and the furnishings are older, but very well maintained. The location is unbeatable, walking distance to 100s of bars and restaurants, and about a 15 minute walk to the convention center or Petco Park. While I loved the room, the view, and the whole feel of the place, what really set it apart was the service. Every night at 8, (I was usually not in my room) they'd come in for turn down service. When I got back, the bedspread was removed, leaving a pretty white duvet , sheets turned down, chocolates, dressing robe, and a card on the bed with the weather for the next day, ice, free bottled water, and classical music playing...it was heavenly. The room service was friendly, fast and amazing. The big food portions were hot and delicious and in my room 15 minutes after I called, with all the trimmings and a fresh rose. The staff was kind and willing to help at every turn. 
Downsides: I mentioned the TV already, and the bed was a bit hard. Not an issue for me because I like a firm mattress, but it's far from one of the best I've slept in. There's a lot of street noise (maybe because of the big window?) but it's par for the course downtown. Also, parking is valet only and $28/night, but this is standard for pretty much anywhere you stay in downtown San Diego. 
Can't wait to go back!

title: “Perfect place to stay in NY”
text: I booked this hotel after reading reviews on various websites, including tripadvisor. It is a fantastic hotel, I can't think of a bad thing to say about it. The postition is fantastic. The subway is not really that far from the hotel, and we found we didn't use it much anyway as the hotel is walking distance from some of the main attractions. The room was HUGE by New York standards. The room was cleaned to perfection every day.... the cleaners even folded clothes that we had left out to dry!!! The room/hotel facilities are fantastic and the Top Of The Tower bar is a must. The view is superb as are the drinks. The hotel staff were amazing, always helpful, friendly. Everytime you would walk through the door they would ask how you were or wish you a nice day. I stayed there when the transport strike was on and they were so helpful with any information needed. I honestly can't say enought about how great this hotel is. I would recommend it to anyone!!

title: “Beware of the NY super sized roach!”
text:
I booked a one night stay at the Essex House for my husband and myself. We live in Long Island, but just wanted to be "tourists" in the city. The hotel is in an excellent location. Not far from all of the most desired locations one would like to see in NY. It's directly across from Central Park. We didn't get a park view room, but we did book a King bed on a high floor. The check in was very quick, the front desk was extremely pleasant. We were given a room on the 16th floor. There weren't any surprises with the booking. We were given a King bed and a marble bath just as described during the booking. The room was very comfortable. We just weren't "wowed" by the room. 
What upset me the most was that the next morning, we found the LARGEST roach you could imagine "hanging out" in one of the corners of the room!!!! I was SOO happy that we were on our way out when we noticed it!!! Listen, I know NY...I was born and raised here and have seen a lot, but how did this "bugger" show up on the 16th floor in of ALL rooms....ours??? 
Unfortunately, this is my memory of the Essex House....the bug. However, for those that are lucky enough not to encounter a bug, it's not a bad place to stay. The morning of our check out, we were still planning on doing some sightseeing and we were able to store our luggage at the hotel until we returned without any hassle. The staff was definitely accommodating.

title: “Stylish hotel in perfect location!”
text:
My boyfriend and I booked a room at Hotel Union Square through Hotwire on a last minute July 4th weekend trip to San Francisco. After reading the reviews about how tiny the standard rooms are and seeing as how cheap we got the room in the first place, we decided to upgrade to the Executive King Room for an extra $20 a night and I am so glad we did. First off, we were greeted very warmly and enthusiastically by the front desk staff when we checked in and were offered help with our luggage.
We stayed on the 2nd floor facing the courtyard so we avoided hearing a lot of the street noise at night. The hallway felt like you were walking in a trendy bar or a brothel, very low lighting and red and grey carpeting. The room was huge with modern looking furniture but still has that old building feel (and smell unfortunately. It smelled a bit musty in the hallway and in the room). The lighting was a bit dim (even when we turned up the dimmer switch) although the LED bedside lamps were excellent for reading. The bed and pillows were super comfortable and the ceiling fan kept us cool at night. The bathroom was nice and clean even though I would have preferred a bigger counter space. 
Hotel parking rate at $30 a day was a little steep but considering parking for a day at Fisherman's Wharf on 4th of July can run you $40 I guess it's okay (at least by SF standards). The hotel is a few steps away from the main cable car line so getting around the city was easy especially if you buy a Muni day pass. The location is also perfect for shopping since H&M and DSW are right across the street and Westfield Shopping Mall is only a couple of blocks away. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay at this hotel!

title: “No doubt about it..this is a good hotel”
text: Just left after a long weekend in DC. You just gotta love this hotel. Staff is very friendly and helpfull. They truely surprised us! Charming room on the 3rd floor. Very clean and nicely decorated. Smaller bathroom but everything you need was there. Room had a desk, chairs, flatscreen tv, comfy bed, minibar...even an umbrella was provided. Hotel is only 2 minutes from chinatown, within walking distance of the whitehouse and all the museums. Area felt very safe! Valet parking for just over 35 dollar per day. Checking in & out went really smooth and fast. Absolutely a very good hotel. Beautiful building, very well maintained and just one of those hotels you would recommend to anyone you know. Thanks for a great weekend!

title: “Not top of the Mark anymore”
text:
We love San Francisco and keep going back, but each time we've tried different hotels in different areas ranging from Fishermans Wharf to the Market Street/Union Square area, and this time we opted for Nob Hill.
So we stayed at the Mark Hopkins for 3 nights over a long September weekend; and as a platinum IHG Priority Club member I used my points to pay for the stay. So I can't really comment on rates; except to say that had we had to use our own money for our SF accommodations we would have probably chosen somewhere else.
Let's start with the pros:
First off, the Mark Hopkins isn't a bad hotel, it's just that it was once a grand old lady, and now is more of a convention or business type hotel. It still has some nice character features and charm, such as the antique postal chute at the elevators, and the location is pretty good, depending on your reasons for visiting SF most things are accessible; there are 2 cable car lines intersecting a block from the hotel. The beds are pretty comfortable, which is always an important consideration when like us you've been travelling for 15 hours, and are in a totally different time zone. The staff are also fairly friendly, particularly the porters who were all very helpful and always seemed in good spirits.
However, for us there were also some unfortunate cons:
The soundproofing on the rooms isn't good at all. We were often disturbed by other guests flushing their toilets, and by people walking past in the corridor; plus as our room was on a fairly low floor, overlooking the front of the hotel where the porters use a loud whistle to attract taxis for guests, this would disturb us late into the evening, and again early in the morning.
The rooms themselves were fairly small by US standards, with very little storage for guests with a reasonable amount of luggage (SF was the start of a 2 week vacation for us). I guess it's due to the age of the hotel; but as I mentioned earlier as a platinum Priority Club member one of the perks is an upgraded room; so if ours was small I would imagine the standard rooms would be even smaller.
Breakfast at the Top of the Mark was the most disappointing element of the whole stay though. We happened to go up there on a foggy morning, which of course is not the hotels fault, but we didn't obviously get the famed view as an accompaniment to breakfast. However without anything of a view but a blanket of white to look at out of the windows, then it brought the breakfast itself into much sharper contrast. 
The breakfast was a very average buffet; if you travel at all for business it's the same breakfast you'll have had time and time again at just about every chain hotel out there. We didn't go particularly late for breakfast, but there was very little of it left, and what was there had clearly been out for some time. So the selection we were faced with almost felt like the leftovers that other people hadn't wanted. Also we felt that the prices being charged were way too high. This was the most we were charged for breakfast anywhere in California, and that included some individually prepared gourmet breakfasts (with gourmet coffee and freshly squeezed OJ) at five star resorts in the Napa Valley - which isn't exactly known for it's good value. 
Our last gripe with the breakfast, was that along with the bill came a 'guide to gratuities for international guests' suggesting an 18-20% gratuity on top of the already very high bill. Now we really don't have a problem tipping for good service, and we are fully aware that service staff in the US rely on tips to make up for low wages; but we found it offensive to suggest a gratuity of that level for a very ordinary buffet - where nothing at all was prepared fresh for us, no-one took an order from us, or brought anything to the table for us and other than a busboy filling our coffee there was no other actual 'service' involved.
A few blocks away from the hotel down the hill towards Union Square is a bit of a cliched but charming nonetheless, 50's style diner, which prepares fresh food, has friendly and efficient service; and which blows away the breakfast at the Top of the Mark. Not to mention it costs about half as much. For us there was no comparison.
If you do choose to stay at the Mark Hopkins, then one other tip for you: We bought MUNI cards for the duration of our stay after being advised that they were the most economical way to use the cable car to avoid having to walk up and down the steep hills in the area. However on a September weekend, the cable car itself is a major tourist attraction and not really a reliable method of public transport. We would wait at the cable car stops for ages and ages, whilst car after car would go by completely full up with people. At the terminus on Market the queue would often be in the region of an hour or so wait. It's almost like relying on the 'Pirates of the Carribbean' ride at Disneyland for your transportation. So in the end we used a 3 day MUNI pass for two cable car trips, and walked up and down the hills every other time; so they didn't turn out to be such great value for us as we'd hoped. Luckily we were fit enough for that not to be a problem, but that's us, we happen to like walking.

title: “Nestled in the heart of downtown El Paso, the Camino Real Hotel is a historic treasure that makes you feel like stepped back in”
text:
I recently stayed at the Camino Real Hotel for the first time. Based on my experience, it will definitely not be my last! The hotel itself is beautiful. The instant I walked in I felt as though I traveled back in time. The Dome Bar inside the hotel is also charming. A jazz band played as hotel patrons sipped their spirits. It was very classy indeed! 
Our hotel room was very spacious and the beds were very comfortable. But besides the many amenities the Camino provides, the hotel staff made our stay all the more enjoyable. Will Varela, the front desk supervisor, was especially helpful. He gave us great recommendations on what local bars to visit and also arranged our transportation to the Union Plaza, a bar district in downtown El Paso. 
Thanks again Camino! I cannot wait for my next visit!

title: “Great value if you just need somewhere to sleep”
text:
We went to Denver for a three night getaway. Chose this hotel because of the price (we don't spend much time in the hotel when we travel).
Good:
This was the lowest priced hotel among the various packages (we don't spend much on accomodations when we only intend to sleep there) so take that into consideration. The place was clean and service was very helpful. I have to admit we didn't plan our trip very well (last minute thing) so I had to bother the front desk frequently for recommendations on dining, entertainment, and transportation, and each time they were very friendly, patient, and offered great advice. Parking at the hotel is free as is internet use and complimentary breakfast. The rooms were clean and we had a great view of the mountains even without the optional upgrade. The hotel was about a five minute walk to the lightrail which took us straight to downtown Denver.
Bad:
The complimentary breakfast was very limited (some muffins, cold cereal, juice, coffee) but, again, it was a budget hotel. The indoor pool is just an oversized bathtub so if you plan on getting your swimming time in at the hotel you may want to make other plans. It seemed clean enough, but unless you have it to yourself, it may be a bit awkward, especially since one wall of windows faces the traffic (you could sit in the pool and wave at cars waiting at the red light). The beds were like sheets of plywood. I actually liked it since I have back trouble but I think anyone else would find it uncomfortable (my wife did). One of the beds in the room actually sloped to one corner - just unacceptable considering that this isn't something that could go unnoticed by housekeeping staff and reported to the management. The hotel is quite a distance from the airport and I think it's a $30 cab ride since there are no shuttles offered by this hotel. We just opted for the extra rental car day since it worked out the same.
Summary:
If you are like us who just check-in, get dressed, go out, come back to sleep, wake up early, and leave again, then this place will serve your needs quite well. All in all, for the price we paid, I was rather pleased, especially with the staff.

title: “Solid”
text:
My wife, 11yo daughter, and I just completed a 5 night stay at the Casablanca. I am not going to gush and say "greatest ever" or "can't wait to return" but felt the hotel definitely met our needs. It is clean, quiet (we were in room 309, a Jr. Suite at the back side of the hotel), and comfortable. Please note other reviewer's comments re noise at the front of the hotel. Housekeeping was excellent- room always looked great when we returned daily. Please see other reviews re "Rick's"- it was a nice extra. There is a free computer with internet in Rick's but I was able to use my laptop via a wireless network named "Casablanca".
 Pros: Location was convenient and close to major subway stop (NY Port Authority/ Times Square). You can walk easily to the harbor cruises, Rock. Ctr, Empire St. Bldg, Central Park, etc. Times Sq (you're right there) is VERY touristy and crowded but the hotel is just off the major crush of people and is like an oasis of calm. Room was not large but efficiently designed. Bathroom clean, excellent water pressure in shower, AC worked well but fan stays on continuously. Overhead room fans were also nice. Room had a safe lager enough to hold our small MacBook laptop (amazingly, when I called the hotel the person told me their safe's were too small to hold a laptop). Towels were adequate and were changed twice daily. 
 Cons: front desk folks were polite and pleasant but I did not find the restaurant suggestions to be that great. They seem to quickly suggest the place next door (Tony's) when there are tons of better places within easy walking distance. I asked for a suggestion for a special place to take my wife for our anniv. and never got an answer. I was told they would send up a bottle of Champagne (which never arrived). I would HIGHLY recommend buying a Zagat restaurant guide (a small paperback book). It was spot-on in it's reviews and even categorized restaraunts by location (eg, W 40's), cuisine, view, special occaision, etc. I felt that the front desk staff had basic knowledge and were decent with directions but they really aren't (by training or professsion) a real concierge. 
 Also, bathroom lacked counter space although they had a small set of drawers to put things in.
 Neutral: Room furnishings and beds, and linens were decent. One flat screen TV and one reg TV in the suite. Variety of food, wine, cheese, drinks at Rick's was limited (NOT a great variety as described by others) and got old quickly for me. Nevertheless, it WAS nice to have the option of having it. Free newspapers to read as well was a nice touch.
 OK, if you've read this far: Hotel has a very high percentage of European travelers. Likely word of mouth and strong Euro and Pound. No one was unpleasant but our experience was that interaction/ conversation was very limited (some reasonably based on language differences). Others seemed indifferent, shy, aloof, I don't know. I enjoy talking to other guests and this hotel was not positive for us in that regard. Take it for what it's worth. It was my disappointment and not an indictment of all European travelers.
 Overall, the hotel met our needs but it is unlikely that I would stay again based on the huge variety of lodgings available in NY.

title: “Very nice stay here”
text:
We just spent 3 days in SF and at the Argonaut. The front desk was very helpful and let us check in 6 hours early when we arrived and even upgraded our room.
The nautical, yet modern theme of the hotel is very nice and the room was clean and roomy. The noise from the streets was a bit noisy at times but the sound of the famous cable cars was kind of fun to hear from our room. For some reason neither one of us could comfortable in our beds though. Not sure if it was us or the mattresses though.
The staff at the restaurant was nothing short of amazing! Friendly, smiling and always willing to strike up a conversation. The location of hotel is a bit touristy but close to almost every great neighborhood, either by foot, bus or cable car. Thanks Argonaut!

title: “Overpriced, poor value, and needs renovating!”
text:
I am staying at this hotel now for the third time within three months. My client requests that I stay here but if I had a choice, I would avoid this hotel at all costs.
First of all, I guess because of its location, in downtown Washington and just two blocks from the White House, it is incredibly expensive. I have stayed here at my client's request and have gotten their "discounted rate", which is $365 per night! And what does one get for that rate? Its easier to state what one doesn't get.
At that rate, Internet service is not free. It costs an additional $14 per night. If you are a Hilton Honors Gold or Platinum member, then of course your internet is free. 
The hotel is old and every room I've stayed in, including my current one, is in the oddest layouts I have ever seen in hotels. My room now has a sofa with no lights or tables next to it. As I am sitting here typing this. I need to have my entryway light on so I can see. When I checked in last night I ordered room service, but there was nowhere for me to eat! The person who brought up my food had to leave the cart in my room so I can eat off of it. I do have a desk, but it is in an alcove, facing the wall!
I've been in rooms where the TV is so far away from the bed that if I want to watch TV in bed, I need to raise the volume so I can hear it. These rooms are old and need major renovations.
The bathrooms are small. And this time, for whatever reason, the water pressure in my bathroom is incredibly low. I notified the Front Desk about it this morning but no follow-up and no change in the water pressure.
The TV itself is a wide screen HD with plenty of HD channels, so that's one positive about this hotel. 
Another positive is the location. It is within two blocks of the White House and an easy walk there. Also within walking distance are a variety of restaurants, shops and other government buildings and museums. Metro has two stops that are a short walk from the hotel, so if you wanted to go visit other parts of DC, it is very doable.
Overall, this Hilton does not meet my expectations of what a Hilton hotel should be like, I would stay here only if you have to. There are other hotels all around, which I'm sure are just as expensive as the Capital Hilton, but I'm sure in much better shape.
If you decide to stay here; Buyer Beware!

title: “Great location, nice to be in Embassy Row”
text: I like the feel of this neighborhood, next to all the embassies in dc, two blocks from dupont circle. Very nice. The hotel is a nice mix of historic and modern, pretty good service. I would recommend.

title: “great price, excellent service”
text: We stayed here 3 nights recently and the first room we were in could not get internet -- it was the furthest room from the main lobby. The reservations manager immediately gave us another room, no questions asked, and it was a much better and bigger room -- all at no extra charge. But I was at the front dest several more times and saw people come in with various concerns and each time, the person at the desk was amazingly patient and accomodating. We stayed here becasue it was one of the least expensive, but the room was very nice and the service was way above par.

title: “dirty net curtains”
text: staff were very helpful and friendly and the hotel was ideally situated for Time square,central park etc ,i would stay at this hotel again ,The only snag was the net curtains were filthy and the doors in the room were dirty ,

title: “Great service”
text:
We stayed at the Surrey for 3 nights before a cruise to the Caribbean from New Jersey. We used it as a base and didn't eat there; the breakfasts seemed quite expensive and there are loads of great diners in the area which give a great feel for the City.
The room was first rate and could not be faulted; comfortable, large beds with excellent bedding. A tea and coffee maker would not come in amiss however. The service in the hotel was attentive and discreet.
The hotel is well positioned for access to great shopping, and even better for the Whitney and Guggenheim galleries. We used taxis a lot and found the fares very reasonable. Ground Zero was very moving and is being made into a very appropriate memorial. The UN HQ is worth visiting as is Grand Central Station which is close by.
All in all, a great place to enjoy New York and prepare for our cruise. We can thoroughly recommend it. We'll be back to enjoy more of New York!

title: “Awesome hotel experience”
text:
We arrived at Hotel Palomar whose decor is modern elegance. Because the room was not quite ready, we were invited into ther bar/lounge for cocktails of our choice. Within a few minutes the room was ready. The furnishings, design, cleanliness and linens over the top. A bottle of champagne, fresh strawberries with a chocolate dipping sauce awaited us, gratis. 
There is a fabulous 17th floor terrace with great views and lots of cushioned seating to enjoy your own byob drinks along with a indoor lap pool and gym. Each evening 5-6pm, there is wine tasting and yummy flatbreads. The staff are courteous, warm and friendly. We highly recommend the Hotel Palomar.

title: “Adorable”
text: This hotel is tiny but mighty. If you're used to cruise ships and Europe, the rooms will suit you just fine. Quite an affordable price for being so incredibly well-located. I would recommend to any experienced traveler.

title: “Excellent hotel at great value”
text: Excellent location in downtown SF, overlooking Union Square. The lobby had a modern feel to it and the rooms was large and comfortable. The view from my room (on the 22nd floor) was stunning. The service (especially the concierge) was great. All of this was for a price of about $125 a night, which was very low given the location (at least one other hotel in the area was asking for twice that).

title: “Professional, friendly staff in a beautiful hotel”
text: Chose this hotel due to the excellent impression made by a senior hotel manager and later by all staff we encountered. Room was quiet, clean and had a beautiful view of Times Square. Location convenient to everything in midtown Manhattan, especially the theater district. Will stay here again based upon this satisfying experience.

title: “Great Weekend”
text: We had a great weekend at the Hotel Monaco, a mother-daughter getaway. We arrived Saturday morning by train and were able to check into our room at 10:00. We requested a coffee maker and goldfish at check-in. The coffee maker arrived within minutes, and the goldfish arrived in the afternoon. The window seat was absolutely fantastic. From the 7th floor we were able to watch the city below, including the river. If at all possible, get a window seat! Theaters and shopping are all convenient - easy and enjoyable walks. The staff always welcomed us and seemed to enjoy their jobs. The room was well-appointed and comfortable. The el (elevated train) turns a corner near the hotel, and is loudly squeaky outside, but it didn't bother us in our room. Great hotel, great weekend! We'll definitely be looking at Kimpton hotels in other cities in the future.

title: “One Night at HI Kearny-Mesa”
text: Stayed one night at Hampton Inn Kearny Mesa - Clean rooms, comfy beds. Staff was super nice and helpful. Good location to Mission Valley area and a quick hop on the freeway to downtown. Neighborhood is a little run down, but we felt safe. Breakfast was good. Would stay again.

title: “One of the best hotel stays***”
text:
1st the bad-Checked in with Jeffrey upon arriving. Jeff didn't seem to know what he was doing. Our room was prepaid via Priceline, but Jeff claimed he couldn't locate our ressie. He did a manual ressie and charged us $0.00 for the room since it was prepaid. Lo and behold when we checked out we found out that we were charged $126.03 for unscheduled cancellation?????? Can't refund our money for 5 business days....
Now the good~ Our room 253 was absolutely wonderful. The furniture, bed, and wall decor was gorgeous. The king bed was the most comfortable bed I've ever slept on including my own. The rain forest type shower head was the best...Everything was very well laid out for a Holiday Inn....Even the hot continental breaksfast was nice....Kudos to Holiday Inn Express.
The only downfall is the location..Not a nice neighborhood at all...And BEWARE the parking is not free ($10.00 per day), but there aren't signs posted anywhere to tell you that it is not free...It should be free because no one would want to park their car in this neighborhood without it being in a gated lot.

title: “Good Airport Hotel”
text:
We stayed here for a night before a cruise. The weekend rate ($79), made it well worth the money. As you would expect, it is your average business hotel. It was clean with good pool, bar and rooms. Nothing fancy. Pickup at the Airport was fast with a shared van (hotels share van service). Some tips:
Restaurants at Marriott next door were pretty good. They have 3 
If you rent a car, you can pick it up at Marriott (Hertz) next door. You can save $20/day on average vs an airport rental. Just take van to hotel then walk next door.

title: “Close to Times Square”
text:
A very clean and busy hotel only minutes from Times Square and all the nearby attractions. Before travel I emailed the hotel for a room near the top, and was put on the 50th floor which was great (hotel has 52 floors). The view from the window was of a skyscraper that was getting built, but with the excellent soundproofing there was not a problem.
Room was large with a good size bathroom. Safe, iron, and hairdryer also in the room. No problem leaving luggage as we arrived early and could not get in the room until 4pm, same on departure with a 12pm checkout time.
One tip is, if you have booked a return transfer, do not call the company from the hotel as I was charged $26 for a less than four minute call from the hotel room.

title: “Great Hotel, Location and Value”
text: My two granddaughters and I stayed one night and were very satisfied with the service, the cleanliness and the breakfast. We arrived early and was able to check-in at noon instead of waiting for 3:00pm. Our room was adequate and enough room for the 3 of us. The location was perfect; we were able to walk to all the attractions. We will be staying here again for our future visits.

title: “Excellent Stay at Sofitel Washington DC”
text:
Sofitel Washington DC
Date: Nov. 18 & 19, 2008
I have just returned from a two night stay at the Sofitel Washington DC. Wow, what service!!! Nothing about this hotel was a disappointment. As usual, DC was crowded and hotel rooms were in short supply. The Sofitel Management at the hotel worked with myself and my business partner to ensure that we had the extra room that was needed at the last minute. 
What an experience, from the time we got out of the cab until we left the hotel, the service was impeccable. Denis Dupart, the General Manager, and his staff, makes sure that every need is taken care of. The restaurants are wonderful, with quick breakfasts for getting to those meetings in time, and the bar, (apparently a local favorite) was great. Rooms were beautiful with more than the usual amenities, and spotlessly clean.
This was my second visit to the Sofitel in Washington DC for business, and it will be the only hotel I stay at on future trips.

title: “Comfortable and central”
text: Stayed here recently. Was upgraded on arrival to a premium room. Clean, modern room with good central heating in early March. Bathroom was small (common in NYC hotels) but clean. Good location, close to supermarket on 6th Ave near 55th. Overall, a very good hotel and a satisfying stay at a centrally-located, Midtown hotel close to everything.

title: “Brilliant stay at The Hilton!”
text:
Universal City was the first stop for us on a trip from NZ to LAX/Vegas/Cabo San Lucas, so after a 12 hour flight the Hilton was bliss!
About a half hour drive from the airport and check in was a breeze. We were tired so ordered room service and had an excellent burger- this was the only time we used the hotel for meals, as we spent all other time just up the road at CityWalk.
Universal Studios the next day was fantastic although the 'June Haze' in LA was a little disappointing- still managed to get a bit sunburnt through! Cannot recommended the 'Front of Line' passes enough at the Studios- we were straight on all rides and spent most of the day in the park. Food inside was expensive but you could leave and go to something like Subway at CityWalk, and then head back into the park later.
The best thing about the hotel is its location and closeness to Universal Studios and CityWalk. Honestly, we had the best time each night at CityWalk, eating out and popping into some bars. Its open until at least 2am each night and stores are also open until 11pm I think.
Best places to eat and drink at CityWalk: Saddle Ranch Chop House (amazing T-Bone) and great bars like Howl at the Moon (something like that) and also the Brewhouse.

title: “Excellent overnight stay without reservations”
text:
There's a reason we're Marriott Rewards members. This was a quick "going-through-town" stay on our way home from Arizona. We didn't have reservations. Rate was under $80. Free wireless internet. Easy access to IH-10.
Room was spotlessly clean, bed was extremely comfortable, shower was strong and hot. We liked the fact that the vanity sink was separate from the shower/tub/commode room. Our view left something to be desired but that didn't matter to us. 
They offer a buffet-style breakfast for an additional $11 per person, but we didn't stay for that in the morning. However, Marriott is known for its good food.

title: “Elegant Hotel, not the usual chain atmosphere”
text: Stayed at the Nob Hill Hotel for one night. It has the feel of a small Parisian hotel. The first thing I was greeted with upon my late arrival was wine and cheese they serve in the beautiful lobby every evening.After that I took the 1920s elevator to my room. It was tiny but very stylish, with Art Deco design. If you are into spacious rooms and hotel chain's familiar feeling, this is not the place for you. Yet, if you want a European feel that would add to your overall SF experience, I highly recommend this affordable hotel.

title: “Fantastic hotel”
text: My husband and I traveled to Chicago for baseball games. I was really nervous about staying at a hotel that we weren't familiar with. But boy was I wrong. I booked this hotel through hotels.com. We were pleasantly surprised. Everyone was so helpful and pleasant. We had a wonderful stay at a reasonable price. It was a great trip and we will stay at the hotel again. The rooms were very nice and spacious. It was walking distance to Cellular Field and a short cab ride to Wrigley, Navy Pier, and the airport. It was perfect. The hotel was only 3 years old in an area that is building up. We couldn't have asked for anything nicer. Compliments to the staff and hotel management. You have diamond in the rough.

title: “Outstanding service and staff!”
text:
I arrived on a Thursday afternoon and was welcomed by three front desk staffers who could not have been more accommodating! From the valet to the waitstaff in the restaurant, service was excellent, friendly, and overall superb! 
Hilda quickly answered questions about my bill and there were several members of the staff who asked if there was anything I needed . Superb! The waitstaff were fun, professional, and really friendly. I will definitely stay here again when in Houston!

title: “A week in NYC”
text:
My company put my partner and I up at the Alex for a week. We had a 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom suite on the 16th floor. The suite was great, although there were some "flaws". There was not a lot of dresser space. Although their was a lot of closet space. One of the closet doors would not close due to being to close to the wall.
Loved the room, Loved the big bathroom, loved the maid service and over all staff. Was not so fond of the front desk staff.
One major draw back was that they wanted to put a 5,000 hold on my credit card. When I told them my co. was picking up every thing, they said they would not put a charge on my card. When I did check out, I found that they had put a 4,000 hold on my card. They did not seem to care to much about it when I asked them about it.
I would only stay there again if my co was paying the bill.

title: “Pricey, Ok, Rooms aren't very clean, super staff otherwise”
text: The grounds are nice. The meeting space is ok. Giant stains on the carpet. The staff is very accomodating. No coffee makers in the room-unheard of. Location is ok., $15 to downtown La Jolla in a cab. My room had dried liquid of various colors on the wallpaper, a gob of tooth paste on the bathroom door and the tub took an hour to drain. The maids did not clean my tub. When I went to take my second shower all my hair was still in the tub. There were seeds on my carpet (maybe trail mix?). The nice flats screens are blurry, not a clear picture. Restaurant on site are very nice but very $$$. Plumbing is so loud, when others use it above you. No b usiness center - no practical for a business hotel. Nice pool. Fitness club is like $13/day.

title: “Not a child friendly hotel and the worst customer service”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights with my spouse and two children. We slept with a fan every night because the A/C doesn't cool the whole room. The hotel said an engineer would come up the first night and he never showed. The next morning they said someone would check it and when we returned for the evening it wasn't checked. Finally an engineer came up on the second night and stated that some rooms cool better than others. The next day the manager said she would find another room, check it herself, and make sure it is cool. When we returned the receptionist didn't know anything about it, no plans to change rooms was made. The last night we took the kids to the pool in the early evening only to find that the hotel allows people from the community to join as members to swim in the pool and has pool parties. It was 6pm but it looked like 10pm at a strippers bar. My 6 year old witnessed a woman raise her skirt and a man feel her private parts. The girls were dancing very seductive, everyone was drinking beer and the music was like a club. I was shocked and highly offended. This is my last night. We enjoyed the city but would never recommend this hotel to anyone that we cared about. 
The staff is very unfriendly and uncaring. I have traveled all over the states and this was by far my worst ever experience. The only reason we stayed was because the hotel was paid through 1800 hotels. Needless to say, I will not use them in the future so that I have the freedom to leave a bad hotel if I choose. I hope you choose a better hotel than we did.

title: “We missed the Courtyard Marriott Long Beach”
text:
Ok, so it's an airport hotel. But - it's not cheap. The lobby is nice (although single story) - there is also a large shop and three restaurants. 
The room first. We checked in with a coupon for the night (but under an elite reservation). We were told we were getting concierge accommodations, which silly me, i thought meant nicer than usual. We got to our room. We did have a partial view thanks to the 15th floor, but the room was absolutely claustrophobic. The bathroom literally did not allow more than one person at a time, and the furniture was crowding the room. The refrigerator didn't work. I called and maintenance was a no-show. The bed was much less comfortable than the one at the Marriott Courtyard Long Beach - didn't realize how good we had it.
On the plus side - free work out, which isn't so common these days. Another down side - they charged for internet access. Glad I have my Droid hot spot.
Finally, the breakfast restaurant had one woman on the critical path for the whole place. While empty tables abounded, people were stacked to the entrance waiting on tables. Once we got seated, the buffet food was decent and our server was good.
If you do stay here and want to drop off a rental car first, know that the rental car street is right next to the Marriott. We wished we would have dropped off our rental car and then had the shuttle drop us on the corner (saw someone do that too late) - the parking was expensive and we paid extra for more rental car time than we needed.

title: “Amazingly HORRIBLE”
text:
My husband and I went to San Antonio with a fellow couple for the weekend after Thanksgiving 2006. We had paid for the rooms online and reserved 2 King size rooms. I called that morning before leaving Houston to confirm and was told we had 2 King size rooms on the same floor. When we checking in, we not only did NOT have the 2 King size rooms but they were also on different floors. We had 1 double queen room and 1 King room and the only offer they made to us was to have a roll away bed brought in. (I'm still not sure how this would have remedied ANY part of the situation.) The staff was very rude and acted as if we were inconveniencing them because THEY screwed up our reservation.
When we finally got to our rooms, they smelled stale and I don't think our room had been cleaned. The toilet paper roll was jagged not even torn straight and we had a pile of dirty towels in the corner.
