Our friends' bathroom was wheelchair accesible (so no divder from floor to shower) and the entire room was dripping with water. The remote control didn't work and we never got a new one (after about 5 calls to the front desk). Needless to say we left EARLY the next morning and found a different hotel.
I complained to management and coorporate and the only compensation they were willing to give me was a free night in their hotel. Seriously?! I can't think of 1 reason why I would stay there EVER again.

title: “Great location and value for money”
text:
We are relocating from Sydney Australia with two young children and this hotel has really been great. Its not fancy but it is clean and a great location. Everything is in walking distance that you would need . The Upper West Side is just lovely and very kid friendly.
Will recommend all my friends coming over to NYC to stay here.

title: “Another Wonderful Kimpton Experience”
text:
My wife and I stayed here one night to celebrate her birthday. We've stayed at other Kimpton hotels in SF (Hotel Monaco) and in Seattle (Hotel Vintage Park). The decor is different from the 2 other Kimpton hotels but it works really well.
Pros -
- The decor was very appropriate for the area and wonderfully done.
- Leo the conceirge did a great job with the flower arrangement for the room. He actually did the arrangement himself and the flowers were gorgeous. Leo also made some excellent suggestions with activities and restaurants. A lady was walking by and thanked him for the excellent hair stylist recommendation. Thanks Leo!
- The staff was very friendly and attentive.
- My wife and I are Kimpton In Touch members and they had a bottle of wine and cookies (in the shape of a whale) to celebrate my wife's birthday. Nice touch!
- The room was a decent size and the bed was very comfortable.
- Excellent location near the waterfront. It is within walking distance to North Beach and to Pier 39. It is also next to the cable car stop.
- Last but not least let's not forget the 5pm wine hour.
Cons -
- The view was a wall of windows. Basically I had no view so it wasn't worth opening the windows except to get some sunlight in the room. This was a basic room and a room with a view would have cost another $100.
- As a Kimpton In Touch member you would think I would get the best deal. The best deal that I was offered via the website and through a phone call to the hotel directly was the same as non-members. I then remembered I got an email from Kimpton offering 15% off so by going through the link offered in the email I got a better rate. I shouldn't have to do that.
- Parking is $40 per day ... ouch! 
Overall an excellent experience and you won't be disappointed.

title: “not good, not good at all”
text:
We went there and read their notice about how "everything works" when nothing in our room worked..the toliet didn't even flush! so we told the very unhelpful staff who didn't get anything done till the third time we asked them. By then it was our last night and still had many problems with other broken things in the room. In addition they need to sort out their heating systems..
mwhahaha basically dont go there to save yourself from a bad experience.

title: “Terrible night's sleep”
text: This is a great budget hotel but make sure you don't get stuck in one of the rooms on the four corners of the hotel like we did. The hot water pipe for the whole hotel runs through the room and is right next to the bed. The noise that this makes throughout the night is unbelievable and it is impossible to sleep through it. Opt for a room with a private bathroom and you'll be ok - the hotel is in a great location and the decor and cleanliness is fine - just make sure you're in a room without a hot water pipe if you want to get any sleep!

title: “Renovated entirely - $13 million dollars”
text:
This hotel is beautiful now. The entire thing has been renovated with completely new guest rooms that feature plasma tv's, internet access, a beautiful design, etc.
Customer service was great, so was the food (but it was slightly expensive)

title: “This hotel is fine”
text:
Just completed a long weekend in New York.
After reading the reviews we were a little worried but this hotel seemed to have less poor reviews than others. I'm not sure what people expect for their money but this is a budget hotel.
Requested a quiet room and this is what we got, no problems with traffic noise but no views either, we could also open the windows as it was warm but not hot at night. As we were not in the hotel very long each day we were very satisfied. The room was massive which was a surprise after reading many reviews refering to small rooms.
Decor could do with freshening up but was OK.
Booking in and out was not a problem and any issues were dealt with quickly and positively.
Breakfast at the hotel was fine, I would definitely recommend the pancakes!
Taking the excellent position of the hotel and it's closeness to the subway into account I can easily say we would stop at the Wellington again. It is not top notch but then you are not paying those prices either.

title: “Wonderful experience”
text: Large, clean and spacious. Quiet with a beautiful view of tree tops outside our windows. Staff was very helpful.

title: “Pretty - but had to check out after way less than a day!”
text:
Stayed there in February with my 7 year old after reading the reviews on tripadvisor. While the room was pretty, there was some sort of problem with the vent system and the room smelled like the inside of a fireplace. Switched to another room after a couple of hours and had the same problem. Was offerred to switch to another room in the morning but we switched to the Fairmont where we had no issues.
I do however have to praise the staff at the hotel! My son became sick on the flight to Seattle and had a fever when we checked into the hotel. One of the staff members whose shift was ending was kind enough to go to the drugstore for me to buy a thermometer and gatorade for him. It was really appreciated!

title: “Hotel Penn, OK, but we'll never stay there again”
text: My first trip to NYC was for business, this time it was just for fun. I understand that Hotel Penn is old, but there is no excuse for having burn holes in the bedding of a supposedly non-smoking room. My biggest complaint would have to be the pure volume of people in that hotel, it's huge and cheap so every tour bus stops there. You would think that with 12 elevators, you could get to your room quickly but on average we waited for 3 cars to go by before we could get into one. The location was great, the price was too, but if you don't mind walking a little bit, stay somewhere else. :)

title: “Great stay!”
text: My resent stay at the Palmer House Hotel in Chicago was outstanding! What a great guest service team. The Concierge Tracy and Phillpi went above and beyond to make sure we found the resturants and the shopping we were looking for, Sussan the housekeeping manager fixed our housekeeping problem with a big smile, and Mike the S Guard in the lobby was really friendly and helpful. I'll be back!

title: “Too little for too much money”
text: This hotel is nice don't get me wrong, but no breakfast, no pool, or hot tub, $18 for parking, and a broken elevator. The location is perfect, but even a few more blocks away is no big deal. I've stayed farther away and felt safe, and I don't mind walking or taking the trolley, even at night. So if you have alot af money to waste, stay here, but otherwise, stay farther away and spend your money on bbq and beer instead. Besides who comes to Memphis to hang out in their room anyway?

title: “Worst hotel experience”
text: Perhaps one the worst hotel experiences ever. The front desk clerk was rude and arrogant. When I asked to speak with a manager she stated she was the GM even though her name tag had no title. That was the start. Our room was dirty, the place smelled like stale swamp water. Our toilet didn't work, when I called to complain to the front desk a woman answered, (I assume the same one who checked us in) she hung up on me. One can only hope that in this economy that hotels like this will go out of business. If you stay there expect nothing but bad customer service, shabby, dated and dirty rooms.

title: “Great stay at the Best Western”
text:
I stay at the Best Western In Dallas Tx. On Market Center Blvd.
Quite often. I have found that it is a great place to come to just relax around the pool or in the room. My room is always clean and I injoy staying there. I have recomended the hotel to all my friends.

title: “Grand Hyatt was a Grand Experience”
text: I really wanted to give this hotel an excellent review, however, our original room was small. Especially for two adult females. (The King room had much more room tham we originally did.) With that said, the service was great. The free breakfast was a fabulous addition. And due to hotel construction, we were able to change rooms in the middle of our stay and the 2nd room was perfect. All their double rooms should be that size. If this is your 1st or 2nd time to NYC and you don't want to stay in Times Square, The Grand Hyatt is perfect. Besides Grand Central Station being attached to the Hotel, 5th Ave shopping is only a short walk away.

title: “BoCo auditions”
text: Stayed for an audition at Boston Conservatory. Very close for that purpose. Location was excellent- near BoCo, Berklee and Newbury Street and there is a way to get to the Pru Center through the Sherton directly across the street (thus minimizing our time in the biting cold wind in Feb). Staff was friendly and helpful. Tried to 'beat the system' and not order the pig out al you can eat breakfast, but ended up paying more for my small breakfast all due to the $8 a la catre coffee. Went with the $20 breakfast buffet the next day and just chalked the price up to traveling. We were offered an upgrade at check in and we paid a little bit more for the higher floor, flat screen TV, etc.

title: “Perfect location”
text: In walking distance to The Magnificent Mile and Millenium Park. A good looking neighbourhood. Staff was friendly and the hotel was clean. One day the elevator didn´t work and we had to walk all the way down from the 17th floor... Other than that, I have no complaints...

title: “Comfortable Updated Hotel”
text:
We spent two comfortable nights at this Courtyard during our visit to Austin. The lobby and rooms of the hotel have recently been updated. Everything looked and smelled new and fresh. The lobby is one of the “new-concept” Courtyards with Starbucks products and a Bistro, which we did not use. The lobby is very spacious. The rates were very reasonable, with free parking. 
Convenient location along IH-35. It is an easy and short drive to get downtown and to the University of Texas campus. There is not much in terms or restaurants within walking distance, but several are located within a short driving distance. Our room was on the quiet side of the hotel, away from IH-35. It was clean and very quiet. The bed was comfortable. The staff was friendly and professional. The Wi-Fi worked well in the room. The climate control for the room worked well.

title: “great city base - large rooms”
text: We visited the Crowne Plaza Times Sq in April 2010 and were delighted with the hotel. Our standard room was large with two king sized beds and generous en suite bathroom. Definitely the largest standard room of any hotel in NYC that i've stayed in.The views of the city from the room were great and the furnishings modern and clean. Check in was v straightforward with minimum queuing. The lobby bar was a nice spot for (rather expensive) cocktails. The Gym was very large & well equipped. However, bear in mind that it is a public members-club so is VERY BUSY. I believe there is a swimming pool (v unusual for manhattan hotels). There is a charge for hotel guests to use the facilities. The real selling point of this hotel is its location in the heart of theatreland. It is literally steps from times square itself which is great if you like the hustle and bustle but definitely avoid if you can't stand crowds of tourists.

title: “Pillows....Pillows....Pillows!”
text:
This was not our first stay at the ole Peabody, but I don't previously recall so many pillows. There comes a time in ones life when you can't have too many pillows of all shapes and firmness to ensure a good nights sleep. Each bed in the Peabody has 10! Our Aussie traveling companions were in awe. The only thing comparable that stay was the obligatory duck watching in the lobby. Nothing like that in Australia they told us.
Staff was uniformly friendly and helpful. Drinks from the lobby bar weren't outrageously priced with a pianist on duty during the evening.
Self parking no longer seems to be an option, but the valet was quick and efficient. Entrance to the "front" door...actually the back door....for vehicle drop off may be found on the west side of the hotel. Got it? Good luck.
One dining note: The short walk out of the Peabody's real front door on Union St. and down the alley to the Rendevouz is still fun, but the ribs weren't. Mine were almost cold and not that tasty. Maybe the Rendevouz is slipping....or maybe they were having a bad night.

title: “Don't have a pleasant memory, want stay there again”
text:
The hotel is located in the Fisherman's Wharf so in the heart of the one of the main tourist attraction in SF.
Disadvantages: the neighborhood is way too crowded especially on weekends.
Parking outside of the hotel for the ones traveling by car is really expensive. Moreover, like what happened to us, the staff working at the reception doesn’t give you the alternative parking option. Thus you end up paying $39/night for a regular size car. don’t’ want people to go through what I went through: spending first 2 hours at the hotel room searching a cheaper parking on the Internet, and walking around the neighborhood the find a more reasonable parking option. So here’s the tip: you can park your car in nearby Anchorage Square Parking Lot and get a special overnight parking rate when you give the name of your hotel, but you have to do that before you get into the parking lot.
Even though your hotel rate includes free wireless in the room, once you want to get connected to the Internet, the hotel asks you to register your personal email address to Kimpton Hotels’ website. Once you call the front desk confirm whether this is the only option to get wireless in your room, they insist that you are obligated your to register your email to the website (and receive junk mail from a company that you have no interest in hearing from) to be able benefit from a service that they call “free”.
In addition, after I returned back home I realized that I left something in the room and emailed to hotel and never got a response back.
In summary, me and my family don't have a pleasant memory of this hotel, will not stay there again.

title: “Okay. Nice Hotel, small bathrooms, EXPENSIVE parking”
text:
The hotel looks very nice. Very spacious and modern decor in the lobby area. Upon check-in, there seemed to be a shortage of rooms, so we had to wait awhile -- but not too long.
The hotel parking is sooooo expensive! Make sure you budget that in before you book. It was $57.00 per night. When you have kids and luggage, you really don't want to walk the block or so from the cheaper parking building down the way for $32.00 per day.
We were two adults and two children. With this, keep in mind that the beds are double beds and not queens. They were a little cramped for all of us. The bathroom area is way, way too small. You literally have to squeeze into the toilet/shower area before you can close the door. And, if you have the bathtub towel on the floor -- forget it. You have to move it out of the way first.
The location is good, but I do think I would try another hotel first. Like I said, the price was extreme, rooms small, parking price insane.

title: “Rooms nice, valet and elevators not so much”
text: Got this hotel through Hotwire for a great deal. Suites were wonderful. Only drawbacks are the long waits for the elevators. We waited over 45 minutes for our car one time. Little hard to be patient waiting that long with a three year old that just wants to go to the zoo.

title: “Presidential suite upgrade”
text: I stayed at the OMNI about 3 weeks ago ( april) for 2 nights. My bf booked the room and I arrived later than him. My first impression was that the room was quite small. The bathroom was also very small, with hardly any counter for ladies makeup, and to be able to shower you climb into the bathtub. But we were late to dinner and did not deal with it , but on the way back we ran into the manager at the front desk and decided to ask for a bigger room with a big tub/ separate shower etc. He said only the presidential suite was available which normally runs for $ 1200 or 1500 I don't remember ( tried to look on their website now but its not listed) ANYWAYS, he upgraded us for $300 extra per night ( we were paying $250 already for the regular suite ) so it came out to 550/per night. He escorted us back to our old room, waited outside and took us personally to the suite. I jokingly said " I hope this deal comes with a bottle of champagne" .... well 10 min after we switched rooms .... knock knock on the door, and a champagne bottle and 2 glasses arrived at our door. That was so thoughtful and we had a lovely evening taking a bath in the huge jacuzzi sipping champagne and talking. The suite has a small kitchenette, a large living/dining area, the big tub, separate large shower, 2 TV's, one in the bedroom one in the living area. Overall I would not pay this much every time but it was a nice experience. The decor is very traditional. Staff is helpful, busboy is attentive.

title: “Very comfortable and pleasant stay at the Ritz”
text:
I booked my 4-night stay at the Ritz for a conference so the rate was reasonable. The hotel lobby was elegant and my room was very nicely appointed, with a generous supply of L'Occitane products, complimentary bottled water, double sinks in the large bathroom, plenty of towels and a robe/slippers. The staff was exceptional; knowledgeable, helpful, efficient and courteous; I could not have asked for more! The location was excellent right on Michigan Avenue. I could see Navy Pier from my room. The John Hancock building was across the street, Navy Pier was a 10 minute walk and the Lincoln Park zoo was a 20 minute walk. 
The room was clean, relatively quiet and very comfortable. There was a small firehouse and a large hospital nearby and I could hear occasional sirens, but definitely not constant so the disturbance was minor. The restaurant food was very good and the staff remembered me although the prices were high. Complimentary wired internet is available in the rooms but I was able to get wireless access in my room and in the lobby. 
The lobby and restaurant are on the 12th floor which is rather unique. Take the ground floor elevator to 12, then get off, go around the corner to the elevators that take you to the rooms. This seemed odd at first, but wouldn't be a deterrent for me. I would stay here again without hesitation. Beneath the hotel is a multi-floor mall which I loved.
 All in all, this was a very problem-free, enjoyable stay and I loved my first visit to Chicago!

title: “It's not often i'd go back to the same hotel but...”
text:
Christmas in New York! This place is spot on. Had a first bad night with a leak in the ceiling drip drip drip dripping all night. Was offered an upgrade but declined as it was right next to the elevator and would have been noisy. Moved rooms next day and problem sorted.
Didn't expect free breakfast so was pleased with it ( its only fruit and croissants/pastries/toast and cereal) but hey, it's free. Gets a little busy too.
Hotel is fairly small but lovely and clean. Staff are the greatest asset. Not got a bad word to say about them. Almost didn't stay here as the room photos look a little "frumpy" and we love contemporary. We chose it purely on the trip advisor results and were not disappointed. This was our 3rd trip to New York at Xmas and probably our last as we've kind of worn it out. If we were coming back we'd go back to the Pearl. Location is spot on - just off Times Square. 
Warning - get in quick as at some point due to the great reviews this place gets the prices will surely go up. 
Tip, go in the grill next door ( EE Grill) Food is gorgeous if not a little limited on the choice side - make sure you don't get seated near the washing up area - its noisy and on the second visit that's where we ended up. We moved! 
Found the bed rather small and unfortunately pretty soft and due to the mattress protector uncomfortably hot. The manager said this was the first time anyone had mentioned it and she'd actually tested out several protectors to make sure they didn't rustle through the night. I actually believe her, because we didn't think it could be a mattress protector causing our discomfort and only realised on the last night when we peeled back the bedding.
All in all, spot on location, staff who were an absolute credit ( Ali, thanks for your help ), lovely oasis in the city that seriously never sleeps. Enjoy!!

title: “perfect location”
text: I stayed Dakota for 5 days with four of my buddies and had an amazing time. We had no problems with bed bugs, but yes the elevator is def. fun sometimes. Suprita at the front desk was very helpful with bars n clubs within the walking distance and she's cute ;)

title: “Christmas at the Ballantyne Hotel”
text: This is one of the very few times that I was not in my home for Christmas. My husband and I went to Charlotte to spend Christmas with our son and his family. The Hotel was beautifully decorated and everyone was so friendly. We hope to visit the Ballantyne Hotel again soon.

title: “Historic, cool hotel, not generic”
text: I loved this hotel even though my husband had his reservations about it at first. He did NOT want a room with a community bath (which are cheaper) so I booked a suite for a little over $100. It was quite large, 2 rooms, brand new sofa, furniture, minimalist decor, little kitchen, TV, clawfoot bathtub, comfortable double bed, and freshly painted. We had a great time walking around the Marketplace and surrounding area. The desk clerk was very helpful, telling us where to park (across the street $15) showing us how to catch the free bus to ChinaTown and how to get back. We even went to hear live music next door at the Moore Theater! If you want a place with character, and not a generic chain hotel, this is the place! Do be aware that there is a significant amount of homeless people, panhandlers and dope dealers, but I find this element in most major cities in the U.S.

title: “Good hotel for a business stay”
text:
I stayed here for a long weekend for a business conference. It's a good hotel, overall. The staff was very helpful and always super polite. The beds were comfortable and the rooms were spacious enough. I had a small electricity problem upon checking in, and they were attentive in fixing it promptly. The conference room was nice and seemed to meet everyone's needs. 
I chose not to rent a car so I pretty much had to stay in the hotel the whole time and eat their food, which got a little old by the end. It's your basic hotel food. Not terrible, but not too high quality either. My one real complaint is that they don't provide a continental breakfast, you have to pay for it, even just a cup of coffee. 
This was in a good location for a business event because they are fairly close to the large international airport. I mean, Houston is really, really big, and the airport is way on the north side, away from downtown. This hotel was close by, which was very convenient. This might not be a good place to stay for tourists hoping to take in the downtown area. Also, they have an airport shuttle, which is very nice, and it is complimentary! So call ahead, and don't take a cab from the airport.
All in all, a pleasant stay for its purposes.

title: “Good value hotel near Times Square”
text: We traveled in mid-December on a weekend. I had booked this hotel before it even opened, so got a fantastic rate. I think that if you can get a room for around $175 or so, you should consider this hotel since it is brand new and about a 5 min walk to Times Square. It's on the west side, near many of the theatres. We traveled with friends and they said their room was very noisy at night - we were on opposite sides of the hotel and seem to have been a litle more buffered. The rooms are clean, nicely decorated, but small (as to be expected in NYC). The complimentary breakfast is ok - great if you have a family and don't want to go out and pay at least $20 for breakfast.

title: “Nice in every way...”
text: great location in the financial district, a 12 minute walk to Wall Street -- sleek, modern design -- rooftop bar is a nice respite when the weather is good -- excellent restaurant, every meal was quite good -- the room was well appointed and comfortable -- front desk and restaurant personnel were very friendly and well trained. All in all, a very fine experience.

title: “Nice hotel, staff went above and beyond!”
text: The hotel itself and rooms are very nice and what you would expect for an upscale hotel in NYC. The room and bathroom were very clean, no complaints. What really made our visit was the staff though. I was visiting overnight with my sister to go shopping for my wedding dress. We checked in early, and they said we could have the regular room we booked right then or they would hold our bags for us and upgrade us to a suite around the normal check in time. Not only did they upgrade us to a beautiful suite with a fantasic view, but upon returning from dinner and a show that night after dress shopping, waiting for us in the room was a platter of chocolate strawberries, mineral waters, and champagne compliments of the hotel with a personalized note from the manager saying how he hoped I had a great time dress shopping. Now, my dad has stayed here before many times on business, but this reservation was booked under my sister's name, just a regular person. I understand that staff are paid to keep guests happy, but the room upgrade and food/drinks/note really just went above and beyond! We will definitely be staying here again next time we find ourselves in NYC.

title: “I wanted to like it but..”
text:
I choose this hotel because the location is great, near Fillmore and not too far from Haight. I know it would be noisy but I am used to that so it didn't bother me. I was given a big king room which was very comfortable but my first two nights were ruined by the horrifically inconsiderate couple who screamed and swore at each other whilst their little kids cried. I managed to at least be given a new room to sleep in and thankfully the couple left to whatever horrible life they had created for themselves eleswhere. It would have been nice if the hotel had cleaned the dirty diapers that they left outside their room for the time they spent there. The rest of the stay was ok except the TV reception stopped working and I was given a half hearted "nothing we can do sir it's the win' response. I gave up trying to get it fixed. The internet service was really patchy perhaps because the band width is not enough for all the people staying in the hotel. Frustrating when you are trying to use it for business. One day it stopped working altogether
 The restaurant is now closed Monday and Tuesday which is a pain but there are plenty of restaurants in the area. It is also not open for lunch. However when I ate there I thought the food was very good and the staff were very pleasant. The other staff at the hotel were a mixed bag of very helpful and surly and useless. I think they need to work on this very quickly. All in all an average hotel which was needs to sharpen up it's service. I am not sure I would stay there again as I was frustrated by the TV and internet which mayt be very petty but staying at a place for two weeks on business it is good to be able to relax in your room and just watch some TV some nights.

title: “very comfortable stay..”
text: I stayed one night at the Mayflower as I took my husband to D.C from Va. for his birthday. I stayed in a suite on the 5th floor. They did say they have been going through some renovations but I couldn't tell. The lobby was magnificent! lovely chandeliers line up from the lobby all the way to the back entrance. The front desk staff was very helpful and attending staff pleasant. We did get a complimentary bottle of red along with some chocolate covered strawberries for his birthday-which I thought was a nice touch. The bed was absolutely divine and I sank into the pillows. Everything you can expect from a luxury hotel. My husband loved it. I would stay there again in the event I want to splurge in D.C!

title: “Great place to have an event or just rest.”
text: If you are planning a wedding, a reception, a birthday party, or any other function, you should check out thier facilities. They also do conferences. And the breakfast there are exceptional. Plus, if you are lucky enough to have the buffet, usually at Easter and Mother's Day. the food is abundant and very tasty. Prices for the buffet are somewhat less than the other places. Oh, this hotel is also very close the the Casino and the Mall. About 15 minutes from downtown and about 20 from the International Bridges.

title: “Modern hotel with exceptional service”
text:
Stayed here for a Business trip and it is hard to find anything negative to say. Staff is super friendly --people actually smile at you when you walk in the door here. My room was a decent size, and decorated in what I would call modern elegance. Location is in the heart of Boston, a stone's throw away from the Boston Common and the red and green T (local train) lines. 
Their restaurant, KO Prime, was top notch as well. Great vibe when I was there --and really tasty food. It also works well for business travelers who want a solo dinner at the bar. 
Definitely a recommend if you are coming to boston and like the experience of a good boutique hotel.

title: “Great Stay”
text: This was our second time staying at Park Central and we chose it, due to the great localization close to Central Park, Times Square and the Broadway shows. All staff were very attentive and friendly, specially Elizabeth. We will return definitely.

title: “Fire”
text:
We got a great deal for the grand opening of this hotel. It was very clean and modern with a Japanese flare. The rooftop bar and restaurant were great along with coffee and muffins in the morning.
Cons of this place are simple. Work out the bugs before opening doors to the public.
Upon returning to the hotel at 1 am on Friday night the elevators were out. My wife and I were staying on the 20th floor. Not a fun walk! Then after falling asleep we had a fire alarm for roughly 30 min @3:30am.

title: “It was OK; Great location”
text: Walking distance to Central Park and the theatre district. This hotel is very old, and the walls are thin. The people staying next to us partied in their room, and security never bothered to do anything about it. Location is great, and the room is comfortable. Water pressure in the shower is great. So, if you're the type who doesn't care much about the hotel room and just wants a great location, this is the hotel for you. The price is right for what you get.

title: “Clean, Comfortable, Great Staff, Great Location.”
text:
Just got back from a 4 night stay. Excellent Staff, excellent location. Small rooms and a bit of trouble with the plumbing, but no big deal. Much better than the rooms we had in Venice and Rome. Would definitely stay here again! Very good continental breakfast, comfortable beds, location can't be beat, affordable, clean, GREAT value.
Attitude is everything. If you are looking for master bedroom sized rooms, the Marriott Marquis is just 5 minutes away, but will cost you a bunch more.
What makes this hotel special is the Staff. They will take care of you. We found the rooms comfortable, the a/c worked great. I'm recommending this property to everyone I know who is going to NY on vacation.

title: “A Grand Hotel”
text: I just returned from this grand hotel. The service was excellent. We had an executive level floor. I was a bit disappointed in the executive lounge. There wasn't enough help to keep the tables clean. I would've bused my own but, there was no where to place the dirty dishes. The refrigerators didn't seem to work well. The soda and water was always cool at best. The rooms are large but, need updating. The hotel is supposed to be going through a renovation. The decor in my room was definitely 1980. But, it was spotless. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was huge. A must see is the ballroom. I hope when the renovations are complete they do not destroy the magnificent walls and ceiling paintings. They are a definite indicator of the years gone by and why the hotel is the flagship for the Hilton brand. Cabs are readily available at the main enterance 24/7. The Chicago Trolley Tour has a stop just outside. The food choices were limited in the restaurants and snack shop. But, with all the great eateries in Chicago, you will not go hungery. I recommend Ditka's. There was an excellent local diner, the Eleven Street City Diner, just 3 blocks away that has a great breakfast menu 24/7. One word of caution about Chicago and not the hotel--Chicago currently has a gang related crime problem. The police are making their presence known but, be careful going out after dark. We didn't experience any problems but it was all over the news.

title: “We love this hotel.”
text: Great location and we love the pool. The pool is a great place and you can sit outside on the deck. The rooms are great with lots of pillows. We wanted two beds and they kept saying that was sold out so I called the hotel the day before and the desk clerk said she would work on it and she did. We got what we asked for.

title: “Our favorite little hotel in NYC”
text:
We have stayed in many places in the city, always following at least good hotels when they had sales for their rooms. Once we happened to stay at this hotel and it really fits our style. The rooms are typical of NYC but they are not closets with furniture. They are decorated in warm colors with an Italian feel, have cozy lighting, and lots of sunlight. The location is great because it is close to different subways, close to Battery Park and the lovely river-side promenade, close to the East River Ferry terminal that gets you to Brooklyn and Williamsburg (30 minute trip to the Brooklyn flea on the weekends - plan ahead for departure times though). 
We have learned to bring our own bread and peanut butter just because we like those a lot but they have basic foods plus hard-boiled eggs, coffee, tea, and so on. We often prepare a few things downstairs or get some bagels from a place close by and eat in our cozy room. The people at the reservation are not overtly friendly in the American way but have always been very nice to us and have accommodated our requests. The rates at this hotel are really competitive often on the weekends, because Wall Street is quieter. I have tried to stay here during the week but that is harder to afford. Nevertheless, we end up here rather frequently and could not be happier everytime we go!

title: “Will stay nowhere else in NYC!”
text:
Would like to give a shout out of thanks to Trevon who works the PM shift at the front desk. He helped us pull off a surprise for our daughter's engagement this past weekend where he showed such class, professionalism, compassion, human kindness, quick thinking skills & great customer service! We are now officially hooked on this hotel & will stay nowhere else in our travels to NYC! Trevon, you are a rare breed in the service industry today--a cut above the rest! Thanks again for making our weekend so special! 
Also, the hotel has been updated with new decor and the rooms are so beautiful, classy and fresh/clean! We have tried a myriad of NYC hotels but still like this the best for the price. Really nice rooms, good prices compared to other comparable hotels, great service, excellent location...what more do you want from a NYC hotel? Book a room here with assurance. You won't be sorry you did!

title: “Not as great as before”
text: Fully booked and unable to cope. Ran out of breakfast food, valet couldn't cope. Poor check -in. Family weekend, but too many issues to return next time

title: “Beautiful Hotel plus Great Location.”
text: Great experience. Walking distance to many attractions and train. Very good breakfast at the Bistro. Beautifully decorated throughout. Parking the only negative.

title: “Leslie Casey is Awesome!”
text:
Leslie Casey was so nice and professional. She was full of knowledge in regards to the many products available. We wanted a room with an air filter (I have allergies) and we also wanted our room away from elevators and the swimming pool. She answered all of our questions, was flexible with check out, due to my fiance's military schedule and she was so attentive. She listened to our needs and gave us EXACTLY what we asked for along with super service! 
The hotel was reasonably priced. Their Sunday brunch is amazing as well as their location. It was steps away from the mall, the Alamo, and the actual hotel had an elevator that went directly downstairs to the River Walk! 
The allergy filter in the room was a dream. I didn't suffer from allergies the whole time while in the room. The room was also clean, several outlets available, nice flat screen tv, nice view. It was such a great experience!

title: “W STANDS FOR WOW”
text: The moment i step foot in it's unassuming lobby, I knew I will like it. The smell of elevator was like fresh linens. The lobby was uber chic and cool. The views were magnificent. The best part about it -- It's not too crowded like the other hotels in city. The staff were friendly and warm. My room was on the 22nd floor facing the 9/11 Memorial which was very melancholic yet empowering. I love my room. It was modern and sophisticated. The noise from the construction site didn't really affected my sleep so it wasn't really a big deal. The subway stations were less than 3 blocks away which was perfect and easy to navigate. I'm definitely recommending this hotel to all my friends and family.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Staff, MINOR complaints.”
text:
My girlfriend and had a weekend break in Baltimore, and picked this hotel based on pics of the rooms. We were not disapointed! The hotel is beautiful! It is located on most, but not all, of the floors of the old B&O Railroad building. The first impression came from the friendly doorman, and the stunning lobby. We took the elevator instead of the beautiful staircase to checkin, and we soon in our room. When I booked the room I booked a King Spa Room, but at checkin we were given a Mediterranean Suite. The room was gorgeous, with a nice living room with big LG tv, couch, chair, and closet with a safe. The hotel offers 'companion goldfish' but ours was dead (we named him Bob). We called down and another (Al) was up within minutes. The king bed was very comfortable, but the highlight of the suite was the bathroom. It was in the corner of the building, and had and angled wall for some architectural interest, and an incredible, deep spa tub. Overall the room was incredible, with only two small complaints, both identical to the next review on the list...our iron leaked water and the AC struggles to keep the room cool. To sleep comfortably we had to turn the thermostat down to 65. I was till warm, but my girlfriend was comfortable, and she likes being warm, normally keeping her thermostat at about 72. 
As far as the rest of the hotel, every single staff member we encountered was warm and friendly, everyone at checkin, the bartender Eric, the guy bringing a new goldfish, the girl bringing breakfast, the housekeeper, the door staff, the concierge, even random employees in the elevator were all very friendly, and even funny. Great as the room was, the staff were even better. We enjoyed a few glasses of wine at the evening wine reception, and noticed that when a couple showed up for the reception with a kid around 10-12 years old a staff member quickly brought out controllers and games for the Wii in the reception lounge. 
We ate in the restaurant one night, and it was good...not superb, but we only had a burger and fish and chips. It wasn't cheap, but not outrageous either. Over two nights we had two great bottles of wine, both based on the recommendations of Eric at the bar. Nice guy, and a great bartender! We had room service breakfast both days, the first morning we had the B&O Breakfast, which was eggs, bacon/sausage/ham and potatoes with toast and coffee...we both thought there was something odd about the eggs...both taste and texture just werent right...but the rest was good...but it wasnt cheap. The next day we got two continental breakfasts-danish, croissant, and muffin along with some great fruit, a huge glass of fresh juice and coffee. It was good, and really a much better value. 
Several other reviews mention location as a downside of this hotel, and if you are looking for a harbor view it's not for you. I also wouldnt venture too far on foot at night, but the same can be said for a lot of downtown areas. However, in daylight the walk to the harbor is not far, and feels perfectly safe. At night, I'd say take a cab. We ate dinner at a great local seafood place on the water, The Rusty Scupper, and they offer a free shuttle that picks up at the hotel. Guest services were happy to make reservations and arrange the shuttle for us. 
If all you want in Baltimore is a harbor view move on from the Hotel Monaco, but if you dont mind a short walk or cab ride and want a gorgeous hotel with character and an incredible staff, try this one instead. It's worth it, just don't expect ice cold AC and a good iron. But do get the fish. It's kinda cool.

title: “Unfortunately this hotel has gone downhill”
text: Having stayed at Raffaello a number of times, I have considered it one of the top two boutique hotels in Chicago. The location cannot be beat, and our room lovely and spacious. However everything else was very uneven. My daughter and I checked into the room mid-afternoon, left shortly afterward, and returned at 11:00 pm. Then we discovered the sink drain was down and would not disengage no matter how we tried to pry it open. Thus we were without a sink for our stay. My daughter turned the air conditioner on high, as the room was stifling when we returned. The fan was the loudest I have ever experienced in a hotel, and sounded as if it was going to explode. This made for a basically sleepless night. The restaurant does not serve breakfast; one must order from room service or go elsewhere. I never received a receipt for my stay. Checking out, I asked for the manager's business card and emailed her. I was hoping she would say my experience was an anomaly, and that is not what they are about at Raffaello. However, she chose not to respond. Sadly, this is my last stay at Raffaello, and now I am wondering how it remains a four star hotel.

title: “Have Stayed Here Probably 10 Times”
text:
Stayed here in 1998 when it was a Wyndham Garden Inn, then in 2005 when it was a full service Wyndham, did not stay here when it was a Radisson, but have stayed here twice as a Four Points hotel. The best has been full service Wyndham and now. 
The staff is courteous. Our rate is ungodly good. The beds are comfortable. The place serves food. It's within walking distance to our office. How much better can it get?
Once they had a problem with hot water. They reached out to us to offer us some goodies/incentives to give them another shot. Class act. We did give them another shot and they succeeded.

title: “Perfect for us”
text:
My boyfriend and i wanted to get away for a few days so to Chicago we went. We were excited for the Taste of Chi so this was the PERFECT room/location for that. We walked or use the comp shuttle for wherever we went. Easy walk to Grant park, Navy Pier, fast food and fine dining, all museums and we even walked down town to the stock exchange etc. 
The Room was clean. Yes the sink was small....... but so what..... we didnt want to bathe in it. The air conditioner worked. NO complaints. 
Yes the room was a bit small compared to a non-downtown room. We were surprised it would cost 37 per night to park. But thats okay too. We got our room on Priceline for $90 per night!!
We just had a nice time and enjoyed our stay.

title: “Price didn't match the room”
text:
I booked this hotel out of desperation. The rate was $280 for just one night. I waited in line to check in for about 20 minutes, while I waited I visited the restrooms in the lower lobby of the hotel. This was the first sign of a really old, poorly maintained hotel. The hotel has the common Art Deco-ish Manhattan design. When I got to the room I realized that this hotel must have been renovated many, many decades ago. The bathroom tile was covered in mold, the bathtub didn't drain. The carpet was filthy. Even the toilet paper was cheap, come on, it's toilet paper. Beds were OK. Don't expect a courteous staff, I've received better hospitality at a Travelodge next to I-75 in Lake City, Florida at 3am. Although, the people at the luggage storage room ($4 per bag) were somewhat courteous.
If the owner's of this hotel were willing to spend a few dollars, renovating this hotel, it has the potential to become a hotel destination in Manhattan. It has a great location: across the street from Madison Square Garden, around the corner from Macy's, blocks away from the Empire State Building and Fifth Avenue.

title: “Great Service”
text:
I'm from the Houston area and I stayed here one night because the A/C in my apartment was broken. I booked the hotel room about 30 minutes before I checked in.
Upon arrival, I was greeted nicely and offered something to drink. I was also offered a wakeup call for the next morning. I was given a free upgrade into a suite. The room was very nice and clean. The hotel was very quiet and I got a very good night's sleep.
The price was very reasonable, compared to other hotels of equal quality in the Houston area.
I have no complaints about this hotel, but I am from the Houston area, so I have different expectations from my hotel stay here. For travelers, the drawback of this hotel would be it is not that close to anything else. It is Houston, so you would have to drive anywhere you would want to go anyway, but as a frequent leisure traveler, I personally would prefer to have at least one attraction within a couple of miles. I would recommend it for Business travelers, as there are lots of restaurants within a couple of miles (Chinatown, Westchase).

title: “Good Property - watch the extras”
text: The property and staff are very nice at the Hilton Palacio del Rio. Rooms are good, very clean and adequately furnished. If you are a Hilton Honors member you get a lot of discounts...free internet, discounted valet parking, free breakfast, a discount on drinks but if you are not...Internet is $9.95 per day, Valet is $27.00 a day, you get the idea. Location can't be beat, right on the riverwalk and right across the street from the convention center. If you can afford it this is a good choice.

title: “Has left a bad taste in our mouths”
text: My husband and I have stayed at Legacy Golf Resort over a half dozen times -- obviously we have had good experiences in the past. We've had a growing disatisfaction with them the last few times -- keep saying we'll find another place to stay for our Phoenix trips, but have kept going back. I think our trip last week was our last visit there. Nothing major wrong, just have had it with the additional charges they have tacked on over the year -- we've stayed in a room overlooking the golf course every trip, yet this year it was a $10 per day upcharge (this was announced at the desk, not when we booked); and a $10 per hour fee for late checkout, when we've asked for and received late check out for no additional charge every other visit. Additionally, it is disappointing to us that there has never been any acknowledgement of our repeat business -- not even a "welcome back." In a day and age when loyalty is rewarded and respected at the grocery store, the gas station, at restaurants and even the dry cleaner, you would think a vacation resort would would at least acknowledge a return customer. I travel on business and consistently get "welcome back" comments when I check into a hotel for a return visit -- also get emails and mailings with offerings to entice me back. So, we will look around and find another location in the Phoenix area that DOES want and respect our repeat business, rather than nickeling and diming us to death. Bummer, because it is a rather nice place to stay, but they're lack of customer service and awareness has just left a really bad taste in our mouths.

title: “Hotel91 in Chinatown -- good value -- fun location”
text: We had to leave the place we were in last minute so got onto Cheaphotels.com to book quickly. The price was great but we were a little worried about the location, because Chinatown can have rough areas. It was great -- really fun street like old Shanghai! The room was adequate - not fancy, but clean and I felt save and secure. The receptionists in the lobby were kind and professional. I will stay there again.

title: “You SHOULD choose this hotel!”
text: From the door service man to the front desk personnel to the maid service, ALL is excellent customer service at this Hotel Abri in San Francisco. All the employees are very kind and friendly, and are willing to do everything to make you happy. I spoke with the manager as well, and he was very kind and willing to talk to us to make sure we had an excellent stay. If I ever get back to San Francisco, I will stay at the Hotel Abri again. It's in a great location; 1 block from Union Square.

title: “Better than most”
text: We stayed in this hotel after being dissapointed with other hotels in the Los Angeles area. It was reasonable and pretty clean considering the price. The area was not the best, however the people did not bother you and we were able to find parking spaces...barely. The breakfast was nice and room service provided enough towels for all of us. If your looking for luxury, this is not the place to stay, if your looking for a place to lay your head. Comfort Inn is it.

title: “Lots of pros but more cons”
text:
We stayed at The Belvedere during April 2011. There are pros, but more cons.
The pros: Location, fridge, great bed. For location you can’t beat it. West 48 Street is a quiet street nestled between the craziness of Times Square and the restaurants of Hell’s Kitchen. Everything is close. The bed was very comfortable and there was lots of hot water. There’s a fridge and microwave so you can stock a few supplies in the room.
Cons: Concierge, Front Door Staff, Air Conditioning, Elevators, room (general).
First, the concierge. We made the made the mistake of having them get show tickets to a show we weren’t sure we could get ourselves. They tacked a $60 service charge onto a $95 ticket. I’ll be complaining to both the management and the NYC Tourist Associations about this one. We also discussed having them book the airport shuttle for us, and they were ready to charge a $4 premium on a $20 ticket. When I questioned it on them they said it was it included a tip and all tolls. First, every multi-ride airport shuttle includes toll road charges, and second vouchers almost never include tip. Stay far, far away from these people.
The front door staff is completely useless. Most of the time when we came through the doors, they were so busy nattering away in Spanish that they completely ignored us or missed us. In some cases they’d even step out of the way to let us open our own door. The only time they appeared useful was when we arrived and they were quick to get our luggage out of the cab and onto their trolley while we were trying to pay the driver so we were more or less forced to allow them to take it to our room for a tip. I’d stay away from these folks to.
The in-window air conditioning units in the rooms remind me of Motel 6 in the 70’s. They have two speeds – Off and Cyclone. The main building itself doesn’t appear to be air conditioned, and the hallways are incredibly hot. This heat seeps into the rooms meaning that even on cool nights the air conditioning in your room runs almost constantly. If you’re sensitive to that, sleep will be an issue. 
The elevators are not good. They are very small, and very slow. I knew we had real issues one night during the theater rush when we called an elevator on from our top floor room and it arrived with people in it (who had rode up to the top and were going back down, likely because every elevator that had passed them on a lower floor was full).
The room in general had lots of little issues. Windows that were so thin they were almost non-existent so all street noise came straight in, even on the top floor. There are thick marble thresholds at the bathroom door and between the main hall (marble) and bed area (carpet). These are a hazard – very easy to trip over.
Would I stay here again? Maybe. The price was good and the location was great. The bed was great and fridge and microwave a nice touch. If the budget will allow it I’ll likely try other properties that have bigger rooms and more amenities.

title: “The Sugar Creek Rodeway is a Great Value”
text: I am a female who frequently travels alone on business. I feel safe at this hotel due to the alert staff who are customer oriented but not intrusive. It is a great value for the money. You get Bed, Bath, and Beyond in the form of coffee, fluffy towels, micro wave, refrigerator, free internet, CNBC plus many more channels. They always have a complimentary USA Today. The paper is not delivered to your door but you have to walk to the lobby. Work, Work, Work . I hope it stays this way. If it becomes too popular they will have to raise the price. I know I am foolish to write this because it is a diamond in the rough.

title: “very dissapointed”
text: Just got done staying here for one night, not a good experience. 3 main complaints, We had 1 coffee pack in our room, only 2 towels and the thermostat would not let us turn the air on as it said it was winter time and if we had to have cool air open the window. I swear our room was 78 degrees when we got there and I tried the window open but the sounds of the city would have kept you from sleeping at all. My wife and I didn't get more than 2 hours sleep all night it was so warm. The outside temp. was probably about 40. We travel a lot probably staying in hotels 60 to 70 times a year and stay in every 3 and 4 star hotel you can think of and this the first time we could not turn the thermostat down to 69 or 70 for sleeping, a very miserable night!! This is the second week in a row at a marriott and strangely we never got coffee or towels the week before either but we could set the thermostat where we were comfortable. Maybe its a corporate decision to cut back on coffee and towels but never run into this problem at other hotels. We are avoiding marriott's from now on and we have to travel back to Detroit in a few weeks and will no way spend another long hot night like we just had. If you don't like hot rooms avoid!!

title: “A Class Act”
text: This was one of the best city experience I have had at a hotel. I was lost twice and they talked me back, stayed on until I reached the door. The rooms were quiet and very clean. I had to leave for the airport and there was a road race happening. Security gave me perfect directions around the race and I made it to my flight on time. The housekeeper took me to the ice machine, didn't show me, took me. Professional, friendly and clean. Great breakfast. Better than the Ritz Carlton down the street!

title: “do not trust them with your visa card! !”
text: Went to NY as part of a choir to join in the 9/11 commemoration and stayed on in this wonderfully located hotel. Our room was pre-paid by my daughter. They took my visa details and when we left presented me with a payment receipt for some food we had had. Unbeknown to me and unreceipted they had also removed more than £1100 from my account which I did not discover until I returned to the UK and checked my bank statement. Since then I have been trying in vain to get my money back. A member of the Accounts Department acknowledged the double charging and said he would remedy it, but didn't. I was then given an e-mail address for Starwood Hotels and sent a lengthy e-mail setting out the situation. This was not acknowledged. Today I have phoned the MTS and was told that they would get back to me in 10-15 minutes...you can guess the rest. When I eventually phoned back there was an answerphone. This affair has been very expensive in terms of time and money and most disillusioning. I strongly advise anyone staying in this hotel who has given credit/debit card details to keep a close check on their bank statements if at all possible.

title: “Average quality, minimal customer service, starting to show signs of wear and tear”
text: Since this was my first stay in downtown Denver, I can't speak to the quality of other hotels in the area. This hotel is five years old and our room was starting to show signs of wear and tear. Do not stay here if you want any kind of view of the Rockies. The building is surrounded by taller buildings. The breakfast was as expected in terms of foods offered although too many of the sauces, salsa, waffle batter, yogurts, etc. were uncovered and not chilled appropriately. Service at breakfast was great and the breakfast area was spacious despite the large crowd. The desk staff were not helpful even though we requested a high floor room in our initial reservation and had our reservations for nine months prior to our stay. I suspect our rate was low compared to their latest rate posting on the website and this is why the man at the front desk was less than concerned with our only room request. Only one of three elevators was working for part of our stay. For anyone attending a meeting at the Colorado Convention Center and staying alone, I would recommend another closer hotel. The four blocks on the website is more like six and the walk is not one I would take alone at night. At all hours of the day there are homeless people on the street and I was followed at one point during a walk to the Convention Center. The hotel is not as good as other Residence Inns I have stayed in and the lower rate was not worth it.

title: “This hotel is like living at home”
text: I have stayed at many hotels around the world ( including 5 star ) but I rate the Hampton Inn hotel amongst the best . During our 6 day stay we found the staff were caring and helpful . Breakfast time is very hectic but it was clever of the hotel to put up a sign alerting guests to be early as peak hour was usually between 8 - 9 am. There was an excellent selection at the free breakfast and I was very impressed with the kitchen staff who under extreme pressure always had a smile and friendly greeting.The 24 hour coffee /tea facility in the foyer was great and we used it often. So nice to have a hotel provide free internet albeit there was always a queue wanting to use it. The rooms are very large and comfortable as are the beds. We found New Yorkers friendly and helpful.The hotel is a short 10 minute walk to Times square and 2 blocks from in seperate directions to the subway system which we used extensively without any problems .The hop on hop off bus service is a must and a cheap way to see most of New York. A sale day at Macey's is something everyone should experience. A horse and buggy ride around Central Park is a nice way to finish off a day.If you go to Yankee Stadium don't forget to take ID as you won't be served alcohol without it ( no matter your age ) .Can't wait to go back to New York which is truly one of the iconic cities of the world.

title: “Great Hotel Next to Everthing”
text:
Stayed here for a week while attending a conference. The convention center is a 5 minute walk (at most) on the street or a little bit longer using the attached sky-walks. Typical Embassy Suites setup with all rooms facing the inside foyer. Breakfast and evening reception were great, as always with Embassy Suites. I had a standard suite room was was the typical room for Embassy Suites. The bed was very comfortable and the room was clean. Hotel staff were very friendly and courteous and check-in was fast. Elevators were a bit slow at times, but this is always the case in tall hotels. I stayed on the 16th Floor and had an awesome view. The room AC kept the room cool during the heat wave the city was experiencing. The cleaning staff did a great job everyday.
The hotel is in the middle of "everything" in downtown Indianapolis and surrounded by restaurants and a large shopping mall (directly connected).

title: “Fun Weekend in Austin”
text: I took my family to Austin for a long weekend to see the Bat Bridge. We used points to stay at the Westin at the Domain. The hotel is a nice, new, and somewhat typical Westin. The Domain shopping area is right there and very walkable. It is only about 15-20 minutes to donwtown Austin. We especially enjoyed the Platinum breakfast amenity as they had wonderful healthy choices for breakfast.

title: “Excellence on Concierge Service”
text: There never fails to be a time when i show up for the hotel and David Richardson hasn't already seen my reservation and made my stay the excellent experience that i have come accustom to in Phoenix. I cant wait to tell many of my travelers in business what a great hotel from the front desk to the lady in the gift shop that gets me my pecan sticky buns every morning ...this is first class service at its finest thanks Hilton!!!

title: “Most comfortable bed ever!”
text: The room was nice. Nothing too fancy but the view was nice and you could see the Boston Commons. Great service.

title: “Club Quarters Chicago Loop Review”
text: My aunt and I stayed here for 3 nights in November (got the room on Hotwire, payed $198 plus tax per night). It was clean, quiet, small, quite ok for a business person, but it was a bit claustrophobic for 3 nights for us. Every employee we encountered was very polite and helpful. My only real complaint is that every night about 4:30am we were awakened by a loud banging sound. We mentioned it to 2 employees, who had no idea what it was, but a maintenance man was walking by and overheard us, he said it was the sound of steam pipes being turned on too fast. Other than that, a very good stay. Elephant and Castle had fish and chips that melt in your mouth. Hotel is in a great location, if the price is right. Berghoffs and the Grillroom we highly recommend. Had dessert under the Christmas tree in the Walnut Room at Macys, saw the King Tut exhibit, Shedd Aquarium, Art Institute, even got to attend a taping of Oprah. Ginos East Pizza is excellent. Had a great time, stayed an extra night at another hotel, will review separately. All in all, loved Chicago!

title: “Nice Location, Expensive Wi-Fi...”
text:
This Hotel is very well located, with easy access to highways, shopping mall and restaurants area. But still expensive, in all senses...food...valet, and they don't offer wi fi for free as many pricey hotels do...
check other options if you are in the LA area...
Also I stayed at room 1420 and is located right beside the service area door. They talk loud, move things all day...so if you are sleeping you could be upset...

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text:
I was in town for the weekend with friends. I selected this hotel because they offered one of the best rates from a room with 2 beds, and I am a frequent customer of the Millenium Brand in the UK. I have always been extremely satisfied with my stays at other locations, and this hotel did not disappoint. Upon check in, all of my requests were honored (pillows, room location, etc.). The room was spacious, clean, and the bed were the most comfortable hotel bed I've slept in for quite some time. Our room was on a high floor, but, the elevators were swift, and we never needed to wait long. The view from the room was impressive. The AC worked very well, and the bathroom was well stocked with the standard amenities. 
The location is great, just a few steps from Times Square, and only two short blocks to the nearly every subway line in Manhattan. And while the location is perfect for being in the middle of everything New York has to offer, I will admit that on our Saturday night stay, the noise from Times Square could be heard from our room, 46 stories up. Apparently, there was an event being held that had the crowd cheering! Every other evening however, it was very quiet.

title: “Good Hotel”
text:
All round a good hotel. The rooms and communal areas were clean. The beds were very comfortable and large and the staff were helpful. 
The best thing about this hotel is the location; walking distance to Union Square, Chinatown etc.
Be aware the lobby does get very busy.

title: “Satisfied”
text: Stayed new year's eve. Had a great stay. Friendly and helpful staff.

title: “Vintage Elegance and Fun Quacks”
text: We stayed at the Peabody for an anniversary weekend and it was an incredible experience. The hotel is vintage elegance at its finest. The front desk upgraded our room to the 2 story Romeo & Juliet suite...stunning! Later, wine and pastries were sent to our room. What a delightful surprise! The staff at the hotel is one of the warmest, friendliest and helpful that we have ever encountered outside of Disneyworld. The ducks add to the ambiance and are a must see! The duck design throughout the hotel is charming. The Lansky Bros stores have a bevy of well designed upscale stores on the lobby level that are full of history. You must go into the men's store to see all the guitars from famous store patrons! (Elvis, of course, their most famous client.) Put the Peabody on your bucket list! It's a must for everyone to experience! Quack-Quack!

title: “Over the hill Westin”
text:
Property is very tired and needs repair.. My room 835 was not only very beat-up but the bathroom was dirty, no fan, toilet seat un-hinged and door needed replacement.. Carpets shabby and faded. TV had only basic cable.. I'v been in better Super 8's. I know the 4* rating is for the amenities but I can't imagine anyone paying full rack for this dump. I'm a thinking even my rate was high for this place.. I now see why so many bids are won at the Westin...
On a positive note, Office staff were nice, the bed was confortable and the free shuttle is 24/7 which I used a couple of times so I didn't have to pay to park my rental.

title: “Conference in Phoenix”
text:
My wife, myself and our two kids recently stayed at the Palomar for a conference in Phoenix and loved it. This hotel was amazing and the staff were super friendly, always doing whatever they could to help. Any issues we had were immediately resolved in a very professional manner. The rooftop pool area is great for relaxing, lounging or having a few drinks. Happy hour was another special treat as well.
We have stayed in MANY hotels throughout our travels and this rates at or right near the top!

title: “Thoroughly recommend”
text: The staff at this hotel could not have been friendlier. We found them exceptional. The hotel restaurant (Dempsey's) had very good food and we would recommend it if you are staying in the hotel. Service was excellent. Our room was well appointed and our bathrooms were a cut above the usual hotel bathrooms. Everything was very clean and the hotel is very well managed with a dedicated and well-trained staff. I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Modern top line hotel in ideal downtown location.”
text: What more can you ask for. Great location, close to the mile. Hip decor with design flair. Discreet service; present but not imposing. Great workout facilities; rooftop pool with million dollar skyline view. Great pricing. Top line restaurant in house. Would enjoy this over the "W" any day.

title: “great hotel--ambassador club rep annmara superb”
text:
This is a great property ,reasonably priced with a "get it done staff".I had a presentation to do and material for meeting got delayed. Ambassador rep ANNMARRA was of great assistance and saved the day. She does a terrific job. I'll bring all my clients to the Intercontinental in the future.
 Tom Hartnett

title: “It's all about location”
text: When you're two blocks from Grand Central, you as a hotel patron are paying more for location than plushness. The hotel was very nice, great staff and attached to the Wheeltapper, a fine little restaurant. But the room was small and overpriced for a young couple looking for a nice NYC weekend. The beds were very comfy and the bathrooms were very clean. It's in the heart of the city and would be a fantastic deal if you can get a special price. Perfect for two coming to NYC for a weekend, not so great for families or folks on a tight budget. Since I've found better deals elsewhere in the city, I would say take a chance somewhere closer to the park or near Greenwich Village.

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text:
Stayed here for one night before an early flight. This hotel, although a Courtyard, actually had the feel of a full service Marriott. Restaurant and full bar serving decent food and individual TV screens in each booth. Several computers with printers in the lobby for boarding passes. Airport shuttle for your use. Free parking if you have a car, which I did. The surrounding neighborhood is fairly bleak, the closest gas a couple moles up the road and not much else around. But the rooms were large, very clean and the staff 
were very pleasant. The airport is 
about a 5 minute drive away. Overall I was impressed with the amenities here and the decent room rate. I wouldn't want to stay here as a base for a Boston trip but it's an excellent choice for the late arrivers or early departers to Logan.

title: “Pleasant, well-located hotel”
text:
The hotel is in a very good location, convenient to the Upper West Side and the subway. Rooms are small, but they have been refurbished and are modern and clean. The beds and bedding are quite comfortable and the room has a Keurig coffee pot. The only drawback is the lack of sufficient lighting. There is free wireless in the lobby but there is a charge for Internet service in the rooms. 
Try to get a room on a higher floor as the hotel overlooks a very busy thoroughfare.

title: “The other reviewers are right, as usual”
text:
For a first time visitor to New York, this hotel is close to the Midtown action (44th St, just west of 5th Ave ) without being so close to Times Square that you can't sleep, and the previous reviewers are spot on with their comments. Choose a high floor by paying slightly more and the view and traffic noise will be fine; we had the Rockerfeller Center view to the north which was spectacular. The front desk was warm and helpful, the concierge knowledgeable although a little brusque. I recommend avoiding the breakfast in the Gabi Restaurant- sure it was OK, but for a fraction of the price you can eat in a NYC diner or deli, with real New York atmosphere and none of the pretension. The Pax cafe (part of chain) on Bryant Park SW corner with 6th Ave serve anything from fresh pancakes to Granola with fruit- we took it out and ate in the park.
The hotel was clean, everything worked fine, the decor was plain and tasteful- will need touching up soon though, and the beds were soft but very comfy to sleep in. , Be aware that it does have a French air of insouciance about it, but all things considered it was a comfortable, safe choice and we were not disappointed.

title: “Reasonable price trendy hotel in soho”
text: Hotel perfect for soho shopping trip. Hotel is very modern and has a great rooftop gym and bar. David Burke restaurant was ok. The concierge gave great dining recommendations.

title: “Loved it”
text: Very impressed with the Seaport. A lot of little touches that make it great - the doorbells, with do not disturb feature, the gym was great and the room service was also very good but expensive.

title: “Great if you can find it!”
text: I was with a group of 17, with 12 being kids. After traveling all day to our hotel destination, we could not get the kids in the pool quick enough. We first had a reservation at another Comfort Suties just down the road on 281 N service road. As soon as we checked in, we were notified the first hotel's swimming pool was closed. The first hotel helped us find this Stonebridge Comfort Suites with an available pool! Took a bit to re-locate, but we did. Like other said, Stonebridge Comfort Suites is very difficult to find and we too had to call for directions. The rooms were great and breakfast was marvelous. One of our groups ordered pizza for thier room and said it was great! I can't remember who the menu is from but it isn't affiliated with the hotel, just services the hotel. If you want, the hotel is next too a huge movie theater, many restaraunts, shopping, all in walking distance. The pool was great!!!

title: “Excellence is in the details”
text:
The overall experience of a hotel visit is an accumulation of details. As a veteran business traveler, now that I'm retired and choose -- and pay for -- my leisure visits, I take particular notice and tend to grade each aspect of the visit carefully. What makes visits to the San Francisco Hilton at Union Square such a delight is that the details consistently meet or exceed expectations.
My mental checklist begins with, was I made to feel welcome and special at check-in? Was there a prompt elevator and ease in finding my room? Was the room spacious and well-appointed, and not just neat? (Sparkling is best!) 
Is the room arranged sensibly with a place for a laptop and enough electric outlets to recharge electronic devices? (Ah, the power strip on the side of the desk is a nice touch!) Does the bed tempt you to sprawl and sigh with contentment -- and are there way more pillows than absolutely necessary? 
A nice view of San Francisco is always a pleasure. And, yes, they still have Le Source products in the bathroom. Slender, big screen TVs on the wall are a nice touch. Plenty of closet and drawer space, always a pleasure. 
Check-out? A snap, using either the phone or TV. 
High marks on all details. It also helps that the hotel is a short stroll to Union Square shopping, the theater district, lots of dining opportunities for a range of budgets, the cable car and countless buses, as well as street cars and BART, the mostly underground train that connects large chunks of the City and the Bay Area. 
Yes, there are less expensive hotels, but this one is a good value for what you get, and I consistently return to it as "my home in San Francisco". It makes me feel special, and that's all in the details.

title: “Great Location”
text: I really enjoyed staying at the Orchard Garden hotel - the location is fantastic - situated next to Nob Hill and China Town - it's a lovely 15-20 minute walk to Fisherman's Wharf. The room was pretty basic but clean and a decent size. The staff was freindly. Breakfast was not included. Cafe le Presse is across the street - great breakfast there.

title: “Great Location!”
text: Walking distance to the Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, the Mint, etc. Probably about 4-5 blocks. We never got our car out of the parking garage the entire stay. Pool on roof was a little too warm due to the heat wave, but still fun. Rooms were clean, one night got back late to our room not cleaned, but the manager made it up to us and adjusted our bill. Lots of security around with the mint next door. We were told by the hotel staff to take public transportation to the Art Museum for the fireworks, but we decided to start walking and see how far we got. We ended up walking the entire way - it was just over 2 miles on mapquest. It is certainly within a good walk!

title: “Great Rehab Project, fun to see and experience.”
text: Good location to the Garden to see the Bruins play. Upon arrival our car was met by friendly dapper greeter who introduced himself and evidently alerted the reservation desk of our arrival. We were greeted there by name and super friendly service. The common areas are unique and very cool.The bars in the rotunda and the vaulted circular building are very impressive. Rooms were fine but the impact of the entrance is a hard act to follow. The bloody mary bar in unique and the food is innovative. I would return in a heart beat.

title: “would of got a 5 but i had a few issues”
text: 1)10$ per day for the internet 2) Showers were most of the time luke warm and not a lot of pressure. 3) 626 restaurant was good, but i tried sharing their buffet with my wife and they charged me double and we never went back after that. so just be careful if you decide to do that. 4) no private toilet room door. I love the staff at the OMNI, personable and very helpful. From the doormen to the concierge. The rooms were very, very clean. Ours was medium and very pleasant. Chicago is the best US city in my opinion, the food, the architecture and history and the museums are the best the US has to offer!!! Shaws seafood was the highlight, it was packed and i knew why after eating there. Oysters were EXCELLENT!!! Since it is a big city, lots of Sirens, they can get annoying after a while!!!

title: “Great location”
text: The motel has been recently remodeled, so it was much better than the last time I stayed there. It fit my needs perfectly - a place to lay my head, take a shower and internet service was good too.

title: “Roosevelt hotel New York”
text: Bloody rude staff , hotel was like a Faberge egg beautiful to look at but full of rude, incompetent , ignorant workers , exception being the cleaning staff who were lovely , We stayed at the Bentley hotel last year, save yourselves hundreds of dollars and be treat correctly by caring staff and book the Bentley , forget the Roosevelt ...room wasn't ready until 9:30 pm after a 10 hour flight we only wanted to rest ... No excuse given just a very rude " credit card". No welcome to the Roosevelt , no hello, nothing ! Just " credit card" ....followed by , your rooms not ready come back in a few hours leave your bags with the concierge .....4 star hotel 1 star staff ......keep away

title: “Nice room and staff, but ....”
text: The room was very comfortable and the staff was very polite. I especially noticed the sheets, which were comfortable and of high quality, and we loved the rotating tv panel. Some minor cleanliness issues with the room were immediately dealt with to our satisfaction by the staff, which we very much appreciated. Norma's is absolutely amazing for brunch, although you should make advance reservations if you plan to eat here on the weekend. Before you book the hotel, though, be aware that there are extra charges to use the gym and to use the pool, a fee to use the internet, plus parking your car is about $50 per night. These charges can quickly add $100 per night to your bill. If you are used to these sorts of charges, then I would highly recommend the hotel.
