I am a frequent traveler to very nice hotels in NYC, LA and Chicago, and this is the first time I have been charged for gym or pool use and it clouded my impression of the hotel. Perhaps I should have looked more closely at their web site, where I would hope they mention these additional charges.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Great location - close to shopping, the Millennium Park and the Navy Pier but also easy to get around for business. I travel to Chicago for business several times a year. Fairmont Chicago is one of the hotels that I would choose to stay there. The beds and pillows were soft and comfortable. Decor in the rooms was modern. Service at front desk and concierge was attentive. Easy check-in and check-out. I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Oustanding service”
text: This hotel was very clean, spacious and the view of NYC was excellent. The staff went above and beyond our expectations. It is within safe walking distance to everything you could want or need. Five stars from us!!!!

title: “Luxe is Chic and has Superb Service”
text: I have stayed at the Luxe on Sunset twice now and it has many excellent qualities. Foremost, the staff is very customer oriented and they go out of their way to please. The valet staff was plentiful and there was never a wait for my car to be taken or delivered. Room service was fast and efficient even after 10 pm. My room was always made up perfectly; fresh sheets on the beds without requiring a special request and evening turn down. Although the Luxe was some sort of motel in its former life, this is only evident in the hallways. The public spaces and guest rooms are very chic and decorated in soothing natural colors. Standard rooms are not huge, but the size is adequate. Rooms in the main building have balconies where you can sit outside and watch the birds in the foliage, a rarity in LA. The location is adjacent to the 405 freeway, but traffic noise is not a problem inside the rooms. The main negative was that construction was continuing on the 405 and there were detours on Sunset which were inconvenient.

title: “Updated Hotel but noisy”
text: The Curtis staff and rooms were lovely. But it was an older hotel and therefore you could hear the guest coming up and down the halls. Warm cookie on arrival was a nice touch. Staff was very helpful! We had a package and the wine and vouchers were in our room when we arrived!

title: “Nickel & dime you to death/Poor Service”
text:
What a disappointment of hotel...stayed for 5 days from 20th October with my family in a one bed suite with great expectation of it being amazing. Well on arrival we were taken to a room with a flooded unusable bathroom which then took three different calls and three different staff inspections to get us moved, not because it wasn't obvious we needed to be moved but because in a 5 star hotel different teams didn't speak to each other. Also while we waited to be moved a broken rollaway bed was delivered and then taken away by staff even though we had prebooked it. My family desperately need to use the bathroom after a 7 hr flight from London and a horrendous 4 hour journey from JFK (another story) and we were directed to use the bathrooms in the lobby (the men room was also flooded in he lobby). The hotels idea of making this right was not to comp us dinner (which we had to have in the hotel room because it was so late but to send us milk and cookies).
Also this was an expensive suite yet the room didn't even had facilities for making a coffee, the internet was a ridiculous $19 per 24 hours, access to the gym was an extra charge, breakfast which was very so so was $44 per head....I know that NYC hotels tend to charge for most things but this is a hotel with its hand out from the minute you walk through the door.
Finally on the day we left we had a late flight and brought our bags down to the lobby and at check out no one asked us about our stay (perhaps they didnt care) and when I asked for my bags to be stored by the bell captain we got into a bizarre conversation about how the bag store was in the basement and he could take it down for me if I wanted (Isnt that your job?) or i.e. if I tipped him.
A hotel who's culture is based not on service but on milking its clients...very disappointing

title: “Good location - reasonable price”
text: I stayed here during a business trip and it was close to the office and major Chicago attractions. My room was small but sufficient for business travel. Front desk staff very helpful - clean rooms - okay fitness center. Close to major intersections so a bit nosy but overall, not a bad place.

title: “Great Overall Experience”
text:
Overall, I thought this was a great hotel experience. It is a very upscale hotel. The hallways are well lit and spacious. The decor of the hotel was very posh. I thought the beds were very comfortable, and I thought the bathrooms were marvelous.
I loved the morning complimentary hot chocolate with the copy of the USA Today. I thought the hotel staff was very courteous, with one exception... If you are member of a minority group, the hotel security may give you unnecessary attention. My husband had to approach one of the guards to ask why he was was paying him such close attention.
Despite the ignorance and biases of the hotel staff, I thought is was a great stay with a prime DC location.

title: “Beautiful hotel--fabulous staff!!”
text: I chose this hotel based on the recommendation of friends and was not disappointed. The location is terrific, providing gorgeous ocean views and close access to the beach (note, the hotel sits above the beach, so you must use the nearby wooden staircase to get there). The room decor is plush with a tropical flair--comfortable beds, wooden louvered rolling shutters, and premium dark wood furniture. We enjoyed the huge flat screen TV and DVD player. The bath area included a large marble-topped counter and sink with large mirror, separate from the toilet and tub. The countertop housed a small fridge and also a mini-bar. Everything was sparkling clean. The balcony was oversized and included 4 wrought iron chairs and table. Our particular room faced a more southern direction, but the balcony was semi-circular in shape which allowed for a broad view. We did partially overlook the side street and a few buildings, but still had full ocean views, including some spectacular sunsets. (There are also ocean front rooms that overlook the pool area.) The pool was small, but more than adequate; the lounge chairs were comfortable and I really enjoyed being able to see the ocean waves while lounging by the pool. The hotel does not have a restaurant on-site, but there are many places to eat within walking distance. They also have a unique system with a couple of the local restaurants where you can actually charge your meal to your hotel room. There is also the option to have room service provided by nearby restaurants. There do serve breakfast, at an additional cost ($9). We enjoyed it--choice of ham and cheese omelets with breakfast potatoes, bacon or sausage and toast or waffle and bacon or sausage. Plus coffee, juice, milk, and hot chocolate. I can't say enough about the staff. Everyone at the front desk was extremely helpful and accommodating. Check-in and check-out was smooth and efficient. I was welcomed back every time I returned through the lobby. Every single staff member I encountered greeted me. I also noted that members of the staff were constantly cleaning and polishing the public areas. All in all, really top-notch. The room rates are in line with first class status, but I really felt like they went out of their way to earn it. While this is a smaller property, they provide personal touches, accommodations, and service that is equal to or better than the larger resorts. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Fabulous find”
text:
We moved to The London NYC after spending 2 nights at another very pricey hotel in New York which we were very unhappy with.
From the moment we entered the lobby we were delighted. The staff were very helpful and friendly always.The concierge staff couldn't do enough for us, the wait staff in the Restaraunt were always very pleasant and courteous.
We were a family with 3 older teenagers so were delighted to find such a large apartment .
The rooma were always cleaned, the gym was fabulous, and we thought value for money, the whole place was well worth it.
Will definitely be back.

title: “Convenient, up to date and well run”
text:
Spent one night here visiting friends who were attending a conference. Impressions:
- very convenient to the convention center - just a short walk across the street.
- the GasLamp district is also a short walk away. 
- solid, well trained staff. Lines never lasted long during check-in and check-out and they take the time to step out from behind the counter to direct you to the elevators. 
- if you are on an upper floor, there are awesome views of the Bay, even if you are on the side of the hotel with the Dole Foods shipping terminal, as long as you are on an upper floor.
- we were on the top floor, and there was a corporate event in one of their meeting rooms on that floor, and it was very loud from 8 to 10 PM, so if you plan to hit the hay early, make sure you are away from the elevator lobby area.
- our room was very clean and comfortable.
- we would stay here again.

title: “We could not ask for more!”
text:
My friend and I were looking for a weekend getaway to NYC and visit some friends in town. It wasn't easy finding a nice, descent looking and most of all inexpensive hotel (specially in Manhattan) I was fearing not to find the hotel to our expectations. My fears dissapeared once we arrived and noticed that the hotel was just what we needed! I belive the best feature of this hotel is it's location, just 3 blocks from Times Square and 2 from Central Park. I may agree on some of the other reviews about the customer service or lack of profesionalism...since there was a small glitch with our hotel room, but no biggie. And the elevator at peak hours...it can get crowded, so either wait or take the stairs, Ah! and local calls aren't free! so maybe use the lobby phone instead of the room's. Other than that we had no complaints as we practially used the room to crash after a long day of sightseeing and shopping. The beds were comfortable, (I miss the pillows lol!) the atmosphere was quiet and no funny smells were found in the room. I strongly recomend Park Central Hotel!
Kitchener, ON - Canada

title: “Very average experience”
text:
My wife and I just stayed at the Gansevoort Park avenue for 5 nights - just to preface this review, we have stayed at very high end resorts/hotels all over the world including LA, Las Vegas, Europe, etc...here are our thoughts.
Pros:
1. Very good location - there is a starbucks and bread & butter nearby for breakfast. Very central location to most places in NYC.
2. Good size room - we were pleased with the size of the room and bathroom
3. Gave late checkout until 12:30pm on day of our departure
4. Nightclub upstairs - we checked this out on the Fri night - nice venue although it served overpriced drinks and was quite crowded (but nice to have this nonetheless).
Cons:
1. We were never told that the hotel adds a $150/night charge for incidentals - my credit card company saw this as a 'strange' charge and cancelled my card. So for my entire trip I had no credit card - I really wish the hotel had told me about this when I was initialing my invoice so I could have called my credit card company and told them about this extra charge. 
2. Bathroom - the shampoo and conditioner sucked. For a high end hotel, it was quite pathetic. Also the toilet paper kept flying off the stand when trying to use it. Very frustrating. The shower had this weird green stain on it (still not sure what this was). 
3. Bar/Club - drinks waay overpriced - we paid over $30 for 2 vodka/cranberry's. Very crowded too - not somewhere I would return to be honest. 
Overall I found this to be an average experience. I think the location of this place is probably its best feature. For the amount of money that we paid, I have experienced much better hotels.

title: “Not worth the price.”
text: Location is good (depending on your plans), but overall I was very disappointed in this hotel. I expected cleaner, more amenities, a more comfortable bed, a better TV, etc.... more like what you'd expect from a higher end Starwood chain. Instead, the TV was old with poor reception, the bed was very uncomfortable, the AC/heat controls didn't work, everything seemed a bit dingy, had to pay to use the fitness center, and if you wanted to actually look in the mirror as you blow dried your hair, you couldn't since the hotel had what I consider the cheap way out by having the blow dryer stuck to the wall (and the mirror wasn't positioned close to it). All in all, wouldn't stay here again-- especially considering the thousands of other choices in NYC.

title: “So disappointing...not a 4 star hotel.”
text: Parking $52 almost more than we paid for the room.... We had high hopes for our "stay"-cation coming from the Chicago suburbs with our 9 month old. We looked forward to relaxing... Well, we were more than disappointed. First, most importantly, at 8:40 am, we (and our baby!) were still sleeping when housekeeping tried to enter our room to clean it. We wanted to cry since our baby rarely sleeps in. We were told we should have put the sign up but hey in this day in age of computer technology and cell phones you serious cant get coordinated? Overall, the rooms were ok however, our view of multiple homeless sleeping on lower wacker made us reflect on our lives and the lives of the less fortunate - not something we expected for our stay-cation. I do have to say most of the staff was friendly and willing to help. The food at the bistro was ok- but the description for the bbq chicken was plain wrong. Not a 1/2 chicken - a split breast and the description mentioned brussel sprouts... but at first we did not get any and then when we did, it was the leaves from 1 brussel sprout grilled... tasty but really lacking.

title: “Poor Handling of Overbooking”
text:
The hotel could not honor our reservation because the overbooked. We worked out an agreement with the Front desk staff which was later revoked. As a result a member of our party slept on the floor.
I understand overbooking, it happens, but reneging on a compromise agreement and lying about what was offered is inexcusable and horrible customer service. Leaving a second star because the rooms were clean and the location is good for Financial District.
For the hotel's reference we were very disappointed in how JT handled our overbooking situation.

title: “LOVED the Doubletree”
text:
After days of searching for Philly hotels, I booked the Doubletree on Hotwire based on its 100% recommendation. And those reviews were right. The hotel was easy to find on the corner of Broad & Locust, and parking was right next to the hotel... someone from the hotel was even outside to let us know we were in the right place. And although other hotels in Philly had parking charges of $40+, the Doubletree's charge was $22 and was charged right to our room. 
The hotel was in the arts district, and there were a lot of restaurants and shops nearby. My kids LOVED the warm chocolate chip cookies we got at reception, and the pizzeria the front desk recommended for dinner. 
Although the smallish indoor pool was crowded when we got there in the late afternoon, we had the whole area to ourselves Sunday morning which was amazing. The fitness center also looked really nice.
The room was clean, and we loved the modern decor. Even better, our room was like a studio suite, with a queen bed on one end and a sofa bed on the other. Of course, there was also a flat-screen TV, coffee maker, and a huge desk and chair. Although there was only one blanket in the room, we were able to get one in a few minutes when we got cold in the middle of the night.
The only negative was that we were next to the ice machine, which got a little noisy. But I'd definitely trade a little noise for an awesome room and a 'private' pool.

title: “Good Value in Memphis”
text: I booked this hotel not knowing its location relative to the attractions in Memphis. It is a 10-15 minute walk to most Beale street area attractions but the $1 trolley and the hotel shuttle help you overcome this, unless of course you stay out past midnight. The service at the hotel was very good and the staff responded promptly to all requests. The room was clean and looked to be recently renovated. My only complaints about this hotel are the parking fees and the prices at their bar. $15 a night to self park at an "off the main drag" hotel is excessive. $12.50 for two 12 ounce beers (not even pint!) is excessive. I would also add that you do not want to stay at this hotel if traffic noise bothers you. My room looked right out on I-40

title: “Beautiful historical hotel, great location”
text: Great location, right by the main touristic attractions of the Freedom Trail. The architecture of the place is amazing! The room we got was tiny, but really clean and very silent, I had a great night's sleep.

title: “Service was great but hotel was extremely noisy & very poor internet service. Walls very thin. Heard every step & flush.”
text:
Hotel was very neat, clean & great service but, in dire need of upgrade in insulation. Very noisy, heard every flush, steps & words from other guests in other rooms. If you are a light sleeper & in need of rest this is not the hotel for you. Front desk suggested booking a room on the 3rd floor so as not to have people above you. 
Don't buy the internet service don't work 50% of the time.
Beautiful grounds & great service.

title: “Worse Hotel I ever stayed in!”
text: We stayed here because Wyndham is supposed to be a nice hotel. First room was dirty, bathroom was never clean and carpets were not vacuumed and it smelled musty. Second room had a moldy mattress, it was truly disgusting. Third room the sheets had never been changed! Hotel Manger would not return any of my calls, and he was not available both days we were there. Called the customer service line about the Hotel they were less then helpful. Truly disgusted with our stay. Warning stay far away from this hotel!

title: “EXCELLENT VALUE”
text:
Suprised by how spacious the rooms are. Location is AWESOME for doing anything downtown. Walk to beach, restaurants and shopping. 10 dollar cab ride from most areas to go out at night too. There is a free breakfast. The hotel looks small from outside but the rooms are REALLY big. Like - bigger than my apartment. If I could live here I would! 
Beds are super comfy too.

title: “Great value for money!!!”
text: We booked two rooms for our party of five, four of whom were on a first trip to NYC, so wanted to see as much as possible in our 5 day stay. Travel Inn proved to be a perfect location - short walk to Times Square, Theatre District etc. Cross town bus stop outside the hotel and only a short walk to subway and Port Authority bus terminal. We were assigned two large (by NY standards) adjoining rooms - very comfortable and great heating, especially as it was minus 5 one day! The rooms were cleaned daily with fresh towels and toiletries. Added bonus was having full size fridge and microwave which came in handy after a long day's sightseeing. We would recommend this hotel and hope to return in the near future.

title: “Not the best.”
text:
We stayed here for two nights as the last stop on our road trip honeymoon from Vegas to SF. 
It was the most disapointing hotel of the whole two weeks. 
I have not stayed in any other hotels in SF so dont have anything direct to compare with. 
But I did not enjoy my stay here. 
Everything in the room was covered in dust. It was as if no one had been in there for months. The Valet was rude and was waiting for me to tip him - Sorry but I do not expect to have to tip someone who is rude to me! 
Then on my return to the UK I noticed that they had charged my Credit Card Twice for the stay!! 
We had paid in advance for our whole honeymoon - but they still charged us for the bedroom - and so I had to call up from the UK to get it refunded - that was fun - about 10 phone calls and answering machine messages later they finally refund me - but not for the 'Charge' the bank made for using my Credit Card abroad. So It cost me around £10 for their mistake. 
I would not stay here again.

title: “GREAT Staff and Better than Expected Stay”
text: I stayed at this hotel for just one night on 1/21/12 as my company was having their annual party in Denver and figured it would be safest to stay overnight at a nearby hotel that had shuttle service. As soon as I arrived at the hotel to check in I realized the staff were just as I had read on TA...exceptional! The bellhop and concierge Chris immediately helped me with my luggage and got me and my belongings to my room in super fast time. The shuttle driver, Rick, made me feel like a VIP and the shuttle vehicle looked more like a limo than what I was expecting (a regular hotel shuttle 'bus' which is typically what you get when it's free). I stayed very late at the party so had to taxi it back to the hotel which was not a problem. The next morning another bellhop, Michael, was at my door in short order to get me and my belongings safely back to my car. I had slept well in the comfy bed and the room temperature for me was perfect. The only complaint is having other folks who are leaving the hotel while I was asleep would allow the doors to slam closed which woke me every time it happened. Other than that, my short stay was delightful and I will most certainly be returning when I need a clean room and a lovely hotel in Denver. Thanks, Loews! Your staff are wonderful!!!

title: “Well priced, clean and elegant in heart of San Francisco”
text:
This hotel is ideally situated and well priced for any traveller to San Francisco.
We arrived a little jet lagged and confused after disembarking from the BART at Powell.
The hotel is located a short stroll from the Powell Street / Market Street public transport station up the hill, past Macy's on Powell Street about 1 block from Union Square. You can't miss it.
In terms of location you couldn't get any better. The hotel is in the heart of Downtown San Francisco city. It has easy access to restaurants, coffee shops and public transport which provide easy access to all major attractions in San Francisco. At Powell and Market Street you can catch the street car to Embarcadero or the MUNI and BART to all other major areas. The Cable Car runs right outside the hotel although I would recommend any traveller catch the Cable Car a few blocks down the hill rather than outside your hotel as you're more likely to actually get a seat.
A Walgreens Pharmacy and Starbucks is located within 1 minutes walk and a Loris Diner is nearby. Nob Hill is a short 5 minute walk up the hill with access to local shops and restaurants. A coin laundry is about 5 minutes walk up to Nob Hill and around the corner.
The hotel is a very well maintained older building with a charm and elegance of its own and all the features of a modern hotel. The front desk staff were friendly and helpful.
Our room was located on the 10th floor. It was very clean and tidy and relatively spacious. It was equipped with a nice table and 2 chairs, wardrobe (closet) with more than enough spaces for bags, luggage and to sit down.
The bed was Queen sized and is one of the most comfortable beds I have slept in. Definitely easy to sleep here. The curtains are black out and the pillows comfortable. Sheets were clean and changed daily.
The bathroom was sized for one only but had all the features required including toilet, mirror, basin and good sized bath / shower.
From what I have read the place has had a recent renovation and the green and brown really suits the hotel.
There is also a bar and restaurant on the bottom floor. While we didn't make use of the bar, the downstairs restaurant was reasonably priced and breakfast was quite good and service adequate. As good as the adjoining famous Sears Fine Food.
Our room was cleaned daily and the staff at the tour desk were very helpful in booking tours or with directions.
The place also has free wi-fi which was easy to connect to, fast and reliable.
Given the age of the building, the room does not have A/C. In the middle of summer, I didn't find this a problem and given San Francisco's history of a pretty consistent temperature all year around I found the temperature in the room comfortable. If you had a few long hot days, it may get little warm although you can open the windows for some fresh air.
For the price, I find it very hard to fault this hotel and would happily stay here again and recommend to others visiting San Francisco. Worth the 5 stars.

title: “Excellent Choice”
text: Everything about this hotel was excellent. From a spotless, newly refurbished bedroom to the very smartly presented staff. Breakfast was very good too - a wide choice available in a very clean dinning room. The pool area was a bit stark and for much of the day in the shade. But the temperature of the main pool was the warmest so far on our trip. Would certainly stay here again.

title: “Excellent Grand Dame... Fabulous Location, Service”
text: Stayed for the first time recently and was pleasantly surprised. Great location and super comfortable beds. As a Diamond member, we had a access to the Executive Lounge and that was nice... Lavazza Italian coffee machine was fantastic, basic continental bkfst was good, not great... but well staffed and stocked. Amazing views if facing the water/lakeshore dr. A ton of people work here... this is one place where they didn't cut back on staff... and it is well appreciated. Enjoyed this place a lot.

title: “Horrible and disorganized”
text: i booked through hot wire,got there at 1030 after a long day at seaworld only for the receptionst to tell us that we were booked for the following day which was alie..we showed them the proof and they sent to us to a room on the 10th floor which loked crappy jaz by looking at it with one quenn Bed for a family of four. we were stranded for a whole hour with sleepy tiref kids not knowing what to do!!!eventually smone counseled their reservation and we were transfered!!this was the worst hotel experience i ever had...DONT STAY HERE"!!!

title: “Was everything we expected.”
text: We just returned home after a 5 night stay at the Omni. The location was the best in the historic district. We were on the 12th floor and could see the baseball stadium from a distance so we were treated to fireworks at the stadium 2 of our nights. Our children enjoyed the pool it was a little small but suited our needs. The room was a good size and very comfortable. We did order food at the lounge the first night and had breakfast the first morning there but it was a bit pricey so we found other options. We walked or caught the phlash trolley to get around and it worked great. We loved Philly there is a lot to do there.

title: “Lots of Little Things to Improve”
text: Lobby is bright, fresh, and clean. But the rooms are tired and smell just a little bit foul. And they are not suites (2 double beds and a sofa bed all in the same room). Rooms under-accessorized too...no linens for sofa bed, no paper towels or seating for kitchen, only one trash can, etc. Staff is courteous but hard to track down when problems arise.

title: “Pure Luxury!”
text: I absolutely adore the Fairmont Hotel in San Jose. I've stayed at this hotel on several occasions and I enjoy it more with each time. To start, the Fairmont has gorgeous lobby and wonderful resturaunts including the Fountain (which makes a mean cheeseburger, might I add). The rooms are decorated with lovely light tones and provide a relaxing and comfortable atmosphere. And the bathrooms, well...with seperate shower and bath, a television, telephone and a private toilet...the bathrooms are reason enough to book a reservation.The detail in the Fairmont is subtle yet classy, such as the monogramed F's that are found on several objects throughout the hotel, even on the bottom of the pool. There are two great bars not within resturaunts, one located in the lobby (a great place for evening cocktails) and the other found on the fourth floor next to the pool (very nice for fulfilling my fantasies of lounging next to the pool with a straw hat and a drink).In addition to all these wonderful features, the Fairmont has added a tower adjacent to the main hotel which offers more rooms. I would this hotel recommend it to everyone. Enjoy!

title: “Weekend in Chicago”
text:
We arrived at the Westin at 2pm and our room was ready for us. We paid extra for the club floor $60 per night. I thought drinks were included, but it was cash bar. You got a continental breakfast, which was rather nice, cereal, oatmeal, toast,bagels,doughnuts, fresh fruit, juice and coffee. Nice and clean. Night snack around 5pm, two hot bites and coffee and soda. It was all right. You also got free internet in your room. They had a I-Pad on the desk for your use. that was very nice. So whether the $60 per night was worth it I guess so.. We were on the 20th floor, the view was not very good but other than that it was nice.
The hotel was nice and clean and the maid service was nice also. Great location near alot of restaurants and shopping all with in walking. We did not bring coats and it was rather cold, by the water, so we had to buy jackets. Make sure to bring a sweater or jacket in spring weather.
I would come back again.

title: “Love the Bliss Toiletries, Indifferent on the Upscale IKEA-ish Furnishings”
text:
The W San Francisco fully embodies Starwood's branding play for the trendy professional. It's in the perfect location if you're attending a conference at Moscone Center. I wouldn't recommend the W for families or a romantic getaway.
Check-in and Check-out went smoothly. All employees were very courteous and friendly. The room was comfy with an upscale IKEA-like decor. Some things I particularly liked: Bliss shampoo/conditioner/facewash, the massaging roller for your feet under the desk, a rather large wall-mounted flat-screen TV, and the very novel hotel stationery. 
One suggestion for improvement (very minor issue): They need bigger, fluffier bath towels. For a higher-end brand like the W, i didn't expect standard size bath towels with a slightly coarse feel. 
Breakfast at the restaurant was delicious with typical hotel pricing. 
Once again, the W is great for the trendy professional who loves the hustle and bustle. Hope this helps! Cheers.

title: “Not bad for Seattle Center”
text: Reasonably good property. Excellent location within Seattle Center, great connectivity to transit network. Rooms are a little noisy, and elevators/hallways are somewhat dated. Breakfast was decent, service was attentive. I can see where on-site parking can be an issue (is limited to surface & 1 underground deck), though it wasn't for us mid-week. For the money, looked like the best alternative as compared to neighboring properties.

title: “Average hotel”
text:
Not one of the best places to stay in. I suppose if you're just looking for a roof over your head and not fussed by below par living standards.
Breakfast is a mixed bag of nonsense. Rooms are ancient looking and archaic. TVs look like they have been pulled from student halls. Nothing works in the gym, in fact all the equipments are safety hazards, either creaking or broken, don't get me started on the treadmill - almost died!! Ice machine works and the pool works.
I was here for the OTC conference in May and was very disappointed by the general quality. The staff were very nice and plesant however.
I got the wrong bill for my room for the icing on the cake.
Verdict - if you're looking for a bang tidy hotel then avoid but if you're passing through and spending minimal time in the room then why not!

title: “Fantastic Get-Away!”
text: The Westin was a lovely hotel to escape to for our 10th wedding anniversary and first time to NYC. The hotel was beautiful and contemporary looking with its furnishings. Housekeeping was wonderful and prompt. The reservation/ticket counter people were extremely helpful with recommendations for shows and getting tickets at the last minute! They were also helpful with recommending local eateries before and after the Yankees game.

title: “What a Location”
text:
We visited New York to celebrate our 25th wedding anniversary and stayed at the W Times Square. The hotel gave us a corner room which overlooked both Broadway and Times Square. The large bed was the most comfortable one that I have ever slept on.
 The room was modern and clean and the en suite couldn't be faulted. The staff were very friendly and helpful and we really enjoyed a terrific evening in the hotel bar sampling the amazing cocktails made for us. If we manage to go to New York again I will be heading once more to this hotel with its fabulous interiors and its location at the heart of the city.

title: “Comfortable Stay for SC/ND Game Weekender”
text: Friendly staff w/great location. Next door to the Hancock Bldg. Two blocks from Ditka's Steakhouse (new favorite over Smith & Wollensky's). Rec'd Plat. upgrade to Jr. Suite on top floor (Rm 2736). One large room w/couch, dining table, and king bed. View of Hancock & Ferris Wheel on Navy Pier. Normal rooms slightly small w/two beds but comfortable. I plan to stay here the next game. Fight On!

title: “2 Nights at the Marriott Ren Ctr”
text:
I stayed at the Marriott for 2 nights, along with a large group visiting Detroit for an event. The room was nice, clean and a good size. The hotel's location in the Renaissance Center means that there is convenient access to the river, the People Mover, the Tube (a 2nd floor enclosed passage to the building center across the street) and numerous shops, cafes, restaurants and offices located in the Ren Center. 
We did, however, find the layout of the building to be a bit confusing and difficult to navigate at times. Different levels of the hotel must be accessed by different elevators, including the reception lobby. Note that for security, after-hours, your room key is needed to enter the hotel from public parts of the Ren Center (as opposed to entering from the hotel's dedicated valet driveway).
It was thunderstorming when we arrived so we opted to pay extra for the valet service rather than the self-park. This turned out to be well worth the money because once your car is registered with the valet, you can take it out and drop it off anytime during your stay for the same 24-hour rate. With the self-park, you pay every time you come and go. 
Also, most of our group was located on one specific floor of the "Low Rise" part of the hotel (below floor 40). One couple was placed, inexplicably, on a "High Rise" floor. Their room apparently came with some additional in-room amenities, though I don't recall what they were. I would suggest inquiring as to the differences between Low Rise and High Rise room amenities.

title: “Excellent”
text:
I changed my reservation to this when noticed on Google maps that my car rental Avis was across the street. You will have most departement stores very close by, and the station for the monorail out to the Space Needle (1962 World Exibition Event) is less than a block away. The Swedes have a word for a little hideaway where you may enjoy the best in life; smultronstaelle. The Westin Seattle is like Westin Galleria in Houston; Hasslefree!
I try to hold on to my money, but this was worth every dollar spent.

title: “Perfect Mother-Daughter Weekend”
text: This hotel was the perfect balance of elegance and functionality for a mother-daughter weekend. Our 2 double bed room was a comfortable size with upscale decor, provided a good selection of television (for me and my 12 year old) and had comfortable bedding. The hotel is large enough to explore, but not get lost in. Breakfast in the restaurant provided a wonderful 5-star experience without feeling pretentious. The location is superb - close to shopping and the excitement of Copley Square. We had dinner at Douzo (their sushi is amazing), window shopped on Newbury street (very expensive shopping, but there are a few hidden bargain places if you're willing to explore), and visited the Boston Public Library. Be sure to check out the Copley Square organic farm stands that set up carts on the weekends - some really nice herbs, honey, vegetables, etc.

title: “Good Value”
text: Second year that i have staye there, good place for the money. Friendly staff, good food and easy access to Columbus.

title: “Good stay!”
text: My family stayed here for a week for our trip to New York and overall it was a great stay. The location of the hotel is fantastic for those wanting to get right into the tourist attractions of NYC as it is literally in the middle of times square and in walking distance to many other things such as the rockerfeller center, radio city hall etc. The hotel was generally clean and quiet. However in our room overlooking times square it was quite noisy with sirens constantly blaring but we did move to another room where it was substantially quieter. The rooms were quite small but they were clean and comfortable and the staff were always ready to help. Overall we had a great stay here.

title: “Trash outside to welcome you”
text: No, literally during my 3 days stay I found bags of garbage out side the hotel everyday. it may be a norm for New Yorkers. The front desk staff was friendly, Nick and Ashley. Room size is small. No bath tub at least the room I stayed in. The location is not really a desirable either. The bed and pillows were comfortable, however. Fresh warm cookies, a nice touch.

title: “Friendly staff, good location”
text: Good location, especially if traveling through Penn Station (it's right up the street). High Line is also right around the corner. We had a private room, which was perfectly adequate, but given that the price was in line with other budget hotels in the city, the place didn't quite measure up. It's probably a much better value if utilizing the shared space. It was clean, and the staff was friendly and helpful.

title: “You'll be sorry”
text:
I stayed at about a dozen hotels in the DC area over the last two months due to business commitments. I limited my selections to 3 and 4 star hotels. Out of the dozen I would rate this hotel as 12 (with #1 being the best). For the life of me I can't figure out how it has a 3 star rating. A 1.5 star rating would be generous. As far as pros and cons, there are no pros. The cons are as follows:
1. When we checked in there was no valet service.
2. The front of the hotel faces the front of a cancer center across 50 feet of blacktop (unlike the website photo which gives the appearance that the hotel faces the street).
3. In order to get to the street from the hotel entrannce you have to walk through several parking lots and you can't see the hotel entrance from the street.
4. While being on the Georgetown campus sounds attractive, the reality is that the hotel is in the middle of a construction zone as major construction/renovation is being done on the campus next to the hotel.
5. If you chose to park on the street instead of paying the hotel a $25.00 a night parking fee, you need to carry your luggage close to half a mile through several parking lots and around a few buildings because if you leave your car in front of the hotel while you unload your luggage (see above-no valet) you will get a ticket for leaving your car in a no parking zone (we got one and the car was only there for 5 minutes). Complaints to the hotel and the University about their not disclosing this fact on their website remain unanswered.
6. The first room assigned to us had a faded rug, a desk light that didn't work and a window that faced a field with bright lights on all night. We asked for a switch.
7. The second room assigned to us also had problems with inoperative lights. We again asked for a switch. 
8. We stayed in the third room assigned to us. We did this even though we then had to wait close to two hours for the overly loud air conditioner to cool off the room since the air was not on in this room prior to our arrival. At this point it appeared that faded rugs were a problem throughout the entire hotel. After eating wraped candy from the candy dish in this (third) rooom we noticed the next day that the dish also contained unwrapped candy that someone apparently had half eatten and then spit back into the bottom of the dish. It was never explained how housekeeping didn't notice this when they made up the room prior to our arrival. Next time I will inspect the entire contents of a dish of candy before I take one. Thinking I did not have to do this was one of the many things that I erroneously took for granted at this hotel. Expecting to not find half eatten candy in the candy dish, expecting the air conditioner to already be turned on in the room before it was assigned to me since it was 90 degrees outside, expecting valet service (or a legal place to park in front of the hotel while I carried my own bags into the hotel), expecting to not have to go up and down the elevator three times before I was assigned an acceptable room and expecting a reasonable reply to my complaints are other expectations that I had which were not met.
9. The staff appeared to be either poorly trained or too lazy to do their job correctly. They made no offer to help us with our luggage when they saw us struggling with it and when we made a comment about the quality of the rooms and the faded rugs in the hotel they simply said "all the rooms (are) the same". 
I would never stay here again. I paid $70.00 a night and I feel I way overpaid. Both Georgetown University and the Mariott Hotel chain should be embarrassed lending their name to this hotel.
Again, a 1.5 star rating would be generous.

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: We recently held a family reunion in San Diego and based our activities out of the hotel. Our room was very clean and the staff professional and accommodating. The food and service in the restaurant was very good. A hugh "Thank You" to Matthew Baker, Director of Sales and Marketing for making our stay a memorable experience. We will stay there again.

title: “Nice hotel, great location”
text: We stayed in a Deluxe King room, booked via Hotels.com. The room was spacious, clean and well maintained. Hotel Nikko's location was great - less than 5 minutes walk to Market & Powell, where we could hop onto the cable car or F-line streetcar which took us to pretty much everywhere a tourist would go.

title: “Beware! You May Be Left Out In The Cold!”
text: The worst experience I've ever had with a hotel! On March 10, I reserved three single rooms at the Loews Philadelphia through Hotels.com - $1200 was charged to our VISA card right away. The morning of our arrival date, I called the hotel to confirm the reservations, and they were confirmed by the Loews employee. We arrived at the Loews at 3:00 and was told "we have no rooms for you." I said "but you've had out $1,200 for six weeks" the clerk said "WE don't have it - Hotels.com has it." We begged, pleaded, reasoned and argued for an hour, but the "manager" behind the desk just kept saying "I understand" "I understand." To make a long horrible story short - the entire city was booked - apparently a conference of 20,000 math teachers was in town, and there wasn't a room to be had. The hotel they bumped us to was one hour away. We had to get up at 5:45 every morning to drive into the city to attend our seminar. The other hotel was nice and clean, but it had no restaurant, was on a 6-lane highway, and was out in the middle of Po-dunk Pennsylvania. We ran into other people we saw at the Loews lobby - apparently they "didn't have rooms" for 40 people that made reservations, and we were all given a different excuse. Some of the displaced guests arrived at the hotel at 11:00 am and were told their rooms weren't ready, come back at 3:00. These folks came back in four hours and were denied rooms! I guess the word "reservation" doesn't mean anything to the folks at Loews Hotel." BEWARE of the LOEWS PHILADELPHIA - you might end up sleeping out on the street!

title: “yikes.....”
text:
Have to start off by saying I was looking forward to our stay at OPI after reading the reviews here, but alas...
Nice things first:
- staff was very nice
- beds were *very* comfortable (for me anyway)
Yep, that's it.
Not so nice things:
- bugs in room (some kind of mutant, flying ant thingy). not crawling around but found dead in bathroom. you'd think maids, etc. could make the effort and wipe them up.
- what's with the OVERPOWERING chemical cleaners? smelled like someone dumped chlorine in the bathroom and sprayed every inch of fabric with a gallon of ScotchGuard.
- we had an Ocean Front room that overlooked the boardwalk. yes, lots of homeless and not the type of thing that I can look "through" just to see the "view". pretty depressing. 
- maids yelling to each other at 8am. nice.
- slowest elevators ever.
so not horrible, but certainly not the 4-5 rating others gave it.
Would suggest Pismo beach to anyone visiting from out of state. 
Also don't plan on staying at OPI again.

title: “Friendly, welcoming and convenient airport hotel”
text: Stayed 1 night on route from UK to Hawaii. This is a return visit having used it last year. Reception extremely efficient, very friendly and welcoming. We were allocated a large room on the 17th floor with panoramic views across LAX Airport runways. Noise disturbance from the planes was minimal and did not disturb sleep. Room was very clean and well decorated. Bathroom was of a reasonable size. Dined in “The Café” on the ground floor which we had experienced last year. Service friendly and efficient. Meal of soup followed by roast chicken. Good value for money. Hotel offers facility to print boarding cards in the reception at no extra charge. Hotel also offers free shuttle bus between the airport terminals and hotel. Would definitely use this hotel again.

title: “Excellent Hotel / GREAT SERVICE!”
text: I spent several nights at this property, with co-workers. The accommodations, meeting rooms, food/beverage service are truly excellent. The staff is most helpful. They did everything to make our group comfortable. Prices are reasonable. GREAT PLACE FOR BUSINESS CONFERENCES!

title: “We liked it!”
text: Me and my friend have come to the States for the first time and picked this hotel after some research on the internet by chance. It was a lucky pick! The hotel is in walking distance to the Empire State Building, 5th Avenue, Herald Square, Madison Square Garden and if you like to walk you can be at Times Square or Rockefeller Center in about 15-20 Minutes. The hotel has a concierge service in the entrance if you need some advice on how and where to start. There is a popular bar on the rooftop but we did not go there during our stay. We were pleasently suprised by the breakfast which was included in the price. You won't be disappointed. Our room was quite big and they cleaned the room every day. La Quinta Inn has not the newest building but it is good enough. Maybe the only thing I did not like too much was the smell from the neighbour Korean Restaurant. Our hallway was smelling all the time like we were standing right inside the kitchen. But other than that we enjoyed our stay and we would definatley recommed this hotel.

title: “Great Location”
text: Stayed there for a week just recently. The hotel has an ideal location for visits to sights in manhattan & subway to further destinations. The staff is very friendly, the rooms are spacious, and the housekeeping cleans the rooms very well. Overall, very very pleasant stay with no negative point at all! Will definitely go back!

title: “No problems”
text: The hotel is central when visiting Hollywood and breakfast is good compared to standard hotel "continental breakfasts". Parking is a bonus. But that's it: nothing special about this hotel. No complaints but compliments either. I'd definately stay somewhere else next time because this is a place you don't really want to "spend time at": the pool is just a puddle of water without a leisure area.

title: “Almost perfect”
text:
My wife and I just returned home from a fantastic stay at the new MO/NYC during the New Years holiday. The room, bed, and views of Central Park from the 50th floor were heavenly, but didn't get an upgraded room, even though I was promised one at check-in. Aside from this hiccup, service was top-notch during the four nights of my visit (special kudos to the superb bellhop/doorman staff!). Loved the new flat screen HDTVs, even though they had several technical problems. At one point, my TV stopped responding to remote control commands, requiring a 4:30am visit and "reboot" from tech staff (it wouldn't turn off!). Was also unable to get the high speed internet to work during my entire stay, though wireless worked ok (reception was very weak, however). New Years Eve at Asiate and the MO/Lounge were excellent, albeit pricey, and the party ended early (1:30a). Room service food quality was very good, but not quite excellent (one burger was not cooked to order). The surrounding area is great, but the new Time Warner building and Columbus Circle are still a huge mess (tons of construction!). The situation should be much better by the spring of 2004, by which time the new TW shopping concourse will be open. 
Overall...MO/NYC, while stellar, remains a notch or two below NYC's "benchmark" luxury hotel, the Four Seasons. My wife and I would love to come back, though.

title: “I would stay again”
text: Can't really say anything bad about the hotel. It was clean and nice. I would suggest you park in the lot directly across the street and it will save you $16.00 a day. It is a good walk away from downtown, but busses going both ways stop right across the street from the hotel, so it is no big deal. I did wish the hotel had queen beds, a pool and had the bathroom sink area outside of the bathroom with the tub and toilet. That makes it so much easier when there is a family of four. There is a Domincks right across the street where you can get your CTA passes, a fresh salad or donuts, beer and wine, fresh friut, toileteries, batteries, etc. I would have no reservation staying again.

title: “Interior: Nice. Exterior: oldie”
text:
I stayed one night in this hotel located in a good location, near to freeway 5 and 8, so practically you´re in the heart on san diego and can make good driving times to every interesting point: downtown, airport, la jolla, sea world, balboa park, fashion valley, plaza las americas outlet, etc.
I went to a business meeting, and by bad luck I got a very high price for the room $189 per night, and this was because it was the Comic Con during those days, so the prices were very high for the few available rooms in all San Diego, I think the prices were three times higher during those days; try no to make business or pleaseure trips to San Diego during Comic Con weekends, you will have a hard time finding hotels and rental cars.
This hotel was the first one that I stay from the Howard Johnson franchise. And the averall impression was higher than expected. From the outside it seems old, but well conserved... but inside the room it seems new, except for the old tube TV.
The room was clean, the bathroom was nice, except than the towels needed to be more soft.
They offered a breakfast included from 6 to 9 am, but I didn´t took it, but the breakfast area seems no be comfortable.
They free offer WiFi internet, but at my room I catched a very low signal and wasn´t able to connect, my room was the 238, the farest room on the hotel, maybe that was the reason but they need to improve thei network.
Averall I recommend this hotel because the location is one of the best in San Diego and the rooms are very nice.
Also I want to congratulate the housekeeping staff from my room alley, she always had a smiling face.

title: “The best location”
text: Rooms are very comfortable and new, the staff is great and very helpful. Our room didn't have a Times Square view but it had an awesome Hudson River view nonetheless. But I guess nothing beats the fact that the location is incomparable in NYC. You are staying at Times Square, period. It's totally worth the price. We've stayed in other hotels that are also near, but Novotel is, like I said before, incomparable. There's a Duane Reade in the same building and a Starbucks right across the street. And also just around the corner there is Times Square.

title: “Great Price Right Now”
text: My stay was at the excellent rate of $149 a night (incredibly, during the summer and on Pride weekend). You can't beat the location and the history of this place. Service in all areas was polite, friendly and professional. The bed was comfy and room very quiet (shampoos, etc., top notch). There is no coffee maker or mini-bar in room (morning coffee service is free in lobby) -- and there is a small refrigerator (and a safe) in-room. Wi-fi was fast and reliable -- and free in lobby (or $15 a day in-room). The Pied Piper bar/restaurant is historic and worth a visit to see the Parrish painting. The food, however, is just ok -- and the wine by the glass is horribly overpriced. Brunch in the Garden Court was good for about $30. (The quantity of food offered was good, but quality and service just ok.) At this low nightly room rate I would stay here again -- and often. But not at the usual, higher, rates...

title: “Good but needs a refurb”
text:
I spent a week here 10 years ago and remembered it as a great hotel.
Now its more like a standard Marriott you find anywhere. As a Renaissance I would have expected it would have been refurbished by now as its all a bit tired
otherwise everything works, was clean, staff were well trained and polite. No issues really. Great location and the pool are definite plusses. For business and depending where you need to go the newer JW Marriott on West Adam is better.

title: “Could do better”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for 3 nights as part of a driving holiday around Southern California. Had stayed here many years ago at a convention - had some concerns having read earlier reviews. We booked into a Regency Club room in the Tower and the room was fine but not great. The food in the Club was poor and the service pretty much non-existant.
On the positive side the hotel is in a great location with great views over the marina, also its very quiet so guaranteed a good nights sleep.
We didn't eat in the restaurants as the menu was pretty bland and overpriced but plenty of good restaurants within a 10 minute drive

title: “Swanky Digs in a Prime Spot”
text: I stayed here recently with friends and had a great time! The room was modern but comfortable. The sexy silhouette panel in the shower was very cool. The bed was very comfortable and I loved the sheets. This is a great place to stay for a fun night out in Hollywood!

title: “Great boutique hotel”
text: What a lovely welcome to NY! The hotel decor is lovely, the staff are super helpful and friendly. Will definately stay here on my next visit. The only down side was that the rooms could do with brighter lighting for make up!

title: “Good Stay”
text: Good location for the west side of Manhattan. Quiet street. Staff was very welcoming. Rooms are new and bright, ample space for person and things. The hotel includes a good bar. Great hamburger. Overall a convenient and less expensive alternative to the usual New York tourist hotel.

title: “Best park and fly seatac!”
text: I stayed here in Nov. 2012 and left my vehicle for 9 days. The people here are amazing at customer service, being helpful and friendly. They went way out of their way to be helpful. Dina and Khit at the front desk are great. thanks to Daryl, the shuttle driver for being extremely helpful and James is a good shuttle driver as well. I have stayed at three park and fly hotels in Seattle and this was by far the best. I thought the price was very reasonable as well.

title: “Nice hotel, good location”
text: We recently stayed at the Affinia Shelburne for a long weekend trip to the city. The location in "midtown east" was within easy walking distance to the U.N. headquarters, Grand Central, and even Times Square (about 15 minutes away). We booked a flight/hotel through Orbitz and received a decent room on the 11th floor. Only one bed, but it was large enough and the rest of the amenities were acceptable (mini fridge, modern bathroom, flat screen tv). Check-in and check out was quick and easy with helpful staff. We dined one night at the Rare restaurant on premises and found the food quite tasty albeit a bit pricey. Overall, we had an enjoyable stay and would recommend this property to future travelers.

title: “Average for price”
text: After staying at motels I was excited to be staying in an expensive hotel but felt the cheaper motels were much better. The staff were not very friendly, the room was so small we had to pack the suit cases away so we could actually move in the room and there was no mini fridge to store anything. There was also no free wifi in the rooms, we had to go down stairs and use the hotel's computers (for a maximum of 45 minutes) or take our laptop down and sit on the floor to access the free wifi for a maximum of 30 minutes. However, the hotel's location was excellent. Close walking distance to the centre of Times Square and also close to many different subway stations. My favourite part about the hotel was the bed - literally the most comfortable bed and pillow I have ever slept on!

title: “Overrated”
text:
This is without a doubt a beautiful property. The door service was excellent, concierge service okay. It is, of course, a pricey place to stay. What was really galling was the "nickel and diming" that went on as full paying guests. Wi Fi was $14/day. They charged to use the fitness facility. There are no coffee makers in the room, but there is a Starbuck's in the hotel; however it had had no sitting room We purchased coffee and oatmeal, and tried to then sit in the restaurant with it, but were told there is a $25 charge to sit there were we not ordering from their menu. The ice machine on our floor did not function the 5 days we were there, so we either had to go to another floor or order from room service (which of course meant tipping). The bar is obscenely overpriced, with the "well" champagne being $25 per glass.
I cannot see us returning to this hotel with that kind of attitude towards it's customers. There are way too many other choices in the city.

title: “Get what you pay for”
text: My fiance and I stayed in the Hotel Pennsylvania on our 4th trip to NY - we wanted something cheap and central - this is exactly what we got - we booked thru midashotels and got the room for $50 for the 2 of us - what a bargain! Yes the room was small and a bit minging but the bedsheets and towels were completely fine and the bed was HUGE!! we had a fab time. All the hotel is - is a base for warming up, washing, and sleeping in - if you want all the comforts of The Ritz then you know what you have to do..... This is certainly not for someone that wants the best, but for someone that wants a great location and something cheap, then this place is great - you completely get what you pay for. We would DEFINITELY go again.

title: “Best hotel, superb, clean, fantastic location, ticks all the boxes for me”
text:
We ( 2 best mates ) stayed here at the end of Jan into Feb and what a lovely hotel. We arrived to see the amazing lobby it is breathtaking and makes it feel that bit more special.
The check-in lady was really lovely and as we told her it was our 30th birthdays she upgraded us to a king suite for free ! They do ask for a $100 deposit for breakages but you get it back if no damage is done.
The room we were given was on the 14th floor and the view was of some offices but we weren't bothered as we weren't there for that ! The room that greeted us was very clean,
tastefully decorated and had two double beds ! One each ! The bed was soooo comfy and there was peace and quiet apart from the humming of traffic and honking of taxi horns- very NYC ! The bathroom had a decent shower/bath and they provide you with complimentary toiletries, fluffy white towels and a hair dryer ! 
There was cable tv and decent 37' plasma tv to watch it on. The only criticism is that there are no tea/coffee making facilities and you have to fill up a bucket of ice to keep your drinks cold - we used to buy a big carton of orange juice and stick it in the ice and that did us ! There are vending machines for fizzy drinks but I wouldn't waste the money.
You can get room service but it is expensive. The Madison Bar in the hotel serves a variety of alcohol, cocktails coffee etc. Be warned it is expensive but if you are splashing out - well worth it ! Cocktails are around $15 each! 
We would highly recommend this hotel - tip a yellow cab to JFK airport is $45 + tip and tolls - for the same money we got a limo ($55) to the airport from the hotel and it is the ultimate way to spend the last few hours in this glorious city - the position is excellent for times square, empire state, rockerfeller centre, broadway, central park and generally everywhere - I will be staying here again when I visit what I call a home from home

title: “Over-delivered - refreshing”
text:
We chose this hotel based on trip advisor reviews. Weren't sure about the location, but actually PERFECT if you have a car.
Staff friendly and helpful. Breakfast varied, interesting and relaxed - plenty of seating inside and out. Rooms large, great facilities and comfortable - a little dated, but the provision of kitchen facilities (including large fridge and table and chairs) was such a useful twist. Just over the parking lot there are several restaurants, plus subway and starbucks. Supermarket was a little more difficult to find. Lovely pool central to everything - not over-regulated and open long hours. If you can get a room over-looking it you can watch older kids from the comfort of your balcony. Vending machines, fitness facilities, a variety of outdoor terraces, laundry facilities, free wifi plus free use of pcs in lobby - for the money the amenities are just outstanding - everything has been thought about.
It's a quiet area, but close to main links to the city, seaworld and the freeways by car. Lovely walks along the waterfront, with a lovely, safe, family-friendly vibe. Also lovely outlook from hotel.
We had some niggles (a blocked toilet, and extortionate telephone charges) but all in all it is difficult to fault this hotel. I would whole-heartedly recommend this hotel as the place to stay to explore San Diego and the area, especially for families. I would return, but sadly this is unlikely!
Oh, nearly forgot to mention the late afternoon 'specials' - one dinner menu option provided unlimited and free of charge with accompanying beer and wine. The option was 'mainstream' enough to appeal to all family members, but there were sufficient accompaniments (bread, pasta, cheese, salad) to ensure that the kids had something in their stomachs. This is not over-policed, and staff seem happy for you to take the meals back to your room. I cannot stress enough how valuable this was when returning from a day out tired and hungry with kids. The fact that you save a stack of money actually was secondary to the absolute convenience and stress-avoidance. I have never come across this before, but whoever thought up the idea deserves a medal.

title: “Great Value For Money Super Location”
text:
Super room size with excellent views, great food, considering size of hotel very helful/effecient concierge, very good gym and great location. Compared to other hotels in the US300-600 range blows doors. (Go down and see what the Marriott and Hilton or even Le Meridian Parker down the street offer for this price)
Yeah if I was going to splurge at 800-1,000 a room (when I am with my wife etc) many better options. But for in and out business travel this is by far my favourite. Only complain the business center stinks two pay as you go computers.

title: “The 'Jury' is still out!”
text:
Disappointing say. The hotel is very new and is in places not yet finished ( walls not painted, missing panels etc.) The fixtures in our room were showing signs of coming apart (Draps hanging of the rail which was losse to the wall)
The bar is very popular with the locals, especially at the end of the "office" day. Consequently when you descend as a hotel guest, you will be lucky to find somewhere to sit, and even more lucky to get decent service.
Got a wake up call at 7:00am which we did not request, and when explaining our concerns to the front desk, they were totally not interested, they did not even respond to our comments!!
We valet parked our car, and whilst waiting at the door for our car to be returned, the young man waiting to escort us to the car, began explaining how he was tempted to take some of the better cars for "a spin around the block", "infact I may just do that one day" he continued...not with my car, we will not be back!
Punjabi

title: “Convenient location and attentive service”
text: I stayed at this hotel for one night on a short business trip. The location couldn't have been more convenient: about 15 minutes from Regan National, 1.5 blocks from the Metro, on the very charming Embassy row, steps away from Dupont Circle. From the check-in, every single staff member was courteous and helpful. I stayed in a superior room on the 5th floor. Although there was no view, it was quiet, clean and comfortable. The bathroom was modern. I would recommend this place.

title: “Gutes Hotel an toller Lage”
text: We spent 2 nights in a "New Yorker" room with two double beds. Our room was very clean an spacious with a lot of storage place. Bathroom was a bit small but ok. We were located at the 24th floor with beautiful view of the Hudson River. All staff were very friendly and helpful. The complimentary wifi was also a plus.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: Spent another night at the Boston Harbor Hotel, and it was just as great as last time! The hotel accommodations are wonderful and the staff is amazing! it is the only hotel I would consider when traveling to Boston. Kudos to the General Manager on doing such a great job! I'll be back.

title: “My experience was a positive experience!”
text: I would highly recommend it! Would certainly stay again, and the LIGHTING was superb! Every strength on the dimmer made me look 20 years younger! Cancel the facelift!

title: “Horribleeeeeeeeee”
text: this is a terrible hotel with very very unfriendly staff and unhygenic... there is a wierd kind of smell..that comes.. and unfortunately cannot be removed.. i finished the whole bottle of air apray and did notthing.. it catches your head as well.. horrible and horrible...

title: “Hilarious situation”
text:
I stayed at the Shoreham on business, at check in they charged my whole stay on to my credit card as a guarantee. 
I asked to cancel as i was going to pay cash and they were reluctant so i paid my stay up front.
I got to my room put the key in the slot green light but door wouldn't open.
Tried again here flushing sounds and the cleaning person screams just a minute then started screaming that i had no towels and that the toilet was clogged...
I entered the soon and the smell was unbelievable she had been using the toilet and in a nasty way!
I was horrified and she started with an excuse saying it was nothing but I got my bags back in the elevator and left.
Back in reception they were very nice and apologetic. A nicer room was given and apologies presented.
I won't be back there but i do realize this is something uncommon...
Location is great, staff are ok (nyc)...

title: “Very Nice Hotel - Not Best Location”
text: This is a beautiful hotel; especially the Fairmont Gold rooms, but the location is a little out of the way and usually ahve to sue taxis when I stay here. Would defientley recommend it if you cna get a good deal on a room.

title: “Location -YES! YES! YES! - Then come the NO's!!!!!!!!!”
text:
At first ,when you arrive, all seems lovely - Then you go inside!
Reception is manned by two staff therefore check in can be slow, there are loose cables/wires hanging from the ceiling in reception and by the elevators on our floor.
The room can be tiny...actually most are so I was told. A petite or classic room may be a squeeze with the beds being a regular double at best.
Noise from outside the rooms and from the a/c can be rather annoying (we stayed on 8th floor and still heard cars and street noise through the single glazing)!
Breakfast is very good but you have to get there early (before 8.30am) otherwise you have to queue for up to 20-30 mins.
Housekeeping can be a hit/miss situation. We had one day with no room servicing. When we asked for help we were told that due to union rules we may not get any help because it was past normal work hours. We ended up having a department manager clean/service the room!!!
Ok..Ok I know that this seems like I am just syaing all the negatives but I also have to add a positive.
The positive is the fabulous location. Exit the hotel to the right, walk 5 steps and you are at 32nd street subway. This gets you most places without changing. 
Walk 10 steps and you are on Broadway within sight of Macy's.
The hotel is also placed immediately on Korean Way with cool restaurants and karaoke too (if that's your thing!)
Times Square is approx a 10-15 minutes casual walk.
Beware though that there is only one currency exchange nearby and they had trouble with their systems whereby not being able to change money. Banks nearby don't change currency unless you have an account with them and the hotel will not change currency full stop!
To sum up - If you don't care about the room or wether you get enough sleep, but want a FAB location hotel, then this is for you.
If you need to get anything done ask for a manager because the front line staff will answer you with a shirty response and you may even get the reply I had from one staff member when asking about my housekeeping issue- "I'll ask but I can't promise anything will get done, sometimes they cannot be bothered!"

title: “Don't say I didn't warn you....”
text: The staff do try and make up for poor facilities, inadequate staffing levels, tired rooms, long waiting at the reception, inadequate training, exclusion from facilities for private functions, over-pricing etc.

title: “Fantastic Hotel minutes away from LAX”
text:
I'm a big fan of this hotel, esp. when I need to be near LAX to catch an early flight. 
Pros:
-Shuttle to LAX every 15 minutes (5-7 minutes to terminal)
-Generally very friendly staff
-Great success with SPG plat upgrades (club rooms are very large... love the airport view... not as loud as you'd think!)
-Nice SPG lounge with hot breakfast & evening snacks...drinks available all day...great view of the runway... love to watch the planes coming in and taking off!
-Nice gym with pool / hot tub right outside
Cons:
-Personally (purely a preference thing) but I find Sheraton pillows to be way too soft
That's really the only "con" I can think of; like I said, this a great hotel located right near LAX. Highly recommended!

title: “great stay great location”
text: me and my wife haved stayed at this hotel twice once in nov 1998 and jan 2006 we had no probelms both visits, the rooms are clean and spacious compared to some hotels in new york breakfast was good next door in brendans but recommend a steak at night when the restuarant opens,there is a nice bar across the road called o'reillys good atmosphere and great food .alex on reception has the mother of all knowledge on manhattan so ask him anything,we went to see the new york rangers at madison square not far from this hotel 20 min walk all i can say about new york is it has a energy and vibe like no where else cant wait to return

title: “Great Location”
text: We arrived as a group of 7 and they were able to have us on the same floor which was perfect. The location is walking distance from Times Square and various other hot spots. Rooms and bathrooms were always spotless. Concierge Desk always helpful. Would stay here again.

title: “Nice Hampton Inn for Business Stay”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel while in Ft. Worth for business. The hotel is fairly new and in excellent condition. The staff was wonderful and the location is perfect with shopping and restaurants near by.

title: “Must stay while in Chicago”
text: Great location to downtown art and entertainment. The staff was exceptional. Rooms were comfy. The next morning we did NOT feel as if we had just slept at a hotel.

title: “A great base in NY”
text:
I've stayed here a couple of times recently, and I really like coming back to it. Rooms are 1-bedroom or studio apts, with (barely equipped) kitchens so in the mornings I could eat some cereal and make some coffee... from the Balducci's right downstairs, of course. You almost feel like you have your own (rather elegant) apartment in New York. The building is in fact a mix of hotel and condo, I think. A lot of performers coming to Lincoln Center stay there, I hear.
Why I'm giving it 4 stars, not 5: first, the neighborhood -- I was glad to be out of midtown or Times Square, but I wish there were some interesting shops or restaurants right nearby... maybe there is and I haven't found it yet. (Though it's steps from the 1-line subway so easy to get anywhere fast.) #2, as a hotel it's hardly full-service. People are plenty nice but it just doesn't have the services of a 5-star place.

title: “Average hotel......for not so average prices!”
text:
Very disappointed with this hotel. Stayed their on our honeymoon, no special treatmeant from the hotel, room was very small and average.
The hotel itself is lovely but perhaps in need of a make over! One positive is the location. 
All in all I wouldn't recommend this hotel and won't be back. Much better value to be found in NY.

title: “Clean Lines, Light-Filled, Comfortable”
text: We are locals but decided to stay @ the Pan Pacific prior to the Rock & Roll Marathon/Half Marathon, to make the early morning preps easier. We were glad we did! The location may seem further from downtown Seattle than most 4-5 star hotels, but it's deceptively close and quite easy to get anywhere. The hotel team was friendly and helpful. The hotel itself was comfortable - extremely comfortable bed (key before/after running 13 or 26 miles!), well-equipped bathroom (with walk in shower and separate bath), sitting area by the window, plenty of storage. Although we did not have in-house meals, SeaStar, a well-regarded Seattle seafood restaurant, is on-site, as is a Starbucks (good for inexpensive breakfast). Further, WholeFoods is underneath the hotel - you can get any meal of the day there, snacks, a bottle of wine, etc.! 2-3 blocks north of the hotel is the up and coming SLU (South Lake Union) district, which has more and more great restaurants popping up every day. Downtown Seattle, Belltown, Space Needle/Seattle Center, Pike Place Market, are a ~15 minute walk (or 2 minute Tram ride). Space Needle is an easy 10 minute walk from the hotel. We will definitely stay here again when we need a "pied-a-terre" in our fair city!

title: “Tiny, loud, uncomfortable”
text:
We chose this hotel as a jump-off for our cruise, as they provide parking at no additional charge. However, it was a miserable experience, full of large, screaming families, reeking of chlorine from the heavily shocked pool, and insanely small room. The common areas were dirty and run down, the room was relatively clean, but smelled terrible. The window gave a view into the parking lot and the room of the people in the hotel nest door. The bed was so hard I couldn't sleep -- thank God I brought my own pillow, because those were in short supply as well.
The air conditioner works and the plumbing works. But I have a bit higher standards and I would rather forgo the so-called convenience for a decent night's sleep. Lousy start to a vacation, but it made our ship stateroom look HUGE!

title: “Great Boheme”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights from May 22nd and it was fab from the start. We booked a double room and while it was small it was comfortable and spotless. We had a room at the back so we had less noise but more sleep and because it backed almost directly to the next building it did lack natural light and a view however it did not bother us because we didnt plan to spend all day looking out of our hotel window!! Staff were extremley friendly and helpful and the famous nightly sherry was great!! One downside is if youve got a few heavy suitcases the stairs up to the rooms could be a problem.
Location for the hotel was the best. Smack bang in the middle of north beach with plenty of bars and restaurants close by and even though it was hilly both union square and fishermans wharf can be reached easily on foot. (Fishermans Wharf is a 10-15 minute walk). Around the hotel are numerous bars and restaurants and small cafes. Ones worth a visit; Tosca and Vesuvio both bars (5 minute walk towards union square) Marios bohemian cigar store is great for snacks and a drink opposite washington square (5 minutes towards fishermans wharf) and for a meal Trattoria Contadina, an italian, and Manga Rosa a steakhouse literally just around the corner are both great.
One final tip is if your up to it hire a bike and ride across the Golden Gate bridge over to Sausolito. About a 10 mile ride on paths. We did a guided tour with Blazing Saddles and it was an experience we will never forget!! Dont worry about cycling back because you take the ferry!

title: “Dare I say, perfect !”
text:
I expected a great hotel but was further impressed by the look, feel and service. The look is nothing short of breathtaking, the tall glass exterior is stunningly beautiful. The feel is professional, yet manages to incorporate that human factor. They literally make you feel appreciated! From the concierge, Anderson, who welcomes you thoroughly and lets you know just how much he enjoys his job and loves the city to the door men, especially Christopher who knows the city and can give you pointers like he were describing the back of his hand. 
Again, the service. GREAT!! I can't think of the last time I had the pleasure of being happy to be around such magnificent personalities. My girlfriend and i truly didn't want to leave. Hence, the extention.
I'd mention the breathtaking lounge Vertigo a top the roof of the hotel or the deliciously snuck in yet sophisticated restaraunt A a but they are so great respectively that they all deserve seperate reviews.
Whoever wants their hotel staffers to get better training to be 5 star should send their employees here so they can understand what makes a place such as Dana, dare I say greatest thus so far hotel!

title: “OK for the price”
text: The location is very convenient. Surrounded by shops & restaurants in walking distance. Handy to freeways. Rooms (we had the king suite for $59) were clean, modern and tidy. No complaints. Neighbouring hotel is a Super 8 and a bit suspect with long term guests. But we had no problems with security.

title: “National Senior Tennis Tournament”
text:
My four night stay at this historic/majestic property was WONDERFUL...!
My room was large and beautifully appointed.
