The Staff was Friendly, well trained, and attentive to details.
The location in downtown Seattle located on Madison Street was perfect as far as getting on and off the expressways.
Free parking was a major plus.
The 10:30 PM Happy Hour (half price on food and drinks) resulted in my timing my evenings around this feature. 'tis a GREAT HOTEL...!

title: “Great Location although can be noisy”
text:
We stayed at the Affinia as part of our honeymoon in June.
The hotel room was small but we expected that in New York.
We spent little time in the hotel as were out exploring NY and if you're spending your time in your hotel you're not 'doing' NY!
Our one complaint about the hotel would be the noise from the traffic and the nearby Fire Station which seemed to be unending all hours of the day and night. We were on the fifth floor so I would recommend go as high up in the hotel as you can but even this didn't really deter from the fact that the location of the hotel is great. We could walk to Times Square in a few minutes (providing we didn't get lost - which we did quite a few times!).
We used Niles Bar a couple of times for an evening drink after a long day pounding the streets but didn't eat there as the menu was a bit more expensive than the restaurant/bars over the road.
The concierge in the hotel lobby was very helpful with maps and directions when needed.
I would use this hotel again for a stay in NY but would definitely need to be on one of the highest floors.

title: “Nice hotel features...bad customer service experience”
text: At first glance this hotel was very nice looking although it is around a very industrial part of the very south point of the city. Upon check in the desk staff told me that for some reason my reservation did not go through on my credit card and that they would have to charge me the normal room price which is $30 more a night compared to the early booking price. After telling them that this was impossible they said they would take it down but still not as low as the price for early booking. When stating I would not stay for that price, they finally said they would take care of it for me and reduce it to what it was supposed to be, but that next time "I should call to make sure everything is okay". Like I'm supposed to know THEY had an issue with my credit card? After checking in we got to see the room and it was very nice and roomy. The bed was very comfortable and the suite like room is a lot nicer than an average hotel. We did have some bugs/ants in the bathroom, and the blanket smelled not very clean. The breakfast in the morning is okay; Average consiting of egg substitute ,sausage, toast and other small items. I did not appriciate having to pay $10 a night to park and then having to park my car down the street in a parking garage becuase the back lot was full. I was woken up several times in the night to people screaming and yelling in the middle of the night in a surrounding room as well as the very loud fridge kicking on. As we walked in to our room one night from the parking garage down the street, there was a very large group loitering and horseplaying in the drop off zone/ main entrance of the hotel while the desk staff sat outside, smoked and watched them be disruptive. It was a nice hotel, and I am very dissapointed to have had such a horrible experience there with staff and other things lacking. I went to school in Indianpolis and come down often to visit friends, but unfortunatly we will NOT be staying here again. Althought it was a good value in comparrasion to other hotels in the down town area, the reasons are shown by the time you leave your stay here.

title: “An excellent hotel - as long as someone else is paying”
text:
Don't get me wrong - this is a beautiful hotel, the rooms are clean and well furnished, and the beds are very comfy. I stayed here when attending a conference, so I wasn't paying out of pocket for the room. This is a great place to hold a conference because of the ample meeting spaces. Lack of free breakfast and free wi-fi are major turn-offs for me. Why is it that it's the cheaper 2 and 3 star hotels that seem to be able to offer this free?
Pros: Hotel & rooms are clean, bed very comfortable. Staff was friendly and concierge were very helpful. 
Cons: All the extras. Internet cost $13 per night. No free breakfast. The bathroom did not have soap - only some fufu bath bars, etc. The stairs were for emergencies only, so if I needed to go from the 16th to 15th floor I'd have to line up for the elevator. No vending machines and just getting a bottle of soda was $3.00. 
Don't get me wrong - it's a nice clean comfortable hotel and the staff are very nice and helpful. Would I stay here again? Yes -- as long as someone else was paying.

title: “Excellent service and gorgeous suite!”
text: Wow!! It was my first stay at the Trump Chicago and I have to say I am hard pressed to think of any place I have ever stayed that compares to this. The service is very, very friendly, prompt and courteous. The suite was enormous and extremely cosy. It felt more like a luxury condo than a hotel suite. I felt enveloped in luxurious fabric and warmth from the fireplace. Beautiful views of the river and city as well. The restaurant is pretty nice, not the very best, but definitely worth a try. The Spa is excellent - I got the best facial of my life, the Kate Sommerville signature facial. Expensive but worth it! You certainly get your money's worth at the Trump. I don't visit Chicago often but I look forward to staying there again in the future.

title: “Hilton Delivers Again”
text:
This Hilton hotel is a great business hotel in the heart of San Diego. What I appreciate about this hotel is that you're not in the thick of the Gas Lamp Quarter, it has east free way access in any direction, the rooms are quiet with nice views and if you get a room facing west, you can see our Naval Aviators practicing take-off and landings for patrols.
The restaurant serves excellent food and the staff are very professional.

title: “Will never stay again”
text:
Before we booked the room we read all the great reviews so we went for it. We stayed on Wednesday evening 8/29. From check in to check out we had a list of problems. We stayed at Drury because we wanted a suite, pool and breakfast. We were headed home from vacation in Nashville back to Milwaukee. With 3 kids the 9 hour drive was too long. At check in the front desk person seemed friendly but not like he was really listening to what I had to say. The first problem was when we went up to our room the keys didn't work. I had to run back down and get that fixed. Next later in the evening i was washing up my 15 month old, grabbed a wash cloth and it was dirty. After she was in bed I sent down and told the front desk person my issue. He said he couldn't do anything about it but would let the housekeeping manager know so that manager could make sure the room was cleaned better next time. Really? how accomodating. I need to back track a little we did have the kick back dinner snacks. The food was cold and the eating area was dirty and gross (reminded me of gross old country buffet). The pool was fine.
On thursday morning after I took a shower i grabbed a towel and the towel was also dirty and stained. I once again went down to the front desk and the woman there was nice and told me she would tell the manager right away and the manager would call. NO CALL ever before we left. We did eat the breakfast the person cooking had a dirty uniform (not food dirt) dirt dirt and she was standing around with a dirty rag. Once again very gross. 
One of the other reasons we stayed was to search for a hotel that we could meet up with friends from Louisville (halfway point) to spend family weekends together. That will not be happening and we will be on a search for a another hotel.
Terrible terrible customer service. Very lazy staff.
Wish i would have read further into the many pages of reviews and not just the first few. What a waste of money. Will stick to Hilton properties from now on.
We are not rich we are middle class and I would rather spend the extra $$ .

title: “C'mon Hotwire no way thi place is three stars”
text:
I consider three stars to be a place like raddisson or doubletree. This place isn't even close. I would put it on a par with econolodge or motel 6. The air conditioning units in the rooms are the floor style that rattle and make noise, and the only way I could sleep was to shut it off entirely. 
The bathroom is outdated with several black scratches etched into the sink. The shower curtain wouldn't stay closed and water was everywhere. The carpeting is 70s style ala the Brady bunch and the hallways look like they haven't ever been updated.
Read all the comments under terrible. They are almost identical to mine. Some,one should, report Hotwire to whatever agency handles false advertising. To call this a three star resort is a disgrace. 
The staff here is courteous and helpful, but this property needs a few million in renovation to earn my three star rating. I've asked several random people in the elevator what star rating they'd give, people laughed at three star. Usual response one maybe two stars.

title: “Construction, construction”
text: My husband, my parents from Germany and I spent 2 nights here. We did not get any rest in this hotel. Our rooms were located right next to the construction zone. Nobody informed us; booked the rooms over the phone. Therefore price was not acceptable! Hotel staff was not the sharpest in terms of customer service .We enjoyed Boston anyways and made the best out of it, definitely learned a lesson to always ask from now on if there is any construction/ remodeling going on.

title: “Nice discovery in Washington, D.C.”
text: This extremely well located, exceptionally well serviced hotel is a nice discovery. Rooms are spacious, comfortable, neat and clean. Personnel is discrete, attentive and gentle. The price is better than any other hotel chain with a similar quality of service. I have stayed more than once here. Highly recommended.

title: “Great location”
text: We have stayed in many hotels in the Seattle airport area and finally found this gem. The location is great, the beds are the best ever! The shuttle is convenient and the staff are very welcoming and helpful. Thankful we finally found such a great place to stay before our flights.

title: “Great Location, Nice Hotel”
text:
Traveling for business, I get the choice of any Starwood property in a city, and I usually go for the W or the St. Regis depending on location and length of stay. This W is similar to all the others that I have stayed in, which have all been good experiences. It is in a wonderful location downtown, only a short walk to my workplace and many other businesses in the financial district. It is also close to Union Square, and shopping areas.
The hotel room was chic and luxurious. The "Whatever, Whenever" service was amazing, as always. Basically, the hotel staff will bring you whatever you want, whenever you want it, and the W San Francisco lives up to this standard.
Overall, I would highly recommend the W San Francisco, to anyone traveling to SF for business or pleasure.

title: “Solid hotel in the heart of Boston”
text:
I've stayed in about ten different W hotels around the country. Of them all, this seemed the least W-like. Decor seemed more like a Westin than the usual ultra-modern. 
That said the hotel was new and clean and very centrally located to a lot of the sights of Boston. The service was what you'd expect from a W. Breakfast at Market in the lobby was phenomenal.
Overall, the W Boston is an excellent choice for business and pleasure travelers

title: “Very pleasantly surprised. Was not expecting much, but was better than some Hampton Inns I've stayed in.”
text:
The title of the review indicates that I am usually to be found at Hilton HHonors hotels. However, United Airlines misconnected me at Denver and put me up for the night at a hotel prior to the following morning's re-booked flight.
Given the lateness of the hour and the earliness of the flight, I wanted a hotel on Tower Road; most of the others United was offering were near Stapleton (a looong shuttle ride). Unfortunately, the first Super 8 Shuttle that arrived (after a half an hour wait) was completely full. I and another half a dozen or so folks had to wait another 25 minutes for the shuttle driver to take that load and return. This was frustrating in that the hotel DID have a bigger shuttle bus and did know that United was sending them lots of folks.
Check-in was quick and the room was very large, with microwave and refrigerator. Bed was great. Everything immaculately clean. I confess I wasn't expecting much, figuring I was going to get something down-at-the-heels in exchange for being closer to the airport. Was thus extremely pleasantly surprised that this hotel and its rooms were nicer than some Hamptons I've stayed in.
I would have given this four stars except for the shuttle experience.

title: “the onyx is great”
text: We stayed at the Onyx for 2 nights. It was perfect ;our room was immaculate,very quiet, spotlessly clean,with a very comfortable bed.But the main plus point was the staff. Nothing was too much trouble for them, and their courtesy, cheerfulness, and efficiency was the best we have ever encountered.We had come from the UK and only had a two night trip, so every minute counted,and the Onyx ensured that it was well worth it.If you are visiting Boston, don't waste time looking at alternatives. This hotel has an excellent position,wonderful rooms, and above all a staff who convince you that you really matter.It wasn't just one or two of them; they were all superb.We are planning our return trip!

title: “Excellent place, but beware of the railway noise”
text:
This is the second time that I stayed at the Renaissance Denver Hotel. I really liked it the first time -- my only problem was the honking of the trains that pass by the hotel, which woke me up a couple of times during the night. This time I made sure to get a room that was far away from the railway, and I didn't have any noise problems at all.
The management of the hotel should seriously consider upgrading their windows of the rooms that are close to the train. This investment would make a lot of sense.

title: “Great Value and Close to DIA”
text: All necessary ammenities for business travel, wireless in the room worked great, refrig, microwave - everything was great. Free shuttle from DIA to the hotel and back. Big atrium area with restaurant, which was too pricey for breakfast ($5.00 for a sweet roll that was stale and 3 inches in diameter?) But there are plenty of food establishments nearby, so go to Applebee's for dinner and fast-food for lunch or breakfast. Workout room was visible from the atrium area, which was unusual. The best part was the shuttle right to your door.........I'll go back.

title: “Hotel good but the way the charge you is stupid and seriously inconvenient”
text: Place is nice and the location is great, right near CTA lines that go to O'Hare. But the method for me to pay? So stupid and incredibly inconvenient if you, like me are traveling and need access to your money. On check in a hold is put on my credit card of the fee + plus $100. Thats fine, but once I've checked out don't charge me for the room while the ENTIRE hold is still on my credit card. Makes my $380 stay cost me $850 for the week until the hold drops off my card. So stupid... take it out of the hold. Can only rate 1 for value and 2 overall because of this.

title: “Thanks umit, zach, esmerelda, Terese, lauren and Gustavo”
text: Excellent service. For an older hotel once a marriott property, guests can take advantage of large rooms, largw flat panel TVs and an excellent bar.

title: “Great location-loved it!”
text:
Just got back from a two night stay at the Drake hotel with a friend. Had a double room with two full bathrooms! Room was huge and beds were very comfortable. Room was quiet and clean. Staff could not have been more friendly, especially Ben the doorman! Had tea in the Palm Court which was wonderful. Don't expect to be eating a large lunch--it is definitely more of a light snack. Food and service was terrific--its a little stuffy, so if you are looking for a more up beat meal, this would not be the choice for you. It is lovely, though. Tea was fantastic. Also had the buffet breakfast in the Drake Room. It was a great value and food was fantastic. There were huge bowls of every kind of fruit and berry, along with any other kind of breakfast food one could want, including lox with all the fixings. 
The hotel is in a great location on the north end of the Mag Mile, across from Bloomingdales. Its an easy walk to Lincoln Park, too. 
Some of the reviews here said the hotel was "tired". Its an old hotel with a lot of history, so it does look older, but it's well appointed and the rooms are terrific. If you are looking for new and contemporary, this may not be the choice for you. Overall, The Drake is charming and did not disappoint. I would absolutely stay here again.

title: “Nice Hotel in Great location”
text: This is a very reasonably priced hotel for NYC standards, it's only one block from the National History Museum and Central Park, making it a great location. Also the subway is not far. The building is nice and has more charm than most hotels, esp. at this price. There is free WiFi but the reception wasn't always great. There is also free coffee at the reception although they tend to run out--so don't count on it. The nice wooden hallways sometimes carry sound a bit too much...

title: “Horrible Hotel from top to bottom”
text:
We visited the hotel in October liking the location and photos we saw in teNeues. Upon return I contacted the general manager via U.S. mail to express my concerns and then forwarded an e-mail to ascertain why there was no response giving indication that I would share my experience with future traveller if not responded to. Having not been contacted in over a month is a perfect indication on the poor service and care you can expect from a filthy and disgusting hotel. I am going to insert the letter here that was sent to the hotel.
October 22, 2007
Mr. George G. Dfouni, CEO
Amsterdam Hospitality Group Hotel
230 W. 54th St.
New York, New York 10019
Re: Moderne Hotel
Dear Mr. Dfouni
We just returned from an east coast trip and among other hotels, had an opportunity to stay two nights at your Moderne Hotel on October 15th and 16th. I am a Los Angeles architect and had seen the property published in “Cool Hotels, America”, by teNeues in 2004. The pictures were beautiful, giving us high hopes for a great experience.
In our guestroom was a rating card for various categories ranging from Excellent to Poor. I feel compelled to share our opinions with you as some categories may not apply and a more graphic description may be more accurate. Please note that I am extremely busy and do not make a habit of writing letters of this topic.
We were met in the modest lobby and taken to room 802 by the bellman. The path from the elevator through the dimly lit and dark corridor was depressing. The paint was peeling off the walls, light fixtures loosely attached and the ceiling contained tape to hold the brown butcher paper over apparently some sort of construction project. The public carpets areas were stained, and housekeeping materials and cleaning supplies were on full public display that should have been in a closet. (These were never moved during our stay). Our room was incredibly unsatisfying, in fact we felt like we were in a youth hostel. Here is the list of items worth noting:
• The blinds were broken
• The room incredibly dark and dimly lit
• No TV reception, fuzzy at best with a remote control that did not work
• The telephone had a constant yellow flashing “message” light, even though there was no message. It would not go away. Also the buttons were broken
• The bathroom was so small and the toilet paper dispensor placed, that you had to sit sideways on the toilet
• The bath towels were frayed
I could continue and say with confidence that there was no attention to guest comfort whatsoever, no attention to detail, and no question by staff regarding the quality of accommodations to guests. It was an incredibly awful and dreadfully depressing experience.
I would not write this letter except that I feel totally blown away and ripped off in that this experience cost me $612.00. I would appreciate some method of compensation on your end as your hotel certainly under exceeded even the most modest of expectations.
Thank you in advance for your consideration.
Sincerely,
If you ever even think of visiting this hotel it should be out of complete desparation knowing that this place is a total dump.

title: “Terrific Hotel”
text: We recently stayed here over the July 4th holiday and we found both the hotel and the location to be wonderful. We had trouble deciding between Fisherman's Wharf and Union Square but after seeing both we agree that we made the right choice. This hotel is so close to all the Wharf attractions as well as the Muni transportation. Our rooms did not have a view but were more than adequate and the AC was a dream, new and it worked well despite it not being that hot outside! The hotel has complimentary coffee and tea in the lobby in the mornings and wine tasting in the early evening. Definitely a classy touch. We were definitely glad we chose this hotel and feel it is excellent value for the money especially considering San Francisco is not a cheap city to visit.

title: “MINE AND MY FAMILIES FAVORITE PLACE TO STAY IN SAN DIEGO”
text: I have stayed at the Bahia Resort Hotel on several occassions, both on family trips and for romantic getaways and have been extremely pleased with every visit. Though the Bahia is not considered a 5-star hotel, the experiences I have had there have always been quite pleasing. On more than one occassion I have been given an upgrade by the front counter for no apparent reason. Just checking in and the offer was granted. The Bahia is also conveniently located to all major beaches and attractions in San Diego which makes family trips there very conveniant and enjoyable for all ages. I have and would definately recommend the Bahia to friends and family members looking to spend some time away in San Diego. This has been my go to get away place for many years and will continue to go there for many years to come.

title: “Comfortable and convenient”
text: Spent a night at this hotel for a work trip. Surprised to find a suite when I opened the door to room 106. Lots of space in the living room and very comfortable bedroom. Room decor looks like it has been recently redone and the lobby area is in the new courtyard style. All areas are quite clean and well kept. Breakfast was extensive and tasty. Easy access to downtown Dallas.

title: “Better than expected!”
text: The wallpaper peeled in a few places and the fresh fruit was limited to apples, but the hotel was clean and safe. The fridge worked, the in-room coffee maker worked, there was plenty of hot water, the AC was fine, the wireless was fine, the bagels and muffins were well stocked for breakfast and the coffee never ran out. I'd been nervous after reading some of the reviews, but I had absolutely no troubles. The check-in was smooth. The beds were comfy. I didn't watch TV and had no reason to interact with the staff outside of checking in and out, so I can't say anything there, but all the important things about a hotel--safe, clean, working fridge, endless coffee--were present and accounted for.

title: “Do not stay here-leave room for me to return”
text: Delightful hotel. Just nice enough with a wonderfully cheery and capable staff. Someone discovered a hotel business model in which you run the property well and staff it with nice people. Go figure. Anyway, I am conflicted about leaving a good review because the Casablanca will become too popular and there won't be room for me on future trips to New York.

title: “Beautiful Inn on the Mississippi”
text: The River Inn is a lovely boutique hotel in downtown Memphis. It had an old world feel to it similar to staying in hotels in Montreal, Quebec. The included breakfast at Paulette's was delicious, the rooftop terrace romantic, and the staff helpful. Our room was smaller than expected but the bathroom was very roomy and luxurious. The only negative was the walk across the bridge on the way to Beale street for dinner and entertainment takes you through a part of Memphis that we felt uneasy being on foot after dark. The trolley, however, was a fun way to see downtown Memphis during the day.

title: “Hilton Was So-So”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Hilton Charlotte City Center the weekend of November 12 for the Carolina Panthers game. We arrived on Saturday, November 12 and checked out on Monday, November 14. 
Here are some tips that we would have liked to have known prior to our visit. Downtown Charlotte is DEAD on the weekend. We were lucky enough to find a couple of restaurants open (Uno, Fuel Pizza) not far from the hotel. Also, if you self-park, be sure to leave a trail of breadcrumbs to find your way back to the car. You park on the "Red Levels" I believe for the hotel, then get in the parking garage elevator and go three or four floors down to get to the entrance to the hotel, then you have to walk down again to get to the check-in desk. Once you learn how to get to where you parked, it isn't that big of a deal, but learning for me was the hardest part. 
We stayed on the Executive level and were allowed to visit the "food room" whenever we wanted. This was a really nice perk for us since we had never had this before. The food room had a nice variety of cookies, fruit and beverages. Being on the Executive level also allowed us access to the continential breakfast. This was good as well, but I had the saltiest bagel of my life up there. 
Our room was supposed to be a non-smoking room, but someone had been buring some serious cigars in there before we got there. It reeked. Now, I have to say that I didn't complain, so I don't know what they would have done for us. In hindsight, I believe I would have said something if only to let them know that we weren't the ones that stunk up the place. 
The bed was very comfortable and the room was clean. The staff at the Hilton were nice and seemed very eager to help us when we needed it. 
If the Jets were to play the Panthers again, I might stay at this hotel again, but I would probably try the Hilton Garden Inn, the Omni or the Best Western, just so we would have something to compare the Hilton to.

title: “Old New York”
text: A wonderful stay in New Yorks history. Far better than a chain.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: I do not agree with some of the negative reviews on this hotel and I am very picky. My room was large and comfortable and clean. I had all of the things I require for a good stay: clean, clean, clean, comfortable bed, thermostat, refrigerator, Internet access (at $9.95 a day, I did NOT like that, I think it should be free), quiet, newspaper each morning, good location, and good service. I was paying meeting rates and it felt fine for the price. I believe I may have been upgraded as I had a spacious suite with a balcony. The concierge could not have been more helpful and polite as was the front desk staff. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Amazing!”
text: This hotel compares to the Waldorf Estoria in New York City, both in beauty and room accommodations! Worth the extra couple of dollars to stay! Located very conveniently in downtown San Antonio, it is extremely close the San Antonio Riverwalk area.

title: “Super convenient!”
text:
Just back from a weekend stay at the Westin Copley! Great service and fantastic location. We had a junior suite on the 24th Floor which is basically one big room with 2 oversized double beds and a pullout sofa. 
Wraparound windows on 2 walls with great views oi the Charles River. 
Took the Old Town Trolley, which we picked up right across the street and tickets can be bought from concierge desk. 1 block to the Copley T stop. 1 1/2 blocks to all the boutiques on Newbury Street, but you never have to go outside with the skywalks to Copley Place Shops as well as Prudential Center shops and restaurants. My son used the health club and said it was good. We didn't have time for the indoor pool, but my son said it was small. The Seattle Mariners were staying at the hotel as they were playing the Red Sox all weekend. We will be back - so much to see and do!

title: “Do not stay here!!”
text: I just stayed there for one night only. The shower had hairs, and I now have a fungal infection in between my toes in both feet. But that's not the worst of it. My car, which was parked in their parking lot, got broken into and my head unit and GPS were stolen. DO NOT STAY HERE! It's dirty and unsafe!!!!

title: “Loved it!”
text:
My wife and I returned yesterday from a 4-night stay at The Orchard and we were extremely happy about our choice to stay there. The room was attractive and clean - my wife went on and on about the bathtub shine! 
The place is new (which was important to us) but has the look of an older hotel, which makes it classier; wood moulding and nice wallcoverings, beautiful furniture, heavy quality door hardware and faucets, etc. etc. The mini-bar is well stocked with goodies, although it is a bit pricey....we dipped into it on our last night just for two sodas. As some other reviewers have written, try Lori's Diner just one block down the hill. It's a retro 50's diner with an immense menu. Two tips about the cable cars: If you are at the end of the cable car run, where the cars turn around, you will find a lot of people waiting in line to board, and the line does not seem to move. Just walk up the street a couple of short blocks to the first stop and get on there. 
This worked every time. Also, we bought two 3-day cable car passes for $15 each, and the car operator asked to see it only once. That was a waste of money. Beware the pan-handlers...they are everywhere, and quite aggressive! The hotel is near Union Square which is fantastic - great shopping and eating. Eat at the Cheesecake Factory on the top floor of Macy's - really great views and wonderful food with big portions. Overall, San Francisco is a must-see for everyone...it was our best trip ever, and The Orchard Hotel had a lot to do with that! 
Oh, and Cornell really is as good as the others wrote.

title: “Amazing View”
text:
The first thing to say is that the view from the 53rd floor is AMAZING!!! However, I don't understand how being up that high I had no cell service and very little wi-fi? The concierge is very knowledgeable and friendly. They recommended some "out-of-the way" places to eat and visit and they were wonderful. Being directly across from WTC my husband and I (who is a former firefighter) were honored to visit. The Millenium Hilton cares for its guests and we will return if ever given the chance!
The pictures we took just from our room alone were beautiful. The Millenium Hilton helped to make our NYC trip very memorable.

title: “Clean and modern but space was tight”
text: Very helpful staff, went out of their way to provide information and service. Small problem with plumbing was dealt with quickly and effectively. Rooms were clean, furnishings were new and upscale. Only difficulty was tight space but, really, we weren't there to hang out in the room! Good location, convenient, happy with choice.

title: “Great Value - Can't Find Anything to Complain About”
text: Spent one night there with my parents, taking them to NYC for the first time. They aren't used to NY hotel prices and set up, and I was really worried we'd get there and it would be tiny and dingy and, well, a typical NY budget hotel. And I think we got lucky in a lot of ways as far as room selection - non-smoking, two Queen beds, not close to an elevator or other noise-maker, free upgrade to a larger room on the 4th floor with a view of the Empire State Building. They said they try to give preference on the best rooms to people who book directly through them or their website. And we got there shortly after check-in. In any case, it exceeded all expectations in terms of service, cleanliness, and comfort. Great central location, amazing value.

title: “Super expensive and bad service”
text:
For such an expensive hotel, you would think their service is better. The concierge (Blaine?) is simply rude. He acted like we are inconveniencing him by asking him what restaurants to eat. Last I checked, that's why we have concierge.
They also told us the wrong time when we asked them what time their gift shop closes. They said 9pm but when we got there at 8:45pm, it's already closed. Apparently it closes at 8pm. Their staff should be better informed.
Rooms and hotel itself is great. You feel like you are in a palace but don't expect to be treated like a King or Queen.

title: “Distrikt is Perfikt”
text: Excellent value for your hard-earned money. Clean, contemporary, and bright. Friendly, efficient, personal service. Superb location between the dazzle of Times Square and the eclectic Hell's Kitchen. Easy, relatively affordable garaged parking right next door. Two minute walk to 8th Ave. entrance to Times Sq. subway station.

title: “Very Nice!”
text: This is not your typical Hampton Inn. It is leaps and bounds better. It is located in the best little pseudo main street strip. You can walk to a restaurant, movie and shopping. It is all right there. The employees were outstanding. The property itself is well maintained. It looks like relatively new carpeting, furniture and more. Just a stain on a curtain is all I noticed. I will be back. It was a pleasant surprise!

title: “Best feature of this hotel is thier people”
text:
We found this hotel to be very convenient and clean as well as comfortable in all ways. 
 We especisly appreciated their front desk people. 
They were knowlegable and helpfull.They directed us to the sights and how to get to them and to exellent places to eat in the neighborhood. As well directed us on the best ways to get around the city.
 We used their advice and took the subway into the heart of the city(The subway was only half a block away from the hotel.)
Glad I did not try to drive around in the city(many detours and difficult traffic. Were there on tuesday/wednesday. 
 Rather dissapointed in the Cheers bar(expected too much I guess)
 Used one of the tour trolleys to see the sights this worked out well.

title: “Really comfortable”
text:
My coworkers and I stayed at the Sofitel in Chicago for 3 nights while we were in town for business. I was able to negotiate an amazing rate with them since we were a larger group. This hotel is a great value for the comfort and luxury it provides.
Check in was smooth and uneventful. Our rooms were all clean, well taken care of, and the beds were crazy comfortable.
Part of our assignment while downtown was to do some research on retail during the holidays. The Sofitel was a perfect location for us. We were able to walk to Michigan Ave and hit all of the major shopping areas. High End, Department stores, boutiques, etc. Plus we had our choice of great restaurants. We didn't have to take a cab anywhere. A great place to see the sights of downtown Chicago!
When we returned to the hotel at night, we regrouped in the lobby bar and it was a great place to unwind with a cocktail.
Highly recommend. I'd definitely stay here again on my next trip to Chicago.

title: “Historic but that's where it stops”
text: Hard to beat the history or location of the Waldorf but that is where it stops. We had an upgraded room and it still didn't even have a bath tub. Tiny bathroom with a tiny shower. At $500 bucks a night I was very disappointed. Skip the history and spend less for more at other hotels in Manhattan.

title: “San Diego is great, but the Bahia Resort Hotel was not.”
text: The hotel rooms were extremely dirty. Additionally, we had to ensure we did not allow Austin out on the balcony or on the 2nd floor walkway alone. The railings were at least 10 inches apart and the railing closest to the ground was at least 10 inches above the ground. The old construction should be updated to meet current code and certainly the place could be remodeled to be more pleasant.

title: “Dirty and apathetic”
text: I stayed at this hotel due to not being able to get a room at the other NYC hotels I usually use. That turned out to really be too bad. I paid $270 plus all taxes. The lobby is small and dirty, ditto the elevators and my room was dusty, smelled of old smoke (opening the windows never got rid of the smell) and had a small couch in it that looked like it hadn't been vacuumed in weeks. There is no gym or arrangement with a nearby gym. The staff is particularly apathetic and did not pay attention to my payment by way of my office when I checked in, which caused me a lot of inconvenience. Did anyone care? Not really. I felt sorry for the British tourists staying there, but maybe they got a better rate. I will avoid Comfort Inns in NYC at all costs from now on. The only good point is that this one is very near Penn Station. If they redid the rooms, some of them are corner rooms and COULD be quite nice.

title: “I love this hotel!”
text: My boyfriend & I booked a suite for his 30th bday. We did the same for my bday back in Feb and really enjoyed it. His plan was to have friend scome up to the room and hang out then go out downtown. My plan was to throw him a suprise party in the room after dinner at Fogo De Chao (about 3 blocks East). The hotel staff was great and very helpful. They didn't give me any hassle about providing extra keys for guests who were not on the reservation or about decoration restrictions, etc. The party was a success and everyone had a great time. Later in the evening we walked to the bars on Meridian St which are only about 3 blocks south of the hotel. However, after a night of dancing those 3 blocks feel like 8 with sore feet in high heels, ha! I was very happy to see that big comfy bed once we returned to the room. The reservation included a hot buffety type breakfast but it wasn't all that great. Although I would recommend the cooked to order omlettes.

title: “Functional airport hotel-convenient with frequent shuttle”
text:
I took a room for a long layover- the airport shuttle runs continuously so doesnt have to be called and it only stops at one other hotel which is efficient.The room -nothing special- basic and a little dated but proper blockout curtains so you can rest in the day.The airport hotels are all clustered together in an area devoid of anything other than a few fast food restaurants.I had a breakfast included package- it was fine but again just what you would expect form an airport hotel. Free internet and boarding pass print facility are good offerings.
One of their points of difference is you can book for a 24 hour block of time- great for an early morning arrival from Australia- saves the hassle of trying to negotiate an early checkin.

title: “Nice hotel, great pool and the breakfast buffet was delicious:)”
text:
This hotel is 2 blocks from the Wharf. Request the "Balance Package" when making reservations with Hyatt. The package includes free Valet parking-$45.00 value and 2 free buffet breakfasts-$19.00 value each at Knuckles Restaurant located in the hotel. It was delicious! The pool was great and the hotel put our family on the 3rd floor, same floor as the pool. 
Castagnola's Restaurant (on the wharf) Do not waste your time and money!!
The food was terrible, overpriced and the service was horrible and they didnt care..

title: “We loved our first visit”
text: We made our first trip to Chicago for our 12th anniversary. After studying and agonizing over all the hotel choices online - I booked us at Hotel Sax through Expedia. We got good enough rates. The hotel was all we needed - good location, close to public transportation, nice friendly helpful staff, our room was CLEAN, the decor somewhat eclectic - but if you want the same old hotel - stay at one of the major chains. We thoroughly enjoyed our 4 day trip! Nice comfy robes, good quick room service - FANTASTIC shower, nice toiletries.

title: “One of the best in Chicago”
text: Everything about this property is excellent. The staff at the front (bellmen and front desk) are very attentive and helpful. Property is located very conviniently between Michigan Avenue and Lake Shore. The hotel sits far enough off both roads so it seems a little more quiet. The decor is nice as the property balances their history and elegance of their property but not making the guestrooms to over the top and traditional. I would recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “One of the best experiences ever!!!”
text:
Attention to Hilton Management:
The customer service is excellent at the San Diego Hilton Resort and SPA (1775 East Mission Bay Drive); including the staff members at the registration TC, Ramon and Josh Morrison! With their smiling faces and grade confidence of knowing their professional responsibilities, TC and Josh made our stay very welcoming, pleasant and enjoyable! If your organization has customer service rating scale of 1-10, I would give 10 to TC and Josh's services! 
Thank you again for your outstanding services!
Sam S. Yeremian

title: “Not what I expect.”
text: I stayed from october 20th to 23rd. The size of the bathroom of my room was not from a 4 star hotel. The tissue paper was placed on the back of the toilette deposit of water due that it was not sapace on the basin counter. To sit on the toillete you have to enter the bathroom, close the door and remember your wife not to open the door so you don´t get hurt on your legs. When I complained about the size they told me that the hotel was full. If the size of a 4 star hotel depends on your luck if you get a nice room or not, I would say that it is not well rated.

title: “I agree - great hotel!”
text: I was so surprised to arrive and find we had a two bedroom suite waiting, with kitchen, three TVs, three beds, kitchen table, etc. Our rate was like $128, and this included a large breakfast (great buffet), and even dinner - the night we stayed they were providing Pizza Hut. What a value! We were about 20 minutes from Del Mar where there was a fantastic beach for kids. This hotel is not far from several different freeways, so easy access to all of the sites around. The customer service was wonderful too - we had ordered more towels and they were brought up right away. Oh, they have a laundry facility downstairs, and you can buy detergent for $1.00 -very convenient when traveling with kids. One of the best values I have ever seen in a hotel.

title: “Perfect location! Lovely small hotel with great amenities.”
text: On the Ave Hotel is a perfect place to stay when visiting NYC. Amsterdam Ave has wonderful eateries and that's just minutes from the hotel. Zabars is just up the street on Broadway. Can't ask for much more!!

title: “Outstanding Hotel”
text: A friend and I decided to stay that the Conrad for the weekend of ISSMA State Marching Band Finals and we were not disappointed. From the moment we stepped into the beautiful marble lobby, we knew we had made an excellent choice. Check in was fast and easy, and the clerk was very friendly and interested in the reason for our stay and if we required any assistance. We stayed on the highest guest floor in a standard King guest room. The room was amazing, it would count as a studio suite at most properties. The bed was large with lush bedding, complete with a fairly sized sitting area with sofa and coffee table, and a very large desk. The flat screen HDTV was nestled in a very attractive armoir which was slim to the wall and very functional. The bathroom was decorate all in stone, glass enclosed shower with double showerhead, low powerflush toilet, and a very relaxing and large soaking tub. The bathroom also had a smaller flatscreen tv and a phone. Also, in the small hallway leading into the room there was a small table and butler pantry with the minibar. Breakfast from Room Service was great and very fast. We stayed for two nights and had a very relaxing weekend and thoroughly enjoyed this hotel. We will definitely be back again!

title: “Quaint with good location”
text:
We just returned from a night's stay at "The Hotel at Times Square". While, at first, you will notice obvious external renovations being performed, it does not hurt your stay in any way (mind you, this was a Saturday evening stay, so perhaps they weren't working at this time). This is the epitome of a quaint, European-stype boutique hotel. 
We came to New York to take in a show and the "holiday energy" of the city, so did not stay for long in the room. However, the location truly helped us enjoy every part of the city that we wanted to encounter -- from Broadway to Rockefeller Plaza and even a Paul McCartney sighting. While in the room, we found it cozy and comfortable. The TV was large, the free Wi-Fi was highly useful, the bed was clean and restful. For a young couple, the size of the room was fine -- not sure how families would do, but this was definitely meant for 2 people to use, and we found it more than sufficient. If you're looking for wide, open spaces, find a bigger, pricier place. If you're looking for a stylish place to lay your hat, try The Hotel at Times Square.
The only complaint I had concerned parking; had a difficult time finding the correct parking garage to take advantage of the discount, so ended up paying an arm, a leg, and another leg at a different place. Clarification on that would be helpful. Otherwise, a joy. Front desk was very helpful, albeit a little difficult to understand.

title: “Nice enough, but employees are lacking. I expected more for the price.”
text:
Had a 1 bedroom suite which was fine. However, maid service was crummy - didn't empty trash or even attempt to pick up coffee area. No creamer for coffee provided, so I had to go downstairs and pay $3.00 for a paper cup. Parking is $40 or $45 per day, can't remember exact amount. 
Most of the employees have difficulty with speaking English.
Beds were comfortable, room was good. Interesting hotel, but I expected more for the price.
Breakfast buffet was $25.00 per person.

title: “Hotel Edison - Wonderful hotel and location....”
text:
We stayed 5 nights on 8th Floor - Room recently refurbished which I had requested prior to arrival as celebrating wife's 50th Birthday.. Upon arrival she was wished happy Birthday immediately, very speedy transfer to room, great service on reception..
Room clean, tiday and functional while there Hot water tap for bath broke it was fixed completely and replaced within 20 mins of reporting, extra pillows requested and were delivered quickly and promptly..
Food in restaurant excellent eat there twice for breakfast.
Used hotel computer to check in and print boarding pass complimentary .
Hotel location is excellent
Tips for NYC
Deli next door very rude and unhelpful staff
Try Ellens Stardust Diner and Five Guys for food also Sbarro breakfast buffet
Used Bus company outside Starbucks and used 4 day pass- Yellow coats
Woodbury Common a must!!
Please give Edison a try - would definitely return!!!

title: “Great space”
text: The Hotel Whitcomb is a great space in an incredibly convenient location. I am an avid city traveler and was in the Bay Area for vacation and Berkeley tour for my 16yr old. The underground is located steps from the hotel and travel was efficient. The Hotel itself is warm and well kept. The room was comfortable and clean. My son and I walked many areas and never felt threatened. I had absolutely no reservations regarding the location…it is in the city and characters are all around. The Hotel staff was extremely helpful and courteous. Tim, the Reservations/Revenue Manager helped me sort out an issue that was really even unrelated to the hotel, it was a snag with my bank card and he was absolutely gracious. I would recommend the hotel to anyone planning a stay in the city, and will be staying there again.

title: “Positives out-weigh the negatives”
text: I've stayed at this hotel about 6-7 times, all of which were during high school state tournament championships. This is a great hotel that I would recommend to anyone. The location is absolutely perfect for downtown Indy goeers. It is close to everything. The rooms are great. Nice sizes, clean, and they have good views as well. The staff is friendly and gets you checked in and out quickly with no hitches. We've booked through the school every time and have never had any errors. The only negatives to this is the congestion. I think it's hard to get in and out of the enterance because it is small. Also, the other negative is the elevators are pretty slow. The lobby is always crowded, but that is because of the games that are going on at that time. All in all this is a great hotel.

title: “INCREDIBLE EXPERIENCE. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED”
text: What can I say about Night Hotel? It was my first time at New York and I´ve searched the web looking for prices of reasonable hotels in the Midtwon and I bumped into The Night. After reading all the comments that other users made at Tripadvisor (despite the negative ones) I decided to spend 6 nights at the hotel and it was the cleverest decision I could take. I have nothing to say but INCREDIBLE, SOPHISTICATED, ROMANTIC and GLAMOROUS. Let me share my comments about others negative comments: a) BREAKFAST: OK. It´s not a Wow breakfast but you have all the stuff you need for starting the morning. Coffe, hot milk, lots of bagels, some muffins, scrumbled eggs and bacon...the same thing (or even more) that you probably get if you go to breakfast at Starbucks. The good thing here that it´s for free!, b) SHOWER: Despite there´s a narrow glass the covers the bathtub it´s not true that the floor gets completely wet. What you only have to do is to throw a towel just beside the bathtub and ready! No water on the floor!, c) LIGHT: You don´t have to be very wise to realize that if you go to a boutique hotel called NIGHT the atmosphere will be related with the "blacks". I love spending my breakfast listening to chill out music in a darky and glamorous ambient as well as my room. Special details as daily chocolates and the printed weather forecast just over the bed were really appreciated, d) ROOMS: I was at a QUEEN room and I should say that it was perfect! It was not enormous but despite our "hundred shopping bags" we can move freely all over the room with no problems. If you go to NY for sightseeing I can swear you that you will leave the hotel at 10 Am and you don´t come back till 7 or 8 pm so what you will only need is a warm shower and an incredible bed and rooms at THE NIGHT get a 10!!!! e) LOCATION: Great! Excellent! You will only have to walk 50 meters to get at 45st and Broadway were everything happens! You want to buy tickets at TKTS? Ok! Just walk 2 blocks and you will find it. Perhaps some presents for your kids at Toys R us? Ok! Walk 2 1/2 blocks and you will be there! Starbucks? 20 mts from the main entrance. Planet Hollywood? Just at the corner!!!! Everything was near there!!!!!! Last, but not least, an special mention to Mr Thomas Carpenter (the General Manager of the hotel) who takes care personally of all our request and the "Morocco" guy who helped us with our luggage, some umbrellas when raininning and a warm and friendly "hello" everyday. ONLY one thing to mention. The Night is definitely a hotel for couples or business men/women. I would not recommed it for familys with very young kids as the ambient and the facilities are not prepared for "the smallest". Anyway I would not doubt to come back to THE NIGHT if I had the chance to visit NY again!!!! Congratulations and keep improving guys!!!!!!!!!

title: “No complaints at all.”
text: Nothing to complain about at all. The staff were friendly and professional, with the online deal we found the hotel was a good value and in a good location. Would stay again!

title: “Value and Location excellent”
text:
Now the third stay at this hotel. The Greenwich and West Village areas are by far the most appealing in NY if you want to cruise restaurants and get amongst locals and away from Times Square tourists. THe subway is close for visits north and south. The Wash Square Park on a sunny day is entertainment in itself just watching all the music and performance and the crazy people who parade there. And the dogs with their owners. It has a gym with basic equipment but subway stairs are a good workout you can't avoid. Breakfast is suppled and good. Remember that when you are in New York if you just want to 'hang out' in your room and call that an experience, you are missing the point. You sleep in it, you wash and get changed for the next day. These rooms suffice for this purpose - I have stayed in other hotels in NY that don't have a wardrobe or a safe or a decent bathroom. This one does.
At this price I can't see us staying anywhere else and we book in for 2 weeks at a time. It has character and history and location. End of story.

title: “Book It!!! Don't Hesitate!!!”
text:
The one and only concern I had about this hotel is that the bathroom is very small. Especially the toilet bowl. I am 6'0" 230lbs and I could not sit on toilet it actually ruined my trip. Compared to other high priced hotels in DC this was the best value.
Super clean 
Great location
Room was spacious. It was very huge but bathroom small, makes no sense.
Will recommend
Pets accepted
We are from Long Island, NY and hold everything to a high standard this met and exceded our expectations except for toilet or it would have been perfect.

title: “Very well taken care of here & a lovely hotel!”
text: What a staff! We stayed two nights after a long visit with great relatives & anticipated relaxing here - and relax we did with the help of: Eddie G., the bellman who was so helpful & what a smile!, Nick, one of the chefs at Las Ramblas - he went out of his way to make my husband guacamole & chips (which isn't even on the menu), Yesenia, who served us so cheerfully outside, and Jose, the bartender, another of the most pleasant staff. Also, a salute to Gus, the front desk manager who makes alll this happen & does it himself when needed. Thank you all from Larry & Marnee in Maine

title: “Clean, comfortable, basic”
text: We ended up here when stuck in DC for an extra night due to flight delays. While it is no Kimpton Palomar, which is where we had been staying, it was very clean, brand new seeming, and quite comfortable for our one night. We had a 2 doubles room, which was pretty small, mostly just beds, but the bathroom was comfortable, with new granite countertops, and they had a coffee/tea service in the lobby in the morning. The staff was extremely helpful. I prefer boutique hotels, so this wouldn't be my first choice, but for a quick stay or to be convenient to somewhere on capital hill, this place is more than adequate.

title: “Historic-good and bad”
text: Great lobby, beautiful ceiling great lounge and great service but with an old hotel it comes with negatives. Small bathrooms and our room did not have a dresser for clothes. It only had a closet so we had nowhere to unpack. Also the rooms are noisy with plumbing noises and you can hear your neighbors even if they are just talking. The other issue is that the hotel is huge and with a big hotel it can get frenetic. We were on executive floor and in the mornings you could barely get off the elevator due to the crowds. Maybe it was cause of labor day holiday. We would not stay again and prefer the Conrad better if you are looking for a Hilton property

title: “Great location”
text: Stayed for a week at the end of June. Location of hotel is excellent, just off the 'magnificent mile' of Michigan avenue, right near the John Hancock building. Facilities were excellent and house keeping staff were very good. For two people the room would be excellent, though probably the only let down was the lack of free wi-fi for a fairly expensive hotel. The small fitness centre was modern and a bonus. The hotel is very nice

title: “location, location, location - and quait!”
text: I wonder if society hill hotel has changed ownership since the other postings. My experience was just delightful. Close to everything in historic old city, and close any means of transportation to other neighborhoods. the room was just fine for a locally owned b&b, and kind of charming. the bar and resturant was a relaxed place to unwind after site seeing. great beer, great food, excellent and personable service. all and all, a great home base for a philadelphia adventure!

title: “WOW! What a deal”
text: The location could not be any better. It is within walking distance from many of NY's great sites. The price cannot be beat in this city. It is in a safe area. It is clean and the bed was comfortable. Although just a "2-star" hotel, this is a great find. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

title: “Convenient Location”
text: We originally planned on staying at the Hilton Chicago, but switched at the last minute when we were told they could not accommodate a request for two double beds. Having stayed at the Hilton previously, it is hard to not compare the Palmer House. The Palmer House lobby was grand, but the standard didn't carry over to the rooms. Our room was very small, with our two double beds crammed in and a below par bathroom. Our view was of neighboring brick. It was hard to distinguish night from day it was so dark due to our lack of view. The one saving grace of this hotel was the convenient location. Very close to Millennium Park and the rest of downtown. For the price I'd expect better.

title: “Ricki Warren”
text: Been staying at the Radisson LAX for two weeks now, and I have to say that all of the staff has been amazing, accommodating, and gives the very best service you could expect to receive at a hotel. Ricki Warren has been especially gracious from the first night I arrived - a class act all the way. Very helpful and attentive and willing to lend a hand whenever needed. Yay Ricki!

title: “Great location”
text:
I stayed here for 6 nights and
found the room to be very comfortable and clean. The shower was excellent. The best thing about the Farmer's Daughter is the location; right across the street from the Farmer's Market and Grove.
We did not have a car, so after taking tours during the day, we could just walk across the street for the evenings.

title: “Good location but executive room was far from an executive - very tired decor.”
text:
We upgarded to an executive but should have saved the money! When we first entered the room we noticed one of the closet doors was missing and the ceiling near the window looked like it would collaspe at any moment - very tacky.
Mentioned these to the front desk, they said it would be fixed - it never happened. 
Most of the front desk staff was surly and not very helpful, with the exception of Patrice who was delightful. We called the front desk at 10:15 to ask what time breakfast finished, we were told 10am but later found out it was 12 - so much for the breakfast coupons we were given.
Self service laundry facilities were out of order for 3 days.... 
Having said all of this, it is a great location and the beds were very comfortable!!!
Will look at other options before I return

title: “Super Location! Book Early for Huge Savings.”
text: Booked a week in advance and saved almost 40% off the regular room rate, which made the difference between staying one night or two. We arrived hours before the official 3pm check in, and we had no problem getting into our room. The bed was perfection, there was almost no street noise heard on the 34th floor, and the room was large by New York hotel standards. Every Hilton staff member was helpful and very pleasant. Taxis are at the ready and lined up around the block, but this Hilton is only one block from Fifth Avenue and about seven blocks from the Times Square area. Very convenient. We chose to eat outside the hotel since the prices were high -- but that is to be expected in New York. Checkout was a breeze. If I can get the same lower rate with an advance purchase in the future, I will definitely stay at this property again. You cannot beat this location.

title: “Award for Best Housekeeping”
text: A wonderful stay. My girlfriend and I stayed at The Time just after Hurricane Irene. Besides being in a convenient location, the staff at the hotel were amazing. Melissa, at the main level bar, not only served me my coffee and drinks but also offered me some tips on what to see and do in the city including providing me with directions to various spots (Server/Concierge - all in one!) Thanx Melissa! The porter in the elevator offered me to tips on where we can dine, etc. I had a lovely chat with the bartender on the second level lounge my first night there and apaprently Bond St. is a great sushi spot! And I don't think I have ever seen a more efficeint housekeeping service than the one at The Time in a long time. My room was cleaned and serviced in a very timely manner. So thank you Time for making our stay a wonderful one!

title: “We enthusiastically recommend this clean, quiet, friendly, reasonably priced, and perfectly located hotel.”
text: We booked 4 nights on the advice of Trip Advisor, and we give this hotel our unqualified recommendation. It is all that is advertised: a perfect location for sightseeing all areas of town, and the room was good-sized, modernized, clean, and quiet. From top to bottom, the staff made us feel at home. We will definitely return on our next trip to San Francisco.

title: “couldn't keep housekeeping away”
text:
Great location and Great view of the Inner Harbor!
all around excellent restaurant (Ra Sushi, Phillips Seafood, Mo's -only okay, Vaccarro's = excellent cafe, Chiu's Sushi)
sight seeing is great (Aquarium, USS Constellation, Civil War Museum)
Fell's Point neighborhood is waking distance (Must see) 
Semi Negative: Housekeeping woke us up before 10am on Sunday?! Ignoring the "do not disturb" sign, what was smaller sign then I've seen at any hotel, but still. Told the front desk to not to have housekeeping come in unless requested! They came in next 2 days as well. inconvenient when you trying to sleep in or use the restroom middle of the day. but honestly, everything is neat and clean so cannot complain. Late nite request are well met. Internet cost $12/day. Starbucks around lobby that opens at 6 and the oatmeal was right on spot. 
Must mention Annie, the concierge, who was so kind and helpful and just the best service I have had by far compared to any other hotel. Thank you so much, she made our stay just even more joyful and a fun experience.

title: “I Expected More from a Residence Inn”
text: This place just isn't that great. I've stayed in quite a few Residence Inns and this one is my least favorite. While the location is amazing, the hotel just isn't. The rooms are a nice size, however, they're starting to show some wear and tear. There were some mystery stains on the sofa in my room, so I was hesitant to sit on it. Also, there were some stray hairs on the bathroom floor when I checked in. I guess housekeeping doesn't vacuum after each guest - wear shoes in the room. I didn't utilize the kitchen because, honestly, I questioned the cleanliness of the supplies. Needless to say, I won't be staying here again.

title: “Scary.”
text: We stayed at the hotel on 11/23/07 for my sister's birthday as we wanted a budget-minded hotel in a good location. There was a hole in the wall from the back of the chair. The beds were as hard as rocks. Bathroom had hair in it. Worst part, found 3 cockroaches in the room, one of which ran across my face when I was lying in the bed. Disgusting.

title: “Average but Interesting”
text:
As I write this, I'm still not sure how I feel about this hotel! It was a pleasant experience, but it seemed to be a very odd hotel- definitely not what I was expecting!
I booked my stay here as I waited until the last minute to make accommodations for a day and a half meeting I had in DC, the hotel that was recommended to me had filled up, and this popped up as another option. It was cheap, and seemed close to where I needed to be (it wasn't really) so I just booked it.
I had no problem getting there from my airport shuttle, and the staff was very helpful in making sure I had a room that met my needs. 
I was able to get a room that was fully accessible (although still not very spacious) There was a great place to park my electric scooter, right by an outlet so I could charge it. Usually a lack of outlets in hotels are a huge issue. The bathroom had a very high counter, but a roll in shower, with a shower bench right in the closet in the room so you did not have to call down for one. The thermostat was high, but that was my only gripe in terms of the room. The bed was very comfortable, and the free wifi was a flawless connection!
I didn't eat at the hotel, but I had a drink at the bar, and it was a great atmosphere with great service. You also get free chips when you order drinks.
The thing that was odd about this hotel, was, in addition to the fact that it is a bit worn and could use some updating the decor is a bright/retro/African theme. The lamps in the bar had silhouettes of jumping gazelles, and all the bedding and chairs in my room were bright purple and orange. With the hot weather, and the vibe of the hotel, I literally felt like I was in another country, it was very odd. I was expecting a much more contemporary urban feel, being in the heart of DC!
I didn't go anywhere aside from my meeting that was near the GWU campus, and that was a $14 cab ride each way, so I can't comment on the location much, but for the price, this was a pretty decent place to stay! I would stay here again, it beats other budget hotels in this price range- but I can't say this is a hotel I would elect for a true vacation, or conference setting!
Video of my full review of an accessible room: http://youtu.be/aUcCm22pGqg

title: “BEST EXPERIENCE EVER AT A MOTEL”
text: We scheduled a trip to NYC but due to super storm Sandy, we were forced to cance. We wanted to do something special for our 16th wedding anniversary. We decided upon the Royal Sonesta. We checked in, were treated like royalty, explained our canceled plans, and next thing you know we are getting some complementary chocolate cheese cake. Honestly, clean, friendly, well located, not a better place to stay. I will stay at the Sonesta whereever I go if I can. Thank you Royal Sonesta.

title: “a very pleasant and quiet hotel”
text: We stayed in the Kitano hotel for six nights. They upgraded us with no extra costs to a premier room in the corner of the building, which had extra windows. We had a good view on the Empire State Building and we even saw a part of the Chrysler Building from our room. The room was spacious, clean and very quiet, even though the hotel is in midtown Manhattan. Room service was great, every morning a newspaper was ready for us at our door. A nice and convenient service, when you do not travel with your own laptop, is the possibility to use the internet via the tv screen and this service did not cost very much (about 10 dollars for 24 hours). The only thing we did not like was the smell of cigarette smoke from other rooms on our floor, which tended to invade our room as well on some days. Smoking seems to be permitted in this hotel, at least in some rooms, but it would be better if all these rooms were on specific floors instead of between non-smoking rooms.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed at the FS Boston for three evenings. Simply put, the hotel lived up to my expectations for a Four Seasons. The service and staff were excellent, the rooms were nice with the typical amenities and the facilities were excellent. The fitness room and pool were excellent. The location, across from the park, was superb. And what a wonderful park it is. Just beautiful. We did not dine in the restaurants or use room service so we have no view on the food. I cannot say anything negative about the hotel - we look forward to returning.

title: “Incredible service and accommodation of my disability”
text:
Confession here: I usually stay at Marriott properties when I travel for business, but my company booked this property for a sales meeting. It has been years since I stayed at a Hilton property and the Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort won me over. 
I actually landed myself in a wheelchair last fall after a hiking accident. It's temporary until I recover, but nonetheless, terribly inconvenient. The folks at point Hilton Tapatio accommodated my every need. They helped me every day with giving me extra laundry bags so I could fill with ice to ice my ankle every night, the staff was proactive in helping me plate my food from the buffets, help me across doorway thresholds, and the shuttle to get around the property were invaluable--and you don't even need to be disabled to request them.
I was in an ADA suite, which was gigantic! The room was equipped with everything at the right level so I could access and I had bars to hang on to. The one improvement that could be made is to the door. I found myself stuck on how to get inside my room when I don't have anyone around to help. It's very complicated when you're in a wheelchair. I had to ask a bell boy for help one time. Another time when I was alone I got the door open, had to hop out of my chair on one foot while holding the heavy door (heaven forbid if I should break my other leg while doing so). And then I had to figure out how to get the wheelchair in the door, since the breaks were on. Management should brainstorm about how to make this easier for those in ADA rooms, is all I'm saying. Otherwise, loved my room.
The staff at the spa was equally accommodating and helpful, as were the valets at the Different Point of View restaurant and their staff. (I have to tell you, though, the handicap-accessible bathrooms at the Different Point of View restaurant aren't truly wheelchair accessible, as their decal on the outside of the door would suggest. I couldn't get my wheelchair into the handicap stall. My husband (who was traveling with me to assist) had to come into the ladies room with me to help me out. Oh well. Just sayin'. Could use some improvement there. Otherwise, I really enjoyed my stay and was only saddened by the fact that I was really limited in mobility. I wanted to tour the property, but really couldn't do so in my situation. I will have to come back sometime (maybe my company will book there again) and truly enjoy all the property has to offer. 
One more thing. The room service menu could use more choices. Would also like to see more variety, including choices with a southwest flair, since I was a visitor to Phoenix.
Am looking forward to coming back again, though. And hopefully not in a wheelchair or on crutches.

title: “Fantastic hotel, great location”
text:
Cant add much more than the past few reviews in terms of good things about this hotel. Great location, staff were excellent, hotel clean and tidy.
Yeah ok the breakfasts weren't 5 star gourmet food, but it's free and set me up nicely for a days walking. And why are people complaining about having to clean up after themselves. It was a case of picking up your plate and cup and putting it in a bin.
Room was great, cleaned every day. Roof terrace was nice to sit out on. The Metro grill attached was nice with a burger to die for. 
We were honeymooning and one our arrival was a bottle of champagne on ice, and an upgraded room. This kind of attentiveness is what makes this hotel stand out from numerous chain hotels. 
Would I stay again- without hesitation. The location was perfect for site seeing especially with the R train subway at the end of the street. Times Square is a ten minute walk, as are most of the theatres. Empire state building is two minutes away as us Macy's. 
Any negative points? None. This ticked every box for us.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: On my fourth vist to NYC in two years, I finally found a hotel that lived up to my expectations. The room was spacious (for New York hotels anyway), the hotel staff friendly, accommodating, and courteous, and the view of Times Square was fabulous. At that time, they were renovating the elevators, and the only time our wait exceeded a few minutes was on Saturday night when they had some proms and meetings going on. I would not hesitate to recommend the Marquis to anyone who visits NYC where on business or pleasure. No chain beats Marriott in the hotel business...

title: “Patrick made my twins dreams come true”
text:
My wife and I have boy and girl twins who turned 4 years yesterday. We wanted to do something very special for them, so we decided to take them to NY to see Mary Poppins on Broadway.
After we secured tickets on ebay (great 5th row orchestra seats at a super price), we went through American Express to get the special. 
Decided to email the W to let them know how special this trip meant for us.
Patrick Armano replied that he will make sure it was special and wished us a safe trip up there.
First, he gave us a better upgrade than AMEX gave us and the room was INCREDIBLY decorated in a theme of Mary Poppins, that our children were excited and the look on their face....PRICELESS!
We called the front desk to thank Patrick for a great experience!
If you want great service, great rates and great food, stay at the W.
After this review, we will call AMEX to let them know how great the W is.

title: “keep looking”
text:
On a trip through Seattle my two children and I decided to see what Seattle offered. Choosing a centrally located hotel was essential, so we ended up at the Westin. The views were very nice. The room was satisfactory. The staff was courteous. Now, the irritating: why, after paying $250/night would an hotel have the gaul to to charge to park in their lot?
When asked this question, staff looked as though they were sympathetic, yet powerless.
With this experience, I conclude that "nice" hotels can charge for image. So, if you don't mind staying somewhere where the walls are rice-paper thin, the food terribly over-priced and a staff of attentive drones, give the Westin your business. But heed my warning, "you can't polish a ____". However, if you want a stay where you are appreciated as a guest, where someone acknowledges that YOU COULD TAKE YOUR BUSINESS ANYWHERE, choose somewhere else. Posh Spice is in LA, not in the Westin Seattle (regardless of how they portray themselves).

title: “Good choice for Chicago”
text: We checked in for 3 nights 13July'06 & the hotel was full & very busy. Although our room looked onto a wall it was clean, comfortable. The location is awesome, 1 min walk to Michigan Ave, 10min walk to Lake & 10min walk to Subway station. Recommended for price,/location.

title: “Not worth the money.”
text: We spent July 4, 2009 at Paradise Point Resort in San Diego, the place needs a renovation in and out, the carpet in the room was stained, the furniture needs to be replaced. The Barefoot Bar & Grill is the only restaurant available during the day, it was over priced and the food was was below average. There was a morning coffee cart which always had a line and after paying $14.00 for two cups and two pastries, all we got was a luke warm cup of coffee. The employees were helpful and friendly. We rented a boat at the hotel dock and thought we would enjoy the afternoon on the water, except we ran out of gas in the middle of bay, and had to be towed back! They were so busy they forgot to check the fuel. After paying $280 a night, the only regret was, we didn't stay at the Hyatt down the road for less.

title: “Decent hotel with good gov't rate”
text: I work for a Canadian crown corporation and my team comes here regularly for visits with US gov't and international organizations in DC. We go here because they give us the gov't rate (was about $244 when I was here in June). You should ask when you reserve though, otherwise they get upset. The rooms are huge, since they are suites, with a living room in the front and the bedroom after it. Rooms are decent, but there are things that are less than convenient (e.g. LAN connection is only in the living room, not at the desk in the bedroom, which is a bit more comfortable. Also, the power outlet was nowhere near the table where the cabled lan connection was. Big bonuses are the free breakfast (ommelettes made to order, buffet style food but NOT ENOUGH veggies and fruits) and happy hour (if you're into that) free drinks in the evening.

title: “Loved it, will return.”
text: This is really a beautiful hotel and in an excellent location. We booked a signature view room but called and asked to be upgraded to one of the main balcony suite rooms. I was told I would pay 75 additional dollars a night, which I thought was reasonable. Upon arrival, however, i was told that we had been given a complimentary upgrade. I suspected this happened because it was my birthday and they were being generous. The room is a bit old and dated, but the balcony more than makes up for the age of the room. We had a wonderful view of the city and we enjoyed breakfast each morning outside on the balcony. It really was worth the addtional money--which we ended up having to pay (which was one of the downsides of our stay). I didn't fight that because I anticipated paying it, but was a bit disappointed that we had to pay after we were told it was given to us for free. Either way, would stay again in this particular suite and at this hotel again. The parking fee is ridiculous, but what can you do. The internet was in and out, but as I mentioned, the balcony really made up for all of that.

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: We have stayed here a few times and we are always very happy. The location is great if you want to be near the theaters and Times Square. The rooms are of typical size for NYC but they are well appointed and have really comfortable beds. We did not have any contact with staff with the exception of check in, so I can't comment on this. We also did not eat there because it is very expensive. The hotel is also expensive but sometimes you can get a good rate if you shop the websites. I would never stay here if I had to pay the regular rates. (Or anywhere for that matter!)

title: “Quiet, small, perfect location.”
text:
We stayed over 4th of July weekend, and the city was pretty quiet and empty. We had no problem with noise. I grew up in NYC and am used to the subways...we stayed on the third floor, and you could hear a rumble when they went by, but it was nothing more than the same sound of faraway thunder. Might be more noticeable on the second floor, less on higher levels. Never bothered me, slept straight through, not much noise from the street either.
Clean and small lobby, friendly and attentive staff. On checkout, we mentioned a loose tile in the shower area and the maintenance man standing right there immediately made note of it. Also, the lady working the front desk at around midnight on the 4th helped me look up the alternate side of the street parking regulations on the computer by the elevator, to make sure I was parked legally. 
The room is small, but I expected that. The room was plush and looked exactly like the website photos. The bed was huge and soft and wonderful! It took up most of the room, which was perfectly fine with us!
