The furniture is clean and comfortable and modular, the sort of perfect small-space living furniture that those of us who have lived in the city enjoy. Very clean rooms, nice amenities like spa-type shampoos and a bathrobe available to wear. The flat screen TV was very nice, and the cable had a ton of channels!
The location is great: it may be downtown, but the island tapers to a point downtown and it's very easy to catch a west side train or walk through beautiful City Hall Park to catch the east side train.
Overall, it was a perfect weekend and the hotel accommodations added to the experience. I highly recommend this hotel as long as you can handle a small room, it's totally worth it.

title: “Don't even want to say how much I love this place....”
text: My daughter and I stayed here for two nights at the end of March. First time to NYC for both of us. The location could not have been better - close to many famous sights, close to subways, close to shopping. We arrived at 8AM and the hotel told us about the work out room bathroom to freshen up, then stowed our bags for us for the day. When we returned late in the afternoon, we were upgraded to a king bed and were extremely pleased with our room. I kept reading about how small the rooms are, so when I saw it, I actually thought it was quite comfortable in size. I expected to not even be able to walk around the bed! The only time we spent in the room anyway was to sleep and get ready in the morning to go explore. We were always greeted at the front door when we left and returned, the front desk was exceptionally helpful in all ways. And the price was excellent. I'm sure it varies with the seasons but for the time we were there, it was a steal. We stayed on the 11th floor facing the street and were not bothered with street noise at all. I will be back.

title: “Travel agent review”
text:
second time in La Quinta hotel (CLT). Very nice genuine people, service is top. Breakfast is welcomed.
Good size room, all one needs for a short stay. Shutte bus from Airport when one rings for it, very friendly driver.
Would recommend La Quinta Charlotte South to my customers anytime.!

title: “Small but with problems”
text: This is a small hotel in a good location, close to main streets, The Alamo and La Villita. Staff friendly. If you get a street side room it is very noisy from heavy vehicles. The maids' cleaning trolley is always in the outside area making it look untidy. Turn down does not happen in the evening although the service brochure says so. Breakfast is available in the lobby but then has to be carried to your room or second floor, where several tables and chairs are set up. So don't have a second floor room near the lift if you don't want people eating their breakfast outside it. In the main a comfortable stay but this hotel has some quirks!

title: “Perfection”
text: Definitely worthy of the Four Seasons brand. Room was well-appointed and the iPad in the room was perfect for information or ordering room service. Room 303 faces the street and the traffic makes it a little hard to leave the balcony doors open, but it was really too hot to leave open. If interested in open air - ask for a higher floor. Exceptional staff on every level. The gardens and flowers in lobby were lovely. Pool was crowded late afternoon during the week, but no shortage of chairs or service.

title: “nice place”
text: Great place tucked one block off Michigan Ave. Nice reception by the bell man and rooms ready by 3:00 pm. The rooms are nice and large with sitting area. Yes the baths are small but adequate and clean. The room carpeting could use soom updating. The beds are absolutley comfortable. The elevators were never busy because of the size of hotel. Ordered coffee in the morning it only took five minutes, that's service. The Fitzer pub downstairs is a nice relaxing place to unwind after a long day shopping and Manny the bar tender pours a great drink and has personality. All in all enjoyed the stay and will come back.

title: “A Solid Choice on the Riverwalk”
text: I don't have anything negative to say about this hotel. I traveled to San Antonio for business, and would definitely stay there again. From the moment I arrived, the staff were extremely helpful. The concierge made narrowing down restaurant and event options much easier. You can literally walk right out the back of the hotel and onto the riverwalk. The bar is nice if you want to stay in, and room service was tasty and reasonably priced. It's a toss-up between this hotel and Hotel Contessa for best places to stay on the riverwalk.

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text:
Only stayed for one night but was really impressed with the hotel, large rooms, friendly & helpful staff. 
Only complaint was the spa area. The hot tub was only large enough to fit 2-4 people (which would be cramped then). Was looking forward to a soak to relax after a day of shopping/sightseeing but it just wasnt possible given the amount of people waiting to use. Sauna was the same, it wasnt turned on (takes 20mins to heat up) and was large enough for 2/3 people only.
although in fairness to the hotel everything else was really good. Located just off Union Square so was really handy for good shopping/food/transport.
Staff were very friendly and when i arrived back with my girlfriend after a day of shopping/sightseeing it was a really nice touch to find the curtains drawn and lamps on, with after dinner mints on the bedside. A really easy thing to do but a really nice touch from the staff.
Room had a coffee machine, fridge, microwave, cutlerey (basically everything you need if your stay was longer and you fancied saving a few dollars by making lunch in the room).

title: “Simply awesome....”
text: We really had a great time staying here. The suites were beautiful. Lots of history with the place. The restaurant was superb and affordable. The location is awesome!!!! Central and very accessible with the Metro.

title: “Everyone who worked at this hotel was kind and helpful.”
text: We came to Houston because my husband had to have back surgery at the Houston VA Hospital. We stayed at America's Best Value Inn on 9604 S. Maine Street for an entire week. The desk clerks, the manager, and the maids were wonderful. Since I was under a great deal of stress at the time, my husband being a high risk patient, I was very grateful to have a good place to stay. The people working there were so helpful and caring. When my husband returned from the hospital, the evening clerk was so kind to get a wheelchair and help him from our car into the chair and then wheeled him into the room. Everyone was great.

title: “Wonderful stay in a first class hotel!”
text:
This trip was for me, my sister, and my daughter, 11. I booked a city view room and received an upgrade to a beautiful lake view on the 27th floor! Originally I booked the American Girl package but about a week before our stay I changed the room rate to the experience more one (best value). However, they still gave my daughter all the American Girl amenities without charging us the package price! WOW! I thought they made a mistake, but they didn't. My daughter was amazed by the AG travel bed, robe, slippers, notepad, cookies for the doll and daughter, welcome note, etc. 
When we arrived, there was a bowl of popcorn and a bottle of pop on the desk. They sprinkled confetti in one of the two sinks with children's bubble bath, detangler, and soap. It was a great way to start our trip!
They also gave my daughter a folder with the welcome note in it at the lobby desk. Inside had the inviation to make cookes in the hotel's kitchen. The note said to call by 3:00 to participate at 4:00. It was 3:15 when we called but they said "No problem!" We checked in a few minutes early and then went down to the American Girl store (2nd floor of our hotel) for a quck look around. The new store is amazing! After returning to the area to start the cookies, the worker remembered my daughter's name and welcomed her back. She took us (along with a few other guests) to the back side of the restaurant where we washed our hands and the pastry chef had the dough and cookie cutters ready. After making about 5 cookies, we were told that they would bake them for us and have room service deliver them to our room. We left for dinner and when we came back, the cookies were there along with cute little cups full of things to decorate the cookies with (frosting, sprinkes, etc). How fun! This is free by the way.
We checked out the pool area. You have to go through the workout area and spa area to get to the pool. Not crazy about that arrangement. The pool has limited hours for children and the bellhop told us that when he delivered our luggage. It is a pretty small pool (lap pool) but I asked a girl in the elevator who obviously had been swimming if she enjoyed it, and she said yes and that the pool was warm. There are some nicely padded chairs around the pool. I saw a steam room, area to shower, and very nice lockers. If I didn't have my daughter along, I would have loved to spend more time here.
Some people have complained about the elevators, but I found them to be very fast (we never waited more than a few seconds) and the different elevators are right next to each other. Not an issue for me.
A few minor things that could be better: First of all, it would be our arrival at the hotel. We pulled up to the hotel and had to wait quite a while before someone talked to us and helped us with our luggage. Granted, it was 3:00 and close to check in time so I can understand that you need to be patient. However, a nice little conversation to let us know what to do or expect would be helpful. The Park Hyatt has the arrival part down to a science. (They have your luggage out before you are practically out of the car, find out your name which they relay to the front desk, etc.)
Secondly, I put the note on the door to request a newspaper on the first morning. They took the note but I got no newspaper. Then we ordered room service (YUM!) and they asked if we would like a newspaper. Well, they forgot to bring it. I ended up calling and they did bring it this time. However, the next day I had all 4 newspapers (chicago, new york, usa today, and one other that I can't recall) hanging in a bag from my door!
Shower and tub combo: not my favorite arrangement. However, the tub is deep and there is a nice ledge to put your supplies. Plus the toilet is in the same area with the shower/tub and it's a bit cramped in there. There is a much bigger area with two sinks for you to get ready in the AM. 
Loved how close the hotel is to Michigan Avenue and the water. We walked easily to the beach one day where you can rent bikes (even surrey bikes!). If we had more time, I would definitely rent bikes to ride along the shore.
It was also a very quiet hotel. I heard no creaking noises (from the building swaying) or ambulances. The ambulances/police sirens were an issue at the Park Hyatt.
Overall, I would love to stay here again and had a wonderful stay!!!

title: “Impersonal but Central”
text: It's a nice enough hotel and it's in a good location. The elevators can take a while to take you to your floor, but I think the most annoying aspect is that feeling of being just another warm body for them to deal with. I didn't pay - my company did. I don't think I would have stayed if it were me paying, I would have searched out some old friends or thought about staying outside the city. I thought the hotel bar looked a bit soul-less.

title: “Great Hotel, Unparalleled Service beautiful property.”
text: Stayed here on a fun trip downtown and really loved the service. The hotel was perfect everything well kept, top notch worth every penny! You can't go wrong with a stay here! The convenience store across the street has great breakfast tacos and burritos BTW. If you stay Saturday night, Starbuck's isn't open Sunday morning so don't forget to ask for extra coffee @ the front desk.

title: “Wouldn't stay anywhere else”
text: My wife and I are frequently in San Diego visiting our kids who live there. We stay at The Dana everytime we go, which is probably seven or eight times a year. The hotel is located in a perfect spot on Mission Bay. The rooms have balconies that overlook the water. The staff is always helpful and friendly. It is a very relaxing place for us. They even have a marina that we have rented boats at to go play on the water. We have been going to San Diego for 30 years and once we found The Dana we haven't stayed anywhere else.

title: “Christmas Weekend”
text: My husband and I decided to escape for the holidays and we had a great time. We love the city of Chicago and staying at the Hyatt was a complete pleasure. All of the staff we interacted with were friendly and helpful. The location is very central and the view from our room on the 31st floor was awesome. For as large as this hotel was it was very comfortable and felt homey. The elevators were very fast. I would recommend this hotel and will most definitely stay here again.

title: “Tucked away solace...”
text:
This was a great stay at the Hampton Inn! I arrived on a rainy evening to be welcomed by a wonderful front desk staff who quickly checked me in and offered hot soup and cider (served some nights... may be a seasonal thing, but nice touch for the cold weather!). 
My room was on the 17th floor looking down on 31st street. Very clean... Very nice... Very comfortable. The hotel appears to have been a boutique hotel and then converted to Hampton Inn. Mind you... these are smaller rooms given the premium on space in Manhattan. If you like palatial rooms, then this may not be for you. Space is efficiently used... (very small sink/counter and coffee maker is on top shelf of a half-wardrobe closet unit.). However, I was here for nearly a week and did not feel "cramped." And why would you stay in the room all the time anyway given this hotel's great location? I struck out one evening and enjoyed the 10 block walk to Times Square up 6th Avenue and back down 7th Avenue. But its location is tucked away solace... you would not know it is so close to the Garden and Penn Station.
The only possible intrusion of solace could be the adjacen room's TV, which I believe are hung on the sides of the same wall in some rooms. I could hear the tv from the room next door when mine was not on. I kept mine on a low volume on CNN or something like that to mask their sound... problem soloved!
The tucked away solace is also found at the breakfast/dining area at the back of the main floor lobby. It's behind the central elevator block -- a welcome separation from the outside and front desk activity. There is lots of seating and it appeared 2-3 staff members constantly attending breakfast to ensure things were fresh and stocked. There is a tv, tables, booths, and games even. In nicer weather, there is even a small courtyard to enjoy breakfast outside.
Workout room is decent on the bottom floor. However at my stay, they offered a discounted pass to Bally's (I think) a couple blocks away.
Across the street are two handy stores for incidentals, Cafe R has a cafeteria and small gourmet market for easy take-out. (I got a 20% off card for here at check-in -- ask if they still have it!) Jack's 99 cent store has several floors (and sells things for more than 99 cents) and offers some food and drugstore offerings.
All in all a wonderful stay from first to last... I will be back!

title: “Excellent experience”
text: A classy establishment from top to bottom. The desk staff was very professional. The room was well-stocked and clean. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom had great toiletries. Join their rewards club for free internet access and a breakfast beverage. I was at a conference in the hotel and the food there was excellent. The hotel is also right next to the baseball park. I enjoyed the ambience of the fans arriving and the smell of hotdogs and french fries. I was on the other side of the hotel from the ballpark and would recommend it to keep the noise down.

title: “Awesome Hotel, Very Clean, Very Friendly”
text: My flight was delayed and I showed up at 3:30 am. Even though there was a mistake with my reservation, Gwen made sure I got into a room and got some much needed sleep. Breakfast is up to the usual standard of Holiday Inn's. Parking lot, pool area, and other common areas are kept clean and well maintained.

title: “A Charming and Graceful Hotel”
text: The Mark is a large hotel but has all the charm, friendliness and warmth of what one expects in a small boutique hotel. The renovation done about four years ago has transformed it into a high-end modern hotel. Its location in a quiet neighborhood close to Central Park, Madison Ave., and the Museum Mile makes it an even more attractive place to stay in.The efficient staff, without being pretentious, all genuinely desire that guests enjoy their stay. One of the many other amenities of this hotel is the famed chef Vongerichten's eponymous restaurant: "Jean-Georges."

title: “death trap”
text: I can't believe the audacity of this "hotel" and it's employees. These aren't even the pictures of the actual hotel. These photo's have a beach in them and this place is 30 minutes away from one. The golf course isn't in use anymore; the pool is not the one they show in the pictures AND is fenced off the whole time; and the only wheelchair accessible building is the lobby. The actual hotel is more like a half-way home! The cops (not security) had to patrol the property regularly because of all the problems! My family and I stayed in this cockroach infested place for a short time only because they allowed pets for a cheap additional price. They actually made us switch rooms 3 times because of staff errors and offered nothing more than an apology in return. Their version of a kitchenette is a one-person coffee pot, a microwave, and a compact fridge! And the only washer and dryer they had for ALL 102 units needed service about 2 years ago. Couple of tips: If you can, look at this place before you consider renting, don't bring your children or else something might happen to them, and don't even look at the pictures of this "flashy" resort they have up.

title: “disappointing”
text:
King room 377
I love the hotels positioning on top of historic Nob Hill. It is well 
catered for by all 3 Cable car lines.
After entering the hotel past the unhelpful entrance staff and 
ignoring the old smell, you see the beautiful grand decoration of a 
historic impressive building.
Check in staff are pleasant and extremely helpful as are the bell boys 
and the concierge.
The room is disappointing, as its a little on the small side and the 
cupboard smells of 1908. With views of another building the room is 
not full of natural light. The king bed is great, although not my type 
of pillows and the flat screen TV (cira 37inch) has a good variety of 
channels.
Bathroom is quite spacious considering the size of the room. I loved 
the shower with it's very good waterflow. Towels are fine. Miller 
Harris (lemon) toiletries are ok but smell of CIF bathroom cleaning 
products.
Unfortunately due to the positioning of the bed so close to the room 
door you can hear people walking past in the corridor also the light 
from the hallway illuminates the room so if u have a problem sleeping 
with the lights on... You can also hear the conversations in the 
adjoining room (thin Walls) which we contended with a Spanish family 
singing at all hours.

title: “Good location”
text: The location is very convenient. Less than a mile walk to most Smithsonian museums and not much further to the White House, Capitol etc. There are also many restaurants in the area that you can walk to and it is only a few blocks from the Verizon center. The only down side was that our room was right on K street but it was on the 8th floor and the street noise was still very, very loud at night. Couldn't beat the price though, it was $80 per night between Christmas and New Years. I would just suggest an inside facing room to avoid the noise.

title: “good solid hotel”
text:
I've stayed at this location pretty regularly for 5 years. It's clean, comfortable, and a good value for the money, especially during the summer. The staff is professional and effiecient, easy access to I10, and within walking distance to a Cracker Barrel. 
One really ncie thing is if you have a reservaiton, the a/c is turned on before you get there. this a great touch when the temps are in triple digits.
Internet is easy to hook up to but during busy times can be slow. Breakfast is normal HIE hot fare and a great value.
My last stay here the hot water was not very hot, not bad enough to complain about but noticeable. 
if your on the road looking for a clean comfortable hotel with good value this is a winner.

title: “Friendly staff, train line so noisy.”
text: The staff were welcoming and hotel clean. Rooms small but comfortable apart from our room being on the train line. Thank goodness we only spent two nights here because we had no sleep due to trains passing until all hours. The trains were so loud we were woken every time. Good location but I wouldn't recommend. It would have been nice if the pool was open, we really needed some time to relax outside of a stuffy hotel room and have the kids entertained.

title: “Overall wonderful hotel”
text: My boyfriend and I recently came to Houston for one night for a friend's couples shower. When pulling up to the hotel the valet area was extremely busy! There was some confusion about where to go and what to do but we got it figured out. We checked in about an hour early on a Saturday and there weren't any problems. Since the valet area was so busy we weren't sure if we would be seeing our bags anytime soon but thankfully they arrived only a few minutes after us. I will say the elevators were really slow and sometimes you felt like they'd never come. We were very impressed with the room. We had a king bed and the room was huge. We also really liked the bathroom and how the vanity/sink and shower/toilet were separated by a door. The only improvement would have been if there were 2 sinks. The room smelled great when we walked in but not overpowering. We had to get ready and be on our way to the shower so we called down for the car and it was waiting for us when we got down there. When we got back to the hotel we decided to explore a little bit. We went to the rooftop pool which was great! We didn't actually swim or enjoy the hot tub but the next time we come to Houston that is the first thing we plan to do! Also the workout room was small but had really great equipment and was very nice. We decided to walk to the Flying Saucer for a beer, which was only a few blocks away. On the way back to the hotel we decided to stop by Frank's pizza, which wasn't a far walk out of the way, and we got some really amazing pizza! (and they deliver to downtown). The bed was very comfortable and we didn't hear any noise from the hall or anyone closing doors but we also had a room at the very end of the hall. I had stayed at the 4 Seasons just a month earlier and I will choose the Magnolia hotel over the 4 Seasons anytime I come to Houston. Around the hotel there were some bars/night clubs so I'd be cautious of that late at night if you are with kids but they are a few blocks away so not a huge "threat". There are also some great restaurants in this immediate area. I only had two complaints about our stay: 1. the floor in the hotel room was sticky in some places and I have no idea what from 2. the cookie and milk reception was not where we expected it to be. We couldn't find it and I don't know if it was moved/cancelled because of a wedding that was going on but we were looking forward to that and disappointed to miss out on it. Overall this was a great hotel and the best I have stayed at in Downtown Houston.

title: “Great location next to beach.”
text: Location, location, location. Nice hotel. Clean. Tiny bathroom. Small rooms. Off street parking. Minimal breakfast. Pastries and coffee.

title: “Icky and overpriced.”
text: I admit upfront I didn't do my usual research before agreeing to be booked into this hotel. This property is disgusting and the management should be ashamed charging close to 300.00 per night. What did that get me? A tiny , dark room with visible mold and water damage on the ceiling, an a/c unit that was so loud you could barely have a conversation and that worked feebly at best, and atiny bathroom that doesn't appear to have been updated since the 1920's. The mattresses were old. If you must stay here, bring your earplugs.

title: “HORRIBLE”
text: This is the worst hotel I have ever stayed in..... When I arrived to my room it was gross there was hair in the sink hair, hair on the door, hair on the shower, trash in the closet. When I requested them to clean the room, I returned to the room and the window was left opened and there was a bag of opened candy on the night stand. (The Candy did not belong to me) So I don't know if someone entered my room or if housekeeping left a bag of opened candy on the night stand.. When I asked to talked to the manager I was told they were too busy.. At no point of my stay did I get to talk to a manager, because they were too busy. HORRIBLE customer service, HORRIBLE housekeeping. I would not recommend this hotel.

title: “Great Stay !”
text: We had an excellent four night stay recently at the Four Seasons Baltimore. Check-lin proceeded smoothly and we were upgraded (without requesting) to a harbor view corner room on the 14th floor. Service level was overall of very high standard, as you would expect at a Four Seasons. Concierge was able to book a table for us and our party of eight at a restaurant which does not normal accept reservations. We had the breakfast package so we enjoyed a great breakfast at Wit & Wisdom each morning. Overall a great experience.

title: “A bit old...”
text: This was just an average Embassy Suites. The rooms need updating and the bathrooms really need updating. It is near the airport and it isn't dirty or loud. But for the cost, I think you can find better!

title: “Big disapointing”
text: When I found this hotel I was so happy that you still can find something on a good price in a good place.But when we checked in,the guy from the front desk told me that we have a reservation for two rooms.I said that I don't need two rooms and he said"ok".When a sow him next time,he told me just like that ,that everything is ok,but they charged me for the room.After one hour discution ,that this is some sistem mistake,and after he print me some papers ,(that can not be prove,coz the confirmation number in that papers and this that I have in my e-mail were competely diferent.) he told me that this is the internet reservation and he can not do anything,I have to talk with the menager.When I went back to my room I try to call to the internet company on the phone that i found in the web site.Infortunately when I dialed this number I spoke again with the guy from the front desk???After couple days I found the menager,she told me that she will check and she will call me ,but she never did.So I found her finaly,but nothing.She just said ,"sorry"You gave your credit card,so you give a permition for charge.That's it,I paid for two rooms in this hotel,but they never gave me second room,by the way,may be they gave this room to somebody else.I hope that they not gonna charge me some they again,but i will never go again in this hotel.If you think that the room cost 180$,noo it cost at about 370$ nightly.

title: “Service, location, welcome”
text: We couldn't have found a better place for our 5 night stay. Close to lots of great stuff (read other posts). Easy subway access (ditto). Room very clean, comfortable and character filled (definitely bigger than I expected). Loved the kitchen/breakfasts - such an easy and yummy start to the day. And absolutely loved the garden. But, the best thing? The staff. Mainly Rumel and Jubel during our stay and they made it so good. But we also met others (Jay, Troy) and all met the high standard set by our 2 faves. Seriously good. Liz (Australia)

title: “This Place Is A DUMP”
text:
We have stayed at this hotel twice. I am in no way a prude (Hey, I am a Chicago Bears fan- just a bear drinking, football loving gal). 
The only reason we returned a second time, is because they have Chicago Bears ticket packages and we wanted to get tickets. 
They have very few ammenities. The pool and workout room seem OK. There is a cheesy bar- attached to a restaurant (the restaurant serves Dennys style food). The bar attracts some seedier types, in the later evening hours. I wasn't comfortable there. The "outdoor garden" was a weed patch. That's ALL they have. 
The rooms were not easy to climate control. The walls are very thin and the plumbing very LOUD. I did not sleep well all night. Carpets are filty and bathrooms in need of renovation. 
I would never recommend this hotel to anyone. I am surprised that the Chicago Bears organization would even allow the organization to be linked to this level of trash, with the number of awesome hotels we have downtown. Heck, they even host the Bears convention in the Hilton across the street. Much nicer hotel. Stay there instead! 
If you do the Bears package through the Essex because you want tickets- go to the Hilton for your meals and beverages.

title: “Forget Midtown, business travelers, THIS is the place to stay!”
text: Great hotel in hip and real NYC -- great rooms and great location, a true classic with modern amenities. One of those places to see and be seen without being pretentious at all. As I said, totally real

title: “Top Location”
text:
We stayed there as a part of a group during our visit to USA and Canada during June 2010. The Hotel was booked by our tour operator so no idea about the price. We were pleasantly surprised by the rooms which were fairly well appointed and small but adequate bathroom. Tea and Coffee making facilities in the room was a welcome bonus.
 The great thing about the hotel is the location. Walking distance from almost all major attractions in Manhattan. Central Park, Broadway, Times Square, Rockfeller Centre, Macy's(about 15 minutes). Shops and eating joints all within one or two blocks. There is one deli which is about 2 mins. walk (go out of the entrance,turn left and then again left and it is on the right corner of the next block) where we had wonderful breakfast buffet. I forget the name but it fab. breakfast at very reasonable prices.The hotel does not have a restaurant and bar but everything is available around the corner and hence not a problem. Stay in this place to witness the magnificence and pulse of Times Square and walk around to see all the landmarks of Manhattan without spending a dime. At night you can come back to a comfortable bed, Nothing fancy but adequate

title: “Close to the Action”
text: Stayed at the Comfort Inn/Zoo/SeaWorld August 18-21st. Hotel is close to the action, right at the intersections of I8 and I10. Rooms were clean, but beds were HARD. Bathrooms a little small, with a really noisy fan. Breakfast was served every morning on the 4th floor, quite the hub bub, lots of kids but there was plenty of food, cereal, milk, pastries. Also had a cappucino machine, nice touch. Hotel is in need of a make over but for the price and location good value.

title: “great location, great building, excellent service.....5 stars all the way”
text: Checked in on a Friday and stayed until Sunday. Check in was a little crowded but very smooth and they greeted us with hot towels at the front desk. Building is gorgous, all marble lobby. Great for drinks after dinner. Room was a little small compared to other Ritz-Carlton properties but bed was very comfortable and bathroom was luxurious and spacious. Service from all employees was excellent and was greeted every time I came in and left the hotel. Ate dinner in the grill one night and food was delicious and service was just as good as the rest of the hotel. Took a little long to get my car from valet when checking out on Sunday. Would love to come back. Best location in center city, next to city hall. Walking distance to many business and to historic Philadelphia landmarks like the liberty bell.

title: “Great locatoin - dumpy hotel”
text:
The only redeemable aspect to this hotel is it's location. If you want to be close to the Gaslamp District, it's right in the heart of it. This is why I booked it. We needed a place for Halloween festivities. Because I waited till the last minute I had to pay $200 for 1 night. Definitely a rip-off but that's the price for Halloween night.
1) The walls are very thin. We were awoken by the people above us and by the maids cleaning the rooms around us. Made for an earlier morning than normal.
2) The elevator is horribly slow. When the maids are cleaning the rooms the elevator is even slower because they are going up and down. 
3) The sink was in the bedroom, not the bathroom. Very odd.
This is definitely a budget hotel. You get what you pay for.

title: “WEill not go back !!!”
text: Hotel was OK, BUT now we find they have charged us twice, and they do not want to refund!! DO NOT GO THERE!!!

title: “Great hotel for first visit to Chicago”
text:
In advance of our trip the hotel staff was great and during the stay it carried on. We had a club room with a view of the river which was great. The hotel is in the middle of the loop and the mile so it was very convenient. After a full day touring the city the bed was heavenly!
Thanks again to the staff for a great visit!
Ted and Paula from Canada

title: “Very loud at all hours and a shady character working there”
text: The room was dated. Smelly too. Water was cold for a long time so you had to wait for your shower. A person named Robert working at one of the desks, helped himself to a tip while giving me some change for a hop on and hop off bus that I preordered from him. Just a shady character...So many bell hops chatting and not helping. Left a really sour experience for me. Never again. Chicago is my kind of town but this hotel is not my kind even on the 2 star level hotel. The doors were slammed real loud and too much ecco. Did not grt one nights sleep. To the manager please do not write to me, there is nothing you can do to improve. Maybe Donald Trump can fix the place now that he owns the building.

title: “Great, definitely will stay again.”
text: Great location, great door service, great lounge, twice a day maid service. We will definitely stay again.

title: “Best Hotel for the Money in Silicon Valley”
text:
Very recently, I had the opportunity to stay at the Holiday Inn Express in San Jose. The hotel was in a convenient to my business appointment and was easy to find. The check-in experience is one of the factors that sets the tone for the experience for me. The check-in at the Holiday Inn Express in San Jose was very friendly and efficient. 
The room was spacious, clean, and included snacks and bottled water. Very nice gesture for a hotel in this price point. The bed had a choice of pillows and the linens were clean and comfortable. 
As other reviewers have mentioned the entry to your room is straight from the parking lot. While this may be bothersome to some people, it is convenient when bringing your luggage into your room. 
The breakfast area was clean and there were a lot of choices for your meal. The staff at the front desk greeted me and wished me a good morning too. 
With other hotels in the area including a different Holiday Inn Express in the area charging upwards of $300 per night, this hotel is a real gem.

title: “Modern, hip, easy”
text: I stayed here with girlfriends for a bachelorette weekend. It was the same weekend as Lollapalooza, so finding a good location in he city that was reasonably priced was a bit of a challenge. We spent a *tad* more than we originally wanted to, but were happy with our stay. The hotel design is very modern and clean, and the staff were helpful (especialyl with holding multiple keys at the front desk, since member of our group were arriving at different times, from all corners of the country). The room was nice and the bed was comfortable. My two complaints about the room are minor - it was not very well-lit (making it harder for four ladies to shower and get ready for a night on the town; when the bathroom was occupied, there wasn't a lot of other space to do hair/makeup) and the bathroom needs updating. It was entirely functional and clean, but the shower was very small, showerhead was low (I'm only 5'7" and found it annoyingly low), and it just wasn't very nicely decorated. Very minimal complaints. And despite the crowds rolling in from Lollapalooza at all hours of the night, the room was pretty quiet. The location is also pretty easy - walkable to metro (subway) and shopping on Michigan Ave. and a nice stroll or quick cab to grant park/the museums. Also, tip for arrival (especially for those walking to the hotel from the subway at night, as I was): despite its address, the hotel entrance isn't actually located on E. Wacker, across from the Hard Rock Hotel. It's actually just a bit beyond E. Wacker, past the Christian Science building, directly on the riverfront.

title: “Interesting Place”
text:
We stayed there for three days last month. We found this to be a well located hotel. And when we called them directly, they immediately dropped the rate down to an average of $149 per night. Plus, when we got there, they upgraded us to a suite with a very decent bathroom.
Staff was friendly and helpful. We found the lack of a lobby annoying. But, our suite's sitting room helped alot. We could also sit in a sitting area on several of the floors.
Although I did not see a double room, I have a feeling it would have been very tight. The suites, though small were more than adequate. Too bad you can't guarantee a free upgrade before you get there.

title: “Business Travel”
text: This hotel is old, and in need of an update. It's one of those huge, convention-type hotels with a million rooms. It was clean, but clearly dated. As many people have stated, you can get a really nice view if you ask for it. The view was indeed nice. I had business on N. Wacker, so it was a nice short walk away from where I needed to be. Room service was prompt and the food was fine. The gym was fine; nothing fancy. If you need a treadmill run or elliptical workout, you're good to go. There was also plenty of other equipment. The pool area was uncomfortably hot, and I was only walking through to get to the gym. The conference facilities were fine. I probably wouldn't pay to stay there again, but if I had to stay again for business travel, I guess it would be ok.

title: “Fancy hotel, with bad Internet and expensive parking”
text:
Embassy Suites is a very nice hotel. Our room was like a small apartment with two rooms, and a bathroom. Everything was super clean and very appealing. 
The metro station is located only five minutes from the hotel lobby, and it takes around 15 minutes with the metro to the centre of Boston.
There are however a couple of downsides. There is only valet parking at the price of $32 pr. day. We got a parking-voucher of $25 by booking via expedia, which of course reduced the price considerably.
Besides that the Internet was bad. At least on the American east coast it is more or less common to have free wifi in every room. This is however not the case for Embassy Suites Boston. Not even in the lobby was the wifi free. You could however pay around $10 pr. day for connection all over the hotel, or you could use one of the four computers in the "Business room" at the hotel. The Internet connection here was however very unstable and it took us a very long time just to check mail, and do research on what to do in Boston the next day.

title: “An oasis of calm and service in the heart of the airport area.”
text: Stellar service, comfortable, casual and modern atmosphere with high quality bedding and quiet peaceful surroundings make for a great visit business or pleasure. Convenient location just off the highway and very close to the airport but no noise. Fantastic food in the restaurant for dinner much of it local and organic, and very reasonably priced, especially the wine. Breakfast was also excellent if even a bit small. Ample parking, pretty grounds and genuinely friendly and helpful staff across the board. Have not had this level of service since a 4 seasons and at a fraction of the price. Strongest recommendation and will stay there again anytime in the Seattle area if you don't need to be downtown.

title: “BEST HOTEL!!!”
text: Mike Costello,The General Manager, greets each guest with warmth. Mike Costello makes the visitor feel very special. Jackie,@ Front Desk takes wonderful care of everyone. Steve, in the Bar , is effervescent, charming,intelligent! The hotel is beautiful! The food & cocktails are delicious! We had a spectacular visit!!!

title: “Owners,management, staff are fabulous!!”
text:
Al, Jubel, staff were the most helpful we have ever encountered in our travels.
Jay, sorry we missed you. This is a ten in every respect. Great room, close to transportation, wonderful tourist advice and suggestions, relaxing, and a perfect New York setting are only a few of the pluses in staying at Chelsea Pines Inn. We were visiting the city from our home in Colorado. This was a perfect choice for us because we needed assistance in planning our activities. The staff was so helpful and saw to every need we had. Our room was spotless and so relaxing. If you want to stay in a wonderful NYC atmosphere this is it. We cannot recommend Chelsea Pines Inn highly enough. You will love it. I guarantee. We miss you.
Ken & Carol

title: “1st stay in NY and Bryant hotel.”
text:
First time to the city and hotel, from the minute we arrived we were treated special and looked after very well, we had a few problems with our flight and ended up getting to the hotel the day after checking in, the hotel were helpful and couldn't do enough to help (a special thanks to Felix).the room was on level 8 with no view over park but we weren't in there apart from getting home at night which was around 12ish, and then up , shower,and out (tool expensive for breakfast, so we had a coffee and lovely bagels from about six stops up from hotel same side, took them to the park and ate them there before heading off for another full packed site seeing day! Apart from a slight lack of space to store clothes in and a very expensive room bar, there is a nice big power shower, nice bed, nice chocs on yr pillow, and fantastic venue for all the hit list places, I would stay here again tomorrow, fantastic place to visit, lovely new Yorkers that can,t do enough to help you, and an up market hotel to make you feel special, will be back.
 tv and large and bathroom was just a shower which suited us fine, we had a bottle of bubbly as it was a special birthday, which was a nice touch. the bar downstairs was pleasant and residents get a happy hour between 5-6 which is greAt!. The only thing is if u have just co e back from site seeing the clientele in the bar is well dressed and you may feel under dressed. M

title: “Beautiful views of times square”
text: Great locations with beautifu time square views ... The staff will bend over backwards to help ... Ask for just about anything and they will arrange It... We stayed in a high floor room with a time square view , it was snowing and made everything perfect for the holidays ...

title: “Run down”
text: Counter staff was friendly, but unprofessional, the microwave did not work, I was glad I could use the regular oven to heat my pizza. Breakfast was a disappointment. Snacks at the desk were sky high and bad food. No healthy foods whatsoever. Tv digital was, shaky?; whatever HD sets do when they are not working right.sidewalks were very dirty and safety did not seem a concern. Soft bed though and nice selection of pillows.

title: “very very good”
text:
W stayed at the Palomar over Labor Day weekend with our college and high school aged sons, and my mother. Staff was gracious and accommodating, especially to my mother, who is a senior citizen, and to one of my sons, who has severe food allergies. We brought food with us and required a separate refrigerator. They were very helpful.
Here is the lowdown - luxury of the rooms is maybe a small step down from a Ritz Carlton or Mandarin Oriental, where we have stayed before. However - the rooms are enormous, the beds are very comfortable and the staff warm and friendly. Also - during the summer, having the pool was key. It is small but lovely, well-designed and well kept up. And not just for small children. It was a great place for my kids and mother to relax when they had enough of the touring. 
I would definitely stay here again, and highly recommend the hotel.

title: “Awesome if you can afford it!”
text: My partner and I are backpackers, but we wanted a bit of a treat. We got this hotel through Hotwire for half price than usual. We figured, why not have a Times Square experience?! It was a lovely room, so much space. Luckily, our room faced the back, so we didn't have a lot of flashing lights in our room. (They have blackout curtains if you get a street-facing room). There is free wifi in the lobby, but it was sort of spotty. One of the floors in the hotel is a business centre, so they have some computers and printers you can use for free - those were great, and it seemed like not many people knew about them, so they were available whenever we needed them. If you must stay in Times Square, I would recommend this hotel. It was comfortable and quiet and it had a lot of nice amenities. However, Manhattan isn't so big, so you could easily stay elsewhere (save a lot of money) and walk to Times Square. If you are fancy and have spending money, then definitely go for it, we had no complaints!

title: “Great stay at this hotel”
text: Stayed at this hotel for 3 nights to take in a couple of Mariners games and do some shopping. As a Marriott platinum member our room was upgraded and we also got access to the club lounge on the 26th floor. The room - was fabulous, clean, spacious with comfortable beds, mini frig and great bath amenities. Club lounge where we had our breakfast and happy hour daily had a nice selection of food and drinks and wonderful views of the city. non-alcoholic drinks were free an although you paid for alcohol it was a one-time small charge and refillable after that. Snacks that came with it happy hour were heavy horsdervous that if you are a light eater can fill you up so no need for dinner. Only draw back to this hotel is the cost of parking is steep @ $30 night but I suspect that is normal for hotels in the city. Would we stay here again...definately YES.

title: “Great Service in great location”
text: Great hotel to stay in Chicago. A shame this hotel doesn't have a Cafe attached to it. Rooms was great and the biggest plus was for sure the staff. Made a mistake during the reservation process on the internet, result was a room which was too small. One phone call and we were relocated to a bigger room without any (apparent) issue. Staff in the bar was also very customer friendly! Will certainly stay at this hotel if I'm in the area again. Only downside was the lack of free wireless internet which I think should be standard these days.

title: “Better than you think.”
text: I stay at this hotel often for business with my company. I get a corporate rate which makes it even better; but it is still worth more than I pay. Always very friendly staff, rooms are very modern with very comfortable bed. Nice bathroom, well appointed. Free Internet!!! This is a great deal. Free parking and right next to 9A and Baymeadows. I will stay here again in the future.

title: “Great location”
text:
Loved the location! My wife and I stayed here for a night this past weekend and loved it. Definitely a great place and pretty swanky. Great place for young couples.
We walked along the Chicago river and Wacker everywhere. Easy access to the red line train on Grand avenue. We also walked to Millennium Park/ Grant Park which only took probably 20 mins. 
Friendly staff let us drop off our bags early in the day and explore the city then they called us when our room was ready. 
Tip: Don't be scared off by the bar downstairs. My wife and I were initially worried it would be a loud night after midnight but we were on the 6th floor and it was quiet as could be.
Tip: Use the Trump Tower as a reference point to this Hotel wherever you are in Chicago.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: We just came back from San Francisco, and we absolutely loved the Hotel Carlton. The staff, especially Theo, were wonderful and so helpful. Theo always treated us like he knew us personally. It was a pleasure staying there. Our room was nice, clean and comfortable. We even had a toddler with us, and it worked out just fine. The walls of the hotel are a little thin, but it really didn't bother us too much. We were on the 8th floor, corner room, which may have helped. The decor is wonderful as well. You can also access a lot from the hotel's location, and San Francisco is a great place to walk around. My husband and I HIGHLY recommend the Hotel Carlton.

title: “A Wonderful Gem.”
text: I loved this place. The rooms are almost Zen like. The staff was so friendly. I would love to go back and stay on a Wed. night because they show outdoor movies by the pool and bar. The brunch is fabulous! Did I mention I love the bar? Walking distance to everywhere. Susan and Jim

title: “Quick business trip”
text: Ez check in. Small lobby, help was efficient and spoke english! Elevator was quick. Room, mine on 18th , the top floor, was small, but clean. Very quiet. Easy to get to, right off 6th ave.

title: “Wonderful Place to Stay”
text: I put my house on the market and never expected it to sell in 4 days for my asking price. Therefore, I am staying at this wonderful hotel for the next two months until I move to Michigan. The exterior of this hotel is spotless and very welcoming. My room is extremely comfortable and the staff that takes care of cleaning the room do a great job and are very pleasant. I am a single female and I feel very safe throughout the entire property. They allow pets but I have never encountered a problem with odors or unkempt grounds. The breakfast and dinner meals are included in the daily rate and are a wonderful bonus. The laundry facilities are easy to use and the machines look to be new. But one of the best parts of this great hotel is the staff. All of the employees that I have met, Stacy, Marcella and Andrew have been amazing and extremely kind, welcoming, and very eager to help in any way. I cannot remember the last time I was treated so well while staying in a hotel. It’s very evident that customer service seems to be their number one priority and they do it with perfection.

title: “Pure bliss!”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Indigo the Sunday night following Comic-Con. My friends who I was rooming with elsewhere all flew home Sunday so I was on my own. Got an amazing deal through Hotwire for $105 and I could not have been happier. The staff was warm and welcoming and the room was gorgeous, with a comfy king sized bed, beautiful bathroom, tons of space and a nice view! It was about a 10 minute walk to shops, food & more. 
The small bar/restaurant had a great breakfast & offered a free coffee refill to go as I got some last minute shopping done before my flight. When I arrived and left, the staff was helpful and not overbearing. What impressed me most of all? That they didn't treat me any differently because I booked through Hotwire. I've heard of that happening with friends in the past (not here, but in other cities). They totally won me over and I will definitely look into staying here again next summer!

title: “Hardly "grand," poor service, they nickel & dime you to DEATH”
text: Got a good rate on priceline, but the bad service started even before we left Dallas. Tried to call the concierge 3 times regarding a floral delivery, was put on hold forever each time. The exorbitant extra charges started mounting as soon as we got there. $35/night for valet parking?? Your only other option is $24 to self park, OUCH. We got back late the 1st night, so we had to order room service; 1 pizza, an order of wings, and a hamburger cost $100, I kid you not (and the wings sucked by the way).. Yeah, location is pretty good, but rooms are small...normally I don't even notice that, but I got tangled up in the bathroom and closet doors more than once. We valet parked the first night (to tired), but self-parked the 2nd night; when we checked out, there were 2 $35 valet charges on the bill, GREEDY!!!! Avoid this property, it's just not worth the hassle and expense.

title: “Best Staff”
text: I stay at this hotel regularly and I am continually pleased by it's staff's friendliness and professionalism. There are many choices in Dallas and the Renaissance will always be mine!!

title: “Perfectly fine”
text: Perfectly fine hotel with pleasant staff. Zippy elevators too -- a small thing, but nice. Close to cute old town and other such attractions, and right on the water. Other hotels may be a tad more perfectly centrally located, but this is good enough. Can basically walk to most things.

title: “Wonderful Experience...Ideal Location...Professional Staff”
text:
My daughter and I recently stayed at the Boston Park Plaza for a special birthday/college scouting weekend, and after reading some of the reviews, I was extremely nervous, but having spent a lovely weekend in this beautiful, clean, comfortable hotel, I have no idea how you wouldn't love your stay. The staff was friendly and efficient. We checked in with no delays, and even when we walked through the lobby during very busy check-in times, the lines seemed to be moving well. I suppose things might get a little crazy Marathon Weekend, but I have to believe you'd run into that at any hotel during such a huge event weekend. 
The location is ideal. We parked in the Motor Mart, and never moved our car. The "T" stop is a block away, and we were all over the city, including to Fenway Park, easily. The concierge helped us with reasonably priced tickets to a Red Sox game and gave us great dining suggestions in the North End. I'd absolutely stay again...and again.

title: “Liking this hotel less and less”
text:
I booked a room in the newer tower. As I was checking in, the receptionist tried to get me to change to the older tower ("Excellent views") - with hindsight that was a bit cheeky, since those rooms are cheaper.
The good
The room size is more than adequate for New York (or anywhere else). Relatively recently updated, the furnishings are both new and clean. The bathroom is fine. The bed is excellent if you like soft mattresses. The TV is a large, oldish LCD.
The bad
No minibar
Room service at times convenient to the hotel (i.e. not at lunch?!)
No lunch or dinner at hotel restaurant
Breakfast greasy and unhealthy
The lack of both the minibar and restaurant are "temporary". Well, they were also "temporarily" lacking the last time I stayed, which was some way back.
Overall, though the prices are cheap, there are similarly-priced and better options in the area. I will not be coming back if I can help it.

title: “Excellent Stay!”
text: I stayed at this hotel on a recent "quick" trip to Houston! Everything was great! The staff was friendly and the hotel was recently updated! The room was spectacular and the pool was inviting and nice! The lounge was a nice little place to relax, grad a drink and unwind! Over all I will most definitely stay here again!!!!

title: “Wasn't as good as previous reviews”
text:
I booked this hotel on reading previous reviews and found some problems during my stay. First the good points I agree from previous reviews.
Nice neighbourhood location, good size two roomed suite with kitchenette, close to subway about 3 stops to Times Square, Fairway market across street always open for anything !
Hotel cost was far cheaper than Times Square hotels.
Bad Points.
No help with bags on arrival at hotel. We watched a number of elderly people arrive , as we did,and struggle inside with their bags while staff watched. When staff were asked for help you could feel their reluctance. The Concierge had to doulble as a bag man when asked and it was quite obvious it was below him ! Staff on front desk were surly and it certainly wasn't service with a smile.
On a two roomed suite I had the bathroom was very small.
Even on the 18th floor you could here delivery lorries to Fairway Market all through the night with their reversing beepers.
Air conditioning units very noisy.
I understand that only half of the rooms have been reconditioned, make sure you request one.
No ice machines in hotel - you can buy ice at Fairways.
This is just my opinion at the time of my 2 night stay. I was dissapointed as I felt it did not live up to previous reviews.
On my next visit I will revert back to my normal Times Square area and pay the difference in price,

title: “Always a great experience!!”
text: When we're in NYC, which is about 2 to 3 times per year, we stay at the Omni. My wife, my son, and I enjoy the hotel. The staff is friendly and accommodating, the rooms have always been clean and modern and the loyalty program allows for free wifi, complimentary morning beverages, and other goodies! Our concierge experiences have always been positive. We're going back in January 2012 - can't wait!!

title: “Service and quality slipping”
text: I have stayed here many times before but not in the last six months. Despite DC being one of the few booming travel destinations, you wouldn't know it staying at the Hamilton. Across the board the quality of the hotel has declined, from check in to upkeep to even the towels. You will still pay a premium for the ultra convenient location, but it has slipped significantly.

title: “Overall not bad, but a little disappointed”
text: First I'll say that for the most part this was an alright hotel with a Great location right by the Mag mile. It seemed a little "old", but, IT IS! (1928) I made reservations a little more than a month beforehand and requested a " nice street view ." We arrived around 2:45 from Michigan to see the Tigers-White Sox game(7/25), room was ready(?). Went to tenth floor, cards didn't work, went back down and up again, we had a corner room(small, just enough room to walk around the king bed(nice bed though)) and a view of some bricks from the building next door. Really!?? A month's advance with a request and we still got a "brick view. " That was Very disappointing, but at that point I didn't feel like going back down and switching rooms. I normally would have but with the time constraint I didn't want to waste more. Also, we chose to self-park(which you pay for separate in the garage and was recommended cheaper than valet by the doorman(?)) and it actually came out to $44 for 24hrs and 32mins(maybe that extra 32 killed us more than we thought, huh?) Wonder what valet would've been. I just wish I had more time to devote to making sure I was satisfied and content with my stay/purchase. You may need a few extra minutes if you don't like a brick view and a bed for a room.

title: “Great Location, Great Beds, Great place to stay!”
text:
We booked this hotel after reading all the great reviews, and as many have said before, we were not disappointed.
This trip was for my husband's 40th birthday. I also emailed the hotel beforehand and signed up for the Sofitel Privilege card.
When we checked in we were offered a King size room on a higher floor which was great. The rooms are a great size and the beds are sooooo comfortable, you do not want to get up in the morning!
On the first evening a bottle of champagne arrived with a letter of congratulations for the 40th Birthday. A nice and very welcome touch!
The staff were all very helpful and were not at all stuffy.
We ate fantastic breakfasts in the hotel restaurant 'Gaby', about $50 for two of us. The Classic eggs benedict were wonderful and the yoghurt granola with fresh berries equally as good.
The location is superb. Times Square, Fifth Avenue. Grand Central Station to name a few all within a moments walk or so.
Had a fabulous meal in 'The Palm' restaurent on 2nd Avenue. A great experience.
We would definitely recommend this hotel and look forward to staying again in the future.

title: “Highly Recommend for a Place to Stay in Indy!”
text: I had such an excellent stay at this Marriott. I had initially booked the hotel online requesting one double bed, a fold out couch, and a cot. I thought we got a really good rate on it, but boy was I surprised when I arrived! When I walked in there was a full sized kitchen, complete with a tall refrigerator (bigger than a mini fridge but not full size), dishes, appliances, and utensils included. 2 separate bedrooms both with a queen sized bed, and a living room with a couch! The pool was amazing, check out and check in was a breeze. We were so exhausted when we came in that night, that we called for an extended check out, understanding that they would probably be charged a fee, but they let us check out an hour later with no fee! The service was great, the staff was friendly, and everything was clean and easily accessible. I don't have one complaint!

title: “Great hotel for the 500!”
text: After a last minute opening, we booked this hotel for the Indy 500. The room was new and spacious and the location was ideal to get to the Speedway. Rate was very reasonable considering the busy weekend. The only complaint was that the parking lot was not big enough! We plan to stay here again for next year's race!

title: “One of the best Courtyards I've experienced”
text:
I spent one night at Courtyard Camelback and while my experience was limited since it was such a short stay, I was impressed by the service and had a very pleasant stay. The neighborhood is non-descript, surrounded by strip malls, chain restaurants and generic office buildings. It's perfect for a business traveler.
I had a standard king room which was obviously recently updated. Very clean and well-appointed. Aside from the bed, there was a love seat with coffee table and a work (desk) area with a flat-screen TV. The bathroom had a separate tub/toilet area from the sink. In the sink area, there was an additional counter with a coffee maker and a small fridge and microwave. Nice touches. Bed, linens and bath products were as expected in a Marriott property. In addition, there was a hair dryer, iron and ironing board.
The interior rooms face a courtyard with the pool area. There is also a hot tub. The exterior rooms face random office buildings and parking lots. The property is set back from the major roads, so my exerior room was quiet even if the view was dull.
There were two stand-outs with the property. First was the small bar/bistro in the lobby. Serves Starbucks-style coffee/drinks/snacks but also offers a small but good light meal menu with things like sandwiches, chicken wings, etc. It is also a full bar. I decided to have a quick bite after a film event in the evening and had a drink and chicken wings which were surprisingly excellent. Based on that nice snack, I decided to have breakfast there the next morning. Again, simple but very good. There is an outdoor seating area which was a very pleasant place to have breakfast.
The second stand-out was the overall customer service. Everyone, from the front desk to the bar/bistro staff, was friendly and helpful.
Complementary newspapers were offered in the lobby. There was WiFi in the lobby, bistro area and the outdoor seating areas. In addition, there were three computers for guest use in the lobby (one was just for printing out airline boarding passes.)
I can't really speak to the "value" since I used Marriott points for my stay but the rewards point category for the property, which usually correlates to its price-point, is a moderate level.

title: “Great one night stay pre-flight!”
text: We had a wacky itinerary that included a ~9 hrs. overnight layover in LA. This hotel had a free shuttle, and when we checked in, we discovered a really nice clean room. It's obviously been renovated fairly recently; and the results are pretty impressive. The staff were friendly, and the breakfast (included) was a welcome surprise. It was delicious and had a great selection, including eggs and waffles! We felt like we'd won some sort of prize for picking this hotel.

title: “Good hotel, great location!”
text: I stayed at this hotel from 9/11/06 thru 9/22/06. I was there on a business trip. I booked my room a few weeks prior to my stay. When I arrived at the hotel, the front desk staff were very nice and courteous. I had a real nice big room,next to the elevator. When you entered it was a long hallway and then the layout was nice. There was a full size bed,loft ceilings(high ceilings),micro,refridge,tv(22 channels including HBO),coffemaker,desk, 2 phones,alarm cock w/radio,blowdryer(took forever to dry /the one that is mounted on the wall),iron,ironing board,2 huge windows(view to an abandoned bldg). The down comforter and pillows were great but I did not find the bed that comfortable. The bathroom was very big and plenty of towels. The comp breakfast was good and there was always 2 hot dishes(ex:sausage and waffle sticks or canadian bacon and eggs,etc...). I did not care for the eggs, I think they were fake/powder eggs. They also had fresh fruit,cereal,yogurt,bagels,toast,muffins,4 differnt juices,pastries,coffe,teas,etc. The breakfast ladies were always nice and helpful. Then, from 5-6pm there was a comp happy hr that included beer and wine(sometimes) and chips and salsa or pretzels,etc. At night, they had comp fresh hot chocolate chip cookies at the front desk counter. Those went real fast. I also did wash twice on the 2nd flr there was 2 washers and 2 dryers and they were $1 each. So that was convenient. In the lower lobby there was a pool,small gym,and comp computers to check your emails. The hotel was always secure and I saw security at night. The cleaning lady did a decent job w/the room, but did forget to clean it twice so I was not happy about that. The hotel is located in a great location within walking distance to everything including Camden Yards, there is a CVS around the corner,McDonalds,Subway, great pub named Peter's around the block(can't miss it),Inner Harbor, Hooters,Cheesecake Factory, Pizzeria Unos, Power Plant(Babalu Grill good for mojito drinks from 4-7pm 2 for $5 and the Lodge Bar great music and drinks real happening place on Friday night). Took a water taxi to Fells Point, lots of bars and restaurants. Schuckners on the bay/water good food and specials everyday. Overall, had a good time at this hotel and would definitely go back.

title: “Very happy with our experience”
text:
For us, this was a home away from home and we would readily stay there again. The staff was very, very helpful in coordinating our check-in and check-out, since the logistics are always difficult when travelling with young children. We stayed in room 502 - two bedroom suite (upgraded from 1 bedroom). 
My wife was in for a tradeshow and I was Mr. Mom. We were travelling with a one-month-old baby and a 2.5 y/o toddler -so the suite aspect was very appealing to us. The small refrigerator and microwave came in handy. We didn't use the stove since there were no tools / pots pans readily available, but perhaps you can ask for these. 
This is not a traditional hotel, so do not expect a large staff or big lobby or workout room or pool or concierge etc., but I think the trade-offs are well worth it. Of course, we can only comment on the room we stated in (502), which was just so comfortable and inviting. We were happy to have a deck off the living area, although the rain kept us from really taking advantage of it. 
The beds were very comforatable... basically everything feels very new and solid. There were flatscreens in both bedrooms and the living area. This room was in the back of the hotel, and we were not disturbed by any noises. The internet connection was solid (we used the provided ethernet connection). 
Overall, this was the perfect place for our 4-day stay in NY. John and Colin in particular were very helpful and we owe them our gratitude. The other staff were pleasant too, but we leaned on John a bit to assist with moving luggage etc, and he came through. 
We usually stay with friends when visiting NY, but now we have another great option - the French Quarters.

title: “Very satisfying accomodations”
text: My family and I stayed here last week and we were very satisfied with our stay and will definitely come again. The hotel is in a great location if you're interested in walking the National Mall and visiting the museums. The price was just right, the rooms were really clean. The pool was a little cold for my son, but he tried to swim at night, so that is probably to be expected. There isn't a ton of restaurants to choose from in the area, but the front desk was able to suggest a few places that offered free delivery and we took them up on it. Perfect. The breakfast buffet was delicious, one of the best we've had. The scrambled eggs and spinach were especially tasty and our waitress was probably the friendliest person that we encountered in DC. The parking garage attendant was also very helpful to us as we tried to navigate our way into the city and the garage. The monuments are so beautiful at night, but they are quite a hike from the hotel, so plan your transportation in advance. The trollies aren't a great choice for night time transportation and may not even be available. But the rick shaw drivers are all over, and its a fun way to see the sights as you make your way back to the hotel at night. They work on tips only and are a fun choice for a ride. We will certainly come back, and we might even get to use some of our reward points that we earned for our stay.

title: “Good location but very small room”
text:
I wanted a hotel in the historic part of Boston from which I could explore the sites. After considerable research, I picked the Bulfinch, knowing the rooms could be small. I had no idea, however, how small. I arived with 2 suitcases, but there was only one rack, stuck in a tiny closet. The other suitcase had to be used on the bed when in use. As to room to work or get arround, well there really was none. 
The staff at the hotel were nice and helped us plan how to get arround by foot. But in addition to the small size of the room, there was a buzzing noise coming from the wall, possibly the room next door, that made sleeping difficult. 
In my effort to diagnose the noise, I discovered there was a broken glass behind the bed on the floor. I suspect the housekeeping staff had not found this due the cramped size of the room. 
The staff tried to address the noise, but were unable to. They did provide a discount on our stay in apology which was appreciated.

title: “Exceptional extras”
text: The room, bath, check in and out were flawless, typical of a Hampton. Considering its proximity to the airport, it was quiet. There's free breakfast and a quite good free dinner weekdays! If you have an early flight, before breakfast starts, they offer a minimal breakfast bag. Return your rental car the night before - the free shuttle got me to and from the airport in minutes.

title: “Great Location”
text: This Hotel is near plenty of shopping and dining. The room was clean and spacious and it was perfect for our trip. I would definately stay here again.

title: “Double billed and slow to fix.”
text:
I recently stayed at this hotel. It was clean. You could tell it was a very nice hotel in it's day. The work that was done on it seems to have been the minimum investment to make it livable. The room was clean enough. It still had an old feel to it.
My real issue was they billed my credit card for an extra night and said the refund would take a few days. I wouldn't have caught it were it not the holidays and I wanted to check online what I had spent on people. I think checked and to-date the money, MY MONEY, still has not been refunded to me. A lazy weekend out of town has turned into a big annoyance in a very busy schedule because of their incompetence. 
Good luck with this place, stay at your own risk...

title: “Great location and good service”
text: Fantastic location, close to central park, subway, 5th avenue etc. The room was a standard size room with king bed and good quality sheets, generous size bathroom with quality toiletires provided. I did find the room quite dark even with the curtains open, due to the paint colour and dark coloured furnishings and the close proximity of surrounding buildings. The service was good, friendly staff at check in, and the concierge were very helpful in providing me with directions to make my way around NYC. The cafe attached to the hotel served good quality coffee too. If you are looking for a hotel in a fantastic location, I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Good for Partying, not for Sleeping”
text:
My wife and I recently stayed here for our ten year anniversary. The room we got on the 4th floor with the balcony was great during the day and evening, however... Around 2am the craziness started and all hell broke loose in the hallways until around 4:30am. Outside we heard fighting, yelling, smashing and all kinds of trouble and no hint of security.
I still like this hotel and it was partly our fault for choosing a room on the same floor as the nightclub. If you do end up going to this hotel choose a room on one of the upper floors and away from the club if you want to get any sleep.

title: “Great little hotel!”
text: This Holiday Inn Express is a terrific value located a couple of blocks south of Madison Square Garden. The neighborhood wasn't prime, but within a few blocks are restaurants, bars and shopping (Macy's Herald Square). We arrived super early in the morning, were able to store our bags (no charge) and we hit the Grayline Uptown/Downtown Loop Tour (a great way to get the lay of the land). When we returned to the hotel, we checked in and went up to our room. The room was quite small, but spotlessly clean with a nice, new-looking bathroom. We did have a slight bit of noise Saturday night (sounded like there was a dance club nearby) but it wasn't that loud and we were able to put in our earplugs and sleep away. The complimentary breakfast at this hotel is extensive--and delicious!! There are omelettes, sausage, biscuits, cinnamon rolls, bagels and the list goes on and on. It's not a 5 star, but all in all, a great place--highly recommended!

title: “Great midtown location”
text:
We took advantage of a 4 nights for the price of 3 deal that was on offer, which meant the price was great value for the quality of room/hotel for this part of town.
Surprisingly spacious double room with an equally good sized bathroom.
An excellent midtown base for a long weekend / short stay visit to Manhattan; would highly recommend this hotel, especially if there are deals on offer.
Would revisit for sure

title: “You should try it, ONCE and make up your mind”
text:
Really, you should try this hotel once and decide for yourself. This was my third trip with my family and my kids think it is the coolest place on earth; the pool with the word "wet" at the bottom, the fluffy beds and techno beats playing as a backdrop to the whole experience...it is much cooler than well....me. 
I don't like the dark hallways, feel as though they are dark only because the place has something to hide. Frankly, it might. The hotel is not new by any stretch of the imagination; but it is comfortable. 
As I checked in this time, there was a guy in his late 40's checking in with a "girl" in her mid 20's just in front of me. It struck me that if I were to be unmarried or even, having an affair...this would be the hotel where I'd want to make it happen! The place is full of mojo. 
The beds are comfy, the service is fine and the view from the lakeside is lovely. Try it once.

title: “Anonymous hotel”
text:
Good room (big) with a poor (old) bathroom (tube instead of shower)
Is a big but anonymous hotel, the restaurants are poor (fast food only) and the breakfast is quite expensive; parking is fine and hotel location is ok to stay in downtown.
No frigo bar in the room...is crazy!

title: “Great location, do not like parking!”
text: The parking was a bit of a hassel. The parking garage attendant was very rude, and actually citated my car because of an aragant attitude. The hotel was very clean, very nice. All hotel staff were very pleasant and went above and beyond to make sure we were accomodated. If you are staying in a large parlor room, you will be next to elevators. View was also not so great, looked at roof of another building.

title: “Ramada Austin, A Fine Central Austin Choice”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights just before xmas 2009. Place was 75% empty. It was nice and quiet! Staff informed business is often very slow around xmas, due to U of T being closed down.
King Bed was top notch, very comfortable, nice blend of firm and soft. Sheets and blankets were perfectly clean and of good quality. Heat worked very well. 
Room had small closet, which was very good to have. Also a small refrigerator and micro. Bathroom sink was located outside of room which contained toilet/tub-shower, a configuration which I prefer - very handy when travelling with "she" who takes long steamy showers. Provided toiletries were much above average. Plenty of hot water and nice water pressure in shower. Very nice towels.
Room nicely appointed and maintained. TV did the job, a nice assortment of channels. Wireless internet worked flawlessly.
Interior Corridors, good from a safety standpoint imo. No problem with noise from nearby freeways (our room faced west). Was not "out in the country" silent, but nothing more than a non-intrusive hum.
Pool was closed due to it being winter.
Complimentary breakfast was great, cereals, toast, waffles, scrambled eggs, sausage, ham, juices, fruit, coffee, pastries, etc. Free newspapers in lobby.
Plenty of parking. A bit hard to drive to, freeways surrounding hotel are complicated. Strongly recommend mapping out exactly where to turn in advance. 
Neighborhood is okay, wouldn't recommend walking in area after dark, mostly because there is nothing to walk to. Highland Mall area (across freeway to the east, a 2 minute drive) has plenty of shops as well as basic dining options. Note some of the dining options are located on the street behind the mall.
Quick drive to 6th Street via interstate - takes about 15-20 minutes outside of rush hour, less than 8 miles distance. Can also drive downtown without getting on interstate if desired, but adds 5-10 minutes to travel time.
Front desk staff very helpful and polite, particularly the tall slender woman in her 20s who processed our check in, who was positively effervescent and made us feel very welcome.

title: “A great affordable getaway into the big city”
text: The hotel and atmosphere were great, located in Times Square, close to the subway. Concierge was very helpful, staff was very nice. The rooms were clean and actually quit quiet for being in Times Square. Loved it and would def go back.

title: “Wonderful Hotel, Kind of Away from Everything”
text:
We stayed here for one week in October, 2012. I had no knowledge of this hotel, or input from anyone local. I only chose it by the on-line features and reviews I had read.
