We happened to stay here right in the middle of graduation for the USMC, so one morning, the breakfast area was full of people wearing red! It was truly an awesome sight for someone (me) who had no idea that was even happening in the area! The weather was something to be desired for being in California (just chilly), athough we were told it was HOT! HOT! HOT! right before we got there, and was forecasted to be HOT! HOT! HOT! the day we left!
Everything at this hotel was fabulous, including the front desk staff (who always greet you every time you walk through the door), the maintenance people, the housekeeping staff, etc. We were on the second floor, and it was a little noisy due to kids jumping up and down, running, etc., BUT... remember, this is a family hotel - and advertises as such with kids suites - so to those of you who complain about that ... shame on you! 
It is a little bit noisy if your window faces the pool, but again, it's a family hotel, and the pool closes at 10 p.m.
I would recommend this to anyone who isn't uptight and I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Tidy does not equal CLEAN - disgusting room and poor service”
text:
I was convinced to stay at this hotel because the price was reasonable and the reviews made it sound like a nice place to stay. I also thought the wyndham name had a good reputation. I was severely disappointed on many fronts and am shocked Wyndham considers this a value to its portfolio.
The hotel had a recent modernization by adding granite counter top and new brown paint. They also have LCD televisions. This does not make it a value. 
For those wanting the details that matter to your stay - skip to #3 below.
In summary: wear socks to walk on the floor, bring a sleeping bag so you don't have to sleep in the dirty sheets, wear flip-flops in the shower, use a toilet seat protector before sitting down.
Here are my disappointments:
1)The hotel advertises a 24hr shuttle. I called to confirm it would be available for the late time of my arrival. I called when I arrived and waited at the designated area. I waited for quite awhile and noted that no other passengers were at the terminal and I was the last passenger waiting for transport. This was disappointing as the hotel was immediately outside the airport property. I called and the man on the phone sounded shocked they handed come yet and assured me he would call and they would arrive soon. I waited .... and waited. Finally, an unrelated transport van stopped and said he felt bad because he had driven by several times and seen me waiting. He offered to give me a ride to the hotel even though it was not his job.
2) When I arrived at the hotel I anticipated an apologetic reception, but didn't even get acknowledge by the man at the front counter that I was standing in front of and staring at. He was too busy talking to his buddy about meeting him outside. The counter man didn't look up didn't look over but continued his conversation for a couple of minutes with his buddy. It wasn't until his friend left that he finally asked what I wanted. At this point I was really tired and had only about six hours left to get sleep before I needed to go back to the airport.
3) The hallway reeked of smoke beyond explanation. Luckily my room somehow didn't absorb the smell. I arrive at the room ready to sleep for a few hours. On first impression, the room appeared clean. However, the dark brown room and poor lighting was hiding a disgusting and unsavory room. First, there were long pubic hairs on top of the bed (yes, I have pictures of all of the items I will mention here). This made me concerned and got me looking to see if the room was clean. Next I notice the floor has a wad of used toilet paper on the floor, several large pieces of lint that vacuuming would have captured, red stains on my sheets, hair in the sink, mildew in the tub, mildew in the sink, heavy hard water stains on the bathroom fixtures, and dirty toilet. Each of these items are of the type that cleaning with bleach and a scrubber on a regular basis would easily have removed the filth. My impression is that the bathroom was cleaned with a heavily damp cloth that lacked any sort of cleaner or disinfectant. IT was obvious the toilet was not cleaned with a brush for quite awhile.
4) I was unable to get a quality nights sleep because I was worried about what else was on the sheets that I couldn't see. I slept in my clothes to avoid contact with the bed. Even a bargain hotel/motel should be cleaned with cleaner.
5) Upon waking up I put on my flip-flops to shower in the disgusting shower and found no shampoo or soap. 
6) The walls were very thin and I could here casual conversation of the rooms surrounding me.
I was very disappointed. I feel that any guest should be able to know that the room they are sleeping in is sanitary and clean and not just have a tidy look to hide the lack of cleaning. Failure to provide this for a guest ruins the nights sleep and makes any price paid for a room too much.

title: “Excellent location for an excellent price”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel for 4 days over July 4 weekend. We paid 70 dollars/night + tax for a room with a double bed and it was great value for the location. It is situated only a few blocks from Times square and very close to Fifth Ave., Empire State Building, Macy's. The staff at the hotel have been very nice (they are mostly Spanish) and made us feel very comfortable and welcome. The lobby of the hotel is situated on the second floor. The hotel has one tiny elevator (a slow one) that, for security reasons (not really needed but mostly to impress) stops at the second floor every single time so the attendant can see who is going upstairs. The main door downstairs is always locked and you can enter only after you are buzzed in by the attendant (security camera is another welcome security feature). 
Our room was exactly as seen in the Internet pictures. It was really small compared to most hotels, but this is NYC and for the location, we were ready to sacrifice the comfort of a bigger room. The windows are bolted and you cannot open them, but the AC is more than adequate in summer time. A slight inconvenience was the shared bathroom, but there was never really a time when we found it to be used by someone else. They have about 2-3 bathrooms per floor and they are quite clean. The cleaning ladies are very professional and you get towels, soap and a new roll of bathroom paper every day. There a sink in the room which comes in handily when you want to wash your hands or brush your teeth. Overall, the room is very clean and comes with 2 extra safety bolts aside the normal lock that opens with a hotel card (again to make you feel more secure). 
The hotel also has a small kitchenette with microwave and stove, but we never really used it because we mostly dined out. However, if you have a similar room as us and intend to eat in the room, you will have trouble finding a place to put the food. The only "table" is actually a dresser and you will share the surface with the TV (which by the way has mostly only local channels - no satellite). 
As other reviewers have mentioned before, our window was facing the 6th avenue and the noise was quite an "experience" during the night. Nevertheless, our busy days in NYC (shopping and sightseeing) made us too tired to be even bothered by the outside noise. There was a good PAX diner a block north of the hotel (besides Bryant Park) where we usually had our breakfast. On the last day, we had to check out before 12 noon, but since our bus was leaving at 9pm , we were able to leave all our bags safely in their baggage room. 
Since this was my first trip to NYC, I could say that Americana Inn is a good budget hotel with a great location. Their prices definitely allow you to save money and experience this amazing city.

title: “it's okay”
text: I was at this hotel as part of a tour and was a little concerned after having read some of the reviews. I was however pleasantly surprised the hotel room while a little small was clean warm and comfortable It was quite dark in the hallways and rooms there needs to be better lighting but I can’t complain about the room. The staff and the bar was very nice and well appreciated after long days of looking around New York. On my last night though I had major problem I had booked a wake up call first thing in the morning and double checked it again when I arrived back at the hotel which the staff had confirmed. However I never received it and ended up missing my train to Niagara falls and losing out on my pre-paid accommodation. (all up this missed wake up call costed me about $600aus). I received no apology and no real reason as to why the wake up call had been missed. Considering I had received all of my other wake up calls on time I was thoroughly frustrated as to why I never got this one. The hotel would have been great except for that major mistake.

title: “A few niggles, but generally good”
text:
If you can get this hotel through one of the discount sites, then it would definitely be worth it. Unfortunately, we paid full price which came in at around $3500 for two rooms for a week. We had asked for two rooms together, but were put on separate floors for the first night (first niggle). However, this was rectified the next day with a move of rooms. The rooms were spacious and clean and the beds very comfortable, although as has been stated in previous reviews, they could do with coffee / tea making facilities. The bathroom was also very clean, although the plug for the bath didn't work and was not sorted after we pointed this out (second niggle). The hotel is well appointed, but feels a bit impersonal, although having over 1000 rooms, perhaps this is to be expected. 
All the staff were approachable and friendly, with one exception. On moving to our new rooms on day two, we noticed that one of the televisions was damaged and reported this to the front desk. I later had a conversation with a member of staff who advised that all the TVs are checked daily, the suggestion being that we had damaged the TV and were trying to duck out of accepting responsibility for this (third and biggest niggle). However, after some further dialogue he seemed to accept that I wasn't lying to him.
The hotel is in a great location and I would recommend it. However, I don't feel that it is worth paying full price for.

title: “Great hotel, great location, but pricey”
text:
I can't understand how these "business" class hotels still survive. Parking was $57/night, Internet was between $10-$15/day and local calls were $1.00. The only restaurant was very expensive. 
There are so many "all-included" hotels (like Hampton, Embassy Suites, H/I Express), that why would anyone pay extra for these services?
Having said that, I stayed there for a conference. The hotel is very elegant, especially the lobby. Staff are very friendly and professional. The rooms are clean and well appointed, but nothing special.
You could park about 50m down the street for $32/day, but that does not include in/out privileges. So think wisely before you decide where to park.
Otherwise, very nice area, lots of fast food options right across the street.

title: “Good Value”
text: This place was a very good value. Great location, and John, the front desk person was very personable and helpful. I would reccomend this place.

title: “Best NYC Value in 25 Years”
text: I lived on E.10th in my youth and now travel to NYC often. Over the last 30 years,depending on my circumstances, I've stayed at over a dozen hotels between the Gramercy Park Hotel and The Mark, many recognized as 5 star and some less. I recently stayed two nights at The Benjamin and for the money it was as pleasant as any NYC hotel I'm familiar with. Location, for me, was perfect. The staff, from the front desk to housekeeping, was professional and friendly. The suite, similar size to $1500 suite on 57th or Columbus Circle, was clean and comfortable; plus it had a handy granite-toped kitchenette. I don't mean to imply that the space was uber-hip & high design but it was more than functional and a fifth the price of the famous NYC hotels. My expectations were greatly exceeded and unless I have money to burn I'll be returning to The Benjamin.

title: “I love this place!”
text: I stay here frequently for work for the past 10 years and everyone is so friendly here. When I'm here they treat me more like a friend than a guest. I always attend their priority club reception and it gives me a chance to meet other frequent travelers and I have met some great people. I recommend the Crown Plaza and I won't stay anywhere else.

title: “A perfect venue for a NYC weekend”
text: This is a very conveniently located and upscale hotel in midtown NYC. Friendly personnel, very clean facilities and quite large rooms by New York standards. Four of us had 2 Deluxe Double rooms and thoroughly enjoyed our 4 night stay.

title: “A quiet hotel near DuPont circle, but we have stated at much much nicer Kimpton hotels.”
text: Our expectations of the hotel were high and we looked forward to another fantastic Kimpton stay. We were disappointed in the cramped and uncomfortable lobby. A hefty price for use of the public computer was a shock. The room was nice and quite large, the beds comfortable, and the bathroom very nice. I recommend the hotel, but it is not the best Kimpton by quite a bit.

title: “very loud trains”
text: Besides being the noisiest hotel I've ever stayed at, the place was not up to even Comfort Inns standards. Definitly avoid staying on the railroad tract side of the hotel- it's amazing how often the trains go by.

title: “Very Nice”
text: The staff was wonderful and very helpful. I enjoyed my stay.The breakfast selection was good as well....

title: “Amazing value in a great location”
text:
The Americana Inn provides amazing value in a great location. It is less than 10 minutes walk from Penn Central station, and is very centrally located within New York City, only a few blocks from the Empire State Building.
I stayed two nights in September. The hotel was very clean. The office (on the 2nd floor) offers guests use of a safety deposit box to store valuables. There is a payphone in the 2nd floor lobby, as well as a drink vending machine and a single computer with paid internet access (either credit card or cash).
I was in a single room on the 5th floor, and there are a few things for prospective patrons to note to assist with their stay:
* The hotel has vinyl floors,
* The rooms do not have a coffee maker - but you are next door to Pret a Manger and there is also a great deli diagonally opposite,
* With shared bathrooms I would suggest bringing thongs (flip flops). As other guests have noted the bathrooms are very clean. There were at least 4 bathrooms on my floor. Unlike several other reviewers, I did experience one occasion when three of the bathrooms were being used - I think everyone wanted to have a shower at the same time!
* While a washbasin is provided in the room, there was nowhere to hang your towel (other than over the back of the chair),
* There was no lamp in the room, with all the lights controlled by a switch at the door. I would therefore suggest bringing a torch,
* While toiletries, towel and floormat are provided in your room for use in the shared bathroom. no facecloth was provided,
* There is no desk provided in the room, but the chest of drawers can double as a desk if needed,
* No iron or ironing board is provided in the room (I did not ask at the desk if one was available),
* No guest information is provided in the rooms, and
* The single lift can be very slow. I only used it to bring my luggage up to the 5th floor when arriving and back down when leaving and used the stairs for the rest of the time.
The above items are not meant as criticisms and did not detract from my stay. As several other guests have noted downtown New York is noisy at night, but after all it is the city that never sleeps (except seemingly at 7:00am when going out to get breakfast). I did not find the airconditioner particularly noisy even though it was mounted right above the bed head - it probably made less noise than my wall mounted unit at home!
The deli diagonally opposite made great bagels with cream cheese for breakfast. As noted above Pret a Manger is next door and adjacent to Pret a Manger is another deli. The souvenir shop around the corner (corner of 39th and 6th) sells stamps, and there is a post box right outside the shop.
The internet booking price of $145 per night (plus taxes) was excellent value for money for central New York, and I would definitely stay here again if visiting New York.
TC

title: “No free wifi”
text: I scored this hotel on Hotwire and was very surprised that for a $120 per night I still had to pay for wifi. I travel a lot with my job and this is one of the few hotels I stayed at that charged for wifi. It was $10 per day or $2.99 per hour. Other than this the. Hotel is beautiful and comfortable.

title: “Beware if you're looking for 2 beds”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for Spring Training 2004. Yes, this is a little tardy, but I just discovered the site, and, well, deep wounds heal slowly.
I reserved this hotel for my Father-in-law and I to attend spring training. This hotel served as home to the Oakland A's, and we thought it would be a nice opportunity to rub elbows with the players.
Overall, stay was nice, and the included breakfast was a benefit.
What soured us on the trip was that while I received a confirmed reservation for 2 beds, we were surprised that we found only one king bed in the room. When I complained to the front desk that I had reserved 2 beds, the assistant manager snootlily replied, "A confirmation is really just a request. You get what's available when you check in."
Fortunately, the hotel is suites, and the couch is a hide-a-bed, so we didn't have to share a bed, but frankly, I was rather irritated by the assistant manager's attitude, and the fact that I didn't get what I had reserved for.
Nice hotel, but frankly, I don't need attitude from hotel staff. I'll stay somewhere else. I wrote a letter of complaint, but got no response. Apparently, they don't care about repeat business.

title: “Nice Place in the Downtown”
text: The lobby is updated and relaxing, the rooms are large and comfortable, and they have access to a nice larger fitness center, in addition to a little one on site. The beds are comfortable and the staff is very friendly. The hotel also has a nice relaxed bar and happy hour snacks for free. All and all a nice place to stay.

title: “Awsome 4th of July experience”
text:
I stayed at the Embassy Suite Downtown Chicago for this past 4th of July holiday. My experience was wonderful! The manager's reception was great filled with a variety of cocktails and even a specialty drink was offered for the 4th of July! The cook to order breakfast was very good.... This is not my first time staying at the Embassy Suites but rather my first choice! Whenever I travel I like to do it in style! I am looking forward to returning to the Embassy property real soon! 
Tiffany Smith (Chicago IL)

title: “All the Basics”
text: I really like staying at Sheraton Suites (why aren't there more of them) when I need a no-frills, but decently appointed, spacious room. My family stayed at this hotel twice this summer for several days each time. Having the suite worked out well. On the second stay, we found the room had not been cleaned properly and the hotel relocated us to another room. Inconvenient, but they were accommodating. The bell staff was outstanding and timely in helping us with luggage. This hotel has an Omaha Steakhouse as its only restaurant. Not very inviting. We did not go, particularly with the Galleria and its surrounding restaurants and shops close by.

title: “Nothing special. Save your money”
text:
I'd never stayed at a Four Seasons before, but I had heard they were amazing. Maybe those high expectations were the problem. I am a fairly frequent traveler and usually stay at Marriott properties. I was expecting this to be a vastly better, luxurious experience. It was not. The rooms were average in every way and the service was very pedestrian. The one thing I requested from the staff was a mini-USB cable to sync my phone with my computer, but they couldn't provide this. They did offer me directions to a nearby Best Buy. This is the Four Seasons, come on!
My wife and I wanted to go to the Spa, so we called several days in advance and they only could accommodate one of us. Pretty disappointing.
By the standards of any hotel, The Four Seasons Austin is average. By luxury hotel standards it is poor. The place wasn't terrible, I would just say save your money and if you want a true luxury hotel experience, find somewhere else to have it.

title: “Staff Excellent”
text: I always feel like being at "home" when I stay at Hotel Commonwealth. The doormen and front desk staff welcome me by name. The bed was like heaven and of course the chocolate squares were my perfect dessert. Why would I want to stay anyplace else! Tim

title: “Loved Staying here :))))))))”
text: This Days Inn is less then 15 minutes form Ohio State University and we are from Pittsburgh. This is our second time staying here and we loved how clean, comfortable and quiet our room was both times. The free breakfast bar is good and the staff is wonderful. We will definitely be staying here again and again when we visit our son at OSU.

title: “Nice stay in Marriot”
text:
I find it beautiful, well designed. 
things that helps and attract your stay
1. clean rooms
2. Good Washrooms
3. Good elevators and escalators
4. The retaurant is so beautiful. Nice ambience. 
5. Ice Dispenser on all the corners of the galleries of the rooms (i find it very convenient)

title: “Good location, but not equal to the competition.”
text:
Situated in the heart of the city, and directly on the 16th Street Mall, it's hard to ask for a better location. Anything you want to do in downtown Denver is within walking distance; however, if being a pedestrian isn't your thing, the free "MallRide" shuttle bus stops right outside the hotel every few minutes. If tourism or the downtown nightlife are the main focus of your stay, then it's location alone makes the Sheraton an excellent choice.
However, the cost of the hotel should be a major factor when deciding to stay here. Among four-star hotels in the downtown area, the Sheraton comes up lacking when compared to other similar hotels nearby. If you can book it for a significantly cheaper than the competition, you might find it worthwhile; however, if it's only $20 or so per night that you'd be saving, you'd be much happier elsewhere.
The breakfast buffet was one of the low points - our hostess and our waiter both pushed the buffet on us a little forcefully, and even though it was a little cheaper than ordering directly from the menu, it wasn't worth it. Food selection at the buffet was extremely minimal, it seemed to be only minimally attended to, and with only a few dishes to feed the masses they were constantly running out of the main courses.

title: “OK stay!”
text: I stayed at the Dixie Hotel in Oct. The hotel was sooo cheap and we were on a budget. The hotel room is small but then again there were 4 women in one double bed room. The room was clean i must say! The beds were comfy and we had free wifi. Did not use the pool although it was clean. The parking space in front of our room was convenient also. There is a mini mall across the street and subway station nearby. i would stay again next time i visit LA if i cant afford anywhere else. was worth the little money we spent.

title: “Great Place, Great People”
text:
We traveled to Phoenix for a soccer tournament and stayed at this property and booked a three night stay. The staff of this hotel were amazing on so many levels. First, we drove to Phoenix from Denver so we could visit family in Santa Fe. We were delayed in Santa Fe and arrived in Phoenix at 3 am on Friday morning. When we received our bill Sunday morning they had only charged us for two nights. I went to the front desk to let them know we were "under-charged" and discovered that because we had arrived so late they just put us down as a "very" early check-in. Second, my son was injured during the tournament and we needed to make an ice bag which they were extrememly accomodating. Thirdly, the breakfast was great and the person that runs their breakfast was very accomodating of a team with 15 twelve-year-old boys.
I have a client in Chandler and any time I need to visit I will stay at this property! Huge kudos to the staff of this hotel!

title: “Price and location make it a good place to stay”
text: Visited Chicago from Cleveland with a group of friends. We stayed at the Red Roof 5/08-5/10/2008. The hotel was ok. The rooms could use some updating or maybe a good scrubbing. We had a corner room and a wonderful view. Our group was all on the same floor. The shower was clogged, called the front desk and they had someone to my room within a couple of minutes and it was fixed. The staff was friendly and helpful. There is good coffee in the lobby. The price for this hotel makes this a good option if you don't want to spend a fortune but want to stay in great location.

title: “Great Location”
text: Very nice hotel within walking distance of the Convention Center. Has everything you need for a comfortable stay - clean and well appointed. The staff was very helpful and knowledgeable. We will definitely stay here again when business brings us back to Washington.

title: “A Pleasant Surprise!”
text:
What a nice surprise. I had booked this hotel through [----] with a bit of apprehension given some of the reviews but got a good price and decided to chance it. I'm glad I did. The hotel is conveniently located :2 blks from the Blue Line, 2 blocks from the Red Line, and 2 blocks from the elevated loop trains. It was easy to get to from O'Hare, and we never had to take a cab anywhere we wanted to go. It's located across from the Public Library (the gargoyles on the roof of the library made it easy to re-orient yourself when you got off the subway) near the Publisher Row section of Downtown in a failry quiet area. There is not a lot of restaurants or clubs in the area but you can easily head to other parts of the loop to find what you want.
The room was large compared to most Chicago hotels, nicely decorated with a WONDERFULLY comfortable bed! The marble bathroom was large with a large step in shower with great water pressure, hot water, and a "rain shower " shower head, so I didn't miss not having a tub at all. The free wireless internet was a plus. If there was one thing that kept this hotel from being perfect it was that housekeeping did not do our room until late in the afternoon. The room was immaculate as was the bathroom both upon arrival and throughout our stay. 
We did not eat at the Custom House (the restaurant on-site) but saw a lot of locals coming and going at dinner time, which I take as an endorsement. The pizza restaurant across the street is good, and we also stumbled upon the Plymouth Restaurant 2 blooks away. It's casual, not much to look at but with great prices, large and varied menu, and good food and open for breakfast through dinner. My steak dinner with fresh steamed veggies, baked potato and greek salad was $15! 
After having stayed at the W, the Chicago Hitlon, The Swissotel, and Hotel Allegro this is now at the top of our list. The front desk staff was professional, no problems with elebators, our room was on the 4th floor and quiet other than the customary morning traffic noise you'd expect to hear in a downtown hotel in a city of this size. The Hotel Blake has now moved to the top of our list.

title: “Great find!”
text: Stayed one night at the Hotel Griffon. Kevin at the front desk was cheerful and helpful. Room was great. Perry's was fun. Overall great time and will go back. The only bummer was that when we got our car out of valet, it had a scratch (tiny, but still a scratch and didn't notice it until we were already at the gas station heading out of town). This is why a I personnally hate valet parking. Oh well, but things do happen in life.

title: “Great Hotel in Seattle”
text: Great hotel that is a bit away from the noise of downtown seattle. We stayed in a queen, queen deluxe room which was perfect for our family of 3. There was a sofa bed in the room so we all had a bed. The bathroom was rather small, but okay for us. Clean, comfortable , quiet room overlooking some trees . The weather was wonderful and our windows opened which was very nice to have. Beds were extra comfortable. They had coffee in the morning and a wine tasting in the evening which was really nice. The staff directed us to a really good steak house nearby. We walked down to the harbor area and enjoyed every minute. It is a pet friendly hotel (so many are) and they put us on the upper floor as it was a "no pet" room. Room was WONDERFUL and everyone helpful and friendly. We had breakfast in their restaurant food and the atmosphere was very, very nice.Remember most all hotels charge to park downtown. Seattle is a great city and we will be back to stay at this hotel.

title: “Nice choice in San Francisco”
text:
We arrived at the Hotel Monaco late on a Wednesday night after a long drive from LA - check in was super quick and easy and the service felt genuine. My initial gripe or rather, my only gripe at all was the highly priced valet parking - over $100 for 2 nights. Yes, there are local parks nearby but we wanted our stay to be practical and hassle free but you do pay for it here. However wireless was free and super quick which was a great plus.
Hotel location is great - and as long as your not easily offended by the masses of homeless/beggars you'll be fine. During the day they are not as prevalent but standing outside the hotel at night on the second evening we encountered 10 begs for money in as many minutes. I assume it is the same all over SF though.
Within 5 minutes, your at Union Square - and we decided to walk down to the ferry port through the Financial District which took around 45 minutes but was very pleasant and a great way to see the city. 
The rooms although small (three rooms and all very inconsistent sizes - must be luck of the draw!) were immaculate and the beds were super comfortable. The bathroom and amenities were fabulous and the leopard print bathrobes were cute.
We didn't eat here or use the spa facilities as they closed at 9 p.m however the lobby, seating areas around the hotel were lovely and the complimentary tea/coffee and wine hour are a really considered touch.

title: “I will never stay here again...”
text: The room was just average but definately wasn't worth the $89.95...and to top that off my car got broken into during the night and the hotel personel weren't trying to help me with anything. They barely gave me a bag to put the broken glass into...I will never stay at this hotel again!!!!

title: “Best Location, but...”
text: Upon check in after 3pm, our room was not ready. Really? Why did I prepay for the room? Instead, we were offered a handicap room. The clerk was making it sound like it would be an upgrade by saying it was much larger. We were so tired after our 5 hour drive so we agreed. When we got the room, the nice bellman couldn't open the door. He was frankly embarrassed as he asked us to go back to the front desk with him. Another clerk put us in another room immediately. The bellman tells us "well this is a better room anyway...the handicap room faced a wall and this one faces Michigan Ave." Why were we not offered this room with a view in the first place? How did this room "magically" become available? Why was this room not offered to us from the beginning? We also had an issue with the $59 valet parking service. While enjoying my morning coffee at the hotel Starbucks, I noticed our car sitting just outside the valet service door. I immediately inquire the valet person in charge. He insists we called for pick up. He argued with me saying we called even after I kept repeating WE DID not call!! They park the car again and when we actually were ready to leave, they could not find our key!! All of a sudden on of the guys that park the cars shows up and says he will go get our car (he must have recognized us from earlier). When he arrived with our car, he did tell us it was their mistake and he believed me that we did not call. They got it mixed up. Finally! Someone was taking responsibility...but why did it have to be him and not the person I charge? I gave him a tip for at least clearing the air. Honestly, the hotel itself is nice and location is the best, but this was our first trip to Chicago and first stay at Westin and we were disapponted in the lack of customer service. Will we stay there again? Probably not....for the price of a room there, there were so many other hotels in the area to choose from.

title: “Wow! Very nice rooms and a great location.”
text: Like the last reviewer, my wife and I booked our room through Priceline for $70-75 a night and luckily got the Hilton Financial District Hotel. I was immediately impressed with our room, seeing the flat screen TV sitting on the desk that extended wall to wall in front of the window that offered a great view to the North. I love the beds at Hilton's as well. This location is very handy to Chinatown (a block or two up the street is the main drag). The TransAmerica Pyramid is practically next door to the East. Coit Tower is an easy walk up some seriously step sidewalks. North Beach is close by as well. Great location, great rooms, a nice hotel bar area, and friendly staff make the Hilton a great place to stay. I would love to stay there again. The parking comes to $47 a day. Just a little side note. But if you get your room through Priceline, who cares about the parking.

title: “broken and smoke”
text: As I arrived at the LaQuinta on my first trip to New York I already had a bad taste in my mouth because when I had called to confirm the reservations I had been told that I would need to pay a different amount for the hotel than I had originally been quoted. Granted, the hotel was a nice building, but the staff was not helpful at all. Also, the famous elevator that I have read about that has been broken is still broken. During my stay the one working elevator only worked approximately twice during my stay of four nights. Also, because I am allergic to smoke I had made certain that I had a non-smoking room and it was a smoking room when I checked in...when I spoke to the staff they were not helpful in switching rooms for me. Yes, the LaQuinta was priced well, but I would definately pick again if I was doing my trip over. As I walked around New York I saw many more hotels that were priced at the same level that I wished I had stayed at. Beware of the LaQuinta unless you want to tolerate broken elevators, rude staff, and a smoky room!

title: “Failure on many counts”
text:
I'll be honest, this is probably the first and last time I'm writing a review. The Hyatt McCormick Place has moved me enough to do so. They've got a monopoly on the convention center and they know it. Prices are exorbitant and what you get for it is sorely lacking. The rooms are a completely disgrace to any Hyatt. Twice I've stayed here and twice the sheets in a new room showed stains. They were fresh sheets all pressed and tight but there were brown stains on the edges. The bathrooms are quite the joke, a cube like relic from the 90s that can barely fit a toilet let alone a bath. The shower lets out a high pitched whine every time you turn it on and the shower curtains aren't long enough to cover the entire bath and you almost always end up with a wet bathroom floor. The vanity fixtures are dated and barely functional. Even the closet is just a curtain drawn across a small cutout space. 
The absolute worst part is the noise. The walls are paper thin. You here both adjacent rooms at the same time. It's not just a dull muffle, its full on conversations and even cell phones on vibrate. That is just downright ridiculous. Whenever a door shuts 5 rooms away, you get jolted up in the middle of the night. I'm not a light sleeper but this hotel design is a joke. And by the way, you can pay an upcharge for fridge in your room. Seriously???
Unless you absolutely have no choice or just like to suffer, stay far far away from this dump. Great service staff though. Nice, polite and almost apologetic knowing that you got suckered.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: Have stayed here several times while in Chicago. We won't stay anywhere else. Large rooms with huge windows. We always get a room on the side facing the the Wrigley Building with the clock tower that is lit up at night....beautiful! Breakfast is included daily, which has a nice variety of foods. I know they're are alot of great restaurants in Chicago, but on Mon-Th the hotel includes a light dinner and sometimes it is just nice to grab a bite there instead of looking for a place to eat. It is expecially nice on the day that you come in to town to have dinner all set and not have to think about what and where you're going to eat. Since the rooms have a small kitchen, we like to run over to the grocery store, Jewel Osco and pick up just a few things in case we want to make a quick snack during our stay. This hotel, in my opinion is in the best location....a couple blocks from Michigan Ave, Rush St, State....close to Red Line. Love it! Can't wait to go back again.

title: “DuPont is DuPlace!”
text:
We arrived at the front desk with four of us -- two adults and two teenage kids to find out that our single room with a king bed wouldn't accommodate a roll-away. The young lady at the front desk looked puzzled briefly, but then very courteously said "let me see what I can do here" and managed to get us a room with twin double beds -- perfect! It saved me from having to get two rooms and we have a great view of the DuPont Circle Park.
Room service is pricey, but the food is quite good and the service is excellent. The rooms are nice appointed and very clean, but quite small. It's a bit tight with four of us, but not unexpected given the locale and desirability of this area. The decor is modern but not sparse like you might find in a European hotel. The fixtures are bold but with muted colors - they fit the decor and add to the ambience. 
The vibe that we get here is that there are "big things" going on -- the clientele are well dressed and appear to be quite driven. I must admit that I accidentally eavesdropped on some nearby visitors and found the conversation interesting! It sounded like they had some aggressive growth plans for their business.
The DuPont Circle Metro stop is a couple of blocks away and there are plenty of places to get a bite to eat or a snack/coffee/tea along the streets surrounding this hotel. It's just a few stops in any direction to get to the better attractions in DC. We like the location.
The restaurants span the price spectrum from $, $$, to $$$. I personally liked the looks of ShopHouse Asian Cafe - I'm headed there tomorrow and I'll review it after I test it out.
Internet service is complimentary and the connection is solid. 
Overall, the experience has been great and we would certainly both recommend this hotel as well as visit again on a future stop in DC.
Happy Travels!

title: “Lovely Stay at Menger Hotel”
text:
We just returned from a 5 night stay at the Menger Hotel. It was lovely. I had previously stayed at the Menger with my father (who is now deceased), so staying at the Menger brought back some great memories for me. Over the past twenty years, I have also stayed at the Grand Hyatt, Rio Del Palacio and other newer hotels in the area. For me, the Menger has the premier location (you can never get lost) and an incredible history (Robert E. Lee rode his horse right into the lobby!) It has, after all, been in operation since the 1850's. Checkin at the front desk was seamless. We stayed in room 5133 (the newer section), a very spacious room with a large patio overlooking the pool. It was wonderful to sit on the large patio each night to watch the sun set or in the morning to drink my coffee. The beds were very comfortable and had luxury linens. The mattresses were very clean and looked new. The bathroom was clean but showing signs of age/wear and the water temperature fluctuated. The housekeeping staff was very attentive, cleaning the bathroom as requested and supplying fresh towels when requested. We enjoyed strolling through the Victorian lobby. (Note: There is a cigar shop in the hotel and you will smell cigars in this area!) The pool area is beautifully landscaped and large. We didn't feel crowded and there was plenty of room to swim, unlike another newer luxury property with a tiny rooftop pool we stayed in two years ago. The pool closes around 8 or 9, so there is no late night noise or parties. My sons especially enjoyed swimming there. Don't overlook the hotel restaurant, the Colonial Room! My sons were served a HUGE and delicious children's breakfast for a mere $2.95! We took our breakfast each morning in the stunningly beautiful garden where the writer Oscar Wilde strolled with his spiked lemonade. The restaurant staff absolutely spoiled us! Instead of braving the crush of people on the Riverwalk, the slow service we received at Shilo's and the non-kid friendly atmosphere of Boudro's, we opted to eat at the Colonial Room. My salmon filet was perfection, and the service was impeccable. The hotel gave us a 20% discount card to use there. Don't forget to have some mango ice cream while you are there. It is a special treat not to be missed!! (You'll see a picture of Bill Clinton eating this ice cream at the restaurant entrance.) The last night of our stay, the Sisters Grimm brought in a large group for dinner and a ghost tour. We enjoyed hearing some tantalizing ghost stories from other hotel guests. They were staying at the Menger Hotel after experiencing ghosts on the 7th floor of the Crockett. Very intriguing. 
To sum it up, if you want a new hotel with the latest and greatest, stay elsewhere. If you request a room facing the pool with a patio and you understand that this hotel has been operating since the 1850's (It can be a little quirky), you'll enjoy a very unique hotel stay. The valets were friendly and helpful, the restaurant staff spoiled us and housekeeping was attentive to our requests. To top it off, I accumulated lots of STASH reward points (a reward program for independent hotels. The points never expire!). I give the Menger a 4. If the bathrooms were updated with new fixtures, etc., I would definitely give it a 5. The Menger Hotel staff spoiled us in every way possible! Today, my 9 year old son said, "I miss the Menger, mom."

title: “Impressed with The Independent”
text:
I visited the hotel for a brief stay with a group of friends while seeing a couple of baseball games at the outstanding ballpark in Philly. 
We had two rooms, both on the 2nd floor. We were greeted warmly by Gida, whom I had messaged with prior to our stay, and she had all our requests covered at the time of check-in.
Both rooms had very high, loft like, ceilings. One bathroom had floor to ceiling windows with lovely, exposed brick interior walls. Overall, very comfortable surroundings.
Our only issue was with the room temperature controls. After coming back from an extra long baseball game, we couldn't seem to cool our rooms down... the a/c seemed to be out of our control. It took a while, but the clerk at reception was able to help us cool down the rooms by a using a control via their phone system. I have never stayed in a room before where the wall thermostat does not control the a/c, rather the phone console. 
Anyway, once the problem was addressed, we had a splendid stay at the hotel. 
We used their parking lot which was convenient to the hotel and gave us in/out access for a $15 daily fee. 
I hope to visit this hotel again if I'm in Philly in the future.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: Nice hotel but need car because there is nothing in walking distance (restaurants, liquor store, groceries etc) There is shuttle service to major attractions but no service for the airport. Very nice and helpful staff. Excellent restaurant in the hotel.

title: “Great Location, clean hotel, free parking”
text: Great Location, you can take the bus to Fishermen's Warft or you could even walk. Close to cable car station, some nice restaurants around, would definitly recommend Peter D's for breakfast, it is just around the corner, 2 minutes walk. Parking is free, which is a great plus in SF. We had a clean an quiet hotel room, with fridge and microwave, so we could keep and warm up our toddlers food. Staff is friendly and helpful in giving directions. We even extended our stay for another night. Would definitly recommend this hotel and would stay again there.

title: “Fantastic home base in San Francisco!”
text:
I have stayed at many SF hotels and choose the W for this trip as I wanted to be in the SOMA district. From start to finish my stay was superb.
I arrived on an early flight and got to the hotel at 11:00 AM. Rather than take a cab I used the BART this time from SFO. It took about 30 minutes, cost $5.15 and if you get off at the Montgomery station it's only about 2 blocks to the hotel. Even though I arrived early it was still no problem getting a room right away and I was placed in an amazing Bay view room on the 25th floor.
The room was typical for a W although it was fairly large. The list of amenities in the room was substantial. Bliss bathroom products, teeth whitening kits, mini stereo with Sirius satellite radio, big TV, big work desk, very comfortable window seats and fantastic in room coffee to name just a few. The room was spotless and also very quiet.
For other reviewers who mention the price of parking or mini bar items, this is simply true to any hotel in the prominent locations of a big city like SF. As I walked around the area I noticed all hotels were posting $40 parking.
For breakfast each day they set up an amazing spread in XYZ. Each morning I would grab a jumbo muffin and some fresh fruit for only $5, a bargain for hotel prices, and then make coffee in my room and enjoy reading the paper while being distracted by the beautiful view.
The W has a very nice feel to it, extremely comfortable and friendly. On my last day there I needed the business center which happened to be closed as it was MLK day. No problem at all, the front desk sent someone with me to unlock it and give me access within 2 minutes of my request and then they didn't even charge me! All the staff were professional, friendly and more than willing to help out. I have found my favorite hotel in the great city of SF and will look no more the next time I return.

title: “Very Good NYC hotel-Very clean great location”
text:
Stayed here this past weekend. The hotel was very good. The check in process was great, they automatically upgraded me to a deluxe room (which was on a higher floor).
Got free breakfast coupons for myself and the family and let me tell you, the breakfast at the restaurant next door (Pigalle) was really great. Fresh fruit, eggs, egg whites, hard boiled eggs, french toast, waffles, AND pancakes. Muffins, oatmeal.. etc etc etc. Very fresh and pretty well prepared. Probably the best hotel buffet I have had in all my travels. Cute restaurant. We were very happy with this.
The discounted parking for my minivan was $30 a night, great stuff.
The rooms. Pretty standard HGI rooms, being NYC these rooms were small and cramped, but getting 2 queens was a plus. Hotel staff all were very friendly.
Beds were cheap and uncomfortable and the bathroom shower smelled a bit mildewy, but not too bad. Safe and fridge in room were great. 
Pretty standard HGI offering which is exactly what I wanted. Did a thorough bedbug check and the room was pretty clean.
Even on the 11th floor you can feel the subway rumble under the building, but it wasn't too distracting. You can still hear a bit of street noise. Get as high a floor as possible to lessen the problems.
Great stay, would definitely stay here again.
Thank you to the great woman who checked us in and hooked us up with breakfast and waters. The Breakfast was icing on the cake for us.
Oh yeah, great location, 2 blocks from the madness of times square and a 10 minute walk to central park or bryant park. Good stuff!

title: “Mid town and in the middle of it all - a place to rest”
text:
Great Westin Style...in the middle of the hubbub..just opposite the Port Authority Bus station, a block from Times Sq. perfect oasis of corporate comfort in the city's heart. Upper floor rooms with a city view are perfect - quiet with a view! 
heavenly beds and simple showers...can't go wrong.

title: “Good but only a little problem”
text: We stayed here for two nights walking into the room felt great very cold air conditioner, the bed was so comfortable it was a king size bed with balcony to the riverwalk with two chairs outside, the room was clean and spacious, The bathroom is big and the shower head has different settings the only problem was the first night we had a little pet in the bathroom a little cockroach running around besides that our stay was very good. Easy access to the riverwalk, Parking garage is big and elevators in every floor. It was a little confusing the first time because you have to take one elevator from the parking garage to the hotel then they have 3 more elevators one of the only to floors 23 and higher the rest for floors below 23. I would stay here agian

title: “I love Kimpton!”
text:
Stayed here while at a conference and loved it! My room was awesome- so comfy! It also had 2 little window seats looking at the river! Also loved the sangria at happy hour. The location was great- easy to walk anywhere.
The restaurant was just okay and recommendations from the concierge were so so. But if you do your restaurant reviews before you go, this will be a perfect stay!
Everyone was super nice and helpful. I can't say one negative thing about this hotel and that's saying a lot!

title: “Perfect for Business Travelers!”
text: This is a business class hotel, so you don't deal with kiddos much, which is nice. Decor is contemporary throughout the hotel, and all was in great repair & very clean. Guest rooms are spacious with a generously sized living area and bar/fridge/coffee area, and a nice desk/table arrangement. There is a nice assortment of coffee & hot teas in-suite. The beds were very comfortable, countertops are granite, the drawers were spacious, there are plenty of big mirrors, including two full-lengths directly across from each other (check the back of your hair, ladies!). There is a very large TV mounted to be easily viewable from both the bedroom & living area, which are separted by a partial wall. In contrast to most hotels of this type, there is 24 hr. room service (it's not gourmet, but you're not paying gourmet prices, either!). Downstairs they have snacks, sodas, sandwiches & salads that you can purchase when you'd like. Complimentary breakfast with various cut fruit, whole fruit, bagels, hard-boiled eggs, mini-pastries, coffee, juice (think I got it all) is available in the mornings, and they also cook your breakfast to order (for a charge, posted on a blackboard). The downstairs bar is open 'til midnight every night, serving wine, beer & basic mixed drinks with complimentary crunchy snack mix. Outdoors, they have a pool (no hot tub in this hotel). This hotel is in the same class as Aloft, and I think it blows Aloft out of the water on all fronts. Staff members are friendly, welcoming, knowledgeable, and accommodating. The ONLY thing I can think of to recommend is that they have nothing for a vegan to eat. Vegetarians have cheese pizza, salad, or tomato bisque that I saw. Overall, would heartily recommend this hotel!

title: “Money's worth”
text: I stayed at the Belleclaire in the end of June, and was pleasantly surprised. I wasn't quite sure what I'd be getting before I got there, but it was more than I had hoped for. My room, along with one other was closed off from the rest of the rooms on our floor, by a door that we could open with our card key. Travelling alone, I thought this was a nice security measure. I shared a bathroom with the people in the other room, but I never found it to be occupied when I needed it, which was nice. The a/c was working and kept the room at a nice temperature, there's a big walk-in closet with ironing board other necessities, and though it didn't have a mini-bar, there's a small fridge where you can put food and drinks you buy yourself. There's no breakfast served at the hotel (except through room-service), but the Manhattan Diner across the street had some wonderful food for a very good price. The staff was very friendly and helpful, especially the people in the giftshop. They can get guests in to the Comedy Club on 78th and Broadway for free. Great place. Also if you're going to a concert at the Beacon theatre, that's only a couple of blocks north from the hotel. Lots of little shops in the neighborhood, Filene's Basement is down by the subway station on 77th and Broadway, and that subway can take you directly to Times Square, Empire State Building and docks for Statue of Liberty and and bay cruise.

title: “Large Room”
text:
I had a wonderful stay at the Hilton in March 2012. The hotel is clean, the staff is helpful and courteous, the room was huge, the location is walking distance to the convention center and very importantly Steak 'N Shake.
My suite had 2 queen size beds and in a second room a pull out love seat, desk and second TV. I traveled for business by myself, but several people could fit comfortably in the room.
I took the green line to and from the airport which worked out great. The shuttle stop is just across the street from the Hilton. 
Downtown Indianapolis is not big. The location of the hotel made it easy to walk anywhere. 
I wish there was free WiFi in the rooms, but there is in the lobby and at Panera down the street.
I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Everything was great except one bad apple”
text:
We stayed here after a long drive from NC and some touring around CO to meet my husband who was flying in. At check-in there was an issue with my reservation. The young man at the front desk, Drew, was being very kind, polite and helpful. He needed support from his supervisor to fix my problem, and the situation took a disappointing turn. The supervisor, Dustin was rude and condescending. He cut me off mid sentence and made me feel like I had done something wrong when in fact it was one of his staff who had made the mistake by giving me incorrect information on the phone earlier that day. He did this right in front of my kids and other guests who were waiting to check in. I came back down later to speak to him directly, but he was not available, and I did not see him for the rest of our stay. I did get an opportunity to commend Drew, and during my time there, I saw that he works hard to take good care of the guests consistently. He is a gem. 
Otherwise, the room was clean and comfy, and everyone else was delightful. The breakfast was a predictable hot breakfast with disappointing previously frozen omelets, but I have learned that is what you get at a mid-range hotel.

title: “What a dump”
text: I spent a week in this hotel in June and would have moved out immediately if I was able to find anywhere else to stay. The entire hotel and corridors smell mouldy. When checking my room on the final day, I peeked under the bed to make sure nothing had been left behind. I found that I had been sharing my accomodation with a pile of used condoms. They were not mine, and had therefore been there all week. I reported my disgust to the management but the entire response was a mumbled appology. I would never ever recommend this hotel or stay there again.

title: “A Nice Place to Stay”
text:
I've stayed here many times, and it's always been a pleasant experience. The rooms are nice, clean, modern, and cheerful. It's very convenient to the airport. They even have a shuttle that can pick you up if you like. The shuttle will also take you to a nearby restaurant if they are not too busy serving the airport clients. 
It's a good place to stay if your business in Austin is close to the airport. If not, it's pretty far away from downtown.

title: “Not the experience advertsied”
text:
Stayed at Fashion 26 for seven nights in May. Arrived on the official opening night which was definately not the best introduction to the hotel but one that set the scene for the remainder of the stay - appearances are more important than service. 
There are a number of reasons why our stay at this hotel was disappointing:
* On arrival no introduction to the hotel was provided - due to the fact the official opening party was being held in the lobby and it was impossible to hear the receptionist. There is no hotel information compendium in the room either.
* Advertised and highly promoted turn down service was provided on three out of the seven nights we stayed at the hotel.
* Servicing of the room was very poor - first night our beds were not made, the duvet was just pulled up over the crumpled sheets. Used glasses were removed and then not replaced. Only one robe was provided.
To be fair we did contact the Manager on our second night to discuss our issues and she was very helpful and apologetic - we received turn down service the following two nights and then not again during our stay.
When you stay at a hotel for seven nights it becomes your home away from home and particularly when you are in an unfamiliar city thousands of miles from home it is your refuge. Unfortunately Fashion 26 was often more combatative than homely - it's not nice having to constantly ring and ask for towels, glasses, turn down etc - and we came away very disappointed with the whole experience

title: “Beautiful rooms what happened to the service??”
text:
Booked a destination package with this hotel for my mother, sister, and 19 year old daughter for a Saturday night getaway. Being aware that my 19 year old daughter would not be able to gamble I made reservations for us to enjoy a nice dinner at Bourbon Steak. 
Problem started with the check-in process. Even though we were paying cash for our stay, the hotel "supervisor" demanded a 200.00 credut card deposit that you are not informed of until arrival or else you could leave. This policy was never mentioned during reservations. I was told that my credit card would not be billed but used as a way to "hold" the room as most hotels do.
Driving from Ohio through major construction my family and I decided to stay with much hesitation after the way we were treated by the "supervisor". After getting settled in to the gorgeous hotel room my daughter and I decided to go check out the hotel while the others went to gamble.
Here we run into another problem. We find out that Bourbon Steak, the restaurant I made reservations for weeks in advance, was located inside the casino! Therefore, my 19 year old daughter was not allowed to dine there. Out of four restaurants within the hotel only one was accessible for my teenage daughter.
After speaking to the "supervisor" for the second time her ONLY option was to check my family and I out of the hotel and refund our money, without any apology for lack of information during reservations.
With bags in hand and a 25 minute wait for our vehicle to be pulled up by valet, we spent well over an hour looking for a hotel to accomodate us.
Needless to say I will never stay nor will I recommend the MGM Grand Detroit to ANYONE! Not even my worst enemy.

title: “Would Definitely Recommend This Hotel!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at the Rockefeller Center Hotel from October 12, 2006 - October 16, 2006. We had a wonderful time in New York City, and this hotel helped to make our vacation a very positive and fun experience.
The location is excellent. You are right by Rockefeller Center and about a one minute walk from the skating rink and the plaza where the Today Show films. Times Square and the Theatre District are short walks away. You are also close to subway stations which are very convenient for visiting other areas of the city.
Check-in and check-out were very easy. You have to option of checking in or out yourself at the self service kiosks. We checked in with a hotel employee, who was very nice. The process took only a minute or two. We used to kiosk to check ourselves out at the end of our stay - it was very simple and your statement prints out at the kiosk for you. 
The lobby is small as people have mentioned, but it does exactly what it's supposed to do. It is nicely decorated, as is the rest of this brand new hotel. The elevators require you to swipe your room card before accessing any floors - I found this to be a reassuring security measure. One downside is that the staff and guests use the same elevators, which I didn't find to be a big deal but some people may not enjoy sharing the ride with towels or cleaning supplies. 
Our room (509) was fairly large by NYC standards and had a LCD TV (small but nice, and mounted above the desk, which had ample space to work if desired), two nightstands and an open closet area with two drawers. I had to use a nightstand drawer for the rest of my clothes but we ended up having plenty of space. Noise level was very minimal and we found the full size bed to be pretty comfortable.
Our room was a handicapped room, which may have accounted for its larger size. Our bathroom was large to accommodate a wheelchair. The only downside of this was that the shower area was just a curtained off area of the floor, with no ledge to separate the rest of the bathroom. The result was a lot of water on the floor but a few towels solved this problem.
Housekeeping was excellent and cleaned our room everyday after we left, often in the afternoon. They were very respectful of the "Privacy Please" sign we hung outside the door and never disturbed us. On our last night, our maid left a note thanking us for her tips. I found this to be a nice touch - you often don't see these people but it reminded us that they are always working hard to make sure your stay is as comfortable as possible. 
The staff was helpful when we asked for restaurant and store suggestions or locations. When I requested two extra pillows, they were brought up within 5 minutes.
We did not use room service but did order from one of the local deli's in the area that deliver to the hotel (there are menus in the room listing restaurants in the area that deliver to the hotel - the hotel charges an additional $2.50 service fee for this). The hotel staff brought the meal up to our room and just charged our room account. It was very convenient. The food was tasty and warm (soup, a hamburger, a grilled chicken sandwich and fries, our total bill was $34.55 with the hotel service charge. Pricey but worth it for good food if you don't want to go out). 
All rooms have free high-speed internet. You will be able to hook up a laptop to the TV monitor, although this was not yet available when we stayed. There is also a small gym – which we did not use but did walk by. There are all new machines and weights. The hotel will also bring you an “in-room” gym for your convenience. 
This hotel is in an excellent location but it does get quite quiet at night since there are many businesses in the area that close. We never felt unsafe walking in the area at night and there are plenty of restaurants and bars just a short distance from the hotel.
I highly recommend this hotel. Although it just recently opened and is not quite near completion (we noticed some stairwells are still unpainted and the restaurant is not yet open) this hotel offers stylish, comfortable rooms in a great location.

title: “All paid up but they took $250 off my credit card 3 months later”
text:
Having initially booked in for three nights via the Expedia website, we stayed for 9 nights in total costing in excess of $2000.00.
In all a lovely experience BUT 3 months later the Boston sheraton debited my credit card for some $250.00. I queried this with the hotel, they said it was probably because Expedia didnt pay them for the full three nights but they really didnt know. In the end because I couldnt demonstrate that I didnt owe them the money and they couldnt show that I did they decided the debit had to stand.
This was our honeymoon. The hotel is nice and the chambermaids and bar staff absolutely lovely but dont bother with the buffet breakfast, total rip off ($40 odd dollars for a fruit salad with yoghurt).

title: “Fair price - I think”
text:
For the price it is not so bad at all. the room (819) was little bit smelly perhaps. But big TV, Nice bed.. and so on.. Check in and check out went smooth. They ordered a taxi for my to the airport, - "a very reliable guy that we always use". But he never showd up...But cannot really blame the hotel for that.. 
I do sincerely hate shower curtains! It cannot cost that much to install some glass door? 
It also scared me a bit that my "sitrus chicken breast" was served less than 10 minutes after I ordered it. Felt like the chef just had heated up some ready made stuff. 
All in all.. good, and I probably go back several times. 
BIG PLUS: They have "free(ish)" shuttle to the galleria!

title: “Hotel of elegant stature”
text: This fine hotel feels historic and elegant. Wonderful location in midtown Manhatttan. Quality staff, stately rooms, good bar and restaurant. The Warwick makes for a fine visit to New York.

title: “This is no 4 star resort”
text:
I had booked this resort 3 months prior to our stay. The entire family was looking forward to this vacation. The web page for the resort was breathtaking. It made it seem like we would be on a tropical island. As we drove up the drive way it seems tropical. But as we pulled up to the lobby there was no bell man to help with the luggage. That should have been the first clue that this was not a 4 star resort. I walked into the lobby while my husband waited in the car with our kids. The lobby was small and looked a little out dated (clue number two). The gentleman at the front desk told me that we would be charged $25.00 a night for parking, that we had not been told at the time of booking. And if I wanted to park for free that it would be a 15 minute walk outside of the resort grounds. Once we had been given our room number we got back into our car and headed out to find our room. As we drove around we noticed the flat roof style huts with one door but two room numbers. They don't show you this at all on the web page (clue number three). At this point we don't like what we saw but hoped that the inside of the room would make up for the exterior of the buildings. We open the door to our hut and notice two more doors. One to our room and that of another room in the small hallway that connected us, the foor was discustingly dirty. It looked like it hadn't been swept in weeks. Cobwebs all along the walls with dead bugs in them. Once we walked into our room the smell of mold over powered us!! The beds where new with nice headboards and a new flat screen TV, but that couldn't block the smell out. The shower head was rusted and half falling out. All along the tub we could see the mold, crack and rust. The tropical view from our room was one of a fence with dried out plants that gave us a view of the busy street outside the resort.
I couldn't believe this was the same resort I had seen on the web. I felt robbed and cheated. Who rated this place more then 1-2 star was crazy.
We were not in the room for more then 15 minutes when I called the front desk and asked for a full refund and checked out. This resort is fine if you expect a 2 star place. But if your looking for 4 star or above look elsewhere seriously!

title: “Fantastic new hotel!”
text: This probably deserves a higher rating, but I almost NEVER give five points. We had a simply wonderful stay at this hotel, which was only 4 days old at the time. It's decorated beautifully and the beds, towels and sheets were especially great. The location is quiet. Next door is an EXCELLENT restaurant, Freda's. The traffic in Austin IS horrendous but we worked around it in 'off' hours. It was very nice to stay a bit out of town.

title: “Elegant Luxury”
text:
Stayed here as a family for a week a Easter to celebrate a special anniversary and were very kindly upgraded by the lovely Abir for our stay. Huge two bed suite it felt like our very own apartment on Park Avenue. Very luxurious rooms with amazing linen/towels etc. Great breakfast room (and compliments to the girls working there) it is a small room however we were never waiting more than 5 minutes. Lovely selection of breakfast in particular the cinnamon granola.
Beautiful lobby, bars and great concierge service in the Towers. Recommended some good restaurants and some casual ones when travelling with teenagers. Don't bother with the Starbucks in the hotel its madly expensive. There is a great one opposite the main door of the Waldorf. This was our first trip to New York as a family and we will certainly never forget our stay at the Waldorf!!
 If you are travelling with teenagers I highly recommend the Pizza Tour of Brooklyn (book in advance) it takes you to Coney Island too and it was one of the highlights of our trip.
If u get tired of 5th Avenue (because at weekends it does get hectic) shop in Soho or Seaport.
Less hassle and if the weather is nice you can take a walk/bike ride across Brooklyn Bridge (at Seaport) or sit outside and sip a white wine while the teenagers shop!!
We will be back to the Waldorf. Some day!
ps. lots of SUV's outside the hotel offering great rates back to the Airport. 90 dollars all in for 4 of us and 8 pieces of luggage

title: “Tired of the same ol', same ol'?”
text: The Warwick Melrose Hotel, located on the edge of downtown Dallas, provides the traveler with a pleasant and comfortable alternative to high-end national hotel chains. Think "a little bit of Europe" in the US. The Landmark restaurant is one of the best in Dallas, the Library bar is friendly and comfortable, and the staff attentive and responsive. Built in the late 1920s, the Melrose offers very comfortable, old fashioned style with modern amenities including wi-fi, exercise facilities, valet parking and a location close to much of the Dallas "action." While the standard rooms are very acceptable, the corner suites, especially those facing west, are wonderful. We don't and won't stay anywhere else in Dallas!

title: “A catch in New York!”
text:
We stayed at Salisbury Hotel för 6 nights in Jan. 2008. I'd found it through Tripadvior and my expectensions were high. The hotel is locaded at 57th street, walkingdistance from MoMa, Rockerfeller Center, Central Park and Times Sqare. Close to Subway station. So really, the loctaion is great! It has a Starbucks right across the street and a very nice deli ("Green Cafe") right nex to the hotel. 
The hotel and the rooms are a bit worn out, but on the other hand our room was big and came with two closets. They are also clean, so it really had it all for us, especially for the price we payed! (about 1,100 us dollar for the hole stay). 
Breakfast is not included, it's 4 dollar per adult. It's average - bagels. cereals, donuts, some fruitsalad. It keeps you full but you get kind of bored. 
The one bad thing is the elevators. Only two and they are slow! And they have no other facilitys. 
So, you don't get a fancy stay, but a spacious and clean room at a great location!

title: “Best Hotel in SF”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at the Argonaut in September 2003 as the first night of a 3 week touring holiday in the states. 
It surpassed all our expectations. We arrived at 3am UKT as zombies and the staff were wonderful and jested with us which made us really welcome. 
The room was superb and contained all sorts of marvellous goodies to play with.. eg DVD player.. 
Not sure about breakfast as we found a marvellous diner down the street and ate there for that genuine USA experience. 
The location was excellent and _just_ on the edge of all the attractions so it was not too noisey. 
On the day that we checked out, the hotel arranged for a car to take us to the airport... we expected one of the local cab firms to roll up, but we were astounded when we went outside and there was a lincoln towncar sitting waiting for us. 
Top Marks!!

title: “The name says it all”
text:
I found their site on google when I was trying to find a hotel close to Sea World. Im from LA, so I didnt want to drive back home after a day with kids in Sea World. They had good rates, and didnt require online payment for booking. I simply copiedtheir address to my GPS, and called to see availability of rooms.
Once there the next day, I found their place easily, looked at the rooms, and took 2 rooms next to each other with internal door. one had a master bed and kitchen, the other, two beds. Both bathrooms were clean, sheets were new and had a fresh smell, and there was an accecible pool also. Both had sat TV, and room service. 
Breakfast was also included, and although the breakfast area was a little crammed, the choices were plenty, from the simple egges to juices and a variety of cereals. All in all, I paid 170 USD for both rooms. NICE!! 
NB: I found a lot of Comfort Inn hotels next to Disneyland and other theme parks, so in case you're going to those places also, ...well simply put, 1200 USD for a Disney Hotel compared to 200 USD at Comfort Inn, for a simple comfy bed at the end of the day. .. you make the coice :-))

title: “Best hotel in NY”
text: This is the best hotel in NY. The staff is exceptional. I have stayed there at least 10 times [ in fact going back this week] and have never been disappointed!! Great location - GREAT staff.

title: “Another enjoyable stay”
text:
We have been staying at this hotel since it was the Rihga Royal. We stopped going when it started to get dated and returned when it re-opened as the London NYC. We have tried many other hotels in New York but always seem to return here. The suites are simply the best value we have found in Manhattan. They are large by any standard with big bedrooms and spacious sitting rooms. They are contemporary with well appointed bathrooms. 
The hotel bar is busy and has a great vibe. The Gordon Ramsey restaurant Maze is very good - I have not yet tried the more formal restaurant which I have heard is exceptional.
This trip we did not find the service in either the bar or the restaurant to be as good as it has been in the past.By way of example we were having coffee in the bar area one day getting ready to head out for the afternoon. It began to pour rain so we decided to stay for lunch. We approached the desk and asked if they could accommodate us. They said they could in about 15 minutes so we said that we would go back to our room and return in 15 minutes. When we returned the same woman told us that it would be a 45 minute wait given that we did not have a reservation. Call me crazy but when she told us to come back in 15 minutes I assumed she was making a note of it. We then said we would sit in the bar if we could order from the restaurant menu - but that was not possible. Similar service experiences occurred in both the bar lounge area (but not the bartenders who were great) and in the restaurant Maze at breakfast and at dinner - (but the breakfast itself was very good). Another perplexing note was the state of the front of the hotel. The planters of (usually) neatly trimmed boxwood were in disarray with many of the plants dead or dying, which gave the front of the hotel a neglected appearance. It struck me that someone in management was asleep at that switch and that certain of the restaurant staff needed a tune up. Having said all of that my husband is in New York on business as I write this review and when he canvassed with me where he should stay we both agreed - the London NYC. (We have also stayed here with our kids - ages 6 and 8 in the past and the staff had no problem with kids).

title: “Lots of good and bad”
text: My wife and l stayed here for 4 nights in the spring of 2012, and my overall impression is mixed. Great location! Penn Station, Macys, Herald Squre, tons of great restaurants and the Empire State Building are all within a block of here. There is a subway stop almost right outside the door as well. The staff was great, and it was very quiet. You would never know your in mid-town Manhatten until you looked out your window it was that quiet. However, the room was small and smelled bad. I think the smell was due to the air mattress they use. The room we had did not have a bathtub either.. But hey... its New York... who cares about the size of the room. I would recommend to stay in a floor as high as possible

title: “Worst Hotel Stay in Years.”
text:
The single worst hotel I've stayed at in years. The rooms look like they were decorated in 1972. The bed was old, lumpy, and simply bad. Dirty spots on the carpet throughout and peeling paint in the bath. Thankfully Hotwire made it right and got me another room. I travel constantly and expected so much more of a Millenium Hotel. Clearly they are not putting any funds into the property. But with such an incredible location, I cannot understand why they wouldn't make this a showplace. 
The bell staff and front door team were terrific and indicated that the hotel has lots of issues. Front desk staff couldn't care less.
Bottom line: Avoid this place if you want to have a pleasant stay in NYC.

title: “Great Location, Small Rooms”
text: I have stayed at the Eastside, Brooklyn and Downtown Marriott on business travel. Even though the Eastside Marriott has the "best" name its rooms are definitely the smallest and the odds of you seeing anything other than another room from your window are low. The staff is courteous, the location is great, but except for the location the Eastside Marriott is inferior to its cousins.

title: “Good quality hotel in a fantastic central location”
text: Stayed at the Salisbury for 3 nights on a girlie shopping trip with a friend. Having requested a quiet room by email we were both upgraded to a suite each which was huge. The suites are extremely large and comfortable. Decor could be more modern but the beds are comfortable with a coffee machine, fridge and microwave provided as well. The front desk staff are friendly and efficient. We ordered a car via the hotel to take us to the airport and instead we had a limo ferry us there in style! Overall I would stay here again and do not hesitate in recommending it to other NYC travellers.

title: “Lovely place and great value for money!”
text:
We visit NYC at least once a year and we've never found a hotel yet that meets all of our needs! So we keep trying ;)
We were pleased with the location - a few blocks from grand central station and a couple of 24 hr pharmacies that sell most things. There was also a wonderful "Just Salad" shop a block away which did amazing salads if you fancy injecting a bit of health into your veins after a day of typical NYC junk food lol. Mings Delights was a delicious Chinese place just one block away between 39th and 38th on third - I recommend the sesame chicken mmmmm. 
Anyway back to the hotel lol.
