We had a room on the 25th floor - very large studio with a small kitchen and bathroom, a dining table area and lounge area with a sofa and a massive bed. 
The rooms are a little bland and basic but they are very clean and you get what you pay for. 
I could soooo easily turn this into a bona fide 4 star hotel if the management wish to drop me a message! This place really doesn't need a massive overhaul as some reviews suggest it does, but with a little bit of tlc this would become even more of a gem. I think you should consider free wifi too as many people choose their rooms with communication in mind and at present it is very expensive and not worth the price.
Wonderful hotel and area and we are very likely to return next year - thank you x

title: “Great location and great service”
text:
I was here for 9 nights. There was only one time I can remember hearing my neighbor, and that was very faint and didn't last long. i saw a lot of other reviewers complaining about noise so it may be dependent on the location of your room and the types of neighbors you have. I really had no complaints about noise. A coworker on a different floor did complain about the light rail making noise pretty late and pretty early. I was on the 16th floor and faced Curtis St and never heard it.
My only complaint was the air conditioner. It was extremely noisy. Regardless of the fan settings, it was so loud I was unable to hear the tv. It became a huge pain because I'd be watching a show on tv, the ac would kick on and I'd miss all the dialog until it turned off. The Closed Captioning feature on the tv wasn't working either.
Otherwise, I really enjoyed my stay. My room was big enough and very clean. I could walk very easily to the convention center, shopping areas, and restaurants.

title: “Good for our group”
text:
We brought a group of teenagers to this hotel as a stop between Dallas and South Padre Island (where they were at camp). While the room and breakfast were decent for our purpose, they had some serious
cricket issues, and we were on the 4th floor! I was in a room full of
girls, and I had to endure multiple screams throughout the night. They may not be able to do much about that, considering there may be several other hotels with the same issue, but our group will always remember the "cricket hotel."
The safety issue was a little bit of a concern. Our door on the 4th floor didn't shut all the way, and we were able to simply push the door open without using the key. One of our boys had to slam it shut multiple times in order for the door to catch so we could safely leave our room and go about town. Another reviewer also mentioned the
pizza people, which apparently happened to them in October 2006. Well, we encountered the same issue and witnessed the shady coupon delivery on our floor, but assumed it was sanctioned by the hotel. It's true - if they can get in unnoticed, who else can?
As far as cleanliness and accomodation, the staff was friendly, the check-in/out was quick and precise, and the breakfast was actually very decent for a free breakfast. We had bagels, english muffins, cereal, coffee, juice, oatmeal, etc. A good free breakfast is always a plus with a bunch of teenagers :)
Overall, for our purposes, it was a decent choice. Rooms were spacious and clean, and the location wasn't too bad for the price. It
maybe took us a little less than 10 minutes to get into the heart of downtown and the riverwalk. However, if I were coming back to San Antonio with my husband for a weekend, I wouldn't stay here. The crickets and safety were too much of a concern for it to be any more than a group stopover for me.

title: “Good position but small”
text:
My husband and I have just spent three days in the Comfort Inn and we found it in a really good position but the room was very small. We had a crib in the room with our baby and there was hardly any room to move.
The breakfast included is good but you do need to go early on to get a wider selection of fruit and breads.
The staff were helpful but I don't think they clean that thoroughly - when we were leaving I found a receipt at the end of the bed from a previous visitor dated June 2005!
The bed was comfortable but the sheets were very annoying as there was no fitted sheet so the whole bottom sheet and mattress cover kept moving all the night and it was uncomfortable by the morning.
The positon is excellent though - you can walk everywhere. The 16th mall and free shuttle is one block.
This was an okay hotel at a reasonable price but I wouldn't rave about it.

title: “Beautiful, inviting accommodations with *excellent* service”
text:
In true Kimpton style the Palomar is well-appointed, tastefully decorated and supremely inviting. The corner suite on the 9th (top) floor was spacious and quiet with an oversized bathtub in the bathroom and a beyond comfortable king bed in the step-down bedroom area. Large fluffy towels and awesome spa level soaps & lotion. The window seat was a great reprieve to read in as an alternative to the large desk area and the $10 minibar credit for being an InTouch member made cookies before bed a fun treat. 
Enclaves outside of the bar and restaurant were private yet welcoming. The bar was lively and Corey, the bartender, attentive and great with suggestions for food, drinks and score updates for the game playing on the tvs. Indulge in a 'southern heat' - a jalapeno and cucumber margarita on ice and take a walk through the pool area. Inviting with on-point furniture, the cabanas are comfortable and clean and it looked like it would be a happening place during the day. 
Quick, friendly front desk service at check-in and departure were hallmark to the Kimpton brand; the staff throughout exemplary in their friendly nature and genuine easy smiles. Located just off the highway and across from Mockingbird Station and SMU this is an uber convenient hotel for those who need to be close to the university and activity. It was a little further from my office but now my new favorite for Dallas business travel. 
If you can make the time I heard rave reviews on the restaurant and exhale spa on site from guests, locals and colleagues.

title: “Expensive but very good”
text:
It is a very good hotel, but everything is very expensive. Internet, parking, is all overpriced.
You can park your car, half a block from hotel, for 1/3 of the price.

title: “Fabulous Central Park Views and Great Staff”
text:
Just stayed at the MO NYC this weekend and had a wonderful time. I got upgraded to a Premier Central Park View room, there was a birthday treat waiting for me in my room when I checked in, and I love the fact that they actually have a swimming pool! 
For the full review of my stay, with pictures, please read my blog entry: http://www.destinationsperfected.com/2011/01/new-york-city-48-hour-gastronomic.html

title: “Grand Hyatt a little less than grand”
text:
I have stayed at some great Hyatt hotels - even got married at the one in Maui - and the Grand Hyatt's are usually pretty fabulous. 
The Manchester Grand Hyatt has the beginnings of a great hotel - decent location (walkable to the Gas Lamp district, convention center, and shops by the water), nice open entrance area and decent pool area. All of the shops, less one that had a bunch of strange furniture/antique things in it, on my side of the building were under renovation. Strangely, they promoted a coffee shop on my side of the hotel that wasn't in the hotel, and when I finally located it outside the hotel at 2:30 it was already closed for the day. There was one coffeeshop on the opposite side of the hotel. 
The staff was very accomodating (had to change a date for a pre-arranged corporate stay by phone, front desk gave me a packet of tylonal for a headache, and ordered room service a couple of times, bell service was always ready to grab you a cab). 
The rooms were fine. I had a nice view of the pool and harbor. Towels and sheets were 'okay' - not overly plush. Bathroom was okay, had the basic amenities, TV was huge, though had one of those annoying cable remotes that is not super responsive, but had loads of channels. They have mini-refrigerators in every room but no-mini bars (I enjoy having easy access to a quick soda or two w/o having to order room service). 
I was there from Thursday through early Sunday morning and worked in the mornings and evenings out of the room. I was out of the room until about 2p each day and the cleaning staff never made it to my room to clean it. Luckily, I had plenty of towels and other bathroom supplies, so it wasn't the end of the world - just didn't feel as fresh as it should have from a daily cleaning. 
It wasn't a bad experience, just not an amazing 5 star experience. There are several other hotels (the Omni for one) that are pretty amazing if you want a little bit of an upgrade.

title: “Great hotel, great price.”
text: I chose the property because they gave me a base rate of 109.00 per night (plus taxes). This was excellent considering I wanted to be within walking distance of the Moscone Conference center. The hotel was clean and the staff was super friendly and helpful. My hotel room was modest but decorated in a 70s revival theme (think crate and barrell modern hip?). But the room was very comfortable and clean. There was every amenity available including free wireless internet from my room. The room was spacious and I really enjoyed coming back to my hotel room at the end of the day. I had a room at the back of the hotel and it was quiet and had enough privacy that I felt safe but still had lots of sunlight if I so choose to let it in (and provided it was not one of the days when it was raining in SF). The hotel staff were magnificent. They even found a box for me to pack my conference extras in and tape it up so that I could mail it home and save the need to lug it in my suitcase to the airport. The only downside I saw was the hotel bar. It was packed every night so if you are into this that is great but it took some time to get a drink and the bartenders were a little on the snootier side. However, the location of the hotel makes it really easy to venture out to lots of other establishments with great food and ambience more to my (older) liking. And the hotel staff are great sources to ask about places to go. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone staying in SF.

title: “So close, but not quite”
text:
We stayed at the Ritz Carlton with our young children. The staff was always very friendly and professional, the room was excellent. The location is perfect - a very short walk to the commons. I also have to say the rate, for this class of hotel very good for a weekend stay. 
 My hesitations... the service (whether it was the switchboard or waitstaff ) which was well intentioned but slow and the fan/air conditioning in the room was very loud (maybe it needed maintennance). Beware if you have kids looking for a swim - the pool is located at a next door fitness club (fantastic facility to be fair) - but children are only allowed to swim from 11-3 on Sundays.

title: “Great Stay!”
text: My husband and I stayed one night at Nine Zero. We reached Boston and made a wrong turn and we were not able to find the hotel too easily at that point. I called the hotel and asked for directions. John stayed on the phone with us giving us directions turn by turn until we reached the hotel. What amazing customer service! The hotel is clean and the beds were great and had a great night's sleep! The location was within walking distance to everything. Only one minor thing - someone on my floor was smoking and the odor made me sick. Brian at the font desk said he would address it and offered vouchers for breakfast. We declined as we were meeting family for brunch. Next time, Brian. Thank you.

title: “Service with a SMILE!”
text: Don't have a single thing to complain about. The hotel room was nice and clean. Updated everything. Location perfect for a quick walk to the river. Nice if you don't want to spend the extra $$$ for "on the river." The entire staff was helpful and friendly. Breakfast was tasty and included in your room price. Fresh fruit, bagels, and hot items available. Warm cookies at night by the front desk, and coffee's brewed all day for guests. It's the extra touches that completed our stay. Plenty of information, maps and coupons readily passed out by the staff. Would stay again in a heart-beat.

title: “Very Nice Property”
text: First time staying here and I am super picky about hotels. I am super impressed with Courtyard's new modern look that are in most locations. The rooms are very nicely decorated and very inviting. The bathroom was good and the TV was a huge flat screen. They are nothing like the Courtyards of before. I enjoyed my stay here. The staff was nice. The location was convenient and parking at hotel was very easy. I would definitely stay here again. The rates were good too for such a nice place because generally Houston has high rates.

title: “Very convenient and clean..”
text: My friend and I enjoyed our stay here. We have all good things to say about it except the bathroom was small and I would have liked a microwave for popcorn. Other than that, great price, great location and comfy beds.

title: “Very happy with our stay at the Chestnut Hill Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Chestnut Hill Hotel the last week of October for 3 nights. Originally we wanted to stay in Philadelphia but were glad we decided to stay at this hotel outside of the city. The train into the city was only a few blocks away and very accessible to downtown. Also, staying in Chestnut Hill allowed us to explore a very nice quaint town where we found some great restaurants and nice shops. The staff at the hotel were very accommodating especially Erin who provided us with many good recommendations on where to go and how to get there. We also enjoyed the breakfast which was included in the price as well as the restaurant attached to the hotel where we had dinner one night. We would not hesitate to go back to this hotel again…we had a great time!
Fern and David

title: “Good Location - Clean Hotel”
text: Just returned from a 5 day break in New York stopping at the Hampton Inn. Hotel location is excellent with times square a 2 min walk as is Mamma Mia Winter Garden Theatre. Enjoyed our stay very much. Hotel is clean and tidy with helpful staff. Breakfast is plentiful with free internet access and tea/coffee available 24hrs a day from the hotel lobby. Would definately recommend this hotel.

title: “Impeccable Service”
text:
Our recent trip to Denver, CO included a stay at the AAA Four Diamond Hotel Hyatt Regency at the Colorado Convention Center. The hotel features 1100 rooms, making this 7-year-old hotel the largest in Denver, and the second largest in the country.
During our five-day stay, we had the opportunity to sample almost all of the facilities and can say with enthusiasm that we would recommend it to anyone coming to this area. As for the hotel room itself, it was basically unremarkable: comfortable, but lacking some of the amenities that make other hotels special. It would have been convenient to have had a small refrigerator to keep soft drinks cool but we opted not to spend the $20 required to have one delivered to the room. A microwave would have also been nice along with a much-needed new mattress on the bed. The size of the room was adequate but the bathroom was small and in need of a facelift. As for other areas at the hotel, the only pool was small and seating around it sparse, especially considering that you could have 2,000+ people who might like to use this area at any one time. The workout area was comfortable and nicely equipped.
Now for the even better news...the view from our room was priceless as we could easily view the beautiful Rockies from this spot on the 22nd floor; the sunsets were spectacular. Go to the 27th floor to The Peaks Lounge for even a better view.
The one aspect that impressed us the most, without a doubt, was the level of service that the hotel is fortunate to have. We travel often and I don't think we have ever had the consistency of excellence from every employee starting with the doormen, the front desk, the workout room staff to those working at The Strata Bar. Special kudos, however, have to be extended to the restaurant staff, especially those at the Altitude Restaurant, located on the lobby floor. They went out of their way to make sure we were satisfied with our meals and seemed genuinely concerned with our comfort. They were simply outstanding.
Located only a few blocks from the famous 16th Street Mall, the Hyatt puts you where you need to be in order to access public transportation (buses and trains). It was particularly helpful to us as we arrived at the hotel on a shuttle and did not rent a car during our stay. We used the free bus service to access Coor's Field, a short trip away. A trip to the airport can take approximately 40 minutes, depending on traffic.
Traveling to Denver? You can't miss with this stop.

title: “Great Service”
text: I stayed at the Sheraton Gateway for 5 days for a conference and I could not have asked for better services from the staff. In particular, Miss Estela Estrada went above and beyond to make sure over 100+ guests in our group were well taken care off with food and beverages. She always had a smile on her face and made me feel very very welcome and confortable. Thank you for the excellent service!

title: “Wonderful Place for a stay in DC”
text: Just came back yesterday from a long weekend in DC to celebrate my wife's birthday. Room was spacious and very clean. Joined the Kimpton Club online (free) this includes free internet access & $10 coupon to raid the minibar. Rate was $104 night + tax, with their summer special. The manager pours wine (red & white) & sangria from 5pm - 6pm every evening in the lobby . Great opportunity to relax and mingle with the other guests. Also, they have brand new Hybrid bikes that you can borrow at no charge (first come first served). A great way to see the area especially since DC has over 100 miles of protected bike trails. The hotel is located within walking distance the mall & capitol as well as 2 blocks from Union Station (Metro connection, trains, restaurants (reasonably priced to inexpensive) & shopping), Starbucks is a 1/2 block away. Last but not least , the staff are great , responsive & helpful.

title: “Wonderful Boutique Hotel in Downtown Location”
text:
I came to San Francisco for the Ring Cycle at the opera and wanted a downtown location convenient for theater, transportation, and museums. I found exactly what I needed at the Adagio. This was a splurge for me and I had a great time and was most comfortable in my room. Lovely furnishings - quiet decor, very modern. My 10th floor room was quiet - there are double hung windows, so you can block out sound. There is a portable air conditioning unit and ceiling fan in the room, but I mostly kept the windows open and used the fan only, as the nights were quite cool - in the low 50s. Room electronics are up to date and there was a fridge with goodies, plenty of towels, etc, and high-speed wireless for my laptop. There's a safe in the room and plenty of closet space.
There was a burst pipe in the room above me and I was moved to the Caruso Suite in the Penthouse, which was quite opulent, compared to my room, but it was more than twice the price anyway, though I paid only what my original room cost, and the management went out of their way to make up for the inconvenience. I only wish that this had happened earlier in my stay! If you can afford it, it would be a great suite for a couple. I was on my own, and felt safe in the hotel. 
I had one meal in the restaurant, which was comfortable and attractive, and the bar seemed lively, but I was out every night and didn't drink there, and I didn't use the spa or swimming pool. There are iMacs available for use on the main floor and the lobby is spacious and comfortable. Door staff and concierges were so helpful and friendly. I highly recommend this hotel if you want a downtown location. There's a Walgreens nearby and a deli if you're hungry, and you can get a cab easily on Geary Street. You're also only a few blocks from Union Square.

title: “Affordable (but nothing luxurious!)”
text: Stayed here the night of the Madonna concert which was in Seattle, early October. Good walking distance to the Space Needle and Key Arena. The hotel itself is very average - not the worst I've ever seen, but definitely in need of upgrading. Bed and bedding was actually quite comfy though. No bed bug experience here, thank god. Parking out front is limited (and not free) but can also park in the back alley (not so desirable). Walls are thin (could hear the loud people on the floor below right after concert) - complained to front desk, and they dealt with it promptly - no more noise after that. Overall, not overly bad though and reasonably priced if you're on a tight budget.

title: “Great value and location”
text: Stayed here january 2012 on a getaway weekend with my wife. We used points and found it to be a very good value. There is light rail right across the street with a new airport one on the way so very convenient for getting around! There were issues with our tv that they were unable to resolve and they gave us 2000 point refund for our trouble. This is a stand up operation. No restaurant but dining very close by. Very nice appointed rooms and a nice bar and snack bar. Great place!

title: “Soho Not So Grand Deja Vu”
text:
After reading the review from "Soho Not So Grand" I thought the guy that wrote it must have stayed with us. We had much the same expereince. The hotel overall is not guest friendly, is statring to look dated, the rooms are very small and the attitude - even for a so-called "hip property" is unaccepable, through the roof. 
In my opinion, hip is great if it can be backed up with across-the-board service and quality accomodations. The Soho Grand may have been all that a few years ago, but now it's just all flat. 
Just a few of our disapointments with the hotel on our recent stay.
When we booked our room, I specifically told the reservationist that we were bringing our daughter down to the hotel to see the July 4th fireworks. Naturally my first concern was that we'd have a high floor room with a view toward the fireworks. No problem, assured the reservationist. There was a problem. Upon checking into the hotel they only had a higher floor room on the opposite corner of the hotel facing away from the fireworks. Note: After scoping out the surrounding buildings I determined it was highly unlikely any room would have given a view of the Macy's fireworks. By the way, when we checked in and explained this to the front desk clerk he told us we'd be able to see them since they were shot off from around Macys! I didn't have the time or energy at this point to explain that the fireworks are shot off from the East River. This was the second desk clerk to help us, and at least he made an effort. The first one didn't know anything about anything, but she made sure to give free champagne to three people who walked up to the desk while we wre attemptiong to check-in. I eventually asked a third desk clerk if we too, paying customers, might actually be granted the bounty of their kindness with a glass. She instructed clueless clerk # 1 to pour us some. So anyway, that first clerk upon being told of the fireworks-view room didn't even seem to realize it was the Fourth of July. Then she said, rather disinterestedly, that she had no idea if the room had any view. I inquired further if I might have a look at the room, and she said they couldn't allow that since housekeeping was still cleaning. Okay. Then she tells me I should tallk to the concierge. Now, I go from attitude to super attitude. She hands me the phone and the concierge is on the other end. I explain that the front desk connected me to her (though I'm not sure why) and that we were told our room would have view of the fireworks. The concierge is obviosuly mad that the front desk would lay this on her, and I have to somewhat agree (the front desk should know their own rooms), but it didn't call for Super Attitude. Her cocky reponse was "Are you kidding?" No I wasn't. I should have cut my losses right there and gone to another hotel, but I had my wife and baby and we were all getting tired. An hour later we checked in to our closet and had a nice view on the wrong side of the hotel. The service throughout the stay was cold, or at the least aloof. And it's not aNew York thing, I lived there for years and have stayed in numerous hotels across the city. This place is just run bad and the physical look of the hotels just shows that they don't care anymore. as oftentimes happens when a new hotel opens (the Tribeca Grand) the better staff make abeline to the newer property. I don't know if that's what's happened here, but I threw away $500 for arotten stay. We ended up trudging downtown in the rain and saw about fifteen minutes of the fireworks.
One major exception: Did these guys even work for the same hotel? The guys (part of the bell staff) out front and the man who delivered our bags to the room were top-notch, friendly and professional. Now if we could just take them to a better hotel!

title: “First Class”
text: Absolute first class all the way. Check in started the second my car door was opened by a hotel staff member at the valet parking area. My key card was ready by the time I got to the check in desk and with a quick swipe of my credit card I was escorted to the elevator where my bagage and a bell boy were waiting. The room was perfect in every sense. I struggled to find some minor thing that was not perfect, I couldn't find anything. My room was cleaned twice daily, I never saw the maid. Valet parking was perfect. Every individual I encountered went out of their way to give me anything I had requested.

title: “good place for the money”
text: clean hotel in a quiet neighborhood. Very accomodating clerk, who quickly resolved our minor issues. room was big and bright. dont expect top of the line amenities or furniture, but you are not paying for that either. if you want posh amenities that come with a hefty NYC price tag then stay elsewhere, but if you are a tourist like we were and looking to esxplore NYC and have a clean and comfortable place to sleep, then book this hotel. We found shared bathrooms not to be a problem as there are 2-3 on each floor and only 8-10 rooms per floor. a word of advice: book directly on their website: [---------------------] so that you dont have to pre-pay for yoru reservation in advance. We booked on orbitz and had to pay upfront, and only later found this hotels website that had a better rate, but of course online travel sites charge you a big cancellation fee to discourage cancellations, so it wasnt worth cancelling this time around. well, we know for next time.

title: “best hotel in the world?”
text:
Could Drury Inn at University Place in Charlotte be the best hotel in the world?
Maybe. It's the only establishment I've ever been in around the world where the sanitation grade is 100% (certified by the state) and has remained so. The staff are uniformly helpful even when sorting out problems. They remembered our names and our preferences. They were just nice southern people.
We've stayed at some of the flashier, expensive, big name hotels around the world but this place is one of our favourites.
Excellent value. No wonder they win so many awards!

title: “Great family hotel”
text: We stayed in this hotel with two toddler/preschool boys. The great, downtown location made it easy to walk and take public transportation to major attractions. Ghiradelli Square is an easy walk even for tiny legs. The hotel is on two busy streets, so there is street noise, but I've never stayed in a San Fran hotel that wasn't noisy. I'd recommend opting for a higher floor if you want more quiet. We also appreciated the free breakfast, especially since eating out all the time as a family can get pricey. Staff were helpful in navigating public transportation and locating nearby parks. We would definitely stay again.

title: “wouldn't recommend”
text:
The Wolcott is not somewhere i would recommend to stay. Granted it is in a brilliant location you can't argue with that. We really only used the room to sleep but the bathroom was really disgusting. The drain was just a hole that someone had sledgehammered into the floor, the shower would go from hot to cold so didnt have a decent shower for a week. The staff were rude, minus the girls at the concierge they were very helpful. The airconditioner was so loud it made getting a good night sleep almost impossible but you needed it on as it was so hot. But the bed was comfortable. 
I would only stay here again as a last resort!

title: “What a weird place!”
text:
This place is off the wall, and does not function well as a hotel. Staying at this "Hotel" is more like staying with your in laws, rather than staying at a hotel. 
At one point during my stay a group of people tried to break into my room. This group first tried to kick my door down and when that did not work they left briefly then returned with an axe. I called the front desk and informed them of the current situation and they asked me "what should they do about it?"
This wild group of people with the axe ruined my stay, other than that this is a wonderful hotel, except for the awful odor!

title: “DIAMOND IN THE MIDDLE OF IT ALL”
text:
I stayed at the Roosevelt in Hollywood for a week during March... It met all of my expectations and more. 
Ever since I was little I dreamed of staying there and it was just amazing. 
The rooms were spacious in the cabana area and it also allowed us to have access to the tropicana bar even during functions. The beds were really comfy and the location was perfect. close to all the main sites as well as any cabs etc. 
Hotel staff are really helpful and have a lot of knowledge so be sure to ask them any questions. Also the available computers in the lobby come in handy instead of always having to pay for internet. 
All in all it was a perfect experience and i'm planning on staying there next yr too.

title: “Best hotel experience to date!”
text: Outstanding service and courteous staff. Great and prompt room service. Delicious food. Will stay there again.

title: “My medical trip”
text: I had to make a trip to Dallas to see a doctor, and my daughter found this hotel on the internet. She told them the requirements I needed due to my handicap needs, and I must say this hotel was wonderful in meeting them. The suite was very spacious and exactly what we wanted. The hotel had a kitchenette with full refrigerator, microwave, dishwasher, dishes, and coffeemaker. I really enjoyed the fanned washcloths and towels and the accessible shower and tub. I would stay at a Candlewood Suite anywhere I traveled.

title: “Excellent location. Goox breskfast included”
text: Centraly located. We walked everywhere by foot. Room very large and clean with all facilities. Free huge breakfast. Free wifi around lobby only. Parking a bit expensive usd 41 p/day, but good valet service. Front desk very attentive - look for Robby! Concierge very profetional. Knows everything. In short - good value for money.

title: “what a great place for a great price!”
text: i stayed here at the end of june for 5 days and have to say that i loved it! Now if you are expecting a 5 star hotel, please rethink your travel plans! But for a place that feels like home, with a great staff you can not go wrong staying here. The rooms are of good size, the breakfast in the am is fresh and you can even make your own waffles, The pool area is well kept and very relaxing. This is the one of the best hotels i have stayed at and i usually do stay at 5 stars.. Thank you to Len and Dave for making me feel so welcome and i will stay here again when i come back to san diego!

title: “Close to everything”
text: Great location. Corner of 8th and 43rd. Bar 10 is a nice spot. Ask for corner room on a higher floor is possible.

title: “Comfortable Hotel - with some interesting twists”
text: Fortunately we paid a fair price for this room since it was deeply discounted for our four night stay. The location is excellent, in theatre district, across from Macy's and an easy walk to the Miracle Mile and Millenium Park. The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was clean, however there were stains on the cover of the chaise lounge. The hotel has the history of being a medical office building that was converted into a hotel. The coversion was done well and gives the small hotel a unique ambience. Each room had been a doctors office or suite (ask about the connection to Al Capote). As stated by previous reviews the rooms are small, and the bathroom lacks counter space. Small like European small. The hotel was quiet with a slight buzz of outdoor activity during the day as you'd expect in any city hotel. The bed was comfortable, and the room had a thermostate with a specific tempeture setting. The disappointments included a lukewarm shower each morning and a bad television (very dark picture on an old fashion anlog TV) which could not be seen unobstructive over your feet as you lay in bed. (I did not complain about the water tempeture thinking that it would be corrected each day). Yes they have free coffee in the lobby but for some strange reason it is removed prompty at 9 or 9:30 am, and there is no coffee in the rooms. They have a strange policy of hanging communal ladies under garments - leopard printed teddy and panties - in your closet for use by the guest. This has to be the strangest hotel perk I've ever seen. Who really needs a one size fits all teddy for a romantic tryst? The bell person assured us that it is washed after each guest (yeah, like that was my concern).

title: “Best hotel ever”
text: best hotel ever, just like a dream... what a room!

title: “Wonderful!!!!!”
text: Everything was clean...friendly...helpful...this is my favorite hotel to stay in when im in la

title: “good for what we needed, but service not as great.”
text: We checked in for a weekend trip to NYC. We've stayed in smaller format rooms before so the size of the room was not a problem. If you need alot of space to navigate, and don't want to bang your shins on the bed frame, you may want to find more spacious accomodations. The room was clean and tidy, and bathroom was a manageable size. The only complaint I would have is that the TV in the room didn't work and despite calling about asking to have the problem fixed, therew as no resolution before we checked out of the hotel.

title: “Pleasant stay. Noisy Neighbors.”
text:
The Hotel is a very beautiful old property, well maintained and operated. We never experienced a line, or a wait for any service. We may have been lucky, but having stayed at the Waldorf and the W right in the area on past visits. Overall, we felt that the rate was less than those two (corporate block rate) and the visit just as pleasant and convenient to the activities we were looking to participate in over our three night stay. 
We did have room service for dinner and though it wasn't spectacular, the butternut squash soup was very good. 
The room next door seemed to have at least four people in it who were very loud around 6 AM and when they returned at 11 AM. Thankfully, it was the morning we were sleeping in and we fell back asleep once they left. 
Though the trip was business, we found time to tour, as always and the location is one of the best. We used the subway system more this trip and the hotel is right on the green line and 2 blocks from Grand Central. We really like staying in this part of the city. 
The amenities we liked: the Keurig coffee system (though mate wanted tea); the large walk-in closet in the King room we had; the bed was very comfortable; the bedding was very nice; the room temperature and heating system was very comfortable; the spare table under the desk; the concierge and the bell station looking after our luggage the day we toured after checking out; The amenities we missed: comfy robes, wi-fi, free internet, and yes, a larger bath would be nice. We appreciate the older properties don't have modern infrastructure, and we just got closer using the mirror together! 
The water was warm, the windows open and the spaciousness of the room, compared to most older properties, had us happy to be there. Next year, will we choose there or the W or the Waldorf...we'll let you know. We were just as happy here as there. 
As Angel, the doorman said when we checked in, "we are smaller and more personal than the Waldorf." He was right. That was how we felt during our stay.

title: “Convenient”
text: Convenient location with timely shuttle to/from the airport. Room was clean and quiet. The hotel was standard Hilton. Nothing special. Nothing disappointing. Would stay here again for business reasons.

title: “Excellent location for seeing this fabulous city”
text:
Parking is at a premium in San Franciso but it is free at the Coventry.
The room was great and although there is no restaurant there are so many eateries in the area it is easy to find a variety of food. If you are looking for breakfast turn left and walk a couple of blocks to "Mel's Diner" for a great experience.

title: “Helpful staff!”
text: I had a wonderful experience here. I had to call the front desk a couple of times getting info right after I checked in and went touring for the day, and both times the front desk was kind and accommodating. The location is fabulous, and the bed was INCREDIBLY comfy! The room was more spacious than I expected, and I was quite comfortable the whole time I was there. Wish they provided breakfast, but there are lots of places for that at Reading Terminal and other places nearby.

title: “Beautiful, historic hotel ... and priced as such”
text:
I've stayed in the Hilton Chicago for over a week each of the past 3 years so it feels a bit like a "home away from home" to me by now.
The good:
It is a grand, historic hotel in a decent location (directly across from Grant Park). The staff is helpful, the rooms are relatively comfortable and the bar (Kitty O'Shea's) is an authentic Irish Pub -- brilliant! I love the blues and Buddy Guy's Legends blues club is on Wabash, across the street from the back of the hotel -- easy. There are some decent dining choices walkable from the hotel that include a good sushi restaurant and pizzeria (Lou Malnati's). Most other activities require a cab ride.
The not-so-good:
Other than Kitty O'Sheas (pub grub) the hotel's dining choices are very limited. The location is OK if you want to stroll through Grant Park or Millennium Park -- other than that you'll pretty much need a cab since the hotel is ~ 1 mile south of the river and most of the coolest places to visit in Chicago are north of the river.
The downright ugly:
Very expensive for what you get. Not sure if they hike up the rates during trade show periods (which is when I stay) but it costed $279 + taxes for a total ~ $329/night. What made the price harder to swallow was the fact that I had just stayed in The Whitehall Hotel up near the top of The Magnificent Mile (same age as Hilton but much smaller and boutique-y) in a bigger room, better restaurants, excellent staff and a MUCH better location for just over $110/night!!

title: “Super deal”
text: For the accomodations and the serive you receive for the price, this place is quite a bargain!

title: “Best Option in Manhatam”
text: I have stayed in Hilton New York in Dec 2011. I was very lucky to get a 50% discount in the rate using booking.com This is so far the best hotel I have ever stayed in NY. I loved the location on the hotel service. It is a walking distance from Rockfeller Center, Central Park, 5 Avenue, Times Square, etc. The room is good, very confortable bed and good amenities. The only suggest I have is that they offer Free wi-fi in the rooms. Today it is only avaiable in the lobby and it is really difficult to find a seat.

title: “Beautiful rooms”
text: The rooms were so modern and new. I really enjoyed staying here. The beds were extremely comfortable and it was roomy. The entire room screams stay in here and don't leave! But of course we weren't about to do that. The reception staff were rather cold when we first checked in. But the staff that checked us out were very friendly and bubbly. The location was good as it was close to Dupont Circle metro station. There were also several restaurants around the area, we ate at this pizza place that was recommended on Trip Advisor (sorry can't remember the name).

title: “Good upper west side hotel”
text: The Lucerne is a very nice basic hotel. My room was small but very comfortable. Not much of a lobby but a nice area--close to Columbia University.

title: “Kitsch but cool”
text:
Underneath the kitsch decorations there is a very decent hotel fighting for airtime.For me the attempt to recreate Tuscany in Texas fails miserably but the rooms are large and well furnished,the service is top notch with a very motivated team and the pool an oasis of serenity in a bustling city.
It is well located close to The Galleria and interesting shops ,bars and restaurants are nearby.The Hotel also runs an excellent complimentary car to nearby shops .
Cooking in the in house restaurant is accomplished,but on this visit the dining room was dominated by two large corporate groups.
Continental breakfast is complimentary but a little meagre for a hotel of this quality.
It is not a cheap place to stay but if you want quality and space you will find it here.
Perhaps over time the hotel will offer some of the swords,shields, suits of armour etc to an aspiring Italian theme park operator!

title: “Great place to stay for every reason.”
text:
I'll mainly address the few complaints I've seen in a few reviews:
- small rooms. Welcome to Manhattan, friend! I can tell you haven't been here before from your foreign beliefs on room size. This is actually average to above-average for a hotel room here, and because the room is well laid out, it takes good advantage of that. There's a decent amount of space for clothes and there's space to sit outside of just your bed.
- noise. I've stayed on the 4th, 5th, and 11th floors over the span of over 20 days, including weekends. I've never had a problem with noise aside from typical NY street noise (cars honking, people hooting and hollering). And I'm quite picky about noise. I don't know if their club has been closed over my visits or what, but in general, this place isn't noisy. (I should say my visits have been during the winter, so it certainly is possible it gets noisy in the summer, since their bar area is an outdoor lounge that does not appear to be very functional in the current weather).
- it's dark or dinghy. There is a dark, almost moody vibe to the place, yes. The lights in the common areas are kind of dim, and they chose dark paint colors to accent this. It is intentional. The rooms light up bright if you want, and I've never seen any part of this hotel that would qualify as dirty or worn down. The decor may not be your style, but it certainly does not need updating no more than a civil war re-enactment needs more lasers (okay, admittedly the tiny tvs are comically small and could be replaced).
I'll also add a few things:
- they've given me, on two of my stays here, a complimentary bottle of wine that was just sitting, welcoming me to my room. This is pretty neat.
- their bathrooms are pretty good. They're clean, and I like the shower walk-in and how this means there's no door.
- pretty cool that the windows open slightly to let air in.
- great location near transit, and like most of this area of manhattan, perfectly safe.

title: “Great Location for First Time NYC Visitors”
text:
Just got back after visiting August 4-8. We chose this hotel for the all suites rooms since we had a teenager with us and like to have some of our own space. It is a good mid level hotel but would not be considered top notch in service or furnishings.
The breakfast buffet is just okay. Standard plates and silverware but the food was more on par with what I have experienced at Embassy Suites. The first day was very crowded at 9:00 A.M. but subsequent days at 7:30 A.M. it was empty. Overpriced at $30 (we got free breakfast being Diamond members). Families are going to be better off going to Starbucks across the street. 
Times Square is crowded. Don't stay here if you can't handle huge crowds starting as soon as you leave the hotel. The positive is the location next to a main subway line and 2 blocks from another. We never had to take a bus or taxi and saw all of NYC without any problems.

title: “Good hotel in convenient position”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights between Christmas and New Year. The hotel is well located - walking distance of just about everywhere we wanted to go and very convenient for China town. 
The room was fine, but I think that maybe we got the disabled room - we had 2 spyholes in the door - at waist and head height (the room next door only had one spyhole) and the hanging rail in the wardrobe was about about 3 feet off the ground - on the other hand, apart from the wide sliding door into the bathroom there didn't seem to be any adaptations to suit a disabled person - no grab rails and just a normal shower over the bath - so I don't know what it was meant to be - it was just a bit odd. But apart from that the room was fine, the bed was very comfy and we have no complaints.
Just one thing to be aware of - especially if you have just got off a long transatlantic flight - we had stayed at the Orchard Hotel in the past which is a couple of blocks up the road. For this holiday, I booked the hotel and my husband booked the transport from the airport and he assumed we were going to the Orchard Hotel and we ended up at the wrong place. Luckily, we discovered our mistake before the car left - we stuffed our cases back into the boot and were taken to the correct hotel.

title: “OK, NOT SUPERB”
text:
I travel a lot for work so I'm more picky than most hotel guests and for my money, the Omni is just ok.
 My brother and I stayed at the Omni Berkshire for one night and they could not promise a room with two beds since they were near capacity. They offered us a rollaway bed, which we accepted. When we got back to the room late at night and saw what they delivered we were appalled. It was an old (1960's maybe?) metal cot with exposed springs that folds in half. Something your Aunt Ida would make you sleep on when you were a kid visiting. The mattress was so cheap and foamy soft, that it sagged horribly in the center when you laid on it. Classy! I ended up putting the mattress on the floor and the frame in the hallway for pickup. No one, I mean NO ONE could possibly sleep on this bed comfortably, even if they were 85 pounds. The Omni must get complaints but yet they still wheel the old beds up to unsuspecting guests. A word to the Omnni - it's 2009--buy some air mattresses and ditch the reform school bedding.
The furnishings are a bit dated, too. a 19" tube TV and a 1980's radio/CD and CASSETTE minii boombox was set up plus a standard clock radio. I can only assume no one at the Omni owsn an I Pod. 
Thje rooms are clean and quiet, though so if you spend under $200 a night you should feel all right with Omni: the hotel that got a bit stuck in time.

title: “Close to Alamo. Great service.”
text: Nice roomy 2BR suite. Nice to have refrigerator to freeze bottled water to take out on excursions. 39th consecutive day over 100 degrees; why did we go in the summer? All staff greeted us whenever/wherever. Good breakfast spread. Pancakes, French toast, croissants and regular RI food changed daily. Steam in laundry set off fire alarm at about 11 pm, so we all had an outing. Good location- about 2 blocks from Alamo and 4 from Riverwalk. Secure, gated, adjoining parking ramp.

title: “A wonderful experience”
text:
My wife and I spend 3 nights at the Seaport last week during our summer getaway to Boston.
We were expecting a great experience based upon the research we did on line to find the hotel, and we were not disappointed.
The hotel staff provided excellent customer service, every interaction exceeded our expectations. From bell staff, to bar servers to check in and concierge service, all were stellar. The service definitely has a personal quality and feel to it. 
Having spent many hundreds of nights in hotels over many years as a "road warrior" I can attest to the Seaport Boston being one of the nicest hotel stay experiences I have ever had.
The Seaport neighborhood of Boston is very vibrant and alive at night with many pubs, restaurants and other points of interest. The "T" transit system (Silver Line) is a 3 minute walk from the hotel and was our gateway to the city of Boston.
This was our first visit to Boston and we will definitely be staying at the Seaport when we come back next time.

title: “An Absolutely Perfect Place To Stay !!”
text: I am a VERY PICKY PERSON ........so, I tend to look for something to be wrong. I could NOT find anything wrong with this hotel. From the moment we arrived, it was a perfect choice. The hotel is clean, clean, clean.....hotel staff is wonderful......breakfast is delicious...and is kept spotlessly clean. The gentleman at the front desk even took the time to draw us a map directing us to a great restaurant !! The staff is superb ! The bed linens were delightful.....the mattress was soft. Another really nice surprise.....the bedside phone has a very long cord on it that will allow you to take the phone into the bathroom with you. The vanity was the perfect place to put the phone. Each room is equipped with everything you need in their kitchen area.......great refrigerator ! My husband was thrilled with the new HDTV......reception was superb...........and the TV is located so that you can see it perfectly from either the bed or the sitting area. The greatest perk was that we could arrange to leave our car while we flew to a wedding. The shuttle left promptly as scheduled the night before. Upon our return, I called the hotel and they came to pick us up in their nice shuttle. The driver deserved a huge tip for the professional manner in which he worked. If you are looking for a fantastic hotel.....stay here. You will not be disappointed...........even if you are VERY PICKY like me. One warning that has nothing to do with the hotel.............. if you are trying to find the hotel.......don't depend on the directions from Mapquest..........it is wrong. We were driving from Austin to Houston Intercontinental area...........it tells you to turn on a street called Heathrow..........that is wrong..........you turn on John F Kennedy right next to the Holiday Inn Express. Be careful...........we drove around for an hour tryng to find the hotel.

title: “Great, friendly place to stay”
text: Great hotel. We have been coming here for the past 4 years for the charger game. The staff is friendly and remembers us from year to year. It is very clean, great free breakfast, spacious rooms and bathrooms. It is across the street from the trolley station, but not noisy. Within Walking distance to Old Town with some great restaurants.

title: “Good location, free parking and wi-fi”
text: We spent 4 nights with our two young daughters at this property. The room itself was on the small side, but was clean and included a microwave and small refrigerator. The air conditioner however, was a window unit that blew dust everywhere when we first turned it on and did little to actually cool the room. Our room sat right on the marina as well, which was lovely, but the the air was very damp and our towels and swimsuits never really dried. They do have a coin operated laundry onsite which is helpful if you're traveling with kids. The hotel states that the pool was heated but it was freezing (this didn't stop the kids from swimming in the 70 degree weather). That said, the pool/patio area was very nice and had hot tub to warm up in.The staff is extremely helpful and accommodating, and there is a small park across the street to take the kids and watch the boats and guys fishing from the pier. With the small drawbacks, the Island Palms is still a fantastic value and overall good hotel.

title: “Reservations don't matter to them”
text:
They do not honor reservations: On Sunday, January 22, I completed a reservation for a stay at Homestead Studio Suites located at 10020 Skinner Lake Dr., Jacksonville, Florida, 32246. On 1/28/22, I received an email reminder regarding the reservation. When I arrived at the hotel on 1/29/12 at about 3:00 PM, I was told that my room was not available due to some type of maintenance. I waited about 2 hours for the front desk clerk to check various Extended Stay hotels in the area for availability. It was quite clear that none of the other hotels had rooms available that resembled the one that I reserved. I ended up staying in a smaller room just to end the issue. I left a voice mail for Brooke Bobo and Jason Parks in Guest Relations. Neither one returned my call. I sent emails to the following Extended Stay Hotels/HVM LLC managers:
Brooke Bobo, Dir of Guest Relations - Gary A DeLapp, President and CEO - F. Joseph Rogers, EVP of Accounting and Finance - No one bothered to respond. I am not sure if this problem is isolated to the location at Homestead Studio Suites, 10020 Skinner Lake Dr., Jacksonville, Florida, 32246, but clearly this chain does not honor reservations at all. It’s no wonder to me that this company is experiencing financial problems.

title: “Location, great! Service... could have been better”
text:
The Good:
This is a great location. You're right downtown, just walking distance from the Fashion District and what not. Sure, there is construction going on, and some sidewalks are closed, but that was no big deal for us as we are from NYC. Clean rooms, cute decorating. Free internet, spacious rooms. I felt very safe in the hotel; security was top notch. 
The Bad:
We were a little confused on how to get here. The street starts out as a two way street, then changes to one way right in front of the hotel, so that threw us for a loop (or two) a few times. There is a new building being constructed across the street, but the view should be better once it's complete. Staples Center is near, which can be good if you're attending something there, but we did not realize that a championship game between the Lakers and Spurs was going on the first night of our stay, so it was kind of packed in the lobby and bar, but we probably should have researched that. 
The Ugly:
Paper thin walls. So, at just after midnight, there are kids screaming and running up and down the halls. The headboard of the bed next door (or maybe it was from upstairs) banged against our wall for about ten minutes. The customer service is terrible. We've called the front desk several times and rarely get an answer. Going to a Dodgers game, we asked the attendant to hail us a cab. What pulled up was a REALLY nice luxury sedan. The attendant said this to us: "Oh, here is our hotel's courtesy taxi. Enjoy your game!"
Now, there were three of us, and we all heard that. 
So, we get dropped off at the farthest place possible at the stadium, and as we get out of the car, the driver tells us that its a $30 charge. So much for a courtesy taxi.
Game was awesome, we call back to the hotel just shy of 9pm, asking for their "courtesy" taxi to come pick us up. She tells us that they have no courtesy taxis, just a taxi company they have a contract with and "every employee here KNOWS that." Then she says that all of the drivers have gone home for the day, so we should just call another taxi company. Then click. Didn't offer to call a company for us, much less give us the numbers to one. 
So its raining outside, and we found a cab parked MUCH closer to the stadium, and it was only $11 from the stadium to the hotel. This was even after we were stuck in traffic for a while. 
Bar closes at 10pm. 
Oh, and they don't have a free shuttle to and from the airport. 
Next trip to LA, we'll be looking for another hotel.

title: “Great staff”
text: We stayed at the Fairfield Inn for a hockey tournament. The staff were all very friendly, in particular the front desk. The hotel is super clean, the room we were in was spacious and clean, and the outside patio/grill area was a nice added perk, and so pleasant! Lots of good restaurants close by, and the hotel is not far from downtown so it was an easy drive to see/do stuff in Charlotte.

title: “Killer Location”
text: Enough with all these whiners. There's nothing wrong with this place. Yes, some of the furnishings are dated. But the bedding is brand new and fantastic. The equipment in the gym is state of the art. I had a little problem with my a/c and the engineer was there in three minutes to fix it. Every room has a balcony, with chairs. Mine overlooked the Riverwalk. Don't be deceived by all those hotels claiming to be "on the Riverwalk". Many are in very obscure locations, far from the restaurants and bars. The Hilton is right in the heart of it all. Come out of your room, take the elevator down, and BAM, you're on it. Great Irish pub right there.

title: “Awesome location for Orioles Park and M&T Stadium”
text: Got room from Hotwire for about half the price it actually goes for. Right next door to Orioles Park, perfect if your going to see a game. Modern looking mostly business hotel. Room was standard, bed was comfy, definately built for business travelers. 28 bucks a day for parking at the hotel, so keep that in mind if driving there. Had no problem checking in, quick and efficient. Would stay there again if the price was right.

title: “How to Ruin a Hotel Stay”
text:
I don't ask for much. A hotel that's worth the money with good service and speedy and accurate check in and out. The Andaz, a boutique hotel that is trying a bit too hard to be trendy, was a failure for us. It started out a bit weak. The hotel is difficult to find with no discernable marking and only one spot out front. Nevertheless they managed to take the car after we doubleparked and brought in the luggage. They have the oh-so-cool kiosks with young staff dressed in black. We were in quickly. The room was ok, nice modern bathroom, obligatory impossible to figure out lighting and minimal free snacks. But ok.
Nice big bedand we had a good sleep. Excellent breakfast. Brought our stuff down and checked it with the bellmen and told them to keep our car until later. Got the claim checks and went out for the day. When we checked out at 4 the chaos began. They charged us $300 for a late check out (we left at 11:30). The brought us the wrong luggage. Then the wrong car! (worse then mine so I sent it back). They tried to console us but the damage was done. Pay a little more attention to service and a little less to trying to be hip (impossible in NYC--the hotel is so 2010). Please, no canned management comment about how sorry you are. Own up to it and travelers will return.

title: “Brilliant location, clean and friendly hotel.”
text: The headline really says it all. We had four quiet and comfortable nights here. The staff were very kind and helpful. The room whilst a little small was clean throughout the stay and the bed was superb with fresh linen daily. The location couldn't have been bettered for the price. We would recommend this hotel to all.

title: “Not 5 stars but impressive makeover, fantastic location and service”
text:
I stayed at this hotel while attending a business conference for 4 nights. The hotel is in an ideal location to all downtown attractions. Literally within walking distance of everything you would need or want to see. I was impressed at the modern decor and attractiveness of the lobby and bar. I was also impressed by the room. It had great window with a view of downtown, super comfy beds, a large armoire and roomy dressing area and the room was very tastefully decorated. The room was also quite clean. I found the staff to be always incredibly friendly and helpful, so much so that it really stood out for the service alone. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay and it was perfect for my business trip. 
There are only a few negative things about my experience: that there were a few minor details that needed tweaked in the room such as a small area of peeling wallpaper, recent repair that was not yet painted on the ceiling. (honestly though the rest of the room was so clean and nice it didn't bother me) The elevator is old and during one break in the conference when it was enduring a lot of use, it just quit and we all had to use the stairs. I ordered room service 3 times for convenience and it not only took a long time to get my food but the food was alway just mediocre. There was no refrigerator in the room, a small one to keep drinks cold would have been a nice touch. 
All in all, this is a nice hotel with great service, comfy rooms, great decor and a location that cannot be beat. This place is perfect for business. I would skip eating at the hotel though (at least room service). There are some fantastic places within walking distance or a short cab ride for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

title: “Fabulous hotel - great location.”
text: We had planned to stay at the Affinia Chicago for four nights in April. But then the Icelandic volcano erupted, and we ended up staying for nine nights! But we couldn't have chosen a better hotel (or city) to be stranded in. The Affinia is just steps away from the Magnificent Mile, and our room on the 25th floor looked across to Big John - the John Hancock Tower. The room was a good size, the bathroom was fine. There was no mirror in the main room, which was a bit odd. And the coffee machine never really worked that well. But the bed was superb - we chose buckwheat pillows - very nice to sleep on. The staff were superb - always courteous and helpful - and they didn't try rip us off when we had to stay extra nights because of the volcano. Regarding local restaurants, we weren't impressed with pizzas at Gino's East next door - but far nicer was The Indian Garden on E Ontario; and Ditka's (owned my Chicago Bears favourite, Mike Ditka).

title: “GREAT Location - Clean - Friendly”
text:
If you want a affordable and clean room to stay, in a wonderful area and close to transport this is your place. Close to the freedom trail, nice restaurants, Newbury st shopping. 
Stayed for half a week and loved it. Nothing to complain about. Staff dealt with anything minor with a smile on their face and helped with directions. 
Recommend to anyone wanted a trip to Boston. Will use again. :)

title: “OK”
text: Nicer on the outside. Room smelled like smoke in a non-smoking room. Noisy air con.

title: “Didn't want to leave!”
text: We had our best hotel experience here! Everyone we came into contact with was exceptionally nice and helpful. We were expecting big city feel but received a small town welcome! From the amazing breakfast to the wine reception, fresh baked cookies and turn down service with bottled water and chocolates every night we had trouble going home! Thanks Wayne for your amazing hospitality and suggestions of things to do/see and eat in the city. We loved the boutique feel of the hotel and thought it was exceptionally clean. The hotel has a super great location on a quiet side street but right downtown in the middle of everything. Everyone was so nice and helpful from booking our hotel room to reserving a cab for our departure we sure felt spoiled! Thanks again for everything. We'd make a trip back to the city just to stay here again!

title: “Spring getaway”
text: Perfect place to stay for the price. Rooms are clean and comfortable. Service is abundant and very friendly. Great place for kids. Pool is nice but you may need to make sure towels are available. Continental breakfast is somewhat modified. Great central location to see all that San Diego has to offer. Free parking.

title: “Best Pool in San Diego”
text: I have stayed at several hotels in San Diego and this is the only one I have stayed in that I have bothered to review. The rooms are a little small I think but very clean. The views are spectacular and the staff is great. I would definitely choose this hotel again. LOVE the pool!!!!

title: “Great service...great food!”
text: The hotel was super clean, great service and great breakfast and lunch. Can't wait to go back again!

title: “Great city hotel”
text: Spectacular service from arrival to departure. Valet greets you with towel and water bottle after a morning jog. Great dining at shuckers. Easy location to all major Seattle sights. We even walked to game at Safeco Field

title: “Nice Budget & Family Friendly Hotel”
text: Stayed here with two family members and it was a decent choice. The location wasn't as good as the Renaissance Times Square or the Waldorf, the other 2 NYC hotels I've stayed at, but for the money, the location was not bad, especially to the Broadway theaters. And the value is excellent with the free full breakfast. Only small criticism is that the breakfast area gets super busy, where long lines can form. Other than that, this hotel was clean, staff were polite and accommodating, and I give this place 2 thumbs up!

title: “Right in Midtown, can't beat it!”
text: Had a weekend at the Roosevelt for a friends birthday. Found a godo price for the Roosevelt for the wknd. Right in Midtown so can't beat that...the rooms were roomy, the classic decor for the hotel, but nice and clean and didnt smell old. The lobby was terribly crowded all the time, but that is to be expected for the location. Would stay again! Would go back to check out the Rooftop Bar Mad 46 once the weather gets nicer.

title: “You are in New York! its a place to crash after a busy day!”
text:
We arrived after midnight and were very tired, the night receptionist was lovely very helpful he checked us in quickly and efficiently. They had double booked so put us for the first night into a top floor suite, i was quietly disapointed on seeing this as it had two rooms but only one bed and a pull out sofa bed. We looked for extra bedding and there was none apart from a sheet and a pillow already on the pull out bed. Who cares we were so tired it didnt matter! the next day we were moved to a 7th floor room and that was fine.
The rooms seemed clean, they provided an ironing board, hairdrier etc normal things.
There is an ice machine on the 7th floor. There is no mini bar.
I am used to having a safety deposit box in the room and was disappointed to have one in the reception area, so didnt bother and kept my stuff with me.
It would have been nice to have a kettle in the room, perhaps thats just a British thing, its quite sad but we bought tea bags and boiled water through the coffee maker(you have to be quite resourceful).
Breakfasts were ok, you are seated on arrival in the dining room and offered orange juice and tea, coffee or chocolate.
Most of the menu involved an egg in some form or another, the pancakes were nice and the french toast was lovely! They always offered just Corn flakes but there were quite a few others so just ask.
Every thing was charged separately and we had a priority club card which had points accumulated on it and this provided a discount of $10 off the bill.(it normally cost around $20.00 for 2 of us each morning.
The location was really good its near most of the attractions we only had one taxi and walked back every night from the Time Square area.
We regretted only turning right out of the hotel every day when on the last day we discovered the amazing cafes and resturants when you turn LEFT! 
This hotel was practical its all you need if your priority is sightseeing and sleeping(recovering from blistered feet!). 
Sign up to the Priority Club card through this chain of hotels as we had accumulated enough points to benefit from 2 free nights and a discounted breakfast. (It all helps as you can spend the extra on a good show or some Comedy Club tickets.

title: “Amazing Hotel - Be careful though...”
text:
I stayed in the WOW suite ($599.00 per night) and it was amazing. The view was the best part. The 158 sq. foot baclony overlooks the American Airlines Center. The rooms are nice, but definitely could be nicer given the price.
The Good: The Hotel is very hip and trendy. Friendly staff. I was escorted to my room. Great pool even though it should face the opposite direction towards Dallas. The bed was very comfortable and the showers were nice. 
The Bad: The price...WAY TOO EXPENSIVE. It's not worth it. I'd pay $400 maybe for what I had. You have to be very very careful about what your final charge will be. They nickle and dime you to no end! Everything is overpriced. My room was $599 and my final bill was over $800!!!! I got a room, a beer, and some jelly beans and next thing I know I get an $800 charge. Absolutely insane. I will not stay there again to be honest.
Helpful tips: Don't tip the valet until after you check out ($24 overnight). Bring your own alcohol. Hide it in your luggage. Don't eat anything at the hotel or in the room!!! Don't touch anything that has a seal on it or you'll get charged. Be prepaired to pay much much more in taxes for the room. There's a list a mile long of different taxes. USE A CREDIT CARD! NOT A DEBIT CARD! If you use a debit card to pay, they will pre-authorize your account with a very very large amount of money (my room $599, they authorized $840). They say it's to cover any incidental damage if needed. They won't tell you any of this when you check in. 
Overall, the hotel was very nice and my guests has a great time. I won't be going back there until I'm a multi-millionaire without a care in the world about what I'm charged. If you don't know to ask something, they won't tell you so keep reading these reviews. On a scale of 1 to 10, I give it a 6.
Bottom line: If you're filthy rich, this is the place for you.

title: “Great stay”
text: Checking in was a breeze and we got in earlier. After a long flight from Australia and then LAX this was very welcome. We had booked a double so the room was large enough. The bathroom was adequately sized for three of us and was clean. We paid for a fridge which turned out to be a good idea as we could store food and drinks that we bought from the Saveway across the road. This was also a bonus as there was a Radio Shak that we bought our cheap phone from. The only downside was where our room was which was above the driveway. This was quite noisy at night when your trying to sleep. My advice is try not to get these rooms! Otherwise good location and clean.

title: “Great Place”
text: The hotel is very nice. The front desk staff could not have been nicer when I checked in. I signed up for the Select Guest program and it was totally worth it. Free coffee delivered in the morning (and you can order a really delicious blueberry muffin to be delivered also for only $2.95 extra), newspaper and internet. My room was very nice and the housekeeping service was very good also. My neighbors were a tiny bit loud in the halls (talking really loud, calling out to each other down the call and slamming their doors), but that is true most places and was no worse at the Omni. The elevators tends to be very crowded, but the riders are mostly jovial and make room for you. I ate one crab salad meal at the restaurant and it was really delicious. The fitness center was spotless and had surprisingly nice equipment and plenty of it. The Metro stop right across the street makes it so easy to get around and there are a lot of great restaurants in walking distance also. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Amazing Hotel”
text: We stayed here on our road trip around the west. It had great service, great location (close to Phoenix), very clean, cheap, and a good warm breakfast. Staff were pleasant. Room was clean.

title: “......Do You and Your Family a Favor, Stay Somewhere Else!”
text: We were in San Antonio for the San Antonio Rock and Roll marathon Nov. 13th, 2011. We decided on the Rodeway Inn based on price and location. Well, be careful! You get what you pay for. It was so bad that my wife decided to stay with family that live on the outskirts of San Antonio. Although the room was "non-smoking", there were ashtrays on the table and nightstand AND the room smelled of cigarette smoke. We had to call the front office for a TV remote. They brought one of the universal remotes and even asked me to program it. I would not step foot in the shower. It was very dirty and there was what appeared to be mold on the caulking. I'm not sure about the location, but there were a few people walking the parking lot that seemed to be a bit suspicious. I called the front office requesting a 6:10AM wake up call. I got the wake up call, only at 5AM instead of the requested 6:10AM. We will look elsewhere for another hotel next year. I will gladly pay more for a nice, clean and reliable place to stay.

title: “On Duport Circle--convenient to Metro and all of DC”
text:
We normally stay at another hotel close by, but decided to give the Dupont a try. We were pleasantly surprised, but it is not for everyone. I would stay here again if my favorite hotel is totally booked.
Pros: Great location on the circle, close to Metro station, free wi-fi, and we were able to walk practically everywhere. The wall-to-wall windows on the lobby level give a great view to all the action outside. The entire hotel is very modern and stylish, but the atmosphere is still warm and inviting with great service. There is coffee in the lobby and many places to just sit and lounge, and The Cafe was convenient for a nice weekend brunch. We were impressed by the large bathroom, which was spacious and modern, with a heated floors and an actual functioning window (in the shower area). The beds were also very nicely dressed with triple-sheeting and cozy duvet.
Con: Stayed in a double-bed room with 3 people and it was very tight. With 2 beds and a huge desk, the room size was better suited for a single king bed. As stated in other reviews, there is no door to the bathroom area--the vanity area is open to the room--and the only door is a frosted glass door separating the vanity area from the toilet and shower. People not comfortable with sharing their personal space may look elsewhere. Poeple looking for a bathtub will also be disappointed. There is only a glass partition separating the toilet and shower, meaning a lot of water everywhere. The plantation shutters on the windows look nice, but not very functional as the sun started shining through the slats--a huge negative for anyone wanting to sleep in.

title: “Good Price, Good Location, Good Hotel”
text:
This was our first trip to San Francisco and we chose this hotel based on the reviews from TripAdvisor. We were not disappointed. If you want lots of extras, this isn't the place for you, but it is a very basic hotel with everything you'd expect. The free parking was a huge bonus. It's within easy walking distance of Pier 39 and all the other Piers and attractions that are on the way to it (Hyde St. Pier, Giradelli Square). It is also a doable walk to North Beach (don't miss this neighborhood), if you don't mind walking up a few monstrous hills, we did it.
The breakfast in the morning was nothing to brag about, just some fruit (either apples or bananas) and then some pastries. The rooms all have coffee makers in them.
All in all considering the price, location, and free parking, I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone, especially if they don't need a 5 star hotel to feel comfortable. You won't be disappointed.

title: “Not as enjoyable as it used to be”
text: We've stayed here three times in the past and this last visit will be our last. We had asked for a quiet room and were put on the ground floor. It was very noisy due to the foot traffic and road noise. The most annoying part were the pizza flyers that were stuck in our door at late hours of the night and early morning waking us from our sleep. This is not the hotel's doing but they could have monitored this a little better. The room itself was clean and fine if you just need a place to sleep and the location is central but we will be staying elsewhere next time.

title: “Excellent Location”
text: Good location, close to all of the downtown hotspots, staff was excellent

title: “Great location for Home Base”
text:
Arrived and was in awe by the most elegant lobby. The check in was easy and fast, but moreover got some great tips on local eateries and a fantastic little wine bar not far. Room was super clean on the Executive level. Bath was small, but would expect that in San Fran - but a little counter space would be nice. 
Restaurant and Bar above average and wait staff very pleasant and fun to talk with. The wine tasting was fun and discovered a little bit more about "wine country". 
Major plus was the responsiveness of every person who works at this hotel. I felt appreciated and moreover like a friend. By the 4th night most staff that I encountered called me by name. Very nice way to end a day of sightseeing. 
Highly recommend.

title: “outstanding on all fronts”
text: Stayed here in early January with 18 year old daughter. This place is very well positioned opposite Penn Station and a short walk from Times Square. The rooms are a little bit dated but clean, warm and more than comfortable. Our room was huge and had a functional kitchen. We ended up staying an extra 5 nights after snow storm closed JFK causing us to miss out on our flight but nothing was a problem and the staff were most helpful. The hotel bar is as good as you will find within walking distance and more comfortable than most of the tourist trap bars around Times Square. Very good gym on site as well. Would not stay anywhere else based upon this experience.

title: “Good Value for the Price”
text:
I stayed at The Hayden Hotel in April, 2006. I got a single room w/private bath. The bathroom was literally 3 ft. wide by about 12 ft. long but it was very clean, had new tile and new fixtures, and I was never without hot water. Showerhead was one of those typically weak, watersaver kinds found in most motels. 
I had 2 twin beds in my room even though I had requested a double bed but I didn't ask for a change because a twin was fine for me. One of the twin beds was hard as a rock. The other was a little softer but still too firm for my taste. The room was heated by radiator which worked fine and there is a window that opens when you need fresh air. I was on the 7th floor, very far from street noise so I slept well. 
The only noise problem I experienced was because the door to my room seemed to be too thin to keep the noise of guests in the halls out. I could hear people talking and walking to their rooms at 1, 2 and 4 in the morning but once they got inside their rooms the noise was gone.
The lighting in my room was OK but the lightbulb in the bathroom was very dim. They did change it for me when I asked.
My room cost $140 a night not including the ridiculous 14.5% city tax. For New York prices at the last minute, this was about the lowest price around. The Hayden is located 1 block from a 24-hour diner, 1 block from a 24-hour Duane Reade drugstore, and 2 blocks from the subway. A very convenient location!
The room was small but clean. Night desk staff was more helpful and brighter than the day desk staff. I peeked into the shared bathrooms and they were very large and also very clean. I would stay there again and recommend this place to friends.
