title: “Excellent position, reasonable breakfast but public areas a little small”
text:
Hi 
I satayed here with my wife and 2 daughters in July 2012 using reward nights. Having stayed in a couple of the UK SBS I was unsure about what to expect as while over here they are quite spacious but I know from previous trips to New York that space there is at a premium and in retrospect that is the only slight down side to this hotel. The room was a squash with the 4 of us in it and the public areas are not big enough for the number of people in the hotel, I did on one occasion have to eat my breakfast standing up. 
However the rooms were spotless and modern with all the amenities you could require, the gym was satisfactory and never busy, the free food and drink between 5pm and 7pm is always welcome and while the wine was a little rough the beer was very welcome as were the snacks and finally the breakfast was also acceptable. What I also appreciated was the PC and printer access in the reception which you can use to print out boarding cards, vouchers etc.
All in all this is a nice hotel and gives you what you need
Tips: If you walk out of the hotel and turn left on the corner you will find a $0.99 a slice pizza place that is very nice, if you turn left again and walk up that street (9th Ave) there is a number of reasonably priced restaurants and take-away food shops as well as shops that sell wine, beer and food
Hope this helps

title: “Great Place to stay”
text: Our family of four enjoyed our recent 4 night stay at The Talbott Hotel. The location of the hotel is great. Delaware Place is a quiet side street running between the main avenues. You can walk to almost all of the main tourist sites or go for a run along Lake Michigan. The subway, taxi's and bus system can get you anywhere else you need to go. We never had a need for a car. All of the staff is outstanding and friendly! The concierge is great and helped us book several tours and shows. From the doormen to the maid service, everyone had a smile and was always helpful. There is a stylish restaurant and sidewalk cafe adjoining the hotel that provides an attractive place to hangout if you get tired of spending time in your room or just want to have breakfast or a cocktail. Should we have the good fortune to return to Chicago, we will stay at The Talbott again!

title: “Perfect after a long flight”
text:
I chose this hotel because of the reviews and the location.
After a long flight from AMS to IAH and the long line at the immigration we had to drive 40 miles from the airport to this hotel. It was our first in Houston and it was a good choice.
Vipor, the man at the front desk was extremely nice and we got a nice room on the first floor as requested. There were free chocolate chip cookies in the lobby and there is a nice pool which unfortunately we didn't use. The room was clean, spacious and even had a plant in it !
A fake plant but I like the created atmosphere. There were glasses (no plastic cups very good) and the bed was comfortable. Breakfast in the morning was fine and check out quick.
The hotel is perfectly located if you want to visit the Kemah Boardwalk or the Johnson Space Center. Do not hesitate, book this hotel !

title: “Location, Location, Location!”
text: I have found Holiday Inn hotels to always be clean and comfortable. This was no exception, but what we liked most was the location. 2 blocks from Fisherman's Wharf and walking distance to Pier 39 and other atrractions. Would stay again and reccomend.

title: “I wasn't used to this kind of luxury!”
text: My wife and I stayed here the first two nights of our honeymoon. We stayed here as a stop before we headed up to Maine for the remainder of our honeymoon. Since it was our honeymoon, I booked the nicest room within reason in this hotel. We were on the top floor with an excellent view of the city skyline. The view was impressive and if you're afraid of heights, it's not for you! The room itself was impressively large for an NYC hotel room. It was very clean, the bed looked spectacular and was VERY comfortable. The TV was a large flat screen. The bathroom was very nice as well. The shower had duel shower heads and had lots of room for the both of us to have some fun in there! The hotel's location is great, within walking distance of the Broadway Show we saw and plenty of great restaurants. It is within easy walking distance of the subway for further ventures. The rest of the hotel was spectacular and the amenities were first class. When you pull up in front of the hotel, be ready with the valet key to your car. The bell hops help get your vehicle unloaded and then it's taken away. You won't get it back until you stay is over. Be prepared to shell out $50 plus a day to have the vehicle stored for you... The hotel was expensive, but the over all feel was in that price range. I am not the type of guy and probably won't ever drop that kind of cash again. For a special occasion, this place is great!

title: “Great Stay at a Great Price!”
text: I spent one evening at the Hilton while in NYC on business. The staff were super-friendly--from the front desk to the concierge. They went out of their way to welcome me and make me feel comfortable. The rooms were well-appointed and of typical size for Manhattan hotels. The hotel is very centrally located with plenty of places to eat and shop in the area. And the price for my Sunday evening stay was reasonable by NYC standards. I would DEFINITELY stay here again!

title: “Great Staff, Great Location, Great Place”
text: The staff were wonderful! The front desk clerks were kind, thoughtful, helpful. I can't say enough nice things about the staff throughout the weekend of a conference I attended. The room was exceptionally comfortable to me-beds, TV, balcony. The little things make a difference. Friendliness and helpfulness from everyone I met-housekeepers, dining room, valets, bellmen, I especially appreciated Socorro, Diego, Josie, and Orlando who helped me feel comfortable at a conference. For instance, Orlando drove a golf cart to help me and my bags get to the rooms. I enjoyed the pools. There are several different pools in various locations so that helped as far as helping people be comfortable. I really enjoyed the grounds and the location because we were able to catch public transportation easily for our times to sight-see. The food was great, too!

title: “great stay”
text: my family got together for our parents 50th anniversary in mid july.. the hotel, while far more expensive than our usual accomadations, was well worth the extra money. It was conviently located in the center of the inner harbor. our party consisted of 14 children from 18yrs. old to 1. we found that the second floor bridge allowed us to cross pratt st safely with the kids without worrying about traffic. The rooms were very large and clean. the pool was clean and well staffed. check-in was a breeze. Cleveland Indians in town that weekend, stayed at the hotel.skip the valet parking, and park your own car. You'll save money, and be able to access your vehicle whenever you please. This will not be possible if using the valet service.

title: “Tired and uncaring staff”
text:
Have fond memories of staying here about 5 years ago, but upon my return I was thoroughly disappointed. The staff are uncaring and seem to do the bare minimum required (nothing is more frustrating when receptionists/concierges interrupt your conversation with them to answer the phone- or speak to another member of staff)
We stayed on the Exec floor and as a family were offered 2 rooms on different floors- we weren't escorted to the rooms, or explained anything about the hotel, which is strange considering we were there for leisure for a few nights and weren't regular guests. 
There are definitely other better places to stay nearby for better value.

title: “Average Marriott, But in Top 5 Downtown”
text:
I stayed at this Marriott for approximately 5 months and I will say it is as average as it comes. The staff is great and concierge lounge is nice and large and a bit nicer than average, but the decor is a bit outdated in some rooms, the fitness center is small for this size of the hotel, and elevators don’t seem to handle the morning traffic. However, when looking downtown LA, there's really not too many that are better for the business traveler.
As with other hotels downtown, the busyness of this hotel ebbs and flows when there are conventions in town or when the foreign bus tours are in town. When that happens, it seems to slow everything down dramatically. Waiting for an elevator between 8am-9am can be painful even if you are on a high floor as you'll stop at every floor and the elevator will likely be crowded with tourists with huge suitcases. If you're on a low floor, good luck with the stairs or the maintenance elevators. Over the months I was there (May- Oct) the issues with the elevators were always apparent whenever the hotel was near capacity. All in all that's only a minor setback, but can grow to be a major annoyance if you stay here for a while.
There really aren't too many options downtown for the average business traveler, but this hotel offers all of the standard amenities you'd expect for in a Marriott. If you stay for a while, the staff becomes even friendlier as they get to know you… once again kind of what you expect from this tier of hotel, but you don’t always find that everywhere you go.

title: “Trendy Boutique Hotel near DuPont Circle”
text: We stayed for a girls birthday weekend celebration and had a very pleasant stay.. Our room was very spacious, trendy and in a good location close to nightlife. The staff was very attentive and friendly. We did not bring any pets but noticed it was a pet friendly hotel and a few guests brought their dogs. All in all it was a great deal (we purchased on Hotwire).

title: “An ace hotel!”
text: A very reasonably priced hotel in a great location in Seattle. We spent two nights here and found the room and staff to be great. The communal showers were immaculate and we never had to queue. The breakfast was also great. There was a bit of street noise coming from below (we were on the first floor) but there were ear plugs in our room. I would also highly recommend the bar (Cyclops) below the hotel.

title: “Not a 4 Star Hotel!”
text: This hotel somehow got a 4 star rating and it is not even close. The staff were great - so nice and accomodating - if I was rating this hotel just on Staff it would be 5 Stars. On the good side - location was really good. The restaurant in the hotel - Serafina was really good. The staff were great. The rooms - not so much. If this was listed as a 3 Star hotel I'd say okay it is fine. But as a 4 star hotel? No way. It wasn't very clean (sheets and bathroom were but the carpet had stains and some of the walls were a bit sticky). It just didn't 'feel' clean. This hotel needs to be relisted as a 3 Star hotel and the rates should be more in the $160/night range.

title: “perfect hollywood location!”
text:
My sister and I stayed for 3 nights during July 09. Check in service was very friendly, pointed us in the right direction for things, surrounding attractions/buildings. Felt very welcomed.
We were in room 111 on the first floor, it was a very quiet apartment style room. We were very impressed with the full kitchen after having come from Las Vegas which were shoebox hotel rooms. We shared a super king bed (to try save on cost lol!), the bed was a bit uncomfortable - there was a plastic sheet on the mattress that acts as a protector I suppose, every time you move it makes a lot of noise so if you are a light sleeper this is going to annoy you.
Location cannot be beat - just through the back alleyway you hit the Hollywood walk of fame, Kodak Theare etc. We had lots of fun coming out several different times of the day to see which character dress ups we could take pictures with. We found a favourite diner, Johnny Rocket, which is located inside the Hollywood/Highland shopping centre. It was apparently Elvis' favourite burger joint! Burgers are priced from $5 upwards, very handy when you want a quick, cheap meal. 
The pool is very small, but the hotel is not big so I suppose it is adequate. We had fun just mucking round there.
Really appreciated the free breakfast every morning between 8-10am. The area gets quite crowded, there are only 4 sets of tables/chairs so we often took away breakfast in paper bags (provided). Breakfast included croissants, muffins, cakes and coffee/tea. The free internet station is also located in the breakfast area, so using the internet at this time is impossible. Very handy having this free service though - we had just come from hotels that charged $0.50 per minute!
Besides the uncomfy bed, I cannot fault this budget hotel. We paid $150 per night (including taxes), we were very happy with this rate as surrounding hotels so close to Hollywood attractions were much more. Just what we were after!

title: “A Generally Good Experience”
text:
We stayed here for two nights as we were in town for a short weekend trip, also our first trip to Boston. We chose this place because it looked ultra-modern (it is, it's a very visually striking place) and it's located extremely close to TD Banknorth Garden, which is where we were going to see a concert the second evening of our trip. 
Generally this was a good experience: the room was ready when we got there, the staff was welcoming, and we enjoyed the bar and breakfast (it's just a basic breakfast buffet but it was certainly convenient.) Getting to the subway was a piece of cake (it's just a block or two away,) and there are a few pubs and places to eat in the immediate area. 
Unfortunately my spouse and I left one of our belongings in the room (which we realized very shortly after checking out and immediately called about), and regrettably the staff was not especially helpful or empathetic. 
This one's obviously mostly on us for leaving something behind, but we had to call repeatedly to even get a yes or no as to whether they'd seen it, and it didn't seem like anyone at the hotel really cared about helping us. I wasn't expecting any sort of compensation or even that they would find the item in question, but I hoped they'd be able to let us know if they'd seen it within the day after we checked out. That sort of put a damper on things, considering it was a costly item and not easily replaced.
I would still say we had an overall good experience here and I would more or less recommend the place (I only wish it hadn't ended on that somewhat sour note).

title: “You take a chance by asking”
text: We have stayed at this hotel before and everthing is always excellent. So when we checked out and Ennio asked if everything was alright I got the impression he really wanted to know. It wasn't a question just asked by rote. And then I thought, Wow, he must be very confident about the answer he would get. New Yorkers and New York tourists are quite fussy and very vocal when things aren't right. And, of course, the answer he got was "great, as usual". By the way, the room was quiet, clean and the bed was heavenly. Breakfast was included and you couldn't have asked for better. You can plan a trip to this hotel with confidence.

title: “OK for a night”
text:
Needing a place to stop for the night, we pulled in (no reservation). Had I read the reviews, I would have kept going, but it just proves what they say about opinions.......
The front desk people were nice and helpful, rate was $50, nice exterior, room OK, funky smell but clean, bed comfortable, carpet worn, continental breakfast the norm, next door to off site airport parking garage but no noise. The experience was about what I expected; not the Ritz but OK for one night.

title: “super stay!!!!”
text: everything was great. the rooms are clean. you need a car when you stay in this hotel.

title: “Great Value, Great Service, Great Location”
text: We really loved this hotel. We stayed over the Thanksgiving holiday and we were close to the attractions. A quick walk to Roc Center, Radio City Music Hall, Times Square, St Patrick's, great shopping. We booked is just a week in advance and got a very competitive rate, and yet, the service was excellent. Evening turndown service, when they refreshed our towels, filled the ice bucket and left us chocolate. The bellman brought our luggage upstairs and coordinated the parking and pick up of our vehicle. Front desk was friendly and clearly on the ball. They were in the middle of coordinating a returning soldier's marriage proposal to his girlfriend, trying to make it as special as possible and simultaneously being friendly and professional with our check-in. Housekeeping did a great job getting us our rollaway bed and later they phoned to confirm that it had in fact arrived. When we passed the cleaners in the halls, they were super friendly and seemed to like their jobs. Best of all, no bugs! I checked thoroughly. We dined in the restaurant and the chef came out front to check on our meal and the waitstaff could not have been better. Even the elevators were rapid and not crowded. The folks at the concierge desk seemed also to love their jobs. The beds: I slept like a baby -- very comfie bed with white sheets and spotless white comforters. There was also a comfortable chair and ottoman in the room as well as plenty of closet space and lamps that dimmed -- and it was a very quiet room we heard nothing. We were on the 15th floor. Little comforts that added up to a great stay.

title: “Great hideaway location”
text: The staff is always top notch, especially the guys out front. This is a great hideaway location off Dupont Circle next to Kalorama neighborhood. Starbucks is just down the street. The bar is one of my favourite dark, paneled bars with a fire. Perfect place to get away from the crowds. Small and intimate describes this entire hotel. The lobby is small, rooms are good size and the new renamed restaurant is very good. The Jockey Club name is gone but the food remains the same. Competent but pricey. Still kudos to the staff; after many visits they always have been kind to us.

title: “impeccable Hotel - Perfect Location”
text: My husband and i stayed at the Four Seasons in New York for 4 fabulous nights. We loved the hotel, the service, the elegant surroundings, the location. Everything was perfect. I had very high expectations and they were met, as one would expect from a Four Seasons property. It was very expensive, but I suppose, in the end - you get what you pay for!! If you are looking to treat yourself in a great city like New York, I don't think you could go past this hotel.

title: “Excellent Service and Great Hotel”
text: You cannot beat the service, from the minute you walk in the door. The rooms are very modern (some Embassy Suites are getting dated) and the happy hour is nice with lots of snacks. The breakfast was excellent and plentiful and the staff was just fantastic. The rooms were very clean as well.

title: “Another great stay - friendly staff, no issues, definitely recommend for a short stay”
text:
I stayed at this Super 8 location on my first trip to Los Angeles back in 2004, and rebooked for January 21-23, 2011 after deciding to take a last-minute surf holiday. 
I was able to find a highly discounted rate on priceline for $52.00 per night, which was excellent considering it was a weekend. As the Super 8 is a value chain, of course one can't go there expecting the Ritz-Carlton! With that being said, the staff were great from start to finish, very nice people. Before even completing my request for a cab company number, they were on the phone calling for me. Great customer service!
This location has a free shuttle service to and from LAX. They can be contacted at any of the courtesy phone touch-screen kiosks that are located in just about every baggage claim area. You are patched directly to the front desk, they'll waste no time answering, will tell you exactly where to wait, and the shuttle will arrive quickly.
On this particular visit, I stayed in room 230, and everything was in excellent shape. The only thing I noticed was that the king bed was actually two twins that were pushed together, but I didn't realize this until it was time to check out so obviously didn't have any issues. The room was located overlooking the courtyard, which was a lot quieter that the room on the parking lot side I had on my last visit. Free wifi is always a big plus, and the Greek restaurant at the rear of the property is awesome - Aliki's Greek Taverna. 
The property has a pool, free coffee/tea, and complimentary cereals and toast, although I didn't utilize any of these amenities. The ice machine in the parking lot was in great working order and could only be turned on by inserting a room key.
As some other reviewers have mentioned, yes, airplane noise will be heard. I've talked to lots of friends that have stayed in just about every hotel in the LAX airport area, as far as 8 miles down the road from the terminals, and this is not a problem that's unique with just the Super 8, you'll get it anywhere. If noise is an issue, book miles away from the airport.
I was having a hard time finding locations of nearby stores and restaurants within walking distance before my trip, and this area is generally nothing but hotels and rental car agencies, so here's what's around: Burger King is on Airport Blvd. about a block and a half away, on the opposite side of the road. It's visible from the front of the property. 7 Eleven is up the road in the other direction, on the corner of Airport Blvd. and Manchester Ave. Walking down Westchester will take you directly into an area of Sepulveda Blvd. which has In N Out Burger, Ralph's Supermarket, Boston Market, Pizza Hut, and many others.
Great stay. Definitely recommend!

title: “Beautiful Hotel, warm and welcoming”
text: My sister and I stayed in Omni Parker Hotel from 14th January for 3 nights. When we arrived at reception. we were informed that we had received a complimentary upgrade to Junior Suite. What a great start to our holiday. The room (804) had 2 double beds (sooo comfortable) and plenty of room besides. The bathroom was tiny but what the hell.... We ate breakfast in the restaurant every morning $21 each. The buffet was adequate but the selection was much smaller than previous years. Staff were very friendly and helpful. The area is marvellous adjacent to T, Shops, restaurants. We loved our stay. The hotel is warm and welcoming. We will definitely return. Maureen

title: “Wonderful Honeymoon Destination”
text:
My husband and I were looking for a good honeymoon hotel. We stayed at The Library on the recommendation of a good friend. We were very pleased with our stay. Each of the rooms has its own theme, and is equipped with theme-related books. When my husband made the reservation, he booked us into the larger "Love" room with the Erotica Package, which included many tasty and fun amenities. The staff was very friendly and helpful upon check-in. The complimentary daily wine and cheese reception was fantastic, as was the complimentary breakfast. The rooftop bar is very expensive, but a wonderful place with views of the New York Public LIbrary and the beautiful expanse of Madison Avenue.
Our reservation actually included two rooms. The "Fashion Design" room was the same basic configuration as the "Love" room, but was a bit larger. The "Love" room has a lovely terrace overlooking Madison and 42nd. In lieu of the terrace, the other .006 rooms have more floor space - very large, in fact, by NYC hotel standards. Both of our rooms were very comfortable. The beds where plush, and the linens seemingly new.
Finally, because of horrible winter weather, we had to leave our hotel a day early, after the standard checkout time. The hotel staff was unbelievably helpful. The doorman braved the elements and knee-high deep snow and actually found us a cab. And the hotel desk clerk did not charge us for the last day of our stay. Excellent service with no problems.

title: “We were extremely pleased with our stay! Wouldn't hesitate to recommend.”
text: My daughter and I just got home from a 10 nights stay at Hotel Alexander, in NYC. Having read the reviews of others, many of them negative, we were unsure what to expect. We shared a double bed, which was very comfortable, had a T.V., 2 nite stands w/ lamps and large closet.. The room was small but clean and located next to one of the 2 shared bathrooms, which was nice. Our stay was wonderful! My only complaint is the lounge (free coffee) was closed but the hotel staff were very pleasant/helpful. The location is ideal, close to the subway and the main road, Broadway, has several nice restaurants/shops/markets etc. McDonald's too. We walked to Museums, Central Park and with the Metor card, we were able to get everywhere we wanted to go within minutes. While our room had "no view", we only used it to sleep & shower. The rest of our time we were seeing that amazing city. We found all the many people we encountered to be very friendly and helpful. We LOVED NYC!!!!

title: “You might want to think about it...”
text:
We took my 16 year old daughter and a friend to S.A. Oct. 18th and 19th...First problem was that they got the date wrong and charged my credit card for the room a week before our stay. When I called to inquire about the charge, they explained that they had us down for the 11th and thought that we had stayed, and so charged the card. They resolved the issue by "comping" the room on the 18th, so we were all even.
Upon arrival at 3:15 PM (check-in is 3:00 PM), we were informed that the room was not ready because they had a full house and that they could not tell us how long it would be before it was ready. It turned out to be 1 1/2 hours later!
We stayed in a 2 room jacuzzi suite so the girls could sleep on the sleeper sofa. When we asked for linens for the sofa, we were told that they had a full house so they only had sheets-no pillows or blanket available. I don't know what percentage of full they are actually equipped to handle.
On the bright side, the pool and hot tub outdoors is nice, but we were unable to use it in the evening as they had a private dinner, so you might want to check that all of the facilities will actually be available prior to staying here.
The room was reasonably clean, although we found some envelopes left behind by the previous guests. The room was large, but there is not a kitchenette, although there is a refrigerator and a microwave in the living area. There are no plates, etc, so you need to bring your own. 
The best thing about the room was that the bathroom is very large and the jacuzzi is suitably large for 2.
Although the hotel was unable to provide a timely check-in, they had no problems making sure that the complimentary breakfast foods were picked up and gone by the 10:00 AM end time. They couldn't get anything else done with a full house except that.
The manager's special of free drinks from 5:00 to 7:00 is a nice touch, but again, the bartender showed up a few minutes late. Although I wasn't at the bar at 7:00, I'll bet he was gone on time though!
Overall, we were disappointed in our stay and wouldn't stay there again, although I wouldn't be just miserable if I had to stay there again for some reason. I think that in this price range, you would enjoy the Marriot Residence Inn much more. You might also want to think about spending another $50 and trying the La Valencia. The hotel itself is reasonably nice, but the service fails to meet expectations for the price range.

title: “Always a Great Stay”
text:
My husband and I love to escape to San Francisco for the weekend. The Hyatt Embarcadero is always dependable for a clean, quiet, and relaxing stay. A perfect couples weekend hotel. The staff is attentive and friendly. The rooms are nice. The bar and restaurant in the Lobby are nice and not too overpriced.
The ferry building across the way is always dependable for something to eat or drink. . Location is fantastic. A definite favorite hotel of mine!

title: “Beyond my exectations”
text:
I recently stayed at the Manchester Hyatt San Diego for three days. I was very please with the service from the from desk to maid services.
The hotel has outstanding facilities, the rooms are pretty average for a Hyatt hotel but the size are acceptable. The hotel is divided in two towers one of them has been completed renovated in 2007. I stayed at the old tower but I did not see any of the complaints from previous travelers.
I went to the free gym (there is another one for club members only) but it was more than what I needed the equipment was excellent and the gym was very clean.
The pool is managed just like any other big resort with full day of activities (most of the free of charge) 
I was there for a conference I was also very impress with the ballrooms and the business center.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to everyone specially families.

title: “Perfect location, friendly service, great value.”
text: Hotel is an older building, but inside is very nice. Check-in was smooth as could be, they upgraded our room from 2 doubles to a queen for free. Would of went to king but there wasn't any available. Rooms are small but we aren't living In it Just sleeping so it was fine. Bathroom wasn't as small as some reviews made It seem but it is pretty narrow and long. Shower was great. Only complaint I have with hotel is the breakfast. $15 a person for the buffet and it wasn't good at all. Total waste of money, especially when there are tons of restaurants within a quarter mile walk. Rest of our 2 night stay was fabulous. Location was everything.

title: “Nice hotel; attractions within one mile”
text:
We had a large queen suite with sofa, easy chair, desk, and TV. Water pressure, lighting and air-conditioning: excellent. Furnishing, carpets and curtains were in "mid-life" but kept clean. Only one nightstand. Coffee-maker located in an alcove immediately outside the bathroom on a good-sized counter. No clothes drying cord in bathroom. Walls: Thin. Could hear water/shower running next door; otherwise quiet on 12th floor. Wired and wireless internet available. Must ask for the free WiFi code at the desk. Walking distance (about one mile) to major historical attractions such as the Liberty Bell. Banks and restaurants close-by. Chinatown about half a mile away. Can get cheap ($5-$7/pp.), non-touristy, authentic, good food at Ting Wong Restaurant on 10th St. in Chinatown. Because the hotel is located in the heart of downtown, stay on major streets when walking at night.
Please check "yes" if you found this review helpful.

title: “Park at your own risk!”
text: Hotel is clean and typical of the Hilton Legacy. Walking distance to Hollywood Bowl. Have had many friends and family stay there overnight and enjoy the Bowl. Do not park there, $30 for parking or in my case scratching my car by the driver door handle. Not taking any responsibility, Towne Park, Ltd excuse was there is not enough evidence to prove without question that they are liable. My friends could not leave at their convienience due to all the double parking in the lot. They did not contact me in person as they said, just send me a letter from claims office in Maryland. Weak effort towards longtime customer! Very disappointing in customer service.

title: “Very Good Hotel”
text: Very good hotel. Staff very friendly. Rooms exceptionally clean. Beds great. Bathrooms "spic and span".A few blocks off Broadway. Close to many of the shows. Would stay again next time in NY.Check in and check out quick, friendly and 100% accurate. Stay on top floors and very good breakfast and cocktail hour included in room rate.

title: “this hotel does not deserve even a rating”
text: This weekend an event was held at the Hotel Nikko. Their bargin priced rooms for attendees were $149.00. A reasonable price for a four star hotel. This was not even close to being a four star facility. I could have booked the Huntington months ago for $179.00. The dinner that accompanied the event was priced at $65.00. They ran out of food so at least 25% of the attendees paid $65.00 for the remaining left over fried rice. Okay, no problem, you got nothing for your $65.00 other than the company of the other fools that bought into this event as well. Go back to your room and order room service so that you will not starve. Nope. What decent hotel in San Francisco, a cultural and food mecca, does not have a late night dining menu. If you are considering this facility, one word, DON'T.

title: “AVOID”
text:
Awful hotel. Awful staff. Noisy, tiny rooms. Poor security. Dreadful wifi.
We were staying at The Empire when Sandy hit, and the staff COULD NOT COPE. No communication, little assistance.
Do not stay at this hotel, unless you enjoy arguing with front desk everyday. Seems like since they've been a filming location for Gossip Girl, they've forgotten all about hospitality.

title: “Top notch, all around.”
text: It's hard to find anything negative to say about this hotel. It's a stunning, well-kept property, with an impeccable service team. Loved the gym, the spa, the pools, the room was spacious, the food was outstanding. I was here for a conference but had some free time on the front end. Love this place. My only regret is not having my husband fly out to meet me here. Would definitely come back. It's hot, sure, but with the pools, and the AC, it's totally manageable. Love!

title: “Nice getaway!”
text: I had the chance to get away with the wifey so we chose the Omni. The room was small but it served it's purpose, we were able to relax and enjoy the riverwalk. We experienced no problems during our stay.

title: “Very Classy Hotel”
text: First time in Boston and I picked the hotel from site reviews. Staff was wonderful, helpful and friendly; nothing was too much. The Deluxe King was beautiful, clean and the best bed ever. It rained 3 days out of 4, but they put an umbrella in each room which came in handy.Great location in Back Bay area and in walking distance of many sites and close to the hop on/hop off trolley. I would definitely stay again. You will not be disappointed.

title: “A convenient airport hotel”
text: One of the better airport hotels. Very nearby, friendly staff, and nice room.

title: “Good location at a reasonable price”
text: Great stay.. rate was reasonable (under $200/night) and was clean, nicely appointed and close to many of the things I like to do in NY (Times Square, Madison Square Garden, etc.).

title: “A Unique Hotel”
text: We stayed in this hotel as part of a coach trip to New York. The rooms and bathrooms are older, but interesting. The beds were very comfortable, and we did not notice much noise from the street below. When you leave the hotel, it is just a short walk around the corner-and there is Times Square in all its glory! The hotel has a small cafe attached to the lobby, but we ate Danny's Deli, next door to the cafe. It has a great breakfast, at a modest price.

title: “Love this elegant hotel but encountered a few problems......”
text:
Came here during Cherry Blossom Festival with a total of 5 families.
positives:
- very elegant hotel, huge lobby with great sitting areas, spacious rooms, beautiful garden (would love to get marry here)
- as hotel member, get free wi-fi and complimentary coffee and hot chocolate with marshmallow. Both are hot and good and delivered to room on time.
- ate dinner at Robert's Restaurant. The restaurant is elegant with high ceiling and huge chandelier. Enjoyed my char-grilled rib eye steak ($26), cooked perfectly.
- "cooler" with 2 free bottle of waters 
negatives:
1. reserved a suite with 2 queen beds but got a king which was NOT comfortable for 4 persons. It is very IMPORTANT to provide the correct bed arrangement. It is just not 5-star treatment when you sleep on a fold-up roll-away bed even in a 5-star hotel. Hence my 3 star rating for sleep quality.
2. checked-in online the day before arrival but key was not at express check-in box, need to wait at front desk to check-in again
3. I had reserved 5 rooms under my name, one for me and 4 for other family members and friends. I was stuck in local DC traffic but 2 families arrived the hotel before me. They provided their own credit cards and considered "checked-in" as rooms were assigned but front desk refused to give them room keys until I arrived and asked them to wait in the lobby. This was so unreasonable after a long drive from New York and with small kids. The keys were finally distributed to them more than one hour later after I called the front desk and complained from my car (still stuck in traffic).
4. the hook at bathroom door (room 452) is closed to the top rim of the door. It is way to high for usage. 
Took off a star for the above problems.
This is a very nice hotel in many other ways. Just hope that I will not encounter the above problems again on my next stay. If I do not get my bed types, then I will stay away from this hotel.

title: “Great way to spend an evening”
text:
This was one of the best hotels that I have stayed in and I travel alot. The people at the hotel were so friendly and helpful. They took care of all of the questions we had about tours, delivered and picked us up at tour sights. 
The rooms were clean, well stocked and quiet.
Breakfast area was well stocked with all kinds of food and the dining room was veruy pleaseant.
Checking in and out was so easy, I booked on line, and I would highly recommend this hotel and the outstanding staff.

title: “Room are way too noisy!”
text: We chose this hotel because we got a good weekend rate, but wouldn't return. The rooms were way "too" noisy. We heard every door slam in the hall, heard people's conversations in the hall through out the night, and my boyfriend said he could hear the elevator during the night too (I didn't notice the elevator noise.) The lobby was nice and large, and our room was nicely decorated. BUT the beds were very hard, and I had a hard time sleeping the whole night because of the "hard" beds and the noise from the hallway. I tried going to the concierge's desk two times to get directions and suggestions on restaurants, but never found him or her at the concierge's desk. I called one time to the concierge's phone and no one answered. I found it unusual to not be able to get a hold of the concierge for help. Parking costs about $28 a day at the hotel, but you can park in an outdoor parking lot across the street for $8. The hotel says it is on the Riverwalk which we found to be true but deceiving. The River is right next door to the hotel, but you have to walk about two blocks to the actual Riverwalk where all the restaurants are. It is very close, but I wouldn't say it is on the Riverwalk like the Westin or Holiday Inn are. IF you can get a good deal here and hard beds and noise don't bother you, this could be your hotel. But HARD beds and NOISY rooms do bother me and I won't be back.

title: “Phenomenal Location, Exceptional Staff, Beautiful Property.”
text:
I'm a longtime fan of the HGI brand, and I've enjoyed another HGI when I've visited NYC several times previously. I am SOOO glad I took a chance on this property. 
LOCATION: The location is unbelievable: From my room I could look UP and see the Empire State Building (which is a block away) and I could look DOWN and see Herald Square and Macy's "The World's Largest Store." Just a few steps from the hotel entrance is a subway entrance, and Penn Station is one block west. Having Herald Square about 30 yards from the entrance is a real treat, especially now that Broadway is closed to vehicles so there are numerous places to sit and take in the scene. While first time visitors will of course walk 6 minutes north to Times Square, but repeat visitors will savor Herald Square which is vibrant without being overwhelming. Plenty of restaurants and shopping to keep you busy, and you're right in the Fashion District too! (Project Runway fans may want to walk by Parsons New School for Design and holler Tim Gunn's classic line "Make it work, Designers, MAKE IT WORK!" And you can also walk around the corner and scream "THANK YOU MOOD" at Mood Fabrics.)
STAFF. I stay at Hilton Garden Inn properties and have come to expect good service. This property really exceeded my high expectations. Restaurant staff, housekeeping, front desk, front door, and the maintenance staff all made eye contact and spoke to me every time I passed by. They made sure I knew about the evening "fresh cookies and water with orange slices" snack, encouraged me to ask questions, and repeatedly asked if there was anything else I needed.
PROPERTY. HGI is one of Hilton's newer brands and so it feels fresh, modern, clean. My room on the 28 floor had an exceptional view, was very clean, and as a bonus had a shower with glass wall--made the bathroom seem bigger. (1st time visitors to New York will need to reduce their expectations of room size--but by New York standards the room is fine.).
I'm already wondering when I get to come back to this hotel. Until I make it, I hope YOU enjoy it as much as I did!

title: “A few days in SF”
text: I was impressed that the hotel's common interiors were actually modern with a little style. The exterior showed its age. The location was a half a block away from public transportation and a few blocks to Powell Street. It was very easy to walk to Union Square, China town and North Beach. But the location had a large number of homeless as it is close to the Tenderloin district, but then again, this is city life. The rooms were very clean with newer and stylish furnishings. We went during the high season and paid $190 a night. It is a nice, clean and comfortable hotel. I am not a fan of the location, but would stay there again.

title: “Excellent Location and Good Service at a Great Price”
text:
My sister and I recently stayed at the Grand Hyatt Seattle because of the great rate of about $150 a night. We arrived on a Sunday morning and although we could not get into our room at that time, they did take our numbers and called us when the room was ready. They stowed our luggage and we ate breakfast at a nearby restaurant. About the time we were done eating, they called and informed us that our room was ready.
Overall, the room was clean and well furnished. There was some wear behind the nightstand. It looked like the room used to have a single king bed with headboard instead of two doubles. But that is my only gripe. The bathroom is beautiful with a huge soaking tub and separate shower, very roomy. The lights are dimmable over the tub which was great to relax in after long days of sightseeing. The beds were okay for me. I was able to sleep, but not as well as I would like to on vacation. There was a full closet, bathrobes, and ample dresser space. A very roomy room. Also the electric shades were a cool touch.
I found the staff of the Grand Hyatt Seattle to be friendly and obliging.
The location of the hotel is a BIG plus. We walked to the Public Market almost everyday of our four day stay. Shopping is nearby and so is the monorail to the Seattle Center where they have the Space Needle, the Experience Music Project, and Science Fiction Museum. Good restaurants are also in walking distance and so is the Columbia Tower observation deck and Seattle Library. The only reason we rented a car was because we were taking a road trip to Olympic National Park and then heading down to Portland, OR.
Overall it was a great stay and I would definitely return to the Grand Hyatt Seattle for the same rate.

title: “A gem on the upper west side!”
text: I am torn about writing this review, I am afraid if too many more people discover this wonderful hotel, getting a room here will be that much more difficult! Since discovery this hotel about 8 months ago I know I found my home away from home. In the beginning there were a few difficulties, no shower cap or enough towels in the room, no ice machine, and elevators too slow! But the friendliness of the staff more and their desire to make the stay there more comfortable made it apparent that they really care. I've stayed at the hotel 5 times and it really does continue to get better. The bell staff are great, always there to help with getting a cab and making car arrangements. Anderson is awesome! All the ladies at the front desk are sweet, and welcome you with a smile. I come in late during the week and usually check in with Crystal or Wendy. I don't have to tell them that I am tired, they can tell! Giving me a room towards the back away from that city noise is what I need most after a long flight and early morning. Looking fwd to going back this summer, and maybe finally trying a penthouse.

title: “This is the perfect airport hotel!”
text: This is amazing, we overnighted here both ways on a vacation to Central America, the convenience is great, we arrived at Terminal E and the Terminal Link driver dropped us right at the elevators for the hotel, check in was quick and professional. They had an airport police officer come up and check our ID's and fill out some forms so we could go through security and eat in one of the restaurants in Terminal E. The exercise facility and pool have a wonderful view and the fully stocked lockerroom with steam room was also excellent. 10 minutes after we checked out we had checked our bags and cleared security for our flight. On our return trip, once we cleared customs and rechecked our bags, the escalator up from the customs level exits right where the escalator for the hotel is, so 5 minutes after clearing customs we were checked in and in our room! Room service was good as well, we preordered our breakfast the night before to be delivered at 5 AM, and we got it at 4:55! All airports should have a Grand Hyatt in the terminal.

title: “great hotel and location”
text: Just stayed here with my fifteen year old daughter for a 'girlie' weekend. We loved the location. Convenient for Grey Line buses just over the road - highly recommend the all loops tour - worth every penny! Taxis no problem, theatre last minute bookings just over the road, theatres within a few minutes walk and my daughter is still raving about the Hard Rock Cafe along the road. I agree the lobby is deadly dull, but the staff were very helpful and that is what really matters. The suites are good as we each got to have our own space and privacy and with two doors to the bathroom we didn't disturb each other in the night. Breakfast was good, though had I not been a Hilton Honors member, and so recieving it free, I would not have been willing to pay $38 for the two of us. Over all I could not fault the hotel and would certainly return. Now we just need to sleep off the jet lag tonight!

title: “Nice Hotel in a Good Location”
text:
For a Holiday Inn this has to be worth every penny. I don't know if Holiday Inns are a better quality in the USA than the UK but this one was a pleasant surprise. When I booked this hotel as part of our Honeymoon I was a little aprehensive. Holiday Inn's do not have a great rep in the UK, but I did my reaserch on Trip Advisor & it appeared to be a very good option for a buget hotel. I guess they must recoup their room rates from the on site car park. Stupidly I never checked th rate before parking & ended up paying approximately $50 a night for a 3 night stay. This was the biggest disappointment about our stay here. It left a sour taste in my mouth & my last thought after a nice stay was I had been ripped off. 
The hotel itself was very smart & the check in process was very organised & prompt. The room was very clean & a reasonable size. The location of the hotel is great, you have many pubs & bars within walking distance & I guess you can walk to the Fishermans Wharf area within 30-45 minutes, though we never tried it. We took the tram during our trips which you can pick up from a 5 minute walk from the hotel & then a 10 minute tram ride to the wharf area.
The hotel has a lovely bar & restaurant on the top floor which has panoramic views of the city. The view from up there is magnificent. The restaurant is a little pricey, but the food was top notch. I don't mind paying a little extra for quality & this surely had that in abundance. My wife & I ended up having a lovely eveing up there enjoying the great food & view.
We never encountered any issues or problems with service, other than the rude parking attendant. Who thought it was hilarious when he saw my reaction to the $150 parking bill for 3 nights. The concierge, check in & room service staff where all very friendly & helpful & cannot be faulted.
The hotel seemed quite busy at all times & did have a lively buzz about it whenever we walked in to the foyer area. The rooms however were very quite & we never encountered any noise during rest & sleep times.
Outside of the hotel we did the Alcatraz Tour which was superb & worth every penny. If you have never done this & have wanted too or are thinking about it then get it booked. We turned up on the day & waited approximately 1 hour to purchase our tickets & get on to the boat. I would recommend booking the tickets in advance. The boats leave every 30-45 minutes all day.
We also did a tram tour of the city & took in the usual sightseeing stuff. Getting so close to the Goden Gate Bridge & driving over it was the highlight of that tour.
Fishermans Wharf is a lovely area. Lots of gift shops, restaurants & coffee shops. We found it a great place to unwind after a long day shopping or doing tours.
Also close by to the hotel was a superb shopping mall. Especially good for us UK shoppers with the dollar so weak against the GBP. The mall was full of shops with all the labels you can think off with lots of bargains to be had. The mall is situated right next to where you will pick up the tram to go to the Wharf area.
All in all we had an enjoyable experience & would recommend this hotel if you are on a budget & don't mind travelling on the tram to the wharf area.
Regards,
Jason & Anne (London)

title: “Consistent service and accomodations”
text:
We have always enjoyed consistent and predictable service here. While showing its age a little, the quality of the rooms and spa are always up to Four Seasons' standards. The best location for a hotel in downtown Austin. While surprisingly quiet, you are just a few blocks from all the entertainment and restaurants downtown Austin has to offer. We walked the Lady 
Bird Lake trail which adjoins the hotel and is one of the best urban trails we have ever hiked. The spa and restaurant were great. We look forward to our next visit.

title: “On it's way to being one of the best!”
text:
My wife and I just spent a quick weekend in Chicago and thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Blu. While it still has some issues to iron out (temperamental elevators/not enough maids/no towels at pool), it is well on it's way to becoming a phenomenal location. 
The rooms are very compact, yet we never felt claustrophobic. Judging from the floorplan on the back of our door, we had the smallest room on the floor. But we didn't mind. We could see the river, the lake and Navy Pier from our tiny room. And that blue carpeting is just so welcoming. The rooms boast energy efficient light switches and Euro-style toilets. If it's not already, I would think this hotel will be LEED certified soon. 
Both nights, we had evening cocktails in the wonderful Filini bar. The decor and service were top notch. The hotel's service from top to bottom, was exemplary. It's refreshing to see a staff (who work so well together) that is so interested in your happiness. I wouldn't surprised if the staff is comprised of some of the best employees from other Radisson Blu's around the world. 
Highly recommended.

title: “a bit cramped and noisy...”
text:
Rooms are indeed a bit small, and if you're not used to small spaces, you could be even feel cramped (especially in the bathroom).
Our neighbours were too noisy and even tried to enter the room through the doors that connect the room if you open them, but the hotel can't help that.
Since the room isn't that big, I would advice the hotel to adapt the term 'less is more'..:-) They've put way too much in the room!
It was a bit dirty when I opened one of the small cupboards in the room, because there was 1mm of dust on the bottom of the cupboard. I immediately closed it again.
Room is way too dark and our 'view' (which I requested by sending them an email upfront) didn't allow us to open the curtain without being watched at..
So not very positive about the room since the rate is quite high (but I know, it's NY...). 
Positive is that the lobby and the bar/restaurant are cosy and welcoming. Staff very friendly!!
I think they do need to make some changes in order to keep their status.

title: “Can't wait to return”
text: Refreshing change of pace from the typical "fast food" hotel chain. Friendly staff, comfortable beds, charming atmosphere. Beautiful refurbished building in Mount Vernon area. Easy parking. My favorite place to stay in Baltimore.

title: “Great stay”
text: Great 4 day stay with family. Clean comfortable rooms, friendly staff. Heated pool was great. Club room could use a few more food choices that appeal to a broader age group.

title: “by far the most helpful staff ever”
text: I stayed here recently with a colleague during a business trip to the US.The location was perfect, a really nice cozy hotel with the most friendly and helpful staff I have ever come across, a special mention to the duty manager and concierge on duty on 29th April forgive me for not getting their names but we were rushing to the airport. Top marks and I look forward to staying there again and would recommend to friends and colleagues.

title: “My First Motel 6 experience”
text: l stayed at this location 7/5-7/6/2010. It was a good value for the location and the pool was in working order. We were in room 214 and experienced no bed bugs. The bathroom did have a slight hint of mildew but not enough to complain. The desk clerks were nice to us. My only complaint was no iron in the room. A $10 deposit was required to obtain one. The hotel had a security guard who was actually doing his job and you can only access the elevators with you key card. I would stay again.

title: “Not Bad”
text: This property is rated 1 or 2 stars depending on which site you use. I noticed when researching this property there weren't too many recent reviews and that is probably because this hotel is primarily used by travellers for flight departures and layovers since it is only 5 minutes form airport (no airplane noise) and that is exactly what we used it for. I booked this hotel using my trip rewards in order to be close for our early flight out the next day. My husband, two sons and I were very happy with our overnight accomodations. The room we stayed in was clean and was just like the pictures represented by their hotel pictures. Even though the rooms have exterior facing doors(motel) we felt safe on the 2nd floor, because you can't enter the 2nd floor up the outside steps w/o a room key, nor can you enter from the steps inside the lobby after 11pm, because the doors are kept locked. The hotel has a pool which we did not use and offers a continental breakfast as early as 6am consisting of bagels, cereal, milk, juice, coffee/hot cocoa and apples. If that doesn't appeal to you there is an IHOP and Krispy Kreme next door. I spoke to two staff members regarding our reservation and both were nice and professional. For an overnight stay at a reasonable price, I believe most would be pleased w/ these accomodations.

title: “An extremely hospitable staff makes the visit most enjoyable”
text: We have stayed at this hotel many times and keep coming back because everyone is extremely friendly and helpful. The price is reasonable,

title: “New but Chaotic”
text: The location of this hotel is FANTASTIC and no more than a 10 minute walk to downtown. Other than being new, it doesn't have a lot going for it. The rooms are tastefully decorated and have that nice Embassy Suites feel to them. However, the many other aspects of the hotel are in need of some attention. Food from room service was old and stale. Free breakfast buffet was a free-for-all with not many food or seating options available as the tables were left dirty from previous guests. On Sunday my room wasn't cleaned until 7 p.m. Overall, it just wasn't a good experience and I would not stay in this facility again. There are many other options available in San Antonio that have got to be better managed. I attempted to share feedback with the General Manager about these issues but the front desk could not provide any contact information for he/she. Crazy!

title: “Location, location, location!!!”
text:
I stayed in this hotel with my husband for 10 nights, during Christmas period. 
We liked:
Location, location, location
Free Wi-Fi
Super fast check in / check out
Friendly stuff
Super comfy bed
Coffee maker in the room
Complimentary hot chocolate in the reception (every day)
So and so...:
Small room (we didn't mind because when you are in NYC the last thing you want to do is spend your days in the hotel; we also found it difficult to put our suitcases in a place that wouldn't get in our way)
The bathroom was of a good size, but, we had to let the water running for quite a while, in order to be able to have a HOT shower (we were on the 14th floor, I don't know if this was the reason for this)! 
Cleaning service
The location of the hotel (that mattered the most) was excellent!!!! Just a minute away from the overcrowded Times Square, Broadway theaters, restaurants and the metro, but yet so quiet, that we just could not believe it. Even on New Year's Eve with all the fuss in Times Square, we could only hear a tiny bit of the music. We found it really easy to walk to all the major attractions. The location is unbeatable!!!! Would stay in this hotel again.

title: “disappointing”
text: We have stayed at this hotel many times in the past and used to really enjoy it. It has been a couple years, but remembering it as a fun and cool place to stay, we decided to stay there this past weekend. The location is great, but the hotel itself was really disappointing. As Starwood Gold members, we were upgraded to a high-floor room overlooking Central Park. The view was great, but the room was very tired and dated. The hotel rooms are in serious need of renovations. The bedspread was stained (I just pulled it off and left it on the floor the entire time), the walls were very scuffed (I am not the type to "look for" stuff like this, but it was very noticeable) and the swiveling console that houses the tube television (no flat screen) ate up so much of the space in the room we had to negotiate ourselves around it. The decor is really starting to look tired. Even the bed, which is usually a selling point to Starwood properties, was pretty uncomfortable. I thought it was just me until my husband commented how uncomfortable it was. Having spent a fair amount of time in NYC hotels, I know not to expect huge rooms and bathrooms, however our bathroom was so tight that the bathroom door just about grazed the toilet and sink as I was closing it. Getting in the bathroom and closing the door required maneuvering yourself around the sink and toilet. I'm a small person and I could barely function in it. Even the lobby, which used to be fun and hip, was lackluster (although "The Burger Joint" is still a great place to grab great burgers and fries). When my husband and I went to use the pool we were told there was a $10 fee per person, per day to use it. There was no mention of that fee anywhere on the website or paperwork we received. We used to enjoy staying at this hotel, but will probably not be staying there again in the future.

title: “First Class Customer Service the way it should be at the Hyatt Regency Dallas at Reunion!”
text:
I have just returned from a five day business stay at this Hyatt and my stay was perfect and I don't give a "perfect" rating very often. From the time that I arrived by car, I was treated like I was the only guest there. 
Now, I absolutely hate to pay for parking but when I arrived, the valets were actually fun. The current rate was $19.00 per night with unlimited in and out privileges. They were quick to my car, opened the door for me and greeted me with bottled spring water. In the short amount of time from arrival to securing a bellman for me, my valet really tried to get to know me and to show interest in the purpose for my stay. He stayed with me and my luggage until the bellman came, making sure that I had someone to take care of me.
The bellman was equally attentive and stayed with me until I checked-in. The reservation staff pulled up my loyalty card profile and added amenities that I had even forgotten that I was entitled. I didn't have to ask her, she just did it. That is was good customer service is about, anticipating the client's needs.
The bellman was very careful with my luggage, not just slinging things everywhere. He was prepared with a master key and did not have me fumbling to find mine. He gave me safety tips before he left and pointed out the exit routes. Because of all the recent tornadoes that we have had in the South, the bellman made sure I knew what to do and where to go in case of danger.
I had a Deluxe King Room with very simple traditional, clean lines. My bed had a white duvet cover, crisp white sheets and plenty of pillows. The mattress was a little firmer than I was accustomed to but that did not cause me discomfort or problems sleeping.
There were two upholstered chairs at the adequately spaced work desk with in-room high-speed internet access. I did not have any problems with accessing the internet and not problems with interference or dropping connection. There was also a large upholstered sleeper chair. 
The 42" LG flat paneled television had a wonderful picture and great sound quality. The television sat atop of a large credenza with 4-large drawers and two open shelves for storage.
I do not have an Apple device so I am not sure if I am describing this properly but the clock radio had a built in ipod/nano adapter. The clock radio had a night light that you can adjust the illumination.
I really loved the bathroom because even though this property had been around a long time, it did not seem old. The bathroom now has double French doors with etched glass inserts. The coffee maker is in the bathroom which I do not like but since I don't drink coffee, that is really irrelevant to me. The pendent lighting, granite-like counter tops and the contrasting color scheme gave the bathroom a real sophisticated feel. There were high quality Portico toiletries.
I can't say enough about the hotel staff. Everyone was excellent. I had really gotten disgusted at the level of customer service at domestic hotels but this hotel rose to the occasion. As much as possible, they tried to call you by name (I know, I know I had a name badge on but it still makes you feel special when someone calls you by name). They were so attentive, I almost felt like I was on a cruise ship. If they said that they would do something for you, they would do it or come tell you why they could not do it. 
There were a lot of us at this convention but they kept the common areas spotless. And they were smiling. I know everyone was working very hard but they were still smiling and made me feel very welcome. Hotel managers would stop you and ask if there was something they could do for you and would do it. They just didn't assign it to someone else, they did it themselves if possible.
This hotel is adjacent to the convention center with a connecting corridor. It also has the famous revolving restaurant atop the Reunion Tower. It is now the home of Five Sixty by Wolfgang Puck. I did not eat here on this stay buy I have eaten many times before Puck so I know the view is spectacular. The convention meals and snacks we were served were excellent with lots of creativity and variety. When I would enter our dining room, I felt like I was walking down the red carpet at the Oscars!
When I checked out, things went just as seamlessly and smoothly. I really did not mind paying the parking because I felt that I actually got something for my money. Some of the valets were in training but the managers were instructing them every step of the way to make sure they learned their job correctly. They opened my car door for me, gave me a bottle of spring water and wished me a safe trip.

title: “Marathon Rip Off”
text: Gross bathrooms, stained carpets, chipped paint, moulding falling off of walls, radiatior falling off of wall. Our room was the size of a dorm room. The location was great. The remodel they talk about must have only applied to the lobby. We paid about $190.00 a night - Not worth it!!

title: “Good location and good value”
text: Unlike previous poster, we didn't think the hotel was dirty. The staff was super friendly and helpful, our room was well furnished and the hotel had all the amenities as advertised. It is located just off the main strip for a good night sleep. We are a family of 4, 2 adults and 2 young kids under 7yrs old. We would recommend this hotel to others with young kids. The breakfast is acceptable but it gets busy after 7AM.

title: “Looks can be deceiving”
text: When we saw the hotel and the area. We were initially excited until we had to deal with the customer service. First of all, I would highly recommend not booking a room at Empire through one of the cheap hotel sites, or priceline.com, or hotels.com. First, after booking a room for 3 people, we were told that we were reserved for a Queen standard room, with one bed, we told them that we needed double beds and the worker informed us that we would have to pay an extra $100 for our room if we wanted a room with double beds, because they had nothing available. After realizing that we were not going to budge, she then said, we do have a double bed room in the smoking area. We suffer from some breathing issues, but in order to be comfortable, we had to take the room. We were told that we did not have Wifi because our hotel rate did not include free wifi. There was an evening I had an important event to attend and when I was going to take a shower, there were no wash clothes. We called 4 times and did not receive the towels. By this time it had been well over an hour and I had to wash up with my hands and soap. This was one of the worse hotel experiences I have ever had and I did not realize that booking a hotel through one of the discounted web sites would result in us not receiving all the amenities that we would have received if we had paid the regular price. The rooms are small and you can hear everything outside of the rooms.

title: “NIce stay”
text:
I recently stayed at this hotel mainly due to it's location to sites and friends who live nearby. I also based it on the reviews on this site, which were mostly positive.
I booked a king deluxe room on an upper floor with a view. My room was at the back of the hotel on the 8th floor. I believe some people did mention about the noise of the trash pick up, I will say this was a bit of a problem some mornings, and as far up as I was, it was pretty loud, but I didn't consider it something the hotel could really do anything about. The room itself was clean and contemporary, with cool furnishings, and my view was great, especially at night. I did order breakfast the first morning I was there, but at nearly $16 with tip for a continental style breakfast, I thought it was way overpriced, in fact, the entire roomservice menu was beyond overpriced I felt. There are so many dining options for less outside the hotel, I just decided to eat out. I did have a drink at the bar at Firefly, the restaurant located in the hotel. It's seems like a cool place and very popular with the locals.
 It's location almost can't be beat. There are so many restaurants near by I had a tough choice somedays on where I wanted to eat, and all within walking distance. If you're a sushi lover, stroll down to Sushi Taro or Raku, both are close by and both have awesome sushi! There's also a great Chinese restaurant nearby called Mei Wah which not only has great food, but has been popular with many political stars.
The metro is near by, but I only used it once and that was coming back from my day. I simply didn't need it. Dupont Circle is a five minute walk away, a great place tro just sip coffee from the Starbucks close by and people watch for a while, especially on Sundays. The monuments are a bit farther if you're not much of a walker, it took me about 20 mins or so to walk to them, but I didn't mind the walk at all, and it didn't feel like it took that long. If you don't want to walk, the metro is five minutes away and a cab ride wouldn't take but 10 minutes.
There is plenty of nightlife close by, both gay and straight, in which I did both since all my friends there are straight. Check out K Street Bar (straight) which is a short cab ride away, great place to dance and strong drinks! If you're looking for the gay scene, the gay area is just a 10 minute walk from this hotel, with plenty of bars and clubs to go to. Check out Jacks Restaurant and Bar, great outside patio to watch the boys stroll by and AWESOME crabcakes! They make mean drinks too :o)
Besides the roomservice issue I had, everything was great. Very friendly and personable staff who were always willing to help out with any questions I had. They also had complementary internet which I had no problems with, and a business center downstairs with a printer to print out boarding passes if you need it. All in all I look forward to my next stay at the Hotel Madera.

title: “Great Resort for Families - fun in the sun!”
text:
We visit the Point Hilton at Squaw Peak at least twice a year. All the rooms a suites, as a Hilton Diamond member we get upgraded most of the time but the standard suites are very nice and comfortable. The property has a water park with multiple activity pools, a waterfall, waterslide, lazy river, jacuzzi, and a toddler pool. Additionally there is a minigolf course and tennis courts available at a small charge. The kids never want to leave the waterpark...hours of fun guaranteed.
There are also pools in each main building that include swim up bars, hot tubs, and a toddler pool. The lounge chairs are very comforatble.
There is also an "Adult" (no kids) pool on the property. As well as a few smaller pools near the bi level casitas.
The beds are very comfortable. My only complaint this trip was the A/C unit was noisy...usually this is not the case.
The restaurants are good - Sunday more breakfast at the Lantana Grill was packed...I think they could be more efficient in the Buffet setup - most things people wanted were cook to order vs available on the buffet which resulted in very long lines.
I WOULD recommend this to anyone - especially if you have a family.

title: “BEAUTIFUL HOTEL”
text:
What a beautiful hotel. It was previously a Bank and it has been so tastefully converted into a hotel, with great decor. Rooms were very elegant and spacious and beds were very comfortable.
Reception staff were very helpful and greeted you warmly at every encounter, likewise the doormen.
Breakfast was delightful and the fresh fruit - Strawberries, Grapes, Pineapple etc., were all fresh and none tinned! Good selection of fruit juices too. Plus cereals and toast, muffins etc.. For me nothing to complain about.
There was also a "lap" pool in the basement. A delightful roof top terrace which had amazing views and played soft music all the time.
Around the corner on S.Main Street was a bar called Locale and this bar did amazing fish & chips. It was huge but great.
Went to Sun Studios a cab ride away and that was very good and interesting and well worth a visit. Take the street tram for only $1.00 and sit and ride the whole route to get a look around.
Gracelands - well what can you say. It was our highlight obviously, and not disappoinited. Pre booked before we went and did the VIP tour, and booked with Viator. Excellent. You sure did get ahead of the queue treatment, which was great and this also gave you unlimited access to the house. We went back for a second viewing. 
We prebooked our airport shuttle with Tennco Express which was great. Great service both by e-mail and when we arrived. We also booked with them to take us and pick us up from Gracelands. So very friendly and nothing too much trouble.

title: “More Than Expected From Airport Hotel”
text:
This would be a great hotel anywhere. Nice clean rooms. Great beds and amenities. Plus it has the added convenience of being right on the terminal.
I came in from a flight from Asia and needed to overnight in Detroit before my flight home the next day. What a luxury to walk from my gate to the hotel, get a good night sleep and be right there at the airport for the early morning flight home.

title: “Very average, but clean and sufficient for airport travelers.”
text:
I stayed at this hotel twice in one week: once when I arrived in Seattle, I called the shuttle and spent one night, then at the end of my trip in Seattle, I spent another night and took the shuttle back to the airport. 
The shuttle service was very nice. The first driver I had, I can't remember his name, but an older black gentleman - he was really nice! He definitely struck up a conversation with me and made me feel welcome my first time in Seattle. He made me leave my bag so he could get it for me. Great guy. He dropped me and another passenger off at the entrance due to renovation. 
Check in was very simple. Kaisa was very nice, a pretty lady with a great name. 
The rooms looked and felt clean and were basic. I liked that there was an easy chair for me to relax on facing the TV, but the TV is in a dated entertainment center type piece of furniture and even with the doors pushed in, it's hard to see the TV from the bed or the other side of the room, so I can't lay out clothes, go back and forth to the bathroom while primping, etc and watch the news in the morning. My 2nd room was identical. 
The first night, it was about 9pm and I considered the restaurant for a late dinner, but the menu was bland - pizzas and a few salads, nothing special, really plain, easy to make things. Fortunately, Seatac has several places that will deliver and I found a Thai place in the directory that was about a half mile away and they delivered some pad Thai. Yeah.
The biggest gripe that I had were the room keys. Seems they were having issues with the keys working. I stay in hotels quite often so I know how the key cards work. I had to go back to the desk both times I stayed to have my keys remade. That is really annoying when you have luggage and have to go way down hallways, up the elevator and down another hallway and back. The second gripe is when I got in late for my second stay, I went to the "business center" to print off my boarding pass and the printer wasn't working. The printer was on and ready, but the PC that controls the printer (there is a sign saying in order to print, the far left PC has to be on and running) was locked up, so nothing would print. I had just gone downstairs to have my key remade and I was too tired to go back, so I just got to the airport earlier. The girl at the front desk was busy and being so late, she was probably the only one there and I didn't want to wait around for someone to fix it. 
I had breakfast one morning. Some fruit, yogurt and juice/coffee. Everyone loves those make-your-own-waffle stations but I hate them because that means whining kids everywhere...especially the Sunday morning that I checked out (Easter). I just grabbed juice and left. I wanted to take a cup of hot tea with me - they had a decent tea selection, but the to-go cups had no lids. That's weird to me because without a lid, I didn't want to hike way back up to my room without one. I asked Kaisa at the front desk and she said they were out. Strange. I threw my tea out. I didn't want to risk spilling it on my way up to the room to grab my bags and leave the hotel.
In all, I'd say the hotel is average, nothing special - comfortable bed, clean room and something is offered for breakfast - that is really all that is needed for airport travel and the price reflects exactly that. I stayed on a Wednesday night and also on a Saturday night. I will add that there was a big difference in occupants. Wednesday was nice and quiet. Saturday night there were a lot of kids literally running around. Up and down the halls. That annoyed me, but not really the fault of the hotel (does anyone walk the halls?). 
I would stay here again for more budget airport travel, but not if I was looking for a getaway. I think folks with kids will use this for a budget getaway since they have a pool, so beware of this on weekends. It's a very sufficient airport hotel.

title: “Beware the "specials"”
text: Purchased hotel's offer of special rate with large discount /coupon for dinner at hotel restaurant. After purchase, was told that I couldn't have dinner at hotel restaurant -- already booked throughout all dinner hours. Hotel manager offered no refund of my wasted purchase of hotel's "special" offer and, on top of that, charged me a cancellation fee.

title: “Downtown convenience, but little historic charm”
text:
As someone who enjoys historic hotels, I found the San Carlos to be a major disappointment. The hotel does have some interesting copper-plated elevator doors, but other than that I really saw very little in the way of historic charm or original detail. The public areas are fairly nondescript and do almost nothing to recall the hotel’s heyday.
I had no major complaints about my room itself, though the bathroom was quite small and the shower had a little sign about unpredictable hot water. I realize that some quirks are inevitable with historic buildings, this is really more a question of deferred maintenance and the hotel’s misplaced priorities.
The best things I can say about the San Carlos are (1) the staff were reasonably friendly, (2) there is small outdoor pool that was a nice surprise, and (3) the downtown location was very convenient for walking to the Convention Center. However, downtown Phoenix is quiet at night, with only a sprinkling of shops and restaurants. People coming for a vacation would probably be better-served by staying in one of the more lively resort areas.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: We were at the Nine Zero hotel for a three night stay in Boston. The hotel is located directly on the Freedom Trail, next to a subway station and an easy walking distance to Quincy Market. The room was modern, clean, very comfortable and identical to the pictures shown on their website so no bad surprises. We enjoyed the free wine tasting held in the lobby every night. A great way to relax after a day of sightseeing. I have no negative comment about this hotel. We would definitly stay there again.

title: “Booked on Priceline - Excellent Value”
text:
We decided to take a long weekend trip to San Diego to visit some friends that live in the area, and booked this hotel by selecting a 4-star "name your own price" deal on Priceline. I believe we only paid $95 per night.
Overall, for $95 a night, this hotel was excellent value. We had a nice large room, with a balcony overlooking the marina. The room was spacious, clean and had been renovated, although the hotel itself is quite old. We ate the breakfast buffet which was also good.
PROS:
- Excellent value @ $95 per night when booking on priceline.
- Good breakfast buffet
