- Great location (close to Downtown and the Airport)
- Nice, clean, spacious rooms
CONS:
- Older Hotel
- Rates may by higher when not booking through priceline

title: “Delightful NYC weekend in bright, airy new hotel”
text: Found Wyndham Garden Chinatown on Priceline, good deal for a wonderful, bright, clean room with a wall of floor-to-ceiling windows. The free breakfast is a work in progress, with slow (but earnest and polite) service. All staff were helpful, pleasant, and enthusiastic. Lobby is bright, all-glass. Rooms are comfy and efficient, wonderful linens, contemporary walk-in shower.

title: “Go There”
text:
I stayed at the Chandler Inn for one night - i found the room to be clean and of enough size. The staff were so friendly and helpful. I thought they went above and beyond. Good location- not far walk from beacan hill. for the price, i would recommend
Edward Williams

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 5 nights 2nd - 6th Sept 12. We stayed here six years ago for 2 nights and always said we would go back.
centrally located nice rooms great staff. Lovely roof top bar. Very good customer service and nothing was to much trouble. It is situated on 57 & Lexington ideal for all attractions - central for everything.

title: “Great location, so-so property”
text:
We were booked into the Park Plaza as part of a package. It's a mastadon of a city hotel -- a pile of fairly small and outdated rooms on top of a pile of restaurants and retail occupying a full city block Imagine a mid-point between the two New York paragons of this style: the luxury Waldorf-Astoria and the package-tourist-and-overnighting-stewardess Hotel Pennsylvania. As such, it does a decent job, but you wouldn't want to spend much time in the rooms or the very busy lobby.
We didn't dine at the hotel or use any of its services besides parking, but we did use the gym and want to note that it has the best hotel gym we've seen in years -- the full equivalent in range of equipment to a typical private gym, in a spacious purpose-built space, the kind of thing one tends to expect only in top-tier resort hotel or in a hotel which hosts a regular private gym and has it double-duty for guest accommodation.

title: “Just for location”
text: Overall it fit the purpose ..cheap and around the corner from CBS studios.I didn't like the sink being in the sleeping area instead of in the bathroom and barely warm water in the morning.Cigarette burns in carpet and bedding.(smoking room)No pool.Parking garage is small with a scarey ramp,little cars only.Great cold air conditioning!I would stay there again just for location.

title: “Don't have expectations and don't need hot water you'll be fine.”
text:
Had I been left to book my own room for this trip, rather than an office assistant this never would've happened. Lesson learned. Rooms are dated, bathrooms are tight and hot water in this hotel flucuates from cold to tepid. Told front desk about water, very nice man asked "How long did you let it run? / "15 minutes." / "You need to let it run for twenty... (all with a smile... and he was serious.). Everytime I washed my face I hit my head on the shelf above the extremely small sink. Toilet, small. The room was loud and echoy. You could easily hear people talking in the adjacent rooms. Close to a subway you can hear at odd times. Room is dingy.
Front desk guys are really nice... But because you're nice does not mean I sleep better at night. Anyways, I hate complaining. It's a drag, but I don't want you to learn the hard way.

title: “Great location! Hotel not great!”
text: Hotel is in a great location, right near Macy's, Empire state and a Subway station. 5-10 min stroll to Times Square. Hotel comes with complimentary breakfast, this is fairly basic; toast, doughnuts, cereals and bagels. But great to fill up in the morning and will certainly save you a few dollars. Hotel is far from luxury, could prob compare to a UK travelodge! Can be quite noisy so request a higher floor, we were 7th floor and especially at the weekends there was a lot of street noise until approx 4am.... But then that's New York. Staff friendly, if your travelling with Virgin you get a big breakfast free on your 1st morning, however don't buy from your rep they RIP you off! Not for families, more suitable for couples who literally need somewhere to rest ....

title: “Beautiful Lobby, average experience.”
text: I just returned from a 3 night stay at the Palmer House. I am a Hilton Honors Gold member and stay at Hilton properties all over the country. I booked a room with 2 doubles from an email from Hilton on great getaways almost 3 months prior to my trip. Upon arrival the lobby was packed, which was to be expected on a holiday weekend. I was very disappointed to wait significantly longer to check in through the HHonors line than if I had just waited with everyone else. Then I was told they had a king bed for me. I explained I had another guest coming and this was not what i reserved. I was then told they would "comp" a rollaway. I also advised this was not acceptable because neither myself or my guest wanted to sleep on a rollaway bed. Eventually we were given a handicapped double bed room, 11-280. The room size was fine, however the howling noise every few minutes from the elevators was less than awesome and continued all night. The fitness center was nice, executive lounge was always packed with people just sitting and taking up tables which was frustrating. I may stay here again, but would like go back to the Double Tree on East Ohio.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Great hotel in a great location to riverwalk and rivercenter mall. Staff was friendly. No issues.

title: “Great Location”
text: The rooms are clean and walking distance Times Square and a lot of local attractions. The staff are friendly and helpful and when I left my sunglasses behind, they offered to post them to me, only costing me $3 for the postage. The staff are honest, which, in this day and age is very refreshing to come across and the front desk staff were always friendly and willing to offer assistance. We would definately stay there if we make it to New York City again.

title: “impressive,comfortable stay !”
text: STAYED: April 25, 26, 2003We enjoyed our stay , front desk was extremely helpful,gave us printed directions to wherever we wanted to go. Had everything u needed in the room, micro, fridge,couch etc. very clean. Shower heads not the best but i'm not complaining ...Had booked on expedia for $ 48.00 a night . thought it was worth it . great breakfast in the a.m. too ! u won't be dissapointed

title: “The Palace or Waldorf Astoria?”
text: My NY office is located in between the Palace and Waldorf Astoria Hotels and has a corporate arrangement with both hotels. I therefore stay one of either hotels when I visit NY. I don't remember how many times and days I stayed there but if you need to make a choice then I prefer the Palace better. Both hotels unfortunately are rated 5 stars but when compared with hotels in Asia, they are both sub-standard. Rooms at Palace is slightly better off then Waldorf. Restaurants at Palace is also better. Anyway, you will not find a good hotels in NY unless you have minimum of junior suite room. So my conclusion is that don't expect too much.

title: “Convenient and reasonably priced”
text:
This is a good hotel if you want to avoid the high price of parking in the city. Parking is free and the complimentary breakfast is a plus.
The hotel was renovating their rooms when we were there and we stayed in one of the renovated rooms so it was nice and clean. There is a microwave and refrigerator in the room which is very handy.

title: “Avg. Westin”
text:
stayed here for 2 nights. location is good, walking distance to everything. staffs are friendly. the lobby is nicely done, but once i step into the elevator the hotel shows its "true age". room is decent, with signs of wear and tear (carpet a little torn, bathroom tiles a little worn out). shower is good.
if this is a sheraton i'll give a 4-star, but for a westin i'd expect more...so 3.5 star from me

title: “"Perfect Stay..."”
text: This hotel was perfect for us in many ways; you'd be smack in the middle of Manhattan & minutes from the rest and relaxation that Central Park offers. It's beautiful & convenient. Within easy traveling distance of most of New York's biggest sights, restaurants, theaters & museums. This is central New York. Its convenience to all of Manhattan, plus proximity to Central Park, Times Square, Rockefeller Center & more. The staff couldn't have been more helpful during our visit and everyone was more than friendly. They provided information about sites to see & events to take part in.

title: “Simply Beautiful”
text: My husband booked for one night for my birthday. We were able to check-in early, received a room with a view upgrade, not to mention when we got to the room there was a small (delicious!) cake waiting for me as compliments of the hotel! What a nice personal touch! The staff was very nice, the rooms were very nicely decorated, the showers were AMAZING, and the location just can't be beat! Overall, it was a beautiful and memorable stay and I would love to return one day.

title: “locked in the bathroom”
text:
I have stayed at the Wellington on many occasions, and until October of this year, my experience with this hotel has always been a positive one. This time a friend and I rented a non-smoking room with two beds and the rate was substantially more than I've paid during past visits. The rate increase would have been all right had it been justified by a room of quality. Our stay was for 3 nights beginning October 28.
 We arrived early and had opera tickets for a performance to begin at 1 p.m. The receptionist took our names and credit information, but could not give us a room number until later in the day so we left our luggage and left for the opera. When we returned, we were allocated the worst room I've ever had in NYC, and certainly the worst one I've ever had at the Wellington.
 The room was tiny with two twin beds on the 13th floor. Entering the room on the left is a small closet with a door opening onto the entrance way across from the small bathroom. If the closet door were left open, you could not open the bathroom without bumping it against the closet door. The carpets were stained. The room desperately needed painting. The woodwork was chipped. It was possible to open the window a crack in a lopsided fashion. This was important for ventilation because the air conditioning/heating unit was installed such that the lid could not be lifted to access the controls. 
 There was in the closet an iron and a small ironing board. There was a hair dryer, but it was in bad shape and the pieces were loose. The vent in the bathroom was affixed to the wall with, I kid you not, gray duct tape. There was no counter space on which to place toiletries. There was no provision for coffee or tea, no cups. And, one night, there were no towels, an oversight not recongnized until stepping into the shower because the rod from which the towels are suspended is placed over the tub, behind the pulled shower curtain.
 As my roommate napped, I went into the bathroom and closed, but did not lock the door. My need for bathroom privacy turned out to be a big mistake because I could not open the door to get out despite all efforts. Fortunately, I did have a roommate, and I was able to bang and yell loudly enough to awaken her, and she called the front desk and a maintenance man came up and removed the entire door knob/lock assembly and replaced it with another. How long I would have been there had I checked into the hotel alone, I have no idea. I'm sure I would have missed the evening theatre production.
 Before catching our shuttle to the airport, I asked to speak to the manager. I asked if the hotel were under new management or had been purchased by some conglomerate, and I gave him my tale of woe. He was gracious and polite and assured me that he would see to it that the problems with the room were addressed, and he took $100 off the bill, which made the third night $211 instead of $311. 
 For the things I like to do in the city, the Wellington is in a good location. I can walk to Lincoln Center, Carnegie Hall, the City Center, the theaters, and because of my past good experiences I will give it one more chance, but I will not recommend the hotel to friends and family anymore until I'm sure I can guarantee them a positive experience. (I had even recommended this hotel to friends who had reservations at the beginning of November.)

title: “A very pleasant stay”
text:
The location -- a few blocks south of the Riverwalk, across the street from the Alamo -- is perfect, easily accessible to the main tourist areas, but set apart enough to be quiet. The rooms are huge, and the bathrooms are bright, modern, and very comfortable. The building itself is a gem: the designers who are responsible for the conversion into a hotel deserve high praise. Great care has been taken to preserve the historic lines of the old building: you walk down a hallway, decades old oaken doors and beautiful marble finishing lining the walls, and you feel like you've stepped into 1926.
I can't say enough good about this place!

title: “Excellent Road Stop”
text: Great hotel, right off of the highway. Check-In was ideal, the room was very spacious and clean. Plenty of food available in the lobby. Cambria Suites is an excellent chain, I look to stay at them when I can. Free WiFi as well which was a huge plus.

title: “Good for business, not really for vacation”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for a conference at McCormick Place. It was conveniently located, but the parking was pricey (good thing I didn't have a car) and dining places are too. There are more relatively reasonable places nearby, I just didn't realize it at first. It is a few blocks to the subway/elevated train station, so that is convenient. There was also a taxi stand and shuttle available to the airports, for a fee. The room itself was large and clean and the bathroom was ok, the lack of a fan for moisture control and the buzzing of the only light were the minuses. I think it would be a little too busy of a hotel if I was looking for a place to crash while exploring Chicago. 
But for a nice place to chill during a business trip this is a great hotel. There is internet available, a little area with internet access (for a fee), and a ton of other services that are probably too much for the casual traveller but are welcome during business trips.

title: “Excelent Hotel”
text:
I had a last minute lay over in AZ. and need a room quick and close to the airport. I opened my laptop and searched Holetls near the Phoenix airport and found the Holiday in to have a reasonable price and asfree shutttle to and from the hote. I booked it last minute and was supprise to see what a great hotel it was. The breakfast in the morning was a great start for my flight into Los Angeles.
Thanks A Million.

title: “Charming”
text: Heritage hotel with the excellent service and accommodation. I must thank the parking valets for their assistance. After hours of sight seeing, we really appreciated the hotel`s fantastic in-room dining. Great sightseeing nearby including a wonderful art gallery, aquarium and market. If you would like to sample the oyster-clam bar on the lower level, I suggest making reservations to secure a better table. As walk-ins we were disappointed.

title: “frequent and happy customer”
text: We have been coming here as a family for a few yrs. The staff is unbelievably accommodating. I know that the hotel is in need of renovation ( which they are in the process of doing). I have traveled and stayed at many places, this is the best value for entertainment, convenience, and service. They welcome children w/ goody bags. Allow pets!!! Its great for all ages. We no longer bother to go elsewhere. I love the easy access to metro and underground mall. On rainy days, we can go and explore w/o getting wet or feel the cold. How neat is that?!! We have such a warm relationship w/ the staff that each yr we are greeted w/ a hug. So, the rug needs to be removed ( and it will be soon), the sinks may leak. But, the staff far exceeds the problems that this hotel has. ALL hotels have problems. You can't satisfy everyone. This hotel satisfies all of us in our family. See you soon.

title: “Good Service”
text: Had difficulty with limo service. was handled very well by staff.

title: “Very good for short business stay”
text: This suite is close to the business district (qualcomm and Motorola offices). Very hospitable staff and great breakfast in the morning. Also close to the super markets and shopping complexes. You could also use the complimentary shuttle service for short trips around the hotel.

title: “Great hotel!”
text:
Stayed one night at the Kimpton Monaco Seattle first week of November. Booked the hotel thru Priceline so wasn't sure what this hotel was all about. Arrived around 9pm. Check in was very quick. Front desk staff was very nice. The decor of the hotel is very modern, artistic design. It looks like it was recently renovated. Everything was clean and comfortable. 
Overall surprised by how good the hotel was. I normally stay at the Westin and Hyatt's so this was an unknown change for the good. The only thing preventing me from giving a 5 star rating is the high valet parking cost. After taxes, parking cost $47! There is street parking but downtown Seattle doesn't come across as super safe!

title: “Decadent Stay”
text: Wow! I am truly a picky traveller when it comes to hotels and this place has all the comforts of a 5 star hotel. Travelled with 3 girlfriends for the weekend and we were more than comfortable sharing a room. Everything seemed new, they checked us in early. We all used the pool, steam, sauna etc each morning. The changeroom had a ton of towels available and amenities for your use. The fitness room was one of the nicest I've seen at a hotel, lots of equipment and space and a large room for yoga etc. We ordered room service and it was prompt and 25% off. Our only complaint was the cheese lady in the lobby could use some people skills. Overall its a great hotel within easy walking distance of shops and belltown.

title: “Pleasant staff, safe bike storage, good location- walkable to Market Square”
text: This was my second stay at this hotel. Note: The actual address is 318 W. Cesar E. Chavez Blvd, not Durango. Rooms have been renovated, bathroom nicely done. Wish they offered double queens, instead of seemingly tiny double beds. I appreciate the lovely live oak trees on the property anf ample free parking; this city seems to charge for every foot of curb space, even evenings and weekends.

title: “Will not stay here again”
text:
We stayed here as part of a wedding group and it was great to be in close proximity of those folks. Otherwise, after spending one night here I can find no good reason to step foot inside the Hard Rock Hotel Chicago again.
My wife and I regularly spend long weekends in Chicago and had been staying at the House of Blues because we loved the vibe and funky decor. Sadly, the HOB has long been tired out and we haven't stayed there for two years, instead bunking at the Sofitel, W Lake Shore, Hotel Indigo and Hotel Monaco looking for a new "home away from home."
We had looked forward to trying the Hard Rock as a new hip place to stay but were disappointed at every turn. Our room was beat-up and dirty, the staff members pretentious and rude when we called to register our complaint and ask for another room, and the bar was laughably small when we tried to drown our sorrows. 
Oh, there was one good thing - the elevators were fast. Which was nice, because we couldn't wait to leave!

title: “Worst noise ever in a room, paper thin walls”
text:
I have never felt motivated to write in but a couple of reviews back someone complained about the noise and Argonaut management reply that they had made renovations to fix the problem. They havn't. We stayed on May 25th, 2008.
The sound level in the room was the worst I have experienced in 15 years. I travel over 120 days per year so you do the math on how many rooms I'm comparing this too. 
Not only could I hear the TV in the room next to our, I could clearly make out that they were watching Law and Order. I went into the hall and realized that their TV was just as loud as ours, which was at normal volume. Later I could hear the guy next doors coughing. 
Too make our room even worst, we were in room 258, the stairs to the lobby and the elevator were right behind our heads. People were slamming the stairs door until late and started early. You could also hear the elevator whine. To add insult to injury there is a water/sewage pipe running through the ceilling and it swishes every couple of minutes when I first heard it I thought it was rainning. If we hadn't just flown in from Hong Kong we never would have fallen asleep..
This hotel sells rooms based on their location. It was clean and the service was friendly but slow. The nautical theme is probably great for kids but is too disneyesk for me. Furnishing was comparable to a higher end holiday inn. 
A note to the management of the Argonaut , you spend a night in that room. Once you have, if you don't pull that room out of your inventory then you have not interest your guests.

title: “Ignore the bad reviews!”
text:
Firstly, I am really surprised by how some people seem find it difficult to research their hotel before they travel. The Hudson Hotel doesn't pretend to be anything else other than a hip and trendy – and if you were to check out the hotel's official website beforehand, then you would be able to suss this fact out.
Add to the mix that The Hudson Bar is renowned in Manhattan for being 'cool' and a 'place to be seen' you begin to get a measure of the place before you've even stepped on to the plane!
I was very worried about some of the complaints that had been posted, especially about the size of the rooms and the attitudes of the staff – but I needn't have been. We stayed on the 23rd floor in a Deluxe room (which wasn't much more than a standard) and there was plenty of room! I could seriously have swung about 3 cats around it! Yes, I have stayed in much bigger rooms, but it was completely adequate for our needs, very clean and decked out to a high standard. People who complain about the size of the TV and the toilet need to get out more! I don't think I switched the TV on once during our 4 night stay. You've come to NYC to go out and about – not sit in your room ordering room service!
The staff were friendly too and were quite happy to help whenever you asked for it.
Go there, enjoy and try not to let small details drag you down, the location is fantastic, right next to Central Park, Columbus Circle Subway and about 10 mins walk to 5th Ave, and Times Square. The Cosmopolitans in the bar are also very good!
Have fun!

title: “Great Location”
text: This hotel is in a great location close to loads of amenities and access to attractions and transport. Walking distant from Penn Station. Great Diner and Bar linked to hotel. Rooms although small and dated are clean and air conditioned but do provide value for money. Free Wi-Fi but can be slow, you can pay for a faster connection. If you catch the NYAS bus, it is not as frequent as NYC and instructions are poor as you have to book the pick up in advance but you are not advised, hence we waited over an hour for the next one. NYC is much more frequent and visible.

title: “A Huge Hotel - But Good at What They Do”
text:
The Hyatt is a huge convention hotel located in the very best place you can be if you are visiting Chicago as a tourist. If you stay here you have to take it as it is - there is not a lot of quiet and intimacy in a huge covention hotel with thousands of people everywhere. 
On the other hand this hotel is as good as I've seen at handling this kind of situation. Check-in and out went very smoothly, and Hyatt's automated check-out is pretty slick. Elevators can be a huge problem in busy hotels of this size and for our trip the waits were acceptable even though the place was packed. The room was perfect. The newly remodeled rooms (East Tower) were excellent in every respect except that they were too dark - a common issue these days. 
You don't have to spend a fortune on food here, there are a many very reasonable choices as close as the ground floor walk-through area in the West Tower, and many more on the street. You definitely don't need a car to visit Chicago from here as much as nearby and public transportation is excellent. If you park a car here it is expensive. 
It is not necessarily the case that an upper floor has a good view, so if the view is important to you be sure to mention that when you check-in. I had a wonderful view on the 7th floor. 
The Hyatt charges just short of $15 a day for Internet access - no excuse for that in this day and age except it shows Hyatt's willingness to gouge people. Plan ahead to minimize or avoid paying this charge.

title: “Nice hotel rooms, great location but public access to pool is ridiculous”
text:
Have stayed at this hotel many times. Always enjoyed staying here Nice sized hotel rooms, free wifi. There is a parking charge. Good location - grocery store and lots of nice restaurants nearby.
The most ridiculous thing this year that we have never had an issue before is allowing non hotel guests to use the pool for a day pass.
One particular day there wasn't a single chair available and we saw so many people who had bracelets which means they paid for a day pass. I think this is ridiculous - hotel guests should be able to use the chairs and pool without it being overun by non hotel guests. Total turnoff
Also loud music playing at the pool and then movies shown at night is not very relaxing or appealing

title: “Great location but prepare to be nickeled and dimed for everything....”
text: This is a nice hotel from the outside and a great riverfront location. I was there for a conference on a business trip for 3 nights. Enjoyed the riverfront and the restaurants around but the hotel was a bit much. The lobby and the front of the hotel are well done. Inside be prepared for an older hotel room with older amnities (not modern). The service at the check-in and Bell desk was average at best. Prepare to pay for Internet and pay a nice rate for parking overnight as well. Not a great Hyatt property in my opinion but the location is superb.

title: “Best hotel in Boston for the price”
text: We have stayed in every luxury hotel in Boston and this hotel really knocked our socks off. Prompt and friendly service and great food. Extremely clean rooms. The fitness center and lap pool were wonderful. We especially loved the casual atmosphere. Usually luxury hotels are stuffy. Not this one. Our only complaint was the location could be a little closer to Boston's attractions. However, for a fit couple like us, we enjoyed the walk to Fanuil and the other attractions. There are safe and interesting areas near the hotel to go for a run. Be prepared for the expensive parking and steep hotel taxes in Boston.

title: “The "W", our wonderful weekend away from home!”
text: From the moment we arrived, everyone was not only helpful but went the extra to make sure we felt special. Guess what, we did! One person in particular, Jamie Torres, (I believe her title is IPO Greeter?) went out of her way to make us feel at home and our stay memorable. Everyone greeted us with smiling faces no matter what time of day or how busy they were. Our room was comfortable and everything we needed was quickly taken care of. We will definitely visit again and will recommend the "W" to friends and family visiting Chicago.

title: “Overpriced hotel with unfriendly personnel”
text:
Location in Fisherman's Wharf district is the greatest asset of this hotel. 5 min walk to Pier 39/ 10 min to Alcatraz landing/ 20 min to Lombard Street/ 30 min to Chinatown
Rooms: efficient, fresh, but very small
Restaurant: nice for breakfast or dinner, reasonably priced, with attentive and friendly service
Free coffee every morning/ wine tasting & snacks from 5 to 6pm
Personnel: below average - not friendly, not helpful
Prices are outrageous: $300+/ night for a closet-sized room; valet parking is ridiculous @ $50/ night. Park your car at the next door multi-storey parking for $30-35/ night or further out for less

title: “So, So...”
text: Had to stay in SA for a few days business meeting. Reading the reviews, I thought I would give this hotel a chance. The location on the Riverwalk is good. Not to busy, easy walk to the "hot spots" You can take the elevator to the Riverwalk level and step right out, avoiding the not so great street area. Just outside the hotel main door is a major bus stop (must be a transfer area, always lots of people there). Lots of buses, day and night. Lucky for me, my room was toward the back of the hotel and on the river side(no street - other side of hotel is drive into parking deck). Yes, the traffic noise was noticeable and was glad I was not in the front of hotel or on a lower level. The staff was great, always upbeat and friendly. The room was well kept and housekeeping did a good job. However, the room overall was worn around the edges. Furniture needs updating (this means old) The bed was on the soft side and regulating the water temp in the shower was difficult, extremely HOT. People showed up in droves for the "free" food, am & pm. Tried the breakfast the first day, just average. So headed to the Starbucks, just a short walk away (both street access & Riverwalk access). So many people were trying to get the free evening drinks and food, I didn't even get to try it. I believe the reason the ratings for this Hotel are faily high are based on the room rates (and people like the "free" food). While a lot of Riverwalk hotels run over $200 a night, you can get a rate here from about $135 - $160, depending on the nights you are staying, weekends of course, the higher rates. Since I was out of the room all day and out in the evenings, I decided to stay. I would recommed this hotel, with reservation. It is NOT an up-scale styish hotel. But reading reviews, I was expecting better. Also, they allow pets, which I did not know, I prefer a hotel that does NOT.

title: “Didn't want to leave!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights and 5 days arriving on the 14th. We booked the hotel online. The pics were beautiful, and when we actually got to the hotel, the pics didn't even do it justice! The room, lobby, outside, the pool, spa, laundry room and fitness rooms were all AMAZING! The service was wonderful, and their breakfast was worth waking up early for! :) Not one complaint!

title: “Great Place!!!”
text:
We stayed at The Muse March 30 - April 2 2005. We had gone to NYC on a sightseeing/theatre trip. The place couldn't have been better. When we arrived (at noon), we were told that our room wasn't quite ready, but the GREAT bellstaff took our bags to storage. We arrived back at the hotel at 4pm, our bags were waiting for us in the room. We had a GREAT room on the 12th floor.....decent-sized per Manhattan standards. THe bed was excellent. The bathroom was awesome, as were the bath amenities. High windows afforded a small view over to Times Square (1/2 block away), and another view east on 46th St. But we didn't stay at The Muse for the view - the location was perfect for our needs. Across the street is a little deli (so you don't have to spend a fortune on the stuff in the mini-bar), and the nearest subway is about a block. After a full day in NYC, we had NO problems going to sleep. I heard no terrible noises. One MUST keep in mind that this hotel is in the center of the busiest city in the world, so SOME noise is expected. But quite frankly, I didn't hear a thing. If noise is an issue for you, I suggest asking for a room on an upper floor. But...we had NO issues with noise at all. The good-sized umbrellas in the room came in VERY handy, too!
We had a TERRIBLE experience with a car service we hired from JFK to the hotel(Carmel Car Service, the driver drove 35 MPH in the left lane on the Van Wyck, nearly had a half-dozen accidents, was on his cellphone swearing for half the trip, and got LOST in Manhattan...I had to tell him how to get the the hotel!)....so for our return trip to Newark, I asked the bellman about my options. He told me that he can get me a taxi (for about $65, including tolls & tip) or a hotel town car for a flat rate of $90. We chose the towncar. No pressure to take the hotel's car service. I don't remember our driver's name, he was a young guy....and he was excellent. We made it to Newark in about 50 minutes, in traffic.
I cannot imagine anyone not loving The Muse. When we return to NYC later this year, we will definately stay there again.
Our rate for 3 nights was around $900.00. Not bad for a beautiful hotel right in the middle of the theatre district.

title: “Great location, very clean room and friendly staff”
text: This is such a great location, that we have been staying here for the past eleven years. This year the room we had was much better than other years, as the room was very clean and everything worked like it should. I think management is trying to improve the rooms as this year was better than the previous years.

title: “Stylish Hotel, but Unfriendly Service”
text:
We booked this hotel, after seeing the rooms and amenities on the website. There are good and bad with the hotel.
The Good:
- Stylish hotel. Modern decor and clean rooms. We were on the Regency Club floor and had a beautiful view of Los Angeles. It got noisy though, with the large buses that park outside of the hotel.
- Drinks in the Lobby bar were good. The dessert was mediocre, but the service was good.
- Fitness center is well equipped with plenty of cardio machines. If you are a Diamon member, it's free. Otherwise, it's a pricey $20/day.
- Lobby is bustling and busy. Active area.
- Westfield Mall is 2 blocks away - incredibly convenient.
The Bad:
- Service, Service, and more Service. The front desk reception was rude and cold. We asked for other options outside of the Regency Club, and they said there were none. We went to the Concierge and asked for other options, and they said there's no other options -- even though the sign outside of the Regency Club specifically says to "see Concierge for other options." (This was Thanksgiving Day, and the Club was closed.)
We asked the hostess at Breeze Restaurant if we can just have dessert, and her immediate answer was "No." She just looked at us, and didn't offer any other option. 
All in all, it was a rude reception.
- The Hyatt charged us for drinks and food that were delivered to our room, even though it was free for Diamond Club Members. We had to go to the front desk to remove the charges.
- No car parking. There is valet, but they charge $31/day. (We parked next door, which is $20/day.)
The next day, the staff was much friendlier. However, we've already had a foul experience.
I recommend the hotel for location and decor, but not for service.

title: “Beautiful hotel for the price.”
text: The accomodations are splendid. Many foreign travelers know a good deal when they see it, judging from the people choosing the club lounge level. Tasty food at all hours of the day. The staff were hard-working and courteous. I felt

title: “superb city location hotel”
text: stayed at this hotel for 3 nights in dec 2011 . fantastic location for times square and broadway . just outside a metro link as well so easy to explore the rest of new york city from this hotel . the room we had was very spacious and clean and the staff were very helpful overall a fantastic hotel for our first trip to new york .

title: “Petite Auberge-Cozy and cute!”
text:
It was such a delight to stay at Petite Auberge for two nights. It is centrally located and the walk from Market/Powell is about ten minutes. As a Joy of Life Member (apply for free on the hotel's website), my boyfriend and I were upgraded to a queen guest room with a fireplace. We were also given a complimentary split of red wine and bon bons which was included in the free membership. The evening reception was fantastic (gourmet cheese and crackers, vegetable tray, apple streusel, and wine (red, white) and sherry. Bottled water is free. The complimentary breakfast was delicious (scrambled and boiled eggs, sausage, quiche, danishes, scones, croissants, assortment of breads (great sourdough, wheat, white), fresh cut fruit, coffee, tea, orange juice, and cranberry juice). The local paper was delivered every morning and they had USA Today available in the lounge with a fireplace. The hotel is very quaint and cozy and really does feel like a small French country inn. The hotel staff from the concierge to housekeeping were friendly and knowledgeable. The front desk recommended a great tapas place in the Mission District and also printed by boarding passes for me.
I met a couple during the evening reception that told me they stayed at Petite Auberge 16 years ago. I can understand why they returned and I certainly plan to do the same the next time I visit SF!

title: “chinese torture”
text: i booked this hotel because i thought it was near union station, stupid me.I also had it booked before i read the reviews here,which made me think ,my gawd what kind of a dump have i booked myself into..i did not cancel however (unfortunetly) people say you get what you pay for ,location was good near the EL the room was basic but acceptable, no bugs to be seen ,Trying to sleep however proved next to be impossible the room was too hot for me and i could not open the windows as this let in the sound or the air conditioners outside .I slept for about 4 hours that night,the following day i complained and changed rooms, this turned out to be worse than the first room as directly outside the window in the alleyway between the buildings was a small tin hut which pinged when it rained .I slept for about 2 hours the second and last night . This hotel is by far the worst place i have ever stayed and i should have taken the advice of the people who said DO NOT STAY HERE. they are telling the truth as i now know to my cost.

title: “New Year's Stay”
text:
This hotel is NOT a dump. All other things being relatively equal, I will choose a Hilton property for the points. So, I would probably stay there again. The hotel is right on the riverwalk, NOT two blocks off it. It is quiet along this section but a very quick and pleasant walk to the hustle and bustle found nearer the Alamo and mall. Another reviewer wrote it is on the seedy side of town. To me, most of the downtown was a little seedy (it is a city), but all along the riverwalk felt safe and well lit. There was no armed guard in the lobby or the parking area. There is a bus stop across the street were locals, who work for a living, wait for the bus but I didn't think anyone looked dangerous in any way.... Mostly just tired. 
 We traveled with family and appreciated the breakfast and "welcome home" happy hour with meals. We feel that being able to eat so much at the hotel saved us a lot of money. However, there are many good places to eat in San Antonio, so there is that. The food was not great, generally generic cafeteria fare.
 We found out that you can book which suite you want when you book on line. I wish I had known that, because we had two suites with views of the brick wall of the Westin next door. 
 All of the staff were wonderful! The guy at the front desk answered my question, drew me a map with directions, checked someone else in, and answered the phone simultaneously. It was an amazing feat of multi-tasking to behold! He was pleasant and patient with all! The ladies at breakfast and welcome home meals were friendly, kept the food coming, and managed to wipe tables in between, keeping everything neat and tidy. 
 I will say that the mattresses were not up to Hilton standards (I love Hampton Inns because they have great matteresses, and I thought Homewood Suites did too...) but lots of pillows and quality sheets and towels. The suites we stayed in did not have windows in the living room part which made them dark and dreary. We like to play games and eat snacks together and the living room area was too small for our comfort. The bedroom sections were much bigger and more comfortable. Bathrooms were clean but SMALL and worn. Tiles were chipped as were corners of floor boards, etc.
 The valet parking was a hassle. They would say ten minutes, but always took longer. The guys working there worked hard and were great, its just a bad arrangement We are used to using valet parking. Its just too bad that San Antonio doesn't have better parking downtown.
 All in all, I thought it was pricey for what it was. If you can get a good deal, by all means stay here. If you want to be in the middle of some kind of night life, well, don't go to San Antonio. If you want a clean quiet place with friendly staff and don't plan to drive much, stay here! Most of the guests I talked to and saw seemed happy and seemed to be having a good time. Especially during happy hour!

title: “Great stay and super comfy bed”
text: We always have a great time when we go to the comedy zone. Great restaurant and wonderful rooms. So comfy to sleep there. Beds are always great and clean

title: “Needs better housekeeping”
text:
I stayed at the Omni and was a little disappointed by how thorough housekeeping was. Overall the room was nice and clean except that there was a used, dried up towel hanging on the back of the bathroom door and a used bar of soap in the shower.
Upon checkout I mentioned this to the front desk and they were very apologetic and offered to buy me breakfast.
BTW, I booked through Priceline and I would recommend that you request a room on an upper floor when you register. I took what they gave me and it was on the lowest floor. This is an atrium hotel and the noise of people talking at the restaurant or bar on the first floor is quite loud.

title: “Intolerable deafeningly Loud”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights paid a considerable sum for a queen room and were give a room on the second floor over the bar which we later discovered turned into a private night club at night. The noise from the bar was extreamly loud for three of the nights but we put up with it as it was off time square and to be expected and it generally finished at 2am and with ear plugs it was just about possible to sleep however on the friday night it was deafening and after several hours actually made me feel pysically sick as the base was actually causing vinrations in the roomi and the music was beyond any acceptable levels of tolerance a hotel bedroom. They had a private party and the Dj and base may as well have been in our room even with ear plugs we couldnt deaden the noiseat all. I complained so vehemantly after 1am that the night porter moved us to a room on the 9th floor.The problem with the rooms as i see it on the lower floors is that the central (escape i might add) stairwell is open all the way down from each floor no fire doors until you reach the gorund floor and then you enter directly into the bar. There is no sound proofing worth taking about to the floor slabs or to the circulation routes nothing to stop the noise travelling up several floors. The staff were unfriendly except for one of the door men and the service man. Yes we actually met the service man..3 times in fact which brings me to the next problem, the air conditioning it was making a terrible persistant squeaking sound that lasted several seconds then stoppen and came back randomly. It was too warm to not to have the Aircon on at night so this was annoying. The service man couldnt identify or fix the problem. Also reception when we complained a few times twice didnt pass on the message to him and we had to call again. The final problem was with our toilet which was prone to blocking and not though the excessive use of paper either i might add. We were heading out the first time one morning and reception assured us they would have it fixed. We came back late that night and it was as we had left it. We called recption again and when the service man arrived he said he had never been given the message the first time. He was very helpful and lovely more that i can say about any of the recption staff. In summary if you want to sleep during your stay and expect a reasonable level of service and value for money dont even consider staying here.

title: “Outstanding”
text: The Microtel Inn & Suites accommodated our daughter and her new husband, their bridal party, our family and friends. The hotel staff was extremely friendly, helpful, organized and just went above and beyond to take good care of us and provide us with what we had asked for. When we arrived before the wedding reception (which was at the Indianapolis Zoo) they were prepared for us ~ getting us checked in very quickly so we could get to the reception on time. After the reception they had set aside a meeting room for us so we could have late night pizza and beverages so we could just relax and unwind. The hotel was immaculate and the rooms were outstanding. I would definitely stay there again and would highly recommend the Microtel Inn & Suites.

title: “Improved- nice!”
text:
I had stayed here previously and did not remember being as impressed as I was this time. I did not make use of the lobby but it looked like it had several different areas for eating, computer use or relaxing. Also a small Starbucks. I like the convenient covered free self-park garage. Only thing was I had to walk through smokers to enter the hotel through the side entrance.
As SPG Platinum I was given a room on the club floor which was nice. Room 1201 was all the way at the end of a hall with an odd angle and separated from the other rooms. It was a bit eerie and I almost asked for another room for safety reasons but since I was only there for one night I stayed. The room also had an odd angle as did the bathroom but it all was functional.
The club lounge was very nice with lots of seating. The hostess made me feel special and she was very accommodating. Awesome lemon bars.
I ordered the battered cod for dinner (room service) and it was the best fish and chips I have had for a long time! Even the tartar sauce was different and very good. I appreciated they didn't expect an extra gratuity and did not even add a line for it on the bill. 
I also like that they have done away with those big useless "decorative" square pillows on the bed. They had HBO AND Showtime. Shower and water pressure was good.

title: “Excellent location with friendly and helpful staffr.”
text: This is the second time we have stayed at the Liaison in the last seven months. The staff is professional and helpful from the moment you arrive at the hotel. You are within walking distance of Union Station; the Capitol building is right down the street and a short walk away; and it is a good starting point for a walk along the Mall and access to the museums and the DC sites. The on site restaurant is very good and you just have to walk or ride down E Street for some more excellent choices. The hotel has a Euro-boutique feel, and we plan on staying there during all of our future trips to DC.

title: “Disappointing lack of professionalism”
text: I booked this hotel with great expectations. I had family visiting from outside the country and wanted them to have a good experience in Chicago. Upon arriving to the hotel (at the exact time I indicated in my reservation) I was told I’ve been “downgraded” to a lesser quality room. I travel very often and never had this before. Moreover, I did not hear a single “I’m sorry”, it was like usual business. What bothered me the most was that the receptionist kept telling me “I will decrease the rate for you” “what do you think, nice eh?” like he was doing me a favor!!!! They decreased the rate to that of the rooms they gave us of course (which is the legal thing to do, since I am sure is illegal to charge me for one room and give me a lesser value one for the same money). They did not care that I wanted higher level room independent of value. I did not know what to say, since this never happened to me before, also with family present did not want to start arguing. The rooms were nice (not as nice as I thought) and location is good, however be aware that they might not honor your reservation and not even apologize for this. That is enough for me not to go back again.

title: “Bait and Switch”
text:
Don't be duped by room descriptions - I reserved a King Premier but was booked in a full bed in a tiny room. Desk tells me that I shouldn't have relied on reservation description, as they only offer run of the house (least acceptable room) reservations. Even upon showing them a confirmation letter with details of room, they claimed they have no control over those descriptions.
I was not able to negotiate a lower rate for a threadbare, well-worn room. Much complaining resulted in being moved to a King bed room, but it was well worn - you could see the floor through worn spots in the carpeting and chunks of the wall was missing. Nothing at all like the pictures on their website.
Many amenities in description did not exist or were no longer available. Service was rude an argumentative. Take a pass on this hotel, even if it appears to be more affordable than others. For the price here, you can get a much, much better room through a discount broker.

title: “Overrated hotel, 1-2 star hotel”
text: upon our arrival at the hotel we were rudely greeted by the person at the front desk. We were also early and checked our bags at the desk which seemed to cause a problem. We returned later to a much nicer person at the front desk and the concierge was friendly. Walking into the room was the WORSE...there were flies and hair on the "clean" bathroom towels. It was sooo gross!! It was like the maid did a quick job so she could go home. The bed was uncomfortable and i had the worse night sleep. It reminded me of a hostel in Europe and was not worth the price we paid. Never going back

title: “Excellent Location”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights in April 2009. Couldn't have picked a better location. Right in the heart of Times Square and right next door to a subway station.
Location:
Being right in TS, the outside doors tend to get a little crowded, but nothing major. You have to get on an elevator to get to the lobby, then another elevator to get to your room. That become a little 'annoying' after a few trips.
Lobby / Amenities / Staff:
The lobby feels a little crowded and looks NOTHING like the pictures on Hilton's site. I didn't notice any construction, but maybe that is the goal... We didn't use the fitness center, but walked through and it was pretty small. The business center was very hot. I used it to print a few items and had some minor problems which were resolved fairly quickly.
I used the pre-order feature which allows you to have items (extra towels, pillows, toothbrush, etc.) to order a dental care 'kit'. That wasn't in our room when we arrived, but I called down and they delivered it within 5 minutes.
We ordered a cheese/cracker tray which was good, but VERY overpriced. 
Staff was outstanding overall. We had an issue with 2 employees (one front desk, one bell boy), but everyone else was extremely helpful and friendly.
Room:
We had some HHonors points, so I can't speak to the value, but we were on the 29th floor with a times square view. We were on the corner so we could so both ends of TS and the water from our room... It was outstanding!
All of the corner rooms are right next to the elevator, but I didn't really notice once inside. I only heard them in the bathroom, but not at all in the living room or bedroom. The room (suite) was on the smaller side compared to other DoubleTree's I've stayed in, but probably very large when compared to other NYC hotels. 
The beds were extremely comfortable. We haven't slept that well in a long time. We couldn't really hear any noise from the ground level unless you opened the windows.
Bathroom was half remodeled, but the shower was very old. Overall, we couldn't have imagined a better location and overall experience. Definitely recommended (Especially if you have HHonors points!)
We had very low signal on the wireless internet in our room. I never brought this to the staff's attention, but it did get quite annoying (on again, off again).

title: “Friendly staff and 4 star hotel”
text:
My stay was very nice; however, the hotel had some technical issues that prevented pay movies from being available for up to 24 hours after purchase, room key being deactivated prior to check-out date, and a couple of small items went missing duringthe first day after the "turn down" staff visited the room.
Overall the stay was nice and the hotel waived one day of the $22.00 parking fees as compensation for the missing items.
The most notible points for this facility is the nice pool area, the view (magnificient), and the friendly staff.
I would stay again when the opportunity presents.

title: “Customer service”
text: I stayed at the hotel for 2 nights. The last night, I had a severe toothache. I called the front desk at 4am in the morning and requested for some medicine. DORIS HEARN came up to the room and provided me with the pain relief medicine. That was very kind of her!

title: “This was not a family place”
text: We would not recommend thishotel for anyone. The service was awful...when we arrived, we were not offered the traditional cookies.....our room sheets had stains all over them . When we asked for a change of sheets, it took over two hours for that to be done. AT the swimming pool, there were smokers and pets present and certainly didn't set the mood right..I didn't want my daughter hanging out around a cloud of smoke. There were no towels by pool side and it took over an hour to get some when we asked.....we have stayed at other doubletrees expecting just as pleasant of a stay , but this is not a place we would recommend.

title: “Roosevelt stay in June 2006 for 4 nights”
text: We paid $259 per night which was a good price as compared to others in the same area. However, we had problems with the elevators. There were often long waits and it seemed as if only a few were working. We had two rooms in our group. My room had no problems with the air conditioner but the other one barely worked. The staff were very friendly. The food in the bar (late after a show) was very good. I would stay here again but I would definitely try and get a better rate. From what I have read, it is possible to get a better deal.

title: “Fabulous, as always!”
text: I arrived at 9 a.m. for a legal conference--unfortunately, I was suffering a kidney stone attack and was not looking forward to sitting in a ballroom until I could check in at the normal time of 2-3 p.m. The staff at reception immediately knew something was wrong--I explained and they found a room for me instantly, an upgrad in fact at no charge, and got me upstairs in no time. I am always impressed with the staff and the hotel.

title: “Perfect place to spend a weekend away!”
text: The hotel is located so close to everything! You can shop around soho, go down to canal & spring street. Tons of great restaurants & places to party. Great area for shopping. The hotel itself is beautiful and elegantly understated. The hotel has a wonderful bar, that always has a crowd. Great food at there restaurant & a killer margarita! Rooms are lovely with great views of the city!

title: “Disappointed”
text: Hard to access, turn from 1 way street; hidden $25/day parking fee automatically added. Pretty lobby; good access to LAX. Burger king across street(6 lane blvd). Lots of walking, staff seemed undertrained, no free food ammenities, pay for everything. Very, very expensive, room fairly basic.I really expected more.

title: “Avoid this hotel.”
text: This hotel was a headache from the start. First thing my room key doesn't work. They have no respect for there guests. I was repeatedly woken up by knocking at my door from the hotel maintenance. The only good thing here is the t.v.

title: “I wish I was in my twenties...”
text: I have to admit that it was an awesome hotel when I first stayed there in 2004. It is getting older so am I... I stay there almost every year and I don't see any improvement and/or addition they did in seven years. Also I have to say it is pretty hard to keep up with the partying crowd every night. Even when the rooftop club is shut down at 1AM people continue to party in their rooms and it might get pretty obnoxious. If you are in your twenties and want to stay in a party house don't think twice...

title: “Above and Beyond what you'd normally expect”
text: Right away we were impressed with this hotel. The beautiful lobby is quite the eye catcher when you enter the front doors at the Beacon. Originally booked a regular king size room on Expedia for a great price only to be surprised with an upgrade to a king suite at no additional charge. We didn't ask why, we just accepted! (*note* There is only valet parking and its $28, just to warn you) We noticed that you need your room key to activate the elevator which is a nice touch and makes you appreciate the added level of security. Our suite was in the middle floor of the hotel and had a view facing the front street. The sitting room area is roomy with a business desk and chair, couch, and armchair surrounding a small coffee table with a television on the opposite wall. The full efficiency kitchen was amazing (we didn't get to use it because we only stayed one night) there was even a dishwasher! The sliding door to the bathroom is a bit funky at first but you get used to it. The gorgeous marble and spacious area make it seem almost spa-like. There is a dining area with two chairs in the front of the bedroom and you can sit and people-watch from your front windows. The king size bed is very, very comfortable and there is a second television as well. This sounds like it should be a very cluttered space but its not which is why we were so pleased with our selection. Not to mention the complimentary bottle of champagne that arrived on a silver platter with two glasses! You are surrounded by some other hotel chains and quite a few embassies but its pretty quiet at night which means you can sleep quite well. My boyfriend and I really liked this hotel and if we find ourselves in the area again will try and stay there. Just to warn you though, you may not want to leave!

title: “Incredibly unsatisfactory”
text: I am a business traveler and Diamond member; this hotel was possibly the worst Hilton property I have ever stayed in. I was traveling with a colleague, and to the manager's credit, he returned my calls promptly and gave us a credit on the rooms. He's trying. Nevertheless, these were the problems: no internet access due to the hotel being full (!), room was either too hot or too cold, hot water took forever, inconsistent turn down service (only one night out of two), seriously overcharged for parking. The air was stale and moldy smelling. The first morning, we saw a 5 STAR rat run down the sidewalk as we ate breakfast. There are other properties nearby...

title: “below expectations”
text: I was here for a conference, and the hotel is really well located for the conference center, as well as restaurants/bars around the 7th street area. But, for a Hyatt, I felt the place disappointed. We had problems with the shower pressure (which, it's worth noting, was fixed immediately after we complained). The wireless is neither free not reliable.I purchased 2 days worth of wireless for my room, and the signal was so poor in my room that I ended up having to sit outside the elevators to get a decent signal. The food in the sports bar (Grand Slam) was mediocre-- it might just be fries, nachos, burgers, but that doesn't mean it needn't be fresh. The cafeteria in the lobby didn't open until 7 am, and even though there was a line up of 4-5 people at 6-55 am, the staff stubbornly refused to start serving until 7 on the dot. I don't want to go on too much here-- the place was basically OK-- but I just expect more for the price and from a Hyatt.

title: “An amazing 'stayaction' for my gal and I at one of San Diego's little gems.”
text: My girlfriend and I decided to visit the other side of town for her birthday earlier this week. We rode our bikes across town from Golden Hill to a favorite spot of ours, The Pearl Hotel. The ride was great, nice weather and fun stops along the habor on the way over. We arrived at the Peal to warm greetings and relaxation at the pool with cold beverages. My gal loved the little note in the room from the hotel with the weather. We had reservations at another local restaurant for dinner but opted to stay at The Pearl instead, good choice. We sat at the bar with a nice gal (can't remembe her name, short black hair) and had a great meal. I mentioned to my girlfriend that it was nice to find items like foie gras and steak tartar on the menu, the cocktails went great with dinner too. Nice finish with donut dessert and desset wines. Overall a recommendable experience at The Pearl, great job!

title: “Great location location near Moscone”
text: The Westin is in a great location about two blocks from Moscone Convention Center. Rooms are tad bit small. Although bath and entry are quite large. It must be the width of the room as a king eats up all the space. Great LCD and traditional Westin features. Views from higher floors are good.

title: “Great value and clean rooms”
text:
Last minute i had to stay in a hotel in san antonio due to plane delay. I didnt want to spend $100 or more for a couple hour stay. This hotel was $54 plus tax. Ratings weren't that great but it was only for few hrs so i went with it. Glad i did. All rooms inside. Its either a new hotel or refurbished. Rooms clean. Quietest ac I've ever had in a hotel. Free wifi. Shuttle to airport. Flat screen tv, comfortable bed and pillows. 
I was pleasantly surprised. Beats a $100 hotel. Theres no breakfast, just coffee but with $ i saved I'll go out to breakfast

title: “Beautiful Facility & Convenient”
text: This new property is in the middle of downtown Indianapolis, across from the Convention Center and the Indiana Indians ball field. The hotel was beautiful and the rooms had plenty of space. Prices for restaurant food and room service was very reasonable, which was a pleasant surprise. The breakfast buffet had plenty of delicious options, including eggs/omelets made to order. We never expected this upscale Marriott hotel to have affordable food. There was also a Starbucks kiosk in the hotel. The only thing that was disappointing was that the hotel was very humid. Our room was on the 25th floor and the hallway was extremely warm and humid, as if it does not get ventilated. The temperature in the room itself could be set down to 66 degrees but it never got cooler than 70 degrees. That is pretty typical for all new hotels these days. If you like sleeping in a cool room, stay in an older hotel. Regardless, we would definitely stay here again.

title: “High end quality”
text: We stay at this hotel every year that we go to San Diego. They've built a second half to this hotel so there is what we call the new side and the old side. Both are great sides to stay on. We always want a room with a view of the bay because its so beautiful. The room service is grade A. This hotel is a great value for your money. The only trouble we've ever encountered is the parking. If your going to be out late at night your parking close is slim to none. They have a brand new parking structure attached to the new side but if your all the way on the other end you are out of luck.

title: “Great Location”
text:
This was a great location for New York City. Just off the hustle and bustle of Times Square, but closer enough to be in the thick of it within minutes. The Rockefeller Centre is seconds from the hotel, and close to the Subway station too.
Staff were friendly, and seemed helpful enough. Rooms were compact, but very comfortable and clean.
Would definitely consider this hotel again on my return NYC.

title: “Huge Disappointment”
text: We stayed here before - but it has been 6+ years. Obviously, they have done no maintenance in those 6+ years. The first room they assigned us stunk (smoke?) and the AC unit was dripping on the floor. We were given another room. That room also stunk. These are non-smoking rooms?!! The window had a large crack in it with a hole in the screen. There was a cobweb on the bedside lamp. There was a large area in the bathroom ceiling where they'd obviously had a flood from the room above. There was a hole punched in the inside of the bathroom door. The floors were filthy. The kitchen did not have the minimum dishes and silverware and there were crumbs in the silverware drawer. While we should have appreciated the peanuts left on the carpet beside the bed, we did not. Bottom line is that they do not appear to do any maintenance or cleaning in the rooms or on the outdoor stairways. We've never had a problem like this with an Extended Stay hotel and were very disappointed. We will not stay here again.

title: “Perfect, Perfect, Perfect!”
text:
I travelled from London and was lucky enough to stay at the hotel for two fabulous weeks last summer (late June-early July). The hotel catered perfectly for us, from the service, to the cleanliness of the rooms it was wonderful. We loved the pool area, the gorgeous waitresses were especially helpful, bringing us endless free water and the food in the pool area is divine. I recommend the Kobe sliders and the sorbet! 
There was also a man (don't know his name but he was tall and bald, excuse the unflattering description) he was SO kind and helpful, always looking out for us and the fellow guests especially when there were public pool parties. He always made sure that we had priority over sunbeds etc, sounds basic but it was thoughtful and we appreciated it.
The rooms were spectacular, MASSIVE power shower, excellent ipod dock and television. I particularly loved sitting at the window seat, looking at the stunning view in the evening with a book.
The only negative I can think of is that the hotel is ridiculously expensive, nothing is free (apart from the water and green apples in the gym) but from you get great value for money.
The location is excellent, don't listen to the moaners, the Kodak theatre, The Roosevelt etc is all a 10 min walk away. Who wants to be staying literally on the door step of such a tourist attraction anyway, imagine the noise.
We spotted a number of celebrities including STEVIE WONDER who walked in and randomly performed in the lobby, it was so surreal and so Hollywood!
I am planning to return to the W next summer for a couple of weeks and I could not recommend it highly enough if you have the money and want a glamourous and fun experience.
Top things to do at the hotel, a light lunch in the lobby (you can access free-wifi there so don't know why people have complained), treat yourself to dinner at Drais (roof-top of the hotel) and then maybe go to the nightclub Drais after 10.30pm. You have it all in once place, utilise it!
There is often live music in the outdoor space and they also show classic films.
Writing this review has made me really nostalgic. One of the best hotels, I've ever stayed at and I can't wait to return.

title: “Awesome experience!”
text: The decor was great and totally embodied the purpose of our trip...fun fun fun. The staff was friendly and helpful. The food in the restaurant was excellent . The rooms were comfortable and chic! We will definitely be returning!

title: “Just what I expected.”
text:
My expectations on this hotel were realistic. I was looking for a reasonably priced hotel in a good location for sightseeing. Thats exactly what I got.
Drinks in the hotel were expensive.
We found the staff to be quite helpful and friendly.
The room was large, clean, simply decorated but adequate.
Location is superb - within easy travel of all the sights.
This was our honeymoon - it was a perfect base.
You go to New York to see the sights - not for the hotel. The only time we were in the hotel was to sleep.
If you book a cheap hotel - that what you get. Why waste money on an expensive hotel in New York?

title: “Absolutely outstanding, ignore the negative reviews....”
text:
My Wife and I stayed at the Westin in Seattle for 6 nights as part of a two week trip around the Pacific Northwest. We arrived on the Saturday of Memorial Weekend and paid $119 + tax booked indirect with a UK provider. This was $60+ tax cheaper than the best rate available direct from the Westin website.
Whilst appreciating the great price for a Downtown property in Seattle we were rather concerned by the negative reviews that seemed to be consistently posted by Tripadvisor users, but as it turned out a number of these were one review contributors and I did start to believe that there was some kind of vendetta against the Westin. Whether this is true or not, I don’t know, but it did leave us feeling rather uneasy before travelling to Seattle.
We didn’t need to worry at all.
We arrived from the airport using the Light Rail, which takes about 35mins to the Westlake Center and is $2.50 per person. It is a 2 minute walk from here to the Westin entrance.
First impressions were excellent. The hotel does have a lovely lobby area which is huge, with a number of seating areas along with a bar, and a breakfast/lunch café at one end. The reception desk was well staffed and we were able to check in immediately. We were greeted by a lovely young lady who seemed as happy to see us as we were to see her and she kindly provided us with a King Bed Space Needle view on the 20th floor of the North Tower.
Our first experience with the ‘notorious’ Westin elevators was put to the test and passed with flying colours. It was seconds before we were up on the 20th floor. The public areas on the 20th floor are very well maintained and certainly up to a 4* level.
Upon entering the room we were blown away. There was a small reception area leading to the bathroom and a mirrored wardrobe directly in front of us. To the right was a small walk through to the main bedroom and a glorious Heavenly King Bed, a sofa, chair and desk and a rounded window which had one of the best views I have ever seen in any hotel throughout the world.
It really was a stunning room, the bed was perhaps the best I have ever experienced and most importantly it was spotless, with no sign of the wear and tear mentioned in other reviews.
The bathroom was also spotless and a nice size. The much talked about Heavenly Shower was outstanding, again one of the best I have ever experienced and a nice vanity area with plenty of towels included as well.
To top the room as a whole off, there were his and her robes, an ironing board/iron and an easy to use safe. What more could you want? It really was a 10/10 room.
A really big issue at the Westin seems to be the wait for the elevators. There was on occasions a sign up saying that due to the number of people staying at the hotel there may be a wait, but I would say we had to wait a minute most each time and this was over Memorial Weekend and also with a few large conferences taking place. It really isn’t as much of a deal as some previous reviewers have made out.
We didn’t dine in the Cornerstone Café in the Westin as there are so many great restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. We did however have breakfast a couple of times in the 5th Avenue Café and we found this to be good value. There was a special available each morning of a pastry and coffee for $3.00 which was a great deal, and the service was always spot on as well. We didn’t experience the lack of seats/tables like some have on here but if the room was full, I would expect people to utilise the seats in the lobby. It really isn’t such a big deal.
Another huge plus point for the hotel is the pool area and hot tub. My Wife enjoyed heading down to the 5th floor for this on a daily basis and her experience was very positive.
As for location, well I doubt it can be beaten in Seattle, minutes from the best shopping and attractions in the Seattle, all within an easy walk. I did laugh earlier when I read a review stating that Pike Place and the Waterfront were a bit of a trek from the Westin, it really isn’t very far at all. 5 minutes on foot to Pike Place and then just a short walk down (easier than up) to the Waterfront. It is quite hilly, but that is Seattle. For easier access to the Waterfront, I would recommend the 99 bus which is free and goes up 1st and around via the Waterfront.
Seattle Center was easily reachable via the Monorail (station 2 minutes walk from the hotel) and a 90 second train journey but you could easily walk there as well. The area seemed very safe at day and night with plenty of people about. There was also a station for the Lake Union Streetcar directly across from the hotel which was another transportation option available.
Overall, this is a great hotel in a fantastic location. I would definitely take some of the reviews which have heavily criticised the hotel with a pinch of salt. This is easily a 4* property. As for Seattle, what a wonderful city and we both can’t wait to return again in the future.
Highly recommended all round.

title: “Friendly staff made for a great stay”
text: This hotel is in a great location, the rooms are comfortable, and the staff is wonderfully accommodating. I arrived early in the morning and my room was all ready. I was also able to get a late checkout my last day. I had a fantastic breakfast in the restaurant. The restaurant staff was friendly and the service was very fast. It's a great place for breakfast if you're on business and need a quick bite. A short walk or trolly ride to the conference center and nearby restaurants.

title: “Very Nice, maybe worth it to upgrade”
text: We thought the Dana was very nice. The lobby and pool area looked new and modern, staff was very friendly and helpful. The actual room we stayed in was ok. It was more like a motel where the doors to the rooms were on the outside of the building (we weren't expecting that). There is a newer building we could have stayed in...for an extra charge. That one looked a lot nicer with balconies overlooking the bay. Would probably pay the extra $ for one of those rooms if we were to stay there again.

title: “Horrible experience.”
text: Horrible service. Called twice to have television looked at and no one ever came. Called twice and waited 45 minutes to have luggage picked up. Vent over the shower was missing and crammed with plastic. Windows were so dirty you can't even see out of them. Very old worn out rooms that are not maintained and staff that take themselves far too serious and customer service far too lightly. You can stay a 1/2 block away for half the price and double the service.

title: “tourist in NYC”
text:
I put lots of research in to the perfect place for my girlfriend and I to stay for our 4day stay in NY. 
THe reviews on the site were spot on. We had a fantastic experience. I totally recommend the hotel. The next time I go to New York, whilst its nice to 'try somewhere new' I shall be do my best to stay in the Dumont.
We asked for a view of the Chrysler building, Id recommend this. What a site! 
The only other point Id make apart from all the other ones on the site are that the Kingsize bed was the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in. Having a bad back and being 6ft 4 in height, I can be quite particular about the bed. I could have slept for years. Infact it was so comfortable that at times its hard to get up at all! 
Also I used the gym. Its the first Hotel Gym I have been in that actually provides enough good equipment to work out with!
If youre like me and you spends ages researching a hotel online before you book it, stop researching, the reviews ring true. This is a fantastic place to stay.
We stayed over the third weekend in January having travelled over from Ireland.
Finally theres a great Italian restaurnat on 3rd avenue. Take a right as you go out the door and its just across the street.

title: “Great location and great service”
text: The staff were very helpful, the location is excellent, the room were just the right size for us. I think I'm gonna come back in Christmas and I definitely will stay in this hotel. The only thing: the lobby is too dark. I think they could use more lights in it.

title: “Experience at La Quinta , Phoenix-Arcadia”
text:
This is our second stay at this motel. It is clean, cheerful and convenient to airport, malls etc.
Large rooms with refrig, microwave and 2nd sink.
Very reasonably priced. Would return again.

title: “An excellent hotel that allows you to have a very "un-touristic" stay right in the heart of the city. Great location!!!!”
text: This of course is a luxury hotel, however its location really makes it great for leisure stay in the city. The design of the hotel is very different in that it doesn't "scream" hotel, but resembles more of a residential structure. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay over the weekend and walked everywhere. The only small negative is that there is no Wi-Fi in the rooms, so trekking down to the Business Center in a robe (provided) to use the internet is out-of-the-question. Rooms are beautiful and the view of Market Street is beautiful day and night. We had no trouble with noise or anything else - strongly recommend this hotel!

title: “"TERRIBLE!"”
text: The service sucks! No breakfast, elevators don't work, t.v. and phones also don't work. Well i got a story 2 tell: Once when I was coming up from the pool, me and my Mom were staying on the second floor, So when I was coming up 2 the second floor, I was texting my friend Caroline, I opend the door, and all of a sudden from the right of my head, I heard a little girl say "Hello" to me!
