title: “Brand new. Plenty of room for improvement”
text:
We stayed here two nights (3/16 -3/18) during Spring Break to visit Fiesta Texas. It was open about a week. It is close to the park. It is not a bad place but....some of the issues/problems I noticed were as follows:
It was tough to find this place. The phone number on my Priority Club confirmation was wrong and the address didn't show up on my GPS. I know that is because it is so new (I get quarterly GPS updates) but I couldnt even call the front desk and had to get the number from Priority Club while I was trying to find it. There is a Sam's right next to the hotel. Punch that in and you will be fine.
The bed was really hard. The couch they had in the room was hard as a rock also.
Lighting in the room was dark. They all worked but it just wasn't enough to me.
Rooms are on the small side. 
Housekeeping seems to still be trying to get thier timing and routine down. We came back from the park at 9 pm and they were just bringing towels to our room. They had forgotten to bring face towels so they had to bring us those also.
It is new and clean. Hopefully they will improve as they get their feet on the ground. I would stay again and Priority Club points are important to me but for $135 a night, I think there might be better options for the same price range nearby.

title: “A relic of the golden era of Hollywood, great location but needs work”
text:
Driving along Ventura Boulevard you arrive at the Sportsmens Lodge, our hotel in LA at the end of our roadtrip down from San Francisco. It is like stepping back in time, you can imagine the greats of the silver screen staying here in their heyday. Now it is still a nice hotel but needs bringing back to it's former glory.
The hotel is huge, with a large car park to match so no problem finding anywhere to park. The staff are really nice but on your way to your room you will see what I mean, the decor is dated as are the rooms with a 1970s feel. The rooms though are comfortable and clean, and our trip was one where we weren't spending any time in our room so it's wasn't like we were at all disappointed, but just to let you know what it's like so you know.
We didn't use the restaurants at the hotel, they did seem a bit pricey, so we headed outside, walking down to Jerrys and also Twains, two diners very nearby
One main advantage of the Sportsmens Lodge is the location, especially for Universal. The hotel offer a free shuttle to the park, all you need to do is tell them what time you want to go. You can also book the shuttle for later on, I think the latest one is 8.15pm, which we were going to get but found a good spot on City Walk at the Hard Rock Cafe so stayed for much longer and caught a cab!
Also a good spot for the Warner Studio Tour, which is brilliant and along with Universal I would recommend. We drove to Warner in 10 minutes or so and drove into downtown LA in 20 minutes. 
Again, if you are staying here for a short period, then i would definitely recommend the Sportsmen Lodge and if the hotel owners decided to spend a siginicant amount of money on this place it would rise up and be great once again!

title: “Beautiful, but not great serice”
text:
Although it is a beautiful hotel on a nice property, the service was somewhat bad. When asked where to go dine, the conceige flopped 2 huge books in front of me with a grumble and nothing more.
 Unlike other hiltons we have stayed in, this one makes you pay for everything, and pay alot. A cheeseburger for lunch was over 12$. Breakfast was 22$. Also on the last day we stayed there, they skipped us on cleaning up the room. After tiding up the room ourselves we called for some towels and coffee. We received some towels with no other ameties, as if they were bothered that we picked up on their mistake. For the $$ that you pay the service was not up to par. We are Hilton Honors members and usually receive great treatment. Not so at this one. Prepare to Pay!!

title: “The perfect place to stay while in Memphis”
text:
I stayed there one night while in business trip. This was a great surprise for a boutique hotel.
The staff is very friendly, you are welcome at check in with a glass of champagne, get chocolates in your room, complimentary breakfast at Paulette's ( and what a great breakfast!), complimentary wifi, and a great lobby with a real fireplace!
Either on vacation or on business trip, it is to me the perfect place up stay in Memphis.
The big plus is the free access to the local fitness center a block away.
Cannot wait to come back to Memphis to enjoy that hotel and go to Paulette's restaurant again!

title: “Good location”
text:
The hotel is in a good location and is ok (just getting a bit old now) but neat and tidy and Internet is free.
The only disappointment is that they say that breakfast is included in the room rate but only give you $20 credit at the in house restaurant and if you both have a coffee and a juice you have used $12 before you start to order food. I think they need to look at increasing the amount that they give you or inform customers that this is all you receive and not a full breakfast as stated on the net.

title: “Will never return to this hotel”
text:
This is my 12th visit to New York from the UK and every time I like to stay in a new Hotel. But I have never experienced such bad service from a hotel as from this one. This trip I took with my mother. 
We arrived at the hotel to some "not mentioned about before" renovation work being done in the Lobby and to the lifts. Above the noise of the drilling I was told that we had been upgraded to a better room. Thanking them we went up to a nice, but small corner room with only one double bed. I went down to explain that I was with my mother and a double bed was out of the question, The surly, miserable and unhelpful receptionists (they would call themselves professional, I would could call them surly) explained that although it was only 2pm, there was nothing they could do and refused to change the room at all. Not even to the room that was originally booked. Their sighs under the breath and shrugged shoulders infurated me. After speaking to the sweating manager he promised a rollaway bed would be delivered at once. Two hours later - no rollaway bed. Another trip to the reception. "Its on its way!". When we returned from Dinner - still no rollaway bed! Many trips on the hour down to reception right up to Midnight - no rollaway bed was ever delivered. The receptionists and Manager are well trained in fobbing people off. They appeared to be running around in circles, unable to cope. On my regular trips down to reception many others seemed to be experiencing similar problems - "The room's not ready yet - come back in an hour" seemed to be their catchphrase.
There are many Hotels in New York and anyone would be MAD to choose this one. But if you want to take a chance - be my guest! I have never been so thankful for a holiday to finish.

title: “Cheap Place to Stay, Great Location, Friendly Staff”
text:
I saw one reviewer mention an uptight concierge. I think I know who you mean. I think she was just being civil, clearly should not be desk staff. The other desk staff members were very cordial and would make suggestions when I had a question as to getting to the airport, what to eat, where to go, and so on. The lobby area has a nice fireplace area and tons of travel literature. 
When I checked out the breakfast buffet, it was quite ample. I must have come at a bad time because there were no staff on duty and lots of tables were not bussed. Also they were out of coffee. This was not the case the next day, so perhaps a fluke. 
The elevator is pretty clunky. The door closes slowly and should be repaired or made to be smoother. 
The room was great and eco-friendly. Recycling is encouraged. The bathroom area has lotions, shampoo and conditioner in dispensers rather than little bottles. This is great for the hotel especially from guests who like to rip off bottles. Probably saves money for them, certainly. 
I heard mention of homeless. Well, they're in every city, and to criticize the hotel for a city problem is not fair. If you're city smart they usually are not a problem. 
I also appreciated the follow-up call from the Best Western staff to ensure I had a good stay. 
Proximity to the Monorail and the Space Needle and museums was also perfect.

title: “One of the best....”
text:
We didnt stay here but did a sight inspection as part of work (I am a travel agent).
Located once again in the heart of Union Square this hotel would be one of the nicest in San Francisco. This hotel was built in 1904 and was burnt down in 1906. It was rebuilt in 1909 and is now a historic, luxury building. 
The rooms are of a medium size and all feature the trademark ‘Westin Heavenly Beds’. The hotel offers its own arcade of shops in the lower level, and a 5 star dining restaurant – Michael Mina. Michael Mina is a 3 hour dining experience not to be missed.

title: “Clean Hotel with the basics covered”
text:
We needed a place to stay way after midnight (2:30am). The Days Inn had smoking rooms only left but it works for $75 on Saturday night. Our double queen room (119) was very clean with a full kitchen, microwave, dishwasher, electric stove top and full fridge! Don't forget the granite counter tops in the kitchen and bathroom! The beds were a little hard but plenty of nice big pillows(3) each. The decor was minimal and there was a table and chairs for two. I believe the tv was a 27 inch but we never turned it on. 
This place was great for the price and took care of us for the night. No funny smell, no strange findings and the A/C worked very well! The location was quiet and our room faced the freeway. Only downfall was the lighting was inadequate for the size of the room.

title: “Great location but....”
text: We came on the train to San Diego so the Holiday Inn was very convenient to the train station, the water front, Little Italy and downtown. The deli in front had really good breakfasts. The hotel is average but the location is perfect. This would make a good location for a pre/post cruise stay because it is just across the street from the cruise ship terminal.

title: “Enjoyable Stay”
text:
The value for the type hotel and room I stayed in was good compared to other hotels in the immediate area.
Kept busy and didn't spend a lot of time at hotel, but very nice with polite and helpful staff. 
Pros: Stayed in roomy King Room with clean, updated and modern decor. Most comfortable bed I've ever had in a hotel. Large nice tile walk in shower with very large rain shower head, plus hand-held. Luxury robe and slippers also provided, along with bottled water and mints bed side.
Cons: There is no refrigerator or microwave for personal use. 
 An in room stocked refrigerator and snack bar is provided, but really pricey!

title: “average food service; hard to get copy of bill”
text:
the grounds are beautiful and the room was ok. All of the dining facilities were average with the best food at Trellis's. 
My biggest frustration was losing my bill (in order to get reimbursed by my company). There is no direct e-mail and I had to leave a message on an answering machine stating to leave my address so that they could mail it to me. I had/and still have no idea whether the message was heard and whether the bill is on it's way. Doesn't it make more sense to just have the bill sent to my e-mail? Only place I've ever run into that has this practice.

title: “Excellent”
text: Great Hotel Excellent amenities and service. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Eveything is ok”
text:
Good location. We had a clean, quiet and nice room. Parking ok. Very comfty king size bed ! May be missing some arrangements and a hair dryer in the room. But it's a good hotel, effective. We had a good stay. OK. I recommend it.

title: “Smallish rooms excellent service”
text: some of the great things about this hotel is thr excellent staff, location near Hollywood, great buffett,, good bartenders. I thought the rooms were too small for two people.

title: “HATED IT, KEEP AWAY FROM THIS THE WORST SERVICE YOU`LL EVER GET”
text:
This hotel calls itself a 4 star hotel , it deserves less than 2 stars. 
I recently stayed at the Stay hotel in nyc. I always book hotels in ny and i am always satisfied with the service and value of your properties, but this time i am very upset. The stay hotel has the worst service i ever experienced, the staff is always angry, the do not like to service. I arrived and was assigned a small room instead of the medium i booked. I came downstairs and told the desk person called derek that i didn't like the room and he offered me to check out if i didn't liked it. I wanted to speak to the manager and he said the manager was not available. After an argument he moved me to a medium room. Rooms are not nice, they are partially refurbished (it used to be a quality inn) no servibar, not a nice decoration at all.
 later on i wanted to cash a 100 usd traveller check and he would not take it. He refused to exchange it, this never happened before. The housekeepers were rude and kept knocking on the door in the morning even with the do not disturb sign on. Later on, they didn`t want to clean the room after 3pm. The staff as i said is rude, very rude, they never say hello, even when i said hello to the people in the entrance when i was coming in and out. My experience in other hotels in ny have been fantastic, i loved the empire, the night, the jolly madison, the carlyle (of course), the sheraton ny, the time, the six columbus and many more, but the stay i hated it and wil never, never return. Just to let you know, so you do not sell this hotel, it is really a bad travel experience. Thanks. Claudio Carrera , [-]

title: “Needs some TLC”
text:
While this hotel wasn't too bad, in my opinion it just doesn't live up to the other great reviews here. We received a (supposedly) upgraded room, but the toilet handle was loose, the sink drained poorly and some TV channels were missing. In the common areas, some elevator buttons were unmarked and carpeting was worn. The hotel's sign on the building was not lit, making a difficult-to-get-to hotel even more hard to find.
Does any of this affect your night's sleep? No, but hearing the music from a wedding on the 3rd floor does.
Breakfast buffet food was poor; I don't recommend it, even for free. We've stayed at several Marriott Renaissance hotels and this one was disappointing. You don't want to pay more than $120/night here unless you're desperate. But in spite of the facility's shortcomings, the staff was truly accommodating and deserve recognition.

title: “Expectations are high when it's Wyndham”
text:
I was a part of a group wedding rate and was assigned Rm 111. upon returning from the wedding ceremony and reception i found cockroaches in my room. They were the about 2' in length. After whacking the living daylights out of them, I looked around and saw their easy entrance--under the door as there was at least a 2" -3"gap! when I checked out the next morning I brought this to the attention of the young man on duty. I was hoping for more of a reaction, a sense of urgency, apology, a cup of coffee to go. Anything to show he and the management cared. I got nothing! It was as if it were expected. Isn't it amazing how this situation tainted my entire stay there?! If only he had brought someone in management out to express an apology. For that amount of money per night, I was NOT expecting to have cockroaches as room guests! 
I have 8 years experience of business travel throughout the Western states. I have never experienced this or the lack of concern or apology.

title: “Perfect Location, Perfect Room, Perfect Hotel for our needs”
text:
We spent four nights at the Millenium Bostonian at the end of July after researching a number of Boston hotels for many months & the second we opened the door to our room we knew we'd made the right decision.
It's a short 5/10 minute ride from the Airport & on arrival the hotel looks ok but hardly impressive externally. The lobby has been created to provide the guest with a warm, cosy feeling with a small contemporary-style library in one corner which in fact contains a lot of rather impressive coffee-table type books. General decor throughout the hotel was modern & recently refurbished.
The room we were allocated was as impressive as we would expect in a major city centre hotel without moving into the realms of sheer luxury which brings a much heftier price tag. Very tastefully appointed, the bedroom was large, with a lot of light filtering in through the large windows which opened up onto a balcony overlooking the always bustling Fanueil Hall & Marketplace. The Hard Rock Cafe was directly ahead with rock music blaring out adding to the hustle and bustle but once you'd closed the baclony doors the outside sound was virtually non-existent & after 10pm outside noise was at a minimal level anyway. The bed, bedlinen, pillows etc were heavenly.
We had a "Dressing Area" bewteen the bedroom and bathroom consisting of large wardrobe/closet with free digital security safe & Dressing Table & Stool with space to store luggage, this was a lovely touch when travelling with four large items of luggage. 
The bathroom was very impressive, all fixtures were top quality with a huge shower & all very modern.
Location-wise we felt was impossible to beat. As first time vistors to Boston, we considered three different areas to stay but on extensively checking out each of these areas when visting, we were extremely pleased we stayed at the Marketplace. A whole array of shops, restaurants & the amazing food on offer at Quincy Market is steps from your room, The Waterfront is 5 mins & Downtown Crossing is approx 10/15 mins walk as is Boston Common. Most places you'd want to visit are well within walking distance although if you did want to walk to say Fenway Park I'd guess this would probably take upto an hour perhaps, we visited when doing a trolley tour & walked to the Prudential Centre from there.
We had considered staying at the Fairmont Copley Place & 2 other Copley Square hotels but whilst I'm sure they were fine, we were extremely pleased we'd gone with the Millenium. We'd also looked at the 2 Marriotts & Hilton and again were glad we didnt stay there.
We found Reception Staff to be great & the guys at the door were always on hand with an umbrella or to help with luggage & cabs without coming across as tip-hungry. We didn't use the hotel bar, restaurant or mini bar as there are so many alternatives on your doorstep.
Cost-wise we found most hotels of what we'd call a 4 Star level to all be around the same cost ($150 - $200 per night) during our stay & we were pleased with what we got for our money. 
Overall, we were delighted with our stay at the Bostonian and are staggered that as of July '09 it's only rated as thirtysomething in the list of hotels rated in Boston. This must reflect many reviews during a refurbishment or something similar as there is no way there are 20+ hotels better than the Millenium in this relatively small city. We weren't looking for a pool, gym, extensive number of public computers, "cool" coffee shop in the lobby during our stay. We wanted a great location with a great room & we got exactly this here at the Millenium Bostonian.

title: “More than we bargained for!”
text: I had stayed in this hotel previously in 1991 and enjoyed the location and easy access to the areas of the city we were visiting - but what a scruffy, run-down establishment it has now become. There is a peculair smell in the lobby area and the corridors and rooms are delapidated and showing their age. Chipped paint, peeling wall-paper and frayed carpets were a feature of our room along with a major infestation of bed-bugs which bit me extensively! They did agree the room would be fumigated following my complaint but they did not appear surprised to hear about the additional room occupants! If you know what is good for you - STAY AWAY!

title: “What a excellent hotel! Brilliant location, brilliant service! Excellent room! Couldn't wish for more! :-) 10/10”
text:
This hotel was AMAZING! Brilliant location within short walking distance of everything you want to see in New York. 
We went here for my partners birthday for 4 nights while the Christmas season was starting. We were upgraded to a HUGE suite on the 26th floor with amazing views of Times Square, the river, Maddison Square Gardens and many more pleasant views especially at sunrise and sunset especially from out huge balcony!!! 
Our room had a big bedroom, living room, dining area, kitchen, en suite, bathroom, walk in wardrobe and a massive balcony. 
The room was cleaned, bed made daily. 
The reception was a big area with plenty of assistants to help with anything you wish.
I will DEFO go back to this hotel it was just what I wanted and well worth every penny I paid to stay here. Couldn't of asked for more. :-) 10/10

title: “Hated it!”
text: I wish I would have listened to the reviews. This hotel was nothing but problems for us. First we were given a room that was completely demolished and was under renovations. Oops. Then the next room had stains on the furniture, peeling wallpaper, smelled of smoke and was so scary that we slept with the bathroom light on. I can't forget to mention the mouse that found its way into our room and decided to greet us. We were then given another room which was much better but after my experience at this hotel, I would never stay there again! The only good thing about it was the bar connected to the hotel where we met some some great people.

title: “Very nice and friendly place”
text: Was very impessed with this hotel. Staff was helpful and rooms were very nice. would definately go stay there again. Only thing i didn't like verious other starwood properties such as the downtown Sheraton was that at the Sheraton you had a free breakfast and the Westin didn't. Other then that it was great.

title: “Beautiful hotel in downtown San Diego”
text: This is one of the trendiest hilton hotels I've been to. I wish they made more of them like this. It's a gorgeously appointed hotel. The rooms are large, and the special wing of the hotel (I can't think of the name if it of hand) is really nice. We had a huge jacuzzi tub that looked out into the bedroom. It was very romantic. It's convienently located in the gaslamp district, although I'd recommend renting a car if I were you, since San Diego is a city that can't merely be traversed on foot. Service was good at this hotel, as well. I'd highly recommend it.

title: “Renita”
text: Renita the desk clerk was very helpful and kind. I got in at 5am on Friday and the desk clerk really wasn't very helpful. All she did was hand me my key and pointed me to the elevator. Where as Renita told me everything that I needed to know on Sunday, July 22, 2012.

title: “This Hilton is not up there with other Hilton properties.”
text: Arrived at 7 PM. About $30 cab ride from airport. The bell hop was quick and helpful. The "check-in" kiosk did not print out room info but did issue key. Front desk staff not particularly helpful or apologetic. Room a bit tired. An old phone message on the system from several days earlier for a previous occupant. Safety latch on door missing a couple of screws. Room generally a bit "tired" looking. Internet is $13 for 24 hours. Small single cup coffee maker was terrific! Delmonico's is OK for dinner, not great, just OK (but very expensive).

title: “We Love the Giraffe!”
text: We stayed at the Giraffe for a week. The young staff were amazing-friendly, very helpful and altogether impressive. It was good value, very comfortable and the housekeeping was spot on. We will certainly return to the Giraffe for our next visit to New York City.

title: “Not What I Expected”
text:
I recently stayed at this hotel during a business trip to San Diego. The hotel's website made the place look better than it actually was. First, the bathroom in my room was dirty (such as the floors and bathtub). In addition, a couple of the lightbulbs in my room were dead. 
Like most hotels that I've stayed at, this place has a business center with computers for guests to use. However, unlike most hotels, this place charges guests to use the computers (such as to surf the internet). You should also know that this hotel does not offer a complimentary continental breakfast.

title: “Great”
text: We were stuck in Columbus late at night after one of my friends tires went on his car, and it was too late to get it fixed anywhere. We managed to get a room here. It was at a great price. The breakfast was good, and I loved the pool.

title: “Very unorganized”
text: Arrived at 4:30 and rooms were not ready. Given a key to a room and the bed had no sheets. Went back down and the receptionist couldn't find a room that was ready...while waiting at the front desk one guest came up and said there was construction going on in her room and another guest was requesting sheets so he could make up his own bed. The lobby was dirty...cups and straws on floor and glass top table was full of fingerprints. While waiting we tried to download and print our boarding passes but could not. The receptionist told us the printer was out of ink and said, "Couldn't we just print our passes at the airport?" We left and went to the Comfort Suites...great room and a little bit less in price. Will never stay at a Microtel again!

title: “Nice hotel and good location”
text: Stayed here for a week on business. Nice property and well maintained. The staff is very competent and pleasant. It met the two must important points for me, a good shower and comfortable bed. Close to restaurants and shopping (there is a Macaroni Grill next door). I will stay here again if the opportunity arises. Can't go wrong here for this type of lodging.

title: “fantastic hotel!”
text: The location of this hotel can't be beat. Right in the heart of Nob Hill, way up on a hill with views of the Bay Bridge, Grace Cathedral, this hotel is great for someone wanting to explore SF. The room is small but clean and modern and comfortable. You'll of course pay for the location but its worth it.

title: “great palce to stay with friends”
text: I stayed at this hotel about a month ago. Me and a couple friends were visiting Houston. Its really cozy and feels at home. The staff was very nice and although, there were multiple desk clerks, they were very well mannered. And the pool was a great place to just go and relax. We weren't looking for anything fancy, the rooms there were just enough. Great beds, mini fridge, TV, sofa, and free internet. I would definitely come back to this hotel. just need to make a trip back to houston

title: “Location location location.”
text:
On arrival the staff were very pleasant and we checked in. Our room was a decent size and clean. Plenty of cupboard space with a free safe to use. The shower worked well. The room was a little cool though.
Staff were helpful and gave us a map to get around. 
We found the location great with the central station just outside ( try the oyster bar for a meal there) Times Square was about a 10 min quick walk. 
The hotel kept our cases on the last day so we could fully enjoy our last day to the full. They booked a taxi for our return to JFK airport which cost $65. ( taxi from the airport to the hotel will cost you $60 all in.)
All in all good value , clean good location and would recommend it either for a long weekend or a weeks holiday to visit New York . Ps : recommend a 3 day pass for the attractions and the lion king .

title: “Terrific Hotel Experience”
text: Just returned from 3 night stay over the Labor Day weekend at the Hotel Monaco Seattle. We met some friends of ours, who also stayed there in a separate room. The location was good for us and anyone who doesn't have issues with moderate walking -- it was a multi-block walk to Pikes Market, the waterfront, etc. -- you do have up hill walking when you return to the hotel from Pikes Market or the waterfront, though we found some streets to be less steep than others (Union Street, for instance). From the moment we arrived at the hotel we found the staff to be friendly, professional and helpful, and this continued throughout our stay -- the valet, doorman, front desk reps, concierge, housekeeping, etc. Each time we were leaving the hotel, the front desk people would acknowledge us with pleasantries such as "have a nice day"; upon our return they would again acknowledge us with "welcome back", or something similar. The evening wine event in the lobby was a very nice touch. The overall feel of the hotel was that it was nicely decorated and clean and felt welcoming. The room was also nicely decorated and clean and larger than the average hotel room. There was ample comfortable seating, i.e. two upholstered chairs and a very comfortable desk chair at the large desk. Also, the room had multiple sources of bright lighting -- best lighting of any hotel we've stayed in. There was a nice size flat screen TV, stocked mini-fridge (items for purchase), stocked snack tray (also for purchase), and a room safe as well. Though coffee service is provided in the lobby each morning, there is no coffee service in the room, however, you can request a set-up for your room, if desired. The beds were extremely comfortable, i.e. the mattress, linens, comforter, and pillows. The air conditioner worked great and you are able to control the temp. to your liking from the in-room thermostat. The bathroom, too, was larger than usual. The shower head was to die for and with great water pressure, so you didn't have to spend a longer-than-usual amount of time in the shower trying to shower with a trickle of water, as is the case in many hotels (especially important to those of us with longer, thicker hair). They also had a wall-mounted rack containing full-size pump bottles of shampoo, cream rinse, and liquid bath soap. A hair dryer was also provided. You should know ahead of time, as we did, that many of the rooms face directly towards another high rise, in close proximity, especially if you want a room with two beds versus a king; we were told that there are no two bed rooms not facing the building; besides not having a view or much natural light, this necessitates keeping your curtains closed for privacy -- but, again, at least there's great lighting provided in the room. There are only two things I would add to my wish list for the hotel -- one is to have at least some two-bed rooms that don't face a building and the second is to provide larger than the standard size bath towels. All in all, this was a terrific hotel experience and we will definitely return there on future trips. This was our first stay at a Kimpton Hotel but, based on this experience, it won't be our last!

title: “Fantastic Hotel!”
text: I can't say enough good things about this boutique Manhattan hotel. Terrific location, great rooms, good breakfast and reading lounge and attentive staff. I did a ton of research trying to find the best hotel for a long weekend trip for a birthday trip and this hotel is as good as it looks We booked a room with a Queen sized bed, and it was not big, but has absolutely everything you need. It's not cheap, but you get what you pay for. Bottom line: stop searching, this is a great place.

title: “Nice, clean hotel with very friendly helpful staff”
text:
stayed at this hotel for a long weekend of shopping and sightseeing. The location is great, the room wasn't the biggest but it was very clean and maids came in everyday.
All the staff were extremely helpful and friendly, especially Sam the doorman, lovely guy!
The subway is a five minute walk from the hotel. Basically, the hotel is clean, cheap and cheerful and i would definately stay there again.

title: “Smart choice”
text: I have stayed at the onyx hotel several times, and each time seems better then the last. it is a fabulous hotel with staff to match. overhearing me and my friends were staying on behalf of a birthday, mr. howlzworth sent an adorable card accompanied with a bottle of wine to our room. he was also increadibly helpful with recomondations on resteraunts, local attractions and nightlife. other than the staff the onyx is hip, clean and has a convienient location. based on my stays here i would recomend the hotel anytime, you will not be disappointed.

title: “Nice location”
text: The location of the doubletree is great as it is nearby to everything. The staff is very friendly, the beds are comfy, and the restuarant & bar was wonderful.

title: “Great staff but construction noise intolerable”
text:
My client decided to hold a week long meeting here. While I have stayed at Hyatt Regencys before, this one fell well below expectations. But there were some positives.
First the positives. If you are attending a conference or convention at the Columbus Convention Center, this place is ideally located. There is a walkway directly to the Convention Center. Plus, the Arena is about a block away which makes this a convenient place to stay if you are going to a concert there. 
The food during our meeting was phenomenal. Everyday was like a gourmet lunch! And the attention paid to us during our week long meeting was exemplary. As a matter of fact, in any interaction I had with the staff, they were terrific and very customer focused.
I found housekeeping to be very good, although my room could have been vacuumed more than just the one time I was there.
There are plenty of restaurants, pubs, bars all within walking distance. If you go, I would recommend a trip to North market, which is an indoor market with some very interesting food selections. And all reasonably priced.
Now the bad news. This hotel needs a major workover. Having stayed at other Hyatt Regencys, I was disappointed in the decor and style of the rooms. I got "upgraded" to a larger room, but it was actually a little uncomfortable as the chairs were not very comfortable to sit in. I would have preferred a regular room. Plus the lighting in this larger room was very poor. Even with every lamp on, the room was still very dark.
But the biggest issue was the construction going on outside. Evidently, because this is a very busy part of the city, and the streets and sidewalks all around the hotel are being overhauled, the city of Columbus must have decided that the best time to do it would be at night. I realize the hotel cannot do anything about this,but it does not discount the fact that the jack-hammers and construction trucks started their work at about 8:00 PM and it went on all night! If you go here, definitely ask if there is still a lot of construction going on right outside. And if there is, go somewhere else. I was on the 12th floor and the noise, even with my air-conditioner on, was still enough to disturb my sleep for five straight nights.
I was also disappointed in the TV service. There was a large screen HD TV in my room but no HD channels. Really? In today's day and age, an upscale hotel like Hyatt Regency has no HD channels available?
Internet was also expensive. A basic daily package was $9.95 per day, but if you want a higher speed service, it was $14.95 per day. I know all high end hotels charge for internet service, but it doesn't make this right.
If you are attending a convention in Columbus, you can't beat the convenience of this location. But ask if there is construction going on and ask for the highest floor you can get, to try to minimize the noise. If it wasn't for the construction, I would give a three star review, because the rooms are still old and run down.

title: “What an incredible hotel!”
text: There isn't a nicer place to stay in Manhattan from my point of view. Mandarin is phenomenal, with great service and attention to detail that they are famous for around the world. The New York City property is one of the best. The spa is luxurious and perfect. The restaurant, Asiate, is delicious. The Lobby Bar great for a light lunch, supper or tea with mom, and MOBAR is the best hotel bar in NYC. The suites are always nice with great views of the park and Manhattan. It's not inexpensive but worth every cent.

title: “A Perfect Ten!!”
text: We stayed at the Westin Times Square February 10-15 - it was our 30th wedding anniversary. We cannot say enough good things about the staff and management of the Westin. I might add that on night #2, a blizzard struck the area and the only 'glitch' was a note that housekeeping would be a bit late. Room service was exactly on time each and every morning. We had a corner room on the 44th floor - the view was great and the hotel very quiet. The room was extraordinarily clean, the bathroom a bit compact but everything was stocked. If we needed anything, we placed a call and within minutes - MINUTES - our requested items were at our door. I've never seen such service. The concierge staff was very responsive and had taken steps to assure a very late arrival was no problem. The hotel management arranged for late check out so we could enjoy our last day in New York City. Would we stay at the Westin Times Square again? In a New York Minute.

title: “What a great and delightful stay !!”
text:
When we first arrived- lobby was beautiful and the front desk clerk was very sweet and helpful. Upon going in room- everything was perfect. Very clean, had a great odor, bed very comfortable and high speed was great. Had a great night sleep. They had a very good hot breakfast. Everything was fresh. The breakfast lady was also very sweet and helpful. I will DEFINENTLY stay there again and I recommend this hotel to everyone that is looking for a hotel that will meet all their requirements and more.
AGAIN, IT WAS AWESOME !!!

title: “Omni not worth the money”
text:
Parking is terrible. Lot charges $10 per day and will re-charge you everytime you leave the lot.
Hotel knickle and dimes you to death. Wireless internet is not free. Discovered this when I got a $10 bill for logging on with my smartphone. 
Mini fridgerator can not be used, because it is full of goodies and booze. The items in the fridge are way overpriced. The 24hr kitchen is nice, but the cooking is terrible and food is terrible.
The bed was not made correctly. There was no fitted sheet on the mattress; it was a top sheet just tucked in. The pillows were not comfortable at all. I might sound picky, but this is supposed to be a 4 Star hotel. Holiday Inn Express hotels provide more comfort than the Omni.

title: “Always a Pleasure”
text:
I've stayed here three times in the last year, and it's always a great experience. The staff is very quick to respond to any requests I have, and the rooms are very comfortable. The renovation has brought in nicer furniture and flat-screen televisions (at last!), but the rooms still had a pretty strong "new paint" smell, which will pass in time.
The location is great for downtown, superb for the Music Center, and also very close to the Pershing Square subway station.

title: “absolute filth”
text: I was in new york and needed somewhere cheap to stay last minute and the hotel carter was all i could find. I think I paid about 120 dollars a night (think i lasted about two) for the room which wasn't exactly cheap. I strongly recommend to try and find something better. Even if you don't stay long in the hotel room just to sleep,it's just not clean enough. i've stayed in a lot of places all over the world but this was definately the worst. It's a very depressing place. It is in a good location but definatley not worth it. How much money must they be making though with all those rooms?

title: “Great hotel, great value”
text:
For a hotel located in the middle of Times Square, the room was large and a good value through travelzoo for our three day stay in April. Most of the other hotels were more expensive and had smaller rooms. 
We stayed in the main tower on the 46th(?) floor. The furnishings seemed new and modern. The bathroom was clean and in good condition. Really fast elevators! 
The staff was accomodating to our request for a higher room with a nice view of Times Square. They also helped us find tickets to see Chorus Line. 
Had a bit of trouble with ordering pay per view movies. The ordering system was too complicated for me, but it's a minor issue. 
Overall, a great experience and when I return to NYC, I'll go back to the Millenium Broadway.

title: “Enjoyed a lovely weekend- Great Concierge Desk~”
text:
MY husband and I stayed at the London back in January for a long weekend. We both love NY and like to try out different hotels. I normally do not post reviews but my husband adamantly persisted me to write this review. We will definitely be back and here's why. 
One- the rooms are spacious and very beautiful. We stayed in one of the apartments and it blew our minds. Our room faced Central Park and just absolutely breathtaking. The bathrooms are beautiful-- nice big tub with a glass shower. The living room was so comfortable and it was such a beautiful apartment. We got a great deal for it.
Two- Richie at the concierge desk made our visit so enjoyable. My husband usually doesn't deal with any of the restaurants/shows/shopping but when we arrived on Friday night, we were starving. I had to run to the room to get ready so he went to the concierge for some recommendations. After 30 minutes and he still hasn't returned. I thought it was because the desk was so busy that he couldn't get any information. That was not the case. I saw him chatting away with the concierge and they became best friends for the weekend. Richie sent us to this great little Italian restaurant on the West Side, a fabulous steak house (Benjamin's) then sent us to this amazing Japanese noodle shop!! We are back in the Windy City and still CRAVE the noodles. By the time we we leaving, he already knew us by our names and the nicest part was that he stepped out from the desk to shake my husband's hand. That is called top-notch service. Basically, my husband would like to say Thank You!! 
The reason why I didn't give the hotel 5 stars is because of the restaurant (MAZE). We had breakfast there one morning and it was a diaster. There were so many empty tables but we weren't allow to sit because the staff were not cleaning up the tables quick enough. Then when we sat, our server was unattentionive and did not care about us. They were rude, obnoxious and for the money we were paying, it was not OK. IF you're going to stay here, stay away from the restaurant. The food isn't that great. We spoke to the manager that morning, Carlos, about it and this poor guy seems more frazzled than anyone else.

title: “Loved it”
text:
Although I booked with Priceline (at a very nice price), I was upgraded to a larger room since one was available - thanks to the very cordial staff. The room had a mild old hotel smell - well, it IS an old hotel that has been nicely redone in an interesting decor. There are great local dining/eating places in a university streetlife setting. Take the Metro bus from the airport for $1.75 and walk 2 short blocks to the hotel or the Shuttle Express van for $19.00. The hotel shuttle picked me up at my conference location and brought me back to the hotel gratis! 
The main thing was that the room was spotless and the bed was extremely comfortable with crisp bedding. The staff was very welcoming and the decor harkened to 1940's in a lovely way.

title: “Nice beds, good food, but noisy and service sub par”
text:
I stayed at the Sofitel LA twice on business trips, for about 5 nights each visit. I had a mixed experience. Not horrible, but you should know what you're getting into. Beds are very comfortable and sleep-conducive -- and good thing because the restaurant downstairs is very noisy well past 2 am most nights. Nice fitness center, pool, and outdoor sitting area above the pool where you can enjoy a drink in the evening. I never sat down at the restaurant but the food they send up to the rooms is very, very good, and comes up unbelievably fast. (So don't take a quick shower after you order.)
My biggest complaint about this hotel is that the staff, while abundant, seem poorly trained or maybe just slow upstairs. Example: On my second trip, my colleague and I arrived very late (around 4 am) due to a delayed flight. We called ahead to make sure our reservations weren't lost, but when we arrived, they only had one room booked. I said that was an error and we'd like two rooms, but the check in attendant told us we were out of luck, that the hotel was fully booked, and maybe I could arrange to get a second room the following day. Well, the one available room had only one king bed, so I asked whether we could change that to two doubles. And the guy said, "yes, I'll give you a different room." ! So obviously I replied, "that means you have two rooms available and you're NOT fully booked." So we got the two rooms.
Anyway, it was irritating because it was very late, we were dog-tired, and the whole process actually took like half an hour. It was so unnecessary and somewhat embarrassing because under the circumstances, it would have been really inappropriate for my colleague and I to share a room. I complained about the guy the following day, but the morning staff seemed surprisingly blase about it -- their attitude was like oh well, this kind of thing just happens from time to time. No apology, just "ohhh . . . but you ended up getting the room, right?" Big smile.
Anyway, to end on a positive note, the pillow menu is awesome.

title: “Not Up To Standards”
text:
Took family for July 4th weekend. We arrived around 1:45AM Saturday morning and they took us to our room. The problem is we had booked a "resort view with balcony" and we were given a ground floor room with small patio with lame view. We called front desk to complain and it took them a good 25 minutes to sort out the problem by giving us a proper room with balcony on 8th floor.
The rooms are ok, nothing extraordinary. In my experience, Marriott tends to cheap out on room finishes and decor. We usually stay at Starwood, Hyatt and Ritz Carlton properties and Marriott seems to be out of touch with contemporary style and comfort. Bedding thread count and bed comfort did not compare to Westin's heavenly bed and the room showed obvious signs of cheap elements where it's obvious Marriott opted for low cost vs. quality. Toilet tissue was single ply and the toilet was not enclosed. The balcony had cigarette buds from previous guest. The facility and resort property is stunning and the view of hills was awesome. The first night we dined at 18 oaks and the food was excellent despite poor service. Steak ordered medium arrived well done. Although I didn't demand a new steak the server insisted and promised it would not take long. 15 minutes later a new steak arrived. Unfortunately, it was only marginally less done than first. Despite the issue with doneness the steak was excellent in taste and seasoning. 
For July 4th we dined at Cibolo Moon and were pleasantly surprised with food quality. Bare in mind it was overpriced IMO. The major disappointment was the special of the night (duck enchiladas). They tasted fine - however, it was not duck! It was chicken! The server lied to us. I'm no Chef, but that was NOT DUCK. Lying to guests is never cool.
Overall we think the JW Marriott is overrated and overpriced. From a quality and comfort standpoint we've had much better experiences at Hyatt Lost Pines and Starwood Properties. The pool is very nice! That said, we didn't like wearing arm bands. Our 3 night stay racked up close to $2,300 in costs and having to wear arm bands feels downright cheap and petty. For room service they could not accommodate my simple request for a Cappuccino. It is odd that a resort the size of a small country cannot serve Cappuccino.

title: “ok, but not great”
text:
Location: close to town center but not ideal. It is at the edge of the city and by the bus transit center, where lots of teens hang around at night.
Room: looks clean and new with contemporary decoration, but not very practical. It comes with kitchen and huge fridge. I don't know how many people will stay here for family trip, for business trip, it is not necessary. The bathroom and closet is in the other side of the mirror and door. For dressing up in the morning, i need to go across the room the check. The linen and pillow is not comfortable. I was on the 13th floor, but still can hear street noise. 
Amenity: Small lobby, no drive way for taxi. small pool and gym.

title: “Great location”
text: Very convenient to downtown, right off main highway to other attractions, great dining options, so close to airport but no noisy plane issues while in the room!

title: “Outstanding service at the Edison”
text:
I recently spent two nights at this hotel, in a Signature Room (2nd and 3rd November). I had booked for six nights, but due to Hurricane Sandy could not get into NY until four days later. The room reservation and transportation staff were incredibly helpful and understanding, and had no problem with two delays in my arrival. On finally reaching New York, I heaved a sigh of relief!
The hotel is fantastically located half a block from Times Square, and although it was only five days after the hurricane, you wouldn’t have thought anything had happened to the City. Everything was running as normal in the mid-town area – subway, buses, shops open, Broadway shows back in business, etc. 
I’d stayed at the Edison once before, but this time I elected to book one of the new “Signature” rooms, with a queen bed. It was not enormous, but tastefully decorated, with everything I needed, including a coffee machine and flat-screen TV, and plenty of closet space. The bathroom was a bit on the small side, with not much surface to put one’s toiletries, but once again had everything I needed (including a bath-tub, which I especially requested). The room was quiet, with a nice feature being that you could open the windows to get some fresh air.
The cherry on the cake was the exceptional service I received from Victor Aybar, the Night Manager. I was struggling at one of the computers late on my second night, trying to do an online check-in for my flight the next day. Victor came to check on whether I had a problem, and if he could help. He was like a knight in shining armour! Long story short, he personally assisted me by phoning the airline (waited on the phone for half an hour for a reply), got to the root of the problem, and then sat with me at his own personal computer and helped me print a boarding pass! This was now 1am in the morning! I just couldn’t believe his kindness and patience with a female in distress! That was definitely a highlight of my very happy stay at the Edison. I will never think of staying anywhere else in the future.

title: “Updated courtyard, comfortable beds, ok service”
text: Updated hotel with nice lobby area and bistro. The bistro is a new Courtyard dining set up - more like a coffee shop/walk up counter with seating around it. The service is inconsistent. Some days I waited for a person to help me, and when I ordered oatmeal each day, what was included with the oatmeal was sometimes different. Overall, however, the hotel is comfortable and great for business or personal use. The rooms are large, the beds are great, and the room was in working order. My husband didn't love the fitness center, but it is typical of most Courtyard hotels. When I returned to Houston the following week, I rebooked at this hotel.

title: “Not Bad”
text: This is a great place if you want to go to the mall or a nearby eatry. The walls are paper thin I could hear the guy next room taking a p---, at about 2am. TVs could use replacing with the newer HDs, counter was great.

title: “Great location and staff”
text: Had to find a hotel after Hurricane Sandy. So glad to have found Amsterdam Court. Very nice rooms. They are small but the beds and bedding are as good as any you will find in NYC. The front desk staff, especially Vana, were very accommodating in the face of an extremely stressful time. I would stay here again any time and definitely will be back.

title: “Rather Disappointing”
text:
Spent a few days/nights here as I was in a conference held at the hotel. First the good things I noted:
1) For an old building the hotel was rather clean, impressively so; perhaps they have recently remodeled, but not sure
2) The thermostats worked well in the rooms, with no vent above the bed blowing air onto you while sleeping
3) The bathroom lighting was GREAT, as was the blow dryer; having long thick hair this is a much appreciated appointment. I'm always amazed how dim the lighting in some hotel bathrooms are for the sake of style. 
4) The style of the room itself was very nice; rather small, it would have been too tight for two, but for me, it was doable.
Now for the items I felt ratcheted down my experience:
1) The hotel, perhaps because it is in an old building, was very very cold.
2) The meeting room on the top floor was especially cold and the thermostat provided no real control; it was all or nothing, so we'd go from freezing (most of the time), to finally feeling some warmth, when it became too much for some of the men.
3) For a meeting with a group of Finance folks how could the hotel not expect everyone to have computers????? When we asked the staff if they had extension cords with power strips to allow us of the power outlets around the room they replied NO. Really? You had folks computers on the floor next to the wall outlets charging up as much as folks could get to them. This is just plain ignorant when a meeting is held.
4) Housekeeping was erratic, sometimes they left me toiletries, and sometimes not. When I called down for some I was brought a different assortment than prior days (ie. shampoo/conditioner on some days, shampoo/body wash on others???????). I think the line up was supposed to be shampoo, conditioner, body wash, and body lotion.
5) for two days I requested that my kleenex be replenished, each time I received a "no problem"; alas, I even pulled up the dispenser, pulled out the empty box, and left it on the counter for them to easily see I needed another. I even called down, went to dinner, came back, and they left me shampoo, but no Kleenex? 
6) The hotel offers to print your boarding pass; I called and requested this service, provided the confirmation number, and indicated they should have it in an envelope for me at check out. Went to the front desk during a break, and they had no knowledge of it, asking "who did you talk to?". Hhhhm, I did not think to get the individuals name and position while requesting this offered service. I had to go back to the conference, get my confirmation number and go back to the desk. 
7) Not controllable by the hotel, but the first night sleep was disturbed by the garbage trucks and breaking bottles, the second night there was some event with loud music and late/early morning revelers. After two nights of bad sleeping conditions the third night I slept fine.
The days I stayed here they may have been off for the hotel, but I will not recommend this hotel or stay again, and I do travel to Philly quite a bit.

title: “A mean hotel at Philly Airport”
text: This one is nothing special, an averaged airport stay for people not needing any means of luxury comfort. The continental breakfast wasn't really something to go for. I was disappointed a little bit as none of the pictures on the hotel's home page was showing the room we recently stayed in. The rooms would need a renewal, many of the furnishings are aged and look time-worn. At least it was acceptable at the rate we have paid. A recommendation for budget travellers only.

title: “Execellent Staff”
text: The staff is outstanding,they go out of there way to help you out,Great Shuttle service to downtown Denver.The hotel is dated and is good for a night or 2..If your looking for turn down service,this is not the hotel..Th Skybox Bar on the 14th floor has a great view of downtown.....

title: “This Place is Not Worth It!”
text:
The place is nice. The rooms were definitely nice with nice linens and bedding, as well as furniture. 
The service was absolutely HORRIBLE and I can say that the niceness of the hotel could never make the LACK OF SERVICE better than it was, nor make me EVER EVER want to go back or even refer someone to go there. 
REASONS:
1.) Check in/Service - the ladies at the front desk ignored everyone, including me, my spouse and his best friend, a groom, who was having his wedding at this location. After 5 minutes of standing there, in front of them, while they failed to acknowledge our presence, they proceeded to check in my spouse and I. This part of the check-in seemed semi-decent; I've seen better. Then it was the groom's turn to check in. This turned into hell. Maria, the lady checking us in, ignored the groom for about 2 minutes while she was on the phone; she failed to acknowledge him properly. Then while she was checking on his room, she said that his future wife already checked into their "day of" room and honeymoon suite. She was confident about it, stating it was a fact. We called the bride to verify; she said she was in her parent's room and did not check in, so, obviously she did not check in. Once we informed her that the bride did not check into the rooms, Maria replied with "Oh... Yeah... well, no one has checked in yet." SERVICE FAIL #1 because she has no idea how to do her job. 
2.) Service - I had some wedding guests in my room prior to the ceremony. There was a wardrobe malfunction and we needed some safety pins. Knowing this was supposed to be a 4 Star Hotel, I thought it would be an easy task for them to complete, especially because another4 Star Japanese hotel in San Diego was able to successfully complete this task in the past. I called down to the front desk and asked for 2 safety pins; they responded stating that they would call housekeeping to see if they could get some and then call me back. 5 minutes pass by, no response. I call back down and ask again. They said the same thing. 10 minutes pass by and nothing happens. I call down for a THIRD time. They responded angrily and said they would check and that they would place me on hold; they hung up. I waited for another 10 minutes for someone to come up to the room. They didn't. I walked downstairs to the front desk and asked how difficult it was to get 2 safety pins; one lady with curly hair responded angrily and said that she heard the lady who answered say what she said and that the phone disconnected and that me "waiting" for 30 minutes was not true. If the phone disconnected, and they know which room the telephone call is coming from, why didn't they call back? They obviously don't know how to do their job and especially don't know what "Customer Service" means. SERVICE FAIL #2. 
3.) Service - After the wedding ceremony, we went down to the Azalia Restaurant. Nice venue and decent but not average service. Due to their inability to maintain the side entrance from the STREET, 2 wedding crashers walked in and grabbed drinks and appetizers. People from the wedding party had to kick them out. I don't know why the hotel didn't take the precaution of blocking off the STREET entrance when they knew a party was being held there and that anyone walking on the street had access to the entrance. SERVICE FAIL #3.
4.) Service - Breakfast in the Azalia on Sunday morning. Definitely not worth $17.95 per person. No one came by to serve water or greet us. I had to search for a spoon. We had to track people down to get the check. If someone was there to give us service, we wouldn't have to search for spoons or water (which I never got the entire time because by the time I was done with my breakfast I didn't need water anymore), which then would also allow for them to properly figure out how to break up the checks. SERVICE FAIL #4.
5.) Service - Parking. Parking was decent in itself. The worst part of it was when my spouse was getting the car, they made him pay cash only. He had to back up and park, then go find an ATM and get cash. It cost $25.00 to SELF park over night. That's ridiculous in itself. We got home later that day and checked our account. They billed us extra on our room to include parking, something we already paid for because the guy made us pay cash, not even asking for a receipt from the front desk. The lady on the phone was unrelenting, saying that the parking guy is supposed to give us a receipt. She wanted us to show her a receipt showing we paid for the parking. This entire weekend we were never given a receipt (we never got one when we checked out - most places provide receipts... but apparently this one doesn't because the front desk people don't know how to do their job), so how would we be able to show a receipt that didn't exist? After 5 minutes of convincing her that we paid and that we never were given receipts anyways because of their failure to do their job, she decided to refund us the extra amount they OVER charged us for no reason. How do they even know we used a car in the first place? How to they charge for something that they can't prove we had. SERVICE FAIL #5.
I mean, seriously, how difficult is it for CUSTOMER SERVICE professions to actually provide customer service? Apparently it's rather difficult here. Their employees were obviously not chosen accordingly to help improve their customer service. Who ever hired the managers to hire these dumb hourly employees should be fired. I also don' t know if training would even help these employees become better or more equip to perform their jobs. If this hotel has amazing employees, they obviously don't work weekends when a majority of their clientèle are there.
This place will forever be marked in my book as the worst place to stay ever. I wouldn't even send my worst enemy to stay here and get the horrible service I did. No one deserves to be subjected to this crap for $200 night.

title: “Liked the Marriott”
text: We spent a few days here as part of our honeymoon in October of 2005. It was a nice room - comparable to other Marriotts. It's a very nice location on the water and very close to the Gaslamp District. I would say the Marriott is comparable to other Marriotts but the location is great.

title: “A Fabulous Hotel!”
text: As a frequent business and leisure traveler, I have stayed at many a hotel. This is one of the best hotel experiences that my family and I have ever had! Official check-in time was not until 3:00 but we were able to get a room before noon as we arrived early. The desk clerk took the time to give us very detailed and helpful information about the hotel and its amenities. Our room was clean, had nice bedding, furniture and a wonderful view. Twice during our 5-night stay, we received a basket full of fruit, cookies and other goodies. Because I am a Hilton Honors member, my family received a free continental breakfast and evening goodies (fruit, hors d'oeuvres, soft drinks, etc.) every day which allowed us to save a considerable amount of money. However, we did experience the hotel restaurant's breakfast and luncheon buffets and the food was quite good. The hotel is just minutes from Universal Studios and the Citywalk with a free shuttle. I was most impressed by the outstanding customer service. Every employee, from the outdoors staff who cheerfully and promptly opened the front doors to the cleaning staff treated us professionally and made sure that we received prompt service. Indeed, I felt that the 3 of us were celebrities! I wholeheartedly recommend this hotel!

title: “best location and room for the money I paid”
text: I stayed there for some days and then had to go to LA for a few days. I returned straight to Marina Inn when I came back to San Diego till my flight back home. Sea Port village, Little Italy, and Harbour Drive with cruise terminal are in 5 minutes of pleasant walk. Train terminal is also at 3 minute walk. You are staying right in the fun area. Airport just 5 minute taxi ride, worth of less than 15 dollars. Check map. Ample free parking too.

title: “Home Away From Home”
text: We enjoyed our stay at the MarQueen; the property is clean and the staff are very friendly. Management has really kept the historic character of the building alive, which we enjoy as we live in an early 1900 home. Additionally, we have enjoyed the addition of the continental breakfast. We are looking forward to our next visit to Seattle!

title: “Best hotel if you want to be in Time Square”
text: The hotel is located in the middle of Time Square. We got a discount on our room, so paying normal price would be expensive but the location would still be worth it. We got a room with two twin beds as requested. The room was very nice and the staff was friendly. The only negative thing about the hotel was the slow checkin.

title: “It could be better”
text:
When we arrived we couldn't find the entrance as they use the same entrance as the restaurant downstairs.
As we were paying in cash we were told we had to leave a deposit of $50 per night so it was $200 for us as we were staying 4 nights this was to cover any damage or anything like that... They never told us about this when we made the booking.
Location is really good as it's close to great attractions.
Cleanliness is excellent.
I thought breakfast was going to be much better.
(it was just Fruit, juice, bread and cereal)

title: “Great "Home Away From Home"”
text:
This hotel reminded me of the style of a Key West Cottage. The hotel was clean, comfortable, and the work space allowed me to spread out in my room. I also love the kitchens to cook some of the easy home dishes that I enjoy!
The staff was always willing to help with any of my needs. They even went to CVS to pick up a prescription for me when I was "under the weather" without me asking!
Great folks and a comfy hotel.

title: “Everything you could ask for and the price is right.”
text:
I stayed here with my mother March 23 to 29th to attend the World Figure Skating Championship at Staples Center. I took the advice of the tripadvisor forums to book my room at the Hollywood Orchid Suites. I had seen the pictures, so I was not surprised. The staff are very friendly and helpful and they just started providing free continental breakfast at the hotel. They had bagels, muffins, toast or waffles, bananas and apples, coffee and juice. It was very convenient. We used the tram to go to the event and got home every night after midnight. There is always a security officer standing down where the shortcut is between the mall and the hotel. We NEVER felt scared. There were always plenty of people around even at that hour of the night. Hollywood has really been cleaned up and I wish i had more time to explore. If you go here, don't forget to go to Mel's Diner right across the street from hollywood Blvd. and Highland. It's across from Hollywood High. Also, I walked down to La Brea/Melrose to stand in line for an hour at Pink's for a hotdog. I wouldn't do it again, but it was fun. The room was clean, even the kitchen, the hotel was quiet and I must say the mattress was extremely comfortable in the bed located in the living room. We had the suite with one bed in a bedroom (no door, though) and one bed in the living room. There are two TV's with HBO (2 channels).
The pillows were too big and I had forgotten to bring mine, so I bought one from Target and it worked out great. There's a target on La Brea. I would definitely stay here again. No complaints whatsoever. Also, some people said the free underground parking lot was tiny. I found it just fine for my Honda Accord.

title: “GREAT STAY AT A GREAT HOTEL”
text: My wife and I visited The Surrey while enjoying a pre-Christmas weekend in New York. From the time that our taxi pulled up in front of the hotel until the sad moment when our taxi whisked us away, The Surrey proved to be one of the top hotels we have experienced in our years of travel. The accomodations are so beautifully decorated and throughtfully designed and the quality of those accomodations is only exceeded by the quality of the staff. By the way, you must have the full traditional French breakfast basket of bakery in the morning--biting into their croissants and pain au chocolat were Proustian moments and worth very calorie.

title: “Great location, reasonable prices and have realistic expectations”
text: I have stayed here twice in the past 2 years, one time alone, once with my grandson.. Location is great -- Penn Station, subway & bus lines nearby & plethora of passing cabs makes getting around easy. Diner off the lobby is 24 hours. Restaurant in the hotel was acceptable to good. Rates are reasonable for NYC. The poor reviews given to this hotel may well be due to poorly considered expectations. Folks, this is an historic hotel and room sizes won't match bigger, newer ones but work well for two people. As for staff attitude ... I lived in the City years ago so was not expecting Mayberry. Reasonable questions asked in a respectful, polite manner were answered in kind, albeit with the classic NY lack of smiles & prolonged eye contact, which should not be taken personally. I will stay there on future trips.

title: “One of the best hotels I've stayed at during a business trip!”
text: I loved, loved this hotel! Very ecletic and so unsual. A breath of fresh air. Nice to stay someplace that offered something different than your typical "business" stay hotel. Loved hearing some of my conservative collegues' reaction to the art in the ladies bathroom, LOL! Ran into Eddie van Helen in the elevator. The VIP suite, loved it, even though I wasn't staying there! One of 2 best hotels I have stayed at during a business trip! My only complaint, was the cook...my filet mignon was rare and not medium well. tried to send it back, but was told the wait would be an additional 30 minutes. Only ate a salad and dessert that night. Billing was off too, but after a phone call was resolved. Also, the pool was closed and converted to a dance floor. Made for a very nice company pic.

title: “Sadly Disappointed”
text:
I read several reviews about this hotel and decided to give it a chance still. 
Unfortunately i was disappointed. Their staff wasnt very helpful any bit and at times seemed a little rude. 
This hotel definitely has a motel feel instead of a hotel feel. The rooms are very small as are their bathrooms. The bathroom sinks literally are the size of a large bowl. They rooms arent lighted very well either. They do have great clean up service thought. They women who clean our room each day was very detailed about everything, even organizing our little mess =)
The resturant is still closed... looked nice from what we saw...but closed lol...
The location was great thats my biggest Pro to this hotel. You are across the street from Grant Park. Short walking distance to the museums which is a plus. Apparently they have shuttles that take you there. But they failed to inform us that they are only at certain times of the day.
They dont have complimentary water!!! I was really shocked by this!!! NOt even bottled water that you can purchase in the room. They also dont have ice machines on every floor. 
They do have vending machines though....but i got robbed four buckets because they didnt dispense anything....
They do offer free wifi...but its extremely slow (like your page with take a long time to load slow thats if it loads) but you can always upgrade for a fee hahaha
I guess in this case you really get what you pay for. I probably will not stay here again unless its a last resort. 
I really recommend that they clean up a bit. Their location is amazing and im sure their hotel would really benefit from a little face lift

title: “Great stay - better staff!”
text:
Book it..
A great hotel, with tons of "philly charm". Every single staff person I came in contact with went above and beyond expectations. Thank you again, for a great stay!

title: “Laid back”
text: This hotel exudes a very laid back vibe but is probably not for everyone. It caters to touring bands and the center courtyard seems permanently tinged with a slight odor of marijuana. The rooms are on 2 levels with a motel layout. Rooms come with orange floral bedspreads and have a faded quality, all the while being rather new and clean. Parking is included and they have an attached parking lot in front of the main entrance. There's an included continental breakfast that's not bad if only looking for tea and coffee. The hotel staff and clientele seemed to skew young, and/or towards types who would religiously read Kerouac or Ginsberg. I enjoyed my stay but am not sure everyone would.

title: “Customer Service Lacking at Front Dest”
text: Decent place to stay with plenty of lighting throughout the complex. Rooms are comfortable (great chair to relax in), clean, and a nice desk to work and eat from. However, the front desk person I encountered spoke very little English. I asked for extra clothes hangers (I was staying a week with lots of clothing) and she gave me towels! Then on the day I checked out, I inquired about credit for United Air Miles, and she couldn't understand what I was talking about. GEEEZZ, why can't people in service positions learn at least basic English.

title: “I'm still grossed out”
text: I really needed to stay on budget. I chose this hotel because it was very affordable and had high review ratings. It was filthy dirty, the carpet was so dirty, the walls had dried food on them. There are small curtains hanging from the ceiling above the beds and you can see the 3 inches of dust on them, as well as breathe it in too. The plumbing did not work. Staff was nice, location good. I needed a cab ride to the airport for a 6am flight. The staff offered to set it up with a personal driver who charges a flat rate. He no showed! Thankfully another cab company was able to get me to the airport at a moments notice. Was a gross and stressful stay.

title: “4* Not on your nelly”
text: This hotel is classed as a 4 * no way, it just about hits a 3*. The rooms are a joke, there is no where to put clothes other than hanging space. The decor isnt great, the window wouldn't shut and was blowing a draught... The room was just awful to be honest....No where to put toiletries in the bathroom .... We had to put our toilet bags on the floor. The only decent thing in the room was the large flat screen TV!!!

title: “Beautiful and very trendy!”
text: Love this hotel! Walking distance to the the lovely shoreline and in a great spot downtown! Spiro was such and amazing help with making me feel welcomed! The staff was so friendly and helpful, geez is the whole town like this? Very very accommodating, I will definitely stay here again!

title: “Thank You!”
text:
Our experience was great from the time we phoned in for directions and were fortunate enough to speak with Julianne, through our check-in process and beyond, when Maria expertly took care of our every need. This is an outstanding facility; and our room was beautiful. Clearly, the multi-million dollar upgrade was well spent! We were there celebrating our anniversary, and we were looking forward to a great time. We were THRILLED at our room, which overlooked the park and the lake. Room 1218. You won't go wrong. In addition, the concierge recommended and secured reservations at a great restaurant; The Gage, which was close, not too expensive and very good. All in all - this was a 10 out of 10 experience.
Oh yea - walking distance to the Blue and to the Red El lines if you're familiar...

title: “Great Location”
text: On our first trip to New Yorak , we were very pleased with the Novotel. Short walk from some of the best sights and places to visit. The room was quite large and comfortable but a little shabby, especially the carpets. Don"t bother to book breakfast at the Hotel. Although perfectly adequate there are so many good places to eat around the Hotel. The Majestic Deli and Applebees were two places the had healthy, cheap options. Staff were pleasant and helpful and we would certainly stay there again.

title: “average”
text:
average hotel. A lot of noise from the street.
small pool side.
friendly stuff. great for bussiness purpose
B

title: “A wonderful stay at Sofitel Los Angeles”
text:
Stayed at the Sofitel Los Angeles for 2 nights during March Break. The 4 of us had 2 SoFab suites (each suite is 850-sq.ft. big). The spacious room and upscale amenities made our stay so wonderful that we just didn't want to leave. I was most impressed by the newly renovated bathroom which was totally amazing with a big patterned glass window that looked out to the bedroom & you could watch TV while taking a shower, or you could turn on a switch and the glass would become frosted so it's not transparent any more. The shower stall had a hand-held shower or you could use the less powerful but nice big round ceiling shower. The 2 suites had different lay-outs & the spacious bathroom in Suite 921 had 4 shower heads so a couple can easily and comfortably take a shower at the same time.
Valet parking was great and we never had to wait for more than 5 minutes for our car. Overnight parking was $29 per day (pretty expensive but OK in Beverly Hills) but there were always at least 2 people around you and at your service. They did make us feel like Royalties. 
Opposite the hotel near the gas station on N. La Cienega Blvd. there was a DASH bus to Hollywood Blvd (Kodak Theatre, Mann's (Grauman's) Theatre) and each journey was 25 cents (10 cents for senior). When we arrived at Kodak Theatre we found out that we could park the car there for 4 hours for only $2 as long as we bought something from the Theatre shops (even a coffee would do). I didn't recall reading about the cheap parking from other travellers, otherwise we would have taken our car there so my parents didn't need to wait for the bus that ran every 15-20 minutes. 
Sign up online to eat at Todai Japanese Buffet ($5 off) in Beverly Centre opposite the hotel. It's yummy! We ate in Todai in Planet Hollywood Hotel in Las Vegas and it was great!
It's free to sign up online to become a Sofitel Privilege member, you'll get a free drink (champagne, wine, cocktail, etc.) each day during your stay from one of the bars. 
The business centre at the hotel near the check-in counter was the best as there were 3 computers for guests to use and they were all connected to a nearby printer. Internet access & printing service were all free of charge. We did our web check-in easily and printed out our boarding passes with no problems.
We bought two 2-litre bottled soda for $2 at the gas station opposite the hotel. One bottle was $1.79 & $2 for 2. So we bought 2 bottles and left the unopened one at the hotel for staff to consume should they choose to.
Buy a map with locations of famous Movie Stars' homes & it also provided you with driving directions to get close to the spectacular 50-ft. high "Hollywood" sign viewed from Deronda Dr.
This is basically the only problem we found while staying in the hotel: Please be aware of the kids' noise early in the morning as the hotel was opposite a daycare or elementary school. Kids' activities took place in the school yard early in the morning and we got waken up as early as 8 a.m. as our rooms were facing the side street.
The location of the hotel was great as it`s close to L.A. airport (20 minutes`drive even in morning rush hour) and it`s close to Hollywood, Santa Monica, Griffith Observatory (where you can see L.A. from the hilltop) and they were all within 30-minute drive from the hotel.

title: “Ideal location, top notch service”
