text: Spent 4 nights @the Westin Copley Place for the 2012 Boston Marathon, and could not have been more impressed. Traveling to run, I had my family (1 king room adjoining 1 double room), my 81 year-old dad (king nearby) & friends (king room one floor up) in tow, all with different room requirements and arrival dates. Reservations (thanks Kelly & Sarah @the front desk) handled all details correctly & w/aplomb. We were particularly amazed by the attention to detail in all facets of the hotel, especially considering the chaos the marathon added to the equation. Still, the service was impeccable. Food -- especially breakfast in the Huntington -- was perfect for my little ones, and the Starbucks practically inside the hotel lobby was perfect for the big kids. Having the adjacent mall w/shops & restaurants is an added bonus. Just steps to the finish line, this property is a no-brainer for the 2013 Boston Marathon. The opportunity to stay here again next year is one of the only reasons I'm happy I deferred :)

title: “good”
text: Stayed here two nights and everything was excellent except the shuttle service which was lacking due to one of the shuttles being broken. In a great location 10mins away from Union Station and the National Mall. Small pool and hot tub.

title: “We will definitely come back again”
text: We stayed three nights here while doing sightseeing in New York. The location was perfect and the staff was friendly and helpful. The shared bathroom was never a problem. The only problem we had was the noise at night from the street. But this is more of a problem of New York City rather than any hotel.

title: “Impressive views, Fantastic location walking distance to Universal Studios”
text:
Beautiful room with stunning views from windows spanning the length of the room. 
Excellent close vacinity to Universal Studios, fantastic to save money on the travel costs getting there. City Walk two minutes away next to Universal with an array of restaurants and shops.
The most comfortable bed I have ever stayed in, was like sleeping on clouds.
No refridgerator or microwave etc, has a mini bar if you can afford it, lovely experience.
Only draw back is the dismal elevators, I'm convinced my hair grew 3mm each time we endevoured the long long wait for the elevator, it may have been quicker, if I was superfit to run up to the 38th floor have a ten minute rest and await my husbands arrival in the elevator..... I jest and exagerate on the length of time but it felt very timely and then to jostle with the growing que ha ha. I suppose on a relaxing holiday time is not of the essence.. he he.. Fantastic hotel.. Lovely.

title: “Close to Everything + Beautiful Views”
text: My wife and I stayed three nights at this Sheraton and were impressed with how close it was to all that summer in Chicago has to offer. A wonderful view of Lake Michigan and the Chicago River, 15 minute walk to Navy Pier and short walk to the shopping on Michigan Ave. From Navy Pier a water taxi took us to the Museum Campus in about 20 minutes for a nominal cost. The room was very clean and comfortable. Olga at the front desk was very helpul when we checked in and Alex in the LB restaurant started our days with his very friendly and efficient service. A very nice place to stay.

title: “Good Value For The Area”
text:
Small room, 2 beds. But for $200 per night instead of $400, it was a good deal relatively speaking. The neighborhood is not great; it's on a side street where there was some litter, but not that bad. Location was very convenient to all locations in Manhattan. 
Maid service was ok, it was clean, but had trouble getting enough towels.
Got a good sleep, room was small but functional and bed was a bit soft but still ok.
Overall, if you are trying to conserve cash, this is a very reasonable choice. You can spend a lot less and get a lot less, or spend a lot more and get a bit more, or spend a whole lot more to get a lot more. That's New York City.

title: “Excellent Service and Value with some valuable extras”
text: Hotel Clerk (Bob) gave welcoming treatment and was helpful in referring me to a good restaurant in the area. Capable, personable service. Breakfast is available, but very light. The trade off is you save dollars while getting a clean and comfortable place to stay.

title: “Great Hotel With Great Service”
text: I have just returned from a stay at the Sheraton New York. I have read many reviews prior to booking this hotel. I can honestly say that I don't know why people complain about this place. The concierge was awesome. Regardless of who was there working it, they made reservations and provided advice in a timely fashion. Whenever I needed more shampoo or body wash, the hotel was quick to respond and always provided more. The rooms were clean and renovated. They look great! The hotel is just a short walk to Times Square and to Central Park. There are plenty of cabs waiting nearby. The lobby is nice and NOT overly packed as others have suggested. Honestly, this hotel should be rated in the top 100 and not deserving of the rating it currently has.

title: “Made a mistake”
text: Last time I stayed in this Hotel, it was a pleasant experience. Front desk was friendly and helpful, the room was nice. BUT that was in 2009. This time the experience has not been so great. On June 26, while taking a shower, the water stopped running. Called the operator and to my shock I was informed that water will resume in about 20 minutes. With Shampoo on your head, it is unheard that in any hotel in New York, water wilol stop running. On june 27th the air conditioning did not seem to function. Called the operator and to my utter shock I was informed that the air conditioning system would start functioning not before Tuesday i.e on Ju8ne 28th. A guest expects that atleast there would be a notice or an apology but probably iy appears that Midtown Holiday Inn takes its guests for granted. I was also made to feel as if booking the hotel through a site other than Holiday Inn was not welcomed.

title: “Well placed hotel”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights prior to a QM2 crossing. We enjoyed our stay, though we only used the room, not the bar or restaurant, but these seemed popular. Our room was clean and well presented, with two flat screen TV's! 
The staff were helpful, though the car booked by the hotel did not appear and a taxi was hastily summoned.
My only, minor, criticism is 
we only saw two small lifts servicing 16 floors and quite often had to wait several minutes during peak times.
The hotel is well located in a pleasant area of town with several good restaurants nearby, 
particularly on Broadway. 
Access downtown is simple. If you're of reasonable fitness it's a pleasant stroll through Columbus and Times Square. There is a subway station close by outside the Natural History Museum, with 
access directly onto 81st Street.

title: “Small, but nice”
text:
We stayed at the Hudson Hotel July 2-July 4. We had a great time. The rooms are small, so do be prepared for that, but they're also very clean and nice. The location is very good being just off Columbus Circle where the Time Warner center is (along with a subway stop) and also only a block from Central Park. Time Square is walkable, but the subway is easier (we did both on several occasions).
Everyone at the hotel was very kind to us. My only problem with the hotel is that the rooms are very small for the price you pay. We got a low price off Priceline.com, but it was still expensive given that it was a holiday weekend. Truth is, though, that most of the other hotels with this good of a location and in this price range probably have similarly sized rooms in NYC. I would certainly stay there again.

title: “Even the corridors are cool!”
text: Loved this place. After much research on hotels around the world The Clift kept coming up as the place to check out in San Francisco so I did and it was well worth the money. Stayed for three nights, the room was a great size, very cool and relaxing. The location is great and the staff very helpful. And I loved the thoughtful design of the corridor space! I will definitely return.

title: “Absolutely horrible”
text:
I Would never stay here again. My husband and I have traveled to New York for the past 5 years, and I have never stayed in hotel as bad as this. The front desk staff was rude, the rooms were the size of "matchboxes", the shower floor was full of mildew, and finding someone to help you with luggage was impossible. I was told before arrival that they offer double beds in the room, in which they don't!!!!
I complained about this, and I was told I could leave and check out, after I had already been billed. Please think before you book this hotel, that by the way, charges $350.00 per night or more.

title: “very friendly staff/nice place”
text:
i was skeptical at the beginning because of the construction going on in the front. the friendly staff, from front staff to wait staff, have been a plus. 
free breakfast and close proximity to the airport.

title: “Not bad at all, actually quite pleasant!”
text:
Stayed at the Amsterdam Court Hotel for 5 nights in November. I travelled as one in a party of five people.
I have actually stayed at the Amsterdam Court hotel three years previously and thought that for the price it was a pretty good deal, so when I saw the the hotel was reasonably priced again I booked again for the whole family.
We had three people in one room, the room was a decent size with a fold up bed placed in the room (this was not a childs bed and was suitable for someone 6ft tall!), the room was clean, large with large TV. This room was at the front of the building, so the only downfall of the room was the noise.
Two people shared the other room, which was also very clean, with a nice bathroom.
Both rooms were cleaned daily.
Staff were very helpful at all times, dealing with luggage, check in took less than five minutes, booking transportation to the airport etc.
Free tea and coffee was also available.
The hotel is in an excellent location for all the general tourist attractions, Times Square, theatres, Top of the Rock, Central Park, museums ..... the hotel is ideally located to travel all across the city.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for a nice, pleasant hotel in an excellent location.

title: “Friendly hotel... great location...best cookies”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights and found it all to be a thoroughly enjoyable experience. The staff were efficient , friendly and attentive - and, having e-mailed the Manager, Wes, before arriving, he gave some great advice about what to do in our limited time in the city.
Location is fantastic - just by Union Square. Best of all - the great cookies on reception. Yum.
If you're looking for somewhere to eat nearby, the Bangkok Noodle bar, just a block down the road is an unassuming, great value place with knockout food - particularly the soups.
The Chancellor was a great place to stay in San Francisco.

title: “Great location...”
text: The hotel is a 5 minute walk along Spring Street where all the action happens in Soho. We arrived and were upgraded to a room with a view - NYC and the Hudson River! We thought we won lotto. The rooms was spacious, clean and filled with trendy furnishings. The staff are very friendly and helpful as are the polite doormen who can help out with directions, taxis and local knowledge about the area. Public transport is easy with buses and the train line a minute walk away. Whilst you have to pay for wifi in the rooms, it is free in the downstairs foyer - otherwise goto Starbuck's across the road. We ordered room service which is very reasonably priced and delivered within 25 minutes. We had a great customer experience and would stay here again.

title: “Comfortable room with a great location”
text:
We had a seven night stay at the Handlery. We had a room in the rear tower that faced the pool, which was relatively quiet for a downtown hotel, and had a small balcony if you like to enjoy a bit of fresh air. 
Getting to and from the room was a little complicated going around up some stairs to get to the lift lobby, the flip side is that the lift will take you straight down to O'Farrell St. 
The Deluxe King room was a great size, airconditioning was not great (but not an issue at this time of year, and for its price point was good value for money. 
Staff were very helpful, and especially the bellmen, who went out of their way to help us.

title: “Fantastic value, great stay.”
text: We stayed 2 nights and chose the hotel for its location. We had a rehearsal dinner in La Jolla and a wedding on Coronado. We knew that we also wanted to visit Old Town and the Gas Lamp area. The hotel was perfectly located for access to freeways and one could easily walk to Old Town. We were happy to have free parking, in a safe and well lighted parking lot. The hotel is spotlessly clean and maintained. The staff were friendly and always helpful. Breakfast is included and is a nice touch. We chose toasted whole wheat bagel and a freshly hard boiled egg, washed down with OJ and a cup of tea. There were choices of cereals and waffles as well. A nice way to start the door at no extra charge. We highly recommend this hotel for a perfect stop over.

title: “Good location, wi-fi needs work”
text: Stayed two nights 12/29-31st, great breakfast and social hour. Staff friendly and shuttle bus to airport prompt. Only complaint is the wi-fi didnt work in our room, they sent a tech up to reset the wireless router. It didnt help, but the front desk quickly removed the charge from my bill. Workout room adequate , would stay again.

title: “Great stay!”
text: We drove from NJ to Baltimore after Hurricane Sandy left us without power. After 3 days of being in the dark and no heat, and being in the same predicament as a year earlier with Hurricane Irene, we decided that 3 days was our limit. I called the hotel to see if they were affected by the storm. Happy to hear they were fully operational, we packed and left for what turned out to be a 3 nite stay. Thorughly enjoyed Baltimore and the hotel and our waterview room was perfect for our needs. A half block stroll from the harbor and all the attractions makes the location perfect. Very clean overall, with comfortable beds, and a friendly staff. Parking and internet are an additional charge, our only negative. We recommend a stay! Hopefully, next time, under better circumstances.

title: “Perfect!”
text: 8 miles from Sea World, 13 miles to Coronado Island, trolley to downtown, shopping mall across the street, and the best part is the very friendly, smiling, & courteous staff, from smooth check-in to no hassle check-out. And, for $159.00 per night that includes parking, a family movie, and breakfast for four, there's nothing more that we can ask for. We just wish they have a fridge in the room so we can put our child's milk in there. Overall, it's a superb choice for a short stay in San Diego.

title: “Great Hotel for it's Price Category”
text: This is a great hotel in the heart of NYC for it's price category. The hotel is geared toward the business traveler and definitely has the feel of such. I like the place and would stay again. The staff is great and they all try to make each guests stay special. A can't beat hotel for the price.

title: “Another great stay at the Crowne Plaza Times Square”
text:
Another great stay. The room was high up (41st floor) and it was nice and quiet. As a frequent stayer with the Holiday Inn chain, I gained access to the club lounge with complimentary breakfast / afternoon tea. 
The room seemed as if it had been recently refurbished. It was clean and in great condition. My only gripe would be a preference for a bath rather than a shower, but this is a minor thing and in no way would prevent me from staying in this hotel again. 
Location remains great. It is a terrible shame that Virgin has left Times Square. That said, the part pedestrianizing of Broadway makes it quite pleasant outside.
The other gripe is with the swimming pool. It is a great, but I do not really wish to have a mandatory bathing hat. 
Staff were friendly and helpful, and I discovered the free internet access (first ten minutes are free) and this useful. The concierge was very helpful and found me a store I'd be looking for. 
As before I'd recommend this hotel to anyone going to Manhattan for a generic holiday. It is very central with all parts reachable. You can walk down to Macy's in about ten minutes, and slightly less time to walk to 5th Avenue to the big stores. 
One final point, there is very good security in the hotel with someone checking key by the lifts (elevators to our American cousins).

title: “Best and Strategic Location in Manhattan with very friendly services.”
text:
The Service team from the Front Desk for Cleaning Room, passing for Room services and restaurants are very sharp, polite but precise and expend a lot attention for the customer. I think it is the best and friendly service I have experienced in New York.
This location bring you the Central Park so close, nice brands around for shopping, close to Theater District but without collaterals (crowded) and of course very nice restaurants at walk distance.

title: “Fabulous hotel!”
text: I really appreciated this hotel. It's small but very comfortable and located in a strategic position to visit the city. Staff is extremely nice and polite. The room was perfect and not too small. Wireless everywhere and 3 brand new mac at clients disposal. Awesome shower and very comfortable bed. I will definitely come back.

title: “Value is good, but some serious attention needed here”
text: There are two primary concerns with this hotel. First is that housekeeping is VERY poor. My room was not attended to properly and we were out of the room by 11 a.m. I have stayed at this HoJo for many years, and closers of the doors have been in disrepair all those years. The doors slam shut to the point they are dangerous . If you or a child has their hand/finger in the door, it will likely cut them off. Sleeping with the slamming doors is a problem also.

title: “Love this place”
text:
Great location in the middle of Beverly Hills, amazing beds, and really accommodating staff. 
If you can find a good rate online, you won't go wrong with the SLS... as long as you don't mind a bit of quirkiness and clubby-vibe during your hotel stay!

title: “Outstanding for Universal Studios”
text:
We stayed here for our first night in California specifically for it's location next door to universal, and it really is NEXT DOOR. From the front door you can walk to the park entrance and Universal CityWalk in 4-5 minutes.
The room was massive, clean, very comfortable and a had a great view of North LA. The front desk staff where great and very helpful. The morning buffet was excellent with an extremely varied assortment of European, Asian and American items.
Parking was about $14 for the night.

title: “a Delightful Place To Stay!”
text: As I was planning a weekend getaway for myself and my adult daughter, I considered two or three locations in San Francisco, and in retrospect, we are both very glad that I decided on the Harbor Court in the Embarcadero neighborhood. In general, it's a great location, close to all sorts of public transport options for exploring the city, but in particular, the features offered by this hotel chain and the welcoming staff that delivers that corporate philosophy have everything right. Smiling faces on check in, very well appointed and quiet rooms, an amazingly comfortable bed, fun tiger print bath robes and snuggle socks for getting comfy for an in-room movie...and yes, there's the happy hour with wine and beer, but for the warmer summer weather, they've added a refreshing white wine sangria with fresh strawberries that truly hit the spot! (And if you find yourself in the lobby at a different time, there is still an iced coffee bar with assorted syrups to slake your thirst, along with the ice water...). I like the list in the bathroom, indicating the supplies they have available if something was forgotten, I like the addition in the room of the right-sized plastic bag required by the airport TSA that can be used for those small liquid cosmetics, I like the assortment of newspapers that is complimentary, I like the way the staff makes a point of chatting with the guests as they gather for the happy hour (which sometimes includes great live music). I even like the music in the elevator, which also plays softly in the lobby and was specially selected for the summer season, according to one of the staff. There is creativity, attention to detail, and pleasant and professional service at this Kimpton Hotel which should assure you of a very comfortable and pleasant experience. Gotta quit for now, so I can come up with a good excuse for my next trip back...

title: “Gorgeous!”
text:
What a beautiful well run hotel. Having stayed in numerous luxury hotels in New York and around the world, the Bowery Hotel really does stand out. The design of the place is amazing, both dark and cosy, but at the same time terribly cosmopolitan and luxurious. From the beautiful doormen, to the barmen, every member of staff was a delight. The room, although not terribly big was perfect in everyway – great bed, great view from the large window and a brilliant shower in the bathroom.
I would thoroughly recommend this hotel.

title: “Best Value in the City”
text: Amazingly clean; excellent staff; large room; new bathroom; not any wear and tear evident; silent. This hotel had it all and, on top of all that, the price cannot be beat. It's out of the way for what we usually do in NYC, but considering the short amount of time that anyone really spends in the room, the extra time spent in a cab or on foot is more than made up for by the exceptionally reasonable price. Truly, I will first look for an Affinia in every city that I visit from now on. It was that good. Last time, we stayed at the Loew's Regency and it was a dump compared to this hotel.

title: “Hotel Pennsilvania is perfectly located, but it's just to sleep don't expect any more.”
text:
The hotel is perfectly located, with all public transportation near by as well as some major attractions.
Forget all the rest of the hotel though. Come to sleep and nothing more. Hotel personell is not friendly and not service oriented. The superior room is not as superior as it indicates, with a window that does not close, a television set that didn't work and no further comfort what so ever.
To me the Pennsilvania hotel was more a factory then a hotel. Crowded and personel biting instructions rather then trying to satisfy and help, with one exception though. The cleaning ladies were friendly and helpful, and the room was kept reasonably clean.
Just use it to sleep and shower and than the price of this midtown NYC hotel fits.
So,despite all this, I still would recommend it.

title: “Beautiful hotel but again operational issues are problematic”
text: The room (625) looked beautiful when I entered, so did the lobby, Starbucks and the gift shop. I set my bag on the round coffee table and obviously someone spilled coffee, how they got it up under the glass I will never know, but putting my bag caused the fluid to come out in little bursts, I took a towel moved the glass and cleaned it up, willing to over look the incident. I go to connect to the internet and there instructions are very unclear, I was told I would not be charged but it asked me to approve being charged anyways I called to inquire and the front desk person said she would take it off. She Did it never appeared. Later in the evening I made 3 toll free calls which they charged me $6.00 for there was no phone card in the room indicating that so I called the front desk and they had indeed overcharged me by $4.00. It was supposed to be $2.00 for the first 60 minutes. Even though there was nothing to indicate that. So I get up to take a shower turn the water on and jump in because I saw a bottle I assume was shampoo, wrong there was a bar of face soap, no body soap and a little bottle of conditioner no shampoo. I was already soaked and had to make do. Honestly I expect a lot better from the Sheraton. So I called down to hotel services and the perfectly nice lady, said she could give me 1200 points on the Starwood program equivalent to $8.00 . At this point I said whatever and hung up. The problem is the staff was nice, the property was nice but these small issues are what make a difference between a superior class hotel and a average/poor hotel. I have had a bad streak with hotels lately because in this economy you expect what you pay for, I have stayed at a Day's Inn and were more satisfied then at the Sheraton and to me that seems very strange especially considering the huge price difference. To sum it all up, if you stay here double and triple check to make sure you ave all your essentials dont assume anything. My mark of poor maybe a little overstated, but it is not above average. I did take pictures of the coffee stained towels (I dont drink coffee and the face soap and conditioner in the shower after the fact). Not really a satisfying experience for me sorry.

title: “Excellent hotel, ideal location”
text: We spent four nights at Hotel Triton and will remember it for a long time. Excellent staff, great design and feel of the place. Wine hour (complimentary) in the evening with other guests is just one of the features that puts you, the guest first and makes you feel you belong. No corporate feel. Genuine, friendly, incredibly helpful, knowledgeable. They're interested in making your visit memorable. Excellent location for everything too. Can't recommend it highly enough.

title: “A FANTASTIC weekend getaway!”
text: We went to Fort Rapids to celebrate my stepson's 5th birthday. We had 2 rooms booked that adjoined. Immediately upon getting settled into our room, the front desk called & asked if they could upgrade our two rooms to a 2 bedroom villa.....heck yeah! the villa had a king-sized bed in a loft with a bathroom/shower upstairs & 2 double beds, a pull out couch, bathroom, & kitchenette downstairs. The dryer in the room was a GREAT idea & we used it several times to dry our swimming clothes. Our room was spacious & clean. The coffee table wasn't in the greatest of shape but really, who cares about that?! The waterpark was perfect and entertained ALL of us: mom, dad, kids ages 4 & 5 & grandparents! We all had a really nice time there. The restaurant was very, very tasty & in my opinion, reasonably priced for a hotel restaurant. We ate there for dinner & breakfast. The breakfast buffet was wonderful and a real value @ $9.95 a person (kids were not charged). The made-to-order omlette station was a nice touch and very yummy! The staff were all very nice & accommodating and I thought the lifeguards were extremely attentive, especially in the kiddie area. LOTS of lifeguards everywhere! Safety First! I would highly recommend this hotel to families for an affordable weekend getaway. Our kids loved it & can't stop talking about how much fun they had.

title: “Comfortable "Fancy" Hotel”
text: I stayed here with my two elementary school aged children during a quick fall break getaway. The location was perfect for that downtown big city feel. Upon arrival we were greeted by helpful and pleasant front desk staff who gladly stowed our bags until our room was ready. We were told it would be couple of hours before we could check in, but only moments later we were offered a suite that was available. A better description would be spacious one bedroom apartment! The high ceilings and exposed brick & beams create a feeling of room to roam in these suites. We were only staying one night but the size of the room, full sized refrigerator, electric coil cook top, pots & pans and dishes would make for a comfortable and convenient longer stay. The decor was current but subdued and the room was very clean. The sectional couch in the living room area was comfortable as were the two queen sized beds down the hall in the bedroom. There was a great deal of noisy sidewalk construction directly in front of the hotel, but in our 3rd floor suite we didn't hear a thing. The construction is currently a bit of an inconvenience all around downtown Indianapolis but it appears that once completed it will compliment and improve the downtown area. This hotel offers a full meal in the evening with complimentary beer and wine and breakfast is more than mere continental muffins & fruit- it is a full fledge eggs, sausage, biscuits, waffle, etc. situation. The staff at both the evening reception (which was, as mentioned, really a full meal offering) and at breakfast were above average friendly and helpful.

title: “Great Stay...”
text: My only regret about this hotel is that I didn't get to stay longer. I was there for one night. I was upgraded to a suite and the room was beautiful. Large, especially for a city-hotel. I also had access to a beautiful private deck. The room was clean, the staff was friendly, and the location was great. The only downsides were that the water pressure in the shower was very low, and the restaurant opens late, 7:30 a.m. As an east coast traveler, I was awake at 4:00 a.m and hungry. The only option was to go out at that time to get some food as they don't have vending machines in the hotel. So, if you're going to want to eat something before 7:30 just bring some food with you to your room!

title: “the worst hotel in the world!”
text:
This hotel is the most disappointing hotel I have ever stayed in.
I arrived at the hotel after a long journey to discover this hotel was located on the side of the interstate. The hotel front desk told me that nothing was within walking distance - despite the advert on the website implying most attractions were.
When asked how guests without a car manage I was assured the public transport system was easy to use. I was given an information sheet on the attractions and how to get there by bus etc...
To get to the bus stop I had to cross a dangerous interstate. I was told the buses were every 15 mins and I needed to change twice to get to downtown san Diego (where I was recommended to visit). This was incorrect. In the daytime the buses were every 30 mins and I actually did not need to change at all. To make matters worse in the evening the buses were less infrequent - every hour- and none actually went near the hotel. I then spent an hour on the bus to be dropped no where near the hotel. I was nearly attacked and had to call the police for assistance. I then had to call 15 cab companies before one would come to my location to collect me. I am a stranger to San Diego and am a 26 year old single female. I had never been so scared in my entire life.
Upon arriving to the hotel -after also requesting a quiet room, I heard the neighbor a few doors down having a party with 10 people in the room. I complained to the front desk as it was now 1230am and they said they couldn’t hear anything and wouldn’t investigate. I complained the next day to the general manager. All she offered me was 10% discount on my stay. My whole vacation has been ruined. I have been left witha horrid image of San Diego and actually cut my trip short by a day and checked out early.

title: “Awsome Place To Stay”
text: We just sayed at this hotel in mid-March 08 and it was great!! They helped us with (but didnt guarantee) an early check in and the valet ($25 per day) had the car waiting when we got down to the lobby in 2 or 3 minutes at worst. They also helped us in calling a cab right from the front desk and there are a few resturants within the hotel as well. You could walk to the Inner Harbor in 10 minutes or its a 5 minute car ride. They also have a shuttle that will take you to and from the Inner Harbor. This is the place for people looking for location to everything. Its probably a 20-25 minute walk to the Orioles and Ravens stadiums as well. I check Trip Advisor evry time I'm looking for a hotel to see what people are saying and it seemed good as far as reviews and the hotel exceeded our expectattions. Definately a winner.

title: “Odd set up but OK for what we wanted”
text: We stayed here for 6 nights while we holidayed in San Francisco. It's an odd set up - there are 3 Holiday Inns within a few blocks of each other, oben of them being a Holiday Inn Express. We checked into the main reception on Columbus Avenue no problem, but our room was in the "Beach building" in the next street and next to the Holiday Inn Express. The reception there is only open during the day, and it's not as secure as I would have liked -one of the reception entrances is through the undercover car park and anyone can come inand out. The lift is not supposed tobe able to be activated unless you put your room key in the slot, but this feature was broken so anyone could access the lift and wander in and around the hotel. The room was functional, the bedding clean and the bathroom the same. To be honest, it was ideal for what we wanted, but anyone choosing to stay in their room during the day would be better off either asking ot be housed in themain hotel or going to a differen thotel completely. Location wise, it's ideal - near the tourist area, not far from the cable car turnarounds, and ideal for Pier 39 and some nice restaurants. The "tourist information guide" only works 8am to 1pm so if you need help, make sure it's within these times. The onsite catering at this part of the hotel is "Dennys" which takes up space in reception. Not ideal for us Brits, but I'm sure others love it

title: “Awesome hotel”
text: I previously stayed at the Eastgate towers in December of 2006 and had a follow up trip in October of 2007 and the hotel was just as great! This time we had three people going and had the Junior bedroom suite which came with one queen bed, a pull out sofa bed (which was VERY roomy and VERY comfortable!) and what a very spacious room is general! You definitley get great quality at the hotel. The staff are very helpful and the bags can be put on hold before checking in and after checking out so you can get the most out of the city. This is a perfect location because it is outside of all the hustle and bustle and is quiet and nice. Everything is in a reasonable amount of walking distance, Grand Central is particularly close. There are some good restaurants and eating locations just around the block, so no need to fear with the hotel restaurant under renovations. Anyway, highly recommended! AWESOME hotel, next time I go to NYC I will be staying yet again at Eastgate Towers.

title: “Much Better than Expected”
text: This Fairfield Inn was really pretty nice. The rooms were larger than older Fairfield Inns (this property is two years old). The bathrooms are nicely tiled. Everything worked in the room. Internet was wireless or hard-wired, your choice. A modest work-area desk is in the room. Beds were comfy. Rooms are equipped with a small fridge and microwave. The breakfast is complimentary, and slightly better than average for a free hotel breakfast. A movie theater is next door. Several chain restaurants are in the are, including a Cracker Barrel, Chili's, and a Fuddruckers. The hotel is adjacent to Interstate 10, but on a hill overlooking, cutting down on road noise. The property is 15-20 minutes west from the airport. Reception staff was friendly and efficient. If you do not need to be near the airport this is a solid choice.

title: “An excellent hotel close to Union Square”
text:
We ( coming from Switzerland) had been mooving our son from Tennessee to San Francisco,and we had been staying for a month in the Donatello. We had been absolutely satisfied. First of all a very warm reception has been given to us. The room had been spacious and very nice, and it had always been spotlessly clean.
The hotel has also a nice bar an a very good restaurant. We enjoyed our stay so much and we absolutely recommend this hotel.

title: “Don't stay here if you want to walk to Old City area”
text: This Embassy Suites is too far away from the Old City area of Philly to be convenient. We walked down some rough and seedy streets to get to where we tourists wanted to be. I NEVER would have felt safe if we would have had to walk back after dark. For that reason alone, I would not recommend this hotel. On the good side, although old and somewhat tired looking, this hotel is clean and comes with the made to order breakfast and manager's reception that Embassy Suites are know for. The service here was excellent! Everyone from the desk staff to the bartenders were so nice, friendly and helpful.

title: “Can't get much better than this”
text: I just got back from a three day stay at the Affinia Dumont and the experience was amazing. We were three professional women travelling for a bit of fun and culture. We were not able to check in early, but were upgraded to the fitness suite which was FANTASTIC. The in room sauna was an expecially nice feature. I rarely been in a Manhatten hotel room that had as much floor space as any of the three rooms we had to choose from, all with a spectacular view of the Chrysler Building. The staff was knowledgeable, courteous and extremely helpful. The place was spotless, well appointed and overall a delight. I would recommend the hotel to anyone who wants a little extra space. The location is fabulous too - very close to the Queens Midtown tunnel, so if you are flying to LaGuradia the trip isn't painful at all. Centrally located, easy to catch cabs or transit ... You can't say enough about it

title: “Pleasant, clean and quiet”
text: We requested and received a renovated room and were pleased with our overall stay. The hotel was obiously under renovation which makes it difficult to rate more than our room. We were visiting Columbus for pleasure - not business - and the best part of the hotel was its proximity to German Village. The hotel was not much more than a room, but it was quiet and clean.

title: “Nice place, nice value”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights recently and found it to be a very nice place to stay and we felt the price was great for what we got. My husband, daughter and I were in San Diego to take in the Zoo, Sea World and to do some general sightseeing. We had a Studio Suite which was big enough for the 3 of us, our daughter slept on the sofa bed and while we did not have the privacy a one-bedroom would offer it was fine for such a short visit. The staff was very kind and helpful, the free morning breakfast was good, rooms were clean, as were the grounds and rest of the facility although the pool could have been warmer. Even though it is in Del Mar we found the drive to all the attractions to be fairly quick and enjoyable. We would stay here again no doubt!

title: “very nice facility”
text:
I allowed him to book the hotel for a romantic weekend and even though I had checked here before going (and knew what I was getting), I was still was very pleasantly surprised (at the fact that he selected such a great hotel (THAT close to shopping - my weakness). The decor is modern and vibrant and the lobby is inviting. Depending on the time of day that you arrive, you may find hot freshly baked cookies (of which I MAY have had too many), chocolate covered strawberries, a variety of fruit and the best lemon/mint/cucumber infused water ever! Everyone from the doorman to the hospitality staff greeted us warmly. We even sat outside in the umbrella covered patio and relaxed before taking in a movie on Saturday afternoon.
We were on the 6th floor so not a lot of foot traffic and we didn't hear a lot of noise from the other rooms. Hotel bathrooms and beds are deal breakers for me and I am happy to say that the Renaissance passed my inspection on both :) 
So, if you're going to Charlotte and you want to be comfortable, stay close to fantastic shopping and restaurants, this is the place for you.
Definitely will be staying here again!

title: “Great little hotel”
text:
We booked this with a great rate from book it .com.
Hotel is nicely presented and even though we arrived late we received a warm welcome although had to handle our own luggage to room minor gripe but these things do make a difference.
Room was very clean and well laid out with an en suite bathroom with plenty of towelles and quality toiletries.
To sum up KP Hotel is like being wrapped in a warm blanket by an old freind and makes you feel warm, valued and welcome.
It does not pretend to be five star and it is not but it is a dam good three star and I would return in a heart beat.
Thank you Bob for your advice about local places to eat and how to get where !

title: “Great value for midtown”
text: I've stayed at The London a few times and absolutely love it. In Manhattan generally the hotels are either crazy expensive or really claustrophobic. The London is neither. The rooms are all very spacious and luxurious and configured for business travelers that need to get work done, and for the same price as the shoe boxes down the street. The gym and restaurant are both great. And, if you're traveling on an expense account that only reimburses for the most basic room type, you can game it a little by staying here because all the rooms are suites. Highly recommended!

title: “Awesome Place”
text: I have to say this was the best place to stay. Granted it has been a while since I have been there but I am looking forward to returning on my 1 year anniversary next May. (I hope construction will be completed) I was treated so well by the staff I thought they had mistaken me for someone important. LOL. They had ample space to launch my boat and store my boat trailer. The beds were comfortable and the food was great. You will not find a better place to stay in Austin if you are looking for a boating weekend.

title: “Excellent Value - Would Recommend and Will Stay Again”
text: Stayed at the Eastgate Tower for 3 nights, and found it to be an incredible value, in a great location, and within walking distance of major attractions and transportation. I found the staff to be courteous and helpful in all respects. I stayed in a junior suite, and a friend stayed in a studio apartment in the hotel as well. Both of the rooms were very clean, with a kitchen and ample room. If you are looking for luxury and a modern feel, this is probably not the place for you: the rooms and furniture are a bit dated (although very clean and comfortable). I found the hotel to be outstanding, and will not stay anywhere else in NY...and I used to live in the city a few years ago. Best value for the money, hands down.

title: “Excellent service, really enjoyed the club lounge”
text:
We apparently had some bad luck on this trip because upon check-in, we found out somehow RC lost one of our reservations (we had 2 rooms reserved and even talked to this RC's house manager 2 weeks ago who assured us we can get 2 connecting rooms for our stay). So check-in took a very long time and at the time it was mid-afternoon and we've been driving for a couple of hours from the cape and everyone was tired. Needless to say, we were frustrated when we found out one of our 2 reservations were lost. 
Ashley at front desk was very apologetic and offered us free dinner and complementary club lounge access for the duration of our stay to make up for the mis-hap. She went ahead and gave us access to the lounge so we could go there and rest while she continues to work on getting our 2 rooms ready. At the end they were able to give us 2 rooms next to each other but not connecting.
The club lounge was excellent. The lounge concierges were all great and very helpful and recommended local restaurants to us. It was in the 90s on Friday so after going out for a couple of hours in the morning in the heat we decided to cancel our afternoon plans and just hang out in the club lounge for the rest of the day. Breakfast at the club lounge was excellent. Homemade granola was really great, even I liked it and I normally do not eat granolas. The smoked salmon was capers and cream was good too and pastries are always excellent in RC. The dessert was great too, loved chocolate covered strawberries.
The location of this RC was very good. Normally we do not stay in RCs located in center of city but did this time. The 3 restaurants we had planned to go were all within a couple of blocks from the hotel and there was a movie theater right around the corner. The park was also just a short walk away although it was so hot we didn't spend as much time in the park as I'd hoped.
Overall the services were excellent. The complementary services they offered us definiteily made up for the mix-up with the reservation. Would definitely stay at this location again if we visit Boston in the future.

title: “My stay at Capitol Skyline...”
text: We came up on New Years Eve to Party and chose this hotel...I haven't stayed there in a while in it was upgraded and they really did a good jod there...The front desk was good and the beds were comfortable.....The only thing I was surprised over was that the parking use to be free and now they charge $30.00 and a bottle of water in my room was $4.00...What in the world...I would stay there again...It's close to the club....

title: “Recommended”
text:
It's a perfect hotel for couple. My boyfriend and I love it so much. We love the decoration in the room too. The location was really good, about 10 minutes walk from the Union Square and the cable car station.
The staff was quiet friendly.

title: “Central Location, Great Service, Average accomodation”
text: The Villa Florence is located close to the centre of San Frans shopping area very convenient to the cable cars & dinning areas, making it easy to get around the city, the hotel staff were super helpful & friendly but unfortunately the room was a bit of a dissappointment, we a had a double double room, thats a room with two double beds but it was really designed for one we found the room cramped for 3 adults with a tiny bathroom and in need of an overall upgrading

title: “Pretty nice”
text: Try priceline to get a good deal. Very good service. Clean rooms.

title: “Great area, comfortable hotel, pity about the noise”
text:
We enjoyed the situation of this hotel which is near Greenwich Village and away from the main tourist drag. Our de luxe room was fine with two excellent double beds, plenty of storage space and a decent bathroom with good shower. Breakfast was not exciting but good enough with fruit salad, and a bread basket with bagels and muffins. Cereal was also provided on request. Fresh orange juice and coffee were very good.
On our first evening we dined in the hotel restaurant which was excellent and very convenient after a long flight (we booked a table on arrival - the restaurant is usually busy). There are lots of good restaurants within 10-15 minutes walk of the hotel - it's a good idea to book, especially at the weekend.
The real downside for us was the problem of noise starting with deliveries or refuse collection well before 6 am and also the very intrusive building noise which is taking place close to the hotel at the moment. This starts around 8 am and is LOUD! It was possible to reduce the noise to a small extent by keeping the window closed (but it did not appear to be double glazed - so this did not make a huge amount of difference). If the window was closed the room got warm (even in April) and the air conditioning was also extremely noisy. We are not light sleepers and can usually sleep through the sort of noise you might expect in a city , or with air conditioning, but this was really bad.
Overall we liked the hotel and there is little choice in Greenwich Village area. However I think we would only book again if we were going in a cool season when it would not be necessary to use air conditioning and we would check first to see if the building work had finished. Our room was at the side of the hotel - it is just possible that rooms at the front may be quieter.

title: “No hassle customer service - if you haven't been in a while, give them another try!”
text: My sister and I were snowed in NYC the weekend before Christmas and moved to the W when our first hotel refused to let us extend our stay on points and demanded an exorbitant rate for the "privilege". The W not only let us stay on points in prime season, the staff made our stay the one part of the trip that was hassle-free. They were friendly and every request was met with an attitude of "no problem, we'll take care of it". We didn't know from day to day when we would be able to get a flight out, and the front desk staff made sure we didn't have to worry about it - they blocked us in the same room and were extremely flexible with us, recognizing that we had no control over the airline dilemma! In past years, prior to the renovation at this hotel, I had experienced an attitude among the staff that was in no way backed up or warranted by the quality of the experience. They were riding on the coattails of the W Hotel chain's reputation. The rooms and hallways were very worn and past their prime, yet the staff often acted like we were lucky to be there since it was so "cool." The rooms are still small, but they are much nicer post-renovation, and the attitude of the staff has completely changed for the better - we were made to feel that our business was appreciated and that they were happy to help. I will definitely go back, and would encourage others who may have had mediocre experiences in the past to give them another chance - you may be pleasantly surprised.

title: “LOVED IT!”
text:
What more can you ask for ....Beautiful location/clean rooms/friendly staff!
I love this hotel (fun or business)
Can't wait to go back!

title: “Modest chain inn with courteous and thoughtful staff”
text:
This is a Ramada. A Ramada is a Ramada is a Ramada. It's on the side of two freeways.
It's clean. 
But what sets this place apart is the realization that most chain hotels are franchised and thus individually owned. That can set a place apart. We made reservations and indicated we had our 11 year old Golden Retriever with us. We got there and the owning couple greeted us warmly, greatly looking forward to meet our dog. The gave us a nice corner room close to a place for her to go potty at night. Overall, you could just tell they cared about their hotel and placed energy unto their guests. Ambiance can't be more bland - but if you need a place to lay your head in the area, this is the kind of place I want to find.

title: “Average Marriott Property and Overpriced”
text: I am a Marriott Rewards member of over 10 years. I have stayed at Marriotts an average of 15 stays per year. The hotel is in a good location. Friendly staff. Average lobby. But.... Most overpriced Marriott property that I have stayed at. It is definitely not a great value. The rooms are average in size. The decor is not as modern as you would expect for a JW property. The bathroom is very small. I would not recommend this hotel to business travelers. There are much better choices at a lower price in DC. It does not help that I am here during the Cherry Blossom Festival. Paid $500 per night for something that is probably a $200 to $250 value.

title: “Loved it!”
text: Loved Hotel Elysee! Very romantic and quaint! Loved the breakfast and happy hour. The staff was very professional, helpful and friendly. Will definitely stay there next time in NYC.

title: “Retro Hollywood Motel w/ Pool near Greek Theatre”
text: My son and I were making a quick visit to LA for campus tours and after having enjoyed a luxurious 3-week family vacation in Europe, I decided I would venture to check out some lodging in the less than 3-star range. I discovered the Travelodge Hollywood. The layout is the typical 50's U-shaped, 3-story structure with outdoor hallways and pool in the middle of the parking lot. It was a great departure from what we had been staying in, but for 1 night I thought I could maybe, probably, hopefully tolerate it. What the heck, if it turned out to be really bad we would sleep in the luxe car we had reserved. When we pulled in the driveway, I felt we had gone back to my early childhood. It was the typical retro-motel-style with the big sign out in front. I loved it! The rooms, bathrooms, pool and landscaping were all neat and clean and the front desk staff was very pleasant, and accomodating (unlike other reviews I had read...maybe they hired all new help!) and attentive. The continental breakfast was only muffins and coffee as I recall, but other than that, it was a comfortable place to stay at a cost of only a tad over $100.00, taxes included. I think we would do it again!

title: “My favorite hotel in Austin”
text:
I stayed here for one night and truly believe this is one of the nicest W hotels I have seen. I love the interior and would definitely go again. 
It is in a great location! Everything you need is within walking distance. The staff is extremely friendly and helpful.

title: “Not as”
text: Good points to start with, the location isn't bad. It is only 2 blocks from a great shopping district in the Fillmore and across the street from Japantown. The service was very accommodating and friendly from beginning to end. I was even allowed early check-in on arrival and given one of their three high-room floors with two windows. Beds are comfortable and the rooms kept clean. Bad points: the price and the bathroom. The bathroom is dark and crowded and really unpleasant. Difficult sharing with two adults. The main reason we changed hotels after 4 nights when booked for 8 was the price. For about $20 more, you can stay at a much higher-end hotel with much nicer amenities elsewhere in the city. That said, it's hard to know where to book in this city as there are so many rooms with various locales, price tags, and levels of service. Tomo isn't bad, but not all that trendy. It's an old, dumpy Best Western that was given a cheap makeover with some IKEA products. That's all.

title: “Do not stay in the Tower”
text:
I researched many hotels when looking for a place to stay in Denver and the pictures and reviews seemed great on this hotel. The Starwood name and recent renovations were also a plus. 
I had a problem booking the room online and had to call which took a great deal of time. Upon arrival, there was an issue with the type of room booked and we were assured that we were going to be sent to a room on the club level with a great view. The view was great but the room was TINY. There was barely enough room for more than the bed and the bathroom was also incredibly small. In addition, the room was not cleaned when we arrived back the next day at 5pm after being out for the day. We had to call to ask someone to come to the room to clean. 
In short, I would not choose to stay in this hotel. The overall experience was not good and definitely not one that I would recommend to another person looking for a place to stay in Denver. There are other hotels in walking distance that I would choose if I were to return.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
It was a special birthday trip for our daughter, the hotel offered her a excellent birthday chocolate cake, she loved it ! Many thanks. 
We all enjoyed the hotel, very quiet, clean, nice staff. The rooms are a little "old style" but it is part of the history.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Really enjoyed our stay here. We updgraded to the Huson Suite for one night but actually preferred the city views on the other side in our deluxe king room. Stunning! The roof terrace bar is great too. We had a problem with the air con in our room which they couldn't seem to fix but apart from that no complaints. Very friendly staff and decent breakfast.

title: “Good comfy hotel with new facilities”
text:
We enjoyed our stay in this hotel (4 nights), so much so that I decided to write this review for the benefit of other travellers.
I would strongly recommend this hotel to travellers for the following reasons:
1. 5-10 mins walk from a metro, Union Station. The walk is easy even if you lug your luggage (which we did).
2. Within 10 mins walking distance to the Smithsonian Museums. White House is another 10 mins walk away.
3. Newly renovated, so the hotel feels and looks new - Large flatscreen TV, 2 queen size beds (which fit 4), a FOC pillow menu to choose your pillow from, free hot cider drink at the lobby, free wi-fi at the lobby, free printing service at the business centre, clean carpets and modern sofas etc.
4. Service was good. The guy at the reception was patiently explaining to us the route to the super market, etc. A large supermarket, Safeway, is merely 10 mins walk away.
All in all, the hotel made our stay in DC very pleasant and I will certainly go back if I visit DC again.

title: “Amazing Hotel”
text:
This hotel was amazing, it is based Lower East Side near China Town and Little Italy and easy access to everything. We had a room with Soaking Tub and Balcony, we were on the 16th floor and had views out to Manhattan and Brooklyn Bridges. 
Our room was great, with the floor to ceiling glass windows giving great views of the sky scrapers! Loads of wardrobe space and spacious room. The bathroom was great with a shower looking out to NY (the floor to ceiling glass windows continue into the bathroom) and a soaking tub which was so big I could take a swim...they provided you with candles and matches and really did think about the little touches, with fresh cookies placed in your room every night. The bed was a memory foam mattress so made for a good night's sleep after a long day taking in the city.
The conteniental breakfast was bagels, toast with a choice of cream cheese or jam and fruit, but it was a bit unorganised. Room service was great also, enjoyed the food in the hotel.
Staff were not very attentive however, we asked three times for a folder that was meant to be in our room giving us details of the hotel and room service menu etc, we never recieved it. They also charged us twice!!
Overall the hotel was great and the room was a haven from the 24hr madness that is the fabulous big apple!!

title: “Excellent location!!!!”
text:
We were intially sceptical based on travel reviews read. Upon arrival (8am), they gave us a good room w/o additonal charges. Room generally clean though heater didn't quite work (fast enuf) to warm the room in winter. The location is perfect as it is close to Times Square yet away from the hustle & bustle, it's just a 5 mins walk!
Will we go there again....definitely, but hopefully we can find a better rate (paid US799 for the first nite and approx US350 for subsequent 2 nites).
It was our first trip to NY and the hotel did enuf to make us wanna come bck to NY and this hotel.
Siti Murni, Singapore
Travel Period 8-11 Dec 2007

title: “Excellent service, charming neighborhood”
text: Great value for upper West Side. Good markets (Fairview, West Side, Zabar's) . Within walking distance to Museum of Natural History , Central and Riverside Parks . Every block within walking distance is full of interesting sites and stores. Rooms are small but comfortable. Staff at reception and in rooms always helpful. Our room looked out at a brick wall, but that provided for a very good sleep.

title: “Nice "grown up" hotel...but great for kids too!”
text:
I am often surprised by how the nicer hotels make children feel unwelcome. I know some kids are noisy and unruly, but for the most part well disciplined children shouldn't be made to feel like they don't belong.
The Omni was the exact opposite. Upon our arrival, we were greeted at the door by a friendly lady who presented little goodie bags to my two boys. Nothing fancy, but one of the toys in there kept my 6 year old son busy for much of our trip. It was a very nice touch. Also the cookies and milk left in our room the first night was very sweet.
The hotel is beautiful, nice clean rooms and has a great staff. 
I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Horrific”
text:
I left the key in my room and they would not let me back in until the "engineer" returned in the morning, which turned out to be just the key man. They put me in another room and I had none of my belongings. This new room had no air conditioning in 100 degree weather. I asked for another room. They yelled at me and put me in one with minimal A/C. The staff was horrible, the sheets, towels, etc. were dirty, and I could get maybe one channel with the "rabbit" ears they provided. Stay away. Stay far far away!!!!
Cameron

title: “Great Location, Old World Charm”
text:
The Phoenix Park Hotel in Washington DC is a charming combination of old-world charm and fantastic service in a great location. The decor may be a little over-the-top for the average traveller (especially if you're 25 like me!), but that's nothing when you're in a nice and safe hotel that is central to all the top attractions in DC. 
The service is top-notch, especially the doormen who I appreciated beyond words whilst in DC - they're the only way you are going to attract a cab in this city! The people on the front desk can be a little gruff, but they're nice enough and are quick in checking you in and out. I was also very pleased that they hold their luggage for you upon check out if you aren't leaving DC until later in the day.
The hotel is also in a fantastic location and only metres away from Union Station, which was great for this traveller who arrived via Amtrak and relied on the metro to get around most days (one word of warning though, make sure to take motion sickness tablets on the Metro. I became very ill whilst using the Metro one day due to the jerky driving). It's a very quick walk down to the Capitol building, and from there you can walk just about anywhere in DC.
The rooms, as I have said, are slightly over the top in their decor, but that hardly factors in to my opinion of this hotel. The rooms are fairly large, with beautiful plush and soft beds, flat screen TV's, mini bar and wonderful, clean bathrooms. Room service is also perfect and always on time - definitely recommend a breakfast or two from the Dubliner restaurant downstairs. The hotel is quite quiet, so there's no need to worry about noise affecting your sleep. The only time it was noisy was on a Friday or Saturday night due to the Dubliner downstairs, but the noise usually stops around midnight. The accommodation is also very well priced and was just about the best priced hotel I could find in DC (and I looked at A LOT). 
The only downside to this hotel would be the cost of parking, which is approx. $40 a day. Thankfully I did not have a car that I needed to park!
All in all, I would recommend this hotel. Well priced, good location, very nice staff (doormen in particular!) and clean, well appointed rooms. Perfect hotel for your stay in DC.

title: “A nice hotel, some drawbacks”
text:
The Crescent is a nice hotel, the staff were invariably pleasant and helpful, the hotel is in a good location, it has character and we had a hassle free visit.
It isn't without its drawbacks though, which would make me think twice about staying there again. As other reviewers have said, hotels in San Francisco are generally expensive and I'd think the Crescent overpriced in other cities. The breakfast was fine, nothing very exciting but nothing wrong with it either, but the breakfast room is a soulless and disappointing place to start the day. It can't be that difficult to improve the environment. The noise from the garbage collection is real, but not a huge issue and a bit later in the day than experienced by other reviewers. My major gripe is with the room itself. Although completely clean, for the price it was pretty small with a small bed that after 4 nights I was relieved to be leaving; and some small additions would make it a more user friendly experience - central light switch by the bed rather than only by the door, hangers for towels by the sink and is it too much to have coffee and tea making in the room?
All-in-all a fine experience but underwhelming.

title: “Hipster hotel needs things that actually work”
text: We had 2 different rooms in this hotel. I turned in a list of things that didn't work to the front desk but by far the most annoying is the air conditioning. There were 2 a/c units and 2 thermostats but both thermostats controlled only 1 A/C unit while the other just sat there. The decor is a welcome change from the normal hotel but so many annoyances can effect a trip; clocks had wrong time and were a mystery to change, bathroom supplies weren't refilled, hooks that don't hold towels, etc.

title: “A wonderful home away from home.”
text: This was an amazing find. The staff were so friendly and welcoming.The rooms were very clean and comfortable. We really enjoyed the decor, and the breakfast restaurant was superb. The location could not have been better, just able to walk along the road to Stephanies and many other local restaurants that were recommended to us.Being straight across the road from the supermarket and the 104 shops in The Prudential Centre makes this an ideal location.

title: “Large rooms, so-so decor, good service,”
text:
I stayed at this hotel while at a Publishing conference. I checked in and was lead up to my room. I went into the bathroom to freshen up and noticed the toilet had not been flushed. Gross. Then when I walked into the room to call down stairs and just make the staff aware of this (not to complain so much as to raise their awareness), I noticed many stains on the carpet and on the wall paper. While the modern amenities were all present and the room was large with an incredible view, it didn't look completely clean. 
The room service was prompt and decent but one item - a goat cheese with truffle honey (on the cheese platter) was to die for !!! Just phenomenal. The lobby gets very very busy on weekend evenings as does the London Bar which was a fun place where I met up with friends each night for drinks (I was there for 5 nights). 
Staff was helpful and kind, concierge was also good in organizing a private car, giving me directions, as well as re-confirming several dinners we had planned (Buddakan, Nobu etc.)
Getting a taxi on that street by the lobby is ridiculous. Each time I tried to get taxis (with the help of the doormen), it took at least 15 minutes and there was always a line waiting. (Not sure how they could fix that but it is good to know if you have an appointment to keep!)
Bottom line, I enjoyed my stay, but on our next trip (in September) we will return to our usual hotel, The Palace.

title: “Very basic!”
text: I was in San Diego for a working trip in May. Coming from Singapore and having just stayed 4 days at Park Hyatt, this inn was a bit of a shock. Its a scene from Hollywood movie. The whole area is very open. Anyone can walk in and out of the compound. I did not feel safe at all when I first arrived. The room is very basic, clean and a bit small. The location is very NEAR the airport and a ride on Supershuttle pick-up to Airport will only cost $ 5 before tips. If you have a car, it is easy to get to anywhere. I did not hear any sound from aeroplanes. I also did not hear a sound from the slamming of door since my room was just next to the breakfast room. Apparently my room was facing a small road. I heard other guests complaining of noise coming from traffic. Breakfast is not impressive. Imagine my surprise that I was charged insurance $2 per day for using the room safe which I did not use! Have you ever stay at an inn or motel that charges insurance for usage of room safe? Think about it! Staff were friendly which is a plus. I will only recommend this Inn if you need to stay near the airport and if you are not a solo traveller.

title: “Not Great, Not Bad - Good Stopover for a few days.”
text:
Was visiting friends in Charlotte, cheap little hotel, the staff were friendly and courteous to me, room was clean enough. Service daily (towels etc), Cable TV, Smoking Rooms - I would avoid the 'Continental Breakfast' though - Muffins and Bagels and a singular toaster, with some Coffee ;)
Overall, I was quite happy here, close to Charlotte centre (Maybe a 15 Min Drive), there's a great Mexican food place next door.

title: “Good location, overall pleasant stay”
text:
I recently spent 4 nights at this Westin and generally enjoyed my stay. We arrived to DC via Reagan airport, which was a $22-26 cab fare. The location was in a safe area, close to restaurants and some bars. The area felt safe even late at night. I cannot comment on the distance to the metro, since I did not use it, but I hear it's not far. The White House was about an 10min walk, the Washington Monument approx 12min, and the Holocaust Museum about 15-20min, all without metro. If you are reasonably healthy, you can walk to most places. There is a 24hr CVS right around the corner, which is convenient. There is also a car rental agency just a couple blocks away, but parking is a nightmare of course and hotel parking is $43/nt. We were able to park after Sat 6pm to early Monday for free on the street.
The hotel room was reasonably clean. The only thing that grossed me out was a used disposable coffee cup that was placed as if it were clean and new, and so I was caught off guard when I attempted to brew coffee in the room. The rest of the room was fine, however. Our mini fridge seemed to have conked out midway through out stay, but I didn't notify the front desk, so I cannot comment as to how they would've resolved it. The bed was incredibly comfortable. The lobby area of the hotel is nice and comfortable as well -- it is a huge atrium. 
We had dinner at the hotel restaurant. The food was excellent the main server was great. The assistant server was terrible, however. He clearly hated what he was doing. When serving fresh bread, he placed it on a plate with trash on it rather than pull a fresh plate. I had to politely request the bread be placed on clean plates, not trash. No other staff or supervision came by to see how everything was going in our party of six. 
The service was generally okay. The bellman and doorman were very helpful. Cabs are available in front of the hotel at a whim's notice. The front desk was helpful, too, but they often seemed understaffed (lines, waiting, etc.), but once you got to them, they were great. The concierge was very helpful, informative, and courteous. The concierge had printout suggestions and walking instructions to nearby restaurants and places of interest. My only problem there was that the concierge suggested using 'The Old Town Trolley' to tour DC in the off-season for a promotional rate. The 'Trolley', however, was terrible, and though not the concierge's fault, I really wish we hadn't followed the suggestion. The off-season trolley runs every 30min supposedly, but it is disorganized and crowded. You're not exactly sure where to wait for the trolley, and when it finally gets there it's filled to capacity and the driver cannot accept you on board. The narration is not great, and the service isn't either. The employees also provide inconsistent information.
Overall, it was a good stay but mostly due to location. Next time I'll probably try a different hotel, though.

title: “Perfect Location, Excellent Staff”
text:
We would definitely stay here anytime we visit San Francisco. The proximity to Chinatown, Fisherman's Wharf and Union Square made it so easy to navigate that we didn't need to rent a car. The newly opened Executive Center was terrific for breakfast and light snacks at happy hour.
We spent a lot of time there using the free ipads, watching the flat screen TVs and chatting with other guests.
The staff went out of their way to accommodate our every need. The facility exceeded our expectations in every way.

title: “I'll be back!”
text:
It was quite difficult to choose a hotel. I searched for weeks for a hotel that would suit me and my son properly during his fall break. After 5 days staying at Hotel Carlton, I was very glad I had made the right choice. This boutique hotel is very nice. Rooms have a very decent size for San Francisco standards (we even had a closet). It was a nice room with two windows, very comfy twin beds.
The people at the front desk were extremely nice and friendly. The lobby is absolutely cosy, with a fireplace and a few art books as well as books about the history of California. I will be back with my husband this year.

title: “My new hotel on trips to LA”
text: I travel in to LA every couple of months for business from Scottsdale, AZ. A friend of mine recommended Hotel Angeleno because of its great location and courteous staff. My friend was right. The staff here was outstanding, especially Chris! He was outgoing, pleasant and gave me great information. Everyone was smiling, it seemed as if they really loved their job. The hotel and room was very clean and the views from the room were amazing. I will definitely stay here again and recommend this hotel to everyone.

title: “I expected a lot better service”
text:
I was at this hotel recently for the CSI Conference. I checked in on a Saturday, dropped off my luggege and then headed down to the tradeshow area to see if my booth had been set up. Later in the evening, I returned to my room and was sitting on the edge of my bed, talking on my cell phone, running my hands along the bedspread when I hit something crusty. There were several thick white stains over the bedspread. It really grossed me out to say the least. I called the service desk to complain and to request clean bedding, and the lady who answered said they'd deal with it ASAP. Over the next hour and a half I waitied for someone to come, spoke numerous times with the service desk before someone showed up. The cleaning lady they send was very rude, and had no idea what the problem was. I showed her the stains, she gave me a dirty look, stipped the cover off the bed and left, saying she's have to fins a clean one. Likely 20 minutes later she returned and didn't speak at all to me, except when she was leaving she asked if she had to trun down my bed for me. She left without saying anything else, even when I said thanks, etc.
Over the course of my 5 night stay I made 6 phone calls which lasted less than 1 minute each (checking VM). Minimum charge for long distance calling is $13 and change. I couldn't believe it....over $80 in phone charges for 6 brief phone calls, all under 60 seconds.
A friend at the same conference woke up one morning and had no cold water. Someone else's toilet wasn't working properly. It just seemed like there were a lot of little issues. My favorite was the spitefull cleaning lady who I asked to leave while I changed my clother and brushed my hair. I must have left a bit of a mess of hair in the sink, when I came back later she had taken the time to tighly wind it around my bar of soap and put it back in the soap dish. I am not sure what kind of statement she meant to make with that, I just found it to be odd.

title: “Great Location!”
text:
The location (for the price) can't be beat. The staff was super nice and helpful, putting my husband and I on the top floor so we could be away from the street during the busy weekend. Yes, the rooms are small. However, it's been emphasized quite a bit here that this is more of a boutique hotel. My husband and I used the hotel as a crashing place, we were in the city to visit and see the sites - not hang out in the room. The bathrooms, again, are small but very, very clean. We had a wall A/C unit which was fine for our room but the temps in Philly were pretty cool for June (around 70-80 all week). Breakfast was fine for me (pastries, toast/bagels, hard boiled eggs, bananas, etc) but my husband always had to stop somewhere to as he needed something "more substantial". 
Overall, my husband and I had an excellent time and I would recommend this property to those looking for a good place in a great location for a very reasonable price.

title: “Great view of the bay”
text: Wow, this is a dream place to stay if you are travelling to Baltimore for business or pleasure. Situated in the heart of Baltimore, it has a beautiful view of the inner harbor. If you are travelling for business, they have great facilities for conferences as well as access to nearby convention centers. No need to mention that the staff are courteous and the rooms clean. Conveniently located near to some great restaurants as well as the national aquarium.

title: “Great Place To Sleep In a city That Doesn't”
text: Times Square is a very busy, congested area so creating a tranquil, calming oasis in the midst of it all is no little feat. The Westin is a perfect hotel for business. The staff is well trained and attentive, the rooms are spacious (by New York standards) and are outfitted with a large desk and high-speed internet. The gym is OK and room service is average. I often rotate among the Westin, The Marriott Marquis, The Hilton Times Square and the W Times Square. I'd give the Westin the top grade among these otherwise fine choices.

title: “Wonderful stay”
text: Stayed at the Drury Inn 1 night during a recent visit with my daughter to see UNC Charlotte- Great service and location. 5 minutes from the campus and 5 minutes from Concord Mills- great shopping and restaurants. Wonderful full breakfast and 5:30 "kickback"- 3 cocktails per peson and appetizers. Would definetely recommend!

title: “Luxory in the heart of planet Earth”
text:
My husband booked a stay here the night he proposed. 
The room was luxorious and had quite the view of Times Square. The bed was appointed in the finest quality linens and down pillows and comforters. My husband booked a romance package that included strawberries and champagne in the room upon arrival and a dinner at the rotating restaraunt. The strawberries and champage were top quality and so was the food at the restaraunt. The restaraunt staff were polite and courteous in reconciling an error on our dinner bill. The food selection and taste were impecable. 
The room and bathroom were spotless. As for the location, what can I say? You are in the most exciting location on Earth. The possibilities are endless surrounding this hotel.

title: “Nice place for families with kids”
text:
We stayed three nights at this hotel because my kids loved the museums. It was 5 minutes walking distance from the air and space museum. Room was very spacious. The facilities were worn out a bit. But spending much times at the museums was wonderful merits of this hotel. Many other sites were very close, We took taxi to White house and Lincoln memorials and so on. It is less than 10 minutes and taxi fares were very cheap too. I will stay this hotel next time. 
The restaurent was really good. We have two dinners at this restaurent. The stake was absolutely good. My kids and we all enjoyed it. Next night we tried the buffet, which was good but not as good as the stake. Please try it. You will love it.

title: “great rooms - fantastic location”
text:
Friendly, helpful and professional concierge and lots of them - but only one receptionist meant a queue to check in and a queue to check out, not what I expect of this class of hotel. The room was very large and stylish, room cleaning was excellent. Location is fantastic on 54th St. which is a quiet street next to Broadway which also has a handy Irish pub and a great cafe/diner for breakfast.
We dined at Maze but it was a disappointment. I've experienced better menu's, better food and more knowledgeable staff in plenty of other restaurants. My ($50+ a bottle!!) of NZ wine was served too warm and then the waitress was reluctant to put an ice bucket next to our table - never worked out why though.
