In summary we'll definitely stay at The London again but won't bother with the restaurants.

title: “good location, clean, good business hotel”
text:
This is not a luxury hotel but it meets all standards for a quality business stay. Bed is comfortable, internet works, iron works, towels are fluffy, toiletries were very nice (lemon scented), and there is a bar downstairs and an Au Bon Pain. Also, parking is plentiful and free.
There is a little wear and tear, and the elevators are slow, but this is the Four Points-not the Four Seasons. The people are very nice here also. 
I would stay here again.

title: “Updated Best Western, not so great area.”
text:
Stayed here for one night with friends. The front desk staff were nice. Our room was nice and clean. We had a bottle opener on the wall...that's interesting. 
Only negative was parking but this is LA area we are talking about. We had to park next door at the restaurant and I was not too thrilled about parking away from the hotel.
Breakfast was nothing special, but there are plenty of places to get food across the street and the freeway is just down the road. If you want a location close to attractions without a high price tag, this would be the place to stay.

title: “Location Good - OK hotel”
text:
I stayed at Radisson firshermans wharf on a work trip last year and found it to be ok. The location is fantastic if you want to be right in the heart of Fisherman's wharf and walking distance to Pier 39, shops etc.
The actual hotel itself is a little on the old side for the price you are paying. The rooms are quite small though have a comfy bed and nice bathroom.
Overall I would say this is a good 3.5 star hotel in a great location - it is a little overpriced for what you are getting though. I suppose you are in fact paying for the location

title: “Ripped off”
text:
Nice hotel but they charged an extra 450.00 on my credit card and were not helpful when i called them about it.
Scary part they said i presented a card for the items,,,never did

title: “Sleep with the lights on”
text:
This is where USAir dumped me when I missed my connection. I should have known better. Check in was quick but I guess it was because of the long line of folks. Step into the elevator and immediately smelled marijuana. This is the kind of place that attracts bugs. I slep with the light son. 
I should have just jumped on the Courtyard Marriott shuttle van and paid for my own room.

title: “Absolutely Wonderful!”
text:
I stayed at the Hollywood Hills Hotel for 4 nights this month and I absolutely loved it. I found out about the hotel after many hours of research and ultimately chose the hotel based on the positive reviews from Tripadvisor. My main reason for choosing this hotel was to get a great view without paying an arm and a leg for a room and that is exactly what I got.
 Our room was #404 and the views were spectacular. The room was open yet cosy and the down conforter and pillows was a great treat. Really beats sleeping on those glorified curtains you get at most hotels. Even the tiny shampoo and soaps they give you were wonderful. Normally I just ignore those at other hotels but these were like ones you'd get in an expensive luxury hotel.
The balcony was my favorite part of the room. It was big and had a table and chairs and the view was GREAT. I really can't express that enough. It was so nice to come "home" to a quiet room above the city and sit on the balcony and just relax before going to bed and waking to another day in the busyness of L.A. 
I also want to say how nice the staff was and how great the service was. The ladies at the front desk were so friendly and helpful and every person I came in contact with there were the same way.
All in all I had a wonderful time at my stay here, better than expected and will most definately stay here again in the future. In fact, I wish I was still there! In all my years of traveling, I'd have to say I enjoyed staying at the Hollywood Hills Hotel more than any other place I have ever stayed at and believe me I've been to many hotels and many nice ones at that.
Thank you Hollywood Hills Hotel for making my vacation a stress free and wonderful one!

title: “The Experience was delightful!!!”
text: Everyone at the inn was just wonderful...we really used the free shuttle service to the fullest...We stayed an extra night and now are looking to come back to do more things in Detroit as we have found a new home away from home...The rooms & houses were very clean , the breakfast was great & the beds are very comfortable...

title: “Weird place”
text:
Found this place on Expedia and needed an extra night in NY before we flew home. Very strange place, hardly slept at all as I was always expecting something bad to happen. We couldn't wait to leave. 
The hotel doesn't have a sign outside and I think has people living there as well. I had tried to find reviews of the hotel on here before I booked it but couldn't find any. I will never book anywhere again if I can't find a review! 
The only good thing about our stay was the nice Italian restaurant on the main street. We had a great meal there on our last night!

title: “Good Location for Sightseeing. Little Local Nightlife”
text:
As a first visit to Washington, I wanted to book a hotel of assured quality and near to everything. Read loads of reviews on this hotel and decided it was in the right location.
Firstly about the location, it's excellent for sightseeing. Close to the National Mall, all the Museums and 5 mins walk from L'Enfant Plaza Metro station. You can buy an all day ticket for $7.80 per person (after 9:30 during the week and any time weekends and public holiday). It is a very safe area as it is near all the Government buildings so security is tight, which is reassuring. There are little or no restaurants nearby, so if you want a nice place to eat it's a tube ride away, which I didn't find a problem.
The hotel itself. Standard Holiday Inn really. Nice big rooms. I made sure I was not overlooking the railway line as I was warned by previous reviews this might be a problem. Was in room 362, overlooking the courtyard, which was quiet. I am a platinum Priority Club member but could not get a room upgrade (same problem in NY too in Feb). The beds are incredibly comfy and there is the usual Holiday Inn pillow menu, which I never use as they always seem to provide the right pillow for me first time. There is a fridge in the room and we liked the huge pile of towels in the clean bathroom.
We used Supershuttle for a transfer from Washington Dulles Airport, so did not park at the hotel, but understand it to be quite pricey (a lot less than London though).
Public areas. Very clean, lots of marble and never crowded, with a small gift shop which is also slightly pricey. There is a CVS store next door which is much cheaper, but keeps to business hours so closes early and is not open Sundays.
Hotel facilities. There is a breakfast dining room called Smithonian, which provides a fair variety. I was travelling with my son and we were given some $2 off vouchers. Kids eat free is 12 or under. We ordered the breakfast buffet every day which is $15 a day. My son is 14, but they kept giving me his breakfast for $2 so didn't complain (they obviously thought he was 12). The quality of breakfast was OK, lots of coffee, Orange Juice, there's fresh fruit, cooked items, cereals etc.
Bar. There is a bar that has live music playing on Weds-Fri eves. This makes it very popular with the locals and it does pack out. The music is excellent quality though and well worth a listen. Drinks are expensive, as you expect for a hotel in this location. A standard 1/2 pt beer is about $6. The bar has an outside on-street terrace, which is nice if you find the bar too cold (due to aircon) but is near the road and train line so can be a little noisy)
There is a business centre that is free to use, which is handy for checking e-mails while away and doing your online check-in for your flight home. 
There is a rooftop pool, which is accessed by going to level 9 by lift then taking a staircase to the roof. The pool is small but clean and there are loads of loungers, which we found really nice at the end of the day, after a day walking the sights. There is a nice view of the Capitol building and the roof is a great sun-trap. There is no bar or services up there, so you need to take your own drinks etc., which you can buy from the vending machines on each floor (there is also ice on each floor). The pool is open 10am until 10pm.
Overall if you want a functional hotel, near the sights then you can't go too far wrong with this one.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
5 nights stay in early september 10, room was nice, on 12 floor the noise was not a big problem, the hotel is 2-3 block from union square on the edge of tenderloin but no problem at all.
The hotel has free wifi in all room which was fantastic.
Will stay again.

title: “Very good hotel and great location”
text: I stayed here on a 2-day business trip where I needed to be close to Times Square. I found a good rate at this hotel and stayed here for the first time. I was not disappointed. The room was a good size and clean. The location was PERFECT. It is a little odd that you have to take the elevator to the floor that has the lobby, but other than that, the hotel was great. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Good situation but do not expect Art Deco”
text: We appreciated being right in the center of Dallas and in a quiet room. Just a few details disappointed us : none of the 1930 decoration is left, apart from... the area around the lifts; and the breakfast area is small and awkward, breakfast itself could be better.

title: “Great location, a bit noisy but good value for money!”
text: We stayed at this hotel in November 2011. The location of the hotel is on Lombard street , one of the busiest streets in SF but it is close to the bus station and many other attractions including Golden Gate Bridge. You can walk around the area, it's a safe area. Being on a busy street you can hear the noise from the cars during the night also, so if you want a really quiet hotel this is not the place for you. For us it was ok, we got used to it and we only spent 2 nights there. The staff of the hotel is great, they waited for us when we arrived even though it was 11.30 pm in the night. They were helpful in giving tips about what we can see during our stay. The room was clean and spacious, we had everything we needed, nothing to complain. There is free parking with a large parking lot so there is space for everyone.

title: “Wish I could have stayed longer”
text:
On the outside, this place doesn't look like anything to write home about but the suite we stayed in was very comfortable and great value for money. Actually, the room itself was tiny, with barely any room to move about but the living area was very spacious. We had a view of the pool and the ocean.
The hotel staff was very helpful in providing us with a guide of what to do in San Diego. The complimentary breakfast was great and parking was free (open lot).
Locating this place wasn't easy or may be it was just my GPS' issues.
Location: You need a car/taxi to get into downtown San Diego where the night life rocks but if you are looking for just calm relaxation, this is the place.
I am a light sleeper and I didn't get bothered by the plane noise that some people mentioned.

title: “Nice efforts by staff member!”
text: I stayed at this hotel over the weekend and was reminded again why I continue to be loyal to the Marriott hotels. The entire staff attended to my needs but one in particular stood out to accommodate my requests, Saeid Dantism. He was pleasant, patient and resourceful...I needed to book another night stay in the same room last minute using my Marriott points and Saeid assisted me in accomplishing this with a willingness to serve me! I appreciate his attention to my needs and it helped my family to enjoy our trip even more. The rooms were clean, parking was secure and the location was great walking distance to many areas of interest. I would recommend this particular Marriott to anyone looking to stay in Charlotte.

title: “A true GEM - Managed by truly amazing Staff”
text:
This is a perfect spot for visiting downtown Seattle - I chose it because of its price - the parking is a block away and secure ($20 over $40 at other hotels) so that was another major consideration. I was working so I had a car full of books and papers. Internet is free and it is wireless.
The room was perfect - the towels fresh and new and they have the best coffee machines ( Keurig) in the room - the staff gave me fresh milk so I was happy at 5 am to have this perk - I hate powdered creamer.There is a great free breakfast and when the lady at the front desk heard I was leaving at 4 am she packed a bag for me to take along - on the outside she wrote a personal note to wish me a safe journey - The STAFF ROCK!

title: “highly recommend”
text: I could not fault this hotel. Great value, location, rooms, service, staff. MY husband and I really loved staying here.

title: “This is by far my favorite hotel in NYC”
text: I am a New Yorker who lives in Virginia. I have stayed in many hotels in NYC as I visit often. I absolutely highly recommend the Giraffe Hotel. First, the location is fun - not touristy, very convenient in Union Square. It is modern, super clean, warm and inviting. They offer a free wonderful continnental breakfast in the lobby with coffee, bagels, eggs, cereal, fruit - it's amazing. From 5:00 - 7:00 or so in the evening, they offer their guests a free happy hour with champagne, wine, cheese and a piano player. It's really lovely and classy. Everyone is very helpful. It is truly a gem!

title: “Awesome!!”
text: Was very pleased with this hotel, my husband and I wanted a nice quite place to get away and get pampered and this hotel fit the bill. The staff was very accomadating, the rooms were beautiful and quite, the beds comfortable , and the location perfect. Even though the hotel was peaceful from the moment u enterd it was actually on a very busy part ofthe river

title: “Wonderful place to stay in San Fran”
text: We stayed here for six nights and had a great stay. There are so many great touches in this hotel and the staff is kind and responsive. The morning coffee and newspapers gratis in their cheery lobby was a nice touch. There were comments about the size of the rooms and they are smallish but hey you're in a city. The beds were comfortable, the rooms very clean, and nice nice touches, real bathtubs, a dimmer switch in the bathroom, free wifi, black out blinds, and every evening they have a wine reception in the lobby for their guests.

title: “Pretty shotty overall...”
text:
This was really disappointing and not up to the standards of other W's I've stayed at. Upon checking into our room (travelling with a buddy) we noticed that the top sheets on not one but both of the beds had tears on them. Worried that we'd further rip the sheets while sleeping, we called and had housekeeping change them out.
We then noticed the desk had some sort of dried gunk on it in a couple spots (leftover dried sauce from food?) The same desk was really beat up and scuffed, too.
The next morning, after my shower, the tub wouldn't drain and the bath was filled with about 1/2 a foot of the shower water. As such my friend couldn't take a shower. So we went out and told the guy at the desk about the issue, which he promised to address. He gave us 2 free drink tickets for the lounge, which was fine, if underwhelming. ("We can't really do anything else for you because your room was pre-paid") A comp night on the expensive parking ($45 a night) would've helped. Not being able to shower in your room is a fairly major inconvenience.
I imagine Starwood must have plans to redo this W soon, because it's really starting to feel faded and worn. I'm sure there is better value for $$ in the 4-Star range in Seattle. Cheers!

title: “nice place to sleep”
text: We were on a one night stopover on our way to San Antonio so just needed somewhere to cook a meal and get a sleep. It served it's purpose well. The room was very very clean and spacious, kitchen was suitable and a supermarket was just across the highway. Staff were friendly however check in and out was laborious compared to other Staybridge suites. The gym was ok, it had machines and bikes. Breakfast was standard

title: “Very basic and noisy.”
text:
This hotel is fine. It's clean and affordable. If all you need it for is a place to sleep and shower, then it serves it's purpose. We found the street noise from our room to be very loud. We could also hear everything through the walls-including whiny kids, couples being intimate, etc...We were usually so tired that we were usually able to sleep through it.
The location is close to the GG bridge and presidio. It's also not far from Fisherman's wharf and some good shopping areas.

title: “great costomer service”
text: prior to our trip, i tried to book this hotel throught priorty club .com, of witch i'm a platium menber with hunders of thounds of points, i travel ever week on bussiness. that experence was a nightmare, could not understand person i was talking with,they was very confused with procedure, almost 30 mins. on the phone and got nothing done. i was so upset we dicided to call the hotel direct and just pay for the rooms. that when we meet Sandra, at Hotel Indigo Dallas Tx. she was wonderful, not only help me with the booking process with points, got us the exact type of rooms we wanted, we r so looking forward to our stay there this comming weekend,she was great and hotel mang. should b glad to have staff like her!!!!!

title: “Excellent Location, Friendly Staffs”
text:
My boyfriend and I went down to SF for the Easter long weekend. We came across the promotion deal online and honestly I didn't expect much at first after reading the reviews in regards to the room sizes, etc. On the other hand, my dad who is a frequent traveler to Japan has recommended Hotel Nikko to us, he has reassured us that we wouldnt be disappointed at Hotel Nikko chain services - and he was absoulutely right.
First- very convinent location, we got the map from SFO and took the Bart to DT Powell. The hotel was just couple blocks away and the prime location just made us love the hotel right away.
They have assigned us the room early, staffs were friendly, but be aware that they will try upselling you with various upgrades, or accesses to the hotel amenities.We were assigned to a one king bedroom, and the size is okay, providing the location of hotel and the price, we definitely are satisfied with whats provided. Staffs are extremely friendly and helpful in providing directions, deals, etc. Bathroom are big and clean, except we were little disappointed that over the course of 4 nts, the housekeeper has not changed our toileretes and at the end of our fourth night, we were kinda running out of shampoo and conditioner.
The concieges is extremely friendly, without realizing the BART doesnt operate till 8am on Sunday, they managed to help us arrange a last-minute shuttle that came ontime on Sunday at 5 am.
Overall its a really pleasant stay, shops and 5 stars restaurants are nearby. My boyfriend and I have already planned for another trip to NAPA/SF Bay area this fall. And we would definitely stay at Hotel Nikko again.

title: “Wonderful recognition as a Platinum member”
text:
We arrived at the Crowne Plaza Los Angeles Harbor Hotel mid morning and were greeted at the desk and recognized as a Platinum member. Because of my status the two rooms I had reserved were both upgraded to suites. I had booked these on points breaks and had booked separated rooms for my 18 yr. son and for my husband and myself. We were thrilled with the arrangements. The suites were right across the hall from each other situated on the corner of the hotel. They were laid out nicely and were very clean. The check in attendant also told us we had access to the executive lounge for a complimentary continental breakfast and for evening happy hour. This was totally unexpected as I didn't realize they even had an executive club lounge. 
We did take advantage of this amenity and I really appreciate the hotel offering it, but I do think they need to refine things a bit here. The women staffing it were very nice but did not seem to be as aware of what is required to keep a buffet going as they should be. One morning they were out of decaf coffee pods. The next morning it was regular coffee pods. I had to ask for more cream and spoons to be put out. They ran out of english muffins. At the evening happy hour they didn't have water in the cooler. The food selection for both events is very basic which is certainly fine if that is the level the hotel wants to provide. However, they should train their staff a bit better to keep what they do decide to offer stocked.
We had lunch in the restaurant one day and took advantage of the lunch buffet which included fresh grilled items that they were doing for 4th of July. We all enjoyed it and thought it was a very good value. Service was very nice.
We were very pleased with our stay here and the service was very nice and friendly. This seems to be a somewhat older property but very clean. It is convenient to walking to the harbor area. We had free parking in their underground garage which was nice. I was also very impressed with the way they treated Platinum members. Thanks again for the recognition and the suite upgrades!!

title: “Good Location, Very Nickel and Dimey”
text:
Don't get me wrong this hotel is in a great location in the city and has the Heavenly Bed which is usually a very pleasant experience. 
I have a very specific issue with this hotel and others following this trend - I was disappointed by the hotels approach to in-room expenses. My room had not one, but two, minibars. It also had the required bottle of water, available to you at charge, on top of the minibar. This bottle however was on top of a sensor and if moved placed the water charge on your hotel bill. When staying at a higher quality level of hotel I expect to not be faced with cheap attempts to get my money. If I drink a bottle of water, fine charge me for that act. Do not make me come down to the front desk and explain that I accidently bumped the bottle and put it back on its sensor and I shouldn't be charged. It is an annoyance and an action I would expect from a far lower class of establishment.

title: “Satisfaction”
text:
We recently stayed overnight at this Best Western Independence Park Hotel and was quite pleased. Greeted with a warm and friendly front desk person (Chris) our stay was off to a great start. The quiet and cozy atmoshpere was pleasing and the rooms were great; clean (which I am overly concerned about) fresh and very quaint. The internet options, the free movie channels and the continental breakfast was fabulous. I loved the fact that we could make our own belgium waffles and the assortment of bagels, bread, muffins, cereals, yogurts, juices, coffee etc... (I know a few complained about the lask of food in previous reviews; maybe it has improved. Anyway, we were impressed and will definately come and visit again. Cannot beat the price for such a wonderful stay and such an ideal location.
About the ghost... still wondering if it was in my dream or the real deal here... hoping it was a dream!!!!! 
BEST RESTAURANT: SFIZZIOS (block away) Amazing Italian food and greta prices.

title: “Our wonderful weekend at the Langham Hotel in Boston”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Langham Hotel the weekend of December 9,2011. We could not have asked for better service. Attention to detail from the staff was amazing. Our ride with Salim in the pink taxi was one of many highlights of our weekend. We are looking forward to another great weekend in the Spring.

title: “Good value and location!”
text: Stayed in one of the newly renovated rooms with a view of Pike Market. Great location for the market, shopping, convention centre, monorail and tram. Good value.

title: “my review”
text: The first room we got was dirty. The manager moved us to another one immediately. It was noisy the second night. The breakfast buffet was pathetic, with very little selection and a dirty room that was like a 60's rec room that hadn't been updated or cleaned since the 60's.The manager was the one good thing about the stay. Sincere and helpful. Give him the money to upgrade the hotel. The Damon's restaurant had good food.

title: “Good Location for Very Good Price”
text:
We arrived at 7:00 am and had to stow our bags in their luggage room.I had read a lot of complaints about this service, but don't agree with them. A hotel is not in the storage business and we thought $2 a bag was very reasonable to keep them alll day while we played.
I only had two concerns about the stay. Our reservation said "King Size Sleep Number Bed," but in order to check in early we settled for a queen. Not a huge issue, and really not their fault. The other issue was with the included breakfast, at the next door cafe. When the staff heard you were from the hotel, they handed you a different menu with only a few choices. #1) 2 eggs, OJ, toast and your choice of breakfast meat. #2) Danish and coffee #3) Fruit cup and roll, etc. These may have filled us up, but weren't exactly what we were expecting for a vacation breakfast.
Otherwise, this was a clean, affordable place to rest our heads. beautiful lobby, good staff, good concierge, free business center to print your return flight tickets. The location was excellent- on 48th, just off Lexington. Walking distance to all of midtown and 1 block to subway. 
Some advice: Ask that your room face 48th St., rather than 49th St. as those rooms have windows that don't actually face the street, but back up on buildings that face 49th and windows could not keep up with the roar of the HVAC from those buildings. Would rather have had the sounds of the city, horns, etc.

title: “Elegant and well located”
text:
I got the Palmer on Hotwire for a great price. I traveled with my mom and we planned to see AIC and Taste of Chicago so loved the location. It is an easy walk to the AIC and there is public transportation as you exit.
Our room was beautiful, check in was a breeze and the service from every employee was terrific. At one point the TV remote wasn't working and someone arrived with a replacement within 10 minutes.
The lobby is not to be missed, a throw back to old charm.
There is no breakfast or coffee machines but there is a Corner Bakery just outside the hotel and a Starbucks in the hotel. 
I would love to return!

title: “Awesome Hotel, Awesome Location”
text: This is a fantastic hotel. The location cannot be beat. It may be on the higher end price wise, but for the time we saved because of the location (used cabs only at night time) it was worth it. The room was very very clean and the beds very comfy. Instead of typical hotel lines there were duvets which made me feel right at home. There are only 4 rooms to a floor so at night it was so quiet. The staff very helpful, made reservations, gave directions, and made recommendations in a friendly manner. Will absolutely return when I come to NYC again, Times Square and the subway (and almost everything) are a 5 minute walk.

title: “Quaint and great location”
text: Near the Grove (shopping) and where they film Extra, literally across the street from CBS studios and the Farmer's Market. There is a CVS within walking distance in case the airport took your liquids (shampoo, body spray, etc). The Hollywood area is not far, if you are moderately fit you can actually walk there; it took me a little more than 30 min at a leisurely (tourist) pace. Just don't act like a jay-walking site-seer and you will get there fine (or take the bus which is 20min/ taxi 10 min). Down side: the bed's mattress are freakishly hard. However, when you are tired from a day well played...they give you tea and chocolate chip cookies in the lobby and you can lie down in a clean bed...it's all good. TART has a good food. The people are very very nice. :)

title: “ok where to start - avoid unless you don't need peace and quiet”
text: i've stayed in the phoenix at least fifteen times over as many years and it's gone through many different hands. jdv have owned it for a while and it's been a mixed bag of late but this time was unbelievably awful due to the excessive noise from the newly opened chambers bar which adjoins the hotel. now the drinkers of that bar wander through the hotel courtyard by your room, shrieking and tottering around till 10pm on weekdays and till midnight on fridays and saturdays. then we had the added pleasure of a 6 hour crappy burning man music party in the actual courtyard of the hotel from 1pm to 7pm on sunday. this meant that about 200 revelers in thongs and bunny ears crashed around listening to deafening dance music for the whole afternoon. the bed was literally shaking so there was no way you could stay in your room during that period unless you felt like joining in. "you were warned" was the response from the angry hipsters who run the front desk. no, we were not "warned", no-one told us that for about half of sunday our room would be basically out of commission and we wouldn't be able to use the facilities. we also had to run the gauntlet of the security guard who wouldn't believe that several of us were guests because the night entrance lock barely ever works with your room key. sorry jdv but you can't run a nightclub and a hotel in the same venue, especially when the rooms have no soundproofing. this hotel is definitely no longer for families, forget it if you want to go to sleep or relax before 10pm. if the noise doesn't bother you, then you'll love it. the location is great, the rooms are fine and it's a lovely place when you're not getting bombarded by drunken idiots who aren't even guests of the hotel. they also need to do something about the reception staff who for the most part are just unfriendly, with the great exception of the night guy on sunday who handled us with utter professionalism and kindness after one of our party finally lost it with him over the conditions. sorry for the long rant, but you have all now been "warned" properly.

title: “Great”
text:
We arrived by train, which was a short walk through Pioneer Square to the hotel. The staff greeting us were very friendly.
We booked the steam room and it was amazing. Private, relaxing - just what the doctor ordered.
Unfortunately, we don't drink so we couldn't take advantage of the evening wine tasting in the lobby, but it looked very inviting. The bed was huge and very comfortable.
I would recomment this hotel to any visitor to Seattle.

title: “Outstanding Facility”
“Best stay in NYC”
text: Thank you St.Marks for the pleasent stay, we stayed 5 nights, the shower was warm, the rooms clean, not much comfort, but you just fall into bed when you do sightsseing in NYC, and therefor it'S perfect (100 metres from the next subw.-station. Geli and Franz from Germany

title: “very poor experience”
text: This is a very nice 2 star hotel with great location, but definitely not a 4 star hotel as it is advertised. The rooms are tiny and there is no room service, i.e. they say they don't have it and there is no chance to order even a cup of tea. Don't go for this hotel!!!!

title: “Pros and Cons”
text:
I just returned from a two night stay at the Omni. I was there to attend a convention located in the hotel and an adjacent hotel.
Pros - 
 - I loved the Select Guest program! I signed up online for free. I received free wireless internet for my stay (normally a $10 per day charge) and complimentary breakfast beverages and newspapers in the morning. I did not, but if I had responded to the email suggesting I preregister at the hotel a day before my trip I would have been able to access the Express lane to receive a room already prepared for me. I'll remember next time, and avoid the line.
 - Customer service was great! Hotels are so smart to have all of their employees make their guests feel valued and comfortable.
 - Rooms were roomy.
Cons - 
 - I used room service but was never impressed with the meals. Edible, but not spectacular.
 - Rooms were unusually noisy. I was awakened at 1:00 AM to hear the ladies in the room next to mine talking. I considered confronting them when I realized they were not talking loudly at all, just conversing in normal tones. That I heard that and it was loud enough to wake me from a deep sleep was disappointing. Luckily they went to sleep soon afterwords.
 - Continuing on that theme, be sure to request a room on the highest floor available. I asked to move from the 7th floor and was moved to the 11th (of 14.) It helped. The location right next to I-35 means a lot of noise at all hours. It helped to be higher.
 - The bed was not very comfortable.
 - Although I could access wi-fi in the lobby, I could not in the meeting rooms on the first floor. That's unusual.

title: “C.I.S. in Jacksonville meet my expectations”
text: I love the Country Inn & Suites in Jacksonville. I have high expectations for where I decide to have my beauty rest after a long day of fun or business. Most people say " Oh its just a hote,l its not like you have to live there" but that's not the way I see it. Im more like if Im paying my good money to stay here it better be worth every dime even if im paying for a discounted package. This will be your home and place to unwind after a long flight, day out with family, or business meetings and you want to be able to relax and come HOME to a clean, comfortable, and quiet place. This hotel was all that and above rooms were clean, bathroom was spacious, clean, and up to date, beds were comfy and the staff were very nice. I stayed here during my tryouts for American Idol and I was very stressed out so Im glad I picked a nice hotel like this to relax me for one of the biggest things in my life.

title: “Most amazing experience!!”
text: Where do I even start. My husband, friends and I all stay at this hotel every time we come to Seattle for a Seahawks game. It is amazing. Clean, friendly, comfortable and the location couldn't be better. So it may be a tad bit on the expensive side but it is well worth it. On game day, we wake up, go to their restaurant/bar (Jimmy's on 1st) and get ready for the big game with a ton of other fans. Their food is great and the environment is ideal for football fans. Not only is this hotel great for games, but we are able to walk right down to Pioneer Square and to Pike Place Market. I have never written a review for a hotel but I had to for this one. I don't have a single complaint and i recommend this hotel to everyone of any and all ages!!!!!

title: “Had a Very Nice Stay in Midtown Manhattan”
text: As many others have said, the room we stayed in on the 8th floor was small. That being said, the hotel lobby and room were clean, the bed was soft and comfy, and the bathroom was nice for a hotel room. Everything in the room worked and the water was hot. We didn't use room service so I can't speak to that. We are not hotel snobs and didn't spend our day in the room so lack of space and creature comforts was not a problem. Location was excellent. We arrived at the hotel about 9:30 a.m. intending to leave our suitcase with the bell captain until later in the afternoon. They had a room ready for us so we checked in right away. After checkout the next morning we did leave our bags with the bell captain until we left town that evening. There was no charge for bag storage and no trouble retrieving them. We really enjoyed our stay at Stay and will definitely use them again the next time we stay overnight in Manhattan.

title: “"Good Experience, great location"”
text: I have to say that I was a bit skeptical to staying here...not much luck staying by the airport. But, the staff was exceptional and service was wonderful. My room was very clean and quiet. I really enjoyed Victor at Brewster's Bar...he was always friendly and after a long day working, his drinks were cold and delicious...I ordered room service for breakfast and it was always fast and hot and very good. I appreciate the late check out being my flight did not leave until mid-night. It's a great place for business trips that last a few days....very close to Manhattan Beach which was nice. I'll be back for sure!

title: “Our hotel in ny..”
text:
We come from Rome,Italy, and we have been in ny twice, always staying in the park central hotel.
The position is perfect, very close to times square and central park, but in a quiet position.
The rooms are large and comfortable, not the same for the bathroom, but the beds deserve 5 stars!!!
5 stars as well for ELIZABETH, our favourite receptionist, always smiling and kind with us.
We'll be back in December!!!!

title: “Looks good, lacks finer points.”
text:
Hotel Valencia is a nice hotel in a great location, but in the end I would probably choose a different hotel the next time I'm in San Antonio. 
The good:
-The rooms and common areas are decorated very nicely and exude cool sophistication.
-Service from room service was very quick and very friendly when was called to ask for a cork screw and some wine glasses.
The bad:
-The valet parking situation is really bad. I would go so far as to call it incompetent. When we first arrived, the drive was full of cars so we could not pull in. We had to sit on the street blocking traffic while we watched two valets standing around sipping Red Bulls. There is absolutely no hussle from the valet staff to get cars moved . There appeared to be plenty of staff, but there was always a lot of standing around without much sense of urgency. For $29/night, the valet staff really needs to be better.
-Bathrooms are small and the shower in our room drained very slowly leading you to stand in several inches of water while showering. 
-While I understand the dark corridors and lighting are part of the atmosphere of the hotel, it would be nice to be able to get more light in your room if you so desire. The rooms are pretty dark, even with the window shades fully open.
-The service in the lounge was pretty poor. We went in and sat for over 20 minutes without a cocktail server coming by to take our order. I finally went to the bar and asked one of the bartenders if there was a server for our area and she said there was, but that she was in over her head (she actually used a different word to describe her, but I'll leave that out). To the credit of the bartender, she took our order and brought drinks out to us.
Like I said in the beginning, I don't think I would stay here again on a return trip to San Antonio. On the surface, Hotel Valencia looks like a really nice hotel, but there are enough flaws that knock it down a few notches.

title: “Mostly a great hotel”
text:
For the most part this was a very good hotel. Some of the minuses are common to all hotels. For instance the make-up mirror would have been perfect for most males or a tall female but not for a short or average height female like myself and my roommate. Although there were two of us staying in the room, there was only one bathrobe provided. The first two days the maid only provided towels for one person. We did not have to request extra towels because I showered after swimming in the pool. The pool was swimmable but small. These, unfortunately seem to be common to all hotels.
Other negatives are not common to all hotels. The bathroom door would not stay open by itself; we propped it open with my backpack so that we could use the mirror on the door. I needed to plug the phone cord in my laptop so that I could dial up my office network but the phone cord on the desk phone was caught in a cable-holder that would not allow me to pull it up onto the desk. The phone cord for the bedside phone was more flexible but there was not an empty electrical outlet to plug the laptop into; this limited the length of time I could work to the battery life. The inflexible desk phone cord also meant that you could not move the phone around the desk. I would have loved to watch TV and work at the desk since there was a very good selection of channels; you cannot see the TV when sitting at the desk.
There was a great CD/radio/alarm clock but there were only instructions for setting the time. We were able to figure out how to set the alarm but a colleague was not able to figure out how to switch to radio from CD.
Although we were in a room with two double beds, there were only two very, very small drawers. This would barely meet the needs of one person in the room but was totally inadequate for two. They did provide us with extra hangers based on my request in my Marriot Rewards profile. Unlike many hotel rooms with two beds, there was plenty of open floor space. We were in an upgraded room at not extra charge. This meant that we faced the river which was a very nice view. Otherwise there were no differences in our room compared to colleagues in non-upgraded rooms. The beds were comfortable and bathroom was roomy and attractive.

title: “Good location, Great hotel -the stay”
text: The stay was a great hotel! It is just around the corner from time square. Everything you want or need is in the area. The staff members were amazing. They were friendly and helped me with every issue I had, including a parking ticket. They went above and beyond in assisting me with that. I also liked the fact that there was a lounge down stairs. Great hotel for those who love to party! The stay is the place where I will literally stay every time I visit the city that never sleeps. Keep up the good work.

title: “A night at the museum”
text: Once you step into this place you feel like you're in the apartment of your rich, old Parisian aunt. Everything is decorated in a French chateau style, and the room even smells a little bit that way - in a good way. You may think everything looks really old, but on second look you realize its probably not and its all very well maintained and very clean. The room was big for New York, the bathroom clean and functional, but no tub just a shower. I had a partial view and the room was facing the back, so no street noise. My rate included breakfast and early evening wine and cheese snacks so overall it was a total steal. The place is somewhat upscale, and definitely for the older, more conservative set. No hipsters and party lounges here. Which is just fine with me. The staff is very friendly. Is this really the #5 hotel out of all Manhattan hotels on Tripadvisor? That seems a bit high, but it is a nice place never the less.

title: “A great value hotel in the coolest part of NYC”
text:
I stayed here for five nights on a b&b basis, and it was a lovely place. Very reasonable with a boutique feel, very friendly staff and a great (basic) continental breakfast. The piece de resistance for this hotel is most definitely the roof terrace - as a dirty smoker (sorry) I really did get to smoke in style(!), perched on a lounger, with a panoramic view of downtown and midtown New York. Absolutely stunning, especially with the NYC blue sky backdrop. The rooms are very small but very well equipped - clean, modern and with a really comfy bed. The location is also second to none if you want to explore the Shoreditch-esque part of NYC (basically all of the cool bars, clubs and some wicked vintage shopping). It is also about three doors down from the Katz Deli and they were unbelievably friendly and helpful in there. It's also right by one of the Subway stations if you want to go to Mid or Uptown (although I walked, you can walk to Central Park in about 50 minutes) and only 10 mins walk from Broadway (where all of the shops such as Urban Outfitters, Topshop, AllSaints, downtown Bloomingdales etc are).
 I would most definitely stay here again!

title: “Fits the bill”
text:
First off, I need to disclose that I was previously staying at the Waldorf Chicago where I checked out to go on an overnight trip to Tampa. The Waldorf didn't have availability for the rest of my trip so I chose the Hilton Suites. I needed to adjust my attitude rather quickly.
The stay didn't start out well at check-in, primarily because this seems to be a huge Lufthansa crew hotel. Be prepared for an enormous rush of activity in the very late afternoon when one set of crew check out and then when the next arrive. It was at precisely this moment that I tried to check in and that one desk clerk decided to take a coffee break. After the calm of the Waldorf check in I realized I really needed to adjust my attitude. 
As a Diamond level Honors member I received an upgrade to a lake view room. I was assigned room 2504, which trust me was more a "peep into the neighbors living room" view with a bit of a lake view to the left...if you squinted. I went back to reception to enquire if there had been a mistake and was assigned 2316 with a fantastic view. So far so good.
The room was clean if somewhat dated and given the Chicago heat wave the air conditioning worked well. The rooms come with a microwave, coffee maker and refrigerator. Additionally, there is an ironing board and iron, which I frankly think should be required by law. There is no minibar. The Internet worked well generally, but not necessarily the strongest of signals. The shower was weak, but this seems endemic to all hotels lately which install over zealous flow restricters. (ok, this didn't seem to be the case at the Waldorf).
I found the bed and bedding to be extremely comfortable and I slept well. I found the employees to be very service oriented and felt well taken care of. This hotel is a fine choice for a stay in Chicago as its location next to the John Hancock building is close to Michigan Ave shopping and Rush St nightlife. Room rates are also very reasonable and provide good value.

title: “Terrific location - no frills but who needs them!”
text: This La Quinta is inside Chicago's Loop, within an invigorating but quite doable walk to Millenium Park for some great, free summer music, and just two blocks from the Willis (former Sears) Tower. You can walk to two L stops easily, the hotel is clean and safe, and breakfast was more than I expected. My husband came for business, and I wouldn't let him leave me at home with all that Chicago offers in the summer. If you don't mind short walks in a flat, fun, city - this is an excellent hotel for the price in the middle of everything.

title: “Lack of customer service training”
text:
I stayed here with my baby Grandson.I am a single grandparent who looks after my Grandson quite a bit.I decided to take him to Seaworld and stay at the Westin as it was the closest to the railway station.Once checked in and hauled my bags up to the room (no one offered to help).I needed to use the business center.I carried my Grandson downstairs thinking it would not take long to find out where the business center was.I waited at the concierge desk for about five minutes (seemed much longer as I was carrying a toddler).She was given loads of information about San Diego.Never once did she acknowledge me even though she had to of seen me (I only needed one question answering) All the FD were busy checking in so I waited.eventually I walked overto look at the menu outside the restaurant,I was away from the concierge desk literally one minute and when I got back to the concierge desk another family just arrived,instead of her saying something or acknowledging our existence she started to help them they started off "what is there to do in the area" Oh boy this was going to take forever.Five minutes later it was my turn by now I was peeved at the lack of customer service (use your initiative if a person is carrying a baby are they likely to take much of your time up).I asked where the business center was and she told me I said ok and left she shouted to me in a loud but Sarcastic tone "THANK YOU" When I asked her for a comment card she said they didn't have one and I could tell her if there was a problem.
Josh at the FD was great.The restaurant staff were great.Housekeeping sucked never got my room cleaned as I was out all day,got back to the room at 4:30 pm and they had not been to service.I called the operator and they said it was because they were busy but they would let them know to service my room next.I told them I would call back for service as my baby Grandson was about to take a nap after being out all day.Ten minutes later the maid knocked and walked in (no communication) I told her to just give me coffee.
The next morning was my check out day (Check out was 12) The maid knocked and walked in I told her we were checking out that day (it was only 8 am) She did the same at 10 am normally they would wait till you had checked out but this housekeeping were obviously not intouch with what was going on.
I have worked in Hospitality and realised the service lacked big time at this hotel

title: “Outstanding Resort to have a business meeting”
text: Great Location, Great Rooms, Great Rates, Great Food and Outstanding Service!

title: “Don't Be Fooled By The Name”
text: I was very pleased with our stay at the Comfort Inn. Although, not my usual hotel of choice, this was quite a bargain. The rooms were large (by New York standards) and clean. The location was unbeatable: a subway stop right outside your door, Macy's 1/2 block away, the Empire State Building on the next block, and walking distance to another dozen sights. Throw in a complentary continental breakfast and an Irish Pub, it was truly a delightful experience. You could do a lot worse for a lot more in The Big Apple.

title: “This place has a great staff, great location and even great food.”
text:
This is a pretty new hotel so it's extremely clean and modern. I've now stayed here twice and was impressed both times. I found some great rates on it too so that made it an easy decision. The staff are very friendly and accommodating which is always a plus.
Rooms aren't huge but a bit bigger than average for New York. The corridors are a bit tight but it's to be expected when crammed in between so many existing buildings. One thing I do find difficult is the bathrooms have no real counter space so you're hard pressed to leave anything in there. 
On my last stay, I got in late from work each night and ordered room service. The service was great and the food was both reasonable and very good. 
The hotel is a quick few blocks from Penn Station and right around the corner from the 28th St stop of the 1 train so it's pretty easy to get anywhere in the city from here. It's also a quick walk to Herald Square/Macy's, Empire State Building and most mid-town attractions. 
I'd definitely recommend this place for anyone looking to be close to everything and stay in a clean and modern hotel with very reasonable rates.

title: “Best hotel in San francisco”
text:
Best hotel in San Francisco. Beautiful room and service was outstanding. Located right in the shopping and theater district. 
Couldn't have been a better experience

title: “Great Start now slowly going backwards”
text:
This is still a good Hyatt property with one of the world's best roof top pool/bar/lounge. no doubt. And really attentive staff.
Having said that the management is still struggling with the main restaurant, the wine bar is marginal at best, and food not at their best. The hotel is again trying a new operator in the restaurant and hoping that it works, otherwise that will be my last stay and it's a shame. 
Rooms are starting to fray a bit and need attention

title: “Not to my Satisfaction”
text: One of the best things that I encountered at this Days Inn was the attentiveness of the front desk staff. From there on it was unsatisfactory for me. The building is detached from the front desk area and is old, has no elevator and not in the best neighborhood. The room that I stayed in was ok and could have been a little cleaner. The bed sheets looked rather worn out, but, the bed was comfortable. The TV is not flat screen and the reception was not all that great. One of the big pluses is that I had a microwave oven and small fridge which came in handy. The A/C is rather noisy, but, works just fine and kept my room comfortable. Would I stay at this hotel again? The answer is no. There are a lot more hotel choices around this area that look more promising although a bit more expensive. Hope this helps.

title: “Overall a very good experience”
text:
This stay was overall a very good experience. There were a few little hiccups but the hotel staff responded excellently.
The front office staff were particularly helpful, polite and efficient throughout the stay. The staff in the attached restaurant Urbana were also were good.
The rooms and general hotel decor is very hip and tasteful. The rooms are large and come with a reasonable sized desk to work on. The rooms also have a stocked mini-bar (although you need to get a key for it) and a large flat screen TV. The bed was kingsize and very comfortable. The bathrooms were quite roomy, the shower pressure was good, and the toiletries were of a high quality.
The urbana restaurant in the hotel was top notch in terms of the quality of the food, the atmosphere and the service. Although I did not eat breakfast at the hotel, my colleague who did indicated it was very poor, and made use of the many breakfast options nearby in the street after his first experience.
The hotel is reasonably central in the city. In fact we walked back to the hotel from meetings downtown on the one occassion and it did not seem very far at all to us (say 15 mins). The hotel is located in P street, which has many restaurant and cafe options to choose from that are reasonably priced. There is also a small shopping centre / grocery market directly across the street and a pharmacy closeby.
I believe the metro/train station is very closeby although we did not use it. 
If you have a car you will need to use their valet parking as there is no other parking available elsewhere on or off-street nearby. The cost was $38 per day for us.
Apart from the parking the only negatives that come to mind are that the room had quite a musty smell (which you got used to after 5 or 10 minutes of returning), they did not replace the toiletries every day, and the printing/other functions in the business centre were quite expensive (e.g. $2.50 a page to print in colour).
There was one major problem I encountered when they failed to put one of my smaller bags in the car when we checked-out. I only realised it when I arrived at the airport for a flight out and with very little time to correct it. Fortunately the hotel was super efficient and responded superbly by getting a staff member to drive it out to the airport for me. I must say that they went the extra yard to fix the problem which was very much appreciated.
I would certainly return here and would recommend it to others.

title: “'Adequate to Good' for Business Travellers”
text:
I was here for three days for a conference in April 06. Even though I have attended meetings there before, this was my first time as an overnight guest. 
The staff was wonderfully courteous - an A+.
Like other Marriott properties, this one is comfortable and attractive with very comfortable rooms. I have to give the Marriott and Renaissance chains' beds a special mention. They are fabulous. If you are considering other hotels in the same price range and the quality of the bed is important to you, choose the Marriott / Renaissance.
In terms of this property, it is close to the Columbus Airport (as the name suggests) and is primarily for business travel. Between these two facts, there isn't much to see outside within walking distance. Therefore, if you do not have a car with you, be prepared to be limited in surrounding attractions - other hotels, a business park. a Waffe House, a TCBY Yogurt, and a MacDonalds - all with limited sidewalks ... and I mean limited as in none in many places.
In terms of conference facilities - it is adequate - certainly not the best. However, given the location, perhaps these facilities are good enough.

title: “generally good for the price, helpful employees”
text: Good experience, stayed up the road before at Days Inn, prefer Howard Johnson. The requirement that the review must be 100 characters is abit much.

title: “Smelly, dank, dirty - YUCK!!”
text: This is for the Days Inn on 1101 Hollister St. The hotel looks run-down and seems to be poorly maintained. The first room they gave me had painting tarps all over the floor, it was in the middle of being painted!! There wasn't even any furniture in the room!! The second room, which unfortunately, we did take because it was almost midnight, was a major disappointment!! The room is dank and musty. The beds are so hard, it would be softer to sleep on the floor. I killed 2 spiders. The walls have poorly patched sections. The toilet is filthy! The curtains are filthy and the heater blows up through them, so you get the smell/stink of the curtains blown into the room! We have reservations for several nights, but, we are cancelling them in the morning and definitely looking for a NICE hotel, which this is not.

title: “Happy Nani 9405”
text: My granddaughter and I just returned from a wonderful weekend in NYC. When planning the trip, I consulted Trip Advisor and booked the Hilton Garden Inn based on TA reviews. Upon our arrival at the hotel, we were greeted by Tolbert at the reception desk and were able to check in immediately. I've stayed in New York many times at a variety of hotels and the rooms frequently look well used. This is not true at the Hilton Garden Inn. Our room was pristine, the bedding snow white, with a sleep number bed, comfortable work space, microwave, refrigerator and coffee maker. The bathroom was beautiful with granite countertops, shower massage and thick towels. Every staff member we met was delightful and eager to please. In addition, the location is spectacular - within walking distance of all major attractions. We're already looking forward to our next trip to NYC and the Hilton Garden Inn.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This hotel is very pretty. The rooms are very nice. the bed are memory foam. nice sleep. Bar & restraunt downstairs. Best part is FREE PARKING

title: “A good hotel with a terrific location”
text:
I spent five days here attending a national conference. It is a close walk to Carnegie Hall, Times Square and Broadway. Contrary to other comments on Tripadvisor, check in on a Friday evening (5 p.m.) was prompt and professional. Staff was extremely friendly. We booked a musical and the staff again were courteous, professional and met our needs. My 16-year-old daughter and myself stayed in room 3034; we felt very safe and had no difficulties with the room. We had enough space in the bathroom; shower and towels were very nice. Good toiletries; coffee products were replaced every morning. Even though we were on the 30th floor, the wait for the elevators was no more than any other major hotel in a busy city. There were several large groups staying at this hotel simultaneously and the housekeeping staff were still very courteous, always said 'good morning' and 'have a nice day' whenever we encountered them in the hallways. We even encountered the housekeeping managers coming through our floor, making sure the rooms had been properly cleaned. And yes, they did have their carts in the hallway in the morning, but that was the only place to put them when they're cleaning the rooms! They were gone by late afternoon. 
The Market (restaurant) was a bit pricey, but hey this is New York City!! There are lower priced alternatives in the area--multitude of Starbucks within short walking distance and even some Subways and Cafe Metros (for a quick sandwich), so you don't have to pay $30.00 for breakfast. We found a Duane Reade and picked up some fruit and soda for our room. Concierge staff very knowledgeable and helpful. 
Room was nice, we didn't hear noise from the traffic or other guests on the floor and the heating/ac worked fine. Nice flat screen tv, good choice of channels, bedding was very comfortable (loved the pillows!) and no bed bugs...
I did meet other conference attendees for cocktails in the Bridges lounge--the drink prices again are a little 'steep', but it is very comparable to drink prices at other locales in this area (theater district, Carnegie Hall, etc.). 
Closet had a good number of hangers. I did not need Internet as there was an Internet Cafe offered to us in the Exhibit hall. The exhibit halls were on two floors and a nice layout and spacious. Our banquet wait staff were top notch; it was very elegant and the food was good. Checkout was again quick and prompt, clerk asked if we enjoyed our stay. To me, they couldn't have been more friendly.

title: “OTTIMO HOTEL SITUATO IN UPPER...”
text: OTTIMO HOTEL SITUATO IN UPPER WEST SIDE IN ZONA TRANQUILLA E MOLTO GRADEVOLE CON DUE FERMATE METRO NELLE VICINANZE. CAMERA PICCOLA MA MOLTO PULITA COSI' COME IL BAGNO. PERSONALE GENTILE E DISPONIBILE. HOTEL SICURAMENTE DA CONSIGLIARE.

title: “Just like Home”
text: I stayed their for more then 2 months, but never got any feeling that i am staying away from my hown. Always i think i am staying in a Home. This is not a Hotel, but a place where you can spent good time, they have pool. Their breakfast is really good.......

title: “Stay for the location not the comfort”
text:
1. When we pulled up, no valet came over... even as we removed baggage from the car. My husband finally went and got one who handed him a ticket and said overnight valet would be $24.00. Well, needless to say we declined the "service" and still ended up with a $16.00 per night self-park fee. 
2. The front desk service was much better. Very friendly, pleasant smiles all around. Quick, kind service is always good. 
3. The room was super outdated. Heavy old patterned drapes and cheap posters in thin gold frames. Not what I expected from a downtown location in Austin, or for the price we paid. It was clean though!
4. Very uncomfortable bed! It was a Sleep Number, which may be wonderful for others, but we hated it. Both nights were terribly uneasy. BTW: If you are couple who use the middle of your king size mattress to cuddle, or whatever, this is not the bed for you. 
5. On the plus side, the location is perfect. On the river with a perfect view of the bats exodus. Head East for restaurants, bars, shopping, and a farmers market on Saturday. 
We stay downtown often and I must say there are much nicer options for the price of rooms here. However, if you get a good price give it a chance for location and nice desk service.

title: “Over-rated tourist hotel in a tourist trap.”
text:
I stayed here for two nights on business. The room I had was small to tiny with one window that looked across the 12-foot wide light well directly into other rooms, so for any privacy at all the blinds had to be shut at all times. This made the room seem even more closed in than its little size. The bed, pillows and linens were comfortable. The bathroom was small but functional. Everything worked fine. The room was furnished in a clean modern style, if a little over the top in terms of colors and patterns. The room and hotel seemed in good repair and clean throughout.
The location is what is to be expected from Fisherman's Wharf: cheesy, cheesy shops and rip-off tourist restaurants line the street heading east. Thankfully, in the opposite direction is Fort Mason and some lovely open spaces. Except for doing the cheesy Wharf thing, most everything else one would want to visit in S.F. is a cab ride away. Union Square is a much better location for a stay.
Check-in was a nightmare, taking about 20 minutes. Getting the car parked was just as bad. Check-out was a repeat of check-in, but I had to wait literally 40 minutes for the valet to retrieve my car!
The staff seemed pleasant and professional, but not particularly helpful.

title: “Relaxing and fun”
text: We stayed in a studio - nice room with sitting area, small kitchen. Lots to do - lazy river, pools, slides (for adults & kids), 3 hot tubs, nice patio restaurants. We really enjoyed the 3 days and 2 nights. Nice place to stop and watch the hummingbirds and listen to nature. Highly recommend.

title: “Not a 5 Diamond Hotel but met my basic needs”
text: This is my first time at a W hotel. I love the look of the place and the staff seemed ok. I have heard the W was the new best luxuary hotel, but it did not win me over. I understand now that the W brand is considered an upscale hotel and is not luxuary. It just seemed to be missing the little things. I guess I am spoiled. No turndown service and it just felt like it was way understaffed. Not a bad hotel just not a top notch place. I don't think I will go back.

title: “Not for more than an airport layover”
text: The room was smoking when I requested non smoking. Loud - street, airplane, and hotel guest noise. There is an attached Denny's.

title: “Great Location and View; Otherwise Run Down”
text: The Edgewater in on a pier in Seattle. You can walk the water front, walk to Pike Street Market, and the fantastic water front sculpture garden just to the north. The hotel has a nice public area and a bar that have great views. The downside is that the hotel is a serious need of renovation. Everything seems beat-up with dirty hallway carpets and the like. I was taken aback by all this when we checked in and felt mostly like I was staying in a dump the three nights I was there. The standard rooms are very small, the ones on the eastside ("City View") get train noise from the tracks that are a couple hundred yards away, there is no place to park other than valet which ends up costing an additional $40+ a day, and there is no free Wi-Fi. If I had not gotten the booking via Hot Wire for fairly cheap, I would have been very, very unhappy. No way is this place worth even the typical discounted rates.

title: “Great Hotel in a fantastic location!!”
text:
Stayed in the Hampton Inn (Manhattan Times Square) for an extended weekend break to take in the final two baseball games at Shea Stadium.
Was fully aware of the high costs of any hotels within the vacinity of Times Square, so opted for the Hampton Inn due to the good reviews on Trip Advisor and also to make use of my Hilton Honours status.
I was not to be disappointed from arrival to departure from this hotel. Check-in was a breeze and the reception staff were wonderful and helped to ensure that my stay was a memorable one. I had booked a twin room (2 x Queens) and the rooms were large and extremely clean with very comfortable beds. This is definately a plus for me as I do a lot of travelling on business and 'beds' and 'sleeping' is the one issue that really makes travelling around a pain sometimes. This was not to be the case as the four nights spent in this hotel, I had fantastic sleeps which certainly helped for the following days when I was walking the streets of Manhattan shopping or watching baseball!!
As a Hilton Honours member, I was was greeted on arrival to my room with complimentary water, snacks and a personal welcome letter which I thought was a nice touch. There was also a FREE complimentary breakfast offered, but I never got to try this as either I was rushing around in the morning or I preferred to sample a proper US Diner for some Pancakes and Coffee!!
The location of the Hotel on 8th Avenue / 51st Street was ideal for Times Square and all other attractions within New York. Times Square was probably about a 5 minute walk or a 10 minute walk to Central Park or 5th Avenue. What I also appreciated was it was a bit quieter near the hotel with being slighly set back from Times Square and I wasn't once woken up in the middle of the night due to noise.
Overall, I really enjoyed my stay at the Hampton Inn and would probably choose this Hotel again next time I'm in New York due to location and value for money.

title: “25th Anniversary trip NYC”
text: This property is newly renovated and is absolutely perfectly situated just off Times Square. There are plenty of ammenities close by, Starbucks, groceries, conv store and the Conceige staff at this property were fantastic. It was easy to come and go. The rooms are extremely clean and all new linens, carpets, bathroom, beds, pillows, reading lights and the list goes on. If you are going to NYC and want an excellent hotel experience, go here for sure. Fantastic spot.

title: “Very Spacious”
text:
I booked a room through Airport Accommodation for a great price of $69 when my flight was canceled. I chose Timbers because their airport shuttle ran the latest. When I called the hotel for the shuttle, the lady was very friendly and told me where to wait. The shuttle was a little deceiving because it doesn't actually say Timbers on it. Also it took more than 20 minutes to get to the hotel partly because of the blizzard and also because the shuttle stops at one other hotel.
The check in lady was decent but obviously tired. I was impressed by the room, especially since I did not know that all the rooms were suites. Definitely too big for just me lol. The room was very clean and spacious. I would definitely come here again if my family was with me. The bed was nice and comfy too. 
One puzzling thing happened. The fire alarm went off in my room and I don't know why. I'm guessing it was because of the toaster or maybe the heater, but it gave me a mini heart attack. 
The shuttle started at 4am. I asked for a wake up call at 3:30am. The call was a little late but I had my cell phone alarm set anyway. Overall, I think I would have enjoyed the stay more if I wasn't so anxious about my flight.

title: “They just don't care”
text: The hotel is in a good location, close to subway lines and walking distance to many SOHO restaurants. The rooms are quite new and the bed is comfortable. too bad I could not sleep too much. I have stayed in the hotel for 7 nights and was awaken everyday by a squeaking noise in the morning. On the third morning day I realized the noise came from the elevator door (unfo my room was close to the elevators..), spoke to the reception and they said they were going to take a look at it, no offers to change room or anything like that, just reassured me that they would take care of the problem. I went out for the day, came back late in the evening to be waken up in the following morning by the same noise. Complained again, heard their promises to solve it and next morning more squeaking.. by the 6th day I had given up complaining, it was simply not working. The funny thing is that I was actually expecting to be asked on the check out how my stay went, but no questions were asked. The staff really did not care. Will not stay in this hotel, and have serious doubts on how Sheraton is training its staff in NY, a shame. Do not recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a hotel to relax.

title: “A wonderful hotel in a great location”
text: I stayed here with my son for 2 nights in July 2011. It is probably located in the best area for us, since we do not like renting cars in LA. It is across the street from the Beverly Center as well as a drugstore, discount clothing store and near AT&T (where we bought a prepaid phone for use while in the US). The property itself is dark in the lobby, which isn't my particularly taste, but the room was beautiful and the breakfast in the hotel restaurant is exceptional. My only disappointment in the layout was the significant distance between the pool and the fitness center since I wanted to work out and my son wanted to swim. There was no way for me to keep an eye on him. Other than that, we would definitely stay there again.

title: “Place All to Yourself on Summer Weekdays”
text:
We came for a few nights during the work week (Tues-Thurs) and the place was virtually empty. My wife and 10 month old daughter had the entire place to themselves while I was in meetings during the day. I guess it's more of a weekend/family holiday venue and we were there off-peak. Our King Bed Suite was $139 + taxes a night. It's a pretty good rate for the access to the free water park. 
For those that don't know, the hotel is split into 3 primary building areas. The North Building, the South Building and then the River Ranch complex (see my photos for a resort map). We stayed in the South Building. We loved the fact that each building had its own swimming pool. The lobby is very posh and modern looking, though the rest of the hotel is more like a Spanish-style outdoor entrances (more like a motel than a hotel).
River Ranch was pretty impressive for a hotel, but not quite on par with a real water park. There's a main pool, plus a few water volleyball pools. Then of course the Lazy River that doesn't really let you be so lazy as the current was non-existent. You kind of had to paddle the entire way, but when you have the whole place to yourself, you can't really complain.
We had a King Bed suite which was perfect for us. They had a pack-n-play available for our baby and the room as spacious. We liked having a separate living room area with a TV. The room itself was what you'd expect for $139/night. There was a couch, TV, mini fridge, balcony, TV in the bedroom. 
Internet was about $15. Parking, however, was free.
Service was great. As soon as we pulled up, they were right there to help us with our luggage and walked everything to our room. Check in/out was smooth and painless.
We didn't really eat at the hotel but did have a few beers at the River Ranch. Note: the BBQ restaurant wasn't open while we were there. I think they only open it when the resort is full.
Nearby, there's a bunch of quick service restaurants on the corner of 16th and Glendale. It's a 20 minute drive to Scottsdale and downtown Phoenix.

title: “Best so far in Denver”
text:
The decor has stripes on its stripes, but somehow it's whimsical and a teeny bit Alice, not over-bearing. The whole experience (5 nights) was truly pleasant. Yes, they allow pets. And they have a dog-director of pet relations. If you don't enjoy dogs, you can borrow a goldfish. Really. But everything is very clean and in good condition. (BTW, if the presence of pets concerns you, the Four Seasons allows them too)
Evenings they host a comp. happy hour for guests with wine and light snacks. The restaurant is fantastic and rated highly. Breakfast is not included, but it is also at Panzano and includes classics and innovative options. WiFi is included when you are in your room.
We had a junior suite because I was travelling with my mother. It was very spacious and in good condition. The location is fantastic. You can walk to a dozen high-end restaurants and shopping. The valet parking is pricey, but they are fast, courteous, and always offer to give you directions.
Overall, we've stayed in several Denver hotels, and this one had the best combo of personality, intimacy, location, staff, food, and guests. Yes, the guests were nice too - nothing sours a stay in a good hotel faster than when the guests cannot bring themselves to be civil to the staff and other patrons!

title: “A really mediocre place, despite the renovations...all due to poor management”
text:
I stayed at the hotel from 4-8 January as part of a large business meeting. Overall, I am very disappointed. I fully expect one of the managers to write one of their disingenuous responses to this review. Which tells you that talk is very cheap.
The problems were significant and impacted virtually every colleague I met.
1. The entire hotel was freezing cold. Even men were complaining. This was a systemic issue. Rooms had to be set to 78 degrees to get any warmth.
2. The carpets were not vacuumed. They renovated. There was lint everywhere. Huge lint balls formed on everyone's shoes. Disgusting. There is no excuse for this. It is just evidence of the way they do not take care of their hotel.
3. The housekeeping staff did a half-baked job. Shower gel was not replaced. Shaving cream was not replaced. It too multiple days for open bottles and coffee cups to be tossed out. Trash was left behind. Other colleagues had similar fates with food not being picked up. Clearly, this is a managerial issue.
4. Cocktails tasted good but were low on alcohol. Clearly, they are penny pinching here.
5. Multiple people had problems with the remote in the room working properly.
6. They overcharge for internet...as usual.
There are a few strengths-- the hotel has been renovated. The bar staff are nice. The food service staff were friendly and attentive. The laundry was done correctly.
Overall, please try to avoid this place.

title: “Shouldn't Call Themselves a Westin!”
text: I was so excited when my husband told me he booked us at the Westin in Los Angeles, because I love staying at Westin. This hotel should not have the Westin name!!!! It is old, dirty, and slow! Do not let pictures of the lobby fool you. That is obviously the only place they updated when they purchased this property. The check in took forever; even as a Starwood Preferred member. We were then given a room on the 4th floor that was disgusting. The room smelt like old cigarettes (supposedly the hotel is non-smoking), and the carpet was so disgustingly dirty that I would not walk on it with bare feet. When we asked for an upgrade, we were told they were sold out. It was a real disappointment, and we did not get a great price on priceline like other reviews mentioned. We booked it through Westin. I am so disappointed that I am going to write them a letter. I do not usually waste my time on such efforts, but I think their PR people should know. If you stay here, make sure the rate is cheap and you bring your sanitizer!

title: “Nice, but not a great staff.”
text:
This hotel is located between two larger hotels in a block just East of a park facing the Mississippi River. The other side faces the streetcar tracks. The Memphis streetcar takes you to the Civil Rights Museum and a couple blocks from Beale Street. The Mud Island Monorail is pnly a block walk from the front door. So the location is excellent. 
 The hotel's physical condition is good, rather new-looking. attractive (if small) rooms. A very good continental breakfast. The ice and soda machines were only on alternating floors, and the soda machine on the third floor wasn't working. 
 the staff was rather inattentive. My room wasn't serviced one of the two nights I stayed there, and I didn't get the wake up call I requested. The clerk cancelled the price of my praking because of that. 
 Overall, noy a bad place to stay, especially for the price. But don't expect first-rate service.

title: “Close to the Pool, that's all I can say”
text: This hotel left a lot to be desired. It was chosen for it's proximity to the aquatic center and, for that, it was great. However, the rooms were terrible! The beds were uncomfortable. the linens and towels were old and ripped. The bathrooms were the highpoint of the bad quality. There was only half of a door on the shower and that leaked. There was water EVERYWHERE. To top that off, they've put in this huge sink that takes up all of the counter space so there's no room for your toiletries. Not that you'd want to put on make-up in there, the light if quite dim. The internet is not free. We were told there we could rent a refrigerator but when we got there they told us there were no refrigerators. THEN we found a maid on our floor wheeling a refrigerator. CRAZY! Breakfast was not included. There was a buffet but it was pricey. I'm hoping we can try for another hotel next year. This one wasn't worth being close.
