The wait for the elevators alone took up too much time...

title: “Easy Access to LAX and Bus Interchange Stop”
text:
This was an overnight stay before heading to Reno from LA. i guess most of the customers here are on transit due to its great location nearby LAX airport. Apart from that, being a part time tourist, the location is 2 blocks away from the public bus interchange so it was handy to catch a bus for a hollywood blvd trip.
Rooms are standard and decently decorated and the breakfast is plentiful. Wifi signal is commendable. Other than that, the free shuttle to and fro hotel/airport is a plus point.
We are not in time to utilize most of its facilities as the turnaround time for the next flight is transitory.

title: “Love this hotel!”
text: I will tell you why- 1) the suite was perfect for a family of 4. Plenty of sleeping space with a sofa bed and 3 window seat beds. You could have 4 kids and stay in the suite with room for everyone. The suite has a jacuzzi tub that is like a small swimming pool. It also has a mini-fridge. 2) free coffee/tea in the morning, juice and chips in the afternoon, and wine from 5-6pm. 3) you can have a goldfish in your room- kids loved it 4) the staff is awesome, everyone is super nice and so helpful - i told them it was my son's 3rd bday and they had cupcakes waiting for us in the room when we checked in 5) great location- walking distance or a $5 cab ride away from everything in downtown. being right next to the river, you can also take a river taxi everywhere. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Average”
text: Service, food and beverage leave a lot to be desired. A $60 charge to receive a package at the business center. A breakfast restaurant where I had to almost trip the waiter to get coffee. $8 for soup that frankly tasted worse than what you would get in a can. Wifi constantly crashes. Guest folio still wrong 24 hours after checking out. Noise travels, you can hear doors slamming on rooms. Front desk just shrug and smile inanely, smug in the fact that there are few other options. Currently on the Platinum challenge with Starwood; after this stay reconsidering whether its worth it.

title: “Not quite royalty, but still good”
text:
If you enjoy over the top decor and furniture, this is the place for you. One or two niggles prevent it from being perfect. 
First, the good bits. The atmosphere is very friendly, the staff very efficient and extremely helpful. The hotel is in a fairly quiet location (although this being SF there is bound to be some traffic noise)., but it is a pleasant area and attractive with good restaurants and convenient for buses to the main attractions. Breakfast is more than adequate.
Now the not so good. Our otherwise very pleasant room was marred by a cracked basin, a loose tap and downright filthy net curtains. The elegant guest lounge is spoilt by having an adjoining room for smokers, and of course the smoke drifts in. Far better if they simply banned smoking on the premises, as a lot of hotels already do.
Overall though. good value and the staff make up for any small failings

title: “Good choice”
text: Great location. Quiet clean rooms. Would have given this an excellent rating if it wasn't for the poor advice we got from the conciergie who told us it would take 45 min to get to JFK airport in the rain. It took almost twice as long, we missed our flight and had a 7h wait at the airport. Not happy!

title: “Value & conditions”
text: Knowing this is a older hotel, it's condition was wonderful for it's age. Great location for just about everything in the part of town, rooms were in great shape, painted like a new one, and bathroom was above average for being clean, all fixures worked great. Breakfast was very under priced I thought compared to everything around it, service workers were very kind, and free parking is the best thing. Only problem which is not the hotels fault is, a GPS will not find it, not knowing this area I had a very hard time locating it (not hotels fault. I flagged down a cab and had it take me to the hotel and wife followed in car (: maybe advertizement should say located at la salle & superior ? We go to chicago 4 to 5 times a year and this will be our hotel from now on. Also very value priced.

title: “Will stay here again”
text:
My wife and I came to New York for a four-night combination of work and vacation in early October 2004. We've previously stayed at the W hotel on Lex a few blocks away, but we much preferred the Omni this time. The staff were all very friendly, the rooms were spacious and very comfortable, and the cost was reasonable (by Manhattan standards).
The only minuses were a small amount of inter-room noise through the wall from the adjoining room and the lack of a view (we had a window overlooking a drab utility space).
The best part about the Omni, though, was it's location. Fifty-second street is pretty quiet on this block (very little street noise), yet the hotel is within walking distance of lots of great places: Central Park, 5th ave shopping, subway access, classy restaurants, Times Square, and Rockefeller Center. We will probably try to stay here from now on whenever we come back to New York.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text: This was the perfect hotel for our trip to Baltimore to see the Orioles vs Yankees and other Inner Harbor sites. The hotel is so close to the stadium you can hear the annoucer calling batters to the plate!!! Buffet breakfast was fully stocked each a.m., free popcorn in afternoons, and fresh baked cookies in the evening. (24 coffee/tea in lobby as well.) Staff very friendly and rooms spacious and clean. Only downside was odd pool hours (5pm-10pm) which didn't fit into our schedule. Short walk to Inner Harbor as well. Will definitely stay here again!

title: “Had a Great time at the Hyatt Hill Country”
text: The Hyatt Hill Country is a beautiful resort, about 30 minutes from the San Antonio airport. The grounds include several swimming pools (all outdoor), a floating river, golf course(s), tennis courts, a walking trail, workout facilities, kid’s arcade and of course a Hyatt Spa. Nearby, the Hyatt time-share location (about a mile away), has an indoor-outdoor pool with slides, so if the weather is not cooperative and you want to sit by a pool or swim, you should inquire as to a visit at the time-share. The concierge did a great job setting flowers up in our room that I had ordered for my wife and I to enjoy. The hotel’s bar is very nice and was fairly priced. The breakfast buffet was wonderful with a vast selection of foods, again at a fair price. A peeve of mine was the fact the hotel rooms still has older “square” tvs. Although I did not find the rooms to look old or un-renovated, these tvs are a dead give-away that the rooms are due for a renovation (or at least new tvs). In addition, I struggle at renting a in-room movie for $10 or so, when it will be shown on the non-HD tvs.

title: “Lovely hotel but ...”
text: This is a lovely hotel with a great location and helpful staff. The room was comfortable. My only problems with it were: 1) Wireless is not free and when ordered is only for one device so the two of us had to pay twice. I was there for a week and there was a 5-day rate with the next price point at a month. 2) Breakfast was good but Continental should have fruit. Worse, when breakfast room closed at 11 AM there was no coffee in the hotel and no coffee maker in the room I was directed to Starbucks - not far but it was pouring rain.

title: “Funky Purple Hotel”
text: After searching through almost all the hotels in San Francisco, I ended up selecting Hotel Cosmo because of the modern & contemporary style I saw on the internet. Upon opening the door though we entered into a room (smoking) not at all like I had seen on the internet. We called the front desk and were switched to a room just as shown in all the pictures. I believe that some or all of the smoking rooms have not yet been renovated so they can be a disappointment. Once we switched I was thoroughly happy though. The bathroom was small, and the nightstands & dresser could be updated a little, but the rest of the decor in the room made up for it. The valet service was a little expensive @ $25 a night, but hey, it's San Fran. The staff was so incredibly nice & willing to make our stay as wonderful as possible. The hotel is within walking distance of many things, but you will need to either take the trolley car or a rental car unless you want to walk some very steep hills to get to your destination. I strongly suggest asking about the room before you book it (if not online). If you want a smoking room & want the one shown on the website ask if it's been renovated.

title: “Plenty of room”
text: This hotel has lots going for it - large rooms with well appointed kitchen and everything you need. It has conveniently located laundry facilities, ice maker and vending machines. There's a pool on the roof - not luxurious but great to cool off on a hot Philly day. Location is quite convenient - you can walk into town, museums nearby and a number of very good restaurants in walking distance. There is a bar downstairs that is great for a quiet drink. Staff seemed friendly - although we didn't interact much. It is a little tired and dated but this is a small downside to an otherwise satisfactory hotel.

title: “Business Meeting in Center City”
text: This was my first stay hear. The price we paid was very high for this property through Expedia, but this was based more on availability than usual price I think. That said, I still have to add this to my review equation. As other have stated the service was fast, friendly and everyone was helpful. I was expecting less, but got more. The bed was decent, though I didn't endeavor to try and figure out the mattress switch. I like the Westin mattresses much better. Hotel was clean and excellent location. The meeting I attended should have had a larger room the first day, so I'm not sure that this was the hotel or the organizers fault. I feel we got squished in. All aside, I'd stay here again, but if I was going to pay the higher price I'd certainly take the Omni over this at the price ratio.

title: “Perfect Chicago Hotel”
text: We loved this hotel--a great room, a fabulous location ..all for a very great price.

title: “Not a great place to stay.”
text:
This is a two-star hotel masquerading as something nicer.
I'm saying that as a road-warrior who spends 50-ish nights in hotels yearly.
During a 2 night stay, nothing was quite right; the entire hotel WiFi & back-end computer systems went out for 3 hours one night - housekeeping simply did not service the room at all one day, the front desk people were somewhat surly - the 'guest help' line was never answered (just rang and rang), and overaly, it was just a very meh experience.
The one plus; the rooms are large, I'll say that.
Next time I'll pick any number of other options in town over this hotel.

title: “Glad it was only one night”
text:
This hotel has seen better days and seems to be understaffed. 
Here were the cons:
- The check-in process was very slow and there always seemed to be a long line at the front desk. I think this is because the front desk staff were also acting as concierge and hotel operators. 
- When I went up to my room, there were two full bags of garbage in the hallway that had apparently been left there by housekeeping. Note that this was at 8 PM, when I would have expected housekeeping to be done. In general, all of the common areas, with the exception of the fitness center, were in poor condition.
- My room had seen better days. The faux leather fabric on the desk chair was flaking off, there were spots on the carpet, and mildew in the bathtub. And the bathtub had those non-slip adhesives that always end up icky. I showered wearing my flip flops. The linens on the bed at least seemed clean. 
- There is no wifi in the rooms, which meant that I couldn't work on the bed but instead had to sit in the deteriorating chair to work. 
- Decaf coffee I had with breakfast was just about undrinkable; I think it must have been sitting around for a while.
- My room was very small. The bathroom was so small that they couldn't fit a sink in it; the sink was outside the bathroom. 
Pros
- Free bottled water
- Very close to the airport with a free shuttle. It took about 15-20 minutes for the shuttle to pick up from when I called for it, but the ride to the hotel was quite quick. Of course, there were a bunch of guests on the shuttle, so we all ended up standing in line for a long time to check in.
- Oatmeal that I had for breakfast was actually quite good. Steel cut cooked the right amount of time.
- The fitness center was small but everything seemed to be in working order. Not the best equipment, but for a quick, on-the-road workout, it was fine.

title: “You Get What You Pay For!!!!!!!!!”
text: Yes this hotel could do with some updating, but if you want better then pay more. The location was great, the staff we found to be very helpful and it was a great idea that you had to show your room key before you entered the lifts to stop non guests entering the floors of the hotel. We could not fault the room apart from it beng very warm and there was definatley no bedbugs!!!!!!! If you want a great basic hotel with a great location then this is it and ignore all the other bad reviews - We just don't know what people expect. We would return to this hotel if we went to New York again.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: clean, friendly staff & great location, overall i enjoy everything that the Radisson Martinque has to offer - keep up the great work and thank you for making my stay enjoyable

title: “Nice... But No More Than 3 Stars”
text:
When I entered the Fairmont Olympic hotel, my first thought was "wow, this place has some class!" On the way to our room, we visited the fitness center, which again was very well kept, well designed and lovely. Unfortunately, that's where the great experience stopped. Our room was musty, and was definately in need of some updates. Carpet seemed old, bedding was torn in places, and wallpaper was stripping. Shower water was normally lukewarm. We were so taken by the exterior and lobby of the hotel- but that was it. 
While this hotel has a lot going for it (GREAT service, good amenities), but we felt like we could have gotten more for our money by staying in a nearby 3/4 star hotel.

title: “Luxurious balance to family vacation”
text:
Not a traditional choice for a family vacation, but we're not a traditional family. My 8 year old and I booked a trip to Legoland in Carlsbad. A frequent business traveler, I've had my share of chain hotels at budget prices. The US Grant is a fantastic, opulent hotel which I scored at a ridiculously low price. It does not have a pool or free breakfast. I never use them, so could care less. The valet parking, $32/night, was very prompt (no waiting after a quick call down) which is terrific. The front desk checked me into my flight and printed my boarding passes. They also brought up my delivery order (on the 1 night out of three I didn't order from room service) and refused a tip. As for the room service...
The Grant Grill is a 5 star establishment and my son and I ordered the kids pasta with marinara and beef tenderloin from room service after a 10 hr day at the amusment park. Bliss. The kid's pasta is a huge portion as is the tenderloin. We were both stuffed and he scarfed the asparagus that came with my dinner. For breakfast I had the spa breakfast with a giant puffy egg white frittata, 9 large slices of fruit, dense (in a good way) whole grain bread, jams/jellies, coffee, and juice! My son had 3 micky chocolate chip cakes (huge, adult plate sized, not too chocolately, puffy) and a side of bacon (thick sliced).
Walls are thin, I heard a wedding party in the hall late night and just turned on the TV after the kid went to sleep. Windows are thin, sirens, loud folks outside are easily heard. I personally don't mind these things, neither does my kid. If you do, you probably won't like it. Also, no one looked twice at my Star Wars outfitted child nor me in Keds/shorts. I would have fit in dressed more nicely but no one made me feel out of place. 
Will come back, for sure.

title: “Ramada Canoga Ave :(”
text: Location good but front desk staff very abrupt and seemingly unfriendly. Toilet won't flush twice during my stay. Free breakfast selection very poor. Other Ramadas in the area offer a better deal. Won't stay again.

title: “Palmer House is our new favorite hotel!!!!!”
text: Ok, based on the reviews we were a little nervouse about staying here. However that all changed as soon as we stepped in the lobby and saw how beautiful it was. Our room was a two double with sitting area and two...yes two closets!!! Our room was huge!!!! We have stayed all over the country and different countries,,, this room was very large and nice!!! We slept great!!! no noise whatsoever...The location is great!!! Walk out the door to state street and bam, there is the Christmas parade!!!! The starbucks is over priced since it is inside the Palmer house, and we did eat at the Lockwood restaurant, very good!!! A little pricey, but what nice hotel restaurant isnt? The service was phenomenal!!!! The only complaint I had was with the concierge...I asked the lady where the lady for directions to the parade, and she just looked at me and said "state street"....uh...I tolde her we weren't from Chicago, so where is state street??? She coldly replied " take the escalater down and turn right, walk out the doors and thats state street...???Like we were supposed to know that since it was our second day at this hotel...I guess she was unhappy about working on Thanksgiving...oh well...Her problem, not ours...They should also have flatscreens in the rooms by now, there was still a huge tube tv in our lovely room, so that was outdated....I wonder if Palmer purchased any flatscreen hd tvs with the 179 Million they spent on renovations?? beside those two quirky things we loved this hotel!!! We will stay here everytime we visit Chicago!!!

title: “A Grand Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Drake with my husband for a get-away in December. This was our second visit the Drake and we were not disappointed. When we checked-in they said welcome back. Let me say up front we a Hilton Gold members and each time we were upgarded to a large room (might be a junior suite) on the executive floor, which might color my review. The room was lovely and elegant -- crown molding, rich fabrics, a sofa and chairs, bathrobe and slippers and about every amenity you can think of in the bathroom. The heating was a tad bit noisy. The bed, oh the bed. I usually look forward to my own bed after a hotel stay, but the Drake beds are truly heavenly, at least for me. I slept so well! Overall, the room and lighting were just sooo comfortable just visiting for a second time felt like home. The staff were all gracious and in the morning at the executive lounge the hotel manager came by to see how we enjoyed our stay. When we were checking out, as our parking was being validated, he came by again to make sure we weren't delayed. Great Service. 
The executive lounge has an absoutely wonderful view of Oak St. beach and Lake Michigan. It's a great place to unwind for appetizers and drinks. After dinner we we there again for a nightcap. Lovely furniture and muted lighting. The food was of high quality (salmon, good cheeses, fruit & veggies) and the service was great. The only drawback, if you need a pool, there is none. We will be back for another get-away.

title: “One night”
text: Great location and the staff was great.. Take a little time and head to the rooftop deck. Great views.. Staff was great..

title: “Too Tiny for Two”
text:
I've stayed at a couple of these hotels now, solo and with spouse- and this room was not comfortable for two people. This hotel scores high on cleanliness because it is new. It's a fun and funky design that doesn't take long before it begins to wear on you . The front desk staff need further training as they were unaware of Starwood Program benefits. Because it is a new concept I'm sure they are stil working out the kinks so here's how I see it.
Cons: Trying too hard to be trendy, relevant, and unique. Overbearing music at check in (confirms my old age). Room size: 2's a crowd. Over priced food, liquid soap (i prefer bars), Big Screen TV interface (no one could get it to work- the second Aloft property that had this problem), noisy HVAC, charged for parking
Pro: Rooms comfortable for one person. creative way of fitting all the design elements into a compact area, the sink area is outside of the shower toilet, tubless Shower, Big Screen TV.
I'd stay here when the price is $120 or below.

title: “Lovely, quiet, great location”
text: Nice room, ample by NYC standards, with great amenities and modern, comfortable, and very attractive furnishings. Nice midtown location.

title: “Disappointing First Time Stay at W Hotel”
text: My wife and I had looked forward to our stay at the W Hotel on Adams Avenue in Chicago. Although the hotel's location was hard to beat, the hotel itself seemed dull and drab. It was more like an industrial building that had quickly and cheaply been converted to hotel quarters. The lobby was very hard to navigate to get to the elevators. The wallpaper in the elevators was a psychedelic style that left us dazed and confused. The room itself was decorated in a "post industrial style." Room windows looked into an office building with office workers looking back at us. Employees were friendly and helpful - no complaints there. The lobby and lounge areas seemed to cater more to a swingers crowd. This hotel did not suit our tastes in any manner. In conclusion, we'll not stay at another W Hotel.

title: “Excellent choice”
text:
I stayed at this hotel after a last minute change of mind and after reading TA reviews. I have no regrets whatsoever.
The hotel is central, well maintained and rooms are a good size and well equipped. Bed was extremely comfortable.
Staff was generally helpful and friendly. The only exception was a room service waiter who seemed to expect a tip even though the hotel added 17 or 18% service charge. The hotel has, to its credit, responded to my comment about this.
The only downside relates to the lack of breakfast service at the restaurant. However this is a purely personal desire and may not influence others.

title: “Ideal for intended use”
text: If you want to make your air travel lodging as trouble free as possible, this is the way to go. The hotel is extremely well managed, attractive (in a minimalistic sort of way) and very easy to use. The security entrance to the terminal could not be handier. All that being said, Westin knows when it has a captive clientele -- and the food/amenity services are priced accordingly. Nonetheless, this was a perfect choice for making an early morning plane.

title: “I woke up with bites on my body”
text: Look, mistakes can be made. But something was not right. I a few bites on my body. Could of been a spider, I have no idea. My daughter (5) slept in the bed with me, I checked her over, she lacked any bite marks. I did the mattress check, no signs of discoloration but, just a general reminder keep your suit cases off the floor. Also I know this just sounds a little more crazy but it was the week of the 4th and I had bought a bottle of vino, and keep it in the room to take to the pops concert. A few days later couldn't find it. How does the maid mistake an unopened bottle.? My Jewlerly was fine though. And finally postitive feedback the staff was great. Great location. Pool area looked fun. Whole foods just around the corner! Fantastic! I'm comming back to Boston in a few weeks and I'm going to try somewhere else. PS .Parking was not cheap!

title: “Great Hotel...Just some issues 1802”
text: Hotel was great, historic and pretty. Did have an issue with the shower stop stuck on, no ice in room with ice maker, had to go from 18 to 3 to get ice with a big glass bowl because there is not an ice bag in room. Robes were not very clean and itchy and blender did not cut ice well. Worth the stay, but some details should not be overlooked.

title: “An OK hotel”
text: The hotel was located on a very busy street in SF. The service was average. The room was rather small. There were no fridge nor microwave. We stayed on the 3rd floor and the street noise can be heard during the night. However, it is one of the cheaper hotels we can find over that weekend, so can't complain. The continental breakfast was average. One upside about this hotel is that there is a AMC theater very close by if you are in the mood of watching a movie in the evening.

title: “it's all about location”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with a bunch of friends. I think we got the suite which the reservation email referred to as the "deluxe double" - so there was a little inconsistency there, and it was also a little vague regarding the details of what a "suite" or a "deluxe double" gets you. What we ended up with, was a 2 double, 2 bathroom room. 
Note that during the week there is construction near by - you won't be able to sleep in due to the noise.
The room itself was pretty adequate. For the price in NYC and for the location, you cannot really complain. The hotel is within walking distance from several metro stops and IN Japan town with a 24hr grocery store on St Marks St and plenty of pizza and other food near by. The truth is, the room had very little by way of flat surfaces. We made due without it, but it drove me crazy. I didn't have a place to put my cup of water! Again, these are minor things, when all you need is a clean place to sleep in the busy city. As well, the toiletries were not so great, so I would recommend that you bring your own (or if you forget, then walk down to the 24hr walgreens). Also, if you're sensitive to air conditioning, then you will not like this hotel. The window units are used, and it's difficult to get the right setting. Bring a small blanket and you'll probably sleep better.
I gave this hotel an average rating because the hotel itself is average. I've stayed in 4 star hotels in Manhattan, near times square and in the financial district, and I would recommend this hotel over the others solely based on its location close to many metro stops and great food! It is clean, but a little old. There are zero amenities, but the location is what saves this hotel.

title: “You don’t want to stay there.”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this hotel for 7 nights, from 2 to 9 May ’11.
The first problem we encountered, on arrival, was that at 15:00 hours, check in time, the room was not ready and we had to wait for an additional hour and a half in the lobby. Then we found out that the internet services in our floor were not available. We complained and were moved to another floor where this service worked well. 
Additional problems we encountered were: cold and unclean rooms and bathrooms and bath mats not always available. The excuse was that the air conditioning was on in the whole hotel and, since there were no individual thermostats, there was nothing that could be done to warm up our room. One evening we could not enter the room because both keys were not working.
Finally, never did the three elevators work simultaneously, one was always inactive or being used by the staff for towel delivery to the guest floors or food delivery to the restaurant.
We will never stay here again.

title: “Excellent experience in the heart of DC”
text: I was very impressed with the price (at least the weekend rates) and the rooms. I felt my (standard) room was relatively large for the price and mid-city location. It was maybe twice as big as downtown hotels in NYC or SF of similar vintage. The furniture, bedding, TV, etc., were almost new and well above average. The small bathroom was equally well-appointed. Had no issues whatsoever with the staff or services - it's not meant to be a full-fledged family or tourist hotel. Do-it-yourself chilled bottled water on each floor, two free PCs in the "club room" and recent bestselling books available in the room and in the club room. I was on the 7th floor facing I Street which was noisy due to traffic and sirens; on the south side there's a major construction site. The nearest entrance to the Metro (Orange/Blue Lines) closes on weekends so you have to walk an extra block.

title: “Very disappointed”
text: I've been staying at this hotel since 1991. It fact it had always been my first choice until last week. Since it has been taken over by Affinia, the standards have dropped while the prices have gone up. One of the things, I valued most was a spacious suite or room in the heart of Manhattan. This time we were given a room hardly large enough to turn around in and with a small window with the view of a wall. I was honestly Clautrophobic Appeals to the front desk did nothing. All of this for over $500. I will never stay there again.

title: “Comfortable with historical charm”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed at the Chancellor on our roadtrip. Our first issue was stopping the car and it was difficult given the tight streets with the cable car tracks right in the middle. We had to do a big loop in order to drive up facing the right direction, but that’s just San Francisco. Stopping in front of the hotel for the valet parking was difficult when we arrived in the evening since the whole block was full of parked cars despite it being a no parking zone. Eventually, we got the valet to take my car to their undisclosed parking location. Be aware that you need to give 20 minutes notice to get your car back. There was a mix-up one time when I asked for my car and they somehow brought the wrong one. But the error was corrected quickly and the staff was friendly. The valet parking cost seems like a lot but considering the price of the rooms and the nature of driving in San Francisco, it’s quite reasonable.
The room was a touch on the small side, but given the location and history of the building, it was a minor concern. We were provided with a spacious closet that included a safe which was a nice touch. The bathroom was fine and the little touches made it feel cozier (like the rubber duckie and the not-often-provided cotton swabs). Watch the lip walking into the bathroom though because you might trip or at least hurt your toes. Another nice touch to the room was the pillow menu. We couldn’t be bothered to ask for different pillows, but knowing that they had a varied selection of interesting pillows was comforting.
The Chancellor had one computer in the lobby for public internet use. The set-up seemed like the computer was off-limits, but all you have to do is ask to use it. The room is set up for wireless internet access, but you need your own laptop of course.
One really helpful thing was the map they provided. It had all of the major tourist attractions and really made it easier for us to plan our trip.
All in all, we were quite comfortable at the Chancellor and the staff was very friendly (including answering our questions about the 4.0 earthquake that happened while we were in San Fran). Considering the charm of the building coupled with the excellent location next to Union Square, the Chancellor proved to be a good choice for our vacation.

title: “Great location for a weekend.”
text: Met a friend for the weekend and we wanted a place to stay near everything. The rooms were very nice. My friend was able to check in early. I had called to request early check in and the staff member very helpful. The breakfast was great as well. We walked everywhere but the el stations were close if we needed them. I would highly recommend.

title: “It was an extremely pleasant stay!”
text: This was a family trip. We travelled to Philadelphia a few days before Hurricane Irene to visit with family. We would stay there again. The staff-front desk, housekeeping, and restaurant staff were all very nice to us. Our room was clean. The food in the restaurant for breakfast and dinner was very good. There is a pool which we went in one time. It was clean. The staff was still very pleasant even during Hurricane weather. Hotel Management even took care of staff by allowing them to stay overnight during the bad weather. The hotel is close to many things--shopping, restaurants, and attractions.

title: “Grat Place to Stay on the Riverwalk”
text: Lovely room with a Riverwalk view, comfortable lounge chair, and great spa. Excellent front desk staff. Jose Rosales made check out super easy.

title: “Bed Bugs!!!”
text: December 2011 - Bed Bugs! Entire boy, including face, was bitten by bed bugs. The rash, boils, and incessant itching caused nausea and insomnia. Bed bugs invaded suitcase and were involuntarily brought into car! NIGHTMARE.

title: “great for the money”
text: This hotel is in a great location right off Broadway. Perfect for going to the theatre. We had a nice room and it was a good size. A good deal for the money.

title: “Lovely staff, very comfortable, good location”
text: I stayed here for one night after a longer stay in Santa Monica. In some ways Santa Monica was more convenient for driving places, but this Hilton is very convenient for those with downtown business or events. The immediate area is lots of corporate stuff, but I was able to walk to lots of restaurants, as well as the Disney Concert Hall, Cathedral, and Staples Center. Staff was great, from front door to desk to bar. Bed and bath were very nice, made for a very relaxing day!

title: “Great location, fantastic views - horrible elevator system.”
text:
I stayed At the Swissotel several times this past summer, and all of the stays were great. Nice, quiet rooms, well-appointed. The staff is very attentive and helpful, although at certain peak times the hotel front desk is understaffed for an influx of check-ins or check-outs. It is a fairly busy hotel - plenty of energy humming.
The location couldn't be better: it's within walking distance of the Miracle Mile (to the north) and to Millennium Park and the Museum district to the south. Parking a car is very expensive anywhere in Chicago - it often costs more than the daily cost of the car rental - so I tend to cab it around.
The room service is pretty good, although with a pretty limited wine list available (swing buy Mariano's market and pick up a good bottle on your own). The Palm restaurant located in the hotel is very expensive and sort of old-fashioned; trying to be Sardi's without any charm. Definitely geared for the expense account crowd. There are many much better alternatives nearby. The little chocolate chip cookies available in the hotel gift shop are worth every penny (of which you will pay many) - but you will love them.
Try and get a waterfront room, it is worth the view of the river, Navy Pier and the Lake.The corner rooms facing the water are sublime. I booked my rooms on the Swissotel website...they often have really great internet-only deals available.
The hotel has a huge and nicely-equipped health club on the top floor, incredible views while working out. 
A rant: the elevator system is horrible. It has a centralized input that directs you to an individual elevator. But if the elevator is full, you might not get a new elevator available to your floor for many minutes.There are no buttons inside individual lifts. It works (or rather, doesn't work) the same way descending or ascending. At peak times a trip to your room can take 30 minutes. And - since the hotel has a fair bit of convention business - peak times can be anytime during the day; when a conference let's out fro a break....bam, it's peak time. Walking up 36 floors isn't in my fitness program...but I did think about it more than a few times.
Check out 'Maison Brasserie' and Mariano's market nearby. Also 'The Gage' and 'Henri' restaurants on South Michigan. 'The Goat and the Girl" and 'Gilt' are also cool.
If you can get a good on-line the deal, the Swissotel is an unbeatable value. Even if you don't, the location, facilities, staff and ambiance make for a great stay.

title: “INCONFORMIDAD”
text: QUEDE TOTALMENTE INCONFORME QUE NO ME PROPORCIONARAN TOALLAS A LA HABITACION POR ESCASEZ DE LAS MISMAS...NO PUEDE SER POSIBLE ESE MOTIVO!!!! HASTA NOCHE DESPUES DE SOLICITARLAS VARIAS VECES O CANCELABA EL SERVICIO Y ME RETIRABA ME LLEVARON TOALLAS PEQUEÑAS !!! NO ME AGRADO NADA ESA SITUACION, TE MOLESTA MUCHO !!!

title: “Good, but not Grand”
text:
I always like to give a quick bit of background info and disclaimers to put the review in perspective, so here goes. After working for Hyatt Hotels for 15 years I am a bit of a hotel "snob" so take some of my pickiness with a grain of salt. In addition, this was a buisness trip that didn't allow me to use, explore or appreciate all of the facitities at the hotel so my reivew will reflect that perspective.
Checked in arond 1pm to a well staffed front desk in a beautiful lobby. The desk clerk was efficient and helpful and gave me all the information that I needed and I was on my way. There are two towers in the hotel, Harbor Tower (older tower) and the Sea[something] tower (newer tower). From comments that I heard from fellow meeting goers, the Sea[something] tower rooms were a bit nicer and more up-to-date. The room itself was very spacious with nice dark wood funiture that included a big desk (w/outlet) end tables, dresser and a chair ottoman combo. The dresser contained a room safe, fridge (no mini bar) and three drawers on the smaller side, two phones, iHome clock radio, wired and wireless internet connections. Both we complimentary for me but that could have been a meeting perk. Big 42" flat screen with usable computer monitor and HDMI connections. Hair dryer and magnifying mirror in the bathroom. The carpet looked relatively new. No balcony rooms from what I can see. My room had a decent view of the opposite tower, with downtown to my left and the harbor to my right. The bed was decent but not the most confortable I've ever been in. The pillows did not appear to be feather but seemed to stuffed with some kind of chunky synthetic filling. The conforter was a bit thin as well. The bed was well worn on one side but quite firm and more comfortable on the other side. General hotel bed tip - if you like a firmer mattress, always sleep on the side of the bed opposite the alarm clock. Most people will sleep on the alarm clock side and it will wear down quicker. 
The bathroom was simple but clean and in good shape. OK counter space. The tub/shower was a bit on the small side and did not have a bowed shower curtain as I've seen in other hotels. The shower pressure itself would make Karen Silkwood proud. Shower pressure is a real hot button of mine but I can say this is the first hotel where I would have liked to turn it down a bit. I did feel better though knowing I started each day here radiation free. :-)
Location, location, location. The hotel couldn't be better situated. About a 5-10 minute walk from the Gaslamp Quarter and Petco Park (Baseball/Padres). Tons of shopping and a restaurant for any type of food you can imagine. Nice place to just walk around as well. In addition, there is the Seaport Village directly behind the hotel. More shopping and restaurants that is literally two minutes from the building.
The train tracks are near by and you can hear the train whistle on a fairly regular basis from both the light rail and Amtrack style trains. It didn't bother me much but I could see how some folks could get a little bonkers from it although they do seem to stop running by 11pm or midnight.
I didn't swim but the pool looked well kept but small. The do run three good sized fire pits at night in the pool area.
That's about all can speak to. Overall it was a very nice stay but did not live up to the image I had in my mine when I heard it was a Grand Hyatt (a title Hyatt usually reserves for their more spectacular hotels).
I would stay here again for business without hesitation but would at least investigate other options if I was bringing the family back for a vacation.
Happy Travels,
Sulu

title: “Sofitel”
text:
I've been upgraded to a Suite on the 26th floor with very nice view. 
My Bed was just so marvellous... 
Lobby disappointing as well as housekeeping.
Very well located.

title: “Good downtown location”
text:
This is a great hotel to stay at if you have lots of downtown Seattle activites planned. We spent three nights here and weren't disappointed. The ONLY complaint I have (which really is minor in the scheme of things) is that there is only one computer in the lobby with internet access and it was really difficult to get on it with the hotel being very busy. I think for the size and capacity of this hotel, they should definitely have a second or even a third computer. I also think that travelers who want to spend time on myspace and other sites like that should bring their own computers and have the common courtesy to not monopolize the only computer available for guests. With that being said, the rest of our time here was great.
Public transportation has a pick up right in front of the hotel. We opted for this for trips to Pike Place Market, as parking down there would have cost us $15 and the bus cost us $6.50 round trip. We walked to the Space Needle, restaurants, and also walked to the dock of the Victoria Clipper (Pier 69). We found it much easier (mostly beacuse of parking prices), and left our rental car parked in the gated parking lot beneath the hotel. Breakfast was abundant, but the breakfast room was WARM and always full so we did take the food back to our room. The people at the front desk were incredibly friendly and helpful with travel ideas, bus routes, restaurant suggestions, etc. The Mariners were in town and they had sign-up sheets at the front desk for shuttles to the games for $5/person. 
We had a room that had a sliding glass door to an outdoor area where everyone from the hotel had access to. I wasn't happy the first day back when our curtain had been opened by the housekeeper so everyone could see in and see what we had. The next day the curtain was kept closed which I was thankful for. Our room was always made up and cleaned very well. I did a load of laundry and found it reasonable at $1.50 per machine to wash and dry.

title: “Was this really the Hard Rock Hotel?”
text:
My wife and I just spent the Labor Day weekend in the city, choosing the Hard Rock Hotel as our pad. We've stayed at the HRH in Orlando twice and are blown away by the ambience there. It's not that way here.
These may be all ticky tacky things, but they added up to us.
First of all, the room. We upgraded our reservation thru the HRH website for a room with "an Incredible view". Well, our 9th floor view was of nothing more than the venting on top of the building next to us. That was all we could see. So there was no view. 
The room was muggy. We had the air turned down all the way and it never got below 74. We woke up sweaty both days. When we opened the window to get a breeze, the noise from the rooftop next to us was overbearing.
The room was small and dark, but it didn't bother us that much. The bed may have been the mosr comfortable bed I ever slept in. And we even joked about stealing the pillows! 
We had the same issue with the honor bar as a previous poster, but they removed the charges no prob.
Throughout the entire hotel, I counted a total of 3 pieces of music memorabilia. I thought it was a pretty cheesy attempt to renovate an old hotel, throw a Styx guitar on the wall, and slap a HRH emblem on the outside.
The hotel itself was very clean and did not look like a renovation. The location is good, right on the south end of the mag mile, but there are 10-15 better hotels in a better location to shopping, quality eats, and Navy Pier.
If you have a car, parking will cost you $38/day, which is prob normal for downtown.
The hotel restaurant was a Chinese restaurant. The bar was small and trendy, and I guess the kicker to it all was that my wife tried to order a Pina Colada and they told us they didn't have a blender. WHAAT???? A HRH without a blender? Did they not know that Jimmy Buffet was in town???? Mind blowing!
I would never, never, never go back here. Like I said, there are many better hotels in much better locations. I will stay at the HRH in Orlando or elsewhere again.

title: “Great value, undergoing renovation.”
text:
Stayed there for business in new York. New rooms are very modern, simple and neat, which I really enjoyed. Rooms are quite small, corridors are dark and elevators are quite slow. That is probably because of being an old building. Had some construction noise in the morning though.
Right in the heart of the theater district, great location.

title: “Not as good as last time”
text: We stayed as a family in August after having stayed previously. We arrived early afternoon, the first room we were given had stains on the carpet and curtains. We asked to change rooms and the second was fine. we did not eat at the hotel, but ate in a diner a couple of blocks away which was excellent. The hotel is near Grand Central so is easy for the subway and great for exploring both lower and upper Manhatten. Other hotels which I have stayed in in America, the porters always offer to assist with luggage when arriving and offer help to your room with the luggage, however on both occaisions I have stayed at this hotel, nobody did, and was out on the pavement chatting to what looked liked friends. The second room had good views of the Empire State Building.

title: “Great hotel, Clean & Friendly”
text: We recently stayed at the Best Western Island Palms hotel for a family vacation where we had 3 rooms, two of which we had small children in. We did a lot of research on hotels and this hotel had the most positive reviews and the best price so we went with it and could not have been more pleased with our stay. All of the staff including the front desk, housekeeping, and servers in the restaurant were incredibly friendly. The rooms were very clean, the beds were comfortable and the bathrooms were some of the nicest hotel bathrooms I have seen. The views from the hotel are gorgeous - the marina is on one side and the other side looks out the bay and downtown San Diego. The location is great for sightseeing - we were easily able to get to the San Diego Zoo, Sea World, Coronado Island, Old Town, and La Jolla. It has a great central location for people wanting to see a lot of the touristy attractions. We would definitely stay here again if we return to San Diego.

title: “Stay only if you get a bargain”
text:
Stayed there couple times in the past mainly due to location (very good !).
This time was the worse, very noisy, thin walls, work in progress (or noisy neighbors), takes 15 mins on average to go up/go down from room in the morning as staff uses the elevator for cleaning.
I got a good deal so can't complain but usually this hotel charges $200-$250/night this is when you want to also look at other options.
Reception is helpful and trying to help but limited to what they can as far as facility, noise etc.
Would consider staying again only if price justifies ($120-$150/night)

title: “A hidden gem”
text:
A few weeks before I arrived, I called to ensure that my reservation was accurate. At that time, the person I spoke with was very polite and helpfull. I was surprised because of the reviews I had read concerning staff unfriendliness. 
When I arrived at the hotel, the staff was eager to answer my plethora of questions concerning directions and getting about LA (the first time I've been here) and being from a small town, I was very appreciative of this service. 
The room was small, but it was just me and my husband, so it was plenty of room and for the price, I wasn't expecting anything much bigger. At least what little room there was was very clean. Only one problem with the TV being difficult to work, although someone came up to help me with it and got it working right away. 
The complimentary breakfast was more than I expected- plenty of pastries and cerial, even waffles. 
I stayed for three days total and overall enjoyed the experience. Not sure why there's so many bad reviews, my guess is the hotel has undergone some big changes since then... or maybe just crabby people.

title: “Weekend Vacation”
text: I had an opportunity to place a slient bid on this weekend vacation close to home. I checked in without any issues. The hotel registration went perfect. The hotel was grand, everything about it. I live in Houston but have never ventured downtown to explore the venues. I was impressed at the room and the view. The extras I requested were waiting for our stay. My wife and I had the breakfast bar in the hotel and that was amazing. There was never a shortage of employees to accomodate anything you desired. I would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Houston. I will definetly plan another weekend away at the Hilton America.

title: “Great Time”
text: Our stay at the Edison was great. The hotel and staff are amazing. Close to everything we wanted to do. Our first trip to New York was made even better by staying at the Edison. I am returning in May!!!!

title: “Nice place though I found some former guests items left behind in the room”
text:
Great location, nice hotel though i have to wonder about the thoroughness of the housekeeping staff. I had a nice room on the 7th floor and it was nicely appointed and very quiet. The bath was spacious and has white granite. Shower drained well and had excellent spray. What was a bit disturbing though is i noticed a few things someone had left behind that housekeeping didn't even discover.. Found some clothes in a drawer and also found a bag of opened almonds someone had placed in the ornamental box on the table. Additionally, they charge $15 a day to use the gym and $35 a day to park. :-( 
I opted to walk into Georgetown both days. Great, easy walk to trendy shops and restaurants

title: “Loved it.”
text: This hotel has lovely rooms, is very clean, and the staff is friendly and helpful. Most SF sights are easily accessible from the location. The continental breakfast is small but serviceable. For the money, it can't be beat.

title: “Clean rooms”
text:
We stay at this motel for a few days. 
The rooms were comfortable, we had two double beds, alarm clock, a bathroom with a tub, a mini kitchen area which consisted of a sink, coffee maker + coffee packets, microwave, and a mini bar fridge.
You can book transportation to the airport at the front desk with a couple days notice. The front desk clerks with very friendly and willing to provide you with any information you needed to know. Jay was a really friendly guy. 
This motel was in walking distance to the piers, it wasn't a short 5 minute walk but it wasn't too extreme. Probably a 20 minute walk. There are buses close by that will take you to the downtown area and the piers as well. A taxi to pier 39 was between $10 and $15.
It's located close to a little restaurant called Marina's pizza which is worth checking out.
It was probably a 15 minute walk up to the crookedest street. It was a difficult walk as the last two or three blocks was straight uphill. The front desk told us that there were no buses that could take you there but once we got to the bottom of the street we noticed that there was public transportation. I would recommed finding your way to the bottom and taking the staircase to the top of the street.

title: “My favorite place to stay in NYC”
text: This was my second stay at The Kimberly and was just as enjoyable as the previous! All personnel I encountered stemming from Lola and Linda in the Reservations Dept., Marcia in Sales and all of the wonderful doormen always have me feel as if I'm visiting my 'home' in NYC! I've had the pleasure of experiencing the one bedroom suites which are a wonderful accommodation for both relaxation and entertaining. Space is abundant and the rooms not facing the street are much more quiet. The roof top lounge and breakfast room is certainly an added plus to enjoying a 'true' NYC experience with its magnificent views. A special mention to Christine from the Front Desk for her assistance and suggestions. The Kimberly is a gem of a hotel in a large city where 'exemplary' customer service is always the standard!

title: “First time here, won't be the last time!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stopped over in New York City for a couple days on our way to Montreal, Canada. We were taking an early morning train to Montreal so we wanted to stay at a reasonably priced nice hotel in walking distance from Penn Station. Staying at the Comfort Inn Chelsea exceeded our needs and helped make this leg of our trip a really nice experience.
Check-in went quickly and smoothly; staff was very friendly. We were pleased with our king room, it was a little small as our bed dominated the room but the room was clean and in good condition. We thought it had been recently renovated as everything seemed newer (i.e., paint, wallpaper, etc.) The bathroom was also clean and in good condition, though also a little on the small side. My only complaint was there wasn't much space to put anything in the tub area, i.e. full size shampoo, conditioner, etc. The refrigerator worked well as did the nice sized flat screen tv. The bed was huge and very comfy; we both slept very well and the room was very quiet despite the building work and renovations being done. We had no problems with wi-fi, which was fortunate since you have to pay by the minute to use the internet in the hotel business center. The A/C worked really well too.
Location was great; I felt it was a very safe neighborhood and centrally located to the attractions we wanted to visit. The concierge was friendly and helpful in directing us as well. Getting to the subway was an easy walk and there were a lot of close by places to eat and buy stuff that we needed unexpectedly.
Breakfast was pleasant; there was a nicely appointed dining area that was large and well maintained. There was an array of hot and cold items that was plentiful, plus Belgian wafflemakers were available. We had a very early start to go take the train at Penn Station but breakfast was ready and waiting! Check-out went smoothy as well.
I would definitely be willing to stay here again the next time I'm in NYC; the reasonable prices, great location, amenities and proximity to Penn Station make it a great value!

title: “Phenomenal”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 6 days and they "wow'ed" me at every turn. The staff was extremely helpful and friendly. My wife got lost coming to the hotel and they stayed on the phone with her for 25 minutes and directed her right to the front door. The room were especially clean and the free parking is a huge plus in an expensive city like Philadelphia. I highly recommend this hotel if you are going to be in the Philadelphia area.

title: “Great location and friendly staff”
text:
The Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf wasn't the cheapest option but we had stayed with the Sheraton brand before and have never been let down by the service or standard they provided. On arrival to the hotel we were happy to see that there was a good atmosphere around the hotel, it was busy but not in a cramped way, and the quirky interior gave the lobby a bright and inviting feel. Check-in was very quick and easy and were very happy with our room. 
The beds are incredibly comfy and the room whilst not large is big enough. The hotels location is what sealed the deal for us, its incredibly close to the boardwalk and pier, it's about a 5-10 walk to pier 39 but you don't really notice it if i'm honest because of the atmosphere and lively nature of the area. 
We never ate in the hotel so I can't comment on that but within a stones throw from the lobby there are a number of restaurants, whether it be fast-food chains such as subway, johnny rockets and mcdonalds or classier restaurants serving fresh seafood.
One of the best things about this hotel was the fire pits situated outside the lobby, we LOVED them, they were warm and it was a nice place just to sit outside with a coffee or play some cards with the family. 
Whilst at the Sheraton the staff were all very friendly, especially the doormen who i must give a special shout-out to as they were very kind and funny, even giving us umbrellas when they saw it was raining outside (which it did a lot :)
There was a decent size pool however, it was too cold for us to use it in february although we did see a few brave people enter in :D
Overall, not the cheapest option in San Francisco but as always Sheraton delivers.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
This hotel was excellent. The hotel is located right on the Red Line subway, dont even have to cross the street to get to the station either. The rooms are very clean and neat. 
Check-in was simple and quick. We had 2 beds, and they are very comfortable, i saw a post about having adjustable mattress so it can be firmer or softer but it was set just right when i was there. There was a pool in the hotel, but i didn't go to it. 
Parking was a bit expensive, $41 for self park in the hotel parking garage, or $49 for valet (both for a 24hour period).

title: “A hotel to return to in San Francisco, CA”
text: The location is perfect for the business man or the leisure traveler with walking distance to Union Square or a one block pickup on a historical trolley. The staff will remember you and the rooms make you feel right at home. You will return to this hotel.

title: “Pure elegance and attention to detail!”
text: After having stayed at many of the finer hotels in NYC, the St. Regis was a welcomed surprise. Everything from the beautifully appointed suite, to the butler who seemed to guess our every whim, to the fabulous afternoon tea - this hotel was by far the most luxurious stay that I've had in the city. I can't say enough about it and can't wait to go back and be pampered again!

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: Finally a hotel that lives up to its rating! Beautiful hotel on a quiet street steps away from Rittenhouse Square. The service was excellent, the room while tiny was just lovely. Great breakfast downstairs in the morning. We will be back for sure.

title: “Service Level is going down”
text:
My family has stayed at the trump hotel four times this year. Our Room varies from a Deluxe King to a Suite, depending on our needs. The reason why we keep coming to this hotel is because of the service, and if your service is no different from any other Hotel why bother coming back? My husband planned a birthday celebration for me with the Trump Hotel, he requested very simple things we thought the Hotel could accomodate. Upon Arrival when I checked in I had problems because the front desk thought my name was not on the Hotel reservations with my husband. Which I had to call him out of his meeting and let the hotel get his approval so I can check-in. Second issue, when I checked in the room there was no birthday welcome package, no WII which was requested during the time of reservation. Third issue, my husband ask them to bring cupcakes to my room he dropped off at the hotel, of course they took a very long time to do this. He had to keep calling the hotel to make sure they were getting things done in a timely manner. I understand hotels are busy, but if you are overwhelmed and can't accomodate your guests, maybe hire more staff...As the night went on, I requested the WII in my room, which was suppose to be there when I checked in, took them an hour to bring one up. The final thing, My husband and I were out to dinner and we called Valet to let them know we will need to take our car, and when we arrived 20min later at the hotel, our car was still not ready, and we were late to our next event. I also noticed they have stopped putting the box of chocolates on your bed. 
I expect these things to happen at other hotels, but not ones that consider themselves luxury hotels and rave about their service.
Trump do better, You are not the only Luxury Hotel in Chicago.
Mr. and Mrs. Wright

title: “Rooms are very old and dirty”
text:
At first glance the hotel is nice looking. My company booked this hotel so I didn't have a choice. After talking with some colleagues they had said their rooms were nice enough but a few had bad opinions of the room quality. I had to take pictures for them to believe it.
Cons.
The paint was peeling off of the ceiling. The wall paper was peeling off and was stained in places. The door jam has been painted multiple times and was peeling in spots. There was something disgusting stuck in the textured wall paper in the bathroom. The caulk in the shower was stained and looked to be installed by a 5 year old. the screws in the vent in the shower were falling out. The vanity was scraped and very worn. The light switch had dirt/dust lodged inside of it.
Pros.
The bed was comfortable and the water pressure in the shower was very good.

title: “The Absolute WORST Place I have ever stayed”
text:
OK, just for the record, I wrote a review of the Travelodge in Grants Pass Oregon and I am pretty sure in that review I referenced the fact that it was the SECOND worst hotel I have ever been subjected to stay at.
Well....say hello to number one! This was the skankiest, nastiest hotel I have ever had to stay in...and to make matters worse, I was there with my husband on our HONEYMOON! We must have been in a state of pre-marital delerium when we booked this one!
The room was a filthy dirty den of cooties, bedding was torn and soiled, and there was a tiny sink bolted to the wall. Yes, a sink. There was no toilet or shower in the room....no, you have to walk down the hall to use those amenities...and share them with every street derelict who happens to be crashing on the second floor with you.
The whole place stunk like bad curry. I think the hotel manager and his entire extended family lived on the first floor, and did nothing but cook up pots of wicked smelling devil-curry 24-7. We could not escape the stench! Well, I take that back...sometimes the pervading odor of B.O. in the hallways helped drown it out.
After two nights (we had booked ourselves for five nights), we couldn't stomach it anymore, and ended up hightailing it out of there and heading to the bowels of Chinatown for a hotel upgrade.
Oh, and one more thing...the "continental breakfast" that was supposed to be included with the room consisted of one box of butterhorns per day put out early in the morning (there were maybe 12 danish per box). When they were gone, that was the end of breakfast...you snooze, you loose.
We did not think any of our friends or family would believe us when we came back home and tried to tell them exactly how gut wrenching this place was, so we actually used our video camera to record the levels of filth that were present in this room.
Anyway, this is a great place for people who enjoy playing the game: "guess what made THAT stain", and spending time contemplating what might scurry out of the sink drain once the lights are turned out. If this describes you, you'll really dig this place.

title: “Great location”
text: stayed at the mil broadway for four nights and had a great time. minutes from times square and close to all amenities. stayed on the 34th floor and had an amazing view. wasn't too happy with the cleaning staff not changing the sheets everyday, but oh well. overall if you get a deal, like we did from travelzoo it is worth it.

title: “Was fine, not as bad as other reviews.”
text: Stayed there one night, 3/22. Place is very nice on the outside. Room was great. Nice all around. Staff was good. Location is great, in La Jolla. Had a room next to kids that were a little noisy early in the night but they got quiet after going to bed. What you gonna do about other people's kid anyways? Not anyone's fault, no big deal. Wasn't too pricey when bookin online, would definitely recommend it.

title: “The Menger Hotel Day Spa-A Must!”
text:
My boyfriend and I went on a small get away from Houston, and traveled to San Antonio. Though we did not stay at The Menger we did stay at the sister hotel (The Crockett). We were able to use the facilities at The Menger (pool, work out room, and spa). The hotel is absolutly beautiful, grand, and clean. I did have to ask a staff member where to go for the spa, and she was friendly and willing to help.
 I wanted to do something romantic with my bf (oogling over each other over a bottle wine is not our thing) so we booked a couples massage at The Menger's spa. It is conveniently located in the basement of the hotel down a small spiral stair case. It smelled so nice inside. The staff was so friendly, and the massages were the best ever! Even better than one I had in Las Vegas. We were treated to a steam before our massage, and we even got to pick a scented oil. My massage therapist really took care of me. I had the sniffles, and she brought me lavender to smell which helped my sinuses open. I really recommend this. I looked and looked, and the prices are very reasonable. It was 180 for a couples massage (we tipped each therapist a 20 on top of that), from start to finish I say we were there about 2 hrs...maybe 1 45 min. It was more than just a massage, but a true romantic and relaxing experience. Other than the massage and steam, we were given a small intimate room to shower and change after the steam. Smells incredible, low/no light, romantic music, friendly staff! I recommend, this is a hidden gem in the SA.

title: “You don't need a black light to see the uncleanliness”
text: I reserved a room here because my usual choice was booked due to Anime Convention and X games being held in the area at the same time. First room, had dried soap scum on the sink and visible stains and crud on the ice bucket. I asked for a room change only to find that the room didn't have luggage racks and my stuff would have to go on the floor. I used a black light and it glowed in the dark (no exaggeration). The floor, where my luggage was to be placed, had dust and hair in every corner, fridge and ice bucket were covered in glowing material. I didn't bother checking the bed, I called Best Western and had them cancel my reservation without charges. Checking in, unloading, moving rooms, checking out and reloading the car within an hour took its toll on me, physically, and left me with a cough for the remainder of my vacation.

title: “Great Rooms”
text: The rooms at the Westin are very relaxing and clean. The new LCD TVs mounted on the walls really transport you to another level of comfort. The only downside would be the $40+ for valet per night. When I asked the Bell Man said there were no other places to park, your out of luck.

title: “Chaos that is booking in”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights in June and was amazed at how disorganised things were... It took 45minutes to check in and the queue behind us was growing. A great first impression!
When we got to our floor, my heart sank, as I saw the state of the corridors and doors (very grimey). We entered the room to find the bathroom, whilst broadly clean, had been fitted decades ago. The rest of the room was reasonable but lacked maintenance and genuine cleanliness.
In summary, the location was fantastic, the lobby looked good, the room had just about been kept clean but I would NOT recomend this hotel.

title: “Good Stay”
text: We stayed in Milenorth just when they changed owner in June from Affinia to Milenorth. Our room was clean, spatious with a good view on the skycrapers around. Nothing to complain about. Good receptionnist, clerk very nice and helpful at the lobby.. Good breakfast. Quite expensive but a very good stay at the level of our visit of this fantastic town, Chicago

title: “Great Value Location, Accommodating Staff”
text: I was here with a group of 70 high school studant. There is not mauc in way of ammenities but there is a continental plus breakfast. The staff was extremely accomodating, rooms were updated and very clean but they are small. Location is excellent if you are trying to stay in the middle of lower Manhattan (couth of Central Park).

title: “Nice spot, awesome staff”
text: Nice spot close to Southcenter mall, and a 20/25 minute drive to Safeco Field. Not too far from on ramps to I-405 and to I-5 Room was very clean, place was quiet. Internet service was good, breakfast was what you expect at Homewood, but maintained a bit better than most. Parking is more than adequate. Hotel backs up to a trail system. Staff at check in was fantastic. The gentleman on duty when I arrived was abou the best I have ever encountered. .

title: “Booked before I read the reviews.”
text: The reviews are true. We had to wait 15 mins for the Elevator and the stairs are twice as long due to the high old fashioned high ceilings. After being told twice by people that it was too full I had to push my way in. There was a woman who was terrified that the elevator cables would break even though there was room so that's why they told me "no room in this elevator". Only stay there if you get a smokin deal and you are young and going to the Gaslamp to party. Valet was a joke...I think they had to call the valet from some other property to deal with the cars so you are going to wait. Mixed reviews on the staff. The hotel is in a great location which was the saving grace but I would not return. If you can afford it stay at the Prava or the Courtyard which are a block away. FYI, I paid $150+tax+$15 valet on a Saturday. Ouch.

title: “Beautiful!”
text: I had a great stay hhere! Beautiful rooms and greets staff. Great nightlifenin this hotel too. Non smoking rooms, which make it tough for me but it's ok, ! This was a great place, would love to stay again!

title: “A good stay (apart from the Jazz!)”
text:
This was a stop on a 1500 mile roadtrip that we had.
The hotel was clean and the staff very friendly.
The breakfast was not included in the room rate and so I paid for this at the point of booking - however when we arrived it became apparent that the rate I paid "online" was more than that being charged in the hotel.
Drinks at the bar were exceptionally expensive - even by city standards (and with a 20% resident discount).
The hotel is quite some way out from the city and there is no free shuttle bus service, which is a shame.
However, the hotel was clean and comfortable and a good place to rest weary feet!
Be aware that the hotel pipes jazz throughout the public areas morning, noon and night - great if you like jazz, not so great if you don't!

title: “An Organic Delight”
text: Rooms were sleek, clean and environmentally responsible. Staff were friendly especially the valets. The food, appetizers and wine selection were fantastic along with the guide to environmentally conscious shopping/eating. Never a bad steer. The only improvement could be the continental breakfast which was somewhat uninteresting, bland and non-organic.

title: “Small, loud room”
text:
I stayed at the Marriott at Renaissance Center as part of a 4-day conference. Being a solo female traveler, I felt a little uneasy in the circular hallway leading to my room. You can't see more than 15 feet in front of you or behind you because of the constant curve of the walls. It seems like it would be easy to be surprised by someone and at the same time difficult to get help from others. The only other thing I noticed as I walked down the hallway was some sort of loud hum that grew to a roar by the time I reached my room. Right across the hallway was what must have been the loudest (and oldest) ice machine on earth. (Later that night I woke up and thought a freight train was going by before realizing it was the ice machine's motor kicking on. Seriously.) My room was quite small and very shabby--the cushion on the chair (which was awkwardly stuffed between one of the beds and the wall) was almost flat and looked dingy. The bathroom had nice granite countertops, but the room was so small that you had to back into a corner to shut the door and access the shower. The towels were grayish. And my shower curtain had what I really hope was shampoo splattered on it.
Now for the good: Beautiful view of the river, bridge, and Canada from the room and throughout the hotel. Lots of convenient restaurants and entertainment right in the Ren Center. Friendly staff. Clean rooms (other than that shower curtain).
One final note: On my last night, my key card stopped working. I called from the hallway of my floor, and the front desk was very prompt in sending someone up to help me get into my room. The man who helped me was very nice, but after I thanked him for his help he said, "Ma'am, when you shut the door, be sure to use your deadbolt AND privacy lock, OK?" I found the statement a little unsettling. Was it because they've had problems with people trying to break into rooms? Did it have something to do with my key card? Was it just a note of caution for a woman staying alone? Once again, I wished the hallways weren't circular and that the stupid ice machine in the hallway wasn't loud enough to drown out a commotion.

title: “Good location; RvrWalk & Alamo; comfortable stay (business trip).”
text: Very satisfactory hotel; I had no complaints. Great walking location for my 1st trip to SA. Did not realise how good my hotel deal was (free parking, breakfast, including to-go bags) until I came home and read reviews of other nearby hotels (high prices, pay-to-park etc). Great location for Riverwalk and Alamo. You won't need a car (but the parking is free).

title: “Great location, but a disappointing hotel”
text:
We chose this hotel primarily based on TripAdvisor reviews, so we had mixed expectations. Unfortunately we were severely disappointed.
About a month before we were due to arrive in NYC, we contacted the hotel to a) confirm and b) make the full payment. It took three separate emails to the hotel to get a reply, and once we did get the initial reply, it took a further three or four emails to confirm that they would charge the credit card before we arrived. We waited and waited, sent some more emails, and the credit card was still not charged. This was not a good start. I actually received a reply a week before we were due to arrive, to the FIRST email I sent about three and a half weeks earlier. My friend's credit card was charged about half way through our stay, even though she had not approved it. Upon check out we were told not to bother asking for a refund on that card because it would be too much trouble. 
After this initial let down, our expectations were not high. The size of the room did not bother us too much, as long as it could fit three suitcases and (many) shopping bags, we weren't too fussed. However, it was the state of the room that disappointed us. It was run down; dirty and marked walls, peeling ceilings and lots of cracked tiles in the bathroom. 
The heating was also EXTREMELY loud, to the point where it woke us up during the night with banging and clanging. It got the point where we didn't even turn it on. However the heating did drown out the noise of the people in the room next to us. I woke up during the night thinking that there were people opening our door and coming into our room - that's how thin the walls were. 
Also, don't bother buying the wifi, there are free wireless spots all over the city. This was the only hotel we had to pay for wifi, and like others have commented, I find a bit strange considering all the other hotels we stayed in across the USA provided free (and fast) wifi. 
On a positive note, the location was great as first time tourists to NYC. I wouldn't stay in this location next time, but it was fine for what we wanted. Also the concierge (mainly Robert) was fantastic, gave us some great tips for restaurants and bars. There is a fantastic Thai restaurant nearby called Yum Yum Two, which is on the end of restaurant row on W 46th St. AMAZING food, better than the food we've eaten in Thailand!!!

title: “Loved the Fairmont!!!”
text:
My husband, six year old daughter, and I stayed at The Fairmont from April 6th-April 8th. We had a spacious, L-shaped suite with plenty of room for a big rollaway for our daughter. It was clean, well taken care of during our stay, and very reasonably priced.
The concierge and staff were more than helpful and friendly..We had two lovely breakfasts at their restaurant, Juniper. My daughter enjoyed the pool and overall it was a lovely experience there. We would definitely go back to the Fairmont when visiting D.C. again.

title: “Great Hotel at an Immaculate Price”
text:
My best friend and I stayed here the week after Thanksgiving (11/28 to 12/1). It was a last minute trip to NYC and we were lucky to find this place at at great price directly through the hotel's webiste ($135/night). You can't beat the price, especially for the location of this hotel. We were very close to several subways, 2 blocks from Madison Square Garden, about 5 blocks from the world's largest Macy's, and about a mile from Time Square. The walk to Time Square isn't bad at all. 
The service was great. We arrived at the hotel 4 hours before check-in. I didn't think a room would be available to us but it was. The rooms are small but enough for the two of us. Plus, it was ok for us since we didn't stay much in the hotel - mainly just to sleep and get ready. The bed and pillows were comfy. The heater/airconditioning worked great. The bathroom had marble countertops and tile flooring. The decor was very modern. The bellhop helped us with directions, restaurants recommendation, subways lines to take, etc.
The continental breakfast was excellent. It was much better than the standard continental breakfast. It inlcuded sticky buns, donuts, bagels, bread, english muffins, fruit, yogurt and an array of cereals. That's not it - it also include hot breakfast items such as scrambled eggs, sausage links/patties, french toast sticks, hash browns, and pancakes. I couldn't believe it. 
There is also a fitness and business center located on the lower level. We used the business center quite a bit to find info about areas to see during our stay in NYC and of course to check email. 
I would definitely come back to this hotel and recommend it to others. I would rather walk the distance to Times Square than pay $400-$500/night in that area.

title: “Nice view...”
text:
I found this to be an average hotel - check in not overly-friendly, concierge very friendly, the room was large (nice office area with large desk and working space), great view of the river, and average amenities. 
Great location for walking around the city and seeing the sites. 
Breakfast was very good in the cafe. Room service was "ok"...nothing special. Probably would stay somewhere else next time.

title: “Wonderful Stay!”
text:
Our stay at the JW Marriott in Cherry Creek was truly wonderful. The room was
quite nice, clean and spacious and I was impressed by the details of everything from
room service, restaurant and car services. Being in such a lovely location made it a great
getaway and easy access to shopping or just window shopping at all of the very nice boutiques.

title: “Amazing view and Bar!”
text:
Even though I live in Seattle, I have stayed at this hotel twice. I spent both nights after having too much fun with friends :)
The bar is very cool and cozy. It's facing the Sound and on the Sound!
Staff were really friendly and hotel has been consistenly clean on both night I stay here.
Overall, it's one of the best hotels I have stayed in Seattle.

title: “Awesome value for money”
text:
