This hotel is near perfection considering low price by Manhattan standards. Rooms are fair size, bed was comfortable, bathrooms are bigger than other hotels we have stayed at in NYC and breakfast was a good way to start the day. Drink prices are steep on roof top patio but spectacular view!
We will be back.

title: “Very upscale, at a reasonable price!”
text: I stayed over the weekend for a business trip--what a treat to relax in a mini-apartment after an exhausting workday! The hotel is very upscale, modern, and clean. Close to the airport, Easton shopping and dining, and only a short hop to the interstate. Buffet breakfast was good, offering cooked-to-order omelettes in addition to the buffet. Rooms are spacious, nicely appointed, and quiet. The price is quite reasonable for this quality, and the size of the suite. I've stayed in lots of ordinary hotel rooms at this rate, so it's well worth it.

title: “Great Value for a great hotel!”
text:
I have to admit I was a little skeptical booking this hotel based on some of the negative reviews. I was in town for a week long business trip and was looking for an affordable nice hotel. The great thing about this hotel was I didn't have to rent a car my entire stay. The shuttle picked me up from the airport for free and took me to the hotel, it was only about a 15 minute drive. The staff was great there, the doorman Mohammed was very helpful and always pleasant. The rooms were great, loved the bed, soooo comfortable. The whole hotel and rooms are very modern and look recently updated with flat screen tv's in the lobby and in all the rooms. 
The food at the hotel is decent, although I only ate there a couple of times as there are so many great restaurants nearby. Across the street there is Wal-Mart, Panera, McDonalds, IHOP and more that are very easy to walk to or the hotel will take you. Just 5 minutes away, is a fantastic shopping area, like an outdoor mall. There is plenty of shopping to keep you busy along with great bars and restaurants. My favorite was Ling & Louie's, they have a great happy hour! The hotel will take you and pick you up from that area. There is even a movie theater close by.
I use to live in Denver, so I am familiar with the different areas, this is a great business hotel. I can't tell you how many times I have traveled for business to be stuck with nothing around me eating hotel food all week and watching tv. This was a pleasant surprise!

title: “Clean, tidy, great location!”
text: The rooms are small but who spends a whole day there when your in new York.. The hotel is clean, the service is great, wifi is awesome. A little street noise but nothing headphones can't fix. A little wait on elevators but it didn't bother us. Street is a little suss at night but in general great location! Check in and out was fast. No dramas. Great hotel.

title: “Hidden charges, charge for internet even though advertised as free”
text:
Overall we were happy with our stay except for a view problems. The first problem was out 3rd night when someone's car alarm kept going off. It must of went off 4 times after 10pm and lasted 1 minutes each time. I called and complained to the front desk and after about 2 hours they dicovered that someone from the nearby Motel 6 had parked their car in the Ramada lot because they thought that it would be safer. 
My other complaint is the fact that there are hidden charges on the bill. My wife and I left without reviewing the bill. Once we were able to look at it I discovered that they charges us $1.75 a day for the in room safe and $2.50 for telecom charges. They charge you this every day that you stay. We had booked through Ramada.com and we're told about these hidden charges. I called the Hotel and got no where with them and then called Ramada's 1-800 number. They filed a case number and said that the hotel's owner would get a fax and call me about the complaint. I think that they should be up front about these charges. The web site advertises free wireless internet in the rooms and I was under the impression that if you don't use the phone that they don't charge you for it. Hiding all of these charges is how they can show a lower rate per night.

title: “Minutes away from ALL attractions, afordable, comfortable beds, and modern rooms.”
text: We stayed three nights here, very close (under ten minutes) from beaches, Sea World, and SD zoo. We stayed in a standard double queen, very affordable, beat the prices of all other hotels within the same area. The rooms were very clean, new carpet, all new modern furniture with granite counter tops in the vanity, bedside table, and TV stand. Brand new fridge, stainless steal microwave. The beds were comfortable (pillow top) as advertised. Hot water, which is always a must, decent size rooms.

title: “Perfect hotel for a weekend getaway”
text:
We stayed at the hotel for three nights during the May (Canadian) long weekend. First and foremost, we don't think our stay would have been the same without the recommendations of the wonderful concierge, TK. We had some restaurants and activities in mind when we arrived. TK advised against a few restaurants and suggested Sable and Prosecco - both were amazing. Sable had American cuisine appetizer style. It was a great choice for Friday especially since we were dining late after our 9 hour drive. Highlight: duck fat fries and lobster rolls. Prosecco was a romantic Italian restaurant with a great atmosphere. We had the duck prosciutto, lamb, gnocchi, and tiramisu. All highly recommended - gnocchi was the least favorite. Out of the activities our favourite was the Architectural boat cruise - also a TK recommendation. 
The hotel itself was very nice. The shower had good force, which isn't usually the case in hotels. Bed was comfortable and rooms were very large and cozy. We stayed on points an were upgraded to he next room level which is always a nice touch. We at breakfast at the hotel restaurant twice. Food and service were fantastic. The best part about the hotel was te complementary Acura service - saved us a tonne in cab fare, and not a bad way to travel (provide water an wet wipes inside as well)

title: “Dissapointed.”
text: A bath couldn't be filled with water in my room because a plug didn't work. It is very relacxing time for me to take a bath. Called and asked the front desk, there was no apology with insincere talk. It was very dissapointing. Can I stay 4 more nights here?

title: “Great Value $269 Weekend Internet Rate”
text:
We stayed at the Sofitel Saturday and Sunday, March 3rd and 4th. I checked on-line at the Sofitel website and booked us an “Internet Special” rate of $269/night. Rates at many other 4-star + hotels were $400 - $600, so things were looking pretty good. 
The purpose of the trip was to spend some quality time together and have some fun, so I didn’t want to start our weekend with a dirty, stinky cab ride to the hotel. I “googled” airport transfer services and settled on Jet Black Limousine Service, based on the quality of their website, www.jetblackonline.net , their pricing and their fleet of Mercedes and BMW’s. Tony met us in baggage claim and drove us from LGA to the Sofitel in a beautiful sparkling Mercedes S Class, black & black car. Bottled water or other beverages are also included and pre-requested on the website. Pricing was $65, plus a bunch of NYC fees/taxes and a 20% driver gratuity, ending up at $98.96 total. A taxi is approximately $35, so the Mercedes transfer was a special treat.
Now, about the Sofitel: 
1. We received a complimentary upgrade from our Internet special $269 rate for a queen bed room to a king bed room, upper floor, #2203. 
2. Next to us, rooms 2201 & 2202 are at the end of the hallway, with a door that closes off the end of the hallway. So by closing the hallway door; you would have a small private locking foyer between the two adjoining, across the hall rooms. This would be perfect for a family who didn’t need connecting rooms, but adjoining rooms (across the hall) with a private foyer. So, if that’s the case for you, with older teenagers, or elderly parents, inquire about rooms ending in 01 and 02.
3. The guest room was beautiful, as mentioned by many previous reviews. The only amenity that I would like to see in the future would be a plasma/LCD with high-definition signal feed.
4. We enjoyed two breakfasts at Gaby’s, the hotel’s only restaurant & bar. The food and service was excellent. Continental breakfast was $18, and the full American breakfast was $21. Classic Eggs Benedict was also $21. Juice and coffee are included in that price, and the coffee is served tableside in a “French Press”, and was very robust, which we, and I’m sure the French guests, appreciate.
5. The Lobby isn’t large, but sufficient, with about 5 or 6 gathering areas for small groups to congregate before heading out. There is also a small room off the lobby with a couple of computers for you to check your emails or flight status.
6. From the hotel, it’s just a couple of blocks to Times Square, the Broadway theatres and Fifth Avenue shopping. It’s a $10 cab ride to the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
7. We had dinner at the Russian Tea Room and Trattoria Depo Teatra, and I posted reviews for those two restaurants. 
For the price, $269/night, for a weekend stay, The Sofitel is an excellent choice for a New York City weekend getaway. I hope that this review and the pictures have been helpful.

title: “Great View”
text: This place is great I'm a local and decided to stay here for a night out of town. Great location and room decor was cool. Didn't really interact with the staff besides the initial c/in process. They are right across the street from Petco Park and have a bar facing the stadium.

title: “would go back”
text: The room was clean and comfortable and looked like the pictures on their website. The view depends on the room you book. We only stayed one night and didn't get a bay view room. If we went back again I would get a better view, as it makes a difference.

title: “awesome”
text:
just got back from another business trip to nyc.... going to nyc at least twice a month... it was my first time at the edison... Located in the heart of time square...subway station,restaurents,stores ... everything is close by... the hotel itself is a bit old...but the rooms are verry clean... customer service is exelent... i got there at 7am...and they gave me a room right away even if the check in is at 3pm...no extra charge...
there was NO BED BUGS.
this hotel is a great value for your money if you whant a good product with a great location for a small budget... 
im going back to nyc this week end and i booked 1 night at the edison again...and since i stayed there a week ago the reservation agent i spoke with gace me 10% off... i didnt ask for but its always apreciated..

title: “More Than I Expected”
text: other places looked at staying were The W, the ritz carlton, radison, the hilton. Upon arrival, i was greeted on a first name basis, they had been expecting me. my flight arrived very early, and the room wasnt supposed to be ready until checkin time. i was put into a room 5 hours earlier than was supposed to be, and more importantly, i was given a room which i had requested but was undecided about, since this was a very important date, valentines day, this was a deal breaker. the room was big, very nice and comfortable queen size bed, very clean, had amnenties that most other uber expensive hotels did not offer, bathroom in all black slate, with flosted glass, ie huge tub, big shower room. the staff was friendly and was a great help on the dining suggestion given. upon leaving i was helped in keeping my bags, longer than the check out, as how my flight was delayed. the price was great, and i believe what i paid was far less than i should have. 2 night stay was 560, and given other stays around the world, i loved it, already have a stay booked for july 4th wkend, it helps i received an offer for complementary stay.

title: “Fantastic”
text: My wife and I absolutely loved our stay at the Orchard Hotel. It is tastefully decorated and very comfortable throughout. The use of high quality materials made us feel like we were in a much more expensive hotel. Where other hotels use "hotel grade" furniture and decorations, the Orchard uses quality items that you would want to have in your own home. Our room with a good size, had a large bathroom and a well stocked bar. We also loved the complementary breakfast in the morning. There was good coffee, a choice of juice, fresh fruit salad, cereal, yogurt, scones, and other bakery items. It was the best free breakfast I've had a hotel. The doorman was very helpful and friendly, as were the people front desk. There is also a complimentary DVD movie library with plenty of selections. And the movie was great on the Sony home theatre system and Trinitron TV in our room. I think the only down side to our stay was that our room had a view of an alley, but that wasn't enough to change our opinion of the Orchard. I am definitely staying there the next time I go to San Francisco and I have recommended it to many others.

title: “Surprisingly nice”
text:
Very nice Hampton hotel for the price in the area! Clean well maintained. Outstanding service. Definitely worth the money, close to seaworld.
You'll get an upgrade to a bigger room if you are an hhonors member.

title: “Comfortable, quiet, close to Universal”
text:
Very comfprtable, everything clean and updated. Stayed in a King Suite - great decor for a Holiday Inn. The only reason you know its a Holiday Inn is the sign, everything else says boutique hotel.
Good buffet breakfast, free shuttle to Universal. Staff helped us with a few problems and went above and beyond to be sure we were more than happy.

title: “Fairly nice hotel, but don't expect much”
text:
I stayed here mid-week in order to do some business nearby. I chose this based on my past history with the Best Western chain, which has generally been good.
When I went to check in, the person at the front desk didn't seem to want to move away from her laptop and surfing the web in order to check me in. Even after checking me in (signing, initialing, giving my car information), she proceeded to hand me my key and turn back to her laptop. I had to actually ask her what my room number was!
Along with other reviewers on this site, I was somewhat amazed to find that you went outside to get to the elevator or stairs, and it dumped you into an 'interior' hallway! The 'interior' hallway was cold, and the decor was dated, but it was clean and smelled fresh.
The room (I was in 115) was interesting to say the least. It had a king size bed and a fold-out couch, but there was no room to fold out the couch! There was a coffee table, a chair, the desk chair, and the desk all shoehorned into the side of the room, and it was impossible to open the couch (not that I needed it, though).
The desk was nice sized.. there was a 2008-9 edition of the Best Western directory in it, which seemed a bit weird. The Wireless was only mediocre, and very slow. I wonder if she was using most of the bandwidth at the front desk.
The bed was very comfortable, which surprised me. There weren't enough pillows, and I was told that there weren't any more... there was no bedding for the fold-out couch either. I guess they took the '1 guest' literally and took out the rest of the bedding and towels!
The decor was very dated -- but the room was comfortable. The alarm clock being on top of the TV was a bit weird as well. But the room did include a TV (non-LCD), a DVD player, a refrigerator, a microwave, a coffee pot, and -surprise- a whirlpool tub. (I didn't have time to partake of it, but it looked well kept up.).
I don't know if I'd stay here again, as it was a bit out of the way from my work location, but it was a nice stay.

title: “Adequate Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Marriot in Sept. The staff was wonderful. We even were able to get early checkin. The housekeeping was good. No problems with getting the room cleaned. The beds were comfortable. The hotel is located on the cable car line. We could just hop on and take the cable car to Beale street. We would stay here again.

title: “Loved the Governor's House!!”
text:
My husband and I just returned from a long week-end in Washington DC, where we stayed at the Governor's House. We had a fabulous experience from the time we stepped into the hotel. We had an early flight, and arrived at the hotel around 10:30. Because they had a room available, they let us go ahead and check in. After a full day of sightseeing, we returned to the hotel for a drink in the bar, and a wonderful meal in the newly remodeled restaurant. We had the best salmon we have ever eaten. The new chef is a gem, as are the waitstaff and bartenders!
Our room was clean and comfortable, and also very quiet. The construction on the new part of the building did not bother us at all noise wise. We plan to return to Washington in the future, and will definately stay at the Governor's House again and again! Thanks for making this a week-end to remember.

title: “great”
text:
We booked the Wellington for a trip in March 2006.It was our first time in New York and wanted a central hotel.After reading all the negative reviews on trip adviser we were slightly worried but decided that we wouldn't be at the hotel much,and prefered to spend the extra money on shopping/eating than upgrading hotel!!
We were pleasently suprised.The staff were great especially the doormen who more than happy to help,book taxis etc.
We requsted a corner room as advised on a web-site,this was honoured to my husbands delight(who spent every evening watching out the window!)
The location was FANTASTIC.We spent 5 days on foot.
Yes I admit that it was slightly shabby and dated.BUT,everything worked,it was clean,and for the money and time we spent in the room it was all we needed.
We are considering booking another trip to New york and we are hoping to book the Wellington again.
If you want a cheap,basic hotel with a good location then the Wellington is great.

title: “Over-rated”
text: Shabby furniture, (the armoire looked as though it had been dragged behind a truck, and the chair had a rip/cut in it), stains on the carpet, and wallpaper peeling in the bathroom were the first things I noticed. The hotel staff were polite/curteous, but not exactly friendly. Hotel fitness center requested an extra $10/day to use their treadmills and basic machine weights. Overall, a decent hotel, but not worth the price. They seem to be relying on their location (across from Central Park) as a selling point to keep the business coming in.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
I don't undertand the negative reviews of this hotel on here.
I brought my mother to New York for her 72nd birthday in April/May this year, and we had 2 standard rooms for 4 nights. I booked through Expedia and got flights and the hotel for less than booking Virgin Atlantic flights only direct! Both rooms were very large with 2 huge king size beds in each room. The beds were the most comfortable I have had in a hotel. We were in rooms 2604 and 2606. We had views of the river from the huge picture windows. The rooms were spotless - as was the whole hotel. Amazing for Manhattan given how grubby the city is! The housekeeping was excellent - cleaned daily with fresh fluffy towels and toiletries renewed daily. The rooms were incredibly quiet - not a sound at night. There was a flat screen TV, free tea and coffee maker replenished daily. A real hairdryer, shaving mirror, and an ironing board and iron were provided automatically in the rooms. And this was in a 'standard' rooms! I personally wouldn't bother worrying about an upgrade or 'view' because there are views from the lounge, restaurant and bar, and New York is all around you! Having said that our view of the river was beautiful and at night everything was lit up and we could see the boats on the river. For New York it was exceptional value.
Location was brilliant - a short stroll from Times Square and the Hop on Hop off Tour buses were right outside. It was so central yet so quiet and relaxing - even though there was a large conference group staying.
We had breakfast daily from the amazing buffet - all anyone could need. The restaurant was new and spotless with great views of Times Square. We had dinner one evening in the hotel. The food was the best we had during our stay. Portions huge and delicious, and a 3 course meal with service was 90 dollars for 2 - great value. The starter Tuscan soup was enough for a whole meal! I had grilled prawns in garlic then steak with frites. Lovely. The bar overlooked Times Square and was lovely and good value. 
The hotel was a calm quiet haven from the city and we loved it. The staff were extremely helpful and friendly. We called up an engineer one evening as my key didn't work - it was sorted out in a jiffy. There was internet access in the room, but that was 9 dollars per day - whereas there was also an internet room in the lobby with several computers and printing facilities and access was free for 20 minutes for hotel guests.
Security is outstanding. They have guards at night by the elevators and you have to show your key card to get in. This was a great relief to me as my mother is 72 and it was her first time in New York. We didn't worry one jot about security. 
As I say I don't understand the negative reviews on here. I went into the Marriott Marquis and it was no where near as clean and new. Other 'brand' hotels - Sheraton and Hilton were not as well located and not as spotless as the Crowne Plaza. The CP is newly refurbished, spotlessly clean and the staff work hard and are extremely friendly and courteous. We had no problems whatsoever. Check out was super fast and my bill spot on. I was so pleased with my choice as it was such a special occasion. The check in even said happy birthday to my mother and hoped she would have a lovely stay. My mother loved it at the Crowne Plaza and thought it was wonderful. When others on here say there are better alternatives in the area they don't say what - and I certainly never saw any. Location, cleanliness, staff - all top notch. Even the staff at the Marriott looked a bit grubby. The staff at the CP were all in uniform and so helpful. The concierge provided advice and guidance on tours etc. and were so pleasnat and helpful. I would rate the hotel nearly 5 star. It was outstanding and I would definitely return and recommend. I can't speak highly enough of the hotel and staff.

title: “The reports are true - Cassablanca is #1”
text:
Best service, beautiful little hotel, location is AMAZING. 
This was a return trip for us. And we will be back.

title: “Rooms are okay. The lobby is cool and...”
text: Rooms are okay. The lobby is cool and comfie. Very convenient to Reagan International via yellow line and 1 block from the convention center. There is an AWESOME gym on floor 3. Wireless signal throughout hotel was not great. All in all, a fine place to stay.

title: “Great business meeting”
text: Our company had its annual awards party at the Hard Rock last week. It was so much fun I hope we go back next year. We had a very large audio-visual production associated with the event and the staff was able to handle everything without a hitch. It was like being at the Oscars! But the best part was the food. The quality and selection were top-notch, and the event staff took great care of us. My wife and I have decided to go back after the holidays for a weekend in San Diego. I love that city.

title: “Downtown Gem”
text:
My girlfriend and I took a quick weekend trip to Dallas to catch up with friends and catch a Stars hockey game. We wound up staying at the Joule and were blown away. The service was top notch from the minute we pulled up front and were greeted by the valet. We were in a hurry to get over to the American Airlines Center, as the hockey game was just about to start as soon as we got into town, so after we quickly dropped off our bags, we took advantage of the Joule's courtesy driver and were quickly chauffeured there in time to see the puck drop. It was a nice day so we opted to walk back after the game as it's only about a mile away.
The room was stayed in was very chic yet amazingly comfortable. High end details throughout the room and a very comfortable bed. My girlfriend got a chance to enjoy a soak in the jacuzzi bathtub, but I, being over 6'4, was partial to the rain shower head in the shower which I could stand (upright) under WITH ROOM TO SPARE (this rarely happens for me). Checkout was a breeze and we got a couple of complementary waters for the road as well as some of their hand lotion which the girlfriend was addicted to by the time we left. For our next stay we need to remember to bring swimwear so we can take advantage of the rooftop pool and poolside bar, which looked like it had a fun vibe to it. Next time we're in Dallas we'll definitely be staying at Joule again.

title: “Decent”
text: This is located very conveniently close to the bay and Qunicy market. The T stops right by at the aquarium. Rooms were a good size with a huge bathroom. Well stocked toiletries and spares. No view from room as looked into central atrium. Little bit dark but then its just a place to sleep so that works ok. You can get free tea and coffee in the lobby but there is no breakfast or bar. So this is literally just a place to lay your hat while you're in the woderful city of Boston. Some building work going on in the lobby while we were there but this wasn't intrusive. Staff friendly and polite.

title: “Great value and great location”
text: This is a really nice hotel in a great area, within an easy walk of the Metra (public transport) and a bit longer walk to the downtown if you're up for it. The staff was very helpful, the room was nice with a great view and the housekeeping staff does its job well (if a wee bit early). I would absolutely recommend this hotel to anyone. One word of caution: the hotel restaurant's breakfast is not included -- some of the materials seem to indicate that it is, and one poor elderly gentleman in the restaurant got into an argument with a server when she presented him with a bill. You can get a better breakfast nearby at any number of great restaurants and coffee shops either in Dupont Circle or in the Adams-Morgan area to the north.

title: “Nice Stay”
text: I have stayed in NYC many times at the Mercer (5 star), the Gansevoort (4 star), the Hudson (3 star) and now the Amsterdam Court. I can honestly say that there is not much of a difference between them other than the price point and a few SLIGHTLY more luxurious details. The Amsterdam Court is a good value for the money, is clean, comfortable and has an excellent and helpful staff. The location is great for tourists as well. It's not worth spending the extra $$$ to stay at a more expensive hotel when the size and amenities will be more or less the same so I recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Fine facility if you have to stay downtown, but weak on service”
text: I stayed here recently for several nights. We had to change dinner plans one night on very short notice, and the very young desk staff (early 20s) couldn't recommend a single "fine dining" restaurant. Also, a call to housekeeping regarding a lost item reached voicemail, and my message wasn't returned. I was also surprised that the hotel charges $10 a day for wireless access. The facility was fine, but we learned that staying in downtown Phoenix is not a good idea, since there's no central area in which to walk around, and the whole town shuts down around 9 PM.

title: “Wonderful boutique hotel”
text:
The Library Hotel's location is perfect--just a short walk to Grand Central Terminal, where I could take the subway or make connections. The hotel is in easy walking distance of many New York attractions. Since I was traveling alone, I wanted a hotel that was in a good, safe location. Because of the hotel's proximity to the subway system, I never took a cab during my stay. I was able to walk or to use the subways to get everywhere I needed to go (including many different areas of Manhattan, the Bronx, and Queens).
I stayed in a petite room, and I was booked into 800.003, the poetry room (just as I'd requested). The room was very comfortable and quiet. I enjoyed returning to the room each night to find turn-down service. The hotel staff were friendly and accommodating. 
The second floor lounge was a wonderful place to sit and read, and the foods offered throughout the day were plentiful. At breakfast, the offerings typically included several different cereals, eggs, fruit, various types of bagels, croissants, pastries, and assorted muffins. Beverages included coffee (plain, espresso, cappucino), tea (numerous types), milk, and juice. Throughout the day (including late night), one could enjoy cookies, pastries, coffee, tea, water, and lemonade. In the evenings, the staff served wine (white, red, and sparkling), assorted cheeses, crackers, breads, and mixed nuts.
Madison & Vine--the restaurant on the ground floor--offers room service to guests at the Library Hotel.
I have recommended this hotel to several of my friends since I returned from New York. I love the small size of the hotel and the truly luxurious touches. Since I am an English teacher, I regretted not having more time to be in my room to read the books of poetry there!

title: “Fine all the way around”
text: The Meridien is our hotel of choice in NYC. The combination of location, amenities, food and workout/spa is decisive. Service is smooth and discreet, as well.

title: “Fantastic top notch property”
text: Brought two soccer teams here to stay for the weekend for a tournament. The hotel staff was outstanding from minute one and never once dropped the ball. Had stayed here once before and had a good experience so chose this hotel again for that reason. The property is beautiful, kept immaculately clean and very well appointed. The staff is outstanding and the level of service is better than many larger or competitor properties that I have stayed in. Rooms are comfortable, have microwaves, refrigerators and coffee in the rooms. Nice fitness center and even a guest laundry. Good location and easy access to the highway and the businesses in the area. I will stay here again and again anytime I am in the area.

title: “Top Notch Service!!”
text:
I had heard about the service at Hotel Commonwealth, but you have to stay there to really believe it. We wentfor the bedtime story event and to spend a night "staycation" with the kids in town, they had a blast. The service was phenomenal and best of all, genuine. I have seen "forced" customer service, this was not. I travel a lot for business, i was impressed with how the kids were treated (respecful, and with the goal of letting them have fun). The events were well run, from the check in packae for the kids, milk and cookies, the bedtime story through to the pancake breakfast, this was one of the best hotel packages we have have ever seen. The wine and cheese for the adults was a nice touch, along with the champagne at check in. The slippers were a huge hit!
Very well done....we will be back and we will tell everyone!

title: “loved this friendly well located hotel!”
text: This was a first time stay at this hotel and I very much enjoyed the facility, the reasonable rates that don't fluctuate from day to day,the friendly staff and all the ammenities offered. I would return, or reccomend this to anyone wishing a center city location, with indoor discounted parking nearby. They have a great breakfast buffet and leave it out till !0:30 on weekdays. Free movie channels, comp e-mail computers and other things I did not get to use, like the fitness center. It was very clean and a felt very safe walking around at night. There were restaurants in every direction and they gave a list of different suggestions for each meal. Try it, you'll like it too! Miami Guy!

title: “Never AGAIN”
text:
The rooms in this hotel does not look like anything on their website. Its like a totally different hotel,,,, Only booked this hotel as it was the only one left available the weekend we were there now I can see why. Our room was tiny and a very odd long shape. Not much air got into the room so it was very hot and that was September cant imagine how you would survive during the summer months with only a fan.... Unless you dont mind the heat you will end up melting in your room..... Great location for all the shops and malls the hotel is literally surrounded by them. Weather was really nice during the day but got very chilly at night so beware.. There was also a lot of homeless people on the streets but once you told them no or gave them some change they didnt bother you at all. Even with all the homeless about it still felt really safe. 
Pier 39 is only a short taxi ride away and worth the trip also did Alcatraz which was amazing.

title: “Excellent stay in New Yorks Yotel Hotel”
text: Excellent hotel to stay in New York for the money! Free coffee and muffins are great in the mornings! Really clean rooms and modern hotel that is about a 10 minute walk to Times Square. Would highly recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to New York!

title: “A little bit of Paris in Philadelphia”
text: Excellent hotel -- high quality, friendly service, great location, good value. Excellent sleeping accommodations. With a free upgrade to a junior suite, the room was spacious and useful for small business meetings. Lots of world travelers here.

title: “As always a fantastic stay”
text:
This is the third time i've stayed at the Tribeca Grand and the only reason i keep returning is because i know i can relax and am guaranteed flawless service.
NY is famous for its hotels - i've sampled quite a few of them, many in a higher price range. This one tops them all every time in terms of ease and convenience.
Its not the most beautiful, but you're sure to be met by polite, friendly staff who have your preferences recorded from previous stays. Check in is as easy as presenting your credit card, and from that point on nobody bothers you unless you request something, in which case it will be dealt with promptly and professionally with no mistakes.
This particular trip i spent the first half of the week at the St Regis because it had been booked for me by family who were also staying there. Once my family left the city i couldn't WAIT to check out and head back to Tribeca. The contrast was noteable - the one had uppity staff who made a long trail of errors (how is that even possible in 3 days?), and checking into the Tribeca Grand was a breath of fresh air.
Cannot recommend it highly enough. And who expected such good service from somewhere so cool?! Try it - you will not be disappointed.

title: “They make you feel like it's home”
text: Senadra & Michael work the front desk and they always take very good care of me. They are both extremely pleasant and accommodating. Bradley and Ray are the bellboys they see to all my needs when checking in and out, in addition to daily occuerences. I always have a clean and comfortable bed and room. The block the Hotel is located on, is a bit scary but once I get to the front door I feel safe and secure, but who wouldn't with the big and strong security they have there. I am overall pleased with this hotel and would highly recommend it.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: Just got back from a 4 day stay in NYC with my 13 year old daughter. I spent a lot of time researching on trip advisor and because of that decided on this hotel. I was not disappointed. We arrived at the hotel at 1 pm and they gave us a room right away. The room was spacious, clean and well stocked. People have said that the lower floors were noisy but we were on the 3rd floor and didn't hear a thing. I loved facing 8th Ave and being able to open the windows to the NYC hustle and bustle. The staff of this hotel is great. Larry the concierge was exceptional, providing us with itinerary advice, directions and dinner suggestions and reservations. We didn't try the restaurant attached to the hotel as there were so many other options. We will definitely return to this hotel.

title: “super staff and hotel”
text: The staff at the Omni need to be congratulated for such friendly and efficient service. Always welcoming you with a smile, chatting with you and going that extra mile to ensure you leave thinking "I wasnt just another guest". If I had to suggest anything to the hotel staff I would say upgrade the lifts, they can be a bit slow during busy times in the morning or evening.

title: “A charming really great hotel”
text: The front desk makes your feel welcome as soon as you walk in the door especially Neal he is very helpful with directions etc.The valet is very fast and the hotel is clean the house keepers are very good.The breakfast is the standard free breakfast but has fresh squeezed orange juice and grapefruit juice.I rented a car from Enterprise 2 blocks away they picked me up.I was here on business for 14 days.But you can walk to many restaurants or shopping or sightseeing.I am a Hilton Diamond and Marriott rewards member but this hotel is just as good for less money.

title: “Very noisy room”
text:
We stay at a lot of hotels and this room has to be one of the noisiest ever. You can hear every foot step of the room upstairs. There was a 1/2 inch gap under the door(Room 117) and a 1/4 inch gap on the handle side of the door. So not only does more noise come through, but a very cold breeze because they leave the building door open all night long. Needless to say, I didn't get much sleep.
The bed is OK, workout room is good and the breakfast had plenty of choices. However, we wouldn't return again.

title: “Convenient Location”
text:
I have stayed at the hotel from the 26th of October to the 2nd of November right trough hurricane Sandy.
We had a very nice stay, friendly staff and good location, close to the subway and main tourist hotspots. The room was clean and comfortable maybe not the biggest room on earth but spacious enough for a family of four and two suitcases. We didn't spend much time in the room as we were always out to enjoy the amazing city of New York. Our room was on the 4th floor which made easy for us to use the lift. The few times we did use the lift we didn’t encounter any problem. Breakfast is nice and free, the selection of food could be improved in order not to be the same everyday.
On our last day we didn’t have any arrangement in place to get to the airport, but the hotel concierge arranged everything for us and we treated ourselves to a limo ride.
I am a flight attendant and I use hotels quite often and I can easily say that this hotel is good value for money especially if you are looking for a good location and a nice place to sleep.

title: “Nice hotel but a couple of annoyances”
text:
When I was assigned this hotel, I was a little nervous since i have read some pretty bad things about it on several websites.
However, I have to say that it was nothing like that. It certainly wasn't a Hilton, but it was still definetly nice.
The room was very cozy. It had nice colors and it had a decent sized desk with a bookshelf. For the laptop on that desk there was free wireless with actually a great signal. The bathroom was definetly on the small side but it was designed very efficiently. Finally, I loved the free bottled water that they provided.
On the negative side, the bed was rather uncomfortable. We both woke up many times in the night. Also, the TV was placed in a very strange place and it was difficult to see it from the bed. 
Also, the vending machines were all the way on the 12th floor and one of the nights one of the elevators stopped working.

title: “Cool nights”
text: Great location. Very convenient to China Town. Shopping is abundant and within easy walking distance. Locals will give great dining ops and some of the best in Chinba Town are not the fanciest. Rooms are a good size with comfy beds. Breakfast is a plus to start the day. Coffee is complimentary. Really did not need a car as location was good for walking and finding transportation as well as being so centrally located. I would stay here again and are planning a trip in the Fall. I was surprised how cool the nights were in June.Very chilly and I packed mostly summer type clothes. I imagine a Fall trip will require a coat. Love the area!

title: “Big in a word”
text: I do agree witha few posts regarding the rooms being a little tardy. But I have to say, if you can see past that, it has a lot going for it. The bed was very comfortable, and the room huge. The staff were very friendly, and the location was great for me, with most business meetings being within walking distance. Nice pool and functional gym. We also got a great deal regarding room rate, which is why I have rated the hotel very good and not average. Value for money, I think you would be hard pushed to match, especially with the facilities available.

title: “Great hotel near airport”
text:
Stayed here for a convention. Despite it being a bit far from downtown Phila, getting to the hotel was not a problem. Initially before arrival, I called the hotel and asked the how far they were from the Eastwick station of the SEPTA (I was coming from NYC via Amtrak and connecting to SEPTA) and the woman told me it was around the corner and a short walk away. Upon getting off at Eastwick, I was pretty much left in the middle of no where. The hotel is about a 20 minute walk from the station and you have to pass multiple lanes of a busy street as well as under a freeway with no walkway connecting one side. Luckily I had Google maps on my side and upon getting to the front desk, they told me the following...
Catch the shuttle from the airport -- no apologies or anything. Anyway, like I said, if you're trying to get to this hotel, just take the SEPTA to the airport and follow the signs for ground transportation to get the shuttle.
Anyway, about the hotel. It's your common Four Points. Friendly staff and great rooms. Breakfast was a bit overpriced and there is free coffee in the lobby. Despite it taking 45 minutes to refill at one point, I had no issues. There aren't many options for dinner nearby so we just went to the Sheraton which is in the same complex. The complex consists of 3 hotels. There is only free wifi in the lobby with free WIRED internet in the rooms. If you're lucky enough to pickup the wifi from the lobby, you are golden.
Other than that, for a quick stay, you will have no problems here.

title: “The Wellington Experience”
text: Wow.... was this hotel a let down. Don't think you are getting the room on their web page. This is a very old hotel and the rooms are living proof. First night there AC problems. The maint staff changed out 3 different used AC units in a 2.5 hour time period. The last one they changed out was the first one they took out (we marked it). So the night was not very comfortable at all. Then there came the plumbing issue. It was taken care of, it took another hour. I know what you are thinking....why didn't we change rooms, beleive me we asked. No can do, no rooms in the hotel.The manager on duty was not helful or was he concerned at all with our comfort. We spent a total of $334.00 for one night! Hey another thing, check out the mattress before you jump in one of their beds, you will find springs poking through and nasty stains.The mold on the wall by the AC was just down right unacceptable. This hotel is need of major renovation!

title: “Will definitely stay here again”
text: Great hotel. Sylvia at front desk was outstanding. We stayed here for 3 nights (July 2012) for our 40th wedding anniversary. Sylvia sent a lovely dessert tray to our room congratulating us. We were able to get a mini fridge in our room at no charge. Clean rooms, helpful staff and location, location, location! Nice east side location without all the "mob scene" 24/7 of Times Square - 10 minute walk to Fifth Avenue and an easy 20 minutes to Times Square. Right next door is a drugstore, Duane Reade, that is open 24 hours for beer, soda, bandaids etc.!! Also one block up on 52nd St between Lexington and Third Ave are all kinds of quick places for lunch - Potbellys, Chipotle, Subway etc. We had a wonderful stay here and will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Location and nice hotel.”
text: the hotel is in a great location, near harbor and Orioles stadium. A little pricey but high quality hotel.

title: “No services nearby"”
text: Great room at a good price. Was shocked to learn that there were no stores or restaurants open in the area. was informed that the hotel is in a business park and that the restaurants close on weekends! Was a little noisy as there was a Little League competition in the area and all the teams seemed to be staying here!

title: “Such a dump- room made me cry :-(”
text:
I cried when i got to our room. We complained and were given an upgrade but it really put a damper on our trip.
The room was dirty dingy smelled of damp and the bathroom-eughh!!
I was impressed by the photos of the grand lobby thats why i booked- nice surprise for my boyfriend-NOT!!
The upgraded room was bigger and cleaner but still in desperate need of a make over. The hotel owners need to spend their money on rooms not fancy marble(which was lovely in the lobby by the way!)
I didnt spend a minute longer than we had to in the hotel and it was a real let down.
The "candid photos" taken by other travellers in the hotel were exactly what we faced. Horrible.
It was about £120 a night for 2 people and you can get a much nicer place elsewhere in New york so unless you are guarenteed a newly decorated room- do not go there!!

title: “Lock up your valuables”
text: Hotel was ok. Small room. View of a parking garage. Icing on the cake was when I got back from a cubs game to find my iPad missing from my room. No signs of forced entry. The manager eventually got around to checking the locks the next day. ' the only people in your room were supposed to be there' was the response i got... Needless to say they have serious staffing issues. And theft problems that they do not seem very concerned about. For the price it cost to replace my stolen property, I could have stayed at the ritz. Absolutely Ridiculous! Do yourself a favor and stay somewhere else.

title: “Great Seattle Hotel”
text:
The Maxwell was a great find for us. I usually stay in Bell Town and The Maxwell is only a 10 min walk to Bell Town for food but without all the noise and vagrants. 
The staff here was awesome, especially the housekeeping staff. I really liked the decor and feel of the hotel and liked they didn't nickle and dime you on everything. They provided complimentary water, coffee, wifi, and parking which was really great considering all the other hotels were charging outrages prices for parking. 
We were attending a concert at the arena, and the location was perfect. It was right across the street so we were able to have a few drinks and walk over and not have to deal with traffic. The food at the restaurant located in the hotel was pretty good too as far as hotel food. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Value, Great Accommodations”
text:
We stayed for one night (a Saturday) to check out the hotel. We were recommending it for our out of town wedding guests, and wanted to make sure it was OK.
We stayed on the first floor, and were able to park outside of our bedroom window. This property is set up "motel style", so your room opens to the outside instead of an interior hallway. We found this to be convenient, and we felt very safe at the hotel. It is in a quiet area, although close to the SR51 freeway, and is surrounded by small office buildings.
I was pleased to find that the rooms were updated, clean, and modern. We had two flat screen TVs in our room, granite countertops, etc. I was pleasantly surprised, because I felt that this was more like a 3 1/2 star hotel vs. the 2 1/2 stars it is rated.
My only complaint about the room is that the shower was a little wonky, and we could hear our upstairs neighbors clear as day through the walls/ceilings. I think the hotel is older and not as soundproofed as newer properties.
We took advantage of the free happy hour, and had two sodas and a glass of wine. It was a pleasant way to unwind at the end of the day. The lobby is nicely decorated, and has a fireplace. The breakfast/happy hour area is small and basic.
We really enjoyed the breakfast in the morning - there were plenty of options, and the hot foods were great.
Overall, I think this is a fantastic value, and we had a pleasant stay.
Friends who ended up staying here for our wedding raved about the hotel, and were extremely pleased with their experiences as well.

title: “Great hotel, in the right place at the right price!”
text:
We stayed here for one night on Jan 2, 2012. I booked the hotel after much debate after reading mixed reviews on TripAdvisor, Google, and other travel sites. However, for a price of $102 for a Deluxe King Room, I couldn't argue. Our room was on a corner of the building and was sizeable. The linens were fresh, the bed seemed fairly new, the carpet was plush and everything was really clean. They even had a sizable LCD TV, with actual HDTV. Most places you go have the LCD TVs, but regular standard def. Anyway, the room was perfect for what we needed, a place to relax in the evening and get a nice night of sleep. I didn't encounter any issues with the thermostat, I simply lowered the temperature to 68 and it was perfect. I could even cut off the heating/cooling unit, had we gotten too hot or cold, so those complaints from other reviewers are unfounded. 
Complaints about the bathroom are valid, it was pretty small. Barely enough room for the shower, toilet and sink. However, being a guy I don't have an issue with it, as I shower, or use the sink and toilet and get out, and don't plan on spending hours at a time in front of a mirror. For that, it was adequate. Also you should remember that this hotel was built in the 1920s, so its historic and things may be small. 
In the end, this hotel is a great spot to spend a few nights. Its got a great location, its relatively cheap, and its easily a 4 star hotel. Is it 5 star? Definitely not on account of the bathroom. I feel like some people may be a bit picky on this site and expect a Ritz Carlton. The fact is, the price is much lower than many other hotels in the area, so any 'issues' you may run across are compensated for. Also, the complaints about $12.50/day for wifi are valid, BUT you have to remember EVERY other hotel in Boston, as well as most chains - Marriott, Hilton, Ritz Carlton, charge that amount or more for wi-fi. Its a way for hotels to make money. Back in the 80s-90s they made it off of phone calls, but now with cell phones they have to make up for it somewhere. If you don't like it, go to a Starbucks, McDonalds or get a smart phone like the rest of the country.

title: “Not that great and not that bad...”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights in late January of this year. We booked on www.expedia.ca for a rate of $120 CAD/night.
+ve: great service from front desk and housekeeping staff. spacious room and clean bathroom.
-ve: bed was not that comfortable plus there was a few stain on the duvet cover, air conditioning was very noisy, but worst of all are the tight parking area (we had to park elsewhere twice) and the fact that there is no elevator (we had to carry our heavy luggages upstairs!
Overall, the surrounding area is not that great. It was quite dirty and noisy. If I visit Hollywood again, I would fork a bit more cash to stay at the nearby 4 star hotel. 
Tip:
Check out the yummy Thai restaurants in Thai town, which is very close to there.

title: “Great staff, great accomodations”
text: We spent a weekend at the Eventi while visiting our daughter. We were welcomed by a friendly, accomodating staff who arranged for our luggage to be stored due to an early arrival. Once we were checked in later, we found a sleek, European style hotel room (a bit small which is usual for NYC) with robes and slippers, flat screen TV, and all other amenities. The glass enclosed shower was convenient and clean. The hotel also boasts a spa, fitness center, restaurant and bar, and a veranda which looked spectacular, but which was closed due to cold weather. Complimentary wine was available from 5-6pm. The hotel is pet friendly, and was populated with a myriad of dogs (many of which we expected were pets of families displaced by Hurricane Sandy). All staff members greeted us warmly. We felt like welcomed guests. It is a bit pricey, however. We were fortunate to get a deal through a discount website. Check it out!

title: “Great Service at the Westin Bonaventure”
text: I stayed at the Westin Bonaventure recently during a very busy weekend. The staff was incredible, and went above and beyond for us. When we called down for an additional blanket, it was sent up immediately, we had at least two of the hotel employees that stopped by the room during our stay to ask if there was anything that they could do to make us more comfortable. I will definitley stay there again. The rooms are cozy, but very beautiful. The only problem I encountered during by stay was that the sausage at breakfast wasnt hot, other than that...they get 5 stars from me!

title: “Great hotel!!!!”
text:
Loved it!!!
 Clean, comfy,spacious,relatively close to dining, shopping, etc.; yet not so close to Times Square, Central Park, etc. Otherwise, no hidden fees, no over-billing, no problems.
 The noise from the construction at Ground Zero was not insupportable either, they did offer earplugs and told us that we could request what they called a "sleep machine" were we to have trouble sleeping. As one can imagine, after an entire day of sightseeing,who needs earplugs? 
 We were really fascinated by their extremely fast elevators: they go from the lobby level to the 43th floor,where our room was located, in the blink of an eye. The way they just fly between floors is awesome!
 The only minor complaint we have was the fact that in the room adjacent to ours, a.k.a that shared an in- room door, there was someone who really enjoyed watching loud TV past 12 am...situation that of course,created some tension between us, as one of us felt like calling the front desk and informing them of the situation.
 Otherwise, we wouldn't doubt staying at this hotel again.
 On a personal note, we were really sad to see the Towers gone...which of course won't last long as they are very busy rebuilding them.

title: “Terrible Service, Understaffed and Not Clean - but Good Location”
text:
We stayed at the hotel for 5 nights for an event for our kids. Consistently throughout our stay, the service was poor:
1. The room never had enough shower towels, and on at least one occasion when I ordered additional towels they never arrived.
2. They have only one car valet at a time, and i had to wait several times for quite a while to get my car pulled up and on at least occasion they forgot or missed that I had called ahead to have it pulled up, so I had to wait. 
3. The room supplies were NEVER replenished - anything you use does NOT get replaced - no toilet paper replaced, no pen or paper replaced, and no card for breakfast the next morning(that you leave on your door) was replaced - ever, every night. . 
4. Our bed sheets this afternoon, after coming back to the room, appear to have been replaced with stained sheets. The towels once had a yellow stain. 
5. A room service meal was also wrong (forgot a dish) and some of it was inedible. 
6. Lastly, the hotel was admittedly full of younger guests, but it was INCREDIBLY loud until very late at night. The walls and doors are paper thin. Moreover, when the partying next door went until after 2 AM (and our kids had an event at 7 AM the next morning) and I called downstairs to ask them to intervene, they apologized and sent security once. When it continued for an additional two hours and I called downstairs again, but they never sent anyone again. If it recurred the next night, I was going to call the police. It was that bad. I understand from other guests at our same event that they too had to call security, and it did nothing.
If I come to San Jose again, I will never stay at this hotel. It has a good location for the Convention Center, but other than that, you would get better service at a $16 night hotel.

title: “this place should be condemed”
text: My sister and I and some of her friends wanted a weekend in New York as their annual trip. We took the advise from one of the girls in the group as to where to stay for less money and we were sooooo wrong. When we got thier the people were rude short with my sister who made the reservations. We got to our rooms and they were on seperate floors, it looked like the building had not been cleaned or updated since it was built and I found a map in our room that said the hotel dixie so you know that they don't go through the rooms very well. our room was cleaner then the other girls room but we had a revolting bathroom and the coax cable for the tv was broken the tv was unplugged and all the outlets looked like a fire hazard from the turn of the century. The other girls room had a nicer bathroom but the toilet was behind the door and was not only hard to get to but the door did not close all the way. They had a nice whole in the celling with mold and falling plaster. We we arrived we saw one of the bell boys drinking out of a paper bag. We left the second day but didn't get any of our money back.

title: “Great location excellent service!”
text: We really enjoyed staying at the here. The rooms have a nautical theme; squid wallpaper and sea glass accents. The friendliest staff we've encountered. Fun fact#1: the only hotel in San Francisco that allows pets. The bellman was giving squeaky toys and dog cookies out when we arrived. The hotel is very clean, so don't let that worry you. The location is a few blocks from Pier 39, and a very easy walk. The onsite restaurant, The Blue Mermaid, won best chowder in San Francisco; they'll give you a voucher for a free cup. There is a free wine gathering in the lobby in the evening, which was a nice way to rest up after a long day of sightseeing.

title: “Pleasant, inexpensive stay in a great city!”
text:
Our stay at the Mount Vernon was very pleasant. We parked right around the corner from the hotel on the street. The front desk staff were friendly. The room wasn't anything special, but totally acceptable. The breakfast in the morning was great. 
Overall, we felt very lucky to get this room for $100/night on the weekend of the Preakness when everything else was sold out or at least $300/night in Inner Harbor. We just took a 10-minute cab to the Inner Harbor.
Our stay was great and we would do it again!

title: “Home away from Home”
text:
My family of 4, which includes 6 ft. twin16 year old boys, had a great time at the Wingate. It was walking distance from Penn station where we arrived and departed from Newark. It was walking distance to Times Square where we boarded our Viator hop-on/hop-off buses daily. But the hotel was just far enough away from the "madness" on a quiet street in the garment district.
The room on the 17th floor was clean, nicely decorated and large enough to accommodate us and our 4 suitcases. I did exhausting searches on line, viewing many hotels, their various room sizes and amenities. By far the Wingate was the best location,comfort and value for our family budget.
The beds were very comfortable and room service was great. We always had clean towels and tidy beds when we arrived home each night. 
The buffet/make-your-own breakfast was very good and became our morning routine while we discussed our plans for the day. My only suggestion would be to have more staff in the dining area and create a nicer "oasis" outside on the patio with more flowers, plants, garden art and umbrellas for the rain. 
All of the staff were friendly and helpful. Overall it was a great experience.

title: “Great location. Great service. Great shower. Good price.”
text:
I wasn't expecting much from the Holiday Inn but was very pleasantly surprised. Very friendly service from all staff. Excellent location in the heart of downtown. Nice clean, simple room with a great shower and fantastic view. Comfy bed. Good wifi. All for $180. Pretty good deal i reckon.
Only complaint was lack of safe in room. Otherwise highly recommended.

title: “Marriott safe bet for comfortable stay”
text: We stayed 4 nights at Marriott Suites and had booked the Romance package. Good value for money and room was fine plenty of room for just the two of us. We should have been given vouchers for breakfast but did not find out until after first day but quickly sorted by hotel. Staff were efficient and friendly. Would benefit by upgrading TV/Hi Fi but minor point. Also used the Hotel shuttle in the evenings to go out to eat which was great as we could enjoy a drink. Johnny Ray was our driver every night and just trust his recommendations, he took us to some great places at different costs and ensured we either jumped the queues or got complimentary appetisers/desserts!! Downtown was only 5 - 10 minutes drive and we found parking during the day easy to find and cheap. We also stayed for a night later in the week at Embassy Suites Love Field and Rennaissance which just confirmed what good value the Marriott Suites was, best of the lot.

title: “Stroppy staff”
text:
Having just stayed at the hotel, our overriding memory was of rude, unhelpful staff, many who could barely speak a word of english. We also found the staff at the restaurant extremely rude, refusing to provide room service for breakfast for anything under $10, (even though it was $8.50 and they charge $3 room service charge!!)) - room service should mean ROOM service, and you would have to order a whole lot of breakfast to get over $10 every day. Pointless. 
We were also very surprised after a sleepless first night that the rooms that front onto 10th Ave do not have double glazing (it felt like you were sleeping on the street with the noise) which ensued a room change after having another stroppy conversation with reception. 
The heating in the hotel is also a joke, the room heaters, even when off, blow out hot air, wont blow out cold air, so the rooms get too hot at night and you cant have the window open because of the noise, hence more sleepless nights. 
Whilst the rooms were clean and the hotel generally acceptable, it is the staff that make your stay a pleasant one. I will therefore choose to take my custom elsewhere next time I am in NY.

title: “Great Value”
text: Great value and good service at this historic downtown hotel. I would stay at the Magnolia Dallas again.

title: “Great stay for work and play”
text: This was a great stay during my birthday weekend and then for work the rest of the week. Everything was crisp and clean. The housekeeping was great in respecting my privacy as well as having everything fresh. This hotel was a perfect distance from universal and staying away from the spotlight. Definitely will stay again.

title: “Don't Forget the Saturday Night Earplugs”
text:
This was our second (and last) stay at the Club Quarters in Philadelphia. 
On the plus side, the rooms were perfectly functional, the location is good, and the room rate was competitive.
On the minus side, the noise levels were simply not acceptable. We are not prudish, and we did not get back to our room until after 1 am. Unfortunately, from our second story window, it looks like a lot of other people got to bed after us. 
From 1 until about 2 we got to listen to drunks pour out of a bar a block over. From 2 until about 3 we got to listen to bars unload/smash their glass bottles into the dumpster directly below our window! This did not make for a restful sleep.
When we checked out, the front desk asked if we enjoyed our stay. I mentioned the noise. Her reply, "Well, you didn't call us to complain about it." Gee - another possible reply would be "we are so sorry this disturbed your trip, we will look into it and try to make it better for guests in the future."
Oh well, we plan to vote with our feet next time.

title: “Quirky, Hip and Very Nice”
text:
This is not your typical chain hotel. Very hip and trendy furnishings from the unusual sit down with an agent front desk to the trendy quality room furnishings. 
The Amalfi was very clean, bright and warm. The hallways were bright and well lit. The room was large with quality furniture, a big comfortable bed complimented with plush bedding. The pillows were comfortable. 
The bathroom was also very large with marble vanity and a large shower with great water pressure. 
The breakfast was unusual in that they set it up on each and every floor instead of a room on the ground level. The food offered was nothing special, your typical continental fare. 
The free wireless internet was fast and reliable throughout my stay. 
This place is a winner and i'd happily return.

title: “Amazing Value/Close to Airport!”
text:
This hotel was super and had an amazing price. It's also almost brand new and the rooms smelled like new. I loved how close this hotel was located to the airport, however, it was not close to anything and the shuttle will NOT take you anywhere else other than the airport. The taxi's weren't too expensive if you wanna grab dinner in Plainfield. I think I paid $10 to get to the local Buffalo Wild Wings Restaurant. I also run everywhere I travel and this hotel wasn't near any of the amazing trails and runs that Indy has to offer.I used to live in Indy and knew that I was going to be kinda in the middle of nowhere. However, I did find a great little almost abandon road near the hotel and got my run in! 
The hotel was everything you expect from a Hilton Garden Inn, and as a gold member I was treated great! I received my waters and the desk has complimentary cookies! The staff was super friendly. As a matter of fact they were very friendly and maybe some of the best front desk staff I have seen in a while and I travel a lot. I was pleased with the room. The hotel was clean and definitely served it's purpose. If traveling for business or just passing through, this hotel is for you. If you want to see Indy, then try downtown at the Embassy Suites, it's also amazing and you'll be in the middle of it all.

title: “One of the better Four Points if you're keeping track”
text: I requested an early check in and was able to book a "Starpicks" rate online that I thought was an excellent value. They were accom at the front desk even though it was very early and I didn't really care about the Starwood VIP floor unavailability. The room was clean and I had no issues with street noise or getting to and from LAX. And as a final note, how refreshing not to see "Fixed" (Fox) news on the channel selection. GOOD CHOICE!

title: “We stayed in a sute with a 14 month old and it was amazing!!”
text: I can't say enough about this place. The people were nice, the breakfast was good, the room was goregous and the room was very quiet.

title: “Great Budget Hotel”
text:
Stayed at the Wellington Hotel from 21 April through to 25 April 2005.
A work colleague recommended this hotel to me - and what a recommendation!
I requested a high level room and was given a room on the 26th Floor (27 in total) overlooking Central Park. The room was average size and fairly basic but very clean and certainly sufficient for a nice break.
Would like to have tried out the diner attached to the hotel however you had to get in there quick as it was a very popular place but due to the great location, there was no end of alternative diners, restaurants etc. to visit without having to venture too far. Hotel also in the next block to Broadway and subway right outside the door.
All staff at the hotel were very helpful and the gift shop allows you to pre-book taxi transfers back to JFK, Newark and La Guardia as well as offering opportunities to book various sightseeing tours. 
In addition, as checking out time is midday, they have a facility whereby you are issued with a voucher free of charge to store luggage if you have a late afternoon or evening flight.
The Wellington charges very reasonable rates considering its superb location and I would definately stay here again when I return to New York.

title: “What fun!”
text: The pets are welcome policy makes a friendly clientele. The staff is kind, helpful, and gracious. We arrived without a pet, and were offered a goldfish to cheer the room. Love it! The decor was unusual and pleasing, a place with a difference (besides the dogs!) Happy Hour was attended by canine and human guests, and again, the dogs made conversation with strangers easy. Breakfast the next morning was delicious with good service. Comfortable bed, nice linens, dog dishes and pad on floor...all made for a relaxing and good stay.

title: “Amazing hotel amazing staff”
text: Well what can i say but thank you all at chelsea inn for making our first trip to new york so much better. From moment me and my fiance arrived they were curteous, helpfull, friendly etc . Cant wait for next trip and will stay in chelsea inn .will recomend to friends and family also. We were bit sceptical about shared bathroom but it was never a problem and was also clean.thanks chelsea inn from michael and gemma

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We had a great stay at Hotel George in Washington, DC. Great location.....friendly staff......and great rooms.

title: “Complete Dump, Don't waste your money”
text: I will never stay here again. No clock, iron and ironing board stolen, not all the lights worked. Mildew on shower curtain, parking lot was full of broken beer bottles in the parking spaces, stayed here for 2 days and no one cleaned up the mess. You are suppose to use a keycard to gain access into the halls from the parking lot. That was disabled. Anyone could walk off the street and walk right in. I felt very unsafe as I was traveling without my husband but had my youngest daughter with me. Towels were a joke. My daughter and I had to share a towel. We only had a half of a roll of toilet paper. The next day when housekeeping came in and made the bed, the did not give us more toilet paper. I didn't feel safe to even walk upto the front desk. There was no internet connect in our room. The tv only had 9 channels and 2 were fuzzy. The refrigerator didn't work. We plugged it in for 2 days and the light came on and never got cold. No phone book, which I needed. Cable Wires hanging all over the outside of the building. Our room was missing 3 outlet covers, I was expecting an electric fire. I'm really upset I didn't get the chance to take photos of this dump. This was definitely not even worth $44.00 a night. I had asked my daughter if she would rather sleep in the car. For our trip next year, I wrote a list of nice hotels which were next door as I will never stay here again. Creepy, gross, filthy and truck drivers wondering around the parking lot to go to the Male Bar next door. Never again. Don't waste your money.

title: “Really wanted to like but was disappointed a little”
text:
This hotel is not your average smelly, small roomed hotel room. The decor was cool and fresh but the cleanliness was something else.
The service is really good as far as the politeness and immediate response to issues.
I stayed in a 3rd floor room with the Kind size bed. I entered the room and noticed the fan was on in the bathroom. The whole weekend their was a smell from the shower. I used flip flops. 
The nice hardwood floor was not swept and as you can see from the pictures there was coffee grounds, hair and dirt. There were also some sugar ants. I found a dirty hand towel and a ladies bathing suit shield (when you buy a new bathing suit they have that to keep the swimsuit clean) in the closet on the floor. The white comforter on the bed had two stains (see pics) and the cow hide long bolt I took off because it had stains and did not want that near my head. 
I did call down to the front desk and they sent a housekeeper to bring me a new comforter but why did she take the old one off and leave the new one on the chair? 
They did also offer to change my room but I was already unpacked. They sent someone to sweep but they didn't get all of the dirt in the corners. A maintenance man came to spray around the base boards. 
The room was nice and open and airy and their is adequate parking. The front desk told me upon check-in that there would be a $13.00 charge per overnight. I read the rolodex information of the hotel in my room and it said $10. I inquired of this with the front desk and they adjusted my rate. Read your information and it works in your favor.
Also the Aveda products they say they have were only two small bars of soap. The one bottle of shampoo was by Breck. Sad.
I would give this hotel another shot but I was disappointed with this stay.

title: “Very nice!”
text: We are just back from a 4 night stay at the Courtyard. We took the Bart from SFO and walked with our suitcases 3 blocks on a slight incline to the hotel. The hotel is very clean and nice, we had 2 adults and 2 teens in a King Suite, there was plenty of room. We had a great view, the bed was very comfortable and the room was very clean and neat. The staff was also very helpful. My only complaint is the noise from the outside. We were on the 14 floor facing 2nd Ave, the sirens, car horns and construction noises in the morning and during rush hour was horrible. Directly in front of the hotel is the route to the bay bridge, this is where all of the traffic comes from, there is also lots of construction going on in the immediate area. Other than the outside noise, I would recommend the Courtyard

title: “Great location, Great bed, Great staff”
text:
First time at this hotel and is still currently being built. location is ideal, 2 streets away from 5th avenue & times square, amazing beds which you dont want to get out of in tnhe morning, staff and very friendly and rooms are clean. only down point is the room does not have free wi-fi and the cupboard space is tiny, only about room for 3 hanging items otherwise will be returning there very soon.
RECOMMENDED

title: “Great Stay and Location at Washington D.C. Sofitel”
text: Went there on buseinss. Great location. Great bar. Great rooms. I really liked this hotel. Will stay there again whether it be business or vacation.

title: “Can't say enough about the staff!”
text:
My wife and I needed a close-in getaway for our 1st anniversary. I had never been to the inner harbor, so we chose the Renaissance pretty much at random. I reserved a king room away from the waterfront. At check-in, the desk clerk gave us a free upgrade to a waterfront SUITE when informed of the purpose of our stay. We also received a coupon for a complimentary breakfast the next morning.
The room was clean and well-appointed. The view of the inner harbor was fantastic. The room was quiet, but not soundproof. We only stayed one night, so we didn't get to experience all of the amenities the hotel has to offer, but there are many.
Although the hotel itself is a fine hotel, the thing that impressed me the most was the friendliness and responsiveness of the hotel staff. I've traveled a good deal and I can honestly say I've never encountered a more upbeat, positive, and friendly group of people. Nearly each and every time we came within earshot of one of the staff, we were greeted with a smile and a cheerful greeting. I'm told that Baltimore is trying to change its once well-deserved reputation of being an unfriendly city. The Renaissance staff is definitely setting a new standard in that regard.

title: “Excellent hotel, staff and location!”
text:
From the moment we arrived we have had an amazing time, the staff on reception are excellent and more than helpful to help with an questions us 'first time chicago visitors' had. 
The location is perfect and is a 2 min walk from the magnificent mile, a 5 minute walk to state street shops and the navy pier. 
The room is a great size with a HUGE bed! and lots of space which im sure is useful for a family trip. 
Food is also provided the breakfast buffet has lots of opyion, cooked, fruit option, porridge, juices, pastries, amazing! breakfast is superb! and with the added extra of a dinner buffet mon-thur which we werent aware of was the icing on the cake, tea/coffee/hot choc options are also available 24/7 in the reception, execellent service!
Although this is a holiday i still use the gym and swimming pool, these both over look the city and provide a welcome distraction from exercise and makes the time go faster! 
i have no negatives at all for this hotel - none!

title: “Best hotel experience ever”
text: Georgetown Inn was our best hotel experience ever. The rooms and building are very clean, inviting and well maintained. The staff is very courteous and friendly. The manager was very personable and went out of his way to make sure we enjoyed our stay. We will definitely be back.

title: “Not a 5 star Hotel”
text:
There are many variables that can lead to a 5 star experience. However, the one that can NEVER be left out is service. This hotel lacked quality service, and falls well short of other FS hotels or Ritz Carlton hotels. Things like waiting in line for 15 minutes at check out... not acceptable. Paying $15 per day for "premium" internet service that doesnt work well (and then having the staff refuse to remove the service from your bill). 
I don't stay in Philly often, so this may be as good as it gets for this city, but it did not live up to what I normally expect of five star service. 
Beds are good. Bathrooms are ok. Rooms are ok, but could be better for the class. 
The food and service at the Fountain restaurant was impeccable. Vince, our server in the private dining room was world class. However, service in the bar was slow and not pleasant.

title: “Nice, Clean Hotel with Great Service”
text: My son and I stayed at the Hampton Inn, Chelsea after reading other reviews. We couldn't have been happier. For a New York City Hotel, it's reasonably priced, and we got a fantastic deal with our Hilton Points. We stayed in a room facing the street with two queen beds. Even though the room was on the fourth floor, we were not bothered by noise. Check-in was the fasted I've ever experienced, and when we requested a mini-fridge at the last minute (if you want one, you should remember to ask ahead of time), the staff person at the desk checked immediately to see if one was available. A fridge was brought to the room immediately. The room was large and clean, we found the beds to be very comfortable, there's free WiFi and everything in the room was well-organized. Breakfast is free, there is coffee, tea and hot chocolate available 24/7 and they have warm cookies and cider in the afternoon. There is a fitness center in the hotel, but I didn't visit it. I am thrilled to have found this place and, now, can't imagine staying anywhere else. If you like to walk, the location is perfect. It's about 10 blocks from Greenwich Village and about 20 blocks from Times Square. It's also convenient to the subway.This Hampton Inn had everything I needed and the staff was helpful and pleasant. I couldn't ask for more.

title: “Great Location off the Riverwalk for a wonderful Price”
text: I've stayed here on numerous occasions over the past two years, and this is by far one of my favorite hotels.
