Even though it's not directly on the Riverwalk, it's only a block away, and if you head a block the other direction you're at the Alamo. You can't beat the room for the price, with a mini kitchen with fridge, microwave and dishwasher. The bathrooms have a HUGE shower, and the free breakfast in the mornings is a great way to save some money and start the day off right. This hotel is also PET FRIENDLY!! There is a fee in order to bring your pet, but it's a flat rate for the stay, not a nightly rate which most of the hotels on the Riverwalk charge. Again, highly recommended hotel. Try it once and you'll be hooked.

title: “1 Week was long enough”
text: On entrance to this hotel it looks glorious.Flowers & ,greenery everywhere. I was there for the San Diego Jazz festival for the 3 rd. time and the conference centre suited the purpose. However the place is a bit run down The rooms are dull and the bathroom was tiny for 2 people with no shelf space. although there was plenty of hot water. In one of the restaurants the wrong food was served and in another the service was very slow and the buffet breakfast was cold. I was told by a staff member that that was the way the Americans liked it. !! The staff in Charlie's bar twice said you can have 1 game of pool then we are closing. It was 11 pm on a Friday & Saturday nights. Kelly's Steak restaurant was much better but the 10oz. Rib eye steak could not have been 5 ozs even allowing for shrinkage. The hotel staff were pleasant and helpful except for one of the bellboys whole told us to get off the trolley at a station which was at least 3 miles from where we should have been. We had to walk for ages because the return trolley's had broken down and the area is so desolate that taxi's don't go to that area...

title: “Nice Hotel and great staff, still nothing much in the area”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights in June 2010 for business. The hotel which was once a Wyndham Hotel has been renovated by Hilton and it looks good. It has a vast lobby area and seems to get a lot of convention business. The hotel is used a lot by local companies like Haliburton to house personnel that are taking training in preperation becoming contract workers in Iraq and Afganistan, but there was also a convention of teenage girls that are on school dance teams (how is that for an interesting combination). The workout room was bigger and a lot nicer than the old hotel and the outdoor pool on the second floor also looked very well maintained. The lobby bar was converted from a sports bar to a wine bar, which is too bad, because the pool tables are gone and that was one of the few fun things to do there. Now it is just a bar with lots of TV's like every other bar. The area around the hotel is still bleak, although it looks like they are doing some renovation of the Greenspoint Mall across the road, which the locals refer to as the Gunspoint Mall, since there has been a high incidence of crime around its parking lots. The hotel is safe, but I wouldn't go wandering to far around the area. The staff at the hotel was super nice from start to finish. If your buisiness takes you to the Greenspoint area I would recommend the hotel as a nice place to stay, but not a tourist spot (are there really tourists to Houston?) Don't even think about going to this hotel without having a car.

title: “Large suites, helpful staff, clean but worn”
text: We booked a deluxe king suite for $279.00 a night for Thanksgiving weekend. Our suite had a large living room/dining area, a small separate kitchen with a gas stove, microwave, coffee maker full fridge, utensils, etc. There were 1-1/2 baths, one with a tub and shower head. The shower was great! Everything was clean but the furniture was worn and scratched. The sofa had a slipcover on it that kept coming off and exposed the slightly stained upholstery. We had a king bed which was very comfortable and our daughter slept on a roll-away bed that we requested ahead of time. We didn't try the pull out sofa bed because we've never slept on one that was even slightly comfortable. The restaurant, called Top of the Tower, was very elegant and and romantic . A pianist was playing on a grand piano and it was dark with candles and soft lighting. The view was stunning. Unfortunately we didn't eat there because we had only brought casual clothing. Room service is available. The staff and the doormen were very accommodating and were always available to help. Valet parking was $52.00 a day and you weren't able to access your auto until check-out. That was fine with us because we mostly walked or took taxis. A parking garage down the street was only $2.00 less per day. The neighborhood is mostly residential and very quiet and safe. We had a view from the bedroom of the East River which was nice. One block west on 2nd Ave. were lots of shops and restaurants. We had breakfast both days at Morning Star Cafe which was inexpensive and the food was good but typical diner food. One thing we loved about it was that they serve breakfast all day for those late risers, like us. The burgers and fries looked great too! The other restaurant we ate at on 2nd Ave. was Zarela. The food here was some of the best Mexican cuisine I've had! Not typical enchiladas and tacos but they offered very inventive and fresh dishes. We also purchased some wine at the liquor store on 2nd and brought it back to our room..To get into midtown, we took a cab which was under $10.00. We also purchased Grey Line Hop On-Hop Off tickets and would walk to the U.N. to get on it a few times. Just a hint on driving to the hotel...enter 1st Ave. at 40th St. or below. Make sure you stay in the center lane on 1st Ave. and go through the tunnel. Whatever you do, don't keep left or you won't be able to get over to the right easily to make the right onto 50th St. It's an accident waiting to happen. From 50th make a right onto Beekman Pl. and then a right onto Mitchell Pl. The hotel will be the last building on your right, on the corner of Mitchel and 1st. There are spaces for unloading. My GPS kept trying to take me on the FDR but I later realized I had it set for highways vs. local roads. I used my own common sense to get there anyway.

title: “Awesome”
text:
We've stayed at this Holiday Inn Express last spring and it was great. It's not too far from the mexicain festival and it's walking distance from the shopping center , restaurants bars and even the riverwalk ( 15 min or so). There is a shuttle service as well, so it is very helpful. The continental breakfast was a good thing too. It's very clean and I think I've never seen a hotel that quiet , we seriously thought we were the only people in the hotel because there was no noise at all ! But you know what, the hotel was almost full.
The lady at the front desk was nice and help us with directions in the city.
Perfect for family and friends !
Guests from QC, Canada !!

title: “Excellent place at a very low price”
text: We stayed there one night and it was very comfortable, clean and quiet. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Dirty, noisy, run down in a very sketchy neighborhood.”
text: We spent four nights in this hotel during a conference. Check-in took over an hour due to only one staff being able to check in guests and a cumbersome paper form check in process. Our room did have nice bedding, but the room was in poor repair, dirty and smelled of cigarette and marijuana smoke. The bathroom floor and bathtub was filthy with smears all over the glass shower doors, black dirt accumulated in all of the corners and pubic hair/dirt/food remains on the bathroom floor. Our window didn't close. It was noisy and the neighborhood was really sketchy - we were unable to leave the hotel and walk the four blocks to the Mascone Center without being repeatedly hassled by aggressive panhandlers and homeless people. The breakfast is not at the hotel, but at a small cafe on the corner and was terrible. The fitness center was across the street in another dumpy hotel. Staff offered us another room, but it was just as dirty and the tiles in the bathroom floor were all cracked and it smelled worse than the first room. We asked them to please just clean up the room we were in and when we came back, it had not been touched. We live in the city and are used to urban areas (not our first time in San Fran) but did not feel safe in this area. This neighborhood is full of strip clubs, xxx theaters, marijuana centers and unsavory characters and you have to walk through it to get anywhere else. It was very noisy outside at night and loud enough to disturb us in our room on the 4th floor. Worst hotel stay I've ever had, and we travel frequently. We booked through BookIt.com and they were extremely unhelpful.

title: “Would stay there again!”
text: It was a nice clean place with a comfortable bed. We arrived at 1am to the hotel and check in was easy and the staff was very nice. Both restaurants were very good - the Waffle King and the Amigo Spot had very good food and great service! The price was affordable and I would definitely recommend it to my friends who head to San Diego. SeaWorld was an easy close drive away. We weren't able to try the pool or jacuzzi, but we will next time!

title: “Great Stay during the hard NY Winter.”
text:
Pros:
management (worked proactively with me to make sure i was able to make the reservation -- due to weather issues)
service (from bellhop to the cleaning staff)
cleanliness (i stepped out for two hours and my room was cleaned by the time i came back!)
Location (shopping, metro, central park)
Internet in biz room
Bathroom is large
Modern hotel
Great Value
Cons:
Walls a bit thin
Room slightly small
I didnt make much use of the metro but it is nearby... The location might be far for what you want to do, but again, it depends on what you like to do in NY. Central Park is very near, so is the Time Warner building at Columbus circle, but SoHo, East, West Village, Meat Packing, will require subway rides or taxis. If you decide on the taxi route, after numerous cab rides you'll fail to realized any value from this hotel. The best restuarants are pretty far south in Mahanttan so you may feel like you're a bit far from the action... but ive been to NY several times and i enjoyed the quiteness and the new location, b/c there are still numerous shopping areas and restuarants nearby.

title: “Convenient Airport Hotel”
text:
The Sheraton Park n' Fly is the reason I stay here (LAX Marriott has the same program), that and my SPG points. I like the hotel, it is convenient for the airport, the pool is nice and Shula's is good, but overpriced. The rooms are nice and the beds comfortable and they have good business services.
All good so far.
The negatives are the parking and the elevators. You HAVE to valet unless you want a half mile walk for self parking. The elevators have been messed up for a while now. They are so bad you have to use the staff elevators more often than not and it has been this way for a while.
Will I stay here again? Yes. 
It has some good positives. It is a great hotel for someone looking for an overnight stay or maybe two days. If you have to been in L.A. more than two days there are a lot better places to stay and better locations.

title: “Huge surprise”
text: Stayed here while husband was at convention here. Make sure to ask for an ocean view. We overlooked the aircraft carrier during ship week and was pleasantly surprised by all the fireworks my kids watched before bed. The hotel was clean but huge since it is a convention Mecca. It is very easy to get around with the train stop just across the street and ferry a few blocks away. My 4&5 year olds had a blast trying out all the modes of transportation. With so much to do in San Diego we really didn't spend much time there but did appreciate its convinent location

title: “Can't wait to come back!!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at the Westin at the end of January 2004 and loved it. I had emailed the reservation team from the UK, and requested a corner room after reading reviews on this site. When we arrived it had been noted and we had a fantastic room with an amazing view(We could see the Empire State, the Hudson River and Times Square). The staff were very cheerful and there were no delays checking in.The Heavenly Shower was our highlight, we were like shrivelled prunes we stayed in there so long!Shula's restaurant also deserves a mention, the evening meals were gorgeous. I am very fussy with steak, and can safely say the Fillet steak they served me was the best I've ever had. My partner ate the 48oz steak and got into the 48oz club. The side of creamed spinach was also delicious-and huge!The location of this hotel is perfect, we got the bus straight from Newark Airport to the Port Authority stepped outside and there was the Westin.We love Manhattan, and try to visit twice a year. Now we have stayed at The Westin Times Square, we will try to book here each time.

title: “Very hip spot”
text: Stayed for the first time the weekend before the 4th of July. My girlfriend and I had plenty of food and even more drink by the pool and at Dragonfly. You can run up a pretty substantial bill over a fun weekend but it is a very fun spot that has the rare combination of being both elegant and 'hip' - I guess you would call it 'swanky'. Only issue I had was my credit card was billed for what I assume is charges to the minibar but I never received an itemized bill, it seemed a bit high. Enjoyed the stay so much I am going back this weekend, hopefully will be able to get a copy of the bill from my last stay.

title: “Clean, efficient, good location”
text: We stayed at the hotel 5 nights and service was impeccable. Newspaper was at our doorstep each morning and near reception desk self service coffee table is available for guests. I also needed to use the hotel's overnight dry cleaning service and my coat was ready for me early in the morning. Concierges were also friendly and helpful. Other than that location is very good although in weekends you may feel a wee bit deserted. Our room was spacious and the veranda with view to the bay bridge was magnificent. I would expect, however, a free use of internet.

title: “Wonderful Stay in Baltimore in January!”
text: There are so many positive things I can say about this hotel, I don't know where to begin. A girlfriend and I went to watch the Texans and Ravens playoff game and chose this hotel because it was directly on the harbor. We stayed in mid January. Our first night there we met up with friends at a local pub and they gave us a complimentary private car ride to the pub. Our phones were stolen @ the pub and they did everything in their power to help us out. The long distance phonecalls were $10 a minute and they cut our phone bill in half. That is a little pricey as well as the almost $45 a day valet parking, but half off the phone bill was better than nothing. They upgraded us to a harbor view, complimentary movie. This may be all because I'm an Ambassador member but it was fantastic. We got fresh fruits and chocolates daily along with the newspaper. We had a fully stocked mini bar with all kinds of goodies. Again the staff, location, friendliness, cleanliness, etc. was just amazing. I would def. stay here again! Thanks Intercontinental Baltimore for a wonderful and rememberable stay.

title: “Bate and Switch”
text:
Let's start with the good first. The front desk clerk was very friendly and helpful. The rooms were dated but clean and comfortable.
The bad. I was traveling in the area and booked a room last minute for the same night. I choose the pay in advance option as it was a significant savings (booked through Hampton's website). When i arrived they told me I had booked the wrong night and needed to charge me a significantly higher rate. When I showed the front desk clerk my confirmation number and confirmation email detailing the correct dates and that i paid in advance he realized the error but there was nothing he could do without calling a central 800 number. I proceeded to wait in the lobby for an extended period of time as they tried to figure out what to do. After a long wait, the only option they offered me was to rebook me at the higher rate. Total bate and switch. Very disappointing as I have stayed at Hampton Inn in various locations and always have had the best experiences. This experience takes Hampton off the list until they fix this situation. I have referred the issue to the Better Business Bureau.

title: “good location staff nice rooms needed to be cleaned and hotel needs big update”
text: Upon arrival they gave us a room that the bed wasn't big enough for my daughter and I to sleep in and the sheets were dirty and ripped. TV did not work. They came up to give us new sheets and expected me to change my own sheets (which should have been clean to begin with). They changed our room and there were no light bulbs and the room was filthy. They straightened it up but I still felt that the room couldn't get clean the carpets were stained and sticky. The staff for the most part did try to work with what they had. I have stayed in 2 star properties but was glad to leave this one behind.

title: “Old World Charm”
text:
We had a wonderful Four Day visit to San Francisco, based from the Delightful Queen Anne Hotel. It was a Girls' Finishing School during the time when buildings were vibrant, alive with color, and every gaze, inside and outside, was rewarded with splendor and interesting design.
 A beautiful Bay Window, old world furnishings, and the warm glow of a true wood-burning fireplace provided a unusual ambiance (when was the last time you were treated to a real wood-burning fireplace?).
 We walked to many attractions, took the trolley to others, and when were at home in the Hotel; we were treated royally. The food was delicious and the other guests were interesting and as happy as we were. This was an exciting get-away from the usual and a wonderful entrance into the unusual world of old San Francisco. 
 PS: Do not miss the stroll to near-by Japan Town, you will also find this to be a rare treat. "Five Stars" for exciting and wonderful, and for a change from 'the usual'.

title: “Posh and Stylish Boutique-style Property!”
text: I travel to Chicago every quarter for business, and have stayed at the Dana on the past two trips to town. The experience has been top-notch both times, from the initial greeting by the awesome Bellman, TJ, to the friendly and attentive check-in personnel. The rooms are extremely well appointed; I particularly enjoyed the glass rainshower and high-end toiletry products in the bath. Add to that smart wood floorboards, iPod docking station with speakers, and Keurig coffeemaker, plus an extremely comfortable bed. I will make the Dana Hotel and Spa my hotel of choice every time I visit Chicago!

title: “Lobby is interesting”
text: And it stops there. Rooms were in need of renovation, though mine was clean. I booked a king and at first they put me in a double. Went back to the desk and they switched me to a king. A little heads up here. I booked a king on priceline and paid a little more just to get a king. The person at the desk said they DO NOT guarantee room type. Our room had no towels, we had to call 2 times to get them about 8 hours later. I think that they were under staffed.

title: “Loews Hollywood Hotel - Great Rate and Great Stay”
text: The room was comfortable and quiet even though it overlooked N. Highland. I love the fact that it was connected to a multilevel mall. I would definitely return with my family, because I think its location is great and its offerings would meet the various needs of each of us.

title: “Large Conference Hotel”
text: The Hilton is a very large conference hotel with a cavernous reception area. We spent a couple of nights there in March but not at a conference. It's a great hotel, breakfast in the Hilton's adjoining building was excellent and the staff are very friendly. The room had two double beds and was spacious with a very good bathroom. For a view we were overlooking Camden Yard but there was no game on, I can see these rooms being popular in season. Hotel is very clean all round and I couldn't fault anything. It is a good stretch of your legs to the Inner Harbour but that wasn't a problem and there are lots of restaurants there. A few bars nearby, not plush but a lot cheaper than the hotel's very nice cocktail bar. Highly recommend this hotel

title: “Very comfortable, reasonable weekend rates”
text: A group of us went to Jacksonville to visit a mutual friend and go to see the Jets play the Jaguars. This was the hotel our host recommended and it was a good choice. Clean, comfortable room for under $80/night with taxes. Will stay here next time I'm in town to visit this friend.

title: “A great place”
text:
For the money, this is a fantastic hotel.
All hotel rooms in NYC are small, this was no different but big enough for our needs. If going to NYC in summer this hotel is perfect - the Private roof terrace/pool/bar are first class.
Great part of town, not overly noisy, and 2-3 minute walk from Central Park. The oysters and burgers in the bar on the ground floor are also excellent.
I will definately look up this place again when I return.

title: “Great Location, Great Price”
text:
We just returned from San Diego where we attended a national conference, and for our needs The Bristol Hotel was a great place to stay. It was just a short trolley ride to the convention center and just a few blocks of walking to get most anywhere in the Gaslamp District. In comparison to many of the other lodging options in the immediate area, it was by far the best deal for the price.
Overall, the rooms were nice and clean. The beds were comfortable, the spacious room was decorated with a modern flair, and the in room wireless was a nice amenity. The only complaint that I had was the bottom of the tub was peeling and the closet door and bathroom ceiling were unpainted.
I won't lie, the noise level is rather high, especially when you're trying to sleep in. However, it is in the heart of the business district and next door to a trolley stop and bus terminal. 
I guess the real question is - would I stay there again? And the answer is for the price, the location, the amenities, and the overalll presentation of the hotel - definitely yes. I would also recommend it to my friends and family.

title: “Great location, but "shabby chic" takes on a new meaning here”
text: You can't ask for a better location than the Triton - right across from Chinatown Gate! Too bad you couldn't see it from my room, which looked out into an ugly airwell festooned with pigeon netting. In window air conditioning units blocked the view - not a bad thing - but also meant that the airwell was noisy all night long - like being parked next to an idling truck. The furnishing are hip(ish), but frankly beat to death. The underside of my desk was so beat up that there were splinters of wood hanging down from beneath it. On my desk there was an odd wind chime device that apparently needed (but did not have) batteries to work. The tub was old and gross, and when I ran water into it for a bath, an oily filmy substance rose to the top of the water. No bath for me! The "business center" is one computer in the cramped lobby! I love Kimpton Hotels, but this one is off my list permanently; don't care what the cost of the room may be. Also, the day staff was not very friendly - my check-in concluded with a bored, "Do you NEED me to explain the hotel amenities to you?" This is far, far from the friendly greeting I've received at Kimptons all around the country. Night staff was courteous and helpful.

title: “Great stay in a great location, for a great value”
text:
We made our reservation through the 888 number for Starwood Preferred Guests for December 20-23, 2009. While organizing my inbox in early December, I noticed the reservation was actually for November 20-23. As soon as I noticed the error, I contacted the hotel and easily reached the Manager, Michael Zayas. Mr. Zayas was friendly, accommodating, and not only recified the mistake, he also gave us a great deal on a suite. In short, Mr. Zayas demonstrated excellence in customer service and problem management skills.
The hotel is on Charlton Street between Varick and Hudson. The hotel block is fairly quiet with easy walking access to the bars, restaurants, and shops of SoHo and the West Village. 
The check in process was fast and very easy; the front desk staff was consistently friendly, smiling, and, welcoming. This consistency was uniform at all times of day and with all staff.
The room itself (#2103) was clean, had updated furniture, and a sharp looking bathroom with good water pressure. The best feature, however, was the view. We had 2 large windows facing uptown with views of the Empire State and Chrysler buildings. A motorized window shade operated by a wall switch provided privacy. This is a 1 bedroom suite with pocket doors separating the living room from the bedroom. It had flat Screen TV’s in both rooms and the space was fairly large by New York Standards. We requested in advance, and were provided with, a small refrigerator. 
The ice and vending machines are in the basement. Also in the basement was a small, but adequate exercise room which had: a well working treadmill, TV, elliptical, free weights and a stationary bike. 
My one criticism was I was unable to get change for the vending machine from either the front desk or lobby bar. 
In short, this was a great stay in a great location, for a great value.

title: “Only The Menger”
text:
I brought my entire family down to San Antonio to celebrate my birthday and for Thanksgiving, and The Menger staff pleased everyone from ages 3 to 70. Everyone, everywhere was attentive and helpful in making our stay a memorable one.
The children loved the pool and all of us loved the bar, the restaurant and the historic ambiance.
Not only is the Menger historic, but it's location next to the Alamo makes it so special, essentially the heart of San Antonio. Other hotels may be on the river, but none have the sight of the Alamo out of your window.
Thank you, Menger Staff, for a wonderful week of memories.

title: “Very Nice Establishment & Great Price”
text: This is one of the best La Quinta's I have ever stayed in. I booked the suite and it was actually two separate rooms (normally it is one big room with a half partition wall). The first room was huge! It had a pull out coach, a long working desk, microwave, refrigerator, sink, and large television in it. The king bed, large closet, and another huge television made up the other room. The bathroom was very mod feeling with an interesting sink, and a shower that was very spacious (no bathtub). Everything in the room was perfectly clean, also. Everyone here was very nice and pleasant, and when their was a problem with my bill, the staff was happy to fix it immediately. I will definitely stay here again when traveling through Austin!

title: “Does not honor platinum guarantee”
text:
I stayed with this hotel for a few nights for my sisters wedding. At check in, I notified the front desk that I was a platinum member. The agent thanked me and handed me my keys. At check out, I mentioned that I had not received my platinum gift. The hotel informed me that they would not honor the Marriott guarantee!
I followed up with a letter to Marriott corporate that was then sent on to the general manager 3 months later. The general managed informed me that he had talked to the front desk and they stated that someone else had checked in for me and that is why they did not have to honor the guarantee. 
My issues about this hotel are that they do not honor the platinum guarantee, front desk employees will lie, and they don't seem to think there is a problem having other people check into your room (even though it was not true in this case)!
\
If you are a preferred member with Marriott do not stay here.

title: “Good value in central San Diego”
text: Stayed here 3 nights on a mini vacation. I've spent some time in SD in the past and have stayed at many hotels which didn't come close to offering the amenities of this Residence Inn at the price. Granted, the location isn't immediately near anything touristy, but it's a straight shot one way to the Zoo and the other way to the Wild Animal Park, plus La Jolla and the airport are only 15 min away. Yes, you need a car but there is adequate free on-site parking here. Inside, the queen suite came with a well equipped kitchen and updated furnishings. However, the bed appeared to be full size, not queen, and the comforter was a bit small. There was occasional noise from the unit above. The breakfast was varied and quite good, the internet access in the room (wired) was flawless. One problem we had was that when we used the fireplace with a duraflame log, the smoke began to come into the room even though the damper was open. The alarm went off but the service man was instantly there and took care of the problem. The front desk staff were all polite and usually helpful. We would stay there again and recommend the inn to friends.

title: “A Big NY Favela (Slum) !!!”
text: This place should be close imediatly for renovation, it is a shame as the location is very good. The hotrel it is disgusting, dirth, old and very bad care, and is possible to hear everything from the rooms near. NO PRIVACY, No Internet, No Safety deposit box, No Service in Room or front desk. How can this being call a Hotel ? I coming from Brasil, Rio, and have my own B&B in Rio, them more I see Hotels more sure I am that I have a great place. The Hotels are rip of people, and not worried with anyone. The location do not bit my confort to sleep. So never again and dont reccomend even to a not friend .

title: “Excellent Value, Clean, and Convenient.”
text: I live 20 blocks south of this Holiday Inn and pass it all the time. We are having some repair work done to our house and needed to stay somewhere close for two nights. I had it narrowed down to the Holiday Inn Express, Hotel Nexus, or Comfort Inn. This one was a hands down winner for the following reasons: 1. Very clean grounds, lobby, room, and bathroom. 2. Included breakfast. 3. Free Wi-Fi. 4. Has a pool/hot tub (comments about this later) 5. Great rates with Entertainment Card. 6. King Suite has a mini fridge and microwave. This is one of the nicer budget places I've stayed in for a long time. Pick up a Seattle Entertainment book online if you're planning on being in Seattle for a few days or more. I believe the current edition has a coupon for Kidd Valley burgers a half block north of here. You can walk there and eat dinner there and save a bit of money.

title: “mixed review”
text: We used our American Express reward points to stay here and I have to say that we were disappointed. Our room was small and dark. I went to the front desk and spoke with Michael and he moved us to a nicer room. The location was ok, within walking distance to the Sears Tower and the theatre where we saw Wicked. But, I just felt 'pent up'. We had a choice between here and the Westin on Michigan Ave and I picked this since I had stayed at the Westin (and LOVED it) so I wanted something different. All in all, I wish I picked the Westin or didn't waste the points. Oh well ...

title: “I should have bought 10 more vouchers.”
text: KGB deal: 2 nights for $200, all in. Five star location and bed, the latter a welcome joy after climbing those hills all day. The room was large, well-appointed and super-clean. Love the seamlessly built-into-the-bathroom-mirror TV. Its got all the standard (?) amenities: 2 robes, microwave, safe, refrigerator, dishes, silverware, glasses, coffee maker, ironing board, etc.and plenty of towels. Staff was very friendly but they needed more of them. It tool a while to get simple things done. Not that big of a deal. In room coffee was crappy but they had delicious and STRONG Petes (tea as well) on the 10th floor Club Level which is open to all. I didn't use the gym so took no notice of what they did and did not have.The sauna in the ladies room was nice (turn it on for 30 minutes before you go in if you want it hot) and the changing rooms were very clean as well. Jacuzzi was equally so, though the jets were poor, but it is co-ed so bring a suit! Nobody was in either when I went in and it was nice to have it all to myself. The lobby is boring. It is just a place to check in, not hang out but who cares when all of Union Square is at your feet. I requested a room off street and got a lovely corner one with a view of the back of buildings. Fine with me as quiet is what I wanted and it was very much so. I actually just called Animod, the place who had the vouchers for sale, to try and buy 5 more nights but the deal is no longer available. I would definitely go back!

title: “Don't believe the negative reviews !!”
text: I almost overlooked a gem after reading all the negative reviews. I checked in late and I was given an upgrade until they found another standard room the next day. The manager walked me to the room and was extremely polite, respectful and waived any late check in fees......The front desk guy was just as polite every time I went to the desk. One time the key did not work, but I took it up front and no problem with re-activating it quickly. Rooms cleaned and new towels given every day. Breakfast is decent. Off the Hwy so a little noise if you are in front , but not a major issue. On the weekend there is a club across the street , I never saw or heard anything to affect safety or opinion of the property. Not fancy , but decent moderate clean hotel at great rates and not far from Harbor area and you can pull up to your room at no cost!

title: “4th report”
text: this place just keeps getting better.Stayed over thanksgiving this year and jerry did ask to put down that the prices will unfortunately have to rise again next year but this place is a real gem clean tidy tv's updated again jerry and wife could not help more even offered use of spare sat nav now planning for next year.Only small gripe was that one night there was a sports event that went on till 1 am but hey! thank you jerry.

title: “Small but clean”
text: This was our 1st time to San Fran and this hotel was a great location to walk everwhere. Rooms are small and your suitcases can get in the way, but the room was very clean and there was a good size bathroom. Afternoon wine was cute too. Would stay here again.

title: “Friendly Staff, Large Room, Comfy Bed”
text:
The staff was so friendly and helpful we couldn't believe it. They were like that the entire stay. We enjoyed our conversations with some of the staff.
 The 24/7 restaurant was great. We would order using the kiosk and then the food was ready in about 10 mins. They have a Starbucks coffee bar with yummy desserts.
 The room was really big and clean. The bed was very comfy. We will definitely stay there again.
 Some have compalned of the walk to the Riverwalk. It only took about 5 mins of walking. I have no complaints. A 5 min walk in exchange for FREE PARKING at the hotel. That's great. Most hotels charge $18-25 a night to park.
 Great place. Stay at the Hyatt Place.

title: “Very nice!”
text: My wife and I had a great stay at the Hilton Columbus/Polaris. Clean rooms; comfortable bed and pillows; clean, well kept property; modern, elegant decor; friendly staff. Short walk to a couple nice restaurants for special occasions (Eddie Merlots, Mitchell's) that worked out great. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “A Great quiet location close to Manhattan's best attractions”
text: We really enjoyed Loews Regency and were treated very well. It is only a few blocks away from Central park and the main shopping area. It was on Park Ave which is a major street but very quiet. It was very easy to walk to all of the places we wanted to see in Manhattan. The concierge was great about helping book activities. We were fortunate to get a fridge in our room so we could keep cold drinks and snacks and not have to rely on the mini bar. My only complaint is that there are no coffee makers in the rooms. That was a bit frustrating not to be able to have a cup of coffee in bed (yes you could order room service coffee... but that was $12!). All in all a great location a great price as we booked on Travelocity. We would recommend it to everyone.. families, business, couples.

title: “Trendy, clean, good location”
text:
We spent 9 nights in the Pod hotel and we loved it! Very clean, very trendy, young residents, polite personnel! What else to ask in Manhattan, where hotel prices are far too expensive? Walking distance to Times Sq 15 min. The room was small, but we managed it pretty well, even after our shopping extravaganza in Woodbury Common! 
Have to mention the great french restaurant -bar just under the hotel "Le bateau ivre" , great service, wide selection of french wines.

title: “Good Service but Noisy location”
text:
We stayed at the Magic Castle Hotel for 3 nights in October 2005. The reason that we picked this hotel was to have a kitchen and be close to our destination - Universal Studios. 
As previously stated in all of the other reviews, the crown jewel of this hotel is the very good service given by the young staff. 
Also previously stated, the layout of the hotel is as the set of the Melrose Place TV show. All of the rooms surround a small courtyard with a small pool in the middle. No elevators, just stairways. 
The rooms themselves are reasonably sized for a suite-type hotel. They have been recently renovated, but not particularly well. In our room, the bathroom door didn't shut properly and the baseboards were already peeling. The kitchen was fully stocked with pots, pans, utensils, etc. Besides the TVs, there was also a small stereo system in the living room and a DVD player - nice. The sofa bed was not comfortable as the mattress wasn't well supported to the metal frame. A nice feature is that they use down comforters instead of regular blankets. Of special note, was the great water pressure in the shower. It was like standing underneath a giant waterfall!
The continental breakfast is good, not great. As previously mentioned the baked goods were above average. 
Parking is $8/day for the small gated garage. The garage is a little tight, but we didn't have problems finding a spot every night. 
The main reason that I'm only giving an average rating was the level of night-time noise. The walls are pretty thin. Eventhough the location of our room was supposedly one of the more quiet sections, there was much traffic and weekend-partying noise until 2am. Of course, this isn't solely the hotel's fault, but rather the nature of their location - 1 block away from the night-life hub of Hollywood and Highland. 
On the plus side for the location:
a) the hotel is a 4 minute walk from Grauman's Chinese theater
b) we took the metro to Universal Studios, which was another 2 minute walk from the Chinese theater
Here's an example of the good service: 
One of the female staff asked me if I slept well when I went to get breakfast and I complained about the noise. She purchased some ear plugs for us, and the plugs did help somewhat. In general, the staff is pretty attentive and helpful.
For me, the good service and other perks didn't overcome the fact that it's an older building without good sound-proofing.

title: “We liked this hotel”
text:
We stayed one night at this hotel with 2 friends. I was in two minds about this place because of the reviews about vehicles being broken into, and we had a Bose sound system in the vehicle that one of our friends use for her music concerts. But we had no problems. 
The suites are quite spacious. I wish the bathroom sink counter space was bigger, but it was adequate. A couple of lights in our room didn't work, and our friends said that some in their room didn't work either, but there were enough light fixtures that the room had sufficient light. We arrived late night and having the in-room microwave was so convenient for us to heat up the dinner that we brought in. (I do wish Comfort Suites would provide a couple of disposable plates and utensils in the rooms though. That would be so convenient.)
Breakfast was ok. The food was hot and plentiful. But the orange juice was pretty watery. We only stayed one night so don't know if this is usual or a fluke. 
All in all, the place suited us and we would stay here again if we are in the area.

title: “Stylish and comfortable”
text:
This is a very upbeat hotel. Before arrival, I called and spoke with a guy by the name of Andrew. I explained that my parents and granparents both would be traveling along with me. However, my grandparents are in their late 80's and I would need to be sure their rooms were close to mine. Even though the hotel was full, Andrew stayed on the phone with me until he could accommodate my requests. He was very frindly andhelpful. By his phone mannerism, you could tell he enjoyed his career choice. Once we arrived, a gentleman by the name of Mina checked us in. He was speedy and offered his help immediatley. He was friendly and even asked if we were familiar witht the area and offered suggestions to local restaurants. Later that night we needed ice an could not find the machine on our floor. We called downstairs and Andrew actually sent someone up to our room with the ice! That is real customer service! Once leaving, the maintenace guy asked us was everything ok. He was just as nice as theother staff. There was also a lady on staff (didn't get her name but she had blonde hair and she worked at front desk) who was always smiling and willing to hold conversations with my grandparents and parents. This made them feel wonderful. 
As far as the room goes, the matress is great. After an auto accident, I have had trouble sleeping in bed. This was not the issue here at Aloft. The matress allowed me to sleep a full night in bed (which had not happened in over 8 months)! The rooms were spotless and I felt at home. I will most def return here in the future.

title: “All that you need in an airport hotel”
text:
You are travelling in a busy airport. You only need to get fast to your room, take a shower and have a decent bed. The LAX Travelodge can help you. Don't expect a fancy place (it looks that the hotel is still living in the 80's) but the overall experience is fine
My only complaint is they have a strange parking lot behind the hotel. And you have to get there trough a dark alley. If you want to avoid this experience, park your car in front of the Denny's and carry your luggage to your room.

title: “Great location!”
text:
We were recently in NY for 3 days (2 nights) and I was pleased with the cleanliness of the room. I was hoping to get the upgrade but it seemed to become unavailable at the last minute (I was keeping an eye twice a day up unitl that day and it was available)...anyway dissapointed but the room was fine. I booked a premium suite with a supposed view but could only see a very small portion of Times Square....
You cannot ask for a better location -walk to Central Park, shows, restaurants...and the sightseeing buses are across the street. The staff were very nice and accomodating. I would stay here again.

title: “great place”
text: I just stayed at this hotel with my two teenagers and their two friends, we got a Junior Suite which came with two queens beds and a pullout coach. this has to be the biggest room I've ever stayed at in NYC. I've stayed at several different hotels, where I paid more and always got very very small rooms,. this was the best as far as room size goes. The bed was comfy, shower and bathroom appeared new. TV worked good. I got free internet even though they charged for internet. Plenty of open access around there. Hotel location was great, too. I parked for $25 on the next block - they give you a special rate because of the hotel. There was no restaurant but did offer continental breakfast on the 4th floor. It was ok, got coffee and donuts, but not much to choice from. For the price, location and size of room, this was a GREAT deal. I will be back!

title: “Moderate Hotel. 10 min. drive to dwntwn.”
text: We read some bad reviews online but our experience proved otherwise. The hotel lobby and our room were clean however the room smelled slightly musty as if it hadn't been used for a while - nothing we didn't get used to after 10 minutes. The hotel is about a $10 cab to Beale. The hotel shuttle costs $9 anyways per person, one way, but the value of this hotel is much greater than what you will pay right downtown. The free breakfast was great: cereal and pastry selection, muffins, fruit, toast, bagels with cream cheese and a waffle maker. The coffee was good but the hot water for tea was cold every morning. The latch lock on our door was broken but the dead bolt still worked. The staff were helpful and friendly. We stayed here after staying at a 4-star in Nashville to save some money and thought we might be disappointed but we were very pleased, This is a great stay if you're not overly particular and are on a budget.

title: “OK Hotel, Crappy Downtown Area”
text:
The room was nice, the breakfast was OK, but the service at the Washington Grille next door (hotel bar and grill) was terrible. Only one waitress on staff, but the place was nearly empty and it took me 45 minutes to get one lousy order of sweet potato fries (which were terrible). Took cabs to the casinos, and they were some of the nastiest cabs I've ever ridden in--dirty, no air conditioning. The people mover would have been my choice, but not my sister's. I would definitely not walk anywhere, though.
If you're going to gamble, pay the extra bucks and stay at the Atheneum in Greektown.

title: “not a bad place to sleep in the city that never sleeps”
text:
This monstrous, full service atrium hotel offers rooms with Times Square views. A room on a high floor allows for viewing the constant activity below without too much noise. We took our teenager for her first trip to the city and stayed here in February. She loved the high energy location, walking to and from Broadway shows through Times Square, and hopping on the glass elevators and soaring up through the lobby. Personally, I prefer other parts of the city, and smaller more intimate properties. But, this was a good choice for us for this particular trip.
Our room was large by NYC standards for about $300 per night (Presidents weekend). But, it was not particularly clean. We found trash and lost belongings under the furniture. 
The concierge desk helped us with dinner reservations twice and, despite knowing we were going with a 16 year old girl, they sent us to a campy Moulin Rouge-themed French restaurant one night where the food wasn't bad but our daughter was seated directly beneath a life-sized nude painting. I would have appreciated a little more info before being sent in that direction!

title: “# Okay...customer service is lacking”
text:
We used a coupon, so we got a low rate of 39.99. However, they tacked on an extra phone charge of 2.28 per night without telling me. 
The not-so-friendly manager offered to remove this extra charge--for the first night. After I had "been informed" then I would have to pay the fee I chose to stay. 
While I was there, I got two broken coffee pots, so that was a hassle. As for the room, it was clean and generally comfortable. These hotels are built of wood, so you can hear people walking around and bumping into walls, etc.
There are several restaurants and fast-food chains within walking distance.

title: “Complete satisfaction”
text: We stayed in this hotel over the very busy Thanksgiving weekend. We were greeted by friendly and helpful reception staff - who always seemed to find time to acknowledge us every time we entered. The room was spotless and was kept that way every day. The room facilities were fine, the personal touch of pumpkin pie on Thanksgiving day is evidence of that bit of extra care given to the guests. We were delighted with every aspect of this hotel and we will use it again. Thank you to all the staff!

title: “Very nice.”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Westin overnight to celebrate her birthday. We were both very pleased and very happy with our room. The room was very spacious and clean. The staff were very courteous and helpful. We had the Executive Suite and believe it or not, it was under $200 for the night. I know, I know, we stayed in February and not much going on at that time but even so, they could have made a few more bucks off of us if they wanted to. Over all, a very nice and clean hotel.

title: “Return Visit”
text:
If I returned it shews that I was not unhappy first time round last year.
As I commented last time it is not the typical La Qinta in its own grounds with very spacious rooms. But you cannot expect that at a reasonable price in Manhattan.
My wife is very fastidious and we have no complaints about cleanliness. The linen is clean and the bathroom, though small, kept spotless. 
The rooms do tend to be decorated in rather dowdy wallpaper, which can become scuffed around the doors and peel slightly in the bathrooms. This can lead to an initial downbbeat impression.
This time we were on the 4th floor witha view of the street; last year we overlooked the light shaft. It was more pleasant but we did not spend time looking out of it! To live in the hotel room is surely not why most able-bodied travellers visit Manhattan!
The major gripe I had last year was the reception desk staff. This year a complete change. Personable staff who smiled and 
actually communicated with guests. The telephone seemed to have been re-routed elsewhere too, which meant they could concentrate on dealing with guests.
The breakfast must be one of the best complimentary ones going, particularly now the waffle makers, for which guests refused to follow the instructions, have been discarded. The room is perhaps too small for the numbers in the hotel, but it too is kept clean, well stocked and pleasantly managed. 
We too were using Return Points and there was no feeling of being given second best. With so much still to see and do in New York I am sure we will be back.

title: “Solid, business-traveler frendly hotel”
text: This hotel is about 5 minutes from my company's office in San Diego and this is my first time staying here as I typically stay downtown or in LaJolla. The hotel is typical for a Courtyard and has all the amenities a business traveler appreciates: spacious room with a mini-fridge which is helpful for those doing a longer stay and lots of electrical outlets for all your devices as well as an iPod docking station. Nice desk and comfortable office chair in the room which makes it easy to work when needed. The hotel has a pretty good gym with lots of machines although one morning I was shocked to see all the treadmills were being used. In this case, I ended up taking my run outside and did a few miles around the area of the hotel which was pleasant. There are lots of restaurants near the hotel and it's a short ride to downtown (less than 20 minutes) and the airport. The hotel has a humongous lounge area including bar and a lovely outdoor patio with a fireplace. My colleagues and I hung out at the bar one night and the outdoor patio another and both were pleasant. I didn't eat in the hotel so I can't speak to the food but I saw others eating and their plates looked pretty good. Overall I had a nice stay here and would consider staying here again the next time I come to our San Diego office.

title: “Outstanding Customer Service And Excellent Guest Recommendation”
text:
I had the recent occasion to be a guest at your fine hotel with the dates of my stay being Saturday, December 24th, 2011 thru Monday, December 26th, 2011, and upon my arrival on Saturday the 24th, I was promptly and politely greeted by guest services agent Randy Alan Ogoff who said he would be right with me as he was attending to the check-in needs of another hotel guest. I was then quickly assisted with my check-in by the on-duty security guard who was also polite and offered me a cordial greeting to your fine hotel. I was checked in and went to my room which I believe was #805.
Upon entering my room I observed a rather small television in the room and thought for a 3 star hotel, they should have flat screen televisions by now and at this time I went down to the front desk and spoke with G.S. A. Randy Alan Ogoff. I asked him if there were any other rooms available with perhaps a larger television. I then offered him my reasons for being in New York City during the Christmas Holiday. In short, my parents and sister were killed last year in a motor vehicle accident and I had no immediate family anywhere in the New England area and that my partner of 5 years and myself were here in New York City to get away and kind of enjoy but yet forget about the holiday because it is such a tragic time for me in my life. It was around the holidays that my family was killed by an off duty truck driver who was also drunk behind the wheel of his large truck. G.S.A. Ogoff handed me a room key and told me to check out a room, I believe it was #1205 to see if there was a larger television in that room. I was saddened to find that that room also had a very small television with a vhs tape player installed as well. We are clearly in the DVD era and the hotel really needs to upgrade their televisions. I promptly returned to the front desk and upon my arrival G.S.A. Ogoff handed me an envelope and said based on my family circumstances and my request for a larger television as I would be spending a good deal of time in my room for the two days that I would be a guest in your hotel, he had upgraded me to a junior suite at no additional charge for the two day stay. I was just beyond words and quickly expressed my gratitude and thanked him kindly for being such a sweet, caring and concerned about his guests employee of the hotel.
I went up to my junior suite, room # 1110 I believe and found it to be a beautiful room with a flat screen television and large enough for me and my partner to enjoy for the two day stay at the hotel. And throughout my entire stay I bumped into, said hello to and spoke with G.S.A. Randy Alan Ogoff on many occasions and always found him to be smiling, kind, caring, gentle, and willing to help me in any way possible. He went well above and beyond what one would expect from a guest services agent at any hotel, let alone The Roger Smith Hotel! He is indeed an asset to your fine hotel and I can’t say enough about this man and the wonderful way I was treated as a guest during my stay at the hotel. I truly wish all guest services agents and front desk personnel at all other hotels were as nice and caring about their guests as Randy Alan Ogoff was and is for and from what I observed all of the guests that came and went at the hotel. He was always smiling and seemed truly happy to be at work during the Christmas holiday weekend…unlike many other employees that I observed in other stores and restaurants in the city during my stay. Many clearly did not like the fact they had to work during the holidays…G.S.A. Randy Alan Ogoff was indeed the exception to the rule and I believe he is truly an asset to be appreciated as an employee of The Roger Smith Hotel.
Upon getting home from my little vacation, I could not wait to sit down and compose this letter and send it off to you at the hotel to tell you about my wonderful and pleasing experience and that I will surely be staying at your hotel in the future should I be returning to the fine city of New York in the future.
If you would like to reach me for any reason as it relates to this letter and my personal opinions and observations of Guest Services Agent Randy Alan Ogoff, please do not hesitate to contact me at the address, phone number or email address listed above. I would be happy to provide you with any and all information that you may request as it relates to my letter.
I truly enjoyed my stay at The Roger Smith Hotel because it is s very beautiful hotel, the junior suite I stayed in was gorgeous and because G.S.A. Ogoff went well above and beyond his job description and duties to see to it that I, as a guest of the hotel, enjoyed my stay and was comfortable.
Thank you in advance for your time, patience and cooperation as it relates to my letter of personal thanks and reference about the fine work ethics and skills that G.S.A. Randy Alan Ogoff possess and implements while employed at The Roger Smith Hotel. He is an asset that should never be allowed to leave!
Very Truly Yours;
Richard W. Thunberg Jr.

title: “Dark and disappointing”
text:
I stayed at the Bryant for 3 nights from a Saturday to a Tuesday last week. It was my first time staying there. It was a hugely disappointing experience.
The Bryant is a great location. That is it's best feature.
 However the room I had was unbelievably dark...in fact the whole hotel is in perpetual twilight. This may be regarded as trendy but for me it was just simply too dark and depressing. During the morning I had all the lights on in my room to simply sit and work on my laptop. 
The room itself was small, bland and dark. The room table looked like something made by a 1st year woodwork student. I had to be within 4 feet of the TV to turn the power button on...simple things that completely drive a guest crazy.
All this would be fine if it was cheap...but it is an expensive hotel. I paid $55 for a breakfast....I felt positively guilty afterwards.
The staff are very friendly but it is easy to be friendly when the product is overpriced, dark and depressing. 
I will not stay there again...ever. I can do much better

title: “Awesome affordable hotel with Great Service, Location and Amenities”
text:
Stayed in a king suite and room was very nice. Had a separator between bed and L shaped comfy sofa. GIANT HD Tv in the room that was on a swivel and could be seen from the living room or bed. Tv reception was good as hotel has several HD channels. Hotel was very clean and has very nice people working there. Monica Robinson, Director of Sales was especially nice and cordial. The complimentary breakfast is simple, but efficient. Complimentary high speed internet was fast and efficient. Location is close to main road with supermarkets, restaurants, etc. Although across the street from a fast food joint, you will need a rental car for sure.
Will definitely stay here again when visiting the area.

title: “Hotel Boheme - Home Away from Home”
text: This little gem of a hotel is located in the heart of North Beach (SF's Little Italy). The location is an easy walk to the Financial District, Chinatown, and Fisherman's Wharf. The hotel is a second and third floor walk up so you will need to carry your bags. The front desk staff greet you by name, ask how your day was, and leave a complimentary sherry out in the evenings for a nightcap. There are a zillion restaurants, carry outs, and ATMs in the neighborhood. The staff graciously provide tips and directions to local restaurants and places to sight see. Stan always asked if his dining recommendations met our expectations - they did. The rooms are cozy, tastefully decorated, and clean. Room 107 offered a small wicker table and chairs for desk use. The TVs are small and the outlets are few. The free WiFi cut in and out a bit. Charles was happy to print a document when needed for a meeting - quickly and at no extra cost. If you want a great location and a comfortable room this is the place. They also made flawless arrangements for an airport shuttle. If you are a light sleeper, ask for a room on the quiet side of the building. If you want to feel like part of the neighborhood instead of a visitor in some impersonal business hotel, this is the place for you. A great find!!

title: “Great for Fly In/Fly Out Business Meetings”
text:
Have hosted several fly in/fly out gatherings at the O Hare Hilton in the past few months. Couldn't be better.
Accommodations are well maintained for a large airport hotel. The housekeeping crew seems busy all day long so I've never had a problem with showing up too early for a room. They know their clientele's schedule.
The staff seems to be trying to be accommodating. Sometimes I think they they should have a few more folks at the desks but when things back up they start handing out waters to those waiting in line. A nice touch and courtesy that seems typical throughout the hotel.
I really like the Hilton Honors floor with the view of the runway. You can't beat looking down at the folks riding the shuttles, taxis, and buses who are being dropped off at the airport check in counters and realizing with gratitude that, baring severe security delays, you are only 8 - 10 minutes from phone check out in your room to standing at your boarding gate!. 
The two restaurants are both very good and the breakfast is especially wonderful. (And at Christmas time, the music at breakfast was spectacular -- a welcome change from the typical elevator Santa music.) One warning about the Gaslight Club. One of the women in our party was really offended at the very revealing Gay 90's fishnet garb of the waitresses. You might want to ask to see a waitress as well as a menu before deciding whether you'd rather go for Italian at Adiorno's!

title: “Really cool hotel and the most confortable bed ever.”
text:
This is an amazingly cool hotel, I loved loved loved it. Fantastic location.
Downsides - tiny room for $400 a night including tax - although seriously we still loved the hotel and will absolutely go back. No prices on the (extensive) mini-bar meant that I paid $8 a bottle for three of the smallest bottles of water (200ml?), and didn't know how much I would have to pay if I used the fascinating personal oxygen cannister. Taxis don't know where it is - is it uncool to put a name outside? In fact that last point is almost an upside as well....
Upsides - where do I start? Must be with the bed, which was like no other. This was at the end of a trip where we had slept in 14 beds in some great hotels, and this one was in a completely different league. So very comfortable, plus amazingly comfortable pillows and duvet - going to NY and raving about a hotel bed seems somehow wrong on all sorts of levels, but there you go. Other upsides - lovely staff - so friendly, great bar area, nice glass of wine when you arrive. Plenty of anecdotes for later - for example the bar is dark and when my husband wanted to read, a very friendly member of staff suggested the library. This was equally dark, so the helpful man brought him a scented candle to read by....21st century New York City!.

title: “A Good Night”
text: Needed a place to stay for a quick one night trip to SF on President's holiday weekend. We spend quite a few weekends in SF and usually "bid" for a hotel room. Having no luck with that route, decided to check out Kimpton Hotels. We have stayed at two other Kimpton properties, The Palomar and the The Prescott. I was delighted to find that the Harbor Court Hotel was having a special rate for the holiday weekend of $109 per night. Checked out the reviews on Tripadvisor and the general theme was that the hotel was good but the rooms were small. Booked the room and headed for SF. The location is good at the embarcadero although a good walk or muni is needed for a trip to Union Square. The front desk staff were friendly and efficient. We stayed in #616 which was SMALL but well appointed and the bathroom was well stocked. Overall we had a comfortable stay and would definitely consider the Harbor Court again if the circumstances dictated it.

title: “Great update”
text: With the Reno almost done, the lobby and rooms are great / bathroom was very small and I hate that there is no minibar just a fridge - this needs to be fixed it's crazy. Wireless is ok and I'll return

title: “Great PLACE and great LOCATION”
text: My friends and I stayed april 4 for an event at reliant. It is a great location with friendly staff the suite that we had originally requested was not available but they were able to upgrade us to a bigger suite witch worked out better for us since there was three of us it was a two bedroom suite one room had a king bed and the other room had two queens and living room area was great it was not too small and not to big perfect size with plenty of sitting space. Everything in the room work perfectly!. The only down side was that you have to pay six dollars a night to park there but other than that everything was perfect!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Gina K.”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at the Inn at Longwood to visit our daughter overnight on June 30, 2012. Everthing was wonderful from the room, staff to the excellent breakfast. Thank you Longwood!!

title: “Great location, great staff, lovely room”
text:
I did a lot of research before booking an ( inexpensive-relatively) hotel for a 4 night stay . Booked a standard two bed-room. When we got there, they said the only such room that was available was on the 3rd floor and would be too noisy so they upgraded us to a suite on the 12th floor. It worked out sooooo well for us, as as soon as we got back to the room at night, my son could go into the bedroom and watch cartoons ( we dont have TV at home, so this was part of the thrill for him!) and my sister and i could talk/plan/watch better shows. I think I read of another case of this exact thing happening to another family, down to the fllors, which is kind of odd, but it worked out really really well for us. 
Also had read that the desk staff was surly, which was absolutely NOT THE CASE when we were there. Everyone was very friendly, efficient. 
Also read that the rooms were hot. Not so with our AC unit. It was all really really nice. Great value for the money, great location in a funky neighbourhood, and really close to the subway.

title: “Pretty stuck on itself”
text: Got to town early, room not ready, left bags and went to riverwalk. Nice enuf, sat and people watched after one pass back and forth, needn't come back again. Back to hotel, Room finally ready. Staff just so so, we are too old to matter. Hallways dark, room modern, which i like. Uber hip lounge and restaurant but mike didn't want beef cheeks for dinner so we went to Landry's for seafood. Yuck, worst meal ever. Morning.. Shower is cool but built for basketball players, i'm 5'1"" couldn't reach robe hook over door. HA

title: “How this hotel is not the top ranked in San Jose is beyond me..”
text: This was the nicest hotel I've stayed at. Ever. I was in town for a conference at a local hospital and upon arrival was greeted by everyone in sight. Check-in was smooth with no issues. My room was on the 17th floor with an excellent view of the mountains. Very large room and bathroom, beds were super comfortable. There is an European bakery attached to the hotel that is AMAZING and reasonably priced. Very close to restaurants and I felt safe walking around the area by myself. If I had to make one complaint, is that the sink in the bathroom was a little slow draining. And that's extremely minor b/c it didn't effect my stay at all. LOVE the Fairmont.

title: “Good Hotel”
text: The Hotel was quite smart, The rooms were spacious and clean and the staff on the desk were helpful and friendly. Although there was a bar area and a restaurant we didn't use either for breakfast. we brought in preparded fruit and Yogurt and kept it in the fridge ( I hate having to get dressed and go looking for a place to eat) and popped down to starbucks for a morning coffee. We did however have a snack in the bar area the night we arrived, Burgers and chips & salad ( My husband said the grill needed cleaning as his char grilled burger tasted sour).Fairly good area for the shops etc a good walk to the parks and the Cheers bar. We didn't go up the Prudential as it was raining but the shopping was ok. Visited the area around Faneuil Hall - a good place to eat and shop.

title: “exclusive location”
text:
very clean, but very basic service. Parking is addiitionally charged at around 45 usd/night. 
We had reservation for months before we came and on our arrival there was no room available. Finally, we have been given a very noisy room, facing the tram street. the isolation is not good at all. 
there is a free internet access provided

title: “The bed was nice”
text:
It is a lovely looking hotel and the bed (Hastens) is fabulous. Also, great location - one of the major draws. The staff were just "okay" when we checked in, but could have been better considering they screwed up our reservation.
Our issue was with the non-existent stay 3 and pay for 2 night deal they advertised (http://hotelandra.com/packages/stay-3-pay-2/). In the end, we paid for 3 nights in a extremely expensive room and they graciously took $40 off the bill. I even left a note when I booked online to confirm the deal and rate, which they didn't.
Would I stay again? Probably not. There are better deals in Belltown.

title: “Bathroom doors are strange!”
text: The Omni is a beautiful hotel located in a fantastic area of San Diego. We loved the location. The strange thing about the hotel is the bathroom doors. They are frosted glass schich makes everyone aware in the middle of the night when you need to use the facilities. It also doesn't seal which makes your business known to all. A little uncomfortable for sharing rooms with others that you are not very close with. Great pool!

title: “perfect stay”
text: I stayed at The Monaco April 17-20 and my visit was nearly perfect. I arrived by 1 pm and was pleasantly surprised to learn that my room was ready. It was comfortable with luxurious linens. I ordered room service the first evening and it was delicious and delivered quickly. I did not eat at the Grand Cafe, but did walk through.. it's beautiful and does a bustling business. Both common areas have fireplaces and lots of comfortable furniture. A great place to mingle at Happy Hour.. or to read and relax. The concierge was very helpful to me, and I enjoyed being able to access my e-mail in the Business Center (there was a small charge). The hotel completely met my needs. I was attending a conference and we were encouraged to stay at the Marriott or Hilton - but no one I spoke to was as happy as I was at the Monaco!

title: “An ideal place for a couple of nights.”
text:
We stayed here for three nights whilst on a short break to New York. The rooms are very small but very clean and well appointed. Ideal location, just a short stroll from Central Park and Broadway. The hotel offers excellent friendly service and is very trendy with a good bar and restaurant, and the roof terrace is superb. We used the hotel purely as somewhere to lay our heads as we were out sightseeing from dawn to dusk. If breakfast is not included in your deal, I suggest the Applejack Diner at the corner of 230 W. 55th St. and Broadway, a couple of hundred yards away, plenty to eat and excellent service.
Would definately stay here again.

title: “Perfect”
text: After alot of trawling for a fab place to stay this was perfect. Location walkable to times square, 5th avenue and close to tube stations. Local people in the area friendly and fab bagel place on 3rd ave and funky rooftop bar directly across the road. The darker style rooms were a blessing for resting and the breakfast is a nice touch that it's free but as been said before don't worry if you miss it. The staff are lovely and helpful and the rooms kept spotless. The beds and pillows were fantastic along with the small bathtub to rest your feet. It was good to have tea/coffee fascilities in the room. We would stay again if we are to come back to NYC. P.S. the Indian restaurant next door is also worth a visit.

title: “Good quality hotel, but not spectacular”
text: I ve stayed here for 7 days in April 2010, eight floor (out of 9). As PC Platinum member got free wireless internet (that would otherwise cost me 10 USD/day), free parking (otherwise 19 USD/day), and as I booked executive room also free breakfast. Breakfast is standard american, nothing special and suprising. Hotel is very clean, house keeping is doing good job, but are on some days very late (room not cleaned until 3pm). Otherwise, good hotel on good location.

title: “Nice Hotel but not if your a light sleeper”
text:
Me and my husband were in San Francisco for a weekend getaway. We chose this hotel because my husband is with the Priority Club. So it was nice because we got an upgrade to the 14th floor. The room and bathroom was nice and clean. It seem like the hotel has been remodeled since the decor was very modern.
We also had dinner within the hotel because it was convenient. Service in the beginning wasn't that great. There was no host when first arriving at restaurant. After being seated we waited for our server who actually approached another couple who got seated 5 mins after us. It didn't help that I was very, very hungry so I made sure to get the waiter's attention so that our order went in as soon as possible. They offered a menu as well as, their buffet. The buffet seemed nice but I'm not a buffet person. So I ordered calamari as an appetizer, which was okay. As my entree, I had the NY Steak and my husband ordered Chicken Alfredo. We were both pleased with our food.
After attending an event, we went to our room which was situated in a way that picked up the traffic noise from Market St. Fortunately, I was so tired that it didn't bother me come time to sleep. But if you are a light sleeper you may want to ask for a room that avoids the street. If they offer one. The bed on the other had was very comfortable.
Just keep in mind this is a Holiday Inn Hotel and not "HI Express". So they have breakfast just don't expect a free breakfast. You also have to pay for parking but with SF hotels, this is unavoidable. Overall, the hotel was nice but I don't think I'd stay more than one night because of all the street noise.

title: “good location , expensive, stylish”
text:
near beverly hills and hollywood, very stilish, colored, of couse expensive. each room is different.
we reserved in advance the big roof mirror room but we got a standard room, without any explication, and without paying less..So, not really an excellent experience..
private parking inside, complimentary, with a guy who park your car and evry time wants a tip..And not just a small tip..
don't know if I would suggest it..Of course really nice and well furnished but maybe too expensive and pretentious..

title: “Outstanding!”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Amalfi over Memorial Day weekend. I found a great deal on travelzoo.com and I'm glad we found this hotel. It is in a great location, about two blocks north of the river and about three blocks west of Michigan Avenue. The hotel features a small lobby, but the service at check-in was friendly and efficient. Our room was at the end of the hall and was large. I would say the features of the room were comparable with most other luxury hotels in Chicago. The room was very clean and comfortable and the king bed was great! My wife and I especially liked the free continental breakfast and the free evening reception on the 6th floor. The only drawback of our stay was that our room was right above an alley, which was constantly noisy. But, this was a minor setback compared to everything we loved about the hotel. I would definitely recommend the Amalfi to anyone staying in Chicago. 
TIP: Do not park at the hotel. Way too expensive. There is a parking garage about two blocks away on LaSalle and Kinzie that charges way less.

title: “had trouble canceling!”
text: Warning: I canceled an October reservation for Hotel 140 in January and misplaced proof of same, then received an e-mail before starting our October trip saying they were looking forward to our visit! I called to cancel again and received e-mail confirmation. Upon returning from our trip I discovered an e-mail saying we had been a no-show and our credit card had been charged for one nights' stay. It took several e-mails and phone calls to clear this up. Be sure to keep any cancelation proof!

title: “Pleasantly surprised at cleanliness and roominess”
text: We were staying overnight in San Francisco during Labor day weekend and out of desire not to spend $400 on a room for a Holiday Inn we found this place on Tripadvisor. When we first pulled up I couldn't believe their idea of a parking garage consisted of 10 spots...don't let that trick you like it did me because there's another level underground. The parking was ample and spacious there. On first taking the elevator up to our floor I feared the worst because the ride up was slow and run down. Walking into our room I was speechless--for the price we paid the room was incredibly roomy with comfy chairs, a desk and still enough room to run around if we wanted to and best of all super clean!!!!! The bathroom had a sterile white theme but wow was it clean up to my standards! I was so thrilled for the luck we had on finding such a place. The street the hotel is located on is really busy and you'll need to take a car to see the touristy stuff but its worth it. This place is a great find and I hope the management decides to keep up with such stellar upkeep. :)

title: “Location and service”
text: Love the location and service beyond the norm. Would highly consider coming back next New York trip

title: “You get what you pay for”
text: I was visiting family so I wanted to find a hotel close to the lower valley. Since I wasn't going to spend much time in the room I opted to select a cheaper hotel. I really don't care about the brand name I just want a clean, comfortable, convenient and safe hotel. With this hotel I got what I paid for. It wasn't the fanciest, no frills or thrills which is fine however the hotel is in serious need of renovation. It's old and you can tell. The overall room was decent; it could've been cleaner. I had several issues during my stay and had to call the front desk numerous times. I will say that the front desk was very responsive in addressing my issues which was nice. Near the night stand it smelled moldy like the carpet had gotten wet and never dried. The first night I opened up a drawer to put my clothes in it and there was a pizza box in it. Several times during my stay the T.V. signal kept going out. At one point I received a call back advising the technician was gone for the day so they couldn't send someone to fix my T.V. They did offer to move me to another room. Fortunately I was able to get the T.V. to work on my own and declined the offer but it was nice they offere. The blow dryer didn't work so I had to call again to have someone come fix it. The morning that I checked out I got up really early to take a shower for my 6 am flight. The water was ice cold and didn't warm up until I was ready to get out. The bed was pretty comfortable. I would stay at this hotel again if it was a last resort however it wouldn't be my first choice. There is a Denny's next to it which is convenient for meals. The hotel is pretty close to I-10 but I didn't hear the traffic since my room wasn't facing the interstate.

title: “The worst hotel I have ever stayed at!”
text:
I had a horrible experience at the HJotel Des Arts. When we checked in at 3pm our room was not ready. We waited 45 minutes before 
getting into our room. I was also told that I could not park in the unloading 
zone as they would have me towed, however on two other occasions I heard them 
tell clients that 10 min would be okay. Next the shower barely trickled...
