though when I mentioned this to the manager he basically said that if I was 
expecting a nice shower I should have stayed at a Hilton...I didn't know that 
boutique hotels don't think that guests like water pressure...
Next we were woken up at 130 by kids pounding on our hotel door to see if we 
had a lighter.
The next day my husband and I walked in on the hotel maid looking through our previous days shopping 
bag... When I told them that I was unhappy they were 
rude and condescending. They told me that the manager doesn't work
weekends. When I spoke to Hero (the manager) he was more rude and 
condescending then his receptionists. I too have bug bites!
They try to nickle and dime you and don't have valet or people skills stay away from this hotel, if at all possible!

title: “DUMP - Don't stay there, EVER!!!”
text: The place is filthy, I'd expect to find a cleaner bathroom in a crackhouse! The staff have no control over the guests and parties carried on, on both levels of balconies, until after 3am. Repeated complaints had no effect and no got any sleep. In the morning we told the desk clerk how unhappy we were and his answer was " Guess you shouldn't have stayed here." I did but I'm urging everyone else to avoid this dump like the plague, you'd be better off sleeping in your car!!!

title: “Central location for exploring NY”
text: We enjoyed 5 days at the Grand Hyatt before our cruise departed. Booked by our travel agent, she said it was a deal, we loved the location, central to everything. Our room was ok, a little small, but comfortable. At check-in the clerk asked about our plans. I thought, how nice, and started telling her how excited we were to be in NY. She got this look on her face and continued an up-sale of some theater tickets. Oh, I got it. She was not being personally friendly or interested in us, just doing her job of pushing the services from a script. So I put my heart back in my pocket, settled down and enjoyed the rest of my stay. Services were fine, they cleaned the room and changed the sheets. But the big draw is LOCATION. Amazing. Try to get a better price and avoid what looks like a car payment each day you stay.

title: “Good position, good price but you get what you pay for!”
text: The reception staff were really friendly and helpful especially with putting our belongings in the safe. Cleanliness of the bathrooms was great but the bedroom was not that clean. The blanket looked very worn and I'm not entirely sure the sheet was clean. I would definitely stay here again because of the price and position but it could do with improvement.

title: “Would stay there any time”
text:
Business was all day and work part of the night in the room. The hotel has great services that made my week there much easier. Door cards for breakfast, great dine-in menu--never got anything that wasn't good and I ate in the room 4 nights. Prices were very reasonable. The mini bar had 2 of my favorite things. Wake up calls were never late. Staff was so nice and went out of their way to be helpful and friendly.
I've stayed at a lot of downtown upscale hotels and this was by far the best as far as quality of food and the outstanding guest services are concerned.
Pam (from Houston)
Didn't have a car so didn't use parking or the spa. Never ate in the restaurant--always used room service.

title: “Boston stay.”
text: We stayed here for 5 nights in October. I would highly recommend this hotel. We had a room on the 23 rd floor. I had read a lot of complaints about the lifts been slow etc but we had no problems. The only negative is that our room was next to the lift shafts and it was very annoying especially during the night. The beds are very comfy and the rooms were spacious and very clean and comfortable. This is a great hotel to stay in when sightseeing in Boston and I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
the service in the hotel was excellent, everyone who worked there were so friendly and so helpful. the rooms are not big but for the price we paid and the amount of time you spend in there it is definitely worth it. the beds are comfortable and we always came back to a room that had been cleaned. 
there are no faults with this hotel whatsoever. we will definitely be staying there again when we go back to new york.

title: “unexpected service”
text: checked in clerk helped find coupon in book saved 20 dollars. woke up with migraine asked to pay for extra 4 hours stay .said we could stay no charge .checked out at1 pm manager chris was super. b bobby selder pgh pa

title: “Outstanding”
text: Luxurious accommodations including a huge room with an extraordinarily comfortable mattress and pillows. The bathroom was incredible with a jacuzzi tub, seperate shower, 2 vanities, and plush robes all done in granite and marble. Great location if you're flying into Seattle and plan on visiting Mt. Ranier.

title: “Really nice stay, near HP Pavillion”
text: My son and I stayed there to see the men's gymnastics national finals. We parked and never had to drive again. Easy walk to some nice restaurants and the Pavillion. I liked the grounds, nice landscaping, the hotel had a nice look to it. The breakfast was great, the dinner was ok (don't expect much, but hey it is free). The room was good, but had a couple of things that need attention, otherwise, for the price, it would get 5 stars. You can't go wrong if you are looking for a nice place to sleep and save some cash.

title: “Wonderful Hotel and Staff”
text: I love this hotel. It is one of the best that I have stayed in. The lobby was beautiful and the room was nice and comfortable. The made services was terrific. No matter what time we left the room it was made up when we came back. I asked the maid for a couple of extras and she was very nice and friendly. That is what I liked about the hotel the staff was so nice and friendly. I was there with my daughter for a girl's weekend from Thursday - Sunday. Everyone from the doorman to the concierge to the people at the desk etc. was wonderful. I can't say enough good about this hotel. Yes the bathroom was small, but I wasn't moving into the room. I was just staying there a few days and was hardly in the room anyway. I will definitely stay there again

title: “Best on a budget”
text: If you are one of those travellers with a tight set of needs, then go for this. Close to Central Park - good for your morning activities, close to Times Square - good for evening recreation, 2 cafe options, just above a tube station, surrounded by restaurants, no nonsense service, just excuse the always bustling lobby completes the offerings. One of those hotels that you can't go wrong with.

title: “The good, the bad, and the ugly.....”
text:
The good: the room was clean, the bed was comfortable and it's close to the airport.
The bad: the place has a sketchy vibe, it wouldn't hurt to run a vacuum over the floors in the restaurant and the public areas.......just doesn't look all the clean.
The ugly: bags of trash left overnight in the hallway, stained filthy carpet in the elevator, and the restaurant seats, bored gormless looking reception staff, and worn out looking bathrooms with no bath tub.
Verdict: No way this is a three star hotel. Go another two exits to Quebec St and stay at one of the hotels there. You will pay less and and the place will be clean and professional.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This is a great hotel for anyone travelling to New York. It was our first time in New York and it had a great location, based in Times Square with broadway shows at a walking distance. The rooms were excellent, we had a good view of times sqaure and both room and bathroom were really spacious & clean. I would go back again myself.

title: “I can't possibly imagine a better place to stay in New York”
text:
Look, this hotel is in downtown New York. It's a stepping stone away from Times Square, a casual jog away from Central Park and mere minutes away from the Empire State Building. Please, please do not expect that you will get a large room!
So, if you resign yourself to the fact that your room here is probably going to be smaller than your home bedroom, then there is simply nothing else negative to say about it. As stated before, the location is just perfect. The rooms themselves are exquisitely finished to the highest standard that I recall ever seeing in a hotel. It's not cheap, but by New York standards, it's certainly not expensive either and represents great value for money. 
In short, it's just a brilliant place to stay in New York. Highly recommended.

title: “Good, friendly hotel in a great location”
text:
Just returned from 5 nights at the Shelburne. A good, friendly & comfortable place to stay in a lovely area. Very friendly & well-trained staff. Restaurant staff are especially friendly and the breakfasts are a distinct improvement on the usual hotel fare. Rooms are newly renovated - spacious and bright with large, really comfy beds.
Some small details need attention - there were two very useful LED reading lights attached to each side of the bed, but neither was working in my room.
You will probably have to pay a little more to stay here but it's definitely worth it.

title: “With a little work, could be great”
text: Spent 5 nights here with my family. Got guaranteed connecting rooms! Almost unheard of anywhere else. Rooms were roomy with a decided lack of storage. Noticed one room had an umbrella but ours didn't. We had two glasses but they had only one? Recently updated and adequately comfortable with the exception of lack of control on temperature. loved the burger bar, Knaves lounge, and the ultra expensive and delicious Norma's. Most of the concierge were quite helpful, but ran into some condescension, hey I'm from the sticks and don't understand mass transit. Only real gripe is when we showed up at 3:30 they said our 2nd room wasn't ready? How is this acceptable and what were you willing to do to compensate us? Never got an answer.

title: “TOP NOTCH!!”
text: My hubby and I stayed @ the Embassy Suites this past weekend to celebrate our anniversary. And boy...were we surprised at the absolute, genuine hospitality of the whole staff. We couldn't have asked for a better place to stay! SO VERY CLEAN! The rooms were just the right size for us. Everyone there was so helpful. It is located so very close to restaraunts, shopping, etc. Lina (the front desk agent) is the BEST!!! We will surely stay here again. The comp breakfast was great! It was all great! NO KIDDING! Eugene (the shuttle driver) was just wonderful. My hubby and I enjoyed his conversation. Just all around great people and hotel!

title: “Excellent! Would Use Again!”
text: Had a 4 night stay in what I would describe as a huge room, 2 of us 2 double beds & loads of space to swing a cat! We were in 1702 on top floor, room had windows on 3 sides & a view from one room looked down towards the East River, location was great, everything touristy within walking distance. Booked directly with the hotel & got a good deal which basically meant we had 3 nights for the price of 4, could not beat their price on any of the hotel booking sites, so well worth checking out the hotel site first imo.

title: “Our stay in this hotel was extremely fantastic”
text:
Specially the location (Chelsea, Meatpacking District and Greenwich Village on walking distance). And the subway in 14th with 8th Ave. The room was really comfortable and being a single for two was more than enough. 
Some other great things: the Daily News, a sheet of paper with proposals for the day and the breakfast, incredible (specially the onion's bagels and the cookies)
The only thing to comment: no lift. The 5th floor is so high specially if you do long trips walking in the city.

title: “Best in its class in downtown Denver”
text: I have stayed at a number of hotels in downtown Denver for both business and pleasure, and on my most recent trip I stayed at the Downtown Westin. For the price point, this Westin is heads above the other downtown hotels in its class. The location in the Tabor Center is hard to beat - Palm Restaurant and Starbucks in the lobby, the best of Lodo right out the front door. This Westin does justice to the Starwood brand - large and recently renovated rooms and bathrooms, comfy beds, flat screen tvs, mountain views. My only recommendations are that (1) the hotel should offer free wireless internet to guests and (2) that the hotel could improve its restaurant (where I admittedly only ate breakfast) - the food was great (albeit, as you would expect, overpriced), but the oversized tables are awkward and the decor is nothing to write home about. All and all, a very satisfying stay.

title: “Great Location, Great Food”
text: If you want to stay on the upper east side, it's a superb location. Overall, the staff was great - especially front desk staff that was extremely helpful. We did not use the spa but it is supposed to be amazing. The amenities, bed linens, quality of materials used in the rooms was very nice and comfortable. If you didn't know, Cafe Bouloud is in the hotel but also provides the food for the entire hotel - including the bar, room service, and a gorgeous outdoor penthouse bar/lounge = so the food is truly first class. If you need a spacious room then look elsewhere. The only other negative thing I can say about the hotel are that the housekeeping service was a bit slow to both get the rooms cleaned, and if we left later they didn't get back to cleaning the room until late in the day despite us calling. I do expect more from a hotel of this category in this respect. i also found it offensive they charged so much for wireless internet given the room rate.

title: “Kick back and enjoy the ride....”
text: I needed a central location and a close restaurant (in house) for a business trip to San Diego. What I received in the Lafayette was a great deal, great restaurant, pool and atmosphere that helped my trip turn out relaxing and so incredibly enjoyable! The decor is classic old Hollywood and the rooms perfectly sized. The staff appeared so happy-smiling and greeting me always. I saw a ballroom-the Mississippi -downstairs and it is where I will be booking my company Christmas party. The whole place is full of little 'discoveries' to find..details..courtyards, giant chess set, pool, outdoor spots, indoor spots..little surprises that kept my stay delightful. I am completely in love with this place! What a great find indeed! Eat at the Imig's restaurant and you will never want to leave...comfort food with zing. It's crazy-good!

title: “Too hipster for me”
text:
I'm only 31 and I felt I needed to get glasses because it was so freaking dark in there. The service was good. The room was a good size but I need light people! I liked the kitchy touches. 
Not a fan of the Breslin though. I booked there especially to eat the burger and it was so salty that I couldn't finish it. Also we sat next to these obnoxious guys that gave New Yorkers a bad name. They were trying to out do each other with how awesome they both were. I lost count after the first 50 high fives they gave each other. They were so bad people moved away from them. We moved to the Standard for the rest of our stay and I am glad we did. Sorry Ace!

title: “Good value for the price”
text: This is a good choice for the area, especially at the very reasonable price we paid. It is easy to get to from I-40 and is close to the Wolfchase Galleria mall. Check in was quick and friendly. The hotel appears to be new, so all of the fixtures and furnishings that we saw were in good shape and attractive. The room was reasonably sized and well organized, including a refrigerator and microwave. The beds were very comfortable, although the pillows were odd -- I'm not sure what they are filled with but they weren't like typical pillows. Nevertheless, they didn't give us any problems. Wifi worked well from the room. The breakfast was fine. Across the board, the amenities at La Quinta are slightly below that of chains like Hampton or Holiday Inn Express (such as a slightly less generous breakfast buffet), but the hotel is new, well maintained and the staff was pleasant, so we had no complaints.

title: “Great hotel with amazing views and friendly staff”
text: Stayed at Hyatt Regency McCormick Place June 20-23, 2012. This was my first trip to Chicago, and I must say, the staff and their legendary customer service made my trip even better. I first arrive to check in, and I am acknowledged at a Hyatt Platinum Member, and as a result, I find out I've been upgraded to a skyline executive suite. A room that usually runs 400-600 a night, and they upgraded me for no extra cost. I didn't even ask for it! Got the room key, and the bellman, a very tall man with a Jamacian accent (wish I could remember his name!) loaded our luggage up and said he would take it to our room while we parked our car (Self parking is 32 bucks, not bad considering it's 50+ within the Loop) We got to our room on the 32nd floor, and found that our bellman had unloaded everything for us very neatly, had the curtains opened to reveal the full panoramic view of the beautiful Chicago skyline. For the first day of the stay, I had to continuously look out the window to actually make sure I was where I was... My three night stay FLEW by like no other stay before, and I hated to leave. Every single staff member, from the woman that checked me in, to the bellman who brought our luggage up, to the maids who cleaned the room, to the turndown service staff whom left chocolates on my pillow each night, down to the bellman who brought our luggage to our car as we left, I cannot say I've ever experienced such a kind and friendly staff elsewhere. I've already booked me another stay within the next month, just to have a longer experience at the hotel and in Chicago. It's easy to get to, also, right off the Stevenson Expressway (I-55). It wasn't busy at check in, so I cannot attest to how it would be during peak check in time, but my particular experience was one to remember. Hyatt Regency St. Louis has been my destination of choice for the past two years since becoming a Gold Passport member, and I now have a new destination of choice...Hyatt Regency McCormick Place!

title: “Good Business Hotel”
text:
Stayed there last week on business. The room had everything one would expect plus a large flat screen television.
Room overlooked Ground Zero....I think most do. 
If you are interested in exercise you are close to Battery Park and the exercise path near the west side highway. I got 4 or 5 miles of jogging in without feeling stressed about dodging traffic.
Lower Manhattan is still not "right" and certainly lacks the evening options of midtown. But if you must stay in the area this hotel works.

title: “Exellent view of Times Square, Great Suite and Value”
text: Upon arrival, the front desk had our reservation wrong but quickly corrected the problem. We really enjoyed the suite, having 2 tvs and a corner room (conference room) which gave multiple views. Good location. Rooms were clean. Enjoyed the cookies. We did not go to the restaurant. Be careful with the minibar, as it mischarged us and had to get the bill corrected. Overall, we would definitely stay here again.

title: “Loved it! great value for NYC”
text:
My partner and I stayed here for 4 nights and it was great value for NYC. When we arrived we were upgraded to a deluxe room which by new york standards was huge. There was downside, it was on the 5th floor and there is no lift and it faced out on a busy road but that's new york. It didn't bother us too much.
Staff were very friendly and location is great. I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “Wonderful Staff”
text: We arrived for a family retreat meeting family members from all over the country. We booked on the La Quinta site online requesting rooms near each other. upon arriving our request had already been taken care of an our rooms were all together. The staff is some of the most friendly and helpful as any I have encountered. Everyone especially the people at the desk were great going above and beyond making our stay pleasant. We stayed for 4 days. The pool area and lobby made a great visiting area for our party of 12 to visit. This hotel is very family freindly. There were people from Seniors to toddlers enjoying themselves. I will stay here everytime I go to San Antonio!

title: “Loved the UN PLaza”
text:
Have just come back from a week New York and stayed at this fantastic hotel. Although it was absolutely freezing, we had an amazing time! We stayed on the 35th floor and had breathtaking views of the Empire State and the Chrysler building. The night views are just amazing! Hotel room was neat and tidy, just a little dusty- but the bathroom was clean. 
Room was cleaned to a high standard every day. Hotel is in a great location, a short walk to Grand Central Terminal.There is a fantastic chinese restaurant across the street called the Sichuan Palace which delivered to our room after our long days exploring the city. Food is amazing, we lived on the prawn curry & rice for days! I will definately be going back to stay there and I cant wait! But next time I'll be going in the summer!

title: “Great value”
text:
This is not a luxury hotel - but it's great value for the location. It's so close to Rockefeller Plaza and Times Square, you're right in the middle of the action when you step out of the door. The rooms are a decent size (we travel around Europe regularly and just got back from Japan, so we thought they were a pretty normal size. Americans may find the rooms small I suppose.) 
Most of the staff at the desk were very friendly.... the only exception was when I had to pay to use the internet in the lobby, and the printer didn't work. The guy working at the desk told me that the particular computer I was using wasn't connected to the printer. Since I had just paid 50 cents to print, I complained that there was no sign or warning ahead of time.... the response from the guy behind the desk was "Well what do you want me to do about it?!?". Not exactly what I expected to hear. So don't use the computer off to the side to print - it's not connected to the printer, and won't warn you, and will charge you money anyway.
But the rest of the staff were great - I gave one of them our unused Radio City tour tickets because he was really nice and helpful. You can have a cheap and good breakfast next door at one of the two almost identical cafes. Overall it was very good value for money in a very overpriced city.

title: “recongnizing a pleasant staff member”
text:
I would like to take a moment to recognize the outstanding service of Lassandra. She was our "breakfast chef" for the three days we stayed at the Embassy Suites earlier this month (March 5 - 7). Lassandra was extremely pleasant and very helpful each day. She made an awesome omelet and always served it with a smile. We will be returning for business several more times throughout the year and I will be looking forward to Lassandra's service each and every time.
Regards,
Carlene Harper
B Braun Medical

title: “Classic luxury hotel right next door to the White House....”
text:
My mom and I stayed 2 nights here while visiting Washington DC. We had a room with double beds and a small, French balcony that looked directly over to the White House. Truly a gorgeous view!!! The room and bathroom weren't huge, but were very comfortable. The decor is clean and classic with a comfy bed, nice linens, and large closets.
The staff here are extremely professional and treat guests like they should in a 5 star hotel. Our hot water went out and the staff was quick to fix the situation. They gave us the choice of switching rooms or just letting me shower in another room to avoid missing a dinner reservation (the repair in our room was going to take at least 30 minutes).
We ate at the hotel restaurant for breakfast which was good, but not my favorite and extremely pricey ($70 for two people). We felt a bit out of place dining there in regular clothes since most of the patrons were in suits and clearly conducting business. We ate dinner and had drinks in the downstairs bar area (you can get the formal restaurant menu served down there as well). You must stop in...even if it's just for dessert or a cocktail. It is classy, RED, warm, and inviting. We just loved it there. The people watching and ease-dropping weren't too bad either!!!
The location is great....the Metro station is just up the street and there is plenty to walk to nearby (we checked out a great little tea house about 1/2 block down the street and a tasty coffee shop 2-3 blocks away). The gym area is small, but workable. I wished the hotel had a spa....it would have been a nice way to relax. It definitely caters to a bit of an older crowd (I'm 32 and felt a bit too young there) in terms of style and decor and I'm not sure it's the best place to bring kids to (though I did see a couple of families there), but it truly is a 5 star hotel with great service and lovely views.

title: “Good location, friendly staff, reasonable prices”
text:
We stayed here as part of a block of rooms reserved for a wedding in mid-August. We were there for two nights and had no problems at all. I thought the room was a good size for New York City; there was plenty of room to maneuver around the bed and to the closet. The bathroom was also more than adequately sized. A nice perk was the "mini-bar" area that provided a small refrigerator, full size mirror, and an extra sink. 
My only, very small, complaint was that the elevator was quite slow and stuffy. Really, in the grand scheme of things this was nothing more than a minor irritation. If we hadn't been on the 12th floor and already walked all over the city, the stairs would have even solved that problem!
We found the staff to be very friendly and knowledgeable about the area. They were able to quickly give us directions for subway routes to use to get to our destinations. 
We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Be careful of the valet”
text:
Valet charges $42 a night!!! it's unheard of in LA. Someone at the valet stole a set of keys out of the center console(initially we thought they were misplaced), and wasn't returned until we made formal complaints with the hotel management. We also found that one of our house keys was missing!!! We had to have our house locks replaced, as well as having a security system installed. 
I will never stay at this hotel.

title: “pretty decent hotel”
text: I stayed here recently and they were very helpful. They will pick you up and take you back on their shuttle. The staff was friendly and the room was fine. They have a nice little pool, restaurant and bar area, also they have two computers that you can use for free. Overall it was a good place to stay if you aren't looking for a lot of nightlife.

title: “Prime location in Fishermans Wharf”
text: Stayed here on March 25th-29th. When searching for hotels, I wanted a hotel that was recently renovated, and located near alot of stores. This hotel fit that criteria. The rooms were very clean and modern. I requested a high floor, due to reading reviews about the nearby hooters and the music at night. I was given a room on the 3rd floor. There was some music on the Saturday night we were there, but we were so tired, it phase us. There is an Avis rent a car right next door to the hotel, where we rented a car for a one day trip to Napa. There's a Walgreens and Starbucks right around the corner from the hotel which was ver convenient. The staff was very friendly and the concierge even arranged a town car pickup for our ride back to the airport ($45 which is the same price as a taxi). There's a very good breakfast place around the corner called "Hollywood Cafe". We walked to Chinatown and Little Italy with our two small kids (3 and 7 years old). Will definitely stay here on our next trip to SF.

title: “The Crowne Plaza”
text: We always stay at The Crowne Plaza when we are visiting NY City. The rooms are spotless and roomy. Excellent staff. Very helpful and so polite. From the second we arrive the staff can't do enough for you. I will continue to stay at The Crowne Plaza knowing it will continue to be a lovely experience.

title: “Great view!”
text: We recently decided to splurge on a nice hotel in San Diego to celebrate our 25 anniversary. We were very pleased with the "Stay 5 nights, get a night free" with a guaranteed view room at the San Diego Sheraton's West Tower. We stayed in a beautifully refurbished room overlooking the San Diego harbor and skyline. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful. It was pricey, but worth it!

title: “rooms”
text: Nice old charm. Rooms a little small but ok. Texas de Brazil was a great restaurant here and its just outside the door. they have a great exercise gym with quality eguipment. Can't say on the restaurant as we ate outside.

title: “Hospitality Kitchen”
text: I stayed at the Embassy Suites INDY North for 4 days on business recently. Can I tell you I have never been treated so well by anyone in food services in all my years of travel? This hotel has a restaurant and a hospitality kitchen which serves complimentary hot breakfast and a nightly manager's special. Well, as it goes in the IT world I was stuck on a conference call in the room and made it downstairs just minutes after closing. The screen was down and the kitchen already appeared to be cleaned. (BTW it's kept clean even when it is open and serving). This was the third day of my stay so I guess the Chef remembered me. I'd like to think I was getting special treatment because she appeared from nowhere as she saw me shuffling around looking for fruit or whatever I could find. I heard a voice say "have you had anything to eat"? or something to that effect. It sounded so kind, sincere and nurturing to me. I was taken aback because as you know with most places when they’re close they’re close. (doesn’t matter if it is 3-4 minutes after the hour) First, you would not see anyone anywhere and if you did they would be cleaning and closing up shop, and pretending you weren’t there. You gotta picture it, I wasn’t standing at the counter looking for someone the greet me; I was shuffling past the counter when I heard those kind words. After a few uhs an umms I said no actually I haven’t. She ask me what she could make for me…I ordered an omlette which was deliciously made with love and to perfection. (not to hard and not too mushy) Excellent! I had already seen this lady in action earlier in the week with 4-5 orders rolling on the grill at one time and she was handling every guest with the same level of attention and care. 5stars for Lassandra she runs that kitchen likes it’s her own business with love and care for each and every guest I’m sure. I will certainly be back.

title: “Excellent Front Desk Service”
text:
I recently stayed at the Rittenhouse 1715 and have to say that I have never stayed at a hotel where I felt like fmore like amily rather than merely a hotel guest. Marian, Robert, & Renee are excellent - they went "above and beyond the call of duty" in making me feel welcome and helping meet my needs. 
The only negative thing about my stay is $8.00 for a waffle is a ridiculous. At the price to stay at the hotel, waffles should be free. Cheap hotel chains provide FREE waffle breakfasts!
The service is what makes your hotel! Give Marian, Robert, & Renee raises - they are the reason I would come back to visit!

title: “Really small rooms”
text: The place was clean, but I was shocked when I opened the door and saw how small the room was. The bed was small and it crunched when you sat on it, it sounded like it was full of hay. If I didn't pay so much for it, it would have been a good value. I couldn't find a hotel in the city for the Saturday night I was there, so I took what I could get. If I paid $150 for it, I could have dealt with it, but I paid $260.

title: “Excellent value for NYC! Great Location!”
text:
Not much more I can add to what has already been said about this place. It was great! Don't look any further if you want a place to stay in Times Square. 
Positives:
1. Great Location!
2. Excellent Value
3. Large, clean rooms
4. Efficient maid service
5. Good room service
6. Great view (if you face Broadway. Otherwise, you might be looking at something less desirable)
7. Check-in/out was smooth and staff was friendly (especially Rhonda)
8. Bellmen and Security did a good job
9. Great Location! Did I mention that?! Ha, Ha!
Negatives:
1. Conceirge could have been better. Not the friendliest, but I am being pretty picky. However, they were adequate.
2. Billed me twice for internet and overcharged me on the room rate. However, this negative was turned into a positive by their quick response to correct the errors.
Neutral:
1. Did not go to bar or restaurant
2. Did not go to play area
Have fun. I am ready to go back to NYC, but I just got back yesterday, so I guess I've got to do some work before I can go again! I won't look any further than the Doubletree for my next visit. By the way, I'm obsessive-compulsive, so I researched hotels for hours before going with this one. The research paid off!

title: “average!”
text:
The location is good and the hotel is family's friendly- these are the 2 good things we can say.
We arrived Saturday night at around midnight. The room was not ready for 5 people; in spite of the fact we called earlier to make sure it will be ready for 5! They run out of linen. The man from the reception was unwilling to assist us, the security guy notice our frustration and went to the laundry room by himself and helped us!
The breakfast hall is old and the furniture are not clean. The dryer wasn't working properly which was a problem for the families who arrived one by another to use it.

title: “Excellent Hotel, especially for families.”
text: We stayed her for 5 nights last Sep/Oct as part of a 1month US trip. Excellent value & facilities for families: inclusive breakfast was great value; rooms were clean, roomy and well-appointed. The neighbourhood was excellent: we walked daily to/from the metro (15min) and felt completely safe. Concierge was superb - friendly, and fantastic with heaps of local knowledge... The washing machines & dryer were a huge bonus for families: only $1 per load!!! My only gripe was paying for the in-room wi-fi , especially as it wasnt the best in terms of speed... but yes, downstairs they had free Internet. Also, as someone else mentioned here, the in-room coffee was abysmal, and only 2 papercups, that you had to ask to be replaced. But you really cant go past this place for value & amenities for families.

title: “nothing special giving the price paid and expectations!”
text:
Hotel is really nice from the outside, however once you step in, you will see that the lobby is too small, the staff are mehh !
Was supposed to get an upgrade but front desk was like unfortunately we can't !
Room is like 300$ and prepaid, yet the front desk refused to wait till I get a credit card for incidentals and kept me on wait till i got it !
Needed to print a paper, they said we have no access, you will have to pay 5$ and DO IT YOURSELF !
I'm on a 3 weeks vacations and have stayed in many hotels in different cities, this is yes not the worst to be honest, but the most i feel sorry about booking !
Only good thing about the hotel was the location to be honest and that they offered us a room in 50th Floor !

title: “Hotel was nice, service not so much.”
text:
A group of ladies were staying at the Resort for a bachelorette party. We were not loud, obnoxious 'party' girls but we did want to have a good time and enjoy ourselves. The Resort was able to accommodate our request for an early check-in so that we could play at the water park only to find out it closed at 4pm. We ordered food and drinks at the pool bar. The bartender was helpful and courteous - the ‘server’ of our food, not so much. He walked up to our table, didn’t say a word or smile and put the tray of food down and walked away. We left the water park and headed to the ‘Adult Only’ pool. Well, it wasn’t an ‘Adult Only’ pool! There was signage of it being adult only yet families with children were allowed to use the pool as long as the children were not screaming or splashing. What’s the purpose of an adult only pool when there were other family pools? We proceeded to indulge in adult beverages at the adult only pool only to have them taste as though there was no alcohol in them. We called the restaurant back and they assured us there was alcohol in the drinks and that next time we should order doubles. 
We thought it would be fun to play at the water park only to be disappointed by the hours and service we received. We have stayed at other resorts here in the valley and received more bang for our buck. It’s too bad, this is a nice hotel but we won’t be coming back.

title: “Great Place, Spacious Rooms and Great Breakfast - will be back!”
text:
Great hotel! The room rate was not ovelry expensive for Midtown Manhattan and located the perfect distance from Penn Station and all the Midtown stores and restaurants. had the free breakfast in the morning and was very happy with the food - especially for free!
The room was very spacious for NYC and had a mini fridge and microwave which worked out great for a late night snack. There are only 6 rooms on each floor so you are always close to an elevator/stairway. The bathrooms were very clean and the bedding was extremely comfortable. Our room was facing the courtyard/breakfast area (not the street) so it was very quiet and we slept well. I would definitely reccommend and return again!

title: “A Loyal Hyatt Client says stay away”
text:
I stay at Hyatts at least 10x a year I will find somewhere else to stay when in Indianapolis The Hyatt Regency Indianapolis was terrible.
Staff was rude The toliet was soiled with feces. They charge you $5.00
a package for anything sent to hotel. The alarm went off and i walked down stairs and front desk didnt even know alarm was going off

title: “Great hotel in good location”
text:
We thoroughly enjoyed our 4 night stay at the Donatello hotel.
We had read the reviews and were hopeful that it would be good but it exceeded our expectations.
It is in Post Street very close to Union Square which makes everything very accessible.
We were on the 14th floor in a nice modern room.
There is quality nightly entertainment in the bar/casual dining area.
The staff were all very good and attentive
Yes,it would be nice to have a breakfast facility but given the location yiou are spoilt for options elsewhere.
We would deffinately stay here again if we are lucky enough to return to SF

title: “Very nice but not inexpensive”
text:
Everything was very pricey $60 per night for parking. $40 for three drinks in the rooftop lounge, and $24 for the buffet breakfast. Go to Mel's Diner half a block away.
The staff is very helpful from the minute you check in. The bellmen briefed us about everything all the way to our room. (great information) We asked for a room in the back of the hotel away from the main street and all the noise. The bed was wonderful and came with four different types of pillows. The shower was the best hotel shower I've had in the US.

title: “A winter weekend in Beantown”
text: From the moment you arrive at Battery Wharf, you will be amazed at the level of service offered to you. The staff ANTICIPATES most every need and responds in kind. You won't be disappointed

title: “Not quite up to par for an InterContinental”
text:
Having stayed at many InterContinental hotels, I've developed certain expectations. This Boston property fell a bit short in many respects. Let me start with the positive before touching on the shortfalls:
1) The hotel is conveniently located--less than a 15-minute cab ride from Logan Int'l and less than a 10-minute walk from Faneuil Hall and the Quincy Markets. 
2) The hotel has great meeting space.
Now for the shortfalls:
1) Room service--don't both. Both times I ordered it, my food arrived cold. For $50, I would expect at least a 'warm' waffle and 'warm' breakfast potatoes. Oh no, they were stone cold.
2) The furnishings are showing significant wear and tear. 
3) The property seems to cater to Chinese clientele, which means the beds are rock hard. 
4) The hotel's cleanliness is lacking. The lamps and tabletops in my room hadn't been dusted in ages, and the bathroom floor of my first room (I asked to be switched) hadn't been mopped. The toilet was also running incessantly. 
5) Not the best value in town. I was able to secure a reduced rate of $199/night (down from $299) but this hardly seems a bargain. 
Would I stay there again? If I had to, but I'd look around for another place first.

title: “Lovely hotel, great service, good location,”
text:
We stayed at The Lexington in NYC from the 14th November for 5 days and had an absolutely amazing time. The hotel exceeded our expectations from the moment we walked in to the lobby. The service was really impressive, especially the concierge desk who couldnt do enough to offer us any help we needed. 
As a group of 3 adults sharing a room, we were very surprised and pleased to be given quite a large room with two seperate bathrooms. This made things much easier when we were getting ready to go out. There was a full length mirror, a flat screen tv with lots of free channels including ESPN so I was able to watch a live premier league football game in bed one morning.
The rooms were clean, and towels changed daily, however all three of us ended up with really itchy skin and rashes so can only presume this was due to the washing powder used. Really hope it wasn't anything nasty living in the linen!
We didn't visit the main restaurant as the prices looked a bit too expensive, however we did go there for a few drinks one night, and it was pleasant. For breakfast we visited 'Raffles', connected to the hotel, and although good food and service, we found this very pricey, paying around $30 per day for a pretty basic breakfast. You can get much cheaper breakfasts out and about, but Raffles was convenient. There is also a Starbucks connected to the hotel. 
We were supplied with one hours free internet usage in the business centre even though we were staying as leisure, which came in handy as we had to print an email for a return transfer to the airport. 
It takes about 20 minutes to walk to Times Square, 5 minutes to Grand Central Terminal and 10 minutes to the Chrysler Building. There is a hop on/hop off bus stop just outside, across the street.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone planning a break in New York, we were pleased with everything it had to offer. The one downside was the rashes and itchy skin that we can only presume was caught from the linen and towels.

title: “All factors considered, not bad”
text:
The Harrington is steps away from everything worth seeing, this is the most important part (for my husband and I, anyway). If you are looking for a spa-like retreat, this hotel is not for you. 
The hotel is old and run-down (some might find this charming?), but the staff is cheerful and helpful. Because of its central location, book early - we stayed there at the end of May 2011 and there were at least 2 large groups of teenagers staying there (we're talking 60-75 people per group) and the hotel was booked solid.
Our small queen room faced a brick wall (it was on the inside of the building, on the 9th floor) but we did not hear a sound from the busy streets below (this was a common complaint we overheard from other guests - the hotel is at a very busy intersection in Washington DC's business district)
There is no parking on the premises, their parking garage is about two blocks away, a brisk 5 minute walk from the hotel; they charge $15 per day. It is best to park the car and walk, as almost everything you want is very close by, including shopping, restaurants, coffee shops and monuments.
There are two restaurants downstairs, one a breakfast place (which we did not visit) and sports bars with mediocre food, tired wait staff and $12 pitchers of beer.
We would definitely stay here again, you can't beat that location!

title: “Great Location, But ...”
text: The location is great, but after that, it's all downhill. It's an old, tired hotel with a loud window A/C unit, a heater that can't be turned off, old TV with a remote that didn't work, no hair dryer, and old furniture. The bathroom had been renovated so it was fine. There is a computer in the lobby, but you have to pay to use it. The staff are very friendly and helpful. I'm sure that they are used to hearing the same complaints. If you are looking for a CHEAP hotel with a GREAT LOCATION in CHICAGO - this is the place!

title: “Nice place, though service can be lacking...”
text:
My family stayed at the Arizona Grand for four days in March 2009. Though the hotel and water park are enjoyable, the service seems to be lacking in a couple of aspects.
Foremost, waiter service at the water park was poor if available at all. Even when I went to the service window my one item order took over 20 minutes. It seemed due more to short staffing than effort on the part of the wait staff.
In our hotel room, though the room was cleaned satisfactorily, it always appeared that any room service dishes left outside the door were not picked up for almost a day. 
Great place for the kids and always a relaxing time.

title: “Amazing service”
text: I've never had a bad experience at any Kimpton hotel, and this experience continued that trend. Upon arrival the staff is so friendly and accommodating and the rooms are so trendy and comfortable! We loved the happy hour (everyday!) at the 5th Floor restaurant and had a great time exploring the city from the convenient location. Definitely plan on returning again soon.

title: “Very pleasant Hotel in a great location”
text: A stay was very enjoyable, loved their homemade Roast Beef hash for breakfast and pigged out on the potato chips they make in the bar. Room was spacious and well appointed. An easy walk to Union Square and many of the popular spots.

title: “Excellent Location !!!”
text: Before i went on my trip to New York i searched and searched websites of Hotels and in the end i gave in and booked this hotel. Many people told us we were mad to go there but 1 of my friends said she stayed there and it was basic but great location and she was correct. The only thing that i could complain about was the hour and a half we had to wait for check-in soooooo slow but very nice when we eventually got to the desk........ The rooms are basic but thats New York for you and what we paid. If its shoppin you are goin for it is the idea spot to be all you do is sleep and shower in the rooms. The bathrooms and rooms were cleaned everyday and towels changed everyday without having to be ask...... The staff in the information desk in the hotel are very very rude so have your research done before you go and just get a map and off you go !!!!!

title: “Cute hotel in a great downtown location”
text: Very welcoming hotel in downtown Denver. Close to walk everywhere (was there for business and took a taxi to/from the airport.) Great service from the staff. Room service was fast and good (and loved the healthy menu options as well.) Fun eclectic decor. Pet friendly. Would definitely stay here again next time I am in Denver.

title: “Great Location and Good Hotel.”
text:
Check in process was smooth and the front desk worker was very friendly. They also have kiosk where you can check in and out with your Credit Card. Lobby is nice setting. Some rooms have nice view of riverwalk. The room was spacious. The bed was very comfortable. 
Only con: Rooms by elevator sound like a roller coaster is coming at you at times.

title: “Four Points DC was nice stay”
text:
The Four Points Sheraton in DC was very nice. The staff was very friendly. We ate in the restaurant for dinner and breakfast. Dinner was delicious. Fernando was very attentive. Wine selection nice.
Pool on the rooftop wasn't so appealing. It was very small and crowded. Probably really nice for kids. The outdoor patio was nice, but it was such a hot, humid day that we just took a quick look.
Valet parking is VERY expensive at $44 per day. 
We would stay again since the White House is right down th street.

title: “Another wonderful stay”
text:
This is a great hotel. Very modern and chic. Service was excellent, someone always ready to check you in or out, offer you coffee, help with directions, etc. The rooms are quite big, enough room for table, chairs, king bed etc. Nice size shower and bathroom as well. Really like the modern decor. The complimentary wine hour is the best, the wines they server are phenomenal and it's so cozy to sit in the lounge, listen to music and sip wine. 
Complimentary breakfast is very small, but enough to tide you over fo a little. Small muffins, cookies and some candied walnuts. Also coffee or espresso which is all we needed.
Location is good for all the downtown sites. You can easily walk to WTC-911 memorial, south street seaport, shopping at Century 21, World Financial Center, Statue of Liberty etc. You can take a subway to Soho, Village, Union Square, little Italy, Chinatown, etc just about anywhere. I really like the downtown location versus Times Square area, to many lights and tourists everywhere. But from this location you can really enjoy downtown and if you really wanted to, you can easily take the subway uptown.
They have a nice and clean gym, used it a few times. Free weights and weight machines, treadmills and ellipticals.

title: “Great Location!!”
text:
My daughter and I stayed here for four nights and found it to be a very clean and well kept hotel, they are doing some renovations now which should give it a nicer look.
We had room 204 with a private bath which we would recommend, it was on the second floor and was very clean.
It was a great location and was just five minutes from the subway.
Our only drawback was the steep stairs as you enter the building which make getting large suitcases up a challenge, so try and get the first floor or second.

title: “Great deal”
text:
This is a great hotel for someone who isn't going to spend a lot of time there...i.e. there is no pool/spa/gym. However our room and bathroom were very clean. The staff were very nice and helpful. It was so close to Union Square (about 4 short blocks) and the start of the Cable Cars (a few streets down). My friend and I were even able to walk to Chinatown in 20 minutes but public transportation is right outside the door if you are not up for walking. There is a daily continental breakfast included in your stay and if you want something more there is a really cute cafe attached to the lobby. My friend and I took the airport shuttle from the hotel for $14 or you can catch the BART which is a few blocks away.
All in all I thought this hotel was excellent for the $85/nt price tag right in the middle of the more expensive hotels. I am going to suggest it to everyone I know planning on visiting San Francisco.

title: “Great hotel, popular with the young party crowd”
text:
Lobby area is small and often crowded and loud. Actually upon checking in I was having 2nd thoughts about this hotel; was it too busy, loud, young, etc...
Staff was friendly, but always appeared busy with 3 guests in line, 2 phones ringing etc...
I wouldn't stay here if you wanted or expected lots of personal attention.
Once we got into the room, it was excellent. Make sure to reserve a corner-king if you want those awesome views with floor-celing windows on 2 sides of the room.
Shower and bathroom were very nice; yes, there is a clear window in the shower(with a curtin), and the bathroom door slides shut without a lock - so not a ton of privacy.
Again, the hotel is extremely popular with the 25-35 crowd, if you are bit older/quieter, you might be put off. With the crowd, the hotel guests like to party. I could hear people above us and in the halls around 2am - but it wasn't horribly loud.
But I found the room excellent, very comfortable and stylish without being overly modern.
I highly recommend it for that $150-250 price-point room, for the same money I would never stay at a {Hyatt etc...} if i could stay here..but if you want that luxury/special feeling and you can afford $100-200 more a night, you'd probably like the Peninusla, Trump or Elysian more.

title: “Great Location for site seeing”
text: This was a great hotel. The location made it really easy to get around the city. The building and the lobby areas were beautiful and historic. The rooms/halls/etc were typical Courtyard. Huge TV, nice area for Starbucks, bar and breakfast buffet. My only criticism was that the staff just wasn't all that friendly. The fitness center was top-notch if that is important to you. Reading terminal is just a block or so away and is a great place to go to get lunch -- especially if you're traveling with teens. It's like a giant food court but with much better food. My only complaint is that the staff just wasn't all that friendly. They were cordial but with the exception of one of the front desk staff (wish I could remember his name) most just weren't all that cheerful. Seems like an odd statement but we stay at a lot of Marriotts and most of the time you feel like they are incredibly happy to see you. This one not so much...

title: “Fantastic Location & Good Value”
text: Inn staff absolutely wonderful, helpful, knowledgable and friendly. Hotel fantastic location, easy to access as subway just 1 block up. Rooms cleaned every day, bathrooms clean (shower curtains could do with changing). Welcome pack of slippers and shampoo/conditioner/soap on arrival. No lifts but building only 5 storeys so not a problem, staff offer to assist with baggage. Desk manned 24hours nothing too much trouble. Will hold bags for 5 dollars each and organise shuttle back to airport if required. Did not find the hotel particularly noisy only normal noise of other patrons when they returned to their rooms. Rooms could get a bit stuffy but room had ceiling fan and air conditioning unit. No sink in basic private room but plenty of bathrooms on each floor.

title: “Close but not quite”
text: Staff service excellent - at the level I expect for this type of hotel. Room nice, good size. Love the beds. Not sure why they chose for such a large soaking tub and smallish shower in the bathroom, but rain shower a nice touch. However, there were several small details that missed the mark - damaged light switch, toilet paper roll holder loose, and (strangely) two of the wall outlets and the temp control unit were all mounted at an angle - perhaps the electrician was having an off-kilter day. Nothing that affected the comfort of the room, but details that I don't expect to be missed at a westin. Lastly, and most annoyingly, they had installed the pressure-sensor mini bar (both the fridge and non-fridge items). These bother me as I feel they imply that the hotel can't trust me to not steal those precious $10 mini bottles of booze.

title: “Will stay here every time”
text: Our daughter gets medical treatments at St. Joseph's hospital near the hotel. We stay here every time--not only for its convenient downtown location but because cleanliness is so important to our daughter's health. This is absolutely a clean, nice and comfortable place. And I'm pretty picky! It seems new and smells good. The staff are helpful and got us through one time when we locked our keys in our rental car. The free breakfast is bigger than the usual continental breakfast and helps keep expenses down. We will stay here every single time.

title: “This is the definition of a 5* hotel.”
text: People who love their jobs, appreciate their customers and look you in the eye, smile and speak to you. Our stay could not have been more pleasant. The concierge was fabulous and the location perfect. Lunch with a view was a really nice touch! This is our new Boston home away from home. Loved everything about it!

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE-bed bugs”
text: I was a guest of the capital hilton about a week ago. While I love DC, I will NEVER stay at this hotel again after what happend. I recieved bed bug bites the weekend I was staying there from my room. The bites became so severe and swollen that I had to go to the ER when I returend home. The bites were definately from my room. I called the hotel to speak to manager to inform them of what happend. I called THREE times and no one returned my calls. It's bad enough to have bed bugs in your facility but to not acknowledge it is even worse. I would NEVER stay there again and am informing the DC Board of Health.

title: “Historic gem--nice updates--great lobby”
text:
The Algonquin is an OLD hotel which has recently undergone major renovations. As others have noted, rooms are small, even for NY standards but this hotel was built long ago when folks had different priorities. The room in which I stayed was quite comfortable and the bathroom compact but modern. The TV, which is hundred in a frame like a picture was a bit fuzzy but not worth dealing with for my short stay. The room had a rather spacious (relatively speaking) walk in closet. But what I'd like to comment on is the beautiful old fashioned but redecorated lobby. 
After a night at the theater I just wanted a drink in a comfortable place. I want up to the Blue Bar so I sat in a comfortable over stuffed chair in the lobby which is arranged so that many solos, couples, groups could sit together with a sense of privacy and comfort. The service was excellent, and while the drink was typical NY pricey, it wa a generous pour. It was a delightful way to end an enjoyable evening.

title: “Excellent hotel in the perfect spot!”
text: This hotel is great! Cheerful, helpful staff, clean, well appointed, and in the absolute perfect spot. It is within walking distance to everything in downtown San Diego. It is right next door to PetCo park. As a Marriott Platnium member, I can say this is a great hotel and highly recommend it, just make sure to leave me a room!

title: “Great location, pricey parking, nice staff.”
text:
I stayed here during a conference. The hotel location is terrific, and easy to access. My only two complaints from start to finish are the reservation systems and the parking. It would have also been nice to have free internet, especially as a SPG.
I initially had my reservation Monday through Friday, and called the hotel the week prior to the stay in order to modify the reservation to depart on Thursday. I had reserved two rooms under my name, and I also added my SPG number to the reservation.
When we got to the hotel, they only showed ONE room under my reservation. Unfortunately I had not brought my confirmation email to show the information indicating there were two rooms reserved. The reservation also showed that I was staying through Friday. I informed them that I had contacted the reservation number the week prior in order to change the departure date. All in all, it was not a big issue, as the manager made the appropriate changes, and added the second room. I did call downstairs once I was in the room, in order to request being moved farther from the elevator. They informed me that since I had requested double beds, they were not able to move me. I had not, in fact, requested double beds, but they apparently had a note in the system that someone had talked to me and noted a request for double beds. I informed them that they had not talked with me about the double beds, and I was told that the note must have been put on the wrong reservation. I ended up staying in the initial room for the duration of my stay.
The hotel room was very nice, clean and spacious. I had a very nice view of the harbor and the city. The housekeeping was fantastic during my entire stay. Any questions we had were quickly and nice answered by the staff throughout the hotel. The gaslamp district and plenty of restaurants were within walking distance.
Parking was steep at $32 per day. It's amazing to me how so many of the hotels charge such high fees for parking your vehicle. There was a parking lot up the street, where parking was $15 for 24 hours with in and out privileges. 
When we were ready to check out, the front desk informed us that they had us staying through until Friday. I informed them that that had been changed already.....twice. Westin SERIOUSLY needs to re-examne its reservation system! It was ridiculously frustrating.
Overall, I would consider staying here again, and park up the street. Next time I stay, I will also bring my email confirmation.

title: “Gone Downhill in the past few months”
text: I almost lived in the property for about 18 months on 2010 and 2011 right when it opened as my company has office in the NY Times building at the end of the street.. Stayed here for a few nights last week and it has gone downhill. Here are the issues; carpet in room is nasty dirty and stained. GROSS.. Shower barely drained. Mold in bathroom. AC did not get cold enough. Free Breakfast not as good as before. Price has gone up considerably. Internet is super slow. Could barely even check my mail let alone work in the evenings. This place was awesome last year but now it's below average and the rates have gone up. No way would I spend the money for this now as for these prices there are better options in the area.

title: “Not going back.”
text: First of all the $47 charge for one night's parking was ridiculous, as was the long wait for the car to be returned in the morning. Old, but not sufficiently restored. Carpets were ugly and stained, and the elevator was not reliable. Room was small, but it was fairly quiet at night.

title: “Look no further! Whether you're a couple...”
text: Look no further! Whether you're a couple or a young family looking to stay in New York this hotel is excellent. Just off Times Square and flanked by two excellent restaurants this hotel has exceptional service. Although rooms are smaller than usual they're fairly standard for NY and ours was quiet despite being 10 yds from the busiest place ever. Breakfast is excellent and the complimentary cheese and wine sets you up nicely before catching a show. Book it now!

title: “great location in east village”
text:
i came here with a friend using a snique away deal for two nights- a good value, around 240 a night with taxes.
the location in east village was great- just a couple blocks south of st. marks place in cooper square, right by the subway, and easy walk to shopping in soho. 
the hotel room was small, as can be expected in ny, with a huge, comfortable bed. the bathroom was surprisingly large (and nice) for the city. 
overall, very clean, and no complaints. 
the lobby area and sitting areas with a fireplace and library were cozy, modern, and stylish. 
had breakfast there once, and was underwhelmed by the spinach and goat cheese omelette.

title: “Great location for price”
text: I was pleased with this hotel. Location and cleanliness were very important to me and the Phoenix Park met my expectations. From reading previous reviews, I had some concerns regarding noise from the restaurant/bar and ensuring double beds in our room. I contacted the hotel prior to my visit and had no problem with getting double beds. When checking in, I reiterated my request for a quite room away from the bar and was accomodated with no problem. The only downside to this hotel is the size of the rooms...they are very small.

title: “No Room for us”
text: This is the worst hotel I have ever had the displeasure of dealing with!!!!! Six weeks before our Washington DC vacation I made a reservation for this hotel. We show up at noon to check in and are told that our room is not ready yet and to go site seeing. We come back at 6:30 pm and are told that we have no room!!! 1000+ miles from home in DC and we do not have a room!! The hotel was overbooked!! And why is it my room that was overbooked! The people at the desk were unconcerned. One lady pretended to get me a room at another hotel, but when we got to the Marriott they told us noone had called them to get us a room. Thankfully the lady at the Marriott was extra helpful and we had a nicer place to stay. Do not use the Embassy Suites in Chevy Chase. The whole atmosphere was not icky. The parking garage was poorly lit and very dusty. My car was filthy just being in there the few hours while they were supposed to be readying our room. And the best thing when I called corporate office, I was offered a certificated for a free night, like I want to try again at a Hilton property. DISGUSTED with Hilton!

title: “Convenient but...”
text: Convenient hotel to Smithsonian and Mall. Walking distance to metro. Staff was helpful. But the room we stayed in was mediocre. For almost $200/night, the tv did not work, I had to call twice to get a crib, the furniture was not in good condition and rooms were barely clean. Located next to a CVS and Mcdonald's too.

title: “The staff at Stay were awesome!”
text: We had a pleasant stay at Stay. Before we arrived, I took the advice of other travelers and requested a corner room. Angie arranged this and kept her word. She was so very pleasant. Sammy, helped us when checking out, by storing our luggage for us and helping us get it into the car. He was so gracious for the tip that we gave him. The chocolates given to us on our second night were great. The room was VERY small, as was the elevator, however, we didn't have to wait long. Again, the staff was unbelievable. We also requested extra towels and they were delivered promptly and we even received a follow-up call. Again, we had a great stay at Stay!

title: “Good location, ideal for quiet types”
text:
This is a little gem in Boston. It requires no keys, they send you access codes through email, and you never have to fumble around for keys to get into the hotel or your room. The room itself is lovely, with a little kitchenette, good percolator for morning coffee and the fridge for milk and extras. 
There were a couple of annoyances, which when added up are really not that important to spoil from the general well being that the hotel offers:
1. The smell in the hallways was peculiar, perhaps another air-freshener would be better?
2. Little bottles of shampoo and conditioner were great, but a bottle of shower gel would have been wonderful.
3. I never knew the hotel offers a clean up service only on request. I came in the second day of my stay to find my bed exactly the way I left it. Either there ought to have been clearer instructions on ordering a cleanup, or then it ought to be offered as standard for a luxury little hotel like this.
4. Beware the fancy lamps in the room, many of them are with blown up bulbs and don't work.
This said, the staff was friendly and helpful and replaced the bulbs immediately, sent some staff in to clean up, connected me to the room's TV easily (a bit complicated, but instructions are all there). The TV was great fun since its size calls for some great viewing from the bed.
This hotel is really very lovely and makes a trip to Boston that much more cozy with a sense of being somewhere you already have been to...

title: “Worst Customer Service”
text: i just stayed here 4 nights. The front office staff including the manager Paresh Patel were rude and uncaring, the opposite of customer service in fact. When I asked why the complimentary breakfast was late (it was 7:20AM and it was supposed to be out at 7AM) the Genl Manager was rude and didn't give a crap, telling me "it's complimentary" when I told him it was not OK for the breakfast to be late like it was so nice of him to do that, I shouldn't complain when it's late?? He apologized in a tone of antagonism and when I told him I didn't believe his apology he said "I take it back then". This is the general manager! The check in guy was rude as well, just not friendly. The rooms are larger than normal, but there's no utensils or cups or anything at all in the kitchen. The place needs work, easy enough things to fix, just looks run down, and a bit shabby. I won't stay there again, mostly because of the attitude of the staff there, as the other things could have been overlooked if the staff were friendly and the manager was truly apologetic about the breakfast being late.

title: “A nightmare to deal with. Overbilled for several extra nights. Had to chargeback.”
text:
If you or family are receiving treatment at one of the area hospitals, the location can not beat.
However, the hotel was a nightmare to deal with. Booked a stay of over a week while a family member was having surgery at Children's. We were advised to book based on our longest projection and that we could check out early if there was an early discharge. This was confirmed verbally when the reservation was made, at check-in, and at check-out, as well as in writing.
The hotel ended up booking us for nearly an extra week, despite advising the hotel 3 times that we were checking out both via phone and the front desk. They repeatedly refused to correct the problem and forced us to chargeback the additional nights.
Other thoughts...
Pros
* Room was fairly large
* Location can't be beat for visiting the area hospitals
Cons
* Hotel Hallways are kept very dark
* Non-Smoking floor constantly reeked of smoke
* Water pressure in the shower was extremely week
* Attached restaurant was poor

title: “Very Nice”
text: Stayed one night this past weekend while moving our son into his apartment. Used valet parking which went quickly as did check in. Front desk was polite and accomodating - we were assigned the room type we requested (room 3010 on the 30th floor). The view of the Hudson River was spectacular. We couldn't see the Statue of Liberty as another building blocked it, but didn't mind at all. The room is traditional furniture & offered a very comfy bed and a chair w/ottoman & lamp for reading. Bathroom was clean and nice. I have already booked this hotel again. We paid $279.00 which included a great breakfast buffet plus $40.00 for parking. Didn't need to move the car until 5pm day of checkout, so we were able to buzz around all day by subway. We liked this hotel very much, but even better was the walk around Battery Park along the water and through gardens. This is across the street and two blocks over. The area is quiet. We used the subways with ease so the location, though away from uptown & theaters, was not a problem.

title: “If we are ever in DC again we'll come back here!”
text: Nothing more to say other than this place was perfect for a family. The added bonus of a kitchenette is just what is needed when you've kids that can't start the day without breakfast! David the general manager and all of the other staff were fantastic. Perfect location, away from the hussle and bustle of DuPont Circle but within a short walking distance of restaurants and the metro. A great stay in a fantastic city.

title: “Lackland Air Force Base Graduation Trip”
text:
My experience to Comfort Suites by the Alamo/Riverwalk was simply amazing. From the beginning to the end non stop great service. 
I wish I could remember everybody's name because they were all wonderful. Megan was so sweet with explaining to me and my family all the beautiful sites to see. Manuel at the front desk was excellent also, he even helped me with my laundry, could you believe that, he was truly awesome. There was a second Manuel who also helped us out by the pool area very pleasant gentleman. Mrs. Georgia Rios another great lady, she worked the kitchen area and she made sure that my daughter, Tiana who has Cebral Palsey had her breakfast and simply made it very easy for me, anything that i needed she provided it to us. The cleaning crew, thank you for keeping my room so clean and tidy.Jessy gave me a beautiful tour of the Riverwalk and the Downtown area. And all the staff, everyone was very professional, courteous , and very kind to me and my family. Thank you all once again.
The famous Riverwalk......WOW.....how beautiful..... I took oh so many lovely pictures of all the Historic Buildings, the Beautiful Restaurants, the enormous Mall, where I went on a shopping spree like always.
I must not forget the miniature golf course, the hot tub, and the great pool in which my mother, my kids and myself enjoyed so much.
Well to sum it up I recommend this hotel to everyone. Come with your significant other or with your family and I guarantee you that you will have an exceptional time.
See you all soon,
Antonia Rosa & Family in room #103. 
From August 29, 2012 thru September 4, 2012.

title: “Great Location!!! I would recommend this hotel to everyone.”
text: The location was great. We were in New York celebrating a friends birthday. A half a block from Times Square and two blocks from 5th Ave. Bubba Gump is my favorite resturant, which is in walking distance from the hotel. There is normally a 20 min wait--but it's worth it (try the hushpuppies). The only thing that I have negative to say about the Muse is: the bed skirt around both beds were filthy and someone's sock was found underneath the bed. It made me second guess how clean the bed was--but everything worked out just fine. The wine hour was also a highlight. I would advise the Muse Hotel to WASH everything, including the bed skirt when it comes to taking care of there customers. I am already making plans to go early next year.

title: “Great value”
text: La Quinta was a pleasant surprise, the exterior doesn't scream out to you but the friendly front desk staff and location more than made up for it. We felt that for the money, we got more than a bargain. The rooms were very clean, beds were very comfortable the building next door was a bit close as far as view but we didn't spend enough time indoors for it to matter. The free breakfast was adequate and everything was a walkable distance.. Space needle, Pike market etc. Just be sure to bring walking shoes. Overall we had a great time.. Don't forget to say hi to Danny Q, front desk extrodinaire !!!!

title: “Not impressed”
text:
I stayed here with an old friend for a girls weekend. I love modern hotels like the Standard, W, etc. but, we got a good deal here and thought the location would be good & willing to try something different. The room was SO hot when we got there & we couldn't figure out how to turn it down. Waited and waited for someone to help but, got impatient and went out to shop & eat. We came back hours later to find all they did to fix it was crack the window open. 
The room was ok size. The bathroom was ok. No hairdryer. We weren't in the room that much anyway. Decor was stuffy & old fashioned but, we expected that. 
Totally unimpressed with the dated lobby. We asked the concierge for lunch suggestions and they sent us to a closed restaurant. The next day we asked for a reasonably priced brunch recommendation. They suggested Oscars (the hotel restaurant). We had the buffet - it was gross. Watery eggs, burnt coffee, a bagel & potatoes - $100 for 2 w/ tip. INSANE!!!!!!!

title: “Perfect UWS hotel”
text: I've repeatedly put my elderly parents up at On the Ave and have always been impressed with the kindness of everyone at the desk as well as the neatness and comfort of the rooms. For out-of-town visitors, I highly recommend this hotel. And for New Yorkers--especially those living on the Upper West Side--looking for a hotel to put up visiting family or friends, I think On the Ave is a great choice.

author.location: New York, New York, United States

title: “GREAT MANAGEMENT AT A WELL RUN HOTEL”
text: This is an excellent hotel, only eight years old and beautifully maintained. Great location near everything with beautiful rooms and comfortable beds and all the tech amenities a business person needs to conduct their work. The highlight of the hotel however is the management at least the manager I spoke with who wanted to insure my stay was going well. His name was Ryan and he was the resident house manager. I have traveled millions of miles my entire career and tend to be loyal to the hotels that are managed well. This hotel is certainly in that category. Their management and staff are excellent, genuinely concerned that your stay is comfortable and that you will be returning. I am not surprised that they rank Number One on Trip Advisor. This hotel is five star, not just because of their nice rooms but you get a sense that they care and for that one can ask no more. Highly recommend this hotel.

title: “A little gem - Whitehall Hotel”
text: Recently, we spent 3 nights at the Whitehall Hotel just to the north of downtown. The lcoation was excellent - 2 blocks from Michigan Ave. & 1 mile to Navy Pier. The hotel staff were very courteous and the room was decorated very nicely with terrycloth robes. We booked a show through the concierge and was offered a town car to take us to the show -- no charge! Although we did not eat at the hotel, there are plenty of restaurants within walking distance. Very nice place to stay and reasonably priced for the downtown area.

title: “Fantastic Hotel - Great location - Service Outstanding”
text: just got back from our 4 night stay at Nine Zero. My husband took me there for my 40th Birthday and we were treated exceptionally well. Champagne and chocolate dipped strawberries on arrival along with a complimentary room upgrade. The staff are are incredibly helpful and friendly. The hosted wine evening is a nice touch and a great way to meet fellow travellers. The location however is what truly makes this hotel. Thank you so much for making our stay special and look forward to coming back in the future.

title: “Hobo in the Palace ....”
text: Nice! What can you say but the service was excellent, everyone was super-friendly, and don't miss the cocktail show from the Rosewood Mansion bar seat. Think clubby decor and heritage drinks from the 1930s and ’40s. Food was a bit steep in price but worth every expensive, precious little bite, especially the mini burgers, smoked short rib tacos, and ceviche. Definitely would return as this felt like 'home' even if we were not as dressed up as our Mansion cohorts. Tip: Go to the Mansion bar at happy hour and have the bartender make you one of his custom liquid specials. Totally worth it.

title: “Just perfect!”
text: We've just come back from a one-week stay in NY with our kids and stayed at this hotel. It was just perfect: the price was very good; the bedroom had two king beds and was on16th floor (no noise); only the bathroom was a little old and the shower tap was not very convenient; but everything was clean; receptionists were very friendly and helped us when necessary; breakfast was exceptional and we could even bring in a pizza one evening and eat it there; also the position is strategic: there were many subway stations nearby so that we could go back to the hotel very quickly to let the kids rest; but it is possible to reach Times Square on foot very easily; one block away there is Eataly that I recommend for a perfect Italian coffee. We'll go there again if we happen to visit NY in the future.

title: “Great location, good service”
text: The location is perfect. You can walk to the Chicago subway station(red line), to Michigan ave, to the bars/restaurants on rush street, to downtown... The service was good and the room was nice and clean so was the bathroom. I called before our arrival to confirm my reservation and asked for a room with a view, since the street is very narrow, there is only one side with a view on delaware street. They did provide us with a room facing the street on the 15th floor.

title: “Excellent”
