text: I love to stay at the holiday inn dfw the staff is amazing the food delicious the rooms are so comfortable i just want to stay there and never go back home it has all the accomadations I really and truly recomend the stay there you will love it!!!!!!!:)

title: “Great stay at Stay!”
text: Stay was an excellent hotel to stay at! We were on the 7th floor in a corner room, which I heard were the most spacious. We had a very comfortable bed which provided much needed sleep each night. The staff was great and even awarded us 2 complimentary drinks and free chocolate covered strawberries due to it being our 2nd anniversary. Thank yous go out to Angie and the other female associate who helped us check in. Unfortunately we ran out of time and were unable to redeem the gifts, but it was a very nice gesture none-the-less. The hotel was only a couple of blocks from the heart of Times Square and very convenient to the subway/restaurants/etc.

title: “I will be back”
text:
Our room was clean and comfortable, the location was very convenient to Seattle Center, there was free on-site parking, and the staff were generally very friendly and helpful. If one likes to walk, there are many restaurants to choose from, but not next door. 
The next time I am in Seattle, this will be my first choice. My only suggestions are that one not rely on the shuttle service. While they do their best to accommodate people, they can't always be available at the time people would like. It might be useful if they set up a reservation system so one would know whether or not the mini bus would be available when needed. Also I did miss the continental breakfast which many other Best Westerns provide, although there was tea and coffee, as well as apples and cookies if you were in the lobby early enough.

title: “Great Hotel, Prime Location”
text: My husband and I spent 3 nights at the Best Western Pioneer Square Hotel and it was great. The hotel is a very old one that has been completely remodeled and is just beautiful. The people who work there were very friendly and extremely helpful. The rooms were nice, large, clean and inviting. Every night the staff came by and offered more towels, turned down your bed and put candy on the pillows. The location, in Pioneer Square, was fantastic. You walk up half a block and catch a free bus to anywhere, walk down a block to the waterfront and catch the ferry to one of the islands. It was so easy to get around that we didn't bother to rent a car. We definitely enjoyed our stay and would stay there again and would recommend it to anyone.

title: “Very Nice and Peaceful”
text: I stayed at the Town and Country last year and am back again now. It has large rooms and is very clean. I love the firm mattress and the warm pool. It is nice to have a few options to eat at on the hotel grounds and that it is so close to the mall.

title: “Gracious Hospitality”
text: Okay, first off, I'm not someone used to paying in Euros, nor am I someone who takes a vacation to "party" in the hotel. I laugh when I read reviews regarding "no 24 hour room service". You're in freakin' NYC...live a little...get out of the hotel!!! Or how about: "There was no jacuzzi or sauna". Here's a tip: stay HOME! Invest the money in a health club membership! I am not a novice to travel or to NYC. I've stayed at 2-star hotels (The Pennsylvania House) and 5-star hotels (The Waldorf). So, what do I think of the Hilton? First off, if your idea of fun is being in the thick of Times Square, close to subway transportation and smack-dab in the heart of all the tourist-y things to do (and that is my idea of fun)...you're there. Secondly, the rooms are an impressive size for NYC (I will agree that the electrical outlets are a little limited), they are clean and well maintained, mattress and pillows are comfy and bathroom was clean (wah-wah, no toothbrush---bring your own!). Here is the reason I would go back: from the moment we set foot in the door, every employee we came in contact with gave the impression that our choosing the Hilton for our stay was appreciated. "Will you be needing help with your luggage?" "Thank you for choosing the Hilton. Enjoy your stay." Not only were they gracious to us, but they extended courtesy to one another. Can't say that for the manager at Au Bon Pain in Battery Park who was screaming at a cashier or the flight attendant on Continental who was serving beverages and barked at a younger flight attendant "This would go a lot faster if you'd stop talking" (the flight had been delayed an hour; the younger FA was trying to be pleasant...and, no, she wasn't talking to me!). Whether Hilton drills that attitude in to their employees, or it comes from within, everyone I came in contact with (door man, maid, maintenance, front desk, concierge, mail room) made me feel that I was appreciated, a "guest", as opposed to just another inconvenience until it was time to clock out. My suggestion: shop for a bargain (they're out there), stay in a safe, comfortable and clean room at the Hilton and, for goodness sake, GET OUT AND SEE THE CITY!!!

title: “Lovely place- be it a long or a short stay!!!”
text: This was the second time we have stayed at the Hotel Andra.. and we just really love it! Close to the shopping areas, several great restaurants, Pike Place Market, Paramount and Moore Theaters, the monorail to Seattle Center-- basically all of the areas that travelers would want to see on a trip to Seattle. The staff is courteous, the rooms well appointed = the bed was SOOOO comfortable... definitely would recommend!!!

title: “Great Getaway”
text:
I stayed here with my husband and two kids for 3 nights. We went to Indy to visit the zoo and children's museum. 
The Hilton is next to the state capital and monument circle at the intersection of Market and Illinois. Great location close to lots of restaurants and the Circle Centre shopping mall. We parked in the onsite garage which was $19.00 per day. The lot directly across the street on Illinois was only $12.00, but Hilton assured us they monitor their parking ramp.
The hotel's bar/restaurant features $1.95 meal specials from 4-6 each evening. However, the specials are only available in the bar and no one under 21 is allowed in the bar. We were somewhat dismayed by that. Coming from the beer state, no one is turned away at a bar!
We had a queen suite which was probably the largest hotel room I have ever stayed in. There were two sinks, (1 in and 1 out of bathroom) two TVs, two queen beds and a pull out sofa. There was also a nice desk/computer area for business travelers. The queen beds were separated from the sofa sleeper/desk area by french doors. The bathroom was very large. The queen beds each had 4 pillows. The weird thing was there was only 1 waste basket in the whole room. I would of expected at least 3.
The kids liked the pool & hot tub. It is located on the top (19th floor). There is also a nice work out room on the 18th floor.
We walked every night to Monument Circle and got ice cream at the Chocolate Cafe/South Bend Chocolate store. The steps of the monument are a great place to rest and people watch. Over the weekend it was packed. There is also an interesting FREE Civil War museum but it is closed on Mon and Tues. 
We ate breakfast every morning at Le Peeps, an Indy landmark. There are several locations throughout the City. The restaurant is just north of the Hilton on Illinois. 
Our best dinner was at Buca di Beppo almost directly across the street from Hilton on Illinois. It is a fun restaurant that is very family friendly. Their meals are served family style. I would not hesitate to go back again.
The Children's museum is fantastic, well worth the trip. The zoo was also fun and has a dolphin show. The canal is a fun place to people watch as well. There are several places of interest at the White River State Park. It is where the zoo is located.

title: “Basic”
text: Stay at this hotel only to save money. The room was clean enough, but the bed was rock hard and you're sandwiched between hiways. Bring earplugs. The highlight of the Comfort Inn is its shuttle service. The driver to us straight to our destination & would pick us up. When in Philly, you really want to be leave your car parked for the duration of the visit. The hotel is in safe enough area to feel that your car is secured and that you can walk from there, but be aware that you're going to be a bit of a distance from food. Comfort Inn doesn't have a restaurant and the vending machine selection was weak. Not many restaurants seemed to deliver there either, so plan your meal strategy in advance. The shower faucet dripped the entire time and the TV remote didn't work. THis is a great place to leave your belongings then trek around the city and return to your room exhausted enough for a deep sleep. Another plus of the Inn is its proximity to all of the historical attractions. But if you want comfort, amenities, and style, don't stay here!

title: “Good choice for extended stay”
text:
I was looking to get as close as possible to the Denver Airport because of a very early AM flight. Was told that the shuttle runs continuously, but for very early in the morning, I had only the choice of a 4 AM shuttle, which would have put me at the airport too early, and a 4:45 AM shuttle, which was cutting it too close. 
Rooms are quite pleasant for an extended stay with cooking utensils, full refrigerator, microwave, etc. They've tried to create a separate living room/bedroom area with a TV that swivels in each direction on a divider wall, but the end result is that each side feels a little cramped, and, again a space saving measure I assume, the bathroom door swings apart at the middle a little like a saloon door....and there's a fairly large gap so it doesn't fasten snugly. The bedroom area has nice room darkening shades, but there is a smaller window in the LR area that has blinds on it that allow for quite a bit of light leakage. 
I love the walk-in shower, but in this case it means no tub. Closet for hanging clothes is INSIDE the bathroom, so a little inconvenient for two people sharing room. The remote system did not work on our TV, so front desk came up quickly to try and resolve. End result was that we could use the remote, but there was no volume control capability on the television. All in all, I liked the look of the place, and appreciate the design, I liked the location, but the functionality did leave something to be desired.

title: “Putting on the Ritz @ LA Live”
text:
We have been very psyched about staying at the Ritz Carlton in Los Angeles at LA Live because of all the hype surrounding the area. The building is a very fascinating new addition to the Downtown LA skyline. Overall, we were not disappointed. The Ritz is chic and substantial. It made for a memorable stay and a welcome break. The views are awesome. Location is an urban oasis (albeit almost too new and sterile), very unique for Los Angeles. The pool area is delightful. Definitely a great choice to celebrate a special occasion (in our case, it's our wedding anniversary).
Now to the quirks/observations. 
We realize after we checked-in that the place is still under "soft" opening. The real opening is May 17, 2010. Didn't make much difference to us, since we get all the great services & amenities with very few others around. 
The valet parking fee at the Ritz with in/out privileges is $50 per day. Yikes. It is posted on a sign at the entry and I saw groups of people reading the sign and gawking. Every time we came back the valet will greet us by name as they open the car door.
We were persuaded to upgrade to "Club Lounge" privileges for $70 per day. It turned out to be the best decision of our stay as the Lounge is not crowded, and had non-stop delicious snacks (rotating daily between morning breakfast, noon light lunch, afternoon hors d'oeuvres, and evening desserts with all the drinks, cheeses, candies, etc. you can eat/drink). The ambience is very relaxed and casual. The staff are attentive and professional. They couldn't wait to customize drinks for us (I loved my decaf soy capuccino... never had it before!). The lox during breakfast is very good quality. Being locals, we were not eager to leave the hotel to see any sights, and between our room, the Lounge, and the pool/fitness center, we were well entertained and nourished. The fitness center is not extremely large, but is nicely equipped and clean.
The lobby seems about 1/100 the size of the adjacent JW Marriott lobby (I guess the PC way to call it is "intimate"). 
The room is tastefully chic, as urban "loft" hotels should be. Lots of carefully placed items designed to delight the senses. Colors and materials are pleasing. Our room is spaciously laid out at 450 sq ft. Since the room is thermally sealed (obviously the windows are not operable), even with the thermostat set at 70 degrees F, we ended up slow-roasting under the fancy comforter at night. During the semi-consciousness of sleep, we didn't think to look into the closet and bring out the THIN blanket until after 6 am. I think the mattress was a bit flat (not flexible), but the husband didn't seem to mind.
The Ritz Carlton hotel is on the 22nd floor to the 26th. Meaning if you look at the building from the outside, the hotel is still part of the "shorter section". The floor plan of the entire hotel is a "T", same as the JW Marriott below. The north/south tall part of the building that sticks out into the sky is NOT the Ritz hotel, it is all part of the Ritz Carlton Residences/condos. 
In case you didn't know the Ritz is owned by the Marriott chain. Meaning the Book of Mormons is laying side by side with the Holy Bible in the night stand drawer, and that there is absolutely no adult programming available in the entertainment system. I find that rather quaint and charming. Gives the place some subtle character.
The shower has low water pressure, but for once it didn't matter because it is a convincing rain shower that can be diverted to a movable shower head. The only thing that I thought could be improved is that the wood sliding door to the bathroom sticks out too much when it is opened. I keep feeling like I will bump into the giant metal door handles, especially since the room is full of mirrors and glass.
All in all the Ritz at LA Live is a welcomed new addition to downtown Los Angeles. I look forward to read everyone's reviews after your stay there.

title: “Great!”
text: Just returned from an overnight getaway with my husband and stayed at this hotel. Great experience. The rooms and bathrooms were immaculate and brand new. The location (close to Penn Station and all the "action") and price were awesome. The only complaint was that the beds were a little hard and uncomfortable, and they did not have a relationship with the local parking garage, so you have to pay full price to park. Those were minor problems, though. We will stay here every time we come to New York!

title: “love this hotel for C2E2!”
text: free parking, walking distance to McCormick place (tho we DID drive and pay the parking since parking is free at the hotel) CLEAN rooms, great food in the restraunt, Cant wait til April!

title: “Worst Nightmare”
text:
Recent stay in Fitzpatrick manhattan Hotel very nice room recently refurbished but had an awful experience as it was infested with cockroaches
Although we were given one night accommodation and a complimentary breakfast this was definately something you would not expect in a 4-5 star rated hotel
We moved into a temporary room at 3am in morning which was freesing cold and we ended up getting very bad colds
Overall this put a damper on our holiday and definately should not happen in a top class hotel
When we got back into our room after it was fumigated a paper with a dead roach on it had been lifted from the bath by housekeeping or the fumigator and left on a shelf in the
bedroom, how insensitive
The roaches could travel so fast from room to room and up walls and curtains everywhere it was really awful and when we opened the room door they were even travelling along on the corridor outside
The night porter was very understanding but reception were not and really did not have 
any idea of what we had been through

title: “Lovely, elegant hotel in great location”
text: We were torn between staying at a larger new hotel or the Talbott. So glad we chose the Talbott! It is a small but very elegant boutique hotel with loads of charm. The service was excellent, the bed was amazingly comfortable with exquisite linens. I also appreciated the hotel's efforts at energy conservation with extremely modern sensor thermostats that lower the temperature when guests are not in the room. The location is excellent, wonderful restaurants everywhere you turn, and don't forget a stop at Sprinkles Cupcakes for dessert!

title: “Not what we expected”
text: We stayed at the Hotel des Arts in San Francisco for the first time in May, 2009. We were excited because my friend and I were really like some of the artists that painted the rooms. However, our excitement quickly turned to disappointment when we discovered how little art was really on the walls in the room we were given. Some of the rooms probably have more art but ours was just one wall. This is one of the nosiest hotels I have ever stayed in. It wasn't even the other guests that were being noisy specifically. Their was a bathroom located right in the hallway by our room. You could hear everything going on in there. The housekeeping in the morning was very noisy and our bath tub was not stable so everytime you stood in it it rocked. I'm sure that it was loud and bothersome for other guests to hear. The employees were friendly enough except for one girl who was there in the evenings who didn't seem to know what was going on and gave us wrong directions at one point. The bed was one of the most uncomfortable beds I have ever slept on. We slept on our friends air mattress one of the nights of our trip and it was more comfortable than the hotel bed. I never felt comfortable in the room. It was really awkward having the sink in the same room as the bed. The location is the only thing going for this hotel. I'm sure that is why the prices are what they are. This hotel is more like a hostel and it is has only a two star rating. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone. You can probably find a better deal in the same area.

title: “Perfect location and well worth the price!”
text: We stayed here for a long weekend to meet up with family for a mini reunion. This could not be a better location. The Inner Harbor is directly across the street and Camden Yards is a short and safe walk. The room was lovely. My nephew loved the flat screen in the bathroom so he could watch tv while taking a bath. The service is excellent. Check in was smooth and the employee behind the front desk must be beating suitors off with a stick with his friendliness, French accent, efficiency and smile/wink. Check in literally took about 3 minutes and we were off to our room. Late one night my husband simply wanted a soda and the security guard noticed us looking around and opened the coffee shop that was closed to get him two bottles of soda. How nice was that? We plan on writing a letter to his boss about how nice that was of him. Every time we entered the hotel, the valet would open the door for us even though there is a revolving door. We asked for additional towels and had them at our door within five minutes. You can valet park or turn right on Lee Street and self park in the Harbor Court garage with an easily accessible secure entrance. Very easy. We parked the car and walked everywhere. The beds were extremely comfortable as well. Again, an impressive hotel due to location, service and beauty. You don't go on vacation to save money, so if safety, location and top notch service are important, it is well worth the price. HIGHLY recommend.

title: “Eastgate came up trumps again!”
text: our last trip was a bit niggly but was promised an upgrade on next stay and the eastgate delivered and we are spoiled! thanks to Deborah. location of hotel is amazing the hotel in need of a bit of a decor update but our suite was spotless and no bedbugs! see you next year! should have free internet access though!

title: “Historic with basic rooms/service”
text: Stayed five nights on a business trip because space was not available at the larger hotels. Historic nature of the hotel gives it a unique flavor. Location next to Alamo is central, though better is possible for Henry B. Gonzalez Convention Center. Room was slightly run down. Shower had great water pressure, but no shower wand. I used room service once and the food was delivered ten minutes later than promised with hot food and cold food both lukewarm. Bed was comfortable with lots of pillows. Air conditioning in room was easily controlled to maintain a comfortable setting (average temps in high 90s during my stay). WiFi in room was mediocre relative to higher end hotels. One afternoon I put a DND sign on the door to catch up on sleep and room service called the room phone to let me know I could ask for towels - while I was trying to sleep with the DND on the door! When I asked to check out the night prior to an early departure, I was told that the new system would not allow it - I might get charged twice - but they could close out the next day and e-mail me the receipt. Not ideal for an early morning departure in a hurry or business traveler who wants to leave with all receipts in hand. Over-all, left me with a disappointed, tepid impression of what I had thought would be a stellar hotel.

title: “Not bad...easy to find...”
text:
This is a typical Fairfiled Inn. Clean, quiet and comfortable. Breakfast was so-so (average) but didn't seem to be quite the variety as I am used to at other locations...but what there was was good. The entrance to the hotel is a bit tricky as my Tom-Tom told me to get onto the I-35 service road and turn right into the parking lot. I did that and found the turn but not an easy thing to do in the dark with traffic all around you! I found that there was a back entrance into the parking lot which I used from that time on. 
Overall...will stay there again!

title: “Thoroughly enjoyed it!”
text: What a beautifully appointed property! The decor was very upscale & contemporary. Very nice & very spacious business center. Was not there long enough to use the hot tub. The entire staff was outstanding from the valet to housekeeping. We enjoyed our stay to the fullest and would definitely stay here again as well as recommend it to others.

title: “Solid stay at Orchard”
text: We booked the Orchard Hotel based on three things; positive Trip Advisor Reviews, price, and location. Overall it was worth it. We were early for checkin by a couple hours and our Deluxe King Room wasn't ready so they upgraded us to a suite, so we were off to a very good start! The suite was superb, very spacious and very nice. Overall we thought the reception service was excellent, doormen were top drawer, location was great, and noise from adjacent rooms and street was nil. We did not eat at their restaurant, but were in the lounge for a few hours one evening with mediocre service. We agree with prior reviews that this hotel is not exactly "boutique", as it is more of a simple and efficient "medium to high end" hotel with a great location just a couple blocks from Union Square and on the Cable Car route. This was our second trip to San Fran and this hotel was much better than the one we stayed at before, in a similar location for about the same price.

title: “Excellent Hotel, Excellent Location”
text: Don't know why this hotel has some bad reviews, its a brilliant Hotel in a superb location, its clean the staff are super and the beds are so comfortable (with sheets changed everyday), its the best sleep ever, will definetly go back for sure ITS FANTASTIC

title: “Great Service, but.... be careful with your credit card!”
text:
This hotel has a great location, all the personnel are very courteous and nice, a few blocks from the station and a nice neighborhood, I had only ONE inconvenience. I decide to pay with my Master Card and not with my American Express, unfortunately both credit cards were charged. If there was a mistake or a confusion couldn't be better just to let me know in the same moment? so I didn't have to be billed double? 
Now I already paid both credit cards and have to go through all papers and calls to the credit cards. What a waste of time! 
Other than that... I would come back, but next time I'd pay CASH

title: “Best Western Shelter Island, San Diego”
text:
We spent 5 nights at this hotel. It is a beautiful setting. Shelter Island just begs to be walked and enjoyed. The staff at the front desk is very helpful and always smiling.
What we had a problem with is the room. It took us complaining 4 days in a row to get the TV fixed. The reception was bad. Twice the repair guy came and looked at it but did not fix it. It took us going to the front desk and taking to a manager to get the darned TV fixed. That should not have been that difficult.
My husband took one of the coffee cups from the room filled with coffee to the dining room one morning. He left it in the dining room after we finished our breakfast. That coffee mug was never replaced in our room. Also, one of the bedside lamps had a burned out bulb which was never replaced.
But with all that, we still had a great time. It is well located and just down the road is Humphrey's which has concerts almost every evening.

title: “Amazing place to be, friendly and helpful workers.”
text: I couldn't have asked for better service while staying at this hotel. I will definitely be coming back. The location was perfect, it was quiet when I wanted to sleep, the room was clean and the decor was beautiful.

title: “Make Sure You Get What You Asked For”
text:
Be aware that a "Standard Room" is a tiny room with a full size bed. I booked a room FOR TWO six weeks in advance from a major hotel booking website. On my arrival in NYC, I was issued a cubicle with a full sized (double) bed. When I asked if I could upgrade, I was informed that the hotel was completely booked. My son had to stay with a friend in Brooklyn as there was no way we could both sleep comfortably there. I contacted the manager on my return and was informed that I was given the correct room and was told to contact Hotels.com so they can "explain the situation from their operation side."(?) I was told I should have upgraded to a Deluxe room or contact the hotel directly beforehand to ensure I got what I wanted. 
From the responses here, I suspect I will get another defensive response. May I suggest to the manager that HE contact the major booking website I used so that they can clarify this issue for future customers. 
To be fair, the front desk staff was friendly and courteous and the hotel was very clean. You have top pay $1 for every five minutes of internet use. The hotel does not have a restaurant and there is no breakfast offered. I would not pay this kind of money for this type of accomodation or service again. I have stayed in many other hotels in NYC that offer more for less. Look around or ask questions before booking with this hotel

title: “Such an elegant hotel and superb service!”
text: We enjoyed the wonderfully central location of the Jefferson, the handsome décor, the careful choice of objects in good taste in every room and the delicious food in the restaurants. The pleasant and cheerful staff are surely a good sign of efficient management and a well-run hotel. It is certainly an address to retain and recommend without hesitation.

title: “wasnt that bad”
text: reading endless reviews of this hotel made us wary of staying here. but really it wasnt that bad. the room was modern, everything worked, plenty of pillows and towels and friendly staff. we tried the breakfast one morning and you could see the ladies making everything. id definately stay there again.

title: “good place”
text: fairly priced nice and clean rooms, staff was very helpfull close to downtown and UT campus.

title: “Loved location of hotel”
text: I travelled with two sisters & two nieces for a long weekend for my first visit to the Big Apple. After being out in the hustle & bustle of Times Square the hotel is an oasis of calm & quiet. The staff are all very friendly & accomodating. Loved the cookies at check-in & the delicious martinis in lobby bar. Our room was on 41st floor offering a great view of the M&M billboard etc. The rooms are definitely a good size for females getting ready for theatre, shopping etc. We had no problem getting taxis whenever we required them. I would stay at hotel on a return visit.

title: “A nice stay for the money we paid”
text: It's a good hotel. Nice area, close to everything. Staff was friendly. I would go there again.

title: “A nice hotel”
text:
My family and I recently stayed at The Blake. The exterior gives a rich feeling to the hotel and once you walk in, you are greeted with a feeling of comfort, sense of belonging. Too many times you go to a hotel and clearly feel "out of place", this was not one of those moments.
The staff were very helpful, helping with a couple issues I had (i.e. in room internet, more pillows and a wake up call). The room was huge, the bathroom was decent sized too, bathtub/toilet and sink in one private room with door while another sink sat outside that door with a mirror, this was excellent because it allowed my daughter and I both to get ready at the same time without being in each others way. The TV and cable were awesome, loved the office area of the room and the thick curtains kept outside light from entering the room too early in the morning. The pillows are amazing as I like firm full pillows, not the standard hotel pillow full of air that squish. The bedding was soft and comfortable too. 
Cons that are fixable: low hard beds, internet not available in all rooms, wake up call came 2 hrs earlier then requested and the then there is the LOUD restaurant/bar. The waitresses didnt seem happy to be at work, the menu had dried food on it and when my family of 5 (children to) walked into this 10 table restaurant, we were chased out by music louder then I have heard at a Lady GaGa concerts. Which by the way, of those tables, the ones located anywhere near the music were empty because it was so LOUD. If they could have toned it down to a reasonable decible, they could have filled the joint. I only bring these cons up to give the owners the ability to fix them by next March when I roll into town again and need a place to stay. I understand they are renovating the place, so start with these cons and you'll be a 10!

title: “Anniversary Outing”
text:
Well 21 years of marriage deserves a well deserved night out at a luxury hotel. We arrived at the hotel and was offered a suite upgrade. The suites were very well appointed, and enjoyed throughly. Down comforters, nice bathroom ammentities, and flat panel tv's everywhere. 
We started the day with spa services and a couples massage which was EXCELLENT and needed. The staff was always more than helpful and we really enjoyed our stay. 
A premium hotel commands premium pricing, but the name says it all. We had a great time?

title: “Great Service - Henry is a gem!”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel for a 3 night business trip and everything was terrific! I can't say enough about Henry and his incredible service & demeanor - Henry is made for this business and it's clear he loves his job AND making people feel special. I'm in the service business and it is celar Henry is a superstar!!

title: “Great place to stay”
text: If you are looking for some place different this is your place. Not the standard chain hotel, you feel special here. Loft style with high ceilings, modern furnishings and a great location. Would go back in a minute.

title: “Great stay and wonderful location”
text: Checked in around 8pm and was met by wonderful staff at the reception who were very very helpful with directions. Room was clean and well maintained and yes the elevators were slow but I was on the second floor so taking the stairs was not a problem. Friendly porters and they also have a business center where you could use the compterd for about 5$ for 20 minutes. Would be back again soon.

title: “Best Value Luxury Stay Ever!”
text:
Stayed here for a Staurday and Sunday on the way back from a wedding, and loved every second. I joined the ambassador programme for $150 back in May before a trip to another Intercontinental Hotel, but we still had the 'free weekend night voucher' that covers the second night of a 2 night weekend stay.
The room (upgarded as part of Ambassador thing) was really spacious and overlooking Pensylvania Ave, we even got to see Obama's motorcade come past the hotel as it is right next door to the White House.
I suppose I would desribe it was very luxurious, great service but a little tatty if you looked hard enough at certain things, but overall only the pickiest and most anal person would have any grounds for complaint.
All in all, with the voucher etc we paid $291 for 2 nights with parking and tax, incredible bargain and worth the Ambassacdor fee in itself as the cheapest rate i could find anywhere else was over $800!
Join the programme if you travel much, and stay here if you visit Washjington, its so historic and central that it feels like you are right at the heart of it all.

title: “Good, clean, nice place to stay.”
text:
No complaints here. The staff are really friendly and sweet, there's free internet/computer usage at reception, and free breakfast (pastries, oranges, cereal, toast, coffee) is always a nice touch. Location is a bit out of the way for sight seeing, not sure how close it is to public transport as we were only here for a night.
The rooms and beds are comfortable, nice bath products etc. Curtains for the main room window would be nice as it was a little too light to sleep in with the see thru shade.
Good value for the price in NYC.

title: “hotel was VERY dirty!!”
text: we stayed here fro 2 nites unable to cancel for 2nd nite due to "prepay" bargain price. room was dirty..food in fridge..qtips on floor..GUM stuck to wall. pool was utterly unacceptable. no hot tub, although current AAA book sates there is? hmm? noise in hall at 3 am was unbelievable. coffee pot filthy! maid who re-cleaned our room very pleasant and aplogetic but when you check in and want to rest before dinner this is impossible when your room is being cleaned. Never would recommend.

title: “Another great Club Quarters location”
text: My company usually places us at the CQ Wall Street location, but switched us to WTC location this season. All the usual amenities at this locale, but with added bonus of being a squeaky clean, new property, with lots of light and views. Staff are very hospitable and helpful – a missing TV remote was replaced immediately. Great incentive to re-cycle: $5 credit for restaurant/bar if one forgoes daily maid service. Location is somewhat awkward for cabs at certain times of day, due to general area congestion with WTC construction, security, and crowds visiting the memorial area. Subway service short blocks away gives easy access to city. Rooftop bar is quiet, comfortable and convenient for evening drinks. My room, 19th floor faced the river, so no noise concerns. All in all, prefer this locale to CQ Wall St.

title: “Overall great, just a few gripes; the good BY FAR outweighed the bad”
text:
Pros: 
1) Jonah in Bell Service; very friendly, quick with our baggage, engaged our kids
2) Substantial breakfast
3) Kids loved the pool on the 19th floor
4) Location of hotel is PERFECT
5) Very close to red line station and to other bus stops on Michigan
6) Free wi-fi was easy to set up, worked flawlessly (a rare feat it seems these days!)
Cons:
1) Timing of housekeeping staff
2) Temperature controls in room
3) Room could use a bit of TLC; peeling wallpaper, etc.
4) Pack N' Play was promised but not delivered
5) Valet parking $42./day with in-out privileges, but we literally never got the car out while we were were; there should be a lower price if you don't intend to use your car
**
We have visited Chicago 5-6 times prior to this trip. This was the first trip with our two boys (ages almost 4, and almost 1). The hotel was perfect for them. They boys slept in the main room, in the pull-out couch and our Pack N' Play (we reserved one with the hotel, and the front desk person at check-in indicated it was or would be in the room, but it wasn't there; we had brought our own from home, because I kind of figured there would be a problem with this).
The location was absolutely perfect for walking to most attractions, including Millenium Park, Navy Pier, shopping on Michigan Ave., etc. We took the #146 bus to Shedd Aquarium with ease.
The pool is more than sufficient for splashing about with the boys. Not too big, but big enough. At its busiest, there were maybe 10-12 people in the pool, and it wasn't bad as everyone was courteous. If there had been more people, and/or the ones in the pool had been unruly, it would have been bad. But it wasn't. it was great!
The breakfast was a very nice addition, allowed us to save time and money by eating at the hotel before venturing out each day. Plenty of seating, high chairs, variety of foods for both parents and adults, etc.
**
When we arrived at check-in, the room was very warm, which was a surprise, as it was only about 50 degrees outside on May 27th. Jonah with Bell services noticed the temperature, checked the vent and indicated that they had had to switch back and forth between heat and AC because of the big temperature fluctuations. We tried a variety of combinations, between opening the windows, turning the AC on and off, etc., but couldn't get the temp quite right. Also, it was strange to me that the AC control was in the main room, and we'd have to "sneak" in there in the evening from the master bedroom, trying to adjust the controls while not waking up our kids.
The issue with the portable crib wasn't a big deal, and I'm sure they'd have brought one if we'd reminded them, but since I specifically called to add same to our reservation, and then at check-in the staff reiterated that one would be in the room and wasn't, that was kind of annoying.
We stayed 3 nights. On the first full day, after the first night, we returned from a day of sightseeing about 3:15pm and the room hadn't been cleaned. Not a big deal, but we put the kids down for a nap and about 4 housekeeping came knocking. We got fresh towels and asked if they could come back later, and that wasn't an option. The following full day, they came and cleaned between about 4:45-5:30pm, which I thought was pretty late, but it is a big hotel. Also not a huge deal, just struck me as a bit unusual. The room was cleaned very well when it was cleaned.
The room itself was overall nice. Some peeling wallpaper and cracks. Just a bit unsightly, nothing more. The bedding was nice. The kitchen is well-appointed with some cookware, place settings for 4, etc. Enough that if you were inclined to save money by cooking some lunches and/or dinners, you certainly could do so. We even had a garbage disposal and dishwasher, along with two-burner stove, microwave and full-size refrigerator with freezer.
**
Overall, we would definitely return, mainly because of the location, 2-room kid-friendly suites, friendly customer service, and free breakfast. Keep up the good work!

title: “Fantastic hotel, fantastic location!”
text:
If you want to stay in the heart of Boston, with almost everything within walking distance then this is the hotel for you. Firstly, the taxi from the airport was $28 and back to the airport $18, so cheap and easy to get there. The hotel was clean, and the people who worked there friendly and helpful- I had both the consierge and porter help me with queries.
I stayed in an Economy room which, while small, was everything I needed for my stay (although the shower pressure could have been a little better). A full sized bed, small wardrobe, bathroom and TV, was everything I required. If you're used to larger hotel rooms, don't stay in the economy room, but for $100 a night, it was brilliant value!
I travelled on my own, and would highly recommend this hotel for lone travellers. I felt safe and secure staying there, and if I ever visit Boston again I won't hesistate to stay here.

title: “Small room with good location,”
text: Small room, small bed, small sink and bathroom. Bed had some crumbs in it, shower has tiles missing on floor, and we didn't we get our room serviced until we requested it around 3pm. Nothing great here, move on.

title: “A must stay!”
text:
I stay with this Hotel twice a week, and feel like I am at home. The staff treats me like family, and make being away from home that much easier! I totally recommend this Hotel!!!!!
Sincerely---Brent

title: “Benjamin is a Great Choice!”
text:
We stayed at The Benjamin in April of 2008. As a family of four, with two teenagers, this was the perfect hotel. My husband and I had a king sized bed, son had the pull out sofa and daughter had a roll-a-way. There was plenty of room for all of us. The galley kitchen came in handy for breakfast.
We were on the 8th floor facing Lexington and did have some street noise, but hey, this is NYC! I am sure that rooms on the other side of the hotel are quieter. 
The staff could not have been more helpful. We were greeted each time we returned to the hotel. The doormen were always there to help. We had one small glitch with housekeeping, but quickly received a phone call from the housekeeping manager apologizing and asking if there was anything she could do for us to make up for the mistake. (They forgot to make up our sofa bed, and we had to wait about 45 minutes for housekeeping to come and take care of it.)
The hot chocolate in the lobby was a nice treat as we returned to the hotel each afternoon. It is delicious!
The Benjamin advertises itself as the luxury choice among the Affinia line. I have to agree. We have stayed in every type of hotel, from The Ritz Carlton to budget hotels. While The Benjamin isn't The Ritz, it ranks very high on our list as one of the nicest properties we have stayed in. The amenities are excellent, the staff helpful, the property spotless and in a great location. What more could you ask for? We will return to this hotel again on the next trip to NYC!

title: “Excellent service and accomodations...but beware of extra charges”
text:
Arrived late evening and was greeted very well from every member of the hotel staff that we came across. I must note that I got a great rate of $150 per night. This hotel is in the heart of the Denver night life with short travel access to the Pepsi center, Coors Stadium, convention center, main 16th street strip and numerous bars and clubs. 
The room was spacious and elegant. This property is very new so it has all the bells and whistles. 
Upon reaching my home destination, I checked my bill and was surprised to find out I had been charged and extra $120!!! I put a call into hotel management to discuss the charges and found out that I was charged for premium wi-fi, 6 mini bar drinks and overnight valet parking (considering we had a car valet parked for dinner only...2 hours and where still charged the full rate! absurd)

title: “Friendly staff”
text: We stayed at the Sheraton for 3 nights, we went down for a football game. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Mike Rodriguez was happy to accomodate us in any way. The rooms were outdated but very clean. Would stay at the Sheraton again.

title: “We had a great stay!”
text: We stayed at the Affina 50 in early November. I'd stayed on previous occasions at other Affina properties in New York. The room was large and very nice. We had a great view on the 22nd floor. The staff was helpful with recommendations on neighborhood services. The hotel is very well located. All in all, it was a great visit!

title: “Small, clean rooms in a fantastic location”
text: I have come to expect excellence in a Kimpton property, and this is no exception. The location is really great being right next to the Ferry Building with it's shops and Farmer's Market and just a 5 min. walk to the Embarcadero BART station, which you can jump on and be at SFO in about 30 minutes. You can upgrade to a view room if you want to, but a smaller, less expensive comfortable room was fine with me traveling alone. No gym on site, but you can get into a really great YMCA next door for $5. The cardio equipment comes complete with a great view of the bay and the Bay Bridge. Prices were much less expensive than other Kimpton properties in SF. The wine and cookies are always appreciated!

title: “Good value in NYC”
text: We were pleasantly surprised when we arrived at the Fairfield Inn. Arriving mid morning we were expecting to have to put our bags in storage but all three of our rooms were ready. While the rooms were not huge they were typical for NYC and VERY comfortable and well appointed. The beds were comfortable and the rooms looked like they had recently been re decorated. Very clean with lots of towels, etc. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The hotel was not right in Times Square but it was only a few blocks walk and we actually liked the location. A bit out of the way of all the bright lights and noise. Close to subway.

title: “Just reserved but must tell anybody who wants to go there”
text:
I read all the reviews here and i decided to reserve this hotel for our 12-hr stay in DTW. As I was booking, i booked the Southfield Detroit Westin by mistake and the booking was a non-refundable reservation. I called the DTW and Southfield Westin. But the reservation couldnt be transferred. Reaching there at 4 Am I was not in the mood to drive 25 miles to Southfield. So i called again and this time the managers were present and they found a way for me to cancel the reservation and make a new one with DTW. The people were also very friendly and very helpful inspite of the wierdness of the request. 
With this kind of service, Westin has earned another customer for life. I will update the review after i complete my trip...
Thanks

title: “Very Nice Hotel with TERRIBLE Customer Service”
text:
My goal as always is to give an accurate description of the hotel and our experience. The Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Hotel is Lovely. Large windows, lots of seating areas, centrally located with your standard nice rooms. However the customer service in the hotel is terrible. If you are not dressed to impress in your finest business attire then do not expect the hotel staff to take you seriously or give you the time of day.
My husband and and I were in town for a conference that he was speaking at. I called ahead to confirm that check-in was at 3PM and ensured that we were good to go. The person on the phone said um yeah check in is at 3PM. When we arrived at 3:35PM we were given the up down look over by the lady at the counter who was checking us in. She informed us that our room was not available and offered to DOWNGRADE us at no charge, or we could wait for an hour and a half for our room to become ready. My husband asked what time check-in was and the issue with the rooms not being ready. She explained that housekeeping had not gotten to it yet. I asked the lady at the counter if there was not any other same cateragory room available in the entire hotel as we would not want to downgrade or wait with an infant in the lobby for over an hour. She looked irritated at this request and asked again if we wanted the double bed room instead of the king that we had requested, we replied "no". She then magically found a King Room. it was a handicap room, but a king. 
On our way to the elevators and the room I noticed the well placed advertisements offering starbucks refreshments in the hotel and decided to go once we were settled in to our room. When I came downstairs I looked around and then went to the concierge desk to ask directions. After waiting for the concierge desk employees to finish their personal conversation, i asked if the starbucks was in the lobby, she replied yes, i then asked where, she replied "around the corner" .... so i motioned as to the direction and she mmm-hmmmd... I stood at the counter for a few minutes waiting for someone. then i see the employee coming to stock the cold cases. she asked was i waiting for a drink - yes. she replied "we are open at six am" oh. --> back to the concierge desk. asked if she could point me to "an open starbucks" she replied across the street.... i am not sure if this person thought i lived in downtown phoenix or didn't realize that the hotel has more than one side to it with multiple exits so i inquired again.... she replied "the arizona center" oooooh once again.. i don't live here, work here, and am asking simple questions. 
When I returned to the hotel I spoke with Duncan the manager. He did a good job of acting shocked and abhored with the customer service in the hotel and promised that the hotel would exceed any and all expectations from that point forward. However, any customer service could have exceeded my expectations at that point. Nothing was done. Nothing else was said. We will not be back. We mentioned to the conference planner that we would never want to stay at that location again as the hotel employees seem to only care about people dressed in business clothes and who does that on Sunday when you are not working?

title: “Calm area and good comfort”
text: Great for recreation. There were busses passing by, but we used car to get downtown. About ten minutes to sixth st. Surrounding were calm and with good services, take a walk and visit The Veranda, a small pub with locals and waiters that'll do shots and beers with you!

title: “I would definitely stay here again”
text:
The hotel location is excellent especially if you like to visit Chinatown, Little Italy, Soho, Greenwich Village and etc. There were also good bars and restaurants very near. Didn't feel unsafe or anything like that by the surrounding area. Subway was around the corner and the excellent Katz's Deli. The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. The breakfast which was included was well enough too. 
The room was small and the bathroom quite big compared to the room size. It was still well enough for our use. We did miss a proper closet space though as the only closet we had was full from our two coats. A coat rack could be useful. Our room was situated on the second floor but the noise from the street didn't bother us at all. Slept like babies.
Would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “A great stay in an excellent location to Beale Street”
text:
Location: Not far from the Amtrak station which is how we travelled to Memphis, literally 1 block away from the trolley system, access to a few food shops and supermarkets. There is a bank located opposite the hotel itself which was handy for cashing travellers cheques. It is a pleasant 5-10 min walk from Beale Street which has to be seen! Also only a few blocks away from the Mississippi River and Mud Island. We were given a number of a luxury transport service, which offered us transportation to and from Graceland which is a 15 min drive and cost 25 dollars each way. I thought this was reasonable and the car was great.
Hotel: The general appearance of the hotel is good, the lobby area is very nice looking. We were checked into a suite on the 8th floor, the room was great. We had a fully equipped kitchen with dishwasher, fridge freezer and a hob. Everything was clean and tidy. The bathroom was also great. I have to mention the free breakfast which was of top quality, best free hotel breakfast ever!
Overall: For easy access to the main attractions of Memphis and a pleasant and affordable hotel this is a great option. My only criticism is that if you are on the rear side of the hotel, there are fans/generators outside which make a fair amount of steady noise. I am a light sleeper and luckily had my earplugs. If I didn't however I would have raised a complaint and requested to be moved to the front of the hotel which I am sure they could have dealt with.

title: “Good location near the airport”
text: We had a 12 hour layover at LAX from 11am-11pm and decided to get a room rather than stay at the airport. We waited about 10-15 mins for a shuttle to La Quinta then rode the short distance to the hotel. The hotel was fully booked and we had about 30 minutes until a room would be available (which was great since it was still an early check-in) so we went over to Taco Bell for a quick bite to eat. The room was large and comfortable, service was friendly, overall a good stay. We really didn't think much of the neighborhood/area but then again, we were there for less than 10 hours.

title: “If the price is right for you, it's fine”
text:
I spent the weekend of July 29-30, 2006 at 70 Park. 
The location is convenient. The staff is polite. The building and rooms are clean. The decor is tasteful. If 70 Park is in your price range for a good but not great hotel, it's a fine place to stay.
If you are considering 70 Park as a possible luxury accomodation, it's not. The rooms are small - not places in which you would casually lounge for extended periods of time. The beds and linens are not the top class that you would find in a luxury hotel. The bathrooms are very small - mine was probably 4x8 feet, so that things like the toilet paper holder and bathmat had to be constantly shifted to use the bathroom. A number of electrical fixtures in my room did not work. One of two elevators was out of service, which made for long waits. The pastry and coffee offered for breakfast in the lobby were a step above a motel's, but not a huge step above - and certainly not as good as what could be purchased at any shop in the area. The polite staff was not particularly friendly or helpful, other than one or two of the doormen. I had no fewer than five knocks on my door from maid service on the morning I checked out - when they obviously should have known enough to wait for me to check out. 
I list all of the above not as complaints, but to illustrate that while 70 Park may have pretentions of being a luxury boutique hotel, it's in reality a good, limited, small hotel. 
If you're looking for luxury, you're likely to be disappointed. 
If you're looking to splurge, this is not the place to do it. 
If 70 Park's prices seem reasonable to you for a good small hotel in a central location, you'll be satisfied.

title: “Conveniently Located, but.....”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Hyatt for eight days in January, and we found most of the employees to be extremely friendly and helpful. Just about every employee acknowledged us in passing by wishing us a good day or just saying "hello." When we arrived, the staff quickly located the items that my husband had shipped to the hotel via UPS days earlier. All of the bell men were friendly and seemed to genuinely enjoy their jobs. 
The only issues we had were with the room and the rude staff in the Bistro. Our sheets AND blanket were ripped. We had to ask them twice to provide us with new bedding. We thought we could live with the ripped blanket if they would just give us new sheets. After a night of waking up multiple times with the ribbing of the blanket wrapped around either my neck or one of my arms (no...I'm not kidding), I couldn't take it anymore. We also had a rather unpleasant experience during breakfast at the Bistro (the restaurant on the 2nd floor). The servers were rude and one of the cooks actually approached our table and asked my husband if he had a problem because he thought my husband was staring at him from across the room. That was the last time we had a meal in the hotel. We decided that we won't be staying at the Hyatt when we return in January '06. While most of the staff seemed to give 110%, that experience in the restaurant left us with a bad taste in our mouths.

title: “Top Class Hotel.”
text:
Great hotel, great location, and excellent staff. We stayed here from the 28th October 2012 to 3rd November 2012 and arrived as the city was preparing for Hurricane Sandy to hit. The staff kept us up to date with what was going on and might occur, and were helpful every time we spoke to them. Our room was on the 7th floor and suited us perfectly, and was kept spotless all the time. Well done to Vivien who done this. We used Tavern 17 a few times and the beer was fine and reasonably priced for a hotel. Food was also nice, but i would recommend the bar snacks to anyone. Great value for money. The coffee shop was fine for coffee and tea but i never ate there so i cannot comment on the food. The hotel is in an excellent location and there are loads of decent bars and restaraunts nearby within easy walkind distance, and across the road is a typical American Diner called "Little Petes" which did filling breakfasts and supplied plenty of coffe for very reasonable prices. Don't expect a la carte but it filled my needs and was always jumping before 09.00 so you may have to queue.
When i travel all i really want is a nice clean room, decent bed and helpful staff and i received all this at the Radisson Plaza Warwick, yes they may have been a bit noise in the corridor, in the early hours, but this was just people enjoying their stay and only lasted seconds. If i go back to Philadelphia i would certainly stay here again.Thank you very much to all staff i came in contact with.

title: “Smart and stylish”
text:
Myself and my boyfriend stayed here for 5 nights in June 2012 and it was a perfect base for us in NYC.
In terms of its location it is really not far from the Empire State Building which is a bonus and we found the surrounding area to be absolutely fine so no complaints there.
The hotel itself is very stylish and I really liked the overall design and feel of the place. We were on the 5th floor in a standard queen room - the rooms are small but this is expected in NY. Despite the size, the rooms are comfortable (especially the amazing beds!) and the bathroom was very nice with an impressive shower. Being on the 5th floor we didn't find it too noisy. 
One thing I was impressed with during our stay was the efficiency of the maid service - our room was, without fail, cleaned every day with fresh linen and towels etc. 
The only downside to our stay was the fact that we visited the hotel not long after its transition from Hotel LOLA to the King and Grove, and this was fairly obvious as there was no real identity to the hotel apart from the odd small thing with 'King and Grove' written on it. We actually found it very difficult to locate the hotel when we first arrived as it was not obvious from the entrance what the hotel was called! I would also say that another downside was that I felt the staff were not particularly talkative - it would have been nice when we checked in to be given some information about the city i.e. a map etc. We also felt that the lobby area (as nice as it is) lacks any real atmosphere, and the lobby bar was noticeably empty every night that we stayed. 
Overall I would choose this hotel again if I were to visit NYC as it was a really comfortable base, I just think the hotel needs a clearer and obvious identity which was lacking during our stay.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
The hotel is in a good location - between Carnegie Hall and 5th Avenue, it is only about a 15-20 minute walk from Times Sqaure. 1 block back from Central Park.
We stayed for 5 nights and found it a decent hotel. The only problem we had was our room was roadside so we had problems sleeping due to the noise of the traffic - I would recommend to anyone that they ask for a room at the back.
Other than the noise the room was great and spacious, when checking in we where told we could order take aways and get them delivered to the room, also a supermarket up the road too if we wanted to take any food/drinks back - there was a fridge/sink/coffee machine in our room.
Didn't have any problems with the lifts at all, ok they might have been a little bit slow but no problems.
Only had the hotel breakfast once which was 4 dollars each, didnt think much to it as it was only continental i.e. toast, danish pastries, cereal and there wasnt much to choose from. There is a diner 5 mins up the road which does excellent breakfasts and value for money.
Hotel has internet service in reception area - just swipe your credit card and go.
Hotel staff where friendly all the time. Asked them to arrange a taxi for us when we left as had to leave at 5am - ended up in a full size limo which only cost 60 dollars (£30) between us both.
I would definatley stay here again the next time I went to New York and would also recommend it to friends.

title: “Not what I expected”
text:
I stayed at the InterContinental for a weekend shopping trip and while the overall stay was okay, I expected something more.
The rooms were extremely dated and small considering the high rates. Linens were thin and well used. The walls are thin - we could very clearly hear the individuals around us - making sleep very difficult. We also noticed stained lamp shades, peeling wall paper and dirty air returns.
On the plus side - we experienced very good service at the front desk and the bell desk. You also cannot beat the location for shopping Michigan Ave, walking to Navy Pier and vicinity to restaurants. We also purchased the Breakfast package with our room and it was very good.
Overall, the hotel is just average and I would not stay at it again when there are many options for the price on Michigan Avenue.

title: “Excellent Hotel Experience”
text: My stay with La Quinta Dallas-Love Field was first class all throughout my stay!! The staff were friendly and professional!! The staff went above and beyond the call fo duty to serve my needs and requests. The room was extremely clean and quiet!! I felt safe and secure in this hotel!!

title: “great location , best service”
text:
We are a family with 3 teens. For the kids it was the first time in NYC, so the location was perfect. Otherwise I wouldn't stay in such a noisy and crowded location. If you would like a central and touristy area this is your hotel.
The service was great! Especially the concierge service

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
We lucked out and "San Diego Concierge" (in the San Diego yellow pages) found us a room here for $139 a night. It was a great hotel and the pools were really nice, but I felt things were way overpriced here. The restaurants were out of our budget and the market charged $6 for a 6 pack of Diet Coke. We drove down the road and there is a KFC and a Wendy's and a grocery store where we bought breakfast items. 
For what we paid, I feel this was a reasonable price. But when I heard the normal rate was $400 a night, I was in shock. Do not pay that much to stay here!!!
We had a lot of fun here, but I just recommend to anyone staying here to not agree to pay the high rate.
The staff were very friendly.

title: “Nice little hotel with a good location”
text:
I have to admit, the name threw me off (never having stayed in a "motor inn"). But, the hotel is pretty nice for the price. I have stayed in the Union Square area in the past, this was my first trip to stay in another location. The Marina/Cow Hollow location was quite nice. There is a bus stop right outside the door and plenty of restaurants/bars/shops in the surrounding blocks. It took us maybe 15 minutes to walk to the pier 39 area from the hotel.
The rooms are fine, nothing amazing, but clean and comfortable. Bigger than i expected. The windows do overlook the street and if you are a light sleeper, the street noise (cars, busses, people walking home from bars) is pretty loud. No noise from other rooms though! The bathroom is fine, lots of towels and they do a good job refilling the shampoo/soap/etc. The water pressure was good and hot was very hot. If you are over 5'5", the shower head is too low (just have to crouch in the shower). 
The staff was friendly and willing to help with any request.

title: “Ideal Location”
text: We reserved a room at the Hotel Abri, sight unseen, when on a girls' weekend in San Francisco. We weren't even sure just where the hotel was! Imagine our delight to discover it was just off Powell St. a block or two just up from the cable car turn-around, near Union Square. Our room was a suite, clean, not huge, but big enough for three, all the amenities we wanted (TV, radio, room fridge, computer hook-ups). Not a good view from our room, but who spends much time in their room anyway? There were restaurants, bars, and shops aplenty all around us. We would just hop on the cable car & ride over to Fisherman's Wharf for a day of fun. The hotel staff were very helpful, also. An easy walk back to the BART station for our ride back to the airport. An ideal location!!

title: “5 mins from union square, great stay!”
text: Lovely hotel for our busy stay I'n San Fran loads to do so diddnt spend much time I'n the hotel but was a great base to explore. The staff pointed us I'n the direction of some lovely restaurants and a lovely piano bar at the top of the Wyatt so were very helpful. Very clean and tidy hotel with great service!

title: “A wecome sight at the end of a long day when you come up the steps from the metro”
text:
As the heading said a welcome sight as you come up from the metro system at the end of the day. The hotel is ideally situated on a metro line just around the corner from Central Park and a very short stroll from the hustle and bustle of Times Square.
We stayed at the NEW YORKER last visit and tended to compare the two hotels, but both are ideally located the only downside to this hotel was lack of a bath plug and a very short bath! At the end of the flight or from just walking each day it would have been lovely to have stretched out in a nice hot bath. We used tissue to bung the hole then put the plug on top so we did use the bath, but as I said a longer one would have been better.
Broadway is the block behind the hotel, here you will find Mama Mia and the famous Iridium Club where Les Paul still plays on a Monday eve. On the corner of the winter gardens theatre is a traditional American Dinner where wanna be staff sing there way throughtout your time in there! Althought the bill spoilt it a bit, as after the staff had send a bucket around for there tips etc the bill then had a 18% surcharge on it which made the meal a little on the steep side. There is a little shop called Fuffys dinner across the road from the hotel that has a great cheap menu and the staff are great, will explain stuff or make reccomendations. 
We bought city pass tickets which saved us quite alot of money as it covers most things visitors want to do in New York. 
Once again a great visit, we have seen New york from top to bottom and loved every minute.

title: “Close to the fun!!”
text: What can I say, the price is good, it's close to the Aquarium, restaurants, train station, well... everything!!!. The service is great, some rooms has a nice view of the port, the food on the hotel restaurant is very good but if you are on a low budget avoid it is very expensive. highly recommended.

title: “Great value and location”
text: We were looking for an affordable one night stay while attending a Giants game. Arrived in the morning, yet able to check into our room. Fernando, the desk clerk, was speedy, friendly and helpful with directions and general information. The hotel is old, but clean and located close to Union Square and easy access to public transportation. We garaged our car and used the bus to get around town. We would stay here again.

title: “good but double booked rooms?”
text:
Room reserved with hotwire, great price and the hotel is dated but for the price, I have no complaints. I was very disappointed when I get a knock on the door at 11:30pm for housekeeping to clean my room. Thought nothing of it, maybe just a mistake till at 1:35am, someone opens the door while I'm sleeping!
Clearly they were trying to check in, not someone breaking in...needless to say, ruined my sleep and would have said something to management but needed to rush off in the morning for business meeting.
Hopefully Paul, as the general manager, this is not a pattern for your hotel?

title: “ratther busy comfortable hotel”
text: complimentary breakfast coffe available reasonable furnishing view not good from 3rd floor reminded me of vertigo looking into stircase adjoining raher unhelpful reception staff porterage needs improvement

title: “Good Location, good Value!”
text: THE QI Downtown Baltimore is in the city center and walking distance to the convention center. Parking garage is right next to the hotel, making it a good option for travelers with own vehicle. The lobby is a bit dated but ok. The staff is very helpful. The rooms are on the small side but clean. The decor is a bit strange with a combination of classic and modern. Walking distance on Charles Street are numerous small restaurants.

title: “Love this place!”
text: The hotel is very nice , rooms are a good size and always clean, we stay here at least once a year. The location is great, you can walk to Gaslamp District or enjoy a nice stroll along the bay down to Seaport Village. Location,location,location!

title: “Impeccable, worth the money”
text:
No complains at all. Adequate size room, decent price, great roof top bar and very good breakfast. Excellent location and very polite and helpful staff. Soundproof at night, so good night sleep.
Parking across the street at a very decent rate. Great location

title: “A FANTASTIC GETAWAY SPOT”
text: We used TownePlace Suites Keystone as our home base. We shopped, at the many near by store, visited the Titanic exhibit and had a great dinner, across the street, at P F Changs. We returned to get a wonderful nights sleep on those oh so relaxing beds. In the morning ,a short walk, to Le-PeePs for a yummy brunch. We look forward to returning .One could not ask for warmer ,friendly place to stay, with such great service.

title: “Good Hotel”
text:
It was good to stay at Days Inn metrocenter. I always stay there when i go to Phoenix, Az. 
The only problem was the internet access. I was there 2 days without internet.

title: “Best luxury hotel in Chicago, for sure!!”
text: Fabulous luxury hotel. Best in Chicago and I have stayed at the Four Seasons, Park Hyatt, Ritz, and many others. Location is great. Very convenient to dining, shopping, and Michigan Ave. Staff is very very friendly, extremely polite, and pleasant. Everyone smiles and is cheerful which is refreshing these days. Not stuffy and overly formal like some of the other luxury hotels. The rooms are larger than most and tastefully decorated. Unbelievably clean. If you are looking for a luxury hotel in Chicago, give the Elysian a try...you won't regret it!!!

title: “Comfortable, reasonably central location and clean”
text: My experience with this hotel was very positive. I found a great last minute deal on Travelocity, and was more than satisfied with the value I received. While it isn't as centrally located as Copley Square, it is less than a block from a "T" subway station (orange line, New England Medical Center/Tufts), and if you like sightseeing on foot, it is within walking distance to Boston Common. (Chinatown is also just a few blocks away, where there are Vietnamese, Thai and other Asian restaurants in addition to Chinese.) This hotel seemed like a newer property, or else was very well maintained and had been redecorated. The furnishings in my room seemed new and the king size bed was very comfy. Everything was spotless. Although there was a lot of bustle in the lobby, my 2nd floor room was very quiet and I had a good night's sleep. The staff was friendly. There is a restaurant, bar and also a Starbucks in the lobby, but I didn't try them out. The rooms are also equipped with minibars. Evidently they have a tradition of offering guests a freshly baked chocolate chip cookie upon check in, which was a nice surprise. Overall, I recommend this hotel.

title: “Dissapointed In This Hotel”
text: Just stayed at The Mayflower. I had read information on this hotel and was looking forward to staying in a very nice historic hotel. My room on the 7th floor was very outdated and dirty. The bathroom was DIRTY - baseboards and ledge around sink had layers of dust - had not been cleaned in months. I understand the hotel is old - but it needs to be clean. Housekeeping needs to step it up. Fixtures were rusted and there was pink mildew around the tub. My room faced another building so the view was not good. Disappointed as a Marriott loyal customer. For the same price, I would choose another DC hotel. It's been a few years, but my room was much nicer at the JW Marriott.

title: “Great San Antonio location”
text:
Very conveniently located to Alamo and Riverwalk. A little pricey for a one bedroom suite, but take advantage of breakfast and free evening drinks and food. Ran into a famous Dallas Cowboy staying at the hotel for the football camp. Employees are very helpful.
If we came back, would stay here again.

title: “Excellent - would definitely stay again!”
text:
Let's begin with the fact that I'm 60 & very picky. We were traveling with a pet, so Staybridge was on our short-list of hotels in Memphis that didn't break the bank. The price was right, and it was in a safe location. 2 primary musts. Our suite was excellent. LR/kitchen combo (full size fridge, all necessities furnished, flat-screen TV. Bedroom had king bed - very comfortable. Bath was dual room - vanity area/closet and then toilet/tub/shower. Showerhead was to die for.
Once in our room, there was absolutely no outside noise. With this being a pet-friendly hotel, you would never had guessed there was an animal on the premise. Rooms must be very sound-proofed, because we heard no hall noise, or nothing from rooms above. Like a private apt.
The bathroom vent fan didn't work and my DH mentioned it to the desk clerk the 1st morning there. Within an hour, the maintenance man was knocking on our door to replace it. I was shocked!
Breakfast buffet was adequate for a good start to the day. Appetizers (meatballs, nachos, etc) were provided in the evenings, along with beverages. Fitness room had every type of equipment imaginable. Outdoor pool was also secure.
Great experience. Wish all hotels/motels would follow their lead.

title: “A unique and beautiful Inn with outstanding customer service”
text: We chose the Chelsea Pines Inn because of its value and location, what we got was the whole package! Our room (Ann Margaret) was delightful, quiet and very comfortable. We did have to use the stairs but we think exercise is a good thing, and we knew about it in advance. The breakfast was full of great choices and had a friendly atmosphere when joining other guests. It's location to area attractions, food, post office for mailing postcards and the subway is excellent. After we left, we received a personal email from the owner which just shows you how amazing this place is. I would def go back - recommend, recommend, recommend! A++

title: “Gem of a hotel in the downtown core!”
text: We stayed here overnight before taking an Alaskan cruise and found the location perfect with helpful staff at the front desk and home cooking in the restaurant. We would stay here again if in Seattle.

title: “Well placed for Fisherman's Wharf and cable car access.”
text:
Stayed at the Argonaut for four nights at the end of our recent holiday. Had a suite that was on the corner of the second floor of the hotel. The room size was fantastic and it was nice to have a separate living room area to relax at the end of a day pounding the streets! 
We arrived relatively early before the guaranteed check in time of 3pm. I enquired as to whether the room was available and was informed that due to the hotel being full the night before (Friday) they were still in the process of turning around the rooms. We left our bags for a couple of hours and walked around the local area. Upon returning at 3pm, we were informed that the room was ready and keys were issued etc. When we arrived at the room, the housekeeping team were still inside but left a few minutes later.
I had been nervous when making the booking having read some comments about being able to hear noise from other rooms. I had requested a quiet room, however, appeared to suffer the same problems as other reviewers with loud banging noises coming from above. The city also carry out street cleaning on Tuesday mornings with a street sweeping vehicle and then also pressure wash the sidewalks. I would recommend a high floor and either the south or eastern side of the hotel to avoid most of the noise.
Wine hour between 5pm-6pm was very nice and was a good opportunity to see some of your fellow guests in the lobby.
Location is great for Fisherman's Wharf attractions and ferry services, as is access to the San Francisco Cable Car to make your way to Nob Hill and Downtown.

title: “I heart the Flatotel”
text:
My mom and I were planning a long weekend in NYC for my birthday. When we arrived, the hotel was very acommodating and helpful with our questions and needs. 
It's a great location near time square, NBC/Rockefeller center, subways, food, etc. This is a very central location for NYC visitors. I've stayed in NYC before and this was a huge room and bathroom in comparison to other hotels.
When Hurricane Sandy hit, the staff at the Flatotel went above and beyond. They kept us updated with notes under the door. They turned up the music, lights and music in the lobby the day of the hurricane to keep things lively. Additionally, they provided unexpected breakfast. The staff continued to clean our rooms while the city was shut down. Everyone was friendly and patient with our endless questions. They let us continue to stay at our original rate as our flight was canceled again and again.
A quick shout out to the staff: Stephany from HR, Monica, Sammy, Victor, George, Omar, Jeff, Rasham & Aby...and everyone we missed. Thank you!!

title: “Very nice hotel with a good location”
text:
We went to this hotel before flying to Washington. The room was very clean, spacious with a lot of amenities. The front desk associate was very helpful, she answered all our questions and provide us all the informations concerning the things to do in Jacksonville.
However I was a little bit disappointed with the breakfast. The food as a good value but I found the staff rude. Breakfast is served from 6am to 9am. At 8:55 the room was closed and the staff started to turn off all the equipment (toaster, waffle maker, orange juice machine…) It was 9:05 and the buffet was already broken down.
Except this little disappointment I recommend this hotel, the location is great if you have a car, if not they have a shuttle and they can take you wherever you want in Jacksonville.

title: “Not Nearly Meeting the Standard”
text: What made the situation more acceptable was getting a low conference rate. But attention to details is lacking. The hotel's climate is erratic. The lobby is exasperatingly hot, while some conference rooms are chilly. There were mysterious problems with our reservations, which had to be ironed out at the front desk with undue frustration. Expect to pay unreasonable parking fees if you stay here. The standard room rate is an absolute ripoff. If you get a very low rate (i.e. conference rate of $87.00) it may be okay, but not a good deal.

title: “A safe Haven in Times Square”
