text: This hotel has a great central location. While the sidewalks in Time Square are packed with people and noisy, once you walk through the doors of this place you find a safe haven. Helpful staff and tasty cookies upon arrival. Our room was spacious, quiet and clean.

title: “Small rooms in an otherwise excellent hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Chandler for my wife's birthday in Aug 2012 over a long weekend. My selection of the hotel was based on the price point and overall reviews, and pictures of the hotel.
Location: Good location - close to the subway but easy to get to and we never had to wait long for a cab. I've been to NYC several times so I didn't go to many tourist sites but the Empire State building is nearby. Times Square is a bit of a walk but doable.
Hotel: Rooms were nicely appointed albeit slightly small. Bathrooms looked newly renovated, as did the room in general. The lobby was beautiful and bright. I didn't get a chance to use the gym facilities. Internet station in the lobby was a nice touch as you could print out maps/boarding passes etc. on it. If there is one knock on the room, it is a lack of natural light - our room faced an interior courtyard and it was relatively dark, even without blackout blinds. 
Service: Excellent - from the doorman to the concierge to the cleaning staff, the service was excellent and everyone was super friendly. Great job - it makes a good hotel excellent in my opinion. 
Overall: Outside of the small rooms (it is Manhattan), it was a great hotel with excellent value. I would highly recommend it to friends visiting.

title: “Terrible pillows, Slow internet”
text: The pillows at this location are lumpy and have no support. Terrible on the neck. They advertise High Speed Internet, but after 5 speed tests with Tech Support, it never even got close to High Speed - 64KB. I'm finding the bad pillows and the slow internet at many La Quinta locations. This chain have been one of my favorites for 17 years, but it's time to move on. The quality has greatly decreased.

title: “Skip this one”
text:
We had a mini family reunion at this hotel recently. Some in our group had stains on their sheets which had to be changed. My room had a latch that wouldn't open unless I put my shoulder into it. The pool was a little cloudy and the cabana that should have had drinks and extra towels had 2x4's and chain link fence closing off the bar. Looking around the hotel there was really a need for a good vacuum and floor waxing. The breakfast buffet was overpriced with poor service. Food was ok but just ok. 
The biggest thing wrecking our stay was at 2 am there was an alarm that sounded like a foghorn 2 inches from my ear that went off. Apparently there was a fire alarm malfunction occurring during a minor rain storm. It went off at least 5 times until about 430 am. The next morning ther was a long line at the front desk asking for a refund. Those who didn't insist got charged for 1/2 a night. The rest of us did get the room comped for the night. 
I had previously stayed here when it was a Radisson and it was a much better operation. I think the management is fairly poor in this one and will never stay there again.

title: “Good location for the MGH”
text: This Holiday Inn is very close to the Massachusetts General Hospital and a large variety of restuarants, also the Charles Street Subway stop. While it lacks the scenic aspects of places closer to the Harbor and Quincy Market, or Harvard Square, it is a well-kept hotel and is certainly ideal for people having any business at the MGH.

title: “Clean, big rooms”
text:
The Embassy Suites sits among several hotels near the airport and I-670. The suites are very clean and very large. The bathroom is very big too, but cold, and my room didn't have a bath mat. The bed and bedding were very nice. My only issues were with the safe, which was awkwardly located on the back wall of the closet. Very hard to get to and almost impossible to see. The shape of the safe is also very odd -- it's vertical and fairly narrow. To put a laptop in there you need to set it on end. In any event, the safe didn't even work. There are directions posted, you need to insert your room key, but it didn't work for me.
In this day when everyone carries multiple devices, hotels really need to improve their safes -- size, location and function. The Embassy Suites flunks on the safe front, but is otherwise a nice place.

title: “Sofitel Ruined our Vacation”
text:
We booked our stay at sofitel not knowing that it will be a disaster in waiting. For a hefty amount we booked a room for 5 nights. When we go there on 5/27 1:30 am the manager Melisa got rude with us when we asked for the King room. She said we will only get the Queen room. She forced us to contact price line if we wanted king room. Priceline was closed at that time so we disappointingly settled for Queen room. She was also not willing to give us any room above 15th floor.
Next day we talked with Priceline to ask for King room and they said it was upto Hotel management. I was on phone for almost one hour with Priceline and Sofitel managment tossing me to each other. This was our first trip to New York which had already started on a bad note. Eventually Sofitel management asked us to pay $100 extra per night if we wanted the King size room. Interestingly another staff person at the desk had asked for $80 earlier and yet another one for $50. Me and my wife were so frustrated and disappointed with Sofitel that we settled with our Queen room and focused on the NY City and tried to forget the worst experince that we had with Sofitel and Priceline.

title: “Great location, average facility, bad service”
text:
This is the worst Le Meridien Hotel I've stayed. During check in and check out, i overhead the staff arguing with customers both times. Once I told the manger that I will give bad reviewers they even don't send their own internal reviewers to me, they tried to hide...
Location of the hotel is not bad, you can walk to all major downtown area. Room and facility is average. They will nickel and dime you so watch your bill statement when you check out.
I won't be back.

title: “Amazing Hotel - Great Location in the Galleria Area”
text:
This is a super nice hotel that provides top notch service and recognized PC members. 
Brand new property, fast internet, clean rooms, great service, great water pressure, great everything! 
I was upgraded to an amazing suite, with K-cup machine, lots of room! To make it even better I was just a few steps away from the executive lounge. 
The lounge had a small continental breakfast and evening cocktail hour which was super nice. 
If in the area again, I will without a doubt stay at this hotel!

title: “Hotel close to Jazz Fest venues”
text: We could not have found a better location for visiting during Jazz Fest. Hotel was very close to parks and music venues. Our room overlooked the Navy Pier, and we watched the fireworks from our hotel. We found excellent restaurants in the area around the hotel. We would stay again.

title: “My stay”
text:
Overall, I did enjoy the stay. My only issue was the heater. I typically like my room pretty warm, and the heater kept blowing both warm air and cold air. To the hotel's credit, they did get the maintenance man on it right away the one day that I did ask. The extra blanket helped me sleep better the other nights. 
Otherwise, the free parking and wi-fi were pluses.

title: “taste of Vegas Hard Rock in the Gaslamp”
text: stayed with my GF one night at the HRH since we were flying out of SAN the next morning. I upgraded to a suite and was given a Woodstock suite. Great room, and good folks at the front desk. We did not party in the hotel much but did eat at Mary Janes. Great vibe in here. A lot of flash but some San Diego chill. I will be back...

title: “Very nice...”
text: Lovely hotel -- stylish, clean, nice staff and the Hitchcock theme was nicely done. They don't do breakfast but there was some nice diners and cafes very close-by

title: “I'm so disappointed!!”
text: I'm staying at the hilton to ten days! every day the maid left the room in a way! sometimes missing glasses, sometimes leaving wet towels! the concierge and is very arrogant and not friendly nothing! 'll still six more days here, but I'm not happy with the service! only the location is good! I really expected more! Omar

title: “Great location”
text:
We loved being so close to the Ferry building and some great restaurants. The Farmer's Market on Saturday was such a great venue for people watching, not to mention the amazing food. 
Rooms are very small, and most do not have a view of anything except walls or other windows. The rooms are almost too small for two people because of the lack of storage space for two suitcases. Closet is tiny and there is not a dresser. Lighting is not good and there is not a full length mirror. If you expect a high level of service then this is not the hotel for you. Staff is friendly but not polished. Room maintance and housekeeping are average - visiable defects but no real deal breakers. The breakfast was good with fresh pastries, bagels, juice and cereals. Room decor and public space decor is comfortable.
We got a good rate (about $150 a night) and we booked it for the location so we were pleased overall with the value that we received.

title: “Absolutely Fabulous.Wonderful Hotel-”
text: Just returned from this beautiful Hotel. The staff are probably the most courteous and friendliest staff I have ever encountered. The Hotel is a delight and has to be seen. Beauty is everywhere from the display of white tulips at reception to the whimsical furniture.The bedrooms delight with lovely colours and white linens. I was nervous after reading the comments on tripdvisor . Now I will be booking the Hotel directly for visits to Sf. I would NOT stay anywhere else.

title: “Nice, affordable hotel”
text: A few blocks from Times Square, this hotel is affordable and clean. Rooms are comfortable and fairly quiet. Good breakfast buffet each morning.

title: “Fabulous Hotel with great service!”
text: My husband and I stayed here as we were coming to Denver to see the spectacular Van Gogh exhibit at the Denver Art Museum. The hotel is perfectly located across from the Four Seasons and off the 16 Street Mall which is filled with cute shops and restaurants. Ideal location. We thought the staff could not have been more helpful and we loved the guys who take cars and open the door - so friendly. They even got us a town car to the airport for the price of a cab! We will return on our next visit to Denver. Well appointed rooms too!

title: “A perfect weekend getaway”
text: I just got back from a two night stay at The Palce Hotel and loved every minute of it. The staff was extremely helpful and friendly as they allowed us to check-in early and assured us that they would notify us as soon as a fax that I had been expecting arrived, which they did. Being a member of Starwood, they stood by the room upgrade benefit, giving us a lovely CLEAN large room (no view however), with bathrobes (I had read earlier that none were given), a comfortable bed, and luxurious linens. The conceirge was helpful when we need directions/addresses, and recommended a Japanese restaurant that wasn't too fancy, but the sushi was delicious which was fine with us being that we should've done our own research ahead of time if we wanted to find the best sushi in the city. Location wise, it's a block or two away from all the great shops and just a short cab ride (no more than $10.00 ride) away from some great restaurants. Overall, I truly enjoyed my stay and recommend The Palace Hotel to first timers in the city who are looking for a comfortable/clean stay and excellent service.

title: “Lovely hotel, felt elegant - from the entrance to the bedding.”
text:
What a lovely, grand, hotel! We were in DC for a weekend visit and found The Churchhill
to be in a great location (park your car and walk 2 blocks to the metro - shopping, coffee and stores on the way.) They have great weekend rates, the staff is efficient and friendly, the room was big, the mattress perfect and the bedding was a welcome delight to two tired sightseers. We had a drink in the bar late in the evening - small but welcoming - there was fun chatter between tables.
The bathtub/shower units have been updated but aren't a snazzy as the sinks and vanities (which are new with granite tops). The rooms are really nice, tall ceilings, big windows and lots of space with warm colors and fabrics. We'll be back.

title: “Great staff,”
text: Staff went above and beyond to accomodate us for arriving early right off of a cruise ship. Great free breakfast and cookies and popcorn in the afternoon. Never been to Jacksonville and a great, affordable place to stay. Walking distance to a lot of things.

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text: Stayed here on the third leg of our honeymoon. Fantastic location (just five mins walk from the White House), and very reasonably priced too. Bedroom, bed and bathroom all very generously proportioned (only booked a double room, but got two king size beds in our room). Ran into a wonderful barman working at the hotel, who couldn’t be more helpful. Only issue we had with this hotel was the fact that it’s in a very business-orientated area of Washington and everything (including all cafes and restaurants) seemed to be shut over the weekend. Likewise, we had to travel to Georgetown ($20 cab ride) for any form of nightlife outside the hotel bar, or the brilliant one local restaurant – Old Ebbits. Would definitely recommend this hotel to others though, on the basis that tourist attraction proximity is more important than evening entertainment)

title: “Unique place to stay”
text:
I am at the Tryp Hotel in New York, MSG.
The hotel is so unique and fan. The food is great and the drinks are super nice and 
The service is excellent and the location is very good.
I will come back any time to this hotel. The lobby is also a unique touch.
Rooms are big and the hotel has a room to cover every need.
Great job!!!!

title: “Great Stay!”
text:
Please don't be turned away from the reviews my experience was terrific from start to finish. My reservation was prepaid before arrival and that did not alter my check in one bit. It was Quik and efficient. The young lady at check in was not rude but her tone and posture could be taken the wrong way. Being from Rhode island I was not bothered by it.
I appreciate the spacious rooms, free Internet . The reception monday was pleasant and a first for a Wingate that I've been to. the breakfast is simply a wow! Scrambled eggs, sausage , biscuits and gravy. What more can you ask for to get your day started.
Kudos Wingate I'm impressed and will be back with my future trips to Charlotte!

title: “Foreigners like it, Americans think it's a dive.”
text:
Shared bathrooms and only one shower on each floor. The bed smelled fresh but the comforters are the kind that scare you. The hallways remind you of a guys dorm in college. If the whole place looked like the front desk, it would be fine. Maybe wait until they are done remodelling to stay here.
I would recommend this hotel to people who love hostels and to guys who are in the city for the purpose of drinking a lot, want to have a good location and don't plan on sleeping much.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
Pro's
Good location five minutes from times Square; friendly staff; clean and well appointed rooms. The gym is basic but clean.
Con's
The Wifi is expensive - should be free.

title: “A Rip Off”
text: The room, if you want to call it that. My closet is larger. There were no bureau's. Could not fit one in the rm. The quilt was really worn. I have thrown out better. It was a very challenging experience. You did not even have rm to roll a suitcase. The tub was a foot bath size. The price was way to expensive for a night. I have stayed in the city at other hotels that were considered economical and received a lot more for your money. Not at the Belnord. The only thing on the positive side was that the mini stamp rm was clean.

title: “Not Great... No where to sit at breakfast...”
text:
I have stayed in many Marriott hotels, many of which being Towneplace Suites. They are typically for Long-Stay purposes, but I was in Denver and got a great rate for one night. The TV sets are tiny! They don't seem up to date with the flat screen upgrades most Marriotts provide. The room we stayed in had a pull-out sofa bed, which was terrible and took up the entire room when unfolded. The fridge smelled funny, and the room just felt gross. 
One of the worst things about this hotel is the breakfast. There is NO WHERE TO SIT while eating. There is a bench that most people sit on, but if you sit on the bench you have to hold your bowl of cereal on your lap, put your O.J. between your knees and your yogurt and apple can rest on the floor or in your pocket I guess... There were 15 people trying to eat breakfast in this tiny room, and everyone seemed quite annoyed. 
Staff were friendly, but dressed kind of sleazy. I wouldn't recommend this place.

title: “New hotel with excellent location”
text:
Got a great last minute deal on Christmas Eve, the hotel is new with contemporary decor. Loved the location, right next to a subway station and short walk to time square. And the parking operators right next door and across cost a lot less than valet parking.
The room is roomy by NYC standard, we got a room with two full size beds, sleeps 2 adults and 1 child comfortably. There is no bathtub in our room but a very contemporary over the head shower, I have never seen my son more excited in taking a shower.
The hotel provides bathrobes and slippers which is a surprise.
The hotel has a nice gym but no pool.

title: “Tiny, but adequate for visiting New York City”
text:
Be prepared for small rooms and corridors, but remember this is New York City, where space is at a premium. The front desk staff is friendly and the warm, gooey chocolate chip cookies that everyone raves over should be eaten immediately! They aren't that great when they are room temperature, which is a mistake I made in eating them later. 
I was upgraded to floor 26 with a complimentary breakfast voucher and a bar discount. Breakfast is okay - the usual hot and cold items. The gym is underground and the approach is through a narrow corridor from the reception area, but the gym itself is a decent size. The TV remote is unnecessarily complex - it controls the Cable TV box hidden below the TV and not the TV itself. Make sure you point it at the cable box to change anything on the TV. The room was small but clean. The King bed seemed short and I ended up sleeping diagonaly to keep my feet inside the bed.

title: “Lovely and spacious suites..”
text:
Location:
Located out of downtown Los Angeles in an area called Silverlake. This is a very Mexican style community and no staff around appeared to be American. The area was OK, shops were a good 15 mins walk. I recommend the 99 cents store to stock your fridge up!
Check In:
A reasonable check in experience. The lobby is nice and has a pretty fish tank on display.
Hotel:
The hotel itself is very good. The suite we had was very spacious so we had a lot of room even with our cases laid out on the floor. Bathroom was good. We had free wifi, fridge, microwave, coffee maker, HBO, free breakfast.. (Bagels, cereals, waffles, fruit, juice, coffee, toast etc...) all very good for the $114 a night rate we picked up.
Staff:
The guy who checked us in was a nice guy, however I was disappointed when I checked out as the lady serving me wasn't paying any attention to me at all. She was on the phone dealing with another customer and trying to serve me at the same time. Also she was speaking in Mexican the whole time to her collegue so I had to keep repeating myself to her as she wasn't listening and couldn't hear me over her speech. She was very rude in my opinion. Kind of the only real downer to the whole hotel experience, but I left disappointed due to this poor customer service/acknowledgment.
Overall:
This is a very well priced hotel. You receive a great spacious room with all major amenties you require. The location is a bit of a let down and the area is rough, but you can commute fairly easy downtown, Hollywood or Santa Monica. I would recommend this to anyone looking for cheap LA accommodation.

title: “Nice Hotel With Character”
text: I recently stayed at the Brown Palace while on business. This is a nice historic hotel with a lot of character. The grand lobby takes you back to the turn of the century . Room decor is maintained for the period with comfortable beds, huge windows but updated with well-controlled central air and a nice large screen TV. The one downside was the plumbing. The bathrooms have been maintained with the original tile floors and walls, the tub is the original tub so, the bathroom is somewhat dated but large and functional. My bathtub had a drain problem with water not emptying out for quite some even after calling maintainence. Also had a problem with the sink (severely leaky faucet) but otherwise a nice room. If you need a modern bathroom this might not be the best choice for you. Staff were very attentive and helpful and the location is convenient to most downtown attractions. Free internet access as well as a nice bar and restaurant in the hotel. There is also a spa but I didn't utilize that. Overall a nice historic hotel, comfortable, with character.

title: “Don't Make a Reservation!”
text: I made reservations for my husband and myself several weeks in advance at the rate of $130.00 per night. We were arriving after midnight--we checked in at the front desk and were given room keys and directions to our room (231). The light switch at the door did not work, so my husband walked into the room and turned on the light on the desk. Roaches were everywhere! On the desk, on the floors, on the walls...we quickly got our suitcases out of the room. There was no way that we could stay in that room! What was surprising was the fact the parking lot was full and there was a no vacancy sign posted--surely ours wasn't the only room riddled with bugs. We stood in the parking lot frantically calling other hotels nearby--only be told that all were full, of course it was nearly 1am at this point. We were told we could not get a refund, that we would have to contact hotels.com to get a refund to our credit card. The picture on the website is deceiving, as is the price...I would have expected the bill to be about $40.00 for a place like this! The Hampton Inn, about 2 blocks away, took pity on us and found us a room at a reasonable rate.

title: “Hilton Times Square: The best place to stay!”
text:
I stayed at the Hilton Times Square during the pre-Christmas rush. I got a real bargain on the price by booking directly via the website in September. We stayed from 13th until 17th December (4 nights) in a 2 bed deluxe room for only 1,279.32 USD. This was amazingly low if you take the exchange rate with Sterling into account.
The room was spacious (much bigger than any other NYC hotel I’ve stayed in) and spotlessly clean. We had a spectacular view of the Empire State Building. The hotel was quite festive with a large Christmas tree in the lobby and a Menorah, since it was Hanukah during our stay.
The hotel is in the best possible location if you want to be in the heart of the action. Noise is not a problem inside. I didn’t eat at the hotel. There are many food outlets nearby, including Applebee’s, located on the ground floor of the hotel, which is good for breakfast, burgers, milkshakes etc. The BB King Blues club is located across the street and is a good place to see a live band. The subway station is at the end of the block, making it easy to get to Fifth Avenue and Bloomingdale’s via Grand Central Station. Macy’s is a short walk down town.
Staff members were very friendly and extremely helpful. I asked for information about shipping something back to Ireland and they arranged everything for me, including packaging, without any service charge. I also made use of the safety deposit boxes at reception. These proved to be very useful as I didn’t want to leave my laptop in the room safe. When it came time to check out I asked to check out an hour late. They agreed to this with no charge. Closer to the time I decided I would like to stay for another hour and they said that would be no problem but that there would be a small charge of $25. When I finally checked out they didn’t charge me at all. We also had the free nightly turn-down service with chocolates left on the pillows.
This was my fourth trip to New York and this is the best hotel experience I have had yet. (I am particular about hotels!)I will definitely consider staying here again.

title: “Great Place”
text:
This place has a great staff, pool, rooms and is close (walking distance) to old town. The breakfast is great and coffee is available all day. Book and video library is available. We would definitely stay there again.
Gerry and Carole Sauve
Gibsons BC

title: “Loews is the BEST in Philly!”
text: My husband and I frequently visit Philadelphia. We have stayed at many of the center city hotels while visiting friends and family. None of the other hotels can compare to the outstanding service and comfort of Loews! The rooms are spacious, the staff is professional, friendly and helpful. The restaurant offers excellent choices for all diners with nightly entertainment in the lounge area. The location works great if you are visiting the historic areas. There is easy access to public transportation and most attractions are walkable from Loews.

title: “Location is all this place has going for it.”
text: I attempted to enter the hotel at the main entrance to check in but due to some private party I was told I couldn't enter and had to walk around and enter thru a side entrance. Not only was it very late to walk by myself but the side entrance has numerous steps and I have a broken foot. As a paying guest of the hotel shouldn't I be afforded the same consideration as a party goer? The gentlemen at the front desk were very kind and professional. My room on the 4th floor was quite shocking when I walked in. The carpet was spotty and filthy, absolutely no bathroom counter but the worse - a very large ring around the bathtub! The furniture was in dire need of replacement, the shower door did a very poor job of keeping water off the floor, as a matter of fact I needed to call the maid to bring more towels just so I could mop up the floor. Thankfully the bed was clean and comfortable. The party noise could be heard in my 4th floor room and ended promptly at 2 am. Shampoo & conditioner provided, no lotion or shower gel, things that I would expect from a hotel of this caliber. Location is wonderful but at the end of a long day and relaxation is in order, this room doesn't provide it.

title: “Old school grandeur, modern amenities, great location, slightly overpriced”
text: The common areas of the hotel are stunning. The food in the hotel and room service are usually fairly good as well. Some of the rooms are slightly outdated. However, all the usual amenities you expect of a 5-star hotel are present. All in all it's a very good hotel. Though I would suggest that it is slightly over priced.

title: “dont believe everything you read”
text: I went to the roosevelt with my daughter for her first trip to new york. This was my 4thtrip so i have stayed in a few hotels. We had read some dire reviews so i was a little worried. I LOVED IT. the location is perfect as you are walking distance to all the major attractions. The rooms were clean with amazingly comfortable beds. Slight critisism would be very old air con. Loved the old style glamour of the foyer and we found no lack of lifts even if it was busy. Can only think that bad comments were made by people with ridiculously high expectations. Try the wardorf Astoria if you are that fussy.

title: “Best Location Possible”
text: Wonderful,helpful,courteous staff just a few of the many good things I could say about my stay at Jurys.Great location ,for all attractions in the city.Staff very good in giving unbiased information on the many queries which I posed at them.Tip regarding their bar Cuffs ,can be very busy at the weekend so get there early,if you can get a seat meals are excellent.Will be back in the future as our time at Jurys was all and more I could have asked for.

title: “excellent location”
text:
my friend and I just spent 2 nights at the Cadillac Hotel in Venice beach. We were referred by my daughter, and she advised that it was a quaint hotel in a very neat part of Los Angeles. My 65 year old friend and myself were delighted with the hotel. It was spotless. Lovely linens, brand new bathroom, nicely painted room. Wonderful lobby with fresh coffee, 2 computers to check emails, and couches to relax on. The staff was extreamly helpful with directions etc. Yes, the homeless came out after dark, but we all knew about it. We will go back again for sure.
Gail Morrison
Terrace, BC

title: “Fantastic Staff make for a Fantastic Experience”
text:
I was looking for a hotel close to LAX as my family was flying into LAX in on Thursday(18th October) and returning back to Sydney on Friday evening(19 October) at 9:15pm. I didn't want to stay in Hollywood as we have an 18month old son, and really didn't want to do alot of traveling back and forth on the day. We really just wanted to "relax/wind down" before our return to Australia.
 The MOST important requirement was that the hotel be "clean" and offer a "late checkout" option-6:30p.m(additional fee was perfectly acceptable)., as our flight was departing LAX at 9:15pm and we didnt' want to get stuck sitting around LAX international with an 18 month old with nothing to do(those of you familiar with LAX international.......CAN RELATE-I need say no more) if we were reqired to abide by most standard hotels 12:00pm check-out times-any other perks the hotel had to offer us would be an added bonus.
We looked at the reviews from the "Courtyard Marriott" and noticed it had just undergone a recent full renovation and was receiving mostly positive reviews from tripadvisor users, so it seemed like the most obvious choice as we wanted to stay within the Marriott hotel organisation.
I called Marriotts' US reservations and enquired as to rates and availability for this location-to which availabilities were on offer, it was only when I enquired about the "late check-out" option, and after their US reservations customer service employee contacted the hotel directly to advise me that a late check out was NOT an option-I would have to pay a Full Days Rate to check out later than the normal check-out time (again we were requesting a late check out time of 6:30p.m.). 
I then turned my attenton to Los Angeles Airport Marriott-once again calling their US reservations centre to checking pricing/availability and late check-out options with their reservation representative. Upon checking with the hotel directly, the representative advised me "yes-late check-out is available for a US$75.00 fee". "BONUS". I chose a single king sized bed on an high floor with pool views with access to the concierge lounge for my family for $279.00/night + $75.00 late check-out fee. 
I then proceeded to review the comments left on tripadvisor-some good, some not so good-but I thought "nobodys perfect???right??? lets see what happens-in a positive light".
We arrived at LAX on Thursday, roughly at 815p.m. exhausted from the 5 hour flight-got our baggage and proceeded to the shuttle pick-up area to go to the hotel.
Upon Arriving- as I was walking inside I noticed a Starbuck's Coffee and thought to myself "looking good so far"....we proceeded to the Conserciege check-in and were waited on by a very nice employee who was a "trainee", but extremely polite non-the-less. I provided him with our reservation details and he was able to pull up the reservation, but couldn't find any particulars regarding the reservation (I.E. late check-out, concierge lounge access, high floor with pool views ect). He politely advised me that the hotel had very few vacancies and that we would be on the 5th floor. I wasn't impressed with this detail, but went up anyway. When we got to the room it wan't facing the pool, it was facing traffic-I was Very dissappointed to say the least. I pulled up our reservation details contained within the confirmation e-mail-which actually stated the particulars of our reservation and proceeded downstairs to concierge to see if this issue could be resolved. The original concierge employee was pre-occupied helping another guest, so we were helped by another very nice/polite gentleman. I explained what was going on and showed him the original e-mail from Marriott outlining the details of our reservation(lounge access, high floor room with pool views, late check-out ect.), he was very apologetic and advised me that they were truly booked up, but he would see what/if he could to
to rectify our situation. He came back a short while later and advised me that he didn't have any rooms available on a higher floor, but he could provide me with a room with 2 double beds and a poolside view. "I'll take it", I advised.. as we were already on the 5th floor it was only a reletively short walk to our new room. In a word "FANTASTIC"-a nice little balconey quiet and very clean room.
We ordered a hamburger, glass of wine, and desert(hot chocolate cake) from room service it arrived within 30minuted and was not only still hot, but absolutely BEAUTIFUL!!!!!!!!
We awoke Friday Morning (19th October), and proceeded to the concierge lounge for breakfast and again encountered the most wonderful/pleasent mature aged employee who said hello to us and true to form was very, very, nice to our son. We struck-up a conversation to which she told us about her 3 grandchildren currently in Germany she proceeded and was polite enough to show us a picture. 
We proceeded back to our room-specifically the balconey to look at the pool below and decided that would be our little "excursion" for the day. We were just about to leave when we discovered the safe in our room wasn't working, to which maintenance arrived promptley and fixed the problem on top of replacing our defective coffee machine for a working unit. The Maintenance worker was a young African American (I apologise I don't remember his or anyones names) man who through conversation told us he had previously worked behind the counter for roughly 2 years-he told us that we had just recently missed the space shuttle landing at LAX to which he was gracious enough to show us photos and a video-VERY, VERY COOL(Again I cannot Stress HOW POLITE/PROFESSIONAL/Respectful this young individual was-Truly an asset to the Marriott organisation). He replaced the batteries, apologised and left. We then realised we needed "little swimmer" nappies-I ran downstairs to the Marriotts giftshop to which they advised me they didn't have any, but offered to call a couple of local stores to see if they could locate some for me. They contacted CVS, whch had them in stock-to which I took a short (5-7minute) taxi ride to procure said nappies(Again-VERY, VERY HELPFUL/POLITE).
We had our excursion to the swimming pool area - Very nice I must say, the poolside attendant/employee was extremely polite. Our son absolutely LOVED his first experiece in a pool. 
We finished off the day with a luch at the hotels restraunt-which is were we had the pleasure of meeting "Willie" our Waiter. He was Amazing-polite-upbeat and made an amazing recommendaton of the turkey burger, which I can honestly say I would never normally entertain the thought of consuming, but enjoyed every minute of it along with the apple cobbler.
Thanks Willie-your're the Best
The only issue that we experienced was with the WiFi-which apparently only made allowances for 1 guest, even if there were two individuals in the room who needed access at the same time. We found it difficult to sign-in to the service, and roaming through out the hotel trying to utalise the WiFi signal seemed difficult, But really that's just splitting hairs.
I would rate the hotel, it's staff, and our experience a 9.995 on a scale of 1-10.
We would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to our family and friends and will deffinately be staying here again if the opportunity arrises.
I would like to give a very heartfelt sincere Aussie "Thank-you" to all of those wonderful employees we were lucky enough to come in contact with during our brief stay.

title: “The Argonaut was Excellent!!!”
text: We just got back from our 3 night stay at this wonderful hotel (July 26-28). Upon arrival we were greeted by the very friendly and helpful staff. The rooms were very nice with the most comfortable beds I've ever seen in a hotel. The location of the hotel is excellent for visiting the Wharf. I will definitely recommend this hotel to friends and relatives.

title: “Fantastic Location”
text: I can't believe that you can get this nice of a hotel with this great of a location in the center of DC for this price level! Everything you might want to see in DC is within walking distance, and if not the Metro is only 2 blocks away (which also runs straight to DCA). The hotel, while maybe not the newest on the block, was great. Our room was clean, the staff were wonderful, and you can't help but feel safe (FBI headquarters is around the corner), and I swear the (free) WiFi signal in our room was stronger than my router at home!Clean,helpful staff, easy to get to, & a fantastic location all mean we would gladly stay here again on our next trip to DC.

title: “Cheap but very unclean!!”
text: Our room was VERY dirty. The carpet had dirty lint buildup all around the edges like it hadn't been swept in years. There was mold all over the bathroom walls and ceiling and the toilet was nasty both items which staff came in and mostly cleaned after we complained. The furniture in the lobby was all ripped and torn and the walls in our room were ripped/torn and the stairwell leading up to our third floor room made me think I was going to get mugged. We had a clock that didn't have the right time and you couldn't adjust it. I would certainly not recommend this hotel.

title: “excellent room, shuttle did not arrive”
text:
After a long 11 hour flight we went to the shuttle pick up spot out side the airport and waited and waited all the other hotels shuttles came and we scrutinised all the signs for the crowne plaza and nothing.So after nearly 45 minutes we had to get a taxi and even after arriving at the hotel people were waiting for the return shuttle to pick them up and we finally saw one and nothing of that colour went past us so don't know what happened that day.
check in was very slow so we eventually got a nice room but it was on the airport side to had quite a bit of aircraft noise, it was a lovely room otherwise and could not fault it, thats why we gave the rating of 4 stars, had to get a taxi next morning as we just could not rely on shuttle after the previous experience
to go to the car rental pick up.We also got a very good price through our agent.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Great location on the water. Lobby is beautiful, staff were helpful. Self parking was $16 per day, little steep but there is no where else to park. Hotel is next to seaport village, and the Seaport tower overlooks the Midway aircraft carrier which is open to the public . Rooms are average size, bathrooms have been updated with all modern amenities. Would recommend.

title: “a great hotel in nyc”
text: I stayed here for one night with my husband. Got a good deal on this hotel from priceline bidding. The wonderful lady at the check-in desk upgraded us to a one bedroom suite. The room was fabulous, roomy and very clean. It is the size of a regular nyc one bedroom apartment. I would definitely stay here again with the kids next time. This hotel would be great for a families with children. It is a bit away from the touristy time square/theater area but if you willing to walk a bit - this is a great location.

title: “friendly is an understatment.”
text: Excellent stay at an excellent hotel. My girlfriend and I were only in the city for a night but, the hotel and friendly staff had us contemplating staying another night. The wharf is somewhat of a tourist trap but, if you're a tourist, this is your spot. Great location.

title: “Feels like home!”
text:
I have been traveling on business to the Four Points Sheraton every other week for about 1 year. Every time, without fail, as I arrive at the hotel I am greeted by name and with a handshake from Kyle.
The service is always great, the room always very clean and the meals always hot and fresh.
Thank you making me feel at home!

title: “Dated but loved the space!”
text:
My husband, 16 year old son & I stayed here for nearly two weeks over Xmas & New Year. We chose this place after reading some of the reviews & liked the sound of this hotel being an ex apartment building. The last time we stayed in New York, we stayed in a room no bigger than a shoebox, so it was a refreshing change this time to stay in a one bedroom suite. Apart from the separate bedroom, it had a living/dining area, a large bathroom & a small self catered kitchen. We were on the 8th floor, so had a pretty good view of the buildings.
The hotel itself is quite dated, but if that's not a problem, which it wasn't for us, then it's fine. The location is pretty good...you're about a ten minute walk to Grand Central Station. There are various shops just down the road from the hotel (convenience store, chemist, liquor store, pizza, burgers, McDonalds, chinese etc). The convenience store is very handy for bread, milk etc. 
Although it was freezing (snowing) outside when we were there, it was always toasty warm in our room. Some nights, we even slept in a sheet. The housekeeping ladies were always lovely. The only problem we really had, which isn't a biggie, was that every time we wanted to watch a pay per view movie, we had to keep ringing reception to get it uploaded, which was a bit of a pain, but as I said...no biggie. The only other little complaint was sometimes there was a weird smell on our floor once we got out of the elevator, but the smell was never in our room, so it didn't matter.
There is a laundry in the basement for you to wash & dry your clothes. Definitely buy your own detergent as I brought some laundry powder from the lady at the counter & it ruined some of our clothes (bleached some of the colour out). This was really annoying because I specifically asked her if it was safe to wash my clothes in it & she said yes.
It looks like there was a restaurant at this hotel, but it was closed for renovations when we were there. Also, you have to pay for the internet which was about $50 for the week.
All in all, we had a great stay in this hotel & would stay again.

title: “Check Your Bill!”
text:
After 3 phone calls, almost a week later, I still have charges on my credit card that are in error. I had read similar reviews, but did not think it would happen to me. It has soured my opinion of this "just average" hotel. 
If you are just going to Memphis for a leisurely weekend to experience downtown, I would recommend staying at the other Marriott properties which are located closer to Beale Street.

title: “Friendliness and Warmth in the Snowstorm”
text: We keep coming back to the Giraffe every time we visit New York. The extra goodies like the complimentary breakfast, the evening wine and munchies, pianist in the lobby, and chocolates on the pillows don't hurt either. This time we ended up staying an extra day because of the snowstorm that cancelled our flight. The Giraffe was happy to extend our stay at the low rate we'd been given on a pre-pay basis a month earlier. The neighborhood is off the beaten path, which for us is a bonus. The restaurants within walking distance are great--Blue Smoke, Les Halles, Artisanal, and Gramercy Tavern are our favorites. The hotel also offers room service from Park Ave. Bistro and Dos Caminos, which are right next door. Rooms are a good size, by NY standards, with small balconies and motorized window shades. Decor is modern, perhaps needing a little updating here and there, but generally pleasing. Everything is clean and our rooms have always been serviced in a timely manner. Questions and requests to the desk are always dealth with in a friendly and prompt manner. I love this place!

title: “Great hotel on a prime location”
text:
This is my second stay at the Fairmont Copley Plaza Boston. My previous was in Jan. 2009. Both experiences had been very positive. I loved their friendly staff rarely found on deluxe hotels. 
My queen bedded room was perfect for me, lovely furnishings. I enjoyed the large mirrors on the closet's doors and the plush robes/ towels. Being my second stay I did not have to pack my own toiletries knowing their Miller Harris toiletries were there, waiting for me :-) (You can purchase them at their gift shop)
The restaurant service was very good and so the room service. Food was excellent on both sites. 
I truly like the hotel location. 
Concierge service was great and I loved the restaurant suggestion.
If you have walking issues ask for a room near the elevator.

title: “Super cool”
text:
I was astonished to see the hotel had some bad reviews, so before writing mine I carefully read them... And it´s true, our room was tiny (but then I don´t expect to spend much time in it when I´m in NYC), it had fantastic and very open views and I loved the modern and stylish look. The bed is a platform bed so if high beds is what you are used to, or you have difficulties getting up from low furniture, this is NOT the place to come to. The bathroom is small ... but does one need much more than that: unless you want to wash your hair in the sink why would one want a larger one? Don´t know, this is a diverse universe and luckily NY offers all kind of different options to different people. 
We stayed four nights (in july) and I personally absolutely recommend this place: the design is stylish, location is just perfect (right next to the highline and the Chelsea Market), the staff was really nice (perhaps a bit slow to react) , the place has an great vibe, the terrace is ... how can I put it? amazing, breathtaking. To float in the swimming pool looking at the Empire State was an experience in itself. 
It´s modern, stylish and hip ... with a latino flavour. And that is something that I just loved!. 
We travel a lot, stay in tons of hotels in different part of the world, and I know for sure I have found my place in NY. Whenever I´m coming back, I´ll stay at the Americano.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
I've stayed in many hotels through business travel. The InterContinental in Chicago was definitely a very nice hotel. Service was friendly and helpful. Even the valet guy was really nice.
Rooms were clean and the bed was VERY comfortable.
Wish I had stayed a few days longer...cause I never got to try the pool.

title: “Great Customer Service / Very Nice Facility”
text:
My wife and I purchased the room from priceline.com, name your own price. We got an unbelievable price for a room on New Years Eve. Upon arrival, Jon at the front desk gave us a great room on the 7th floor overlooking the marina. He was very professional and explained the facility in detail. We eat at the Swim Bar and the food was very good. The jacuzzi was large enough for about 15 people, and was positioned with views of the pool and tower. Very Nice. 
The best was the customer service given by Manager Michael, the night manager. Unfortunately, we had a someone in the room next to us with a crying baby. We are not ones to complain about much, but finally we call down to the front desk. Understanding Michael or the Hyatt could not do anything about the crying baby, Michael let my wife vent and offered a few freebees. We asked for Michael to add comments to our account should we want to take advantage of the offers. 
Later in the morning we did take advantage of the offers and had to speak with the day manager, Robert. He was equally as nice and could see what Michael had written on the account. I can say that Michael and Robert went far beyond the original offer for compensation, and we were well cared for. Front staff Ruth finished the checking out process, and was continued the great service. 
Even if the mishap hadn't occurred, my wife and I would still recommend this hotel. Its just good to know the staff and customer service etiquette would be there should you need it. Thank Hyatt and the staff for a great stay.

title: “Chicago: The Wit Hotel, Chicago, IL, EXCELLENT!!!!”
text: You are right down in the heart of Chicago, just off the Chicago River, within walking distance of Magnificent Mile (Michigan Ave) and about 4 miles (at most) from Navy Pier. You are surrounded by culture, shopping, restaurants, and views. The hotel has it's own restaurants and even a night club on the top floor. The rooms are very Modern. One of the prettiest hotels I've stayed at in Chicago, and rooms aren't terribly expensive. I would definitely go back.

title: “Great deal - & you can't beat the location!”
text: I just spent the weekend at the Edison and was impressed. The location was perfect and as a woman traveling alone, I felt very safe and comfortable. The room was small but immaculate and quiet. Note: bring your own hairdryer: you can get one from Housekeeping, but they bring it to you and want it back in one hour!

title: “West Coasters... consider this hotel before booking a red eye...”
text: I frequently have to travel to the East Coast and want to maximize time with my family until I have to leave. Instead of a red eye, I sometimes will fly into Ohare, stay at this hotel and wake up the next morning to fly to my destination. This is a fine hotel with very good service. The staff at the front desk is excellent and make sure that you know where and when to eat. The rooms are very tidy and the location makes it very easy to wake up and be on your way, relaxed and refreshed. They do a good job maintaining a high level of service at this hotel.

title: “Fabulous "Find" in the middle of everything”
text:
We were very pleased with our experience at the InterContinental NY Times Square, from our terrific corner room view to the terrific (huge) television set to the stylish and large tiled shower. We also had a great dinner at Ca Va.
We came into the city for a show, and decided to stay closer to Times Square than we usually do because of our short trip. The service was tops and we loved how everything was designed. The location couldn't have been more convenient, a mere block or so from the theater.
The only thing we were slightly unhappy about was that our car was parked outdoors by the valet service. This isn't a really big deal, but the sudden winter snow meant the car had an icy layer on it when it was time for us to leave. We would've self-parked in a garage if we'd known that the car would be exposed with the expected weather.
We will put the InterContinental at the top of our list of hotels to stay next time we're in NYC and recommend it to others. Thank you to the staff!

title: “Quiet, Comfortable and Inexpensive.”
text: Quiet, Comfortable and Inexpensive, all the necessities without the high cost of an SF hotel, and close enough to the Folsom SoMo Area.

title: “For the price...you don't get much”
text: I have always wanted to stay at any W hotel so the one in Times Square was such a great location, I decided to stay there for my birthday with my hubby even though it was 400.00 US a night and thank God it was only one night!! We were quickly disappointed. When we arrived, we had to take an elevator up to the 7th floor to check in then another elevator to the 46th floor to our room. The bathroom had mold in the shower, the bed creaked, the view, for the price, sucked...we looked at another hotel and not Broadway and the wireless was terrible(I was on the phone with someone trying to get it to work for 15 mins! and it was $14.95 for 24 hrs. It should have been free!!!) I would have been more happy at the Marriott, where we usually stay. I will never stay at this W again......

title: “Amazing experience”
text: From the time you enter into this hotel, you receive an excellent client experience. Everyone working at the Eventi are extremely pleasant and helpful. Oneill went out of his way to enhance our experience. He was extremely helpful and made sure our stay was an outstanding experience. My mother-in-law joined us on our trip. She is almost 80 and had not been back to New York since she travelled on the Queen Mary over 50 years ago. She was overwhelmed by the level of service and attention she received. We all loved the great tasting water every day and coffee and tea in the morning. All thoughtful touches! Highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Great location! Great value”
text:
Loved the stay. Breakfast great staff very helpful
Elevators long queue in morning

title: “Great stay!”
text: We had a great stay at this hotel. Very clean rooms and the staff would always go above and beyond, especially Randy and Maria. We stayed there for almost a week for my sisters wedding and had booked several rooms, everyone was very satisfied. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Fresh clean hotel”
text: Everything was great about this place except for the noise from outside that came through the thin windows and kept us up half the night (which seems to be a problem with most nyc hotels)and the fact that when I called housekeeping for toothpaste they brought it about 10 min later and then again about 40 min later when we were asleep and they did not believe us that we got it so they went ahead and called us waking us up again.

title: “Okay stay at the Orchard”
text: The reviews here are correct - the doormen are friendly; the bathroom is large; the rooms are quite large (compared to other SF hotels); the DVD library is nice and the TV's stereo system is great, and breakfast included helps you start your day. And no-one mentioned the lovely duvets on the beds. However, we were emailed that we'd have a non-adjoining room with a view. Our view was of fire escapes, an alley and pigeon droppings. A higher room was offered but was adjoining. The room was quiet except for the garbage removal one morning. The breakfast includes mostly meats and cheese and as you have to eat by 10 a.m., it was too early for that for me. The bathrobes we never used. It's a good hotel, but a bit pricey for what you ultimately get. Were booked for 10 nights, stayed only 4 and moved to another hotel.

title: “Just the facts: Very pleased with the Hotel Alexander”
text:
A hotel that is quiet, clean and convenient. 
Quiet street ($350 fine for honking), one block away from the W. 96th 1-2-3 subway stop. Riverside Park is 1/2 block away, Central Park is within walking distance. Nearby markets and restaurants on Broadway. A 24hr restaurant is at 90th and Broadway. Parking garage across the street from the hotel.
Staff was courteous and took the time to thoroughly explain charges, facilities and services available. 
Our nicely kept room was a on the 1st floor, one double and a twin (firm, no sag). Relatively large room with a/c and radiator heat. Closet, bedside table and desk. Venetian blinds, no curtains or shades.
Bathroom was small (4.5' x 6') but clean and tidy. Soap and shampoo provided.
There is a lounge with couches, coffee, HDTV and internet access w/printer ($1.00 per 10 minutes).
The price was right for the weekend we chose and is even less at other times.
In short, the Hotel Alexander is economical, clean and efficient. The quiet Upper West Side neighborhood (for NYC) makes for a great place to recuperate in time for the next day's adventures.

title: “Family Hotel”
text: The hotel worked out well for my family stay. The one downfall of a pet friendly hotel is your room can carry the after effects, as my first room did. I brought this to the attention of the manager, who quickly moved me to another room without question. The rooms are large, and most have views. They offer a well put together continental breakfast, and the hotel is very family friendly. I would recommend to all those traveling on business, or with family - not a romantic getaway.

title: “A hidden gem safely off the beaten track!”
text: As everyone knows, New York is famous for being both a fantastic city and an expensive place to find a room for the night. As someone keen to be close to the main attractions of the city but off the beaten track - and the premium you pay for being there - I was really pleased to discover Ink48 and the Kimpton Hotel group. Not only does Ink48 offer stylish comfort, all mod cons and impeccable customer service but you also get far more for your money than just 10 minutes walk away on the main drags. What you may have to sacrifice in terms of being right in the thick of things (if that's what you want) you more than make up for with the personal touch of the staff and the relaxed atmosphere. The rooftop bar must have one of the best views of the NY skyline in town. Make sure to go for the higher levels, ideally requesting a view over the Hudson if you can. The restaurant is worth visiting in its own right. finally, don't be put off by the Hell's Kitchen location; sounds foreboding but it's perfectly safe and 10 minutes walk from the main city vibe.

title: “I love The Lafayette Hotel!”
text:
This is now my third week in a row, and 6th time overall staying here. I have had nothing but wonderful experiences! 
My first few times here was over a year ago, while they were doing renovations. One room then was a bit out-dated, but still very clean, and was right next to the pool and had a gorgeous balcony over looking it! 
Now just a few weeks ago I got to come back, and I am so impressed with the renovations! This hotel is beautiful! They really kept the old/vintage charm, while making it new and beautiful. My first room was 116, I loved this room! It was HUGE! The next time I had a regular size room, and then today I got upgraded to a beautiful suite complete with balcony and fireplace!!
I LOVE the wall paper, carpeting, and colors they decorated with. The beds are always comfortable, the lobby and pool are beautiful, staff is always SUPER nice, especially Sydney! 
I also like the area, theres some good restaurants within walking distance and theres a piano bar attached to the hotel that is really cool. They also have another bar/restaurant inside that is really nice and has great service. 
www.crosscountryvegan.com

title: “Club Level Lounge”
text: I've stayed in many hotels for business but had the opportunity to stay here on the club level for an event the week of July 4 for pleasure. The hotel was completely sold out but the experience is one of the best I've had thanks to the Club Lounge Concierge, Shawn Zenser. He always tried to make sure we were taken care of and made the experience one to remember. I usually don't write recommendations but this one certainly warranted it.

title: “Excellent location and staff”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Radisson Plaza-Warwick for one night when we traveled to Philadelphia to participate in the Rock-and-Roll Half Marathon. We took the train to 30th Street Station and walked (with one carry-on with wheels) less than a mile to the hotel, which is in an excellent location in the center of the city, near Rittenhouse Square, City Hall, the Franklin Institute, Art Museum, etc. If you like to walk, the Radisson is in an ideal location. 
From the moment we arrived, the staff was gracious, pleasant, and professional -- both check-in and check-out were completed in less than two minutes. I had requested an upper floor with a view and they put us on the 11th floor in a very spacious, clean room with a view of the river. My husband said he thought the king bed was uncomfortable, but I slept soundly and was ready to race when I woke up. Everything in the room was clean and in working order -- the flat screen TV was huge and had HD and free HBO. The bathroom was clean and functional -- not the greatest water pressure, but lots of hot water. 
We ate dinner at the Tavern, which is one of (I believe) three restaurants in the hotel. Together we had two appetizers, two entrees, and three drinks for about $75 -- everything was delicious and the wait staff was attentive. 
I would stay at the Radisson again and recommend it to anyone who wants a central Philly location with a friendly and professional staff.

title: “What a Treat !”
text: Stayed the night at OTA and had a fabulous time. The staff was top notch and treated us with the utmost respect and courtesy. Our room was quiet and clean. There was construction across the street from the hotel and Cris offered us a room on the courtyard so that it would be quiet. If you need to stay in NYC overnight, I would recommend OTA. Be sure to check out the lounge on the 16th floor for an incredible view. Thanks to all the staff for making our stay wonderful.

title: “This hotel definately needs an overhaul of its rooms. It...”
text: This hotel definately needs an overhaul of its rooms. It needs new carperting, new painting and some repairs on its walls. One of the heaters in my room was broken and had to take another room. It needs a cleaning up.

title: “Loved the HGI”
text:
Booked 3 rooms at the HGI this past weekend thru Travelzoo for 89$ back in November. It was a mom and kid's weekend and the hotel couldn't have been any nicer. We had requested an early check in which they accomodated and set us up in a corner of the 22nd floor all together.
They rooms are fairly laarge with a microwave and fridge and Neutrogena products. Everyone at the desk was helpful for directions, transportation. The location was EXCELLENT. We walked everywhere and the Red line was right outside. The Navy Pier Trolley right up the street.
I would definitely stay here again and would recommend it.
Only drawbacks.....the hot tub was not filled the entire time we were theree and after a cold day would have been appreciated. Secondly, I would Not recommend the Webber Grill for breakfast...long lines at the buffet.

title: “Godd and Bad”
text: The rooms were huge, location excellent, beds comfortable, and bathroom amenities wonderful. However, we found the staff unpleasant. The desk clerk when we checked in was friendly, kind and welcoming. However, everyone else we encountered in the hotel over the weekend (with the exception of the doormen) were all pretty sullen and grumpy. Breakfast was sparse and low quality.

title: “Nicer than normal Sheraton”
text:
This was a decent Sheraton. Not the absolute best I've stayed at but one of the nicer ones.
The only thing I didn't like is that we were in a handicap room. Why not love it? The bathroom was huge but didn't have any counter space. I ended up moving the tray that the shampoo was on, the tissue box, etc off of the area by the sink just so I had space to use my bathroom stuff. The bathroom itself was huge, but I'm guessing that the reason it was so empty was because it had to be accessible. The door that opened out into the hallway was strange too. Only room in the hallway that had that type of door.
Parking was convenient enough. There were these weird gates though that made me think that after the construction that appears to be going on you might need to pay to park??
I did like the location. Elevators were quick & available. Staff was nice. No real objections. I'd stay there again.

title: “Will visit again soon.”
text:
My son and I stayed for four nights and this is one of the best hotels we have ever stayed in. One little scheduling glitch was handled by the front desk in such a professional and courteous manner that it was as if there was no problem at all. Rooms were beautifully furnished, clean and well maintained. Serivce staff was courteous and helpful. Location is ideal for transportation and shopping as well as dining. Traveling alone just the two of us we felt safe in this hotel and in this area, even at night. Metro station is steps away from the hotel.
Nice touch: Hot chocolate with your morning wakeup is a wonderful way to start your day, especially with kids.
Looking forward to our next stay.

title: “Disappointing... watch out for incidentals!”
text:
I stayed at the Westin Downtown over the weekend. I picked the hotel because of my Starwood loyalty, and because Westin is usually a nice place to stay. 
I can't say that the hotel itself had any glaring problems, but overall I was disappointed. The location is good, with many things to do within walking distance. The staff was helpful and friendly too. Our room was clean and everything worked just fine. And, of course, the Westin bed was very comfortable. But, I was very surprised to find that many of the things you expect at Westin were just not there. For example, they have no concienrge lounge, no gift shop/news stand and the restaurant is only open until 11:00 am. Yes, there's a Palm restaurant downstairs, but it's not open until dinner. You are "on your own" for lunch, which I found strange for a full service, downtown hotel. I'll also admt that I was not too happy to have to walk two blocks in the rain to get to a 7-Eleven for bascis that a hotel gift show would offer in most hotels.
Also concerning is the incidental costs at this property. For example, overnight parking is $28 per night. I thought it seemed high when we arrived, but assumed this was the typical cost of parking in downtown Denver. Not so, the Chase bank garage (right across the street) is only $19 per day. Why would a hotel be more than an office building? Then, after checking out, I found that minibar charges had been added to my bill. (We never even opened the mini bar.) I have contacted the hotel to get this refunded, but if you were not paying careful attention, the hotel would have just added charges to your bill after you left. 
For me, even as a loyal Starwood guest, my choice for downtown Denver hotel would be the Hyatt. It's appears to be brand new and is in a very good location. The Westin has just enough shortcomings to knock it off of my list when staying in Denver.

title: “Outstanding property”
text: This is a georgous property with outstanding service, food service and the pool/waterslides were so much fun.

title: “This hotel is being upgraded. Good thing, that.”
text:
Somewhat distressingly, I was in an upgraded room. Much of the furniture is old, there is an obvious mildew issue, and you're close enough to the airport to have trouble sleeping (and I am a sound sleeper) due to the RUMBLE from the airplanes. Parking is cheap but you have to pay, it's behind a fence with a lot of other hotels.
The good note is that the staff is friendly, nice, effective, and, well, quite good. They were the high point of this hotel, to say the least.
The hotel restaurant is barely there, but there are several other hotel-captive restaurants across the parking lot, and although I didn't use any, I suspect they would be acceptable. I'm giving this one a thumbs down, that may change after the full renovation is finished.
Great staff, though.

title: “Very very nice stay”
text:
Stayed over Feb. 5-8, 2007 ... very cold outside, very nice inside. The staff at this hotel was awesome, even though they were freezing inside the lobby due to a water line break.
The hotel is located two short blocks east of the Michigan Mile, near a post office, restaurants, and public transportation on Ontario Street. The king room we had was immaculately clean, one of the cleanest we have ever stayed in. The morning breakfast was very good, with waffles, breakfast sandwiches, hot oatmeal, cereal, etc. If you leave hungry, it's your fault. Then entire staff was very personable, cheerful, and went out of their way to please us and other guests.
It's about an $8.00 cab ride from the hotel to Union Station, and we were right on the bus lines we needed to go to the various attractions, like Navy Pier and the museums. We highly recommend getting a CTA visitor pass and map, and it's not hard to travel in Chicago. All in all, we will return again and stay at this hotel.

title: “Avoid the Rooms Next to the Elevators”
text:
This was one of those nightmares. While the hotel seemed decent and was recommended by the locals, everything was a disappointment.
Upon check in, it was explained to me that they only put reservations from the service I used into rooms with two beds. No exceptions. I couldn't even pay for an upgrade.
Once in the room, the big surprise was revealed. The room was directly behind the elevators. And you could clearly hear the elevator cars each time they passed. This was not a minor sound, it was like a cart slowly rolling by each time. To make matters worse, I could clearly hear anyone in the elevator lobby having a conversation. It's like there is no soundproofing at all in these rooms. When I requested to move to another room, I was told that there were none available -- which I suspect was related to me using a discount service to book the room (the hotel did not seem that busy.)
There are signs throughout the hotel reminding guests to keep noise to a minimum in the evening. I guess that's because this place is too cheap to soundproof and insulate the rooms. The short story is this: I got virtually no sleep in a room that cost me good money.
The constant noise, unhelpful staff and lack of sleep really put me off of this property. Maybe they will step up their game when the new Hilton opens later in 2012. In the meantime, I cannot recommend this property. If you have to book here, absolutely demand (and keep a record) that you NOT be put in a room by the elevators.

title: “Elegant”
text: Just a short stay but memorable for the spacious, comfortable rooms, handy town car within a three mile radius and helpful staff. Lovely.

title: “Wonderful Boutique Hotel in Heart of DC”
text:
Excellent service from the moment you enter the doors. The greeters and the front desk were efficient and super friendly. They know you by name during our 3 day stay. Kid friendly. Staff was always making sure the kids were taken care of. And they would give them high-fives. My 3 year old son loved the attention!
The hotel is about 2 blocks from White House. When I made the reservation, they said it was across the street from the White House, but it wasn't so. 
Hotel is clean. Great L'Occitane amenities. Shampoo, Conditioner, Body Lotion, Qtips, Cotton pads, Nail Files, Shower Caps. Free coffee & tea in the morning downstairs. Bathroom was nice & open. Marble, standup glass shower, tub, 1 sink vanity. Beds were super comfortable. Bose alarm radio was nice. Reminds me of home.
They even gave the kids a plate of cookies & milk our second night. That was a great touch!
We ate at the Hotel restaurant Ici and the food was wonderful. Staff was great & attentive. Could have been slightly faster service. Entrees about $27, dessert about $10. Try the guava mousse & lichi ice cream dessert. Wow!
While we were at the hotel, we visited the White House, Toured the Capital Building, Walked the Mall to see the Washington Monument, Lincoln Memorial, Reflection Pool, World War II memorial, Air & Space Museum, The National Zoo.
Go to Founding Farmers Restaurant for breakfast. Delicious! About 1/2 mile walk. 
Don't go to AuBon Pain on G and 13th street. Super small and not a great selection.
Parking at hotel is about $46 per night. In & out valet privileges. Wish the pull up area to the hotel was larger. Seemed it was only convenient for 2 cars at a time.
Wish they would add strollers to borrow at the concierge desk as they have at the Peninsula hotels. 
Would highly recommend.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
Nice hotel on Lexington Avenue, we had no problems in getting around. Rooms are a reasonable size and very clean, we used to have breakfast in the restaurant attached to the hotel which was convenient, but if you venture out down Lexington Avenue you find some nice diners that serve big American breakfasts. 
Would stay here again.

title: “dont stay here”
text:
Regardless what rate you can get, do not stay at this dirty and rude hotel.
Front office and concierge staff very rude.
Room was dirty, bathroom floor was wet from prev guest, and white bed cover had long black hairs all over it. If had been one hair could deal with it but i mean at least a dozen hairs on bed which would lead you to think room was not that clean. When called recept to have complain and have bed remade up was advised that change of staff shift time, and so had to wait two hours for the room to be re done. Amazing when a 24 hour airport hotel.
when room re cleaned no phone call or apology from any member of staff.
Bathroom was dirty and a sewerage smell.
the only thing this prop had going for it was the comp shuttle to LAX, other than that avoid it, crowne plaza and sheraton up road look nice as a suggestion.

title: “Excellent!”
text: I was so thrilled at the location of the hotel and the prices. The rooms were super clean, and the check-in was extremely quick, took about 5 seconds it seemed. This is where I'll be booking any future trips to San Antonio.

title: “It's not all that bad!”
text:
I stayed here with my boyfriend to celebrate my 21st from 26th Jan - 30th Jan 2005. It was much better than expected after reading some of the reviews, afterall we only paid £330 each so i wasnt expecting the Hilton.
It's in a fab location, i have no complaints about the hotel. Obviously as with everyone else the coffee machine didn't work (but i don't like coffee ;-) so i wasn't bothered, plus there's a starbucks on every corner) etc etc, but it really isn't that bad a hotel! I've stayed in a lot worse, and the location more than makes up for it.
The bed was comfy, the shower (after having to get the caretaker to show us how it worked) was ok, the radiator worked (too well sometimes!), the TV was mainly news...but i wasnt in New York to watch TV, i was there to see the sights and do lots of shopping! If you're thinking about booking this hotel and you're on a budget, go ahead! If you have more money to spend, perhaps look for somewhere else, but i'd probably stay here again because of the location and the price. After all you get what you pay for. I hope this helps, and it doesn't put anyone off! Thanks for reading! x

title: “Very pleasant stay”
text:
Room accomodations clean and great for price
Near airport, restaurants, right off of I-35
staff pleasant and courteous
Would recommend to anyone

title: “EXCELLENT...AS USUAL!”
text:
This is my 4th time staying at this hotel. I like it because it's away from the hustle and bustle so driving there by car is stress free. I have never had a complaint about anything, planning on returning for Black Friday. My ONLY complaint actually is the $55.00/day for parking. 
Looking forward to my next visit!

title: “loved this hotel!”
text:
My boyfriend and I went to Lollapalooza in 2008 and stayed at the Omni for 5 days. It was perfect! The location was amazing, especially when you take into consideration the free trolleys that run in the summer. Heads up: there are tons of tourists in this part of Chicago, mostly drawn to the shopping at the Magnificent Mile, so the trolleys can fill up rather quickly. But they take you pretty much anywhere you want to go. We took it to Grant Park in the mornings and walked back each night when the concerts were over. There are also tons of great restaurants within walking distance of the Omni.
The staff were great, and they were always helpful. Our room was immaculately cleaned, and the bed super comfortable. It was expensive, but I think it was well worth what we spent to stay there.

title: “Nice”
text: The Warwick NY Hotel was fine. Clean, no bed bugs, friendly staff, and best of all, great location. Not their fault that the no honking ordinance is TOTALLY ignored in this city! We were up early every day due to street noise. Taxi drivers are generally insane. Our 7-night stay went smoothly. My very minor complaints are: the lack of a full-length mirror, (and mirrors in general), in our room, and that the lobby bar always closed relatively early. Isn't this the city that never sleeps? No big deal. Our mini-bar tab probably made them very happy! :)

title: “Great place”
text: I would go back in the future. There was nice staff and very helpful. Very friendly.

title: “Execellent every visit!”
text: The Adolphus is one place I know I will always be treated well, have wonderful accommodations, and a fun and friendly environment. I love this hotel!

title: “There are better options”
text: I stayed at the Radisson the week before,the Marriott a couple of years ago (and was satisfied) but partner booked this place for 40 dollars more so I was expecting more. The look of this hotel is minimalist not plush.Lots of pilots staying there. The room was noisy as it faced the runway!! I needed a certain store but the concierge sent us on a wild goose chase to Manhattan Beach.On top of it he denied it.I reported it to the manager and he was great.There are better optionsfor the money.

title: “Beautiful & Convenient Hotel”
text: The Fitzpatrick Grand Central did everything it needed to do for us. It gave us a place to sleep and call home for the weekend. It's conveniently located across from Grand Central where we always come in on the train from CT. It's beautiful, though tiny rooms -- but it's a very nice hotel with very nice staff. We use this hotel whenever making a trip into the city. The prices have gone up quite a bit, but if we have the extra money lying around, we are there! Love it here. I recommend it to anyone looking for convenience and a comfortable place to stay.

title: “SCARY PLACE”
text:
I stayed at the Zaza for work from Dec 2-5th. this place is likea haunted castle- its old and musty and even feels dirty.
I was given a handicapped room- which i didnt want or request- then moved to a suite- there were pictures of naked women on the walls (they were literally ripped out of magazines) and there was a glass shower in the middle of the room and in the bathroom, just a tub. the room service is gross and the business center has a broken printer.. the lobby looks a abandoned motel with a srtung up mannequin display.. so strange. i have no idea what the concept is- wont stay here again.

title: “Super accomodations and value for the price!”
text: Henry (property manager) and his staff's hospitality and friendliness gave me a good initial feeling when I was looking for a San Fernando Valley hotel for my monthly business trips. I was extremely pleased with the room accomodations, especially for the rate. One of the best values in the SF Valley, bar none. The rooms are very clean and spacious. Bed and pillows provide a guaranteed restful night. The only thing I personally would like to see improvement on is a bigger toilet. Just a little on the small size...seems trivial, but for big guys like me (6' 235lbs) it is a bit "tight' on the throne, if you know what I mean (grin). Otherwise, I look forward to my business trips to the SF Valley because of the Ramada-Canoga Park!

title: “Warm caring staff, super location, comfortable rooms”
text: I don't usually write reviews but I wanted to share what a great experience I had at the Hotel Mela in July 2010. As a solo women traveler, I especially appreciate a place that feel welcoming and warm where the staff treat you like family.
