They went out of their way to be helpful, courteous and efficient... from the front lobby and bell assistants, to the desk help, to housekeeping, they all made me feel right at home. And when you spend alot of time in your room due to work requirements it's nice to have a home-away-from-home feeling. The location can't be beat for ease of getting around and accessibility to everything. You are close enough to be in the thick of things in either direction but once you are in the hotel it's a little oasis from the craziness of NY that can surround you. And finally, the building isn't new but the rooms feel really comfortable because they've taken care to keep everything contemporary and as up to date as they can.... so you get quaintness combined with comfort.

title: “The only good thing is the location”
text: I've stayed in this Hotel several times and the only reason i came back there was the price, but after my last visit i'm not going to come back. Each floor has several rooms which are close to the elevator,If you are coming to this hotel make sure that you do not get a room near the elevator. After a long day in New York you will probably want to sleep well and in these room you won't be able to do that because of the noise of all the people using the elevator, I stayed in these room for one night and after a really horrible night i asked from the guy at the reception to change it. Anothe thing that really bad about the hotel is the fact that they have 3 elevators for 600 rooms, and at the morning it takes forever to get a free elevator, on our last day we were waiting over 25 minutes to the elevator and we had 3 suitecases so we couldnt use the stairs. there was a taxi waiting for us at the lobby and my boyfriend had to take the bags 8 floors so we will make it to the airport on time. So we left the city very nervous, and that's why we will never go back there, This is one of my favorite cities, and it's no fun to leave the city feeling like this.

title: “Great Central Boutique Hotel with Breakfast!!!”
text:
This was a great hotel to stay in for a 3 day shopping trip. It was so central we could walk to Macy's, Daffy's, and all the other great shops. It was down the road from the port authority bus terminal and so handy to catch the bus to Woodbury common (another great shopping experience!).
The rooms were very small but comfortable and clean but additional storage available at reception if required. 
The staff were very professional and friendly with any queries we had. It was great to get breakfast each morning before we set off. It was continental breakfast, which was sufficient - juice, crossants, bagels, jam & cheese, tea/coffee. 
We had dinner one night at the hotel which again was perfect. This Hotel is just off Times Square and it was lovely to be able to wander around the streets at night soaking up the atmosphere.
We intend returning to New York later in the year and will stay there again and would certainly recommend it. 
Josephine Keane
Ireland

title: “Hilton Back Bay recommended”
text: We stayed at the Back Bay in January 2006. I travelled with my wife and 18 month old son Charlie. It was the first time we had been on a flight with him, and were a little concerned about him getting bored/ suitable food availibility etc at the hotel. We needn't have worried. Although there was nothing actually for children to do at the hotel, childrens meals were availible, and our room was so big and airy that Charlie managed to amuse himself with a few of his toys in there and had plenty of room to play. All the staff were so friendly, and couldn't do enough to make our stay enjoyable and easy, from the minute we arrived to the moment we left. We all also enjoyed the (newly refurbished) pool area, and although this is clearly designed for adults, Charlie was made welcome by staff and other guests. The hotel is situated in a great area, a short walk down the best shopping roads to the city centre, or slightly further down the much more scienic riverside. Overall, I'd rate this Hotel as excellent. Its not particularly child-designed,but certainly has all the basics you need for your stay with the little-ones. Probably better suited to adult only visits, but certainly don't discount it if you're travelling with kids. Recommended.

title: “Great Place for a Great Price”
text:
I traveled to LA for a business trip in June. I stayed at this Americas Best Value Inn for 4 nights. The room was clean and the staff was courteous. There were no frills - no tub, only a shower; had to get the TV remote from the front desk; there was no High Speed Internet Access. 
The parking lot was well lit and I felt safe at this hotel. The management was very helpful - recommending restaurants, driving tours, etc. 
I recommend this hotel for a value minded traveler. I would stay there again.

title: “Staying at the Comfort Inn & Suites hotel in San Antonio”
text:
This is a good hotel for a short stay. It is not too close to the Riverwalk or other downtown attractions but you will save money by staying here. 
It is a bit difficult to get to the hotel if you ar not used to driving on the highways but if you get lost, ask any gas station or any other hotel and they all seem to know Vance Jackson road. 
The check in was prompt for us , though I'd recommend they add a second person in the afternoon, as one check in person was swamped when several people came all at once to check in later on.
The room was clean and averagely comfortable. One night, there was a sort of bad scent in the hallway but it never got into the room. The beds are fine. 
There is a IHOP right next to the hotel and a Wal-aArt behind it. 
Free parking ! 
i would recommend this hotel as it is quite decent and the staff are polite and nice and there is free parking. Not downtown but that was okay for us.

title: “All business, no pleasure”
text: Not the hotel for anyone on vacation. Impossible to find, even with Mapquest directions and the hotel on the cell phone. While the lobby is large and modern, giving the appearance of a first class hotel, we found inconsistencies everywhere: old, dirty carpeting and walls; dirty bathroom, rooms that were not even cleaned daily, dirty, worn furniture in the pub, a broken refrigerator in the room (this should be requested in advance anyway;) ac that didn't always work; no docking station for music; old T.V.; a pool that closes at 9:30pm; a daily charge for wi-fi (who does this anymore?!) Most disappointing was the location...while we thought right behind the National Mall would prove convenient, there is nothing around the hotel. We were trapped into eating only at the hotel, unless we wanted to take the subway to the more enjoyable areas. On a positive note, the staff were all pleasant and the bed was very comfortable. This hotel is definitely for the business traveler on a budget.

title: “Ideal weekend family getaway”
text: Great family vacation spot. Lazy river, playground, outdoor movies and s'mores. My only complaint is that they try and get money wherever they can. Even charge for kids shows. Watch the fees as they try to sneak them in on you. Also the beach needed more sand.

title: “Great airport hotel”
text: Super hotel in great location. Can walk to easily from terminal without going outside. Super quiet and comfortable rooms. We woke up a little late after coming in on a redeye and were going to be closed out of breakfast, but the manager Brian took care of us and made sure we could still eat. And the quality of the food was excellent. We enjoyed lemon griddle cakes and a delicious vegetable frittata. A no-brainer choice for an easy stay near the airport!

title: “Great location and decor. Clientele, eh...”
text: The Roosevelt is conveniently located right on Hollywood Boulevard which means you can actually do some sightseeing on foot. A rarity of course in LA. The hotel gives you a taste of old hollywood and the staff are very courteous. The rooms are small but comfortable. Only gripe is the very loud AC.

title: “Great hotel at a great price!”
text: I've always had good experiences at Hampton Inns and this one was no different. The staff was extremely friendly (Christina Marie gave me some wonderful local restaurant suggestions), the breakfast buffett was great, the pool was nice, the rooms were clean and the beds were super comfortable! i liked the fact that the hotel was only about 15 minutes away from the airport (and it had a shuttle which picked me up to take me to the airport at 4am - impressive!) The hotel was also only a 15 minute drive to downtown Austin. Perfect! The only ONE negative is that I stayed in a room on the non-smoking wing of the 2nd floor, but as soon as I walked out of my room, I could smell the smoke lingering down from the other end of the hall. That was definitely a negative, but not enough for me to give the hotel any bad ratings.

title: “Owners Need to Reinvest in Cleaning and Updating!!”
text:
The TV, AC and breakfast were the only redeeming qualities of this hotel. The room wasn't as clean as I'm used to (aka, the bathtub was dirty, the carpet needs to be replaced, and the linens need to be replaced.). Also, the service from most of the employees was disappointing - excluding the servers/waitresses and one lady at the front desk. The business center is completely UNRELIABLE and the computers take at least three minnutes to upload even one page of the internet. The computers and internet (business center AND room) are too slow need to be upgraded to match today's need for reliable computer and to conduct business.
The only areas that seemed to boom with business are the "Comedy Zone" and the restaurant where you eat the breakfast buffet. But the "Comedy Zone" is adults only comedy when I was staying there with my family, which was not good considering you could hear the crude jokes throughout the lobby/restaurant area. I cannot speak for the conference rooms, but I sincerely hope the rooms are nice areas.
I sorely wanted to give a great review for such a great breakfast, but I cannot lie about how I found the hotel lacking in important qualities such as cleanliness and reliable WIFI/computer usage. The rooms are also connected, I think for bigger parties, but its not safe-feeling when the folks on the other side are trying to figure out how to open the locked door in their room.
Some more good thoughts: great location, next to I-295 and shopping and restaurants.

title: “Old and New - Avoid the "Tower"”
text:
I have previously stayed across the street in the newer part of the hotel and the rooms were pretty good. This time, I was put in the "Tower" on the other side of the street. The room was the smallest I have seen in quite a while. The heat did not work, no matter how high I turned up the thermostat. I was told by colleagues who stayed on the other side of the hall that their rooms were oppressively hot and could not be cooled off. While taking a shower, the water temperature varied annoyingly.
While attending a conference, we were given an internet code to access wi-fi in the meeting rooms. Many of us kept getting a message stating that the access for our group was full with other users. Again, extremely annoying.
On the positive side, the banquet food was above average.
There are several other better full service hotel options in downtown Denver. I recommend trying one of those.

title: “Pet Lovers Dream”
text: Loved this hotel first and foremost because I could bring my 4 legged baby with me. The staff were all very friendly and there are many "extras" at the Hotel Allegro, such as chocolates brought to your room as a thank you for staying and a complimentary wine hour each evening. Also, if your 4 legged baby has an accident, the staff is so nice and understanding. I was so embarassed but was assured by the doorman that he would take care of it. The rooms are large compared to other hotels in chicago that i have stayed at but the bathrooms could use some of that extra room. We had a great time and will definitely return. Only complaint, I would love an extra mirror above the desk, especially since i was traveling with my sister and there was not enough room for the both of us in the bathroom at the same time. Other than that, it is a fabulous hotel in a wonderful location.

title: “Our favorite hotel in Memphis”
text: We stay at the Madison every time we're in Memphis, which is quite often since we have a daughter attending college there. The rooms are lovely and the hotel is 5 Star in our books. The staff is friendly, knowledgeable and always ready to help. An added bonus is Grill 83 - the food is always amazing! We don't stay anywhere else when we're in Memphis.

title: “great hotel right in the heart of Chicago”
text: This is a great place to stay if you are visiting Chicago. It may not look like much from the outside but its clean and fairly modern. The breakfast was great, lots of variety to choose from not just pastries and coffee and internet access was included. The beds and pillows were ultra comfortable and the room I had was very quiet!! Can't wait to go back.

title: “Nice Business Hotel”
text: Hotel has recently been renovated, stayed on business in anticipation of Hurricane Sandy. Hotel is split into 2 towers, my elevator bank was on far side of entrance. Queen room was small as expected, but extremely clean, bed is comfortable, modern light switches and plenty of outlets. Bath was huge with working window. Even had a decent view of Manhattan. Free WSJ in lobby next morning. I will stay here again.

title: “The Rex is Inspiring!”
text: I recently had the opportunity to stay at the Rex while on business in the "City by the Bay". The Hotel has what can be described as a majestic old home "Library" theme that encourages a guest to curl up with a good book. I kept imagining myself wrapped up in a old fashioned bath robe with a glass of cognac in one hand and my favorite book in the other. The rooms, which are also decorated with a similar theme, are small, but given the hotel's central location within the city close to the Union Square, the Financial District and Chinatown, it simply made the hotel seem all the more cozy. Keep in mind that the hotel is in downtown San Francisco, so parking is typically by valet. You can try to "self park" on the street, but take advantage of the valet which makes you feel like a VIP without the cost! There is a small restaurant within the hotel which has great food, however, there are about 1,000 other restaurants within walking distance to the hotel. If your planning a visit to San Francisco, you owe it to yourself to stay at this hotel or another belonging to the same holding company "Joie de Vivre" (Joy of Life).

title: “Great Historic Hotel”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel twice now and have had great experiences both times. The staff has always been extremely helpful and friendly and on my first visit, I was upgraded to a junior suite, which gave a bit more room in a city where hotel rooms are typically quite small. 
The hotel is just really nice overall and has a very grand feel both in and outside of the rooms. It's very conveniently located, right next to a metro stop and about two blocks from another. Cabs are always available outside, so getting around the city is always a breeze.

title: “Horribly noisy”
text: Stayed there one night and could not go to sleep! They put me next to the service elevator room 2128... They should not rent this room, worse noise than NYC traffic all night! They sent up a tech. After complaining and he said "oh well" you can't help machinery noise. Thank god used price line,,,,,this hotel is a 1/2 star!

title: “Good hotel only if paying $70 or less”
text:
I had reviewed TripAdvisor prior to a weekend trip. San Antonio hotels can still be pricey in August even with a 2-week advance purchase. Arranged a stay at BestWestern for it's 2-week advance price that I was comfortable with. This hotel is not a super quick drive to downtown attractions, you may hit traffic as well. But, for my party, we were very content with the drive. This hotel seems close enough to a waterpark in the area. No restaurants were close, but a quick drive down a few exits provided some commonly known restaurants. 
The room was perfectly chilled the way I like it, the A/C was fabulous- I love it when hotel rooms let me choose my temperature--- I prefer 64-67. The rooms are supposed to be smoke-free, but my party could smell that a smoker had visited- it wasn't heavy, but noticeable. Room was small, decent Queen beds were clean with small fluffy pillows. Table & chairs included. Older TV in room, good reception. Split bathroom, sink countertop tiny. Tiny toilet/tub area. Plenty of towels & washclothes & handtowels. Toilets seemed really low. Maids were quick to tidy the room & refreshen our towel stock. 
Breakfast was Texas waffles-only one waffle maker made for long lines around 9 a.m. Cereal & Juices well stocked. Hot biscuits and watery gravy were available. Nice to watch TV while eating. Small breakfast dining area. Friendly evening & day staff worked the lobby. 
Pool was a nice rectangular, depth of 5 feet, entrances on all 4 corners of pool. Crystal clear, tidy, and made for decent lap swimming. Parking was limited, but an open dirt area was used by trucks & cars alike. Trees lined the parking lot though, and so your car could stay cool in the shade--very nice Perk while in Texas. Ice & Vending machines are well-placed. 
Overall a good hotel for a decent price, I'd price the place at $70, anymore than that I would be uncomfortable. I gave extra in ratings primarily for the fabulous A/C in our room--my sleep & value ratings reflect this.

title: “Expected More, Got Less”
text: The best thing that this Hyatt has going for it is its location. It is located within walking distance of many popular DC attractions, such as the National Archives, the Newseum, and other Smithsonian sights, as well as China Town and the Verizon Center. There is also internal access to the DC Metrorail system via Metro Center station. The reason this hotel did not get a higher rating was the room: not enough power outlets to charge all of the electronic devices we traveled with, poor lighting, noisy location, with a great deal of construction taking place on H Street. Perhaps a higher rating when the construction project concludes.

title: “Simply the best!”
text:
Just back from a wonderful visit to Chicago. Could not fault the Residence Inn in any way, the staff, the room, housekeeping, breakfast, evening meal/drinks reception (Mon-Thur) are all excellent, as is the Hotel's location for access to Clarke/Lake - blue line to O'Hare Airport and also for the sights. Incredibly easy to get around the city on foot from this fantastic hotel. Theater Land and the Magnificent Mile are only a very short distance away. 
The hotel was in great condition and very clean and tidy. The bed was also very comfortable and the air conditioning worked well. 
My wife and I were over in Chicago to celebrate my wife's birthday and we were very kindly given a free upgrade to a corner suite that had a lovely view of the city. We were also allowed to check out late as our flight back to Dublin was not until 7:15pm. 
A fantastic experience from start to finish and I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is visiting Chicago. We hope to be back in Chicago some time and we will be staying right here in the Residence Inn Downtown/River North. 
The gym is a real bonus and has a good view over the city.

title: “Loved it- Great Service”
text: Stayed over Easter weekend and despite other reviews reporting paper thin walls, I didn't notice it, even though we were by the elevator. Very comfortable and wonderful wonderful service!! We had fish delivered from the market place to take home and when it arrived they took it right to the freezer--not that it NEEDED it, but they certainly were taking care of us. Didn't like the television on the side of the room, but I'm not sure how they could reconfigure the rooms since it is a round hotel!! Would definitely stay there again!!

title: “Surprisingly good for airport hotel”
text: Stayed here for 1 night cuz the conference hotel was too expensive the first night. Pleasantly surprised - free shuttle from airport that arrived in a flash. Unfortunately they didn't have my reservtion but that was because Expedia messed it up. But room was excellent, clean, really good size suite and bathroom, nice big desk for working. Bedbug check was negative. I also arrived late and ended up ordering room service. Excellent seafood scampi pasta - big tasty shrimp, scallops, and clams with plenty of fresh parsley and a good deep sauce. The food came quickly and was still piping hot. The next morning I took a chance on the breakfast buffet (included in price) - plenty of options, excellent omelette bar, hot coffee, waffle wedges with strawberry topping, all very nice. Needed a few more people to clean off tables or where people had stacked dirty dishes though. But overall excellent value. If I were to stay in Boston for a vacation or something I would use this hotel as my base of operations. It's not right downtown but easy access to T and airport and plenty of space, cheaper than being right in town generally.

title: “A Gem of a Hotel in Venice!”
text:
Hotel Erwin is a wonderful find in Venice! It is close to the boardwalk, the restaurants (Mao's Kitchen is great!), and only a few minutes away from LAX. it is a nice relief from the airport hotels. It is a boutique hotel, an old building beautifully done up. The driveway is short and the lobby is very small, but the staff are very nice. The elevator is tiny but the surprise of the hotel are the beautiful rooms all done in contemporary boutique style, and most, if not all, have ocean view! The rooms are spacious and have beautiful art, one has a giant clock made of sneakers! Even though it is close to the beach, it can get quiet inside the rooms.
The rooftop is where the action is, you get a view of the city, the beach and boardwalk, and on a clear day, downtown LA. On beautiful sunny days it is just magical, esp when you watch the sunset while you sip cocktails. Sometimes it can get too cold or windy, and the staff readily hands out blankets.
Or, you can simply walk down to the beach and catch all the action with the shopping, street performers, muscle beach show offs and medical marijuana hawkers. Venice beach is quintessential Southern California, and Hotel Erwin is right in the heart of it!

title: “Great service”
text:
This was my second stay (and review) on Elan Hotel, this time, I've ordered some products only and have requested it to be delivered at the hotel. All my packages except one got delivered. The hotel staff and manager went out of their way to sort out what had happened (the shipping company delivered elsewhere) and helped to locate the package.
The hotel is at a great location, with several dining options and a shopping mall a block away.
The rooms are very clean and have a good size. The internet/wifi had a fast connection.
This is my hotel of choice whenever I'm going to stay in LAX.

title: “An oasis”
text:
I had a 7 hours layover in DFW and we were travelling with our 18 month son... After the 9 1/2 hours international flight, this was like a mirage. Since we arrived at 6 AM and our flight was leaving at 1 PM we were given a special rate.
The rooms was ample and had very comfortable beds. Everything was sparkling. The bathroom one of the best I have seen in any hotel and had both a shower and a tub (which allowed us to give a relaxing bath to our baby). Loved the way you can open the shades! That allowed our kid to be entertained by watching the planes taking off (through the almost soundproof window).
When it was time for checkout, the front desk gave us passes so we can go through security faster (using the First Class and Crew lines).
I can't recommend this hotel enough. Whoever manages this place should be given a promotion!

title: “Nice place”
text:
Picked this hotel out of a lineup of potential hotels when I booked a package with Southwest Airlines. I took the family to AZ for spring training. It was a short drive to the Brewers and White Sox/Dodgers facilities. I am not really sure of the price, as it was in the package, but based on comparable hotels, it was probably pretty good.
Room was nice, but a little on the smallish size I thought. I had a King, and I could tell by the layout of the exterior, my room was a couple feet shorter than other rooms. I did have a loveseat/hideaway bed, which was nice to have.
Free wireless internet, which was nice. I hate having to pay for that. The breakfast is NOT free. They have cook to order and continental, but even the con. is 6 bucks. A little pricey for what it was I thought.
If you see a picture of the pool on their website--it looks big, and it is. Much larger than a typical hotel pool. Hardly anybody was ever in it. The hotel obviously caters to the business traveler, who probably isn't a big swimmer. My kids loved it, and the hot tub was nice and big too.
Staff was very friendly. Never really used them that much, but always hellos when going by the front desk, and if I did ask anything, they were always nice-no surly attitudes. Had a better than average fitness center too.
It was close to the freeways, easy to get to, and had a couple shopping centers close if you needed to pick anything up.
I would recommend, my only surprise was the charge for breakfast, which seemed a little on the high side for what it was. Otherwise a pleasant, clean, safe, convenient place.

title: “Excellent location”
text:
The orchid garden hotel was really good. Though pricey the rooms were well kept and neat. The location of the hotel was quite close to the union square and the BART station.( though i never did take the BART). The ferry terminal is walking distance and is a must see, especially the farmers market on Saturday. The rooms are a little small, but since i never really stayed long in the room, it was fine. And before i forget to mention, Chinatown is right next door ( literally). The restaurant inside the hotel was pricey, ad i never cared to eat there.
I did have some trouble with the hotel though. The rooms were all overbooked, and when we arrived late at night, they transferred us to the Orchid Hotel nearby for one night( a sister hotel). I wasn't too pleased about this and hope the management looks into this issue. Not the way to treat customers who arrive late at night only to find that they have been moved to another hotel. 
But overall a good hotel and i would recommend it.

title: “Clean hotel with art deco style”
text:
I booked this for 5 nights because I was looking for a reasonably-priced hotel in the village area that hadn't had any reports about bed bugs. Previously we've chosen to stay in midtown hotels but were looking for something a bit more relaxed and I was so glad that I found this hotel. 
Washington Square itself is a lovely park/public area with dog-walkers, guys playing chess, joggers, birds, squirrels, pushchairs, low key musicians. Walking through it was a very pleasant way to begin and end the day.
Hotel staff were friendly and helpful throughout. Decor was generally very good and had a bit of quirky character in the hallways. Our room was small (but I've stayed in smaller), and the view from our window was uninspiring (but I was prepared for that after deciding to book their most budget-friendly room). However the room was spotlessly clean and the bedsheets were crisp, white and good quality. I'm slightly embarrassed to admit that I'd brought a torch to look for bed bugs but after a close inspection I was reassured that the beds were clean everywhere. Despite paying a purse-friendly price for our room there were lots of amenities to make a stay more pleasant: bathrobes, hairdryer, bathroom toiletries, a great coffee maker, ipod alarm clock. Minor niggles were that I could only see one free electrical socket (2 people with a phone each need 2 sockets) and there was only a small supply of coffee/milk for 2 people. There wasn't a fridge but there was an ice bucket and ice available.
The continental breakfast (bagels, croissants, cereals, fruit, yoghurt, juice, coffee, tea) was a bonus as was the free wi-fi. We didn't take our laptops but used my iphone to look up local directions to restaurants, subways, stores and cinemas and so found the wi-fi a lot more useful than expected.
The hotel really added to the enjoyment of our holiday.

title: “PLEASE do not stay here. Car was vandalized!!!!”
text:
Please do not stay at this hotel! We booked three nights at this place because of the low low price hotels.com was able to get for us. Well, booking this hotel was the biggest mistake ever! We have an infant and all three of us were kept up half the night due to kids running and screaming up and down the halls of the 4th floor. When we called the front desk THREE TIMES, they promised to take care of it. We stood in the hall and waited for them to come and they never did even though we were assured that it was taken care of. 
We checked out the morning of July 4th and found that someone had smashed out the entire back windshield of our SUV and stole a cooler no less! The hotel manager was somewhat nice and had one of his maintenance employees tape up the hatch with plastic wrap and vaccuum out the glass that was EVERYWHERE! (I had to ask him to help us with this though - i guess he figured that we would know where to get ourselves some tape, plastic and a vacuum cleaner as out of staters from VA (rolleyes) However, the hotel manager did try to claim that the glass might have imploded due to excessive heat. It was unseasonably cool there, so to make an assumption like that was pretty silly. Plus, we found later on that our cooler had been stolen. We called the police, but they didn't do anything and the hotel manager assured us that he would review the video surveillance that was pointed directly at our SUV, but we haven't heard anything back. 
NO MATTER what kind of deal you get for this place, please please please do not stay here especially if you have children!! IT IS NOT SAFE!!!!!!

title: “I love this place and have stayed there anytime I come to Charlotte”
text: Everything is perfect at this hotel. Great rooms, location and customer service.

title: “reasonably priced accommodation in phoenix, arizona”
text: reasonable price: 50 dollars per night for 2 people with 2 queen beds. good comfort. good access to I10 east for tuscon or mexican border. recommended to us by the locals.

title: “A Good Stay”
text: This hotel has a good location if a little complicated to get to the actual hotel. Getting to the room requires using two different sets of elevators and some "winding about." The hotel does have some remarkable views of the Chicago skyline that would be a good reason to stay here. Other than that the hotel is just a typical Holiday Inn in a major city.

title: “Close to the waterfront”
text: My wife and I arrived at 11:00 AM due to early morning flights. The person at the front desk was able to find a room that was ready. She was very pleasant and provided us with a map of San Diego and recommended restaurants and places to visit. The hotel is definitely not new but the room was very clean and modern in appearance. Coffee maker, microwave, and fridge included. Sliding glass doors opened onto a large balcony but no chairs or table. ( a bit of a dissapointment) Continental breakfast is provided - a very nice touch was coffee, tea, and hot chocolate, fresh baked cookies, and bowls of apples in the lobby. The swimming pool is small but clean and refreshing. Lots of free parking is available. The location of this hotel is close to the water so if you are into boats, seafood, and enjoy walking this place is great. Restaurants, stores, and liquor stores are all within walking distance.

title: “Troubled stay”
text:
When checking in, I noticed the lobby was extremely warm. I guessed that the public area air conditioning was not working and was worried that the room would also be warm. The check-in staff was friendly and efficient even though they had to be warm in their suits. I do wish they had said something about the obvious air conditioning problem.
The room (710) was well appointend and comfortable (initially). I did have to call housekeeping because there was only one cup with the coffee maker, one robe (needed two) and lipstick on one of the bar glasses. Response was quick.
Returning after a show on Friday, I found the room to be warm. At around 11 pm I called the front desk about the lack of cool air and was told that they were working on air conditioning for the whole hotel. Around midnight, I called again because the room had become uncomfortably warm. This time a new person on the phone said they'd send maintenance up. Maitenance arrived quickly and found that the AC wasn't working properly even after a reset. (The first phone call was obviously mistaken because the hotel's air conditioning is apparently separate from the AC units in each room.). At about 12:30 am they moved us to a new room (1107). Room 1107 was acceptable but I was disappointed that I lost a bathtub, an armoire and a night stand on my side of the bed in the move. Even though I had to change rooms in the middle of the night, no one ever apologized. AC in room 1107 worked flawlessly.
Apparently we weren't the only ones with problems. When I was in the elevator with clothes on hangers, I encountered a couple who said their sister was in her third room since checking in. I've rarely had to change rooms due to mechanical problems, but other times the hotel offered an apology along with something else (wine, fruit basket, upgrade to a better room, discount, etc.). Some sort of apology would have been appreciated.
Just so you know, the door on 1107 doesn't close completely unless you give it a good push/pull.
Small issue, but the services listing in the room said newspapers were available on the 2nd floor. I went to the 2nd floor on the first morning, didn't find any newspapers, but did find them in the lobby on the first floor.
Video check-out didn't work. The buttons on the remote didn't always match the on-screen requests when using the menus (was there an "A" button somewhere?)
Now, on to the good things! Here's what I really liked:
- The staff was uniformly friendly and efficient (even though they had to be warm!).
- The rooms were very well appointed with quality items. The furnishings, bathroom fixtures, and electronics felt high-end.
Very comfortable bed and bedding.
- The lighting in the room was very versatile and accommodated all of my needs.
- That coffee maker was amazing. I thought I did something wrong because my first cup of tea came out so quickly. I am a tea drinker and my friend is a coffee drinker. The machine made really good beverages for both of us without cross-contamination. (Tea often tastes like coffee in hotel rooms!) Thanks also for having good green tea available.
- Housekeeping was fast - I never did see a housekeeper. The cleanliness was very good (except for the comment above).
- Although the elevators were small, they did not make me wait too long.
- The hotel provided the Times on Sunday. Bravo! (I don't mind picking up the paper in the lobby.)
- H2O products were excellent. 
- Providing Internet access without an extra charge was great (and all hotels should do this)
- Wonderful channel lineup on the TV (yeah, BBC America!)
- I was surprised at how quiet the room was. Hard to believe I was in midtown Manhattan.
My one regret - I had hoped to peek at a smaller room but never had the chance. The King Deluxe was wonderful but I don't know how I'd like a Standard Queen room.
Not a bad stay, but I was really disappointed at the hotel's lack of response at the time of the problems and when I emailed the problems to the manager after the stay.

title: “Location Location Location”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Chancellor for three nights in March 2004. 
The location of this hotel could not have been better for us, we put the hire car to bed and walked all over the city. The cable car stop was just right outside the front door (walk down to the truntable or you will never get on). The room was a little bit small but the walk in wardrobe helped with hiding the luggage. Breakfast was included in our deal and it got us of to a good start. Would I stay at the Chancellor again, yes I would.

title: “Old lady in dire need of makeover”
text: Hotel is old and tired, rooms have wallpaper peeling off walls and years of grime. I arrived late at night, hiked upstairs only to discover I had been given a smoking room. Why do these still exist? I dragged everything back downstairs where initially the surly front desk clerk told me there were no other rooms. Well lo and behold upon my insistence there was indeed another room. Understand the hotel is renovating floor by floor; this can't happen soon enough. If we're going to pay through the nose to stay in Manhattan it should at least look like they're trying.

title: “Prescott: Practically Perfect!”
text:
The Prescott Hotel was perfect for us. Two blocks from Union Square, on Post between Taylor and Mason.
We stayed on Club Level, room 434 (two double beds), for $299 per night.
Club Level amenities included a very nice continental breakfast available every morning from 6am to 10am (cold cereals (choice of 4), hot beverages, delicious juices, fruit, pastries, breads and bagels, toasters for self service, etc. You could have that in the nice lounge, or bring it back to your room. In the afternoon there was an open bar with a bartender, cheese and crackers, and fine quality pizza from the Postrio restaurant next door (a Wolfgang Puck enterprise.)
Our room wasn't shabby,but there were a few minor signs of wear and tear, and a bellman mentioned that the hotel's rooms are being renovated bit by bit, though all were renovated in 2004, and so looked spiffier to me than the last time I'd stayed there, years before. Our room wasn't large, but it was comfortable, with plenty of space to walk around and to keep two large suitcases open. The bathroom again wasn't large, but it was functional, attractive, and immaculate. L'Occitane toiletries, great towels and bed linens. Almost all services were prompt, efficient, and helpful. One of the concierges forgot to get back to me on a dinner reservation, but I followed up on my own and no harm done. I highly recommend this hotel, and would stay there again. Given S.F. hotel prices, I think this one is a bargain.

title: “Great location to stay in NYC!”
text: For our (me and my spouse) first trip to US we decided to start with NYC. After a long research on the "right" hotel for our trip we found this hotel at an appropriate price; and our finding was the best I can imagine. The hotel is very nice. Also the location is outstanding as I can say as tourist. Nice restaurants around; travel around NYC is very easy because subway stations at 79th St is very close. Also with express trains you can use 72th St. station. We had a Superiour Suite which for me was a bit tight. However, super bathroom and a really nice roof garden. The staff is very, very friendly and helpful. I can really recommend this hotel and would book it myself again.

title: “Cool New Property, Snobby Staff and Security”
text:
The Gansevoort is a really beautiful new building in a cool area of town, and it's really great that they took advantage of their rooftop space for breakfast and for a small pool area. The rooms are nice; with all the mod amenities. The hotel is only mediocre overall though. It's unfortunate because with its location, pool, rooftop and rooms it could be great.
However, the major issues are twofold: (i.) service mentality and (ii.) construction quality. 
Towards the first point, the hotel is a little too cool for its own good. There is a line to get in the door at night and every time you walk in someone will accost you and demand impolitely if you are a guest. Then, security at the pool will rudely instruct you that you are not authorized to use the pool because the check-in agent didn't record the correct number of people staying in the room (2). It's not that any of this is awful; its just that no one in the hotel was half polite. The security manager was particularly self-important; declaring "I am not being rude; I am the manager" when I explained that I was feeling a little unwanted in my own home away from home.
Secondly, it seems that while the room is nice it was painted very quickly without any attention to detail. The closet doors did not close (they were too big for the frame) and the tub and tiles in the shower were cracked during installation. It's almost as if they realized they won't need ot be around for very long; they just need to be cool long enough to make their cut.
Overall, I would rather spend $600 / night somewhere where I could be treated nicely; although the pool is a nice touch. If the property wants to be successful in the long-term, though, it needs to develop an entirely different guest service mentality and also realize that one space may not be compatible with use as a nightclub, lounge, restaurant, pool, breakfast area, and deck. The roof is special: they should realize that and preserve it's quality instead of herding club-goers up there to make a buck off martinis.

title: “friendly staff and great service”
text: i was very comfortable with the hotel room and their service is very friendly, clean rooms. restaurants and shopping mall is near.

title: “Wow, Wow, Wow!!!!!”
text: You have to stay at this hotel! Especially if you are visiting the American Girl Doll store. I just returned from a weekend getaway at the Park Hyatt March 18th-20th. We stayed in their standard room, and let me tell you there was nothing standard about it. Everything was top of the line. Top shelf bottled water and fresh fruit awaited us upon arrival, the room was immaculate, flat screen t.v.'s with free movies in the bedroom and the bathroom. The bathroom was like having our own personal spa. Complimentary sea salts,loofah, and scented candles were just the beginning. We were worried about the room because we usually stay in a suite, but we booked last minute and this was all they had available. I was so suprised, and pleased! The room had huge windows with window seats over looking Michigan Ave. They even had a present from the doll store for each of my daughters sitting on the window seat when we arrived, and specialty cookies and milk for them before bedtime, all complimentary!!! We left in the evening to go to dinner and when we returned they had 2 doll beds awaiting my little girl's dolls and slippers and robes set out for us. The beds were heaven. I have stayed in some of the nicest hotels in Chicago and their beds cannot compare. I could go on for days on how great our stay was! Strange for me because I am very picky about where we stay. If you're big on service come here, it's the best service I have ever received in Chicago. The breakfast at Nomi was very good. I've been to the Ritz, Drake, and Peninsula, and the Park Hyatt has been my most memorable experience!

title: “Nice stay in SD”
text: Very nice to visit warm, sunny San Diego. The Hacienda Old Town was a great place to stay. The price was reasonable, staff pleasant and helpful with a wine and cheese reception one evening and outstanding cookies and coffee seemingly available all the time. The king suite seemed a little cramped, especially the bathroom, but the bed was great.

title: “I felt like I was pampered!”
text: I loved staying at this hotel! I would definitely stay here again! I can't go on many vacations because I am on a ventilator and have a lot of medical equipment. I also do not get first class treatment very often. So I felt like I was treated like royalty! They staff accommodated all our needs when we called and helped us load and unload all my stuff from the cart. Whenever I neded the lift to get down the stairs or the doors opened, they always noticed me and helped me because I can't use my hands. I liked the intimacy of the place. Because it was not too big, the staff could get to know you. One guy asked me if the route he gave me to a destination was wheelchair friendly. I liked his comment after that when he said he asked so he could help other disabled people because he knew I experienced things he normally would not notice. He also noticed when my friend, mom and I wanted to take a picture. The staff also helped with finding the most suitable accessible room for me when we were planning our trip. The head of house cleaning saw me in the hall and even told me to call her if I needed anything. The bathroom was very accessible with a roll-in shower and ample room. They even have a spacious room for happy hour!

title: “One Night Here Was Enough, Especially at that Price”
text:
I moved to this hotel for the last night of my work stay as prices at the W skyrocketed. It has a decent enough location, but i think I'll opt for one of the other Starwood's in the future. 
I arrived around 9:30pm, apparently right after a tour bus had dropped off an entire load of people and when I asked if they have a starwood preferred counter, the said no. They had 2 people checking people in and it took about 20 minutes until I was helped.
I had had my wallet stolen on a previous flight so my husband had called with his credit card and asked them to charge that. Well that turned out to be a disaster and took multiple phone calls, including to my credit card company (the hotel said it wasn't going through) to get everything straightened out but finally it was.
The room is not what i am used to at other Starwood. The bed was comfortable enough, but bedding is not as high quality. The bathroom especially lacks and the room itself is much smaller than other starwoods. I'm Platinum at starwood and I don't think there are room upgrades at Four Points. Also, often breakfast is included at sheraton's, but it wasn't here.
It was a complete joke that the price was close to $300. You could really tell a difference between the staff here versus at other Starwoods. The level of service and professionalism just isn't there. I would say this is a fine option, but only if you get a much better deal than I got.

title: “Excellent Location...”
text: Family and I took the train down from LA to SD and then walked 5 minutes to the hotel. Was a nice walk. We stayed on the 8th floor and had a nice view. The greyhound station was outside our window we could head buses leaving all night. That was the only downside. The service was great, room was very nice, we walked to the mall. Overall a 9 out of 10.

title: “Nov 2012”
text: Several guests checking in at the same time, so it took longer than I would have liked. In the past stays at this BW, I believe it's had 3 fruits...this stay it only had apples and oranges...was missing bananas. I requested for a room in the back of the property, but was given a room in the front of the property facing Clairemont Mesa Blvd.

title: “Never never never”
text: make sure that they don't have celebrities or else you would be scored through the hotel as If you are a criminal--- aggressive and uncomfortably rude. Had the worse experience ever-- during dinner we were ok at the nine thirty room--but next day we wanted to be by the pool and were asked during lunch to put our cameras away because of some teen idol or something. when I got up to go to the bathroom a manager asked me and my 5 year old daughter to leave the area and that we were not welcomed there just because my 5 year old took the other side of the pool on the way back and I guessed the celebrity was there. I couldn't believe their horrible attitude and demeanor I have never been treated that way. Good thing that was our last day --- and for sure will never go back again

title: “Convienent location.”
text: We picked this hotel via Expedia due to its cost and location. The hotel staff were very friendly and quick to offer any assistance that we needed. Though the room was small on the small end, it was clean and comfortable

title: “Great service-great value-wish it could have lasted longer!”
text: From the bellhop to desk clerk to housekeeping everyone that we came in contact with at this hotel was fabulous! We didn't ask for anything that seemed to be a problem for these folks. Room wasn't tiny like I had expected from the previous reviews nor was the place worn. I thought the rooms were perfect and the hotel was just fine in all respects. It is a little hike from the metro but for the value and service that is a small price to pay. We also mostly used cabs when we traveled. We did walk to Dupont circle once for dinner and we walked to the metro and the trip wasn't bad at all. We would definitely stay in this hotel again. We did not dine in the hotel restaurant.

title: “Good hotel, great location”
text:
Hotel was in a fantastic location in the south of Boston within easy walking distance of both Copley Square and downtown Boston.
The room was a reasonable size and clean. 
They were also fantastic at offering a late check out - 2pm on a Friday afternoon - much appreciated.
Only negative comment is that the windows do not give much sound insultation and as the hotel is above a bar and on a busy bus route you should come prepared with ear plugs.
By the way, you can get a great breakfast at the coffee shop around the corner.
Would definitely stay there again.

title: “really good hotel”
text: We have just returned from a week's stay at the Salisbury and we found it to be a really good hotel in a prime location. Our room was quite big - two double beds and two huge closets. The staff was helpful and eager to assist us with any queries we had. The main good points are the size of the room, the quietness of the hotel and the quality of the housekeeping. We feel we got value for money and we would definitely stay there again.

title: “Hotel Palomar how do I love thee, let me count the ways...”
text:
We just returned from a trip thru Dallas, and stayed for the first time at the Hotel Palomar and must say that it was the HIGHLIGHT of our trip!!!
Although we did not have our puppy with us, we plan on returning and bringing her along next time. In the meantime, we can now bring her to dinner with us at the local Kimpton property here in Scottsdale, Arizona. Coincidentally, we recently attended a wedding at the FireSky Resort in Scottsdale and never realized this was the very same chain of Kimpton properties.
So back to our love affair with the Palomar, here are just a few of the many reasons why we loved staying here:
1) Nightly welcome reception with complimentary drinks and appetizers. (during our stay they served a refreshing white sangria, chardonnay and a great red wine with the most delicious deviled eggs with shrimp)
2) Super friendly staff who cannot do enough for you!
3) the ULTIMATE BENCHMARK in pet friendly hotel properties, we loved meeting some of the interesting guests along with their well behaved pets during the cocktail reception. WARNING: If you don't have a dog, you'll want one after staying here!
4) Plush towels ~ in fact I would say that their towels should win an award for best hotel towel in America.
5) Comfy bathrobes
6) Bathroom Menu of various things one often forgets, so if you forgot to pack your toothbrush, etc., they offer everything at a super low price, (2.00 average) so not only are they super thoughtful, but the hotel is not trying to rip you off on these amenities. 
7) L'Occitane shampoo - conditioner - soaps - body lotion
8) Magnifying mirror
9) Adjustable gooseneck bedside reading lamps
10) the most comfortable sheets I have ever slept on~under~between
11) the most amazing mattress, we hated to get up to leave our room
12) Large Flat Screen television
13) On site spa and salon
14) FABULOUS restaurant - don't miss their dessert menu!!!
(shout out to our lovely server "Medley" who recommended the chocolate fudge waffle, with caramelized bananas and peanut butter ice cream. ~ WOW, I am still thinking of that dessert days later...LOVED IT.
15) Large rooms - you will have plenty of room to move around in their standard room, without paying for an upgrade. WHY DOESN'T EVERY HOTEL GIVE YOU ROOM IN YOUR ROOM??? They all need to take lessons from Kimpton.
16) Beautiful pool area and hot tub
17) Dog run with large grassy play area
18) SUPER QUIET hallways and rooms ~ NO PET SOUNDS or smells could be detected anywhere on the property, which is an amazing feat in itself. I guess all the dog guests are on their best behavior ~ they know how lucky they are! 
19) FREE WI-FI in your room 
20) Need I go on...?
This place is so wonderful, we cannot wait to return with our little dog Lucy.
And all these great amenities are at no extra charge, and they don't even charge a pet fee.
We have stayed in various hotels where there is always a pet fee, usually 30.00+ per night, and you must have your dog with you at all times. Here if you want to go out, they will even watch your pet for you, walk your pet, etc...UNBELIEVABLE SERVICE with a smile. 
We paid a low nightly room rate, but I won't mention the rate in this review...as no matter what you end up paying, it is well worth ANY price to stay here!!! 
PS) they even have a website dedicated to their fabulous amenities, it seems I am not the only one who wanted to purchase the bed linens. check out: KimptonStyle . com
By the way, you might read this review and think I am associated in some way with this hotel chain, I assure you I am NOT. My husband and I were just so thrilled to discover this hotel on Trip Advisor (THANK YOU, Trip Advisor!) that I wanted to write an indepth review so that everyone can "experience the experience" before they step foot into the 
hotel.
Jovan & Bill Millico
Scottsdale, Arizona

title: “Great Room, Below Average Staff”
text: I stayed at The Rittenhouse Hotel on June 29th for 1 evening. I had extremely high hopes for this hotel & some of it was met. First of all, when I arrived, there was no doorman to open the door for me & when I did see one, he never spoke to me-this wasn't a big deal, but for a 5 diamond propert, I just expected the door to be held open for me. When I went to check-in, my room was not ready, which I assumed, due to the fact that it was 9 in the morning. However, Michelle, Mary, & Timothy at the Front Desk were not apologetic & never smiled & were not really friendly-I mean, they weren't rude, just not up-beat, polite or friendly in that 5 star hotel way--no better than checking in at a Sheraton, but I don't expect that special touch at a Sheraton. When I called down to get a room change with a sofa, Mary hung up once I said "thank you" & when I went to check out, I asked Timothy a question & he kind of mumbled--un called for & unacceptable. He also screwed my bill up, but it was fixed. The concierge, Susan & Frank were decent. When I asked to get an umbrella, Frank said there was one in my room, but I hadn't even checked in yet...& when he loaned me one he asked me to be sure to bring it back...I don't know...I'm in the Hotel business in New York, so I pick uo on alot of things, so maybe I'm just being picky, but I expect the best when I'm paying alot of money. Susan also gave me incorrect directions to a bakery. One of the bellman was horrible, and met me on the 5th flr for a room change....he was at the end of the hall and yelled, I'm over here....he should have been waiting at the elevator for me, and for that matter, should have came down to my room and escorted me there---what a joke! I did sort of raise my voice at him, but I expected more. However, my Deluxe room was fantastic---Huge, great bathroom, an amazing bed, great park view, etc....Room Service staff were excellent and very polite. Amanda was a pleasure to speak with over the phone in Room Service. The other bellman I encountered was great as well, and very nice. The overall feel of the hotel is very residential, and the rooms have that same feel as well. The room was amazing---very understated, with traditional decor. Housekeping was excellent--again, very friendly! Great location as well, near lots of upscale shops and dining. The park is nice, as well. Overall, I was very impressed with the rooms, just very let down by the service--they should be ashamed, except room service and housekeeping. Would I stay again--for the room, yes, but knowing the service was nothing special! Oh well---live & learn!!!!!

title: “Great hotel and excellent location for tourist”
text: First trip to Chicago as tourists. Found the location perfect and the staff was great. Will stay here again.

title: “A Home Away from Home”
text: Austin's Super 8 Motel had a free snack and water bottle waiting for us when we arrived. On the bed was a teddy bear with the pillow bar info tied to its neck. I sampled a few pillows during my stay. We had a computer in our room (and I know there aren't computers in every room... possibly we got one due to staying for over a week) with internet access, and free internet for our i-phones etc. The bed was super comfy, and we slept well. The windows allowed for almost total light block out which was great. The breakfast in the morning was more than just buns and fruit, and included these and waffles, eggs, bacon, and much more. The staff was very friendly. We will stay here again!

title: “Great customer service!”
text: Justin Lope and Genaro Alfonso were a GREAT help to me!! Awesome people!

title: “Very Accommodating!”
text: We stayed here for a weekend event. Even though we live in Indy, wanted to make a fun weekend of everything! I was very impressed by this hotel. The lobby is amazing. It's very elegant and unique, due to the fact the building is an historic landmark. The rooms were quite nice and modern. The beds can be adjusted, though they are very confusing to use, and I didn't notice any difference in settings, but they were quite comfortable all the same. I requested a late checkout, and was offered 2pm! This was amazing to me, as 1pm is typically the cut off. I typically stay in Marriott properties, but this Hilton will be high on my list if I plan to stay in downtown Indianapolis again!

title: “this is the place to stay when in Dallas”
text: I was looking for a hotel that had a free shuttle to Love Field and this is the one I chose. The hotel was CLEAN, the staff was FRIENDLY, the room was spotless, the bed was sooo comfortable. This is the hotel I plan on staying at if and when I ever return to the Dallas area. The only thing I will suggest is a more friendly shuttle driver!

title: “Beautiful place to stay.”
text: We had 2 young children with us and everyone at the hotel was very accommodating and helpful. It has a classic hotel feel with clean, modern finishes. We would definitely stay here again and recommend to friends. We had a friend getting married across the street at the Merchant Exchange building and the location was perfect. Valet is also great, we were able to take our care in and out without extra charge and they were fast! Awesome stay overall.

title: “A great place”
text: We, 3 women, spent 2 nights here during Fleet Week (just a coincidence). We had reserved a 2 bedroom but were upgraded to a 3 bedroom, which was ab-fab, as we each had our own bedroom and bathroom. Room and common areas were great, as was the staff. We ordinarily would not stay near Fisherman's Wharf, but this hotel offered us what we looked for--a living space and at least 2 bedrooms. Only difficulty was getting from the hotel to our show on Sunday early evening due to the incredible traffic caused by Fleet Week. We were originally told the house car was not available and there wasn't a cab to be had. Finally, one of the staff took pity on us, got the house car and delivered us only slightly late. Everything else was top-notch.

title: “Shoebox with a great location”
text:
For around $200 per night The Milford has some positives, excellent location behind times square, broadway theatres & close to numerous subway lines and for a hotel with 28 floors the elevators are surprisingly efficient.
 It also has many drawbacks. In 2012 it is criminal to charge $15 per day for wireless Internet as the majority of travellers now rely on the internet when travelling. The newly "renovated" rooms are not much more than a single coat of paint and a poster on the wall at the head of the bed & the rooms are tiny. A queen room at the Milford is comparable in size to a single room at any budget yha hostel.

title: “LOVED OUR STAY!”
text: A very nice looking hotel that was clean and comfortable. The lounge and milk & cookie bar were very nice to. 5 STAR Hotel.

title: “Location, location, location.”
text: The staff was incredible. Michael J, Svetlana, Daniel, Wendy et al.were great. I love the cookies. Easy check-in, check-out.

title: “Lovely Experience”
text: I thought the Mayfair New York was the quaintest little hotel. We found it very late on a saturday night when no one else had available rooms. The man at the front desk was very accomodating. He let the three of us stay in a single room, and even went so far as to get us an extra futon mattress. Since it was so late (around 4am on sunday morning), he checked us in as sunday morning so we wouldn't have to check out until monday at noon (thereby getting two nights for the price of one). Our room was very small, but it was clean and comfortable. We had plenty of clean sheets, extra blankets and pillows, cable tv, air conditioning, and a clean bathroom with a fairly large shower. We slept in on sunday and no one bothered us, it was very quiet, and the curtains were very effective at keeping the room dark. Our room was on the top floor, and there was a very sturdy fire escape right outside the window that allowed us to climb up one level to the roof and look out over 49th and Broadway (shh don't tell). Overall, I would definitely recommend this hotel. It was very affordable as well, our room was $90 + tax for the night.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
Located close to the airport with a free shuttle service that runs on demand (from airport) and on the half-hour (to airport) this is a nice place to stay if you don't mind being in an industrial area. If you have a car there's no problem in getting around and finding places to eat. If, like me, you're limited to the hotel restaurant that's no problem either.
The restaurant has moderately priced menu and the food is definitely better than most hotel fare.
This hotel is well kept and a good buy. I'd recommend it to a friend in a heartbeat.

title: “Was A 5*.... Is Now A 3* (Hope they turn it around soon)”
text:
Have visited before (last time was Sept. 2006) and loved the hotel @ that time.
This time?
Room is aging, wasn't as clean as it should be. Room service just so-so. Worst of all is that the staff is not as friendly and helpful. There were a couple minor technical problems but those can happen anywhere and aren't worth mentioning.
I hope improvements are made, as this property is in a terrific location and deserves to be top-notch.

title: “Great Hotel for the money.”
text: Stayed here for 4 days in 2010 for. Great Room. Parking a little expensive though. Central to everything airport, Downtown LA. Would Defintately stay here again....

title: “"Just as Good as The First Time!"”
text: Stayed at this perfectly located, clean, friendly boutique hotel in 2010 and now in November, 2012. Just completed my recent stay while attending my conference at McCormick. This place has the right amount "cool" -- a friendly and helpful staff (everywhere), orange infused water and hot chocolate at the front door, free newspapers, a computer kiosk area, and a decent gym. The bar is under the radar and the turn down service with a Primehouse treat is a nice touch. I could always count on housekeeping for a clean room et al. Nice little touches such as filtered water at the bedside were cool, too. The beds are some of the most comfortable I have ever slept on for a hotel. Oh yeah, if our buddy with the Audi Q7 is available, you can request a ride to somewhere within reason. Bottom line: The James Chicago has a certain "cool factor", and for the $$$, it is well worth the price of admission at Rush & Ontario. We did have our nightly conference rate which I thought was very fair for the Magnificent Mile area. No question, I'll be back in 3 years!

title: “Loved it”
text: My first trip to DC & I did not have a clue where stay. I found this gem on a discount web site and decided to take a chance, Im glad I did! Beautiful hotel in a a great location. Restaurants, transportation and a even a 24 hr drug store across the way! The neighborhood is hip & all the businesses were filled with locals. Hotel bar has a great Happy Hour! We enjoyed our stay and definitely will stay again!

title: “Love the Sofitel Lafayette-Top Notch Staff”
text: Beautifully decorated and comfortable rooms even though ours was on the small side, with a large and luxurious bathroom. The entire staff was professional, warm and courteous especially the concierge staff. Every one I came in contact with was a pleasure to deal with. Outstanding breakfast in the restaurant and a lovely bar for afternoon cocktails. How refreshing to stay in a hotel where service is the number one priority.

title: “Mixed review”
text:
While reviewing another hotel I came across this Hampton we stayed at last summer and thought I'd give my two cents worth. 
I booked our room 2 days before our stay on the phone directly with the front desk. We were meeting friends in town for some downtown nightlife/restaurants and stayed one night. 
Pros: Beautiful hotel. Gorgeous room and ultra comfortable bed w/ down linens. Huge bathroom and very clean. Great location for walking downtown to a variety of upscale dining and shopping. 
Cons: Upon arrival they had no record of our reservation despite a confirmation number and the name of who took our reservation. Last-minute room not located anywhere near our friends. HAVE to pay valet parking in a parking garage attached to hotel. Didn't sleep a wink due to hallway noise - evidently a drunk crowd was also staying on our floor and attending a wedding reception. Our room was on the second or third floor, not near where the festivites were, but evidently where alot of the guests were staying. Called twice to front desk to control noise, once at 2:00AM and again at 4:00AM. 
Needless to say, Hampton's policy is that if your not 100%satisfied you stay free, and we stayed free. They had record of both our calls and that our orginal room was canceled so the front desk guy pleasantly and without question refunded our money. 
I would stay there again despite the problems and unruly crowd. Beautiful hotel in a prime location for walking to fabulous restaurants. However, be prepared for panhandlers in the evening hours if your walking back.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: Very clean, no bed bugs, and a very helpful staff!!

title: “Great choice - the only place we'll consider next time...”
text: We stayed at the Independent for two nights with our 6 month old - couldn't be happier with it. Great location, great staff, great rooms - we didn't notice the street noise like some other reviews stated. A basic continental breakfast is delivered to your door at the time of your choice. It was nice to be greeted by name upon arrival and each time we passed the desk. Staff was super helpful with every request, from directions to restaurant suggestions, a pack n' play for DD, booking the taxi back to the airport - each little detail was CHEERFULLY taken care of. Our room was really nice, decor was fresh and slightly eclectic, super comfortable and roomy. The only negative I noted was the bathroom lighting -could have been a little brighter. DH pointed out that there are neither security chains nor peepholes in the guest rooms. I didn't feel unsafe at all, especially since the staff seemed to know exactly who belonged in the building and what room they were, in, but I can see some people having an issue with this little detail.

title: “Thumbs up for the Milner”
text: Before going to Boston but after booking the Milner, I read the reviews of other people and felt sick to my stomach. I considered canceling my reservation but was too busy so decided to just go and was pleasantly surprised. Yes, my room was small, but very cute and cozy. The hotel had a very nice atmosphere as well. If you've ever traveled in Europe and stayed in 2 - 3 star hotels, you'll know what I mean. No, it wasn't new and, being an older hotel, the oldest in Boston apparently, not everything was in perfect condition, but I think you have to expect that. The manager was great and very receptive to my concerns. The staff were professional, friendly and helpful. As for the breakfast, also very nice, especially because of the fresh fruit. I don't mind eating with plastic utensils. I thought my stay at the Milner was very good. I slept well, was very centrally located, and was treated well by the staff. I would stay there again.

title: “super location”
text:
We stayed at Belleclaire from March15th until March 21st. It was excellent very clean and the staff were helpful and friendly.
 The neighbourhood is really lovely and safe. with lots of shops and restaurants.Manhatten Diner across the street very good for breakfast, sets you up for the day.
 Our beds were changed a couple of times over the few days and we had fresh towels every day. We had a blocked loo a couple of times but they were fixed in a matter of minutes.
Close to 2 subway stations with 79th street the closest.
We travelled with people who had been to New York before and had stayed in more central hotels but they loved this one. Do check out the neighbourhood it is lovely.

title: “A Little Gem!”
text: We were staying in LA last week for my son's spring break and decided to spend a couple of days in San Diego. After researching areas and hotels we chose the Gaslamp Quarter of the city for it's character and cost as compared to the more expensive hotels on the beach. I had read other reviews of the Solamar and while most were good, I was a bit concerned about the area. Boy was I surprised! What a fabulous location close to everything! The hotel is in great shape with very modern decorating and amenities. The rooms were all updated, clean & comfortable. We were on the 9th floor which I would recommend as it was a non-pet floor. The rooftop pool and bar were absolutely beautiful and I wish I'd had more time to spend there. We went to the hotel restaurant Jsix for breakfast and while they had a very limited menu and it was a bit expensive, the food was excellent. The hotel has a wine hour in their lobby from 5-6 with complimentary wine. We did this both nights we were there. What a nice way to start our evening! We met so many nice people from all over the world. The area was a bit touristy and the restaurants a bit spendy, but it's not anything we didn't expect. The "barkers" at the front doors of every restaurant were a bit obnoxious, but the food was delicious and the bars were fun. The hotel valet parking was expensive, but there are much cheaper options conveniently located within a block of the hotel &I didn't mind not parking on site. Overall our stay here at the Solamar was a wonderful experience that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for a great place to stay in San Diego.

title: “Hotel Edison - not during half term!!!”
text:
This was the second time we had stayed at the Edison, so we knew that the hotel was not the plushest around, but our previous stay had shown it to be clean and the staff friendly so opted to stay again.
Bit of a mixed experience this time. We again had one of the older rooms (despite asking for an upgrade - I was told none available with 2 beds!) but the room although dated (which at a casual glance, can make it look grubby) was extremely clean. 
However, the hot water seemed to run out by the late afternoon (although when I spoke to the reception, they said they would send someone up. no one came but the water got hot. Same happened next day - do they have a tank which they turn on when someone complains???) On our second day our room was not serviced. We had been out since 8.30 am and this was 6.30 pm. The desk was not very pleasant about it - almost implied that it was my fault somehow - but I stood firm and they cleaned it before we came back at 10.30 pm. It was however unusual for the staff to be so unfriendly. BUT the worst thing was the school parties - felt like every teenager in the UK was visiting during half term week The noise on the first night was unbelievable. The desk said they had 800 staying!! Because of this I would not stay during holiday periods again - it settled down after the first night, but was still noisy at times. 
The hotel couldn't be better situated however and feels safe. It has been perfectly clean on the two occasions we have stayed there.

title: “great location”
text: currently staying at the hotel. despite the few negative reviews, this is a very nice hotel! I asked for a complimentary upgrade but john (who checked us in 3/10) said he didnt know how and was afraid to, so we are spending an extra $10 a nite. so far, other than that, very nice!

title: “Superior hotel. Great service, great location, top notch all around.”
text: Fabulous, fabulous, fabulous. This hotel is a notch above the rest. The service is unbelievable. You need dinner reservations at a restaurant perfectly suited for your mood? No problem. Great theatre seats? Piece of cake. The staff is falling over themselves in an effort to make your stay more pleasant. The rooms are extremely nice. This hotel easily surpasses the average Westin, Intercontinental, etc. I can't recommend this hotel enough. You will love it.

title: “fantastic fitzpatrick”
text: We have just returned from a 4 day holiday in New York, and our holiday was made even more special with the stay at the Fitzpatrick. The room was outstanding, the people were so nice to us and the food in the Wheel tappers Bar was great. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in New York. The position is great because you are so near all the attractions.

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Location!”
text:
Lovely hotel, location is great if you go a certain direction. But the side of the hotel leads to a very undesirable part of the city that tourists should stay away from. When checking in, we wasn't advised of any places in the city we shouldn't stay away from, but clearly there are!! There's a lot of homeless that navigate around the hotel too. 
Had to pay to wifi, found it expensive.

title: “Wonderful from check in to check out”
text:
Returned yesterday (22 July 2010) travelled with my husband and 17 year old daughter. Arriving at the hotel mid afternoon, check in was smooth, efficient and the staff courtious. Got a room on the 11th floor with fab views of the Empire State Building and Macy's. The beds and pillows are the best every - just didn't get enough time in bed to enjoy them too much to do in NYC.
The breakfast in the morning was adequate and there was something there that you would like. Bit of hot food, buns, waffles etc. with hot and cold drinks. Get down there before 8.00 am to avoid the rush.
I cannot recommend this hotel enough. It is so close to everything. Spotlessly clean with very helpful staff.

title: “Consistantly great”
text:
I have stayed at the Bryant Park Hotel three times and have loved it every time. It is located, obviously, on Bryant Park - a great area in which to stay. It is close enough to Times Square to get to the theaters easily (without being in the middle of tourist central) and close to the subway.
The vibe is trendy without being intimidating and the service personable and attentive.
The decor is clean and comfortable (think Scandinavian) and I highly recommend upgrading to the queen deluxe room with a view. I was there on a lovely summer weekend with a balcony overlooking Bryant Park; it was a lovely place to have breakfast.
Highly recommended.

title: “Liked it Alot”
text: Recently stayed at the Manhattan Club. It was a timeshare exchange through RCI. Check in was quick at the Manhattan Club. We were assigned to an interior view 1 bedroom on the 24th floor. The room was clean and the facilities were in good shape, minus the elevators as others had mentioned. It was slow. It seemed to me the issue was that two out of the four lifts were reserved for the penthouse units/floors. Several times, we used the two freight elevators behind the lobby. The suite was kept nice and cool and noise wasn’t an issue. The 1 bedroom consists of a bedroom separated from the living area via a door. In addition to the one bath in the bedroom, there was a ¾ bath in the living room area. This was nice as there were 3 of us. There was a microwave, however no cooking stove top. There was a mini fridge in the room. It’s NYC anyways… Who cooks? Daily cleaning was provided and the housekeeping staff did an excellent job everyday. All the staff appeared cheerful and we experienced no problems. The were no spas or pools, however there was a good gym on the top floor. There were 3 flat panel TV’s along with all the necessary machines, including free weights to work off all the great meals to be had nearby. I slept on the sofa bed one night and that was enough for me. Did not feel comfortable, but was okay with my little one. Overall, liked it a lot. It was in a great location with the subway a block away. You couldn’t ask for a better location. Tip: at 55th Street and 9th Avenue, there is a laundromat where you can do some laundry if you have to. Also next door on 9th Avenue, there is a bike shop, Liberty Bicycles that rents bicycles for $6 an hour. Looking forward to coming back.

title: “Affordable luxury”
text: Excellent location, about a block from Michigan Ave. and two blocks from Water Tower Place and John Hancock Tower. Beautiful hotel, felt very luxurious and high-class for being a moderate priced hotel. Staff was excellent -- friendly and accommodating.

title: “like going home”
text: It is a nice hotel nothing fancy the staff is nice and it is close to shopping, super markets and many great places to eat.

title: “Best sleep ever!”
text:
Prior to arriving to Melrose, I visited over 4 hotels on a work trip in duration of a week. I must tell you, this hotel offers the most comfortable bed. I got a single room, with a king sized bed. The rooms are large, equipped with comfortable furniture, excellent room for luggage storage, providing all the hotel necessities.
I think the hotel staff at the front desk could be a bit friendlier, however they still helped me out with resolving many quesitons. Also, I am used to free wifi at least in the lobby of a hotel, but this one charges 10 dollars a day - so beware. 
I think the housekeeping and front desk should have better coordination with regards to services. The housekeeping woke me and my other colleagues up twice, even though I notified the front desk of a later checkout and there was a "privacy please" sign outside of the door. Overall, I enjoyed staying at this hotel just because the comfort of the room, including the bed means a lot for me :)

title: “Our family had a wonderful stay at the New York Palace!”
text: We recently returned home from our families first visit to New York City. We selected the New York Palace Hotel because of its location and we were not disappointed.
