The rooms were large and very clean. We stayed in a tower room overlooking the cathedral, which allowed us access to the concierge room. My husband and I enjoyed the foods and beverages very much, but the kids didn't appreciate it as much. Not their kinds of foods! My 8 year old daughter wanted to stay at this hotel because it was so close to the American Girl Doll store. On the day we went to visit the store my husband arranged with the concierge for a package from American Girl to be waiting for her in the room when we returned. She was thrilled to open it and find a bed for her doll as well as a small palace robe that matched the one in the room for her! That made the trip very special for her! We would definitely stay here again!

title: “The best hotel ever in DC”
text: We did our reservation last minute and I was surprise how gorgeous the hotel is. I still dream about the breakfast we had there every morning i wake up!. The staff are very friendly and always smily. The hotel is just two blocks from the white house, excellent location, nice lounge cross the street. It was really fun. C/in agent offer ed free early checkin. The room is new, I beleive the entire hotel was recently renovated. We Definitly will stay here every time we visit DC.

title: “Uber cool at an affordable price.”
text: Ace is as hip and cool as everyone writes. It is a very affordable New York hotel I was surprised at how friendly and nice the service was at the Ace. The lobby is like being inside of Christmas tree dripping with hip 20 and 30 somethings. The Breslin was great for dinner. Loved our cubby booth and the dark wood out of "Harry Potter" decor. Great service as well. The Ace was a nice surprise, exceeded my expectations for a reasonably priced New York hotel.

title: “Great place - close to everything”
text:
We spent one night at the Doubletree after spending 3 nights in Westmont traveling into town each day. Both have their pluses, one being the cheaper prices out of town! We thoroughly enjoyed being within walking distance of everything! We parked our car early in the a.m. at the garage and checked in later. The next a.m., we walked around a bit thinking we'd be charged by the hour since we were past our 24 hour limit and were happy to still be charged the set $41 price that came with our room. 
My son and I walked to Navy Pier that evening and I felt relatively safe walking back at night with just the two of us. Since it's a tourist area, you can always find someone to hang close behind. 
The rooftop pool was nice, on the 5th floor, but ran out of towels on a chiily evening. They were replaced shortly after we left. We paid extra for a lakeview room on the 23rd floor but could see very little of it with the other buildings blocking the view. 
Elevators were prompt and staff was very friendly and helpful.

title: “Good Location”
text:
We stayed here for a long weekend. It is a sheraton, so you get the standard large hotel service. Rooms were good, especially if you get one like ours looking down the river towards the downtown area. We simply asked for a good view when we checked in and the staff did a great job to oblige.
If you are in Chicago for a short time, it is the best location for shopping on "the miracle mile" , a quick walk across the river to the millenium park and a grant park and not too far away from navy pier. There is actually a free trolley run by the city council that runs a loop from State street, (where the closest subway station is that links with the downtown area), within a block of the hotel and Navy Pier. This therefore makes everything much closer, and is a good way to get around this end of town.
Overall good experience. Bed is interesting, mattresses are very soft and is hard to find your bed buddy!

title: “hype, not hip”
text:
Booked a high floor corner king with balcony. I don't know, maybe it's me, but floor twelve in a 20 story building isn't exactly "high floor" and there was no balcony. The included breakfast consisted of toast and coffee, served by snippy wait staff who were waiting to be discovered by DeNiro. Try to get back into the hotel after the club on the first floor opens and you'd better hope that a doorman recognizes you because the bouncer won't let you in.
The pictures on the website were terrific, unfortunately, the reality was in dire need of a reburbishment. The shoddy workmanship mentioned by previous reviewers shows. The interior decor isn't all that special (better stuff at Ikea). The neighborhood is definitely still iffy (it IS the Lower East Side) and every bit as grimey as expected. The proximity to clubs is nice, but that's about it.
It's very much like the Schrager hotels in that the emphasis on design precedes comfort and service. Stay here for the experience - once - and only if you get a decent rate as I did (under $400). However, for their standard rate of $650 per night, they have to do better. There are hipper hotels, in better locations, and with better service for what Rivington charges.

title: “Awesome!”
text: We stayed 3 nights at this beautiful resort. Our suite had a gorgeous view of the bay which we truly enjoyed. The location is fabulous with it's own beach or you can cross the street to Mission Bay. My girls loved the parrots!! The staff very extremely accomodating bringing us whatever it was that we needed. The front desk staff recommended a great restaurant on the beach (World Famous). The pool was large and fully enjoyed by the kids.

title: “Excellent, would definitely recommend”
text:
Really impressed with the hotel. For us noise wasn’t a problem. For one we were on the 29th floor so although we could hear car horns it wasn’t enough to keep us awake, and to be honest, I would expect that noise in any hotel in the area due to the volume of nearby traffic. There are only 12 rooms on each floor and they are situated around the lifts so you never really hear people walk past your room as there would only ever be 2 or 3 rooms who need to walk past.
The hotel is only 6 weeks old and as you’d expect this meant everything was super clean. Rooms were excellent – really spacious. For us the self catering kitchen facilities were wasted as we only used the kettle and fridge once, but I can see that they would be excellent for families or business travellers. Great view from the window – Rockefeller and 6th avenue ahead of us, Chrysler to the right and Conde Naste to the left.
Breakfast was good. The eating area is lovely – it is spread out over the 3rd floor which doubles as a lounge area in the day, so is nice and relaxed and you don’t feel on top of people when eating. Usual buffet food – cooked, organic cereals, bagels, sweet breads, fruit, waffle maker. Something that we loved was that the hotel had a 24 hour coffee machine available on the 3rd floor so we regularly stopped off here for a free take out coffee to either take with us or back to the hotel room at night.
Bar was unexciting. We went there for a few drinks on the 2nd evening cos we were still jet lagged but wanted to adjust to NY time so thought a drink here would be a way of staying up but not too full on! Bar attendant was lovely – really nice girl who we chatted with. Very quiet in there though, and they barred a guy (non resident) who was smoking in the billiards room. Can’t see many people using the bar as there are much better bars all around NY but nice for a night cap.
Agree that on occasions it took a few minutes for the lifts to arrive. Also I always seemed to get static electricity from them!
Vast majority of the staff were really helpful - directions to local shops, turning the apple juice machine on just so that we could get a late afternoon drink etc.
Would definitely stay here again when we’re next in NY. Central location is so handy for popping back quickly and an advantage of 6th avenue being busy is that it was always really easy to get cabs!

title: “Great hotel and very convenient”
text:
Don't know if I had better luck with this hotel as apposed to others but I really enjoyed my stay here. Check in was smooth and with no problems and we were on our way up to our room. I had 2 special requests and both were fullfilled (I had asked for upper floor with a quiter spot). We walked into our room and were amazed as to how clean it was. Very spotless from living room, bedroom, and bathroom. The balcony was a little dirty but really it is the inside that counts. The view of the pool from our room was nice as well it just added a little more to the room.
The bed was very comfortable. The pillows and bed were both so soft and molded to your body. The room was also very roomy which was very surprising to me because most rooms with a bedroom, the bedroom usually lacks in space.
Getting around the area was a breeze due to the trolly stopping almost right on the parking lot. Very convenient for anyone wanting to go downtown and the trip is at most 2-3 minutes. Arriving back we were always greated by the staff in front which was nice. The woman in the front desk was very helpful all weekend long, I forgot her name but she was awesome.
The lobby was very nice and the restaurant area was very clean. We did not eat there for breakfast. Breakfast is not complimentary which is a little dissapointing.
The parking lot has no security (wish it did) but all ran well so I have no complaints other then there were leaves everywhere which actually hid a few parking spots. Also parking is free which is hard to find in the downtown area. 
We did not go into the pool or jacuzzi do to the weather so I have no review on that.
Overall I thoroughly enjoyed my staff and would recommend it to anyone.

title: “Fab Location/Great Value”
text: Booked Four Points off Priceline -- we were surprised at the great location; close to 3 different train lines & NJ Path train; quick walk to Union Sq, Penn Station & Time Sq. My husband & I walked from a comedy club on W3rd Street after 1am - safe & comfortable walk. They have a really good happy hour and great restaurant. Best of all, Wholefoods is on the corner!! Yes, the room is small & quiet but who goes to NYC to stay in a room? The room was comfortable and perfect for sleep.

title: “a great week end at Chicago”
text:
I went there for Memorial weekend and booked at expedia. The price was very low for an Hotel closed to the loop. Arrive in late morning but was able to check in with no problem. Room was very clean . Swimming pool and excercise rooms are great . The view over chicago river and sears towers was fantastic . Expect a lot of kids everywhere.
Additionally it is very well situated, walking distance from the loop and the magnificent mile ( a good walk however, but no problem streets are friendly and taxis are easy to catch. Certainly an excellent choice for its price at week ends. Only minorl problem, Restaurant is very pricey. Breakfast is ok but it's over 13$ plus taxes. However, have a walk and you'll find plenty of other choices.
I will come back. Chicago is a great city and you must stay there several days if you want enough time to visit the great museums, walk around (it's a town for people who like walking) , have boat tours on the river and listen to jazz music.

title: “Average at best...”
text:
I stayed at the Warwick Hotel on 12/17-12/19. I had reserved a room with a King size bed, but upon arrival was told that I had been "upgraded" to a Deluxe room with a queen size bed. I believe the "upgrade" terminology was a lie as the room did not seem to have any extra amenities. I think the lie was a way of getting around the "King" bed request. The room was average at best with the bathroom being above average, but most other aspects average to slightly below average. The bed was terrible and the TV was tiny dating back to the late 1980's/early 1990's. I will admit that I can be a bit picky, but I will warn anyone thinking of staying at the Warwick that the beds are definitely not "comfortable." I was not in NY to watch TV or spend significant time in the room, which is why such inadequacies did not bother me, but a bed is important and in this case, the Warwick failed. 
The most positive attribute to the Warwick is its location. The hotel is situated close to everything which means you can walk, within 5-10 min, to 5th Ave., Central Park, Times Square, Rockefeller Center, etc. That fact, in itself, makes choosing the Warwick somewhat attractive. 
In conclusion, I would recommend the Warwick if you are not too concerned about your quality of sleep. I would also recommend the Warwick if location is important to you. However, I think there are many other hotels in NYC for the same price or slightly more that would provide a more luxurious and enjoyable experience... try any Westin hotel.

title: “Bad in every sense.”
text:
Our bathroom was NEVER clean, it usually smelled of urine. The filth, hairs and dirt behind the bathroom door were there when we arrived and stayed there when we left, a week later.
Breakfast had nothing to do with the colorful picture they have at the entrance.
Our TV didn't work properly and we had to watch pay movies with continuos interruptions of other channels (after alot of arguing, we managed not to get charged for them).
Internet never seemed to work correctly, we had to keep logging in or restarting our computer. As soon as our week was through we moved to another hotel in San Diego.

title: “Perfect location, high-class stay.”
text: Wonderful stay! Valets out front. Walk in to a large, elegant lobby with front desk. Booked it by walk-in and use of "reservation phone" in lobby. No problems and operator was friendly. Front desk staff were friendly and efficient, but busy lobby. Took elevators to room on the 18th floor (spacious for a single room in NYC!). Room was clean and hallway was quiet. Short 3 min. walk to Times Square! Maintenance man promptly fixed stuck door bolt. High-class hotel with professional hotel staff and proper facilities. Bathroom, towels, carpets, bed very clean. Definitely would stay here again and again!

title: “Great Service”
text: Took an eairlier flight than expected because of blizzard conditions expected out of Cleveland. Ended up with a 9 hour layover at Philadelphia. Since the Marriott was attached to the airport, asked about getting a room for the day. The cost of the room was very reasonable. Was able to spend the day swimming and napping as opposed to sitting in a crowded airport waiting for an overseas flight. The service and admenities were excellent. Was money very well spent!

title: “Chic, Relaxing NYC Hotel!”
text: I just got back from NYC. I've been to New York 3 times and have stayed at a variety of hotels in the city. The first time I went I stayed at the Sofitel. Great hotel, but nothing superb. The second time I went I stayed at the Ritz Carlton Central Park. I was not impressed. For being so expensive, I expected a better hotel. This time I went I stayed half the time in Hotel Iroquois and the other half in Hotel Giraffe. I loved this hotel! The staff was nice and helpful. I had a horrible experience at Hotel Iroquois so this hotel seemed like heaven. The lobby was a great place to come relax, have a drink, and chat. There were lots of seats/tables and the environment was nice. The rooms were gorgeous/roomy. Definitely get a suit overlooking Park Avenue. The color/decor was beautiful. The location is also wonderful! I personally prefer the lower part of Manhattan as opposed to uptown. The buildings are lower and it seems more like home. The location is perfect because wonderful restaurants are nearby in Greenwich. And of course, SoHo shopping isn't too far away. Overall I loved this hotel.

title: “Luxury Hoel with great location”
text: Our room at the Michelangelo was one of the largest hotel rooms that we've ever had and in New York, that's certainly a luxury. This is an elegant, well maintained hotel, centrally located and close to subway stops. We will look forward to staying here again!

title: “Quite nice, but beware the very slow wireless connection.”
text: Nice hotel, as others have written it's not luxurious but still quite nice given the price compared to other surrouding properties. Great location with a cable car stop literally right outside the door and only two blocks from Union Square. It's also not too far from Market Street where more nice shopping can be found, and if you're up for a 1 mile walk or so, you can easily get down to The Embarcadero to sightsee around the Port of San Fran, and then walk a bit further into Fisherman's Wharf (or if you're feeling lazy, take the cable car). Staff was very friendly and my room was clean and well-attended. My only real complaint was with the wireless, which was SO SLOW....1.3 Mbps for you techies, and this was both in my room and the lobby, so it was not a proximity issue. Apparently other folks have complained about the same pathetically slow wireless, so let's hope an upgrade is on the to-do list, espeecially if you need to get work done wirelessly while staying here. Otherwise, as previously noted, the hotel was quite nice, in a great location, and a good "buy" for the money.

title: “A great hotel!”
text: We stayed here in June while visiting family in Columbus. We were amazed at how nice this hotel was. It was close to the shopping center which was nice and lots of restaurants around. The only thing I wish our room had was a refrigerator. The staff was great and very helpful because we didn't know our way around town.

title: “Excellent hotyel for NYC”
text:
Stayed there for a few days right after they had opened - this is a great place for staying in NYC. Got a very nice opening deal. The staff was very supportive (though they needed 3 attempts to get me working keys to my room).
Pros:
*Brand new and very clean
*Thick soundproof windows
*Nicely decorated rooms with partial view
*Internet included
*Nice bathrooms
*Walking distance to Times Square
Cons:
*Very small rooms (but hey, its NYC!)
*Breakfast pricey and so-so (better go to one of the coffee shops or diners)

title: “Excellent location”
text: I really enjoyed this hotel. We did not have a car so it was a few blocks from the Metro, Chinatown stop. We didn't get in until 11pm, I called the front desk to tell them and she said it was fine, they would be expecting us. She checked us in upon arrival with no problem. The building is an old bank building, it still has that larger, older quality, but with modern furnishings. My sister said it was spooky, but I liked it. Our room was very compact, the king is definately a one or two person room. The tv was a nice flat screen. There was a coffee pot, can't remember if there was a fridge. The bathroom is supermodern, no tub which might be a turn off for some, but I didn't mind having shower only. It was quiet. I didn't hear anything until a lady knocked on our door at 4:00am. I opened it and she said "Oh, sorry". I guess she had the wrong room. The area seemed pretty safe, a lot of tourist activity. We had a White House tour scheduled at 8:30 am the next morning so we walked over and was happy it was 7 or 8 blocks from there. The valet asked if our car was with us, we said no we were walking, he ignored us from that point. He had waters and everything (it was already 90 degrees and was up to 106 that day). He only gave water to the car people, I guess because they were tipping. I wanted to ask him which direction to walk in, but he would no longer make eye contact. You could just hang a right directly outside the hotel if you are going to do a few Smithsonian institutions museums which were right across the street, and then another 5 or 6 blocks the main Smithsonian drag with more museums. We walked for hours after the tour, came back to the hotel and checked out. We asked the front desk if we could leave our bags because our flight was not until later, she said "of course, valet would assist". New valet guy on duty from the morning shift. Very helpful, great guy, made small talk, tagged our bags and gave me a slip. We tipped him. Upon picking up our bags, another valet guy gave us our bags, he was nice also. He also offered us WATER though we had checked out and were just retrieving our bags. I would definately stay here again.

title: “Not as bad as some of the reviews say; a pleasant stay”
text:
I stayed at this hotel about 5 years ago before the rooms were redone. Some of the recent reviews made me a bit concerned about my choice to stay again, but I ended up having a positive experience. I was greeted in the lobby near check in right away. I was waiting in line for maybe 2 minutes when an employee took me to the check in area for Hyatt Club guests which I am not a member of, so I thought this was a nice attempt to keep things moving in the lobby.
The rooms have been updated, and the decor was modern yet warm. The room was well sized with a side view of Grand Central Station. The bathroom was not terribly small,and it was clean.
There was a healthy choice of television stations for the family though we weren't in the room that much. I had to call for some help with setting the time on the clock and a light that kept buzzing, and the gentleman who fixed both was pleasant and efficient. If we asked for more towels, they were there immediately.
It was a nice stay. The bar was fine for a drink, but with so many amazing bars and restaurants in NYC you should go out and explore. The location is a plus with the amazing shops right next door in the station and Times Square about a 20 minute walk. Bryant Park is a 5 minute walk.
I would stay here again.

title: “A classic old style boutique hotel”
text:
Great location beside the Boston Library in the Back Bay area.
Close to great restaurants and entertainment.
We loved the Lenox for the room, the staff (Jimmy is a real gentleman and hotel treasure) and the little extras like the nightly chocolates on your pillow.
Next time we return to Boston there is no other place we'll stay.

title: “A Good Night's Sleep in the City”
text:
Full disclosure: I am a Westin loyalist. I prefer to stay at a Westin no matter where I'm traveling - for the reliable service, relaxing ambience, and heavenly bed (which I also bought for home!). 
The Westin on Market Street (it's actually on 3rd between Market and Mission) was average for a Westin. Here are my pros and cons:
PROS:
- central location, near BART and shopping, a few great food options
- clean, updated rooms with gorgeous views (get the deluxe rooms above floor 30)
- Heavenly beds and quiet rooms mean you get a good night sleep
- Cleaning staff was EXCEPTIONAL. Friendly, great attention to detail, super helpful
- really nice fitness center on site
- staff was responsive to a few issues we had and did their best to make good with us
CONS:
- front door staff was terrible. These guys were all either oblivious or rude. my partner just had surgery and they wouldn't even open the door for us. Very tacky, especially since this was our first impression of the property. Speaking of tacky, we asked one of them for a towncar to the airport and after tagging one, he literally stuck his head in our car door and asked the driver for his cut of the tip. I was embarrassed FOR him it was so cheap.
- room service food quality was pretty poor. Forgotten ingredients, missed condiments, cold food, once I even got a completely different dish than I ordered (they said afterwards they changed their menu, but they should have informed me of that when I placed my order). 
- internet accessibility on multiple devices. At check-in we were told we had free premium internet included in our rate, but when we logged in it defaulted to standard internet, which supports only one device at a time. We spent literally three hours on the phone with tech support trying to get online on our 2 iPads and 2 laptops. Tech support was a total nightmare (I actually cried out of sheer frustration) and it turned out that all that they needed to do was check with the front desk that premium internet was part of our rate. Once this was confirmed it took only seconds to get online. Why couldn't they have done that FIRST??? 
At check-out, I reported these issues to the front desk staff and they offered to credit my bill for $100. This was nice, and I didn't even have to ask for it - very classy Westin. However, given that our total bill was $3800, I'm not sure $100 was proportionate...
So all in all, this property is pretty good and I'd recommend it for business and tourism. Just hit up American Box next door at the Jewish museum for lunch, Tropisuena for dinner and avoid the room service. Don't park a car if you can get away with it. And make sure you ask about the internet plan when you check in!!

title: “Five Diamond Service”
text:
This is my third visit in 3 months at the Hilton Post Oak. I have never been treated so well at any hotel. I am very familiar with what "exceptional" service is and it is here.
What an incredible staff everywhere you go. It could be 5:30 in the morning and the graveyard shift is cleaning, polishing floors, etc. and they are still helpful and the best of all, give a hello and good morning. A good cup of coffee in my hand and it would have been a perfect start of the day!
Checking in at the front desk with Stephanie and Anthony was a pleasure. Along with Toya, they were always smiling and asking if everything was okay. Rooms were very clean and roomy and, It doesn't hurt that the beds are so comfortable.
Venus the hotel operator. You don't see her but you sure can feel the smile when she answers the phone. Doesn't matter how many times you have to call her, she is a joy!
Tony in banquets is absolutely a hidden gem. His exceptional service makes you feel as though you are in a fine dining restaurant. His staff is amazing.
Last but defiantly not least, DaVonna and Niki in the Sales department. What a pleasure to work with. They will make you feel like your best friends and have known you for years. Always coming around to see if we needed anything. 
I can't say enough about the Hilton Post Oak except that, I will be returning. 
Thank you and I will be back again! 
Heather Acrie

title: “Love The New Look!”
text: It had been 2 years since I have stayed at this location, and I must say I like the new look. The color scheme of the lobby gives the hotela fresh modern look. This location is very close to Midway. Check-in was smooth and as usual the beds were very comfortable. I look forward to staying at this location the next time I visit Chicago even more than before.

title: “Great Hotel right at Metro Center”
text:
We stayed at this Marriott during a very busy Cherry Blossom festival in Early April. The staff were all very friendly and efficient. The room was a bit cramped, but nicely appointed. The best thing about this hotel (apart from the Starbucks on the first floor) is it's proximity to Metro Center, which is a transfer station. The Metro gets you all around the city and is modern and efficient. The elevator/escalator at the 12th and G Street entrance is just a few hundred feet from the the Starbucks exit. We loved the convenience, especially as we have two young children.
We did have an issue with the service at the Fire and Sage restaurant (reviewed separately), which nearly ground to a halt on what seemed like a typically busy Saturday night. After being there an hour (and 45 minutes after we had ordered), we were still awaiting our food. Once it did arrive, it was pretty good, but certainly not worth the wait. The mananger of the hotel was very sympathetic the next day gave us credit for our parking and a nice reward bonus. The Sunday brunch there was terrific, however.
We will definitely be back!

title: “Great Hotel- will definitely stay again”
text: We had a great two night stay in Dec 2008. Hotel staff were very accomodating with our 18 month old- providing a cot, toy and stroller for him. The staff were friendly and upbeat. Our room was also upgraded. Our only dissappointment was the food at the downstairs restaurant- way too expensive and did not meet expectations.

title: “Too expensive for what you get”
text: The hotel is pricey and although it is very grand and ornate (to be honest it made me feel uncomfortable) you don't get what you pay for. To be charged for internet access on top of the prices you pay seems really tight fisted and frankly the pool complex isn't very welcoming either. The room was big but in such a strange layout you didn't want to spend too much time there which made the choice of dual TV's and various sofa's a waste. I imagine it may be limited by the age of the building but the air con was pretty industrial and out dated too. Don't stay here but do go to Shuckers !

title: “Noise”
text:
If you are over 50, this is not your hotel. They have a CLUB NITE on Thurs, Fri, and Sat. The vibration from the amplifiers could be felt through the floor and walls. This hotel is located in the heart of the Gaslamp quarter. There are many fine resturants in the area. It is near everything. The hotel is MODERN. Our friends had a shower with glass walls right near the bed.
Our sink was a steel bowl in a glass case. The staff is very friendly and courtious. I would stay again, but never on CLUB NITE.
 Tony (70 + )

title: “Horrible Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the L'Enfant Plaza Hotel for seven nights during the first week of July. The location is NOT worth the extreme pain of staying at this establishment.
My room on the 15th floor was filthy; some areas could not have been cleaned for months. The carpet was frayed and coming loose in the corners of the room. The closet was full of dirt and dust on the floor and shelves.
The air-conditioner did not work; the room was balmy all the time - even when on high fan and the lowest thermostat setting. The air vent is located in the ceiling over the bathroom door and had water running from it constantly. When I say "running" - I mean "running" - it was not a drip. The carpet underneath the vent was soaking wet and I had to put several towels down to contain the water and remind myself not to step in it.
The television did not work - only had five channels which changed everyday. The pool requires a lifeguard and was seldom open. The entrance is impossible to find from the street. The front desk workers are unfriendly and are probably sick of hearing complaints; I do feel bad for them.
I don't even want to get into the whole construction problem occurring at this property - there is not enough room here to write about it - just know that there is a ton of major construction happening outside all the rooms. If you like to be waken by jackhammers on your balcony - then this hotel is for you.
The only reason I completed my stay is because I was in Washington for a convention, was assigned to the hotel and could not find an alternative in the city due to it being the Fourth of July week.
DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL - there are many hotels worthy of your business that are in equally great locations. When I brought my concerns to the management, they offered a free drink - that was it.

title: “Great Hotwire price, but beware high parking costs!!”
text:
We stayed for 5 nights in November. The Hyatt was fine for the discounted price we paid on Hotwire. However the hotel does not have its own car park and the parking fee of $26.00 per day (or$36.00 per day for valet parking) adds a substantial extra to the cost. 
The pool/gym area was very nice.
Overall everything was fine at this hotel, nothing was outstanding.

title: “Wonderful location with a few surprising touches!”
text: Stayed here for 3 days for business, and the location was perfect. Close to office as well as all downtown shopping, restaurants and activities. The room was on 12th floor with a nice view, descent size, awesome hair dryer, walk in closet, nice TV. The water pressure was pretty bad, so was the bath towel size. To make up for that, they offered wonderful cookies every night, and I saw other people taking full advantage of the happy hour. The breakfast was descent - who serves eggs without any breakfast potatoes? Not a big deal, but it was quite surprising! Overall, I would stay here again if I am travelling for business.

title: “Another excellent stay & good value”
text:
This was our second stay at the UN Millennium Plaza. We recommend you book direct with the hotel and ask for 'In House reservations' rather than the call centre. They are very obliging & helpful. We chose a superior room in the refurbished East tower, but were upgraded to a Junior Suite, free of charge on arrival, which has the advantage of a lounge & 2 bathrooms. 
Like most NY sensibly priced hotels, this is not ‘posh’ but it is clean, spacious & comfortable with the friendliest staff you could wish for. Ideally located opposite the UN, it is in a quiet spot, but only 10 minutes walk from Grand Central Station & 15 mins to 5th Ave. We did not eat in the hotel, but turn right out of the front doors and head for John’s Diner for a super breakfast & you will be treated like friends and quickly feel like a ‘native New Yorker’. There is a super deli a few doors away & Fabio’s Italian restaurant, two doors from John’s Diner is superb.

title: “Not a 3 star, maybe this is more about Hotwire than the actual Hotels”
text: My hubby and I stayed at La Quinta Inn & Suites on Sept. 11th before the 7 day Mexican Riviera cruise on Royal Caribbean for the 12th-19th. We purchased on Hotwire for a 3 star hotel which ended up costing $74. We got the LAX La Quinta Inn. Definitely, not a 3 star, more a 2 star. Front desk service was efficient, a little slow and seemed very aloof and indifferent. Small rooms very basic, no frills, no thrills. Appreciated the free breakfast the next day, however, very mediocre. For our purpose of just putting our head down and heading to the pier the next day, it was fine, but it should have cost $$40-50, not $74. I've already complained to Hotwire that they need to reevaluate their criteria for assessing star ratings, as I complained that they advertised The Westin Bonaventure downtown LA as a 4 star that clearly wasn't and that they need to reevaluate some of their contracted hotels. People can make mistakes, but please correct them ASAP and don't advertise a 2 star as a 3 star or a 3-3.5 star as a 4 star. It's misleading and that's a big no-no in doing business and maintaining your client base.

title: “Very convenient location!”
text:
If you have business in downtown Indianapolis, this Residence Inn is very clean and convenient. The staff is very friendly, greeted this weary traveler warmly and my room was ready and clean.
Unlike many Residence Inns, the breakfast buffet is spread out a bit. The bagel and muffin stations are in two distinct areas with separate toasters. Seems like a trivial detail but that is a feature I notice as I stay at this chain quite often and see the backup at other locations. Great idea!
One feature that would be nice to have here would be automatic doors at the lobby. I noticed folks with large bags struggling to open the doors.
Given the price difference between here and the JW Marriott who probably have the automatic doors but no free breakfast, I will stay here again!

title: “Fantastic Staff..... Dreadful rooms”
text:
We had a double room booked via Airmiles for my partners 40th Birthday. Prior to arrival I sent several emails asking about the availability of Airport Transport and the potential purchase of a bottle of champagne prior to arrival. I did not receive an email back having re sent them a couple of times. I rang twice at a 'business hours time' only to be transferred and on hold without reply on two (very expensive calls) occasions.
On arrival after a 16 hr journey we were told our room was not available for a further hour as it had not been cleaned. So our room was not available till 1500 hrs.
Room 1253 overlooked an interior brick wall, the air condition unit was extremely noisy and the furniture was simply old and of poor quality. Draw handles were broken whilst the carpets were very worn. The bathroom had been refurbished to an adequate standard but nothing special. Within the room we had a hand written note left wishing my partner a happy birthday....nothing more. There was no basic tea/coffee facilities within the room. On checking out we were charged for three drinks from the room bar which we had never had and a number of telephone calls which were not connected.
In conclusion the room for our three night stay was very expensive for the standard received. It is important to state that the staff were extremely helpful, with good recommendations and advice. This is a tired hotel with some minimalistic modernisation.

title: “2 Day sray”
text:
Room needs updating. TV picture snowy.
Door frame needs insulating. Noise from the freeway goes right through the cracks.
Staff very friendly and helpful.

title: “Really great hotel and Great location! loved the breakfast!”
text:
I stayed here with my parents in October a year ago and it was more than what we expected! the room we booked had a separate kitchen (we cooked instant noodles on one of the nights, when we were to lazy to go out haha). The room was really big, we had two double beds and there was a dining table aswell. We really enjoyed the breakfast, the best continental breakfast I've had so far :) we loved the bagels especially! I thought it was quite cool that you could put your breakfast on a tray and take it to your room to eat, as the breakfast area is quite small.
There was a guest computer with complimentary use of internet, which was a bonus! In terms of location, I don't think you could get any better it was right behind Hollywood Boulevard! and easy access to the metro. The staff were very helpful with giving directions to everywhere we wanted to go and stored our luggage for us as we had an evening flight.
I feel we got a bargain with this hotel and both myself and my parents had a most enjoyable stay in LA. I would definitely recommend this hotel to my friends and family and will return when I am visiting again.

title: “I would probably just sleep at the airport next time...”
text:
Bed was really uncomfortable, the pillows were hard and thin, and the mattress was worse than a 20 year old pull-out couch... 
You could hear EVERYTHING going on outside the room - footsteps upstairs, footsteps outside... 
There are two good things - proximity to the airport and the front desk guy was really nice.
All in all, I would probably just sleep at the airport next time. I would probably get a better night's sleep.

title: “Loved it!! Look no further...”
text: This is a great spot. This was the first time I stayed at this hotel. The staff was very pleasant, helpful and professional. The rooms are clean, comfortable and spacious. My sisters and I came to New York for a shopping trip. The beds were so comfortable and the room was quiet. I loved that there was a microwave & a mini fridge in the room. There is a lovely restaurant inside the hotel and the cuisine there was wonderful as well. The staff there was great. They offer complimentary breakfast to hotel guests and it was great. You will love the location. It is just around the corner from Macy's! I am looking forward to my next trip to NYC, will definitely stay at this location. If you are looking for a place that is in the middle of great shopping, just a few blocks from 5th Avenue and other sights to see, you will really like it here!

title: “Clean & great location--plus wonderful apples, cookies, coffee”
text:
We stayed here 3 nights in February and really enoyed our stay. It's on the cable car line and right at Union Square where you can shop, take an on-and-off bus, etc. We loved the apples at the front desk and the coffee (or hot water for tea) and cookies near the elevator. OK, our room wasn't very big (although we had the biggest bathtub I've ever seen), but it was big enough and very clean. It had a huge closet where we kept the things that might normally have been kept out in the room. And though we had sunny days the whole time we were in SF, we were delighted to know that an umbrella was in the closet for use if needed. I'm not sure about this, but I think I read that this hotel is not air-conditioned, so you might want to check on that if you are staying in the summer.
We were on the third floor, and I like to take the stairs whenever possible. The stair well is narrow and a bit twisty--an interesting reminder from this historic hotel that people weren't always the super-size we often are now. Anyway, because I used the stairs, I discovered a tiny wall-niche take-one, leave-one library (on the second floor, I think). Anyway, although I didn't end up getting a book, it was fun to look at all of the books in languages I don't read, certainly a commentary on the kind of international clientele served by the Chancellor Hotel. We would very definitely stay here again.

title: “The service was terrible!”
text: The location of this hotel is the only good thing. I had a block of rooms there for my wedding guests. We stayed there for 2 nights and had over 30 other room booked by our guests. We were treated terrible. Both nights in the bar my guests and I were yelled at for various reasons. On Saturday night, they had 3 different workers talk to my friend, about an incident that was over. The worker hit my mom in the back with a door. The lost my aunt's luggage then when they foiund it they ran over her foot with the cart without an apology. When having breakfast with my guest Sunday morning before they left, the waiter yelled at my husband about moving a table so we could sit with them. However, another waiter was able to make it work. All we kept hearing was "we have other guest to worry about" No one was worried about me as a guest at that time. I will never stay here again.

title: “room was nice, but...”
text:
Room - that I stayed was facing to backyard so very quiet, nice and clean. Bathroom - good. Bath tub - big but dirty so I couldnt take a bath even I really really wanted (Actually, it looked clean, but when I touched I was able to tell it was not clean enough to take a bath). Closet - i think its good sixe. Bed - I had a great sleep. Free coffee and tea - I enjoyed. Front desk lady told me I can have free coffee and tea, also pastries when I checked in, but I didnt see any pastries...
The only problem of this hotel is the people who are working at front desk.
I saw total 4 people(2 male and 2 female), and two guys were nice, especially one of them was sooooo nice, kind and has great smile. However two of both ladies were not nice at all. Especially the lady at the front desk who took care of me when I checked in, she seemed didnt even want to have me in the hotel!(its just what I felt, you know) It was really disapointed. Fortunately I saw the lady only once when I checked in. I was so happy and excited when I got to San Fransisco, but she messed up all of my feelings on first day of SF....

title: “Quite acceptable”
text: Not too big on hotel chain but wound up here by default. Room was clean and well-appointed. Excellent electronics from WiFi to TV. Very comfortable bed. Would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Loved the Amalfi!”
text:
The Amalfi Hotel was great, and I agree with the other postings, hotel was much better than many 4 or 5 star Hotels I have been to. The key things that made the Amalfi better:
- best continental breakfast (located on each floor, so you don't have to put shoes on or get dressed, you can stay in pj's)
- Manager's reception - free cocktails/appetizers each night - great way to meet other travellers and relax
- Local jazz cds, books and magazine were much appreciated, I feel asleep to Chicago jazz everynight
- Bed - was fantastic, so comfortable
- Bathroom - stocked with Aveda products and had a double head shower. 
Plus, all the staff are really friendly and very helpful. I would definately recommend the hotel and I would return. 
Book this hotel, you won't regret it, great location, amenities and service!

title: “Just OK Sums It Up”
text:
This is my second disappointing Westin stay in as many attempts.
I travel back to L.A. frequently on business and normally stay at Hilton Checkers, the Biltmore or the Omni, but I have been trying to pump up my Starwood points so I thought I'd give the Bonaventure a try.
The hotel has a number of problems. Number one might be it's size. Other than Las Vegas I try not to stay in places with more 400-500 rooms, 1,300+ is just too big.
It was very warm in LA this weekend so I went to the pool to cool off. The pads on the lounge chairs are so filthy I hardly wanted to lay on one. I did what most people there were doing, covered them in towels. They do offer poolside cocktails and snacks, but only if you place a call from the house phone by the pool entrance.
The rooms are decent sized, but there were no amenities (soap, mouthwash, toiletries, etc) on the bathroom counter. I found that surprising. I had to reach into the bath tub to get soap. There were also no hand towels on the counter. I had to reach into the shower to get a hand towel. That seemed weird too.
This is supposed to be a business hotel and they want to charge me $13 a day for Internet access? I get free Wi Fi at almost any place I stay these days on business. And then they charged me $42 to valet my car? I called down to have the car brought up. When I got to valet they had no idea what I was talking about, no one was getting my car. I had to wait ten more minutes. I paid $42 for service like that?
Another odditiy here are that the elevators don't stop at every level. If you drive in to the valet entrance on Figueroa, you have to take an escalator down to the lobby, the tower elevators don't stop on levels 2, 4 or 6. So when you come down from your guest room to get your car you have to get off at level 1 or 3 and then stake stairs or escalator to get your car.
The plus side of the Bonaventure is the mini mall on levels 2-6 and the bridges to other parts of downtown. When I worked in downtown L.A. I ate at the food court on 4 often and it has some good places. Mandarin West and L.A. Prime are also pretty good upscale restaurants.
The Galleria and Starwood points won't be enough to get me back anytime soon though. I will go back to Checkers or the Biltmore for my December trips.

title: “Felt Like Staying With Friends/Family”
text:
I LOVE this hotel. It's in the perfect spot, has free parking-limited, but there is plenty of safe street parking in the area-Raymond greeted me like an old friend and was really helpful getting me and my small dog settled the day we arrived. He went out of his way to make us feel welcomed and even recommended a few places to grab dinner and gave us extra towels for my dog since it was stormy. Bruce was also awesome and was the one who helped me with my reservations. 
I highly recommend this hotel, and will be staying here again next time I am in SF.

title: “This Hotel should come with a warning !”
text: I got out of my taxi having crossed the Atlantic to be greated with cement and builders rubble - got to reception and was given a room on the tenth floor ( no mention of an upgrade- inspite of holding a platinum Ambassador Card - the room was fine a bit dated - no fridge !! - but comfortable - I showered and went out - must never sleep after an Atlantic crossing - need to get the body and mind on to American time ! - The night was good and comfortable - I had received vouchers for breakfast - however it was in the lobby area - The Hotel was under a major refit - however no one told me ! - The Restaurant had been moved to the 15th Floor however not for my two nights ! - The General Manager - Andy Duymovic not happy enough with a major refit and all of his guests already upset closes the temporary restaurant so he can take in a group in from Fulbright gives them the 15th Floor and makes all his guests eat breakfast in the lobby - a complete insult to anyone - not enough tasbles , chairs, food stored on the floor under tables - a total mess - no one was bothered - this GM is either greedy or perhaps should go back to school to learn how to loook after his key clients ! - I would give this hotel a wide berth - it is poor value for money /dated and needs a new GM who understands service ! - Boston can do a lot better .

title: “Great stay front desk staff is awesome!”
text: Stayed three nights here and was not dissapointed. Stayed here when it was Holiday Inn which was very dated the Fairfield did a total renovation the rooms are upgraded to marriott standards. This hotel looks brand new now and u cant beat customer service. Check in isnt until 4 but they held our luggage when we arrived at 4 we were suppose to get 2 queens balcony view but all they had was a king which has no pullout sofa when i voiced my concerns to the staff they immediately upgraded us to a suite! It was very nice this hotel is close to everything has a good breakfast free use of computers in lobby and u can park in the street and save on parking in the garage. Would definitely come back again Marriott hotels cant be beat!

title: “Great place to stay in the city”
text:
This is an extremely nice place to stay in San Francisco.
The good:
• Free WIFI with a large lobby.
• Close to the Cable Cars (which my daughter loves) and (like all of San Francisco) transportation.
• Plenty of great places to eat all within walking distance.
• Right on Union Square.
• Clean and very comfortable rooms.
The bad:
• Like every place else in the city they charge for parking (come on – you build a parking structure in your building and then your guests don’t even get a discounted rate?)
• The hot tub/Jacuzzi is too small for the customer base (there is only one). 
We stayed 2 nights (and should have stayed longer) and really enjoyed our stay. All in all a very nice place to stay, and we will be going back.

title: “Hmmmm tough one - Nice hotel but has drawbacks”
text:
The property is a nice historic property. I found the staff helpful, hotel was clean, location is close to many good restaurants but I had the following issues:
1. Rooms are tiny. The hit my elbows as I was trying to use the sink. 
2. Not enough plugs in room to plug in three devices to charge. 
3. Lobby while historically welcoming is dark and dreary. 
4. No A/C in hallways. Very hot. 
5. Bottle of water, in room, cost $7. I know Boston is not cheap - but come on - $7?
6. We had to circle the block for almost 15 min while waiting for a space to open in front of the hotel so we could check in. 
It was nice that Internet wireless was fast and free. 
I'm sure some people will enjoy this hotel but it was not for us.

title: “Great Location and Friendly Staff”
text:
Hampton Inns are always reliable, and this location is no exception! Just a few blocks from Times Square and near both Times Square Station and Penn Station, it's super easy to hop on a subway and go nearly anywhere you want in NYC. Staff were friendly, and were very accommodating when I asked for a late checkout on the day we left. Breakfast was good, and actually varied a bit from day to day. It was nice to not have exactly the same items each morning. Good coffee also. 
Rooms are small, but it's NYC! I doubt you'll find other similarly priced hotels nearby that are any bigger. Besides, you should be out on the town, not hanging out in your room all day and night! 
If you're looking for a reliable mid-level hotel near times square, I'd highly recommend the Hampton Inn Times Square South - I'd stay here again in a heartbeat!

title: “Loved the Marriott”
text:
Wonderful hotel. Good location, great views, nice staff. I would definitely return.
I called shortly after my arrival to inquire about the availability of a product in the hotel sundries store, and was told a complimentary supply would be sent right up. Nice touch.
The valets were so nice, making you feel very welcome on your return. More often than not there were two to attend to each arriving vehicle, opening all doors. While waiting for a ride the valet even offered me bottled water.
A very nice touch was the airline check-in station, with printer for boarding passes, next to the front door. 
The restaurant was very nice. The service was impeccable and the food tasty. We had a late night dessert and the buffet breakfast the next morning and both experiences were pleasant.
One of the nicest things is the street elevator located just north of the hotel that takes you up from the waterfront to the next street. It's a pretty steep hill. From there it was a short walk to downtown shopping or trendy Belltown.
Contrary to rumors that cabs are difficult to find, I had quick success with each attempt to hail a cab. But the downtown bus service is exceptional as well. I was a little worried about hailing a cab after the ballet, so the hotel arranged for a towncar pickup. The driver was waiting for me right on schedule by the front door of the Phelps Center on Mercer, and the price was only a little more than a taxi.
I will definitely be staying at this hotel the next time I'm in Seattle!

title: “Perfect”
text:
Took my wife to NYC for her birthday and really wanted to make it special. After reading review after review of hotels in the area, I settled on the Trump Intl. It was the right choice. And this after staying in the cheapest room overlooking the Starbucks and newly constructed Time Warner building, otherwise known as a city view. 
Service was impeccable. They made sure to wish my wife a happy birthday every chance they could and even brought up a complimentary bottle of champagne with a birthday card. I requested my suit be pressed before dinner (in 3 hrs) and they got it back to me ahead of time and did it all complimentary ($25 value). For turn down service, they'd lay out a robe, put the Trump slippers by the bed and bring up chocolates, bottled water and ice. For those concerned about security, there's always someone waiting by the elevators and you must insert your room key into the elevator panel before you can select your floor.
The room was small. But this wasn't a big deal. The linens were top notch, the room was comfortable and attractive, there was a kitchenette, a refigerator stocked with bottled Trump water (complimentary) and the flat screen widescreen TV was unobtrusive. Curtins open/close with a remote. My wife complained a little about the bathroom counter space but this was a little gripe. There's a DVD player and the staff was more than willing to send out a runner to bring us back any movie of our choice.
The location is superb. Right on central park and Columbus Circle, you're around 15 blocks from Time Square but more importantly, there's a subway station just 30 yards from the hotel front door.

title: “No A/C = Terrible Nights Sleep”
text: We arrived on a Friday afternoon, looking for a relaxing anniversary weekend. When we entered the room, it felt like a sauna. We were told to adjust the settings and that it would be fine. WRONG. When we returned from dinner, it was no cooler than before and made sleeping unbearable. We complained the next morning, and were given one fan and were told that they were 'working on it'. By saturday evening, we were again sweating again, and mentioned it to the staff, who brought up another fan. Two fans blowing hot air in our faces was not conducive to sleep. Our romantic weekend away without the kids was a completely flop. To top it off, the remotes didn't work. The rooms were old and faded. Not what I expected for that price or by the website descriptions.

title: “Good Location, Plenty of Space, Just what we needed”
text:
Just returned from a week in New York, staying at the Eastgate Tower. Excellent location on 39th and 3rd with easy access to all the sites and Grand Central Station. It felt very safe walking about at night, but we were only 2 blocks from the UN so that might have had something to do with it.
We had a one bed apartment and as I travelled with my sister and didn't fancy sharing a bed with her, I slept on the double sofa bed - it was the most comfortable bed too! 
The room was very spacious, clean and had everything we needed. Definitely recommend having a kitchen so you can do your own thing instead of eating out all the time. There were plenty of "order in" options locally too.
The decor was a bit 80s, but the furnishings weren't that old. View wasn't much but we didn't choose the hotel for its view.
Lovely staff, if a bit slow. I had to ask 3 times for my sofa bed to be made up and 3 times for an extra blanket, but we got there in the end. It didn't detract from the stay at all.
Would definitely stay here again. 
Lots of eateries within a block or two. Docks Seafood Bar on 3rd & 40th was expensive, but very good. Frontier Restaurant on the fcorner of 39th & 3rd was excellent low priced, wide choice - great breakfasts! Also, plenty of mini marts and grocery stores to stock up the kitchen!

title: “A very costly hotel with lesser facility”
text:
I have stayed with Grand hayyat for 12 days in USA. It is a very grand hotel with more than 20 floors. But, the facility wise it is not so good. The room doesn't contain mini bar, press, microwave. The staff are very rude and they are very money centric.
There are three different kind of hotel inside and food facility is good.

title: “AWESOME DOWNTOWN CHICAGO HOTEL!!!”
text: Very nice hotel in downtown Chicago! ... staff where wonderful ... lol everytime i ask for a warm cookie or two they gave me one ... front desk was superb!!! ... the rooms are very clean and nicethe bed is heavenly ... you night not be able to make that event u had planned!!! ... there is a cash bar in every room! ... dont u dare bump into it or touch it! dont even think about it if you do it goes on ur bill! .... i asked for a friddge for medical purposed i was granted one on the spot! ... very nice bellmen they even gave great tips! ... a 15 ride or less from the megabus stop!!!!dats awesome! ... big bathroom very clean!!! ... overall ... i sooooo enjoyied my stay!!!

title: “Very nice and excellent location”
text:
This small hotel next to Time Square is cozy and of good quality. The rooms are small, but you do not need more as you don't stay in your room in New York! There are rooms on the street, not too loud, but you have also rooms in the back, which are really quiet.
The only thing which is tough is the breakfast : breakfast is allright , but the person, who is serving is, is really unfriendly!

title: “Nice Stay!”
text: Area is great; lots of restaurants and bars to walk to. There is a cigar bar, sports bar, and convenience store type shop with a starbucks in the lobby. Room was clean and comfortable, would return.

title: “Exactly what we expected...”
text: This property was a cute boutique hotel. I enjoyed the decor of the room, the restaurant had tasy food and the staff were uber friendly. We didn't have any issue parking on the street and our room was directly over the restaurant but we didn't have any issue falling asleep. We will return!

title: “Great location, easy to get around from here”
text: Great area to stay in - full of restaurants, close to Mag Mile shopping, easy access to transit and one block away from Hop On Hop Off bus stop. Hotel was quiet, and had friendly staff. You do not need a car if you are staying at this hotel. Will definitely stay here again when we return.

title: “Excellent True Green Experience”
text: Element is ahead of the curve when it comes to being green. They even give preferred parking to hybrid vehicles. The entire hotel has an ultra-modern decor. The rooms have full kitchens, very comfortable beds and the showers make you feel like you are underneath a Hawaiian waterfall. I loved their bath soap which reminded me of the smell of green apples. The morning free-breakfast was fantastic with a choice of several great seamingly fresh juices and the egg wraps were so good. The staff is very accomodating, I even got to hang out in their large pool just a bit past closing. Although Houston was just too hot, the Element was just right. I would highly recommend a stay at this property.

title: “This place is Awesome!”
text: Our family stayed here between Christmas and New Years and loved it. The rooms were clean. Breakfast in the morning was always great and lots of variety. The staff were always friendly. Location was great as well. We did like having the lobby not at ground level as we could sit around safely and look down at the streets. Their was also a great Eisteins Bagle Restaurant that you can access without going outside! My kids only comment is they wished there would have been Disney Channel or Nick on the TV!

title: “Not a bad place to stay”
text: For the most part, we enjoyed our stay here. We did have a problem when they did not read my requests that I made with my reservation. When I complained about it, the manager gave us free breakfast at their breakfast buffet. We enjoyed the buffet. I was a bit surprised that they did not have a swimming pool. They had a sport area that was outside, but I'm not sure how that is intended to be used. I did not see any basketball nets from the inside. I thought the fitness area was well equipped. Most of the cardio equipment had a television attached. I did get a little hot while exercising. I think it was because the room has skylights. Maybe in the summer you'd have better air conditioning. We did not experience any problems with our room. The parking seemed a little quirky to me. It would have been better if they would have explained the parking garage. I chose to park outside. The lobby has free wifi, but you have to pay in the rooms. I did not mind taking my laptop to the lobby.

title: “It was decent”
text: I was a little concerned by the other posts but overall the hotel was clean, the conference rooms were very adequate. I loved the coffees and teas provided for the attendees. The restaurants on site were helpful for those of us who did not want to leave. The rooms weren't fancy and very new but everything was clean. For one night and for business meetings it really is ideal. For an extended vacation the only bonus would be the water park.

title: “Good Price, No problems!”
text: Went to Denver, CO for 5 days booked hotel through Booking Buddy. At first sight the hotel was disappointing...it wasn't amazing to look at, just OK! After checking in I found the staff very helpful and pleasant. The room was large, clean and well tended by house cleaning staff. I paid very little for my stay there and was not expecting luxury. Was expecting a clean room, nice bathroom, sufficient towels (white fluffy ones), plenty of pillows, warm blankets I wasn't afraid to handle ( nice white comforter on bed) windows that opened, handheld shower head, nice size bathroom appointed in ceramic tiles and stone..maybe a lookalike stone. I got all of this plus a breakfast that covered full range from eggs to waffles. What I didn't get and expected was a flat screen TV, pay per view...was disappointed. wanted to watch movies on rainey day...went to bar in hotel instead which was fun too. So, would I go back, sure. I'd book online through a booking service like Booking Buddy.

title: “great hotel for quick visit in LA”
text: my wife and i stayed at this hotel for 2 nights from 23-25 November 2012 while visiting family in LA. The location was very handy, but the hotel is very outdated and old and needs a complete make over, but fot a short term visit, it suited us as we only spent evenings sleeping here. during the day we were out and about. Our room was a good size and the bed was very comfortable and soft. Surprisingly our room had no mini bar or fridge and once again a bit outdated with furnishings and an old airconditioning system.

title: “Fun, fun fun”
text:
What a fun place to stay. The staff are very polite, helpful and very nice. They made us feel as though we were the most important guests in the hotel. 
The elevators are also fun as they give you a wonderful view of Los Angeles. All four elevator blocks give you a different view of LA. The lobby offers free internet, which is fairly fast. The rooms are comfortable and the beds are wonderfully comfortable.
We stayed for 3 nights and enjoyed the downtown location.
But get real, how could a Westin hotel actually be anything else but good. It lived up to its reputation.
The breakfast buffet was delicious with plenty of choice and all the food was hot when it should be and on ice when it should be cold.
We had a dog with us and the hotel was extremely accomodating. The only negative is that I would not recommend the high-speed internet of 60 to 120 kB.

title: “Good oasis.”
text: We are Bostonians who sadly have to work elsehwhere . We found this to be a well situated hotel in an interesting area of the city. Thanks to the ease of its shuttle other central areas of Boston proper are easily accessible. The hotel was pleasing, very clean, excellent rooms. The breakfasts are a bit pricey but there are other eating establishments withing walking distancea and are worth seeking out . No complaints and we would come here again. Beautiful spot inthe summer and most likely interesting in the Winter season. Go without fear but bring your own hardboiled eggs.

title: “Excellent hotel, amazing staff”
text: I'm a business traveller and I've been working in the Ballantyne area for almost 12 months now, commuting pretty much every week from Chicago. The aloft Ballantyne is awesome. Extremely clean, organized and the staff is so friendly! They know we're frequent guests so every night when we arrive at the hotel they have everything prepared for us: keys programmed, check in process, all we need to do is swipe the credit card and go to our rooms. I am very happy we found the aloft. The only minor suggestions I would make are to change the alarm clocks to a digital one (the ticking of the second hand sometimes kept me awake at night) and evaluate alternatives to the window AC unit. Disclosure: I am probably more sensitive to noise than the average person.

title: “Good for the price!”
text:
Overall for what we paid this hotel was great. We got a special summer deal for a 4 night stay - we paid $139 a night plus tax. That included a voucher for breakfast per day (value of $10 a day). We had a non smoking twin on a high-ish floor (can't remember which one!) that overlooked the street to the front of the hotel. The beds were big and comfy, the room was clean, and the bathroom was good. yes its a bit worn at the edges and the lifts are really slow but lets face it you're in NYC! who wants to spend ages in the room! all you need is a clean comfy room to grab some rest before another great day shopping and sightseeing! The lobby is amazing too - very old grandeur!
If i could get the same price again i'd definately stay here. its really close to grand central, a 10 min walk to times square and overall a good stay for the price.

title: “Great location & great rooms not so sure about club lounge......”
text:
Booked Parc 55 as part of Travelzoo offer for $165 plus taxes for club room & club lounge access for 3 nights. Really great location right by Powell St BART , so easy to get to from the airport, just come out of the subway look for the BofA and it is the tall brownish building on the other side of the road, you cannot get lost !! Checkin was prompt & efficient and allocated room on 27th floor with amazing views over the city. Quite a large sized room with sofa and great big comfortable bed which was very sleepable. Good sized bathroom with big tub & lots of soaps & gels & earplugs (not needed). Noise was not an issue except for police & fire sirens in the night sometimes from street level. Overall a good room and spacious. 
However club lounge was a bit disappointing as it was quite small and not a whole lot of table & chairs.The breakfast options were limited to cereals & pastries with some ham & cheeses, juices & coffee. When it was busy in the morning it was hard to get a seat & you had to wait for someone to vacate. The cocktail hour canapés were just cheese & crackers with a small hot snack, the soft drinks & juices were free but the wines/beers were payable. For the extra $25 that it cost I did expect a little more & was disappointed as I have been in better hotel lounges where all drinks (soft & hard) were free & you had a better experience.
Apart from that the hotel was fab, Lobby was massive, 3 free computers by the lobby lifts (6 lifts) to check email & print boarding passes. The location is spot on for tourists & first time visitors to the city, all the BART, buses & tram go along Market St past the hotel & there are stops moments away from the hotel as well as the Powell Street cable car turnaround. The 3 day MUNI travel pass available form the sales desk by BofA is fantastic value @ $21 for 3 days & includes unlimited travel on the cable card, trams & buses. Also check out the tourist information office in Powell St BART subway for free wifi & free local calls from the phones on the walls !!The Cheesecake Factory is just around the corner on Union Sq in the top floor of Macys and stays open very late and has a nice open air terrace overlooking Union Sq. If in town again would probably try elsewhere but in same neighbourhood.

title: “Worst Hotel I've Stayed in - NYC”
text:
We have traveled to NYC numerous times and unfortunately the hotels we normally book were not available. We settled on the Hotel Pennsylvania, which sadly we came to discover upong check-in was filthy, had broken fixtures and lights in the rooms and halls, torn and stained carpets, disgusting bathrooms, old broken-down beds, stiff cheap linens and the type of clientele that screams, sings, and runs up and down the halls all night. 
It took a hour to check in due to the line and their poor staffing. They refused to honor our booking preferences because we booked through Expedia. The staff is rude beyond belief. I would rather sleep on a park bench or in the subway than repeat this experience.

title: “average hotel on the riverwalk”
text:
Hubby and I usually stay at the Hilton, but decided to try bidding online for a room and we got the Crowne Plaza at a rate of $89.00.
When we arrived, the rate for valet was $28 a day with in and out privileges. We were prepared for this, but it still sucked. The lobby is nice, but the rooms and floors are in very much need of a renovation. The bed was okay, not plush or anything, but the linens are comfortable. We had to spend the first night on a smoking floor which reeked so bad, I barely got any rest. They moved us to a non-smoking floor the next day, but the smell of smoke was still lingering on my clothes. It was quite gross. Anyhow, the second room was a lot cleaner, but there was no remote control in the room. Oh well,.........Anyhow, while this hotel is technically on the riverwalk, it's about a 15-20 minute walk to where all the fun is. We bought a river taxi pass for $10 a day/person, but found out that it can sometimes take longer to get to your destination if you're sharing the taxi with a lot of people. Also, you may have to wait a while to get picked up again later. It also stops running at 9pm. Even with these inconveniences though, it still is quite a pleasant ride, and it offers you a different view of the riverwalk.......While we saved a lot of money staying at the Crowne, next time around, we will probably stay closer to where the action is......

title: “Absolutely Loved It”
text:
I had to go to Charlotte on business and was looking for a place to stay Uptown because the hotel where the seminars I was attending was completely booked. The Omni was in a good location, but I have to admit that I was reluctant to book because of the many sub-par and borderline negative reviews. Time was running out, so I bit the bullet and booked anyway, hoping it was at least clean.
What a delightful surprise! Not only was the hotel - and my room - spotless, it was very nice and I had a lovely view. The staff could not have been nicer. This was a top notch experience from the moment I arrived until the time I left. I travel frequently and the Omni held its own for any of the finer hotels in the same category. I absolutely would not hesitate to recommend it to anyone visiting the Charlotte area. It is in a prime location with many nearby attractions, dining options, and conveniences. I will definitely go back again, for both business and pleasure.

title: “Lassandra-The Best Customer Service”
text: What a pleasure to arrive for breakfast each day to a smiling face that was truly happy to see you and help. Lassandra kept the line moving and made sure each person was treated special. She is truly an asset to your organization!

title: “Great Location, Awesome staff”
text: We stayed at this Comfort Inn for 4 nights and was greatly pleased with our stay. The staff members were all very courteous and super nice. They offered lots of dining and nighlife tips of the best places to go. The room was very small, hardly any room to walk around in. I had a corner room with 1 king bed and this is the first time i seen the type of layout for a room. When you walk in the room there are 2 small hallways i guess you can call them before you get to the main room. The bathroom was super small. Overall it was really clean. We didnt spend much time in the room anyways so it wasnt a big issue on the size other than trying to find places to put our luggage. I didnt like the front entrance at all, you have to walk up a small flight of stairs to get to the front desk. This is not a fun thing to do when you have large luggage! It had a great location, within walking distance from metro...i guess it is within walking distance to the mall......but im lazy and didnt want to walk that far lol. Good area of town.

title: “Yet another great relaxing stay”
text: I pulled in to the motel and checked right in. I got a GREAT rate even for a Sunday 59.00 + tax. Free wireless internet that worked great. The bed was ok it was a single room with a full size bed, being that I was by myself that was, but had anyone else been with me, that would have been way too small. Comfortable bed tho. Even the pillows were nice and comfy. The water pressure in the shower was PERFECT! Felt like I was standing under a water fall. It felt SOOOOO Good! So relaxing. The cable tv was just of course your run of the mill cable, very basic. The breakfast was GREAT. They had fruits, bagels, english muffins, cereal, milk, pastries, sausages in a blanket, pre wrapped waffles, juices, coffee. Much better than your normal "cont. breakfast" The location was perfect, literally right off the interstate Great view of Juarez MX. Its neat at night you can see where El Paso Ends and Juarez begins. Juarez has yellow street lights and EL Paso has White. No traffic noise from the interstate, I was in the back side of the motel. A restaurant within 500 ft. two convience stores with in a block. Safe area, I highly recommend.

title: “Top of the Line Hotel”
text: We've been to the Liberty before. Although an expensive place to stay, there's not a hotel like it anywhere in the area. Perfect ambiance, food, drink, decor and the service/rooms are beautiful. This time we were there during the "surprise October snowstorm". We had planned a birthday weekend and had to cut it short in order to get back before the storm hit. Without any ado, the front desk cancelled our reservation, apologized for the inconvenience (like the major storm was their fault?) and wished us luck getting home. I was delighted (and surprised) that they did not make us pay a cent for the night we didn't stay - even though there wasn't a 24 hour notice. This experience just makes the Liberty the only hotel choice we'll make when visiting Boston!

title: “Nice Stay - Great Staff”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for a conference 5/20-24/12. Check-in was quick and easy and the hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. Soon after arriving, I discovered that I had left a bag in the backseat of the cab that brought me over from the airport. The valet staff immediately called the cab company and assisted in retrieving my bag. I was very impressed with their concern and quick action. Much appreciated guys!
The lobby was nice, spacious, and contained a sports bar as well as a piano bar. Their food was great and the beer was cold. Servers were very friendly and fun to talk to.
My room was very clean, including the bathroom. It also had a nice size refrigerator and the beds were comfortable. My only concern with the room was that is was not very sound proof. The door had a large gap at the bottom which allowed noise in from the hallway. Could also hear the occupants from the adjoining room, and depending on their activity, it got a little noisy for a brief duration a couple of times during the night.
Great location, clean hotel, excellent staff! Highly recommend and would stay here again.

title: “not bad, but.....”
text:
I stayed in this hotel on the weekend of 5/13/05. The lobby was really tacky, but the desk staff was excellent. The room was huge by NYC standards, and had a great view, but was somewhat worn. The AC didn't work, and a call to the switchboard promised that someone would show up, but they never did - but since the windows opened, it was no big deal, (and actually quite refreshing to have a nice breeze in the room) 
All in all, I was quite pleased with the room and the rate - you would go far to find a better accomodation for such a price in this location - but there were some shortcomings. In my book, they weren't too bad, but it's worth reporting.

title: “Happy all around”
text:
The wife and I really liked our stay. I too was nervous about the room size, but not overly concerned, as we have stayed in small European hotels. Our solo room was fine - queen or king bed that was ultrasoft and comfortable with many pillows, there was decent leg room around both sides, and the bathroom was small but ample enough for one person at a time. 
Service was great, and the business center was helpful, but there are only 2 computers, so plan accordingly. Small gym on the 2nd floor. 
The only negative was our TV image was kind of dark and the volume was different for each channel. It worked well enough we dealt with it, but if you're planning a night inside for movies, check your TV first.

title: “WSI - Why WSI -Where WSI - Who WSI - What WSI”
text: Well let me tell you about the WSI Hotel. What an experience. Lots of people say WSI Scam WSI Scam WSI Scam. I like the hotel. Sure it is not pretty. But Certainly not a WSI Scam in my humble opinion. I really enjoyed the WSI service and the support that we had at the door. WSI gave me alot of confidence from the beginning. OK WSI is not a pretty hotel... I will give you that but not a Scam in my opinion. Value for sevice and price. WSI met my expectations and they were not a SCAM. No not on your life. WSI gave me the service i desrved at the right WSI Price.

title: “Cant believe anyone would say anything negative...”
text: We stayed at the La Quinta for four days during our holiday to LA and I thought it was a great hotel. Extremely welcoming and courteous staff who seemed to go out of the way for us. Although they are currently doing some renos we stayed in one of the new rooms and I thought it to be perfect for a hotel stay. I believe the price was reasonable as well. Its hard to believe people would have anything bad to say although I understand that some have champagne taste on a beer budget...Its great for the price!!!
