The location isnt super central but we rented a car for a very reasonable price just down the way. Very happy to reccomend this to other travellers.

title: “Just returned from an excellent 10 day stay at a truly world class hotel!”
text: We just returned from a 10 day family vacation to San Francisco where we enjoyed 2 connecting rooms at this exquisite hotel. Every moment spent at the San Francisco Omni Hotel was truly a pleasure! I could not have expected more from our entire experience at this hotel. From the timely communication about the reservation and on-line check-in options, the attentive and warm reception received from each staff member at the time of arrival, the wonderful daily amenities received as simply being a member of the FREE Select Guest program, impeccable housekeeping, exceptional dining through room service and Bob's restaurant, the special kid's program that allowed my daughter to feel just as special as we did each and every day...this hotel has all the bases covered! If you wish for your stay in San Francisco to be a true pleasure for both business and personal travel, you will not be disappointed by staying at this truly world class hotel!

title: “Big on space, small on service”
text: About the only good things I can say about the Sheraton Brookhollow was very nice and comfortable bed and the room was clean. On the downside, Internet connection was not free despite how it was advertised and still it was not working. Nor was the 800-lines, nor was the on demand cable. No Guest Services book inside the room. No fire map on the back of the door.

title: “Large room, attentive service and extremely quiet”
text: We just returned from a Chicago weekend - a parent's escape from our children. The hotel location was fabulous with easy access to the L and sights. The room was clean and larger than some of the hotels we have stayed at in the city. I usually don't sleep well in hotels, but the room was so quiet, I slept solidly. The pool and exercise areas were fantastic with a spa-like feeling. We only ate at the Novo Bar once and found their small plates were reasonably priced. The nachos were a bit bland, but they were still a nice option for a light dinner. Overall, the hotel was great and we'd definitely return.

title: “3.5 - Nice older hotel in a good location”
text: This is NOT a 4 star hotel. Nice older hotel -- beds were comfortable, staff friendly and it's a good location. But the rooms, bathrooms and general quality of the property are not up to par for 4 stars. Would give it 3.5 if possible. There was a wedding in the lower, public area so perhaps access to that area that would have added something, but the main floor lobby is lacking - small, with minimal, uncomfortable furniture.

title: “Not for the romantic couple”
text: I booked two nights at the W as a surprise for my wife. I read the reviews and thought that the place would be okay. The staff was friendly and very attentive. When we checked into our room what a surprise! The room was very small. I requested one bed but got two. There was very little room to walk around the room. The bathroom was tiny. They could probably do without the large desk that takes up 1/4 of the room. If the room was a little bigger or had only one bed the place would probably be okay. We checked out of the hotel quickly (Starwood Preferred Guest Customer) at no charge and checked into the Westin Horton Plaza with a much bigger room and more amentities.

title: “SMALL ROOM...WALL TO WALL”
text:
Stayed at The Bentley from Feb 19th to 21st... 
Booked a King Deluxe Room for my boyfriend and myself for his birthday weekend. Not at all what I thought it would be, our room was very small, wall to wall. The amenities listed on the website had not been in the room upon our arrival. Our bathroom light switch was not working, No i-pod dock, No Fresh towels were set out and we had no control over our air vent. After my boyfriend called and made complaints to the front desk they made sure to come correct their mistakes immediately. 
For our troubles The Bentley provided us with a Complimentary Bottle of Red Wine & Boxed Chocolates and Complimentary breakfast at their ROOFTOP restaurant.The sites were amazing from the rooftop overlooking Queensboro bridge. But the breakfast wasn't so great, we ate "Bentley Omelets" but the eggs were runny, but the pancakes and cinnamon toast was passable. The Front desk provides print out of near by dinning, our favorite was "Burger Heaven". I'm not quite sure if I'd recommend Bentley to a friend but that was just our experience.

title: “love the kimptons”
text:
as usual a great experience with a kimpton hotel, the chain has become our preferred choice of hotels when traveling. Great decor, staff, rooms, service , etc
This is an excellent location in westwood, very close to most parts of LA and less than 20 min from LAX.

title: “Great Location”
text: This was a great location for a hotel! The rooms are a little small. As I was getting ready each morning I would constantly be hitting something with my elbows. The view on the other hand was STUNNING! absolutely perfect! The staff was courteous and helpful

title: “Great location, but had some problems with the staff.”
text: My family and I were in town for vacation. The location of this hotel was PERFECT! We were literally across the street from Alamo Plaza and within walking distance from the Riverwalk, La Villita, the mall, etc. When we arrived, at check-in time, we were informed that the rooms were not ready because "it was a full house the night before and some people didn't leave on time." My family and I were forced to wait in a lobby full of people while they finished cleaning rooms. After a long drive, this was not the way we wanted to start our vacation. When we finally got checked-in, the room was big enough for my entire family and provided an adequate place to stay after a long, hot day in Texas. The breakfast wasn't spectacular, but served our needs and it was free. The staff was a bit unresponsive to our needs, though. We informed them on the second day of our stay that our TV didn't work properly and it was never fixed. We also went a few times to the Market to buy items that were out and never restocked. My husband even asked if there was any more bottles of wine and the clerk told him, "Yes, but it's in a room way in the back." No effort was made to ever get that bottle for us. Overall, this hotel suited our needs and I probably would stay here again, but you really need to keep on top of the staff if you want anything resolved.

title: “Loved San Jose, Hated this Hotel”
text: All I can say..... is read the reviews and don’t stay here. What a dump. The people in the office were down right rude, our room looked ok at first but when I went to take a shower it had black mold in the corners and on the wall over the shower. The grout in the tile floor was filthy. I booked the room for 3 people and I only got two sets of towels. When I tried to ask for another set, the gal who was cleaning didn't speak any English, but a least she smiled. There were holes in the walls, blood stains on the side of the mattress. The blankets on the beds had cigarette burns in them. Light fixtures were broken. The window had no screen on it. If this represents Travelodge then they have truly gone down hill. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Superb value”
text: Very impressed with the hotel on a recent stay. The hotel is well located close to the centre, and includes many amenities including a well equipped gym, attached restaurants, an inclusive breakfast, and large clean rooms. Also, the staff are very helpful. Cannot be beaten for the price.

title: “Good location, tiny space”
text: This hotel is in a good location. It is easy to access the subway from here. The walk to Times Square is also very short. It is right across the street from the Port Authority, which caused our driver (from the airport) to warn us that it can be a little dangerous at times. We were fine throughout our stay. The lobby is bright and clean. Everything about the hotel is tiny (which is common in NYC). The rooms were very small (and the air conditioner was LOUD). The hallways and elevators were small. The breakfast room was the worst. There was no room to move and it had a poor setup. The only coffee station was in the corner and it could accommodate just one person at a time. This led to a line being formed, which further bottlenecked to room. Overall, breakfast was not a relaxing environment. However, everything else was fine. All we really did in the hotel was sleep and shower. We were out all day and night, so all we really needed was a place to sleep and this hotel was fine for that. It is certainly not a luxury hotel or a place you just want to hang around in for any length of time. There is a nice bar on the roof of the hotel. Young people were lined up down the street to get in to the place. We went up there one night, but could not get anyone to take our order. I guess the waitresses only wanted to wait on young men. My group of four girls was totally ignored. We left after 20 minutes and went to the Blue Ruin right around the corner. The was way less pretentious. We were served right away.

title: “Go to the Sohotel instead - do not stay here!”
text:
I strongly advise anyone not to stay here. I read previous reviews before booking and most mentioned clean/good location. Location is good for downtown and if clean is an overpowering smell of bleach that never dies then maybe yes!
Booked for three nights. First night noise was awful with staff going up and down creeky stairs/slamming doors constantly. Second night we were woken at 11pm by a member of staff coming into our room using a key and without knocking - maybe hoping we weren't there?! A few hours later I was woken by boiling water gushing out of the raditor onto my bed. 
Complained about both incidents in the morning to a very unapologetic and arogant guy on reception. Asked for a partial refund and told if we left all our details with them they may be able to claim something on their insurance eventually. 
On our way to the Sohotel (stay here if you want a decent budget hotel) overheard man on reception laughing with colleague re a guest who had lost his wallet. Maybe a night time intruder?!

title: “Never Again...”
text:
Will I stay here.
Upon check in, the staff was rude & unwelcoming. The room appered to be "clean". However, the coffe pot had a molded used coffee pod still in it. Yuck.
There was VERY MINIMAL hot water & it took 20 min. or so for the tub to fill.
The pool & hot tub were unavailable/ someone had thrown up in it.
The house cleaning staff knocks but doesn't wait for an anwer before entering the room. With three small children...this was a huge issue because they could have gotten out while my daughter was in the shower. It happened not once but twice! So when we called the front desk to let them know the lady actually said to me," What do you want me to do about it?" I found the staff here very unfriendly & not customer service oriented. Stay at your own risk. :(

title: “What a Gem!”
text:
My fiance and I stayed at the Dana this August. I was a little concerned because I had read the hotel was under renovation but you would never know it. I called to make sure I booked a renovated room and was assured that I did. From the moment we arrived we just loved it. The staff was great. Everyone we encountered was so nice and would stop whatever they were doing to help us. The firefly restaurant is really cute. We went there for breakfast each morning. It can be a little pricey but well worth it. We didn't get the chance to try their other restaurant but heard it was good also. 
About our room..if possible book a Bay View Room as we did. The view is terrific!! The rooms are very spacious, the bathroom is BEAUTIFUL and you have a balcony facing the bay.
The housekeeping service was on point and the property itself is super clean. 
The hotel's location is great too. Seaworld is literally walking distance. They are very close to Mission Beach which is really nice and downtown is like a 10 minute car ride. Parking is $12 per day at the hotel which we were a little surprised by. We live in NYC so we aren't complaining but we just weren't expecting it. 
My fiance and I both agree we would stay here again. It isn't ideal for young single people but for couples and families it is perfect. Can't wait to go back.

title: “Perfect staff and location”
text: The staff was outgoing and friendly with an obvious desire to please. Our room had a wonderful view of the city. Bathroom a bit small, but no surprise for NY hotels. The hotel was sparkling clean, well appointed and suited perfectly for a weekend getaway to the city. The mid-town location was perfect since we were going both up and downtown. Easy to get to a variety of subway stops, restaurants and galleries.

title: “Great Location, Good Hotel”
text:
Location! Location! Location!
Very good little hotel just a block from the Inner Harbor, and 2 blocks from the Convention Center. You can easily walk to the Power Plant food and entertainment area, and to Camden Yards for Orioles games. Plenty of restaurants within an easy walk from a Subway shop across the street to a McCormick & Schmicks just a block away.
The room decor is dated and worn. The carpet in my room had lost most of its color in the well traveled areas. The bath was nicely appointed. Though small, the room had a mini-fridge, microwave, wet bar, coffee maker, and larger flat panel tv. The rooms are clean. No issue there...just well worn. The street noise in my room was nearly intolerable. I was on the 2nd floor facing Pratt Street, and I was awaken each of the 3 nights by street noise. My sleep quality there was very poor and was a real drag on this trip.
The complementary breakfast buffet on the top floor (Cloud Club) was excellent with wide and tasty choices. Free wireless internet was included with the room.
The staff was personable with what little I interacted with them. I found the business center off the lobby useful for printing boarding passes for flights.
I got the room at a very good rate through a bid on a 3 star hotel on Priceline. Great bang for the buck.
Other than the street noise issue, I really like this place for visiting downtown Baltimore.

title: “Good location”
text: Location to the river walk, mall, food, and the Alamo was great.

title: “Great staff and great suite for the money”
text: Just wanted to take the time to say that this little hotel exceeded all my expectations. Booked a standard was upgraded to a suite and it was wonderful. The staff were very courteous of the area. The only draw back for me was the location. as it was not centrally located as I suspected. The hotel was renovated about two years ago and has a new feel I will stay here again next year. My job requires internet access and this was the first hotel that I stayed at that I did not have to struggle to simply utilize the net.

title: “I didn't know San Francisco could be so easy.”
text: Ours was a very brief stay - just one night. Drove into the easy parking, marveled at the wonderful location, and then set off on a comfortable and delightful walking tour of the area. I too, agree completely with all the good things said before me. I didn't know SF could be so easy - for price, for transportation, and for comfort and security. Oh yes, we were there on the night the Giants won the World Series. It was fun to stand on the balcony and watch the celebrations in the friendly neighborhood and when I was tired I went into my room, closed the door, and not a sound could be heard.

title: “Great breakfast, but confusing layout and dated rooms.”
text:
As a typical "conference" hotel the layout was very confusing. Were were upgraded to a large pool-side room with full window view, but due to the lack of clear signage or directions we literally had to walk around the entire hotel to find our room.
While the room was large, the decor was dated and worn. The room was also musty smelling, and the corridor halls smelled like bug spray. The strangest thing was the TINY bathroom with a corner-mounted toilet and awkward pocket door. One of the worst hotel bathrooms I've ever seen. 
Where the room lacked in quality, the staff made up for in service and friendliness. Everyone was great. In the morning we had free breakfast vouchers, but upgraded for a few bucks more to the All American breakfast. What a treat! The hotel has one of the best breakfast selections and varieties I've ever seen! The waitstaff was friendly and attentive. 
Overall, If you are loyal to the Hilton brand as we are and need a hotel next to the airport and not there for a conference I would choose another Hilton family hotel near there...there's one just down the street that has free cookies.

title: “Great location and nice hotel.”
text: Stayed here for two days and found the location to be a good one for easy access to shopping, the waterfront, Faneuil hall and the freedom trail. Not too far from Boston commons. Had a great time. Would stay here again!

title: “First class hotel, fabulous views, and attentive staff. 5 stars!!”
text: We had our small wedding reception at the Hotel Commonwealth and all of our guests stayed there (including us) as well. The food, which was provided by the neighboring Eastern Standard, was phenomenal, as were the staff, who ensured that everything went smoothly throughout our ceremony and reception without being intrusive in any way. All other staff--from valets to reservations to bellhops--were exceptionally friendly and helpful, even with our multiple special requests. The room in which we stayed had a lovely view of Kenmore Square (we heard that some of the other rooms offered spectacular views of Fenway Park!). The room was impeccably clean, beautifully decorated, and had a palatial bathroom with a huge spa tub and well-lit make-up table. Although we were in the middle of all the action that Boston has to offer, the room was almost completely sound proof and the curtains blacked out 99% of the outside lights--we slept like babies. Overall, we'd highly recommend this hotel for a small event or for a Boston vacation. It truly deserves all of the accolades it has received from various travel mags.

title: “Average in all aspects”
text: This hotel room is average in every respect. From the front desk personnel, to the room itself it's all just okay. If you're looking for something special or memorable this is NOT the place for you! (i'd suggest you spend an extra $40 dollars and stay somewhere plush like the Pan Pacific) But if your objective is an affordable, safe, clean hotel room, without the frills, the Executive Hotel Pacific may be just the place for you.

title: “Good Hotel in Good Neighborhood”
text:
This is a very nice hotel with very courteous staff. The reservations agent who originally took my reservation, the valet, the doorman, the desk clerk were all polite and efficient. The only staff problem was the concierge. There was never anyone at the concierge desk the entire weekend.
My room was on the 18th floor and I was assigned a handicapped accessible room (which I didn't require but as they were sold out it was the only king bedded room available). It was a very large room with 3 windows. The bathroom counter was huge. I've never been a fan of the handicap tub, so my review of it would be biased. Everything in the room was definitely new. The room was definitely sound proof. When I opened the windows, the noise below was quite loud.
The hotel is in a very nice neighborhood near a college. The Prudential Center, a high-end shopping center was just down the block, where you can catch the green line of "T" or the subway. Boylston Street had many nice shops and was a block away. There were a few fast food restaurants a block down on Massachusetts Avenue. Copley Square was a few blocks down and I could see Fenway Park from my room, but I never had time to make it there. There was so much to do nearby.
Several tours leave from the hotel. Even for Boston, I thought they were quite expensive. As a matter of fact, a lot of the area is expensive, but so are most of the cities along the Northeast.
If in Boston again, I would definitely return.

title: “Great hotel with some "hot spot" atmosphere”
text: Stayed for three nights during NY Fashion Week. Really enjoyed comfort, view, friendliness and that kind of "hip" atmosphere. Good location with Apple store just around the corner :-) Only downside is the breakfast service: takes ages once you have ordered. In case you are really (!) hungry, go for pancaces! All in all, it is a super hotel with 24h wlan and nice interior design. Will be again my hotel for the next NY trip! Thanks!

title: “What's up with the bad reviews??”
text:
Stayed 2 nights July 24, 25. 
I read so many bad reviews. There is NO hotel we found this nice for the money. I am so thankful we chose this hotel. Yes, it's an older hotel. I felt like we were in a luxury resort. Our room was on the side facing the traffic.... Shut the door, you can't hear anything.
 Yes, they even have crooked toilets.... On purpose. Who wants to hug that wall ?? Great idea.
Staff was great and extremely helpful.
 The only thing negative I would say is that if you eat breakfast in the hotel and in a hurry. Don't eat there.
This hotel was beyond our expectations. Thank you Beverly Garland.
We even tried to come back the following weekend....No rooms available.

title: “Nice enough for the price”
text: We stayed July 2012. The service was wonderful, the beds were fabulous, the bathroom was small, but sufficient. Only (minor) issues we had was not enough towels, back of battery compartment on tv remote going missing, and coffee not restocked. Each only took one phone call to resolve, so we were very pleased. Yes the location is a good mile walk from the touristy areas on riverwalk, but we enjoy walking. Yes the parking fee of $18/day is a bummer, and the parking lot does fill up quick, but just think of the price for the room when considering this fee. We did not eat at the hotel, so no comment available on the food. Overall, we were satisifed for the price.

title: “Fabulous hotel in perfect location”
text: Spent a few days at the Amalfi and enjoyed every moment. The decor and service were both womderful. Highly recommend this hotel to everyone.

title: “Dissapointed”
text:
Upon arrival we found that our room was on the 7th floor. In my booking I had requested a low floor room. 
There are two elevators. The one was out of service and the other one is ancient and very slow. I discovered it also stops at floors where noone has pressed a button. 
We stood a good five minutes waiting for the lift to arrive and finally ended up walking up 7 flights of stairs, carrying our heavy suitcase!
The TV only had 3 channels on it, so we had to call someone up to reset it.
The room was so hot (and no way to control the heat), that we had to have the window open about 12 inches all night...this was in Feb.! It was still uncomfortably warm all night.
The pillows were lumpy.
The water during a shower kept going from hot to cold to very hot back to cold!
Overall, not a plesant experience.
Not recommended, except for the cheaper price!

title: “Extremely Pleasant !”
text: Great, comfortable, well maintained hotel. Stayed here for 7 nights on business. Always welcomed here by the friendly staff who always go that extra mile to ensure your stay is comfortable. The room is spacious, clean and comfortable. Bed is changed daily as you'd expect, but the room is also thrououghly cleaned daily as well. The staff are the biggest asset here, its impossible not to smile and chat with each of them as you meet with them. Domingo, John, Carlos and Jose are exceptional. I was always greeted with a smile and a chat at breakfast, lunch and dinner. Taken out wherever I wanted within 5 miles on the hotel shuttle - nowhere was a pain, always with pleasure. I really cannot fault this place. The staff are really passionate about what they do and that's what makes this place 5 stars.

title: “Terrible customer service, hotel has a bad smell, stay away!!!”
text:
This is the first time I have written a complaint regarding a poor stay at any of the many hotels I frequent. I arrived at the Hampton Inn Houston-Hobby Airport on 03-15-2011 around 3:00pm. Upon my arrival the employee at the counter (later determined to be Carlos Sierra, the assistant General Manager) said nothing to me and just stared at me. I told I was checking in and he assigned me my room. He seem annoyed by my presence, but that did not bother me as I understand we all have our good and our bad days. Upon my arrival in my room on the 3rd floor, I noticed a very rank smell permeating the room. The smell was a wet, moldy type of smell. I looked at the air conditioner unit and saw that the unit was filthy and covered in some green and white moldy substance. I went down to the front counter and spoke to Mr. Sierra again. I explained my problem with the room to which he responded that the only other room he had was on the smoking floor. I asked if he had a maintenance person that could come take a look at the AC unit in hopes he might be able to clean it so I could stay in my room. Mr. Sierra stated he did and said he would send someone right up. I went back up to my room and waited about half an hour (during which no one arrived, granted it was a short amount of time). I then decided that even if they could fix the unit I didn’t feel the smell would leave the room for some time. I went back downstairs and re-contacted Mr. Sierra and asked again if he had another room. Mr. Sierra said a room on the first (non-smoking) floor had just come available. I accepted and went to that room. Upon arriving at that room it smelled of smoke and I saw 2 used cigarettes in an ash tray on the desk. I again went back to Mr. Sierra who at this point looked very aggravated with me. I explained that the room smelled very strongly of smoke and there were two cigarettes in the room. He then told me he had no other rooms and just stared at me. I asked when or if more rooms were coming available and his response was “well I might have one in a few hours, if you give me your cell phone I will call you if one opens up.” I explained that I did not want to wait for a few hours to see if one would come available and asked if there were any other Hiltons in the area. Mr. Sierra told me there was a full Hilton near the airport. I had to ask Mr. Sierra if he would call the Hilton to see if there was a room available for me. He called the Hilton, never explaining the situation to them, then told me they were full and I would have to find another hotel myself if I wanted to move. Mr. Sierra never apologized, never tried to reconcile the issue and never even went to the rooms with me to check on the issues I raised. After calling the one Hilton and discovering it was full, Mr. Sierra just stared and me and offered nothing else. I called the Hilton Diamond customer service line and they were able to find me a room at the Hilton at the University of Houston campus (a beautiful and well-staffed hotel, but one that was 6 miles further away from the airport). The diamond customer service agent was polite and helpful but the best price I could get at the room was still $22 more than my reservation at the Hampton Inn, plus $15 parking. These are incidental costs but ones I should not have had to cover since I was moving due to issues at the Hampton Inn (with the so called 100% guarantee).
I understand things happen, guests smoke in rooms they aren’t supposed to, air conditioners break, things happen…but what should not happen is a total break down and indifference to customer service. I felt as if I was bothering and annoying Mr. Sierra and to me this is completely unsatisfactory. 
I would not stay at this hotel again.

title: “Won't be going back.”
text: You are told there is room service and charges can be added to your room. Tried 3 times to do that but the manager of restaurant refuses and hotel management hasn't informed the front guest. Bathroom wreaked of mold. A/C unit was broke on arrival. You cannot role under the accessible sink - counter edge is too low. TV reception is poor as well.

title: “Awesome conference and experience!”
text: I stayed at the Catamaran for a conference. The grounds are beautifu. The birds and animals are awesome. I was upgraded to a suite with a view of the bay. I could not have asked for a better room or view. Everyone at the resort was more than helpful and friendly. Loved this place!

title: “Second stay even better”
text: This was our second visit to the Hampton Inn Kearny-Mesa. We found it a couple of years ago while trying to find a place near Santee to visit my niece. I prefer Hilton hotels in general - they seem to be the quietest- and this one was right off of HWY 163, one of the more pleasant freeways to drive in San Diego. Both times the hotel was extremely clean from lobby to rooms, the entire staff - front desk to housekeeping, was professional, courteous, and helpful. We had two rooms, both times the staff was extremely accomodating in getting them close together. The parking lot was full, but we heard very little noise from other guests. The front lobby has been remodeled and is a cool place to hang out. We didn't do breakfast but my mom got her coffee and mingled with the morning crowd off of the lobby. While the location seems a bit "seedy" we found quite a few restaurants in the near vicinity and even tried the one next door at the Ramada, Proud Mary's, which had delicious pub food. All in all, this hotel is one we will be returning to, as it's location is fantastic for our needs.

title: “Great Place!!”
text: Great hotel along with excellent customer service and a terrific front desk staff. I was totally impressed with this hotel.

title: “Basic accomodations”
text: No frills here, but a basic reliable hotel experience. The rooms are on the small side and mine was quite dark due to a single small window, so there wasn't much natural light. The bathroom was small and cramped. The room was clean and the bed comfortable. The hotel features an evening happy hour with hot food (nachos, hot dogs), snacks and complimentary beer/wine or limited cocktails (max of 3 drinks). The free hot breakfast was average. These are the same things you get at an Embassy Suites or Staybridge, but the rooms here are much smaller and somewhat cheaper. Staff were friendly and helpful. A good value in a convenient location just off I-465 at Michigan Rd.

title: “Great shopping location”
text:
My husband and I thought this would be a fun hotel to try with our 7 and 10 year old daughters. It is a great location to shop Michigan Avenue and the Northbridge Shops. It is a bit far to walk to Millennium Park in the August heat. We arrived a 3 to find our room was not ready - which I always find annoying. We got snack chits to use in the restaurant, which was better than just indoor pool passes. 
Our room was ready at 4 after sharing a DELICIOUS flatbread and pretzel nuggets with dipping sauce. The room was very nice and clean with 2 queen beds. The only thing that was odd was the bathroom door that slides like a barn door. This does not give adequate privacy, if you are not with the closest of friends or family (ie: you can be in total view while sitting on the toilet).
A nice touch is the complimentary "wine hour" in the lobby from 5 -6, where red, white and sangria were offered. The indoor pool was slightly less inviting - more of a lap pool than a pool that kids would enjoy splashing around in. The outdoor terrace adjacent to the pool was quite nice, but no snack or beverage service was offered.
Overall, I think it was a good value, as we paid $159 and comfortably accommodated 4 of us in a room. There are quite a few dinner options to walk to, which is nice as well.

title: “Small Bathrooms otherwise a good hotel”
text:
Stayed three nights in May.Vibey hotel with friendly service. Very good location to access the museums and I would recommend it for both Business and leisure. 
One problem is that they the should give you free internet in the rooms as it feels like the are desperate to get more cash out of you. Most good service hotels give you free internet!

title: “Excellent service”
text: We stayed at the Eldon last week 3/28 thru 4/2. We had a fantastic experience at the Eldon. The service was outstanding from the staff. Great restaurant recommendations, metro planning on overall the most helpful staff in any hotel we have ever stayed. Although the neighborhood was a bit seedy, the metro station was extremely convenient. We would stay here again.

title: “Slightly Creepy”
text:
This place had a very strange layout. You had to walk for what seemed forever to a room in the back of the property. The parking was also very strange. The room was drab, and no matter how many lights I turned on, it was still dark. The bedding did not smell fresh, and the bathroom was dirty. For the price it's OK, but I felt dirty after spending a night there.
On the positive side, it is very close to LAX and the car rental return areas for Dollar and Enterprise, and offered the lowest rate in the area.

title: “A classy choice I'd return to”
text: There are SOO many options of hotels to choose from in Chicago, especially in the epicenter of the Loop and Michigan Avenue. The Amalfi hotel located on Kinzie street a block from the Chicago River and next door to the Trump tower (that is STILL under construction at the time of this posting) is in a perfect starting-out-point for a nice walk to explore the urban landscape. Millennium park, Michigan Avenue, the Loop, its all within an easy walking distance from the Amalfi. Being an independently owned hotel, the Amalfi is in a position to show off it's individuality. The rooms are impeccable, a daily complimentary cocktail lounge opens on one of the floors at 5:30pm. Serving hors d'oeuvres and their signature Amalfi-tini, amongst soothing mood music, this is a must see before heading out for a night on the town. The rooms are plush, luxurious, and comfortable. The bathrooms are fully stocked with Aveda-brand products. I couldn't find anything I didn't like about this property; I'd recommend it to anyone. Probably not the most kid-friendly, but for couples it's def. a must.

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Omni for 1 night early in April. It was a local getaway splurge, so we went for a junior suite with the "Night on the Town" package. It is an expensive hotel, but the package offers a better value, including dinner at McCormick & Schmicks and valet parking for much less than the standard rate for the room only.
Our junior suite was a true suite with a separate living room with couch, desk, TV, etc. divided by a sliding door from the large bedroom with a view of the Coronado Bay Bridge. We've stayed in many so-called suites that were simply slightly larger rooms - not the case here! The bath had none of the problems described in earlier reviews - it was large, with a separate tub and shower enclosure and a regular door. We had no noise problems what so ever!
As mentioned in other reviews, the location is great, especially for our purpose, attending the Padres opening game! The bellstaff and front desk staff we interacted with were very friendly and helpful. The food and the service in the restaurant were excellent.
Also as already mentioned, definitely sign up for the "Select Guest" program. Turndown service is automatic with the program and we also enjoyed the complimentary morning beverages and late checkout which enabled us to stay until just prior to the ballgame.

title: “I would stay here again in a heartbeat”
text: I selected this hotel based on location and its high ratings from other travellers and I wasn't disappointed. The hotel is perfectly situated in the Rush Street area and close to the Magnificent Mile - the room was comfortable and clean and the bed was probably the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever slept in. The bathroom was large with an awesome shower. Hotel staff were incredibly friendly and helpful - all in all a fabulous experience - and as someone who travels a lot for work and pleasure I could find nothing to fault at all. I will stay there again next time I am in Chicago. Would prefer free internet and cheaper parking, but these were minor downsides.

title: “Perfect boutique hotel with excellent service”
text:
I just returned from a fabulous three (3) night stay at The Lenox Hotel (Mar.28-31). I took the lead on booking our hotel stay and chose this hotel after reading numerous positive reviews on various sites - I was not disappointed. 
Check In: I had booked two "Classic Queen" rooms and requested that they be on the same floor. We arrived about an hour and a half early and were accommodated for check-in immediately. However, one of the two rooms was not yet available, but rather than asking us to wait, we were provided with an upgraded room on the same floor. This is always a crowd-pleaser! 
Rooms: I found the beds incredibly comfortable. The rooms were very clean, and came with a mini-fridge (stocked with free water). The upgraded room we received was quite spacious while the "Classic Queen" was fairly cozy (read: small but not cramped, with the exception of the bathroom which was very tiny!). The hotel also had a list of items available for request - i.e. candy/treats; meds (nominal fee of $0.25); toiletries or other items people may have forgotten to pack (i.e. nail file, clean nail polish, playing cards, loufah, etc). 
Customer Service: From check-in to check-out, we felt like welcomed guests and appreciated the genuine service from all hotel staff. Justin at concierge was particularly helpful to our group, and we appreciated his service.
Food: We didn't order any room service but there was coffee & tea out in the mornings in the lobby; as well as a large bowl of bananas at the front-desk. 
Location: This was my second time in Boston so I knew I wanted to stay in Back Bay. The hotel is easily in walking distance to many great attractions. For perspective, it took us about 35-40 minutes to walk home from TD North Garden one night - and that was at a very leisurely pace...and without cutting through the park. 
Misc:
+ I don't know what they're pumping into the air, but the lobby always had a very nice scent!
+ Aveda products in-room were a nice touch
+ Turn-down service at night with chocolates
+ Free wireless internet
To wrap this up, it was a great hotel with excellent customer service. I'd recommend this to anyone planning a trip to Beantown!

title: “Very poor”
text:
Had to walk through crowded noisy bar to reception no lobby
Lift noises al night
Problems with bill -discount promised due to initial overcharge had to be requested
Room Carpet and furniture stains 
Stayed on 24 th floor
Gym okay
Absolutely nothing special about this hotel
Very poor value

title: “5 Star !”
text: Wonderful, comfortable rooms and very quiet. Never heard any noises in the hall or in other rooms.

title: “Perfect location”
text: We couldn't have picked a better spot. Not only was it on the riverwalk, (which was terrific) but we could easily walk to the Alamo, the tower, everything in San Antonio. The neighborhood felt safe and clean while right inside the business district. Price was decent, breakfast was simple but fine for a hotel breakfast. The nightly 'snack' would be a fine meal for kids but if your traveling in this area you surely want to hit one of the other great restaurants. We used it for an early snack then just went out for hors d'voirs later. Rooms were great, though ours didn't have much of a view.

title: “Not fancy, but clean and in a awesome location!”
text: I was not expecting much after reading some of the reviews, but we were pleasantly surprised. Very reasonable price, and the location is unbeatable! Right at Market and Powell. Near everything. The room was on the top floor at the end of the hall. It was a little dated, but clean, with a flat screen TV and upgraded mattress and bedding. There was a desk and a dresser and a big closet. The bathroom was tiny, but updated with granite counters and new fixtures. I will stay here again. We arrived early and the staff was nice, took our bags and made sure we had directions to where we were going. We walked to AT&T Park for an afternoon baseball game and when we returned our stuff and room were ready for us. Check out was a breeze. We weren't there for the happy hour coctails and didn't eat the complimentary breakfast, so I can't comment on them. Overall, I think the Powell is a great hotel value.

title: “Overpriced and noisey!”
text: Spent one night here in Room 419. Room was average but the noise was horrible. Trash truck at 5am under our window sounded like it was in the hallway. Windows so dirty you couldn"t see out of them. Bell and Valet staff were super nice but the front desk staff leave alot to be desired. When I complained about the noise, all I got was a" um sorry".

title: “Amazing location - cool boutique stay in a big big part of the City”
text: I'm currently staying here on a business trip but will be back for personal (and business). I got a great corner room. Very clean, courteous staff, cozy feel but next to the major attractions of Rockefeller Center and Radio City. The East Village is my fab part of the city but this is where I'll stay when needing to be uptown.

title: “Clean, Friendly, great location for getting around on transit”
text: Stayed here three nights last week with my teenage son. Very clean. Desk staff friendly and helpful. We purchased the three day Muni passes for $21 apiece and were able to catch buses right outside the hotel, and cable cars and trolley cars a few blocks away. It was very convenient location for getting to all the downtown sites, Alcatraz cruise departure pier, Haight Ashbury, and fisherman's wharf. Chinatown and Union Square both walkable from hotel. Complimentary continental breakfast of pastries and fruit included. Requested a quiet room on a high floor as I am a light sleeper. We were on 7th floor, and even so, the evening street noise bothered me. So bring along some earplus. I would recommend to others and definitely stay here again myself.

title: “HIGHLY recommended - fantastic service great location!”
text:
We have just arrived back in the UK and miss the Cassa already!! The staff Abraham P, Roger, Henry L, Patrick P, Nick S, Miguel E, Alby M, Nari S and co were absolutely welcoming and made our stay memorable. I cant stress how fantastic the service was here - best service ive received. Although the restaurant is still being built - this did NOT hinder our stay at all. The hotel is situated in a great location - mintues away from time square, 5th avenue and other great attractions! We will be coming back to this hotel for sure!! We thank the staff for everything - we miss you all and hope to visit very soon.
Kindest Regards - Shreya and Parvinder

title: “One Of The Best Hotel's In New York”
text: My husband and I spent our 1 year anniversary in New York. From the minute we stepped into to Flatotel we were treated like royalty. The room was beautiful with a private balcony. When we walked into the room there was a bottle of wine in the room as a anniversary gift. We felt very special and will definitely be staying there whenever we're in New York.

title: “Front desk staff needs customer service skills”
text: Location is great if your an Elvis fan, a nearby restruant will pick you up free in a pink limo for meals which are excellent. Shuttle service van drivers are great but would have been nice if this was a free service downtown. Bartender was great but house keeping was lacking and front desk service was very poor. The Days in down the street which we stayed for 2 nights before the Heartbreak for 3 was much better service, nicer pool area and cheaper.

title: “This hotel has deteriorated”
text:
In the past I have always stayed here and it has been very good. Now it has changed. The bathroom had no soap. I had to request it be brought. The room cards repeatedly do not work and it requires you go back to the front desk to get a new card. This happened everytime I left the room. The wireless connection is spotty and slow and costs extra. The helpfulness and friendliness of the staff has deteriorated.
The location is great.
I will not pay the prices they charge to stay here again.

title: “Great Boutique Hotel”
text: I loved the location of the hotel; the comfort of the beds and the overall atmosphere. The breakfast was really good--not just your average continental breakfast. The rooms were small but comfortable--it was an older hotel that had been redone very nicely. The location couldn't have been any better; right across the street from Union Station and the Old Red Courthouse on the other corner; close to West End and all the great restaurants.

title: “I was very disappointed with the Staff!”
text: I couldn't be more disappointed with the staff they were very unprofessional rude people! I will not refer anyone at Days Inn.

title: “Good Value”
text:
Clean hotel by the airport with surprisingly spacious rooms. The price is good compared to the surrounding airport hotels, and you are right by the Interstate highway which runs right through Philadelphia, giving you a fifteen or twenty minute drive to downtown.
Service could have been friendlier, and there is no restaraunt in the hotel, but there is a Ruby Tuesday's across the parking lot that is pretty good, and other hotels in the compound have places to eat as well.

title: “Everything you want for a visit to NYC”
text:
We booked this hotel from the reviews on Trip Advisor and are so glad we did. A small but smart lobby housed a number of friendly and knowledgeable staff, once we were given our room card we couldn't wait to find out what floor we were on, I had e-mailed ahead asking for a high corner room, BINGO!! top floor corner room with views of the East river and the Chrysler Building.
The room was big and clean and the kitchenette and desk area made it bigger. The massive bed was comfy and the air-con worked a treat. Had e-mailed ahead for a bag of toiletries and a I-pod walking guide, neither were in the room on arrival as promised but a quick phone call rectified this, bath robes were also provided on request at no charge.
 **** NEWS FLASH **** the TV's that so often get a mention on TA are due to be upgraded to flat screens next month!! They still charge for internet in the rooms but it is free in the lobby. There was washing and drying facilities down-stairs and an ironing board and iron in the room.
 The hotel is a short walk to the Empire State Building, the Chrysler Building and Grand Central Station a bit further away and we found that even Times Square was walkable. The Barking Dog next door does room service and we ate there twice, perfectly decent meals each time.
The hotel is in just the right spot, walking distance to pretty much everywhere as you can get the tube and taxi to everywhere else. It was in a quite area with a couple of deli's for supplies. Already recommended the hotel and would definitely stay there again.

title: “Pure charity - practice tolerance”
text:
I traveled together with my students and colleagues and stayed here 1 week, This apartments are a charity. And if it was a true business, then you would be paying at least the double. The rooms are much better than dorms, in my opinion. You share a shower and a restroom with other 2 or 3 rooms staying 2-3 people in each. If your "roommates" are polite and easygoing, then it is just perfect. There is a stove, fridge in some rooms or a shared fridge, a PC with internet connection. There is one locker in the room, and you can lock your door if needed, except for the rooms facing fire exit.
If you consider we only paid 17 USD + tax for our stay in double or triple rooms, means 34 - 51 USD + tax a room, it is pure charity. Thanks to the people keeping and running this place.
The neighborhood is very safe and quiet compare to downtown however I still recommend a room on the second floor and up and facing 73rd street instead of York av. 
If you talk with the staff in a friendly way then you will get a positivity in return, otherwise they are too busy to be friendly with everyone in 120 rooms :-) They are sure helpful at anytime.
If you have a lot to do in downtown then I suggest buying a metro card with unlimited use, that would save both time and money, which together would compensate staying slightly outside downtown, still very central.
If still anything goes slower than you might have expected, please remember that this is pure charity and you should practice tolerance. I liked truly the people I met. I would return, no question on that.

title: “Extra's prove costly”
text: We stayed at this hotel for the last three nights of our three week trip to the US. There is a Maritime theme throughout the hotel including the guest rooms and this makes it somewhat different I guess from the usual hotels. The room was clean and comfortable. Prior to arriving at the hotel we has telephoned them to ask if we could have some packages delivered to the hotel as this was the only place we intended staying three nights and they readily agreed. I was somewhat suprised however to see an acceptance charge for each package on my bill when I came to checkout. I was also suprised to be told that the computers provided for guest use onto the internet wold be charged at $6 dollars per fifteen minutes. Prior to arriving here we had stayed in various Holiday Inn's, Best Western's and Hampton Inn's, all of which were excellent value and gave free guest internet access. A nice hotel, well located, but beware of the extra's

title: “Great experience, Great location”
text: We took my wife's parents to mark their 60th wedding anniversary. The Casablanca is like having a home on the edge of Times Square. Rather than the typical visit where you drop by Times Square, here we could do a quick look at many different times of the day and night. The 2nd floor "Rick's" is a great place to drop in and warm-up with a cup of tea and make plans for the next trip out on the town. We covered mid-town and lower Manhattan and loved having such a quaint place to return to. The guest rooms were what we needed--a warm, clean place to sleep, not hang out. You are on the doorstep of all that NYC has to offer. We will definitely return again.

title: “Nice hotel .... good price”
text: When I first arrived at the hotel, I wasn't too sure what to expect after reading some of the reviews, and some advice from various travel booksabout the area. It however turned out to be an extremely good choice for a traveller on a budget. The staff were polite, if a little detached, but also helpful if you asked questions - i.e. where was the pay phone? Yes, you can hear the traffic from outside, but then again it's not that different from New York (or London) for that matter. Earplugs will help if you are easily disturbed during the night.The room and bathroom were spotlessly clean, although the safe in the room is chargable at 50cents per day.As for the area, I felt totally safe - I was walking back to the hotel from the Powell Street cable car terminus most nights without any problems. Yes there are a few panhandlers around, but they never bothered me. My tip - just walk with confidence and purpose.If you want breakfast, try "Mel's 50's Diner" on the coner of Van Ness - one block from the Hotel. It's fantastic food, excellent value.Oh and if you stay on halloween, don't be too suprised of you get woken by an improptu performance by an american brass band playing outside the Farrell Bothers Theatre - but only on halloween ;-)Would I stay there again? Yes I would.

title: “Great value!”
text:
We just returned from a very nice overnight stay at this Microtel. My wife and I had traveled around Colorado and wanted a place close to the airport for our last night there. Having never stayed at this brand of hotel, we were a bit apprehensive. I read the reviews on TripAdvisor and rolled the dice.
This Microtel was clean, the staff was wonderful, the area seemed safe, and you couldn't beat the location, if you want to be close to Denver International. We never heard the planes and getting in and out of the airport was a breeze. And, they offered a free continental breakfast, which was average, but just fine for folks who want to grab a free bite and run.
There are numerous nice "chain" restaurants within just a few minutes drive of hotel, but not much else in ways of entertainment/shopping.
If you want a clean room and hotel for a great value near the airport, roll those dice. 
Good traveling!
Hatterasman

title: “Great location for Sports and Nightlife”
text: Spent two nights here (Sat and Sun). Was in town for a Whitesox and Bears game. Hotel was clean and friendly staff. Concierge was helpful. Has a sports bar next to the lobby. Subway entrance outside front door. Had to take subway to both Whitesox game and Bears game. Felt very safe on subway. After the games, hit some sports bars around the hotel. Streets were lively, bars were fun. Felt very safe walking around the area of the hotel, lots of people on both Sat and Sun night. Also, a lot of restaurant choices around the hotel (all different $$ levels). Hotel is a little pricey (190/night plus 15%). Would definitely recommend the hotel for both its cleanliness and location. Did check for bedbugs (like I do everywhere), found none.

title: “Very Cute and Sweet Hotel”
text: this is a very spacaious hotel room that we stayed in . End of the hall , corner junior suite . there was 3 of us and we each had our own bed and our own dresser / table to place / spread out our items . The bathroom was small and needs to be remodeld as well as the pipes that are visable in the corners of the floor along the wall of the room . But other then that it was very clean and comfy bed with minimal improvements needed .

title: “best hotel in Seattle”
text:
I've stayed at a few hotels in Seattle, and this is by far the best. I live here but it's nice to stay somewhere and get away from all the worries at home once in a while. The customer service here is top-notch, the rooms are really nice, the pool area is AMAZING (do NOT forget your swimsuit or swim trunks!) and they have a jag that can take you around the downtown Seattle area. Oh, and ART restaurant has great food. I have never stayed at a FS before, but I think I might just be a convert!
I checked in on a Friday night, since I would be going to a winemaker's dinner at ART restaurant and didn't want to worry about getting home for the night. (And to wind down from a family vacation in the woods during the previous week.) I was checked in quickly (seriously, 2 minutes, tops! And that's probably because we requested a shaving kit, haha) and directed up to the room. On the way to the elevator there was a pitcher of apple cider to drink, and apple rings and a little thing about apples since it's fall and you're in Washington.
The city view room was small, but nice - a bit dim, but clean and with an amazing bathroom! marble everywhere, tv inside the mirror so you can watch from the shower, ridiculously deep bath tub for soaking, and a shower with 2 heads - rainshower and normal, and you could have them both on at once or just one at a time. L'Occitane soap and shampoo, fluffy towels and robes. Heaven! The bed was super comfortable, and I could only barely hear the sounds of the street 8 floors below (the room looked out over the SAM).
I'd heard a lot about the rooftop infinity pool, but didn't get a chance to check it out that night. Instead, I got up early for a swim. Well, we've been having some beautiful late summer weather lately, and I was surprised it was completely empty. Went for a swim and called room service to have breakfast delivered to the pool. YES, that's right. Pool breakfast. I figured if they can bring room service to your room, then why not the pool?! They sent someone down with menus, and sadly he didn't come back for like 10 minutes so we just called up again and told them what we wanted. Swam some more and then had a plate of hot, fluffy lemon ricotta pancakes with sides of lemon curd and blackberry jam, plus a nice big glass of ice water (yay! I hadn't asked, but was going to!) and a side of chicken sausage. Best breakfast I've had in a while - I am definitely going to get this again the next time I stay. $16 well spent!
Really, my only complaint is that parking is $40/day, so we took the bus - I can think of much better things to spend my money on than that. Other than that, this place is just amazing - I think staying there is going to become a a regular occurence. I can't believe I paid even more to stay at the Edgewater recently! I'll just have to stay at the FS more until that is just a faded memory :)

title: “Great, historic hotel, but terrible service”
text:
This place was recommended to me by friends. It is very nice and is probably a historic hotel, but the service is very disappointing. No one attended to my request when I called "0". 
Also, this hotel DOES NOT allow you to bring in your own bottle of alcohol, Something to do with them not wanting to be responsible if anything happens. But a hotel employee told me -- "if we don't see it, we can't stop you!"

title: “Customer Safety is not their concern!!!”
text: My review of the hotel would have been a positive one for my recent stay in washington, dc. That is until I went to breakfast Sunday morning and my wallet was stolen!!!! Although several people stated they saw a strange me the asst gm said "it couldn't be him because he stays here often." I felt violated and the staff of the hilton garden in did nothing to make me feel better. I was told no one had access to the video cameras except the gm and asst gm. I called to speak to the asst gm and was told "I was lied to about there being cameras!!" I really feel there is no concern about how I feel and the safety of its hotel patrons. Please be advised that wallets are stolen from this hotel/restaurant and the staff doesn't seem to care!

title: “Luxery on fishermans wharf!”
text: Loved the rooms, service and location! Two blocks from fishermans wharf! You're right in the middle of it all! Rooms had a great view! Had many nice amenaties. Also near public transit of all types. Wifi included. Overall great stay!!!

title: “Value and a good stay”
text:
It's a perfect location because you're near restaurants. Suites are more than comfortable. Great hot breakfast. They give you discounts for local eateries. Staff are adequate. 
We like this hotel for business trips. Good value and a great breakfast.

title: “Shabby like many Marriotts”
text: Stayed with my wife for a conference. The building is shabby in details: leaking window pans, dents in the bathroom. Common problems for American "un-hospitality" industry. you can't get a real price of a room , taxes etc., they only give you some fantasy number. The more expensive the hotel, the worst is their greed. The two of us stayed in the room with two beds, but there was only one bag of coffee in the room. They save on shower caps. What a shame! Internet access? $12 a day. In every Hamptons we have complimentary bottled water. In Marriott - a small inviting bottle in the room for... $6. We haven't seen an average hotel in the US lately without a complimentary breakfast, and it's unheard of in Europe. Here - fat chance: have you $20 ready, or stay in a long line to Starbucks.

title: “If you have to get snowed in - make sure you're staying at the Rouge!”
text: What a great hotel. We were meant to spend 4 days in Washington, which we had to extend to a week because of bad weather. All the time we were there the streets were knee-deep in snow and most of the city was closed down. And yet it was a really great experience, thanks to the style, quality and wonderful service at this hotel. It was a stylish, comfortable hotel anyway with a good bar serving reasonable food, a hosted free wine hour for guests each day, spacious rooms and pleasant staff. Once we (and others) got snowed in there, they could not have been more helfpul, laying on food at times they didn't normally serve, giving us an excellent rate for the extra nights we had to stay, and generally taking care of us. On top of all this, it's really well located, just a few blocks from the White House and with all of central Washington in easy walking distance. Loved it.

title: “Expensive for what you get”
text:
The location was great and the staff was friendly and helpful.
 As I took some trips in the US, I had to return back to the hotel
two times apart from my first visit.
My first visit I took a double room which it was roomy and comfortable.
My second and third visit I took a single room which it was very small
and the bath tab on my third visit was not clean.

title: “GREAT LOCATION AND FRIENDLY STAFF”
text: I stayed at this hotel twice this summer while relocatiing my daughter to DC. We love the location and convience to great thee metro and great resturants. Love walking the beautiful neighborhood behind the hotel. We plan to stay there every time we visit our daughter.

title: “Very convenient!”
text: My family stayed here one evening because we had an early morning flight. We had to leave the hotel at 6 am. Breakfast was available earlier than the official serving time of 6 am and we were able to eat at about 5:40 am. The room was very spacious, clean and comfortable. The shower was great with extra jets. The shuttle to the airport was very good. When we returned 5 days later, we called the hotel and the shuttle picked us up at the airport within 30 minutes. The cost of the hotel was a good deal since we saved 5 days of parking fees. Highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Very Cheap, and Very Worn”
text:
The rate I got on line ($27.00) should have clued me in, I had a very late arrival at DIA, and needed a place to crash for the night, so I made the reservation on line for a few hours sleep for $27.00.
The carpeting was filthy and VERY stained, a LOT of mildew on the shower curtain, carpeting pulled up in the corners, two holes in the walls, towel rack in bathroom missing (yet one bracket was still there, curtain on window literally half hanging off curtain holder, stained furniture.
(I have included one picture), note the stains on the couch!
This hotel looks more like a weekly rental place.
On the good side, the staff was very friendly.
frankly I am surprised Day's Inn permits to have their name attached to this property, I was very disappointed

title: “Great location!”
text:
We stayed here for the Comicpalooza and got a great deal on rooms for the convention in a hotel that's otherwise pretty pricey. We were able to get our room upgraded to a corner room which has windows on 2 sides, the view was amazing! This hotel is clean, beautiful, huge and in a great location.
We ordered room service once while we were there, it was expensive of course, but fantastic. Our room was clean, the bed was very comfortable. The pool area is also very nice, they have a huge indoor pool on the top floor with a jacuzzi area as well, and an outdoor sundeck with great views of the city. 
Sadly this hotel was booked for the weekend we're planning to go back for the Texas Ren Fair, but I'd stay here again in a heartbeat. Only advice is to look for their specials and packages, you can get some really great deals, but the hotel is worth the extra money!

title: “Great Value”
text:
Two night stay here, suggested by a NYC-based colleague. Paid what I think was a rack rate of $109 per night, and was incredibly impressed by the price/value relationship. Located just two blocks from Union Square, can't beat the location. Front desk clerks were very friendly and helpful. Rooms were small, but a pleasant surprise. Clean, refurbished, nicely appointed -- queen sized bed, small desk with ample light, small couch, smallish bathroom (but clean and new!). 36" or so flat screen on the wall. 
Rate included a very spartan continental breakfast, bagels and cereal for the most part (I didn't partake). The worst part of the place is the elevator, which takes forever to arrive if it's "up" when you're "down" or vice versa. Many times I walked the five flights of stairs to my room. 
All in all, a tremendous value. I would definitely stay there again, especially if traveling solo on business.

title: “Nice Hotel on south Michigan Avenue, great pool!”
text: Spent 5 nights at the Essex Inn. The hotel is in the middle of Michigan Avenue, at about 10-15 min walk from the Art Institute. It takes 30-40 min by wlk to reach the top of North Michigan Avenue and the mall. Quite a long walk to go to the Mc Cormick Convention Center, don't even try it because the bottom part of South Michigan Avenue looks a little bit unsafe. Actually the Essex is located when the Avenue starts to become enjoyable, with some restaurants around (not too many going south, but plenty when heading north). The lobby is basic (I think it is going to be redesigned soon, as far as I understood) - rooms are all right, a little bit outdated (bathroom) but very clean and tidy. On the contrary, the pool is stunning - actually on the 4th floor with a large terrace with a nice view on the lake and the business district - and the gym all right with a small sauna. There is no actual complimentary breakfast - the brasserie in the hotel is ran by another company (a french guy actually), but they can charge directly your room. During my stay the brasserie was just opening and the staff was obviously new in this business - however, everybody was helpful and keen to satisfy you. Overall, it was a nice stay with polite staff in a nicely located hotel with a great pool. I will definitively stay here again in the future.

title: “A true room with a view---can you meet Ms. Liberty from the window”
text:
The marriott is always dependable and this one lives up to it's word too! It's very clean and well-maintained. The staff is friendly and helpful. There is a concierge too that will get you tickets and reservations for dinner. For a few $$ you can upgrade if it's available with a room with a view. You can see the Statue of Liberty from the window! Amazing. The beds are comfortable and you have lots of pillows! 
The restaurant downstairs has a nice hearty breakfast and the hotel is connected to a Starbucks. 
If you want a final nightcap you can get a drink at the bar! Lovely.

title: “great location and very comfortable room and nice staff.”
text: Valet service was a little slow but all other services especially room service was fantastic.

title: “Best hotel in downtown Phoenix”
text: I have stayed in many hotels in downtown Phoenix and the Sheraton is simply the best! When you walk into the lobby, you are amazed by the high-ceilings, marble floors, and open floor plan where a lobby bar is conveniently located. The guest rooms are very comfortable and clean. The fitness center and pool invite you in for a great workout. There is also a nice restaurant in the hotel as well as several right across the street at the Arizona Center. This hotel is not only very welcoming but is also perfectly situated in the heart of downtown Phoenix and is within walking distance of so many restaurants, offices, etc. I highly recommend you check into this hotel!

title: “House keeping”
text: We just met the kindest most helpful lady. Violeta in house keeping started our trip out perfectly.

title: “Average Westin”
text: I was here for a conference and found the hotel wanting. I found the arrangement of the hotel lobby, restaurant, conference area to be confusing. I admit my visit got off to a bad start when I discovered that the toilet in my room was neither clean or flushed when I checked into my room. The next morning when I went to make coffee I discovered that all of the half and half that they leave in rooms was spoiled. These two things made me wondered what else was wrong that I couldn't see.

title: “LOCATION AND HOTEL FABULOUS.................”
text:
I had emailed the hotel before departure, explaining that it was a surprise trip for my husbands 40th birthday to see if we could have a room with a view of Times Square, we were emailed back and told it would be $60 dollars more per room per night, so bearing in mind we had 2 rooms booked we declined.
 Arrival and check in was easy and quick. 
My mum in laws room had a view of the Hudson river and our room had a fantastic view of Times Square and also a lovely bottle of wine chilled for us which was a lovely touch and at no extra cost.
Rooms large, airy, clean and beds comfy. Could hear a bit of honking of taxis and subway but was not a problem.
Location fabulous right on Times Square and central for all attractions most a short walk away.
Staff friendly and very helpful.
Loads of restaurants all around so you are spoilt for choice.
Will defiantly be returning just need to save now............

title: “Stylish but noisy”
text: This is a fashionable boutique-style hotel right at the corner of 26th St and Broadway, so close to Fifth Avenue shopping and an easy walk to Penn Station and Times Square. My room wasn't large but was well appointed with contemporary furniture, including electric drapes controlled from a bedside switch. The bathroom had the tech gimmick of a TV built into the mirror (which I had no interest in, and which, when switched off, meant there was a dark rectangle in the mirror when I was shaving). The shower was a highlight: a combination of overhead rain showerhead and front-on body sprays: you could select either or both with the rotating knob. The main problem with the accommodation was that no amount of flashy technology could conceal the underlying dated infrastructure. The heating was crude: every few minutes it came on with a huge whirr and blasted the room with hot air until it began to feel oppressive, then it switched off again and the temperature dropped away until the cycle was repeated. During the night I switched it off to avoid the noise and the big temperature swings while I was under the covers. But at least the room had heat: the bathroom, on the other hand, was distinctly chilly. It seemed that there was no heating there at all, except when you opened the door to let a little drift in from the room. Hotel staff were very friendly but another annoyance was the restaurant/ bar on the ground floor, where at check-in a band was playing so loudly that I asked for a high-floor room. The receptionist chuckled, obviously knowing exactly what I was talking about, having had to work with it all evening. In summary, a great location and nice fitments in the rooms, but with issues caused partly by their own making and partly by the fact that this is a conversion of an old building.

title: “Phone calls don't mean a thing...”
text:
We've made reservations well in advance, called the hotel twice to confirm it, called them again twice from the airport to inform that our flight was delayed and won't get into San Antonio until 2am, and not to give our room away because we are definately arriving late. We did this to ensure that we're guaranteed a room upon our arrival after reading all the aweful reviews about this hotel, and knew that they will screw-up things if we didn't do so. Apparently, they did; we arrived at the hotel at about 2.30am and learnt that our room was given up. 
Obviously, we weren't too pleased with it considering that we have called 4 times, and none of those calls were taken seriously. They almost sent us over to the 'nearby' Emily Morgan Hotel, but after telling the night-audit manager about how incompetant the agents who answered my 4 phone calls were, informing how the hotel is receiving horrible reviews on various websites, and clearly showing our dissatisfaction of the whole situation that could have been avoided if the staff acted upon the phone calls, they finally gave up a no-show reservation, and handed that room to us.
Other no-nos: [1] When we arrived at the hotel, there were two Hotel Valencia staff arguing and cussing at each other and did not even look at us when we were about to go enter the door; a very nice 1st hand experience and impression. [2] Extremely unhappy with agents who answered the calls, both away and from the hotel. They lack customer service skills and puts Hotel Valencia (a member of the Small Luxury hotels group) to a shame. [3] Front-of-the-house staff don't smile and lack hospitality you usually experience in other boutique, 4-star or 5-star hotels.
Despite these experiences, the upper-staff we talked to did all they could to make up to it. The Audit Manager who told us the situation when we arrived went beyond his line of duty to accomodate us that night, and offered a comlimentary upgrade on our 2nd night. The Assistant Front Desk Manager was helpful, took the concerns seriously and offered us complimentary breakfast, and champagne in the room that evening.
Rooms are in excellent condition as the hotel is only 8 months old. The decor is pretty much what you would find in a W Hotel- modern, chic, vibrant, fitted with simple-but-smart, asian-esque furnishings.
Considering Hotel Valencia wanting to be a premier hotel in San Antonio and currently a member of the Small Luxury Hotels group, I don't think this establishment is competant enough if the customer service aspect does not change. If you like a modern, hip hotel but not bothered with the service you will receive, Hotel Valencia would be a good choice. 
But for a spoilt, discerning, and frequent traveler like myself who appreciates excellent hotels that has flawless service to match, you might want to consider giving your business to another hotel.

title: “Reasonable and so handy”
text: We typically stay here anytime our travels bring us to The Stockyards. Easy and convenient. Clean rooms and adequate breakfast offerings. Warm cookies too. Room cards twice did not work and had to be re-keyed but front desk apologetic.

title: “Nice but not luxurious”
text: My boyfriend and I spent 4nights here. The room was a good size and everything was clean and the bed was fairly comfortable. Overall, the minimalistic decor was cold and not comfy or luxurious. Bathroom was small and the sink area and closet were tight, if we were staying longer, there would not have been room for our bags. I love the fact that they offer free bike rentals but beware, they are only 3 speed and Seattle has some very steep hills and one of our rentals had some maintenance issues. Our likes of this hotel far outweighs the inconveniences. All the staff was fantastic, helpful and professional. Any issues we had were promptly remediated. The location was great. We we walked from Pioneer square to the Space Needle and were only a few blocks from the light rail and monorail stations. The hotel was a little noisy, next to the monorail and our room was across from the elevator, but nothing we lost sleep over. I think a somewhat noisy environment is to be expected of an urban hotel.

title: “I will recommend the hotel & stay there again.”
text: I stayed overnight to catch a very early morning flight. It was a most convenient location & provided a free shuttle too and from the airport. For a fee I was able to park my car at the hotel until my return. The desk clerk was very pleasant and helpful with assistance on the computer & recommendations for dinner. I'm very happy with the hotel & will stay again as needed.

title: “No interest in garment district or Hair emporium”
text:
Located next to the Hair emporium (they sell 100% real hair or 100% synthetic hair NO BLENDS!!) in the very unfashionable garment district, the Broadway Plaza is only for the budget minded. 
The downsides: All street vendors in all of New York must meet outside this hotel both before and after work and that’s not a good thing. The hotel rooms are clean but a bit dingy. The drop ceilings and florescent lighting make the hotel experience feel more like a night at the office instead of a night a hotel—complete with lumpy bed. Guest will feel safe knowing there are lots of sprinklers in some rooms—mine had 5. Elevators apparently must run on the top and bottom of the hour as there was always a wait to get one. 
The upsides: The hotel is cheap, located close to other areas you might want to visit, and some rooms had great views of the Empire State building – I wanted to jump out of it instead of return to my hotel room.

title: “Okay if you like to be nickeled and dimed to death.”
text:
The rooms are very large. They have a large desk dresser set a closet and a small table and chair. Plenty of room. The room was okay. I suspect that the bathroom was not cleaned because a note was left in the bathroom for room service and it was not touched. The bathroom floor looked dirty and we found a hair on the commode. Toilet paper roller was broken and the toilet paper finally was taken off and put on the back of the commode to keep it from falling off the roller.
The nickeling and diming was outrageous. They charge $12.00 per day for self-parking. A 12 oz soft drink is $2.17, the charge for using their ATM is $3.80 per transaction. They did not provide for a free breakfast not even a Continental style. Instead they charged such expensive prices that we went to find breakfast elsewhere. Hotel staff refused to make extra change when making a debit card transaction. Evidentially, the Sheraton chain has not learned about guest centered hospitality.
The hotel is conveniently located close to the Fort Worth Convention Center, Water Gardens and the hot night life of downtown Fort Worth.

title: “Excellent!!!”
text: Very nice hotel with a great location. Walking distance to everything. Very helpful staff. Would stay again and again!

title: “Beautiful Hotel with wonderful service”
text:
We took our 35 month old son for a short break to Washington DC and chose to stay at the Mayflower.
What a great choice !
The Hotel was quite magnificent , the rooms were very nice but it was the exemplary service that we will never forget. 
Every person from chambermaids , bellboys to reception desk colleagues were so friendly and they all had so much time for all of us and especially our son.
Our room had a nice view of Conneticut Ave and was reasonably quiet, although you could here the Metro running 4 floors below. 
The complimentary hot drinks delivered to our room each morning was a lovely touch.
We loved Washington and will definately return, we wouldnt look further then the Mayflower.

title: “pleasant surprise”
text: Got this hotel as part of a package and were concerned as we usually stay at higher end Marriotts. The hotel shares building with a Residence Inn (one on one side one on the other). Although the room was small, there was a nice sitting area with a chaise and a basic but very clean bathroom. Great view. Decent breakfast included in nice breakfast room. Staff went out of their way for us and we actually felt cared for. You cant beat the location -close to everything. We took public transportation from airport and it was a breeze (but there are a lot of stairs at subway exit). Chicago is a great city with superb architecture , great restaurants and lovely citizens.

title: “Good value hotel”
