text: We stayed for three nights and found this to be a good value, well located hotel. Room was comfortable, and service friendly. Lovely "Club" style bar & lounge which is good for a nightcap. Bus is just outside the door, and there is a good selection of restaurants and bars just down the street. Only downside was difficulty in getting a taxi one morning. The front desk had booked one for us and called again after 15 mins, but none appeared so we ended up just catching a bus! Staff mentioned that many taxi drivers don't know the hotel.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
When I travel I enjoy staying at the Kimpton properties. I prefer the boutique style properties as opposed to the standard cutout business variety.
My first stay at the Monaco in Seattle and I was not disappointed. Good location for me, great room, shower, flat screen and room service. The attached Sazerac bar and restaurant is a nice place to relax, especially during happy hour. Good appetizers and great wood fired pizzas.

title: “Nice Hotel on the Riverwalk”
text:
Recently returned from a really nice relaxing stay at the La Mansion. We stayed in a suite on the 4th floor with a balcony and riverwalk view. Lovely view from our room. As mentioned in other reviews, rooms facing the riverwalk can be somewhat noisy late at night and very early in the morning with delivery vehicles and trash collection. You need to remember that this is a city so if you don't want noise you should request an interior room. The hotel is very spanish in decor, loved the comfy beds with great linens, nightly turn-down service, and very nice cleaning staff. The pool was small, maybe they need to add more lounge chairs! Definitely not enough for the crowd that gathered in the afternoon. 
Restaurants to recommend: Pesca for a very nice (two hour) meal. Somewhat pricey but very nice atmosphere. Bourdes, loved this place! the steaks are amazing. Make sure you get reservations. For mexican food, Iron Cactus and Rita's were both good and reasonably priced. Hard Rock is nice eat on the upper balcony if you don't like the loud music. Also ate at an italian restaurant adjacent to the Hard Rock. It was also good. Breakfast at Pesca is wonderful. Sergio was our waiter at both dinner and breakfast. He was very nice and gave recommendations for places to see and directions! 
Make sure you do the barge tour. Very informative and fun at night. If you are there during the summer, make sure you attend the Rio del Noche show at the theatre on the riverwalk. This is a great latin inspired dance show sponsered by the Kiwanis Club. The show is Friday and Saturday nights at 8:30 purchase tickets for 15.00. Also, go the Mexican Market (El Mercado), and the Alamo. 
Lovely stay in San Antonio and the La Mansion.

title: “Not a wonderful time”
text: We stayed there for a week. The people were nice, but the room wasn't clean enough. There was candy left on the floor when we arrived. The room itself didn't have any windows! The bedroom had two windows that looked at the wall of the next building. The nicest feature of the hotel was the roof which had chairs and a lovely view. We wouldn't choose to stay there again.

title: “Great location for two night stay, close walk to everything!”
text:
Nice hotel, walking distance to Ouincy Market, Freedom Trail, Harbour, and North End.
 The rooms are well appointed and very clean. We travelled as a family of four with two teens. Our room had two queen beds, plenty of space and a large bathroom with a walk in shower, soaking tub and vanity mirror.
 We booked on Hotwire and stayed for a very good rate.
We ate breakfast at Panera bread. When you exit the building go left a couple of blocks.
We enjoyed parking the car down stairs and walking to everything for the three days of our stay.
The pool is located on the second floor, at the spa and gym area. We found it not to be too kid friendly. It's more of a lap pool than a kids on vacation pool.
If you have not stayed at a four and a half star before, check this out. It was a highlight of our vacation! Be sure to do the Boston Gliders Segway tour. It's a fun way to see the city!

title: “overall good hotel, small bathroom”
text: Overall, this hotel is a good choice in S.F. It has a good location, friendly staff,clean and quiet rooms (our room was on the side facing another building) and comfortable bed. Free internet in the business center is a nice plus as is the complementary afternoon wine reception and chair massages.The only negatives would be the small bathrooms with minimal counter space (pedastal sink) and a shower curtin that tend to blow into the shower giving you an unwanted massage! The pillows are strangely smaller than standard. Overall, we enjoyed our stay at the Serrano and we would stay there again.

title: “Simple, affordable, walking distance to airport, friendly staff.”
text: The pictures are actually pretty accurate, our room is newly furnished, clean, nice. Bathroom fan is dying but at least we have one unlike many high end hotels, and the bathroom door cannot close but not a big deal. Will stay here again and happily walk to the place thanks to the new overhead walkway.

title: “Hotel was as terrific as San Diego”
text: The staff met every need that I had. On my last night, the snack/coffee bar was closed and the front desk clerk went to housekeeping to score some awesome chocolate chip cookiies for me. I requested a room with a flat screen tv and also a room on a higher floor. Both requests were granted although my room wasn't quite ready when I arrived at 3:15 p.m. They sent us in to McCormick & Schmick's for cocktails on the house until the room was finished. Definitely use the self park across the street. Since we were out most of the day, we were generally only paying the overnight rate. It was much easier than waiting on a valet and then having to tip in additio n to the $35 daily valet parking rate. I think the most I ever paid in a day was $15. Got a great rate on this stay through TravelZoo. $119 a night. Stayed for 4 nights and enjoyed the area, played golf nearby and had some great meals too.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Ended up with a room on the 20th Floor. Gorgeous view, clean, quite - everything you can ask for. No negetives that I can think of. Good location, not in the middle of busy "touristy" stuff, and that worked for us. Would def go back!

title: “STAY HERE IS YOU FEEL LIKE BEING TREATED LIKE SH*T”
text:
PLEASE SAVE YOUR MONEY AND YOUR NIGHT!
Nice hotel in a nice location, but be WARNED: The Workers are the most arrogant, least helpful, and incompetent service people you will ever run across. You will spend a lot of money to be treated like third class citizens. I swear. If you feel like relaxing and want a drink, V-BAR (Hotel Valencia's Bar) has the RUDEST BARTENDER AN MANAGER. I cursed out the first service preson in my life at V-BAR. Don't even bother talking to the manager-- they don't care.

title: “Great location”
text:
Stayed here for a girl's trip to Seattle for the weekend in May. For the price (we got a deal) for the 4 of us, it was a steal...mainly because the location was great right in the middle of downtown for us to walk everywhere we wanted for shopping, going to the market during the day for lunch, and out at night to a couple bars and clubs. We cabbed once but that was to Pioneer Square which is a little too far for walking in my opinion. 
The room was nice, super clean, and had a great view of the city because we were on one of the top floors. Staff was nice and efficient checking in, but the downfall is the parking - SO expensive! But valet was really fast - we had our car out in 5 minutes, compared to other places downtown, this is pretty quick. All in all, I would recommend and definitely stay here again.

title: “2nd visit went okay but still not my first pick”
text:
THE GOOD:
Free town car use in town (they expect tips and don’t go to the airport)
Fast check-in/check out
Free internet and its fast and consistent (big plus)
Pretty in old-fashioned way 
Very good food in restaurant/room service (but limited selection)
Tea maker in room makes excellent tea (loved it)
Friendly staff in each department
Bed was decent and lighting in room was good
Good bath products
THE BAD:
Checked into wrong room (had suite, checked into regular room); they fixed when I asked about it Water in shower is extremely inconsistent and dangerous. It went from cold to scalding hot in seconds and wouldn’t maintain a steady temperature (actually burnt my skin) Very strange strong odor in hallways (but not in rooms) Heat did not work in my room (they sent up heater but took 2 days) No clock in room (had to ask for one, which they sent) No sound proof windows; street sounds were extremely loud (sirens, cars, train whistles in early am, even heard what sounded like drag racing several nights) No bathtub in a suite room is ridiculous; only had a tiny shower Not close to Pike Street/tourist area (but short cab/car away)
I’ve given this hotel two chances. Would I stay here again? Maybe but I would definitely look elsewhere first. (W, Four Seasons, Pan Pacific, etc.) The shower burn was a big turn-off and not easy to forget. 
The level of service is not up to par with 4 star hotels at all but the staff is nice enough and they’re trying. Half the issue is the building is just old. Half appears to be a lack of anticipating basic needs or informing guests of items. Ie>No bathtub in an upgraded room was a rude shock. 
It’s not completely horrible but so much ends up not going smoothly or to guest expectation that it ends up feeling like a hassle. I upgraded to the junior suite on this visit because I thought it would be better than the regular room on my last visit but there was barely any difference and the lack of basics was still the same. 
I also do not remotely understand anyone rating this a 5 star hotel. Maybe based on friendliness yes, but execution? No way. Not if you’ve traveled at all and stayed at a true 5 star hotel. 
And they seriously need to work on the water situation. It's not only a hassle but dangerous. What if I'd been someone that couldn't jump out the way fast enough? I moved REALLY quickly and still got hurt.

title: “Fabulous NYC Hotel in Soho”
text:
60 Thompson is a charming boutique hotel located in Soho. The location is ideal for all the shopping and restaurants in Soho. The rooms are clean, spacious (for NYC), and well decorated. The bathrooms are beautiful and bathrobes are provided.
There is also a very cool bar and restaurant in this hotel. The hotel staff is very friendly and helpful.
I would absolutely recommend this hotel - its one of my NYC faves!

title: “Loved the Free Bikes”
text: This is a great hotel with lots of nice touches. We stayed in June and had a fabulous time making full use of the free bicycles to travel around Seattle - the pool and the gym are very good too. I loved the little touches, like the free trolley, delivered to the room, with the foot spa, back massager and chill-out music. The wine tasting was another lovely touch. In fact, there are so many free 'extras' that it is hard to fit them all in. The rooms are very modern, without being stark and the location is great. The free taxi to the downtown area was also a boon and the staff were incredibly friendly with great service all round. The hotel was very reasonably priced and I would recommend it most highly. The hotel manages to anticipate what its guests might enjoy and succeeds in ensuring that they feel welcome and pampered. We came back to the UK fitter and more relaxed - which can't be bad. I only wish hotels in the UK could meet these kind of standards.

title: “good location, disappointed in the hotel”
text:
My husband and I went for a birthday weekend. The hotel is rated as a 4 star hotel.
We were disappointed with the staff, and the room. The staff were rude at check in.
The room could have been cleaner, the bathroom tub drain was broken. We were on the 20th floor and could still hear the taxis honking their horn! We watched an on demand movie and it was very expensive.
The only good thing was the location, in Times Square.

title: “Christmas Tree Trip 12/3/11”
text: Took the family to see the tree this year, we booked a junior suite. Perfect room for mom & dad and 2 teen age girls. Loved the holiday decorations in the lobby!! Staff is in general terrific but the front desk could smile a bit more. I shouldn't feel like an imposition if I have to use the lobby bathroom (which they lock and keycard). The girls swam in the pool at dusk, just as the lights were coming on in the city, beautiful view from the pool deck. Off to the tree - I guess the warm weather brought everyone out - it was really crowded. Line was tooo long for skating but the shopping was great. Mom & dad got up early (not an easy feat, the beds are comfy) on Sunday to take in the Hell's Kitchen Flea Market only a few blocks away, a nice brisk walk and some good buys. The new bar & grill inside the hotel PJ Bricks was good for lunch on Sunday and a nice place to wait out the kids shopping! All in all another great stay. Can't wait to do it again.

title: “lovely stay - fabulous breakfast.”
text: close to the boston station (making trip to new york easy) .breakfast was varied and had a large selection which we thoroughly enjoyed.free internet facility was very useful and for keeping passports/valuables safe lockers were avaiable at the reception.luggage carrying trolley was big and easy to handle

title: “Despite Irene, Ink 48 Made up for it all...”
text: I have to say I never write reviews but felt I had to in this case. We were at this hotel during Hurricane Irene where the whole city was shut down. The hotel was fantastic, we upgraded our room (recommended) and it was awesome, everything was perfect. My husband is not a fan of anything under a five star and he also loved this hotel. Jeffrey was great. Highly recommend this hotel, location, everything.

title: “Not much bang for your buck”
text: Convenient location. Rooms are small and unless in the upper half of the building dark, with no view, and noisy (not from 7th Ave. but from the AC/ventilation); bedding is of low end quality. Overall: There are many better places for the same or even less money.

title: “Meh”
text:
I wanted to like this place, but I really have no idea how it gets the reviews it does on here. 
So, starting from the top...
Valet is fine - he wasn't out there when I arrived and so I waited, unsure of where you were actually supposed to pull up to for 5-10 minutes. Upon retrieving my car on other days, it took a good 15 minutes, so be sure to call down early.
Check-in was fine - front desk staff is extremely nice and helpful.
Rooms look good on the surface - stylish and redone fairly recently. Bed was comfy as were linens and pillows. Walls are VERY thin though. I had to run to CVS for earplugs as I could hear every word of the person in the room next to me. The balconies are also a little sketchy - I could have climbed into my neighbors room, especially since the maid undid the lock and bar that drops both days so that anyone could enter from the outside.
The maid also turned on the alarm on my second day - imagine my surprise when it went off extremely early and had not the previous day. Water pressure in the shower was nice, but no fan.
The continental breakfast was nothing to write home about - seriously, the Hampton Inn is better. Hardly any healthy options - mainly sugary cereals and muffins and cereal bars. A few bananas and apples and no whole grain toast or bagels.
The wine and cheese was nice - surprisingly the wine wasn't the cheapest out there - it was all Penfolds. Good cheese selection too.
Worst part was the lack of fitness center. They used to have an agreement with a nearby club, but its since closed and they make no mention of this on their website or when checking in. You find out early in the morning when you want to go to the gym. Come on - can't you convert one room to a fitness room?!
Overall, there are many better options for the price. And frankly, if you're willing to spend just $25-50 more, you can stay at the much better Sofitel a block away.

title: “Perfect Location and More”
text:
We booked a room here for one night through a third party site, and though the hotel's site says to book through them for artists rooms, we actually ended up getting the room we wanted, decorated by artist Sam Flores.
Bed is comfortable, room is a good size, mini fridge is a plus. But water pressure in bathroom was very low, claw-foot tub/shower was tiny and there's no shelves to put toiletries on. 
Complimentary breakfast was thin, but works if your strapped for cash. Recommend going somewhere else to really get a substantial meal to tackle the San Francisco hills!

title: “Nice NYC hotel experience”
text: Can't say enough about the friendly service! The entire staff was amazing. This is a very clean hotel and the space is quite roomy (especially the bathrooms) for NYC. It's quiet and the beds are comfortable. I would recommend to anyone wanting a stylish,clean, comfy room in a great NYC location!

title: “Great location in Memphis”
text: Just got back from a weekend in Memphis. I picked this hotel based on other trip advisor recommendations. Some people were concerned with the noise from Beale st. but we were on the back side of Beale st. and didn't hear a thing. We went to Graceland, Sun Studios, Barbecue tour(tastin around the town) and ate at the Majestic and went to the Peanut Shoppe. Love all of it. The Hampton is very clean, the breakfast was very tasty, and you are right around the corner from crazy Beale st.

title: “On the list of super cheap NYC hotels with private bathrooms”
text: I'm on a quest to find a list of 10 hotels that I would recommend in NYC for under $200 with private bathrooms. The POD 39 tops the list. This one is awesome, and the cheapest on the list, if you want to stay in Times Square (right next to the stage door for The Book of Mormon). The lobby will freak you out (so worn down), but stick with it. The bed was clean and comfortable, the bathroom sizeable. Shower head and dryer needed fixing but the front desk people seemed thankful to know this. So this stays on the list of "under $200 with private bathroom and clean bedroom." It was actually under $150. TV works, comfortable bedding.

title: “old and noisy”
text: So-so hotel. rooms good size. tired looking lobby. doors slam and really need modernizing to keep noise level down. We moved after a night to Holiday Inn Express. Much better there.

title: “Terrible, and cost us $180 a night. Had...”
text:
Terrible, and cost us $180 a night. Had a reservation for 3 nights, left after one!
Here's why:
-location horrible, lots of homeless right outside hotel, location is literally one block from Tenderloin (not good area)
-pillows had blood stains on them
-an old pair of womens shoes were left in our room on arrival (hard to believe a maid would see them)
-there is a noisy bar next door, that has people outside shouting until 2am every night
-no bell desk, no help whatsoever with luggage (which would be fine if I wasn't paying $180 a night)
-hotel staff leave in early evening, we came back from dinner and someone was a sleep in the lobby on a chair (very scary)
Bottom line, I woudnt pay $50 to stay here, and never will again. Can't understand the 4 star rating.
Just being honest, would have ruined our vacation if we had stayed here entire time.

title: “Great Home Base for San Diego Area Vacation”
text:
We vacationed in San Diego for 8 days this summer and made the Residence Inn in Mira Mesa our home base. There are five of us, so we like the larger suites that are available in Mariott's Residence Inn.
Room: We stayed in a 2 bedroom unit, which is definitely more like an apartment than a hotel room. Plenty of adequate space. It's the second time we used this chain, and they are very much alike. The only bad part was the volume of the A/C unit, which we could tell was the same for the entire complex.
Location: It's located 15 minutes north of San Diego (Balboa Park, Sea World) and maybe 20 minutes south of Carlsbad (Lego Land). It was really conveniently located, just a few blocks off of I-805. The area is a large commercial business park and afternoon "5 o'clock whistle" traffic exiting the area was thick. Otherwise, it was a really great spot.
Extras: The complimentary breakfast is really a plus. There's fresh eggs, sausage, hashbrowns, oatmeal, fresh waffles, etc. etc. The pool is average but adequate.
I'd definitely recommend this place for families on vacation or for business travelers on extended stay.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
A persistant problem with my room key and staff's attention and subsequent manager's response to my inconvience really ruined my four-day stay there. I was locked out of my room on two consecutive nights (with one wait in the hallway for 45 minutes, being assured help was soon to arrive) and, since the malfunctioning lock was not fixed, essentially locked in my room on my last morning. 
Some of the rooms may be suites with "spa-like" bathrooms, I did not have one of them despite what I thought I had reserved. For getting a pantry, having to request a coffee machine seems odd.

title: “Great Place”
text: This was all in all a very positive experience. There were no problems with check-in and check-out. The room was wonderful and there were NO bedbugs at this hotel. We stayed in the junior executive suite and felt very at home in the spacious room. The price is a bit high, but the location in the city is excellent and the service was fantastic.

title: “Good value for money...”
text: The Buena Vista Motor Inn is a good venue for SF visitors driving a car, because parking is free and the staff is very friendly and helpful, plus the rates are reasonable for a city where hotel, and especially parking, is expensive. A word of warning, the parking in the motor inn's two garages is tight, so be patient, try to back into spaces, and have your partner outside to guide you in. We parked our car and left it for entire days using a muni pass on street and cable cars, there's a street car stop just a block away, and they run frequently -- don't even think about driving to Union Square, a hopeless array of one-way streets and horrendous traffic . Ask the Desk to advise good hole-in the-wall restaurants nearby, especially terrific Chinese restaurants.

title: “Nice Hotel, Good Service!”
text:
My wife and I stayed up here recently as part of an executive offsite for my company. Upon check-in we were impressed by the atomosphere and style of the place. The room was small yet cozy and reminded me of the Hudson in NYC.
Since we were there on business, we had a snag getting one of our rooms available and the manager Jenny jumped right into action. She made one phone call and within 5 minutes we had the Tokyo board room set up with waters, napkins, etc. I was impressed.
We had dinner for 12 at the Grand Cafe that night. Plenty of good selection and interesting pairings available. They did close down the bar early so for you night-owls you may have to travel outside.
Overall good stay, cool place, nice people.

title: “By far, best value for the dollar - especially during the holidays.”
text: The Swissotel has long been our favorite downtown hotel. The rooms are luxurious, the beds are extremely comfortable, the service is great and the people are very friendly. We asked for a lakeview room and got a view of the lake and Navy Pier - not a view where you had to crane your neck so that you could see a little sliver of the lake. We were there December 27 and their holidays rates were far better than anything else we had seen. The location is away from the congestion of Michigan Avenue, but it's a very short walk across the river to all the sights and sounds of Christmas in downtown Chicago.

title: “Nice Place Very Clean Rooms”
text: I enjoyed my stay here. They are still working on the building but the main parts are done (the rooms) once they finish the hallways and stairwells this place will be perfect. It's a clean affordable hotel near the downtown L.A. with free parking, internet, satellite TV, and dogs stay for FREE. The staff is very nice and helpful. Yea, you have to ask for the iron but you have to do that at many other hotels. I will come back again and hopefully when I come next year it will be fully finished. To be honest I really don't want anyone to know about this place b/c I want to keep it my little secret. Please excuse my poor rating on the pool it should have skipped it because it's unfinished.

title: “AMAZING......”
text: This resort is amazing.. Absolutely fabulous.. IT the best resort for families... WE loved everything about the hotel and the staff.... My kids say it is better than Disney World...

title: “Best Kept Secret”
text: Last weekend, several friends got together to have a fun 'girl' weekend going to a show and shopping. The Affinia 50 is such a awesome boutique hotel that offers so much. Where can you in NYC to find a hotel that offers kitchenettes in a small suite. Planning ahead certainly plays into getting the best rate; however, the room/suite rates are quite reasonable for what you get in return. The hotel location is E 50th Street which is truly a convenient place to stay. You can easily walk to Rockefeller Square, 5th Avenue for shopping, the UN Building - even the theatre district. The Staff at Affinia 50 is friendly and so accommodating. Like the title says - It's the Best Kept Secret - will maybe not after this posting.

title: “Great sized rooms for reasonable price”
text: Huge suites for reasonable price. Great restaurants only 2 minutes drive away from here. Rooms were clean and well appointed. I loved the automated check in/out process which saves a great deal of time. Great breakfast buffet with endless choice of breakfast.

title: “Not Quite New Courtyard”
text: Had I not been in a brand new Courtyard last night, this location would have seemed adequate. The lobby has been remodeled to equal the newer Courtyards, the furniture in the room changed, however the layout of the room and particularly the bathroom is a throwback to earlier Courtyard styles. It was clean, about 2 miles off I77,and attempting to be aucourant, but a little lacking. The staff is very friendly, which goes a long way to a more pleasant stay. If room size and modern accommodations matter to you, find a newer Courtyard.

title: “50th percentile”
text: The best part of this property is the swimming pool and hot tub. Downsides include a breakfast buffet in a building separate from the hotel (without the ability to take a tray back to your room) and rather strange access to one's room from the lobby, especially later in the evening. But it is adequate as a place to stay on the north side of L.A.

title: “First class!”
text: My first stay at the Sofitel Water Tower last week. The room was beautiful, very stylishly decorated, enormous TV set. Service was good, staff very helpful. Definitely recommend to others.

title: “Great location, great room, great service”
text: I was a bit nervous about staying at the Latham Hotel after reading all of the less than positive TripAdvisor reviews -- but I have nothing but praise for this hotel. I am learning not to take most people's groaning and complaining too seriously on this site. I also suspect that many of the people who report getting rude service must behave quite rudely themselves in order to be treated as poorly as they suggest! The Latham Hotel is in a fantastic location (a couple of blocks from Rittenhouse Square). Our room was lovely, spacious, and clean, and the front desk staff and doorman were all very friendly and helpful during our three-day stay. We paid the $30 per day for valet parking so that we could come and go as we pleased anytime during the night and day. Our car was always ready within about 10 minutes. I would highly recommend the Latham. It is quite a bargain for the location, as other hotels in the same area (Sofitel, Ritz Carlton, The Rittenhouse) are much more expensive.

title: “Not recommended”
text:
I have to agree with most of the posters.
Great location, but a poor hotel....Dirty, beds are like you're on a ship, dirty..(but not small)
International payphones were out of order (both).
Brusque staff. We payed for luggage storage when we checked out, but noone to attend to the luggage (might as well have left it in the lobby).
Once you check out, you cannot use the restrooms anymore...
Next time we'll try the Southgate Towers, 1 block down

title: “Parking is a Major Problem”
text:
We attended a wedding reception at the Bristol. The reception on the 9th floor was good with the dancing under the open ceiling. But other than that, it was a disappointing experience. The major problem was lack of parking. Then had none when we arrived. I believe they accept local shoppers and business parking and don't hold spaces for guests. We had to park four blocks away in a pay lot, and about the same distance for street meter parking, that had a 2 hour limit. Constantly having to walk to the car to feed the meter or pay more at the lot took much of the enjoyment from the visit. Also the hotel front desk would not make change for the meters, but other local merchants would. I was able to move my car to the hotel about 6pm. The only other overnight parking a few blocks away required pickup by 6am or 7am.
I would never recommend staying at the hotel. There are too many other choices in the area.

title: “Great room easy access to gas lamp fun”
text: Stayed here for a couple of nights while in town for a conference. Let's start with positive and work our way down. Rooms were great. I stayed in a king deluxe. The room was large clean and very sleek. The bed and pillows very comfortable and the windows do open so fresh cool air is always available. Bathrooms are also nice and contain a very roomy shower. Down side to the rooms are that since the hotel is across the street from the greyhound station, there can be a lot of noise. That being said te rooms which are the most important consideration one makes when choosing a hotel are comfortable and a good value. The hotel is overall very clean. Down side to this establishment is that there is very little available in terms of service. There are no bellman to assist with bags. I also noticed that the front desk attendant would sometimes be absent leaving a cue of people awaiting their return. The gym is lacking. There are a couple of cardio machines as well as a muti use weight machine. There should be more dumbbells and more machines to make this gym more user friendly. Since three people were already there working out I was unable to do as all machines were in use.

title: “Excellent Stay and Nice Restaurant”
text: This hotel has nice rooms that are small but nicely appointed. The staff was very friendly and the hotel restaurant was good too. On my next business trip to Houston, I will stay here again. Great job to Magideh and her colleagues.

title: “Pleasant Stay”
text:
I usually consider Hampton Inn's a safe bet, and this one was no different. This hotel is just south of the NASCAR Hall of Fame and the Convention Center. It shares a parking lot with the Hilton Garden, which is right next door. The parking is free for guests, which appeared to be a rarity in downtown Charlotte. 
Check in was quick and easy. I had a suite which had a couch, TV, and small kitchenette in one room and the bedroom and bathroom in the other room. Plenty of space in both rooms. The kitchenette had a mini-fridge, microwave, sink, cabinets, and counter space. There was also a small desk and chair in the first room. The rooms were clean and relatively quiet. I could hear some people talking loudly in the halls, but no noise from other rooms.
As with all Hampton's, a hot breakfast is included. Waffles, scrambled eggs (with cheese and some seasoning), sausage, as well as standard continental breakfast food was all available. There was a marathon going on the morning I was there and even with all the athletes eating before their race, there was plenty of food brought out.
The morning I checked out I had a meeting downtown. I asked if it was OK to keep my car in the Hampton lot during the day and I was told it would be no problem.

title: “Great Hotel. But just that”
text: We stayed at this hotel for a long weekend. The accomodations were great. We were given a double room at check in so the first night, we slept in one of the beds just like at home. On the second night, we decided to sleep in the second bed. The frame seemed to be broken so we phoned the front desk and were brought keys to a room across the hall from us. Got in the room and checked the bed and it was the same issue. They use those cheap snap together metal frames so when you sit on the foot of the bed, you can feel the box spring touch the floor. The bed was super comfy though. I even purchased their linens that you can buy online. They are quite expensive but I love the way they feel. They give you cookies whenever you ask and the Einstein Bros bagels downstairs is a plus. This place is a really nice place to crash but activitied beyond that you will have to leave and find elsewhere. Will stay here again in the future.

title: “A total suprise!!”
text: This place was exceptional. One of the nices places I've stayed at for years. Highly recommended!

title: “Tried very hard to like this place”
text:
On previous trips while staying at another 5 star property in town, I kept finding myself at The Time Warner center for dinner, drinks, walks in the park etc. Therefore , I thought, why not try it out?
While there were no disasters, and nothing particularly bad about the hotel, it came across as dissapointigly average. The park views were terrific. The service was friendly. But the overall experience feels more like a convention Hyatt. There's nothing wrong with that, but its very dissapointing if you are expecting a five star experience. 
That fifth star is all in the details, and thats what the hotel lacks. From the service, to the finishes in the rooms. 
Most of the problems come from the building itself. Even though the hotel is only a couple hundred rooms, you definitely feel like you're in a massive structure. And everything, from the spa to the business center feels like its miles away, down random corridors. For example, the entrance to the gym is located just outside a ballroom area: so at best, you have to walk through a dark empty banquet area with a piano covered in the corner, but I couldn't help thinking of the alternative if the room were in use, which would be making your way through a black tie affair in your sweaty workout clothes. 
One afternoon I returned to my room to find the maid cleaning the room, but noticed she had the TV turned on and was watching a soap opera. Little things like this give the impression there is very little oversight of the smaller details by management. 
The area rug in the lobby has an ugly rubber band around it like an airport would have, and the tile and fixtures in the bathrooms, while attractive, look cheap and institutional. The rooms have an office-chic feel to them, like a first class airport lounge. Nothing wrong with that, but certainly not the height of luxury one might expect.

title: “Perfect for hipsters: business travelers, not so much.”
text:
If you like W Hotels and minimalist design, this place for you.
For my tastes there is too much emphasis on form and not enough on function and comfort. Definitely not a room to relax in or do some late night work.
For reasons I don't understand the bed practically sits on the floor. 
Lobby is busy and loud with people seeing and being seen.

title: “Wonderful At The Westin”
text:
The hotel is a business type hotel but we were there for a weekend away and found it wonderful. It was a good rate advertised by a grand opening or something. Our room was clean, very comfortable (the beds were fabulous!!!) and the room was quiet at night.
On a negative note, we tried two different times and attempted to be waited on in their bar. We were ignored both visits by several cocktail waiters and after 10 minutes had to go up to the bartender to get a drink which took another 10 minutes. One drink and we left. The second time we were again ignored so we never made an attempt to enter the bar or eat at the restaurant in the hotel, assuming it was the same type of staff. 
The only other negative thing which we were really disappointed is, on their hotel tv, they advertised rather than to go out for the night, to stay in order a first run movie, relax and enjoy yourself. Well, on our second night after dinner, we decided to do that. We got all ready with our snacks and cocktails we purchased from the local store and nothing. For two hours that we attempted to try and order a movie and enjoy our room, the system was down and we were unable to order a movie. A very big disappointment!!!
Overall we were quite pleased and as long as their rates are about the same in the future we will definitely go back to this hotel, but bring our own cocktails next time!!

title: “Great stay at the Roger Smith. . .”
text: I chose this hotel based on the ratings here and extensive online research. I wanted somewhere to lay my head after arriving in NYC after a late arriving flight before I traveled to my home an hour outside NYC. I made my reservation a day in advance and luckily for me there was a 72 hour special which coincided with my travel date and afforded me an upgrade to a junior suite for just $12!! Once I got to the hotel, I was very pleased with the size of the room and the layout. This hotel is not new by any means, but if you're from the Northeast and New England, you will certainly appreciate the historic nature of the buildings and rooms. The bed was very clean and comfortable. I slept like a baby. Loved the free Wi-Fi, state of the art flat screen TV, and Henry's Rooftop bar. Awaiting for NYC to approve it, but looking forward to the opening of Lily's. All in all considering the location, amenities, helpfulness, friendliness of staff and final cost; Roger Smith was definitely worth the stay!!

title: “A grand old hotel with a few quirks”
text: This was my second stay at the Mark Hopkins. It is truly a landmark in a wonderful location, if you don't mind grueling walking workouts up and down hills. The staff is quite friendly and helpful and the interior is out of the past. My one complaint is to echo what has been said by other Tripadvisor contributors: the pipes are noisy! We had to change rooms after our first night due to noise in the pipes. This noise goes beyond hearing flushing toilets which is minor compared to the plumbing moans and groans in the wall. Our second room was better but not flawless. Other that the musical accompaniment from the bathroom walls, the room was lovely and I really enjoyed being able to open the windows to get some fresh air. There is a wonderful Italian coffee shop one block away at the back of the Fairmont Hotel that is an oasis, great for breakfast or an afternoon coffee. I really enjoyed being so close to Chinatown and Northbeach, either by hoofing it or by the trolley. I would return to this hotel, maybe with some good earplugs.

title: “A Wonderful Vacation Experience”
text:
Staying at the Rancho Bernardo Inn was a wonderful experience. It was definitely one of the most peaceful and idyllic vacation spots I have ever visited. I reserved the room for five days through a discount online broker but I was treated like a regular high paying guest. The entire staff was courteous, knowledgable and attentive without being intrusive.
The minute I drove onto the grounds, the hustle and bustle of the real world melted away. The grounds, fountains and gardens were well kept and provided wonderful scenery. Everything about the place exuded old world charm and seemed to belong to a different more serene time.
The room was spacious rustic and very clean. The only thing that seemed out of place was my laptop and the DSL hookup. The food was expensive, but I didn't dine on the premises. There were plenty of places in the area to eat.
I look forward to a return visit.

title: “A beautiful little hotel”
text:
This was my first visit to San Jose and I must say I'm glad I choose the Montgomery over the other bland chains.
You can stay at any number of the generic chains in San Jose. Take your pick. It's a town full of hotels but if you want something a little less like the McDonalds of hotels then try here.
As expected the staff were friendly, the cleaning frequent but the extra little touches were magnificant. The rooms were generously sized (compared to big cities especially) and the interiors lovely.
There were only two things that annoyed me:
a) The TV is in the cabinet and very hard to angle towards the bed. There was plenty of room to put a table in for the TV.
b) The pillows were pretty poor quality. They were the type that fluff up nicely but when you actually put your head on them they dissapear.

title: “My own little San Diego apartment”
text:
I had to be in San Diego for business for a while and wanted something different. Some one who had worked at the theater in town recommended this hotel. They were so right in doing so I could kiss 'em. Having lived all over the country, in various pre-war apartments and condos, this is perfect for me. Give me hardwoods and vintage cabinetry!
I've been to San Diego many times but never to this neighborhood. It's a great little area and quite convenient. Easy to get to from the airport. Doesn't look like much from the outside. Love that its across the street from a park, not only a nice view but you're can always go walking, or take a picnic or join the yoga class I seen one day. There was a line to check in so I browsed the very nice lobby filled with European antiques.
When I arrived in my room I squealed that it feels like home. Very nice, big, comfy inviting room. Full kitchen with dining room. Lots of windows. There was no air conditioning in my room but you didn't need it. There was a bit of street noise, which I'm used to and doesn't bother me. Bed was clean and comfy. Decent amount of channels to watch when you want to veg. Bathroom was clean and big. The staff was quirky and very helpful.
Really a great little hotel. Especially great for extended stays or people who like to cook.

title: “Excellent location, value for NYC”
text: This location is fabulous - easy walk to FlatIron, Times Square. It's clean, a great price, the staff is super friendly, and overall it was a great place to be. I was here for work, so I didn't spend alot of time in the hotel rooms, but when I was here, I felt very relaxed and sheltered from the bustling NYC streets. Would definitely stay again!

title: “Fills expectations - single night visit”
text: Booked a suite and the hotel was very nice, very clean, modern, and with a very friendly staff. I had booked an internet rate that was non-cancellable, but I got caught unable to go due to the Valentine's Day ice storm. They rescheduled my suite to two weeks later with no issues, did it immediately. Very happy with my stay, as others have said location is great

title: “Great hotel in a great location!”
text: Hotel is in a great location, just a couple of blocks from the river, Michigan Ave & right on the redline that can take you to Wriggley Field. Service was excellent and the rooms were contemporary. We'll stay here again.

title: “A wonderful, clean, convenient hotel; we'll definitely return.”
text: The Conrad Hotel was just perfect for our traveling needs. Our king size bed suite featured a large bedroom with full bath (tub and shower), a separate living room area with a sofa bed and a small powder room as you enter the room. The room is perfect for 4 people. There is plenty of closet and drawer space if you choose to unpack. There is a coffee maker in the room, but there is also free coffee/tea each morning in the lobby area. The hotel is conveniently attached to Nordstroms and a small up-scale shopping mall. The concierge is very helpful and will spend as much time with you as needed. The front desk is helpful and friendly. The hotel is very clean and comfortable.

title: “Great base for San Diego”
text:
This hotel is in the perfect location and is quite nice. It is right off of the 8 in San Diego (Hotel Circle) and very convenient to the 5. It takes just minutes to get anywhere! The hotel has a nice lobby, concierge, computer for guest use. We have stayed here often when visiting our son, and the staff is always wonderful and helpful!
They have a pool and a hot tub. Always clean. The hotel has a restaurant and bar. I have not eaten is the restaurant, but have had a drink at the bar.
The rooms are very clean, large tv. If you leave your balcony door open on the Interstate 8 side, there will be some traffic noise. I keep the door closed, so no problem with noise at all. 
Target is right across the interstate from the hotel (can't walk easily, but drive within minutes). Coffee Bean and Starbucks right by Target. Tons of restaurants in that area, as well as Fashion Mall. Best Buy, Nordstrom Rack, numerous grocery stores, movie theaters very close to hotel. Trolley is located behind all of the above stores, and can take you downtown or to Old Town.
Zoo/Balboa Park very close - you just cannot beat this location!
When we stayed at the hotel, parking was free. This is not typical in San Diego. Most hotels charge for parking.

title: “We have a new home in Chicago.”
text: We stayed four nights in late July to visit our daughter who lives in Chicago. Having been to the city many times and looking for a "home base," we have stayed at several hotels. We are normally Marriott customers, but we like to stay nearer our daughters apartment north of the downtown. This hotel is THE PLACE to stay. I booked on Travelocity because it was such a good deal with the combo of airfare and hotel, but I was treated like a big shot by everybody there. David and Glenn at the front desk are in the top tier of hotel desk personnel we have encountered anywhere. We were greeted with enthusiasm, professionalism, and humor. We had a Junior Suite on the 7th floor with a nice view of the park and the lake, Lincoln Ave., and the city to the west. The bed was great, the bath amenities are wonderful, the flat screen TV was fabulous, and the room was very large. We had a refrigerator and microwave in our room so we could enjoy drinks (and leftovers from Malnati's). When we were in the room relaxing, I had a nice time just looking out the windows at the view. The furnishings were cool, and the lobby is a good place to relax, as well. Every staff member was polite, efficient, and friendly. On Wed. and Sat. there is a farmer's market right across the street in Lincoln Park that was fun. The 22 Clark bus stops right in front and the 151 Michigan Ave. stops on the other side of the park (maybe 200 yards away--I know it wasn't far). The rooftop bar was not open when we were there, but it looks to a a fabulous place to go. Excellence abounds here at the Lincoln: decor;location;service;attitude. We think it's worth the price.

title: “I will definitely return to the Casablanca next time I'm in New York”
text: We have been to New York City many times and have stayed in many hotels - large and small. The Casablanca is by far the best as far as value for the money. Reasonably priced rooms (for New York), larger than usual rooms (for New York) and many more amenities than we've had in any other hotel (in New York.) The staff is very friendly and welcoming. The hotel is clean. The breakfast excellent. The wine and cheese very nice. The cookies and coffee available at all hours a treat.

title: “Wonderful experience”
text: Great location, service was excellent provided by top notch staff. We enjoyed the all aspects of our stay.

title: “The Very Best Urban Hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed at Fairmont Battery Wharf in Aug 2011 for a weekend getaway. 
It was without a doubt the very best urban hotel I have ever stayed, both within and outside the States. Their level of service was phenomenal! 
It was a little difficult to find the main building and entrance to be honest, but upon arrival the doorman opened the door as soon as he spotted us with a sincere smile and greetings. 
The check in was very smooth. Then the front desk person walked us to our room. Upon leaving he said to let him know if there was anything we needed. He was very polite throughout our encounter. I was very impressed because he was such a young man yet so polite, kind, and professional. I wish I remembered his name! 
Our room was bright, sophisticated, spacious, and spotlessly clean. It had a lovely harbor view from the large windows. The room decor was modern yet very warm and relaxing. I immediately felt home. The bathroom was elegant and very well designed. 
We wanted to have some coffee before heading out, then thought the coffee maker in the room was not working. So I called the front desk. Then he sent us help immediately! Before even hanging up the phone two gentlemen knocked the door. Both of them were very polite. One of them found that the power switch was off. I felt so sorry for the trouble I gave them, but they were so polite and friendly. 
The following day (Saturday), we went to the front desk to ask about the area. This day the same person who checked our coffee machine the previous day (his name was Brett, I think and I hope I remember his name correctly!) was there. Then we learned about Hey Market. It was a few minutes walk from the hotel and sounded like a fun place to visit. So we decided to check it out. There were many vendors selling a lot of interesting fruits and vegetables for a fraction of price we normally pay. We bought a lot of them and brought them back to the hotel. 
Our hotel room had a small fridge stocked with snacks and drinks, so we removed some of those and put our fruits in it. After that I talked to Brett at the front desk to let him know about it. What he did was so impressive. He offered to bring additional fridge to our room for us to use freely without worrying about the other fridge with electric counter. Within just a minute the fridge was delivered. A gentlemen brought the fridge and set it up for us. He was very polite and professional too. 
Throughout our stay, their level of service was beyond anything we could imagine. We felt completely pampered and deeply impressed. I do not recall receiving such attentive and heart warming service at any other urban hotels in the world! 
For that, I highly recommend this hotel to anyone who visits Boston!

title: “one of the best ever”
text: Love staying here when I can. Perfect location mixed with the perfect staff and attention. Can't say enough about them.

title: “Hudson is a Bar not a hotel”
text: Booked the Hudson despite its high price. The photos showed on the Internet made me believe it was a fantastic place. The reception area, bar, library and restaurant and indeed great. Took an elevator to my room and when the door opened I could not believe how small it was. The bed was not a King, not even a Queen, I do not know what size it was, but at 6´1" my feet stuck out the end. The TV was from 20 years ago, maybe 15". There was no real closte only a curtain with a space maybe 10" deep to hand 2 shirts. The toilet was even smaller. The desk is a joke, totally useless from its size. You could not walk around the bed, you had to walk sideways since there was no space. The bathtub was kid sized, with vertical ends so you could not get in and relax, you had to sit. The bathtub plug did not work. The phone suddenly stopped working and was never fixed. Don´t even think about room service, the tray will not fit in the room. We were two in this room and I had to leave the room to pack 2 suitcases. Despite booking a 4 night stay I left after the first night and checked in at the Waldorf Astoria, much cheaper, lots of luxury and a large room.

title: “Business Trip To Indy. Stayed here for 5 nights”
text: Just an okay hotel but the price was right! Not as expensive online if you book through priceline!

title: “Expected a little better for the price”
text:
I have to agree with many of the reviewers below. Two years ago when I had business in the area I stayed at the Marriott a few doors down. I went to the bar, used the gym, and thought the room and hotel to be nice overall. I hoped the same from the Lex but in a side-by-side comparison the Lex was a bit tired looking, and at $325/night for my room I was expecting a bit more.
I will say my room was clean and my sleep was comfortable. Checkin and check out was quick. I was on the 6th floor facing 48th street so there was the expected sounds of the city.... But the Bose noise counseling headphones I bought for flying have paid off with dividends - highly recommend for the business traveler. But there was a worn feel about the hotel. Stepping off the elevators you could see it in the halls of the hotel. The Hotel room was similar. My biggest issue was with the bathroom where the shower curtain was spotty with mold towards the bottom and the hinges on the door were rusty.... Those are cheap fixes, but they must have been like that for some time. Not a dealbreaker for me, something I'd expect at a lower end chain off I-95 to deal with for a night for a hundred bucks. But regardless of the fact that this was the city, for the price I paid I expected better. Being turned off I didn't use the gym, but did stop in and checked it out... Give it a thumbs-up. Checked out the bar but the scene was dead (on a night the Yankees were playing a playoff game). So I went around the block to Connelys on 47th for a bit more life.... Good for a beer and the ambiance....
So similar to what others said, if you're in and out of the room, the place is fine. I'll be checking out one of the other area hotels next time I'm in for business though for a better price and ambiance. Marriott gets the head to head for my two experiences....

title: “Absolutely Wonderful Resort!!!!!”
text: I do not understand how anyone could possibly give this hotel a bad review. It is absolutely gorgeous. It is a luxury hotel with impeccable service. We just got back from a week stay (May 23-29, 2004). We have three children (ages 4 1/2, 2 1/2 and 7 months). The kids loved the hotel and are already asking when we can go back. We stayed in a regular guest room. Upon arrival, we asked for a microwave and refrigerator for our room. These items were quickly brought to our room and were great to have with the small children. The rooms are spacious and very clean (I am very germ-conscious because of the children). The staff at the hotel is wonderful. Every single employee (from pool staff to bell hop to front desk, etc.) would say "hello" and ask if we needed anything when we walked by. They definitely want to provide 5-star service. The hotel grounds are beautiful. There is a botanical garden and waterfalls all over the place (beautiful at night). Our children loved the pools (there are 5 of them). There is a water spray area for toddler/small children and the slide and lazy river were great for our 2 1/2 and 4 1/2 year old. I saw much older children enjoying them as well. We researched many hotels before choosing this JW Marriot, and we have vacationed in many luxury hotels and this definitely ranks as one of the most classy and prettiest hotels we have ever stayed at. We will be back!!!!!

title: “Great Concierge named , Jeffrey”
text: although the check in was a little rocky , our stay was magnificent. the rooms were clean and modern. it was a little strange that each of the restaurants was under different management which left the guests feeling slightly disjointed. concierge was helpful and kind...great with the kids. hotel was pet friendly.

title: “Enormous room!”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights at the start of our trip to the US and were very pleased with the accomodation. The rooms were absolutely enormous -ours was a king which had an interconnecting door to a 2 x double bedded room for our 2 kids. We could have all easily fitted into one room and still had room to spare.
We thought the location was fine, as it was close to the exhibition centre and also close to the metro station to catch a train to Hollywood. The facilities within the hotel are also good, with plenty of exercise options for those who are keen. Breakast was complimentary and had plenty of variety. We had dinner one night at the bar downstairs which had a good atmoshere but the food was average. The restaurant Louie Bottega was only a block away and was a good dinner option. All in all a good start to our holday and we would definitely return.

title: “Great choice and would go back”
text: Orchard Gardens turned out to be a great hotel. We stayed for 2 nights enroute to a Seattle cruise and were very comfortable. Staff were very friendly and helpful and rooms were great. The hotel is located very near to Chinatown and the San Francisco cable cars so everything was very accessible. Would definitely stay here again

title: “What a great hotel”
text:
Stayed in the Palomar for a week in Feb.
Got a great deal through Priceline and then a fantastic upgrade from the hotel itself.
My wife and I were visiting Washington DC for the first time and following research on TripAdvisor, decided to go for Dupont Circle location and was so lucky to pick the Palomar.
Our room was spacious, bright, modern, and clean.
Every amenity was provided with some nice extras such as wine evenings between 5 and 6pm, daily newspaper delivered to the room, and fresh coffee in the lobby each morning.
All the staff were fantastic - very pleasant and always helpful.
Its a great location, just 5 minutes from the Metro and has a choice of great restaurants and bars in the area.
If you enjoy walking, 15 minutes gets you to Georgetown with nice scenery on the way.
A great hotel in a good location, I will certainly use a Kimpton hotel again.

title: “great room, great location”
text: We were in Denver for a wedding and we all stayed at the Magnolia...we loved our room. Very comfortable. Great location. All of the other guests shared the feeling that it was a great place to stay. Free breakfast, free internet, a Starbucks attached that will deliver to your room AND a discount. We were able to walk around, use the free transportation in Denver on the 16th street mall,

title: “Great Place”
text: Great location, excellent room and friendly, helpful staff. This was our second stay there and it will be a primary choice for future trips. If you are looking for a great, small hotel in the mid town area, this is an excellent choice.

title: “Very comfortable and friendly hotel”
text: I like NYC very much, it's the most European like city in the US, and the Upper West Side with the Beacon Hotel is a charming part of NYC's atmosphere. The museums, cafes, restaurants, foodstores, travel agencies, boutiques, Central Park, subway stations, - just a step out of the hotel. I stayed at the Beacon - very comfortable hotel with friendly staff - for one week in July 2001. I'm planning to visit NYC this summer and to book a room at the Beacon Hotel again. I'm happy that almost three years after my previous stay the visitors of the TripAdvisor still rank the hotel very, very high. And surely it deserves that!

title: “Broken AC”
text: We stayed here on a Thursday and Friday night. When we checked in on Thursday it took forever for our room to cool down. It wasn't until middle of night till the room was at a comfortable temperature to sleep. then Friday morning when we got up our AC made a funny noise but was still blowing cool air so my family and I went to saw world. When we returned that night our AC was completely off. We called downstairs to complain because it was so hot. They sent a guy to look at it. He said a breaker was flipped but he got it blowing cold air. It took hours of cooling back down and making this awful noise all night long that it was hard to sleep. Then that morning it quit working again. It was only blowing hot air. I wanted to speak to manager that morning but she wasn't available to this afternoon after we were gone. She couldn't do anything for us because we booked with expedia and not through them. All she could offer was half off next time we stay. Umm I won't be going back. She also blamed us for not reporting noise it made Friday morning. I'm not an AC repair person. It was working when I left so I didn't report it. Pay a little more and stay somewhere else where the AC works properly and doesnt take hours to cool off.

title: “Stylish Hotel in a convienent location”
text:
I stayed at the Liaison Hotel with my husband and toddler for one night in early May. I had found an excellent rate through travelzoo.com. The hotel is located about 2 blocks from train station so if you are traveling by train it is a very easy walk. We opted to park our car at the train station because it is about half the price of using the hotel parking. The hotel is also fairly convienent to the Mall attractions. We walked, I believe it was not more than a mile. 
We arrived fairly early in the day and we pleasantly surprised that they had a room ready for us and we were checked in right away. The decor of the hotel is sleek and modern. Our room was typical in terms of size and was very clean. The beds were VERY comfortable and the furnushing seemed to be fairly new.
I was happy with our stay and would definitely stay again and would recommend this hotel to friends and family.

title: “In the middle of everything”
text: We decided to have a staycation in Charlotte without the kids. I put a bid in through Priceline and got it for $85/night, kind of shock I got it for that price. The hotel is nice that has a nice bar, and plenty of eating places around. The room was what you would expect it to be, but honestly since it is right in the heart of Charlotte your not trying to be in your room too long. We walked Uptown just to explore. Internet is complimentary for the weekend which seemed to work perfectly. The check in people were very professional. We had a king room with a large bathroom. Parking was $18/night but that is expected if your staying downtown anywhere. All in all it was a great place to stay and we would consider staying here again in the future.

title: “Good for New York Standards”
text:
We stayed for 10 nights, ideal location to 72nd street subway which has an excellent service to Times Square and Penn Station. Across the road Fairways supermarket and deli next door, plenty of restaurants nearby.
Hotel staff - typical New York but not service focused, hotel itself dated, good for New York standards.
Our room was a 1 brm suite on the 18th floor facing Broadway, kitchen facilities were good, room cleaned every day, bathroom on the small side.
View from room was overlooking the roofs and Broadway, with the wooden water tanks on top of buildings and being entertained at night by the ballet dancers practising at the ballet school.

title: “half good half bad”
text:
I stayed here 2 nights in May. 
The Bad half: I had arrived early and let them know I was there, check in was 3:00 and so I joined my party who had their rooms. I waited until 3:40 to go up to the front desk and was told my room was not ready and they would call housekeeping to get an update. In the meantime, she started to handle another guest while I stood there so I sat down on their couches and at 4:00 was motioned up to the desk. Now it was ready, they apologized and asked IF I would like a complimentary breakfast. I was still in a good mood, said it wasn't a big deal and said that's okay, turning it down. As I walked away I thought why didn't they just give it to me, why do they ask me if I want a freebeie? What they are doing is telling me they don't want to give away anything unless I am cheap enough to accept. It's just never happened to me like that and I thought it was odd. A couple hours after claiming my room I was in a state of undress and hear a knock. While I was grasping for clothes and before I could even say just a minute, the door opens and it is a hotel employee not knowing the room was taken (obviously). He got halfway in the room (I am female) and could hardly speak English enough to apologize and quickly shut the door. I didn't report it because I thought no harm done, it was a mistake and made sure I had the chain on for the rest of my stay. One morning for breakfast I joined a party of three at a table who had just ordered their breakfast. Knowing that, I didn't ask for a menu, I just asked for a cup of coffee. Twice. In the meantime, he brought them their food, etc, and never got coffee for me. It was like he was ignoring me because I came late and wasn't expected. So don't expect any special consideration from servers here , they have a high expectation of protocol. The cream on this crappy weekend came when I got home and for a whole week had $400 taken off my credit card as a "hold", meaning that amount was taken away from my purchase ability. I called the hotel and it was their room hold for incidentals. I had checked out on a Sunday yet by Thursday it was still on. They said it is up to the bank to release it. I don't know if that was a story or not, my company paid for the room, so that $400 was for my snack bar and movies? I didn't use any of extras and I checked out on Sunday, so I don't know why the hold took so long to clear. I didn't call my bank to verify who really is responsible, but I am in my 40's, stayed in rooms around the U.S. and Italy and this has never happened. It is like this hotel is too good for their own clientele and doesn't trust them . If you a good person, go with the flow, and not demanding or a diva, you may get taken advantage of like I felt I was. I probably should have done more to make a stink about all these issues as they happened, people can't take advantage of you unless you let them. However, I am of the Show-me attitude, and if you don't, I won't come back and will tell everyone I know how crappy I was treated. We are as dangerous as demanding customers. 
The Good: Very nice rooms, clean and good bedding, And a nice view. Good location.

title: “Wow”
text:
This hotel is beautiful, very ornate setting. We were asked if we would like to upgrade for a moderate fee, we agreed and had an executive suite on the 23rd floor. The room was huge with two double beds, lounge, two bathrooms, breakfast, non alcoholic drinks and nibbles all day including savory nibbles in the evening.
The staff were fantastic, couldn't do enough for you and we're very forthcoming with any information you required. 
I would recommend his hotel.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: I really liked this hotel and its staff. Every staff member we met (from doorman, bellboy, reception etc) was extremely friendly and helpful. The hotel and rooms are very nicely decorated and have all the necessary conveniences. Would definitely recommend it.

title: “Excellent service, great management”
text:
For my friend's wedding celebration, I wanted to do something really special for her.
So, I called the Sheraton's concierge, and they worked closely with me to plan a beautiful surprise for my friend and her new husband. They decorated the room beautifully. They called me to make sure everything was perfect and followed up with me afterwards to make sure everything was to my satisfaction. 
I also want to thank Kyle Overacker who went above and beyond to make sure everything turned our perfectly.

title: “Typical Marriott, good location”
text:
The San Francisco Marriott is a great choice if you are attending a convention at Moscone. Only a block away, it's a relief not to have to walk too far after spending a whole day on your feet at a convention.
It is a standard, full-service Marriott. The beds are comfortable and the rooms are an okay size for being downtown. Overall, it didn't leave me with an overwhelming impression one way or the other, which is sad because I really wanted to be impressed by the hotel. 
The service was good and the bellmen especially helpful. Room service was the typical Marriott menu. Yet, I'm frustrated by the charge for internet service.
There are several good restaurants close by, with a movie theatre across the street. The Whole Foods Market is a few blocks away if you want to get some nice snacks. 
I would probably stay here again for convenience sake because how close it is to the convention center. However, if I was staying in San Fran for other reasons, the Fairmont and the Palace would be my first choices.

title: “Highly recommended”
text: My wife and I spent 8 days over Christmas and New Year’s at Hotel Elysee. It was our honeymoon and we were treated like royalty – from the porters, the concierge through to the hostesses in the lobby / lounge area, the service was personal and truly impeccable. After 8 nights, the Elysee really began to feel like our 2nd home. The hotel is quiet, comfortable and “old-fashioned” in a good way. With its close proximity to 5th Ave & Rockefeller, Park Street, Central Park etc, the location could hardly be better. Our room was very spacious – enormous by New York standards – with a bath & shower, separate reception / cupboard and storage area and a large balcony. Breakfasts are not extravagant but more than adequate – a buffet consisting of fruit salad, yoghurt, cereals, eggs, bagels and juice/tea/coffee. I was initially sceptical about their evening wine receptions, but those actually turned out to be really pleasant, with reasonable wines and great cheese and olive platters; a great pre-dinner reprieve after a long day of sightseeing and shopping. Our biggest gripe was perhaps the fact that all the floors are serviced by one elevator only; however it was only during the busy morning periods that we experienced the lift slow and congested. All in all we had a fantastic time at this hotel, and we would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a calm and relaxing mid-town location. Provided that the high levels of service are maintained, we will most certainly be back.

title: “Fantastic service!”
text: I am writing this review for the people who think customer service is gone! A young man named Jada at the W hotel in Seattle should teach everyone about customer service! I called to make a reservation for my sons wedding night and Jada took care of everything! He made sure that it will be a special night.Thw W hotel is the place to stay in Seattle! The location is great and the hotel is fantastic! Top all of this off with the best customer service in Seattle and this is a must stay for everyone when coming to Seattle! Every hotel should have a Jada! Thanks!

title: “Reasonably priced, but noisy”
text:
I stayed here for vacation days following a business trip.
Plus: quaint, incredible location for Pike Place Market, good value for what you pay.
Minus: one of the noisiest hotels in which I've ever stayed, despite signing a notice about "quiet hours." The quiet hours don't apply to their building noises or trucks loading/unloading - they just want the guests to be quiet. Only one key per room, and staff watch you go in and out - not much privacy. Desk staff seem scatterbrained - really need multiple people at the desk at peak hours. Difficult to shower in old-style tub. I didn't see any handle bars for people with limited mobility. My tub kept rocking back and forth as I showered. Not especially comforting.

title: “Great Location”
text:
We stayed at the Park Savoy for 10 days,First five days on the 6th floor which was a tiny room however we managed as we are petite people.The room was safe and clean,daily fresh towels and amenities. We were very happy until the early wake up call from the construction site which was just behind the room.The second room was more spacious it was on to the roadside however the noise was unbearable worse than the construction as there was no sound proof.
Overall we were very happy with the hotel the staff were friendly and helpful, we thought the hotel itself was good deal with its location for the price of 150 usd per night.Located on the 7th avenue with the metro stop just 2 mins away,10m mins to coloumbus circle,5 mins to central park and 10 mins walk to 5th avenue and lots of eateries around.
The wifi is not free its usd 9.95 for 24 hrs and only one pc can get connected once its purchased.

title: “really nice”
text:
I stayed at the Hyatt Regency Chicago back in Sept of ’06. I was attending a conference there and I thought that hotel was very well accommodating to the massive amount of people. The rooms are typical Hyatt, clean and new, the bathroom was kinda of small, I have stayed at many lower end hotels that had bigger bathrooms, nevertheless, it was all marble and very clean.
Overall, I really enjoyed my stay and would recommend it.

title: “Love this place!”
text:
My family and I just spent 5 nights at this great hotel. We had a room on the 5th floor facing the internal courtyard. 
Hotel location is central for shopping and convenient for using the public transport system.
Wine reception is great for a couple of pre-dinner drinks, love this about Kimpton Hotels.
We experienced great service at this hotel. Bobby on reception is a great operator, really friendly and checked in on how we were throughout our stay.
Veronica from housekeeping was also really friendly.
Another friendly front desk person recommended The Grove (Mission & Third Street) for great food.....highly recommend this place or breakfast, lunch and dinner and only a short walk from the hotel.

title: “Very good stay”
text: This is a very nice hotel. Clean and very nicely appointed rooms (contemporary style). The staff is outstanding. Depending on where your business in the city is, the hotel might not be be walking distance to your destination - other hotels in the city might be more convenient from this perspective. However, the hotel is only 2 blocks from the North Station T-stop - green and orange lines. I stayed here during a convention when other hotels where I usually stay were much more expensive, and the saving was well worth it.

title: “Good Hotel, dirty swimming pool”
text: We stayed for two nights. Very courteous and helpful staff. Really good breakfast. Room was clean but the carpets were old. The bathroom's curtain smell. The pool was not swimmable. There was layer of dead bugs on the pool water.

title: “"Excellent place to stay"”
text: I recently stayed at this hotel for the 2nd time in approximately 4 months and had a great experience both times. The staff was particularly helpful especially Terence, Samad and Cody. I arrived prior to check-in time and they were very good about helping me to check in early based on availability. Not only that, but Cody, the restauraunt manager was very gracious. We sat for 10-15 minutes and a waiter/waitress never showed up. He was very good about managing this situation appropriately and was very apologetic and even explained why that was the case. I used priceline.com to book this hotel both times and I am very happy that I got this hotel both times. They make it very for someone moving to JAX in a few months to feel comfortable with the decision to make JAX my new home.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: I'm relectant to write this review, because this hotel is one of those best kept secrets in NYC. I was tasked with finding a hotel to stay in for a business meeting. What a find! First, the hotel is situated in a great location. You are within walking distance of Times Square, Broadway shows, The Diamond District, Fifth Avenue, Central Park, Rockefellar Center. The rooms were great...they were very clean, cozy and spacious for NYC. The beds were something else...you felt like you were sleeping on a cloud!! We ate in the dining room for lunch and also had breaks during out meeting. The food and the service is very, very good. No complaints were uttered by anyone in the group. The overall ambiance of the hotel is wonderful. It's quaint, yet sophisticated. The staff was very personable, prompt and accomodating. Is there a down side to this hotel?? Just two small items...the street noise at 3:30 a.m. when the grabage truck comes is annoying...night two I turned on the A/C with the fan to drown out the noise..so night two I slept like a baby. The meeting rooms are on the small side. The next time, we will pick a week when the larger meeting room is available. As you can see, we will definitely be going back!!!!

title: “Good hotel, excellent location, comfortable and clean. Make sure you get your parking validated every day.”
text: A good hotel within reasonable (1-2 miles) walking distance of many Philadelphia attractions. Clean and modern. Rooms are a bit on the small side but not uncomfortably so. I didn't try any of the restaurants on premises. Fitness room was large, well equipped and open 24 hours.

title: “Great location”
text:
We go to SFO a few times a year. I love staying at the Westin's for the Heavenly bed. And I get SPG points. The hotel is nice, nothing spectacular. It is clean, that’s the most important thing for me. The bathrooms were small. The front desk staff was nice and helpful. 
We like the locations; everything is a short walk away. This time we got a Corner Grand Deluxe King room

title: “Great place to stay for a vacation with your girlfriends!”
text: Stayed at the Belvedere in August with 3 of my girlfriends when we went to NYC for vacation. This hotel was perfect in the sense that while you're in NYC you only need a place to crash and take a shower! The room was big enough for all of us, our luggage, and our shopping bags we aquired while there. The staff was great and helpful at all times. THe room we stayed in was a little outdated, but very clean and not noisy at all. Its in a great location...only 2 blocks from Times Square and the subway. THe bathroom was a little small, but that's the only negative I have to say about this place. If you're looking for a resaonably priced, adequdaely sized hotel near all of NYC great attractions, then I highly recommend this place!

title: “Was pleasantly suprised”
text: At first I was skeptical about staying in a Days Inn. I have been at a Days Inn before and was not very pleased. However, this has to be the CADILLAC of Days Inn. The room was clean, spacious, smelled good, updated everything. And the PRICE was GREAT. I travel a lot and when I travel to Houston Hobby again I WILL stay here. They picked me up at the airport by very friendly and informative staff. You can't go wrong with this location.

title: “Best Place to Stay in Charlotte”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for a 2 week trip. We came here for me to have a surgery and recuperate. I picked this hotel after reading the reviews on Trip advisor. Not only is the cancellation policy awesome (until 4pm the day of arrival), but the hotel is extremely clean. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The cleaning people in the rooms do a great job (and even do the dishes!!). The hot breakfast buffet every morning changes up daily and the happy hour food Mon thru Thurs could be enough for dinner (most nights). You are within walking distance to Charlotte's uptown area. Lots of restaurants, coffee shops, Sabrett's hot dog stands, the performing arts center, and a discovery zone (for kids) are really close.
