Suggestion: (1) Go to the grocery store and get a couple of things for snacks since the room has a full size fridge/freezer, microwave and stove top. (2) Don't walk around too much at night (gets pretty desolate after dark during the week). (3) Venture out to Huntersville (take I-77 North to Exit 23, go right off exit ramp) for some good home style restaurants.

title: “Fab hotel, great location!”
text:
Just got back from the Omni. Had a twin room on the 18th floor facing the bay. We'd booked a standard room so were happy to get such a great room. We had two double beds which were so comfortable. The room was spacious, modern and clean, the bathroom was spotless and the shower was perfect.
The breakfast was expensive, but the hotel is next door to the Gaslamp where there is plenty of choice for food. The trolley is outside the hotel so you can get to anywhere you want easily.
The doormen are always cheerful and helpful, whenever I popped out the front for a cigarette they would always chat and pass the time of day.
You can hear the trains, but it's not that bad, the odd bell now and then, which didn't bother us at all. We heard no noise from inside the hotel. I travel a lot and have stayed in many hotels, this one was lovely and I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again.
As two girls we felt really safe in the area, we were coming back late at night and had no problems. 
If you stay here make sure you walk to Seaport village, 10 minutes walk, really pretty shops, restaurants and views. our other choice is Fred's Mexican restaurant on the Gaslamp, a good happy hour and tasty food.
We had a good look round San Diego and feel we couldn't have stayed at a better hotel. Easily a four star!

title: “Clean, good value, right price”
text: This hotel is exactly as others reviewed it; very clean small room place in a good location for a good price. The retro bathroom was very clean, hot water pressure no problem, air conditioning worked. A no-frills place whose reasonable cost enabled us to stay in NYC. For a clean, safe place to just sleep and leave, it was fine. Being near subway 1 and R, very convenient, and a Starbucks on back side street for wifi in the am. Our visit was a Saturday night, all my other bids on 3 stars through Priceline had failed. This met our needs and budget. We were allowed to check in early, and leave our bag as we traveled around, that was very appreciated.

title: “Comfort after arriving on a late flight”
text: I arrived late at night after a late flight and it was nice to arrive in the hotel. The lobby was very nice and the room was very nice. The staff by the check-in desk in the lobby were very friendly. I had a refrigerator and microwave too in the room. My minor complaints about the hotel are as follows: the free breakfast only had one choice of 2% milk (there was no skim or low fat option) and also there were no bananas left when I came to eat my breakfast. Also, the free computer in the lobby had a very slow Internet connection. I stayed at a different Super 8 and had the same slow Internet connection, so it may be that these hotels are required to subscribe to some Super 8 Internet connection. This connection could use a speed improvement. I would most likely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Already planning a return visit !!”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights recently with my daughter and would not hesitate to recommend.
Requested a king size room on a higher floor looking on to the street and got exactly that. Our room was on the 16th floor with a fantastic view of the empire state building. the room was a goog size(by new York standards), bathroom lovely and the bed, oh the bed, most comforatable bed I have ever slept in! The staff, we found were always friendly and helpful.
The breakfast was good and a nice start to the day, our experience of the breakfast room was good and also maybe we were lucky, but no real problem with the lifts, ok you maybe had to wait a few minutes, but hey your on vacation, whats the rush ! Rather stay here anyday than some large chain hotel near times square.

title: “Loved the waterfront location and all the top-flight amenities”
text:
Got a decent Hotwire rate here. We were both a bit worried about staying at this hotel based on some tepid reviews. But we really had no serious problems.
The desk clerk was very nice when we arrived at 11 a.m. and gave us a spacious room on the 8th floor with a view of Fort Point Channel. The room was very comfortable, cool, and quiet. We both liked the huge bathroom with separate shower, which had great water pressure. The translucent window that slid open above the bed was an odd accent, which meant if we got up in the night to visit the bathroom we had to grope around in the dark, so as to avoid illuminating the bedroom and thus wake each other up. But really, no big deal. 
To avoid the steep hotel prices, on the first morning, Sunday, we brewed cups of coffee in the room (wished there was enough coffee for more than one cup apiece!), then walked over to South Station, 4 minutes away, and had breakfast at the Au Bon Pain for a total of $10 for two. The second morning we went to Scali Deli across the street, also around $10 for two.
Since we had prebooked the Provincetown ferry for a daytrip this was a perfect location; we could walk there in about 10-15 minutes. We also walked to the North End, Park Street, the new Harbor Walk, and the ICA. People who have never been to Boston may find the location a bit remote, but we loved being by the water and enjoyed the super-easy airport access via the Silver Line bus to/from South Station, $2 per person each way. We also enjoyed the water view at the back of the hotel, very pleasant. 
The only negative was an insanely LOUD post-wedding party that jolted us awake at 2 a.m. in a nearby room the first night. Security visited them and told them to quiet down, but they didn't shut up for an hour. People can be so rude!

title: “Excellent Choice for what we wanted”
text: We went to Boston to see history and a great town. My wife and I have been to Boston several times before but this was the first time with our 9 year old. Millennium fit exactly what we wanted. Walk the Freedom Trail, take the Duck Tour, see all the historical aspects of Boston - this is a great location to do it all. The service was fantastic - late night check in, early morning help, cleaning staff - consistently nice, helpful and fast. The cookies next to the front desk helped whenever there was a short delay. We were able to book a last minute table at a high end restaurant through the front desk when no tables were available. The room was a bit tired, though it was kept nice and clean with supplies refreshed, but then were not there for a dramatic/romantic room, just sleep then off to the next adventure. I'd avoid the fixed price breakfast, the variety is nice, but it's a bit expensive. Overall I'd recommend the Millennium to any one who is going to Boston to do what we did.

title: “Valentine Celebration”
text: A wonderful time and a great feel to this hotel . Feeling like we were in a time capusle we enjoyed the ambience. Our room was a bit worn, and we were not aware that hotel was under renovation - till the day before our arrival - given that- we enjoyed this Seattle Classic and will have great memories - we spent Saturday nite in the lobby with a drink and a great pianist. Our room was spacious and clean. Customer service is great and I was treated to a plate of choclate covered strawberries , as I was celebrating my Birthday . We enjoyed Sunday Brunch at the Georgian, elegance and liesure - It is possible to stay in Seattle and not leave this hotel- although shopping in the city has to be enjoyed. We live about an hours drive from Seattle so we enjoy an overnite stay in the city, this is one of our best nite's out - I was raised in the Northwest and had always wanted to stay here - I was not disappointed.

title: “Amazing Hotel with Top-Notch Service”
text: We loved our stay at the Park Hyatt. Our suite was impeccable. In advance of our arrival, the hotel had set up a nice wooden crib (MUCH nicer than hotels typically have) for our baby (complete with a "baby welcome pack" including Bumble&Bumble baby bath products). We couldn't have asked for better service - we were able to check in early, and the front desk was very helpful in general with our questions/requests. I would absolutely stay here again.

title: “Great for families. "OK" overall”
text:
We stayed at Paradise Point for about a week after the Labor Day holiday. The property is great for families, as there are lots of kids and kid-friendly activities (feed the ducks, swimming pool a 0 grade that eventually deepens). They set up a Pack and Play in the very large walk-in closet that became our 2 y/o's "own room."
Hotel grounds were nice, but not "pristine" or particularly serene. It was definitely tropical in feel, but there's no mistaking it for a secluded island retreat, as some have suggested.
The tropical theme does not extend into the guest rooms, which is a little strange. The decor is light and colorful, but much more reminiscent of Cape Cod than Hawaii. Some have criticized the armoirs in the room as old, dirty and in need of a paint job. That's the way it's SUPPOSED to look, but it is not particularly aesthetic.
The room was large enough, the furniture too big for the space. We found the a/c to be effective at cooling, albeit loud. Same goes for the mini fridge-- also keeps you up at night.
Location was nice. Especially convenient to Sea World, though it would be nice if they ran a shuttle. I can understand why people are upset at having to pay $20 a night for parking (they comped us b/c we checked in as the place emptied out after the Labor Day holiday), but it allows them to advertise competitive room rates.
We did not have problems with light flooding the room in the a.m. We had blackout curtains on your sliding glass door and a wood front door. But I noticed not all rooms were this way. We also didn't have dirty carpet, as some complained of. 
Paradise Point offers a very interesting hotel concept. It is in need of some updating, but overall we enjoyed ourselves. However, if you're paying well above $200 a night on average, you are not getting a good deal for your dollar.

title: “Good but not great..”
text:
we stayed at the Millenium Hilton from the 4-7June... very busy weekend at the hotel...unfortunately we were checked in by the guy with attitude... so any request was too much for him... but the other front desk staff were fantastic... concierge was so so, too busy checking his emails to give me his attention.. the porters were always wanting to hail down a cab-don't know if they make money on the side??? we declined their offers and took the subway-very convenient. I do agree with the comment about the turndown service, they must only do it when the have time(as it was done the first night only)... We returned late one night after being out all day and our bed linen was filthy, changed but not clean... so at about 2330 we called to have it changed.. 
This was my first visit to NYC, next time I would stay somewhere in midtown or uptown... a smaller hotel maybe...but we did get great rates here when most hotels were booked out.
p.s we used a cab from JFK to the hotel and they charged the standard US45 + US10 for tolls and tip.. Because i really can't stand getting cabs we took the subway from the hotel back to JFK very easy...Take the A line to Howard Beach and change to the AIRTRAIN to your terminal...US7 ea in total.. The other option is booking a car to and from the airport i think their standard rate is US55 + US10 for tolls and tips..

title: “AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE!”
text: Numerous car break-ins, 2 cars were stolen from the front entrance. Daytime staff was very helpful, Nighttime is a different story; PJ the so called "security personel" is a shady character, he keeps the company of hookers, alcoholic friends at night. It's been going around that he is involved somehow with the break-ins and car thefts. MANAGEMENT needs to run background checks on their employees! The location is bad, right near the ghetto. The closest store in walking distance is the Dollar Store. The room was clean but beware of hidden charges. My 3G is faster than their 10.00 a week internet service. STAY HERE AT YOUR OWN RISK! The rooms are WAY smaller than the website shows.The TVs are from the 80's that half-way work. The laundry machine charges are outrageous. STAY AWAY!

title: “Historic Landmark Hotel in Downtown San Francisco”
text: We stayed at Sir Francis Drake for 4 days and found the accommodation and service exceptional. If you like a central downtown location and heritage hotels, which we do, this is the place for you. It is easy access away from all the places you want to visit in the City (i.e. shopping, restaurants, transite, theatres, etc.).

title: “DO NOT STAY!!!”
text: Do not stay here! Staff was rude and behind bullet proof glass. Terrible neighborhood, room was located facing Sherman way. Hookers live there along with others, this is more of a dirty apartment complex than a hotel! The pictures on the website was not the same hotel, they lied. Dirty rooms, the amenities listed on the website were not what the hotel had. Horrible experience and would NEVER again stay or recommend to anyone.

title: “Travel Lodge Century Blvd, LAX”
text: It was really fine for a quick stop over between flights. Nice service, good enough condition of our room. A little loud being on Century Blvd near the airport, but what can one expect being so close to the airport. Shuttle service to airpost every half hour, nice helpful man that drove the shuttle. They store your luggage if you have many and don't want to take it all up to your room which is good because they don't have elevators. For the price, we'd stay again for a quick stop-over.

title: “Average Location”
text:
As I entered the hotel, it looked like a typical Hampton Inn with the cleanliness and quality I have come to expect from this brand. They served free cans of light beer, wine, chicken wings, and cheese for the happy hour which was a nice surprise. The disappointing part of the stay was the hotel location. The only restaurant close by to this hotel was in the hotel next door according to the front desk. I have not had great success with food at hotel restaurants, so we elected to take a 15-20 minute drive to the nearest group of chain restaurants. It would be nice if restaurant selections were a little closer to this hotel, especially after enjoying the nice happy hour.
This hotel is in the flight path of the airport, but I did not notice the airplane noise after about 10pm. I'm not sure if I slept through it or the planes stopped flying for the night.

title: “nice hotel, conviniently located”
text: Very nice hotel: comfortable small clean rooms, small fridge comfy beds. Friendly staff and very close to convention center. The breakfast was extremely disappointing. I would recommend for business travelers.

title: “Super Nice and Convenient to Convention Center”
text: We opted for this hotel rather than the expensive conference hotel and were so glad we did. This is a very nice hotel with great linens and flat screen TV. Close to the convention center and a few blocks from some nice restaurants (but not much right next to the hotel). Hotel offered a shuttle if you didn't feel like walking. They offered free bottled water and even a breakfast to go if you didn't have time for the buffet. Staff was very nice. There was an error on the bill when we checked out but it was easily resolved. Free parking in the garage. If you're a NASCAR fan, the Hall of Fame is across the street.

title: “Outstanding service, nice hotel.”
text: This is a nice hotel at a descent price for San Fran. Located at Market & Powell, 10 minute walk or a cheap cab ride to Union Square. Very quiet. Beds ok. Room service ok. Dog friendly. Our room was very clean & moderate size. nice bathroom, some rooms have tubs. Has a pool & spa, we didn't have time to go. We would stay there again if we get a similar price.

title: “Amazing location, but...”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Pennsylvania (New York) for 2 nights. The room was big, but very old bathroom and not clean at all. This Hotel is very well located, downtown NY, just in front of MSG! You can reach every good place to visit by walk. But, they really need to fix/upgrade their bathrooms soon...

title: “Sleep cheap, Eat well”
text: Forewarned was fore-prepared. Having read the reviews of this hotel we took a flier and were pleasantly surprised. We saved almost $100 over comparables available in the same general area and wound up with a clean, quite room with a comfortable bed and a pretty convenient launching point to visit Philadelphia. Parking was easy and free. The only services/amenities we used except for check-in/out was fixing a dying smoke detector which was accomplished 15 minutes after I reported it at 11:00 pm. Everyone was courteous. So we took the savings and had dinner on the Moshula (see review) which was wonderful and wound up with a really memorable experience to take home, something we would have been unlikely to get from spending $100 or so more for a hotel room elsewhere. Stay here and spend the difference on something that REALLY makes a difference.

title: “Stay somewhere else”
text: For this price, I think you can definitely find a better hotel. The pictures on their site are a bit deceiving. The bathroom is so tiny that two people would not be able to stand in there. There is no closet to hang your clothes, no lobby--everything is sooo narrow, you felt claustrophic. On top of that, the location is absolutely horrible. We didn't even feel safe walking around at 8 p.m. to get food. The area is dark and scary at night with trash piled everywhere. However, I must say, the staff was very friendly and courteous. They helped us with our baggage as well as helped get us a taxi any time we needed one.

title: “good value, great location”
text:
I rely on Trip Advisor to book my hotels and find the reviews extremely helpful, the ones for Georgetown Suites no exception. I discount the errant review and the occasional bad review about snippy service or the ironing board that didn't show up at 2 a.m. when requested. So, in booking, I disregarded the supposed rude front desk and the bed bugs, not finding them particulary credible.
This was a very good experience at Georgetown Suites. The location is terrific, steps from the activitiy of Georgetown but wonderfully quiet, right off an historic canal which is still seasonally operational for touritsts. This is a property which is geered towards extended corporate stays. With that, in my experience, comes a certain "hands off" attitude from the proprietors. After all, most of the residents don't need the more touristy, attentive services. But I found the staff here more than accommodating, albeit not flowering me with attention which I don't crave anyway. They provided me with maps, gladly called cabs and were professional in all respects.
The generous breakfast, included in the price, was more than ample with fresh fruit and more predictable fare like cereal and packaged buns. 
The rooms are indeed huge. The front desk let me take a look at two to see which one I preferred. The furnishings are corporate-bland but absolutely fine. Huge, working kitchens and dining room tables! Some tacky ornamental flower arrangements were quickly secreted away for our stay, too painful to look at, and reinstated upon check-out.
No bugs or thieving maids.
I stayed with my parents and slept on the sleeper couch. They had a separate bedroom with a king-sized bed. My parents sleep like Republicans, in separate beds, so were a little disappointed they had to bunk together. Go figure. As for me, after two nights I felt like I'd been bent over picking strawberries all day in the field. The sleeper mattress was as sway-backed as an old mule which approximated my energy level after a couple of not-too-rough nights. But put the kids on it; your back is too unforgiving.
All things considered, this property is a winner. I would highly recommend it for families, less so for young lovers or romantics. But with the money you save you can dine at one of the terrific gourmet or romantic restaurants within blocks of the hotel.
I hope this is as helpful as the reports I read before booking at Georgetown Suites. By the way, their site beat all of the travel site prices: $ 180/per night for three people with breakfast and local restaurant discounts.
Robert G., Boston

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
We have just arrived back home after a one week stay at the Hotel Mulberry . The hotel was excellent. Great location in Chinatown, and just by Little Italy. Not far to the subway.
What can I say; the room was great and spacious, even with to queen size beds. The bathroom was nice, with clean towels everyday. And the staff were excellent.
So if you want a great stay - Stay at Hotel Mulberry.

title: “The best hotel ever!”
text: We spent a long time researching hotels in downtown Seattle for our 25th wedding anniversary. We are so glad/thankful we selected The Inn At The Market! It was perfect. We had a beautiful room overlooking Puget Sound. (Deluxe water view-8th floor) We watched the ferries and boats go by our window. The hotel was extremely quiet - it was like we were the only guests. We were treated kindly. On our arrival they set out a card and special chocolates for our anniversary. I can't say enough - I wholeheartedly recommend this hotel to anyone who wants a very special place to stay. We plan to make this a yearly event - we had the best time!

title: “Estela Estrada of banquet department”
text: Estela Estrada in Banquet department is taking such great care of me and my team. She is extremely polite and helpful. She is a delight to work with and we will request her to work our functions when we return here later this month.

title: “You can do MUCH better in San Francisco. And BEWARE of the RIP-OFF mini-bar.”
text:
I certainly wouldn't have chosen this hotel if it were not for a convention that had us staying there. 
There are definitely a few things that make this a decent hotel
- good service
- super responsive and friendly staff
- super comfortable beds, sheets, pillows - i mean, REALLY good
- good rates
- if you're in tower 1, the views are beautiful from most floors
HOWEVER - 
- the rooms are totally hit or miss - my room in Tower 3 had a tiny window and was really dark but a room I stayed in in tower 1 was nice a few years back and my co-worker had a much bigger room with big windows and a view of the parking garage. no consistency. 
- the mini-bar is OUTRAGEOUS - $8.75 for a small Snickers. They hide the price sheet to screw with you. SO angry about the $20 nightly snack - A vitamin water and a rice krispy treat for $20? Are you serious?
- it is a MAJOR conference hotel. There is nothing unique, charming, or warm about this place. It is meant to "house" thousands of people at once
- The restaurant downstairs is a complete rip-off. $20 for an omelette. A very light breakfast for 2 with no alcohol = $75 plus tip. I mean, really. I live in Manhattan and wouldn't pay that for a limitless brunch with mimosas and MUCH better food. 
- The internet is SUPER slow and it is not wireless. So you have to practically rip the in-room router off the wall to get the computer anywhere close to your bed
For the rate I paid, I would be tempted if I were in a financial pinch. But you can find MUCH better places in this city (Hotel Vitale, either Westin, etc.)

title: “Gem in the rough”
text: We were bumped up to this property from the regular Marriott next door when everything was overbooked due to Midway closing at 2 am in the morning. I couldn't have been more thrilled. The property is either brand new or completely renovated recently - it smells brand new inside and everything is sparking clean, modern and crisp-looking. The cafe' area is adorable with healthy and quick, simple (and inexpensive!) options for breakfast as compared to the airport... and much better quality. Free Starbucks coffee in the morning while you print your boarding passes from the dedicated terminals in the lobby area, too! The staff (Nicole, I believe?) was SO sweet and welcoming after what had been a long night full of delays and lines. She welcomed us as we walked in and knew our party by name without consulting the computer - said she had been expecting us and had everything ready so we literally could just get the key and head up. She made sure to offer us toothbrushes and other ammenities knowing everyone coming in hadn't gotten their bags back, and gave us extra pillows just in case. She was really so very sweet, but also knowlegeable and efficient, which speaks volumes. The room was fabulous, with a separate bathroom door closure, a king bed and a sparkling clean room. I loved that there was a focus on being green here with notes about it on the bedside table (very prevalent in Chicago in general - love it!)! The experience was short - 5 hours before we had to be back at the airport - but the people who were there were all great, smiling and very congenial. The hotel has a great vending area with healthy and even heatable meals (if you have a suite with a microwave, or maybe there was one for general use?) and lots of great lobby space. All in all, a gem in an otherwise normal "airport hotel" strip, which usually means well-used and shows it. Highly recommend! Oh, there is also a free shuttle to/from Midway right outside the front door.. every 20 minutes!!!

title: “Comfortable, convenient, well-appointed, and affordable”
text:
The River Inn is a great find. Thanks, Trip Advisor! There are clean hotels in the District for less money, but not much, and I thought River Inn a cut above usual hotels. 
The rooms are simple studio apartments - ideal for a business traveller. If I ever have a long stay in DC, I'll choose the River Inn. You have a full kitchen, a big desk, Wifi included in the room rate, a good couch for sitting and working, a comfortable bed, and a modern bathroom. Linens and carpets and kitchen were all immaculate. 3G network coverage on AT&T was good throughout the building. 
The walk to the well-served Foggy Bottom / G.W.U. metro station takes about 4 minutes. The walk is through residential streets, but busy ones. 
The front desk staff were cheerful and helpful. I imagine that this is a top choice for visiting family among university students. I had business in several neighborhoods across DC and in Arlington, and I arrived by train from BWI to Union Station. I found the location most convenient.

title: “Great location, choose another hotel”
text:
With what you pay here, you can do better. The walls were paper thin, we could actually
hear the neighbors engaging in normal conversation. The bed had a sinkhole in it and needed replacement and the ice machine in our floor and the one right above were broken the entire week we were there.We were extremely disappointed

title: “Nice remodel, fantastic beds, nicest hotel at LAX!”
text:
The "new" Sheraton Gateway, after an extensive lobby overhaul, the addition of the overpriced but above-average Shula's, and room renovation (but not the bathrooms) is a pleasant place to stay. Like many reviewers state, it's a bit cold - check the pics - greys, blues, and black. While it's a modern feel that looks contemporary, it doesn't feel welcoming, but that will change once you try the new beds, the best part of the renovation. The pool area is fine, small, shaded, and
close to the runways (only the Radisson sits closer), but you won't hear much noise from the room. This hotel is a good deal if you're not looking for a warm feel and can spend between $70-100 through Hotwire or LastMinuteTravel. Also, be aware - parking is a nightmare, valet is good but expensive, and street spots are non-existent. The Sheraton's the newest remodel in the area at the 4 star level, far nicer than the Westin, Marriot, or Crowne Plaza.

title: “Our stay here was great”
text: Our stay at the Drury Riverwalk was great. The room was very clean, the bed comfortable, we had no problems at all. The hotel was very crowded as this was a summer weekend, so the breakfast and happy hour were both very crowded. The breakfast was very good and the happy hour was OK. We liked the location at the far end of the riverwalk, so you did not have a lot of noise from all the people. We had no problems here at all.

title: “Fantastic! I want to come back SOON!”
text:
Love this place! It is absolutely beautiful with stunning views of Hill Country. We live in Houston, turned a business trip into a long weekend with our young kids (5 & 7). We were able to eat dinner at the resort and leave the kids at the Kids Club. They begged to go back they liked it so much. You get 1/2 off a 4 hour session if you eat at either restaurant on the property.
Our room was spacious with a sleeper sofa, free internet, large bathroom, friendly & accomodating staff. Quick check-in and very impressed that they allowed us a 3pm check out. 
My husband played golf at the Palmer Course on site and said it was one of the most beautiful courses he's played on.

title: “Best hotel I have stayed at in Chicago.”
text: Great location, great service, great rooms! I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great atmosphere, central location, friendly staff”
text: I enjoyed staying here and was sorry I couldn't stay longer. The hotel is in an excellent location in the heart of San Francisco close to everything. The staff was very friendly and professional, especially the manager, Tony Abboud. My room was very large and nicely decorated and the bed very comfortable. The wine reception in the lobby in the afternoon was a nice touch. Highly recommended!

title: “Stylish hotel, decent sized rooms, lives up to it's rating”
text:
Stayed here with my husband and seven month old baby for a week. It was quite a large, well appointed room, with room for the travel cot supplied by the hotel. We didn't have much contact with the hotel staff, other than to ask for the cot which took three requests to be brought up.
The 4pm check-in time was a bit of a pain, as was the fee for looking after our bags (charged per bag, and we had quite a few with us because of the baby!). 
We ate once in the hotel restaurant from the fixed price menu, which was very nice. Breakfasted in Fluffy's cafe across the road, very reasonable and tasty! Room service was available, but we didn't use it as the menu was missing from the pack in our room.

title: “Try Pergamino for breakfast”
text:
Stayed at the Holiday Inn for 4 days and it was fine. I had been a little concerned after reading some reviews. We were in the Beach building - no problems with noise. Staff were courteous and friendly and the maid service was excellent. Had only one meal in the hotel which was ok but there are so many good restaurnats in the area that I would suggest going out. I read on here about Pergamino's being recommended for breakfasts, so we tried it and went back each morning. Straight over the road from the main hotel, wonderful, freshly cooked food made to order, extremely friendly staff who make you feel most welcome. They say they make the best waffles and they do - try them with the fresh berries - absolutely gorgeous. Even though we had an early departure on our last day, we dashed round for our final breakfast, treated to free drinks seeing as we had been such good customers and got a hug from the owner when we left.
Excellent location for walking around. Cable car near Argonaut hotel couple of blocks away - go early to avoid long queues.

title: “The reviews were right. A great place to...”
text: The reviews were right. A great place to stay. Nice clean and comfortable rooms. Great location!

title: “Hotel Paradise, Hotel Valencia”
text: The Staff, Valet, bar tenders, rooms, food and drinks are all amazing! You have to come and enjoy! It is a must experience type of situation... :) Party right downstairs!

title: “Met Our Needs”
text: My family (husband, 14 yo & 12 yo) stayed here for 3 nights. Definitely in the heart of the city. Fairly quiet for being downtown. Extremely helpful and friendly staff. Free happy hour from 5:30-7:30 nightly. Very hearty breakfast. Clean room. Would stay here again.

title: “Fantastic Service and Location”
text:
We have stayed at many hotels throughout the years, but the service and value of this hotel are outstanding! We were celebrating our 35th Anniversary with our children. While dining at a local restaurant, we were surprised by a complementary bottle of wine sent over from the hotel manager, Jennifer. Now that's service!
The food, wine and beer were included in our visit were more than generous and allow the stay in Chicago to be more affordable. The only change we would like to see is a more comfortable mattresses on the fold out couch.

title: “my nightmare”
text: i made reservations and after reading reviews i decided not to stay.i cancelled my reservations and did so 3 weeks before my arrival date.after i got home i found out i was charged 80.56 for nothing.no one has any record of my original reservation nor my cancellation number however they have my bank numbers to charge and thanks to that i incured a total of 209.00 that no one wants to be responsiable for.i called the so called customer service number and have had better luck in playing the lottery and have never won a dime playing it......i ended up staying down the road at a great hotel.......run

title: “Nice Hotel by Times Square”
text:
Although I prefer lower Manhatten, my husband and I decided to take a spontaneous trip to NYC over memorial day weekend, and found the location of this hotel and the price somewhat affordable.
When we arrived, they told us we were to check-in down the hall in the Premier section of the hotel. We didn't book anything special, so I'm not sure what was going on there. Maybe the other side was full. Either way, our room was great! It was very clean with modern style. My only complaints were that we reserved a king and got a double, and there was only a view of a brick wall. Otherwise, it had nice furniture, and a nice sized bathroom. It was the nicest room I've stayed in in NYC. 
If you haven't been to NYC or simply enjoy being near the hustle and bustle, as well as good shooping at Macy's, this hotel is ideal. It literally took maybe 2-3 minutes to reach time square, less than a block. Macy's was probably 2 blocks. The nearest subways were 2-3 blocks.

title: “Why Stay Anywhere Else?”
text:
I stayed here one night while in town with my sons (11 and 8) between business trips for an Astros game and other Houston area fun. 
This hotel is less than a year old and is great! I am almost overwhelmed to describe everything, so here goes:
Suite - As my son put it, this really has a super-modern theme to it. Everything was clean and in good working order. The bed was comfy; the foldout sleeper sofa was ok. The bathroom door was interseting - it was a sliding door that didn't latch and could be pushed out slightly at the bottom - sort of hinged at the top where it slides along the wall. The bath towels were plush and thirsty. Flat screen tvs in the bedroom and living area were just the right size and there was a great selection of channels. The microwave was just the right size for some left-overs or a bag of popcorn and the fridge kept water bottles cool. 
Breakfast - The dining area is very large and although there was a considerable line later in the morning, it moved well and there was always a table to be found. The bacon was very good - thick, not that thin microwaveable stuff. Bear with me here, while riding the shuttle back to the hotel, we were stoppped at a red light and a car pulls up next to us and the driver signals to roll down the window. I obliged and the driver asked, "did you have breakfast there this morning? (The Cadillac Escalade shuttle has the Embassy logo on it). I replied that it was our first day there and had not been able to yet. He introduced himself as Gregory, the omelette chef, and said to be sure and see him in the morning. Wow, talk about someone who loves what they do and loves to make people happy! Gregory is a hoot! He knows how to cook and go ahead and try his secret seasoning if he offers it. Needless to say, breakfast was way better than average. The coffee was delicious and the juices were not watered down like at some places.
Swimming pool - How cool is it to have a tropical oasis in the middle of downtown Houston? The outdoor pool, surrounded by palm trees, is located on the 3rd floor and is bigger than the average downtown hotel pool anywhere I've been. The water coming into it was actually heated, so it was the perfect temperature. The hot tub seemed nice and hot to the touch, though I never got in. There are some sitting and lounging areas around the pool in full sun, complete shade and under an arbor for partial shade.
Parking - relatively steep when you consider it's $28 and valet is the only option. 
Service - Everyone was friendly and had that "how can I make your stay more enjoyable?" attitude. I was met with smiles and greetings from the moment I drove up to the unloading area, at the front desk, and by any employee I saw. Cesar, the weekend shuttle driver, is a wonderful person who genuinely enjoys making people feel at home. The free downtown area shuttle is great in case you don't want to make the relatively short walk to or from Minute Maid Park or other downtown locations. 
We did have one problem during the stay, nothing completely horrible or anything, but when I brought it to the manager's attention, he quickly remedied the situation and was glad to do so. He wants everyone to enjoy their stay and return. I know I will any time I am going to spend the night in downtown Houston and I recommend you do as well!

title: “A Fabulous Place to Stay!”
text: I really do love this hotel. The staff was very, very friendly and willing to help in any way that they could. We wanted to get a room with a microwave and refrigerator but didn't receive it when we first arrived. When we mentioned this to the staff we were immediately moved to a room that did have those things without any trouble or a sideways glance. This place is so comfortable and quiet and I truly got a great night's sleep there. They even have a shuttle that not only takes you to the airport, but to several of the shopping centers that are close by the hotel. The shuttle drivers also offer you bottled water whenever you get in the shuttle bus. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who would be staying in the Denver area. GREAT!!

title: “A bad decision to even come to this hotel.”
text: I was in town for a conference the 2nd week of November 2005. I tried my best to stay at any hotel but this one based on the feedback here yet I was unsuccessful as this hotel was the only one with any vacancy. Now I understand why! It would have been better for me if I had just missed the conference. This hotel was simply miserable. From the rudeness of the front desk staff, to the filthy conditions of the hallways and guest rooms, to the lack of any taste of the food in the restaurant. Upon checkout, I did speak to the front desk and advised a nice young lady about the problems and she advised me that the hotel had just been sold and that the new owners had let all of the "good" managers go and that the morale in the hotel was terrible. Well shame on them! They have a hotel with a great location but that has no concept of cleanliness and friendliness. I was unable to find out the name of the company that bought it but if I can, I'll never stay at any of their hotels again! You shouldn't either.

title: “What a little gem!”
text:
This is a great place to stay!
This hotels location is fantastic, the staff are delightful and the rooms are superb. Need I say more?

title: “Outstanding service”
text: The property was very nicely furnished and spotless, but you can find that at any of a number of fine hotels in the area. What makes the Omni worth coming back to is the staff - every one of them was fantastic and went out of their way to make our stay enjoyable.

title: “Great hotel!!!”
text: We really liked our stay at this hotel, clean , nice rooms, comfortable, great location and good value! it's a very good place to stay... Complementary breakfast good too... Wifi free just in the lobby... the people at the front desk (asian) were not very frindly... but you can't have it all right?!!! but I would stay there again for sure!!! It's very close to most of the attractions and to the cable car stop... that we enjoyed very much!!! Great place!!!

title: “Different in a good way”
text: My sister and I stayed at the Hotel Valencia 2 weeks ago and I love this place!! You have to be in the mood for a mod, hip sleek and minimalistic experience. I read the reviews here before I visited and listened to what some said about it being too dark, but I frankly loved it. Yes, it's a bit dark, but not dark in a weird way - just in a neat way. The staff was very accomodating. Our room was great and I loved those faux mink bedspreads! If I had to complain about anything, the only thing I could come up with was the odd choice of music in the bar on Saturday night. The entire crowd was 40+ and white, but the music blaring was hip/hop, almost rap (bad choice). Not a big deal; we just walked past the bar and to our room. This hotel is a pleasantly healthy walk from the main part of the Riverwalk and it is nice that you pass all the other hotels, restaurants and bars on the way back to this hotel because, after a big meal, the walk was invigorating. I will definately stay here again when I visit San Antonio. P.S. there's a great German bakery right across the street in an old hotel.

title: “Great location and a good hotel”
text:
We chose this hotel for a Christmas time visit to see our daughter in Los Angeles. I am Starwood Preferred and they were haveing a great promotion based on your birth year. So, the older you are the better they rate. This hotel offered a nice clean room at a better than average rate in North Los Angeles area. The staff in the hotel were very helpful especially the morning waiters in the restaurant. I think his name is Roman! Very nice man. He made you feel like you were having breakfast at home.
No complaints!!! Good Hotel!!!

title: “Perfect”
text: We went to Philly for a long weekend and stayed at the Rittenhouse....It was A+ from beginning to end....I highly recommend it. The accommodations, staff and location were perfect for a visit to Philadelphia!

title: “Love it! Great location!”
text: I stayed at Distrikt hotel during the Memorial Day weekend holiday with my mom and sisters. Parking was very simple, the garage was right next door and you get a voucher for a certain rate. Hotel was very beautifully decorated and modern looking. Our room wasnt ready till 3 pm but they took our bags and we walked around until they were ready. When we got to our room, we loved every part of it. They were clean, nicely decorated, and pretty spacious. We loved the location of the hotel because it was right in the middle of everything. I will for sure come back to this hotel every time I come back to NYC. Thanks for a great stay!

title: “Great choice for Midtown”
text:
I stayed here to be close to some meetings that were near Times Square, and also I'm a pretty loyal Marriott member. 
PROS: The staff are superb... 99% of them. They have a great attitude and seem eager to help you with most anything you need. The check-in and bellman teams in particular was delightful. Due to my Elite status I got an upgrade to a great Times Square view room. Bellmen were always happy to give directions. The rooms themselves were pretty good. Great beds, good workspace, plenty of outlets, and I appreciated the night light in the bathroom. Good food, albeit pricey. Fast elevators, an ample gift shop with anything you could need, a Starbucks downstairs, and you're in the middle of everything when you walk out the door. Great lobby with free wifi... good for a quick meeting or to spend a few hours while you are waiting to check in or leave for the airport. Super fitness center with tons of machines and great view of Midtown rooftops. 
CONS: I checked in close to midnight after a long flight, and when got to my room realized there was no water. I stay in hotels around the country, and don't think I've ever been in one that didn't offer bottled water in the room, whether it's free or fee (usually fee). NYC has terrible tap water, so this should be obviously offered. It took my luggage a good 30 minutes to get up to the room. This was a huge inconvenience when I got in so late and was sitting there in my room waiting for my stuff. If I'd known it would have taken so long I would have lugged it all up myself. Room service got my order wrong - TWICE - even after reading it back to me on the phone. And the gal running the fitness center watched a few of us try to keep opening the door with our card keys and then we realized it was unlocked. She could have told us this or motioned to just open the door; instead she stood there and folded the towels. When I suggested she put up a sign to say it's open during the day, she said something to the likes of that it was my job to make a comment... (I'm not sure where or to who? I'd obviously just shared it with her.) And a few housekeeping indiscretions, like there was no plastic bag for my dirty laundry the entire stay, and they didn't replace the bottle of lotion I'd nearly used up. For a room that ended up being over $400 a night (much more after NY taxes and fees), some of these things just seemed a bit off.
If you are a light sleeper I suggest you bring earplugs or play some background noise (I love the White Noise app on my iPhone.). Even on floor 20 it was loud enough to be irritating at night. It's NYC Time Square, and you'll hear horns, jack-hammering, people cheering, you name it. 
Overall I would stay here again ... and I think it's a great option for midtown. Just don't expect top notch!

title: “Great, clean hotel close to downtown”
text:
I stayed here with my wife for a few days while visiting friends in the Boston area. 
We arrived via airplane and took the Silver Line from the airport to the hotel since we wouldn't be needing a car for the first two days we were there. The World Trade Center stop on the Silver Line is just one block from the hotel, so that was very convenient. (I believe the Silver Line Way stop is also one block away, in the other direction). Check in at the front desk was a breeze! They gave us a corner room, which was a little more spacious than the standard rooms. The room was very nice. It had a king bed, sofa, desk and tv. We didn't need to access the internet while we were there, but I believe it was around $13 per day.
We did get rent a car the second day we were there (since we were visiting friends outside the realm of the MBTA transportation network). The only downside to that was the parking at the hotel was $42 per night (although the valet was very convenient). We did a trolley tour while we were there. The trolley stopped less than 100 yards from the hotel.
The only reason I couldn't rate this hotel with 5 stars was that while we were there the hotel pool was temporarily closed for some reason so we weren't able to use it.

title: “Priceline Purgatory”
text:
The Bad:
Check-in was pleasant enough. But the guy at the counter asked us if we’d prefer smoking or non; and when we said “non;” he said, “Well, with Priceline – they always just assign the SMOKING rooms.” Okaaay. (These days – the classy hotels like the Hyatt and Hilton diplomatically just say something like “Oh, your room has already been prepaid.”)
We were put in building #7 which was way on the outskirts of the property. I had left my laptop in the car; and I literally got lost trying to find our vehicle just outside of Building 7. The hallways are a veritable labyrinth. Speaking of corridors – they are lined with “artwork” that was quite hideous. Outside our room was a painting (print ?) that looked liked Little House on the Prairie with absolutely NO perspective. The Priceline “view” from our third floor room was the ugly roofs which looked like giant, dirty, empty cement swimming pools. The flora/grounds surrounding the buildings were very scruffy and unkempt (at least out in “Siberia” where were stationed). 
The Good and Not So Bad:
The room was fairly attractive (nicer than it was when this was the Hyatt). It had a big (if a bit narrow) bathroom. Very nice minty bathroom amenities – lotion, soap and shampoo. The shower spray was very good also. The bathroom had stripy green wallpaper. The counter was marble. There was a very high wrought iron towel rack. There was a picture of Captain Morgan over the toilet. The coffeemaker only made one cup at a time.
There were five pillows per queen sized bed. There was only one on my bed that was soft enough for me – the others were like giant hard, fluffy marshmallows. The linens were very nice and soft. The beds were high – which I like. The dark wooden furniture was highly varnished – as was the armoire that held the TV. (However, there was a “naked” swirly light bulb hanging from the ceiling that was not covered with a fixture.) The room had new greenish carpet. The walls were a yellow/taupe color – not terrible – but not very pretty either. There was a picture of dueling elephants over one of the beds. Over the other bed was a picture of scary clowns (I’m afraid of clowns) so my sister had to sleep in that one! The housekeeping staff was very nice.

title: “Lower budget hotel, but for price and location, rates 5”
text:
4th year in a row here, always clean, friendly.
Wifi throughout. Bathrooms are shared on corridors, rooms are New York sized, i.e. not huge, but on the edge of Union Square, and very nice.
Also they store your baggage free on last day, reception always very helpful.

title: “beautiful hotel. Incredibly nice and attentive employees”
text: The best hotel experience I've had in years. Jason in the restaurant was the best. I work for and airline and he treated us as if we were "real people". That doesn't always happen. All of the staff are incredibly nice and I can't wait to get back!

title: “Great location, nice hotel, friendly staff”
text: We stayed here for my wife's birthday weekend. It was a great hotel. Very conveniently located to restaurants, shopping, the Reading Terminal Market and attractions. Check in and check out were very fast and hassle free. Housekeeping did a fantastic job. The room was extremely clean and well appointed. We ended up with a nice corner room that had a great view.

title: “great location!”
text:
We really enjoy our stay at the millennium Times Square, it has a great perk and that is the location just steps away from the main broadway plays, shops and dinning.
This our third time at millennium and we are looking forward in returning.

title: “Very Professional”
text: This hotel was very accommodating and professional. It was easy to work with them and they had a great attitude.

title: “Unbeatable value - in the right rooms!”
text:
Just had our second visit at the Charlesmark, this one a three-night stay after we were in Boston for the Paul McCartney concert. Got a really amazing deal on Travelocity -- $118 per night -- which was so cheap it was an offer we couldn't refuse. The Charlesmark did not disappoint. Rooms, although small, are clean and well-designed and the location is fantastic. Staff is helpful, and the bar is a great place to have a drink at the end of your night. Speaking of the bar, if you are someone who likes to go to bed before 2 a.m. on a weekend, *do not* let them put you in one of the two rooms on the first floor (106 and 107). I read someone else's TA review that the noise wasn't a problem. Well, we were in 107 and it was fine on Thursday night, but on Friday night the noise was outrageous. The hotel was good about moving us the next day to a quieter room. (Really, they should just charge less for these rooms and let folks know the bargain they're striking!) Other than that, absolutely no complaints. A great deal.
P.S. Go to JP Licks on Newbury Street for the best ice cream you've ever had.

title: “Great Location.”
text: Stayed here for two nights. The hotels location was ideal. I flew into SFO and took the BART straight to the Powell station which is located in union square, then walked 5 minutes to the hotel. The hotel staff was very accommodating. We did have one incident, the sheets on our first night weren't in the cleanest condition we called the front desk and they delivered some clean sheets. Overall i enjoyed my stay at the Drake.

title: “Staff is friendly. Hotel is new.”
text: It was a decent hotel for a business trip when my favorite was full booked for my extended stay. The Holiday Inn is a brand new hotel and it shows in the modern take on furnishings. The staff was friendly and accommodating.

title: “Great Location & Great Value”
text:
Nice hotel, great location, helpful staff and all at a great price through RoomsNet. If you're looking for a good value hotel in mid-town Manhattan then this is for you. Located just off 5th Avenue at 44th Street, you can easily walk to all the mid-town attractions from here such as Times Square, Broadway. Empire State Building, Rockefeller Centre, Grand Central Terminus etc. 
Like other reviewers have mentioned, there was no complementary breakfast on offer. There is a paying alternative within the hotel but the Red Flame diner just along the road (67 W 44th Street) was a better option for us.
All in all we would definitely return to The Mansfield when next in NYC.

title: “It feels like home.”
text: I am on the road for 21 days out of a month. This hotel makes me feel very comfortable. The staff are very friendly. Whenever I leave and return, they always make me feel welcome. I always enjoy coming back.

title: “A good hotel with great views”
text:
Stayed at the Holiday Inn Mart Plaza over President's Day weekend, booking the rooms on Priceline at $75 per night.
We were in Chicago for a weekend to enjoy the city, so our time in the hotel was limited. The location is convenient for driving in and the parking lot is more than adequate. If you're on a business trip to the Loop, this would certainly be a good choice. For a weekend/family getaway, you may want to look for something like the Hyatt Regency just to be closer to Michigan Ave and the main tourist sites.
The layout of the hotel, entering through the building lobby and then proceeding to the hotel lobby on the 15th floor, is somewhat inconvenient, but certainly not a problem. Unload your bags before you park.
Parking is $27 a day with unlimited use, so if you'll be traveling by car during your stay, it's a good value. Otherwise, the El Brown line stop at Merchandise Mart is located a block east (through the Mart building). Michigan Ave is a six block walk to the east, certainly doable, even in winter.
Room had a great view looking over the Chicago River and the Mart. Room was very good size, bed was comfortable and the bathroom was fine - all in all, this is a very nice Holiday Inn. It's certainly a great value on Priceline, and would be a good value in general.

title: “I have spent over 20 nights in this hotel and it is nice.”
text: I stay at this hotel for business a couple times a year. It has a stylish lobby and nice views. I have no complaints about the staff they all seem pleasant. I do not reccommend eating at the resturant or drinking at their bar as their pricing is outrageous. There are plenty of good resturants within a 10 minute drive and if you are on foot, simply walk up to the carnival atmosphere of the Universal City Walk, which while somewhat overstimulating and full of tourists has some decent resturants and bars that are, if you can believe it, cheaper than at the Sheraton.

title: “Kitano gets my thumbs up”
text:
My wife and I were in New York the weekend of 6/9 and had the pleasure of staying at the Kitano New York Hotel the night of 6/9. I did my research as usual on Tripadvisor.com and liked what I read about the place. We had sites and restaurants we wanted to visit and they were all over Manhattan and Brooklyn Heights so no one hotel in any one location would have been ideal for us. However, the Kitano was very convenient in regards to its location to Grand Central Station and Penn Station. Additionally cabs were easy to get. The area is clean and safe as can be found in NY.
The hotel does have services and ammenities for the Japanes business person or toursit such as a Japanese TV channel and a Japanese newspaper delivered to your room if you'd like. As my wife is Japanese this was great for her. There were Japanese speaking staff though not all were and we observed many Japanese guests. Anyone would feel welcome and comfortable here, not just someone from Japan.
The hotel has a very relaxing aura to it upon entering. All of the staff were most pleasant and helpful. Our room was on the 10th floor. Bags were brought up to the room immediately and when we placed a call for some extra towels they were there within minutes, delivered by a smiling person. The hotel and the rooms are extremely clean. The room, ours had a king size bed, was spacious enough and had a very nice bathroom with high quality bath products by Shiseido. 
There was a charge for wired high speed internet access, $10 for 24 hours I seem to recall. The room was very quiet with the windows closed but you could open the windows, they tilted open from the top, if you wished. The bed was comfortable.
We didn't eat at the main restaurant on the first floor or the Japanese restaurant on the lower lever though we did go inside both and they looked like good places if you didn't want to wander far. The bar was lively when we returned from dinner Friday night. Jazz is their thing there on certain nights, Friday being one of them. I think the cover charge was $17 and it was close to the end of the performance so we opted not to go in. We went back to the room for a quiet drink from the mini bar and capped off a perfect day in the city.
We will stay at the Kitano New York on our next visit as we feel we have found a home away from home here.

title: “W Hotel - Lexington Avenue”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel before, loved it before, and wanted to share it with my wife during this brief business trip to NYC. I like the W chains in the Starwood Group but my miserable experience this weekend at this site prompts an update.
Driving in from Quebec yesterday afternoon, I dropped my wife and all of our luggage outside the front door at the valet stand before taking off to return the rental car a few blocks away. You'd think that one of the staff would have offered to help her. Didn't happen. I returned to find her glaring, and frazzled, in the lobby.
Not a good sign.
Being a Starwood Gold member, I naturally got in the Gold/Platinum SPG registration line. The staffer at the reception desk really couldn't be bothered, and directed me to the line that everyone else was in.
Not a good sign.
After finally getting to the point of registration, I was welcomed nicely and thanked for being a SPG Gold member. He would, as a benefit, upgrade us. Great! (Foolish me, I believed him. We were upgraded to a closet where work is difficult and getting by each other and the luggage required one of us to climb on the bed.)
Not a good sign.
My sense is that, at least at this W, customer service is just not a priority, even for Gold SPG members. Maybe once one achieves that status they feel that they can slack off. Very disappointing for an otherwise terrific hotel group.
There are plenty of other SPG hotels in NYC. Think strongly about one of them first.
ATBster

title: “If your visiting Chicago this is the hotel for you”
text:
We stayed in this wonderful hotel may 2012.. If you are staying in Chicago this is the hotel for you... Charming, clean, and friendliest staff we have ever encountered. Rooms are clean and so comfy..As a kimpton member we were even given a 10.00 raid the bar coupon what a treat! So make sure you sign up to become a member it's free and well worth it.
Every day when we left the hotel and returned we were always greeted by the front desk..and the bellman at the front door were also outstanding...Everyone always willing to help to ensure your stay is a great one. 
This hotel is close to everything...shopping,site seeing , restaurants..it has it all.
We look forward to returning and will def be staying at the Burnham ..:)

title: “Small rooms, excellent value in downtown SF for the price”
text: My husband and i stayed for 5 days for a wedding and were able to walk to all the major spots--Coit Tower, the waterfront, union square etc--within 20 minutes. the rooms are small but the beds are comfortable and there isn't a lot of noise since it's downtown near the financial district. would definitely stay again!!

title: “Great Stay”
text: My stay was great. The hotel was clean and very comfortable. I think breakfast time should be extended to 10:30 rather than 9:30. Everything else was great.

title: “Nickeled and dimed to death”
text:
I travel extensively, and this is one of only two hotels I've stayed at in recent years that CHARGES FOR INTERNET! While the front desk warmly informed me that if I'd booked a "business class room," I'd have free internet (a lot of good that did mid-evening!), I was forced to purchase a $9.50/day temporary pass from T-Mobile Hotspots. Worse, they tried to mark the price up at the front desk.
Adding insult to injury, the hotel charges $10/night for parking. While I'd expect this in a large or dense city, the extra charge seemed inappropriate for the hotel's location. Incidentally, the paid parking is across a 6-lane road and a grass median strip.

title: “A beautiful, relaxing Inn, close to the beach”
text: My experience at the Inn at Mayo Clinic was a very good experience. The room was very clean, newly decorated, well furnished and accomodations for 3 people, equipped with a cook stove top, a microwave, dishwasher, toaster, coffee pot and a large refrigerator and 2 last flat screen televisions. Since we were there for testing at Mayo Clinic, this was perfect for us. We enjoyed the exercise room, the laundry room and especially the continental breakfast, complete with waffes, even grits for us southern girls! We were 5 minutes from the beach and less than 5 minutes from the chain restaurants, shopping malls and even fast food places. The convenience, the cleanliness and the kindness of the staff is reasons I will go again. The only negative that I have is the reason I was there was not for a happy trip, but to be close to my daughter who is very ill and having testing at Mayo Clinic, but I would certainly recomment this Inn to anyone looking for a nice place to stay.

title: “noisi, dark, a shame!!”
text:
Beautiful building, located near union square. But in the night we couldn't sleep because next to it there were very noisi pubs. Is also a very dark hotel, and the breakfast zone is small and a mess. 
The good new is that is very easy to fix, an isolant windows renovation, new lighting and electric system and new restaurant layout.

title: “Poor hotel but superb location.”
text: By far too expensive hotel considering what it has to offer. Don't get fooled by the "complimentary beverage area", which offers only coffee, tea and water. The same goes for the "complimentry breakfast", which is probably the lousiest I've ever had. Half an hour before the breakfast time was out, the staff discontinued to fill up what was finished. The staff was however very friendly and helpful and the location is of course superb.

title: “Very classy with excellent service in a stunning environment!”
text: Used a Snique Away deal for this hotel. Great discount for a really classy hotel. Beautiful environment for Deco enthusiasts. Excellent service including quick room service for breakfast. Be sure to join Kimpton for free wireless and $10 towards the interesting mini-bar. We would stay again.

title: “Return Visit from Previous Wasted Trip”
text:
Last year our visit to the Hampton Inn was a very long wasted trip (see review March 2011) but I am pleased to say that the "compted" visit was very enjoyable. We are pleased to report the positive reviews are accurate. We had a King bed suite that was very clean and updated .. two nice size televisions and a mini kitchen, We brought along another couple and they said the queen sofa bed was comfortable. The complimentary breakfast buffet was very good .. my favorite was the scrambled eggs. My only complaint for the entire visit was the temperature control .. had a tough time keeping up with the outside temp .. which was upper 90's during the day. Pool and hot tub were very nice .. the sauna was broken.
All of the staff were extremely friendly and helpful .. the location was perfect for walking to Navy Pier and Downtown Chicago... many bars and restaurants in the area closeby.
Looking forward to our next stay .. highly recommend.
Again a "thank you" to the General Manager for his excellent customer service!

title: “Awesome staff”
text: We stayed at the Magic Caste Hotel on a recent side-trip to a family reunion. We arrived early and unfortunately were not able to check in. That was fine as we had just travelled from NY and were starving. They sent us to "The Grill" for lunch and said they would call when the room was ready. We walked around the corner to the the Hollywood/Highland Complex and had lunch. The front desk called within an hour to tell us the room was ready. I had asked to be put on a waiting list for a 2 bedroom but there weren't any available. They offered to move us if we wanted the next day when one became available. The thought of packing up again didn't appeal to us so we stayed put! The room was fine- very clean and spacious with plenty of space to have 4 people spread out. We had 2 yound adult kids with us- 18 & 20. The 20 yr old got the sleeper sofa and the daughter shared the 2 queen beds with us in the bedroom. The bathroom was small but certainly adequate and it was nice to be able to open the window as there wasn't a fan. The 2nd day we returned hot and exhausted to our room at 4:30 and it hadn't been cleaned yet. The cleaning staff was just entering it when we got to the hotel. We were a little disappointed but just got a drink and waited on the pool deck with the free snacks. The parking garage is really different- you need 2 people to operate the entry system and it is very tight quarters. We never used the pool- it was closed the day we arrived -very milky white. The following 2 days people swam in it and it looked fine. Again ,everything around us was very clean. The 3rd day I asked if we could take the bath towels withus to the beach. Before I knew it - the girl at the front desk had packed us up a beach bag with beach towels, snacks and cold water. She even wanted to give us sunscreen!! This service is what MCH is all about. There wasn't anything they wouldn't do to make your stay wonderful. The location is perfect for Hollywood in a very safe residential neighborhood. My only concern was when we checked out there were 2 calls from our room which we never made. We had cell phones and honestly never even saw the room phone. Also- there was no one in LA for us to call! It was a local # and I would bet that housekeeping probably used the phone. That was the day we were at the beach the whole day. We paid the $2 fee and that was the end of it. It could use a coat of paint to spruce things up but other than that- it was great and we would return. There is nowhere else in LA you can stay for the price. The breakfast was fantastic and my kids loved it. The snacks came in handy and we even walked around the corner to Longs and bought a bottle of wine! I would highly recommend MCH.

title: “Great location...great staff”
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at this hotel in July when we came to see a couple of ball games. It's in a prime location. The hotel is an older building but has tons of character. The beds were very comfortable and the price was reasonable. We did leave something behind and the amazing staff went way out of their way to have it returned to us at home. Thank you so much!! We'd be happy to stay here again.

title: “Awsome Chelsea Lodge!”
text:
I spent months researching accomodation in NYC before I decided on the Chelsea lodge, mostly because of the reviews on this sight. I didn't want to do the backpacker thing, and had a small budget. Given there were so many good reviews, I figured that there must be truth in them, and I was correct. The Chelsea lodge was just awsome. The room was small but perfect in size. Hot water never ran out in the good shower in my room. Bed was comfy and the room warm. Each floor had a shared toilet, but I never once saw anyone on my floor in 4 days. The guys there were so helpful and friendly. 
The whole hotel is done up similar to what I would describe as an English pub - very homely and cosy, with interesting paintings and knick knacks decorating the halls and stair well.
Location wise, there is 18th St subway a block down, or 23rd St a few blocks over. It was a great base to explore NYC. And no street noise at all! There are heaps of places to eat and have a drink - the area is very safe, as is all of New York. Travelling as a single white female for the first time to New York, I never felt threatened or worried walking about at night (only a little out of place as there are mainly gay bars in the area).
In summary, I would recommend the Chelsea lodge to anyone, and I plan to be returning later this year.
Thank you Chelsea lodge for a perfect stay!

title: “Unique - each staffer could run his or her own restaurant or hotel”
text: I am retired but travel to NYC about monthly and have adopted the Mark as my hotel there, after "auditoning" several others. You can read glowing reviews elsewhere on TripAdvisor, but what impresses me about the Mark is that each staffer seems to treat their job as a career, not just a job, from Judy at the bar to the front desk staff to Isabel and Robert, concierges, to their exclusive Lobb shoe shine stand man. For example, the head waiters in the dining room actually pay attention and move around constantly to check on details. There reportedly are staff meetings every day, and it shows. This ineffable atmosphere is hard to put into words, but it stands far above the usual burn- out cases of staffing. One of the room attendants, Leonora, came close to expressing it. When I didn't have exact change for her gratuity (I left the gratuity later with the front desk), she said "that doesn't mater, just that you are happy". That about expresses the attitude of the entire hotel. I look forward to every return trip.

title: “Big, persistent Internet problems, otherwise OK”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel before, and would have given it a top rating in the past, but I just can't now, for one reasion: The advertised free, wired Internet in each room just doesn't work (and there is no in-room wireless available), and I am not certain the hotel was being completely up front with me about whether it even could work. Here is the full story; see what you think. To net it out: There had been a changeover to a new system about a month before, and the in-room Internet had never really worked after that.
I checked in on a Tuesday, and discovered that the wired Internet in my room did not work. (The problem in what follows was generally that I could connect to the system, but my laptop would tell me that the connection, though present, was not functional.) I was told at the front desk that the system had been down since that morning, technicians were working on it, and it would be back up the next day. However, I was then warned by other guests that it had actually been down at least since the preceding day, and despite repeated assurances that it would be repaired the following day, had not been. (I received such assurances through Friday, but it never was fixed.)
However, I was assured that I could bring my laptop to the south lobby, where free wireless was available. I did so, kept getting the same problem, and was told to go to the north lobby, where the wireless was working. I did so, could not make the connection work there either, and was then told that (1) there was likely something wrong with my laptop, which theory I dispelled quickly with the desk clerk by showing him that I could connect fine to the much weaker wifi signal from George Washington University, complete with a page showing campus photos, though I could not then "borrow" their signal since it required a logon; and (2) that the State Plaza server had just crashed and would be back up in a few minutes, though ten minutes later there was still no service.
It was at this point that the desk clerk admitted that there had been an upgrade to the system a month earlier, which he appropriately referred to as a "downgrade", and the Internet had never worked correctly thereafter.
A technician did come to my room to check the connection using a hotel laptop, and told me that my room seemed to be one of those in which the Internet no longer worked. Judging from the many folks who complained to the desk clerk while I was there, this was likely the norm rather than the exception.
There is a business center with two computers with working Internet connections (for which one had to compete with many others who thought they had in-room Internet but didn't), but it is loaded with some commercial software to manage Internet connections that kept tossing me off when I tried to connect to my organization's Outlook web server, so I had to give up on e-mail from the hotel. There is a Starbucks a block and a half east of the hotel that has free wifi for customers, and that became my lifeline during the hours they were open (and, as I was sure would be the case, my laptop had no problems whatever with their Internet; no, it wasn't my laptop's fault).
This hotel's location is within walking distance from the Mall and the White House, and for the price it has been great in the past for me. However, unless and until I can be assured that the new Internet system has been replaced with one that works, I can't return. My work depends too much on having reliable Internet access.

title: “Really nice”
text:
Sure, rooms are really small (it's New York, so face it). But the room was really nice. Great stuff in the bathroom (mmmm, that lemon smelling shower gel - you MUST buy it).
Location is also good. It's just a few blocks from 5th avenue. BTW, bed was worth staying longer in the room.

title: “Pleasant Stay”
text: My sister and I have been on the road almost four weeks so we are getting to know our way around B&B's and hotels :-) We had never heard of Silver Cloud properties but after reading reviews thought we would give them a try and were not disappointed. Our rooms were spotless and nice size; front desk very courteous and helpful when asked about restaurants; nice internet speed; some of the things mentioned about other Silver Cloud properties were missing at this property, a little disappointing (example, living room with drinks and snacks on each floor -- I could find that anywhere on the fifth floor at this location but it was a maze so I might have completely missed it). There is no restaurant at this location but you are in the center of some great places to eat so that's not a big deal. If you don't want to get out, they have several places that will deliver to the hotel. You are five minutes from the Space Needle, which for a tourist, is a must-visit. Our room had a view of Lake Union which was wonderful. Overall, a very pleasant stay.

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text: First of all, the location was perfect. We were close to the subway and train station. It was also a very safe area. We had two rooms, the larger one was a handicap room which we did not request but it was so nice. Our boys were in a small room but it had everything they needed. There is no view but that was ok. We had a table top fan that we brought to drown out any noise. You will hear sirens in the city. The beds were wonderful and the staff was very helpful. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: We just returned form a business trip and stayed at the Orchard Garden Hotel. It was very clean, quiet and had a very comfortable bed. The staff were all very friendly and helpful with dinner reservations. It's a 10 minute walk to the Convention Center and only a few minutes to Union Square. Lots of shopping and restaurants nearby. The only negative is the water pressure. Because it is a "green" hotel, it was very low. Not sure you actually save much water when it takes 5 minutes to get the shampoo out of your hair! Also, the "fitness room" is a treadmill, a bike and an eliptical machine. However, we got plenty of exercise walking everywhere. Both of these were minor issues for us. We will stay here again!

title: “Graduation Visit”
text: Stayed at this hotel while visiting Houston for a Graduation Ceremony. The staff was truly amazing!! The food delicious. Who designed this hotel?! OMG--They did an Amazing Job! I could not stay in the room. I wanted to explore the fascinating decor. The fitness center is very well equipped. The pool area welcoming and beautiful. Although the Valet charge was $28, it was worth every penny. We moved around a lot and it was nice to walk out and have the car waiting for us. We will definitely return.

title: “A quiet oasis in the hub of Times Square”
text:
My wife and I stayed for five nights and found it a perfect location right in the heart of Times Square. We found it to be a friendly, personable little hotel attached to the larger Millenium Hotel. The concierge, Monique, would have to be the most friendly, helpful concierge we have ever encountered in our stays at hotels throughout the world. We left for a week in New England and then returned to New York for another 3 nights. We had not pre booked our accommodation in case we were not happy with the hotel. After our stay we had no hesitation in rebooking at the Premier.
The rooms were spacious (for NY), clean and quiet.

title: “Let us sleep”
text: We just needed a place to stay for the night, after an event we attended.... Well I can not remember what floor we stayed in, the room was very nice... everything in the place was magnificent, except for the service... the people from there kept on barging in since we got there... they told us they had a water problem with the room above us... we did not see any water come into our room... we asked then if we could be moved... we were told the hotel was booked solid... no other rooms available... well just great, we had workers trying to come into our room at all hours, as if they had moved us out...hate the place just for that experience! >:(

title: “Perfect satay”
text:
Its the second time that I stay in the Gansevoort.
Everything was fantastic. I love your rooftop bar and pool. The service was excellent.
I would like to thank Luisa at the front desk for all her help. She was always very helpful and professional. I will be back in november next year... I hope everything is the same.

title: “My Fave Hotel in Denver”
