text: I find myself in Denver often for business and as often as they have room my choice is the Teatro. I only wish everyone could experience the staff and understated elegance that this hotel provides. True there is construction going on across the street, but the pluses of this hotel far outway the construction. Just ask for a higher floor, when booking

title: “Outstanding Location”
text: Live in the area but stayed here for a breakfast meeting to avoid the nightmare traffic. Location is awesome in the West End of DC. Dupont Circle is to your north, Georgetown to your west and Foggy Bottom to your south. All of these neighborhoods are a fairly quick walk (5-15mins) and are popular with lots to see and do and places to eat. Several subway stops are nearby as well. Entrance is a bit crowded with valet, cabs, etc. Room was fine but your room could be noisy due to fire station nearby and dignitaries and their motorcades staying at the Ritz Carlton. Like most full service hotels the internet is not free unless you are an elite member of Marriott Rewards in this case.

title: “Our Second Visit”
text: This was our second stay at this property, so needless to say we found our first stay to be pleasant and comfortable. We found the rooms to be spacious and clean and quite nicely furnished. Having read some of the other comments, I'm suprised at people's opinions. This BW is excellent value for the money...we thought the pool and hot tub great, the breakfast excellent, (especially compared to what we've had in much higher priced hotels), and the staff friendly. We stayed at the front, on the highway , our first visit, and at the back, where planes were taking off, this time. We found neither the traffic noise, or the airport noise the least bit bothersome, didn't even notice. We did experience trouble in finding our room, and had to go back and ask at the front desk for directions again...I suppose this could be annoying to some, however, we found it quite amusing...I guess we weren't as weary as other travellers who seemed to find it a huge problem. Overall, we enjoyed our stay, were more than pleased with the cost of the room and the amenities, and will most definitely be staying there again.

title: “Great Locaton”
text: Good location next to convention center and close to Pike Place Market. Rooms are good and have been updated fairly recently.

title: “Business floor....even better”
text:
I've reviewed this hotel 2 other times and I must admit, each time I stay there is better than the last. 
My boyfriend and I stayed the weekend after New Years and hoped to get the same room we had had in the second building the last time we visited. BUT we were bumped up to the business floor free of charge (must have been a slow weekend) and wow...
Just having a microwave and fridge was great, but the free computer/internet service and printing was above and beyond what I expected.
The only downside (and it is a small one) is that I found there to be too many youngsters (aged in the teens) on the floor. But I didn't dislike it enough to have that hinder my overall enjoyment.
When I next visit San Francisco, I will pay the extra twenty dollars a night to repeat the great experience.

title: “I'd recommend THE BENJAMIN!”
text:
Very nice hotel - Khady at the front desk was super helpful and upgraded me for free.
Nice lobby, cool "pillow selection" menu. 
Rooms are clean and quiet - a little bit dark window-wise, but plenty of lamps and light to make up for it.
Carpets in the hotel hallways could use a refresher, and the place is in need of a little "updating" style-wise, but if you're looking for a solid, reasonably priced, good-bet in NYC, The Benjamin is a great place to choose.

title: “Very Small Rooms , but Modern & Adequate”
text: Pros: Location is very good; easy walk to the heart of times square. Room was modern and clean, and even the gym was nice. Cons: The Elevator and hallways are extremely dark. The standard room, about 10x10 is small, even by NYC standards and comes with a small bed (smaller than queen), you get about 3 feet of space around 3 sides of the bed. No desk in the room, no dresser, other than a little round table, no room to set anything. Internet is not free. No coffee maker in the room. No Bible in the room. The bathroom has a pedestal sink, so again, no room to set your toiletries. When people were loud in the hallway, you could hear them in your room. So if you just need a place to sleep it might be fine, but if you’re a business traveler like myself, it just lacks the space and basic items you would expect in any hotel, especially a 3 star hotel.

title: “Nice Hotel, terrible experience”
text:
I booked my 'comfy king' room over 2 months in advance and was placed in a dungeon. The hotel's description of a comfy king includes 'a half wall of floor to ceiling windows' and the only window we had was on the door to the small balcony. There was no where to put clothes other than the hangers in the closet so we had to keep everything in the suitcase in the already cramped room. 
The 'free breakfast' is actually a $10 voucher towards breakfast, which would be fine if they did not advertise it as a FREE BREAKFAST. Service in the restaurant was horrible. we had to ask for things multiple times from multiple people. The 'Complimentary Wine Tasting' was comical as well. It was entertaining to watch the bartender and a person whom appeared to be the restaurant manager scramble to try and find the cheapest wines to pour during this hour, I must have been there on the busiest day they have ever had because they were running in circles. 
The phones in the room did not work, the staff was fairly friendly but unattentive until our checkout day when I had recieved a late checkout and the maid knocked on the door twice and I got a phone call, which was hard to answer because you had to try and find a phone that actually worked. I told both individuals that I was told I could checkout late and the lady on the phone stated that there were no late checkout that day and when would I be ready to leave. Ha, I told her I would be ready at 2pm like I had agreed upon with whomever gave me a late checkout and hung up the phone.
There are other hotels in Chicago that I would go to before I go back to the Dana Hotel and spa. It is a nice hotel aesthetically but way too much attitude and terrible service in my opinion. ( I did go during a very busy time in Chicago so you may have a different experience if no one is at the hotel since they staff it the same way regardless it seems)

title: “Great location, comfy rooms”
text:
We didn't plan to go to San Diego during Comic Con, but that was the weekend we went. Hotels were impossible to find but Hotel Indigo had rooms available because they were newly opened.
Great value, cute boutique hotel. Nice bathrooms (showers only, tho) and really comfy beds. Big rooms with great views of the ballpark. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Value on South side of Chicago”
text: We recently traveled to Chicago to spend time with our daughter who lives on the south side of Chicago & stayed at the South Loop Hotel. We also stayed in Room 541 as had a previous reviewer. Our experience there was wonderful! The staff were very courteous & helpful & seemed happy to assist us in any way we needed ( often a real rarity in today's world)! We enjoyed our king-size suite with the large soaking tub. There was also a small refrigerator & an individual cup coffee/tea maker in the room which were not advertised on the website. It is true that there is no microwave in the room, but that would not prevent us from staying there again. We did hear /feel the Bass from the lounge on a couple of the nights on the weekend, but it was not loud enough to bother us. And being on the bus route & near the trains is a definite asset to us! We were not bothered by the noise of that either. And the FREE parking is a huge benefit in the city of Chicago! We hope to return soon & would definitely stay here again!

title: “???? Travelodge”
text:
Arrived here on a saturday afternoon firstly if you have a car you have to pay $23 per night tp park plus any tips this is not clear anywhere before
Receptionist didn't look too welcoming we asked for a room with a boulevard view we were given a car park view
Rooms are painted chocolate brown and white furniture is choclate brown rooms are very unwelcoming fairly big but hardly any furniture too fill it dont expect any soft furnishings
I thought it looked very much like a travelodge/premier inn these are cosier
in my opnion toooo expensive you are payng for location not room
you'd be better off staying somewhere else and walking through hotel

title: “Large rooms and right in Times Square”
text:
Had the pleasure of staying in this hotel for 4 nights at the end of April. All staff were friendly
and efficient. Found the room to be large and well kept by the cleaning staff.
Was an ideal location to access just about anything from Times Square to subways to Port Authority and easy walking to just about anywhere.

title: “Bad Choice”
text: If you're interested in a well worn dirty place with bugs (I didn't identify them} and a staff that is disinterested in making you feel comfortable....thjis is the place to stay! Oh yes, if you want ice and go to the basement ( a spooky place at best).make sure you bring a saddle. the rats are large enough to ride.

title: “Really pleasant surprise!”
text:
I was a bit worried from the reviews here, but from the moment I walked in, I knew it would be a fantastic stay! I arrived at 7:15 on a Saturday morning and my room was already ready, which was so wonderful. It was a gorgeous, spacious room that I was sad to leave (I actually cut some of my plans short so I could come back and hang around the room for a bit). 
It was really chilly in NYC and I called about turning the heat up before I left. When I got back, they'd left a space heater by my door, which was very much appreciated. The staff was very friendly and I would go back to this place in a heartbeat. Only regret is that I was only there for a night.
Not sure what people mean by outdated, etc. I had a huge flat screen, great toiletries and the room was well decorated. The towels were lush and soft, the bed was incredibly comfortable and the layout of the room was great for moving around and spreading out. The only disappointment was that wireless was $16.95 a day, but there's a Starbucks across the street.
Check in here!

title: “Newly Renovated, Close to Airport”
text: We stayed here on our way to and from Hawaii. The hotel is very newly renovated and very nice. We used the hotel shuttle and it came around every 15 minutes. The staff was very friendly. We arrived during the manager's reception and while we didn't attend, everyone seemed to be having a good time. We did eat in the restaurant and the food was very good. Highly recommend the chicken fettuccine. If I was coming to LA for a longer trip, I would stay here the rooms are spacious enough that I didn't feel like I was in a cramped hotel room.

title: “Wonderful Weekend Getaway”
text: I wanted to take my partner for a weekend getaway. We wanted to go somewhere that provided an excellent value while still being conveniently located and comfortable. Watching the planes land and take off at LAX provided an excellent and scenic backdrop to our weekend away from home. The service staff were friendly and professional, the bar and lounge areas were quite neat and the food at the restaurant matched our tastes. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Tired Inn Close to Graceland”
text:
On our last leg of our cross- country trip, we decided to visit Graceland, which we really enjoyed. We didn't realize the area surrounding it was very commercial, almost industrial, and we should have done some research before staying in this hotel.
The desk clerk couldn't be nicer. The hotel was busy (lots of truckers) and close to the highway. The hotel had seen better days. The room was small. The bedspreads looked old and we removed them.
The desk clerk recommended a Chinese place close by for carry-out. When our food didn't show up after 45 minutes we called them and cancelled our order. Two hours later they showed up anyway (and took $4 off our order). I wonder how long they would have taken if they weren't so close by!
The same desk clerk checked us out in the morning. Again, she was very pleasant, but we won't be returning.

title: “Excellent hotel - value for money ”
text: My wife and I spent 5 nights at this lovely boutique hotel which we had booked from Mumbai , India based on reviews we had read earlier on the net. Truly, this hotel lived upto our expectations in every manner possible. We were welcomed by the very friendly bell boy when we arrived and the check-in was a cakewalk, what with hotel vouchers, passport and credit cards. Our room was fairly large & well done, with lots of space and every imaginable detail taken care of. Every thing was clean as clean could be and the room was like a second home. The hotel is very close to the subway station, bank, restaurants and just a block away from Pennsylvania avenue; indeed an excellent location in a safe neighbourhood. Meron Ayele and her team were always on their toes ever-willing to help their guests. A good buffet breakfast was on the house with hot and cold beverages available in the lobby round the clock. With a pool, it would definitely be termed 5star. Strongly recommended. Meher & Rustom Dadabhoy Aug. 29th, 2012

title: “Beautiful luxurious property in OK location”
text:
This is one beautiful hotel!! From the moment you walk in, the impressive lobby décor is welcoming and we really had no problems with the staff - they were quite attentive and helpful. The rooms are fabulous – plasma TVs, phenomenal luxury bedding, tasteful carpeting and drapes with every amenity you could wish for in a hotel room (except no coffee machine) and really nice lighting. We loved the lighting in the headboards as well as the stylish individual reading lamps. Robes, slippers, glass scale, organic herbal toiletries – all top of the line, not to mention the marble and granite bathroom with full wide bathtub and separate glass-encased shower, all of which was the highest quality material and really clean. I also enjoyed the user friendly electronic DO NOT DISTURB and HOUSEKEEPING buttons. The rooms were mostly quiet, although you could hear the next room door opening and closing and I could hear the shower on the upper floor as well. There are over 70 TV channels and every amenity in the room, so there wasn’t much more one could ask for, especially paying under $100 via priceline. I don’t know if the hotel will hold up over time, since it is such a new property, but I somehow think it should. We loved it and would definitely stay here again.
The only negative aspect to this hotel is the location. It faces a dirt pit of sorts, as this whole area is undergoing much rebuilding and renovation and although not a far walk from Quincy Market, I think it is more convenient for tourists to be situated in a more central area such as Copley. The area is totally dead day and night but you are only a two minute walk from South Station which is so convenient for using the T. We did not mind, as I’d take this kind of luxury hotel any day over the older more run down properties located centrally.

title: “Excellent”
text: Beautiful hotel, particularly foyer. The room was a decent size and had plenty of natural light. The resident dog, Caty, is a legend and has its own bed in the reception area. The hotel has even produced a book about her! The hotel is situated in really classy area of Boston and a 20 minute walk to downtown

title: “Good hotel, mildly frustrating”
text:
I stayed 6 nights in Oct. 2011 for a conference in town. The hotel is appears fairly well kept, generally clean and attractive, although perhaps slightly dated-looking. However, being in the Fisherman's Wharf area, I understand there is a height restriction on buildings---this hotel is 4 floors---as a result, I believe it is a wood-construction building (not concrete floors)? I say this, because the floor above me creaked noticeably with every step the occupant took---and the occupant above me seemed to enjoy a kind of stomping-pacing for 45 minutes at a time. It became very distracting whenever I heard it; fortunately I sleep with earplugs, so my sleep wasn't impacted.
The room was a good size, though being low, the street noise of traffic was fairly noticeable in the mornings. (The hotel faces at least 3 streets, the way it is laid out---my room was on the side facing the busiest street.) The desk lamp had a faulty power outlet (ie, to plug your computer into, rather than reaching under the desk) and the building engineer quickly swapped out a new one when I called about it. All of the staff I encountered was friendly and polite.
Dining at the hotel is pretty limited. There is a restaurant that, as far as I can tell, only serves for breakfast. Room service is the only option at dinner time (though the hotel bar has two entree options that can be ordered at the bar.) But being 3 blocks from the actual wharf water's edge, there are plenty of dining options nearby; the location is great for exploring Fisherman's Wharf, Nob Hill, Russian Hill, etc, if you're prepared to walk San Fran's imposing hills.
In-room internet costs extra (always a disappointment, somehow!) but is free in the (small) lobby. I don't know whether it is a Hilton policy or a happy accident, but I was only charged 3 nights' of internet for my 6-night stay---a huge relief, since 6 nights worth of internet there costs more than a month of internet at my home!
I might consider staying there again, if I were specifically visiting that part of San Fran. However, I don't know how good the rates are---I was getting a conference rate, but would certainly not want to pay that amount, for this room/hotel, if it were a personal / vacation trip! Yet it was my first hotel stay in San Fran, so I have no basis for comparison.

title: “Budget minded”
text: This is a basic hotel that has parking, frig., and microwave. I'd recommend this to students or the budget minded, but not for a memorable experience. If you are well-to-do, just find something better.

title: “Perfect!”
text: Have stayed here a few times. Can't beat the price and location. Free parking a bonus! One of the few hotels in the city with a pool. Would stay here anytime

title: “Waldorf Towers "Not Impressed"”
text:
I stayed at the Waldorf Towers along with my 2 children in October. During Check in process we were given our room cards, but no inform ie; where to go for breakfast, the lift to take to our room, "we had to be ask for this information or work it out ourselves" (a bit disappointing for the Waldorf). The staff ie; Bell Boy's, Waitresses, Chamber Maids where wonderful and some of the receptionist. A minority of staff seemed to undermind us, MAYBE because we were not wearing designer clothing. 
Business facilities are overcharged, for an average of 15 min, I paid £21. 
Continental breakfast is included with a good selection, but be preparded to wait for a few minutes if the room is full (again the waitresses were very accommodating).
We stayed in a 2 double room, which could have done with being re-decorated (although it was cleaned at a very high standard), the wallpaper was lifting in places but, was spacious and the shower door was broken on arrival although they fixed it as soon as I complained. 
I feel that the name is what makes this a 4 1/2* hotel and they need to treat all of their guest equally. 
I would recommend this hotel for its location but, overall was not very impressed.
If you have been to Dubai and stay at some of the hotels there, I think you will understand my disappointment.

title: “May 22 stay”
text:
Normally, my stay here is great but this time due to the room I had it was less than desirable. I had room 215 and the noise comming from the mechanical room next door was non stop. It would wind down and start up again like an airplane engine. Then it would just run constantly. I had to take a sleeping pill to get any sleep. Next time I will go somewhere else rather than have to sleep in that room. I cannot believe something cannot be done to stop the noise. I come down to Houston every couple of months now and this Hotel is close to our office so I would like to continue to stay there.
Hope something is done.

title: “Amazing!!!!”
text: Stayed two nights and was amazed how close this was to the strip. Easy access to a good sized mall. Definitely a lot to do in walking distance. It was a beautiful room and hotel. I would recommend this hotel. The option of self-parking was nice and cheaper than other hotels in Hollywood at 10 dollars a day. Had a room with a view of the pool. Washroom and room itself were large and spacious and very clean. Excellent value. Awesome!

title: “very nice”
text: I stayed here August 24/25 2012 for the Michael Jackson Fanvention. The room was great. I used the exercise room and the computer room. We had a dance party event in the restaurant, lots of fun. I felt safe and comfortable the entire time.

title: “You get what you pay for”
text:
Initially booked this hotel for a cut-rate price, but in the end you get what you pay for. An "upgrade" to two double beds cost an extra $20 ( a roll away was $10 extra), along with the $15 self parking (no other available) and all taxes pretty much brought our one-night stay to double what I thought I'd be paying. None of this information was displayed on the hotel's website, I had to call to get it.
The staff was friendly enough, although they did not answer the phone initially when I was trying to get some other hotel info. The rooms and common areas were dingy even though they advertised a recent renovation, and the room heater/AC had a musty smell. The parking lot was crowded and confusing, but the shuttle service to LAX was convenient.
Overall a poor but not horrible experience. I would not choose to stay here again or recommend it.

title: “Loved the vibe!”
text: This is truly a cool place to stay if you're into music. A totally different feel and look, not like any hotel I've seen. The staff is friendly and helpful but not overly peppy. The room was well done and the media center had everything we needed. Valet parking only which is to be expected in any downtown area, but it's not cheap. Overall, I would have to say we spent our money wisely with the Hard Rock. If you've never been and you love music, check it out ;) And try the 207 if you dare. Great drinks.

title: “Very Nice!”
text: This was no question a value and nice place to stay. My kids and I were comfortable and enjoyed the amenities. I would recomend this hotel.

title: “Had two good stays here”
text:
Stayed here twice recently. Both rooms were good, one in the south wing and one in the north. My first room had two good windows and the second three, so both were light and airy. Both rooms had good beds, plenty of natural light and an abundance of electrical sockets for powering laptops etc. Both rooms were smallish but for large enough for a single traveller. 
The hotel is in a good location, near the United Nations Plaza and Grand Central Station. The lobby is small and the gym adequate with a couple of cross trainers, running machines and a single bike. 
Staff good and helpful.
Would be happy to stay here again.

title: “Clean, comfortable, affordable”
text: My husband and I stayed here for a weekend, with our daughter and her family in a room nearby. The rooms were spacious, clean, with comfortable beds. We loved that the air conditioning/heating vents were in the wall, not under a window where frigid air blows across the beds at night. The breakfast buffet was amazing, with lots of choices. Our daughter and family enjoyed the pool/spa and used it frequently. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Also, the rooms were quiet and well insulated. Excellent value for the money. One other plus: Very helpful cancellation policy--only 24 hrs., vs. 72 hrs. at many other hotels!

title: “Nice rooms but indifferent service”
text:
I think your view of this hotel depends on how much you pay for it. I was there for work, attending a conference and our company paid over $200 per night. For that, I expect a good-quality business hotel, and the Beacon is not that. Rooms are a good size and were clean, although the carpet was a bit dirty. 
However, several things did not measure up to what you expect at a quality business hotel. Examples - not enough cables to connect my PC to the internet, so I had to wait for one to be returned by another guest; the in-room air-conditioner was very noisy (the engineer came and looked, and said that was normal) so that it was difficult to hear the TV; and the bar shuts early. Reservations staff were surly and not very helpful on the phone. No concierge and no help with recommendations for restaurants. Front desk and bell staff were short-handed and not very helpful. All these things you can put up with if you are paying less than $100, but they become annoying when you are paying more. 
I stay at a lot of business hotels - this one measures up to about Marriott Courtyard level, but has aspirations to be a lot more it seems. Still some way to go.

title: “Perfect location for non-car visitors.”
text: Coming in from the east coast to run the RnR marathon, we were able to save on rental car by taking the light rail from the airport which took us to just half a block from the hotel. Good thing too because parking is valet only and costs 28 dollars a day. Getting around was easy as we could either walk or take public transportation which was either free or very inexpensive. We stayed for 3 nights and enjoyed the resturaunt which served up some delicious meals, the pool which was very relaxing after the marathon, and the comfortable plush king size bed. The staff was very friendly and accomodating. We were given specific directions that even I could follow on how to get to our destinations. When we asked for a good breakfast place, of course we were told about their in house resturaunt but in addition, we were also given a few other staff favorite options in the area. (The Fire House Grill serves up some tasty french toast.) I like the fact that they made us marathoners feel welcomed by posting information on how to get to the expo, start line and how to get back as well as offering up a carb-load dinner. Many hotels I've stayed at for other marathoners have made us feel like intruders. So thanks Marriott for a great experience.

title: “Perfect stay”
text:
My boyfriend, his Mum and I stayed here in August 2012. He was on a business trip and his Mum and I were sightseeing. Location was great for Newbury St and Boylston St (shopping, cafes, restaurants). Rooms were a decent size, though our bathroom was a LITTLE cramped for two people - nothing to stress about however. The hotel and our room was super clean, free wi-fi in the lobby. The hotel was attached to the Hynes Convention Center (for those on business) and also the Prudential Center shopping mall - though the CambridgeSide Galleria is much better, I think. The staff were SO helpful. Nothing was too much trouble. Glayson, especially, was very helpful with restaurants, shopping, trips out advice. Lovely fella. 
Nothing else to say, really. Was perfect!

title: “Overall good experience”
text: Cheapest hotel on Tower Road. Closest block of hotel rooms to DIA. Read the fine print, even though you are booking the park and fly deal, you will still be charged an additional $5 per day upon check in. Hotel rooms were clean and quiet. When we arrived back in town, we called to check on the status of the shuttle. We were told she was there and would wait for us. So nice that they waited instead of telling us we had to wait for the next shuttle in 30 minutes. Will definitely stay again.

title: “Shuttle problems, bad internet, but otherwise a decent place”
text:
My stay here began very badly due to problems getting their shuttle at the Woodley Park Metro. While the hotel is only 5 minutes away from the metro, I waited 45 minutes in 90+ degree DC heat before the driver came (after three phone calls to the front desk).I think this was due to bad communication from the indifferent front desk staff to the shuttle driver. So if you are staying here, call and get the driver's cell phone number (he gives it out readily) so you can bypass the front desk and deal with their friendly driver directly. Also note that the shuttle doesn't run from about 1030am to 4pm and this hotel is FAR from the metro if you are on foot, so you'll be taking the bus during those hours.
Also, beware that the internet here is really bad. At least it was in my room. Sometimes it was so slow, things would time out. Very frustrating if you are relying on this to get work done. 
That said, there are several things to like about this hotel. Beds are comfortable, rooms are large and have a fridge, desk is set up well (good plugs) with a good chair for computer work. Breakfast staff is very nice. Several restaurants and Whole Foods close by.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: Great service, well appointed rooms lots of eating spots 2 blocks up on 9th. room available early for check in which was helpful. Room Service was good. Did not go up to roof deck bar but seemed very active. No Ice machines on floor....need to contact front desk,for delivery of ice.

title: “Loved it”
text:
The hotel is great in all aspects. It's close by to everything San Diego has to offer (downtown - 29 minutes, Coronado - 25 minutes, SeaWorld - 15 minutes, La Jolla - 15 minutes, Torrey Pines - 10 minutes, Legoland - 15 minutes). The hotel is located close to the Interstate 5, but it's just far enough from the highway that you are not even aware that it is nearby. The pool is good even though we did not spend too much time there (only once when we arrived) - there are just too many good things around San Diego to be in a pool. The room was spacious, clean, and well decorated. We had to use a room that had only one king-size bed (we were travelling with two children (4 and 8)) as the room with two double beds was not available. However, the room had a pull-out couch which suited our kids just fine. One final note - the parking is complimentary and was always available (the parking lot was quite big).
To sum it up: I definitely recommend a stay here if you are heading to San Diego area.

title: “Awesome Staff”
text: The Hotel Commonwealth is an amazing place to stay. We were in Boston for four days on a road trip from Boise, ID. When we first arrived we were greeted by Yohanes, a great friendly valet. He helped us with our luggage and it was a nice welcome to the hotel. Then the Front Office Manager, Mr. Ryan Burns, was extremely nice and welcoming. He made us feel like family. He then guided us to the Eastern Standard, which has amazing burgers. Then the next morning we were greeted by another valet. He noticed my Kansas City Royals hat and commented on baseball. Nick Macdonald, "Nicky Mac", was a nice and friendly person. He made us feel welcome and was very nice to all of us. Overall our stay here was amazing. Great staff, great food, and great location. You need to stay here if you are in Boston.

title: “Great place to stay in Chicago”
text:
We spent a long weekend at this hotel and had a fantastic time. We had an Executive Suite that was on the corner of the building so we ended up with views of Michigan Avenue and the Water Tower, AND the lake and Navy Pier. The room was huge, with a large sitting room, separate bedroom - two tv's etc. My only complaint was that there was only one sink in the bathroom and the bathtub wasn't large. The service at the hotel is top notch - extremely helpful and friendly all round. We had drinks in the bar a couple of times, and there was some great music. Bar prices were reasonable for a Four Seasons, and you have to try the Scotch egg bar snack - just the best!!
The location of the hotel was perfect for walking to all the places we wanted to go to, including some fabulous restaurants, but taxis were right there when we needed them. Highly recommended - I would definitely go back!

title: “Excellent and Convinient Location”
text:
The Marriot East Side is conveniently located and it is very easy to visit all of New York from there. The subway station is just around the corner and the many sights of New York, like the Rockefeller Center and Broadway are at walking distance.
The hotel is very confortable and has a good breakfast.

title: “Kudos to The Orchard!”
text: The Orchard is a lovely, affordable oasis near enough but not in the heart of the Union Square rush. The cable car is right on the corner and the bus just a few blocks away making the hotel's location very convenient. The rooms are attractive and clean and were kept that way throughout our stay. The bed was exceptionally comfortable. All personnel we dealt with were friendly and knowledgeable about the city and environs making good recommendations about transportation and places to eat. A nice touch is free DVDs to borrow and play in your room after a long day of sightseeing. We would return to this hotel and recommend it to others as a real value in the heart of the city.

title: “Terrible”
text:
1. A torned rubber band and previous guest's luggage tag found in the middle of the floor. Much bread crumbs between a coffee table and a couch. Housekeeping obviously did not vaccum. Rubber band was gone but luggage tag and crumbs stayed whole time. Kitchenett trash was collected only every other day.
2. If your room is facing the back, expect to be waken at 4 and 5am by trash collecting trucks.
3. Bathtub drains slow. By the time you finish showering the water is several inches deep. Takes 20-30 mins to completely drained. Shower curtain was very moldy.
4. Parsimony with bathroom amenities. We stayed for 5 nights. Body soap was given twice, shampoo once and body lotion once. Had to use our own supplies.
5. Room phones were out. Were fixed right away but were broken again.
6. Black lumpy dust was expelled from AC and landed on the bed. Playing with AC because it was not cool enough resulted the breaker to go up.
7. Horrible valet parking. We had a rental car for 2 days. First day, it took 25-30 mins to bring our car. The second day, it took 20 mins to locate our car, was not in a garage, was parked across from the hotel entrance overnight and which happened to be in front of a fire hydrant. A parking violation ticket was on the windshield. The car key bellboy handed was a wrong one. It took a while to find the right key. Then the right car key had an extra attachment - somebody else's house key! Two days later, upon our check-out, the front desk finally took the responsibility for the parking ticket. We will observe whether the hotel really take care of it.
Enough reasons not to go back.
Great location. The hotel is under renovation.

title: “Pleasant Surprise”
text:
I recently attended a 3 day meeting at the Hyatt and must say it was a great stay.
Because the hotel is on the other side (south) of the Congress bridge, i worried that it would not be easily accessible to the great dining and entertainment places on the north side - i was wrong - those places are easy walks or cheap cab rides.
the hoptrel itself was fresh, clean and offered a great lobby bar where my fellow meeting participants spent A LOT of time. The bartenders were great.
the only drawback/disappointment, which is otherwise a great benefit to the Hyatt location, was that the bats had left the bridge for the winter :(.

title: “as advertised”
text: stayed here in late may for 4 nights and was satisfied in every aspect of my stay. the staff was courteous and attentive. the location ( upper west side ) was, well, one of the nicest locations in manhattan. great restaurants, bars, within walking distance, the subway less than 1 block away. value? show me a better value in manhattan. would i stay here again? absolutely. jm 6/16/03

title: “Best Downtown Hotel in NY”
text: The hotl staff is wonderfull, the food in the Concierge lounge is the best I have had at any Marriott! Tuesday nights are the best when the Chef turns himself loose and gets creative. The hotel is convenient to all transportation, minutes away from the Hudson River walkay along Battery Park, and Tribeca is a short walk as well.

title: “What Happened This Year ?”
text: My husband and I always stay at this hotel prior to our annual vacation and always enjoy it . This year , people were arriving at an alarming rate and we thought there was some type of convention . We later found out these people came from a flooded apartment complex . Small children and adults constantly in and out of the pool and all areas of the hotel , slamming doors , running down hallways, and making all lobby areas a hazzard due to the little bit of snow outside and around the pool area . There were also security guards walking around the hotel , making us feel very uneasy . We have never had this situation in our past stays here and hope it does not happen next year .

title: “Nice place”
text: Nice hotel, conveniently located across the street from the SD Convention Center. Rooms were nicely decorated, sort of modern with funk thrown in for good measure. Restaurant on-site was somewhat limited and expensive (breakfast buffet was $30 with tip), but on the other hand there are probably 100 restaurants within 10 minutes walking distance of the hotel, so this is really not an issue. Front desk and all staff were very service oriented, and all had a positive attitude. Fairly new hotel - I loved the fact that this property actually has windows in the room that OPENED!!! There's nothing like some fresh air in a room.

title: “fantastic, romantic, Alaskan Lodge on the water, perfect, great bargain”
text: No bad view. beautiful Lobby. Great vews from the bar area. would hands down stay here again.

title: “Horrible!!”
text: The Congress Plaza Hotel was horrible! I do not recommend this hotel! The pictures on their website made the hotel look so nice and elegant. We thought it would be a good idea to stay here since it's not very expensive and it has a lot of nice history to share with the family. One of my family members had previously stayed here around 10 years ago (long time) and said it was a nice place! It's not! We first got into the main lobby... It's very beautiful! But.. The hotel staff were very rude and abrupt. We had a few questions and they did not take the time to answer them. As soon as we got in the room, we were appalled. The room was disgusting! The carpet was moldy and wet, which gave off a weird odor. Our standards were not high considering the look of the place. The bedding of the beds was a weird yellowish color. The pillows were nasty and looked like they were very old. We could live with this considering we wouldn't spend any time in there, only to sleep. A couple days went by- the bedding was replaced which was nice, but the floor was consistently wet and stinky. Also the bathroom had no fan to clear out the steam for the shower so it was impossible to do anything in there while another person was showering. The tub was small, but okay for the time being. The housekeeping was nice and brought us extra towels.. But do not trust them. There were four people in the room. Each person had an ipad.. Well, all of them were either in a bag concealed or in the safe. The two that were in separate bags were stolen. My iPad was out on the night stand and was not stolen. We found that unsettling. We contacted security right away- they sent someone up. The guard was nice. He checked the doors and made sure no false keys had been used. There had been some suspicious activity though. We came back to the hotel at 4:30 to get dressed to go eat at a nice resturaunt. We came back at 11:00 only to find two ipads missing. The security searched the room and the door. Between the time we left and came back a housekeeping key card had been used. But, they hadn't been able to pinpoint who exactly was in there. The security refused to do anything else. We contacted insurance and credit card companies to make sure that they couldn't spend money. They told us the hotel could do more and had to file it on their insurance. It has been two weeks and after numerous phone calls still won't tell us anything. The next night two of our family members were woken up because of some teenage boys on the fire escape. They were singing and being very loud. We contacted security as did our next door neighbor. Security did nothing. This went on for 4 hours. Eventually waking up me and my other family member. All in all, I do not recommend this hotel. The service is rude. The hotel rooms are very dirty. If you do stay here, keep all valuable things kept in the safe!

title: “Surrounded by the N. Mountain Preserve, the location is fantastic if you enjoy hiking.”
text:
Of the many things we liked about the resort, my favorite thing about Tapatio Cliffs was the location. Although convenient to much of Phoenix, it is pretty much surrounded by the North Mountain Preserve. A hiking trail runs right by the resort, and taking this trail in either direction leads you to a network of trails. I hiked every morning and was able to take a different trail each time. I loved being able to get up and go hiking early each morning without having to drive to a trail head.
Our next favorite thing was the breakfast at Pointe in Tyme. As Hilton Honors members, we got the cold breakfast buffet free, with the option to upgrade to the hot buffet. The hot buffet included omelets cooked to order. Hotel buffets (especially free ones) can often look and taste like they've been sitting for hours, but not at Pointe in Tyme. Everything was really fresh and very good, and there was a wonderful variety of various sausage type things, oatmeal, waffles, fruit, etc. - along with the usual bagels and other things you expect to see. We ate breakfast there every morning of our stay because it was so good and was such a good deal. The wait staff was always very nice and helpful, like just about everyone we encountered at Tapatio Cliffs.
Although the resort appears to be older and perhaps in need of some upgrades, nothing was objectionable to us. Our room layout was like a suite, with the bedroom (with balcony and view) separated from the living area by the bathroom. We found the beds to be wonderful, and our room was very quiet, so we slept quite well. The only real downsides we found were that it was sometimes difficult to find a parking space near our room, and it was extremely confusing to find our way around the resort. I've got a pretty good sense of direction, but I managed to get myself lost within the resort several times. Don't leave your room without the resort map they give you! I didn't find the signage particularly helpful and many of the buildings look alike. The place is a maze. I had to call my husband on my cell phone to try to find my way back to the room one time (and I hadn't even been drinking).
The topography within the resort is VERY steep, and we were staying in one of the buildings located on the upper area, so it was something of a work-out getting back to our room from the restaurant. But there is a shuttle available, and the drivers are very nice, and I think you can just call the shuttle whenever you need it. If you are mobility-impaired or you aren't in good cardiovascular condition, I would strongly recommend staying in a room in one of the buildings at the bottom area of the resort, near the lobby and Pointe in Tyme. 
Although we didn't use the pools or hot-tubs, we noted that there were a number of them and they looked wonderful. Some had waterfalls and views, others were tucked away in little areas of the resort. I assume there are so many so people don't have to walk too far to get to a pool. There's also a workout building which looked very nice, but I didn't use it because I prefer to hike outside when I can. The resort even has its own herb garden. It's kind of in disrepair, but is still nice.
Tapatio Cliffs is also just beautiful, with views and lush vegetation and interesting architectural features. The restaurant at the top of the mountain, Different Pointe of View, has one of the best views in the Phoenix area, and is a wonderful place to have a drink and enjoy the view. Take the shuttle to the top. The road is narrow and steep and probably not the safest place to walk, especially at night.
There's a strip mall with an AJ's (a wonderful local grocery store) only a mile or two north of the resort, which added to the appeal for us.
We visit Phoenix every year or two to visit with my husband's family, and we will most likely stay at Tapatio Cliffs next time and the next time and the next time.

title: “Hotel Belleclaire”
text: Prior to arriving we call;d to say we would like a quie, renovatedt room off the street and arrived to find that's what was given us. The staff were ALL friendly, and never too busy to help with any question or situation. The guest lounge was a great idea, fitted out with free wireless and coffee, tea and water as well as breakfast bars and snacks. The location, with the subway just 2 blocks away and a wonderful market a short walk away was terrific for late night "noshing". We would definitely book here for another visit to NYC.

title: “Ready for at Least A Moderate Makeover”
text:
I'm a long time Hilton Honors business traveller so have experienced many other Embass Suites (and other Hilton Properties). This one is a ready for a makeover. TV's are old tube sets with small screens; TV in bedroom located in a cabinet but doors won't open all the way and swung out so you hd to push them out of the way to walk by. Bathroom clean but dated as was the rest of the hotel. 
Very friendly staff and they get A+ for service and interactions with guests.

title: “Vegas in San Diego”
text:
This is a quick review. We stayed as a family of four only for a night, and oh what a night it was. Screaming kids in their 20's, drunk as can be, ran along both hallways by both our rooms for the night, giving us minimal sleep. Forget about going to the pool with the family. It's all smoking chubby men with hot young plastic women (sorry-cold hard truth). Pool was filled to capacity, waitresses were wearing bathing suits-you get the idea. There was minimal service catering to families also. 
On the up side, the King Suite room was superb, very modern, clean, and smart with a separate bathroom, shower, and sink. Food at MaryJanes and Nobu was fantastic (Nobu never fails me-I looove sushi, and they have the BEST in San Diego). And location, location, location. This place had probably the best location of any hotel in San Diego-walking distance to everything. 
If you are with a family, we checked out the Marriott Marquis, and I HIGHLY recommend staying there. On the water, marina, huge pool, little streams and waterfalls, next to the trolley stop, and GREAT service.

title: “Great location and good value for the money”
text: Hotel is in a great location between Market Square and Riverwalk. We found that we were in walking distance to both places. The staff was great and always helpful!. When they found out we were there for my birthday they surprised us with a "Movie Night" gift including free rental, drinks and snacks. The room was good and clean for the price. They do have an indoor pool. And the breakfast was really good with fruits, cereals hot and cold, hot sandwiches and more. They even had Texas shaped waffles! We were really pleased with our stay and would stay again.

title: “Inconsistant Service”
text: The hotel is an oasis in the area where it is located. After driving toward "Little Tokyo and seeing some seedy looking hotels and blighted, vacant areas , it is truly aesthetically pleasing Hotel. The decor and rooms where quite comfortable and the Japanese Garden was a peaceful pleasure. The Desk staff, when we arrived were quite welcoming, but at other times, they seemed more interested in conversing amongst themselves, than waiting on patrons. We only ate breakfast at the hotel. The greeter was slow to come to seat me and at least on one occasion, I had to seat myself, get my own coffee cup and pour my own coffee. While the room was clean, it appeared that the cleaning staff took more care in cleaning the room the day before we left than during the rest of our stay ( my wife and I were there for 3 nights and 4 days.

title: “Great location; great hotel.”
text:
This is a small hotel that looks like it would be apartments or something from the outside. Location is ideal; with the hotel just a couple blocks from Grand Central you are literally able to get anywhere in the area without much hassle.
The rooms definitely aren't huge, but the layout is intelligent. It gave me plenty of room as a solo traveler, but may be a bit cramped for multiple people as there isn't a ton of extra space.
One of the first things you'll notice is that there are several little details they have thought of so you don't worry about your stay. Along with common hotel amenities like robes, there is a card in the bathroom telling you to contact the front desk if you have forgotten anything. If they don't have it, they can get it, though there is an extensive list of complimentary items such as shaving kits, toothpaste, and voltage adapters.
Upon arriving to the hotel, the A/C was already on, and was actually a tad chilly (which is rare for me, usually in NYC hotels it's OFF and it takes 30 minutes to get to a decent temperature). The shower had plenty of hot water - though take note that the water lever goes beyond 180 degrees (around, not temperature-wise) from its starting point if it doesn't seem hot enough at first.
Bed was comfortable, with plenty of pillows; typical NYC street noise during normal daylight hours but reasonable at night.
There's a Duane Reade drugstore a block over on Madison if you find you need any minor items (like mini-bar items that you don't want to pay mini-bar prices for) as well as several restaurants within easy walking distance. There is an eclectic collection of food within Grand Central if you can't make up your mind - but if you like steak and don't mind paying a bit for it I highly recommend checking out the Benjamin nearby.

title: “Worst Service I've Ever Encountered”
text:
A block of rooms was reserved at this hotel to accommodate the large number of out of town guests for a wedding. At check in, the woman who gave me my room key was criticizing her co-worker for not writing the room number on the envelope. As someone who works in Hospitality, I thought perhaps she could've waited until I left to correct the other woman. I dismissed it and moved on. I should have taken that as a sign of things to come. Tiny elevators, dark and dingy hallways and a humid room awaited me. Suffice to say that the servers in the bar or restaurant are NOT happy to see you. They do not smile, and it seems to take a great effort for them to answer any questions you may have. Our group also encountered a manager who screamed at us and accused us of being liars over a misunderstanding. I actually found it funny that another review on here experienced the same thing, except it was a waiter. My husband 'complimented' the screaming manager on her great customer service skills, to which she screamed at him "I'm not talking to you!" . 
If you like dark, worn out, borderline dirty hotels and an abusive staff, this is the place for you. I am grateful that I live close enough to the Philly Airport that I will never have to stay here again.

title: “Pretty disappointing”
text: Stayed on a busy weekend for three nights. At $250/night +. Not at all impressed. They neglected to clean my room one day: left at 9am and got in at midnight... No maid service at all. They don't bring your dry cleaning up (which matters when you're running late and have 5 minutes to change.) Room service took an hour, was expensive, and was awful. Very rude lunch bartender/manager in the main floor lounge (she clearly didn't want me at the bar). I'm not surprised they didn't ask me how I enjoyed my stay as I checked out to walk across the street and finish my time in Philadelphia at the hotel across the street.

title: “Quick trip to the Big Apple”
text: The location of this hotel was great. A pretty quick walk and you were in Times Square and not far from Rockefeller centre. Free breakfast was a bonus. The front desk staff were very friendly and helpful when we asked questions. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone going to New York

title: “This is my favorite place to stay when I'm in Boston.”
text: You get more for your money here. The square footage in the rooms is much more substantial than any other hotel I've stayed at in Boston. During the many years I've been staying at the Hotel Commonwealth, I can always expect consistently excellent service. The few times I've stayed elsewhere in town, I've always regretted it. This place is a winner!

title: “Nice Modern Hotel”
text: This is a very nice hotel with modern amenities.... Unfortunately my only complaint is in regards to one of the modern amenities. The hardwood floors.... While these are very nice while you're in the room and add a nice modern touch, sadly they really amplify the noise from the room above. We actually had to call the front desk and ask them to call upstairs the first night since the noise of what I assume was small children (at 1130 pm) running around was making it very difficult to fall asleep. The second morning we were there it sounded as if someone above us was pacing back and forth in their room wearing dress shoes or high heels from 8 am until we left at 11. I truly can't describe just how loud this is when you are in the room below. Other than this one complaint I have nothing but good to say about this hotel. The staff was very nice and professional. The furnishings were clean and modern. The location is not right in the middle of downtown but it is just a three minute ride on the monorail. And of course there is the included parking which makes it easy to just leave your car and explore the city.

title: “Loved it! Highly recommend!”
text: This was a combination business/family trip and our hotel stay just increased the greatness of the trip. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the hotel was close but not too close to everything we needed - the convention center, museums, sports stadiums - and it was a reasonable price. and the pillows were great!! Thank you for help to make this one of the best trips we've ever taken!

title: “Perfect Place to Stay in NYC”
text: This was my third stay in this fabulously located hotel. It had been updated since my last visit. You cannot beat the value or location. The staff was friendly and helpful and the room was clean, fresh looking and generously sized when compared with other NYC hotels. The bed was so comfy! The bathroom is a bit small but clean and modern. This is my permanent go-to place in Manhattan. When I returned, an acquaintance asked where I stayed. To my surprise, she revealed that Hotel Edison is her go-to place in the city as well.

title: “Pricey but nice”
text: Stayed in a full ocean view room with a beautiful view of the pacific ocean. Nice room with great looking furnishings. Only drawback if you leave the patio door open the air conditioning shuts down. The do go green at this hotel. Not impressed with the breakfast room, can be improved. If you eat outside their is a fly problem.If you drive or rent a car pay the 22.00 dollar parking a night, since their is very little parking available. It is underground and you can come and go as you please, it is also secured. You can walk to many restaurants in the area.

title: “too hot, too small”
text:
Yes I know "too hot" in the winter is a funny complaint, but it made my stay at this hotel pretty unbearable. There was no cool air setting on my heating unit, and the window only opened about 4-inches, so there was no air circulation. My room was on the 8th floor, and probably never dropped below 75 or 80 degrees. To make it worse, the bathroom had no air fan so taking a shower increased the temp of the whole room.
The room was tiny. I was glad I was only having to sleep there and not spend much free time because the size of the room would have gotten to me. The walls were thin too, so I could constantly hear my neighbor's coversations. 
On the plus side, there is a Seattle's Best Coffee in the lobby which was great in the mornings. And there were some nice restaurants nearby too. The neighborhood is not the best though.

title: “Super Hotel - Excellent location”
text:
Just a "long Weekend" break in New York - but how pleased we were to have chosen The Michelangelo....
Upgraded room was excellent, plenty of space (including our own bar!!)
Staff could not have been more helpful and depite it being in the centre of everything - we found it very quiet.
I note a previous writers experience with the Computer/ Camera shop on the opposite corner!
We were well and truly ripped off by the charlatans - overcharging us by some $500!
Dont know how they mange to keep getting away with it!! 
Love the Michelangelo just dont buy anything from their neighbours.......

title: “Service Recovery was top notch.”
text: Had an issue with overbooked rooms when I arrived after 7 p.m. I was told that I would be put in an executive conference room and had to sleep on a sleep-sofa. I was not happy after a day of travel. Staff was very apologetic, but that didn't make me feel better. At that time of night, my desire to find another hotel was nil. So I took the sleeper sofa. Staff offered me a discount on my stay but since it was business travel it would be of no benefit to me. So they comped my breakfast for two days at The Grand Cafe and comped my dinner for one night at its upscale Cure restaurant which was yummy; and they gave me additional gold points. I was stiff and sore when I woke up the next morning, but they went the extra mile for service recovery. When I arrived back after my meetings, the staff had moved all of my stuff to a 'real' guest room. Grand Hyatt gets an "A" for effort. Drawbacks: Didn't like that I had to pay for internet service (not at the right gold point level yet); and at 4:30 a.m. I was awakened by loud trucks on the loading dock - not sure if it was trash pickup or some type of delivery service. Wait staff and front desk staff were excellent in customer service. I would not hesitate to stay there again.

title: “Great location but a few issues”
text:
We stayed here for two nights for a shopping trip to Chicago. Parking is typically big-city expensive ($51 valet/$39 self park) so we opted for the self park. It's a little hard to find the entrance to the garage, I recommend that you pull into the front of the hotel to get directions. Once you're parked, finding your way into the hotel lobby is a bit confusing. They could use more signs. There was a line of about 5 people ahead of us for check in but it didn't take too long. The room itself was okay with a view of the roof below, so not much to look at. The bathroom floor could have been cleaner. The beds were very comfortable. The water pressure in the shower was good but the shower head had a problem causing it to spray some water towards the ceiling which then dripped down. Some water also sprayed outside the shower which was annoying.
Our second evening we were tired and wanted to eat at the hotel. Unfortunately dinner options are limited to Shula's Steakhouse or the Chicago Burger Company, neither of which appealed to us so we ended up having to leave the hotel for dinner. 
We booked this trip at the last minute so our options were limited. I'll probably look for something else next time I visit Chicago.

title: “Two Star Hotel in a Great Location: Priceline It”
text:
We spent the weekend at Stay on 47th Street (just off 7th Avenue) in Midtown. You simply can't beat the location. You can leave the hotel and be at a Broadway show in 10 minutes. That being said, our room, as other reviewers have said, was minuscule. Think cruise ship. There's about 18 inches of floor space on the 3 sides of the bed that are not against the wall. There is nowhere to elevate your bag and it won't fit in the 12 inch closet; so it has to be on the floor, which means you're stepping over it constantly. But that's fairly typical of New York rooms. Other than that, the towels were cheap and threadbare, and the drain in the shower couldn't keep pace with the shower; so I had to keep turning the shower off to avoid flooding the bathroom. 
The nightclub noise didn't bother us on the 4th floor, but I have three additional gripes. First, the hotel is very under-elevatored. There are two elevators (I think there are 8 floors), and each one can hold a maximum of 4 people, or two people, each with a bag. If you are on a low floor, forget trying to get a down elevator. Every one that opens on your floor is already full from the higher floors. I recommend asking for the highest floor you can get; otherwise you'll never get out of the hotel. There are stairs, but if you have bags, you don't want to have to cart them too far up the stairs, and if you get a room on a floor low enough to use the stairs, the nightclub noise will bother you.
My second gripe is the ice procedure. You have to call the restaurant and they'll bring it up. I tried twice, both around 11 pm when we returned to our room. Both times, the ice didn't arrive till an hour later, at which point we had given up and gone to sleep (only to be awakened by the doorbell). The lack of ice machines is also fairly standard in NY hotels, but it bugs me. 
And third -- the bellman is the same person as the doorman. This mean that if you want help with your bags, or if you're trying to put your bags in storage or get them out of storage, you have to wait for him to come back in the hotel. Yesterday he was out trying to flag taxis for several guests, so we waited about 20 minutes to get our bags out of storage. As a result, I missed my plane. My bad for cutting it that close, but 20 minutes is too long to wait, when all you need is for somebody to unlock the closet door so you can collect your stuff.
My recommendations if you're considering this hotel, which you should if location is important to you (I would stay here again, with reduced expectations provided I could pay what I paid this past weekend) --1. Priceline it. We paid $215 per night for Friday and Saturday through Priceline. I don't know what the regular rates are, but $215 is the right price for what you get. I wouldn't pay more than that to stay here. 2. Ask for a high floor if you ever want to catch a down elevator. 3. If you store your bags, allow a lot of time to get them back. 4. If you want ice, buy it yourself at a liquor store before you go up to your room.

title: “Smokers allowed???”
text:
I am copying the letter that I have sent to the general Manager of the Hard Rock Hotel in chicago, same letter that I had never got an answer from....
You have a magnificent building in an amazing location, but hotels are made of people not of buildings, the lack of service and will to help attitude of your staff is AMAZING, they don’t give a damn about costumers ant their well being. Also a 1000 dollar stay for 3 nights I don’t think is cheap for the kind of service you provide.
Here comes the facts:
Check inn was fine, and let me tell you that the only guys that look happy and willing to help guests are the bell boys and doorman, they are really good and friendly.
But when I came down to your concierge to ask him for help changing my flight, this was his answer:
I don’t have time to help you because I am busy helping other guests, also the music is to loud and I would not hear what they told me on the phone, I can get you the phone number from the airline and you can do it your self!!!! Is that an answer from a concierge!!!! Amazing service attitude, he was really busy watching the Bull´s game on his computer!!! He really had the game on the computer screen , do you let them use internet while they are “working”??? wow, amazing!!!
But this was the worse and the cherry on the cake, on Friday night we notice a strong cigarette smell on our room, I call the front desk to report it, I have to tell you that I hate cigarette and even worse if I have to sleep in a room that smell like an ashtray, a 300 collar ashtray!!!
Costumer service sent a housekeeper with a scent spray, and it was fine for the night.
Next morning really early it got really bad, the smell was really strong, we went out of the hotel and return until late at night, we notice that the smell came from the room 1008 which was a connecting room with ours 1007 and all the smoke came from the connecting door. I call again the front desk and they send three security guards, they knock at the 1008 room and when the guest told them that he was indeed smoking, the only thing they told them was, do you know that there is going to be a fine for smoking?? Who cares if there’s a fine, the guy told them, yes I know, so what??? He paid the fine and screw the others!!!! What if I have asthma, what if I am allergic to cigarette, what if I don’t want to stay in a room that smells like hell!!! I am paying a lot of money for it!! I had to place wet tissues on the door to avoid the smoke getting in to the room!!
I got a call from the front desk and told me that the hotel was sold out and that they couldn’t move me to another room, they offer me drinks on the bar or free breakfast next morning, what a poor way to solve things, the main purpose of a hotel is to make people feel home and safe, not to buy drinks or breakfast.
I think that for health and security reasons guest on 1008 should be aware that if he didn’t stop smoking, you would call the police or something stronger than fine him, I mean all the property has carpets and fire risk is high, what about smoke detectors??
Also I want to mention something else, I know that this is a Rock focused hotel and its decoration is Rock Oriented, but let me tell you that is not nice to wake up with a Marilyn Manson picture in front of your bed!!
The security guard that is on the entrance of the elevators is rude and not friendly, he doesn’t even say goodnight or else.
Any way, I hope you even read this email and take some actions to all the mentioned.
Luis Ojeda

title: “Excellent Front Desk Help”
text: My family of five stayed for a week recently. Although I had lived for five years in Manhattan, that was a long time ago. We knew that NYC is the city that never sleeps, we have become accustomed to the quiet of living in a rural area. The noises at the hotel are normal for NYC, but we found it hard to sleep. One morning I stopped by the front desk and met Jenny, who upon listening to our concerns, was able to locate another room for us that morning. The new room reduced the amount of noise significantly and we were able to sleep better. Thank you Jenny for listening and taking action!

title: “Excellent”
text: We have always enjoyed Hilton Garden Inn. Compared to other 5-star hotels, HGI offers value for the money. We had a room facing the mountain, and had a beautiful view of the mountain and the sunset. The bed is wonderful to sleep on. The room is equipped with a fridge, and micro-wave, but the only shortfall is that the room does not have a safe.

title: “Very decent place, great location!”
text:
Stayed for 5 nights with my wife and 2 teenage sons. The 2-bedroom "suite" was perfect. Clean and neat, with large-screen flat-panel TVs in both rooms. No amenities outside the room, but location is a few blocks from Safeway and Trader Joes, as well as two cable cars. The bus right outside will get you to either end of the city. About 4 blocks from the wharf area.
 If you are getting the AAA discount, be sure to check the bill before leaving. Refridgerator was an extra $5/night.

title: “Grate Place to Stay”
text: Having scanned numrous websites and reviews found the Edison purely by chance at the last minute. Ended up being an excellent move. My sister and I were in NY for 6 days during the blizzard, chaos on the streets but this hotel was so central we could literally walk most places. the location is right off Times Square. The lobby is a bit old fashioned but the room was really good with a double bed each even though only expected singles at best!!!! Would definitely stay there again if or should I say when I go back.

title: “Don't Go There”
text: Our weekend visit was a disaster. Had to ask housekeeping for washcloths. Satellite TV did not work all weekend. Complained about that and was moved to a "suite." Turns out that was two rooms, sitting room and bedroom, but the sitting room had no heat outlet, so we actually had to close off that room to keep some heat in the bedroom. No washcloths again - apparently that is this Sheraton's official policy. Remarkable. Stay away.

title: “December in New York”
text: This is a terrific hotel to stay in. Less than a 10 minute walk to everything including Times Square, Central Park, Radio City and more restaurants than you could every sample. The staff was excellent. They were helpful and extremely friendly. I want to particularly mention a bellman, Mr. Nevzat Eksoz who is so proud of this hotel and loves working there. This would be on my first choice list for my next stay there.

title: “Great rooms/views, bad value/service”
text:
Did a family vacation here with 2 kids under 10. My expectations were high after reading the reviews and knowing what I was paying. The rooms were very comfortable, furnished nicely, and and kept in great shape by the staff. Slept great every night, so either I was really tired or the beds were very comfortable. Had an ocean front room on the 3rd floor, north side. The views can't be beat from there, and the balcony was very nice to sit on and people watch.
The 3 main complaints I had were:
1) The service was definitely not up to what a hotel charging these prices should be. There were a couple times where I was impressed by someone, but for the most part, it was a disappointment.
2) Not many choices for family atmosphere places to eat in the area. Most nights, we ate with our small kids in the midst of rowdy 20 year old college crowds. Nothing against them - I was one once - just kind of felt out of place.
3) Hot tub was out of order for 2 full days, and 1 washer/dryer out of the 2 they have was out of service the entire time. A five star hotel would have had both of these things fixed within hours.

title: “You can't print a receipt?”
text:
Checked out 5am 10/26/10 
Overal fine, upon checkout I wanted a receipt printed out. 
The counter help said I should have gotten one in my email, to which I said ok, but would you print one out anyway. "Ok, but it will be blank". I find it suspicious that any hospitality front counter staff member cannot access the most simple of records. I smell lazy. I won't be back, there's a lot of other cheaper hotels near Charlottes airport, you can do more with your money, and not have indifferent staff.

title: “Great stay!”
text: I stayed at Hotel Chandler for 5 nights and I had a great experience. My room was on the small side, but I was travelling alone and this was a minor issue. More importantly, the room was confortable and quiet which guaranteed good rests after a busy day in NYC. The bathroom is great and shower is perfect!

title: “Mediterranean Inn doesn't have enough stars!”
text:
This is the 2nd time we've stayed there and will return if ever in Seattle again. The location is perfect, close to everything but in a quiet mixed (residential and commercial) neighborhood. Everything was clean and working, the business center is a real boon if I don't want to lug around a laptop, and the on-site Starbucks is a convenient quick-food feature.
At the end of the day, if the rooms and public areas are clean and amenities are as advertised, the only distinguishing factor between one property and another is it's people. These people seem to 'get' that, and everyone we encountered, from the multiple front desk staff to the housekeeping staff was top notch: friendly, polite, dedicated to ensuring a comfortable stay....even made GREAT in-room dining delivery suggestions.
This is a great place to stay in Seattle, relatively inexpensively.

title: “Great staff - clean rooms - great little extras!”
text:
So many important qualities I liked about this hotel: very clean, the staff is extremely helpful, and several little 'extras' that were not expected but very appreciated! I was traveling for the first time with my 1 year old and the staff helped by sending up a refridgerator for his milk, a microwave to help sterilize his bottles, and accomodated freezing a cold pack for my flight back to Dallas. The staff were very, very helpful. :) The hotel has a wonderful breakfast, they even pack a 'to go' version too! The little extra surprise was on the cold weather day, I was greated with warm apple cider, warm cookies out of the oven, and hot soup! 
The only negative to my stay was the slow elevators, not all the time, but a few times. I can live with that given the clean hotel and the accomodating staff.

title: “You can do better”
text:
Hotel Max pretends to be hip at the expense of safety and comfort. The rooms are so small a young person feels closed in and the elevators are so small that we felt claustrophobic. At one point, they stopped working and we were trapped. Staff
was not helpful. Service workers were seen using guest elevators, and on and on and on... Get the picture? Plus, the beds were not comfortable. Go over to the Vintage Park.

title: “Good hotel near LAX with excellent service”
text: Arrived after long flight from New Zealand. Shuttle was quick and they were helpful with the luggage. No problem changing rooms to good sized room with view of city lights. Food was easy and a high standard of service. After leaving, we discovered that I had left my handbag in the room as we were boarding our flight. We contacted Gloria Aleman, the Lost and Found Manager, who immediately found the bag, kept it safe and arranged with us to ship it overnight to our next destination. She was very professional and courteous and we felt confident that everything was well in hand. Thank you so much Gloria for putting minds at ease and helping us in a stressful situation!

title: “Would not stay here again”
text: Great location in the city but that is the only positive about this hotel. Our "nonsmoking" room smelled like smoke and had holes in the sheets on the beds. We hasked to have our room switched and that room had holes in the sheets as well. There was hair on the floor in the bathroom, the curtain was dirty, and the vent in the bathroom had blue painter's tape on it so it can stick to the wall.

title: “The perfect family hotel to explore Washington”
text: This really is a nearly perfect home-base for families who want to explore DC. Having a great breakfast included and easily accessible, along with a great (complementary) happy hour to help frazzled parents unwind, really makes the life easy. There are many wonderful restaurants only a few blocks away (Uni, Otelo, and many others), and the Dupont Circle Metro stop is an easy walk for most. Having the pool makes a big difference with young kids -- even it can get a little crazy in there (it's not very large), but nothing to complain about. We would absolutely go back there again and recommend it to anyone.

title: “great hotel”
text: This hotel is new, modern, and very clean. The lobby is impressive with high ceilings from a former bank. The rooms are spacious, nicely furnished and include a kitchen area, sleep sofa, and a flat screen t.v. The bathroom has granite countertops and is a good size. Free wireless internet and full breakfast are included. Most importantly, the staff is very welcoming and helpful especially the general manager, Rob K. Rob was extremely helpful and professional and spent over half an hour rectifying my priceline reservation. Definitely a hotel we will come back to.

title: “Problems with a wedding reception below our room”
text: We selected the Fairmont San Francisco for a romantic getaway celebrating our anniversary. It's a beautiful hotel in a great location. We reserved a room in the "tower" section to have a view of the city and requested a high floor, which we got. Check in was smooth, although we had to carry our own bags from our car into the hotel. The room was lovely and everything we expected until we went to sleep. The hotel had booked a wedding reception directly below our room in the courtyard. Even though we were high up, we could hear the very loud band playing. When we called the front desk to find out how long this loud music was going to continue, we were told midnight. This was not acceptable to us and we called management. We were offered another room, but by this time it was 11:30 pm. Exhausted, we agreed to pack up our stuff and move to a different room. (I would have expected the hotel to move us, they didn't offer to do so.) We schlepped our luggage through the hotel lobby to the other side of the hotel to our new room...at 11:30 pm. Why the hotel books rooms over a large reception area when they are aware of the potential disturbance, I'll never know. Certainly a hotel that charges $$$$ for a room, and has the reputation for excellence that the Fairmount has, should know better. We probably would make a different choice in the future.

title: “Friendly staff, comfy beds”
text: The staff at this hotel was friendly, helpful, and easy to get along with. The rooftop pool was great (Our room had a door right outside to it!) and it the Metro was right in the basement of the hotel!! Definitely check out the little pub downstairs, the the food was good and they mix a great amaretto sour. I would stay here again.

title: “Fire front desk and restaurant staff”
text:
Every question I asked staff got an automatic "No" answer. No one went out of their way for anything. What I was most shocked about was the fact that we has a huge seminar with about 400 people and they closed the dining room for dinner! What poor customer service AND a loss of money for them. The staff at the restaurant did not understand why I thought it was a big deal that it was closed when we had more than 400 people walking down stairs who could have filled the dining room in minutes if it was open. 
 Managment, the employees you have on staff have declined over the years. I used to come to your place alot when staff was friendly and looked to see how they could get YES answers for customers. The front desk staff today had terrible customer service skills. I won't be coming here again unless I hear from others that there was a HUGE change to staff and customer service. 
'

title: “We adored this place!!”
