text: Mom and i stayed here last night and we absolutely LOVED this place!! the hotel is a gorgeous, historic, beautiful restored hotel with wonderful history and super quality. the people that work there were so friendly, and helpful, and caring. the rooms were so clean, so cute and the layouts were awesome! comfortable beds,stocked old fashioned frig in the room, a basket full of goodies (that you pay for,if you eat, but it's always nice to have that option!) although the place is antiquated, the amenities are not. room service was spectacular, the towels were plush and plenty, they have their own brand of soaps, lotions, shampoos. flatscreen tv mounted on wall for perfect view from bed. basement lounge is sooo kool, the restaurant was to die for!! the food is outstanding!! there are so many patios and porches and lounge areas, it was just super. the only thing to make it perfect would have been cooler weather...it was 107 degreen outside!! nice and cool inside and the ac worked wonderfully despite the HEAT and big ceiling fan over the bed was heavenly. we cannot wait to return again and again, especially when the tempurature in TX cools off!! it sits right on the river and that is also glorious!! thanks HAVANA, we loved it!!!

title: “Great once inside”
text:
If you are coming from LAX in a rental car, be prepared for a bit of a tough U-turn on Century Blvd. in order to get to the driveway, which could honestly be marked better. Leaving is no picnic either. That aside...
This is a nice property. The updated rooms are cozy and quiet. The gym is a nice facility where you can actually get a workout. The lobby has several dining options, which is also good. You can grab food on the go or have a couple different experiences eating in.
The lobby looked like it could be a bit of a scene. Lots of activity in there all the time and the bar is a bit livelier than other properties on this strip.

title: “What a treat”
text:
Traveled to San Francisco with my family, including two teenagers. This hotel was quite a find. We've stayed at the larger hotels in SF, Parc 55, Holiday Inn in Fisherman's Wharf, but we loved the smaller size of this hotel. The french cafe across the street was very good and so convenient. There is also a wine bar next to Cafe de la Presse that was very good. We had wine and a salami and cheese plate that was very tasty.
The past reviews have already said it all; conformable beds, great shampoo, friendly staff, best location for walking the city.
One thing I was happy to find out about in these reviews, and I'd like to state again, was the parking. We drove here from the Central Coast. So we had a car to deal with. Parking is expensive in the city. It is $40 per night at this hotel, which is typical. We used a previous reviewers advice and parked around the corner at the St. Mary's parking garage on Kerney and California. Friday night was $32, then it was only $7 for Sat. So you can save some cash with that option.
Overall, we loved this location. We will more than likely stay here again if we can the great rate that we got from their website, which beat out all the other travel websites for this hotel.

title: “Absolutely Fabulous!”
text: From the minute we arrived at the front door to the day we left we were made to feel like the most important couple in the hotel. The staff were friendly, attentive and nothing was too much trouble. Our room was gorgeous, modern, clean and really spacious and the bed was extremely comfortable. We booked our trip through Virgin Holidays for our twentieth wedding anniversary and on arrival received a bottle of prosecco and chocolates from the general manager with a card which we found really touching. We then received a bottle of chardonnay from the front desk to say congratulations! The location of this hotel is fantastic, close to Central Park, Fifth Avenue & Times Square. Also the subway on 57th is really handy for going downtown to 9/11 memorial and Battery Park. We will definitely stay at The London again, can't wait!

title: “Wonderful historic hotel”
text: We enjoy staying at the Palmer because it is historical and the facility has been restored beautifully. Make sure to check out the ballrooms. The Lockwood restaurant is excellent and the service is the best. It has a very friendly hotel staff. The typical room is a little on the small side as most older hotel rooms are. We always recommend this hotel for out of town guest because of it's historical significance and proximity to the museums and M. Park.

title: “Great Stay! Great Value!”
text: Our family of 4 had a great experience at this property (which is brand new)! The staff was courteous. The rooms were nicely furnished and clean. The beds had wonderful down comforters and very soft pillows. We used the free internet which was convenient. The pool was small, but nice for our 2 kids, ages 4 and 7. This hotel was just across the parking lot from 2 restaurants: Longhorn Steakhouse and Ruby Tuesdays. This made it convenient to walk to dinner. The JAX airport was just 2-3 minutes away. We stayed at nearby Hilton Garden Inn earlier in our trip and the Hampton was a great value. The Hilton was way overpriced (by at least $40) for the same, if not less, accommodations. We would definitely recommend this to anyone!

title: “We were happy”
text:
We had a great comfortable stay with a really friendly service. The first night we stayed in a room with a connecting door to the next room. That was quiet noisy and we tried to change the room next day. The staff was really friendly and gave us without any problems another room. We appreciated the really comfortable beds and the modern bathroom. I have never slept so well in a hotel bed. We were happy to get a breakfeast, which was much better then the common continental breakfeast in other hotels. They served, with a great view at the 8th floor, toast, cornflakes, ham&cheese, jam, honey, eggs, fruits and cones. For me it was really ok. I was also happy that the hotel have had a fitness room, which I used twice times for my own.
We have known before that the surrounding of the hotel would no be good. Anyhow, as german tourists we were shocked about the many homeless and poor people around the hotel. Some of them lay just on the pavement. You should durin the day using the recommend walking route by the hotel to reach the bus station to downtown. To avoid any stress we decided to use a taxi when it was dark. I hope you will get such a good stay like us.

title: “Pleasently surprised”
text:
We have a certain level of expectation when you stay at a Marriott brand. We had flight problems and Continental was putting us up for the night. We were afraid until we heard it was a Springhill. No this isn't top of the line stuff,but for how crowded this place was and all the hotels in the area, we were happy with the selection.
The room had a desk and a sofa area and the bed was very relaxing.
Good choices for breakfast even with all the people they weregetting served.

title: “Loved It”
text: My FI surprised me with a one night stay for my birthday and I just absolutely loved the hotel. We stayed in a riverview suite which had beautiful furnishings, an amazing bathroom with a larger than average tub and great water pressure and one of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in at a hotel. The view of the riverwalk was amazing and this hotel was so romantic for my special day. The service was impeccable--front desk even called to make sure we liked the room after we had been there about one hour. The rooftop pool looked absolutly great but we did not have time to utilize it. This hotel is in an excellent location just steps from the restaurants on the riverwalk. Their own restaurant was really good for a quick drink and some tapas before heading out to dinner.

title: “Great Customer Service/ Good for a quick stay”
text: Recently stayed there, the hotel needs a bit more care, you can see it once you get there, and to me that was the only downside I can speak off. Customer service is FANTASTIC (at least in my experience), did a late check in (there to visit Lackland AFB) and needed milk for my baby, the girl at the counter gladly gave me milk free of charge and even asked me if I needed any more, before arriving I would send emails with a bunch of questions and not once were they rude to me and answers came back faster than I expected. Before check out, I had a problem with the payment, was charged twice through the reservation website I used and then directly at the counter, spoke to them and they helped me solve everything. It's great for a short stay, good for what your paying.

title: “Best kept secret in SF!”
text: We stayed in the Hotel Adagio for 2 nights in September. The food, service, and overall experience was excellent. Things that slip under the radar when chosing hotels is the life around the hotel. Adagio is walking distance to downtown and all kinds of nightlife!

title: “Comfortable Clean City Stay”
text: We booked a room on an upper floor but not on the executive level. The view was a side view and if you leaned in the bay window, you may see a bit of Puget Sound. The room was compact but very comfortable. We ate 1 breakfast at the top floor restaurant and that was very good. You can get a table with a fabulous view there. The parking garage is a bit tricky with sharp turns but it's always nice to park your own car. The walk to Pike's market and Pioneer Square is not bad. A few blocks but the downhill stairs will tire you. After walking around all day we opted for a taxi back anyway.

title: “Poor night's sleep ;-(”
text:
We spent a weekend at the Grand Hyatt. The first night was on the 25th floor near the elevators, and as we found out, under the 26th floor lounge. Guests using the elevators and slamming doors kept us awake until about 2 am, then sometime before 6 we heard footsteps above, lasting several hours. We asked for another room for our second night and got a corner on a lower floor. Certainly quieter, but slamming doors were still an issue (some hotels have now figured this out). Additionally, the king bed was too hard for us - I still have upper back pain 3 days later. Most other high (and mid) tier hotels have more comfortable beds. I travel about 40 nights per year and this was one of the least comfortable beds I've had.
The staff was great. Downtown's always noisier (sirens) and we knew that when we decided to stay in the city center. It was worth it for us to be able to walk to restaurants and shopping.

title: “Very nice!”
text: Great hotel! Everything was top notch for us! Two couples went to enjoy a weekend away from the kids...and we enjoyed our time there. Breakfast was a very nice touch! Not a typical continental breakfast!

title: “Very accommodating”
text: There was a slight mix up with our reservation (those things happen -- it was no big deal) and the staff and manager was quick to accommodate our family and make our stay very comfortable. The hotel is nicely located. We were in town for Cubs-Reds game and the hotel was full of people going to the game. Our boys had a great time and the hotel was very clean, quiet and comfortable. When we come back to Chicago, we will stay again at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers. Nice quality for the price and you don't have to deal with the traffic. The managers and staff were so pleasant and helpful and professional --- and that still matters.

title: “Nice golf setting, worn furniture, expensive fees”
text:
Very nice and tranquil setting within a golf course. Freeway close yet no noise can be heard from the room. 
Room was spacious and clean. 
Lampshade and seats by the "sitting area" were worn; lampshade was so disfigured I covered it with a towel and didn't bother turning on the lamp. 
Front desk people are always very pleasant; this was my third stay. 
The breakfast buffet is pretty good, however the menu never changes so it does get old (my last stay was for 5 nights).
The parking fee is outrageous so take that into consideration.

title: “Room was nice, room service wasn't”
text: The room was nice, the bed was comfortable. Everything was clean. I ordered breakfast as room service. They managed to screw up my order TWICE.

title: “Great Location!”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Palomar over the Memorial Day weekend while in the city for a friend's wedding. From our arrival to departure everything was above par. 
 Upon arrival we were greeted by the valet. When we asked for an option other than valet parking, he graciously directed us to a parking garage two blocks away. The bell hop took our bags and they were in our room by the time we returned! Check in was a breeze. Our two younger children each received a voucher for milk and cookies to be delivered to our room. The two older chidren received a voucher for an in-room movie and snacks. 
The rooms are spacious, comfortably decorated and very clean. I would highly recommend a stay here if you are planning a trip to Phily. The hotel's central location is within walking distance of many great restaurants and attractions.

title: “Not as Nice as Most Hyatts”
text: I came to this hotel with a conference attended by about 600 people. Although this Hyatt was pretty and clean, and the staff were friendly and helpful, it wasn't what you would expect from a Hyatt. Very poor lighting in rooms, especially bathrooms, making makeup application pretty tough. Very low water pressure in shower. Cheap thin towels, like what you expect at a lesser hotel. Horrible broadband - it was extremely difficult to get on, and then it often shut off in the middle. Elevators were extremely slow and there were often long waits. I had a noisy room near the elevator. So, while perhaps they were stretched thin because of the big crowd, I really wouldn't recommend it.

title: “Not worth the price.”
text: The only nice thing at this resort is the water park, but you have to get in line at least an hour before it opens to get a chair. Our TV's in our room are so old that the picture has lines going through it. Service at the on site restaurants are awful. Were seated then waited 10 minutes and never got served or even noticed. The deli they are not friendly at all. The two off site restaurants that allow you to charge to your room are good but dont forget your card that is in your packet when you check in that they dont explain to you or you cant charge it to your room. Have little ants on our vanity which were all over our tooth brushes, even after they said they would take care of it. When we went to management we were given $50 to spend at the pool area on food (but it cost us over $100 to feed four people). You could here other guests stating that rooms at Marriott are way nicer than here. The workout area is also really nice and a ton of great equipment. But at $350 a night it isn't worth it.

title: “Great hospitality, great location”
text: I stayed at the Westin for an academic conference conducted there. As far as conference hotels stays go, in my experience, I've never stayed in one with a better atmosphere. The staff was unfailingly helpful and polite; the room was very comfortable; workout facilities were top-notch. And the location is hard to beat--easy walking distance to both the waterfront and the Gaslamp district, both of which hold a wide range of fine restaurants. Last but not least, it was EXTREMELY convenient to the airport, with a free shuttle: flying out on Southwest, it took us only 30 minutes from the hotel lobby to our assigned gate. I would definitely stay there again whenever in San Diego, and I recommend it most highly.

title: “Tut visit-I was VERY impressed with the staff's friendliness & helpfulness.”
text: The lady behind the desk at check-in was extremely helpful in getting our King Tut tickets. We needed them all on Friday since we were going with children & couldn't get everyone together on Saturday. Also, the manager that evening went out and skimmed the leaves from the pool so the children could try to go swimming. (They were so looking forward to swimming.) He was right that it was too cold, but the kids appreciated being able to get wet a couple of times before they started to turn blue & we got them out. Also the air conditioning went on the fritz Saturday night & the staff gave us vouchers for another night. We hope to use them.

title: “2nd class citizens at this hotel”
text:
Booked this hotel 4 months in advance. My family and I show up and the manager says my reservation for a room with 2 beds can't be honored. Finally the mgr agrees to give us a room with 2 beds. We go out for a walk and when we get back, the room is gone. Mgr says he can't help. Apparently if you book through a "3rd party" like travelocity then you are a 2nd class citizen at this hotel. 
Right now we've been waiting an hour for a rolling bed. No luck. So far we've been treated like crap with terrible service. Been lied to several times by the mgr about our room. Who knows if well ever see the rolling bed.
DO NOT RECOMMEND. AWFUL SERVICE. TREATS SOME CUSTOMERS LIKE 2nd CLASS.

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text:
Stayed 2 nights during summer tourist season. Hotel is in convenient location (Copley Place) with plentiful shopping, restaurants all within walking distance. The "T" and Commuter stations all very nearby.(Back Bay and Prudential stations) (We actually took train in from suburbs, since Boston driving can be a hassle.) Staff very friendly and helpful (I know - it doesn't fit the common view of Boston and, truthfully, everyone in the Boston area was helpful when we asked for information.). By the way, the staff all wear a puzzle piece pin on their jackets to signify that they are all part of the service puzzle - it seems to work. Concierge desk provided plenty of useful help and advice about getting around and what to do. Hotel has been recently renovated so rooms were sparkling - all have a mini-frig and the beds VERY comfortable.
We had access to the Concierge Lounge and the staff there was unbelievable - so ready to make sure we were happy. The Lounge is a bit small so can get congested at peak breakfast time but the staff made up for any shortcoming with their attitude.

title: “disgusting, had rats”
text: ok, it said it was a 3 star hotel on expedia and had nice pics. Turns out they were both wrong. After waiting for 2 hours to check in, I saw many disgusted guests leave for another hotel. A mouse came in my room from crack of floor and wouldnt leave. Looks more like a jail cell. Add $5 and stay in a real hotel. I signed up on this site just to ***** at that hotel cuz it was so nasty.

title: “i love this hotel”
text: small hotel in chelsea area of nyc. little things mean a lot to me. the air conditioner works well. the room is ideally planned with a big picture window of other nyc buldings a nice bathroom with counter and elongated shower curtain. very comfortable room. only 6 or so rooms per floor. very nice staff who seem genuinely interested in your well being. nice small bar and breakfast area. small lobby with mirror fountain and two elevators. i would definitely stay here again. hotel is small enough that the help seems capable of handling all that comes their way. good choice for a trip to nyc.

title: “Great little hotel”
text:
Yes our room was small, but you do not come to New York to stay in the room all day.
The hotels cleanliness and the staffs' helpfulness and friendliness more than made up for the lack of room space.
Our room was on 41street side of the building and was very quiet.
The location of this hotel is perfect for the sites of New York; 2 minutes walk from Times Square etc.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Hotel seemed new and everything was in great shape.

title: “Give the Embassy Hotel a Try!”
text: Having not been to San Francisco in over 25 years, I was not familiar with the various neighborhoods of the city. My instructions were to find a hotel that included complimentary (or very inexpensive) parking, convenient location to the heart of San Francisco, and at a reasonable rate. What I found was the Embassy Hotel. At a room rate of $129 per night, double occupancy, FREE overnight parking and COMPLIMENTARY continental breakfast every morning - I thought it was too good to be true. After booking the reservations, I then found reviews saying that it was "sub par" and not a pleasant experience at all. Having arrived home just a few hours ago, I am exhausted but compelled to write this review and to report that the Embassy Hotel was a most PLEASANT EXPERIENCE. The hotel is on the VERGE of the tenderloin district but it is closer to the Financial District and directly across the street from the California Culinary Institute. We heeded the advice of friends to not venture down the next 2-3 blocks at night, but during the day it was fine. Honestly it didn't look that bad to us at all, and several mass transit options are available for travel to and from the hotel. The staff was very knowledgeable about the city and extremely polite. The room was very clean and the whole hotel had the appearance of being freshly painted, it was very cheery and an extremely pleasant atmosphere. The decor was that of Art Deco with the pink and black tile in the bathroom, and the room furnishings were very authentic. The beds were extremely comfortable and the entire room, bathroom and closet included were immaculate. I loved the hotel entirely! The continental breakfast consisted of delicious breads, jams and fruit in the adjoining pub. The whole hotel had a very European feel to it which was noted in that most of the guests seem to be European. If there was a complaint to have it was that the walls were a little thin but that is to be expected with the age of the hotel. I would return to the Embassy Hotel every time I come to San Francisco and definitely recommend to all of my friends. For the cost and convenience, I don't think there is a better deal to be had in the city of San Francisco. I trust that you will have a most enjoyable experience.

title: “The Warwick is an Uptown secret”
text: The location of the Warwick is great. A guest can walk downtown to any business meeting, or at least to the 16th Street Mall and catch the free ride on the bus. The staff are friendly and very professional, and the restaurant is top notch (although slow.) The rooms in the Warwick are very spacious, and the desk/work area is nice. The bedding is fantastic. The only drawback is paid parking, but the valets are professional and the fee isn't as high as it would be downtown.

title: “Bean Town a A+”
text: Came to Boston to watch the Jays and Sox in their three game series and picked this hotel again. Its great that they have free parking! Sure you might think its not the best place for a hotel, but once you get inside you are welcomed by friendly staff and a very clean lobby. The room we got on the 5th floor was big enough room for three guys. It was very clean and the beds were very comfortable. The pull out couch helped out, even though it is a little uncomfortable. The wifi worked great in our room as well. The breakfast was a let down but luckily McDonalds saved the day. The shuttle was a plus because driving around would have been a pain, but taxis from Fenway were about $10-$12 which was really good. The hotel is really nice and it is very inexpensive, I will definatley stay here again!

title: “Awesome!”
text: Everyone from the valet to the front desk was awesome! I can't say enough good things about this hotel. We loved having a kitchen for our family! Pool was great and my husband loved the work out room. Breakfast was your normal free hotel breakfast...but there were a lot of people during our stay so we ventured out the 2nd day for breakfast at Denny's. We were so happy that the hotel was walking distant to everything on the Riverwalk. We even walked to the Market.( a long walk..about seven or more blocks) but worth it to walk off all of the great food we ate. Yes there is a valet charge...but we only had to use it once..and the valet was super quick! We will stay again!

title: “Disappointing.”
text: During my last visit in June, it was a hard time in my life personally. I came down to the bar to be greeted by the most pleasant, welcoming, and friendly bartender I have ever met. She made me feel so comfortable I felt as if we'd been friends for years. I ordered some appetizers that were fairly good and during happy hour at 50 percent off what's to complain about?! Unfortunately, I came down this month to find this bartender no longer works there. I had a few complaints about my stay previously and this particular bartender was so helpful and assured me all of my concerns would be addressed. She was an absolute delight and one of the reasons I chose to return to this hotel. I think perhaps I will try the Marriott down the street as I know there amenities are pleasing, and the hotel is always in superb shape.

title: “Best Wharf Hotel Ever!!!”
text: We went to San Francisco in 2011 and stayed here. The staff is genuine, helpful, happy, and an excellent source of information. We liked it so much we came back to vacation here again in 2012. Trust me you're going to love it. No pool but at the wharf you'll never miss it. One of our favorite things besides the friendly staff is the rooftop. 360 degree view you can see the Golden Gate bridge alcatraz to the Oakland bridge. Love Love Love it!!!

title: “a 20th anniversary to remember”
text: when I made my online reservation at the Palomar , I was asked if there was a special occasion and I disclosed the fact that we were celebrating our 20th anniversary (july 1990 in France). Unlike other places, they did act on that information. We were warmly congratulated at check in, upgraded to the largest room available , on the top floor of the hotel. Charming attention.. but that's not all. When we returned from our celebration dinner, a bottle of champagne and anniversary card was waiting for us. This level of attention will be hard to beat and I am looking towards our 25th anniversary to see if Kimpton keeps this high level of service and classy touch!

title: “Hugh, old but in a great booming area”
text:
The Westin Bonaventure is pretty old. Especially the lobby looks and smells terrible (tons of concrete and chlorid from the artificial pools). But the rooms in the higher levels offer a great view and the hotel is located in the booming Downtown Los Angeles area. Plenty of new restaurants and bars are now open.
Would definitively recommend, if you have platinum status with starwoodhotels, since you get a nice upgrade.

title: “Don't stay here!”
text:
This had to be the worst hotel experience we have ever had. First of all, our reservations for a King room was changed to a double room. The room was nasty. Hair in the bathtub and sink, unidentifiable substance on all of the furniture, carpet wasn't even attached to the floor and the wallpaper was peeling off of the walls. Friends of ours staying there this same week also got changed from a king to a double room in which had no furniture except a bed, but immediately got moved. After complaining several times and a night later, we finally got moved to a king room. The king room was much nicer, however, in the move, our reservations "got lost" and the staff tried to kick us out of our room every morning for the duration of our stay. (4 days) Housekeeping insisted on cleaning our room even with a "do not disturb" sign on the door. One morning, housekeeping just let herself in without even knocking. The hotel front desk clerk called and said that we must check out because we haven't paid for another night and that I must do this "right now" even though our reservations were paid in advance. When complaining to the front desk, we were told "we'll tell a manager and sorry for the mix up." They didn't even try to make things right. Again, the next morning, housekeeping insisted on coming in. They were loud and very noisy while cleaning adjoining rooms. Rooms are definately not soundproof!!! The staff in the hotel were unaware of locations of the vending machines. 
Upon checkout, and complaining once again, they were unconcerned about how unhappy we were and just brushed off because there were other guests checking in or out. 
Overall, our stay in the Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel was terrible!! All I can say is at least we had somewhere to lay our head.

title: “Perfect for Aussie family with two kids (9 and 10)”
text:
Hi,
We stayed in September last year 2011. Finally (after having moved house etc) to reviewing our holiday.
We booked the Washington Court as the rate was good and a few people on Trip Advisor said it was a good location. They were right.
We arrived from New York via train so all of us had a backpack and large suitcase on wheels. The train was delayed so when we arrived the taxi queue was huge. We decided to walk and it was very easy - 5-10mins on flat pavements. 
Lovely hotel, very modern, clean and safe. Seemed to be a lot of business people staying, conference etc. This did not affect anything though - not noisy or too busy in areas - would rather see people staying than not.
The room was clean and modern. We shared beds on this holiday to save costs - for nearly the whole holiday was one adult with one child however that had not been our original plan!!
The hotel is an easy 10 minute stroll to Capitol Hill.
We did not spend a lot of time at the hotel nor using their facilities as we only had a couple of days in Washington and wanted to see as much as we could.
Had dinner at a nice Irish pub just around the corner at night. 
Great that it is so close to the main station as after dinner we walked there and got icecreams, yogurt, some fruit etc. 
Plenty of people around at 8pm-ish and felt safe walking from the train station back to the hotel.
Would definitely stay again and happy to recommend.

title: “Favorite Hotel”
text: The Greenwich is one of my favorite Hotels in the world. The desk staff is right on target, courteous helpful and makes you feel like a VIP without being obsequious. The rooms are beautiful, the scent in the rooms divine, the bed and bedding, pillow etc are perfect. Free snacks and drinks in the room are great, but they should have some kind of dark chocolate. If you are staying in the Tribeca/SoHo area you have a number of wonderful choices. It is really a toss up between The Mercer and The Greenwich. I do prefer the Greenwich.

title: “Worst Experience. NOT pet friendly like they say!”
text:
This hotel should be ashamed of how they run their business. 
Firstly, the internet did not work for 4 out of the 7 days I was there for WORK. They claimed it was because the routers were in peoples rooms and they had "Do Not Disturb" signs up, so they couldnt enter those rooms while people were out. 
Also my phone was broken. I told them that my phone rang but I couldnt hear anything when I picked up. I approached the front desk about this twice and they never fixed it yet continued to call me for house keeping and such. 
lastly, and most importantly... the staff was outrageously rude. This hotel CLAIMS to be pet friendly, but they were abusive to my dog. My dog was in his crate in my hotel room when I left for work at 7;15pm on a Saturday night (I'm an actor). He usually barks for about 5-10 minutes after I leave and then he is quiet the rest of the night. I had been at this hotel since the prior Sunday and had had NO complaints whatsoever. After work I grabbed some quick food and came back to find me dog was NOT, i repeat NOT in my room, and neither was his crate. I had a completely panic attack because obviously i thought my dog had been stolen. I rushed down to the front desk crying thinking he had been removed from my room and was gone forever. I went up to the lady in the front desk justifiably upset and concerned and said "Miss please help my dog is gone I think he has been stolen," she was on the phone at the time and said "We have him." and put here finger up as if to tell me to hold on because the PHONE CALL was more important than me (the crying, panicked, devastated woman in front of her). She continued to talk to the person on the phone as if i was not important for the next probably 45 seconds. When she finally got off she could not show me my dog, which had been locked in a back closet. She had to call the bellhop to have him unlocked and brought out. He was panicked, scared, upset, and still in his crate. The crate i supposed to be gis safe place and they had removed him from my room and rolled him down the hall and into a closet while still in his crate. She also called me "rude" "hysterical" "inappropriate"... the list goes on. She was so incredibly disrespectful I cannot even put it into words. She acted as if she had done nothing wrong by removing property from my room when i had the DO NOT DISTURB sign on my door as well, and they had not even tried to call me on my cell which they had, or my work phone which they also had. The manager wouldnt even apologize until they next day when she only did it cause I asked her for an apology. I got no compensation, no nothing. They thought they had done NOTHING wrong and had treated my dog fine. He is not TERRIFIED of his crate and hotels in general. DO NOT STAY HERE F U HAVE PETS! I travel for a living, and have been staying in hotels for the past year and I have never once heard of anything like this happening at any other hotel. 
Also the walls after paper thin, bathrooms are gross and carpet disgusting.

title: “A Great Affordable Find In An Expensive Lodging City”
text:
We stayed at this location on a September trip to San Francisco when all we needed basically was a bed and shower each night. So, we wanted a place that wouldn't cost us a forturne (hard to find in S.F.).
We paid only $79 a night here; a real bargain in this town.
The location couldn't have been better for us as we were withing walking distance of the cable cars, BART, etc. We had rented a car, so the free parking was a real nice bonus. We were steps away from some restaurants as well.
Room was small, but adequate for our needs. We found things neat and clean and had no problem with the maid service. I don't remember the place being noisy, but perhaps I just didn't notice.
If we return to S.F. again, I'd definitely check this location for price again and consider it for a stay.

title: “Average place near a great part of town”
text: Spent one night here for a meeting. Breakfast was not included in the room rate. The room was adequate. The shower was OK, not great. Clean and comfortable. Very close to beacon Hill and Charles Street shops. The rate was fine for Boston.

title: “Staying here was a real pleasure!”
text: What a pleasure staying in this hotel. Everything was topnotch from the time we entered the lobby. The staff was very accommodating, room was lovely and clean and the restaurant served good food. We stayed here three nights before catching a cruise ship. We found plenty of things to do, like beautiful walks, The ArtWalk, The Red Car, Maritime Museum, Carillo Beach and Aquarium, Farmers Market and the quaint downtown area. The location of this hotel is "wonderful" if you are catching a cruise ship. The locals are so friendly, even had an offer for a ride to an LA attraction, but we found plenty to do right in the San Pedro area. Don't miss staying at this one.

title: “Close to Metro and Georgetown, Clean and spacious room”
text: Cute Foggy Bottom neighborhood, less than 5 minute walk to metro, 15 minute walk to Lincoln Memorial or Georgetown Waterfront, Clean room.

title: “Good overall experience! Would definitely go there again”
text: The room was clean, comfortable, and quiet. Johnna at the front desk was MAGNIFICENT - friendly, helpful, and went way above and beyond to make sure that my daughter and I had a great experience. Give that woman a raise!!!

title: “Staying in S F”
text:
We stayed as a family of four at The Mayflower inAugust with our room on the 3rd floor. Our room was clean and tidy with what turned out to be more than enough space to hang all of our clothes, 2 adults and 2 teenagers.
The hotel appears to have kept a good deal of its original characater with the old fashioned lifts (elevators) as well as a good deal of the decor. The continental breakfast , though the same everyday, was more than ample to keep us all going to lunchtime.
Both of the ladies were very helpful with any questions we had regarding SF and keen to ensure that you have a pleasant stay in the hotel.
It is not that bad a walk to downtown or China Town, we did both, as well as catching the cable car from California & Hyde.
Overall we felt that the hotel gave very good value for money. The only negative is the lack of hotel parking, but I was given a good rate at an off street parking garage around the corner.

title: “Wonderful Staff and Hotel”
text:
My partner and I stayed here during the All-Star Game, and I have to say, this was by far one of the better Embassy Suites we've stayed in....and we've stayed in a few. It is about 5 minutes away from Dallas-Love Field and they have a complimentary shuttle that will pick you up and take you to the hotel...or to the mall...or anywhere for that matter. Simply stop by the front desk and ask them nicely to take you to your destination, and they will do it! When you're ready to be picked up, a call to the hotel is all it takes.
The room, an executive suite, complete with a soaking tub, was wonderful. There was a strange odor on the first day (the best way I can describe it was that it smelled "old"), but after placing a call to the front desk, the smell was eliminated almost immediately. Plenty of closet space, water pressure was good, and we had a nice view of the forest and creek below, along with the downtown Dallas skyline. Very serene.
No trip is absolutely perfect, as my partner and I found out. We had a situation whereas we were at the Galleria Mall waiting to be picked up by the shuttle. Apparently the shuttle was side-swiped by another driver, so instead of having us wait in the cold, Jessica (the front office manager) asked us to take a cab back and the hotel would pay for it!
We will definitely be staying here again. The staff truly made it worth it!

title: “Paramount Hotel”
text: Stayed here for 5 nights in January and could of asked for a better hotel. Room was really good and comfy bed. Decor was great throughout the hotel. The mirrors telling you the weather outside was a good surprise as well. Staff were really helpful and concerige were a help when trying to get to different parts of the city.We were on the 17th floor and had no bother with a/c or traffic noises. Would definately recommend this hotel on our experience, we were over for a birthday and this was made more special with the service provided by the hotel. Possibly looking to visit again next year.

title: “location matters”
text: The hotel is like a European hotel. The rooms are small but you are not in them for long so doesn;t matter. The beds and bedding are very high quality. We stayed in the room on the first floor. This room was very loud in the morning with breakfast starting at 7:30. Would definetly stay again just not on the first floor. Front desk was extremely helpful.

title: “Luxury Lodging in the Midst of Fells Point”
text:
How I love this hotel! Or, I should say WE. My daughter and I took a long weekend trip to Baltimore. Our destination? Fells Point. Why? Because we love the shops and restaurants and bars there and have such a fun time every time we go. And, for the last couple years of this annual trip, every time we passed by the Admiral Fell Inn, we'd say, "Next time we're staying there." And now that we finally did, we wouldn't stay anywhere else!
Why? From the few steps up into the lobby, the staff is extraordinarily friendly and accommodating - actually, even before we got there we were contacted by the hotel staff to see what more they could do to make our stay more comfortable, more interesting and more convenient. I like that!
The room was gorgeous! Two beautiful mahogany, four poster canopy beds dripping with cotton lace awaited as we entered the room. Everything about the room suited the quirky, historic twists, turns, narrow hallways of the history contained within the hotel. Every room even has a name! Ours was Forbes. 
We did have a little noise outside of the windows around 3:00 a.m. on Friday night, but rolled right over and went back to sleep. After all, if you want to stay in the midst of where it's happening in Baltimore, what else do you expect? I'd rather have that than have to take a cab back to someplace quiet and boring. And Saturday night was quiet as could be...or else I just slept through it. 
We can't wait to go back and repeat our experience all over again!

title: “Great value and location in downtown Denver”
text:
Our stay at the Magnolia was just what I expected. I have stayed at the Magnolia in Houston before, so had a good idea what to expect, and the Denver location did not disappoint. Given the quality of the facility (which is not luxurious, but certainly better than just about any other hotel at this price) and the great downtown location, you would normally expect to pay more. That's why I rate the Magnolia as "excellent." You can find a nicer, more luxurious hotel, but it will certainly be much more expensive. In my experience, the Magnolias are priced about the same as a Hampton Inn, but offer a much nicer experience for the money. 
Great, friendly service, a clean room and generous breakfast buffet only add to the experience.

title: “I had no expectations, this was a great surprise...”
text:
1) I went to Texas, first time, for a special guy's graduation.
2) I booked a flight and hotel through one of the online resources,
the deal for Comfort Suites was the best, so I chose it.
3) I hadn't check the facility online, so I didn't know what I was going to find.
What I found was a staff that was professional, cordial, helpful beyond expectations, Dan, the Front Desk clerk assisted me in getting into my room quickly, and printed out the directions I needed to get to the graduaiton. As I quickly learned, Texas is very much about highways and driving, and the road kindness of Texans greatly surprised this guy from New Jersey. The room, was, in fact, a suite, and a SWEET one at that. Sofa bed, beautful king size bed,Large flat screen TV, HBO channels, WI-FI, clean bathroom, updated decor, amenities that bring comfort to the traveler, microwave and large size (clean) fridge, secured away in a nice cabinet,, even a laundry room for guests to use as needed. Let's face it, if I moved to Texas, I'd let this be my home!! Last, checkout was quick and easy, no delays or additional expenditures, I was able to get to the airport early enough to get my tickets and checked in, Thanks to the work of this one facility. 
My first trip to Texas was memorable, if I go back, I'm making a similar deal for this hotel.

title: “Nice stay with a good location”
text: This is my 3rd stay on the Marriott Marquis on 4th street. The location is convenient to our annual convention at the Moscone Center. Check in was slow (even though I have Silver Elite status) because of the large number of guests checking in. The room was nice and clean. There were 2 wide screen TVs. Internet service was expensive ($12.95 per day) and not very good. Bed was comfy. Convenient to the financial district and Union Square. Good concierge. The gym has been fixed up, with a good number of machines. Check out was fast.

title: “Great hotel and location! Shame about the building work!”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights at the beginning of December 2010. 
We were very impressed with this hotel the location was ideal for us, out of the busy city and only a 5 minute walk to central park. 
Staff were friendly and helpful. 
This hotel's big downfall at the moment is it's building work! We did not mind very much as we were not at the hotel all day, however being woken up at 7:30am every morning became very annoying. I complained after 2 days and was moved to a room on the 9th floor which was perfect. 
If you find your on a floor were the building work is move immediately don't wait to be woken up. 
The rooms were a good size very clean and well serviced everyday. 
This hotel is highly recommended and a good price!

title: “Great stay for a last moment reservation”
text:
My family and I recently booked a suite here for a three-day weekend. We weren't too sure whether we had wanted to go to Chicago for a trip, or not. At the last minute, my family and I decided it was a yes. Given only one day before actually leaving for Chicago, I booked a suite at Comfort Suites. To my surprise, Comfort Suites is located in the middle of downtown! I loved that part! The room had a kitchen, too! The elevators were fast, so it didn't take forever for us to reach the 23rd floor. (The view from the 23rd floor was absolutely beautiful.) Complimentary breakfast was okay. There weren't too many options to choose from, but I'm happy with complimentary breakfast than not having a breakfast at all.
As for the cons, the internet was down on our first night staying there, and there were quite a few complaints that the internet had been down for almost the whole day, when my family and I checked in. The lobby was a little dirty when my family and I checked in, but it may have been caused by the traffic coming in and out throughout the whole day. Other than that, everything else was wonderful.
I probably would book this hotel again, if I were to visit Chicago again. The location, price I booked our suite for, and the service was very nice.

title: “WONDERFUL HOTEL”
text: The hotel is everything you would expect from a 5 star hotel.From the bellman to room service the staff is outstanding.The grounds are a delight to walk around,You can't go wrong at this hotel.

title: “Horrible Experience!!”
text:
My husband and I travel to San Jose often to visit our grown kids and their families. Typically we stay at the Hotel Valencia on Santana Row, the hotel was sold out so we decide on the Moorpark and thought the change would be nice. 
It was too bad that there was only one person checking people in, we waited for almost half an hour to get registered. Then I asked the nice girl why she was so busy, I had no idea she would tell me everything. Apparently someone had been fired that day and another person did not show up to work. She rolled her eyes and basically told me how terrible the management was there and that nobody wanted to be there including her! As we neared our room I could tell the room would be loud, the hotel is located right off the freeway and all you can hear from the room and the pool is the traffic. It was loud all the time! There is nowhere to go and nothing to do in walking distance from this hotel. From now on if the Hotel Valencia is sold out we will postpone our trip, I never want to experience that again.

title: “Some problems, but very good overall”
text:
First the bad. We had an unengaged and poorly trained desk clerk, who tried to convince us that we had reserved an exercise room, rather than a spa room. We produced the reservation in writing, and, without apology, he announced that no rooms were ready, but that it would be ready "very soon." We went out for a walk, returning after 3 PM, and were told that he had called our cell phone half an hour earlier to tell us the room was ready. There was no call. He checked us in and sent us up to the room, and the maid was in it, saying that she had just started on the room. We went back down, and, again, no apology -- it was the maid's fault. We were ultimately give another room, but the whirlpool bath was broken. We didn't feel like changing at that point.
Now the good: the room was quite spacious and well-appointed. All of the other staff were very friendly, competent, and helpful. The restaurant was great for breakfast. The hotel is convenient to the metro and in a nice neighborhood. 
We will go again, and hope for a different desk clerk/

title: “Great Location for a first visit to NY”
text:
We had never stayed in New York before and so have nothing to compare the Sofitel with, and it seems that all well placed hotels are eye-wateringly expensive.
The Sofitel is superbly located for tourists, with Times Square/Broadway, the Empire State and Central Park all with 5-15 minutes walk in different directions. Despite its central location, the street the hotel is located on is quite quiet. 
Our standard room was a good size, spotless, with a very comfortable bed and large bathroom. The restaurant is 'French' but the menu seems to be the same every night. However there are numerous options within a short walk, both 'upmarket' and more basic. Breakfast at the hotel is good, but most days we ate at the Red Flame, a basic diner about two minutes walk away. The food is half the price and you get a taste of more typical New York life.
Some reviews mention building noise. There is building work going on nearby and some noise does reverberate up through the hotel, but this is only during the day, when you spend little time in your room.
Even walking back to the hotel past midnight we felt very safe - safer than in the average UK city centre after midnight.
In summary this is a superbly located hotel, especially for tourists. It is expensive, but so it seems are its competitors. The hotel is of good quality in every way, the only downside for us being a restaurant menu that didn't change.
If we go back to New York, we would stay here again without hesitation.

title: “Great Experience”
text: The staff was excellent. My king room was everything I needed it to be in cleanliness, space, & furnishings. The mountains/city view was very nice. Free internet was provided, which I appreciated. The hotel was a convenient walking distance to shopping & restaurants. My favorite part of this hotel was the pleasant scent of the room upon opening the door each time. It smelled clean & fresh, like the toiletries in the bathroom. If it had a refrigerator I would give it another star. They should be standard in a hotel in this price range.

title: “Small, personal hotel in great location”
text:
A smaller hotel with excellent personal service....
LOCATION: wonderful midtown location (54th Street between Park and Madison) walking distance to shopping, theater district, most major museums. 
CHARM/ COMFORT: Our rooms were very clean and traditionally decorated with antiques. The bathroom was small, but had been remodeled and had a terrific shower with lots of water pressure. The bed was a huge King-size with a lovely soft pillowtop mattress. Note: we were on the 9th floor facing the street, and it was noisy at 2 in the morning. If you're sensitive to noise, I'd try for a room on the 14th or 15th floor, or maybe one facing the back. 
AMENITIES: Very nice breakfast with coffee, juice, baked goods, fresh fruit salad, yogurts, cereals. Also, Monday - Friday there's a happy hour buffet with wine, cheese and crackers, etc. 
SPECIALS: Check the website for special promotions. I booked a suite months in advance, then saw their "sweet deal" offering on the website -- $75 per night off on any suite during the month we were traveling. I called the hotel and they advised me to make a new online reservation, then cancel the old one, which I did, for a savings of $375.

title: “The Best value for money in Manhattan!”
text: Myself my wife, and two of our friends stayed at Best Western for 6 nights and can not speak highly enough about it! As soon as we walked in the doors the guy behind reception said "you must be the (insert surname here) party, welcome to Best Western!". From there on in it was a great stay. As others have already said, its like having your own place in NYC with with a reception area at the bottom! Bags of room. Very clean. Breakfast muffins, bread, jam, pastries, milk etc is perfect for a quick breakfast before you hit those busy streets. The bathroom was clean and vast array of toiletries refreshed every day, made us wish we have lugged our own over from the UK. Little Pizza place just outside on the right is cool for a quick bite. 10 Mins walk away from everything. Staff were all amazing, really exceeded our expectations. We will definatley be back!

title: “Good Hotel for Veteran NYC Visitors and Unfussy Travelers”
text:
As anyone trying to visit NYC knows, hotels in Manhattan are very expensive. Unless you are traveling with a group of friends, or if you don’t mind staying in hostels and/or having shared bathrooms, a good chunk of your travel budget will be spent in your accommodations.
For the price I paid, $110 per night, the Comfort Inn Convention Center was a great bargain that allowed me to have additional funds to enjoy some of the city’s superb restaurants and a couple of Broadway shows. 
Room:
Similarly, to all the other NYC hotels I have stayed in the past, the room is small. This is common and to be expected. If a large room is one of your requirements, you might want to try staying in Brooklyn or Long Island City. However, you must also take the subway fare into consideration if you decide to stay outside of Manhattan. 
The room was appropriate and comfortable. It was cleaned every day, and due to the location of the hotel, it was quiet at night. I believe this is the first time I have stayed in a Manhattan hotel in which I could not hear the traffic below. 
The hotel provides free wifi in the room, which was useful for making reservations and getting directions. 
Breakfast:
This hotel offers a complimentary breakfast. It is not a huge buffet, but again, I thought it was appropriate for a budget hotel. There were juices, yogurt, whole fruit (banana, apples, and oranges), boiled eggs, bread, English muffin, batter for making waffles, coffee, instant oatmeal, cooked sausage, and some sort of frittata. Of the three nights I stayed there, the breakfast area was only overly crowded in one of the days – the space is tiny, but again it was not a surprise to us. For this reason, we just grabbed some bananas and yogurt and went on our merry way. 
Location:
For folks who are not familiar with NYC, the location may look a little scary and out of the way, but it was only about two blocks from the nearest metro entrance at 8th and 35st. The hotel location is also an easy walk to Times Square and the Theater District. We even walked all the way to 62th street to catch a movie at the Lincoln Plaza Cinemas. The hotel is also within walking distance to Penn Station, Madison Square Garden, and several of the interstate bus stops (Bolt, Megabus, etc…).
Returning to the hotel at night was not a problem, but as in any large city, you need to be alert and aware of your surroundings. 
Overall, I think this is a good hotel if you want to stay in Manhattan, have your own bathroom and you are budget conscious and street savvy. If you need luxury accommodations, large rooms, and to be in the middle of Times Square, you should prepare your pockets and look somewhere else. I certainly plan to stay in this hotel again: It is a clean and quiet place to rest your head in the city that never sleeps.

title: “excellent location, but seriously($50/night parking)”
text: The Parc 55 is in an excellent location, literally across the street from the metro with shopping and dining in any direction. We watched Cirque du Soleil - Totem at AT&T Park and walked back to the hotel which was probably a 15-20 minute walk. We booked online at hotwire and when we checked in I asked for an upgraded room - for $40/night we got a 29th floor city view room with access to the Club Lounge on the 31st floor. Free continental breakfast, drinks, amazing views...worth the extra few bucks a night. So with taxes, internet, parking and the upgrade...what we paid on hotwire was cheaper than the costs we were charged at checkout. Worth it...for sure, but be aware that you pay for parking($48/night) and internet($15/night). All in all, we were very impressed with the Parc 55.

title: “Valencia Time”
text:
I've been a regular visitor to the Valencia over the last several years while traveling on business. I'm not a huge fan of the Santana Row area however compared to the rest of San Jose, at least there is something to do and a few restaurant choices. 
With respect to the Valencia itself, the hotel decor is modern but dark (dark woods, dim lights, dark carpets). Generally speaking the hotel is obviously high traffic and shows some wear but is well maintained. Lighting in the rooms is dim but work areas and bedside lamps have bright enough lights to read/work by. Standard rooms are relatively spacious. If you are unlucky and get a lower floor room in the wrong place, it can get a bit noisy on Thursday and Friday nights. Generally speaking though, this is just a bit of bad luck. 
Hotel staff are helpful and courteous. As a regular visitor, they generally remember me by name which is a nice touch. Breakfast is excellent with a modest amount of variety. The coffee is good but not great. An extremely nice touch is having good newspapers (New York Times, Wall Street Journal) available every day. 
I basically have two things about the hotel that bug me. One is the lighting in the restaurant. It's so dim that it is impossible to read in there unless you get one of the two or three tables which have a light fixture directly over them. There is no reason to have crappy lighting at breakfast. The second is parking. Unless you valet, you're basically on your own to find parking in one of the three Santana Row parking areas. That starts getting sketchy on Wednesday night and can be impossible on Thursday/Friday nights. 
Complaints aside, the Valencia is always my first choice when I go to San Jose.

title: “Great location and even better staff”
text: We just got back from a West Coast trip which ended with 5 nights in San Diego. We wanted a nice hotel in a good location with a pool where we could relax at the end of a busy trip and this ticked all the boxes. The room was amazing, nice decor and very comfy bed and the staff really made it. Great advice, helpful directions and a genuine customer focus yet informal and welcoming. The pool area is very nice and great for a city hotel but the location is perfect - right in downtown and easy walking to the marina area and loads of restaurants. The evening free wine service between 5 and 6 is a nice touch as is the comp coffee and tea in the mornings. I would stay here again and has also made me think that I would try another Kimpton hotel when travelling in the US. Highly recommend.

title: “Rosei-Concierge”
text: I have stayed at this Hilton for several months. One of the highlights is the concierge lounge. They have a good breakfast in the morning and an exceptional appetizers in the evening. The staff, especially Rosei who is there in the evening, are very friendly and helpful. She is quick to warmly greet you after a long day at work, very willing to help you with refreshments and make sure you have cookies for a late night snack. Being a road warrior, it always nice, but far too rare, to find hotel staff who make you feel like you are home and welcomed.

title: “Had the best time! Am now friends with the staff. Excellent!”
text:
Located in the fairly quiet neighbourhood, Queen Anne, this hotel became my proper home from home in the first week of my first ever visit to the states.
After bansihing the hideously ugly bed spreads to the closet as soon as I arrived, I settled in, but never had I expected to get so comfy in this place!
Clean, good shower, dated decor & vcr system (though tapes are availble to watch & my English dvds wouldn't work there anyway).
Having a kitchenette in the room is a HUGE help as a gluten/dairy/meat free traveller, and having a Safeway across the road means food is always readily available and reasonable. There is also a cinema across the road, & the hotel is situated one block from key arena which hosts music events and basketball... 
There are 2 computers for quick use in the lobby, (you have to stand to use them) but there is also a 'Business Center' (not exclusive for business customers use) where you can sit for longer periods. A small exercise room stores the stacks of leaflets on things to see & do-if you want ideas (I discovered these on my last day!) but you shouldn't need them as Seattle is such a great city & there is plenty going on if you just walk into town & look around.
The centre of town *is* a bus ride away, (fares $1.75 tickets valid for 2 hours) but you can always use the monorail for two bucks more (return) & this gives you reason to walk into the wonderful Seattle Centre each day, host of the Experience Music Project, The Fountain Dome, & of course the Space Needle-(aswell as many other delights!) 
I was particularly keen on checking out live music while I was in town, and the reception staff were sooo helpful, looking things up for me while I ran errands or was out sight seeing, we have kept in touch!
I would definately stay here again, it's just the right amount of home you need, and an excellent, safe base to explore this wonderful city. 
One more thing-Fabulous view on the roof top terrace. See the sea at sunset & the city skyline by sun rise. Amazing.

title: “Perfect. Again.”
text:
I stayed in the Kitano for the second time from February 3-8 and just couldn't fault it. The previous time, last September, I really liked it, but like one of your previous reviewers, felt it was a little dull and rough around the edges. However, I too appreciated the quality of the furnishings on closer inspection and realised the "dullness" was probably better described as the Japanese way of not intruding. 
Before I went, I spent countless hours cross-checking reviews on tripadvisor and other sites to get a real feel for some of the hotels I was considering staying in for a change and there was a recurring theme of bad service, technology not performing, noisy, shabby and small rooms (even in the 5 stars) and I didn't want to be disappointed by making the wrong choice. With the Kitano, I didn't.
I was welcomed like an old friend and felt completely at home. The bar is a more popular place than I had thought, particularly for business people and the jazz sessions are a great addition. I had received a response from the General Manager to my comment form from the previous visit, and this time, the robes and towels were brand new and sumptious.
It's not to everyone's taste: it's not cool and trendy, it doesn't have plasma screens, free high speed internet access, cookies at bedtime and heavenly beds, but it does ooze discreet quality, has fresh sheets and turndown service every day, is spotless and has a good minibar. You won't hear a sound in the large, reasonably-priced rooms and you will probably get a view of either the Empire State Building or the Chrysler Building, just a few (very safe) blocks away. 
I can't compliment this hotel enough and will automatically book in again in another few weeks. They also thank you for staying with them and mean it; nice to know you're appreciated, isn't it?

title: “great value”
text: My boyfriend and I went to NYC on January 8th 2004 for my birthday and we stayed at the Quality Hotel. The staff was quiet, but helpful, the interior when we walked in was very nice and clean. the elevator is very very small. the hallways are also pretty tight, so if you have large bags you may have to make a trip sideways to your room. when we entered our room we were very pleased and surprised. the bed was perfectly made, the sheets were clean, the coffee maker was set up with a pack of coffee on top for us. the bathroom was clean (but towels weren't big enough to dry off with) and bring conditioner because there wasn't any in my room. the bed was comfortable and big. our room was a good size. the television was hidden away in a very nice wooden dresser/entertainment center. .good sized tv, good reception. we also had a desk that was nice and a chair (the chair was comfortable but dusty) we had a refrigerator and an alarm clock, and also an iron, ironing board and a hairdryer. we were very pleased with our stay, and we only paid $71.95 for the night (thurs-fri) not including tax and fees. when we got to the counter to check out, the woman asked us if we had used the safe in our room and we said no... so she didn't charge us the daily fee. we had a wonderful time in new york and at the quality hotel and we will go there again... P.S. my room # was 907, so if you want a safe room (size-wise) and with refrigerator(free) ask for that room. great value.

title: “Location Bargain”
text: Terrific central walking distance location. Excellent windows - I think any view is buildings. Atypical of many NY hotels - larger walkin shower bathroom. I was happy with my high floor, next to the elevator noiseless king. This property exceeded my expectation. It is an absolute first consideration for my next visit.

title: “You will feel like family!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for three nights and had the best time. I have never met a nicer hotel staff. Everyone was wonderful and I did not get all the names. However, I did learn Shane's and Orlando's they were very helpful and kind to us. We had some very busy days in NYC and it was so nice to come back to the hotel and relax. We even spent about an hour one afternoon hanging out in the lobby talking to the staff. The room was spacious and very clean. We ran into the cleaning staff one morning and they were very friendly and smiling. You will have a wonderful stay!

title: “Unable to communicate with this hotel by email!”
text:
I find it quite amazing that it is not possible to communicate with this hotel by email, concerning a forthcoming stay!
When I asked Marriott Customer Care for the email address of Nick Welker, Director of Operations at JW Marriott Denver Cherry Creek I was told "The JW Marriott Denver Cherry Creek hotel does not currently have a publicly listed email address and we are not permitted to provide guests with employee's e-mail addresses".
Not very customer friendly!

title: “Excellent Customer Service From Staff”
text: This is our third time staying at the Grand Hyatt and my first time rating this hotel. My wife and I arrived around 3:00p.m. on Thanksgiving Day. Front desk staff were busy checking in guest as expected, one of the staff members led us to the kiosk to check in and was very helpful, and in no time we were checked in! The other thing I would like to add is that we had made reservations around 3 weeks prior for 99 per night. Two nights before leaving we had seen they had rooms for 69 per night. So we called to see if we could get this rate, without hesitation, they gave us that rate. As we were leaving to go shopping, it was raining, the staff member at the front told us about the umbrellas they furnish to guest,so we went to the front desk and assigned one to our rm. to use during our stay, FOR FREE!! The only downside is parking. We always park across the street and pay 9.per day(no in or out on the same day). But this will not stop us from coming back again and again. The rooms are clean, roomy, and comfortable. THANK YOU GH staff and cleaning staff.

title: “Top notch.”
text:
My second stay at the Palomar could not have been better. Upon arrival we were at the door with treats for my dog and hospitality from all at the front desk. Our room located at the corner of the top floor had a great view towards the Mall. The swimming pool was a nice diversion for my daughter. They even had a lifeguard on duty--and perhaps more important to her MANY water toys to chose from. After catching a great Nationals game we returned to the hotel in the evening and the vibe was definitely European with guests of all cultures and languages visiting outside and in the lobby with some fun music playing in the background.
Super comfy beds and great amenities-I won't hesitate to stay here again!

title: “Very Enjoyable Stay”
text: Comfortable, soothing, quiet, friendly & conveniently a minute's walk from Times Square.

title: “I wouldn't stay here again!”
text:
The best way to describe this hotel is, you can dress up a 90 year old woman with make-up and new clothes, and try to make her look 30, but she still is a 90 year old woman! 
The hotel has been renovated, but the rooms still are outdated by their layout. You have to close the bathroom door in order to use the restroom, and the toliet paper holder is right in your lap.
The rooms are very noisy as you can hear everything in everyone elses room.
I have stayed at many Courtyards and this one ranks among the worst!

title: “location is all about it”
text:
stayed for 7 nights on the 6 floor in a room facing the 56th street.i asked for a room away from the elevator,just to avoid the noise,but i couldn't avoid the street noise .when i asked the receptionist diane,she said in a unfriendly way that has no rooms available:"maybe later".the other receptionist sent me to talk to the manager ,like this was a really great deal of business to talk about and nobody else could solve it.
so,i've had 7 sleepless nights.the connecting door gave me the chance to hear at every 4 am ,that week,the moaning of my neighbours.all the time the flushing toillets could be heard as well from the other rooms.
 the room was old ,not very well appointed ,and in need for deep cleaning.
the washing sink was outside the bathroom and the closet was opposite to it.not much space for storage and the closet's door would get stuck most of the time.
no fridge in the room or minibar.
if you need to do yourself the laundry you find a convenient laudromat on the 9th avenue between the 52nd and 51st street,wich is more convenient than sending the laundry with in the hotel.
around are hundreds of restaurants which serve breakfast,brunch,lunch and dinner,plus a lot of take aways
the only things i liked about this property were the location,the bartender ben and the housekeepers.i would like to go back to this place if i have the assurance that i get a room facing the court,not the streets which, i guess, would be quieter

title: “Location! Location! Location!”
text: My daughters and I came to the Edison on the recommendation of a friend. We couldn't believe the location as we were dropped off at the door. We were a little early for check-in but the front desk was able to find a room for us. This was just the start of the welcoming atmosphere that we found at the Edison. All of the staff that we dealt with, from the front desk to the concierge to the wait staff in the adjoining restaurant were very friendly and helpful. It is an older hotel but the rooms are clean and the beds are comfortable. Times Square is practically outside the front door and we found we were able to walk to many of the sites we wished to see. I have raved about this "find" to one and all and would definitely come here again.

title: “A Oasis in New York”
text: We stayed here recently at the end of our trip to the USA. The hotel has a great location just a short walk from Times Square, The Rockefeller Centre and 5th Avenue. The rooms were smallish but this is to be expected in NYC. Having said that the rooms were very comfortable and clean. the hotel is an older building and so this gave it more character and the staff could not do enogh to help us in our stay. They really made us feel that we were in a home away from home

title: “My Favorite NYC Hotel Hands Down”
text: This hotel delivers were other 5 Star NYC hotels fall flat. Great in every way. Clean and fresh rooms, amazing location, great Central Park views (Central Park View rooms only), 5 Star service at every turn. I love this hotel. Unlike The Four Seasons Central Park (57th St), this is a true 5 Star experience. You cannot go wrong here!

title: “A very pleasent experience>”
text: I found the staff friendly and personable. The hotel has a "Crabby Hour" hosted by a very polite and friendly hostess(unfortunately her name escapes me) where different crab concoctions are prepared for you to sample accompanied by microbrewery beer and regional wines. Accomodations outstanding and great food. This hotel is a jem tucked along the Inner Harbor. I enjoyed this venue far greater than the larger chain hotels in the area. The food is great on the premises. You are within easy walking distance of Little Italy with its restaurants. The rooms are well appointed and I slept well. The only criticism is that the television picture was a bit distorted. I will visit here again.

title: “Great Find”
text: Stayed here for a short weekend trip to the City. Room was clean and comfortable. The room was small, but that is typical for NYC. Lowest price I could find for staying in the City. Staff was exceptional. Very Friendly - Check in was a breeze. Would definately stay here again.

title: “Noisy hotel, great breakfast in lounge”
text:
We had made a reservation for a Tower room with access to the lounge, with complimentary breakfast and afternoon drinks.
At first; the room seemed amazing. But at 6.30 AM we suddenly woke up because it sounded like a train passed outside our window. At 48. floor... We knew about some construction work at street level, but really didn't think it would bother us. We demanded to change room, and got a new one at the same floor, this time facing the cathedral. Much better view, much more quiet, but half the size. I would guess this was a cheaper room, but we were not offered any discount.
The drinks at the Palace Gate (the courtyard bar) were over-prized; 16$ for a glass of wine! But overall; we have a good impression of the hotel, and really recommend getting access to the Tower Lounge; where breakfast, light lunch and afternoon drinks are complimentary.

title: “Great Location and Staff”
text: This hotel has probably seen some better days, however, it was clean. It was very busy in the breakfast room so there was lots of food, but not enough seats. They did have trays so that made it a little better. My husband was there for business so I just tagged along. The staff was just wonderful. Everyone I came in contact with was very friendly and always spoke. It was very refreshing since I spent most of the day in the hotel.

title: “Wow, what a great experiance.”
text:
We stayed at this hotel the night before our cruise on the Princess Sapphire, over Valentines weekend.
We have traveled all over the worl and I have to say that this Inn and the stay & cruise package was the best deal in southern California.
The sushi bar in the parking lot was a huge bonus, and then front door srvice to the cruise ship was fantastic.

title: “Great stay - meeting went perfectly”
text:
Just stayed here the other day & had a meeting at the LAX Marriott. I read some of the other reviews & some people said this hotel had a rude staff. I felt completely the opposite. I had a great check-in experience at the front desk. I had a concierge level room and had a good experience in the concierge lounge with the staff there. I asked for some area restaurant recommendations & we ended up at a decent on the water restaurant (Tony P's). I was there for a company event at the hotel - our organization used the whole ballroom area downstairs and as far as I could tell, the whole thing went extremely well without a hitch - the event team did an excellent job. Catering was great - lunch was good & the break drink/snack service was well executed.
I had a great room - I don't stay in full-service hotels often - mostly Courtyards, so I'm more used to the Courtyard bed - I slept fairly well - had to take some pillows off the bed (I think there were 7 pillows on my bed). 
Shuttle service is free to/from airport & shared with the Renassiance...I think I waited about 2 minutes for the shuttle, so that was quite efficient.
Pool area seemed nice - wish I had the time to use it as last time I was in LA it was freezing cold! 
There was a business center & free wireless in the lobby.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
Was very disappointed by my stay at Home2. The location is good, but that's the only positive point about this hotel. 
When I checked in (Friday evening) nobody at the reception. Only a "back in five" sign. Which hotel worth that price is not able to have at least 2 employees for the weekend rush ?
The room and the premise were clean except the windows which seemed to have never been cleaned outside. The room itself was very noisy because of the fan in the WC that you couldn't turn off. Normal street noise for a city centre hotel, but some improvement could be done on the windows. 
The breakfast was just a joke. Nothing fresh, no eggs, just some kind of mini pizza (tasteless and calorifull). The so-called pool is twice the size of a bathtub. 
I won't recommend this hotel to anybody. For that price you can find a real hotel nearby.

title: “Very Nice.......Mini Vacation”
text: This was a quick trip to Seattle and we needed a hotel close to the action but not too close. We were in town for a show at the 5th Avenue Theater. The Vintage Hotel was perfect! Awesome greeting at the front door, front desk right on the spot!! We arrived at the wine reception, we declined because I don't drink. Just as we were settling into our room chocolates and sparkling water on a lovely tray showed up. Now that is class!!!! We were traveling with our small dog Cody Coyote and he was most appreciated with a welcome package as well. We will definitely stay here the future for sure. The restaurant down stairs is also top notch and accommodated dietary needs superbly. Fun and restful stay. Did I mention St Patrick's day? Everywhere else it was noisy but not here, we slept like babies.

title: “Best Belated Christmas Present!!!”
text: I brought my nephew (11 years old) and his younger brother (6 years old) who is also my Godchild to New York last weekend as their belated Christmas present. WOW, did we have a great time! They are already planning their next trip to NYC. The hotel was great - from the spacious well-appointed lobby to the restaurant like feel of the breakfast cafe to the more than ample room space. And the staff was SUPERB!!! Mary, the concierge couldn't have been nicer - she deserves a gold star for her upbeat, professional, personality as well as her knowledge. Christian, another concierge deserves many kudos as well. Another name worth mentioning is Samuel, the bellhop, he couldn't have been nice nor more accomodating! And the boys highlight of the Hampton Inn was the 24/7 hot chocolate! I never saw them drink so much hot chocolate in their lives. We definitely will all be back very, very, soon!!!

title: “Excellent value!”
text:
I brought my15 year old niece to NYC for a girls' weekend. Fashion 26 served our purposes perfectly! The room was comfortable; not large, but very clean, a quite comfortable bed, and an excellent view from the 19th floor. The front desk staff was very welcoming, and the concierges were friendly and helpful.
I'll bring my husband here next time for gallery-hopping in Chelsea!

title: “A must stay if you are in downtown Detroit!”
text: We stayed here in July 2011 for a wedding and were astounded with the modern style and overall cleanliness of the Westin Book Cadillac Detroit. Short walk from Comerica Park, Joe Loius and Hart Plaza. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “What's not to love”
text: We stay here every year in December...on the evening of our company Christmas party. Room is lovely and very comfortable. Whiskey & Rye hosted our pre-party festivities. Drinks were fantastic and service was superb.
