title: “Unique”
text: Very innovative redesign of former jail - enough of the prior jail remains to get a true feel for the central cell block. Clearly one of the pricey Boston Hotels but seems to be worth it. Would rate staff a full 10 of 10. Lobby scene later night is worth watching although unclear how long the current "It Place" will remain so. Somewhat concerned that the rocking lobby bar would impact ability to sleep but there was zero transmitted noise. Similar concern about arriving ambulances at Mass General but once again not an issue. Our room was not one of the rooms with a view but it was comfortable and nice. Location is excellent as it sits at the base of Charles Street - the trendy uphill walk up to Beacon Hill. Also easy walk to North End, Boston Garden and Fan. Hall area.

title: “Redroom bar... awesome... !!!”
text:
Have stayed at Clift for the weekend with my friend, two girls (27-28 y.o) coming for a short weekend in SFO and looking for a luxury ( but not boring) hotel with a good location to explore the city and some entertainment later in the evening in the hotel bar... We could not have found a better place! Were totally satisfied. I must say we did not even want to go anywhere else and spent most of the evenings there... Thanks to the Redroom... Clift is known for its very welldesigned lobby and the Redroom. A stunning, elegant lounge with beautiful digital paintings, an enormous, luminous bar, and intricate, chic redwood paneling and a nice crowd.... The Redwood Room is one of the most luxurious night spots in San Francisco. Get quite crowded in the evening. Great place, nice crowd, we loved it ! 
Have been checking other hotels for a drink / dinner while staying in SFO and were very happy that Clift was the choise... See many people are saying the staff was rude, was not the case with us. Everybody was friendly and very helpful... To put it short if you are single and looking for the hotel with the nice bar to hang out in the evening ( together with the good locations, service etc ), this is the place. I would not dare to recommend it though for the families with the kids. Depends on what you are looking for. We were extemely happy and satisfied... And have a had a great weekend. Thank you, CLIFT ! ;-)

title: “nice time”
text:
Nice hotel in Queen Anne close to Seattle Center (Space Needle, EMP, Monorail, Key Arena). The rooms are clean and comfortable with kitchenettes. There is NO A/C - do not be surprised by this! We went in late July and were fine with the ceiling fan and window, but if you must have a/c, don't book here! There is a cool rooftop deck with good views of the city and the water. The staff was friendly and helpful at all times.
I have to disagree with those who say the hotel is on a "very busy street". I just didn't see that. It is a one-way main road, but we did not see a high volume of cars nor people in this area at all. I thought it was a nice area and there are several restaurants you can walk to.
We had a lovely time here - I recommend it!

title: “Very good for the price...”
text: This hotel was probably at its peak in the 80s. The elevators were slow and the rooms along with the lobby need to be updated. It is within walking distance to pretty much every attraction in the area. Front desk was pleasant, parking garage was about 3 blocks away, room service was good. I found a great deal on the internet and if I found another one I would gladly return.

title: “Excellent Hampton Inn”
text: Excellent, very well managed nice clean hotel with helpful staff. All the little extra's like a personal letter from the manager and a note with places of interest etc. Reasonable breakfast most things available and Chili's next door for dinner what more could you want. Well done.

title: “Wonderful old hotel, but could use more diligent cleaning crew”
text:
The Algonquin takes you back to what New York used to be before all the mega-hotels came to town. It's a small - around 150 rooms - luxury hotel, rich in history, and we were absolutely charmed. The public rooms are open to the lobby (not closed off) but still clubby in feel - comfortable, intimate - and of course the restaurant features the famous round table where various literary lights gathered decades ago. The food was pricey, but excellent. The included continental breakfast was both generous and tasty. Great service all around.
Our room was small (to be expected) but comfortable and well-appointed. The bathroom, which had no tub, was just a step above a cubby. That wasn't really a problem. What was disappointing was that it was poorly cleaned. We arrived late on our first of two nights and so didn't notice until the next morning. Then because we had only one more night there and weren't spending much time in our room anyhow, we decided not to make an issue of it.
I would still definitely recommend this hotel. I feel sure that with the kind of service they offered, if we'd complained, they would have responded promptly. Do shop around for rates. We got a great deal through Expedia.
Business travelers, be aware that their Business Center consists of one computer and one printer that's poorly maintained. You can connect to the internet from your room though.

title: “Escape from reality”
text: Once again we had a wonderful relaxing visit. One can always find a quite nook at the resort to relax, have a drink or enjoy a fire in one of their many outdoor fireplaces. They are consistent in their high standards of maintenance of the resort and the attention to detail they provide their guests. I wouldn't change a thing. The spa is an oasis for the senses.

title: “We got more attention from the hooker outside our room than the front desk.”
text:
Seriously, we pick Holiday Inn and the Intercontinental brand for quality and reliability. Sure, in New York City you are going to expect some diversity and crowds; however, nothing could have prepared us for the experience at this hotel. First, there were several "interesting" guests (which we later learned were hookers who ran their business out of their rooms). Second, not one but two large school groups (of teenage girls). This meant loud running in the hallways and hallway congregating until all hours. Then, the first and second categories mixed together leading to loud shouting and much drama (which woke us up two evenings in a row). 
The first comment relating to the hooker created a problem repeatedly during or staff from the very loud woman (and her roommate) as well as the men who visited her.
The front desk NEVER answered their phone. We had to walk to the front desk to ask them to quiet down the hallway (no security to intervene). The second night the phone was broken.
Cleanliness was very good and the room was attractive (this is what we expect from IHG and a Holiday Inn).
Would not recommend this hotel. They are under staffed and could not promise a good night sleep.

title: “Mr/mrs m notts.Paramount is fine by us.”
text: Just got back from a stay at the paramount times square(2nd sept/9th 20/11)the hotel is fine as long as you upgrade to at least a queen room.We were put on the third floor it was noisy from the air conditioning we asked for another room and the next day were moved up to the 18th floor,the hotel staff were fantastic there was nothing they wouldnt do for you.The location is second to none turn left out of the hotel and within 1minute you are in times square,turn right cross 2 roads and your in the hells kitchen district where you can eat from nearly every cuisine under the sun even ethiopian,and its a good deal cheaper than times square.We would certainly stop here again.But please remember dont book 1 of the smallest rooms.

title: “All good except lounge/Bar 10 service”
text: Spent 29JUN-03JUL in NYC at Westin, doormen, front desk, housekeeping were all really great. Lounge service at Bar 10 was TERRIBLE! Brutally slow service.

title: “Where was our complimentary upgrade?”
text:
I see in the previous review that those people were given a complimentary upgrade to a suite. When we checked in, we were offered to be upgraded to a slightly larger room for an additional $150 per night although it was clear that the hotel was very empty the days we were there. I am now curious as to why some people are offered a complimentary upgrade and some people are asked to pay for an upgrade. Nevertheless, we did not want to pay even more than we were paying, so we declined. 
The room was nice. It was on a high floor facing away from Market street, which I suppose is quieter, but not completely quiet as you can still hear sirens, for example. We could also hear our neighbors through the connecting door. Luckily there were not many people on our floor and it was very quiet floor. We never saw any housekeeping staff at all. That is a nice feature. Many times we have stayed at hotels and the housekeeping staff is always in the hallways. 
The breakfast was at the hotel was pretty good. That is the only meal we ate there. 
The gym is a huge two story facility with about every piece of equipment you can imagine, but it is a local gym which services the hotel. So while it has everything you need, it also has a large clientele working out there. It's nice that it has a pool, but at the same time, I had to wait for a lane to open up. We had massages, which were average, nothing special. 
The staff are all very helpful. The only problem was upon leaving the hotel, the hotel's printed instructions to the airport sent us through construction work in the neighborhood and it took us 20 minutes to leave the immediate neighborhood. I think the staff should have known that this was going on and redirected us to a less congested route (which there was).

title: “Expected Better”
text:
I just got back from a four night stay at the Renaissance Chicago Hotel. Before my trip I read all the reviews and was excited to stay here, but after my trip I don't know if I would necessarily stay here again. 
The room: The room in general was really nice. It was spacious, well appointed, and very clean. We had a view of the construction site next door, but that was expected since we are associates of the company. The bathroom was great. It was nicely decorated and a decent size. What we didn't like however was the temperature in the room. The room was at a constant 74 degrees all four nights of our stay. On the second night we called the engineer to come take a look at it. He told us that the hotel was having problems with the heating/cooling system and that unfortunately there was nothing he could do. He offered to comp us a movie, however that did not make up for the fact that it was ridiculously hot. His only suggestion was to open the windows, which we did, but being in downtown Chicago all we heard all night long were sirens, car horns, and the sound of the train. Needless to say we were unable to sleep well at all. 
The pool: I was hoping for something nicer. The atmosphere was very tranquil and sirene which was relaxing however the temperature of the pool and hot tub were not regulated properly. The pool was pretty cold each night we were there, and down right freezing our last night (mind you this is supposed to be a heated indoor pool) and the hot tub was so hot it burned your skin. Now, I understand that it is supposed to be hot, but this was definitely hotter than the regulation 104 degrees. The pool water was pretty murky and the one day it wasn't you could see obvious dirt on the bottom. Also the pool closes at 11pm which is kind of disappointing. 
Guest Services: The staff of the hotel was under par in my opinion. We had a very nice gentleman check us in and give us some details about the area, however he did not explain any of the amenites of the hotel. Is there a business center? Which floor is the pool on? Where is the restaurant located? These are little things but it should be explained at check in. The concierge is helpful if you go downstairs to speak with them directly; don't try to call them from your room because the phone will ring 50 times and when they do pick up the will say "all lines are busy can we call you back?" At check out we ran into a few problems. The desk clerk never bothered to ask us how our stay was, to which we would have told him we didn't get any sleep, but I guess he's not too worried about that. He did find it difficult however to charge two separate credit cards. I wanted the room and tax on one card and the incidentals on another. He was unsure of how to do this, which was fine, and asked another associate for help. She helped him out and said everything was all set. When I finally got home I noticed that the clerk charged the same card for both charges so I called up the hotel and asked them to fix it. The woman at the front desk said she took care of it, however now the other card was charged both charges. Honestly, it is not that hard to split the charges between two credit cards, and I won't call back to have it fixed a third time but its not worth it. 
The restaurant: The restaurant food was great. I loved my fish entree. However our server was a little off. He poured my boyfriends beer, foam over flowing, and just walked away from our table!! Left the soppy mess right there and didn't look back. 
Overall our stay was ok, however I think I'd chose another hotel if I'm ever in Chcicago again.

title: “Nice hotel.. but can be loud on the 4th floor”
text: I recently (10/6/12) stayed at the Fairmont because I was running in the San Jose Rock N Roll Half Marathon Series the following day... with that said.. I really needed to have some rest that evening. At around 10PM I could hear a live band playing in one of the ballrooms (2 floors below). I figured it was from a wedding or some event and that it would end around midnight.. finally at 3AM I called the front desk to see where this noise was coming from and why it was going on so late. They apologized and said it was from a wedding and it should have ended a half hour ago.. REALLY.. for something that loud to travel 2 floors up and still go on until 2:30AM is crazy!!! I know I wasn't the only person on the 4th floor that could hear this.. we even walked out into the hallway to try to follow the sound. The stay would have been excellent if I wasn't up all night with this loud noise. I really enjoyed having a room with a patio and a private entrance and exit to the pool. I liked the location of the Hotel, there is a lot of things to do in walking distance, but if need rest and it's a weekend, you might want to request a room on a higher floor because if there is any event taking place in the ballrooms, you will hear the noise!!!

title: “Couldn't even stay here for a night. This place is terrible.”
text:
My mother booked this hotel for their first time visit here in the US. The only room available for 4 people is a smoking room which cost $140+/night. We really didn't care if it was smoking or non-smoking since a room is a room, as long as it's clean then it should be ok, right? We we're very much mistaken, the moment we entered the room I almost wanted to vomit because of the stench of the place. Not to brag, but I do quite a bit of travelling myself, and I know what a decent hotel room looks like, this place is just absolutely ghastly. So I got on my computer and I immediately checked out the nearby hotels thru hotwire, thank God I found a room at Westin with 2 beds for 4 people that costs $89/night. Can you believe it? So we called the frontdesk and asked the lady to just cancel our reservation. When asked why, I politely told her that the place simply wasn't right and I found a different hotel to stay for the night. She was rude and nagged about how we we're spending money at their hotel and we wouldn't even use it. I was just thinking in my head that THIS PLACE IS SO BAD THAT I WAS WILLING TO PAY HER GOOD MONEY JUST TO GET US OUT OF THERE.
Save yourself a headache and a few bucks, get a room from one of those hotel booking sites and get a deal unlike this one. This place is simply terrible.

title: “An Excellent Hotel”
text: Stayed for the first time at a hotel close to Logan airport, normally stay downtown in Boston, and could not have picked a better hotel. From the moment we checked in with the very friendly and helpful staff you knew it was going to be a pleasure to stay here. The reception that opens up onto the bar & restuarant area sets the tone, very clean & spacious, its modern design is friendly to the eye. The suites themselves are again spacious featuring 1 bedroom with two double beds & television, they also have a lounge that has a small kitchen area & a sofa that opens up into a double bed & television with nintendo for the kids (extra charge). Although more expensive to stay that the hotels i previously had stayed at in Boston (5th time) ie Copley Square, Midtown, etc, this has to go down as the best in standard & value for money!! Plus within the price is a complimentary Breakfast (excellent choices available) & on some evenings a complimentary managers buffet. My only complaint and it is a small one was the size of the indoor pool, more like a large bath!! but there was a nice sized gym there. And one last thing to consider is that both Hertz & Dollar car rental premises are only 2 minutes away on foot, What more could you want. Overall an excellent hotel!!!!

title: “OK for a quick night.”
text: Selected this hotel as was arriving at IAH late one night and departing from IAH the next morning. I selected this hotel based on a number of Tripadvisor reviews. The complimentary shuttle was nice, the checkin staff were friendly, but maybe I just received a poor room, 324. The A/C didn't seem to work well, maybe a thermostat problem. But I was very disappointed and disgusted with the amount of dirt buildup on the a/c unit. For the money it was OK, but not enough to recommend or book again without looking elsewhere.

title: “How did I not stay here before?”
text: We were in town for the GABF and I was thrilled my husband had booked this adorable, classy boutique hotel not even three blocks away from the Convention Center. The location is great , nearby all the fun shopping, theaters and convention center. We had numerous adventurous "rickshaw" rides around town to different events. The entire hotel s comfortable and classy. The staff was so friendly and helpful organizing a rental car for me and having the hotel Suburban take me to the care rental after tracking me down at Starbucks. I hope we stay here on our next trip to Denver

title: “Nightmare, beware!!!!!”
text: I have just arrived home after spending 6 days here. The city itself was fantastic but as for the hotel, well it should be closed down. As the other reviews state the moment we arrived at the front desk the staff were unfriendly and rude, which was just the start. Once given our room, it was an utter disgrace it hadn't been cleaned from the people who were in there before us, with old sheets on the bed and dirty towels on the bathroom floor. Went straight down to complain, here the staff didn't seem at all surprised, they obviously have got use to it. I would never ever go back here you would have to pay me to stay there again, even then I would still not go. Maybe the management of this hotel (if there is any!) should read through these reviews maybe then something will be done, and maybe health and safety, and the environmental agency should be advised on the state of this place!!!!!

title: “Not a 4 star property as indicated on Expedia! Maybe 3 star?”
text:
Stayed here 6/18/12 for one night with my wife and two kids in a standard room. This was one of those special last minute Expedia deals where all you know is the general location and star rating. 4 star for $68 seemed like a good deal. When you first walk up to the property, the carpet is worn and threadbare and the brass/gold fitting and hardware on the doors are tarnished and dented. So I was bracing myself. Check-in went OK and the lobby is quite large and impressive, though quite dimly lit (to hide wear?). My first hint of possible trouble was that only rooms with King or (2) double beds were available. From my limited experience, it's a bad sign when there are no rooms with (2) queen beds in that the hotel has possibly not been renovated in decades. 
Went to our (2) double bed room and it was clean and appeared to be refurbished, although oddly enough the door hardware and toilet seat (see pics) had appeared to be "original equipment" from the 60's or 70's. Worst thing about the room were the beds. At first I was pleased that there was a mattress topper, but then later that night it became evident why. I could not find a comfortable position to sleep in; I could feel the bed springs in the mattress whichever way I turned! I can only imagine what it would be like without the topper. 
At best I would assign a 3 star rating to this property, but the beds were horrible. If it weren't for the lousy beds and the nasty toilet seat, I probably wouldn't have written this review. Due to the very poor bedding, I don't think it was worth $68 to lose a night's sleep. Maybe the king beds are better? Location is good with plenty of eateries only a 1/4 mile away and the pool area is nice. I though a 2 rating would be a little harsh, so I gave it a 3.

title: “Sofitel our favorite in Philadelphia”
text: We have traveled often to Philadelphia over the past four years and the Sofitel was always our first choice. Unfortunately the price on busy weekends would sometimes force us to look elsewhere, but whenever possible we chose the Sofitel.

title: “Ideal location for Pier 39 and Fishermans Wharf”
text:
We stayed 3 nights. The hotel is ideally located for Fisherman's Wharf and Piers 39. It is 2 blocks to walk to the waterfront. It is only 1 block's walk to get on the city tour bus. The concierge was very knowledgable and helpful. Little Italy and Chinatown are also within walking distance. The rooms are nice and clean and we found it very comfortable. We had breakfast in the hotel and also ordered room service for dinner one night. The food is very good. 
I wouldn't suggest bring a car with you. You don't need one in San Francisco anyway and the hotel charges $36 a night for car parking due to the limited number of spaces available.

title: “very good value for money”
text:
This hotel is very good value for money and the staff are helpful. The only slight problem was a noisy party next door one night , but the desk staff attended to this when I complained and there was no further problem. The rooms are a reasonable size, I had a view of Coit Tower, and the location is excellent. 
The breakfast area gets a bit crowded at the weekend but that is a small price to pay. I would go there again.

title: “Great value option upper west side”
text: Hotel was excellent option for exploring NY and visiting friends. Room was small but quiet and well-appointed with contemporary design. Bathroom small but very nice with marble, stone and steel finishings. Upstairs terrace over city offered great views and was a quiet place for breakfast (no restaurant but market across the street was great) or visiting with friends. All staff from doormen to front desk and cleaning personnel very friendly and accommodating. They clearly care about guest satisfaction both when you are there and as you can see by their responsiveness to comments here in Tripadvisor (which I read before booking). I would definitely return with my family. If available, request rooms with balconies, they look great.

title: “Great location, but expected more”
text: Booked their suite special 2 nights $450 (1/2 price second night). Although I am aware check-in is at 3pm, my son and I arrived at 10:30am. They told me to check back soon for an available room. I came back at 1:30pm and was sent to what appeared to be the only room available. The stentch of body odor from the prior occupant was so offensive we could not stay in the room. They had the window open to air it out. Not a great first impression. I was then told there was no other room yet, but then after the someone checked with the manager, a new room was available. It was recently renovated so much cleaner and nicer than the first. The hotel location is key to it's appeal. Central Park, museums, restaurants all within walking distance. The major problem I have with the hotel was that I came down with a virus the morning we checked in. It was so bad that I asked my husband the next morning to check with the front desk to see if we could cancel our reservation for that evening (the 2nd night) without penalty as I could barely get out of bed and wanted to go home (we live an hour away). The front desk said no problem. We made it clear that if there was a penalty we would stay (as my husband could have taken my son out while I rested). Upon checkout, they charged us $300 for the one night. We told them we would stay then but they said they already "sold" the room. They indicated I signed upon checkin something that indicated $300 first night, $150 second night (which I knew, which is why we asked if we would not be penalized and pay half of the entire bill or $225). They refused to honor their prior agreement to not penalize us. Although not a really big deal, it did not leave a "good taste" in our mouths or wanting to return here. I would suggest Affinia hotels (the Shelburne has under $200 suites that are larger and brand new, they were booked which was why we chose the Lucerne). NOTE: although they charged us $300, if I booked this room for one night, the online cost is $290.

title: “Attention to detail”
text:
The hotel is perfectly situated across from Central Park and close to 5th Avenue shopping. 
The rooms are luxuriously decorated with all details covered. Robes, comfy pillows and mattress, flat screen, spacious bathrooms, etc. There were even motion activated lights under the night stand if you got up at night. The TV and lighting controls was interesting but didn't always work to my touch.
The breakfast area didn't match the luxury of the hotel. I asked for a private space for a breakfast meeting and arrived to find that my table was in the middle of the restauarant. Not much privacy for a business conversation.
The front desk staff was attentive, professional and personable.
I had a great stay and would stay again!

title: “A property with potential”
text:
The property appears well maintained and makes a good impression. 
Pros:
We were able to have breakfast at 5:00 am before heading to the airport.
Vanity is outside of bathroom which works well for 2 people getting ready at the same time.
Night light in bathroom was a good touch.
Keurig coffeemaker was great - but only had green tea for tea drinkers.
Cons: 
No air conditioning. We were on first floor with no screen so that was not an option either. We did report this but it seems to be a hotel issue.
Pillows were "neck breakers". After 10 minutes of trying to sleep we called the desk but no options available.
Heavy doors that do not shut quietly on their own.
We won't be able to use this hotel again because of the lack of sleep due to pillows that will easily last for 14 years and the temperature which was not conducive to a good nights rest. We liked the park and fly but not well enough to be exhausted the next day.

title: “My husbands 60th Birthday weekend”
text:
We had a fabulous experience this past weekend for my husbands 60th birthday. Earlier that week I contacted the hotel through email and Laurelin Hefter, the W insider, replied. She upgraded our room, provided complimentary Prosecco and chocolate covered strawberries as a surprise for my husband. We were also able to check in early as we got to the city before check in time. Everyone and everything was top shelf and we were even asked if we needed a late checkout. It was a perfect weekend thanks to Laurelin and the W staff.
Colleen Judge

title: “Good with the bad”
text:
PRO: Great location especially if you are into retail, hotel anchors not one but two upscale malls and ritzy Newbury Street is a few blocks away; lobby bar seems like a local hot spot; hotel has its own Starbucks in the lobby; rooms are smallish but well appointed; public transportation is plentiful; Amtrak Back Bay station is a three minute walk; killer views from upper floors.
CON: not exactly a quiet, intimate location; infuriating, fidgity keyless room entry system is prone to not letting you into you room on-check-in (last stay required presence of hotel engineer to gain admittance); meager water pressure on upper floors; hotel proximity to convention center means room rate price gouging on convention days; absolutely inexcusable $13.00 surcharge for Wi-Fi; beds on the soft side with barely adequate duvets; Lifetime Platinum Elite membership is met with typical Marriott staff indifference
BOTTOM LINE: If you are Marriott's Dream Guest (business traveler who can write off onerous surcharges on an expense account), go nuts. Vacation/person business travelers looking for a nice quiet taste of this great city should look elsewhere.

title: “PERFECT !!”
text:
My wife and I (35 and 39 years) stayed at the midlle of March 2011. If you are in NY for the 1st time been in Times Square it is an excellent choice, Service, rooms and locationas are really good for USD$200.00 a day. 5th av 1/2 a block, times squae 1 1 /2 block. Delis open 24 hrs 1/2 a block rockefeller center 2 blocks away, Intrepide museum 5 block away.
Bed, bath and closet excellent.
Im from Guadalajara, Mexico

title: “Beautiful, quiet, friendly hotel”
text:
Beautifuly located, large and convenient family rooms, very quiet, very nice breakfasts and evening receptions. 
The hotel staff was also exceptionally friendly, helping out with directions and tips regarding the area.

title: “Great Location. Disappointing Hotel”
text:
This was the first time we had stayed in NY City. Hotel Mela is in a great location for Times Square. A 2 minute walk and you are In Times Square, 5th Av, subway etc
We were disappointed with the hotel. We booked a Superior room and it was extremely small. Very little room to store any clothes or suitcases. There was only 2 foot space each side of the bed from the wall. The bathroom was clean and tidy tho.
The air conditioning in the room was very noisy and kept waking us up every time it kicked in. We opened the window and this was even noisier than the air con as there was the noisiest fan you have ever heard, so not much sleep!! This happened all 3 nights we stayed and we were glad when we left so we could get a good nights sleep.
The location was the only plus point for this hotel. We wont stay here again when we return to NY..

title: “Every aspect of a two night stay was miserable”
text: I have never felt the need to write a review but our experience at the capital Hilton was so bad I am compelled to do so. My husband who is a Hilton honors member hosted a conference there this weekend for 20 people and was embarrassed by the treatment and service in all aspects.

title: “Nikko worked great!”
text: My partner and I stayed at the Hotel Nikko this past weekend during the gay pride weekend. The hotel was very centrally located, one block from union square, and next to public transportation. We asked and received a room with a view of nob hill, the consierge was very helpful, and the room was very clean. Our only problem was the very limited late night room service menu...only offering three or four items. Once they arrived, the chips were stale and the salad wasn't very fresh. The next day upon check out the front desk person was very appologetic and took half off the meal price. WARNING parking costs 44.00 per day, with in and out privledges. A great stay overall.

title: “Cosy but lovely”
text: Small rooms but is a lovely cute little hotel that is surprisingly quite. Free coffee in the mornings, free wine in the arvo, won me over!! Close to the trams and shopping centres. Short tram trip to Fisherman's Wharf and all the touristy things to see in San Fran. Will definitely go back!!

title: “I've stayed at better Ritz-Carltons”
text: For the price, I was very disappointed. While the staff was friendly and accommodating, the rooms were very outdated. Temperature was hard to regulate, the bathtub was a problem (had to call plumber at 11:00pm) and for a suite, the amount of space was minimal. The view is spectacular, and the location is perfect for those needing to travel quickly by subway.

title: “Great Place, Great Location”
text: I stayed there for three nights and each night was perfect. The hotel is very classy and everyone there was more than helpful. No matter what we asked for they were pleased to help. Great location. My room was in the rear so we didn't have a biew but next time I go to NYC I plan to stay here and get a room with a view.

title: “The Agony of Deceit”
text:
We were given a room with a dripping heater, slow/clogged drains, and bad sewer vents. The desk's first solution was to happily pretend everything was fixed. Their second solution was to pretend everything was fixed and turn off the hot water to our heater.
"Why did you turn off our heater?" I asked the desk.
"Oh, the hotel's boiler is off tonight, since it's so mild." she replied, smirking.
What a pro to be able to say that lie without flinching! But, no, It was super cold in Chicago. They begrudgingly gave us another room. Sure enough, the hotel boiler was 100% on and working in the new room.
This hotel has seen better days. The lobby is a joke, with drafts blowing across the room every time the door opens, and mismatched, sagging ceiling tiles. The rooms are cramped, the elevators are slow. The vending machines are pretty cheap, I'll give them that. So I guess it's no surprise that they have service to match.

title: “A pleasant stay”
text:
A very large room with a marvellous view of the lake and an extremely comfortable bed. The staff was very pleasant and efficient in spite of the hotel being very full and very busy.
The only problem was that insulation from street noise was not perfect and the window panes could have been cleaner. A very positive impression on the whole, however.

title: “Good Business Hotel”
text:
Located in downtown DC this is a typical upscale hotel. The room was well appointed but there is no in room safe nor is there a mini-fridge. 
The entry drive is somewhat spartan but the lobby is very nice overall. There is a Starbucks and a small, pricey deli type establishment. There is free wifi in the lobby and it works well. I have noticed more upscale hotels offering lobby wifi for free. I assume this is to dampen the legitimate complaints about charging for in room wifi (a long time ago some of you might remember hotels charging for TV by having to put a quarter in a slot on the TV). 
I had a meal at a meeting at the hotel and it was quite good so I assume the restaurant would be as well.
The staff, as others have noted, is very service oriented.
No compalints or other negative observations.

title: “Wonderful Location”
text:
The hotel is in the perfect location if you want to be in Back Bay. It is connected to the Prudential Center and in the middle of Copley Square and Back Bay, with easy walking access to Newbury Street for shopping, Boylston for nightlife, and though a bit of a hike, walkable to Fenway, the theater district and Boston Commons. If you put your sneakers on, you can take a half hour walk to Faneiul Hall.
The room itself was standard business class - clean, comfortable and spacious. The room lacks anything jawdropping or romantic. It is more for the business traveler with conservative, luxurious decor. The beds were comfortable and the view was poor, but if you want to feel comfortable in a clean, well maintained hotel, this is perfect for you. The bathrooms were mediocre, no granite or marble... I didnt have to wear shower shoes, but I didnt exactly feel like the shower was sparkling.
The lobby was always super busy, and cans are lined out front all the time. Insider's tip - if you want to take the T, walk through the Prudential Center to Boylston and you wont have to go outside... Perfect tip in the rain.
I would stay here again.

title: “Amazing hotel”
text: We went to New York City for the first time last week. The night we got engaged we splurged and got a room at the Rivington Hotel. I had spent weeks on trip advisor looking up hotels. I picked this one because of the view. We were only staying one night and I thought a view of the city would be better than star-quality treatment. We got both. The service was amazing. We requested an iron and it was there in less than three minutes. The front desk called to make sure it was delivered. They hailed cabs every time we needed one. The day we checked out they held our bags all day so that we could explore the city. Upon check-in they escorted us to our room and gave us a tour to explain how everything worked (dimmer switches on lights, tub fills from the ceiling). The service was really wonderful. The room was tremendous. I was nervous because it's very modern and my taste isn't. I wouldn't put bright yellow carpet and tile in my house but here, it was great. We had the unique room with the soaking tub and a separate shower. It was huge. We dimmed the lights and soaked in a bubble bath while looking at the lights in the city. It was beautiful. The beds are to die for. I did not want to get up in the morning. We are definitely coming back.

title: “nice play to stay”
text: I enjoyed my stay and would visit the hotel again. The room was clean, I used the business center, and I enjoyed the fruit at the breakfast. I had a rental car and it was a reasonable drive to travel to the many places that I chose to visit. I have a minor complaint. The free breakfast only had regular 2% milk. I like skim milk so I went to a store and bought skim milk which I placed in the refrigerator in my room and used during the 3 days that I stayed at the hotel. I wrote about this point to Newton Bunce the General Manager and hope that he can implement that change so that health-conscious individuals can enjoy skim milk during their stay.

title: “Great Location - Comfortable Rooms”
text:
We had tickets for Lincoln Center and dinner reservations at Gordon Ramsay @ the London, Maze. The hotel was convenient to both. We were literally two blocks through easy covered "cut through" lobbies in public buildings to the restaurant. It was a $4.70 cab fare to Lincoln Center. 
The lobby of the hotel is sleek and modern. The room keys are ridiculously long cards. Some designer thought they were cool, I guess, but they didn't fit in a pants pocket or wallet. 
The room was done in an early 60's retro look. Brown and orange color scheme with lots of velvet. We were upgraded to a suite so we had very spacious accommodations. My husband did not like the "old" look - but I didn't mind it. I knew it wasn't really old. I knew it was sylistically a "retro" look.
The hotel is an easy walk to Carneghie Deli and Carneghie Hall. We really enjoyed our stay. I would stay there again. Comfortable beds with good pillows. Nice big shower. The main complaints were no coffee pot or ironing board in the room. We love to make our first cup of coffee in the morning to have while we are getting ready.

title: “Great Stay in West Houston”
text: Booked through Priceline. Very easy access off of Beltway 8. Great stay. Was in town for a wedding outside of Katy. Very nice bar area. no free breakfast though. but full menu for food. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Beautiful property that offers the Ahhhhh!”
text: Enjoyed two nights on the club floor, Elizabeth & Paulina were wonderful hostesses! Every aspect of the property was beautiful with scenic views, pools, health club, dining & shopping so close. We'll be back!

title: “No, Don't Go”
text:
I am a consultant and as such I get the opportunity to stay in many, many, hotels.
I have learned the difference between bad individuals and truly bad management. I also recognize that a few hairs in the sink doesn't necessarily mean that the entire "hotel is dirty".
I like to also say that I typically do not like to complain nor do I share my opinions in forums like this, but my experience at this hotel compelled me to write something...
Let me begin by saying my wife booked a 2-night stay as a last minute surprise for myself and the kids. She paid upfront, online using the "Great Getaways" promo.
When we first arrived, a large barking dog confronted our 3 yr old in the lobby who promptly started crying (yes, pets allowed in this resort). The observing doorman and porter did nothing to calm to situation.
When checking in, I specifically inquired as to whether or not the room was a "connecting" room ... yes it was. I was told the hotel was booked up for the weekend and that nothing else was available. At which point, I pulled out my Diamond Honors card hoping that this might prompt a change in the response ... apparently there were a few non-connecting rooms left.
When we opened the door to the newly assigned room, we discovered that is was a connecting room too.
Another visit to the front desk and we were given another room on the 1st floor facing out to the main parking lot.
Some peeling paint, a shower stall that had not been cleaned, and a lot of furniture that has seen better days (see pics). That's fine, I have seen worse ... (was too tired to make another visit to the front desk).
After a night of itching in their "serenity beds", I was convinced the previous occupants had used them for their pets to sleep on. A trip to the front desk after breakfast informed me that there were no rooms available (again) but to check back at 2p. Breakfast vouchers (bkfst should have been incl in the rate) and smore tickets were offered with a packaged "I'm sorry".
Several other encounters both witnessed and experienced, with staff and facilities completed our stay.

title: “Nice Stay”
text: The position of the hotel is great!!! The staff is also great, in particular Elisabeth at the front desk, she has been really nice and helpful. I got reasonable rates for a very good service. I'll be back next trip to NY.

title: “The Secret Is Out”
text: SO this is our hands down favorite hotel in SF. You cannot find a better view. 2 downsides to the rooms for the more discerning (picky or private) patron....the bathrooms are not really too private- there is a sliding door that makes it pretty easy to hear whats going on. Also, there is limited closet space in the average room. We love the circular suite...a must do for a special occasion and probably worth the splurge (700$ per night); absolutely beautiful. Room service and all service is fantastic and Bar Americano is fun, though crowded with thirty somethings on Thurs, Fri, and Sat. Concierge Monique is an amazing person; very kind and helpful. One other thing....no storage in the bathrooms, so bring your essentials in an organizer that you can stow.

title: “The Palomar is phenomenal”
text: From the hotel, to the location, to the staff there is not one thing I can actually complain about. I had such an amazing time at the Palomar, DC in June I looked no further when I decided to return in August. Stephane Vogel the Hotel Manager is AMAZING contacting me after our stay and is helping with our staff in August. Staff-friendly is an under statement. The Spa room is amazing to espically with the complementary wine and chocolates we reciever!! What more can you ask for on a vacation. LGBT SAFE AND FRIENDLY!!!!

title: “Great Hotel, neighbourhood not as bad as some say”
text:
I've been here twice this year, both on business. Having previously stayed at the Holiday Inn at Fishermans Wharf, its true to say that this is a very different view of San Francisco as you'll get up there.
That said, the neighbourhood is ok, if a little "real". There is a lot of homeless people around, and the check cashing stores get a little lively outside, but I've had no drama on the twice daily walks up Market and back. My first visit I was fairly cautious here, but spending more time here its not actually too bad. As usual, just keep your wits about you. Be careful about heading directly NW up into the tenderloin (again, not exactly dangerous, but not a comfortable place), head down Market and by the time you hit 5th it's all good.
As for the hotel, whilst the outside might not look too great, cleanliness and service are just excellent. Staff are always very helpful. It's a Holiday Inn, so you're getting their usual fayre - it isn't a Hilton by any stretch, but its a good 3*+, brilliant value, and if you're working downtown also a great location (albeit a good bit of exercise).
Gets a little noisy at nights, especially if you are on the lower numbers on each floor near 9th Street where you get all the traffic off the freeway and the dumpsters etc, but its not any worse than a central London or an Airport hotel.

title: “No A/C, mediocre service, overpriced”
text:
I booked our stay at the Inn on Ferry St. through Orbitz in December 2007 in preparation for the Detroit Electronic Music Festival 2008. I read lots of good reviews and decided to go for it. 
The problems started the day I got there, but I gave them the benefit of doubt. We arrived earlier than the check-in time, the room wasn't available, so no problem, we knew the time was 3pm. Well, we go out and about and come back at 3pm only to find out our room isn't ready and wasn't finally checked out until 3:30pm. No biggie, it happens.
Our room has wet spots on the carpet, the shower is decrepit, old, and barely working with little water pressure, and despite booking 6 months in advance we're pushed all the way to the 3rd floor. Again, I can live with it, I'm not a wimp and it's an indie business, can't expect perfection.
On day two, the room is blazing hot. 80+ degrees. I'm usually okay with warm rooms, but after dancing and being outside all day, and paying premium money, I want a room that's nice and cool. Well, I go to change the temperature on the thermostat and it's LOCKED. Okay, whatever, I'm just going to take off extra clothes, crash, and deal with it later. We're out again most of the night to enjoy the parties, and don't come back until the next morning. 
Again, the room is blazing, hitting 90 degrees. Can't change the thermostat. I get a few hours of poor sleep and decide to enjoy the rest of the festival. We come back that night around midnight to get some good sleep before we get on the plane home the next morning. Well, the room at this point is still at 90 degrees and blazing, so I decide to call the front desk to ask why it's so hot. Well, Terrence explains to me that they don't turn the A/C on until June, no matter how hot it gets. I ask if he can't make an exception considering this is our last night and it's summer...I mean come on, I just dropped ~$200 per night and I just want some A/C...it would be one thing if I was staying in a 3rd world country, but jeez. Well, he says he can't do it, owners won't allow it. I ask if he'll at least bring us some ice and waters since it's so hot and there's no fridge. He first resists, and says I can come get it. So I politely say, "Well, my room is blazing hot, it's 1am, and I've been out and about all weekend, I'd really appreciate it if you just brought it to us, it would really help out" (which I should NEVER have to do at ANY hotel, much less some fancy bed and breakfast that costs way too much money). He says "fine, I'll be there soon." And I wait. And wait. And I realize he's never going to show up. Fine, be that way, I'll quietly go home, and be sure to write the most scathing review of your hotel on every website I can. 
Really, for the price this place costs you'd think they'd turn on the A/C on the third and hottest floor, or at the very least bring us free ice and water. Nah, let 'em rot. They already paid Orbitz, no way they can get their money back now.
I overlooked some of the rude behavior of the manager and receptionists early on. But this cut the cake. I'll never go to this amateur establishment again.

title: “When it says 4 stars, divide by 2 and take 1 away - its that bad....”
text:
Well it started badly, when we checked in, we had pre-ordered a cot for our 11 month old baby. The guy on the counter told us he had one, but it was broken. 
It was advertised as 4 star hotel and to be honest it struggled to meet 2 star standards.
The shower was disgusting, actually the whole bathroom was pretty much in a state of disrepair and basically not up to the hygiene standards you would expect in the USA.
When we got there I nearly crashed our car (well beached really!) in the car park. It was dark and the only space that was left had a massive drop in the middle of it that I couldnt see with the light available. The bottom of the car ground on the floor - dont tell Thrifty!!!
I didnt do the complimentary "continental breakfast", but it was by far the worst of our trip with absolutely nothing of any substance. 
There was no fridge in our room either.
We stayed one night and if the rest of Hollywood was not booked out or extortionate prices I wouldn't have even stayed that long!
They did take $ 20 off for not having a cot available for us, so that was something.

title: “good location”
text:
The hotel is very well located in the midtown, between the rockfeller center, the empire state building and time sqaure.
Good looking hall and rooms.
The room was quite big and clean.
Employees were kind and friendly.

title: “Great Hotel, well located.”
text:
We stayed 3 nights in this hotel, and were very pleased with it. We had my 94 year old mother in the room next door and she was also very pleased, except with her stringent breakfast requirements. The rooms were spacious and very comfortable. The bed was exceptional. The staff were very friendly and attentive. 
As far as we were concerned there were only 2 negatives. Each room has a coffee maker, which is not good for making tea. They took about 50 minutes to get the water hot enough to make coffee or tea, and did not get it hot enough to add milk. I enquired about a kettle or jug, but they did not have one, so it meant making the tea, adding milk, and putting it back into the pot and wait another 15 minutes, so having a cup of anything took at least an hour. At least they did have refrigerators in the room. The second was the onsite Restaurant. We travel a lot, and this was our 20th World trip, each over a month, so are well used to hotels. It is an Italian Restaurant , and the food seemed fine, but not everyone wants to eat Italian all the time, and there was nothing else on the menu. The breakfast was served there, and it was a la cart, with a fairly limited range, but the pricing was good for what they had. This made getting breakfast a slow process, not getting what you actually wanted. On the last day, we found the Restaurant at the Marriot, about 150m down the road, this was a full buffet and was excellent, but a bit more expensive, so we were annoyed that we only noticed in time to have one dinner and the breakfast there the next morning. Both were excellent, the breakfast was a bit more expensive, but a lot more varied.
As far as the hotel went, we were very pleased, except the minor problem of making tea. They were happy to bring a jug of hot water on request, but that was out of their coffee maker, so not exceptionally hot, and the San Francisco water is very chlorinated, where pure water was $3/gallon at the nearby 7-11.
The free Wi Fi was very appreciated.

title: “Why ask what kind of room we want if you can't provide it?”
text:
We booked our stay directly with the property and was asked during the booking process if we wanted smoking or non-smoking. Since the person making the reservation smokes, she requested smoking. When we arrived for a multiple day stay we were told there were no smoking rooms available at that time but that we would be able to get one for the next day on if we wished. We decided at the time that unpacking for one night and then re-packing to move the next day was not something we would be happy to do, and elected not to take that optiom at the time. A few hours later it seemed like a better idea, we called the desk are were told that all the smoking rooms were taken for the next few days. Here is the good part; they have 497 rooms. 492 of those rooms are non-smoking. There is a placard advising of a $250 cleaning charge if a non-smoking room is smoked in, so in reality they have 5 smoking rooms at the rack rate and an additional 492 smoking rooms at rate plus a flat $250 surcharge. The shift manager was not in the least accomodating. The room was well furnished with premium linens and such, but a very inconvienient floor plan with a hinged closet door that virtually blocked access to & from the bathroom, where the toilet overflowed on our last night there. 
The final insult was that the evening before our early morning departure we inquired of the concierge if there would be any problem getting a mini-van taxi to the airport early in the morning rather than a sedan and were told to simply request a mini-van with the doorman when we were ready to leave. We did so at about 6:00 A.M. the next morning. He called the cab company and clearly requested a mini-van. Shortly thereafter two sedan taxis showed up and got into a shouting match with the hack that was next in the queue at the hotel. This was rather embarrasing to us, plus it interfered with other guests needing to get to the airport, so we ending up cramming our bags and a very tired prothetic knee into an uncomfortable sedan back seat complete 
with an un-eaten cheeseburger on the cushion for a 
land speed record attempt ride to the airport. Let's just say we are in no hurry to go back to Indianapolis, and should we be so unfortunate, we won't be staying at the Hyatt. Perhaps they should consider updating their lexicon to not refer to their customers as "guests", but rather as victims.

title: “Great Hotel Choice - Value and Quality”
text: I had a two week business trip. I was having trouble getting a reasonable rate on a local hotel and so the Hilton reservations agent was nice enough to check all the Hilton brands around the same area to see what was available in my price range. Upon arrival, the front desk clerks were extremely helpful and friendly. The lounge serves great appetizers and a filling breakfast with great staff that run the room. The room is the usual Hilton great condition and great bedding. I would stay here again the next time in the San Diego area.

title: “Noisy room”
text: This hotel was in a great location but staff were very impersonal .While we were checking in the clerk kept answering the phone.The room was fairly spacious but the A/C was very noisy. We turned it off to discover we could hear other rooms aircon. All we wanted was a quiet room. I would not stay at this hotel again.

title: “The room and hotel appointments are excellent. Security and management are terrible. Use caution if you stay.”
text: The hotel rooms are very nice and its location is good. The views from the one side of the tower is not very good as you overlook a parking lot or power station. The other corners are much better with a beautiful park view. Staff was very good at immediately addressing a security issue that occurred during my stay. Management unfortunately dropped the ball by their unwillingness to reduce the length of my stay. If your staying alone in the hotel I would be very cautious of people coming and going through the hotel to make sure your not being followed to your room. This incident is the reason for my negative ratings listed below. Again the rooms themselves are beautiful and very comfortable. The wait staff for the food service far exceeded expectations.

title: “For an Embassy Suites - Not So Great”
text: I stayed here one night in July 2011 for business. The previous night, I had spent the night at the Embassy Suites in Downey, CA, so i was able to do a direct comparision. The Embassy Suites at LAX was over $200/night compared to $180 at the Downey location, and the rooms at LAX were less updated, especially the bathroom. The window had this weird film over it so that you couldn't see outside. I kind of felt like a prisoner in my own room. It looked like a sliding door, so I tried to open it and it triggered some alarm. So, needless to say, there wasn't much of a view. The inside of the hotel was nice, lots of plants everywhere, and there was a convenient shuttle to the airport, only about a 5 minutes ride. The room served it's purpose by giving me a place to sleep, but I found the room to be overpriced, and if i was traveling on vacation rather thatn busienss, i probably wouldn't choose this hotel again.

title: “Exactly what we were looking for”
text: I was in town playing with a band for a couple of nights. We booked this hotel based on recommendations read here. The hotel is right off Hollywood Blvd. There was secure, monitored parking with no additional fee. We didn't worry about our gear at all. The hotel was quiet, & there were bagels, etc. for breakfast. Good coffee around the clock. Rooms were very clean and staff was friendly. Lots of international guests. Good place for families, but no pool. Many great things to see within walking distance.

title: “Nice place to stay in SF”
text: Lombard Motor Inn is a very nice and comfortable place in San Francisco. We stayed there for a couple of nights and everything was great. They don't have breakfast but you can find bakeries and restaurants around the property with good prices. Location is good, it's right on the intersection with Van Ness, easy to commute and in a walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf, Fort Manson and Lombard St. gardens. Front desk guys were always friendly and helpful and they have free parking. I'd definitely stay at Lombard Motor Inn next time I go to SF, it's a great deal.

title: “The W in DC - Very Nice Hotel”
text: I had to attend to some business in Washington and last time stayed at the St Regis and was totally beyond impressed and was planning on staying there again next time I came to town but I was meeting up with a friend who is a W fanatic and insisted we stay here. (in fact we are still here as I type) It does not live up to the St. Regis but then again it is several hundred dollars a night cheaper so..... ;-) Anyway, It is a great hotel however, it is maybe, just a little "too hip"??? is that possible, LOL?? I don't know how to describe it, almost trying too hard? I guess I just don't get the whole W concept, I know many people who adore them. Anyway, the service is spot on, the hotel is beautiful (if you like hip and modern), and the roof - top lounge is absolutely stunning and filled with Washington's beautiful people, very interesting to enjoy a evening up there. The room, a Fantastic Suite (actual room name) is medium size for a suite, but plenty big for Washington. My friend is flying out tomorrow and I am moving over to my old stand-by the Willard in the morning but I expect I might try another W out again in the future.

title: “Unique and Consistently Excellent”
text:
I spent four nights at Giraff over a long weekend. I was disappointed that my intended traveling companion had to cancel, so I was prepared to find fault. However, everyone was so helpful and efficient when I arrived that I couldn't find any. My room and amenities were as requested. The balcony was a fun addtion to the ambiance.
Nearby Madison Square Park is a little jewel. Go watch the dogs play and you'll have a great day for sure.
The breakfast buffet was a wonderful convenience and offered wonderful variety. The wine and cheese party in the evening was a welcome stop on the way in or out.
It has some restrictions on amenites such as room service - they get you takeout from a restaurant. So I just went up the block and ate at each of the restaurants they use - the food was excellent. Those who are not used to staying in a boutique or niche hotel might find that disconcerting, bu it is easily mde up by the relaxed atmosphere and personal attention to service. Employees quickly recognize and acknowledge you in all areas. The maid and I had a fun chat on the elevator.
The free internet access was a plus and you really feel welcome in the lobby - newspapers and a laptop you can borrow to check your mail.
Hotel Giraffe is farther downtown than I have usually stayed, but I would definitely book there again or recommend to any friends.

title: “This B & B has history!”
text:
The staff were outstanding to our needs. The room although small was furnished with old antique furniture. The bed was clean & very comfortable. We enjoyed the sherry & cookies each night and sitting in the lavish old parlors....you felt like royals!
Breakfast consisted of cereals, pastries, bread & bagels, fruit, juice & coffee, hard boiled eggs & sausage. Free wi-fi. If you don't have a laptop or notebook there was a computer downstairs that you could use with a printer for no extra cost.
The hotel booked our tours for us & we were very happy with their choices.
Parking was $15 plus tax but that is not unreasonable for San Francisco & just across the street.

title: “Best location, lovely room.”
text: Our stay at the Omni Parker House was everything I expected. We were lucky enough to get a room on a very busy September long weekend, it was pricey, but no more than any other local hotel and maybe even a little less. We had a delightful corner room, queen size bed and the room itself was just fine with a view of the Old City Hall. The bathroom is very very small, but to be expected in such an old hotel. We did join the loyalty program, but did not inform the hotel until our arrival, so the services associated with this were a little slow in coming. I recommend you do this ahead of time. Our check in was also a little delayed because of how busy it was, that was disappointing - but I understand these things happen. The staff were friendly, helpful and welcoming - we did use the valet service, a tad expensive, but the local parking garages were very full with the long weekend. The location of this hotel could not be more perfect and although I would not hesitate to return to this hotel, I also like trying different places too!

title: “Excellent Suite”
text: Awesome place to stay. Hotel was fairly new so everything was above acceptable! Washer/Dryer facility located within the hotel which is a great help if you have children. Room had temperature control which was excellent because I had the flu during my vacation. There's no room service, but with all the extra amenties there it makes up for what you don't get.

title: “Excellent Customer Service!!!”
text: I recently stayed at the Radisson Blu Aqua Hotel in Chicago, IL. The customer service from the time I stepped out of the taxi from the airport was amazing!!! Everyone had welcoming smiles and made sure that I had exactly what I needed!!! The service of the staff ranging from the bell hop to the servers during our events to the room service attendant was outstanding!!! I felt right at home and welcomed, which is a hard thing to find in hotels sometimes. Thank you Radisson Blu Aqua Hotel in Chicago, IL!!!

title: “If you don't like soulless chain hotels”
text: than this is the place to stay. It is a small, romantic B&B in the middle of a large city. The staff is extremely courteous. Steve at the front desk is a font of information about the city and directed us to several great restaurants and site-seeing locations. He is friendly, polite and as asset to the hotel. The cleaning staff (who's names we, unfortunately, did not get) were there immediately whe we requested a room fan. It was an exceptionally hot weekend in SF. That, plus the water, the incredible breakfast and hominess of it made for a great stay. We had never stayed there before, but the people made us feel like we were valued regulars. Sure some of the rooms are small, but how much time will you spend in a room in such a fantastic city? Plus, the afternoon cookies were always delicious. I highly recommend this hotel for adults.

title: “Great Value”
text: My family and I stay at this Hotel every time we have to stay overnight, in Houston. We encounter no problems, but we do usually just stay one night. The staff is very friendly and the rooms are clean. The breakfast is good. This location is perfect for our needs and an overall great value.

title: “A jem in the windy city”
text:
Stayed there Nov 2011, booked via PL for 105$ a night (2 nights)...a bit pricy but was it worth it.
Arrived early (9h30AM) and was provided a room on the 6th floor with a good view of the Lakeside park across the street. Check in was super courteous and friendly. The room itself was just accross the gym entrance, and was huge. The bed was delicious (slept like a baby), the wall mounted LCD TV had close to 90 channels, a nice work station with a good chair and a huge bathroom (with shower only, but i'm a shower person myself) well appointed with good toiletries. A bathrobe was also available, as well as a safe (didnt use either). Very good Wi-Fi available for 12.95$ per day, not a bad price, but do keep in mind it runs noon to noon, so if you buy it at 9PM an evening, it will run till noon the next day, not 24 hours as in most hotels (management was kind enough to credit me one day).
The gym was quite big, well appointed with 3 of each ellipticals, bikes and treadmills, loads of Nautilus equipment, and freeweights. Also available are lemon infused and regular iced water, earbuds earphones, small towels, and cold damp hand towels. Nice view of the park mentionned above. Downside is that there is no pool, mind you, this is an older building (1920s methinks) so they did not build pools back then...didnt miss it.
The lobby is quite nice, mixing classic 1920s elements with modern ones. The concierge was super helpful, and provided me with maps and what nots. The business provides free internet access and printing (no gouging here) so I checked in and printed my boarding pass online for my return. There are a few restaurants on site, but I used La Bodega downstairs for my breakfast, 6.50$ for a breakfast sandwich and a fruit or pastry...delicious German sausage, with eggs, Mahon cheese, caramelized onion...a good deal (they have 5$ deals weekdays, so even better if your staying then). A few inexpensive places around also: Harold's fried chicken on Wabash, South Loop Club and a pizza place , KFC/Pizza Hut/DD on the same street....plenty of choice for cost conscious travellers.
Ran out of shaving cream, and within 5 minutes was provided with some Barbasol (travel size) and a good quality razor!
Only downside: there was a marriage going on my last night, sounded fun...but also loud! Given the 6th floor is the lowest guest floor, the music could be heard in my room...called the lobby and was offered a room on a higher floor...but since they told me the party would end at around midnight (and I was watching TV late), I stayed put and the music subsided by 11PM...went to bed then.
The hotel is 5-10 minutes walk from Harrison on the red line. Plenty of buses in front of the hotel...the CTA is quite good and efficient...all in all, good location!
In conclusion, I loved this place...hope i can get another good deal on PL for this!

title: “Aloft continues to impress”
text: This was my third time staying at Aloft Phoenix Airport, and I was extremely pleased once again with this trendy, modern hotel. The beds are slightly firm, but the room is delightful. Whoever designed them needs an award! Power outlets and light switches NEXT TO THE BED?? WHOA! Also, the desk connecton-point and charging station for iPhones, iPods etc was very helpful this trip. It was inconvenient that I couldn't print US Airways Boarding Passes from the Touchscreen Kiosk, but I was able to print them easily from the full desktop computers in the lobby. The fitness center is top-notch, I love that I could control my iPhone's musuc from the touchscreen. And Starwood has knocked it out of the park withj free airport transfers from Aloft. We stayed at Aloft the night before a morning flight to New York, and we left our car at Aloft the whole time. After we landed back in Phoenix, I called Aloft to see if we could arrange for transportatoin back to the hotel to get our car, and they sent a black towncar to Sky Harbor for free to get us back. Outstandnig service, bravo Aloft!

title: “will report bed bugs to texas dept of health”
text: when i arrived the hotel was hot, no air conditioning. i was told they were renovating. i went out for a while , got dinner and brought it back to the room. i was in room 205. i changed into my nightgown turned the bed down, and propped the pillows so i could watch t.v. and eat. i was sitting in bed when i felt like something was biting my back and neck and making me very itchy. i was hysterical and went to the front desk. the manager was there did not tell me her name, and said they had had a problem with bed bugs. she credited my room, but i was afraid to stay there, because of the health risk. the only place they could find me was the marriott which was outrageously expensive, but i didn't have a choice. i have reported this hotel to the texas dept. of health and i have contacted my attorney. PLEASE DO NOT STAY HERE IT IS NOT SAFE THERE WERE BUGS ALL OVER MY BED AND I SAVED THEM TO PROVEIT!!!!!!! Lorraine Kudirka

title: “Perfect Weekend”
text: I took my wife the NYC for our 10th anniversary. The room was fantastic and the service was great. You have to be careful of some of the concierge recommendations for restaurants. They are more interested in the 'scene' than the cuisine. Rooms this big at this price are hard to find.

title: “Almost perfect”
text:
We just returned from 3 nights in New York City, staying at the Casablanca on recommendations from TripAdvisor. I was not disappointed! It's a lovely hotel, reasonably priced for its location (we paid a little under $280 a night for a single room with king bed, on the top floor). Times Square is literally half a block out the door, but somehow, the Casablanca seems like a quiet little boutique hotel anyway. Sandwiched between a couple of restaurants, the front entrance is, literally, a doorway. The staff is mostly friendly, the decor is pretty cool, based on the movie Casablanca, and the little details are well thought out. 
Downsides are relatively minor, but need to be mentioned. Wifi is free throughout but was touch-and-go in our room. The only windows we had looked out the back, onto fire escapes and the backs of other buildings. (From what I've heard, that's preferable to a streetside room which can be noisy.) Room was small and too hot. Elevator was tiny and slow. No coffee maker in the room. No bathroom heater (even in a hot room, one likes a little extra heat coming out of the shower). No business center, just one slow computer in the corner of the breakfast room.
The upside? Too many to mention. Free breakfast (there's an espresso/coffee machine in the breakfast room, but the espresso that it makes is pretty lousy, so stick to the quite-good drip coffee) is hearty. Rooms are very very clean. Beds are comfy and have soft sheets and real blankets -- not those plastic blankets you get in chain hotels. Service was great - I requested a small fan ahead of time and it was in the room when I got there. 
Location of course is ideal. We were able to walk to a Broadway play, walk to Central Park, walk to Rockefeller Center, etc etc etc. 
In short, I highly recommend the Casablanca.

title: “Party central, if you like parties.”
text:
If you're in the right demographic, the Maritime is like dying and going to heaven. I am not that demographic.
“That” demographic is young nightclubbers from New Jersey, or gays, or some combination thereof. I am an old businessman. Most of my travel is business travel. I look for places that are clean, comfortable, not overly fussy, near my work, and – if possible – quiet.
The Maritime is clean, comfortable, and not overly fussy. It's also right across the street from where I happened to be working, an office in the bustling Chelsea Market. However, the one thing The Maritime is NOT is quiet.
More about that in a minute. Here's what's nice about the place:
Rooms are small but smartly laid out, with practical and rich wood touches befitting and resembling a ship stateroom. Size-wise, they're not really much larger than the claustrophobic cubicles at the Hudson (stay away!) but much more ergonomic and pleasant. The bed is comfortable, the shower like a pleasant tropical rain. In addition to the standard amenities, you get your own little stereo system, a DVD player, and a bedside clock radio that accommodates your iPod. The room's three lighting zones are all on dimmers, creating a nice mood. All rooms face the west, and from about the 5th floor up you can see the Hudson River and New Jersey. Wireless internet is fast, reliable, and free. Points off for the little toy ironing board, good luck with those shirts. Everything here is kept clean and fresh.
The lobby has cozy little gathering areas with couches and chairs that people actually use. Just off the lobby are a really nice wood-paneled bar with booths and a big pool table, and La Bottega, a sort of Italian trattoria serving pretty decent food at mid-to-high-endy prices. About a third of La Bottega is indoors, and the other two-thirds are outdoors on a large, colorful patio. They do room service too.
The staff is courteous and efficient, but not overly friendly; don't expect a smile or a hearty “good morning!” from anyone here.
Here's the problem for me, The Old Guy: this section of Ninth Avenue used to be the frontier, the sparsely-populated outer fringe of Chelsea. About eight years ago, two blocks to the south, the Meatpacking District exploded with trendy clubs and nightlife. It ceased attracting the Beautiful People two years after that, and has since morphed into a playground for bridge-and-tunnel club kids.
This is now a very busy, and very noisy neighborhood, at least during the warm-weather months. There is traffic and endless horn-honking until past midnight every night. Thursday through Sunday nights are just brutal. The kids flock to La Bottega and turn into a seething mass of noisy seagulls until one a.m. No floor is high enough to escape the din.
Then there's The Cabanas, The Maritime's open-air rooftop lounge. It's open Thursday until 2 a.m., and Friday/Saturday until 4 a.m. There is a DJ until 2 or 3. At least I think it's from there; maybe it's coming from the trendy rooftop bar next door, at the Dream Hotel. Regardless, window closed and locked, curtains drawn, there is no avoiding the music.
Finally, we have “8,” the new, velvet-roped party nexus for the real glitterati. It's literally right next door. The cab and limo line for this place winds around the block, and right under your window, from dusk to sunup. And you know how NY cabbies love their horns.
To be fair to the Maritime, staying in Partytown and complaining about the parties is as silly as staying in Antarctica and complaining about the cold. Nonetheless, I believe tripadvisor readers deserve to know exactly what they're getting into. For me, the racket is really a dealbreaker. You might be OK on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday, but any other night it's caveat emptor. Remember, I'm an older gentleman; if you're a young big shot out for a late night on the town and have $300+ to spend on a room, this could be heaven.

title: “You will love this place has it all!”
text: Great location. We loved our 79 rate we got a hot breakfast that had it all. We ordered room service that was excellent. My wife complimented on the accent wall. Beautiful place.

title: “after staying 150 plus nights a year i vow to never stay at this property again”
text: this is not a property that deserves to be in the marriott chain. the rate of $265.00 per night cannot be justified for the level of quality of the rooms and the staff. when checking in the clerk was very short and impolite. i was also told at check in that there was a concierge room that was open. we i called downstairs the next morning i was told that the lounge was closed. i called again and asked for confirmation that it was closed and the desk clerk asked a guest who said it was open. i had to take a cold shower which facilitated me being moved to another room. i had to wait 15-20 minutes for a valet to show up and take my car. the internet did not work in the room so my wife had to call ibahn to resolve the issues that the hotel staff could not. i called marriott platinum line and asked to change hotels and was told by Kim with marriott platinum customer service that i was to late 4pm to change hotels now so i would have to apy 134.00 before i could leave this hotel. kim was as inept as the staff at the hotel. she was not able to facilitate anything to resolve my complaints nor were the hotel staff.

title: “Great place--good value”
text: Front desk was very friendly even though I arrived after midnight. Accommodations were comfortable and clean. I would stay here again the next time I go to Seattle.

title: “comfortable and friendly”
text: The hotel is well located, small and comfortable, with plenty of space in the rooms. The staff is friendly, and helpful.

title: “Decent Hotel,pathetic Service”
text:
I booked my stay online since it was advertised as a special to park my car while we cruised. I paid for the night before the cruise and the night after the cruise in advance. Upon my arrival I found out for some reason my cared did not go through, but they still had my room for me at a higher rate. No one bothered to call me or email me and let me know that card did not go through. A very nice lady told me no problem, she would take care of everything for me, but my room would not be ready for another hour and gave me points of interest in the city and directions so we would have something to do while waiting(we was a couple hours early) After going out for dinner and returning, we found a different lady working the check in and she proceeded to tell me everything the first lady tole me was wrong. 1 I could not have the lower rate promised by first lady and the shuttle service, I had to pay an additional $54 for, but they would bring me back to the hotel. 
Now that it is later in the day and we are leaving the next morning for a cruise, we had to accept the reeming she was offering, figured I would contact corporate when we got back from our cruise and tell them about the "bait and switch" we received. The first lady told me that they would schedule our shuttle ride for us, however the second lady said she could not do that to just be ready between 11 and 1. Well, next morning comes, no calls from her to meet shuttle,finally around 12 we decided to go see what happened and was told she tried to call us and even came to our room to tell us it was time, funny thing is we was there and no one ever knocked on our door, nor did the phone ring. We decided to just stay in the lobby and wait for next shuttle where we was packed in like sardines, my children had to sit on my lap, yet I had to pay $54 for them to have their own seats. Shuttle ride to cruise port was ok other than cramped conditions.
When we returned from our cruise we found there was only 2 shuttles running and not only were they servicing our hotel, but also 3 others.
