We waited for almost an hour to catch our shuttle back to the hotel. When we finally got back to the hotel, the 1st lady was there and was appalled at how we was treated by the nightshift clerk. She printed up a refund and promised me the manager would refund it asap. It has now been 1 week and the manager still has not had time to refund me my money for the seats we did not use. Everytime we went by the office while there he was on the internet.
Now for specifics of the hotel, beds were horrible, we rented a suite to have seperate rooms from the kids only to find the room was joined and no doors. The sleeper sofa might has well been made of concrete as it was to short to sleep on couch part and the pull out mattress was about 1" thick. On second night stay, we used the laundry room only to have machines take several dollars from us, what did the second shift lady tell us? Sorry, not her problem, call number on machine. Great,we called and got a recording. Ok great, another reason to not come back. After checking into our room the first night, we was stopped by another guest and was told people were breaking into cars everynight and to make sure we did not leave our stuff in our car. Now we had to go to walmart and by another suitcase and take all of our car video players with us on a cruise. Fortunately when we returned our car had not been touched. 
The second night stay, the room key machine was broke and we had to walk all the way to the front desk to have them call someone to let us in our room. 
I would not recomend this hotel to anyone. Save your money and call the best western across the street. They also offer shuttle service to the cruise port, except they have more dedicated vans to only their hotel. While waiting on our shuttle I met the manager of the hotel who was there himself to make sure his guest were picked up quickly and taken back to his hotel.

title: “You can't get closer to lake Michigan. Get ready for $60 parking fee!!”
text:
Stayed 5 nights during oncology convention in June. Even though I live in Chicago, I couldn't pass up a company paid room in a premium location in the city. 
The hotel is modern, trendy, and offered free local rides via the Acura driving experience. Everything at the hotel is expensive even for Chicago. $18 dollar grey goose Martinis at the bar to the $60 valet parking fees. 
Good view from the hotel especially if you have the lake view, but since you are right next to the lake shore drive, its a long walk or short can ride to the Michigian ave for shopping. 
If you are in to the spa thing the Bliss Spa on site is amazing of course at astronomical prices.

title: “Very Welcoming!”
text:
We stopped in Memphis for a night during Memorial Day weekend. Our stay at the Courtyard Marriott was wonderful, from the time we drove up to the time we left. When we pulled up to the hotel, the parking attendants were so nice and helpful in assisting and telling us what was up for the weekend. All the staff was so nice and inviting. From the circle drive at the hotel to the lobby to the room to the exercise room/hot tub/deck, everything was modern and well kept. 
I was worried that the hotel was would be too far from Beale Street. Found out it was a healthy walk away from the hotel but not too far or too close. It was about six blocks away and as the streets around got very busy and crowded, we realized the Courtyard Marriott was in a perfect location. We got back from hanging out on Beale Street and sat out on the patio and watched as people and carriages went by that clear night.
After seeing the room and bathroom, I immediately called my family and told them how nice this hotel was. I definitely recommend this hotel if in Memphis and will probably stay again. Overall, great stay!

title: “Excellent hotel & Service & breakfast to die for!!”
text:
2nd stay with the Sofitel chain, 1st in NYC. Perfect location for everything on 44st. Very pleasant staff. Room was on the 17th floor - as usual extra comfy beds, plenty of towels and very clean. Turn down service was lovely. Nice space for a NYC hotel.
Breakfast was amazing. Try the waffle!! Yum! My partner is french so he adored it! It is worth getting out of the comfy beds for. 
We got a great deal - 3 nights for price of 2 including brekky totalling $720 booking directly with the hotel. This was for Valentines Weekend! Book well in advance to get the deals. Great value, great location, Megga Breakfast.
Cant wait to go back!

title: “Great location, room and breakfast”
text: Stayed 3 nights and the location of the hotel was wonderful. A 10 minute walk to the Hard Rock restaurant to pick up the Double Decker Hop On/Hop Off Trolley. Portobello's hot dog restaurant there as well and Gino's Pizza, easy walk to Michigan Ave. and we walked to Millenium Park with no problem. The breakfast had a great variety and different everyday, the happy hour was a plus as well. The corner view room is very spacious and it was so nice to have a dishwasher, coffee maker and full size refrigerator. I booked in advance and got the AAA rate of $225 and was pleased with the rate and the hotel. It was the weekend of the Rider Cup so all hotels were booked and rates were well above the $225 price.

title: “Very good experience”
text: Visited twice. First visit December 2008 as a couple. We were offered a large room with amazing view however there was no mini-bar in the room. Second visit as a family with a baby July 2010, they first gave us a room with small windows and no view and after complaining they gave us a much better room with excellent view, again no mini-bar in the room. Very expensive internet connection.

title: “Beautiful hotel with wonderful grounds”
text:
We have stayed many places in San Diego, but we really loved the setting of this hotel. We were there for Mother's Day weekend visiting our son at USD. You feel you are in a tropical resort but in the heart of Mission/Pacific Beach. The lagoon in the back has it own beach with fantastic walking/biking trails all around Mission Bay. We loved the location to all the action on the main drag, but how quiet and serene you feel once you enter the hotel. You feel like you are in another world.
Very beautiful and romantic setting for weddings (which we got to witness) on the grounds. The staff was super accommodating! We love the location to all the bars and restaurants in the area. The ocean is directly across the street. I love the fact that you can rent bicycles and ride to La Jolla from here. We had a wonderful time and are planning to return in August when we take our son back to college.

title: “A Nightmare at the Premier”
text:
Upon entering my room (1019), I was shocked by a wall where the previous guest had scrawled, "wash me" in soot. I should have left then. If the housekeeping staff could overlook such obvious filth, what else in the room might have been overlooked and never properly cleaned?
The room was cramped and unwelcoming. The carpeting and the room in general were dirty and unkempt. The uncomfortable sofa was a worn sectional in two pieces with wooden arms. There was no lap blanket. The magazines were piled carelessly on the table. There wasn’t even a pen in the room. A Zen garden with a broken rake rested on the desk.
The ironing board was not properly attached to the door, so it banged loudly every time I opened the closet. There were no bathrobes and only three very small bath towels for two adults. The paint on the exposed ceiling pipe was peeling off.
I cannot stress enough the disturbing effect of the hotel’s disappointing and dirty facilities had on me. We didn't book two rooms at a luxury hotel for nearly $900 a night to have such a shabby, careless and poorly maintained accommodation.
 On Sunday morning we never received an in room checkout or a hotel evaluation card, making me wonder if the staff suspected we would comment negatively about our stay. Prior to check out we called the desk for our car. We were told we had to go to the Millennium Hotel Bell Stand for information about it. We had to drag our luggage through thePremier to the Millennium lobby to the 45th Street entrance. The bellhop did not know how we would be able to get out of 6th Avenue. The parking attendant handed us our car keys and parking stub, left us facing a crowd of people and a wooden barricade, and told us to ask the police to let us drive through it. Only after we approached some NYC police officers did we get help. We had to turn our SUV around and the police officers guided us the wrong way down a one-way street. Finally we were on our way.
When I am on a vacation I do not like to confront service personnel. I choose hotels and resorts with the highest ratings for service and accommodations. I do not want to voice complaints, have confrontations, or draw attention to myself. I try to choose recreation that is stress free. And mostly I do not want to be concerned about the sanitary conditions of my bed or bathroom.I looked at your web site before I booked. I expected a relaxing stay at a luxury hotel. Your advertisement clearly misrepresents the quality, service, facilities and attitude of the Premier.Your customer service director is quoted in one press release as saying she wants consistently satisfied customers and that the Premier guarantees it will "meet and exceed the expectations of our guests." The Premier facilities are far from hitting that mark.
My stay at the Premier last night was most unpleasant. I keep recalling the sooty writing on the wall and am unnerved by the unseen filth it may represent. I feel I have been grossly cheated, not only because of the high price I paid for a very bad experience but also because my weekend was so hurt by this situation. I can see no reason to stay at your hotel again and I will certainly share my experience with as many people as I can.
I hope you will address my complaints and respond. 
I sent my letter September 18, 2005 and I have not heard anything from anyone at the Premier Hotel in New York City.

title: “Fab Location and Great Breakfast!”
text:
It was my first time to New York and I absolutely loved this hotel.
The location is fantastic- within spitting distance of Macys and Times Square. 
The rooms are quite large and are very clean and comfortable. We had a nice bathroom and walk-in closet plus ironing facilities, mini bar and snack basket.
The breakfast in the morning is one of the best bits- I can't believe
they throw it in for free! Loads of fresh tasty muffins and bagels as
well as bread, spreads, pastries and cereals. The hotel also does comlpimentary tea and coffee all day long- another bonus!
Another great feature of the hotel is its rooftop terrrace. Here you can enjoy the view of the city including Macy's and The Empire State Building. t's a great suntrap and they even open up a bar at certain times of the day. Next to it is the indoor gym and there is also a handy drinks vending machine and ice machine.
I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great time in Boston!”
text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel 140 for two nights while visiting the Boston area and the location was awesome. You literally walk out of the hotel and are within walking distance of restaurants, sight-seeing and shopping. The room wasn't huge but has a neat city vibe and I thought the price was right. Parking is expensive no matter what, but the hotel discounts the nightly rate for you, I believe we paid $23 for every 24 hours our car was kept in the garage. The hotel is also about a 5 minute walk from the 'T' station which we took everywhere that wasn't in walking distance so there was no need to take out the car. Oh, and everyone at the front desk was very nice, polite and helpful.

title: “Great location in the Galleria”
text: If shopping is your objective, this is a great property. I stayed here one night for a conference and thought it had a super location in the Galleria mall. The front desk staff was wonderful -- very helpful, fast and friendly. Having some of the meeting rooms actually across the mall was a little strange. Additionally, the elevators were more than frustrating. I don't know if some were out of order or what, but they were excrutiatingly slow to arrive. I also did not find the pillows and bed heavenly or whatever Westin calls them now. And as with so many hotels recently, the shower was lacking. I wish hotels would simply opt for one adjustable shower head with good pressure. However, this is a great hotel for a shopping trip to Houston -- plenty of great places to shop and eat. Nice conference location for the same reasons.

title: “Find somewhere better”
text: I would not recomend this hotel unless travelling alone as our room was far to small for a couple and our friends were the same. Bath room small also. There was nowhere to put anything .I expect if we paid more it would be a different story.We have all been in many hotels over the years and this was probably the worst for space. The only plus was it is very central. Thank goodness it was only for 4 nights.

title: “Consistent quality of a Marriott chain, service of a "Beverly Hills" hotel”
text: This hotel was everything I come to expect from a Courtyard/Marrott chain hotel. The piece that stood out to me was the valet parking service; they were outstanding! Location is nicely situated with easy access to interstates, Beverly Hills, Century City and a quick drive to Hollywood.

title: “Good place for a layover”
text:
Stayed one night. Shutter service was complimentary. Overall, a good place for a night stay. However, serivce from housekeeping was not very nice. The guy who brought us the rollaway bed, left without helping to set up the bed. When asked to do so, he got impatient and was quite rude. Tiny bathroom but adequate. 
Front desk guy was quite nice to throw in a free breakfast for the 3rd pax. 
I'll come back if I need a place to sleep to catch my next flight. This was more pleasant than my stay at another property in the LAX area.

title: “Fabulous gem, Great location!”
text:
Went to the city for the first time. We were nervous because we booked the hotel over Priceline. This hotel is a fabulous hidden gem. There is an outstanding Italian Restaurant Vice/Versa across the street. It is within walking distance to every major attraction that New York has to offer. We were able to walk to the theater at night. We also did the hop on/off grayline bus tour. We would highly recommend this tour if you only have a short time to explore the city.
The hotel rooms were small, but more than adequate. They have incredible toiletries from Austrailia. All and all it was an amazing experience!

title: “Great Location”
text: The location of the hotel was great, staff very nice, room was nice with the exception of the shower, some mold on tiles and vent very dirty. The location of the room was not ideal, on busy street and nosiy

title: “TINY rooms, Huge service, Convenient and Cozy.”
text: I stayed here for two separate nights mid January 2011. One night in room 21 and one night in room 65. Both rooms were 'ballet suites' and VERY TINY! I wondered how in the world the staff put in a queen sized beds in these rooms. There wasn't a desk to put the lap top on(no room) and when I spent a few hours in my rooms, I felt a bit claustrophobic. I picked this hotel because of location and convenience for what I was here for and overall have very much enjoyed my stay. The bed was very comfortable, staff is extremely friendly and helpful, breakfast is cozy and I'd compare this hotel's feelings to a hotel you might find in Europe. This is a good place to stay, I will be coming back.

title: “Location, Location, Location!!!”
text: The Hotel Harrington was a great place to stay. It was so close to all of the sites. You can book a tour right from the hotel gift shop. We had a family room and it had four very large beds for six people at a very reasonable rate.

title: “Couldn't wait to leave.”
text:
I stayed there in September. The bed was hard as a rock. It was like sleeping on planks of wood. The only saving grace is that my room had a lovely view of the Space Needle. I pre-booked and paid for two nights, but was so fed-up and disappointed that I left a day early. They wouldn't give me my money back for the unused second night. They said that I would have to do that when I returned back to Australia.
I was also disappointed and extremely surprised that they didn't have Room Service.

title: “Our home away from home!”
text:
We have stayed at many of the 'Grand Dames' hotels in NYC over the past 20 years, and wonder why it took us so long to discover The Elysee Hotel. Is it the best kept secret in hospitality in the city? As the hotel is generally fully booked, it looks like the secret is out!
What makes this hotel stand out? It doesn't have pzazz, it doesn't do shoe cleaning. It doesn't even have large bathrooms, in fact they are quite small, but then we don't live in our bathrooms! It can suffer from outside noise, as commented on by others. We certainly did enjoy the unique ambience of the Club Room, with its great complimentary breakfasts and convivial evening wine and appetisers, before going out to dinner.
So what does make this hotel special? Well you have to experience the genuine help from all staff, from doormen to the highly commited manager, John Avina. Nothing is too much trouble, and the response to a comment on the linen was honest and immediate. We were more than impressed, and the small problem did not re-occur.
So for position, comfort, value and above all service, we have indeed found our home from home in NYC, and as a previous commentator mentions, a little bit of England with a French name!
Dr & Mrs Lando

title: “Not up to Par”
text:
The hotel is in a great neighborhood location. The rooms are nice but at the price charged they should be. We found the staff not very helpful (taxis not ordered, parking not explained, etc.) The continentail breakfast is not as good as ones I've had in Days Inn on the road and everything is served in styrofoam with plastic utensils - find for an overnight place on the road but not what one would expect from a hotel trying to imitate a fine english hotel.
I think there are definitely better values and I would not stay at this hotel again nor recommend it. A luxury price should equal a luxury experience rather than just an ordinary stay.

title: “Started out a good stay, but check your sheets and mattress.”
text: Check your sheets, I went to the front desk twice asking for clean sheets for my bed. Upon changing the sheets myself, I notice the mattress had some bad stains on it. It was brought to the attention of the front desk and was told it was water damage even though the stains were red. My concern was brushed aside. A follow up email was sent and has never been acknowledged by the local hotel. However, cooperate did acknowledge their email quickly. Still to this date, the local hotel had not had the courtesy to respond with a mere "We're sorry."

title: “I wish I could always stay here”
text: Sitting in the lobby of the hotel, right on top of the sound, feels like sitting on a luxury cruise ship. We had a great evening, sitting there by the enormous fireplace, playing the available board games, and watching the sun set over the Olympic Mountains and Puget Sound.

title: “Loved this Hotel!”
text: It's been a long while since we've stayed at a Holiday Inn because we felt the chain had deteriorated. However, on a recent trip to Jax to visit family, this newer hotel was just a couple of blocks away & the reviews were great. It's now our choice of lodging for all future trips to Jax, I'm happy to say. Lovely lobby, the rooms were tastefully decorated & very clean, quiet & very comfortable beds. Nice breakfast area with small buffet, but you can also from a menu if you desire, though I wasn't aware of that until our last day there. Ample parking, outdoor pool. Bar area in lobby to relax in after a long drive. Free wifi. Highly recommend this hotel, and we are very picky! Usually stay at more expensive hotels, but this was a gem for the money.

title: “Won't stay here again!!!”
text: Our experience at the Hilton was not so great. We made our reservation back in April which at that time it was the Wyndham. I made the reservation directly through the Wyndham website and become a member of "Wyndham by request" which gave me certain perks such as a snack and drink on arrival, free internet, free local calls and long distance calls, plus 500 frequent flyer miles. I booked the room as a DELUXE two bed room, 460 square feet.......Well, when we arrived, if not for a very nice person from Boston to help us out, we wouldn't have found the hotel because it was now a HILTON. I was never notified in anyway of such a change. We were first given a room so tiny that you could barely squeeze past the 2 double beds. THIS WAS NOT A 460 square foot room! We had a family of 5!! This was all stated on my reservation confirmation print-out which luckily I had with us. The front desk argued with us in giving us a larger room and stated that there would be an extra $75 charge per night for the larger room. We argued right back and were willing to go to the room and measure it to see that it indeed was NOT 460 square feet---we estimated it at being approximately 250 square feet and that's being generous. We could never get a roll away bed in there for our third child. FINALLY, after the front desk person belittled me a bit by saying that 'most people--98%, who are not in the travel industry do not know how to book rooms properly over the internet and this was bascially my fault', we were given a suite which had plenty of room for our family at no additional charge. Also, we were NOT given the "perks" I mentioned earlier. This was not the greatest way to start out our visit to Boston and I personally will not stay at a Hilton ever again. I would like to say to this front desk person---if so many people are inept at making reservations over the internet---then why offer this service? This was the first time I ever had problems with a reservation on line and I have done it plenty of times!

title: “Classy and convenient”
text: The view from the rooms is terrific; the front desk handled checkin, messages and check out quickly and flawlessly. The hotel reflects New York's glitz and edginess while the rooms are serene and comfortable. If only the elevators came more quickly.

title: “Lots of character and great location but could do with refinement”
text:
I stayed here for six nights in March whilst attending a conference. The Figueroa is ideally situated for downtown/LA Live and is better value than some of the newer, plusher hotels. However, the shabby chic des sometimes leave a little to be desired such as singe pane windows that don't eliminate traffic noise or draughts and a heater/air conditioning unit that sounds like a small jet aircraft. 
My room was a good size with a huge bed, just wish it had been more recently refurbished to add a bit more comfort. Having said that, I'd probably stay here again if visiting LA.

title: “Another good LaQuinta Hotel”
text: Excellent location near the Baylor Medical Center. Room was clean and well lit. Many restaurants within walking distance. Will stay here again.

title: “Great location, price and service. What more could you ask for?”
text: We got this hotel through Hotwire and paid $83 per night. We arrived at 7am to the hotel where they gave us both our rooms right away. They also allowed us a late check out for one of our rooms. I would say this is a typical NYC hotel, older and small but it is in a great location! You are a block from a bigger subway station on the red line which takes you right into lower Manhattan. There is a great Corner deli that has more food options then you can imagine. We ate there every morning and the prices were great. I would stay here every time we go to NYC!! Can't wait to go back!

title: “Belnord - not the Ritz, but doesn't pretend to be”
text: I stayed at the Belnord one night. It was cheap for NY so I didn't expect 5 star accommodation. It's true the room was minuscule, the aircon growled and burped all night, and the bathroom was down the hall. But my bed was comfortable and clean, and the hotel staff gave useful advice when I needed it. A porter carried some of my stuff up to the 4th floor. While I wouldn't want to commit myself to a lifetime at the Belnord, I thought it gave me basically what I needed, a roof over my head and clean bed-linen

title: “Poor Delivery!”
text:
Overpriced, Attitude and for what ???
Go accross the street to the Monaco or back to the "W"
The Clift is all wrong.

title: “Wonderful hotel with wonderful staff”
text:
I chose the Hilton Garden Inn on 35th Street because of its great reviews on Trip Advisor and because of its proximity to Penn Station (oh, and the room rate, which was less than most other hotels in the city). My teenagers and I arrived at Penn Station via Amtrak around 10:30 am on a Monday. We walked the short couple of blocks (bags in-tow) to the Hilton Garden Inn. We found the hotel easily and walked into its small (but clean and inviting) lobby. Ryan at the front desk greeted me warmly and checked me in for our stay. Despite the early time, our room was available and we were allowed to go up to it immediately. Ryan had placed us on the 19th floor with a view of the Empire State building out our window (yay!). The room and bathroom were very clean and we were very pleased with the accommodations. At night, the room was very quiet.
Prior to leaving for our excursion out into the city, we stopped by the concierge stand in the lobby. Andrew was a great help in getting us oriented and helping us find where we wanted to go. He was a great resource every time we entered or left the building, as I asked him questions whenever we passed by.
We stayed one night, but our return train was not until late afternoon the day of checkout. I checked out around 10:30 am, and Ryan, once again, was wonderful to deal with. He joked with me, asked about our stay, and explained that the hotel would gladly hold our bags (for free) while we enjoyed the city for a few more hours. We returned at 4 pm to collect our bags and walk back to Penn Station. There were warm cookies and iced lemon water in the lobby when we returned, and despite having checked out, we were invited to help ourselves to the refreshments. We also used the restrooms downstairs by the fitness center to wash up prior to leaving. Those bathrooms were spotless and well-stocked.
Overall, we had a wonderful stay at the Hilton Garden Inn on 35th street, and I would like to give special kudos to Ryan and Andrew for treating us so well. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Nonrefundable deposit - beware”
text:
I booked a room online in January for a July stay. I wanted to cancel 3 months prior to July, but Hyatt charges $50 to cancel. They would not even let me transfer my payment to another Hyatt. No other hotel I deal with (major or minor) has this policy. Most hotels will allow cancellation outside 72 hours.
Beware of this before you book online.

title: “Management policies corrode otherwise great hotel.”
text:
Management policies at the St. Francis Hotel in San Francisco have corroded a great hotel. The high rooms in the modern wing with great views are worth the $300 base rate. The hotel has ambiance, history, and the best location in the city. But our most recent stay -- our third over a span of four years -- will be our last.
Security takes precedence over guest service. One morning my wife sought out the maid on our floor to give her a tip and tell her when the room would be vacant for her to clean. After briefly returning to the room, my wife walked out, realized that her sunglasses were left behind, tried to reenter the room, and found that her card key no longer worked. She asked the same maid that she had just tipped to let her into the room. The maid responded by saying that “I’ll have to call security.” 
My wife met me in the lobby, and jointly we found a room clerk -- who would not recode by wife’s keycard without a picture ID. My wife got her new card because I showed a picture ID. The room clerk pointed out that my wife’s handbag had a magnet clasp which was the reason that her keycard lost its code. Maybe the keycards at the St. Francis are overly sensitive because they are designed for multiple recoding; the magnetic clasps on my wife’s purses do not affect credit cards. (If a women traveling alone leaves her purse in a room, one wonders what the procedure would be for new keycard.) 
Cutbacks in labor and service are justified by being “green”. On the bedside table was a green card titled “make a green choice” and the following text:
You have the option to decline housekeeping service for the day. For helping us conserve natural resources, we are happy to offer you a $5 gift card for use at participating food and beverage outlets with our hotel or 500 “Starpoints” redeemable at checkout. 
decide to decline. Simply hang this card on the door before 2 am to decline housekeeping. Program not offered on your day of departure.
refresh you room. Please place this card on your bed for fresh linens and leave towels on the floor that you want cleaned.
Note the default: if the guest leaves the card on the bedside table, the maid cleans the room but does not change the bed linen. This of course flips the common practice whereby guests can put a card on the bed if they are willing to go without fresh linen.
For insults to guests, this take the prize. In a $300 room, the hotel hands out a $5 discount at the coffee bar. No doubt enough people take up the hotel’s offer so that the housekeeping staff can be reduced, and two or three maids can join the ranks of the unemployed. The accountants must have calculated that the $5 is less than the direct labor cost of cleaning one room. Hiding behind green virtue is disgusting.

title: “Worst Experience Ever”
text:
My wife and I decided to book at Motel 6 to save a little money. We will never do so again! I left my cell phone turned on and sitting on the bedside table for several hours as we visited the sites. When we came back, housekeeping had cleaned the room and the phone was gone. When I called my number I found that the phone had been turned off. The maid stole my phone. The only response from the front desk was, "Wow. That sucks." Do yourself a favor and avoid this motel!
I also prepaid for WIFI, but the only way I was able to use it was by taking my laptop to the lobby since the room we were in could not get a signal.
One more thing: When housekeeping brought new towels, we found hair on them.

title: “Spa Chakra @ Conrad....GREAT!”
text: Escape in the city of Indianapolis at Spa Chakra at the Conrad! First class spa with first class staff, products, fitness area and pool. No need to travel out west or Chicago seeking the ultimate spa treatments or therapies. I highly recommend the 90 minute massage, 2 hour hydrating body wrap with vichy shower, and a facial! Top off your day spa experience with an overnight at the Conrad. In-room dining had limited food options but the bed was amazing with fluffly pillows, comforters and cool 400 count sheets. They do need cd players in the room. I could have had a room on a higher floor. I was on the 14th floor with a limited city view. I brought my own dvd's and watched movies, ordered room-service and drank wine during my escape. Breakfast in-room was delicious and fast the next morning. Valet parking was great and the bell man helped me manuever out onto the busy street and on my way the next morning. Also note, the hotel is right across the street from the mall and in close proximity to many restuarants. The Capital Grill is right in the hotel and has great steaks!

title: “Good Hotel”
text: Good little hotel. Staff was very helpful. Room was clean. They upgraded us to a junior suite which was a surprise and very helpful with two children. Central Park is close by and lots of playgrounds for the kids, and musuems are within walking distance. Neighborhood has plenty of good places to eat.

title: “Old World Charm, Convenient Location, and Million Dollar Views”
text: Walking into the Congress is like taking a step back in time. Luxury and old world charm surround you at every turn. Our room was warm and inviting with wonderful linens. Sadly, no frig or microwave, so we had to eat the old fashioned way -- at one of the hotel dining rooms or at close-by restaurants on Michigan Avenue. The views of Lake Michigan, the Buckingham Fountain, and Navy Pier from our room were breathtaking. Nothing will ever compare to watching summer storms over Lake Michigan -- nature's light show. And the light show at the Buckingham Fountain, whether from our room or close up at the fountain were pretty stupendous for a man-made visual feast. Also, this hotel is within easy walking distance of Millennium Park (and the Bean) and the world class art museum, the Art Institute of Chicago.

title: “Good location”
text:
We had a decent stay at the hotel, with sufficient parking lots in the garage. Security was not bad as room card is required to enter the lobby into the lift. Pity our room window faces the wall outside with no view. Pillow was too soft, would prefer to be harder as it would be nicer to sleep with.
Location wise is good, as Mel's Drive-in is just opposite the street, and many shops around the areas.

title: “Exceptional Staff!”
text: We were moving my son to New York to start his new job. My wife surprised us and booked a room at the W, around the corner from his apartment. We have stayed at "W" hotels in the past so I was expecting great service! This location was exceptional! The rooms were very comfortable, yes, they are small, but this is New York! There were three employees that were phenomenal! Dominique, Christine & Kristine. They went above and beyond to accommodate us! We will definitely be back here again soon! Thank you "W" hotel staff!

title: “Older but well maintained”
text: I spent 4 nights at the Double Tree Suites in Foggy Bottom. This is obviously an older hotel but they've done a good job of keeping the rooms modern and nice. The rooms were very clean and comfortable, the kitchenette is outdated but functional and I enjoyed having a big desk/table to work at in the living room. The location is great. It's close to the Metro and walking distance to many historic sites. I felt very comfortable walking at night coming home from tours, one at the White House (I actually took the metro) and the other at the Lincoln Memorial (ended at 9:30pm and felt like about a mile walk) There is a Whole Foods store close by with a good buffet, and TGIF a few blocks away for a quick lunch or dinner.

title: “Great location next to shopping and clean, modern hotel!”
text: We stayed here for two nights. It is located near Union square, great for exploring the city and next to shopping. The hotel was clean and the lobby/check in area was very modern.

title: “Great Value”
text: Stayed 1 night, got great deal off priceline. Very friendly staff and easy airport access

title: “Wonderful Wonderful Wonderful”
text: This was the greatest one night stay in my life. This was my very first trip to NY but because of this hotel, it won't be the last. Everyone was very friendly and the hotel was very modern and clean. I was only there for one night with my teenage daughter and niece. This was a side trip to a college pick up trip for summer break. I had no expectations but was very pleased at what I found. Everyone was so helpful and full of smiles. Jose the bellman always happy to help and gave good info about dinner. But Denise the doorman, where do I begin. If you need information from breakfast spots (Scotty's) to internet usage, he is the man to see. He is the main reason I will return to this hotel and have already told several people about it. The location is great, the price is right and the service is outstanding.

title: “a hidden jewel”
text:
I was advised by a friend to try it out. I have stayed in NY 100 times over the years. By far, this is the best value I've found in the city. Great location, minutes from everything. Helpfull, courteous and knowledgable staff. The room was new, quiet, clean, amazing bed, and had a flatscreen TV. The bathroom was spacious, bright and had a large shower and bath.
The history of the hotel was quite interesting in itself. I was there for a week in early November. I have highly reccomended it to friends and family. 
Overall it was an outstanding gem and will be staying there on my future trips to NYC. The website is also done in the great spirit of NYC. Have fun , live high, and save alot of money.
Mark from Los Angeles.

title: “Ok but not great”
text: I stayed at the Sheraton recently while attending a conference. The proximity to the Convention Center and to Pike Place Market was a plus. The hotel is currently undergoing some renovations so the lobby is small and there was construction noise downstairs - but I couldn't hear the noise from the room. The room itself was fine but smallish. For the price, I have stayed in bigger places but I guess Seattle is expensive. The staff was pleasant but not over friendly.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
Stayed here 2 nights for a work trip. This isn't the closest to the convention center, however if I were to go back for personal reasons I'd stay again. 
The layout of the room makes it feel very spacious and the bathroom is huge with a sepearte shower stall and bath tub. The bedroom has doors which is nice if traveling with family and need privacy. 
The staff is very friendly and room service was good. Everything you expect from a starwood hotel.
There are a lot of great hotels all within a few blocks, but again I'd go back.
Try The Fish Market for dinner. Excellent seafood.

title: “Glad I got a good deal”
text:
Just returned from a two night stay. I booked two rooms for my family of four, which is really required because hotel rooms in NYC tend to be small and these were no exception. We got an excellent rate on Orbitz, something like $220 per room, so my complaints - to follow- are to be taken in the context that I would be alot unhappier if I'd paid the full rack rate.
First, all the reviews that mention the two small elevators are correct - it is a hassle and the elevators are tight, something I really don't like. It's an old building and the hallways are rather narrow, so if you are used to the major hotel chains, it will feel somewhat tight.
The rooms themselves were spotlessly clean, with well appointed bathrooms. However we had a lot of problems with the roman-type shades, which wouldn't roll up and weren't fixed, despite my complaint. I also had a lot of problem with the keys not working and needing several replacement. One of the rooms was as hot as a sauna, despite adjustments to the thermostat which I would say was broken. 
Despite the other reviews here, we had no problem at all with noise, maybe because we had rooms at the back that overlooked airshafts - OK with me, if the tradeoff is the quiet. If noise is a problem for you, then make sure you get a room away form the street. The hotel is in a really convenient mid town location and the tradeoff for that is of course, the noise.
The staff were all nice and helpful - no problems there at all. We had a decent stay, but as the title says, I'm glad I got a good deal because I wouldn't have been happy if I had paid a lot more.

title: “$18 PARKING PER NIGHT!”
text:
From the outside, Dana on Mission Bay looks beautiful. It is by the seaside, near Seaworld, and even the front desk looks inviting. 
On the inside, the rooms are small and no different than a room of a 3 star motel. We had something stolen from our room, but we couldn't prove it, so we weren't able to do anything about it. Overall, we were very disappointed with this place, because we read the reviews and expected more.
The $18/night parking fee is a complete rip-off and if you add that onto your nightly rate, I know you can find a much better place to stay.

title: “Tourist heaven”
text:
Make no bones about it - if you are staying near Fishermans Wharf you are a tourist; so why not just behave like one?
This hotel has comfortable rooms with all appropriate facilities; It even gives guests free wine each evening at a drinks reception - just tip the barman a dollar each time you go up to collect a round.
Free biscotti's and coffee in the mornings are also awaiting you, and you're just moments away from a shedload of tourist attractions, bars and restaurants.
Their own restaurant is excellent, the waiters are excellent, and even though the barman was a pompous beggar, a few words in his shell-like soon reminded him who was paying his wages. After that he was excellent.
If you are in SF for fun, it may as well start at your hotel.

title: “good and bad about this hotel”
text: we arrived on nov 28th at hgi,the plus sides were fantastic location-take a left out of hotel and a left again and youre right in the heart of times square.the adjoining restaurant served good food but there was better to be had at the olympic diner opposite the hotel.minus points were-intermittant hot water,the heating pipes banged continuously as if someone was knocking on a door-which by the way i looked out several times to see who it was before finally realising what it was.and the hotel seems to have been built directly on top of the subway which vibrated in the rooms (even though i was on the 6th floor)-and yes the sirens and horn blowing in cars were constant but then thats what i went for-to enjoy the real new york and oh boy i did,i probably wouldn't stay at the hotel again the carpets were stained and peeling wall paper and could do with an overhaul.

title: “Loved Everything about the Inn at Union Square”
text: Just got back with my 12 year old daughter from SF and stayed for 4 nights at this wonderful Inn. Everyone did a wonderful job making us feel cared for and welcome....and safe. I really can't say enough good things about the place. First, the staff is fabulous. A special thanks to darling Ann at the front desk who could not have done more to help in every way. And, David, who we never met because he works the night shift.; but, who offered so much helpful information and enthusiam by phone before we even arrived. The location is perfect and because I am a very light sleeper I asked for a quiet room. We were in #406 in the back and we never heard a sound. The place is beautifully maintained and even thought the room was SF size we still had plenty of room. In the morning, included in the price, they served a huge breakfast buffet...juice, pastry, bagels, cereals, eggs, fruits, tea, coffee, etc. In the evening wine and cheese, fruit, etc. About 2 weeks before we arrived I mentioned I was allergic to down pillows and they even remembered and had great foam pillows waiting. Also, business center with computer at no additional charge. Loved the place and the people. They sure helped make our visit special!

title: “old school hotel”
text:
we had a great time at the fairmont, we decided to upgrade to the tower room over looking alcatraz and what a veiw it cost $60 per night extra.
the bed was comfortable queen size triple sheeting, turn down service had to be requested by ringing house keeping. The bathroom was nice and separate shower, toiletries were of there own make shampoo conditioner body lotion and soap, no little extras like cotton wool nail files ect.
the staff we found were very nice and helpfull, the hotel itself was of the old school which i liked, yes its at the top of nob hill but i would say its one of the best, we walked to sears restarant for breakfast which i would recomend near union square, but get a taxi back up the hill its about $5.
we had a pot of coffee the first morning delivered to our room then i discovered a little coffee take out down stairs near the tonga room a bit like starbucks. have fun.

title: “DILAPIDATED and TIRED”
text: I've stayed at the Clarendon the last two years and have to say the property looked sad and more run down on my most recent trip. I arrived to a mix up with my reservation so I begin my stay on a bad note. I reserved two beds and had evidence of that fact with my my confirmation but because they were running full I was supposed to be appeased by a category upgrade with one bed. Not good. In addition, I was checked in to a room with a moldy, gross shower curtain. I of course addressed all my concerns with the Owner/GM Ben Bethel he apologized and made the usual excuses for his inadeuqate staff with a useless explanation of hirings/firings etc. He did however offer a comp night stay upon my return to the Phoenix area. When I did reach out to Ben to take advantage of his offer to "right the wrong" he never resopnded. GREAT FOLLOW UP Mr. Bethel! Needless to say ,I will never stay at the Clarendon again. I travel to the Phoenix area quarterly and have already found a great Midtown replacement.

title: “Perfect location. Amazing room!”
text: We were "downgraded" from the Westin due to overbooking so I thought this new hotel would be less than stellar. I was absolutely amazed! Our room was phenomenal. Two walls of windows with a spectacular view. Perfect for a NYE stay!!

title: “Amazing hotel in perfect location! Minus the puke filled elevator!”
text:
To begin, I travel quite extensively for business and pleasure. This hotel is perfect for both types of travel. 
Rooms: The rooms are beautifully laid out with very comfortable beds and roomy bathrooms. Our room overlooked the river with no obstructions on the 25th floor. If you can request a river front room I would strongly recommend that option.
Food: There are many places to eat in this city. We went to an AMAZING Argentine restaurant near Wrigley. It was called Tango Sur[--]
The food was right on the money for Argentine taste and the atmosphere is great! Remember to bring your own alcohol is you go because they do not have a liquor license. There is a CVS down the street, which, oddly to our surprise, was well stocked. 
A great French restaurant is Avec, [--] Chicago. This is a different type of restaurant, but well worth the slightly higher prices. They have an amazing sparkling rose' wine. They will recommend you order slowly-take this advice! You will be surprised how quickly you fill up.
Brazilian Steak House Restaurant - Fogo De Chao, [--] Chicago [--]is a must!
Hotel Service: Room service was prompt, coffee was great, fruit plate was fresh, and muffins were tastey. A bit pricey, but expected by a Marriott hotel.
Recommendation: If you can go during baseball season make sure to go to a game at Wrigley Field. It is always a good time and you will enjoy it with tremendous pleasure.
Flaw: We were there the 4th of July weekend, so it was busy as expected. On one of the nights we arrived back to the hotel at around 12midnight and as we began to walk into the elevator we were hit in the face with the rancid smell of puke. Someone had thrown up quite extensively in the elevator and no one had cleaned it up yet. I am unsure how long it was in there, but it covered the entire elevator. It was horrible and I would never expect something like this from a Marriott hotel. So, this was our discouraging moment of the trip.
Also, the pool is very, very small. As is the work out facilities. If you get stuck inside due to rain (as we did for a day) the pool will be packed with people (only about 12 people fit in the pool area). If you think it may rain bring some videos to watch.

title: “Superb!”
text: Just returned to the UK from a 5 night stay at The Lenox staying in a Junior Suite. The hotel, the room, the staff, the location, the food, the bar (an Irish Pub) were all Superb! The staff throughout the hotel were all very helpful, polite and courteous and they all understood my english accent (Most Bostonians struggled to understand me even though I come from Wiltshire and really haven't got a strong accent. One or two people remarked that I spoke very old fashioned english!) Our arrival and booking into the hotel from the moment we stepped out of the cab was swift and very professsional. The valets moved with almost military prescison. The reception staff and concierge were perhaps the best I ever encountered. The room and the beds were perfect and the maids kept the room very clean and tidy. Cab fares to from Logan are very reasonable and perhaps present the most stress free option even though the price arriving at the Lenox was more expensive that the departure. $28 arriving and $19 departing. Both journeys free of traffic. The hotel is centrally located and in easy reach of excellent restaurants and shops. The Prudential shopping Mall and Newbury Street (more shops!) are minutes away. Copley square and the "T" rail transport link are also minutes away. I loved the hotel and location. I recomend the Union Oyster bar. The lady that served us was a little gem of a person and certainly an ambassador for the city. Fenway Park isn't that far way and is definately worth a visit. The people that run the stadium tours were very friendly and helpful. Salme isn't that away and is also worth a visit. We frequently have short stays in the States. Visiting as many cities and States as we can. We love the US and the people. Boston itself is a great city though I did originally think that perhaps New Yorkers were the least friendliest but I now think in general Bostionians win hands down. I lost count the amount times I was reminded how little England was how the Colonists booted us oppressors out. Obviously the Mel Gibson's film Partiot is taken as gospel here. I love history and Boston has it by the ton. The only thing is its presented very, very inacurately. Overall the hotel and staff were brilliant and I fully recommend it. Boston's architure, shops, restaurants and culture is wonderful. Just be prepared, if you're English, to hear the same old tired comments and jibes that wears a bit thin after a while.

title: “Will stay here again!”
text:
I've been to many hotels in and around Columbus, but this one by far is the best one!
The hallway was smelling literally of roses the entire time I was there. No smoke smell except for the last day when the cleaning person came through....for some reason I could faintly smell smoke but it was hardly noticeable.
The pool was lovely, the room was lovely. Marble in the bathroom, fresh smelling linens, clean bathtub, sink and toilet, not a spot anywhere in the room. 
In the hallway there was a rather large white stain of some sort a few rooms down from mine, but nothing that got in the way.
TV reception was alright, the TV itself was perfect, SUPER fast internet, was able to watch netflix on my downtime with no problems. 
Not too bad of a drive to downtown, whether you go up I-270 to I-70, or you take W Broad all the way to downtown...either way the drive is manageable and you can't go wrong. There's also several COTA bus stops around the hotel so public transportation downtown is good, too.
I've been to several hotels and this one by far is the best one!

title: “Great place to party, poor place to stay.”
text:
We stayed at the Public Hotel in Chicago for three nights over Labor Day Weekend. The positives were that the location was just two blocks from Lake Michigan and six blocks from a Red Line stop. It was only two blocks from many restaurants, bars, and shopping opportunities. There was public parking across the street. The hotel itself has a very popular bar and restaurant which was packed every night we were there. Great place to hang out if you want to see and be seen. The hotel offers bicycles which you can borrow for free. Wireless wifi is included with each room. Their service was fast and friendly. Check-in and check-out was a breeze. When we called down about a light bulb which had burned out, facilities was there within minutes to replace it. 
The negatives were that the pillows were flat and offered no support. The rooms are small. There are no drawers to store your belongings. The bathroom is tiny. I’m not a large guy but when using the toilet, one leg was pressed against the sink and the other against the door frame. I’m not sure really large people would actually be able to sit down. There was no sheet between the comforter and us while sleeping so be prepared to turn down the thermostat so you can keep the comforter on OR turn up the thermostat so you can sleep completely exposed. Speaking of the air-conditioning/heater, if the window curtain is closed, it completely covers the vent. So if you want to feel the heat or the cold you have to leave the curtain open. There is no fan in the bathroom so if you shut the door while showering, the mirror will fog up. Perhaps most annoying was that there was no coffee in the room and it was $3.75 for a cup of black coffee at the bar.
For downtown Chicago this was not a bad price. There’s definitely a happening vibe with lots of people hanging out if the evenings. However there were enough idiosyncrasies about the room that I would look elsewhere for a place to stay.

title: “Don't get blinded by The King”
text:
If you want to see Graceland, of course you want to stay at the Heartbreak Hotel, right?
The hotel is located next to Graceland, so there is no need for travelling by car. The hotel is old and way below average. It is in very poor condition and does not raise any Elvis spirit or offer anything that The King lived and what kind of things he preferred. The Elvis thing inside the hotel is Elvis pictures all over and a souvenir shop that offers the usual Elvis souvenirs.
Rooms are quite spacious, not in very good condition and the air condition makes more noise that is needed. Even in the lowest fan speed it is very noisy.
Breakfast is poor, very poor. It is a below average continental breakfast. With this price level you would expect some Elvis favourites or even an image of what he would like for a breakfast.
There are so many ways to improve this hotel to what it should be and those little things would not even cost too much but surely would give the right atmosphere what the guests are looking for. This hotel is shabby below average hotel and offers next to nothing what their guests are willing to pay. But Graceland is there and that might be the only reason why to book this hotel. Of course, stying at the Heartbrake Hotel is kinda cool, but don't expect too much. The Hotel does not offer you any special, but it is surely something that you can brag to your friends =D

title: “Sleek and Convenient”
text: With a sleek and inviting first floor, the Renaissance hotel is a hub of activity while maintaining an intimate feel. The front desk staff offered great service and even allowed us to check in early morning after seeing our wary children. The room was clean and offered a beautiful view of the skyline. The hotel is conveniently located near all major attractions. While parking was a bit pricey, we were able to enter and exit the hotel on multiple occasions with one standard fee that allows parking for up to 30 hours. Bertha's was a quick drive, as well as Faidleys, and the aquarium is within walking distance. Hotel dining was not as extensive as we would have wished but the kids' breakfast meals offered a large quantity for a very small price (under $6.00). This hotel adequately met our expectations; if there were "magical touches" that would offer each guest a sense of the Renaissance trademark, this hotel would be a must visit in MD.

title: “Don't Let The Fancy Name Fool You”
text:
I was in town for the weekend on business and found the hotel to be a marginally average place to stay if you will not be spending a lot of time in the room. I reserved their "deluxe suite" which was quite small (I'd hate to see what the standard room looks like, probably a closet). It was only manageable for a single traveler. The bed was comfortable and the TV had a nice array of channels. 
The bathroom was quite small as well and not built for someone over 5ft6. You cannot close the door without lifting up your knees if you are on the commode. The tub appeared to be stained which wasn't very nice to look at but the shower was nice. I found the heat/ac unit to be rather old and clunky. You cannot do much to control either. There is just a fan option. When I arrived the room was super hot and stuffy. The window only opens 6 inches (to prevent people from jumping since the room is so hot I assume) so it took a while for the room to air out and cool down. 
The front desk staff seemed rather aloof and disinterested in their customers as well. Do not use the vending machines in the hotel, they charge $2.00 for a can of soda!! Instead, take a walk to the Bartels drugstore just a few blocks south of the hotel and purchase beverages and snacks. 
On the bright side, the fabulous Seattle Public Library is right next door and there is decent WiFi in the room.
This hotel is best for those who do not plan on driving since parking is expensive and minimal. One guest was given the incorrect parking instructions and was told he had to pay $87 for parking since the staff told him the wrong complex so beware if you are parking there, make sure you are given directions to the absolute correct complex. Also, Spring Street is a pretty vertical hill so if you are walking there from a Light Rail terminal, stay on 4th or 5th Ave to avoid having to walk up that crazy hill with your luggage. Other than that, it was an okay stay. I would only recommend this hotel if you do not plan on spending much time in the room, aren't brining a car, aren't too picky about temperature, are a single traveler on a budget, or enjoy walking up hills.

title: “Best ever for conventions”
text: There were some 700 very picky people at this hotel for a conference, and every single person I spoke to agreed emphatically that this was the best hotel we have ever experienced for a conference. The location is good, the room was very spacious, and the management clearly knows what guests want. The staff was well trained to respond to guest requests quickly in a courteous manner. All six elevators worked promptly. The hotel was beautiful and clean.; iIt looked new. The convention staff was superb in every way -- responsive, courteous, anticipating our needs. All meetings were on one floor-- a big plus. The food was outstanding, the best I have ever had at a conference. As I was leaving, a kind employee insisted on helping me with my bag. Turns out he was the General Manager. Clearly he is out there among the guests. Now that's good management.

title: “good location but a bit of a dive”
text: a bit of a grubby dive this - cheap for l.a. but did not feel clean. also noisy. wi-fi did not work in our room. in good location though for bars and restaurants in echo park.

title: “alright”
text: alright the rooms could be bigger and beds could be larger and more channels on television

title: “Good for the Budget and an OK location”
text: I went to the city with a co-worker and we split the price of the hotel while we were in town for a convention. For a Saturday night, we both paid $67 which is great considering the location is near Broadway, Times Sq, and a few convention spots. The hotel is easy walking distance from Port Authority and there are some convenient places nearby - an Irish Pub restaurant, a pharmacy, etc. I would recommend this for a brief stay as the rooms are small, the hotel needs a little improvement (it's a well used hotel, so expect some stains, or missing caulking in the bath, etc). We had no problems with bed bugs, noise, internet, etc. I think it's perfect for someone who needs a bed and a bath and wants to explore the city all day! I would return if I needed to.

title: “Quick stay but very nice”
text:
Stayed here for a quick Chicago weekend. Nice hotel extremely nice staff. Very helpful. Great view of the lake and river. 2 blocks to Navy Pier and 2 blocks to the magnificent mile.
Staff was very nice and you felt they genuinely wanted to help you and make sure you had a great time and stay 
Would stay here again in a second.

title: “I'm not sure this place passed inspection”
text:
Firstly, this place is horrible.I wouldn't recommend it to anyway. I'm a college student and I am in no way used to splendor but sheesh.. This place was so old run down, and reeking of a nursing home I hate that it's the place I chose to stay four nights in. The kitchenette is gross and the mini fridge is not sanitary, cold, or packed with pricey goodies. My friend and I took a trip around the corner and bought a bottle of disinfectant spray and two fleece blankets to take the place of the linens they gave us. The undercover was burnt all over with maybe cigarette burns or something else. Honestly I hate it and i would never recommend it... Ever. 
Ps. It is nicely located a block from the Civic Center But the neighborhood is quite sketchy.

title: “Good location, great rooms”
text: Stayed at The Belvedere for a couple of days this past week and I was very pleased with this hotel. The rooms are a decent size for New York because I have stayed at other hotels before and those rooms are a shoe box compared to this one. I had a fridge and sink with microwave and coffee maker which was good. The rooms are clean aswell. The location is great just a couple of blocks from Time Square and Rockafellar Centre. On the corner of 8th Ave. and 48th there is a store with a deli that will make you some sandwiches. All in all the rooms are clean and decent size, and the location is a plus. PS the elevators are slow.

title: “Bravo Marriott Marquis!”
text: My family of four stayed here over Christmas weekend and we loved it! The rooms were surprisingly large with two comfy double beds and a large window with a partial view of times square at no additional charge. The elevator system was simple and we never waited even a minute for one. The staff was very friendly and the location can't be beat if you enjoy times square. My kids loved that Toys R Us is right across the street as well as Good Morning America. The theatres are at your doorstep, as are many great restaurants. We liked Carmines and Ollies Noodles. We walked everywhere except downtown of course, but the subway was only a few blocks away for that. Duane Reades drugstore is also nearby for inexpensive sundry items. The 8th floor has a lounge with amazing views but the drinks are a bit pricy. The only noise we ever heard from our room on the 11th floor was an occasional siren. I would definately stay here again, in fact after seeing in person the location of some of the other hotels, I can't imagine staying anywhere else.

title: “Westin Seattle-don't eat in”
text:
I have loved most of the Westin's I have stayed in & usually prefer Westin's over other hotel chains. They are usually beautiful, are respectful environmentally, have great food and allow dogs, which just makes me smile. 
This Westin is dated. There are attempts at remodeling but there are still the popcorn ceilings, small bathrooms, ugly carpet, the brass/glass lobby, even a polyester-type comforter for the top layer of bedding with a cotton comforter cover over it. It's just not like the down filled comforter covers at the other hotels.
It has a good location in downtown Seattle and great views with a big floor to ceiling windows of Puget Sound.
The worst part of all was the food. I ordered at the lobby restaurant and the food was so unoriginal, bland, unappetizing that I sent 2 things back (which I never do). Thinking that their food sounds like some of the other original plates at the other hotels, I ordered the goat cheese/mushroom pizza. It was the boring pizza you get from a delivery service and it was topped with bleu cheese not goat. Ordered a berry parfait for breakfast and it came in a bowl (not a fountain glass) full of mushy granola mixed with milk-like yogurt, basically like cereal with milk that had been sitting out for a while. I ordered salmon in one evening and it was so chewy. It was served on top of some sweet potato/spinach combo that looked like something in the frozen food section. Not anything like the side of fresh sweet potatoes and spinach that I imagined.
Not a great experience

title: “Wasn't terribly disappointed, but not as good as expected”
text: You can tell the hotel was once something special, but Hilton has really let it slip; especially considering what they're charging. Staff was excellent, but the rooms are ancient - I felt like I was visiting my grandparents house. Hilton desperately needs to pony up and gut the rooms.

title: “Decent downtown Dallas hotel”
text: Stayed here for 2 nights during a conference last week. Smooth check-in process. A rather shaky elevator ride up to the 36th floor. I usually don't like to be up that high but the hotel was full. I figured at least I would have a good view. And I would have, if the window wasn't covered in a thick film of dirt. The room itself seemed very clean. And it's a large room. Good assortment of pillows (as someone with a trick neck this is an important feature). VERY nice cyber-lounge area that connects to the nicer of two bars, a great place to relax. Location seemed safe but any decent restaurant is about a half-mile walk at least. The convention center is a little over a mile walk. If I were to go back for another conference at the CC I would probably look for something closer and also closer to restaurants.

title: “Nice Hotel with great staff...”
text: I was happy with staying at this hotel....stayed for 12 days on business. Warm greeting from the start and that continued each and every day. Front desk staff were always ready to help and for business they were awesome. Made copies I needed, received and sent faxes numerous times..for business purposes this was a plus. The room was nice, clean and comfortable. Recently updated with some renovation still ongoing in the hallways. Breakfast was ok, nothing great but a few hot items available as well as the standard breakfast items for a hotel. The grounds were pretty clean but could use a little attention on a regular basis...dirty tables that stayed dirty for a few days. Location was good for getting around, area is not the best at night but still felt safe on the hotel property. Overall, it was a nice stay and I really appreciated the friendly helpfull front desk staff.

title: “Grand Chicago Weekend”
text: From Dayton, Ohio to Chicago makes a great 3 day weekend road trip - 300 miles with good roads all the way. The Allerton, is a grand old hotel in the perfect location on the Magnificent Mile. Shopping, tourist attractions, the lake, the theatre district and world famous restaurants are all within walking distance. Parking rates are shocking. The lot next to the hotel charged $50 a night. We found it a few blocks away for $35. With our Group-On discount coupon for the hotel we received complimentary glasses of wine on our first night there. For round trip gasoline, hotel, parking, tips and tolls we spent only $150 each. Dining and shopping were luxury extras! All in all, a grand weekend - highly recommended.

title: “Great location, great views”
text: The Ritz is a beautifully historic hotel located in the heart of city center. It's walking distance to shopping, restaurants, historic Philadelphia locations and the convention center. A room facing city hall will give you an amazing close up to the top of the historic building.

title: “Scary”
text: Stayed here with my husband and our six children. They will only give you five wristbands for the pool ...so that sucked. The fact that you need wristbands and a room key card to even be able to use the elevator should tell you about their security issues. And I'm pretty sure there were some unsavory activities happening nearby based on the clientele we saw coming and going.

title: “Excellent stay!”
text: We had a suite for our family of five. The housekeeper introduced herself the first day and made our room home away from home!

title: “Loved the Talbott Hotel!”
text: We stayed at the Talbott for three days in September and really enjoyed it. The room was spacious, not as big as the Drake but not small either. Bed was comfortable, linens nice. The TV was perfect (love to watch in bed late at night!). the restaurant Bice was OK, had better but the service was prompt. My favorite thing was not only the location but you receive a pass to the awesome Equinox Gym in the Bloomingdales mall. That really was the best! Great location in the GOld Coast but I do have one negative: the valet parking is $50.00 a day, we had a mercedes and found out from someone on the street they way they were driving our car when they brought it around! Husband not happy..

title: “Very nice place to stay”
text: We stayed at the Doubletree in Times Square and it was a great place to stay. We had a room on the 29th floor so we were away from the sounds of the city but there was still some very minor noise. Certainly nothing that kept us awake at night. The windows had room darkening shades which were very good at blocking the lights of Times Square. I was exhausted after a day of shopping and sight seeing so I slept like a baby but I did find the bed very soft. I have to say though that my bed at home is memory foam so it's hard to find a bed I'm happy with. I don't feel it's the fault of Doubletree that I have an awesome bed at home that is hard to compete with! This area of the city is VERY crowded but I knew that going in and didn't mind it at all. TS is centrally located to several walkable areas and public transportation is nearby. Every staff member we came across was friendly and helpful. We were taking advantage of Hilton Honors points so we had complimentary breakfast. The dining area was attractive and clean, the wait staff was friendly and attentive, and the food was all very good. We would like to stay in other areas of NYC to experience them better but when we choose to stay in Times Square again we will certainly book at the Doubletree.

title: “Supremely elegant hotel - hidden fees and charges though, parking”
text:
Pros first, cons last.
We booked this hotel through Priceline for a spectacularly low price relative to what Expedia was asking (approx. 1/3). When we got there, we were quickly checked in and experienced nothing but positive and friendly service. The hotel lobby is old world, gilded and worthy of a movie set. My fiance and I took engagement photos in the lobby and the second floor ballrooms and hallways. I would not be exaggerating by stating that the hallways on the second floor look palatial, with china cabinets and porcelain statues and vases on pedestals.
Our rooms were very well appointed, although the carpets are a bit dated. Nonetheless, everything was very clean and daily maid service was perfect. Messages were left for us when we had our "privacy" sign out, turn down service included filling the ice bucket, it couldn't have been more perfect. We heard the next door neighbors literally and figuratively "banging" but otherwise very well insulated from room and street noise.
There is a small, but well-appointed gym, but no pool.
The location is excellent. Less than 2 miles from the airport and right next to the Horton mall one block away. 7-eleven next door as well for snacks and drinks. One issue though, San Diego downtown is a bit sketchy - there are a lot of homeless and bail bonds places right around the corner from 4-5 star hotels like this and the US Grant. We asked the concierge if walking to Little Italy was possible (at 10 pm) and she cheerfully said yes. After 3 blocks, we had to turn back and get the car. The streets became rough and dark with underpasses and highway crossings. I wouldn't do it and she shouldn't have given us the advice.
Now for the bad part - and this is big. Parking now costs $32 per day! And there is no street parking at all in the area (for over 30 minutes). Much of San Diego downtown is like this so you have no choice but to pay.
Next, there is now a Mandatory, HIDDEN $15 room fee! This is over and above your Priceline total. So if you think all you're paying is the Priceline total, you are WRONG! Add $15 to it. The attendant told us that this was a new policy and that it covered wireless internet, 2 bottles of water a day, and a newspaper. We could not opt out of it. This is flat out wrong. People use priceline in order to pre-pay and get a total and fixed cost. What's to stop a hotel from charging $50 extra per night when you show up??? Even if you book this hotel directly from their website, you may miss this extra $15 charge.
Al in all, I tolerated the extra fee and parking charges because the hotel was exquisitely elegant. Plus, we had great service and beautiful engagement photos. If I had paid full price, the ratings would have dipped.

title: “Locaton..location”
text: Very easy check in, and kind staff. The hotel it self is run DOWN, small, and could use a major overhaul. I took my own blow dryer,thank godness because the own in the room was brocken. With that said the location was great, it is in walking distance to fishermans wharf, and union street. Everything is with in arms reach as far as food and places to go. We stayed a total of three nights, and for the price it was worth it. The Hotel did offer a continental breakfast that had coffee and oj, bannans and sweetbread, in the lobby. Next time I might spent a little more money for a better Hotel, but all in all for the price and location you cant go wrong. Parking is tight but free+++....

title: “not bad”
text: good location, 2 min walk to subway, nice staff etc. One of the best beds ever, great linen and very good new towels. Carpet looked dirty. Rooms are not very big. However we were given a room with a connecting door and we could hear everything next door. W felt we had no privacy. we complained but nothing was done as promised. eventually we were offered to move but it would've been 3rd time we were moving during our stay and refused. ...and never eat at the restaurant downstairs Fatty crab...what a rubbish food...and they say it is thai, but having travelled so many times to Asia i would say has nothing to do with asian food.

title: “Excellent”
text: Excellent hotel, moderm bulding, friendly people in reception. Very good location just in front of the John Hancock, Water Tower and Magnificient mille. Rooms are very good, moderm and with everything you need for a business/pleasure trip. Free internet in the business center.

title: “A Fairly pleasing Fairmont”
text:
This was a 6-night stay and while I've been a guest at various Fairmonts in the past, I'm not sure I would call this one luxurious. It's certainly a notch above your standard Hilton, Hyatt, or Marriott, but this particular property i would not call luxurious. If so, then the bar has moved down for the definition of luxurious. 
I stayed on the 8th floor and I was disappointed in the room. I know little about their available inventory (i.e., room types and sizes) so I suspect I had what's called a standard Fairmont room (king) with a city view. The bed was comfortable (yeah!), the bathroom was clean, but the carpet was clearly worn. The room had a tired, lackluster appeal to it. The good news is that there was ample storage space in the dresser - lots of drawers and a good sized closet. And, the room had a small refrigerator, but stuffed with items people never really eat. A note on the desk from management indicated that they were currently installing new TVs so there might be service interruption. That they're just getting around to installing flat screens in late 2012 should tell you something about much money they're putting back into this hotel - not much.
Service by the door men, front desk, and restaurant staff vacillated between good to very good. (On soap-box: I'm sexiest. I think men make the WORST front desk attendants. They're not good at multitasking and the answer is always "no" even before they hear the question. They are, in generally, completely useless. Off soap-box.) The Concierge was another matter. In general, I avoid the Concierge desk because 1) they're usually under-staffed and 2) they generally have poor attitudes, or both! Here, the first Concierge I encountered was short, unfriendly, and unhelpful. The second one was great and I'm sorry I didn't get her name. She was helpful, gracious, friendly, and she smiled.
Housekeeping was perfection! I asked for an extra towel and not only did I get one (I got several), but she left extra towels every day without me asking. Then, I asked for extra tea bags. Did she leave 1 or 2 extra bags each day? No, she left several - every day. Thank you! (The Fairmont Organic English Breakfast is good tea for American tea.)
I'm picky about my breakfast eggs and there were challenges in the restaurant. I never do buffets with its (often) cold, carb-rich, picked over, and over-cooked food (belch) so I ordered from the menu. I had breakfast on 5 consecutive days and it wasn't until the very last day they (finally) correctly prepared the scrambled eggs. Overall, the food was fine (when it was prepared correctly). The mushroom fritta was particularly good.
The gym was fine - it had enough treadmills, decent equipment, and space. The lobby was fine - bright, comfortable, and spacious. The lobby bar is rather small (I think too small) so if you're looking for that type of atmosphere, this isn't the hotel for you. Not being a Fairmont Gold member, I can't comment on the Gold Lounge. Parking was pricey, but given its location, one would have to be naive to think it's going to be inexpensive. Parking is expensive in congested metropolitan cities.
Upon check-out, I asked about the worn carpet in the room. The desk clerk told me that the room had been recently updated. Then, he said that all the rooms had not yet been updated and when I asked about the 8th floor, the answer didn't make any sense. He rambled on about floors 9 and 10 (which are the Gold? floors) and floors 2-7. He never mentioned 8 and when I asked about 8, again, he mentioned 9 and 10. Weird conversation. I just left it alone. :-)
Not a bad hotel; it's somewhere between good to very good, but it's certainly not luxurious. There are several hotels of this type in the area so this isn't the only option.

title: “Awesome Location, Great Value & Friendly Hotel, Highly Recommended”
text: It was my first visit to San Francisco and I stayed here for 5 nights. It was a great experience, the location is very central; walking distances to most of the main attractions, and the room was clean and comes with free internet to use. The manager, Rodel was very helpful in how to go around and about in SF, very handy for a first time traveller. In short, this may not be a luxury 5 star hotel, but the services and cleanliness, and for the price you pay and the location you are in, it just become exceptional

title: “Pre Cruise Short Break”
text:
Our first visit to NY. Reception was slick efficient but above all very friendly and welcoming. Our room on the 30th floor has recently been refurbished. All the furniture was new and the carpets, bedding etc were spotlessly clean. We used the room service on the first night for dinner and it was like a scene fron "Diamonds are Forever" with the waiter bringing a fully dressed dinner table in to the room.
