The trick was watching as the table had to have a leaf dropped to put it out on the corridor after the meal. (We could have called for its removal but wanted to clear away to get some sleep).
The location of this hotel is superb being a relatively short walk from iconic venues such as Central Park, Rockefeller Centre, St Patrick's Cathedral, Broadway and Times Square. For the slighly more energetic Grand Central and the Empire State are walkable but ts only $10 to the Empire State in a taxi.
Subway stations for getting to Lower Manhattan, Brooklyn etc are close by and this really opens up NY.
Breakfast in the hotel was slightly more expensive than in local diners but had the advantage of extensive choice and a leisurely atmosphere. We tried both but preferred the hotel.
Positioned towards the top of 6th Avenue the traffic and pedestrian noise was limited and enabled us to get really good sleep. 
I would not hesitate in staying here again.

title: “Very Good Stay - Recommended”
text:
Stayed at the Hyatt for three nights. When we checked in the front desk staff was very efficient and friendly. Check in was very fast and no wait. We liked the modern style of the room and the bathroom/shower is very nice. Loved the shower head in the roof. The bed was not the best but was ok. The room was clean and was cleaned promptly when we left each day. 
The location is great. Being about two blocks off the main street made it fairly quiet in a very busy, loud district. Easy walk to everything. Several good restaurants close by including the must visit Hollywood Cafe right across the street. 
Highly recommended and we will return. We got a government rate which was exceptional for the area. I searched numerous hotels and actually got the best rate at the Hyatt ($150/nt).

title: “Wonderful Hotel, once again”
text: This was my second time staying at this hotel and I loved it again. Clean, friendly, great rooms and great staff. Ricks cafe is fabulous and offers free breakfast and a nightly wine and cheese evening. The location is great and accessible to everything. I will always choose the Casablanca when I visit New York.

title: “Very adequate hotel”
text: This is a very adequate hotel, just a few miles south of downtown. Nice rooms, pool area, free parking, free internet, free continental breakfast. Nothing excellent, but everything OK. One extra: there are two lobby computers to access the internet free for guests...you can even print your boarding pass for free.

title: “Favorite NYC hotel”
text:
This is the fifth time I have stayed at the Affinia Eastgate Tower hotel. It is not the newest or fanciest hotel, but what I find exceptional are two things; first, the service of its entire staff, and second, the fact that this hotel is a converted apartment building. AND... No Bed Bugs, ever. I have never seen them in the hotel and have never brought them home from the Eastgate or from being in NYC. We take some minor precautions, but this hotel is clean.
My family has seen all the NYC tourist events and places through our various visits. We really like the NYC life style in the neighborhoods. We choose to stay at the Eastgate Tower hotel in the Murray Hill neighborhood to be away from tourists and to live in NYC as if we were residents. Because the Eastgate has spacious rooms, a dining room, two bedrooms (1 king bed and 2 queen beds, and pull out couch), full kitchen including full stove, plates, cups, pan, etc., and two baths we have the space to live as residents. On either end of Eastgates city block is are convenient supermarkets, Gristedes at 39th St and 2nd Ave, and in the other direction the 38th Street market. You can drive into town, leave your car in the hotel garage, bring dry goods and staple groceries from home to stock the kitchen cabinets (NYCgrocery stores are expensive and you can only buy what you can carry, also you DON"T want to eat and pay for medium quality food at franchise touristy restaurants). You can get meats, dairy, and perishables at the markets to stock your fridge.
About the service... you can count on JERRY the doorman, he can get you anything anytime, This hotel has 2nd generation doormen! ANNALISA has been the best housekeeping service personnel during our stay, BETSY at the front desk was superb with registration, and CAROLYN always fulfilled our needs and anticipated them by calling our room one time asking if we needed more towels for our kids. I know I have left out other staff people, but they were just as great. Carolyn did that because she hadn't heard from us, we called that often - and they never complained and didn't seem to mind. They even delivered us a vacuum when we requested it.
We requested that service never come into our room while we were away and they honored that. Not that there is a problem, we just preferred it. We went out of our way to always bag up our towels and linen and place them out the door into the hallway each day. We also bagged up our garbage and did the same. This made it easy on the hotel staff and assisted our personal preference to not have the room serviced daily. We didn't want hotel service, we just wanted to live and exist as "New Yorkers" in the neighborhood.
Although the hotel provided coffee, we picked up our own coffee at the Dunkin Donuts below the hotel (cheaper than grocery store) and got junior size filters (under $2) at the market. The hotel gave us plenty of kitchen towels, kitchen wash towels, and plenty of dishwasher soap tablets. It was very easy to afford to eat in the hotel with a kitchen and the supplies we brought with us and was given by the hotel. Much less expensive than eating around town, but do plan to treat yourself out now and then and have at least one real good meal out somewhere. Many great pizza places, ask around, many great suggestions. Always check food network website site for ideas for diner, lunch, snacks ,etc, NYC is full of great foods.
At Eastgate you are a 10 minute walk to Grand Central Terminal, 15-20 minutes to Times Square, about 15 minutes to the Empire State Building, and there are many restaurants on 3rd avenue. Try Dukes and above that El Rio Grande (Texas on one side, Mexican on the other, and you can "cross the border" by going through the kitchen.) Also try The Hudson and an Organic Burger joint, all on 3rd Avenue between 39th and 32nd.
The best way to learn the city quickly while seeing all the sights is to take the tours on the red buses known as gray line, the hotel can assist you with that. Better yet, buy all tickets for the bus and to sites online for an overall lower cost to enjoy the sites, use the "City Pass".
I could go on and on but you get the idea.... enjoy!!

title: “Luxury of a hotel and the convenience of home”
text:
We were visiting friends in the DC area and doing some sightseeing. The apartment was in a great location close to shops and restaurants and only a short metro ride from the main sightseeing attractions. 
The apartment was spacious, well furnished and had excellent entertainment facilities (plasma TV, cable, WIFI, desktop PC). It was great staying in a place with kitchen facilities rather than having to rely on a minibar, room service and expensive bars/restaurants.
All in all a great experience.

title: “Location / views at least make up for a lot of shortcomings”
text: Huge hotel which hosts big conferences and trade shows. Tired decor and many inconveniences, especially woefully inadequate lifts for the number of guests - up to 10 minutes wait at busy times (walking's not an option to the 44th floor!). Expected far more from a $300+ room - long overdue for a makeover and upgrade, although for a Manhatten hotel it was a decent size (unlike the bathroom). Wifi is only free in the executive lounge/ public areas - resulting in the vast marble lobby areas often being full of even business-suited guests sitting on the floor huddled over laptops and iPads. Fabulous views over the city from exec lounge on 44th floor and the location - 6th and 56th - is convenient for everything.

title: “More like a Westin than a La Quinta”
text: I hadn't stayed at a La Quinta in years, so I was pleasantly surprised to see one so plush. The bedding was extra cushy and cosy, it had a double-head shower, a new flat-screen TV and everything looked new or newly renovated. The breakfast was pretty standard for a hotel, but better than most. Had three kinds of coffee (although none that great), waffles, biscuits and gravy, breakfast burritos and all the other standard fare you'd expect. We were even successful in negotiating the price down, even though it was the week of Christmas and they really didn't have to. I was even impressed by their recycling efforts and delighted to see a Whole Foods right behind the hotel. I'd definitely stay again.

title: “Convenient”
text: Stayed 2 nights here for business. Rooms are good and I had a big room with kitchen and good bed, bathroom,etc... Yes, there is noice outside but that's because you are in the centre of NY and that's why I chose it. Breakfast is a bit on the 'cheap' side and could be improved in terms of choices, etc... It's a small hotel, so small lobby (if any), 2 heavily used elevators (it's high) and narrow corridors.

title: “newyork at christmas”
text: The Pod was a pleasant surprise .I traveled with my 19 year old daughter,she loved the room. It was small, clean and funky.Glad we got the room with private bath. Great location for a midtown Manhattan vacation. We were not in our room for much of the time,sleep ,shower and off we went. Great time to see new york ,all the window decor was amazing ,the rockerfeller tree,saks .Two days of sight seeing great time ,sore feet.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: Stayed here for business on recommendation of a local. Outstanding service, clean rooms, and a great location. Not to mention the reading room with the fireplace was great on a cold, snowy day!

title: “Best Service Ever”
text: My mother and I were in town for a funeral. Flew in late one night and the shuttle picked us up once we landed with no prior notice in just a few minutes time. From the front desk to the maid service were friendly and very helpful! They were conscious of our grief and went the extra mile with every question and request we had. The rooms were clean and the breakfast was tasty as well as hot and plenty of food for us. When we checked out to go back to the airport, they gave us snacks to take with us so we would not be hungry at the hotel. Their thoughtfulness was apparent throughout our entire trip. I would highly recommend anyone staying at this hotel!

title: “Excellent!”
text: Excellent, Fun place to take your family. After you're tired of Sea World, enjoy the pools and water slides. Our 11 year old had a ball. Staff was friendly and it made for a really nice vacation. We would definitely go back! Prices were appropriate.

title: “A Magnificent Stay !”
text: From check in until check out, the service at this hotel was impeccable. The hotel is very centrally located. We were able to check in early and were given a lake view room on the 39th floor. Other hotels in Chicago charge an additional fee for this, but it was complementary at the hotel. The floor to ceiling windows provide an amazing view of the lake/downtown. Being a fitness fanatic, I was pleasantly surprised at the fitness center. It has all the basics needed for a good work out. We will definitely stay at this hotel on our next trip to Chicago !

title: “Tiny but Inexpensive with Great Location”
text:
These rooms are VERY small, like a dorm room with a bathroom. What makes this hotel worthwhile is it's location and the cost; it is half the cost of the next cheapest hotel in the city center, and this location allows you to walk to Boston Common, Copley Square, Theatre district, Fenway, and much much more.
The room was clean; staff friendly; we did not find it noisy but, we travel with a noise cancelling machine.
The shower (no tub) is quirky in that there is NO shelving anywhere to put shampoo, soap, whatever??? The trick, for not flooding the bathroom is to turn the volume all the way down, then adjust the temp, then get in before readjusting the volume.
We stayed at the Hotel 140 two nights and figure we saved over $300 to spend on other aspects of our vacation. We would stay here again.

title: “A great location, OK accomodations”
text:
We booked our stay in October for a New Years weekend. My husband and I have spent New Years eve in Boston for many years and have stayed at several hotels. I chose this hotel because I was interested in something closer to Boston Common and after reading the reviews decided this was a good choice. I also decided to upgrade our room to a Tower queen which I must say was a mistake. The room and bathroom were extremely small which was very disappointing. Also the water temperature in the shower was tricky to regulate since the water knob would slip. So it was either on the cold side or very hot. My last complaint...a $12.50 per 24 hour WiFi fee!! Hotels of lesser quality offer free WiFi.
On the plus side...I will say the staff were friendly and pleasant. 
I'm not one to complain but If I had this to do over I might have requested a room change. This was not what I imagined or expected.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
My daughter in law and I stayed in this hotel for three nights. It is a new hotel and our room was very nice. It had a room with a couch, desk and refrigerator and a separate bedroom area. The beds were very comfortable and the room nice and clean. 
We chose this hotel because it wasn't as expensive as hotels in downtown Columbus but was very close (about a mile) to the arena district. The hotel offered a shuttle, free parking, and continental breakfast. The staff was extremely accommodating and made sure all of our needs were met. We will stay here again next year when we travel to Columbus.
Feel free to PM me if you have further questions.

title: “Really nice”
text: Stayed one night while on business. Beautiful, updated room. Will stay again.

title: “The Celebrity Hotel is a gem”
text:
After reviewing Hollywood hotels on trip adviser, my wife and I chose the Celebrity for a two night stay. If you want clean, comfortable and quiet at a budget price, you should like this. See other reviews for general info. 
We discovered that the Metro subway is a short walk from the Hotel. For the senior rate of 45 cents, each, we rode it one stop away to the bottom of the hill leading to Universal Studios, which provides a free shuttle bus right to the main entrance. The alternative is to drive through crowded traffic to park in Universal's lot for $10.00 or $17.00 to park closer, but not as close as the free shuttle bus will take you.

title: “This hotel has it all”
text: This hotel already has great reviews but their after care service is exceptional ! We stayed in November and had an issue afterwards and I have never known a Hotel to go out of their way to make things right ! So rest assured this Hotel wants to make your stay in NY the best it can possibly be and whilst many places say this, only the Andaz actually mean it !

title: “Small Scale but Elegant”
text:
I attend a Convention annually in Washington and have stayed at a variety of hotels in this area. This year, we are on a budget and so i chose the Comfort inn. Based upon the price, my expectations were for a clean room within walking distance to the Convention Center and not much else.
What a plesant surprise! our company booked 5 rooms and we were thrilled! The decor was beautiful, the rooms were clean, the hotel was quiet and breakfast was very appealing and adequate. I will definitely be back!

title: “Amazing!”
text: This hotel was lovely! The room was spotless and very modern looking. The towels were plush and the robes were great. We loved everything about it. The hotel staff was helpful and friendly. We will definitely stay here again in the future!

title: “Overpriced but nice enough”
text:
We left booking accommodation in San Francisco too late and this was the only place we could find for the lowest possible price (although not that low) that had ok reviews. 
Having been staying in hostels/motels for 3 months, I thought this place was fine and just what we needed. Obviously for the price you are paying, it is not really worth it - but it was the cheapest place we could find.
Saying that, I found that the building itself was nice and the room was fine. Ok, it was a little outdated looking with the patterned wallpaper and carpet - but it was a fine size, it was clean and just what we needed. We stayed there for 3 nights.
Breakfast wasn't great, but was what I was used to from staying in hostels/motels. Coffee/tea, orange juice, toast and hard boiled eggs. There is a little area where you can eat your breakfast which is nice, or there are trays to take it to your room. I did think it was a bit weird though that they don't provide any cutlery or plates - there is only a knife to spread your toast so you end up eating your toast off a napkin. For the room rate and basic breakfast, I think they could at least give you a plate and cutlery!
The location was good for us as its near a bus stop that will take you to all the other main areas/to another stop for a connection elsewhere.
I found the reception staff to be very friendly and helpful - both the lady and man who worked during the day/evening. They let us leave our bags there all day and organised a shuttle bus for us to the airport which made life a lot easier as we had a late flight.
I would recommend booking accommodation in SF early to get somewhere for a decent price, but this place is fine enough if you can't find anything cheaper.

title: “Crowne Plaza Hotel Is awesome”
text: From Check in to Check out, Crowne PLaza staff made it feel as if i was at home. They should include parking for guests who stay at the hotel. But i love the Location thats its a Block away from 16th street mall. And Close to Cherry Creek where i had business. Even the cab drivers they recommend are friendly and most give you a discount. The beds in the room oh my so comfortable. And the room service was above par. I will stay here next time im in Denver.

title: “Great for inexpensive short stay”
text: We stayed here while getting treatment at the Mayo Clinic for a week. The hotel price was less than others located reasonably close to the clinic. The hotel needs an update but it is clean. The rooms are too small with a queen bed. Furniture bumps up against each other. The room gets smaller the longer you stay in it. It located at the intersection of I95 and Butler Hyw. but not so close to be noisy. Unfortunately it is not easy to get to except if traveling S on I95. There is nothing within walking distance but other services are a short a drive away. Basically it is better than a "Motel 6 type" but not as good as a "Courtyard type".

title: “A fabulous Hotel”
text: We stayed here over a July weekend. Absolutely a lovely Hotel, perfect location and great staff. Wish we had been able to stay longer. Walking distance to Quincy Market, Fanueil Hall and the waterfront. Would suggest that you do ask for a quiet room on an upper floor if you are staying during the summer. They gave us beautiful room with a great view of the Marketplace on the 7th floor - just like we asked for. We can't wait to go back again for another stay.

title: “Location”
text: The location was perfect. We were near the muni transportation and the staff was very helpful. The price is high but with walgreens around the corner, we were able to purchase items there to have breakfast in the room for our sleepy children. The beds were very comfortable but it was annoying to have only one sink and the toilet right near it in the bathroom. Our room was near the parking garage so we were away from the noise of the street. If you are traveling with children, i would mention it so you give up a view to get the kids to bed. The city has enough views so we were grateful for a quiet room.

title: “Pretty good value, all told”
text:
Like others, good price & location swung it for us, especially as we were in NYC in the run up to Xmas. Was fully aware of the refurb going on in the lobby at the time so no surprises there. Service at reception was prompt & friendly. A suite converted into a temporary breakfast room during the refurb was adequate, but regularly overcrowded. However I will concur with many other guests on the AC / heaters in the rooms - a tendency to kick in noisily at 3am, waking me up abruptly with the noise and the intolerable heat - during what was a pretty mild spell for December, not a pleasant experience. I barely slept a wink in 3 nights, but hey you don't go to NYC for a good night's sleep! Rooms best described as compact. Bathrooms clean & trendily decorated. 
Really close to Empire State building, short walk to Macey's, Broadway etc... Loads of bars & restaurants nearby means this was a good spot to be for a short stay and worth the 4 point rating for that alone.

title: “A DIVE!”
text:
After reading the reviews (the honest one's, which means any that gave negative reviews) I was expecting this place to be a dive, and it is! Since we were here with a group and only staying for one night, I thought I'd give it a try. The first thing I noticed when I walked through the door was the musty, mildewy and "bug spray like" odor. The small window near the closet doesn't have any curtains so the bright sunlight penetrates into the room and on to the bed. If you like to take naps during the day, stay away from this place!
The room is small, dirty and the bathroom is a joke. My husband just tried to get a tissue and the whole box came out of the wall. There is no bath mat for stepping out onto after the shower, there was hair from the previous patron on the sink.
Yes, there is Bath and Body works toiletries, small and used.....can't they see it's been used and at least try to fill it to the rim?
I don't normally walk barefoot in hotel rooms and this is one you definitely do not want to be without shoes or slippers...I do not even think I can take a shower barefoot!
Granted, I knew going into this that this place would be a dive, but I just do not understand how any of the other reviewers can rave about how great this place is. 
If I ever have to return to San Diego I will stay at a Courtyard Marriott (which I see many of around here) or similar, at the very least.
This place needs to be totally refurbished.

title: “Functional Motel Near Wallingford n Fremont”
text:
We needed a economical place to stay while we found a place to live in Seattle. This worked for us for 5 days. The furnishings and linens ARE OLD but we found the place to be clean. They do have coffee and packaged muffins in the morning. It is convenient to have a small frig and microwave in the room, computer for use in the office, free wifi (we were in a room near the office and it worked great), and laundry facilities on site. The parking is also free which can save you alot in downtown Seattle. You can walk to Wallingford and Fremont which both have groceries, restaurants, entertainment (movies, pubs). We walked during the day and at night, together and solo, and did not feel afraid.
The staff are very helpful. They gave us directions for catching the bus (right up the street) to downtown; the trip took about 10 minutes including stops.

title: “Location is hard to beat”
text:
I stayed here with friends for two nights. This hotel has kind of a 1960s motor hotel theme going on. Our room had two queen beds but was a little cramped. The location and the breakfast were easily the two best features of the hotel. We were only a few blocks from the Space Needle and the Sci-Fi Museum/Experience Music Project. It was an easy walk to the "free zone" for the buses, which allowed us to get to Safeco Field for a Mariners game without driving or paying for a cab. The breakfast was a full hot buffet, with biscuits/gravy, sausage links, etc. Pool looked nice, but we didn't use it.
The parking situation left a lot to be desired. There were no spots left the night we arrived, so I had to park on the street (no charge) and move the car at 8:00 the next morning to avoid feeding the meter or getting a ticket. A tip: Use your keycard to get into the underground garage off of Thomas St. I saw the gate and didn't realize guests could use it until after I'd already found a spot in the regular lot. The desk staff didn't make it clear that it was for guest use.
Internet access was flaky in our room on the third floor near the end of the hall. I tethered with my BlackBerry for most of our stay.
My last complaint is that it cost me $2 to receive (not send) a one-page fax. That can't really be justified in my mind.
I would stay here again.

title: “Nicely renovated older property”
text: Reading the other reviews, I was concerned. Upon arrival, I was pleasently surprised. Now you can tell that this is an older property, but you can tell that they have renovated and updated the rooms. I was on the 11th floor which is the Hilton Honors member floor. The bed is relatively new, nice and comfortable with no sags. Flat screen large televisions with microwave and mini frig. The only slight downside is the small bathroom. This is of course typical of older properties, but well maintained. And the value for the cost of the room compared to neighboring hotels is large. The rate is extremely lower, and I say worth it.

title: “Good value, location and service”
text:
Stayed here for a week on business and was pleasantly surprised after a disappointing arrival which was my only gripe.
The hotel had me in a different room to what I had booked and it was right next to a massive air-con generator which blasted away all night. As I have been travelling ffom the UK and up for 24 hours I was not impressed at all. However I was moved in the morning to an excellent room and not charged for the first night which cheered me up. There was no hassle with this as the management were very easy to deal with.
The rest of the stay was very pleasant; the staff are helpful, friendly and polite.
Breakfast is somewhat basic but is included in the rate so totally acceptable; WiFi is also included in the room rate.
There is no bar but there is a small in-house shop where you can buy from a limited stock of beers, wines, soft drinks, snacks, microwave meals and toiletries.
Location is excellent if you like shopping as it is at the head of St Johns town center which was a good place to browse in free time - great restaurants too.
Overall a good experience.

title: “Great hotel - close to Space Needle and cool bars”
text:
This is a new hotel and still has the new smell to it! The room was spacious and well equipped - a microwave as well as a fridge. The bed was large and comfy, and the bathroom modern, spacious and clean. The hotel has a small pool and gym room - again all new and clean. 
Although this hotel seems far out from the centre of town, it's only a 5 minute walk to the Space Needle and Seattle Centre, and then a couple of minutes on the cheap and reliable monorail into downtown Seattle, which runs until 11pm. We got a cab back from downtown which was very reasonable.
It's also a 10 minute walk to the trendy bars and restaurants on Mercer St - a better bet than downtown for good food and nightlife.
All in all - would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “One Washington Circle: Fabulous Hotel, Great Staff, Incredible Rooms, Perfect Location”
text: In March 2004, my wife and I planned a trip to Washington, DC to attend a leadership conference. Since I hadn't been to DC since I was a kid, we decided to extend the trip and do some sight-seeing as well.After reviewing several Washington hotels, we decided on One Washington Circle (hereby referred to as OWC). We wanted a hotel within walking distance to the National Mall, but also within easy access to a MetroRail stop. OWC provided both of these. It was approximately six blocks down 23rd Street from the Lincoln Memorial / Vietnam Memorial end of the National Mall, and about seven blocks down Pennsylvania Avenue from the White House.In addition, it was only one and a half blocks from the Foggy Bottom/George Washington University stop on the orange and blue lines of the MetroRail, Washington's excellent subway/surface rail system. (The hotel is affiliated with GWU and is adjacent to campus).OWC was also a short walk (about 15 minutes) from the Georgetown area, with its excellent dining and shopping opportunities.Rate: We booked online via expedia and obtained an "Expedia Special Rate" of $179/night for the first two nights, with the third night free. With tax, the total for three nights came to just under $420. Not bad for a three-night stay during spring break, a popular time in DC. The only negative with the Expedia Special Rate program is that you have to pay the entire amount up front at the time of booking.Checking In / The Room: After a harrowing ride from BWI airport (the driver was clueless and easily lost), we arrived at OWC about 1:30 on a Wednesday afternoon. The lobby was very nicely decorated, with modern furniture and a circle motif that carried through to the end tables, wallpaper, and the mirrors on the walls.The desk staff were very friendly, and told us that the room we'd be getting was not the room we'd booked. Instead, they had upgraded us to a 3rd floor suite! Cool!We rode the elevator upstairs. Again, the hallways featured the circle motif, with round mirrors and circles on the carpet. We found our room, tucked into a corner of the floor, and opened the door.And were absolutely blown away. We travel a fair amount, but don't generally stay in suite-class accommodations. This was, by far, the nicest hotel room we've ever stayed in. The door opened up into a short hallway which led into a large living room. This room featured a sofa, easy chair, glass-topped coffee and end tables, a large desk, and a armoire with a 32" TV inside.To the immediate right as you walked in was a small coat closet, and then the suite's kitchen. The kitchen was fully-equipped, with a refrigerator, stove, microwave, dishwasher, coffee maker, and even a coffee grinder!! And yes, the hotel provided fresh coffee beans each day of our visit!Past the TV on the right side of the room was a dining area, complete with a black dining table and six chairs. The table was lit by a funky set of four overhead lights with colored shades.At the far side of both the living and dining rooms, sliding glass doors led out onto a large balcony, easily 25 feet wide. This balcony didn't have a great view, overlooking 23rd and L Streets.To the left of the living room was the entrance to the bedroom. This room featured a king-sized bed, two end tables, a dresser, a 19" TV, and a large closet. The suite's bathroom was connected to the bedroom, and was huge and well-stocked. The shower stall (no tub, unfortunately) was huge.The hotel also offered turn-down service and left chocolate mints on the nightstand each night.Food / Beverage Service: The first night we stayed at OWC, we left the hotel for dinner and a few drinks. As we were walking back to the hotel, we were snowed on, and decided to stop in the hotel's bar, the "Circle Bistro," for a nightcap and to warm up. We were pleasantly surprised to find a wood-burning fireplace in the bar, and spent a couple hours enjoying the atmosphere. The bar was elegantly decorated with comfortable furniture and several little nooks to tuck yourself into for quiet conversation.Drinks were typical hotel prices -- that is to say, expensive. As an example, a martini was $6.50, an Amstel light $6.00! However, while we were there, we noticed advertisements and menus for their happy hour specials, 5-7 PM each day.So two days later, we returned. We only had about an hour before we needed to leave the hotel, and the bartender (same one from two days earlier) was happy to expedite things for us. They had several drink specials, and several happy hour hors d'Ouevres platters for only one dollar each!! My wife and I had a different snack in mind, though. We'd seen, in the hotel room and in the elevator, advertisements for "Chef George's Swiss Fondue."We ordered the fondue, and it came in about 15 minutes, as promised. It was a deliciously creamy Swiss cheese blend, served with cubes of fresh Italian bread and various fruits. Delicious!!We didn't have occasion to eat any other meals from the hotel restaurant, but if the fondue is any indication, the food is superb! The Circle Bistro restaurant serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and also provides room service to hotel guests.Checking Out / Miscellany: Checking out was a breeze, and the hotel staff was happy to hold our luggage for about six hours while we traveled to Arlington National Cemetery and then spent the afternoon in Georgetown. They also arranged for a cab to our next destination when we departed.The hotel provided high-speed Internet access at no charge. Since I had my laptop with me, we simply connected the Ethernet cable provided on the room's desk and were online. For those traveling without laptops, Internet service was also available through the TV set and a wireless keyboard.We had one billing discrepancy that showed up on our account, an $18/day charge for hotel parking, even though we didn't have a car. The hotel staff resolved this, although it took two calls to the front desk.About the only other negative aspect of OWC was its proximity to George Washington University Hospital. Ambulance sirens were quite noticeable during the day and early evening, though neither my wife nor I were bothered by them while sleeping. I can be a fairly light sleeper, so I assume the frequency and/or volume of sirens at night are lessened.All in all though, a fabulous hotel. 100% recommended.

title: “Great hotel, Great location”
text: We just stayed there for 6 nights on our first visit to NYC. There were 4 of us so we booked a 2 bedroom, 1 bath room. Our room had a refrigerator and closet and the other room had the bathroom. The beds were comfortable and the staff was very helpful. There's a subway station 2 blocks away so it was very convenient to get downtown. The location is in a nice neighborhood with many options for dining (Nick's, Manhattan Diner, Ruby Foo's, Europan - to name a few that we enjoyed). The space to the bathroom was a little tight - maybe 12 inches wide from the foot of a bed to the wall. The exercise facility was large. We definitely would stay there again and will recommend this hotel to friends. We also used Gotham Limousine service to get to and from the Newark Airport. Taxes, toll fees and gratuity were all included in the price. The drivers were very professional and the vehicles very clean. We enjoyed this option to a cab.

title: “Good location and very comfortable”
text: I stayed one night while in DC on business. The room was very clean and super comfortable. Service was wonderful -- including the check-in, room service, luggage hold, and check out. Staff were friendly and accommodating. The bed was nice and the room was really quiet too. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Scabies from hell...”
text: We stayed in room 539 and the first night my wife said she felt things crawling on her legs. When we returned home to our dismay we found that we all had contracted scabies as a result of our stay. The hotel staff was incredibly unhelpful! When I contacted the Manager of Operations, Francis, he told me that I could not prove this! Our doctor cited the hotel as the probable source. I have tried corporate recourse but they have not returned my phone call, and I have been unsuccessful. My wife and I have missed work, incurred doctors fees, and are currently taking medication to resolve the infestation. We have gone through copious lengths to prevent further infestation of our home, which has been extremely difficult and time consuming. Scabies is very hard to eradicate, . Whatever you do, save yourself the time money and heartache and do not stay at this hotel!

title: “Best Hotel Ever”
text: We stayed for 7 nights at the fabulous Trump Hotel and Tower to celebrate my 50th birthday and it has been the best birthday I have ever had, We were amazed to find out we had been upgraded to a one bedroomed suite and could not believe the size of the room, it was huge and everything was just perfect, I really liked the birthday cake that was left in our room, the staff were really professsional and courteous and made us feel really special. I would certainly stay here again if we ever return to Chicago and would recommend the hotel to anyone thinking of visiting the Chicago area, its a fantastic location, I could not fault anything, we have stayed at many hotels all over the USA but this one surpasses them all, thanks to everyone who made our stay there a really special occasion and a birthday I will never forget

title: “A Fabulous Stay”
text:
If you are an exercise enthusiast, the Westin offers the best workout facility that I've seen in a hotel. Plus, Sam, the manager of the workout room will put together a program for you and walk you through it. He's amazing.
The hotel is centrally located, close to many restaurants and shopping, making it very walkable.
We had a large corner room facing the river. The service was excellent.

title: “Outstanding Elegance”
text: My boyfriend and I made a trip to Chicago in March for a weekend. I had never been before and wanted to really experience the downtown area. The location of this hotel is excellent. We had a nice view of the river and the busy streets. The inside of the hotel was extremely clean and the staff was very courteous. We received valet parking and someone brought our bags to our room. We decided to tour the downtown area on Saturday but didn't know where to leave our car. Although we had checked out of the hotel already, we were able to leave our car in their parking garage all day. When we returned, we turned in our ticket and the car was brought right to us. This is an outstanding hotel full of elegant features and exceptional staff. I would recommend it to anyone!

title: “We loved the Oasis Water Park & Arts/Crafts for the kids!”
text: Water park doesn't open till 9:30am so arrive a little early to get a good seat in the shade during a Holiday weekend.

title: “Great Hotel!!!”
text: We stayed at this hotel the night before an early morning flight. the front desk staff was very nice, as were the shuttle drivers. The hotel is clean and newly updated or just a new hotel. perfectly placed with the airport very close and not noisy at all!! close to resturants as well. will stay again!!

title: “"Resort" Hotel with Motel Service”
text: This hotel is beautiful. It even smells fabulous. But, I am not at all impressed by the services I received. I was here on business with a convention. Everyone “passes the buck” and seems to have no clue about anything. I asked the valet a simple hotel question and they sent me to the Bellman. I ask the Bellman the same question, they sent me to the Front Desk. I see the Front Desk, they send me to the concierge. The concierge, Ashley was incredibly rude. This was by far the worst encounter I have ever had with anyone, anywhere. She looked up from her computer and replied “I don’t work for the Sheraton, so you would have to ask someone else”. This hotel is beautiful but the service is lack luster. There is no shuttle to downtown and the rooms do not have microwaves or refrigerators either. There is also no free internet in the rooms.

title: “Good hotel but expensive”
text: The J W Marriott hotel product is far better than the usual Marriott experience and this hotel reflects the "premium" end of any Marriott owned property. It's a good hotel with pretty good service throughout, from check-in to departure. My 30th floor KS bed room had a spacious bathroom (big shower/no old tub) and a nice view to the west. I will definitely return after this three night stay on visits to Indianapolis as it's likely the best hotel in town, but take note. It's not cheap. Over $400 a night for a standard room when you add in almost $60 of sales and occupancy tax. If it were $300-$350, I would have given five stars, but what you get (which is definitely good) is a bit overpriced.

title: “Avoid this place!”
text: The hotel is filthy,including the rooms and the smell throughout is terrible.

title: “Great Location, requires some updates”
text:
The location of this hotel couldn't be any better. Right in the thick of the Magnificent Mile. Within reasonable walking distance of Navy Pier if you like walking. Only 2 blocks to the El.
However, in this city with so many options, the rooms really could use some sprucing up. The caulk between the walls and ceiling and windows was peeling off and it made it look pretty skeezy. And what hotel doesn't have a dressing/makeup area outside of the bathroom these days? The room was tight, and didn't have enough outlets either. We could not find enough plugs to plug in our cell phone chargers, coffee maker and hair appliances at the same time. In the age of technology considering the only time travellers can charge up is when they're in the room getting ready to go out for the day, this is a negative by far. I was never more than half charged when we left the room. As a rewards member we were given a free day of internet usage, but again, in this day and age it should be the standard, especially since cell reception in these high rise buildings can be limited. The only way i could receive texts was when i was connected. 
The staff was extremely polite, and attentive. We checked in about 3 hours early with no hassle, we were originally put on the 24th floor and were bumped up to a room with a nice view on 34 just for asking. The hairdryer punked out after i used it for about 5 minutes and they promptly brought me a new one. We didn't use housekeeping so I can't comment on that.
The bar area is nice, and spacious, not nearly as swanky as it looks in the photos though. The area is very brightly lit. The drink prices were insane. We went to fancy restaurants that charged less! Hubby kept wanting to grab a drink on the way out, but I convinced him our money would be better spent elsewhere.
The fitness center was one of the best ones I've seen in a hotel in a long time. Large, with a separate area for cardio and weight lifting. Many machines available to use.
The concierge was extremely attentive. We did self park and checked our bags with the front desk after check out so we could stroll the city for awhile before leaving. They were so quick and effecient. Very chatty and eager to help.
In summary, my thoughts are, you could probably get a nicer room with wi-fi for cheaper or the same cost elsewhere. But the staff was courteous, the rooms were clean and the location was impeccable. We didn't have any noise or issues with water, bed bugs or rudeness. It was a great hotel. I just hope they take our advise and move into 2012!

title: “One night in Boston”
text:
I was traveling through Boston, without a hotel reservation, and was lucky enough to get the last room available at this very nice hotel on a Friday night. I called the hotel directly from the Transit (blue line), after arriving late to Logan airport on a hot and humid August Eve. The clerk at the front desk offered a rate that I thought was a bit high. She asked if I was a AAA member or had any other such affiliations. Fortunately I am a Best Western rewards member. As a member I got a VERY reasonable rate for the night. And it was the very last room available. The hotel was sold out !
Upon arrivng at the hotel, I was warmly greeted by a lovely receptionist who already had my room key in hand. I signed in and headed for a great nights sleep. The room was nice and cool with the A/C already running. The room had two double beds (very comfortable), a wide screen HDTV, clock radio, Microwave, minifridge, coffee maker, ironing board....all the creature comforts. The bathroom was clean and spacious with a shower, but no bathtub.
Breakfast was included in my room rate. I took full advantage of the very nice American buffet hot and cold breakfast. My check out time was extended one hour upon request to the curtious staff.
This hotel is in brighton which is not directly in the heart of the city of Boston. However, it has very easy access to the Transit system and is only about 45 minutes to an hour by metro transit to Logan International Airport. The area surrounding the hotel is mostly reidential neighborhoods and retail shopping. I would highly recommend this hotel for your next visit to Boston. MA.

title: “Nice Location for Tourists”
text:
The Argonaut is a good hotel if you want to stay in crowded Fisherman's Wharf. It is family friendly and even allows dogs. The front desk staff is very nice and housekeeping people are nice. The rooms are nice and clean.
The only negative is the restaurant in the hotel. The staff was incompetent and the hostess was downright nasty, yelling at older members of our family for not noticing the "wait to be seated" sign. If we had not been with elderly people we would have gone somewhere else to eat!

title: “Nothing outstanding”
text: Had to query the bill twice. Had charged twice for wifi and twice for breakfast which was included in room price. Staff did not like errors being pointed out. Great location. Room was OK but bathroom was tiny. Would not stay there again if ever visiting Boston again though.

title: “Hip hotel with few flaws...”
text:
The Muse is a hip little hotel in a great location. Within walking distance of Times Square. 
I had to travel to NY on business and brought my mom along since she wanted to visit NY. Here's the scoop...first the good...as I said, great location and clean for the most part. We had a junior suite reserved on Travelzoo and it was quite large enough with a BIG bathroom. The bed was fantastic, wonderful linens, comfortable mattress. Had 2 TVs in room, sofa, sitting chairs, bathrobes, wardrobe and the ever expensive mini bar which we didn't use. Room was pretty quiet; I had the fan on which helps cover up outside noises as well. Now for the downside, fortunately nothing major... check in time was at 3pm. We arrived right at 3 and had to wait almost 45 minutes since we were told the room wasn't ready. The doorman had to check with the front desk 3 times for us. The radio/allrm clock had issues and I couldn't get it set. We called for room service and he came promptly to fix it. He couldn't fix it either and brought us a different radio/alarm. Some dust around base of furniture and on bedside stands, but other than that, it was pretty clean. The worst flaw was the view. OMG - we looked out at a roof covered with what looked like garbage, burnt materials, ac units, scrape metal, etc... Kept the curtains closed to block OUT the view. It made the room pretty dark, but then again, we were only in the room at night and out all day so it really didn't matter all that much. But really, for the prices they charge in NY, this room should have a huge discount for such a horrible view. I would stay at this hotel again though.

title: “Great location...but the hotel needs some work.”
text: The best thing about this hotel is the location. I've stayed twice now and the second time was purely due to location. You can walk to Pike's Place and it's a very short cab ride to downtown, capitol hill etc. The staff is friendly and you can't beat the view if you get a waterfront room. Also, the restaurant and lounge are beautiful with good food and drinks, although pricey. So that's the good...now for the bad! Parking...uggg. $30 per night to park the car...no fun. Unless you get one of their premium rooms don't expect much. Sure there's a cool ottoman shaped like a bear in every room, but that doesn't hide the popcorn ceilings or the occasional hole in the wall. For the price you would definitely expect more. Also, this last time, the hallway was constantly filled with cleaning carts. I'm not talking one or two...when you exited your room and looked down the hallway it looked like a cleaning service convention. Not a huge problem, but unsightly just the same. Also, back to the waterfront rooms, expect to hear lots of noise. This isn't the hotels fault mind you, but all night long you hear boats screeching against their docks. And not the pleasing sounds, we're talking metal on metal. On the other side you get the train throughout the night. I actually like train sounds, but consider yourself warned if you're a light sleeper. All in all I would stay here again for the location, without a car, and at a reduced rate. I would NEVER pay full price for any of their rooms...you can find better. I would recommend this place to a friend IF these conditions were met. That being said, enjoy your stay in Seattle, it's a wonderful town!

title: “AWESOME”
text: Booked this hotel based on reviews from this site, and the hotel exceeded my expectations. Perfectly located, short walks to anywhere you wanted to be. Times square close but far enough away to be out of the bustle and central park well within walking distance. Arrived at 11 am and room not ready but called from lunch at 12:30 and room was ready early. The room was very nice and spacious. If you are like me and book rooms based on reviews you can not go wrong with staying here I promise. Also, Ruth Chris steakhouse is right next door which has awesome steaks. Many resturants well within walking distance. You won't be sorry staying here.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: This is an older hotel with the flavor of New York years ago. The rooms are small compared the newer hotels, but comfortable and clean. Everyone on staff was helpful and polite. When we needed something delivered to our room, it arrived immediately. The location could not be better. It is close to theaters, stores, restaurants, subways, other sights and tour busses. I would gladly stay at this hotel again. It is perfect for a vacation in New York.

title: “Overall good, would stay again”
text:
Just returned August 16th, all in all this hotel is good not quite up to the Sheraton standard though, the rooms are clean the bathroom could use a fan, and it would have been nice to have a fridge in the room, the beds were comfortable . We had a room in the Marina tower which is the bigger of the two towers we had a room facing the city/Airport which at first I thought might be an issue (noise from Airport) but actually it was not an issue you do hear airport noise whilst sitting on the balcony but when you close the door you don’t hear anything, the walls had good sound insulation which is good because I’m a light sleeper and I did not experience any problems. Food is fairly expensive here we booked a package through Allegiant Air and received breakfast free everyday which was great you had the choose of buffet or menu breakfast it was good, we ate in the bar once food was ok! There are no restaurants close to the hotel so if you don’t eat at the hotel you would have to go downtown which is a 10 minute drive away, if you don’t have a car like us you can take the hotel shuttle to the airport then take the bus to downtown a little inconvenient but it worked. The pool is very nice lots of chairs to lounge around on they do have a pool bar which is convenient the staff do walk around to take orders, I found the food here a little greasy for my liking.
The hotel does have lots of conferences here but it did not affect us to much they have a big conference centre so they are really well take care of over their own side of the hotel.
The hotel front desk staff we found to be very unfriendly it seemed like they were going out of their way to help us, on the over hand housekeeping went out of their way to help you and were very friendly even though English was clearly their second language.
Parking your car here is expensive $25 a night and more for valet parking however most hotels charge the same rates. It would have been nice if they had a shuttle that took you to the downtown area where you can pick up a bus or the trolley system which is very easy to get around on.

title: “Fabulous-- Can't wait to go back!”
text: I just returned a few hours ago from a WONDERFUL wkd in NY. My was traveling w/ my 2 boys & was able to get an incredible rate on Hotwire for the room. The location/staff was great! The rooms are larger then most NY rooms & the location cannot be beat! This morning when we checked out we had a charge of $17.42 from the mini bar that we did not use--after talking w/ the front desk he informed us that if an item is removed it will charge you. Well my son did remove a bottle of water to store his mountain dew a few times.. Lesson learned :) The charge was removed with no questions asked. Don't think twice about booking this hotel :)

title: “Great value for the location”
text: The hotel is located in an excellent position, great value (89$ per room per night). Rooms are clean, daily maid service, breakfast included, very nice staff. Nothing more to ask if you want a cheap holiday in New York!

title: “Terrific Room, Bed, Location, Style”
text: Royalton's Superior Queen room was large, fun and enjoyable. Great HD TV, firm queen mattress, lots of room (especially for NYC), great amenities, full minibar all contributed to a wonderful stay. The front desk check in guy, Travis, really greeted me warmly and helped get the visit off to a great start. Being right on 44th between 6th and 5th is a GREAT NYC location. iPad in the room makes it easy to request wake up call and a time specific for housekeeping. Great stay.

title: “Nice but rooms need updating”
text: Great location and very friendly staff. Room we stayed in needed a remodel. Also, for these prices, wi-fi in the rooms should be free, not $9.95 per day. Sports bar in the hotel was a nice place to get a quick meal. Overall, not bad, just expected more from a Grand Hyatt.

title: “A nice place to stay but”
text: First of all let me say the the Inn is a very nice place. It is clean and the staff are very friendly. The rooms are very nice though there is a significant lack of storage space in the room my wife and I stayed in. Now for the but. Calling the Inn at St Botolph is a misrepresentation of the highest order. Nutri-grain bars, bagels, and a fancy espresso machine do not a B&B make. Not having enough coffee in the room does not help improve the situation either. Instant coffee really doesn't cut the mustard. the Inn is located in a great neighborhood and is very centrally located but it is not worth the rather hefty price tag that is associatted with it. Another complaint is the lack of attention to detail regarding the upkeep of the Inn. Again for the monies paid there should never be lights out in the common area, ever!. During my stay i counted no less then 15 lights out between the floor i stayed on 3 and the elevator, the first floor, and the ground floor. Just not acceptable for the price. The bedroom doors in my suite did not close prperly and were missing hardware. Again a lack of attention to detail. As they say the devil is in the details.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We booked this hotel not knowing what to expected. The hotel was very nice. The rooms was clean. We stay in the two bedroom two bath. One of the rooms was up chairs. It was so much space. A full kitchen, and cheap. Next time we are in Dallas for the cowboys game, we will stay here again. Ohhh yeah, staff is very nice. Free breakfast and social hours with food. Love it. Thanks for a good stay.

title: “Great location and friendly staff”
text: The staff was very friendly. The location is very Convenient to the Pier 39 and the cable car.

title: “Nice place.”
text: Spent two nights here. It's clean and convenient to the inner harbor. The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was not luxurious, but the bathroom seemed very updated and had a really good shower. The room service was great for breakfast (although I see their restaurant did not get very high reviews from others). I would recommend this for business or a couple wanting to visit the inner harbor for a getaway.

title: “Better than expected, Loved the Shuttle, Good Value”
text:
I got this hotel through Priceline for an excellent price, given that I was there for a holiday weekend. At first I had some misgivings about location and the ease with which I would be able to get dowtown for inside the loop activities. Luckily, it was much easier than I had expected.
The hotel is about .5 miles from the Racine Blue Line stop, so it's not too bad of a walk. If you are not a walker, there is a hotel shuttle bus that will take you to and from the train station for free. The shuttle takes hotel guests within a 1 mile radius of the hotel, so it won't take you all the way downtown, but will take you to the train station, restaurants (Giordano's was great!), Little Italy, Greektown, the hospitals, Harpo studios, etc., all of which are within 1 mile. I had no car and a CTA train pass and things worked out very well. Whenever we called the shuttle for a pick up, it never took more than 10-15 minutes, and the shuttle drivers were very helpful and full of suggestions for tourists. 
The hotel itself was nice, typical Marriott quality. The front desk staff were curteous and helpful. We had a non-smoking room, but it smelled a bit of old smoke, so that was a minus. The room was large and the amenities were good (Bath & Body Works toiletries, cofee/tea in room, good tv channel selection, excellent bed/linens). Another bonus is there is free internet access in the lobby and in the business center for guests. 
All in all, I was pleasantly surprised. I would certainly consider staying here again. Not the best hotel if you want to be right in the heart of the loop and near all the attractions, but well worth it for the price. A nice respite from the downtown hustle and bustle, but still close enough to be convenient.

title: “You will think you've stumbled into a PALACE! and RIGHT by the airport!”
text: Went into this thinking to just get a clean room, at a reasonable rate. What we found was absolutely unbelievable. I've stayed in 5 star hotels that didn't have as many amenities! Mr. Patel and his family have literally thought of everything, and I do mean, EVERYTHING! Right down to a bathroom scale, plush robes, ceiling fan in the delightfully appointed room, etc. You will love this princely palace at a price barely higher than a Motel 6! I also cannot say enough about the staff and their attention to detail. They even give you a choice of about 1 dozen styles of premium pillows to make sure you have a comforable night! the bed was heaven,and even the regular pillows on the bed were awesome! When we go to Austiin, its this hotel for us! That's for SURE!

title: “Old hotels CAN be well maintained and kept comfortable!”
text:
I was in town fir the weekend with my wife and son for a certification exam for my job. This hotel is a perfect example of how to keep an "old grand dame" hotel in pristine condition! As a hotel & restaurant industry pro with 20+ years under my belt, I know how hard it is for an older property to maintain her charm, well done Kimpton!!!
Doormen A+, front desk, A+, bellmen A+, housekeeping A+, Bartenders A+++!!! room service C+ (Continental breakfast waaaay over priced- don't be lazy & go to Starbuck's around the corner or to Luci's diner accross the street).
SFD- we'll be back!!

title: “Exceptional service sets this place apart”
text:
Starting with a summary first:
*Wonderful service - best I've had from any hotel. 
*Decent location - close enough to shopping attractions and very good for bus routes.
*Room - Had a basic Dbl bdrm, but very comfy, clean, tidy with nice decor.
*Hotel itself - Well maintained, clean, offers great lounge/breakfast options also with free high-speed internet.
I'm usually a solo traveller wherever I go and I booked the Elan after a bit of research and some convincing reviews from Tripadvisor. And I wasn't disappointed. I've stayed at many different star-rated hotels but the service from the Elan staff tops the lot. Very good with directions, maps, bus timetables and assistance for when I requested to add another night on. Oh, and this the only hotel that I have ever stayed with that had a room ready for me when I arrived early (4hrs early).
The lobby area is well appointed, clean with 2 computers with hi-speed internet. There is the wine and cheese option for everyone from 5-7pm and the breakfast that is available every morning has a decent selection. 
I had booked a standard dbl bdrm and was put on the lower floor, just around the corner from the lobby. The room is small-ish but manages to fit what you need in there pretty well. Don't expect a view though. Bathroom is a decent size and clean, the t.v. is also good with a variety of channels to choose from. The fridge is small and mostly packed with mini-bar refreshments, but was good to have anyway. Where I was, it did get a little noisy but I expected that over the weekend period.
The location is very good, especially for the price. The beautiful grove/farmer's market area is probably about 15-20mins walk away (or take #14 Dwntwn LA bus service). Up the road is the Beverly Centre (which is also where I caught most bus services from). The DASH bus service can also take you to places like the Sunset Blvd/Walk of Fame/Hollywood for only a quarter.
All in all, a wonderful experience, wouldn't hesitate to stay there again and make sure you check this place out when thinking about booking in the West Hollywood area.

title: “Remarkable Hotel”
text:
First of all, we arrived in Boston on an early flight, and with only 1 day notice, the hotel staff was able to provide us with an early check-in. This was really great as we left home for a 6a.m. flight and our connector in Toronto was at 8:50...with little sleep it was nice to have someplace to unwind and freshen up before starting our day.
The room was very clean and modernly updated, with plenty of storage in the closet and on the shelves provided. One night table had two large drawers for more clothing. The lighting was good, and also had two windows that opened. We were on the 8th floor with a city view of Columbus Park, and the marina...very pretty at this time of year. It was a bit noisy but we were there to experience everything, and were typically not bothered by noise at night.
This hotel is in a great location, close to the TD Garden (hockey game), the Harbor, the Aquarium, Legal Seafoods, Quincy Market and other touristy type attractions.
This is one of the first hotels that I've stayed in that the bed was actually comfortable and i got a good nights sleep. The bathroom was a little small, but ok because we didn't spend a whole lot of time in the room anyhow (also, i think we may have had a Halloween ghost as the bathroom door would close on it's own...lol)
We loved this location and when we do return to the area will stay here again...

title: “What more could you want?”
text:
The Four Seasons' tradition of luxury, class and sophistication continues unabated at the Washington DC location. From the staff who seem to have a psychic ability to anticipate your needs to the rooms which are elegant without being stuffy, this is a first-class hotel.
I had a wonderful stay here and will certainly keep the Four Seasons at the top of my list both in D.C. and likely just about everywhere else I can find one. 
They haven't let me down yet!

title: “This hotel is great for someone looking...”
text:
This hotel is great for someone looking for an upscale, clean 
place to party and sleep. It is literally across the street and overlooking the Salvation Army homeless shelter with an overflow of homeless people left on the streets. The majority of the rest of 
the rooms overlook a brick wall and air conditioning systems courtyard. 
The valet guys are GREAT! And they have a free Escalade service to take you around town. The front desk people also go out of their way for you and are great. Food is awesome! The housekeeping people are also great. Those are the positives for sure. 
The "queen" rooms are VERY tiny with no place to put your extra bathroom items and absolutely no drawers. Just a very small closet. The "king" rooms are substantially better, just a terrible view. Had to keep the curtains closed. I noticed all the rest of the inside rooms did as well. 
If you're looking for a place to crash, this place is great. If you want a room with a view, a spa to relax at, or sunshine in your room - look elsewhere. This hotel doesn't have it.
I overpaid for a long 5 day stay.

title: “Incredible value.”
text: Best Western Market Center is in a nice area just NW of downtown. There are excellent restaurants close by. The service is excellent. The building and rooms were clean and tastefully decorated. I have been in hotel rooms in the $300 price range and they had nothing on my room at the Best Western Market Center.

title: “Great place, but kind of rip you off on extras”
text:
We stayed 3 nights in Dec over Christmas. From the reviews we read, this hotel is usually booked for conventions, but they had a great deal, "Stay two nights, get one free", so we got a good deal on the price. We stayed in a corner room, which does NOT mean you have windows on two sides; it just means you have a few more square feet of space. The room was very nice, with high quality furnishings and the bed was very good. There was an IPOD dock, which was handy. The location is great for getting to the 16th Street mall. 
That said, there were some disappointments. Internet was not free, which stunned me. Much lower priced hotels provide free internet. There is no mirror outside the bathroom, which would be a great plus for two people getting ready for the day. They are not one of the higher buildings in the area, so views are quite limited, which was only indicated to us when we explored getting a better view. There is no coffee available in the lobby in the morning. There is a Starbucks right across from the front doors, so I guess they figure you should go there. We discovered newspapers in the lobby, but when we had called earlier for a newspaper, we were told there were none? Parking was $28 per day. The front desk help was politely cold most of the time. We did not have time to explore the other hotel amenities such as the exercise facilities or the pool. After reading of high prices, we also did not eat there.
Overall, our experience was OK. We had never stayed in a Hyatt before, and it is not likely we will return. We have stayed in the Hotel Monaco or Hotel Teatro downtown, and had a much better experience.

title: “Just the basics....”
text:
Stayed here 1 night in June. It was close to home and as our AC was out and temps were over 100 we had to spend the night in a hotel. The property used to be much nicer but now the exterior is run down. Crumbling and missing concrete fencing all around the property, dead shrubs, etc. A minimal investment could really spruce up the exterior. Room interior was just ok. It too is overdue for an upgrade. Tired looking carpet, bathroomarea showing a lot of wear. AC unit was difficult to control for comfort. Sometimes it ran too long and sometimes not long enough to keep it cool, probably a thermostat issue that needs to be addressed. Toiletries are very basic. On the upside the front desk staff was efficient and friendly. The morning breakfast was unappealing. Instant coffee machine, the usual thawed out frozen pastries and some really unappetizing looking frozen omlette looking things. There are a number of close restaurants that are within walking distance, (Ihop, Chili's, Chuy's, Mamacitas, Texas Roadhouse, Starbucks, Chipotle, Applebee's and others. Property is about 1 block off of Highway 290 and Highway 6.
Do not plan on returning here again and would not recommend to friends until this place is upgraded. The rate was good, about $80 with AAA rate.

title: “wow,wow,wow !!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: We Stayed at the w Times Squares for a week-end with my nieces end nephew, we booked the " suite fantastic".....but the suite wasn't ready and we complained at the desk....Finally the manager came and he upgrade us to a better wonderful suite!! It was amazing, beautiful.....everybody, so kind and helpfull. We definetely return to this hotel. The food at the restaurant was delicious, thank you for an amazing trip W !!!!

title: “Plan a Party at this Fabulous Resort”
text: Last month I was involved in helping plan a 90th Birthday party for a lady who looks and acts no older than 60! She invited 231 guests and 204 responded "yes--they would attend"!! Randy, Birthday Lady, was in charge, but without the expertise of Lauren Peterson, Catering Manager, it would have been impossible. We arrived at the Hotel early--and it was wonderful! Everything was set up beautifully, just as Randy had requested. The room Captain, Victor Andrade, was there making sure the food, bar, extra Chairs, assisting the D.J. in any way he could was all just perfect! And then Lauren was also there double checking! If you want perfection on planning an event, I highly recommend the San Diego Town & Country Resort and be sure and ask for Lauren and Victor. Nancy Brock

title: “Not impressed”
text:
When I first entered the Boston Park Plaza Hotel and Tower, I was very excited to be staying here. The décor was impressive and I had high hopes of an exceptional stay. It did not take long for that go downhill almost immediately.
When I first got in line to check in, I was told there was another line – although there were no signs to indicate as such, nor any clear delineation on how to “register” with the registration desk being so long. Seems like a small irritant, so at the time I didn’t think much of it.
I registered and got my keys. I went up in the elevator and was excited to see my room; if the entrance was that plush, I was sure my room was going to be exceptional.
Oh how I was so wrong. Oh how I was so disappointed. As I walked in, I was surprised at how small the room was. I thought to myself, “for almost $300/night, I would have thought I would have had a lounge chair or a small couch – some room to do some business”. 
As I walked in the room, I noted the wobbly “sewing” chair for a desk chair, an unremarkable desk (stained I might add) with a partially functional light, and a wall that had cracked paint, chips, and even a long hole around the perimeter. 
As I was on business travel, the first thing I did was plug in my computer and access my webmail. Surprisingly, this hotel charges “extra” for “fast” internet (such as that which would utilize VPN). 
Again, as I was on business and needed VPN, I signed up for the more costly connection. If it is faster than the other one, I suspect the other one is using a 19.2k dial-up modem. I ran a speed test on the internet connection and it was rated BELOW 56k in speed. It was not even equivalent to today’s dial-up standards!
Disgusted, I needed to use the wash room. Not even a light switch in the washroom; the light switch was on the outside. The décor was circa 1950 and it was the smallest restroom I have been in in probably 20 years.
Returning, I tried to call down to the front desk to see if there was something wrong with the internet connection – but my phone did NOT work. Of course. So on my way out to my convention, I let the front desk know that both my internet and phone was not operational. I was told it would be taken care of before I returned.
Upon my return, I checked the phone – ahhh…a dial tone. But when I tried to use any of the quick programmed buttons (i.e., “Concierge, Guest Services, etc.) they were non-operational, so I was forced to dial 0 and be connected.
I then tried to access the internet and was again disappointed to see a ridiculously slow connectivity. I had better speed on the Airtran flight that I took out here.
Wanting to unwind, I tried to order a movie. The service was not operational. I once again called down and was told it was out of order and would not be available until sometime tomorrow.
The Boston Park Plaza Hotel and Towers has made my first visit to Boston a very disappointing and unpleasurable experience! I do not recommend staying here.

title: “Nice hotel, better location.”
text: The Bay Club was a decent hotel, great price, great location. The breakfeast was a disappointment we stayed at two lesser hotels on the trip with a much better breakfeast. The pool was just OK. With this said the staff was wonderful more than helpful, the area was great. Great restuarants, the view of the bay was awsome to wake up to. The fact that Humpreys is right next door with great entertainment is a plus. I would recommend this hotel but I would try a different place next time.

title: “Excellent place to stay!”
text:
Stayed 3 nights in second week of nov. Hotel is in a fantastic location - walking distance to Michigan ave, shopping, restaurants etc. Stylish and modern decor throughout the hotel. Rooms and bathroom were very clean. loved the toiletries in the bathroom! Very refreshing and had an excellent shower! Especially nice after a long flight! 
Adequate space in the room to keep our luggage and walk around. The view from our room wasn't great- overlooking the roof of an adjacent building but that didn't bother us at all. I pod deck was a bonus. Bed and pillows were super comfortable. 
Complimentary wifi was a nice touch, since I didn't expect it. Wifi worked well without having to sign in and out repeatedly like in some other hotels. 
Only compliant, if any- we were given a double bed when we would have preferred a king. But they were full that weekend and that couldn't be helped. So we understood. 
Staff were otherwise very polite and always helpful. Will highly recommend. 
Tip: We didnt try the restaurant at the hotel- but however, as mentioned before in a few other reviews- there is an excellent breakfast spot abt 2 blocks from the hotel called the 'eggsperience' - delicious crepes n pancakes, we went there everyday! Also, there's a frozen yoghurt place called 'pink berry ' nearby- yum! Am still dreaming about their peanut butter frozen yogurt :)

title: “Amazing veiws in the perfect location!”
text:
I was in Seattle for work and was booked into The Westin Seattle. This hotel was top of the line and had a wonderful staff. Yet the views of downtown Seattle topped everything! The unique design of the hotels 2 towers lets everyone have a wonderful view of this great city.
The hotel offers a heated in door pool and a Reebok gym. The location is within walking distance of all major attractions: Pikes Market, shopping and the Space Needle. 
If you have never been to Seattle I would encourage you to stay at the Westin, I know I will be back.

title: “Mid Sized Pension and Retirement Plan Conference”
text: Easy access, nice walk from the train station. Very nice rooms, service was excellent, cordial and accomodating. Meeting rooms were comfortable temperature, chairs were nice also.

title: “Excellent value, good hotel”
text: The location is out standing. The room was large with a nice bathroom and was veyr clean. I jad a high floor so there was little noise from the street. Check in was extremely fast. The carpets in the hallways are begining to show their age but are clean. All of the staff were very helpful.

title: “Good price, clean room, good breakfast in central Manhattan”
text: This hotel is on 38thSt, between 9th and 10th Av. You have to walk a nice few blocks to catch a subway, but cabs were readily available on the corner. A 24 hr Duane Read drugstore was on the corner, also. We had a king bed, which was ridiculous for such a tiny room, but we had a good laugh about it. The staff was extremely friendly and accommodating. We would definitely stay here again!

title: “worst housekeeping service and car parking!”
text: We always stay at a Holiday Inn property and always have great results...however other than location, I was very disappointed in this hotel. we could not get our room cleaned. We would call and request and be told 30 min. we'd leave for hours and come back to a dirty room. this happened more than once in our 3 night stay. ALSO,,,,,, I paid $25 per day for car valet service and when I got my car back it was COVERED in bird poop. It was almost comical but I was too mad to laugh. I did love our bed and the room was very nice but the service was lacking BIG TIME!

title: “Gorgeous”
text: Beautiful hotel. Great valet service - which you have to use as there is NO visibe parking. I have no idea where they parked my car. Was only there briefly so not able to provide review on anything other than appearance, valet service, front desk & room. 2 negatives: major elevator down @ time of stay was a pain. And there is no sign outside the hotel & the street address is Jackson Place - that "street sign" is tiny and off the road. We drove by it once - only by luck and prayer did we find it again and there is A LOT of action right there. That would be my only advice to the owners - put up a sign for heavens sake!!

title: “Mold, rat poo, and a funky chair.”
text: A few friends and I decided to find a cheap hotel in Denver after a week long camping trip in Utah. Anything had to be more comfortable than sleeping in a tent in below zero temps, right? Wrong. The minute we stepped into the room we were overwhelmed by an indescribable stench, sort of a mix between B.O. and old food, but worse. A quick look around revealed a giant bubble of mold hanging over the tub, a staggering amount of rat turds on about every surface, and a chair that was coated with about an inch of some crusty white funk. We stood in the room for about two minutes, none of us willing to sit or even put our stuff down before we decided to get out. Of course the manager was gracious and apologetic and immediately refunded our money......NOT. The woman at the front desk seemed livid at us for having the nerve to point out the squalor that her hotel indeed was. She told us that as soon as we signed the bill we forfeited our money and "there was nothing she could do". Stay out of the Stay Inn, at all costs. There is a Quality Inn next door, spend the extra money, it is easily worth avoiding this nightmare of a hotel.

title: “Good size family suite close to LAX – great breakfast includes”
text: I booked our family of four in here for a one night stop because we were on a flight arriving late into LAX. I was surprised how quite it was in our room considering its close proximity to the airport. The room was spacious and clean and I liked the second vanity unit in the bedroom, which freed up the bathroom for showers. The complimentary breakfast supplied was great and I would have to say it was the best breakfast provided during our 33 day holiday in the US. We were also impressed with the free shuttle service provided from the airport.

title: “Very enjoyable!”
text: My friend & I stayed here last week for 3 nights. Aside from a glitch with the room that we had with our 3rd-party travel website, we really liked the hotel. The manager was very sympathetic to our problem & offered us a free breakfast & free parking. The room was very clean & nice with a great view of the city from the small balcony, although it would have been nice if a second chair was provided so we both could sit on the balcony. The bed was very comfortable!
