There was a noisy party near our room the first night, but the valet that had been to our room immediately took note of it & called security, who then took care of the problem. I really appreciated that after 10:30 PM they have restricted access to the rooms-this cuts down on the partying. The concierges were all very friendly & helpful. I loved the breakfast buffet & the lobby bar-great Mojitos!! One note of caution-if your room faces south or east, you'll likely get lots of noise from the 6th Street entertainment area, which can't be helped. Fortunately, we were tired enough that we could tune it out!

title: “The Only Place I'll Stay!”
text:
I have stayed here several times and each time has always been better than the last. But most recently the staff, particularly Christol Keane went above and beyond. My company booked me at another hotel and let's just say I left after being there briefly. I called Fashion 26, and Christol gave me an amazing rate, helped me get settled, and just made the rest of my stay wonderful. I have recommended this hotel and the staff to anyone I know that travels to New York and is looking for a very personal and wonderful experience. 
Kipenzi

title: “Never more disappointed”
text: We thought staying here for our anniversary and taking in a game would be a great experience.......however......the roof was leaking - the bathroom fixtures were not working properly....and when I complained I did not receive any help. In the morning I told someone different at the front desk and they told me that no one was suppossed to be booked in that room......I wrote to the headquarters of holiday inn and contacted the manager and never even received a "we're sorry".

title: “Absolute Bliss!”
text: We stayed 3 night at the St. Regis for a wedding. This hotel was absolutely beautiful. The staff is very welcoming and they are always very attentive. The room service is 5 star! Everything in this hotel is 5 star. From the furnishings to the tv in the bathroom mirror. The concierge are at your beck and call. The butlers are very helpful as well. I will not stay anywhere else in DC ever again!

title: “Good Experience”
text: We stayed here 3 nights over Thanksgiving week. Our room was spacious, very clean, with a comfortable bed. They offered a simple continental breakfast every morning in the lobby. Staff was eager to please and professional. Even though our room was next to the elevator, we experienced minimal noise from there because the building is well-insulated. We most definitely will stay again. It is close to Georgetown shopping, the Potomac and Kennedy Arts Center. Next visit, we will ask for a room not adjacent to the street because we are not accustomed to city traffic. The worst that I can say about this place is the elevator is from another century (slow).

title: “Great experience”
text: Spent the 4th of July weekend at the Peninsula Hotel. This is a fantastic hotel. The location right off of Michigan Ave. adjacent to the Old Water Tower is very convenient. The service was outstanding. All of the staff were very friendly. The facilities are first class. The room was terrific with a very large bathroom with a separate shower and tub. There was a TV installed in the wall adjacent to the tub area so that you could watch TV while taking a bath. Everything in the room (e.g. lights, TV, A/C, etc.) can be controlled from a console next to the bed. There is a wonderful spa located at the top of the hotel with a great view of Michigan Ave. from the fitness area and the pool. This is a true spa and not just your typical hotel fitness room and pool. They have a great restaurant in the main lobby that offers a coffee and dessert buffet with live music on Friday and Saturday nights known as Chocolate at the Pen. The Sunday Brunch is simply amazing. We truly can't say enough nice things about this hotel. We are anxious to return as soon as possible.

title: “Incredible courtesy by personnel at the lobby desk”
text: I met the niece of a very good friend on checking in, Erica Hollner. She was so pleasant, she sent a dish of fruit and mineral water to my room with a lovely card, it just made my stay there. She went above and beyond to ensure great customer service. Her roomate did as well when I was checking out, Laura, I don't know her last name. She was courteous and helpful, dividing up my room expenses separately for my travel expenses. I have and will continue to recommend your hotel to my peers. Beautiful rooms, great food, conference rooms have comfortable chairs!

title: “Amazing Hotel & Staff”
text: Beautiful hotel! Super clean and comfortable! Erin Brown has excellent customer service skills! She made our stay in Charlotte perfect! Kids loved the pool! Awesome restaurants and shops within walking distance! We'll definitely be back!

title: “Nice Dallas location”
text: I usually work offshore so its always a treat for me to get away for the weekend. So last month I headed up to Dallas for the weekend and stayed at this hotel. The location and hotel staff were great. Clean room, nice bed. and hanks to some good restaurant referrals in the area from Leshawn (sp), I ate pretty well too. I will definitely return to this hotel the next time I am in the area.

title: “Okay but not up to Hilton standards”
text:
we stayed twice at this hotel. once during the summer and the last time in May. The last time we ended up moving 3 times because the airco wasn't working properly. They tried to fix it but were unable to. Even in the 3rd room it was muggy. Beds are great, porch area dirty and very small. Waterpark is great for the kids. What we did miss comparing it to other Hilton hotels we stayed at: free internet (no where to be found), free water bottles to keep us hydrated, possibility to to a breakfast buffet. Great that the fridge is now usable to keep yor own food & beverages in. Before you had to pay extra for the fridge and microwave.
On mother's day the waterpark was very crowded with visitors, there was no room for the regular hotel guests which I don't think is the correct way.
Not sure if I'd like to stay here again, am looking into other resorts in the Phoenix area.

title: “Nice Stay at the Burnham”
text:
My wife and I booked the Burnham through Hotwire for $134 and stayed two nights this May. We considered it a great value for such a charming and well located hotel in Chicago.
The Burnham is relatively small, but the hotel is very pretty and has a classic look. The lobby is quite small but cozy, and there is a complimentary wine reception there from 5-6 pm everyday. Most of the lobby area is taken up by the Atwood Cafe, which is a very popular (and expensive) place to eat.
The hotel maintains many of the original touches from when it was built in 1895, like marble stairs, doorknobs, and iron work. Kimpton Hotels made it into the Burnham in 1999. The decor is modern feeling but not overwhelming; just cozy and inviting.
Our room was a standard queen on the 10th floor. The bed was nice and the view was impressive: our huge windows overlooked the corner of State and Washington, including Marshall Fields and the Chicago Theater. The bathroom was tiny and the tv and radio were a little dated, but these were not negatives for us. Everything was very clean, and the bath amenities were L'Occitane.
People have complained about construction noise from the huge project going on across the street. We stayed directly overlooking the construction and didn't hear a thing. Not only that, but Looptopia was going on below us late at night and we were not disturbed at all. I was worried about this a little, but no issues to report.
The location is excellent for shopping, bus and train access, and walking to and from Millennium Park/Michigan Ave. The only complaints we had are: one of the elevators broke down the Saturday we were there, which made it impossible to get down from the 10th floor. We had to walk down the stairs all day. Also, the business center is way overpriced (although wired internet is free in your room). Ultimately, these things kept us from giving the Burnham 5 stars, but this a strong 4-star hotel in our mind. It is a very charming and welcoming boutique hotel in the heart of the Loop, and you really feel like you are staying in one of the great historical buildings from an earlier era (I believe this was only the second "skyscraper" ever built in Chicago). We would gladly stay here again for these reasons.

title: “Great hotel, Excellent staff”
text:
We stayed for one night on the 15th Sept with 2 young kids (3 and 5). Parking was easy and porters took all our stuff upstairs which was great. We checked in early (at 10am) with Vicky Martin who was great and involved the kids. Our room wasn't ready yet so we went out to come back later. When we returned getting the room key was easy, and we had bags brought to room. We had a room with two doubles and it was fine for one night with the kids - room was furnished well with K-cup coffee maker. Bathroom was small, smart and clean but grout on tub area was a little run down.
To our surprise, Vicky had arranged for a tray of cookies and milk for the kids in our room - which made it very special for them when we arrived and highlights the special attention she gave to our stay. Thank you Vicky.
We had a great overnight stay and would definitely stay here again.

title: “Excellent location and decor but staff need better training.”
text: I stayed at Le Meridien in Philadelphia in order to attend a nearby conference. I found the hotel to be conveniently located, with an excellent Starbucks just up the street. The hotel atmosphere was chic yet cosy, with a decor that was a cross between Euro-minimalist and American comfort. The hotel costs were reasonable. Wi-fi was not free, but cost $10.79 for 24 hours of service. The down side: when I arrived there were no towels in my room (!). That is a fairly significant oversight. Also, I was misinformed by the reservation staff on policy for government rates and forms. The front desk staff didn't have anything to do besides assist me (no-one else was in the lobby at both check-in and check-out). Though there were two receptionists each time I went to the desk, they didn't bother to look up relevant information or gain clarification on the policy. I was friendly and upbeat when I asked, so it wasn't as if they were dealing with a disgruntled customer. Given that the cleaning staff had forgotten to leave towels, and that the front desk staff were clearly clueless, I left with the impression that the staff are neither supervised nor trained. Other than that my stay was comfortable. The restaurant serves excellent French food.

title: “Great Location for Staying in the City, Ok for the Price”
text: The Castle Inn is an older motel type establishment. Slightly run down and sparten but clean and very well managed by a friendly and helpful couple. Our room was clean and the only issue I had was that the walls and floors did little to keep out noise from other rooms (were those elephants above us?). Stay in an upper floor I would guess to lessen this problem. Here's the bonuses: FREE PARKING! Also, you are situated right on the edge of a fun neighborhood on Polk Street. Lots of good restaurants, bars and local shops in easy walking distance. Also if you want to get around town, a cable car is 3 blocks away (best way to get downtown!) and a bunch of city buses (MUNI) stop nearby to take you almost anywher in the city pretty quick. I'll be staying here again.

title: “Great Birthday Celebration”
text:
My husband and I stayed in this hotel last weekend of July 2011 to celebrate my birthday. Long line for check-in, i guess due to summer holiday. Valet parking is a bit pricy $33 + tax. If you want to self park, the parking garage is across the hotel.
we had great room with the Alamo view..Very simple, clean and modern room. The swimming pool on the roof top is small for hyatt hotel. 
Landing jazz on the river has great live music on Saturday nite, Brunch at the Q restaurant is a must.
Hotel location is great. Walking distance to so many great places on the riverwalk..

title: “Great hotel in a good location.”
text: We stayed in this hotel with our 2 yr. old and we enjoyed it. It was conveniently located near 2 grocery stores, shopping, even a movie theater. The only downside we noticed was a little bit of noise from a sports bar with an outdoor patio across the street - but it did not keep us awake. The Biltmore area is very nice and easily explored on foot.

title: “Great Location, Great Service”
text: I stayed at this hotel over the weekend with a few girlfriends and it was definitely a great place to stay. We were in a very convenient location directly in the city - close to plenty of restaurants, shopping, bars, etc. The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful with directions and tips about the big city. The rooms were comfortable and clean. I look forward to staying here during my next trip to NYC!

title: “Great service”
text: The resort is really nice and it is great for a convention. Lots of room, great bar, and several different restaurants. Great golf course. Plus the service was amazing. I had a cough and the front desk gave me a hand full of cough drops when I asked if the gift shop had cough syrup. Great star and great location.

title: “Best Hotel in Times Square”
text: I have stayed at many hotels in NYC and this is by far the newest and the best property in Times Square. The new Westin New York beats W Times Square entirely. While the "W" tends to be noiser and more friendly toward party-goers, the Westin draws a more sophisticated crowd such as business travelers. The Westin's service is better than all W and Sheraton properties in Manhattan, eventhough it is occasionally understaffed. Rooms are large (for NYC), clean, modern and very efficient. Room rates are, however, too high, unreasonable and uncompetitive at times.

title: “OK hotel,”
text:
We arrived at the Yotel and were greeted by several employees who helped us with the computerized check in and explained how everything at the premises worked, where to find what and what time the breakfast was served. So far so good.
We took the elevator to the 4th floor, to the Mission Control, were we switched elevator and went up to our room on the 24th floor. 
There was nothing wrong with the room, sure it was small but there was plenty of room to move around as long as the bed was in its upright position. Everything was fresh and clean, but do to the fact that it's a new hotel I would have been surprised otherwise. 
One little thing I didn't really like about the room was the glass-wall separating the bathroom area from the bedroom area. There is a curtain to separate the two areas, but that doesn't give me the privacy that I want to have when I am...powdering my nose.
The air conditioning is working great but the air is bouncing of the bathroom wall and on to the person lying at the right side of the bed. The Internet is fast even though the signal sometimes is a bit week. 
The view from the room is a bit boring, but that is not really the hotels fault. 
Now to the breakfast, if we should call it that. 
There were only muffins, danish, croissants, other sugar stuffed things and some bananas and apples. The coffees were great tho, strong and not at all what you are used to here in the US. You could choose between decaf and regular coffee. The only other choice of beverage was tea. 
If you want something more breakfast-like, something to keep you going for a longer period of time, you can pay extra for oatmeal, orange juice, eggs etc. 
Overall we found the hotel to be OK, for what we paid (150 $ per night), but we don’t think it’s worth more than that.

title: “Love Fisherman's Wharf Area”
text:
Love Fisherman's Wharf. Sights are wonderful, food is excellent.
Tuscan Inn is within walking distance of all Wharf attractions. Many choices for eating, shopping and activities.
Parking is expensive, Rooms are on the small side. Staff is very helpful. Happy Hour each day from 5 - 6 PM.
Still......a great place to stay.

title: “Ok hotel but wouldnt recommend..”
text:
I booked this hotel online even after reading these reviews. I liked that it was pet friendly with no extra fee's. It seemed fairly safe, except late at night it was very noisy outside our room I found myself looking out the window a lot at my car to make sure it was ok. lol The bathroom was very clean. The carpets had a few stains on them and felt/looked dirty. The bed was comfortable. Don't go to the mcdonalds by there either..its horrible - the menu isnt even by the speaker...how are you supposed to order like that? lol 
I wouldnt recommend this hotel, on my way back to NC from CA I will look for a different hotel to stay at.

title: “Wouldn't stay there again”
text:
I was disappointed that the hotel was not right on the water, since at the time I booked it it stated "on the riverwalk". It's only 2 1/2 blocks away. But I really wanted to be 'on the walk'. But, once I arrived I decided to make the best of it. 
On the first day, someone tried to barge into our room. Scared us to death. We asked "Who is it?" but no answer. Since we have the security bar locked, they could not get in. Once they stopped, we looked in the hall and no one was to be seen. We notified security who promptly did a "lock down" and investigation. They found out that it was a maid trying to clean the room, but forgot the 'protocal' to knock first and announce who you are, then repeat. 
For our trouble, they offered us free parking and a key to the 12th floor for a free continental breakfast each morning. So we were somewhat satified...but you wonder if their story was true. It's easy to blame a maid. And she was not only very strong for forcing the door so hard, but quick to get her and her cart out of site in a matter of seconds. 
The walls are very very thin. You can hear every word of every conversation in the rooms next door as well as the hallways. The doors are heavy, so you hear slamming at all hours of the night. 
Breakfast buffet was very expensive and not great. The only thing worth the trip down the elevator is the ommettes. 
The bed is very uncomfortable and the pillows are even worse. There were strange floaties flying around the room. Not sure if it was dust or down feathers. 
So for the price. You get get much better.

title: “Great rates and wonderful front desk staff BUT marijuana smoker and dysfunctional door!”
text:
We booked two rooms right next to each other, when we returned at 4:30 pm one room had been cleaned, the other had not. When I went to the front desk, the attendant was very helpful and staff was immediately sent to our room. The man who is charge of housekeeping greeted us and made numerous excuses why the room had not been cleaned--asking numerous times about the "do not disturb" sign (which was not on the door) and the dead bolt. Turns out the door was not locking/unlocking properly and he thought someone might have been sleeping. I asked if a courteous call was made at all through the day and he said no. I felt like we were being blamed rather than assisted.
Later during our two-night stay, we smelt very heavy marijuana smoke. Turns out someone had been smoking pot right outside our door--the window at the end of the hallway (right by our room) had been opened and their ashes lay right on the windowsill. When we approached the front desk they said that had never happened before and they would investigate. We asked for an air freshener and returned to our room.
Even thought the rates were great, the front desk staff was wonderful, and there was a Mexican restaurant & Bob Evans right next door, the other issues made for an unpleasant stay. I would not stay here again.

title: “If you stay longer”
text: If you stay longer in Memphis, this is agood hotel to stay as it offers a small flat for the usual price of a room. The suites are well equipped and cleaned and furbished daily. There is a cooked breakfast every morning with an open kitchen area where you can tell the cook directly how you would like your breakfast. there is also a manager's reception in the evening with free drinks. There are several good restaurants in walking distance from the hotel. The hotel is easy to find, near Poplar Avenue only 20 minutes drive from town centre.

title: “Nice Place”
text:
While on my trip @ this hotel, I was upset by how far it was from any store for someone without a car! The bed was nice and comfy, the TV sucked a really old TV without any hook up for a xbox!
Way to many people just roaming around & the cameras everywhere made me feel kind of unsafe, like the only reason they need that many cameras is there is way to much going on over there

title: “Lovely Staff”
text: Those who are writing bad reviews here must not get it. This hotel is a select service hotel for extended stay. We enjoyed our time there, did not want to leave. The staff was great and ever so friendly. I see people complaining about the breakfast which is clearly noted as a grab and go breakfast. Not a sit down breakfast. The selection was good. The rooms were comfy. I love how they have free wired and wireless internet access. All in all a good stay with great staff

title: “Simple hotel”
text: The Redwood Inn is a small hotel located on Lombard Street which is a very convenient location for public transportation in the city. It has a small parking lot, but any parking in San Francisco is a major advantage. Just don't try to park a large SUV because it will take quite a bit of maneuvering! The rooms were simple and clean, as were the bathrooms. There is only 1 pillow per person and 1 blanket per queen bed. When we asked for some extra we were grudgingly brought an extra pillow and a blanket. We wanted to sleep in on Saturday but were awakened by a call from the front desk wanting to clean the room. You must notify the front desk if you don't want to be disturbed. The usual Do Not Disturb signs are only available upon request in the office. The price is pretty good for San Francisco so not a terrible deal.

title: “Great hotel, location, service”
text:
I stayed here from 10/26/12-what was supposed to be 10/29 for the Marine Corps Marathon. The location of the hotel is wonderful, a beautiful area right next to a metro. I loved that there was a running trail directly behind the hotel so I could get my last run in the day before the marathon. The trees behind the hotel were beautiful as they have turned all the gorgeous Autumn colors. I felt very safe walking around the area as well as running on the trail alone. The lobby of the hotel is very pretty and clean, as is the rest of the hotel. The dining area which comes directly off of the lobby, was extremely nice as well. We ate breakfast as well as dinner there throughout the stay. Here is what I liked the best: due to Hurricane Sandy, my flight back to Houston was cancelled which meant I had to stay 2 extra nights in the hotel. The man at the reception desk was gracious enough to honor the price I paid through a third party website for the remainder of my trip, which saved me a great deal of money. I love that they value their customers. The bedroom was very nice and clean as was the bathroom. The bed was extremely comfortable, which was so helpful for my run while in DC. Given that the Metro and the city were shut down for a day, we were stuck in the hotel, which we actually enjoyed. We took our laptops as well as magazines down to the lobby and just enjoyed sitting at the tables, having a Starbucks coffee, while playing around on the internet. There is a great diner across the street that was delicious and about one metro stop away is a great Italian restaurant called Sorriso Ristorante & Pizzeria...I HIGHLY recommend this hotel as well as the two restaurants. 
Thank you Omni Shoreham, I will definitely return when I run the Marine Corps Marathon again.

title: “Very Impressive!!!!!!”
text: My family & I stayed here May 1 2011. This was the best day of our 2 week vacation in California. I was beyond impressed with our room (Bigger than any appartment I have ever seen). We had sliding glass doors to a huge patio. It was extremely clean and did I mention it was right on the beach. The location could not have been better. A short walk to the boardwalk but nice because the hotel itself was so quite & peaceful. There was even coffee & breakfast in the morning. The manager Greg is so friendly and helpful. I WILL definately be back soon.

title: “Great Hamptons inn experience, just like expected”
text: Two nights at Hamptons. Room was good, big comfortable bed and clean bathroom. Internet connection was included to the room rate like normally, unfortunately connection speed was quite low. Self made waffles at the breakfast are very good. I recommend this hotel to everyone who needs overnight close to main roads.

title: “Sweet Dream”
text: Other reviews seem quite mixed, but I found this to be a pretty good Manhattan hotel. Initially they tried to put me in a room (901) that was so small it didn't actually have anywhere to hang your coat. But after pointing this out to the front desk I was quickly re-located to another that seemed the size of a small suite (905). Service, decor & location are all good. The gym in the basement is a bit of a joke - but they've got free access to the Gold's Gym around the block, which is fine. I was able to get a good price from expedia (c.£125 inc. tax), so all in all Recommended

title: “Fantastic Stay”
text: This was an amazing place to stay. The hotel is clean, staff is friendly, and rooms are amazing. The location is great and very convenient to many of the downtown attractions. We loved being offered a glass of sparkling champagne on check-in and the complimentary newspaper in the morning. The free wi-fi was also a great bonus!

title: “Very disappointing!”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a conference. I had a "Junior" suite with a mini fridge. No mini bar. Coffee machine present but only had paper cups with it. Way below my expectations for a 4 star hotel. Carpet was old, worn and actually had holes in it. None of the usual extras I would associate with the price like shower cap, bath robe, cork screw, shoe horn, etc. etc. Amenites included small shampoo and conditioner and a small bar of soap only.Room was large enough and with an OK view (on the 18th floor) but and furniture was old, worn and ripped in places. WiFi is extra. Overall a very disappointing experience. I got MUCH less than I expected for the price.

title: “Bathrooms need updating & NO FITNESS ROOM”
text: I am a tried and true Hyatt guest. I always try to book Hyatt because the quality is CONSISTENTLY good. However . .. I found myself extremely surprised and disappointed with my stay at this location. I stayed for 7 days. WHen I arrived I was disappointed to find out that the fitness room cost money! That was surprising given the rates. Also . . . the pool was VERY small and crowded. The sauna and steam room were a huge disappointment as well. Finally . . and maybe the worst blow was the tub/shower was filthy. I felt dirty after I got out. Everytime I showered I find more grime, rust, and filth. The cleaning service was hit and miss. At times they didn't refresh the towels, shampoo, conditioner, soap, coffee, etc. On at least three occasions I had to call the front desk late at night so the stuff could be brought up. The front desk staff was extremely helpful. The concierge was hit and miss. Half the time they were really helpful . . other times I got the sense that they were just trying to make a buck by sending you some place that they got a "cut" if you showed up with a "coupon" with their name on it. SO it was hard to trust they were giving us "good advice" about the best places to eat . . or if they were trying to pad their wallet. One guy was excellent. Beard . . works days. Young gentleman with dark hair . . works afternoons . . felt like a bit of a scam artist.

title: “Excellent location, service, but small rooms”
text:
This hotel is a step above what you'd expect from a Day's Inn. The service is exceptionally great, and the rooms are nice but small. I got an "upgrade" this visit and I be afraid of how small the un-upgraded rooms are! The size of the elevator is a good indicator of the room sizes.
The reception desk helped me find a good place to eat nearby and overall were very friendly. The bell staff worked very hard to get me a cab at a peak time too. 
The rates are high, but this hotel is almost always sold out when I try to stay there to visit a friend in the neighborhood, so I'm usually just happy to get a room. The room I was in was somewhat close to the elevator and I heard a lot of hall noise through the door.
The free wi-fi is very much appreciated too. Breakfast was included too but I didn't give it a try - preferring to go to the Chicago Diner.

title: “Avoid this Hotel”
text:
I stayed a week on business. I chose the Hilton because I'm an HHonors member. This was the worst Hilton hotel I've ever stayed in. Why? Let me just list the reasons:
Cramped outdated room, no tv remote had to call, left me a breakfast room menu one day out of 5, Food was overpriced and disgusting, I had free coupons for breakfast ate once and threw the rest of my coupons out!
slooooooow elevators, not enough parking, your room view is the airport parking lot, no bath soap they only had women's facial soap (yes I asked)
Air conditioner would not cool the room.

title: “Fantastic for a long weekend”
text: My wife and I like to take a break without the children at least once a year, and visit different places that are either not deemed our kids 'cup of tea' or giving us an opportunity to splash out a bit more as it is only the two of us. This year we ticked off the new York box, and through lots of searching for hotels, settled on the Marriott Marquis. Why?, because of the central location, the only revolving restaurant in NYC and the excellent facilities. The rooms are perfectly adequate and sizeable, and we had great views over times square. The location is right by TKTS where you can get discount show tickets if you are prepare to queue up, (worth it in my opinion) and right in the middle of the theatre district, and taxis are easy to get and will take you from battery park to Central park and anywhere in between. The Hotel has a great revolving restaurant and it is best to book a reservation to avoid disappointment. While it is not cheap, it is excellent quality and service, and the 360degree views are fantastic.. There are excellent other facilities such as the gym, several bars and other eateries, and plenty nearby shops and activities. I would thoroughly recommend this Hotel based on our stay.

title: “Great Expectations !”
text: We found the hotel perfectly adequate.I often wonder when I read the reviews if I have stayed at the same place.Our room was clean no livestock whatsoever.The towels were replaced daily which in fact is too often in these energy saving times.The air con was a bit noisy but welcome in the heat and humidity.The lift was not speedy but not as slow as the one we experienced in Boston.The hotel was ideally situated for subway lines blue and red.Amsterdam Ave. was a great place to eat with lots of choice.I would recommend the hotel for those wanting a double go for the mid-size.Expectations are a funny thing

title: “2 gals and a Courtyard”
text: This was a great experience!!!! Staff was courteous, friendly, helpful and PROFESSIONAL!!! Location is GREAT!!!! The hotel is an old bank transformed into a lovely Courtyard- the vault is still visible in the restaurant. Food was delicious, security at door was outstanding- had to use your key to access the elevator- doorman got taxis for us, though we walked everywhere- and I mean EVERYWHERE!!!! Excellent location- close to all we did! Rooms are comfortable, clean, just what you expect from Marriott- can't wait to come back! Price was great, too. Several wonderful restaurants within walking distance-

title: “Not Bummed Out By The Vagabond!”
text:
We liked the Vagabond very much! 
The Vagabond is a nice little inexpensive place to stay while checking out San Diego attractions. I was drawn to it by some reviews I'd read, the location and the price.
The staff is easy going and friendly. The room was clean, beds were comfortable. Our room had a desk, T.V., refrigerator, microwave, coffee maker and free wi-fi. 
The free breakfast consisted of coffee, fruit, muffins and pastries. Coffee was always available in the lobby. 
There isn't an on site laundry. There's a coin op laundry about four or five small blocks away but it was closed while we were there. I drove less than 2 miles to another coin laundry called Ocean Breeze Wash & Dry. Its address is 4745 Point Loma Ave, San Diego, 92107. It was very nice and I folded my clothes while looking out at the ocean. I was there at around 9 am on a Saturday morning and had no trouble getting machines.
One thing that I though would be a good reason for staying at the Vagabond was the Fish Market next door where you can get fresh sandwiches, tacos, crab cakes etc.. I was less than impressed by the food and the prices were very high. 
We had a fabulous dinner at Filippis Pizza Grotto (address 1747 India St, San Diego, CA 92101). Filippis is in Little Italy, about 4 miles from the Vagabond. 
Other things that are next door is a Whale Watching boat trip company and fishing trip service company. I wish we'd had time for those.
I'm sure I'll be visiting this Vagabond Inn again.

title: “Horrible and RUDE!!”
text: Upon staying at the hotel we had placed phone calls to the front office to see if they had offered amenities such as an iron and a refrigerator. The person on the end of the phone was extremely rude every time. Upon arrival to the hotel, the person in the front office suggested we upgrade into a bigger room that had been newly remolded and less noisy. However this room was placed directly in front of the office and was super noisy all night long from the drunken people walking by on the street. During our two night stay, we had a few visitors (who did not stay the night) that came to hang out and go to the beach with us. When checking out the person in the front office made my fiance sit down while he scolded him for having visitors. He said that he had been watching us the whole time and counting our guests that entered the room. He then ended up charging us $10 for every person he counted having gone in our room. We told him numerous times that they did not sleep there, but the man continued to treat us with disrespect and inappropriate rudeness. The stay was absolutely not worth it! the employees are horrible to the guests and spy on their every move! do not stay here!!

title: “great price for this location”
text: We stayed at this hotel for a couple of nights at the end of August/first of September. It is a newer hotel within walking distance to the Magnificent Mile and restaurants. We were upgraded to a one bedroom suite with two double beds. The rooms are small and the bathroom is tight on space as there is no counter space and had a sliding door to the bathroom which got stuck a few times when someone was in the bathroom. We did have some trouble with our entry cards and had to get it reset a number of times. Staff is fairly attentive, but everything is tight, the gym is small as well. Our main purpose of the visit was to shop and see some of the local sights, which this hotel is perfect for- we were able to walk to many places to eat ,shop and sightsee! Even though you are right downtown, we did not find it noisy and slept very comfortably.

title: “Strip Club Across the Way Is a Feature; Not a Problem”
text:
Place offers ideal entertainment once the wife and kids are put down for their very long afternoon nap. Unlike other clubs, business here picks up to an energetic pace in the mid-afternoon with just the right level of crowd flow and there is always a good number of very doable dancers.
Oh, the full-range breakfast buffet is pretty good, especially convenient when traveling with several young children and a fussy/uncooperative wife.

title: “Excellent”
text: Just returned from a holiday in California which started with a short stay in this very conveniently situated hotel, excellent staff, excellent room, excellent food and an excellent situation close enough to walk to the major waterfront attractions like Fisherman`s Wharf and also the routes closeby of the trams, and hop on hop off buses, couldn`t really fault it and would recommend it to anyone

title: “Can't afford the peper glass covers?”
text: Sometimes the bathroom looked like it had barely been touched and can guarantee you that the glasses you touch have NOT been properly cleaned and sanitized as I came in one day and found one I used in the sink - full of what appeared to be soapy (bar soap off my sink) water. At that point, I saw the paper cover laying there, put a smidge of eye shadow on he back side and threw it in the garbage can.....low and behold, the next day was right back in service again. The rest of my stay I used paper cups. Most of the time, the coffee maker was also not serviced. Doubt I would stay again, cannot even get free internet access in your room. But the breakfast buffet was good.

title: “Couldn't find a single fault with the hotel”
text:
I can't say enough good things about this hotel.
I took my Mum away for Thanksgiving weekend to celebrate her retirement. I had written to the hotel in advance to tell them about this special event. We couldn't believe what was in the room on arrival - a retirement card signed individually by about 20 members of staff and a platter of cookies. The cookies were replaced everyday by the lovely lady who cleaned our rooms.
The rooms were so clean and comfortable. The location is fantastic for shopping. Boomingdales is a few blocks north and Saks is a few blocks west. We walked to Times Square on a chilly but crisp evening and it was lovely to soak up the atmosphere of the city.
We were so well looked after in this hotel. We had a call from the Careline and also from the Accomodation Manager Mr Holmes to check that we were OK. 
My Mum felt really special and we had a holiday to remember. I'll be telling all my friends to stay here.

title: “More than I could have ever expected.”
text:
I planned to take my three children to see the Orioles play at Camden Yards but arriving downtown on a limited budget I quickly discovered that I would not be able to afford a hotel for the evening, attend a game with the children and feed them dinner which was my plan.
The assistant manager and the manager were angels in disguise. Not only did they help make my room affordable, they found me four tickets to the game. The seats were fantastic, the children had the best time of their life. Without the managers help, we would have had to go right home after the game and not enjoy the city. Thank you both.

title: “magnificent smiles!”
text: There were so many warm, friendly people at the Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile made this stay great! From the bellman, Miguel, who was such a great embassador, to the concierge staff, to the housekeeping staff that helped make my visit memorable!

title: “Wonderful service”
text: I had the pleasure of staying here with my best friend. We both needed a vacation. The staff here are outstandingÂ¡!!!!!!!!!!! I could not get a shuttle from the airport. One of the staff's Brandon came to pick me up and was very apologetic. I had a situation with my bill and I was given a free night. I wish there was more transportation but I loved the water taxi. Hope to visit again soon.

title: “A Grand Hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Palmer House Recently. It is still a grand old hotel. The lobby is the epitome of elegance. The rooms are large and nicely decorated. Walking around the hotel takes you back to the past, when big name entertainers performed in the Empire Room. Lining the walls of the hallways are pictures of the entertainers. You can picture the guests walking around in their suits and dresses, occasionally bumping into one of the stars. The hotel is the same, the service is still topnotch, the food is excellent, but the guests are much more casual now. And the neighborhood around the hotel is not conducive for walking at night. It is sad, but the reality of the times. If you are looking for an elegant hotel that will transport you back to a grand old era, with the same great service, stay at the Palmer House.

title: “Wonderful hotel, but did have one issue”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for a surprise trip for her birthday between Christmas and New Year's. The hotel was in a great location and was chosen (based on TA reviews) as we were planning on spending three days exploring Manhattan. There is a parking garage directly next door, and they have a discounted rate for Hotel guests. We were immediately greeted very warmly by the staff upon arrival, and they were wonderful throughout our stay. The hotel was clean as was our room. They have umbrellas at the front desk you can borrow in case you don't have one (or forget one... oops!). We enjoyed the breakfast, and overall truly enjoyed staying at the hotel. 
But we did have one issue while we were there: internal noise. We stayed in room 51. The first night we were awoken by loud banging - it sounded like someone hitting a pipe with a metal wrench. This occured several times and totally disrupted our sleep. We thought it might be the heating pipes, so the second night we turned off our heat. We were awoken yet again by the same noise, and guessed that instead it must be the hot water pipes being used by other rooms (maybe the pipes run through room 51's walls). The noise was so loud, my wife at first thought someone was kicking in our bedroom door! We told the front desk staff about the problem after the second night and they were very accomodating and upgraded us to a bigger room on a different floor. They moved our belongings while we were out that day so it was ready to go when we returned that evening. That night we slept wonderfully! No noise at all! If it weren't for the room noise the first two nights, I'd have rated the hotel a 5.
We will definately return to this hotel, we'll just make sure we're not in room 51!

title: “good value for the price”
text:
Stayed here on 6 April for 3 nights. We found it very clean and well equiped. The rooms were a good size and had a massive bed!! We would agree with one of the other reviewers that the sound proofing was not so good, we could here people coming in late at night, chatting, coughing and walking around but only for a short time, we were so worn out we went back to sleep and they must have been just as tired as the noise only lasted a couple of minutes!
 There was a very strange vibrating noise one morning which stopped when we stood on a certain place on the floor, we thought it may be a shower and would stop but it went on and on , we called reception and needless to say it stopped when they came to see!! The guy on the desk said to let him know if it happened again and he would gladly find us another room. Really nice friendly staff.
 We didnt use the breakfast facilities but they looked great. We preferred to go further west and stop at a Dennys or similiar en route somewhere. There were plenty of places around and the hotel was a fairly good location, quite easy to find and easy access to other main places of interest. You obviously need a car here and the car park was very handy , secure and safe . Definetly recommend this place.

title: “Excellent hotel; loved the fitness area”
text: Stayed at the Westin in early March, 2012. $85 + taxes and fees on Priceline. Immaculate room with nice view. All personnel were pleasant and helpful without exception. It's a nice plus that a Lynx (light rail) station is literally right outside the hotel. Parking is $18/night to self-park, but hey, that's life in the big city. Fitness area is absolutely superb. Best I've seen in any hotel. Would be improved with some fans, though. Hotel is quite close to several museums. We've stayed here 2-3 times before and haven't encountered any problems. For $85, it's a good deal.

title: “Excellent service and room”
text: We arrived at the hotel at 6 am after a 10 hour flight from Brazil, they gave us a room right away and after a shower we were able to enjoy NYC on our first day!!

title: “Great stay”
text: This is a nice place! Clean and well maintained. We had great customer service from the staff and had no complaints with anything. Our room was nice and clean and i was especially impressed with the bathroom cleanliness - and I'm really particular! We will definitely be back again!

title: “Great Location, nice looking Hotel but very noisy at night with security eventually sorting out the problem guests”
text:
On checking in my first impressions of the hotel were very good. The location of the place is a plus due to its quiet side street setting. Reception staff are polite, friendly and assured me that I would get a great nights sleep (little did he know). The rooms are very small but are well maintained, modern,clean and well equiped with a nice flatscreen tv etc. The bathroom is great and was spotless.
The downside of the stay was the general noise. The corridors are very small, cramped and I was constantly woken by doors slamming, people talking loudly and antisocial behaviour. Having gone to sleep at about 10 I was woken by noisy guests coming in and out of the lift. This lasted for about half an hour and then I drifted back to sleep only to be woken again by more people and noise in the corridor. I eventually opened the door to find a small group of people lying drunk by the emergency exits. I called security who eventually came but the group had left. Same thing happened 15 mins later and by this time I was fully awake. Security was called again and dealt with the issue.
Overall the hotel was very good but I suffered at the hands of some very noisy guests and think that security could have reacted quicker.

title: “I Can't Say Enough Good Things...”
text:
I have stayed at the Ritz Carlton in Philadelphia twice and each time the experience has been excellent. Once for business and once for pleasure. Last week I stayed there was business. I took Amtrak from Harrisburg to Philadelphia grabbed a taxi and headed to the Ritz Carlton with a co-worker. As soon as our taxi pulled up in front of the Ritz Carlton the door man had out bags out of the taxi and brought them into the building as he held the door for us. As soon as we walked up to the desk to check-in we were warmly greeted like long lost friends. When I checked in I found out they had upgraded my room free of charge! Next, they offered to have someone bring our bags up to our rooms. We politely refused since we each only had one small suite case. Several more employees saw us carrying our bags as we apprached the eelveators and asked us again if we needed help. We didn't, but it was nice that they offered.
When I got to my room I was totally impressed. I had room 2002, which is on the 20th floor. It had 2 double beds. It was a corner room over looking City Hall. The clock tower was right outside the window. The bathroom was huge! I had a walk in shower and a separate bath tub. The bathtub had a window next to it that overlooked City Hall. You could see the beautiful view as you were taking your bath. Totally awesome!
Every where we went in the hotel the staff asked us if we needed anything. As soon as we walked out the front doors the door men were ready to call us a taxi. The service could not have been better!
I would most defintiely recommend this hotel for business or pleasure travel!

title: “Nice hotel with specious rooms”
text:
I was very impressed by the superb room - very specious, nicely decorated and well furnished. I used the kiosk for automated check-in and check-out and it was very quick. The shuttle took longer than expected to arrive to pick us up at the airport terminal. The shuttle from the hotel to the airport was also full and could not accommodate all the people that were waiting.
The staff was friendly and welcoming.
Had breakfast in the restaurant - it was quite average and the service was slow but I didn't have high expectations to begin with.

title: “Asolutely Ideal”
text: Great location. Short walk to Union Square. Bus 777 from water front to stop almost outside the hotel. Courteous, friendly, helpful staff. Just refurbished and all spic and span. Loved it. Great value.

title: “Great location, huge rooms - but some glaring flaws”
text:
After coming from and returning to friendly North Carolina, the curt front desk team was a shock! The only person there who was friendly and welcoming was Lawrence, the Maintenance Engineer who delivered our car as we departed. ($36/day for valet)
The rooms, while not shabby, are dark and outdated. The sheets for the pullout bed were worn well past their useful life, and for all the available space in the room, I am left wondering why the bathroom is the size of a postage stamp; it would be easy to move the door over and include the nice little closet area inside the bathroom so there is room to turn around.
We got caught in a major downpour during our trip to DC, and had to run for cover back to our room (in a taxi), and once we were locked in there, we discovered that the TVs didn't work; we called the front desk and were told that was due to the rain - WHAT??? I stay 50-60 nights a year in hotels and have never encountered this; we were stuck inside and couldn't even watch TV. Time for a different cable provider.
However, the neighborhood is pleasant, and the Metro nearby ... if you can get over the unhelpful staff, this might be the place for a large family, or a lengthy stay.

title: “Stay somewhere else”
text: I usually like the Residence Inn brand, and while I appreciated the two bedroom suite upgrade, being a single traveller, this could not make up for the fact that when I checked in after arriving late due to a thunderstorm in San Antonio I was checked into a room that was under repair. Coffee cup, caulking guns and dirty rags welcomed me to my room. I called down and was quickly moved to a similar room without the construction. This hotel is in desperate need of an upgrade to meet my expectations as a Marriott property. Dirty, fraying carpet, worn furnishings cheap televisions and a poor location await you at this property.

title: “Pretty Darn Good”
text: Great economical motel. I booked based on some other reviews from some other Website, where it got good reviews. You also have to understand that I spent the 4 previous nights at the JW Marriott Desert Ridge, so this was quite a change, however, I found the rooms clean, new paint and new carpet, The first night I found out that I did not have heat at about 11pm and I called the desk and told them I did not want to move. They immediately took 50% off, which I thought was generous. I then moved the next night to a bigger room with a king bed and the room had a microwave and refrig. Now, my girlfriend gets here tonight and she is used to something like the JW and I wonder what she will say. She best not say much or she can pay the difference and move us. The La Quinta also has a nice pool area and is in a nice middle class neighborhood where I went jogging this morning. I was very happy here.

title: “For Midtown Manhattan the price is a Great Deal!”
text: 1st and foremost, you cant beat the location. You are right smack in the middle of NYC, a short walking distance from 4, 5 and 6 Subway lines. So if you want to take a quick ride into Wall street, South Street Sea Port, China town, The Met or a number of other Museums, it is only a 10-15 min ride on the 4 or 5 and slightly longer on the 6 train because it makes all the local stops. The Staff was incredibly friendly and professional. The room decor is old Victorian, it's almost like bed and breakfast decor but with the noise of NYC. If peace and quite are important to you I would recommend a higher floor to drown out some of the city traffic noise. On cleanliness I am going to have to give them a less than great rating, only because the toilet in my room had something I would rather not describe, I do fault the cleaning person for it, they should have noticed it before I did. I would skip their Restaurant mainly because they charge an 18% gratuity on any bill larger than $50 which in NYC that is not a difficult thing to do. There are so many places to eat and shop in the area, that I would recommend walking around the big city and discovering all there is to see. Otherwise if you don't mind over tipping, then do try their restaurant. Again I give this Hotel an 8 out of 10 and yes I am very particular about hotels and how they measure up.

title: “Perfect for families”
text:
We stayed in a one bed apartment here in July 2012. Our party consisted of 3 adults and 2 children. From the outset the service was perfect. We were offered a baby cot, humidifier, new kettle and toaster within the first few hours of checking in.
There is ample room in these apartments. Everything works fine. Beds are comfortable. Kitchens include a dishwasher a huge fridge freezer. There is an iron plus ironing board.
The hotel also provides a walking tour of NY which is a box of guidebooks, guide walks and other useful items which we thought were great. The choice of pillows is also fantastic. All the staff are very friendly and helpful.
Maid service is daily, this includes bathroom, kitchen and arranging the beds. It didn't include a daily vacuum clean and tidy up which we thought was strange but not a deal breaker for us.
Wifi is exortionate, and this would be my main complaint. The trip was part business and part vacation and although I was paying for wifi, the connection was very poor. I had to end up going to the business center downstairs to get the full bars on wifi.
Despite this, if I was doing a vacation trip again with the kids, I would stay here again and really try and get a ground floor suite that has a garden.
Location was great for us. 10minute walk to central Park which was perfect for the kids. the metro is a 5min walk, and most evenings we walked it to Times Square, 5th Avenue and the museums.
Overall a great stay.

title: “Dream was fabulous”
text: Just got back from a wonderful weekend in the city. My husband and I stayed for two nights at Dream. We were very hesitant after reading many bad reviews. However, we had a great time and really loved the hotel. The hotel is very modern/trendy, perfect for 20 somethings looking for a fun atmosphere. Our room was quiet and the bed was very comfy. I would recommend a King size bed as an upgrade from the queen. These rooms are much bigger. The location is PERFECT...within walking distance of Time Square, 5th Ave, Central Park, MoMA, and Rock Center. The bathrooms are small but you are not in your room long enough to care. Hope this helps put your mind at ease if you are worried about choosing this hotel!

title: “The not so upgraded experience”
text:
This hotel is beautiful and has lots of history. The rooms are pretty with classic beauty. (not incredibly fancy).
In my personal experience the main problem with this hotel is the lack of motivation, dedication and customer focus from all the staff.
The Ugly
I had to open my own door and drag my luggage from the cab to registration while bellstaff and porter spent their time conversing.
I had to drag my luggage to the executive level (The upgraded experience). 
I arrived into a room of medium size and average amenities only to find a toilet which had been used and not flushed. The fermentation caused for fetid gases to float all around me
My room also had a desk with a white crust that I could scratch out with my nail. lots of it (food perhaps).
On my closet door I noticed a few stains of what appeared to be dried blood. 
I notified my "special" concierge in my "special" floor of the problems and requested his help in addresing the issues while I went out for dinner. Upon my return I walked into the same nightmare. 
When I approached him again he offered an alternate room and gave me a key if I wanted to go take a look prior to relocating. This one had lovely long hairs in the room evidence of a prior guest with a lush mane...
When I requested the opportunity to talk to a Manager on Duty I was told by my "special" concierge that they did not have one. Finally he located someone from the front desk who assisted with finding me a clean room. 
I am now in my clean room enjoying rather comfortable linens, I took a bath in my clean bathroom with a missing shower mat or rug. the water pressure was low but the water was sufficiently hot. 
To be continued... I still have 5 more days

title: “Great location for downtown Austin!”
text:
We stayed at The Hampton Inn for 1 night in September 2008.
The hotel was easy to find and drive too, being just off the interstate, and parking was easy too. We used the valet parking at $18, which was easy, efficient and quick, but there was also adjacent self-parking at $14, although this is not associated with or recommended by the hotel.
Our room was spacious, clean and well-appointed, with a large and well-equipped bathroom. We slept very well and thought that the hotel represented very good value for a city stay at a weekend.
Location-wise we were very handy for all of the sights. We walked up to the Capitol and Texas Museum during the day, found our way to the evocative bar in the Driscoll late afternoon, and then walked a short distance to see the famous Austin bats in the early evening. From the hotel it was a short walk later to find a choice of bars & restaurants in the evening.
Sad to say, we treated ourselves to a lie-in so missed breakfast! 
In summary, if you are visiting Austin then The Hampton Inn is a good quality/high value hotel, well located, well appointed and well worth a stay.

title: “Simply Unforgetable”
text:
This was my first visit to Chicago and my stay at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers was great!The staff was friendly and responsive to my requests and when I had an issue related to my door lock the response was very fast and the problem was corrected.
The food and beverage and the atmosphere of the Sheraton Lounge was exceptional. Just tell me one thing - how did the bell captain and the bell staff know I was from Toronto!
My entire stay was great and I look forward to my next vist to Chicago and the Sheraton Towers.

title: “Convenient old grand dame that needs a nip and tuck”
text:
Used to be when you said Boston, Parker House was the next word out of your mouth. At more than 150 years old, it's been around the block and then some. The rooms are small because the hotel is old but you could not ask for a better location at a 10 minute walk to many of the Boston sites and directly opposite the historic Old Granary Cemetery, where Paul Revere is buried.
If you are heading to Boston place a bid on Priceline. At somewhere between $59 and $99 this hotel would be a great buy. At any more than that, I would think twice. Avid the packages at the hotel's own website. They are overpriced.
The service here was great. On 2 separate occasions our room key wouldn't work and security was there in an instant..............then there was a fire alarm incident and the staff hurried all the guests in the lobby and were very calm and professional.
Now, while the room was clean, there was no tub in the room and the bathroom was so tiny that you could barely turnaround without bumping something.....not to mention the well-frayed shower curtain which needed to be replaced.
Finally, you're in the heart of downtown here so don't expect quiet. I hate sleeping in NYC.........and I hate sleeping in Boston. Unless the windows are noise-cancelling, there isn't much you can do about that.

title: “Brand Does Not Live Up To Reputation”
text:
I spent one night at the Waldorf Astoria, for a work event, and it did not live up to the brand's reputation.
Let me start with the good points. The hotel is in a great location...walking distance to just about everything (MOMA, Madison and 5th Avenue shopping, Central Park). The architecture and grandeur of the hotel is amazing--it is like stepping into history.
The stepping into history is also the downside. The hotel is in need of a major overhaul, as it has not been properly maintained. They are in the process of renovations. Unfortunately, the first room I received was situated on the 4th floor roof, which was being worked on. It was bad enough to hear the drilling but the workers were able to peer directly into my room. That was enough for me to request a new room. 
The second room was much better, and as other reviewers have stated, the newer tower is much better. The room was nothing special and the chipping paint on the door and leaking faucet were all indicators of wear and tear.
The service was good--definitely not becoming of a 5-star hotel. After being on hold for 20 minutes to get my room changed--I ended up gathering my suitcase and going directly to the front desk. The agent who assisted was very nice and helpful.
Overall, I would not recommend. It's nice to tour and get a piece of history and then move on to more modern times.

title: “Ok, not really 5 stars, but they don't deserve some 1 stars they're getting, either”
text:
My husband booked this hotel for my second Boston Marathon. When I read the reviews on here about the place, I had a definite sense of foreboding. However, it was a fine place. I wouldn't knock myself out to stay here again, but we had plenty of room (but we did book a suite), a bathtub (I've seen complaints about a lack thereof), NO issue with noise (we were on the 12th floor, though), the room was clean and odor free, and the staff were smiling and helpful at all times (and patient with a 3 year old who wanted to "pay" with our room key each time we went through the lobby so he could get a piece of candy). The location is definitely a plus if you happen to be going for the marathon, this is a GREAT location--just a couple of blocks up Tremont to the shuttle pick up (which means also very convenient to Boston Common and Boston Gardens), and the family meeting area is on the way back to the hotel after the race. My husband was able to entertain my son at the frog pond while I suffered through this year's record heat for race day. We were concerned about the temperature of the room when we arrived, bc we got there about the same time as the heat wave. But before we got the complaint to each other out of our mouths, they had turned on the air. This could be an issue, as the windows open only about 3 inches. The building is OLD. Many buildings in Boston are old. To me, that is part of the charm and character. If you are expecting a shiny new building, look elsewhere. However, each time I got in the elevator, I was stunned at its speed. It has to be one of the fastest I've ever been on! 
The only downside is there is NO room service--this is usually not an issue for me, as I hate to waste $$ on room svc, anyway, but the night before a race it would be nice to not have to battle crowds. We beat this issue with an easy reservation on Open Table at a nearby spot. However, there IS a bar downstairs, for a little liquid sustenance, which is pretty important to my husband. We also had a small fridge in our room, a necessity with a 3 year old. 
There is no pool, but the fitness room had enough treadmills to accommodate all of us marathoners, and seemed outfitted with solid basic equipment. 
Oh yeah! And wireless is free! I love free!

title: “Wonderful for easy access to the Hospital and the University of Pennsylvannia”
text: My spouse had surgery scheduled at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvannia so we stayed at the hotel for the night prior to the surgery and I stayed on for a second night. The staff were exceptionally helpful and courteous and the room had every comfort. The hotel was quiet, the bed and the pillows excellent and the bathroom was beautifully appointed. We particularly appreciated the lighting system in the bathroom and the capability to have a nightlight without lighting up the bedroom. We had excellent meals in the hotel restaurant. We would highly recommend this hotel for a short break and its easy access to the Hospital and the University.

title: “Nice and Clean!”
text: Went down to San Antonio for a night and stayed here with my family. The hotel itself looks new and is very neat and clean. The rooms are nice size, not big not small. I was pleasantly surprised by the size of the restroom, which was a pretty good size, meaning my knees didn't hit the door while sitting on the toilet; some are really that bad! lol The bed was comfortable hence no backache in the morning. The hotel is right off of the highway so I requested a room in the back to avoid the traffic noise at night, which worked out perfect; peaceful as can be; not to mention we felt like we were the only ones staying at the hotel that Sunday night! Even though I'm a Hilton Honors member I didn't get the free upgrade I'd asked for, which is okay; apparently they only give those to Diamond members. I wonder how many stays I'd have to have before I get to THAT status! lol All in all the hotel was a great value. The only two complaints I have, which are huge ones to me, are that the complimentary hot breakfast, which is great because it's free, but the food wasn't to say the least in my opinion. Now, my husband and my two little boys thought the food tasted pretty good, which is a plus, but I didn't enjoy it. The only thing I thought tasted good was the orange juice; although I didn't have any waffles! Also, anytime my family and I go out of town we love to get in the pool and hot tub. I chose this hotel specifically because it had an indoor pool. Well, the pool are was too cold for us to swim. I don't get why they air condition pool areas...it's supposed to be at least a little warm don't you think?! Furthermore, there was an issue with the hot tub not be "hot." Apparently there had been some type of renovation of the hot tub and pool and there was a note on the door which explained why the hot tub would not be warm. I don't remember the reason but it was unacceptable for us. It really put a damper on our stay at the hotel. The hot tub was just as cold as the pool which is not a good thing. It could have at least been luke warm!

title: “Great location, left disappointed”
text:
I booked this hotel for 4 nights for our one year anniversary trip and had been told I would receive an upgrade if available. The hotel was nice, had a great location in Union Square. Upon arrival at 2:30 I was told our room was not ready and it would be about an hour BUT "They had a spectacular room for us!" So that got us excited and we left our bags with the people in the lobby and headed out to get lunch while our room was being cleaned. We came back an hour later and checked in and were told our room was ready, at the very end of our check in the front desk person throws in there that our room was a handicapped room and that the bathroom had been "slightly" altered. No big deal because we didnt wanna wait any longer for another room. We then went up to our room and while it did have the "city view" that we paid for the bathroom was extremely awkward with a sliding door that did not lock or shut well along with rails everywhere. At first we thought it wasnt too bad, until we showered later that night and the different shower head installed for handicapped people barely put out pressure turning showers into a 30 minute ordeal. By then my wife had unpacked everything and did not want to pack everything back up and move rooms after our long flight.
I booked this room for 4 nights directly through Parc 55, so it's not like I booked through priceline and got the bottom of the barrel for a room. While this room might be good for our 50th anniversary, it was not ideal for our FIRST anniversary which I mentioned to the front desk before check in. I stayed in 4 other hotels on our West Coast trip and got better rooms at every other hotel, and I used priceline for a couple of them. I left Parc 55 very disappointed. Sliding bathroom door, that doesn't shut well in a hotel room.......just not ideal for a 1 year anniversary.

title: “A riddle...”
text: What do you find between a freeway and a stripclub? Ahh..that would be Hampton Inn Sea World of course?!? Yes, that is not part of the website. How awesome is that, a strip club literally within a block and half from your hotel front door. The rooms were nice, pool and jacuzzi all-right, the weight room a bit tiny, and the food a bit okay. But for 99 bucks a night, I can't complain too much. Close to the beach, and Sea World.

title: “Excellent boutique hotel in San Francisco with great location”
text:
The Hotel Adagio is a wonderful boutique hotel located in the heart of San Francisco. When we arrived we were warmly welcomed and since we arrived around 1800, the front desk person, Joel, offered to make us restaurant reservations at a small Italian place up the road. We felt that was very helpful, allowing us to drop our bag offs and just go straight out to dinner instead of trying to decide where to go on our first night there.
The lobby is modern and very classy. They have a nice small bar and restaurant there. We never tried it, but it looked very inviting. 
We had a wonderful room on the 14th floor. If you don't mind heights, I would definitely ask for a high floor as the views are very nice. The room had a flat panel television with a nice selection of channels. They also provide a stereo and you can request an adapter from the front desk to attach your ipod to it. There is a mini-fridge in the room which is your typical mini-bar. We asked the person who brought our bags to the room if it was a refrigerator, and he said no, it was a mini-bar, but did we want the items removed so we could use it to store our own items, some wine and cheese we brought along. We said, yes please and within 10 minutes all the contents were removed and we had our own little fridge. I thought this was a very nice touch, it shows they were more concerned with our comfort than with the profit they may have made off the min-bar ( which wouldn't have been anything anyway as we don't use them). A very nice touch.
The room was clean, bed was very comfortable, furniture very nice. The windows even opened here! We loved the cool San Francisco breezes at night. Of course you are downtown and on a busy street, so if you don't mind the traffic and fire engines, then enjoy the open windows. If not, you can close them and have peace and quiet, as they are all double paned.
The hotel is located in the Tenderloin area. Not the best, but I used to live about a block away in the 70's and the area has been undergoing some improvements. You are a few blocks from Union Square where all the great stores are, large and small. From Union Square you can get anywhere, North Beach, Chinatown or Fisherman's Wharf. We walked back to the hotel many times at 2200- 2300 at night, no problems. 
While you are there, I would suggest heading around the corner to Dotties True Blue Cafe, 522 Jones St. Best breakfast in the city. Get there early or be prepared to wait in line. It's small, but the food is excellent and well worth the wait. The hotel staff gave us this hint. The next street west is Jones and you can walk there and see Dotties down the street. If there is a line, you can call in your order and then go down, walk to the front of the line, pick up your order and eat it in your room.
A Great hotel in a great city! Highly recommended

title: “Fine for what we needed.”
text:
This is a budget Motor hotel. We took advantage of their stay and cruise package. We drove in from Phx, spent the night, walked to our cruise and left the car for the week. Came back a week later, picked up the car and left. 
No problems and excellent price. We did find it odd that they do these fly, cruise, and park packages, because they have very few parking spaces. In fact, they don't guarantee that guests will be able to park on premises. If your on a budget or just need a place to easily reach the airport or cruise ship pier, this place will meet those needs.

title: “Very average hotel in good location”
text: I live in Washington, but stayed at this hotel because my husband had a work assignment that meant he had to stay at the hotel for several days, and I joined him. I haven't stayed in the rooms at other DC hotels, although I have gotten familiar with the restaurants/bars in some of them and have been in the rooms when friends have been here to visit. This hotel is just adequate. It is by no means in the league of the luxe DC hotels like the Mayflower, Willard, Hay Adams, Jefferson, Four Seasons -- which I am sure are also far more expensive. However, if the prices here are comparable to one of the many Kimpton hotels in the area, I would recommend checking out the Kimpton hotels. These are boutique-type hotels, but I think generally reasonable in terms of prices. The Tabard Inn is also in this neighborhood, and might be an option (although it is on the old side, and I haven't seen a room there.) The room at the Beacon was just adequate; on the small side, and was clean. But extremely bland and generic. Furnished like a very mid-range hotel (perhaps a Doubletree). The bathroom was quite dated -- small bathtub not suitable for bathing, small sink. There was a "free" breakfast included in the price of our stay. This amounted to a danish, some fruit, a glass of orange juice from concentrate, average coffee. If you are not a carb eater, you will have to order off the menu (very average omelet for $14). The design of the hotel lobby and restaurant is off. It tries to be stylish, but just misses the mark by the extreme "busy-ness" of the decor. There will be some cool elements (e.g., stylish lighting fixtures, use of bamboo style wood at the desk), but these are combined with really ugly and unstylish ceilings, wall treatments, etc. The staff at check-in weren't all that friendly, but they weren't terrible. The maids in the hall were very nice and friendly. The neighborhood is in DuPont Circle, and I think that this would be a good area from which to explore DC. Relatively close to the Metro, and near some neighborhoods that will be nicer to explore in the evenings than downtown DC. Bottom line: I think you can probably do better in DC.

title: “VERY NICE!!”
text: Hotel was very nice. Prompt service at check in. Parking people were friendly. Service people at pool were helpful & friendly. Will definitely stay again! The food at Texas Spice was under cooked and very salty. But that will not stop us from staying at hotel we just won't eat at the restaurant there.

title: “Not a four or five star experience”
text:
I was checking in as an spg gold member for an 8 day stay at the W. My wife and son was going to be joining me later for the fouth of July celebration so I had booked a room with two queen beds. I was offered an upgrade to a suite for an extra $150 which I said I would consider for when they were arriving.
The room I got was indeed with two queen beds and with the usual cool W layout, but not really clean (e.g. hairpins in the sofa, hairbands on the floor) and with a view to a wall maybe 10 yards away. Not what I expected for $600 plus taxes per night.
Then my family arrived and the upgrade was now $200 plus $30 for a roll away as there would only be a king bed in the upgraded room. I kindly declined the offer....
When I learned that my son would not be allowed on the hotel's roof top on the fourth (while my wife and I would be welcome for a fee of $250 per person) I decided to find another hotel in town.
JW Marriott just around the corner from the W is by my scale better value for money. Not cheap and of course not the hip boutique style decor, but we got a great room on the concierge level overlooking the Ellipse and the Washington monument. And that's for about half the price of the two queen bed room with a backyard view at the W.
The bar staff and the bellman at the W are nice and smiling folks for sure, but it does not make it up for such overpricing. Neither for business nor for leisure travel.

title: “First Class!”
text: I was there for one night. I travel extensively. This is one of the finest boutique hotels I have ever stayed in. The rooms are large, well furnished, and comfortable. The service, both at the front desk and in the restaurant could not have been better. The food was excellent . Finally, this hotel is very well maintained and has an old world charm and impeccable taste. The price of the room and the meals were surprisingly affordable and the location of the hotel is within walking distance of Chicago's "magnificent mile". Well done!

title: “Best by far”
text: Must admit that I selected this hotel by default. Had no idea just how convenient and spectacular this hotel is. Friendly service, very clean, quiet rooms and terrific location. Steps from the north end, T station right out the door, major water events within a 9 iron and awesome views, this is a magnificent hotel for visitng Boston. We were with our grandson and everything was perfection. Loved it.

title: “Super Sleek, Great Terrace, Just half a block from Central Park”
text:
While on a business trip in NYC, my girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel for three nights. I thought the decor was super sleek and very close to the pictures on their website. One night we went up to the terrace and had a great time just taking in the view. Since it was only half a block from Central Park, we were able to walk a couple of afternoons after I had gotten back from meetings. My girlfriend really loved the wide bed and soft sheets.
It wasn't cheap for our standards but we were able to find a reasonable price during a week where everything else seemed packed. We payed a little more than most mid-town options we had looked at but it was well worth it.

title: “The time. & kids??”
text:
We stayed in a "Blue" suite for five nights, 2 adults a 15 year old and a 2 year old. Having done no prior research we soon realised this was not the best choice of hotel for a family. The rooms are on the small side for a family and a little on the tired side for a 4* hotel (we were on the eighth floor). However they were exceptionally clean and well equipped. 
The staff at the hotel are very helpful and understanding. A cot/crib was bought to our room within 5 mins of requesting, along with extra towels and bedding. We had to have our mini bar emptied as our toddler loved "playing" with all the very expensive contents, again our request was dealt with within minutes and a smile!!!
The only real problem we had was our air conditioning didnt work, an engineer came to our room, again quickly but coudnt fix it. We were offered a room change but declined (after all we had just unpacked and it wasnt really too warm) and instead we were given breakfast vouchers. 
My husband and I returned to the hotel at 11pm and ordered a very nice bottle of wine in the bar, We were disapointed to find the bar to be closing after 5mins of arriving. We took our bottle up to our room, which was fine but $100 botttle i did expect a little more customer service! 
All in all, This is a great trendy boutique hotel ideal for couples. Location Is fantastic, staff are gorgeous in every way!

title: “Watch out....”
text:
