My husband and I purchased a Living Social certificate for $99.00 for a room. What the coupon did not say was that it was for a double room on the 2nd floor. They have a very popular loud bar with music and samba on Tuesday nights and we opted to upgrade to a King room on the 4th floor for an extra $69.00 to avoid the loud music. I never checked the website to find out how much the room normally cost on a Tuesday night and I found out it costs$139.00. We got ripped off and the room was dirty and our $75.00 bottle of vodka was a small bottle of Sky. The drawers consisted of a hanging shoe container and the glasses in the room still had lip marks on them. I had seen bad reviews on Yelp before we checked in and other guests had talked about bed bugs. I really checked for them and there were no bed bugs. 
To check in, they require you to sign all these papers and take a copy of your drivers license. It was difficult to get the copy of my license back. When we checked out, they do not give you a statement. They said we would get an email copy. I never received a statement until I called and complained. They charge you $100.00 extra on your card for the mini bar which is still pending 3 days later.. ADVICE:: Stay away and be careful of coupons

title: “6 star service”
text:
Great location, design, comfort, privacy and staff. If you can afford it, just book it.
We stayed at The London last time we were in NY and there is no comparison.

title: “Great rooms, Great customer service, but NOISEY!!”
text:
Great Breakfast buffet- make sure to ask for what's not on the buffet, but included in price. 
Housekeeping comes around early (7am at my room) - make sure to put 'do not desturb' sign
Great Beds, very comfy!

title: “Best Baycation”
text:
For my birthday I wanted to spend the weekend in SF with my friends shopping,eating &clubbing ALL for an inexpensive price. Hotel Union Square full-filled my needs. We we're just blocks from West-field Shopping Center and surrounded by all the my favorite stores, FOREVER 21, BEBE, DSW shoes, PAUL FRANK and my favorite pizza place BLONDIES right across the street! 
Hotel Union Square has GREAT customer service. The hotel was very up to date and had a modern style. The rooms were pretty spacious for being in the city. Most Hotels that I have stayed at in SF, were VERY small and expensive. The beds were very cozy and soft. I really enjoyed the complimentary wine and found it very convenient that they had a computer and WI-FI available for their guest. 
We paid about $100-130 plus tax and $30 for parking, which is a GREAT price for its location!
I would recommend this hotel along with their other "Personality Hotels" to anyone. I also recently stayed at Hotel Vertigo and Hotel Metropolis, their other Personality Hotels and LOVED my stay there too!

title: “Hurricane Sandy Stay at the Commonwealth”
text: Despite their great location, excellent service, comfort and three restaurants within the perimeter of the hotel property, their lack of human compassion and common sense was apparent during the passing of Hurricane Sandy. My wife and I were staying at the Hotel Commonwelath visiting our daughter who is a law student at Boston Univ during the weekend of Oct 26-29,2012. As it is known Hurrican Sandy roared into the Northeast Corridor on October 29, 2012. All of the flights from and to Boston as well as the Northeast corridor were cancelled. Logan Airport was not opened until the afternoon of October 30 and our flight back to San Juan, PR was scheduled to fly out of Logan on October 31, 2012. We asked the hotel if it was ok to stay for the nights of the 29th and 30th of October which they said yes, but charging us @ $359.00 per night. I asked if there was some type of compassion rate due to the fact that we were stuck in Boston. They said no. As I read on the Boston Globe, other hotels in Boston and Cambridge offered compassion rates at lower rates than the Hotel Commonwealth. Hotels such as the W, the Omni offered better rates. We could have moved but we would be far away from our daughter's student dorm.

title: “Don't go there...please!!!”
text:
My review has been a long time coming but I feel the responsability to do it once and for all. I stayed 2 nights at this hotel in February during the course of a school trip. We were a group of 3 teachers and 23 grade 9 students from Montreal that were on a school trip to California and the Grand Canyon. We had stayed in a Hampton inn in South San Francisco and then took a bus to get to LA. I had called the hotel a week before to ask them to put us on the second floor since we were with minors and we did not want them going out the window in the middle of the night. The guy on the phone assured me that everything would be in order when we would get there.....are you guessing the end of the story? Almost all the rooms were with a window facing a large balcony that other rooms could access. I immediately went downstairs to have the issue resolved, even if it was past 10 o'clock at night, and I have to give thanks to the night manager that changed every room to other rooms that did not have balconies. He was not too happy but I did not give him a choice. I told him that they were minors and that it was his responsability to do so.
The kids were very disappointed because we had been in a nice and clean hotel room in San Francisco and ended up in dirty hotel rooms that were scary. I did not sleep a wink all night because people were going up and down the corridor. I looked through the peephole and noticed that it was gentlemen with women. It is probably a hotel where prostitutes take clients. Let's just say that it is not a hotel where you want to take 15 year olds!!!!
The rooms were disgusting....the curtains were dirty....the sheets were dirty....the bedspread was dirty....I was thoroughly disgusted with the place. It was also scary as hell.
The only redeeming aspects are the fact that they switched my students to rooms that did not have balconies and the fact that they allowed us to have a pizza party in their breakfast room. We came in late from our day of sightseeing and did not feel like going out to dinner to a restaurant in the area...did I mention scary area also? The night manager, Peter I think is his name, helped us find specials on pizza and the kids were so happy to come down in their pyjamas to eat pizza and talk until curfew time. Since we did not allow them to have parties in their rooms, the setting was perfect for them. 
I would discourage anyone to stay there. It is a vile place where the manager does his best with what he has. It is not his fault at all that Comfort Inns keeps an establishment like this one under their banner!

title: “Convenient”
text: Found location to be good for sightseeing... within easy walking distance to the Magnicficent Mile and Navy Pier. Many good restaurants in the area as well. Hotel is huge so there is no personalized service. Desk clerks and bellmen were friendly and helpful but the advertised concierge service was non-existent when we were there. Breakfast is included... nice variety and tasty food but the lines are very long and seem to move at a snail's pace. Rooms are OK but are rather dark and dreary and could use some sprucing up. Not much closet space. Pool is very tiny for the size of the hotel. Overall it is a good place to stay if you just want a convenient room and don't plan to spend a lot of time there but not the place if you are looking for a "luxury suite to relax".

title: “So nearly a winner”
text: Location - excellent. Staff - excellent. Room - nearly excellent. The bathroom was agitatingly small, and from what I gather, our bathroom size was indicative of the rest of the hotel. Not that one should ever book a hotel based on the bathroom, but even for 3 nights, the constant banging of elbows on walls whilst at the vanity drove me nuts. I would dearly love to stay here again, but I just couldn't cope with the bathroom again.

title: “Will return!!”
text:
Maybe it was because we were coming from staying in the Embassy for a couple of nights, but I was totally impressed with the InterContinental Chicago. We were in the new tower and the room was small but decorated really cute. Beds were comfy and rooms were clean.
You can't beat the location -- within walking distance of everything!! There is even a free trolley that goes to Navy Pier and drops you off literally within steps of the front door. The concierge were very helpful and polite. If you like wine and atmosphere, Eno is a must!! Very, very cool! I got this hotel for $90/night on Priceline so that may be another reason I liked it too.

title: “Attention to Details!”
text:
On the surface there isn't anything overly spectacular about this hotel; you have to look closely and you'll see why this is one of Seattle's little gems. 
I came to Seattle, once again, on business and the Parmount has so many small details that I kept noticing throughout. You walk in and they have cold, refreshing water available, one regular and one citrus infused, which I'm partial to. They also have fresh apples at the front desk too! And the employees are very friendly, informative and pleasant. I always request the highest room available whenever I travel but most hotels don't really pay attention to it, putting me half way up or so. Not the Paramount; they put me on the highest floor they had!
In the room the details don't end... We're all familiar with the tiny bottles of toiletries hotels provide for you, which lasts one day unless you're a girl then they don't even last that long. Well the Paramount gives you a 10 oz. Bottle of shampoo, conditioner and body was. They also provide Scope, lotion, cue tips and cotton balls! You really don't need ro bring much!
Another little detail is the amount of outlets available. It may not mean much to some people but when you're on business charging a computer, 2 phones and an iPad it's very important; and there are two on the vedside table which is very nice. In addition the location is great. Close to a mall, restaurants and a short walk to Pike's Place Market and the warf. 
Overall a great place, value and location!

title: “Excellent small hotel”
text:
Sophisticated small hotel located on the edge of Beacon Hill. The entrance and the (very small, perhaps too small) reception area are unassuming and, I must say, do not necessarily exude luxury. The rooms, however, are wonderfully appointed with the highlight being a gas fireplace which you can switch on at the push of a button. The hotel underwent a recent renovation and, for the most part, the rooms and communal areas do reflect this. However, some of old furniture seems to have endured in the rooms and is starting to show signs of wear, though, in the scheme of things, this was not an issue at all. In fact, if anything, I think it gave the rooms more character. 
Another definitive plus point is the complementary Lexus car service, something I have never come across before. It certainly beats taking your chances with cabs, which, frankly, are not the best thing about the US. I’d much rather give the $10 it normally costs to take a cab in central Boston as tip to the hotel driver. It didn’t require much planning ahead either – apart from a couple of occasions, the car was available at short notice (30 minutes or less) or no notice at all. 
A la carte breakfast at Moo was also good, if a tad on the expensive side, and the service is first rate across the board.
As mentioned above, the hotel is well located, on the edge of Beacon Hill, a wonderfully quaint neighborhood, 10 minutes walk away from Charles Street, its main thoroughfare. It is also a 20 minutes pleasant walk through Boston Common away from fashionable Newbury Street. However, in my view, the location of the Taj hotel is marginally better – at the very top of Newbury Street and about equidistant to Charles Street as the XV Beacon, I reckon.
Another advantage that other hotels such as the Taj, Four Seasons and Mandarin Oriental may have over the XV Beacon is the view, which is rather limited at the latter. We had two rooms: one was a Corner Studio Room, which had a partial view of Boston Common, which was pleasant (as good a view as you can get at the hotel, I’d imagine) albeit limited, and the other was a Traditional Room, also on a corner, which faced two adjacent blocks, with very little natural light coming in. I’m only speculating here, but I suspect most rooms at the XV Beacon have a similar view, or lack thereof.
A final, minor quibble. The rooms have a good, if slightly antiquated sound system (obviously a remnant of the original rooms), which plays radio and CDs (of which I understand there is an extensive library). However, the system is not connected to the TV, nor is there a connector for iPods (there is a separate iHome device for iPods which isn’t brilliant, really). 
They sent up a cable to connect my iPod to the main sound system but it didn’t really work properly, so I just left it at that. I’m sure that with relatively minor technical fiddling it is possible to have the system connected to both the TV and an iPod dock, which would make better use of the system’s potential. Also, the signal for pretty much every TV channel was patchy. On the plus side (as far as technology is concerned), internet is free and very fast (faster than any hotel connection I have experienced so far). 
All in all, despite the small issues above, I would definitely return to the XV Beacon when in Boston again. The pluses far outweigh the minuses in my view (with the fireplaces and the car service at the very top of the plus list). So much so, that I do not feel it necessary to reflect the minuses in my rating, though I thought they were worth mentioning for the sake of completeness.
A couple of recommendations for the hotel: improve the connectivity of the stereo system in the rooms and perhaps have an additional drawing room at the lobby level where people may linger (the bar at Moo can get busy and, if I remember correctly, does not have any couches). The latter may be difficult to implement due to space constraints but I can’t imagine the former presents many difficulties.
P.S. XV Beacon’s minibars are the most lavishly stocked minibars I’ve ever come across. The one in my room included half bottles of Cheateau d’Yquem, Opus One, Chateau Mouton Rothschild and Chateau Haut Brion (all late 90s vintages and hovering at around $200), Krug champagne, and a very large collection of super premium spirits. So impressive, it verges on the ridiculous.

title: “Great location”
text: We enjoyed staying here because of the proximity to everything - the Sears Tower, great restaurants, and architectural tours on the Chicago River. We found the concierge to be very helpful, making us feel a little less lost in this big city. The parking valet suggested we park ourselves and save some money (parking fees are $28-30 but valet is $38). Be aware of the height restriction on their parking structure - 6'7" and our Honda Element with roof rack was too tall, so we needed to find another parking structure. This hotel is beautiful and while the rooms are small, they are comfortable and clean.

title: “Great location, clean and friendly”
text:
My husband and I recently stayed at the Marriott RiverCenter in San Antonio. We found the hotel very clean and adequate. We made our reservations on the web and got a good rate. Check in was simple and took just minutes. 
The hotel has a lovely lobby area that we enjoyed sitting in to read and talk. There are plenty of elevators to get to the upper rooms. We had a room on the 23rd floor on a corner which had a nice view of the city. The room was clean and was made up daily. It smelled a little musty but that soon faded. Probably due to the humidity. The beds are very comfortable. The room had Bath and Body works products which I thoroughly enjoyed.
The hotel has a nice pool and whirlpool on one of the lower floors. It also has a well stocked exercise room. There is a business center but we did not use it. We appreciated a free airline check in computer in the lobby to print boarding passes at.
We LOVED the location. We chose not to get a car because San Antonio is pretty compact. We found it extremely easy to get around without one and we avoided the car rental fee, the parking fee and the gas. We took a cab from the airport and that was very easy too.
The RiverCenter Hotel is connected to the RiverCenter Mall and to the River Walk itself. Just a very short escalator ride takes you down to the river level where you can shop, eat, get a river boat tour or taxi. There was live music in the outdoor mall area which we enjoyed hearing. The one restaurant near the hotel that we tried was Luciano's Italian. It was excellent for lunch.
What I liked best was the close proximity to the River and the river boats. What I liked least was that we had to go in search of breakfast each day because breakfast is not included with the room (but that seems to be standard in San Antonio). All in all we had a good experience at the San Antonio RiverCenter Marriott.

title: “Characterful Hotel”
text:
We last stayed in this hotel 13 yrs ago. The rooms are still as compact now as then despite a renovation programme. Although small, the room was clean and nicely decorated with some Art Deco character. It has a great location, especially as we arrived by train in Penn Station from Boston and only had a block to walk. It is handy for shopping and has easy access to several subway routes
Check in was quick and smooth and it was nice to see security taken seriously without being heavy handed - you couldn't get to the lifts without showing your key. The Tick Tock diner continues to provide a good range of reasonably priced food around the clock. As someone we met said, "You don't need to go out to eat!"

title: “Good NY Hotel Even for Business”
text:
I stayed here with my wife for 7 days in March in a one bedroom apartment on the 27th floor. The renovation was tasteful. The kitchen knew and unused. There was no toaster which we understand has been deleted from the inclusions but we did request one which was supplied. We used the kitchen for breakfasts and some evening meals and would recommend that the hotel provide additional chairs in the living room to make eating easier. You need to use the coffee table but the desk was suiitable if there had been chairs. 
Check in was annoying as the room did not become available until 4 pm. This is becoming a common problem everywhere. 
The contractors on the Concierge desk were excellent and show tickets were arranged as requested although the service fee of $60 per ticket is a little steep.
I was working and the hotel is fine for getting around NY. My wife enjoyed its central location. It does tend to fill with guests attending Madison Square Garden performances so can be loud with basketball/fight/ concert goers.
We recommend a high floor which ensured it was relatively quiet by NY standards.

title: “It's cozy....not bad..”
text: The hallways remind me of the shining movie. It has what a basic hotel should have, even if it was not "top class" it was good for the trip for the days we as a group used it for. If you just need a get a way place and aren't looking for a "special high dollar" place this is it. So I would rate this as a good hotel but like others say, don't take your wife for an anniversary get a way hotel like this.. This hotel is for people who just need a place to stay and not planning on staying indoors all day.

title: “Not quite there yet...”
text:
I stayed here for three nights last week. I'm not sure if I wasn't impressed because I came from an awesome hotel in San Diego... or if it was truly sub-par. The room was clean but small. I really think the building is haunted. Not just because it's really old and refurbished and the hallways are pitch black... I swear I heard someone open the bathroom door when I was in the shower and my boyfriend woke up in the middle of the night and thought the room was filled with smoke. WTF. 
The room is just meh, but the staff was pretty bad. If you're in the hospitality industry, I'm fairly certain you're supposed to be hospitable. When I first walked into the lobby, the people at the desk looked at me like I was lost. We asked them to book us a trip to Napa as they said they could via email, and we had to remind them the next day. No one had confirmed. When we still didn't hear from them, we went to the desk. The manager was there alone, and had no idea what we were talking about or how they book tours. I asked if I could call myself, and he said sure... I gave him a look like, really? You're going to let a guest make their own reservations? So he called while we stood there and waited. Lamesauce. When we walked upstairs (because the elevator was broken), we found that our room hadn't been made up... it was at least 6pm. We had to call the desk once again and they did send someone up and made another excuse about being understaffed. Perhaps they could hire some of the unemployed who loaf around on the sidewalks outside their doors?
Our sink had no water pressure and the TV turned itself on and off (ghosts, I'm telling you). So we asked for a new room, however the new room was even more creepy so we ended up staying. The only upside is that the manager took $20 off of our room which was nice. And necessary. They had free breakfast (just pastries and yogurt and some toastable waffles), a bar that tried to be trendy, and flea market vintage books in each room. It has potential, but it's just not there yet unfortunately.

title: “Location, location, location”
text: We stayed a night at the Raffaello and enjoyed this small hotel. The doormen and hotel clerks are very nice and helpful. We loved going up to the lovely rooftop and enjoying the city views and some wine. Close to the lakefront and Michigan Ave shopping.

title: “We loved this hotel!”
text:
What a find! We loved this hotel. It's in a super location, around the corner from Grand Central Station, a short walk to Times Square, and lots of great restaurants within walking distance. We traveled as a family of five, with three teenage/young adult kids. 
The hotel was one of our favorites ever. The books in the rooms were fun. The rooms were comfortable, super clean and well appointed. Most notable, however, was the friendliness and helpfulness of the desk staff! We appreciated their warm greetings and helpful suggestions. This was probably the friendliest hotel staff I have ever encountered.
We enjoyed the wine and cheese hour. There were juices and waters for the kids and nice wines, cheeses, crackers and fruits.The complimentary breakfast was better than we expected! 
When we return to NYC, we will definitely book here again!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We were upgraded to a suite which was a nice surprise. Stayed 2 nights could have stayed for more. Front desk staff very friendly and helpful. Hotel close to downtown shops, although we found it a little difficult walking up and down hills. Great YWCA next door which served nice and cheap breakfast. We would recommend this hotel.

title: “Staff was great, room was so-so”
text:
I was in a room that had a tiny bathroom, so small that the door almost hit the toilet when you opened it. The bathroom had such limited counter space i had to store some of my items in the closet. The room was clean and quiet so good on that front but i had a hard time sleeping here though i'm not sure why.
As a top tier Marriott rewards member i asked if any room upgrades were available but was told only a hospitality suite with a murphy bed. No thanks- I need a real bed. 
The location is great if you are going to Georgetown though its 4-5 long blocks to walk to a metro. The front desk and concierge staff were great and very helpful so almost rated this as a 4 instead of a 3.

title: “Perfect place to stay in Seattle”
text:
Inn at the Market is the perfect place to stay if you're visiting Seattle. The location is the best in the city - at the Pike Place Market, which is so much fun! You can also walk to upscale shopping, the waterfront and aquarium, dozens of great restaurants, museums (including the must-see new Olympic Sculpture Park), and so much more.
The staff was gracious and friendly. My room had an incredible view of the Market and the water. Be sure to visit the outdoor deck on the fifth floor - even if the weather doesn't cooperate, the views will impress. I slept very well in the comfy bed. I loved the daybed by the window, too - wish I had one at home!

title: “superb”
text: The Allerton hotel is a nice hotel and well situated for sightseeing The staff were very friendly and helpful The rooms were clean and all towels and bedding were in good condition

title: “Wonderful stay at the Boston Hilton”
text: Stayed 3 nights in Boston as part of a trip to celebrate our Silver Wedding anniversary. We were made to feel welcome from the moment we arrived. The girl at check- in was very pleasant & asked if we were there on holiday. When we said it was for our anniversary she looked to see if a suite was available & upgraded us to one for no extra charge. The room was vast with facilities to make tea/coffee, lovely soaps etc in the bathroom & wonderful fluffy bathrobes - heaven! The hotel was bright, clean & airy & the air-conditioning was up to date. The area is quiet but only a 5 minute walk to Faneuil Hall, Quincy market & the harbour. We did the tram tour & the Freedom trail during our visit. We ate breakfast just across the street in a small cafe where we could get omlette with bacon, home fries & toast for less than $6. The food was freshly cooked & if you didn't mind using plastic plates, knives & forks it was great value. We found the people of Boston very friendly & helpful & throughly enjoyed our trip.

title: “Nice hotel but disappointing room...”
text:
Excellent breakfast. Staff was really helpfull and nice.
Nice hall and lounge bar.
Room very very tiny with a view direct on ... another room (2 meters distance) and noisy due to air conditionning and traffic. Very dull.
Bathroom : bottom of the tube broken 
WC : too close from the wall. Impossible to sit straight and confortably
Not a really good experience.
I appreciated free wifi access in the room.
Luggage fee : 2 $ per piece of luggage : I never paid for luggage before my experience in your hotel.

title: “What a fantastic hotel”
text:
We stayed for 6 nights at The Hotel Boheme and thought it was fantastic. As we had done our homework and read other reviews we understood that this was a small boutique hotel with no lift and were expecting the rooms to be small maybe noisy if we were on the front.
However, I am not sure if staying in room 208 has a distinct advantage over the rooms but it was perfect. We didn't think the room was too small at all, especially compared to hotels in the Centre of London. We had plenty of natural light on the back and it was quiet. It didn't bother us in the slightest that we had to carry our bags up some stairs.
The staff were extremely polite and helpful and couldn't do enough for us. The location is absolutely a plus point, it is safe with plently of restaurants and bars. Washington Square is round the corner, the Beat history on your doorstep and a 20 minute stroll takes you right down to fisherman's wharf and the piers.
The only thing that slightly frustrated us was the noise of the showers when guests woke up early, they were very loud in our room but we used our ear plugs we had bought just in case and we were able to sleep really well.
I would definitely recommend this hotel to friends and stay there again without hesitation.

title: “Great Stay”
text: From the young lady at the front desk to the nice rooms but Gabby the hotel breakfast manager was a joy to be around and she was very helpful in accomodating needs. The rooms were so clean and the service lady for 204 took pride in keeping room up to par!!

title: “As the real estae agents would say Location Location Location”
text: Have to agree with nearly eveyone, the staff are so off, we took the attitude that it was better than the other place we had been stopping at in NY and we tried not to care about the ignorant staff. We are going to stay there again later this year and again will ignore the rude staff.

title: “Skyline: Great Deal for Those Traveling by Car”
text:
We stayed at the Skyline Hotel on the July 1st/July 4th long weekend. The hotel is a great deal particularly if you are planning on driving to New York. Parking is less than half the price of other hotels and the location is very easy to access by car (limited in-city navigation needed). 
We had no problems at all during our stay. The bathroom and room were super clean. The location of the hotel is close walking distance to lots of attractions and the subway for longer distance travels. 
We were confused about the comments made on this site that the hotel was in a bad area. It did not seem that way to us at all and we were two females who traveled around the town at all hours of the day/evening.
Hotel staff were not particularly friendly as some reviews have pointed out however not rude at all. 
I think the negative reports on this website reflect people looking for a luxury hotel. You will not get that in New York for $100 a night! The Skyline is a great deal for the price and is more than adequate for those of us whom don't need a mint on their pillowcase.

title: “Pre baby escape to NYC”
text: First time in NYC and our final holiday as a couple before our first baby arrives so we were after a hotel with a bit of extra room and kitchen facilities. The Eastgate was simply excellent, the decor could possibly do with a little updating but the staff and room were great. We went for a junior suite which was superbly equipped with a good sized kitchen and a comfortable king size bed and pull out sofa. Good shower, clean room and plenty of space in the lounge area. We requested a room in a quiet part of the hotel and were located on the 24 floor which was ideal as the lifts were quick and easy to access. The reception staff were excellent. We had an evening return flight to London and were allowed to keep our room until 2pm without extra charge. Safety depost boxes were available for no charge in reception. A big thank you to Negesti Thompson who was so helpful to us and also booked us tickets for an excellent helicopter flight to see the sites from up in the air. Other staff we met were really helpful including the guys who booked us a town car to return to JFK. Hotel was clean, safe and friendly, we will stay again on next trip and recommend to friends.

title: “Convenient”
text: Very easy place to stay near the airport. We arrived around midnight and had a second flight the next morning. The shuttle from this property runs 24 hours and came to pick us up soon after the luggage came off the carousel. It was a short minibus trip back to the hotel. The room was generously sized and had a separate sofa to form a sitting area. Shuttle service back to the airport was similarly convenient. The front desk clerk was especially helpful and the room was clean and comfortable. They had a quick breakfast option until 6AM when the full service restaurant opened. We didn't stay long enough to explore all of the amenities but the time spent was very pleasant and I would definitely return.

title: “Needs to be more pet-friendly”
text: The hotel is nice and does have great views. There are two towers and they are not close together. I stayed in the Marina Tower which seems to be the main building. I had booked this hotel because it was near Ocean Dog Beach, Balboa Park, and Mission Bay. Plus, the website and even the employees state it's a pet-friendly hotel. Pet-friendly in that you are sequestered to the lower level rooms off to the side (think they call them “villas”) facing the tennis courts and parking. If you have a pet, this is where you will automatically be placed. They claim it’s great because the room leads off to a patio area with grass. That’s fantastic if the view happens to be the harbor and not a high chained fence surrounding the tennis court, and if you were with another person in the room and not alone since the patio isn’t closed off. Anyone could walk from the parking lot to your patio door. Also, the room they gave me felt like a dungeon so I’m thinking the rest may be the same. Since I was alone, I asked for a different room on a higher level. I was given another room but had to wait for the key outside the new room over 20 minutes because they said it was busy at the front desk. I finally had to walk back to the front lobby (no easy feat with suitcase and curious dog in tow) to get the key that was forgotten. Because of this ordeal, I was given free breakfast the next morning. I was appeased because I had a room on the second level where the balcony faced the hotel pool and free breakfast. That is until I tried to claim my free breakfast. The breakfast is in the restaurant as buffet style. The policy is not to leave your dog in the hotel room alone. But I couldn’t bring my dog into the restaurant either. The hotel has a great patio area but it’s not used for breakfast. So I was a bit irritated and showed it. The staff sprung into action again and allowed me to sit on the patio and be waited on. The lovely waiter brought me coffee and juice and watched my dog while I went to the buffet. If you are going to advertise as being pet-friendly then make it pet-friendly. I felt at the time that this hotel didn’t fully understand what pet-friendly meant, but I guarantee you they do now. I just hope they open up the patio for meals so guests with dogs can enjoy. It’s not just about accommodating for a pet but for the owner too who has a pet. The plus of this hotel for me is the bonfires along the harborside. I was able to have a glass of wine (yes, I walked my dog to the bar and ordered a glass…how else would I have gotten it?) at a bonfire area and speak with other guests for several hours so I found it very relaxing.

title: “Horrible Customer Service”
text: Horrible customer service, horrible parking situation, hung up on by customer service staff, no compensation for unsatisfactory experience. Huge line for parking garage. Construction was unbelievable. Ended up paying $20 to park in the Casino Garage despite our staying at the actual Greektown Hotel. Greektown would not validate our parking at this garage to park overnight. Complete dissatisfaction for entire stay. Would not recommend this hotel to any family, friend or enemy. Poor upkeep. Was offered a buffet voucher for our trouble? Not a chance. We will not be staying here again.

title: “Never Again”
text: Had to stay because of business. Check in was fine. The towels were spotty. One towel even had hair entwined in the fibers. Yuck! There was hair on on the sink that didn't belong to either me or my roommate. The bed spread was dirty and the bed sheets were ragged/torn. The heat/air conditioning unit did not work properly. It was hot in the room so I had to open a window then at some point the air kicked in so during the night it got too cold. I will NEVER stay here again. Gave comment card to front desk and employee didn't ask any questions. Just said OK.

title: “Surprising Little Gem”
text: I had my doubts about this hotel when I first blind booked through a third party site. The price was just a little too good and the location too perfect for it to be real. We breathed a sigh of relief when we walked into our room. Upon arrival they "upgraded" us to a top floor, corner room and what an awesome room it was. We were staring right at the Hancock building and lake Michigan. For those of you planning a visit to the American Girl store, you will be happy to know, it is half a block away and within view of the hotel. The beds were comfortable and not too small. The bathroom was very nice, updated and clean. The shower was a bit finicky but that is to be expected in an older building. And the room did have a slight musty odor upon arrival but that went away after a few hours - again, older building. The hotel staff was courteous and attentive. They were more than happy to point us in the direction of cheaper parking rather than pay for valet - they do not have a parking lot on site. There are plenty of shops and restaurants in the area as it is just off of Michigan avenue. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I came to Hollywood on for my Jetski rental business in which I was referred to use this hotel by my friend. I realized the hotel is in a great location, rooms are as expected, and the staff is attentive. Since then, I've stayed here multiple times and will continue to stay here. I definitely recommend this place.

title: “Unforgettable stay”
text: I visited New York at the end of February with a friend for a three night stay at the Waldorf Astoria. Upon arrival at check-in we were ignored by the majority of the desk clerks but a charming lady called Monika smiled at us and welcomed us to the hotel and indulging me by not laughing at my faltering few words of Polish (she could speak flawless English by the way). We stayed in a lovely double/double room with separate dressing room and bathroom on the 17th floor overlooking Park Avenue (and consequently further away from the traffic noise which was a definite bonus). I have visited New York twice in the past and stayed in rooms the size of a shoe box so it was a definite bonus to be so well accommodated. I wouldn't say the room was spotless or perfectly decorated but it had a certain elegance and charm which you rarely find. All in all worth every penny. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Hilton Finally Hits a Homerun!”
text:
I have been growing very tired of Hilton's less than imaginative room decor in all of their new hotels. While they are nice, they are very corporate. With the likes of Aloft by W Hotels, along with Element - Hilton had been ignoring market trends and pricing.
I stayed at this property for an work event at the convention center. The walk to the Harbor and Convention Center area is about 1/2 mile downhill (on the way there....) and very do-able in the morning, however, when the sun goes down the sense of safety and security disappear with the daylight. I've been traveling to Charm City for work for five year now, and as the recession has been prolonged, the crime in the city has sky rocketed. However.... the neighborhood around the hotel is very safe, and I wasn't afraid at all to walk in the neighborhood at night.
The hotel is fantastic - the concept is totally different than anything else that Hilton is doing. The property has a very small and comfortable feeling - while having hundreds of rooms, there only 9-10 rooms on each floor - so it feels very small.
The breakfast service is a game changer as well - it's a departure from a buffet style, and yet there is still something for everyone.
The rooms are very well appointed, spacious, and geared toward the extended stay traveler - they are well suited for a night or a month. It's great having the kitchenette in the room.
The decor is very trendy and comfortable!
If you are planning a stay in downtown Baltimore, I definitely suggest the Home 2!
Great stay, friendly staff, and fantastic rooms!
I had a AAA rate of $103 - and instead of paying $25 a night for Valet parking, I parked a couple blocks away in the garage next to the Basilica - and that was only $24 for two nights. I parked in front of the hotel, took my luggage to my room, and then moved my car to the garage. The garage is very safe, well lit, and easy to access. I'm not a fan of Valet parking - I want my car when I want it, not when the valets have time to get it.
As with nearly all hotels that have a food shop available in the lobby - everything is very over priced, so avoid it if at all possible.
The only negative was the ice machine on my floor wasn't working.
So, Hilton, you finally caught up with the trends, now let's continue to repeat the success!

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text: Stayed here for two nights after a long haul trip. We were immediately upgraded to a suite. We have nothing but praise for the quality, location and service of this hotel..

title: “Welcome respite”
text: Arrived at the Nikko at 11pm after about 18 hours travelling. I asked for a quiet room on an upper floor and was straightaway upgraded to a corner superior room on 19th floor. I was so grateful and had a fantastic night's sleep. Room was large, with floor to ceiling windows looking over downtown San Francisco. Lovely bathroom. Shame I couldn't negotiate a late checkout but there was a huge convention in town, so understandable. Overall, highly recommended.

title: “Excellent Location”
text:
Pros: 
* Excellent location between Millenium Park and The Magnificent Mile
* Huge bathroom with glass shower and bathtub, seperate "toilet closet", hanging line across bathtub for line drying hand washables
* Nice big room and good view even in a lower floor room
* Heavenly beds! Very comfortable, nice linens and duvet, plush pillows
* Very clean and minimalistic in decor
* Excellent maid service daily
* Room service delivered on time each morning...beautiful set up
* Friendly staff
* Quiet
Cons:
*No drawer space!
*$14.95/24 hours internet - This is 2011, please provide internet free of charge for a $300/night room!!!
As you can see, the pros far outweigh the cons! We will be returning in October for our fall vacation!
*
*

title: “Nice hotel in downtown Philly”
text:
This hotel was exactly what I'd expect from a Ritz-Carlton hotel...service was excellent, the room was nice, and the was restaurant wonderful. I would definitely stay here the next time I am in Philadelphia. 
We took Amtrak from DC and the hotel was a quick cab ride from the train station. The hotel is also walking distance to numerous shops and restaurants. The distance to Independence Hall was a little far to walk (depending on the weather, maybe) but it was again a quick cab ride.

title: “Stay here for the location and service”
text:
It is smack in the heart of Manhattan, a few steps from Times Square, although quite enough not to get disturbed by the street.
we stayed at the Casablanca for three nights in the beginning of february.
We stayed in the junior suite on the fourth floor facing the back. There was no view to speak of, but you could see the reflections of the neon signs from times square in the windows on the opposite building. There were some generator sounds that had a low humming sound from the neighbouring building, which was disturbing on the second floor but tolerable on the fourth. Not sure if this sound was a temporary sound or something thats always there.
The reception and breakfast personell was outstandingly nice and accomodating. Truly top level. Breakfast was nice, although not a very wide selection. But nice. The afternoon wine and cheese was also a nice touch.
Rooms very slightly dated in the decore and standard but comfortable beds and clean. There where no minibar or fridge, but you could have one put in your room if you needed one. The bathroom had alot of basic toiletry that you could use, although not top quality but not something you would expect for this price range. A nice touch.
Depending on your departure time during the day, be sure to reserve a cab well in advance since there is some sort of driver shift aroung 1800 that made drivers hesitant to go out to the airport around that time.
The italian restuarant next door was very nice with extremely large portions and a family style atmosphere. Well worth a visit.
All in all, the best with the hotel was the location, service on the staff and several small benefits like the wine and chees, etc that makes it stand out as a really good choice for a short visit.

title: “Great Value”
text: A great value for a place to sleep and shower. Modern and efficient design readapting an old office building along the lines of a European hostel (although in this case a luxury European hostel). Breakfast was nothing special, but the fact that one was offered in a New York budget hotel is exceptional.

title: “Has No Idea What Cust. Service Is”
text: Customer service can make or break a hotel. Many things can be overlooked if the staff is helpful, courteous, and knowledgeable. And when the customer service is bad, it makes everything else sour in comparison. My recent stay at the Hyatt Regency Chicago feels like a disaster. When we first arrived, we had paperwork stating that we had pre-paid. Our card had been run 9 days prior to our stay, when we booked it, and the hotel had conveniently forgotten this when we checked in. They assured us that we would not be double-billed and demanded we give them our card again. So we spent the whole trip worried that a rather large charge (we were staying many nights) would end up charging twice to our card. We were also given a discount on valet through AAA, the hotel at first knew about it, then had no idea, then knew again, then ended up charging us the full rate. The final straw on this camel's back was that our brand new car was damaged in excess of $1000 by the valet, who backed the car right into a pole and attempted to cover it up.

title: “LOVED IT, Great Staff and Excellent Location.”
text: I booked a Two Double Beds Room in this hotel at a very good rate for 2 nights arriving on March 24. Because of the mixed reviews I went to the hotel with not so high expectations but it turned to be VERY nice!!. We arrived at 3:00 PM on a Wednesday an we greeted by a friendly bellman called Johnny who was always very helpful during our stay. There was nobody in the qeue for check-in and three people in the desk. We were asked if we wanted high or low floor and were given a room on 23 floor with an excellent view of the river, the beds were sooo comfortable. The hotel a GREAT place called the Club Level Lounge on 33 floor were you can go an have complimentary acces to Wifi, computers with unlimited printing, beverages and some food. At this place there was a guy called Rene that was veeeery nice to us and would always chat and give us cookies to take to the room. Also, my son used the pool which was complimentary. The location is excelent, over the river, two blocks to Michigan Ave and has a taxi stop right on it. There are also shuttles to Ohare running every hour from the hotel. All in all, we had a great experience!!

title: “Very nice but some serious design flaws”
text:
Spent 5 nights at the Sheraton including New Years Eve. Booked on Priceline and got a very good rate at $85 per night. A good rate, especially for New Years.
The Sheraton claims to have just been redone, and the room appeared to be very fresh and nice, with large flat screen TV and nice linen. The lobby is also fresh with a good lounge and comfortable spaces.
The location is excellent, far closer to the wharf then I had expected, an easy 3 minute walk from all the action but far enouugh off that the hotel is very quite. Also, it is mid way between the wharf and pier 39 which makes it very convienient. 
The rooms run somewhat on the small side. In fact, we requested a roll away bed in our room with 2 full size beds and were told that the hotel does not have roll away beds anymore. The room would have had (barely) enough room for one but apparently it would have been a fire hazzard. OK - so the teenagers had to share a bed.
The bathrooms was decent, but with one MAJOR mistake... the sink in outside the door to the room with the toilet and shower. For some reason, there is only one light switch that turns on the lights both over the sink and in the bathroom - thus if you want to shower or... at night while others are sleeping, you do so in the dark or wake everyone up. Not well thought out. Also of note in the bathroom, the toilet is very small - if you are of generous perportion, you know how uncomfortable this can be. Beware.
The 3rd and final negative of this hotel was that the air conditioner/heater had not been replaced. In this day to not have a proper thermostat is annoying. The unit on our room required constant adjustment and turning on and off to regulate the temp. 
Overall, I considered this hotel a bargin for the price I got, but I would not have paid more or booked directly. I really liked the location but would probably try the Raddison right accross the street in the hopes that the issues above would not be repeated.
P.S. If you are at Fishermans Wharf, try the "Crab House" for dinner.... really a fabulous meal!

title: “Great Location, SPG Member Beware”
text:
Let me start by saying that this hotel is in a great location for visiting Little Italy, China Town, Tribeca, and Brooklyn. The area to the right of the hotel is a little seedy, but otherwise it is lively with plenty of sidewalk shopping.
The hotel itself is clean and modern with standard Sheraton amenities.
On the 21st floor there is a Club Lounge with an amazing outside terrace with an awesome view of the city. I believe Gold (not sure about Gold since the first time we stayed we were not offered free breakfast) and Platinum members can eat breakfast there for free. Food is good, coffee excellent.
On our second visit to the hotel in January, we were promised, as now Platinum members, a Suite upgrade. Excited we went to check our room on the 5th floor and were immediately disappointed. The rooms was not much larger than their standard and the view was terrible. The small windows looked out at a brick wall. We then called the front desk, She told us there were no suites available, however we could have a room on the 17th floor with a better view. Of course we took it and it was a beauitiful view, directly across from the Empire State Bldg., but the room was standard, not an upgrade. Upon departure, we did not convey our displeasure due to the fact that they did change our room. However, when I returned home, I immediately contacted Sheraton. I received an apology from them as well as an email contact from the hotel itself with an apology and a promise to do better next time.
I am not saying that I would not stay at this property again. It is convenient to visit the above-,mentioned areas for a short trip. We had reservations at Patricia's in Brooklyn which was a short taxi ride away. Patricia's is a great place for good fun and authentic homemade Italian fare. However, I would not choose it if just visiting NYC due to the lack of better treatment for Platinum members.

title: “Overnight in Chicago”
text: Very nice facility. Staff was very polite and friendly. Breakfast choices were good and staff re-stocked continuously, dining room was well attended. Comfortable beds. Thank you.

title: “Ok at normal rates but not at higher than normal rates”
text: Stayed twice due to flight cancellations and it was fine. Then I stayed for one week when every single hotel downtown was booked except the Four Seasons and paid the highest rates I've ever seen listed at this location. A big plus was dining at the bar and room service was very good. The staff was also helpful for getting a package sent and other requests. Overall, food and service compensated for old rooms and noise. At normal rates this is average, but at near full rates, you can't help but feel let down.

title: “Worst hotel for a conference or meeting ever”
text:
BEWARE! You will not have a smooth meeting here. I do tons of meetings at hotels and have never had such a sub-par experience. They're not service-oriented enough and honestly a Motel 6 would do better in terms of quality. 
-Unresponsive Convention Services Management. Expect to make requests 3+ times prior to and during your event before they acknowledge your needs, let alone take action- that will require you to follow-up another 3+ times. Then they will make excuses or blame you. Check every order, contract, reciept for accuracy. 
- The meeting rooms are in the basement so you won't have cell service at all and have to go to the lobby to make/ recieve any calls. 
- You should also know that the whole place smells like Glade airfreshener and stale cigarette smoke.
-Often when staying for business the hotel will send a gift basket or bottle of wine to the VIP's, like our client who happened to be the CEO. They wouldn't tell me what was sent to him but did say it was "very nice"- it was an old orange, old pear, and old apple in a bowl covered in plastic wrap.

title: “Wish I had stayed somewhere else”
text:
Stayed here for my burthday using Hilton Hhonors points last year and, as one other reviewer aptly put it, it was a disappointment. The entrance is grand but the carpet not only looks like it is from the 70s but has all the stains to prove it, which I found kind of disgusting and not something I think should be tolerated at a luxury hotel. At the front desk I asked if it was possible to have an upgrade but no, according to the manager the hotel was completely booked. When I arrived at my room, it was very small and looked just like any other hotel room, I am extremely sad to say. A view of another building, and right next to the elevator. I assumed they saved the 'bad' rooms for Hilton Hhonors guests. The carpet had a horrendous moldy odor, and the light switch and doorbell were literally haning off the wall, which is at the least unsightly and at the most a fire hazard. When I called to complain they couldn't offer any solutions. The next morning I asked the concierge where I could get breakfast in the hotel and he informed me that the restaurant had closed. There was a huge breakfast buffet being set up in the lobby behind us. When I queried about that he looked at me dubiously and said, 'Yes but that breakfast is [XX amount] dollars". How insulting! I can't believe someone would actually say that in real life!
I have stayed many many places around the world, and at hotels I felt were much more luxurious - and much more well-kept - than the Waldorf. I do not plan on staying here again. Wish I had spent my points elsewhere.

title: “Remarkably nice”
“if you get a crib make sure you ask for bedding for it!”
text: We arrived at the hilton at 12:30 a.m. after a late flight. I had called ahead of time to ask for a crib in the room. It was not in the room when we got there although they brought it a short time later. Keep in mind it is 1 o'clcok in the morning and I have been traveling all day with two small children who just want to go to sleep. When the crib arrived my husband went to the door and did not see that the crib only had a vinal covered mattress in it with no bedding at all. We tried several times to call the front desk to have bedding brought up to the room but no one answered the phone. The baby ended up sleeping with me who didn't get any sleep because I was worried he would fall off the bed. With that said the beds were very comfortable, the room was clean, and quiet. So I would stay there again with not kids. ps. the breakfast (2 eggs, bacon, juice and toast) is $26.00...no kidding!!

title: “Nice Location but lacked warmth”
text: I have mixed emotions about writing this review. I've stayed at numerous hotels across the country and am quite particular on what I like/don't like. So I don't want to sway people, just write my opinion. I stayed at this hotel in late May and the hotel was very busy, booming actually. The lobby seemed to always be busy, busy, busy. It wasn't relaxing to walk into after a few long days of work. I do admit that this could be attributed to my state of mind at the time. But to make matters worse, my room was quite small with a very limited view. While the hotel focused on being trendy, they missed the boat on some rather simple emenities such as what was offered in the rooms. Simple things like useful toilettries. The location was the saving grace of this hotel, but I don't think I would ever re-book. Plenty of good hotels in the DC area.

title: “Overall decent hotel - but not what we expected”
text:
I'd like to start this review by mentioning we also stayed at the Embassy Suites downtown hotel and thought it was a gazillion times better than this Hyatt for several reasons - mainly it's warmth as well as location.
The location of the Hyatt was great in regards to Sea World - and the hotel provided a water taxi to the park for a minimal fee of $7 each. Also, the view from the room was amazing.
The room was clean and the bed was comfortable but overall we would not stay here again. There simply wasn't much to do in the area (aside from Sea World and Mission Beach a few blocks away) and we felt isolated from the rest of the city. If you're going for isolation, then this is the place for you.
The pools looked like they were nice and the slides looked fun - but it was frankly so windy in the area we never went in. 
Also, the hotel, while overall beautiful and nice, it was extremely "cold" and uninviting. We paid for the upgrade to a free breakfast (sounds funny, no?) and literally walked out of the breakfast area due to the snobbiness of it all. My husband and I are "upper class" so it wasn't as if we were out of place - it was just frankly too exclusive and cold and not something we wanted to be a part of. Instead we went to the Einstein Bagel shop and had an enjoyable and relaxed breakfast on a pier and had a great time. 
Another con was the parking situation. We realize most if not all hotels have a required valet in the area, but the valet was $25 and the self-park was $20. Seemed ridiculous when we should have been able to park in the HUGE lot for free. This hotel really seems to nickel and dime you.
Again, overall it was a decent hotel - but we wouldn't return to it and really really wished we didn't leave the Embassy Suites downtown hotel which was better in every way.
PS - One comment about Mission Beach was the incredible amount of seaweed washing up. Coming from NJ, we've never seen anything like this and it was amazing and fairly gross. Perhaps more can be done to keep the beach clean? When I say it was a lot of seaweed, I'm not exaggerating when I say that it was literally washing up in piles larger than a big person.

title: “Great Service”
text: We stayed at the US Grant over the 4th of July and had a great time. The location is near all downtown activities. The service exceeded our expectation. One day, we left the do not disturb sign on the door until 5pm!! We removed it and went to dinner. We did not expect to get any service that day but to our surprise, when we returned at 8pm, the room was clean and the beds were turned down with little chocolates on the pillows. Slippers were placed on the side of each bed and the light were on but dimmed!! Fantastic US Grant!! We love you!! Now that's the kind of service that makes your day!! Also the beds were soooo comfortable I sank right down into the soft sheets and slept like a baby. Dreaming..........

title: “Great Hotel..Clean, Comfy, Great Service”
text: We loved our stay at this hotel. It was clean and the look was great. We loved our beds and slept well in comfort. My only complaint...we were right next to the back enterance. I truly believe I would have slept better if the back door was required to be locked by at least 10:00pm. Several young people who were partying kept coming in and out the back door at all hours of the night. They were smoking, drinking, and making a hell of a loud commotion. Itwoke my baby three times! The hotel command should make it a priority to only allow guests to enter from the front entetance past 10:00 pm or maybe even 9PM. After 1:00pm, the commotion finally ended and me and my kiddos could sleep. Great hotel, just needs to monitor innapropriate and intoxicated guests entering the building. LOCK BACK DOORS AT APPRORIATE HOUR at night.

title: “Excellent Hotel and Service! Best Hotel I lived in”
text:
I am a frequent traveler and I have lived 80 or so nights in this hotel. The hotel staff is customer excellence personified. Every night is an experience in itself. The staff is so much friendly that you feel like you are in home. Philip Marcano, Candis, Salahah, Edward (EJ), Ryan Todd, Tony, Brianna etc, great and extremely friendly folks. They have been nice every time I have stayed here for 25 weeks. Thank you folks, for your courtesy and I look forward staying you are the hotel for many more nights. 
For Hotel:
Excellent and cosy rooms
Great Beds, really comfortable
Nice Breakfast Buffet, very good selections
Lounge with necessary snacks and drinks for Platinum
Very Good Room Service
Great Location
Best Part - GREAT STAFF!!!!!
It has been a pleasure staying at this hotel
Best,
Jitesh Desai

title: “Staff response to event”
text: During our staff at this hotel, we encountered an issue with another guest and were concerned for our safety. I called the front desk to express our concerns and received prompt response from all of the staff. There were no questions. Once we stated our concern, we were quickly moved to another room so the staff could deal with the other guest. I felt the staff's response was excellent. It was unfortunate we encountered this event, but the event is not just defined by something bad. The response to the event many times can ultimately define how we feel about the event. I will feel comfortable returning to this hotel because of the staff. Specifically to Sarah and Deborah...thank you so much. I spoke with Annalesha (manager) to express my satisfaction, as many times they only hear the not so pleasent situations. I would also like to thank the Engineer and Security Officer that assisted us. All were very professional and put the customer first.

title: “Wonderful experience at the Palomar”
text:
I wanted to write a review because not only did we have a wonderful experience during our recent stay at the Hotel Palomar in Philadelphia but also because this was in contrast to a visit a year and half ago when we did not have a good experience. We gave them another try because after our earlier visit they genuinely seemed to want to make it up to us. They had just opened then so we thought we'd give them the benefit of the doubt. 
This time the staff was attentive and responsive. For this trip we had a baby with us and they made every effort to make sure baby, Mom and Dad were comfortable and happy. It's the little things that count, the staff remembered our baby's name and what activity we did and asked how it went. All hotels will give recommendations but the staff at Hotel Palomar provided me with a map and hand written directions so I could walk with a stroller to my destination. 
Besides the personal attention from the staff, this hotel is a very cool place to hang out. We loved the happy hour nightly in the lobby, we had wine and truffle popcorn each day to unwind.

title: “Nice clean rooms, short on everything else....”
text: Clean rooms, lobby and breakfast area was hot, lady working in breakfast area was not very friendly or helpful. Had spilled milk on floor and did not bother to wipe it off. I almost slipped and fell. she kept bending over and could see her thong, not very pleasant when you are trying to eat. Restrooms were very dirty. Had to use mens restroom because the womens restroom was unusable.

title: “Lovely little place”
text: It was our first trip to LA and after a long journey from the airport (due to the traffic which seemed to be a nightmare the whole time we were in LA)we were pleasantly surprised with the Brentwood Inn. It looks quaint from the outside and it was nice to be able to park right outside our room. It was a nice touch that they baked fresh cookies and muffins which were left in Reception and were sooo good. The room was very clean and cosy. If I for some reason ever was to go to LA again then this would be where I would stay as its in a nice area and near enough to Santa Monica for the restaurants etc.

title: “Excellent Location!!!”
text:
Spent two nights at the Witt for some shopping and meeting friends. We took the train from Indiana, the hotel is about a five minute walk from the station. The location of the hotel is a plus for shopping it is within walking distance to Water Tower Place and Macy's. 
The hotel is very nicely decorated, the rooms seemed to be a little small but very comfortable. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We enjoyed our stay at the Witt and would return for another stay.

title: “Beautiful Resort, great service, bring some cash.”
text:
I stayed in this resort for 2 nights/3 days. It is quit possibly the best overall customer service I have ever experienced. When given the wrong room number for my meeting by an employee because of last minute changes, the same person tracked me down and corrected the mistake. I was most impressed with their detailed information.
While eating lunch a fellow colleague of mine asks about the calories of the desserts and the employee working the lunch knew what each of them were. I spoke casual with one of the bellmen and he did a very honest job in selling the extra family events offered like: A duck race, nightly movies at the pool, caged animals for the kids to see, etc. The employees of this J.W. Marriott have been trained well and work with sincerity.
Like most resorts it is made to be all inclusive. When looking at the prices during peak travel times, I guess for my family of 4 to stay, play, and eat here it would be $450 a day.
The pool is very nice. The lazy river is 3/4 of a mile long. There are two 300 foot slides. The exercise room is wonderful and open 24 hours a day.
It is pricey in every way. As impressive of a place as this is, I don't feel it would be one in which I would want to pay. Valet parking is $25 a day plus tax; wireless internet is 14.99 plus tax; and spa services for massage therapy was $130 for 50 minutes. It reminded me of cross between the Gaylord Texas and The Great Wolf Lodge

title: “amazing service”
text: I must say the staff at this hotel made a rough business trip relaxing. KELLY NORTON in the resurant was the highlight. Her energy for servng us was unbeleivable. She is an asset to you staff and should be thanked by managment for they positive attitude she displays on behalf of the hotel.

title: “Lovely hotel with a disappointing experience”
text: We loved everything about the Chancellor Hotel: its location, the cosy and clean rooms, the free cookies in the lobby, a good breakfast at the Luques restaurant, and so on ... except the view! After writing to the manager and being assured we'd have a room on a high floor with a view over Union Square, we ended up on the 7th floor, with a view onto..... the wall across the street!

title: “"Start spreading the news..."”
text: I've been a yearly or bi-yearly guest at the Blakely (formerly Gorham) Hotel in NYC for over twenty years. Each visit just gets better. I often wonder - is this really the best hotel property in NYC? I comb the hotel and travel sites, visit web pages, but in the end, I continue to book at the Blakely. Why? Convenience, comfort, ambience, decor, cleanliness, safety, and service, service, service. These are not attendants or a staff, they are people with names, helpful faces, encouraging knowledge of the vast city. From Betty in reservations, to the front desk attendants (Sherwyn and Alex are great) to the concierge staff (Jonathan, Edouardo, Reuben) to the doormen, bellmen, housekeeping staff, these people become your family during the stay. The rooms - luxurious - always spotless, flawless, welcoming, comfortable. The marble baths, the kitchenettes, the beds - oooh - the beds. Rooms are almost too comfortable to leave. Bars, bodegas, breakfast diners, great dining, grocery stores, and the Carnegie Deli within five minutes walk. During my recent stay, 4/11-4/17 - my party was scheduled to check-out on the 16th. However an unexpected Nor'easter kept us extra days. The hotel staff were immediately at my disposal promising us our room, even under over-sold conditions, and any other assistance to make us feel welcome, allay stress, and to get us home quickly and safely. NYC has much to offer - great theatre, incomprable dining, Central Park, tourist sites, shopping, but at "the top of the list" - the Blakely on W. 55th. Your home away from home "in the city that never sleeps. Surely Kander and Ebb had the Blakely in mind when they wrote their anthem, "New York, New York."

title: “Frustrating Check In - Strong Service”
text: I had booked my two night reservation thru Expedia several days in advance. Upon arrival late at night I was informed that they were overbooked and no room was available due to a very large convention in town. Front Desk Manager Dustin got me comped at the Double Tree at the Tech Center and paid for cabs to hotel and back in the morning. It had been very frustrating, but they got my first night reimbursed back from Expedia and put me in a massive suite for the second night. Hotel staff were all very friendly and helpful despite an uncomfortable screw up.

title: “Excellent staff, great customer service, perfect location= One Magnificent Hotel”
text:
I would like to take a moment to talk about my stay at the Omni Hotel in Chicago (6/26-7/2). My complaints were: having to use 2 seperate elevators to get to my room, that my carpet had a strange dampness to it, and the lack of appliances. Since my stay was 6 nights, these details were probably more noticeable. I did call for a mini fridge, which they promptly installed and I should have asked if a microwave was also available, but I did not. While I may have used these "inconveniences" as a reason to consider staying elsewhere next time, the customer service I received completely outshined those things. My friend and I were there for a nursing conference and both stayed at the Omni. From the moment we arrived, the doorman, Mirham, welcomed us with such a genuine smile and pleasantness. As busy as he was he took the time to introduce himself, get our names and a little background info on us and offered to help with anything during our stay. Being a manager in healthcare who has attended numerous customer service courses, I know that they are all "trained" to do these things however, I must admit I was very surprised when Mirham greeted me by my name the next morning and every time he saw me during my stay. I watched how busy they can get with people constantly arriving and departing, needing directions or a cab, & assisting with luggage. His ability to to tend to everyone's needs and still take time to greet his guests by name and make them feel special is the truest example of GREAT customer service! 
 All of the staff were wonderful. The front desk clerks were very polite and accomodating to my requests and ensured I was happy with my room. The housekeepers did an excellent job of cleaning my room and were always so friendly and smiling when I would see them. I even declined turndown service one evening but did have her help me decide on which shoes to wear. She really took the time to talk with me and help me make a decision and I think we both enjoyed just having a conversation with each other. Every single staff member I came in contact with during my week stay was professional, courteous, and made me feel important. 
Everytime I walked into their hotel I felt like I was at home. Recognition is extremely important so please let your staff know that what they are doing IS truly making an impact and is not going unnoticed. I have told numerous people about my experience at the Omni Chicago and will reccommend you to everyone I know. I look forward to returning in the very near future.
